100212.label: Project Objectives
100212.value: To design and prepare classes of helical metallopolymers derived from metal-Schiff base moieties that exhibit different conformations and crosslinking properties. To investigate environment- and stimuli-induced dynamic conformational changes occurring in helical metallopolymers, and monitor associated chiroptical and photophysical responses. To design and prepare crowded metal-organic assemblies that can function as host scaffolds, and undergo self-assembly processes directed by pi-interlinked interactions, and study structural and substituent effects on aggregation behavior. To investigate applications of helical metallopolymers and pi-stacked assemblies. [Work on application studies will be reduced in scope due to insufficient funding.]

100212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100212.value: Interest in artificial helices stems from the prevalence of helical structures in Nature and their remarkably diverse functionality. The focus of this proposal is the design, synthesis and application of helical metallopolymers and pi-stacked multinuclear architectures. Notwithstanding coordination polymers, in which the metal cores are often saturated and inert, functional metal-organic polymers (featuring unsaturated metal centers) that undergo helical self-organization are underdeveloped. New classes of helical conjugated metallopolymers of different topologies are proposed, which are susceptible to dynamic conformational changes because the helix formation is directed by intramolecular non-covalent interactions. Studies focusing on chiroptical and photophysical properties and responses will be conducted, and a primary consideration is the spatial arrangement and alignment of metal-organic functional groups and luminophores. The development of stackable aromatic systems that can undergo pi-mediated self-assembly, and examination of the effects of structural and substituent effects on aggregation behavior, will be undertaken. It is envisaged that applications in luminescent and chiral sensing can be realized, and potential biological and materials functions will be investigated. In essence, this research concerns the design and control of intermolecular versus intramolecular interactions in metal-Schiff base and related systems. 對於人工模擬螺旋體的興趣源於自然界中廣泛存在的螺旋結構以及它們功能上的多樣性。此研究計劃重點是設計、合成以及應用螺旋狀金屬有機配位聚合物和堆積多核架構。儘管配位聚合物已有發展，其中金屬中心通常是飽和的、惰性的，然而具有自助裝功能的螺旋狀金屬有機聚合物，特別是具有非飽和金屬中心，仍有待發展。研究計劃提出了新類型具有不同拓撲結構的螺旋狀金屬有機聚合物。此螺旋結構的形成是基於分子間的非共價作用力，所以對動態結構變化具有敏感性。研究工作主要集中在手性光學信號以及光物理性質和變化響應方面。主要考察金屬有機功能基團和發光體的空間排佈；同時發展具有調控自助裝能力的可堆積性芳環體系，研究結構以及取代基對堆積行為的影響；探索其應用前景，包括螢光探針應用。本質上，此工作涉及到設計和調控基於金屬唏呋鹼及相關體系中分子間與分子內相互作用力的研究。

100212.label: Realisation of objectives
100212.value: The project has been completed and all objectives have been achieved, resulting in several publications. One research student has been wholly trained under this project. Objective 1: In this project, several classes of luminescent coilable conjugated metallopolymers bearing natural chiral building blocks, which are introduced to confer helicity to the polymer backbone, have been prepared by Pd-catalyzed polymerization of terminal phenylene-ethynylenes and metal-organic units. Dynamic, environmentally responsive ortho- and meta-type (geometrically related to o- and m-PPE) metal-Schiff base polymers with controllable helical sense have been developed. The synthesis of helical metal-based polymers with tunable conformational properties and chemical characteristics (including solubility/polarity, side-arm substituents, binding properties/reactivity) have been undertaken. The judicious modular incorporation of metal-organic moieties, as well as control over their relative spatial arrangement, have engendered well-defined coordination geometries with potential binding sites and cooperative effects. Objective 2: A wide variety of analytical methods, including GPC, FT-IR, 1H NMR, UV-vis and emission, and circular dichroism spectroscopy, have been employed to characterize the helical metallopolymers and study their photophysical and chiroptical properties. The consequences of varying side-chain substituents as well as the extent of inter- and intrachain aggregation (pi-stacking and M...O(salphen) interactions) upon the folded helical structure have been investigated. Conformational changes caused by environmental effects (e.g. temperature, solvent polarity and coordinating capacity) and external stimuli (e.g. chiral guests) have been monitored by UV-vis absorption, emission and CD spectroscopy. Taken together, the observed results point to the flexibility, reversibility and dynamic nature of the helical conformation in these polymers. Objective 3: The development of crowded host architectures, bearing a shape-persistent binding pocket in the immediate vicinity of environmentally sensitive metal-organic luminophores, have been undertaken. For binuclear systems, cooperativity between metal-organic moieties was achieved with regards to photophysical properties and sensing capabilities. Families of crowded coordination frameworks have been designed and synthesized, for which the control of inter- and intramolecular interactions and aggregation processes was an underlying consideration. Furthermore, a series of biocompatible phosphorescent probes with tunable lipophilicity was developed (see Objective 4). Objective 4: The applications of helical metallopolymers and pi-stacked assemblies have been developed, and notable results have been obtained for chiral recognition and luminescent biolabeling. The employment of the helical metallopolymers as macromolecular hosts for binding and sensing chiral guest substrates has been investigated. Significantly, selective luminescent and chiroptical sensing of guest substrates, including chiral amines, has been observed. With regards to crowded host scaffolds, colorimetric and phosphorescent responses in the presence of selected metal ions have been detected. Biocompatible Pt-based compounds with potential applications in luminescent signaling and sensing have been developed. Mitochondria-targeting phosphorescent complexes has been investigated as live cell imaging agents.

100212.label: Major findings and research outcome
100212.value: A new class of conformationally rigid binuclear platinum(II) and zinc(II) complexes bearing tetradentate aromatic Schiff base (salphen) ligands with limited rotational freedom has been prepared and characterized, and the molecular structure of a bis-(Pt-salphen) derivative has been determined by X-ray crystallography. Their UV-vis absorption and emission properties have been investigated and are ascribed to different excited states depending on the metal and the extent of intramolecular pi-stacking interactions. Colorimetric and phosphorescent responses by the bis-Pt(II) complexes in the presence of selected metal ions have been observed. The nature of the host-guest interactions have been examined by quantitative binding studies, mass spectrometry and DFT calculations. [Publication 1] A readily tunable series of oligo(ethylene glycol)-substituted phosphorescent Pt(II) complexes has been investigated as live cell imaging agents. Suitable structural modification and changes in lipophilicity has been demonstrated to confer good cellular uptake, traceable mitochondria-specific localization in HeLa cells and potent cytotoxic characteristics to these non-planar cationic probes. Collaborative studies with Soochow University revealed that these complexes exhibit dual inhibitory activities on tumor cell proliferation and migration/invasion via intracellular trafficking of beta-catenin. [Publications 2 and 5] Conjugated poly(Zn-salphen)-alt-(p-phenyleneethynylene)s with a coilable structure have been synthesized, and their photophysical properties and conformational behavior have been studied. Their CD spectra confirm that these systems are chiral, and signify ordered (helical) coiling of the polymer backbone arising from chirality transfer from the glucosyl substituents. Analysis of the effects of different solvents on these polymers by UV-vis absorption, emission and CD spectroscopy indicate that low-polarity solvents give a tighter, more compressed helical conformation with increased CD intensities, while coordinating solvents can insert into the folded conformation to afford a more extended helical structure with decreased Cotton effects. These results point to the flexibility and dynamic nature of the helical conformation. [Publication 3] Luminescent conjugated Pt(II)- and Zn(II)-based ortho- and meta-type polymers (geometrically related to o- and m-PPE), bearing L- or D-forms of arabinose, have been synthesized. GPC results indicate that all polymers display high molecular weights and degrees of polymerization. The L- and D- arabinose substituents give rise to mirror-image CD signals, thus confirming the helicity of these polymers and that opposite helical senses have been induced. Changes in photophysical and CD measurements in different solvents have been ascribed to conformational transformations between compressed and more extended helical structures. Investigation of the helical metallopolymers for binding and sensing chiral guests has produced evidence of enantiomeric differentiation. [Publication 4]

100212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100212.value: Several classes of new luminescent poly(M-salphen)-alt-(phenyleneethynylene) materials and crowded M-organic assemblies (M = Pt, Zn) have been developed. The continued development of ortho- and meta-type polymers (geometrically related to o- and m-PPE), with distinctive structural and conformational characteristics, may be undertaken. Due to their modular and readily tunable nature, structural modification (of side-arm substituents, solubility and polarity) would afford new dynamic, environmentally responsive helical metallopolymers and crowded M-organic assemblies. Investigations into their conformational, chiroptical, and photophysical properties would be of interest. Due to the contrasting nature and structures of the helical metallopolymers, differences in conformational and aggregation behavior may be envisaged. The incorporation of natural chiral building blocks, which can selectively bind to chiral guests or other bioactive molecules, would be amenable to applications in living and biological systems. Regarding development of mitochondria-targeting phosphorescent complexes, future work can exploit the easily derivatizable characteristics of this system and pave the way towards greater understanding of the chemical and structural factors affecting cellular localization, uptake and cytotoxicity. Further applications for the polymeric materials and crowded M-organic assemblies may be developed, including chiral recognition, biomimetic materials, and asymmetric catalysis.

100212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100212.value: Artificial helices have long attracted attention because Nature has demonstrated the diverse range of functionality that can be attained by the precise positioning of functional groups within coiled structures. Synthetic helical polymers can be employed as scaffolds for biomimetic functions, while the incorporation of abiological components can lead to applications in molecular recognition, sensing and materials science. This project concerned the design, preparation, characterization and application of helical metallopolymers and pi-stacked multinuclear assemblies. Notwithstanding coordination polymers, in which the metal centers are often saturated or inaccessible, the study of helical metallopolymers with controllable helical sense remains in its infancy. New families of helical conjugated metallopolymers of different topologies, displaying tunable conformational and dynamic behavior, have been created. Studies focusing on chiroptical and photophysical properties and responses have been conducted, and an underlying consideration of the design approach has been the relative spatial arrangement and alignment of metal-organic functional groups and luminophores. The development of cofacial bimetallic and biocompatible metal-organic systems, and examination of the effects of structural and substituent effects on photophysical, sensing and biolabeling properties, have been undertaken. Applications in luminescent and chiral sensing, and as live cell imaging agents, have been investigated and realized.

100612.label: Realisation of objectives
100612.value: OBJECTIVE 1: To seek Donati-like compatibility conditions on a surface, with application to linear shell theory. Donati compatibility conditions on a surface constitute characterizations of symmetric matrix fields guaranteeing that their components are the covariant components of the linearized change of metric and change of curvature tensors associated with the displacement field of a surface, which in the applications that we had in mind, is the middle surface of the reference configuration of a linearly elastic shell. In a joint paper with Oana Iosifescu, we have been able to identify such Donati compatibility conditions on a surface, which take the form of integral equations to be satisfied by divergence-free tensor fields. This is the first instance of such compatibility conditions, which up to now were only known for open sets in R^n. We were then able to use these Donati compatibility conditions to re-formulate the classical problem of the equilibrium of an elastic shell modelled by the well-known Koiter’s equations as a minimization problem with the linearized change of metric and change of curvature as the sole unknowns, thus identifying and justifying an “intrinsic approach” to linearly elastic shell problems. While the previous intrinsic approach applies to any type of shell, we were also able, in a joint paper with Cristinel Mardare and Xiaoqin Shen, to find specific Donati compatibility conditions on a surface that correspond to the special cases of linearly elastic membrane shells and linearly elastic flexural shells, and that are substantially easier to implement. We also identified and justified the corresponding intrinsic approaches, which consist in a minimization problem with either the linearized change of metric or the change of curvature as the sole unknown. OBJECTIVE 2: To seek nonlinear Donati-like compatibility conditions, with application to nonlinear plate theory. The nonlinear Donati compatibility conditions that we had in mind constitute characterizations of symmetric matrix fields guaranteeing that their components are the components of the nonlinear change of metric and linear change of curvature tensors associated with the displacement field of the middle surface of a nonlinearly elastic plate modeled according to the Kirchhoff-von Karman-Love theory. In a joint paper with Giuseppe Geymonat and Françoise Krasucki, we were able to identify such nonlinear Donati compatibility conditions on a surface, which take the form of nonlinear integral equations to be satisfied by divergence-free tensor fields. This is the first instance of nonlinear Donati-like compatibility conditions. We were then able to use these Donati compatibility conditions to re-formulate the classical problem of the equilibrium of a nonlinearly elastic plate as a non-quadratic minimization problem with the nonlinear change of metric and linear change of curvature as the sole unknowns, thus identifying and justifying an intrinsic approach to nonlinearly elastic plates. OBJECTIVES 1 AND 2: In another joint paper with Oana Iosifescu, we were even able to identify and justify Donati-like compatibility conditions that correspond to shells (Objective 1) that are nonlinearly elastic (Objective 2), in the case of nonlinearly elastic shallow shells modeled according to the Koiter-Donnell-Mushtari-Vlasov theory. As expected, we encountered numerous technical and functional difficulties (this is why I asked for a six-month extension), but eventually we were able to overcome all of them. More specifically, we were able to identify nonlinear Donati compatibility conditions on a surface that applies to such nonlinearly elastic shallow shells. This is the first instance of nonlinear Donati-like compatibility conditions for nonlinearly elastic shells. We were then able to use these nonlinear Donati compatibility conditions to re-formulate the classical problem of the equilibrium of a nonlinearly elastic shallow shell as a non-quadratic minimization problem. CONCLUSION: Both Objective 1 and Objective 2 have been 100% achieved.

100612.label: Major findings and research outcome
100612.value: There are several entirely new (at least to the best of my knowledge) major findings and research outcomes: The identification and full mathematical justification of Donati-like compatibility conditions that can be successfully applied to the mathematical modeling of general linearly elastic shells, linearly elastic flexural and membrane shells, nonlinearly elastic plates, and nonlinearly elastic shallow shells.

100612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100612.value: The main features of an intrinsic approach is that the “new unknowns” need only be in the space L^2, instead of being in some Sobolev space like H^1 or H^2 and that these new unknowns must of satisfy in each case specific Donati-like compatibility conditions. It would therefore be quite worthwhile to devise and analyze numerical methods that could approximate the solutions found in the various intrinsic approaches that have been identified and fully mathematically justified in this research.

100612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100612.value: In the classical approach to the modeling of commonly encountered elastic structures, such as plates and shells, the unknown that is computed is the displacement that the structure undergoes when it is subjected to specific applied forces and boundary conditions. In an “intrinsic approach”, one instead directly compute the “strains” (changes of lengths and changes of curvatures) that correspond to a given displacement and which in turn immediately provide the “state of stress” inside the structure. This research lays the mathematical foundations that allow to devise and analyze such intrinsic approaches in the case of linearly elastic as well as nonlinearly elastic plates and shells, thus paving the way for the direct computations of the strains.

101112.label: Realisation of objectives
101112.value: The use of global meshless radial basis function collocation method (RBFCM) will suffer from the well-known ill-conditioning problem due to the resultant full matrix. In this project we applied successfully the recently developed local radial basis function collocation method (LRBFCM) to simulate the solution for the thermo-driven fluid-flow problem. The LRBFCM enjoys the advantages of RBFCM on truly meshless, highly accurate, and easy implementation without the ill-conditioning problem and hence is ideal for solving large scale problems. The LRBFCM is readily parallelized for solving high dimensional problems. In particular, the well-known open problem in choosing the optimal shape parameter for the RBFCM no longer exists. This local variant has been applied successfully to solve some benchmark test problems. In compared with the classical benchmark test problems, we posed a Neumann condition on the upper fixed boundary for velocity, which imposed an extra difficulty in seeking numerical approximation. Moreover, the recently developed Artificial Compressibility Method (ACM) was firstly combined with the Characteristic Based Split (CBS) method to deal with the pressure velocity coupling system. The LRBFCM was tested on thermal-driven fluid flow problems under free surface for various Rayleigh numbers with results published on paper (#1). The theoretical formulation and mathematical analysis for solving problems in partial differential equations with fractional orders had been investigated. Both well-posed and ill-posed problems were considered. Particularly in the ill-posed case, we had developed a new mathematical model for the determination of unknown temperature distribution and heat flux history from measurement of scattered noisy data in an accessible media at a particular time. In general, a complete recovery of the unknown initial temperature and heat flux is not attainable from mere scattered final temperature measurements with noises. We first gave a theoretical justification on the efficiency and convergence of combining the kernel-based approximation method and discretized Tikhonov regularization technique for solving these kinds of highly ill-posed problems (paper #2). The theoretical part had been extended to solving higher-dimensional heat conduction problems via the use of more general kernels (paper #6). The first objective of the project had been realized. Based on the theoretical results, an efficient computational method had been developed by combining the methods of fundamental solutions, radial basis functions, and adaptive regularization. The computational method had been shown to be effective and accurate in solving these kinds of multiphase liquid-solid flow problems. The method is a truly meshless computational method which can avoid the tedious meshing problem in using some traditional computational methods like finite element or finite difference. Numerical verification on the efficiency and accuracy of the collocation methods (RBFCM, LRBFCM) had been performed with results published on papers (#3, #7, #8). The objectives 2-4 of the project had been realized. Furthermore, the newly developed numerical methods had been successfully applied to solve inverse and ill-posed problems. Several papers on both theoretical stability analysis and numerical computation were published (papers #4, #9 - #12). Paper #13 indicates the applicability of the methods in solving inverse problems related to option pricing models in which real financial option data had been collected for the verification on the accuracy of the numerical method. The objective 5 of the project had been realized. More recently, a completely new numerical method, namely Finite Integration Method, has been developed and found to provide highly accurate, efficient, and stable numerical solutions to partial differential equations. Two papers (#5, #14) had been published on the application of this new FIM to solve nonlocal elastic problem under both static and dynamic loads.

101112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101112.value: Both the localized kernel-based numerical algorithm and the regularization techniques have been proven to be efficient in solving various types of multiphasic fluid flow problems and inverse and ill-posed problems. A new proposal on the further exploration of the method for solving inverse identification of variable coefficients problem has been submitted for the next round GRF research grant application.

101112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101112.value: Based on the recent rapid development of meshless kernel techniques, the project has incorporated new and efficient localization scheme combined with pressure correction algorithm and adaptive simulation technique to provide solution of engineering turbulence modelling for simulations of microstructure evolution. Instead of using cellular automata, the local meshless kernel approximation method adapts the use of point automata for the simulation of mesoscopic grain structure and microscopic dendrite growth. Numerical verification on the efficiency and accuracy of the kernel techniques has proven to have high potential in solving larger scale complicated physical problems.

101212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101212.value: 設計具有雙發射性質的分子是一項非常有挑戰性的工作，因為它必須對不同激發態之間的能量傳輸進行有效的控制。大部分雙螢光單分子的設計都是通過具有不同的發射性質的單元聯結起來實現的。有關這些設計，以及對這些產生雙發射性質的單元進行修飾和微調的方法，諸如改變發射波長或者它們之間的比例等，都已經被大量報導。由於任何對於發射激發態的改變或者發射單元的修飾，都無可避免地會引起不同發射激發態能量傳遞效率的改變，從而導致雙發射行為變得難以預測。 本研究課題包括設計和合成各種具有電子受體的配體以及激發態分子內質子傳遞性質的過渡金屬配合物。同時，它們的反應性、互變異構、電化學以及光物理性質，尤其是它們的結構與雙發射之間的關聯以及基於金屬到配體電荷傳遞(MLCT)的激發態分子內質子傳遞的反應性亦會被詳細研究。通過審慎的設計，可以合成出具有適合需要的互變異構體能量差異的和藍色三重態發射體的配體，而最終得到雙發射白色磷光配合物。本課題所涉及的研究，將為這類新穎、具有互變異構的過渡金屬配合物的研究，特別是它們的激發態屬性、光物理以及反應性方面奠定基礎。與此同時，也將給利用雙磷光過渡金屬配合物研發單分子白色磷光材料，光學感測器及探針提供新的方向和系統性策略。

101212.label: Realisation of objectives
101212.value: All objectives have been accomplished. A wide variety of luminescent transition metal complexes newly designed ligands such as those of rhenium(I) diimine, rhenium(I) isocyanide, rhenium(I) N-heterocyclic carbene, ruthenium(II) diimine, osmium(II) diimine, copper(I) diimine, cyclometalated iridium(III) complexes have been synthesized. These luminescent transition metal complexes exhibit interesting photophysical and emission properties derived from different excited states as well as a mixture of emissive excited states. Applications of these complexes as anion chemosensors, emissive materials for light-emitting devices, photosensitizers and photocatalysts have been explored. All the new ligands and their metal complexes have been characterized with various spectroscopic techniques, such as NMR spectroscopy, IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry and elemental analysis. The structures of many of these complexes have been confirmed by X-ray crystallography. To provide fundamental understanding of their photophysics, excited state properties and the structure-properties correlation, all these newly designed luminescent transition metal complexes have been investigated by UV-VIS absorption spectroscopy, emission spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, transient absorption and time-resolved emission spectroscopy. Moreover, DFT calculations on selected luminescent transition metal complexes were performed to elucidate the natures of electronic transitions, emissive excited states and the impacts of the ligands on the transition metal complexes. On the other hand, as many of these phosphorescent transition metal complexes are positively charged and cannot be processed by vacuum sublimation, which is commonly used for device fabrication and thus limiting their potential for device applications. We have also designed new strategy for converting cationic phosphorescent transition metal complexes to strongly emissive charge-neutral transition metal complexes through the use of strongly -accepting anionic ligands. Using this design strategy, the phosphorescent energy and quantum yields of the charge neutral complexes become comparable or even higher than those of the structurally-related cationic triplet emitters. The stability of many of these charge neutral luminescent transition metal complexes have also been investigated by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), which confirmed that most of them are thermally stable and vacuum sublimable. In view of the excellent phosphorescent properties, electrochemical reversibility and vacuum sublimability of some of these charge neutral triplet emitters, doped electroluminescent devices from these complexes have also been fabricated by vacuum sublimation. The device fabrication and the study of the electroluminescent properties were carried out through the collaboration with coworkers in the Department of Applied Physics and Material Science as stated in the proposal. Optimization of the device structure to maximize the device performance using these phosphorescent transition metal complexes are currently in progress through the collaboration with coworkers in Department of Applied Physics and Material Science as well as an industrial collaborator.

101212.label: Major findings and research outcome
101212.value: The research was conducted in accordance with the proposed research plan and methodology. A wide variety of luminescent transition metal complexes with newly designed ligands such as those of Ru(II) diimine (Chem. – Eur. J. 2013), Re(I) diimine (Chem. Mater. 2014; Inorg. Chem. 2014; Polyhedron 2015; Chem. – Eur. J. 2015; Dalton Trans. 2016; Inorg. Chem. 2016), Re(I) isocyanide (Chem. Mater. 2014; Inorg. Chem. 2014; Polyhedron 2015; Chem. – Eur. J. 2015), Re(I) N-heterocyclic carbene (Inorg. Chem. 2014; Dalton Trans. 2016; Inorg. Chem. 2016), Os(II) diimine (Organometallics 2014), Cu(I) diimine, cyclometalated Ir(III) complexes (Dalton Trans. 2016) have been synthesized and characterized with various spectroscopic techniques. The structures of many of these complexes have been determined by X-ray crystallography. These complexes exhibit strong phosphorescence with tunable emission energy covering the entire visible region. As some of them possess long-lived excited state, they can serve as photosensitizer and/or photocatalyst (Dalton Trans. 2016). For luminescent complexes with H-bonding donor, their anion-binding properties and chemosensory applications for anions have also been studied (Inorg. Chem. 2016). The photophysical, photochemical, electrochemical properties of these complexes have also been investigated. Detailed photophysical study have revealed that their phosphorescence are derived from different excited states as well as a mixture of different emissive excited states. Through the investigation of these complexes, the structure-properties correlation have also been elucidated. To enhance the device performance and applicability, we have also designed new strategy for converting cationic triplet emitters to strongly phosphorescent charge-neutral transition metal complexes through the use of strongly -accepting anionic ligands (Chem. Mater. 2014; Organometallics 2014; Chem. – Eur. J. 2015; Dalton Trans. 2016). Using this design strategy, the emission energy and quantum yields of the charge neutral complexes become comparable or even higher than those of the structurally-related cationic triplet emitters. The stability of many of these charge neutral luminescent transition metal complexes have also been investigated by thermogravimetric analysis, which confirmed that most of them are vacuum sublimable. The device application and the electroluminescent properties of some of these complexes have also been investigated (Chem. Mater. 2014). Apart from the publications, the above results have also led to the award of The Distinguish Lectureship Award as well as invited lecture and oral presentations at a number of international conferences including 93rd Chemical Society of Japan Meeting, 20th ISPPCC, 12th ISABC, Artificial Photosynthesis Conference, 20th EuCheMS Conference, 9th ICCEOCA, 27th ICP, 5th ACCC, 42nd ICCC and 1st IC3EM.

101212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101212.value: As described in Sec. 6.1, a number of different types of luminescent transition metal complexes have been developed. Many of these complexes are potentially useful photosensitizers, phosphorescent materials and luminescent chemosensors. Further optimization of these complexes for device applications such as electroluminescent devices and dye-sensitized solar cells is now under investigation. Moreover, we have started to collaborate with industrial partner to explore the OLED applications of some of the complexes. Besides, our finding also revealed some of the transition metal complexes can serve as anion chemosensors, however, their selectivity, aqueous solubility as well as emission responses towards specific analyte still have room for improvement from practical application perspective. Structural modification on the ligands to improve these important characteristics is in progress. On the other hand, the triplet emissive excited states of many of the newly developed luminescent transition metal complexes have been demonstrated to be very long-lived and strongly oxidizing/reducing. These excited state characteristics are ideal for bimolecular energy transfer and electron transfer processes. With these properties, we are planning to develop new photocatalytic systems using these luminescent transition metal complexes to facilitate organic transformations, solar energy conversion and storage.

101212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101212.value: In this project, various new classes of metal-based phosphorescent (light-emissive) compounds have been developed. In the developing these compounds, new design strategies and preparative methods have been invented. Through studying of the functional properties of these compounds, the scientific understanding of the properties have been examined. This knowledge is very important to provide insights for the future development of phosphorescent materials for wide varieties of applications. Efficient light-emitting devices using the compounds developed in this project have been fabricated. Besides, applications of these compounds in different areas such as chemical sensors, photocatalysts and photosensitizers have also been studied. Some of compounds developed in this project have also been demonstrated to be good photocatalysts. It is expected that further optimization on these compound would lead to the development of photocatalytic systems for storing light energy into useful chemical forms such as fuel. Some of the results of this project have been reported in internationally-refereed journals and led to the award of “The Distinguished Lectureship Award on Luminescent Transition Metal Complexes” from the Chemical Society of Japan and numerous invitations to lecture at international conferences.

101512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101512.value: The selective C-H bond activation of hydrocarbons is a key step in the oxidation of petroleum to useful organic chemicals. The search for highly efficient and selective oxidation catalysts that would save energy and raw materials and reduce polluting wastes remains a challenging task for chemists. There have been numerous studies on using metal oxo species for alkane/alkene oxidations and we have been interested in making use of Lewis acids to activate stable metal-oxo species as oxidants. In this project, we propose to study theoretical aspects of the activation of oxo and peroxo species of ruthenium, chromium, vanadium and osmium by Lewis acids towards the oxidation of alkanes, alkenes and arenes using density functional theory and polarization continuum model. Ruthenium forms an extensive series of oxo complexes from +VIII to +IV. It would be interesting to compare the activation of these oxo species by Lewis acids. Chromium oxo species have been used as an oxidant in organic chemistry for decades; an understanding of the activation of these species is of fundamental interest. In particular, a study of the methane oxidation by dichromate may provide insight on the oxidation mechanism of methane monooxygenase, which is believed to make use of an analogous diiron(IV) μ-oxo species to oxidize methane. Vanadium forms various oxo and peroxo species. Our preliminary studies show that these species may be activated by Lewis acids to oxidize hydrocarbons. Relevant DFT calculations would provide information on whether the Lewis acid binds to an oxo or peroxo ligand. We plan to explore the potential energy surfaces, determine the activation barriers, and elucidate the reaction mechanisms for the alkanes/alkenes/arenes oxidation by Lewis acid−activated metal oxo/peroxo species. We are also interested in studying the steric and electronic effects of the Lewis acid on the reactivity of metal oxo/peroxo species. The Lewis acid catalyzes the oxidation by enhancing the ability of metal oxo/peroxo species to accept electrons from hydrocarbons. We propose to study the correlation of the barrier heights of oxidation with the energy of molecular orbital responsible for accepting electrons. We will examine the dynamic changes of electron density en route from reactants to transition state structure to products. Our proposed studies should contribute to the understanding of the interaction of Lewis acids with oxo/peroxo species of ruthenium, chromium, vanadium and osmium at molecular level and the role of Lewis acid on the catalytic activity of these complexes. 在將石油氧化成各種有機化合物的反應中，烴類特定C-H鍵的活化是關鍵的一步。若尋找到高效且具選擇性的氧化催化劑，則可以降低能耗、節約原材料以及減少污染。目前有很多關於使用金屬氧化物對烷烴和烯烴進行氧化的研究。而我們感興趣的則是如何使用路易斯酸去活化穩定的金屬氧化物。在此項目中，我們將使用密度泛函理論和極化連續模型對被路易斯酸活化的釕、鉻、釩、鋨氧化物及過氧化物氧化烷烴、烯烴和炔烴的反應進行理論研究。釕能形成從+VIII價到+IV價的系列氧化物，路易斯酸對這些不同價態氧化物的活化能力值得進行比較。含鉻氧化物在數十年前就被當做氧化劑在有機化學中使用，對這類氧化物活化作用的研究也從未停止過。例如，一次使用重鉻酸鹽氧化甲烷的研究揭示了甲烷單氧酶的氧化機理，即用類二鐵(IV) μ型-氧化物去氧化甲烷。釩同樣能形成各種各樣的氧化物和過氧化物。我們的初步研究顯示這些化合物能被路易斯酸活化，而後用於烴類的氧化。相關的密度泛函計算將進一步提供路易斯酸是否橋接在氧化物或過氧化物配體上的信息。 我們計劃對路易斯酸活化金屬氧化物及過氧化物氧化烷烴、烯烴和炔烴的反應進行研究，重點在于尋找勢能面、決定反應能壘以及闡明反應機理。我們還將研究反應過程中路易斯酸的位阻效應及電子效應。而路易斯酸之所以能催化整個氧化反應，是因為其增強了金屬氧化物及過氧化物的得電子能力。同時，接收電子的分子軌道能量、金屬中心的電子密度，這兩者與氧化反應能壘之間的關係也值得研究。而在從反應物到過渡態再到產物的整個過程中，電子密度的動態變化也是我們將要探索的一個方面。我們的研究將有助於理解在分子水平上路易斯酸與釕、鉻、釩、鋨氧化物及過氧化物的相互作用，以及路易斯酸在提升這些化合物催化活性中起到的作用。

101512.label: Major findings and research outcome
101512.value: Alkane Oxidation Catalyzed by [MnV(N)(CN)4]2- DFT calculations have been performed to study the mechanism of cyclohexane oxidation catalyzed by [Mn(N)(CN)4]2- with H2O2 in CF3CH2OH. These theoretical suggests that the mechanism for catalytic alkane oxidation by [MnV(N)(CN)4]2-/ROOH involves initial rate-limiting O-atom transfer from ROOH to [Mn(N)(CN)4]2- to generate a manganese(VII) nitrido oxo active species, [MnVII(N)(O)(CN)4]2-, which then oxidizes alkanes (R’H) via a H-atom abstraction/O-rebound mechanism. The proposed mechanism is consistent experimental results obtained by Co-I. The work is published in J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2014, 136, 7680−7687. Catalytic oxidation of alkanes by a (salen)osmium(VI) nitrido complex using H2O2 as the terminal oxidant The osmium(VI) nitrido complex, [OsVI(N)(L)(CH3OH)]+ (1, L = N,N0-bis(salicylidene)-o-cyclohexyldiamine dianion) is an efficient catalyst for the oxidation of alkanes under ambient conditions using H2O2 as the oxidant. DFT calculations suggests a mechanism that involves O-atom transfer from H2O2 to [OsVI(N)(L)]+ to generate an [OsVIII(N)(O)(L)]+ active intermediate and the results are consistent with experimental data. The work is published in Chem. Commun., 2015, 51, 13686−13689. Theoretical and Experimental Photoelectron Spectroscopy Characterization of the Ground State of Thymine Cation The threshold photoelectron spectrum, recorded over ∼0.7 eV above the ionization potential shows rich vibrational structure that has been assigned with the help of calculated anharmonic modes of the ground electronic cation state at the PBE0/aug-cc-pVDZ level of theory. The adiabatic ionization energy has been experimentally determined as AIE = 8.913 ± 0.005 eV. The corresponding theoretical value of AIE = 8.917 eV has been calculated in this work with the explicitly correlated method/basis set (R)CCSD(T)-F12/cc-pVTZ-F12, which validates the theoretical approach and benchmarks its accuracy for future studies of medium-sized biological molecules. The work is published in J. Phys. Chem. A 2015, 119, 5951−5958. Vibrationally Resolved Photoelectron Spectroscopy of Electronic Excited States of DNA Bases: Application to the A State of Thymine Cation While ground state investigations are currently straightforward, those of electronic excited states are not. Here, we characterized the A electronic state of ionic thymine (T+) DNA base using explicitly correlated coupled cluster ab initio methods and state-of-the-art synchrotron-based electron/ion coincidence techniques. The experimental spectrum is composed of rich and long vibrational progressions corresponding to the population of the low frequency modes of T+(A). We carried out theoretical calculations to study the electronic structure of ionized DNA bases that could be generalized to other medium-sized biologically relevant systems. The work is published in J. Phys. Chem. A 2015, 119, 1146−1153.

101612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101612.value: This project is mainly concerned with fundamental studies of the oxidation chemistry of manganese(V) nitrido complexes (MnV≡N) and other reactive nitrido species generated from them. Metal-catalyzed oxidation of organic compounds is one of the most important processes in organic synthesis. The use of manganese complexes as oxidation catalysts continues to be of great interest since they are relative inexpensive and less toxic than 4d and 5d complexes. However, most manganese catalysts reported so far are in +2 or +3 oxidation states, which are usually high-spin and are intrinsically not very stable. In this project we propose to investigate the use of MnV≡N as oxidation catalysts, these d2 complexes are in general stable since the MnV center is stabilized by the strongly electro-donating nitrido ligand. For example, we have recently discovered that (PPh4)2[MnV(N)(CN)4] is a very robust and efficient catalyst for the epoxidation of alkenes and the oxidation of alcohols by hydrogen peroxide at room temperature. By replacing the four cyanide ligands in [MnV(N)(CN)4]2- with multidentate anionic ligands, it is possible to generate more robust catalysts. Also, by designing water soluble MnV≡N catalysts, one can perform green oxidation of organic substrates in water. Apart from hydrogen peroxide, various other oxidants such as PhIO, peracetic acid and m-chloroperbenzoic acid will also be studied. There is evidence that with H2O2, the Mn(V) center acts as a Lewis acid; but with other oxidants a novel MnVII(N)(O) intermediate may be involved. Although the nitrido ligand in MnV≡N is in general rather inert, our preliminary investigations show that MnV(N)(salen) can be readily activated by a few equivalents of Lewis acids such as BF3 to undergo hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) reactions with aromatic hydrocarbons at room temperature. An understanding of the mechanism of this novel reaction is of fundamental interest, and may also lead to the development of a system that can carry out selective C-H bond activation. We also propose to study the reactivity of manganese(VI) nitrido complexes. Report by Weighardt and preliminary investigation by us show that MnVI≡N can be readily generated from MnV≡N by electrochemical or chemical oxidation. These nitrido species are expected to possess rich electrophilic reactivity, similar to ruthenium(VI) and osmium(VI) nitrides. Our studies should contribute to fundamental understanding of the reactivity of manganese nitrido complexes. It could also lead to the development of green, highly efficient and selective methods for oxidation of various organic substrates based on manganese nitrido complexes.

101612.label: Realisation of objectives
101612.value: 1. We have synthesized a series of manganese(V) nitrido complexes 2. We have studied the catalytic oxidation of various organic substrates by the manganese(V) nitrido complex [Mn(N)(CN)4]2- (1) using various oxidants. In particular excellent yields were obtained in the oxidation of alkanes, alkenes and alcohols using 1/H2O2. 3. We have studied the intermediates in catalytic oxidation using various techniques, including UV/Vis spectrophotometry and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry. In collaboration with my colleague Dr. K. C. Lau we have also done DFT calculations on the reaction mechanisms. 4. The effects of various Lewis acids on the catalytic oxidation of alkanes by [Mn(N)(CN)4]2- has been investigated, The Lewis acids include Fe(III), Sc(III), Al(III), BF3 and Zn(II). Our results indicate that these Lewis acids have little effects on [Mn(N)(CN)4]2-. 5. A manganese(VI) nitrido species has been generated by treatment of [Mn(N)(CN)4]2- with various one-electron oxidants. The Mn(VI) species is an active oxidant for alkenes and various aromatic hydrocarbons. 6. Although manganese(V) nitrido complexes are active and highly efficient catalysts for the oxidation of alkanes, we found that they are relatively inactive towards aziridination of alkenes.

101612.label: Major findings and research outcome
101612.value: We have carried out experimental and computational studies of highly efficient alkane oxidation (>95% yield) catalyzed by [MnV(N)(CN)4]2- using H2O2 and various other oxidants at room temperature. We provided evidence that the active intermediate is a novel manganese(VII) nitrido oxo species, [MnVII(N)(O)(CN)4]2- (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2014, 136, 7680-7687). There has been great interest in the study of manganese complexes as water oxidation catalysts (WOCs) because they can serve as models for the oxygen evolving complex of Photosystem II. So far most of the reported Mn WOCs are in oxidation states III or IV, and they generally gave low turnovers, especially with one-electron oxidants such as CeIV. We found that the complex [MnV(N)(CN)4]2– is an active homogeneous WOC using (NH4)2[Ce(NO3)6] as the terminal oxidant, with TON > 180 and a maximum TOF of 6 min-1. Our work suggests that active WOCs may be constructed based on the MnV(N) platform (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2015, 54, 5246-5249). We have also carried out related work on metal oxo species. Although ferrate(VI) is a very strong oxidant that readily oxidizes water in acidic medium, at pH 9-10 it is relatively stable. However, we found that ferrate(VI) is readily activated by Ca2+ at pH 9-10 to oxidize water to give O2. These results together with DFT calculations suggest that the function of Ca2+ is to facilitate O-O coupling between two FeO42-ions by bridging them together. Similar activating effects are also observed with Mg2+ and Sr2+ (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2016, 55, 3012-3016). We have also done work on ruthenium nitrido chemistry. Proton-coupled electron transfer reactions of phenols have received considerable attention because of their fundamental interest and their relevance to many biological processes. Here we observed a remarkable four-electron oxidation of phenols by a (salen)ruthenium(VI) complex in the presence of pyridine to afford (salen)ruthenium(II) p-benzoquinone imine complexes. (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2016, 138, 5817-5820). We also found that hydroquinone is readily oxidized by a (salen)ruthenium(VI) nitrido complex in the presence of pyridine to give benzoquinone. Experimental and computational studies suggest that the reaction occurs by a novel mechanism that involves an initial electrophilic attack at the aromatic ring of the hydroquinone by the nitrido ligand (Chem. Commun. 2016, 52, 11430-11433).

101612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101612.value: In this project we have carried out fundamental studies of the oxidation chemistry of d2 manganese(V) nitrido complexes (MnV≡N) and related d2 iron oxo and ruthenium nitrido complexes. We have demonstrated that a manganese(V) nitrido complex bearing cyano ligands is a highly active and efficient catalyst for the oxidation of alkanes and various organic substrates using the green oxidant hydrogen peroxide. In future we will design more robust MnV≡N catalysts by employing various oxidation-resistant multidentate anxilliary ligands. Also, by designing water soluble MnV≡N catalysts, one can perform green oxidation of organic substrates in water. We have also shown that d2 ruthenium(VI) nitrido species are highly promising reagents for the nitrogenation of various organic substrates. In future we will develop efficient nitrogenation catalysts based on Ru(VI)≡N. In this project we have also shown that Ca2+ and other group 2 metal ions can activate an iron oxo species to generate dioxygen. In future we will design highly efficient water oxidation catalysts based on Lewis acid/metal oxo systems.

101612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101612.value: The design of efficient catalysts for the oxidation of alkanes is a grand challenge for chemists. Metal-catalyzed oxidation of water is considered the bottle-neck reaction in artificial photosynthesis. The oxidation of water produces protons and electrons which can be used to make renewable fuels by reduction of protons or carbon dioxide. The use of manganese complexes to carry out these two important oxidation reactions is of great interest since they are relative inexpensive and non-toxic. However, most manganese catalysts reported so far are in +2 or +3 oxidation states, which are usually high-spin and are intrinsically not very stable. In this project we have discovered that d2 MnV≡N complexes are highly efficient catalysts for the oxidation of water and alkanes. We also have demonstrated that related d2 ruthenium nitrido complexes are promising reagents for the nitrogenation of organic substrates. There is a constant demand to develop new methods for incorporating nitrogen into organic molecules since many pharmaceuticals are nitrogen-containing compounds. We have also developed a new method for the oxidation of water based a Lewis acid/d2 metal oxo system. Overall specking, we have demonstrated that d2 metal nitrido and oxo complexes are a new class of highly efficient oxidation catalysts.

101812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101812.value: Biological fluorescence imaging is one of the most important and interdisciplinary researches involving chemistry, biology, life science, and biomedicine, and has been widely used for various in vivo and in vitro studies. Particularly, fluorescent biological probes are an essential tool for bioimaging. For optimal imaging and tracking of biological cells, the probes should be water-dispersible, anti-bleaching, luminescent, and biocompatible. The excellent biocompatibility (anticipated) of silicon makes fluorescent silicon quantum dots (SiQDs) a promising candidate capable of fulfilling all the necessary requirements of an excellent bioimager. Nevertheless, it is widely recognized that SiQDs have not reached full potential, primarily because they are generally hydrophobic, weak in fluorescence, and poor in stability. Our preliminary results have revealed that SiQDs can be facilely produced via a novel microwave-assisted approach. Significantly, our results have indicated that the prepared fluorescent SiQDs could concurrently possess excellent water-dispersibility, ultra-high photo-, pH-, and storage-stability, as well as favorable biocompatibility; i.e. such prepared SiQDs appear to possess all the salient features required for an ideal bioimager. Inspired by those promising results, we aim in this proposal to further develop this methodology for the facile synthesis of multi-color fluorescent SiQDs, and to exploit the use of such SiQDs as a reliable and efficient biological fluorescent probe for in vitro and in vivo imaging. 102012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102012.value: Given the current rapid development of plasmonic structures and metamaterials, both the electric and magnetic properties of artificial materials can be manipulated in order to achieve unconventional optical properties, including negative refraction, cloaking and subwavelength imaging. However, rather than manipulating the magnetic and electric responses separately in the first generation of metamaterials in order to achieve such promising properties, we are witnessing a new wave of development that is searching for new and interesting functionalities of metamaterials by investigating low-symmetry metamaterials and more complex artificial atoms that have dedicated localized plasmons. Such localized plasmons often couple electric and magnetic dipolar responses in different directions by breaking the geometric symmetry of the particles. This stream of research has already resulted in interesting phenomena about asymmetric transmission through absorption, alternative routes to negative refraction and anomalous optical activity. In the study proposed herein, we aim to further explore the non-reciprocal effects associated with localized plasmons in these low-symmetry metamaterials. This proposal will (i) develop an intuitive local effective medium theory for realistic and complex metamaterials by using corresponding S-parameter simulations to help design complex metamaterials for manipulating waves and (ii) provide a deeper understanding of how complex artificial local plasmonic structures can give rise to wave manipulation and non-reciprocal propagation. We will also aim to establish a numerical procedure in order to extract and study the local effective media of complex metamaterials based on the S-parameters obtained from the full-wave simulations. In contrast to the case-by-case approaches that have been used in previous similar studies, our approach can cater for general metamaterials that have complex constitutive tensors, including the cross-coupling tensors between the electric and magnetic fields. Although the proposed tool is not fully analytical and has to work with simulations in order to extract the local effective medium, it will help us study complex metamaterials in this project. An inverse problem approach for complex metamaterials can also be used. We will assess whether metamaterials that have particular functionalities related to non-reciprocal effects can be designed. First, we target a particular non-reciprocal device function from the S-parameters. Second, we derive the corresponding local effective medium. Third, from the effective medium, we construct dedicated plasmonic structures, giving rise to the prescribed effective medium response. Finally, we simulate the structures again in order to validate our design and assess whether a metamaterial gyrator, a completely asymmetric polarization convertor or a metamaterial circulator is possible. 等離子體結構和超材料的研究正在急速發展，人工材料的電氣和磁學性能皆可以被操縱。第一代的超材料通常分別調諧電氣和磁學性能以達到負折射，隱形斗篷和亞波長成像等超常規的光學性能。然而，我們正在目睹一個新的發展浪潮。通過研究低對稱性超材料和以更複雜的人工原子產生局域化等離子體振子，我們可以耦合不同方向的電偶極子和磁偶極子，以產生更有趣的光學現象，包括通過吸收實現非對稱傳輸，負折射的替代方案和異常光學活性。在這項研究中，我們的目標是進一步探索與這些低對稱性超材料和局域化等離子體振子有關聯的非相互性效應。我們將會（i）制定一個使用S-參數的有效介質理論以描述及設計複雜超材料，（ii）更深入了解複雜人工原子及其局域化等離子體振子產生的非相互性傳播的原理。我們將建立一個數值計算方法，以提取複雜超材料的有效介質參數。跟過往逐一應付不同類型複雜超材料的研究不同，我們的方法可以應付廣義性的複雜超材料，包括處理電場和磁場耦合的整個張量。雖然建議的方法必須通過數值模擬而只具有半解析形式，但通過這方法，我們可以逆向設計特定超材料應具有的有效介質。我們先對一個特定的非相互性器件功能的S-參數進行研究，包括迴轉器，循環器和非對稱偏振轉換器。然後我們推導出相應的有效介質參數。最後，我們可以建構出相對應的等離子體結構及以數值模擬驗證其非相互性傳播原理。

102212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102212.value: This project aims to develop luminescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal glucose and fructose complexes as a new generation of cellular probes for sugar uptake, bioimaging reagents, and metabolic indicators. Due to the hydrophilic nature of glucose, it is transported through the plasma membranes via facilitative glucose transporters (GLUTs). As extra energy is required for uncontrolled cell proliferation, most cancer cells overexpress GLUTs and show enhanced glucose uptake and metabolism. The substrates of these transporters are not limited to glucose but also include other hexoses such as fructose. Thus, a number of glucose and fructose derivatives have been developed as sugar uptake indicators and imaging reagents for cancer cells. Although radionuclides have been commonly used in imaging cancer cells, optical methods have emerged as an alternative as they offer excellent spatial and temporal resolution. Also, fluorescent reagents allow uptake in individual cells to be monitored and enable simultaneous bioimaging and measurements of other intracellular parameters. As cell metabolism is closely related to the expression of GLUTs and glucose uptake, fluorescent sugar reagents can provide an effective screening method to study the metabolic rates and viability of cells. Although many fluorescent sugar derivatives have been developed, the use of luminescent transition metal glucose and fructose complexes in sugar uptake and bioimaging is relatively unexplored. We anticipate that luminescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal glucose and fructose complexes will be attractive choices as new cellular probes for sugar uptake and bioimaging reagents due to their environment-sensitive emission properties, high photostability, and long emission lifetimes. The use of transition metal complexes means that cellular uptake can be conveniently measured by ICP-MS. Also, strategies to control the cellular uptake efficiency and cytotoxicity of these complexes have been developed. In this project, we will design new luminescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal glucose and fructose complexes, and study their photophysical, photochemical, and electrochemical properties and lipophilicity. The cytotoxicity, cellular uptake, and bioimaging properties of the probes will also be examined using various cell lines. Emphasis will be placed on understanding the possible interactions of these complexes with GLUTs and their selective uptake by cancer cells. Ultimately, the potential use of these complexes as cellular probes for sugar uptake, bioimaging reagents, and metabolic indicators will be examined. 此項目旨在開發發光無機和有機過渡金屬葡萄糖和果糖配合物作為新一代的糖攝取細胞探針、生物成像試劑和代謝指示劑。由於葡萄糖的親水性，它需要在葡萄糖運載蛋白的幫助下才能進入細胞。大部分癌細胞通過過度表達葡萄糖運載蛋白，增加葡萄糖的吸收和代謝，以提供細胞失控增殖所需的額外能量。這些運載蛋白的底物不僅限於葡萄糖，還可以包括其它己糖，例如果糖。因此，許多葡萄糖和果糖衍生物已經被研發成癌細胞的糖攝取指示劑和成像試劑。雖然放射性核素已被廣泛應用於癌細胞成像中，但是光學方法以良好的空間和時間分辨率提供了一個新的選擇。此外，利用螢光試劑，我們可以監測單個細胞的攝取並同時進行生物成像和細胞內參數測量。鑑於細胞代謝與葡萄糖運載蛋白的表達和葡萄糖的攝取密切相關，螢光糖試劑可以提供一種有效的篩選方法來研究細胞代謝率和細胞活力。 儘管已經有許多螢光性糖的衍生物，然而使用發光性過渡金屬葡萄糖和果糖配合物在糖攝取和生物成像的研究還相對空白。鑑於發光無機和有機過渡金屬配合物對環境敏感的發射性能、高耐光性以及長發光壽命，我們預計，它們的葡萄糖和果糖配合物將是作為新一代的糖攝取細胞探針、生物成像試劑和代謝指示劑極具吸引力的選擇。過渡金屬配合物的使用意味著可以很方便地通過電感耦合等離子體質譜測定細胞的攝取。此外，對這些配合物細胞攝取效率和細胞毒性的控制也已經發展起來。在這個項目中，我們將設計新的發光無機和有機過渡金屬葡萄糖和果糖配合物，並研究其光物理，光化學，電化學性能和脂溶性。我們還將使用各種細胞系審查這些配合物的細胞毒性、細胞攝取和生物成像性能。重點將放在了解可能存在的配合物和葡萄糖運載蛋白之間的相互作用以及這些配合物被癌細胞選擇性地吸收。最終，我們將審查這些配合物作為糖攝取細胞探針、生物成像試劑和代謝指示劑的潛在用途。

102212.label: Realisation of objectives
102212.value: All the objectives of this project were successfully achieved. In this project, a number of new luminescent transition metal complexes appended with a sugar unit were synthesized by different strategies and fully characterized using a range of spectroscopic methods such as NMR, ESI-MS, IR, and elemental analyses. The fundamental UV-Vis absorption, photophysical, photochemical, and electrochemical properties of the complexes were also examined. Additionally, the water solubility, lipophilicity, cellular uptake properties, and cytotoxic activity of all the complexes were investigated. The photocytotoxicity of selected complexes was also studied in detail. Ultimately, the complexes were utilized as sugar-uptake probes, imaging reagents, and metabolic indicators. More specifically, we developed luminescent rhenium(I) and iridium(III) polypyridine complexes containing a fructose, glucose, or galactose unit and examined their basic properties. The emission properties of these complexes were similar to their sugar-free counterparts, indicating that the incorporation of a sugar pendant did not perturb the electronic structures of the complexes. The most important discovery is that the cellular uptake of these transition metal sugar complexes can be designed to exhibit a high degree of selectivity toward eukaryotic cells. For example, the cellular uptake of a luminescent rhenium(I) fructose complex showed preference on human breast adenocarcinoma cell lines (MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231) over nonbreast cancer cell lines (human lung epithelial carcinoma A549 and human hepatocarcinoma HepG2) and nontransformed cell lines (mouse embryonic fibroblast NIH/3T3 and human embryonic kidney-293 HEK293T). This leads to strong support that the fructose transporter GLUT5, which is overexpressed in the breast cancer cells MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231, plays an important role on the uptake of the rhenium(I) fructose complex. Similar findings were observed in related luminescent iridium(III) fructose complexes, rending them to be new luminescent probes for fructose transporter and breast cancer cells. Interestingly, upon irradiation of MCF-7 cells stained with the complexes at > 365 nm, the cytotoxicity of the complexes was dramatically increased due to the photogeneration of singlet oxygen. These interesting results imply that the complexes have a high potential to function as cell-selective photodynamic therapeutic reagents. In another study, we designed a series of luminescent iridium(III) glucose and galactose complexes. The lipophilicity, the cellular uptake efficiency, and cytotoxicity of the complexes toward HeLa were examined. Temperature dependence and chemical inhibition experiments indicated that the transport of the bt–glucose complex across the cell membrane occurred through an energy-requiring process in additional to a pathway that was mediated by glucose transporters (GLUTs). Inhibition experiments involving insulin and estradiol were also designed and performed. It is known that insulin not only enhances glucose transport and increases glycolytic enzyme activity in normal human cells, but also plays an important role in the stimulation of glucose uptake in cancer cells. Upon stimulation by the hormone, the uptake of the glucose complex by HeLa cells was enhanced. Interestingly, when the cells were pretreated with an insulin-desensitizer wortmannin, the stimulation effect of the hormone on the cellular uptake disappeared. Thus, the GLUT-dependent cellular uptake of the complex responded to external hormonal stimulation and inhibition. The sex hormone 17(beta)-estradiol (E2) plays an important role in the growth and progression of estrogen receptors (ER)-positive breast cancer cells. Binding of E2 to ER in responsive cells such as MCF-7 cells is known to stimulate cell growth, which requires a large amount of energy to be generated from upregulated glucose metabolism via glycolysis and the citric acid cycle. The amount of the glucose complex taken up by MCF-7 cells upon pretreatment with E2 was found to be almost doubly increased. Thus, the glucose complex was responsive to cellular metabolic changes, which can be exploited in the development of screening methods to study cell metabolism. In addition to the design of luminescent transition metal sugar complexes, we also extended the study by developing bioorthogonal probes to target the sugar unit of glycans located at cell membrane. For example, luminescent iridium(III) and rhenium(I) complexes containing a dibenzocyclooctyne (DIBO) moiety were synthesized and designed as bioorthogonal probes for azide-modified sugar units. These DIBO complexes underwent facile reactions with azide derivatives and can selectively label azide-modified proteins, leading to the formation of strongly emissive bioconjugates. Upon incubation of CHO cells with these complexes, intracellular emission was observed, indicative of nonselective staining. However, upon pretreatment of the cells with the azido-sugar derivative 1,3,4,6-tetra-O-acetyl-N-azidoacetyl-D-mannosamine (Ac4ManNAz), intense emission was observed from the cell membrane, indicating that these DIBO complexes can target the modified glycans and are novel candidates for imaging azide-labeled biomolecules. There were no major difficulties encountered in this project. One obstacle would be the low water solubility of the transition metal complexes, which limits their potential as biological probes. Also, most of the complexes were considerably cytotoxic, making it difficult to probe live cells. Fortunately, these problems were circumvented by the attachment of PEG pendants to the metal complexes. For example, we designed a new class of luminescent cyclometalated iridium(III) polypyridine poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) complexes and studied their photophysical, photochemical, and biological properties. Upon irradiation, all the complexes exhibited intense and long-lived green to orange-red emission under ambient conditions. Cell-based assays indicated that the complexes were noncytotoxic in the dark. However, most of them became significantly cytotoxic upon irradiation, indicating of potential photocytotoxic activity. Laser-scanning confocal microscopy images revealed localization of the complexes in the mitochondria of HeLa cells and the induction of rapid necrotic cell death upon light activation. The lack of dark toxicity and application of the complexes as a visualizing reagent were also demonstrated using zebrafish as an animal model. In conclusion, all the objectives of this projects were achieved. A number of luminescent transition metal complexes containing a sugar moiety were developed as cellular probes for sugar uptake, bioimaging reagents, and metabolic indicators. The project was also extended to the rational design of novel bioorthogonal and PEGylation reagents, which are anticipated to offer unique luminescence and cellular uptake properties to transition metal complexes for a range of biological applications.

102212.label: Major findings and research outcome
102212.value: In this project, we designed a range of luminescent transition metal complexes bearing a sugar moiety. In the first study, we developed a new luminescent rhenium(I) fructose complex and its fructose-free counterpart. ICP-MS measurements revealed that the fructose complex entered MCF-7 cells much less efficiently than its fructose-free counterparts. Importantly, the uptake of the fructose complex by MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells was much more efficient than other cancer cells and normal cells, suggesting that related rhenium(I) fructose complexes have a high potential to serve as sugar-uptake indicators and breast cancer imaging reagents. In another study, three luminescent cyclometalated iridium(III) fructose complexes and their fructose-free counterparts were synthesized. The emission intensity of MCF-7 cells stained by one of the fructose complexes was higher than that of non-cancerous HEK293T cells. Also, the intensity was significantly reduced in the presence of unmodified fructose, implying that the uptake was regulated by membrane-bound fructose transporters. In addition to fructose pendant, we also isolated luminescent iridium(III) complexes containing a glucose or galactose moiety. The lipophilicity, the cellular uptake, and cytotoxic activity of the complexes toward HeLa cells were examined. ICP-MS experiments indicated that the cellular uptake of one the glucose complexes occurred through an energy-requiring process in additional to a pathway that was mediated by glucose transporters. Importantly, the cellular uptake efficiency of this complex was strongly dependent on hormonal stimulation and inhibition, rendering it a luminescent metabolic indicator, which is the first of its kind. Luminescent iridium(III) and rhenium(I) complexes containing a DIBO moiety were designed as bioorthogonal probes for azide-modified sugar units. These DIBO complexes underwent facile reactions with azide derivatives and can selectively label azide-modified proteins. Upon incubation of CHO cells with these complexes, intracellular emission was observed, indicative of nonselective staining. However, upon pretreatment of the cells with the azido-sugar derivative Ac4ManNAz, intense emission was observed from the cell membrane, indicating that these DIBO complexes are promising candidates for imaging azide-labeled biomolecules. We designed new luminescent cyclometalated iridium(III) polypyridine PEG complexes and studied their photophysical, photochemical, and biological properties. The complexes were noncytotoxic in the dark, but became significantly cytotoxic upon irradiation. Confocal microscopy images revealed localization of the complexes in the mitochondria of live HeLa cells and the induction of rapid necrotic cell death upon light activation. The lack of dark toxicity and potential application of the complexes as a visualizing reagent were also demonstrated using zebrafish as an animal model.

102212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102212.value: We have demonstrated in this project that the modification of luminescent transition metal complexes with a sugar moiety allows them to exhibit selective cellular uptake properties. The most important finding is that the uptake of all the complexes was mediated by GLUTs. Since cancer cells show enhanced sugar-uptake, our results are extremely useful in the development of luminescent sugar uptake indicators and probes for cancer cells. In recent years, there has been a rapidly emerging interest in the applications of luminescent transition metal complexes in bioimaging; many of the complexes display interesting organelle-target capability. This feature, together with the favorable photophysical properties of transition metal complexes (for example, environment-sensitive and long-lived emission with a large Stokes shift) will facilitate the development of efficient bioimaging probes in specific intracellular locations. We have also shown that the modification luminescent transition metal complexes with DIBO and PEG units renders them to display bioorthogonal labeling characteristics and photocytotoxicity, respectively. On the basis of these interesting results, we believe that this project can be further developed, resulting in the strategic design of new sugar uptake indicators, selective cellular probes, and related inorganic therapeutic reagents.

102212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102212.value: The aim of this project is to design luminescent inorganic and organometallic transition metal glucose and fructose complexes as new cellular probes for sugar uptake, bioimaging reagents, and metabolic indicators. The membrane-bound proteins glucose transporters (GLUTs) are known to facilitate the transport of glucose and fructose through the plasma membranes. Since cancer cells require extra energy for uncontrolled cell growth, most of them overexpress GLUTs and show enhanced sugar uptake and metabolism. Thus, a number of fluorescent glucose and fructose derivatives have been isolated as sugar uptake indicators and imaging reagents for cancer cells. Despite this development, the use of luminescent transition metal glucose and fructose complexes in sugar uptake and bioimaging is relatively unexplored. In this project, we have designed and synthesized a range of luminescent transition metal glucose and fructose complexes, and studied their photophysical, photochemical, electrochemical, cellular uptake, and cytotoxic properties. As expected, these complexes display environment-sensitive emission properties, high photostability, and long emission lifetimes. The most important discovery is that they reveal selective uptake by cancer cells, rendering them to serve as a new generation of luminescent cellular probes for sugar uptake, bioimaging reagents, and metabolic indicators.

102412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102412.value: Multiple charge carrier pairs (electrons and holes paired as excitons) can be generated in semiconductor nanoparticles by the absorption of individual photons. When this happens the light to electronic charge generation process is much more energy efficient than normal. This has the potential to make solar cells more efficient, and nanocrystal based optoelectronic devices (lasers, optical switches, etc), much more feasible and less hindered by inefficient heat generation and other deleterious processes. Though multiple carrier generation (MCG) has been observed in many types of semiconductor nanoparticles, the precise mechanisms are not yet fully understood. There may be several processes depending on the type of semiconductor, and factors such as material quality and surface states influence the degree to which MCG is manifest. Initial enthusiasm for its application in the solar field has been tempered: some see the theoretical benefits to be less important in practice than initial experimental measurements appeared to indicate. Even so it would be advantageous to: (i) understand the basic nature of the MCG process(es); (ii) understand how material quality factors (degree of crystallinity, presence of surface charge trap sites, nature of the external environment at the particle surface) influence MCG and; (iii) be able to manipulate the electronic energy level structure of nanocrystals (through composition and size control) to favour enhanced MCG (lower photon energy threshold and increased probability). MCG occurs in bulk semiconductors and is a well known phenomenon, occurring via a process known as Impact Ionization (also termed a reverse Auger effect). This is the mechanism behind avalanche photodetectors and it has been used in low bandgap and semi-metal systems such as mercury cadmium telluride alloys to develop highly sensitive IR detectors. In that system MCG is enhanced by choosing alloy compositions that put the split-off band energy at resonance with the material’s bandgap energy. We believe that an analogous approach may be possible in our nanocrystal version of this particular material system, but with the added degree of freedom of tuning the bandgap via the nanocrystal’s size, to allow the two energies to be independently adjusted. A goal will be to obtain efficient MCG over a wider range of bandgap energies than in the bulk material. In addition, these materials can be engineered to have very low electron effective masses and this reduces the energy threshold for multiplication to very close to the ideal of twice the bandgap energy. 半导体纳米晶颗粒吸收单个光子能够产生多重载流子电对(电子-空穴对即为激子)。当这一现象发生时，光电转换效率比常规情况下可以得到显著提高。这有利于制备高效能太阳能电池、优化纳米晶基光电子器件(如激光和光转换器件等)、减少由于不充分热激发及其他有害过程的阻碍。尽管在很多半导体纳米晶颗粒都发现了多激子激发现象(MCG),但是确切的产生机理尚未得到充分的阐述.根据半导体材料不同,可能存在不同的机理,比如材料的特性以及材料表面态等因素都会影响多激子激发(MCG)的明显程度。在太阳能领域的应用表明，多激子激发理论上的优势在实际的实验测试结果面前就显得不那么重要了，人们最初的研究热情受到打击。尽管如此，对以下几个方面的研究也是十分必要的：(i)探索多激子激发现象产生的本质，(ii) 理解影响多激子激发(MCG)的材料特性因素(如结晶度,表面电荷陷阱存在情况，以及颗粒周围外部环境的情况)，(iii)控制纳米晶电子能级结构以有利于增强多激子激发(MCG) (如通过成分和尺寸调控来降低光子激发能量阀值,提高多激子激发现象产生的概率)。 众所周知，多激子激发(MCG)通过一种已知的碰撞电离的过程（也称为反向俄歇效应）发生在块状半导体中。这是雪崩光电探测器背后的机理，它已被用于低带隙和半金属的系统，如利用碲化汞镉合金开发高度敏感的红外探测器。在该系统中，通过选择合金成分调控分裂带隙能与材料的带隙能产生共振, 进而增强多激子激发(MCG)。我们相信在这种特殊材料体系中，类似的激发途径可能存在于我们的纳米晶体形式中，而且通过改变纳米晶的尺寸具有更大的带隙调节自由度，并且可以实现两种能量独立调控。与块状材料相比，在一个更宽的带隙能量范围内，将更有利于实现高效率的多激子激发(MCG)。此外，通过材料设计，可以使其具有非常低的电子有效质量，这将 减少倍增能量阈值至非常接近理想的带隙能量的两倍。

102412.label: Realisation of objectives
102412.value: All objectives of this project have been fully achieved. On the synthetic tasks (objective 1), we showed how compositional control of CdHgTe nanocrystals by exchange of Hg2+ in place of Cd2+ ions can be used to tune their optical properties across a technologically useful range, from 500nm to almost 1200nm. We provide data on composition-dependent changes in the optical properties: bandgap; extinction coefficient; emission energy and spectral shape; Stokes shift; quantum efficiency; and radiative lifetimes as the exchange process occurs, which are highly relevant for those seeking to use these technologically important QD materials. For CdHgSe nanorods, we observed that the Hg2+ ions diffused into the rods to a point limited by stacking fault formation due to the different lattice structures of the two limiting cases of zinc blende and wurtzite. HAADF-STEM and EDS analyses confirmed that the Hg substitution did not occur uniformly throughout individual nanorods, with Hg-poor and Hg-rich regions coexisting around the stacking faults. The formation of NIR emitting alloyed CdHgSe nanorods in an aqueous medium highlights the subtle dependence of the ion exchange process on the differences in the crystal structures of the two endpoint lattices. On the spectroscopy tasks (objective 2), we systematically investigated the high-pressure photoluminescence and time-resolved carrier dynamics of thiol-capped CdTe nanocrsytals (NCs) of different sizes, at different concentrations, and in various stress environments. The zincblende-to-rocksalt phase transition in thiol-capped CdTe NCs is observed at a pressure far in excess of the bulk phase transition pressure. Additionally, the process of transformation depends strongly on NC size, and the phase transition pressure increases with NC size. These peculiar phenomena are attributed to the distinctive bonding of thiols to the NC surface. A number of different composition CdxHg1-xTe alloy quantum dots have been synthesized using a modified aqueous synthesis and ion exchange method. Transient Grating measurements revealed a composition dependant carrier multiplication process which competes with phonon mediated carrier cooling to deplete the initial hot carrier population. The interplay between these two mechanisms is strongly dependant on the electron effective mass which in these alloys has a marked composition dependance and may be considerably lower than the hole effective mass. We obtain evidence to suggest an impact ionization process analogous to the inverse Auger S mechanism seen in bulk CdxHg1-xTe. The investigation of sub-nanosecond exciton dynamics in HgTe quantum dots using ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy has shown that differential transmittance spectrum immediately after pumping is dominated by a bleach blue-shifted by ~200-300 nm from the photoluminescent emission band. Comparison with a tight-binding model of the electronic structure by Allan and Delerue allows this feature to be attributed to the filling of band edge states. In other samples , this bleach is superimposed with a broad photo-induced absorption feature that is attributed to the effects of surface trapping. The form of the pump-induced transmittance transients is dependent on the excitation rate and the rate of sample stirring. For moderate pumping of well-stirred samples, the transmittance transients are well-described by a mono-exponential decay associated with biexciton recombination, with a lifetime of 49 ps. For samples that are strongly-pumped or static, the decay becomes bi-exponential in form, indicating that trap-related recombination has become significant. On the objectives 3 and 4, for CdxHg1-xTe NCs with a composition x=0.52 we have determined a maximum carrier multiplication quantum yield of 199% +/- 19% with pump photon energy 3 times the bandgap energy, Eg, whilst the threshold energy is calculated to be just 2.15 Eg. For HgTe Ncs, we identified the occurrence of multiple exciton generation, which results in a quantum yield of 1.36%+/-0.04% for a photon energy equivalent to 3.1 times the band gap, in good agreement with the the theoretical model of Allan and Delerue.
