102412.label: Major findings and research outcome
102412.value: The major findings of this project related to the 4 objectives are summarized under 5.3. The research outcome related to those objectives constitutes 6 original publications and 3 review articles in refereed journals. On top of that and very importantly, this project has allowed us to move on towards the use of narrow-bandgap semiconductor nanocrystals in photodiodes. Specifically, a single layer, aqueous HgTe QD based photoconductor structure with very fast temporal response (up to 1 MHz 3dB bandwidth) is demonstrated. The device was fabricated using a simple spray-coating process and showed excellent stability in ambient conditions. The origin of the remarkably fast time response was investigated by combining light intensity-dependent transient photocurrent, temperature-dependent photocurrent and field-effect transistor (FET) measurements. The charge carrier mobility as well as the energy levels and carrier lifetime associated with the trap states in the QDs are identified. The results suggest that the temporal response is dominated by a fast bimolecular recombination process under high light intensity and by a trap-mediated recombination process at low light intensity. Interestingly, we found that the gain and time response of aqueous HgTe QD based photoconductors can be tuned by controlling the QD size and surface chemistry, which provides a versatile approach to optimize the photodetectors with selectable sensitivity and operation bandwidth. We also developed a well-controlled fabrication strategy to incorporate Au nanostructures into HgTe quantum dot (QD)/ZnO heterojunction photodiodes. Through an electrostatic immobilization and dry transfer protocol, a layer of Au nanorods with uniform distribution and controllable density is embedded at different depths in the ZnO layer for systematic comparison. More than 80% and 240% increments of average short-circuit current density (Jsc) are observed in the devices with Au nanorods covered by ~7.5 nm and ~4.5 nm ZnO layers, respectively. A periodic finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation model is developed to analyze the depth-dependent property and confirm the mechanism of plasmon-enhanced light absorption in the QD layer. The wavelength-dependent external quantum efficiency spectra suggest that the exciton dissociation and charge extraction efficiencies are also enhanced by the Au nanorods, likely due to local electric field effects. Our fabrication strategy and theoretical and experimental findings shed new light on the applications of metal nanostructures to enhance the performance of organic/inorganic hybrid optoelectronic devices. The findings of this work have been reported in 2 original publications.

102412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102412.value: This project has generated a considerable body of data, both from the ultrafast spectroscopy measurements and also from the supporting synthesis and characterization tasks. We will establish contacts with theoretical groups active in the nanoparticle MCG field , drawing together empirical relationships between carrier dynamics and MCG on the one hand, and material factors such as particle quality (degree of crystallinity), size, shape, surface/ environment and composition on the other. Fuelled with a coherent set of experimental data combined with the considerable theoretical inputs we will elucidate the role of structural and compositional elements in MCG; show how to realize the potential improvements that should be available, but which to date have not been fully achieved; and to develop a model for Carrier Multiplication that will allow further efficient materials to be designed on a firm engineered basis.

Though multiple carrier generation (MCG) has been observed in many types of semiconductor nanoparticles, the precise mechanisms are not yet fully understood, and factors such as material quality and surface states influence the degree to which MCG is manifest. This project focused on the following points related to semiconductor nanocrystals: (i) understand the basic nature of the MCG process(es); (ii) understand how material quality factors (degree of crystallinity, presence of surface charge trap sites, nature of the external environment at the particle surface) influence MCG and; (iii) be able to manipulate the electronic energy level structure of nanocrystals (through composition and size control) to favour enhanced MCG (lower photon energy threshold and increased probability). The goal is to obtain efficient MCG over a wider range of bandgap energies than in the bulk material. In addition, these materials can be engineered to have very low electron effective masses and this reduces the energy threshold for multiplication .

102712.label: Project Title(Chinese)
102712.value: 关于汗气运动中的非线性及强隅合抛物方程组的数值研究

102712.label: Project Objectives
102712.value: Mass and heat transfer in porous fibrous media can be found in numerous industrial and engineering applications [8,11,12,13,14,19,22,25,35,39,40,46]. Even though the physical models are similar in these applications, there exist unique characteristics for each problem. One of important features in functional clothing, such as clothing assemblies, is its structure of lamination and weaving such that many textile materials in the applications can be considered to be transversally isotropic/periodic. New formulations for these features of textile materials will be studied in this project. Another important feature is the complex phase changes, condensation/evaporation, absorption and radiation. The water content distribution, which is mainly determined by the phase changes, plays a key role in the study of functional clothing. More precise description of the phase changes is necessary. Usually the condensation/evaporation can be described by the difference of vapor pressure and saturation pressure, $i.e.$, Hertz-Knudsen equation when the batting area is wet. A truncated Hertz-Knudsen equation may be introduced to describe the condensation/evaporation for the general dry-wet case. In all the previous works, the fiber absorption was described by an evolution equation along the fiber radius with a saturated condition on the surface of a single fiber. This implies that the absorption on the fiber surface is enforced to be in saturation for a given relative humidity. This may not be realistic for textile materials. A resistant coefficient should be introduced on the interface between the fiber string and free air, with which a flux type condition would be more reasonable in this case. Here the resistant coefficient is material/structure-dependent. The sweat transport in porous textile media can be described by a nonlinear, degenerate and strongly coupled parabolic system in general. However, mathematical analysis for these models is very limited mainly due to the lack of a reasonable link between modeling in engineering and analysis in mathematics. In this project, we shall study existence, uniqueness and regularity of solution for a more general system with a class of commonly used boundary conditions. The difficulties arise mainly due to the strong coupling and complex phase changes. When the transversally isotropic/periodic media are introduced to the current model, multi-scale and homogenization techniques will be used in our analysis. More important is that the analysis proposed in this project can be applied to those multi-component heat and mass transport models in many other areas and also, our analysis will provide a fundamental tool for theoretical analysis of numerical methods. Another important issue is to develop an effective numerical scheme with either finite volume or finite element methods for solving the system of nonlinear parabolic equations. Due to the physical features, the proposed method should be able to handle more complicated cases. (i) Due to the complex three dimensional geometries, an uncoupled FE/FV method with an unstructured mesh could be more suitable for this system. (ii) An unconditionally stable scheme is expected for numerical simulation in a long time period (8h-24h) of the practical interest. (iii) A variety of physical boundary conditions, nonlinear, local and nonlocal, and possible interaction with human thermoregulation system should be included. (iv) A moving interface may arise due to the jump of some physical parameters in a cold environment. A more efficient approximation around the moving interface, such as immersed approximations, will be investigated to improve both the accuracy and stability of numerical methods. The optimal error estimates and stability analysis of the proposed method will be conducted, in which a priori estimate of numerical solution is a key issue. In addition, numerical simulations for some practical cases and comparisons with existing experimental results will be made during the period of this project.

102712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102712.value: The aim of this project is to develop efficient numerical methods for a class of nonlinear, degenerate and strongly coupled parabolic systems. Applications of the systems can be found in many areas of engineering and science. Our attention will be paid to the sweat transport through porous textile media. Proposed numerical methods should be able to handle complex three-dimensional geometries, complex phase changes and moving interfaces. Numerical simulations will be compared with existing experimental data. 该研究计划的主要目的是要发展有效的数值方法,求解一类非线性,退化及强隅合的抛物方程组,此类抛物方程组在许多科学及工程领域有着广泛的应用。而我们将集中于多孔纺织,材料中水汽运动方程组。我们希望我们的数值方法能够处理,复杂地三组几何,相变及移动的界面。

102712.label: Major findings and research outcome
102712.value: We have studied the heat and sweat transport in porous textile materials with a non-local thermal radiation and phase change. The model, based on a combination of these classical heat transfer mechanisms (convection, conduction and radiation), is governed by a nonlinear, degenerate and strongly coupled parabolic system. The thermal radiative flow is described by a radiation transport equation and characterized by the thermal absorptivity and emissivity of fibre. A conservative boundary condition is introduced to describe the radiative heat flux interacting with environment. With the conservative boundary condition, we prove the global existence of positive/non-negative weak solutions of a nonlinear parabolic system. In addition, an uncoupled (splitting) Galerkin method with semi-implicit Euler scheme in time direction is proposed for the system. In this method, a linearized scheme is applied for the approximation to the Darcy's velocity simultaneously in the mass and energy equations, which leads to physical conservation of the method in the flow convection. The existence and uniqueness of solution of the finite element system is proved and the optimal error estimate in an energy norm is obtained. Numerical results are presented to confirm our theoretical analysis and compared with experimental data.

102712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102712.value: An unconditional error analysis and simulations for some practical three-dimensional cases are of high interest.

102712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102712.value: Numerical methods and simulations play an important role in the design of functional clothing. In this project, a mathematical model was introduced to describe the sweat transport in porous textile media, based on a combination of those classical heat transfer mechanisms (convection, conduction and radiation). An efficient Galerkin finite element method was proposed for solving the system. Our numerical simulations compared with existing experimental data showed the accuracy and efficiency of methods and confirmed our theoretical analysis.

102912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102912.value: 這個建議的目的是利用掃描長光程差分光學吸收光譜儀（LP-DOAS) 觀察二氧化氮 (NO2) 在香港的分佈，從而制造出香港獨有的污染地圖。目的是利用空間分辨的數據來監測和改善空氣質素(如附近的交通控制氮氧化物的熱點，煙霧事件預測)。二氧化氮在區域的準確濃度和它們的分佈是有必要知道的。首先，這些資料可 用作評估化學運輸模組的質量。二，亦可用作區分及分配總排放量的來源。第三，並可利用數據分析作不同地區污染物的研究。 在這LP-DOAS計劃，我們將利用城大現有的LP-DOAS儀器， 並配合安裝全新的反射器在不同的地區及方位上，作不同高度和距離的量度。這種科技，使用紫外/可見光一種復古的反射光，並測量反射光，準確量度二氧化氮濃度的特徵和吸收結構。 LP-DOAS系統將連續測量NO2濃度沿光路，以獲得長期的數據集並創建濃度地圖。測量路徑的範圍可以從幾百米到2.5公里以便可以覆蓋一個寬闊的面積。LP-DOAS所得出的數據將用作於數據模組 (CMAQ) 的驗證。

102912.label: Realisation of objectives
102912.value: All objectives have been achieved in this project, including setting up a LP-DOAS instrument with multiple reflectors, combining measurement paths in different directions to form concentration map and derive vertical concentration profile, exploring ToTaL-DOAS, validation of CMAQ model and improving OMI NO2 data validation. Overall, this research has produced 4 journal publications (3 published and 1 under preparation), and 5 academic theses (2 Philosophy Doctor and 3 Master of Science). Below is the discussion of the objectives: Objectives 1, 2 and 3: Setting up an active long-path DOAS instrument with multiple retro-reflectors in different directions, develop concentration map and concentration profiles. A total of three retro-reflectors were installed in three different buildings, which includes Langham Place Hotel, Maryknoll Fathers’ school, and Tai Hang Tung Estate. Both Langham Place Hotel and Maryknoll Fathers’ school were first installed at the beginning of the sampling, while the retro-reflector from Tai Hang Tung Estate was installed in December 2015 due to the problem of getting permission from the property management (i.e., it took us more than 1.5 years to obtain the permission). As a result, the sampling period of Tai Hang Tung Estate didn’t fall within the study period. To resolve the issue, we processed the minute-by-minute data of LP-DOAS into hourly data, and integrated with the monitoring data from Hong Kong Environmental Protection Department (HKEPD) to derive the concentration map for Mongkok and Sham Shui Po areas. In terms of vertical concentration profile, we performed Cavity-Enhanced DOAS (CE-DOAS) measurement at both Langham Place Hotel (both South and North wings) and Tai Hang Tung Estate for determining the vertical concentration profiles of NO2 in Mongkok and Sham Shui Po. A technique was developed to link those data of HKEPD with LP-DOAS, which is documented in the thesis of Miss Melanie Bräu (please note that the study of vertical profile measurement is documented in the thesis of Mr. ROETTGER Clemens). Objective 4: Exploring the possibility to use Topographic Target Light scattering DOAS (ToTaL-DOAS) to increase the spatial resolution of the concentration maps. The technique of using LP-DOAS to perform Topographic Target Light scattering DOAS (ToTaL-DOAS) has been performed. A new algorithm has been written to control the motor of LP-DOAS telescope (See the thesis of Mr. Ivo Lipkowitsch – after page 31) to back and forth measuring the sunlight intensity reflected from buildings and pre-defined reference plates, which mimics the operation of ToTaL-DOAS. Overall, the results show that there are still many technological challenges in this method, which include 1) how to reduce measurement errors produced from ToTal-DOAS; 2) Identify sufficient building materials and its reflective properties, and 3) how pollutants (i.e., PM2.5 and O3) and local visibility affect the measurement of ToTal-DOAS. Due to these outstanding issues, we have decided not to use the measurement data from ToTaL-DOAS technique for generating concentration map. We recommend that further investigation would be needed. Objective 5, 6 and 7: Validation of CMAQ runs with LP-DOAS, Ozone Monitoring Instrument (OMI) and derives better OMI retrieval for CMAQ simulation. In this study, CMAQ air quality simulation has been performed for 2006 and 2012. In terms of 2006 simulation, it was designed to develop a better OMI retrieval technique for the CMAQ validation. The reason for selecting 2006 was due to the fact that OMI data in Oct 2006 to Jan 2007 in South China was much better than other years because of less cloud coverage. Moreover, air quality observation for the entire Pearl River Delta was coincidentally available on this time period. As a result, a full study using 2006 data for developing new OMI processing algorithm for better extrapolating OMI pixel resolution into finer resolution grid for CMAQ comparison had been developed. This part of the research has produced 1 PhD dissertation and 2 publications in the high impact factor journals (i.e., AMT and ACP) of Atmospheric Science. In terms of 2012 CMAQ air quality simulation, NO2 measurement data (e.g., LP-DOAS, OMI and HKEPD stations) were used for the CMAQ validation. In order to fully utilize the benefit of the rich dataset from local observation, we have implemented a multilayer urban canopy model with updated Sea Surface Temperature (SST) in WRF (the meteorological model for use in CMAQ simulation) to produce a better local and regional transport pattern of air pollutants. The sensitivity test using local NO2 observation has also been performed to calibrate the local emissions in CMAQ. The result of CMAQ air quality simulation was validated with local NO2 observations. The detailed discussion on the implementation of CMAQ with urban canopy WRF is documented in the PhD thesis of Mr. NG Chak Piu.

102912.label: Major findings and research outcome
102912.value: In this study, we established the first NO2 LP-DOAS monitoring network in Hong Kong. This network not only provides the real-time NO2 air pollution in urban Hong Kong, but also is useful for detecting regional transport of air pollutants from Pearl River Delta. From the modeling study, we have demonstrated the data derived from LP-DOAS (e.g., concentration map) can be used to calibrate or validate the fine-resolution air quality simulation in CMAQ. The implementation of urban canopy WRF in CMAQ offers a great improvement on the pollutant transport on a local scale (e.g., reduced overestimated wind speed and improved wind direction of land-sea breeze). Several findings/outputs have been produced from this research, which includes 1) new technique to link data from LP-DOAS to local observation using local vertical NO2 profile derived from CE-DOA; 2) new retrieval algorithm for extrapolating OMI pixel into finer resolution grid in CMAQ; 3) technique for comparing CMAQ simulation with OMI data. Overall, the study has developed a total of 4 journal publications (3 published and 1 under preparation), 3 conference papers, 2 PhD theses, and 3 MSc theses).

102912.value: Further development of this research includes 1) More investigation on how to use LP-DOAS as ToTaL-DOAS for NO2 profile measurement (A master student from LMU as an exchange student will take this topic as his master thesis in September 2017). 2) Develop a better approach to measure NO2 vertical profile and be used for developing 3D urban NO2 map (A proposal has been written for Environment Conservation Fund to develop that). 3) Develop land-use regression model for alternative 3D NO2 map that links between 1 km-resolution CMAQ with street-level NO2 concentration. (GRF proposal has been submitted on this topic this year).

102912.value: In this study, the first Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2) monitoring network using LP-DOAS technology has been developed. The network not only provides the real-time NO2 air pollution data at the elevated locations, but also provides a way of detecting regional transport of air pollutants (e.g., Pearl River Delta) through a minute-by-minute monitoring. Data collected from the LP-DOAS network (a map of NO2 pollutants) offers rich NO2 measurement data for use in calibrating and validating regional air quality model. This study has contributed and developed several tools and techniques to link NO2 satellite and LP-DOAS data with regional air quality model to achieve a better air quality prediction in ultra high-resolution for the purpose of air quality management in Hong Kong. Overall, the study has produced a total of 4 journal publications, 3 conference papers, 2 doctoral theses, and 3 master theses.

103212.label: Project Objectives
103212.value: Design and synthesize a class of shape-persistent, linear aromatic carboxylic acid molecules functionalized with the thiol (-SH) function. Crystallization with hard metal salts to construct the targeted sulfur-functionalized porous metal-organic frameworks. To preclude the thiol groups from coordinating to the metal ions, we here focus on using chemically hard ions such as Eu(III), Zr(IV), Al(III), and Cr(III). The standard and highly effectively solvothermal synthesis techniques will be employed. Diffuse soft metal species (e.g., BiBr3, HgCl2) into the porous host net to directly generate the covalent (strong), electroactive metal-thiolate links across the molecules. We also plan to conduct preliminary measurements/studies on the resultant materials with regard to porosity (e.g., pore volume/surface area measurement), conductivity and optical absorption properties.

103212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103212.value: 我们提出一种通用的方法合成含有多孔结构以及高电子活性金属-硫功能团的刚性结晶固体材料，从根本上影响广泛的传感器技术，多相催化和光电化学电池。金属-硫键因其强的键能和多功能电化学活性而著称。然而，将此类化学键融合到结晶性多孔材料仍然是一项挑战，因为键能和结晶度之间存在着固有的冲突：这种非常强的金属-硫键形成速度非常快并且不可逆，最终形成的框架材料就倾向于无序排列。将结晶过程从金属-硫键形成中分离出来是解决键能和结晶度之间矛盾的一种有效方法。为此我们倡导一种循序渐进的策略：首先，我们采用较易可逆的金属-羧基配位键来形成前驱的结晶网络；其次，我们在该预先建立的框架中引入强的金属-硫键。合成方法的有效性源自于我们在合成分子设计和网络工程上的长期努力。此分子有两方面有机功能特性：一方面，化学硬性的羰基极为倾向于化学硬性的金属离子（例如，Ln3+ 或Zr4+）；另一方面， 化学软的硫醇（-SH)功能团相对于硬的金属离子更倾向于软的（例如， HgCl2，SnCl2）。这种双功能团分子使下列叙述成为可能。首先，我们先使硬的羰基与硬的金属离子反应形成最初的网络结构，此时，软的含硫功能团不与硬的金属作用--它们在此步保持自由状态且不影响前提网络的形成；其次，我们向这个主体网络中引入相对软的金属化合物（例如，BiBr3, HgCl2），以便其与硫醇反应而形成共价（强）金属-硫键而非仅仅去增强前体网络骨架，更重要的是，可以提高整个网络的电活性和电荷转移。

103212.label: Realisation of objectives
103212.value: The realization of objects 1 and 2 (which focus on design and synthesis of thiol decorated linear ligands and crystallization with hard metal salts to form metal-organic frameworks) can be best illustrated by our published papers. As a major breakthrough of implementing this project, we successfully install free-standing, accessible thiol functions (-SH) in robust, porous coordination networks for wide-ranging reactivities and properties in the solid state. Application of the hard-and-soft strategy is best illustrated by the combination of chemically very hard carboxyl groups to suppress the soft thiol-metal interaction, especially hard metals ions such as Al(III), Cr(III), Eu(III) and Zr(IV). The frameworks published (especially 4, 5 and 6) are assembled by reacting ZrCl4 or AlCl3 withH2DMBD and H2DMTD featuring the hard carboxyl and soft thiol functions. The resultant Zr-DMBD, Zr-DMTD and Al-DMBD frameworks are of the UiO-66 and CAU-1 topologies, respectively, with the carboxyl bonded to the hard Zr(IV) or Al(III) center, and the thiol groups decorating the pores. The strong affinity of the thiol groups for soft metal species thus provide for a wide range of opportunities for accessing nanostructured metal species within porous coordination net-works for energy and catalysis applications. The realization of object 3 was accomplished by further exploration into metal species loading and potential applications in catalysis and metal detection. The fruitful results are well demonstrated in paper 1, 4 and 5. We started with thioether decorated Zn(II) frame-work to pave way for more sophisticated and reactive thiol MOFs. Highly specific, distinct color change in response to Pd species was discovered in the crystals of a metal-organic framework with pendant allylthio ether units. The color change (from light yellow to or-ange/brick red) can be triggered by Pd species at concentrations of a few ppm, and points to potential use in colorimetric detection and quantification of Pd (II). The effective uptake of the Pd(II) analytes by thioether and alkene functions within the porous solid also offers rich potential for catalysis applications. To apply such strategy in catalysis application, self-standing thiol groups within a Zr(IV)-based MOF Zr-DMTD was synthesized, anchor-ing Pd(II) atoms by simple soaking in Pd solution for catalytic applications. The spatial constraint prevents the thiol groups from poisoning the Pd center, while the strong Pd-S bond precludes Pd leaching and enables multiple cycles of heterogeneous catalysis. In addition, thiol function in Zr-DMBD proves especially useful for accessing the Hg2+-laden solid of ZrBDSO3-Hg, with enhanced catalytic activity in C2H2 hydration under mild conditions. In particular, the Zr-DMBD with free-standing thiol groups was found to react readily with I2 molecules to form sulfenyl iodide (S-I) units (paper 6), which are normally high un-stable, and exhibited distinct stability even at elevated temperatures (e.g., 90 ºC). On a conceptual plane, this simple and effective solid host also captures the spatial confinement observed for the complex biomacromolecular scaffolds involved in iodine thyroid chemistry, wherein the spatial isolation and consequent stabilization of sulfenyl/selenenyl iodides are exerted by means of the protein scaffolds. In addition, linking to advantages provided by the thiol systems, we designed a novel and simple covalent metal-organic framework on the front of symmetrical rigid thiol systems, by directly reacting a triphenylene hexathiol (HTT in paper 2) molecule with PtCl2. Besides the very rigid, symmetrical shape imposed by the fused aromatic core of tri-phenylene unit, the chelating dithiolene unit of HTT is poised to form rigid, well-defined bonding motifs with metal ions; the sulfur atoms are fully conjugated with triphenylene core to provide conductive pathways in the prospective solid state frameworks. The HTT-Pt (as demonstrated in paper 2) features substantial porosity, redox activity and ion exchange ca-pability.

103212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
103212.value: Imbedding metal ions in porous frameworks offers great potential for opening novel reactivities, and electronic properties, and thiol-laced frameworks will remain uniquely important in these studies. As a quick and inexpensive method for screening Pd species, ASMOF-5 (especially the more stable as-made crystals) should be of potential use. Dangling thiol groups within Zr-DMTD framework lead to spatial constraint effect and feature biomacromolecular scaffolds. Future deployment of the ZrDMBD-Pd solid in a continuous flow setup would serve to boost its overall turnover numbers. Oxidizing ZrDMBD-Hg into more rigid and catalytic active ZrBDSO3-Hg casts light on a variety of novel hybrid materials with minimized loss of metal and environmental impacts, while at the same time optimize catalytic activity by simple post-modification. For wider-ranging applications regarding catalysis and sensing, more robust systems based on harder metal ions such Al(III) and Zr(IV)-based MOFs should offer the ad-vantages of better stability.

103212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103212.value: This project studies a series of shape-persistent, linear aromatic carboxylic acid molecules functionalized with thiol (-SH). Several types of metal organic frameworks were success-fully constructed by crystallization with hard metal salts (especially Al and Zr). The strategy of hard-and-soft is applied to preclude the thiol groups from coordinating to the metal ions. The standard and highly effectively solvothermal synthesis techniques were employed. Sulfur as electron donors readily bind various metal ions and offers flexible control over the amount and type of metal ions to be deployed in the pores. The pendant allylthio ether con-taining ASMOF-5 changes into distinct brick red color highly specific in response to Pd species at concentrations low to parts per millions, as a promising colorimetric detector. The most significant part lies in ZrDMTD, which anchors each Pd to single seperated dangling thiol group within the framework. The spatial constraint prevented Pd from being poisoned while the S-Pd bonding prevented leaching. Flexible control over the amount and type of metal ions (even iodine) can be obtained for application in diverse catalytic reactions. A novel covalent metal-organic framework of conjugated aryl thiol and Pt was also studies in the semiconducting and ion exchanging properties.

103312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103312.value: Endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) can disturb development of the endocrine system and organisms directly or indirectly exposed during prenatal and early postnatal life. The current methods for the determination of EDCs involve time-consuming detection processes and complex pre-treatment steps, which are not suitable for in-situ monitoring of samples and rapid processing of multiple samples. The high number and structural diversity of EDCs calls for the urgent development of multiplexed biosensors/sensor arrays integrated with high-throughput sample processing power for monitoring activities (or measuring effects of the EDCs) rather than only the concentration of a single, or a set of, compounds. The objective of this project is to develop high performance microparticle-based assays which will be incorporated in microfluidic devices to create analytical systems that are rationally multiplexed for selective and quantitative detection and discrimination of multiple EDCs and for parallel processing of multiple samples. Specifically, we will develop biomimetic microparticles (BMMPs) that allow detection and discrimination of different EDCs via two distinct and complementary mechanisms. The first mechanism is based on the ability of EDCs to bind with specific endocrine receptors (ERs), with each EDC exhibiting a different and distinct affinity profile towards different types of ERs and ER-like receptors. We will develop a set of BMMPs with different linker-modified estrogen / EDC molecules immobilized on the surfaces, which can bind with different estrogen receptors (ERs) / estrogen-related receptors (ERRs). The receptor proteins will be conjugated with signal-generating and signal-amplifying elements, and competitive binding of EDCs in solution will lead to decrease of signals from the BMMPs. The second mechanism is based on recent studies that many EDCs interact strongly with, and even disrupt, artificial phospholipid bilayer membranes such as liposomes. By creating a set of multiplexed BMMPs, each displaying different phospholipid bilayer membranes with a different chemical character, we will be able to directly detect patterns of membrane partitioning, transport and disruption attributable to particular EDCs, and detect extent of reaction for different EDCs with specific endocrine receptors entrapped in BMMPs. Two separate breakthroughs developed by our research team, microfluidic-based microparticle display technology, and biomimetic microsphere technology, will be combined in a collaborative effort to develop a unique and powerful microanalytical approach that will allow point-of-need, field-based detection and profiling of EDCs. 103312.label: Realisation of objectives
103312.value: The objectives of the project have been achieved successfully.In this project, we have developed binding assay of endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) with endocrine receptors (ERs) and ER-like receptors by incorporating chemical/biochemical recognition elements on sensing surface. and verify the feasibility of the proposed signal generation and amplification method, Thiol-labeled long chain hydrocarbon with bisphenol A (BPA) was synthesized as head group and self-assembled on the Au nanoparticle surface of the sensing probes, with optimizing of the SAM layer and binding of ER-to SH-BPA on SAM, which showed a linear response upon the binding of estrogen receptor (ER-α) ranging from 1 to 30 nM. Detection of estrone, 17β-estradiol and BPA was achieved by integrating a competitive binding assay with the piezoelectric sensor. To validate the accuracy and application of the developed method, we spiked 5 nM of E1, E2 and BPA, the general concentration level of EDCs found in surface waters, tap water (pH 7.6) and seawater (pH 7.8) and conducted the recovery experiments. The recoveries of E1, E2 and BPA from tap water were in the range of 94.7 % to 102.6%, and the values from seawater were 106.4 % - 109.8%. The results confirmed that this binding assay would be a useful screening test for EDCs residues in environmental samples. We have also developed an Au nanoparticles decorated TiO2 nanotube arrays (NTAs) as a recyclable sensor for photoenhanced electrochemical detection of bisphenol A. The Au nanoparticles decorated on the tubular walls of self-organized TiO2 NTAs improved both the electrophotocatalytic activity and the electrocatalytic properties of the electrode. A key advantage of the high photocatalytic activity of TiO2/Au NTAs is that UV irradiation can be used during the detection processes to provide a fresh surface with high electrocatalytic activities continuously. The electrochemical system showed a widened detection linear range, increased sensitivity and decreased LOD for BPA detection with the ability to remove surface fouling during the detection process. The results demonstrated that the TiO2/Au NTAs have great potential as a sensitive and recyclable electrochemical sensing platform for online monitoring of BPA and other EDCs, which provide benefit to other integrated detection system. Furthermore, we have developed a microfluidic device consisting of sieving microstructures by single step photolithography for the formation of single layer array of microbeads for multiplexed bioanalysis. Without the need of specific geometry design of microchannels and peripheral equipment for liquid manipulation, microbeads with the diameter of several micrometers could be immobilized and aligned automatically into a linear array alongside the microchannel simply by exerting negative pressure from a manually-controlled syringe. Several protocols were established for developing microfluidic bead-based assays which include functionalization of microbeads with specific probes, formation of single layer array of microbeads in the microfluidic device, on-chip reaction, image acquisition and data analysis. We have demonstrated the feasibility using the microfluidic device to develop multiplexed assays for discrimination of viral genotypes and for parallel analysis of a panel of protein markers. This microfluidic device provides a universal platform for on-chip bead-based assays by combining the rapid binding kinetics of homogeneous microbeads assay and the efficient liquid handling capability of microfluidics, and can be used to develop other multiplexed assays for high-throughput analysis of biomolecules.

103412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103412.value: In the study of gas and fluid dynamics, there are many problems on limiting processes which are believed to be true in physics, but have not been justified rigorously in mathematics so that they remain as challenging mathematical problems. Related to what we are going to discuss in this project, let us first recall the following now well known limiting processes. In the study of rarefied gas, the Boltzmann equation was derived from a system of coupled Newton equations through the Boltzmann-Grad limit; when the Knudsen number tends to zero, the Boltzmann equation converges to the compressible Euler equations; and when the Knudsen number is close to zero, the Boltzmann equation can be approximated by the compressible Navier-Stokes equations. Moreover, when the viscosity and heat conductivity coefficients tend to zero, the Navier-Stokes equations converge to the Euler equations. On the other hand, when the Mach number tends to zero, the compressible systems tend to the corresponding incompressible systems. Furthermore, in some time scale and/or near some boundary, for example, with non-zero temperature gradient, there are other non-classical limiting fluid systems for the Boltzmann equation. In this project, we will focus on the limiting processes to the compressible Euler equations with wave interactions. Precisely, we will first consider the convergence rate of the vanishing viscosity limit of general hyperbolic systems with artificial viscosity. Secondly, we will consider the limits of the Navier-Stokes equations and the Boltzmann equation to the Euler equations. Note that even though there have been extensive studies on these problems and substantial results have been obtained in some settings. The mathematical justification with wave interactions basically remains unsolved.

103412.label: Realisation of objectives
103412.value: The project objectives have been achieved. The vanishing limits of the Navier-Stokes equations with interacting waves have been studied together with the limits of the Boltzmann equations to both the classical and non-classical fluid systems. Research results have been written into seven research papers, among them, five have been published in international refereed journals. In the first paper, we study the vanishing viscosity of the Navier-Stokes equations for interacting shocks. Given an entropy solution of p-system that consists of two different families of shocks interacting at some positive time, we show that such entropy solution is the vanishing viscosity limit of a family of global smooth solutions to the isentropic Navier-Stokes equations. The key point of the proof is to derive the estimates separately before and after the interaction time and connect the incoming and outgoing viscous shock profiles. Under the diffusion scaling and a scaling assumption on the microscopic component, a non-classical fluid dynamic system was derived in Bardos-Golse-Levermore-Yang that is related to the system of ghost effect derived by Sone in different setting. The second paper aims to justify this limit system for a non-trivial background profile with slab symmetry. The result reveals not only the diffusion phenomena in the temperature and density, but also the flow of higher order in Knudsen number due to the gradient of the temperature. Precisely, we show that the solution to the Boltzmann equation converges to a diffusion wave with decay rates in both Knudsen number and time. By constructing a non-trivial solution to the limiting system that is closely related to the Korteweg theory, we prove that there exists a sequence of smooth solutions of the Boltzmann equation converge to the limiting solution when the Knudsen number vanishes. This provides the first rigorous non-linear derivation of Korteweg theory from the Boltzmann equation and re-emphasizes the importance of Korteweg theory for the problem of thermal creep flow. The third paper is concerned with the existence of time periodic solutions of a compressible Navier-Stokes System in the whole space. We first solve the problem in a sequence of bounded domains, and letting the sequence tend to the original unbounded domain, we obtains the existence of a strong small periodic solutions as the limit of the corresponding sequence of solutions in the bounded domains. Even though the system of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations is not a limiting system of the Boltzmann equation when the Knudsen number tends to zero, it is the second order approximation by applying the Chapman-Enskog expansion. The purpose of the fourth paper is to justify this approximation rigorously in mathematics. That is, if the difference between the initial data for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations and the Boltzmann equation is of the second order of the Knudsen number, so is the difference between two solutions for all time. The analysis is based on a refined energy method for a fluid-type system using the techniques for the system of viscous conservation laws. In the fifth paper, we consider the initial value problem for the bipolar Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (bVPB) system and its related modified Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (mVPB) system. We give the spectrum analysis on the linearized bVPB and mVPB systems around an equilibrium state and show the optimal convergence rate of solutions to the equilibrium. It shows that the electric field decays exponentially and the distribution function tends to the absolute Maxwellian at the optimal convergence rate for the bVPB system, and both the electric field and the distribution function converge to the equilibrium state at the optimal rate for the mVPB system. The sixth paper concerns with the global existence and large time behavior of viscous compressible fluid in an infinitely expanding ball that involves the study on the time dependent boundary and degenerate density function. Due to the conservation of mass, the fluid in the expanding ball becomes rarefied and eventually tends to a vacuum state. This physical phenomenon is verified mathematically by obtaining the exact lower and upper bound on the density function. As a continuation of the sixth paper about the global existence and large time behavior of smooth compressible viscous fluid in an infinitely expanding ball, the seventh paper concerns with the case of inviscid fluid. Precisely, the flow is described by the 3-D unsteady potential equations with linearized operator that is degenerate at infinite time. It is expected by the mass conservation that the density of the flow tends to a vacuum state in time. We confirm this phenomenon and further show that there is no appearance of vacuum in any part of the expansive ball by establishing an exact lower and upper bound on the density function.

103412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
103412.value: There are many other kinds of limiting problems with wave interactions for both fluid and kinetic models. We hope the research in this project can be useful for the future study in different settings so that the limiting problems in the framework of weak solutions with wave structures can be investigated. Along this direction, one of the well-known and unsolved problems is the vanishing viscosity limit of the Navier-Stokes equations to the Euler equations for entropy solutions with bounded variation in one space dimension.

103412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103412.value: In the mathematical models in various physical considerations, there are physical parameters that are negligible compared with others in some settings. In particular, in the study of gas and fluid dynamics, there are many problems on limiting processes such as the vanishing of some physical parameters that are believed to be true in physics, but have not been justified rigorously in mathematics so that they remain as challenging mathematical problems. Among them, the vanishing viscosity limit and the vanishing Kundsen number limit, both to the compressible Euler equations, have attracted a lot of attention with important progress. 103712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103712.value: Convergent flows occur in many industrial applications. They represent an extremely important research field in fluids and in granular systems. For fluids, the dynamics is governed by a set of nonlinear partial differential equations and boundary conditions. Studying convergent flows in fluids poses a number of challenges, but the difficulty increases significantly when studying convergent flow in granular systems, in which the collisions between granular particles are inelastic. Many surprising and counterintuitive phenomena occur in such systems. However, the dynamics of convergent rapid granular flow is far from well understood. In this proposal, we plan to carry out a detailed study of the convergent rapid flows in a granular system. We will perform detailed numerical simulations for this complicated system to identify key phenomena and then achieve a good theoretical understanding of the fundamental mechanisms that underlie the behavior. In particular, we will conduct a careful study of the phenomena of intermittency in which a system alternates between two states. A good understanding of the phenomena of intermittency is very important in machine design in order to achieve stable operating conditions for the machine. 會聚性粒子流在件多工業應用中出現。它是流体和粒子体系中一個極其重要的研究領域。流體的行為是由一組偏微分方程組和邊界條件來確定。關于會聚形流体的研究存在許多困難。但關于會聚形粒子流的研究則更是難上加難。其中粒子之間的碰撞是非彈性的。許多吃驚的和反直覲的現象會出現。人們對會聚形粒子流的行為還十分不了解。在本課題中我們打算對會聚形快速粒子流作一個細致的研究。我們將對這個十分複雜的体系作仔細的數值模似以確定其主要的現象o這能讓我們從理論上對導致這些行為的最根本的機制得到一個很好的理解。我們將對這個體系在兩個狀態之間不斷地轉換的間歇性行為作仔細的研究。在機械設計中對間歇性行為有正確的理解是十分重要的。它可以讓機械保持在一個穩定的工作狀態。

103712.label: Realisation of objectives
103712.value: We have successfully achieved all objectives of this project. Surprising results have been obtained and published in Europhysics Letters and in Comptes Rendus Mathematiques. The following is the outline about how the objectives were achieved. 1. “Develop an efficient method to simulate convergent rapid flow in granular systems” The behavior of granular particles is stochastic. In contrast to fluids, there are no underlying partial differential equations governing the complicated dynamics of granular systems. Numerical simulation plays a critical role in the study of granular systems. An important issue in numerical simulations of granular systems is how to efficiently detect and to resolve inter-particle collisions. For a system with N particles, intuitively, it needs N^2 operations to detect inter-particle collisions. This is the event-driven collision detection algorithm which is only suitable for dilute systems in the absence of the formation of clusters. However, even for dilute particle systems, due to inelastic collision between particles and between particles and the boundaries, clusters may form. In such cases, a large number of collisions can occur within a short period of time. Then the event-driven algorithm is no longer suitable and the soft potential model will be more suitable for detecting and resolving collisions. We developed a hybrid algorithm that combines the collision detection method for low volume fraction regions and the potential method for high volume fracture regions. This allows us to propagate particles linearly in N even in the presence of clusters. 2. “Implement the numerical method and perform validation tests” To achieve our goal of propagating N particles and resolving collisions in just an order of N operations, we divide the particles into two groups: particles that have sufficiently long contacts are in the group using the potential method for propagation, and particles in low volume fraction regions are in the group using collision detection method for propagation. If a rapidly moving particle, originally in the collision detection method group, is sufficiently close to a high volume fraction region or if three or more rapidly moving particles collide during a time step then it will be transferred to the group that uses the potential method. On the other hand, if a particle, originally in the potential method group, moves sufficiently far away from any other particle, it will be transferred to the collision detection method group. In addition, an underlying mesh is used to achieve a fast detection of particle collisions. With a carefully designed data structure, we implemented an efficient and accurate numerical simulator for granular systems. The complexity of our numerical method scales linearly with number of particles, which is optimal. 3. “Carry out a detailed study of convergent rapid flow in granular systems.” We conducted detailed and systematic studies of convergent rapid granular flow. Since the systems are stochastic, we conducted a large number of simulations for each parameter set to determine the statistical properties of the system. 4. “Conduct a detailed study of intermittency in this system. Intermittency, a phenomenon that a system stays alternatively between two fundamentally different states, has not been observed for dilute rapid granular flow. Since the intermittency has not been observed in rapid nozzle flow in compressible gas dynamics, one believes such phenomenon will not occur for dilute rapid granular particles flowing through a nozzle. Surprisingly, we showed in this project that the phenomenon of intermittency did occur in dilute rapid granular flow. We conducted detailed studies on the phenomenon of intermittency for systems with various parameter values including a wide range of the nuzzle angle and a wide range of values for the coefficient of restitutions of the particles. We examined carefully when intermittency occurs. 5. “Identify new key phenomena in the convergent rapid flow in granular systems” We identify there are two qualitatively different states: a quiescent state and an excited state. These two states are related to two different types of particle trajectories: short trajectories and long trajectories. Particles with short trajectories typically do not experience inter-particle collisions and consequently have simple trajectories and short residence time. Particles with long trajectories typically experience several inter-particle collisions and have complicated trajectories and long residence time. Particles with short trajectories drive the system towards the quiescent state and particles with long trajectories drive the system towards excited state. At low injection frequencies, the probability of inter-particle collisions is low, most particles are short trajectories and the system is quiescent. By nondimensionalizing physical quantities, we show that, when all particles followed free-fall trajectories, the number of particles above the bottleneck would be exactly equal to the dimensionless injection frequency. At high injection frequencies, there are large number of inter-particle collisions. Therefore many particles have long trajectories and the system is in the excited state. At intermediate injection frequencies, the system could alternate between the quiescent state and the excited state in certain parameter ranges. Then the phenomenon of intermittency would occur. This behavior is very surprising since gas dynamics contains no analogue of this type of intermittency. 6. Provide a good theoretical understanding for the phenomena observed We have achieved a fundamental understanding why and when intermittency occurs. First, we explain the phenomenon of the transitions from quiescent to excited states. In the quiescent state, the particles have almost free-fall trajectories. This leads to a very low probability of inter-particle collisions. However, inter-particle collisions can cause initially short-trajectory particles to deviate from their mainly downward motion, become long-trajectory particles and hop back and forth between the walls. Long trajectory particles have significantly longer residence times and this increases the probability of more inter-particle collisions, which further converts more short-trajectory particles into long-trajectory particles. This positive feedback mechanism changes the state of the system from quiescent to excited. Therefore, the transition from a quiescent to an excited state occurs as a result of a low-probability collisional event. The probability of this type of event occurring determines the typical longevity of quiescent states. Clearly, the higher the injection frequency, the more likely a triggering event will be and hence the more short-lived a typical quiescent state will be. Second, we explain the phenomenon of the transitions from excited to quiescent states. In the excited state, there is a generation and loss of long-trajectory particles. The loss occurs because long-trajectory particles fall through the nozzle under gravity. The generation occurs because short-trajectory particles are converted into long-trajectory particles due to inter-particle collisions. The system needs a sufficient number of long-trajectory particles to maintain an excited state. However, there are significant fluctuations in the number of long-trajectory particles in excited states. At moderate injection frequencies, statistical variations can cause the number of long-trajectory particles to drop below the level required to maintain the excited state. The loss of long-trajectory particles leads to a feedback mechanism that reduces the rate of inter-particle collisions between long-trajectory and short-trajectory particles. Thus, fewer long-trajectory particles will be generated and the system can transition to the quiescent state. We further establish an order parameter, which is an analogue of Mach number in gas dynamics. The results from numerical simulations show that intermittency occurs at the regions where this order parameter is one. This further confirms our theoretical understanding of intermittency in granular systems.

103712.label: Major findings and research outcome
103712.value: In this project, we conducted careful and detailed studies on the phenomenon of intermittency in the rapid nozzle flow in granular systems [1,2]. Nozzle flow, involving the movement of gas through a narrowing opening, is of critical importance in applications such as turbines and rocket engines. It has therefore come to be considered as a basic setting for studying compressible gas dynamics. For high-speed flows, nozzle flows readily form shocks, but nevertheless, within the nozzle, the flow patterns tend to be relatively simple. Particularly, intermittent flow within the nozzle does not occur. It is widely believed that, in the absence of cluster formation, highly dilute granular flows exhibit qualitatively similar behavior to compressible gases. It is therefore natural to expect that the flow of a highly dilute granular material through a nozzle would be relatively simple and would not exhibit intermittency. However, in this project, we find a surprising phenomenon: intermittency can occur for very dilute granular particles falling under gravity through a nozzle. By intermittency, we refer to a system in which the boundary conditions and any external forcing are time-independent, but, even after any initial transient effects have died away, still exhibits alternation between two phases of fundamentally different dynamics. We determine the mechanism that leads to intermittency in nozzle flow in dilute granular systems [1,2]. This mechanism has no analogue in the corresponding fluid system [1,2]. Nozzle flows in granular materials are widespread in a broad range of industrial applications in which falling particles are caught and channeled into a small hole. Some design objectives often need to be met for such devices, such as controlling the velocity of particles passing through the nozzle and minimizing the wear on the nozzle. Particularly, many applications require that a steady flux of particles be maintained through the nozzle and hence intermittency in the flow can clearly constitute a serious problem. The results presented in this project represent an important advance obout the complicated dynamics of granular systems [1,2]. [1]. W. X. Guo, Q. Zhang and J. J. Wylie, "Dynamic Behavior of Convergent Rapid Granular Flows", Comptes Rendus Mathematique, 354, 864-868 (2016). [2]. W. X. Guo, Q. Zhang and J. J. Wylie, "Intermittency in dilute granular flows",Europhysics Letters, 115, 14003 (2016).

103712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
103712.value: The importance of understanding convergent flows in granular systems can hardly be overemphasized. For example, numerous industrial applications involve particles falling under gravity and interacting inelastically with each other and with rigid boundaries. Many of them require devices to guide falling particles through a thin exit. There are various industrial goals that such devices are designed to attain in applications, which include reducing the time that particles stay in the device in order to lower the possibility of particle interactions or jamming. The mechanism of inter-particle interactions and details of their trajectories are important information for realizing these objectives, and they may also help to obtain methods for minimizing excessive wear on devices. The results obtained from this project and new fundamental understanding about complicated dynamics of the granular particle systems will be very helpful for solving these important industrial problems.

103712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103712.value: In our world, huge portion of materials are in granular form. It is extremely important to understand in the dynamics and behavior of granular systems. However, granular systems are much more complicated than fluid systems. This imposes great difficulty in understanding the dynamic behavior of granular systems. The behavior of granular particles is stochastic and there is no partial differential equations governing the behavior of granular systems. In this project we conducted a detailed study of granular systems in the fundamental setting of nozzle flow and discovered a surprising phenomenon: intermittency, a phenomenon that a system stays alternatively between two fundamentally different states, can occur in such a fundamental setting. This phenomenon has never been found in rapid converging granular flow and there is no analogue phenomenon in compressible gas flow. We provided theoretical explanation why such a surprising phenomenon occurs in granular systems and identified the mechanism that lends to such phenomenon. The phenomenon of intermittency is important not only for the purpose of theoretical understanding, but also for industrial consideration, since it can cause serious problems in machine wearing and jamming in industrial processes. Thus, the results from this project will also be very helpful for many manufacturing processes and for material transportation since many of them involve granular particles.

103812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103812.value: Noble metal nanoparticles are powerful optical nano-antennas which significantly enhance the light that is incident on them and scattered. These unique optical properties of noble metal nanoparticles find useful applications in the non-destructive, non-invasive, non-toxic and ultrasensitive characterization of biological samples. Conventional Raman scattering typically provides a weak spectroscopic signal of molecules, rendering it useless for most practical purposes. However, when the molecules are introduced on the rough surfaces of noble metals or their nanoparticles, the amplified field provides an enormous enhancement of the Raman signal, thereby making the detection of a single molecule possible. Among the two field enhancement factors of Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS), the electromagnetic interactions are conceptually well understood and quantitatively accounted for. By contrast, the other component contributed by the chemical interactions is still only qualitatively explored and not quite clearly understood. An atomic level understanding of these two factors and their interplay in SERS is imperative for optimizing the enhancement effect in bio-sensory applications. We propose to develop a theoretical approach which will adequately account for both the components of SERS. The development of computational procedures that couple light with both nanoparticles and molecules at sub-nanometer scale is challenging. Appropriate theoretical models addressing such a broad length scale is needed for a quantitative extraction of the chemical contribution to SERS. We will implement an effective computational model for SERS into the versatile and efficient density functional tight binding method (DFTB) at the quantum mechanical level. The effects of shape, size and distribution of noble metal (such as Ag and Cu) nanoparticles on the silicon nanostructures will be thoroughly examined to maximize the dielectric sensitivity of our SERS substrate, which provides a vast surface area available to adsorbates. We will address the response of the dielectric-sensitive nano-antennas to the introduction of molecules, starting with simple molecules for standardization and gradually switching to complex bio-molecules pertaining to sensory applications. We plan to develop our approaches for practical bio-sensory applications, say, for immunoassay readout. Our many years of experience in computational approach development and study of nanostructures and surface adsorption will ensure a successful fulfillment of the proposed research. 贵金属纳米粒子具有强的光学纳米天线，显著增强了其上的入射和散射光。贵金属纳米粒子的这些独特光学性质在非破坏性、无创伤、无毒和超灵敏的生物样品的表征方面具有很好应用。传统的拉曼散射只能提供较弱的分子光谱信号，用处不大。然而，当分子引入到贵金属粗糙表面或它们的纳米粒子上面时，放大的电场极大增强了拉曼信号，从而使得单分子检测成为可能。在两个场增强表面增强拉曼光谱（SERS）的因素中，电磁相互作用的概念很好理解，也容易定量化。与此相反，化学相互作用的贡献尚缺乏定性探索和清楚的理解。原子水平理解SERS这两个因素及其相互作用对优化其在生物传感器应用中的增强效果是很有必要的。本项目将充分考虑这两个表面增强拉曼光谱因素并发展相应的理论方法。 发展亚纳米尺度的纳米颗粒和分子光耦合的计算方法具有挑战性。尚需要描述这样一个大尺度的定量提取SERS的化学贡献的适当理论模型。我们将发展一个研究表面增强拉曼光谱的有效计算模型，将其同灵活高效的量子力学水平的密度泛函（DFTB）方法相结合。将彻底考察硅纳米结构上的贵金属（如Ag和Cu）纳米粒子的形状、尺寸和分布的效应，以最大限度地提高SERS衬底的介电灵敏度。我们将讨论介电敏感的纳米天线对引入的分子的响应，从利用简单分子进行标准化开始，并逐步扩展到有传感应用的复杂的生物分子。可望能开发出实用的生物传感应用的新方法。我们对纳米结构和表面吸附计算研究的多年经验可确保圆满完成本项目的研究。

103812.label: Realisation of objectives
103812.value: (1) Development of SCC-DFTB framework for broad length scales ranging from molecules (sub-nanometer) to noble metal nanoparticles (a few nanometers): We have finalized the parametrization of the Ag-N Slater-Koster files. The files can be used together with the mio-1-1 set to model the interaction of molecules with silver surfaces. The files can also be used for excited state calculations. We have prepared also an overview over the fitting procedure and general performance of the silver files. The new Ag-N files allow also to model amine molecules on silver. Some calculations using the SCC-DFTB have been based on for higher level DFT calculations used in many of the researches we described below. (2) Chemical Mechanism and Tunability of Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering of Pyridine on Heteronuclear Coinage Metal Diatomic Clusters: As surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates, coinage bimetallic clusters offer high SERS enhancement and potential for applications in precision molecule detection. Here, we elucidate the chemical mechanism and reveal the tunability of the SERS of a pyridine molecule (Py) on coinage bimetallic substrate by investigating various possible heteronuclear coinage metal diatomic clusters (HCMDCs) interacting with the pyridine molecule. We obtain the Raman spectra, molecular orbital, and binding property of each HCMDC−Py system using density functional theory. (see Part C-8-1 for more details) (3) The mechanism of N–Ag bonding determined tunability of surface-enhanced Raman scattering of pyridine on MAg (M = Cu, Ag, Au) diatomic clusters: Binary coinage metal clusters can show a significantly different enhancement in surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) from that of pure element clusters, owing to their tunable surface plasmon resonance energies affected by the composition and atomic ordering. Yet, the tunability by composition requires a deep understanding in order to further optimize the SERS-based detection technique. To fill this deficiency, we conducted detailed analyses of the SERS of pyridine adsorbed through N–Ag bonding on the homonuclear diatomic metal cluster Ag2 and heteronuclear diatomic metal clusters of AuAg and CuAg, as well as the involved charge transfer under an intracluster excitation, based on calculations using time-dependent density functional theory with a short-time approximation for the Raman cross-section. (see Part C-8-2 for more details) (4) Strong Core@Shell Dependence in Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering of Pyridine on Stable 13-Atom Silver-Caged Bimetallic Clusters: Using time-dependent density functional theory, we conducted detailed analyses of the SERS of pyridine adsorbed on 13-atom icosahedral M@Au12 and M@Ag12 (M = Mo, W) clusters. (see Part C-8-3 for more details) (5) Nonresonant chemical mechanism in surface-enhanced Raman scattering of pyridine on M@Au12 clusters: By employing DFT, we study the nonresonant surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) of pyridine on M@Au12 (M = V−, Nb−, Ta−, Cr, Mo, W, Mn+, Tc+, and Re+)-the stable 13-atom neutral and charged gold buckyball clusters. Changing the core atom in M@Au12 enabled us to modulate the direct chemical interactions between pyridine and the metal cluster. (see Part C-8-4 for more details) (6) Reproducible and recyclable SERS substrates: Flower-like Agstructures with concave surfaces formed by electrodeposition: Direct synthesis of three-dimensional Ag structures on solid substrates for the purposes of producingreproducible and recyclable SERS applications remains challenging. In this work, flower-like Ag structures with concave surfaces (FACS) were successfully electrodepositedonto ITO glass using the double-potentiostatic method. (see Part C-8-5 for more details) (7) A durable surface-enhanced Raman scattering substrate: ultrathin carbon layer encapsulated Ag nanoparticle arrays on indium-tin-oxide glass: The application of Ag nanostructures to surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is hindered by their chemical instability. Fabrication of durable Ag-based SERS substrates is therefore of great significance in practical applications. In this work, ultrathin C-layer-encapsulated Ag nanoparticle arrays (UCL-Ag-NAs) are successfully fabricated on the surface of indium-tin-oxide (ITO) glass, using a hydrothermal method, for use as durable SERS substrates. (see Part C-8-6 for more details) (8) To accumulate more knowledge for designing efficient SERS substrates, we have further studied the interaction of functional molecules with substrates, including physisorption of benzene derivatives on graphene and the critical roles of steric and stereoelectronic effects of the substituent, the stability of graphene containing defects covered by a water layer, and signatures in vibrational and UV-visible absorption spectra due to the interaction between cyclic hydrocarbons and graphene fragments. (see Part C-8-7, 8 & 9 for more details) (9) Vibrational and excited-state properties of nanoscale systems: Stable Isomers of (SiO)n(0,±) (n = 2-7) Clusters, graphite under uniaxial pressure, two dimensional silicon nanosheets, ultraviolet photoreceptor UVR8. (see Part C-8-10, 11, 12 & 13 for more details) (10) Designs of functional nanoscale systems: heterometallic molecular junctions, chiral molecules with enhanced environmental-confinement-induced stability, two-dimensional topological insulators with binary honeycomb lattices: SiC3 siligraphene and its analogs. (see Part C-14, 15 & 16 for more details) (11) Nanoscale substrates for photoelectrochemical applications: carbon dot/TiO2 nanorod array nanocomposites with carbon dot loading and TiO2 nanorod length dependence of photoelectrochemical properties. (see Part C-17 for more details)

103812.label: Major findings and research outcome
103812.value: We find that the Raman characteristic peaks, adsorption energy, charge transfer, geometry parameters, and molecular orbital distribution are all closely related to the compositions and binding sites of the heteronuclear coinage metal diatomic clusters (HCMDC), providing the possibility of optimizing the SERS substrate by tuning the bimetallic cluster composition and adsorption site. (see Part C-8-1) The complexes based on heteronuclear metal clusters can produce varied electronic transitions owing to the polarization between different metal atoms, which tune the SERS enhancements with altered optical properties. (see Part C-8-2) Surprisingly, the signals of pyridine on M@Ag12 at charge transfer (CT) transition excitations are twice as much as that of pyridine on M@Au12, and the corresponding energies used for SERS excitations are significantly different in the low-energy region of 1.63−2.10 eV. The interactive modulation between the core and shell can produce varying strong CT transitions from metal clusters to pyridine, which tunes the SERS enhancements with altered optical properties. The complexes of pyridine on silver-caged clusters are more easily influenced by the tunability of the core than that of pyridine on gold-caged clusters. (see Part C-8-3) The magnitude of the chemical enhancement is governed, to a large extent, by the charged properties of the metal clusters. Polarizability and deformation density analyses clearly show that compared with the neutral and cation clusters, the anion clusters have more delocalized electrons and occupy higher energy levels in the pyridine–metal complex. Accordingly, they produce larger polarizability, leading to a stronger nonresonant enhancement effect. (see Part C-8-4) Our experimental efforts guided by our theoretical understanding further led to important findings. An enhancement factor of the order of 108 has been achieved using flower-like Ag structures with concave surfaces, exhibiting a SERS signal intensity 3.3 times stronger than that measured from Ag nanostructureswithout concave surfaces. A cleaning procedure involving lengthy immersion of the sample in ethanol and KNO3 was proposed to recycle the substrate and confirmed by using rhodamine 6G, adenine, and4-aminothiophenol as target molecules. The findings can help to advance the practical applications of Ag nanostructure-based SERS substrates. (see Part C-8-5) The problem of Ag nanoparticles dissolving during the hydrothermal process is solved by using ZnO powder as a pH-buffering reagent. This methodology can be generalized to improve the durability of other dimensional Ag nanostructures for SERS applications. (see Part C-8-6)

103812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103812.value: When molecules are introduced on the rough surfaces of noble metals or their nanoparticles, the amplified field provides an enormous enhancement of the Raman signal, thereby making the detection of a single molecule possible. One of the two field enhancement factors of Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) is the conceptually well understood electromagnetic interactions. However, the involved chemical interactions is still only qualitatively explored and not quite clearly understood. An atomic level understanding of these two factors and their interplay in SERS is imperative for optimizing the enhancement effect in bio-sensory applications. In this project, we have demonstrated a theoretical approach combining semiempirical theory and first-principles theory to adequately account for both the components of SERS. The approach allows us to optimize the shape, size and distribution of noble metal nanoparticles and thus maximize the dielectric sensitivity of our SERS substrate. In particular, we revealed chemical mechanism and tunability of SERS of pyridine on heteronuclear coinage metal diatomic clusters and strong Core@Shell dependence in SERS of pyridine on stable silver-caged bimetallic clusters. Our theoretical understanding further guided us to experimentally design efficient SERS substrates for molecular detection.

104012.value: 最小误差熵准则的学习理论方法及一些学习算法的逼近分析

104012.label: Project Objectives
104012.value: Learning theory approach to minimum error entropy criteria. A learning algorithm of error entropy minimization in an empirical risk minimization setting involves a scaling parameter. When the parameter becomes large, we shall show that under some conditions on the approximation error and covering numbers of the hypothesis space, the output function produced by the algorithm converges to the regression function with confidence. Possible limits of the output function will be analyzed under various symmetry, peak and convexity conditions of the conditional distributions when the parameter becomes small. Minimum error entropy regularization schemes will also be considered. Approximation analysis of some learning schemes dealing with multivariate data. We shall study multivariate quantile regression problems involving sets of directions in frameworks of empirical risk minimization and regularization. Error analysis will be conducted by error decomposition techniques. The group effect and sparsity of the elastic net will be analyzed when the hypothesis space is data independent or is a data dependent subspace of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Ranking algorithms will be analyzed by an approximation theory approach involving various loss functions. Some problems on peptides, alleles, and binding affinity arising from bioinformatics will be considered from viewpoints of kernel methods in learning theory. An interesting approximation theory problem on positive and positive semidefinite reproducing kernels will be discussed in order to deal with powers of kernels from bioinformatics.

104012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
104012.value: Least squares method is an important computational tool in various fields of science and engineering, and has been well developed in learning theory. An information theoretic alternative of this method is minimum error entropy criteria based on entropy and high order statistics. This project aims at mathematical analysis of minimum error entropy criteria by a learning theory approach and approximation analysis of some learning schemes dealing with multivariate data. We shall first show that an empirical risk minimization algorithm for minimizing empirical error entropy is consistent when the scaling parameter becomes large. Analysis of possible limits will be conducted by some ideas from wavelet analysis when the parameter becomes small. Then we shall study regularization schemes for multivariate quantile regression and ranking problems by error decomposition techniques. The group effect and sparsity of the elastic net in various settings will be analyzed. Methods from approximation theory and properties of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces will be applied to deal with various loss functions in our analysis. Finally some learning theory problems on peptides, alleles, and binding affinity arising from bioinformatics will be considered and an approximation theory problem on positive and positive semidefinite reproducing kernels will be discussed. 最小二乘法在不同的科学及工程领域中是一种重要的计算工具，在学习理论中已得到良好的发展。在信息理论中的一个替代方法是基于熵和高阶统计量的最小误差熵准则。本项目旨在用学习理论方法给最小误差熵准则提供数学分析并给一些处理高维数据的学习算法作出逼近分析。我们将首先证明一个最小化经验误差熵的经验风险最小化算法当伸缩参数变大时是收敛的。当伸缩参数变小时我们将利用小波分析的一些想法去分析可能的极限。然后我们将利用误差分解技巧研究几个应用于高维分位数回归和排序的正则化算法。弹性网的群体现象及稀疏性将在不同框架下得以考虑。来自逼近论的方法和再生核希尔伯特的性质将在我们的分析中用于处理不同的损失函数。最后，一些产生于生物信息学的关于氨基酸，对偶基因及其捆绑能力的学习理论问题和一个关于正定半正定再生核的逼近论问题也将在本项目中讨论。

104012.label: Major findings and research outcome
104012.value: We study in [1] the consistency of the empirical minimum error entropy (MEE) algorithm in a regression setting. Error entropy consistency and regression consistency are introduced. The error entropy consistency is shown to be always true if the bandwidth parameter tends to 0 at an appropriate rate. We prove that the error entropy consistency implies the regression consistency for homoskedastic models where the noise is independent of the input variable. For heteroskedastic models, a counter-example is used to show that the two types of consistency do not coincide. The regression consistency is shown to be true true, provided that the bandwidth parameter tends to infinity at an appropriate rate. In [2], Lin, Rosasco and the PI consider the problem of supervised learning with convex loss functions and propose a new form of iterative regularization based on the subgradient method without constraint or penalization achieving generalization by early stopping. We prove consistency and finite sample bounds on the excess risk in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces under general regularity conditions. Our study provides a new class of efficient regularized learning algorithms and gives insights on the interplay between statistics and optimization in machine learning. Within the last few years, there has been considerable work on analyzing learning algorithms with pairwise loss functions in the batch setting. There is relatively little theoretical work on analyzing their online algorithms, despite of their popularity in practice due to the scalability to big data. In [3], Guo, Ying and the PI consider online learning algorithms with pairwise loss functions based on regularization schemes in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and establish the convergence of the last iterate of the online algorithm. In [4], Ying and the PI consider unregularized online learning algorithms and derive explicit convergence rates for classification associated with a general Gamma-activating loss and a general condition for the convergence of the last iterate. In [5], Yuan and the PI establish minimax optimal rates of convergence for estimation in a high dimensional additive model assuming that it is approximately sparse. Our results reveal a behavior universal to this class of high dimensional problems: in the sparse regime, the optimal rates are identical to those for high dimensional linear regression, while in the smooth regime, the rates coincide with the optimal rates for estimating a univariate function, and therefore they are immune to the curse of dimensionality.

104012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
104012.value: Research results produced and methods developed in this project lead to some ideas for studying further online learning and learning with pairwise loss functions. We shall investigate these problems in our future work.

104012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
104012.value: Least squares method is an important computational tool in various fields of science and engineering, and has been well developed. An information theoretic alternative is minimum error entropy (MEE) criteria based on entropy and high order statistics. This project aims at mathematical analysis of MEE criteria and approximation analysis of some learning schemes dealing with multivariate data. We consider the consistency of an MEE algorithm for regression, and study error entropy consistency and regression consistency in detail. For iterative regularization dealing with multivariate data, we consider supervised learning with convex loss functions and propose a new form of iterative regularization and early stopping based on the subgradient method without constraint or penalization. Within the last few years, there has been considerable work on learning with pairwise loss functions in the batch setting. Due to the scalability to big data, we consider online learning algorithms with pairwise loss functions in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces with or without regularization, and carry our error analysis of these learning algorithms for dealing with some multivariate quantile regression and ranking problems. We also study estimations in a high dimensional additive model and establish minimax optimal rates of convergence under an assumption of approximate sparsity.
