104512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
104512.value: The recently discovered spin-Seebeck effect provides an easy way to generate a current of pure spins, without the simultaneous transfer of electric charge. This is a fundamental leap forward towards the final goal of spintronics, which is the elimination of the heat generated in traditional electronics. More generally, this discovery has triggered the emergence of a new field, called spin-caloritronics, which aims to study and exploit the interplay between heat flow and spin current. The spin-Seebeck effect could extend the frontiers of spintronics to a different field of applications: energy harvesting and conversion. The traditional Seebeck effect is commonly used to convert heat flow into electricity. Its converse effect, the Peltier effect, is used for solid-state refrigeration. The application of these so-called thermoelectric effects is limited to niche market where reliability and durability are more important than cost and performance. This is because the conversion efficiency is low and getting better performance is costly. The goal of this project is twofold. On one hand, it aims to contribute to a deeper understanding of the fundamental physics behind the spin-thermoelectric effects. On the other hand, it aims to explore the potential of specifically designed devices based on these effects for practical applications. 最近發現的自旋塞貝克效應提供了一種簡單的方法來產生電流的純自旋，沒有電荷的同時傳輸。這是一個根本性的飛躍向前邁進，這是消除產生的熱量在傳統的電子的自旋電子學的最終目標。 更普遍的是，這一發現引發了一個新的領域出現，被稱為自旋熱電子，其目的是研究和開發之間的相互作用，熱流量和自旋電流。自旋塞貝克效應的自旋電子學的前沿延伸到不同的應用領域：能量採集與轉換。 通常是使用傳統的塞貝克效應轉換成電能的熱流量。它的逆效應，珀爾帖效應，用於固態製冷。這些所謂的熱電效應的應用是有限的利基市場是更重要的成本和性能，可靠性和耐久性。這是因為轉換效率是低的，並獲得更好的性能是昂貴的。 這個項目的目標是雙重的。一方面，它的目的是促進更深入地了解背後的旋轉熱電效應的基本物理。在另一方面，它的目的是探索專門設計的設備，基於這些效果，實際應用中的電位。

104512.label: Realisation of objectives
104512.value: We studied the generation of pure-spin currents in magnetic films, which is at the basis of the spin-Seebeck effect. Therefore objective 1 has been fully achieved. Despite the effort made by the scientific community to achieve high conversion efficiency, the devices still have conversion efficiency that are low relative to conventional thermoelectric modules. Yet, the devices based on spin-Seebeck effect can be deposited as bilayers on glass surfaces or other amorphous surfaces for energy harvesting. Therefore, in this respect, objective 2 is achieved. We investigated a large number of ferromagnetic oxides for energy conversion, ranging from dilute magnetic semiconductor oxides to zinc oxide-graphene oxide nano-composites. The significant number of scientific papers we published on these materials makes objective 3 fully achieved. In order to characterize the devices, a new setup was assembled in our laboratory that can be used for the characterisation of spin thermo-electric modules. This setup allows the application of a gradient of temperature transverse to the sample. The temperature is monitored by thermocouples for the measurement of the gradient of temperature, as well as the local absolute temperatures. The sample is wire-bonded to a chip for detection of the induced voltage. This setup can still be used for future experiments. In the first part of the project we studied transverse spin-Seebeck effect. In these modules, the gradient of temperature is applied longitudinal to the sample and the induce thermo-spin current is converted into a voltage through inverse spin-Hall effect by depositing platinum strips. While this project was running, a so-called longitudinal spin-Seebeck effect was discovered. In this configuration, a metal with large spin-orbit coupling is deposited on a ferromagnetic layer and a gradient of temperature is applied across the bilayer. A thick copper layer is usually deposited under the ferromagnetic layer to work as heat sink. A gradient of temperature can be applied by using an halogen lamp. In this configuration, an additional effect was accidentally found that was not predicted. If the ferromagnetic layer is an oxide, a photo-spin voltaic conversion takes place, with the generation of longitudinal additional voltage. As discussed later, this effect has great potential for further development. The study of spin-current in ferromagnetic oxides has inevitably led us to deposit and characterize magnetic semiconductors. During this phase, new effects have been discovered that have been published in top-tier journals. In particular, we discovered that magnetism in zinc oxide is an effective way to narrow the band-gap. The work was published in Applied Physics Letters and has been listed as a top downloaded paper for two consecutive years. Similarly, the electrical and optical characterisation of the samples have led to the discovery of a giant negative magnetoresistance and tunable surface Raman scattering. Both discoveries were published in a Nature Publishing journal.

104512.label: Major findings and research outcome
104512.value: Spin-Seebeck effect could be measured in either standard transverse configuration, in which two strips of platinum are deposited on a ferromagnetic layer with the gradient of temperature applied longitudinal, or in longitudinal configuration, in which the gradient of temperature is applied across the bilayer and the voltage is detected longitudinal to the sample. In the latter case, an additional signal was detected, which is due to photo-spin voltaic conversion. A great effort has been made to engineer new ferromagnetic oxides to increase conversion efficiency. The magneto-electric and magneto-optical characterisation of these materials has led to new discoveries. We list the three most important here. We discovered that magnetism is an effective tool to engineer the band gap of oxide semiconductors. The work was listed as a top downloaded paper for two consecutive years in Applied Physics Letters. We have discovered a giant negative magnetoresistance in manganese-doped zinc oxide. The work has been published in Nature Scientific Report. If manganese-doped zinc oxide is nanostructured and capped with gold, surface Raman scattering can be enhanced by applying an external magnetic field. The work has also been published in Nature Scientific Reports.

104512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
104512.value: While studying longitudinal spin-Seebeck effect, scientists in Colorado realised that an additional spin-voltage could be detected that was not due to a gradient of temperature. If a metal with large spin-orbit coupling is deposited on a magnetic insulator, spin-polarised carriers at the interface can be optically excited and move in the opposite direction, according to their spin, because of inverse spin-Hall effect. The effect was named photo-spin voltaic effect. We could easily reproduce their results in our laboratory by using the setup assembled for this proposal. A new proposal on photo-spin voltaic effect has been submitted to the same funding agency, which is now under consideration.

104512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
104512.value: New phenomena related to generation and propagation of pure-spin currents are being studied around the world. A pure spin-current carries information without transferring charge, therefore with minimum dissipation. In recent years, a number of ways have been found to generate a pure spin-current. One is thermal. We have studied the generation of a pure spin-current through the application of a gradient of temperature. Another way, accidentally discovered in Colorado while this project was ongoing, is by using light. We have reproduced these results in Hong Kong to lay the basis for a further project. In both cases, in order to target applications, a pure spin current can be converted in a voltage by using inverse spin-Hall effect. This leads to new devices for thermo-electric and photo-electric conversion.

104712.label: Project Title(Chinese)
104712.value: 氣候變化和城市化對香港極端降雨事件影響的模式研究

104712.label: Project Objectives
104712.value: To set up a very high resolution numerical model capable for capturing the urban impact on the climate conditions of the Pearl River Delta region, and in particular for Hong Kong; To study the urban effects on extreme rainfall in Hong Kong in a simulated environment; and To project the future rainfall characteristic over the Pearl River Delta and in Hong Kong, with the impacts of both global climate change and urban development incorporated.

To study the urban effects on extreme rainfall in Hong Kong in a simulated environment; and
To project the future rainfall characteristic over the Pearl River Delta and in Hong Kong, with the impacts of both global climate change and urban development incorporated.

104712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
104712.value: According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change Fourth Assessment Report, the surface air temperature over East Asia is projected to rise by 3oC or more by the end of the 21st centaury. The same report also indicates more frequent or more intensified extreme rainfall events in the Asian monsoon region under global warming, mainly due to the increased moisture in the atmosphere. Changes of the water cycle and weather patterns might lead to more natural disasters and even post threats to health and security. Recently studies using more advanced models have shown that rainfall associated with intense typhoons or hurricanes also tend to increase in an environment with more greenhouse gases. In Hong Kong, extreme short-term rainfall events have been observed to become stronger and stronger since the 1850s. Torrential rain can cause disastrous landslides in the territory’s hilly terrain, causing economic and human losses. Hong Kong and its neighboring region have also experienced rapid urbanization in the last centaury. Scientists have long recognized that the urban environment can enhance precipitation, due to changes in the physical properties of land, the urban heat island effect and perhaps aerosols in the atmosphere which modify rain formation. Thus both global warming and urbanization can contribute towards the increasingly intense precipitation over urban areas. Some recent studies have provided observational evidence that rainfall intensity tends to increase with an even faster pace in urbanized locales. However, there is still no conclusion as to how important the urban effects are in determining extreme rainfall characteristics, in comparison with the change of the background climate. Here we propose to use a high-resolution numerical model to study the urban impacts on rainfall, and to project the future rainfall characteristics based on the up-coming round of IPCC results. In Part 1 of the study, a 1-km resolution regional model capable of resolving clouds and the underlying terrain will be adopted, in order to study the urban impacts on rainfall over Hong Kong. The observed current climate state will be use to “drive” the regional model. In Part 2, coarse-scale IPCC projections will be downscaled using the same model, so as to obtain local-scale simulations for the future climate state. Our results will lead to better understanding of the urban rainfall impacts on Hong Kong. Attributions of extreme precipitation changes in the future to urbanization as well as to the background climate change will also be made. IPCC第四次評估報告預測, 在全球變暖背景下極端降雨事件將會加劇。事實上, 香港的極端降雨量自19世紀50年代以來亦有明顯的上升趨勢。與此同時, 香港及其鄰近地區也經歷了快速的城市化發展, 而熱島效應和大氣中的氣溶膠改變等城市化效應亦能改變降雨特徵。然而, 城市化的影響對極端降雨相對於氣候變化有多重要，在目前還沒有結論。在這研究項目中, 我們將使用高分辨率的數值模式模擬在全球變暖背景下未來香港的氣候及降雨特徵, 並研究城市化效應對此降雨改變的影響。

104712.label: Realisation of objectives
104712.value: After the completion of this project, we have fully achieved objective #1 by setting up a high resolution mesoscale atmospheric model (with horizontal resolution up to 1km x 1km) for simulating extreme precipitation events over Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta (PRD) region, using the meso-scale atmospheric model WRF coupled with an urban canopy model (UCM). Parameters value used in the UCM is based on values suitable to the highly urbanized PRD region, with reference to those found in literature and reports from various HKSAR departments (such as Building Department). This model setting has been verified to be able to simulate extreme precipitation events that happened in this region. For objective #2, the model setup was subsequently used to study how anthropogenic heat (AH), as well as the size of the (PRD) megacity may affect the local precipitation amplitude over urban and non-urban locales in the area. It was found that probability of extreme rainfall occurrence can be rather sensitive to the AH value over the whole PRD region. Also, such AH effect on the local precipitation extremes over urban area depends on the size of the city. These results were presented in international conferences and published in 2 peer reviewed journal papers. Thus, while not all aspects of urban influences on rainfall were examined, we have nonetheless achieved objective #2 by identifying AH and the size of the megacity as two important parameters to which heavy rain rates can be sensitive. For objective #3, we first studied the impacts of global warming on extreme rainfall in South China/PRD based on coarse-resolution GCM simulations. Indeed, heavy precipitation tends to be intensified in the future with a warmer background climate, consistent with other studies. These GCM outputs were then dynamically downscaled, using the same WRF-UCM setup, in order to explore the dual impacts of urbanization and global warming on extreme rainfall in PRD. It was found that the urban heating effect, at least based on downscaled heavy rainfall cases found in the GFDL-ESM2M simulations, can be as strong as that due to global warming (according to the RCP8.5 scenario). This is a new result and has been presented in international conferences. This also has significant implications for future climate projections over highly urbanized areas. Overall, we have demonstrated that urban effects cannot be ignored and have to be incorporated, in order to project well future rainfall characteristics over the PRD megacity.

104712.label: Major findings and research outcome
104712.value: First, by conducting simulations of a past record-breaking rainfall event with a high-resolution WRF coupled with an urban canopy model, we found that rainfall rates and the spatial distribution of accumulated rainfall can be very sensitive to imposed urban surface heat fluxes. Heavy precipitation rates show a higher sensitivity than lighter rates, meaning that the extreme tail of the distribution is more affected (see Holst et al., 2016). Using the same high-resolution model, it was also shown such urban effects depend on the geographical extent of urban development. Thus only mega cities of sufficient size can expect to experience such effects. Less urbanized or smaller cities are much less prone to these effects. In other words, as cities grow, their effects upon precipitation appear to grow as well (see Holst et al., 2017). Such urban heating impacts on extreme rainfall was further compared with that due to global warming. Heavy rain episodes affecting South China from the GFDL-ESM2M simulations for the present and future (RCP8.5) climate were dynamically downscaled using the above high-resolution model, in two parallel experiments with and without anthropogenic heating in the PRD megacity. It was found that, with heating present, near-surface air temperature can rise substantially in the city area. This in turn leads to an increase of the mean as well as the extreme rain rates by ~10-15% in the urban domain. The latter is comparable to the impact of global warming alone on heavy rainfall, according to the RCP8.5 scenario. Our results highlight the importance of incorporating urban physics when carrying our future climate projections for megacities based on dynamical downscaling (see Fung et al. 2017, abstract to AGU Annual Meeting 2017).

104712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
104712.value: During the course of this project, we have also investigated the sensitivity of precipitation characteristics of the regional climate model from ICTP (RegCM4) to different combination of model physics (see Li et al., 2015). This model is relatively inexpensive to run and can serve as an intermediate step for dynamically downscaling AOGCM outputs to very high resolutions. More tests will be carried out to explore its feasibility. Also, regarding the future projection for extreme rainfall, only one AOGCM (namely the GFDL-ESM2M) was used. More AOGCMs can be downscaled, so as to obtain more robust results for future protections. This will also be carried out in the near future.

104712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
104712.value: Hong Kong and the PRD region are prone to severe rain storms, which sometimes bring huge economic and human losses to society. It is now well accepted that global warming can lead to more extreme rain rates over many locations in the world. At the same time, urbanization can also intensify precipitation over some city areas. This work examines the importance of urban effect on determining extreme rainfall, and compare the latter with the influence of global warming over the PRD area. This can be achieved by using a very high resolution numerical model that incorporates urban physics. By simulating heavy rain cases in the historical record, it was demonstrated that urban heating can greatly enhance the probability or intensity of heavy rainfall over the urban area. High-resolution future climate projections for the PRD area were also carried out, using the same model. It was found that the impact of urban heating on extreme rain rates can be as important as that due to global warming. The urbanisation factor, therefore, needs to be taken into account when considering precipitation characteristics over the PRD megacity in the future climate.

104812.label: Project Title(Chinese)
104812.value: 光催化剂/功能化石墨烯复合材料：提高电荷传输、反应活性和选择性

104812.label: Project Objectives
104812.value: To develop a universal strategy for the designing of novel functionalized graphene-photocatalyst composites, which are capable of enhanced charge transfer, reactivity and selectivity. This includes the molecular functionalization of the rGO-photocatalyst interface for efficient charge transport, as well as engineering specific reactive sites on the graphene structure. To advance fundamental understanding on charge transport characteristics of the functionalized rGO-photocatalyst composites at various interfacial levels, in relevance to the band structures of the photocatalytic materials as well as the resulting mechanisms of photocatalytic reactions. To demonstrate the applicability of the functionalized rGO-photocatalyst composites for various classes of photocatalytic reactions, namely the oxidation of organic pollutants, remediation of heavy metals and photoelectrochemical water splitting.

This includes the molecular functionalization of the rGO-photocatalyst interface for efficient charge transport, as well as engineering specific reactive sites on the graphene structure.

To advance fundamental understanding on charge transport characteristics of the functionalized rGO-photocatalyst composites at various interfacial levels, in relevance to the band structures of the photocatalytic materials as well as the resulting mechanisms of photocatalytic reactions.

104812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
104812.value: 近几年来，石墨烯复合材料在异相光催化领域取得了突破性进展，已有报道指出，将还原的氧化石墨烯（rGO）和具有光催化活性的材料结合起来，能够使其光催化活性提高一个数量级，这主要归因于rGO和光催化剂界面处的电荷转移速率的提高，反过来其又增强了整个体系的电荷分离效率。考虑到该体系的研究尚处于起步阶段，许多问题仍有待探索，rGO-光催化剂复合材料的全部潜能，尤其是对于复杂体系来说，更需要深入的研究。 在一个一般的和新颖的概念范围内，我们首次提出功能化的rGO-光催化剂复合材料的设计理念，旨在提高界面电荷传输能力以及在rGO上建造活性位点。第一条准则是指利用不同的化学连接器和配位策略将rGO和催化剂通过化学作用结合在一起。连接器为光生电荷的界面转移提供了有利的桥接路径。这一策略的应用对于当前的rGO-光催化剂体系来说是一种改进，因为在当前的体系中，rGO 和催化剂的接触主要是通过物理的范德华力，或者很少部分地是通过石墨烯边缘的羧基相互结合来实现的。第二条准则是指将“延伸的反应位点”嫁接在石墨烯上来进行选择性的有目的性光反应，这些“反应位点”包括具有晶面选择性的金属颗粒或是有捕获能力的分子。通过设计这样具有特定的反应位点的rGO，那么光催化过程中的氧化和还原反应位点就可能被分隔开来，使得电子和空穴的传输路径的交叉最小化，借此可以提高整个体系的量子效率。 该研究工作将开展大量的经过仔细挑选的光催化反应（代表不同的反应类型），包括一系列的有机化合物的氧化反应和重金属离子的修复，对于不同的功能化的rGO-光催化剂所发生的特定的反应机理给予一个全面的综合的评价。另外需要考察的则是光催化剂的敏化作用，即把量子点和rGO结合在一起。敏化剂-rGO-光催化剂复合材料将通过光电化学分解水来评估其性能。 该研究计划的成功将引领新一代的光催化剂，即不仅仅具有高的量子效率，同时也具有反应的选择性和可调性。具体到该研究计划，第一个这样的原型将针对废水的修复补救和氢气的制取。该研究计划所提出的策略具有普适性，它可以非常灵活地应用于其他的光催化反应中，例如，二氧化碳的还原。通过该研究工作所建立的基本原理也将同样适用于其他领域，例如太阳能电池和生物传感器等。

104812.label: Realisation of objectives
104812.value: All the objectives as laid out in the proposal have been fully met. Under objective 1: We have established a number of strategies for the design and synthesis of functionalized rGO-photocatalyst composites. Most prominently, we introduced the universal procedures for the one-pot solvothermal synthesis of rGO-based tricomponent composites, and the facile spatial decoration of cocatalysts on the specific sites on rGO-photocatalyst composites. In other words, these procedures can be universally applied to the synthesis of a variety of composites beyond those demonstrated through this proposal. We further developed the molecular functionalization of rGO to enhance its selectivity in capturing and reducing heavy metal ions. These procedures were developed based on the interfacial engineering of the photocatalytic composites to enhance the interfacial charge separation and transport. Under objective 2: We have characterized the interfacial charge transport properties of the composites using (photo)electrochemical and transient spectroscopic techniques. These fundamental characterizations were the basis for the rational design of high performance composites reported under Objective 1. In particular, we were able to design efficient ohmic contacts at the photocatalyst-rGO interfaces that resulted in the fast interfacial charge transport. This allowed shuttling photoelectron transport between two different photocatalysts with different band structures. Furthermore, we also characterized the cocatalytic surface charge transfer from the functionalized rGO to the targeted molecules. Overall, we have been resolved some of the most important charge transport components of the functionalized rGO-photocatalyst composites, which later formed the basis for high performance photocatalysts targeting various reactions (Objective 3). Under objective 3: Building on Objectives 1 and 2, we have achieved a number of breakthroughs in the in the applications of functionalized rGO-photocatalyst composites in the targeted reactions. By establishing the fast interfacial charge transport at the rGO-photocatalyst interface, and subsequently adopting the spatial decoration of cocatalysts on the rGO-photocatalyst composites, we improved the efficiencies in the photocatalytic oxidation of a range of organic pollutant classes by up to 4-fold relative to the Schottky-barrier type photocatalysts (previously most active class of photocatalysts). We also reported the high selectivity photocatalysts towards heavy metal remediations, and in the process discovered a new mechanism of hexavalent chromium reduction. We also developed the highly efficient rGO-based tricomponent composites for the photoelectrochemical water splitting. In fact, by carefully engineering the interfaces between the rGO transporter and the sensitizer as well as that with the acceptor, we achieved the relatively rare Z-scheme excitation that resulted not only in high photocurrent (as a result of efficient charge separation) but also high electron potential for the efficient reduction of water to hydrogen.

104812.label: Major findings and research outcome
104812.value: Throughout the project, we have developed a number of techniques to enhance the efficiencies and selectivities of functionalized rGO composite photocatalysts. They include the one-pot solvothermal synthesis of rGO-based tricomponent photocatalysts (Journal of Physical Chemistry, 2013) strategies of spatial decoration of cocatalysts on rGO-based photocatalysts (Journal of Catalysis, 2015), and molecular functionalization of rGO surface for selective and enhanced capturing of metal ions (RSC Advances, 2014). These are core techniques or methodologies that can be easily extended to a wide range of composites beyond the specific ones reported in this proposal. Importantly, these techniques were developed based on the rational approach of fundamentally manipulating interfacial charge transport between the photocatalysts and the functionalized rGO. Prior to us developing the strategies for spatial decoration of cocatalysts, the highest efficiency photocatalysts were based on the conventional Schottky-barrier type charge separation, e.g., at the metal-photocatalyst interface. At the same time the metal deposits also act as the cocatalyst for surface electron transfer, and the amount required are often different. By capitalizing on this and the electron conductivity of rGO, we reported the spatial decoration strategy for the first time, where metals are deposited on the photocatalysts to establish the Schottky barrier while cocatalysts for charge transfer are independently optimized on the rGO surface (connected to the photocatalysts). As a result, we improved the photocatalytic activity by a remarkable 4-fold compared to the previously most active Schottky-barrier based photocatalyst in oxidizing a wide range of organic pollutants. The work was published in the Journal of Catalysis (2015) and received overwhelming response among top photocatalysis experts at the IPS-21 conference (2016). The same type of spatially-decorated photocatalysts were found to be equally efficient in oxidizing heavy metals such as Pb2+, but is less efficient in the photoreduction of heavy metals such as Cr6+, Cu2+ and Hg2+ due to the electrostatic repulsion with the rGO surface. To overcome this problem, we chemically modified the GO with cross linkers to complex with the heavy metals and attain high selectivity in capturing these heavy metals for further reduction (RSC Advances, 2014). In the process, we also identified new mechanisms of Cr6+ reduction (Applied Catalysis B: Environmental, 2016). We identified the presence of various types of defects, both intrinsic and extrinsic, as the main obstacle in yielding highly active photocatalysts for water splitting (Materials, 2013, and ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 2014). Although the photocharges do not necessarily recombine at the defects, they are trapped and hence cannot be harvested. To overcome this limitation, we carried out careful interfacial engineering by introducing rGO as efficient electron transporter to harvest the surface trapped electrons between the CdS sensitizer and the TiO2 acceptor. This was carried out using the one-pot solvothermal synthesis, where we also elucidated the chemistry of synthesis. The charge transport within the new rGO-mediated interface was so efficient that a Z-scheme excitation was achieved. As a result, solar-to-hydrogen of ~3% efficiency was achieved – one of the highest reported to date on such system. The results were reported in the APL Materials (2014) and The Journal of Physical of Chemistry C (2013). Based on the collection of work described above, a critical review paper was published in the Chemistry of Materials (2016), which was the No. 2 Most Read in the Journal in the first 3 months of its publication. Overall, the project also contributed to the graduation of 3 PhD and 2 Masters students.

104812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
104812.value: The new approaches developed in this project for the synthesis of highly active rGO-based photocatalysts pave the way for their wider energy and environmental applications. Besides environmental remediation as demonstrated in this project (with potentials for targeting emerging micropollutants), the spatially decoration strategy can be easily adapted to construct the most efficient Schottky barrier and independently deposit a wide range of cocatalyst on the rGO for the targeted reactions without direct interactions between the two. For examples, metallic Cu cocatalyst can be used for CO2 reduction, Ni(OH)x and MoSx for water reduction, and Co3O4 for oxygen reduction reactions. These are otherwise not suitable for establishing efficient Schottky barrier. Here, the spatial decoration technique ensures the most efficient Schottky barrier and cocatalytic charge transfer, thereby assuring the highest activity possible in any photocatalysts. Likewise, the one-pot solvothermal synthesis ensures photocatalysts with the most efficient interfaces for charge transport between two different photocatalysts via rGO bridging. Besides maximizing the quantum efficiencies of a wide range of photocatalysts combinations, the resultant Z-scheme electron transport enables the applications of highly reductive reactions such as the highly demanding CO2 reduction reactions. In our lab, we are currently pursuing advanced photocatalysts in these two directions. Given the wide combination of photocatalytic materials possible using our new syntheses, we are pursuing the combinatorial chemistry approach for targeting the abovementioned applications.

104812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
104812.value: The project is concerned with the development of functionalized graphene-based photocatalyst composites for the remediation of environmental pollutants and photoelectrochemical water splitting. Here, the graphene is applied in a number of creative ways to manipulate the charge transport characteristics of the composite photocatalysts. By applying the various fundamentally-driven methodologies that were developed in this project, we have developed environmental photocatalysts that perform 4 times higher activity than the conventional Schottky-barrier based design, which was known to exhibit the highest photocatalytic activity. These advanced photocatalysts were efficient in the oxidation of organic pollutants and selective reduction of heavy metals present in wastewater. Similarly, we have also designed the high performance graphene-based semiconductor electrode for the photoelectrochemical water splitting. The tricomponent photoelectrode (consisting of graphene and two types of semiconductor materials) demonstrate ~3% solar-to-hydrogen efficiency, which is one of the highest reported for such materials. All in all, the fundamental understanding as well as the general methodologies developed in this project by interfacing functionalized graphene with semiconductor materials help to elevate the level activities and selectivities in photocatalysis. This is a step closer towards realizing a sustainable solar-induced chemical processes.

110012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
110012.value: 一個結構的模態屬性是其物理屬性（剛度，質量，拓撲）和動態響應的連接體。他們主要包括固有頻率，阻尼比和振形。基於測得的振動數據來識別這些模態屬性是一個在振動控制，結構健康檢測，或者損傷識別中經常實施的重要任務。由於在實施過程中的經濟性，用環境激勵振動數據來做模態識別已經在理論發展和工業應用兩個方面引起了越來越多的注意。在足尺實地試驗中，很多要求獲得一個結構的詳細的振形但是傳感器的數目受到限制的情況存在。一個常用的方法是通過多次試驗來完成，每個試驗覆蓋這個結構的一個不同的部分，同時在不同試驗中有一些共同的自由度作為參照。一些傳統的方法已經存在，這些方法可以把在單次試驗中識別的振形組合起來去形成一個可以覆蓋所有測量自由度的全局振形。然而，他們不能闡述識別的振形的質量從而這些結果可能被一些低質量的試驗損壞。正如在最近的研究中所展現出來的，這可能導致一些在組合的振形中有問題但是在實際的實地設置中很難去判斷的特徵。這個項目計劃提出一個新的貝葉斯頻域方法來去進行模態識別，該方法符合概率的邏輯並能結合在不同的試驗中測得的所有數據。這個方法允許通過考慮在不同的試驗中的數據的質量來決定全局振形。其允許用戶在頻域範圍內只利用在選擇的共振帶寬內的信息從而合理的避免了在別的不相關或者沒有被模擬的的頻段內的模型誤差。此外，對於最大可能值， 通過數據提供的信息，這個方法也可以決定與模態屬性相關的不確定性，其在現代模態識別中日益重要。為了允許應用於實際， 一種可以決定最大可能值和他們的後驗不確定性的快速計算方法將會被開發。在理論研發的同時，通過利用來自從模擬的數值模型，實驗模型以及足尺的實地結構得到的數據，廣泛的實施和驗證工作也將被提出。

110012.label: Realisation of objectives
110012.value: The project is of great success. All objectives were completed, and the Bayesian modal identification method developed in this project (objectives 1 to 3) has been well received by the researchers in the field. A total of eight SCI journal papers together with over ten conference papers were published with the support of this project. The PI of this project was invited to give three session keynotes for sharing research findings in this project. The developed modal identification method calculates the modal parameters, such as the natural frequencies, damping ratios and mode shapes, of the target structure utilizing ambient vibration data from multiple setups (Objective 1). The use of ambient vibration data (no external force is needed) makes the method very suitable for applications on existing structures, such as buildings and buildings, without affecting the normal operation of the structures. With the ability of using data from multiple setups, a high resolution mode shapes can be obtained even the number of sensors is limited. One outstanding feature of the developed method is the capability in calculating the posterior uncertainty associated with the identified modal parameters without calculating the sample variance. The calculated posterior uncertainty provides information on the reliability of the measurement and so as the identified modal parameters. Another outstanding feature of the developed method when compared to similar methods is the required computational power and time. The fast computational algorithm was developed for identifying the most probable values of modal parameters (Objective 2) together with the corresponding posterior uncertainty (Objective 3) for well-separated modes. It must be pointed out that the developed method is suitable for on-site application, for which, the modal parameters together with the uncertainties can be calculated in almost a real time manner. A series of MATLAB codes was developed for the implementation of the developed modal identification method. The calculation can be carried out by a notebook computer (suitable for field test) instead of a very powerful desktop computer. This is very helpful for the measurement team to make on-site decisions (e.g., re-test some selected measurement points or consider to increase/decrease measurement points depending on site situation). The developed Bayesian modal identification method was first carefully verified through numerical case studies and experimental measurements under laboratory conditions (including the scaled transmission tower of 2.5 m height and the 4-story shear building model of 2 m height). Fine tuning of the method was carried out based on the verification results. To ensure the practical value of the developed method, a series of field tests were carried out for collecting ambient vibration data of existing structures for the verification of the proposed method (Objective 4). The tested structures include the pedestrian bridge at the main entrance of City University of Hong Kong (CityU), the coupled long-span slab system of a recreation center at Tin Shui Wai, 36 m long (6 m span) footbridge in Hong Kong, and a 14-story reinforced concrete factory building in Hong Kong. Modal identification is an important step for many existing or developing structural health monitoring (SHM) methods. The modal identification method developed in this project is valuable to the field of SHM. This can be reflected form some of the published SCI journal papers of this project (e.g., Lam, Peng & Au 2014a; Lam, Yang & Au 2015).

110012.label: Major findings and research outcome
110012.value: A new Bayesian modal identification method was developed in the project. The method calculates the modal parameters, such as natural frequencies, damping ratios and mode shapes, based on ambient vibration data from multiple setups. The method considers not only the most probable values of modal parameters but also the associated posterior uncertainty. With the fast computational algorithm (implemented using MATLAB code), the developed method can be used for on-site estimation of modal parameters, which is very important and useful for the measurement team. A total of eight SCI journal papers were published with the support of this project. The details of the developed method were published in three SCI journal papers (Zhang et al. 2015; Ni et al. 2015; Zhang, Au & Lam 2015). Both numerical and experimental verifications were considered in these three papers. The application of the proposed method in a pedestrian bridge was published in (Ni, Zhang & Lam 2015). The application of the proposed method in model updating of a coupled long-span slab system is published in (Lam, Peng & Au 2014a). With a more robust MCMC-based model updating method, the results were published in another SCI journal paper (Lam, Yang & Au 2015). The verification of the proposed method together with the MCMC-based model updating method using a scaled transmission tower model was published in (Yang, Lam & Hu 2015). Apart from buildings and bridges, the proposed method was also applied on vertical axis wind turbine (VAWT) for studying the structural dynamics and aerodynamics behavior of the system. The findings were published in (Lam & Peng 2016). Furthermore, over ten conference papers were published in this project. Among them three are session keynote papers. The PI of this project was invited to share the findings in this projects in three conferences (Lam et al. 2013; Lam, Peng & Au 2014b; Lam et al. 2016) as session keynotes.

110012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
110012.value: The method was mainly developed for well-separated modes. One possible extension of the method is to consider the situation of closely spaced modes. Another possible extension of the method developed in this project is to consider the cases of forced vibration, in which, external forces must be applied onto the target structure to increase the signal-to-noise ratio. It is believed that forced vibration test can result in more reliable modal parameters. However, it is not easy for the property owners to allow researchers to apply forces onto the structure to induce vibration at detectable level. The PI of this project is now developing a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) based modal identification method, which is applicable in ambient, free and forced vibration tests. Apart from extension within the modal identification area, it is possible extend the scope to model updating or structural health monitoring. With the recent collapse of roof and building in Hong Kong, structural damage detection and structural health monitoring will get more and more attentions to ensure the safety of publics. The PI is planning to submit a proposal in this area for the continuous monitoring of the structural safety of long-span structures.

110012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
110012.value: The project developed a new modal identification method, which calculate the natural frequencies, damping ratios and mode shapes of the target structure based on ambient vibration data from multiple setup without applying any artificial forces onto the structure. As no external applied force is needed, the method will not affect the normal operation of structures (e.g., buildings or bridges). Furthermore, the method is applicable with data from multiple setups. High resolution mode shapes can be obtained with a limited number of sensors. In the verification field tests, only six sensors were used to measure the mode shapes of buildings (e.g., the 14-story factory building) and bridges (e.g., the 36 m footbridge). The fast algorithm developed in the project ensure the developed method can be used on-site in an also real time manner. When compared to most existing modal identification methods, the newly developed method can calculate the posterior uncertainty of the identified modal parameters. This is extremely useful for engineers in ensuring the reliability of the measurement results.

110712.label: Project Objectives
110712.value: To investigate the global behavior of the nonlinear dynamics of semiconductor lasers under grating-assisted feedback. Detailed numerical simulation based on the rate-equation model is to be conducted as the grating parameters vary. Experimental verification will be performed through fabricating fiber gratings of different bandwidths. To analyze chaotic time-delay signature suppression by grating-assisted feedback. As compared to the chaotic states generated from conventional feedback with mirrors, distributed feedback with gratings leads to suppression of the time-delay signature in the autocorrelation curve. Minimization of the time-delay signature will be sought through optimizing the grating bandwidth, reflectivity, and chirp. To demonstrate narrow-linewidth photonic microwave generation using a dual-grating configuration. By keeping the round-trip times of the external cavities incommensurate, linewidth narrowing with high side-mode suppression ratio is feasible. Tunability can be realized by introducing a continuous-wave optical injection. Extension to the terahertz frequency range is possible through appending a photonic crystal fiber for nonlinear wave mixing.

110712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
110712.value: Fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) have attracted much attention for introducing optical feedback into semiconductor lasers in various applications. Optical feedbacks from FBGs have long been adopted for mode selection in high-power multimode semiconductor lasers. Recently, new developments on such grating-assisted feedback were achieved on single-mode lasers. The laser output is stabilized as the grating defines external cavity modes. It is also known that single-mode lasers under grating-assisted feedback exhibit different low-frequency fluctuations. However, more complicated high-speed dynamics such as periodic oscillation, quasi-periodicity, and chaos have not been investigated thoroughly. In this proposed work, we intend to investigate these high-speed nonlinear dynamics of single-mode semiconductor lasers subject to feedback from fiber gratings. The dynamical states will be mapped for the first time as a function of the feedback parameters when a number of the grating parameters vary. Our preliminary numerical simulations show a strong dependence of the dynamics on the grating bandwidth. Experiments enabled by the laboratory facilities for fabricating different gratings will be conducted to verify the simulation results. Moreover, optical chaos obtained from the grating-assisted feedback will be examined for improvements over chaos in conventional feedback using mirrors. The conventional approach usually results in chaos with with a prominent autocorrelation peak that reveals the round-trip time-delay from the mirror. The time-delay signature undermines security in chaos communication. Grating-assisted feedback, on the contrary, can be regarded as a distributed feedback with no clear definition of the time-delay. Suppression of the time-delay signature will be investigated through simulation and experiments. Furthermore, the periodic oscillation states will be investigated for narrow-linewidth photonic microwave generation. A dual-grating configuration is considered for narrowing the linewidth of the oscillation state, while inclusion of optical injection and highly nonlinear photonic crystals will possibly lead to generating tunable continuous-wave signal in the terahertz range. The overall outcome of the proposed work is expected to add new degrees of freedom through incorporating fiber gratings to harness the nonlinear laser dynamics for the photonic microwave applications. 利用布拉格光纖光柵（FBG）為半導體激光器提供光反饋在多個應用領域引起了人們的興趣。長期以來，利用FBG引入的光反饋一直被用作大功率多模半導體激光器的模式選擇。最近，光柵輔助式光反饋在單模激光器上的應用有了新的發展。由於光柵定義了外腔模式，激光器可以有穩定的輸出。目前已經為人熟知的是光柵輔助式光反饋單模激光器會表現出不同的低頻波動。但是，更多復雜的高速動力學現象，例如周期振蕩、準周期以及混沌現象，仍然沒有被系統的認知。此項工作便是致力於研究這類基於光纖光柵光反饋單模半導體激光器的高速非線性動力學現象。通過改變光柵的參數，以反饋參數為變量的動態特性狀態圖將被首次提出。初步的數值仿真顯示了動力學特性與光柵帶寬有強相關性。我們實驗室已有制造光柵的設備使利用實驗來驗證仿真成為可能。此外，將光柵輔助式光反饋生成的光學混沌與常規的鏡面光反饋相比較，其優勢將會顯現出來。常規方式產生的混沌信號會在鏡面引入延遲的時間點上有一個突出的自相關峰值。這種延時特征將破壞混沌通信的安全性。相反，光柵輔助式光反饋等效於一種無明顯延時特征的分布式光反饋。此類延時特征的抑制現象將會以實驗和仿真的方式來驗證。此外，周期振蕩狀態將被用作窄線寬光子微波信號生成。雙光柵配置可以被用來進一步降低振蕩狀態的線寬，配合光注入和高非線性光子晶體，實現產生連續可調太赫茲信號成為可能。此項工作的主要目的在於通過光纖光柵引入新的自由度，將激光器的非線性動力學應用在光子微波的應用領域。

110712.label: Realisation of objectives
110712.value: The project explored on a new technique of invoking nonlinear dynamics of semiconductor lasers using grating-assisted optical feedback. While fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) have long been adopted for mode selection in multimode lasers, they were adopted in this project for realizing distributed feedback on single-mode lasers. Complex high-speed dynamics including periodic oscillation and broadband chaos were investigated thoroughly. The project added new degrees of freedom for harnessing the nonlinear laser dynamics in specialized photonic microwave applications such as high-speed tunable random bit generation and narrow-linewidth microwave signal generation. The objectives have been progressively achieved during the project. Objective 1 was concerned with the global behavior of the nonlinear dynamics of semiconductor lasers under grating-assisted feedback. The objective was completed by developing a numerical rate-equation model. It was based on modifying the well-established Lang-Kobayashi equations by incorporating the impulse response of the grating. The dynamical behavior was mapped in the parameter space of detuning frequency and feedback strength, where two wide regions of chaos were identified. Experimental results were in general in good agreement to the numerical results. Extensions to polarization-resolved chaotic emission intensities from a vertical cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) subject to FBG feedback were also developed. Objective 2 was concerned with suppressing the chaotic time delay signature (TDS). The TDS in a chaotic waveform is an undesirable feature detectable in the autocorrelation function. In place of mirror feedback, FBG feedback was demonstrated for the first time to suppress the undesirable TDS. With a positively detuned FBG, the chromatic dispersion associated with the edge of the grating reflection spectrum was found to effectively reduce the TDS. Experimentally, an optimized generation of the chaotic waveform was demonstrated with the TDS suppressed by over ten times to below 0.04, where application to tunable random bit generation was followed. Objective 3 was about the generation of narrow-linewidth microwave signals using a laser subject to dual-feedback. The photonic microwave generation was based on the period-one (P1) nonlinear dynamics in the experiments. By adding an optical feedback to the laser, the P1 microwave linewidth was found to reduce as the feedback strength and feedback delay increase, in which an inverse-square dependency was discovered by detailed numerical simulations. Signal generation of over 60 GHz was illustrated using the P1 oscillation that formed a basis for cascaded wave mixing to higher frequencies. Extensions were experimented by considering a recently proposed anti-colliding pulse mode-locking technique. Furthermore, square-wave generation was also attained by applying mutual feedback on semiconductor ring lasers to reduce the signal linewidth to the order of 1 kHz.

110712.label: Major findings and research outcome
110712.value: The research outcome contributed to 6 journal publications, 1 newsroom article, 2 invited conference papers, and 4 other conference or symposium papers. The project also contributed to training 2 Ph.D. students. Collaboration with the University of Glasgow was also fostered through the project. The major findings are summarized as follows. The project developed the model for the distributed feedback on single-mode lasers. The global dynamical mapping was revealed as consisting of regions of stability, quasi-periodicity, and chaos without asymmetry with respect to the detuning frequency. An extension to VCSELs was developed based on the spin-flip model. The maps formed the fundamental guideline on identifying the regions of operation for obtaining different nonlinear dynamical states for the proposed scheme of grating feedback. Details of the modeling and experiments on the dynamical regions were documented in journal publications [1, 5] and conference publication [5] in Part C. Then, since the TDS in a chaotic waveform is an undesirable feature detectable by self-correlation, the distributed reflections by the FBG were investigated for suppressing the TDS. Best TDS suppression was attained using a positively detuned FBG in utilizing the dispersion near an edge of the main lobe of the grating reflectivity spectrum. The TDS suppressed by over ten times to below 0.04 was demonstrated experimentally, which enabled high-speed random bit generation with an output rate tunable from 0.3 to 100 Gbps. Details of the modeling, experiments, and applications of TDS suppression were documented in journal publications [1, 3, 5] and conference publications [1, 3, 5-7] in Part C. Additionally, variations of feedback were investigated for generating microwave signals with narrowed linewidths. A semiconductor laser was studied comprehensively in the P1 dynamics for widely tunable microwave generation. The P1 microwave linewidth was first numerically examined using a Langevin term, where dual feedback was devised as an effective method to reduce the phase noise over a wide tuning range of the P1 frequency. Anti-colliding pulse mode-locking was also experimentally demonstrated through adjusting the intra-cavity feedback for microwave generation with reduced amplitude fluctuation and timing jitter. Another extension was on adopting mutual feedback on a semiconductor ring laser for square-wave switching, where the associated electrical linewidth was reduced. Details of the photonic microwave generation incorporating optical feedback using single-mode lasers, mode-locked lasers, and ring lasers were documented in journal publications [2, 4, 6] and conference publications [2, 4] in Part C.

110712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
110712.value: (maximum 200 words) The project developed the new scheme of grating-assisted feedback for invoking nonlinear dynamics in lasers. It would be interesting to continue with the research to address the following questions. 1. Can the modeling be generalized to other filtered feedback? Instead of evaluating the convolution independent of the differential rate equations, the generalized feedback can be viewed through an integro-differential formalism. Novel dynamical state can probably be unveiled by a properly designed filter. This is of importance to the understanding of the fundamental route to chaos in lasers. 2. Can the distributed feedback for chaos generation be integrated with the laser? Such an integration would be of practical importance as a hardware platform for tunable generation of random bits. Possibilities currently being pursued include the use of all-pass filters that can be implemented using passive ring waveguides. 3. Can the phase noise subject to feedback be explained theoretically? A theoretical explanation has remained a challenge due to the complication of the nonlinearities, but the cumulated amount of numerical and experimental data can now guide the development of such theoretical explanations. For instance, the simplified inverse-square dependency of the P1 phase noise is related to the Schawlow-Townes limit in lasers.

110712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
110712.value: Nonlinear dynamics in semiconductor lasers provides a special means to generate a variety of microwave waveforms for applications such as tunable microwave generation in wireless communication and truly random bit generation in secure communication. To obtain these dynamics, a laser has to be properly perturbed through a range of schemes. A new scheme is investigated in this project using feedback from an optical grating, which provides distributed reflections into the laser. The project has successfully developed a model for understanding the laser under grating feedback, obtained maps of different regions of operation, identified operating conditions for yielding broadband chaotic waveforms, and demonstrated improvements of chaotic waveforms by suppressing the undesirable TDS. The project also yielded narrow linewidth photonic microwave generation using dual feedback as well as mutual feedback. As an illustration of the potential of the laser dynamics under grating feedback, the undesirable TDS has been eliminated for improving the technology of random bit generation with a bit rate tunable up to 100 Gbps. In short, the gratings provided new degrees of freedom in the yielding nonlinear dynamical waveforms that can potentially lead to future applications in microwave generation, wireless communications, and secure communications.

110912.label: Project Objectives
110912.value: Consensus of sampled-data network configurations subject to data quantization. (i) Study the sampled-data effects on convergence performance of consensus of complex networks with general linear or nonlinear node dynamics, particularly when mobile agents do not share the same sampling period or the sampling period is not constant. (ii) Carry out the design of a proper sampling period associated with a control algorithm towards optimization of the closed-loop network, subject to a cost function such as maximum convergence rate or minimum total information exchange. (iii) Investigate the convergence time for various quantized consensus algorithms as well as the quantization effects on the convergence performance, especially for networks of general linear and nonlinear mobile systems. Distributed formation control of mobile multi-agent systems. (i) Study the formation tracking problem as well as the leaderless flocking problem, towards global inter-agent distance stabilization, collision avoidance, and initial structural pattern maintenance, and some possible combinations of them. (ii) Investigate adaptive formation control with respect to the events performed by the whole group of mobile agents, under some constraints such as input saturation, quantization and/or power limitation. (iii) Examine the robustness issue in applications involving noise and disturbances. (iv) Study the connectivity maintenance for consensus and formation control of discrete-time multi-agent systems. (v) Investigate the effects of time delays when they obey their own dynamics, and study coordination control subject to both time delays and other physical constraints simultaneously under a unified framework. (vi) Develop distributed coordination control algorithms for partially-actuated or underactuated systems such as nonholonomic mobile robots. Distributed estimation and control of mobile multi-agent systems. (i) Study joint estimation and control for distributed multi-agent coordination and formation, where neighbor-based information alone is not sufficient for controllers design. (ii) Investigate task-oriented coordination control systems for which distributed estimation is either necessary or appropriate as replacement of expensive centralized measurement devices. (iii) Study design and control subject to some physical limitations such as bounded inputs, asynchronous communications and/or signal quantization.

110912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
110912.value: This proposal aims to study distributed coordination control of mobile multi-agent systems over a complex communication network, targeting efficient methodologies and some engineering applications in such areas as communication-networked multi-vehicles (e.g., unmanned aerial, ground and underwater vehicles). This research direction has been very active in the systems engineering and control communities, however still with many important theoretical and technical problems outstanding for further studies today. Recent research in this filed can be categorized into several related directions including consensus, formation, estimation and control. The PI has been devoting great efforts to the basic research on these important subjects in the past decade, and is making a continued endeavor towards several important topics along the same line in this proposal. Specifically, this project will focus on three advanced topics, namely: (i) consensus of sampled-data network configurations subject to data quantization, (ii) distributed formation of flocking mobile systems, and (iii) distributed estimation and control of multi-agent dynamical systems. The approach to be taken and the techniques to be used are based on mathematical algebraic graph theory, automatic control theory, dynamical systems theory and distributed algorithms design methodologies, which are within the PI’s expertise. The completion of the proposed project is deemed to have significant contributions to the filed with deeper and better understanding of the fundamental theory of multi-agent dynamical systems and, in particular, to provide some more effective automatic group control techniques and distributed algorithms towards engineering applications. 本項目研究複雜通信網絡環境下移動多智能群體的分散式控制策略，包括（i）數據獲取和量化網絡結構下的移動多智能群體一致性問題；（ii）移動多智能群體隊形分佈的協同控制；（iii）多智能群體的分散式估計和控制。研究方法是基於數學代數圖論、自動控制理論、動力系統理論和分散式演算法設計。

110912.value: This research project investigated the consensus problem for sampled-data network configurations subject to data quantization. Distributed algorithms have been developed for achieving consensus and formation control for networked mobile agents to form a pre-designed geometrical configuration through local interactions, with or without a common reference.

110912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
110912.value: This research project investigated distributed coordination control of a group of autonomous mobile machines such as unmanned aerial, ground and underwater vehicles. The main objective is to have the whole group of vehicles working in a cooperative fashion under a distributed protocol embedded on their communication network. Here, coordination refers to a cooperative relationship among all agents in the group where information sharing plays a central role. This project takes a distributed approach, which does not require global information and centralized control, but utilizes locally available data and devices such as sensors, controllers, filters and actuators, to achieve desirable global cooperative performances with low operational costs, strong robustness, high adaptation, and flexible scalability. The project has developed some distributed control algorithms, which can successfully achieve the above-described objectives.

111012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
111012.value: Recent advances in broad fields of science and engineering brought forth new issues and challenges to the area of time-delay systems. Delays in communication networks and biological systems, for example, have been found to play a critical role in the system behavior and toward system performance. While understanding delay effects has risen to be ever more important and is gaining visible research attention, existing tools for analysis and design of time-delay systems fail to address the new issues, which are exemplified by difficulties imposed by random, time-varying, and multi-scaled delays. This project is intended to answer to these challenges and needs. Built on the PI’s research strength and success in the area, we seek to develop a small-gain analysis approach for systems subject to random, time-varying, and multi-scaled delays, which consist of initiatives in developing 1) small-gain input-output stability criteria, 2) modeling and approximation techniques for time-varying, random delays, 3) efficient stability tests and computational algorithms, and 4) potential applications to delay problems found in communiaction networks and biological systems. The project is believed to have the potential to impact theoretical and applied research in a broad range of scientific and engineering areas, including the fields of systems and control, communications, and biological systems studies. 近年來科學與工程的進展對時間滯後系統的研究提出了新的挑戰。例如，通訊網絡和生物系統中的時滯對系統的表現及性能有舉足輕重的影響。為此，對時滯影響的理解日益重要，其研究亦受到顯著的關注。然而現有的時滯系統分析和設計方法不足以應對諸如隨機、時變、多尺度這一類新的問題。本項目旨在對此類新問題和新的需要提出解決方法。基於在這個領域以往取得的成功和經驗，我們試圖發展針對於隨機、時變、多尺度時滯系統的小增益分析方法，其主要創新點包括：1）小增益輸入輸出穩定性判據，2）時變、隨機時滯的建模和近似方法，3）快速穩定性條件與算法，4）針對於通訊網絡及生物系統中時滯問題的應用。相信本研究對一系列理論與應用的科學和工程領域都有意義，尤其對於系統與控制、通訊和生物系統領域的研究。

111012.label: Realisation of objectives
111012.value: We believe that this project has been highly successful. All objectives (the revised Objective 1-Ocjective 3) are nearly entirely completed, resulting in five journal publications and one research monograph. Of the five journal papers, all are published or accepted for publication by the leading journals in the field of systems and control, of which Automatica and the IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control are the top 1 and top 2 journals. One full-length paper is published by the IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control. This outcome represents a high level of scholarship. Major results and findings are summarized in Section 6.1-Major Findings and Outcomes. The project has not only led to solutions to important problems in stability studies of time-delay systems, but also to the developments of new problem areas and solution techniques. In particular, the project has led to the PI’s investigation and successes into other related research areas, such as the stabilization and control of networked systems subject to delay effect, and the consensus attainment of multi-agent systems under delayed communications. In the due course, a high quality Ph.D. student, Dr. Jing Zhu, was produced, who co-authored all the papers reported herein. Additionally, based on Dr. Zhu’s Ph.D. thesis, we have completed a substantial manuscript for publication of a research monograph by Springer.

111012.label: Major findings and research outcome
111012.value: The primary objective of this project is to develop stability conditions for systems subject to time-varying and possibly random delays. Stability analysis of systems with time-varying delays proves to be a rather challenging problem. Employing operator-theoretic methods, we developed both L-2 and L-infinity small gain stability conditions, which are both conceptually appealing and computationally efficient, thus offering novel and enabling solutions. We have also attempted to apply and further develop these results for applications to networked control problems and multi-agent systems, which may operate under deterministic or stochastic communication uncertainties. These latter works have been or will be reported under related GRF grants support. The project has led to our investigation into the fundamental, longstanding delay margin problem, which addresses the robustness of feedback stabilization of systems with uncertain, time-varying delays. The problem asks such as questions as what is the largest range of delay such that there exists a single feedback controller that can stabilize all the systems subject to delays within that range? Using analytic function interpolation techniques, we derived fundamental bounds on the delay margin, within which the delay plant is guaranteed to be stabilizable by a certain linear time-invariant output feedback controller. More specifically, for single-input single-output systems with an arbitrary number of unstable poles and nonminimum phase zeros, we provide an explicit, computationally efficient bound on the delay margin, which requires computing only the largest real eigenvalue of a constant matrix. Second, for multi-input multi-output systems, we show that estimates on the variation ranges of multiple delays can be obtained by solving LMI problems, and further, by finding bounds on the radius of delay variations. Finally, we show that these bounds and estimates can be extended to systems subject to time-varying delays. When specialized to more specific cases, e.g., to plants with one unstable pole but possibly multiple nonminimum phase zeros, our results give rise to analytical expressions exhibiting explicit dependence of the bounds and estimates on the pole and zeros, thus demonstrating how fundamentally unstable poles and nonminimum phase zeros may limit the range of delays over which a system can be stabilized by a linear time-invariant controller.

111012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
111012.value: Time delays are ubiquitous in natural and engineered systems/networks and present significant challenges to scientists and engineers in a wide variety of fields. A current research focus on time-delay systems is the stability of systems subject to time-varying and possibly stochastic delays, and their application to networked control systems. This project sets out to develop small gain stability conditions for such systems, which have the advantages of being conceptually appealing and computationally efficient. In particular, small gain conditions are especially susceptible to solving the more challenging problems of feedback synthesis. In this spirit, we developed both L-2 and L-infinity small gain stability conditions, which are applicable to stability notions measured by signal energy and signal magnitude, respectively. The project has also led to the outgrowth to solving a fundamental stabilization problem, known as the delay margin problem for time-delays systems, which seeks to answer the question: What is the largest range of delay such that there exists a single feedback controller that can stabilize all the systems subject to delays within that range?

112212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
112212.value: 等離子體表面技術已經廣泛應用於微電子、冶金和生物等工程領域。 在等離子體浸沒式注入沉積過程（PIII&D）中，含能的等離子體處理會產生許多協同效應，如在傳統鍍膜的過程中實現了離子混合。 因此，這項技術在整形外科植入體等生物醫用產品上显得非常有用並且有望商業化。 然而，儘管該技術在近期也有所改善，但是傳統的PIII&D技術畢竟具有一些內在的局限性。 由於膨脹的等離子體鞘層無法準確地模仿樣品的外在形貌，所以離子流量在複雜形狀的試樣上并不均勻。 離子入射角將隨表面變化進而會導致離子注入深度和劑量在側向的不均勻性。 另外，高偏壓會导致等離子體消失，所以改性層通常很薄，這對於要經歷大量微動磨損和磨粒磨損的醫用植入體來說是遠遠不能满足要求的。 對於具有複雜表面且應用於複雜骨裂手術的骨固定器件等醫用植入體，就很有可能出現陰影區域，如果採用傳統的等離子體浸沒技術，他們接收不到足夠的等離子體來進行表面處理。 因此，這些缺點阻礙了PIII&D技術進一步廣泛應用於許多醫用器件。 本項目中，我們著眼于開發一種適合複雜形狀整形外科植入體的先進等離子體浸沒技術。醫用鎳鈦形狀記憶合金在整形外科應用領域比傳統的不銹鋼和鈦合金更為引人注目，所以我們選其為研究對象，並通過合適的表面改性來顯著提升他們的機械性能和生物學特性。 我們的策略是依據樣品幾何外形來設計出一個三維帶網格的金屬籠，進而遮擋樣品以調整等離子體鞘層的形狀。 通過這種方法，當高的負偏壓作用于樣品時，等離子體鞘層的擴張將會在接地的籠子處中斷。 網眼的共形性越好，越能實現均勻和保形的表面處理。 首先，我們利用網格法和流體模型從理論角度研究在等離子體密度，氣壓和樣品電壓等不同實驗參數下的等離子體鞘層動力學。 在對等離子體物理和等離子體/材料相互作用具有了較好的認識基礎後，我們再將優化的參數應用於骨固定器件實驗，從而驗證表面處理的有效性，並生產出具有較好的機械性能和抗菌性能的醫用植入體。 在這裏，除減少來自材料的有毒鎳的釋放外，額外的等離子體處理將用來改善表面抗菌性能進而減小術後感染和重複外科手術的可能性。 表面成分，硬度，腐蝕性能，阻擋性能和相關的生物學性能（包括細菌粘附和增殖等）等諸多表面特徵也將會被測定，其結果也將會重複使用來優化實驗方案。 通過和向我們提供商用骨固定器件的工業界同行們合作，我們也期望在項目完成後能夠獲得專利並能推進其商業化進程。 此外，從本申請專案中獲得的基礎性認識和開發的實驗方案也很容易延伸到其他類型的醫用植入體中。 總之，本申請的目的是開發一種新型的等離子體浸沒技術用以滿足目前整形外科界越來越迫切的實際要求。

112212.label: Realisation of objectives
112212.value: Plasma surface engineering has many applications in microelectronics, metallurgy, and biomedical engineering. In plasma immersion ion implantation and deposition (PIII&D), the energetic plasma treatment produces synergistic effects such as ion mixing as well as those inherent to conventional coating technologies. However, some intrinsic limitations such as ion fluence non-uniformity for specimens with a complex geometry because the expanding plasma sheath cannot accurately mimic the sample surface topography. With regard to biomedical implants with complex surfaces such as bone clamps and fixation devices used in the surgical treatment of multiple and complex bone fractures, there are likely shadowed areas that receive inadequate plasma treatment if conventional plasma immersion techniques are adopted. These drawbacks have thus hampered more widespread applications of PIII&D to many biomedical components. In this project, we have developed advanced plasma immersion technologies suitable for orthopedic implants with a complex shape. Our strategy is to modify the shape of the plasma sheath by enshrouding the specimens with a 3-dimensional cage and metallic mesh designed with a geometry similar to the sample. In this way, expansion of the plasma sheath is stopped by the grounded cage when negative high voltage pulses are applied to the sample and more uniform and conformal surface treatment can be conducted through the more conformal mesh. We have theoretically investigated the plasma sheath dynamics and conducted experiments using the optimized parameters on bone fixation devices to verify the process efficacy and produce biomedical implants with better mechanical and antimicrobial properties. In addition to mitigating the leaching of toxic substances from the materials, additional plasma treatment has been performed to improve the surface antibacterial properties in order to minimize post-surgical infection and repeated surgeries. The various surface characteristics including surface composition, hardness, corrosion resistance, barrier properties, as well as pertinent biological properties such as bacteria adhesion and proliferation have been determined. The fundamental understanding and experimental protocols gained and developed in this project can be easily extended to other types of biomedical implants.

112212.label: Major findings and research outcome
112212.value: We have designed a special sample holder for biomedical components with a complex geometry and performed a series of experiments to determine the optimal conditions for the plasma treatment of 3-D samples such as surgical bone fixation devices. The treated samples exhibit a golden appearance indicative of TiN on the surface. The golden color is also very uniform around the samples implying that the entire surface of the bone fixators have been uniformly treated with the plasma. Our subsequent analysis reveals insignificant leaching of toxic Ni ions from the treated materials and details about the technical improvements. Besides Ti and Ti alloys, the apparatus and experimental protocols described here are applicable to another metal, magnesium, which is naturally biodegradable and other materials such as diamond-like carbon and biopolymers. We have subsequently expanded our investigations to these very interesting and important materials and studied the effects of the plasma-based treatment on the wettability, hardness, morphology, microstructure, corrosion resistance, bacteria resistance, cyto-compatibility, and other pertinent properties of different types of biomaterials.

112212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112212.value: The fundamental understanding and experimental protocols developed from this project can be easily extended to other types of biomedical implants. We plan to work with our industrial partner which provided us with some of the commercial bone fixation implants used in this project for further development of the technology and commercial adoption in the future. We may also seek additional funding from the Hong Kong ITC to support the work.

112512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
112512.value: 在人類社會愈發注重生態保護的今天，智能電網技術的飛速發展正積極影響著電氣工業的改革，而這種趨勢正在從大型集中式電廠轉向應用了新能源和可再生能源的小型分佈式電源。最終將更加智能的分佈式電源控制和終端管理結合起來，從而提高電網的整體效率和可靠性。 無論分佈式發電單元的類型如何，可再生能源發出的電能最終都通過一個由多個功率變換器組成的功率調節系統進行處理。這些功率變換器通過一根直流母線相互連接，並由一組電容器進行穩壓，大多數情況下這個電容器組將決定著系統的體積和成本。電解電容由於具有容量大體積小的特點，成為電容器組的首選。然而，它有一個致命缺陷在於其使用壽命相對較短，尤其隨著溫度的上升將更為顯著。統計表明30%的電氣系統故障都由電解電容的失效引起，也因此電容往往成為制約系統可靠性的瓶頸。 對於高壓大功率變換系統，出於安全可靠性方面的考慮，母線電容需要進行定期檢查和更換，這會帶來十分可觀的維護成本和大量電子垃圾。為了提高電容可靠性和使用壽命，人們往往會用一些高性能的電容來替換電解電容，但這又不得不犧牲體積效率。 為了減小對於大容量母線電容的依賴，人們提出了許多減小母線電容容量的方法，但是這些方法通常是針對某一類電路結構。而且很多方法必須要犧牲電路某些方面的性能，或是在減小容量方面效果不明顯。 此項目著眼於應用全新的“有源式母線電容”技術將傳統的電容器組直接替換掉，旨在功率調節系統結構方面取得重大突破。初步研究結果表明這種技術能夠有效減小功率因數調節器的輸出電容，且不影響系統的整體性能。後續將系統闡述相關的理論使其能夠應用於不同類型的功率變換器，研究此技術對整個功率調節系統在穩態、動態和瞬態性能方面的影響，並進行成本效益分析。

112512.label: Realisation of objectives
112512.value: All objectives as planned in the proposal have been achieved successfully. Totally seven journal publications, one book chapter, three conference presentations, three patent applications, and one PhD thesis are generated. The achievements of each objective are described as follows: 1. Implement a digital controller for the basic unit of the “active DC capacitor” The basic module of the proposed “active DC capacitor” has been studied in [J1]. Its implementation on a grid-tie inverter with digital controlled is fully disclosed in [J5]. Moreover, the digital controller was integrated with a new control method which is presented in [J6] and [C3]. 2. Perform evaluation, circuit optimization and design of the basic unit It was found that the parasitic components would affect the performance of the inverter and active DC capacitor. Thus, a detailed analysis on the parasitic components on power electronic converters was done. The results are disseminated in [J2]. Later, a novel level shifter that can improve the switching pattern was proposed in [J3]. It can solve the problems of shoot through in the inverter and the compensator in the “Active DC Capacitor”. When the inverter is applied to control a motor, it was found that there is an overvoltage phenomenon under long-cable condition. Thus, the research team investigated the problem and came up with a solution, as discussed in [J4]. 3. Derive a generalized circuit structure and control method for the “active DC capacitor” allowing bidirectional power flow A generalized circuit structure of the “Active DC capacitor” was discussed in [J1], which describes the power flow and control method. The circuit structure of the series voltage compensator was further generalized for multiple units through a novel coupling technique. The structure is discussed in [J7]. 4. Investigate into a method of controlling the flow of the active and reactive power in the “active DC capacitor” to enhance the static, dynamic and transient performance of the entire power conditioning system Detailed analysis on the static, dynamic, and transient performance of the inverter with the proposed “Active DC capacitor” is given in [J5], [C1], and [C2]. A cost comparison is also given in [J1]. Later, a review on various techniques for reducing the DC link capacitor is given in [J8]. Note: [Jx] - x-th journal article listed in Part C. [Cx] - c-th conference article listed in Part C.

112512.label: Major findings and research outcome
112512.value: The proposed technology called “Active DC Capacitor” has been successfully developed. It has been applied to a grid-tie solar inverter for reducing the high-voltage DC-link capacitance. As the required energy storage of the DC link, formed by a reduced value of the DC-link capacitor and the series voltage compensator, is reduced, the architecture allows replacing popularly used electrolytic capacitors with alternatives of longer lifetime, such as power film capacitors, or extending the system lifetime even if there is a significant reduction in the capacitance of electrolytic capacitors due to aging. A 2kW, 220V, 50Hz prototype has been built and evaluated. The theoretical predictions have been compared favorably with experimental results. Finally, the implementation costs with electrolytic-capacitor and compensator for the DC link have also been compared. Detailed descriptions can be found in [J1], [J5], [C1], and [C2]. A literature review on various capacitance reduction techniques has also been done and reported in [J8]. With further extension of the usage of the concept of series voltage compensator, a modular and scalable voltage regulation structure for enhancing service continuity and flexibly changing the system power rating has been proposed. The methodology is based on paralleling multiple series-voltage compensators, namely multi-parallel-connected series-voltage compensator (MSVC), to regulate the load voltage. The output voltage of each compensator is controlled locally by adjusting the phase angle of the output voltage of the inverter in each compensator, while the output current of each compensator is coupled to two adjacent compensators via two coupling transformers. The coupling transformers form a daisy-chained structure. The operating principle, steady-state and transient current-sharing characteristics of the architecture have been discussed and illustrated. A 3-kVA MSVC test bed with three parallel-connected single-phase compensator units has been built and evaluated. Detailed description can be found in [J7]. When the research team was working on the design of the inverter, many technical problems on the control scheme, stability issues, and driving methods, appeared. Later, different control methods and driving techniques were derived. They are reported in [J2], [J3], [J6], and [C3]. Such investigations have generated a PhD thesis. Finally, when conducting the experiment on using an inverter to drive a motor load, the research team found that the cable length would affect the system performance. Thus, a new filter to suppress long cable effect was designed. The results have been reported in [J4]. Note: [Jx] - x-th journal article listed in Part C. [Cx] - c-th conference article listed in Part C.

112512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112512.value: The proposed “Active DC Capacitor” concept has been proven to be feasible for inverter and AC-DC power application. It can be extended to be implemented on an integrated circuit for low-power applications, such as LED drivers, battery chargers, etc. Then, the "Active DC capacitor" will become an integrated and standard module for general applications. Such proposal can help reduce electronic waste.

112512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112512.value: In today’s eco-conscious world, the trend is shifting from large centralized to small distributed power generation units utilizing new and renewable energies. Regardless of the type of the distributed power generation unit, the electricity generated by the renewable energy source is processed through a power conditioning system that contains multiple power converters. Those converters are interconnected through a DC link. The DC-link voltage is stabilized by a capacitor bank, which is sometimes the dominant part in terms of both volume and cost. Electrolytic capacitors are a popular choice for the capacitor bank, due to their high capacitances in a small form factor. However, their life expectancy is comparatively short and is reduced dramatically with elevated ambient temperatures. Statistics reveal that up to 30% of electronic system failures are caused by malfunctions of capacitors. Thus, capacitors are usually a reliability bottleneck. This project aims at making a breakthrough in the architecture of power conditioning systems by exploring a new technology named “active DC capacitor” as a direct substitute for the capacitor bank. It allows a significant reduction of the output capacitance in a power factor pre-regulator without performance degradation.
