In paper “On View Consistency in Multi-Server Distributed Virtual Environments,” we analytically classified basic user movements within a DVE in one time step into three types. Based on these three types of movements, the client-server delay, and the server-server delay, we could estimate the amount of view inconsistency over time. We proposed an optimization algorithm to minimize the view inconsistency as well as the server workload. This optimization algorithm has two main steps. The first step is a Knapsack-based partitioning algorithm to cluster all the cells in the VE into a number of partitions. The second step is then to assign each partition to an appropriate server in order to minimize both view inconsistency and server workload. 2. In paper “Dynamic Load Balancing in Distributed Virtual Environments using Heat Diffusion,” we explored two problems. One was to develop an efficient and simple load balancing algorithm, and we proposed the heat diffusion approach for load balancing. The other was to address the workload drifting problem in load balancing. 3. In paper “Robust Object Tracking via Locality Sensitive Histograms,” we proposed the locality sensitive histogram (LSH) for visual tracking. The LSH is a special histogram technique that can capture the image features extremely well. Based on the LSH, we proposed a robust tracking framework that could run in real-time even with hundreds of LSH regions. Our objective of this work in our project was to be able to track human from real scenes. 4. In paper “Leveraging Long-Term Predictions and Online-Learning in Agent-based Multiple Person Tracking,” we proposed a multiple person tracking method, by combining particle filters and an agent-based motion model called reciprocal velocity obstacles (RVO). Our objective of this work in our project was to be able to capture real crowd movements and then use them to better model user interactions in a DVE.

115112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115112.value: There are two directions of future works. First, we are following up on the tracking work, and currently trying to automatically differentiate individual crowds in a real scene and then analyze their interaction behaviors. We would like to develop algorithms for automatically classify crowd behaviors. Through identifying crowds and then capturing their behaviors, we could use these data to model user interactions in a DVE more accurately. This way, we can investigate the load balancing process in a more precise manner. We aim to develop an efficient and non-heuristic method to address the load balancing problem and the view inconsistency problem. Second, we are currently investigating another approach for the optimization algorithm. We are applying genetic algorithms to determine more optimized load balancing solutions, based on the estimated client-server latency, server-server latency, user movement behaviors, and network bandwidths. Our initial results suggest that genetic algorithms can generate more optimized solutions.

115112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115112.value: In this project, we have investigated the view inconsistency problem and how it is inter-related to the load balancing problem. We proposed an optimization method to optimize between view consistency and load balancing. We have evaluated our method in terms of computation time and the ability to avoid server overloading. We compared the proposed method with some popular methods. Our results show that the proposed method can effectively reduce view inconsistency while being efficient. We have also investigated the server workload drifting problem, and studied two approaches. One is for each server to redistribute the workload difference uniformly to its adjacent servers. The other is for each server to track the user movements across its adjacent servers, in order to more accurately redistribute the workload difference non-uniformly to its adjacent servers. Our results show that while the first approach is effectively, the second approach performs better, in the expense of a higher computational cost. In summary, we have addressed a difficult problem of reducing view inconsistency in multi-server DVEs. We have also addressed a novel problem of server workload drifting. As a future work, it would be interesting to find a way to simplify the overall load balancing algorithm

To design a generalized encoding framework to incorporate network coding into scheduling algorithms designed for data broadcast systems without jeopardizing the original performance criteria stipulated by the application requirements. 115312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
115312.value: With the popularity of powerful mobile devices such as smartphones, mobile users can now enjoy a wide range of information services such as content distribution and file download, which become key drivers of the mobile market. For instance, it is common to find people around to download and store information such as digital newspapers into their smartphones for online or offline reading. It is not hard to envisage a growing demand for efficient information dissemination provided by these data services in many advanced mobile and wireless applications. The strength of data broadcast for information dissemination is its ability to answer multiple queries for the same data in a single transmission through a shared communication channel. Recently, many effective data scheduling algorithms have been proposed in the literature, each excels in achieving its targeted application-specific performance objective. Thereafter, no significant breakthrough has been achieved because the performance is bounded by the fact that only clients requesting the same data can be served at a time by transmitting the requested data on the shared channel. In this research, we propose a generalized encoding framework with caching strategies to incorporate network coding into data broadcast systems. With network coding, clients requesting different data can be served simultaneously by mixing multiple data together. This not only significantly reduces bandwidth consumption, but also improves system performance. On the server side, the encoding framework integrates network coding with existing scheduling algorithms to exploit the synergy between data scheduling and network coding in order to maximize resource efficiency without jeopardizing the original performance criteria stipulated by the application requirements. On the client side, a network coding-cognizant caching strategy can improve data availability by increasing the chance for clients to decode data of interest. Therefore, requests can be served locally without sending explicit requests to the server via the slow communication channel. This improves the request response time and reduces workload at the server. More importantly, this saves bandwidth and the limited client resources. We speculate a non-incremental improvement in terms of both system performance and resource efficiency in data broadcast systems with our proposed encoding framework with caching strategies. By enabling efficient information dissemination, many emerging wireless and mobile applications can provide better quality of services guarantee to the ever-increasing number of sophisticated users, which is their key to success. 随着智能手机等功能强大移动设备的普及，移动用户如今可以获得丰富的信息服务，例如内容传输和文件下载，这已成为移动市场兴起的关键驱动。例如，人们常常需要使用智能手机下载并存储电子刊物等信息以便在线或离线阅读。不难预见，许多先进的移动和无线应用所提供的数据服务对高效信息传输的需求越来越高。数据广播在信息传输方面的优势是其能够在共享通讯信道通过单次数据传输来服务多个对于同一数据的请求。近年来，大量文献提出了有效的数据调度算法，它们在各自特定的应用中都有优异的性能。因为之前所有算法都基于一个假设，即只有请求相同数据的用户才能通过接收共享信道中传输的被请求数据而一次性获得服务，基于此限制，此后算法性能一直未有明显突破。在此，我们提出一个包含缓存策略的广义编码框架，将网络编码融入于数据广播系统中。通过网络编码，请求不同数据的用户可以通过多数据混合而同时得到服务。这不仅显著节约了带宽消耗，同时也提高了系统性能。在服务器端，编码框架通过集成网络编码和现有的调度算法，寻求数据调度和网络编码的协同，从而使资源效率最大化且不破坏原有应用需求所规定的性能标准。在客户端，网络编码 - 认知缓存策略可提高用户解码所需求的数据的机会，从而提高数据可获取性。因此，请求可以在客户端得到服务，而不用通过较慢的通讯信道专门发送请求到服务器。这样既改进了请求响应时间，也减少了服务器端的负载。更重要的是，这也节约了带宽和有限的用户资源。我们推测，通过提出的包含缓存策略的编码框架，数据广播的系统性能和资源效率都会有显著的改进。有了高效信息传输的支持，许多新兴的无线和移动应用可以为日益增长的高端用户提供更好的服务质量保证，这也是这些应用成功的关键。

115312.label: Realisation of objectives
115312.value: All the four project objectives have been fully achieved. Details of how each of them has been achieved are listed in order. 1. To formulate the coding problem in data broadcast environments, we have defined and constructed a graph to represent the relationship between mobile clients and their data requests. This graph is used to make encoding decisions at the server side to serve as many clients as possible in each broadcast and also to eliminate redundant encoding. The strength of coding-based broadcast is that an encoded packet can satisfy multiple requests for different data items simultaneously. We have proved that the coding problem of serving the maximum number of clients with each encoded packet can be transformed into the problem of finding the maximum clique in the graph. 2. Besides maximizing the number of requests which can be satisfied in a broadcast, we also need to consider the performance criteria stipulated by the application requirements. A generalized encoding framework has been designed to incorporate network coding into data scheduling algorithms without jeopardizing the original performance criteria. Basically, we have defined a weight function of attributes associated with each request and an optimized function in different applications. Using these two functions, we can incorporate attributes of individual requests into the aggregated weight of the optimal clique in the graph. Under the generalized encoding framework, scheduling algorithms can be migrated to their corresponding coding versions using one formulation with different inputs. 3. Based on the framework, we have proposed two novel broadcast algorithms at the server side to exploit the synergy between network coding and data scheduling. The first algorithm considers them in two separate phases and the second algorithm integrates them into a single step to fully exploit their combined strength. The experimental results showed that both algorithms considerably outperform existing algorithms over a wide range of settings. In particular, the second algorithm not only serves the maximum number of mobile clients in each broadcast but also significantly improves overall system performance in terms of request response time and broadcast bandwidth utilization. To make the algorithms practical and implementation-efficient, we have introduced two mechanisms to reduce the overheads and computation complexity of the algorithms. First, an efficient data structure and a pruning technique are used to reduce the search space. Second, the degree of a vertex in the graph, i.e., the upper bound of its maximum clique size, is used to skip computation, thereby saving processing time in searching for the most rewarding data item to be broadcast. 4. Based on the outcome of the first three objectives, we have proposed a novel cache management scheme on the client side which considers both access time and decoding contribution of data items in making cache replacement decisions for coding-based data broadcast systems. We have also designed a cache admission control policy that allows mobile clients to cache decodable and potentially useful data items by observing the global data access pattern from encoded packets broadcast by the server. The experimental results conclusively demonstrated that the proposed schemes can fully exploit the potential of network coding, thereby improving overall system performance.

Using these two functions, we can incorporate attributes of individual requests into the aggregated weight of the optimal clique in the graph. Based on the framework, we have proposed two novel broadcast algorithms for the server to exploit the synergy between network coding and data scheduling. The experimental results showed the algorithms not only serve the maximum number of mobile clients in each broadcast but also significantly improve overall system performance in terms of request response time and broadcast bandwidth utilization. Second, the degree of a vertex in the graph, i.e., the upper bound of its maximum clique size, is used to skip computation, thereby saving processing time in searching for the most rewarding data item to be broadcast. On the client side of coding-based data broadcast systems, we have proposed a novel cache management scheme which considers both access time and decoding contribution of data items in making cache replacement decisions [C.8.4]. 115312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115312.value: In this research, we have incorporated network coding into data broadcast systems. With the recent development of peer-to-peer (P2P) wireless communication technologies, a new information sharing paradigm appears. Mobile clients can not only retrieve information from the server, but also share information among neighboring clients (peers). However, it is still a challenging problem for mobile clients who are not peers to cooperate. Since network coding has the potential to exploit cached data items to serve multiple mobile clients simultaneously whether they are peers or not, it is possible for network coding to bridge the gap between non-neighboring mobile clients and further improve the system performance of cooperative caching.

115312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115312.value: Data broadcast has been increasingly used to disseminate information to large populations of mobile clients in many new mobile applications, such as location based services and intelligent transportation systems. In traditional on-demand broadcast, only requests for the same data item can be satisfied at a time. In this research, we incorporate network coding into on-demand data broadcast. The strength of coding-based data broadcast is that an encoded packet can satisfy multiple requests for different data items simultaneously. This not only utilizes communication bandwidth more efficiently, but also improves system performance. Next, a generalized encoding framework has been formulated to incorporate network coding into data scheduling algorithms without jeopardizing the original performance criteria stipulated by the application requirements. Based on this framework, we have proposed efficient broadcast algorithms at the server side to exploit the synergy between network coding and data scheduling. Last, we have proposed novel cache management schemes at the client side which consider decoding information in making cache replacement decisions and observe the global data access pattern in performing cache admission control. The proposed solutions can fully exploit the potential of network coding, thereby considerably improving overall system performance.

115612.label: Realisation of objectives
115612.value: [Objective 1] In the preparation stage, for each vertex, our approach first computes its visibility function. For each vertex, we first render two cubemaps: visibility cubemap and position cubemap. The visibility cubemap is a binary cubemap which can be obtained by rendering the 3D scene from the vertex’s point of view. During rendering, for each pixel in the visibility cubemap, we also store its position vector. The recorded position vectors are stored in another cubemap. We call it position cube map. With these two cubemaps, we can prepare the vectorization as follows. First, we locate all pixels at the boundaries of the occluded regions in the visibility cubemap by the flood-fill technique. Second, we retrieve the position vectors of the boundaries from the position cubemap. Last, these position vectors, namely control points, are put together to form some sequences. For each visible region, we obtain a sequence. For an easier manipulation, we concatenate the sequences of a visibility function into a single sequence. To reduce the data size and the computational load, we subsample the control points. In this way, the final sequence can be considered as a sparse representation of the original binary visibility function. For each vertex, we obtain a sequence of position vectors. For a general surface point, the visibility sequence can be approximated from the visibility sequences of its nearest vertices based on a geometric method. [Objective 3] After obtaining the visibility function, we perform the lighting evaluation based on the summed area table (SAT) technique. The lighting evaluation becomes a number of SAT lookups. Since the original SAT technique is suitable for handling the axis-aligned rectangles only, we develop a new SAT technique that can handle the integration over non-axis-aligned rectangles. We also generalize our technique to handle specular lighting component. To enrich the appearance of the objects, a number of texture mapping and color mapping techniques are considered. We have implemented a per-fragment GPU rendering engine. Given a triangular patch with three vertices and a surface point in this patch, we can obtain three visibility functions for this surface points based on the some geometric computation. To have a more reliable lighting evaluation at the surface point, we consider all the three versions and obtain three lighting evaluation values. The appearance of the surface point is a weighted sum of these three values. [Objective 2] For high quality rendering, the per-fragment GPU rendering engine can achieve an interactive frame rate. However, its rendering speed may not be fast enough for some real-time applications. The rendering speed can be improved by considering the per–vertex rendering. In some high frequency regions, such as the boundaries of some shadows, artifacts may occur. To improve the rendering speed and to maintain rendering quality, we consider the concepts of per-vertex rendering and the dynamic tessellation inside GPU. In our algorithm, we develop a method to evaluate the high frequency components in a triangular patch. We then subdivide the patch into a number of small triangular patches. For the newly generated vertices, their lighting values can be obtained based on the aforementioned method. [Objective 4] We have implemented two GPU engines. The implementation of rendering engines involved several techniques, including fragment shader, vertex shader, and geometry shader. Especially, the concept of geometry shader helps us to handle the newly generated vertices in the dynamic tessellation implementation.

115612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115612.value: In order to achieve the all frequency rendering based on the vectorized visibility, a number of basic techniques have been developed. Those techniques have a lot of applications in other areas. The developed SAT lighting evaluation technique has a lot of applications in other areas. For example, it can be used for texture mapping to reduce the artifacts. The developed data completion technique can be generalized to handle spherical data. In such extension, we may need to define some new tools to measure the rank of spherical data, The noise tolerant algorithms can be extended to handle a lot of problems in machine learning.

115612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115612.value: This project developed a new geometric based rendering algorithm for direct illumination. It can effectively and efficiently handle all-frequency lighting components, including shadow and highlight. We use a vector-graphics like representation for visibility functions. Hence lighting evaluation is based on a number of table-up operations. Our technique can preserve all frequency lighting effects even though the 3D objects are not tessellated densely. Our technique allows user to control the shininess of the object, the lighting environment, and the viewing angles in the real-time manner.

115712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
115712.value: Hydro turbines are generally considered a clean power producer. There have also been negative consequences, mostly associated with the dams normally required for power production. Dams are altering the natural ecology of rivers, potentially killing fish, stopping migrations, and disrupting peoples' livelihoods. A new design of hydro turbine based on a different working principle is needed. The proposed new turbine is capable of generating renewable energy in turbulent wind/water and suitable for use in densely populated cities. Due to the recommendation of previous reviewers, the proposal is restricted to water power only. The axis of rotation of the new turbine can be vertical or horizontal. The blades can be supported at multiple locations so that the structure is much stronger than most existing ones which allow for just one point of support at the hub. Therefore, the material requirement is less demanding and cost can be reduced. A small model, as shown in Figure 1, has been built to demonstrate the working principle. In brief, the model, as shown in Figure 2 and illustrated by the plan view in Figure 5, consists of four flat blades, each of which is fixed to one of the four planet gear wheels. Each planet gear wheel is connected to the central gear wheel (the sun wheel) via an intermediate wheel. The tooth numbers of the sun wheel, the intermediate wheel and the planet wheel are in such a ratio that when the sun wheel turns 180 degrees, each planet wheel turns only 90 degrees. Alternatively, the dummy wheel can be substituted by a bicycle or posi-chain (Figure 6) to eliminate noise. When properly aligned, each blade has the maximum exposed area along the flow in receiving the drag force but minimum exposed area moving against it when returning. The device can be completely submerged and works in cyclic flow induced by waves and tides. Research works towards the production of a prototype are described in detail in Part II of this application. The Hong Kong Housing Department has already shown interest in the proposed turbine and they have agreed to support the project by providing space for prototype testing. Yau Lee Construction Ltd has also agreed to provide laboratory space for manufacturing the prototypes. Negotiation is going on to implement a real one in Lamma Island. Some value added applications including water metering without wire and condition monitoring against leakage are investigated. 水輪發電機一般被認為是清潔能源。其也有不良後果，主要是與電力大水壩有關。水壩改變河流的自然生態，有可能殺死魚類，阻止候鳥遷移，擾亂人民的生計。從損壞的渦輪機部件飛濺出來的碎片是非常危險的。根據不同的工作原全新設計水輪機理是必要的。 新建議的水輪機是在水湍流或平流中可再生能源發電，適合在人口稠密的城市，如香港。跟隨上次的評論員的建議，本提案僅用於水利電力。這水輪機的旋轉軸線可以是垂直的或水平的。葉片可以支承在多個位置，使該結構是比大多數現有的只允許在一個點的支撐結構強得多。因此，對材料的要求是要求不高，可以降低成本。 如在圖1中所示，一個小的模型已被建立來證明的工作原理。簡單地說，在圖2中所示的模型，通過在圖5由四個平的葉片組成，每一個葉片被固定到一個行星齒輪。每個行星齒輪通過中間輪連接到中心齒輪（太陽輪）。太陽輪和行星輪的齒數目，是有這樣的比例，當太陽輪旋轉180度，每個行星輪轉動只有90度。另外，中間輪可以由一種自行車或位置鏈（圖6）所取代的，以消除噪聲。面向水流時，每個葉片具有最大的沿流暴露面積的拖曳力，但回車時，暴露面積最小，沒有拖曳阻力。該設備可以完全被海水淹沒，在循環流動引起的波浪和潮汐而發電。 在本申請的第II部分有朝向生產原型研究工程中有詳細描述。香港房屋署已表示有興趣支持該項目并提供空間原型測試。有利建築有限公司也同意提供實驗室空間製造原型。我們計劃在南丫島實現一個真實的水輪機。本項目的增值應用包括沒有電線和電源的監測防滲漏水計量研究。

115712.label: Realisation of objectives
115712.value: Objective #1 Literature review and Hydro- dynamics study on flat, curved and twisted blades At the beginning of the project, the research team conducted a comprehensive literature review on wind/hydro turbines to summarize what has been done in the past decades and identify the research gaps and point of start for this project. The research team used k-ε and Shear Stree Transport models for modelling the flow in our simulation study of Hyro-dynamics on three different blade types (flat, curved, and twisted). The simulation results indicate that flat blade should be used in our micro hydro-turbine design. Objective #2 Gear box and generator design; their Strength and stability Different design options, including gear, belt and chain types, as well as different types of available generators are thoroughly studied in the project for evaluating their output power efficiency. The strength, fracture and stability of rotating shafts had been studied. A miniatured testbed is built in the lab to simulate the physical environment in sewage pipe and water pipe. A scaled down model of the water turbine is assembled and evaluated in the testbed environment to validate the performance obtained from simulation. The scaled down model deployed in the testbed show that the turbine can generate electricity under turbulence flow of water. Objective #3 Energy generator and dynamos and Site installation Based on the validation in the testbed, a full scaled turbine is manufactured following the same design of the scaled down model and installed in the site. However, the field test was not successful. Improvements were made and implemented on the water turbine, resulting in an improved model. The 2nd full-size model was sent to Shek Wu Hui site of the Drainage Service Department of HKSAR and installed in the sewage channel with a size of 960 x 2200 mm in cross section (water level at 50%). The improved model can generate electricity when the sewage water went through the turbine. Objective #4 Water metering; Condition Monitoring of water and oil pipes The developed micro water turbine power generator with storage battery is paired in the digital water meter (DWM). By connecting our improved turbines to the DWM, our micro turbine can provide the necessary power supply to the DWM, and no additional external power supply is needed. Excessive energy was stored in the battery for releasing the energy for the DWM when the generated power is under the demand by DWM.

115712.label: Major findings and research outcome
115712.value: Based on the work carried out in the project, the following findings and outcomes are achieved: 1) Design of new turbine can generate renewable energy in turbulent water, through simulation and optimization; 2) The simulation results are validated in the scaled testbed environment; 3) A full scale turbines using our optimized design is manufactured and installed in a sewage channel. The developed turbine can supply the necessary energy required by the digital water meter, making it self-powered.

115712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115712.value: There is good potential of the study to be further developed and extended into the following areas: First, the turbine can be extended for tide/wind harvesting; Second, energy output prediction model development and validation, which might be useful if the turbines are connected to the grid in the future; Third, further improvement on design is towards the mass production of the new turbines.

115712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115712.value: The study aims at designing a new and effective turbine, which can work in turbulent water and is suitable for microgrid applications. Simulation, testbed study, and field test have been conducted in the study, resulting in an optimized turbine design. By optimizing the design of the blade supporting system, the demand of high strength materials was reduced, resulting in lower investment and maintenance cost. The improved design allows the turbine to work effectively when it is submerged fully under turbulent water. With the advantages of our new design, the turbine can be implemented in different locations (e.g., water supply pipe, sewage pipe/channel) in dense cities, providing clean energy for the citizens.

115912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
115912.value: Today, wireless communications have played an important role in both business and social activities. In wireless systems, antennas are very important because they directly affect signal transmissions and receptions. Recently, dielectric resonator (DR) antennas (DRAs) have been investigated extensively because of a number of advantages such as their small size, low loss, low cost, and ease of excitation. In mobile communications, a transmitted wireless signal will normally travel to the receiver along different paths, leading to different wave components at the receiver. As a result, received signals have amplitude and phase fluctuations, which is known as fading. Fading is an inevitable problem in mobile communications. A common technique to tackle it is to deploy diversity antenna systems. Diversity antenna systems can improve the channel performance and, thus, increase the quality of received signals. In this project, new polarization-diversity antennas will be designed using DRAs. Most of the polarization-diversity DRAs are excited in their broadside radiation modes, and only a couple of designs can provide omnidirectional field patterns. Those omnidirectional designs, however, make use of monopole-antenna modes instead of DR modes, causing inconvenience in matching the antennas. In this project, fundamental TM DR modes will be used to design omnidirectional polarization-diversity DRAs for the first time. Novel dual-polarized designs with omnidirectional/broadside and omnidirectional/ omnidirectional field patterns for their two ports will be given. Engineering formulas that determine DR dimensions for the new dual-polarized DRAs will be obtained. Since TM DR modes are used, matching can be achieved easily by simply varying the length of the excitation probe. All reported polarization-diversity DRAs have been limited to single-band designs. In this project, dual-band dual-polarized DRAs will be studied for the first time to meet the need of modern wireless systems. Also, since circularly polarized (CP) systems are extensively used in wireless communications, novel full-CP dual-polarized DRAs that have CP fields for both ports will be investigated. Thus far, only one three-port polarization-diversity DRA has been reported, and no attempt has even been made to investigate any four-port designs. In this project, both three- and four-port polarization-diversity DRAs will also be covered to provide more choices for engineers. Ansoft HFSS will be used to simulate the various polarization-diversity DRAs, and measurements will be carried out to verify the simulations. Design guidelines will be provided to facilitate designs of the polarization-diversity DRAs. 如今，無線通信在商務和社會活動中發揮著重要的作用。在無線系統中，天線是非常重要的部分，因爲它們可以直接影響信號的傳輸和接收。近年來，介質諧振器天線因爲小尺寸，低損耗，低成本，容易激勵等諸多優點而被廣泛研究。 在移動通信中，發送的無線信號通常會沿著不同的路徑傳播到接收端，這將導致在接收端出現不同的波分量。其結果是，接收到的信號出現振幅和相位的波動，這種現象被稱爲衰落。在移動通信中信號衰落是不可避免的，解決這個問題的一個常用技術是采用分集式天線系統。分集式天線系統可以提高信道的性能，從而增加接收信號的品質。在這個項目中，介質諧振器天線將被用來設計新的極化分集式天線。 目前，大多數的極化分集式介質諧振器天線工作在其寬邊輻射模式，可以提供全向場輻射的天線設計只有幾個。然而，這些全向的天線設計利用的是單極子天線模式，而非介質諧振器天線模式，這會給天線的匹配造成不便。在這個項目中，我們將首次利用介質諧振器的橫磁基模設計全向的極化分集式介質諧振器天線。我們將給出兩種新型的雙極化天線設計，一種是兩個端口的場輻射爲全向和寬邊輻射，另一種是兩個端口的場輻射均爲全向輻射。另外，我們將給出可以用于計算新的雙極化介質諧振器天線之尺寸的工程公式。由于使用了介質諧振器的橫磁模式，天線的匹配可以通過改變激勵探針的長度去實現，從而使設計變得簡單。 已報告的極化分集式介質諧振器天線只局限于單頻段的設計。在這個項目中，我們將首次對雙頻段雙極化介質諧振器天線進行研究，以滿足現代無線系統的需要。此外，由于圓極化系統亦被廣泛應用于無線通信，新型的雙圓極化介質諧振器天線也將納入我們的研究範圍。 迄今爲止，已報告的三端口極化分集式介質諧振器天線只有一個，並且沒有任何關于四端口極化分集式介質諧振器天線的設計。在這個項目中，三端口和四端口的的極化分集式介質諧振器天線的設計將被涵蓋，以提供給工程人員更多的選擇。 我們將利用Ansoft HFSS軟件仿真各種極化分集式介質諧振器天線，並且對其進行測量以驗證仿真的准確性。同時，我們將提供設計准則，以方便極化分集式介質諧振器天線的設計。

115912.label: Realisation of objectives
115912.value: The first objective has been achieved successfully. We made use of the covariance matrix adaptation evolutionary strategy (CMA-ES) to curve-fit the simulation data of the polarization-diversity cylindrical DRA. Engineering formulas for the radius and height of the cylindrical diversity DRA have been obtained successfully. The second objective has been achieved successfully by designing the dualband dual-polarized cylindrical DRA, which is simultaneously excited in its HEM111 and HEM113 modes. The single-band design can be obtained by consider either the HEM111- or HEM113-mode band. Ansoft HFSS was used to simulate the dual-polarized DRA. A prototype was fabricated to verify the simulations, and good agreement between the measured and simulated results was obtained. A wideband design by merging the HEM111 and HEM113 modes was also demonstrated. The third objective consists of two parts, namely the three- and four-port DRAs. The former has been achieved successfully by using a 2.4-GHz cylindrical DRA, with good agreement between the measured and simulated results. For the four-port part, a design with good diversity performance has been simulated using HFSS. A prototype was also fabricated. However, a significant discrepancy was found between the measured and simulated reflection coefficient. It is because the feedline design is complicated for a four-port design and the parasitic effects in the measurement can be strong. The true reason needs to be investigated and this part has not been completed. The last objective has been achieved successfully. It was demonstrated by using a compact circularly polarized (CP) cylindrical dual-polarized DRA. The design makes use of the omnidirectional TM01δ mode and broadside HEM12δ+1 mode of the DRA. The measured and simulated results are in good agreement. A second CP diversity DRA was also designed successfully. In this case, the DRA is excited in its TM01δ and TE011+δ modes. Omnidirectional CP fields are obtained for both ports, with, again, good agreement between the measured and simulated results.

115912.label: Major findings and research outcome
115912.value: Objective 1: To obtain engineering formulas for designs of polarization-diversity DRAs We have successfully obtained two engineering formulas to calculate the radius and height of the cylindrical diversity DRA, which is operated in its HEM12δ+1 and TM01δ modes. The frequencies of the HEM12δ+1 and TM01δ modes of the DRA were solved simultaneously, and the data was curve-fitted to obtain the formulas. The result has been used to design a three-port polarization-diversity DRA (Objective 3) and published in paper #3 (Part C, Section 8). Objective 2: To design single- and dual-band two-port dual-polarized DRAs The HEM111 and HEM113 modes of the cylindrical DRA were used to design the dualband dual-polarized cylindrical DRA successfully. It entirely covers the DCS (1.71–1.88 GHz) and WLAN (2.40–2.48 GHz) bands, with a very high port isolation of more than 36 dB across the two bands. A wideband dual-polarized design was also designed successfully by merging the HEM111 and HEM113 modes together, with bandwidths of over 30% for both ports. The wideband diversity DRA entirely covers the WLAN (2.4–2.48 GHz) and lower WiMAX bands (2.3–2.4 GHz, 2.496–2.69 GHz). This work has been published in the paper #1 (Part C, Section 8). Objective 3: To design three- and four-port polarization-diversity DRAs By using the formulas obtained from Objective #1, a three-port polarization-diversity cylindrical DRA was designed successfully at 2.4 GHz for WLAN applications. It makes use of the TM01δ mode and two degenerate HEM12δ+1 modes of the cylindrical DRA to obtain a three-port design. Good agreement between the measured and simulated results was obtained. The result has been published in paper #3 (Part C, Section 8). A four-port polarization-diversity DRA was also designed with good simulated results. However, the simulations deviates our measurements significantly and this part needs to be improved. Objective 4: To design circularly polarized dual-polarized DRAs A compact CP cylindrical dual-polarized DRA was investigated successfully. There are two CP modes. The first CP mode combines the TM01δ DRA mode and dipole mode, giving an omnidirectional CP radiation pattern. For the second CP mode, the HEM12δ+1 DRA mode has been excited by a balanced slot to give a broadside radiation pattern. The work has been published in paper #2 (Part C, Section 8). A second CP diversity DRA with CP omnidirectional patterns for both CP ports has also been done. The results have been summarized in paper #4 (Part C, Section 8), which is to be submitted.

115912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115912.value: In this project, the dual-band dual-polarized DRA has been investigated successfully. Since multi-band systems are increasingly popular in wireless communications, the dual-band design can be extended to the tri-band design to cope with the need of modern wireless systems. To do this, we need to handle three frequencies and therefore at least three degrees of freedom are needed in the design. This requirement can be met by using the rectangular DRA, which has three independent dimensions to provide the required degrees of freedom. Its TE111, TE113, and TE115 modes can be utilized in the design. The resonant frequencies of the three modes can be determined by using the dielectric waveguide model. A large number of data sets need to be generated by numerically solving the dielectric waveguide model. Using the covariance matrix adaptation evolutionary strategy (CMA-ES), the formulas of the three dimensions can be obtained in terms of three frequencies.

115912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115912.value: Over the last two decades, the dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) has been studied extensively because of its small size, low loss, low cost, and ease of excitation. To alleviate the multipath problem and improve the signal reception, diversity antennas have been widely used in modern wireless communication systems. In this project, the polarization-diversity DRA has been investigated successfully. Since this diversity technique does not need any additional antenna element, the design is compact and cost-effective. The cylindrical DRA has been used in this project. To facilitate the design, engineering formulas that determine the radius and height of the DRA have been obtained for the first time. Different polarization-diversity DRAs have been investigated in the project, including two-and multi-port designs, dual- and wide-band designs, and linear- and circular-polarized designs. In each design, an antenna prototype was fabricated and measured, and good agreement between measured and simulated results was observed. All of the designs have very good port isolation, which is an important index to assess the performance of a diversity antenna. It is hoped that the results would be generally useful for the design of diversity antennas.

116212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
116212.value: 许多工业过程，比如半导体封装中的芯片固化过程，都是分布式参数系统。由于复杂的时空耦合特性，对这类过程十分难于进行建模、设计和控制。另一方面，长期以来，无论是在学术界还是在工业界，控制和设计都被视为两个截然不同的领域。这种分割妨碍了工业的过程优化，对时空分布式过程提出了更艰巨的挑战。 本项目针对固化过程的分布式控制，在时空分离的框架下，提出了一个基于模型的优化设计方案。首先，在时空分离中将设计变量考虑进参数模型里；通过优化设计，使过程的主要动态特性更线性化，这样便于解耦控制的实现。通过线性额定模型，设计基于观测器的解耦机制，可以抑制过程和模型的误差以及所有外部扰动；这样在满足时空分离的前提下，将过程近似转变成一个等价线性系统，由此便于简洁控制的实现。最后通过调整额定模型和各控制回路的设定值，在整个空间域上近似实现固化控制的优化。

116212.label: Realisation of objectives
116212.value: The project has been successfully completed and achieved all the planned objectives. Objective 1 – Space/time separation based process design for cure control The cure process is a complex distributed parameter system (DPS) that is difficult to design and control due to the strong space-time coupled dynamics. Without the external control, the cure performance will fully rely on the oven design. A novel data based robust design approach is constructed to design a new type of the curing oven. Under the concept of space/time separation, the coupling influence between design variable and model parameter will be separated, which makes design relatively easier. Only the dynamics affected by design variable is considered, and the influence of parameter variation on the performance can be minimized in the design. The complex process will have a complex model that can be represented as a combination of nonlinear functions. This kind of model will be difficult to optimize due to the nonflat property or the large scale of computation for the sparse matrix. For the purpose of robust design and optimal control, we have conducted following work: • For the nonflat property caused by the combination of nonlinear functions, a least square regularized regression algorithm is proposed for the nonflat function approximation. This algorithm can approximate the multi-scale frequency component of the function with multi-scale kernels and improve modeling of the complex process. • For large scale of computation of the sparse matrix, computation reduction will be needed. An effective method is developed to project the linear parameters out of the problem, leaving the nonlinear least squares problems involving only the nonlinear parameters. This method not only reduces the optimization dimension but also increases optimization performance. • For the nonlinear process, the parameter optimization is not easy because of no available math-based optimization method. One possible solution is to use evolutionary computation methods, which are studied in this project for parameter optimization of the system. Objective 2 – Space/time separation based intelligent control of distributed parameter system Fuzzy control is one of good approaches to control the unknown process when the process model is not available. DPS can be classified into Parabolic and Hyperbolic type. Different intelligent control approaches are developed for the following DPS. For the Parabolic DPS: It can be transformed into finite-dimensional ordinary differential equations (ODEs) by using time/space separation, each ODE can be considered as a subsystem to be controlled by one traditional fuzzy logic controller (FLC). Based on the multi-models concept, DPS can be considered as a combination of multiple subsystems. A multivariable fuzzy control system is designed for DPS with only one set of membership function (MF) and one rule base used. Scaling gains are used to adjust for the dynamic difference, which can be optimized using the particle swarm optimization (PSO). For a time-varying process, SVR learning is applied to learn MF from the process data. A dynamic switching based fuzzy control strategy is developed for a better spatial performance. For the Hyperbolic DPS, modeling and control will be more difficult. The T–S fuzzy hyperbolic partial differential equation (PDE) model is proposed to accurately represent the nonlinear DPS. Then different kinds of fuzzy control, including the observer-based control design and a distributed fuzzy observer, are proposed for DPS control. The exponential stability of the closed-loop DPS system is studied. Different fuzzy control approaches are also studied for the DPS cascaded with ODE system that represents a multivariable dynamics. Objective 3 – Application to the IC cure oven The robust design method developed in objective 1 has been successfully applied to design the cure oven. The newly designed oven has a simpler structure and can have a more uniform spatial performance.

116212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
116212.value: The modeling technology developed from this project will be also applied to other field, like thermal management of battery system, which can be regarded a generalized thermal process with more disturbed dynamics. Deep learning technology can be integrated with the space/time separation method for a better spatiotemporal dynamic modeling. Reinforcement learning and evolutionary computation could also be helpful in parameter optimization of the control system.

116212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116212.value: Complex distributed parameter systems (DPS) widely exist in the production industry. These processes are usually described by nonlinear partial differential equations with complex boundary conditions. The outputs of these processes not only vary with time but also vary at different spatial locations. Typical examples include curing ovens in semiconductor packaging plants, where material moving, gas flow and thermal heating interact together to form a nonlinear distributed temperature environment. The production quality relies heavily on the spatial temperature distribution profile that will vary significantly between operating conditions. Good process design is a first step toward the satisfactory performance. So far, no design is for DPS due to its difficult space/time coupled nature. Various design approaches are studied in this project, resulting a new oven in simpler configuration. Control is the next step toward the better performance. Various intelligent control approaches are studied, with particular emphasis on fuzzy control. Data-based learning and evolutionary computation are also introduced for the parameter training. The research has produced novel results on system design and intelligent control of DPS. It is the first time to develop system design for DPS, and some of fuzzy control methods are also new for the DPS.

116312.label: Realisation of objectives
116312.value: 1. To overview and modify the existing daylight prediction models The PI has previously proposed a number of mathematical expressions for estimating daylight illuminance on heavily shaded building facades under various overcast and non-overcast skies. External obstructions affect daylight availability in two ways: obstruction of the sky patch and visual reflectance. The overview and modification of the daylight models is mainly on these two aspects. The amount of reflected light is dependent on how well these surrounding surface are illuminated and the reflectance of these surfaces. The established daylight models can handle sky component for various sky conditions including real and standard skies. Outdoor illuminance data particularly on vertical surfaces are crucial to architectural and daylighting schemes. There are great demands for the knowledge of daylight illuminance data on vertical surfaces for high-rise buildings with substantial glazed area. In 2003, the Hong Kong Government issued a practice note on lighting and ventilation requirements. Based on a performance-based approach, the note adopted the vertical daylight factor (VDF) to specify the daylighting performance of the building. The impact of daylight on the physical environment can be analyzed using lighting simulation packages. However, many architectural and engineering practices consider a full scale computer energy analysis too complicated, costly and time-consuming. Simple design methods in the forms of simple equations, charts and diagrams through comprehensive simulation studies are useful during the initial-design stage, when various design schemes and concepts are being considered and evaluated. It is envisaged that such convenient design tools can give architects and engineers certain basic and concise insights into the interdependency among various daylight parameters. Building professionals do make computer simulations after the design schemes have been finalized for submission and presentation. Manual calculations based on simple computer spread sheets would be more apposite for students to appreciate such daylighting designs. Consequently, mathematical expressions for the vertical sky component (VSC) under the 15 CIE Standard Skies were established to predict the vertical daylight illuminance on building facades and the results were assessed against those achieved by computer simulations. 2. To develop appropriate calculation approaches for estimating solar irradiance for obstructed buildings; Calculation approaches to compute solar radiation on obstructed fenestration for both overcast and non-overcast skies are required for the assessment of both active and passive building energy saving techniques including shading and building integrated photovoltaic systems in metropolitan environment. In subtropical Hong Kong, buildings are subjected to substantial cooling requirements throughout most of the year. Solar heat gain, particular via vertical windows, presents the major part of the cooling load. The estimation of solar heat gain is thus important in the cooling load estimation, air-conditioning system optimizations and energy-efficient building designs. Horizontal solar data from routine meteorological measurements are sufficient in studying solar heat gain through horizontal glazing such as skylight. There are greater demands for the knowledge of solar radiation on vertical surfaces particularly for high-rise curtain-walling buildings with large window areas. Daylight is the visual part of solar radiation and same approaches can also be applied for the estimation of radiation. Recently, the International Commission on Illumination (CIE) adopted a range of 15 standard sky distributions covering the whole probable spectrum of skies in the world. Sky conditions of the same category would have similar solar radiance and sky luminance distributions and the corresponding solar and daylight parameters would be within certain ranges. Such analyses can help the identification of sky patterns and complicated mathematical expressions to model the sky distributions are not required. Meteorological variables in terms of solar irradiance are more available than daylight data particularly those based on horizontal measurements. It would be more appropriate to establish the criteria for identifying the CIE Standard Skies using such climatic parameters. An approach to estimate the solar irradiance on obstructed building facades under the 15 CIE Standard sky conditions was proposed. 3. To establish solar irradiance and daylight illuminance databases for obstructed building façade designs and daylighting schemes Solar irradiance and daylight illuminance data on various sloped planes facing different orientations are crucial to the active solar energy applications and passive energy-efficient building designs. To receive maximum solar energy, solar panels are often installed on an unobstructed roof. In modern urban areas, however, high-rise buildings are compact and the limited roof area does not favor stand-alone PV systems. In such cases the concept of building integrated solar façade, which replace parts of vertical walls with solar panels, would be an appropriate alternative form of the system. It has been shown that in Hong Kong solar radiation through the fenestration is by far the most significant component of heat gain in OTTV equation. Regarding the natural light as the visible part of solar irradiance, it is an economical means of light source for a building. Strong recognition has been given to the contributions that the daylight-based lighting controls can make to energy conservation in buildings. Long-term data measurements should be the most effective and accurate approach of setting up the databases. In many parts of the world, however, the basic outdoor solar irradiance data for the planes of interest are not always readily available. In Hong Kong, only hourly horizontal global solar irradiance data have been systematically recorded by the local meteorological station as part of its routine work but there are no measurements of solar irradiance on any inclined planes. It is impractical to measure the long-term solar irradiance for every inclined plane to establish the required databases. However, each of the CIE Standard Sky represents a unique sky-diffuse distribution. Upon the classification of the standard skies, the solar irradiance and daylight illuminance data at any planes of interest can be computed. It means that a comprehensive solar irradiance and daylight illuminance database can then be established for building façade designs and daylighting schemes. 4. To examine the building energy and environment implications for various building design schemes Daylight entering through a window produces strong illuminance gradients, from high levels near the window to low levels at the back of the room. The rear part tends to look gloomy for a low uniformity value and supplementary electric lighting will be required. Glare from windows can rise from excessive contrast between the luminance of the visual sky and the luminance of the internal surfaces within the field of view. The most effective control tools would be the devices including curtains and venetian blinds monitored by facade sensor (open loop control). For daylight-linked lighting controls, the appropriate control methods and the number of switching operations required for lighting controls depend strongly on the daylight level available in the workplace concerned (closed loop controls). Further, it is important to estimate the interior daylight on all surfaces. Internal surface reflectance and the distance between the window and the point concerned are factors affecting the illuminance level. The lighting savings, solar factor/OTTV, building envelop cooling load, glare index and room uniformity, durations of sunlight and shadowing for rooms at different floor levels under overcast and non-overcast skies should be estimated. For active solar application systems, the output energy of opaque and semi-transparency BIPV systems can also be determined.

116312.label: Major findings and research outcome
116312.value: An overview of the existing daylight prediction models was made. The prediction approaches on vertical sky-diffuse components under various unobstructed and obstructed overcast and non-overcast sky conditions were examined. The vertical sky component (VSC) for the 15 unobstructed and obstructed CIE General Standard Skies were computed and established. The findings can be used to classify the CIE standard skies and determine the vertical daylight factor (VDF), average daylight factor (ADF) and vertical sky-illuminance data for various CIE sky conditions under obstructed and unobstructed environments. A paper [Journal paper 3] presenting the work on these issues has been published. In view of the fact that outdoor illuminance and solar irradiance have similar characteristics, the models developed for daylight illuminance can be employed in estimating solar irradiance. An approach using VSC and VCR for classifying CIE Standard Skies was developed. Based on the classified skies, the climatic indices using the horizontal solar radiation and daylight illuminance measurements were computed and analysed [Conference Paper 1]. An approach to estimate the solar irradiance under the obstructed 15 CIE Standard Sky conditions was proposed [Conference paper 4 and Journal paper 5]. Once the sky type has been identified, the inclined solar irradiance and daylight illuminance facing various orientations can be easily computed. Based on measured vertical and horizontal sky-diffuse components, they were identified as various CIE General Standard skies. The climatic indices determined from the solar irradiance and daylight illuminance data under these CIE skies were examined. Calculation procedures for solar irradiance on inclined planes including vertical surfaces facing various orientations from categorized CIE Standard Skies were developed [Conference paper 2, Journal paper 4]. Solar irradiance and daylight illuminance data are essential to solar energy applications such as solar electric and solar thermal, and the daylight linked lighting controls. The building energy and environment implications were conducted. The energy, financial and environmental aspects for solar thermal and solar electric installations were analysed. A paper entitled an analysis of potential applications of wide-scale solar energy in Hong Kong has been published [Journal paper 2]. Another study on the visual performance [Conference paper 5] and electric lighting energy use for an atrium building using high frequency switching [Conference paper 3] and dimming controls were conducted and presented [Journal paper 1].

116312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
116312.value: The prediction of the daylight illuminance for a given location in a building is the key step in daylighting designs. The usual method for computing natural illuminance is the daylight factor approach which is based on the traditional CIE overcast sky without direct sunlight. Initially, it has shown convincingly the effectiveness of daylight-linked controls in saving energy on electric lighting. Based on split-flux theory, average DF (ADF) which is directly related to window area and less detailed input data than those provided by the DF could be a useful daylighting criterion. Recently, vertical DF (VDF) representing light coming directly from sky and reflected daylight from surrounding buildings and ground which is quite appropriate for compacted urban areas with large external obstructions. However, DF approaches cannot take into account realistic and time-varying climatic conditions when the sun position varies. As the CIE adopted a list of 15 standard skies in 2003, it is necessary to determine the various forms of DF under these 15 CIE Standard Skies. The findings based on the research studies can be employed for such analyzes to formulate new designs and assessment benchmarks in terms of daylighting performance, energy conservation and visual comfort.

116312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116312.value: Solar radiation and outdoor illuminance are essential climatic parameters for solar energy system assessments, cooling load determinations and daylighting designs. There are great demands for obtaining solar radiation and daylight illuminance on a vertical surface. Hong Kong features many urban and suburban building projects that are squeezed into limited land areas. In this environment, it is common for the quantity of daylight and solar radiation falling on the facades and penetrating into building interiors to be substantially restricted by shading effects caused by the proximity of surrounding buildings. However, the solar radiation received by building integrated solar panels and solar heat through window glazing are often estimated under unobstructed skies and the required solar radiation and daylight illuminance data cannot be accurately obtained. Computer simulations that allow for solar radiation and daylight illuminance on obstructed vertical facades to be calculated under a variety of overcast and non-overcast conditions may be quite time demanding for a full-scale analysis. The project aims to provide an overview of daylight prediction models and modification of these models to assess solar radiation in heavily obstructed buildings. The findings would be useful to building professionals engaged in building facade studies, building energy calculations and daylighting investigations.

116912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
116912.value: 我们将基于光诱导介电泳（ODEP）力，开发出一套简单，廉价，灵活的自动化制造方法，用于制造三维铰链维结构的光敏生物聚合材料（如：PEGDA水凝胶）。传统的微光刻技术需要紫外光源和造价昂贵的掩膜板才能实现微结构的制造，与此不同的是，我们已经证实利用静态或动态的非紫外光作为虚拟电极产生光诱导介电泳力，便可以在特定区域制造三维的固化水凝胶微结构，并且制造出的水凝胶结构的厚度可以小到几个纳米，水平尺寸可以小到几个微米，另外该水凝胶微结构的厚度可以通过调节光诱导介电泳力的作用时间灵活控制。该项目的最终目标是开发出一套自动化和实时的ODEP平台，该平台连接着一个内嵌有ODEP芯片的微流控系统，平台可用于快速地制造三维聚合物结构。为了达到这个目标，我们必须探索这项先进制造技术相关的几个基本问题：1）理解电动力现象并对其进行准确建模，包括对聚合物结构形成过程中的电渗流力和电热力作用的分析；2）解释时间在利用ODEP制造聚合物微结构过程的作用机理，比如，ODEP力是如何在芯片表面作用并随着时间影响聚合物的最终形状；3）研究聚合物结构在ODEP力作用下的固化形成的动态化过程，比如，我们已经发现在特定的溶液浓度下，一个静态的光斑可持续地诱导微结构形成；4）研究并且优化诱导聚合过程的ODEP参数，用于更好地设计微流控系统，作为一个可实现聚合物微球和微结构的连续生产的“聚合物自动化生产工厂”。我将在该项目的资助下，通过大量实验和理论仿真去分析和解决这些基本问题。这个项目将取得以下成果：a）构建一台ODEP系统，可用于制造分辨率为~1m的微结构生物材料；b）一套微流控系统，用于和ODEP平台协调工作，在其微通道中实现微结构连续生产；c）一套软件算法，用于自动化检测微结构在微流控系统中的制造过程，并且实时控制将生产好的微结构运输到特定的储藏室。d）通过这个项目中的交叉验证试验和理论仿真数据，进一步地理解基于ODEP聚合物微结构的制造过程和机理。我们相信通过这个项目开发的这套新技术将给聚合物微结构制造领域带来全新的范例，这将在诸如组织工程，药物传输，光谱编码等领域有巨大的应用前景。

116912.label: Major findings and research outcome
116912.value: Our research team has produced the following research outcome through the funding of this project: 1) Developed an ODEP (optically-induced dielectrophoresis) Platform to enable the generation of micro bio-polymer structures with lateral resolution of 3 m and vertical resolution of ~100 nm; 2) Integrated a microfluidic system that synchronizes with the ODEP Platform and facilitates the continuous generation of micron-sized bio-polymer structures in its microchannels; 3) Collected experimental results and formulated an accurate model of the electrokinetics phenomena, including AC electro-osmosis and light-induced electrothermal forces, during the bio-polymer formation process under the ODEP force field; Our team’s major findings include: a) It is possible to rapidly fabricate 3D free-standing bio-polymer structures in a microfluidic system using localized electric field and ODEP force. The novelty of this concept is that the process requires no ultra-violet light source (hence eliminates the need for a “yellow room”) and no physical micro-lithographic masks; b) We have elucidated the time-dependent formation process of ODEP-fabricated polymer structures, i.e., we have determined how the ODEP force field evolves near the ODEP chip surface and affects the resulting structural shape of the polymer over time; c) Polymer-based microlenses could be fabricated rapidly using this new technology. These microlenses could be used to enhance the resolution/magnification of microscopes and endoscopes. d) This generalized ODEP+microfluidic system micro-fabrication process could be extended to fabricate non-polymer structures such as metal electrodes and carbon nanotube sensing elements. The above finds are (or will be published) in the following journals: - "New Approach in Quantifying Lateral Repulsive Optically-induced Dielectrophoretic Forces", PlosOne (submitted in July 2015; reviewers' comments received; manuscript under revision). - "Exploring Pulse-Voltage-Triggered Optically-Induced Electrohydrodynamic Instability for Femtolitre Droplet Generation", Applied Physics Letters, 104, 264103 (published in 2014). - "Extracellular-controlled breast cancer cell formation and growth using non-UV patterned hydrogels via optically-induced electrokinetics", Lab on A Chip, 2014, 14, 1367 (published in 2014). - “Rapid Fabrication of Nanomaterial Electrodes Using Digitally Controlled Electrokinetics”, IEEE Trans. on Nanotechnology, Vol. 13, no. 2, 2014 (published in 2014). - "Super-resolution endoscopy for real-time wide-field imaging", Optics Express Vol. 23, Issue 13, pp. 16803-16811 (published in 2015).

116912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
116912.value: Through this project, we have explored the frontier knowledge of optically-induced electrokinetics and bio-polymer fabrication processes, and developed a novel technology for rapid, precise, and relatively low-coat manufacturing of micro-scale bio-polymer structures. We believe that this advanced technology will have important applications in the fields of drug delivery, tissue engineering, and spectroscopic encoding eventually. We will continue to apply for research and development grants, and also seek collaborative/sponsoring industrial partners, in Hong Kong and China to further develop and apply this technology to the technical fields mentioned above.

116912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116912.value: Currently, not a single fabrication process for bio-polymers possesses all the desired qualities for micro-scale bio-polymer-structure production, i.e., high-resolution with high precision and repeatability, reconfigurability, low-cost, and rapid manufacturing. Through the funding of this project, we have developed a simple, rapid, inexpensive, and automated method for fabricating three-dimensional micro-/nano-scale bio-polymers controllably by applying optically-induced dielectrophoretic (ODEP) force in a microfluidic device. Instead of using traditional micro-photolithographic techniques, in which a bio-unfriendly ultra-violet light source and relatively expensive masks are required for patterning bio-polymers, we have demonstrated that optical patterns could be used to induce localized electric fields, and hence localized ODEP force, which could be controlled to induce 3D solid hydrogel formation in a microfluidic device. This novel technique has been demonstrated to produce hydrogel structures with thickness dimensions down to nanometer scale and lateral dimensions in the order micrometer scale. The thickness of these structures can be well-controlled via the exposure time of the hydrogel solution to the ODEP force. We believe that this new technology will provide an entirely new paradigm for micro/nano bio-polymer fabrication, and will garner interests of researchers from diverse fields, e.g., cell/DNA manipulation, molecular self-assembly, drug delivery, spectroscopic encoding, and tissue engineering.

117612.label: Project Objectives
117612.value: To determine, to what extent, the external stresses will induce atomic-scale relaxations and significant damages through systematically modulating the stress level and cyclic frequency. To characterize and elucidate the stress-induced relaxation and damage processes in atomic scales and then to correlate them with the mechanical properties of BMGs. In particular, emphasis will be placed on mechanistically understanding the fatigue mechanism of BMG materials under cyclic elastic stresses. The understanding of the stress-induced relaxations and damages will lead to the development of scientific principles used to design novel BMGs with superior fatigue resistance.

117612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
117612.value: Bulk metallic glasses (BMGs), a new class of metallic materials, have many attractive mechanical properties, such as extremely high strength and hardness, large elastic strain limit and high wear resistance, due to their complex disordered atomic structures. Such non-crystalline structures are thermodynamically metastable in nature, and they have a strong tendency for structural relaxation upon suffering from stress perturbations or temperature changes. Although encouraging progresses have been made in the study of temperature-induced structural relaxations in BMGs, the stress-induced structural relaxation process is rarely addressed. Also, an in-depth understanding of the damage mechanism induced by external stresses in BMGs remains a long-standing fundamental problem. As a result, this proposed research is aiming at elucidating the stress-induced relaxation and damage process in the atomic scale and then correlating them with the unique mechanical properties of BMGs. We intend to develop a scientific scheme to quantitatively correlate stress-induced atomic migrations/rearrangements with mechanical behaviors, especially fatigue properties, through a combination of theoretical calculations and the state-of-the-art experimental techniques. Based on the simulation and experimental outcome, the ultimate goal is to understand the stress-induced deformation and relaxation mechanisms of BMGs in the atomic scale. An BMG with a composition of Zr50Cu40Al10 (at.%) will be selected as the model material, cyclic deformations (tension and compression) of the BMG will be modeled utilizing classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with embedded atom method (EAM) potentials to describe the interatomic interactions. During the cyclic deformation, the corresponding atomic structure will be recorded simultaneously. Through a systematic variation of applied stresses and cyclic frequencies, the structural change in atomic clusters and free volumes will be quantitatively identified as a function of the deformation parameters. Besides the systematic theoretical calculations, comprehensive cyclic loading experiments will be performed on the Zr50Cu40Al10 BMG to induce different levels of atomic-scaled relaxation and damage. Then, multi-scale mechanical tests and structural characterizations will be carried out to progressively reveal atomic migration/rearrangement information caused by the relaxation and damage. These systematic investigations coupled with our previous structural model will allow us to identify the microscopic evolution of stress-induced relaxation and damage and thereby elucidate their atomistic mechanisms. The implementation of this proposal will expect to lead to an in-depth understanding the correlation between the atomic structure and mechanical properties. Furthermore, it will offer a scientific knowledge for the design of novel BMGs with superior fatigue and other properties. 塊體金屬玻璃是一種新型的金屬材料，具有諸多優異力學性能，例如高強度、高硬度、大彈性應變、耐磨性高，這些特性源于它們複雜而無序的原子結構。 非晶態結構是熱力學亞穩的結構，在應力及溫度作用下極易發生結構弛豫。對於塊體金屬玻璃中由溫度誘導的結構弛豫已有了一定瞭解，但對由應力誘導的結構弛豫仍知之甚少。另外，塊體金屬玻璃中外加應力對材料的破壞機制仍是懸而未決的問題。因此，本研究計劃致力于在原子尺度上解析應力誘導的結構弛豫及破壞過程，并將它們與塊體金屬玻璃的力學性能進行關聯。我們的目標是結合理論計算和先進實驗手段，建立應力誘導的原子躍遷或重排，與力學性能尤其是疲勞性能兩者之間的定量描述。我們的最終目標，是在計算和實驗結果的基礎上，在原子尺度揭示塊體金屬玻璃中應力誘導的變形和弛豫機制。 我們擬採用成份為Zr50Cu40Al10 (at.%)的塊體金屬玻璃作為目標合金體系。採用經典分子動力學方法模擬此合金的循環變形（拉伸和壓縮）行為，以“嵌入原子勢”描述原子之間的相互作用。循環變形過程中同步記錄原子結構的演化。通過系統地改變應力和循環加載頻率，我們將建立原子團簇的和自由體積的結構變化與變形參數之間的函數關係。理論計算之外，我們將對Zr50Cu40Al10塊體金屬玻璃進行循環加載，誘導不同程度的原子尺度結構弛豫及破壞，再通過多尺度力學性能測試和結構表徵手段逐步瞭解弛豫及破壞引起的原子躍遷和重排過程。結合我們之前提出的結構模型，本研究計劃擬展開的系統研究將使得我們瞭解應力誘導結構弛豫和破壞過程中的結構演化，從而在原子尺度揭示它們的機制。 本研究計劃的成功實施將使得我們深入瞭解塊體金屬玻璃原子結構和力學性能的關聯。另外，它將為設計具有優異疲勞和其它力學性能的新型塊體金屬玻璃提供科學依據。

117612.label: Major findings and research outcome
117612.value: Recent studies indicate that metallic glasses (MGs) contain two major regions: liquid-like regions and the solid-like region. The objective of this program is to characterize the stress-induced relaxation and damage processes and then to correlate them with the mechanical properties of bulk metallic glasses (BMGs). In particular, emphasis will be placed on the mechanistically understanding of the relaxation and damage mechanisms of BMGs under static and cyclic stress conditions. The major research findings are given below: 1. A Electric Contact Resistance (ECR) Monitoring System with high resolutions developed recently is used to capture the atom-scale reconfiguration of BMGs before and after fatigue tests under static and cyclic loading. In this study, electrical currents traveling through the samples of both as-cast and fatigue-tested Zr50Cu40Al10 BMG specimens are in-situ monitored under the auxiliary stress. By employing the Zimen-Kelton Spaepen’s model, the transient atomic-scale damage and relaxation inherited from the fatigue test is revealed by ECR. A microstructural model is inferred such that the origin of unusual fatigue performance of the BMG is attributed to the evolution of liquid like cores manifested as the concurrent atomic-scale damage and relaxation during the fatigue test. The understanding of the stress-induced relaxations and damages will lead to the development of scientific principles useful for the design of novel BMGs with superior compressive and fatigue resistances. (Research Output 4, 6, 7 and 9) 2. The jerky flow behavior of metallic glasses (MGs) under compression tests is systematically investigated in this study for various alloy compositions, ranging from the commonly conceived relatively more “ductile” MGs, such as those based on Zr and Cu, to the relatively more “brittle” ones, such as those based on Mg and Fe, on the microscopic scale. Through extensive compression studies, a clear sample size and base-element dependence of the jerky flow in MGs is revealed, which shows that the stress-drop amplitude, as normalized by the corresponding MG yield strength, reduces with decreasing sample size or increasing elastic modulus during compression tests. Meanwhile, the temporal discontinuity of the jerky flow, as characterized by the duration of the stress-drop events and the delay events, also displays similar size and base-element dependence. Finally, a unified theory based on stick–slip dynamics is proposed to explain the coupled size and base-element effects in BMGs. This study contributes to a fundamental understanding of the share-band formation and propagation in BMGs. (Research Output 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 10)

117612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
117612.value: Metallic glasses (MGs) have attracted extensive scientific and technological interests because of their unique mechanical and physical properties. In spite of these promising properties, their widespread applications are limited primarily due to the inhomogeneous deformation localized in extremely thin shear band (SB), displaying catastrophic failure with little plasticity. Our studies had revealed the SB mechanism of BMGs under both static and fatigue tests; however, most of the work was based on macroscopic approaches with low mechanical resolutions, making the intrinsic behavior of the shear banding blurred. Thus, the mechanism of shear banding is still far from fully understood. While nanoindentation with nanoscale resolutions offers an excellent opportunity to tackle this nano-localized process. It is our belief that the future research should aim at elucidating the physical origin of the dynamics and stability of SBs, resulting in developing a scientific scheme to bridge the gap between the SB dynamic process and the atomic structure of MGs through a combination of the state-of-the-art experimental techniques and theoretical calculations. The outcomes from these studies will extend the SB research on other amorphous materials, including borosilicate glasses and granular materials. The ultimate goal is to establish a unified SB theory for all amorphous materials.

117612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
117612.value: Bulk metallic glasses (BMGs) constitute a new class of metallic materials with many interesting properties for structural and functional applications. For instance, BMGs, such as Ni-based BMGs, generally have extremely high strength, with their yield strength to 4,000 MPa at ambient temperatures. In comparison, the yield strength of high-performance steels is less than 1,000 MPa. However, the major problem of BMGs is their brittle fracture with very little plastic deformation. The objective of this project is to have a mechanistic understanding of the poor ductility and brittle fracture of BMGs. Our study have revealed that BMGs contain both liquid-like zones (LLZs) imbedded in the solid-like matrix. When static loads or cyclic loads (fatigue tests) are applied to BMGs, these LLZs evolve and then line up along 45 degree to form a shear band. The propagation of the shear band results in catastrophic failure of BMGs with little plastic deformation. Our understanding of the shear-band formation mechanism will provide us with a way to enhance the plastic deformation of BMGs. For instance, the introduction of second-phase particles forms multiphase BMGs. These crystalline particles are expected to trigger multiple shear bands for enhanced plastic flow prior to fracture.
