118212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118212.value: Water resources management is important for today’s society to better utilize the limited water resources. The rapid increase of urban modernization results in an increase of pollutant loads by, at least, one order of magnitude over natural catchments conditions. Typical water pollutants include suspended solids, nutrients, biochemical oxygen demand, pathogenic organisms and trace metals. The water quality in urban river networks has been worsening by intake of surface runoff and sewages in day-to-day consumption cycles. Nowadays, the distribution and restoration of water quality play a key role in sustainable development in modern cities. In addition, the water pollution resulting from sewages is not negligible because of relative high ratio of water in urban river channels. However, the river water quality monitoring is performed mostly by collecting discrete grab samples at single points in the channel but the temporal and spatial variations of water quality in urban river networks could not be measured. In particular, the sudden water pollution caused by unpredictable pollutant divulging due to sudden natural or manmade disasters is beyond routine management. This proposal aims to investigate the real impacts and possible resolution of fluid flow in confluence urban rivers and potential water pollution under sudden natural or manmade disasters. First, the target sites will be chosen by the research team in terms of on-site investigation and surveying of actual river networks in Hong Kong, e.g., Yuen Long Creek marked with bad water quality. Secondly, the morphology and water quality records of selected site will be collected via site surveying and historical database search from Hong Kong government information centre. Thirdly, the computational mock-up will be generated and implemented to the self-written computational code, which contains the integrated hydrodynamic-water quality model developed so far in the Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering, City University of Hong Kong. Fourthly, the scaled, experimental mock-up will be established in the State Key Laboratory of Hydraulics and Mountain Engineering, Sichuan University, PRC and relevant measurement will be carried out. Finally, the measured data will be used to validate the performance of the developed computational model for further improvement, which, in turn, will be used to predict the evolving trends of water quality towards a beneficial application of water quality monitoring in Hong Kong. 隨著人口膨脹及都市化進程的不斷加快，人類面臨日益嚴重的水資源短缺及隨之而產生的城市河道集水陡增，水質監控管理，等诸多挑战。应由日常表面徑流及排泄彙集導致的城區河道水質惡化及營養富集已成為目前城市可持續發展的主要障礙之一。此外，由氣候突變導致的河道過流量暴增及淤積也成為當前大都市日常運行及管理過程的不定因素。本課題以城市交匯河道流動為研究物件，選取典型河道流動，研發數值計算模型，類比交匯河道中複雜流動結構，紊流影響尺度，不同流量比條件對主支流交匯及通流狀況之影響。預期研究結果將對進一步研究交匯河道污染漂移，擴散及積澱奠定基礎。

118212.label: Realisation of objectives
118212.value: With the rapid development of urban area and population, besides the existing natural river streams, the number of manmade sewage waterways has been continuously increased to discharge municipal wastewater and urban surface runoff. The water quality in urban confluence river networks has been worsening by intake waters from surface runoff and sewages in day-to-day consumption cycles. Impervious surfaces cause high runoff from the catchments during rainfall, which, coupled with the increased drainage efficiency through roadside channels and storm water pipes, leads to rapid increases in storm runoff and peaks in the storm hydrograph. Hence, the management of urban storm water in rainy season represents a huge task due to the extreme spatial, temporal variations in water quantity-quality characteristics as well as the high uncertainty of evaluation. The public concern has addressed the attention of scientists and engineers worldwide and put forward new challenges for them to carry on studies of assessing water resource, water quality, solvable/non-solvable water pollutants and the impact on urban environment. This project aims to carry on a fundamental study of the impact of turbulent flow structure on water quality in confluence section between sewage waterways and urban river networks with the detailed objectives mentioned in 5.2. To fulfill the above objectives, we carried out some research works including literature review, model development, and model application and assessment with details listed below: 1. Literature review: We compared the advantages and disadvantages of existing hydrodynamic and water quality models like QUAL1, QUAL2, QUAL2E, MIKE11, DUFLOW-EUTROF1, etc. and realized that the direct usage of existing commercial model cannot assist to accomplish the proposed targets. Hence, it is necessary to develop and/or revise the existing model concerning our targeted cases with available experimental database. 2. Model development: This part includes three major steps: Step 1: To investigate the flow structure in open confluence channel, which is commonly encountered in natural rivers and urban river networks. Such flow phenomenon is much more complicated than the one in straight channel with the introduction of additional terms in the momentum equations, i.e., dissipation and dispersion terms. In addition to using the routine depth-averaged k-e model, we explore the impact of these two items on the flow patterns in open confluence channel. We developed self-written program to simulate the flow structure in open confluence channel and validated the simulation results with available experimental data. The results indicate that the turbulence induced by separation and free shear flow can be evaluated via the dissipation terms in the momentum equation, while the influence of dispersion terms, evaluated by vertical non-uniformity, is both flow-condition-dependent and location-dependent. The outputs of the study have been recognized and published in prestigious, international referred journal “Hydrological Processes”. Step 2: Furthermore, to trace the variation of free surface along the river confluence junction, we also developed the model with dynamic mesh scheme to simulate/capture the free surface of flow in open confluence channel. The model is also implemented in our self-written program. The outputs of the study have been recognized and published in prestigious, international referred journal “Advances in Mechanical Engineering”. The results indicate the key elements in modelling confluence flow and are helpful for selecting suitable numerical model and solving engineering problems encountered in confluence channel. Step 3: To develop an appropriate operating framework of sluices in river networks. Many river networks are controlled by sluices, especially in plain area. To prevent potential floods, maintain water level, and improve water environment in the inner river, the water transfer of river networks is needed and executed often in terms of optimized operation rules of sluices planned in advancing. The traditional modelling of physical processes is regarded as physically-based modelling (or knowledge-driven modelling) because it targets to explain the underlying processes. In opposite to the routine model, we developed an appropriate framework of optimizing operation rules of sluices in river networks based on the knowledge-driven and data-driven mechanism to guarantee maintaining optimized operation status and decision-making concurrently with multi-objectives and multiple constraints, in which, River Networks Mathematical Model (RNMM), Artificial Neural networks (ANN), Genetic algorithms (GA), Operation rules Optimization Model (OROM) and Optimal Operation Rules of Sluices (OORS) are combined in terms of fast learning and rapid simulation based on the actual database monitored. The framework could achieve rapid response and provide practical water transfer of tidal river networks in reality. The application and outputs are satisfactory, recognized and published in prestigious, international referred journal “Water Resources Management”. 3. Model application and assessment: • The above developed models, i.e., numerical model for simulating flow structure in open confluence channel and framework for optimizing operation rules of sluices in river networks, have been validated with the corresponding experimental measurements and application case. Particularly, the later one, upon testified with the actual operation case in Pudong New Area of Shanghai in mainland China, presents the reliable performance. The research outputs have been published in several prestigious, international referred journals and international conferences. • In addition, we also developed/modified soft computing models, based on our experiences, to predict the trends of air pollutants in Hong Kong urban areas. The research outputs are also recognized and published in several prestigious, international referred journals and international conferences. • All-in-all, the research outputs produced from this project are fruitful and beneficial to the society of Hong Kong.

118212.label: Major findings and research outcome
118212.value: 1. Identified the impact of dissipation and dispersion terms, additionally added to the hydrodynamic model, on the flow structure in open confluence channel using self-developed computing program. The outputs are presented in international referred journal article [1]; 2. Explored the influence of free surface on water depth in open confluence channel using dynamic mesh scheme combined in self-developed computing program. The outputs can be found in international referred journal article [2]; 3. Developed an operating framework of sluices in river networks to optimize the sluices control in urban river system using knowledge-driven and data-driven mechanism with self-written self-code on Matlab platform. The results of real testing case indicate the superiority of the developed framework over the routine one. The developed framework could achieve rapid response and provide practical water transfer of tidal river networks in reality. The results can be seen in international referred journal article [4] and international conference paper [3]; 4. Other relevant research outputs can be seen in published international referred journal articles [3, 5-13] and international conference papers [1-2].

118212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118212.value: Further development will be expected on the coupling between the hydrodynamic model and the water quality model. According to literature, the existing water quality models mainly deal with nutrient and oxygen balance in water but not able to reflect the impact of turbulent flow structure on water quality and, the relation between water quality and sediment motion in confluence junctions between sewage waterways and urban river networks due to various simplifications. Hence, the combination of hydrodynamic model and water quality model presents a challenging topic to further study in considering the characteristics of streams-rivers or main rivers-waterways selected. The coupled model, if succeed, is expected to forecast the evolution and trend of water quality, provide the temporal and space distributions of hydrodynamic parameters and water quality variables, put forward the potential effect of sudden runoff and waste water scouring on the urban water environment.

118212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118212.value: The frequent occurrences of urban waterlogging in mega-cities of China and the resultant negative impact on urban environment has addressed wide attention of scientists, engineers as well as urban planners and, meanwhile, put forward many challenges to proceed advancing studies in water resource exploring, water drainage planning, water quality assessing, and potential waterlogging forecasting/precaution, etc. This project carried on a preliminary study to improve the hydrodynamic model via implementing additional terms, tracing dynamic free surface level in confluence river junction, optimize the sluices control in urban river system and dynamic hydraulic parameters in open waterway confluences. An improved hydrodynamic model was developed to address the impact of vertical non-uniformity and turbulent separation on simulation accuracy and validated with the available measurements. An optimized operating framework was established for sluices control and regulation in urban river networks. The research has achieved good, promising outputs and published 13 international referred journal articles with SCI index and 3 international referred conference papers.

118412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118412.value: Microstrip patch antennas became very popular for various mobile wireless systems as they have the characteristics of low profile, cost effective fabrication and easy of integration with devices and components. Microstrip patch antennas are also very suitable for applying in wireless communication operating in microwave frequency bands. Examples include second and third generation base stations in the top of buildings and miniature antenna hidden inside mobile phones. Recently, many millimeter wave systems have been proposed, such as the 60 GHz license-free indoor broadband personal area networks and 77GHz automotive sensor systems. However, at millimeter wave frequencies, microstrip patch antenna may suffer from poor radiation efficiency as the metallic loss from the metal parts of the microstrip line and the patch increases with operating frequency. Some approaches are using parabolic reflector or horn antennas but they are not recommended for civilian application as their size are quite large. In this project, we will modify the conventional microstrip patch antenna and develop a new type of antenna element with no metallic loss and high radiation efficiency in millimeter wave frequencies. Based on the novel antenna element, several innovative antennas with high performance for millimeter wave communication systems will also be developed. 微帶貼片天線非常適用於各種移動無線系統。因其低剖面的特性，便於組裝於其他器件內，達到非常顯著成本效益。微帶貼片天線亦非常適合應用無線通信中微波頻帶，包括第二代和第三代基站天線，及隱藏於移動通訊部件的微型天線。最近，許多毫米波系統方案已被提出，如60 GHz的室內個人寬頻區域網路和77GHz汽車感應系統。但在毫米波頻率，微帶貼片天線受制於天線微帶線部分的金屬損耗所引起的低幅射效率，使其工作頻段提高。有些方案建議使用抛物面天線或喇叭天線，但因它們的面積比較龐大，所以並不採納。在這個項目中，傳統的微帶貼片天線將被改良，並開發出一種新型的無金屬損耗及高幅射效率的毫米波貼片天線。而在上述新型天線單元的基礎上，可應用於毫米波通信系統的天線亦將被研發。

118412.label: Realisation of objectives
118412.value: The project has been completed with all the four objectives realised. In fact, we have achieved more than expected. The results represent a major achievement in the antenna field, which attract much interest in the antenna community worldwide. At the beginning, we have studied the performance of conventional microstrip antennas when they are operated at millimeter waves. The results have been used to benchmark the performance of the new antenna developed in this project. Next, we have investigated the performance of the dense dielectric patch antennas operated at around a few GHz. Detailed simulation results and experimental data were obtained for verification. The results have been used to benchmark the performance of the new millimeter wave dense dielectric patch antennas developed in this project. With all these basic findings, a dense dielectric patch antenna with broadside radiation was developed. Different kinds of dielectric materials were considered. Different kinds of excitation techniques were studied. The ways to improve the bandwidth were investigated. For developing antenna arrays of dense dielectric patch antennas, different kinds of feeding networks were investigated with the objective to achieve high efficiency and simple antenna structure for low cost fabrication. We have also studied to use water as the dielectric substrate for realising the novel antenna. Exciting result was achieved when the antenna is operated at the fundamental broadside mode or at the higher order omni-directional mode.

118412.label: Major findings and research outcome
118412.value: The dense dielectric patch antenna is a new kind of planar patch antenna which has the major advantage of high efficiency when operated at high microwave frequencies. it pocesses the advantages of conventional metallic patch antennas and dieelctric resonator antennas. With the support from a Ph.D. student and a research engineer, we have studied the characteristics of the dense dielectric patch antenna operated at lower microswave frequencies, with experimental verification. The antenna is fed by a coaxial probe. it was found that the antenna performs very well in comparison with the conventional metallic patch antenna. The investigation on the dense dielectric patch antenna has been extended to the 60 Ghz band. Uisng a PCB of dielectric constant equal to 10 to realize the dielectirc patch, a 4 by 4 dense dielectric patch antenna fed by a microstrip line network was designed, fabricated and tested by the conventional fabrication technique. The antenna is fed by an aperture coupled feed network. The bandwidth achieved is about 23%, which is highly desirable. The gain is 16.5 dBi which is also acceptable for practical applications For achieving higher efficiency and lower fabrication costs, a 4 by 4 dense dielectric patch antenna array fed by a substrate integrated waveguide corporate feed network was developed successfully with the dielectric patches realized by introducing perforations into a dielectric substrate with relative dielectric constant equal to 10. The antenna array has 23% bandwidth and 17.5 dBi peak gain, which is attractive for practical applications. In addition, we have used water to build dense dielectric patch antennas with broadside and end-fire radiation patterns. It is interesting to find that if pure water is used, a high-performance patch antenna with more than 70% radiation efficiency can be achieved.

118412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118412.value: The research has high potential for further development. It opens up a new paradigm for antenna advancement as the dense dielectric patch antenna incorporates both the advantages inherent to the microstrip antenna and dielectric resonator antenna. It is low in profile and low in ohmic loss. It is attractive for developing low-profile antennas operated at sub-millimeter wave and terahertz frequencies for future high speed wireless communications. With the use of different dielectric materials for realising the dense dielectric patch antenna, such as water or wine, transparent and flexible antennas can be developed for various applications.

118412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118412.value: Antennas are the crucial components in any wireless systems or devices, including mobile phones, RFID, Wifi, Android TV, etc. The number of antennas in the world is larger than the total population globally now. Most of these antennas are made of metals such as copper or aluminium, which limits the application areas of the wireless devices. Although dielectric resonator antennas were proposed more than 30 years ago, it was not popularly used due to its difficulty in mass production and bulky antenna structure. The success of this project provides the possibility to develop low profile antenna with non-metallic materials. The antenna can also be fabricated using standard PCB techniques. More importantly, the success in using water in realising the dense dielectric patch antenna opens up the paradigm for developing low cost transparent and flexible low profile antenna for various wireless applications including on-body and off-body communications.

Relevant algorithms will be developed on model representation, interrogation, manipulation and visualization. Special attention will be given to the targeted applications in isogeometric analysis. Volumetric subdivision model construction: Given a volumetric model defined by known boundary surface information, we are interested in constructing a volumetric subdivision model for downstream isogeometric analysis. Different strategies will be applied for defining a control mesh of the volumetric model with good parametrization. Robust algorithms will be developed for handling different boundary conditions. Techniques on volumetric model reconstruction from other field data will also be investigated. Isogeometric analysis using subdivision-based modelling: The volumetric subdivision model will be directly extended to higher-dimensions to represent various behaviors of a physical object and will be further utilized in isogeometric analysis. Given a volumetric model with known boundary conditions and external loading, we find the actual distribution of the behaviors within the object based on the underlying governing equations of the field physics. Case studies for testing and validation: To validate the research outcomes, the developed subdivision schemes and relevant algorithms on isogeometric analysis will be implemented in an own developed C-programming environment. Various case studies will be produced throughout the project on volumetric data modelling, model construction, model manipulation, and isogeometric analysis.

118512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118512.value: Subdivision-based modeling offers numerous advantages over classic splines and NURBS, the de-facto standard of today’s CAD (computer aided design) and graphics industries. Different from NURBS, subdivision surfaces can be defined by a set of control vertices of arbitrary topology. They allow the design of efficient, hierarchical, local, and adaptive algorithms for modelling, rendering and manipulation of free-form shape with arbitrary topology. Crease and sharp features can also be easily embedded on the same surface. Subdivision-based algorithms have been widely studied for surface modeling. The objective of the proposed project is to further extend subdivision-based modeling for higher-dimensional representation of both spatial information of an engineering object and its primary behavioral information by the same set of underlying basis functions. The investigation will lead to the integration of two important activities on design and finite element analysis (FEA) to be carried out using the same CAD representation. These activities are now connected through model translation and mesh generation. The integration will eliminate many difficulties and restrictions encountered with FEA by directly using the exact CAD geometry for FEA. The computation efficiency, accuracy and quality of the analysis results can be substantially increased. This is an active research area of recent years and was coined by researchers as isogeometric analysis. Most existing work on isogeometric analysis are mainly built upon spline-based representations. With subdivision-based isogeometric analysis, there will be added capability and flexibility in handling complex engineering objects. Key areas to be addressed in the project include theories and practical algorithms for higher-dimensional subdivision-based modeling, volumetric model construction, robust algorithms for handling objects with crease and boundary features, related algorithms on model manipulation, and their applications in isogeometric analysis. Case studies on both representation and isogeometric analysis will be conducted to test the proposed modeling schemes and the developed algorithms. NURBS是目前计算机辅助设计(CAD)和计算机图形学(CG)领域几何造型的工业标准。同NURBS相比，细分造型方法具备更多的优点。细分方法能够很好地构造和表示拓扑结构复杂的几何体，并具有层次细节，算法简单稳定等特点。尖锐特征亦可被容易地定义到一般的细分体上。等几何分析（Isogeometric Analysis或IGA）的主要思想则是将CAD中用于表达几何模型的基函数作为需计算物理特性的场函数，因而实现了计算机辅助设计（CAD）和计算机辅助工程（CAE）的无缝结合。目前用于等几何分析最多的基函数为传统样条函数及T-样条函数。本项目近一步探讨用多维细分造型方法进行等几何分析。主要研究领域包括高维细分及相关理论，便于进行等几何分析的实体重构，体尖锐特征的定义，及用高维细分进行等几何分析的基础算法研究。

118512.label: Realisation of objectives
118512.value: The main objective of this project is on subdivision-based modeling for isogeometric analysis (IGA). For easy integration with today’s computer aided design (CAD) environment, the emphasis of the project is on subdivision schemes that generalize various forms of splines. Key areas addressed in the project include the development of analysis-aware schemes for subdivision-based modelling, a general study on volumetric subdivision based modeling, isogeometric analysis using subdivision-based modelling and other alternative basis functions, and case studies on isogeometric analysis for testing and validation. The emphasis of the project is on the development of some foundation algorithms on subdivision based modeling and relevant enriched basis functions for isogeometric analysis. All project objectives have been achieved with major activities described as follows. (1) During the initial phase of this project, a general study on volumetric subdivision-based modeling and other related subdivision schemes have been investigated for possible applications in isogeometric analysis (Objectives #1-2). In the literature, one may find various works on subdivision-based volumetric data modeling, including Catmull-Clark subdivision and several other subdivision schemes. One may also find some work in this area on isogeometric analysis based on the parametric evaluation proposed by J. Stam in an article published in Siggraph 1998 using Catmull-Clark subdivision and Loop subdivision schemes. (2) In connection with subdivision based modeling, a generalized B-spline surface subdivision scheme of an arbitrary order with a tension parameter is developed (Objectives #1-2). Several well-known subdivision schemes, including Doo–Sabin subdivision, Catmull–Clark subdivision, and several other subdivision schemes built upon trigonometric and hyperbolic B-splines, become special cases of the proposed scheme. One can also construct exact analytic geometries, such as conic section curves, spheres, cylinders, cones, etc., using the generalized subdivision scheme. (3) Subdivision schemes produce smooth higher order models in regions of regular topology. However, only C1 continuity can usually be achieved at positions of extraordinary vertices. During this project, mapped B-splines are developed for both modeling and isogeometric analysis using control meshes of arbitrary topology (Objectives #2-3). The proposed scheme produces higher order smooth models in both regular and extraordinary regions. For mapped B-splines using cubic B-spline basis functions implemented through the project, e.g., the scheme produces models with global C2 continuity including at positions of extraordinary vertices. For regular regions in this case, the scheme reproduces cubic B-splines or Catmull-Clark models, while for extraordinary regions, the scheme produces higher order continuous models compared with that of Catmull-Clark subdivision. (4) Interpolatory subdivision schemes and other alternative basis functions have also been investigated for applications in isogeometric analysis (Objectives #2-3). A truncated interpolatory basis function was proposed for both modeling and isogeometric analysis. A method was also developed for parametric evaluation of interpolatory subdivision schemes useful for isogeometric analysis. A combined scheme using unstructured T-splines with mapped B-spline basis functions was also developed for modeling and isogeometric analysis. (5) A comprehensive study has also been conducted on convergence analysis in isogeometric analysis using mapped B-splines, unstructured T-splines and Catmull-Clark subdivision with a particular emphasis on convergence analysis in extraordinary regions (Objectives #3-4). (6) Some case studies in linear elasticity have been conducted on isogeoetric analysis using mapped B-splines, truncated interpolatory basis functions, mapped interpolatory basis functions, and a combined scheme using unstructured T-splines with mapped B-splines for extraordinary regions (Objectives #3-4). Based on the results obtained through the project, an article on generalized B-spline subdivision was published in Computer Aided Design [J3]. Some further work on parametric evaluation on interpolatory subdivision schemes was published in Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics [J1]. Two other articles were published on mapped basis functions for isogeometric analysis, one on mapped B-splines and one on mapped interpolatory basis functions respectively, in Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering [J2, J4]. Some further work on a combined scheme using unstructured T-splines with mapped B-spline basis functions were presented in the IGA 2016 conference [C1]. The work on convergence analysis were presented in SIAM GD/SPM 2015 and IGA 2015 conferences [C2-C3]. Some other results mentioned above were also presented in three other conferences, namely IGA 2014 [C4], CAD/Graphics 2013 [C5], and SIAM GD/SPM 2013 [C6].

118512.label: Major findings and research outcome
118512.value: Major research findings in this project are briefly highlighted as follows: (1) A generalized B-spline surface subdivision scheme of an arbitrary order with a tension parameter was developed [J3]. The scheme reproduces uniform generalized B-splines, including classic B-splines, trigonometric B-splines and hyperbolic B-splines. Several well-known subdivision schemes fall under the newly proposed generalized B-spline subdivision scheme. One can also construct exact analytic geometries, such as conic section curves, spheres, cylinders, cones, etc., using the generalized subdivision scheme. (2) A new scheme, named mapped B-spline basis functions, has also been developed for both modelling and isogeometric analysis [J4, C6]. The scheme can use a quadrilateral control mesh of arbitrary topology for both modeling and analysis. The scheme can achieve an arbitrary higher order global continuity, including at extraordinary corner positions where only C1 continuity can be achieved with most of the existing subdivision schemes. For cubic B-spline basis functions used for mapping to others, a global C2 continuity can be achieved. For regular regions in this case, the scheme reproduces cubic B-splines or Catmull-Clark models, while for extraordinary regions, the scheme produces higher order continuous models compared with that of Catmull-Clark subdivision. (3) In addition to mapped B-spline basis functions, a new kind of interpolatory basis functions was also developed for both modeling and isogeometric analysis [J2, C4, C5]. Different from Catmull-Clark subdivision and mapped B-splines basis functions, this new modeling scheme is an interpolatory scheme. The scheme is useful for direct analysis of models interpolating the given control vertices. The scheme was initially implemented for modeling and analysis using regular control meshes in both 2D and 3D [C5]. It is further extended for modeling and isogeometric analysis using control meshes of arbitrary topology [J2, C4]. (4) In collaboration with other researches, a method was also developed for parametric evaluation of interpolatory subdivision curves [J1]. The proposed method can be used for the evaluation of both positions and derivatives. Combined with the Stam’s algorithm for exact evaluation of extraordinary patches originally introduced for Catmull-Clark subdivisions (Stam 1998), the proposed method can also be extended to 2D and 3D for both surface and volumetric models with a control mesh of arbitrary topology. (5) In this project, an exploratory study was also conducted in developing a combined scheme using unstructured T-splines with mapped B-spline basis functions for extraordinary corner patches [C1]. A comprehensive study has also been conducted on convergence analysis in isogeometric analysis using mapped B-splines, unstructured T-splines and Catmull-Clark subdivision with a particular emphasis on convergence analysis in extraordinary regions [C2, C3].

118512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118512.value: Subdivision-based modeling received extensive attention in free form shape design, multi-resolution representation, and computer graphics. In connection with isogeometric analysis using subdivision-based modelling, the following areas can be further addressed. (1) Enriched basis functions for isogeometric analysis (IGA) based on generalized subdivision schemes: Generalized subdivision schemes provide a further extension of many know subdivision schemes. They can also exactly represent conical and other analytical shapes commonly used in engineering applications. The use of enriched basis functions with generalized B-splines and generalized subdivision schemes can thus further extend the applications of isogeometric analysis for a wider class of engineering models. (2) Combined schemes for isogeometric analysis: Isogeometric analysis was initially developed based on the concept that basis functions used in the solution space will be the same as that of the CAD geometry. For practical applications, however, there is no need to use the same basis functions on both sides. In case of subdivision schemes or other CAD representations with no ready local refinement algorithms, one may use T-splines with excellent local refinement operations in the solution space while maintaining the original basis functions for the CAD geometry.

118512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118512.value: This project falls in an active research area on isogeometric analysis (IGA) in directly using exact CAD representations for integrated design and analysis. The integration eliminates various difficulties and restrictions encountered with traditional finite element analysis. The computation efficiency, accuracy and quality of analysis results can also be substantially increased. Most existing works on isogeometric analysis are mainly built upon spline-based representations. The main objective of this project is on subdivision-based modeling for isogeometric analysis (IGA). Subdivision based modeling provides added capability and flexibility in handling complex engineering objects. Key areas addressed in the project include the development of application- and analysis-aware subdivision-based modelling, a general study on volumetric subdivision-based modeling, isogeometric analysis using subdivision-based modelling and other alternative basis functions, and case studies on isogeometric analysis for testing and validation. The emphasis of the project is on the development of some foundation algorithms on subdivision based modeling and relevant enriched basis functions for isogeometric analysis.

118812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118812.value: 现实生活中，存在着一类难以用文本描述的搜索查询，但如果查询者能够提供一些图像/视频作为例子，这些查询通常会变得很容易。然而，对传统的桌面电脑用户来说，提供这种多媒体辅助信息很不方便，因此基于文本的查询仍然是主要方式。近年来，移动设备的兴起已经对传统的搜索查询产生了冲击。凭借带有大量传感器的移动设备，用户可以方便快捷地在互联网上查询信息。在不远的未来，用户便能够以“拍照”加“提问”的方式随时随地搜索信息。例如，用户搜索的问题可以包含一段文本信息：“怎么制作这个小孩子的玩具？”和一个玩具的图片或视频。基于现有技术，开发针对多元问题的搜索引擎是非常困难。因为，从大量非结构化或半结构化的多媒体元数据中理解语义和搜索答案都是很有挑战的问题。 该项目将解决移动设备上多媒体问答系统的两个关键问题。第一个问题是实例搜索，即如何从大规模多媒体数据中搜索和理解视觉实例。由于待搜索的视觉实例可能会从任意角度拍摄，并且其背景可能会与目标实例不一致，所以搜索视觉实例是个极具挑战的问题，其中包含若干技术难点。因此，现有的近重复（near duplicate）搜索技术对这一新的实例搜索不再适用。第二个问题为问答（QA)，即对用户提出的多元问题进行回答。不同于传统的基于文本的问答系统，本项目中的问题可以用图像，视频，文本，或其任意组合来回答。这一问题及其关联问题都是从未研究过的新问题，包括多元问题的语义理解，基于问题类型与移动设备特性的答案选择与可视化。 该项目创新点在于提出一个基于问答（QA）的搜索模式，解决了在移动环境下，如何用多媒体信息提问与回答的问题。本项目的贡献体现在两方面。对实例搜索，我们寻求近实时的，分布式的，省内存的，适用于大规模网络多媒体数据的实例搜索算法。研究重点在于鲁棒的特征描述，快速的匹配与搜索算法，以此进行大规模信息检索，并以此区别于近重复搜索和垂直搜索。对多媒体问答，研究重点在于移动设备上问答信息的集成，归纳总结，和可视化。这些都是现有研究文献中从未研究过的新问题。

118812.label: Realisation of objectives
118812.value: The project was divided into three major phases in line with the project objectives: instance search algorithms (objective-1), multimedia answering and presentation (objectives 2 and 3), system prototyping and benchmarking (objective-4). PHASE-I: INSTANCE SEARCH Instance search is to identify the same instances of a given object query. The main challenge comes from the fact that the object could be non-rigid and non-planar, and hence the instances can change wildly in visual appearance. Search of visual instances depends heavily on the distinctiveness of visual feature, and the feature used in this project is bag-of-visual-words (BoW) learnt from salient local points (SIFT) sparsely sampled from videos. We studied the problem of instance search from three aspects: 1) topological representation of visual words for instance matching, 2) mining of visual instance for search re-ranking, 3) feature encoding and indexing for fast search. The developed algorithm is named as DT for using Delaunay Triangulation to represent the topology of visual words on space. The basic idea is to model the spatial configuration of visual instance with triangulation meshes formed by BoW. In such configuration, each edge and triangle model the relative position of visual words. Given a query and a video, the matching coherency between them is computed by enumerating the number of common edges and triangles. Furthermore, the importance of edges/triangles is quantified by goodness of match based on Hamming distance. Each edge/triangle carries a weight for enumeration. The near real-time performance of the algorithm was realized by indexing BoW with inverted file and sampling of words (<= 30 words) for online construction of triangulated graph. The former skips a large number of unnecessary comparisons and the latter approximates similarity by partial enumeration. For a video dataset of 1 million keyframes and assuming a vocabulary of 1 million words, the algorithm consumes around 30G of main memory and retrieval speed is around 1.3 second/query (using one core). The speed basically meets the requirement for real-time retrieval. While the algorithm offers high precision, retrieving the instances that appear visually different from query is difficult. We addressed the problem by offline mining of common object instances from videos. The problem of mining is that there is no query to start with and hence requires pairwise comparison of keyframes which can be extremely slow. We addressed the problem by proposal of a new feature, thread-of-features (ToF), which is keyframe set sharing similar patches. ToF is extracted based on inverted index but with tighter spatial (neighbourhood configuration) constraint and hamming signature pruning to exclude false candidates. ToFs are clustered by min-Hash algorithm and each resulting cluster ideally corresponds to the instances of an object. The algorithm is highly efficient because mining can be completed in 2-3 hours for one million keyframes. With this algorithm, the candidate object instances are hyperlinked. For online search, we proposed an inverted index like data structure to index the hyperlinks. Given a query, not only the visual instances are retrieved but also the hyperlinks relevant to the query are utilized to retrieve the instances not in the initial search result for re-ranking. Our approach successfully boosts the retrieval performance in terms of precision and recall. We also studied VLAD (vector of locally aggregated descriptor) for instance search to reduce the time and space complexity. We investigated VLAD encoding in frequency domain and successfully reduced the space complexity of BoW by more than 50 times. Nevertheless, the retrieval accuracy was not as good as BoW and VLAD was not considered in the final system for instance search. PHASE-II: MULTIMEDIA ANSWERING AND PRESENTATION The search scenario is that user want to ask a visual related question but has difficulty in query formulation. The solution is to allow user ask a text question by referring to a picture snapped by mobile phone. The user can draw a circle to indicate the instance under question in the picture. The basic approach is by issuing the visual instance as query to search for similar images and then employ natural language processing to infer the name of instance. The instance name is then augmented into the text question for search of answers. As there is no benchmark for multimedia QA, we started by constructing a dataset covering four question types, with around 1 million images from Flickr and 1.5 million QA pairs from Yahoo! Answers. Our research focus was on visual naming, question matching and answer presentation. Visual naming is tackled by fusion of visual scores (as a result of instance search) and phrases extracted from metadata. Similar question search is conducted by a syntactic tree parsing matching algorithm. Only high confident QA pairs are retained and presented in list-wise manner for interactive browsing. We particularly studied opinion QA because opinion-based questions are popular in social media and video is a better medium than text as answer. We developed a feedforward neural network to compute the similarity of QA pairs, where the answers are speeches extracted from videos. The focus of study was on localization of opinion clips and training of the neural network for similarity measure. We constructed a dataset with eight controversial topics and 340 hours of videos for experiments. The empirical study was focused on effectiveness of answer presentation with different mediums. PHASE-III: SYSTEM PROTOTYPING & BENCHMARKING Finally we integrated work done into a MQA (multimedia question-answering system) which is composed of three modules: (1) BoW indexing with components such as vocabulary training, hamming embedding and instance hyperlinking; (2) online retrieval with multiple-word assignment and topology checking, (3) answer presentation with visual instance naming and search of QA pairs. The system was exhibited internally within university and internationally in conferences and symposiums. We also participated in the annual TRECVid benchmark evaluation for the task: Instance Search (IS) during the years 2012-2014. In addition to the aforementioned technical components, we also engineered the system with two more components for context modeling and result fusion. Context refers to the background surrounding object instances, and fusion is required because a given query could consist of multiple visual examples. We developed a “stare” model, which simulates human perception system, for contextual matching. For the latter, we adopted video-level fusion strategy with delayed normalization to combine the results of DT from different visual examples.

118812.label: Major findings and research outcome
118812.value: Through three years of TRECVid participation, we confirmed the merit of topology verification in searching visual instance and the advantages of stare model in boosting recall. Particularly the result verified that topology, which keeps relative positions of words, offers a more powerful representation than modeling of absolute word positions. The result was published in IEEE Trans. on Multimedia (2015), where the proposed DT algorithm outperforms classic methods such as WGC (weak geometric consistency checking) and GVP (geometric-preserving visual phrases) and with comparable speed performance. The improvement of instance search also depends on the quality of mining. When more hyperlinks are found for a query, the chance of improvement is higher. We have verified the improvement through significance test. Another advantage is that the “over-norm” problem can be naturally tackled. Specifically, instance-level (instead of video-level) feature normalization can be applied to boost the retrieval scores of object instances in small-size. This step is practically useful to improve recall and can diversify the search results because otherwise the top-rank results are often instances in large size or near-duplicate videos. The result was reported in another journal paper IEEE Trans. on Image Processing (2016). Our approach was empirically shown to be much better than random walk and query expansion techniques on both image and video datasets. Among the TRECVid participants (20+ teams), our system was rated as one of the most efficient systems in retrieval. When integrated with question-answering, the system can return answers in about one minute. Except when answer is not available in the dataset, the system has a good chance in finding three related questions with an answer out of ten QA suggestions. For opinion-based QA, we also verified the performance of the proposed deep network by comparing to similarity measures including TF-IDF and BM25, a subspace method named partial least square, and a recently proposed DeepMatch neural network. In addition, user studies were also conducted to assess the user experience in QA and answer presentation. We compared the system to asking visual-related questions in Yahoo! Answers. The results were fairly encouraging because users spent less time in formulating questions and the developed system delivered answers faster. For opinion QA, the study verified that video answer is a preferred medium than text description for vivid displaying of sentiment/emotion signals. The results were published in ACM Multimedia (2012) and ACM Trans. on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications (2015).

118812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118812.value: The performance of current system is bottlenecked by the power of SIFT descriptors and the topological modeling of visual words for similarity comparison. Basically both the feature and similarity measure are “hand-crafted” for matching object instances undergone certain degree of scale and appearance changes. There are still cases that some of instances could not be retrieved due to large changes in geometric and photometric transformations. With the advancement in object detection techniques due to deep learning, it is now possible to design network architecture that models complex and nonlinear changes. For example, a network to simultaneously locate common object instances while evaluating their similarities. There are a number of problems along, nevertheless. First, pairwise comparison is not scalable to large dataset and hence efficient employment of the network for large-scale instance mining is a challenge. Second, to avoid exhaustive online matching due to pairwise comparison, the deep features should be extracted and offline indexed. However, different from BoW, deep features are dense and could be in very high dimension if spatial information is kept. How to effectively compress and index deep features, either using the existing techniques (e.g., VLAD) or inventing new data structure, remains interesting problem worth further investigation.

118812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118812.value: We have developed two key techniques for answering of multimedia query composed of text question and picture. The first technique performs search of similar visual examples from large database. As visual instances could undergo changes due to geometric and photometric transformations, topological information which models the relative positions of salient visual points is utilized for object matching. In addition, candidate instances are mined and linked so as to recall true instances as many as possible while ranking them high. Currently, the technique runs in real-time and consumes a reasonable amount of memory space. The second technique infers the name of visual instance under questions and conducts the search of similar questions crawled from the Internet. The question-answer pairs are then ranked and presented to users. As video is a preferred medium for answering opinion questions, a deep neural network was developed to evaluate the similarity between text questions and speech transcripts extracted from videos. Empirical justifications were conducted to validate different components of the proposed techniques by comparing to state-of-the-arts, and have confirmed the merit of both techniques. Both techniques were integrated into a system for user studies, which also confirmed the usability of the system for multimedia question-answering.

119212.label: Project Objectives

To characterize the cluster-scale structure and magnetic properties of the BMGs, as well as to investigate the effects of crystallization and structural relaxation induced by thermal treatments on structure and properties of the materials To simulate the atomic scale structure of Gd-Fe and Gd-Co metallic glass and to examine their magnetic properties based on the local cluster structure using commercially available simulation software packages

119212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
119212.value: 在過去的十多二十年，大塊金屬玻璃逐漸從純粹科研興趣發展為一系列擁有獨特性能的工程材料，並實際應用到不同的範疇。這理想的發展乃建基於眾多基礎研究，包括金屬玻璃的原子結構。加上近年實驗及電腦模擬技術的發展，科研人員對大塊金屬玻璃的結構與性能的相互關係，特別是玻璃生成能力及變形機理等，獲得更多更透徹的了解。 最早在工業應用的金屬玻璃是鐵基軟磁材料。此外(釓-鐵)基(Gd-Fe based)金屬玻璃亦可用於磁性記憶及磁光應用。Gd-C0-Al大塊金屬玻璃亦被考慮作為磁製冷材料。因稀土及過渡元素之間的相互作用會受原子間距及近鄰數目等因素影響，在這些稀土基金屬玻璃上就會展現豐富多變的特性。在應用層面考慮，對近鄰原子結構和特性的深入瞭解有助更有效設計及處理擁有合適特性的新釓基(Gd based)金屬玻璃。 在這研究計劃，我們會探討Gd-Co和Gd-Fe金屬玻璃的原子團簇結構跟磁性的關係。使用的合金成份會接近已知的金屬間化合物。因此預計金屬玻璃的原子團簇結構會跟金屬間化合物的相似。但因為金屬玻璃缺乏長程有序，其磁性就相信會跟對應的金屬間化合物有些微偏離。 實驗方面，除了標準的微結構及熱分析外，我們會用振動樣品磁強計量度金屬玻璃樣品從低溫到室溫處於高磁場下的特性。金屬玻璃的原子團簇結構就會通過電子衍射及在上海光源(Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility)進行的X射線能量吸收譜瞭解。此外，我們亦會輔以非晶結構的電腦模擬，作為實驗結果的互相參照。從計算結果當中可確認Gd-Co和Gd-Fe金屬玻璃的原子團簇主要結構及其相關參數。這些結合實驗和模擬的結果可提昇我們對玻璃生成能力及其他性能例如變形等現象的理解。磁性特徵亦可通過計算與實驗的比較從而對非晶材料的磁性根源作出探討。當此計劃完成後，預期我們對稀土-過渡金屬非晶結構及其磁性的根源會有更進一步的認識。

119212.label: Realisation of objectives
119212.value: During the project period, the PI and the research team carried out systematic experiments on alloy design and characterization of the samples. Numerical simulations using ab-initio molecular dynamic approach was also done in conjunction with the experiment to establish the atomic scale cluster structures in the alloys developed in this study. The details of the work done for realization of the project objective are described in the following. Series of Co-B-Si and Gd-Co glassy alloy compositions were designed based on the possible cluster structures in the respective phase diagrams. In the case of Co-B-Si, the glass forming ability of the alloy was improved by destabilization of the crystal cluster structure by alloying beyond the nominal solubility limit in Co. The alloys with different compositions were found to have different glass forming abilities and distinctively different magnetic properties. The cluster structures were determined by EXAFS in conjunction with numerical simulations. These works were done to address all three objectives. Gd-based metallic glass with composition Gd4Co3, which is that of an intermetallic phase in the Gd-Co system, was also prepared. The atomic scale structure and the associated electronic structure were studied to correlate the magnetic properties of the Gd-based metallic glass and its structure. By long term annealing of an alloy with nominal composition of Gd4Co3, it was found that the composition of the well-known Gd4Co3 intermetallic compound was actually Gd6Co4.85. This thermodynamically equilibrium phase exhibited peculiar properties, such as negative thermal expansion and large magnetocaloric effect. These activities were done to address Objectives 1 and 3. Fe2P-type Gd6FeBi2 alloy was also synthesized successfully, and the compound shows good soft magnetic behavior at room temperature with a Curie temperature ~350 K. The relatively high Curie temperature and good magnetocaloric effect were explained in terms of the structure and electronic structure of the alloy. These works were done to address Objectives 1 and 2. The results of the above research activities are described in more details in Section 6.1 and published in SCI journals as well as reported in a conference, as detailed in Section 8 and 9. All the objectives had been thoroughly addressed and achieved completely.

119212.label: Major findings and research outcome
119212.value: Gd-Co and Co-B-Si metallic glasses and Gd-Fe-based crystalline alloys were prepared and they were characterized in detail to reveal the correlations between their atomic scale structures and magnetic properties. By studying the possible clusters in the metallic glass based on that of the Gd4Co3 intermetallic phase and the experimentally measured electronic structure, it was concluded that both Gd and Co atoms in the metallic glass contribute to the paramagnetic moment per Gd atom in the structure. This was supported by the Co 3d peak in the electron structure of the Gd4Co3 metallic glass, and this finding was in contrast to those reported in the literature. These results were reported in a SCI journal. (Item 1 in Part C, Section 8) During the course of investigation of the Gd4Co3 metallic glass, it was found that the composition of the well-known Gd4Co3 intermetallic compound was actually Gd6Co4.85. The detailed atomic scale structure and other peculiar properties were studied. The structure was described as a Gd6Co5/3Si3-structure type or a deviation of Ce6Ni2-xSi3 type with two disordered sites for Co atoms. With such crystal structure, the Gd6Co4.85 compound was found to exhibit negative thermal expansion and large magnetocaloric effect. These novel results were reported in a SCI journal. (Item 4 in Part C, Section 8) The Co-B-Si metallic glasses were examined using EXAFS in conjunction with numerical simulation for detailed atomic scale structure determination. Independent ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations of the atomic structures of Co63.1B27Si9.9 and Co65B24.4Si10.6 were performed within the framework of density functional theory (DFT), as implemented in the Vienna ab initio simulation package (VASP). The clusters structures of the two Co-based metallic glasses were found to be substantially different from each other in spite of the rather similar overall compositions. Such difference in the short-range order was used to explain the big differences in magnetic and mechanical properties between the two metallic glasses. The results were reported in a Gordon Research Conference (Item 1 in Part C, Section 9) and published in a SCI journal (Item 2 in Part C, Section 8). Gd-based compounds have attracted a great deal of interest as materials with large magnetocaloric effect and as materials for spintronic applications. Fe2P-type Gd6FeBi2 alloy was synthesized successfully, and the compound shows good soft magnetic behavior at room temperature with a Curie temperature ~350 K. The compound exhibits non-Curie-Weiss behavior in a large temperature range above Curie temperature, and slightly enhanced Gd moment at low temperature. The elevated Curie temperature and enhanced Gd magnetic moment were discussed based on measured electronic structure and the results from another isostructural compound Gd6CoTe2. The magnetocaloric effect was also measured in terms of the maximum magnetic entropy change of -4.3 J kg-1 K-1 at 50 kOe and -2.3 J kg-1 K-1 at 20 kOe, respectively. These results were reported in a SCI journal. (Item 3 in Part C, Section 8)

119212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
119212.value: From the outcomes of this research project, there are several aspects that can be further developed or explored. The intricate relationships between the magnetic properties of metallic glasses or their crystalline counterparts and the atomic scale cluster structure, especially the nearest neighbour configuration, can be a very powerful tool for studying the structure of magnetic metallic glasses. The use of EXAFS in conjunction with AIMD simulation has been shown to be effective for deciphering the atomic scale structure in metallic glass. It was demonstrated by our results that, even with a very minor change in overall composition of the metallic glasses, as long as the local atomic environment of the magnetic atoms changed, the overall macroscopic magnetic properties could change drastically. This may be used as a probe of the local cluster structures in metallic glasses or crystalline alloys and provide useful structural information for interpreting the properties of the materials, for instance, deformation behaviours, magnetic properties, etc. In addition to the scientific aspects, some of the alloys investigated in this project exhibit promising magnetic properties for applications. For instance, the CoBSi glassy alloy can be a good soft magnetic material for high frequency circuit applications. The Gd-based alloys having large magnetocaloric effect can be used as working substance in magnetic refrigeration systems operating at around room temperature or sub-zero temperatures. Such refrigeration systems are totally free from gases which damage the ozone layer in the atmosphere.

119212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
119212.value: Metallic glasses has long been used for soft magnetic applications. In this project, we prepared a series of metallic glasses and relevant crystalline alloys based on a rare-earth element gadolinium and transition elements like cobalt or iron. The materials were characterized in detail to establish the structural origin of their magnetic and thermal properties. By combining experimental and numerical simulation techniques, the atomic scale structures of the Gd-based metallic glasses and intermetallic compounds are revealed. The correlation between such atomic scale structural information and the magnetic properties can be used for probing the local atomic environment in metallic glasses. Most of the metallic glasses studied in this project exhibit very large magnetocaloric effect and are promising candidates for applications in magnetic refrigeration systems, which are friendly to the ozone layer in the atmosphere. One of the unexpected results from this project was that the reported structure and even the composition of a well-known gadolinium-cobalt intermetallic compound were found to be incorrect. By using the techniques we used for studying the Gd-Co-based metallic glass, we had unambiguously reported the real composition and atomic scale structure of the Gd6Co4.85 phase which was reported as Gd4Co3 in earlier works by others.

119612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
119612.value: With advantages such as non-physical cell contact and relatively high efficiency, the application of optical tweezers for manipulation of biological objects such as cells has received increasing attention both for medical applications and for making fundamental advances in biological sciences. However, manual intervention and the low throughput of existing optical manipulation systems create substantial hurdles that prevent the widespread adaptation of this emerging new technology. The automation of such techniques has hence become a key enabler for further advancement of optical cell manipulation. In this proposed research, we will show how automation technology considerably improves the optical manipulation of cells. This proposal will address four important issues in the development of automatic cell manipulation tools with robotically controlled optical tweezers. The first issue is characterizing the dynamics model of optically trapped cells. With this modeling information, we will determine how various environmental factors affect cell behavior and thus control these influences and optimize the manipulation setup for automatic operations. The second issue is developing a closed-loop control methodology for rapid and accurate positioning of single cells while locating the trapped cell within the optical trap. This will provide substantial technological development by controlling both cell positioning and cell trapping simultaneously. The third issue is extending the single-cell controller towards a parallelized control mechanism for manipulating multiple cells in parallel. This research outcome will enable many biomedical applications that must be done automatically, e.g., the transport of a group of human embryonic stem cells (hESC) into an array in right pairs for fusion, and manipulating multiple T cells while maintaining the fixed cell patterns for study of cell-to-cell interactions. The last issue is studying motion planning for automatically transporting the cells to a user-defined goal region while avoiding collisions with other cells and obstacles present in the workspace. The minimization of optical damage to the trapped cells is treated as a new important criterion aside from the criteria of obstacle avoidance and shortest path, among others. This research represents an important step in determining how engineering can provide new fundamental knowledge and advance cell-based medicine. Many cellular studies are limited by the availability of novel high-resolution, high-throughput tools. Automation technology will greatly advance the field of cell manipulation and profoundly affect the device industry for health care in the near future. 在应用机器人辅助技术实现细胞光学自动化操作过程中，我们将解决以下几个主要问题。第一是建立表征光学捕获细胞的动力学模型，以此确定各环境因素对细胞行为的影响，并且控制这些因素优化自动操作。第二是设计一种闭环控制算法用于快速、准确地定位被光镊捕获的单细胞。第三，在单细胞控制的基础上，发明并行处理多个细胞的并行控制机制。第四个问题是自动规划将细胞运输到目标区域的路径。这一研究成果将有多项生物医学应用，如将一组人体胚胎干细胞运输到阵列中进行组队融合；或者在维持一定细胞模式的情况下操作多个T细胞以研究细胞间相互作用。

119612.label: Major findings and research outcome
119612.value: 1. Characterize the dynamics model of optically trapped cells and examine mutual influences on cell behavior. We have developed an actin cytoskeleton model to probe the distinct underlying F-actin remodeling mechanism and show quantitatively how cell mechanical behavior of cell is associated with alterations in the cell functions. We further modeled the cell protrusion force quantitatively and probed the protrusion force distribution at the cell leading edge. These modeling approaches could help us characterize the mechanism of cell migration and lay a solid foundation for further proactive control of cell movement. 2. Develop a closed-loop control methodology for the rapid and accurate positioning of single cells. We developed a novel unified controller that manipulates cell positioning and cell trapping simultaneously. A geometric model was proposed first to confine the cell within a local region around the optical trap. The connection between the cell and the optical tweezers was formulated by using the concept of cell–tweezers (C–T) coalition. Then, we developed a controller based on a defined potential field function to drive the C–T coalition to the desired state while avoiding collisions with other obstacles in the environment. We further developed a vision-based observer for optical manipulation to estimate the velocity of cell. The stability is analyzed using Lyapunov-like analysis. 3. Develop a parallelized control mechanism for manipulating multiple cells into an array while maintaining cell patterns. We investigated control methodology to manipulate a group of cells into a region of interest to form the required pattern using robotically controlled optical tweezers. A novel multilevel-based topology was designed to present different cell patterns in the region of interest. A potential function-based controller was developed to control the cells to form the required pattern. A pattern regulatory control force was developed which particularly addresses the special case when cells stop at undesired positions. 4. Plan optimal motion algorithms for transporting cells to the desired region with collision avoidance. We finally designed a path planner based on the rapidly exploring random trees (RRT) algorithm for calculating a collision-free path for cell transportation. Both static and dynamic path planners were developed. For the dynamic path planner, an online monitoring strategy was employed to dynamically avoid collisions with randomly appeared obstacles caused by environmental influence such as the Brownian movement of microparticles. Experiments of transporting yeast cells were performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

119612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
119612.value: Further development of the research will be a study toward an automated robotic control system for cell surgery. Robotically controlled optical tweezers can be used as a special robot end-effector to achieve numerous cell surgical operations at both cellular and sub-cellular levels. We will explore this new technology in the development of an automated laser-induced cell surgery robotic system. The precise manipulation and dissection of subcellular organelles with optical manipulators will be conducted for high-throughput submicron surgeries.

119612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
119612.value: In this project, we have successfully addressed several important issues for automatic cell manipulation with robotically controlled optical tweezers. The first issue is characterizing the dynamics model of optically trapped cells, which will help us determine how various environmental factors affect cell behavior and thus control these influences and optimize the manipulation. The second issue is developing a closed-loop control methodology, which can help us to achieve rapid and accurate positioning of single cells while locating the trapped cell within the optical trap. The third issue is extending the single-cell controller towards a parallelized control mechanism for manipulating multiple cells in parallel. This research outcome will enable many biomedical applications that must be done automatically, e.g., the transport of a group of cells into an array for many further biomedical applications. The last issue is studying motion planning for automatically transporting the cells to a user-defined goal region while avoiding collisions with other cells and obstacles present in the workspace. Currently, many cellular studies are limited by the availability of high-resolution, high-throughput tools. The research outcome of this project will greatly improve the existing automated cell manipulation technology and potentially affect the healthcare device industry.

120512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
120512.value: Particle breakage is of fundamental importance to the mechanical behavior of sands and is related to many geotechnical engineering problems such as low pile capacity in carbonate sands and large settlement of high rock-fill dams. The source of particle breakage effects lies in the change made to the sand fabric during deformation process, a critical geometrical factor which governs the macroscopic sand behavior but must be evaluated using a microscopic approach. Despite considerable research dedicated to the micromechanics of sands associated with particle breakage, the nature of particle breakage is not well understood. Particularly no linkage is established between the particle breakage behavior and the intrinsic particle microstructure. Consequently, prediction of particle breakage and quantification of its effects on the sand behavior remains a difficulty. In view of the above deficiency, we propose an advanced investigation of the behavior of sand particle breakage using combined techniques of high-resolution nanofocus X-ray computed tomography (CT) and 3D discrete element modeling (DEM). The nanofocus X-ray CT allows the visualization and characterization of the morphology and microstructure of sand particles during the particle fracture process. This information will be fully incorporated into the 3D DEM model of single sand particle fracture. Furthermore, a probabilistic approach which is based on the statistical law of single particle fracture and probability density function of particle contact force will be employed to predict particle breakage inside an oedometer specimen. This innovative research will unravel the nature of sand particle breakage by establishing a linkage between the breakage behavior and particle microstructure. Particularly, the role of intrinsic particle flaws in the fracture pattern (e.g., grain splitting or asperity breakage) and fracture strength behavior will be elucidated. This research will also establish a novel probability-based modeling approach for crushable sands. This proposal requests HK$1,495,960 (equivalent to US$192,154) to support a PhD student and a senior research assistant to conduct a three-year research on this topic. The outcome of this research will produce both scientific and engineering impacts. The former comes from an improved understanding of the fundamental behavior of crushable sands and its possible contribution to the research on other related breakable granular materials. The latter is mainly reflected in the enhanced ability of engineers to make improved design and construction of geotechnical systems in crushable soils. This is very relevant in Hong Kong where highly decomposed granite or volcanic soils exhibit distinct breakage characteristics. 颗粒破碎对于砂的力学特性具有根本的重要性而且与许多岩土工程问题相关，例如在碳酸盐岩砂中桩的低承载力及高堆石坝的高沉降的问题。颗粒破碎的影响主要产生于变形过程中砂结构的变化，这是控制砂宏观特性的一个重要的几何因素，但必须用微观的方法进行评估。尽管已有相当的研究致力于与砂颗粒破碎有关的细观力学，但是颗粒破碎的机理还不是很清楚。特别是在颗粒破碎特性和颗粒内在微观结构之间仍没有建立联系。因此，对颗粒破碎的预测及量化颗粒破碎对砂特性的影响仍然是一个难题。 鉴于以上不足，我们提出了结合高分辨率的纳米焦点X射线计算机断层扫描（CT）和三维离散元模型（DEM）的综合技术对砂颗粒破碎的行为进行深入的研究。纳米焦点X射线（CT）可以在颗粒断裂过程中观测并表征砂颗粒的形态和结构。这些信息将被完全纳入到三维DEM的单个砂颗粒断裂的模型。除此之外，基于单个砂颗粒断裂的统计规律和颗粒间接触力分布的概率密度函数的一个概率方法将被用于预测固结试样中的颗粒破碎。 这种创新的研究将通过在破碎特性和颗粒微观结构之间建立联系来解开砂颗粒破碎的机理。特别是颗粒内在缺陷对断裂模式（如晶粒分裂或凹凸体破碎）和断裂强度特性的作用将会被阐明。本研究也将为可破碎砂建立一个新的基于概率的建模方法。 这项方案需要HK$1,495,960（约合US$192,154）用于支持一名博士研究生和高级研究助理进行为期三年的围绕这一主题的研究。这项研究成果将对科学和工程都产生影响。前者来自于对可破碎砂的基本特性更好地理解以及可能对其他相关可破碎颗粒材料的研究作出的贡献。后者主要体现在对工程师在可破碎土体中设计和施工土工结构能力的提升。这在香港是非常切实的，因为香港的高度风化的花岗岩和火山土壤均表现出明显的破碎特征。

120612.label: Project Title(Chinese)
120612.value: 云环境下的虚拟数据中心的动态重配置

120612.label: Project Objectives
120612.value: To derive an appropriate timing for resource defragmentation and select a set of existing VDCs for re-provisioning. VDC re-provisioning, on the one hand, can improve the performance of the data center. On the other hand, excessive VDC re-provisioning may lead to undesirable effects that increase the re-provisioning cost. To address the tradeoff, algorithm designs and experiments will be conducted to identify both the appropriate timing for resource defragmentation and the set of affected VDCs, where the benefit of re-provisioning these VDCs can offset the re-provisioning cost. To design a maintenance schedule with the aim of minimizing the number of affected VDCs and the cost for re-provisioning those affected VDCs. In general, preventive maintenance allows the system to decide when it is the best time to conduct the maintenance as long as it is done before a deadline. In this project, we will explore such flexibility and design an optimal maintenance schedule so that the minimum number of VDCs will be affected and the re-provisioning cost is minimized. To provision newly arrived VDC requests with the awareness of the given maintenance schedule in the future. Maintenance schedule may make it mandatory to re-provision some VDCs if the maintenance period is within the life span of such VDCs. We can proactively consider the unavailability of the servers and/or network components to be maintained when provisioning new VDCs with the aim to reduce the future re-provisioning cost. To optimally allocate backup power supply and gradually recovered power after a power outage to support the best set of VDCs. Following a power outage, the cloud data center runs in a partial operation mode until the power supply comes back in full. In this project, we will study the optimal re-provisioning of VDCs to minimize the violation of SLAs and re-provisioning cost. To this end, we take into account the backup power schedule, gradually recovered power supply, and the option of downgrading some VDCs.
