120612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
120612.value: With the rapid development in recent years, cloud computing technologies have enabled more efficient, flexible and collaborative computing models. In cloud computing, one of the most important service models is infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS), which allows a large number of application service providers to share the same physical infrastructure. To implement IaaS, a cloud data center usually hosts hundreds of virtual data centers (VDCs) with various sizes and service level agreements (SLAs). With the dynamic creation, resizing, and termination of VDCs, there are many open issues and major challenges to efficiently and dynamically provision and re-provision VDCs in a cloud data center. In this proposal, we will address these timely and challenging issues. In particular, we will study the following scenarios. Firstly, the dynamic creation, resizing, and termination of VDCs often result in the fragmentation of cloud resources. To optimize the system performance, it is essential to defragment resources by VDC re-provisioning. Nevertheless, it is very challenging to understand and manage the tradeoff between the re-provisioning cost and the performance improvement of both the cloud data center and VDCs. Secondly, to ensure high availability of the cloud infrastructure, a cloud data center often needs to conduct periodical software and hardware maintenance. During the period of maintenance, some affected VDCs must be re-provisioned to ensure the smooth running of such VDCs. Thus, one big challenge is to find the optimal timing to conduct the required maintenance activities before their deadlines and to minimize the disruption to VDCs. Thirdly, following a power outage, a cloud data center will be running under a limited power budget before the power supply comes back in full. In this scenario, a major challenge is how to minimize the violation of SLAs. This involves integrated backup power scheduling, selectively downgrading of VDC performance, and VDC re-provisioning. In summary, this project will investigate how to optimize dynamic VDC re-provisioning, whenever it is appropriate or mandatory, to achieve high utility of the cloud data center and to provide the best possible SLAs. We expect to develop solutions to empower the cloud service providers to make the appropriate decisions under various situations, i.e., to balance the tradeoffs between the cost of dynamic VDC re-provisioning and the system performance. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to systematically study VDC re-provisioning in a cloud data center. 云计算的一个很重要的服务模型是允许多租户共享同一个物理平台。 在这个服务模型下， 一个云服务的提供商可能同时支持数以百计的虚拟数据中心。这个课题旨在研究在虚拟数据中心的动态构建、调整和终止的过程中，如何有效地动态地提供虚拟数据中心的资源。 具体来说， 我们将研究以下几个场景。 首先，虚拟数据中心的动态构建、调整和终止经常会导致云环境里的资源碎片。通过对虚拟数据中心的资源重分配以实现碎片整理对优化系统的性能变得很重要。 当然，在碎片整理的过程中， 我们需要研究并均衡考虑虚拟数据中心的资源重分配的代价与系统性能提高之间的关系。 其次，为了保证云计算服务平台的高可靠性，数据中心需要进行周期性的软/硬件维护工作。在系统维护期间，某些受影响的虚拟数据中心将需要进行资源重分配以保证其平滑的运行性能。因此，一个重要的研究课题将是如何为系统维护找到最优时间点，以使其在维护最后期限内完成并且最小化其对虚拟数据中心运行的影响。 第三方面， 当系统电力能源断供/短缺时， 数据中心将在电力紧缺的情况下运行直到系统电力全面恢复。在这种情况下，主要的研究难点将是如何最小化对提供商和用户之间签订的服务等级协议的负面影响。这将涉及到一体化的备用电力调度方案，选择性降低虚拟数据中心的运行性能，和虚拟数据中心的资源重分配。 总体来说，这个研究项目将研究如何（在适当的或强制的时机）优化动态虚拟数据中心的资源重分配，从而达到较高的系统资源利用率和尽可能高的服务质量。 我们期望找到多种有效方案以帮助云服务提供商在不同应用环境下做出恰当的决策， 例如如何在动态虚拟数据中心的资源重分配代价与系统的总体性能之间达到有效平衡。据我们所知，这是目前第一个尝试系统性的研究云计算环境下虚拟数据中心资源重分配问题的研究计划。

120612.label: Realisation of objectives
120612.value: There are four objectives in this project and we have successfully achieved all four objectives. The detailed report is as follows. The first objective is to derive an appropriate timing for resource defragmentation and select a set of existing VDCs for re-provisioning. Resource fragmentation happens because a cloud service provider needs to dynamically create and terminate a large number of virtual machines (VMs). Fragmented resources are difficult to be further utilized. To solve this problem proactively, most existing studies have been based on server consolidation, with the main objective of minimizing the number of active servers. Although this approach can minimize resource fragmentation at a particular time, it may be over aggressive at the price of too frequent VM migration and low system stability. To address this issue, we propose a novel provident resource defragmentation framework that is revenue-oriented with the goal to reduce unnecessary VM migration. Within the proposed framework, we formulate an optimization problem for resource defragmentation at a particular time epoch, with the consideration of the future impact of any VM migration. We then develop an efficient heuristic algorithm that can obtain near-optimal results. Extensive numerical results confirm that our framework can provide the highest profit and can significantly reduce the VM migration cost in practical scenarios. The work has been accepted to be published in IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computing. Since both objective 2 and object 3 are related to coordinated resource provisioning and preventive maintenance scheduling, we will report three problems that we have studied under these two objectives together. As for the first problem, given the available resources in a data center and the required maintenance activities with maintenance deadlines, we consider the joint VM provisioning and maintenance scheduling problem to maximize the revenue of the data center. We tackle the problem by firstly considering the resource provisioning under a given maintenance schedule. We propose a heuristic algorithm for such a case which can achieve a constant approximation ratio when no VM migration is allowed. Using such a heuristic algorithm as the building block, we then propose another heuristic algorithm to solve the joint resource provisioning and maintenance scheduling problem and also derive its upper-bound. Extensive simulations have shown that our proposed heuristic algorithms can effectively maximize the revenue of the data center. The work provides the guidelines for data center operators on how to conduct the proper preventive maintenance while mitigating the disruption to the VMs in the system. The work has been published in the proceedings of IEEE INFOCOM 2013. As for the second problem, considering the increasing system stress and the higher cost brought by the unplanned downtime events which are mainly caused by untimely preventive maintenances, besides the objective of maximizing the revenue of the data center as in the first problem, we also intend to find out the appropriate starting time to implement preventive maintenance activities. Specifically, we aim to carry on the maintenances as early as possible so that it can minimize the negative effect brought by the unplanned downtime events such as server failures. We propose the novel heuristic for the problem solving. Sufficient simulation results verify the effectiveness of our heuristic algorithm in the aspect of thwarting the server failure events and also preserving the high system revenues. This paper has been under review at IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing. As for the third problem, different from previous two problems where preventive maintenances are considered individually, we consider the preventive maintenance in the batch way where multiple units of available resources in the cloud data center can be maintained simultaneously through one batch. Such new kind of maintenance scheme can contribute a lot to the cost savings of maintenance activities due to the fact that the system-scale maintenances can be completed by applying just a few numbers of batches if scheduled appropriately. Moreover, with the early starting time of batches, the maintenance costs can be reduced even further. Therefore, in this problem, given the available resources in a data center and the initial resource provisioning of VMs, we aim to implement the system-scale maintenances as early as possible through the minimal number of maintenance batches. And such maintenance scheduling should be optimized without affecting the service continuity of cloud tenants. We propose a novel heuristic to solve the problem and also derive the problem lower-bound. Extensive simulation results verify the efficiency of our heuristic algorithm which can well achieve the problem lower-bound. The result has been published in IEEE Communication Letters. The last objective is to optimally allocate backup power supply and gradually recovered power after a power outage to support the best set of VDCs/VMs. In cloud computing, it is crucial to maintain service continuity, while power outage is one of the most common but serious threats. To improve the resilience of cloud against power outage, a service provider usually deploys emergency energy supply (e.g., UPSs and generator) in a data center, and may replicate services to other data centers soon after the outage occurs. However, there is a lack of theoretical study that addresses how to efficiently exploit these two approaches during power outage, which is very challenging not only because the energy supply can be limited, but also because each service can require a distinct service duration in the affected data center. We tackle this challenge and investigate the cloud service continuity problem. Specifically, we consider that revenue is associated with maintaining the continuity of a service, denoted as service continuity revenue. Based on that we first formulate an optimization problem that aims to maximize the total revenue subject to energy constrains. After showing the hardness of the problem, we focus on the design of approximation algorithms for solving the problem, where we consider two practical cases. In the first one with sufficient number of servers for re-provision, we develop a constant approximation algorithm of which the worst-case performance approaches the optimal solution within a constant factor (≈ 4.5-6.4). In the second one, we consider the general case with limited number of servers for re-provision, and we develop an approximation algorithm with approximately 5.7- 8 of approximation ratio. By combining these two algorithms together, we can achieve both good worst-case performance and average performance. Trace-driven experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can lead to near optimal solution in various scenarios. The work is currently under review at IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking. In carrying the project, we find out that the dynamic formation and deformation of platoons in vehicular networks share the similarities with the aforementioned problems, so we have also studied how to use mobile cloud to assist the communications and message delivery of vehicular networks. The results have been published in IEEE Communication Surveys & Tutorials, IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology, and Transportation Research Part C.

120612.label: Major findings and research outcome
120612.value: To design resource provisioning strategies under disruptions brought by preventive maintenance and power outage is important to cloud service providers. The research outputs generated from this project provide solutions for cloud service providers to face the aforementioned disruptions. One main finding of this project is that we have developed algorithms with constant approximation ratios to find the best strategies of running VMs to maximize the revenue with the limited backup energy when power outage happens. This will provide very useful operation insights for cloud service providers under the critical situation of power outage.

120612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
120612.value: Though there are many disruptions to operating clouds, most of them share the natures of the disruptions studied in this project. We will work with China Telecom through the joint lab between China Telecom research institute and CityU to see how to adopt and adapt the results generated from this project to solve the real problems that they are facing in operating clouds.

120612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
120612.value: This project studies how to efficiently provision resources subject to planned or unplanned disruptions. In particular, we have studied how to provision resources taking the planned preventive maintenance scheduling and unplanned power outage into consideration. Besides that, we have also studied how to re-provision resources so that fragmented resource can be further utilized.

121212.label: Project Objectives
121212.value: We aim to evaluate the potentials, to analyze the behaviors and to improve the performance of SiNW-based MOS transistors for future CMOS technology. 121212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
121212.value: According to the prediction made by the International Technology Roadmap for Semiconductor (ITRS), the downsizing of the metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) transistor will go on for some more decades and eventually sub-decananometer gate length MOS transistor will be used in future semiconductor manufacturing. However, new device structures and new fabrication processes are to be developed in order to maintain this trend. Silicon nanowire (SiNW) MOS transistors are considered to be the most promising devices for the ultimate technology node in the sub-decananometer range due to their simple fabrication process and excellent immunity to short-channel effects. However, many properties of this new type of transistor are still unexplored and some of the device characteristics, as well as its fabrication process, still need tremendous improvements before this type of device can be used in actual integration circuit (IC) manufacturing. This work aims at fabricating and characterizing SiNW MOS transistors. Based on the proposed experiments, we shall develop some optimal processes for the device fabrication; we shall also develop some theoretical models to explain and to predict the performances of the transistors so as to provide useful guidelines for designing high-performance SiNW MOS device and rules for its applications in future CMOS integrated circuits. 在未来的十年内，用于半导体集成电路制造的MOS器件的沟道长度将缩小至十纳米以下。要达到这一发展趋势，就需要引进新材料和新结构。硅纳米线堆晶体管SiNW MOS被认为是达致这一极限器件结构的最有前途的方案。但是，现在我们对很多SiNW MOS的特性还不是很清楚，而且它的制造工艺还需要不断的细化和改良，才能和现有的集成电路制造技术相结合。本研究的目的在于深入分析SiNW MOS器件的特性及其制造工艺，为将来的高性能SiNW MOS集成电路提供实用的器件模型和设计方案。

121212.label: Realisation of objectives
121212.value: This project aims to evaluate the potentials, to analyze the behaviors and to improve the performance of SiNW-based MOS transistors for future CMOS technology. Most of the project objectives have been achieved completely or have been achieved to a great extend. This work led to 9 technical publications in international peer-reviewed journals (including 3 papers under minor revision) and a number of conference presentations. The major achievements are grouped into three subject areas for the future CMOS technology and are highlighted below: (a) Process development for nano CMOS technology One of the objectives of this project is to optimize the fabrication technique for the proposed multiple-SiNW MOS transistor in various aspects, including material and process selection, as well as the fine tuning of the processing conditions. The key process involved in the realization of SiNW transistor include (1) Stacked nanowire preparation; (2) Source/drain doping; and (3) Gate stack deposition. For the first two key processes, the co-investigator Hiroshi Iwai’s team has developed some optimal processes for the device fabrication. We adopt these techniques with minor modifications in our device fabrication. To achieve subnanometer EOT gate dielectric film for nanowire transistor applications, it is still an extremely challenging issue in particular in the aspects of metal/high-k interface, and high-k/silicon interface, and thermal stability of gate stack. In this work we have conducted extensively on the process optimization for preparing La-based subnanometer EOT high-k gate dielectric films. A lot of useful results are obtained. CeO2/La2O3 stacked dielectric was found to have lower amount oxygen vacancies and can enhance the device reliability considerably. We studied the effects of high-temperature annealing on the gate stack. We found that the thermal process can enhance O, Ce, La, and Si diffusion and result in the intermixing of CeO2/La2O3 stack, growth of interfacial silicates layer at the La2O3/Si interface. A small amount of Ce3+ reoxidation and significant interface oxidation were found for thermal annealing at 600 °C. We also studied the impacts of thermal annealing on the interfacial reactions and bonding structures between the tungsten metal gate and CeO2/La2O3 stacked dielectrics were investigated by x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurements. We found that the amount of W oxidation increases with the depth closer to the CeO2 layer. In addition, as the annealing temperature increases to 600 °C, out-diffusion of Ce and La atoms to the bulk W, leading to the formation of Ce-O-W or La-O-W phases at the W/CeO2-La2O3 transition layer, were observed. These observations indicate that the high temperature annealing would not only lead to a significant oxidation of tungsten film, but also promote the material intermixing at W/CeO2 interface. The mechanisms of interfacial reactions and their effect on EOT were discussed. These results have great technical impacts on the nanowire transistor fabrication. However, as we have spent a lot of efforts and time in these studies and as the first batch of nanowire transistors was delayed, the high-k integration has not been realized yet. We are looking for the possibility for further study in the aspect in future. (b) Device characterization The carrier transport mechanisms, the device characteristics, and the reliability issues of the SiNW MOS transistors were studied in detail. We observed different geometry and temperature dependencies of electrical characteristics of silicon nanowire transistors with gate length of a couple microns. Several abnormal characteristics degradation were also observed. In particular, charge transport along the corners/boundaries of the nanowires may enhance or degrade the device characteristics depending on the gate length and nanowire sizes. Current enhancements were observed because of the higher mobility and larger density of states at the corners where the surface states have opposite effects on these parameters. Temperature dependence of the threshold voltage shows a linear decrease as the temperature increases. This trend is ascribed to the charge states at oxide/nanowire interfaces. Hence corners and surfaces of nanowire thus should play an important role for ultra-short nanowire transistors and that calls for shape of nanowire optimation for device design. (c) Computer simulation and compact model development Based on the experimental results as well as on computer simulations, we have developed some compact models for describing the current-voltage characteristics of this kind of devices. This model is important for process evaluation, device and circuit designs. A physically based subthreshold current model for silicon nanowire transistors working in the ballistic regime was developed. This model is based on the electric potential distribution obtained from a 2D Poisson equation and by performing some perturbation approximations for subband energy levels. Our results further revealed that the top of barrier (ToB) approximation is not accurate enough at large gate and drain biases; tunneling current and better electrostatic model have to be taken into account. Our models agree well with TCAD simulation with different geometries and under different biasing conditions. We also developed analytical model for tunneling source nanowire transistor (TFET). The model was derived by dividing the source, drain and channel regions into several portions so that some simple approximations for the surface potential across the tunneling junction and the channel can be achieved. Tunneling current is then calculated analytically by integrating the generation rate using the developed surface potential expressions over different regions. The results are verified with TCAD simulations and good agreements were obtained.

121212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
121212.value: Due to the delay in sample fabrication and the constraint of fabrication facility as well, the fabrication process for nanowire transistors has not been fully optimized yet. In the device characterization aspect, further investigation on the fabricated nanowire transistors in particular the reliability study such as high-current stressing is under investigation.

121512.label: Project Objectives
121512.value: AKE under Bad or Resettable Randomness – it has been known as a real threat to some computing devices such as smart cards, and computing environment such as Virtual Machines in cloud computing, that random coins in different sessions of AKE protocols could be maliciously controlled or reused, which result in making many of the existing AKE protocols insecure in this kind of hostile models. This objective involves the investigation of existing AKE security models such as BR, CK, CK-HMQV, eCK, seCK and so on, existing AKE protocols such as signature based, encryption based, Diffie-Hellman key exchange based (e.g. (H)MQV and its variants), explicitly authenticated (three-pass), and implicitly authenticated (two-pass or one-pass) AKE protocols, new AKE security models for maliciously controlled and/or resettable randomness, and new constructions of AKE protocols which can be proven secure in the new models with bad or resettable randomness captured. State and Randomness Leakage Resilient Password-based AKE (PAKE) – due to the low entropy of passwords which are the long-term secrets in a password-based AKE (PAKE), it has been a challenge to construct or model a secure PAKE with session state reveal or ephemeral secret leakage attacks considered. Negative results found in the literature also showed that pure PAKE protocols do not exist if ephemeral secrets of test sessions can be compromised. It is unknown if a hybrid setting in which a PAKE protocol is used in conjunction with long-term cryptographic keys can defend against session state or ephemeral secret leakage attacks while this hybrid setting is also the most commonly used one in practice (for example, web-based email login or remote access to a secure cloud computing/storage service) than pure PAKE protocols. The objective of this aspect is to study the construction and security models for PAKE protocols in hybrid settings under various leakage models which include session state reveal, ephemeral secret leakage, and bad or reused randomness. Privacy-Preserving AKE Protocols for Secure Roaming – identities of communicating parties of an AKE protocol are generally sent in clear. For protocols, such as IKE main mode or encryption-based IKE aggressive mode, where the identities are protected, they only consider the user privacy of each session individually. The untraceability may not be guaranteed when an entity carry out an anonymous AKE protocol with different entities while traveling around. We study and construct privacy-preserving AKE protocols which allow entities to roam around heterogeneous networks without letting other entities to find out the whereabouts or trace multiple sessions involving the same entity even if other entities collude. Various state and randomness leakage models are to be considered, and constructing highly efficient, such as one-pass or two-pass privacy-preserving AKE protocols for secure roaming is our objective.

The objective of this aspect is to study the construction and security models for PAKE protocols in hybrid settings under various leakage models which include session state reveal, ephemeral secret leakage, and bad or reused randomness.

121512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
121512.value: 認證密鑰交換（AKE）一直以來都是密碼學領域內的一個重要研究課題。隨著新的計算環境（如雲計算中的虛擬化和不斷增長的用戶隱私意識等）的不斷湧現，使用惡意控制的或重用的隨機信息的新攻擊已經成為現實威脅，而且新的安全性要求（例如異構網路上的隱私保護通信）也已經成為需要實現的首要特徵。例如，雲計算中的虛擬機惡意重啟已經被證實是一個嚴重安全威脅，能夠導致認證金鑰切換式通訊協定的主密鑰的洩漏。 在這個項目中，我們主要研究認證密鑰交換通訊協定的兩個方面：（1）形式化（基於口令的）認證密鑰交換的安全模型，並設計相應的認證密鑰交換通訊協定，使其能夠抵抗各種洩漏相關攻擊（包括會話狀態揭示、臨時密鑰洩漏、壞的／重用的隨機信息等）；（2）研究具有隱私保護的認證密鑰交換協定，這種協定能夠在一個實體與異構網路中的多個不同實體執行認證密鑰交換協定的多個會話時保證通信實體的不可追蹤性和匿名性。由於用戶能夠方便的在各種無線網路（例如4G蜂窩數據網和WiFI熱點）之間漫遊，這種異構網路在當前正變的越來越普遍。 作為密碼學中一個持續興起的領域，認證密鑰交換面臨著許多新的安全威脅，也有大量的有意義的研究問題需要解決。考慮到這些問題在理論研究和實際應用中的重要意義，以及我們研究團隊的專業能力，我們將專注於認證密鑰交換中這些問題的研究。

121512.label: Realisation of objectives
121512.value: All the three project objectives have been achieved, thanks to the financial support of this grant. Throughout the project, two PhD students have been trained and graduated. The research results have been published, and 7 journal papers together with 2 conference papers have been published, that include IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security, Theoretical Computer Science, and RSA Conference, Cryptographers' Track. On the first objective, we successfully formalize a suite of security models which capture the bad or resettable randomness, and devised efficient key establishment protocols that satisfy the security requirements. For the second objective, leakage resilient security model has been considered, and a collection of provably secure schemes have been proposed. For the last objective, new privacy preserving mechanisms have been proposed and shown to be able to effectively protect the identity of the entities.

121512.label: Major findings and research outcome
121512.value: In the paper on three-party password-based key exchange protocol with formal verification, we considered the leakage resilient scenario in the three-party setting, and proposed an efficient password-based key exchange protocol, which can be shown secure through formal verification. The result has been further formalized and a new identity-based identification technique was proposed which not only is secure against various leakage resilient scenarios but is also secure even if some randomness sources are controlled by adversaries. The results above have been further enhanced so that it can support anonymous roaming. In the paper on privacy-preserving mobile roaming authentication with security proof in global mobile networks, we considered the roaming scenario in a heterogeneous environment and proposed an efficient scheme which can perform multi-party mutual authentication while ensuring the anonymity of a roaming entity. Recently in the paper on a DFA-based functional proxy re-encryption scheme for secure public cloud data sharing, we further formalized the bad randomness and leakage resilient in the setting of secure sharing over public cloud, and proposed a provably secure scheme under the models we defined.

121512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
121512.value: Post-quantum cryptography is an important research direction in information security. We plan to extend our research results so that we can formalize and propose schemes which are secure in the post-quantum era. Potential areas that we plan to investigate include lattice-based cryptographic techniques under the bad randomness and leakage scenarios.

121512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
121512.value: The research results obtained in this project help enhance our understanding of the security of a computer systems in the real world. This is because in reality, the secret keys are generated from some random sources, which are not truly random, instead, the sources could be partially controlled by an adversary. In this scenario, we investigate a formal way to analyze the security of a crypto-system and propose new techniques which allow us to ensure the security of the system. Furthermore, we also study another real-world scenario where the secret keys are partially leaked, for example, due to partial memory leak, and we propose new methods for renewing the keys and reducing the damage caused by the leakage of some keying materials.

122212.label: Project Objectives
122212.value:  Real-time high resolution depth sensing We propose to first upsample the low resolution depth images captured by an active depth camera using the corresponding high resolution RGB images captured by a passive stereo camera. The new method promises an edge-aware, real-time and accurate solution to range data upsampling problem.  Fast motion depth sensing Active depth camera motion deblurring will be also considered in this project. We propose to use the images captured by the passive stereo camera to estimate the point spread function (PSF) in the active depth camera. The estimated PSF will be used to deblur the depth image using existing image deconvolution algorithms. The result of the second phase of the project will be a depth sensing system capable of capturing fast motion.  Robust depth sensing The final phase of the project involves integrating the upsampled and deblurred depth images into an energy minimization framework, combining the advantages of active depth sensing and passive stereo. The output will be a depth sensing system that is robust to low texture and highly textured regions, and has wide measurement range.

122212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
122212.value: 这一研究项目的结果将是一个强大的和高效率的深度感测系统。系统可以用于在计算机视觉和计算机图形包括几何结构中的各种任务重建，机器人技术，人机交互和混合现实。 基于所使用的传感器，可用深度感测技术可分为两类： 主动和被动的深度感测方法。有源主动式传感器发出的能量向着目标 调查。然后，从目标反射的能量被检测到，由传感器测量的。被动 传感器，在另一方面，不具有自己的能量源，并可以使用，只有当 自然发生的能量可用。 通过主动和被动传感器提供的信息，在很大程度上是互补的。有源传感器需要一个比较大的量的能量充分照亮目标的生成，因此，一般的低分辨率，敏感的纹理区域，容易受到运动模糊，并具有短的测量范围。相比之下，无源传感器的高分辨率，支持的纹理，并有小的运动模糊和宽的测量范围。 我们提出协同创建国家的最先进的深度结合被动式和主动式传感器 传感系统，具有以下优点： 1）实时高分辨率的深度感测 我们建议以提高捕获由一个活跃的深度的深度图像的空间分辨率 相机使用高解析度的被动立体相机。新方法有望edgeaware， 上采样问题的一系列数据的实时和准确的解决方案。 2）快速运动的深度感测 该项目下调查活动的深度相机运动去模糊问题。我们建议 使用由被动立体照相机拍摄的图像来估计点扩散 函数在有源深度相机。该项目的第二阶段的结果将是一个 深度感测系统，能够捕捉快速运动。 3）快速运动的深度感测 该项目下调查活动的深度相机运动去模糊问题。我们建议使用由被动立体照相机拍摄的图像来估计点扩散函数在有源深度相机。该项目的第二阶段的结果将是一个深度感测系统，能够捕捉快速motion.Robust深度检测最后阶段的项目涉及集成上采样和去模糊的深度图像到能量最小化的框架中的作用深度检测相结合的优势，和被动式立体。输出将是一个低纹理的鲁棒性的深度感测系统且极具质感的地区，并拥有广泛的测量范围。 在此建议的初步结果发表在诉讼的IEEE国际研讨会多媒体信号处理2010（MMSP'10），IEEE计算机会议视觉与模式识别2010年和2007年（CVPR'10和07）和IEEE交易模式分析与机器智能2009（PAMI'09）。

122212.label: Realisation of objectives
122212.value: Objective 1: Real-time high resolution depth sensing We develop a new upsampling method to enhance the spatial resolution of depth images. Given a low-resolution depth image from an active depth sensor and a potentially high-resolution color image from a passive RGB camera, we formulate it as an adaptive cost aggregation problem and solve it using the bilateral filter. The formulation synergistically combines the median filter and the bilateral filter; thus it better preserves the depth edges and is more robust to noise. Using adaptive weights computed from a registered high-resolution RGB image based on a joint bilateral filter operation, the developed weighted median filter based upsampling method can upsample 160 × 120 depth image to VGA size at a rate of 1200 Hertz with few noticeable errors. We also develop a minimum spanning tree (MST) based upsampling method. We extra an MST from the high-resolution color image, and then use the MST to upsample the low resolution depth image. Unlike exiting methods, the developed MST-based method is good at preserving the shape of the thin-structure objects. The significant improvement resides in the non-local property of the developed algorithm and the new similarity measurement on an MST. They ensure accurate location information for depth seeds that are reliable to a miss-sampled pixel (even if they are far away) and can effectively filter out depth seeds that are non-related but close to a miss-sampled pixel. Although edge-preserving filters can use the color (edges) as the guidance to upsample the low-resolution depth image in order to preserve the depth edges, the color edges do not always align well with the depth edges, especially around textured regions. Unlike previous manually-designed edge-preserving filters, we use deep convolutional neural network to learn a filter kernel utilizing both the dense/high-resolution color and the sparse/low-resolution depth information. The use of deep CNN can better extract the mutual information between the low-resolution depth image and the high-resolution color image. Objective 2: Fast motion depth sensing Time-of-flight (TOF) depth sensor normally contains visible noise and the noise can present a serious problem in motion deblurring. We thus develop a new non-reference image quality metric that can be adopted by the state-of-the-art image/video denoising algorithms for auto-denoising. The developed metric is extremely simple and can be implemented in four lines of Matlab code. The developed metric aims at maximizing the structure similarity between the input noisy image and the estimated image noise around homogeneous regions and the structure similarity between the input noisy image and the denoised image around highly-structured regions, and is computed as the linear correlation coefficient of the two corresponding structure similarity maps. Numerous experimental results demonstrate that the developed metric not only outperforms the current state-of-the-art non-reference quality metric quantitatively and qualitatively, but also better maintains temporal coherence when used for video denoising. The major study for this work is reported in [2]. Our original plan was deblurring low-cost depth sensors. However, the latest TOF depth sensors have powerful illuminators and do not have noticeable motion blur any more. Indeed, the motion blur is more obvious in RGB cameras because most of the TOF sensors can only be used in the indoor environment. As a result, we have to give up this topic. Objective 3: Robust depth sensing In low-texture regions, the lack of visual features makes depth from stereo matching a challenging problem. Matching cost aggregation is a fundamental step in stereo matching. While effective and efficient, cost aggregation methods typically aggregate the matching cost by summing/averaging over a user-specified, local support region. This is obviously only locally-optimal, and the computational complexity of the full-kernel implementation usually depends on the region size. The cost aggregation problem is re-examined and a non-local solution is developed. The matching cost values are aggregated adaptively based on pixel similarity on a tree structure derived from the stereo image pair to preserve depth edges. The nodes of this tree are all the image pixels, and the edges are all the edges between the nearest neighboring pixels. The similarity between any two pixels is decided by their shortest distance on the tree. The developed method is non-local as every node receives supports from all other nodes on the tree. It is theoretically better than traditional local solutions for low texture regions. This is straightforward as the window used by the local methods cannot guarantee to cover the whole low textured region. As can be expected, the developed non-local solution outperforms all local cost aggregation methods on the standard (Middlebury) benchmark. Besides, it has great advantage in extremely low computational complexity: only a total of 2 addition/subtraction operations and 3 multiplication operations are required for each pixel at each disparity level. It is very close to the complexity of unnormalized box filtering using integral image which requires 6 addition/subtraction operations. Unnormalized box filter is the fastest local cost aggregation method but blurs across depth edges. The developed method was tested on a MacBook Air laptop computer with a 1.8 GHz Intel Core i7 CPU and 4 GB memory. The average runtime on the Middlebury data sets is about 90 milliseconds. Alternatively, we develop a new bilateral filtering method specially designed for practical stereo vision systems. Parallel algorithms are preferred in these systems due to the real-time performance requirement. Edge-preserving filters like the bilateral filter have been demonstrated to be very effective for high-quality local stereo matching. A hardware-efficient bilateral filter is thus developed. When moved to an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 580 GPU, it can process a one megapixel color image at around 417 frames per second. This filter can be directly used for cost aggregation required in any local stereo matching algorithm. Quantitative evaluation shows that it outperforms all the other local stereo methods both in terms of accuracy and speed on Middlebury benchmark. It ranks 12 out of over 120 methods on Middlebury data sets, and the average runtime (including the matching cost computation, occlusion handling and post processing) is only 15 milliseconds (67 frames per second). Traditional stereo matching algorithms were obtained based on the intensity consistency assumption, i.e., the intensity should be the same in both images if it corresponds to the same world point in the scene. In practice, there will be radiometric differences caused by exposure and illumination changes. The most popular affine illumination invariant similarity measure is Normalized Cross-Correlation. It is used in many other vision tasks besides stereo matching. However, it suffers from the fattening effect around occlusions. We develop a new similarity measure that outperforms the state of the art in terms of both accuracy and speed. It is invariant to global and local affine illumination changes and is valid only for Lambertian scenes. The similarity measure is derived as follows: 1) finding an optimal local affine transform at every correspondence based on local linear model; 2) computing the similarity according to the affine transform. The computation of the affine transform is formulated as an image filtering problem that can be solved efficiently and effectively using edge-preserving filters like the tree filter [5] we developed. The computational complexity of the tree filter is the same as the box filter.

122212.label: Major findings and research outcome
122212.value: Three novel depth/disparity upsampling algorithms were developed (see Part C 8.1, 8.5 and 9.4). A new non-reference image quality metric that can be adopted by the state-of-the-art image/video denoising algorithms for auto-denoising was developed (see Part C 9.2). Two real-time stereo matching algorithms were developed (see Part C 8.4 and 8.5). An edge-preserving filter named tree filter was developed, based on with a novel stereo matching algorithm which is robust to illumination changes was developed (see Part C 8.2 and 8.6). Efficient sparse and dense motion estimation algorithms were developed (see Part C 9.1 and 9.3).

It has many direct applications like 3D digital mapping, auto-driving, 3D movie and computer game, city modelling. It is also very important for virtual reality, next generation computer human interaction techniques, training and simulation applications for emergency management, civil protection, disaster control, and security.

122512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
122512.value: The min-sum product (also known as min-plus product, distance matrix product, and distance matrix multiplication) is a fundamental operation that has many applications in computer science. It is well known that the min-sum product problem is equivalent to the all-pair shortest paths problem. The time complexity of the best-known algorithm for computing the min-sum product of two matrices in the worst case is only slightly better than cubic time by a poly-logarithmic factor. A truly sub-cubic algorithm for the min-sum product problem in the worst case is a long-standing open problem. In this project, we will focus on the average-case time complexity of the min-sum product problem. Some recent work in the literature showed that min-sum product can be computed significantly faster than cubic time in the average case. However, there is still a gap between the expected running time of those algorithms and the trivial quadratic lower bound. We aim to develop faster algorithms for random inputs that are distributed according to different distributions. Experimental evaluations will be conducted to test the performances of the algorithms in real-world applications. 距離矩陣乘法是電腦科學領域的一種重要計算，可以用來計算全點對最短路徑。該計算問題的已知最快算法只比三次方的複雜度好一點。長期以來，人們一直在尋找完全比三次方複雜度快的算法。 在這個研究課題中，我們主要研究該計算問題的平均算法複雜度。我們的研究目標是找出在隨機輸入的情況下的更快的算法，並且在實際問題中利用新算法更快地完成計算。

We have finished this part quite early during the project span. 2. Develop faster algorithms for random inputs in different probability distribution models. We achieved this goal and the results are published in ISAAC 2015. 3. Conduct experimental evaluations of the developed algorithms in real-world applications. We did the experimental evaluation and the result is published in ISAAC 2015. 4. Design parallel algorithms on the GPU (graphics processing unit). For this objective, we did try to make our sequential algorithm parallel by replacing the sorting part by parallel algorithms. The time performance is better on a multi-core CPU. However, we didn't have GPU and therefore didn't try in on GPU.

122512.label: Major findings and research outcome
122512.value: We study the average-case complexity of min-sum product of matrices, which is a fundamental operation that has many applications in computer science. We focus on optimizing the number of “algebraic” operations (i.e., operations involving real numbers) used in the computation, since such operations are usually expensive in various environments. We present an algorithm that can compute the min-sum product of two n×n real matrices using only O(n^2) algebraic operations, given that the matrix elements are drawn independently and identically from some fixed probability distribution satisfying several constraints. This improves the previously best known upper-bound of O(n^2 log n). The class of probability distributions under which our algorithm works include many important and commonly used distributions, such as uniform distributions, exponential distributions, and folded normal distributions. In order to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm, we performed experiments to compare the running time of the proposed algorithm with previous algorithms proposed by others. The experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm achieves significant performance improvement over the previous algorithms. We also tried parallel algorithms and observed some improvement in time spent on the algorithm.

122512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
122512.value: Although our algorithm is asymptotically better compared to previous works, the simulation advance of our algorithm is not much better than other algorithms. One way to improve this is to select a better threshold value to decide the division of numbers. If certain accuracy can be sacrificed, there may be faster algorithms to calculate the result. This direction is especially meaningful in the big data era where the size of data is too large. Sampling method may be used in this scenario.

122512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
122512.value: The min-sum product (also known as min-plus product, distance matrix product, and distance matrix multiplication) is a fundamental operation that has many applications in computer science. The most notable application is to use the min-sum product to compute all-pair shortest paths. The time complexity of the best-known algorithm for computing the min-sum product of two matrices in the worst case is only slightly better than the cubic time by a poly-logarithmic factor. A truly sub-cubic algorithm for the min-sum product problem in the worst case is a long-standing open problem. In a practical application of the min-sum product problem, the average-case time complexity is more interesting, because the worst cases are unlikely to happen. Some recent work in the literature showed that the min-sum product can be computed significantly faster than cubic time in the average case. However, there is still a gap between the expected running time of those algorithms and the trivial quadratic lower bound. In this project, we improve the state-of-the-art of the min-sum product problem in the average case. We develop faster algorithms for random inputs that are distributed according to different distributions. Experimental evaluations are conducted to test the performances of the algorithms in real-world applications.

122612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
122612.value: Polymeric materials have been widely used in our daily applications. In building fires, many of such materials are prompt to ignition and burning resulting in actively involvement in flame spread and combustion generating enormous amounts of heat and smoke which impair escapes of building occupants and rescue operations of fire brigades causing injuries and fatalities. Flame-retardant polymeric materials are often deployed to alleviating hazards. Traditional halogen-based flame-retardants were proven to be harmful to environment as such strict abatement or prohibitions of their applications are imposed in many countries and areas. Recently, advancements have been made to using nano-phosphorus based flame-retardants for polymers such as polystyrene which is one of the most commonly used polymers in our daily life. Research studies revealed that such flame-retardant technique improves the fire retardancy, environmental-friendliness; promotes char formation; enhances mechanical and anesthetic properties of polystyrene. In this research, state-of-the-art, comprehensive and robust fire model based on computational fluid dynamics techniques will be developed for flame-retarded polystyrene to further understand and predict their fire characteristics and performances for full-scale applications in buildings and assist performance-based fire engineering designs. The established fire model and the associated methodology can be a generalized framework for fire behaviors and performances of other flame-retardant polymeric materials. 高分子聚合材料已廣泛被應用在我們日常生活裡。很多這種材料是會迅速燃點及燃燒的,從而引起建築物火災,造成火焰蔓延和燃燒,產生大量的熱能和煙氣,往往妨礙大廈住客逃生和消防隊伍的救援行動,引致嚴重傷亡事故。阻燃高分子材料的應用通常可以減輕火災危害。然而,基於傳統無鹵阻燃劑的阻燃高分子材料已經被證證實會導致環境破壞,在許多國家和地區,已經規定嚴格禁止或減低它們的應用。最近,使用基於納米磷阻燃劑對聚合物(如其中最常用的聚苯乙烯)方面的研究已經取得了的進步,調查研究顯示這種基於納米磷的阻燃劑的技術可提高聚苯乙烯的防火阻燃性能,減低環境破壞;促進碳層形成;增強其機械和外觀性等。在目前這項研究中,採取先進、全面和可靠的算流體動力學技術可用以研發出全新而有效的火災模型,將為納米磷阻燃聚苯乙烯的阻燃機理提供進一步瞭解,從而預測他們的在火災中的阻燃特點和性能,有利於在建築物中的全面開發及應用,並為性能化消防工程設計提供協助。長遠而言,這研發成果及火災場模型和關聯的方法可以作為研究其他阻燃聚合物材料的防火性能提供可靠和有效的框架。

122612.label: Realisation of objectives
122612.value: Objective 1: Develop a pyrolysis model for FR-PS embracing fully phase conversion, pyrolysis and char formation due fires: The three-dimensional (3-D) pyrolysis model for the phosphorus-based inherently flame-retardant PS nanocomposites (FR-PS), incorporating properties the migration of gases through the solid and molten phases to surface and their emission which involves the complex combination of the chemical and physical processes in the solid and molten phases, had been formulated. In the developed model, the pyrolysis process of FR-PS (i.e. thermal decomposition reaction) has been modelled by an Arrhenius expression. The energy conservation equation conforming to Fourier’s law for heat conduction, internal migration due to movement of volatile gases has been formulated accounting fully changes of densities of solid FR-PS, heat of conversion from solid to molten phases, mass losses of molten FR-PS, heat of pyrolysis, internal heat transfer due to conduction through the solid and molten phases and emission of the volatile gases at the surface, etc. Thermal properties of the pyrolysing FR-PS such as thermal conductivities and heat capacities have been represented by functions of solid and molten phases as well as char densities and temperature. Volatile gases were assumed to be in thermal equilibrium with the solid or molten phases, respectively. Convection and radiation heat transfer at interface of FR-PS and gaseous combustion domains were exchanged as boundary conditions. Migration of pyrolysis gaseous products (i.e. volatiles) to the surface of the FR-PS was assumed to be instantaneous and will be obtained by integration of local quantities over the pyrolysing zone. The resistance to gases migration through the solid and molten phases was assumed to be negligible. With finite volume techniques, the pyrolysis model was discretized to give a set of simultaneous linear discretised equations. A computational code had been formulated to solving numerically the pyrolysis model incorporating formulation of the surface regression of FR-PS. Objective 2: Establish the kinetics for the pyrolysis model: Experimental studies employing the Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) coupled with a Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) instrument (TG-IR) has been used to characterize the evolved gases in the thermal degradation. The TG-IR technique for the dynamical analysis has been used for continuous monitoring of both the time-dependent evolution of the gases and the weight of the residue to provide essential data for establishment of the kinetics for the pyrolysis model. These experimental studies were carried out and the key kinetics parameters of the thermal decomposition of the FR-PS had been successfully deduced. Objective 3: Develop a robust fire field model comprising pyrolysis and gas-phase combustion models: For the gaseous combustion of the FR-PS, the behavior of a turbulent buoyant fire has been modeled using Large-Eddy Simulation (LES) including coupled turbulence, combustion, soot chemistry, and radiation effects. The three-dimensional, Favre-filtered, compressible mass, momentum, energy, and mixture fraction and its scalar variance conservation equations have been closed using the Smagorinsky subgrid-scale (SGS) turbulence model. In the present gaseous combustion model, the SGS combustion model had been formulated by adopting the conserved scalar approach where the chemical reaction rates were assumed to be fast in comparison to the rate at which reactants were mixed. The mixing has been described by a conserved scalar and the instantaneous species concentrations are assumed to be functions of only the instantaneous conserved scalar. Due to nonlinearities of functions, the PDF of the conserved scalar has been employed. The mixture fraction has been selected as the conserved scalar. The relationship between the thermochemical scalar properties and mixture fraction were known as state relationships. Multi-steps chemical reactions for the reactants have been employed for the combustion process. The soot model incorporating the essential physical processes of soot nucleation, coagulation, and surface growth has been employed in the current study. Soot production has been determined predominantly by the large-scale turbulent advection, SGS turbulent diffusion, and finite-rate soot chemistry effects. Thermal radiation from combustion products and soot were solved by the filtered radiative transfer equations (FRTE) for a non-scattering gray gas using the S4 discrete ordinates method (DOM). The gray gas assumption and the S4 approximation which allowed for more efficient computations was adopted. A finite-volume method was employed to discretize the filtered governing equations. All the spatial terms were approximated via second-order central difference to ensure adequate numerical accuracy. Numerical implementation of the model was based on a two-stage predictor-corrector methodology for Low-Mach-number compressible flows. The simultaneous discretization equations were solved using the Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient method (PCG). The pyrolysis and gaseous combustion models was coupled numerically to form a 3-D computational code (i.e. 3-D Fire Model) for burning of the FR-PS. Objective 4: Perform fire experiments for FR-PS samples at various fire scenarios and validate the fire field model with the experimental results: In order to understand the FR-PS burning characteristics and further validate the LESFR3D fire model for FR-PS, fire tests for FR-PS samples were performed using the ASTM Cone Calorimeter - a standard testing facility developed for the measurement of the ignition time (i.e. the time to reach sustained flaming), rate of heat release and smoke production of combustible solids. FR-PS samples of 100 x 100 mm and 5 or 10 mm thickness were prepared and tested at various irradiation conditions at 20, 40 and 60 kW/m2. Ignition time, rate of heat release and smoke production were measured in the fire tests and validation of the current LESFR3D fire model for FR-PS by comparison of computed and measured results from cone calorimeters of FR-PS samples at various irradiation conditions at 20, 40 and 60 kW/m2 with good agreements based on the kinetics parameters obtained described in Objective 2 above.

122812.label: Project Objectives
122812.value: To fabricate and study the optical response of simple planar and near-planar plasmonic nanostructures using spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) combined with optical numerical simulations via Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD). To use complimentary characterization to guide and provide feedback on the implementation of significant FDTD modeling of the structures fabricated. This includes structural (AFM, SEM, TEM), far-field optical (PL) and near-field (NSOM) characterization. To study the ability of FDTD numerical models to yield quantitative information about simple planar and near-planar structures that can be correlated with far-field techniques like spectroscopic ellipsometry thus providing quantitative confirmation on the optical model. To use the multiple approaches outlined in objectives 1, 2, and 3 to optimize the use of the fabricated structures as advanced plasmonic-based sensors yielding superior sensitivity, reproducibility, and specificity. To evaluate the suitability of FDTD-SE approach to extract detailed sample characteristics, such as optical properties and/or morphology, based on the proposed FDTD-SE approach.

122812.label: Realisation of objectives
122812.value: The project objectives have been completed entirely. With the execution of this project we achieved groundbreaking results and we are the first group that systematically demonstrates the use of FDTD as the first alternative strategy to the conventional Rigorous Couple-Wave Analysis (RCWA) to study complex structured samples. Alternatives to RCWA to study the SE response of complex materials including nanostructures are needed as RCWA becomes too computationally expensive for 2D periodic structures. Instead, we demonstrated that SE-FDTD modelling can be done for 1D and 2D structures fast enough, using a modest desktop server. This has enabled us to perform iterative processes, such as parameter sweep and particle swarm algorithm, to retrieve the best-fit optical model to fit real experimental data. Importantly, the FDTD method is naturally suited to solve for non-periodic structures and also for non-linear media. Our work thus lays solid foundations to continue developing the applications of FDTD to determine the SE response of materials. We have already applied for a GRF proposal to continue this work to develop this method for the characterization of single structures. To achieve the projects objectives we first used idealized (numerically generated) SE data simulated from standard matrix transfer algorithm and Fresnel coefficients to guide the optimization of the FDTD simulation. Thus was also needed to optimizing the computational performance. As a result we developed a solid and sound strategy to identify, correct or minimize artificial and numerical errors and artifacts in the modelling. This included for example numerical resonances that appear when Block Boundary Conditions (BBC) are used which result because the light injection angle is wavelength dependent. Our strategy was to use custom light injection sources into the modeling region that included to standard Gaussian sources set up such that the compromised spectral components will interfere destructively. This approach was guided using the idealized (numerically generated) SE data and not only improved the accuracy of the calculation by 3 orders of magnitude but also improved the speed by almost estimated by the (chi)^2 figure of merit for modeling of SE data at angles as large as 80° AoI with respect to the standard solution As a result, SE-FDTD modelling of 1D structures can be performed fast enough using a modest desktop server to retrieve the best-fit optical model using iterative processes such as parameter sweep or the more sophisticated particle swarm algorithm. More recently, these results have been extended to include 2D planar chiral metamaterials. Together, the achievement of the objectives set in the proposal demonstrate that the combined SE-FDTD approach is a realistic alternative to RCWA method. We have also extend the above results to include the temperature dependence response of nano-imprinted gratings with strong diffractive properties. These gratings were fabricated from PMMA films prepared on gold coated silicon substrates. It is known that the diffraction grating will increases the in-plane wavevector of incident light by multiple integer of its own spatial frequency. This momentum boost acts following the grating vector, which for a 1-dimensional grating is perpendicular to the orientation of the grating grooves. The simplest result of this interaction is a change in the propagation direction of an incident wave, which is often exploited in order to increase the distance over which light interacts with matter. This is useful in a solar cell or optical sensors in order to improve the performance of such devices. However, when properly form these gratings and their effects can also result in the formation of surface plasmon polaritons, (SPP). In our case the sub-wavelength structures formed on the substrates have been shown to support both surface plasmon polariton waves and guided modes. This was verified through a combination of spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) measurements and analytical modelling that enabled us to identify light-matter interactions in the spectra of reflected light. We have measure the spectral SE response of such structures versus temperature and used the FDTD-SE approach to identify changes in both the refractive indices of the materials PMMA, Silicon and gold) and the structural characteristics of the gratings (period, height, etc.) as function of temperature. This work is not published but a manuscript is under preparation (see attached files). Our results demonstrate that SE is a powerful, non-contact characterisation technique for simultaneous morphological and dielectric function determination of complex nanostructured surfaces involving plasmonic effects. We have finally pursued additional tasks that include the modelling of 2D gratings in the shape of planar chiral metamaterials (PCM) our investigations show an improvement in our model with better agreement to published experimental data compared to the published (not ours) experiments. These studies can be used to design chirality sensors with superb response and with full modelling oftheir spectral optical response, this work however will be the further subject of following on work as it was not part of the current proposal.

122812.label: Major findings and research outcome
122812.value: Our group’s work is the first to validate and systematically determine the basis for the quantitative use of the FDTD method to calculate the SE response of subwavelength periodic structures based on the far-field propagation of the near-field response calculated using the FDTD method. We have shown that this approach can be optimized with outstanding capabilities that enable us to: i) calculate the SE response for angles of incidence (AoI) as large as 85o ii) compute highly accurate simulations with precision equivalent to half-monolayer oxide-layer thickness sensitivity; and iii) achieve improved computational time between 4x to 20x faster than the standard FDTD solution. Furthermore we have demonstrated all the above using modest computational resources and our results suggest that there is room for additional improvements in terms of computational speed and accuracy. Importantly, we also demonstrate that SE-FDTD modelling can be done for 1D and 2D structures fast enough, using a modest desktop server. This thus enable iterative processes, such as parameter sweep or the more sophisticated particle swarm algorithm, to retrieve the best-fit optical model to fit real experimental data. We have published 9 publications in international and well recognized journals (indexed in SCI) that describe the main findings and applications of the research conducted. In all of these publications we have acknowledgment to this proposal that the Research Grants Council of Hong Kong. We have also participated in important and highly relevant conferences including two of the most important international conferences in the filed, namely the International Conference on Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (ICSE) in Kyoto, Japan (2013) and in Berlin Germany (2016).

122812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
122812.value: There is much potential for further development, for instance a recently received a France/Hong Kong JRS grant (F-CityU108/16) to study electromagnetic enhancement: (EME) in all-dielectric multilayers with self-assembled nanostructures to develop alternatives for SERS. While the EME in multi-layers can be calculated analytically, the interaction between the enhanced field and sub-wavelength structures will be done numerically using FDTD except for the simplest structures. This is a collaboration including Prof. Claude AMRA, founding director of the Fresnel Institute and one of the objectives is to re-apply for CNRS funding; in 2015 we were shortlisted for full ANR/RGC JRS (proposal A-CityU103/15) “Multi-scale photonics and plasmonics for advanced light control, management, and harvesting.” We have also submitted three CRF proposal with the support of a strong international team including: i) Ludvik Martinu Professor and Chairholder – NSERC Industrial Research Chair in Coatings and Surface Eng, and ii) David R. Smith, James B. Duke Distinguished Professor, Center for Metamaterials and Integrated Plasmonics of the Pratt School of Engineering, Duke University. One CRF proposal (C1014-16EF) with title “Advanced broad-band optical characterization for quantitative studies of next generation materials, devices, and bio-diagnostics” was invited for full proposal in 2016, however it was not shortlisted for interview.

122812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
122812.value: Prior to our work the only systematically demonstrated approach to study the far-field optical response of sub-wavelength and nanostructured materials was RCWA. However RCWA is strongly limited to study 1D periodic structures. The need to find alternative or complimentary numerical techniques is very well known and there have been many attempts to do so using several techniques. Before our work few people could have believe this was possible: as one referee of our original proposal said: "While the FDTD method may not be accurate enough in predicting the correct optical behaviour, the combination with SE and experiment can be sufficiently adequate to optimize a given sensor design task." Our results demonstrate systematically that FDTD has the ability to provide accurate data modeling at a level comparable to the superb sensitivity of SE measurements using modest computational resources. Importantly, the FDTD method has important advantages respect to RCWA, including generality and suitability to address complex structures as well as non-linear effects and/or single, non-periodic, structures.

123012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123012.value: Abstract Given the growth, complexity and size of the Internet as well as growing concerns regarding energy consumption, there is a need for new network design methodologies to achieve cost effective and energy efficient operations of the Internet. We will provide a cost-based near optimal solution for a multi-layered network serving traffic streams modeled by Long Range Dependent (LRD) processes, where a given number of transport technologies operating in layers are supported by all the switching nodes. The aim is to optimize both the routing path and the choice of transport technologies for all traffic where the cost metric includes the effect of network resource utilization in various layers. Given the size of the Internet, the solution must be scalable. Therefore we seek heuristic algorithms where traffic streams are transported on their least cost path. Since cost and routing are mutually inter-dependent, we iterate routing and capacity assignment heuristics until convergence is achieved. A novel and key feature of the project is the inclusion of LRD traffic in the optimal design problem of multi-layer networks. We use a Poisson Pareto Burst Process (PPBP), which is known to accurately model Internet traffic and exhibits large variability in flow sizes. By using a realistic stochastic traffic model, together with flow-size dependent routing as a technology which can intelligently handle this traffic, we are able to thoroughly explore an important approach for improvement in the network efficiency and performance. Both dynamically set-up paths and permanently established paths are included in our analysis. Our solutions will produce near optimal link capacity assignments for the physical and virtual links, and near optimal virtual topology. Furthermore, using realistic prediction of traffic demands and cost of energy and transport equipments, the project will provide means for predicting future technology usage, e.g., under what traffic conditions will the core Internet become all-optical. The project will also result in important fundamental contributions by providing statistical characterization of splitting and merging traffic streams modeled by PPBP processes. Additionally, we will develop solutions that will enable telecommunication engineers and researchers to design new networks, upgrade them, and predict network evolution. In this way, the project will make industry impact, potentially leading to a “greener” Internet and lowering the cost for telecommunication providers and users. 众所周知, 当今因特网的架构庞大而复杂, 考虑到因特网未来的高速发展以及其越来越受到人们关注的能源消耗，我们迫切需要一些新的网络设计方法来使因特网的成本和能源消耗具有更高的效益。在此项目中, 我们将会对多层式数据流网络的优化问题提供一个基于成本考虑的近优解。 在这个优化的过程中, 我们使用长时相关的过程来对数据流进行模拟，并假设网络中所有的交换节点在网络各层中分别支持各种相关传输技术。 在同时考虑各层网络资源的成本和利用率的情况下, 我们的方法旨在对所有的数据流的路径选择与传输方式进行优化。考虑到因特网的庞大规模，提出的解决方案必须是可扩展的，因此我们用启发式的算法使得数据流采用最小成本的路径进行传输。由于成本和路径选择的关联性，我们通过迭代该启发式算法来寻找数据流的最优路径及分配网络带宽直至总体成本收敛至最终结果。 我们的项目一个重要的创新在于其在多层网络的优化设计中引入了长时相关的数据流。在此项目中, 我们采用了泊松帕累托突发过程，这是一个已知的能够精确模拟因特网数据流的模型, 因为现今的因特网数据流在流量大小上具有巨大方差的统计特性。通过使用接近真实的随机过程模型和依据流量大小来选择数据流路径的技术，我们获得了一个能够全面地提升网络效率及性能的途径。在我们的分析过程中，数据流路径的建立既可以是动态的也可以是永久的。 我们的解决方案将给出近似最优的物理层和虚拟层的带宽分配方案，并且得到近似最优的虚拟网络拓扑。此外，在考虑实际的数据流量预测和真实的能源及传输设备成本的情况下，该项目还能预测未来技术的可用性，比如未来在何种数据流条件下,全光纤的因特网主干网会成为现实。 通过基于泊松帕累托过程对流量进行分离和聚集的统计特性研究，此项目还具有重要的基础性贡献。此外，我们将开发能够使工程与科研人员设计，升级及预测网络未来发展的解决方案。此项目通过这种方式来降低电信服务的供应商和用户的开销并影响业界，使我们朝着更加“绿色”的因特网前进。

123012.label: Realisation of objectives
123012.value: Ovelrall, all the objectives of this project, have been successfully achieved, To address the first objective, we have developed a scalable cost-based heuristic solution of optimal design problem for a multi-layered, multi-technology network, where the traffic is modeled as a mixture of constant bit-rate (CBR) and variable bit-rate (VBR) streams and where one particular model for the VBR traffic is the long range dependent (LRD) Poisson Pareto Burst Process (PPBP) and another is a short range dependent (SRD) Gaussian process. Our VBR traffic streams are therefore a combination of PPBP and Gaussian processes. Note that a special case of the Gaussian process is the case of zero variance which enables us to add a deterministic (CBR) component to any end-to-end variable rate stream. Our model includes a number of transport technologies operating in layers that are supported by all switching nodes. The transport technologies may include Optical Burst Switching (OBS) and Optical Circuit Switching (OCS) that operate in the Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) layer or packet switching that operate in the TCP/IP layers, or many other present and future technologies (e.g. flexi-grid). Our solution enables traffic flows to be classified according to their sizes, and each class is routed independently. The incorporation of layering and PPBP traffic introduces a complexity, which cannot readily be managed in the framework of the traditional network optimization methodologies. Fortunately, a radical simplification ensued by adopting shortest path routing in each layer as the overall design philosophy. The optimization algorithm then becomes an iterative application of shortest path routing together with link-by-link dimensioning in all layers. This iterative algorithm is based on fixed-point solution that involves all the layers with shortest path algorithm in each layer. The statistical behavior of the traffic is taken into consideration using an approach called parametric decomposition (which guarantees that GOS requirements are met in each link for each layer) and the cost includes the concept of modules. For example, if only half a wavelength is used, the traffic that uses the wavelength still must "pay" for an entire wavelength (amortized CAPEX and OPEX). The algorithm is demonstrated for a range of networks including the 100-node ``CORONET'' network. We call our multilayer optimization Multilayer Market Algorithm (MMA) because it is similar to a market economic system where at each layer a choice is made between the cost of performing the task in that layer or outsourcing it to the layer below. The demand for transport comes from the layer above and the cost for comparison comes from the layer below. In MMA, we have considered static virtual link assignment as well as dynamic flow assignment. Dynamic flow assignment is sensitive to the cost of connection set up. We have optimized the network for a variety of setup cost values to learn how it affects the optimal proportion of traffic assigned to dynamic (short term) links. In addition our optimization also enables us to predict higher use of the optical layer as traffic and flow size increases. To address the second objective, MMA can be used to optimize the classification of flows based on their sizes. Then, each class may use different routes and different layers on its transport to its destination. For example, small flows may use IP layer but large flows will use the optical layer (e.g. WDM), and in this way, significant cost savings is possible because all the packets at a large burst can be transmitted as one unit and there is no need for routers at the IP layer to handle individual packets. This mode of transport can be used, for example, by either circuit or burst switching. Optimizing the classification of flows by MMA is done by a brute force algorithm trying different values of thresholds between the class sizes and running the optimization. Because our algorithm is so scalable (e.g. less than two minutes for a 100 node network) such brute force solution is possible. Moving from a single size to classification into two classes "mice" and "elephants" have led to around 40% reduction in total network costs. MMA works with an interface called Netml which enables inputting data that describes a realistic network of any size and topology. In http://www.ee.cityu.edu.hk/~zukerman/netml.wmv we provide a demonstration of MMA (and Netml) performed by the PhD student Yu Peng. See also Peng's PhD thesis on http://www.ee.cityu.edu.hk/~zukerman/thesis_PENGYu.pdf for full details on MMA (including flow size dependent routing and its validation). The reader will appreciate that this is a large and complex software, so significant amount of time was spent of validation and debugging of the software. In particular, key challenges that we had to overcome included how to validate (1) the correctness of the software (that it does what it supposes to do), and (2) that the optimal solution it provides is close to the real optimal solution. These challenges are discussed next. Given the importance of software validation, and to address the third objective, we have validated our results in three ways. Firstly, we use, as a benchmark, an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) solution where the dimensioning is done according to the principle of peak rate allocation. In this case, the traffic steam demands for each origin destination pairs are assumed to be deterministic (CBR). The accuracy and of the MMA is validated based on the ILP solutions in the case of small networks. We demonstrate that in the special case of 100% CBR traffic between every origin-destination pair, the ILP slightly outperforms our heuristics. This is expected as our solution is sub-optimal. However, as the percentage of VBR traffic increases, our heuristic solution (MMA) increasingly outperforms the ILP solution because MMA considers the effect of statistical multiplexing. Secondly, we use the results of the ILP, but in each link for each layer we allocate capacity based on the principle of statistical multiplexing. Thirdly, we validate the accuracy of the software by making sure that the sum of the amortized costs of the flows used in each layer on each link is consistent with the total OPEX and CAPEX costs. This third approach is based on the accounting principle known as double-entry bookkeeping and is described in the ITNAC 2015 conference paper by Addie et al. and also in the thesis by Yu Peng. Implementing double-entry bookkeeping provides confidence in the correctness of MMA in the same way that this accounting approach provides a check on accounting correctness in real businesses. In addition to the validation, another issue that we have encountered is a convergence of the algorithm. Fix-point network solutions are known to converge only in very special cases of circuit switched networks with fixed routing. It is also known that such algorithms do not converge in more complicated settings involving for example alternate routing. We have encountered cases where the MMA does not converge to a unique solution. In such cases, where the MMA fluctuates between more than one solutions, we select the least cost solutions that the MMA provides.

123012.label: Major findings and research outcome
123012.value: We have developed a working software (MMA + Netml) that provides near optimal routing, choice of technology, and capacity allocation on each link and each layer for any given multilayer network of realistic size with VBR and/or CBR traffic steams. As mentioned above, the PhD thesis by Yu Peng provides a complete accord of the results of this project, and the conference paper in ITNAC 2015 by Addie et al. provides a key method that we used in software validation of the project. Also, PI Zukerman was invited to give a keynote address in the Australasian Telecommunication Networks and Applications Conference (ATNAC) in November 2014, and an important part of the presentation was the MMA description, demonstration and results. Publications that so far resulted from the project include research papers on various aspects of the project. They are listed in Part C. We discuss some of them in the following. We have published several papers that address some aspects of network design related to this project for certain specific optical network applications. The papers by Wang et al. and S. Li et al. and the PhD thesis by S. Li provide new results on analyses and performance evaluation of circuit switched and burst switched networks using various fixed-point algorithms. The paper by Cai et al. uses an iteration based heuristics aiming to optimize routing and spectrum assignment in elastic optical networks. The paper by Lin et al. considers an important aspect addressed in this project on the effect of set-up cost of dynamic links and how to design networks to minimize this cost effect in the context of datacenter networks. The paper by Lee et al. rigorously analyzed the efficiency of a distributed energy trading scheme. The work can be extended to a more general multi-level system. In the paper by F. Li et al., various control methods (including several neuron based methods) used to improve performance of the two layer system (TCP and AQM) have been studied and compared.

123012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123012.value: We plan to further develop the research beyond the scope of the present project in the following directions. Firstly, we plan to extend the MMA to also include network design provisions for protection and survivability. This extension will build on our experience in various projects involved GOS evaluation (e.g. S. Li et al. PTL 2015) and capacity provisioning in network involving survivability and protection over the last quarter of century. In addition, we plan to slightly improve the traffic modelling and GOS evaluation by considering a traffic model based Poisson Lomax Burst Process (PLBP) instead of the PPBP. The Lomax has certain benefits over the Pareto in the inclusion of small flows in the modelling. Finally, last but not least, we will aim to make industry impact by building on this project to provide consultancy to industry, so that the MMA will be used for network design of telecommunications networks to achieve cost and energy savings. We also plan to publish further work on MMA that will lead to dissemination and further impact of the results of this project.

123012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123012.value: This project provides a cost-based near optimal solution for a model that accurately captures the structure of the Internet and its traffic behavior. As in the Internet, our model considers a given number of transport technologies operating in layers. The key novelty of the project is the inclusion of realistic traffic modelling within a realistically complex multi-layer network structure that leads to scalable and near optimal solutions. We optimize both the routing path and the choice of transport technologies for all traffic flows where the cost metric includes the effect of network resource utilization in various layers. By using a realistic traffic model, together with flow-size dependent routing as a technology which can intelligently handle this traffic, we are able to thoroughly explore an important approach for improvement of the network efficiency and performance. Furthermore, using realistic prediction of traffic demands and cost of energy and transport equipments, the project will provide means for predicting future technology usage, e.g., under what traffic conditions will the core Internet become all-optical. Overall, the project provides important fundamental contributions as well as practical solutions that have the potential to lead to a “greener” Internet and lower the cost for telecommunication providers and users.
