123212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123212.value: Current state-of-the-art computer vision solutions are largely based on the adoption and adaptation of machine learning algorithms, such as boosting, support vector machines, and probabilistic graphical models. The main advantage with using machine learning is that it allows the computer to discover an optimal model (e.g., object detector) directly from the data, which often performs better than models designed by ”hand” by the researcher. In recent years, Gaussian processes (GPs), a non-parametric Bayesian approach to regression and classification, have been gaining popularity in computer vision. GPs have several properties that are desirable for solving computer vision tasks, such as robust learning on small training sets, probabilistic predictions, and the capability of using diverse image representations. Because of these advantages, GP regression and classification have been applied to many computer vision problems, such as object classification, human action recognition, crowd analysis, stereo vision, and anomaly detection. However, despite their successes, many of these methods attempt to ”shoe-horn” their computer vision task into the standard GP regression framework. Hence, heuristics are required to convert the real-valued GP prediction to a valid task- specific output, which is not optimal in the Bayesian setting. For example in crowd counting, the real-valued GP prediction must be truncated and rounded to generate a proper count prediction. Furthermore, many methods regress functions with multivariate outputs (e.g., human pose angles, bounding boxes) by assuming statistical independence between the output dimensions. However, this is contrary to the actual computer vision data, which tends to have significant structure. Therefore, current computer vision methods based on GPs are not able to fully exploit the Bayesian framework for prediction or for modeling the underlying structure of the multivariate observation space. The goal of this project is to develop new Gaussian process models that allow computer vision solutions to take full advantage of non-parametric Bayesian modeling. In particular, the project aims to develop a parameterized family of multivariate GP models that unifies existing GP models into a single framework. Using this unifying framework, algorithms (e.g., approximate inference) developed for specific GP models will be generalized to all other models, and new GP models can be easily created by changing the parameters of the family. The result is a non-parametric Bayesian multivariate regression framework that can be easily adapted to a diverse set of computer vision tasks (e.g., pose recognition, tracking, reflectance spectra estimation, crowd counting, and surveillance). 當前最先進的機器視覺解決方案很大程度上依賴於機器視覺算法的採用和改進，例如：boosting集成學習，支持向量機和概率圖模型等。機器學習方法最主要的優勢在於，它可以通過計算機直接地從數據本身找到一個最優模型（例如：物體檢測器），並且通常要比由研究人員人為設計的模型表現地更好。近年來，一種用於回歸分析和分類的非參數概率貝葉斯方法—高斯過程，在機器視覺領域引起了越來越多的關注。高斯過程具備解決機器視覺問題的一些理想特性，比如：對小樣本數據具有學習魯棒性、概率預測和適用於多樣化的圖像特徵表示。因為這些優點，基於高斯過程的回歸分析和分類已經被用於很多不同的機器視覺問題，比如物體分類、人體動作識別、人群分析、立體視覺和異常檢測。然而儘管有這些成功的應用，當前的問題在於已有的很多應用總是把機器視覺問題“硬塞”到一種標準的高斯過程回歸分析框架中。所以，通常需要採用啟發式方法將高斯過程的實值預測轉換為特定問題需要的有效輸出，而這種轉換後的輸出並不是最優的貝葉斯設置。比如在人群計數問題中，實值預測必須被截斷和四捨五入以產生合適的計數預測。再者，很多具有多元輸出（例如：人體姿態角和約束框）的回歸函數需要假設不同輸出維度之間具有統計獨立性。然而該假設和現實是背離的，因為現實中的機器視覺數據傾向於具有顯著的結構。所以，當前基於高斯過程的計算機視覺方法並不能充分利用貝葉斯框架來進行預測或對多元觀測空間的隱含結構進行建模。本課題的目的在於創建一種新的高斯過程模型，該模型可以使得計算機視覺的解決方案能夠充分利用非參數貝葉斯建模的優勢。特別是，該課題旨在創建一系列參數化多元高斯過程模型，該系列模型可以將現有的高斯過程模型規一到一個統一的架構。通過採用該統一框架，為某種特定高斯過程而開發的算法（比如：近似推理）可以被擴展到所有的其它模型中，此外新的高斯過程模型可以很容易地通過改變系列模型的參數來得到。總之我們的成果是一個非參數貝葉斯多元回歸分析框架，該框架可以很容易地適應多種不同的計算機視覺任務（比如：姿態識別、跟踪、反射譜估計、人群計數和監視）。

Develop a software library for the proposed GP family that is extendable, allowing new GP models to be easily created. Release the library to the computer vision and machine learning communities.

123212.label: Major findings and research outcome
123212.value: 1) The formulation of the multivariate GP has been finalized, and approximate inference algorithms have been derived. (Journal outputs 4 & 5). 2) A new approximate inference method for GPs using density simplification methods has been developed, we are working on the paper. 3) The developed models have been applied to computer vision and computer graphics applications, including eye-gaze trajectory modeling (J-1), human pose estimation (J-3, C-1, C-2, C-3), generative models for fonts (J-9), people counting (J-10), people detection (J-11, C-4). These have led to follow-up works in pose estimation (J-2, J-7, J-8), and people tracking (J-6). 4) The first version of the GP toolbox has been released.

123212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123212.value: 2) The new approximate inference method can be further extended and applied in other areas of Bayesian modeling. 4) The GP toolbox will be updated with new functions as needed.

123212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123212.value: In this project we developed a new machine learning model that has wide applicability to computer vision and computer graphics. The new model was applied to human pose estimation in images and videos, modeling eye-gaze trajectory for laying out graphic designs, counting people crossing a line in a video, counting the number of people in an image, and detecting the location of people in a crowd. These works have applications in surveillance, urban planning, graphic design, and human computer interaction. Software developed for this project was released for the research community to use.

123312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123312.value: In the last century, we have witnessed astounding technical advances in neuroscience studies. These have shown that the nervous system represents information and initiates actions through ensemble spiking activity of its neurons. However, biological processes underlying spike transmission across neural circuits are difficult to study in vivo. This is because they are highly nonlinear dynamical processes and are often time-varying during development and learning. As the amount of experimental data made publicly accessible has gradually increased in recent years, it is now possible to reconsider many of the longstanding questions in neuroscience, such as when and where neural development and learning occur. However, comparative studies which investigate changes in the neural dynamic in different parts of the nervous system do not seem to exist. The proposed study aims to develop a novel modeling methodology to identify the time-varying properties of nonlinear neural dynamics by observing neural spike train inputs and outputs only. The first objective is to estimate the time-varying nonlinear dynamic models of local neural circuits during development and learning using the new electrophysiological recordings now made publicly accessible. These data-driven models would provide valuable information to the development of treatments, and neural prosthetic devices to address neurologic diseases. The proposed project will also provide a new computationally efficient tool for neurobiologists to study local neural circuit changes in real-time during different experiments by adaptive signal processing techniques. For post-experiment analysis when statistical validation of the changes is required, the variation in model parameters will be approximated by weighted sum of orthogonal basis functions. The changes in functional input-output properties of local neural circuits will be correlated with observable changes in functional properties of the nervous system and with variations in performance and/or task variables. The final step of the project is to attempt to reconstruct time-variant connectivity models between brain regions through developmental or learning rule(s) which define how to modify the system models with input and output spike trains only. It is expected that such rule(s) would help us understand the underlying mechanisms of development and learning of the brain. 上個世紀，我們共同見證了神經科學技術取得的顯著進步。研究成果表明，神經系統在整個神經元的放電活動中描述信息並產生行為。然而，在活體中對神經環路電傳導的潛在生物機制進行研究卻非常困難，因為這樣的進程屬於高度非線性動態進程，並且在發育和學習過程中隨時間不斷變化。隨著近年來公開實驗數據量的增多，我們可以將很多擱置已久的問題進行重新考量，比如：神經系統在發育及學習過程中的變化會發生在怎樣的時間和位置。 本研究的目的是開發一種新型的建模方法，通過僅觀察神經元放電序列的輸入和輸出，來識別神經系統的時變屬性。首要目標是使用在發育和學習過程中記錄的電生理數據，來估計局部神經環路的時變非線性動力模型。這些數據驅動模型將為治療神經系統疾病提供有價值的信息。 本方案還將為神經生物學家提供一種新型的高效率計算工具，通過適當的信號處理技術，在不同的試驗過程中對局部神經環路的變化進行實時研究。實驗後期的分析工作需要對這些變化進行統計學驗證，對於這樣的分析工作，模型中的參數變動將由正交基函數的加權求和來逼近。局部神經環路功能性輸入輸出屬性的改變，不僅將與可觀察的神經系統功能屬性的改變相關聯，也將與性能及（或）任務變量中的變動相關聯。在最後一個步驟中，本方案將試圖憑藉發育或學習規則（定義如何僅利用放電序列的輸入及輸出來對系統模型進行調整），在大腦區域之間對時變的連通性模型進行重建。這樣的規則將幫助我們理解大腦發育及學習的潛在機理。

123312.label: Realisation of objectives
123312.value: To identify the changes in neural dynamics in local biological circuits of the mammals as stated in the first objective, we have developed a system identification approach to study the long-term synaptic plasticity using natural spiking activities. This approach consists of three modeling steps. First, a multi-input, single-output (MISO), nonlinear dynamical spiking neuron model is formulated to estimate and represent the synaptic strength in means of functional connectivity between input and output neurons. Second, this MISO model is extended to a nonstationary form to track the time-varying properties of the synaptic strength. Third, to meet the final objective of this project, a Volterra modeling method is used to extract the synaptic learning rule, like spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), for the explanation of the input–output nonstationarity as the consequence of the past input–output spiking patterns. As a special case, STDP is equivalent to a second-order learning rule describing the pair-wise interactions between single input spikes and single output spikes. Using simulated input–output data, we have shown that this modeling problem can be solved with the series of systems identification methods developed; it is possible to infer STDP-like synaptic learning rule purely from the input–output spiking activities. Towards the second project objective, our team has curated datasets of neural recordings with agreements from research groups to investigate how changes in these networks are associated with the physical functions of respective parts of the mammalian nervous system. We have looked into the electrophysiological data from two perspectives. First, using the framework developed, a modified generalized linear model (GLM) with L1-norm penalty was applied to investigate the functional connectivity of entorhinal-hippocampal network using 10 experimental datasets from the Collaborative Research in Computational Neuroscience (CRCNS) program. These datasets contain spike-train data collected from the entorhinal-hippocampal region in the brains of rats performing different tasks. Different tasks could result in the difference in size of the reconstructed network for the same rat. When the training time increased in the same task, more neurons and more connections were involved in the functional network. The analysis also showed that entorhinal-hippocampal network of well-trained rat demonstrated significant small-world features, i.e. short path lengths and large clustering coefficients. However, when the original network is sparsely sampled as in these experiments, the average path lengths and average clustering coefficients could be quite different from that of the actual network. Therefore, we have utilized several quantitative methods to evaluate the small-world-ness in simulated networks. Our comparative studies found that the connectivity structure generated by distance-dependent models could be responsible for the observed small-world features of the reconstructed networks. These models were then utilized to simulate a subset of units recorded from a large biological neural network using multiple electrodes. Two metrics for quantifying the small-world-ness both suggest that the reconstructed network from the sampled nodes estimates a more prominent small-world-ness feature than that of the original unknown network when the number of recorded neurons is small. We have shown that it is feasible to adjust the estimated small-world-ness results based on the number of neurons recorded to provide a more accurate reference of the network property. We have also compared the similarities and the differences of neural networks at different training stages after the adjustment. When the rats conducted different tasks, their brain functional networks still showed significant small-world features. Such techniques could be applied to estimate a more accurate small-world-ness compared to that of sub-graph in a wide range of real-world applications when there are only sampled data available. Second, we had looked into the changes in theta-frequency oscillations of Local Field Potential (LFP) and the phase locking of single neural firings to the ongoing theta oscillations. Working closely with Professor Ying Li’s team at the Department of Biomedical Sciences in CityU, we have investigated the electrophysiological data collected from their experiments, which covered a diverse range of behavioral tasks. This collaborative effort studied the effects of cisplatin, an anticancer drug used in chemotherapy, on induction of long-term potentiation (LTP) in the basolateral amygdala (BLA)-anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) pathway, characterized the coordination of spike timing with local theta oscillation, and identified synchrony in the BLA-ACC network integrity. The quantitative analyses showed that cisplatin disrupted phase-locking at ACC, suppressed LTP, and interrupted synchronized theta oscillations in the BLA-ACC pathway. These changes are associated with the post-chemotherapy emotional and cognitive deficits, which was investigated by elevated plus-maze test, Morris water maze test, and rat Iowa gambling tasks in Professor Li’s lab. Along the way, we had investigated three additional aspects for this project. First, we had reported different elements of a reconfigurable architecture aimed at real-time modeling or prediction of neural activity, which is important for speedup in large-scale data analysis at the early stage of the project. Second, the team had looked into the behavior of zebrafish, which is a simpler animal model to begin the study of neural system. Using machine-learning techniques, we had successfully identified the Wild Types (WTs) and mutants with neurological disease by observing their locomotion profile only. We had also studied the differences in zebrafish behavior for both WTs and mutants across different days post-fertilization. Third, we had developed mutual information (MI)-based unsupervised feature transformation (UFT) method for the pre-processing of heterogeneous data, which can transform non-numerical features into numerical features without information loss. Utilized with the conventional k-means algorithm, this heterogeneous data clustering method was developed for future studies to correlate even larger scale behavioral data with the quantified neural system changes.

123312.label: Major findings and research outcome
123312.value: One of our key contributions is the development of a system identification approach for studying the synaptic plasticity using natural spiking activities. The nonstationary modeling and learning rule identification methods were tested with simulated spiking input–output data. The modeling framework and validation results were published in Journal of Neuroscience Methods (Song et. al. 2015). Results of the collaborative projects with Professor Ying Li’s group were reported in Molecular Brain (Mu et. al. 2015). Meanwhile, we explored the properties of different network topologies (Gao, Chen, & Chan, 2014). We then analyzed the entorhinal-hippocampal network of well-trained rats and reported the significant small-world features of this neural circuit in an oral presentation session at IEEE EMBC (She, So, & Chan, 2015). The experimental results and the simulation results are both recently reported in Scientific Reports (She, Chen, & Chan, 2016). Along the way, we had investigated three additional aspects for this project. First, we had reported different elements of a reconfigurable architecture aimed at real-time modeling or prediction of neural activity, which is important for speedup in large-scale data analysis in ISCAS (Li et al. 2013) and IEEE EMBC (Li et al. 2014) at the early stage of the project. Second, the team had looked into the behavior of zebrafish, which is a simpler animal model to begin the study of neural system. Using machine-learning techniques, we had successfully identified the Wild Types (WTs) and mutants with neurological disease by observing their locomotion profile only (Gao et. al, 2014; Gao et. al., 2016). We had also studied the differences in zebrafish behavior for both WTs and mutants across different days post-fertilization. Third, we had developed a mutual information (MI)-based unsupervised feature transformation (UFT) method for the pre-processing of heterogeneous data (Wei, Chow, & Chan, 2015), which can transform non-numerical features into numerical features without information loss. Utilized with the conventional k-means algorithm, this heterogeneous data clustering method was developed for future studies to correlate even larger scale behavioral data with the quantified neural system changes.

123312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123312.value: As a summary, a modeling framework is developed to study the underlying mechanisms of learning and memory formation in behaving animals, and may serve as the computational basis for building the next-generation adaptive cortical prostheses. It is hoped that the modeling framework developed in this study will be applicable to both in vitro and in vivo electrophysiological studies of different animals. It will be easily modified to handle electroencephalography (EEG) recordings, electromyography (EMG) data or input data from optogenetics experiments. Such computational tool for neurobiologists tracking nervous system changes will also have very significant impact on neuroscience studies. Reliable mathematical models of different parts of the nervous system are, meanwhile, critical to the development of treatments and to the development of next-generation neural prosthetic devices to address neurologic diseases.

123312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123312.value: Nervous system represents information and initiates actions through ensemble spiking activity of its neurons. Using spike train data recorded from rats performing a range of behavioral tasks, we have estimated the nonlinear dynamic models of some local neural circuits. For example, we have reconstructed the functional connections of the entorhinal-hippocampal network, an important region for learning and memory, of well-trained rats and analyzed its small-world features. Intensive simulations found possible adjustments to the small-world-ness measures to reflect the actual network properties from sampled data. After the new adjustments based on the number of sampled neurons, the small-world measures of the entorhinal-hippocampal network remained significant. The modeling framework developed here could facilitate the study of mechanisms underlying learning and memory formation in behaving animals, and may serve as the computational basis for building the next-generation neural prostheses.

123412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123412.value: Neural implant aims at restoring lost functions of mankinds with artificial means. The rapid development of technology leads to the success of deep brain stimulator and cochlear implant that restore motion and auditory functions of patients. Retinal prostheses (implant) are designed to treat outer retinal diseases, like age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and retinitis pigmentosa (RP), which blind hundreds of thousands each year worldwide. Despite the progress of potential treatment of RP including gene therapy and transplantation, no effective treatment is yet available. Clinical trials of the prototype retinal prostheses have shown the promise of giving the blind to see again. Despite the loss of the photoreceptors, a significant number of inner retinal neurons survive such diseases as RP and AMD. Activating the intact ganglion cells using electrical stimulation from a retinal prosthesis device can restore functional vision. An electrode array is placed close to the surviving retinal neurons to elicit activities that are then captured by the retina and transmitted along the visual pathway to the brain. Individual recipient of the implants are able to detect light and perform visually guided tasks with a low-resolution implant. Simulation results showed that advanced visual tasks could be achieved only using a high-resolution implant (>1000 pixels). To fit more than 1000 electrodes on an electrode array within the eye, electrodes should be small and closely packed. Current spread and thus crosstalk between electrodes will become more prominent when electrodes are in close proximity to each other. Crosstalk will impair the resolution of the high-density implant. Study of the interaction between electrode array and retina tissue has solely been done on a simple passive monolayer retina in computer simulation. Responses to electrical stimulation were only studied in healthy retina using small electrodes. We propose to study the spatial extent of the high-resolution electrode array by building an electrode-tissue interface using a computer model of the diseased retina, and also by recording electrically elicited neural activities in the visual cortex in rodent experiment. The novelty of the proposed study lies in the use of degenerate retina in computer simulation and using rat with retinal degeneration with a high-resolution electrode array. The expected results will have significant impact on the design and stimulation strategies of the high-resolution retinal implant. The experimental setup and computer model built in these studies will also benefit in treating other neurological disorders using electrical stimulation as a therapeutic approach as well.

123412.label: Realisation of objectives
123412.value: Objective 1: Summary - We have successfully characterized the electrically evoked responses in the primary visual cortex induced by multi retinal electrical stimulation by positioning a clustered electrode (2 x 2 electrode arrangement) on rat’s retina. We have also implanted flexible electrode array in rat’s eye. However the positioning of the flexible array on the epi-retinal surface is a challenge. The challenge will be discussed in detail. Methodology - Long-Evans adult rats were anesthetized and maintained with an anaesthesia machine by isoflurane throughout stereotaxic surgery and later neuronal recordings. The body temperature was monitored and kept at approximately 38°C by a heating pad. Tropicamide was used to dilate the pupil and eye gel was applied though the experiment progress to maintain the moisture and clarity of the stimulated eye. The stimulating cluster electrodes (2×2, diameter for each electrode: 50 μm) penetrated though the upper sclera near the margin of cornea, close to the ventral retina near macular. A craniotomy was performed at the occipital lobe to access the visual cortex contralateral to the stimulated eye with the skull piece and dura carefully removed in this opening. A 32-channel Utah array (Omnetics array: length of electrode: 1mm, arrangement: 4×8, size of array: 2.8mm× 1.2mm; Blackrock Microsystems, Salt Lake City, USA) was inserted 1.0mm depth in the exposed visual cortex for in vivo electrophysiological recording to retinal electric stimuli. Charge-balanced, cathodic first, biphasic currents (20-200uA, 1ms/phase) were applied to the epiretinal surface. The impedance of the electrode ranged from 10 to 20 kΩ using a 10-mV (r.m.s.). The stimulation began from single electrode (yellow, black, red, and blue), followed by the combination of two of those electrodes (red+blue, red+black, red+yellow, yellow+black) stimulating simultaneously. Result – Thresholds for electrically evoked potentials: Firstly, electrically evoked potentials (EEPs) were recorded from the contralateral visual cortex using a 32-channel Utah array after retinal electrical stimulation for the determination of threshold. The amplitude of EEP was normalized with respect to the largest amplitude of each current. The responses saturated after the retinal stimulation current reach 120 μA or so. We chose the current required a potential equal to 20% of the maximum response as the threshold for EEP. Objective 2 : Summary - We have successfully evaluated the effect of spatial extent in the primary visual cortex of rat using a clustered electrode (2 x 2 electrode arrangement). We have also examined the effect of spatial extent on various stimulus parameters including stimulus frequency, interpulse interval and pulse duration, using single channel stimulation on retina. Result 1 - Spatial Correspondence of EEP Responses to Single Channel Retinal Stimulation: The spatial correspondence of EEP responses to single retinal stimulation was examined in this study. Electric stimulation through blue, black, red and yellow retinal electrode was used to induce the responses in the contralateral visual cortex. The spatial map was divided into 32 grids by white dotted line. The spatial responses recorded in visual cortex were elicited by blue, black, red and yellow retinal electric electrode. The approximate corresponding area for blue, black, red and yellow stimulating electrode are site 27, 18, 32 and 17, respectively. Note that their threshold to induce EEPs are also different (blue channel: 70µA, black channel: 90µA, red channel: 42µA, yellow channel: 43µA). Result 2 - Spatial distribution of electrically evoked responses to two adjacent retinal electric stimulation: Following previous examinations are the spatial responses induced by a series of stimuli from two adjacent (140 μm) retinal stimulating electrodes and obtained the corresponding spatial map. With the increase of retinal stimulation, the spatial responses were also increased, with different increment ratio, until the spatial responses merged each other. The spatial interaction of responses recorded in visual cortex and the retinal co-stimulating were recorded from two electrodes. In most spatial maps, the responses to co-stimulating current from two retinal electrodes merged when the current increased by above 10%. Result 3 - Effect of stimulus parameters on visual cortex responses to single channel electrical stimulation of the retina: A 16-channel recording array (length of electrode: 3 mm, arrangement: 4×4, size of array: 1.2mm × 1.2mm; Spacing: 0.4 mm; Clunburry Scientific LLC, Minnesota, USA) was inserted 1 mm depth in the exposed visual cortex for in vivo electrophysiological recording to single channel retinal electrical stimulation. A total of 10 amplitudes (20 µA – 200 µA) were used, each lasting 500-ms to 10-s with 4 stimulus frequencies ranged from 1 to 20 Hz. For each amplitude, 10 identical stimuli were delivered. For each stimulus frequency, 4 pulse durations were used (200-µs, 500-µs, 1000-µs, 1500-µs) Spatial activation maps were generated according to their location relative to the stimulating electrode. Each grid bin represents the summation of responses for 20 amplitudes in one recording electrode. Long pulse duration (~1-s and 1.5-s) could better activate the neurons in the primary visual cortex than short pulse duration (0.2-s and 0.5-s) in 3 of the representative experiments, as shown in Fig. 5. Neurons in the primary visual cortex were better activated in low stimulus frequencies (1 Hz and 5 Hz) than in high frequencies (10 Hz and 20 Hz). These results may suggest that visual cortical neurons tend to prefer low stimulus frequencies. Challenge - Experiments have been conducted to implant flexible microelectrode array (MEA) in rat’s eye. One of the major challenge is to position the MEA onto the epiertinal surface without separation between the MEA and the retina. A second prototype of the array will be proposed to include a microchannel to deliver a “bio-adhesive” material. We will test several types of “bio-adhesive” material, including polyethylene glycol (PEG), Sortase A (a commercialized enzymatic conjugation platform, http://www.moradec.com/products_sortases.html), for positioning and anchoring the array on the retinal surface.

123412.label: Major findings and research outcome
123412.value: In the present study, we explored spatial interactions arising between electrical stimuli given to electrodes on an epi-retinal prosthesis approach. We employed a paired pulse stimulation regime using a clustered electrode (2 x 2 electrode arrangement) to study the visual cortical responses in rat model. We firstly used single retinal electrode for stimulating and found that the retinal electrodes can uniquely elicit their own spatial response without interference. Later, we carried out the paired-pulse stimulation and acquired the corresponding spatial distribution in visual cortex, which showed that the responses which were induced by two retinal electrodes merged when the initial stimulation current increased above 10%. The merging of response in visual cortex induced by two individual retinal stimulating electrodes, with the distance of 140 μm, may suggest the response are considered to be elicited by one stimulating line/ area under this condition, rather than the two separate points in retina during the visual imaging process. These results provide preliminary, insightful clue for understanding the parameter of epi-retinal stimulation, such as electrodes spacing, resolution and the interaction of stimulating current. We have completed this work and presented in the International Conference on Biomedical and Health Informatics (ICBHI2015), Haikou, China, October 9-10, 2015. We have also systematically investigated how a range of stimulating parameters (current level, stimulus pulse duration, and stimulus frequency) influences the spatial interactions in the neural network of the primary visual cortex. Previous studies have revealed that short pulses (for example, 0.1 ms) excite retinal ganglion cells preferentially, whereas longer pulses (for example, 1 ms) excite both retinal ganglion cells and bipolar cells. However, there is little information about how stimulus pulse duration and stimulus frequency affect the spatial extent of primary visual cortical neurons activation. In the present study, we mapped the activation patterns of primary visual cortical responses to a range of stimulus pulse durations, from 0.2-ms to 1.5- ms. Long pulse duration (~1-s and 1.5-s) could better activate the neurons in the primary visual cortex than short pulse duration (0.2-s and 0.5-s) in 3 of the representative experiments. Neurons in the primary visual cortex were better activated in low stimulus frequencies (1 Hz and 5 Hz) than in high frequencies (10 Hz and 20 Hz). These results may suggest that visual cortical neurons tend to prefer low stimulus frequencies. This work has been completed and the manuscript is on-going.

123412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123412.value: There are three suggested future developments of the present study. First, the effects of retinal degeneration (RD) on primary visual cortical response patterns could be conducted. Response shapes in RD rats could be compared those of wild-type. Second, thresholds of short pulse and long pulse could be compared, to study whether there will be an increase of bipolar cell thresholds during degeneration or whether the retinal ganglion cells thresholds will remain unchanged or not. Third, a longer pulse duration (~25 ms) could be employed to study the spatial extent of the primary visual cortical response patterns. Fourth, a chronic implantation of the flexible electrode array should be investigated to achieve precise positioning and anchoring the flexible array on the rat’s retinal surface.

123412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123412.value: Devices to electrically stimulate the retina have shown great promises to elicit visual percepts to patients suffered from a rare genetic eye condition called Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP). The green light from regulatory bodies for the two retinal implant devices (the Argus II Retinal Prosthesis System, Second Sight Medical Products, Inc.; and the Alpha IMS, Retinal Implant AG) gives hope to those blinded by RP. Much progress has been made from benchtop to bedside, but the development towards a high resolution retina implant is still in its infant stage. Optimal stimulation strategy and competent conditions for therapeutic efficacy still remain an open question. The present study has systematically investigated the effect of stimulus pulse width, stimulus intensity, stimulus frequency on primary visual cortical (V1) response patterns. For each set of stimulus parameters, the V1 responses thresholds were mapped in space with respect to the stimulating electrode position. After the single-electrode stimulation experiments, paired-pulse stimulation was performed to assess the spatial interaction dependent on stimulus intensity. The study of these spatial interactions will provide essential knowledge for developing high-resolution retinal implants.

123512.label: Project Objectives
123512.value: To design efficient, dynamic, and scalable detection method to detect deadlocks for the testing of multithreaded programs. To develop effective techniques to measure the comprehensiveness of the testing progress in detecting deadlocks. To demonstrate to the industry the usefulness of dynamic detection technique and test correctness criteria to reveal deadlocks from the executions of multithreaded programs. To develop a prototype tool for demonstrating the feasibility, effectiveness and scalability of our framework. To demonstrate to the industry the advantages of using advanced testing framework via case studies and controlled experiments. To educate research students to meet the industrial demands in the current trend of concurrent program development.

123512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123512.value: Software testing is the de facto approach to find out problems from programs. It consumes 30-50% of software development budgets. With the advent of multicore processor, companies should develop concurrent programs so that their software products can stay competitive. Multithreaded programs are a popular kind of concurrent programs. However, writing multithreaded programs is notoriously difficult, and many existing multithreaded programs such as Apache, Google Chrome, and Firefox have concurrency bugs such as deadlocks. Deadlocks are widely considered as severe bugs that can cause the programs to halt. However, many applications are browser-based. This trend will be intensified as cloud computing becomes increasingly popular. The lack of progress due to deadlock will cause software unable to complete their tasks. Companies that ship products that may suffer from deadlock will put themselves into serious disadvantages. Static analysis or model checking techniques are well known to be unable to scale up enough to handle commercial-scale programs. Our recent work has further shown that existing state-of-the-art dynamic techniques to detect deadlocks cannot consistently scale up to handle real-life software such as Apache, Google Chrome, and Firefox because they need excessive amount of memory or time to complete, if ever. Company products built on such software platforms may require excessive amounts of time and budget to assure their own products. This problem prolongs the development cycle, greatly reducing the competitiveness of the companies. Existing techniques also provide no guidelines on test comprehensiveness for companies to measure to what extent their products can be confidently free from deadlocks. This project aims at developing a novel framework that addresses both the test oracle problem and the test adequacy problem in the dynamic detection of deadlocks from large-scale multithreaded programs. We propose to investigate a lockset-based, iterative and classification-based strategy to address the scalability and adequacy issues. The success of this project will provide a highly efficient and scalable framework to the industry to detect deadlocks and educate research students so that they can contribute to the growth of the software industry after graduation. 软件测试是从程序中找出问题的工业上通用的方法，它会消耗约30%到50%的软件开发预算。随着多核处理器的出现，很多公司都应开发并发程序来使他们的软件产品更具竞争力。多线程程序就是其中一种很流行的并发程序。然而，众所周知，编写多线程程序是非常困难的。目前已有的多线程程序，比如Apache服务器、谷歌浏览器（Chrome）、火狐浏览器（Firefox）等，都有死锁等并发错误。死锁被普遍认为是能够引起程序停止的严重错误。但是，很多应用都是基于浏览器端的。这种趋势将会随着云计算日渐流行而增强。由于死锁而导致的进程缺失将会导致软件不能完成它应该完成的任务。如果公司引入了可能有死锁的产品，他们将处于非常不利的地位。在死锁检测方面，静态分析或者模型验证技术被普遍认为是无法用于分析商业级别的程序的。我们最近的工作也进一步表明：现有的最新动态死锁检测技术不能用于现实生活中的大规模软件，比如Apache服务器、Chrome浏览器、以及Firefox浏览器。因为这些技术需要一般情况下无法满足的过多的内存或者过多的时间才能来完成他们的检测过程。基于上述软件平台的企业级产品则需要更多的时间和预算来保证这些的产品的正确性。因为这种问题会延长软件开发的周期，从而降低了他们的竞争力。现有的技术也没有提供测试全面性的准则，使得公司可以测量他们的产品在某种程度上是没有死锁的。该项目的目的是开发一种全新的框架，用来处理针对大规模多线程程序中死锁动态检测的测试准则和完备性的问题。我们提出通过探究一种基于锁集（Lockset）的、迭代的、和锁分类的策略来解决扩展性和完备性问题。该项目的完成将会提供一种非常高效和可扩展的框架。这个框架可用于工业界进行死锁检测，以及指导从事研究的学生，使其毕业后可以为软件业的发展做出贡献。

123512.label: Realisation of objectives
123512.value: To achieve objectives one and two, in the project, we had examined different samples of deadlocks in real-world multithreaded programs and applied prior techniques to assess to what extent the deadlocks could be identified. To examine these samples, we have extracted the relevant code excerpts, and this process unavoidably involved scenario simplifications. Most prior techniques worked nicely to identify the deadlocks in these samples. Thus, we had gradually increased the scenario complexity by involving more and more code excerpts taken from the original applications in these samples, and prior techniques gradually showed up signs of their limitations. This process involved a lot of trials and errors due to the selection of code excerpts to be included, and experimental validation through collecting the execution profiles of the selected samples. As have been interested in the scalability of a technique as well, we had purchased a computing server to speed up the discovery process. To ensure that there is no loss on the latest innovation in the area of concurrency bug detection, we have reviewed from time to time the latest work and referenced to their excellent ideas. In particular, we had examined the designs of prior techniques in relation to these limitations, and have formulated strategies to handle each identified major limitation, which came up a series of prototype detectors for dynamic deadlock detection and further distilled the essence of those prototypes to formulate a version of the deadlock detection technique to find potential deadlock occurrences efficiently. We have also examined methods to check the progress of the execution of multithreaded programs, in which have studied the use of dynamic instrumentation techniques to insert code probe into strategic locations and profile the program states and instruction performed at the probed locations. Moreover, since we have to produce executions of the same test cases multiple times, we have looked into methods to run higher priority test cases so that deadlock potentials can be encountered faster. We have also experimented different scopes of profiling of essential and nice-to-have data to balance between effectiveness and efficiency of the formulating prototypes and final detector. We have run real-world software applications with their test cases and examined the thread interleaving patterns in generating lock order events. To do so, we have designed trace representation to log each lock dependency and the order of these lock dependencies while executing test runs. To achieve objectives three to five, we have picked a set of real-world and complex deadlocks experienced by some of widely used software applications in the evaluation. These applications included both server-side applications and desktop applications, and all of them were open-sourced applications so that the industry were able to replicate independently our work in their workplace. We have compared our formulated technique with prior state of the art in the same area and measured the size of the resultant lock order graph or its equivalent as well as the time cost to produce such a resultant graph. To make the evaluation realistic in the industry setting, we have restricted the experiment to be run in a computer setting simulating a commodity computer configured with typical amount of physical memory. To achieve objective six, we have educated students who worked for this project and had research interests in dynamic deadlock detection and related topics on dynamic program analysis and testing. This environment has strengthened the collaboration among students and educate them to be team players in research projects. Moreover, students can cross-reference how other work in different sub-projects, which motivated them to strive for more innovative ideas and tangible realization. We have provided training on research methodology, realization, and result dissemination, and support their conference trips to both local and overseas venues.

123512.label: Major findings and research outcome
123512.value: We have found and validated that deadlock potentials can be efficiently identified from executions of large-scale applications efficiently [J1]. These deadlock potential scenarios are important as they may potentially manifest into real deadlocks in some alternative executions of the same applications [J6, C1, C6, C11]. To identify them, we need oracle information [C5], which we have used a subset of the sufficient condition to form a deadlock as the criterion. We have also observed that test cases are not necessarily simple in structure. Some test cases include structure [J2, C3] and variation patterns [J3, C4, C10, C15], and some of them may be applicable to test multiple versions of the same codebase [J4, J8, C9] with or without additional constraints [C18]. We are aware that techniques using them may have structural relationships among them [J7] and different ranges of data populations may lead to different degrees of test effectiveness [J5, C8]. There are other issues to consider to make a technique efficient. For instance, monitoring execution [J9] typically incurs non-trivial runtime overheads, and may be tuned through different aspects such as compiler optimization [C2, C7] and location to conduct the profiling [C12, C16] or event generation [C20]. We have also found that abstraction of program entity instance [C13, C14, C17, C19, C21] is essential in dynamic analysis including deadlock triggering. The above approach and the consideration of various factors have been demonstrated to be successful. We have shown that lock order graphs can be significantly reduced by removing irrelevant lock dependency and folding up equivalent lock dependency. We have found that such reduction can be iteratively performed by examining whether the resultant graph of the last iteration contains subgraphs that each relates to single thread in the execution under analysis. Once a reduced graph has been constructed, we have formulated a non-redundant search over the reduced graph. Applications may have a pool of worker threads to process a collection of data, where their execution patterns are similar. This design is essential to make multithreaded programs to run faster. We have used this property to find equivalent classes and further reduce the graph stated above. This tool chain has been validated to be effective to make the detection scalable enough to handle large-scale applications in a series of large-scale experiments.

123512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123512.value: Our technique is efficient in handling executions that incur alternative scenarios of real deadlocks. In a test suite, not every test case has the potential to trigger deadlocks. Since each potential deadlock may be a false positive or as a real deadlock. It is essential to reduce the amount of false positives incurred. It requires the collection of more information on top of lock dependency, but it will make the technique heavier weighted, less scalable and less efficient. It is essential to address the false positive issues in effectively detecting potential deadlocks faced by a technique that should still be efficient and scalable. To address these issues, we consider that the interconnection among test cases to prioritize potential deadlock instances appearing in a set of execution traces could be explored. We have also found that graph construction, reduction, and searching are essential research in detection of potential concurrency bugs. It is advised to invent new data structure and algorithms to handle graphs with diverse information on both edges and nodes.

123512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123512.value: Programmers can make a program to output a result earlier by making the program to execute its parts in parallel. However, writing such programs are error-prone. Deadlocks prevents the program to make progress while computing the result, which should be detected before end users experience such problems in their own situations. Large programs run quite long due to executing many steps, and analyzing a long sequence of execution steps is a major obstacle. This research project solves this bottleneck by developing a new tool. Its central idea is twofold. First, it shrinks a relationship graph to a smaller one by either removing or hiding redundant information. Second, it searches the smaller graph based on the property that the ordering of threads involving in the same deadlock is the same irrespective to the starting point of the search. This project has shown that deadlock potentials can be available to programmers who use commodity computers to detect deadlock bugs in their programs, which makes dynamic deadlock detection significantly more affordable to the society, in particularly for individuals and small and medium-sized enterprises.

123612.label: Project Title(Chinese)
123612.value: 物聯網的安全架構和方法研究

123612.label: Project Objectives
123612.value: To investigate a layered architecture targeting security for low-power small-area Internet-of-Things devices. To perform analytical studies for low-power security methods targeting IoT devices. To implement software and hardware models and evaluate the area-time tradeoffs. To perform side-channel analysis and propose countermeasures on the rapid prototypes of the IoT designs.

123612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123612.value: When the DARPA of the USA first funded the ARPNET in 1960s, no one could foresee that nowadays over 2 billion people (over 30% of world population) are connecting to the Internet. According to Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), currently new IPv4 address is unavailable to be allocated; we are now switching from the old IPv4 to IPv6, the new Internet address protocol. In the Internet of Things (IoT) era, each person will carry multiple devices that require multiple IP addresses for connecting to the Internet. For instance, your refrigerator or even a toaster at home will need an IP address, such that a smart environment can be facilitated for future families. A parent can remotely access a smart home grid and pre-program a toaster to start at a later time and temperature. However, if a hacker broke into the smart home grid, and overloaded the toaster or even produced unwanted power shortage to the family, this could potentially cause a major inconvenience or even endanger everyone in the family. Thus, the use of IoT poses new security challenges for the research communities and governance authorities to enable a vibrant and vital global community. This proposal aims to carry algorithmic complexity analysis and efficient hardware / software designs for public-key cryptography targeting IoT devices. These can foster an innovative and trusted Internet for people worldwide. The uses of our novel techniques on Montgomery multiplier using residue number systems (RNS) and spectral arithmetic are attractive and will be explored for IoT devices. We will develop both the software and hardware models which will then be plugged into the proposed IoT security specification. Next, we will perform the run-time side-channel analysis on the designed components. The corresponding countermeasures will also be introduced with the techniques described in this project. By achieving the objectives described in this proposal, it is expected that a resilient and secure IoT will become more favorable to everyone. 當阿帕網首次由美國國防部高級研究計劃署的資助在二十世紀六十年代，那時沒有人可以預見，現在有超過二十億人（世界人口的三十％以上）連接到互聯網。根據互聯網工程任務組，目前沒有可用的網際網路協議版本4地址是新分配的;我們現在在從舊的網際網路協議版本4過渡到新的網際網路協議版本6的，新的互聯網地址協議。在互聯網物聯網時代，每個人都會攜帶多種設備需要多個網際網路協議地址連接到互聯網。舉例來說，你在家裡的冰箱，甚至烤麵包機將需要一個網際網路協議地址，這樣一個智能環境可以促進未來的家庭。家長可以遠程訪問智能家居網，在一定的時間自動運行預設的溫度烤麵包機。然而，如果有一個黑客闖入的智能家居網，破壞烤麵包機，甚至產生不必要的電力需求。這可能導致一個重大的不方便，甚至危及孩子們或我們每一個人。因此物聯網的應用也帶來了新的安全挑戰，需要更優化的研究。 此項研究旨在開展物聯網設備的公開金鑰加密算法的複雜性分析和高效的硬件/軟件設計。這可以促進全球物聯網的創新和建立值得信賴的互聯網。我們的新技術，蒙哥馬利乘法器餘數系統和波譜算術的用途是有吸引力的，將探討和應用在物聯網的設備上。軟件和硬件模型將會被開發和應用在建議的物聯網安全規範。旁路分析在設計的部件上和它的相應對策也將被提出了在這個項目。通過實現在本方案中所描述的目標，我們相信一個安全的物聯網將使大家更有利益。

123612.label: Realisation of objectives
123612.value: The project has been completed with successful research outputs targeting arithmetic for building low-power and small-area IoT devices. We have developed two types of arithmetic methods using residue number systems, and spectral arithmetic for building up the underlying cryptographic software components and also for hardware components. The proposed modular architectures can be applied to perform the public-key cryptographic algorithms, including Rivest-Shamir-Adleman, elliptic curve cryptography, and pairing-based cryptography. The implementation results conﬁrm the advantages of the novel RNS and R2NS modular arithmetics, we also provide side-channel attack study and their countermeasures for this research project. We also provide arithmetic level analysis and improvements for both polynomial multiplication and Montgomery Modular Multiplication (MMM). For MMM, the computation is performed by exploiting the spectral technique in multiplication and addition, and leaving the remaining operations of MMM in time domain. We denote it as FFT-based Montgomery Modular Multiplication (FFTM3). In terms of the improvements for FFTM3, carry-save arithmetic are used to parallel the accumulation. Moreover, pseudo-Fermat number transform is used to enrich its supported operand sizes. A detail complexity analysis and a systematic procedure to select suitable parameter set for the FFTM3 are also provided to facilitate eﬃcient implementation for the area-time tradeoffs.

123812.label: Project Title(Chinese)
123812.value: 濕熱氣候下建築用再生能源冷凍及供熱的複合系統設計

123812.label: Project Objectives
123812.value: To develop appropriate system design strategies of renewable cooling and heating (RCH) for buildings through hybrid use of solar energy, geothermal energy and bioenergy. To optimize the design and operation parameters of the feasible strategies of RCH for buildings. To generate design guidelines of the feasible strategies of RCH for buildings in the hot and humid cities.

123812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123812.value: 本研究項目是發展混合使用可再生能源，提供建築用空調、供暖和熱水供應。在常規設計中，空調設備是由電力驅動，而供熱可由柴油、 燃氣和電力產生。除非能夠積極使用再生能源，否則在未來數十年，化石燃料仍會被大量使用。政府間氣候變化專門委員會（IPCC）於2011的報告中，強調可再生能源對緩解氣候變十分重要，但如何令可再生能源被廣泛使用？可否在建築樓房全面採用？ 雖然太陽能供熱及冷凍（solar heating and cooling）已漸見成熟，大部分的建築項目都位於溫帶和寒冷區域，其設計乃著重供熱而非空調。近年來，太陽能供熱和冷凍的意念已逐漸轉化成可再生能源供熱和冷凍（renewable heating and cooling），令到在能源供應上，除了太陽能外，仍可有其他選擇。然而，在溫寒氣候下，空調需求並不是重點，另外在冷凍和供熱整體設計上，也較少作探究。有見及此，可再生能源冷凍及供熱（renewable cooling and heating）的概念應運而生，目標為炎熱和潮濕氣候下的建築物所使用。就太陽能空調在單層建築的應用，已制定了多款有效的系統設計。由於屋頂集熱器安裝面積有限，倘若其他可再生能源能共同使用，應用潛力可以擴展到多層建築。在這項研究中，建議用淺層地熱能配合地源熱泵，在太陽能空調上提供額外的冷凍量，此外，利用生物質供熱，為熱驅動的冷凍設備提供輔助加熱。這樣便能混合使用太陽能、地熱能和生物質能源，藉此為建築物提供空調、供暖和熱水供應，這就是本研究項目的核心理念。 為了達成可再生能源冷凍及供熱，將提出各種綜合性系統設計策略，通過全年動態模擬，評估各項策略的成效。基於可行的策略，擬定出一個優化的系統設計，能適用於炎熱和潮濕氣候下的建築物。希望透過在建築廣泛應用，混合可再生能源冷凍及供熱設計能有助緩解氣候變化和空氣污染等問題。

123812.label: Realisation of objectives
123812.value: This research project is to develop and generate feasible system design strategies of renewable cooling and heating (RCH) for buildings in hot and humid climate. All the project objectives have been achieved, and realization of the objectives is reported as follows: Objective 1 – System design strategies of RCH In this study, three system design strategies of RCH have been explored and formulated. These feasible RCH approaches include: • Hybrid renewable cooling system (HRCS) – for building cooling • Hybrid renewable cooling and heating system (HRCHS) – for building cooling and heating • Renewable trigeneration system (RTS) – for building cooling, heating and electrical power The HRCS is primarily designed with solar energy and shallow geothermal energy. On the basis of solar absorption cooling, part of the building sensible cooling load was shared by the ground-source radiant cooling. Although the sole solar absorption cooling system or the sole ground source heat pump system has been individually proven energy-efficient, the area of solar collectors or size of borehole field would be limited by the available space for installation. In this regard, the performance of HRCS through joint contribution of the two renewable energy sources is found more energy-efficient to provide air-conditioning for single-storey building in hot and humid climate. Through the development of the HRCS, the HRCHS is then established with the hybrid use of solar energy, shallow geothermal energy and bioenergy, in order to provide space cooling and water heating for low-rise building in the hot-humid region. Solar energy is basically used for water heating, yet also associated with absorption cooling for handling the ventilation load and zone latent load. Shallow geothermal energy is linked to radiant cooling through a ground source high-temperature chiller for treating the zone sensible load in different occasions. Auxiliary heating is necessary for absorption cooling, biogas is therefore involved in lieu of the traditional fossil fuel. As such, solar energy, shallow geothermal energy and bioenergy can be worked together in building cooling and heating for more than single storey. Although HRCS and HRCHS are technically feasible, they can be only used to serve a single floor and a low-rise building respectively. In the course of development of those strategies, the idea of RTS is evolved to see whether high-rise building can be handled by a renewable mean. The system design approach of the RTS is different from HRCS and HRCHS, which is based on the use of bioenergy and the principle of trigeneration. Apart from cooling and heating, the RTS is able to provide electrical power as well. Actually, biomass, biodiesel or biogas can be involved, depending on the type of prime mover to be adopted in trigeneration. With the features of high electrical efficiency and possible use of biogas, the solid oxide fuel cells (SOFC) become an emerging type of prime mover for trigeneration. As a result, a preliminary study has been conducted to evaluate the performances of SOFC-trigeneration system. It is found that the SOFC-trigeneration is technically feasible for high-rise building application. Objective 2 – Design and operation of RCH systems In the HRCS, appropriate design and operation between the ground-source radiant cooling and the solar absorption cooling have been worked out. In a typical office building, the appropriate sharing of total cooling capacity is found two-third from the solar-driven part and one-third from the ground-source part. Through the year-round dynamic simulation, it is found that the HRCS can have 43.8%, 53.3%, and 68.0% primary energy saving when compared to the sole ground-source heat pump system, the sole solar absorption cooling system, and the conventional vapour compression air-conditioning system, respectively. This demonstrates the merit of hybrid use of solar energy and shallow geothermal energy in renewable cooling. The strategy of HRCS is therefore effective for sustainable air-conditioning and green building design in hot and humid climate. In the HRCHS, effective control and operation scheme has been advocated for the ground-coupled radiant cooling system according to the ambient conditions in order to minimize the system energy demand. Three operation modes are involved: Mode 1 is to have simultaneous functioning of the absorption chiller and the high-temperature chiller. This occurred when the ambient temperature is above 20 degC. Mode 2 is operated when the ambient temperature is between 15 degC and 20 degC. In this situation, the high-temperature chiller would stop with only the absorption chiller functions and the ground heat exchanger borefield would be directly coupled to the radiant panels. Mode 3 is activated when the ambient temperature falls below 15 degC, in which the absorption chiller would also stop. The system is then operating in a free-cooling mode by radiant panels and the untreated outdoor air only. Under this effective control scheme, the HRCHS using passive chilled beams can achieve 44.4% saving in year-round primary energy consumption compared to the conventional air-conditioning. The zone temperature and relative humidity are also maintained well at the design levels. As a result, the strategy of HRCHS has both the environmentally friendly and thermally comfortable merits for building application in hot-humid city. In the preliminary study of SOFC-trigeneration, two different design and operation means of SOFC-trigeneration have been proposed and evaluated: full-capacity approach and partial-capacity approach. The former is to design the rated capacity of SOFC by matching the demand peak of electrical power without the need of power grid connection. The latter is to satisfy the peak electrical demand partly by the SOFC and partly by the power grid, but still maintaining net zero grid-electricity in a year time. Compared to the conventional provisions of cooling, heating and electrical power for building, the full- and the partial-capacity of SOFC-trigeneration systems would have 7.1% and 2.8% year-round electricity savings respectively. Even using conventional natural gas, the full- and the partial-capacity systems can have 51.4% and 23.9% carbon emissions cut per annum respectively. As a whole, the full-capacity SOFC-trigeneration would assure both energy and environmental merits for high-rise building for the subtropical climate. Objective 3 – Design guidelines of RCH systems In the HRCS and the HRCHS, the feasible system design and operation have been fully generated for building application in hot and humid climate. In particular, parametric study has been conducted for the essential design parameters like radiant panel type, ground thermal conductivity, borehole length and water heating demand. Control and operation schemes have been developed for the corresponding RCH strategies. The entire design and operation information of the HRCS and the HRCHS, including schematic system designs, equipment members and specifications, design and operation parameters, control and operation schemes have been covered in the respective journal papers already published. It is expected that these feasible design strategies of RCH can be effectively disseminated and applied in the building sector.

123812.label: Major findings and research outcome
123812.value: Through this research project, effective system design of RCH has been developed through the hybrid use of renewable energy sources, including solar energy, shallow geothermal energy and bioenergy. These RCH strategies do not rely on the traditional fossil fuel anymore for building application in the hot and humid climate. At first, the hybrid renewable cooling system (HRCS) has been established, which makes use of both solar energy and shallow geothermal energy rather than a single renewable energy source. For single-storey building application, the HRCS can outperform other renewable cooling system designs, and have significant year-round primary energy saving against the sole ground-source heat pump system and the sole solar absorption cooling system. Then the RCH strategy is put forwards and the hybrid renewable cooling and heating system (HRCHS) has been generated. In the HRCHS, three renewable energy sources can be jointly used, the application is therefore extended to low-rise buildings instead of a single floor application. In the HRCHS, solar energy is harnessed for absorption cooling and water heating, shallow geothermal energy for radiant cooling from high-temperature chiller, and biogas for auxiliary heating of absorption chiller when necessary. An effective control and operation scheme is proposed for the HRCHS so that the various equipment members, hence the corresponding renewable energy sources, can be called in around the year. For both the HRCS and the HRCHS, their system design configurations, equipment members involved, design and operation parameters, equipment specifications, year-round control and operation schemes have been fully mentioned in the two associated SCI journal papers as attached in this report. In order to advocate RCH for high-rise building application, a design idea has been emerged in this project. On the basis of trigeneration, it is found technically feasible to provide not only cooling and heating, but also electrical power by using a prime mover of high electrical efficiency such as solid oxide fuel cells (SOFC). Through the preliminary study of SOFC-trigeneration system, it is worth noting that the renewable trigeneration system (RTS) has high potential for further development since SOFC can be energized by biogas. It is expected that the renewable cooling, heating and power, on top of RCH, would be more beneficial to building application, so that the problems like urban heat island and air pollution can be effectively mitigated. The preliminary study of SOFC-trigeneration is covered in a SCI journal paper as attached in this report.

123812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123812.value: As mentioned before, this research project has good potential for further development in the field of renewable cooling, heating and electrical power for urban heat island mitigation. Through the preliminary study of SOFC-trigeneration fueled by natural gas, it can be moved forwards to the strategy of RTS which is potentially driven by biogas. Further study can also be directed to the hybrid use of solar thermal energy, solar electrical energy and geothermal energy for integrated system design in the range of cogeneration, trigeneration and polygeneration for building applications. Although both energy and environmental merits of RTS is expected, the economic return depends on the extent of primary energy saving and carbon emission cut, as well as how the corresponding financial terms can be considered. As a result, this provides a tangible research opportunity for development of renewable cooling, heating and power through a holistic energy, environmental and economic assessment.

123812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123812.value: In this research project, feasible system design strategies of renewable cooling and heating (RCH) have been developed, which are achieved through the involvement of multiple renewable energy sources, including solar energy, shallow geothermal energy and bioenergy. As such, building cooling and heating can be offered in hot and humid climate, without emphasizing on the use of fossil fuels. Since a number of renewable energy sources are jointly utilized, the application can be extended to low-rise buildings, rather than the single-floor application as handled by solar cooling before. In the hybrid system design of RCH, solar energy is used in absorption cooling and water heating, while shallow geothermal energy is adopted by high-temperature chiller for radiant cooling. Effective system control scheme is also established for year-round system operation in building. Bioenergy would be involved so that auxiliary heating of absorption chiller does not demand fossil fuel. In this study, a potential renewable strategy based on the idea of trigeneration has been emerged, which does not only provide cooling and heating, but also electricity for high-rise building. These design strategies of RCH would certainly enhance primary energy saving and carbon emissions cut, undoubtedly contributing to mitigation of urban heat island in metropolis.

124012.label: Project Objectives
124012.value: We will construct a WSN for a large-scale lecture theatre in City University of Hong Kong as a platform and testbed to strengthen the research of WSN for HVAC applications. The possible deficit and potential measurement problems will be studied when the wireless sensor nodes are installed at the places reachable by occupants. We will retrofit the conventional control design for the VAV boxes. The whole large space will be virtually partitioned into several local areas (each area is served by one VAV box) and the thermo-coupling problem due to heat and mass transport phenomena, such as natural and forced convections, diffusion and dispersion etc., will be modelled in term of control. Then, a robust MIMO control algorithm will be developed to solve the coupling problem and to improve the temperature tracking ability of the thermostat under unevenly distributed and time-varying load conditions. The control performance, thermal comfort condition and energy consumption will be compared with the original control design. We will study the feasibility of demand-based temperature control, which supplies cooling only to the areas with cooling requirement, by concerning thermal comfort. The energy saving potential will then be studied by considering the thermo-coupling problem under several typical occupancy conditions. The results will be used to qualify the energy saving potential of the demand-based temperature control for large-scale rooms. We will economically analyze the proposed design and strategy using the example lecture theatre. A report on the economical analysis will be submitted to the office of Facility Management for considering retrofitting the example lecture as a showroom for technology-transfer DEMO by the university.

124012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
124012.value: Large-scale rooms, characterized by large volumes, are widely used in university, government and commercial buildings to provide professional accommodation for lectures, seminars, conferences and large formal meetings. To condition large-scale rooms consumes energy heavily, especially in hot regions like Hong Kong. A typical control design for the air-conditioning systems for large-scale rooms is to use a single thermostat to synchronously control all variable-air-volume (VAV) supply air boxes according to the temperature differential between the measurement at the return air duct and the room temperature set point. Actually, this single-input-single-output (SISO) design may not ensure thermal comfort because the vertical temperature gradient and the uneven distribution of cooling load in the occupied level cannot be taken into account. Also it may not be energy efficient because areas without cooling requirement (e.g. no occupants) are conditioned simultaneously. This research will investigate how to improve the thermal comfort and energy efficiency of the air-conditioning systems for large-scale rooms by capitalizing a wireless sensor network and advanced control techniques. At least one sensor node will be installed at the occupied level in each area served by a single VAV supply air box. All of the sensor nodes and receivers constitute a wireless sensors network, which will be deployed to measure and transfer the temperature to a more sophisticated thermostat. In this thermostat, a robust multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) control algorithm will be developed to control each VAV box separately so as to deal with the unevenly distributed and time-varying load and improve occupants’ thermal comfort. This thermostat will also be designed to realize a demand-based temperature control, which will supply cooling only to areas with requirement and no cooling will be supplied if the areas have no requirement (e.g. no occupants). Energy saving potential of the new control design will be investigated and evaluated under different occupancy conditions by comparing it with the conventional design. Economic analysis will be performed to estimate the payback period for retrofitting the original control design. A large-scale lecture theatre in City University of Hong Kong will be used as an example platform to carry out this research. The outputs of this research will be used as a guideline for upgrading/retrofitting the conventional control design for large-scale rooms in terms of thermal comfort and energy saving. 大空間空泛應用于公共建築，包括大學，政府和商業大樓，為各類大型會議提供專業場所。在濕熱地區，如香港，大空間空調系統的能耗非常高。傳統的大空間空調變風量系統多采用單輸入單輸出的溫度控制器設計。這類設計根據在回風管内單點測量的溫度來調節送風量，以便將房間溫度控制到設定值。研究與實踐表明這類設計不能滿足熱舒適要求，也不能滿足越來越重要的建築節能要求。原因在於這類設計不能解決大空間溫度（垂直和水平）的不均勻分佈和負荷的不均勻分佈及時變特性。本課題將研究如何集成多輸入多數出的魯棒控制技術和無限傳感器網絡技術來解決上述問題。新設計將在用戶呼吸區安裝無限傳感器網絡來準確測量用戶呼吸區的實際溫度，采用多輸入多數出的魯棒控制技術來實現變風量系統的末端調節單元的獨立控制。獨立控制可以實現基於需求的溫度控制。如果一個區域沒有用戶，該區域將不再供給冷空氣。新設計的控制性能和它能帶來的節能潛力將通過模擬和試驗的方法來驗證。研究成果將用於指導大空間變風量空調系統的節能改造。

124012.label: Realisation of objectives
124012.value: Research Objective 1: we will construct a WSN for a large-scale lecture theatre in City University of Hong Kong as a platform and test-bed to strengthen the research of WSN for HVAC applications. The possible deficit and potential measurement problems will be studied when the wireless sensor nodes are installed at the places reachable by occupants. Research activities: A wireless sensor network was constructed at a studio in City University of Hong Kong. It has been used to collected data for several months. During this period, potential measurement problems have been identified. It was found that the wireless data were not reliable as wired data. Abnormal data were occasionally found, and data repeat, data loss and measurement outlier were the main types of abnormal data. In order to improve the quality of the measurement, a data process algorithm based on correlation analysis was developed to detect and reconstruct abnormal data. The algorithm has been test using the experiment data and the result was acceptable. Research Objective 2: We will retrofit the conventional control design for the VAV boxes. The whole large space will be virtually partitioned into several local areas (each area is served by one VAV box) and the thermo-coupling problem due to heat and mass transport phenomena, such as natural and forced convections, diffusion and dispersion etc., will be modelled in term of control. Then, a robust MIMO control algorithm will be developed to solve the coupling problem and to improve the temperature tracking ability of the thermostat under unevenly distributed and time-varying load conditions. The control performance, thermal comfort condition and energy consumption will be compared with the original control design. Research activities: A retrofit scheme has been developed, in which the whole large space was virtually partitioned into several zones (each zone is served by one VAV box). At least one wireless sensor is installed at each zone at the breathing level to measure the representative temperature around occupants. A robust temperature control approach has been developed by taking account of the thermal coupling between neighbouring zones. The control performance, thermal comfort and energy consumption was compared with the original control design, which shows that the proposed control is superior to the conventional control. Research Objective 3: we will study the feasibility of demand-based temperature control, which supplies cooling only to the areas with cooling requirement, by concerning thermal comfort. The energy saving potential will then be studied by considering the thermo-coupling problem under several typical occupancy conditions. The results will be used to qualify the energy saving potential of the demand-based temperature control for large-scale rooms. Research activities: To study the feasibility of the proposed demand-based temperature control, a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model was constructed. Energy saving potential was them investigated based on this model. Results showed that using the WSN and the developed demand-based control, energy saving potential can be larger than 10% whether at full load or partial load condition. Additionally, during this research, we developed a simple but practical control strategy for air-conditioning processes, which can be described by a first-order-plus-time delay model (such as heat-exchanging processes). We also carried out an experimental study using a typical classroom in our campus, inside which a number of wireless sensors were installed at the breathing level to investigate the temperature profiles. By comparing with a traditional design of temperature control (i.e. temperature sensor is installed inside a return air duct), 22% (216m3/h) and 32% (205m3/h) of supply airflow rate can be saved in fully and half occupied conditions in the mixing ventilation without scarifying thermal comfort. In the displacement ventilation, even though there was no supply airflow rate saving in fully occupied condition, 15% (86m3/h) reduction in the supply airflow rate was achieved in half occupied condition. Research Objective 4: We will economically analyze the proposed design and strategy using the example lecture theatre. A report on the economic analysis will be submitted to the office of Facility Management for considering retrofitting the example lecture as a showroom for technology-transfer DEMO by the university. Research activities: We carried out an economic analysis of the proposed design and strategy using a lecture theatre in our campus. It shows that the proposed design is economically feasible but may suffer from unpredicted occupants’ behaviors (as the sensor nodes should be installed at the breathing level, safety is a problem). We actually kept discussion with our colleagues in the department of facility management on the research process and they showed their interests in our work. We also collaborated with a colleague in the department of Electronic Engineering in this project on wireless sensor network.
