124012.label: Major findings and research outcome
124012.value: In this project, we carried out a study on enhancing the thermal comfort and energy efficiency of air-conditioning systems for large-scale rooms by integrating robust control and wireless sensor network. The major findings can be summarized as below: • Wireless sensor network can efficiently solve the temperature measurement problem of large-scale rooms. The temperature collected from wireless sensor network at the breathing level is more representative than that measured in the return air duct regarding to occupants’ thermal comfort. • The developed data process method can efficiently improve the measurement quality of wireless sensor network. As a large-scale room is still a closed space, sensors are more or less correlated in measurement. When an abnormal data is found from a sensor, its most correlated sensor is identified and used to reconstruct the abnormal data. This method is reliable and accurate to reconstruct abnormal data or lost data. • The developed demand-based control is robust and able to improve the temperature control of large-scale rooms. In the control, the large-scale room is divided into a number of zones, each of which is served by an independent variable-air-volume box. A collaborate control scheme manipulate the operation of those VAV boxes to provide cooling for the occupied zone. Both full load operation and partial load operation has been considered and validated. • Energy saving potential of the proposed strategy can be significant in both the mixing ventilation and the displacement ventilation scheme. In our experimental tests, the energy saving may reach to 15%. Research outcome: through this research we published 4 international journal papers and 2 international conference papers to report our main findings.

124012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
124012.value: In this project, we have demonstrated that the use of WSN and demanded-based control can efficiently improve the thermal comfort and energy efficiency of large-scale rooms. Theoretical development, numerical simulation and simple experimental studies have been completed. However, there is potential for further developments in order to promote practical applications of the proposed strategy. Further developments includes (1) comprehensive test of the proposed strategy; and (2) control package development. Currently, the proposed strategy was only tested in our campus. We hope to carry more tests in different large-scale rooms, such as shopping malls in commercial buildings. Different large-scale rooms may have different A/C layout and different inner shape, which will affect the quality of WSN signals and control performance. More tests will help us to understand the strength and weakness of the proposed strategy. Control package development will help HVAC engineers to understand the developed strategy. Comments from them should be very useful to improve the proposed strategy and promote its application. In the future research we will collaborate with industry to carry on the potential development.

124012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
124012.value: This research solves the temperature measurement problem in large-scale rooms. Conventionally, the representative temperature of a large-scale room is measured inside return air duct. However, this temperature cannot represent the temperature around occupants due to both vertical and horizontal temperature differences, where are naturally existent. Thus a temperature control based on this measurement may not satisfy the occupants’ requirements for thermal comfort. Wireless sensors are proposed to use and install at breathing level to collect temperatures. We have demonstrated that wireless sensors can measure the temperature around occupants and the temperature control based on the wireless measurement can significantly improve the thermal comfort. This research solves the temperature control problem in large-scale rooms. As large-scale rooms are always partially occupied during operation, a demand-based temperature control is proposed to save energy use. This method divides the large-scale room into a number of zones, each of which is served by an independent variable-air-volume box. Only the occupied zone will be provided cooling. We have shown that the demand-based temperature control can save over 15% of energy use annually. As a summary, this research contributes to building thermal comfort and building energy efficiency, and thus to building sustainability.

124212.label: Realisation of objectives
124212.value: We investigated cell migration with detailed quantifications of intracellular characteristics. We showed that the subcellular cytoskeleton arrangements including both actin filaments and microtubules were highly correlated with migration behaviors of both single cells and cell populations. Nucleus and cell body characteristics were also demonstrated as potential indicators of cell migration behaviors and even the subcellular contractile force distributions, which might provide an alternative and non-invasive approach to characterize the CSK contractility of cells and intracellular cytoskeleton organizations. Detailed conclusions of this work were as follows: 1. Both ROCK and MLCK could distinctly regulate the arrangements of cytoskeleton. We quantitatively investigated the distribution of subcellular actin in single cells by defining ratios of actin at cell periphery (P-actin) and actin in cell inner parts (C-actin). Actin stress fibers exhibited two distinct organizations after inhibiting ROCK or MLCK, where most of actin stress fibers in cell bodies were disturbed but with apparent actin at cell periphery after inhibiting ROCK activities, inducing a relative high ratio of P-actin/C-actin. Importantly, our results also demonstrated that microtubules distinctly exhibited in single cells, which may indict the dynamic interactions of cytoskeleton might play critical roles in cell migration behaviors. 2. We investigated single cell migration behaviors with different actin arrangements by considering the correlations among them. Our results showed that cells with lower ratios of P-actin/C-actin shown reduced cell migration velocities. Specially, our study on control cell migration behaviors demonstrated a positive correlation (Pearson’s coefficient is ~0.67) between ratios of P-actin/C-actin and migration velocities, which implied that subcellular cytoskeleton distributions were largely involved in cell migration behaviors. 3. We examined morphometric characteristics of cell bodies and nucleus by considering the cell migration behaviors and subcellular contractile force distributions. Our results indicated that relative low ratio of P-actin/C-actin facilitated the alignments of cell bodies and nucleus, which could be demonstrated by the high correlations between stress fiber and cell body orientations, stress fiber and nucleus orientations. Our results also showed the possible correlations between cell migration velocities and alignments of cell bodies and nucleus. In addition, subcellular contractile forces measured by micropost array detectors also exhibited distinct distributions for cells with alignments of cell bodies and nucleus, which demonstrated that intracellular characteristics including cell bodies, stress fibers and nucleus were highly consistent with CSK contractility status and cell migration behaviors. 4. We studied behaviors of cell population migration by applying a simple yet efficient wound-healing assay with patterned PDMS stamps. Consistent with single cells, ROCK and MLCK play distinct roles on regulating cytoskeleton arrangements and cell population migration. Differently, our results on statistics of nucleus orientations showed that cell populations with relative low ratios of P-actin/C-actin exhibited a strong ability of maintaining the nucleus characteristics. Therefore, it appeared that intracellular characteristics including actin distributions, cell body and nucleus were highly related to both single cell migration and cell population migration. It provided us a feasible method for studying the capabilities of cell migration and intercellular/intracellular contractile force organizations, which might shed some light on the mechanisms of differentiation in wound healing and even embryonic morphogenesis. This research mainly focused on thecell migration and intracellular characteristics including cytoskeleton arrangements, cell body and nucleus morphology. For single cell migration studies, one possible concern was the diversity of cells inducing the variance of conclusions. We can suppress this by conducting the statistics analysis based on large number of samples. From the view of cell populations, most of cell biological behaviors included not only cell migration, but also cell proliferation in wound healing process. Short-term (<2 hr) cell population behaviors might be dominated by cell movements, but we cannot exclude the effects of cell proliferation on subcellular cytoskeleton arrangements. Furthermore, considering the potential regulation of cell population contractile force on morphogenesis, this work were lack of adequate demonstrations on coordination between cell-population cytoskeleton arrangements and contractile force profiles, which might be improved by combining the wound-healing assay with micropost array detectors.

124212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
124212.value: This research investigated the possible relationships among cell migration, CSK contractility and intracellular characteristics under different cytoskeleton arrangements in the eyes of crosstalk among different subcellular organelles including actin filaments, microtubule networks and nucleus, which might shed light on the essential functions of cell migration on wound-healing process. 124212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
124212.value: Cardiovascular disease remains the human health problem causing the largest numbers of death for decades. This proposed research aims at developing a unique platform to quantitatively investigate the human vascular endothelial wound healing process using a novel cell patterning technique. Human vascular endothelial cells are first patterned in microchannels under variable microenvironment with the defined spatial dissolved oxygen (DO) profiles, supplying either the atmospheric DO (~20 %) to maintain local cell viability or the fully oxygenated level to kill cells in the unpatterned ‘artificial wounds’. Subsequent cell cultivation is then performed by supplying atmospheric DO over the entire channels to support cell growth towards the wound regions. The quantitative analyses on both dynamics of the cell distribution and the intracellular components are performed to determine the dominant factors such as shear, cell contractility and morphology. The major contributions of this work are to provide an unprecedented cell patterning technique for the endothelial wound healing analysis, to characterize quantitatively the healing process, and to provide insights on the responsive mechanism and the potential treatments for the vascular diseases.

124312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
124312.value: 由於其獨特的電子和光電特性，氮化鎵材料一直是一個研究熱點。氮化鎵光電子器件的消費市場包括激光二極管和節能的發光二極管。基於氮化鎵的功率器件能夠確保高效的功率轉換。射頻氮化鎵電子器件目前已應用於無線數據傳輸，並將在不遠的將來擴展到整個電信行業。雖然矽依然是最為普及的半導體材料，但氮化鎵獨特的材料特性將來一塊傳統矽基電子器件所無法覆蓋的新領域。相較于氮化鎵光電子器件與電子器件所取得的研究進展，此材料優良的機電特性所帶來的應用潛力還幾乎未被挖掘。 在過去15年中，研究人員對於利用矽製作機械振動器件（稱為諧振器）以便與矽基集成電路進行整合進行了大量研究。諧振器給幾乎所有的電子產品提供了脈搏。目前，矽基諧振器技術已經日趨成熟並在最近6年間孵化出了大量公司。相較而言，對氮化鎵機電諧振器的研究最近才展開並且停留在較低頻率（MHz範圍）。由於氮化鎵受到射頻電子器件的青睞，因此製造氮化鎵機械諧振器（工作在GHz頻段）的方法以及潛在的科學理論具有重要的研究價值。 這項研究計劃的目標在於探究并實現工作在接近1GHz側向振動模式的氮化鎵微機械諧振器。這種諧振器目前還未有研究團隊成功實現。高頻率通常以犧牲性能為代價：導致較低的品質因數（Q）和較大的運動阻抗。本研究計劃中的0.75GHz氮化鎵諧振器預計將實現大於1000的Q值以及小於10kΩ的運動阻抗。 通過與香港科技大學的陳敬教授合作，我們將開發製作此器件的制程工藝。我們將採用側向體振動模式來取代常見的彎曲振動模式，從而在0.75GHz的工作頻率實現預計的Q值。我們將結合優化器件設計，改進制程工藝以及採用新的換能機制來有效降低運動阻抗。這些方法包括在側向體振動的諧振器中建造一顆諧振體高電子遷移率晶體管來提供主動式的機電增益。諧振器將首先工作在基本模態，然後激發高階諧波達到0.75GHz的工作頻率。

These include piezoelectric transduction, integrated HEMT, and switchable transduction through control of the 2DEG layer. Objective 2: We have investigated and implemented higher order GaN resonators with Q factors over 1000 using the methods explored in Objective 1.

124312.label: Major findings and research outcome
124312.value: We have found in the implementation of the concepts explored in this project that the fabrication process required is mostly similar to what is used to fabricated radio-frequency HEMT devices. As such, the process is compatible with the technology for fabricating HEMTs, which was a driving motivation for this project. We have implemented HEMTs on the same process used to fabricate the GaN resonators. We could also track the depletion of the 2DEG layer as a bottom electrode through our measurements of the GaN resonator.

124312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
124312.value: During the course of the research, we found that the piezoelectric coefficients of GaN were not as high as assumed in the literature. Furthermore, fabrication of the GaN resonators was complicated. Purchasing of GaN wafers to fabricate the resonators was financially challenging with the limited funding, compounded further by a lack of options of vendors willing to sell. Given these limitations, we have found that AlN resonators would be a more sustainable direction to develop the research in this area. The project has led us to collaborations with a research group in Germany who have come to the same consensus that this would be prudent direction to move towards.

124312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
124312.value: GaN has been a material of interest for lighting (note the Nobel prize for blue LED based on GaN), high power and high frequency electronics. In contrast, their use to make mechanical devices that can be fabricated in a process that is compatible with the technology for fabricating current electronic GaN devices has hardly been explored. The research in this project fills that knowledge gap. We have demonstrated the feasibility as well as challenges in realizing GaN resonators through the research in this project.

124412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
124412.value: Indoor air quality is an important public health matter because people in the developed world spend ~90% of their time indoor and inhale over 14,000 liters of air per day when performing normal activities. This topic is especially relevant and important in Hong Kong as it has the largest number of skyscrapers in the world with over 7,600 and in this densely populated city of 7 million people, many economic and leisure activities are held within indoor environments. One public health risk in the indoor environments is the transmission of contagious pathogenic microorganisms through the airborne route and sick building syndrome, where occupants experience acute health effects, discomforts and allergic symptoms, is another health concern that is thought to be associated with bioaerosols. The economic losses due to sick building syndrome can be substantial if employees require time off from work to recover. At the moment, much of the scientific knowledge regarding the bacteria that are present within indoor air has been derived from culturing studies. However, given that >99% of microbes are not culturable under standard conditions in the laboratory, this suggests that the bacterial diversity within indoor air has been substantially underestimated. Therefore, to gain better insights into the bacterial diversity within the indoor atmospheric environments, we propose an innovative research plan that uses advanced culture-independent molecular methods to query the composition and dynamics of airborne bacteria for the purpose of air quality improvements. Specifically, we will apply high-throughput pyrosequencing of the bacterial DNA to circumvent the drawbacks of culturing methods. By sampling diverse indoor environments that have different ventilation systems, construction materials, occupant loads, and building functions, we will come to understand the composition, diversity, gene content, and viability of the airborne bacteria as well as the correlation between environmental conditions and the dynamics of the bacteria. A throughout understanding of the airborne bacteria within the indoor built environments will ultimately enable us to derive best practices for improving indoor air quality and design buildings that can best protect the health of the occupants.

124412.label: Realisation of objectives
124412.value: The overarching goal of the proposed project is to establish a culture-independent method based on DNA sequencing to detect the composition and diversity of airborne bacteria within indoor environments. This represents a substantial advancement over the current method of culturing microorganisms on agar plates, which is known to capture less than 1% of the overall microbial diversity. Through this project, we have successfully established the standard operating procedures to apply DNA sequencing to monitor bioaerosol within indoor environments. Specifically, we have developed the methods for sampling bioaerosol, extracting DNA from the low biomass air sample, sequencing the samples with a next-generation sequencing platform, and analyzing the sequencing data with a custom developed bioinformatics pipeline. Subsequently, we have applied the methods to a number of interesting indoor environments in Hong Kong including subways, residential homes and an energy-efficient building. From these studies, we have obtained a mechanistic understanding on the factors that are important and can affect the microbial composition and diversity in different indoor environments; hence, all objectives in this project have been achieved. As part of the education plan of this ECS project, we have also trained a number of undergraduate students to become familiar with indoor air quality and they gained hands-on research experience.

124412.label: Major findings and research outcome
124412.value: The results from this project have been published in a number of journal publications (Part C). The manuscript of Leung et al. (2014) describes the airborne bacterial communities in the subway network of Hong Kong. Extensive spatial and temporal sampling was conducted both inside and outside the subway. We found that different phylogenetic communities were present in each subway line and the composition of the bacterial community was dependent on the architectural characteristics, the nearby outdoor air bacterial composition, and connectedness with other subway lines. Temporal variations of the bacterial communities as well as the influence of environmental conditions were also noted. From our subway study, we noted that a lot of airborne bacteria are associated with the human skins. Upon further review of the literature, we found that skin associated bacteria of the Chinese population have not been extensively studied. Hence, in the next part of this project where we investigated residential homes in Hong Kong, we analyzed the bacterial communities in air and on objective surfaces as well as on occupants’ skin. In residential homes, as detailed in the manuscript of Wilkins et al. (2015), we noted that surfaces in homes bear the bacterial fingerprint of household occupant skin and the indoor air contained abundant human-associated taxa. However, we found that that there was little transfer of skin bacteria to the indoor air. Hence, we postulated that the indoor air bacterial communities largely originated from the outdoor and other body sites. In our parallel work to analyze the occupant skin bacteria (Leung et al. (2015)), we described that age, gender, and household were associated with differences in the skin bacterial populations. Interestingly, comparisons with different population groups showed race-based clustering of the bacterial communities. This study represents one of the first to characterize the Chinese skin bacteria. Other contributions of this project include the development of a new bioaerosol sampler (Wubulihairen, et al. (2015)) and characterization of the bioaerosol in a Zero Carbon Building, showing that how the ventilation system is operated for energy saving purposes can affect the bacterial composition (Leung et al. 2016). In addition, this project allowed us to start investigating fungi (Leung et al. 2016) and we prepared a review article discussing the bacterial communities found indoors (Leung et al. 2016). Overall, the findings from this project provided a fundamental understanding of the bacteria that are present in the unique indoor environments in Hong Kong.

124412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
124412.value: In a densely populated city with over 7 million people and over 7,600 skyscrapers, the people of Hong Kong, like many other citizens in urbanized cities worldwide, spend majority of their time indoor. Hence, indoor air quality, in particular the composition airborne bacteria, is of significance to the health and comfort of the occupants. Most of our current knowledge regarding airborne bacteria originated from traditional culturing methods, which fail to capture the vast microbial diversity as most bacteria cannot be easily grown under standard conditions in the laboratory. In this project, we have successfully implemented a culture-independent method based on advanced DNA sequencing methods to detect airborne bacteria. The diversity of bacteria detected was relatively high in a number of indoor environments that we have studied. Furthermore, we found that architectural design, outdoor conditions, occupant density, and ventilation modes can alter the composition of the airborne bacteria. Overall, we have developed an in-depth understanding of the composition of the bioaerosol within indoor environments and determined the factors that can influence the airborne bacteria composition.

124512.value: 蛋白質是在活的生物體中發現的最重要的分子，如酶，抗體，傳感器，運輸，其他無數角色之間的運作。蛋白質的功能基本上是確定于其3維結構，在最近幾年，這些結構的識別已經受到大量深入的研究。人體内有10萬种左右的蛋白質。然而，在准备这个项目的时候， 所有生物中，只有76,288所有生物體的蛋白質結構已發現 并存入了蛋白質數據库。有兩種常見的生物實驗室的技術來估計的一種蛋白質的結構：X射線晶體衍射和核磁共振（NMR）。在PDB中的大部分結構，绝大多数用X光透視技術，通過NMR測定中只有約9106。結晶機制的限制X射線晶體學，從確定重要的結構動力學，如運動的電子迴路。缺點是不存在的NMR光譜，它允許以確定環路的動態性能和域結構。然而，目前，NMR譜是昂貴的，並且需要非常繁瑣的實驗室工作執行。一個單一的結構通過NMR確定的成本估計在美元150000美元，需要一個訓練有素的博士後研究員半年的工作。很明顯可以通過新的結構計算系統较少這些費用，它需要較少的NMR數據是錯誤的，容错的，是算法更有效。為了實現這樣的系統，我們把獲得的專門結構預測研究的知識用在NMR結構計算中。這兩個問題在許多方面重疊：而輸入的結構預測的氨基酸序列，NMR結構計算的輸入將是一個氨基酸序列和一組從NMR譜得到的約束。在這兩個問題，輸出的是蛋白質三維結構。

124512.label: Realisation of objectives
124512.value: Objective 1 To calculate the structures, we first need to align structures. Although assessing the similarities and differences between protein structures is a common practice in structural biology, efficiently performing this comparison is critical in some applications. The need to obtain structures similar to the new protein from these databases motivates the neighbor protein structure retrieval problem: given a query protein structure and a database of protein structures, retrieve all the structures in the database that are similar to the query structure. We have impleted ContactLib, a complete contact group library, which is to be used as fingerprints of protein structures. FragBag and local feature frequency profile (LFFP) are two promising tools that are closely related. Our ContactLib is different from FragBag and LFFP in following ways: (i) FragBag and LFFP are developed on general structure fragments, whereas ContactLib introduces both local and remote contact groups eliminating potentially weak contact groups; (ii) FragBag and LFFP use 3D coordinates or 2D distance matrices, whereas ContactLib introduces 1D distance vectors that can be efficiently indexed; (iii) FragBag and LFFP require a predefined word alphabet, whereas ContactLib avoids such word alphabet and introduces some freedom of specifying similarity thresholds at runtime; and (iv) FragBag and LFFP use word frequency profiles and distance functions from the text information retrieval problem, whereas ContactLib introduces a combined hit-rate scoring function for the neighbor protein structure retrieval problem. Because the word alphabet of LFFP is not publicly available, we focus on comparing ContactLib and FragBag in this article. We built two ContactLibs: ContactLib-9L, which models local contacts, and ContactLib-3R, which models remote contacts. Using one or both of ContactLib-9L and ContactLib-3R, we tested our method on the high-quality protein structure subset of SCOP30 containing 3297 protein structures. For each protein structure, we retrieved its neighbor protein structures from the rest. According to the Receiver-Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, the best area under the ROC curve (AUROC), archived by ContactLib, is as high as 0.960. This is a significant improvement compared with 0.747, the best result achieved by FragBag Objective 2 We have developed a computational approach capable of predicting and describing side-chain polymorphisms—one that does not require experimental inputs such as electron density maps. Our approach is an extension of a particular class of algorithms for side-chain prediction that are based on belief propagation (BP). The conformation of a protein side chain can be parameterized by a sequence of dihedral angles. Each side chain may rotate about its dihedral angles, as long as there are no steric collisions. These dihedral angles are continuous in nature, but most computational approaches discretize them. Our primary extension was to model these dihedral angles more appropriately as continuous variables rather than discrete ones. Straight-forward as such an extension may sound, it would have remained difficult within the BP framework if a variation called “particle belief propagation” (PBP) had not become available. Using PBP, we were able to make inferences about residue-specific distributions in the continuous domain, and it is clear that these distributions encode information about the conformational polymorphism of each residue. We then compared the polymorphisms that we predicted with the ones extracted from crystallography data by Ringer. Overall, we found the two sets of results to be in reasonably good agreement with each other. Ringer has successfully uncovered side-chain conformations that were formerly considered mere artifacts of (or noise from) electron density data. While Ringer found these alternate conformations by re-evaluating electron density maps, we can predict them with an improved—and, in fact, fundamentally different—side-chain prediction algorithm, one that works in a continuous domain. Objective 3 To refine the structure, we first obtained a set of candidate structure from database. We develop an approach to detect the conformational changes from unbound states to bound states. Our approach examines a set of scaled structures as candidates for the bound structure (possibly with conformational changes), and uses a new energy function to select the best solutions. To obtain the set of scaled structures, we maintain a database of structures, from which raw candidates for the conformationally changed residues can be rapidly selected. These candidates are then refined through an efficient method based on multidimensional scaling. This allows accurate near-native structures to be constructed with a minimal number of sampling steps. One advantage in this approach is that, whereas the large search space of existing methods requires intensive computational power and produces a large portion of conformations different from the native complex, in our method the geometrical constraints—imposed by the distance between two residues respectively at both ends of an interface fragment—eliminate a substantial number of unlikely candidate structures. One caveat is that for our method to work, the regions far from the interface should be almost unchanged in the protein complex. We then carefully constructed an energy function for structure candidate selection, since the effectiveness of the function is a crucial factor in determining the resultant structure. We develop a new statistical energy item, which is combined linearly with four other energy items to rank the poses and to direct the search of the plausible conformations. We also identify two new features for structures calculations: the coupled dihedral angles on the interfaces and the geometrical information on π–π interactions. Inspired by dihedral angle biases in conformations, we perform a systematic study on the dihedral angles formed by the interface residues. We use a mixture of bivariate von Mises distributions to model the correlation of the coupled dihedral angles. The attraction of π–π interaction depends on the relative orientation of two aromatic rings. We use a mixture of bivariate normal distributions to capture the orientation of two aromatic rings on the interfaces. Using 6,438 complexes, we parametrize the joint distribution of each new feature to denote local structural biases of the interface residues. These two features can be adopted to limit the search space, for discovering near-native poses. Then, we produce a new method to construct the energy function for protein–protein interface prediction, which includes the new features as well as the existing energy items, such as dDFIRE energy, side-chain energy, atomic contact energy, and amino acid energy. The dDFIRE energy is an all-atom statistical function. The side-chain atoms of interface residues are packed by SCWRL4, and the side-chain energy is extracted. The problem of modeling side-chain is a well-studied. The atomic contact energy is produced by an atomic energy measure. The amino acid energy is constructed by probabilities of the interface residue pairs. Based on these energy items, we train 79 SVM models, one for each complex in the training set. Finally, given a pair of input proteins, we define a score to select one of the 79 SVM models and use such an SVM model to further select the output poses. We develop a software package, NewDoBi, to include all the proposed ideas. Experiments show that our method achieves better results than the state-of-the-art methods.

124512.label: Major findings and research outcome
124512.value: We proposed an implemented efficient algorithm for protein structure confirmation [6]. In the algorithms, we adopted multidimensional scaling (MDS) to rebuild protein conformations. MDS takes a set of (noisy) distance constraints as input. We develop a new energy item for determining the orientation of docking subunits and selecting of plausible conformational changes. Experimental results illustrate that our implemented program FlexDoBi achieves better results. On 20 complexes, we obtained an average iRMSD of 1.55Å, which compares favorably with the average iRMSD of 1.94Å for FiberDock. Compared to ZDOCK, our results are of 0.27Å less in average iRMSD of the medium difficulty group. A variety of structure alignment algorithms and programs has been designed and implemented for this purpose. A major drawback with existing structure alignment programs is that they require a large amount of computational time, rendering them infeasible for pairwise alignments on large collections of structures. To overcome this drawback, a fragment alphabet learned from known structures has been introduced [1]. The method, however, considers local similarity only, and therefore occasionally assigns high scores to structures that are similar only in local fragments.We propose a novel approach that eliminates false positives, through the comparison of both local and remote similarity, with little compromise in speed. Two kinds of contact libraries (ContactLib) are introduced to fingerprint protein structures effectively and efficiently. Each contact group of the contact library consists of one local or two remote fragments and is represented by a concise vector. These vectors are then indexed and used to calculate a new combined hit-rate score to identify similar protein structures effectively and efficiently. We tested our method on the high-quality protein structure subset of SCOP30 containing 3,297 protein structures. For each protein structure of the subset, we retrieved its neighbor protein structures from the rest of the subset. The best area under the Receiver-Operating Characteristic curve, archived by ContactLib, is as high as 0.960. This is a significant improvement compared with 0.747, the best result achieved by FragBag. We also demonstrated that incorporating remote contact information is critical to consistently retrieve accurate neighbor protein structures for all- query protein structures. We discovered in the HMC II proteins, some residues are more significant the others. Less than two dozens of residues can classify most of the HMC sequences successfully [2]. In [3]. We proposed a method to solve the side chain packing problem via particle belief propagation.

124512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
124512.value: This project together with our FALCON system will be extended as a cloud based system. Protein structure related research studies have steep learning curves. It usually takes excellent candidates one to get into the area. One of the major reasons is due to intensive codes. We will build pack our code into modules to reduce the learning barriers. We will apply learning in solving the protein folding protein. Most of the current existing methods for ab initio assembly are based on Monto Carlo search, which is inefficient. In each step of Monto Carlo, some torsional angles are altered randomly and a new protein structure candidate is then built. This structure is then evaluated by an energy function. This step is consuming as most of the structure candidates are filtered by the energy function. Yet, nature folds a protein fast. Most of the structures are folded within microseconds. It implies that nature does not adopt a Monto Carlo approach, and there are some intrinsic patterns in structural folding. We will utilize the super computers, and apply deep learning methods for structure folding. This will enable us to obtain the intrinsic patterns and help us to fold a protein efficiently in silico.

124512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
124512.value: Proteins are the most important molecules found in living organisms, functioning as enzymes, antibodies, sensors, transporters, among myriads of other roles. The understanding of these functions of proteins has great implications to the study of the biological and medical sciences. Since the function of a protein is essentially determined by its 3-dimensional structure, the identification of these structures has come under intense study in recent years. To understanding these roles, and to understanding life, we need to know the 3D (three-dimensional) structures of the proteins; that is, we need to know the 3D coordinates of atoms. Two common web-lab techniques are used to estimate the structure of a protein: X-ray crystallography and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR). Most of the structures in thePDB were determined using X-ray techniques. NMR spectroscopy, determines the protein structure based on the magnetic properties of its constituent atomic nuclei. The measurement of structures can be performed in a very short time, thus allowing the technique to identify loop dynamics and domain structures. NMR spectroscopy is expensive and requires very tedious lab work to perform. In this work, we have develop models, algorithms and program which can relieve the tedious work.

124712.label: Realisation of objectives
124712.value: All three objectives have been achieved. Stratum ventilation can be coupled with different air side systems. The air ducts/plenums are installed in cavity partition walls instead of in false ceiling or in elevated floor voids. The installation of duct, plenum and/or terminal is safer without scaffold. Since the air circulation is not higher than that of the conventional systems, the ductwork of stratum ventilation does not occupy more indoor space. For stratum ventilation, supply air streams from two directions can minimize the influence of obstacles. Personalized ventilation and stratum ventilation, both are non-whole-volume ventilation, share similar principles ― making full use of the freshness and cooling effect (movement and low temperature) of the supply air. Stratum ventilation is less flexible (the flexibility could be improved later when in-situ adjustable air terminals are developed specifically for stratum ventilation). Whereas the advantages of stratum ventilation are: 1. single system (no background ventilation system is needed); 2. serving mobile occupants, e.g. the cases of homes, retail shops and corridors; and 3. simple and inexpensive design and installation because no ductwork runs in the occupied zone. An equivalent draft temperature (EDT) for stratum ventilation is defined and found to be an effective simple evaluation tool for determining thermal comfort in a stratum ventilated room.

124712.label: Major findings and research outcome
124712.value: As a non-whole-volume air distribution method, stratum ventilation has been found to maintain a reverse and modest temperature gradient between the head and ankle levels with the lowest temperature and best air quality at the head level. Experiments and human subject tests were conducted in an environmental chamber. We measured velocity and temperature profiles, and collected the occupants’ subjective responses on the thermal sensation and comfort of the whole body and of different body segments. The parameters studied included air supply and return types and positions, ventilation rate, supply air temperature and velocity, thermal length of air jests and furniture arrangements. The emerging methodology of computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with a human body thermoregulation model has been improved and applied in simulations to reduce costs of the study. The data measured and collected in the chamber were used to further improve and validate the CFD model. Optimal design conditions for stratum ventilation were determined. A simple evaluation tool characterizing room thermal comfort conditions under stratum ventilation was developed. Design guidelines for stratum ventilation has been established.

124712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
124712.value: Previous research projects on indoor air quality, energy performance and thermal comfort by means of objective experiments, human subject tests and CFD simulations since 2005 suggest that stratum ventilation performs well. Stratum ventilation was thought to maintain non-uniform thermal environments, but this study, by means of measurement and human subject test, suggests that the occupied zone of a stratum ventilated room is a uniform thermal environment. If this is confirmed, the knowledge on stratum ventilation will be fundamentally changed on the following two aspects: (1) the mechanism of thermal comfort under stratum ventilation; and (2) the methodology for stratum ventilation design. This is also important for the practical application of stratum ventilation because the design methodology for a uniform air distribution is mature and familiar to the practicing engineers.

124712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
124712.value: To reduce energy use in buildings, significantly higher room temperatures are recommended by several governments in East Asia in recent years. To maintaining thermal comfort under this warm condition becomes an imminent challenge. This project provides a solution for small and medium sized rooms under warm conditions. Stratum ventilation supplies air directly at the most important body part - head, stratum ventilation allows the ambience to be warm while maintaining thermal comfort. It also improves air quality since the supply air is directly delivered to the breathing zone. Besides the locations of air supplies, the equipment of stratum ventilation is almost the same as conventional systems, except that cavity partitions, instead of the ceiling/underfloor voids, are most likely to house the air duct and/or plenums. The installation is therefore safer and cheaper without the need for scaffold. The space occupied by the system is less because the needed cooling capacity is smaller due to better energy performance. 125012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
125012.value: 神经系统疾病一直是人類健康的重大威脅之一，全球影响超过一亿人。僅阿尔茨海默氏癥在香港就有超过11万例的患者。然而，对许多極具破壞性的神經系統疾病仍然缺乏有效的藥物和治療手段。針對神經系統疾病的藥物篩選的成功率也極低，主要受限於現有的藥物篩選技術。 人類大腦所具有的獨特性和複雜性需要一個全新的高通量的篩選模式， 允許針對特定的神經功能並行篩選數以千計的化合物或生物製劑。在此擬進行的研究中，我們計劃開發一種全新的神經-電子接口，可以在硬幣大小的嵌入微电极阵列的生物芯片上創建可靠地、具有生理功能的神經元網絡。這個全新的系統將允許以合理的成本，從分子和電信號多個不同角度高通量的檢測特定藥物/生物製劑對神經網絡功能的影響。成功實現本研究計劃，將有機會極大地幫助神經系統疾病的藥物篩選，顯著提高藥物開發的成功率。

125012.label: Major findings and research outcome
125012.value: In this study, a combination of electrical engineering, bioengineering and neurobiology approach was applied to develop a novel integrated system for high-throughput screens targeting CNS. This system permitted the creation of reproducible, reliable, yet physiologically relevant in vitro neuronal network for modeling critical aspects of brain functions on a coin-sized chip embedded with microscale electrode arrays, and thus allowed high-throughput detection of both molecular and electrical changes in neuronal networks in response to specific chemicals/biologics at reasonable cost. Importantly, the on-chip neuro-electronic interface provides a simple way to probe the neuronal network dynamics at single cell resolution. Changes in such dynamics is directly resulted from synaptogenesis and synaptic plasticity, which is closely related to advanced brain functions such as learning and memory, as well as many neurological diseases and disorders.

125012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
125012.value: It is our vision that successful development of the technology can significantly increase the chances of success in pharmaceutical drug screens for neurological diseases and disorders.

125012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
125012.value: Neurological diseases and disorders have been one of the greatest threats to public health, affecting over one billion people worldwide. For example, Alzheimer’s disease (AD) alone affects over 110,000 patients in Hong Kong. Despite the expenditure of billions of dollars on the development of new pharmaceuticals targeting the central nervous system (CNS), there are still no therapies against many devastating neurological diseases and disorders. Hence, there is an urgent need to find better drugs for developing therapeutic intervention targeting CNS. Yet, the success rate in drug screens for neurological diseases is extremely low; limitations of existing screening technologies have seriously hindered discovery of new pharmaceuticals. The brain possesses a unique and dramatic complexity that requires a new paradigm in pharmaceutical screening: a high-throughput platform that allows parallel screening thousands of chemicals/biologics targeting the most sophisticated neural activities. In this study, we developed a novel neuro-electronic interface, which allows high-throughput detection of both molecular and electrical changes in neuronal networks in response to specific chemicals/biologics at reasonable cost. Such technology can significantly increase the chances of success in pharmaceutical drug screens for neurological diseases and disorders.

125212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
125212.value: A remarkable feature of the growth in wireless data usage is that many new devices today are operating in the wireless spectrum that are meant to be shared among many different users. Yet, the sharing of the spectrum is far from perfect. Due to the broadcast nature of the wireless medium, interference is a major source of performance impairment. Current systems suffer from deteriorating quality due to fixed resource allocation that fails to consider interference. It is therefore of paramount importance to study optimal resource allocation techniques to fully realize the untapped benefits of shared bandwidth use and to mitigate the harmful effect of interference. As networks saturate, new wireless technologies like Femtocell are deployed to improve link quality and extend wireless service coverage indoors by connecting to the backbone network via the digital subscriber line or cable. This greatly multiplies bandwidth use and capacity. Because femtocells utilize spectrum currently employed by macro-cellular networks, interference can result between cells. For example, a macrocell with a femtocell or a femtocell with another femtocell. The greatest challenge will be to coordinate the sharing of spectrum between the macrocell and the femtocell, and then coordinate the sharing of spectrum between the femtocells. This is especially important because sharing must be done fairly in a collaborative and distributed manner. Maintaining a balanced egalitarian fairness operation however becomes highly problematic since interference rises rapidly with the density of ad-hoc femtocell deployment. Without appropriate resource coordination, the network can become unstable or operate in a highly inefficient and unfair manner. To understand this wireless balancing act is one of the challenges faced by femtocell networks. These fairness resource allocation problems are nonlinear nonconvex optimization problems that are notoriously difficult to solve. Building on our recent success of using advances in nonlinear Perron-Frobenius theory to solve several open problems in this field, we shall provide several novel theoretical frameworks and techniques to solve these problems. Under these frameworks, we shall develop several distributed algorithms under realistic nontrivial power and interference constraints, channel fading effects and low-complexity requirement. This proposal further proposes a unifying framework to analyze cross-layer adaptation for multi-hop transmissions and multiple antenna beamforming in a jointly optimal way. This project will make significant profound contributions to the nonlinear Perron-Frobenius theory and optimization theory. Its impact is even larger on applicability to future wireless networks as society’s reliance on wireless networked communications continues to expand tremendously.

125212.label: Realisation of objectives
125212.value: The scope of the investigation undertaken in this GRF Project includes proposing a nonlinear Perron-Frobenius theory framework to analyze wireless network optimization problems that are relevant to next-generation networks such as femtocell and cognitive radio networks. We also analyze the design of power control algorithms and rate adaptation algorithms for cross-layer optimization. We also prove theoretical analytic results, make computational evaluation, and make initial progress in developing wireless network resource adaptation algorithms and study the applications to mobile data trading in wireless networks. Notably, all the project objectives have been achieved successfully and the project outputs consist of the publication of nine top-tiered international journal publications as well as the training and successful graduation of two Ph.D. students supervised by the PI. We have also developed experimental methodologies and conducted extensive experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithms in the real-world mobile networks.

125212.label: Major findings and research outcome
125212.value: Our major findings and research outcome are summarized as follows: We have analyzed how to solve wireless network optimization problems that find important applications in next-generation wireless networks using our developed nonlinear Perron-Frobenius theory framework. These problems are typically hard to solve due to the non-convexity hurdles and the requirement for distributed algorithms. In particular, we propose a novel approach to solve a class of non-convex max-min problems that can guarantee egalitarian fairness to wireless users. The key is to analyse the set of specially-crafted fixed-point equations corresponding to the optimality conditions. Many important wireless features can be incorporated in the optimization such as outage probability due to channel fading and beam-forming control of transmit antennae. Our results with applications to single-hop heterogeneous wireless networks were published in IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking (2013), thus fulfilling Objective 1. The developed distributed power control algorithms and interference management techniques were later extended significantly to the joint optimisation of beam-forming and power control in IEEE Transactions on Wireless Comms (2013) and IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing (2012) thereby fulfilling Objective 2. We have also developed experimental methodologies and conducted extensive experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithms in the wireless networks using mobile computing software to adapt the transmit powers and evaluating the overall wireless performance. In the IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications (2013) and INFOCOM 2014, we studied the optimal signal-to-interference-noise ratio assignment problem to analyze performance merits and trade-offs for network utility maximisation in cognitive radio networks. We also extended the techniques into femtocell so as to satisfy performance requirements, fulfilling Objective 4. In the two publications in IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications (2014), we also developed distributed rate adaptation schemes with cross-layer optimization for multi-hop heterogeneous femtocell networks by leveraging the relationship between Lagrange dual solution and the nonlinear Perron-Frobenius theory, thereby fulfilling Objective 3. In fact, these work were extended to beam-forming control for maximizing throughput in IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications (2015), fulfilling Objective 2. In INFOCOM 2015, we expanded the application of the Perron-Frobenius theory framework to design computationally fast mobile data trading algorithms together with pricing schemes. In the Foundations and Trends in Networking monograph, a highly-regarded journal output authored by authoritative author, we provide a tutorial overview and report of the development of the Perron-Frobenius theory to solve non-convex wireless network optimization problems.

125212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
125212.value: One of the most interesting directions for further development is to explore the use of our developed Perron-Frobenius theory framework to analyze algorithm design and optimization techniques for the wireless Internet of Things network which have heterogeneous network connectivity such as WiFi. It is important to understand whether non-convexity hurdles arise from these optimization problems and how to adapt the optimization algorithms for this new network application. Our study builds up a strong foundation for broadband cellular connectivity, and it is expected that our results on characterizing the wireless performance and computational algorithms for wireless cellular connectivity can be generalized to the heterogeneous setting of combined cellular and WiFi connectivity. As further development, we can study how to utilize the Perron-Frobenius theory framework to design cross-layer optimization algorithms for the wireless Internet of Things. Lastly, a proposed further course of action is to extend the applicability of these frameworks to more practical diverse application setting such as the mobile data trading in wireless networks that we have explored in our recent INFOCOM work on using the Perron-Frobenius theory.

125212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
125212.value: There has been a recent surge of demand for mobile data and wireless access, and this has led to increased interference and unfairness in resource allocation in wireless networks. The problem of maximizing the total network utility subject to interference management requirements and to guarantee performance fairness is difficult to solve in a distributed manner due to the non-convexity hurdles in the formulation. Finding the global optimal solution efficiently can lead to more robust and effective wireless performance for all the mobile users. We have developed a nonlinear Perron-Frobenius theory framework to analyze the mathematical properties and to design algorithms to overcome the non-convexity hurdles as well as understanding the algorithmic solvability of such problems. We also develop new applications for this novel approach of solving optimization problems with applications to mobile data trading and new Internet applications, where data, information and computational access have to be optimized jointly. The project output demonstrates the significance of our developed Perron-Frobenius theory framework in designing high-performance fixed-point algorithms that can compute the global optimal solution for various important wireless network utility maximization problems and advance the state of the arts in this area.

125312.label: Project Objectives
125312.value: Develop surfaces with hierarchical roughness and tunable wettability. We will develop a two-step process that combines wet and dry etching to fabricate surfaces with multiscale roughness including smooth patches, microscale and nanoscale roughness. Through judicious control of surface wettability, the hierarchical surfaces can be imparted for dropwise condensation or nucleate boiling. Study the condensation phenomenon on hierarchical and chemically homogeneous surfaces. 125412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
125412.value: Energetic materials (EMs) including explosives, pyrotechnics, and propellants have found various civilian and military applications. Nanoenergetic materials (nEMs) have improved performance in energy release, ignition, and other properties compared to conventional EMs. This makes nEMs have promising applications in actuation, ignition, propulsion, power, welding, fluidic, and electro-explosive devices at the micro and nanoscale. This proposed project will synthesize novel core/shell nEMs with nano fuel as the core and nano oxidizer as the shell on a silicon substrate. The first step is to synthesize two kinds of nanoparticle seeds on a silicon substrate. As the initial work, the PI has synthesized well-separated CuO nanoparticles, which will be used as one kind of the seeds. The second step is to combine the nanoparticle seeds with glancing angle deposition to synthesize well-separated vertically aligned (or close to so) Al nanorods and Mg nanostructures as the fuels. The PI has synthesized vertically aligned Mg nanostructures, but they are not well-separated. The separation will be achieved by using the nanoparticle seeds in this project. The third step is to integrate CuO around the well-separated Al nanorods and Mg nanostructures by self-assembly to realize novel Al/CuO and Mg/CuO based core/shell nEMs. The fourth step is to systematically study the fundamental reaction and ignition characteristics of the novel nEMs including exothermic reaction, onset reaction temperature, activation energy, heat release, ignition power, ignition delay, and ignition energy. Compared to previous approaches, the novel nEMs have the advantages as follows: (1) the fuel core is protected by the stable oxidizer shell. Consequently, the nEMs are more resistant to the environment (e.g. moisture) and suitable for long term storage/usage; (2) the nEMs only contain nanoscale fuel/oxidizer (no microscale fuel/oxidizer exit), resulting in better mixing uniformity, enhanced contact, and improved performance; (3) the proposed synthesis methods are facile, low-cost, and also scalable. This project aims to provide the EMs community with novel nEMs that have improved performance including enhanced exothermic reactions and reduced ignition delay and energy. Especially, the nEMs are resistant to the environment and suitable for long term storage/usage, which is very desirable for many practical applications. Furthermore, the nanoscale core/shell structure will significantly improve the overall mixing and spatial uniformity of the nEMs and provide an ideal platform for scientific researchers to study the fundamental thermodynamic and kinetic properties of energetic materials. 納米含能材料比傳統含能材料在起爆、點火、能量釋放速率等性能上有很大提高，因此其在微驅動、微點火、微推進、微功率、微焊接、微流體、微小型電爆裝置、以及提高傳統含能材料性能方面具有廣泛的應用前景。本項目將合成基於鋁(鎂)/金屬氧化物的新型核/殼結構納米含能材料并深入研究其反應和點火機理。第一階段是在硅基體上合成納米顆粒種子，第二是用斜角度沉積法在納米顆粒種子上製備燃料鋁(鎂)納米棒陣列，第三是將金屬氧化物和鋁(鎂)納米棒整合來獲得納米含能材料，第四階段是系統深入地研究其反應和點火機理。此類新型核/殼納米含能材料具有下列主要創新性優點：（1）性能活躍的鋁(鎂)燃料被性能穩定的氧化劑外殼所保護，所以適合長期儲存和使用；（2）只含有納米尺度的燃料和氧化劑，因此反應物之間混合更均勻、界面接觸更優良、性能更好；（3）合成方法簡便、低成本、適合批量製備。本項目的研究能夠為含能材料領域提供一類（多種）高性能新型納米含能材料。

125412.label: Realisation of objectives
125412.value: (1) Well-separated nanoparticle seeds on the surface of silicon substrates have been synthesized. A strategy has been developed for in situ synthesis of CuO nanoparticle seeds on various substrates by the simple controlled thermal heating of copper foam in static air. The density, morphologies together with the sizes of the nanoparticle seeds on substrates can be easily controlled by tailoring the experimental parameters such as the distance between the foams and substrates and the heating temperature. The porous structure of copper foam is beneficial for the generation of compressive stress during the heating process. The stress promotes the formation of CuO atoms/clusters in air, which evaporate from the copper foam surface and deposit on the substrate. The CuO nanoparticle seeds are then formed via structural rearrangements. (2) Well-separated Mg nanorods on the silicon substrates have been synthesized. A simple approach has been proposed to realize 3D Mg nanorods, which has several advantages over previous investigations such as suitable for mass production, reduced impurities, tailored dimensions, and easier integration into microsystem. Mg nanorods have been realized onto silicon substrates using a conventional thermal evaporator, where the incident angle of Mg vapor flux with respect to the substrate surface normal is fixed at 84°, which is also called glancing angle deposition. Al nanorods have been synthesized on the silicon substrates; however, they are not well separated. So only Mg nanorods are used for the following research. (3) CuO has been integrated with the well-separated Mg nanorods to achieve Mg/CuO based core/shell nanoenergetic materials (nEMs) with the fuel (Mg) as the core and the stable metal-oxide (CuO) as the shell. Mg nanorods are first prepared by glancing angle deposition. CuO is then deposited around Mg nanorods by reactive magnetron sputtering to realize the core/shell structure. Various characterization techniques are used to investigate the prepared Mg/CuO core/shell nanoenergetic arrays including scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, x-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy, x-ray diffraction, and thermal analyses. Uniform mixing and intimate contact between Mg nanorods and CuO are confirmed both from visual inspection of morphological images and analyses of heat release curves. Al/CuO based core/shell nEMs are not synthesized due to the reason in (2). Moreover, Mg/fluorocarbon core/shell nanoenergetic arrays are prepared onto silicon substrate, with Mg nanorods as the core and fluorocarbon as the shell. Mg nanorods are deposited by glancing angle deposition technique, and fluorocarbon layer is then prepared as shell to encase the Mg nanorods by magnetron sputtering deposition process. Scanning electron microscopy and transmission electron microscopy show the core/shell structure of the Mg/fluorocarbon arrays. X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and Fourier transform infrared spectrum are used to characterize the structural composition of the Mg/fluorocarbon. In addition, sandwich-structure superhydrophobic CuO/Mg/fluorocarbon nanoenergetic composite is prepared on the silicon substrate. An adhesion layer of Cu2O is sputtered on the clean silicon substrate. Cu thin film is then deposited on it by E-beam evaporation. Nanostructured CuO is formed by thermal oxidation of Cu thin film. Mg and fluorocarbon layers are then deposited sequentially by thermal evaporation and sputtering, respectively. The nanostructured energetic composite is characterized by scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Accelerated aging test is performed in a temperature and humidity chamber (35 °C, 95% relative humidity) and the heat-release characteristics are studied in detail by differential scanning calorimetry. (4) The fundamental reaction and ignition characteristics of the Mg/CuO based core/shell nEMs have been investigated. The Mg/CuO based core/shell nanoenergetic arrays exhibit low onset reaction temperature (~300 °C) and high heat of reaction (~3400 J/g). Most importantly, the nanoenergetic arrays possess long-term storage stability due to the stable CuO shell. This study provides a potential general strategy for synthesis of various Mg nanorods based stable nanoenergetic arrays. For Mg/fluorocarbon core/shell nanoenergetic arrays, it is found that the as-prepared fluorocarbon layer consists of shorter molecular chains compared to that of bulk polytetrafluoroethylene. Water contact angle test demonstrates the superhydrophobicity of the Mg/fluorocarbon arrays, and a static contact angle as high as 162° is achieved. Thermal analysis shows that the Mg/fluorocarbon material exhibits a very low onset reaction temperature of about 270 °C as well as an ultrahigh heat of reaction approaching 9 kJ/g. Preliminary combustion test reveals the rapid combustion wave propagation, and convective mechanism is adopted to explain the combustion behaviors. The shorter molecular chain of the prepared fluorocarbon compared with that of bulk PTFE is beneficial to the decomposition of fluorocarbon to gaseous species, which further promotes the low onset reaction temperature of Mg/fluorocarbon. The prepared Mg/fluorocarbon nanoenergetic arrays exhibit fascinating superhydrophobic property, which is believed to enhance the resistance to the changeable environmental conditions so as to improve the long-term storage stability. The superhydrophobic Mg/fluorocarbon can even be envisioned as an underwater energy source. Thermal analysis results demonstrate the excellent energetic capability of the Mg/fluorocarbon. The high heat release and available gas generation indicate very promising application potentials such as microactuation/micropropulsion. Initial combustion test has already shown the rapid combustion wave velocity, which is indicative of the high reactive power. We expect that the new Mg/fluorocarbon nanoenergetic arrays introduced will contribute to the research of nanostructured energetic composite, and the design concept adopted here can be further extended by the engineering community to advance the development of this field. For sandwich-structure superhydrophobic CuO/Mg/fluorocarbon nanoenergetic composite, it is found that Mg intermediate layer acquires the nano-texture from the underlying nanostructured CuO and consequently, a superhydrophobic surface forms after fluorocarbon coating. Instead of being a dead weight, the fluorocarbon coating also reacts with Mg exothermically, and interestingly, the heat releases of Mg/fluorocarbon and Mg/CuO can be adjusted almost independently. The superhydrophobicity enables the CuO/Mg/fluorocarbon to resist to highly humid environment and preserve the chemical energy well after long-time exposure. The CuO/Mg/fluorocarbon holds part of reactivity even after 6 h underwater storage. (5) Many interesting results based on CuO nanostructures have been achieved (please refer to the publications in item 8 of Part C: Research Output), which are considered as the by-products of this project.

125412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
125412.value: Although much progress has been made in this project, the limitation is also evident. The combustion propagation speed for nanoenergetic composites developed in this project is lower than half of detonation velocity of TNT, a commonly used explosive. In order to achieve a high combustion propagation speed, the volumetric loading density of nanoenergetic composites should be very low. One key factor leading to this kind of phenomena is related to gas generation during the combustion process. Thermite reaction of the nanoenergetic composites developed in this project is featured with little/no gas generation. Therefore, the combustion wave propagation is within conduction regime for compact energetic composites, and thus the combustion propagation speed is low. When the volumetric loading density is decreased, there will be much void space among nanoenergetic composites. The air trapped in the void space will get hot and pressurized, thus boosting the combustion wave propagation in a convective way. So adding some gas generators to them is a promising way to enhance the performance. We will synthesize novel explosive-embedded nanoenergetic composites which are based on nanoenergetic arrays developed in this project and further study their energetic properties and combustion characteristics.

125412.value: Energetic materials such as explosives, pyrotechnics and propellants have various civilian and military applications. Nanoenergetic materials (nEMs) have improved performance in energy release, ignition and other properties compared to conventional EMs. This makes nEMs have promising applications in actuation, ignition, propulsion, power, welding, fluidic, and electro-explosive devices at the micro and nanoscale. This project has successfully synthesized novel core/shell nEMs with nano fuel (Mg) as the core and nano oxidizer as the shell on silicon substrates and has systematically investigated their fundamental reaction and ignition characteristics such as exothermic reaction, onset reaction temperature, heat release, ignition property, etc. Compared to previous approaches, the novel nEMs developed in this project are more resistant to the environment (e.g. moisture) and suitable for long term storage/usage because the fuel core is protected by the stable oxidizer shell. This project provides the EMs community with novel nEMs that have improved performance including enhanced exothermic reactions and reduced ignition delay and energy. Especially, the nEMs are resistant to the environment and suitable for long term storage/usage, which is very desirable for many practical applications.

140412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
140412.value: The policy choices that developing and emerging economy governments make in Africa, Southeast Asia and Latin America in response to the continuing Global Financial Crisis will have significant implications for the future of world production, trade, investment and growth, and therefore for Hong Kong SAR and China in the global economy. Preliminary evidence suggests that regional (African, Asian and Inter-American) Multilateral Development Banks are playing a crucial role in shaping and coordinating the choices that governments make, but their role is under-studied, and no comparative study of their analysis and policy advice has been undertaken. Against a background in which developing and emerging economies as a whole are growing between three and four times as fast as the advanced economies, these organizations appear to be encouraging the former not only to pursue broadly market-oriented strategies, but also to ‘decouple’ from the West by focusing on regional integration and South-South trade. At the same time, there is evidence of a renewed interest, especially at the World Bank (the ‘parent’ of the regional banks) in forms of state intervention in pursuit of industrial development – a partial return to strategies rejected in the last quarter of the twentieth century. This adds up to a new development strategy, which if sustained would transform the global economy, hastening the shift of its centre of gravity from the ‘North/West’ to the ‘South/East’. The study will explore and document the policy advice and activity of the regional banks and other related organizations (IMF, World Bank, OECD; G20), assess the extent to which they have developed a common agenda, and investigate the receptiveness of their regional clients to the policies they propose. In particular, it will explore the themes of state activism, regional integration, and South-South trade and investment. The hypothesis put forward is that the response of governments is significantly influenced by the analysis of appropriate development strategies provided by the multilateral development banks both prior to and during the Global Financial Crisis. The project will provide a new understanding of the role of multilateral regional banks and illuminate the development strategies of African, Southeast Asian and South American governments as they emerge from the crisis. It will also provide advanced training, research experience and publishing opportunities for two research assistants, and therefore leave a tangible legacy in addition to its specific findings. 摘要: 發展中和經濟新興地區政府比如非洲，東南亞和拉丁美洲對於持續的全球經濟危急的對應措施將對未來世界（包括香港和中國）生產、貿易、投資和增長產生深遠的影響。初始分析表明地區（非洲，亞洲和美洲）多邊發展銀行在規劃和協調政府決策中發揮關鍵作用，但其影響被大大低估，相關的比較研究非常少。如今發展中國家和新興經濟體的增長是發達國家的三到四倍，這些機構不僅僅鼓勵前者追求更廣泛的市場主導的發展戰略，更鼓勵其擺脫對西方國家的依賴，將戰略重點放在經濟一體化和南南貿易。 与此同时,有证据表明世界银行開始改變上世紀的做法，更多的採取国家干预追求工业发展的形式。這意味著一個新的發展策略：從北／西轉向南／南，這一策略如果持續下去將改變世界經濟格局。此研究將研究並紀錄地區銀行和其他相關組織（世界貨幣基金組織，世界銀行，經濟合作與發展組織，二十國集團等）的政策建議和活動，評估在多大程度上他們已經開發出一個共同議程，並研究他們的區域客戶對這些政策的接受程度。此外，研究將探討政府干預，地區一體化，南南貿易和投資等問題。研究提出的假設是，政府對策很大程度上收到多邊開發銀行在全球金融危機前後提出的合適的發展戰略的影響。此研究將對於多邊開發銀行和非洲，東南亞和南美政府的發展策略提供新的理解視角，此外，項目還包括對兩個博士提供訓練，研究經驗和出版機會，進一步深化研究成果。

140412.label: Realisation of objectives
140412.value: The identification and comparison of the interpretations of the Global Financial Crisis from three Multilateral Development Banks (Asian Development Bank, African Development Bank, Inter-American Development Bank) (Objective 1) was the principal objective, to be explored further in two parts, both included in Objective 2: (a) to identify and compare the resulting policy prescriptions and assess their internal coherence and their complementarity, with a particular focus on the risks identified and the strategies proposed to mitigate them, and (b) to assess the mechanisms through which policy advice is disseminated to governments and other relevant actors, and the extent to which selected national policies (Brazil, Indonesia, South Africa) reflect the orientation of the Development Banks. The first objective was realized in full, primarily through extensive analysis of primary documents. The first part of the second objective was also realized in full, in that a clear picture emerged of the complementarity of different regional proposals, and the extent to which a focus on risks arising from the state of the global political economy illuminated the logic and practice of the development banks. On the second part, only an outline impression was gained, this being the major part of the project that was left aside. Correspondingly, proposed expenditure on this aspect of the grant did not take place. The third and fourth objectives reflected the underlying hypothesis that a shift was taking place in the global economy in the wake of the financial crisis and ensuing recession in North America and Europe. This was to be explored in relation to the extent and logic of advocacy of state activism, regional physical and institutional integration and ‘South-South’ trade and investment (Objective 3), and the role played in the analysis in each regional bank by perceptions of the character and significance of the ‘rise of China’ as a trading partner and source of Foreign Direct Investment (Objective 4). Both objectives were realized fully, not only in that they were investigated as intended, but also in that they proved indeed to identify key aspects of the approaches of the MDBs, and therefore also fulfilled the overall goal of Objective 3, this being to identify the implications for the evolution of the global economy. The fifth and sixth objectives related to collateral gains from the project. The intention to build networks between the academic community in Hong Kong and the Multilateral Development Banks, and especially their Research Departments (Objective Five), was realized in only a very preliminary way, with one brief visit made to those of the Asian and Inter-American Banks, and none to the African Bank, the latter because of security concerns. A proposal put forward to hold a conference at City University (Objective Six) after the formal completion date of the project was rejected for reasons I do not understand (I was due to leave the institution), so was not achieved at all. Again, relevant funding was not drawn upon. As regards publication (Objective Seven) six working papers have so far been published, along with one journal article. A single-authored monograph is under completion with a target completion date of July 2016. The first draft is complete.

140412.label: Major findings and research outcome
140412.value: The African, Asian and Inter-American Development Banks all seek to promote the transformation of the social relations of production in their region, in ways that respond to a logic of global competitiveness, but vary in content in accordance with local circumstances. Their response to the global financial crisis was to take advantage of the opportunity to press ahead with structural reform aimed at developing regional and global markets. This finding is potentially far-reaching because the convergent policy proposals of the MDBs in relation to Africa, Asia and Latin America give a first intimation of the transformed character of a future regulatory framework for capitalism on a global scale. All three banks aggressively promoted the agenda of structural reform and social transformation put together primarily by the World Bank and the OECD. But in addition, they responded to the new shape of the global economy by strongly advocating inter-regional and South-South trade and investment, and promoting strategies of industrial development focused on competitive advantage and selective insertion into global value chains. In particular, they explicitly addressed the means by which labour markets and social protection might be made compatible with (and constitutive of) competition on a genuinely global scale. For each, the principal objective was growth in productivity, whether through moving from low-productivity assembly to more capital-intensive and skills-based production (Asia), linking in to regional value chains (Africa), or promoting ‘productive development’ (Latin America). In all three cases, the MDBs, following OECD-World Bank models, encourage their country partners to develop systems of social protection that promote availability for work, and capacity to work productively – regimes of social protection that may be prototypes for a global social protection regime supportive of the maximum availability of productive workers across the world market. The focus on active state involvement in promoting industrial development became more pronounced during the period, and was accepted by both the IMF and the World Bank, partly under the influence of senior appointments from China and India. By the end of the period covered, as the developed world slowly began to emerge from the recession that followed the financial crash of 2007-8, it could be concluded that the shape of the global economy had changed, and that the MDBs in Africa, Asia and Latin America had converged on a strategy that located the dynamic centre of that economy in their own regions and investment and trade between them.

140412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
140412.value: The work on the multilateral development banks makes a central contribution to the monograph now in progress (Item B in section 8 below). Although I am retired, I have a three-year honorary appointment at the University of Manchester, and I shall be pursuing three projects for which the grant reported here provides essential background: an examination of the role of international organizations, including the MDBs, in social reproduction (the relationship between households, families, and the global economy in terms of day-to-day life and longer term growth); a study, dropped from this grant as noted above, of individual national case studies in each region; and a major study of the policies developed by the same organisations to combat rising inequality, which has been widely identified as a significant source of risk. More generally, the MDBs are still rather under-studied. It is clear from the research that there is substantial scope for more detailed studies which other researchers might take up, to explore further the shared and regional-specific agendas of the MDBs and their contribution to global economic governance.

140412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
140412.value: The aim was to find out what role multilateral development banks in Africa, Asia and Latin America were playing, in policy advice and guidance, in managing the regional economy, contributing to global governance, and promoting development after the ‘global financial crisis’. Were they following the lead of the advanced economies, or developing regional projects? How far were their actions coordinated or complementary? And were they still committed to neoliberal development, or were they more keen to regulate the market? I established that they remained absolutely committed to the further development of the market, and particularly to pursuing competitiveness. They responded swiftly to new global circumstances to advocate greater intra-regional and ‘South-South’ links and to promote active state policies to ‘move up the ladder’ to more capital-intensive and skill-based activities through labour-market reform and the attraction of inward investment. They also showed increasing concern for equity and sustainability. These finding suggest that the banks are playing an important role. They are active agents in the transformation of the world order from a market-led system dominated by Europe and North America to one which is Asia-centred, with strong South-South connections, heightened competitiveness, and unconditional support for ‘sustainable and equitable’ capitalist development.
