146112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
146112.value: Casual observations suggest that the extent of globalization and economic interdependence among nations increase over time. Recent researches also suggest that changes in the world economic conditions would affect even the price movements of housing in some Asian countries. Thus, for academic research as well as policy analysis, it is important to understand the dynamics of the world economic condition even if the research orientation is completely local. Yet the "world economic condition" is not directly observed. Too many economic variables, both locally and globally, are potentially important and it is not practical to include all of them in the statistical model. Some of the existing literatures often need to rely on strong assumptions to construct proxies. Recent years witness a fast-growing literature which develops the theoretical foundation, as well as employs dynamic factor models (henceforth DFM) in the empirical research of economics. A merit of DFM is the capacity to summarize statistically useful information from a large number of time series data in a few factors, and hence facilitate predictions and policy analysis. Among others, James Stock (Harvard) and Mark Watson (Princeton) have demonstrated in one of their 2002 papers that 6 unobserved factors can account for much variation of 215 time series of the United States. It means that many macroeconomic variables are inter-related and the statistical method identifies only 6 significant and independent sources of shocks in the United States. Ayhan Kose (IMF), Christopher Otrok (Missouri) and Charles Whiteman (Iowa) apply DFM in the study of the world business cycle co-movements. In particular, they decompose the country macroeconomic variables into a world common component, a regional-specific component, a country-specific component, and an idiosyncratic error term. This research builds on their work and applies DFM to study the business cycle co-movements among a panel of countries. In particular, we will consider the interactions among different groups of countries, including the G7, selected Asian countries and emerging markets. We will apply a dynamic factor model with a multi-level factor structure, which allows different factors to be correlated over time. For instance, the world factor may be influenced by previous period country-specific factors, and the country-specific factor affected by previous world common factor. Moreover, the previous period country-specific factors may impact other country-specific factors. Our framework will be able to identify all these dynamic interactions and would contribute to a deeper understanding of the world business cycles. 本研究計劃將採用統計學中的動態因素分析方法, 以分析世界各國間經濟周期之互動。

146112.label: Realisation of objectives
146112.value: We have achieved the project objectives. We estimate and compare different dynamic factor models based on a panel dataset with more than 20 countries and several macroeconomic variables in each country. We find that the models which assume the existence of three "world factors" perform the best. We also find that the frequently adopted assumption of the existence of regional shock may not be necessary. Our analysis suffer from a relatively short sample size. We have recently updated our dataset and re-estimate and refine all the results. We are in the process of revising the paper.

146912.label: Project Objectives
146912.value: Examine the key drivers, process, and contingent factors that affect the outcomes of consumers’ engagement in value co-creation. Provide managerial implications for firms to better stimulate, facilitate, and manage value co-creation with consumers.
rows: Examine the key drivers, process, and contingent factors that affect the outcomes of consumers’ engagement in value co-creation.
Provide managerial implications for firms to better stimulate, facilitate, and manage value co-creation with consumers.

146912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
146912.value: Value co-creation is an emerging paradigm that dramatically changes how marketers, managers, and professionals collaborate with consumers in idea generation, as well as new product development and launch. The popularity of Web 2.0 technology and the vast amounts of information that consumers exchange in various types of virtual environments (e.g., online communities, open-source sites, social media) push many innovative firms, including IBM, SAP, Microsoft, Nike, Volvo, and Nokia, to consider how they might benefit from the collective wisdom of millions of consumers. Two streams of research have contributed to theory on value co-creation. Prahalad and Ramaswamy (2004) emphasize the unique role of consumers in offering specialized competences, skills, and knowledge that a firm and its employees cannot provide or understand internally. Vargo and Lusch (2004, 2008) adopt a service-dominant marketing perspective and regard consumers as unique resource integrators and producers of their experience and perceptions, which determine value-in-use. Both streams suggest that firms should work to free consumers’ creativity and foster experimentation and exploration among this newly empowered, entrepreneurial, and liberated group (Zwick, Bonsu, and Darmody 2008). Despite the significance of this topic, little empirical or quantitative research examines its dynamic and recursive processes. Existing studies mainly use case studies or cross-sectional data, which capture a single moment in the process, from either consumers’ or firms’ perspectives. The goal of this project is to propose and test a more comprehensive model of the critical factors that affect the ongoing value co-creation process and its outcomes during the ideation stage. Drawing on value co-creation literature, we propose that consumers continuously evaluate the benefits they receive and adjust their motives and extent of participation in value co-creation. Firms’ continuous technological and social support significantly affects the process and value generated. Moreover, consumers’ ability to attract high-quality interactions with others results in different values. To achieve these goals, this project adopts longitudinal web data, continuously retrieved from chosen websites, four rounds of online surveys with users, and in-depth interviews with involved firms. The findings should contribute to value co-creation literature and provide feasible strategies that firms can employ to harness the power of value co-creation by stimulating, facilitating, and improving the process. 價值共創是目前新興的研究領域，正顯著地改變市場營銷者、管理者和專業人士如何與消費者合作共同產生創意，新產品世界以及推廣。Web 2.0 技術的普及和消費者在各種各樣的虛擬平台（如網上社區、開放式程序網站、設計啊媒體）大量的信息交流也極大地推動了很多創新的企業， 例如IBM, SAP, Microsoft, Nike, Volvo, and Nokia 考慮如何從數百萬的消費者的集體智慧中獲益。 目前有兩個主要的學術流派為價值共創的理論發展作出貢獻。Prahalad 和 Ramaswamy (2004) 強調消費者所具備的獨特的一般企業員工和企業內部難以產生和理解的才華、技能和知識。 Vargo 和 Lusch (2004, 2008) 提出服務為主的市場營銷導向並認為消費者作為消費體驗與感受方面獨特的資源整合和產生者決定了使用中的價值。兩個學術流派都一致認為企業應該致力於釋放消費者的創意並推動這群剛被授權的、富有創業家精神、並解放的人群的試驗與探索(Zwick, Bonsu, and Darmody 2008) 。 儘管該議題的重要，目前只有少數的實證和定量研究是關於動態和遞歸的價值共創過程。 目前的研究主要是採用案例分析或者在某一段時間從企業或者消費者其中一方收的橫截面數據。因此本研究方案的研究目標是提出一個更全面的模型闡述在創意產生階段影響持續不斷的價值共創過程的關鍵因素和其結果。我們根據過去在價值共創方面的文獻，認為消費者反复地評估他們在價值共創過程中的得益並修改他們的參與度和參與動機。同時，企業持續的技術和社會支持也將顯著影響到共創過程及其產生的價值。除此之外，消費者在吸引高質量的互動和信息交流也將產生不同的價值。 為了實現以上的研究目標，本研究項目將採用從企業社區網展持續而長期收集的數據、四輪與參與研究的企業的消費者的問卷調查、四輪與參與研究的企業的管理層的深度訪談。我們相信研究的結果將豐富價值共創理論的發展並為企業提供可行的策略通過鼓勵、協助、改進價值共創過程去掌握共創共創所帶來的具深遠意義的價值。

146912.label: Realisation of objectives
146912.value: In the past three years, we have worked on specific value co-creation context, idea crowdsourcing through which consumers collaborate with other consumers to create ideas for the firms. In order to achieve the objectives listed in the proposal, we have conducted multiples studies to investigate the drivers, process, and contingent factors that affect the outcomes of consumers’ engagement in this salient and specific form of value cocreation—idea creation, how firms can better stimulate, facilitate, and manage the idea creation together with the consumers. Specifically, we have conducted the following studies which provide insights on the process and key factors influence consumers’ engagements as well as the outcomes of their engagement in value cocreation. Our first study is to examine how social network and different direction of online social interaction in the value cocreation process influence the likelihood of consumers’ engagement in the process (i.e., their idea generation likelihood). Firms increasingly engage customers in idea generation (or ideation) to sustain their competitive advantages. Drawing from social interaction literature, this study adopts a social network perspective to investigate empirically how the characteristics (i.e., direction, size, and strength) of customers' online peer-to-peer (P2P) and peer-to-firm (P2F) interactions, moderated by customers' past efforts to post ideas (i.e., past ideation participation), influence their likelihood of generating ideas in an idea crowdsourcing community. With four years of data from a popular online crowdsourcing site, this study demonstrates the significant impacts of P2P and P2F online interactions on customers' likelihood of subsequent idea generation. In particular, a potential double-edged sword of past ideation participation emerges: A high level of past ideation participation strengthens (weakens) the impact of P2F (P2P) interactions on customers' subsequent idea generation. These findings suggest implications for how firms can cultivate customers' online social interactions with peers and firms and enhance their capabilities for capturing the wisdom of the crowd. This project was accepted and published in Journal of Interactive Marketing in 2015. Our second study is examine how different sources and valences of feedback that consumers influence the quality of ideas consumer generated. Recent studies show increasing concerns of the quality of ideas generated through crowdsourcing. Grounded in the feedback intervention and social influence literatures, this study explores how feedback influences ideation performance. We posit that the effectiveness of crowdsourcing feedback is not only determined by valence (positive vs. negative), but also by its source (firm vs. peers) and contingent on ideators’ ideation experience. Data collected from a crowdsourcing community and an experiment shows that negative firm and positive peer feedbacks enhance the idea quality of those ideators who have accumulated more ideation experience. Specifically, negative firm feedback exerts contrasting impacts on different ideators such that it decreases (increases) the idea quality of those who are less (more) experienced. Moreover, the effects of positive firm feedback and negative peer feedback on idea quality become weaker for more experienced ideators. Our results empower managers with feedback strategies to boost customer ideation performance in crowdsourcing. This project was now under review and revision under Management Science. Our third study focuses on how firms might manage the value creation process in terms of selecting the right ideas for implementations. Idea crowdsourcing allows firms to reach the best ideas from the crowd. However, emerging research shows that firms often fail to consider those novel ideas due to the uncertainty and risks they may cause in innovation process. Meanwhile, the remarkable increase of number of crowdsourced ideas creates the crowding effect that further narrows firms’ attention and reduces their openness to the most novel ideas from the crowd. This can be detrimental to the effectiveness of idea crowdsourcing that firms aim to achieve. Given these critical challenges, studies examining firms’ idea implementation decision in idea crowdsourcing context, in particular, the relations between idea novelty and idea implementation, are surprisingly rare. This study extends the literature by taking a new theoretical angle by adopting the Path-of-Least-Resistance (POLR) theory to examine the role of idea feasibility as the key cue that firms use to filter novel ideas for their implementation. We further explore the factors that might amplify or mitigate the mediating effects of idea feasibility. Using data collected from a leading crowdsourcing community, and coded by expert judges and text-mining techniques, this study reveal the mediating role of idea feasibility on the negative relation between idea novelty and firm’s implementation decision. Moreover, we have conducted two more experiments to verify the mediating role of idea feasibility. Besides, such negative mediation effect becomes stronger when relevant ideators have greater ideation participation in the past, while is weaker when ideas are popular (i.e., receiving greater favorability of peer comments). Our findings provide firms with implications on how to effectively manage customer ideation crowdsourcing in achieving product and service improvement. The manuscript is to be submitted to Academy Management Journal . We believe our above research greatly advance our understanding on the processes, contingent factors that affect consumers’ engagement as well as the outcomes of their engagement in the value cocreation process. Our findings also provide different managerial implications for firms to stimulate facilitate and harness more value from the co-creation with the consumers.

146912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
146912.value: Based on the reviewers comments in each round of our paper review at different top tier journals. We have shortlisted new idea crowdsourcing websites and recruited part-time RAs to collect web data, help do the content analysis as well as text mining on some textual data newly collected. With new data sets and richer information based on the text mining results, we believe that we can further explore the value co-creation from a more refined, deeper, as well as more unique angles which can contribute to both the literature as well as managerial practices. Experiments can also help us to tease out some alternative psychological explanations which we can’t test if we solely rely on our web data. We are already in the process of new websites data collection, launching different experiments based on reviewers’ comments in our projects.

146912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
146912.value: Our first study show that the more experienced the consumers are, the stronger (weaker) the effects of firm (peer) feedback on their likelihood to generate more ideas. Our second study shows that consumers will generate better ideas for those who are more experienced and receive negative firm feedback. For those who are less experienced, they will generate better quality of ideas if they received positive firm feedback or negative peer feedback. Our third study shows that firms rely on the feasibility of ideas as a short cut to evaluate the novelty of ideas to decide on which ideas they should select and implement. Moreover, firms will rely more on idea feasibility as a filter cue when the ideas are generated from more consumers with greater ideation experience or the ideas are less popular among peers. These findings suggest implications for how firms can cultivate customers' online social interactions with peers and firms and enhance their capabilities for capturing the wisdom of the crowd. 147112.label: Project Title(Chinese)
147112.value: 價格、貨架和商品組合聯合決策：一種增量優化方法

147112.label: Project Objectives
147112.value: We will examine the effects of shelf space on product demand. This study will validate, complement and consolidate existing empirical studies on this issue. Particularly, we will investigate how display space influences consumer behavior, which will be incorporated into our demand model. We will propose a new demand model following the address approach. The model will incorporate particularly prices and shelf space in addition to major product attributes. The effectiveness of the proposed approach will be validated with empirical studies and compared with existing demand models. We will propose an iterative improvement approach to assortment planning. Due to the increased complexity of our demand model, it will be extremely difficult to solve all decisions optimally. Therefore, we aim to identify from a given assortment the structural features that will the room for improvement. We aim for more realistic, continuous, iterative and structural improvements to an existing assortment rather than formulating an ideal optimal assortment. We will make available some data sets on a few select product categories, which are valuable to the research on assortment planning; the performance of the existing methods is largely unknown and an assessment and comparison of the methods will demand such representative data sets. Research findings from the project will are expected to lead to three to four high quality journal papers.

147112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
147112.value: 商品規劃,亦即決定出售的商品組合,對於零售商的盈利能力非常重要。然而,到目前為止,學術界和業界對此問題並沒有一致的解決方案,主要原因是有效的商品規劃牽涉到多個因素的成功結合:對於消費者行為和需求的透徹理解,能夠準確反映因素的需求模型,以及能高效優化模型的演算法。近年來,由於業界大量資料的積累,情況正在發生變化,開發基於資料的商品規劃的科學方法的條件日趨成熟。在本專案裡,我們提出綜合解決定價、貨架分配和商品選擇三個問題。我們相信當前的商品規劃研究有三個方面的缺陷:一是假定商品價格是給定的,二是展示空間對於需求的影響被忽略,三是目前廣泛使用的需求模型有很大的缺陷。本專案致力於提出一種新的商品規劃的方法來解決以上缺陷。我們將分析研究貨架空間對商品需求的不同影響,以決定應如何將貨架的影響嵌入我們的模型;我們將提出一種「位址」需求模型,把價格空間決策嵌入到商品規劃的決策模型裡面。基於新模型的高複雜性,我們提出一種「增量」優化的演算法。其理念是從一種現有的商品組合出發,找出在現有方案基礎上逐步提高的新方案。換言之,我們的目標不在於一個全新的新組合,而是一條不斷優化的商品組合的路徑。我們相信這樣的一種方案,因為其低風險和容易實現的特點,更加適應業界的需求。

147112.label: Realisation of objectives
147112.value: This has been a very fruitful project. The collaboration with industry partners ensures the validity of the research findings. We have first studies the impact of shelf space on retail demand. In fact practitioners are well aware of such impacts. Mengniu Dair has in fact conducted some trials in a few stores. We have found that it is desirable for a product to be allocated a shelf space no below than a threshold (like a critical mass) in order to realize its basic market potential. Specifically, it's found that the demand is a S-curved function of shelf space. This also means a lot to a retailer who needs to allocate shelf space among competing products. However, so far there is no effective optimization algorithms for such kind of non-convex optimization. Nevertheless, it presents an interesting and practical shelf space allocation problem, which is very different from those in the literature. We have proposed two assortment planning models. Both models take the idea of "incremental" update of assortment. One model considers customers' variety seeking behavior and the other models the time decay effect of a given assortment, and both are motivated by industry practice. Essentially firms face a trade-off between updating an assortment by incurring some cost and thus attracting refreshed demand and keeping the incumbent assortment while receiving declined demand. We have proposed DP formulations for both problems and discovered some structural properties of the optimization, which are used to speed up the DP solution procedure. In particular, we have found that under our dynamic assortment planning setting, many well-know findings in the assortment literature may be invalid. For example, it may be optimal for a retailer to have an assortment with products overlapping with each other. Simply speaking, this is to address customers' declining willingness to buy over time, due to either variety seeking or declined attractiveness of a product. Alternatively, it may be optimal to have some an assortment with some customers unsatisfied at the beginning, namely, products in the assortment are necessary to be exactly adjacent to each other. All such interesting findings have enriched the literature.

It's been confirmed that the demand as a function of shelf space is more like a S-curved function. Namely, the marginal effect of shelf space is first increasing then decreasing. This has particular implications to both manufacturers who need to bargain with retailers for an ample shelf space for their products and retailers who need to allocate their limited shelf space among their products.
We have proposed two assortment planning models based on the address approach. The first model captures variety seeking behavior and the second models the time decay effect of an assortment.

For both models, we have proposed novel dynamic programming algorithms. We have also developed some structural properties for solving the DP model efficiently. We also proposed several heuristic approaches to capture some more realistic way of updating assortment over time. A comparison with the ideal, optimal solution shows that the heuristic approaches work well in most situations.

147112.label: Major findings and research outcome
147112.value: In short, we have found that (1) The retail demand as a function of shelf space is better modeled as a S curve; (2) Dynamic assortment planning has some interesting properties absent from static assortment planning. Dynamic assortment planning is necessary due to incomplete demand information as found in the literature or, as we model here, customers' variety behavior or declined willingness to buy. Research findings of the project have been present at several major conferences in our field, including INFORMS Annual Meeting and POMS Annual Meeting and some other conferences like POMS Hong Kong Chapter annual conference. Two journal papers have been drafted and nearly ready for submission, whose status will be updated in the future.

147112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
147112.value: First of all, we will continue to refine our research papers and work on them until they are published. Another line of research is perhaps to investigate effective optimization model and solution for shelf space allocation. It's also an interesting research direction to study data-driven assortment planning, which has received some attention recently from the research community.

147112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
147112.value: In planning their shelf space allocation, retailers need to keep in mind the impact of shelf space on retail demand. Nowadays, shelf space is such a scare resource and it is far from accommodating all possible products. Therefore, retailers need to make deliberate decisions in assortment planning on what to be included in their assortments and how much shelf space to be allocated to each of them. Manufacturers and retailers need to be well aware of the fact customers' willingness to pay changes over time and are affected by many factors. Among them are the variety seeking behavior and time decay effect of a product. Therefore, the firm needs to consider whether and when to update its assortment by introducing new products into its assortment, which means removing or replacing some existing products some time due to limited shelf space. The present project has shed some lights on these issues and proposed solutions for some of such problems.

147212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
147212.value: User resistance to enterprise systems (ES) has long been an important concern to corporations striving for system implementation success. Apart from ensuring the provision of a clear vision and sufficient resources, corporate executives in power must understand how they should (or should not) leverage their institutional power to manage and change user resistance. In this proposed study, by extending power-dependence theory to the system implementation context, we develop a multi-level research model to explain how institutional power affects user resistance. The model incorporates two key aspects of institutional power, coercive and reward power, by examining how they each directly affect user resistance and mitigate the adverse impact of IT-induced loss on user resistance. To this end, we have gained consensus from the senior management of a large commercial bank, who allows us to use the bank as the data collection site for the proposed study. We plan to test the model through a survey of users from 35 subsidiaries of the bank that have recently implemented an enterprise system. Data will be analyzed using hierarchical linear modeling (HLM) technique. By extending power-dependence theory to the system implementation context, we anticipate the study contributing to the literature by enhancing our theoretical understanding on enterprise systems implementation success as well as generating managerial insights to guide future system implementation efforts. 對於力求成功推行企業信息系統（ES）的企業來說，用戶的抵制行為一直是一個重要難題。除了給出清晰的前景展望，確保足夠的資源供給，企業主管們必須明確如何運用制度性權力來管理用戶的抵制行為。在本研究中，我們將權力依賴理論應用於系統實施的課題中，並提出一個多層研究模型來解釋制度性權力如何影響用戶抵制行為。本研究模型涵蓋了制度性權力的兩個重要部份，即強制權與獎賞權，并研究了這兩種權力如何直接影響用戶抵制行為。同時此模型也研究了這兩種權力如何緩和企業信息系統給用戶帶來的損失對於抵制行為的不良影響。爲了驗證研究模型，我們聯繫了一家不久前推行企業信息系統的大型商業銀行，并取得管理層的同意，可在該銀行收集數據。我們計劃以問卷的形式調查該銀行35家分行的系統用戶。我們將會採用多層線性模型（HLM）來分析數據。通過將權力依賴理論擴展至系統實施的課題中，我們期望本研究可以增強現有文獻對於企業信息系統成功實施的理論理解，并給日後的系統實施提供可行性建議。

147212.label: Realisation of objectives
147212.value: The objectives of the project, as stated above, have been fully achieved. In relation to the first objective, Institutional authorities have long used reward (carrots) and punishment (sticks) to regulate employee behavior. However, prior research has not examined the extent to which the institutional authority’s power to grant reward or inflict punishment affects employee resistance behavior in the context of enterprise systems (ES) implementation. Furthermore, there have been few multi-level studies of user resistance, even though the influence of institutional authority on user behavior requires a multi-level analysis. To address these research gaps, this study examines the effect of institutional power perceived by employees in an organizational unit on individual-level user resistance to introduced enterprise systems through a multi-level analysis. By integrating social exchange theory and power dependence theory, our study suggests that the reward power and coercive power that the institutional authority exercises at the unit level have differential impacts on user resistance at the individual level. Furthermore, we identify cross-level, differential moderating effects of reward and coercive power on the relationship between user resistance and different types of two IT-induced losses; namely, IT-induced role overload and loss of power. In relation to the second objective, the model was tested through a survey of 254 users from 27 subsidiaries of a large financial institution that had implemented an enterprise system. The results generated interesting insights and useful guidelines for practitioners on how institutional authorities can better leverage on rewards or punishments to mitigate user resistance.

147212.label: Major findings and research outcome
147212.value: Our empirical results yield two important findings. First, we found that the coercive power of an institutional authority has a cross-level positive impact on user resistance. Second, we found that, in addition to the direct effects, these two institutional powers have cross-level moderation effects on the impacts of different types of IT-induced losses (i.e., IT-induced role overload and IT-induced loss of power) on user resistance. Specifically, reward power weakens the positive effect of IT-induced role overload, while coercive power amplifies the positive effect of IT-induced loss of power on user resistance. This research offers several important research outcomes. First, its primary contribution lies in introducing power dependence theory to the user resistance literature to provide a more complete theoretical understanding of this important IS research issue. Second, drawing on power dependence theory, we extend the user resistance literature by providing insights into the contingent effect of IT-induced loss on user resistance. The extant literature has extensively studied the direct effects of IT-induced loss, role overload, and power loss on user resistance. Our study pushes forward this line of inquiry by revealing that these direct effects are not unconditional, but can be maneuvered by different types of institutional power. In doing so, we provide a theoretically grounded understanding of the boundary conditions under which IT-induced loss affects user resistance through the lens of power dependence. Third, our study also contributes to power dependence theory by extending it to the context of ES implementation. Power dependence theory has previously been used to explain a variety of relational behaviors, such as inter-firm relationships and interpersonal relationships; however, its ability to shed light on the (institutional authority) employer–employee relationship in the context of ES implementation had yet to be formally tested before the present study. Our research findings extend power dependence theory to the ES implementation context. Finally, our study contributes a multi-level research model to explain individual-level user resistance by theorizing the nested context of the power dependence relationship between institutional authority and organizational unit. Prior research has predominantly been single level or focused on investigating how resistance at the group level emerges from individual user resistance. Our study makes a distinct contribution by constructing a multi-level model to accounts for antecedents at both individual and group levels. This approach provides a more integrated understanding of the user resistance, thus offering a richer portrait of organizational reality and explicating previously unexplored relationships.

147212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
147212.value: As with any study, this study has several limitations that need to be take into consideration when interpreting the results. With that, there are also several opportunities for further development of this research. First, we used a cross-sectional research design. This data collection method is limited in establishing causalities between research variables. Future research could employ a longitudinal design in order to further our understanding of the antecedents of user resistance. Second, our survey study was conducted in one large corporation with multiple subsidiaries. This survey design not only allows reasonable variances of key variables in our research model across different subsidiaries, but also naturally controls for variances due to factors external to the organization. Future research could augment the generalizability of our study by replicating it in other organizational settings. Third, our study involves only one type of enterprise system; this may further limit the generalizability of the findings. Future research could include more types of information systems to increase our understanding of user resistance. Finally, our analyses showed that common method bias is not likely a major concern; however, future research could collect data from multiple sources to completely rule out any potential threat of common method bias.

147212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
147212.value: Our results suggest that an institutional authority which chooses to implement an enterprise system using a typical top-down approach should be mindful of its power relationship with employees. First, the institutional authority should avoid exercising coercive power to enforce compliance. Coercive power may obtain tentative compliance but it will ultimately intensify resistance behavior. Moreover, coercive power should be particularly avoided when the implemented system undermines user power by, for example, restructuring decision rights, changing communication patterns, or removing control over key information. Coercive power further strengthens the negative impact of an IT-induced loss of power. Second, the institutional authority can mitigate user resistance by nurturing employees and reminding them of the potential benefits of the introduced system. Particularly, the institutional authority should consider signaling reward power when the new system increases workloads, because reward power can mitigate the negative impact of IT-induced overload. Finally, consistent with earlier studies, we recommend that managers explicitly address user role overload and loss of power, as these are two of the most salient threats to employees resulting from the introduction of a new system.

147512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
147512.value: Helpful vote is a common feature on many websites that utilizes the “wisdom of the crowd”. It allows visitors to vote on whether a piece of information (e.g. a product review) posted on the website is helpful to them. The aggregated helpful vote is supposed to reflect the underlying quality of the information. Given a plethora of information available on the Internet, helpful vote lowers people’s search costs to locate the most valuable information. The effectiveness of helpful vote is based on the belief of “wisdom of the crowd.” Although the “wisdom of the crowd” effect has been supported in both academic research and popular press, recent studies show that under certain conditions, aggregated judgment may lead to inaccurate information. For example, Lorenz et al. (2011) show that social influence may undermine the “wisdom of the crowd” effect. Further, inspired by Arrow’s impossibility theorem, List and Pettit (2002) show that voting based on multiple criteria may result in a set of logically inconsistent aggregated judgments and thus, also undermine the “wisdom of the crowd”. Motivated by these studies, this project examines the effectiveness of helpful vote on product review websites. Specifically, we intend to address three questions: (1) whether the aggregated helpful vote reflects the underlying quality of a review, (2) under what conditions the aggregated helpful vote reflects the underlying quality of a review, and (3) how we can design better aggregation mechanisms to help people locate truly helpful reviews. We argue that the aggregated helpful votes will not reflect the underlying quality of a review because of (1) social influence (i.e., the existing helpful vote affects future helpful vote), (2) multiple criteria for judging helpfulness and the subjectivity of the judgment, and (3) non-random information selectivity (i.e., consumers select reviews based on existing helpful vote and other cues provided by the website). We test our hypotheses and develop new aggregation mechanisms using a multi-method approach that combines verbal protocol analysis, computational modeling, and archival data analysis. Specifically, we first investigate how individual consumers cast helpful vote via verbal protocol analysis in an experimental setting. Based on this understanding, we develop computational models to simulate reviews, consumers, and their helpful votes. We then validate and refine the models by comparing the simulated helpful vote with real-world data collected longitudinally from Amazon.com. Finally, we develop and test different aggregation mechanisms that can accurately capture “wisdom of the crowd.”

147512.label: Realisation of objectives
147512.value: In this project, we propose to examine the “wisdom of the crowd”, i.e., whether aggregating individual opinions generates truthful knowledge. Specifically, we look at the effectiveness of aggregating helpful votes on customer-generated product reviews, a prominent phenomenon on many e-commerce website. We intend to address three questions: (1) whether the aggregated helpful vote reflects the underlying quality of a review, (2) under what conditions the aggregated helpful vote reflects the underlying quality of a review, and (3) how we can design better aggregation mechanisms to help people locate truly helpful reviews. The objectives of the project have been addressed using a multi-method approach that combines verbal protocol analysis in lab setting, computational modeling, and archival data analysis. Specifically, the verbal protocol analysis allows us to understand how individual consumers cast helpful vote. Based on this understanding, we develop agent-based models to simulate reviews, individual consumers, and their helpful vote. We then validate and refine the agent-based models by comparing the simulated helpful votes with real-world data collected from Amazon.com. This allows us to address the first research objective: whether the aggregated helpful vote reflects the underlying quality of a review. Our assessment is that we have satisfactorily and completely addressed the first research objective. To address the second research objective, we first theoretically identified the boundary conditions for effective aggregation of individual votes. We then modeled these boundary conditions in the agent-based models. Varying these boundary conditions allows us to examine if these theoretically identified boundary conditions actually impact the effectiveness of aggregation. Our assessment is that we address the second research objective satisfactorily. A challenge is that addressing the second research objective requires us to first theoretically identify the boundary conditions. While we have identified the major factors that affect the effectiveness of the aggregation, it is impossible to exhaust all possible factors. We are confident that through a comprehensive literature review and careful theorization, we have identified the major factors. We address the third research objective based on our understanding of the boundary conditions. Since we have identified the factors that render aggregating individual votes ineffective, we can design aggregation mechanisms through different ways of information presentation that eliminate these factors. Our assessment is that we address the third research objective satisfactorily.

147512.label: Major findings and research outcome
147512.value: Our first major finding is that the multi-method approach generates a computational model that predicts real world outcomes with high degree of precision. The computational approach easily links the behavior of individual agents and the emergent group-level outcome, but a potential weakness of computational modeling is lack of realism, that is, the simulated results may not conform to the real world data). We compensate for this by validating our model by comparing the model results with real-world helpful vote data collected longitudinally from Amazon.com. We also show that the predictive power of our agent-based model outperforms other models in this domain. Secondly, we show that the current way of aggregating individual votes does not reflect the underlying quality of the reviews. If the aggregation of helpful votes from a crowd of customers is effective, the aggregated vote should reflect the underlying quality of the review. Since it takes time to accumulate helpful votes, reviews posted very early on the website generally have higher aggregated vote than later reviews. However, if the aggregation of helpful votes is effective, the aggregated vote of a high quality review should eventually be higher than the aggregated vote of a low quality review. Our simulation model shows that a substantially large proportion of high quality reviews generated on later times will never “catch up” with low quality reviews generated on earlier times. This suggests that the aggregation of helpful votes is probably not effective. The aggregated vote does not necessarily reflect the underlying quality of the review, especially for the reviews generated at a relatively later time. Lastly, this project identifies the conditions that render the aggregation of crowd judgments “ineffective”. Although we focus on a specific form of judgment aggregation (i.e., helpful vote), we theorize at a higher level of abstraction such that the conditions may also apply to other online judgment aggregation problems.

147512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
147512.value: The first future development is to relax the assumption of our computational model. A limitation of our model is the assumption of Bayesian belief updating. There is a large body of psychology work showing that people’s judgment/decision-making often deviate from Bayesian updating. In our context, this means that the existing helpful votes may have a smaller or larger impact than Bayes’ rule predicts. A future extension is to take into account people’s deviation from the Bayesian updating and examine if it leads to better predictions. The second future development is to consider more contextual factors in the computational model. Another limitation of our computational model is that it does not take into account the impact of our emotion embedded in the reviews. Emotion may affect helpful vote in both the selective attention and helpfulness judgment stages. In the selective attention stage, the impact of emotion can be modeled by adding the valence of the reviews. In the helpfulness judgment stage, the impact of emotion can be modeled by expressing the precision of the reviews as a function of emotion and other factors. With these two modifications, emotion embedded in the reviews can be incorporated in the simulation.

147512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
147512.value: First, this research identifies the conditions for effectiveness of helpful vote aggregation. The effectiveness of judgment aggregation on the web has so far received limited attention among business researchers. If crowd judgment aggregation does not always provide “unbiased” information, then it opens avenues for future research to investigate the conditions under which crowd judgment aggregation can be misguided as well as the underlying psychological and social processes that lead to validity or invalidity. The current paper identifies the conditions that render the aggregation of crowd judgments “ineffective”. Second, this paper has practical implication of informing the design of judgment aggregation mechanism on the Web. Practitioners can improve the organization and presentation of the reviews based on our findings. With modifications on the behavioral model, practitioners can also use the agent-based modeling approach to analyze their impact of their design decisions on the effectiveness of judgment aggregation. In the long term, this will benefit consumers in in making crowd judgment aggregation a more reliable source of valid information for their decision-making.

147712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
147712.value: Protecting information from a variety of security threats is a difficult organizational activity that is increasingly expensive. Traditional IT security efforts focus almost completely on technical methods to achieve protection and yet these methods continually fail while security breaches become increasingly brazen and threatening. Accordingly, many researchers now recognize that security efforts must also account for individual, social, and organizational influences to be more effective. Technical solutions alone are insufficient. In this vein, recent studies emphasize that organisational insiders are not just security threats but can be key security allies to better protect organisations. Managers within firms must recognize the roles that organizational insiders have in protecting information resources rather than solely relying upon technological advancements to provide this protection. Unfortunately, compared to negative insider behaviours, extant literature provides little coverage of beneficial insider activities. Our research thus focuses on protection-motivated behaviours (PMBs), the volitional behaviours organizational insiders can enact that protect (1) organizationally relevant information within their firms and (2) the computer-based information systems in which that information is stored, collected, disseminated, and/or manipulated from information-security threats. We have worked for several years to build the foundation for examining (theoretically and empirically) the set of all major PMBs practiced by industry insiders. Based on systematics, we have applied qualitative and quantitative approaches to develop a taxonomy and theory of diversity for PMBs to better inform theory and practice. The biggest limitation of the extant work in this area is that it has focused primarily on Western culture. Research demonstrates the influence of culture in information-based organizational environments. Because PMBs also involve technology- and information-based attitudes and behaviours in organizations, we have every reason that culture matters to PMBs. For example, Hong Kong insiders working with investment data will give different priorities to certain PMBs, because they will consider what is appropriate and inappropriate differently than Western financial professionals. Accordingly, our grant proposes extending our taxonomy of PMBs and theories to account for practice in Hong Kong. We propose a methodology for extending the current knowledge of PMBs to include practice in Hong Kong using the classification techniques of multidimensional scaling, property fitting, and cluster analyses. We propose leveraging these techniques explain how Hong Kong insiders collectively classify and thinking about unique Chinese PMBs. By further understanding Hong Kong practitioners’ mental models of PMBs, we can then inform theory and practice to better protect multinational organizations from security threats. 从多种安全威胁信息保护是一项艰巨的组织活动已经变得越来越昂贵。传统的IT安全的努力几乎完全集中于技术，以达到保护的方法，但这些方法的不断失败，而安全漏洞越来越无耻和威胁。因此，许多研究人员现在认识到，安全工作也必须考虑个人，社会和组织的影响，能够更有效。单靠技术解决方案是不够的。 在这方面，最近的研究强调，组织业内人士并不只是安全威胁，但也可以是关键，以更好地保护企业的安全盟友。在企业内部的管理人员必须认识到组织内部人士的角色，在保护信息资源，而不是单纯依靠技术进步提供这种保护。不幸的是，相比为负的内幕行为，现存的文献提供了有益的内幕活动的报道很少。 我们的研究，从而保护积极性的行为，侧重于（PMBs），组织业内人士的意志行为可以制定保护（1）组织在其公司的相关信息，及（2）以计算机为基础的信息系统中存储该信息，收集，传播和/或操纵信息安全威胁。 我们已经工作了几年打下了基础研究（理论和实践）的一套业内人士实行所有主要PMBs的。系统分类的基础上，我们运用定性和定量方法，开发了一种分类的多样性和理论PMBs理论和实践，以更好地了解。现存的最大限制这方面的工作，它主要侧重于西方文化。 研究显示信息为基础的组织环境文化的熏陶。由于PMBs还涉及到技术和信息为基础的组织的态度和行为，我们有充分的理由，文化事项到PMBs。例如，香港业内人士与投资数据将给予不同的优先级一定PMBs，因为他们会考虑什么是合适与不合适的，不同于西方国家的金融专业人士。因此，我们的资助建议，我们的分类在香港执业的PMBs和理论来解释。 我们提出了一个方法，，为扩展当前的的PMBs知识，包括使用多维标度，物业装修，分析和聚类分析的分类技术在中国的实践。我们建议利用这些技术来解释中国的业内人士共同进行分类，并认为有关中国特有的PMBs。然后，我们可以进一步了解中国学员的心智模式PMBs，通知的理论和实践，以更好地保护从安全威胁的跨国组织。

147712.value: A key limitation of organizational security work on protection motivation behaviours (PMBs) is that it has focused primarily on Western culture. This is particularly limiting considering that culture greatly influences attitudes and behaviours. Hence, in Hong Kong, the undermining cultural inclinations of insiders at large investment banks will have a significant bearing on how insiders view PMBs. Thus, Hong Kong insiders working with financial data will give higher or lower priority to certain PMBs, because they will consider what is appropriate differently than typical Western banking professionals. Hong Kong professionals will also likely think of PMBs that will not be thought of or as highly valued by Western practitioners—such as group- and consensus-oriented approaches to protection. Discovering these differences is imperative to implementing successful information security practices in organizations located in cities such as Hong Kong. SETA programs, training initiatives, written procedures, job descriptions, policies, assessment of compliance, and language about PMBs that are created with only Western cultures in mind will likely fail Chinese cultures—and no one will know exactly why.

148012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
148012.value: Research management is an important task for government funding agencies and research institutions. Research information systems have been developed to automate the processes of research project management. However there is a need to build the formal framework for measuring research performance and forecasting research trends in research management. In this project, a Research Analytics Framework (RAF) will be proposed to measure research performance from three aspects, namely research productivity (e.g. no of refereed articles in journals or conferences, citations and h-index), research relevance (e.g. in a research discipline) and connectivity (e.g. social network analysis). The proposed RAF will be implemented with data collection, analysis and visualization capabilities to support decision making tasks in research management. The project results will provide new methods and techniques for developing next generation research information systems. It will change the way for lean research management in government funding agencies and research institutions. 科研管理是大学和政府科研资助机构最重要的任务之一。目前已经开发了不少科研管理信息系统用于提高科研项目管理流程的效率，但是还没有一套有效的方法对科研表现作客观的评价和对科研的未来发展作预测。本项目将提出一种科研分析框架，从科研产出（如质量与数量）、相关度（如科研领域）与合作度（如合作者）三个角度来分析科研表现。本项目提出的科研分析框架可以用于支持科研管理的数据分析与图形化展示，也可以指导开发新一代科研信息系统。项目的成果将会促进大学与政府资助机构走向精细化科研管理的道路。

148012.label: Realisation of objectives
148012.value: A research analytic framework has been proposed for lean research management. It measures research from three dimensions of quality (e.g. number of publications and their citations), relevance (e.g., disciplines and keywords) and connectivity (e.g. co-authorship). In particular, business intelligence methods are used to measure the quantity and quality of research, data mining and text mining methods are used to measure the research relevance, and social network analysis methods are used to measure the connectivity. New methods have also been proposed to extract data from multiple sources (e.g. bibliographic databases and patent databases), to transform the data into the uniformed format and to load the data into a research social network platform (i.e., ScholarMate). The proposed research analytic framework has been used for recommendation applications in reviewer assignment in government funding agencies and in performance management of funded research projects, e.g. statistical and benchmark reports. Visualization tools have also been developed based on the proposed Research Analytic Framework for the purposes of statistical and benchmark reports. They can support administrative users with ad-hoc queries for relevant information in research management. They support management users with statistical and benchmark reports with key performance indicators. They also support decision makers to do sensitivity analysis for research trend analysis. The proposed methods and developed tools are used to assist in the reviewer assignment in the National Natural Science Foundation of China, and to recommend relevant articles for researchers in supporting their daily research and innovations. The experiments have shown the good results as the proposed methods consider the research from three aspects, it well balanced the limitations of existing methods of considering only one aspects. 148812.label: Project Objectives

rows: 1. Does managerial spillover benefit the local Chinese firms in their management innovation?
2. Are local firm‘s absorptive capacity and the local FDI density associated with the relationship between managerial spillover and management innovation?
3. Does management innovation contribute to local firm performance?

148812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
148812.value: Multinational corporations play two key roles in implementing management innovations: inventing and implementing new management practices, and being involved in the diffusion of management innovations including the transfer of new management practices to other countries. However, management innovation is still under-researched (Birkinshaw & Mol, 2008). To fill in this gap, this proposed research investigates the effects of managerial spillover from multinational enterprises on management innovation of local Chinese firms as well as the moderating effects of absorptive capacity and the local FDI density. 对本土公司管理革新的管理溢出效应及本土公司吸收能力和地域外国直接投资密度的调节作用 简要 跨国公司在实施管理更新中扮演两个重要角色：发明和实践新管理知识， 参于向其他国家扩散包括新管理技能在内的管理更新。 然而，目前在管理更新方面的研究还很欠缺。为填补这方面的知识， 本研究建议旨在调查分析跨国公司对中国本土公司管理革新的管理溢出效应及本土公司吸收能力和地域外国直接投资密度的调节作用。

148812.label: Realisation of objectives
148812.value: A total of 400 firms from diverse industries and regions participated in the survey. The sample consists of 180 firms from Central China, 110 firms from Western China, and 110 firms from Eastern China. 91.5 % firms are from manufacturing sector, and 8.5% are from service sector. We conducted confirmatory factor analysis using Mplus 6.12 on the four latent constructs consisting of 33 items. Initial CFA assessment of the measurement model produced respectable fit: χ2(df=489) = 1153.27, p < .001; CFI = .912; RMSEA = .059; SRMR = .052. Additionally, the CFA results revealed reasonable reliability, convergent validity and discriminant validity for all scales. We conducted the analyses using PROCESS SPSS provided by Hayes (2013) to test the impact of managerial spillover on financial performance that is mediated by management innovation. The results of analyses (Model 58) with 1,000 bootstrapped samples shows a significant direct effect of managerial spillover on financial performance (B=0.072, p<0.01). The results also confirmed evidence of moderated mediation. We requested estimates of the conditional indirect effects at different levels of absorptive capacity. The indirect effect of managerial spillover on financial performance with 95% bias-corrected bootstrapped confidence interval was significant at high level of absorptive capacity: one SD below (B = -0.0076, SE = .0135; 95% CI [-0.0378, 0.017]), at the mean (B = 0.0076, SE = 0.0085; 95% CI [-.0081, 0.0256]), and one SD above the mean level of absorptive capacity (B = 0.0171, SE = 0.0077; 95% CI [.0049, .0364]). These results also provide significant evidence that managerial spillover has positive effect on management innovation (B=0.3476, p<0.01), and absorptive capacity has positive effect on management innovation (B= 0.6126, p<0.001). As the empirical data that we present above show, all of the objectives have been achieved. In other words, the data indeed show that 1. Managerial spillover benefits the local Chinese firms in their management innovation, 2. Local firm‘s absorptive capacity and the local FDI density are associated with the relationship between managerial spillover and management innovation, and 3. Management innovation contributes to local firm performance.

149412.label: Co - Investigator(s)

149412.label: Project Objectives
149412.value: To develop a novel methodology to support decision making on quality inspection policies and to reduce inspection errors; To design a modeling method to represent the domain knowledge of the inspection environment, the inspection capability of various measurements, and to estimate the production behavior of supplier through logic reasoning; To validate the proposed method through implementing it in a prototype system of decision support for quality inspection policies and conducting laboratory experiments.

149412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
149412.value: Product quality inspection, carried out to determine whether or not a product conforms to quality requirements, is an important instrument to assure product quality and is widely adopted in industry practice. However, errors can happen when a supplier deceives in the inspection to conceal the real quality through producing a “conforming quality” that satisfies the requirement. An inspection error may lead to serious consequences. For example, in 2008, some suppliers for Sanlu, a well-known Chinese dairy manufacture, diluted milk for profits and added melamine to dupe an inspection for determining protein content, affecting some 294,000 infants and killing six. This tragic scandal has revealed a serious problem: the quality inspection processes are lack of effective methods to avoid inspection errors when suppliers deceive in order to maximize their profit. The solution to this problem relies on incorporating domain knowledge into the inspection policies that guide an inspection process. However, domain knowledge cannot be captured in the traditional mathematical or statistical models used in quality management. To fill this void, we propose a belief-desire-intention modeling approach to factor the domain knowledge the inspection environment and the inspection capability of various measurements, and to estimate the production behavior of supplier through logic reasoning when analyzing the risks for inspection errors. The proposed model can be used as a foundation to design intelligent systems to monitor and detect quality problems timely and effectively. To validate the approach, a prototype system is to be developed based on the proposed belief-desire- -intention model to support flexible quality inspection policy decision making and laboratory experiments will be conducted to examine if such an intelligent system can enhance the decision outcome of quality inspection. This research will have significant contributions for both theory and practice. First, this research will provide a novel methodology to facilitate decision making on quality inspection policies. Second, by taking account of the domain knowledge regarding inspection methods and processes, our modeling approach can significantly reduce inspection errors in quality management and thus our research will have important economic implications for companies worldwide. Third, as a measure of technology transfer, we will make our prototype system available over the Internet and accessible to quality control managers, quality inspection decision makers, and other professional consultants. 产品质量检验用于确定一个产品是否符合质量要求，是保证产品质量的一个重要手段，也是广泛应用的行业惯例。但是，当供应商在检查时隐瞒产品的真实质量状况，并顺利混过质检时，检查便出现错误，这种错误可能导致严重的后果。例如，在2008年，作为中国知名乳品制造企业的三鹿集团，其生产的奶粉严重地危害了294000个婴儿的健康，并直接导致六名婴儿的死亡。这个悲剧的发生是由于三鹿集团的供应商想通过稀释牛奶获利，为了通过蛋白质含量的检测，不惜向牛奶中添加三聚氰胺。三鹿奶粉丑闻事件揭露了一个严重的问题：在质量检验过程中缺乏有效的方法用以检测供应商为了追逐利益最大化时的欺诈。 这个问题的解决方案依赖于将领域知识加入到质量检测的政策中，并指导检查过程。然而，在质量管理中，这种领域知识并不能在传统的数学或统计模型中使用。为了弥补这一缺憾，我们提出了一个基于信念-愿望-意图(BDI)的建模方法，把领域知识，检测环境以及不同检测方法的检测能力引入模型，并在分析检验错误的风险时，通过逻辑推理估计供应商的生产行为。该模型可作为一个基础来设计智能系统，这种智能系统可以及时有效地监控和检测质量问题。为了验证这个方法，我们基于提出的BDI模型开发了一个原型系统，用以支持灵活的质量检验政策，并通过实验模拟来检测这样的智能系统是否能改善质量检测的决策结果。 本研究对于理论和实践都有重大的贡献。首先，这项研究提供了一种新的方法，在制定质量检验政策时，促进决策支持。其次，通过考虑关于检验方法和流程的领域知识，我们的建模方法可以显著降低质量管理中的检测错误，因此我们的研究对于世界各地的公司都将具有重要的经济意义。第三，从技术转让层面上讲，我们会让我们的原型系统让全世界的质量控制管理者，质量检验决策者，以及其他专业顾问都可以通过互联网访问。

149412.label: Realisation of objectives
149412.value: We have completed all the original objectives of this project. First, we have developed a service-oriented methodology for the analysis and design of supply chain quality information systems to facilitate the decision making in supply chain quality management. In previous research, the quality management problem is often addressed from a contract design perspective. We argue effective information systems could also support supply chain quality management and propose a service-oriented approach for the analysis and design of such systems. Our proposed approach contains two parts: 1) a visual language for modeling the coordination and integration of the business processes and domain knowledge in quality management at knowledge level; 2) a mechanisms to connect the conceptual model with the Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) technique for symbol level modeling and system implementation. The validity of the overall modeling methodology is shown through a case study and the development of a prototype for a dairy supply chain context. Second, we improve the BDI framework and develop a modeling approach specifically for quality inspection. Putting in the context of dairy supply chain, suppliers may deliberately manipulate the products and falsify results of the specific testing methods for their benefits. To predict the supplier’s behavior and deal with this problem, we enrich the BDI framework to represent the supplier’s knowledge about the supplier chain. We develop reasoning rules that can mimic supplier’s reasoning process. By putting the supplier’s knowledge and reasoning rules into the system, we can infer their deception intention. For evaluation, we compare proposed approach with classic machine learning methods in terms of prediction accuracy. Users commentate that the DSS significantly reduce their decision difficulty in supply chain quality inspection. Third, we developed a prototype system of BDI-DSS and leverage it to further study the system’s impact on supply chain through laboratory experiments. This part is particularly interesting since the quality inspection process in supply chain is a repeated game between suppliers and buyers. The buyers may change their inspection policy by observing the suppliers historical activities, and vice versa. So, we conduct a laboratory experiment to examine the problem. In this experiment, we are interested in how the BDI-DSS may affect the buyers' behavior considering the existence of different contracts. The experiment shows that the adoption of BDI-DSS improves buyers' decision-making efficiency, in terms of decision time, inspection cost, and correctness on rejecting suppliers' fraudulent shipment, if there does not exist strong instruments to punish fraudulent suppliers. The DSS design may need to fit the contract type to further improve quality inspection effectiveness. This study extends prior research on the impacts of information technologies on supply chains.

149412.label: Major findings and research outcome
149412.value: The research contains both design science and empirical findings that lead to several publications (including the ones under review) as shown in part C. From a design science perspective, we propose a service-oriented system design and analysis approach, including a visual language for conceptual modeling and a mechanism to map the conceptual model to the BDI framework for implementation. This part of research is reported in paper # 3 in part C. From the BDI model extension’s perspective, we enrich the BDI framework for diary supply chain quality inspection. We designed special primitive propositions and reasoning rules for the quality inspection context. Based on such extensions, we can effectively estimate supplier intention and deal with deception. The research is reported in paper # 4 in part C. In addition, we show that in a general business process, agents’ goals can be learned from historical data, which can support the modeling of stakeholders in supply chain and other business processes. The research is reported in paper # 1 in part C. From the empirical understanding of BDI-DSS’s impact on buyer’s behavior in supply chain, we found that the adoption of BDI-DSS improves buyers' decision-making efficiency if there does not exist strong instruments to punish fraudulent suppliers. The research is reported in paper # 2 in part C.

149412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
149412.value: Our research shows the effectiveness of using the BDI framework in supply chain quality inspection context. It is possible that the framework can be also used to address other problems in supply chain. It would be worthwhile to explore the extension of our proposed framework in such different contexts.

149412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
149412.value: Quality management is one critical problem in supply chain. If the quality of raw materials is not appropriately controlled, the final products may be low quality and lead to serious outcomes. To combat with the supplier’s deception activities, this project takes an information system approach and provides systems & models to support manufacturer’s inspection policy making (i.e., when and what method to use for quality inspection). The project designs a modeling language to depict the context of supply chain for the design of quality information systems. The project models supplier’s beliefs and desires to infer their intentions to defraud, which provide hints for buyers to decide inspection policy. Experiments show the effectiveness of the approach and also show that the use of the system can improve the buyers' decision-making efficiency. The project provides a good exploration to the information system approach of tackling supply chain quality management problems.

149512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
149512.value: Over the past decade, business-to-consumer electronic commerce has seen tremendous growth, opening up vast opportunities for retailers to operate on a global scale. In Hong Kong, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are increasingly participating in business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce to expand their geographical reach, better target customers, or harness synergies between their online and offline businesses. Yet, participating in e-commerce can also have significant drawbacks. One problem is the online retailers’ limited ability to respond to customers’ problems during online shopping tasks (and specifically, during difficult or complex tasks, such as using product configurators). Such service failures have been shown to contribute to negative emotions (e.g., anger and frustration), which can lead to the termination of transactions, negatively influence repurchase intentions, and increase people’s tendency to spread negative word-of-mouth. At the same time, effectively addressing the customers’ problems and recovering from such service failures can have positive effects on customer retention and positive word-of-mouth. In a face-to-face, offline retailing context, detecting customers’ negative emotions is relatively easy, and appropriate action can be taken to remedy the situation and retain the customer. However, online retailers lack the ability to directly observe their customers, and need to find other ways to infer customers’ emotions. The proposed study will attempt to discover ways to detect users’ negative emotions in online environments, so as to mitigate negative effects of e-service failures. To this end, we will bring together research from human-computer interaction, marketing, and psychology, and hypothesize about how users’ emotions can be detected in online contexts. Further, we will develop a system to infer users’ negative emotions “on the fly;” such system can be used to provide users with additional help or guidance if negative emotions are detected. We will test the efficacy of the system in different cultures, so that online businesses targeting global customers can benefit from our findings. The proposed study will have some important long-term implications, as it will help online retailers compete in the global marketplace; in addition, the results will serve as a foundation for further research into detecting negative emotions in other contexts, such as in mobile applications. Overall, given the increasing importance of the Internet for Hong Kong’s economy, this study will be of great importance to businesses in Hong Kong as well as mainland China. 在過去十年，企業對消費者模式（B2C）的電子商務有顯著的增長，對零售商踏進國際舞台帶來無限的商機。透過B2C的電子商務，越來越多香港的中小型企業（SMEs）擴大其地域覆蓋範圍，更容易對顧客作出針對性銷售及服務，大大提升在線與離線業務之間的協同效應；然而，電子商務網購過程中也有明顯的缺點。其中一個缺點就是當回應顧客在網上購物時的問題（尤其是，在遇到困難或複雜的任務時，又或在使用產品配置時）網上零售商的能力是有限的。而這服務上的缺點已證明有助於產生負面情緒（例如，憤怒和挫折感），這可能會導致顧客終止網上交易，對再購意欲產生負面影響，及提高傳播負面口碑的傾向。 但是，如能有效地解決顧客在網購時的問題，對顧客忠誠度和服務口碑就能帶來正面作用。而在線下面對面的零售時，發現顧客的負面情緒是相對容易的，同時可採取適當的行動去糾正錯失，挽留顧客。相反地，網上零售商不能直接觀察到顧客的即時反應，需找一些方法來推斷客戶的情緒。建議的研究將試圖在網絡環境中尋找方法來檢測網上顧客的負面情緒，從而減輕對電子服務的負面影響。為此，我們將匯集人機互動，市場營銷和心理學，及在不同網絡環景下如何檢測到顧客的情緒假設推測。此外，我們將開發一個系統來推斷用戶的即時負面情緒，該系統當檢測到負面情緒會為用戶提供額外的幫助或指導。我們將在不同的文化下測試這系統的功效，使電子商務的全球客戶可以從我們的研究成果中受益。擬議的研究將有一些重要的長期影響，因為它會幫助網上零售商在全球市場的競爭；此外，研究結果亦可作為進一步的研究基礎，如在不同的情況下(例如：移動應用中)檢測負面情緒。總體而言，互聯網對香港經濟的重要性日益增加，這項研究將對香港以及中國大陸的企業有相當大的重要性。

149512.label: Realisation of objectives
149512.value: Overall, the objectives of the proposal have been satisfactorily achieved. First, using multiple studies, we have demonstrated that consumers’ negative emotions during interactions with online retailers can result in detectable behavioral changes, and that mouse cursor movements are a real-time indicator of users’ emotions. Second, drawing on the biopsychological theory of personality, we explain how the behavioral inhibition system primes behaviors leading to changes in mouse movements—specifically, changes to speed and distance in mouse movements, such that users experiencing negative emotions will exhibit slower mouse cursor speeds and longer distance. Third, based on this theoretical explanation, we have developed a way to measure mouse cursor movements in real time, and to calculate relevant movement parameters. Using a series of studies, we have demonstrated that participants experiencing negative emotions indeed have slower mouse cursor speeds and longer distance, that these effects can be attributed to negative valence, but not arousal, and that it is possible to predict negative emotions from mouse cursor movements.

149512.label: Major findings and research outcome
149512.value: In the paper “A Taxonomy of Web Personalization,” we have provided a conceptual framework of the dimensions and characteristics of Web personalization. Applying this taxonomy shows that implicitly acquired usage data (such as click path data or mouse cursor movement), which has a relatively short life span, has the potential to be used for dynamic, system-driven adaptation of content, presentation, or structure of Web sites on an individual level; for example, decisions aids may be dynamically presented when it is detected that a user is experiencing negative emotions. Relatedly, in the paper “User Modeling of Online Consumers: Between-Gender Differences in Click Path Data,” we demonstrated that it is indeed possible to use implicitly acquired data to make inferences about users, so as to build user-adaptive systems that can aid in providing each individual user with the interface that helps to best achieve the desired outcome. We demonstrated that readily available click path data can be used to distinguish female and male Web site visitors, in that women tended to need less time and have shorter click paths than men in online product configuration tasks. These inferences could then be applied to present different interfaces based on known preferences. Finally, in the paper “Inferring Negative Emotion from Mouse Cursor Movements” (currently under third round of review at MIS Quarterly), we demonstrated that negative emotion during system use—potentially influencing important user behaviors, including purchasing decisions, technology use, disclosure of information, and customer loyalty—can be inferred by differences in mouse cursor movements. Specifically, we extended and developed theory to explain how negative emotion activates responses in the brain’s behavioral inhibition system, which can influence how hand movements are programmed and executed. These reactions in the hand ultimately influence mouse cursor movements on the computer screen. A series of four studies in different settings supported these predictions. These studies consistently demonstrated that slower average cursor speed and greater cursor distance can indicate negative emotional responses.

149512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
149512.value: In our studies, we focused on predicting negatively valenced emotions in goal-directed tasks. We propose further research on which mouse cursor features predict negative emotion in hedonic tasks. Further, a natural next step would be to compute other statistics that may also be predictive of emotion and could potentially increase the negative emotion detection rate. Likewise, with the increase in the popularity of mobile devices, other popular input devices, such as touchscreens, sketchpads and in-air sensors (the Microsoft Kinect or the LeapMotion), have the potential to capture more sophisticated information than does the computer mouse; for example, touch screens touchscreen can capture the diameter of the finger and thereby infer pressure, in-air sensors can capture the z-dimension in addition to the x- and y- dimensions, and mobile devices can provide accelerometer data. Finally, future research could extend our findings to other contexts beyond negative emotions. For example, given emotional reactions accompanying fraudulent behavior or deception, future research can hypothesize what observable metrics can be used to detect such reactions, helping to minimize fraudulent or deceptive behaviors in a wide range of settings, ranging from online job applications to tax forms.

149512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
149512.value: In this research, we have explored whether it is possible to predict Internet users’ negative emotional states by analyzing mouse cursor movements. Building on research in psychology, we hypothesized that experiencing negative emotions will influence people’s hand movements; these difference in hand movements can be recorded by tracking computer users’ mouse movements. Through a series of studies, we confirmed that users experiencing negative emotions will exhibit slower mouse cursor speeds and longer distance. These findings suggest that the analysis of mouse cursor movements may provide researchers and system designers with an easy to deploy, but powerful, tool to infer users’ emotions in a broad range of contexts. For example, these findings can be used for testing different designs of Web sites, so as to reduce usability problems. Likewise, mouse cursor movements can be continuously monitored over a user’s entire interaction with a website, allowing managers to identify real-life “failure-points” in the interaction—i.e., points in the interaction that cause negative emotion and may ultimately cause the user to leave the site. Finally, our methodology also helps to build a foundation for proactively responding to customers’ negative reactions during website use in real time.

Analyze retailers’ mitigation strategies and evaluate their effectiveness in dealing with supply disruption and consumer stockpiling. Examine the impact of fixed-quota policy on consumer behavior.

149812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
149812.value: The aim of this project is to build an analytical framework to understand consumer stockpiling behaviors and retailer mitigation strategies under supply disruption risks. Supply disruption refers to the interruption of normal supply of goods due to various causes such as industrial accidents, natural disasters, labor strikes, and terrorist attacks. An industrial survey shows that 66% of supply chain managers consider supply interruption as one of their most significant concerns among all the supply chain related risks. Facing supply disruption risks, retailers and consumers may take active hedging actions instead of passively accepting whatever happens. For instance, consumers often stockpile in the events of supply disruption. Common disruption management strategies of retailers include stockpiling inventory, diversifying supply, contingent sourcing, adjusting price, imposing limiting-quote policy, and improving supply reliability. The interaction between consumers' stockpiling decisions and retailers' disruption management strategies is quite complex. First, supply disruption may lead to consumer stockpiling. Consumer stockpiling may further exacerbate the consequences of supply disruption, as large amounts of stockpiling may lead to substantial stock-out, which may induce more customers to stockpile. Second, consumer stockpiling may happen due to the "fear'' of supply shortage instead of actual supply disruption, due to reasons such as incomplete information and false belief about the supply availability. Third, retailer decisions such as increasing price, limiting supply, and imposing purchasing quota can greatly affect consumer behaviors. Due to the tight coupling and complex relationships, it is natural to jointly study the decisions of consumers and retailers under supply disruption. Unfortunately, the existing literature in this area is rare. The goal of this project is to build a conceptually unifying, mathematically rigorous, and practically relevant framework for analyzing the interaction between retailers' disruption management strategies and the consumers' stockpiling behaviors, in both monopoly and oligopoly markets. We will also explore useful guidelines for governments and non-profit organizations to deal with large-scale supply disruptions. The PI and Co-Is have strong research expertise in related research areas and have obtained interesting preliminary results. For instance, we find that ignoring consumer decisions under supply disruption could lead to substantial cost for retailers (as large as 25% profit loss). Furthermore, the cost is most significant when the risk of supply disruption is moderate. We also show that facing strategic consumers, the retailer may not always benefit from a limiting-quota policy. 本项目的目的是建立一个理论分析框架，以研究在面对供应中断风险的情况下常见的消费者抢购行为和零售商的有效对策。 供应中断是指由于各方面的原因，如工人罢工，自然灾害，恐怖袭击，或政府政策变化导致的商品的正常供应中断。调查结果显示，66％的供应链管理者认为供应中断风险是其面对的所有供应链相关的风险中最重要的问题之一。[1] 面对供应中断的风险，零售商和消费者可能会采取积极的应对方法，而不仅仅是被动地接受或者等待。例如，消费者往往会出现抢购或者囤货行为。零售商也通常会启动突发事件应急管理方案，常见的的策略包括提高安全库存，分散供应，后备采购，调整价格，限制顾客购买数量，提高供应可靠性等等。 消费者库存决策和零售商的中断管理战略之间的相互作用是非常复杂的。首先，供应中断可能会引发大量消费者抢购行为。而费者抢购可能进一步加剧供应中断所带来的后果，导致大量缺货，引发更多的消费者囤货。二，消费者抢购行为可能源于不完全信息或者消费者对未来供应短缺的错误估计，而不是实际的供应中断。第三，零售商的应对方案，比如提高价格，限制供应，并限制购买配额的决定会极大地影响消费者的行为。由于两者之间紧密又复杂的关系，需要我们把他们放在一个共同的框架下研究。 这个项目的目标是建立一个统一，严格，切合实际的框架，以分析供应中断如何影响消费者行为，以及在不同情况下零售商该如何有效应对。本项目的主持人是具有在相关研究领域的丰富的专业知识，并取得了有趣的初步结果。例如，我们发现，忽略了消费者的决策下供应中断可能会给零售商带来巨大的损失（比如，我们的数据显示达到25％的利润损失）。而且，这类损失在供应风险中等时达到最大。此外，我们也发现，面对战略的消费者，零售商可能并不总是受益于限制配额政策。

149812.label: Realisation of objectives
149812.value: We have successfully achieved all the above-stated project objectives. We have conducted comprehensive analytical studies on consumer stockpiling behaviors as well retailers’ optimal inventory and quota policies under supply disruption risks. We have also investigated the impact of supply chain structures and the critical issue of information asymmetry. Our research provides useful insights for retail managers on how to better understand consumer behaviors and how to use effective mitigation strategies to deal with supply disruption risks. Parts of our results have already been published in leading journals.
