149812.label: Major findings and research outcome
149812.value: First, we characterize consumers' stockpiling behavior when facing supply disruption risks. Based on the rational-expectations equilibrium analysis, we characterize the production valuation threshold above which a consumer would stockpile product for future consumption. We show that the threshold value has monotone property with respect to the price of the product, the holding cost of the consumers, and consumers’ risk attitudes. Our numerical studies also show that if the retailer ignored the consumer stockpiling behaviors, it would lead to substantial profit loss. Moreover, the loss is largest when supply risk is medium-level. This counter-intuitive result provides important managerial implications to retail supply chains. The key results are summarized in paper #6 in Part C. Second, we analyze retailers’ mitigation strategies and evaluate their effectiveness in dealing with supply disruption and consumer stockpiling. We derive the optimal inventory policy and show how it is affected by the risk attitude of the consumers, the product valuations as well as the risk of supply disruption. We also study the impact of limited capacity and the effectiveness of quota policies for the retailer. We identify the conditions under quota policy benefits the retailer. We have also examined the impact of disruption risks under different supply chain structures. Using a Cournot competition model with two competing supply chains, we show that supply chain centralization is a dominant strategy and hence the equilibrium strategy; nevertheless, if the supply risk is low, centralization could actually decrease the supply chain profit, compared with the case where both chains do not choose centralization. The key results are summarized in paper #2 and #6 in Part C. Finally, we study an important issue of asymmetric information related to supply uncertainty. We consider the supply uncertainty information disclosure decision in export-processing systems. Our results provide plausible explanations to the diverse information sharing behaviors observed in practice. We also show that the effect of non-disclosure is exacerbated by the effect of double marginalization, resulting in severe efficiency loss for the supply chain. We propose three corrective mechanisms (i.e., vertical integration, mandatory disclosure, and production restriction). We also study the problem of uncertain supply information asymmetry in wireless service industry and propose optimal capacity allocation, pricing strategies and incentive designs. The key results are summarized in papers #1, 3, 4, and 5 in Part C.

149812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
149812.value: The fast development of information technology and social networks pose new opportunities and challenges to the relationships between suppliers, retailers and consumers. Based on the models and results in this project, we can further consider the impact of social influence in retail supply chain management. The PI is conducting some preliminary research along this direction. Related empirical and experimental studies will also be interesting and important directions to explore. The PI is exploring possible collaboration opportunity with leading retailers to obtain field data for study.

149812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
149812.value: In this project, we provide the first analytical study in the operations and supply chain management literature on consumer stockpiling behaviors and retailer mitigation strategies under supply disruption risks. We characterize the conditions under which consumers tend to stockpile products. We derive the retailer’s optimal inventory policy and show how it is affected by the risk attitude of the consumers, the product valuations as well as the supply disruption risks. We also illustrate the retailers’ substantial profit loss if ignoring consumer behaviors. Furthermore, we study the impact of limited capacity and identify the conditions under quota policy benefits the retailer. Finally, we examine the impact of disruption risks under different supply chain structures and the issue of asymmetric information related to supply uncertainty. Our findings provide very useful insights for practical operations and supply chain management. Parts of our results have already been published in leading journals and conferences.

151012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
151012.value: Differences between public and private organizations have held the attention of academics in a range of social science disciplines for a number of decades, and are fundamental to public administration. Differences were, and sometimes still are, portrayed starkly—typically based on ownership. Conceptual development points towards the multidimensional nature of ‘publicness’: organizations vary by ownership (private, public, nonprofit), funding (government grants versus consumer payments) and control (by political or economic forces). This project will undertake: 1. The first large-scale stratified random probability sample from all ‘registered organizations’ in Hong Kong to contribute towards theoretical debates on the relationship between publicness and managerial and organizational characteristics. 2. A first time examination of intraorganizational variations based upon respondents’ position in the hierarchy. Longstanding assumptions about publicness in the academic literature will be placed under the most rigorous empirical microscope to date. The project will ascertain if some of the most widely cited publicness differences are maintained. The most widely reported difference is that managers in organizations with higher levels of publicness (public ownership, public funding and high political control) perceive greater administrative constraints on incentives--pay, promotion and disciplinary action--than do those with low publicness. Answers to questions on this topic and others (organizational environments, structures and process) have been to date undertaken in ad hoc studies with small samples, focused on limited functional categories (e.g. hospitals, airlines), implementing elite surveys typically in the USA. Hong Kong represents an ideal location for a study of publicness and its antecedents because there is a sampling frame of ‘registered organizations’: 287,000 companies (with ≥ 10 employees) plus public and subvented agencies. Stratified sampling by industry type and organizational size will be implemented, maintaining appropriate confidence levels and intervals. The study will be conducted by academics grounded in research on publicness (Bozeman, Rainey, Walker), managerial and organizational antecedents (Rainey, Walker) with appropriate methodological skills (Bacon-Shone, Jung). The outcome of the project will allow for inferences about the implied effects of publicness by cross-walking organizational attributes with levels and types of publicness. It will contribute towards a more comprehensive understanding the new global political and economic landscape resulting from organizational forms and behaviours that changed publicness boundaries following the global economic crisis. This challenged understanding of ‘publicness’: private banks were brought into public ownership (UK), government’s used public resources to spend their way out of difficulty (China), and political control over private companies has increased (hedge funds in the EU). 两者之间的差异被僵化地描述，其中以组织所有权为区隔基础的论述最具代表性，迄今有时仍为如此。根据概念的发展现况，组织的公共性具备多重面向的性质，会随其所有权（私营、公共、非营利）、资金来源（政府挹注、消费者付费）、控制权（通过政治或经济力量）的不同而改变。 本研究计划之目的有二，分别为： （1）自香港全体的注册组织中，实施大规模的分层随机抽样，以增进公共性、管理与组织特征之关联性的理论探讨； （2）根据受访者在组织阶层中的职位，检视组织内部的变化情形。 在学术文献中被长期采用的公共性假设，将会被本研究计划最严谨的实证研究来仔细检验。本研究要确认最常被引述的一些公共性差异是否将存续。当中最常被谈及的差异，乃是高度公共性之组织（如公有、有公共资金挹注、高度的政治控制）中的经理人，他们对于薪资、晋升、惩戒等诱因所感受到的行政约束力，强于低度公共性之组织中的经理人。为寻找本主题及其它相关主题（组织环境、结构、流程）的答案，美国曾特别聚焦于少数的功能类型组织（如医院、航空公司）进行小样本研究，对组织中的菁英阶级实施调查。 香港因具备 “注册组织” 的抽样框架，是研究公共性及其前因的理想地点：有287,000家至少有10名雇员的公司行号，以及各公共与政府资助的机构。在维持适当的置信水平与区间之下，本研究将依据产业类型与组织规模来分层抽样。本计划将由研究领域为公共性（Bozeman, Rainey, Walker）、管理与组织前因（Rainey, Walker）的学者执行，并以适当的研究方法（Bacon-Shone, Jung）实施。 本研究藉由公共性的高低水平与不同类型来分析组织属性，结果将得到公共性之隐含影响的推论。它将使我们对崭新的全球政经样貌有更全面的认识，而这新样貌乃是在全球经济危机之后，由改变公共性边界的各种组织形式与行为所塑造的。这也挑战我们对公共性的认知：在英国，有私营银行成为公有；在中国，政府通过公共资源的支出来走出困境；在欧盟，则是增加对私营公司（对冲基金）的政治控制。

151012.label: Realisation of objectives
151012.value: This project sought to examine publicness across a sample of organizations in Hong Kong and to explore variations in dimensional publicness and managerial and organizational characteristics. In doing this the project aimed to make methodological contributions (intra-organizational variations, comparisons between data sources). However, the project was unable to meet these objectives because of fundamental difficulties that were encountered in data collection. These difficulties are elaborated below, along with the actions taken by the research team to overcome them. The survey instrument was designed by the research team (including face to face meetings with the Co-Is in the USA). It examined organizational goals (and influences on those), organizational decisions (and influences on those), social media, performance information use, and strategy, rules and compliance. The survey was completed was translated into Chinese. The sample was developed in keeping with the research proposal. Source material to build the sample from Government departments, ICAC (publicly available list), NGOs (S88 organizations and HKCSS, Kadoorie Institute HKU and Jockey Club Community Chest lists), and private firms (Census Department) were identified, and contact information collected. There a number of challenges in building the sample. No information on organizational size was available for the NGOs, and the disaggregate way data from private firms was held made it difficult to accurately estimate organizational size (for example each branch of KFC is registered as an organization and the full size of the enterprise cannot easily be identified). These difficulties meant it took a long time to build the sample. The final sample, stratified by organizational size, resulted in 1010 organizations. Of these organizations 600 were private firms (of 8151 organizations), 98 ICAC organizations (census to be taken), 230 NGOs (460, a 50% sample taken) and 83 government departments (census to be taken). The project faced the biggest challenge in the field (late 2014 until the February 28 2016). The SSRC survey team at HKU (Professor Bacon-Shone was a Co-I) undertook the following data collection procedures: Standard interview procedures were adopted: SSRC interviewers were trained on the project and survey. All organizations were contact by mail, and followed up by telephone to secure an interview (each organization was followed up three times). Respondents could complete the survey by paper and pen, by email, online or by a telephone interview. The following challenges in data collection led to a number of decisions to make changes to the research design, and eventually abandon data collection. 1. An organization was defined, for the purposes of this study, as having more than 10 employees. However, after several months in the field we decided to change this to 100. The primary motive for this was the difficulty encountered in identifying a ‘trustworthy’ contact in smaller organizations. The information we were able to build was very spotty and was not representative, thus we could not populate the appropriate cells in our sample frame. 2. Private firms would not cooperate. It was not possible to access the respondents that we were seeking (largely senior managers) because gatekeepers (secretaries) barred our access. Given these difficulties rather than approach senior executives we focused attention on the communication departments/person, as an outward focused unit. Some slight progress was made here (a small number of respondents) but once the correct respondent was identified a gatekeeper would often again bar access. In total 3,954 firms were approached and 17 interviews achieved: 0.03% of our target of 600, or 0.004% of those approached (noncontact 2,395, no answer 899, fax number 210, disconnected 221, busy/refuse/partial 212). Zero successful interviews were achieved with the ICAC list of organizations. 3. When we accessed an organization, particularly in government, they were unable to answer some of the questions posed. These questions typically related to organizational decisions. Respondents were asked to identify some important decision they had made in the last year. After this we followed up with a number of questions. Many had not personally made decisions (these issues did not emerge in our pilot). Thus, the survey design was changed to ask about decisions in the organization that were connected with or knew about. Alongside this the question order was changed with the more contemporary social media questions posed first. The last change we made to increase response rates was to remove a section of the questionnaire to reduce its length. 4. Most success was had with NGOs. However, only 47 completed surveys were achieved, a response rate of 20.4% of our target sample of 230. To achieve these responses 457 NGOs were approached: noncontact 245, no answer 99, fax number 3, disconnected 7, busy/refuse/partial 56. 5. Gatekeepers again blocked access to government officials. After six months in the field 2 questionnaires had been completed (noncontact 44, no answer 13, fax number 1, disconnected 0, busy/refuse/partial 25). As alterative approach the Government Telephone Directory (available online) was used to make a new sample frame of 567 senior officers. After repeated attempts to contact these civil servants 7 additional responses were achieved (noncontact 114, no answer 92, fax number 3, disconnected 3, busy/refuse/partial 290, retired/resigned 56). In the February 2016, some 16 months after entering the field, only 69 responses were achieved. The decision was made to abandon data collection. RELATED RESEARCH During the early part of the project it was decided to also work on related projects on publicness to move the research agenda forward, and ensure contribution towards theoretical debates on publicness. A survey vignette study was conducted, and published in “Public Management Review”, on perceptions of public ownership and governmental performance (efficiency, equity, and probity) across East Asia and the USA. A second manuscript examining different performance dimensions was prepared and presented at a conference. This study brought a methodological innovation to studies of publicness by implementing a survey vignette methodology. The project team also turned to a secondary dataset, the National Administrative Studies Project data on public and non-profit organizations. The study was rejected from Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory on the third round of reviews because of growing concerns within the discipline about common source bias (our data were cross-sectional). The study was revised to implemented a novel methodology using interactions to tackle the common source bias problem. To our knowledge the approach has not been implemented before. It was submitted to Public Performance and Management Review where it is currently R&R. This work made contributions towards intraorganizational perspectives through the methods used to aggregate individual respondent data to the organizational level. The project also started to examine publicness in the university sector and an abstract was accepted for presentation at the Institutional Design Frontiers: Higher Education Summit at Arizona State University. This drew in Professor Rhys Andrews (Cardiff University) to the project. However, Professor Andrews because very seriously ill in the late 2014 and only returned to work at the end of 2015. Work is ongoing on this project.

151012.label: Major findings and research outcome
151012.value: Publicness has many influences on organizational design and achievements. Three studies were undertaken in this project drawing on different aspects of publicness, examining different management and organizational characteristics from different perspectives. Study 1 (Walker et al. 2013; Brewer and Walker 2013) ownership publicness is tackled. Ownership has been long debated in theory and practice, and questions raised about whether services should be provided by public or private organizations. This study, employing a survey vignette experimental research design, examined the potential impact of cultural differences in East Asia and the USA on perceptions of public ownership and government performance (efficiency, equity and probity). Findings indicate few public ownership and limited country differences, but a consistency in the rating of vignettes, suggesting convergence. In study 2 (Jung, Walker and Brewer 2013) ownership publicness is examined. longstanding bureaucratic characteristics (i.e., rigid personnel systems, high levels of red tape, and excessive risk avoidance by employees) were examined in public and non-profit organizations in the USA (ownership publicness). The study findings, drawing upon the perceptions of employees, showed that bureaucratic pathologies are more heavily concentrated in public organizations compared with nonprofits, and have more harmful effects on work quality. The results further show that efforts to clarify work tasks, which is widely touted as a cure for bureaucratic pathologies in both sectors, enhances work quality in nonprofits but not in the public sector. The study also implements a novel approach to address common source bias in multiple regression models that use cross-sectional data by presenting the results from interactions, rather than independent tests. Study 3 examines funding publicness and uses secondary data from the UK university sector. Analysis of the data shows that funding publicness has a nonlinear relationship with research and study performance in the shape of an inverted U. This suggests that at some point too much public money in the university system has a negative impact on research (quality of publications and grants) and teaching outcomes (PhD graduation rates, student satisfaction and continuation rates).This suggests that at some point too much public money in the university system has a negative impact on research (quality of publications and grants) and teaching outcomes (PhD graduation rates, student satisfaction and continuation rates). Together these studies indicate that careful thought has to be given to questions of organizational design: People outside government may not be so concerned with who actually provides public services (Study 1). However, an employee perspective indicates that the characteristics of public and non-profit organizations vary and implications for organizational outputs (Study 2). Finally, Study 3 draws attention to the level of public funding and suggests that within public ownership organization too much funding can damage organizational outcomes.

151012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
151012.value: Publicness remains an important issue for the research and practice of public management. Further work is required to examine the relationship between publicness (funding, ownership and political control) and organizational characteristics to inform theory and practice about the most appropriate organizational design for public service delivery. Given the challenges faced in this project (a response rate of 0.14% from the 5000+ organizations we contacted) future research might consider different research methods such as experimental research designs in the laboratory and through survey vignette methodologies.

151012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
151012.value: Publicness, that is ways in which organizations vary based on ownership, funding and political control sits at the heart of many debates about the delivery of public services. Should they be delivered by a private firm or government? Should private firm experience high political authority to ensure public goals are met? What level of public funding is appropriate in publicly owned organizations? This study set out to examine such questions through a large-scale survey on this topic in Hong Kong. It was, however, not possible to collect robust data due to problems of overwhelming nonresponse from the 5000+ organizations approached (0.014% response rate). The study, therefore, turned to three different datasets to progress knowledge on publicness and concluded that careful thought has to be given to questions of publicness and organizational design: Study 1 found that people outside government may not be so concerned with who actually provides public services. Findings from Study 2 indicated, from an employee perspective, that the characteristics of public and non-profits vary and have implications for organizational outputs. Finally, Study 3 draws attention to the level of public funding in universities and suggests that within public ownership organization too much funding can damage organizational outcomes.

151212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
151212.value: With its broad explanatory power, agency theory has been widely used by researchers in a variety of social sciences (Eisenhardt, 1989). The classic principal-agent models highlight the information and incentives problems between agents (e.g., employees, contractors) and their principals (e.g., employers): in the absence of impeccable monitoring and incentive schemes, principals are vulnerable to agents’ opportunistic behaviors, including unethical and deceptive actions (Jensen, 1976; Williamson, 1984). The major focus of agency theory, however, ignores people’s moral motivations (Heath, 2009) and the social consequences of principals’ and agents’ actions (Dee, 1992). As a result, scholars suggest that the uncritical application of agency theory has already led to inadvertent mischief in organizations (e.g., Heath, 2009; Ghoshal, 2005; Kulik, 2005). Thus, this proposal seeks to amend agency theory by theoretically and empirically addressing the moral issues of principal-agent relationships in a broader social context. To exonerate themselves from ethical responsibility, principals often choose to hire an agent to delegate ethically questionable actions (Hammman, Loewenstein, & Weber, 2010). Similarly, agents may also feel less accountable for engaging in unethical actions dictated by principals. This view seems consistent with the popular public belief of often untrustworthy agents (Murnighan, Cantalon, & Elyashiv, 2001). In this research, however, we propose that agents don’t always behave less ethically as a result of the diffusion of moral responsibility (Darley & Latane, 1968). Instead, we suggest that their actions are a function of principals’ reputation, the ethical nature of principals’ commands, the social consequences (harm vs. benefits) of the delegated actions, and the incentive alignment between principals and agents. For example, accessing multiple principals (Dee, 1992) gives agents the opportunity to choose more over less ethical principals. When incentives are similar, agents will be motivated to work for more ethical principals who are less likely to dictate unethical orders. On the other hand, the social costs of delegating unethical actions (e.g. the harm to others) may loom large to agents when principals enjoy more benefits. Thus, all else equal, the lack of a seamless incentive system between principals and agents may discourage agents from carrying out principals’ unethical orders, especially when agents’ smaller gains don’t match others’ greater losses (Gneezy, 2005). We propose three complementary experimental and field studies to test these propositions and a new principal-agent model of moral relations in organizations. 代理理论凭借其强大的解释能力，已被社科领域的各类研究人员广泛运用(Eisenhardt, 1989)。经典的委托代理模型强调了委托人（如雇主）和代理人（如雇员、承包商）之间的信息以及奖励的问题:当缺少完善的监管以及奖励机制时，委托人容易受到代理人机会主义行为的伤害，包括不道德的以及欺骗性的行为(Jensen, 1976; Williamson, 1984)。 然而，代理理论的主要关注点却忽略了人的道德动机(Heath, 2009)以及委托人和代理人行为的社会后果(Dee, 1992)。因此，学者认为，不加辨别地使用代理理论已在无意中对机构造成了伤害(e.g., Heath, 2009; Ghoshal, 2005; Kulik, 2005)。因此，此项提案将在更广泛的社会背景之下结合理论和经验指出委托代理关系中的道德问题，并最终达到修改代理理论的目的。为了逃避自己的道德责任，委托人往往会选择聘请代理人并将存在道德问题的行为委派给他(Hammman, Loewenstein, & Weber, 2010)。同样，代理人也可能觉得从事由委托人委派的不道德行为时，自己负较少责任。这种观点似乎与不可靠的代理人的大众流行观点相一致(Murnighan, Cantalon, & Elyashiv, 2001).然而，在这项研究中，我们提出的观点是：因为道德责任的传播(Darley & Latane, 1968)，代理人不总是存在不道德的行为。相反，我们认为他们的行为是以下要素的应变量：委托人的声誉，委托人命令的道德本质，委派行为造成的社会后果（损害与收益）以及委托人和代理人之前的激励准则。例如，接触多个委托人让代理人(Dee, 1992)有机会选择更加道德的委托人。在奖励相近的条件下，代理人将倾向于为更加道德的委托人工作，他们委派不道德任务的可能性比较低。另一方面，代理人接受委派进行不道德行为的社会成本（如对他人的伤害）很高，但委托人往往得到更多利益。因此，在其他条件相同的情况下，委托人和代理人之间缺少无缝奖励制度可能会打消代理人接受委托人不道德行为的念头，特别是当代理人的收益与其他方面的损失不匹配时(Gneezy, 2005)。因此，我们建议进行三个互补的实验以及实地考察，以在机构中测试这些命题以及全新的加入道德关系的委托代理模型。

151212.label: Realisation of objectives
151212.value: **Note: Sadly, the CO-I, Prof. J Keith Murnighan passed away before the project was completed. Thus, I used “I” or “the PI” instead of “we” in some places when I described the research outcomes of the project. We have achieved most of the objectives we planned before. Specifically, we have completed two different papers investigating the dynamic moral relationships between principals and agents. The two papers have adequately addressed the first two objectives in different aspects. Our results in both papers show that agency theory’s fairly narrow assumptions overlook people’s common moral and social motivations: economic incentives do not always dominate human motivation and both principals and agents can influence each other's moral choices in their dynamic interactions. We did not, however, fully address the original third objective about developing a new model in principal-agent relationships. The data we collected are not entirely consistent with our original predictions. Thus, it was difficult for us to entirely achieve the original third objective. Following our original proposal, we still initially developed our first paper in the context of agency theory. After the paper was rejected by Organization Science, Management Science, and Organization Behavior and Human Decision Making Processes, however, the PI realized that the paper needs to be considerably rewritten to fit it better with readers in management. For example, one editor said "our readership is already convinced of the limitations of agency theory and we have already published a number of articles that offer exactly the type of theory that not only describes but also explains your findings (for example, research on obedience, on identity, on social norms, etc.)." Thus, the PI collected more data and developed two different papers by investigating the dynamic moral interactions between principals and agents. Specifically, the first paper tested different predictions by moral diffusion models and moral similarity hypothesis in principal-agent relationships (the new, fourth objective). Unlike previous research, which often focused heavily on untrustworthy and/or unethical agents, we investigated how agents would choose and respond to a principal’s honest vs. dishonest orders when they had the discretion to choose their preferred principal. Our results suggest that moral considerations rather than just economic payoffs had a big hand in determining agents’ moral choices in dynamic principal-agent relationships. The PI is currently revising the paper and plans to submit to Administrative Science Quarterly. In the second paper, we investigated the (indirect) influence of agents on principals in their dynamic moral relationships. Our results suggest that agents can also have a strong impact on principals’ moral choices, not only via their unethical advice but also through the signal of their moral character. This paper contributes to the literatures of principal-agent moral relationships by presenting one of the first studies investigating the influence of agents on principals’ moral decisions. It has been published in Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization (See Part C). (A final note on additional attempts to address the third objective: As note, we had initially tried to achieve the third objective. After the paper was rejected by three management journals, the PI decided to make different attempts to partially address this objective. Specifically, the PI collected quite a bit new data by investigating the dynamic moral interactions between principals and agents. Although the new data did not allow us to develop a brand new model, we wrote two different research papers to further investigate the moral relationships between principals and agents in the realms of business ethics and social preferences. In particular, we expand the existing models by testing different predictions by the moral diffusion models and moral similarity hypothesis in principal-agent relationships (Please also see the new objective 4 we included in the section of 5.4.).

151212.label: Major findings and research outcome
151212.value: As noted, we have written two different papers to investigate the dynamic moral relationships between principals and agents. In the first paper, we tested different predictions by moral diffusion models and moral similarity hypothesis in principal-agent relationships. On the one hand, moral diffusion models predict that, to reduce their own moral responsibility and maintain an appearance of innocence, principals will be motivated to hire agents to engage in immoral actions. They also predict that agents will be more open to immoral actions requested by their principals than they would be to those same immoral actions taken on their own. On the other hand, however, the attraction paradigm in psychology (Byrne, 1971, 1997) and the homophily principle in sociology (Lazarsfeld & Merton, 1954) suggest that agents will choose to work for principals with a “moral similarity” instead of simply being more open to immoral orders initiated by dishonest principals. Our results support moral similarity hypothesis instead of moral diffusion models, suggesting that agents did not display diffused moral responsibility when they had the opportunity to choose honest over dishonest principals. In particular, having a free choice among several principal orders decreased moral diffusion, leading agents to act at least as honestly as when they acted alone, or more. In addition, a prevalence of dishonest principal orders led to increased dishonest behavior by agents. I am currently revising the paper and plan to submit it to Administrative Science Quarterly. The second paper has been published in Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization (See part C). In the paper, we went beyond the research on the diffusion of responsibility by investigating the influence of agents’ character on principals’ moral choices. In one study, we allowed principals to choose an honest or dishonest agent. The results showed that having the opportunity to choose dishonest agents, regardless of the agents’ ultimate intentions for their previous lies, increased the likelihood that principals would subsequently hire the agents to lie on their behalf to harm others. In another study, we randomly paired principals and agents to avoid potential self-selection effects and found that observing agents telling harmful black lies or seemingly harmless white lies led to increased immoral actions by their principals. Our results contribute to the literatures of moral diffusion and principal-agent relationships by revealing some of the inherent dynamics in the principal-agent moral interactions.

151212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
151212.value: Our research suggests additional avenues for future research. First, our research suggests that both principals and agents can have positive effects on each other’s ethical choices. Because previous research often focuses on the diffused moral responsibility in principal-agent relationships, future research is needed to understand how to increase moral actions by both principals and agents. Second, future research might further investigate how principals and agents have influences over each other’s moral actions in their repeated and dynamic moral interactions. Our two papers only addressed the influences of principals and agents on each other separately. Also, we did not investigate repeated principal-agent moral interactions. Thus, our research opens the door to a host of important questions concerning moral actions by both principals and agents, and what factors influence their dynamic moral interactions. Third, although our second paper (Wang & Murnighan, 2016, see Part C) suggests that observing agents’ white lies can increase principals’ dishonest actions, we did not test whether white lies told for social or psychological reasons have different effects on the perceptions of an agent’s moral character. Future research might further investigate the moral signals of different kinds of white lies and how they may influence principal-agent moral interactions.

151212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
151212.value: Diffusion of responsibility models suggest that principals often seek to shift their moral responsibility by employing agents to engage in immoral actions instead of acting on their own. On the other hand, it is also easier for agents to accept principals’ immoral orders than acting immorally themselves because they are “merely taking orders”. Our research provides new insights into the moral dynamics of principal-agent relationships. In particular, our results suggest that both principals and agents are more likely to collude with counterparts who have shady morals. For example, devious principals are more likely to hire devious agents to lie for them and unscrupulous agents are more likely to work for similarly unscrupulous principals. In other words, even in the moral realm, we suggest that birds of a feather will flock together. Thus, our research suggests that simply assuming that agents are untrustworthy does not seem warranted, with future research being clearly needed to extend agency theory by clarifying the theoretical dynamics of principal-agent relationships in the context of organizational and business ethics.

151612.label: Major findings and research outcome
151612.value: Online shopping facilitating information, such as product review, is proving to be critical information for online consumers’ shopping decision. Online shopping facilitating information refers to the shopping decision aiding information that originates from a recommendation system and the descriptions of the assessment of a product composed by either product experts or customers who had previously purchased the merchandise. To this end, consumers are constantly confronted with unmanageable shopping facilitating information during the online shopping process. Consequently, being unable to process the online shopping facilitating information systematically, they opt to abandon the purchase. This research seeks to understand how consumers could be better aided when facing with product reviews. Through our empirical investigations, we observe that an online shopping website can offer varying genres of product reviews at different junctures to enhance consumers’ decision-making performance by understanding the information foraging nature of consumers. Elaborately, we observed that consumers tended to use two different genres of product review information sequentially: 1) following product attribute-oriented review information during the screening phase, and 2) foraging for product usage-oriented review information during the evaluation phase. Additionally, contextual review cues could be introduced to moderate the relationship between product review content and consumers' judgment of product review helpfulness. Specifically, in the presence of temporal cue, concrete product review content is perceived as more helpful when the temporal cue indicates near than distant. By contrast, the abstract review is perceived as more helpful when the temporal cue is distant than when it is near. When social cue is considered, concrete product review content is not perceived as significantly different in review helpfulness regardless of the social cue; however, an abstract review is perceived as more helpful when the social cue indicates near than distant.

151612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
151612.value: Our empirical investigations focus on product review information and the influence of its provision on consumers’ decision-making performance within a shopping website. Considering cross-website foraging of information is beyond the scope of this research. Moreover, expanding the research endeavor beyond a focal website could provide further macro-level insights to consumer behavior. Additionally, our study focuses on the product review information with little regard to the valence of the review content. Future studies could consider how review valence influences consumer evaluations on review helpfulness that varies in concreteness.

152012.label: Realisation of objectives
152012.value: All research objectives had been addressed over the project reporting period. Specifically, with respect to Objectives 1 and 3, we first examined the impacts of litigation risk (which we use auditors’ sanction risk as proxy) on auditors’ reporting behavior and the audit quality in China. The findings had been reported in two research papers, whereas one working paper was presented in an international accounting conference (and now under review in a prestigious international accounting journal – Journal of Accounting, Auditing and Finance) and another paper has been published in the 2014 issue of a peer-reviewed scholarly accounting journal (namely Journal of International Accounting Research). A related research paper (based on our examination on the institutional environment in China) has been generated during the process, and the paper has now been published in the 2015 issue of an accounting and finance journal (namely Journal of International Financial Management & Accounting). With respect to Objectives 1 and 2, we collected individual auditor’s characteristics and began with examining how these characteristics affect a CPA firm’s audit quality in emerging China. The results show that a closer monitoring within a CPA firm (which we use the ratio of staff-to-partner as a proxy), a higher proportion of qualified personnel, and a higher proportion of female accountants are associated with a higher audit quality. These findings had been reported in a working paper which was accepted for presentation in 2014 Asia Conference on Economics & Business Research, and now is currently under a second-round review by another international accounting journal – Journal of International Accounting Research. We have also compiled a dataset of individual auditor’s turnover incidences, and performed analyses to address the three research objectives. Consistent with our expectations as stated in the research proposal, we find that individual auditor’s characteristics and litigation risks significantly affect auditor’s turnover decision, and thus audit quality. The findings had been reported in a working paper that fits for conference presentation and ultimately targets for a journal submission. Section 6 provides a summary of the research papers produced in relation to the project objectives.

152012.label: Major findings and research outcome
152012.value: This project is the first to comprehensively examine the association between individual auditor switch, litigation risk exposure, and audit quality, using a natural experimental setting. Specifically, our research findings reveal a significant impact of litigation risk on an individual signatory auditor’s turnover decision. Besides, we find that an individual auditor’s characteristics (e.g., gender and education) together with the extent of monitoring with firms (in terms of staff-to-partner ratio) substantially affect audit quality supplied and audit fees received as well as the turnover decision. Below is the list of major findings. 1. A higher CPA firm’s litigation risk is associated with a higher propensity of signatory auditors’ turnover decision. 2. Auditors’ reporting conservatism (audit quality) associated with signatory auditors is improved after they change their employer. Besides, they tend to charge lower audit fees after the turnover. 3. Individual auditor’s characteristics, e.g., education background, gender, role in engagement, are also found to be significantly associated with the turnover decisions and audit quality. 4. Litigation risk faced by auditors (i.e., sanction risk) is found to be a key factor in improving audit quality where sanctioned auditors report more conservatively after receiving the public criticism. 5. While CPA firm’s size is important in affecting audit quality, the impact is present only for CPA firms with high litigation risks. 6. A closer monitoring of audit personnel by signatory auditors (i.e., a smaller staff-to-partner ratio) results in higher audit fees. As for the research outcomes, a dataset of auditor’s litigation risks, individual auditor’s characteristics, and individual auditor’s turnover decision has been compiled. Besides, five research papers had been initiated throughout the project reporting period. Two papers had been published in the prestigious accounting and finance journals, namely in the 2014 issue of the Journal of International Accounting Research and in the 2015 issue of the Journal of International Financial Management and Accounting; one paper was presented in the 25th Asian-Pacific Conference on International Accounting Issues in November 2013 (which is now under review in the Journal of Accounting, Auditing and Finance); one paper is currently under a second-round review in the Journal of International Accounting Research; and one paper is ready for presentation in conference/journal submission. Part C contains details of these five research papers.

152012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
152012.value: Based on the dataset compiled (together with possibly further data collection), there could be more research projects generated. For example, whether the turnover decisions will have impacts on investor decisions (i.e., market reactions) and to what extent such decision is conditioned on signatory auditors’ characteristics. Besides, surveys on accounting practitioners and students about their perception of individual auditors’ changes could be done so as to have an in-depth understanding of the auditors’ turnover decisions and their impacts on various stakeholders. We will continue exploring the possibility of conducting these projects and formulating research proposals, if feasible, as for further development of the research.

152012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
152012.value: To date, little attention has been given to the employment preferences of certified public accountants (CPAs). In contrast, there are many studies of CPA firms that investigate issues such as independence, fees, and audit quality. Very recently, however, there is a call for research on individual partners who are in charge of specific audits (Gul et al. 2011). Our project examines individual auditor preferences as regards who they wish to work for. In particular, we investigate auditors’ work-place choices from the view point of litigation risk. The data are from China where an auditor’s exposure to risk varies a lot. We (1) empirically investigate the impacts of increased/decreased litigation risk exposures on an individual auditor’s turnover decision, and (2) examine if such turnover decisions are affected by an individual auditor’s characteristics (e.g., gender, age, education, etc.). We also (3) examine what happens to audit quality after a partner changes employment. The findings of this study are important for researchers, accounting practitioners, and regulators and enable them to better understand the impacts of litigation risk exposures on individual auditors’ turnover decisions and post-switch audit quality. The research findings also contribute to our understanding of the impact of auditors’ legal liability exposures.

152512.label: Realisation of objectives
152512.value: 本研究計劃成果基本上達成並顧及了原定的五個目標： 1.本計劃通過研讀《十誦律》、《五分律》、《僧祇律》、《四分律》、《根有部律》等多部漢譯律典以及巴利語《律藏》，說明它們的來由、結構、流傳，檢出現存各種版本及原語本等；以及縷述中土僧人對律藏和律典的研究、律宗的成立及流布，並搜羅中、日、英、德、法等語文的二手研究和文本整埋。整合成以中土律學為中心，對戒律自印度至中土的傳承和演變的論述。(目標1、2) 2.中土律宗之祖道宣繼承眾律，總攬前輩律著、博採抉擇異說、自成體系，著「南山五大部」，其中《四分律刪繁補闕行事鈔》為集大成之作，論述僧團的運作和管治、守持的戒條和違犯的懺罪，以至衣食行止等行事規範等，儼成佛弟子的龜鏡，歷來為習律者所必讀。本計劃詳研這著作，檢索所引全部律著的出處，條分理析，辨明各律典律師的說法以及道宣的取捨，展示中土律學發展的大貌和成果。 (目標1-5) 3.道宣之前的律著差不多全散佚，唯其師智首的著作仍殘存，雖然智首疏釋不及道宣般簡潔和到位，但從中可見其兼收並蓄的律風以及對後人的影響。本計劃比對智首和道宣的作品，恢復智首在中土律學史上的應有地位。(目標1、2) 4. 義淨是道宣之後的另一重要律師和譯經家，他遊印修學，回國後以印度律制為標準，批評中土僧人的歪行和陋習，寫成《南海寄歸內法傳》，對中土律制是一大衝擊。本計劃詳細譯注了此書，指出中印律制實踐之不同。(目標1-3) 5.佛教律制中一些課題，例如結界、安居、藥食、犍椎、鉢頭等，雖然較瑣碎細微，但涉及僧眾的日常生活，違者犯戒，嚴重妨礙修行。本計劃以這些課題為主線，匯聚各律藏、律典、律師的相關說法和詮釋，提出己見，揭示佛教律制的複雜性，可供實地考察者作文獻上的參考和對照，互相補足。(目標2-5) 本計劃進行時遇到之困難及應對情況，主要有以下四方面： 1.漢譯律典卷秩浩繁，部份行文及用語晦澀難解，有時需跟巴利語、梵語或藏語本相對照，才得以理解，花費甚多時間，亦未能聘得通這幾種語文的助理協助。筆者雖粗通這些語文，但仍需借助辭典和二手資料，加以推敲，亦感到掌握古印藏語文的困難和自身之不足。 2.有關漢譯律典的檢視或考查律制課題或觀念，非通過電腦檢索或研究助理所能意識到，而全要由筆者第一手接觸篩選思索，難以假手於人，費時極多，這或許是人文科學研究不能逃避的工夫，以致未能處理更多課題。 3.中土佛教徒依《四分律》踐行，至今未輟；不過按律制，非出家人(包括筆者)連律藏都不應閱讀，僧尼也鮮言自家的生活，遑論評點戒律的漏洞或實踐上的困難。本來通過實地考察，如探訪寺院、訪問僧尼，應可更瞭解律制的細節以及收跟文獻互相印證之效，惜囿於原初計劃的擬定和佛教偏保守的傳統，未能實行。 4.本港有關各派系律典的巴梵藏語本，以至英日法德專業期刊等二手外文資料，委實不足夠，通過館際管道亦往往未能借到，令參考文獻未齊備，誠美中不足。

152512.label: Major findings and research outcome
152512.value: 本計劃主要有以下成果： 1.有關戒律研究的介紹，之前湯山明、Charles S. Prebish之大著僅介紹印度律制，筆者則以漢譯律藏和中土戒律學史主線，網羅基本文獻和研究用書，編纂成研究指南，為漢語學界首部。(成果8) 2.綜合漢譯藏譯和巴利語律藏，對《四分律‧藥犍度》作詳細注釋，儘量查考難解和偏僻的術語，展示律制藥食的大貌及細節，亦為漢語學界首部。(成果10) 3.漢語戒律論著已不多，有者或囿於佛教傳統，未詳述僧團運作，筆者以《四分律行事鈔》的基本材料，參考唐宋律師的疏釋，論介僧團的運作，成中土佛教律制的詳細導論。(成果7) 4.筆者在前輩學者的基礎上，白話譯注《南海寄歸內法傳》，屢發現前人的誤讀和錯解；並指出此書不少內容抄自律典，當中或更滲入義淨私意，而非如前人所以為全是印度律制的實錄。(成果9) 5. 就一些律制課題，如追溯結界的緣起和「自然」和「作法」兩類界的關係，指出中安居的安排在中土律師間惹起爭論，或出於對方便適應的容忍度大小有關。根據漢譯律典和中土律，考察犍稚和缽頭的製作、式樣、使用，以及考察律制中經常出現的「由旬、俱舍盧、弓、肘」等長度單位的意義，望能補律制研究的空白。(成果1-6)

152512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
152512.value: 基於本計劃的研究成果和心得，可循三方面再作探討： 1.繼續就律藏的其他部份進行跨語本的對比研究，令古印度僧團運作和僧人生活的面貌得以逐步釐清。 2.繼續就律制其他課題(例如自恣、懺罪、乞食、僧衣等)，作仔細探究。 3.建基於傳統律制的研究，可作佛教及其律制在今天的適應和調整，提供文獻和教學上的基礎。 按漢譯「根本說一切有部律」或是最早出的律藏之一，其梵語和藏譯本在國際學界備受注目，筆者已以「從漢譯『根本說一切有部律』看印度佛教僧團的組織和運作」為題，申請新一年研資局的資助。

152512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
152512.value: 戒律是佛教徒行為守則與僧團運作規範的統稱，為佛教教學重要的組成部份，相傳由佛親說、弟子記錄，編纂成律藏流傳，漢譯現存多個部派的傳本，在中土引發許多討論，以及促使律宗的成立。本計劃通過研讀和對照各種漢譯律藏和中土律師的著作，以及參照中外學者的研究，對律宗之祖道宣以及著名律師義淨的律著作釋述，並考究一些律制課題的細節，揭示中土佛教律制的大貌，並望有助對中國佛教作更立體的了解。

153112.label: Project Title(Chinese)
153112.value: 内部资源、外部资源与中国创业企业的创新：时间动态模型

153112.label: Project Objectives
153112.value: First, while both internal and network resources are critical for firm innovation, the relative importance of each has seldom been examined. This study will thus compare and contrast these two types of resources and evaluate their respective roles in firm innovation in a transition economy. Second, we will take a fine-grained approach to examine what types of internal resources and network resources may change their impacts on firm innovation over time. Specifically, we investigate a firm’s human capital, including its stock of talented scientists and the experience of its top management team, as well as a firm’s social capital, including its network positions such as degree centrality and brokerage position. This analysis will help us better understand the unique roles of each resource in firm innovation over time. Third, we will further delineate the theoretical boundaries of the above dynamic comparison between RBV and social network perspective by identifying some critical contingencies. We argue that firm ownership, regional development and technological dynamism will moderate the main effect between internal/network resources and firm innovation. Last, this study will contribute to the innovation literature by analyzing the unique innovation activities in China, compared with traditional studies of innovation in the Western world. Specifically, we will investigate about 200 firms in China to understand how the particularistic attributes of a transition economy will affect the role of firm resources in innovation over time.

153112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
153112.value: There exist two ways for firms to develop product innovation. One is to rely on internal resources, and the other is to take advantage of network resources. We argue that as the locus of innovation is shifting from firm-centric to network-centric, the roles of internal and network resources in innovation will also evolve. Specifically, we compare and contrast the dynamic impacts of internal resources and network resources in high tech start-ups in China. We argue that a firm’s internal resource attributes such as human capital (e.g., talented scientists and top management team experience), compared with network attributes such as social capital (e.g., firm centrality and brokerage position), will have more impact on the innovative output of a high tech start-up at an earlier stage rather than at a later stage, whereas a firm’s network attributes tend to exert more influence on firm innovation at a later stage. Further, these dynamic impacts are moderated by firm ownership, regional development, and technological dynamism in China. We will collect survey data from 300 high tech start-ups in China to test our hypotheses. This context is suitable because firms in China are facing increasing demand of product innovation and have embarked on the transition from original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to original design manufacturer (ODM) and original brand manufacturer (OBM). The findings of this study will inform researchers, practitioners, and policy makers on the relevant importance of different resources in product innovation. This study contributes to the academic literature by delineating the theoretical boundaries of both resource-based view (RBV) and network theory from a dynamic angle. 该研究旨在比较在中国创业型企业中内部资源与外部资源对其创新的动态影响。我们提出，与企业的外部资源相比，企业的内部资源如人力资源会对高科技创业企业初始阶段的创新起着更为重要的作用。相反，企业的外部资源如企业的网络特点会对其后期的企业创新起着更为重要的作用。并且，这些资源的动态影响作用会受到企业所有权属性、区域发展及技术不确定性的调节。我们将会从300多家中国高科技创业企业中收取数据。该研究有助于我们更好地界定资源理论与社会网络理论的理论边界。

153112.label: Realisation of objectives
153112.value: In this project we have endeavored to understand the relationships among internal resources, network resources, and innovation. In particular, we have approached this research question by 1) investigating the network ties in China and how the network ties may be differentiated into business ties, political ties, and media ties, and how these ties may distinctively affect a firm’s resource access in a transition economy like China. For example, in the paper on “the effects of business and political ties on exploratory innovation” we examined whether a firm’s business ties enhance a firm’s exploratory innovation, while a firm’s political ties hurt a firm’s exploratory innovation. Further, we develop an opportunity-motivation-ability perspective to argue that a firm’s innovation orientation and absorptive capacity jointly interact with business or political ties to maximize the value of resources for exploratory innovations. In another working paper titled “Illegitimacy recovery: The role of strategic networking” we develop a devaluation model of illegitimacy, and differentiate firms’ illegitimacy in both regulatory and social contexts. We argue that a firm’s different network ties (e.g., political and media ties) serve as an important communication platform for the illegitimate firm to communicate with different arbiters, and thus alter the ways that these arbiters react to them. Specifically, political ties help the illegitimate firm communicate with regulatory arbiters, while media ties help it communicate with social arbiters. 2) examining the market competition such as multimarket contact and resource dependence in the multiunit firms, and understanding how the two forces of competition and resources may affect a firm’s entry into a geographic market both respectively and jointly. In doing so, we understand how the resource dependence between firms complement or substitute the competition demands between firms. 3) exploring the role of repeated network ties on a firm’s breakthrough innovations. Specifically, we examine whether the partner repeatedness in a firm’s ego network or alliance portfolio may demonstrate an inverted U-shape relationship with the firm’s breakthrough innovations. We draw on the literature of interorganizational routines to argue for the main effect, and further we build on the recent theoretical development of interorganizational routines to propose that technological dynamism will make the inverted U-shaped relationship steeper. This paper was published at Journal of Management Studies in 2015. 4) Understanding how the asymmetric learning capabilities between firms may affect their resource and knowledge acquisition in alliances. We propose that a firm’s relative capability to learn partner-specific know-how holds the key to understand the learning race phenomenon and its performance consequences. Specifically, we argue that a firm with higher specific learning capability relative to its partner’s will be rewarded with superior stock performance. We also contend that equity alliance governance and market similarity between partners moderate this relationship in opposite directions. These findings are of great importance to understand how firms may acquire network resources in the interconnected world, and how their own resource advantages/disadvantages may be compared with those of their network partners in deciding their performance. This paper was published at Academy of Management Journal in 2015. Overall, these five papers out of this project have addressed the tensions among internal resources, network resources, and the contexts that may facilitate or constrain their roles for firm outcomes such as innovation and performance. Therefore, we have reached a much better understanding of the relationships described in the project, and have realized the objectives of this project as well.

Second, we will take a fine-grained approach to examine what types of internal resources and network resources may change their impacts on firm innovation over time. Specifically, we investigate a firm’s human capital, including its stock of talented scientists and the experience of its top management team, as well as a firm’s social capital, including its network positions such as degree centrality and brokerage position. This analysis will help us better understand the unique roles of each resource in firm innovation over time.

Third, we will further delineate the theoretical boundaries of the above dynamic comparison between RBV and social network perspective by identifying some critical contingencies. We argue that firm ownership, regional development and technological dynamism will moderate the main effect between internal/network resources and firm innovation.

Last, this study will contribute to the innovation literature by analyzing the unique innovation activities in China, compared with traditional studies of innovation in the Western world. Specifically, we will investigate about 200 firms in China to understand how the particularistic attributes of a transition economy will affect the role of firm resources in innovation over time.

153112.label: Major findings and research outcome
153112.value: In this project we have generated the following research findings: 1. In the paper entitled “managerial ties and exploratory innovation: an opportunity-motivation-ability perspective”, we draw on the opportunity-motivation-ability perspective and distinguishe the relationships of business and political ties to exploratory innovation as well as investigates the joint impact of innovation orientation and absorptive capacity on these relationships. The survey data analyses of 212 Chinese manufacturing firms finds that business ties have a positive relationship with exploratory innovation, and innovation orientation and absorptive capacity interactively strengthen this relationship. Yet the linkage between political ties and exploratory innovation is not significant, and it is negatively impacted by the interaction between innovation orientation and absorptive capacity. 2. In the paper entitled “Illegitimacy Recovery: The Role of Strategic Networking”, we show that both regulatory and normative illegitimacy damage firm market value. Further, political ties and media ties have divergent impacts on the performance effects of regulatory and normative illegitimacy because they help firms access to different arbiters holding competing logics. Our findings show that political ties weaken the negative effects of regulatory illegitimacy, and media ties weaken the negative effects of normative illegitimacy. However, political ties strengthen the negative effects of regulatory illegitimacy. 3. In the paper entitled “Resource dependence and multimarket contact” we provided an integrative framework for advancing our knowledge on geographic market entry, which often faces the simultaneous challenges of market dependence and multimarket competition. These findings support the concept that the RDT logic can be applied to firms’ geographic expansions, and this logic complements the MMC logic such that market dependence reduces the MMC logic predictions, while diversification amplifies them. 4. In the AMJ paper entitled “Asymmetric learning capabilities and stock market returns” We set out to examine asymmetric learning in alliances by conceptualizing and testing the performance effects of a partner SLCG in the strategic alliance context. Our results demonstrate that greater competitive learning capabilities yield positive performance benefits. 5. In the JMS paper entitled “Does Familiarity Foster Innovation? The Impact of Alliance Partner Repeatedness on Breakthrough Innovations” we suggest that the trade-off between the benefits and liabilities of interorganizational routines, arising from repeated interactions within a firm’s alliance portfolio, significantly influences the innovation outcome, particularly breakthrough innovations. A moderate level of alliance partner repeatedness appears to be optimal.

153112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
153112.value: To better understand the relationship among internal resources, network resources, and innovation, we may further examine the following research questions along the line of inquiry stated in this project: The relationship between internal resources and network resources. As we found in the AMJ paper, a firm’s network resource acquisition depends on the strength of its own learning capability as compared with other network members. There are many related questions. For example, in acquiring network resources, a firm is actually in the process of coopetition with its network partners. It needs to maximize the value creation with network partners. Meanwhile, it needs to be aware of the potential competition from its network partners. How to manage this coopetition and go beyond the learning race dilemma? A firm may devise a set of network governance to ensure the smooth process of coopetition. In addition, whether internal resources complement or substitute network resources? For resource-poor firms how to move to the resource-rich position in the interconnected world? What are the network strategies that can be employed by the firm? Regarding the interaction between internal resources and network resources, what are the facilitating environment, and what might be the constraining factors? Apart from the learning capabilities, what other internal resources or what other types of network resources may matter here? Although we differentiate network ties into media ties, political ties, and business ties, there are other types of interfirm relationships such as board interlocking ties, professional connections, inventors’ connections, etc. How do these different types of network ties may affect the resource acquisition of the focal firm? These research questions are fruitful research directions to extend research in this project.

153112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
153112.value: This project has examined the relationships among internal resources, network resources, and firm outcomes. In particular, we analyzed the internal learning capability of the focal firm and how varying learning capability of the firm may affect their resource acquisition with their network partners. We found that firms with higher learning capability is better prepared to reap more benefits in the market. We also differentiated network ties into media ties, repeated ties, political ties, and business ties, and examined their role in affecting the innovation outcomes of a firms. We found that a moderate level of repeated ties in a firm’s ego network will demonstrate an inverse U-shaped relationship with its breakthrough innovations. Business ties facilitates the generation of exploratory innovations, while political ties hurt the generation of exploratory innovations. Further, media ties and political tis may play distinct roles in recovering a firm’s illegality in a transition economy like China. Our project also found that market competition and a firm’s resource dependence are the two major drivers for a firm to enter into a new market. The competition logic and resource dependence logic complement and substitute each other in different contexts. Overall, our project provides a better understanding of the relationship among internal resources, network resources, and firm outcomes in an interconnected world.

153412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
153412.value: Urbanization and the social dislocations related to the transfer of land rights have been the major concerns among policy makers and academics. There is a growing literature on the conflicts around the peripheral expansion of cities in Africa and Latin America and the issues of spatial justice have always been, and remain at the core of urban debates in the social sciences theory. China is evidently not immune to this challenge. The intensity of the tension unleashed by the scramble for land is reinforced by the unique features of its development trajectory: decades of suppressed urbanization, massive influx of foreign capital, unequal distribution of fiscal resources between levels of government and pervasive corruption. The resistance of Chinese peasants against the loss of land has however alerted the central government and provoked its intervention in favour of the former. Yet, land-hungry local governments remain undeterred. The form of land grab may have changed, but not its intensity. The most recent attempt at land accumulation by local government is to "elevate the peasant into high rise apartment". Under this new institutional initiative, peasants who are willing to surrender their land contract will be relocated to a modernized apartment in a high rise building. Such vertical extension of residential space would then release more land for development. This spatial realignment could have significant implications for rural life. How do the peasants and local government renegotiate property rights over rural land? Does the new spatial alignment signal the end of traditional rural community in China? Will this new residential pattern undermine the moral cohesiveness of rural community and thus weaken the accountability of local administration? In other words, with its possible impact on the peasants’ economic and welfare entitlement and political efficacy, this change may herald a redefinition of rural citizenship. This research intends to evaluate the impact of this process. Three localities that have introduced this innovative policy are chosen for analysis: Beijing, Chongqing and Zibo in Shandong. The team will deploy a wide range of research tools including in-depth interviews, household survey and documentary analysis to conduct a comprehensive exploration of the issues. The findings should have a major impact on the theoretical debates on spatial justice, local democracy and property right and significant policy relevance related to the issues of social stability and political reform in contemporary China.

153412.label: Realisation of objectives
153412.value: We have successfully secured about 900 responses to our survey in the 3 designated locations: Chongqing, Dezhou and Nantong. The well thought-out questionnaire covers a wide range of issues concerning the peasant's perception of their entitlement to rural land, views towards community before and after the relocation and relationship with local administration. This is supplemented by 93 interviews with rural households, local cadres, officials at national level and experts. The extensive review of official documents, newspaper accounts and academic works published by Chinese and overseas scholars further enrich our analysis. Information gathered from all these efforts enable us to meet most of the objectives listed in the project document. Objective (1): We have a good understanding on the peasant's perception of their entitlement to land after relocation. For the affected peasants, they see the "apartment for land" option a fair deal for their surrender of entitlement to residential plot and allows in most cases, an opportunity for peasants to 'cash in" their entitlement. Nevertheless, the ambiguity over the property right of the new apartment and the contention over their entitlement to other collective assets still available in the original community remain. In most cases, local cadres remain evasive about their rights to transfer the property to outsiders. Although full certification of the occupants' legal right of the apartment is promised, only a minority actually get hold of these papers by the time of our research. Whether these apartments will remain as "petty property right houses" (with no full transfer right) only varies from case to case and there is no standard policy on this matter. Objective (2): the research also enhances our understanding of the dynamics of evolution of property rights. The contrast between Chongqing model and other two cases is particularly reviewing. They represent contrasting policy opportunities for village community, distinctive logic of central-local government collaboration and different patterns of capital inflow into local grassroots. All these variables shape the ultimate module of property rights in the relocated community. In short, the Chongqing model is endowed with maximal policy flexibility and a less rigid divide between rural and urban land transfer enable a much bigger room for local community to pursue and defend their own interest. A better deal for peasants in terms of entitlement to land use is promised. Objective (3): the findings uncover a very comprehensive picture on the impact on village community. Despite relocation or even dismantlement of the original village, peasants are still connected with the original community due to moral bonding and even more importantly, their self-perceived rights to continue to enjoy the return from the collective assets owned by them under the old setting. These factors continue to reinforce the community cohesion. It creates a new challenge for local governance, however. Who can represent their interest particularly if the old village is now gone, physically and politically? There are contrasting patterns in our 3 locations. For Chongqing, the relatively more bottom up process usually allows the retention of the original administrative framework and more freedom for peasant to stay put if they want, thus the challenge is mainly presented in the form of over-burden of village officials and are thus more manageable. The situation in Nantong and Dezhou is different. The more top-down relocation process entails more complete uprooting of villages and in most cases, the original communities are fully destroyed. The peasants concerned with their rights to collective assets accumulated in the past are thus frustrated with the lack of representation in these cases. This could easily convert into confrontation in the long run. Like most research projects, there are always some obstacles that could hinder the progress of the inquiry one way or other. For project like this which is primarily based on a rural survey, the demographic changes in the countryside is a concern. The massive outflow of young labor force leaves most rural households homes for elderly and children only. Different age groups obviously have contrasting attitude towards issues like income prospect, farming, attitude towards authority or hukuo, We have tried to reduce the bias in composition of respondents with longer working hours (so that we could wait for those who worked in nearby towns to return home) or more extensive review of secondary literature. The political development in Chongqing also adds further complication to our work. As the land bill system is Bo Xilai's pet project, the downfall of the Party boss has created a lot of uncertainty to this policy. Local officials, in particular, were ill at ease when the prospect or merit of the practice was raised in the interviews. It required a more careful wording in our questions and greater sensitivity in our conversation with them. Nevertheless, most Chinese villages are closed communities and there are many informal "feedback" and monitoring mechanisms for the authority to ascertain whether the visitors are harmless or dangerous. In most cases, we can convince them of our academic credential and innocence with our non-provocative approach in interviews and deliberate effort in "going local" after a day or two.

153412.label: Major findings and research outcome
153412.value: First, the "elevation" approach appears to be a "win-win" solution for every concerned parties. It echoes the national policy of construction of a new socialist countryside and addresses the various concerns in planning. For local governments, this approach allows new space for urban development and brings in new leverage for attracting capital. For peasants, this is a better deal than the conventional practice of land requisition--a form of state coercion with a longer level of compensation. In the short run, this is a political winner and helps defuse tension. Secondly, the social and political impact of the development should not be underestimated. Whereas the difficult adjustments to new residential pattern or lack of social support may just be "teething problems", the larger issue of handling of collective assets left behind and the consequent burden on village administration are key concerns. Failure to address these two issues could spark off new wave of discontent in the countryside and lead to new challenge to rural stability. Lastly, there are two major options of this "elevation" approach in relocating peasants. Chongqing represents a distinctive alternative to the dominant approach. It allows greater flexibility and room for local administration. In a way, peasants could benefit more as the original village administration could continue to play a role in local community and serve as their representative and intermediary. Yet, this model also accelerates the process of expansion of urban boundary and may further disrupt the urban-rural balance in the long run. These findings were presented in the two conferences in Taipei (2013) and Tianjin (2105) respectively. Three papers are under production at the moment. These papers are focused (1) co-production of space between peasant, capital and state, (2) community membership and entitlement of common wealth, and (3) logic and pattern of negotiation over relocation. (3) is already a fully written paper and is now under review of Journal of Rural Studies (status: revise and resubmit). In our second paper which is now under review by Sociological Review (Shehuixue Yanjiu), we further elaborate on the implications of the change in status from villagers to "residents" on public and private domains.

153412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
153412.value: There are two major areas that could be further explored: entitlement to collective assets after relocation and institutional adaptation to this challenge. The village may be gone and the peasant status could also be replaced by an urban permit, yet there is still one major issue remains unsolved: the substantial amount of asset accumulated by village collective, e.g. local enterprises, land, or cash, are still in the hand of former local cadres and every single member of this community still feel entitled to these resources despite their change in legal status or residential pattern. With the waning of moral binding force and the termination of legal status of local cadres as custodian of community interest after relocation, how could the peasants trust these personnel and how conflicts could be mitigated and resolved. Share-holding company or other forms of cooperative structure have been experimented in different locations. This is a key issue central to the stability and effective governance in rural China. We have secured a grant of 200,000 RMB yuan from the National Social Science Foundation (PRC) and the research team is also considering another GRF in the 2017-2018 round.

153412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
153412.value: At a glance, the latest attempt of "elevating the peasant"--compensating peasant for their loss land with an apartment in high-rise building is a shrewd political move. It helps maintain stability and addresses the macro planning concern, local government's developmental needs and the national imperative of growth. It is an audacious move and is spreading fast across China's countryside. It is so far so good. Yet there are a number of challenges ahead. The dismantling of traditional residential pattern also destroys the moral bonding of rural community upon which the local authority was established. The merger of numerous unrelated clusters into the new neighborhood further compounds the problem. However, it is the management of the collective assets that presents the biggest challenge. Despite the relocation, many peasants who are now living in a neighborhood still see themselves as members of the old community that owns these assets (land, enterprises or cash), and thus feel they are entitled to return from these possessions. However, with the original villages gone and the village cadres should not be their custodian of collective interests, who should manage these assets on their behalf? How could one hold these intermediaries accountable? These could be seed of new round of rural tension.

154312.label: Co - Investigator(s)

154312.label: Project Objectives
154312.value: Investigate the current state of triad-like organized crime in China; Test the applicability of the social capital model in describing the morphology of organized crime in China; Assess the effectiveness of current countermeasures against organized crime in China, especially the measures introduced by the 8th Amendment of the PRC Criminal Law; Propose new measures to combat organized crime in China by considering those adopted to fight organized crime elsewhere.

154312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
154312.value: The rapid development of a modern market economy in China has also engendered the rise of crime, especially crimes associated with acquisition of wealth and the exploitation of illicit markets. As China’s ‘globalized’ economy has grown in scale and complexity so has the sophistication of criminal groups, such that ‘mafia’ or triad-like groups have emerged that can exploit the masses, disrupt development and reduce the competitiveness of markets. In some circumstances such groups, unchecked, may even behave like local tyrants and ‘Sultanistic States’ that undermine the legitimacy of the state. The transformation of such crime groups to more resilient, complex, transnational and risk-aversive forms challenges the need for new approaches by police and courts as well as new ‘metrics’ to gauge change and the impact of countermeasures. Despite concern little is known about the prevalence, seriousness and characteristics of ‘organized’ criminal groups in mainland China. Although a number of studies have examined the role of organized criminal groups in Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan much less is known about the nature of organized crime in mainland China. We also argue even less is known about the effectiveness of current countermeasures including the new measures introduced by the 8th Amendment of the PRC Criminal Law in 2011, and what might be the main focus of reform in the criminal law and policing practice. The proposed study aims to investigate the morphology (structure) and mobility of organized criminal groups in China, and to assess the utility of current and proposed countermeasures. Interviews with police, judges, gang members, journalists and scholars combined with a review of cases, focused on the formation and structure of triad-like groups will enable us to test ideas about the nature and evolution of organized crime in China. Based on our review of the literature on organized crime we hypothesize that a theoretical approach that incorporates ideas about ‘social capital’ may be more useful than a ’structure-control’ or ‘social-network’ approach in describing organized groups in post-reform China. In the light of our review of theoretical approaches we shall also assess the adequacy of current laws, suppression strategies of the police, the role of national and international legal cooperation, and the utility of campaign-style tactics in fighting organized crime. We review these approaches to suppressing organized crime and compare them with many new measures (e.g. tainted wealth laws, pattern and association offences, victim protection, and coercive interviews) adopted elsewhere.

To examine and understand the working mechanism of preferential attachment in the later growth of SNSs: Under what conditions do members of homogenous groups begin to reach out to strangers? How do popular centers emerge? How much does the preferential attachment-driven couple contribute to rapid growth of SNSs?
