210412.label: Major findings and research outcome
210412.value: The research findings and outcomes from this project are summarized as follows: 1. Framework design of user-assisted cloud storage system. We described the system architecture of such a hybrid design, and discussed the challenges and opportunities in [J2]. 2. Investigation of incentive scheme. Observing that private Bittorrent is one of the most successful applications that can motive their users to contribute their resources to the community, we conducted a measurement and analysis study on private Bittorrent communities in [J1]. In [C3], we proposed a novel incentive mechanism, Truth-DR, which leverages a reverse auction to provide monetary remuneration to tenants according to their agreed energy reduction. 3. Mechanism design for resource pooling from contributing users. In [C2], we modeled the resource pooling market as an online procurement auction market, and converted the online procurement auction design problem into an online algorithm design problem. Our auction scheme is proved to be turthful and can guarantee a competitive ratio against optimal offline algorithms. We also applied the online procurement auction technqiue to smart grid market that can maximize the social welfare with competitive ratio of 2 [C4]. 4. Dynamic pricing scheme for storage retail markets. In [C6], we applied core-selecting auction design to solve the pricing problem in a cloud market of virtual machines. In [C9], we design an efficient auction mechanism for the dynamic provisioning and pricing of Network Function Virtualization service chains in a datacenter. In [J6], we formualted the profit optimization problem in user-assisted cloud storage system as a stochastic dynamic programming problem. We developed a heuristic dynamic pricing algorithm together with resource allocation scheme which can automatically adjust the price to adapt to the demand-supply relationship. 5. Efficient coding schemes for data reliability. In [C5], we designed and implemented a parallel CRS coding scheme for GPUs, and acheived 10x speedup on GPU over a quad-core CPU. In order to achieve high coding throughput, we investigated and benchmarked GPU memory hierarchy in [C7, J4]. In [C8, J3], we designed and implemented a reliable in-memory cache for big key-value stores that uses coding technques to supports up to two node failures, while still achieve high throughput and low latency. 6. Reducing power consumption. In [C1], we conducted a comprehensive measurement study of GPU DVFS on energy conservation. We studied 37 benchmark applications and illustrated that GPU DVFS is an effective approach in saving system energy and reducing the eletricity bills of service providers.

210412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
210412.value: This project focused on the architecture design, incentive design, and pricing design of a hybrid user-assisted cloud storage system. We can extend this work from the following aspects: 1. Data privacy and security. Although our current project designed an incentive scheme to encourage users to contribute their storage space to the service provider, the cloud users may be hestiate to store their data on other users' computers. It is imperative to design security schemes to protect the data confidentiality and integrity. 2. Metadata management. Once the service provider store customers' data on the procured storage pool, how to efficiently manage user data and the storage pool becomes a challenging problem. How to make a balance between data redundancy and data availability will be an interesting reserach topic.

210412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
210412.value: Nowadays, people and enterprises get accustomed to backing up their valuable data in the cloud due to its high reliability and availability. Such a wonderful service doesn’t come for free. In order to guarantee high data reliability and availability, service providers make tremendous investment in hardware equipment and Internet bandwidth. This is why we can buy a brand new 1TB hard disk with less than HK$400, but we have to pay more than HK$900 per year to get 1TB storage space from Dropbox. This project aims to reduce the cost of providing reliable cloud storage service. We propose a user-assisted cloud storage system that makes use of the free disk spaces and Internet bandwidth from cloud users as an added asset to augment the data centre resources. Our system uses erasure coding technique that can achieve high reliability and availability with low storage overhead. The calculations of erasure coding are offloaded to GPUs. In order to encourage users to contribute their free resources, we further leverage economical tools and develop an auction-based scheme that incentivizes cloud users to sell their local resources to service provider. We further develop a dynamic pricing scheme for service providers to maximize the profit.

210612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
210612.value: 適地性服務目前已成為移動計算中關鍵的服務內容。在這些服務中，越來越有必驗證用戶的位置，以防範位置欺騙。例如，某些網路上的商用或公眾服務（例如博彩、在線視頻和緊急服務）需要驗證用戶的地理位置。為此我們提出了“時空證言”的概念，即移動用戶針對服務提供商提出的時空斷言，例如“用戶在某時是在某地”，提供自己的證明依據。時空證言在金融、法律等領域也有廣泛的用途。時空證言問題的主要難點在於提供證明的同時保護用戶合理的位置隱私。例如要證明用戶並未離港，並不需要用戶提供其具體的位置信息。現有的研究成果，無論是軟件（例如基於RSA或DSA的數字簽名）或是硬件的，都無法達到這個目標。本項目對時空證言中的隱私保護課題進行研究。研究的主要理論依據是，時空證言與數字簽名保護信息內容完全不被篡改相比要求的只是一個粗略的驗證，因此設計一種私有的類似簽名的機制去保護明文信息不被洩露是可行的。本項目研究面臨的主要挑戰，一是如何在密碼學範疇內設計一種保護隱私的加密驗證結構，二是如何在應用領域內為移動計算平台設計出高效的驗證機制。我們希望這一研究能為學術界，移動通訊業界和香港社會帶來啟示和貢獻。

210612.label: Realisation of objectives
210612.value: After 42 months of research endeavors, we proudly report that all objectives set out in the original proposal have been well addressed. As for the detailed progress, we have fully solve objectives 1 and 2 by the end of year 2014, and accomplished objective 3 by the end of year 2015. Mobile friendly indexes (objective 4) has been resolved in early 2016. For objective 1, our outcome is the formal problem definition of spatio-temporal attestation with private signature. In particular, we resolved the challenging problem of the proper definition of the security model against untrusted third party, based on standard cryptography terminologies (i.e., semantic security and indistinguishability). This lays solid theoretical foundation for the subsequent tasks. As for objective 2, we solved the spatio-temporal attestation problem for window predicates on geo-spatial datasets for location-based services. The solution consists of a compete set of cryptography building blocks, authenticating data structures and network protocols. The most challenging task is the design of a private signature scheme that can authenticate arbitrary size of window predicates while still keeping the user location anonymous. We have managed to adopt some homomorphic encryption techniques to solve this problem. The paper has been revised for publication in Proc. of the VLDB Endowment 2014 (PVLDB '14). As for objective 3, we completed the following studies. First, we solved the spatio-temporal attestation problem for skyline queries. The solution consists of a compete set of cryptography building blocks, authenticating data structures and network protocols. The most challenging task is the design of attestation data structure that can strike a balance between offline signing cost and the online attesting cost. This leads to some alternative schemes for static and dynamic datasets, respectively. We have published the results in IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE). Second, we worked on the "kNN and top-k query attestation for multidimensional spatial datasets". This problem is more challenging than attesting skyline queries as it involves privacy-preserving comparison of two secret values, rather than comparing one secret value with a public value. Some homomorphic encryption techniques are applied to address the intensive computation needs in this problem. The results have been published in Proc. of the VLDB Endowment 2014 (PVLDB '14). Third, we also worked on a highly relevant problem, namely, the secure retrieval of a matching value for a given key from a spatio-temporal database. We have adopted conditional oblivious transfer, homomorphic encryption, and commutative encryption to tackle this problem. The results haev been published in IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering 2014 (ICDE '14). Fourth, we studied the authentication problem in a distributed setting where an untrusted server integrates data from different sources. We have applied secret sharing and homomorphic encryption to allow the server to authenticate the correctness of a variety of complex query types to clients. The results have been published ACM SIGMOD Conference on Management of Data 2015 (SIGMOD'15). As for objective 4, we have designed a mobile-friendly MAC scheme (PMAC) together with two efficient spatial indexes to enable smartphone users to authenticate their location-based predicates without disclosing the genuine location. The results have been accepted to publish in IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing (TMC) under the title "Assuring Spatio-Temporal Integrity on Mobile Devices with Minimum Location Disclosure".

210612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
210612.value: As for further development, we plan to further build and enhance our prototype system, particular that of the last task, for demonstration and knowledge transfer. We believe that the promotion of this prototype system will further make an impact on both research and industry community regarding our privacy-preserving spatio-temporal attestation for location-based services.

210612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
210612.value: Location-based services (LBS) have become increasingly popular in recent years, thanks to the boom in mobile social networking services and the intensive penetration of smartphones and tablet computers. In LBS, there has been a growing necessity against location cheating and for location trustworthiness. For example, some online businesses or public services (such as casinos, copyrighted video-streaming services, and the emergency services) need to verify the user’s geographic location before authorizing his/her access. In this project, we have formalized these applications to a new LBS service called “spatio-temporal attestation”, where a mobile user testifies or attests to a service provider the genuineness of his/her input location against some spatio-temporal predicate, such as “being in a specific region during a time period”. Spatio-temporal attestation has great potential in finance, jurisdiction, and law enforcement situations, for uses such as preventing unauthorized credit card transactions, and ensuring compliance with a home-custody order. With our comprehensive solutions, we expect they can be adopted by not only the research community, but also by the mobile industry (particularly the LBS service providers), and end users in Hong Kong.

211212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
211212.value: 一种推演疾病扩散网络的计算方法及其在传染性疾病监测中的应用研究

211212.label: Project Objectives
211212.value: To design and develop a computational method that can automatically infer the underlying diffusion network of an infectious disease by incorporating (1) surveillance data, i.e., the temporal-spatial distributions of cases of infection, and (2) infection/propagation models of the disease; To conduct empirical validations of the proposed method as well as its application to real-world case studies by implementing a prototype and testing it in modeling disease transmission patterns based on available surveillance datasets.
rows: To design and develop a computational method that can automatically infer the underlying diffusion network of an infectious disease by incorporating (1) surveillance data, i.e., the temporal-spatial distributions of cases of infection, and (2) infection/propagation models of the disease;

To conduct empirical validations of the proposed method as well as its application to real-world case studies by implementing a prototype and testing it in modeling disease transmission patterns based on available surveillance datasets.

211212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
211212.value: The aim of this project is to develop and empirically evaluate a computational method that allows for inferring and predicting transmission patterns in outbreaks of emerging infectious diseases (e.g., H5N1 and SARS) as well as in resurgence of endemic diseases (e.g., malaria) in populations. The spread of infectious diseases can be caused and affected by multiple (or even hidden) factors, which makes accurate prediction of when and where outbreaks may emerge difficult. At the moment, temporal-spatial scan statistics-based clustering techniques have been applied to the analysis and characterization of temporal-spatial patterns of infectious diseases. However, the existing clustering-based surveillance software systems do not infer the underlying diffusion patterns (modeled as networks) of infectious diseases, which can be informative and perceptive as they characterize how diseases are diffused or transmitted from one location to another over time. By integrating both temporal-spatial clusters of cases of infection and temporal-spatial diffusion networks of diseases, existing regional or national surveillance systems can further enhance their functional capacities of predicting/analyzing the impact of disease transmissions and their underlying factors, which can benefit healthcare providers, government infectious disease control and prevention organizations (e.g., Hong Kong Department of Health - Centre for Health Protection (CHP)), as well as international agencies (e.g., World Health Organization (WHO)). Technically, the problem of computationally inferring diffusion networks of infectious diseases is both interesting and challenging because, during the process of disease spread, the interrelationships between reported infection cases are not observed directly; what we have is only raw surveillance data on temporal-spatial distributions of infection cases. Moreover, we need to incorporate different disease propagation models, because different infectious diseases can have different infectious spread mechanisms. In this project, we will develop and demonstrate a computational method to automatically infer the underlying diffusion network of an infectious disease that incorporates (1) surveillance data, i.e., the temporal-spatial distributions of cases of infection, and (2) infection/propagation models of the disease. In addition, we will conduct empirical validations of the proposed method as well as its application to real-world case studies by implementing a prototype and testing it in modeling disease transmission patterns based on available surveillance datasets (e.g., in the practical cases of malaria and respiratory disease surveillance). 本项目研究一种自动的监测机制用以发现传染性疾病疫情爆发之前或期间的传播模式，且该机制适用于新出现的传染性疾病（例如，禽流感和非典型肺炎）和复发的流行性疾病（例如，疟疾和肺结核）。此监测机制对于公共卫生机构预测疾病传播分析潜在影响因素以及评估当前控制策略并提出新的控制手段而言非常必要。传染性疾病的传播受到多种因素（含隐性因素）诱发和影响，因此，准确的预测疾病暴发的时间和地点及其困难。在现阶段，基于时间空间扫描的统计聚类技术已应用于分析和刻画传染性疾病的时空模式。这些基于聚类的监测软件系统在刻画传染性疾病在一段时间内从一地扩散或传播到另外一地时具有很强的信息性和感知性，但是尚不能用以推演疾病的扩散模式（文中模拟为网络形式）。通过整合感染病例的时空聚类和疾病扩散的时空网络，可以增强现有地区和国家层面的监测系统在分析和预测疾病传播和潜在影响因子的能力，从而实现医务人员，国家传染性疾病预防控制机构（例如，香港卫生署卫生防护中心），以及国际相关机构（例如，世界卫生组织）的多方受益。从技术角度而言，计算推演传染性疾病的传播网络是一个既有趣又充满挑战的问题。首先，在疾病蔓延过程中，报告的感染者之间相互关系不能够直接获得，而可获得的是感染病例在时空分布的原始监测数据。其次，由于不同疾病的传播机制各不相同，我们需要整合各种疾病的传播模型。在本项目中，我们将研究并演示一种用以自动推演某种特定传染性疾病扩散网络的计算方法，该方法融合了（1）流行病学监测数据，例如，感染病例的时空分布；（2）疾病的感染传播模型。除此之外，我们将会通过在现有的监测数据基础之上（例如，对疟疾和呼吸性疾病的感染监测）建立一个实验原型并对其展开模拟疾病传播模式测试，在此基础之上对所提出方法进行实证研究和其在现实案例中的应用研究。

211212.label: Realisation of objectives
211212.value: The objectives of (1) developing computational methods for inferring the underlying diffusion networks of infectious diseases and (2) empirically validating the proposed methods and applications to real-world case studies have been successfully realized, while systematically solving the following specific research problems in this project: First of all, we addressed the problem of how disease diffusion may be affected by multiple real-world factors. For instance, in the case of malaria diffusion, the factors can involve the length of P. vivax incubation period, the impact of malaria control at different locations, and the total number of imported cases. In solving this problem, we proposed a novel spatial transmission model, which incorporates the representations of both the heterogeneous transmission potential of P. vivax at individual locations and the mobility of infected populations among different locations. Based on the proposed transmission model, we further formulated a recurrent neural network-based machine learning model to infer the transmission networks based on surveillance data (refer to journal publication [1]). As often encountered in the real world, available observations, e.g., reported cases, are often very limited, and in addition, the underlying transmission mechanisms could be spatiotemporally varying due to the different degrees of risk factors. In order to address this real-world challenge, we put forward a model-based approach. We used the observed geographic spread and the number of confirmed cases of novel influenza A(H7N9) virus infections in eastern China as an example, and developed a computational diffusion model to spatiotemporally characterize and predict the potential impacts of bird migration and poultry distribution on the geographic spread of H7N9 infection. To achieve this, we first developed a method for estimating the likelihood of bird migration based on available environmental and meteorological data. Then, we adopted a computational mobility model to estimate poultry distribution based on annual poultry production and consumption of each province/municipality. Finally, the spatiotemporal risk maps were created based on the integrated impacts of both bird migration and poultry distribution. In this demonstrated approach, the limited observation data was primarily used for parameter estimation and validations of model-based predictions (refer to journal publication [2]). As disease transmission may be effectively characterized by using contact matrices between each pair of different host populations as well as between host populations and pathogens, the most challenging issue lies in that such contact matrices can change over time in the course of disease transmission, e.g., due to changes in physiological properties of the pathogens or due to behavioral changes in host populations (reduced social contacts). To address this issue, we formulated and solved the problem of how to characterize and measure dynamic social contact during an epidemic. We proposed an epidemic-model-based tensor deconvolution framework in which the spatiotemporal patterns of social contact were represented by the factors of the tensors. These factors can be discovered using a tensor deconvolution procedure with the integration of epidemic models based on rich types of data, e.g., mainly heterogeneous outbreak surveillance data, socio-demographic census data, and physiological data from medical reports (refer to journal publication [3]). In our project, we further tackled the problem of how human behaviors (e.g., individuals’ decisions on whether or not to take vaccine) may affect the dynamics of disease spread (that is in turn characterized in terms of diffusion networks) and hence the effectiveness of disease control. Such decisions can be subjected to individuals’ awareness about disease and vaccine, such as their perceived disease severity and vaccine safety. We took into consideration the case of individuals’ vaccination behavior by modeling the spread of awareness in a group of socially connected individuals and examining the associated impacts on their vaccination decision-making (refer to journal publication [4]). Next, we addressed the issue of how to infer a diffusion network based on the spatiotemporal patterns of reported infection cases, which would characterize how the parasite transmits from one township to another. In doing so, we attempted to model the diffusion of epidemics that can be affected by not only the intra-regional factors but also inter-regional and external ones. To tackle this issue, we formulated and studied a unified framework based on Poisson regression for the task of predictions with the three types of factors incorporated. To learn the structure of the diffusion network (or diffusion matrix), we proposed two approaches – utilizing some a priori knowledge (e.g., transportation network) and estimating it from scratch via a sparse structure assumption (refer to journal publication [5]). Finally, in order to further describe the specific geographic variations of an infectious disease that often characterize the spatial differentiation of disease incidences as caused by various both direct and indirect impact factors, such as environmental, demographic, biophysical, and socioeconomic factors, we proposed and evaluated a space-time model that resembles a P. vivax transmission model and a hidden time-dependent process by taking into consideration both explicit and implicit factors. To quantitatively assess the impact of heterogeneous factors on geographic variations of P. vivax infections, we developed a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulation method to estimate the model parameters by fitting the space-time model to the reported spatial-temporal disease incidences (refer to journal publication [6]).

211212.label: Major findings and research outcome
211212.value: This project has made important contributions to both Computer Science (Data Analytics/Machine Learning) and Epidemiology (Infectious Disease Control) fields. Our obtained research results have been well recognized by the peers, and published in the top-quality journals, in the respective disciplines, e.g., TPAMI, TKDE, PNTD and J. Royal Society Interface (as well as top-tier peer-reviewed international conferences, e.g., AAAI). Specifically, we developed and tested a spatial transmission model that took into account both the heterogeneous transmission potential of P. vivax malaria at individual geographic locations and the mobility of infected populations among different locations. Based on the transmission model and a RNN-based learning method, we were able to infer a diffusion network for the P. vivax transmission among 62 towns in Yunnan province, China [1]. We showed the effectiveness of a proposed model-based method for modeling and inferring the spatiotemporal diffusion risk maps based on limited available observations, e.g., reported cases [2]. We implemented and validated a novel epidemic-model-based tensor deconvolution method in which the spatiotemporal patterns of social contact were represented by the factors of the tensors. The epidemic-model-based tensor deconvolution method can effectively infer the dynamic structure of social contacts exhibiting patterns that can be varying both spatially and temporally, by integrating multiple empirically available data sources. By using four specific diseases (H1N1, mumps, seasonal flu, and varicella) as case studies, the efficacy and two important applications of the proposed framework were validated [3]. We provided a novel method for modeling and characterizing the effects of human behaviors (e.g., individuals’ decisions on whether or not to take vaccine) on disease diffusion and therefore the effectiveness of disease control. We demonstrated this method by focusing on the case of individuals’ vaccination behavior as influenced by the spread of awareness in a group of socially connected individuals [4]. We proposed and validated a unified framework based on Poisson regression for the task of predictions, which considered not only the intra-regional factors but also inter-regional and external ones. Empirical evaluations were conducted based on a real dataset that recorded the 16-days-reported cases in Yunnan province, China, for seven years from 2005 to 2011 [5]. We implemented and tested a space-time method for characterizing geographic variations of an infectious disease by considering various direct/indirect impact factors. Since there was no ground-truth information available, the performance of the MCMC method was first evaluated against a synthetic dataset. The results showed that the model parameters could be well estimated using the proposed MCMC method. Next, the proposed model was applied to investigate the geographic variations of P. vivax incidences among all 18 towns in Tengchong, Yunnan province, China. Based on the geographic variations, the 18 towns could be further classified into five groups with similar socioeconomic causality for P. vivax incidences [6].

211212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
211212.value: There are several further developments that we have planned to pursue based on the methods we have proposed and demonstrated here, most of which have been well received, as well as in view of the remaining challenges that we are facing in the real-world disease surveillance and control. For instance, we would like to further develop and demonstrate a general computational method for building efficient, active surveillance systems, which are capable of addressing the issue of limited resources. Such systems will need to compute and identify the most pivotal (sentinel) locations to monitor, so as to gain a comprehensive estimate of the overall situation under resource-constrained conditions. One of the possible ways we can explore based on our current modeling experience is to first develop a method for modeling and inferring a sentinel network (one that only contains limited sentinel/key nodes) from historical diffusion observations.

211212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
211212.value: This project systematically addressed the problem of how to computationally predict when and where an infectious disease may spread in a community. This problem is both computationally challenging and practically meaningful. Computationally speaking, we need to develop the right model for the right problem in the right context. As we know, in some cases disease infections may occur mostly within isolated local regions, whereas in others they may be widely transmitted due to human inter-region, or even cross-county, movements. In view of this, here we provided a unified Poisson regression method for making more comprehensive and accurate infection case predictions. Speaking of local infections, situations could become more complicated if we are to further tackle possible variations among the geographic locations, in terms of impact factors, e.g., their different environmental, demographic, and socioeconomic factors. To consider such a geographic heterogeneity, we developed a space-time model to characterize their varying degrees of impacts on disease diffusion. To make the matters even more complex, it should further be noted that disease diffusion networks could also be subjected to human behavioral changes, e.g., due to perceived disease severity. In view of such a real-world challenge, we developed an epidemic-model-based tensor deconvolution method and a belief-based model of socially-induced human decision-making during an epidemic.

211212.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
211212.value: As a result of the collaborations from this project, the PI and the Co-I (JL and XZ) established the HKBU-China CDC Joint Research Laboratory for Intelligent Disease Surveillance and Control, as a formal collaborative research platform between the Computer Science Department at HKBU and the National Institute of Parasitic Diseases (NIPD) at the China CDC. Together, they have tackled the problem of how to perform risk factor-based active surveillance in malaria outbreak monitoring. Their initiative took on the challenges in the epidemiological surveillance of malaria outbreaks in Tengchong, a high-endemic region in Yunnan. The problem is extremely challenging in that Tengchong is a border county consisting of 221 villages, with 658,207 residents widely distributed across a large, mountainous area of 5,845 square kilometers. Thus far, promising results have been obtained by their joint research team in this regard, e.g., the computational ranking algorithm they deployed and presented at the top-tier publication venues in the fields of both Computer Science and Infectious Disease Epidemiology.

211412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
211412.value: Organic electronics materials are finding broad applications in the state-of-the-art optoelectronic devices. Examples are mini-displays in digital cameras, cell phones, flexible displays, ultra-thin and high contrast TV, and more recently as tablet PC. For applications in displays and in photovoltaic, controlling the motions of charge carriers, i.e. electrons and holes, within the device is essential. Balancing electron and hole currents avoids the accumulation of space charges and is beneficial to the operations of both organic light-emitting diodes and organic photovoltaic (OPV) cells. However, for the study of charge transport of organic photonic materials, it is necessary to delineate the separate contribution of each kind of carrier in the overall current flow. This proposal outlines schemes of tuning the charge injection into organic photonic materials via a charge blocking or trapping layer. In this way, truly unipolar devices can be constructed for reliable measurements of carrier transport parameters. The outcome of this proposal should lead to better understanding of charge transport in organic photonic materials. Finally, we point out how carrier transport parameters can be correlated to device performance in an OPV cell. 有機電子材料已被廣泛應用於先進的光電設備中。例如數碼相機的迷你顯示、柔性顯示器、超薄電視、高對比平板顯示。在應用於顯示和光伏器件中、控制電荷載體的運動（即電子和空穴）至關重要。平衡電子和空穴電流可避免空間電荷積累，有利於有機發光二極體和有機光伏 (OPV) 器件的操作。然而，研究有機光子材料的電荷傳輸，有必要去界定每種載體的單獨貢獻。這項建議概述了利用阻塞或陷印介面層去調控單極載子的傳輸。通過這種介面層，可以為單極載體的傳輸提供可靠的測量。這項建議的結果應導致有機光電材料的電荷傳輸更好地理解。最後，我們指出如何結合電荷傳輸的數據和OPV 器件的性能。

211412.label: Major findings and research outcome
211412.value: 1. A comprehensive characterization of the hole transport parameters of 6 common semiconducting polymers and their selected BHJs using admittance spectroscopy. Poor signals with negative capacitances, arising from undesirable electron leakages, are obtained for the BHJ blends. The problem of electron leakage was circumvented by inserting an electron blocking and trapping (EBT) layer under the cathode. As a result, hole transport properties of BHJ blends can be obtained. Temperature dependent experiments were carried out. OPV performances of BHJ blends are also measured in this contribution. The correlation between device performance and energetic disorder of the BHJ were evaluated. [Ref. 1: J. Polym. Sci., Pt B: Polym. Phys., 51, 649–658 (2013) 2. A detailed investigation on the impact of molecular weight distribution of a photoactive polymer (PCDTBT) on photovoltaic devices performance and carrier transport properties. We found that different batches of as-received polymers have substantial differences in their molecular weight distribution. Photovoltaic devices fabricated with low molecular weight component have reduced power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) from 5.7% to 2.5%. The corresponding charge carrier mobility at the short-circuit region has also been significantly reduced from 2.7 x 10-5 to 1.6 x 10-8 cm2V-1s-1. The carrier transport properties of the polymers at various temperatures were further analyzed. All polymers have similar energetic disorders. However, they appear to have significant differences in carrier hopping distances. [Ref. 2: Adv. Energy Mater. 4, 1400768 (2014)] 3. We investigated the solvent additive effect on both hole and electron transport in the state of the art polymer:fullerene system, namely PTB7:PC71BM, by admittance spectroscopy. For a polymer:fullerene weight ratio of 1:1.5, the electron mobility in the blend film increases by two orders of magnitude with the DIO concentration while almost no change is found in the hole mobility. For lower DIO concentrations, the electron mobility is suppressd because of large, but poorly connected PC71BM domains. For higher concentrations of DIO, the electron mobility is improved progressively and the hole mobility becomes the limiting factor. Between 1.5 - 4 vol%, the electron and hole mobilities are balanced. DIO concentration modifies fundamentally the average hopping distances of electrons. [Ref. 3: Adv. Mater. Interfaces 2, 1500166 (2015)]

211412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
211412.value: The EBT layer design generated in this project is quite general. It should be applicable to other PV material systems including perovskite-based solar cells. More explorations should be conducted in future.

211412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
211412.value: A solar cell consists of a light-absorbing material sandwiched between two charge extracting electrodes. Charges of opposite signs are expected to be collected at these two electrodes. For the development of solar cells, it is important to separately identify the drift motion of one kind of carriers at one time. Thus, means to shut off one kind of charge carriers is essential for a fundamental understanding of developing solar cell materials. This project has successfully developed an electron-blocking-trapping (EBT) interfacial layer for analyzing the hole electrical conduction in photovoltaic polymers used in solar cells. The applications of this EBT layers to different polymer-based solar cell materials were demonstrated. Our results indicate hole conduction is the bottle-neck for common polymer-based solar cells systems (Ref. 3).

211512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
211512.value: 随着智能手机的日益普及和社交网络应用的不断深入，两者的结合已经开启了一个全新的应用领域，即移动社交网络。位置邻近服务是移动社交网络中的一项重要服务。当用户的朋友出现在附近的时候，它可以及时地提醒用户，以增强社交活动如合作工作及信息分享等。为了实现位置邻近服务，现有的系统需要不断搜集用户的位置信息进行邻近性计算。然而，曝露私人位置信息给服务提供者会带来严重的隐私泄密问题。比如，假设攻击者知道某用户在一个专科诊所停留了很长时间，他就可以推断该用户可能是某特定疾病的患者。因此，本项目将致力于开发既能保护用户位置隐私又能准确提供位置邻近服务的新技术和新方法。我们首先会详细分析位置邻近服务所需要的隐私保护要求。基于这些要求，我们将针对不同的位置邻近服务提出一系列新的面向隐私保护的查询处理和位置更新技术，包括基于距离的位置邻近服务、基于区域的位置邻近服务、以及K近邻服务。我们还将开发一个原形系统以验证所提技术方法的可行性、有效性和安全性。2011年8月的一项调查显示智能手机在香港的渗透率已经达到35%，在全球及亞太地區均排名前列。我们希望本项目的研究可以为本地移动用户提供更好更安全的服务。

211512.label: Realisation of objectives
211512.value: The project objectives have been successfully realized. We have identified mutual privacy requirements for typical mobile geo-proximity services in location-based social networks. That is, no location information of any user should be disclosed to the service provider; and a user cannot reveal his/her exact location to friends unless the friends are nearby. Based on these privacy requirements, we have developed new location access and update solutions for distance-based proximity detection and vicinity region-based proximity detection [Journal/1, Journal/4, Conference/1]. A secure query processing framework based on private information retrieval (PIR) techniques has been proposed for reverse nearest neighbor queries [Conference/5]. We have also explored privacy-aware index-based query techniques [Journal/2, Conference/3] and geo-social proximity query techniques [Journal/3, Conference/4]. In all the above studies, experiments based on real/synthetic datasets have been conducted to validate the proposed algorithms and methods. In addition, a demonstration system has been developed to showcase the proposed techniques.

211512.label: Major findings and research outcome
211512.value: To address the privacy issue in location-based social networks, we have identified the mutual privacy requirements for typical geo-proximity services: (i) the service provider should not be allowed to access any user’s location information and (ii) a user should not be allowed to access any friend’s location information unless the friend is nearby [Journal/1, Journal/4, Conference/1]. Based on these privacy requirements, we have developed a new quantitative solution for distance-based proximity detection [Journal/1]. We adopted the grid-and-hashing paradigm and proposed an optimal multi-level grid overlay scheme to increase the detection accuracy while saving the wireless bandwidth. We have also devised the client-side location update scheme and the server-side update handling procedure for continuous proximity detection. Simulation results show that our approach is efﬁcient and scalable under various system parameters and user moving speeds. For vicinity region-based proximity detection, each user can specify a nearby area as his/her vicinity region, and two users are considered to be in proximity only if they are located in each other’s vicinity region. To enable efficient detection, we have designed a shift-and-compare protocol for one-shot proximity queries without revealing users’ locations or vicinity regions [Conference/1]. Furthermore, for continuous proximity monitoring, we have proposed an alert-area-based location update strategy with minimal update frequency, thereby saving communication cost. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed privacy-preserving techniques achieve high efficiency in terms of both computation and communication costs. We have also integrated database indexing techniques with cryptographical tools for private search on key-value pairs (such as WiFi SSID/password pairs) [Conference/3]. We developed an oblivious index traversal framework, in which the server cannot trace the index traversal path of a query during evaluation. The framework is generic and can support a wide range of query types with a suitable homomorphic encryption algorithm in place. To better protect location privacy, we have further investigated privacy-aware secure query techniques. We have proposed privacy-preserving query authentication techniques for location-based top-k queries [Journal/3]. A demonstration system VERDICT [Conference/2] has been developed to showcase the proposed techniques that support the verification of query results while securing the location privacy. In addition, a secure query processing framework based on private information retrieval (PIR) techniques has been investigated for bichromatic reverse nearest neighbor queries [Conference/5]. The framework achieves strong privacy wherein the service provider learns nothing about the query location.

211512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
211512.value: As for further development, we plan to extend the proposed privacy-preserving query techniques in three directions. First, we are going to study more advanced mobile spatial queries. We plan to design a comprehensive set of secure protocols for various spatial query semantics. In particular, with the secure distance-comparison protocol developed in our prior work, we will further study other distance-based queries such as k-nearest-friend queries and spatial top-k join queries. Second, we will investigate the query integrity issue to safeguard the soundness and completeness of geo-social query results while preserving user location privacy in cloud-based outsourcing environments. Third, we plan to investigate the privacy issue in spatial crowdsourcing that aims to support data aggregations without revealing sensitive personal information.

211512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
211512.value: Geo-proximity service is a basic service to find nearby mobile users in location-based social networks. To realize such services, existing systems collect location information from all users for proximity computation. However, the disclosure of private location information to the service provider raises severe privacy concerns. For example, by knowing that a user is in a specialized clinic, an adversary may infer that the user is a disease sufferer. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop more sophisticated location update and query techniques that can support these geo-proximity services while preserving the location privacy of mobile users. In this project, we have first identified mutual privacy requirements for typical geo-proximity services such as distance-based proximity queries and nearest-friend queries. We require the location privacy of mobile users to be completely protected against the service provider, as well as among themselves, except when they are in proximity. Based on these privacy requirements, we have developed a series of new privacy-preserving solutions for geo-proximity query and monitoring services. We believe that the research findings will benefit the continuous development of location-based social networks.

211612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
211612.value: Biometric recognition is accepted as a reliable, robust and convenient means of person authentication and has been employed in many practical applications ranging from personal computer logons to large-scale border controls. The popularity of multibiometric systems, which make use of multiple biometric modalities information to reach a conclusion, has recently grown because they offer a better recognition performance than unibiometric systems. Several large-scale biometric systems such as that used at the Shenzhen-Lo Wu border control in China, the FBI-IAFIS in the USA and the UIDAI System in India have been installed. With the growing use of multiple biometric modalities, there is a rising concern about the security and privacy of biometrics data collected from the public. Because each person has a unique set of biometrics (e.g. fingerprints, face and iris), if these biometric data are compromised, it is difficult to revoke and re-issue new biometric data. The public acceptance of biometric technology not only relies on the accuracy and robustness of a biometric system, but also depends on the security of the stored biometric templates. The central problem in this project is to ensure multimodal biometric templates (a biometric template refers to a set of features extracted from raw biometric data) are secure such that recognition performance is not affected. All existing methods offer a trade-off between template security and recognition performance. In the worst case scenario, the recognition performance of a multibiometric system with template protection is not as good as that of a unibiometric system, and therefore defeats the purpose of employing multiple biometrics. Unlike existing protection methods which provide only binary information on each biometric modality, the new multibiometric template protection method to be developed in this project envisaged here could provide a matching score for each biometric modality. Existing score-level fusion algorithms could therefore be applied to maximize recognition performance. The proposed method will be developed by taking advantage of transform-based and biometric cryptosystem approaches in biometric template protection, as well as traditional cryptographic algorithms. The proposed project will culminate in development of a multimodal biometric template protection scheme and algorithm. Moreover, to address the limited number of publicly available multibiometric databases, this project will create a new multimodal biometric database available to the public. The results of this project and the new multibiometric database will contribute to security and privacy issues arising from and evaluation of multibiometric systems.

211612.label: Realisation of objectives
211612.value: The listed objectives have been realized satisfactorily along three main directions. With respect to the first objective, we have developed a multi-biometric template protection framework that is based on binary feature fusion to achieve high security and recognition performance of the system. This work mainly provides a fusion solution when the extracted features of some modalities are in binary and the feature fusion, which the multi-biometric template protection framework is based on, needs to be carried out at the binary level. With respect to the second objective, we have developed a feature transformation scheme to enable the application of cryptosystem on multiple unimodal biometric sources that are represented by heterogeneous feature representations. When heterogeneous feature representations are involved, the proposed scheme converts the unordered features into an ordered histogram representation without introducing degradation in original performance so that an ordered-feature-based feature-level fusion can be directly applied on the converted representation(s) and other ordered representation(s). Finally, a cryptosystem can be applied to secure the fused features, which results in a multi-biometric cryptosystem that can be applied on heterogeneous feature representations. With respect to the third objective, we have performed a security analysis on a transform-based template protection and demonstrated that a synthetic face image can be constructed from the binary template and the stolen token storing projection and discretization parameters to obtain a highly-probable positive authentication response. Besides that, we have additionally proposed a security measurement model to address the lack of measure for evaluating the security of multi-biometric feature-fusion-based template-protected systems considering two practical attack scenarios. For the security at decision-level fusion, it is not as secure as at feature fusion-based cryptosystems level. It is because the adversarial effort for breaking a multimodal feature-fused biometric template is much greater than the aggregate adversarial effort for breaking multiple unimodal templates used in decision-level-based fusions.

211612.label: Major findings and research outcome
211612.value: As multibiometric cryptosystem based on feature-level fusion offers a more secure solution than cryptosystems based on fusion at other levels, we have designed a binary feature fusion method that extracts a set of fused binary features with high discriminability and entropy (randomness) from the unimodal features. Unlike existing fusion methods that mainly focus on discriminability, the proposed method focuses on both feature discriminability and system security. The superiority in discriminability and security of the proposed method has been verified experimentally using a benchmark multimodal database and two virtual multimodal databases. The preliminary results of this work have been published in [Mai, Lim and Yuen, BTAS 2015]. The paper was selected by the "Best of biometrics 2015" and invited to submitthe full version to Image and Vision Computing journal [Mai, Lim and Yuen, Image and Vision Computing 2016]. To solve the feature incompatibility problem in biometric feature-level fusion for multibiometric cryptosystem, we have developed a geometric Hash-based indexing method to extract a compact Minutia Cylinder Code from the unordered fingerprint minutia. The proposed method is decently structured but the extracted code is not entirely ordered [Wang. Wang, Cheung and Yuen, ICPR 2014]. To overcome this problem, we have developed a generic unordered-to-ordered feature transformation method to enable feature fusion when both ordered and unordered feature sets representing different biometric sources are involved. The proposed transformation learns a discriminative histogram representation from an unordered feature set. By learning a set of histogram bins for each target user, the ordered histogram representation of a sample can be generated by concatenating the normalized frequency of unordered features falling into histogram bins. We have performed experiments on ten benchmark biometric databases to demonstrate the ability of the proposed feature transformation scheme in preserving the discrimination power of the original features. This work has been submitted to Pattern Recognition journal [Lim, Verma, Yuen and Mai, Pattern Recognition 2015]. In term of security of multi-biometric template protection, we have studied a transform-based template protection framework that uses matching score in making “accept/reject” decision. We have demonstrated that a masquerade attack can be used to obtain a false accept with a much higher probability using a generated synthetic face image [Feng, Lim and Yuen, Pattern Recognition 2014].

211612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
211612.value: In solving the feature incompatibility problem in feature fusion, the proposed feature transformation scheme relies on group-correspondence estimation. The estimated correspondences can be prone to error if the unique features are close to each other. A future work along this line is to overcome this issue in order to preserve the performance of the original features more promisingly. In addition, as the proposed scheme does not support the use of feature mask in ordered similarity assessment, another important future direction would be to develop transformation methods that can incorporate the use of mask in the transformation. In addressing the lack of security measure for measuring the security of multibiometric cryptosystem, the proposed guessing-entropy-based security measurement model that quantifies system security based on adversarial guessing effort is a simulation-based approach. A weakness of the simulation approach is the (impractically) huge computational complexity when the biometric features are highly informative. To overcome this issue, a statistical approach can further be explored to derive a security measurement model with higher practicality.

211612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
211612.value: Multibiometric recognition offers higher recognition accuracy than unibiometric recognition. Since biometrics is irrevocable and irreplaceable, the use of multiple biometric modalities in recognition systems has given rise to growing concern about whether it is safe to store such biometrics data (a.k.a. templates) in the system. Most existing approaches offer a trade-off between security and recognition performance. To overcome this issue, it is the objective of this project to ensure that the stored multimodal biometric data is secure and that recognition performance is not degraded simultaneously. The results of this project have contributed to the research in multibiometric template protection in several aspects: We have developed a multi-biometric template protection framework that is based on binary feature fusion to achieve high security and recognition performance; We have developed an unordered-to-ordered feature transformation scheme to allow multibiometric template protection to be applied on incompatible feature representations without introducing any significant degradation in discrimination power of the original unordered features; We have studied and performed security analysis on a transform-based template protection and have proposed a security measurement model to address the lack of measure for evaluating the security of multibiometric feature-fusion-based template-protected systems with respect to two practical attack scenarios.

211912.label: Project Objectives
211912.value: To investigate the role of product reviews in modeling user preferences for contextual uses and fine-grained features. To achieve this, we will: a) structure a product space by considering the special characteristics of feature opinions and conditional opinions on the products; b) model users’ multi-criteria and dependent constraints under the adapted multi-attribute utility theory; and c) elicit/refine user preferences via opinion-integrated critiquing support; To incorporate comparative opinions to strengthen traditional product graph and augment the generation of recommendations in both preference-based and product-related cases; To build a proof-of-concept system to validate our proposed methods in real e-commerce scenarios.

211912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
211912.value: 传统意义上的推荐系统是利用用户的历史交易数据来产生一组相关的推荐，而且这种推荐通常针对于低风险的产品（如电影、音乐和书籍等）。然而，在电子商务领域，许多高风险的产品（如笔记本、照相机等）是很少被用户反复体验的，因此传统的推荐方法有一定的局限性。针对这种类型的产品，如何更为准确的建立用户的多条件喜好，从而在较少的交互过程中能最大化的增加他们的决策准确性是研究的关键。在此项目中，我们通过深入挖掘用户评论信息来解决此问题。用户评论是以文字的形式来表达对已用产品的评价。虽然在市场学中学者已指出其他顾客的评论对潜在的新用户的决策影响，但这些信息并没有被广泛的用于改进当前推荐系统的准确性中。因此，我们的目标是实现一个以评论为增强手段和多条件为基础的用户建模和产品推荐机制。更详细的说，我们致力于从评论中挖掘三种主要信息来提高推荐算法：属性特征的观点、带条件的观点、和比较型的观点。比如，我们计划使用多元线性模型来反映静态和观点属性值之间的对应关系。同时，通过带条件的观点，建立起环境因素与用户需求的分层树状结构，并基于此进一步建立用户的多条件需求模型。比较型观点可主要用来增强产品结构图，从而反映多个产品之间的优劣关系。多学科的理论和实践结果，如数据挖掘、决策支持、人机交互和用户行为分析等，会被有效的结合来实现我们的验证系统。我们期望研究结果不仅可以对观点挖掘和推荐系统等领域有学术贡献，并且可帮助推动本地电子商务的个性化服务。

211912.label: Realisation of objectives
211912.value: Objective 1. To investigate the role of product reviews in modeling user preferences for contextual uses and fine-grained features. To achieve this, we will: a) structure a product space by considering the special characteristics of feature opinions and conditional opinions on the products; b) model users’ multi-criteria and dependent constraints under the adapted multiattribute utility theory; and c) elicit/refine user preferences via opinion-integrated critiquing support; We have made the following four achievements: 1) We have proposed a novel clustering method based on Latent Class Regression model (LCRM), which is essentially able to consider both the overall ratings and feature-level opinion values (as extracted from textual reviews) to derive reviewers’ multi-attribute preferences. The experiment demonstrates the superior performance of our approach in terms of increasing the system’s recommendation accuracy. The research outcomes were published in Journal Knowledge-Based Systems (KNOSYS), 2013 (with impact factor 3.325). 2) We further investigated the three inter-connected tasks in a unified framework: aspect identification, aspect-based rating inference and weight estimation, since the relationship among these three tasks is inherently dependent. We developed an unsupervised model to collectively estimate aspect ratings and weights (shorted as CARW), which performs all of the three tasks by enhancing each other mutually. We conducted experiments on three real-life datasets to evaluate the CARW model. Experimental results show that the proposed model can achieve better performance than the related methods regarding each task. The research outcomes were published in Web Intelligence: An International Journal (WIAS), 2015. 3) In addition, we have considered the contextual information embedded in user reviews to recover their context-dependent preferences. Specifically, we use contextual weighting strategies to derive users’ aspect level context-dependent preferences. The inferred context-dependent preferences are then combined with users’ context-independent preferences (that are also inferred from reviews to reflect their stable requirements over time). To automatically incorporate both types of user preferences into the recommendation process, we propose a linear-regression-based algorithm that uses a stochastic gradient descent learning procedure. We tested the proposed recommendation algorithm with two real-life service datasets, which shows our approach outperforms the others in respect of recommendation accuracy. The research outcomes were published in User Modeling and User-Adapted Interaction Journal (UMUAI), 2015 (with impact factor 2.292). 4) We also addressed the one-class collaborative filtering ranking problem, and proposed a new and improved assumption, group Bayesian personalized ranking (GBPR), via introducing richer interactions among users. In particular, we introduce group preference, to relax the aforementioned individual and independence assumptions. We then design a novel algorithm correspondingly, which can recommend items more accurately as shown by various ranking-oriented evaluation metrics on four real-world datasets in our experiments. The work was published in 23rd International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI’13), 2013 SIAM International Conference on Data Mining (SDM’13), and Neurocomputing Journal (with impact factor 2.392). Objective 2. To incorporate comparative opinions to strengthen traditional product graph and augment the generation of recommendations in both preference-based and product-related cases; For this objective, we designed three alternative sentiment-embedded comparison interfaces to accommodate comparative opinions, respectively called opinion table, opinion bar chart, and opinion cloud. We then performed two user studies on the three interfaces. The first user study verified (1) the important role of comparison matrix in users’ decision process, (2) the benefit of incorporating reviews into the comparison interface, and (3) the positive effect of showing features’ sentiment info on aiding users’ product comparison. Motivated by the first study’s results, we carried out the second user study to in depth compare the three alternative designs empirically. It turns out that the opinion bar chart, which mainly visualizes numerical feature sentiment scores via bars and qualitative adjective words via tool tip window, achieved significantly higher user assessments in terms of perceived information sufficiency, perceived ease of use and perceived cognitive effort. Users also behaved more actively in manipulating the extracted features when using the opinion bar chart, while less frequently viewing the raw textual reviews. The opinion cloud, which primarily visualizes the feature-associated opinion words in form of adjusted tags, was shown with better performance than opinion table, but slightly lower favor than opinion bar chart. In addition, this study revealed the effectiveness of showing opinion features (i.e., features with sentiment) in allowing users to examine the similarity and contrast across multiple products, and hence enabling them to make an informed and confident decision at the end. The research findings were published in Journal Knowledge-Based Systems (KNOSYS), 2014 (with impact factor 3.325). However, due to the sparsity of comparative opinions we are able to extract from existing date resources, the originally proposed task of exploiting them to augment recommendations is not fully accomplished in the current project. In the future, we will exert to investigate other product domains in addition to e-commerce for carrying out this task. Objective 3. To build a proof-of-concept system to validate our proposed methods in real e-commerce scenarios. We implemented a proof-of-concept system and tested it in real e-commerce scenarios though a series of simulations and user experiments (see the experimental findings summarized above). Moreover, we integrated a novel explanation interface into the system for fusing the feature sentiments as extracted from reviews into explaining recommendations. Besides, it can explain multiple items altogether by revealing their similarity in respect of feature sentiments as well as static specifications, so as to support users’ decision making. A user study has been released to collect users’ self-reported preferences and perceptions of the system. From preliminary analysis, we found that that our explanation interface has the potential to increase users’ product knowledge, preference certainty, perceived information usefulness, recommendation transparency and quality, and purchase intention. The idea was published in 23rd International World Wide Web Conference (WWW’14) – Companion.

211912.label: Major findings and research outcome
211912.value: In this project, we in-depth investigated the role of product reviews in modeling user preferences over contextual uses and fine-grained features. To address the inherent characteristics of different types of opinions, i.e., feature opinions, contextual opinions, and comparative opinions, we have developed different approaches. To be specific, feature opinions were taken into account to model users’ multi-attribute weight preferences (i.e., importance degrees placed on various attributes). For this goal, a clustering method based on Latent Class Regression model (LCRM) was implemented, and furthermore an unsupervised model was developed to collectively estimate aspect ratings and weights. Contextual opinions were utilized to recover the conditional relationship between contexts (e.g., location, time) and users’ attribute preferences, so as to build their context-dependent preference model. In our work, we detected fine-grained contextual preferences at the level of item aspects and combined them with users’ context-independent preferences to generate recommendations via a linear-regression-based algorithm. As for comparative opinions, we designed different visualization interfaces, such as opinion table, opinion chart, and opinion cloud, for the purpose of exhibiting their advantages of facilitating users to compare multiple products regarding feature sentiments and make purchase decision. Through experiments (as reported in 5.3), we demonstrated the superior performance of our proposed methods relative to related work, from the aspects of not only algorithm accuracy, but also users’ subjective perceptions like their decision confidence, perceived system competence, and purchase intention. As the research output, we have published 14 papers (see Part C), most of which appear in high-impact journals (such as UMUAI, KNOSYS) and core conferences in the areas of artificial intelligence and user modeling (e.g., IJCAI, SDM, UMAP). Besides, one student, with the support of this project, obtained PhD degree in 2016. We also involved several post-doc and research assistants in doing the research work.

211912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
211912.value: Driven by this project’s findings and achievements, we plan to extend the work in the following directions: 1) to take usage of feature sentiments to elicit new users’ preferences on site in an adaptive manner, so that the system could incrementally refine and construct their attribute preferences for both static values and sentiment features. 2) To perform more user studies, especially those with the help of eye-tracking devices, to measure the system’s interface usability. For instance, we may measure whether users would be inclined to rely more on sentiment information when they specify preferences, evaluate/compare products, and make decision. The eye-movement data could further be based to infer users’ implicit feedback on recommendations. 3) From algorithmic perspective, to investigate the deep learning techniques, such as convolutional neural networks (CNN) and recurrent neural networks (RNN), for processing textual information of user reviews and hence more precisely deriving users’ fine-grained contextual preferences.

211912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
211912.value: In recent years, a variety of review-based recommender systems have been developed, with the goal of incorporating the valuable information in user-generated textual reviews into the user modeling and recommending process. Advanced text analysis and opinion mining techniques enable the extraction of various types of review elements, such as the discussed topics, the multi-faceted nature of opinions, contextual information, comparative opinions, and reviewers’ emotions. In our project, we have addressed the limitations of related work, with main focus on exploiting the usage of feature opinions, contextual opinions, and comparative opinions in the e-commerce environment to augment the competence of recommender systems in handling its typical new user phenomenon. We proposed different approaches to accommodating different types of opinions’ respective properties, and identified the approaches’ distinctive performance in real e-commerce scenarios via empirical experiments.

240112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
240112.value: The project proposed in this application will research the documentary film production of Television Broadcasts Ltd. (TVB) and Asia Television (ATV), the two terrestrial television broadcasters in Hong Kong. This proposed project is an EXTENSION of an existing GRF project: 'Documentary Film in Hong Kong 1959-2006: The Documentary Film Series' (RGC/HKBU ref: 240109), which is due to end 29.12.2011. The 240109 project undertook a critical analysis of documentary film series produced in Hong Kong between the dates given. The project sought to arrive at conclusions concerning the range and diversity of films involved, the authorial profiles and stature of film-makers, the themes, subjects and stylistic characteristics evident within the films, the intellectual, cultural, social, political, organisational and other influences upon them; and the national/international importance of respective films, film-makers and institutions. The original intention of project 240109 was to focus research on the films and archival holdings of ALL the major producers of documentary film series in Hong Kong. These are (a) the Hong Kong Film Unit (HKFU) (1959-1968) and Radio Hong Kong Television Unit (RHKTVU (1969-79) (both of whose films/resources are held at the HK Public Records Office (PRO); (b) Radio Television Hong Kong (RTHK), (c) Asia Television Ltd. (ATV), and (d) Television Broadcasts Ltd. (TVB). However, mid way through project 240109 it became clear that the project could not cover all the new research materials and tasks that emerged as the project progressed; and it was subsequently amended to concentrate on the public sector: the HKFU, RHKTVU, and RTHK. It was not possible to cover the films and resources of the commercial sector: TVB and ATV. The extension project proposed in this GRF application, will cover this area, and resolve this problem. This extension project will be directly linked to project 240109. However, it will focus research exclusively on the resources and films of TVB and ATV. Project 240109 was itself an extension of an earlier CERG project (2007-9) which successfully focused mainly on individual documentary films, and the independent sector. The extension project proposed in this application is necessary in order to fully conclude and thoroughly finalize these first two GRF projects, within the framework of the overall research programme. This extension project will, therefore, serve to effectuate and COMPLETE the overall research programme on the subject area of the documentary film in Hong Kong, and thus constitute a unified study of the subject. 摘要 本申請項目擬研究香港電視廣播有限公司（TVB）和亞洲電視（ATV）兩家香港地面電視廣播公司的紀錄片製作。此擬議計劃是前一個GRF項目“香港紀錄片1959－2006：系列紀錄片”（RGC/HKBU ref: 240109）的延伸，彼項目已在2011年12月29日完成。項目240109對鎖定時間內的香港系列紀錄片作出了批評分析。它力圖得出的結論關切所涉及影片的範圍和多樣性、作者簡介和定位、主題、主體以及影片內明顯的風格特徵、它們在思想、文化、社會、政治、組織以及其它方面的所受到的影響；以及各個影片、作者、機構在國內、國際上的重要性。項目240109最初試圖研究香港“所有”主要系列紀錄片生產者的影片和檔案館藏。它們包括（a）香港電影部（HKFU）（1959－1968）、香港電台電視部（RHKTVU）（1969-79），這兩家機構的影片和資料被收藏在香港政府檔案處（PRO）；（b）香港電台（RTHK），（c）亞洲電視（ATV），以及（d）香港電視廣播有限公司（TVB）。但是，在項目240109進行的過程當中，我們意識到隨著項目的進行，出現了新的研究資料和工作，它們無法被全部涵蓋；於是隨之，我們轉而集中於公共電視部份：HKFU、RHKTVU和RTHK。商業電視部份（TVB和ATV）的影片和資料無法被涵蓋進來。這份申請GRF的延伸項目將解決這個問題、涵蓋商業電視部份。本延伸項目將直接與項目240109關連。但是，它將專門聚焦於TVB和ATV的資料和影片。而項目240109本身是對其之前一個GERG項目（2007－9）的延伸，那個項目順利完成了對個人紀錄片以及獨立紀錄片部份的關注。目前所申請的延伸項目，其必要性在於，它計劃在整個研究框架里，對先前兩個GRF項目做充分的總結和全面的定案考察。所以，本延伸計劃將對香港紀錄片這個主題範圍內的所有研究項目作最終整合和定論，以此構成此主題的統一體。

240112.label: Realisation of objectives
240112.value: Objectives 2, 4, 5 and six were not fully realised because of the more or less total refusal of ATV and TVB management to co-operate with the project, or allow the project team to view their archival data. TVB management stated that they had no obligation to assist an academic research project, and refused me access to their archive. ATV simply ignored all communication to them. Both institutions should stand indicted for their lack of civic spirit here. Despite this inability to peruse the paper archives of these two broadcasters, the project team were able to view the vast majority of films produced by ATV and TVB, and come to conclusions regarding them. (See 'Major Finding' section of this report. Because of the lack of co-operation from ATV and TVB management it did not prove possible to hold an international conference on ATV and TVB documentary films. However, this is not significant, as two papers on ATV/TVB were presented by the PI and RA at an international conference hosted by the PI at HKBU in August 2013 entitled 'The Documentary Film in South and South-East Asia'. In addition, the PI presented a paper on ATV/TVB documentary film at an international conference in Thailand in 2014 (see research output' section of this report). In addition, a significant number of analyses of ATV/TVB films have been placed on the project website. Public exhibition of films has not yet materialised for logistical reasons which were also heavily influenced by the lack of support from ATV and TVB

240112.label: Major findings and research outcome
240112.value: The journal article which was the principle published output of this project concluded by relating the documentary films of ATV and TVB to Jurgen Habermas’ notion of the ‘public sphere’ within civil society. In terms of Habermas’ notion of the public sphere of debate within society, it could be argued that the public sphere never existed as an initial province within ATV/TVB documentary film, as it did within the general notion of the historical development of the public sphere. Rather, there were occasions when such a constituency emerged temporarily, around the Sino-British discussions over Hong Kong in the mid-1980s, Tiananmen in 1989-90, the Patten reforms in 1992-4, the 2003 attempt to introduce national security legislation, the failure to introduce universal suffrage in 2006-8, and political conflict related to the Chief Executive in 2012. Beyond that, though, it could also be argued that during the majority of even those occasions the balance which accrued between that film output as ‘private’ (free) and ‘organized’ (by management) in Habermas’ terms remains indeterminate; and it may in fact only have been around Tiananmen that the films of ATV and TVB achieved true free privatory status in the Habermasian sense. Habermas’ notion of the existence of a ‘phony’ public sphere appears to apply to terrestrial commercial television broadcasting here, and what might have been a powerful voice in the Hong Kong public sphere has been transmuted and diluted. Given this, it can be argued that these television documentary films now play two principal roles. First, along with the films of RTHK, these films help keep the public-service remit in existence within the television system. However, and second, these films also help sustain the existing system, because, as in any hegemonic system, the dominant power must tolerate the existence of intermittent oppositional voices and debate in order that the system be deemed tolerable. As is implied by the concept of hegemony, though, these films are circumscribed, acting more as pressure-release valves than incisive exposés. In this respect it is also worth referring to Habermas’ critique of the increasing preponderance of lifestyle/human-interest material within the public sphere. The executive producers of the X and Pearl Reports felt that, over the years, lifestyle/human-interest films had increasingly come to predominate. Seen through this optic, although the current-affairs documentary films of ATV and TVB may keep the torch of public-service alight they are also assuaging and diversionary.

240112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
240112.value: It may be that the research can progress by continuing to monitor the films of ATV and TVB, say over the period from 2013-20. But this would have to be funded from other sources that GRF. One potential area for development is in relation to policy matters that relate to public-service televison film-making in Hong Kong. Future research could monitor the debate over these issues, and the debate over the role of ATV and TVB within the Hong Kong media. Another future direction of research would be a comparative survey of public-service television documentary film-making within the South-East Asian region, or even the ASEAN collusion. This might be more fruitful given the unco-operative nature of TVB and ATV. I would be grateful to receive advice from reviewers on how to proceed.

240112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
240112.value: Television is a major medium of information and communication, in Hong Kong, as well as elsewhere. Within this the role of television documentary film should be an important one. However, this project has discovered that this is not the case in Hong Kong. This means that a potentially important medium for airing and interpreting ideas does not function well within the city. the research has also shown that television documentary film in Hong Kong, or at least that stemming from ATV and TVB, has rarely been able to act as an important transmitter of debate, and has rarely been able to hold the authorities to account in a substantive way.The research has shown the clear need for change in the existing system to improve the matter, through changing the nature of the films, and the broadcasting organisations which produce them. The research has shown that there is a clear and pressing need for public-service television documentary film in Hong Kong to improve, and in so doing, serve the public better

240812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
240812.value: This research project seeks to examine the political influence of the Catholic Church in Hong Kong. Specifically, this research will use Paul Djupe and Christopher Gilbert’s theory of religious influence on political behavior to investigate how the social context of the Catholic Church shapes the way people react to one another, the bonds they form with others, and how they approach society. This study will use both survey and interview as research methods for a full test of the effects of the Catholic Church on the political behavior of their members. The research findings will provide a clearer understanding of the contributions of the Catholic Church to sustaining civil society in Hong Kong. The theoretical significance of this research project is that, it will explicate a theory of church-centered influences on political behavior based on contextual analysis, which will advance the study of religion and politics in Hong Kong. Regarding the practical significance, it will provide a specified model of how voluntary associations expose individuals to political information and norms, which will help us to understand how public opinion is formed and why people participate in politics. 這個研究計劃考察香港天主教教會在政治上影響。具體而言，這個研究以Paul Djupe和Christopher Gilbert的宗教影響政治行為的理論作為架構，查考天主教的社會脈絡如何形塑人們的互動方式、人們如何互相連結，以及他們如何面對社會。這個研究會同時採用問卷調查和面談的方法，測量天主教教會對其信徒的政治行為的影響力。研究結果將會為天主教教會支撑香港公民社會的現象提供一個清晰的解釋。這個研究計劃在理論上的意義，在於從處境分析的進路去闡明教會影響政治行為的理論，從而提昇香港在宗教與政治的研究。在現實意義方面，這個研究會提供一個特定的模型，幫助我們理解志願團體如何影響個人的政治的行為和規範、公眾輿論如何形成，以及為何人們會參與政治。

240812.label: Realisation of objectives
240812.value: The investigator conducted a survey on the Catholic Church as proposed in the research project, invited clergy from 51 parishes to take part in the research project, completed data collection from 12 Catholic parishes where the clergy and church members were willing to participate in the project, and successfully received valid questionnaires from 12 clergy and 1,124 church members from July 2012 to June 2014. The success rate was 24.86%. The data produced a preliminary report with 92 tables, showing how the clergy and church members responded to the questions. This preliminary report was presented to Cardinal John Tong, Bishop of the Hong Kong Catholic Church, and Rev. Lawrence Lee, Chancellor of the Hong Kong Diocesan Curia, in July 2015. The investigator used the data to further produce 31 sophisticated tables, which will facilitate the writing of his academic papers. The investigator completed one paper entitled “Church Influences on Issue Importance: The Case of the Catholic Church in Hong Kong,” which has been uploaded to the GRF/ECS Electronic System. He will continue to write more papers presenting other research findings, including “Church Influences on the Formation of Political Opinions,” “The Effects of Congregational Status on Political Opinions,” etc. The research findings and the paper are evidence of the realization of the first three objectives. First, the investigator is now using the research findings to examine church-centred influences on church members’ political opinions, which is definitely an advancement in the study of religion and politics in Hong Kong. Second, the research findings and the paper have shown that the Church is a powerful agent in helping to set the agendas of church members. The investigator’s papers should be able to draw attention in academic circles, showing that the Church is a potent filter in highlighting important issues and connecting church members to civic and political life. Third, the 31 sophisticated tables will aid in the production of a number of academic papers. Due to time constraints, the investigator has completed one paper which is under review by Politics and Religion (Cambridge University Press). When other papers have been completed, the investigator will send them to The China Quarterly, Sociology of Religion, and Journal for the Scientific Study of Religion. After completion of all papers, the investigator intends to publish them as a monograph by an academic press, such as Brill or Routledge, although more time will be needed to achieve this objective.
