240812.label: Major findings and research outcome
240812.value: This research project investigated church-centred influences on members’ political opinions using Paul Djupe and Christopher Gilbert’s theory of religious influence on political behaviour. The subject of research was the Catholic Church in Hong Kong. The major research findings are summarized as follows: (1) Formal and informal social networks: Social networks in the Catholic Church highlighted the church-centred influences on church members’ issue agenda-setting. Different models were used to test the effects of church-centred influences, including members’ extreme positions on political issues, members’ opinions compared with those of the congregation, and political discussions with partners in social networks. Most of these variables exerted a positive effect on the respondents’ sense of importance on social issues. These findings are consistent with the results of Djupe and Gilbert’s study on the Episcopal Church, USA, and the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America (ELCA). (2) The church environment: The church environment provided a partial explanation of the church-centred influences on members’ political opinions. Clergy speeches offered no evidence of clergy effect on the issue importance and agendas of church members. The congregation’s average opinions had a limited effect on church members. These findings are inconsistent with the results of Djupe and Gilbert’s study in the United States, which may be due to the different context of the Catholic Church in Hong Kong. (3) Orienting forces: Orienting forces refer to the factors that connect the minority status of a church in a community with church-centred political influences. The findings showed that orienting forces had no effect on the clergy’s and congregation’s influence on members’ political opinions. These findings are also inconsistent with Djupe and Gilbert’s study. In their models, religion that is different from that of neighbours and a belief in isolation are significant in explaining church-centred influences on members. (4) Personal attributes and resources: The findings showed that church members’ issue agendas were shaped by personal political attributes, but these effects were not consistent across issues. Religious commitment had a limited effect on social issues, which shows that religious commitment may lead church members to see certain issues as important or irrelevant without revealing what position their faith dictates on that issue. These findings are consistent with the results of Djupe and Gilbert’s study.

240812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
240812.value: The findings have the following implications for further development of the research: (1) Studies on the political influence of Protestant churches: In addition to the Catholic Church, Protestant churches are an equally potent agent of political influence. The Umbrella Movement is an illustrative example, as the core initiators and many participants came from different Protestant denominations. However, there are divisions among Protestant churches with regard to their theological positions. In Hong Kong, Protestant churches are divided into two theological camps, the mainline and the evangelical churches. The same research could be conducted to examine the political influences of the mainline and evangelical congregations on political issues in Hong Kong. (2) Comparative studies of churches: Comparative studies could focus on the influences of the congregation on church members’ political opinions among churches. On the one hand, studies could be carried out to compare the Catholic Church and the mainline Protestant churches, as well as the Catholic Church and the evangelical Protestant churches. On the other hand, studies could be carried out to compare the mainline and the evangelical Protestant churches. These comparative studies could project a clearer picture of the political influences of Christian churches on politics as a whole in Hong Kong.

240812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
240812.value: This research project examines the effect of Catholic parishes’ influence on church members’ political opinions in Hong Kong using Paul Djupe and Christopher Gilbert’s theory of church-centred influence on political behaviour. This project assumed that the Church is a social and political context that is essential for full comprehension of religion’s influence on political behaviour. The four sets of factors that established the contextual determinant of congregant political behaviour were formal and informal social networks, the church environment, and orienting forces. The fifth set of factors was personal characteristics, which also played a role in determining individual beliefs and actions. The research question of this project is: What individual, environmental, and social conditions affect political learning and persuasion in the Church? The investigator conducted a survey in 12 parishes from July 2012 to June 2014, collecting valid questionnaires from 12 clergy and 1,124 church members. The findings show that social networks had a church-centred influence on the church members’ issue of importance, whereas the church environment had less influence on the members. Orienting forces had almost no effect on the church members’ political opinions, while personal attributes and religious resources showed disparate effects on certain issues but not consistently across issues.

241512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
241512.value: Innovation is always specific to an industry. Understanding the innovation and creativity in Hong Kong’s cultural and creative industries (CCIs) involves understanding the production-innovation network of each Hong Kong-based CCI in the local, China, Asia and/or global contexts. Any CCI policy must be based on detailed micro-level analysis of each CCI sector, and include firm-level and project-based analysis. Such a micro approach is needed because most cultural firms are small and survive only on creative projects. Their production organization and innovation systems are different from those of large firms in traditional industrial sectors, such as toys and textiles. In Hong Kong, there have been very few studies of CCIs and they were based exclusively on macro-level and policy-level analysis, which did not consider innovation capabilities, networks and institutional support for each CCI. The under-rating of micro-level analysis has mainly been due to the non-interventionist ideology of policymakers in Hong Kong. They believe that the market is better than the government at choosing the right sectors. However, even if we agree that direct intervention is undesirable, a thorough understanding of the dynamics of each sector is still needed to formulate effective indirect or market-oriented CCI policies. Micro-level industrial research is very labor intensive; we therefore propose to select for study three CCIs where Hong Kong has competitive advantage: publishing; the performing arts; and galleries, museums and visual arts. We propose to study four aspects of CCI. We will study the flexible and collaborative production systems of small Hong Kong firms and individual artists. We will study collective innovation, which differs from individual creativity because it depends on trust, professionalism, conventions and other institutional factors. The creative process and the role of unions will be addressed through analyzing the changing labor market and labor processes that are critical to the sustainability of a given industry. Lastly, we propose to analyze the active role of the local institutions (Hong Kong’s Arts Development Council, Arts festivals, the West Kowloon Cultural District Authority, Leisure and Cultural Services Department etc.) in shaping the institutional environment. The two objectives of this project include: 1. To construct detailed micro-level profiles of the selected CCI sectors by focusing on their production-innovation networks. These profiles will be designed to allow us to understand collective innovation, networks across borders, and sustainable labor processes. 2. To analyze the interaction and co-development between the CCIs, public institutions and their policies, and urban environment. 每一行業的創新都是獨特的。要了解香港的文化創意產業(文創業) 的創新和創意，我們必須了解以香港為基地的文創業產在香港-中國-全球脈絡下的「生產-創新網絡」。本計劃認為任何文創業的政策必須基於對各別產業的微觀、公司及專案(project)為基礎的分析。這種微觀的方法是必要的，因為香港絕大多數文創業規模小，都是靠接專案生存。他們的生產組織和創新體系，跟傳統工業(如玩具和紡織品)的大企業是不同的。在香港，有極少數的文創業研究，但他們是基於宏觀和政策層面的分析，沒有考慮各別文創業的創新能力，網絡和體制。微觀層面分析不被重視的主要原因，是基於香港的政策決策者有不干預產業運作的思維。他們認為市場比政府更能選擇正確的產業。然而，即使我們同意直接干預是不可取的，我們仍然需要徹底了解各產業的狀況，以方便制定有效的間接或以市場為導向的文創業政策。 微觀層面的產業研究是非常勞力密集的，因此，我們建議選擇在香港較有競爭優勢的文創產：出版、表演藝術及視覺藝術 (註:由於通過的預算減少，原計劃的三個產業研究，可能減少至兩個)。本計劃將研究的文創業的四個面向。一、生產網絡: 香港小公司和個別藝術工作者的彈性且協同的生產組織; 二、集體創新：有別個人創意，「集體創新」依賴信任、專業主義、公約(conventions)和其他制度性的支持。三、勞動過程: 我們也透過分析勞工市場及勞動過程，去瞭解創作過程及工會的角色。四、文創業與體制互動: 分析公共機構（香港藝術發展局藝術節、西九文化區管理局、康樂及文化事務署等）如何形塑文創業的制度性環境。簡言之，本計劃有兩個目標: 一、建構微觀層面的文創產的生產-創新網絡、集體創新及可持續的勞動過程。 二、分析文創業與公共機構(及政策)的互動和共生發展方式。

241612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
241612.value: How economic growth and energy consumption affect each other (the so-called growth-energy nexus) has long been a subject of academic and policy interests. The importance of exploring this relationship is particularly timely and relevant for the case of China. The nation’s rapid economic growth and the accompanying rising energy demand have far-reaching economic and geopolitical impacts on the world. The phenomenon of global inflation in the past decade was driven up by the increase in energy prices, which was at least partly attributable to China’s competition for resources. The new geopolitics and energy security consideration have also led to drastic changes in international relations. The Chinese government has been aware of its economic expansion and growing energy need. It has made great efforts to achieve a more energy-saving and environment-friendly growth in recent years. Formulating sensible growth and energy policies, however, requires an in-depth understanding of the relations between growth and energy in China. Unfortunately, there is only limited understanding available from extant research. This project aims to provide analyses to improve this understanding, by applying state-of-the-art methodologies to new data sets of China. Specifically, a long series of data covering the period 1952-2010 will be used in the aggregate analysis. Moreover, a panel data set covering most provinces for the period of 1991-2010 will be used in the disaggregate analysis. The nature of the data sets allows us to discern whether there exist structural breaks over time and regional variations. We will start with an estimation of the output elasticity of energy, followed by various causality tests. Our research will contribute to energy economics and inform the formulation of China’s energy and economic growth policies in the next decade. 經濟增長與能源消耗的相互作用（即所謂「增長-能源」關係）一直是學術界和政策領域關注的焦點。對於中國而言，當前探索該問題尤具適切性。中國經濟的高速增長以及隨之而來不斷上升的能源需求，對全球經濟和地緣政治有著深遠的影響。過去十年由能源價格上漲引致的全球通貨膨脹，至少可以部分地歸因於中國對能源的競逐。地緣政治與能源安全方面的新變化也導致了國際關係的風雲突變。近年來，中國政府已經意識到國家的經濟擴張和日益增長的能源需求，並在追求能源節約和環境友好型增長方面進行了大量的嘗試。制定合理的增長和能源政策，需要對中國的增長-能源聯結模式進行深入理解。遺憾的是，現有研究對該聯結模式的探索還很不充分。本研究旨在運用前沿的研究方法，以新近收集得的數據進行研究，旨在加深對此聯結模式的理解。具體而言，1952年到2010年的全國性時間序列資料將用作總體分析， 1991年到2010年覆蓋大多數省份的面板資料將用作區域性分析。這些數據的性質可以讓我們檢驗時間和區域變數是否存在結構性變化。本研究將首先估計能源產出彈性，然後進行各項因果檢驗。本研究將對能源經濟學的發展和中國未來十年能源與經濟增長政策的制定作出貢獻。

241612.label: Realisation of objectives
241612.value: The theme of this project has been intensively studied in recent years. Soon after the commencement of this project, a number of studies were published in major energy-related journals, covering part of the work we planned to do in the proposal. Nevertheless, we have tried to make further breakthroughs in this research area by either analyzing the problems with improved estimation methods or linking the issues to relevant polices of China. In sum, we have achieved all the objectives by applying different econometric methods to different data sets. The results are presented in a series of articles. Specifically, 1. We have conducted linear Granger causality tests using China’s aggregate data for the period of 1953-2010 (Cheng, Woo and Wong, 2013). In addition, we have applied nonparametric nonlinear Granger causality tests on the same data set (Cheng and Shum, 2015a). Furthermore, we have applied similar tests on China’s quarterly data during 1998-2015 (Cheng and Shum, 2015b). 2. We have estimated dynamic panel models taking into account the presence of cross-section dependence with disaggregate data for the period of 1995-2011 to perform the panel version of the Granger causality tests. Apart from running the full panel of 30 provinces, we have also estimated separate panels for the Eastern, Central and Western regions of China, yielding new insights for formulation of energy policy (Cheng, Li and Woo, 2014). 3. The output elasticity of energy (electricity) of China can be obtained from the relevant models used for the causality tests (mainly from Cheng, Woo and Wong, 2013; Cheng, Li and Woo, 2014). 241612.label: Major findings and research outcome
241612.value: The findings of this project can be summarized as follows. 1. Using aggregate data for 1953-2010, Cheng, Wong and Woo (2013) find a unidirectional linear causality running from electricity consumption to economic growth. Cheng and Shum (2015a), apart from confirming the same result for linear causality, have also detected the existence of nonlinear causality in the same direction. However, using quarterly data for the more recent period of time (1998-2015), Cheng and Shum (2015a) find bidirectional causality between the two variables. Given the rapid structural transformation of the Chinese economy, the result using long series of data is probably less relevant for policy formulation. We are of the view that the bidirectional causality result for recent years should be taken more seriously, implying that a more cautious approach should be adopted for energy conservation policy. 2. Using disaggregate data (i.e. panel data for 30 provinces) for the period of 1995-2011, a bidirectional causal relationship between the per capita energy consumption and per capita real GDP is found. However, there are clear regional differences between the three broad regions: Eastern, Central and Western. Specifically, we find a. a bidirectional causal relationship between the per capita energy consumption and per capita real GDP for the Central region b. a unidirectional causal relationship from income to energy consumption for the Eastern and Western regions. These findings yield a new insight for China’s energy policy. With the bidirectional results for the full panel of 30 provinces in mind, China should in general adopted a caution approach in energy conservation. However, the regional analysis suggests that a regionally differential policy should be optimal for China to apply more aggressive policy in the energy conservation for the Eastern and Western regions while remaining cautious for the Central region. 3. According to Cheng, Wong and Woo (2013), the output elasticity of electricity consumption (i.e. the percentage change in output in respond to one percentage change in energy consumption) is about 0.6, and there was significant difference for the pre-1978 reform period. Cheng, Li and Woo (2014) provides estimates of output elasticity of energy consumption for the period of 1995-2011. The national elasticity estimate is about 0.6. The Eastern region’s estimate is also 0.6, while the Central region’s and Western region’s estimates are 0.23 and 0.27 respectively.

241612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
241612.value: The underlying motivation of this project is to find out an appropriate approach for energy conservation policy in China. While it is essential to find out the nexus between energy consumption and economic growth, it is even more important to study how they affect carbon dioxide emissions. Along this line of thinking, studies on other countries have been conducted. There are a few preliminary studies on how economic growth and other variables affect carbon emissions in China, but a lot more work is needed to generate an indepth understanding of the issue.

241612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
241612.value: China is the second largest economy and largest energy consuming country in the world. With a low per capita income, China continues to pursue economic growth with an annual growth target of about 7% in recent years. How to balance economic growth and energy consumption has been a major policy concern. Causality analysis helps us to understand their relationship and formulate better policy. Unidirectional causality from growth to energy consumption suggests that promoting conservation is unlikely to have an adverse effect on economic growth. Unidirectional causality from energy consumption to economic growth, however, implies that the same policy can hamper economic growth. Finally, bidirectional causality between energy consumption and income calls for a cautious approach because of their interdependence. Our aggregate analysis for recent years suggests that there is a bidirectional causality between the two variables. Our disaggregate analysis suggests that a regionally differentiated approach should be adopted by China. The Central region’s bidirectional causality suggests caution in China’s energy conservation policy because of its potentially adverse impact on economic growth. The Eastern and Western regions’ unidirectional relationship, however, suggests that more aggressive energy conservation policy can be adopted in these two regions.

241812.label: Project Title(Chinese)
241812.value: 以跨學科研究為本，建立太極「推手」的翻譯研究路向

241812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
241812.value: In the history of translation in China and other cultural traditions, debates about how religious and other conceptual terms should be translated are very common. How, for example, should “God”, or “Buddha”, or the Daoist concept of “dao” (道) be translated? Some argue that they should be rendered with similar terms in the receiving culture (for example, rendering “dao” as “God”, or “logos”). Such a method of translation, called domestication, has been vigorously criticized for obliterating the unique features of the source concept. In direct opposition to this is the method called foreignization, which highlights differences by the use of transliteration (for example, deploying the pinyin “dao” for 道). The frequent occurrence of such debates shows that binary thinking is not so much intellectual quirkiness as a habit of mind that has prevailed in the past. Such a mindset dominates the contemporary world too, as seen in the widespread use of binary opposites such as Self and Other, Us and Them, the West and the non-West, etc. in both academic and everyday discourses. The resultant tension in cross-cultural relation is likely to worsen with the rise of China and the increasing perception that China will become a major threat to the world. Within the PRC, however, sentiments are strong that notwithstanding her economic strength, China is still under the cultural hegemony of the West. Given the resentment simmering on all sides, it is imperative that the momentum built up by recent intellectual endeavours to explore modes of thinking other than that of binary thinking be sustained. This research seeks to add to that momentum by introducing what the PI calls the "pushing-hands" mode of thinking in translation studies. Pushing-hands is a form of Chinese martial art that involves, not one person in solo exercise, but two persons remaining in contact and moving in unison, in a range of pushing and yielding motion. There is the combative form of pushing-hands and also the non-combative form. The research draws inspiration from the latter. The fluid movements of the practitioners are used as a figurative representation of a mode of thinking that affirms the need for constant interaction and dialogue. Translation studies is chosen as the field of inquiry because, with the continual rise of China, translation is certain to play an even more crucial role in the production of cross-cultural (mis)understanding and (mis)communication. 在中國和其他文化傳統的翻譯史中，就宗教和其他概念用詞應該如何翻譯所牽起的爭論，比比皆是。例如，"God"、"Buddha"，或道教中 "道" 的概念應該如何翻譯呢？有些人認為應該以譯入語文化相近似的概念去翻譯（例如，以 "God" 或 "logos" 去翻譯 "道" 這個概念)，不過這種稱為「本土化」翻譯手法卻往往為人詬病，被批評為抹殺了原有概念的特質；與此相反的另一種翻譯手法則稱為「異化」，一般以音譯方式突顯出概念的不同之處（例如，以拼音 "dao" 去翻譯 "道"）。 這樣的爭論在歷史上屢見不鮮，顯示二元思維經常主導過去的學術討論。這種思維也同樣主導了現今的社會，從學術界和日常用語中一些經常使用的二元對立詞 ── "自我" 和 "他者"、"我們" 和 "他們"、"西方" 和 "非西方" ── 可見一斑。這種思維將會因為中國崛起以及在世界多處地方時有所聞的 "中國威脅論" 而令跨文化關係變得緊張。另一方面，中國內地有不少人卻認為，儘管中國經濟強勁，但中國仍然深受到西方文化霸權的威脅。縱觀各方的不滿聲音，我們有需要配合近期開創的學術風潮，努力發掘二元思維以外的其他思考方法。 本研究試圖建立項目主導人所稱的太極「推手」翻譯研究路向，以此推動這個學術風潮。「推手」是一種兩人一起練習的太極拳，有競技推手和非競技推手之分，本研究的意念源自後者。它是綿軟圓渾、大鬆大柔的功夫；兩手接觸，立即憑觸覺探索彼此的虛實，尋找對方的身體重心與動作缺點，聽著對方的勁而走化，引其力量落空，而非以力硬擋。推手雙方練習時表現出的鬆靜自然與身心的和諧合一，使太極推手成為一種練身也練心的功夫，內外整全的哲學，而其既有對立又有互動的特色，更能為人文學的各個學科提供二元思維以外的思考方法。本研究試從太極推手蘊含的哲理，即陰陽相反相濟的原理 ，發展出非此即彼以外的思考方法。選擇以翻譯研究為切入點，是因為項目主導人認為只要中國繼續強大，翻譯必然會在跨文化理解（誤解）和溝通（溝通誤差）中擔當更加重要的角色，如何促進互動、保持對話也就更形重要。

242012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
242012.value: Research on team innovation, i.e., the generation and implementation of novel and potentially useful ideas by individuals working together in a team (West, 2002), has widely applied the input-processes-output (I-P-O) model (e.g., West & Anderson, 1996). Functional diversity has been regarded as an important input (e.g., Bantel & Jackson, 1989) because it potentially provides broad knowledge resources conducive to team innovation (e.g., Taylor & Greve, 2006). Existing team innovation research, however, has yet to develop and empirically test an I-P-O model for functional diversity. Functional diversity may benefit team innovation when team members actually share their knowledge (e.g., Drach-Zahavy & Somech, 2001). Thus, intra-team knowledge sharing may be a mechanism relating functional diversity to team innovation. Social categorization theory, however, suggests that individuals may hold negative views of others who they consider different from themselves (Tajfel, 1982). An implication of such bias is that functionally dissimilar members may not automatically engage in knowledge sharing. It is important to understand when functional diversity influences intra-team knowledge sharing and thus team innovation. The proposed study will examine support for innovation as a moderator in the relationship between functional diversity and intra-team knowledge sharing. West (1990) defined support for innovation as “the expectation, approval and practical support of attempts to introduce new and improved ways of doing things in the work environment” (p. 38). When a supportive climate for innovation exists, functionally dissimilar members may share knowledge because of the external expectation on innovation and a norm on cooperative relations. The enhanced knowledge will improve team innovation. Additionally, we propose intra-team knowledge sharing as a mediator in the support for innovation-team innovation relationship. Despite the ample evidence of the positive relationship between support for innovation and team innovation (see Hülsheger, Anderson, & Salgado, 2009 for a meta-analytic review), we do not know much about how it occurs. We will collect temporally-lagged, multi-source data from 10-15 advertising agencies. We will collect data on functional diversity and support for innovation (wave 1) and intra-team knowledge sharing (wave 2) from employees, and team innovation from team supervisors (wave 3). Upon completion, this program of research will expand current knowledge on (1) how functional diversity and support for innovation relate to team innovation; and (2) when the relationship between functional diversity and team innovation is strengthened or weakened. In doing so, this study advances scholarly understanding of the effects of functional diversity on team innovation. “輸入、過程和產出”(I-P-O) 模型被廣泛地應用在團隊創新的研究上。團隊創新即是通過團隊一起工作來形成並實現新穎的以及潛在有用的想法。由於功能多樣性能夠潛在地提供有益於團隊創新的廣泛知識資源，它被看作是一個重要的輸入。然而，現有的團隊創新研究並沒有發展並基於經驗研究來檢測有關功能多樣性的“輸入、過程和產出”模型。當團隊成員確實共享他們的知識時，功能多樣性可能有益於團隊創新。因此，團隊內部的知識共享可能是一個鏈接功能多樣性與團隊創新的機制。然而，社會分類理論提出個人可能對他們認為與之不同的人持有負面看法。 對於這種偏見的一個寓意就是功能不相似的團隊成員可能不會主動地進行知識共享。理解何時功能多樣性會影響團隊內知識共享和團隊創新是很重要的。 這項擬議的研究將會調查對於創新的支持作為調節變量在功能多樣性與團隊內知識共享的關系中的作用。West(1990) 把支持創新定義為“對於在工作環境中嘗試引入新的和改良的做事方法的期望、批准和實際支持”（第38頁）。當存在支持創新的組織氛圍時，功能不相似的團隊成員可能由於外在的對創新的期望以及合作關系的規範而共享知識。增強的知識會提升團隊創新。此外，我們還假設團隊內知識共享作為支持創新與團隊創新關系中的中介變量。盡管有豐富的證據可以證明支持創新與團隊創新的正向關系，我們並不知道多少有關它如何成立。 本研究完成後將會拓展現有的知識有關（1）功能多樣性和支持創新如何影響團隊創新；和（2）什麼時候功能多樣性和團隊創新這個關系會被加強或減弱。這項研究發展了功能多樣性對團隊創新影響的學術理解。

242012.label: Realisation of objectives
242012.value: We satisfactorily achieved three of the objectives (specifically 1, 2 and 4). In a study (currently under second round of revise and resubmission at Human Relations), we tested the proposed knowledge sharing mechanism linking functional diversity with team innovation. We examined the moderating effects of affect-based trust in a team on the indirect effects of functional diversity on team innovation through knowledge sharing. The RGC’s funding also supported three other projects. In one paper (currently under review at Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes), we examined diversity of knowledge within individual employees through their learning within and outside their specialty area. We developed two types of employee learning and their measurements: domain-specific/outside-domain learning, and examined their validity by testing their relationships with incremental/radical creativity. We also tested the cross-level, mitigating effects of team leaders’ emphasis on outputs for the relationships. In another paper (accepted by Journal of Management), we developed a feedback-seeking typology and examined the relationships of four types of employee feedback seeking behaviors with performance and social outcomes. In the third paper (accepted by The International Journal of Human Resource Management), we examined two alternative roles of emotional intelligence (EI) in affecting job insecurity and psychological strain. All the data were collected from organizations in the Chinese contexts. The first three studies, in general, offer practical implications for understanding and managing individual and employee/team learning and the consequences of such learning on employee performance in Chinese organizations. Managers can learn from the first study about why and how they can foster knowledge sharing and innovation in functionally heterogeneous teams. They can learn from the second study a potential dark side of leader motivational intervention in inhibiting the turning of employee learning into creativity. The third study offers practical insights into the specific types of feedback that can help improve employees’ job and social performance. They can learn from the last study how they may help employee buffer their insecurity experience and associated affective reactions in the last study. Objective 3 was under-achieved. We included the variable in various data collection but the results did not support our predictions. We therefore removed it from the final model of the first study. Nevertheless, we will include it in our future research on team innovation.

242012.label: Major findings and research outcome
242012.value: Overall, we found support for the importance of having diverse knowledge within a team or a person to the creation of novel ideas useful for organizations. Specifically, in the study that examines how and when functional diversity relates to team innovation, we collected a time-lagged data from 443 employees working in 96 R&D teams in an IT firm in China. We found that: functional diversity was negatively related to knowledge sharing when affect-based trust in a team was low; this relationship becomes less negative as the level of trust increased; and the relationship was not significant at high level of trust. The findings support our propositions that the knowledge benefits of functional diversity for team innovation cannot be realized without team members’ sharing their own knowledge, and this knowledge sharing mechanism will not work out affect-based trust among team members were low. In the study that examined when employee learning relates to creativity, we collected data from 175 employees in 59 R&D teams from three high-tech firms in China. We found that: outside-domain learning was positively related to both incremental and radical creativity; and these relationships were weaker when team leaders placed greater emphasis on outputs. In Gong, Wang, Huang and Cheung (in press), we collected multiple samples from employees in various organizations in the Chinese contexts. We found that: there are four distinct types of feedback seeking behaviors as derived from goal orientation (GO) theory; a learning GO was positively related to self-negative, self-positive, and other-positive feedback seeking; a performance-approach GO was positively related to self-positive and other-negative feedback seeking.; self-negative feedback seeking was positively related to job performance, role clarity, and social integration; self-positive feedback seeking was negatively related, whereas other-positive feedback seeking was positively related to job performance. We also collected a sample of 378 employees from six companies in China to further establish evidence for the convergent and discriminant validity of the four types of feedback-seeking behaviors. These results were not reported in the manuscript due to space limitation. In Cheung, Gong and Huang (in press), we examined the effects of EI on job insecurity and psychological strain. The findings based on a time-lagged data from 232 real estate agents from a Taiwanese company showed that: EI reduces perceived job insecurity and subsequent psychological strain; and the positive relationship between perceived job insecurity and psychological strain to be stronger when EI was higher.

242012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
242012.value: Through the studies, we have accumulated evidence for the importance of learning-related behaviors at the individual and team levels for fostering individual and team performance. In future research, we will continue to examine the effects of other types of diversity on innovative performance and the influence mechanisms. Because research on the boundary conditions for the diversity effects has focused primarily on the cognitive factors, we can continue to investigate the effects of other affective boundary conditions in order to provide a complete picture of when the diversity effects will work out for team innovative performance through the knowledge sharing mechanism. We did not achieve the objective of understanding the process linking support for innovation and innovation in teams. In future study, we will continue this line of investigation by examining other team cognitive processes. In a currently ongoing project, we are examining a social information processing model that unfolds the relationship between voice behaviors, support for innovation and innovation in teams.

242012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
242012.value: Our major findings in this project are, first, when team members with different functional backgrounds do not trust their peer members, they would hoard their unique knowledge. The innovative performance of the team will suffer. Functionally diverse members will engage in more knowledge sharing when they have stronger emotional bonds with their peer members. Second, employees’ learning in areas outside their own specialty area facilitates their production of incremental and groundbreaking ideas. Managers’ strong emphasis on the production of novel ideas, however, will harm the effects of such learning. Mangers should encourage employees to diversify their areas of knowledge, while avoid creating strong output pressure. Third, employees may seek different types of feedback due to their tendency to focus on competence development or gaining a favorable performance evaluation. Managers should understand employees’ goal tendency. They should also encourage employees to seek self-focused negative feedback and other-focused positive feedback, because the information will facilitate employees’ understanding of work roles and job/social performance. Finally, employees with higher levels of emotional intelligence will perceive less job insecurity and thus experience less emotional adverse reactions. To protect employees against workplace stress, organizations should develop their ability to recognize and manage emotions.

242312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
242312.value: Job stress is a pervasive, costly, and well-known problem facing the hospitality industry in Hong Kong. Prolonged job stress is not only harmful to the well-being of employees but it also adversely affects the operational efficiency, performance, and reputation of organizations (Alarcon, 2011; Karatepe & Aleshinloye, 2009; de Croon, Broersen, Blonk, Frings-Dresen, 2004; Noone, 2008). Poor customer service quality is a particularly harmful side effect of excessive job stress. Left unchecked it can damage the long-term viability of an organization or an entire industry, particularly the Hong Kong hospitality industry which is heavily reliant on the service excellence of its front-line operatives to compete against a growing number of regional rivals. In the proposed study, we draw on job demands-control (J-DC) theory to develop and test a new conceptual model that is relevant and applicable to advancing our understanding of the job demand-job stress-customer service excellence relationship for front-line service operatives in the hospitality industry. By incorporating relevant social aspects of job demands (i.e., customer variability and colleague task interdependence) with other important content- and contextual- resource dimensions (e.g., service discretion, HRM practices, and service customization), which until now have been absent, we intend to offer new and important insights to theory and provide a guiding framework for scholars and managers alike that can be used to help alleviate job stress and ultimately enhance customer service excellence in the hospitality setting. By employing a robust research design, such an advancement in the theory and empirical work has the potential to not only pave the way for future research in this important domain of hospitality scholarship but also offer important implications and lessons to practice that aim to enhance the competitiveness and sustainability of one of Hong Kong’s pillar industries – the hospitality industry. 眾所周知，工作壓力是香港酒店業的一個普遍和代價高昂的問題。長期的工作壓力不僅對員工的健康構成損害，也對組織的運作效率、表現及聲譽形成負面影響。劣質的顧客服務質素更是過度工作壓力所引致的一個極壞影響。尤以香港酒店業是依靠前線工作人員的卓越顧客服務質素作為優勢時，若不及早解决這個問題，劣質的顧客服務質素可以破壞一個機構或整個酒店業的前景。在這研究計劃中，我們從"工作要求控制理論"推演出一個新的概念模式，這個模式有助我們理解香港酒店業前線工作人員的工作要求、工作壓力及卓越顧客服務之間的關係。在此以前，學術界一直缺乏結合社交方面的工作要求(例如: 顧客多樣化和員工在工作上的互相依賴)與重要的工作內容及環境因素(例如: 工作自主權、人力資源管理制度和服務的固定模式)兩者的研究。因此我們希望對現有的理論提供嶄新、重要的見解,從而提供一套理論與模式來引導學者及管理人員，以舒緩員工的工作壓力並提高酒店業的卓越顧客服務。本研究旨透過準確的設計，使理論及實證研究不僅在學術領域及未來研究上開闢一條新的道路，更為增強香港支柱產業之一(酒店業)的競爭力和可持續發展提供重要的啟蒙及意義。

242312.label: Realisation of objectives
242312.value: All objectives were fully achieved, as follows: We performed an extensive review of JD-C literature to consolidate our model. Hotels were identified from the Hong Kong Hotel Association’s directory and comparable samples were drawn in terms of hotels' quality (rating) and size (number of rooms and employees). We empirically tested and confirmed our model. Findings revealed that job content factor (high customer demand variability) negatively affected employees' job satisfaction. Building on the notion that social stressors deplete employees’ resources and result in negative attitudes, the findings support the link between job demand variability and job satisfaction, thereby advancing the broader literature on work psychology. Moreover, we found that such effects were attenuated by job contextual factors, i.e., service discretion and supportive human resource practices. That is, the potential negative effects of high job demand variability may be offset if employees are provided with sufficient opportunities for service discretion and with the provision of HRM support. Hence, when employees are provided with resources and support for job content and context, they are more likely to exhibit higher levels of job satisfaction. By integrating socio-psychological characteristics of service work, notably, customer-driven job demand variability and service discretion into the JD-C model, we not only advance the job strain literature but also offer a promising new direction for future research. Such a contribution is important because there has been a tendency in prior job strain research to overlook the influence of job characteristics specific to the customer service setting.

242312.label: Major findings and research outcome
242312.value: This study offers a range of major findings and research outcomes, a selection of which is briefly described as follows: (i) Advances and extends the theoretical and empirical development, robustness, and applicability of the proposed extended JD-C model. By undertaking multiple investigations of the relationships among job characteristics, coping resources, and job outcomes in hospitality organizations, we were able to develop a new, robust, and practice relevant model of value to both scholars and managers alike. (ii) Revealed the impacts of job demand variability on employees' well-being and attitudes. For example, a mismatch between high job service demands, discretion, and HR support may result in stress and reduced job satisfaction. Such findings offer important theoretical advancements and practical lessons beneficial to employee well-being and overall organizational performance. (iii) Identified important moderating factors (e.g., service discretion and HR practices). Such findings are encouraging to organizations since the social and psychological context of the workplace can be influenced more readily than the structural aspects of the job itself. That is, it would be far more difficult to change the nature of customer demands than it would be to change the psychological and social conditions (e.g., giving employees discretion and support) in which duties are performed. Moreover, service quality can be enhanced when employees’ quality of work life is improved. (iv) Identified important lessons for improving job design, work climate, and the occupational health and well-being of employees. Results provide practical and timely lessons and guidance to organizations, especially that prevalence of job stress is widely acknowledged in the hospitality industry (e.g., reduced job strain/turnover, improved employee attitudes). (v) Publications. There are four outputs, as shown below: -Chiang, F., Birtch, T., & Cai, Z. 2014. Cornell Hospitality Quarterly, 55, 398-407. -Birtch, T., Chiang, F., vanEsh, E. forthcoming. A social exchange theory framework for understanding the job characteristics-job outcomes relationship: The mediating role of psychological contract fulfillment, International Journal of Human Resource Management. -Servant leadership on proactive customer service performance (PCSP), paper accepted and presented at SIOP, Hawaii, 2014. -Servant leadership and follower proactive customer service performance: A proactive motivation theory process framework. 242312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
242312.value: The project identified a number of important areas and extensions for further theoretical and empirical testing and development, including: (i) The new model developed can be extended with additional job characteristics, job outcomes, and industry contexts. The PI is currently undertaking such work, as detailed in Part C. (ii) Contextual factors were found to be critical to affecting the effects of job demand variability on employee outcomes. Hence, the impact of other contextual factors (e.g., leadership style, colleague relationships) on job satisfaction should also be explored. The PI has already secured a GRF funding in 2014 to undertake further theoretical and empirical research. (iii) Given the project was conducted in HK, the findings are likely shaped by its Asian context, where many hospitality organizations are characterized by high-power distance cultures and hierarchies with limited employee empowerment. Future investigations could test the model in a different cultural setting.

242312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
242312.value: Findings from this research project are significant and expected to be of considerable value to researchers and practitioners. Prior research has highlighted the deleterious consequences of job factors, such as high job demands, low job control, and low social support, poor relationships, and inferior work conditions. This study incorporates socio-psychological characteristics of service work into the job demands–control (JD-C) model to test the extent to which job demand variability influences front-line hotel employees’ job stress and satisfaction. We further investigate whether job resources and support, in the form of service discretion and HRM practices, help mitigate the potential ill effects of high job demand variability on job satisfaction. Results provide new and important insights that advance our theoretical, empirical, and practical understanding of such relationships. In addition to developing and testing a new and practice relevant JD-C model, the findings also enable companies to develop appropriate measures to better alleviate job stress and other undesirable outcomes. The project represents an important step toward improving employee well-being and occupational health in HK and is anticipated to have a positive long-term social impact.

242912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
242912.value: Shangshu is an important canonical work, reputedly attributed to Confucius, in which the sayings and actions of sage kings in ancient times to the East Zhou Dynasty were recorded. This ancient text was difficult to understand, and suffered various vicissitudes of time. The versions that have survived and were excavated in different times varied, and their authenticity has been controversial. The issue has been much disputed by scholars from the Qing Dynasty to modern times. This project proposes to review the controversies concerning the authenticity of the various versions of the canonical text of Shangshu, taking into consideration the various methods of verification used by critics, and with evidence from more recent excavations and cross-references with other authenticated texts, to engage in this dialogue and posit new insights. 《尚書》是五經中很重要的一部經典，傳說是由孔子選編百篇而成，記載了堯舜禹到東周時的聖賢言行，在古代具有崇高的地位。可是由於時代久遠，非常難懂。有許多學術史的問題，聚訟了很久。其中最重要的一個，就是關於今、古文《尚書》之真偽、年代的問題。 今文《尚書》是指在秦焚書之後，西漢（202BC——9）時伏生傳下的28篇（或說29篇）。古文《尚書》是指在孔子壁中出土的《尚書》，經孔子後人整理，比今文本多出了16篇。但是這16篇沒有專門的解說，沒有獲得朝廷的承認立博士，只在民間流傳，後來散佚。 到晉代（265－420），又出現了一種古文《尚書》，後來被朝廷承認。但是有許多學者懷疑它，清代閻若璩、惠棟等專門作文辨其為偽書，得到公認，稱之為“偽古文《尚書》”。清朝學者遂專門只對今文《尚書》做研究，解決了不少問題。民國時期，胡適提出“東周以上無史論”，讓顧頡剛作文論證今文《尚書》中許多篇章不是實錄，寫作年代比所述事情的年代要晚很多，所述事情不可盡信。但是治甲骨金文的學者如王國維、于省吾、陳夢家則較多堅持今文《尚書》多數為實錄的作品。顧頡剛在晚年研究《尚書》，改變了過去的態度，認為今文《尚書》中很多篇是西周初形成的（仍有少數人堅持這些篇晚出）。一些學者更進一步，認為“偽古文《尚書》”也可信，閻若璩的論證有問題。於是今古文《尚書》的有關問題又進入了紛爭之中。 所幸上世紀七十年代發現的馬王堆帛書，九十年代出土的郭店楚墓戰國竹簡及上海博物館收藏的戰國竹簡，尤其是2008年清華大學藏戰國竹簡的公佈，為我們研究《尚書》今、古文及有關的問題，提供了寶貴的新材料。特別是清華簡中出現了《尹誥》、《說命》，內容與“偽古文《尚書》”不同，可能是真古文；也有與今文《金縢》大同小異的篇章，還有一些與《尚書》、《逸周書》相關的篇章。這些竹簡去孔子及其弟子不遠，對於我們討論今、古文《尚書》的有關問題，具有非常重大的意義。 當前的《尚書》研究，借助竹簡、帛書，取得了很多成果。不過在今、古文《尚書》之真偽、年代這個問題上，有一些學者的結論還有待進一步檢討，因為其判定真偽、年代的標準、方法稍失於簡單，缺乏反省。《尚書》的這個問題已經經歷了兩千多年，勢必要利用新出竹簡、帛書材料，綜合正反兩方面的意見，從源流上進行宏觀的把握和系統的討論，才能得出比較嚴謹的結論。 本研究擬以今、古文《尚書》的真偽、年代問題為目，在兩年的時間裏，在前人的研究基礎上，利用新出土材料，結合傳世文獻，對於有關的問題進行研究。

242912.label: Realisation of objectives
242912.value: 本計畫之課題為「新出簡帛與《尚書》研究」，主要研究對象是新出版之出土簡帛與傳世之《尚書》。以出土簡帛與《尚書》互相配合，研究相關問題。本計畫列有五個目標，總體來說，五個目標都能完成，並達到十分滿意之成果。例如第五個目標是「撰寫若干篇論文，供學術界參考」，兩個計畫參與者共參加了八次國際學術研討會（宗靜航p-i/五次、李銳co-i/三次），每次都有發表論文。以下按每個目標，略作分述。 1，對簡帛文獻中與今古文《尚書》問題相關的內容作出考釋，以作為進一步研究的基礎。 自清華簡發現後，有學者認為應重新審視今傳《古文尚書‧說命》之文本意義，宗靜航（p-i）則據出土竹簡、學者之研究成果，配合個人在《說命》所發現之晚出語言現象，指出《說命》並非先秦典籍之原貌。（參宗靜航︰〈《尚書‧說命》臆說〉，《簡帛‧經典‧古史》，上海古籍出版社，2013年8月，頁411-420。）對於《尚書‧高宗肜日》，李銳（co-i）指出王國維根據甲骨卜辭辭例，反對《尚書‧高宗肜日》為武丁祭商湯的舊說，而肯定金履祥等以此篇為祖庚祭武丁之說，有可疑之處，有待檢驗。（參李銳︰〈由楚簡《鮑叔牙與隰朋之諫》看《尚書‧高宗肜日》〉，《人文中國學報》，第二十期，2014年9月，頁1-14。） 利用簡帛文獻，特別是清華簡，探討今古文《尚書》的源流、篇章時代。 對於今古文《尚書》各篇的成書時代，學者多有留意，惟對今傳《書大序》之研究，則沒有足夠之重視。宗靜航（p-i）在參考學者之研究成果上，配合個人在《書大序》所發現之晚出語言現象，指出《書大序》不可能是西漢孔安國之作。（參宗靜航︰〈從語言角度看孔傳本《書大序》的成書年代〉，《揚州大學學報》（人文社會科學版），第19卷第2期，2015年3月，頁59-64。） 對於清華簡《傅說之命》，李銳（co-i）通過研究清華簡《傅說之命》，證明古文《尚書‧說命》確實不是真正的《尚書‧說命》三篇，而是後人掇拾斷簡殘篇而成的偽作，然而，清華簡《傅說之命》也並不是《書序》所說的《尚書‧說命》三篇。（參李銳︰〈清華簡《傅說之命》研究〉，《深圳大學學報》（人文社會科學版），第30卷第6期，2013年11月，頁68-71。） 與此目標有關之論文還有︰ 宗靜航（p-i）〈從語言角度看漢晉孔氏家學群書〉，《新出土文獻與古書成書問題研究》，中西書局，2015年，頁364-383。 宗靜航（p-i）〈《尚書‧說命》臆說〉，《簡帛‧經典‧古史》，上海古籍出版社，2013年8月，頁411-420。 李銳（co-i）〈由楚簡《鮑叔牙與隰朋之諫》看《尚書‧高宗肜日》〉，《人文中國學報》，第二十期，2014年9月，頁1-14。 3 結合簡帛文獻總結學術界考證今古文《尚書》的研究成果。 由於近年不斷有新出土之簡帛，學者對傳世典籍之成書過程，有了新的看法，認為古書的形成和流傳，大多要經過很長時間，對於偽書的態度也有了改變。傳統認為有成書問題之古文《尚書》、《孔子家語》、《孔叢子》等，有學者提出是「漢魏孔氏家學的產物」，其書不偽。宗靜航（p-i）在參考學者之研究成果上，配合個人在這些「孔氏家學」群書中所發現之晚出語言現象，指出「孔氏家學」群書有不少晚於西漢之語言用例，不應誇大這幾部書對研究先秦史事的價值。（參宗靜航︰〈從語言角度看漢晉孔氏家學群書〉，《新出土文獻與古書成書問題研究》，中西書局，2015年，頁364-383。） 對於《尚書》名稱、《尚書》篇名的問題、《書序》來源等問題，學者有不同的意見。李銳（co-i）利用近年出土的戰國秦漢簡帛，研究相關問題，提出個人的意見。（參李銳︰〈由近年出土文獻論《尚書序》的有關問題〉，《清華簡研究》，第一輯，上海，中西書局，2012年12月，頁364-372。） 與此目標有關之論文還有︰ 李銳（co-i）〈清華簡《傅說之命》研究〉，《深圳大學學報》（人文社會科學版），第30卷第6期，2013年11月，頁68-71。 4 對利用出土材料研究傳世典籍，提出新的研究方法，供學術界參考。 對出土簡帛，學者十分重視，但由於部分簡帛出土過程不詳，所以有學者持懷疑態度。宗靜航（p-i）通過比較《清華簡》（壹）所收九篇竹簡的特殊字形，發現這些「特殊字形」在不同的竹簡中出現，例如「隹」字，共見於九篇竹簡四十九次；「之」字，共見於七篇竹簡七十九次；「我」字，共見於六篇竹簡三十次，「舊」字所從的「隹」字也用「特殊字形」。如果說《清華簡》（壹）是由一個或者幾個後人抄寫偽作的，而又能把各種字形出現的情況，分工安排等處理得如此仔細。如果能夠考慮得這麼小心，安排得這麼慎密，或者就不應該出現某些學者所提出的「晚出」、「無知妄說」等不小心的疑點。所以，《清華簡》不可能是後人的偽作。（參宗靜航︰〈《清華簡》（壹）所見特殊字形及相關問題〉，貴州師範學歷史與政治學院、國際《尚書》學會合辦，「2014年《尚書》與清華簡國際學術研討會」，2014年10月12-15日，11頁。） 對於古書的流傳和形成，李銳（co_i）提出「族本」說，以解決相關問題。李銳指出今傳典籍先秦秦漢時期古書的形成流傳過程，由後世的校勘學所發展出的「祖本」或「底本」、「原本」等觀念，在應用於早期的古書文本時，或許應該適當地變一變。是否可以說在最初出現的反映一個人思想的言論，此是思想的起源（但是這個起源也有歷時性差別，有因環境、對象等所致的早期語與後期言的不同）。思想、言論由於記載、引用、篇章別行、乃至前後期寫作不同，口傳到記錄的歷時差別，複述時差舛，而形成了諸多彼此主題思想、主體內容相似的「族本」系統，這是文本的源頭。這些「族本」之間不僅存在交叉重疊的相似性關聯，而且存在一些共同性的本質特徵。（參李銳︰〈從出土文獻談古書形成過程中的「族本」》，《新出土文獻與古書成書問題研究》，中西書局，2015年，頁107-120。） 5 就上述研究，撰寫若干篇論文，供學術界參考。 兩個計畫參與者共參加了八次國際學術研討會（宗靜航p-i/五次、李銳co-i/三次），每次都有發表論文。兩人也分別在不同的學報刊物發表了論文，請參相關欄目。

242912.label: Major findings and research outcome
242912.value: 由於近年不斷有先秦簡帛出土，學者在研究這些材料後，對傳世典籍之流傳、形成等問題，有了與以往不同之看法和態度。對傳統認為有成書問題之書籍，甚或認為並非偽作。兩個計畫參與者在利用出土簡帛和傳世典籍作研究後，指出對傳統認為有成書問題之書籍，仍然應以謹慎態度看待。例如古文《尚書》、《書大序》、《孔傳》、《孔子家語》、《孔叢子》等有成書問題之書籍，近年有學者認為都沒有真偽問題，稱之為「孔氏家學」群書，並以之研究相關問題。宗靜航（p-i）在參考出土簡帛、學者研究成果之基礎上，並配合個人發現這些書籍中之晚出語言現象，指出有關書籍並不可能反映先秦西漢時期之語言面貌，在使時不應誇大其價值。 誠如以上所述，由於先秦簡帛之出土，學者對古書流傳、形成等問題，有了新的看法。但是，對於有相同、相近或相關內容之各種典籍間之關係等問題，學者仍然眾說紛紜。李銳（co-i）在綜合相關材料和學者研究成果後，提出「族本」說，以解決相關問題，或可為學術界提供新的研究角度。

242912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
242912.value: 近年先秦簡帛之出土，幾乎從沒間斷，已經出土之簡帛，部分仍然沒有全數發表，例如清華簡。所以，就如本計畫課題「新出簡帛與《尚書》研究」，利用新出簡帛與傳世典籍互相配合作研究，是有需要繼續的。除了利用簡帛考釋、研究古書之字詞、成書等問題外，亦可利用簡帛直接研究先秦時期之語言面貌，和與傳世典籍比較，以研究由先秦到後世語言改變之情況。

242912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
242912.value: 出土之先秦簡帛，是前人所未見的，現在我們有幸看見，應善加使用來研究我國古代的思想、語言、文化等問題。《尚書》是我國儒家的重要典籍，近年出土的先秦簡帛，其中有與《尚書》相關的材料，正好用來研究相關問題。本計畫利用出土簡帛、參考學者研究成果，和在計畫參與者的努力下，對相關簡帛、古書流傳、語言現象、成書問題等，都作了研究。

243212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
243212.value: 三位一體作品：音樂創作中的大量複製與定相之研究

243212.label: Project Objectives
243212.value: Research into the effects of sound diffusion and filtering on massively replicated and phase-shifted music. The exploration and refinement of new compositional techniques of massive replication and phase-shifting involved in the creation and structuring of musical texture and timbre. Creation of a portfolio of original compositions, utilizing massive replication (in the tens of thousands to millions) and microsecond phase shifting of 5-10 minute spans of music composed specifically for that purpose. The realization and digital formatting for dissemination via public performance, broadcast, and recording of that portfolio of compositions. Published papers and conference presentations of these new works and the compositional techniques involved in their creation.

243212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
243212.value: This proposal is a project that involves the creation of a series of musical works, arranged in groups of three, developing a single compositional concept. Each triptych of pieces will consist of one work for either a single acoustic instrument or a small group of acoustic instruments, a second piece for fixed media based on digital manipulations of the first work, and a final piece that is based on further manipulations of the previous two works and combines pre-recorded sound with the live acoustic instrument(s) featured in the first. The specific research component of the project involves overcoming problems of acoustic masking and other digital artifacts that arise from the particular compositional process employed, as well as solving aesthetic issues to create aesthetically significant works. Innovations in the creating of this series involve the development of compositional techniques with the goals of a) creating multi-functioning material that will stand alone (in the first piece of each triptych) and at the same time yield useful material when digitally manipulated via replication and phase-shifting; b) developing new formal structures within the individual pieces, within the triptych of works, and among the collection as a whole; c) developing new methods of digital manipulations with which to control the original material. The outcome will consist of a) a body of new compositional techniques, b) a portfolio of new compositions, and c) 'products' in the form of public concerts, a radio broadcast and recording of these new works. PI is an established composer with over thirty years of experience;PI has composed numerous compositions for acoustic and electronic media, and has several pieces commercially published or recorded. Please note that the GRF has "no restriction on the type of research proposals" and that a project like this one, incorporating creative work and not limited to traditional research, is specifically considered fundable by the RGC as affirmed by the RGC's secretary Kesson Lee. 這是一個有關創作一系列以三個為一組的音樂作品而發展單一創作理念的計劃。作品會以三個三位一體的樂曲（Triptych）組成，第一首作品會以單一樂器或一小組的真聲樂器演奏；第二首為固定媒體之創作，以第一首的素材來加以數碼操作而成；第三首把前兩部作品作進一步的數碼操作，把預先錄製的聲音和第一首之現場真聲樂器的演出相結合。具體的研究項目組成部分包括：克服聲音掩蔽技術和從數碼加工之創作過程中所產生的困難，以致解決美學問題，創造出更富美感的作品。 這一系列之作品所帶出之創新，包括以下作曲技巧之伸延與發展：一）建立可獨立存在的多功能素材（於三組中的第一組作品），其同時也可透過數碼操作，通過複製或移位的處理產生更多可活用的素材；二）從這獨立的作品，三位一體的作品及一整套的作品開發新的曲式結構；三）開發新的數碼操作方法來調控原有的素材。 其成果包括：一）一系列新的作曲技術；二）一組新的作品；三）以公開音樂會，電台廣播和錄音形式把這些作品呈現。首席研究員是一個擁有超過三十年經驗的作曲家，他創作大量真聲和電子媒體作品，部份作品曾作商業出版及錄音。

243212.label: Realisation of objectives
243212.value: This project involved the development of certain techniques of music composition and their employment in a portfolio of 9 new pieces as three sets of three pieces each, the dissemination of those compositions and the publication of a paper on those techniques. All of the objectives have been attained. The project has been extraordinarily successful. The music portfolio created exceeded the initial proposal—10 new pieces were created using the technique (the additional piece did not require funding from this GRF). The compositions (all publicly presented) are: Triptych I 1. Toccata 2. Wooden Rain 3. Beyond Reality among the empty places (Triptych II) 1. distance 2. greater than 3. “…the liquid mountains of the sky…” Caves of Dunhuang (Triptych III) 1. madhyamāpratipad (the middle way) 2. śūnyatā (emptiness 3. vijñāna-santāna (rebirth) More Moro Lasso Loops Additionally, a published paper and presented at the International Computer Music Conference: The Sky’s the Limit: Composition with Massive Replication and Time-shifting Realisation of Objectives Meeting objective 2 (The exploration and refinement of new compositional techniques of massive replication and phase-shifting involved in the creation and structuring of musical texture and timbre.) began with composing separate acoustic pieces for harp; marimba and almglocken (tuned cowbells); trombone quartet; and a mixed ensemble of erhu, cello, xiao/dizi, clarinet/bass clarinet, yang-qin, and harpsichord. The instrumentation of these works differed from the original proposal because in the time between submitting the proposal and beginning the project, several key musicians had unexpectedly left Hong Kong. This caused a substantial delay and was the entire reason for the required extension and the unsatisfactory mid-project report. Nonetheless, new instrumentation was created that fulfilled the technical requirements of the proposal; that there be: different methods of activating the instruments (resulting in substantially different attack transients); instruments with both short and long decays: and both harmonic and melodic instruments. The acoustic music composed for these instruments also demonstrated the variety called for in the proposal—some traditionally tonal, some pandiatonic, some entirely atonal, some pentatonic. Various styles/techniques of music were employed, from minimalism/process music to aleatory. The music was shaped into three pieces—the projected first piece of each of the three triptychs. Having composed this music, it was then rehearsed and recorded by professional musicians in HKBU’s Laboratory for Immersive Arts and Technology (LIATe). The next step in meeting the objective was to experiment with massive replication and time-shifting. Initially the two parameters most significant were the number of replications (into the millions) and the amount of time-shift of those replications (from fractions of a single sound wave period to entire seconds). The variations of these parameters were directly tied to the nature of the attack transient and the desired outcome. For example, when replicating the harp, with its rather sharp attack transient but moderate decay, microsecond time-shifts blended the multiple attacks into a single attack and the interference of the sound waves often lessened the sharpness of the attack, resulting in an organ-like sound. To a certain point (generally not beyond the tens of thousands), increasing the number of replications enhances this effect. If longer time shifts are employed (approximately tenths of a second or longer), the opposite effect occurs. The resultant sound has multiple recognisable attacks and becomes more percussive. As replication increases into the hundreds of thousands and beyond, interference, sum and difference tones, and digital artefacts increasingly distort the sound; furthermore, gain must be continually lowered to avoid feedback. These highly distorted sounds have their own aesthetic use upon occasion but have lost all recognisable connection with the original source sound, a connection that was, for the most part, considered aesthetically desirable. Following this initial experimentation, PI revised the acoustic compositions to allow for further experimentation with the factors mentioned above, and returned to experimentation with the digital recordings. Additional parameters for variation were introduced, including spatial placement of the individual replications, and filtering, as described in Objective 1. The tendency of excessive filtering to completely distort and mask a complex sound was recognised and at odds with the desired aesthetic, so filtering was used very sparingly and only on those very high replications—hundreds of thousands or more. At this point the original, acoustic first movements of Triptych 1 and 3 were complete (these happened in sequence, not simultaneously). The fixed-media second movements were created via manipulation of the experimental results, as well as the third movements, employing fixed-media and acoustic instruments simultaneously. In these movements, sound diffusion experimentation was carried out to prevent excessive auditory masking. Versions of the fixed media portions of the project were created with a stereo mix, a 4-channel mix, an 8-channel mix, and in one case a 96-channel mix, in another a 128 channel mix. These final, massively multichannel versions may be considered world-leading, as they were created for a unique facility at Virginia Tech, the CUBE, one of only about 4 institutions with similar facilities, and both works were selected through a refereed process for inclusion in CUBEfest 2016 and 2017, a highly competitive music festival for massively multichannel music. Triptych 2 followed a less anticipated path from inception to creation. Although PI had originally intended it for saxophone quartet, the leader of the group it was to be composed for left Hong Kong and the group disbanded. A trombone quartet was substituted and music rewritten and composed. Simultaneously the other Triptychs had progressed much more quickly, and an aesthetic problem of structure revealed itself—the proposed design of the three Triptychs was identical, with a first movement for acoustic instruments only, a second movement for fixed media only, and a third movement combining the two, and all employing at least some of the same material. Rather than repeat the process again, PI re-conceived Triptych 2 as a piece entirely for fixed media, and employing different source material for each movement. The new source material was, as follows: for the first movement, a recording of a Uyghur folk song with voice and dutar; for the second movement, unused material from Triptych 1 and 3; and for the third movement, harp music that had been composed and recorded for the initial proposed (but unused) first triptych. This Triptych 2 (actually the final completed one) employed and extended the techniques of massive replication and time-shifting; but to a far wider variety of material. Consequentially, Triptych 2 is the longest of the three, and from PI’s aesthetic, the most successful. With the completion of Triptych 2, all of the proposed compositional portfolio was complete and Objective 4 met, but an additional work (More Moro Lasso Loops) exploring the same techniques but in a much more complex way, was also created and has been successfully presented in its original fixed audio form, and with a video by Hong Kong visual artist Jamsen Law. The pieces in the portfolio have been widely disseminated in the US, Europe and Southeast Asia. Additionally, a commercially available CD featuring two of the Triptychs, from Ablaze Records, is in production. Objective 5, paper publication concerning the techniques employed, was met with the presentation and publication (in refereed proceedings) of The Sky’s the Limit: Composition with Massive Replication and Time-shifting at the 2016 42nd International Computer Music Conference in Utrecht, Netherlands.

243212.label: Major findings and research outcome
243212.value: A new technique for composing music was created based on technology only recently available. “Massive replication and time –shifting” involves recording acoustic instruments or voices and making many digital copies of those recordings. The number of copies varies greatly according to the desired outcome, but ranges between 16 and over 2 million copies. (Experimentation pushed the number of copies to over 10 million, but this was found to be not very useful aesthetically nor very practical. The resultant sound was so highly distorted that it bore no recognisable relationship to the original, and there are far easier ways to make similar sounds with modern synthesis techniques.) These digital copies must then be time-shifted by various amounts, and experimentation demonstrated that nature of the attack transient of the original recording directly affected the amount of time-shifting needed to create particular desired aesthetic outcomes. While creating massive replications, one must ‘mix down’ to manageable numbers—no commercially available software could handle 2 million channels of audio. Mixing down creates problems of gain and feedback, which experimentation demonstrated are largely solvable with a judicious use of filtering and sonicization through multi-channel playback. PI demonstrated the effectiveness of the technique at a music festival held at Virginia Tech’s CUBE, a unique facility with 128 channel playback. The ultimate goal of the project, however, was not merely the development of a new compositional technique, but also its successful deployment in a portfolio of music compositions. 10 new works were composed and one adapted into a music video. The proof of the success of the technique can be found in the fact that within a year of their composition, every piece had been professionally and publicly premiered at locations throughout the US, Europe and Southeast Asia. Some of the pieces received additional performances or are scheduled for additional performances, and a CD of 7 of the works is in production and will be out in August. In total, pieces composed for this project were featured on 11 different concerts (some concerts featured more than one piece); of those concerts all but two were refereed. The work was presented at the following International or National conferences/festivals: the International Computer Music Conference (Utrecht, Netherlands), the Society for Electro-Acoustic Music in the United States National Conference 2016, CUBEfest 2016 and 2017 (Virginia Tech), Art and Science Days (Bourges, France), and Electronic Music Midwest 2015 and 2016.

243212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
243212.value: PI is preparing another paper to submit to the International Computer Music Conference 2017 in Shanghai. A CD is in production and will be out in August. The technique has proven to be extremely rich with potential to create a new genre of music. The Triptych structure, however, has shown itself to be unnecessarily restrictive. New works can explore the same variety of textures (acoustic instruments, fixed media, and a combination of both) without segregating each texture into an individual movement or piece. Other avenues for development lie in exploring a variety of instrumental or vocal timbres within a single piece. Caves of Dunhuang (Triptych III), with its combination of Chinese and Western instruments, was particularly successful in this aspect, and was well regarded by audiences for exploiting this rich potential. Other non-Western instruments can be recorded and combined with either or both Chinese and Western instruments. PI is currently planning experimentation with the Indian sitar, Thai gongs, Chinese Guzheng and Guqin in combination with various Western instruments.

243212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
243212.value: This project developed a newly created technique of music composition available only with the advent of current technology, both hardware and software. Using this technique, a series of 10 new compositions were created, each exploring a different aspect of the technique. The compositions have been performed extensively in both the US and Europe, with additional performances in Hong Kong—in fact they have been featured on 11 concerts (multiple pieces on some concerts) in different cities, and in 7 different festivals/conferences. A CD is being produced that will further disseminate the music and its generating technique; this is planned to be released in August. The extensive performance history, at prestigious venues on refereed or curated concerts and with a great deal of audience appreciation, is a testimony to the success of the ideas fostered with this grant. Further dissemination will likely lead to a greater adoption of the techniques by other composers.

243312.value: 此研究將探討和比较香港和新加坡的青少年在校内和校外參與使用新媒體的模式以及对培养其新读写能力的影响。基於读写能力的培养需根植于社會行为的理論（Street，1993），本研究将使我们认识到青少年使用新媒體的行为及孕育而生的新读写能力。本研究將分隔電子科技與新读写能力两个概念，重點不在於技術層面，而在於新媒體和读写能力的交集。 這項研究提出了三個問題： （一）不同性別,種族，文化，社會經濟和語言群體的青少年在接触運用新媒體的範圍、頻率和強度有何区别？ （二）新媒體的使用是否需要新的读写能力？他們有什麼特點；對學校的教學方法有何启示？ （三）青少年在校内運用新媒體的模式,範圍、頻率和強度如何？同校外使用新媒體的模式有何不同? 次研究的设计将遵照以下三個步驟: （一）接触和使用新媒體行为模式的實證比較 （二）对新读写能力进行仔细的質性记录和分析以展示新读写行为; （三）從（一）和(二) 得到的結果建設一個概念模型，从而找出一些培养读写能力教学法的原理和启示。

243312.label: Realisation of objectives
243312.value: In order to provide a comprehensive and comparative archive of HK young students’ engagement with new media (Objective 1), we first strived to recruit schools and students across Hong Kong through stratified random sampling in an effort to locate schools in various districts, school bandings, and school types. Eventually, we managed to recruit six secondary schools in Hong Kong including three aided schools, one government school, one private school and one international school. Meanwhile, we deliberately located two schools with ethic minority students (one private and the other aided school) to make sure comparisons could be made across linguistically diverse groups. Three secondary schools in Mainland China were recruited later and joined the study. Second, on account that questionnaire is an important instrument to collect data on students’ digital engagement and practice, great efforts were made to develop a questionnaire that include over 60 questions covering the following eight areas: (1) students’ demographic data; (2) general use of digital devices; (3) use of mobile phone; (4) communication with digital devices; (5) language uses related to digital devices; (6) creation and sharing; (7) gaming and virtual communities; (8) use of technologies for learning purposes. This questionnaire aimed to provide detailed and comprehensive information about students’ overall engagement with digital devices. Eventually, we gathered a total of 2183 questionnaire responses from the nine participating schools. The analysis of the questionnaire data has revealed the patterns, nature, and characteristics of young students’ new media engagement. The second and three stages of data collection included focus group interviews and individual case studies that aimed to get richer and more in-depth data regarding students’ digital literacy practices (Objective 2), and new media incorporation inside schools (Objective 3). In total, 93 students were interviewed in 33 groups (17 groups in Hong Kong, 16 groups in Mainland China). The interviews lasted about an hour for each session. A total number of 24 students (13 in Hong Kong and 11 in Mainland China) also participated in individual case studies. The participants were purposefully selected based on their gender, age, and levels of engagement with various digital technologies outside school. For each case study participants, we conducted individual interviews for about one hour. Each student also kept log of their use of technologies for seven days. With their consent, their activities online (e.g. blogs, interaction on social networking websites) were monitored and related online artefacts were recorded and analyzed. The interviews as well as case studies provided vivid and rich data on students’ new media practices (e.g. what digital tools were used? when and why?). The objective 3 and 4 for the current study warrant comparative and holistic stances that looked into students’ digital engagement in- and out-of-school in an effort to discern the possible gap and explore ways to bridge the gaps. In other words, we sought to compare secondary school students’ engagement with digital devices - mobile phone and computer - for personal and school-related purposes. In terms of technology use for learning purposes outside school, we probed into how students used technologies for searching for information, doing group work, and problem-solving when doing homework. To collect data on their use of technologies inside schools, we visited each participating school, conducted class observation, and had informal interviews with teachers and staffs. We also conducted observation at some places where students had access to computers and technological tools on their own such as computer labs, library. The results show that on the whole, there are noted differences between digital engagement (using mobile phones and computers) for school-related work on the one hand and for personal use and social life on the other. However, there is evidence that digital technologies play an increasingly important role in the learning-related activities. The case studies data also shed lights on how students’ out-of-school digital practices were connected with their formal learning at schools. On the basis of the empirical data, a model of informal learning supported by digital technologies outside school was constructed that highlighted dimensions of information consumption, interaction and participation, sharing and production, and problem-solving. Students’ out-of-school digital practices are contextualized in a social environment, and connected to school-based learning. We have found clear evidence of “connected learning” that is socially embedded, interest-driven, and oriented toward educational purposes. It was further denoted that extra-curricular activities could bridge students’ in- and out-of-school practices. There are also indications that teachers could play a guiding and supportive role in bringing together interest-based and school-based learning. Specific implications of the findings of the study for pedagogy, teaching, and practices are laid out as well. We believe that the insights gleaned from the study could contribute to a vital discussion on how to connect in- and out of school practices and how to better harness the power of digital technologies to enhance students’ learning. Reflecting back on the journey of this study, there are several major challenges including recruiting participating schools and changes of investigators. Our initial plan was to recruit schools in Hong Kong according to stratified random sampling method. Participating schools would be randomly selected based on the districts, school bandings, and school types. However, we only recruited three schools through this process. Eventually, three additional schools were recruited through researchers’ personal connections. Originally, the study also sought to collect data from secondary schools in Singapore since one of the Co-I started to work in Singapore. However, after almost a year, there was no progress made by the Co-I located at the Singapore. We had to change the research site to Mainland China and managed to recruit three secondary schools there. Another even bigger challenge was that the original primary investigator, Dr. Jan Connelly, retired half way through the project. The Co-I, Dr. Liping Deng, had to take the role as PI. Great efforts were made to maintain the scale, direction, and objectives of the research.

243312.label: Major findings and research outcome
243312.value: This study, first and foremost, depicted the prevalence of digital technologies in the life of secondary school students in both Hong Kong and mainland China. Smart phones have been widely adopted and applied for communication, social networking, and entertainment. Second, there has been increasing evidence for the use of digital technologies (e.g. instant messaging, Facebook) for learning purposes such as discussing homework, seeking help, and facilitating group work. Arguably, the use of digital technologies for learning might not be as frequently and extensively as for personal and social purposes. Still, the study indicated that the importance of social networking websites for learning is on the rise. Third, through the comparisons of students’ digital engagements across a range of factors (e.g. gender, age, ethnic backgrounds), age appeared to be a major indicator of difference. Especially, senior students were more likely to employ digital tools for learning purposes. Some gender differences were shown such as boys were more engaged in gaming activities and girls were more avid users of social networking sites. Most of these findings are reported in the conference proceeding titled “Exploring Hong Kong Youth’s engagement with digital technologies outside school”. That paper has won the best paper award of HKAECT 2014 International Conference. In addition to giving descriptive and comparative accounts of the digital engagements of youngster in both Hong Kong and mainland China, the present study also explored informal learning afforded by technological tools and sought to reveal the connection between the informal and formal learning inside school. A model of informal learning been generated that included four dimensions – information consumption, interaction and participation, sharing and production, and problem-solving. Additionally, the qualitative data also provide rich and detailed information on how students employed various digital technologies for each dimension in their pursuit of informal learning. Such interest-driven learning, to a certain extent, facilitated extra-curricular activities and complemented formal in-school learning. It was suggested that extra-curricular activities can bridge students’ in- and out-of-school practices and teachers might play an important role in the process. Most findings in the aspect are reported in the journal paper titled “Interest-driven digital practices of secondary students: Cases of connected learning”.

243312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
243312.value: There are several directions for further development based on the present study. First, research efforts can be made to construct statistical model that could predict the factors that determine students’ digital engagements both inside and outside schools. Second, based on the insights gleaned from the current study, more exploratory and/or experimental studies could be conducted to evaluate the guidance and recommendations arising from the study in the real school contexts. Indeed, more research endeavors are needed to seek ways to bridge the gaps between students’ digital practice in- and out-of school. The third area that will warrant research attention is close studies on how to better incorporate new literacies into school curricula and practices.

243312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
243312.value: The current study has examined the new literacy practice of secondary school students outside school and the impact of such practice on their learning in-school. The researchers collected both quantitative and qualitative data from six secondary schools in Hong Kong and three secondary schools in Mainland China. The results has depicted a wide arrange of new literacy practices the students were engaged in outside school contexts. Comparison has been drawn among the different types of schools (e.g. aided school, government school, international school) and students characteristics (e.g. gender, grade, ethnic backgrounds). More importantly, empirical evidence has been found between the connection of students’ digital practice outside school and their learning inside school. The findings have contributed to much-needed areas for research that focus on whether and how digital practices and informal learning outside schools are connected with school-based learning. This study not only informs teachers, researchers, and practitioners of students’ digital practices, but also offers specific guidelines and recommendations for creating synergies between formal and informal learning mediated by technologies.

244212.label: Major findings and research outcome
244212.value: Findings of this project, some of which still unfolding, cover five major areas: 1) Hong Kong local press personality identified through placement of newspapers on a coordinate of ideology and professionalism and research results show that pro-establishment press is more professional in coverage at the superficial level of accuracy and factual account, but lower in professionalism in terms of power supervision than their counterpart in mass-appeal and elitist groups; 2) Newsroom creativity by journalists is more likely to take place when the innovative practice conforms with existing editorial policy in Hong Kong, but the opposite is true for press in the mainland; 3) Differential coverage of community conflict by local press reveals a pattern whereby conservative press dwells on the negative effect on economy while liberal newspapers emphasize freedom, civil liberties, and democratic processes, showing a parallel-path form of argument; 4) The irrational base of media credibility as public perceptions is demonstrated by the (un-primed) dormancy of the concept of credibility in the public mind and peripheral status it receives even when primed; and 5) Audience evaluation of local press performance has followed the expected route mapped out by the uses and gratifications theory, although some departures are noted.

244212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
244212.value: We have made plans to introduce a new theoretical perspective, Construal Level Theory, as an elaboration of our model of analysis. We are also brainstorming on other possible directions of extension and expansion of the research results.

244212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
244212.value: Our research has yielded several interesting and perhaps surprising findings. Contrary to what most people believe, we found: 1) many local people regularly read newspapers they do not believe to be the most credible, which means that people do not simply read newspapers for information; 2) Hong Kong reporters are more likely to be creative in their daily routine work when their practice is consistent with the editorial policy whereas the opposite is true in mainland; 3) mass appeal and liberal press in Hong Kong pays more attention to supervise power and yet scores lower in accuracy, balance, and other aspects of media professionalism; 4) some people choose newspapers because they agree with or like the issue positions of the newspapers; some choose newspapers because the papers provide entertainment and fun; and still others choose newspapers because of pressure from people in their social network.
