249612.label: Major findings and research outcome
249612.value: Our findings demonstrate that judicial cases are important sources for the investigation of the Chinese local societies in the Ming-Qing periods. The judges’ rulings in these judicial disputes vividly expose the private spheres of the Ming people, such as the toilet, the brothel and the inner chambers of households. In addition, the findings illustrate the risks involved in the waterborne activities of the merchants, sailors and villagers of the coastal areas in late Ming China. As reflected by the late Ming case reports, the institutional protections for commercial activities and long distant transportation were inadequate in the flourishing economy of early 17th century China. In the field of legal history, the late Ming cases powerfully illustrate the functioning of the local judiciary. As early as the mid-16th century, the famous Prime Minister Zhang Juzheng (1525-82) pointed out that the root of banditry was the corruption of officials and their subordinates. Our research on late Ming prisons and the use of judicial torture shows that the problem of corruption significantly undermined the efficiency of the judicial system at the provincial level, and lead to many cases of injustice. However, our findings also demonstrated that institutional and cultural factors contributed to this bad judicial management. For example, the serious punishment of policemen who wrongly arrested normal people forced them to apply a wide variety of lawful and unlawful tortures to guarantee confessions. Also, the late Ming public generally favoured confessions made under torture, and sometimes even asked the judge to apply such bloody methods. Moreover, the complicated reviewing system within the provincial government, which aimed at eliminating injustice, created the opposite and unexpected problem of arrested people staying in jail for excessively long periods, sometimes decades, while waiting for a final verdict. The prolonged period of imprisonment in the filthy jails killed many people, both innocent and guilty.

249612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
249612.value: In addition to building a comprehensive electronic database of judicial cases in the near future, we plan to use the abundant information contained in the late Ming casebooks to pursue new research topics, such as the situation of wandering beggars and other vulnerable groups, the privileges of youths at court, the struggles of clerks and yamen runners in local offices, the methods for selecting sub-officials in county administration offices, the application of forensic science in criminal investigations, the role and challenges of popular and foreign religions in local society. Further funding is needed to continue the unfinished and expanding research objectives of the current project. In 2014, the Principal Investigator sought the support of the RGC through the Early Career Scheme for a related project investigating judicial and social development during the Ming-Qing Transition. Fortunately, that project ‘The Ming-Qing Transition (1619-1740): A reassessment from the legal angle’ received support from the Early Career Award. This funding will allow the Principal Investigator to complete the unfinished research and to apply the findings and methodologies developed in the late Ming project to materials from the early Qing period.

249612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
249612.value: This project investigated Chinese judicial cases from the early 17th century for two reasons. First, it used the cases as social historical sources to examine the authentic struggles and life conditions of the common people in maritime South China. The judicial cases illustrate the daily risks faced by mariners, merchants and policemen, disputes over toilets and some issues concerning the coastal defences and management of foreigners in this region. Second, the study used authentic records of judicial disputes to evaluate the late Ming judicial system. The role of the Ming prefectural judge was thoroughly investigated for the first time. The prolonged reviewing procedures of cases and the prisons of the local government and their fact-finding methods, particularly their use of judicial torture, were full of faults. In sum, the practices of the real world provincial judiciary in the cases were quite different from the prescriptive rules and institutions established in the early Ming period. Another contribution of the project was the building of a framework for an electronic database of all of the casebooks from Ming-Qing China (1368-1911). This database will convert the qualitative facts of each case into quantitative information that can be used for further spatial and judicial analysis.

249612.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
249612.value: In late 2012, as a Chinese legal historian with strong background of the Geographical Information System (The PI worked as the researcher of two historical GIS projects on the cotton cloth industry of the Ming and Qing Shanghai region organized by Professor Kee-long Billy So in 2002-04 and 2007-10, respectively. For details, please see the website of these projects: http://www.iseis.cuhk.edu.hk/songjiang/), the Principal Investigator was invited by the French Sinologists Jérôme Bourgon and Luca Gabbiani to join as a core player in their research project “Legalizing Space in China” funded by the French Agence Nationale de la Recherche that attempts to translate all available Ming and Qing codes into English and French, and to create a historical GIS on legal codes, regulations and exemplary cases from the Qing that would facilitate spatial analysis of legal development during the Ming-Qing periods (1368-1911; please see the project website: http://lsc.chineselegalculture.org/). He worked with them in the capacity of a visiting scholar at the Ecole Normale Supérieure (ENS) de Lyon from May to July 2013. Thanks to the strong supports of the project's international team of Ming-Qing legal historians, he contributed to the creation of a data analysis framework for the Historical GIS for both the French-based Qing project “Legalizing Space in China”, as well as our current GRF project on the Ming judicial cases. This thoughtful framework is a collective achievement for exploitation of meaningful information from all judicial cases from the Ming and Qing periods for spatial, philological and jurisprudential analysis. By collaborating with my French colleagues, in terms of budget and human resources, it is more feasible to build a database of judicial cases of late Imperial China in the near future. If copyright issues can be cleared and further funding secured by our joint efforts, the new database of Ming-Qing judicial cases would soon be opened to Chinese historians and even the general public to access. Supported by the powerful searching and pictorial displaying functions of the GIS, all sorts of judicial cases are promised to be well-categorized and every single term in the casebooks could be quickly located and compared. It should provide a solid foundation for a new high level of researches on Chinese legal history.

250012.label: Project Title(Chinese)
250012.value: 反思香港的高密度發展：空間製造、空間（不）公義及日常生活

250012.label: Co - Investigator(s)
250012.value: Dr Lee, Wai-ying Prof Smart, Alan

250012.label: Project Objectives
250012.value: Build on the existing debates to develop a process understanding of high-density development unique to the socio-historical setting of Hong Kong; Write a history of high-density development in Hong Kong since the 1950s and enumerate the possible social consequences, with respect to the development over time from home for shelter to house as commodity; Concretise these rhythms in the local district of Sham Shui Po, by outlining its historical geography and possible contradictions, with the objective of clarifying the role of space in producing social injustice; Investigate the ways individuals residents in the district have been affected by the process of producing social (in)justice, with the objective of evaluating the role of agency; Synthesise the findings at the individual level with those at the district and territory levels within the scalar problematic; and Contribute to the compact city, social justice and spatiality debates and the research methodology of spatial story based on the Hong Kong experience.

Write a history of high-density development in Hong Kong since the 1950s and enumerate the possible social consequences, with respect to the development over time from home for shelter to house as commodity;

Concretise these rhythms in the local district of Sham Shui Po, by outlining its historical geography and possible contradictions, with the objective of clarifying the role of space in producing social injustice;
Investigate the ways individuals residents in the district have been affected by the process of producing social (in)justice, with the objective of evaluating the role of agency;

Contribute to the compact city, social justice and spatiality debates and the research methodology of spatial story based on the Hong Kong experience.

250012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
250012.value: Hong Kong is a high-density city, the characteristics of which have only been selectively studied, and it is the objective of this research to make up this deficiency. The literature is found wanting as high density is usually conceptualised as things but not social processes, its technical dimension emphasised at the expense of the social one, and the objective conditions prioritised over social and spatial aspects of everyday life. To redress this imbalance, the research proposes a more nuanced analysis of unsettling high-density development that emphasises the role of processes and space. It draws on Lefebvre’s production of space within three spatio-temporal levels and everyday life, and Dikeç’s spatial dialectics of injustice. The former argues that urban space is increasingly produced for the market under state planning and regulation and commodity production. One trend is the disappearing of the town and countryside variation. In this process, based on their everyday practices, people develop dreams, social values, desire, etc. about their living environment and the way that it and the society should prosper. Focusing himself on the issue of social justice, Dikeç challenges the reduction of it to redistribution and, instead, put forward the process argument. While unjust social processes generate various spatial outcomes, spatial processes cause injustice. By combining the two, this research proposes to interrogate high-density as the production of space and investigate the accrued issue of social injustice. This is to be achieved by, first at the territorial level, examining the landed and property development process and the concomitant high-density outcome in Hong Kong since the 1950. Second, it elaborates the concretisation of this process, at the district level, in Sham Shui Po, a highly densed district with its specific historical geography and abundant poor, elderly and immigrant population. The locally mediated territorial processes again meet, at the individual level, with the everyday practices of residents living there. There will be ‘participation observation’ of 20 households for the purpose of elaborating their everyday practices together with the issue of social justice. This research employs a rich array of methods to decipher the physical, mental and social spaces of these residents. Having drawn on the process approach and a case study, the research is able to comment on the sources of generating high-density, the extent to which everyday life practices in high-density environment has perpetuated socially produced injustice, and the possibility of removing injustice.

250112.label: Project Title(Chinese)
250112.value: 遊於藝﹕香港、澳門兩地博物館觀眾與文化消費研究

250112.label: Project Objectives
250112.value: To develop an interdisciplinary approach for studying the experiences of museum visitors that embraces two key perspectives (i.e., museology and marketing), reflecting on the nature of museum visits as a form of culture consumption; To construct a theoretical framework that explores a wide spectrum of art audiences in the wider context of cultural development; To catagorise wide ranges of visitors' museum experiences in considering how people would associate with museums and what might foster their interests in the arts and in cultural activities; To critically examine the role of museums in promoting arts and culture by theorizing about the visitors’ perception of the arts; To generate greater collaboration between academic and museum professionals, and provide guidance on tactical museum management, to promote the competitiveness of museums against other cultural activities and to create a sustainable flow of visitors; To help shape museums as engaging public forums that are relevant to the contemporary society, and to promote culture sustainability in the long-run.

250112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
250112.value: Museums have long been considered as guardians of knowledge, arbiters of taste, and most importantly, patrons of informal learning, in fostering the cultural life of the public. Nevertheless, the cosmopolitan lifestyles of Hong Kong and Macau have intensified the fierce competition within the arts and culture sector, and museums are often competed with a range of arts organizations to attract more visitors (Kotler et al, 2006). A decrease in the number of museum visitors suggests that museums are failing to engage the people by making the museum collections relevant for contemporary society (Sandell, 2007; Weils, 2000; Zhang, 2003). To gain a competitive advantage over other art activities, museums need to reflect on how their services can relate to a wider audience. This study critically evaluates the museum experiences of visitors, based on the gap between their expectations and perceptions, and their emersion in the visiting process. This research is built on museological approaches for understanding visitors in the hope of developing a new museum culture that is proactive to the socio-cultural needs of the community (Liu, 2011; Simon, 2010; Black, 2005). In reviewing the many empirical studies, the focus has been on the visitors’ personal context that helps museums to develop short-term programmes for visitors. These studies have a risk in losing vision about the socio-cultural significance of museum visits in relation to the cultural life of contemporary society. To fill this gap, this interdisciplinary research aims to develop a theoretical approach towards visitor studies for the Hong Kong Museum of Art and the Macau Museum of Art. This study is inspired by the idea of cultural consumption, from cultural studies and the disconfirmation of expectation paradigm from the marketing field. It investigates what museums offer to diverse audiences, such as knowledge, social status, and cultural interests, and the museum experiences of visitors, in relation to exhibits, educational activities, accessibility facilities, shopping and dinning, and architecture and design. Using observations, semi-structured interviews, and questionnaires, this research explores the different patterns of museum experiences of visitors in relation to their socio-cultural background, and general perception of the arts and culture, while theorizing how visitors relate to museums in the context of cultural life. The theoretical model for the experiences of museum visitors can be used to analyse the characteristics of art audiences and their engagement with museums, and to formulate new strategies for managing and sustaining visitor participation. 就文化保育的角度而言，博物館是一舉足輕重的文化機構，肩負著傳承文化知識、宣揚美學品味與教育大眾等重任，以豐富公眾文化生活。近年博物館必須與各式各樣的文化藝術團體競爭，以吸引觀眾，而香港及澳門等生活節奏急促的大都會，更使得博物館大有觀眾流失之虞。博物館的文化競爭力趨弱正顯示出館藏未能緊扣社會的時代脈膊，相關服務無法切合大眾對文化活動的需求。是項研究計劃旨在比較分析博物館觀眾對文化機構的期望及其實際的參觀經驗，探討文化藝術與大眾生活的關係。 博物館因其所服務的觀眾而設立，認識不同觀眾群的需要及期望將有助檢視館務的成效，並促進館方思考如何回應公眾的文化需求。自六十年代以降，博物館界日漸重視觀眾研究，但此類研究著重觀眾對博物館的滿意程度，藉以規劃及管理相關設施或服務。這類以實務為尚的研究雖對博物館的服務質素有所提昇，卻鮮有從宏觀的文化角度闡釋參觀博物館的經驗與大眾文化生活的關係，更未有討論大眾參觀博物館的文化心理因素及參觀博物館如何反映公眾對文化藝術的想像。這類觀眾研究的不足在於只著眼於博物館短期服務的發展，卻難以深入探究博物館的文化價值，藉以規劃藝術文化發展的長遠藍圖。 借用文化消費的理論及巿場學期望落差模式，是項計劃以香港藝術館及澳門藝術博物館作個案研究，從日常生活的消費需求了解觀眾參觀博物館的經驗，以討論文化發展與觀眾拓展的關係。文化研究學者J. Storey指出：「文化既不是文化工業的產物，也不只是消費的挪用，文化永遠是兩者積極結合的結果。」博物館參觀經驗正顯示觀眾消費文化服務，也往往挪用有關服務而創造自我的身份認同。是以參觀博物館的經驗可視為大眾對文化的實踐，由此反映社會大眾對文化生活的期望與需求。是項研究透過問卷調查、實地觀察及訪談等方法，調查博物館如何向觀眾提供智性教育、文化趣味甚或地位品味，而觀眾又如何從展覽、教育活動、場地設施、購物餐飲等方面與館方互動，並從而創造博物館的文化價值。研究員將從觀眾的社會文化背景及其對藝術文化的認識分析不同觀眾群的參觀經驗，並將之置於大眾文化生活脈絡，以檢視博物館作為文化消費活動的社會意義。有關文化消費的理論架構有助博物館掌握不同觀眾群對藝術文化的想象，及其與館方互動的模式，由此推展出觀眾拓展策略以促進公眾的文化參與。長遠而言，是項研究也致力闡釋公眾對文化藝術的期望及其消費文化活動的模式，以思考香港及澳門等大都會發展文化藝術的關鍵。

250112.label: Realisation of objectives
250112.value: This research project is designed to examine various modes of cultural consumption within museum contexts in Hong Kong and Macau. Drawing references from the marketing notion of disconfirmation of expectations and visitor-oriented paradigm from museum studies, the research team conducted semi-structured interviews and questionnaires to triangulate visitors’ experiences in relation to their expectations to museum services, and their reception of what they would encounter in the exhibition sites. The research team developed a theoretical framework by proposing how affective and cognitive, and behavioral engagement would interact with visitors’ expectation before visiting the museum, and consequently affect consumers’ perceptions of post-visit experience. A direct causal link between disconfirmation and satisfaction may be detected, but the research team argued that identification is the mediating variable and that disconfirmation influences social identity of the visitors and consequently contributes to their satisfaction. Conducting fieldwork at the Hong Kong Museum of Art and the Museum of Art in Macau, the researchers have interviewed more than 300 visitors, and identified five visitors’ segments based on 1) entry narrative for visiting the museum; 2) interpretations of the visits; and 3) reflective summary of such visits, especially in relation to their general perception of the arts and culture. The team categorized the visitors’ modes of art experience into five segments: 1) connoisseurs; 2) enthusiastic learners; 3) curious viewers; 4) leisurely wanderers; and 5) passive visitors. The categorization helped examining visitors’ identities and how they relate their visit to a wider context of the general perception of arts and culture. The associations between the museums, visitors’ social identities and their perception of arts revealed how they internalized their meaning-making process and articulated their own notions of art in considering what museum would have offered to them. Museums are considered to be one of the most prominent stakeholders in promoting development of arts and culture in Hong Kong and Macau, and yet majority visitors are likely to see the institutions as an edutainment venue. This suggests that a very different model of cultural infrastructure from Europe and North American where museums are considered to be the drive of creative economy and an important part of the city rebranding. The research project enabled academic and museum professionals to work together in considering the reasons behind museum visitations and various visiting patterns, and developing new museum strategies for fostering art participation and attracting new audiences.

250112.label: Major findings and research outcome
250112.value: Integrating marketing theory into museum visitors’ studies framework enabled the research team to associate museum visitation with individual choices and collective imagination of arts and culture in Hong Kong and Macau. Analyzing the qualitative and quantitative data, five modes of visiting experiences are identified, based on visitors’ personal motivation, interpretation of experiences, and general perception of art and cultural activities. It is clear that connoisseurs and enthusiastic learners are assertive in using the museum content to develop their own interpretations of arts. They recognize the role of museum as educational platform and to some extents, arbiter of tastes. However, the majority visitors, who are the curious explorers and leisurely wanderers, prefer making use of the museum content to articulate their opinions about the artworks. They tend to consider museum as a showroom demonstrating nice pieces of art, and their visit as an entertainment, which is very similar to going to a shopping mall or theme park. Passive visitors, who are least engaged in their museum visits, would consider museum as a venue. In considering what shapes a museum experience at an individual level, the research team appealed to the marketing notion of disconfirmation of expectations and argued that visitors’ demographic profile offers limited explanations of people’ expectation and perception of their museum visits. Instead, visitors’ identities, such as caretaker, learner, art-lover, or recharger, serve as the mediating variable. Informed by visitors’ expectation prior to their visits, an identity-expectation-motivation model shapes their affective, cognitive, and behavioral engagement with the exhibits and museum facilities, and consequently, contributes to the visitors’ perception of the post-visit experiences. Considering individuals’ museum experiences in the cultural ecology in Hong Kong and Macau, it is evident that art has been perceived as stylish, entertaining, and sensually stimulating, and that the role of museum as an arbiter of canonization is likely to be ignored by the local communities. Unlike their counterparts in Europe and North American, art museums in Hong Kong and Macau are unlikely to articulate discourses about local arts and culture, and this leaves a vacuum in creating, negotiating, and appropriating meanings of arts and cultures. The role of museum perceived by the visitors is therefore an indicator highlighting an imbalance in regional cultural infrastructure. The research team suggests that the museums should be more proactive in working with the local communities, especially in taking initiatives to set the discussion agenda about local cultural politics.

250112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
250112.value: This research project is an interdisciplinary attempt to understand visitors’ museum experiences as a form of cultural consumption that feeds into the burgeoning development of local arts and culture. In facilitating future development of museums and its relationship with the local communities, the research team suggested that in-depth museum visitors studies and a detailed plan of audience development programmes should be implemented by the institutions. In addition, academic sector should also develop research projects looking into the following aspects of cultural participation: 1/ general patterns of art participation in Hong Kong and Macau and collective imagination of arts and culture; 2/ the mechanism of art ecology in Hong Kong and Macau, in particular the role of cultural infrastructures and creativity in relation to critical discourses of city branding 3/ complex relationships between art organisations and their communities (including producers and consumers), and the connection between arts and civic culture that brings new dynamics to the cultural life of Hong Kong and Macau The research team is keen to collaborate with museums and different arts and cultural organisations in researching into audience experiences and developing new professional practices and strategies that engage with wider public.

250112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
250112.value: This research project is an empirical study of the experiences of museum visitors in a wider context of general socio-cultural perception of the arts and culture. It is the very first collaboration between academic and museum professions to examine the reasons behind museum visitations and various visiting patterns, and develop new museum strategies for fostering art participation and attracting new audiences. Looking into the relationships between museums and their audiences, this research refers to recent museological discussions on public engagement and museum as a civic space. Drawing from museology – a rather neglected discipline and yet relevant discipline, it helps developing professional practices and cultural theories in considering the public role of a museum in the time of rapid growth of culture. Considering visitors’ museum experiences as a form of cultural consumption, this research examines collective discourses of arts and culture and how this would reflect upon cultural position of the museums from a macro perspective. It highlights a unique model of cultural infrastructure in Hong Kong and Macau where cultural intersections among individuals, organizations, and government institutions seems limited and commercial sector is likely to be in better position to turn discourses of art into a form of spectacle.

250212.label: Co - Investigator(s)
250212.value: Prof Huang, Minxue Prof Zhou, Nan

250212.label: Project Objectives
250212.value: We build on social impact theory (SIT) and argue that two components of a group recovery strategy, namely recovery mode (economic vs. social) and delivery mode (personalized vs. mass), interact and affect a customer’s response to the recovery strategy. We enrich our understanding of SIT by introducing the underlying mechanism – perceived justice – that mediates recovery strategy and recovery effectiveness. We further enrich SIT by investigating the moderating effects of the three social forces in the theory. We operationalize these forces into applicable concepts for group service recovery, in order to provide further evidence to support the validity and practicality of SIT.

250212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
250212.value: 從社會影響理論看群體服務補救 當服務失誤影響一群體消費者，業者應如何補救﹖現存文獻集中討論牽涉個人的服務失誤，然而涉及群體的服務失誤日漸增加，不能忽視。在群體服務失誤中，業者可向每一受影響的消費者各自補救，又或以劃一的補救給予整個受損群體。一般認為劃一的群體補救較符合經濟原則。但個人補救卻可依每位消費者受損情況和各人要求，度身訂造補償。在什麼情況下，群體補救較有效？又在哪些情況下，個人補救較有效？我們試用社會影響理論（Social Impact theory, SIT）探討這問題。 我們將服務補救視為社會影響的過程，理解業者如何以適合的群體補救策略，影響消費者往後的行為意欲（再光顧意欲和傳播負面口碑的意欲）。我們提出補救策略的兩個構成元素，補救方法（經濟上和社會上）及提供形式 （群體的和個人的）。我們認為這兩個構成元素的互動將影響消費者如何理解補救策略的感知公平（perceived justice），從而再產生行為意欲。我們推斷，群體經濟補救（如藉由傳媒向所有受影響者發佈退款消息）向所有受影響者表示了一致性，因此加強消費者對分配公平（distributive justice）的感知。而個人社會補救（如︰以個人電郵道歉）則能顯露公司的誠意，因此讓消費者感受到一種互動公平（interactional justice）。我們假設公平感知是補救方法和提供形式的中介變量（mediator）。再者，我們亦提出社會影響理論中的三種影響力量：影響源頭的強度（strength）、直接性（immediacy）和受影響目標的大小（impact target’s group size），是理論模型中的調節變量（moderators）。 我們將以不同的行業和不同的消費者群作實驗考察，檢測假設。我們希望藉本研究，讓學界更了解群體服務失誤的特質及補救方法，亦希望研究所得能建議業界，制定更有效的服務策略。

250412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
250412.value: This proposal is for funding an expansion and continuation of research tracing the chronology and history of the pipe organ in China; as well as documenting the present-day status of the instrument and its repertory. “China” will be understood to mean the present-day geographical limits of Mainland China, irrespective of changes of administration or government in the periods under consideration. However, given recent research and publication related in some degree to this topic dealing with East-West musical and cultural interchange in Asia (including Japan, Korea, and the Philippines) comparative references will be made to these areas (although a full comparative study is beyond the scope of this project.) Approached from a theoretical perspective of interchange and collaboration (as articulated by Waley-Cohen, Rae, Lindorff, Parker, North, et al.) the research proposed here will continue to investigate existing, ongoing developments in pipe organ construction, installation, and listening culture in China, and the increase in awareness of the instrument and its unique repertory. Three things separate this study from the one previously funded by a GRF: 1. The growth in the census of new instruments in the past five years, some of which it was impossible to visit in the previous 24-month period of research. This research aims to catch up and expand on this remarkable development which reflects shifts in cultural and musical ambitions. 2. The present research will also address additional historical resources, in particular archival resources, which were not previously identified or available, and which need to be examined in order to form a comprehensive picture of the area of study. It was intended in the previously funded research to look at some – though not all – of this material; the lack of time available away from Hong Kong led to a limitation on what sources could be looked at in Europe in particular. At the same time, through contact and collaboration with other scholars, the full range of material of potential value to the study has increased several fold. 3. A third area of new exploration will be the coordination of this project to the larger topic, explored in recent studies, of global interaction and exchange in the early modern era. The outcome of this research will be of value not only to musicologists, but to historians of political, social, and religious studies in East-West exchanges, and to China and Asia-Pacific scholars generally. 本建議書是申請延續及增加「中國管風琴」 研究所需的資助，以便提供足夠資金優化本研究計劃,能繼續於追溯西方樂器管風琴引入中國及其發展的歷史和影響，並記錄此樂器在當代中國的興起及其曲目。在本研究計劃中，「中國」將被理解為當代地理上的中華人民共和國，並不會將不對政府及政權更替予以評論。此外然而，申請人也會參考從近期研究及出版資料，又及在處理與研究相關的領域上，探討關於在亞洲國家之間（如包括日本、韓國和菲律賓）東西音樂及文化交流狀況,並會作出一定程度的參考和比較（儘管完整的比較教研究是在本研究計劃的範圍以外）。 從交流及合作的理論觀點和角度（據魏理高欣、拉亞、林樂詩、帕加與勒夫等學者的研究法），本研究計劃將繼續研究中國現存及正在發展中的管風琴建造、設置和管風琴音樂的欣賞文化，以及大眾對此樂器及其獨特曲目上的認知。下列有三項是從早前獲優配研究金的研究計劃衍生出來： 1. 據統計，在過去五年中不斷有新樂器增加，在早之前二十四個月的研究期時間裡未能逐一親身視察到訪所有管風琴。本研究計劃旨在儘早在趕上及詳細探索說明這項出色的發展,且反映文化及音樂上的傳入。 2. 現時的研究將額外加入從特別的歷史檔案庫所得的資料，那些資料都是過往未能辨識和存取，並需要加以查考以對研究有更全面的瞭解。過往資助目的是為了支援研究計劃去發掘一些儘管不是完整全部的資料；申請人沒有且未能提供充足的時間到外國考察，特別是到歐洲去採集所需資料，限制了研究進度。同時，通過與其他學者的聯繫和合作,會所得到更全面的資訊探討，因而令研究計劃的潛在價值倍增加數。 3. 第三個新領域的探索將配合和令此計劃變加入成為範圍較大的項研究題目，包含探討在近期的研究中，早期的全球互動與交流資料。 這項研究的成果不只是對音樂學家有影響，也對從事研究東西文化交流的政治、社會和宗教學者有啟示，中國和亞太學者肯定會重視它有重要的成果。

250412.label: Realisation of objectives
250412.value: All four of the objectives have been realized in large part. Objective 1 is of the kind that essentially has no end, because new information is coming in every day (historicity) and new organs are being planned and built every year (actuality). Having said that, the major part of The Pipe Organ in China census appears to have now been completed, though many details are still to be uncovered. Nonetheless, there are always surprises (usually pleasant ones) and the network of informants grows every day. With respect to Objective 2, great progress was made during this grant period in terms of documentation. With support from our Library, a large number of archives, institutes, and research libraries around the world, and above all the time made available to me on sabbatical in 2014 through the good offices of our Dean, the material surveyed grew to very large dimensions, so large the the text of the final study now runs 20,000 words over its intended target of 120,000 words. Objective 3 was always the most difficult to address, but by adopting the strategy of the 'micro-history' it has been possible to create a credible set of postulates to tie all these different threads together. Objective 4 is an ongoing project, but the collegial and supportive attitudes of the organ builders working in Mainland China today, and many who have been active in the past have made it possible to come up with basic data. The reticence of Mainland authorities and key people, especially since the ascent of Xi Jinping in 2012, to discuss sensitive matters about the funding of culture and religious activities and institutions, has hampered the collection of data for the final item. Several Mainland library collections and archives which had been open to previous researchers were closed to me. And, finally, my attempt to even place a Mainland-born PhD student in our Department under my supervision, who would have begun to research, laterally, some issues connected with the present-day 'Cultural Great Leap Forward', such as the explosion of construction of 'Grand Theaters', and details of the funding for these structures (and the pipe organs inside them) deriving from the PLA-linked Poly Group, was unfortunately unsuccessful, though this is not surprising in light of my experiences in the past three years.

250412.label: Major findings and research outcome
250412.value: The major findings, so to speak, are contained in the completed book manuscript, "Keys to the Kingdom: A History of the Pipe Organ in China." This has been accepted for publication in the series, Leuven Chinese Studies, edited by the Ferdinand Verbiest Institute at the Catholic University of Leuven, Belgium. The two+ years of research funded by the GRF grant allowed, finally, for a sabbatical in the first half of 2014 which I spent in Europe and Mainland China. The key result was in effect the filling in of many gaps in the historical narrative which I had begun with my first GRF grant in 2008-2010, but which was frustrated by the inability to get any serious time away from Hong Kong for this crucial research. At the same time, the 'organ race' which formed part of the object of study here continued to accelerate from the time I began my new research in 2012. Here, The Pipe Organ in China Project which I have run since 1989 finally became recognized (and requests for information have continued to arrive in my email.) I now have a very comprehensive picture, expressed as a chronological narrative, of the beginnings and development of the pipe organ and its culture in China. Although it may sound obscure, it is actually a very rich history into which a high percentage of the major figures in the mission history of China from about 1600 onward make an appearance. The Census, which begins in 1599/1600, now has over 160 known instruments noted and documented. This earlier history is complemented, after the trauma of 1949, by a history that begins with more destruction, and ends with the extraordinary demand for pipe organs in China today, even though the present culture is little developed. In this year alone, two new organs have been installed in Beijing, and in Shanghai the first China organ festival took place, sponsored by the Shanghai Conservatory. While these are, from a global perspective, small events, they point towards an even more active future.

250412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
250412.value: The Project intends to continue to document new installations, and to fill in the gaps in the data relative to pre-1949 installations. Once the book is published, a future goal is the creation of a website that would provide for continual updating, and the addition of new information. A second future action would be to link this with several other research projects, such as Organographia Philipiana, which is currently pursuing something like the goals of The Pipe Organ in China Project with respect to the history of the pipe organ in the Philippines. Broadening the Project's view to encompass all of the Asia mission fields, at least from the historical perspective, has always been one of my personal goals. A third future action would be additional consultancy. In a sense this has already begun, as I have been approached by organ builders, historians, and even a film maker, all interested in my work and in the possibility of my sharing my research with them.

250412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
250412.value: The present research has sought to amplify, and then codify in a book, a history of the pipe organ in China. This has been approached first by the creation of a census of instruments, beginning in 1600, and running through the present day. The second approach has been to create a narrative linking these installations, mostly in the context of Christian mission work up to 1949, and relating their presence on a local level to Chinese history, and on a global level as examples of cultural interchange. In the case of new installations beginning in 1989, the research has not only documented the instruments as such, but has examined the reasons for the 'organ race' which has become a marked feature of Mainland Chinese cultural life, and related to the 'Cultural Great Leap Forward' which has been the topic of much comment in the past decade. Finally, this study has sought to create a model for future research, not necessarily musical, on aspects of what has been called 'entangled history' (histoire croisee), replacing the polarizing us-and-them approaches which since around 1990 have marked so much critical writing on relations between China and the West with a more nuanced view.

251712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
251712.value: The rise of China as the ‘world factory’ since the late 1970s has been attributed to the export-led development, driven by the cross-border investment of Transnational Corporations (TNCs). However, since the early 2000s, export-led path has encountered unprecedented challenges, owing to the changing business environment at global, national, regional and local levels. Transformation of the prevailing model towards a domestic consumption-driven development has been designated by the central government in China’s 12th Five-year Plan (2011-2015). Rebalancing between exports and domestic market, especially embarking on domestic sales in China has been recognized as a viable strategy pursued by the export-oriented TNCs at the wake of the global financial crisis. Despite such a consensus, selling the products previously target for the Western markets in China has turned into a daunting and complex process, the study of which has been rare in the literature. Drawing upon the evolutionary perspective on global production networks (GPNs) approach and the notion of ‘strategic coupling’, the project investigates the changing interaction between local assets and GPNs and subsequent effects on urban and regional evolution in China and particularly the Pearl River Delta (PRD), a typical export-led city-region which has undergone dramatic restructuring. The process of market rebalancing engaged by export-oriented TNCs, particularly the emerging recouping with China’s domestic market over time and space, will be examined, based on a refined GPNs-inspired framework, which incorporates the dynamic GPNs, changing local assets and institutional transition in the contemporary economic globalization. Through intensive field investigation, in-depth interviews, firm-level survey and case study, the project offers an updated and systematic investigation of how the export-led production networks have been reconstructed in response to the rise of local market in the post-crisis globalization. The study is being constructed at an unprecedented junction, when the world, national and local economies are in flux. The study hopes to advance the theoretical debates on strategic coupling of regional evolution and GPNs, and enrich the literature on urban and regional restructuring primarily dominated by the cases in the western developed countries. As a pilot attempt at articulating host domestic market into the GPNs analytical framework and empirical application, the study ellucidates fundamental implications of evolving interactions among GPNs, institutional transition and market shift for reshaping urban and regional trajectories in the dynamic global-local interactions. Suggestions could be proposed for relevant governments and business to strategically tackle challenges and pursue opportunities arising from the onging restructuring process.

251712.label: Realisation of objectives
251712.value: Thanks for the sufficient financial supports, I as the Principal Investigator, with the collaboration of the two Co-Is, conducted intensive research activities and successfully realized the objectives as proposed during the period of undertaking of the Project. The undertaking of this project sheds light on the market shift engaged by TNCs and vibrant domestic markets have been leading to significant transformation of urban and regional development in China and the PRD in particular. The proposed study attempts to update the analysis of export-led urban and regional development from the evolutionary perspective on strategic coupling of changing local assets and dynamic GPNs. Particular attention has been paid to the market rebalancing of TNCs between exports and selling in China. The research activities have been conducted and echoed to “studying regions by study firms” (Park and Markusen, 1995), MacKinnon (2011) suggest “(B)ringing together the concepts of strategic coupling and regional evolution requires a clearer understanding of the firm” (p.9). Following previous attempts (Yang, 2007 and 2009), the study has highlighted the role of firms and non-firm actors as ‘important and active strategic players” in reshaping urban and regional development (Yeung, 2009). The target firms are export-oriented TNCs which have undergone restructuring, particularly market reorientation. Domestic sales refer to both the selling of intermediate components and final products in domestic market. this study will rely considerably on primary data collection through firm-level surveys, in-depth interviews and case studies. Previous research network and information by the PI and Co-Is have been very useful and helpful for conducting this project and comparison of the pre-crisis and post-crisis situations. First, the PI and Co-I have examined the restructuring of the export-led development model, particularly the transformation from a ‘world factory’ to ‘an emerging market’ in China, and their effects on the evolution of strategic coupling with the GPNs. During the period of undertaking the project, PI and Co-Is conducted on-site field investigation was conducted in the sample cities in the Pearl River Delta, such as Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Dongguan, Foshan, Huizhou, Zhongshan, Beijing and Chongqing, Chengdu, Wuhan, Zhengzhou, to better understand the transformation of production organization and connections with other business activities, e.g. procurement, sales, financing. Major questions in the survey have collected useful information of around 1000 firms from various sources of origins and ownership, including 1) basic information: sales and capital assets, ownership, sector, domestic and export shares of turnover, distribution of markets and customers; 2) investment motivation changes over the past decade, e.g. from low cost to potential market in China, 3) experience of market shift and diversification, particularly domestic sales, 4) connections with global, national and local retailers, wholesalers and customers, 5) spatial relocation in relation to develop domestic market: location destination, customer target, practice in domestic sales, and adjustments of organization and operation. The project will examine the interaction among brand building, technological upgrading, spatial relocation and market rebalancing as restructuring strategies in an integrated way. Secondly, the project has investigated the transformation of the organization and operation of the export-led production networks and practice of domestic sales engaged by the export-oriented TNCs in the fragmented market in China. The PI and Co-Is conducted intensive case studies of sample sectors, including furniture, personal computer industry, and other export-oriented production networks have been examined and compared in different cities of the Pearl River Delta. Interviews with various export-oriented TNCs from different origins of sources in various sectors, e.g. electronics, toys, garments, international, national and local retailing and wholesaling companies with their successful and failure experiences of engaging in domestic sales in China. Both intermediate material/component and final good TNCs have be interviewed to understand the distinct market distribution and sales channels of the export-oriented production networks. The interviews have covered three major objectives, namely, 1) to identify the major factors and institutions in relation to domestic sales by export-oriented TNCs in China; 2) to investigate the changing organization and operation of the GPNs under market evolution; and 3) to compile government policies on and responses from firms and other relevant actors to the process. To facilitate conversation in a friendly environment, all interviews have been conducted in a semi-structured manner. The advantage of this approach is that more information could be collected than might be expected from a formal question-and-answer interview. Thirdly, the project has been undertaken to understand the evolutionary frim-region nexus and its implications for reshaping the trajectories of urban and regional development in China in the dynamic global-local interactions. Firm-level survey and in-depth interviews with foreign-invested firms and domestic firms in different cities and regions, have been conducted to investigate the dynamic interaction between the export-oriented and domestic market-oriented production networks and development trajectories in the changing global-local dynamics. The in-depth interviews have been conducted with four groups of interviewees identified, to supplement the questions which could not be covered in the standard questionnaire surveys: 1) Interviews with export-oriented TNCs from different origins of sources in various sectors, e.g. electronics, toys, garments, international, national and local retailing and wholesaling companies, will be asked to share their successful and failure experiences of engaging in domestic sales in China. Both intermediate material/component and final good TNCs will be interviewed to understand the distinct market distribution and sales channels of the export-oriented production networks. 2) Interviews with government officials at various levels of government departments, e.g. Ministry of Commerce, General Administration of Customs, Bureau of Foreign Trade and Economy, Bureau of Business Administration at national, provincial, municipal and local levels in charge of domestic sale by TNCs, in order to understand policy changes and measures taken by various levels of government. 3) Interviews with business associations and NGOs and participation in relevant working meetings organized by General Chamber of Commerce, FHKI, HKTDC, HKCMA, etc.; and 4) Semi-structured interviews with relevant experts and scholars. The established personal connections of the PI and Co-Is have found very helpful to identify and conduct interviews. The majority of interviews have been conducted for around one hour and will be taped and transcript with approval of the interviewees.

251712.label: Major findings and research outcome
251712.value: As of the reporting date (December 2017), the project has generated considerable outcomes including 17 papers published in peer-reviewed international journals, viz. "Geoforum"(2017), "Cities"(2017 and 2015 respectively), "Environment and Planning C" (2014), "European Planning Studies" (2013), "TESG" (2017), "Growth and Change" (2016), Geografisca Series A" (2017), "Habitat International" (2013), four terms for Encyclopedia (2017), two book chapters, and twenty-one papers presented at various international conferences, such as AAG annual meetings, RGS-IBG annual meetings, Regional Studies Association annual meetings, etc. Please refer to Part C for details. Furthermore, a PhD student sponsored by this project successfully completed her PhD degree and published two co-authored papers in peer-reviewed journals in 2017 and presented at international conferences, including two annual meetings of AAG in 2016 and 2017, as well as Regional Studies Association meeting in China in 2016. Major findings and outcomes are summarized as follows. First, the project contextualizes the production relocation and market reorientation from exports to domestic sell in China, taking electronics industry as a case (Yang, 2016). The findings of the project enrich the literature on the reconfiguration of global and regional production networks and shed light on the rise of strategic partner firms, by exploring the emerging laptop computer cluster in Chongqing (Yang, 2017). It argues that there emerges domestic market-oriented production networks yet with limited penetration to the domestic market engaged by electronics firms (Yang and He, 2017). Secondly, taking furniture industry in Dongguan as a case, the project examined the transformation of the export-oriented labour-intensive industry from exports to sell in China (Yang and Fu, 2017a and 2017b). The research advances the literature on evolutionary economic geography, and firm-specific strategies in GPN 2.0 theory in the changing global economy. Thirdly, taking Shenzhen as a case, the project elucidates the technological upgrading of Chinese indigenous firms (Yang, 2014 and 2015). The case of Shunde, a city district of Foshan demonstrates the strategic coupling of local firms in the global production networks (Liu and Yang, 2013). The project has contributed to the developing literature on regional evolution and GPN perspective, by examining the transformation of export-oriented regional development in the global South, e.g. China. It sheds light on the articulation of emerging markets and the rise of China-based indigenous firms in the dynamic GPNs (Yang, 2014 and 2017).

251712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
251712.value: A number of valuable and interesting issues have been identified and worthwhile for future research. The project sheds light on the rise of China’s domestic market and Chinese indigenous firms which have developed into emerging market transnational corporations through production and market expansion beyond China. Numerous avenues are opened on future research agenda, such as 1) changing dynamics of regional development in the global south in the changing global and local dynamics, 2) the role of emerging markets in the regional development and reconfiguration of global production networks, 3) the rise of emerging market transnational corporations (EMTNCs) in the global south, particularly from China, 4) the rise of China's indigenous firms as lead firms in various sectors of GPNs and subsequent effects on urban and regional development. These potential issues have already inspired the PI to bid for another GRF grant which attempts to examine the transformation of labour-intensive industries in the Pearl River Delta driven by the "Machine Substitution" in response to technological change in the era of the fourth industrial revolution.

251712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
251712.value: This project has examined the transformation of the world factory in China since the late 2000s, especially in the aftermath of the 2008 global financial crisis. The prevailing export-led development has encountered unprecedented challenges in the changing business environment at global, national, regional and local levels. The central government has designated the transformation of the export-led model to a domestic consumption-driven development in the national 12th Five-Year Plan (2011-2015). Rebalancing between exports and domestic sales has been recognized as a viable strategy by foreign-invested and domestic firms. However, in practice, the transformation has been a complex process. Taking the Pearl River Delta (PRD), a typical export-led region as a case, this project demonstrates an emerging production networks driven by the rise of domestic market. By conducting intensive field investigation, in-depth interviews, firm-level survey and case study, the project has examined how the export-led production networks have been reconstructed and the domestic market-oriented production networks have emerged in the post-crisis global economy. The development path of China, particularly the PRD region has turned into more balanced trajectories towards exports to the Western advanced markets and emerging markets particularly China’s rising domestic market.

252412.label: Project Title(Chinese)
252412.value: 西部大開發的生態環境影響：貴洲北盤江流域的區域評價

252412.label: Project Objectives
252412.value: to identify the main progress and issues pertinent to eco-environmental protection in western China under the WDS; to analyze political willingness to implement eco-environmental protection at the local government levels; to evaluate the current limitations of both Central and local governments in terms of administrating eco-environmental protection, in particular, enforcing relevant laws and policies; and to examine public awareness of eco-environmental protection in western China.

252412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
252412.value: This research will investigate the progress of and issues surrounding eco-environmental protection in western China, in particular in Guizhou Province during the period 2000 to 2011 under the Western Development Strategy (WDS). The aim of the research is to identify new approaches towards environmental governance that will help to improve eco-environmental protection and achieve sustainable development in western China. Western China, a vast region with multiple ethnic groups, rich natural resources and diverse ecosystems/biodiversities, holds a strategic position in China’s overall long term and stable development. Concomitant with poverty eradication and socio-economic development, over the past decade western China has experienced massive expansion of its infrastructure, mineral resource exploration, and relocation of industrial companies from coastal areas to this region. This has aroused wide concern regarding its eco-environment, i.e., whether it is well protected. To date, little research has been undertaken to evaluate the progress of eco-environmental protection in western China under the WDS. By adopting a new approach, the proposed research will be constructed upon a theoretical concept of “decoupling” (simply defined as delinking socio-economic development from ecological damage and environmental deterioration), using “disjuncture in environmental governance” as an analytic framework to examine the disjuncture between promise and performance of eco-environmental protection by both the central and local governments in western China. The objectives of the proposed research are: (1) to identify the main progress and issues pertaining to eco-environmental protection in western China; (2) to analyze political willingness regarding eco-environmental protection at local government levels; (3) to evaluate current limitations of both central and local governments in administrating eco-environmental protection in terms of resource allocation, capacity building of institutions, and enforcement of relevant laws and policies; and (4) to examine public awareness of eco-environmental protection in western China. The research will focus on the Beipan River Basin with the study techniques including: establishment of a research network; the collection of 12 years of monitoring data and published information; the use of face-to-face interviews; and will employ both qualitative and quantitative analyses. The outcomes of the research are expected to: (1) develop and demonstrate a model for appraising eco-environmental protection in western China under the WDS; (2) provide future solutions to improving environmental governance, eco-environmental protection and sustainable development in western China; and (3) contribute to the academic literature on environmental studies. 摘要 該研究將調查從2000到2011之間，西部大開發戰略的實施對西部生態環境產生的積極影響以及存在的主要問題。此研究的主要目的是探尋出環境管治的新模式，從而進一步推動西部的生態環境保護和可持續發展。遼濶的西部，生活着許多的少數民族，擁有豐富的自然資源，生態系統和生物的多樣性。它對中國的長期稳定發展具有十分重要的戰略意義。過去十多年來，伴隨着消除貧困和社會經濟發展，西部的基礎設施建設和礦產資源開發經歴了空前的發展。同時，許多污染嚴重的工廠企業也由發達的沿海地區轉移到了西部。這些是否會對已經十分脆弱的西部生態環境造成更大的沖擊引起了國內外公眾的廣泛關注。然而迄今為止，對此缺乏基本的研究。 該研究將建立於“脫鈎”的理論概念之上：既社會經濟發展與生態破壞和環境惡化没有必然聯系。同時採用“環境管理分離”作為分析框架來探討中央和西部的地方政府在承諾和執行生態環境保護之間存在的不一致。此研究將從以下幾個方面展開：(1) 確認有關西部生態環境保護主要的進展和問題；(2) 分析地方政府有關生態環境保護的政治意願；(3) 評論當前中央和地方政府在推行生態環境保護過程中面臨的挑戰，尤其是在資源配置，機構能力的提升，以及相關法律和政策的監督執行；(4) 調查西部地區公眾的生態環境保護意識。 主要研究方法包括：選取北盤江流域為研究重點，建立必要的科研合作關係網絡；收集12年來的相關監測數據和公開發表的信息；面對面的深入討論；以及定性和定量分析。預期的研究成果主要有：(1) 建立和演示評價西部生態環境保護的模式；(2) 為改善西部的環境管治，生態環境保護和可持續發展提供對策；(3) 填補學術領域有關環境研究的空白。

252412.label: Realisation of objectives
252412.value: In order to achieve all objectives of the project, nine field surveys were conducted in the Basin and Guiyang between February 2012 and June 2015. Twenty-eight locations in different cities, counties, towns and villages were visited and in excess of 80 groups/individuals were interviewed. Meanwhile, published government documents, journal and news paper articles were widely examined. The group interviews included personnel from government agencies in the province, prefectures, counties and villages; farms, forests, river sections; national parks and reserves; coal mines, iron and steel plants; urban waste treatment works; and universities, primary and high schools. Individual interviewees mainly were: villagers, factory and construction workers, street cleaners, taxi-drivers, shop-keepers, restaurant and hotel employees, company owners, government officials, teachers, engineers, university students, volunteers, and retirees. Some interviewees were returned labour migrants from the coastal regions.

252412.label: Major findings and research outcome
252412.value: The major findings and outcomes of the research are presented as below: 1. Under China's western development strategy, both the ecosystems and environment in the Beipan River Basin were improved during 2000-2012. This is evidenced by the results of erosion, Karst stony-desertification, reforestation, and the water quality in the Beipan River. However, geology, topography, hydrology, climate, and human impacts will remain major challenges to the future ecological conservation and environmental protection. Future environmental development in the Basin and southwest China will demand a long term and holistic approach to overcome both natural and human impacts. The research is publihed by the International Journal of Environmental Studies (2015), titled as 'Environmental effects under China’s Western Development Strategy: a case study in the Beipan River basin, Guizhou'. 2. This research assesses environmental development and governance in western China under China’s western development strategy (WDS). The results revealed that not only has environmental quality in the Basin improved, but also that public awareness and local governments’ willingness regarding environmental protection have been enhanced since 2000. However, challenges persist in the spheres of human impact and environmental governance. Future environmental effort in western China demands an improvement in environmental governance, which includes financial investment and law enforcement from both central and local governments; public participation; and the capacity building of local governments. A paper titled as 'Environmental development and governance in western China since 2000' was submitted to an international journal. 3. The coal mining is the major source of pollution in the Beipan River Basin and southwest China. This research attempts to discuss the role of sustainable coal mining in environmental protection by (a) using concepts of decoupling and circular economy under sustainable development; and (b), China’s western development strategy (WDS) over the last two decades. The results revealed that: progress in decoupling and circular economy has been made in the area, and that coal mining can make positive changes in environmental quality from the local to the global level. Both decoupling and circular economy have proven useful theories/concepts for promoting sustainable coal mining. The success of sustainable coal mining will largely depend on the national government’s guiding ideology on development, enforcement of laws and policies, the public’s environmental awareness, and the coal industry’s corporate social responsibility. A paper titled as 'sustainable coal mining and environmental quality in southwest China' was submitted to an international journal.

252412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
252412.value: Up to date, some feedbacks on the research are received. The first, the research methods, findings and outcomes should be tested in other regions in western China. In this way, environmental development under China's western development strategy can be comprehensively evaluated and the research will be more meaningful. Second, many staff from provincial to county governments are keen to find out a more practical solution in fighting poverty and environmental degradation. Therefore, they hope the future research could demonstrate a clear way, so that government agencies and local people can easily adopt it step by step in their daily operation. They want to scholars give them more constructive and applicable suggestions, which can really help them to solve the problems and make the Basin better world. Third, the possible contribution from environmental NGOs should be further analysed. Many governmental agencies have expressed that environmental NGOs could help local governments in the region to enhance the capacity building with scientific knowledge and management skills. They welcome both local and international environmental NGOs to play more roles in west regions. How can encourage the contribution from these NGOs could be another interesting research in future.

252412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
252412.value: The main purpose of this research is to review the appropriateness of China's western development strategy. The research takes the Baipan River Basin as a study region to identify progresses and issues of ecological conservation and environmental protection in western China since 2000. In the research, decoupling and circular economy are used as two main theories; field surveies and interviews are main research methods. The research discovered that ecological conservation, environmental quality, people's environmental awareness in the Basin have been improved with implementation of China's western development strategy since 2000. It shows the western regions have departured from the old and insustainable development path. The western development strategy has played very improtant role for western China in moving towards sustainable development. However, the western China is still facing many challenges which include lack of financial investment, poor enforcement of laws, and low capacity of local government institutions. The significance and value of this project include: (1) the first time to comprehensively assesss China's western development strategy; (2) to develop and demonstrate new ways of evaluating eco-environmental protection in western China; (3) to help improve environmental governance in western China; and , (4) to produce journal papers in environmental governance and sustainable development.

253212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
253212.value: 以往很多研究結果顯示消費者會建立自我品牌聯繫(Self-Brand Connection)──使用一些品牌去建立和宣示他們的自我身份(Escalas & Bettman, 2003)。可是，這些研究多集中探究的產生過程，而忽略了自我品牌聯繫的改變歷程。為填補這個知識上的空隙，本研究會從目標系統理論(Goal-system theory; Kruglanski et al., 2002) 的角度去探究個人與品牌聯繫是怎樣產生變化。我們假設自我身份與品牌的關係就像目標與達成目標的途徑的關係，即是說消費者透過建立自我品牌聯繫以建立自我形像。因此，自我品牌聯繫的改變也會受目標系統理論中關於目標與途徑改變的法則所規範。 本研究主要有三大價值:一、使用目標系統的角度去探究個人與品牌聯繫的變化的心理歷程。二、研究引發這些變化的情感和動機因素。例如在怎樣的情況下，對於哪些人，這種關係是較有機會發生改變。三、這個研究將為此課題帶來嶄新的理論角度。研究結果將有助學者更了解品牌建立與消費者的個人目標的關係，也能進一步確認目標系統這理論的實際效用。

253212.label: Major findings and research outcome
253212.value: Regrading objective #1: Experiment results showed that consumers during identity transitions have the goals to create and present the new identity. Such goals drive self-brand connections with brands that signals the new identity and undermine self-brand connections with brands that signals the expiring identity. Moreover, the change in self-brand connections is moderated by how perceived instrumentality of using brands to achieve identity goals. Regarding objective #2: Experiment results also showed that consumers' emotional experience caused the predicted changes in self-brand connection. This finding fills an important theoretical void in the self-brand connection literature, which has primarily focused on the social and cognitive processes associated with self-brand connections.

253212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
253212.value: The goal system perspective proposed in this project is shown to be a relevant and unique theoretical framework in studying self-brand connections. Future research can extend to other identity goals as well as situations involving identity conflicts. In addition, future research can study self-brand connections after an identity transition is completed. Consumers sometimes hold on to their possessions even though the products no longer serve any functional purposes and do not fit any active identity. The identity goals and emotional process involved in such self-brand connections warrant future research efforts in order to build a comprehensive understanding self-brand connection processes.

253212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
253212.value: Self-brand connection (SBC)—the degree to which a consumer incorporates a brand into his/her self-concept—was is an indicator of consumer-brand relationship strength. Some consumers develop special bonding with brands and use the brands in show others who they are. This research examined how self-brand connection changes as consumers go through identity transitions. Prior research focused primarily on the level of congruency between brand image and self-image, which would predict that all consumers abandon brands that match with their old identity and build self-brand connection with brands that match with their new identity. We add to this literature by proposing a goal-system perspective and showing that the emotional experience during an identity transition moderates changes in self-brand connections.

253512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
253512.value: 18世紀自然歷史學界的協同認知文化

253512.label: Project Objectives
253512.value: Original objectives 1-4 are unchanged: To demonstrate that particularly botany’s ever growing need for global information gave rise to an information system that could only function in a collaborative and contributory way. For this purpose various techniques for mobilizing, forwarding, and communicating information deployed in botanic correspondences will be analyzed. What was new about the botanical correspondence of the eighteenth century was its scale, its routine designed to increase efficiency, and, as a result, the central significance of this sort of collaborative information-gathering for the knowledge making process, especially of Linnean botany. To elucidate the reasons that motivated naturalists of different scholarly standing, from the newcomer to the distinguished expert, to work on a collective project: Prestige could be gained as the source of any contribution had to be, and was, acknowledged by name. On the other hand it shall be pointed out that eighteenth-century natural history was able to recruit a broad basis of enthusiastic participants as it required countless local contributions. It allowed many individuals to take part in a scholarly activity perceived as useful, inspiring, and enlightened. To analyze how these factors shaped the knowledge-making process of eighteenth-century natural history. The objective is to carve out that the accumulating and aggregating epistemology of Linnean botany in particular was based on bringing together the insights of many people. The more eyes that were involved in examining the features of a plant which had not yet been definitely identified, the more quickly was certainty likely to be achieved by compiling relevant information through correspondence. To demonstrate how Linnaeus established himself as the center of this contributory knowledge-making process. Given the exponential growth in the number of known species and the resulting need for observation, this was the necessary condition which allowed him to write and update continuously his systematic works, Systema naturae, Genera plantarum, and Species plantarum. Original objective #5, on which I had planned to work in the fourth year of the project, was dropped. There are two reasons for this: On the one hand, only three years were granted so it was necessary to adjust the objectives to the available time and resources. At the same time this allows me to follow the suggestion made by one of the referees: to focus the project on the eighteenth century.

There are two reasons for this: On the one hand, only three years were granted so it was necessary to adjust the objectives to the available time and resources. At the same time this allows me to follow the suggestion made by one of the referees: to focus the project on the eighteenth century.

253512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
253512.value: This project will investigate collaborative epistemic cultures with a focus on eighteenth-century natural history. Collaboration shall be explored as a defining feature that shapes the knowledge making process in this discipline as well as in a number of other scientific fields. As a four-year project it comprises two phases. In the first phase I will scrutinize the fundamentally collaborative and contribution-based knowledge culture of eighteenth-century natural history, the scientific discipline that arguably mobilized the largest number of participants in this period. The analysis will be organized along three axis and examine the knowledge making process in natural history as a participatory and collaborative process (1), that requires contributions from as many participants as possible (2), to aggregate them into a final product (3). As natural history’s need for information was potentially endless, a correspondence-based information system was established, that, as a whole, comprised all active naturalists, and linked them to each other as well as to the center of this system, represented by the Swedish botanist Carl Linnaeus. The arsenal of techniques for mobilizing, communicating, and sharing information that were deployed in these correspondences will be discussed. As a next step, this mode of sharing and aggregating information shall be addressed as prerequisite of the global endeavor of natural history to register nature (plants, animals, and minerals) worldwide. Finally this contributory working mode will be linked with the specific publication style of Linnaeus: to stay abreast of this constant influx of information, Linnaeus regularly published corrected and increased versions of his systematic works. Based on the insights gained from the analysis of eighteenth-century natural history, the second project phase will be dedicated to a comparative screening of other collaborative epistemic cultures in early modern and modern science. The aim is to highlight the epoch-spanning significance of fundamentally contribution-based knowledge cultures in the history of science by elucidating their persistence from the early modern period to contemporary times. The contributive format of GenBank for example, a database of all publicly available DNA sequences, was recently characterized as the greatest existing collection of experimental knowledge, and as such having an essential significance for the comparative dimension of knowledge-making in molecular biology (Strasser: The Experimenter’s Museum: GenBank, Natural History, and the Moral Economies of Biomedicine’, Isis 102 (2011), 60–96). Other examples of collaborative epistemic cultures shall be identified and compared to broaden the typologies of "ways of knowing" in the history of science. 18世紀自然歷史學界的協同認知文化 負責人：Bettina Dietz博士，香港浸會大學歷史系助理教授 本項目將探索18世紀自然歷史學界的「知識文化」之重大特徵之一的協作行為。 「知識文化」是當時動員人數最多的科學學科。此研究將沿三條軸線組織：（1）將知識創造歷程看為參與性和協作性的進程來分析，（2）這歷程必定有最多參與者的貢獻，（3）以匯總成為最終的成果。 因自然科學需求的信息無涯，則基於通信的系統被構成。該系統不但聯結所有在當時進行研究的博物學家，而且將他們亦與以瑞典籍植物學家卡爾•林奈烏斯為核心的系統進行聯繫。本項目將探討各學者於通信中調動、交流、以及共享信息的方法。下一步將是論談該共享和集合信息之模式為自然歷史全球化之先決條件。此外，本項目會將此貢獻性之研究方式與林奈烏斯本人之個別「迭代性」出版風格所相連:林氏多次在短時間內修改和補充他曾出版的系統性專著。

For this purpose various techniques for mobilizing, forwarding, and communicating information deployed in botanic correspondences will be analyzed. The objective is to carve out that the accumulating and aggregating epistemology of Linnean botany in particular was based on bringing together the insights of many people. The more eyes that were involved in examining the features of a plant which had not yet been definitely identified, the more quickly was certainty likely to be achieved by compiling relevant information through correspondence.

253512.label: Major findings and research outcome
253512.value: This project analysed the collaborative dimension of the knowledge-making process in eighteenth-century Linnaean botany. Due to its ever increasing need for information, Linnean botany had to rely more and more heavily on the aggregation of contributions by many people. This, in turn, had a crucial impact on the genesis and form of botanical publications: the more comprehensive the project, the larger the effect. It was the botanist Carl Linnaeus who managed to establish himself as the centre of this contributory knowledge-making process. Given the exponential growth in the number of known species and the resulting need for observation, this was the condition which allowed him continuously to update and correct his systematic works, and allowed them to maintain their status as the central catalogues of a global botany for decades (Contribution and Coproduction; see part C). In a second article (Linnaeus’ Restless System; see part C) I linked translations of Linnaeus’ Systema into various European languages to the dynamics of successively expanded editions of his writings. The intention of most translators was not only to make the Systema accessible for botanical use by a wider readership, but also to supplement and correct it. By recruiting more users, translations made a sigificant contribution to keeping the Systema up to date. The need to incorporate additions and corrections into an existing text, to document their provenance, identify inconsistencies, and refer to relevant observations, descriptions, and illustrations in the botanical literature helped to refine techniques of textual montage. This form of textual engineering, becoming increasingly complex with each translation cycle, reflected the modular architecture of a botanical system designed for expansion. In a third publication, a contribution to an edited volume titled “A Global History of Linnaean Sciences” (s. part C), I argue that this is an approach that was not only used by Linnaeus’ himself but by other botanical authors as well. The focus is on the publication trajectory of Pehr Osbeck’s account of his trip to China (1750 - 1752). After his return Osbeck divided his material between a number of publications that came out successively, building on and supplementing each other, with the intention to present his discoveries to the public as quickly as possible, and then to complete and correct the already published texts by stages. This project was conceived as collaborative from the start, and involved different types of publication and various authors, translators, and commentators.

253512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
253512.value: Firstly, these findings, which I also presented at a number of relevant conferences and workshops, were taken up in international research on Linnaean science. A collection of essays, titled “Nature’s Empire. A Global History of Linnaean Sciences”, edited by Hanna Hodacs, Kenneth Nyberg, and Stéphane van Damme (to be published by Oxford University Press), to which I was invited to contribute, is going to discuss them in its introduction. Secondly, I am going to continue to work in this direction. My insights from this project will serve as a matrix for my ongoing and future research on eighteenth-century natural history.
