254112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
254112.value: This project investigates a unique case in the history of criticism: the rise of modern Chinese literary criticism and its engagement with discourses of revolutionary politics and national survival. It will study the emergence of modern Chinese literary criticism as part of the intellectual globalization that started in the early twentieth century, much earlier than the capital globalization we have been ambiguously experiencing now. Apart from the former Soviet Union, China is the only major communist country where literature and criticism are first-hand witnesses of as well as means to such eventful political events as the Chinese Revolution and the Cultural Revolution (1966-76). By their direct participation in politics, literary intellectuals -- their work, their treatment, and their social place -- have helped index the shifting ideological emphases in the evolving process of the Communist Party’s self-consciousness. My research’s point of departure is the critical consciousness of Hu Feng 胡风 (1902-85) within the historical context of these modernizing and revolutionary transformations. Hu Feng, a prominent Marxist literary critic, a fellow traveler of the CCP, and Lu Xun’s last protégé, was the most representative figure of his generation of radical writers. His institutional life and critical work were central to the key debates of leftwing literary circles. I hypothesize that research into a series of debates between Hu Feng and the CCP’s cultural leaders will show how Marxist literary criticism turned from a creative revolutionary force into a hegemonic formation, especially following the founding of The People’s Republic in 1949. My study is itself an instance of advanced work in the literary humanities, applying the techniques of theoretically informed historical and philological criticism to demonstrate its continuing vital contributions to research and cultural values. I will show that the complex relation between intellectuals and the structure of power was not just one of top-down control, but rather one in which intellectuals willingly interact, negotiate, and even collaborate with institutional powers that treat criticism with suspicion. The principal outputs of this project will be two articles and a publishable book-length manuscript. These outputs will be among the first attempts to reassess a generation of leftwing intellectuals as not just “victims” of Mao Zedong but also as embodied agents of state and institutional power. Mine will also be the first book-length study of Hu Feng in English and, as such, will insert Hu Feng into global conversations about modern criticism and politics. 本研究项目旨在揭示中国现代文论的兴起和中国革命、民族存亡、国际马克思主义等话语体系件的关系。中国现代文学批评是思想知识界全球化的产物，发轫于二十世纪初期，远早于我们目前正在经历的经济全球化。研究中国现代文学批评发展史，为梳理文学和政治之间的关系提供了独特的视角。除了前苏联外，只有在中国这个主要的共产主义国家，文学和批评不仅直接见证了激荡的历史，更是直接参与了重大的政治事件，中国文学知识分子成为中国政治生活中最重要的部分。他们的工作，他们的境遇，他们的社会地位，成为中国共产党自我意识中意识形态上的转移重要的索引。 本研究项目以胡风（1902-1985）批评意识的形成为出发点。作为一个马克思主义文学评论家，中国共产党的同路人，鲁迅的得意门生，胡风是他那一代激进作家中最具代表性的人物。胡风的文学组织工作和批评生活是左翼文中坛的一些主要论战的中心。研究胡风和中国共产党文化领导人之间的分歧和斗争，有助于揭示马克思主义文艺批评如何从一个富有创造性的革命力量转变为政治霸权的过程；这种转变在1949年新中国成立以后尤其明显。 这项研究本身乃是文学人文科学研究的具体实践，以文学批评的技术和手段，恢复其研究和文化上的价值。我将展示知识分子和权力结构之间不仅是一个自上而下，控制与被控制的关系，知识分子心甘情愿地与体制权威合作，互动，协商。这个项目的主要产品为两篇文章和一本书稿。这份书稿将重新评估中国左翼作家，说明他们不仅是毛泽东思想的受害者，而是体现了国家机构权力的代理人。这份手稿将是第一本研究胡风英文专著。

254112.label: Realisation of objectives
254112.value: The project has produced several articles and a book manuscript, entitled, 'The Poiesis of Criticism: Hu Feng 1902-1985' on the modern Chinese intellectual Hu Feng. The book, currently under review by SUNY press, has been written to meet the objectives listed in the proposal. Specifically, it 1. presents the case that Hu was a literary intellectual of his time and that, as such, he set the standard for the way in which future generations remembered criticism’s enduring importance in modern society; and 2. inserts into the history of transnational cultural and intellectual exchange the case of Modern Chinese literature and criticism. Apart from the former Soviet Union, the PRC is the only major communist country where literature and criticism are direct means to such historically unique events as the “Cultural Revolution” (1966-76). By their direct participation in politics, a generation of Marxist intellectuals--their work, treatment, and social place--helped index the shifting ideological emphases in the evolving process of the CCP’s self-conscious “rise.” More important and specifically thanks to Hu, who followed Lu Xun but lived beyond him to witness the politically significant threshold of 1949 by which practicing criticism against orthodox Marxism became a life-and-death matter, Hu’s work provides readers with an antithesis of the modernization values that the PRC has come to indoctrinate not only the nation but also the world in the wake of its “peaceful rise” at the turn of the twenty-first century. This book is, then, both an essential contribution to the cultural and literary history of Modern China and to our collective understanding of the “rising” PRC. This book will be the first one in English fully to study Hu Feng in an effort to bring Modern Chinese literature and criticism into global discussion of the modern critic and the politics of intellectual engagement. In relation, it seeks to augment incipient critical discussion of Modern Chinese writing in the wide scholarly and cultural sphere of global literatures and advanced criticism. For example, this book contains a chapter on Hu Feng and Lu Xun (Chapter 3). Although existing studies of Lu Xun make an important exception to the general rule that Modern Chinese literature is a mere example of “third-world” writings, or, at its best, a footnote to global modern literatures; Hu, who worked closely with Lu Xun, was arguably the next most important figure to Lu Xun in terms of critical consciousness. Ironically, Fredric Jameson’s influential notion of national allegory, based on his reading of Lu Xun’s “Diary of a Madman,” univocally directs Western criticism’s study of the experience of Chinese modernity even as it attempts to “liberate” it from Sinological area studies, which rarely engages with critical work outside itself. My book is a supplement to these successful and substantial efforts. It has the following internal goals as listed in the ECS proposal: • Describing and analyzing the practice of a generation of modern literary intellectuals in the PRC in close relation to politics and literature, and understanding the genealogical formation of leftwing critical practice and its language. • Identifying and assessing Hu’s career for re-situating and reevaluating modern Chinese intellectuals’ employment of literary criticism in negotiating their relations with the structure of institutionalized political power. Given the interests in the leftwing intellectuals’ agency in a structure of power, especially following the political ascendancy of the CCP, I want to reveal not only the ways Hu and other committed critics work, but also the motives of and ethical reasons for their practice and the values inherent in it. • Continuing and enriching on the concept of the “committed critic” in relation to debates about creative freedom and political commitment. In this instance, the PRC has a great deal to contribute to a discussion in which Euro-American scholars have until now had the strongest voice. • Advancing the critical study of modern literary criticism and promote the productiveness and ideal of intellectual globalization.

254112.label: Major findings and research outcome
254112.value: My manuscript will find success in the markets of several fields within general literary and cultural studies: the intellectual and the history of ideas, modern literary criticism, modern Chinese writing, and cultural policy and governmental studies. Readers of this book will quickly discover that this book is: 1. The first English-language book-length study of Hu as a Marxist literary theorist and critic over a span of twenty-five years. 2. A long-delayed reassessment of Hu’s involvement in the politics of critical practice and the significance of it in the history of intellectual globalization. 3. The first to foreground the “Hu Feng case” in 1955 as one of the most significant political-intellectual events in the PRC history. This book will remind future scholars that the CCP’s continuous history of intellectual persecution began with the foreboding case of Hu Feng, which took place at least a full decade before the “Cultural Revolution.” The Hu Feng case has lessons to teach about the efficacy of culture and criticism: the disciplinary act of society does not just operate on the body of subject. In modern societies, to discipline the body is never as important as the governing of the species’ critical and creative imagination. 4. A study of how the first generation of modern Chinese literary critics did criticism--the skills and arguments they used to negotiate their institutional and ideological relations with state-party power. I expect my work will attract and benefit a wide readership among scholars in Chinese Studies and in Cultural and Comparative Literary Studies, and among the broader community of readers interested in the fate of modern Chinese intellectuals. It is also possible that the book would have a pedagogical purpose in China and elsewhere. Not incidentally, my English language publications will make an important figure and period in Chinese history and writing a major part of global studies of modernity and modern criticism.

254112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
254112.value: To further develop the project on Hu Feng, I propose to do a special issue on the place of poetry and criticism in Hu Feng 胡风 (1902-1985)’s career as a revolutionary writer. The issue will contain a collection of essays on Hu Feng by scholars having access to the archives of Hu Feng in their own places and languages. This issue solicits essays that together provide a comprehensive picture of Hu’s development as a poet, critic, and committed intellectual without the indulgence in anecdotes and fragmentations that characterize scholarship in this area. These essays will reconstruct the development of Hu as a complete and available poet, editor, and literary critic. These essays will address the following questions and open lines of research into Hu as an exemplary Marxist intellectual: what were the intellectual tendencies that the CCP imagined and suppressed in the course of “revolutionizing” and “modernizing” China? Others follow: What helped the imagined alternative basis of Chinese modernity and what hindered their development and maturity. This is not merely a question of broad historical interest. Each successive generation of PRC intellectuals increasingly faces questions and problems similar to those faced by Hu and to which he offers some answers.

254112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
254112.value: This research is on the revolutionary career and political fate of the poet, literary critic, and political prisoner, Hu Feng. Hu Feng is at the center of the infamous ‘Hu Feng Case’ of 1955, which is the first major instance of the Chinese Communist Party’s continuing history of intellectual persecution. More importantly, the ‘case’ offers the chance for not only a much needed reconfiguration of modern Chinese cultural history but also for an analysis of literary intellectuals’ own contribution to and alienation from the political system and institutional establishment of the CCP. The research would join the scholarly movement to expose the multiple forms of modernity around the world, bringing China into this field of discussion. At the same time, it would bring the Case and Hu Feng himself into the field of critical discussion as a resource for study. Hu’s work contains exemplary thinking about struggles with authoritarian power while more important, it embodies careful, creative, and humane commitments to imagination as the basis for alternatives to the CCP’s monolithic purpose.

254712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
254712.value: This project proposes to investigate the effects of credit risk of option writers on option pricing by making use of the data of derivative warrants and options traded in Hong Kong. Derivative warrants are like usual options except that they are issued by financial institutions, and they are exposed to the credit risk of issuers. Options are settled through a central clearing house, thus bear no credit risk. There are advantages of using the Hong Kong data. First, many derivative warrants and options with identical contract specifications are actively traded in Hong Kong which allows a clean test on the effects of credit risk. Second, issuing financial institutions of these derivative warrants are mostly European and American banks. Due to the financial crisis in fall of 2008 started in the US and the recent European sovereign debt crisis, the credit quality of issuing banks exhibits a large time-series variation, so the effects of credit risk on the pricing of derivative warrants can be easily identified. 此課題採用香港認股証和期權的數據研究期權賣方的信用風險對期權定價的影響。認股証和期權相似，不同之處在於認股証由金融機構發行，所以暴露於發行機構的信用風險。期權通過清算所結算，不存在信用風險。採用香港數據有如下好處。第一，由於大量具有相同合約條款的認股証和期權在香港交易，信用風險的影響可以被清楚的檢驗。第二，大多認股証的發行機構為歐洲及美國銀行。因為始於美國2008年秋的金融危機和最近歐洲主權債務危機，發行金融機構的信用質量出現明顯的時間序列上的變化，信用風險對認股証定價的影響可以被容易的檢測到。

254712.label: Realisation of objectives
254712.value: We use derivative warrants and options written on the Hang Seng Index from 2005 to 2012 to examine the effects of counterparty credit risk of warrant issuing banks on the prices of warrants. The data of derivative warrants and options are obtained from the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The counterparty credit risk of warrant issuers is measured by their 5-year credit default swap (CDS) spreads, downloaded from Datastream and Bloomberg. To realized the first objective, we divide the sample period into two subperiods by the month when the Lehman Brothers declared the bankruptcy. We find that the level and volatility of CDS spreads in the second subperiod are much higher than those in the first subperiod. We regress the price differences between the derivative warrants and options with the same maturity and strike price against the CDS spreads of warrant issuing banks cross-sectionally, and find that the counterparty credit risk of warrant issuers is priced, but only in the second subperiod. For the second objective, we first examine the correlations between the changes in CDS spreads of warrant issuing banks and the index returns, and find that the correlations are all negative, which suggests that the counterparty credit risk is more important for put derivative warrants. Using the cross-sectional regression analysis, we find that the prices of in-the-money put derivative warrants are more sensitive to the CDS spreads than other warrants do.

254712.label: Major findings and research outcome
254712.value: We find that the counterparty credit risk of derivative warrant issuers is priced in the derivative warrants only after the global financial crisis started in fall 2008. On average, a one percentage point increase in the CDS spreads of warrant issuers leads to a 1.9 percent decrease in the prices of derivative warrants during this period, and the effect of the credit risk is stronger for in-the-money put warrants. The effects of counterparty credit risk are still significant after controlling for the liquidity differences between derivative warrants and options, which are considered as an important factor in determining their price differences in the literature. The results suggest that the counterparty credit risk has become an important factor in determining the prices of derivative securities since the global financial crisis. A paper based on this analysis has been presented in the European Financial Management Association Annual Meetings.

254712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
254712.value: The analysis in the current project is based on linear regressions, which address the question whether the counterparty credit risk is priced or not. The extension of the analysis can be based on a option pricing model with counterparty credit risk, which can quantifies the effects of counterparty credit risk on each individual derivative warrants. We plan to pursue the research in such a direction.

254712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
254712.value: In this study, we examine whether the counterparty credit risk is priced in derivative securities using the derivative warrant and option data in the Hong Kong market from 2005 to 2012. Derivative warrants are similar to options except that they are issued by financial institutions, and subject to the credit risk of issuers. We find that the credit risk of warrant issuers is priced in the derivative warrants, i.e., when the credit risk of the issuing banks are high, the prices of derivative warrants issued by the banks are low comparing with those of options. The effect only occurs after the global financial crisis started in fall 2008. The results suggest that investors are increasingly aware of counterparty credit risk of banks when trading derivative securities.

255112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
255112.value: 中央錄取機制被廣泛應用於世界各地以分配有限的學位。尤其是波士頓機制的各種變體所應用之處，“優惠待遇”現象更是比比皆是。換句話說，很多學校在招生時承諾優先考慮報其為首志願的學生，即使他們的考試分數低於非首志願生。在發掘了學校如此承諾的動機之後（Chiu and Weng, 2009, RJE），本文將重點考慮學生的整體福利，給定各學校仍可在波士頓機制和Gale-Shapley延遲錄取機制間自由作出選擇。 在前文（Chiu and Weng, 2009, RJE）的基礎上， 本文意將通過考慮不同的學校名望集中度下學生福利的差異來進一步一般化其結果。不同地區的學生所面臨的學校群可能呈現出迥然不同的名望集中度。例如，在某個地區，所有學校可能有著相似的知名度，而在另一個地區可能高度集中於極少數學校。從這個角度看，不同地區的學校在招生機制的選擇上可能有著顯著的差異。波士頓機制下，不同地區的學校與學生之間的配對結果亦可能有著不同程度的效率損失。 目前的初步結果（模型中僅討論兩個學校）的確證實了上述推測。以Gale-Shapey延遲錄取機制為基準，我們考慮了存在需求不確定性的環境 （沒有人確定知曉每個學校的具體受歡迎程度，雖然事前每個人都知道各種可能性的概率分佈）。首先，在“絕對”受歡迎的情形下（即在基準情形下，學校1在任何情況下的錄取分數線都比學校2高），隨著學校名望分佈趨於平均，學生福利損失隨之增大。相反地，在“相對”受歡迎的情形下（即在基準情形下，兩個學校都有可能达成比对方高度录取线），學生福利的損失隨著學校名望趨於集中時而增大。總的來說，波士頓機制下，學校集中度的分佈變化對學生福利的影響的確存在，但其間並非單調關係。

255112.label: Realisation of objectives
255112.value: To track and understand the relevance of school popularity distribution, we consider two scenarios of centralized admissions. 1. School popularity distribution over possible states of world In the first paper of this project, we consider a centralized admissions problem in which applicants do not have perfect information regarding schools’ popularity. That is, they are not perfectly sure of the exact popularity of schools that are open for admissions. Applicants’ decision making thus is only based on their prior belief about schools’ popularity distribution over possible states of world. By the degree of relative dominance of school popularity, two cases regarding the school popularity distribution are considered – absolute popularity (AP) and relative popularity (RP). Under AP, although the exact school popularity is unknown, it is certain that one school is more popular than the other in either state of world. Under RP, different state of world corresponds to a different school that is relatively more popular. The leading school is determined through a comparison between the two schools' admissions cutoffs in their respectively more selective states. We show, systematically, how rational applicants report their preferences, strategically and optimally, and how schools are incentivized to provide preferential treatment to those who rank it higher over those who do not, via using Boston mechanism instead of student-proposing deferred acceptance mechanism. Under both AP and RP, we find that the non-leading school has relatively stronger incentive to offer preferential treatment in order to admit more motivated students than otherwise. It is so because there always exist some unenthusiastic applicants with good but non-top quality that the non-leading school would possibly enroll if without offering preferential treatment to those who rank it higher. Using Boston mechanism enables the non-leading school to drive out these unenthusiastic applicants for more admissions of motivated ones. This result is derived from the finding that those students are expected to face with a tradeoff that is otherwise absent if without their prior belief of school popularity distribution and the non-leading school’s use of Boston mechanism. Specifically, when the non-leading school is sufficiently undesirable to these unenthusiastic applicants, it is optimal for them to honestly top rank their most-preferred school rather than misreporting their preferences. The consideration of both AP and RP also enable us to distinguish the incentives of the leading- and non-leading schools. We find that only under RP would the leading-school have the incentive to offer preferential treatment to those who rank it higher as well. The scenario of RP corresponds to the case where the popularity distribution is relatively less concentrated so that even the leading school is likely to admit unenthusiastic applicants who are of good but non-top quality. We figure out the condition under which the use of Boston mechanism would benefit the leading school through driving out those unmotivated applicants for admissions of more motivated applicants. Moreover, the success of the leading school’s adoption of such preferential treatment relies on the non-leading school’s use of same practice, that is, through internalizing the effect of the other school’s provision of preferential treatment. Understanding and comparing these two representative scenarios that correspond to different school popularity distributions, we are enabled to predict that the less concentrated school popularity distribution is, the more likely that schools will each face some unmotivated applicants whose reporting behavior is manipulable, and therefore, Boston mechanism will be more likely preferred to student–proposing deferred-acceptance mechanism if schools concern sufficiently about student motivation. We do notice that the fit of using Boston mechanism relies on not only the school popularity distribution but also the relative desirability of schools in the eyes’ applicants, such that the mandatory use of Boston mechanism could possibly backfire if a school remains sufficiently desirable as to its unenthusiastic applicants. 2. School popularity distribution over regions In the second paper of this project, we consider another kind of school popularity distribution that concerns mostly the case of a developing country where regional inequality of education prevails. Corresponding to the degree of economic development, the relatively more advanced region is typically the place where the higher quality schools locate. In other words, school popularity distribution is generally more concentrated on schools located in the advantaged regions than in the relatively less advantaged regions. Regional inequality of education of this kind has been widely concerned so that quota schemes of various forms, intended to address this problem by providing preferential treatment to applicants from the disadvantaged regions, have been widely adopted. The introduction of quota scheme is one way to manipulate school popularity over regions, artificially. With the opportunity in hand to set up quota over various regions, schools, however, are observed to be inclined to favor their local applicants through assigning a disproportional share of total vacancies locally. Behavior of such born by schools located in the more advanced regions is most controversial as it is believed to result in greater regional inequality, totally contradicting to the original intention of introducing quota schemes. Public support has been raised to change to another so called fair quota allocation scheme, under which each school assigns seats across regions in proportion to the size of applicants therein. Corresponding to the problems raised above and to the different school popularity distribution, we explore, in this paper, not only the students’ reporting behavior under three representative quota schemes but also why schools tend to favor their local students, in particular, the top school who should’ve admitted better students from a wider range of choice rather than restricting itself mainly to the pool of local applicants. Aiming at a comprehensive understanding of how the use of quota schemes affects the fairness of admissions outcome and the magnitude of regional inequalities, we examine three scenarios – the local preferential treatment (LPT), the fair quota allocation scheme (FQA) and Grand Admissions (GA), a quota-free scheme. Our simple model analysis shows that the seemingly fair quota allocation scheme FQA could actually backfire by leading to an admissions outcome that contributes to an even larger regional gap, than in the case of GA. LPT, which is believed to be unfair, however, turns out to outperform FQA in benefiting the less advantaged region as a whole. The counter-intuitive conclusion is that neither form of artificial intervention, FQA or LPT, can outperform GA, under which the absence of intervention allows the regional difference (in terms of both student preferences and overall school qualities) to unravel in the way that renders the disadvantaged region to gain with its weakness. GA is also found to give rise to the most stable matching outcome across regions than do the other two quota schemes, showing that it is not inevitable to sacrifice the more advanced region for the benefit of the less advantaged place. With experimental evidence collected from 832 participants, it is evidenced that insights from the simple theoretical model hold not only in a relatively simple environment with complete information and full reporting of preferences by applicants, under Boston mechanism and Deferred-Acceptance mechanism, respectively, but also apply to the more realistic and complex environment with incomplete information and restricted reporting of student preferences.

I want to explain here that the under-achievement of objective 4 is because of the change from theoretical investigation to experimental investigation, as highly suggested by the referee. Lab experiment is too limited an environment to study the impact of enrollment expansion. Instead, we make use of it to shed light on the systematic differences of various quota schemes that correspond to different school popularity distributions over regions.

255112.label: Major findings and research outcome
255112.value: We investigate school popularity distribution in two scenarios. In the first paper of this project, we investigate the relevance of school popularity distribution over different possible states of world, in the eyes’ applicants, in explaining why schools choose to adopt preferential treatment to those who rank them higher (in their rank-order lists) over those who do not even the latter are of better quality. We find that, when applicants do not have perfect information about school popularity but only a prior belief regarding schools’ popularity distribution over possible states, their reporting behavior may together reach the outcome that incentivize the non-leading school to adopt Boston mechanism (over student-proposing deferred-acceptance mechanism) so that to drive out some unmotivated students who would otherwise be admitted. The leading school may also have an incentive to use Boston mechanism to admit more motivated students via internalizing the effect of the non-leading school’s provision of preferential treatment, when school popularity distribution is not very concentrated. We also contribute to the understanding of the two competing school admissions mechanisms, Boston mechanism and student-propose-to-school deferred acceptance mechanism. In the second paper of this project, we investigate the relevance of school popularity distribution over regions, in the context of a developing country, where regional inequality of education is typically prevalent. Quota schemes are thus typically and correspondingly introduced aiming at offering preferential treatment to students located in the relatively disadvantaged regions. How schools assign quota across regions, together, results in different school popularity distribution as faced by students in different regions. In face of the prevailing quota scheme set to favor local students, we show with a simple theoretical model as well as experimental evidence that switching to a so-called fair quota scheme that assigns school seats in proportion to the size of student population may backfire in terms of rendering even larger regional gap as measured by the proportion of students admitted to quality schools, than otherwise.

255112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
255112.value: Based on the current findings on schools’ motives as well as on the impact of various quota schemes on the student welfare and regional inequality, we plan to conduct further research along this line by carrying out field experiments in mainland China, the largest developing country on earth that has been facing severe problems related to regional inequalities of education. Our current findings shed light on the basic logic behind the problem and propose the direction of reformation. As to how to implement the reformation, step by step, we need to better understand the real world complexity before we can come up with more practical solutions. Conducting field experiment will enable us to see the potential impact of our proposed reformation as well as to see what else real world constraints that we could’ve ignored. The investigation of China’s education system will have significant policy implications to other developing countries as well.

255112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
255112.value: We explore two kinds of school popularity distribution that matter in the context of centralized admissions. When applicants do not know exactly how popular schools are, their prior belief about school popularity distribution over different possible states of world may render them to report their preferences in the way that schools may find it beneficial to offer preferential treatment to applicants who rank it higher over those who do not. In particular, schools may get to admit more motivated students than otherwise via driving out some unmotivated students they could’ve admitted if without offering such preferential treatment. We also investigate school popularity distribution over regions, in the presence of regional inequality of education. How schools assign quota across regions, together, results in different school popularity distribution as faced by students in different regions. In face of the prevailing quota scheme set to favor local students, we show with a simple theoretical model as well as experimental evidence that switching to a so-called fair quota scheme that assigns school seats in proportion to the size of student population may backfire in terms of rendering even larger regional gap as measured by the proportion of students admitted to quality schools, than otherwise.

255212.label: Project Objectives
255212.value: To improve and extend the existing forecast combination methods by imposing a more realistic independent Cauchy type g-prior that yields a robust Bayesian estimator for the combination weights. The posterior mean estimator is a weighted sum of both least square estimator and simple average. The non-constant shrinkage weight allows the estimate to automatically adjust to the performance of the combined forecasts and thus it is more adaptive to structural breaks than the existing ones. To propose a more robust estimator with respect to various kinds of error distributions, especially flat-tailed, asymmetric, or mixture normal error -- the characteristics which can be found in financial data. Enormous papers have compared various forecast combination methods in a setting with well-behaved error. We compare our robust Bayesian estimators with the existing ones through Monte Carlo studies in various data generating process with different kinds of error distribution. Applications to economic and financial data under fixed, recursive and rolling windows are used to verify the robustness of our estimators. We plan to extend this Bayesian idea to combine forecasts at different quantiles. Since Value-at-Risk, which is a major area in risk management, studies the probability of occurrence of extreme events that focuses on the tail distribution, improvement of forecasts at the tail distribution therefore deserves a close investigation. It is argued that when information is available, it would be better to combine the underlying information than forecasts. The performance of various information combination methods will also be compared.

255212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
255212.value: Due to the unknown form of model misspecification and the occurrence of structural changes, consensus has been reached that combining forecasts can improve the performance over individual forecasting models in terms of mean square error. However, over the past decades, empirical findings always suggest that simple averaging forecasts often outperform theoretically optimal methods. Therefore, enormous literature has proposed various estimators to explain and solve this long standing puzzle. In this project, a Bayesian shrinkage estimator for forecast combination is proposed. It draws together earlier work of mine and others to form a robust Bayesian estimator that is superior to simple average and yet easy to calculate. In Bayesian econometrics, one of the controversial and difficult aspects is to choose a prior for the parameters before estimation. The empirical puzzle suggests that simple average can be chosen to be the prior location of the regression coefficients. However, one has to figure out whether the traditional natural conjugate prior is appropriate or not since the prior assumes a particular dependence structure among the regression coefficients and the error variance which is impossible to justify. In spite of its convenient form with constant shrinkage weight, it is not adaptive to model performance over time. Besides, it may not be robust to various kinds of error distribution, for example, Cauchy or flat-tailed error, which is one of the characteristics of the financial time series. Therefore, we relax the dependence structure among the coefficients and variance in this project. Unlike existing estimators, the analytical form of our estimator under independent prior now depends on the prediction error, meaning that it adjusts automatically by penalizing the least square estimators when the underlying models do not respond to the shocks quick enough. It is my belief that such an extension of estimating combination weights can usefully serve in several ways to illuminate the potential difference of choosing a realistic prior over traditional ones in the context of forecast combination and the importance of penalizing the least square estimator when the underlying models perform poorly over time. It also paves a way to extend the current results to density forecast combination that can be applied to risk management. A range of Monte Carlo studies that mimics the properties of financial time series and two applications are carried out to compare the robustness of our estimator. 由於未知的形式結構模型錯誤的發生變化，已經達成共識，組合預測可以提高 個人預測模型的均方誤差性能。 然而，在過去的幾十年裡，實證結果總是表明，簡單的平均預測往往跑贏理論上的最佳方法。因此，大量的文獻提出了不同的估計解釋和解決這一長期存在的難題。 在這個項目中，提出了組合預測的貝葉斯壓縮估計。它匯集了本人和其他早期的工作，形成一個強大的貝葉斯估計是優於簡單的平均，且易於計算。 貝葉斯計量經濟學的爭議和困難之一是要事先估計的參數選擇。實證的難題提示我們可以簡單平均為事先估計的係數。但是，我們要弄清楚傳統的天然共軛是否適當，因為這個”事先估計”假定回歸係數和誤方差存在著某特定的依賴結構。證明此結構的真確性並不容易。儘管它引身出來的方程式很簡單，但是它並不能容納隨著時間推移的轉變。例如，金融時間序列的特點是它的誤差分佈可能是柯西或平面尾的誤差分佈。這可能會引致回歸係數的不穏定性。因此，我們嘗試把這個係數和方差之間的依賴結構移除。 不同於現有的估計，我們估計的方程式跟現在的預測誤差建立了關連。也就是說，它會自動調整。 我相信這個組合權重可以有效地應用到風險管理。在此項目，我們還會進行一系列的蒙特卡洛實驗以比較其他的方程式及我們的方程式的穩健性。

255212.label: Realisation of objectives
255212.value: The 5 objectives (in the following squared brackets) can be summarized to 3 (a) to find a better way to combine forecast to deal with non-normal distributions often occur in real life data [1,2]; (b) to find a way that can estimate the probability of the combined forecasts [4]; (c) to assess the proposed method with existing ones using financial data [3,5]. All the objectives have generally been achieved through 1 published paper, 1 working paper (to be submitted by the August/September of 2016) and 1 working paper (to be submitted by June 2017). Although I have extended the existing forecast combination method to probability forecast combination, I did not use the Cauchy type g-prior in the analysis. To capture the fat-tailed distribution, I find that there is a more flexible way to solve the problem. The density forecasting method as stated in the next paragraph allows a wide variety of distributions. More importantly, the distribution can be time-varying. Because tourism growth rates data are readily available, I started to examine the relationship between error distributions and forecast density. As stated in the proposal, empirical data seldom exhibits normality. In our density forecasting model using tourism growth rates data, we find that the error distributions of the 2 chosen territories (China and Macau) are time-varying. Not only do the error distributions in the China model change over time, it also exhibits heavy-tailed and normal distributions interchangeably. Alternatively, although the error distributions of Macau are generally normal, their means and variances are changing over time. The standard deviations tend to be larger during turbulent period. To “decide” the appropriate distributions, I adopted the use of probability integral transform proposed by Rosenblatt (1952) and Diebold, Gunther and Tay (1998). The idea is that if the estimated cumulative distribution function (CDF) is appropriate, then the CDF evaluated at the actual observations should be uniformly distributed. Equivalently, I just need to obtain a time series of probability integral transform in the out-of-sample period and examine if they follow uniform distribution. One of the merits of this methodology to generate density forecasts can allow us to see the relative location of the actual observation with respect to the density forecast. If the actual observation turns out to appear in the tails of the density forecast, it signals a potential structural break. Another merit is that the quality of the mean forecast can be assessed. Traditionally, whether a forecasting model is good or not is usually evaluated on the mean-square-error basis. Because the current methodology estimates the full density of the forecasts, additional information as to the forecast quality can help in risk management. When the estimated standard error of the density is large, the user of the forecasts can be more cautious in terms of investment planning. The work has just been published in the Annals of Tourism Research. The part on structural break mentioned above was asked to split into another paper. In the original paper, a series of model selection tools for density forecasts such as Kullback-Leibler information criterion, Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Anderson-Darling tests, Berkowitz (2001) tests. In addition, the density forecasts were extended to 3-step ahead. So, all these will be applied to a new data set. I expect the working paper can be done by the end of June 2017. Secondly, the major objective of this proposal is forecasts combination which allows studying the probability of occurrence of certain events. As a result, the forecasting combination framework is no longer linear as stated in the proposal. Existing literature on combining probability forecasts mainly considers linear opinion pool, logarithmic opinion pool and the highly nonlinear method by Kamstra and Kennedy (1998). Recently, Zhang, Lu and Zou (2013) proposed an adaptive forecasting approach which assigns larger weights to the forecasts with higher likelihood value in the out-of-sample period. Stimulated by their work, I added to the proposal the evaluation of existing literature in decision making and a Bayesian machine learning approach in combining probability forecasts. I propose to refine the combination procedure by fitting the adaptive boosting classification (AdaBoost) to the framework. Because there are a few variants of AdaBoost such as real AdaBoost and LogitBoost, the working paper is in the stage of selecting the best approach for the market trend prediction. Since the time varying predictability of the regressors for market trends is most likely attributed to the presence of structural breaks, I adopt the rolling framework and investigate whether the performance of combined forecasts is linked to the business cycles. Given the structural breaks, I also examined if the model selection can choose the representative one for each period. The results turn out the forecast combination still dominates the single forecasting model. In terms of empirical study, since Kole and van Dijk (2016) find that Markov Switching model produces superior forecasts and lead to significantly better out-of-sample performance than rule-based methods such as Bry and Boschan (1971) algorithm or simple moving average, we define the two regimes of the markets by this parametric method. Using both financial and macroeconomic variable data for predicting market trends from 1987M1 to 2015M12, I find that dynamic model is better than static model in both in-sample and out-of-sample periods. Besides, the approach by Kamstra and Kennedy is subject to some limitation, namely, the reliance of the log-odds ratio may yield undefined forecast when the forecasts are close to either 0 and 1, while the linear opinion pool may yield probability forecasts that are outside the unit interval. The probability combination approach using model selection criterion such as Pseudo R-square dominate simple mean, geometric mean, and other more sophisticated methods such as linear opinion pool, logarithmic opinion pool, and adaptive forecasting approach. Existing literature basically picks the “best” model with the lowest quadratic probability score. However, in this working paper, I propose to use Diebold and Mariano (1995) type test statistics and likelihood ratio statistics to evaluate various forecast combination methods. I expect the part on AdaBoost and the write-up can be finished by the end of September 2016.

255212.label: Major findings and research outcome
255212.value: The first major finding is on the role of error distributions in forecasting. The approach is to directly assume error distribution in the forecasting model. The research has important practical outcomes. Traditional mean point forecasts can at best provide a general trend of the time series, and mean square error can only summarize the model performance in the out-of-sample period. Without considering forecast quality, we cannot even assess the accuracy at each time point. Because it is an essential piece of information in risk management, it is necessary to include such a measurement in the empirical analysis. Density forecasts and the evaluation tool introduced in this paper provide a flexible way to accommodate all kinds of distributions. The methodology is used to forecast the growth rates of tourism demand. Using a simple autoregressive distributed lag model, not only can I derive a time series of mean forecasts, I can also derive the standard error associated with each mean forecast. The larger the standard error, the lower is the quality of the point forecast. The practitioners and investors in the industry can then capitalize on the potential investment opportunities and to avoid business planning mistakes. The second major finding is on the forecast combination that can address the probability of events. Research in this area is quite different from combining forecasts for continuous random variables as the framework is changed from linear to nonlinear. The difficulty arising in this literature is that the forecasts have to be within the unit interval and the statistical tools for selecting the model. My working paper addresses both problems. Using financial and macroeconomic data for predicting stock markets trends, I find that simple mean is not always superior to other statistical methods. However, combination methods based on model selection criterion are better than those statistical methods including the adaptive forecasting approach weighted by the likelihood value in the out-of-sample period. To evaluate various combination methods, existing literature emphasizes on comparison of the magnitude of quadratic probability score (QPS, similar to MSE). However, the QPS difference can be simply due to sampling error. Therefore, we quantify the differences by using Diebold and Mariano type statistic and likelihood ratio tests to select models. Using historical average as the benchmark, we find that all variables have predictive power; dynamic models are generally better than static models; combined probability forecasts generally better than single model.

255212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
255212.value: As said in Section 5.3, I was asked to split the structural breaks out from the density forecasting paper. For that part, I plan to modify the error distributions which can accommodate autocorrelation structure and heteroskedasticity dynamics such as ARCH type errors. The structural break indicator is proposed and applied to detect breaks in oil price, housing trends and stock markets. Secondly, my current finding suggests that using model selection approach to select the best predictor is better than combined forecasts in some cases. Therefore, I have started to investigate whether AdaBoost classification techniques can help improve the forecast. The part is to be included in the same paper. On the other hand, my current focus is on the probability of events that take 2 possible outcomes at this stage linking the actual binary observations to a set of probability forecasts. However, when both left and right hand side are density functions, more difficulties arise. I am now trying to merge the above density forecast and probability forecasts combination to answer this question. One of the references is Lu and Su (2015) who adopts the jackknife approach to combine probabilities.

255212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
255212.value: The main objective of this project is to provide additional information to the users of forecasts. Investors always need to gauge the trends of the industry or the trends in the stock markets before making business plans. Given numerous forecasts provided by the analysts, the investors may be confused especially when the range of the forecasts is huge. This project makes 2 contributions. First, we inform the forecasts users about the quality of the forecasts. The methodology is easy to use and at the same time provide a number that quantifies the quality of the point forecast, namely, the time-varying standard deviation. Our results suggest that quality of forecasts deteriorate during the times when the economy is under the influence of extreme good/ bad events. It means that even when the forecast is very good, an investor must be careful in decision making as the forecast quality is bad. Second, we propose a way on how to utilize the given probability forecasts. One way is to combine them, another is to select the best at each time period. When the predictability of the variables is not known a priori, investors can use either way to get a more accurate one.

255312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
255312.value: Previous research in marketing channels has identified mechanisms such as monitoring and incentive devices to deter opportunism by exchange partners (Wathne and Heide 2000). However, whether and how disciplinary actions or punishment can be employed as an effective tool to manage partners’ ex post opportunism remains unclear. In conventional marketing literature, punishment is discouraged because it is thought to produce undesirable outcomes to the relationship such as conflict (Frazier and Summers 1984), lower satisfaction (Geyskens, Steenkamp, and Kumar, 1999), or retaliation (Kumar, Scheer, and Steenkamp 1998). This view dominates in the literature, despite some evidence suggesting that punishment can actually result in positive outcomes (Antia et al. 2006; Henrich 2006; Scheer 1993). In this proposed study, we extend beyond the dyadic view of punishment between a manufacturer and distributor. We consider the effect of punishment on observers – other distributors in the channel network who take an interest in the punishment of a focal one. We argue that a punishment event not only affects the disciplined distributor, but also changes the attitudes and behavior of those in the same distribution network (i.e. observers). In particular, when punishment is viewed as a social event, it implies social norms within the network of relationships, signals appropriate and inappropriate behaviors to observers, and creates perceptions of the manufacture as fair or unfair. From this social perspective, punishment has a significant effect on deterring observers’ subsequent opportunism. This “observer effect” is more critical to the manufacturer’s overall strategy, as it has an impact on a greater number of participants. Integrating insights from deterrence theory, fairness theory, and social network theory, we aim to develop a framework on the social effects of punishment in a distribution network. Our investigation will be based on a survey of distributors from multiple industries in China, with three specific research questions: (1) How a punishment event can directly deter observers’ ex post opportunism? (2) How fairness judgment of the event builds up observers’ trust towards the manufacturer, which explains their reduced opportunism? (3) How the disciplined distributor’s network embeddedness and the manufacturer’s monitoring capability can moderate the direct and the indirect mechanisms as described in (1) and (2) to reduce opportunism. By addressing these questions, the study will not only contribute to a broader understanding of using punishment to manage opportunism in channel governance, but also provide important implications for companies to develop trust and cooperation in channel relationships in China.

255312.label: Major findings and research outcome
255312.value: The GRF has been developed very smooth. I was able to use the fund to conduct two major data collections. The results from the first data collection was published in a Top journal at Journal of Marketing Research. The following summaries the major findings. In a distribution network, a punishment event not only affects the disciplined distributor but also changes the attitudes and behaviors of others in the network (i.e., observers). By moving beyond a dyadic view of punishment, this article considers the effects of punishment on observers and integrates insights from social learning, fairness heuristic, and social network theories. The resulting framework of the observer effects of punishment in a distribution network, empirically tested with a survey in China, reveals two mechanisms through which punishment leads to reduced observer opportunism: (1) a direct deterrence effect and (2) a trust-building process. Moreover, two information-related constructs moderate the observer effects differently. The disciplined distributor’s relational embeddedness, which motivates greater information flow to observers, aggravates the problem of information asymmetry against the manufacturer, making punishment less deterrent for observers. In contrast, the manufacturer’s monitoring capability, which reduces information asymmetry, strengthens observer effects. Due to the encouraging results, we employed the remaining amount to conduct another firm survey. We designed the questionnaire, conducted the survey, and collected the data in 2014-2015. Based on the results, two studies were developed. The first study takes an interesting perspective to understand the double-edged effect of CMO overconfidence on firms' market strategies. The study received Best Paper Award in the 2014 Academy of Management Meeting (in Business Policy & Strategy Track). The paper has been survived the second round, but unfortunately was rejected at the third round review at Strategic Management Journal. After substantial revisions and re-positioning, the paper is now at the final stage to be submitted to Journal of Marketing. Another paper investigates distributors' intrachannel and interchannel behaviors under different boundary conditions. In supplier–distributor exchanges, a market exploitation (intrachannel) strategy emphasizes a distributor’s commitment to its incumbent supplier, whereas a market exploration (interchannel) strategy implies the distributor’s efforts to consider, contact, and seek new suppliers for business opportunities. We target to submit the study for review at Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science.

255312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
255312.value: Conventional wisdom in marketing encourages the use of positive mechanisms, such as monitoring and incentive devices, to safeguard exchange relationships against opportunism. The effectiveness of using disciplinary actions to govern channel relationships however remains unclear. The study highlights the possibility of using punishment to influence network members’ opportunism. This study suggests that although punishment can be a viable tool, manufacturers should assess the situation before any action is taken. If a misbehaving distributor has deep connections with other distributors in the network, severe punishment may go against the manufacturer’s interest, due to the negative reactions from interconnected distributors. Thus, a certain level of tolerance or a more lenient and private approach of punishment may be necessary. At the same time, manufacturers should actively develop their monitoring capabilities, to reduce information asymmetry, align with distributor interests, and build a reputation for fairness and consistency. Strong monitoring capabilities enable managers to impose severe punishment in an attention-grabbing manner while gaining positive reactions from channel members.

260712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
260712.value: The incidence of cardiovascular diseases increases after menopause and at any age postmenopausal women have a significantly higher incidence of CVD compared to premenopausal women. The effect of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) in the prevention of CVD is still under debate. The randomized studies (Heart and Estrogen/Progestin Replacement Study [HERS] and Women's Health Initiative [WHI]) both raised concerns about findings from observational studies but differed on findings related to coronary heart disease. These and other findings have led to great interest in alternative therapies for menopause for improving cardiovascular outcomes has increased dramatically. Black teas are rich dietary sources of flavonoids. Black tea polyphenols including theaflavin (TF1), theaflvin-3-monogallate (TF2A), theaflavin-3’-monogallate (TF2B), and theaflavin-3,3’-digallate (TF3) are derived from catechins by polyphenol oxidase during the fermentation process. Theaflavins have anti-oxidative effects that protects the endothelium from damage by free redicals. The cardiovascular health benefits of drinking tea are thought to be largely due to flavonoids. Tea intake and intake of flavonoids found in tea have been associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular disease in cross-sectional and prospective population studies. Isolated flavonoids found in tea have also been consistently shown to inhibit the development of atherosclerosis in animal models. Several studies show that tea and tea flavonoids enhance nitric oxide status and improve endothelial function, which may be at least partly responsible for benefits on cardiovascular health. Despite the therapeutic benefit of black tea consumption, the mechanisms underlying vascular dysfunction in estrogen deficiency remains elusive. The purpose of the present study is to investigate whether black tea extract (BTE) and TF3 protects endothelial function in estrogen deficiency and possible mechanisms involved. Based on our preliminary data, we hypothesize that BTE improves endothelial dysfunction by activation of PPAR and inhibition of endoplasmic reticulum stress pathways. The proposed research will focus on the protective roles of BTE in improvement of endothelial dysfunction in ovariectomized rats and will examine the important signaling pathways such as PPAR and ER stress. The possibilities include several therapeutic targets in vascular disease, such as eNOS, ROS and ER stress -related markers. The findings will provide scientific support for the role of BTE as a potentially important regimen in the prevention and treatment of estrogen deficiency-related vascular disease by using knockout mice. 260712.label: Major findings and research outcome
260712.value: The present study demonstrates that a 4-week treatment with BT restores the impaired EDRs in renal arteries and aortae of OVT rats. The flow-mediated dilatations in the third-order mesenteric arteries were also augmented in OVX rats receiving BT treatment. These effects are likely associated with an increase in NO bioavailability. We showed for the first time that black tea treatment reduces oxidative stress in aortas of OVX rats, which is associated with the inhibition of NAD(P)H oxidase. The elevated production of ROS, especially superoxide anions is known to inactivate NO, thus to impair endothelial function. Moreover, We observed impaired vasodilatation, up-regulated levels of plasma Hcy, reduced Hcy metabolic enzymes, and increased ER stress markers and ROS generation in aortae from chronic Ang II-infused rats, which were reversed by chronic administration of black tea extract in vivo. The major novel results include (i) black tea extract and its major theaflavins TF3 ex vivo reverse Hcy-induced endothelial dysfunction and Hcy-elevated ER stress in rat aortae; (ii) black tea extract treatment normalizes plasma Hcy levels in Ang II-infused rats, and mitigates high blood pressure; (iii) chronic black tea extract treatment reverses the attenuated endothelium-dependent relaxations in aortae, carotid and renal arteries as well as flow-mediated dilatations (FMD) in third-order mesenteric resistance arteries, accompanied by inhibition of ER stress and up-regulation of Hcy metabolic enzymes (CBS and CSE) in the Ang II-infused rats; and (iv) black tea extract and TF3 normalized the elevated ROS generation in RAECs treated with Hcy and in the aortae of Ang II-infused rats.

260712.value: We suggest to preform the metabolic profile response to administration of black tea extract or theaflavins in hypertensive rats and ovariectomized rats. Furthermore, we can identify candidate marker metabolites associated with black tea extract or theaflavins.

260712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
260712.value: Drinking tea regularly as part of a healthy lifestyle may help maintain a healthy heart. Numerous population health studies demonstrated that drinking tea is linked to a reduced risk of cardiovascular disease. Our research reveals the novel benefits of chronic black tea consumption to reverse endothelial dysfunction and favorably modifying cholesterol profile in a rat model of estrogen deficiency and provides insights into developing black tea as beneficial dietary supplements for postmenopausal women. In addition, our findings found the novel cardiovascular benefits of black tea in ameliorating vascular dysfunctions through alleviation of endoplasmic reticulum stress, which provide insight into developing black tea into beneficial dietary supplements for hypertensive patient.

261312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
261312.value: Studying physiological adaptation to environmental stress at molecular level can help us understand why some species can live in extreme environments, predict the impact of environmental change on the distribution of a species, and discover the evolutionary course of stress tolerance. This study aims to understand the molecular mechanisms of adaptation to several environmental stressors (desiccation, heat and hypoxia) in the apple snail Pomacea canaliculata, an invasive species native to South America now widely distributed in freshwater wetlands of Asia, causing tremendous loss to the rice and vegetable agriculture. We will compare the proteomic responses of P. canaliculata to desiccation, heat and hypoxia under normal and stressed conditions. For each stressor, a time-course study will be conducted to distinguish immediate and prolonged responses, and to test a specific working hypothesis (e.g. roles of the uric acid cycle for desiccation resistance). In addition, we will determine how Pomacea canaliculata (invasive species) and Pomacea diffusa (non-invasive species) respond differently to the same level of stress. The samples will be labeled using an isobaric tagging method, and the differentially expressed proteins will be identified through shotgun quantitative proteomics, followed by determination of protein functional pathways involved in stress responses. To confirm the up- or down-regulation of a set of differentially expressed proteins, RNA will be extracted and Real-Time PCR will be performed. Overall, this study will allow us to gain insight into the molecular mechanisms of adaptation in P. canaliculata, which may help us understand why it is invasive while its congener P. diffusa is non-invasive. The proteomic data from this study may laid a foundation for further research leading to biological control of the pest using immunocontraception. 从分子水平上研究生物体对环境胁迫的生理性适应机制，有助于我们理解生物体如何在极端的环境下生存，进而推断环境的改变对物种分布及扩散的影响，揭示物种胁迫耐受的进化过程。本研究旨在将高通量的转录组学及蛋白质组学的技术相结合，利用高通量的标签测序定量同位素标记的方法研究一种广泛分布的入侵种福寿螺在响应长短期高温和缺氧胁迫时自身及两者间的基因和蛋白质表达水平的变化，找出与高温,干旱和缺氧胁迫相关的基因和代谢通路，阐明福寿螺应对长短期环境胁迫时各自的分子机制。本研究的实验方案将为研究其他非模式生物对环境因子的应答机制提供重要的参考。

261512.value: DKK3在卵巢癌及其轉移的作用

261512.label: Project Objectives
261512.value: To characterize the effects Dkk3 in ovarian cancer tumorigenesis and metastasis. To delineate the molecular pathways in which Dkk3 is involved in ovarian cancer. To evaluate the clinical relevance of Dkk3 in ovarian cancer.
rows: To characterize the effects Dkk3 in ovarian cancer tumorigenesis and metastasis.
To delineate the molecular pathways in which Dkk3 is involved in ovarian cancer.
To evaluate the clinical relevance of Dkk3 in ovarian cancer.

261512.label: Realisation of objectives
261512.value: For objective 1, we have established several Dkk3 stably expressing ovarian cancer cell lines in SKOV-3, OVCA433, OVCA420, OVCAR3, TOV-21G and TOV-122D cells. We have also established a Dkk3 stably knocked down immortalized normal ovarian cell line in HOSE6-3 cells by lentiviral infection of shRNA. In addition, we have established luciferase stably expressing ovarian cancer cell lines (SKOV-3, OVCA433, OVCA420 and OVCAR3). We have confirmed luciferase expression in animals with the animal imaging system. Our results showed that growth rate of luciferase stably expressing ovarian cancer cells were similar to their parental cells. For the in vitro tumor suppressive function of Dkk3, we found that the growth rate of Dkk3 stably expressing ovarian cancer cells was reduced when compared with their parental cells. We also found a reduced size and number of colonies of Dkk3 stably expressing ovarian cancer cells compared with their parental cancer cells in the soft agar colony formation assay. Expression of Dkk3 in ovarian cancer cells increased apoptosis by upregulating the activity of caspase proteins and expression of p21, p53 and PUMA. Dkk3 overexpression also induced cell cycle arrest at the G0/G1 phase and reduced cell proliferation. In in vivo studies, in the orthotopic mouse model, Dkk3 overexpressing SKOV-3 cell lines had reduced tumor sizes when compared to control. As the other ovarian cancer cell lines did not respond well in the orthotopic model, we instead used the xenograft mouse model. In this model too, Dkk3 overexpression led to a reduction in tumor size. We have tried to establish HOSE6-3 orthotopic and xenograft mouse models, but were unsuccessful. For objective 2, we have found that Dkk3 stable overexpression inhibited cell invasiveness and migration in the matrigel invasion and cell migration assays. In the metastatic mouse model, bioluminescent imaging analysis and dissection revealed that the spread of cancer and the number of metastatic tumors in mice were suppressed in mice injected with Dkk3 expressing cells when compared to parental cells. For morphological analysis of Dkk3 expressing cells, Dkk3 expression upregulated E-, P- and N-cadherin when compared to control cells. Dkk3 expressing cells displayed a more compact morphology than controls, adhering closely to their neighbouring cells and an increased actin fiber expression, suggesting a less invasive phenotype. In Dkk3 expressing stable clones, we observed a downregulation of vimentin, Snail and Twist, also indicating a decrease in invasiveness. We found that Dkk3 stably expressing ovarian cancer cells had lower overall levels of β-catenin and an increased ratio of cytoplasmic : nuclear localization of β-catenin when compared to control. Together with results from the TOPFlash reporter system, where we found that Wnt signaling activity was reduced in Dkk3 stably expressing controls, it suggested that Dkk3 expression could inhibit canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Dkk3 stably expressing ovarian cancer cells exhibited downregulated phospho-JNK and Dvl3, and led to a strong inhibition in cell invasiveness, indicating a role for Dkk3 in the non-canonical Wnt/Planar Cell Polarity pathway. We also found that Rho family GTPase activities (RhoA and cdc42) were downregulated in Dkk3 expressing cell lines when compared to parental cells. In addition, inhibition of JNK or RhoA in Dkk3 knockout clones also led to a decrease in cell invasiveness, while expression of a dominant active form of JNK or RhoA in Dkk3 stably expressing clones led to an increase in cell invasiveness. For objective 3, over 90% of clinical samples had downregulated Dkk3 at both the mRNA and protein expression levels. We did not find any correlation between Dkk3 expression and any clinicopathological parameters. As Dkk3 is a Wnt signaling inhibitor, we further investigated the relationship between Dkk3 and other Wnt inhibitors, such as the secreted frizzled related protein family, and found a correlation between the mRNA levels of Dkk3 and sFRP5.

261512.label: Major findings and research outcome
261512.value: 1. We have demonstrated Dkk3 indeed has tumor suppressive function in ovarian cancer. In cell lines, Dkk3 could induce apoptosis by upgregulating caspase proteins as well as p53 and p21. Additionally, Dkk3 could induce G0/G1 phase cell cycle arrest and reduce cell proliferation. Expression of Dkk3 could reduce tumor size in animal models. 2. We found that expression of Dkk3 could inhibit invasiveness and migration in vitro, and in the metastatic mouse model. In cell lines, Dkk3 could upregulate E-, P- and N-cadherin and increase actin fibre expression, inducing a less invasive phenotype. Dkk3 also affected EMT, a key step in the progression of tumors towards metastasis and invasion. Dkk3 upregulated E-cadherin and downregulated vimentin, Snail and Twist. Dkk3 is indeed involved in Wnt signaling. We have demonstrated that expression of Dkk3 could reduce Wnt signaling activity and also inhibit β-catenin expression and decrease its nuclear translocation, indicating that Dkk3 is involved in the canonical Wnt signaling pathway. We also found that Dkk3 could downregulate p-JNK and Dvl3 as well as RhoA and cdc42 GTPase activities, indicating that Dkk3 also plays a role in the non-canonical Wnt/Planar cell polarity pathway, which is important for cancer metastasis. 3. Over 90% of clinical samples exhibited downregulation of Dkk3 at the mRNA and protein levels. We did not find any statistically significant correlation between Dkk3 and any clinicopathological features. However, we did find a statistically significant correlation between mRNA levels of Dkk3 and sFRP5, a Wnt inhibitor in the secreted frizzled related protein family

261512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
261512.value: In this project, we have identified the anti-tumorigenic function of Dkk3 in ovarian cancer, through cell cycle arrest, induction of apoptosis, and inhibition of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. We have also identified the anti-metastatic function of Dkk3 in ovarian cancer, through inhibition of epithelial to mesenchymal transition, Rho GTPase activities, and the non-canonical Wnt/Planar cell polarity pathway. We believe that our comprehensive study on the function of Dkk3 in this project could potentially be applied for the development of Dkk3 as a new therapeutic intervention and potential identification of novel biomarkers for the early detection of ovarian cancer.

261512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
261512.value: Ovarian cancer is the leading cause of death in gynecologic malignancies worldwide. More than 70% of ovarian cancer patients are diagnosed at a late stage, where the cancer has already metastasized. This late diagnosis leads to a poor overall prognosis for ovarian cancer patients. In this project, we have clearly demonstrated that Dkk3 plays a tumor suppressive and anti-metastatic role in ovarian cancer. Dkk3 is a known inhibitor of the Wnt signaling pathway, a pathway important in cancer. We found that Dkk3 inhibited tumor growth through cell cycle arrest, induction of apoptosis, and inhibition of the canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Dkk3 inhibited metastasis and invasion through inhibition of epithelial to mesenchymal transition, Rho GTPase activities, and the non-canonical Wnt/Planar cell polarity pathway. We have also found that Dkk3 is downregulated in a large majority of ovarian cancer patient samples. By understanding the above mechanisms, we can gain insight for the development of Dkk3 as a new therapeutic intervention for ovarian cancer.

261812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
261812.value: Endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) have been shown to cause long-term effects on animal health and development. Emerging evidence suggests that endocrine disruption that are caused by pollutants is directly linked to “the developmental basis of adult disease”, leading to the predisposition for disease or organ dysfunction. The incidence of obesity, diabetes and fatty liver diseases has become highly prevalent globally, but the possible underlying mechanistic action on how EDC’s predispose humans to these metabolic disorders is still a clear mystery. Epidemiological studies in numerous disasters have suggested the link between pollutant exposure to disturbed glucose homeostasis, metabolic syndrome and insulin resistance. Numerous laboratory animal studies have also shown that exposure of mice to the fluorinated compounds (perfluoroalkyl acids, PFAAs) can result in the development of metabolic disorder. However a lot more needs to be done to understand the mechanistic actions involved. PFAAs are persistent in the environment, ubiquitous to the general public and have a long serum elimination half-life in animals. The notorious member of PFAAs, perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) is prioritized as a global concerning chemical at the Stockholm Convention in 2009, due to its serious harmful effects in mammals and aquatic organisms. Industrial production of PFOS has already been phased out in most countries in 2002, except in China where it’s still manufactured and widely used today. In our region, PFAA contamination has been reported in the environment (i.e. water and dust), food and human blood samples, implying the exposure risk of our population to PFAAs. In this proposal, we plan to pin down the molecular targets of PFAA and the associated hormonal and metabolic changes in PFAA-elicited metabolic syndromes, which would help to significantly further our understanding on the non-genetic causes/origin of these metabolic diseases. We will combine molecular, metabolomics and physiological approaches to obtain multiple lines of evidence to identify the molecular targets of PFAAs as well as the consequential molecular fingerprints in blood serum and liver extracts. Using perinatal animal exposure models, the underlying mechanistic actions of PFAAs to adipocytes, pancreatic islets and liver physiology will be deciphered. The findings of this study will help to evaluate the risk of public exposure to PFAAs and its underlying mechanistic actions on human health. This understanding will provide insight for the respective policy makers to devise the appropriate remedial strategies, hence providing long term benefits to the community. 內分泌干擾物已被證明對動物的健康和發育造成長期的影響。新興的證據表明，由於污染所應其的內分泌干擾是直接關係到“成年疾病發展的基礎”，它能導致疾病或器官功能障礙的傾向。肥胖，糖尿病和脂肪肝的發病率已經在全球範圍內非常普遍，但其隱含的機理對於內分泌干擾物如何作用於這些代謝紊亂易患人群卻依然是一個迷。在眾多的災害流行病學研究中表明，污染物的暴露對干擾血糖平衡，代謝綜合症和胰島素抵抗有著直接存在的聯繫。許多動物研究實驗還表明，小鼠暴露於含氟化合物（全氟烷基酸，PFAAs）可導致發展成為代謝紊亂。但是要進一步了解其所涉及的機理， 依然還有許多研究需要從事。 PFAAs可持久存在於環境中，其在公共生活中無處不在，並在動物體中擁有很長的血消除半衰期。作為臭名昭著的PFAAs成員，全氟辛烷磺酸（PFOS）由於其對哺乳動物和水生生物有嚴重的危害，它已在2009年的斯德哥爾摩公約上被優先作為一個全球性化學品所關注。在2002年，含有PFOS的商品已被大多數國家所淘汰，但在中國其生產和廣泛的使用仍然至今。在我們地區，PFAA的污染已在環境（例如水和灰塵），食物和人血樣本中被報導，這意味著我們存在於PFAA暴露的風險中。在此提議中，我們計劃在由PFAA引起的代謝綜合症中，辨認 PFAA的分子靶點和相關激素和代謝變化，這些將對進一步了解由非遺傳原因/起源所造成的代謝疾病有所幫助。 我們將結合分子生物學，代謝組學及生理學方法來獲得多方面的證據，以確定PFAAs的分子靶點以及血清和肝臟提取物相應的特徵。運用孕期動物暴露模型，可破譯PFAAs如何影響脂肪細胞，胰島細胞和肝臟生理所隱含的機理。這項研究的結果將有助於評估公眾對於PFAAs的暴露及其潛在的機理對人體健康的風險。這一理解將為相應的政策制定者提供洞察力，制定適當的補救策略，從而為社會提供長遠利益。
