rows: We have explored the impact of a retailer's quality gatekeeping activity on pricing and quality assurance in a supply chain, which originates from the practices of Wal-Mart, Asda, and Tesco. We have proposed two papers for the research project, which are expected to contribute to the marketing and OM literature, and help practitioners successfully implement the pricing and quality strategies. Even though one paper has been published in European Journal of Operational Research, the other paper is under review in Production and Operations Management. Next, we will work on the second paper and try our best to publish it in Production and Operations Management.

In the paper that is under review in Production and Operations Management, we have analyzed two leader-follower game problems, where the manufacturer determines a wholesale price and a defective rate as a "leader," and the retailer decides on her retail price and identification rate (when she serves a quality gatekeeper). Next, we may improve our game analysis to consider some more cases. Moreover, in the paper that has been published in European Journal of Operational Research, we have used cooperative game theory to find the negotiated retail price for each consumer, and derive the expected demand function. Such a modeling approach (i.e., the application of cooperative game theory for finding a demand function) is new to the literature. In future, we may use the approach to investigate more problems.

We have examined if the retailer can benefit from her quality gatekeeping effort and thus have an incentive to participate in the quality assurance. This is important because, otherwise, the retailer does not intend to spend effort on the quality inspection. In our paper submitted to Production and Operations Management, we analytically showed that the retailer may or may not benefit from her quality gatekeeping, which depends on whether or not the retailer's gatekeeping can generate a channel-wide cost reduction. That is, if the gatekeeping activity leads to a positive channel-wide per unit cost saving, then the retailer should reduce her retail price, which leads to a higher demand and generates higher profits for the retailer. In future, we shall improve our game analysis and results according to referees and other scholars' comments.

We have discussed whether or not the manufacturer can benefit by achieving a higher profit from the quality gatekeeping activity at the retailing level. In our paper submitted to Production and Operations Management, we analytically proved that as a consequence of the quality gatekeeping at the retail level, whether or not the manufacturer's profit can increase also depends on the supply chain-wide cost reduction resulting from the retailer's gatekeeping. In future, we may further investigate such an issue when the manufacturer and the retailer adopt a cutoff level for the retailer to accept the manufacturer's products.

We have found that the retailer's gatekeeping is really useful to reducing the defective rate and increasing consumer demand. The retailer's quality gatekeeping strategy is effective in decreasing the channel-wide defective rate. Therefore, consumers can always enjoy a lower defective rate, when the retailer takes the quality gatekeeping responsibility. In future, we may examine the robustness of such an issue in other settings.

341012.label: Major findings and research outcome
341012.value: We have three research publications that appeared in EJOR (2014a and 2014b) and Production and Operations Management (POM 2015). In our paper POM (2015), we investigated a quality-assurance problem where a manufacturer supplies products with a defective rate to a retailer who then inspects the products as a quality gatekeeper. We summarize our most important analytic findings/insights as follows. First, as the unit penalty cost for the defects sold to consumers becomes higher, the manufacturer agrees to adopt a smaller average defective rate and the retailer reduces her gatekeeping intensity. Secondly, increasing the retailer's penalty charge for each identified defect can help reduce the average defective rate. Thirdly, the retailer's stronger relative bargaining power can always help increase the demand and channel-wide profit, regardless of whether the retailer takes on the gatekeeping responsibility. That is, the channel can always benefit more if the retailer is in a stronger position. Fourthly, the channel-wide defective rate can be reduced when the retailer's penalty charge for the manufacturer is sufficiently high. This shows the importance of the retailer's penalty charge to the effectiveness of the quality gatekeeping at the retail level. Fifthly, by comparing the pricing decisions with and without quality gatekeeping, we find that the change in the negotiated wholesale price only depends on the manufacturer's “individual” benefit, and the change in the retailer's optimal retail price is only related to the channel-wide benefit. Sixthly, the retailer's incentive to take on the quality gatekeeping responsibility depends on the impact of quality relative to retail price on the demand, and also increases with the retailer's relative bargaining power. In EJOR (2014a), we investigated an automobile supply chain where a manufacturer and a retailer serve heterogeneous consumers with electric vehicles under a government’s price-discount incentive scheme that involves a price discount rate and a subsidy ceiling. We showed that the subsidy ceiling is more effective in influencing the optimal wholesale pricing decision of the manufacturer with a higher unit production cost. In EJOR (2014b), we considered an automobile supply chain where a manufacturer and a retailer serve a market with a fuel-efficient automobile under a scrappage program by the government.

341012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
341012.value: For this project, we have successfully proposed three papers to investigate the supply chain problems with the quality concern. In POM (2015), we have analyzed a single retailer’s quality gatekeeping activity in a two-echelon supply chain. In reality, two retailers may compete in a market with pricing and quality decisions. In future, we would address the quality gatekeeping problem for the supply chain with a manufacturer and two retailers. Moreover, as quality greatly influences consumer purchases, we would also consider the competition between supply chains. In EJOR (2014a) we investigated an electronic vehicle supply chain in which only electronic vehicle is produced and sold. In the future, we plan to analyze the effect of price-discount schemes on a supply chain that produces both electronic and fuel vehicles. In EJOR (2014b) we considered a two-level automobile supply chain, where a manufacturer and a retailer serve heterogeneous consumers in a fuel-efficient automobile market under a government’s scrappage program. In future, we may investigate the manufacturer’s investment on its product design. We may also need to consider if and how the program can induce the manufacturer to invest in designing a green automobile for environment protection.

341012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
341012.value: In POM (2015), we have found that the retailer's higher penalty charge can help reduce the manufacturer's average defective rate that results from the negotiation between the manufacturer and the retailer. The channel can always benefit more if the retailer's relative bargaining power is stronger, regardless of whether the retailer takes on the gatekeeping responsibility. Moreover, the retailer's quality gatekeeping can decrease the average defective rate faced by consumers, if her penalty charge for each identified defect is sufficiently high. As a result of the retailer's gatekeeping, the change in the negotiated wholesale price only depends on the manufacturer's individual benefit, whereas the change in the retailer's optimal retail price is associated with the channel-wide benefit. In addition, the retailer's incentive to take on the quality gatekeeping responsibility depends on the impact of quality relative to retail price on demand, and it increases with the retailer's relative bargaining power. In EJOR (2014a), we have concluded that an effective incentive scheme should include both a discount rate and a subsidy ceiling. In EJOR (2014b), we have obtained specific conditions under which a manufacturer may be unwilling to qualify for a government’s scrappage program.

341512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
341512.value: 中國九世紀的譯語人及與東亞的語際交流:以日本圓仁法師838-847年間入華的遊記為依據

341512.label: Project Objectives
341512.value: To analyze the language mediating roles and activities of interpreters in the exchanges between the Chinese and other East Asian peoples in late Tang China in the 9th century. To examine the specific nature and features of interpreting events in the late Tang Chinese society, as witnessed by monk Ennin in the 9th century. To analyze the social identities and linguistic backgrounds of these East Asian interpreters who seemed to have been regular (community or group) rather than isolated interpreting personnel at the time. To examine the criteria and channels from which the Japanese imperial court select interpreters to be included in its embassy. To trace and analyze the emergence of Korean communities and Sillan interpreters in Tang China. To provide evidence verifying the potential theoretical link between certain political landscapes and the predominance of interpreters belonging to a particular ethnic group.

341512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
341512.value: Tang China (618–907) was a time of unprecedented cross-cultural communications in Asia. Language mediators played a critical role in these interlingual and intercultural exchanges in China’s international experience in Tang time. The data source of this project is based on a close reading of Japanese monk Ennin’s (794–864) ethnographic diary 《入唐求法巡禮行記》, written in Chinese. This project will explore the specific identities, interpreting duties, non-interpreting duties, and roles of such linguistic mediators—interpreters, translators, or scribes—in bridging both the spoken and written language barriers between Chinese and Japanese interlocutors primarily. More precisely, the research questions include: Who were these mediators? What was their ethnic background? What were their linguistic background and the extent of their bilingual competence? How were some of these interpreters hired in Japan to be part of the China-bound embassy? How were some others recruited in China? How did they obtain the network to these interpreting assignments? What was the nature of these interpreting tasks? This subject is rarely approached in either the literature of Translation Studies or the historical study of translation in the Asian tradition. One way to understand these questions is through an empirical study of monk Ennin’s diary, which not only documents his nine-year China travel experience, but also presents plenty of concrete references to his and others’ interpreters and scribes at the time. This diary contains thirty-three entries about interpreters at the time. This authentic data source will give us objective and detailed information about the archived interpreters and interpreting events Ennin, with limited spoken Chinese competence, encountered, observed, and recorded. These factual descriptions would also provide a platform on which to undertake further analyses about the interpreting and mediating scenario of 9th-century China with its East Asian counterparts, which was not adequately covered in its official archives. This project has three objectives. The first objective is to examine language mediating and interpreting activities of which the Japanese embassy and Ennin were the interpreting patrons in China, from this dairy. The second objective is to analyze the social and linguistic identities of these interpreters and scribes in Ennin’s travel records and to understand the nature and features of such documented interpreting events that were largely left out in China’s standard archives. The third objective is to trace and analyze the emergence of Sillan (Korean) interpreters in Tang China who were known to be important go-betweens in the exchanges of Tang China and Japan at the time. 中國九世紀的譯語人及與東亞的語際交流:以日本圓仁法師838-847年間入華的遊記為依據 有唐一代（618-907），中國與亞洲各國的跨文化交流盛極一時。中國當時可算面向國際，此中，譯語人在有關的語際及文化交流活動中的角色十分關鍵。本研究的資料源自日本僧人圓仁法師（794-864）以漢語寫的遊記：《入唐求法巡禮行記》。本研究旨在深入探討當時中日兩國國民在口語及書面上的溝通模式，以帶出民間的譯語人的身份、口譯職能、非口譯職能，以及這些口譯人、筆譯人和寫手所起的各種作用。實際上，研究的問題包括：這些協助語際交流的人是誰？屬於什麼民族？其語言背景及掌握漢日雙語的水平如何？日本遣唐的使節團如何聘用這些譯語人？其他的譯語人又怎樣在中國境內獲得招攬的呢？這些譯語人何以在中國境內為不同民族作翻譯？他們是如何接到這些有報酬或沒有報酬的口譯工作的呢？他們的口譯工作有何特性？ 這個題材無論於亞洲的翻譯研究及歷史研究的文獻都很少見。為了就上述問題尋找答案，本研究擬深入研讀圓仁法師的遊記，了解其在華的九年日誌，透析其中所確切敘述有關當時他接觸的譯語人及寫手。憑藉此真確的資料來源，可客觀及仔細地知悉圓仁所描述其所接觸、觀察並紀錄的有關口譯活動。這些紀實的描述在某程度上補足了正史的紀錄，有助對中國與東南亞各國於九世紀時的口譯及翻譯情況，作進一步的分析。 本研究有三個目標。首先，通過圓仁的遊記，本研究旨在探討晚唐日本遣唐使與圓仁入華所涉及的語言交際和口譯活動。此外，由於中國正史有關這方面的口譯活動的篇幅甚少，本研究希望根據圓仁的遊記，可勾畫出這些譯語人及寫手的社會及語言背景，以祈深入了解當時口譯活動的特性。最後，由於當時唐朝與日本的交流往往通過新羅譯語進行，本研究亦旨在分析其冒起的歷程。

341512.label: Realisation of objectives
341512.value: Through careful readings and thorough textual analyses of Ennin's travelogue, I managed to realize all six objectives set out in my original grant proposal. My readings of relevant literature about the background of first-millennium East Asian exchanges in ancient China, Korea, and Japan, also serve to consolidate my grasp of the subject matter. In principle, the focus and objectives set for this project are realistic, and therefore with two years of hard work on this interesting and under-explored topic, I succeeded in completing the project with aims achieved. The focus of Ennin's diary as the major source of data for textual analyses enables me to ruminate, revisit, challenge what have been published in the literature. Eventually, I could come up with a more critical reading for this data source, which makes possible the writing of articles about Sillan interpreters from different perspectives. These were presented in international conferences over the two years of duration of this project. Some of these were accepted to be published in 2015.

341512.label: Major findings and research outcome
341512.value: First, unlike the conventional portrayal of interpreters who work behind the scenes anonymously, the Sillan interpreters referred to by Ennin were resourceful, active, and informative, with good social and commercial networks in China, Japan, and Silla. Second, the Sillan interpreters, like other foreign interpreting communities in first-millennium China, such as the Sogdians and the Tuyuhuns, did more than language mediation. Their multitasking competence in catering to the linguistic and para-linguistic needs for travelers coming into China at the time explains why they prospered for centuries in their respective spheres of influence on the Chinese territories. Third, Japanese monk Ennin’s (794‒864) travelogue of his decade-long (838–847) China pilgrimage contains thirty-eight references to Sillan interpreters. Written in the form of a diary, it is a significant first-hand archive that throws light on our understanding of Sillan interpreters and East Asian interpreting in the first millennium. Based on a close reading of this travelogue, I attempt to clarify the idiosyncratic title of ‘Sillan interpreters’. Fourth, using quantitative and qualitative analyses, I outline finer categories of these interpreters, which in turn address questions pertaining to their identities and roles. I demonstrate the values of empirically pursuing the definitions of ‘interpreter’ in a specific temporal and spatial context. It alerts interpreting researchers to the importance of thorough textual analysis in archival research. Fifth, I identify and discuss six anomalies of these Sillan interpreters. The finding is significant because the unorthodox traits of these East Asian interpreters substantially challenge our perceptions of interpreters in translation studies. Sixth, I identified twelve counts of face-to-face inter-lingual exchanges in which written Chinese was the exclusive medium to bridge the otherwise impossible communication between East Asian interlocutors. Based on these textual examples, an initial quantitative analysis is conducted, followed by a qualitative analysis through which the significance of this norm among the literate speakers in East Asia at the time is discussed. Seventh, Ennin's diary contains thirty-eight references to four Sillan interpreters, of whom one was an interpreting clerk affiliated with a sub-prefecture in eastern coastal China. He was also Ennin’s longest-serving interpreter, from 839 through 847, having been documented twenty-three times. This interpreting functionary, Yu Sinǒn, worked in a regional office of a Sillan enclave and assisted visitors from Japan and Silla. His work was expected to be law-abiding. Yet in his mediating services for Ennin, he frequently flouted the legal limits.

341512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
341512.value: This project opens up scope for further research about diplomatic and civilian (personal and commercial) exchanges in first-millennium East Asia. We are now better informed of the exchange scenario, with the various roles played by Sillan interpreters, at the time of Ennin's pilgrimage in the 9th century. How about the time before the Sillan unification of the Korean Peninsula in 668? I believe the historical archives of early imperial China would continue to be the most significant source from which to outline the features and patterns of earlier East Asian exchanges, especially when written Chinese was then the mandated written language for official writings at the time. I hope to be able to apply for yet another general research grant to pursue the topic on diplomatic and civilian East Asian exchanges in the first millennium.

341512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
341512.value: References to Sillan (ancient Korea) interpreters were prominently made dozens of times in Japanese monk Ennin’s travelogue, which documents his decade-long sojourn in late Tang China from 838–847. To have captured such textual attention, these interpreters must have offered Ennin (794–864), who did not speak Chinese, enormous mediating assistance. This first-hand source in the form of a diary, not commissioned by any imperial authorities, presents an objective account of the life, peoples, and languages in Tang China’s eastern coastal region. During this period of thriving diplomatic and commercial exchanges in East Asia, the mediating role of Sillan interpreters was pivotal. Yet, Sillan interpreters were never critically examined either in historical or interpreting studies. Besides, they were often sweepingly understood as a generic category of Sillans who interpreted between Sillan, Japanese and Chinese languages. Using quantitative and qualitative analyses, I outline finer categories of these interpreters, which in turn address questions pertaining to their identities and roles. This demonstrates the values of empirically pursuing the definitions of ‘interpreter’ in a specific temporal and spatial context. It alerts interpreting researchers to the importance of thorough textual analyses in archival research.

341612.label: Project Objectives
341612.value: To provide the first archival-based account of the political, social and economic history of Aral Sea crisis, with research both in central and peripheral archives. To produce a study about the history of the making and unmaking of the environment of the lower Syrdarya river, its delta and the Aral Sea in the twentieth century. To produce a study with a high comparative relevance for the analysis of state-led developmentalist projects having an impact on complex ecosystems in China. To provide a case-study limited geographically to the lower Syrdarya river, in order to better assess the water management strategies by the rural population and the local administration, and the impact of the degrading environmental situation, in postwar Kazakhstan. To produce a case-study of the social, environmental and economic medium-term consequences of the campaign of sedentarization of the nomads (implemented in the 1930s), and of the Stalinist policies of forced migrations of peasants in Central Asia. To provide a study of the impact, on the decision-making process regarding water management, of the repressive-clientelist relations between the central elite in Moscow, the Central Asian 'national' leaders, and the administration on the ground. To produce a study having an impact on world environmental history, on the history of the Soviet Union, on the history of Modern Central Asia, on Soviet and Post-Soviet agrarian history, on the history of water management policies and effects, on the analysis of the consequences of forced resettlement policies.

341612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
341612.value: The focus of my research is the history of the Aral Sea environmental crisis in Soviet Central Asia. During the second half of the twentieth century, the Aral Sea turned from a vibrant inland sea to a chemically-polluted desert except for two small residual lakes. Aral Sea decline paralleled the final crisis of Soviet economic system. The study will focus on Soviet transformative policies in the economy, the environment, and society through the history of water management. The outcome of my research will be the first general historical monograph on the Aral Sea crisis, covering the period 1930 to 2000: from early Stalinism to the policies of independent Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, with a special focus on the post-war period. Geographically, the study will focus on the Aral Sea water basin, which includes the two biggest rivers in Central Asia, the Amudarya and Syrdarya. Significant attention will be devoted to a case-study of a sub-region in the Aral Sea basin: the lower course of the Syrdarya River and its social, environmental and agrarian history. The study will describe the agency at different levels of the administrative pyramid: peasants, local administrators, Central Asian political leaders, scientists, and members of the central political and economic elite. How each of these groups conceived and made use of water as a resource will be at the center of the investigation. Soviet Aral policies are a case of making of an environment (physical, biotic and social), and of its eventual unmaking. The study will be articulated on two analytical levels: (1) how the Soviet remaking of Aral basin physical and biotic environments from Stalin to Brezhnev interplayed with Soviet population politics: irrigation systems construction; introduction of new species of plants and animals (fish); “sedentarization” of Kazakh and Karakalpak nomads; forced immigration of grain-growing Russians and rice-growing Koreans during the 1930s; voluntary immigration during and after World War II; waves of emigration, starting in the 1970s, resulting from environmental degradation and raising economic problems; (2) the Soviet decision-making process regarding water management and use: how specific strategies at different social, geographical and administrative levels interacted, conflicted and/or coalesced in molding the patterns of water use in the region – and how they modified the environment and at the same time had to adapt to the deteriorating environmental situation. The research will be a relevant case-study about large-scale environmental and social consequences of state-led developmentalist projects. 本研究的重點是位於中亞的鹹海生態危機的歷史。二十世紀下半葉，鹹海乾枯後，分裂成兩個小湖, 其餘區域則變成了貧瘠的佈滿毒物污染的荒漠。鹹海的乾枯伴隨著蘇聯經濟體制的最終危機。本研究將討論水資源管理的歷史，重點揭示蘇聯的政策如何改變經濟、環境和社會。本研究的結果將是第一部有關鹹海危機的歷史專著，其涵蓋的年代為1930年到2000年；內容包括早期的斯大林主義、哈薩克斯坦共和國及烏茲別克斯坦共和國；該研究將重點考察戰後時期。本研究的地理範疇主要涵蓋鹹海流域，包括阿母河和錫爾河。 本研究將對鹹海流域子區域進行案例研究；並將重點放在錫爾河下游區域的社會、環境和農業的發展史。這項研究將描述位於行政架構中不同層次的社會群體如何構思拯救鹹海及利用水資源的行動。這些群體包括農民、地方行政官員、中亞地區政治領袖、科學家及中央的政治和經濟精英。蘇聯的鹹海政策不僅製造了一個新的環境（物理的、生物的和社會的），並導致了最後所有環境的毀滅。該研究將從兩個層次來闡明：第一：從斯大林到勃列日涅夫，蘇聯在鹹海盆地造成的一系列物理和生物方面的變化同蘇聯的人口政策有相互的影響，這些政策包括灌溉系統的建設、引進新植物和動物（魚類）、哈薩克族及卡拉卡爾帕克族的定居、在1930年代強迫移入種植穀物俄羅斯人和種植水稻的韓國人、二戰期間和二戰後的自願移民。環境和經濟的持續惡化導致了20世紀70年代的移民。第二：蘇聯水資源管理政策的決策過程。這些具體的政策是通過不同的社會、地理和行政領域之間相互影響和相互抵觸而最後形成的。同時，他們如何對環境產生影響，並如何通過調適來適應日益惡化的環境問題。本研究以個案研究的方式來闡述國家制定的經濟發展項目對環境和社會的巨大影響。

341612.label: Realisation of objectives
341612.value: During the research, I was able to work in former central Tsarist and Soviet archives in St. Petersburg and Moscow, in central republican archives in Kazakhstan (Almaty), in regional archives in Kzyl-Orda (south Kazakhstan region), and in district archives in Aral’sk, on the former shore of the Aral Sea. In all of these repositories I found valuable materials produced by the different administrative levels and by different institutions. I also did extensive archival research with the files of the Archives of the Russian Academy of Sciences in St. Petersburg and Moscow. During the course of my research, I decided to focus on four scientists and scholars who were crucial in the study of the Aral Sea region's history, ecosystem, and resources during the twentieth century: the geographer Lev Berg (1876-1950), the archaeologist Sergei Tolstov (1907-1976), the ichthyologist Georgii Nikol'skii (1910-1977), and the soil scientist Viktor Kovda (1904-1991). These four scientists were among the most influential in Soviet scientific institutions jn the twentieth century, occupying positions of high responsibility in the Soviet Academy of Sciences, and in international institutions such as FAO and UNESCO. The international career of the soil salinization specialist Viktor Korda is especially relevant in this regard. By making use of the scholars' personal archival files and other sources, my research shows how the careers of these scholars began with their studies of the Aral Sea region. Analyzing their scientific production and their institutional career is both a way to study the history of the Aral Sea region, and the relation between science and politics in the Soviet Union. Their relationship with the political leadership is an important case of the interactions between politics and science in the twentieth century. My research shows how, for example, Soviet scholars were able to use the concentration of state investment for canal digging and irrigation expansion in the region after World War II to further their own research. Sergei Tolstov linked the expenditures for his Khorezm Expedition, the biggest archeological and ethnographic research project in Soviet times, to funding for the Great Stalin Plan for the Transformation of Nature, launched in 1948. On the basis of the materials I collected, I am now writing the manuscript for the book I will submit to a publisher in 2017. The book will detail the “history of the making and unmaking of the environment of the lower Syrdarya River, its delta, and the Aral Sea in the twentieth century”, as per objective no. 2 above. Two journal articles have been sent to peer-reviewed journals (one accepted for publication, the second now under review) detailing the early phase of the period covered by the research. The first paper is about the early colonization of the Aral Sea region and the first scientific studies of its ecosystem and the second paper is about fisheries management and the great famine of the early 1930s in the Aral Sea region. A significant part of the collected materials focus on the river diversion project from Siberia to Central Asia, a planned engineering project that was put forward at the end of the 1940s and abandoned only in the mid-1980s. Given China’s recently implemented river diversion projects, and the ongoing concerns about the environmental conservation of lakes, the research has a clear comparative value for Chinese history, as per objective 3. Working in regional archives in Kyzylorda and local archives in Aral’sk made it possible to collect materials for a regional study of the lower Syrdarya River during the postwar period, as per objective 4. Objective 5 has been attained by working in the same archives. The result of this part of the research is been published as a separate article in the peer-reviewed journal "Nationalities Papers". The research undertaken, thanks to the present research grant, made possible my discovery of archival materials that have changed the overall history of the great famine in Kazakhstan. I am publishing the results both in English and in Russian (in a book chapter to be published in Japan, and in a peer-reviewed article sent to the journal "Ab Imperio"). This new history of the famine also made possible a more general comparison of Communist policies in pastoral Central Eurasia. I detailed this comparison in an article published on the peer-reviewed journal "East/West, Journal of Ukrainian Studies”. Objective 6 has been attained by focusing on the relationships between Moscow and the different Soviet republics, during both the prewar and postwar periods. In connection to this, I recently published an article that focuses on the spatial aspect of Soviet power and the relation between Moscow and the Central Asian periphery in the peer-reviewed journal "Central Asian Survey". The use of administrative documents, memoirs of local leaders, and other materials made it possible to show the dynamics between the center and the periphery during the postwar period as well. The analysis of the dynamics at the local level has been achieved only to a limited extent. Archival materials retrieved in regional and district archives did not always allow reconstruction of decision-making at the local level, or a complete analysis of the communication flow between the republican level and lower administrative units. Therefore, the existing archival documentation has made the aim of writing a local history of water management in a small region unachievable. However, I was able to find documents that will make possible a more spatially-focused study for specific periods. For example, one chapter of the manuscript will be devoted to the history or the Gulag labor camp created in Karakalpakstan during the 1940s. The prisoners of the camp were employed for the construction of the canal from the Amu River to the Caspian Sea, a project that was abandoned by Stalin’s death in 1953. Moreover, I am planning to work in the local archives in Karakalpakstan (Uzbekistan) during the 2017 summer break. I hope to find additional local archival materials about this region south of the Aral Sea. Objective no. 7 has been achieved by the organization of an international conference held in May 2016 at Lingnan University and the University of Hong Kong, "Empires of Water: Water Management and Politics in the Arid Regions of China, Central Eurasia and the Middle East (16th-20th centuries)" (website: http://www.ln.edu.hk/history/conference/wc2016/) . I presented some of the results of the present research at the conference and benefited from the wide viewpoints of the assembled scholars. A selection of the conference papers will be published in a special issue of the "Journal of the Social and Economic History of the Orient" that I will co-edit, and which will be published in early 2018. The book manuscript I am writing will be the first book-length historical study about the Aral Sea catastrophe, and the relation between Russian and Soviet science, politics, and the environment in the biggest ecological catastrophe of the twentieth century. Given the relevance of the topic for modern environmental history and for the other fields mentioned in Object no. 7, I am confident that the book will have an impact on the field.

341612.label: Major findings and research outcome
341612.value: The research was innovative on a number of topics. In relation to the Tsarist colonization during the second half of the nineteenth century, it showed how the immigrant Ural Cossacks imported fisheries conservation policies to the Aral Sea that had originally been developed for the Ural River. Later, the construction of the railway between Russia with Turkestan (1906) made a new wave of peasant settlers possible. It also facilitated the extraction of the region's resources during World War I and the Stalinist collectivization during the early 1930s. This part of my research focused on a regional study of the great famine of 1931-33, showing how the uneven impact of the famine, which killed a huge number of Kazakhs in the north but largely spared the Karakalpaks in the south, permanently shifted the economic center of the Aral Sea southward. My research also provided an outline about the production of scientific knowledge on the Aral Sea ecosystem. The geographer Lev Berg and the ichthyologist Georgii Nikol'skii were the main authorities. However, with the launching of the Great Stalin Plan for the Transformation of Nature (1948), the Aral Sea was consciously sacrificed, since it was clear to engineers and political leaders that the expansion of irrigation and of cotton production was built around an unsustainable pace of local water consumption. Precisely for this reason, the first detailed plans for the diversion of the Siberian rivers to Central Asia were drafted in this period. My research gave to Central Asia its proper centrality in the history of the Great Stalin Plan. It then showed how megaprojects’ construction under Stalin and Khrushchev (especially the Karakum Canal in Turkmenistan) created strong local interests in central investments for irrigation expansion. My research also showed how the very same institutions and scientists that oversaw the expansion of irrigation programs in Central Asia were also instrumental in organizing Soviet international development assistance to Asian and African countries (especially in North Africa) during the 1960s. My research then analyzed how the 1960s transition towards a growing awareness of the environmental problems linked to a growing water scarcity in the Soviet Union was influenced by global scientific debates. Finally, the research showed how the planned megaprojects (first and foremost the Siberian rivers diversion) remained crucial in the expectations of both the population and of the local Central Asian political elites, influencing their choices until the end of the Soviet Union.

341612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
341612.value: The research should be further developed by taking advantage of Uzbek archives, the access to which is extremely difficult. I am planning to pass a month of study in Uzbek archives in the Aral Sea region (Karakalpakstan) during the summer of 2017 to collect additional materials to be used for the monograph. Inside the Soviet Union, my research could open up a comparative study of environmental and economic policies in relation to the Caspian Sea, which also went through a period of decreasing water level in the mid-twentieth century. Moreover, the results of my research about the elaboration of specific conservation practices linked to fisheries by the Ural Cossacks can open up researches about other Cossack communities and their interactions with the populations of the borderlands of the Empire. A further development could be a comparison, in the relation between science, politics and society, for other cases of lakes that went through ecological crises in the world (Lake Chad, Lake Victoria, the Great Salt Lake in Utah). The most promising comparative case is perhaps Lake Chad in Africa. In China, the Qinghai Lake lost more than 10% of its surface over the twentieth century, also because of human water use.

341612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
341612.value: My research is the first comprehensive historical study about the biggest ecological catastrophe of the twentieth century, the drying up of the Aral Sea in Central Asia. The book will outline how scientists, political leaders, and simple fishermen, peasants, and nomads influenced and lived through the environmental transformations of the region. Given the current water usage critical condition in different regions of the world, which is leading to the disappearance of vast lakes in many arid areas of Asia, Africa, and the Americas, the book manuscript I am completing will be an important contribution in order to understand the historical background of the current human-made global environmental crisis, with a specific focus on the arid regions of the Earth. The book will outline how scientists used political campaigns and economic investments in specific regions to push forward their research agenda, and how political leaders, in order to implement their economic plans, selectively used the scientific knowledge created by scientist. The research is also important because outlines a case of interaction between politics and scientific knowledge in an authoritarian political environment and in a tightly controlled public sphere, which can have useful parallel in contemporary situations across the world.

342012.label: Project Objectives
342012.value: Document that the Western developed theory of cooperation and competition is useful to understand how conflict management dynamics affect banking relationships and providing credit in China. Examine the mediating effects of cooperative conflict management between guanxi and providing credit support to firms. Provide a platform for how innovative firms can gain the confidence of banks and enhance their credit worthiness.

342012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
342012.value: Banks critically provide loans and other credit support so that businesses can operate, innovate, and expand. The relationships between banks and businesses are thought to play a critical role in that they affect the extent that banks feel confident and actually provide financial support. Without effective work relationships with companies, banks may consider lending money too risky, as they are unsure that companies will be forthright in their dealings with the bank. Indeed, Chinese banks are often criticized for being more willing to support traditional companies, especially government-supported ones, with whom they have long-term experience to the detriment of younger firms. However, entrepreneurial firms may be developing and marketing new technologies and other innovations that will propel future growth not only for the companies but also for society at large. Indeed, banks may consider innovative firms as very risky; these firms could thrive but they may also crash. The proposed studies argue that banks that have guanxi with firms provide funding because they believe that they can manage their conflicts cooperatively and constructively with these firms. Guanxi helps banks believe that they can manage their risks because they can deal directly and productively with the customer when issues and difficulties are confronted. Innovative top management teams (TMTs) of entrepreneurial firms have potential but they may not translate their new ideas into effective practical solutions that help the organization succeed. TMTs must refine and shape their innovative ideas through constructive, open discussion. Innovative TMTs that are able to manage their conflicts cooperatively are expected to develop useful solutions that foster banks’ providing credit support. However, innovative TMTs that manage conflict competitively and avoid conflict do not gain the bank confidence that results in credit support. The proposed studies use the theory of cooperation and competition to identify important conditions for banks and firms to discuss their concerns and other issues effectively. Banks and firms may emphasize that their goals are cooperatively or positively related. They may also emphasize their competitive goals by focusing on how their goals are negatively related. These different understandings affect how they manage conflict and the effects of their conflict management. When people emphasize their cooperative goals, they discuss their different views and opinions directly and open-mindedly with each other. Specifically, these studies hypothesize that banks provide credit support to firms with whom that they can discuss their various concerns open-mindedly and cooperatively.

342012.label: Realisation of objectives
342012.value: Entrepreneurial and other small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in China are thought to be disadvantaged in obtaining financial credit because banks and other financial organizations consider extending credit to large, ongoing companies to be less risky and incur fewer transaction costs. We argue that entrepreneurial and other SME firms can build upon the traditional Chinese value of guanxi (relationship) to develop a foundation for obtaining credit from banks. However, these relationships have to be carefully constructed, as they involve more than exchanging favors and must reduce asymmetrical information so that bank managers feel more knowledgeable and reassured that their risks and transaction costs are manageable. This project uses Western research to specify the nature of relationships that help SMEs inform banks and convince them to provide credit. We have come up with the above four objectives for the project so as to understand the topic in more detail. To achieve the above objectives of the project, we conducted two studies. Study 1: In study 1, we used the theory of cooperation and competition to understand the relationships between banks and SMEs. This study proposes that the theory of cooperation and competition as developed in the West can help us to understand how guanxi affects the relationships between banks and SMEs. We argue that guanxi strengthens cooperative goals and reduces competitive and independent goals. We have formulated the following hypotheses for the study: Hypothesis 1: Guanxi is positively related to cooperative goals. Hypothesis 2: Guanxi is negatively related to competitive goals. Hypothesis 3: Guanxi is negatively related to independent goals. With cooperative goals, partners are likely to be committed to their relationship because they expect to have a mutually rewarding exchange that will promote each partner’s success. Theorizing that guanxi develops cooperative goals also suggests that guanxi-related activities result in productive conflict. In contrast, independent or competitive goals provide little incentive for partners to maintain their relationships. Therefore, study 1 also has the following hypotheses: Hypothesis 4: Cooperative goals are positively related to relationship commitment and productive conflict. Hypothesis 5: Competitive goals are negatively related to relationship commitment and productive conflict. Hypothesis 6: Independent goals are negatively related to relationship commitment and productive conflict. The theory and research reviewed suggests that guanxi builds cooperative goals between partners, because they believe that their goals are positively related, so that as one partner moves toward accomplishing his or her goals, that success helps the other partners to reach their goals as well. Such cooperative experiences in turn help to strengthen their relationship commitment and their productive conflict that can be expected to maintain the guanxi relationship. We therefore theorize that cooperative goals mediate between guanxi and relationship commitment and productive conflict. Firms with guanxi develop cooperative goals that become foundations for relationship commitment, and the ability to manage conflicts productively, as proposed in the following hypothesis: Hypothesis 7: Cooperative goals mediate the link between guanxi and relationship commitment and productive conflict. Study 2: Studies in the West have directly shown that the interaction and relationships between banks and borrowing firms affect financial support decisions. This study argues that entrepreneurial and other SME firms can build upon the traditional Chinese value of guanxi (relationship) to develop a foundation for obtaining credit from banks. However, these relationships have to be carefully constructed, as they involve more than exchanging favors and must reduce asymmetrical information so that bank managers feel more knowledgeable and reassured that their risks and transaction costs are manageable. This study uses marketing research on customer orientation and organization behavior research on conflict management to identify critical conditions to building effective business–bank relationships. This study hypothesizes that banks that are customer-oriented are able to manage their conflicts cooperatively rather than competitively with SMEs, and this productive conflict management convinces bank loan officers that they can confidently provide credit with reasonable costs. The customer orientation of banks toward SMEs is expected to have its effects by developing the cooperative approach to conflict. A high customer-oriented bank convinces the bank and borrower that they have a mutual relationship where they are concerned about each other’s interests and communicate accurately and directly. Demonstrating these concerns and openness forms the basis for discussing conflicts cooperatively for mutual benefit. Since conflict management approaches are useful to understand the mechanisms by which customer orientation affects interactions and outcomes between banks and firms in the Chinese settings, we focus on examining the mediating effects of conflict management on the relationship between guanxi and credit support instead of examining its moderating effects of conflict management. The hypotheses for study 2 are as follows: H1. High customer orientation promotes cooperative conflict management between banks and borrowing firms. H2. Low customer orientation promotes competitive conflict management between banks and borrowing firms. H3. Cooperative conflict management between banks and borrowing firms promotes bank’s willingness to extend credit and the conclusion that managing the loan incurs low transaction costs. H4. Competitive conflict management between banks and borrowing firms impedes bank’s willingness to extend credit and fosters the conclusion that managing the loan incurs high transaction costs. H5. High customer orientation promotes cooperative conflict management between banks and borrowing firms, and this cooperative conflict management promotes bank’s willingness to extend credit and the conclusion that managing the credit support incurs low transaction costs. To collect data for the two studies, we first approached the loan departments of four banks in Shanghai. The bank loan officers responsible for SME loans were key informants in the study. These officers were each asked to focus on a particular SME, and to rate their collaboration with that SME. We then approached the SMEs concerned, identified the firm’s managers who were knowledgeable concerning their relationship with the bank’s loan department, and invited these managers to complete our questionnaire. We have collected data from 106 pairs of banks and SMEs in Shanghai for the two studies. The results from the two studies provide general support to the hypotheses of the two studies. Therefore, the two studies are able to help us achieve the objectives for the project. The major findings are summarized in the Research Outcome section.

342012.label: Major findings and research outcome
342012.value: Study 1’s findings shed light on how business partners use guanxi to develop their relationships and joint productivity. Results support the theorizing that guanxi partners strengthen their cooperative goals as they support and assist each other. These cooperative goals in turn were found positively related to relationship commitment and productive conflict between partners. Cooperative goals appear to stimulate commitment to maintain relationships, because the partners understand that it is in their mutual interest to continue assisting each other. The results also suggested that the theory of cooperation and competition, although it was developed in the West, is useful for understanding the dynamics and outcomes of Chinese guanxi. Results from study 2 support the argument that marketing research on customer orientation and organization behavior research on conflict management identify how to develop effective marketing relationships between SMEs and banks in China. Banks that were customer-oriented laid the groundwork for managing conflict cooperatively and not competitively with borrowing firms. Cooperative conflict management in turn was found to convince banks that they could confidently provide credit and to convince borrowers that their transaction costs will be reasonable. This study identifies that developing guanxi and the capacity to manage conflict cooperatively are an important foundation for providing credit to SMEs in China.

342012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
342012.value: Results of the two studies are correlational, and causal inferences are not warranted. Findings may not be highly representative, as the data were collected in one country, Mainland China. Research is needed to test the hypotheses in different settings, using experimental and other methods, to develop more evidence about the proposed causal relationships between the variables examined in the two studies. Further research could explore whether guanxi can help to develop cooperative goals between partners in the West. There is currently much discussion about the value of networking and leader member exchange relationships in the Western management literature (Ferris et al., 2009). In addition, close relationships are thought to play important roles for organizations in the Middle East and the rest of Asia (Chua & Wellman, 2015). Future studies could investigate the extent to which guanxi can affect the quality of relationships in international and cross-cultural partnerships.

342012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
342012.value: SMEs have been thought to be under-funded and thus unable to contribute to the development of the Chinese economy as they could. Strengthening the links between banks and borrowing firms can help SMEs obtain needed financial credit. Results of this project found that banks that are oriented toward their customers want a long-term relationship focused on joint problem-solving and mutual benefit; this approach in turn is a foundation for successful relationships. Customer orientation was found to be so useful because it promotes the open, cooperative discussion of different ideas and other conflicts that can inform and reassure loan officers. Loan officials and entrepreneurs realize that there are many issues and changes that will occur over the term of the loan. Although specific conflicts may not be predictable, it is predictable that they will likely have conflicts and that if banks and borrowing firms are able to manage them effectively, they can be confident about providing credit and managing transaction costs of lending. Focusing on a mutually beneficial relationships and strengthening the capacity to manage conflict cooperatively appear to be an important foundation for banks’ willingness to provide credit to SMEs in China.

342412.label: Project Objectives
342412.value: To estimate two frequently used information asymmetry measures, the adverse selection cost and the probability of informed trading, for all A-share listed stocks traded in the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges. To investigate the impact of analyst coverage and earnings forecasts on the information asymmetry. To test how the political influences faced by financial analysts influence the information asymmetry. To show the determinants of information asymmetry.

To investigate the impact of analyst coverage and earnings forecasts on the information asymmetry.

To show the determinants of information asymmetry.

342412.label: Realisation of objectives
342412.value: The data on the Split Share Structure Reform in China including the reform completion dates of firms are obtained from the CSMAR database. The SINOFIN-CCER database provides the intraday quotation and transaction prices of all listed firms on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges starting from 2002. We use the probability of informed trading (PIN) as the measure of information asymmetry for a firm according to the microstructure model developed by Easley et al. (1996, 1997a and 1997b). The model posits the existence of a market maker, who observes the flow of buy and sell orders and assesses the probability that the orders are submitted by informed traders when offering bid and ask quotes. We estimate the annual PIN of each firm on stock exchanges in China from 2002 to 2011. This is to achieve objective (1). We perform a regression analysis on the determinants of information asymmetry. We include industry fixed-effects dummies and cluster standard errors at the firm level to correct for the within-firm correlation between the error terms. We include a set of firm-specific characteristics as control variables in our regression model following Aslan et al. (2011) and Gul et al. (2010). Firm size is measured as the logarithm of market capitalization. Larger firms are normally exposed to the public more than smaller firms and thus tend to have lower information asymmetry. The logarithm of the number of financial analysts following firm i in year t captures the role of stock analysts in shaping a firm's information environment. Firms with more analysts following tend to be more transparent (Kelly and Ljungqist, 2012). Institutional investors are thought to play an important role in monitoring managers and expected to reduce information asymmetry. We compute the institutional stock ownership as the fraction of outstanding shares held by institutional investors. We also control for the insiders' effect using the fraction of outstanding shares held by the largest shareholder. Firm's cash holdings are regarded as an important resource for managers to acquire perks and can increase a firm's information asymmetry. We include cash holding scaled by total assets. Other control variables include firm's leverage measured by the debt-to-total-assets ratio, firm age, which is the logarithm of the number of years since the firm is firstly listed, managerial ownership, which is the fraction of shares held by officers, and directors and growth opportunity measured by the logarithm of a firm’s Tobin's Q. Industry dummies are defined according to the CSRC two-digit industry classifications. The regression results show that the coefficient on the reform dummy for Split Share Structure reform (SSSR) is significant at the 1% level. Consistent with our hypothesis, the level of PIN decreases after the reform. The effect is both statistically and economically significant. On average, PIN decreases by 26.3% after the SSSR. The regression results also show that the estimated coefficients on firm size, institutional ownership and firm age are negative and significant in explaining PIN while that on the ownership of largest shareholder is positive and significant. Therefore, firms that have a larger size, more institutional ownership and a longer history of listing tend to have a lower level of information symmetry. These findings are consistent with those found for the U.S. firms by Aslan et al. (2011). Meanwhile, as expected, the ownership of the largest shareholders, as a measure of ownership concentration, increases with PIN in China. The results are to achieve objective (1). We add firm fixed-effects dummies to the regression model to control for the time-invariant unobserved firm-specific characteristics. Overall, the results with firm-fixed effects are qualitatively similar to those with industry-fixed effects. The estimated coefficient on reform remains negative and significant. According to it, the level of information asymmetry decreases by about 18.1%. The results of most control variables are also consistent with those discussed earlier with industry-fixed effect. The estimated coefficient on the number of financial analysts, becomes negative and significant at the 1% level. It supports the argument of Easley et al. (1998) that the analysis conducted by professional equity analysts can reduce information asymmetry among investors. The results are for objective (3). For objective (2), we find that the analysts’ effects on information asymmetry is stronger after the split share structure reform. Therefore, the structure reform does have an impact about how financial analysts affect the level of information asymmetry.

342412.label: Major findings and research outcome
342412.value: We have undertaken one project that studies how the Split Share Structure Reform in China starting from 2005 influences firm-level information asymmetry. The Chinese government implemented a reform to abolish the dual-class share structure of listed firms and converted all non-tradable shares, owned mainly by the Chinese government, its affiliates and legal person, to tradable shares. It is widely believed that the reform induced a better alignment of the interests between controlling and minority shareholders, and the process of the reform played an information discovery role. Using a difference-in-difference approach, we find that the information asymmetry, measured by the probability of informed trading, decreased significantly after the reform, and the effect is less pronounced for SOEs than non-SOEs. Our findings show that the reform benefits the information environment and the minority shareholder of listed firms. We have completed a draft of the paper and will submit it to international conferences and journal(s). A related project investigates whether the characteristics of the earnings forecasts made by financial analysts provide information about the effectiveness of firms’ investment decisions. We use the dispersion among analysts’ earnings forecasts (standard deviation multiplied by minus one) and the accuracy of analysts’ earnings forecasts as measures of the effectiveness or quality of analyst information gathering and monitoring. We find that high quality analysis is associated with higher investment if the firm is more likely to under-invest and lower investment if the firm is more likely over-invest. We further show that such effects are stronger for the firms with large deviations in investment from their expected level, higher information asymmetry, lower institutional stock ownership, and for the period before the enactment of SOX in 2002. The effects of analysts’ forecast characteristics remain highly significant after controlling for the quality of financial reporting as well as other measures of governance mechanisms and are robust to potential endogeneity concerns. Our results are consistent with the view that high quality information gathering and monitoring by financial analysts can enhance firms’ investment efficiency. The paper now is under review by the Journal of Corporate Finance.

342412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
342412.value: The coexistence of tradable and non-tradable shares in a firm has been the subject of much criticism in China. The Chinese Securities Regulatory Commission launched a reform in 2005 to eliminate the dual-class share structure and convert non-tradable shares into tradable shares. This paper examines how the Split Share Structure Reform in China affects the level of information asymmetry, measured by the probability of informed trading (PIN). The regression results show that the PIN decreases significantly after the reform. This is consistent with the notion that reduced agency costs and increased stock market liquidity are associated with lower information asymmetry in the stock market. We further document that the reform’s effects on PIN are more pronounced for the firms, that have higher trading potential, the firms with enhancement in the blockholders’ exit threat, and non-SOEs. Our study sheds light on the consequences of ownership structure reform in China and provides policy implications for future reforms in developing financial markets.

342612.label: Project Objectives
342612.value: To offer a unified account of practical rationality, the nature of autonomy, and the special status of self-knowledge. To better understand the indeterminacy of desire, the nature of self-reflective judgments, and how consciously held mental states could be more determinate in content and character than unconscious or dispostional attitudes. To make progress on the task of integrating discoveries from empirical psychology into the project of philosophical psychology. To achieve a clearer understanding of the normative dimensions of non-coercive manipulation. To achieve a clearer understanding of the relation ideas of autonomy or psychological integrity should play in normative debate.

342612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
342612.value: Unwilling addicts present moral philosophy with a puzzle. Feeding their addictions seems, in a sense, what they want to do. But it would be just as natural to say that this wasn’t really what they wanted. We’d be more inclined to say that an addict gave in to the addiction than chose to indulge it: we’re inclined to think that the resulting action is not entirely free. The philosophical orthodoxy is that we are free when we are governed by reason, or by our judgments of value. But there is another answer, which claims that desires can be integrated into the agent’s personality, and that there can also be failures of integration. Behavior is free when one’s actions express one’s personality, rather than standing at odds with it. This answer leads to a family of theories known as Deep Self views. Deep Self theories must provide: (1) an account of what is for an agent’s desires to be integrated into her personality, and (2) an explanation of the normative significance of Deep Self autonomy. My position is that Deep Self autonomy is normatively significant not because the state has inherent value, but because the concept fills certain gaps in our larger normative theories. Start with an instrumentalist conception of rationality. Such a theory will be unable to rank courses of action for any agent whose desires are relatively indeterminate with respect to their strength or content. In actual human beings this indeterminacy is rampant. Autonomy should be thought of as a self-reflective capacity for imposing order, or precise rankings and precise content, on one's own psychology. Most Deep Self theories have identified the mechanism of personal integration with some form of motivation, a second-order desire or a long-term plan. I would like to investigate the extent to which self-reflective beliefs could provide the necessary ordering instead. Part of this depends on the extent to which principled reasons could be given for treating self-reflective beliefs as verdictives (see Background, section II.2.a. for details on verdictives). A verdictive theory might explain how a person has privileged knowledge about her own mind: it follows her ability to stipulate certain psychological states into existence. It may also explain the connection between lack of self-knowledge and irrationality: self-knowledge simply is a form of rational self-control; ergo, its absence must involve rational failing. 那些不情願地沉迷於某些事物的人為道德哲學帶來一個難題。在某意義下，他們想要滿足自己的癮癖；然而，說他們事實上不是這樣想亦好像沒甚麼不妥。我們或許更傾向於說這種人對自己的癮癖讓步，而非選擇了沉溺於此──我們傾向於把他們的行為視作不是完全自由的。 哲學上的正統說法指出，當我們受理性或價值判斷支配時，我們是自由的。可是另一說法主張，欲望可被統合到行動者的個性內，以及這種統合可能失敗。當一個人的行動表現出他的個性，而不是與之相牴觸時，他的行為便是自由的。這說法引起了一系列稱為「深層自我觀」的理論。深層自我理論必須(一)說明何謂欲望可被統合到行動者的個性內，及(二)解釋深層自我之自決的在規範層面的重要性。 我的立場是，深層自我的自決之所以具有規範的重要性，乃在於對此之概念能夠填補較大層面的規範理論的一些空隙，而不在於這狀態有內在的價值。試想那些工具理性的理論。 對任何有著相對地不確定的欲望的行動者而言，這樣的一個理論並不能就不同行動方針的強度或內容去排高下。而這不確定性蔓生於現實的人類當中。自決應被想為一種自省的能力，能夠為一個人的心理加上秩序，或準確的次序及準確的內容。 大部分深層自我理論視個人的統合之機制或為某種推動力，或為某種二階欲望，或為一長遠計劃。而我則希望探討一下在甚麼程度上自反的信念能提供必要的秩序。這當中的一部分取決於有沒有具原則性的理由可在一定程度上把自省的信念當作一種判決行為。 這樣一個理論或能解釋一個人如何對其心靈擁有他人無法得到的認知：這來自其（通過自省）規約乃至創造心理狀態的能力。這理論亦能解釋自知的不足及不理性之間的關係：自知不過是理性自律的一種形式；因此，自知的不足必然牽涉到理性的缺失。

342612.label: Realisation of objectives
342612.value: The objectives have been for the most part completely realized. I will start with where they have not. I am recording objectives 2 and 3 as only 80% complete. I have made substantial progress on both, but I don't regard either as completed to my satisfaction. Regarding objective 2, I make use of empirical psychological literature in two of the papers (“The Verdictive Organization of Desire” and “Verdictive Rationalism about Self-Knowledge”) and in parts of the draft book. I would like to include, however, a section in the book providing a more systematic account of why I interpret the results of empirical psychology differently from other philosophers (such as Tim Schroeder or Peter Carruthers). Regarding objective 3, I discuss manipulation and violations of autonomy in pp. 112-132 of the draft book. It is also discussed in "On Rationally Valuing One's Life," a conference paper invited for publication in the Asian Bioethics Review. Since these ideas are not yet in publishable form, I do not regard this as complete. The primary reason these objectives are not fully complete is that the ECS proposal I submitted was for a three-year project, but the RGC awarded me two years. This turned out to be plenty of time to substantially advance the vast majority of the research aims, but some loose ends remain for those objectives furthest removed from my specialization as a researcher. In terms of the other objectives, I have advanced an account of rationality as a form of functional coherence among an agent's mental states. Autonomy is a capacity for self-reflectively maintaining and augmenting such coherence, in agent's like us, which are subject to systematic forms of disunity and incoherence. Autonomy is primarily maintained through the formation of more or less detailed self-conceptions which play a regulative psychological role. These self-conceptions are representations of one's psychology, but because they play a regulative role, they tend to make themselves true, explaining several of the respects in which self-knowledge tends to be unlike other forms of knowledge. Significant portions of the research have been published in a series of articles in journals of high to very high quality. Other portions have been presented at conferences and public seminars. The book is still in progress, but substantial progress has been made toward its completion.

342612.label: Major findings and research outcome
342612.value: As stated in section 5.3, the basic theoretical picture I am trying to develop has the following components. Rationality is a form of functional coherence among an agent's mental states. Autonomy is a capacity for self-reflectively maintaining and augmenting such coherence. Autonomy is primarily maintained through self-conceptions which regulate in addition to representing one's own psychology. Because these self-conceptions play a regulative role, they tend to make themselves true. In research outputs, I argue for the following. Some of the standard reasons for rejecting coherence accounts of practical rationality fail (items 2 and 6), and there is a novel form of constitutivism about reason that can be used to support a coherence-based account (item 12). A clear way of specifying what counts as a failing of rational coherence can be used to explain semantic inconsistency (and entailment) in a expressivist semantic project (item 1), or used to identify various limits to expressivism (items 5 and 11). A clear understanding of rational coherence, then, promises to help better develop and evaluate one popular program for understanding normative discourse. The claim that many of our attitudes are indeterminate in character and content fits in well with standard functionalist accounts of mental states, and such indeterminacy opens the need for higher-order, reflective capacities to impose greater consistency (items 3, 8, and 9). The claim that self-reflective beliefs will play a regulatory role, favoring their own truth, follows from very standard commitments in philosophical psychology (ibid). The resulting picture of autonomy is in some ways more modest, and so is able to answer objections to more familiar theories (items 3 and 9). It is also able to account better for the sense that we can be passive with respect to some of the attitudes most central to our personalities, and is able to provide a simplified account of the value of individuality (ibid). The theory also has implications for how to classify various hard cases as instances of authentic, self-expressive choice, or involving forms of manipulation or other failures to exercise self-determination (items 9 and 10). The resulting theory of self-knowledge has more flexibility and more theoretical modesty than familiar forms of "rationalism" (item 8). A rival theory of self-knowledge possesses less theoretical modesty than standardly thought (item 7). Self-knowledge can in certain extreme cases undermine autonomy, and this shows a popular metaethical account of practical reasons to be unacceptable (item 4).

342612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
342612.value: The most obvious places for work is finishing the book which will show how the various points made in the articles fit together into a larger project. The research completed so far opens up quite a bit of new work to be done on the topic of expressivism as a theory of normative language and reasoning. I have the ambition of eventually do further work tying expressivism to the theory of autonomy and self-knowledge I have developed, likely by appealing to the role that "visualized" or internalized speech plays in both self-knowledge and self-regulation (Dennett; Carruthers). I also wish to account for the special, "verdictive" or self-fulfilling role of introspective beliefs by appealing ultimately to the special inferential properties of first-personal content (see the end of item 8). This sets the stage, I hope, for an extremely reductive account of the self. The slogan is: to have a self is to be fluent in the application of self-locating concepts. On the basis of item 4, I have also been worried about, and exploring, the Kantian idea that there is a potential conflict or incompatibility between the theoretical and practical points of view.

342612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
342612.value: This project provides a unified solution to two standard problems surrounding the nature of the self. First, I seem to be able to stand back from my desires, to control them or resist them, or sometimes to be overcome by them. But, at the same time, my personality seems to be composed of my desires. So in what sense could I be opposed to my desires? Second, I know my own mental states without the need for the kind of evidence needed to know the mental states of others. How is this possible? My answer is that beliefs about one's own mental states create rational pressure on the believer to act and reason in ways consistent with the psychology she believes herself to have. We have special knowledge of our mental states because our beliefs tend to make themselves true. The self, to simplify, is composed of those desires that one recognizes oneself as having. The elements of the theoretical model developed here have implications for the nature of normative language and thought, the nature of authentic choice and self-determination, problems surrounding freedom of the will, moral responsibility, and the value of individuality.

342912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
342912.value: This project seeks to investigate and understand the psychological mechanisms behind human error detection in using medical devices. The factors to be examined in this project are grouped into three main themes: 1) how people detect their own errors; 2) how the task environment affects error detection; and 3) how people detect others’ errors. An understanding of human error detection is particularly important in safety-critical domains, such as, medicine. For example, when prescribing medications using an electronic prescribing system, doctors forgetting to enter patient’s allergy information might have serious consequences on the patient’s safety. However, if one has a good understanding of error detection, one can design the electronic prescribing system to better support doctors’ error detection ability. This then reduces the likelihood of adverse events. With the advance of technology, the dispersion of medical devices is no longer restricted to hospitals but also patients’ home, for example, insulin pumps. The users of medical devices are not only medical professionals but also the general public. Therefore, part of the overall aim of this project is to examine human error detection with medical devices. This investigation will adopt an experimental approach to examining human error detection in a laboratory setting, in which human participants will be asked to carry out tasks using simulated medical devices. This approach will enable us to isolate variables and test them in a systematic and controlled manner. This way we can be confident to pinpoint the causes that affect error detection abilities. Our results will complement the approach in which observations of the phenomenon of interest are made in natural settings. The precision of the experimental approach will complement the realism of the observational approach by completing different parts of the same puzzle. This project is a collaboration with an internationally renowned centre for human-computer interaction (HCI) research, University College London Interaction Centre (UCLIC). We plan to establish and maintain a long-term international collaboration between Lingnan University and UCLIC. The outcome of this project will not only benefit the academic community but also practitioners who want to improve the safety of medical devices. 本研究旨在探討與理解偵測醫療儀器操作之人為失誤的心理機制。本研究項目中所檢測的因素將分成三大主題：1) 人們如何發現自己的錯誤﹔2) 工作環境如何影響人們偵測錯誤﹔3)人們如何發現別人的錯誤。 理解如何偵測人為失誤，對於安全至上的範疇(如：醫學應用)尤其重要。舉一個例，醫生使用電子配藥系統來處方藥物時，如果忘記輸入病人對藥物過敏的資料，便可能對病人的安全構成嚴重影響。然而，要是人們對失誤偵測有深入認識，就可設計一些更配合醫生失誤偵測能力的電子配藥系統，發生醫療事故的可能性則可相應減少。隨著科技進步，醫療儀器不再只限於醫院使用，在病人家中也可採用如胰島素泵等的醫療儀器。使用醫療儀器的人士不只限於專業醫護人員，還包括一般民眾。因此，本研究的其中一個目的是探討使用醫療儀器的人如何偵測失誤。 是次研究將採用實驗方式，以探究於實驗室環境下，人們如何偵測人為失誤。實驗中，受試者將使用模擬醫療儀器執行任務。我們採用實驗方式把變項分隔出來，並在有系統、受控的情況下測試這些變項，因此我們確信可準確地查出影響失誤偵測能力的原因。本研究結果將與於自然環境下觀察相關現象的研究方式互相補足。精確的實驗方式可與現實的觀察方式互補不足。 本研究是一項與國際知名的人機互動(human computer interaction (HCI)) 研究中心--倫敦大學學院互動中心(University College London Interaction Centre (UCLIC))的協作項目。該項目旨在建立並維持嶺南大學與UCLIC長遠的國際協作。是次研究結果將不僅對學術界帶來貢獻，對致力改善醫療儀器安全的從業人員也大有裨益。

342912.label: Realisation of objectives
342912.value: Objective 1. Improve understanding of human error detection by identifying empirical factors that influence one’s error detection of cognitive slips in particular. Objective 1 has been successfully achieved through a series of laboratory-based experiments and a number of empirical factors that influence error detection performance were identified. In the series of experiments performed, we were able to design and develop novel experimental tasks to examine cognitive slips in transcribing and information checking tasks. We were also able to operationalise error detection behaviour in terms of eye movements and utilized an eye tracker with one of our experimental tasks for data collection. We were able to further understand human error detection by examining a number of empirical factors including monetary reward and punishment, working memory capacity, interruption position and interruption task type. Objective 2. Generate recommendations and guidelines for HCI practitioners to design safer medical devices by supporting better error detection. Objective 2 has been successfully achieved: we were able to generate recommendations for practitioners’ consideration for designing medical devices to better support error detection. The recommendations are based on some of the main findings of the project. For example, the effect of monetary reward and punishment suggests that, when errors have consequences, people exhibit more accurate task performance and more rigorous checking behaviour than when errors have no consequences. This finding contributes to understanding error detection in terms of how checking behaviour can be motivated. Regarding motivating more careful behaviour, one recommendation is to consider promoting reward rather than punishment. In situations where reward and punishment are equally feasible to be implemented as a managerial policy, rewarding desired behaviour is likely to lead to better outcomes than punishing undesired behaviour, which may encourage people to cover up errors and no learning can take place. We have also developed a different line of research examining detection performance in anaesthetic monitoring. This research is related to the overall project as it is concerned with safety associated with medical technology. In the context of anaesthetic monitoring, the technology under investigate is auditory display, which uses sound to convey information about patient’s physiological vital signs (e.g. oxygen saturation and heart rate), and error detection is defined as the ability to detect undesired patient status. In this investigation, we have developed a laboratory-based task to compare the effectiveness of two types of auditory displays in conveying patient information: earcons and spearcons. Earcons use abstract sounds to represent different vital signs of different levels, the mapping of the sounds to the vital signs requires learning. Spearcons are speech-based earcons and vital signs are represented by time-compressed speech phrases. Based on the evidence we obtained, we recommend the use of spearcons over earcons as spearcons were shown to lead to better detection performance and require less learning than earcons. Objective 3. Develop a long-term international collaboration between Lingnan University and University College London Interaction Centre (UCLIC), an internationally renowned HCI centre. Objective 3 has been partially, but not fully, achieved because there is no immediate work between Lingnan University and UCLIC following on from the completed project. However, the PI has built good collaborative relationships with Prof. Ann Blandford and Dr. Anna Cox at UCLIC through this project and UCLIC has conferred the PI the title of Honorary Research Associate for the period August 2012 to July 2017. Future collaboration is certainly possible. Despite the above under-achievement, the PI was able to develop new collaborations with other institutions. The PI has established international collaboration with Prof. Penelope Sanderson at The University of Queensland, Australia, and this collaboration has led to a co-authored paper that is currently under review. The PI has also developed local collaboration with Dr. Calvin Or at The University of Hong Kong, which resulted in two co-authored papers: one published and one under review. These collaborations are on-going with regular meetings. The PI has also successfully established research collaboration with Dr. Benny Cheng, a consultant anaesthetist at Tuen Mun Hospital, to carry out healthcare human factors research.
