342912.label: Major findings and research outcome
342912.value: Research output in Part C are summarised as follow for ease of reference: ============================== Article 1: Li, S. Y. W., Cox, A. L., Or, C., & Blandford, A. (2016). Effects of monetary reward and punishment on information checking behaviour. Applied Ergonomics, 53, 258-266. Article 2: Li, S. Y. W., Cox, A. L., Or, C., & Blandford, A. (under review). Effects of monetary reward and punishment on information checking behaviour. Article 3: Li, S. Y. W., Tang, T.-L., Hickling, A., Yau, S., Brecknell, B., Sanderson, P. M. (under review) Spearcons for patient monitoring: Laboratory investigation comparing earcons and spearcons. Article 4: Yau, S. Y., & Li, S. Y. W. (2015). Working memory and the detection of different error types: novel predictions for error detection. In Proceedings of the 33rd Annual ACM Conference Extended Abstracts on Human Factors in Computing Systems (pp. 1031-1036). Article 5: Yau, S. Y. (2015). Effect of self-interruption and external interruption on error detection. Unpublished Master's thesis, Lingnan University, Hong Kong. ============================== The major findings are organised into three main themes: the first theme relates to computer-based transcribing behaviour and there are two major findings. First, when errors have reward or punishment as consequence, people exhibit more accurate task performance and more rigorous checking behaviour than when errors have no consequences. This finding is supported by two experiments (Article 1), and is also replicated by a further eye-tracking study (Article 2). Second, people are able to achieve more accurate task performance when provided with immediate reward rather than punishment. This finding is supported by an eye-tracking experiment (Article 2). The second theme is about cross checking information and there are three main findings: first, when working memory capacity is exceeded, error detection performance gets impaired (Article 4). Second, interruption occurring just before a check leads to worse error detection than interruption occurring during a check. Third, different kinds of interruption task do not have differential effect on detection performance. These findings are supported by a series of paper-and-pencil and computer-based experiments (Article 5). The third theme arises from the work that examines detection performance using medical devices, such as auditory displays of patients’ vital signs, in anaesthetic monitoring. We compared two kinds of auditory displays: earcons (vital signs represented by abstract sounds) and speech-based earcons (vital signs represented by time-compressed speech phrases). The main finding suggests that people are better at detecting vital signs with spearcons than earcons (Article 3).

342912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
342912.value: Understanding how errors may be detected is particularly important in safety-critical domains, such as, healthcare. For example, when prescribing medications using an electronic prescribing system, doctors forgetting to enter patient’s allergy information might have serious consequences on the patient’s safety. However, if one has a good understanding of error detection, one can design the electronic prescribing system to better support doctors’ error detection ability. This then reduces the likelihood of adverse events. This research adopts an experimental approach to examine human error detection in laboratory settings, in which human participants are asked to carry out simulated clinical tasks. As setting up experiments in clinical environments is complex and expensive, it is progressive to test one’s hypotheses in a laboratory setting first before a clinical setting. Through this research, we have identified a number of factors that can influence one’s ability to detect errors when checking information for correctness. These factors include motivation incurred by monetary reward and punishment, limitation of the human memory system, and disruption caused by interruptions. Based on these factors, we have gained better understanding of error detection and are able to generate recommendations for technology designers to consider when they design healthcare technology.

343112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
343112.value: This project studies the early history of exhibiting contemporary Chinese paintings in the United States during the 1940s through a study of the Lingnan Foundation collection of paintings, housed at Lingnan University in Hong Kong. This collection of paintings includes some 150 works collected by Szto Wai 司徒衛, an alumnus and former faculty member of the University. The paintings are primarily by former members of the Guangdong National Painting Research Society (Guangdong guohua yanjiu hui 廣東國畫研究會), one of the largest painting associations in Republican China (1912-1949). Its stance was to preserve and revive the traditions of Chinese painting without assimilating Western ideas. The artists represented in the collection include leading figures of the Society such as Huang Bore 黃般若 (1901-1968), Deng Fen 鄧芬 (1894-1964), Li Fengting 李鳳廷 (1883-1967) and Zhao Haogong 趙浩公 (1881-1947). The Lingnan Foundation collection of paintings was exhibited at the National Arts Club in New York in 1947 under the title of “Contemporary Chinese Painting”. It is an early example of exhibitions of this kind in the United States and part of growing interest among American audiences for contemporary Chinese art rather than artefacts from the imperial period. The event can be compared to other exhibitions under a similar theme held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, around that time. This project will examine the rationale and contexts for these exhibitions, and how they were presented and received. It will consider these exhibitions within the context of Sino-American relations during the heightened political climate of the 1940s. In addition to examining the early exhibition history of contemporary Chinese paintings in the United States, this project will also be the first study focusing on the Lingnan Foundation collection of paintings. It aims to locate the paintings within the oeuvres of major painters in the collection and establish how the collection was formed. In particular, the collection and its exhibition will be studied in relation to efforts to revive the Guangdong National Painting Research Society following its disbandment in 1938 as a result of the Sino-Japanese War. 400212.label: Realisation of objectives
400212.value: The stoichiometric, selective cleavage of aliphatic carbon-carbon bonds of alkanes by transition metal complexes and catalytic hydrogenation with water using paraparacyclophane (PCP) as the prototypical substrate have been accomplished. All group 9 metalloporphyrins complexes of Co, Rh and Ir have been examined. Co porphyrin can only catalyze the hydrogen using DMF as the hydrogen atom donor. Rh porphyrin achieves the catalysis with water as the hydrogen source without generating hydrogen throughout the reaction to give about 85% yield of hydrocarbon. However, carbon-hydrogen bond activation occurs in the post catalytic carbon-carbon bond activation to yield about 15% yield of stilbene. Iridium complexes achieve the hydrogenation with water to give almost quantitative yield of hydrogenated product without any stilbene formation. The trend of reactivity among the group 9 metals reveals the importance of M-C strength in stabilizing the M-C intermediates formed in the catalysis for the hydrogenation with water to occur, otherwise homolysis of M-C (in Co-C) proceeds without the feasibility of hydrogenation with water. Mechanistic studies of stoichiometric carbon-carbon bond action of paracyclophane (PCP) by kinetic studies. The rate law and activation parameters have been measured. Most interestingly, it is second order on Rh(tmp) and first order on PCP, showing a very novel bimetalloradical activation of carbon-carbon single bond. The hydrolysis studies of M(porphyrin)alkyls (M= Rh, Ir) show a novel bimetallic reductive elimination (BMRE) process from M(por)-R and M(por)H to give R-H. This BMRE is even faster than the hydrolysis of of M(por)R with water to give R-H by at least 3 times. This accounts the fact that Ir (por) is the most active catalyst. The direct observation of these metalloporphyrin alkyls in the catalyses and their slow conversion into hydrogenation product supports that the hydrogenation is the turn over limiting step in the catalysis, rather than the apparently difficult carbon-carbon activation. Photochemical hydrogenation with water has been attempted but yet unsuccessful. The above findings strongly support that the catalytic hydrogenation of PCP with water is going through a bimetalloradical activation of C-C bond to give a dimetalloporphyrin alkyl intermediate. Partial hydrolysis to give some metalloporphyrin hydride, which can also exist in solution in the catalysis, further promotes the hydrogenation of metalloporphyrin alkyl to the alkane as the dominant process. The metalloporphyrin hydride is thus a very efficient catalyst for the catalytic hydrogenation. Among the group 9 metal, iridium is the most efficient catalyst. These finding and conclusion enlightens us that 2 metals is better 1.

400412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400412.value: Image restoration problems refer to the recovery of clean images from degraded ones. It is an important task in image processing with a wide range of applications. Typical examples include (i) image denoising—removing noise say in magnetic resonance imaging and (ii) image deblurring—removing blur, e.g., caused by shaking when the image is taken. The task of image restoration is to recover an image close to the true image when we are given the observed noisy and/or blurry image and some information about the imaging system. One standard approach for restoring the image is to minimize a function which is the sum of two terms: (i) a data-fitting term that measures how well the restored image is fitting the observed data under the imaging system and (ii) a regularization term that specifies the properties that the restored image must satisfy. To balance the effect of the two terms, we multiply one of them by a number, called the regularization parameter. How to find the best regularization parameter that balances the two terms and gives the best restored image is an active research area. When the regularization term is quadratic, there are established methods for finding a good regularization parameter. In this proposal, we however focus ourselves on non-quadratic regularization terms because it is well known that the corresponding models preserve edges better and hence can give better restored images. A common non-quadratic regularization term is the total-variation (TV) regularization. Because it is non-quadratic, the optimal parameter is difficult to find. One sometimes just determines it by trial-and-error and therefore has to solve the problem many times. Recently, we have developed an effective algorithm for finding the best parameter of the TV-deblurring problem and proved that the algorithm converges to the optimal solution. Our algorithm determines the best regularization parameter and restores the image simultaneously. Hence there is no need to solve the problem multiple times. The goal of the project is to extend our methodology to design new efficient algorithms that can handle more general image restoration problems with non-quadratic regularization terms. We will derive a convergence theory for these new algorithms, and compare these algorithms with existing ones in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness. We will apply our method to important practical problems in image processing, such as Poisson noise removal (appears in medical imaging), super-resolution image reconstruction (appears in high-definition imaging), and blind deconvolution (appears in satellite imaging). 图像恢复问题是指利用受损的图像恢复出原始图像。这个问题是图像处理中的热点问题，并具有广泛的应用。它包括两类问题：（1）图像去噪问题---例如，核磁共振成像中的去噪问题；（2）图像去模糊问题-----例如，拍摄图像时由于晃动所造成的模糊。图像恢复的任务是利用所观察到的受损图像（指遭受噪声干扰或噪声、模糊同时并存）恢复出真实图像及图像的相关信息。 通常，我们通过求解一个无约束优化问题以恢复原始图像，其中目标函数包括两项：其中一项是数据拟合项，用以衡量恢复图像和观测图像之间的误差；另一项是正则项，用以体现所恢复图像需要满足的特殊性质。为了平衡这两项，通常我们引入一个正的参数作为其中一项的系数，称为正则化参数。 如何找到最好的正则化参数是图像处理领域的一个热点问题。这里所谓最好的正则化参数是指可以使图像恢复效果最好的参数值。当正则项是二次函数时，已经有一些方法可以用来确定最好正则化参数。然而，我们主要关心的是非二次正则化模型中的正则化参数的选取问题，因为对于非二次正则化模型可以更好的保留图像的边界信息和给出更好的恢复效果。全变差正则化模型是最常见的非二次正则化模型。由于正则项是非二次的，所以最好的正则化参数很难确定。通常我们通过反复试验来确定一个最好的平衡参数，这样的代价是需要多次求解原问题。最近，我们提出了一个有效的算法来寻找全变差模型中的最优的正则化参数。我们的算法优点在于，在确定最优正则化参数的同时，恢复出原始图像。这样一种方法克服了传统的通过多次求解原问题来确定最优平衡参数的困难。 本项目的目标是，对于更一般的非二次模型，推广我们提出的有效算法达到同时确定最优平衡参数和求解图像恢复问题的目的。对于我们提出的方法，我们将建立方法的收敛性，并从速度，精度和稳健性的角度与现存的方法作比较。最后，我们将采用我们的方法去求解一些重要的实际问题，例如去除泊松噪声（出现在医疗成像），超分辨率图像重建（出现在高清晰度成像），盲解卷积问题（出现在卫星影像）。

400412.label: Major findings and research outcome
400412.value: 1. We have developed two new methods for solving TV-like problems. One is the non-stationary iterated thresholding algorithm, and the other is the inertial proximal ADMM method. The latter method is especially powerful for linearly constrained separable convex problems. 2. We have developed a powerful approach for image segmentation (2-stage approach). The idea is to smooth the image and then thresholding to get the segmentation. The resulting variational problem is easy to solve (can be solved by the primal-dual approach we designed) new 3. We have extended our methods to new applications: (i) applying the super-resolution image reconstruction technique to ground-based astronomy to get higher resolution of the incoming wavefront, and (ii) designing tightframe to classify and authenticate paintings. 4. We have carried out convergence analysis for the new methods we proposed and systematic tests for the above applications. Note to the publications: 1. 400412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400412.value: Many of the imaging processing problems can be solved via an optimization method. The effectiveness of the optimization method affect how fast and accurate the resulting image will be. In this project, we have developed two new methods for solving a very general type of optimization models: the TV-like problems. One method is an extension of a very general class of algorithm: iterative thresholding method. We derived a non-stationary variant of it. Another popular class of algorithm is the ADMM method. We derived an inertial variant of it. Both are proved to be better than the existing ones. We also consider practical applications in image processing where our methods work. The first one is image segmentation where we proposed a new paradigm for it--SaT (smoothing and thresholding). It transforms a very complex non-convex problem into a simple convex one where our methods can easily solve it. Another one is to reconstruct wave-front in telescope using high-resolution image reconstruction. The resulting model can easily be solved by our method too. Finally, we also consider stylometry where we used tightframe approach to authenticate authorship of paintings.

400612.label: Project Objectives
400612.value: Formulate a general framework that encompasses the generalized Pólya urn models which are widely applied in clinical trials as a tool to generate treatment allocation schemes. The major features and characteristics of this framework will be investigated in order to provide useful guidance to future applications of these urn models. Derive asymptotic results that are essential for model specification and treatment comparisons. Since there has been a shortage of fundamental statistical theories regarding the applications of the randomly reinforced Pólya urns, clinical data analysts are handicapped in their quest for a better understanding of the urn mechanism and a suitable evaluation of the performance of various treatments. This study will certainly fulfill the needs of these practitioners. Develop, under our proposed framework, means to identify and derive superior treatment allocation schemes that yield a higher proportion of patients being assigned to the better treatments in a clinical study. Conduct simulation studies to deliver a complete portrait of findings of our comparative studies of different urn models. Study a wide spectrum of response variables including dichotomous, categorical, continuous and multivariate in order to cover an extensive range of clinical applications.

400612.label: Realisation of objectives
400612.value: The objectives stated in the research proposal have been achieved. Important theoretical results have been developed to encompass the generalized Polya urn mechanism, with special applications to adaptive treatment allocations in clinical trials. These useful theoretical results include the rate of convergence of the number of patients assigned to each treatment under a set of minimum required conditions and the distributions of the limits. Further, asymptotic behavior for the nonhomogeneous case was also studied. Covariate-adjusted adaptive designs were also discussed under the generalized linear models paradigm. To ensure the suggested treatment allocation scheme performs satisfactory, comprehensive simulation studies were conducted to reveal the operational characteristics of the framework, including the treatment allocations, failure rates, and test power for various covariate-adjusted response-adaptive designs.

400612.label: Major findings and research outcome
400612.value: Major findings: 1) The general framework that encompasses the generalized Pólya urn models which are widely applied in clinical trials as a tool to generate treatment allocation schemes is investigated. We successfully derived the major features and characteristics of this framework, including asymptotic results related to the rate of convergence of the number of patients assigned to each treatment under a set of minimum required conditions and the asymptotic normalities. These asymptotic results are important to serve as basis for statistical inferences. 2) We have also, under the studied urn model, derive the distributions of both the limit of the normalized number of patients allocated to each treatment and the limit of the normalized number of balls (treatments) of each type. 3) The more complicated nonhomogeneous model is studied and the updating mechanism of the urn is also examined with important properties being derived. 4) Covariate-adjusted designs were examined that incorporate useful information of patients in order to reduce the number of failure on average being assigned to the inferior treatments. The results are particularly important for clinical studies when a failure case would lead to a fatal consequence. 5) To substantiate our proposed treatment allocation schemes, we have also study small sample behavior through extensive simulation studies.

400612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400612.value: There are at least two directions for further research that are important to this area. First, the suggested designs have been constructed and applied to less complicated clinical settings. However, in the quest for better treatments to cure a particular disease, the clinical studies could be very complicated. For example, it is now very popular to perform non-inferiority trials in which there are three types of treatments, the placebo, the active treatment and the reference treatments. Under these more complicated settings, the adaptive designs developed thus far have to be reformulated in order to cope with clinical considerations such as assay sensitivity and stopping criteria. Second, there have been a vast number of research and approaches in adaptive designs, but a lack of a comprehensive study to give a systematic comparative review of these methods. It would therefore be important to provide an extensive study to produce a guideline for practitioners in this area.

400612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400612.value: In most clinical trials, patients accrual sequentially. It is well recognized that with a randomized treatment allocation scheme, it could reduce treatment assignment bias. The importance of response-adaptive designs is that they offer randomized treatment allocation schemes that assign different treatments to incoming patients based on the observed responses of previous patients. The main benefit of such designs is that they reduce the number of patients receiving inferior treatments while maintaining a high level of test power for statistical inferences about treatment efficacy. In this project, we developed efficient adaptive designs that utilize information (such as different characteristics of patients) and efficacy of treatments thus far to achieve the objective of reducing patients being sent to inferior treatments. It is of vital importance especially in cases when failure of the treatment results in fatal consequences. To substantial the application of the suggested procedures, solid theoretical justifications are also provided.

400712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400712.value: Many important applications of polymers rely heavily on their arrangement and ordering in the solid state. Finding out the fundamental principles that govern this process is very important towards the design of polymers for specific applications. In this proposal we would like to use a special kind of polymer, namely, dendronized polymer as a model to explore new factors that may affect its assembling process. This speciial type of polymer are of immense interest because it has a relatively well defined and rigid backbone architecture that enable it to be used as building block towards the construction of more complex architecture in a predictable manner. In addition to environmental parameters such as temperature and solvent, several inherent structural factors have been found to affect the organization of dendronized polymers in the solid state. The first key factor is the nature of the chemical groups residing on the polymer backbone or/and the side chains. In general, the presence of chemical entities that can interact with each other will enhance the self association strength and can also influence the overall three dimensional shape of the polymer. The second is concerned with the shape of the polymer backbone. If the backbone can easily adopt a defined conformation, its further self assembly into higher hierarchical structure would be facilitated. Last but not least, the length of the polymer chain can also have a profound effect on its self assembling properties. In this proposal we would like to investigate other instrinsic structural parameters, namely, the backbone symmetry, the interacting functional group density and periodicity, on the solid-state properties of dendronized polymers. These are new structural factors that have not been thoroughly examined before. By preparing a series of structurally related dendronized polymers having different backbone symmetry, hydrogen bonding functional group density and periodicity, we should be able to identify new and important insights and parameters for us to design polymers with improved properties for various applications. 聚合物的很多重要應用取決於它們在固體狀態中的排列和順序。找出控制這一過程的基本原則對有特定應用的聚合物的設計是非常重要的。在這份建議書裡，我們想使用一種特殊的聚合物，即樹枝狀聚合物，作為一種模型來探索可能會影響其組裝過程的新因素。這類特殊的聚合物十分有趣，因其具有相對明確的定義和剛性的骨幹體系結構，使其可用作構建單元，以可預測的方式組建更複雜的體系結構。 除了環境參數 (如溫度和溶劑)，我們還發現幾個固有的結構性因素會影響樹枝狀聚合物在固體狀態中的組裝。第一個關鍵因素是聚合物骨幹或 / 和側鏈上的化學基團的性質。一般來說，可以彼此相互作用的化學實體的存在將增強自組裝的能力，也會影響聚合物整體的三維形狀。第二，與聚合物骨幹的形狀有關。如果骨幹可輕易採用已定義的構象,其將進一步組裝成更高層次的結構。最後，高分子鏈的長度也可對其自組裝性質產生深遠的影響。 在這項建議書裡，我們想要調查其他內在結構參數，即骨幹的對稱性、相互作用的官能團密度和週期性上的樹枝狀聚合物的固體狀態性質。這些都是之前未全面探究的新結構因素。通過製備一系列結構上相關的具有不同的骨幹對稱、氫鍵官能團密度和週期性的樹枝狀聚合物，我們相信能夠發掘出新的重要的見解和參數，以便我們為各種應用設計出性能改進的聚合物

400712.label: Realisation of objectives
400712.value: 1. Objectives 1 and 2. The key objective of this proposal is to find out how the arrangement of molecular dipole units inside an oligomer or a polymer can affect the self-assembly properties. Two specific types of dipole alignment were investigated here. In the first type all dipoles are aligned in pseudo parallel (also called as non-centrosymmetric) fashion while in the second the neighboring dipoles are aligned in pseudo antiparallel fashion (also called as centrosymmetric). To avoid the disorientation of the molecular dipoles due to backfolding of the backbone, the oligomer/polymer chain are rigidified by decorating with large side chains. The molecular dipole unit employed was p-alkyoxybenzamide. A. Preparation of non-centrosymmetric (AB-1) and centrosymmetric (AABB-2) amide-based dendronized oligomers and polymers bearing a worm-like architecture were successfully achieved (see Appendix - Figure 1 for structures). Nonetheless, the synthetic work was very difficult as several unanticipated interfering factors were identified which hampered smooth execution of the synthesis. First, considerable time was spent to optimize the structure of the side chain solubilization group in order to confer the oligomers and polymers with good solubility. Second, the linker between the amide units was also found to play a significant role in controlling their solubility and conformational properties. Details of these problems were already disclosed in the midterm report. After optimization, a xylylene linker and a racemic branching side chain were found to be the best in the structural design. B. The structure, self-assembling and organogelating properties of the two synthesized isomeric polyamides (i.e. AB-1 and AABB-2) as well as their analogous oligomers were investigated by various physical techniques such as nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, gel permeation chromatography, infra-red spectroscopy, powder X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy. In particular, the kinetic and thermodynamic parameters of the gelation processes were extracted using differential scanning calorimetry and diffusion wave spectroscopy. C. It was found that the different local dipole-dipole interactions, originated from the different dipole alignments of the AB-1 and AABB-2 polymers, had a significant impact on their self-assembling and organogelating properties. Hence, the dipole parallel-aligned oligomers and polymer (i.e. AB-1) were found to exhibit inferior gelation strength and less-ordered packing in the gel state as compared to the dipole antiparallel-aligned analogues (i.e. AABB-2) based on the measured enthalpy and entropy of melting and also data from powder X-ray diffraction analysis. All these results could be readily rationalized by invoking a local dipole-dipole interaction model. However, the weaker gelation strength of the dipole parallel-aligned oligomers and polymer were not simply due to thermodynamic factors, kinetic trapping of the dipole parallel-aligned oligomers and polymer in a less stable packing arrangement in the gel state was also found to contribute to their inferior gelation strength. This is the most significant finding originated from this project, as previous literature works seldom addressed the importance of kinetic trapping in the self-assembly of organogelators. On the other hand, the degree of oligomerization does not seem to have a strong influence on the strength of the self-assembling if one uses the enthalpy of melting as the assessment criterion. Furthermore, it was found that despite their close structural resemblance, the two polymers AB-1 and AABB-2 exhibited self-sorting in the gel state by differential scanning calorimetry. Again this can be rationalized using the unfavorable local dipole-dipole interaction between the two polymers in the mixed state. 2. Despite numerous attempts, synthetic efforts to anchor the oligomeric fragments into a branching core failed to give pure polymer samples with branched or star-shape backbone geometry. When using the proposed 1,2,4,5-benzenetetracarboxylic acid as the core, the coupling reaction was sluggish and no product could be identified. On the other hand, using the other proposed 1,3,5-benzenetricarboxylic acid, a mixture of doubly- and triply-anchored product was formed (see Appendix - Scheme 1). Despite numerous attempts, these two products were inseparable by liquid chromatography nor size exclusion chromatography. Other coupling reagents were also tried but the reaction could not be driven to completion. In the end, neither the branching nor the star polymers could be obtained. It was believed that the failure was due to severe steric congestion developed when the oligomer chains were brought close to each other near the branching junction. Since pure products were required in order to conduct a comparative study, as a result, we did not investigate their self-assembly properties. 3. Objective 3: Several non-centrosymmetric AB-type oligoamides and polyamides AB-3, AB-4, AB-5 and AB-6 with different spacer chain lengths ranging from two to five methylene units were prepared (see Appendix - Figure 2). The amide functional group density decreases gradually from AB-3 to AB-6 due to the increasing number of methylene units. It was found that oligomers and polymers AB-4 and AB-6 with odd-numbered methylene spacers possessed greatly reduced solubilities but enhanced gelation powers in organic solvents, while oligoamides and polyamides with even numbered methylene spacers (AB-3 and AB-5) are highly soluble. Our preliminary results showed that the odd-even methylene effect played a more crucial role in the solubility and organogelating abilities of the polyamides, while the hydrogen bonding unit density effect on the self-assembling properties was not apparent. While the structures of AB-3 and AB-5 could be ascertained, it was impossible to unequivocally confirm the structures of AB-4 and AB-6 by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy. Due to their extremely poor solubility, the molecular weight information of AB-4 and AB-6 could not be obtained by gel permeation chromatography or laser light scattering technique. As a result, a comparative study of their self-assembly properties was not conducted. 4. Objective 4: Attempts were made to prepare a non-centrosymmetric, AB-type co(dendronized polyamide) AB-7 by the copolymerization of a mixture of bi-functional monomers bearing different oligomethylene spacers (see Appendix - Scheme 2). The resulting polymer AB-7 was expected to have the amide hydrogen bonding units located at irregular intervals along the backbone because the copolymerization should be a random process. Since the different monomers may not possess the same reactivity in the copolymerization, it was necessary to estimate their relative percentage of incorporation in the polymer. Unfortunately, it was impossible to find out the molar ratio of the different oligomethylene spacer units in the copolymer because of 1H NMR signal overlapping of the protons originated from the different oligomethylene chains. Because of this technical problem, their self-assembly properties were not conducted.

400712.label: Major findings and research outcome
400712.value: 1. The alignment of dipole moments along a polymer chain was found to have a significant impact on their self-assembly strength. The local dipole-dipole interaction can be used to explain the strength of polymer chain self-assembly. However, both kinetics and thermodynamic factors should be considered when developing the self-assembling model. 2. Additional factors should be taken into account when studying the self-assembly and organogelation properties of polymers and long chain oligomers. In particular, the process of kinetic trapping, which is of lesser importance in the self-assembly of small molecules, becomes much more important in the study of polymer physical gels. 3. The synthesis and characterization of branched oligoamides and polyamides is a non-trivial problem. This is mainly due to the high polarity of the multiple amide units which led to premature precipitation from the reaction mixture and insufficient solublility properties to allow for structural characterization. In case of mixture formation, it was impossible to separate the side products from the target compound. 4. Every structural elements (side chain, flexibility of the backbone, intramolecular hydrogen bonding) play a role in controlling the solubility and self-assembly properties of oligoamides and polyamides. Careful structural design is needed prior to carrying out the experimental work for this type of molecule. 5. Part of the research results was published in Chem. Eur. J., one of the top journals in chemistry and also presented in an international conference (European Polymer Congress, Dresden 2015, Germany). The work also constituted part of the PhD thesis of a graduate student, Ms Chui-Fan Leung. 6. Additional experimental evidence had been obtained to demonstrate the importance of kinetic trapping in the self-assembling properties of these relatively large organogelators. We are in the process of writing up another paper entitled "Kinetic trapping in the organogelation of oligoamides and polyamides" on this interesting finding.

400712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400712.value: In this project we showed that the alignment of molecular dipoles inside a molecule, in particular oligomers and polymers with large molecular dimension, plays an important role in controlling their self-association properties. Although the research outcome is focused more on the theoretical aspect, but it should find useful applications in many practical areas. It is well established that the photophysical, optoelectronic and materials applications of functional molecules relied heavily on their self-assembly mode. Knowing that one can make use of the dipole alignment to control these properties may open up an alternative method to further improve their functional properties. For example, it would be interesting to compare the optoelectronic performances of a non-centrosymmetric versus a centrosymmetric PLED.

400712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400712.value: The physical properties and practical applications of molecules such as polymers rely on how they pack together in the solid state. In this project, it was found that the packing arrangement and therefore the packing strength, can be influenced by the arrangement of the small molecular dipoles that are residing in the polymer. This finding can help us to design materials with improved application scopes by controlling the dipole alignment inside the polymer.

400912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400912.value: The aim of the project is to develop a general theory of the dissipative structure for a class of symmetric hyperbolic systems with non-symmetric relaxation and also apply it to the study of large time behavior of solutions to the fluid dynamics equations in plasma physics. The subject is mainly concerned with systems of nonlinear conservation laws appearing widely in different fields such as the gas dynamics, electromagnetism, magnetohydrodynamics and kinetic theory. A typical feature for them is that solutions may form singularity in finite time and thus only weak solutions can be considered for global well-posedness with large data. For a general system of conservation laws, a fundamental problem is to investigate the behavior of solution in large time. In fact, a weak solution locally behaves as some wave patterns such as shock wave, rarefaction wave and contact discontinuity. However, a physical system is often followed by additional dissipative mechanism such as diffusion and collision, which in turn makes it possible that classical solutions also exist globally in time, at least near existing steady states. The time asymptotic stability of solutions in such situation strongly depends on interaction between conservation and dissipation as two opposite effects on the system. A well-known criterion to ensure the time asymptotics is the Kawashima condition for general strongly entropy-dissipative system. Unfortunately, it only works for symmetric relaxation source after linearization. So far, a general theory in the case of nonsymmetric relaxation, which is the key issue of the project, is still lack of the satisfactory investigation. On the other hand, as applications, we will also deal with a typical hyperbolic system with nonsymmetric relaxation effect that is the damped Euler-Maxwell governing the motion of ionized plasma under the self-consistent electromagnetic field. Since the large-time behavior for systems without any external forcing has been extensively studied, we will focus on the pointwise estimate on solutions and the convergence to the nontrivial wave patterns when the electromagnetic field is present, with emphasis on investigating the effect of external forces on the large-time asymptotics. It is under the influence of a magnetic field that plasmas may exhibit complex structures such as filaments, beams and double layer. We expect that the potential research outcome of the project will provide some rigorous mathematical understanding of the varied and subtle plasma behavior. 本项目旨在建立一套带有非对称松弛项的对称双曲系统的耗散结构理论，并应用它去研究等离子物理中的流体力学方程组解的大时间行为。 非线性守恒律组是本项目主要关注的对象。它们广泛出现在气体动力学、电磁学、磁流体力学以及分子运动论等领域中。它们的典型特征是解在有限时间可能出现奇性，因此大初值解的全局适定性必须在弱解范围内考虑。对于一般的守恒律组，一个基本的问题是这些弱解的大时间行为。实际上，弱解的局部表现一般是一些基本波，例如激波、稀疏波以及接触间断。 然而，物理系统时常会有附加的耗散机制，例如扩散和碰撞，这些促成可能获取全局经典解至少在稳态解附近的存在性。在这种情形下，解的时间渐近稳定性强烈地依赖于系统的守恒与耗散两种截然相反的效应的相互作用。众所周知，Kawashima条件就是一个判别一般强熵耗散方程组的解是否时间渐近稳定的准则。但是，它仅仅适用于松弛项在线性化后是对称的情形。到目前为止，非对称松弛项的情形仍然缺乏比较满意的研究，此乃本项目关注的重点。 另一方面，作为抽象理论的应用，我们将研究一个典型的具有非对称松弛效应的双曲系统——带阻尼的Euler-Maxwell方程组。该方程组描述的是在自诱导的电磁场中电离化的等离子体的运动。由于不带任何外力的方程组的解的大时间行为已经有了广泛的研究结果，我们将集中考虑当出现电磁场时解的点态估计和解到非平凡的基本波的收敛性，以及着重研究外力对解的大时间行为的影响。 在磁场的影响下，等离子体将会呈现出复杂的结构，例如丝极、电波、双电荷层等。我们期待，本项目可能的研究结果能给出对于等离子体各种复杂行为的一些严格的数学理解。

400912.label: Realisation of objectives
400912.value: The main objectives of this project are basically twofold, namely, developing a general theory and applying it to the concrete models. Specifically, the general theory is concerned with the study of the linear dissipative structure of the first-order symmetric hyperbolic systems with non-symmetric relaxation, and the applications are related to the investigations of the models for the fluid plasma and the kinetic plasma, such as the Euler-Maxwell system and the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system, respectively. In the mean time, some related models have been also considered, for instance, the coupling system of the Fokker-Planck equation with the Euler system through the friction force, and the two-component Euler-Poincare equations. The original four objectives have been completely achieved. For item 1, we found out a class of systems whose form is general enough. We proposed a new terminology for characterizing the regularity-loss type of dissipation of the strictly dissipative hyperbolic system. The general conditions required to assure the corresponding dissipation types are also found, and they can be regarded as the extension of the classical Kawashima stability condition to the case when the regularity-loss over the high-frequency region can occur. The proof is based on the elementary Fourier energy method as well as the suitable linear combination of different energy inequalities. Although the used approach is quite basic, it is hard to treat the estimates for the very higher phase dimensions. Particularly, the point is that we are looking for the optimal dissipation type in the sense that the product rate of the Fourier energy functional is consistent with the one of the slowest component. Thus, the linear combination of energy inequalities with different weights should be made in an appropriate way. Item 2 and Item 3 are mainly concerned with the Green's functions and the large-time asymptotic behavior of solutions for the two-fluid Euler-Maxwell system with damping. We consider the system with physical parameters involving the masses, charges, and temperatures of two kinds of particles as well as the Debye length, and linearize the system around the constant states without vacuum and in the case when the background magnetic field is zero. Then, the first step is to carry out the spectral analysis of the linearized system. Since the background magnetic field is zero and the magnetic field is divergence-free, we can decompose such large-size linear system to two coupling subsystems with one for the density and projections of the velocity and the electric field along the Fourier variable, and the other for the magnetic field and projections of the velocity and the electric field along the plane norm to the Fourier variable. In such way, the Green's functions in the Fourier space for two algebraic subsystems can be analyzed. Eigenvalues and eigenfunctions can be explicitly computed, and the energy method is also applied to treat the regularity-loss subsystem. Our main contribution is to find out the simple linear approximation system in order to characterize the more complex Green's functions. Indeed, we find that the linear approximation system are diffusive equations for each component, and hence make a mathematical justification of the Darcy's law in the context of the damped Euler-Maxwell system at the linear level. In a precise way, we can prove in the perturbation framework that the nonlinear damped Euler-Maxwell system converges in large time to the diffusion waves with the time rates much faster than the decay rates of waves themselves. The proof of the results is based on the Fourier energy method for the linearized system and the bootstrap argument for the nonlinear system. The topic of Item 4 is on the time-asymptotic stability of rarefaction waves. As it is hard to treat the case of appearance of the magnetic field, we start from the situation where the self-consistent force satisfies the Poisson equation. In the mean time, we would also investigate the collisional kinetic equation in the kinetic framework. Therefore, we mainly focus on the construction of the rarefaction wave and its asymptotic stability for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Poisson system and Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system. In fact, by the macro-micro decomposition, the first-order fluid approximation system of the VPB system is just the NSP system. For the construction of rarefaction, we make use of the quasi-neutral assumption to get an algebraic relation of the density and potential function, and plug it back to the fluid system so as to obtain the quasi-neutral Euler system when the viscosity is ignored. This gives us a way to construct the time-asymptotic smooth rarefaction wave. For the study of stability, we use the standard energy approach but make much extra efforts to treat the difficulty from the effect of the self-consistent force on the viscous fluid system. Here, the most key point is to construct the zero-order energy functional and also capture the dissipation of the electric field in the case when the large-time behavior of the potential function is non-trivial in the sense that it connects two distinct constant states at two ending far fields.

400912.label: Major findings and research outcome
400912.value: 1. We studied the decay structure of two hyperbolic relaxation models with regularity-loss, proposed the general conditions to assure the type of regularity-loss, and found out two kinds of energy methods to treat the problem in a general way. See the refereed paper No 2 in Section 8 of Part C. 2. We obtained the Green's functions for the damped two-fluid Euler-Maxwell system around constant states, obtained the approximation of the Green's functions, obtained the rates of convergence of the nonlinear system to diffusion waves, and thus justified the Darcy's law at the linear level in the appearance of the electric and magnetic fields. See the refereed paper No 3. 3. We made a construction of rarefaction waves and gave a proof of their asymptotic stability for the Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations for the fluid plasma and the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system for the kinetic plasma in one space dimension. See the refereed papers No 4, No 5, and No 7. Paper No 9 was published in a conference proceeding. 4. As applications of the developed approach, we studied the Cauchy problem on the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation coupled with the compressible Euler equations through the friction force, and obtained the large-time behavior of classical solutions in perturbation framework; see the refereed paper No 1. Besides, we applied the technique of Besov spaces for well-posedness of the partially dissipative hyperbolic system to studying the Boltzmann equation, and found out the new linear dissipative structure in those Besov spaces; see the refereed paper No 8.

400912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400912.value: The first potential further development could be to apply the tools from complex analysis and semigroup theory to study the eigenvalue problem for a general hyperbolic relaxation operator, the second one is to justify the Darcy's law for the nonlinear diffusion wave, another one is to study the stability of rarefaction waves with a non-trivial magnetic field. Those topics are challenging because there seems no existing research work on them in the literature. If the understandings in some simple situation can be gained, we will open a new research project to continue the research on those topics.

400912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400912.value: System of conservation laws with dissipation is a wide research area in partial differential equations, arranging from the classical fluid dynamics to kinetic theory. A dissipative mechanism is often involved in relaxation, viscosity and collision. Many well-known equations, such as damped Euler, Navier-Stokes and Boltzmann, are relevant in this framework. The subject of the project is such system coupled with the Maxwell equations through the lorentz force arising from plasma physics. So far, many difficult and fundamental problems for the plasma fluid equations still remain unsolved. Due to the complex coupling structure of most two-fluid systems, we mainly focus on the study of the dissipative property and large-time behavior of solutions to the Cauchy problem both in an abstract level and for the concrete examples. Our emphasis is on the role that the electromagnetic field plays in the analysis of the global smooth dynamics near constant equilibriums or nontrivial states. An important feature of the problem treated by the project is the regularity-loss of dissipation production functionals.

401112.label: Project Title(Chinese)
401112.value: 具有重叠结构的迭代函数系统的几何分离条件与算术性质

401112.label: Project Objectives
401112.value: It is proposed to study the relation between the existing different separation conditions (for instance, the finite type condition and weak separation condition) for overlapping IFS in the literature, and to study how these separation conditions will affect or determine the arithmetic properties of the IFS. Furthermore, it is proposed to characterize those IFS which satisfy one of these separation conditions. As applications of plan (1), it is proposed to study some problems raised by Erdos et al regarding of the distribution properties of polynomials with bounded integer coefficients.

Furthermore, it is proposed to characterize those IFS which satisfy one of these separation conditions.
As applications of plan (1), it is proposed to study some problems raised by Erdos et al regarding of the distribution properties of polynomials with bounded integer coefficients.

401112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401112.value: 数学上，一个迭代函数系统是指一族（有限）欧氏空间上的压缩映射。通过反复迭代这些映射，我们得到分形集合与分形测度。如果这些压缩映射都是相似映射，所得到的集合与测度被称为是自相似的。 当对应的迭代函数系统满足强分离条件或开集条件， 自相似集合及测度的几何结构与维数已得到深入的研究与理解。当这些分离条件不满足时，我们称迭代函数系统具有重叠结构；此时对应的自相似集合与测度具有相当复杂的结构。在最近二十多年里，数学中的许多领域，包括分形几何，动力系统，数论及概率，都对具有重叠结构的分形集与测度有很大研究兴趣。 在以往文献中，有一些较弱的集合分离条件被引入到具有重叠结构的迭代函数系统的研究。在本项目中，我们将研究这些几何分离条件的相互关系；并研究这些分离条件是如何影响决定迭代函数系统的算术性质。除了在分形几何领域的应用之外，我们会用它来研究一类有界整系数多项式的相关问题。 我们拟研究的这些问题有不同程度的难度。本项研究将会加强对具有重叠结构的分形及有界整系数多项式的进一步理解。

401112.label: Realisation of objectives
401112.value: In this project, we investigate the relationship between several existing different separation conditions for overlapping IFS, and apply the result in the study of some number-theoretic problems, including an Erdos problem on the topological structure of integer polynomials with bounded integer polynomials, and the problem about the asymptotical behavior of partition functions of numeration systems. We also investigate a couple of related questions on the affine embeddings, intersections of Cantor sets and the continuity property of the dimension of self-affine sets, in which the underlying IFSs have overlapping structures. We succeed in establishing the equivalence of the weak separation condition and the finite type condition for one dimensional homogeneous iterated function systems under a mild assumption. Furthermore we are able to characterize all those homogeneous IFS with integral translations satisfying one of these separation condition. The result is based on our study of Bernoulli convolutions and the geometric structure of overlapping IFS. A key point in our analysis is that, using a dynamical approach, we are able to explore the recurrent structure of those local patterns admitting most ``overlapping'' structure. Based on this geometric observation and certain combinatoric arguments, we are able to show that the weak separation condition implies the finite type condition if there are enough overlaps in the iterations. As an application, we resolve the question of Erdos et al on the topological structure of integer polynomials with bounded integer polynomials. We prove that the values of such polynomials at a specific number is dense in the real line if and only if this number is a Pisot number (that is, an algebraic number with all conjugates lying inside of the unit disc). Moreover, we give the first result towards a conjecture of Kormonik about the distribution of the values of polynomials with 0, 1 coefficients at specific value q; that is, we prove that for a class of numbers q between certain interval, the set of those values have certain concentration property and has no uniform gap in the set of these values. Furthermore, we apply the theory of overlapping IFS to the study of asymptotical behavior of partition functions of numeration systems. We prove that the partition function of number systems associated with a Pisot scale has a fixed polynomial increasing exponent. Such exponent is related to certain dimensional property of the corresponding Bernoulli convolutions associated with Pisot numbers. In the project we also initiate the study of affine embedding of fractal sets, and explore its close relation to intersections of fractals. Under the assumption of open set condition, we show that a self-similar set can be smoothly embedded into another one if and only if that it can be affinely embedded into the second one. If there is no affine embeddings, then there is a dimension drop in the intersection of the two self-similar sets. As a by-product, we obtain a non-trivial result towards the Furstenberg’s conjecture on the dimension of intersections of Cantor sets. In the project we have also established the continuity property in dimension for typical self-affine fractal sets. The generating IFSs of this family of fractal sets usually involve heavy overlapping structures. Using some deep results from ergodic theory and dynamical systems, we associate the study of their dimension to the study of the topological pressure for matrix products and manage to prove the continuity of the corresponding pressure. Finally we manage to resolve a folklore conjecture in the community of fractal geometry. Overall we have achieved the major parts (around 75%) of our original objectives. A further understanding of the relations between the different separation conditions of IFSs (for instance, in the high dimensional Euclidean spaces) is expected, and this might be achieved by using the theory of CP chains developed by Furstenberg and Hochman, and we hope to check this possible approach in the further investigation. Our tool of using the theory of IFS to attack number theoretic problems is the high-light part of this project. Hopefully we may continue to sharpen this tool to improve our partial results on the Kormonik's conjecture about the distribution of polynomials with coefficients 0 and 1.

401112.label: Major findings and research outcome
401112.value: In [1], we investigate quantitatively the overlapping structures of a class of IFS on the real satisfying the finite type condition. We succeed to determine the precise value of the Hausdorff dimension of typical fibres of the corresponding attractors. As an application, we obtain some new results on partition functions in number theory. Indeed, we can estimate the typical increasing rate of partition functions generated by a special recurrent sequence generated by a Pisot numbers (the so-called Pisot scales). Part of the main results was obtained and submitted before the starting date of this research proposal, we revised the original version of this paper and added some new results before the paper was accepted on September 13, 2013. In [2], we prove that under mild conditions, one self-similar set can be smoothly embedded into another self-similar set if and only if it can be affinely embedded into the second one; moreover, if this is the case, then the contraction ratios of the generating IFS of the first self-similar set should be logarithmic commensurable to the contraction ratios of the second one. As an interesting application of this rigidity property, we show that there is a dimensional drop for the intersections of Cantor sets, provided that one of them can not be affinely embedded into the other one. This proves a weak version of Furstenberg’s conjecture on the intersections of Cantor sets. In [3], we prove that for every homogeneous self-similar IFS on the real line, if its attractor is an interval, then the weak separation condition is equivalent to the finite type condition. The result can be used to analyze the arithmetic structure of the underlying IFS. As a particular application, we resolve an open question raised by Erdos et al in last 90's regarding the topological property of polynomials with bounded integer coefficients. Part of the results was submitted before the starting date of this research proposal, we revised and improved a lot the paper before it was accepted on Jan 28, 2015. In [4], we prove a longstanding folklore conjecture in the community of fractal geometry, that is, Falconer's dimension formula for typical self-affine sets depends continuously on the linear parts of generating IFSs of those self-affine sets. The main idea is to study the pressure function associated with these linear parts. In [5], we give the first result towards a conjecture of Kormonik on the distribution of polynomials with 0, 1 coefficients.

401112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401112.value: There are several issues deserved to be further developed: (1) To prove or disprove the equivalence of finite type condition and weak separation condition for overlapping homogenous IFS on the real line for which the attractor is not an interval. (2) To make further development on the problems of Erdos and Kormonik on the distribution of values of 0,1-polynomials. (3) To analyse and characterise the IFS satisfying the asymptotically weak separation condition.

401112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401112.value: In mathematics, an iterated function system (IFS) is a finite family of contractive maps in the Euclidean space. By repeatedly applying these maps, one obtains fractal sets and measures. These sets and measures are called self-similar if all these maps are similitudes. Many interesting fractal objects are generated by overlapping IFS. In this project, we study the relationship between different geometric separation conditions for overlapping IFS. Under mild condition, we prove that the weak separation condition and the finite type condition are equivalent for one dimensional IFS. We apply this result to the study of the topological property of a class of integer polynomial and resolved a related problem of Erdos. Furthermore through the study of IFS satisfying the finite type condition, we obtain new results on the partition function in number theory. We also initiate the study of affine embedding and intersections of fractal sets, and prove the continuity of the dimension of typical self-affine fractal sets, which answers a folklore conjecture in the community of fractal geometry.

401212.label: Project Objectives
401212.value: To study the structure of the ground-state wave function of in in one-dimensional XXZ model and Hubbard model. Then using these wavefunction to explore the role of mode fidelity and other related method from the information science in the BKT-like transitions occuring in the ground states of the two models. To study the structural changes in the ground-state modes during a topological phase transitions. We will take the Kitaev honeycomb model as a starting model to explore new methods to describe the topological phases in the model. To explore the intrinsic relation between the fidelity and topological phase transitions, and how the topological nature, such as the non-local order parameter or the Chern number, affects the fidelity or other related methods from the information science in the transitions.

401212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401212.value: Quantum phase transition has been one of the most important research topics in condensed matter physics for almost two decades. For a quantum many-body system, the quantum phase transition occurs as the system's macroscopic properties undergo a qualitative change when the system's parameter, such as external field and interactions, varies across a transition point. In physics, we are familiar to thermal phase transitions. A typical example of the thermal phase transition is the transition among ice, water, and steam. In order to characterize the thermal phase transition, people usually use the free energy, entropy, and other thermodynamic functions to describe significant changes in the system's thermodynamic properties. For years, a well established theory describing continuous phase transition, i.e. the Landau's symmetry-breaking theory, has been widely applied. When the temperature tends to zero, the free energy becomes the ground-state energy, and its derivatives with respect to system's parameter becomes the derivatives of the ground-state energy to the parameter. In Landau's paradigm, the correlation function of local order parameters plays a crucial role Nevertheless, some systems cannot be described in this framework built on the local order parameter. This might be due to the absence of preexistent symmetry in the Hamiltonian, such as systems undergoing topological phase transitions or Beresinskii–Kosterlitz-Thouless(BKT) phase transitions. Since the nineties of last century, the development of quantum information theory has provided us a new analytical approach to study quantum critical phenomena, and hence opened a new angle to understand the phenomena. Applying concepts used in quantum information theory, some unconventional phase transitions, which can not be described by the symmetry-breaking theory, including the BKT transition and topological phase transition, were analyzed and understood with significant progress. These theoretical methods include typicaly the quantum entanglement and fidelity, entropy majorization theorem. Armed with new method, we are going to study the BKT and topological phase transitions from different point of view. 近二十年来，量子相变已成为凝聚态物理中的一个最重要的研究课题之一。在绝对零温下，当一个量子多体系统的参量，比如外场、相互作用，变化至一个临界点时，系统会产生一个定性的改变，这时就发生了量子相变。在物理上，我们对热力学相变比较熟悉。一个典型的例子就是发生在冰、水、水蒸气之间的热力学相变。为了刻画热力学相变，人们通常用自由能、熵或其他热力学量来描述系统热力学性质的巨大变化。多年来，一个用来描述连续相变的理论，即朗道的对称破缺理论，已被广泛应用。当系统的温度变成零的时候，自由能就成了基态能量，自由能对系统参量的导数也成了基态能量对系统参量的导数。在朗道的理论中，序参量的关联函数起在至关重要的作用。然而，由于一些系统并没有相应的对称性，所以不能用建立在序参量基础上的理论来描述。这些系统包括发生KT相变或拓扑相变的系统。 自上世纪九十年代以来，量子信息理论的发展为我们提供了研究量子临界现象的新方法，从而开启了理解量子相变的新的视角。利用量子信息理论中的一些概念，在理解与刻画一些非传统的，不能用对称破缺理论来刻画的相变，包括KT相变和拓扑相变上，取得了重大的进展。这些理论方法，包括量子纠缠，保真度，熵主序理论。本项目的目标就是用这些新的方法，从不同的视角来研究BKT相变和拓扑相变。

401212.label: Realisation of objectives
401212.value: Phase transition is one of the most important ingredient in modern physics, these include not only the models in condensed matter physics and particle physics, but also in some new-emerging fields such as biophysics, active matter (e.g., bird and fish flocking) and related fields. These phase transitions are generally described mathematically using Landau theory of phase transition based on spontaneous symmetry breaking, which has turned out to be extremely success in history. However, this method is insufficient to describe the topological phase transitions which are described by some global topological index. Thus new method thus should be developed. This project attempts to use the fidelity susceptibility approach --- a basic idea proposed by Prof. Shijian Gu and Prof. Haiqin Lin in 2008 --- to study the phase transitions in different quantum systems, including the Ising model, XXZ model, Kitaev model, Hubbard model and other models. The following objectives have been achieved. 1. Phase transitions in the Ising model, XXZ model and Kitaev model have been investigated using fidelity susceptibility approach, which demonstrates the validity of fidelity susceptibility in characterizing the these phase transitions. Notice that the topological phase transitions in the Kitaev model can not be characterized by the Landau’s theory of phase transition based on spontaneous symmetry breaking. The fidelity is based on the overlap between two wave functions, in which the structures of the functions are all included. Thus this new definition provides new horizon to understand the phase transitions in different quantum systems. 2. The idea of fidelity susceptibility has been greatly generalized. We have established direct connection between fidelity susceptibility and spectral function, thus the fidelity susceptibility can be directly measured in future in experiments. Moreover, we also proposed a new idea --- the fidelity spectrum, which provides a new tool to understand the phase transitions in different phase transitions. We illustrate the validity of this new method using the Ising model and Kitaev model. 3. We have studied the spin-orbit coupled Fermi-Hubbard model using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method. The competition between the singlet pairing and the triplet pairing (the later one is induced by the spin-orbit effect, which has been recently realized in ultracold atom systems) can induce an exotic pairing phase in which the Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov (FFLO) phase and Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) phase can coexist in some parameter regime when the spin-orbit coupling strength is not strong enough. This phase can not be accessed using the mean field theory. 4. We have studied the phase diagrams in the extended Fermi-Hubbard model using DMRG method, in which the phase transitions between the supersolid phase, charge and spin density waves, singlet and triplet superconducting phases and the bond-ordered wave using the fidelity susceptibility. Some of the the calculated phases are consistent with the previous literatures which are demonstrated with other complex methods based on Landau theory of phase transition. To conclude fruitful results have been obtained during the supporting of this project.

401212.label: Major findings and research outcome
401212.value: The fidelity susceptibility approach was developed by Prof. Shijian Gu and Prof. Haiqin Lin in 2008. In this project we use this new developed method to characterize the phase transitions including in Ising model, XXZ model, Kitaev model, the extended Fermi-Hubbard model and the spin-orbit coupled Fermi-Hubbard model. The major findings are outlined below. 1. We find that the fidelity susceptibility can provide a new tool to investigate not only the conventional quantum phase transitions in Ising model, XXZ model and extended Fermi-Hubbard model, but can be used to characterize topological phase transitions in Kitaev model. 2. We have established a direct connection between fidelity susceptibility and spectral function, therefore the fidelity susceptibility can be directly measured in experiments in future. 3. We proposed that the fidelity spectrum provides a new tool to characterize the phase transitions in many-body system, and we demonstrate this validity using Ising model and Kitaev model. 4. We investigated the exotic pairings in the spin-orbit coupled Fermi-Hubbard model using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method and we find that in some proper parameter regime the BCS pairing and FFLO pairing can coexist. This exotic pairing is beyond the accessibility of mean field theory. 5. We investigated the full phase diagrams in the extended Fermi-Hubbard model using fidelity susceptibility approach. Some of the calculated phase diagrams are consistent with previous literatures based on Landau theory of phase transition.

401212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401212.value: We have tried our best to study the topological phases in the extended Fermi-Hubbard model and the spin-orbit coupled Fermi-Hubbard model and we fail to find the topological phases due to two basic reasons: 1. In our calculation the total number is conserved, thus we do not have pairing explicitly. 2. We do not have good methods to characterize the topological phases and the corresponding topological indexes. Thus in future the above two difficulties should be overcame to investigate the topological phase transitions in these two models.

401212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401212.value: In history the phase transitions are characterized by order parameters or symmetries in the standard Landay's theory of phase transition. This method bear some limitations, for instance, it can not be used to study the phase transitions in topological phase transitions. In this project, we characterize the phase transitions using the fidelity susceptibility approach, a new method based on overlap between two different ground state wave functions. Since the wave functions in two different phases should be different in the detailed structures, we find a sharp discontinuity across the phase boundary. So the fidelity susceptibility provides new horizon to understand the phase transitions in modern physics. We use this method to characterize different phase transitions to unveil the validity of this method in this project.

401512.label: Project Objectives
401512.value: Formulation of THz-sideband generation in gapped graphene. We will consider bi-layer graphene as the physical system, in which a band gap can be induced and tuned up to 250 meV by an electrical field. The energy band structures and the electric dipole moments (including both interband transitions and intraband acceleration) will be first determined using the tight-binding model. The optical process will be taken as linear response in which a weak infrared or visible light excites an electron-hole pair, which after acceleration by the THz field, will recombine to emit a photon with up- or down-converted frequency. The THz field will be fully taken into account without perturbation approximation by the gauge transformation method. The optical Bloch equations will be employed to incorporate the exciton effect and scattering-induced relaxation and dephasing. Formulation of the quantum trajectory theory for optically created Dirac fermions under strong THz field and study of the relativistic strong-field physics and the geometric phase effects. Under a strong THz field, the optically created electrons and holes in graphene undergo large-amplitude motion along classical paths with quantum fluctuations, until re-collide and recombine with photon emission. The quantum trajectory theory will be developed to capture the essential physics of such processes, not only for an intuitive physical picture to understand the HSG, but also to explore the unique physics of Dirac fermions under strong field (such as the relativistic effect and Berry phases in quantum trajectories). Numerical simulation of HSG and optimization of the HSG efficiency by investigation on the effects of the band structure, the THz field frequency, strength, and polarization, the optical field frequency and polarization, the sample structure, and phase matching. The simulation will be based on realistic experimental conditions, and will be compared with experimental data. Experimental schemes will be derived from the theoretical research.

401512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401512.value: 系统在受到强太赫兹(THz)场驱动时，近红外光可实现光频的上转换或者下转换。由于光频场所产生的载流子受到太赫兹场的加速，光频转换的频率差值是太赫兹场频率的整数倍。与原子在强场驱动条件下的高次谐波产生相似，这类高阶太赫兹边带产生(HSG)属于典型的强场物理现象。它将导致新的信息技术变革，如太比特速率(Tb/s)的光通信和超快成像。项目负责人及其合作者预测了HSG，加州大学圣巴巴拉分校(UCSB)研究小组在半导体系统中观测到了此现象。HSG的相关研究尚处于起步阶段。实现高效HSG的关键在于寻找具有长平均自由程的材料和能获取高能量的光激发载流子。这对于探索在具有能带结构的固态系统内高阶边带产生过程中的新物理也非常重要。 我们将对石墨烯中的HSG进行系统研究。石墨烯是一种卓越的光子与电光的光透明材料，其带隙可通过外电场调控。石墨烯中的HSG具有以下三个独特的性质。一、石墨烯中的电子属于Dirac费米子，这为新的强场物理研究，如HSG过程中的相对论效应与几何相位效应，提供了平台。二、石墨烯中的电子具有高运动速度(约真空光速中的三百分之一)，这使得电子能从太赫兹强驱动场中获得更高的动能(传递给电子的功率等于力乘以速度)。三、石墨烯具有高的迁移率，因此即使在室温下电子也具有长的平均自由程。在本项目中，我们将研究HSG对太赫兹场、光频场与材料参量的依赖关系，探索相对论性强场物理和几何相位现象，并设计能用于光通信与超快成像的太赫兹光调制器。 本项目的研究方法同时涉及理论与实验的专业知识，如光学理论，太赫兹实验与基于石墨烯的器件。为获得最本质的物理图像，我们将运用量子轨迹理论分析HSG。强太赫兹场作用下的电子运动可近似为沿着大振幅经典路径的波包。我们还将利用包含库仑相互作用和散射的光学布洛赫方程数值模拟HSG，并与实验数据相比较。与此同时，基于现有实验条件，我们将进行相关器件的设计与优化。 本项目旨在探索在非传统材料中的强场物理，并为下一代信息技术奠定基础。

401512.label: Realisation of objectives
401512.value: Objective 1: We have formulated a theory suited for THz sideband generation in graphene. In graphene the electron and hole under THz field driving may not return to the same position again. However, we formulated the full quantum theory and discovered that the quantum diffusion of the electron and hole wavepacket would still allow recomibation, which induces a second and broader plateau of sidebands. This result was published in Phys. Rev. B 89, 121202(R) (2014) as a Rapid Communication. We also studied the effect of the excitation energy on the strength and spectrum width of the THz sideband generation [published in a focus issue of New Journal of Physics - Vol 15, 105015 (2013)]. Objective 2: We discovered the geometric phase effect in THz sideband generation in a range of materials including graphene and transition metal dichalgenides. In particular, we found that the diffusion of a wavepackt under the THz field of elliptic polarization can accumulate both a real and an imaginary part in the geometric phase, which induce polarization changes in the THz sideband generation. This result was published in Scientific Reports 5, 12109 (16 July 2015). Objective 3: We have designed a graphene-based device for THz sideband generation and done numerical simulation of THz sideband generation in bi-layer graphene. We discovered that the spectrum width of the THz sidebands in graphene can be 100 times larger than in conventional semiconductors under a THz field of the same strength. This facilitates the possibility of desktop applications of the THz sideband generation. This result was published in Nature Communications 5, 4854 (2014). In collaboration with Prof. Sherwin, we run numerical simulation for THz sideband generations in realistic quantum wells, taking into account phonon scattering at finite temperature. T theoretical results give an excellent account of the experimental observation of high order THz sideband generation at room temperature [published in Physical Review Letters 111, 267402 (2013)].

401512.label: Major findings and research outcome
401512.value: 1. We discovered a second plateau in high order THz sideband genetration due to quantum coherence of electron and hole wavepacket. This reveals a new mechanism for electron-hole re-collision, which enables higher order sideband generations in a broader range of materials. This result was published in Phys. Rev. B 89, 121202(R) (2014) as a Rapid Communication. 2. We discovered that the geometric phase of an electron wavepacket driven along a path in the momentum space can accumulate an imaginary part. The imaginary geometric phase is due to the geometric nature of the quantum diffusion. The effect can be observed in experiments as the elliptic polarization of the THz sideband generation. This adds a new degree of freedom for optical modulation. The result was published in Scientific Reports 5, 12109 (16 July 2015). 3. In numerical simulation, we discovered that the spectrum width of the THz sidebands in bi-layer graphene can be 100 times larger than in conventional semiconductors under a THz field of the same strength. This facilitates the possibility of desktop applications of the THz sideband generation. This result was published in Nature Communications 5, 4854 (2014).

401512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401512.value: In the future, it is possible to use the THz sideband generation to study the Berry curvature of energy band of semiconductors and insulators (topological or non-topological). We are working closely with the experimental partners in UCSB on this aspect.

401512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401512.value: THz sideband generation occurs when a pair of electron and hole is created by a near-infrared photon from a weak laser, driven by a strong THz (1 trillion Hertz) alternative electric field, and then recombine to emit a photon frequencies separated from the original laser frequency by even multiples of the THz frequency. In the time-domain, the electron and the hole re-collide with each other every half period of the THz field as the field alternates its direction, inducing a sequence of light emission separated by half periods of the THz field. Such high-frequency modulation of light may be of important applications in high bit rate optical communications. We studied the THz sideband generation in graphene. We discovered that the THz sisdeband generation in graphene is 100 times broader than in conventional semiconductors. This greatly reduces the difficulty of desktop applications of THz sideband generation. We also discovered that the geometric phase has an imginary part, which induces elliptic polarization of the THz sideband generation. This adds a new degree of freedom for optical modulation. The results produced from this project reveals new mechanisms in THz sideband generation and may lead to new applications in ultrafast optical communications.

401712.label: Project Title(Chinese)
401712.value: 解釋函數的邊界性質及分形上的分析

401712.label: Project Objectives
401712.value: In previous investigations, we concentrated on the topological aspect of the Cantor boundary behavior. Our new initiative is to study the measure-theoretic and dimension questions related to this boundary behavior. In view of the current development of conformal fractals, we will explore different approaches to investigate the CBB, e.g., to use the Loewner chain and the Koebe n-root transform. The research will lead to different aspects and will be useful for other specific problems in complex analysis and harmonic analysis. Apart from the mapping property on the boundaries, we will continue our original investigation of the Cauchy transform on self-similar sets from the function-theoretic point of view. The associated function spaces, boundary value problems, and harmonic measures will be considered. Besides the Sierpinski gasket, we will also consider the Cauchy transform on some other self-similar sets, such as the snowflake domain.

401712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401712.value: 最近十年，我們看到在分形分析上有很多重要的發展．最引人注目的是應用共形影射及隨機分析建立起來的隨機Loewner方程理論(SLE)，它用來解決布郎運動上有名的分數維數猜測，及數學物理上一些有關共形不變過程的問題． 在這個申請書，我們會研究解釋函數上的幾何及函數理論．我們集中在這類型函數上一種特殊邊界性質，稱之為Cantor邊界性質．它包括了Weierstrass函數，缺項函數，及自相似集上的哥西變換．對有關影射的分數維數，我們會借助SLE上一些啟發，來考慮哥西變換．另外，我們會在Sierpinski墊上及自相似集上，發展一套解析函數的邊界理論． 我們這個研究，需要充分掌握分形幾何，複分析，調和分析及概率論上的知識．由於這方向的研究尚處於萌芽階段，很多問題有待解決．這些問題，有不同程度的困難，有不小是可以用來培養研究生的．申請人在指導研究生及博士後，有豐富的經驗．他會帶領他們，在這個問題上共同探討．

401712.label: Realisation of objectives
401712.value: The Cauchy transform plays a central role in classical complex analysis, harmonic analysis, and geometric measure theory. In the analysis of fractals, one of the interesting topics is to study the Cauchy transform of the self-similar measures, and the associated singular integral theory. In this project, we gave a detail investigation of the Cauchy transform $F$ of the canonical Hausdorff $mu$ on a self-similar set $K$. If we consider the Laurent series expansion of $F$, we see that $F$ behaves nicely away from $K$. For this observation, we carried out a rather complete study of the the univalence and the starlikeness property of $F$ for this situation. On the other hand, we also obtained a Taylor-type series expansion at $K$, which contains a term of fractional power; this shows the fractal behavior of $F$ near $K$. More specifically, there is a very intricate fractal behavior observed by Strichartz from numerical evidence, and he raised a number of open questions concerning this. We formulated this as the {it Cantor boundary behavior}, and answered some of his questions. The Loewner differential equation was introduced in the 20's for the study of univalence functions, and it was the main tool to solve the Bieberbach conjecture in the 80's. The importance of the equation emerged again recently in the study of stochastic Loewner evolution (SLE). In this project we investigated the relationship of the slit curves on the upper half plane and the associated driving function of the slit. Specifically, we considered the tangential slits which were left out in the previous studies. We provided a more complete result of the two fundamental notions in the theory. In another direction, we also consider the problem whether a self-measure $mu$ is a {it spectral measure}, that is, whether the $L^2(mu)$ has an exponential orthonormal basis. This allows us to have an analog of Fourier series expansion on functions on fractals. For this, we obtained some sharp results for the self-similar measures on the Sierpinski gasket.
