401712.label: Major findings and research outcome
401712.value: 1. Our major results were on the Cauchy transform $F$ of the self-similar measures $mu$. In [4], we considered the special class of $mu$ that are uniformly distributed on the self-similar sets $K$, with the convex hull of $K$ a regular polygon. For $F$ away from $K$, it has nice geometric and analytic properties, and we proved the univalence, starlikeness and convexity of $F$. In particular, we found the exact radii of starlikeness of the $F$. On the other hand, in [5], we concentrated our attention on the behavior of $F$ near $K$. For the Sierpinski gasket $K$, we proved a Taylor-like series expansion of $F$ at the dyadic point on $K$, and showed that $F$ has the Cantor boundary behavior. This settled the "Cantor set conjecture" of Strichartz. Also, we obtained other related geometric and fractal properties of the Cauchy transform $F$ such as the dimension of the graphs of the real and imaginary parts and the area of the Riemann region in the image. 2. On the Loewner equation, we investigated the tangential slit $gamma (t)$ that satisfies certain H"older exponent on the upper half plane [3]. Our main result is to give the exact asymptotic behavior of the driving function $lambda (t)$ in terms of the H"older exponent. We also extended this to a general type of tangential slits, and gave an estimation of the growth of $lambda (t)$. 3. A measure $mu$ on $R^n$ is called a spectral measure if $L^2(mu)$ has an exponential orthonormal basis. In [2], we considered the Sierpinski-type self-similar measure $mu_rho$ with a parameter $00$. There is an extension of a well-known result of such characterization for Bernoulli convolution on $R$. 4. In [1] and [5], we studied another type of questions. We asked for a given self-similar set $K$, what is the class of iterated function systems (IFS) that generates the same $K$. We first studied this in [1] under a strong separation condition, then in [5] we improved the condition to be the open set condition. Denoting the family of all such IFS by $F_K$, we showed that $F_K$ is finitely generated if (i) $K$ is totally disconnected, or (ii) the convex hull $Co(K)$ is a polytope, and there exists a line pass through a vertex of $Co(K)$, such that the intersection is a totally disconnected infinite set.

401712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401712.value: Our consideration of the Cauchy transform $F$ is very much concern with the fractal behavior of $F$ and the image of $F(K)$; it is with respect to a single object. A challenging attempt is to consider the functional analytic aspect of the Cauchy transform of function spaces. This is closed connection with the Calderon-Zygmund type singular integral theory on fractal sets, and has attracted a lot of attention recently. The Cauchy transform has also been used to study the analytic capacity of sets, it will be essential in the study of fractals. The (real) Weierstrass function has fascinating fractal property, and has been studied thoroughly. On the other hand its complex counterpart is largely unknown. In connection with the Cantor boundary behavior, we have some initial study of the complex Weierstrass function $f$ on the unit disk $D$, we studied the dimension of the image curve $f(partial D)$, and were able to find the dimension of $f(partial D)$ if we randomize the phase angle of $f$. The challenge problem now is to prove this in the deterministic situation, which might involve some new techniques on the self-similarity under an analytic mapping.

401712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401712.value: From the geometric point of view, it is important to understand how a mapping transforms a set in the domain into the range (the image). For an analytic function on the plane, the image behaves very nicely away from the boundary of the domain, for example the map preserves angles, it maps a circle to a circle; also there is a Riemann mapping theorem to describe the topological behavior of the relation of the domain and the range. However at the boundary, these nice behaviors break down, and the image can become very erratic. In this project, the analytic functions under consideration are the Cauchy transform of the self-similar measure. Because of the self-similar property, we can handle the irregularity of the images of the boundaries in a more systematic way. The Loewner equation we investigated is another topic that deals with the boundary of univalent functions.

401812.value: 超強耦合的拉比模型的量子態研究

401812.label: Project Objectives
401812.value: Characterize the energy spectra and the structures of energy eigenstates of various qubit-oscillator models. In particular determine the selection rules of state transitions as a function of coupling strengths. 401812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401812.value: The Rabi model is a fundamental model describing the quantum physics of a two-level atom interacting with a quantized single-mode electromagnetic field. Such a model plays a central role in quantum optics and it provides an important basis for applications in quantum computation and quantum communication. We propose a theoretical research to investigate the Rabi model in the ultrastrong coupling regime. In this regime, the strongly interacting atom and photons exhibit rich quantum state structures and dynamics. In particular, because the Rabi oscillation frequency can be comparable to the field frequency, the model enables us to explore novel effects in high-speed quantum evolution. We will analyze the energy states and examine the dynamical response of the driven systems. Our focus is placed on strategies to manipulate quantum states by external fields. We will also investigate the output coupling and explore possible generalizations so that three-level configurations can be included. Our research is expected to bring a better understanding of quantum control in the ultrastrong coupling regime, which is important not only for fundamental physics of light-matter interaction, but also for the development of ultra-fast quantum devices relying on ultrastrong coupling. 拉比模型是一個描述一個兩能級的原子與單一的模式電磁場相互作用的基本模型。這模型在量子計算和量子通信起著核心的角色。我們提出對拉比模型的理論研究，用意探討在超強耦合作用的量子物理。在這模型中，強相互作用的原子和光子表現出豐富的量子態結構和動態行為。我們將分析這模型的能量本徵狀態，並檢查在驅動系統中的動態響應。我們的重點是放在操縱量子態的外場以及輸出耦合。我們也將探討可能的概括，使三能級原子模型可以包括在內。對超強耦合機制，這研究將帶來更好的了解，不僅是光與物質的基本物理，同時也為開發超快速量子裝置鋪路。

401812.label: Realisation of objectives
401812.value: We have realized the three project objectives as follows: For the objective (1), by calculating numerically the energy spectra and eigenvectors of the Rabi model as a function of coupling strengths, we have determined the transition matrix elements associated with two driving configurations: (i) Driving of the spin, and (ii) Driving the boson (cavity) mode. We have examined the selection rules and how these transition matrix elements depend on the coupling strengths. Our main discovery is that the counter rotating terms, which are important in the ultrastrong regime, can cause new transitions that are not possible under the rotating wave approximation. In other words, we have identified new transition matrix elements that exist only in the ultrastrong regime. The analysis was carried out by Kelvin Lee, a graduate student, and the detail results have been written in his M. Phil. Thesis in the August of 2014. For the objective (2), we have determined the dynamical responses of the Rabi model under various driving conditions. In the ultrastrong-coupling regime, the most interesting feature is the quantum dynamics due to counter rotating terms. Physically these counter-rotating terms describe transitions due to emission and absorption of virtual photons. We have developed interaction schemes to reveal the dynamical effects of virtual transitions (for details see the main finding section). Our interaction schemes are based on the mechanism that virtual transitions can be turned into real transitions, i.e. emission of real photons, by modulating the system at certain resonance frequencies. The modulation can be realized by applying external fields on the atom or the cavity. Apart from using external fields, we have also discovered the possibility of using adiabatic passage to trigger the virtual-to-real transitions. This is achieved by exploiting the avoided crossings of energy levels of the Rabi-model. For the objective (3), we have formulated master equations for systems in the ultrastrong coupling regime in order to investigate the effects of damping. Our approach is based on Hartmann’s previous work, in which the Lindblad operators are constructed corresponding to transitions between eigenvectors of the Rabi Hamiltonian, and this is important to obtained transmission of real photons from the cavity. We have applied such a master equation to our interaction schemes so that quantum statistics of photons emitted can be extracted. However, owing to the difficulties of calculating higher order correlation functions, our study have been limited to equal-time correlation functions.

401812.label: Major findings and research outcome
401812.value: Our findings have been published in 5 papers in Physical Review A: (a) We have determined approximately analytically the ground state of a generalized Rabi model formed by two identical qubits interacting with a common oscillator mode [ PRA 88, 015802 (2013)]. This is achieved by using a variational method and a transformation method, and both methods are shown to approximate the ground state accurately for a range of coupling strengths in the ultrastrong-coupling regime. In addition, we characterize how the two qubits are entangled as a function of interaction strength. (b) We have found an interaction scheme to achieve vacuum Rabi oscillation induced by virtual photons [ PRA 87, 045804 (2013)]. We show that, with the aid of an external driving field, virtual photons provide a transition matrix element that enables the atom to evolve coherently and reversibly to an auxiliary level accompanied by the emission of a real photon. This oscillation served as a signature of virtual photons. (c)We have developed a type of Raman interaction in a cavity-atom system in which the intermediate states are dressed by the vacuum field in the ultrastrong-coupling regime [PRA 89, 033827 (2014)]. By applying a pump field and a Stokes field, we show how virtual photons in the intermediate states can be converted into real photons with a high probability. Our study shows that the atom-cavity system in the ultrastrong coupling regime somehow plays the role of a nonlinear optical medium, and the interesting source of nonlinearity comes from the virtual photons in the intermediate states. (d) We developed a strategy to enhance counter-rotating interactions [PRA 91, 023806 (2015)]. By repeatedly applying phase kicks to the system with a suitable time separation between successive kicks, we can show that strongly enhance a certain virtual transition for systems with an interaction strength far below the ultrastrong coupling regime. (e) We investigate theoretically the quantum Rabi model when the frequency of the cavity field is near one-third of the atomic transition frequency [PRA 92, 023842 (2015)] . We show that there exists a resonant three-photon coupling via intermediate states connected by counter-rotating processes. We derive an effective Hamiltonian of the three-photon coupling, which determines the magnitude of the energy splitting and the position of the resonance analytically. In addition, we present a scheme of three-photon generation based on adiabatic passage across the resonance.

401812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401812.value: Our study has indicated that there is a rich variety of quantum transitions enabled by counter-rotating terms, and such interaction terms are significant in the ultrastrong coupling regime. In particular, an ultra-strongly dressed qubit in a cavity can have interesting non-linear optical processes. Therefore a further investigation could explore the possibility of exploiting such transitions for quantum control of qubits and also for fundamental study of the role of virtual photons in quantum dynamics. Another direction is the extension of the Rabi model to multi-mode systems. With the similar strategies of using external fields, which are developed in this research, one could enhance the effects of counter-rotating interaction in systems with more than one cavity modes or multiple-atoms. The coupled cavity array configurations, which is of considerable research interest currently in the field of circuit QED, can also be explored.

401812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401812.value: In this research project we have studied theoretically the interaction between light and matter in the regime where the interaction strength per photon is much stronger than that typically appears in Nature. Such an ultrastrong coupling has been achieved by experimentalists in specially designed setups. Our work is to explore the physical consequences of ultrastrong coupling. Through extensive model calculations, we have determined quantum properties of an atom ultrastrongly interacting with a single-mode electromagnetic fields. In addition, we have learned how such a system would behave if there is an external driving field acting on it. Our study reveals the important features of virtual photons bounded by the atom, and how these virtual photons would enable novel quantum transitions that cannot happen in the usual weak coupling regime. Based on the knowledge we learned in this project, we have a better understanding of light-matter interactions, and may motivate further development of interaction schemes to achieve quantum control of related systems.

402012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402012.value: Mirror Symmetry conjecture was originated in the study of String theory in Physics. Mathematically speaking, this is a highly nontrivial identification between two different kinds of Geometry, namely Symplectic Geometry and Complex Geometry. The conjecture was originally stated for pairs of Calabi-Yau manifolds and it has been generalized to other spaces and LG models. Strominger-Yau-Zaslow proposed an explanation of the Mirror Symmetry in terms of a fiberwise Fourier-Mukai type transformation. In this proposal, the PI plans to continue to use the SYZ construction to obtain more general mirror manifolds and analyse the corresponding mirror maps. To achieve this, the PI will further develop methods to compute FOOO open Gromov-Witten invariants. The PI also plans to further study the SYZ geometric Fourier transformation. In particular he plans to give a geometric explanation of the appearance of holomorphic disks in the quantum product of Floer cohomology via convolution in the space of fiberwise minimal paths under the Fourier transformation of differential forms on the mirror manifolds. 鏡對稱猜想是從物理學弦理論中引入。數學以言,它是辛幾何和複幾何的一種非一般的對等關係。 這個猜想已從CY空間推廣至其他空間及LG模型上。Strominger-Yau-Zaslow 提出用Fourier-Mukai 來解釋鏡對稱。 在此方案,PI計劃用SYZ建構來構造更多鏡空間及分析鏡函數。PI會發展新方法來計算FOOO開GW不變量。 PI亦會研究SYZ幾何FOURIER變換。譬如用Fourier變換於垂直方向極小線空間上的微分形式的旋積乘法來解釋在FLOER同倫群上量子乘積中全純盤的出現。

402012.label: Realisation of objectives
402012.value: All these objectives have been achieved. SYZ transformation has been used in the semiflat case to construct mirror manifolds, which uses fiberwise geodesic loop spaces. Twisted differential forms are studied here using these loop spaces, thus producing the correct mirror. SYZ transformations was studied to relate complex geometry and symplectic geometry between mirror manifolds. This includes (i) the mirror of elliptic fibrations as twin Lagrangian fibration and (ii) the mirror of coisotropic A-branes as non-generic complex cycles. The fiberwise loops space construction gave a good geometric explanation of quantum corrections via the SYZ perspective.

402012.value: (1) Generalized Witten's Morse theory to incorporate higher products in A_infinity structure and proved the Fukaya conjecture as the semi-classical limit of these structures is exactly the Morse category. This can also be treated as a special case of SYZ transformation with corrections in the semi-flat setting. (2) Further developed the above techniques and described scattering diagram in symplectic geometry, which is the mirror of corresponding scattering diagram in B-model as studied by Kontsevich-Soibelman, Gross-Siebert. (3) Describe the SYZ transformation between elliptic CY manifolds and mirror CY manifolds with twin Lagrangian fibrations. (4) Construct the SYZ transformation of coisotropic A-branes using the fiberwise Nahm transformations for family twisted Dirac operators in the semiflat setting.

402212.label: Project Objectives
402212.value: To design and synthesize multifunctional MSN for targeted delivery of phthalocyanine-based photosensitizers and doxorubicin, and controlled release of the latter. Firstly, phthalocyanines will be linked to doxorubicin through an acid-labile hydrazone linker. These conjugates will then be anchored to the nanochannels of a range of MSN frameworks prepared by a sol-gel method. The outer surface of the MSN will then be grafted with folate groups to target the folate receptors overexpressed in tumor cells. To study the structural properties, including the morphology, surface area, and pore size of these MSN by transmission electron microscopy and nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherm analysis. The loading of the phthalocyanine-doxorubicin conjugates inside the MSN will also be determined by electronic absorption spectroscopy. To study the electronic absorption and photophysical properties of the free and encapsulated phthalocyanine-doxorubicin conjugates, as well as their stability under different conditions (e.g. light and solvent). The rate of release of doxorubicin from the MSN will also be investigated under different pH environments. To examine and compare the dark and photo-cytotoxicity, cellular uptake, and subcellular localization of these MSN and the non-encapsulated phthalocyanine-doxorubicin conjugates by using cancer cells with different levels of folate receptor expression. The release of doxorubicin inside the cells will also be monitored by real-time confocal microscopy.

402212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402212.value: Combination therapy involves the use of two or more treatment modalities or drugs together. It has shown higher therapeutic efficacy when compared with the individual therapeutic methods, particularly in suppressing drug resistance and preventing disease recurrence. Recently, combined chemotherapy and photodynamic therapy (PDT) has received considerable attention as a promising way to treat cancer. PDT utilizes the combined action of a photosensitizer, light, and molecular oxygen to generate reactive oxygen species to eradicate tumor cells. It is generally non-invasive and can tolerate repeated doses. The cytotoxic effect can be induced specifically at the malignant site through precise delivery of the light. In chemotherapy, targeted delivery of anticancer drugs remains as a major challenge. Functional nanoparticles have found to be excellent carriers which can prolong the half-life of the drugs, improve their water solubility, reduce the immunogenicity, and enhance their localization at the tumor site by either passive or active targeting. To further reduce the toxic side effects of the drugs, it is desirable that they can be released in a controlled manner. As a result, development of nanocarriers that can deliver anticancer drugs specifically to the tumor site and control their release through interactions with some tumor-associated stimuli is of great importance. The aim of this project is to develop multifunctional nanocarriers based on mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSN) for photosensitizers and anticancer drugs with a view to achieving synergistic cytotoxic effects. We plan to prepare a series of multifunctional MSN which encapsulate conjugates of pyropheophorbide a (Pyro) and doxorubicin linked with an acid-labile hydrazone bond. The outer surface of the MSN will also be decorated with folate groups to target the folate receptors overexpressed in tumor cells. On the basis that the extracellular region of solid tumors and some intracellular compartments are acidic, the hydrazone linkage is expected to be cleaved favorably in these regions to release the doxorubicin. Upon irradiation, the Pyro moiety, which is still covalently linked to MSN, will trigger the formation of singlet oxygen, which also causes cellular and tissue damage. Hence, the resulting multifunctional MSN can offer several levels of control of the drug specificity and afford synergistic anticancer effects. 402212.label: Realisation of objectives
402212.value: The first objective of this project is to design and synthesize multifunctional mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) for targeted delivery of phthalocyanine-based photosensitizers and doxorubicin (Dox), and controlled release of the latter. To kick start of this project, we prepared a conjugate of zinc(II) phthalocyanine (ZnPc) and Dox linked with an acid-cleavable hydrazone linker. Having an appended azido group, this ZnPc-Dox conjugate was then anchored to the nanochannels of an alkyne-modified MSN system via copper(I)-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition reaction to afford ZnPc-Dox@MSN. For comparison, we also prepared the MSN system encapsulated only with ZnPc. However, as the ZnPc loadings of two MSN systems were not the same, the cytotoxic effects of ZnPc and Dox could not be differentiated. To circumvent this problem, we prepared an analogous system by immobilizing a hydrazine-substituted ZnPc to the MSNs, followed by condensation with Dox. These sequentially formed systems, labeled as ZnPc*@MSN and ZnPc-Dox*@MSN, respectively, should have the same ZnPc loading so that the additional cytotoxicity induced by Dox could be revealed. It was found that Dox could be released in a controllable manner upon changing the pH of the environment. To enhance the biocompatibility and tumor-targeting property of these MSNs, attempts were made to graft a layer of polyethylene glycol (PEG) on the surface of ZnPc-Dox@MSN followed by conjugation with folic acid. However, IR spectroscopic analysis could not show the vibrational bands due to PEG, and it seems that the treatments could not lead to the surface-modified analogue. We then used another batch of MSNs encapsulated with a boron dipyrromethene-based photosensitizer and grafted folic acid directly on their surface. After several attempts, we still could not observe the characteristic peaks of folic acid in the IR spectra of the resulting nanoparticles, though the zeta-potential was changed slightly when compared with the non-coated counterpart. To reveal further if the surface of these nanoparticles had been modified with folic acid, we performed an in vitro competitive assay. Unfortunately, it was found that the cellular uptake was not affected by co-incubation with folic acid, which suggested that folate conjugation was not successful. Therefore, we did not attempt further the surface modification with folic acid, and changed to other targeting approaches. We then shifted the focus to two other MSN-based photosensitizing systems of which their photoactivities could be triggered by tumor-associated stimuli. In the first system, a 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonated ZnPc and Dox were immobilized through amidation to the mesopores of MSNs via an oligoethylene glycol chain and a singlet-oxygen-sensitive anthracene linker, respectively. It was hypothesized that upon irradiation and interaction with glutathione (GSH), which is often upregulated in tumor cells, the initially quenched ZnPc would be activated by removing the 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonate group, and the singlet oxygen produced would cleave the anthracene linker to release the Dox. Therefore, it served as a potential GSH- and light-activated system for controlled drug release and combined photodynamic and chemotherapy. Apart from this system, we also prepared an acid-cleavable acetal-linked ZnPc dimer and conjugated it to MSNs via click chemistry. These dimeric ZnPc moieties were significantly self-quenched due to the close proximity of the phthalocyanine units inside the mesopores, and could be activated upon acidic treatment or internalization, resulting in enhanced fluorescence emission, singlet oxygen generation, and photocytotoxicity. The activation of this system was also demonstrated in tumor-bearing nude mice. Hence, we have prepared several multifunctional MSN systems for controlled drug release and therapy. Even though we could not graft the MSNs with folic acid, we employed the activation strategy to address the issue of tumor selectivity, which in fact is of much current interest. After preparing these MSNs, their structural properties, including the morphology and size, were examined by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and dynamic light scattering (DLS) methods. As the MSN hosts were prepared by a similar method as described previously where the surface area and pore size of the MSNs had been reported, we did not examine these structural aspects. The electronic absorption and fluorescence properties of all these nanoparticles in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) and aqueous media were also investigated and compared with those of the non-encapsulated guest molecules. All these studies could shed light on the aggregation behavior of the nanoparticles as well as the dyes inside the MSNs. By making reference to the molar absorptivity of the Q band of the encapsulated ZnPc in DMF, the concentration of ZnPc in a known concentration of these nanoparticles in DMF could be determined, from which the loading of phthalocyanine was calculated. For the Dox-containing systems, the release of Dox was monitored by the reduced Forster resonance energy transfer (FRET) from the excited Dox to ZnPc, and the increase in Dox’s fluorescence, from which the loading of Dox was also determined. The singlet oxygen generation efficiencies of all these MSN systems were also studied by a steady-state method using 1,3-diphenylisobenzofuran (DPBF) as a singlet oxygen scavenger. Apart from these studies, we also examined the stability of these MSN systems under different conditions by monitoring their spectral properties. The cleavage kinetics and rates of drug release triggered by acid or GSH were studied systematically. Hence, the second and third objectives have been fully addressed. Finally, the in vitro properties of all these multifunctional MSNs were studied in detail. Since these nanoparticles do not have folate conjugation, we just used two general human cancer cell lines, namely HepG2 hepatocarcinoma and HT29 colon adenocarcinoma cells for the studies. For the hydrazone-linked ZnPc-Dox systems, the high cellular uptake of the nanoparticles was demonstrated by the strong intracellular fluorescence of the internalized ZnPc in HepG2 cells as observed by confocal microscopy. The co-appearance of the Dox’s fluorescence also indicated that the hydrazone linker was cleaved inside the acidic compartments of the cells. Their dark and photocytotoxicities were also evaluated at different drug doses and light doses. The photocytotoxic effect of ZnPc and the chemocytotoxic effect of the released Dox were examined using combination index to reveal whether they worked in a synergistic manner. For the GSH-responsive ZnPc-Dox system, the cellular uptake was studied by confocal microscopy and flow cytometry. Its dark and photocytotoxicities were also investigated by MTT assay. Unfortunately, the combined cytotoxic effects of ZnPc and Dox could not be demonstrated, probably due to the low Dox loading in the MSNs and the low cytotoxicity of the modified Dox fragment. Similar in vitro studies were also performed for the acid-cleavable dimeric ZnPc system and the non-cleavable analogue as the negative control using HT29 cells. In addition, the subcellular localization property and in vivo response of these systems in term of fluorescence restoration in tumor-bearing nude mice were also investigated. With all these studies and results, the last objective of this project is deemed to be completed.

402212.label: Major findings and research outcome
402212.value: With a view to developing a controlled drug release platform for dual photodynamic and chemo-therapy, we synthesized a zinc(II) phthalocyanine (ZnPc) conjugated with doxorubicin (Dox) via an acid-cleavable hydrazone linker, and then anchored it to the nanochannels of mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) (ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, submitted). To facilitate the study of the dual cytotoxic effects, an analogous system was also prepared by sequentially introducing the ZnPc and Dox to the MSNs so that the ZnPc loading could be fixed. The release of Dox under acidic conditions was studied in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) by monitoring the reduce in the Forster resonance energy transfer from the excited Dox to the ZnPc and the increase in fluorescence of the Dox released. After internalization into HepG2 cells, these nanoparticles showed the fluorescence of both ZnPc and Dox, which suggested that the acidic intracellular environment had triggered the release of Dox by cleaving the hydrazone linker. With a certain drug dose, the photocytotoxic effect of ZnPc and the chemocytotoxic effect of Dox worked in a synergistic manner as proved by a less-than-unity combination index. A related system was also prepared in which a 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonated ZnPc and Dox were immobilized to MSNs via an oligoethylene glycol chain and a singlet-oxygen-cleavable anthracene linker, respectively (manuscript in preparation). It was found that glutathione (GSH) in mM range could enhance the fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation by ZnPc by removing the 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonate quencher, and trigger the release of Dox by cleaving the anthracene linker. While GSH-promoted intracellular fluorescence could be seen, the dual cytotoxic effects of ZnPc and Dox could not be demonstrated, which was likely due to the low Dox loading in the MSNs and the low cytotoxicity of the modified Dox fragment. Apart from these systems, an acid-cleavable acetal-linked ZnPc dimer was prepared and conjugated to MSNs (ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, submitted). For comparison, an amine-linked analogue was also prepared as a non-acid-cleavable counterpart. These dimeric phthalocyanines were significantly self-quenched due to their close proximity inside the mesopores. Under acidic conditions, the cleavable system was activated in terms of fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen production. After internalization into HT29 cells, it exhibited much higher intracellular fluorescence and photocytotoxicity compared to the non-cleavable counterpart. The activation of this system was also demonstrated in tumor-bearing nude mice. The intratumoral fluorescence intensity increased gradually over 24 h, while for the non-cleavable counterpart the fluorescence remained very weak.

402212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402212.value: Owing to the many desirable features, mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) have received considerable attention as versatile nanocarriers for pharmaceutical application. This study has demonstrated that MSNs can be used as an excellent platform for carrying activatable photosensitizers and for controlled release of chemotherapeutic agents. The resulting nanoparticles are potentially useful for combined photodynamic therapy and controlled chemotherapy. To enhance the therapeutic efficacy, more advanced photosensitizers can be used, such as those which can be activated only in the presence of two or even more tumor-associated stimuli. This approach can confine the cytotoxic effect mainly at the tumor. A few dual activatable photosensitizers have recently been reported, but to our knowledge, none of them have been encapsulated into MSNs. For the acetal-linked dimeric phthalocyanine system which exhibited an excellent self-quenching effect, the linker can be replaced with the substrates of tumor-associated proteases so that the activation can be more tumor specific. To enhance the chemocytotoxicity of the doxorubicin moieties released upon activation, the system can be redesigned so that the pendant side chain of doxorubicin can be removed. It is believed that this extra substituent may affect the binding of doxorubicin with DNA and lower its cytotoxicity.

402212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402212.value: As a promising and clinically approved treatment modality, photodynamic therapy (PDT) has received considerable attention. While it can be a stand-alone anticancer modality, combining PDT with other therapeutic methods could induce different cytotoxic pathways, resulting in enhanced therapeutic efficacy. The recent advances in nanotechnology enable the incorporation of various pharmaceutical components in a single nanoplatform, which can facilitate the development of multifunctional therapeutic agents. In this project, we have prepared and characterized a series of novel mesoporous silica nanoparticles which are covalently conjugated to phthalocyanine-based photosensitizers and/or the chemotherapeutic drug doxorubicin in the nanochannels. The photoactivities of the phthalocyanines can be activated by acid or glutathione, which mimic the acidic and reducing tumor microenvironment. Doxorubicin can be released in a controllable manner upon interaction with acid or light with appropriate wavelength. These nanoparticles can be internalized readily into cancer cells as shown by the bright fluorescence of the entrapped dyes. The photocytotoxic phthalocyanines and the chemocytotoxic doxorubicin can kill the cells effectively, and under a certain drug dose, these two cytotoxic effects work in a synergistic fashion. The stimulus-responsive and controlled release properties of these nanoparticles can prevent undesired harmful effects and are therefore advantageous characteristics of advanced therapeutic agents.

402412.label: Project Objectives
402412.value: To synthesize two groups of heptagon-embedded polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon molecules, which not only are of theoretical interests due to the negative curvature but also have unique potentials in materials science. To characterize the electronic structure, flexibility and molecular packing of these molecules, and to discover the relationship between these properties and negative curvature of conjugated molecules. To study the liquid crystals of the proposed molecules, and to find how the self-assembly and phase-transition properties are related to the negatively curved aromatic cores. To fabricate and characterize organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) with the proposed molecules, and to elucidate the fundamental links between chemical structures, molecular assemblies and electrical properties for these proposed materials.

402412.value: 向平坦的稠環芳烴分子中引入七元環就會產生負曲率。這些嵌入七元環的稠環芳烴分子不僅具有理論研究價值，而且在材料科學中具有獨特的應用潛力。比如，它們就可以作為片斷或模型化合物，來研究麵包圈型碳納米管等具有負曲率的石墨碳結構。它們還可能成為有機半導體材料，具有不同尋常π-π相互作用和前所未有的性質。 為探索這一類很少被研究的彎曲的共軛分子，我們設計了兩種形如馬鞍的嵌入七元環的稠環芳烴分子。這一設計的基礎是我們近期利用七元碳環作為結構單元來構築功能分子材料的研究。我們計劃合成這些分子，研究其電子結構、堆砌模式及揉曲性，還將研究其液晶相，並在有機薄膜晶體管中測試其半導體性能。我們為這些分子設計的合成路線已經成功地用於其中一個分子，這預示著該合成路線也將適用於其他分子。 對嵌入七元環的稠環芳烴分子在電子結構、分子組裝及半導體性質等方面的研究，特別是與平坦的稠環芳烴母體分子的對比研究，將帶來關於重要的共軛分子的結構性能關係的有趣發現。在此提出研究的一些分子具有形如馬鞍的芳香核和柔軟的烷基長鏈，因而可能產生液晶相，並帶來傳統的平面盤狀液晶分子所不具備的自組裝和相變性質。 這項研究計劃的成功實施將帶來對電子結構和分子組裝與共軛分子的彎曲狀態的相關性的有趣發現，還有助於開拓新的思路來設計有機半導體和液晶這兩類重要的有機功能材料。

402412.label: Realisation of objectives
402412.value: We have successfully realized all the objectives as detailed below. 1. We synthesized two groups of rationally designed heptagon-embedded polycyclic aromatic arenes, which not only are of theoretical interests but also have unique potentials in materials science. 2. With the two groups of molecules in hand, we characterized their electronic structure, flexibility and molecular packing, and investigated the relationship between these properties and the curvature of these conjugated molecules. 3. We found the saddle-shaped polycyclic arenes with long alkyl substituents could form liquid crystals as proposed, and studied the self-assembly and phase-transition properties of these molecules in the liquid crystals. 4. We fabricated organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) using some of these compounds as organic semiconductors and achieved field effect mobility as high as 0.76 cm2/Vs. We investigated the relationship between chemical structures, molecular assemblies and semiconductor properties in the OTFTs for these materials. By realization of the above objectives, we have developed a new group aromatic saddles and a new group of p-type organic semiconductors that have seven-membered rings as a key building block.

402412.label: Major findings and research outcome
402412.value: In this project, we successfully synthesized two groups of heptagon-embedded polycyclic arenes. The first group includes soluble derivatives of C70H26 and C70H30, two new saddle-shaped polycyclic arenes, which were synthesized by introducing two seven-membered rings into the framework of hexabenzocoronene and subsequent π-extension (Journal of the American Chemical Society, 2015, 137, 3910–3914). On the basis of crystal structures, local aromaticity and non-planarity of individual rings in the saddle-shaped π-backbone were analyzed, and were found to follow Clar's rule in general. As commented by the reviewers, this work has presented "elegant and efficient" synthesis and "beautiful aromatic saddle type molecules". The second group of heptagon-embedded polycyclic arenes include soluble derivatives of dibenzo[d,d']benzo[1,2-a:4,5-a']dicycloheptene and benzo[4,5]cyclohepta[1,2-b]fluorene. It is found that the dibenzo[d,d']benzo[1,2-a:4,5-a']dicycloheptene derivatives have a nearly flat C6-C7-C6-C7-C6 polycyclic framework with a p-quinodimethane core, and exhibit field effect mobility of up to 0.76 cm2/Vs as measured from solution-processed thin film transistors (Angewandte Chemie International Edition, 2014, 53, 6786–6790). Containing linearly fused six-, five-, six-, seven- and six-membered rings (C6-C5-C6-C7-C6), benzo[4,5]cyclohepta[1,2-b]fluorene is an interesting isomer of pentacene with quinoidal, dipolar ionic and diradical resonance forms. Two derivatives of benzo[4,5]cyclohepta[1,2-b]fluorene were experimentally investigated with cyclic voltammetry, electronic absorption spectroscopy and X-ray crystallographic analysis, and theoretically studied by calculating the NICS value, diradical character and dipole moment. One of them behaved as a p-type organic semiconductor in solution-processed thin film transistors with field effect mobility of up to 0.025 cm2/Vs (Chemical Science, 2016, 7, 6176–6181). These results suggest that heptagon-embedded conjugated polycyclic hydrocarbons are promising candidates for organic electronic materials. The above works were both highlighted by Synfacts (2014, 10, 810; 2016, 12, 916), which highlights the most significant current results in synthetic organic chemistry from the primary literature. This project has led to publication of 3 primary research articles in top chemistry journals and 1 book chapter as well as 3 invited presentations at international conferences. Moreover, two PhD students were trained in this project. These outcomes are detailed in Part C.

402412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402412.value: Carbon nanomaterials with negatively curved surfaces can in principle be constructed by including heptagons or larger polygons in the network of hexagons. Examples of negatively curved carbon nanomaterials include toroidal carbon nanotubes and schwarzites, which are periodic three-dimensional structures of sp2 carbon atoms with a surface of negative Gaussian curvature as named after Schwartz, a mathematician studying a related set of topologies. To date negatively curved carbon nanomaterials almost remain imaginary, and practical synthetic approaches to pure periodic schwarzites are still unknown. Bottom-up construction of novel carbon nanomaterials from heptagon-embedded polycyclic arenes brings new challenges to synthetic chemistry, and negatively curved, large heptagon-embedded polycyclic arenes are exciting targets of organic synthesis. Further study on synthesis of new negatively curved polycyclic arenes is in progress in our laboratory.

402412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402412.value: With the financial support from the General Research Fund, we synthesized and investigated two novel groups of polycyclic arenes containing seven-membered rings. The first group of molecules can serve as segments, model compounds and, in principle, synthetic precursors for interesting but still imaginary carbon nanomaterials with negative curvature. The second group of molecules function as p-type organic semiconductors in organic electronic devices. This project has resulted in new designs and a useful synthetic strategy for interesting but challenging conjugated molecules, and also led to better understanding on structure-property relationship for organic electronic materials.

402512.label: Project Objectives
402512.value: To design, synthesize, and characterize a series of dendritic acetal-linked phthalocyanine dimers which can be further functionalized with a tumor-targeting ligand, such as folic acid. For comparison, a non-cleavable analogue will also be prepared. To study their aggregation behavior and basic photophysical properties, particularly their ROS generation efficiency, in organic and aqueous media. To investigate and compare their cleavage kinetics at different pH in aqueous media by monitoring the fluorescence and ROS generated by the phthalocyanines. Their pH-responsive behavior inside tumor cells will also be examined by monitoring the intracellular fluorescence and ROS generated. To evaluate their in vitro properties, including cellular uptake, subcellular localization, photocytotoxicity, and the photodynamic mechanism. For the folic acid-conjugated systems, KB human nasopharyngeal cells and MCF7 breast carcinoma cells will be used. The former are known to over-express folate receptors, while the latter will be used as a negative control.

402512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402512.value: Light has long been used for medicinal purposes. By combining its action with that of a photosensitive drug and molecular oxygen, a new therapeutic modality, namely photodynamic therapy (PDT), has been developed over the last two decades for treatment of some localized and superficial cancers as well as certain non-cancerous conditions. Compared with the traditional therapies in oncology, it is relatively non-invasive and has fewer side effects, higher tolerance of repeated doses, and higher specificity that can be achieved through precise delivery of light with modern fiber optic systems and various types of endoscopy. Although the therapeutic outcome has been positive, there are only a few clinically approved photosensitive drugs, which still have deficiencies such as weak absorption of tissue-penetrating red light, sustained skin photosensitivity, low initial selectivity, and inconveniently long drug-to-light intervals (2-4 days). As a result, considerable efforts have been expended in the development of more efficient photosensitizers, particularly those which can be selectively activated by tumor-associated stimuli. As part of our continuing endeavors to explore novel photosensitizing systems, we propose herein a research project to study a new class of phthalocyanine-based photosensitizers in which two phthalocyanine molecules are linked with an acid-labile acetal group and this dimeric unit can be replicated on a dendritic platform. Owing to the intrinsic aggregation propensity, the phthalocyanine units in these dendritic dimers are expected to be self-quenched, which inhibits the emission of fluorescence and generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) through the photosensitization process. Only under acidic conditions as at the tumor site, the acetal linkers in these systems are cleaved and the separation of the phthalocyanine molecules restores the fluorescence emission and photosensitization resulting in effective formation of cytotoxic ROS. We plan to design, synthesize, and characterize a series of these dendritic phthalocyanine dimers, including those which can be further functionalized with a tumor-targeting group such as folic acid, which is a well-known ligand for folate receptors over-expressed in many malignant cells. The spectroscopic and photophysical properties of these systems as well as their cleavage kinetics at different pH will be examined. Finally, their pH-responsive behavior and photodynamic activity will also been studied at the cellular level. It is envisaged that these novel dendritic phthalocyanine dimers can function as “smart” photosensitizers for targeted PDT. 光很早就被應用在醫療方面。在過去二十年，一種通過光、光敏藥物和分子氧相互作用的新型治療方式，即光動力治療已逐漸被發展。它可用於治療局部的、淺表性的癌症和特定的非癌症疾病。與傳統的腫瘤治療方法對比，光動力治療作為一種非破壞性的治療方法，副作用小，重複劑量忍受性高，且通過採用現代光導纖維系統和不同類型內窺鏡檢查技術，可實現光的精確傳送，從而獲得較高的定位性。雖然該治療方法取得長足進步，但目前僅存在少數幾種臨床許可的光敏藥物。這主要是因為這些光敏藥物存在一些缺陷，例如：較弱的能穿透組織的紅光吸收能力；較差的持續皮膚光敏性；低的初始選擇性；長時間藥光間隔的不方便性（2-4天）。因此，科學家花費大量的精力致力於發展更為有效的光敏劑，尤其是能被腫瘤細胞相關刺激物選擇性啟動的光敏劑。這也是我們課題組持續不斷努力探索新光敏系統的重要方向之一。在此研究計畫中，我們提出一類新型酞菁光敏藥物的研究。此類光敏藥物中兩個酞菁分子通過酸性敏感的縮醛鏈結，二聚體單元可在樹狀平臺上被複製。由於內在的聚集傾向，此類樹狀二聚體中酞菁單元在光敏過程中處於自猝滅狀態，抑制了螢光和活性氧物質的產生。只有處於腫瘤細胞的酸性環境中，縮醛基團被切斷導致酞菁分子分離，恢復了螢光和由光敏作用產生的具有藥毒性活性氧物質。基於此，我們將設計，合成和表徵一系列樹狀酞菁二聚體，包括引入腫瘤細胞靶向基團，如葉酸，它是一種眾所周知的在惡性腫瘤細胞中過表達葉酸受體的配體，同時將研究體系的光譜，光物理性質以及不同pH條件下切斷動力學。最後，細胞內的pH回應行為和光動力活性也將被研究。這類新穎的樹狀酞菁二聚體作為＂聰明的＂光敏劑非常有希望被用於靶向光動力治療。

402512.label: Realisation of objectives
402512.value: The first objective of this project is to design, synthesize, and characterize a series of dendritic acetal-linked phthalocyanine dimers which can be further functionalized with a tumor-targeting ligand. As the first endeavour toward this objective, we connected two acetal-linked phthalocyanine dimers to a p-phenylene core (Dalton Trans. 2016, 45, 13021). For comparison, a non-cleavable analogue was also prepared. These tetrameric phthalocyanines exhibited a stronger self-quenching efficiency in the intact state than the dimeric analogue reported earlier (Chem. Commun. 2012, 48, 9065). Even for singlet oxygen production, the quenching was found to be effective, both in aqueous media and inside human adenocarcinoma HT29 cells. As an extension of this study, we attempted to synthesize some dendritic systems which have more acetal-linked phthalocyanine dimers in order to amplify the activation effect. Unfortunately, the acetal linker was found to be unstable under the conditions of copper(I)-promoted azide-alkyne cycloaddition reaction, which was used as a key step. To circumvent this problem, we replaced the acetal linker with a disulfide linker, which could be cleaved by glutathione (GSH). It is the most abundant intracellular thiol and its concentration is often elevated in tumor cells. As a result, GSH has been widely used to trigger drug release and activate theranostic agents inside tumor cells. By making this change, we were able to prepare a series of disulfide-linked dendrimers with 2, 3, 4, and 6 phthalocyanine units (J. Med. Chem. submitted). As expected, these compounds were significantly self-quenched and the self-quenching efficiency increased as the number of phthalocyanine unit increased, particularly from dimer to trimer. Upon activation by GSH, the “On/Off” ratio was found to be 7, 18, 23, and 21 for the dimeric (PC2), trimeric (PC3), tetrameric (PC4), and hexameric (PC6) systems, respectively. This result suggested that trimeric and tetrameric phthalocyanines would be optimal in terms of the self-quenching efficiency and the synthetic effort put to prepare these compounds. As a result, we focused on the trimeric systems in the subsequent study. Attempts to conjugate a disulfide-linked phthalocyanine trimer with folic acid were not successful mainly due to the solubility problem. We therefore employed biotin instead as the targeting ligand, which is also a well-known growth promoter that can bind to specific receptors overexpressed in tumor cells. The resulting conjugate could be purified and characterized readily (Dalton Trans. submitted). Apart from this biotin-conjugated GSH-responsive phthalocyanine trimer, we also prepared and characterized a doxorubicin-substituted analogue as a potential dual therapeutic agent (manuscript in preparation). Hence, even though we could not synthesize the compounds exactly as what we proposed, we did prepare closely related analogues for the proposed investigations. To address the second and the third objectives, the electronic absorption and fluorescence spectroscopic properties of all these compounds were examined in N,N-dimethylformamide and phosphate buffered saline or citrate solution (pH 7.4) with 1% Cremophor EL. This study could also shed light on their aggregation behavior in these media. Moreover, their singlet oxygen generation efficiency was also determined by a steady-state method using 1,3-diphenylisobenzofuran as the scavenger. For the acetal-linked phthalocyanine tetramer, its pH-responsive behavior in fluorescence emission and reactive oxygen species formation, both in aqueous media and inside HT29 cells, was examined. The results were compared with those of the non-cleavable analogue. Similarly, the effect of GSH on these properties of the disulfide-linked oligomeric phthalocyanines was also studied. The results indicated that the acetal and disulfide linkers could be cleaved by acid and GSH (in mM range), respectively. This led to separation of the phthalocyanine units and restoration of their photoactivities. Study of the time-dependent fluorescence enhancement could reveal the rate and extent of cleavage of the linkers upon interaction with these stimuli. Finally, the cytotoxicity of all these compounds against HT29 or the human cervical cancer HeLa cells was investigated, both in the dark and upon illumination with red light (> 610 nm). The results were compared with those of some control systems, including pre-incubation with GSH reduced ethyl ester, which could be readily internalized by cells and rapidly hydrolyzed to generate GSH. For the biotin-conjugated GSH-responsive phthalocyanine trimer, the dual targeting and activation properties were also examined using the HeLa and Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells, which were known to be biotin-receptor positive and negative cell lines, respectively. By using confocal microscopy and flow cytometry, it was found that the trimer was preferentially taken up by the biotin-positive HeLa cells and activated by the intracellular GSH, resulting in fluorescence recovery. As biotin instead of folic acid was used as the tumor-targeting ligand, the cell lines were changed accordingly. Nevertheless, we could demonstrate the cell-selective and activation properties of this dual-functional photosensitizer at the cellular level. Apart from these in vitro studies, we also examined the biodistribution and activation of PC2 and PC6 in the dendritic series in HT29 tumor-bearing nude mice. For both compounds, the fluorescence intensity per unit area at the tumor was found to grow gradually during the first 24 h. While the intensity was then dropped for PC2, the intensity for PC6 remained steady over the following 6 days, which might be a result of the enhanced permeability and retention effect arising from the larger molecular mass of the hexameric system. With all these results, the last objective of this project is deemed to be completed.

402512.label: Major findings and research outcome
402512.value: On the basis of our previous study of a ketal-linked self-quenched phthalocyanine dimer (Chem. Commun. 2012, 48, 9065-9067), an acetal-linked phthalocyanine tetramer was prepared, which exhibited a stronger self-quenching efficiency in the intact state, both in terms of fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen production, and a more remarkable response after activation (Dalton Trans. 2016, 45, 13021-13024). Interestingly, the non-cleavable counterpart showed negligible cytotoxicity even upon irradiation, which implied that the cleavable analogue would remain non-cytotoxic in non-acidic environments, such as the healthy tissues. As this activatable tetramer could not be functionalized readily and the acetal linkers were cleaved partially during the preparation, we extended the study to a novel biotin-conjugated disulfide-linked phthalocyanine trimer (Dalton Trans. submitted). This compound was severely self-quenched. However, upon interaction with glutathione (GSH) in aqueous media and inside tumor cells, it could be activated leading to restoration of its photoactivities. The self-quenching efficiency of this trimer was higher than that of the phthalocyanine dimer and as good as that of the phthalocyanine tetramer with a remarkable activation or “On-Off” response. The additional biotin moiety also rendered a tumor-targeting property to the trimer, making it a promising dual cell-selective and activatable photosensitizer toward targeted PDT. By replacing the biotin moiety with a doxorubicin moiety, a potential dual therapeutic agent was also prepared. Unfortunately, the cytotoxicity of this compound was lower than that of the non-doxorubicin-conjugated analogue as a result of its lower cellular uptake (manuscript in preparation). Apart from these compounds, a series of disulfide-linked dendritic phthalocyanines were also prepared (J. Med. Chem. submitted). They were essentially nonaggregated in N,N-dimethylformamide, but significantly stacked in citrate solution (pH 7.4, with 1% Cremophor EL) as shown by the appearance of their Q-band absorption. Having 2 to 6 phthalocyanine units in a molecule, these compounds were significantly self-quenched, particularly in the citrate solution, and the self-quenching efficiency increased as the number of phthalocyanine unit increased. GSH could cleave the disulfide linkages and separate the phthalocyanine units, thereby reducing the self-quenching effect and enhancing the fluorescence emission and singlet oxygen generation in the citrate solution and inside HT29 cells. Upon irradiation, their IC50 values were found to be in the range of 0.18-0.38 M. Having the largest molecular mass, the hexameric phthalocyanine could be activated and retain in the tumor of tumor-bearing nude mice over 7 days, which might be a result of the enhanced permeability and retention effect.

402512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402512.value: This study has shown that trimeric and tetrameric phthalocyanines are promising candidates of activatable photosensitizers based on the self-quenching approach. These compounds can be synthesized readily by a convergent strategy and modified by introducing an additional functional moiety, such as a tumor-targeting ligand or a chemotherapeutic drug. It is worth mentioning that this kind of dual functional molecular photosensitizers remain very rare to date. To enhance the therapeutic function and efficacy of these compounds, a more tumor-selective ligand can be used. For example, the well-known cyclic RGD peptide can be introduced to target the alpha-v-beta-3 integrin overexpressed in a wide range of tumor cells. For the doxorubicin-conjugated phthalocyanine trimer, additional polyethylene chains can be introduced to the phthalocyanine rings to promote the cellular uptake. The disulfide linker can also be replaced with peptide sequences that are the specific substrates of some tumor-associated proteases. The resulting conjugates could therefore be specifically activated by these biomarkers. It is believed that these further studies can lead to more advanced photosensitizers that can greatly assist the further development of photodynamic therapy.

402512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402512.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an innovative treatment modality for cancer. It involves three individually non-toxic components, namely a photosensitizer, light with appropriate wavelength, and molecular oxygen to generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) that destroy tumor by multiple mechanisms. The use of “smart” photosensitizers that can preferentially localize in tumor and be selectively activated by tumor-associated stimuli can confine the cytotoxic effect at the tumor and reduce the damage to normal tissues. To this end, we have developed a series of activatable photosensitizers based on self-quenched oligomeric phthalocyanines. The photoactivities of these compounds, including fluorescence emission and ROS generation can be triggered by acid or glutathione (GSH) (in mM range), which can roughly mimic the acidic and reducing environment of tumor tissues, both in aqueous media and inside tumor cells. A tumor-cell-selective biotin and a chemotherapeutic doxorubicin moiety have also been conjugated to a GSH-responsive phthalocyanine trimer to impart an additional therapeutic function to this activatable photosensitizer. The tumor-retention property of a hexameric phthalocyanine in tumor-bearing nude mice has also been demonstrated. It is envisaged that these novel oligomeric phthalocyanines can serve as lead compounds for further development of advanced photosensitizers for targeted PDT.

402612.label: Realisation of objectives
402612.value: In this completed project we have achieved all objectives in full and beyond. Regarding the conic inequality, inclusion problems as well as more general problems of the following type: for multifunctions F between Banach spaces X ,Y and their subsets Z and E respectively, (*) To find z in Z such that F(z) meets the target E, we investigate various error bound issues in conjunction with other closely related notions. When Z and E are unions of finitely many polyhedra, and F is a piecewise linear multifunction with nonempty solution set S for (*), we show that (*) is always locally metrically subregular (and in fact boundedly metrically subregular), and we also give some characterization properties for the corresponding global version. In the same spirit, the corresponding results for error bounds are also achieved, and the classical theorem of Hoffman is extended. Applications are given in providing several sufficient conditions ensuring F to have various types of weak sharp minimum properties with respect to Pareto or weak-Pareto optimum values. Another specially interesting case is when Z=dom(F) and E=-C, where C is a closed convex cone in Y, namely one considers the following inequality problem (**) F(x)≤0 w.r.t. the order ≤ defined by C. Our results on the extended Smale’s theory (originally on analytic equations) cover non-analytic equality/inequality cases with weaker assumptions. Here we assume that X is a Hilbert space (or a reflexive Banach space) and let F be C^2–smooth around a point x_0∈X. Then, under some reasonable assumptions (weaker than Smale’s “Gamma”-condition and dropping the surjectivity assumption), we show that the extended Newton method can be implemented with the starting point x_0 producing an infinite sequence (x_n ) convergent to a solution x* of (**) satisfying an error bound inequality and providing some useful stopping rule properties. Let T be the convex process defined by T(x)=F'(x_0)x+C. Let Q denote its inverse process: x∈Q(y) if and only if y∈T(x). Let d_0 denote the distance to the origin from the set Q(-F(x_0)). Given a positive constant γ, let r(x_0) be defined explicitly in terms of γ and d_0. We introduce the weak-γ-condition (wgc) for x_0 which is defined in terms of the norm of the “bi-process” QF''(x). We show that if x_0 satisfies (wgc) and γr(x_0) is bounded by an explicit upper bound (13-3√17)/4, then the extended Newton method can be implemented with the starting point x_0 producing an infinite sequence (x_n) convergent to a solution x* of (**) such that the following error bound inequality is satisfied: d(x_0,S)≤‖x_0-x* ‖≤r(x_0). Moreover, with some explicit positive constant q < 1, one has ‖x_n-x* ‖≤q^(2^n-1)⋅r(x_0), for all n (thus, when an error-tolerance is given, one has a practical stopping rule). Comparing the classical theory of Smale, we note in particular that (a) Our results cover non-analytic and inequality cases in infinite dimensional spaces. (b) F'(x_0) is not required to be onto Y. (c) Our upper bound assumption is weaker while the estimates provided in our conclusion are sharper. There are ten journal publications (of which five are in SIAM J. Optim) solely or partially supported by this project.

402612.label: Major findings and research outcome
402612.value: We consider multifunctions F between Banach spaces X and Y (or special ones such as Asplund spaces or Hilbert spaces), and subsets Z and E of them respectively. A general problem is (1) To find z in Z such that F(z) intersects the ‘target’ E. Let S denote the set of all solutions of (1), and d(x,S) the distance from S to x in X, and let e(∙) be some suitable ‘residual function’ (e(x) measures a degree of violation of x with respect to the problem in (1), e.g. e(x)=d(x,Z)+d(E,F(x))). A constant c is called a global error bound of (1) with respect to e(∙) if d(x,S)≤ce(x) ∀x∈X. Some less restrictive or closely related notions (such as local or bounded versions or under different names, e.g., local or global metric subregularity/regularity) can also be defined. These terminologies and related ones have also be adopted in various problems in optimization especially in regard with the constraint systems in connection with semi-infinite or infinite programming problems, as well as in conic inequalities. Using the majorizing function technique we show that sequences, generated by a Newton type method with suitable starting point and under some reasonable assumptions, converge to solutions and thereby we obtain some explicit error bounds. This has also enabled us to establish the corresponding stability results when the given system is perturbed by some element y in Y (of small norm or small residual value). Another special case of (1) with great interest studied by us is: Z and E are assumed to be the unions of finitely many polyhedral and F is a piecewise linear multifunction (that is, its graph is a union of finitely many polyhedra). In this case we show that F in (1) has bounded (and so local) error bounds with respect to the residual function e(x)=d(x,Z)+d(E,F(x)). Furthermore, a global error bound exists if and only if e(x) converges to the infinity whenever d(x,S) converges to the infinity. This nicely extends the famous classical Hoffman theorem regarding error bounds for linear functions on Euclid spaces. For the special case that Z=dom(F) and E=-C, where C is a closed convex cone in Y, one considers the following inequality problem (2) F(x)≤0 w.r.t. the order ≤ defined by C. For (2), we extend the classical result of Ioffe significantly (from the numerical case to the vector-valued case) as well as the classical theory of Smale.

402612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402612.value: Further extensions and applications are to be explored especially on the stability aspects and also for some more general classes of Banach spaces.

402612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402612.value: Some well known fundamental results including Hoffman’s error bound theory, Ioffe’s Sufficient Condition theorem for error bunds as well as Smale’s “Gamma”-theory in convex analysis and optimization theory are improved and extended in this completed project. For Hoffman’s theory, in place of linear equality systems in Euclid spaces, we obtained the corresponding results for piecewise linear systems and other more general systems in the setting of Banach spaces. Regarding Ioffe’s theory, in place of his numerical case, we now extend, more generally, to vector-valued case. For Smale’ theory, we not only weaken his assumptions on analyticity, subjectivity and on his γ-condition but also provide sharper conclusions on error bounds.

402712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402712.value: 微凝膠是一種化學交聯的三維高分子網絡組成的軟性粒子。由於微凝膠的大小、柔軟度及其之間的相互作用力可以通過外界刺激如溫度、pH、磁場或是電場來調控，微凝膠常被称作“智能”粒子。也正是這種獨特的性質使得微凝膠在軟物質的物理和化學研究以及應用領域非常有吸引力。 微凝膠粒子通常通過沉澱聚合制成。由於單體、共聚單體、交聯劑的反應活性不同，這種聚合方法會導致微凝膠內部的交聯度和官能團空間分佈不均。結構的不可控對於微凝膠的性質尤其是溶脹的時間尺度、孔徑大小的分佈、光學性質、粒子彈性以及生物活性分子的功能化，有深遠的的影響，進而更大程度地限制了它們的應用。因此，微凝膠應用的成功開發需要兩個前提條件，一是一個新的能夠實現微凝膠內交聯密度和官能團分佈可控的合成方法，二是針對微凝結構和應用性能的關聯的詳盡研究。 最近，通過結合半連續和程序升溫的無皂乳液聚合的方法，我們成功地製備了單分佈的，具有溫度和pH響應的，大小在0.3-5.5微米範圍內可控的微凝膠粒子。更重要的是，這種方法提高了交聯劑和功能性共聚物的分佈的可控性，它們或者均一地分佈在微凝膠內部，或者主要分佈在表面。初步的結果很令人振奮，我們準備進一步研究這種具有特定結構的微凝膠的合成和表徵方法，借此來更好地理解它們的結構對其各種應用的影響。特別地，我們打算：（1）找到合成可控形態和大小的多重響應的微凝膠粒子的最佳條件；（2）檢測交聯密度和官能團的空間分佈對於微凝膠粒子在分散液的行為和其組裝體在表面的行為的影響；（3）研究微凝膠的形態和組成的不均勻性對於製備響應性塗層和作為可開關的基底的潛在應用的影響。 微凝膠正在一系列應用中扮演著越來越重要的角色， 包括塗料工業里的流變改性劑，靶性藥物釋放的納米凝膠，生物傳感和生物醫學器件中的塗層。這些實際的應用需要針對其應用目的改造的具有可控結構的微凝膠。現有的製備微凝膠的標準方法不能得到控制良好的微凝膠網絡結構。過去的二十年研究主要集中在微凝膠的廣泛應用，並沒有很多關於微凝膠的內部結構及其對應用性能的影響。因此，這個項目的順利完成不僅可以帶來新的設計與製備可控結構的智能微凝膠的合成方法，而且也會提供關於微凝膠性質的基本知識，和對於如何構造針對特定應用的更先進的微凝膠粒子的詳盡的理解。

402712.label: Realisation of objectives
402712.value: There are four objectives in this project and the details of the realization related to each objective are as follows: 1. To find the optimum conditions for the synthesis and characterization of multi-responsive microgels with various sizes and controllable architectures based on our recently developed facial method. A series of soft microgel particles, ranging from several hundreds to micron-meters in size were synthesized with controlled distribution of crosslinks and functional charges. A combination of semi-batch and starve-feeding was developed to localize the crosslinks and charges in the core, in the shell or homogenously distributed within the microgels and the resultant microgels were fully characterized by laser light scattering and scanning electron microscopy. 2. To examine how the crosslink density and the functional co-monomer distribution affect the physical properties of microgels in response to environmental stimuli such as temperature, pH, and ionic strength of the surrounding medium, as well as the interaction of microgels with polyelectrolytes and polymers. We showed that the crosslink distribution influences the deswelling of microgels in response to temperature. Microgels with a dense core structure exhibit a smaller swelling capability than those with a loose cores structure. Also, the different charge distribution lead to different pH-dependent swelling of microgels. Microgels with homogeneous charge distribution exhibit a large swelling capability compared with those with a charge-rich core and those with a charge-rich shell. We have used total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM) to monitor the induced interactions between a negatively charged microparticle activated by thermal energy and a negatively charged glass surface in the microgel dispersions. The concentration of microgel was varied over a broad density range, spanning the dilute region where they are separated to the concentrated region where they are in contact with each other. We showed that variation of the microgel concentration had a significant impact to the interactions between the two colloidal surfaces. Optical imaging of binary PS colloids and microgels at the same microgel concentrations confirms the interaction variation at higher microgel concentrations. Moreover, the TIRM measurements revealed a coincidence between the transition of the interaction curves and the transition of the confined microgel structure. In addition, the strength of the packed microgels was evaluated. 3. To fabricate responsive microgel surfaces by employing microgels with various architectures as building blocks and then study how the compositional heterogeneity of these contributes to their self-assembly behavior in response to various stimuli. Soft microgel particles with various morphologies were used to fabricate thermos-responsive films via drop-coating. The coating conditions were carefully controlled and the morphology of the resultant films was characterized by SEM and AFM. We also examine microgel particles behaviour with different size, crosslinker contents, charge contents and internal morphologies at the liquid-liquid interface. We discovered that the large microgel particles were not significantly deformed in most conditions, which is consistent with the recently theoretical prediction. Only the extremely solvent-swollen with charges located in the shell microgel samples showed an anisotropic deformation at the interface. This anisotropic deformation was different from our original thought and previous findings. Our results also suggest that the behaviour of large microgels (with diameter larger than 1400 nm) may be notably different at the oil/water interface compared to other studies with smaller microgels. These results renew our impressions and understandings of the deformability of micron-sized microgel particles at the interface. 4. To investigate the influence of microgel architecture on the physical properties of the responsive surfaces formed and the potential use of these switchable substrates for cell culture and recovery. Monodisperse microgel particles were proven for reliable construction of thermoresponsive surfaces. The resultant films can act as a non-toxic substrate for cell growth. Our result demonstrated that HepGe, a human liver carcinoma cell line shows little tendency to detach from the microgel films when the temperature is decreased from 37 C to 25 C. SPR result shows serum proteins, which adhere to the surfaces prior to cells over the course of cell culture, adsorb onto the microgel surfaces in an irreversible way in response to a reduce temperature. Therefore, the irreversible protein adsorption onto the substrates may be responsible for this result, providing a new perspective for explaining cell behaviors. We also used total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM) as an invasive approach to study the interactions between several kinds of protein adsorbed surfaces under Brownian motion. we found that the iep of the protein-functionalized surfaces shifted from the bulk protein solutions in different extents. At pH close to iep, adhesion was found between two protein adsorbed surfaces. They can be related to the reduced double layer repulsion and strong hydrophobic attractions between the adsorbed protein films when the protein-functionalized surfaces become neutral. However, at pH far beyond the iep of the two protein-functionalized surfaces, one of the surfaces that adsorbed with the SP can resist to the surface adsorbed with either ConA, BSA or LYZ proteins due to the strong electrostatic repulsion, and the corresponding potential energy curves fitted well with the classic DLVO theory. This study provides an insight on the mechanism of the protein resistance and the interactions involved in protein-functionalized surfaces.

402712.label: Major findings and research outcome
402712.value: This research project has been successfully accomplished by our group. A series of multi-responsive microgel particles with well-controlled structures were synthesized and assembled them on surfaces so as to construct smart substances for biomedical applications. We also measured the particle-surface interactions in aqueous solutions induced by soft microgel particles with concentration. Moreover, we study the interactions and structures of microgels trapped at an oil-water and air-water interfaces. This project has generated a total of 13 high-quality publications and trained 2 PhD students. The main findings are summarized as follows: 1. Synthesis, characterization and application of multi-responsive microgels. We have developed a facial approach by a combination of semi-batch and starve-feeding for the synthesis of microgels with varied sizes and different spatial distribution of crosslinks and charge groups. The prepared soft microgel particles were then used to fabricate thermos-responsive films We showed that the resultant films can act as a non-toxic substrate for cell growth. 2. Soft microgel particle behavior at liquid-liquid interfaces. We conducted a systematic experimental study to image the synthesized micron-sized microgel particles at the decane-water interface. Our confocal images suggested that the internal elasticity of the micron-sized microgels was not sufficient for the microgels to be spread on the interface by the capillary force unless the particles were pH-responsive and swollen in an alkaline condition. 3. Measuring the interactions induced by microgel particles and protein-coated surfaces. We have used total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM) to monitor the induced interactions between a negatively charged microparticle activated by thermal energy and a negatively charged glass surface in the microgel dispersions. In addition, TIRM was introduced as an invasive approach to study the interactions between several kinds of protein adsorbed surfaces under Brownian motion. 4. Microgel particles at the air-water interfaces. Bubble-confined liquid marbles stabilized by hydrophobic silica particles were prepared and it has been demonstrated that more than one bubble can be inserted and trapped inside one liquid marble so that liquid marble can be divided into several separated compartments. The inner air/water interface thus can be effectively stabilized by soft microgels. 5. Microgel-stabilized high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs) as nutraceutical containers. Protein-based microgel particles were prepared by a two-step desolvation and employed as an active emulsifier to prepare stable oil-in-water Pickering HIPEs. Encapsulating the nutraceutical into food-grade products offers new opportunities for the use of gelatin particle-stabilized Pickering HIPEs in functional food and pharmaceutical applications

402712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402712.value: In this project, we have focused on synthesis of soft microgels with different morphologies and used them as building blocks in the construction of stimulus-responsive films. We showed that microgels will be in some conditions impart to the resulting films their twofold responsiveness to pH and temperature as well as can act as a non-toxic substrate for cell growth, which can thus be further developed as switchable cell culture substrates. We also conducted a systematic experimental study to image the synthesized micron-sized microgel particles with different morphologies and charge distribution at the oil-water interface. We suggested that the behaviour of large microgels are notably different at the liquid-liquid interface compared to other studies with smaller microgels. These results can renew our impressions and understandings of the soft particle behaviour at the interface, and will in turn help to elucidate the connection between the interfacial particle properties and the emulsion characteristics. In addition, we measured the particle-surface interaction induced by microgel particles with concentration dependence and revealed that due to deformability, the soft particles in the condense state is not as densely packed as expected. This will provide a new insight into the soft colloids involved interactions.

402712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402712.value: Touted as intelligent materials, soft particles play an increasingly important role in a wide range of applications, including nanogels for targeted drug delivery, coatings for biosensing and biomedical devices. These practical applications require microgels with tailored structures that are well-adapted to their purposes. However, current standard methods for the preparation of microgels often leads to an inhomogeneous spatial distribution of crosslinks and charges within the microgel particles. This lack of control of the structure has significantly limited their key applications. This project has successfully developed a technique based on a combination of semi-batch and temperature-programmed surfactant-free emulsion polymerization for the preparation of multiple-responsive microgels with a uniform-sized and well controlled morphology. The prepared soft microgel particles were also used to fabricate thermos-responsive films which can act as a non-toxic substrate for supporting cell growth so that they can be further developed as switchable cell culture substrates. We also discovered that microgel with different distribution of crosslinks and charges are notably different at the liquid-liquid interface compared to other studies with conventional microgels. This study provides basic knowledge about the nature of soft particles and a detailed understanding of how to construct more advanced soft particles for specific applications.
