402812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402812.value: 由於全球气候变化和能源危機问题，如何提高光伏电池的效能已成爲這一領域的主要課題。近來我們的研究顯示，表面等離子體激元可有效地改善光伏材料的性能。因此，類似于光晶體，週期性金屬陣列(或稱表面等離子體矩阵)能為提高光伏电池效率開創另一新途徑。但是表面等離子的效能非常依赖金屬陣列的結構。 本項目旨在通過理論和實驗的結合，在金屬陣列的結構發的研究上，發展出一種自下而上的合理方法設計具有超高性能的光伏效能。 我們預計在這研究上在發展出高效能光伏电池, 並且具有可觀的均勻性和可重複性。

402812.label: Realisation of objectives
402812.value: We have fulfilled all the objectives of the project. For objectives 1 and 2, we have developed experimental and theoretical understanding of the effects of surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) on solar cells by using temporal coupled mode theory (CMT). In particular, we use to elucidate the dependence on the absorption of the periodic plasmonic systems on the interplay between the absorption and radiative decay rates of SPPs. Under critical coupling where the absorption and radiative decay rates are equal, the absorption is the strongest, leading to the so-called total absorption. As a result, all the input sunlight energy is coupled to the solar cells for photocurrent generation. Since the radiative decay rate of SPPs is a function of geometry, one can tailor the geometry of the arrays to match with the absorption rate. To confirm such analytical prediction, we have conducted rigorous full-wave finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations and the results agree well with the analytical model. At the same time, we also have performed angle-resolved spectroscopy to confirm both the analytical and numerical results. We have developed methods to measure the absorption and radiative decay rates of SPPs as well as the absorption of the arrays. The experimental results are consistent with the theory, showing the absorption is the strongest when two rates are matched. We also have studied the effects of fundamental processes of SPPs such as mode coupling and group velocity on the field of SPPs, which directly affects the absorption of the plasmonic arrays. For objectives 3 and 4, we understand how the geometry of periodic metallic arrays affects the decay of SPPs. When the hole size is smaller than the wavelength, the radiative scattering of SPPs can be approximated as two-dimensional Mie scattering. Therefore, increasing the hole radius R and depth H for two-dimensional nanohole arrays, for example, the radiation damping rate will scale with H*R^2. On the other hand, the absorption rate is largely dependent on the type of material but weakly on the geometry. The analytical results have been confirmed by FDTD simulations and experiments. In addition, we have studied the formation of bright and dark modes under the coupling of two degenerate modes. For one-dimensional, we find for arrays with small groove width, when approaching to the coupling of -1 and +1 SPP modes, while the radiative decay rate of the high energy mode tends to become zero, the absorption rate decreases as well, forming a “cold” dark mode. At the same time, both the absorption and radiative decay rates of the low energy mode increase, yielding a “hot” bright mode. The situation is completely reversed when groove width increases, turning the high energy mode into a “cold” bright mode and vice versa for the low energy mode. We have attributed such modifications to the interplay between the real and imaginary parts of the complex coupling constant, which are found to be highly geometry dependent. Other than the decay rates, we also have developed new approaches to measure the propagation distance of SPPs. We formulate a new spatial CMT to extract the propagation distance of SPPs from the momentum dependent reflectivity profile. By using a widefield microscope together with a set of Fourier lenses for taking the angle- and polarization-resolved reflectivity Fourier-space images, we have studied the propagation distances as well as group velocities of different SPP modes in nanohole arrays. Finally, we have laid out a rational approach to design metallic array for any given photovoltaic materials and the results have led to a new Innovative Technology Fund Tier Three project and a provisional patent on plasmonic solar cell.

402812.label: Major findings and research outcome
402812.value: By using temporal couple mode theory (CMT), we have elucidated the role of the absorption and radiative decay rates of SPPs in determining the absorption of the plasmonic systems. In general, under a single port model, if two rates are equal, the outgoing waves will destructively interfere with each other, leading to total absorption (part C, 8(2)). This critical coupling, or impedance matching, condition has been verified by using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation and experiment. Based on CMT, we also have derived method to measure the absorption and radiative decay rates of SPPs so that the critical coupling condition can be identified experimentally (part C, 8(2)). The study of the decay of SPPs is of importance since it affects the properties of the plasmonic system. Therefore, we have studied on the effects of geometry on the decay process of SPPs. For example, we find the radiation damping of SPPs from nanohole arrays is strongly dependent on the hole radius and depth, following Mie scattering when the hole size is smaller than the wavelength (part C, 8(2)). In addition, when two degenerate modes couple to form the bright and dark modes, their absorption and radiative decay rates depend on the coupling constant, which contains both the near- and far-field interactions (part C, 8(1,2)). Varying the geometry significantly affects the near- and far-field interactions, giving rise to absorptive bright or dark modes (part C, 8(1)). The interplay of the decay rates leads to many intriguing optical phenomena such as total absorption (part C, 8(1,2)), near field enhancement (part C, 8(2)), and polarization conversion (part C, 8(6)). Other than decay rates, the propagation distance and group velocity also play a vital role in determining the behaviors of SPPs. For example, the group velocity is connected with the density of states of SPPs and they affect both the absorption (part C, 8(2,8)) and emission (part C, 8(3,7). We have developed a new approach in formulating and then measuring these parameters by using spatial CMT and a homebuilt microscope (part C, 8(4,5)). Finally, the results here have led to a successful Innovative Technology Fund Tier Three project and a provisional patent (part C, 11).

402812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402812.value: Our study shed light in how to enhance the absorption of plasmonic systems and this is of great importance in solar cell with high performance. In fact, the critical coupling arising from our analytical formulation has provided us a new approach in maximizing the absorption. The results here have led to a successful Innovative Technology Fund Tier Three project and a provisional patent (part C, 11). The solar cells fabricated in this industrial project have been exhibited in several exhibitions and collaboration with solar cell manufacturers is ongoing. While CMT only provide a simple guideline, a more comprehensive model that takes into consideration of other effects is essential in order to tailor the plasmonic systems for different solar cells. For example, for plasmonic systems that involve higher SPP orders, multiple diffractions are present and the single port model is no longer applicable. A vectorial CMT thus is required for full consideration.

402812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402812.value: Surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) are promising in enhancing the performance of solar cells by increasing their light absorption. In fact, for thin film solar cells where the light absorption scales with the thickness (less than several micrometers), the absorption only reaches 0.1% in near infrared. To increase absorption, proper trapping of light within such small thickness is necessary. Due to their evanescent wave nature, SPPs can trap light effectively of the order of wavelength, thereby maximizing light absorption. In this project, we find the absorption, field enhancement, polarization conversion, etc, are strongly dependent on the decay of SPPs, in which their rates are geometry dependent. By tailoring the absorption and radiative decay rates of SPPs, we produce optical phenomena that are useful in making plasmonic solar cells. Our results have been verified analytically numerically, and experimentally. As a result, it is now possible to optimize the absorption of solar cells systematically, pointing to the direction of developing high performing solar cells in near future.

402912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402912.value: 台風是香港海域夏季的常見現象。每年台風季節，香港近海包括近岸及離岸海水極易受到台風的影響。台風形成海表面強壯的風應力，從而改變上層海洋熱結構、區域海洋環流、海水的生物物理特性。在香港近海，台風引起的近慣性振蕩（Near Inertial Oscillation）海流遠強於潮流，並在台風過后可持續一個月之久。此外，台風引起的垂直切變可導致非常強的垂直混合。因而台風誘導的區域海洋環流、溫度結構的變化是香港近海的重要海洋動力學現象之一，需要仔細的探索及研究。 長期以來，香港近海海域缺乏足夠的海洋觀測調查，以至於對許多基本的海洋環流和溫度結構參數仍不清楚，尤其是強風狀況下。台風給香港帶來大風、暴雨、風暴潮，本項目的工作充分利用最先進的現場觀測、數值模擬、衛星遙感技術，旨在了解上層海洋對台風響應的詳細過程。項目的研究重點在於加強香港近海的海上實地觀測，開發出一個強台風情況下的數值模型並與實地的觀測作對比，以發現海洋對台風響應的動力學機制。研究成果會增強我們對香港近海海洋動力學的了解，有助於極端風力條件下的精確區域海洋預報模型系統的開發與驗証。 該項目將組成一個具有豐富實地觀測、數值模擬、衛星遙感工作經驗，來自香港、大陸、海外的資深海洋學家團隊以確保研究達到國際一流水准。項目的成果可提供新的一手資料，用於香港中文大學新建立的地球系統科學主學科的教學。該項目也可為地球系統科學專業的青年學者、博士研究生、本科生提供培訓機會。

To clarify horizontal, vertical structures and propagation characteristics of typhoon-generated NIOs, elucidate effects of the NIOs on the regional currents of the Hong Kong coastal waters under typhoon influences, understand the role of the NIOs on modifying the ocean vertical thermal structure, and explore energy exchange relationship between NIOs and tides.

402912.label: Major findings and research outcome
402912.value: 1) The summer monsoon onset over the South China Sea (SCS) is an abrupt event in May or early June every year. After the summer monsoon onset in 1998 and 1999, strong near-inertial oscillations (NIOs) in the central SCS were observed with Acoustic Doppler Current Profilers (ADCP) mooring data. The strong NIOs appeared in the middle of the SCS in May when the SCS summer monsoon starts to prevail, which implies that the beginning of the SCS summer monsoon may be a vital factor for generation of the strong NIOs in May (Shu et al., 2016) . 2) In the study on variations of chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) and oceanic conditions in the continental shelf region east of Hainan Island during the fast-moving tropical storm Washi, we found that that there was significant variation of Chl-a concentration in the continental shelf region, with low values (about 0.1 mg m−3) before the storm and a 30% increase after the storm. Power spectral analysis of Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler (ADCP) data at a shelf site near the study region reveals strong near-inertial oscillations (NIOs) in the upper layer. The NIOs intensified mixing and modified the stratification of the upper layer, inducing uplift of nutrients and Chl-a into the mixed layer from below, and leading to surface Chl-a increase (Zhao et al., 2017). 3) The physical dynamic and biological response processes to typhoon Cimaron (2006) in the South China Sea are investigated through the three-dimensional Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS). We show that the ROMS simulation accuracy can be enhanced by adding a wave-induced mixing term (B_V) to the nonlocal K-Profile Parameterization (KPP) scheme. The surface ocean was restored to its equilibrium ocean state by about 10 to 20 days after typhoon’s passage. Simulations show that the phytoplankton bloom was triggered five days after the passage of the storm, reveals the mechanisms of the phytoplankton development and decay (Sun et al., 016). 4) The Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS) is used to simulate the low salinity water (LSW) detachment process forced by real and idealized winds. Modeling results show that the LSW detachment appears under a pulsed southwesterly wind, while tidal mixing modifies the size and salinity of the detached LSW. Further analysis shows that the pulsed, upwelling-favorable wind causes detachment of the low salinity water in the upper layer from the main plume water body (Chen et al., 2016).

402912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402912.value: We will continue the proposed studies of effects of the near-inertial oscillations on the upper ocean dynamics, especially their biophysical effects. Our studies implied that the typhoon-induced near-inertial oscillations can significantly augment the local primary production. In future, with more observation data and deeper simulations, we will explore the detailed dynamics of the biophysical effects of the near-inertial oscillations in the ocean upper layer.

402912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402912.value: The strong typhoon winds generate turbulent entrainments and upwelling and cause subsurface cold water entraining and uplifted into surface layer, resulting in cooling of the surface water and deepening of the upper ocean mixed layer. Typhoons also can modify upper ocean circulations. Near inertial oscillations (NIOs) are one of the most important ocean dynamic responses to typhoon. In the SCS, the observed NIOs may last up to one month or longer after typhoon passage and are more energetic than ocean tidal currents. Because of ocean responses to typhoon, lower layer of nutrients-rich water can be uplifted to the surface to enhance the ocean primary production, and surface algae blooms are frequently observed after typhoon passage. The research project clarified how the upper ocean respond to the typhoons in the South China Sea, and gained new knowledge on phytoplankton booming mechanisms under the typhoon influences. These results can assist developing regional marine environmental prediction systems under extreme wind conditions in the Hong Kong coastal waters.

403012.label: Realisation of objectives
403012.value: In this funded GRF project, we developed two simple and efficient methods for the synthesis of disubstituted carbazoles and tricyclic chromones in the gold catalytic protocols. Both methods could be applied to synthesize small medicinal molecules. Moreover, we developed an efficient protocol towards bridged bicyclo[3.2.1]octenone species and novel cycloisomerization of 1,5-enynes via a gold-catalyzed tandem cyclization, and are applying these strategies in the total synthesis of dhilirolide A and the efficient synthesis of drug or lead compounds in the related pharmaceutical industry that could be derived from bicyclo[3.2.1]octenone units and tetrahydrofuran moiety. These newly developed methods in this project will be available for the synthesis of potential active compounds that could provide the important insights into their structure activity relationships.

403012.label: Major findings and research outcome
403012.value: Supported by this GRF project, we obtained some interesting results and protocol for further potential application in drug synthesis and natural product synthesis. The major findings are listed below: 1) A simple and efficient method for the synthesis of disubstituted carbazoles has been developed. In this approach, carbazoles are synthesized from o-haloanilines and terminal alkynes using a two-step strategy,namely, Sonogashira coupling and intramolecular cyclization to provide indoles, which are followed by a p-TSA·H2O-catalyzed carbazole formation. 2)A simple and efficient method for the synthesis of tricyclic chromones has been developed. In this approach, tricyclic chromones were synthesized from a diverse range of phenols and alkynes through a Sonogashira coupling and subsequent gold-catalyzed intramolecular domino cyclization. 3) Recently, we also observed the useful isomerization of 1,5-enynes to be as an active tool for the synthesis of diversified cyclic compounds in the presence of gold catalyst. Also, as the product structures are novel and the main moiety of this compound has been reported as a main part of structure of various bioactive natural products. Noteworthy, our newly discovered this new gold-catalyzed cyclization reaction, we continued to explore this strategic approach to get the compound effectively and investigate the relevant mechanism for this gold-catalyzed transformation. The finally developed protocol is supported to be applied in natural products synthesis and medicinal chemistry in our group in the near future. 4) Another newly developed efficient protocol towards a versatile synthesis of bicyclo[3.2.1]octen-2-ones was applied to render scarce biologically active natural products containing the functionalized bridged bicyclo[3.2.1]octenone units readily available for chemical and biological investigations. Also, the total synthesis of dhilirolide A ( or other family members) will be completed by the application of our newly developed efficient protocol towards a versatile synthesis of bicyclo[3.2.1]octen-2-ones in our group.

403012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403012.value: Based on our recent development of an efficient protocol towards a versatile synthesis of bicyclo[3.2.1]octen-2-ones and isomerization of 1,5-enynes, we developed an efficient protocol towards bridged bicyclo[3.2.1]octenone species and novel cycloisomerization of 1,5-enynes via a gold-catalyzed tandem cyclization, and are applying these strategies in the total synthesis of dhilirolide A and the efficient synthesis of drug or lead compounds in the related pharmaceutical industry that could be derived from bicyclo[3.2.1]octenone units and tetrahydrofuran moiety. These newly developed methods in this project will be available for the synthesis of potential active compounds that could provide the important insights into their structure activity relationships. These works supported by this GRF should have a high impact in the chemistry of organic methodology and natural product, as well as in medicine chemistry.

403012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403012.value: Today, biologically active natural products act as starting points for drug discovery and potential sources of new medicines, along with being critical tools to learn about biologically important processes. Chemical synthesis of natural products and their analogs has therefore been a key tool for novel drug discovery and development. Unfortunately, the potential natural product is only found in very low quantities in nature, so that supplies, with which to carry out a full physiological and biological assessment, are very scarce; if potential leads or drugs of these natural products were found to be effective, the lack of availability and scalability would be a significant impediment to their further development and evaluation in drug discovery. Due to the biological importance, low natural abundance, and structural complexity of bioactive natural products and their analogs, consequently, the discovery of simpler bioactive analogs and total synthesis are of high demand to facilitate the discovery of bioactive molecules for the further bio-evaluations from natural product. Therefore, our newly developed efficient methods will be available for the synthesis of potential active natural products that could provide the important insights into their structure activity relationships, will have a great effect for the drug discovery from natural product.

403112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403112.value: Multiple group analysis is frequently used in research studies of different fields. Typical examples are the comparison of patient groups that receive different treatments in medical studies, and the comparison of various cultural or socioeconomically groups in behavioural science studies. While a number of statistical methods are available for multiple group analysis when the variables of interests are measured in interval or ratio scales, only limited number of methods are available when the variables are measured in ordinal scale. Existing methods as reflected in the literature for ordinal data analysis can be classified into two major types: rank methods and latent variable methods. Rank methods involve the direct comparison of specific sample statistics that are functions of the ranks of the data points. A commonly used rank-type statistic is the Wilcoxon rank sum or equivalently the Mann-Whitney statistic. Latent variable methods operate on the assumption that the observed ordinal responses are crude measurements of some underlying continuous variables. Probit-type models with normally distributed underlying variables are typical in this regard. Both types of methods have their limitations and many relationships among the various methods have not yet been explored. As a result, it is difficult to interpret the possible different results when different methods are applied in data analyses. In this project, we develop a unified location-scale-family modeling framework for multiple group analysis with ordinal responses. We seek to develop a framework that can subsume and unify many of the existing models. Using this framework, we will establish relationships among existing models, investigate the reasons that give rise to possible different results when different methods are used in data analysis, explore new models for ordinal data analysis to address the limitations of existing methods, and develop analyzing tools that can be conveniently applied to a wide range of existing and new models. 多組比分析是一種在許多不同的研究領域都會經常被用到的統計方法。例如，在醫學研究中對多組接受不同處理的病人的比較，在行為科學研究中對不同的文化或社會經濟背景組別的比較，這些都是非常典型的多組分析的例子。當被研究的變數是按照區間尺度或比例尺度進行度量時，已經有許多可以用於多組比較分析的統計方法；然而當被研究的變數是按照順序尺度進行度量時，只存在有限的幾種多組分析的方法。在相關的研究文獻中，能夠用於順序變數資料分析的方法可以被分成兩大類：秩的方法和潛變數的方法。秩的方法主要利用由資料點的秩構成的特殊樣本統計量進行直接比較。一類常用的秩類統計量是Wilcoxon秩和統計量，它等價于Mann-Whitney統計量。潛變數的方法假定觀測到的順序回應變數是對某一潛在連續變數的一種粗略的度量。Probit類型的模型假定正態的潛變數，成為這類方法的典型代表。兩類方法都有它們各自的局限性，而且不同的方法間的關係仍然沒有被深入的探究。因此，當不同的方法被用於資料分析時，這就很難解釋因方法不同所可能產生的不同結果。在本專案中，我們將對具有順序回應的多組分析提供一種基於位置-尺度分佈族的統一建模框架。我們將設法提供一種既能包含現有的各種方法又能使之成為一體的統一框架。基於這一框架，我們將建立現有的各種方法之間的聯繫，探究不同的方法在資料分析中可能產生不同結果的原因，研究能夠克服現有順序資料分析方法局限性的新模型，同時將提出可方便用於比現有及新方法更廣範圍模型的分析工具。

403112.label: Realisation of objectives
403112.value: With regard to Objective 1, we have developed a unified framework based on a general latent variable model. The framework is built upon the location-scale family and subsumes many existing latent variable models for analyzing ordinal categorical data available in the literature. The framework advances the existing methods by enabling many other popular models for analyzing continuous variables to be used to analyze ordinal categorical data, thus allowing for important statistical inferences such as location and/ or dispersion comparisons among treatments to be conveniently drawn. With regard to Objective 2, we have (a) formulated an identification method and estimation procedure for the proposed framework; (b) developed the asymptotic properties of the parameter estimates; and (c) constructed meaningful statistical inference procedures. The proposed identification method could facilitate interpretation and subsequent analysis, rendering the establishment of user-friendly estimation procedures. Another advantage of the identification method lies in that it facilitates the variances of the location and scale parameters be derived in closed forms, and hence many test statistics can be conveniently constructed. Real data analysis was conducted to illustrate the feasibility and applicability of the proposed framework together with the identification method as well as estimation and testing procedures. With regard to Objective 3, we have examined the relations of the proposed unified framework with several popular models for analyzing ordinal categorical data, including the (a) probit-type model, (b) proportional odds model, (c) Whitehead’s (1993) model on common log-odds ratio, and (d) Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test. Moreover, comparison of two treatments in clinical studies is an important topic, and the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney (WMW) test or the Whitehead’s logistic regression model with the proportional odds assumption for treatment comparison has been widely used. These methods, however, give rise to inflated type I error probability when the two treatments have heterogeneous variances or when the ordinal responses are highly skewed. To address this problem, we have investigated the use of a latent variable approach based on the latent Weibull distribution to conduct treatment comparison. Weibull distribution is a member of the log-location-scale family. We showed its effectiveness when it is adopted to analyze ordinal responses with skewed distributions. The main idea of extending the location-scale family to log-location-scale family is as follows: A distribution of the log-location-scale family is used to describe the underlying skewed distributions, and by using an appropriate transformation, the estimation and testing methods tailor-made for the location-scale family can be conveniently translated to deal with the comparisons of the skewed distributions belonging to the log-location-scale family. With regard to Objective 4, we have developed a step-up testing procedure for multiple comparisons with a control, and have explored its application in a randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled study. We have also extended the work of treatment comparison based on the aforementioned latent Weibull distribution to establish testing procedures in clinical trials with multiple groups, including procedures for multiple comparisons with a control and pairwise treatment comparisons. The proposed methods have been evaluated by simulation studies and results provide evidence that the proposed methods can better control familywise error rate in multiple comparisons. In the process of investigating existing methods such as the Mann-Whitney statistic and in comparing the existing methods with the proposed unified model, new insights have been obtained for developing methods that can address issues identified in the literature. Specifically, by using a latent variable approach, Newcombe (2006) investigated some issues related to the Mann-Whitney statistic for analyzing two groups of ordinal responses, and proposed to construct confidence intervals for the ordinal effect size measure that characterizes the equivalence of the distributions of two groups. We extended the work of Newcombe and developed methods to construct confidence intervals for the ordinal size measure in ordinal responses data with misclassification (or ordinal responses data that is partially validated), which would shed light for models for multiple group analysis. As a special case of ordinal responses, we have also developed confidence intervals of the Youden Index for analyzing two-group binary data with misclassification (or data that is partially validated). In summary, the project has been satisfactorily completed and has produced results that realized all the four objectives. Graduate students have been engaged to work under the project, and project results have been presented in international conferences and compiled into papers for publication. References: Newcombe, R.G. (2006). Confidence intervals for an effect size measure based on the Mann-Whitney statistic. Part 1: General issues and tail-area-based methods. Statistics in Medicine, 25, 543-557. Whitehead, J. (1993). Sample size calculation for ordered categorical data. Statistics in Medicine, 12, 2257-2271.

403112.label: Major findings and research outcome
403112.value: Major findings of the project are published in seven papers and are summarized as follows: Paper_1: A unified framework for the comparison of treatments with ordinal responses Findings in this paper lay the foundation of the research project. The paper establishes a unified framework based on the scale-location family for analyzing ordinal responses, develops the estimation and statistical inference procedures, and explores the relationship of the proposed framework with popular existing models. Findings demonstrate the realization of Objectives 1 and 2 as well as Objective 3 partially. Paper_2: Step-up testing procedure for multiple comparisons with a control for a latent variable model with ordered categorical responses This paper introduces a step-up testing procedure for multiple comparisons with a control. The procedure uses correlation structure of the test statistics under the latent normal model and was demonstrated to perform better than existing testing procedures in terms of familywise type I error rate and power. The findings contribute to the realization of Objective 4 partially. Paper_3: Confidence intervals for proportion difference from two independent partially validated series This paper develops methods for constructing confidence intervals for comparing the proportion difference of two independent groups in the presence of partially validated data. The findings realize Objective 4 partially. Paper_4: Confidence interval construction for the Youden index based on partially validated series This paper develops methods for constructing confidence intervals for the Youden index in the presence of partially validated data, and explores its use in group comparison. The findings contribute to the realization of Objective 4 partially. Paper_5: Comparison of two treatments with skewed ordinal responses This paper investigates existing methods for comparing two treatments with skewed ordinal responses, and develops a procedure based on the latent Weibull distribution to address the limitations of existing methods. The findings realize Objective 3 partially. Paper_6: Confidence intervals for an ordinal effect size measure based on partially validated series This paper develops methods for constructing confidence intervals for the ordinal effect size measure that is used to compare two groups of ordinal responses in the presence of partially validated data. The findings realize Objective 4 partially. Paper_7: Multiple comparisons of treatments with skewed ordinal responses This paper develops multiple comparison procedures for analyzing multiple treatment/group problems with skewed ordinal responses. The proposed method is based on a latent Weibull distribution. The findings contribute to the realization of Objective 4.

403112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403112.value: A unified latent-variable framework based on the scale-location family for analyzing ordinal responses has been established, and estimation and statistical inference procedures developed. There are two main directions for further researches. First, the framework can be extended to develop latent variable models with underlying distribution belonging to the log-location-scale family. In effect, some preliminary work in this regard had been completed during the project period. Using the estimation and testing methods for analyzing the model of location-scale family, analyzing procedures based on a latent Weibull distribution had been established. Weibull distribution is a member of the log-location-scale family and more works for the generic log-location family can be further developed. Second, many studies involve the collection of ordinal responses using a surrogate variable, leading to misclassified results. Some of the ordinal responses can be validated and be classified again by using a more reliable device, resulting to partially validated data. The analysis of ordinal categorical variable with partially validated data by using the unified framework with location-scale family represents another promising direction for further research. Some preliminary works for analyzing partially validated data had been developed during this project period, laying the foundation for future development.

403112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403112.value: Multiple group analysis is frequently used in research studies of different fields. Typical examples are the comparison of patient groups that receive different treatments in medical studies, and the comparison of various cultural or socioeconomically groups in behavioral science studies. In this project, we developed statistical methods for conducting multiple group analysis. The project was designed to achieve four objectives: (1) to use the scale-location family to develop a unified model for analyzing ordinal data; (2) to develop estimation and statistical inference procedures in the context of the unified model; (3) to use the framework to establish relationships among the existing models and to investigate the reasons that give rise to possible different results when different methods are applied in data analysis; and (4) to develop new models for multiple group analysis of ordinal data and to explore their application. All the four objectives have been realized. Major findings of the projects had been summarized in seven research papers that were published in international referred journals. Two directions for further research have been identified with some preliminary works completed.

403312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403312.value: The aim of this proposal is to (i) harvest solar energy for catalytic reactions by plasmon-assisted photothermal conversion and catalysis and (ii) understand the underlying mechanisms. As the largest industrial energy consumer, the chemical industry shares 6.6% of the annual total energy consumption of the world. The increasing demand of numerous petroleum-derived products has further accelerated the energy consumption rate by the chemical industry dramatically in recent years. Up to now, most of the consumed energy comes from fossil fuels, which brings about serious environmental and social concerns. A clean and renewable energy substitute will therefore enormously benefit the chemical industry as well as the society at large. Among the renewable energy resources, solar energy is by far the largest exploitable one. However, the two major means of harvesting solar energy, photovoltaics and solar heating, have not been fully employed in the chemical industry. For photovoltaics, the generated electricity usually needs to be converted into heat. The high cost and low conversion efficiency of current solar cells make photovoltaics inapplicable in the chemical industry. The difficulties with solar heating mainly lie in the technical problems encountered in photothermal conversion and heat transfer. Here we propose to design plasmonic-catalytic heterostructures to efficiently harvest solar energy for catalytic reactions, because most industrial reactions are catalytic ones. The heterostructures will be composed of Au nanorods, on which catalytically active metals will be attached as nanoparticles or coated as thin shells. Under illumination, Au nanorods can efficiently collect photons to generate heat and hot electrons for promoting the catalysis on the nanoparticle or shell surface. We will first prepare several types of heterostructures through wet chemistry. Systematic investigations with two model reactions, Suzuki coupling reaction and ethylene epoxidation, will be conducted under laser illumination to elucidate the working mechanisms and the energy utilization process. We will then load the heterostructures on oxide (silica, titania, zirconia, alumina) microsphere supports and apply this strategy to several other reactions (Wacker process, hydrodenitrogenation, and vinyl acetate synthesis), which are crucial in the chemical industry. Solar radiation will be directly employed to drive these reactions. Central to the world economy, the chemical industry provides over 70,000 products for human society. The success of this proposal is expected to provide an effective strategy for replacing fossil fuels with solar energy in certain chemical processes, and to reduce the emission of greenhouse and harmful gases for the environment. 本項目旨在設計具有表面等離子體共振和催化性質的異質複合納米結構從而實現利用太陽能驅動催化反應並研究其内在機理。化工業的能耗在每年全球能耗中佔據6.6%，不斷增長的對石化產品的需求更加加劇了化工業的能源消耗。由於現在的能源消耗主要依賴石油，這也造成了嚴重的環境和社會問題。利用太陽能這個清潔可再生能源為化工生產提供能量將大大有益於化工業和社會的發展。迄今爲止利用太陽能主要有太陽能電池和太陽能加熱兩種方式，這兩种方式環沒有被用於化工業。主要原因是太陽能電池現在比較貴，太陽能加熱有技術問題沒有解決。我們將要設計具有表面等離子體共振和催化性質的異質複合納米結構用來利用太陽能驅動催化反應，該結構以金納米棒做內核，在其表面連接或是生長了具有催化活性的納米顆粒或金屬薄殼。在光照下，金納米棒高效吸光產生熱和熱電子進而加速在表面進行的催化反應。我們將首先合成不同的異質結構，然後在激光照射下系統研究Suzuki和乙烯環氧化反應的機理和能量利用途徑。然後利用各種多孔氧化物(二氧化硅、氧化鈦、氧化鋯和氧化鋁)微球來擔載異質結構催化劑並應用於包括Wacker、吡咯加氫脫氮以及醋酸乙烯酯合成在內的重要反應，這些反應將直接利用太陽光來驅動。化工業現在是世界經濟的一個支柱產業，化工業給人類提供七万多种產品。這個項目的成功將會極大地減輕化工業對石油的依賴，並且減少溫室氣體和有毒氣體的排放。

403312.label: Realisation of objectives
403312.value: Objective 1 Plasmon excitation can generate hot charge carriers in metal nanocrystals and drive chemical reactions. Because the lifetime of plasmonic hot charge carriers is on the order of ~100 femtoseconds to ~1 picoseconds, methods are required for their efficient utilization. One promising approach is to integrate metal nanocrystals with semiconductors. If an n-type semiconductor is chosen, a Schottky barrier will form. Plasmonic hot electrons with sufficient energy in the metal nanocrystal can overcome this potential barrier and inject into the conduction band of the semiconductor. In this regard, we have developed methods for coating semiconductors onto gold nanocrystals. We have successfully coated titania, ceria and cuprous oxide on gold nanocrystals. There are two reasons for the use of different semiconductors. One is the possible coating chemistry for a particular semiconductor, and the other is that the Schottky barrier height, which varies with different semiconductors. We have developed a general route for coating titania onto various metal nanostructures. Titania has been investigated extensively as photocatalysts in scientific research. Many commercial applications with titania-based photocatalysts have been developed. The synthesis of metal/titania hybrid nanostructures is therefore of great interest. Our key invention is the use of a Ti(III) precursor. In contrast, Ti(IV) precursors have been commonly used in previous works. The reactivity of Ti(IV) precursors is extremely high. Therefore control of the reaction rate of Ti(IV) precursors is very difficult. With our method, we have successfully coated titania on differently sized gold nanospheres, gold nanorods, porous platinum nanoparticles, palladium nanocubes, porous palladium nanoparticles, gold/palladium nanostructures, gold/palladium nanocuboids, and gold/platinum nanostructures. The coating method has been reported on Energy & Environmental Science 2014, 7, 3431 and Nanoscale 2016, 8, 6514. We have further developed methods for coating ceria on noble metal nanocrystals. Ceria has found wide applications in catalysis, gas sensing, solid oxide fuel cells, solar cells, and antioxidant therapy. In fact, ceria is used in every car to convert toxic ingredients in the exhaust into less toxic compounds before release. A peculiar property of ceria is its redox cycle between Ce(III) and Ce(IV), which makes ceria adsorb and release oxygen under different conditions. In our method, cerium nitrate is used as the ceria precursor, and ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid is employed to slow down the hydrolysis rate of Ce(III) ions. We have coated ceria on differently sized gold nanospheres, gold nanorods and gold/palladium nanocuboids. The results have been reported on ACS Nano 2014, 8, 8152. Titania and ceria are n-type semiconductors. Their integration with plasmonic metal nanocrystals can allow for hot electrons to inject in the semiconductor, with hot holes left in the metal nanocrystal. In contrast, a p-type semiconductor can allow for hot holes to inject in the valance band of the semiconductor, with hot electrons left in the metal nanocrystal. These two situations will lead to different photocatalytic behaviors. In this regard, we have further coated cuprous oxide, a p-type semiconductor, on gold nanorods and studied their plasmonic properties. This work has been published on Small 2016, 12, 4264. Objective 2 We have designed a system for liquid-phase photocatalytic reactions. The system contains a quartz cell, a cover, and a water bath. The light source can be a Xe lamp, a light-emitting diode (LED) lamp or a laser. We have several lasers from the spectral range of 325 nm to 980 nm. A thermocouple probe can be inserted in the reaction solution for monitoring the temperature. The water bath can be adjusted either below or above room temperature. We have used this system to study various possible factors (metal nanocrystal size and shape, plasmon wavelength, excitation light power, reaction temperature, position of the catalytic nanoparticles on the gold nanoantenna) that can affect the plasmonic photocatalytic activity of Suzuki coupling reaction. In addition, we have also examined and verified the plasmon-induced generation of various intermediate reactive species (singlet oxygen, hydroxyl radicals, hydrogen peroxide, superoxide anion radicals) using this system. Some of the results have been reported in our Energy & Environmental Science and ACS Nano papers. In addition, we were invited to contribute a review article on this topic (Metal/Semiconductor Hybrid Nanostructures for Plasmon-Enhanced Applications, Advanced Materials 2014, 26, 5274, 36 pages). Objective 3 We have acquired the parts and home-built a system for studying gas-phase photocatalytic reactions. The system is composed of gas-flow controllers, a quartz reactor, a light source, a vacuum pump, and a gas chromatograph (GC). Similar to the liquid-phase reaction system, the gas-phase reaction system can use different light sources, including a Xe lamp, lasers, and LED lamps. The system has been tested. It works well. However, there are two severe limitations for our gas-phase system. One is the lack of monitoring and protection components for handling dangerous gases, such as hydrogen and carbon monoxide, and the other is the GC, which can only detect one type of gas molecules with one particular column, except hydrogen and oxygen, which can be detected simultaneously. These two limitations have prevented us from testing different gas-phase photocatalytic reactions. Objective 4 We have developed an aerosol spray route for the preparation of mesoporous metal oxide microspheres. In our previous studies, the oxide precursors were limited to organometallic compounds. Because of the limited commercial availability of organometallic precursors, we were only able to prepare mesoporous microspheres out of silica, titania, alumina and zirconia. In 2013, we discovered that metal nitrates can be employed as precursors for aerosol spray. Nitrates of many different metals are available and relatively inexpensive. As a result, we have been able to prepare mesoporous microspheres of 13 types of metal oxides. In addition, mesoporous multimetallic oxides can be readily synthesized. Moreover, functional species and components can be readily incorporated into mesoporous microspheres. We have demonstrated the incorporation of lanthanides, noble metal nanoparticles, magnetic nanoparticles and polymer nanospheres. This method is very suitable for loading metal nanostructures into metal oxide supports. Objective 5 The responsive ranges of most conventional photocatalysts are limited in the UV region, but the solar energy in the UV region only occupies a few percentages of the entire solar energy. Therefore, one of our goals in studying plasmonic photocatalysis is to make photocatalysts active in the visible or even infrared regions. We have tested several different reactions with our plasmonic metal nanostructures as catalysts under visible light. The examined reactions include Suzuki coupling, selective oxidation of benzyl alcohol, selective oxidation of 1-phenylethanol, click reaction, and coupling of alkyne and phosphite. The selection of these reactions is jointly based on their scientific importance and our experimental facilities. Our goal is to understand and utilize plasmon-excited hot charge carriers to drive chemical transformations. We have therefore also developed a method for the synthesis of gold nanorods with diameters less than 10 nm. The extinction of such small gold nanorods is dominated by absorption, and therefore their efficiency of hot charge carrier generation will be very high. In addition, we have also realized site-selective coating of silica on gold nanorods and the subsequent selective deposition of a second metal. In this way, highly asymmetric bimetallic nanostructures are produced. They will be useful for studying and understanding plasmon-enhanced photocatalytic activity. These works have been published on Langmuir 2015, 31, 7418 and Angewandte Chemie International Edition 2013, 52, 10344.

403312.value: (1) We have developed robust methods for coating metal oxide semiconductors on pre-synthesized noble metal nanocrystals and nanostructures. The tested oxides include silica, titania, ceria and cuprous oxide. The tested metal nanocrystals include differently shaped and sized gold, platinum and palladium nanocrystals, gold/platinum and gold/palladium bimetallic nanostructures. We have demonstrated that plasmonic hot electrons can inject into the semiconductor and subsequently induce chemical reactions. An essential result is that because of localized plasmon, these metal/semiconductor hybrid nanostructures are photocatalytically active under visible light. Therefore, such hybrid nanostructures will offer a new means for utilizing sunlight to drive useful chemical reactions. Our results on this topic have been reported on Advanced Materials (2014, 26, 5274), Energy & Environmental Science (2014, 7, 3431), ACS Nano (2014, 8, 8152), Small (2016, 12, 4264), Nanoscale (2016, 8, 6514). (2) We have developed an approach for synthesizing asymmetric bimetallic nanostructures. Specifically, the second metal, including gold, silver, palladium and platinum, can be selectively deposited at the ends or side surfaces of gold nanorods. The selective deposition is enabled by the selective deposition of silica at the ends or side surfaces of gold nanorods. The pre-deposited silica components direct the subsequent deposition of the second metal onto the unprotected regions. This preparation method is expected to be applicable to other metal nanocrystals with sharp corners or edges. It will allow for studying whether plasmon-enhanced photocatalytic activity is dependent on the position of hot spots on metal nanocrystals. Understanding this question will guide us to design highly efficient plasmonic photocatalysts at low cost. Our coating method has been reported on Angewandte Chemie International Edition (2013, 52, 10344). (3) The PI has been invited to present the results on the proposed topic in international and regional conferences, such as ACS National Meetings and Exposition and PacifiChem. Attending and presenting research results on these conferences makes the PI group, the department and the university known internationally. (4) Two PhD students, one in physics and the other in materials science & engineering, and one MPhil student in materials science & engineering, have been trained on the related topics on the basis of this grant.

403312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403312.value: We have demonstrated that plasmonic nanostructures can generate hot charge carriers, which can be used to drive chemical transformations under visible or near-infrared light. The visible-light plasmonic photocatalytic activity has been realized through the synthesis of bimetallic nanostructures, which combine plasmonic and catalytic metals, and through the synthesis of metal/semiconductor hybrid nanostructures, which can facilitate the separation of plasmonic hot charge carriers. The plasmonic excitation of hot charge carriers in these nanostructures have has been verified by detecting a variety of intermediate reactive species that are originated from hot charge carriers and by catalyzing a few simple chemical reactions under visible light. On the basis of our results and understanding, we will design suitable plasmonic nanostructures for the visible-light photocatalytic reduction of carbon dioxide and nitrogen fixation. Carbon dioxide reduction has a huge impact on the environment on the earth. Ammonia is widely used as a necessary fertilizer. The industrial production of ammonia is through the Haber-Bosch process, which requires high temperatures and high pressure. Therefore, to develop plasmon-based visible-light photocatalysts for these two reactions is meaningful and of high impact. We have actually started to work on nitrogen fixation with plasmonic nanostructures and have obtained promising results.

403312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403312.value: Photosynthesis utilizes light energy to drive chemical reactions on photocatalysts. It can potentially realize the green-chemistry goals in atomic efficiency, waste minimization and recyclability. So far, metal oxide semiconductors have most commonly been used as photocatalysts. A severe drawback of oxide semiconductors is that their energy band gaps lie in the UV region. They can only utilize a small portion of the solar energy. In addition to the limited sunlight utilization, metal oxides pose drawbacks of low reaction activities and selectivities. Hot electrons have energies higher than that determined by thermal distribution. Upon excitation, hot electrons can cause a variety of physical and chemical processes. Noble metal nanocrystals possess extremely attractive localized plasmon resonance. Upon excitation, the plasmon resonance can be damped either radiatively through scattering or non-radiatively through Landau damping to generate hot electron/hole pairs. In this project, we synthesized plasmonic nanostructures in order to utilize plasmonic hot charge carriers to drive chemical transformations. We demonstrated the generation of hot charge carriers upon plasmon excitation in our nanostructures. Our results out of this project will open up a way to the design of high-performance plasmonic photocatalysts for the photosynthesis of valuable molecules in high efficiencies and selectivities.

403512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
403512.value: 淀粉样蛋白寡聚动力学

403512.label: Project Objectives
403512.value: Prepare true solutions of individual amyloidogenic protein/peptide chains to avoid any possible interference by trace amounts of small interchain aggregates. To be done by optimizing our recently developed ultra-filtration protocol and perfecting our newly designed method of grafting a thermally sensitive polymer chain to each protein or peptide chain via a cleavable –S-S- linkage in order to prevent the initial interchain association under the physiological conditions. Develop novel approaches to initiate the oligomerization of amyloidogenic protein/peptide chains under the physiological conditions after a true protein/peptide solution is prepared. This will include using a micro-fluid mixer to quickly change buffers, varying the temperature to switch the grafted polymer chain from hydrophilic to hydrophobic, and using a reducing agent to cleave the –S-S- linkage and remove the grafted polymer chain. Study the kinetics of the very initial oligomerization and nucleation in terms of the changes of the association number, size distribution and morphology of small resultant disordered interchain aggregates by a combination of static and dynamic laser light scattering with analytic ultracentrifuge and high-resolution transmission electron microscope. Correlate the oligomerization/nucleation kinetics to the mutagenesis of amyloidogenic proteins/peptides by using a series of artificially mutated amyloidogenic proteins and chemically synthesized peptides with different controllable sequences in order to unearth certain structure-kinetics relationships, e.g. the relation between the induction lag time and the amino acid sequence on an amyloidogenic protein/peptide chain.

403512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403512.value: 突變蛋白的聚集通常被認為是造成眾多神經退行性疾病的元兇，從人類的阿爾茨海默病（老年癡呆症）到牲畜的傳染性海綿狀腦病（瘋牛病），都在此列。近來甚至有研究將導致人類近半數腫瘤的p53蛋白的功能異常突變歸因於此種聚集。在過去長達四十年的研究中，澱粉樣沉積物被視為神經退行性過程中的致病物質，然而現在越來越多的證據顯示，真正具有毒性的是一系列尚未完全定性的蛋白寡聚體，而非沉積物本身。這些結論凸顯出研究蛋白聚集的初始階段或成核階段的重要性。 為研究寡聚過程，必須首先得到僅含有蛋白鏈單體，無任何鏈間聚集體干擾的“純溶液”，否則研究就沒有意義。我們的研究結果表明，採用大部分常用於製備澱粉樣蛋白溶液的方案並不能得到真正意義上的“純溶液”，這些樣品總是含有極少量的小聚集體。這些聚集體會像種子一樣誘發澱粉樣纖維的形成並影響聚集動力學，尤其是初始階段的聚集。我們的發現在一定程度上解釋了為何不同的實驗室以同一種蛋白/多肽為研究对象，得到的聚集動力學卻大相徑庭。 最近，通過將已有方案和本實驗室新建立的超濾法相結合，我們發展出一種製備澱粉樣蛋白“純溶液”的方法，為後續的寡聚動力學研究掃清了障礙。我們將重點研究寡聚過程與蛋白突變及實驗條件的關係，包括蛋白的起始濃度，溫度及pH等，以期從分子水準上揭示澱粉樣蛋白的聚集機理。具體說來，我們將 1） 改進超濾法及進一步研究通過二硫鍵將溫敏性高分子短鏈與蛋白鏈相連以阻止蛋白聚集的方法； 2） 在生理條件下，通過改變溫度或切除用於穩定蛋白的高分子鏈以誘導聚集發生； 3） 通過化學基團的交聯人為獲得蛋白二聚體、三聚體及其它寡聚體，表徵其大小及擴散係數； 4） 用已表徵的寡聚體為標準，結合激光光散射、分析超速離心機、透射電子顯微鏡等方法研究不同蛋白的寡聚動力學過程； 5） 對如何用小分子延緩寡聚/成核過程進行初步研究。 這項研究的成果將闡明澱粉樣蛋白相互作用的機制，對合理地設計藥物以延緩神經退行性疾病的發作亦具有重要意義。此研究要求綜合運用分子生物學、高分子化學及物理表徵等手段，作為少數同時具備所需技能及實驗設備的研究組，若能得到資助，我們有信心在規定時間內完成申請項目。

403512.label: Major findings and research outcome
403512.value: Misfolding and aggregation of amyloidogenic proteins are hallmarks of many neurodegenerative diseases, including the Huntington’s disease. The aggregation process involves a series of conformational changes from monomeric chains to toxic oligomers, and finally to amyloid fibrils. Despite its potential significance in understanding the pathological process and developing therapeutic strategies, the detail of the chain association, especially in the initial stage, is still unclear. In the current study, we first developed a convenient and efficient PCR-based method to establish a Huntington gene library, containing the Huntington exon 1 genes with different lengths of polyCAG repeats, which enables us to express different Huntington proteins. Then, we developed a snapshot method by applying the carbene-protein reaction to fix different Huntington protein oligomers formed in the initial aggregation stage. A combination of the snapshot and other methods, especially laser light scattering, confirmed that the oligomerization rate and extent of the HD exon 1 proteins in PBS increase with the polyQ length. More importantly, we found that there is a correlation between the cytotoxicity and the β-sheet content of the oligomers of HD exon 1 proteins; namely, the oligomers formed in the initial stage with a lower β-sheet content are more pathologically cytotoxic, illustrating the importance of studying the oligomerization in the very initial stage. Such a finding that the higher the β-sheet content, the lower the cytotoxicity, supports the recent claim that it is those small oligomers of the amyloidogenic proteins that are more cytotoxic.

403512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403512.value: The methodologies established here cab be used for studying other amyloidogenic proteins. In particular, our newly developed novel, simple and efficient PCR based method is readily applicable for generating a library of other genes with different polyCAG tract lengths in the pathological range. The snapshot of using the carbene-protein reaction is effective to fix the HD oligomers formed at different times in the initial stage.

403512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403512.value: The aggregation of mutant proteins is generally considered to be a possible underlying cause of many neurodegenerative diseases ranging from Alzheimer’s to transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (mad-cow). The importance of studying the very initial oligomerization or nucleation stage of mutant protein aggregation was hindered by many experimental difficulties. For example, it is difficult to obtain a true solution that only contains individual protein chains. Our study of using a combination of those existing dissolution procedures and our newly developed ultrafiltration method has enabled us to develop a novel protocol for preparing true solutions of amyloidogenic proteins; thus paving a path for a further study of the oligomerization in dilute solutions. Our focus on how the oligomerization is related to protein mutagenesis and experimental conditions, including the initial protein concentration, solution temperature and pH, has elucidated the aggregation mechanism at a molecular level. Specifically, we found that the higher the β-sheet content, the lower the cytotoxicity, which is against some conventional wisdom; namely, previously claimed the linkage of neurodegenerative diseases to the formation of long fibrous proteins. The outcome of this research has shaded light on how amyloidogenic proteins begin associating with one another, and also have implications in the rational design of therapeutic strategies aimed at slowing down the development of neurodegenerative diseases.

403612.label: Project Objectives
403612.value: To understand processes of the atmosphere-ocean interactions in the SCS region: Embedded within the large warm pool with SST over 28.5∘C that extends from the tropical Indian Ocean to the western tropical Pacific (Fig. 1), the SCS displays prominent air-sea interactions. In this objective, we will investigate how the atmosphere and ocean interact in the SCS region and how this changes spatially and seasonally. To understand different types of ENSO influences on summertime SCS climate: ENSO is one of the strongest signals in short-term climate variability. It plays an important role for climate anomalies in many regions on the Earth. The influences of ENSO on regional climate can be direct through atmospheric circulation changes. The ENSO impact can be indirect with a time-delay, involving feedback of regional SST changes induced by ENSO (Fig. 2). The direct and indirect influences of ENSO may depend on the evolution of ENSO-related SST anomalies in the tropical Pacific Ocean. In this objective, we will separate different types of ENSO influences on summertime SCS climate and investigate the respective processes for the connection between the SCS climate variability and ENSO. To reveal impacts of tropical Indian Ocean climate modes on summertime SCS climate: Recent studies have suggested the potential influence of tropical Indian Ocean SST anomalies on the South China Sea and western North Pacific climate. Previous studies have identified different climate modes in the tropical Indian Ocean, including the basin-wide warming mode in boreal winter and spring, the east-west dipole mode in boreal summer and fall, and the north-south asymmetric mode in boreal spring. In this objective, we will investigate the connection of summertime SCS climate with these climate modes and the respective processes of the tropical Indian Ocean-SCS connections.

403612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403612.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research to understand summertime climate variability in the South China Sea (SCS) region and influences of the tropical Indian and Pacific Oceans. The climate variability is closely associated with the occurrence of drought and flooding that affects water resources, ecological environment, industry and agriculture, and economics. The SCS climate variability is intimately related to the activity of tropical cyclones/typhoons and the East Asian monsoons - two of the most important weather and climate phenomena for Hong Kong. The SCS is a junction region of the broad Asian-Australian monsoon domain. As such, the SCS climate variability is closely connected to activities of major monsoons in the Asian-Australian regions. The land areas surrounding the SCS are densely populated and the change in the SCS climate can affect the lives of billions of people in these regions. Thus, understanding the SCS climate variability and its factors is highly relevant to the sustainable development in the surrounding areas, including the Pearl River Delta region. In this project, we plan to perform research to understand roles of regional air-sea interaction and remote forcing in summertime SCS climate variability. We will document the processes of air-sea interactions in the SCS region. We will examine the influence of El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and tropical Indian Ocean climate modes on summertime SCS climate. We will distinguish direct influence of ENSO on summertime SCS climate through concurrent atmospheric circulation changes and indirect influences of ENSO through regional air-sea interaction, and investigate respective processes for these different influences. We will analyze the relationship between summertime SCS climate and climate modes in the tropical Indian Ocean to unravel the connections between the SCS and tropical Indian Ocean climate variability. Numerical experiments will be conducted to understand relative roles of the tropical Pacific and Indian Oceans in summertime SCS climate variability. This project will advance the understanding of the roles of regional air-sea interaction and remote forcing, the roles of tropical Pacific and Indian Ocean influences, and the roles of direct and indirect influences of ENSO in summertime SCS climate variability. This will improve our understanding of changes in the Asian monsoon and the SCS typhoon activity. It will also provide a scientific basis for improving the short-term climate prediction. 该项目的目的是研究中国南海地区夏季气候变异的规律和热带印度洋和太平洋的影响。 气候变异与旱涝的发生紧密相联系，并影响到水资源、生态环境、工农业生产、和国民经济。南海气候变异与热带气旋/台风和东亚季风（影响香港的两个重要天气和气候现象）的活动关系密切。南海是亚洲和澳洲季风的交互区。因此，南海气候变异与亚-澳季风区的主要季风的活动相关。南海周围陆地人口密集，南海气候的变化影响着这些地区几十亿人口的生活。因此，研究和了解南海气候变化的规律和因子与周围地区包括珠江三角洲的持续发展紧密相关。 本项目将通过研究了解区域海气相互作用和遥强迫在南海夏季气候变异中的作用。本项目将诊断南海海气相互作用过程，调查厄尔尼纳-南方涛动和热带印度洋气候模态对夏季南海气候的影响，区分厄尔尼纳-南方涛动通过同期大气环流变化对南海夏季气候的直接影响和通过区域海气相互作用的间接影响及其各自影响的过程，分析南海夏季气候与热带印度洋不同气候模态的关系及其联系过程，并进行数值试验来了解热带印度洋和太平洋对南海夏季气候变异的相对贡献。 本项目的研究将改进对区域海气相互作用和遥强迫、热带太平洋和印度洋影响、厄尔尼纳-南方涛动的直接影响和间接影响在南海夏季气候变异中的作用的理解。这将有助于改进对亚洲季风和南海台风活动的认识，并为改进短期夏季气候预报提供科学基础。

403612.label: Realisation of objectives
403612.value: Objective 1: To understand processes of the atmosphere-ocean interactions in the SCS region This objective has been accomplished through the following works: 1) We documented the relationship between seasonal variations in sea surface temperature (SST) and precipitation in the South China Sea (SCS) region. It is found that there are strong interactions between the atmosphere and ocean in the seasonal variations of SST and precipitation. During the transition to warm and cold seasons, the SST tendency is primarily contributed by net heat flux dominated by shortwave radiation and latent heat flux with a complementary contribution from ocean advection and upwelling. The contribution of wind-driven oceanic processes depends on the region and is more important in the northern SCS than in the southern SCS. During warm and cold seasons, local SST forcing contributes to regional precipitation by modulating the atmospheric stability and lower-level moisture convergence. The SST difference between the SCS and the western North Pacific influences the convection over the SCS through its modulation of the circulation pattern. 2) We documented the atmosphere–ocean interaction in interannual variations over the South China Sea (SCS) in different seasons. It is found that the atmosphere–ocean relationship displays remarkable seasonality and regionality. An atmospheric forcing is dominant in the northern and central SCS during the local warm season, and an oceanic forcing is detected in the northern SCS during the local cold season. During April–June, the atmospheric impact on the sea surface temperature (SST) change is characterized by a prominent cloud-radiation effect in the central SCS, a wind-evaporation effect in the central and southern SCS, and a wind-driven oceanic effect along the west coast. During November–January, regional convection responds to the SST forcing in the northern SCS through modulation of the low-level convergence and atmospheric stability. 3) We evaluated the precipitation–SST and precipitation–SST tendency correlation in 24 selected models from CMIP5. The results indicate that the simulated atmosphere–ocean relationship varies widely among the models. Most models have the worst performance in spring. On average, the models simulate better the atmospheric forcing than the oceanic forcing. Improvements are needed for many models before they can be used to understand the regional atmosphere–ocean interactions in the SCS region. 4) By using long-term observational datasets, the impacts of atmosphere-ocean interactions throughout the globe on interannual climate variability over the Eurasian land mass have been evaluated. Particular attention was devoted to the effects of sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific (including the SCS) associated with El Nino-Southern Oscillation phenomena on the changes of snow cover over Eurasia. This diagnostic study indicates that snowcover variability over Europe bears a strong relationship with atmospheric changes linked to the North Atlantic Oscillation, whereas air-sea coupling in SCS and the tropical Pacific does not appear to play a dominant role. Objective 2: To understand different types of ENSO influences on summertime SCS climate This objective has been accomplished through the following works: 1) We performed observational analysis of the relationship of summer rainfall variability in the South China Sea (SCS) region to sea surface temperature (SST) in the tropical Indian and Pacific Ocean regions and of the processes for influences of remote Indo-Pacific SST forcing on the SCS summer rainfall variability. The SCS summer rainfall displays a positive and negative relationship with simultaneous SST in the equatorial central Pacific (ECP) and the North Indian Ocean (NIO), respectively. Further analysis reveals that the above-normal summer rainfall in the SCS can occur when the ECP SST anomalies are positive, or the NIO SST anomalies are negative, or a combination of the above. Positive ECP SST anomalies induce an anomalous low-level cyclone over the SCS-western North Pacific as a Rossby wave type response, leading to above-normal precipitation over northern SCS. Negative NIO SST anomalies contribute to anomalous cyclonic winds over the western North Pacific by an anomalous east–west vertical circulation north of the equator, favoring more rainfall over northern SCS. These NIO SST anomalies are closely related to preceding La Niña and El Niño events through the ‘‘atmospheric bridge’’. Thus, the NIO SST anomalies serve as a medium for an indirect impact of preceding ECP SST anomalies on the SCS summer rainfall variability. The ECP SST influence is identified to be dominant after 1990 and the NIO SST impact is relatively more important during 1980s. 2) We conducted numerical experiments with the CESM atmospheric general circulation model with SST anomalies specified in different regions to validate the impacts of the Indo-Pacific SST anomalies. The SST anomalies are specified in the equatorial central Pacific, the North Indian Ocean, and in both of the above two regions. Additional experiments include SST anomalies specified around the Maritime Continent. The results of the numerical experiments are consistent with the observations, which enhances the credibility of the Indo-Pacific SST influence on the SCS summer rainfall variability. Objective 3: To reveal impacts of tropical Indian Ocean climate modes on summertime SCS climate This objective has been accomplished through diagnosis of observations and model experiments. 1) We performed a diagnosis to identify signals of the South China Sea (SCS) summer rainfall variability in the Indian Ocean and the processes for the influence of the Indian Ocean SST anomalies. It is found that the SCS summer rainfall has a negative relationship with December–January–February (DJF) western-equatorial Indian Ocean (WIO) sea surface temperature (SST), a positive relationship with an asymmetric mode of precipitation anomalies in the tropical Indian Ocean during March–April–May (MAM), and a positive relationship with June–July–August (JJA) South Indian Ocean (SIO) SST. The WIO SST anomalies induce same-sign southeast Indian Ocean SST anomalies through an anomalous zonal vertical circulation. The southeast Indian Ocean SST anomalies last from late winter to early summer and induce opposite-sign SCS summer rainfall anomalies via an anomalous meridional vertical circulation. The asymmetric mode influences the SCS summer rainfall variation via the North Indian Ocean (NIO) SST anomalies with significant cloud–radiation and wind–evaporation effect. Positive (negative) SIO SST anomalies drive an anomalous direct circulation between the SIO and the NIO, and an anomalous indirect circulation between the NIO and the SCS which facilitates the occurrence of cyclonic (anti–cyclonic) wind anomalies over the SCS–western North Pacific and results in positive (negative) SCS summer rainfall anomalies. 2) We conducted a partial correlation analysis to detect the ENSO-independent Indian Ocean impacts on the SCS summer rainfall. The results indicate that the influence of DJF WIO SST anomalies and JJA SIO SST anomalies on the SCS summer rainfall is partly ENSO independent, while the MAM asymmetric mode is mostly related to the preceding DJF eastern Pacific SST anomalies. 3) We conducted numerical experiments with the CESM atmospheric model with SST anomalies specified in the South Indian Ocean. The results of model experiments confirm the impacts of the SIO SST forcing on the SCS summer rainfall variability.

403612.label: Major findings and research outcome
403612.value: Major findings: 1) The processes for the interaction between the atmosphere and ocean in the seasonal variations depend upon the time of the year. 2) The atmosphere–ocean relationship in interannual variations displays remarkable seasonality and regionality. 3) ENSO can influence the summer rainfall variability in the SCS directly through concurrent ENSO-associated ECP SST forcing, or indirectly via inducing NIO SST forcing, or a combination of the above two. 4) In addition to the role acting as a medium for ENSO influence, the Indian Ocean SST anomalies can influence the SCS summer rainfall variability independent of ENSO. 403612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403612.value: Through this study, it is identified that the local atmosphere-ocean interaction processes may vary with season and location in the South China Sea region, the ENSO’s influence on the South China Sea climate can be direct or indirect, and the Indian Ocean influence on the South China Sea climate may be either a medium of ENSO influence or independent of ENSO. The methodology and concept achieved through this project may be applicable to studies of regional climate variability in other regions. Properly designed model experiments with specified SST forcing may be employed to verify the observational analysis with caution of the nature of atmosphere-ocean relationship in observations.

403612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403612.value: This project is a basic research that aims at understanding the role of remote forcing in regional climate variability of the South China Sea. Both diagnosis of observations and numerical experiments of atmospheric general circulation model with specified SST forcing in different regions are utilized to demonstrate the influence of the Indo-Pacific SST anomalies on the summer climate variability in the South China Sea region. This project makes an important contribution to the factors of and processes for the South China Sea summer rainfall variability. Given that the South China Sea is located in a junction of the Indian Ocean to the west, the Pacific Ocean to the east, the East Asian monsoon to the north, and the Australian monsoon to the south, revealing the factors of and processes for the South China Sea summer rainfall may be of great help for understanding the influences of ENSO and the Indian Ocean climate modes on the East Asian climate and the connection between the East Asian and Australian monsoon variability. This results of this project point to the necessity of combining the different types of ENSO influences on region climate, which may be of guidance for seasonal climate prediction.

403712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403712.value: 云层中许多重要的现象都和其中的水滴在微观尺度下的物理过程密切相关。人们普遍认为，云层中的湍流流动对云滴的凝结以及它们之间的碰撞起着重要作用：通过碰撞，小水滴之间发生聚结，从而形成较大的液滴。其中一个例子就是由于云滴的惯性而引起的浓度聚集，这一过程被认为提高了云滴的碰撞率，由此缩短了雨的形成时间。然而，尽管浮力作为云中重要的驱动力之一，几乎所有关于云滴动力学的实验研究都是在非浮力驱动的流动中进行的。为此，我们提出了以空气和水汽作为流动载体的瑞利-伯纳德对流这一实验模型，即湿气瑞利-伯纳德热对流，以此来研究浮力驱动湍流中水滴的凝结和碰撞过程。此研究的目的主要在于探索和理解：（1）水滴通过凝结的增长过程；（2）水滴集聚和热羽流之间的关系;（3）热湍流中惯性聚集随斯托克数的依赖关系。 我们希望此研究的结果能够揭示热湍流如何影响云滴的形成以及其中的动力学过程这些重要问题。瑞利-伯纳德对流的一个优势在于：一方面，对流槽中央区域的流动接近于均匀各向同性湍流，这可以用来比较以往使用均匀各项同性湍流作为研究系统的实验结果；另一方面，对流槽侧壁附近充满了热羽流，因此浮力在这一区域占据主导作用。因此，在一个单一系统中就可以研究水滴在不同流动类型中的动力学行为，这是该研究的一大特色。另外，通过同时测量羽流场和粒子场，我们还可以在实验上直接把涡流位置与水滴的惯性聚集联系起来。这些结果将会和在大气云层中的实地测量以及以均匀各项同性湍流为载体的实验和数值模拟研究一起，在理解云滴动力学这一重要问题上进行相互辅佐和参证。

403712.label: Realisation of objectives
403712.value: We have successfully constructed a convection chamber suitable for conducting moist convection experiment in which the moisture, pressure and temperature can be controlled and monitored. Heat transport measurements in moist convection are then carried out in this apparatus. A new feature of the present study is to conduct experiment under constant driving strength of the turbulent flow while varying the field variable controlling the condensation process, i.e. the difference between the saturation pressure at the condensation and evaporation regions respectively, and vice versa. As a result, new driving parameter, the difference between the vapor pressure in the condensation and evaporation regions, as been identified. We have studied the dynamics of droplets by tracking their motion using Particle Tracking Velocimetry (PTV) technique. We have studied the interactions of droplet with turbulent flows in a convective turbulence environment. We have studied heat transport in the presence of dry air, water vapor, water droplets and investigated the contribution of condensation/evaporation to the total heat transport. Droplet motions in two regions of the convective flow, i.e. the nearly homogeneous and isotropic core region and the plume-dominated sidewall region have been studied through visualization and PIV (particle image velocimetry) and PTV measurements.

403712.label: Major findings and research outcome
403712.value: Our first finding is that the presence of condensation/evaporation dominates heat transport in moist convection and that the presence of water vapor also greatly enhanced heat transfer comparing to the case of dry air alone. We also discovered that the presence of water droplets enhances both the turbulent level and flow strength of the flow field, as revealed by both PTV and PIV (particle image velocimetry) measurements. Another important finding is that the droplets tend to be expelled from the region of thermal plume (an important coherent structure in turbulent thermal convection). A new driving parameter, the difference between the vapor pressure in the condensation and evaporation regions, is identified; we further found that this quantity can be treated approximately as a passive scalar in the problem. Manuscripts reporting these findings are under preparation. We have found that the nature of thermal boundary conditions (i.e. whether it is fixed thermal flux or fixed temperature) plays an important role in the flow dynamics (i.e. flow strength, flow reversals and high order statistical properties) of turbulent thermal convection, in contrast to previously held views that there is little difference in terms of system response for these two different thermal boundary conditions. Our studied our revealed the phenomenon of condensation of coherent structures, i.e. the formation of giant (system sized) thermal plumes under geometrical confinement. This discovery has potential application in heat transport enhancement in microelectronic devices where highly restricted spaces are usually a hinderance of efficient heat transfer (i.e. cooling). Another finding is that under highly confinement geometries, the frequency flow reversals (a fascinating phenomenon that the large-scale coherent flow pauses momentarily and then restarts in the opposite circulation direction) increases dramatically. A phenomenological model has been proposed to include the role of corner rolls in the reversal process, which explained why changing aspect ratio has a strong effect on the flow reversal frequency. The geometrical confinement is also found to enhance turbulent mixing in the bulk of the flow system. Our study of the aspect-ratio dependence of the small-scale properties also reveals that the smallest dimension of the system serves as a cutoff scale of the Bolgiano length of system. The Bolgiano length separates the inertia- and buoyancy-dominated regimes in turbulent convection, i.e. buoyancy should be important above this scale and the energy cascade dynamics should follow a different law.

403712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403712.value: A future direction is to capture the individual droplet-droplet collision and merging process. We plan to construct a high magnification and long working distance special-purpose microscope to study this process, which is difficult to implement in real clouds but is extremely important in the study of cloud physics. High precision heat transport measurements will also be made to pinpoint the contributions of dry air, vapor and droplets separated in a moist convection environment.

403712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403712.value: Many important cloud phenomena are closely related to the microscale physics of cloud droplets. It is widely believed that turbulence plays an important role in the condensations of cloud droplets and the collisions among them (which lead to their coalescence and therefore formation of larger droplets). In the present study, we have shown how the thermally driven turbulent flows affect the droplet formation and dynamics and how they influence global transport of heat and momentum, and the role played by condensation/evaporation in moist convection. These results complement field measurements of droplet microphysics made in the atmospheric clouds.
