403912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403912.value: o-Carboryne (1,2-dehydro-o-carborane) is a three-dimensional relative of benzyne. We have recently developed a very efficient method for the generation of this reactive intermediate. Preliminary results show that o-carboryne can exist in two resonance forms, bonding form vs biradical form, which exhibit significantly different reactivity patterns. The bonding form can undergo a formal cycloinsertion reaction with anisoles to give eight-membered rings cyclooctatetraenocarboranes (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2010, 132, 9988–9989). On the other hand, the biradical form can insert regioselectively into α-C–H bond of aliphatic ethers, affording α-carboranylated ethers (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2011, 133, 5760–5763). Such a pair of reactions demonstrates that carboryne intermediates can serve as useful reagents for generating functionalized carboranes. On the basis of these preliminary data, we plan in this proposal to develop new methodologies for the generation of carborynes, to investigate systematically the reaction chemistry of carborynes, to understand the reaction mechanisms, and to develop new synthetic methodologies for functionalized carboranes. This research will largely expand the reaction scope of carborynes and enhance our basic understanding of the chemistry of carbon-boron clusters. It is also fascinating to discover what lies beyond. 碳硼炔（1,2-脫氫碳硼烷）是三維的苯炔類似物。我們研究小組最近發展了一個非常有效的方法以合成這個活性中間體, 初步研究結果表明碳硼炔可以以兩種共振態存在，一種是成鍵態，一種是雙自由基態。這兩種共振態的反應類型截然不同, 其中成鍵態的碳硼炔可以和苯甲醚類化合物發生形式上的環插入反應得到八元環的環辛四烯幷碳硼烷(J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2010, 132, 9988–9989); 而雙自由基態可以和烷基醚類發生區域選擇性的α-碳氫鍵插入反應，得到α-位被碳硼烷取代的醚類物質(J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2011, 133, 5760–5763)。這兩種對應的反應表明碳硼炔中間體是一類可用于碳硼烷官能團化的有效試劑。根據這些初步結果，我們在這份研究計劃裏打算發展合成碳硼炔中間體的新方法，系統地研究碳硼炔的反應化學幷瞭解反應機理，以及發展新的碳硼烷官能團化的方法。這項課題會極大地拓展碳硼炔的反應化學，幷且增進我們對碳硼簇化合物化學性質的基本理解。我們很期待去探索這些尚未瞭解的領域。

403912.label: Realisation of objectives
403912.value: o-Carboryne (1,2-dehydro-o-carborane) is a three-dimensional relative of benzyne, which was first reported in 1990 as a very reactive intermediate. It was generated by treatment of dilithiocarborane with one equivalent of bromine at low temperature, followed by a salt elimination of 1-bromo-2-lithiocarborane at the temperatures >0 oC. o-Carboryne was not isolable but was trapped by many unsaturated organic substrates. The reaction efficiency is generally low. To improve the reaction efficiency, we hypothesized to introduce the better leaving groups, such as iodide and trifluoromethanesulfonate, than bromide, facilitating the formation of o-carboryne. Subsequently, we found that 1-iodo-2-lithiocarborane and 1-OTf-2-lithiocarborane were much more efficient precursors than 1-bromo-2-lithiocarborane for the generation of o-carborynes via various control experiments. We then used o-carboryne as a synthon for the functionalization of o-carboranes. Several reactions were examined. Diels-Alder reaction of o-carboryne with 6,6’-diarylfulvenes gives a series of carboranonorbornadienes in moderate yields with excellent regioselectivity. The resultant [4+2] cycloadducts can be further derivatized, leading to the formation of a variety of highly functionalized carboranes. This work shows that such Diels-Alder reaction serves as a convenient method for the preparation of a new class of multi-functionalized o-carborane derivatives that may find applications in medicine and materials science. o-Carborynes can undergo -C–H insertion reaction with tertiary amines in the order of 1°>> 2°C–H, producing -carboranylated amines in very good regioselectivity and isolated yields. In this process, more acidic C–H bonds are favored. Mechanistic studies as well as DFT calculations suggest that the bonding-form of o-carboryne intermediate is involved in this reaction. This work represents another unique reactivity pattern of o-carboryne, which also serves as an efficient method for the generation of a series of aminoalkyl carboranes that might find applications in medicine and catalysis. Reaction of o-carboryne with N-protected indoles goes two ways: dearomative [2+2] cycloaddition and formal C–H insertion reaction, dependent upon the nature of N-substituents, leading to the synthesis of a series of carborane-functionalized indoles and indolines in a controlled manner. For N-TMS indoles, only dearomative [2+2] cycloaddition products are isolated, while the formal C–H insertion species are the sole products for N-alkyl ones. On the other hand, both [2+2] cycloaddition products and formal C–H insertion products are isolated if N-substituents are aryls, in which the molar ratios of two products are determined by electronic properties of substituents on phenyl ring. In general, electronic-donating substituents on N atom favor the formal C–H insertion reaction, whereas electronic-withdrawing groups promote dearomative [2+2] cycloaddition. To account for theses experimental observations, a stepwise reaction mechanism is proposed. This work represents the first example observed for indoles to have such [2+2] cycloaddition in the absence of transition metals or without light. Reaction of o-carboryne with nitrones affords, via a formal [5 + 2] cycloaddition, carborane-fused seven-membered heterocycles. In this process, nitrones serve as five-atom building units, which is very rare in the literature. Mechanistic studies as well as DFT calculations suggest that a sequence of [3 + 2] cycloaddition/N–O bond cleavage/oxygen migration/rearomatization leads to the final products. Such unprecedented reactivity pattern of nitrones may also find in other aromatic systems, which can stabilize both the resultant oxide anion and nitrenium ion. This study provides new insight into the chemistry of nitrones. The resultant carborane-fused dihydrobenzo[1,4]oxazepines may exhibit similar biological activities to their benzene analogs. On the other hand, we wondered if the closely related analogue of o-carboryne such as 1,3-dehydro-o-carborane could also be generated for the simultaneous functionalization of both cage C and B vertices. To this end, we reported the first example of 1,3-dehydro-o-carborane featuring a cage C–B multiple bonding character, which is successfully generated by treatment of 3-diazonium-o-carborane tetrafluoroborate with non-nucleophilic bases. It undergoes Diels-Alder reaction with arenes to give [4 + 2] cycloadducts, in which electronic factor governs the regioselectivity. Meanwhile, for arenes bearing benzylic C-H bonds, highly regioselective aromatic ene reaction was also observed with the product ratio of [4 + 2] cycloaddtion over ene reaction depending on the number of benzylic protons. 1,3-dehydro-o-carborane can readily react with a series of alkenes and alkynes, providing a general, high yielding synthesis of B(3)-alkenyl/allenyl carboranes with excellent regioselectivity. Ene reactions are dominant in these processes, which can be ascribed to the highly polarized cage C–B multiple bond of 1,3-dehydro-o-carborane. The results reveal that the hydrogen shift in the ene reaction is a proton transfer in nature. These results suggest that 1,3-dehydro-o-carborane is best described as a resonance hybrid of a bonding form and a zwitterionic form. Thus, it shares some chemical properties with those of o-carboryne; on the other hand, it also has its own unique properties due mainly to the polarized cage C–B bond. This work demonstrates that 1,3-dehydro-o-carborane is a useful synthon for simultaneous cage C,B-functionalization of o-carboranes. We have developed several new and efficient precursors to both 1,2-dehydro-o-carboranes and 1,3-dehydro-o-carboranes and systematically studied their synthetic applications as useful synthons in the functionalization of o-carboranes. The resultant functionalized o-carboranes may find applications in medicine, catalysis and materials. All objectives have been realized.

403912.label: Major findings and research outcome
403912.value: (1) Several new and efficient carboryne precursors were prepared and fully characterized. Their reactivity patterns were examined. They can undergo [4+2] cycloaddition reactions (Diels-Alder reaction) to give a series of carborane-fused cyclics in very good yields with excellent regioselectivity. The resultant [4+2] cycloadducts can be further derivatized, leading to the formation of a variety of highly functionalized carboranes. This work shows that such Diels-Alder reaction serves as a convenient method for the preparation of a new class of multi-functionalized o-carborane derivatives (Pubs #8 and #9). (2) Carborynes can undergo [2+2] and [5+2] cycloaddition as well as C-H insertion reactions to afford a large class of carborane-functionalized heterocycles for possible applications in medicine and materials science. Their reaction mechanisms were studied both experimentally and theoretically. The similarities and differences between carborynes and benzynes were also investigated via reactions with different substrates. The results indicated that carborynes and benzynes share many chemical properties and, on the other hand, carborynes have the unique features of their own owing to the three-dimensional cage structure of carborynes (Pubs #10, #11, #12 and #13). (3) The resultant functionalized carboranes are good ligands for transition metals. As a results, a series of metallacarboranes and supercarboranes were prepared and fully characterized. Their reaction chemistry was investigated (Pubs #1 to #5, and #7 ). (4) The findings of this research project have been summarized in two invited review articles (Pub #6 and #14). In summary, this original work has resulted in 14 peer-reviewed articles published in international chemistry journals including JACS (x 3), Angew Chem Int Ed (x 2), Chem Euro J (x 1), Chem Commun (x 2), Inorg. Chem (x 1), Dalton trans (x 2), ChemPlusChem (x 1), J. Organomet. Chem (x1) and Coord Chem Rev (x 1). PI was invited to give one keynote and two invited lectures at international conferences. Three PhD students were trained, one of which (Dr. ZHAO Da) was awarded Springer Thesis Award.

403912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403912.value: 1,3-Dehydro-o-carborane is a brand new reactive intermediate, which has demonstrated as useful synthon for the simultaneous functionalization of both cage C and B vertices. We plan to continue working on its reaction chemistry and develop other types of carborynes such as 3,4-dehydro-o-carborane and 1,3,2,4-Dehydro-o-carborane.

403912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403912.value: Icosahedral carboranes constitute a class of structurally unique molecules with exceptionally thermal and chemical stabilities and the ability to hold various substituents. These properties have made them as useful basic units in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) agents, in supramolecular design, and in organometallic chemistry. On the other hand, these properties also make the functionalization of carboranes difficult. As a result, only limited methodologies for the derivatization of these clusters are known. To this end, we developed, in this research, several new and efficient precursors to both 1,2-dehydro-o-carboranes and 1,3-dehydro-o-carboranes and systematically studied their synthetic applications as useful synthons in the functionalization of o-carboranes. The resultant functionalized o-carboranes may find applications in medicine, catalysis and materials. This research features extensively in the synthesis of various carborane-containing molecules which may have potential applications and enhance our basic understanding of the carbon-boron clusters chemistry.

404012.label: Project Objectives
404012.value: For I(a), a solution has been absent for long in the literature. The intrinsic difficulties are a priori determination of the joint distribution of the underlying multivariate risks and the inherent mathematical complexity, and we shall overcome these by formulating a nonstandard (non-convex) saddle point problem through which, by combining a recently developed geometric methods by P.I. with a possibly modified application of minimax theorem, we may obtain a large nonlinear generalization of major results in optimal capital allocation theory considered by Dhaene et al. (2002), Meilijson and Nadas (1979), and Rüschendorf (2005). For I(b), a major mathematical difficulty is its non-smooth and non-convex nature as an optimization problem in co-operative game theory. We expect to apply a refined Lagrangian duality approach (recently developed by P.I.) together with hard analysis arguments to seek for an explicit optimal solution. For I(c), we shall consider a Principal-Agent problem in which the reinsurer aims to maximize the average profit by selling tailor-made reinsurances to a huge number of insurers via adverse selection. Being an extensive and completely new generalization of V@R-based reinsurance decision problems (see references listed in Part II), the present problem is a large-scale and complex mathematical question. A duality approach, recently adopted by Carlier et al. (2007) and Horst and Moreno-Bromberg (2008), will naturally lead to a multivariate indirect utility (IU) that is hardly to be directly dealt with if not mathematically intractable; fortunately, an application of geometric methods stated in I(a) with a change-of-variable technique may possibly reduce the corresponding IU into a univariate one that could lead to a complete resolution. For II(i), due to the mathematical complexity of the resulting variational inequality formulation, the study of NZS SD reinsurance games has been missing for long in the literature not to mention over the regime-switching context. We shall study a class of NZS games in which each insurer maximizes the difference of the opponent's terminal surplus from that of his own by dynamically arranging his reinsurance schedule. In contrast to the traditional HJB approach, we aim to develop a hybrid approach invoking both variational inequalities and BSDE techniques (see El Karoui et al. (1997) and Hu et al. (2005)), without the standard restriction on the convexity of the feasible control set, to explicitly establish the Nash equilibrium and the corresponding value processes. For II(ii), because of the dramatic growth of individual investor population, an urgent need of in-depth understanding of collective strategic interactive behaviors of a huge group of investors by using mean field games is crucial in financial risk management. We shall study Linear-Quadratic MFGs that are an organic combination of the classical Linear-Quadratic Stochastic Control Problems and SDGs. The mildest condition leading to the unique existence of both the optimal control and value function of a LQMFG will be identified by developing a hybrid method combining adjoint equation approach and BSDE techniques; numerical study will be carried out to explore consequences of LQMFGs on financial game problems for mean-variance agents.

404012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404012.value: 最近的金融海嘯提醒我們，在現代競爭激烈的金融市場除了尋求豐厚的利潤，確保可行的風險管理策略也是有著最根本的重要性。由於所涉及的複雜數學結構和規模, 大部分相應的技術問題還未得到解答. 正如Saari (1995). Notice AMS，42(2），頁222-230）所說： “......在經濟學入門課程（和金融）中即使是簡單的模型, 都可以遠比在古典物理學或生物學中出現的數學動態行為為之複雜得多，而在社會科學中類似的複雜問題是很常見，亦由於此開發新的數學工具亦變得非常重要......” 在這些問題中，其中有二是最急切需要解決：（一）在多因素影響下, 如在有逆向選擇，非合作博弈等市場機制下, 決定風險最小的保險;（二）在一般保險或財務市場機制下, 制定有效動態管理策略。 在這一研究項目中，我們計劃解決幾個關鍵的長期未解的數學問題: 主題(1): 利用近年風險度量理論, 重新審視最優再保險決策，如：(a) 設計最低風險的再保險; (b）根據BASEL協議, 確定最優風險分擔的保險和再保險; (c) 在有逆向選擇機制下的市場, 確定V@R最少的再保險政策。主題(2):研究兩個通常出現在企業風險管理中的非零和隨機微分方程遊戲：（一）保險公司之間的非零和遊戲，而其中風險擴散過程擁有混合狀態轉換係數;（二）一群團體的平均場遊戲，其中每位成員都有一個線性的行為以及二次邊際考慮。而這兩個問題都不可視為標準的隨機控制問題。 整體來說，我們的研究目標將在以下研究課題有所貢獻：非線性泛函分析，非線性拉格朗日對偶理論，最優運送方法，變分不等式的理論, 倒向隨機微分方程理論。我們的預期結果（1）提供一些在多元風險管理中持久問題的完整解決方案;（2）推進現有的非零和隨機微分方程遊戲理論; 及（3）通過使用幾近明確的表達式, 開發出一些創新有效的數值近似方法.

404012.label: Realisation of objectives
404012.value: For Objective 1: The objective is accomplished with even more extensions as stated as below. a) In [2], we study the problem of optimal reinsurance policy for multivariate risks under the realm of general law invariant convex risk measures. It is often difficult to determine the actual dependence structure of these risks. Instead of assuming any particular dependence structure, we propose the minimax optimal reinsurance decision formulation in which the worst case scenario is first identified. We then establish that the stop-loss reinsurances are optimal in the sense that they minimize a general law-invariant convex risk measure of the total retained risk. Tricks together with applications of minimax theorem, explicit form of and sufficient condition for ordering the optimal deductibles are also obtained. b) By using the method developed in (a) for the present objective together with Breeden–Litzenberger type integral representation formula for increasing convex functions and the theory of comonotonicity, in [1], we revisit the classical Borch Theorem on the characterization of Pareto optimal risk exchange treaties under the expected utility paradigm. c) In another work [8], using the method developed in (b) for the present objective, we revisit the problem of minimizing a separable convex function with a linear constraint and box constraints. We present a new approach of solving this constrained minimization problem explicitly by using the theory of comonotonicity. For Objective 2: The objective is accomplished. In [3], we study the optimal reinsurance decision problem in which the Average Value-at-Risk of the retained loss is minimized under Wang’s premium principle and is also subject to either (1) a budget constraint on reinsurance premium, or (2) a reinsurer’s probabilistic benchmark constraint of his potential loss. The optimal reinsurance is a single insurance layer under Constraint (1), and a cap insurance or a double-insurance layer under Constraint (2); moreover, under Constraint (2), we further establish that under most common circumstances (see Remark after Theorem 3 in [3]), a cap insurance will be optimal. Finally, some numerical illustrations have been provided. Through the course of study, which was smooth that warranted our fast first publication, a refined Lagrangian duality approach with some tricks from hard analysis has been developed to provide with a very simple and illuminating solution. Further technological extension was used to tackle another problem in [14]. For Objective 3: The objective is accomplished with extensions of the method used to resolve two more unconventional optimal insurance problems. In [9], we follow the seminal works in economics (e.g. Landsberger and Meilijson (1999), Mirrlees (1971), Rochet and Chon/’e (1998), Rothschild and Stiglitz (1976) and Stiglitz (1977)) to use the Principal-Agent (multidimensional screening) models (also see Laffont and Martimort (2001)) to study a monopolistic reinsurance market with adverse selection and absence of arbitrage opportunity; instead of adopting the classical expected utility paradigm, the novelty of our work is to model the risk preference of each insurer (agent) by his Value-at-Risk at his own chosen risk tolerance level consistent with Solvency II. Under information asymmetry, the reinsurer (principal) aims to maximize his average profit by designing an optimal policy provision (menu) of ‘shirt-fit’ reinsurance contracts for every insurer with hidden characteristics from a ‘huge’ (continuum) family. Because of the non-convex nature of Value-at-Risk as a risk functional, a non-standard approach via indirect utility function originated from Optimal Transport Theory has been developed. We first establish the nonexistence of the optimal solution among all feasible menus of reinsurance contracts, and hence the non-optimality of the first-best strategy. The same Principal-Agent problem is then completely solved for the following commonly encountered subclasses of reinsurances: (i) stop-loss; (ii) quota-share; and (iii) reinsurance contracts with convex indemnity; in general, we conclude that the reinsurer will normally discriminate the insurers into two groups (of high or low profile) according to their risk tolerance levels, which agrees with the key conclusion found in the seminal works aforementioned in the classical expected utility setting. Extensions of the method developed are used to resolve two unconventional optimal insurance decision problems under behavioral financial framework in [12,13]. For Objective 4: The objective is accomplished. In [4], we provide a systematic study on the non-zero-sum stochastic differential investment and reinsurance game between two insurance companies. Each insurance company’s surplus process consists of a proportional reinsurance protection and an investment in risky and risk-free assets. Each insurance company is assumed to maximize his utility of the difference between his terminal surplus and that of his competitor. The surplus process of each insurance company is modeled by a mixed regime-switching Cramer–Lundberg diffusion approximation process, i.e. the coefficients of the diffusion risk processes are modulated by a continuous-time Markov chain and an independent market-index process. Correlation between the two surplus processes, independent of the risky asset process, is allowed. Despite the complex structure, we manage to solve the resulting non-zero sum game problem by applying the dynamic programming principle. The Nash equilibrium, the optimal reinsurance/investment, and the resulting value processes of the insurance companies are obtained in closed forms, together with sound economic interpretations, for the case of an exponential utility function. Our result obtained here provides the foundational one in the field, which has been absent for long in the literature. The methods developed is further used to solve a few more unconventional problems in portfolio management in [15,16,17]. For Objective 5: The proposed objective complete, which also results in a book, and a number of extensions have been accepted in top-tier journals. a) A book [7], essentially the first research monograph on the mean field game theory, has been written and published in the leading scientific publisher, Springer Verlag. b) In [5], we study a class of time-inconsistent analogs (in the sense of Hu et al. (2012)) which is originated from the mean-variance portfolio selection problem with state-dependent risk aversion in the context of financial economics) of the standard Linear-Quadratic Mean Field Games considered in Huang et al. (2007). c) In [10], we provide a comprehensive study of the linear-quadratic mean field games via the adjoint equation approach; although the problem has been considered in the literature by Huang, Caines and Malham´e (HCM, 2007a), their method is based on Dynamic Programming. It turns out that two methods are not equivalent, as far as giving sufficient condition for the existence of a solution is concerned. Due to the linearity of the adjoint equations, the optimal mean field term satisfies a linear forward-backward ordinary differential equation. As a by-product, we also establish a neat and instructive sufficient condition for the unique existence of the solution for a class of non-trivial nonsymmetric Riccati equations. Numerical examples of non-existence of the equilibrium strategy and the comparison of HCM’s approach have also been provided. Further numerical method is developed which can be extended to resolve some other problems in actuarial science [18]. d) In [11], we consider mean field games between a dominating player and a group of representative agents, each of the agents acts similarly and also interacts with each other through a mean field term being substantially influenced by the dominating player. e) In [6], we provide an alternative approach, based on mean-field theory, on establishing the pre-commitment optimal solution to the continuous time mean-variance portfolio selection problem, and this opens up a new direction of potential application of mean field theory for non-canonical mean field problems.

404012.label: Major findings and research outcome
404012.value: (I) The Principal Investigator participated in five major international conferences and invited talks on actuarial and mathematical finance over the granting period: 1) 17th International Congress on Insurance: Mathematics and Economics, July 2013, in Copenhagen, Denmark. 2) Stochastic Dynamics in Economics and Finance, June 2013, hosted by Hausdorff Institute of Mathematics, University of Bonn, Bonn, Germany 3) 8th World Congress of the Bachelier Finance Society, June 2014, in Brussels, Belgium 4) IMS Annual Meeting 2014, July 2014, in Sydney, Australia 5) SIAM: Conference on Financial Mathematics and Engineering, Nov 2014, in Chicago, USA. Some obtained or preliminary results and accepted works in top tier peer-reviewed journals had been disseminated in these conference talks. For the referencing as stated below, the numbers are referred as those listed in Part C. i) 1 book/research monograph [7] on mean field games has been published by the leading scientific publisher in mathematics, engineering and finance, Springer Verlag. ii) 14 papers [1-5, 10-18] have been published in the top-tier journals in actuarial science, insurance, mathematical finance, optimization and control theory, for example, in IME, JRI, Astin Bulletin, Auotmatica, SIFIN, EJOR. iii) 1 paper [6] has been published in a proceeding after a conference co-organized by University of Tokyo and Tokyo Metropolitan University, Japan. iv) 2 more papers [8, 9] are now under review. The major findings and research outcome have been briefly described in Section 5.3 as above. Our obtained results provide complete solutions to some lasting problems in multivariate risk management, make a marked progress in advancing the existing theory of NSZ SDGs, and build up a systematic approach and some effective numerical schemes for calibrating more tailor-made reinsurances and strategic risk managing analytic quantities. There should be some significant impact brought by my present research project, such as the book [7] written, it is well received in the academic community with the following book review comments from Mathematical Reviews: “This brief monograph is a presentation of some aspects of MFG theory and of a related class of problems, called mean field type control, where the state of the control system is driven by a McKean-Vlasov equation, namely, a stochastic differential equation where the drift depends also on the distribution of the state itself. … I believe the book should be mandatory reading for all mathematicians and engineers working in the field of MFG and related topics.” (Martino Bardi, Mathematical Reviews, November, 2014)

404012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404012.value: Successful accomplishment of all the objectives in our project relies on notable advancements, made by us over the course of study, on the following disciplines: nonlinear functional analysis, nonlinear Lagrangian duality from theory of optimal transport, variational inequalities, and theory of BSDEs and FBSDEs. We shall continue to work on some newly formulated problems originated from our own study. In particular, being germinated from this project, my work in mean field games and mean field control theory is getting matured while my recent research outputs and my book play a dominant position in the related working community, indeed. Another GRF research grant purely based on mean field theory has been recently awarded to me in the 2015/16 exercise, which will facilitate to deepen my research in the area. Besides, I am now writing for another GRF grant proposal for 2017/18 exercise, and this bases on my thorough and original understanding on the theory of BSDEs and FBSDEs after working through the present project. More specifically, we shall propose to involve more use of some infinite dimensional functional analytic techniques, such as Malliavin Calculus, to establish the global existence theory of a broad class neither of Lipschitz nor of quadratic growth BSDEs.

404012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404012.value: In this project, we resolved several longstanding mathematical problems in insurance and finance under two themes: (I) deciding a risk-minimizing protection (e.g. through reinsurance-buying) against multivariate risks under various forms of market mechanism (e.g. via adverse selection, under co-operative or non-cooperative game settings); (II) formulating dynamic managerial strategies for a corporation against his competitors in industrial sectors. Under Theme I, we revisited the optimal reinsurance decision problems in virtue of recent risk-measure-based risk management such as: (a) design of risk-minimizing reinsurances for multivariate risks; (b) determination of optimal risk-sharing between insurer and reinsurer in light of Basel Capital Accord; (c) calibration of V@R-minimizing reinsurance policy provision, via adverse selection, specific to each insurer with hidden characteristics. Under Theme II, we studied two classes of non-zero sum (NZS) stochastic differential games (SDGs) arisen in corporate risk management: (i) reinsurance games between insurers with each of their diffusion risk processes possessing mixed regime-switching modulated coefficients; (ii) mean field games for a continuum of players so that each of them accomplishes his own decision-making by also considering the accumulative effect of marginal impacts from all other players both in a linear-quadratic sense. Both problems cannot be treated by the standard stochastic control method.

404112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404112.value: Photocatalysis is a promising technique for solving energy and environmental problems. This technology can generate a clean hydrogen fuel from water. It can also degrade pollutants in the environment. The most widely used photocatalytic material is titanium dioxide powders. Unfortunately, pure TiO2 powders require UV excitation. They are therefore not effective under sunlight irradiation. A much more efficient material, TiO2 nanotube array, will be used in this study. This advanced material will be further enhanced by forming a composite with graphene quantum dots. A solar-driven photocatalyst with excellent activity will no longer be a dream. With remarkable electron mobility and high specific surface area, graphene can act as an efficient electron acceptor in a composite photocatalyst. The proposed graphene quantum dots/titanium dioxide nanotube arrays composite photocatalyst will be prepared by electrochemical methods. Their physical and chemical properties will be studied, and mechanisms for the enhanced water splitting and pollutant degradation abilities will be proposed. This project will shed light on the future design of broad-spectral-response photocatalysts for solar-driven applications. 納米光催化材料在解決日益嚴重的能源危機及環境污染問題中具有巨大應用潛力。光催化可以生產出氫氣作為綠色清潔能源，光催化也可以有效分解環境中的污染物。二氧化鈦納米粉是目前使用最為廣泛的光催化材料，但過窄的光譜利用範圍仍是其所面臨的主要問題。本研究將充分借助石墨烯量子點的優異特性，製備出石墨烯量子點/二氧化鈦納米管陣列複合光催化材料，從而構築出更高可見光活性的新型光催化體系。

404112.label: Realisation of objectives
404112.value: All the project objectives were achieved. Graphene quantum dot-sensitized TiO2 nanotube arrays (TNAs/GQDs) were synthesized by covalently coupling these two materials. Highly ordered TNAs were fabricated by an anodic oxidation approach. Ethylene glycol (99+%)containing 0.5 wt % NH4F and 2.0 wt % deionized (DI) water was used as electrolyte. Ti foil (2 cm × 3 cm) was used as a working electrode, and a Pt foil (1 cm × 1 cm) served as a counter electrode. GQDs were synthesized from graphene oxide (GO) by heating with a solution of hydrogen peroxide and ammonia. To make GQDs/TNAs, TNAs were firstly immersed in 0.2 wt % (3-aminopropyl)trimethoxysilane (APTMS) in toluene for 3 h, rinsed with toluene and dried. The modified TNAs were then immersed in a beaker containing a solution of GQDs (1 mg·mL−1), ethyl(dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide (EDC) and N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS) for 4 h. The foils were then sonicated in DI water, rinsed with DI water and dried in air. The product was characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectrometry(FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and UV–vis absorption spectroscopy. The product exhibited high photocatalytic performance in the photodegradation of methylene blue and enhanced photocurrent under visible light irradiation. Cabon and nitrogen doping into TNAs/GQDs was also explored. These new photocatalysts were tested not only for their effectiveness on the degradation of organics but also for their potential use in disinfection. We also applied the same approach to enhanced the photocatalytic activity of red phosphorus with GQDs. The composite of graphene quantum dots and red phosphorus was fabricated by a mechanical ball milling method. The ball milling process resulted in particle size reduction and graphene quantum dot deposition at the same time. The composite retained the amorphous nature of red phosphorus, but it became more hydrophilic as shown by the more negative surface potential in water. Moreover, the composite exhibited excellent photocatalytic activity under visible light irradiation. This work may provide inspiration for further chemical modification of red phosphorus-based photocatalysts. While conducting the literature search for this project, we have collected a lot of inforamtion on the graphene enhanced photocatalytic systems. This cumulated in a book chapter "Graphene-based Photocatalysts for Energy Applications: Progress and Prospects," Chapter 9 in Graphene-based Energy Devices, Ed: A. Rashid bin Mohd Yusoff, pp. 277-294, Wiley-VCH, Weinheim, Germany, 2015. (ISBN: 978-3-527-33806-1)

404112.label: Major findings and research outcome
404112.value: A new visible-light-driven photocatalyst was fabricated by covalently bonding GQDs onto amine-modified TNAs. The GQDs/TNAs composite retains the highly ordered nanotube morphology and well crystallized anatase phase. The high visible light photocatalytic activity could be attributed to photosensitization of TNAs by GQDs. This research shows the potential of GQD-based photocatalysts for visible-light-driven photocatalytic and photoelectrochemical applications. Experimental details are given in our 2014 publication in Beilstein Journal of Nanotechnology. We have also added GQDs to other photocatalysts including red phosphorus. A mechanical ball milling method was applied to reduce the size of red P and to deposit graphene quantum dots onto red P. The product was characterized by scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, contact angle measurements, zeta-potential measurements, X-ray diffraction and UV-vis absorption spectroscopy. The product exhibited high visible-light-driven photocatalytic performance in the photodegradation of rhodamine B. This work has been accepted for publication in Journal of Environmental Sciences.

404112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404112.value: The GQDs/TNAs composite may also be used for the reduction of carbon dioxide. The Ph.D. student working for this project have investigated a mesoporous Bi2O3/TiO2 system for photocatalytic carbon dioxide conversion. Preliminary results on the GQDs/TNAs system look encouraging. However, the efficiency of this artificial photosynthesis approach would need to be improved.

404112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404112.value: Graphene has attracted tremendous research interest since its discovery. The smallest graphene material of all is graphene quantum dots (GQDs). GDQs are layered graphene with lateral dimensions smaller than 100 nm. They possess interesting optical and electronic properties due to quantum confinement and edge effects. TiO2 nanotube arrays are well-known efficient UV-driven photocatalysts. The incorporation of graphene quantum dots could extend the photo-response of the nanotubes to the visible-light range because GQDs show a broad absorption from 400 nm to 600 nm. The composite material allows more efficient harvesting of solar energy. This research would shed light on the future development of sunlight-driven photocatalysis.

404212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404212.value: In this proposal we aim to develop simple and reliable methods of preparing polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) foam in situ in microfluidic devices and to apply PDMS foam to integrated microfluidics and cell affinity chromatography. Two types of PDMS foam will be prepared: the foam with closed pores and the foam with interconnected pores. The PDMS foam with closed pores will be prepared by the method of gas foaming. In this method, porogen agent will be impregnated into the PDMS pre-polymer. During the incubation period at elevated temperature, the porogen will decompose into gaseous product, generating closed pores inside PDMS. The PDMS foam with interconnected pores will be prepared by emulsification method. In this method, the PDMS precursor is dispersed in water to form emulsion. During the incubation, PDMS droplets will be solidified into PDMS particles and aggregate to form the PDMS foam. The application of the PDMS foam will be illustrated in two aspects: integrated microfluidics and cell affinity chromatography. In integrated microfluidics, three applications of the PDMS foam will be illustrated. First, a portable and stable vacuum pump will be produced using degassed PDMS foam. The pump requires no electricity and will be especially important for point-of-care testing with poorly resourced health care facilities. Second, a PDMS foam based passive mixer in the microfluidic device will be fabricated. Mixing is expected to be enhanced by passing the streams through the PDMS foam. Third, a reliable nanoliter dispensing and reaction system will be established by integrating PDMS foam in microwells. In cell affinity chromatography, the PDMS foam with interconnected pores will be used as the stationary phase. The PDMS pore surface will be chemically modified to immobilize specific protein ligand. The cell affinity chromatography using the PDMS foam will be validated by separating a mixture of Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Escherichia coli cells. 本課題的目的是發展簡單可靠的方法製備聚二甲基矽氧烷泡沫乳膠，以及將這種泡沫應用于集成微流器件和色譜分離。要製備的聚二甲基矽氧烷泡沫有兩種：不連孔的泡沫乳膠，和連孔的泡沫乳膠。 不連孔的泡沫乳膠將採用起泡法製備。起泡劑將被摻入到聚二甲基矽氧烷的前體中。在交聯聚合的過程中，起泡劑產生氣泡，生成不相連的小孔。 連孔的泡沫乳膠將採用乳劑法製備。聚二甲基矽氧烷的前體與水混合製成乳劑。在交聯的過程中，聚二甲基矽氧烷液滴逐漸固化成顆粒，并進一步聚集成泡沫乳膠。 聚二甲基矽氧烷泡沫乳膠的應用將從以下兩個方面驗證：集成微流器件和細胞親和色譜分離。 在集成微流器件方面，聚二甲基矽氧烷泡沫乳膠將應用於三個例子。首先，脫氣聚二甲基矽氧烷泡沫乳膠將被用於製作一個便攜穩定的真空泵。這個真空泵無需電力，尤其適用於沒有充足醫療資源的現場護理。其次，聚二甲基矽氧烷泡沫乳膠將被用於製作一個被動的微流混合器。液體通過聚二甲基矽氧烷泡沫乳膠時混合的效率會大幅提高。最後，一個基於聚二甲基矽氧烷泡沫乳膠的可靠的納升級液體灌輸和反應體系將建立。 在細胞色譜分離方面，連孔的聚二甲基矽氧烷泡沫乳膠將被用於建造固定相。聚二甲基矽氧烷孔表面用化學修飾固定住特異性蛋白。細胞色譜方法將採用分離酵母細胞和大腸桿菌細胞的混合溶液來驗證。

404212.label: Realisation of objectives
404212.value: Objective 1 was successfully achieved. We developed two different strategies for making PDMS foam: the application of pore-forming agent and the usage of template. Both strategies led to PDMS foam in the microfluidic channels as expected, but with different advantages and disadvantages. In the first strategy, both (NH4)2CO3 and NH4HCO3 were valid pore-forming agent. The method was simple, however, the resulting PDMS foam was not homogeneous in terms of pore size distribution throughout the cross section area. There was an edge effect, i.e., the interface between the liquid PDMS pre-polymer and the solid channel wall inhibited pore formation. Therefore, this strategy is not applicable for small microchannels with the diameter less than 10 microns. In the second strategy, micron-sized glass bubbles were used as the template. The liquid PDMS prepolymer filled the space in the assembly of glass bubbles or sugar gains and crossed linked to form the PDMS foam. The template materials were easily removed afterwards. This strategy involves more steps than the first one, however, the pore size can be controlled and the foam formation is not affected by the interfaces. In the proposal we also suggested emulsion strategy. In the experiment it did not produce reliable results, probably due to the difficulty of controlling the emulsion formation. Therefore, in the following works we used mostly the template strategy in producing the PDMS foam. Objective 2 was successfully achieved. We demonstrated an enhanced passive pump based on degassed PDMS foam and an effective microchannel mixer based on PDMS foam integrated microchannel. The passive pump using degassed PDMS foam presented similar power with the previous passive pumps we developed, however, the lifetime of the pump was substantially increased to hours. Such long-lifetime passive pumps are useful in bioanalysis using microfluidic devices and in point-of-care clinical diagnosis. We characterized the performance of the PDMS foam based microchannel mixer. However, the measurement of rapid kinetics in this microchannel mixer was difficult due to the unknown relationship between the reaction time and fluid travelling distance in the mixer. Finally, we demonstrated the microwell-based platform for screening protein crystallization. The microwell contains the rehydratable gel which was supported by the PDMS foam. The platform was more robust in operation than our previous pure-liquid containing microwells. Objective 3 was successfully achieved. We fabricated the column containing the PDMS foam and immobilize enzymes on the inner surface of the PDMS foam. E. coli and yeast cells were used to test the performance of the cell chromatography using the column. The method worked on separating e. coli from yeast cells. We also demonstrated a second application of the column containing the PDMS foam as a tool in continuous protein digestion, which was widely used in proteomics research and in protein analysis.

404212.label: Major findings and research outcome
404212.value: We developed a simple and robust method of making monolith PDMS foam using glass bubbles as the templates (B. Liu, and B. Zheng, manuscript in preparation). We substantially improved the lifetime of the passive PDMS pump by using the newly developed PDMS foam. This passive pump was used in the studies on the enzyme assay (Biomicrofluidics, 2013, 7, 54116) and on the kinetics of chemical oscillators (J. Phys. Chem. A, 2013, 117, 6402; ChemPhysChem, 2016, 17, 2355). We applied the PDMS foam to assist the loading and storage of reagents in the microwell system for high throughput screening of protein crystallization conditions (Micromachines, 2015, 6, 1629). We greatly enhanced the protein digestion efficiency by using the protease immobilized PDMS foam as the column (B. Liu, and B. Zheng, manuscript in preparation). Two students obtained their PhD for their work on this project. Deyong Zhu studied the formation of double emulsion in the microfluidic devices and the application in protein crystallization. Dameng Guo studied chemical reaction kinetics in the microfluidic devices, in which the continuous supply of the reactant reagents was driven by the PDMS foam based passive pump. Research collaboration has been established based on the research works. We are collaborating with Professor Liming Bian of Department of Mechanical and Automation Engineering of CUHK to work on enhancing the proliferation of stem cells using the PDMS foam as the substrate. We are working with Professor Yong-Qing Fu of Northumbria University to integrate surface acoustic wave into the microfluidic devices for controlling the movement and position of micron-sized particles.

404212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404212.value: The PDMS foam has great potential in cell affinity chromatographic. We plan to increase the pore size of the PDMS foam to about 100 microns, so that large mammal cells can easily pass through the PDMS foam. We will use large glass bubbles to achieve the desired pore size. The PDMS foam based passive pump also has potential in driving the reagent flow in lateral flow immunoassay. The passive pump is capable of provide a stable flow rate for tens of minutes, which is needed for semi-quantitative and quantitative analysis using lateral flow immunoassay. If validated, the new immunoassay platform will be useful in point-of-care diagnosis for patient to perform the test at home.

404212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404212.value: In this project we used micron-sized particles as the template to produce a new foam made of transparent rubber. The pores in the foam had the diameter of a few microns, and the pores were interconnected so that liquid can flow through the foam freely. We used this foam to build a passive pump. The pump can drive the liquid flow without external energy input for tens of minutes. We used this pump in several research works on kinetics measurement in micro-reactors. We used this foam to assist loading and storage of reagents in microwells. In this way, proteins were crystallized successfully by combining two such microwells containing the protein solution and the precipitant, respectively. The PDMS foam greatly improved the reliability of the performance of the microwell platform. We used this foam to digest proteins, which is an essential step in analyzing proteins using mass spectrometry. The efficiency of the protein digestion was significantly higher than the traditional solution digestion.

404412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404412.value: This project studies open Gromov-Witten theory and how it can be applied to further our understanding of Mirror Symmetry. Mirror Symmetry is a deep and mysterious equivalence between the geometries of certain pairs of spaces. Since its discovery in the early 1990s, Mathematicians have been trying hard to understand the secret mechanism behind Mirror Symmetry. In 1996, Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed a ground-breaking and beautiful geometric explanation for Mirror Symmetry. They conjecture that mirror Calabi-Yau (CY) manifolds should admit dual Lagrangian torus fibrations and Mirror Symmetry works as a generalized Fourier transform. Quantum corrections such as open and closed Gromov-Witten (GW) invariants play a vital role in the study of this Strominger-Yau-Zaslow (SYZ) conjecture and Mirror Symmetry. In this project, the PI aims at a more solid understanding of Mirror Symmetry via an in depth study of quantum corrections. A key and essential step is to understand the intricate relations between mirror maps and quantum corrections. Mirror maps lie at the heart of Mirror Symmetry because they serve as bridges connecting mirror spaces. Enumerative predictions cannot be made without mirror maps. Works of Fukaya, Kontsevich-Soibelman and Gross-Siebert have indicated that mirror maps for CY manifolds are intimately related to quantum corrections such as open and closed GW invariants. One main objective of this project is to carry out a thorough study of the geometry of mirror maps using these invariants, building on previous works of the PI. One of our goals is to establish precise formulas relating mirror maps to those invariants. This will significantly improve our understanding of the geometry of Mirror Symmetry for CY manifolds. On the other hand, Mirror Symmetry for non-CY manifolds has received much attention recently. Fukaya, Oh, Ohta and Ono defined open GW invariants and studied Mirror Symmetry for compact toric manifolds by applying their big machinery of Lagrangian Floer theory. Before this, Batyrev, Givental and Lian-Liu-Yau have established Mirror Theorems for these manifolds and verified various Mirror Symmetry predictions. A relation between these two approaches, which will no doubt give us a much deeper insight into Mirror Symmetry for non-CY manifolds, is desirable but missing. The PI has done preliminary work in this direction. Based on this, the PI plans to start exploring the link between the Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono and Batyrev/Givental/Lian-Liu-Yau approaches in order to better understand Mirror Symmetry for non-CY manifolds and broaden its scope. 本項目研究開格羅莫夫-威滕理論，以及它在鏡對稱的應用。 鏡對稱是一個深邃而神秘的對偶現象，它預測兩個空間之間不同幾何的等價性。在20世紀90年代初被發現以來，數學家一直致力了解鏡對稱背後的神秘機制。在1996年，Strominger，丘成桐和Zaslow提出一個突破性而且漂亮的猜想去解釋鏡對稱的幾何。他們推測，一對鏡對稱卡拉比-丘（CY）流形應該有對偶的拉格朗日圓環纖維結構，而且鏡對稱應該是一個廣義傅立葉變換。在Strominger-Yau-Zaslow（SYZ）猜想和鏡對稱的研究中，量子修正如開和閉格羅莫夫-威滕（GW）不變量起著至關重要的作用。 在這個項目中，PI的目的是通過對量子修正的研究對鏡對稱作一個更深入的理解。關鍵和重要的一步是了解鏡映像和量子修正之間的複雜關係。鏡映像作為連接鏡對稱空間的橋樑，是鏡對稱研究的核心課題。 Fukaya，Kontsevich-Soibelman和Gross-Siebert的研究顯示鏡映像與量子修正如開和閉GW不變量是有密切關係的。這個項目的主要目的之一是使用這些不變量對鏡映像的幾何進行徹底的探討，我們的目標是建立一個連繫鏡映像和開GW不變量的精確公式，這將大大提高我們對鏡對稱的幾何的認識。 另一方面，非CY流形的鏡對稱最近受到多方關注。Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono定義了開GW不變量作為研究圓環流形的Lagrangian Floer理論的基礎。在此之前，Batyrev，Givental和Lian-Liu-Yau證明了圓環流形的鏡對稱定理以及驗證了各種鏡對稱推測。了解這兩種方法之間的關係無疑可使我們對非CY流形的鏡對稱有一個更深入的認識。本項目的PI在這個方向做了初步的工作。在此基礎上，PI計劃進一步深入探索Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono 和Batyrev/Givental/Lian-Liu-Yau兩種方法之間的聯繫，以更好地理解非CY流形的鏡對稱現象。

404412.label: Realisation of objectives
404412.value: The first objective of this project was to relate mirror maps for Calabi-Yau manifolds to open Gromov-Witten invariants. The PI and collaborators have established such a precise relation in full generality for all toric Calabi-Yau manifolds. More precisely, a conjecture of Gross–Siebert states that the SYZ mirror of any Calabi-Yau manifold is written in canonical coordinates, which, in the case of toric Calabi-Yau manifolds, can be reformulated as the statement that the SYZ map, defined in terms of generating functions of open Gromov-Witten invariants, is inverse to the toric mirror map. In an earlier work, the PI and collaborators proved this latter conjecture for any toric Calabi-Yau manifold which is the total space of the canonical line bundle over a compact toric Fano manifold of any dimension, thereby establishing a precise and concrete relation between open Gromov-Witten invariants and period integrals of the mirror for these examples. The main tools are the capping-off trick and the closed mirror theorem. By incorporating orbifold techniques, or more precisely, by generalizing the open/closed equality to the orbifold case and establishing the open mirror theorem for toric Calabi-Yau orbifolds, we were able to compute all the orbifold disk invariants (genus 0 open orbifold Gromov-Witten invariants) of an arbitrary toric Calabi-Yau orbifold in any dimension. Before this work, disk invariants were computed in only very few examples; in our work, all such invariants were computed at once. These computations were then applied to prove two important results in SYZ mirror symmetry: 1. The Gross-Siebert conjecture for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds (and orbifolds) in full generality, which is a very precise relation between (orbifold) disk invariants and period integrals over the mirror and in particular gives a geometric and enumerative meaning to the inverse of mirror maps. 2. An open string version of Ruan's crepant resolution conjecture (CRC) for all toric Calabi-Yau orbifolds in any dimension. These results show that the SYZ proposal is the correct framework to explain mirror symmetry in a very strong sense. On the other hand, we have not addressed the relation concerning compact Calabi-Yau manifolds. A main reason is that open Gromov-Witten is still very poorly understand in this setting. Recent results have suggested that one may try to look at holomorphic disks bounded by immersed Lagrangian submanifolds, instead of embedded ones. The PI is hoping to make progress in this direction in a current project. The second objective of this project was to understand the interplay between superpotentials mirror to compact toric manifolds, toric mirror maps and open Gromov-Witten invariants. The PI and collaborators managed to give a complete computation of all the disk invariants (i.e. genus 0 open Gromov-Witten invariants) for all compact semi-Fano toric manifolds of any dimension. Before this work, computations are known only in a handful of examples. A great novelty is the discovery that Seidel spaces are the correct spaces to use in applying the “capping-off” trick. This computation leads to various profound applications: 1. This gives an explicit formula for the disk potential of any semi-Fano toric manifold; in particular, this gives an effective computation of all the disk invariants. 2. This implies that the Lagrangian Floer superpotential coincides with the Hori-Vafa superpotential via the inverse mirror map, which gives an enumerative meaning to the inverse mirror map and explains its integrality property in a geometric way. 3. This implies that the generating functions of disk invariants are convergent - the first of such results known. 4. This gives an explicit description of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono's isomorphism between quantum cohomology of X and the Jacobian ring of the superpotential. Furthermore, these results point to a very interesting and intimate relation between the Fukaya category (disk invariants) and the Seidel representation which should be further investigated. On the other hand, we have not addressed computations of bulk-deformed open Gromov-Witten invariants, which are largely unknown. It is likely that the required techniques are not available at this moment. The PI is hoping to develop new techniques and make progress in this direction in a current project. The third objective of this project was to incorporate open Gromov-Witten theory into the Gross-Siebert program. Applying the results obtained from this project, one of the PI’s collaborators, Siu-Cheong Lau, has proven that generating functions of genus 0 open Gromov-Witten invariants for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds coincide with Gross-Siebert’s slab functions. This establishes our objective in the toric Calabi-Yau case. To understand how open Gromov-Witten theory interplay with the Gross-Siebert program in the compact Calabi-Yau case, one needs to establish a general correspondence between holomorphic disks and tropical disks and also the relation between deformation theory and tropical geometry. This is closely related to a program put forward by Fukaya, and the PI is currently investigating this program in another project.

404412.label: Major findings and research outcome
404412.value: By incorporating the capping-off trick and orbifold techniques, or more precisely, by generalizing the open/closed equality to the orbifold case and establishing the open mirror theorem for toric Calabi-Yau orbifolds, and also applying the equivariant mirror theroems, we computed all the orbifold disk counting invariants (genus 0 open orbifold Gromov-Witten invariants) of an arbitrary toric Calabi-Yau orbifold in any dimension. Before this work, disk invariants were computed in only very few examples; in our work, all such invariants were computed at once. We applied our computations to prove two important results in SYZ mirror symmetry: 1. The Gross-Siebert conjecture for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds (and orbifolds) in full generality, which is a precise relation between (orbifold) disk invariants and period integrals over the mirror, and, in particular, gives a geometric and enumerative meaning to the inverses of mirror maps. 2. An open string version of Ruan's crepant resolution conjecture (CRC) for all toric Calabi-Yau orbifolds in any dimension. These results show that the SYZ conjecture is the correct framework to explain mirror symmetry in a very strong sense. We also gave a complete computation of all the disk counting invariants (i.e. genus 0 open Gromov-Witten invariants) for any compact semi-Fano toric manifold of any dimension. Before this work, computations are known only in a handful of examples. A great novelty is the discovery that Seidel spaces are the correct spaces to use in applying the “capping-off” trick. We applied our computations to prove the following important results: 1. The Lagrangian Floer superpotential coincides with the Hori-Vafa superpotential via the inverse mirror map, which gives an enumerative meaning to the inverse mirror map and explains its integrality property in a geometric way. 2. The generating functions of disk counting invariants are convergent; this is the first of such results known. 3. An explicit description of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono's isomorphism between quantum cohomology of X and the Jacobian ring of the superpotential. Applying our SYZ construction, we also constructed SYZ transforms and proved the HMS conjecture (involving wrapped Fukaya categories on the mirror side) for any toric Calabi-Yau surface and small toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. In particular, this gives the first complete computation of the wrapped Fukaya category of a 6d Liouville domain, which is neither a product of lower dimensional manifolds nor a cotangent bundle, and implies new results on Bridgeland stability conditions on Fukaya categories of 6d symplectic manifolds.

404412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404412.value: Our SYZ mirror construction for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds and orbifolds should be applied to understand another important conjecture in mirror symmetry, namely, Kontsevich’s Homological Mirror Symmetry (HMS) conjecture. Indeed the PI and collaborators have studied the two-dimensional case (i.e. toric Calabi-Yau surfaces which are total spaces of crepant resolutions of A_n singularities) and a three-dimensional example. We demonstrated how SYZ transforms could give rise to a geometric Fourier-type functor realizing the equivalences between triangulated categories predicted by HMS. New techniques and ideas are needed to generalize our results to higher dimensions. On the other hand, as mentioned above, we would like to have a deeper understanding of open Gromov-Witten theory. This would also need new techniques and ideas. The open mirror theorems that we proved suggested that there is some hidden structure among various moduli spaces of holomorphic disks, such as some degeneration formulas, as have been pointed out in work of Gonzalez-Iritani. This is an interesting and important but largely unexplored direction.

404412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404412.value: Mirror Symmetry was discovered by String theorists in the early 1990s. It predicts that there is a highly nontrivial and mysterious equivalence between the Symplectic Geometry of a space and the Complex Geometry of a completely different space. This led to numerous surprising and deep mathematical conjectures. Since its discovery, mathematicians have been striving to understand the geometry of Mirror Symmetry. A breakthrough came in 1996 when Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed that Mirror Symmetry should be understood as a geometric Fourier transform. Lying at the heart of the SYZ conjecture is the role played by quantum corrections, which is the key to explain the miraculous power of Mirror Symmetry. Our full computation of the disk counting invariants (i.e. genus 0 open Gromov-Witten invariants) for all toric Calabi-Yau orbifolds and semi-Fano toric manifolds is an important step in the study of quantum corrections and SYZ Mirror Symmetry. Our results provide important insight on how quantum corrections dictate the geometry of Mirror Symmetry and explain why Mirror Symmetry has been so powerful in making enumerative predictions.

404512.label: Project Objectives
404512.value: We will study curvature type invariants for higher dimensional subriemannian manifolds. We will investigate various geometric inequalities on subriemannian manifolds from the point of view of optimal transportation. In particular, we intend to prove a log-Sobolev type inequality by considering Boltzmann entropy functional on the subriemannian Wasserstein space. We will apply the study of the Boltzmann entropy functional to deduce the behavior of solutions to the subriemannian heat equation.

404512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404512.value: The aim of this project is to study geometric inequalities and behavior of solutions to diffusion equations on subriemannian manifolds under bounds on curvature type invariants. We intend to achieve this by using the theory of optimal transportation. Subriemannian manifolds are manifolds equipped with a velocity constraint, called distribution, and a smoothly varying inner product on the distribution. They are models of many physical systems. This includes a charged particle in a magnetic field, sliding skate, and a ball rolling without slipping. The theory of optimal transportation starts from the problem of moving one mass on a metric space to another in the most efficient way. Over the past two decades, many surprising connections between this simple problem and different areas of mathematics were found. Here we will focus on two of them: geometric inequalities and nonlinear diffusion equations. Geometric inequalities are used by many areas of mathematics especially in geometric analysis and partial differential equation. In many cases, the theory of optimal transportation provide elegant and conceptual proofs to many of them including the well-known isoperimetric inequality and Sobolev inequality. One of our goals is to apply this approach to the subriemannian setting. In particular, we intend to obtain various geometric inequalities for subriemannian manifolds on which the existing methods only work in restricted cases. The theory of optimal transportation also has a deep connection with one of the most important partial differential equations, the heat equation. As a result of this connection, certain long time behavior of solutions to this equation can be controlled by Ricci curvature lower bound. Our second goal is to explore similar relationship between the theory of optimal transportation and the subriemannian heat equation. Research on subriemannian heat equation has a long history dating back to the pioneering work of Hormander. Recently there is a renew interest in this equation due to its connection with neurobiological visual processing. We intend to look at this classical problem from the mordern point of view of optimal transportation. The study of subriemannian geometry involves lots of elementary and classical results in nonlinear ordinary differential equations. Therefore, this program is very suitable for postgraduate and, in some cases, undergraduate students.

404512.label: Realisation of objectives
404512.value: One of the main achievements of the project lies in the study of curvature type invariants for higher dimensional sub-Riemannian manifolds. The original plan was to extend the three-dimensional results obtained in my earlier work (1) to higher dimensional cases. In the case of Sasakian manifolds, this was completed in a series of papers (2,3,4). In fact, these results were obtained under assumptions which are much weaker than we originally anticipated. The best result in this direction was obtained in (9) under the assumption that the Tanaka-Webster-Ricci curvature is non-negative. The techniques used in (1,2,3,4) were not enough to obtain the results in (9) and some new methods were developed to overcome the difficulties. Two other research directions have been developed during this project. The first one was on a new differential Harnack inequality for parabolic equations found in (5) which is closely related to Ricci curvature type lower bounds. The result was extended in (6) to a family of hypoelliptic diffusions. This is also closely related to the second objective of the project. The second new research direction, which is related to the third objective of the project, is on Harnack inequalities for the Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto scheme of the heat equation from the theory of optimal transportation which was found in (4, 8). These results deserved further investigation in the setting of sub-Riemannian manifolds. Time was mostly spent on these two new research directions rather than the original objectives 2 and 3. 404512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404512.value: In recent years, there is a surge of interest in the study of synthetic Ricci curvature type lower bounds of metric measure spaces. Curvature is a differential geometric quantity which measures how far away a surface is from being a flat plane. In higher dimensions, the curvature depends on directions and the average curvature over all these directions gives the Ricci curvature. The original definition of the Ricci curvature that we just discussed briefly depends heavily on the underlying smooth structure of the surface which is not available for more general spaces. Nevertheless, in the last two decades, different definitions of Ricci curvature lower bounds were introduced and studied. One of them is the, so called, measure contraction property which we investigated in the setting of sub-Riemannian manifolds, a special type of spaces which arises from control theory. We showed how the measure contraction property is related to a known differential geometric quantity called the Tanaka-Webster-Ricci curvature, established important estimates, and laid down the analytic foundation in the study of these spaces and their curvatures.

404612.label: Project Objectives
404612.value: Design mathematical algorithms for re-meshing surface meshes with highly irregular triangulations. This will be done by developing methods to compute global conformal parameterizations of highly irregular meshes. Develop algorithms for computing the isometric embedding associated to a given metric and curvature function. This will be done by incorporating Laplace-Beltrami eigenfunctions in a variational framework. Mesh editing can then be done by modifying the metric and curvature function. Develop fast numerical methods for shape matching. This includes: (i) fast method to compute the Beltrami Holomorphic flow and (ii) multi-grid based algorithms for 3D shape matching. Apply the proposed algorithms to practical problems. This includes (i) building efficient solver for partial differential equations on meshes using the re-meshed surface with regular triangulation; (ii) building efficient tools for computing registrations of brain and hippocampal surfaces and (iii) developing tools for effective mesh editing of distorted anatomical structures.

404612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404612.value: 在醫學成像和計算機圖像學中，曲面網格編輯和形狀配準都是很重要的問題。網格編輯是指編輯和改善表示三維曲面的三角網的過程，這對於之後在曲面上進行的高效分析和數值計算是必要的。形狀配準是指尋找形狀之間的一一對應，對於有效地比較和分析形狀來說很重要。在本研究項目中，我們的目標是通過控制定義在曲面上的黎曼度量，發展用於網格編輯的有效數學算法以及用於形狀配準的快速數值方法。 本研究可以被劃分為三個主要部分。研究的第一部分，我們會發展三維網格編輯的數學算法。首先我們將開發三維曲面重新網格化的算法，目標是以規則網格來逼近不規則網格。這個過程對於在網格上進行的高效精確的數值計算尤其重要。其次，曲面的幾何可由它的黎曼度量和曲率來決定，從而曲面網格編輯可以通過編輯黎曼度量和曲率來實現。但是對於給定度量和曲率，如何有效計算等距嵌入（Isometric Embedding）仍然是一個具有挑戰性的問題。基於這點，我們將會致力開發準確估計等距嵌入的數值算法。 研究的第二部分，我們將考慮構建數值方法來計算點對點的形狀配準。我們最近已經發展了被稱為貝爾特拉米全純流（Beltrami Holomorphic Flow）的方法來計算有意義的曲面配準，它可以很容易控制配準的雙射性質（Bijection）。這種方法的一個缺點是數值計算比較慢，因此我們會設計方法來加速其運算。此外，曲面配準通常是一個在曲面雙射映射空間裡的優化問題，這可以進一步簡化為一個線性或者非線性方程組。為了加速數值計算，我們將開發基於多重網格的三維曲面配準算法。 研究的第三部分，我們打算將算法應用於實際的問題。我們將利用我們的重新網格化算法來高效求解網格上的偏微分方程，以應用到計算機圖像學中。我們也將應用形狀配準的快速算法來計算腦部以及海馬體的配準，這對於腦部疾病的分析將會非常有用。最後，我們將利用計算等距嵌入的算法，通過修改度量和曲率，來優化三維解剖結構的表面網格。

404612.label: Realisation of objectives
404612.value: In this project, we have three main objectives. The PI has tackled each proposed problems successfully. Details are as follows. Objective 1: The first objective is to develop mathematical models based on Riemannian metric for remeshing digital surfaces with highly irregular triangulation. The PI has successfully achieved this goal. More precisely, we have developed an algorithm, called the Hooke’s mesh optimization, to obtain an optimized mesh based on the input (discrete) metric. Each edge is treated as an elastic spring associated with some elastic forces. The mesh optimization is based on a modified version of Hooke’s laws, whose stiffness coefficients are different depending on the displacement of vertices. This avoids flipping of triangles during the mesh optimization process. A filtering scheme called the Newtonian Filtering is developed based on the high-dimensional Newton’s method to further preserve the local geometry of the optimized mesh. Results show that the combinination of the Hooke’s Optimization and the Newtonian Filtering significantly enhance the mesh quality, while both smoothness and local geometry of the surface are greatly preserved. Another advantage of this algorithm is that it can handle surface meshes with any topologies, including multiply-connected or high-genus surfaces. Besides, surface remeshing can be achieved through a global conformal parameterization. A high-quality triangulation on a simple parameter domain can be projected onto the original surface to get a good remeshed surface. However, an efficient and accurate algorithm for global conformal parameterization algorithm is necessary. To achieve this goal, the PI has developed effective numerical algorithms using Beltrami differentials to compute global conformal and quasiconformal parameterizations for connected open or closed surfaces. In addition, a remeshing algorithm, called the Teichmuller remeshing algorithm, has been developed. The main idea is to optimally project a regular triangulation to the original surface, which balances between angle distortions and area distortion. The projection is based on a landmark-matching Teichmuller map that minimizes the conformality distortion subject to the landmark constraints. The algorithm has shown to be effective for remeshing a simply-connected surface mesh with highly irregular triangulation. Objective 2: The second objective is to design algorithms for computing the isometric embedding associated to a given metric and curvature function. The PI has successfully achieved this objective. More specifically, an iterative algorithm has been developed to reconstruct a surface from the conformal factor (associated to a given Riemannian metric) and mean curvature. The iterative scheme is guided by the Gauss-Codazzi equation. The algorithm has shown to be effective in computing the embedding associated to an admissible pair of metric and curvature function. With the algorithm, many mesh editing tasks can be effectively done. More specifically, the mesh can be edited by adjusting the metric and curvature function of the original mesh. An edited mesh can be reconstructed from the processed metric and curvature function. With this idea, the PI has successfully designed algorithms to solve the shape morphing problem. Besides, the isometric embedding problem is also solved by formulating the problem as finding suitable coefficients associated to the Laplace-Beltrami eigenfunctions using an iterative algorithm. Objective 3: Our third objective is to develop fast algorithm for effective shape matching. One of the tasks in this objective is to develop fast method to compute the Beltrami Holomorphic flow. The idea is to obtain the variation of the quasiconformal map under the variation of the Beltrami differential. Conventional approach computes the variation using an integral formulation. The computation of integration is time-consuming. To compute the Beltrami Holomorphic Flow efficiently, we propose an efficient algorithm by minimization an energy functional involving the quasiconformal map and the Beltrami differential, using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). The obtained quasiconformal map and the Beltrami differential are associated with each other by adding the Beltrami energy in the energy functional. The method has shown to be effective and efficient for computing the Beltrami Holomorphic Flow. The fast method is useful for obtaining the shape matching between surfaces efficiently. Another task is to develop an efficient algorithm based on a multi-level approach. In this project, the PI has successfully developed a multi-level formulation for computing the surface registration. Intuitively, a coarse shape matching is firstly computed and the coarse registration is further refined using the proposed registration model. The method can significantly speed up the computation of the shape matching problem. Objective 4: This objective is to apply the developed algorithms to practical applications. This objective has been successfully achieved. Firstly, the efficient shape matching algorithms have been successfully applied to register anatomical structures, such as the brainstem surfaces, brain cortical surfaces and hippocampus surfaces. Secondly, the mesh editing algorithm has also been successfully applied to remesh the hippocampal surfaces, which can then be used for further disease analysis. The surface inpainting algorithm is also applied for filling occlusions on anatomical structures, such as the brain cortical surfaces. In addition, the remeshing algorithm is applied to obtain a surface mesh with regular triangulation, so that the partial differential equation involved in the surface registration problem can be accurately solved.

404612.label: Major findings and research outcome
404612.value: In this project, we have developed several mathematical models and algorithms based on Riemannian metric for mesh editing and shape matching, which has resulted in 11 journal publications in different applied mathematics journals. Details are as follows. (Note: ref[]=references in Part C) (1) Development of algorithms for remeshing surface meshes with highly irregular triangulations: We have developed different algorithms for remeshing irregular triangular surfaces. In [9], we have developed Hooke’s mesh optimization, to obtain an optimized mesh based on the input (discrete) metric. Teichmuller remeshing algorithm has been developed in [7], to optimally project a regular triangulation to the original surface, based on the landmark-matching Teichmuller map. Remeshing can also be done by projecting a regular mesh to the surface through a global conformal parameterization. Efficient and accurate numerical algorithms to compute global conformal parameterization for this purpose have also been developed [3,5,8,11]. The method is also extended to point cloud data for surface reconstruction from point clouds [10]. (2) Development of efficient algorithm for computing the Beltrami Holomorphic Flow: In [2], we have developed an efficient algorithm by minimizing an energy functional involving the quasiconformal map and the Beltrami differential, using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). The algorithm can be used to compute surface registration efficiently by adjusting the Beltrami differential [1,2]. (3) Development of fast algorithms for shape matching: Fast and accurate algorithms to obtain shape matching between surface meshes have been developed [1,2]. Using the Beltrami Holomorphic flow method, surface registration can be efficiently and accurately computed [1,2]. A multi-level based algorithm has also been developed to compute the surface registration efficiently [2]. (4) Development of mesh editing tools using isometric embedding: A surface mesh can be edited by adjusting its metric and curvature function. In [4], we have developed an effective geometry processing algorithm by reconstructing a surface from the conformal factor (associated to a given Riemannian metric) and mean curvature. The iterative scheme is guided by the Gauss-Codazzi equation. Using the developed algorithm, tools for surface morphing [4] has been developed. (5) Application of developed algorithms in medical imaging: Using the Hooke's remeshing algorithm, we have developed a tool to build regular triangulation for hippocampal surfaces, which are further used for disease analysis. The developed fast shape matching algorithms have been modified for registering real medical data, such as vertebrae bones and brain cortical surfaces [6].

404612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404612.value: There are several areas for further development of the research. Details are described as follows. (1) Extension of Teichmuller remeshing algorithm to high-genus surfaces: Currently, the Teichmuller remeshing algorithm can only be applied to simply-connected surfaces. For high-genus surfaces, computing an accurate Teichmuller map is still a challenging task. Thus, we are interested in extending the algorithm to high-genus surfaces. An efficient and accurate algorithm for high-genus surface Teichmuller map must firstly be developed. With such an algorithm, it is believed a Teichmuller remeshing algorithm for high-genus surfaces can be developed. (2) Fast and accurate global conformal parameterization for high-genus surfaces: The fast and accurate global conformal parameterization developed in this project can only be applied to simply-connected surfaces. Using a similar idea, we will explore the possibility to develop algorithms to conformally parameterize high-genus surfaces onto a simple domain, such as the Poincare disk, which can then be used for surface remeshing. (3) Extension of isometric embedding algorithm to point clouds: The surface reconstruction algorithm from the conformal factor and mean curvature works on surface meshes. We are interested in extending the idea to point cloud surfaces by developing the notions of conformal factor, metric and curvature on the point cloud surface.

404612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404612.value: In this project, the main goal is to develop effective mathematical algorithms for 3D mesh editing and fast shape matching, through manipulating the metric defined on the surface mesh. In this project, we have explored three research directions: 1. Develop effective mathematical tools for 3D mesh editing; 2. Develop fast numerical methods for shape matching and 3. Applications of the algorithms to practical problems. We have successfully developed and implemented mathematical models for the above three goals. For mesh editing, we have developed mathematical models to remesh irregular surface meshes and geometrically processed surfaces based on adjusting the metric and curvature function on the meshes. These developed algorithms are useful for 3D imaging and can be applied to medical image analysis. For shape matching, we have developed various fast algorithms for the shape matching between surface meshes. These efficient and accurate surface registration algorithms make it possible to obtain shape matching in real time for practical applications. With the developed algorithms, we have developed tools for registering and remeshing anatomical structures. These tools are useful in medical imaging for the purpose of disease analysis.
