404712.value: 從超冷極性分子在2008年製備成功開始，很多的實驗小組都開始搭建新的實驗系統用於產生各種各樣的超冷分子。這些新的實驗中的絕大多數都採用同樣的實驗方案，首先製備超冷原子氣體，形成弱束縛的Feshbach分子，而後用受激拉曼技術轉移分子到基態。這一實驗方案已經在KRb和Cs2分子實驗中成功的展示。 這個全新的領域的最終目標是實現偶極量子氣體，以研究偶極相互作用效應帶來的新奇效應，然而，迄今為止，我們所能製備的數目最大的樣品也只有40,000個左右個分子，這不僅會影響實驗中的信噪比，更會限制一系列後續的冷卻和操控。這一局限主要來自於Feshbach分子製備這一環節，由於快速的非彈性碰撞，Feshbach分子極易被消耗，要得到大數目同時又壽命較長的異核Feshbach分子有很大的挑戰性。在此，我們計劃引入三維光晶格來克服這一困難。首先，我們需要升級現有的BEC系統以搭建光晶格裝置。在新的系統裡，我們計劃用光阱加磁四級阱的形式進行蒸發冷卻和協同冷卻，我們希望這次升級之後可以得到原子更多的量子氣體混合物。第二步，將這些樣品轉移到光偶極阱中，研究Rb和Na量子氣體的混合特性，並通過Feshbach共振來對此進行調節。第三，搭建三維光晶格系統，研究光晶格中Feshbach分子的製備。我們期望通過實現兩組分的Mott絕緣體，使每一個格點只有一對異核原子，由於光晶格的隔離作用，以此形成的Feshbach分子將不會受到碰撞的影響，這將會提高分子的轉換效率和壽命。 大數目和長壽命的Feshbach分子是產生偶極量子氣體的理想出發點，偶極量子氣體和光晶格的結合也是研究有長距離相互作用的多體問題的極佳載體。這一項目的成功將會是對超冷分子甚至整個超冷量子氣體領域的很大貢獻，同時這一項目也是一個可以將基礎研究和研究生，博士後的培養有機結合的完美平台。

404712.label: Realisation of objectives
404712.value: Since the start of this grant, we have achieved the following milestones: 1).A new UHV setup, with better optical access for more flexible control of the internal and external degrees of freedom of the atoms, was built; 2).The double BEC of Na and Rb atoms were achieved in the new setup. The condensate numbers were improved by a factor of 3 reaching more than 2x105 for both species. Part of the results is published in J. Phys. B 49,015302(2015); 3).Feshbach resonance was used to create NaRb Feshbach molecules. We improve the number of molecules by a factor of 10. The result was published in New J. Phys. 17, 035003(2015); 4).Molecular spectroscopy of the NaRb excited state, for both the A^1 Σ^+/b^3 Π and the B^1 Π/c^3 Σ^+ coupled states, were investigated. An intermediate suitable for Raman transfer of the Feshbach molecules to the absolute ground state was observed. The result is published in Phys. Rev. A 93,012508(2016); 5).The electronic ground state X^1 Σ^+ was studied with two-photon spectroscopy. The lowest rovibrational state with v=0 ,j=0 was located; 6). A high stability, ultranarrow linewidth Raman laser system was built. Molecules in the absolute ground state was produced by the stimulated Raman adiabatic passage transfer. The electric dipole moment of NaRb in the ground state is measured. An effective dipole moment of 1.05 Debye was demonstrated. The result was published in Physical Review Letters 116, 205303(2016). Because of our fast progress in making Feshbach molecules and later absolute ground-state molecules in bulk sample, we didn't devote much time on setting up the optical lattices. We note that the purpose of the lattice potential is for optimizing the number of Feshbach molecules and eventually using it as a platform for investigating many body dipolar physics. Although right now, even without the lattice, more than 10^4 molecules can already be obtained, the lattice potential is still necessary for our long-term goal. It is just that achieving the ground-state molecules is a really big effort, we want to make the most out of it now. The current investigation will help us understanding the interaction properties, which are almost totally unknown now, between these molecules. The knowledge gained here will be very important for future work in optical lattice. Since we already have the right laser, the lattice potential can be implemented once the current investigation is finished. Thus objectives 4 and 5 in this proposal are still relevant for our research, i.e., although we didn't accomplish them during the period of this grant, they will certainly be addressed in the very near future.

404712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404712.value: With the high density sample of absolute ground-state ultracold polar molecules now available, we are now ready to study their basic collisional properties. Such investigation is important for gaining a detailed understanding of the molecule-molecule interaction with and without the induced dipole moment. Only with this understanding is it possible for us to fully explore the interesting dipolar many body physics. Although so far we haven't applied the optical lattice potential to our system, optical lattice is still a very necessary toolbox for further investigations. The main current problem is the cost for the narrow linewidth laser for building the lattice is too high. We can only hope to support such effort with other funding.

404712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404712.value: At temperatures near absolute zero, the behavior of particles is governed by their quantum nature. The wavelength of the matter wave decided by the particle-wave duality becomes comparable to the spacing between the particles. In this case, the particles start to behave as if they are just one giant particle. This is the strange regime of Bose-Einstein condensation predicted by Einstein in 1905 and realized experimentally with neutral atoms in 1995. The interaction between atoms is dictated by the short range van der Waals force. However, for heteronuclear molecules, the force can be much stronger and longer range since they can interact via the dipole-dipole interaction. In this project, we created a sample of ultracold polar molecules. This task is achieved by first creating very cold mixture of Na and Rb atoms, and then linking them by magneto-association to weakly bound Feshbach molecules. Since these weakly bound molecules have no dipole moment, they have to be transferred to the lowest energy state. This is realized with two-photon Raman transfer with the help of a narrow linewidth laser system and a carefully selected intermediate level. With such a sample available, we are ready to explore the novel world of dipolar physics.

404812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404812.value: 過去10年的研究表明細胞內蛋白質的羥基化反應會調控基因表達和缺氧狀況誘導的信號傳遞。比如，脯氨酸和天冬酰胺的羥基化調節一個轉錄因子HIF-alfa的活性以及降解速率。最近研究發現Jmjd6可以催化RNA結合蛋白上的賴氨酸的羥基化反應；這一發現引起了一個假說，即賴氨酸的羥基化反應可以調節RNA另路剪切和血管生成。雖然這一發現在生理學上極其重要，Jmjd6的底物蛋白仍然所知甚少。 最近我們觀察到Jmjd6的羥基化產物Luc7L2267-278上的5-hydroxylysine (5-Hyl)能夠被NaIO4氧化得到醛基。由此結果我們計劃聯合高碘酸鈉氧化和醛基俘獲來發現Jmjd6結合蛋白上的 5-Hyl位點。另外方面，我們發現Jmjd6酶能夠跟它的底物Luc7L2 和U2AF65發生二硫鍵交聯。與已經報導的DNA和酶的交聯類似，交聯反應只能在蛋白-蛋白的介面上發生，故而保留了蛋白-蛋白作用的結構信息。因此，我們計劃通過二硫鍵交聯捕獲相對弱的蛋白-蛋白相互作用，并用晶體結構分析的方法得到第一個Jmjd6-底物的晶體結構。 本工作需要精確的化學合成以及深思熟慮的生物實驗。我們在這兩方面都有多年的足夠的經驗。前期實驗結果也表明設計的實驗會取得成功。本實驗的成功將發現賴氨酸羥基化的新的功能，以及第一個Jmjd6-底物的共晶體結構。我們有信心按時完成課題。 我們實驗室的研究著眼于應用化學方法（比如親核進攻，光交聯，以及酶催化反應）來在相互作用的蛋白之間建立共價鍵，可用於結構研究以及共價標記實驗。在這類反應中，二硫鍵交聯是可以基因編碼的。本計劃書與本實驗室的長遠目標一致，故遞交申請Early Career Scheme。

404812.label: Realisation of objectives
404812.value: Both objectives have been fully realized upon the completion of this project. More specifically, we successfully examined periodate oxidation reaction in peptides, followed by reaction with aldehyde-reactive probes to achieve site specific labeling. This active-based profiling method was proven to be a marked advance towards the conjugation chemistry. Also, we thoroughly explored disulfide cross-linking reactions between enzymes and the substrates, which proves to be the most effective method to reveal the recognition of substrate by the enzymes. After fulfilling all the objectives we even conducted more research beyond the scope of the objectives; these extension allowed us to secure more grants.

404912.label: Project Title(Chinese)
404912.value: 用直接成像法研究油污如何進入沙粒間隙，在間隙中的分佈，以及如何清除間隙中的油污

404912.label: Project Objectives
404912.value: Directly imaging the detailed oil invasion process and clarifying the driving mechanism of invasion. In an oil spill, sand is initially filled by water, with oil staying out of sand. One important question naturally arises: what drives oil into sand? We will focus on two possible candidates, sedimentation due to gravity and water evaporation. We will independently study the influence of these two factors in various systems with different wetting properties and grain sizes. We will also illustrate detailed invasion process at both macroscopic and single-pore levels, making a comprehensive study on the amount, speed, and depth of the invasion with direct imaging. Our study aims to bring substantial understanding to the invasion process and its driving mechanism. Elucidating the oil distribution and its time evolution in sand with direct imaging. To effectively clean up the oil, it is crucial to identify how oil distributes in sand. With direct imaging in transparent systems, we can accurately measure the oil distribution and address this important issue. In particular, we are interested in the following specific questions: (1) Does oil distribute uniformly? If not, where does oil prefer to accumulate? This can help to pinpoint the oil-rich regions which require the most clean-up efforts. (2) How deep can oil penetrate into sand? This may provide valuable guidance regarding the required depth of a clean-up process. (3) What is the time evolution of the oil distribution? In particular, how does the natural ebb and flow cycle on sandy beaches influence the distribution of oil? Our investigation aims to provide critical information about the oil distribution and its time evolution in sand, which is essential for designing effective clean-up strategies. Exploring effective strategies to recover oil from sand. With the detailed study on oil dynamics, we aim to understand its fundamental physics and use the knowledge to achieve effective oil collection. We will explore the possibility of concentrating oil at designated locations, using the following methods: (1) our preliminary results show that oil tends to spontaneously accumulate at certain locations. By characterizing the detailed properties of these locations, we aim to artificially create them and accumulate oil at desired places. The subsequent clean-up will then be simplified by focusing on these specific locations. (2) Our previous research [18] has revealed a strong flow from large-pore to small-pore regions driven by evaporation. Using this fact, we plan to artificially introduce small pore regions by placing small particles at designated locations, and create desired oil flow towards these locations. This flow may concentrate oil to these small pore regions and greatly benefit the clean-up process. This technique has the advantage of using spontaneous evaporation process, which is robust and does not require extra energy input. By exploring effective methods of concentrating oil at designated locations, our study may help to design effective clean-up strategies and reduce the damage caused by oil spills.

In particular, we are interested in the following specific questions: (1) Does oil distribute uniformly? If not, where does oil prefer to accumulate? This can help to pinpoint the oil-rich regions which require the most clean-up efforts. (2) How deep can oil penetrate into sand? This may provide valuable guidance regarding the required depth of a clean-up process. (3) What is the time evolution of the oil distribution? In particular, how does the natural ebb and flow cycle on sandy beaches influence the distribution of oil? Our investigation aims to provide critical information about the oil distribution and its time evolution in sand, which is essential for designing effective clean-up strategies.

Exploring effective strategies to recover oil from sand. With the detailed study on oil dynamics, we aim to understand its fundamental physics and use the knowledge to achieve effective oil collection. We will explore the possibility of concentrating oil at designated locations, using the following methods: (1) our preliminary results show that oil tends to spontaneously accumulate at certain locations. By characterizing the detailed properties of these locations, we aim to artificially create them and accumulate oil at desired places. The subsequent clean-up will then be simplified by focusing on these specific locations. (2) Our previous research [18] has revealed a strong flow from large-pore to small-pore regions driven by evaporation. Using this fact, we plan to artificially introduce small pore regions by placing small particles at designated locations, and create desired oil flow towards these locations. This flow may concentrate oil to these small pore regions and greatly benefit the clean-up process. This technique has the advantage of using spontaneous evaporation process, which is robust and does not require extra energy input. By exploring effective methods of concentrating oil at designated locations, our study may help to design effective clean-up strategies and reduce the damage caused by oil spills.

404912.value: 我們的研究目標是使用直接成像技術來觀測油污怎樣入侵沙粒間隙，在其中的分佈，以及探索清除油污的有效方法。 原油洩露已經成為世界上日益突出的污染問題：最近的一次嚴重事故當屬2010年的墨西哥灣的原油洩漏事件。這次事件共導致580，000噸原油瀉入海洋並引起了嚴重的生態危機。在原油洩漏事件中，一部分油污可能飄到岸邊並長時間停留在沙粒間隙中，從而對人類生活和生態環境造成長時間惡劣影響。因此，研究油污入侵沙粒間隙的詳細過程以及在其中的具體分佈就有了重要的意義。但是，由於沙子的不透明性，這一過程很難被詳細研究，從而導致了我們對油污在沙粒中的運動過程的認識嚴重不足。 通過使用光學折射係數匹配的顆粒和溶劑，我們建議製備透明的多孔體系來模擬沙-水-油體系，從而可以使用直接成像法來研究這一重要過程。我們計劃在以下三方面做詳細研究：（1）油如何侵入沙粒間隙？（2）油在沙粒間隙如何分佈？（3）怎樣才能有效的將油污從沙粒中清除出去？對於這些問題的研究不僅能夠對油污的清理有所幫助，而且能對多孔材料中的流體動力學過程這一基礎研究提供實驗上的詳細信息。 基於在使用直接成像法研究流體動力學的豐富經驗，我們將會對這一過程進行詳盡的實驗研究並對清潔油污提供有益的技術支持。由於香港的漫長海岸線長期經受日益增長的污染威脅，相信我們的研究也會對本港的污染預防及環境保護起到有益的作用。

404912.label: Realisation of objectives
404912.value: (1) For objective 1, we have systematically studied the driving mechanism of oil invasion into both wetting and non-wetting sand packs. Our result shows that for submillimeter size sand, gravity cannot effectively drive the oil to enter the porous sand medium. However, once the sand is wetted by another continuous phase (such as water for example), as this phase is evaporating, it will pull the oil into the sand pack. This mechanism is valid for both hydrophilic and hydrophobic environment. The details are shown in the PhD thesis “Studying cracking and oil invasion in porous medium” by Dr. Jin, Qiu. Moreover, we also studied the gravity’s influence by looking at the impact phenomenon of a liquid drop onto solid surface under gravity. Interestingly, we find that compressed air is trapped under the drop, which subsequently shrinks into a bubble. Moreover, when the impact velocity is large enough, the drop will splash due to the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability caused by trapped air. These findings were published in Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA (PNAS) 112, 3280-3284, 2015. (2) For objective 2, we have directly visualized the oil distribution with confocal and optical imaging. The oil does not distribute uniformly at beginning but localizes at some specific regions. However, after we repeatedly add continuous liquid phase and then make it evaporate, which simulates the natural ebb and flow cycles, the oil phase expands with time over these cycles. More interestingly, we find that as concentration increases with time, the colloidal particles can self-assemble into ordered structures. The evolution and kinetic pathway of these structures were intensively studied, which revealed the fundamental question of how disordered structures turn into ordered ones. The results were published in Nature Physics 10, 73-79, 2014. We further extend this study to non-equilibrium active systems, and discovered the role of particle mobility in collective modes. The findings were published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 116, 048302, 2016. (3) For objective 3, we have explored the oil collecting methods in both hydrophilic and hydrophobic environments and found two effective approaches. First we tried different sized particles arranged at different locations, and achieved to create an evaporative flow from large to small particle regions. This flow collects the majority of oil into the small particle region and valid in both hydrophilic and hydrophobic environments. The second method is to make use of the wetting property: we create two regions with wetting and non-wetting porous sand media respectively. Initially the oil can distribute in both regions; as evaporation cycles go on, however, the oil is transferred into the wetting region and stuck there. Therefore wetting properties and size difference can both be used to collect oil effectively. The detailed results are in the PhD thesis “Studying cracking and oil invasion in porous medium” by Dr. Jin, Qiu.

404912.label: Major findings and research outcome
404912.value: (1) During the evaporation cycles of solvent, we found that colloidal particles tend to self-assemble into ordered structures. The evolution and kinetic pathway of these structures were intensively studied, which revealed the fundamental question of how disordered structures turn into ordered ones. These important results were published in the prestigious journal of Nature Physics 10, 73-79, 2014. (2) Furthermore, we extend such study to ordered by non-equilibrium active systems, and discovered the role of particle mobility in collective modes. The findings were published in the prestigious journal of Phys. Rev. Lett. 116, 048302, 2016. (3) On a porous surface such as sand, a liquid drop may interact differently from the common flat substrate. To illustrate this question, we study drop impact on porous substrates. We find that the common splash phenomenon is due to the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability triggered by trapped air at nanometer scale. This result explains the origin of a ubiquitous phenomenon and gets published in the prestigious journal Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA (PNAS) 112, 3280-3284, 2015.

404912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404912.value: The research findings could be used to design reduction techniques for pollution in porous media, such as the pollution in sandy beaches. To reach this goal, we need more experimental research on larger scales such as sand packs in meters or even tens of meters. Such kind of experiment can not be performed inside lab and requires support from the society.

404912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404912.value: We conduct a systematic study on the invasion mechanism and collecting methods of the polluting phase in porous medium, which is inspired by a practical pollution problem that occurs during oil spill to the sandy beach. We build a system in a smaller scale to mimic the practical pollution and investigate the distribution change of the polluting phase as the evaporating cycles increase. We find an obvious expansion of the polluting phase after several flushing cycles for both hydrophilic and hydrophobic bead systems, but with different distributions and expanding characters. We explained this difference by analyzing the pressure distribution in the system at the pore level. Finally, we develop two methods to concentrate the polluting phase in some particular regions, which is beneficial to solve the practical pollution problem.

405012.value: 複雜機率模型的變點估計

405012.label: Project Objectives
405012.value: To conduct theoretical investigations into the use of composite likelihood based statistics in change-point estimation. In particular: i) The consistency and convergence rate of the number and locations of the change-points will be investigated. ii) Model selection problem in each segment of observations between two change-points and the asymptotic properties of the estimates will be examined. To build fast and practical algorithms for computations in the change-point estimation procedure. By means of numerical experimentation, to thoroughly examine the applications of the change-point estimation procedure on various problems involving stochastic systems with complicated structures. The main focus will be on complicated models in univariate time series, high-dimensional multivariate time series and spatio-temporal processes.

405012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
405012.value: 本研究項目的目的是為複雜的隨機系統開發一套一致，準確及具運算效率的變點估計方法. 應用範疇包括非平穩時間序列和時空過程. 在分析數據序列時，是平穩的統計模型一直都被廣泛應用。然而，平穩的統計模型往往有不足之處. 越來越多的實證證據表示，數據序列常會出現結構性的變化。變點分析雖然已在文獻中被廣泛地研究，但大多數以前的研究都集中於“至多只有一個變化”的模式。關於多個變點的問題與還沒有完善的發展. 此外，現時有關多變點問題的研究，主要是局限於獨立的數據模型或簡單的單變量時間序列模型。多變點分析在比較複雜的單變量時間序列模型，多變量時間序列模型或時空模型仍有待開發。 為了填補文獻中這一重要的缺口，本研究項目的主要目標是發展有效的統計方法用於複雜的隨機系統中的多變點估計。具體而言，該項目將開發建基於複合似然函數的自動估計程序，用於同時估計變點的數目,位置，和選擇變點之間統計模型。在複雜的隨機系統中，常用的似然函數往往涉及計算大型矩陣的逆，或高維積分. 所以,現有辦法在變點問題的實際運算或理論漸近分析是很困難的。 另一方面，複合似然函數能通過結合有用的似然函數子集來分析大量而相關的數據。此方法特別適合於處理變點問題的計算以及漸近分析。此外，在許多應用中，複合似然享有不錯的理論特性，包括高效率和魯棒性。這些良好的特性都有利於變點分析的發展。 各領域中, 越來越多在的問題，需要在複雜的隨機系統中作出變點分析。目前的方法不足以精確地解決此類問題。本研究將對此類問題發展高效率運算和理論分析方法。這將有利於廣泛的科學的研究領域，如氣候，環境工程，金融和公共健康發展

410012.value: 圖像去噪和去卷積---不偏估計量方法

410012.label: Project Objectives

410012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410012.value: Image denoising and image deconvolution are standard restoration applications that have been investigated over decades, and many different approaches are available to address these problems. The usual techniques are theoretically grounded on hypotheses regarding the unknown underlying image (sparsity, low high-frequency contents, etc.). Yet, we have recently developed a novel framework, the SURE-LET methodology, that does not involve any prior assumptions on the restored image, at least in pure denoising problems. This approach relies on a statistical estimate (computed from the noisy image) of the quality measure we are interested in --- typically, Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimate (SURE), which provides an estimate of the Mean-Square Error (MSE) --- and on a low-dimensional representation of the denoising process --- typically, a linear combination of elementary processings (LET). The approach then consists in minimizing the quality measure for the (few) parameters of the representation. We have successfully applied the SURE-LET methodology to additive Gaussian denoising, and Poisson denoising. The goal of the current proposal proposal is to extend this approach in different directions: 1) linear restoration problems with noise --- typically, deconvolution; 2) other noise statistics --- in particular, multiplicative noise; 3) optimisation of LET bases (in particular, the linear transformations involved) for different situations (image types, noise types). Investigating these extensions inherently involve the development of (fast) algorithms, able to restore corrupted images which we intend to apply in practical situations (e.g., ultrasound imaging). 圖像去噪和圖像還原是已被研究了幾十年的標準恢復應用程序。有很多學者提出不同的解決方法。 一般的技術理論基礎建基於有關未知的底層圖像的假設（例如，稀疏性，低高頻內容等）然而，我們最近提出了一種新的處理方法，SURE-LET。它能有效地在不涉及任何事先假設下恢復圖像，至少在純去噪問題。 這種方法依賴統計學上的估計（由含雜訊的圖像中進行計算）。在正常情況下，Stein的無偏風險估計（SURE），能提供了一個估計值的均方誤差（MSE）和一個能用低維度表示的去噪過程，即是一些初級函數的線性組合（LET）。然後，用最優化去找出少數用作表達圖像的有關參數 。經過一連測試下，我們已經成功地應用了SURE-LET方法去消除可加性高斯白雜訊和泊松噪。 這個建議書的目的是把原有的方法延申到不同的層面。1）線性恢復與噪音問題，在通常情況下是反褶積2）其他噪聲統計，尤其是可乘性噪聲 3）優化LET的基（特別是涉及線性變換）並應用在不同問題上（例如，圖像類型和噪聲類型）。 硏究這些問題能幫助發展（快速）算法，能夠恢復損壞的圖像，我們並打算把它用作一些實際的應用（例如，超聲成像）。

In particular, a PhD student who had been recruited for that research had to be discontinued because of his low motivation. Fortunately, a new, much more reliable student started to work on PURE-LET deconvolution for fluorescence microscopy in August 2014.

410012.label: Major findings and research outcome
410012.value: The main SURE-LET image restoration strategy was described in a paper published at the inception of the project and which acknowledges the grant (Xue, F., Luisier, F. & Blu, T.,"Multi-Wiener SURE-LET Deconvolution", IEEE Transactions on Image Processing, Vol. 22 (5), pp. 1954-1968, May 2013). This paper has since received 14 Web of Science citations (26 Google Scholar). An important outcome of this project is a novel approach to identify blindly the Point Spread Function of a distortion system from a single distorted image. This approach uses a new unbiased risk estimate and the whole method gave rise to a publication (Journal paper #1), which has since received 9 Web of Science citations (16 Google Scholar). In addition, we have created a website (http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~tblu/monsite/phps/blursure.php) to share the blur-SURE restoration software. Another important outcome of this project is the identification of a novel unbiased risk estimate applicable to multiplicative noise (MURE). We have published two international conference papers that are relevant to this new risk estimate (conferences papers #1 and #2) My collaborator from IISc Bangalore (Prof. CS Seelamantula) and I have been faced with the difficulty of finding reliable students for performing the difficult research required in order to develop further the MURE-LET restoration approach. On the other hand, a new PhD student (Jizhou Li) has been hired to work on the restoration of Poisson-corrupted images (typical of fluorescence microscopy) and has performed a remarkable work. His preliminary results on PURE-LET deconvolution at a local biology symposium ("IAS conference and AoE Symposium on Organelle Biogenesis and Membrane Trafficking", 7-9 December 2015, http://iasprogram.ust.hk/201512obmt/index.html) showed that the PURE-LET deconvolution method is able to provide the same quality as a super-resolution microscope (which uses hardware-based structured light). The student received a best presentation award for his promising results. More significantly, the work done in 2015 by this student was then presented at the main image processing conference (Li, J., Luisier, F. & Blu, T.,"Deconvolution of Poissonian Images with the PURE-LET Approach", Proceedings of ICIP'16, Phoenix, AZ, USA, pp. 2708-2712, September 25--28 2016) where he also received a best paper runner-up award. Finally, we demonstrated how to integrate an unbiased risk estimate like the SURE in an iterative framework (since many restoration algorithms nowadays are iterative), while not losing its statistical properties (unbiasedness). This was the subject of a paper at the main signal processing conference (Conference paper #3, submission date: September 2015).

410012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410012.value: a) The PURE-LET deconvolution method shows very impressive restoration results, in particular when applied to 3D wide-field fluorescence microscopy, showing high-resolution optical sectioning, and significant in-plane super-resolution, comparable to a hardware-based super-resolution microscope (SIM-Structured Illumination microscope: in-plane resolution = 100 nm). This feature is of huge interest for bologists because super-resolution microscopes require significantly more acquisition time and illuminate significantly more the samples (may lead to alterations of their structure) than wide-field microscopes. We believe that our restoration algorithm (which is also reasonably CPU efficient: 20 seconds per full 3D volume on a standard laptop computer) can become a key component for biologists who need to assess the dynamics of protein trafficking in the cell without compromising the resolution. Another potential use of the PURE-LET deconvolution algorithm is to improve the resolution of super-resolution microscopes uniquely in software. b) The MURE-LET algorithm is not currently as well-developed as the PURE-LET restoration algorithm, but an exact parallel can easily be worked out. What is needed here is essentially a very motivated postgradate student, of similar reliability as Jizhou Li.

410012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410012.value: Image acquisition devices usually distort images, sometimes beyond recognition. In the worst case (e.g., medical image scanners) the distortion is computationally inverted (Computed tomography, Magnetic Resonance Imaging, various nuclear imaging modalities). In the "best" cases (microscopy, cameras), the mildly distorted images are in principle ready to be interpreted. Whatever the quality of the hardware, noise is always present in the images acquired. This is even more so in biomedical images, because of the low intensities involved, which is a consequence of the need for a harmless imaging process (low X-ray doses, low laser excitation, low radioactivity etc.). The research developed in this project addresses the problem of integrating the reconstruction process while taking the (possibly high) noise level into account. We develop a novel approach to this problem which is significantly faster than other more conventional approaches and of significantly higher quality. The key for this performance is to use an estimate of the quality of the restoration process that relies only upon the noisy distorted data. This quality estimate makes it possible to predict the closeness of any restored image to the original image without the need to know that image.

410112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410112.value: Pseudorandom distributions are a central object in complexity theory and cryptography, with deep connections to many facets of computation. Complexity theory provides a universal method for obtaining them, but the resulting constructions have large complexity. In particular, they are too inefficient for use in cryptography. In cryptography it is common to argue that a distribution is pseudorandom by reducing to the hardness of some well-studied problem like factoring large numbers. However, owing to increasingly stringent requirements placed on cryptosystems (e.g. fully homomorphic encryptions), as well as efficiency considerations, this approach is not always viable. In recent years our understanding of distributions that are pseudorandom against specific models (low-degree polynomials, small depth circuits, space bounded computations) has advanced significantly. A common theme in many of these works is the use of "primitive" objects, like expander graphs, k-wise independent sets, and small-bias sets. The simple, modular nature of these constructions not only clarifies our conceptual understanding of pseudorandomness, but also provides an appealing alternative way to argue in favor of cryptographic security. The main objective of this project is to obtain new and improved constructions of distributions that are pseudorandom against various models of computation, such as boolean formulas, binary decision diagrams, and monotone circuits. The existence of circuit lower bound methods for these classes suggests that they are good candidates for the task. Towards achieving this objective, we think it is essential to improve our understanding of the limitations of various pseudorandom objects, as well as ways of combining them. We suggest some approaches for obtaining new examples of functions that are hard to fool in this sense. Such functions are often instrumental in guiding constructions of pseudorandom distributions. The insights gained from this project could yield useful principles for the design of cryptographic primitives. 偽隨機分佈是計算複雜性理論和密碼學的核心目標，與許多方面的計算有著很深的關聯。計算複雜性理論提供通用的方法構​​作出偽隨機分佈，但所得出的構造有很大的計算複雜性。特別是，它們在加密應用的效率太低。要在密碼學上證明某分佈為偽隨機的方法，通常是把問題的難度歸約為其他已被廣泛研究的問題，如因數分解。然而，由於密碼系統的要求日益嚴格（像完全同態加密），加上效率方面的考慮，這種方法並不總是可行的。 近年，我們對某些分佈於個別計算模型(低次多項式，淺層電路，空間有限的計算) 的偽隨機性有進一步的了解。這些研究均應用了如擴展圖，k-獨立集，小偏差集等原件，這些建構簡單、模塊化的性質不僅釐清我們對偽隨機概念的理解，並且為證明加密的安全性提供了另一種證明方法。 本項目的主要目的為設計和改進隨機分佈的構造方法，使其對某些計算模型(如布爾公式、二元決策圖和單調性電路) 為偽隨機，而這些模型下限的證明方法是很好的工具。為此，我們必須加深對各種偽隨機物件之局限性的認識，以及整合它們的方法。我們就這些計算模型提出一些方法去構造難以被「欺騙」的新函數。這些函數往往是構造偽隨機分佈的工具。 本項目中得到的知識將成為對加密原件設計有用的原理。

410112.label: Realisation of objectives
410112.value: The objectives were largely realized and documented in the published works as well as some ongoing works for which future publication is planned. In the case of pseudorandomness against monotone functions, we have initiated the study in joint work with postdoctoral researcher Siyao Guo and visitor Ben Rossman. We have proved that there exist efficient pseudorandom generators (PRGs) against monotone functions on n bits of seed length n - Omega(n^{1/3}), and also proved a lower bound of n - O(n^{1/2}) for any such PRG. These results are somewhat surprising as information-theoretically it appears that even constant savings in pseudorandomness may not be possible. On the negative side, we did not manage to make progress in the computationally efficient setting and leave these questions for future work. In the case of binary decision diagrams and boolean formulas, we have investigated a solution based on noisy linear codewords. The problem was essentially completely solved along those lines recently by Haramaty, Viola, and Lee. We have some fundamental insights regarding the utility of pseudorandomness primitives and their composition. Here are two examples that we believe will have impact beyond the scope of this project: (1) Pseudorandom function families that are pairwise independent fool all statistical query learning algorithms. The statistical query model, which originates in computational learning theory, captures a wide class of machine learning algorithms. We showed that the elementary pseudorandomness notion of pairwise independence immunizes cryptographic constructions against all such attacks. (2) In certain cryptographically motivated settings, analyzing ratios of probabilities (i.e. divergences) can yield much stronger results than looking at their differences (i.e. statistical distances). This method composes well with known "hardness versus randomness" techniques. We have used this insight (in collaboration with Guo, Masny, Rosen, and Richelson) to simplify and improve the analysis of pseudorandomness of the Learning with Rounding (LWR) function. The question of finding hard examples for pseudorandomness primitives turned out to be more challenging than we had anticipated. Chin Ho Lee and Emanuele Viola initiated a new approach for the case of sum of small-biased distributions, discovering a connection to coding theory. In discussions with Chin Ho Lee we investigated extending their work to the list-decoding regime of parameters, but despite the promising progress this method did not lead to any interesting conclusion. In a different direction, very recently I managed to discover a new connection between pseudorandom functions that exhibit bounded independence and natural proofs for formula size. While this work was not completed within the scope of the project I plan to document the findings in the future. The relevance to cryptographic design and application was, in our view, the most successful part of the project. In fact all published works have a strong cryptographic motivation. Some highlights are: The relation between homomorphic evaluation and rerandomization in homomorphic encryption schemes; the proposal of new simple cryptographic constructions of weak pseudorandom functions and their rigorous analyisis against several classes of attacks; and the application of techniques from pseudorandomness to understand the connection between the learning with errors and learning with rounding problems which play a central role in contemporary cryptography. Some of the work from this project will be documented in an upcoming book chapter on pseudorandomness that I have written in collaboration with Alon Rosen.

410112.label: Major findings and research outcome
410112.value: We highlight the following findings that were obtained as part of this project: * Monotone functions are weaker distinguishers than they may appear: Even though the "description length" of a monotone function is n - O(log n) bits, such functions can be fooled by an efficient pseudorandom generator of length n - Omega(n^{1/3}). * The rerandomization ability of known homomorphic encryption schemes is not incidental: The ability to homomorphically evaluate ciphertexts implies the ability to rerandomize them. This is somewhat surprising as the functionality requirement of homomorphic encryption is purely deterministic. * Elementary pseudorandomness properties (pairwise independence, lack of correlation with low-degree polynomials) can also imply pseudorandomness against larger classes of adversaries and inform the design of cryptographic primitives. * Information-theoretic tools such as divergence measures may yield better and simpler analysis of cryptographic security, as demonstrated in our examples of rerandomization from homomorphic encryption and learning with rounding.

410112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410112.value: We believe some interesting insights from this work can be leveraged in the design and analysis of pseudorandom functions, both as they are used in cryptographic practice and in their conceptual role as a fundamental barrier towards improved circuit lower bounds. These ideas are explained in more detail in my project proposal "Random Local Functions and Pseudorandom Functions" currently under submission to the RGC.

410112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410112.value: The ability of computations to appear random, even though they are in large part deterministic, is of fundamental importance in cryptography, the science that underpins the security, privacy, and trustworthiness of large networks like the internet. In the last twenty years computer scientists have built a rich theory of pseudorandomness, but many basic questions remain unsolved. In this project we made progress in understanding how pseudorandomness interacts with certain types of computations, how different pseudorandom objects compose, and how they can be used towards building more efficient cryptography.

410212.value: 图修改问题的参数化算法和多项式核

410212.label: Project Objectives
410212.value: To understand how the structure of a fixed graph H affects the fixed-parameter tractability and polynomial kernelization of graph modification problems in connection with edge addition/deletion, and edge contraction.
rows: To understand how the structure of a fixed graph H affects the fixed-parameter tractability and polynomial kernelization of graph modification problems in connection with edge addition/deletion, and edge contraction.

410212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410212.value: Graph modification deals with the transformation of an arbitrary graph into a graph with a given property by performing some operations on edges and vertices. The classical subgraph and induced subgraph problems are typical examples of graph modification problems where the operations are edge deletion and vertex deletion respectively. Though most graph modification problems are intractable, the situation may change when the number of operations is relatively small, which often happens in practice. In this project, we use the framework of parameterized complexity to study graph modification problems by taking the number k of operations as a parameter, and our aim is to design FPT algorithms and obtain polynomial kernels. FPT algorithms attempt to confine the exponential time of an algorithm to a designated parameter k, and therefore solve the problem efficiently when k is ``small'', which gives an effective way to cope with NP-hard problems in practice. To obtain an efficient FPT algorithms, we often try to reduce in polynomial time an instance to a polynomial kernel, i.e., an equivalent instance whose size is only a polynomial of the parameter k. We will consider graph modification problems with respect to the following fundamental operations: edge deletion, edge addition, and edge contraction. For the property the target graph should satisfy, we focus on the property of being H-free for a fixed graph H, i.e., the target graph contains no copy of H, since H-freeness is fundamental and many properties can be described by H-freeness. We will study FPT algorithms and polynomial kernels for these graph modification problems, and attempt to determine the existence of FPT algorithms and polynomial kernels in terms of the structure of the fixed graph H. 图修改问题通过对于边和顶点的运算使图满足给定的性质，经典的子图和导出子图问题即是分别对边和顶点进行删除。虽然图修改问题通常难解，但当所容许的运算次数相对较小时，问题可能变得有效可解。 本课题旨在研究图修改问题的参数化算法和多项式核。我们将针对边删除，边增加， 和边收缩的图修改问题进行研究。 我们着重考虑通过边运算消除图中H-子图的图修改问题，并希望对这类图修改问题的参数化算法和多项式核的存在性按H的结构进行分类。

410212.label: Realisation of objectives
410212.value: Graph modification problems deal with the transformation of an arbitrary graph into a graph satisfying a given property by performing some operations on edges and vertices. The classical subgraph and induced subgraph problems are typical examples of graph modification problems where the operations are edge deletion and vertex deletion respectively. Though most graph modification problems are intractable, the situation often changes when the number of operations is relatively small, which frequently happens in practice. In this project, we use the framework of parameterized complexity to study graph modification problems by taking the number k of operations as a parameter, and our aim is to design FPT algorithms and obtain polynomial kernels. FPT algorithms attempt to confine the exponential time of an algorithm to a designated parameter k, and therefore solve the problem quickly when k is ``small'', which gives an effective way to cope with NP-hard problems in practice. A useful way to obtain an efficient FPT algorithm is to reduce in polynomial time an instance to a polynomial kernel (an equivalent instance whose size is a polynomial of the parameter k only). We investigate graph modification problems with respect to the following fundamental operations: edge deletion, edge addition, edge contraction and vertex deletion. For the property the target graph should satisfy, we mainly focus on the property of being H-free for a fixed graph H, i.e., the target graph contains no induced copy of H. We have studied FPT algorithms and polynomial kernels for these graph modification problems, and, to a large extent, have determined the existence of FPT algorithms and polynomial kernels by the structure of the fixed graph H. Furthermore, we have also initiated the study of graph modification problems on edge bicolored graphs where we require the two resulting monochromatic graphs to satisfy given properties simultaneously. For edge modification problems, a well-known result of the PI implies FPT algorithms for at most k edge addition/deletion operations for every fixed H. However, it is unclear when edge modification problems admit polynomial kernels. Prior to this project, it was only known that edge modification problems admit no polynomial kernel when H is a special graph, a path or cycle with at least 12 vertices. In the project, we have set up a general framework to establish the nonexistence of polynomial kernels for edge modification problems. For this purpose, we have introduced a constraint satisfiability problem to express common propagational behaviors of events, and designed a general scheme for reductions from this satisfiability problem to show the nonexistence of polynomial kernels for edge modification problems. Using this effective tool of reductions from our constraint satisfiability, we are able to fully characterize the existence of polynomial kernels for edge modification (including edge deletion, edge addition and edge editing) by the structure of H when H is 3-connected. Furthermore, for H being disconnected or 1-connected, we show that it is sufficient to focus on 2-connected components or blocks of H. For edge contraction problems, we are able to use some ideas from edge modification problems to obtain FPT algorithms or show its fixed-parameter intractability. For graph modification problem on edge bicolored graphs, where each edge is colored either blue or red, we have initiated the study of obtaining a graph where its blue graph and red graph simultaneously satisfy properties for blue and red graphs. Even for the trivial property of being connected, the problem becomes very difficult for edge bicolored graph because of the interaction of two colored graphs. We are able to fully characterize hereditary properties that warrant FPT algorithms for vertex deletion. As for the property of being connected, we show a colorful spectrum of complexity for edge bicolored graphs for several versions of the problem: polynomial-time, NP-complete, FPT, and W[1]-hard. Our work has already inspired other researchers to follow the direction of this project to work on graph modification problems for edge-bicolored graphs. For a different flavor, we also consider graph modification problems where we also impose some structure on the deleted part. For instance, we consider the deletion of an (s,t)-path of length at most k so that the resulting graph still contains an (s',t')-path. This is equivalent to finding edge-disjoint (s,t)-path and (s',t')-path. We are able to use the color coding technique to obtain FPT algorithms for several variations of the problem, and have used random partition in a clever way to obtain FPT algorithms for two variations when the resulting path has no length limit or length lower bound.

410212.label: Major findings and research outcome
410212.value: 1. (C8.1) We conduct a systematic study of the incompressibility, i.e., nonexistence of polynomial kernels, of H-free edge modification problems (i.e., modifying at most k edges to obtain an H-free graph) in terms of the structure of H, and completely characterize their nonexistence for H being paths, cycles or 3-connected graphs. As an effective tool, we introduce an incompressible constraint satisfiability problem to express common propagational behaviors of events, and we expect the problem to be useful in studying the nonexistence of polynomial kernels in general. 2. (C8.2 and C9.2) We initiate the study of parameterized complexity of finding edge-disjoint paths with length constraints between two given pairs of vertices. We obtain FPT algorithms for 7 of the 9 different cases of length constraints. Our algorithms use random partition backed by some structural results. On the other hand, we prove that the problem admits no polynomial kernel for all 9 cases unless NP is contained in coNP/poly, which also extends to 108 variations of edge/vertex-disjoint two-paths problems for undirected/directed graphs. 3. (C8.3) We study FPT algorithms and polynomial kernels for graph modification problems by edge contraction, i.e., contracting edges in a graph to obtain a graph satisfying a given property. We give FPT algorithms for the clique contraction problem and the K(t)-free contraction problem for each fixed t > 2, and show that neither problem admits a polynomial kernel unless NP is contained in coNP/poly. We also completely characterize the parameterized complexity of H-free contraction for all fixed 3-connected graphs H, and show that the chordal contraction problem is W[2]-hard. 4. (C8.4 and C9.1) We initiate the study of graph modification problems for edge bicolored graphs. In particular, we consider the problem of deleting at most k vertices to simultaneously disconnect red and blue graphs of G, and the problem of finding from G a k-vertex induced subgraph whose red and blue graphs are both connected. We discuss various algorithmic and complexity issues for these two problems: NP-completeness, polynomial-time algorithms, W[1]-hardness, and FPT algorithms. We also give a complete characterization of the complexity of the problem of obtaining a k-vertex induced subgraph H from G that simultaneously satisfies given hereditary properties for H's red and blue graphs. 5. (C8.5) Further to C8.1, we investigate H-Free Edge Deletion/Completion problems when H is disconnected or 1-connected. We show that if H contains a component or block B for which B-Free Edge Deletion (resp., Completion) is incompressible, then H-Free Edge Deletion (resp., Completion) is also incompressible. This allows us to focus on 2-connected H in the investigation of incompressibility of H-Free Edge Deletion/Completion problems.

410212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410212.value: With the work in C8.1 and C8.5, we can concentrate on H of 2-connectivity for H-free edge deletion and completion problems, and it seems possible to obtain dichotomy theorems in terms of the structure of connected H. It also seems possible to determine the status of the problem for most disconnected H. Of course, a more ambitious goal is to extend our results to general F-free edge deletion/completion problems for a set F of forbidden graphs. Furthermore, ideas used for incompressibility of edge deletion problems seem to be useful for proving the fixed-parameter intractability of edge contraction problems. Our work on graph modification problems for edge bicolored graphs gives a new direction for graph modification problems, and introduces many interesting open problems for edge bicolored graphs. For instance, in connection with the classical feedback vertex set problem, is it FPT to remove k vertices to destroy all alternating cycles in an edge bicolored graph? We expect many interesting results in coming years.

410212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410212.value: FPT algorithms and polynomial kernels are effective tools for solving intractable problems in practice when some parameter k of the problem (e.g. solution size) is relatively small, and research on these two subjects is extremely active in recent years. This project investigates FPT algorithms and polynomial kernels for graph modification problems with respect to various operations on graphs. In particular, we consider problems of modifying a graph into a graph satisfying the required property by edge addition, edge contraction, or edge/vertex deletion, where the number k of operations is taken as a parameter. Our investigation is systematic and comprehensive, and, to a large extent, we determine the existence of FPT algorithms and polynomial kernels in terms of the structure of the required property, which represents the state of the art for the parameterized complexity of graph modification problems. We expect several results from this project to become standard references and stimulate further research along the direction of this project.

410512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410512.value: This proposal is to request support for research on the investigation of simple optical techniques to monitor the network and signal performance of the new optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals in spectrum-efficient and bandwidth-flexible optical transport networks. The optical OFDM signal format has recently been widely considered and adopted as a robust optical modulation format for optical transmission, due to its superior tolerance in both chromatic dispersion and polarization mode dispersion, as well as its high bandwidth efficiency and flexibility in various networking applications. Its practicality in the realization of optical transmitters and receivers is further enabled by the recent advances in high-speed electronic digital processors. In order to assure the signal integrity and reliability of the flexible optical transport networks, network and performance monitoring of the optical OFDM signals are indispensable. This projects aims at designing simple, low-cost, yet effective optical schemes to monitor the passband adjustment status of the bandwidth-variable wavelength selectable switches (BV-WSS) resided at each optical cross-connects along the lightpath, as well as to retrieve its signal quality parameters, without requiring the costly coherent receivers. A few code-assisted orthogonal optical subcarriers are proposed to be added to strategic spectral locations within the optical OFDM signal to facilitate simple in-line performance monitoring. By examining the low-bit-rate codes carried by these monitoring subcarriers, via simple filtering of the optical OFDM signal, together with common code recognition technique, based on conventional electronic code division multiple access (CDMA), various different kinds of signal quality parameters of the optical OFDM signal can be estimated, and the possible malfunctioning of the BV-WSS can also be detected promptly. With such extracted signal performance information, appropriate remedy can be made in time to assure the quality of service of the network. The results of this project can greatly enable good practicality of optical OFDM signals to be employed in next generation spectrum efficient and flexible optical transport networks. 這個項目是研究一些新光學技術以便為光學正交頻分复用（OFDM）信號在高頻譜效率及靈活帶寬的光傳輸網絡中作性能監控。由於光OFDM信號格式擁有對光纖色散和偏振模色散的高度容忍性，以及其帶寬之高效率和靈活性，最近它已被廣泛審議為一種可行的光學調制格式作光訊號傳輸。再加上最近在高速電子數字處理器的最新進展，亦加強了光OFDM發射機和接收機的實用性。為了保證光OFDM信號在靈活光傳輸網絡的完整性和可靠性，其網絡和性能監控是必須的。 這個項目的目的是設計簡單，成本低而有效的光學技術以監測在沿光路上各個光學交叉連接器上的帶寬可變波長選擇開關（BV-WSS）的通帶調節狀態，以及監控光OFDM信號的質量參數。建議中的方案並不需要昂貴的相干接收機的信號質量參數，只需要把一些代碼輔助正交光副載波加到光OFDM信號中的特定光譜位置的，便可簡單作信號性能監測。通過檢查及過濾在低比特率的代碼，及應用傳統的電子碼分多址（CDMA）的各種常見代碼識別技術， 便可對光OFDM信號的各種不同信號質量參數作出估計及及時發現可能失靈的BV-WSS。只要提取了信號性能的信息，便可作適當的補救措施，以保證網絡服務的質量。 這個項目的成果可以大大加強光OFDM信號在高頻譜效率和靈活的下一代光傳輸網絡中的實用性。

410512.label: Realisation of objectives
410512.value: In this project, both of the revised objectives have been successfully achieved and the results have been published in international journals and conferences. Regarding to the first objective, we have designed and experimentally demonstrated the use of unique Gold sequences as the orthogonal codes to be carried by two code-assisted optical label subcarriers. They are put as the first and the last optical subcarriers of the optical OFDM signal. The two optical label subcarriers are used for monitoring purposes and their parameters are to be extracted by means of signal correlation at the monitoring points. After the signal correlation process is performed between the received optical OFDM signal and the two designated orthogonal codes, two correlation peaks can be obtained. Both numerical simulation results and experimental results have confirmed the feasibility and effectiveness in detecting the correlation peaks with pretty high contrast from noise floor. By making use of these code-assisted optical label subcarriers and placing them in strategic location within the optical OFDM signal spectrum, we have shown that the relative temporal delay difference between the two correlation peaks is proportional to the accumulated chromatic dispersion suffered by the optical OFDM signal, while their relative power ratio can be used to derive the accumulated differental group delay (DGD), which is the common measure for polarization mode dispersion (PMD). It has also been confirmed to be used to derive the electrical signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), which can further be used to derive the optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR). Regarding to the second objective, we have already successfully designed and experimentally demonstrated three optical performance monitoring schemes, based on the idea of code-assisted orthogonal optical subcarriers, which includes chromatic dispersion (CD) monitoring, PMD monitoring, as well as OSNR monitoring. Each of them has been published in a journal publication. For CD monitoring, a CD monitoring scheme for direct-detection (DD) optical OFDM (DDO-OFDM) system has been designed and experimentally characterized. The accumulated chromatic dispersion, as well as the dispersion signs (positive or negative), of the signal can be monitored by measuring the relative temporal difference of the two correlation peaks. The measurements agree well with the specifications provided by the fiber vendor. For PMD monitoring, we have experimentally demonstrated and characterized the proposed PMD monitoring scheme in a DDO-OFDM system. A pair of data-assisted pilot subcarriers are inserted at two spectral edges of the OFDM signal spectrum. Simple data correlation technique is used to estimate the powers of the pilot subcarriers, and their ratio is used to derive the differential group delay (DGD) value, without the need of demodulation of the pilot subcarriers. Experiments show a DGD monitoring range of 0 to 45 ps in a typical radio-frequency tone-assisted DDO-OFDM system. It has also shown good robustness to optical signal-to-noise ratio and accumulated chromatic dispersion. Besides, simulations and experiments are performed to demonstrate the feasibility of using photodiodes with narrow bandwidth. By inserting one more data-assisted pilot subcarrier, the proposed scheme becomes insensitive to the input angle of the state of polarization. For OSNR monitoring, a novel OSNR estimation method for DDO-OFDM systems has been presented and characterized. It is realized by calculating the ESNR of one pilot subcarrier based on the signal correlation. Simulation and experiment have been carried out in a 15-Gb/s DDO-OFDM system to verify this proposed OSNR estimation method. The OSNR estimation error is less than 0.8 dB, within an OSNR range of 8 to 28 dB, after 100-km and 200-km transmissions.

410512.label: Major findings and research outcome
410512.value: The project has proposed a simple scheme to perform optical monitoring in three important aspects of system parameters, namely chromatic dispersion monitoring, polarization mode dispersion monitoring, and optical signal-to-noise ratio monitoring, via placing just a few code-assisted optical subcarriers at the strategic positions within the optical OFDM signal spectrum, in a direct-detection optical OFDM system. Only simple correlation process and digital signal processing are needed at the receiver end without signal demodulation and the need of expensive coherent receivers. In chromatic dispersion monitoring, two code-assisted optical subcarriers are placed, one at each end of the signal spectrum. The temporal difference between the two respective correlation peaks can be used to derive the accumulated group delay. Similar technique has been applied to realize polarization mode dispersion but the peak amplitudes, instead of temporal delay, of the retrieved correlation peaks are used to derive the different group delay. For optical signal-to-noise monitoring, only one optical subcarrier is placed at the high-frequency side of the OFDM signal spectrum and the peak amplitude of the retrieved correlation peak can be used to derive the electrical signal-to-noise-ratio ratio, which can be further used to derive the optical signal-to-noise ratio value. All schemes have been experimentally demonstrated and characterized with good agreement with the simulation results. The results provide a simple and cost-effective approach to perform optical performance monitoring in optical OFDM systems.

410512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410512.value: The techniques can be applied to other optical multicarrier signal formats, such as discrete multitone, etc. The robustness of the proposed schemes under fiber nonlinearity is yet to be explored and investigated.

410512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410512.value: In recent years, optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signal has emerged as a spectrum efficient and robust format to support high-speed optical fiber transmission. It has demonstrated high spectral efficiency and good tolerance to fiber dispersions. It can also support bandwidth flexible and grid-less networking. In this project, a simple technique of inserting a few code-assisted optical subcarriers into the signal spectrum and using simple correlation procedures for detection, are proposed to estimate various signal quality parameters, including optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR), accumulated chromatic dispersion (CD), as well as polarization mode dispersion (PMD), without requiring the costly coherent receivers, at the intermediate nodes. With such extracted network and signal performance information, the network resiliency and the signal quality of the optical OFDM signals are assured. Hence, impairment-aware routing based on the extracted monitoring information can be enabled and appropriate remedy can be made in time to assure the quality of service of the next generation spectrum-efficient and bandwidth flexible optical transport networks.

410812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410812.value: Following the lead of the European Union (EU), Japan, and several other regions, the Chinese government has set a timetable for emissions trading schemes within China, including the establishment of a nationwide trading platform by 2015. Six regions, including Guangdong Province, have already been preparing for the launch of regional trading markets. From 2013 onwards, the EU will require all CO2 emitters in certain sectors (power plants, smelter, glass, and so on) to balance all of their emissions from the market, wherein the EU sets an overall aggregate quantity, and all emitters procure from the open market for their emissions. Unlike a commodity input that must be available before production starts, the carbon permits that a firm spends in a year requires balancing only by the end of the year. Thus, the firm has the flexibility as to when and how much to buy from the market over time. This feature brings new research opportunities, as well as challenges. Although some industry experts have already observed that many companies in Europe have incorporated carbon trading into their daily production decisions, few academic publications respond to such a development. Indeed, a great deal of attention has been devoted to emissions reduction issues. However, the research into production operations and emissions permit trading decisions is also a noteworthy subject. Two issues were attempted to be addressed: First, how should the firm coordinate its production and permit purchasing decisions in each period? Second, will a non-coordinated (or decentralized) decision-making procedure incur a substantial cost increase compared with a coordinated decision-making procedure? The first question calls for a general model setting and rigorous analysis, whereas the second aims to draw managerial insights. The full coordination of production operations and permit purchasing decisions requires the integration of operations and treasury management. However, this integration is difficult to achieve in practice. Should the efficiency loss be small, the firm would then keep the two functions working in a relatively separate manner. The preliminary study has obtained promising findings under the electricity generation context, which confirms the conjecture to a certain extent. The two abovementioned research issues for perishable (such as electricity) and non-perishable products will be separately addressed. In addition, the risk issues will also be considered with respect to uncertain carbon costs in the late phase of the present study. 繼在歐盟，日本，及其它國家實施碳排放交易之後，中國政府近期也制定了全國範圍內2013年推行碳交易的時間表， 其中包括廣東省的六個地區已經開始著手准備試點。在歐盟，從2013年起，若幹行業（如發電，冶煉，玻璃）需要通過市場平衡它們所有的碳排放量。 歐盟碳排放交易市場上的許可證價格波動幅度很大。猶如其它原材料商品，碳排放許可證已成爲必不可缺的生産要素。不同的是，沒有原材料在手上，生産將無法開始，但 碳排放許可證只需要年度平衡即可， 即在某個日期前有足夠的許可證抵消過往一年生産所排放的（二氧化）碳總量。這個特點爲生産運作決策帶來新的問題， 也爲研究提供新的機會和挑戰。本研究項目試圖探討以下兩個問題。 第一，有碳排放的生産企業如何協調生産和碳排放許可證購買決策？第二，是否生産和碳排放許可證購買分離/獨立決策會造成較明顯的成本提高？ 第一個問題要求新的模型和分析方法，而第二個問題意在産生管理建議。協調生産和碳排放許可證購買決策要求運作和財務管理的整合，但在實踐起來難度很大。如果分離/獨立決策造成的成本提高不是那麽顯著，企業便可以保持兩個部門的相對獨立；反之,運作和財務管理的聯合決策便值得推行。因此，該項研究的成果將具有重要的學術和實踐價值。

410812.label: Major findings and research outcome
410812.value: The use of permit markets to mitigate harmful emissions is on the rise. When participating in such a market, an emitting firm needs to acquire from it permits that cover emissions resulting from production. Thus, the firm has to simultaneously cope with fluctuating permit prices and random demand, and also juggle between the activities of permit trading and permit-consuming production. We shed light on this complex dynamic control problem, while confronting difficulties brought on by fixed as well as variable transaction costs associated with permit trading. We exploit K-convexity variants that are suitable for two-dimensional control, to achieve the partial characterization of optimal control policies. When the selling of permits is prohibited, we prescribe an (s,S)-type permit purchasing policy. For the more general case involving two-way trading, we find it optimal to carry out trading in a three-interval fashion. Heuristics, including one based on the uncoupling of trading and production activities, are introduced. Their effectiveness has been illustrated in computational studies. This is the outcome of our paper "Joint Control of Emissions Permit Trading and Production Involving Fixed and Variable Transaction Costs". Our second paper "Supporting Customers to Sell Used Goods: Profitability and Environmental Implications" is based on the observation that manufacturers in different industries encourage their customers to resell and reuse used goods as their ``Go Green" initiatives. Some even offer online peer-to-peer (P2P) platforms to support their customers to post, sell and buy their used goods. We investigate the economic and environmental potential of encouraging the reselling and reuse of secondhand goods. We consider a stylized, two-period model in which we endogenize the firm¡¯s choice between two sales options, one without and another with a secondhand market, by relative profitability. The firm sells a durable product of Version 1 and an improved Version 2 in periods 1 and 2, respectively. The reuse value of used goods may be lower than the value of a new one, and the value of a Version 2 product may be augmented (value of newness) as compared with Version 1. Environmental impacts are measured in three phases: production, use and disposal. We find that whether encouraging secondhand trading is greener and/or more profitable depends largely on the product¡¯s relative values of reuse and newness (for used goods and new products, respectively), the relative environmental impact of the product in its use phase as compared to the production and disposal phases.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410812.value: The use of permit markets to mitigate harmful emissions is on the rise. When participating in such a market, an emitting firm needs to acquire from it permits that cover emissions resulting from production. Although firms should exert a great deal of effort to reduce carbon emissions, the effect of carbon trading on firm operations decisions also needs to be considered. The current project attempts to address how a firm should coordinate its production and permit purchasing decisions in each period. However, the full coordination of production and permit purchasing decisions requires the integration of operations and treasury management, which brings out another important issue: How much additional cost would a separate (or decentralized) decision-making heuristic(s) incur compared with the optimal joint decision of production and permit purchasing? A major insight gained from this project follows: If the firm can monitor the permit spot market at a reasonable frequency and make trading and production decisions accordingly, a simple disjoint decision-making mechanism may cause little loss of cost efficiency. When such is not the case, however, it is worth following a more complex joint trading and production policy.

412412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412412.value: The aim of this project is to build a virtual incisional microanatomy model facilitating physicians in learning 3-D anatomy in the mastoid, and to develop a virtual environment for the training of microsurgical skills in ear surgery. Training of ear surgery in the temporal bone is mandatory in all structured training programs globally in the field of ear, nose and throat (ENT) surgery. The human temporal bone has a remarkably complex anatomy harboring structures responsible for hearing and balance. Notably ear surgeries are performed with the aid of an operating microscope under magnification. The key surgical procedures on the temporal bone include mastoidectomy or tympanomastoidectomy. However, compared to traditional "go-and-see" surgery, ear surgeons have to be familiar with microanatomic landmarks e.g. honeycomb bone cells and major blood vessel in order to access target via the tiny surgical entrance (incision) without hurting important tissue like the facial nerve within and the brain in its immediate vicinity. Error of the scale of 1 mm may result in total deafness, loss of balance and facial paralysis. An effective training platform for shortening learning curves of novice clinicians is thus indispensible. Current training platform include the use of human cadaveric bones which are not easily available nowadays while cadaveric bone training means simulation on static normal conditions; there is a call for more real life training with dynamics/pathologies like virtual reality (VR) training for flight pilots. This research will be using VR with reference to a database of ultra-high resolution virtual human head and neck datasets for the learner to interactively localize and operate on the target in a virtual space. We will simulate essential mastoidectomy procedures including middle ear pathway constructing, cauterizing, target (e.g. cholesteatoma) removing, suction and suturing; all these involve extensive soft-tissue deformation and thermo/haemo-dynamics. The research issues to be addressed include image segmentation, 3D anatomical model reconstruction, biomechanical modeling, realistic visualization as well as multi-sensory human-computer interaction. To summarize, this is a joint project between a pioneer VR development team and a leading ear surgery team in Hong Kong. We aim to construct a training system with a simulated stereoscopy of microsurgical view, in real-time to the operator’s eyes on a simulated microscope performing mastoid surgery on a life-like mannequin with dynamics/pathologies. The proposed system is anticipated to strengthen and compensate existing microsurgical education and training as well as to become a training standard for existing and future surgeons.

412412.label: Realisation of objectives
412412.value: In this project, we have developed a virtual reality learning system that matches the original project objectives to facilitate the training of otorhinolaryngology trainee surgeons in learning microsurgical incision skills. Key research and development issues addressed in this project include multimodal medical image segmentation and analysis, anatomical model reconstruction, force feedback interaction, interactive interface, and surgical simulation system for anatomy learning. In our developed prototype, interactive navigation of ultra-high resolution Chinese Visible Human (CVH) data is presented to user, while performing a simulated mastoidectomy procedure involving extensive soft-tissue deformation and thermo/haemo-dynamics. We have designed a series of deep neural network based methods to detect microanatomic biomarkers from MR images; such detected microanatomic biomarkers can be further used for anatomical model reconstruction. We have implemented a sparse coding based probabilistic model to segment tumor from MR images. This model can be extended to segment other anatomical structures. We have also proposed a deep contour-aware network to segment glands from histology images. We have proposed an effective framework with the consideration of the piecewise consistent property of the two normal fields to denoise and refine the 3D anatomical models. We have extended the quadric error metrics and integrated it into a mesh denoising framework to smooth bony mastoid models. We have also proposed an optimization of the local spatial quadrics of Bezier surfaces to remove artifacts on general anatomical models while maintaining morphological features. We have proposed an effective medical-oriented smoothing method for eliminating the artifacts on anatomical models, and further proposed a stable and fast point shell collision detection algorithm for haptic rendering. This method is able to smoothly represent key features of the force sensation changing in the drilling process. In order to facilitate intuitive anatomy learning, we have developed a prototype virtual reality learning system with interactive interface. We have proposed a meshless approach for deformable tissue-tissue interaction. Furthermore, an evaluation framework is implemented to evaluate the thermal damage to bone tissue during the bone drilling process.

412412.label: Major findings and research outcome
412412.value: Altogether 4 journal papers and 10 conference papers relevant to this project have been generated. A summary of major findings are given under the following categories: Medical image segmentation and analysis – • In [J04], we propose a 3D convolutional neural network to detect microanatomic biomarkers from MR images. • In [C02], we extend the stacked auto-encoder neural network to achieve low dose X-ray image restoration. • In [C05], we utilize 3D hierarchical features extracted via an independent subspace analysis network to label microanatomic biomarkers in MR images. • In [C06], we propose a multimodal sparse coding based probabilistic model to segment tumor from brain MR images. • In [C07], we utilize deep learning based 3D feature representation to detect microanatomic biomarkers from MR images. • In [C10], we propose a deep contour-aware network to segment glands from histology images. Geometrical modeling – • In [J01], we take advantage of the piecewise consistent property of the two normal fields and propose an effective framework to guide the mesh denoising process. The method can be directly extended to post-process 3D medical models. • In [J02], we propose a feature-preserving mesh denoising framework by employing an extension of the quadric error metrics. This method is particularly useful in denoising bony mastoid models. • In [J03], we solve the morphology-preserving problem of anatomical structures as an optimization of the local spatial quadrics of fitted Bezier surfaces during mesh evolution. This method is able to preserve the morphology of anatomical models. • In [C01], we propose a novel smoothing framework to remove artifacts on general medical mesh models while maintaining morphological features. Force feedback interaction – • In [C04], we propose an effective medical-oriented smoothing algorithm to eliminate the artifacts on mesh models and employ it on haptic rendering. • In [C08], we propose a novel point shell collision detection algorithm for haptic rendering. With this method, key features of the force sensation changing in the drilling process can be represented in a smooth way. Interactive interface – • In [C09], we propose a meshless approach for soft tissue deformation in virtual surgery, where an efficient tissue-tissue interaction scheme is designed for interacting deformable bodies. Surgical simulation system – • In [C03], we propose a framework to evaluate the thermal damage to bone tissue during the bone drilling process.

412412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412412.value: In our future work, we aim to annotate the microanatomic landmarks in the virtual ear environment, conduct more in-depth system evaluations and extend our system to other microsurgical applications. Such a virtual surgical system can truly provide an intuitive learning of ear surgery in the temporal bone based on ultra-fine resolution Chinese Visible Human data. Our proposed course of actions include – • Collaborate with otorhinolaryngology surgeons and physicians for further evaluation and refinement of our existing prototypes. • Provide software licensing for educational purpose and beta testing. • Search for industrial collaborators for technology transfer in the area of virtual microscopic surgery and virtual microscopic anatomy learning. • Continue to seek new research grants to further our research in virtual reality anatomy and surgical simulation.

Training of ear surgery in the temporal bone is mandatory in all structured training programs in the field of ear, nose and throat surgery. Therefore, ear surgeons have to possess a firm knowledge of microanatomy in order to access target via the tiny surgical incision without hurting important tissue. An effective training system for shortening learning curves of novice clinicians is thus indispensible.
