412612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412612.value: The aim of this proposal is to investigate the oxidative potential of PM10 and PM2.5 emissions from several major indoor sources via the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) on the cellular level and identify the chemical components responsible for the toxicity of PM10 and PM2.5. Although we typically spend 80-90% of our time indoors, indoor particulate matter (PM) is yet to be investigated as intensely or as systematically as outdoor PM. Reliable scientific data on the levels of fine particles in indoor pollution sources and the extent to which people are exposed to them, are essential in evaluating the potential effects of indoor pollutants on human health. The physicochemical characteristics free radical generation by anthropogenically derived PM is the primary source of oxidative stress and have the potential to cause cell dysfunction and inflammation. PM-associated ROS generation is the focus in the ongoing efforts to understand the mechanisms of the observed adverse health effects associated with PM. In this study, PM10 and PM2.5 samples from four major indoor sources including cooking fume, cleaning products, cigarette smoke and incense smoke will be collected by different sampling methods. Physical (size and surface area) and chemical characteristics (soot, metals, PAHs, quinones, and carbonyls) measurements will be conducted and various bioassays will be carried out to determine the bioreactivity of different PM source samples in association with their physicochemical characteristics. The effects of indoor air pollutants continue to receive high level of interest within the scientific, regulatory and public communities. This study will address some critical gaps in the understanding of how indoor pollution sources contribute to human health problems. Currently local indoor emission data is not available in Hong Kong and this research will contribute in furthering the understanding in how indoor pollution sources contribute to human health problems. It will also serve as a scientific baseline for formulating effective control strategies for indoor air pollution. 本项目旨在：（1）研究室内主要污染源排放的可吸入颗粒物（PM10）和细颗粒物（PM2.5）与细胞作用产生活性氧自由基(ROS)的氧化潜势;(2)识别室内PM10和PM2.5的有毒化学成分。人们有80-90%的时间在室内度过，但是对室内颗粒物（PM）的研究远不如对室外颗粒的研究系统、集中。获得室内主要污染源产生的颗粒物浓度水平以及人体对颗粒物的暴露水平数据，对评估室内污染物对人体健康的影响具有重要意义。人为源颗粒物引发产生的自由基是氧化应激的重要来源，这些自由基有可能导致细胞功能紊乱及诱发炎症。研究颗粒物的活性氧自由基的生成对理解颗粒物的毒理作用机理具有重要意义。 在本研究中，将采用不同的采样技术分别收集室内主要污染源，包括烹饪，清洁用品，吸烟和焚香产生的PM10和PM2.5样品。通过研究颗粒物的物理性质（粒径与表面积）和化学特征（炭黑，金属，多环芳烃，醌类及醛酮类）、开展不同种类的生物毒性测试，从而建立不同源颗粒物生物活性和颗粒物理化特征之间的联系。室内空气污染物的健康效应一直引起科学界、政府监管部门以及公众的高度关注，人们关于室内污染源对人体健康影响的了解严重匮乏，本研究将填补这项空白。目前香港没有现成的室内污染物排放因子，本研究的开展将有助于进一步认识室内污染源对人体健康的重要性。此外，本研究结果也是未来香港制定室内空气污染有效控制策略的科学基准。

412612.label: Realisation of objectives
412612.value: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) samples from four major indoor sources include, cooking fume, cleaning products, cigarette smoke, incense smoke were collected. The analysis focused on comprehensive physicochemical characteristics (morphology of the particulate matter (PM), metals, organic/elemental carbon, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and carbonyls) in the determined samples. The above mentioned indoor samples were further determined by different toxicity assays. Plasmid scission assay (PSA) was applied to assess the percentage oxidative DNA damage caused by the PM. Reactive oxygen species (ROS, determined by dichlorodihydrofluorescein (DCFH) assay), proinflammatory cytokine (IL-6 and TNF-α), cell viability and phases of the cell cycle, in addition to 8-hydroxydeoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) were all analyzed. Pearson's correlation coefficient analysis was performed to identify the correlation between (1) oxidative stress and inflammation and (2) chemical species with oxidative-inflammation cytokines. The targets have been achieved with an overwhelming success. The outcome so far were all published in various high impact factor journals and further results will follow suit. Nevertheless, the targeted secondary organic aerosol (SOA) generated from cleaning products have reached unexpected outcome. The anticipated concentrations of secondary aerosol in the cleaning products were below detection limits of the analytical instruments. An alternative investigation of ozone-initiated formation of indoor secondary organic aerosols with D-limonene (one of the reactive organic components in cleaning products) in environmental chamber was performed with success. The results were published in a relevant journal with the collaboration of Institute of Earth Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences (IEECAS) (Niu et al., 2017).

412612.label: Major findings and research outcome
412612.value: The chemical and toxicological properties of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) emitted during controlled burning of different indoor sources were characterized from the outcome. The toxicological effects of exposure to smoke from traditional and marketed environmentally friendly types of incense were investigated in this study. The results suggested the marketed environmentally friendly incense generated less PM2.5. However, mixed results were shown for toxic organic pollutants emissions. Several polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and oxygenated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (OPAHs) species were strongly correlated with inflammatory responses (Lui et al., 2016). Monoterpenes, a well-known class of biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) which are widely used as a fragrance in cleaning products, was investigated in this study. The study focused on investigations of ozone-initiated formation of indoor secondary organic aerosols (SOAs) with D-limonene (one of the monoterpenes in cleaning product), in a large environmental chamber. Our results demonstrated that the presence of NH3 could significantly enhance the SOAs formation, with higher levels of TNF-α and IL-6 factors. There was also 22–39% stronger pulmonary inflammatory effect on the particles generated with ammonia (NH3) (Niu et al., 2017). Aside from the proposed indoor sources, domestic indoor coal burning was a proven risk factor for lung cancer in past studies. The effects of PM2.5 emitted from coal combustion on EGFR-TKI response in vitro and the relationships between PM2.5-bound organic compounds (PAHs and their polar derivatives (OPAHs and AZAs)) and EGFR-TKI response were investigated in the study. Samples showed significant and dose-dependent reduction in the cell viability in A549. EGFR-TKI further demonstrated significantly decreased in cell viability in A549 after exposure to the coal emissions (Ho et al., 2016[5]). The chemical composition and bioreactivity of ambient PM2.5 samples collected from Beijing (BJ), Xi'an (XA), Xiamen (XM) and Hong Kong (HK) in China during haze events were characterized in the study. The oxidative potential levels were BJ > XM > XA > HK, whereas levels of IL-6, IFN-γ and TNF-α were BJ > XA > XM > HK. The sulfate, nitrate, ammonium, organic carbon (OC), urea and levoglucosan were associated with oxidative-inflammatory responses (Ho et al., 2016[6]). Biological pathways were identified by proteomic profiling in mouse lungs, the results suggested that WNT/b-catenin was important in the response to haze PM2.5. Decreased WNT/b-catenin expression modulated by haze PM2.5 could be involved in alveolar destruction and inflammation during haze episodes (Lee et al., 2015).

412612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412612.value: This study demonstrated the toxicities of indoor secondary organic aerosols (SOAs) formed from ozonolysis of monoterpene (D-limonene). The finding is important for further indoor air quality (IAQ) investigations. Many studies have focused on the in vitro or in vivo biological effects of specific indoor or outdoor sources. The pitfalls were to put too much emphasis on the primary emissions. The particulate and gaseous source emissions could undergo different chemical reactions/transformations once emitted to the atmosphere. It is fair to postulate that the secondary and primary pollutants can exhibit different toxicities. Several studies have shown that atmospheric aging of particulate pollutants could modify chemical composition of air pollution mixtures, resulting different toxicological potential. Further studies showed that atmospheric photochemical reactions of primary emissions could cause the formation of secondary organic aerosol (SOA), in addition to the alteration of toxicity and mutagenicity of PAH, potentially via the formation of nitro- or oxy-PAH derivatives. Therefore, it is important to have further investigations on the toxicological effects of secondary formed air pollutants.

412612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412612.value: The effects of indoor air pollutants continue to receive attentions from the scientific, regulatory, and public communities. There is a paucity of information on indoor emission data in Hong Kong and this research study contributed a better understanding of how indoor pollution sources relate to human health problems. The chemical and toxicological properties of PM2.5 from different indoor sources were determined in this study. For example, the marketed environmentally friendly incenses generated less PM2.5. Mixed results were identified in other organic compounds emissions. In addition, toxic pollutants (PAHs and OPAHs) were strongly correlated with inflammatory responses which indicated that high exposure of environmentally friendly incense smoke may also trigger health problems. In addition, the results in this study demonstrated that the secondary formed particles contained high levels of inflammation markers. There was 22–39% stronger pulmonary inflammatory effect on the particles generated from ozonolysis of D-limonene (one of the organic components in cleaning product)) with ammonia. The outcome can be used to understand indoor air pollutant sources and corresponding chemical and biological properties. The results can serve as a scientific baseline for formulating effective control strategies regarding with indoor air pollution in Hong Kong and China.

412812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412812.value: The nonlinear output regulation problem is a formulation of many complex control problems such as the vibration suppression of the high speed train, attitude control of the flight vehicles, landing of aircraft on carriers under severe weather condition, and so on. As a result, this problem has been one of the central research topics in nonlinear control for over two decades. In particular, in the recent 10 years, intensive efforts from the control community have been made on studying the global version of this problem without knowing the exosystem exactly, and various results have been obtained for some special classes of nonlinear systems such as output feedback systems, strict feedback systems, and strict feedforward systems. Nevertheless, so far almost all global results are limited to single-input single-output (SISO) nonlinear systems. The main reason is that a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) system may be structurally much more complicated than an SISO system and the key technique for constructing global controllers for SISO nonlinear systems may not be effective to MIMO systems due to the strong coupling of different control channels. However, many practical systems are MIMO systems. There is thus a real need for developing systematic approaches to handling MIMO nonlinear systems. To meet this challenge, we propose to study the global robust output regulation problem for a class of MIMO uncertain nonlinear systems subject to uncertain exosystems. This class of systems is motivated from the speed tracking and disturbance rejection problem of the surface-mounted PM synchronous motor. Thus, an application of our main result will also lead to the solution of a challenging practical control problem. On the other hand, this class of nonlinear systems is general enough to include the class of MIMO strict feedback systems as a special case and is also complex enough to contain systems that do not admit a normal form. Thus the proposed problem is intellectually challenging and academically interesting. Moreover, in order to solve our problem, we need to develop some systematic technique that is applicable to MIMO uncertain nonlinear systemss. We expect that this technique has also potential to handle some other classes of nonlinear systems, and are applicable to some other complex MIMO nonlinear systems such as the non-surface-mounted PM synchronous motor. In summary, the success of this project will not only significantly advance nonlinear control research but also enhance our capability to handle practical uncertain nonlinear systems. 非线性输出调节问题是过去二十多年来的非线性控制的核心问题之一。尤其在近十年来，控制界对含不确定外部系统的全局非线性输出调节问题投入了极大的精力并对诸如输出反馈系统，反馈系统，前馈系统等特殊类别的非线性系统获得若干结果。 目前几乎所有研究仅适用于单输入单输出非线性系统，然而众多实际非线性控制系统却具有多个输入与输出。因此研发能针对多输入多输出非线性系统的方法具有实际意义。本项目将研究一类不确定多输入多输出非线性系统的全局鲁棒输出调节问题。该类系统源于直流异步电动机的速度跟踪与抗干扰问题。因此，该项目的成功实施将直接解决一个深具挑战性的实际控制问题。另一方面，该系统不仅包含了多输入多输出反馈系统，也包含了不具有标准型的非线性系统，所以该系统的类别足够广泛，足够复杂。因此该项目的研究问题具有挑战性且具有学术意义。此外，为解决本问题，本项目执行人需研发能对付不确定多输入多输出非线性系统的系统化工具，这些工具将有效提高人们控制不确定多输入多输出非线性控制系统的能力。

412812.label: Major findings and research outcome
412812.value: The key of this project is to solve the global robust output regulation problem for a class of MIMO uncertain nonlinear systems subject to uncertain exosystems, and then apply the theoretical result to the speed tracking and disturbance rejection problem of the surface mounted PM synchronous motor without knowing the frequency of the reference trajectory. By the last Progress report, we had successfully accomplished this key objective. The major findings were summarized as follows: The surface-mounted permanent-magnet synchronous motor is a two-input, two-output nonlinear system. The multi-input, multi-output nature of the system has posed some specific challenges to various control methods. In particular, when the system is subject to an unknown exosystem, the augmented system contains linearly parameterized uncertainty, and hence is not input-to-state stable. By utilizing some dynamic coordinate transformation technique, and combining some robust control and adaptive control techniques, we have successfully solve the problem via a recursive approach. The results were reported in the following papers: Z. Ping, and J. Huang, “Speed tracking control of surface-mounted PM synchronous motor with unknown exosystem,” International Journal of Robust and Nonlinear Control, Vol. 25, No. 8, May 2015, pp. 1247-1264. Z. Ping and J. Huang, “A control problem of surface-mounted PM synchronous motor with unknown exosystem,” Proceedings of the 2013 American Control Conference, Washington, DC, USA, June 17-19, 2013, pp. 217-222. The research results under this project also directly contributed to four chapters of the following book: Zhiyong Chen and Jie Huang, Stabilization and Regulation: Robust and Adaptive Approach, Springer, 2015, Additionally, we have further expanded the scope of the research to study the cooperative control problems for multi-agent systems via a distributed control scheme. The multi-agent system is a special class of multi-input, multi-output systems. What makes the control of such systems more challenging than the conventional systems is that the control law has to be distributed in order to overcome the communication constraints. We have focused on two cooperative control problems for multi-agent systems. The first one is the leader-following connectivity preservation rendezvous of multi-agent systems. These findings have led to two journal papers in IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, and Automatica, respectively. The second problem is the cooperative robust output regulation for nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems and had led to four other papers.

412812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412812.value: The output regulation problem aims to design a controller which not only achieves the closed-loop system stability, but also enable the output of the closed-loop system to asymptotically track a class of reference inputs and reject a class of disturbances. Here both reference inputs and disturbances are generated by an uncertain exosystem. Some typical control problems that can be formulated as output regulation problem include vibration suppression of the high speed train, attitude control of spacecraft, landing of aircraft on carriers under severe weather condition, and speed control and disturbance attenuation of the permanent magnet (PM) synchronous motor. As a result, the nonlinear output regulation problem has been a focus of the research in nonlinear control community for over two decades. Nevertheless, despite intensive efforts from nonlinear control community for over two decades, so far almost all global results are limited to single-input single-output (SISO) nonlinear systems. However, many practical systems are MIMO systems. In this project, we have studied the global robust output regulation problem for a class of MIMO uncertain nonlinear systems subject to uncertain exosystems, and applied our main results to the speed tracking and disturbance rejection problem of the surface-mounted PM synchronous motor.

413212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
413212.value: 具有位置信息的基於分解方法的在線推薦模型框架

413212.label: Project Objectives
413212.value: The first objective is to develop effective online recommendation algorithms with social information. Traditional recommender systems assume that users are independent and identically distributed. This assumption ignores the social trust or friend relationships among the users. We plan to develop effective and efficient probabilistic matrix factorization methods to improve recommender systems by incorporating users' social information. We will develop on-line learning algorithms to learn latent user factors and item factors. Complete experimental analysis will be conducted to evaluate proposed methods on large scale data sources we collected. The second objective is to enable the proposed recommendation methods to incorporate location information. One strength of matrix factorization is that it allows incorporation of additional information. When social network information is not available, we hope our recommendation algorithms can infer user preferences using some location information without changing the models. The involvement of these data sources can further improve the recommendation quality.

413212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413212.value: As the exponential growth of information generated on the World WideWeb, Recommender Systems have become more and more important. Recommender systems form a specific type of information filtering technique that attempts to suggest information items that are likely to interest the users. Aiming at modeling recommender systems more accurately and realistically, in this project we propose to investigate On-line Recommendation with Social and Location Information problem. The key characteristic different from other challenging problems is the availability of (1) dynamic updating recommendation algorithms to fit potential interest for users in on-line scenarios and (2) effective online algorithms with location information. Several important components will be investigated in this on-line recommendation project. A general online framework for recommender systems would be investigated to update incrementally and automatically the knowledge base obtained from historical usage data and to generate a list of recommendations of potentially interest for the user. Second, the issue of how to incorporate location information and how to make it an on-line algorithm would be explored. 由於在萬維網上產生的信息呈指數級增長，推薦系統變得越來越重要。推薦系統形成了一種可以向用戶推薦他們可能感興趣的項目的特定類型的信息濾波技術。 為了建立更準確、更現實的推薦系統模型，在此項目中，我們提出研究具有社交和位置信息的在線推薦問題。不同於其他具有挑戰的問題，這裡考慮的關鍵特性包括（1）在線情況下，動態更新推薦算法滿足用戶的潛在興趣和（2）帶位置信息的有效在線學習算法。 在這個在線推薦項目中，我們將調研幾個重要組件。首先，我們將調研一個通用的在線推薦系統把從歷史獲得的可用數據以自動增量的方式更新其知識庫，並且為用戶推薦其潛在的感興趣的列表。其次，我們將探討如何引入位置信息，以及如何將此信息設計成在線算法。

413212.label: Realisation of objectives
413212.value: We highlight a few key and major findings that help to realize our objectives to incorporate social and location information in recommender systems in order to improve their accuracy without sacrificing the performance. In the work entitled, "A topic-biased user reputation model in rating systems", we incorporate User Reputation (UR) to improve the accuracy of estimated item scores in rating systems like Epinions and Amazon’s product review systems. Moreover, we propose a topic-biased model (TBM) to estimate UR in terms of different topics as well as item scores. With TBM, we develop six topic-biased algorithms, which are subsequently evaluated with experiments using both real-world and synthetic data sets. Results of the experiments demonstrate that the topic-biased algorithms effectively estimate UR across different topics and produce more robust item scores than previous reputation-based algorithms, leading to potentially more robust rating systems. In the work entitled, "Boosting Response Aware Model-Based Collaborative Filtering", we introduce the response aware probabilistic matrix factorization (RAPMF) framework to overcome these several challenging issues in collaborative filtering (CF) methods in recommender systems. First, most CF methods ignore users’ response patterns and may yield biased parameter estimation and suboptimal performance. Second, some CF methods adopt heuristic weight settings, which lacks a systematical implementation. Third, the multinomial mixture models may weaken the computational ability of matrix factorization for generating the data matrix, thus increasing the computational cost of training. Furthermore, we speed up the algorithm by a mini-batch implementation and a crafting scheduling policy. Finally, we design different experimental protocols and conduct a systematical empirical evaluation on both synthetic and real-world datasets to demonstrate the merits of the proposed RAPMF and its mini-batch implementation. In the work entitled, "Capturing Geographical Influence in POI Recommendations", we propose two models—Gaussian mixture model (GMM) and genetic algorithm based Gaussian mixture model (GA-GMM) to capture geographical influence. More specifically, we exploit GMM to automatically learn users’ activity centers; furthermore, we utilize GA-GMM to improve GMM by eliminating outliers. Experimental results on a real-world LBSN dataset show that GMM beats several popular geographical capturing models in terms of POI recommendation, while GA-GMM excludes the effect of outliers and enhances GMM. Whether recommended locations meet users’ interests depends on three factors: user preference, social influence, and geographical influence. Hence extracting the information from users’ check-in records is the key to POI recommendation in LBSNs. Capturing user preference and social influence is relatively easy since it is analogical to the methods in a movie recommender system. However, it is a new topic to capture geographical influence. Previous studies indicate that check-in locations disperse around several centers and we are able to employ Gaussian distribution based models to approximate users’ check-in behaviors. Yet centers discovering methods are dissatisfactory. This research work has overcome this difficulty. In "Gradient Boosting Factorization Machines", we utilize auxiliary information as additional features to improve recommendation performance. We refer to recommendation with auxiliary information as context-aware recommendation. Context-aware Factorization Machines (FM) is one of the most successful context-aware recommendation models. FM models pairwise interactions between all features, in such way, a certain feature latent vector is shared to compute the factorized parameters it involved. In practice, there are tens of context features and not all the pair-wise feature interactions are useful. Thus, one important challenge for context-aware recommendation is how to effectively select “good” interaction features. In this work, we focus on solving this problem and propose a greedy interaction feature selection algorithm based on gradient boosting. Then we propose a novel Gradient Boosting Factorization Machine (GBFM) model to incorporate feature selection algorithm with Factorization Machines into a unified framework. The experimental results on both synthetic and real datasets demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness of our algorithm compared to other state-of-the-art methods. Social network plays a vital role in Chinese business and is highly valued by business people. However, social network analysis is difficult due to issues in data collection, natural language processing, social network detection and construction, relationship mining, etc. In this research, we develop the Corporate Leaders Analytics and Network System (CLANS) to tackle some of these problems. Our contributions are as follows. First, we collect data from multiple sources and do the preprocessing to make it available to use. Second, we construct a business social network and formulate the similarity relations among individuals and corporations. Third, we conduct further data mining to discover more implicit information, including important entities finding, relation mining and shortest path finding. In "SCMF: Sparse Covariance Matrix Factorization for Collaborative Filtering", existing Matrix Factorization (MF) methods either assume that all latent features are uncorrelated or assume that all are correlated. To address the important issue of what structure should be imposed on the features, we investigate the covariance matrix of the latent features learned from real data. Based on the findings, we propose an MF model with a sparse covariance prior which favors a sparse yet non-diagonal covariance matrix. Not only can this reflect the semantics more faithfully, but imposing sparsity can also have a side effect of preventing overfitting. Starting from a probabilistic generative model with a sparse covariance prior, we formulate the model inference problem as a maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problem. The optimization procedure makes use of stochastic gradient descent and majorization-minimization. For empirical validation, we conduct experiments using the MovieLens and Netflix datasets to compare the proposed method with two strong baselines which use different priors. Experimental results show that our sparse covariance prior can lead to performance improvement. In "TaskRec: A Task Recommendation Framework in Crowdsourcing Systems", we propose a Task Recommendation (TaskRec) framework based on a unified probabilistic matrix factorization, aiming to recommend tasks to workers in dynamic scenarios. Unlike traditional recommendation systems, workers do not provide their ratings on tasks in crowdsourcing systems, thus we infer user ratings from their interacting behaviors. This conversion helps task recommendation in crowdsourcing systems. Complexity analysis shows that our framework is efficient and is scalable to large datasets. Finally, we conduct experiments on real-world datasets for performance evaluation. Experimental results show that TaskRec outperforms the state-of-the-art approach. There are more works that help to realize the objective of using social and location information to improve accuracy and performance in recommender systems. Nonetheless, we believe the aforementioned works are representative of the research undertook by this proposal.

413212.label: Major findings and research outcome
413212.value: From our research, we are able to incorporate social and location information into recommender systems based on matrix factorization techniques to improve their accuracy as well as performance through the demonstration of experimental results. The proposed and completed research herewithin has led to four journal papers, eight international conference papers, two PhD students graduated, and one workshop organized in WSDM'15, Shanghai. More specifically, some of the conference papers are published in top internationally renowned venues such as Neural Information Processing System (NIPS), International joint Conference in Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI), Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI), etc. The research also led to the organization of a workshop named, "Scalable Data Analytics: Theory and Applications" that was held at WSDM'15, Shanghai, China. Lastly, the research also helped at least two PhD candidates to complete their studies.

413212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413212.value: We have done work in incorporating social as well as location information into recommender systems. The next phase would be to include other features or context-based information, e.g., time data, behavior data, intention data, etc. for better prediction. We can also further explore in various algorithms and models that can use these additional features without losing the accuracy. Moreover, the scalability of these algorithms and models should also be investigated as there are many ways to handle the scalability issues such as sampling, parallelism, dimensionality reduction, function transformation, etc.

413212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413212.value: In the past, recommender systems assume each user is independent and identically distributed without considering their inter-relationships nor other features. This proposed and completed research investigates a recommender system framework that incorporates social as well as location information to achieve a better ranking of items for recommendation purpose. One interesting system that we have worked on is the Corporate Leaders Analytics and Network System (CLANS). This is a system where we integrate traditional database information with crawled social media information of corporate leaders from Chinese listed companies. This system allows a person to retrieve not only facts from company's annual report but also can obtain the latest news of the person from popular social media with information of their social communities, e.g., schoolmate, classmate, colleagues, etc. One other application is to predict where a user would like to go next based on the user's historical as well as the user's current information. This has a wide range of potential application in next point-of-interest prediction, traffic routing, traffic balancing, etc.

414012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414012.value: Current IP networks are evolved from data networks that primarily support best effort services only; however, real-time voice and video applications call for much stringent quality of service (QoS) requirements. The bursty nature of internet traffic imposes challenge on utilizing the network bandwidth efficiently. If bursts are provided with redundant bandwidth, the service requirement can be satisfied at a price of low bandwidth utilization. Another challenge is the operational complexity in current IP networks with explosive increase of traffic demand. Electronic routers suffer from bottlenecks due to limited packet processing speed and huge power consumption for the execution of routing and switching. In the light of above considerations, this project aims to design a scalable network architecture, which can handle burst traffic gracefully through low-complexity network operations. We propose a hybrid network: a combination of a scheduled sub-network with virtual circuit switching and a stochastic sub-network with deflection routing. The network can provide stringent QoS guarantees for regulated traffic by dedicated virtual circuits, while best effort for bursty traffic by deflection routing. In the scheduled sub-network, the end-to-end route assignments for virtual circuits are quasi-static. In the stochastic sub-network, burst packets are randomly deflected to neighbor nodes, instead of on-line looking up for next-hop routers. Therefore, the target network has the potential to reduce routing and scheduling complexity at intermediate nodes, which in turn make routers scalable to larger network topology and higher capacity. The project will investigate design, modeling and evaluation of the proposed network architecture. Specifically, the objectives of this project are: (1) Traffic shaping based on two-rate leaky bucket mechanism; (2) Design a hybrid network architecture to provide differential QoS guarantees for diverse internet traffic; (3) Optimal bandwidth allocation and route assignment; (4) Analyze the network performance in terms of throughput, delay and packet loss probability. 當前的IP網絡僅限於最大限度地提供網絡數據服務；然而，實時音視頻應用需要更加嚴格的服務質量(QoS)保證。網絡流量的突發性給提高帶寬利用率造成了很大的挑戰。如果能為突發的流量提供冗餘帶寬，便能以低帶寬利用率來換取服務質量。 當前的IP網絡的另一個挑戰是隨著流量需求的爆炸性增長帶來的操作複雜度。電子路由器的發展瓶頸源於處理數據包時的有限速度和執行路由和交換時的巨大功耗。 鑑於上述考慮，該項目旨在設計一個可以平緩處理突發性流量同時具備低操作複雜度的可擴展的網絡架構。我們提出混合網絡架構：由一個虛電路交換的調度子網絡和一個偏轉路由的隨機子網絡構成。該網絡的虛電路部分能為規則流量提供嚴格的服務質量（QoS）保證，同時偏轉路由部分能很好的處理突發性流量。在調度子網絡中，虛電路的端對端路由分配是準靜態的；在隨機子網絡中，突發的數據包會被隨機的偏轉到附近的節點，而不是繼續等待尋找下一跳的路由。因此，該混合網絡有可能減少中間節點的路由規劃複雜度，從而可擴展到更大的網絡架構和更高的網絡容量。 該項目將研究所提出的網絡架構的設計、建模和性能評估。具體的項目目標是：(1)基於雙速率漏桶控制機制的流量調整；(2)設計一個混合網絡架構能為各種網絡流量提供不同的服務質量（QoS）保證；(3)優化帶寬分配和路由分配；(4)分析網絡性能，包括吞吐量、延遲和丟包率。

414012.label: Realisation of objectives
414012.value: Due to the retirement of Prof. Lee, there is a change of PI of the project in 2013. In spite of the change, the project was completed smoothly. Overall, five journal papers and three conference papers were published based on research outcomes of this project. For the first objective, the research work concentrated on a finite buffer queueing model which has a two-phase Markov modulated service process (MMSP). The fading channels with finite input buffer, Poisson arrivals and two-state Markov modulated service processes (MMSP) are modelled as M/MMSP/1/K queues in this project. Existing performance analyses of Markov channels are almost all based on the matrix-geometric method, which provides little physical insights for system design. By contrast, we focus on deriving closed-form analytic expressions with physical interpretations in terms of system parameters of interest. Our main contribution is to derive the generalized Pollaczek-Khinchin (P-K) formula of M/MMSP/1/K queue from start-service probability to explore the impact of state transitions on the queueing behavior of Markov channels. A paper summarizing the result was published in the IEEE Transactions on Communications. As explained in our previous report, due to administrative delays, the official start date of this project was postponed while the research work had started some time earlier. As a result, the paper was submitted a few days ahead of the formal project start date. But the paper had undergone two major revisions during the project period. For the second task, two problems were investigated, one on the stability and delay analysis of the Ethernet Passive Optical Network (EPON) registration protocol, the other on a perturbation algorithm for embedding virtual data center in multipath networks. The Ethernet passive optical network (EPON) has recently emerged as the mainstream of broadband access networks. The registration process of EPON, which is defined by the IEEE 802.3av standard, is a multi-point control protocol within the media access control layer. As with other contention-based channel access methods, such as ALOHA and CSMA, stability and delay are critical issues concerning the performances of implementing the protocol on systems with finite channel capacity. In this work, the registration process of an EPON subscriber, called optical network units (ONUs), is modelled as a discrete-time Markov chain, from which we derive the fundamental throughput equation of EPON that characterizes the registration processes. A paper summarizing the result is published in the IEEE Transactions on Communications. Network virtualization supports predicted network performance for applications by providing tenants with a virtual data center in multi-tenant data centers. The Hose model was recently extended for the virtual network abstraction and deployed in an Oktopus system, which offers the trade-off between cost and network performance. Embedding algorithms based on Oktopus model were well studied in the single-root tree topology. We investigated congestion-aware allocation of virtual data centers in multipath networks. First, we formulated bandwidth constraints with linear programming, and provide a complete solution with exhaustive searching. Next, to reduce time complexity, we proposed a perturbation algorithm to VM placement, which detects the bandwidth bottleneck of the current virtual machine placement and then adjusts the assignment to reduce congestion. The perturbation algorithm is compatible with both load-balanced and single-path routing algorithms. A paper summarizing the result is published in Globecom 2014 - Symposium on Selected Areas in Communications. For the third task, the project focused on AWG-based non-blocking Clos networks. The three-stage Clos networks remain the most popular solution to many practical switching systems to date. The aim of this paper is to show that the modular structure of Clos networks is invariant with respect to the technological changes. Due to the wavelength routing property of arrayed-waveguide gratings (AWGs), non-blocking and contention-free wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) switches require that two calls carried by the same wavelength must be connected by separated links; otherwise, they must be carried by different wavelengths. Thus, in addition to the non-blocking condition, the challenge of the design of AWG-based multistage switching networks is to scale down the wavelength granularity and to reduce the conversion range of tuneable wavelength converters (TWCs). We devised a logic scheme to partition the WDM switch network into wavelength autonomous cells and show that the wavelength scalability problem can be solved by recursively reusing similar, but smaller, set of wavelengths in different cells. A paper summarizing the result is published in the IEEE Transactions on Communications. For the fourth task, the project focused on the wavelength allocation algorithms in Wavelength Switched Optical Networks, such as Coronet. We examined the question of wavelength reservation protocols in WDM networks. Our algorithm is a hybrid between source-initiated reservation (SIR) and destination-initiated reservation (DIR). The approach is based on based designing allocation sequences with special correlation properties to minimize the probability of conflicts on different lightpaths. The issue of avoidance of conflicts in schedules is closely related to the question of conflict avoidance code design. Based on these work, we published one paper on wavelength reservation protocol and two papers on related topics in conflict avoidance codes in Designs, Codes and Cryptography based on work from the project. We also studied the mutual interference problem of a visible light communication system. A paper summarizing the result was awarded the Best Paper Award at the 10th International Symposium on Communication Systems, Networks and Digital Signal Processing.

414012.label: Major findings and research outcome
414012.value: Generalized Pollaczek-Khinchin Formula for Markov Channels, IEEE Transactions on Communications, Vol 61(8), 2013: Our generalized formula reveals that the performance of wireless channels with varying rates can be fully characterized by a newly defined system parameter, called state transition factor β, which explains the reason that the channel with slow state transition rate owns a larger delay for the same channel capacity. In the extreme case when the state transition factor β approaches 0, we show that the channel under consideration can be approximately modeled as an M/G/1 queue. We use the Type I Hybrid ARQ system with a fixed data-rate as an example in this paper to illustrate our results. Stability and Delay Analysis of EPON Registration Protocol, IEEE Transactions on Communications, Vol 62(7), 2014: By solving the characteristic function, we obtain the maximum waiting time region that makes the registration protocol stable. If the maximum waiting time is selected from this region, we show that a stable registration throughput and a bounded registration delay can be guaranteed. Our results also indicate that it is unnecessary to arbitrarily enlarge the maximum waiting time as long as it is in the stable region since the improvement of registration delay is marginal, yet the reduction of registration efficiency is significant. AWG-Based Non-Blocking Clos Networks, IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking, Vol 23(2), 2015: We proved that the rearrangeably non-blocking condition and route assignments in these AWG-based three-stage networks are consistent with that of classical Clos networks. Thus, the optimal AWG-based non-blocking Clos networks also can achieve 100% utilization when all input and output wavelength channels are busy. A Perturbation Algorithm for Embedding Virtual Data Centers in Multipath Networks IEEE Globecom 2014: We compare the performance of the exhaustive searching algorithm and perturbation algorithm with load-balanced or single-path routing by simulations. The perturbation algorithm with load-balanced routing performs close to the exhaustive searching algorithm while significantly reduces the time complexity. Therefore, it offers a good tradeoff between time complexity and network performance. A Hybrid Wavelength Reservation Scheme for Large-Scale Optical Networks The 25th Wireless and Optical Communication Conference: Simulation results, based on the CORONET model, showed that the hybrid reservation approach can reduce the blocking probability significantly in a variety of network settings. Two papers in DCC 2014, 2016 and a conference paper in 10th International Symposium on Communication Systems, Networks and Digital Signal Processing: Various conflict avoidance codes, which have potential applications to optical and wireless systems, were investigated. The conference paper showed the inadequacy of common Gaussian noise models for such systems and a more accurate BER expression is presented.

414012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414012.value: An important research problem for future study is to design fast and efficient distributed algorithms for routing in optical networks in large data centers. Unlike traditional switch fabric routing problems, cross-switch communication cannot be too frequent. On the other hand due to the size of modern data centre networks, the traffics pattern they handle is complicated and fast changing. Hence, designing efficient distributed routing algorithms poses a great technical challenge.

414012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414012.value: In spite of its tremendous popularity and importance, the Internet in its current implementation can primarily support best effort services only and does not provide Quality of Service guarantees. There are various challenges that need to be overcome in order to realize a future Internet that can offer Quality of Service guarantees. Dealing with bursty traffic is one of the key challenges. The objective of the completed project is to design a new, scalable network architecture that can handle the complex, bursty traffic one encounters in the Internet today. The project studied various resource optimization problems and corresponding design control strategies. Various technical contributions to the related research field were made.

414612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414612.value: The stress induced electrode pulverization problem impose major limit on the practical application of bulk Si for Li-ion battery anode, although Si is extremely attractive due to its large specific capacity being an order of magnitude larger than that of the commercially used graphite. The recent discovery of facile strain relaxation associated with nanostructured Si provides an excellent opportunity to overcome such a hurdle. Nevertheless, a few critical issues, including the mechanical and chemical instability of the Si nanostructures during charge/discharge cycling (and consequently their being unable to maintain both the electrical contact with the current collector and the stable interface with the electrolyte), the inadequate active material mass, and the low throughput processing associated with nanostructures, remain as bottleneck for further developing the Si-based nanostructures into practical anodes of large reversible capacity and satisfactory cycle life. Here we propose to use three dimensional networks of hierarchical metal-Si nanostructures (directly grown on current collectors) to overcome these difficulties. Not only such nanostructured architectures bear all the known merits associated with nanomaterial based Li-ion battery electrode (including facile strain relaxation, volume change accommodation, and short carrier diffusion length), but also have a unique feature—the inactive nanostructured metallic “scaffold” for Si works as the current collector itself. Its chemical inertness to both lithiation and electrolyte, its ductility, and close contact with Si ensure the mechanical/chemical/electrical stability, and thus significantly improve the reversibility during cycling. The largely increased surface area associated with the 3D configuration makes it possible to achieve adequate active material mass in the electrode. The conducting metallic “scaffold” provides the feasibility of using electroplating as the processing technique, which addresses the low throughput processing issue. In the proposed study, we will first identify the key system configuration parameters that affect the anode performance, including the morphology of the metallic nanostructure scaffold, the size, doping, and surface passivation/protection of the Si on the metallic host. These parameters will be varied in a systematic manner by changing the processing conditions, to optimize the configuration of the proposed hierarchical nanostructured anode. By combining research expertise in controlled nanostructure synthesis, local compositional/structural characterization and electrochemical characterizations of Li-ion battery materials from the PI and Co-I’s teams, the present proposal will lead to reversible high capacity and long cycle life anode for the new generation of Li-ion batteries.

414612.label: Realisation of objectives
414612.value: Nickel nanostructures have been directly grown on current collector substrate (Ni, or Cu foil). Two different morphologies have been achieved, i.e, nanowire arrays, and inverse opals. Both nanostructures were obtained using template based electroplating. The chemical composition, phase, morphology and the conductivity of the metallic nanostructured have been examined as functions of the growth parameters. Formation of hierarchical Ni/Si nanostructure have been achieved by depositing amorphous Si onto the surface of the metallic nanostructures using both electroplating and magnetron sputtering. We found that magnetron sputtering results in Si coating with low O content and easy N doping. Nevertheless, it suffers from highly non-uniformity due to the shadowing effect. By employing electroplating, we successfully tackle the uniformity problem of the deposit Si layer. We have then identified the optimum thickness of the Si layer for the best cell performance. We have also evaluated the morphology of the nanostructure on the electrode’s electrochemical performance. The Si/electrolyte interface has also been discussed. Proto-type cells will behave been assembled. The anode performance has been evaluated by its charge/discharge capacity at specific charging/discharging rates and number of cycling. The structural parameters associated with the optimized anode performance have been identified.

414612.label: Major findings and research outcome
414612.value: Metallic nanowire arrays can be easily formed on conducting substrate by electroplating using AAO template [RSC Advances 2013]. The diameter of the individual nanowires and their separation distance are inherited from the AAO template, and the length of the wire can be controlled from a few hundred nanometers to tens of microns. Such nanowire arrays can be employed as the hosting electrode for Si. Magnetron sputtering is effective in depositing a high quality layer of Si on the surface metallic nanostructures, and appears to be relatively resistant to oxidation. N doping can be easily incorporated using magnetron sputtering. N doping is found to not only efficiently increase the electronic conductivity of the Si deposit, but also reduces the activation energy of lithiation in Si, and associates with low Li-ion diffusion coefficient. In addition, the SEI formation during charge/discharge process in the N-doped samples is also found to be different from the undoped samples, resulting in improvement in both rate performance and cyclability of the cells [Applied Material Interfaces 2013]. Nevertheless, the shadowing effect of magnetron deposition results in highly non-uniform Si coating along the metallic nanowire surface. This increases the polarity of the electrode. In this regard, electroplating is found to effectively improve the uniformity of the Si layer deposited on the metallic nanostructures, leading to improved stability and thus cyclability of the anode. The uniform Si layer also enables the investigation of the optimum Si layer thickness. ~50 nm is identified as the best thickness for cell performance. The effect of SEI formation becomes dominant (continuously consumes the active material) at smaller Si layer thickness, while larger thickness will limit the carrier transport in the active materials. [Nanoscale 2013] On the other hand, the utilization of the 3D space is found to be limited using the nanocable array architecture, leading to low volumetric capacity of the electrode. To tackle this problem, we have attempted Ni inverse opal structure, which forms 3D interconnecting conducting networks. Such hosting electrode leads to improved volumetric capacity of the Si anode due to both improved electronic and ionic conductivity, which relates to the specific geometric configuration of the inverse opal architecture. [Applied Materials Interfaces 2014]

414612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414612.value: The present work shows that the electrode pulverization can be solved by releasing the stress using proper nanostructured Si architectures. However, the present Si nanostructures, either the nanocable arrays, or the inverse opal structure suffer from low active material loading, and thus low volumetric capacity. A possible solution is to employ nanostructure Si in flow batteries—a next generation batteries with high capacity and energy density. A flow battery can easily accommodate the volume expansion of Si nanoparticles. We have now identified the optimum size of the Si nanostructure for the best electronic and ionic conductivity. Current we are extending the research into flow cells [Advanced Energy Materials 2016]. In addition, doping and uniformity of the Si nanostructures are critical in determining the rate performance and cyclability of the electrode. All these parameters can be implemented and tested in the flow battery with proper adjustment for the best cell performance.

414612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414612.value: Si is a promising anode material for its high specific capacity, being an order of magnitude higher than that of the commercially used graphite. However, bulk Si suffer from electrode pulverization due to ~300% volume expansion of Si during its lithiation process. Using metal/Si nanocable arrays, the capacity fading problem of the bulk Si electrode can be largely improved due to the benefit brought by the nanostructured architecture. We have identified ~50 nm as the optimum size for Si, below which the solid electrolyte interface becomes a dominant problem, and above which the electronic and ionic conductivity of Si are limited, both leading to worse anode electrochemical performance. We also found that effective doping and the uniformity of Si are critical in determining the anode rate performance and cyclability. Comparing to metal/Si nanocable arrays, the specific geometric configuration of inverse opal structures leads to improvement in both electronic and ionic conductivity of the electrode, and thus enhancing the volumetric capacity of the electrode.

414712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414712.value: Normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) is a curable medical condition prevalent in the elderly, causing gait difficulties, urinary incontinence and cognitive decline. However, the physiopathology is unclear while diagnosis and surgical outcome prediction are inaccurate. Recent studies suggested NPH alters brain mechanical properties, especially around the ventricular horns. It is shown in literature that the brain viscoelasticity of NPH patients can be determined in vivo using magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), however, the contrast of the acquired global average shear modulus between normal and hydrocephalic brains is not large enough for diagnostics. A compact piezoelectric driver with fast response and limited artifacts will be designed for the MRE on the brain, enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and resolution, allowing acquisition of smaller regions around the horns and enabling analysis of local modulus differences. The in vivo bulk modulus of NPH patients will also be investigated as an alternative approach. The acquired data would help in understanding the physiopathology and may even provide a potential diagnostic marker. 正常顱壓腦積水（NPH）是一種多見於老年人，可以治愈的疾病。NPH會造成步態困難，尿失禁和認知能力下降。然而，目前此症的成因還未確定，而且診斷和手術結果的預測仍不準確。近期研究顯示NPH改變了大腦，尤其是側腦室前角位置的粘彈性。有研究證明可使用磁共振彈性成像（MRE）取得NPH患者腦部在體內的粘彈性數據。可是患者腦部的平均剪力模數和正常人的相差不夠大，所以粘彈性數據未能被應用在診斷上。針對以上的局限，我們會設計一個細小的、快速的和小偽影的壓電驅動器以應用於腦部的磁共振彈性成像。使用此驅動器可以提高磁共振信號的信噪比和分辨率，因而可以在側腦室前角周圍的小區域獲取磁共振信號，並以小區域的模數差異作分析。NPH患者腦部的體積彈性模量亦會被研究是否可作以為一種診斷方法。研究中所獲得的數據將有助於了解NPH的病理，甚至有可能提供一個新的診斷方向。

414712.label: Realisation of objectives
414712.value: For magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), several actuators have been designed. Piezoceramic thin disks with spiral interdigitated electrodes on their surfaces were designed and fabricated to generate in-plane torsional vibrations. Reversible bellows made of shape memory alloys (SMAs) in actuation were also considered and investigated. Elastography is an imaging approach to measure the stiﬀness of tissues to provide diagnostic information. To evaluate the use of brain elasticity and viscosity for diagnosis, ﬁnite element method (FEM) has been used in elastography. However, FEM tends to an overly stiﬀ model that sometimes gives unsatisfactory accuracy, particularly using triangular elements in 2D or tetrahedral elements in 3D. In general, it is diﬃcult or even impossible to generate quadrilateral or brick elements to precisely capture the anatomic details for mechanobiologic modeling as the biologic system can be rather sophisticated. In addition, biologic soft tissues are often considered as “incompressible” materials, where conventional FEM could suﬀer from volumetric locking in numerical solution. On the other hand, linear triangular and tetrahedral mesh can be automatically generated for complicated geometry, which signiﬁcantly saves the time for the creation of model. With these reasons, smoothed ﬁnite element method (SFEM) was developed to analyze elastography problems. To identify the regions in the brain that could be most affected by Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH), the mechanical properties of abnormal tissues were inversely computed.

414712.label: Major findings and research outcome
414712.value: Piezoceramic thin disks with spiral interdigitated electrodes on their surfaces were proposed to generate in-plane torsional vibrations. Electromechanical characteristics of the discal piezoelectric transducers were investigated. Working principles of the transducers were explained. Dynamic models were derived to analyze the in-plane torsional vibrations of the disks together with the radial vibrations. The corresponding electromechanical equivalent circuits were also obtained. With different boundary conditions and structural parameters, frequency responses of their electric admittances were calculated. Resonant frequencies, mode shapes, and electromechanical coupling coefﬁcients of the vibration modes were also extracted. Prototype transducers were fabricated and tested to validate the theoretical results (see the first journal paper [J1] and the earlier conference paper, 8 and 9 in Part C). On the other hand, we also considered other types of actuators with shape memory alloys (SMAs). An efficient phenomenological macroscopic one-dimensional model was proposed. The constitutive model was developed within the framework of thermodynamics of irreversible processes to simulate the one-dimensional behavior of SMAs under uniaxial simple tension-compression as well as pure torsion+/- loadings. The presented model can be used to reproduce primary aspects of SMAs including transformation/orientation of martensite phase, shape memory effect, pseudo-elasticity and in particular ferro-elasticity. Experimental results available in the open literature for uniaxial tension, torsion and bending tests were simulated to validate the present SMA model in capturing the main mechanical characteristics (see the second journal paper [J2] in part C). In addition, the feasibility of reversible bellows made of SMAs in actuated applications to transfer pressure and/or temperature into a linear motion was investigated. An analytical three-dimensional model was developed to simulate key features of SMAs. A ﬁnite element method along with an iterative incremental elasticpredictor–inelastic-corrector procedure was developed to solve the governing equations with both material and geometrical non-linearities. The feasibility of reversible SMA bellows in transferring pressure and/or temperature into a linear motion was demonstrated. In this respect, the effects of geometric parameters, magnitude of thermo-mechanical loadings and end conditions on the performances of SMA bellows were evaluated and discussed in depth (see the third journal paper [J3] in part C). Elastography is an imaging approach to measure the stiﬀness of tissues to provide diagnostic information. Currently, ﬁnite element method (FEM) has been widely used in elastography. Smoothed ﬁnite element method (SFEM) was developed to analyze elastography problems. A range of numerical examples, including static, dynamic, viscoelastic and time harmonic cases have exempliﬁed herein to validate that SFEM is able to provide more accurate and stable solutions using the same set of mesh compared with the standard FEM. Furthermore, SFEM is also eﬀective to inversely compute the mechanical properties of abnormal tissue. The obtained results were shown in the fourth journal paper [J4] in part C. In addition, some MRE trials on human brain have been performed.

414712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414712.value: The feasibility of applying MRE on human brain has been studied. Stiffness maps for normal volunteers were collected and analyzed to ensure consistency and reliability of the setup. Some tests were done on hydrocephalus patients. In order to make the related research and technology possible, more studies and comparison between simulation and clinical trials should be further performed.

414712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414712.value: Normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) is a curable medical condition prevalent in the elderly, causing gait difficulties, urinary incontinence and cognitive decline. However, the physiopathology is unclear while diagnosis and surgical outcome prediction are inaccurate. Recent studies suggested NPH alters brain mechanical properties, especially around the ventricular horns. It is challenging to precisely capture the anatomic details for mechanobiologic modeling as the biologic system can be rather sophisticated. In this research, significant results were obtained. Actuators were designed for the magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and resolution, allowing acquisition of smaller regions around the horns and enabling analysis of local modulus differences. For investigating the bulk modulus, the mechanical properties of abnormal tissue have been inversely computed. The studies would be valuable in understanding the physiopathology and may even provide a potential diagnostic marker in the future.

414812.label: Realisation of objectives
414812.value: For this project, all four objectives have been met, with some research outcomes extending beyond the four original objectives. With respect to objectives 1 and 2, together with the well-known TWRC (two-way relay channel) PNC building block, we have been able to identify eight other building blocks. Furthermore, the characteristics of these nine building blocks have been studied in detail, including how to decompose traffic flows so that they can be carried by these nine building blocks in general network topologies. Partial results were first reported in an IEEE conference [1]. The full results were reported two IEEE journal papers [2] and [3]. In addition, we made advances on implementation of PNC in software-defined radio platform [4]. Major findings related to objectives 1 and 2 are summarized in Section 6.1. With respect to objective 3, we looked at broadcasting using the PNC mechanism. The model we looked at is one source wanting to broadcast information to many nodes in a network using PNC [5]. In [6], we looked at the base station positioning issue to increase through in cellular networks making use of PNC. Major findings related to objective 3 are summarized in Section 6.1. Besides the first six publications listed below, publications [7], [8], [9], [10] are offshoots from the main investigations of this project. They go beyond the original objectives under this project. In [7] and [8], we discovered a new way to exploit PNC in non-relay networks (specifically, in the multiple-access setting). 414812.label: Major findings and research outcome
414812.value: Major Findings Related to Objectives 1 and 2: First, using the decomposition framework, the throughput performance of PNC is shown to be significantly better than those of the traditional multi-hop scheme and the conventional network coding scheme. For example, under heavy traffic volume, PNC can achieve 100% throughput gain relative to the traditional multi-hop scheme. Second, PNC decomposition based on a variety of different PNC atoms can yield much better performance than PNC decomposition based on the TWRC atom alone. Third, three out of the nine atoms are most important to good performance. Specifically, the decomposition based on these three atoms is good enough most of the time, and it is not necessary to use the other six atoms [2]. We have also completed the study of ARQ mechanisms to ensure reliable PNC communications. A key result is that for PNC building blocks that exploit overhearing, ARQ designs different from traditional ARQ designs are needed for optimal performance of PNC building blocks. We have also been able to make advances on prototyping of the TWRC PNC building block on the software-defined radio platform. In particular, we demonstrated real-time operation of the PNC building block with nodes exchanging image files over a relay using the PNC principle. This is reported in [4]. Major Findings Related to Objective 3: By proper design of routing and scheduling, we attempted to find the maximum broadcast throughput and its achievability in multi-hop wireless networks. Our specific results are as follows: 1) For single-source broadcast, the theoretical throughput upper bound is n/(n+1), where n is the “min vertex-cut” size of the network. 2) In general, the throughput upper bound is not always achievable. 3) For grid and many other networks, the throughput upper bound n/(n+1) is achievable. Our work can be considered as an attempt to understand the relationship between max-flow and min-cut in half-duplex broadcast networks with cycles (there has been prior work on networks with cycles, but not half-duplex broadcast networks) [5] Other Outcomes: Beyond publications of conference and journal papers, this project also yielded on patent: S. C. Liew, J. He, “Network-Coding Building Blocks and Decomposition Scheduling Based Thereon,” U.S. Patent 9,094,994, July 28, 2015.

414812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414812.value: A patent has been granted (see Section 6.1). Going forward, we will explore the possible commercialization of this outcome. The industry is currently developing 5G cellular networks as future wireless network infrastructure. The possible use of PNC building blocks in 5G networks is a topic that could be further explored. CUHK and ASTRI are currently initiating a joint lab. One of the topics of collaboration between CUHK and ASTRI is 5G networks. We will explore with ASTRI the use of PNC building blocks in 5G networks as midstream R&D.

414812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414812.value: This project investigated the fundamental building blocks of physical-layer network coding (PNC) to enable development of large-scale PNC systems. PNC was originally proposed by the PI’s research group. Since then, PNC has developed into a subfield of network coding with a wide following in the wireless community. Predominantly, these existing works focused on the simplest possible system for PNC application, the two-way relay channel (TWRC). TWRC is just a small three-node network consisting of two end nodes communicating via a relay node. Going beyond TWRC, this project explored two issues: 1) What are the fundamental building blocks of PNC? 2) How can these building blocks be put together to build large-scale networks? With regard to 1), this project identified and investigated in detail eight other PNC building blocks besides TWRC. With regard to 2), this project identified and investigated a decomposition method that makes use of these building blocks to build large-scale networks. Besides 11 academic publications, one patent has also been granted for our research outcomes in 1) and 2). Going forward, possible commercialization of the outcomes, particularly 5G networks, will be explored.

414912.label: Project Objectives
414912.value: Develop a real-time map-free and GPS-free localization method for both indoor and outdoor robots in unknown environments by fusing measurements of inertial sensors with geometric information of natural image features captured by a vision system based on the concept of model-based adaptive control. 414912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414912.value: The objective of this project is to develop a real-time algorithm, which can be integrated into the low-level motion control loop, for localizing position of a robot in an unknown environment without using any global positioning system (GPS) and map. GPS provides a simple solution to robot localization problem, but is not suitable for indoor environments. Inertial localization systems suffer from problems of unbounded error accumulation and noises. Existing vision-based localization methods require an environmental map. SLAM (Simultaneous Localization And Mapping) provides a beautiful framework for localizing robot position in unknown environments, but existing SLAM approaches cannot yield good accuracy and efficiency of localization. In this project, we will develop a map-free and GPS-free localization method by fusing visual information captured by vision systems with measurement data of inertial sensors. There are three unique features that differentiate the method to be developed from existing ones: the robot position is not obtained by integrating noisy acceleration measurements of inertial sensors; it does not employ triangulation when extracting 3-D information from vision; it does not perform any match with the environmental map. The novelty lies in that a simple on-line adaptive estimator, similar to the Slotine-Li algorithm for adaptive control, will be developed to estimate position of a robot using inertial measurements and natural image features. It will be theoretically proved that this method guarantees the convergence of the localization errors to zero. To achieve real-time efficiency, we will implement this method in parallel using GPU. To demonstrate the excellent performance, we will carry out experiments on an indoor autonomous helicopter and an outdoor water surface robot. The research outputs will provide innovative solutions to localization of robots and contribute to development and applications of advanced technology in Hong Kong. 本專案的目的是研究一個不使用GPS和地圖的即時演算法以計算在未知環境裡移動的機器人的位置，該演算法可以與機器人的底層控制器集成為一體。GPS是一種非常簡單的機器人定位方法，但不適應於室內環境；慣性定位法會因為信號雜訊產生積累誤差；現有的基於圖像的定位方法需要環境地圖。SLAM（同時定位和製圖法）提供了一個很好的在未知環境下定位框架，但現有的SLAM法從定位即時性和精度兩方面都不能滿足要求。本項目將研究一個新的不使用GPS和地圖，融合圖像和慣性測量的機器人定位方法。與現有的方法相比，這一方法有三個特點：機器人的位置不是通過對具有很強雜訊的加速度信號積分所獲取的；不採用三角測量法提取圖像中的三維資訊；及不需要與環境地圖進行對比。本項目的獨特性在於研究一個簡單、與自我調整控制的Slotine-Li算法相似，利用圖像中的自然特徵與慣性測量資料的在線估計演算法估計機器人的位置。我們將利用理論證明所提方法可以保證估計誤差收斂到零。為了實現即時性，將利用GPU進行平行計算。為了展示這一方法的特性，將在室內自主移動機器人和室外水面移動機器人進行實驗研究。本項目的研究成果將為機器人的定位提供創新的解決方案，有助於推動香港的科技發展和應用。

414912.label: Realisation of objectives
414912.value: The objectives stated in the proposal have been fully achieved. The details are as follows: 1) In regarding to objective 1, we developed a novel algorithm for estimating position of a mobile robot by fusing the orientation data measured by the odometry sensors and/or IMU sensor with the images captured by a perspective camera. The algorithm employed the idea of the model-based adaptive control, e.g. an adaptive algorithm to estimate the position on-line from visual information. In order to increase field of views, we also developed a localisation algorithm using images from an omnidirectional camera based on a new projection model, similar to that of the perspective projection, which makes it possible to linearly parameterize the projection geometry by the unknown position of the robot. The linear parameterisation enables us to use the idea of the model-based control to design the localisation algorithm. 2) In regarding to objective 2, we proved, using the Lyapunov theory, that by the proposed algorithm the estimation error of the position of the robot is convergent to zero. The convergence was verified by simulations and experiments. Robustness of the developed approaches to the measurements errors was investigated by theoretical analysis, simulations and experiments. 3) In regarding to objectives 1 and 2, we also developed a localisation algorithm without using the velocity of the robot to increase the robustness because the velocity measurement is subject to big noises. The algorithm simultaneously estimates the position and velocity of the robot using image data and IMU data. Furthermore, we also applied the proposed localization algorithm to control of nonholonomic mobile robots. New position controllers were developed for controlling a mobile robot and an underactuated water surface robot without direct measurement of the position. 4) In regarding to objective 3, we developed a GPU-based platform for parallel implementation of the algorithms. It has been demonstrated that by GUP-based parallel computation the algorithms can achieve real-time efficiency. We have verified the performance of the developed approaches for localisation and control by experiments on several robots including a mobile robot, a water surface robot, and an aerial robot. The experiments demonstrated the good performance.

414912.label: Major findings and research outcome
414912.value: The major findings are as follows: 1) We developed a simple algorithm to estimate the position of a mobile robot by fusing the readings of its odometer and the images captured by a perspective camera on it. It is proved that the proposed algorithm can yield convergence of the position estimation to the real position. This result was published at IEEE/ASME Trans. on Mechatronics, 2014 2) A new projection model, similar to that of a perspective camera, was developed for omnidirectional cameras. Based on this model, a novel algorithm has been developed to localise position of a robot from the omnidirectional images and IMU data. The algorithm estimates both the position and the velocity of the robot so as to improve the robustness to measurement errors of the velocity. The convergence of the position estimation error to zero was also proved by Lyapunov theory. The work has been published at IEEE Trans. on Cybernetics, 2015. 3) A novel controller has been developed for controlling a nonholonomic mobile robot without direction position measurement but using the developed estimator of the robot's position. The stability of the controller was provided by the Lyapunov theory. The work has been published in IEEE Trans. on Robotics. The application of the localisation and control algorithms to a water surface robot has been published in IEEE Trans. on Control Systems Technology. Another paper on control of a mobile robot using visual feedback from an omnidirectional camera has been submitted to IEEE Trans. on Cybernetics. 4) The localisation and control methods have been applied to navigation and control of an intelligent forklift vehicle. The Ph.D. students Dr. Luyang Li and Dr. Mu Fang who worked on this project have started up a company to commercialise the vision-based intelligent forklift vehicles. The company is doing very well in marketing and further development of the technology.

414912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414912.value: Further research can be done in the following aspects: 1) Improvement of the localisation accuracy: The current localisation accuracy is about 3-5cm, which should be improved to 2-3cm. Moreover, the accumulation errors on the robot need to be removed using some loop-closure-checking algorithms. 2) Estimation of both position and orientation: The developed algorithms work on the basis of the assumption that the orientation of the robot is known. It is important to remove the assumption. 3) Application of the algorithm to UAV control: It is possible to apply this algorithm to vision-based control of UAVs in the environment where GPS is not working.

414912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414912.value: In the project, we developed a novel algorithm for estimating the position of a mobile root in a GPS-denied environment using the natural features of the environment captured by a camera and the IMU/odometry data. The algorithm has a simple structure suitable for parallel implementation so as to achieve the real-time efficiency. It is proved that the proposed algorithm yields the convergence of the position estimation to the ground truth. The algorithm is further employed to develop a vision-based controller for controlling motion of a nonholonmic mobile robot without directly measuring its position. The algorithms have been implemented using GPU-based parallel computation and their performance were verified by experiments on both indoor and outdoor robots. The technology has been applied to localisation and control of automatic forklift vehicles by the Ph.D. students working on this project. They have started up a robotics company to commercialise the vision-based intelligent forklift vehicles in manufacturing and logistic industries in Hong Kong and the Mainland. In summary, this project not only generated academic publications but also led to commercialization of the research outputs.

415112.label: Project Objectives
415112.value: Develop a general mathematical theory so to understand the interaction of users and service providers, as well as the associated network externality on some new internet services. Apply our methodology and distributed algorithms to several important and representative services like: (a) If a company offers "security insurance" at a nominal fee, will this be a viable service? Also, under what situation will cyber-insurance provide sufficient incentive for users to subscribe? (b) If a company offers to "bundle" multiple internet services as one service at an aggregated reduced rate, will this be attractive under a competitive market? Will there be sufficient number of users subscribe to such bundling service so to create sufficient network externality effect? (c) To make "location-based service" (LBS) viable, one has to have a good information/profit sharing model for all players, namely, advertisers, users and service providers and advertisement service providers. We show how to use Shapley value to provide the proper coalition so to make the LBS service effective. To validate that the mathematical theory can be applied large graphs, we plan to develop a fluid-like parallel simulator on multi-core clustered machines so to validate the theory on different range of network topologies. To validate our methodology and the above mentioned applications, We will collaborate with Tencent Inc., which has the largest online social network in China (e.g., QQ software), to test the possibility of cyber-insurance and digital goods/services bundling. For the location based service, we will collaborate with China Mobile and Huawei Inc. (from China) and Hutchison (from Hong Kong). These companies have hundred of millions of users in China/Hong Kong and this creates an interesting testbed to validate our theory. The academic impact of this research will help the computer and network researchers to gain the fundamental understanding on the engineering and economic issues. This research will contribute to the body of theoretical networking knowledge, and provide insight how to realize new and viable networking services.
