415112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415112.value: 在過去的幾年中，在信息科學領域有兩個新興和令人振奮的發展, 便是"網絡科學和網絡經濟" 網絡科學重點在互連和結構特性的工程網絡（例如，互聯網或電話網絡）， 信息網絡（例如，WWW，線社交網絡如Facebook）以及生物網絡（例如，DNA分子網絡）。這門學科的目的是在確定共同的原則，用來治理，管理和調節網絡，以實現所期望的行為。其理論基礎主要來自圖論和統計物理。另一方面，網絡經濟專注於創造商業模式，如何使用增值價值，利用網絡效應，來使某商品或服務可以提高其他用戶在網絡中相同的商品或服務。網絡效應的一個很好例子是蘋果公司的產品， 當IPhone普及， 它吸引更多的用戶購買蘋果的手機。 隨著互聯網的普及和在線社交網絡（例如，Twitter）和博客網站（如sina.com），這些網絡擔任新的機會，人類彼此連接從而創造出許多新的社會和經濟活動。這些網絡的可用性還意味著大容量的原始數據和信息，如果這些數據可以被處理，分析和正確解釋，它可創做許多新的服務和商品，而這都需要新的工程研究。因此，我們迫切需要發展新的數學理論來理解這些大型網絡和用戶的交互，並從中獲得了一套新的分佈式和並行算法，在過程中組織和綜合信息，以便創建新的網絡服務。

415112.label: Realisation of objectives
415112.value: We have a very successful project. In particular, we use network science theory to understand the interaction with a lot of network economics problems. For example, we examine applications such as network insurance and its feasibility and profitability, price differentiation and control policies for ISPs, how can bundling sale strategy may affect the internet online service markets, how to perform product selection for market entry and sustainability,...etc. All of these are important network economics problems and we addressed them under the contexts of large graphs (e.g., Internet) using some of the methodologies of network science theory. In the internet economic evolution system, we propose a network-aware, macroscopic model that captures the characteristics and interactions of the application and network providers, and show how it leads to a market equilibrium of the ecosystem. By analyzing the driving forces and the dynamics of the market equilibrium, we obtain some fundamental understandings of the cause and effect of the Internet evolution, which explain why some historical and recent evolutions have happened. Furthermore, by projecting the likely future evo- lutions, our model can help application and network providers to make informed business decisions so as to succeed in this compet- itive ecosystem. In the product selection problem, we present a general distance-based product adoption model to capture consumers’ purchase behavior. Using this model, various distance metrics can be used to describe different real life purchase behavior. We then provide a learning algorithm to decide which set of distance metrics one should use when we are given some accessible historical purchase data. Based on the product adoption model, we formalize the k most marketable products (or k-MMP) selection problem and formally prove that the problem is NP-hard. To tackle this problem, we propose an efficient greedy-based approximation algorithm with a provable solution guarantee. Using submodularity analysis, we prove that our approximation algorithm can achieve at least 63% of the optimal solution. We apply our algorithm on both synthetic datasets and real-world datasets (TripAdvisor.com), and show that our algorithm can easily achieve five or more orders of speedup. We perform large scale data analysis to show the effiency and accuracy of our framework. We observe 1,300 to 250,000 times speedup as compared to the exhaustive algorithms, and our solutions can achieve on average 96% of solution quality as compared to the optimal solutions. We apply our algorithms on web dataset to show the impact of customers’ different purchase behavior on the results of product selection. For the online product bundling problem, we aim to understand the underlying dynamics of bundling, in particular, what is the optimal bundling sale strategy and under what situations it will be more attractive than the separate sales. We focus on online service markets that exhibit network effect. We provide mathematical models to capture the interactions between buyers and sellers, analyze the market equilibrium and its stability, and formulate an optimization framework to determine the optimal sale strategy for the service provider. We analyze the impact of the key factors, including the network effects and operating costs, on the profitability of bundling. We show that bundling is more profitable than separate sale in most cases; however, the heterogeneity of services and the asymmetry of operating costs reduce the advantage of bundling. These findings provide important insights in designing proper sale strategies for online services. Finally, we like to emphasize that we have generalize the Kelly mechanism, which is a well-known and classical method to perform resource allocation. We generalize the Kelly mechanism by designing a price differentiation and show that the efficiency gap can be closed. In particular, we analyze the resource competition game under the generalized mechanism and show that any price differentiation induces a unique Nash equilibrium and any non-dictatorial resource allocation can be implemented as a Nash equilibrium under price differentiation. We further characterize the optimality condition under which the social welfare is maximized. Based on this optimality condition, we design a feedback price control mechanism that takes observable system parameters as input and adapts to the optimal Nash equilibrium that maximizes the social welfare. Last but not least, our research work has attract # of companies (e.g., Baidu, Tencent, ...etc) to try out our algorithms on their services.

This allows ISPs to consider this new service model to gain more profit (Please refer to Part C, Journal item #1, item #2) - We consider how one can mind the buyers behavior for Internet goods and services, and howe one can perform product selection so as to maximize the success rate of entering a new market or survive in an existing markets (Please refer to Part C, Journal item #3, Conference item #2 and #3) - We provide the theoretical framework on how to "bundle" multiple internet services/goods so as to increase the revenue of ISPs or sellers. 415112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415112.value: Potential for further developments include collaboration with some ISPs or content providers (e.g., Tencent or Baidu) so as to increase their revenue by (1) bundling multiple services together and offer a single and simple price, (2) decode how to select existing products and offer them as new service so as to increase the revenue, or (3) to collaborate with the network equipment vendors like Huawei so to propose a new service (e.g., network insurance) so that the company may be able to increase its revenue.

415112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415112.value: In layman terms, our research results provide insights and understand on several new business models so that internet companies (e.g., content providers or service providers) can increase their revenues and at the same time, the new business models will be acceptable to users. This is the first research project that links the Internet network with some business models. Although our results are theoretical and mathematical, but one can transform our results to some practical new services so that all players in the society (e.g., users, content providers and service providers) will have a higher degree of satisfaction.

415212.label: Project Objectives
415212.value: Functional personalized service recommendation technologies We will formulate a design paradigm on service recommendation from user's perspective. We first identify users’ potential favorite services from the functions of the services which can meet users’ internal requirement. We will then derive possible solutions for users’ personalized service recommendations, which consist of rule-based recommendation techniques and context-aware recommendation techniques. Theoretical analysis and algorithm development on the methods will be investigated. Recommendation techniques for non-functional performance prediction Quality of service (QoS) is a key component of a good service. Security, safety, availability, and reliability are the main attributes in measuring QoS. Here, we particularly target at the reliability of the service. We focus on the non-functional issue of the service and aim at selecting and providing those services that are reliable and of high quality. We will propose various state-of-the-art techniques such as neighborhood methods, matrix and tensor factorization methods, and temporal-aware methods to evaluate the quality of advanced service computing arena, including Web services, network coordinate, etc. Methodology for scalability and online algorithms Scalability of recommendation techniques becomes a major concern when new services are made available every day. Different end users interacting with different services will also change users’ preference patterns or models, imposing dynamic impact on service quality including reliability, safety, privacy, etc. Hence, we need to tackle the scalability issue and update the models promptly with respect to swift changes of user data. To attain these goals, we intend to take advantages of statistical learning methods, such as bootstrapping methods and stochastic online learning methods, in implementing our proposed service recommendation techniques. These methods not only save significant cost in retraining the models, but also guarantee the robustness of model performance.

415212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415212.value: Service computing is a promising research area, aiming at providing flexible computing architectures to integrate Business Services and IT Services together in order to provide convenient services for customers. Various domains of business sectors require such kinds of services, e.g., transforming labor-intensive retail services into streamlining supply chain management, turning intangible knowledge into asset-based services, etc. Due to its practical deployment and low cost, service computing is particularly attractive to the business-centric sectors, such as financial, business management, logistics and supply chain, in Hong Kong’s economic systems. In providing modernized services, quality-of-service (QoS) is one of the key components leading to the success of the services. Although research work has been conducted on improving the quality of services in terms of security, safety, availability, and reliability, research on personalized service recommendation is still less explored. Currently, due to the complexity of real-world situations and mobility of customers, deploying favorite and good quality services which satisfy end users’ dynamic requirements is a formidable yet critical task. Fulfilling this task will shed light on and advance the development on service computing as well as software engineering communities. This project will tackle the challenges in deploying personalized services and explore systematical solutions for personalized service customization. To attain this goal, we first investigate the theory and algorithms of state-of-the-art recommendation technologies, which was originally proposed in the information retrieval community. After that, we propose and establish new recommendation techniques for personalized service computing. Moreover, we develop new implementations which aim at attacking the scalability issue of next-generation services. Our research output consists of a quality-based and user-focused service recommendation framework as well as a comprehensive toolkit, which can be seemingly deployed by both industrial and academic communities for building high-quality service-oriented systems. Through utilizing our research outcome, the service providers can gain insightful information to know end users’ internal requirements and favorites so as to provide effective and personalized services for the end users. Our recommendation toolkit can also help the service providers consider the end users’ requirements from various contexts effectively and efficiently for reliable service deployment. 服务计算是一个新兴的研究领域，它旨在整合商业服务和IT服务从而为用户提供方便灵活的计算架构和服务。服务计算可以被应用于各种各样的商业领域，比如它有助于把劳动密集型的批发服务转变成流水线的供给链管理等等。受益于其实用性和低成本，服务计算对于香港的商业领域，比如金融行业，商业管理，供给链等，非常的有吸引力。 在提供现代化服务的过程中，服务质量（QoS）起到了一个非常重要的作用。在服务计算领域，虽然针对安全性，可靠性，可用性等已经开展了很多的研究工作，针对个性化服务推荐的研究还很不充分。目前，受制于现实世界的复杂性和用户的移动性，提供符合用户动态需求的高质量服务变的越来越困难。解决这个重要的研究问题有利于进一步推动服务计算及软件工程领域的发展。 这个研究项目将针对个性化服务推荐展开系统的和详细的研究，我们将首先对信息抽取领域的推荐技术理论和算法展开深入的调研，然后我们将结合服务计算的特点提出个性化服务推荐的理论及算法。我们还将实现各种算法从而构建高可扩展性的下一代服务。我们的研究成果包括一个基于服务质量的服务推荐框架和一个个性化服务推荐工具包。这个工具包可用于工业界和学术界的高质量服务系统的快速构建。通过我们的研究成果，服务提供商可以深入了解终端用户需求和偏好，从而为他/她们提供高效及个性化的服务。我的推荐工具包也可以帮助服务提供商进行基于用户需求的高效的及可靠的服务部署。

415212.label: Realisation of objectives
415212.value: All the project objectives have been either completely achieved, or exceedingly achieved. We have proposed and developed the state-of-the-art personalized recommendation techniques for quality-oriented service recommendation. We devoted the funding resources according to the proposed methodology described in the project and achieved all the specified objectives. In the objective of functional personalized service recommendation technologies, we have proposed a design paradigm on service recommendation from a user's perspective. We specifically applied advanced topic modeling techniques to analyzing the functionality aspects of services. Additionally, we considered other contextual information, such as reputation, time information, and location, since it is useful to help identify the users’ requirements and favorite services. Possible solutions for quality-oriented personalized service recommendations were formulated, including the use of techniques of feature engineering, topic modeling, and online learning. Our investigations include both theoretical analysis and algorithm development, and extensive experimental results have been obtained to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed techniques. In the objective of non-functional performance prediction for service recommendation, we focused on evaluating Quality of service (QoS), which is a key non-functional attribute of a service. The achievements along this investigation were remarkable. We have developed a systematic approach to making QoS predictions and personalized service recommendations accordingly. We proposed various state-of-the-art techniques, including hierarchical matrix factorization for location-aware service recommendation, topic modeling for reputation management, and online matrix factorization for runtime service selection and adaptation. These techniques have been shown very useful in evaluating the non-functional aspects for service recommendation. Additionally, we addressed the key scalability issue for service recommendation. In modern service markets, new services are made available every day. This imposes a dynamic effect on user-perceived service quality modeling. We investigated statistical learning techniques for this purpose and successfully established a number of new techniques. Specifically, we proposed a tailed online matrix factorization algorithm for runtime service selection. The algorithm provides timely updating of the QoS model in response to the changes of user data. We evaluated the dynamic impact on service quality using real-world service datasets. We also derived a scalable service-oriented scheme to deploy applications in geo-distributed environment. In addition to the proposed service recommendation techniques for service computing, we extended the proposed approaches to various machine learning problems. We formulated a new tensor factorization technique for pairwise interaction tensor as a theoretical achievement. We proposed a sparse Poisson coding scheme for high dimensional document clustering. We developed a hierarchical entity-based Approach to structuralize user-generated content in social media. We also applied our algorithms to successive point-of-interest recommendation. Finally, we proposed a service-generated big data framework in promoting the concept of “big data as a service.” These studies helped push service recommendation techniques toward achieving dynamic service computing in today’s data-centric environment.

415212.label: Major findings and research outcome
415212.value: Totally 4 journal papers, and 11 conference papers have been published, all acknowledging the support of this grant. These publications cover the project’s objectives in various aspects. We describe the research outcomes as follows (We use [J1] to refer to journal publication [1] in Part C, and [C1] label to refer to conference publication [1], etc.). The first objective focuses on developing functional personalized service recommendation technologies. We investigated different machine learning approaches that are helpful in extracting functional features of services, including topic modeling based approach [J2] and hierarchical entity-based approach [C7]. The functional features can be further used for service recommendation by using matrix factorization and tensor factorization techniques [C9]. The second objective focuses on recommendation techniques for non-functional performance prediction. We systematically investigated the key problem of quality-of-service (QoS) prediction, which is a key non-functional attribute of a service. To enhance the prediction accuracy, we considered other contextual information, such as reputation, time information, and location, since it is useful to help identify the users’ favorite services. We proposed various state-of-the-art techniques, including hierarchical matrix factorization for location-aware service recommendation [C11], topic modeling for reputation management [C5], online matrix factorization for runtime service selection and adaptation [C10], and entropy-based prediction of aging-related failures [J3]. These techniques have been shown very useful in evaluating the non-functional aspects for service recommendation. The last objective aims to work out new methodology for scalability and online algorithms. We investigated statistical learning techniques for this purpose and successfully established a number of new techniques. Specifically, we customized an online matrix factorization algorithm for runtime service selection [C10]. The algorithm provides timely updating of the QoS model in response to the changes of user data. We evaluated the dynamic impact on service quality using real-world service datasets. We also derived a scalable service-oriented scheme to deploy applications in geo-distributed environment [C1] and explored how to tolerate latency variability when scaling online service systems to geo-distributed clouds [C2]. In addition to the proposed service recommendation techniques for service computing, we extended the proposed approaches to various machine learning problems. We formulated a new tensor factorization technique for pairwise interaction tensor as a theoretical achievement [C9]. We proposed a sparse Poisson coding scheme for high dimensional document clustering [C8]. We developed a hierarchical entity-based approach to structuralize user-generated content in social media [C7]. All these algorithms provide the fundamental basis for service recommendation research in this project.

415212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415212.value: In this project, we have investigated quality-oriented personalized recommendation theory and algorithms in services computing. The techniques applied include various machine learning techniques, such as matrix factorization, online learning, and tensor factorization. We made advances in both the theory and applications of these algorithms in the service recommendation area. Further research can be devoted to the design and implementation of a reusable toolkit for service recommendation, including implementation of the proposed algorithms, evaluation metric composition, and module interaction and integration. We will also make an effort to the collection of demonstrable datasets for reproducible research. Some of the datasets have appeared in the WS-DREAM site (http://wsdream.github.io), which we have maintained for Web service QoS datasets sharing. This would allow our formulated service recommendation techniques to be implemented and distributed for wide adoption among researchers and practitioners. To enhance the impact of this research project, we plan to build collaborations with industry partners such as Microsoft and Huawei Technologies, and further apply our developed techniques to a real production environment.

415212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415212.value: We successfully conduct theory development and algorithm design for quality-oriented service recommendation, which achieves the objectives of functional personalized service recommendation technologies, recommendation techniques for non-functional performance prediction, and methodology for scalability and online algorithms. The effectiveness of the proposed techniques in advancing the current state-of-the-art service recommendation has been demonstrated through the design, implementation, and experimentation of the techniques. This project enables application developers to discover and employ services with better quality, which can further guarantee the quality delivery of their applications. The resulting paradigm is both comprehensive and systematic. It formulates methodologies to modern service systems, enables effective, efficient, and scalable service recommendations, and promotes research by opening real-world Web service QoS datasets. The proposed techniques in this project facilitate better application development in general and promote ongoing research in service computing.

415512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415512.value: 機器人手術技術正在變成許多臨床手術的一個集成部分。機器人手術能夠提高手術幾何精准度、增加手術系統的穩定性、減少醫生的疲勞度、以及減少病人的痛苦和恢復時間。 骨頭的堅硬特性使得骨科手術成為機器人手術應用最成功的範例之一。在過去的幾十年裡，人們開發了，甚至商品化了，種類繁多的骨科手術機器人系統。它們大體可以分為被動型、主動型、和半主動型三類。被動型的一般用來固定手術器械的位置和充當手術器械的支撐平台；主動型的則可以按照編制的程序自主控制機器人完成手術步驟。儘管兩者都提供了兩種極端情況的輔助，骨外科醫生還是希望骨外科手術機器人是半自動的，能夠結合被動型和主動型兩者的優點，主動配合和輔助醫生的控制，在醫生的交互式主導控制下輔助手術的完成。 儘管還沒有很多實際的臨床報道，但初步的研究結果顯示半主動型交互式機器人輔助骨科手術系統能夠給醫生提供基於術前確定的手術安全區的監測和控制，使手術器械的運動永遠處於準確的位置和安全區域內，保證其遠優於傳統骨科手術的準確性、安全性和綜合手術效果。 本研究課題蒋研究開發一套具備基於準確力反饋運動限制和先進控制算法的交互式骨科手術輔助機器人系統。我們從設計一個基於精準力傳感的主動型的機器人終端操作器開始，配備先進的控制和運動檢測及限制算法，來提高和確保機器人手術系統的安全性。這套系統可以使骨外科醫生以進行傳統手術的相同感覺和主導方式，實時感覺到手術器械末端於人體之間力的精確反饋並對機器人手術輔助系統實現準確交互式控制，以高準確度和安全性來完成骨科手術。這套系統簡化了複雜的力反饋表顯，減少了整個系統的複雜性，降低了整套系統的製造、使用和維護成本，同時提高了醫生手術操作的透明度和安全性。

415512.label: Realisation of objectives
415512.value: For objective 1, we developed an active interactive end-effector structure with precise force sensing feedback to facilitate and assist surgeon in orthopaedic surgeries. For objective 2, we developed an advanced control system for the robot end-effector structure with precise force sensing feedback to offer surgeon contact force information. For objective 3, we defined three regions in the surgical working space to ensure safety and success of the robot-assisted orthopaedic surgeries. For objective 4, we developed a motion constraint system to work with the control system to ensure the safety and success of the robot-assisted orthopaedic surgeries. For objective 5, we carried out experimental study and evaluation of the developed system and build a prototyping system. So we have successfully achieved all the objectives of the project, with 6 journal and 3 conference publications generated from the project and 2 PhD students are trained by directly participation in the project.

415612.label: Project Objectives
415612.value: Characterize the extremal distributions that arise in computing the boundary points of Marton's inner bound for the capacity region of the broadcast channel. Verify (numerically) the optimality or prove the non-optimality of best known achievable regions such as the Han-Kobayashi region for the interference channel, using the two-letter to 1-letter equivalence approach detailed in this proposal. Obtain a powerful sufficient condition for factorization for functions that can be used to establish capacity regions in many network information theoretic settings. To make progress on the factorization conjectures and solve some of the easier (yet very interesting) ones. We have listed a couple in this proposal; however there are lots more with seemingly different degrees of hardness every one of which will yield new capacity regions in non-trivial settings.

415612.label: Realisation of objectives
415612.value: For Objective 1: The PI, along with collaborators, has come up with a powerful new cardinality bound, published in ISIT14 that restricts the extreme points of Marton's region. The technique combines the perturbation approach introduced by Amin Gohari, in his PhD thesis, along with the idea of concave envelopes that the PI developed during this time (see Journal paper 3). This bound enables one to show that for broadcast channels with binary inputs, Marton's inner bound reduces to randomized time-division strategy. For higher input cardinalities, the bound greatly simplifies the evaluation of the region. For instance, when the input is quarternary, this reduces the dimension of the search space from 15 to 5, making it al east amenable to rather exhaustive search. Of course, there are still problems concerning the extreme points that we are unable to answer especially in the context of relations of extreme points of product channels to the component ones, that would be crucial in proving optimality or sub-optimality of Marton. However, even the current results would be considered a great achievement by the PI since the whole process was akin to fishing in unknown waters. Objective 2: Completely done. Solved a problem that was open for 30 years. This is presented in the conference paper with the same title and uses various techniques developed towards evaluation of regions like the representation using concave envelopes. This result was actually many years in the making but like every counterexamples; once you produce one the years of thought that goes into where to search for one becomes under-appreciated. In this case, the key was to look at binary input interference channels where the evaluation of Han-Kobayashi region was sufficiently simplified, yet no converse arguments were known. This led the PI and his students to the Clean Z interference channels, via a slightly larger class called very weak interference channels. Objectives 3 and 4: While these remain the least achieved objectives in some sense, it is because the research into these objectives opened up a completely new spectrum of relationships, that also immediately justified the inherent difficulty of these problems. There is a notion of tensorization that had been extensively studied in functional analysis, quantum physics. as well as theoretical computer science. The basic idea is the invariance of certain parameters in product probability spaces. Hypercontractivity parameters, log-Sobolev constants, etc are some examples that satisfy tensorization. It was realized during this investigation that the factorization phenomenon we seek are similar to and generalizes known tensorization phenomenon such as hypercontractivity. There is a series of papers by the PI on this topic recently as well as by some of his collaborators that try to express the link between them; these papers have not been listed in this report since they form the basis of a subsequent RGC grant application. The genesis of this line of research was the pursuit of Objectives 3 and 4. Thus instead of solving them, the PI linked this to more deeply studied parts of math and then is various non-trivial connections between them. This link was used in proving new converses as well as new capacity regions. This has also lead to new ways of proving optimality of Gaussian distributions.

415612.label: Major findings and research outcome
415612.value: The research made new connections between problems in network information theory and tensorization phenomenon commonly studied in fucntional analysis and high-dimensional probability theory. Further this tensorization (factorization) property was used to develop a novel method for proving optimality of Gaussian distributions, indeed this happened soon after submitting the grant proposal, so submission of initial results preceed start date of grant. The novelty of this technique can be inferred from the fact that the paper, (Journal paper 2) with PIs student, Yanlin Geng, received the best paper award from the information theory society. It solved a deep and long standing open problem; sub-optimality of the Han-Kobayashi region for interference channels. The factorization phenomenon has also been used to uncover the largest class of broadcast channels where we now know the capacity region. (Journal paper 1)

415612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415612.value: The whole body of work, albeit its success, is still an ongoing piece of work. The more pieces of the big puzzle one seemingly uncovers, the more avenues it opens for future development. For example the link between hypercontractivity and its characterization using information measures could potentially lead to new developments in both information theory and functional analysis. Also importance of using the properties of extremal distributions and their characterization has become apparent and is an active research area.

415612.value: It makes unexpected deep connections between problems in information theory to math and some of these connections were then used to obtain new deep results. In particular a novel way of proving the optimality of Gaussian distributions was developed.

415712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415712.value: The existing quality assessment methods use mean squared error (MSE) or equivalently, peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) to evaluate the quality of the processed video sequences. These objective metrics are appealing because they are easy to calculate, have clear physical meanings, and are mathematically tractable. However, it has been demonstrated that they do not correspond to the visual quality as perceived by our human eyes. Based on our previous studies, we need to consider the video signal statistics and the properties of human visual system (HVS) in order to develop an efficient video quality metric. Depending on the availability of the reference video, the quality metrics can be divided into three categories: full-reference (FR), no-reference (NR) and reduced-reference (RR). FR metrics require the whole reference video to evaluate the processed video quality. In many practical applications, such as super-resolution and restoration, where the reference video is unavailable, NR metrics can evaluate the visual quality by only analyzing the processed video. However, it is an extremely difficult task. RR metrics are the compromise between FR and NR metrics. They are designed by employing only some partial information (denoted as the RR features) of the reference video. The advantage is that the RR features are also available at the receiver. The received video can then be reconstructed taking into consideration of the RR features to enhance its visual quality, thus providing a better end user experience. The proposed work will be the first attempt to develop an effective RR quality metric for video signal processing. It exploits the spatial signal statistics of the video frames and the temporal coherence between adjacent frames. In addition, human visual system (HVS) characteristics are incorporated to simulate the human perceptual viewing process. The metric will be evaluated through an exhaustive subjective test in conformance to international standard. The proposed RR quality metric will be integrated into a perceptual video coding scheme to enhance the subjective quality of its output. The scheme is a joint encoding and decoding process, where in the encoder, the perceptual quality of the encoded video is maintained by optimizing a rate-distortion function such that the measured RR quality metric is above a certain threshold. In the decoder, the perceptual quality is enhanced by referring to the RR features. For performance evaluation, objective and more importantly subjective quality assessments will be carried out on the reconstructed video sequences. 現有的質量評價的方法使用均方差以及峰值信噪比來評價經過處理的視頻序列的質量。這兩種方法之所以被廣泛採用，是因為他們可以很簡單的被計算出來，具有非常清楚的物理意義，以及數學上很容易被優化使用。但是，現在的實驗已經證明這兩種質量評價方法跟人眼感知的視覺質量是不相關的。基於我們之前的研究，我們需要考慮視頻信號的統計特徵以及人類視覺系統的特性來設計一個有效的視頻質量的評價標準。 根據參照視頻信號的可用性，質量評價標準可以分為三大類：完全參考，無參考，以及部分參考信息的視頻質量評價模型。完全參考質量評價模型需要所有的原始參考視頻幀來衡量經過處理的視頻的質量。然而在許多實際的應用中，譬如超分辨率跟重建，原始的參考視頻是無法得到的。在這種情況下，無參考的質量評價模型可以用來分析經過處理的視頻，進而衡量其主觀質量。但是這是一個非常困難的工作。部分參考的質量評價模型介於完全參考跟無參考之間。只需要利用從原始的參考視頻中提取的部分信息或者特徵來設計質量評價標準。它的好處在于提取的特徵在用戶端也是可以得到的。因此接收到的視頻信號可以通過利用這部分特徵來增強視頻的質量以提供更好的用戶體驗。 在工作中，首先我們要設計一個有效的部分參考的質量評價標準以用於視頻信號處理。它需要挖掘視頻圖像幀空間域跟時間域的信號統計特性。更進一步的，我們需要考慮人類視覺特性的特徵來模擬人眼觀看視頻信號的過程。這樣設計的質量評價標準需要通過國際標準所設定的主觀測試來進行驗證。 提出的部分參考的質量評價標準可以被集成到主觀視頻壓縮算法中以提供更好質量的視頻信號。這個算法是一個聯合優化編碼端跟解碼端的過程。在編碼端，壓縮視頻的視覺質量需要通過一個率失真優化的函數來保證得到的質量評價標準高於一個預先設定的閾值。在解碼端，視頻的主觀質量通過利用提取的特徵進行增強。為了進一步的衡量視頻編碼的表現，壓縮重建的視頻需要通過主觀以及客觀的方式進行評價。

415712.label: Realisation of objectives
415712.value: Objective 1: To investigate the RR features which are sensitive to HVS properties and can effectively capture both the spatial and temporal distortions. The reduced-reference (RR) features that are sensitive to HVS properties are derived from the subband statistical characteristics in the reorganized discrete cosine transform (RDCT) domain in an image coding scheme. For the spatial RDCT subband characteristic, the coefficient distribution of each RDCT subband is modeled by the generalized Gaussian density (GGD) function. The city-block distance (CBD) is employed to measure the modeling error between the actual distribution and the fitted GGD curve. The temporal relationship is represented by block-based motion estimation (BME). By pooling the measurements from the spatial and temporal perspectives, both the spatial and temporal distortions can be captured. Objective 2: To develop an RR video quality metric that can accurately depict the perceptual quality of the video sequence based on the RR features, and to evaluate its effectiveness. A novel RR video quality metric is developed by exploiting the spatial and temporal statistical characteristics of the video signals, where the spatial information change simulates the human visual system (HVS) texture masking property, and the temporal relationship is represented by block-based motion estimation (BME). We further extended our work on reduced reference (RR) quality assessment for images/videos to stereoscopic images by characterizing the statistical properties of the stereoscopic images in the reorganized RDCT domain to construct a novel RR stereoscopic image quality assessment (RR-SIQA) metric. By considering the left view, right view, and difference images together, the performance of the proposed RR-SIQA metric can be further improved. Experimental results showed that the above RR-SIQA metric can well represent the perceptual quality of the stereoscopic images, which outperforms other RR quality metrics for stereoscopic images and even some full reference (FR) quality metrics. Objective 3: To integrate the RR video quality metric into a video codec that can produce higher perceptual quality videos for a given bit rate. Instead of transmitting the RR features via a separate channel which may be subjected to corruption by noise, they are embedded into the rate control algorithm as coding parameters to guide the video encoder. Three approaches are adopted: (a) A new objective visual quality metric (VQM) based on the spatial and temporal RR features is developed. A VQM-based window model is then designed to handle the tradeoff between visual quality consistency and buffer constraint in video encoding. (b) A gradient based R-lambda (GRL) model is deployed for intra frame rate control, where the gradient (an RR feature) can effectively measure the frame-content complexity and enhance the subjective performance of the traditional R-lambda method. (c) An adaptive Lagrangian multiplier for each coding tree unit (CTU) is designed according to its perceptual sensitivity, such that the perceptual quality (hence the bit rate) of the reconstructed video is adjusted accordingly. The above-mentioned perceptual sensitivity for each CTU is measured according to two RR features, namely spatial energy ratio and temporal motion activity. Experimental results showed that consistent visual quality, high rate-distortion efficiency, accurate bit control, and compliant buffer constraint can be achieved by the above proposed rate control algorithms. Objective 4: To evaluate the objective and subjective performance of the video coding scheme developed in Objective 3. The performance of a VQM can be evaluated by depicting the relationship of the obtained VQM values and the provided subjective ratings, specifically the mean opinion score (MOS)/difference mean opinion score (DMOS) value of each distorted video. The MOS/DMOS value is obtained by subjective viewing tests, where many observers participated and provided their opinions on the visual quality of each distorted video. Therefore, it can be regarded as the ground truth for evaluating the metric performances. The performance of the proposed metric was evaluated on the LIVE Video Quality Database [1], which contains 150 distorted videos for ten uncompressed high-quality reference videos. There are 15 distorted videos for each reference video with four different distortion types, specifically, MPEG2 compression, H.264/AVC compression, simulated transmission of H.264 compressed bitstreams through error-prone IP networks, and through error-prone wireless networks. Each video in the LIVE Video Quality Database was assessed by 38 human subjects, who scored the video quality on a continuous quality scale. The subjective ratings obtained from the subjective experiments, along with the reference and distorted videos, are provided in the LIVE Video Quality Database. We also constructed our own IVP Video Quality Database [2] for high-defination (HD) images/videos which was not available when we wanted to perform subjective evaluation for HD images and videos. Details of the database are available in [2]. The subjective evaluation was performed in a studio room with lighting condition satisfying the laboratory environment requirement of the ITU-R BT.500 standard [3], located in the Image and Video Processing (IVP) Laboratory, Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, Hong Kong. Eighteen observers participated in the subjective tests. All of them are non-experts. Their eyesight is either normal or has been corrected to be normal with spectacles. Each observer assessed four source videos and 32 distorted videos. The performance evaluation criteria, LCC, SROCC, and RMSE, were computed for measuring the correlation between the VQM values and subjective ratings. The results were reported in the various research publications (see Section 8). [1] LIVE Video Quality Database. (2010) [Online]. 415712.label: Major findings and research outcome
415712.value: 1. The reduced-reference (RR) features that are sensitive to HVS properties are derived from the subband statistical characteristics in the reorganized discrete cosine transform (RDCT) domain in an image/video coding scheme. Two journal papers (Section 8, Papers #1 and #5) and a conference paper (Section 9, Paper #1) based on the research findings were published. 2. A novel RR video quality metric (VQM) is developed by exploiting the spatial and temporal statistical characteristics of the video signals. This is further extended to stereoscopic images by characterizing the statistical properties of the stereoscopic images in the reorganized RDCT domain. Two journal papers (Section 8, Papers #2 and #7) and a conference paper (Section 9, Paper #2) based on the research findings were published. 3. The RR VQM is integrated into the video codec to provide good perceptual quality at a given bit rate, by embedding the RR features into the rate control algorithm as coding parameters to guide the video encoder. Three journal papers (Section 8, Papers #3, #4, #6 and #8) and a conference paper (Section 9, Paper #3) based on the research findings were published. 4. Subjective evaluation of the experimental results attests to the accuracy of the RR VQM in measuring the subjective quality of the reconstructed video with an objective measure. A high-definition subjective video databse (IVP Video Quality Database) was constructed and made available to other users online: http://ivp.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/research/database/subjective/index.shtml

415712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415712.value: The above research findings point to the possibility of applying the similar reduced-reference features for the subjective evaluation of image/video of other modality, e.g., 3D, retargeted, segmented, virtual reality or animated image/video. The task here is to find the RR features that are sensitive to the human perception of those images/videos.

415712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415712.value: The current video quality assessment methods using mean squared error (MSE) or peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) has been shown to be inconsistent with the visual quality as perceived by the human eyes. Therefore, we need to consider the properties of human visual system (HVS) in order to develop an efficient video quality metric. In this research project, an effective video quality metric is designed based on some partial information or reduced-reference (RR) features of the video signal by analyzing its spatial and temporal statistical properties, which are sensitive to human visual perception. The advantage is that the RR features are also available at the receiver. The received video can then be reconstructed taking into consideration of the RR features to enhance its visual quality, thus providing a better user experience. The proposed RR quality metric will be integrated into a perceptual video coding scheme to enhance the subjective quality of its output.

416012.label: Project Title(Chinese)
416012.value: 多項式數據擾動下的機會約束錐優化:解析近似及高效算法

416012.label: Project Objectives
416012.value: Develop analytic and algorithmic techniques to efficiently process, either exactly or approximately, chance constrained conic optimization problems with polynomial data perturbations. Develop high performance computational tools for solving the proposed tractable inner approximations. Study applications of polynomially perturbed chance constrained conic optimization models, such as the relay beamforming problem in signal processing.

Develop high performance computational tools for solving the proposed tractable inner approximations.
Study applications of polynomially perturbed chance constrained conic optimization models, such as the relay beamforming problem in signal processing.

416012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416012.value: 這研究項目主要針對多項式數據擾動下的機會約束錐優化問題。這類問題有很廣泛的應用，包括金融、信號處理、系統控制等等。這項研究的主要目標是要運用概率和泛函分析對多項式數據擾動下的機會約束錐優化問題建立解析近似和高效算法，並應用到信號處理和控制領域裏的實際工程問題上。

416012.label: Realisation of objectives
416012.value: To achieve the first two objectives of this project, we have developed two powerful approximation techniques for tackling chance constrained conic optimization problems; namely, the Bernstein inequality method and the moment inequality method. The former applies to models with quadratic data perturbations, while the latter applies to those with polynomial data perturbations. Both techniques are developed using deep results in probability theory, and the resulting approximations can be formulated as either second-order cone programming or semidefinite programming problems. Consequently, our proposed approximation can be efficiently solved using off-the-shelf software. To address the third objective and demonstrate the viability of our approach, we have applied our approximation techniques to a number of frontier signal processing applications, including transmit beamforming in multiuser systems, transmit strategies for achieving physical-layer secrecy and energy harvesting, and outage-based relay beamforming. In all these applications, our approach yields the best theoretical results and numerical performance known to date. The new design insights arising from our work have generated a flurry of follow-up work in the signal processing community. In particular, one publication in the IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing (the world's premiere journal on signal processing) in 2014 that is supported by this project has already generated 84 citations according to Google Scholar.

416012.label: Major findings and research outcome
416012.value: The major findings of this project have already been summarized in Sec.5.3 above. They have led to the publication of 4 refereed articles in the Proceedings of the 2014 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (ICASSP 2014) and 2 journal articles, one in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing and one in IEEE Signal Processing Letters.

416012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416012.value: Our research suggests two directions for further development. First, our approximation technique for general polynomial data perturbations is the first of its kind in the literature. It would be interesting to develop alternative techniques that can improve upon its approximation quality and/or numerical performance. Second, it would be interesting to apply our techniques to other practical chance constrained optimization problems, such as those that arise in optimal control.

416012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416012.value: In this project, we have developed efficient methods for handling optimization problems whose data contain random perturbations and whose constraints need only be satisfied with high probability. Our research leads to new design insights in a host of problems in signal processing and yields the best theoretical results and numerical performance known to date.

416212.label: Project Objectives
416212.value: ** To investigate innovative algorithms for realistic simulator - Motivated for fabrics-fluid dynamics, we will study the novel algorithms and theories to address the special problem domain, including multi-phase fluid system, anisotropic material simulation, hybrid modeling and interaction with the dynamic systems, efficient parallel processing. We will work on the realistic fabric/fluids two-way coupling and the integrated dynamic system coupled with the SPH models, and approaches to simulate the dynamics at interactive rate with lower resolution yet producing similar qualitative appearance. ** To develop GPU-accelerated solvers for efficient dynamics - Our goal is to fully exploit the powerful hard-wired features and programmability provided by the GPGPU to accelerate multi-fluids system/algorithms, dynamic integrators computing, soft-fabrics deformation /motion, and augmented dynamic simulations. Parallel processes will be specially designed on GPUs to optimize the dynamic structures of soft fabrics. We will develop multigrid solver for the two-way coupling of the fabric meshes and the multi-phase fluids phenomena. We will study the realistic visual/haptic interaction of dynamic surface based on the simulated physical properties. We will further work on the multi-resolution visual/haptic rendering of dynamics phenomena, for the intuitive and tangible computing.

416212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416212.value: Simulating the dynamic natural phenomena in virtual environments has been in high demands in interactive gaming, dynamic media production, special effects and virtual reality. In real-world applications, it is common to observe the soft fabrics inevitably interacting with the dynamic environments, such as coupling with water, burning in the air, soiled by stains. Realistic simulation of such interactions with dynamic nature in virtual/augmented reality is a must to enhance the immersive and creative experiences. Currently, incorporating the soft-fabrics dynamics with the natural phenomena is rather limited, and not present in interactive tangible simulation. Though some approaches were developed to simulate the interaction with the dynamic environment, most work was motivated to model solid-fluid or cloth-wind/cloth-water coupling. Little work reported to specially simulate the efficient, intuitive soft-fabrics interacting with the augmented fluids phenomena such as multi-phase fluid systems, which remains as research challenges to be tackled and realized. In this project, we will focus our study in innovative algorithms for realistic fabrics-fluid dynamics and GPU-accelerated simulator, and carry out research in interactive multi-fluid systems, hybrid dynamic modeling, graphics/haptics rendering, and tangible computing. We will investigate novel multi-fluids dynamics techniques and their interactions to realize motions and fabric deformation. Multi-fluids simulation studies two or more fluids in one system, such as volcanic cloud, bubbles often required in virtual/augmented environments. We will work on the realistic behavior of the fluids and the dynamic system coupled with the particle level-set model. Parallel processes will be specifically designed on the latest GPGPU to optimize the dynamic structures, using layered cell-based representation. We will further work on the multi-resolution visual/haptic rendering on GPUs, and investigate the tangible textures constructed with the intercross of sinusoidal/harmonic surfaces so to increase the fidelity of the simulation. We hope that the advanced fabrics-fluid interaction techniques to be developed can offer long-term benefits of high quality, lower costs, and optimal efficiency for dynamics applications in Hong Kong. The proposed project will contribute significantly to the basic and applied research in the fields of dynamics phenomena, interactive simulator, tangible computing, and GPU-based accelerator. Besides its research contributions and scientific applications, such advanced tools could also serve as a good pilot study to introduce the latest technologies to Hong Kong, and will facilitate the local industry to exploit many related applications thus further enhance the hi-tech/hi-value competitive edge of Hong Kong. 自然动态在虚拟环境中的仿真可广泛应用在交互游戏，动态媒体，特效生成及虚拟现实中。在真实的场景中，动态织物和流体环境的交互显而易见，如水的浸染，火的燃烧，以及斑点/块的形成。自然动态的真实感模拟是实现虚拟/增强现实系统沉浸感以及创新感的必要途径。当前，动态织物与流体环境的交互模拟仍有待开发，并且少有动态触觉反馈模拟。虽然已开发一些与动态环境的交互技术，大多数的工作只限于固体-流体，或者简单的布料-风/布料-水的耦合建模。极少工作是直接对动态织物与多流体的高效、真实感仿真，如多相流系统，这是一个极具挑战与期待解决的研究领域。 在这个项目中，我们着眼于动态织物与流体环境的真实感模拟的创新性算法研究和GPU加速模拟器的开发。我们的研究包括交互多相流系统、混合动态模拟、图形/触觉渲染，实时动态计算等方面。我们将进一步探索新颖的多流体动态模拟以及交互技术，以此实现软织物形变和运动。多流体模拟研究在一个系统中两种或以上的流体交互，如火山灰和岩浆，水泡等在虚拟/增强环境中的自然模拟。多流体和混合粒子集的动态系统及其真实感特性也将是我们的一个研究方向。我们会特别设计基于GPGPU并行计算方法来优化动态结构，有效地采用分层的单元模型。我们将继续深入探索并行的多分辨率可视/触觉渲染，以及研究交互动态纹理来增加模拟的真实度。我们希望研发的动态织物与多流体的交互技术将会给香港动态应用领域带来高质量，低成本，以及效率优化等的长期收益。本项目将会贡献于自然动态场景、交互模拟器、图形/触觉计算、GPU并行加速等基础和应用领域。其研发的高科技平台可作为香港引进先进技术的开拓者，并可协助本地工业去探索相关应用，进而加强香港在高科技/高价值领域的竞争力。

416212.label: Major findings and research outcome
416212.value: Obj-1: We advect the mapping function with high-order BFECC method and the error checking, which is dynamically remapped. Our method brings significant improvement in accuracy, and simply control the level of details of fluid. (J2) We introduce uniform grids to the vortex filament model as the motion carrier to relax the computation cost and efficiently control the locomotion of vortex dynamics under the vorticity field. Our scheme produces plausible fluid effects with macroscopic vortex structure, difficult to achieve using pure grid-based methods. Further, we work on the effective filament-mesh particle-particle method for fast wall-bounded turbulent simulation with ample details. The approach can synthesize the lost small-scale vertical structures, and achieve the fluid-object interaction with vortex shedding in a lightweight manner. (J3-4) We propose a new representation of cloth simulation based on local cylindrical coordinates, which describe the main features of dynamic sequence. The temporal prediction facilitates the high compression rate with fine wrinkle details and lower computation cost. For free surface tracking, we develop gradient-augmented level set for higher accuracy interpolation with octree grid, to capture fluid details well while keeping efficiency. (J5,C5) Obj-2: We worked on the real-time framework for realistic fluid simulation and rendering on GPU. Our framework can exploit the full computing power of the modern GPU and mitigate the computational needs of each simulation step in contrast to the previous methods. The framework can produce realistic results using MC with small cell size. (J1,C2) We develop the novel SPH-based detail-preserving fluid control method, which can effectively solve the fluid deformation and preserve abundant fluid details. We specially designed the control energy transfer for preserving fluid details, which can remedy the inadequate control force in the movement of the control particles. Our method can provide real-time simulation and allows users to interact with the simulation freely. (J6) We propose the novel local-control method easily integrated into the existing fluid simulation frameworks. The continuity of the velocity is preserved along the boundary of the local areas via mixing the local and global velocity fields. (C1) We develop the hybrid vortex model for efficient and stable simulation. Our system optimizes the computational complexity of vorticity-driven model and refines its physical process when used in the fluid simulation. The parallel processing of our hybrid model is also realized on modern GPU for efficient simulations. (C3,C4) (J#-Journal paper, C#-Conf. paper)

416212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416212.value: In order to obtain the velocity on grid with faster convergence and higher accuracy, we will employ more efficient and accurate solvers (such as PCG solver and multi-grid solver) for Poisson problem. We plan to simulate highly turbulent fluids in large-scale scenarios with appreciable quality, and to explore the possibility of extending our method on water simulation by using vortex filaments to handle the simulation of free-surface flow. Our method in cloth simulation cannot automatically determine the optimal bits for encoding the LCC channels when a certain KG error is given as the upper bound. Running much more test cases and analyze the bits-error curves may help to obtain some practical guidance. Currently, we use a simple linear temporal predictor to exploit the temporal coherence. It is still an interesting future work to find effective spatial and temporal predictors based on the characteristics of dihedral angle component for general cloth simulation. We will improve the procedure of turbulence generation and provide more fluid turbulence details. To reduce the artificial viscosity caused by the control force and thus improve the visual quality of the fluid control results is also the direction of our future work.

416212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416212.value: In vortex models, direct simulation has a quadratic complexity when only advecting the vortex elements, so the simulation scale and speed are limited. The proposed vortex filaments in grids scheme balances simulation speed and the scale of details as well as reduces computation costs. Our further work introduces the surface vorticity into the main flow as turbulence (vortex shedding), so that we can synthesize the lost small-scale vertical structures and achieve the complex fluid-object interaction with vortex shedding at boundaries in a lightweight manner. Realistically reproducing the behavior of garments with fine details is computational costly, which makes it impractical for mobile applications or those demanding for high frame rates. We build a local cylindrical coordinate system that outperforms many methods even without delicately exploiting the temporal coherence, because it automatically discovers the strong temporal coherence of dynamics sequence. Our method on fluid control can provide the users and designers with the local-control tool for editing the dynamic fluid scenes intuitively. The detail-preserving fluid control framework can effectively solve the fluid deformation problem and preserve abundant fluid details as well. We incorporate parallel surface reconstruction technique to extract the surfaces of the fluid, which is fast and memory efficient.

416312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416312.value: In recent years, missing children problem has snowballed into a social crisis in China. More than 0.2 million children become missing each year and sadly very few can be found even-tually. Unlike developed countries where many nationwide emergency help channels are available for finding missing children, China does not have a nationwide system to address this problem. Recently, both the government and the society in general start to work hard to tackle this urgent problem partly because of a call to help by a blogger. This particular grass root social network approach has attracted national attention, and has in a way helped to re-veal the seriousness of the problem. Prof. Yu Jianrong of Chinese Academy of Social Science set up a Micro Blog (Chinese version of Twitter) http://t.sina.com.cn/jiejiuqier, called “Saving homeless children through photo taking on the streets”, hoping to help parents to find their missing children. However, as the number of photos increase, it becomes difficult to keep track of all the posts. In this project, we propose to use face recognition technology to help searching photos on the website automatically. We encounter two major challenges when working on the face recognition system: the large appearance changes of children faces over aging and large pose variation. Unfortunately, the performances of existing methods are not satisfactory for this demanding application. To address these challenges, we propose a new age invariant face recognition algorithm based on coupled projection encoding which can reduces aging variation at the feature extraction stage and a pose robust face recognition algorithm based on pose adaptive component alignment which can handle large pose variation efficiently. Then together with existing face recognition algorithms we hope to develop a working face recognition system for missing children faces matching on the internet. 近些年，失踪儿童问题已经成为很严重的社会问题。每年在近20万的失踪儿童中，仅有很少量的最终被找回。很多西方的发达国家有各种不同的覆盖全国的渠道帮助寻找失踪儿童，而中国至今没有类似渠道。最近，由于一个特殊的微博的出现，政府和一些社会组织开始着手解决这个问题。这个由社科院教授于建嵘创建的微博“随手拍照解救乞讨儿童” http://weibo.com/jiejiuqier 吸引了大量的社会关注。但随着微博上照片数量的增加，跟踪和查找照片变得越来越难。本项目提出用人像自动识别技术来帮助查找失踪儿童照片。我们希望能够解决针对这个特殊应用的两个关键性的技术问题，即跨年龄儿童人脸识别和跨姿态人脸识别。我们计划在特征提取阶段用偶合投影编码的方法来减小由于年龄变化而引起的特征变化，同时提出一个基于姿态自适应人脸对齐技术的跨姿态人脸识别算法。通过与现有的人脸识别算法的结合，我们希望人脸识别技术最终能够帮助在互联网上通过照片查找失踪儿童。

416312.label: Realisation of objectives
416312.value: All the objectives in this project have been realized successfully. (1) We propose a method that is capable of separating the variation caused by aging from the person-specific features that are stable. Specifically, we propose a new method, called Hidden Factor Analysis (HFA). This method captures the intuition above through a probabilistic model with two latent factors: an identity factor that is age-invariant and an age factor affected by the aging process. Then, the observed appearance can be modeled as a combination of the components generated based on these factors. We also develop a learning algorithm that jointly estimates the latent factors and the model parameters using an EM procedure. Extensive experiments on two well-known public domain face aging datasets: MORPH (the largest public face aging database) and FGNET, clearly show that the proposed method achieves notable improvement over state-of-the-art algorithms. (2) We propose to learn a set of high-level feature representations through deep learning, referred to as Deep hidden IDentity features (DeepID), for face verification, which is robust to different poses and face variations. We found that DeepID can be effectively learned through challenging multi-class face identification tasks, whilst they can be generalized to other tasks (such as verification) and new identities unseen in the training set. Moreover, the generalization capability of DeepID increases as more face classes are to be predicted at training. DeepID features are taken from the last hidden layer neuron activations of deep convolutional networks (ConvNets). When learned as classifiers to recognize about 10, 000 face identities in the training set and configured to keep reducing the neuron numbers along the feature extraction hierarchy, these deep ConvNets gradually form compact identity-related features in the top layers with only a small number of hidden neurons. The proposed features are extracted from various face regions to form complementary and over-complete representations. Any state-of-the-art classifiers can be learned based on these high-level representations for face verification. 97.45% verification accuracy on LFW is achieved with only weakly aligned faces. (3) We develop an effective method to transfer deep representation learned from a source domain to a target domain. This technique improves the generalization of our deep models. In particular, we formulate a joint face representation adaptation and clustering approach in a deep learning framework. The adaptation of deep representation is achieved without any strong supervision but through iteratively discovered weak pairwise identity constraints derived from potentially noisy face clustering result. Experiments on three benchmark video datasets (including ACCIO dataset with a number of children faces) demonstrate that our approach generates character clusters with high purity compared to existing video face clustering methods, which are either based on deep face representation (without adaptation) or carefully engineered features.

416312.label: Major findings and research outcome
416312.value: As research outcome, 1 journal paper and 8 conference papers are published. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (PAMI) is the best journal on computer vision and machine learning. 8 papers were published on the top three conferences on computer vision (CVPR, ICCV, and ECCV). In this project, we have proposed a hidden factor analysis (HFA) approach to address the challenging problem of age invariant face recognition. The basic idea of the HFA model is to separate the aging variations from the person specific features for pursuing the robust age-invariant face features. Extensive experiments conducted on two public domain face aging datasets (MORPH Album 2 and FGNET) convincingly demonstrate the superiority of our HFA model over the state-of-the-art algorithms (paper in Part C.9 No. 6). Next, to improve face recognition performance, we proposed a random path (RP) measure for face recognition based on the path similarity defined from random walk in the network. To adopt the RP measure for face recognition, we construct two types of networks on face data: the in-face network and the out-face network. The in-face and out-face networks describe the local and global structural information of faces, respectively. Extensive experiments on the Multi-PIE and LFW face databases validate that the proposed RP measure has the superiority of discriminating complex faces with the large intra-personal variations including pose, illumination, and expression (paper in Part C.9 No. 3). We also leveraged the geometric archetype hull model into face modeling. Based on a scalable graph characterized by a compact set of archetypes, we proposed an archetype-driven ranking framework that can scale up to massive datasets. This framework generates a rank vector over the archetype hull, which well captures the relevance between any query and the archetypes. The archetype hull ranking is then carried out on each block of face images, leading to a blockwise face similarity measure. By integrating blockwise similarity measurements with learned importance weights, a sensible face similarity measure is eventually yielded. The performance of the face similarity measure was validated through recognition and verification experiments performed on three benchmark face databases (paper in Part C.9 No. 1). The most important breakthrough in this project is that we found that deep learning method an extremely effective algorithm to learn for robust face representation. We obtained good results on face verification and attribute recognition (paper in Part C.9 No. 4, 5 and 2). Later we found that by representing a large amount of different identities with a small number of hidden variables, highly compact and discriminative features are acquired. The features extracted from different face regions are complementary and further boost the performance. It achieved 97.45% face verification accuracy on LFW (the most important face recognition benchmark), while only requiring weakly aligned faces. Even more compact and discriminative DeepID can be learned if more identities are available to increase the size of the training database (paper in Part C.9 No. 7). In addition, we found that in the absence of precise face annotations on the target domain, one can create a feedback loop in which the deep representation provides robust features for face clustering, and the clustering results provide weak pairwise constraints for learning more suitable deep representation with respect to the target domain (paper in Part C.9 No. 8).

416312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416312.value: In our study, we found that deep learning performs exceedingly well on face recognition under uncontrolled condition comparing to other state of the art approaches. We will further pursue this research direction to develop more powerful deep learning-based methods on other computer vision problems.

416312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416312.value: The key objective of this project is to investigate better approaches to extract robust face features for face recognition. Deep learning shows remarkable performance among the different methods we examined. The approach is not only robust to different poses, but also ages and illumination given a large training database. The method can be used for many real-world applications, such as face recognition to help finding missing children, face clustering in photo album, face verification to provide remote authentication for banking services, and improving human-computer interactions.

416412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416412.value: Tagging has been widely adopted as an effective means for data organization in recent years. In the relevant applications, an object is associated with a number of tags, each of which can be an arbitrary string. Such an organization offers a high degree of flexibility compared to conventional methods of categorizing objects by adhering to a certain hierarchy. In this project, we plan to carry out a systematic study on query processing techniques on tagged data. The major challenges stem from the fact that a query can specify selective predicates on an arbitrary combination of tags, rendering it difficult to decide which information to precompute in order to minimize the query time. The outcomes of the project are expected to benefit applications operating on tagged data (e.g., Flickr, Zagat, Gmail, etc.) and advance understanding of the theoretical characteristics of several fundamental computer science problems. 近年來，標籤作為一種有效的數據組織方式已被廣泛採用。在相關的應用中，一個對象常與許多標籤相關聯，而每個標籤可以是一個任意的字符串。與常規的基于分類的數據組織方法相比，標籤提供了高度的靈活性。在這個項目中，我們將系統地研究對標籤數據進行查詢處理的技術。此課題主要挑戰來自於這樣一個事實：即一個查詢可以在任意的標籤上施加條件，致使我們難以預先決定計算哪些信息，以盡量減少查詢的時間。本項目的成果預計將適用于許多建于標記數據之上的應用（如Flickr，Zagat，Gmail等），並增強計算機界對幾個基本問題的理論本質的理解。

All these journals and conferences are top-tier venues in the database area and/or theoretical computer science. Next, we discuss how the objectives (as stated above in Section 5.1) have been achieved by referring to these papers: Regarding Objective 1, this project has initialized the research on several new computer science problems that involve tagged data. Two representative examples are the "I/O-Efficient Bundled Range Aggregation" problem as studied in our TKDE'14 paper, and the "Concurrent Range Reporting" problem in two-dimensional space as studied our SODA'14 paper. These problems are under the framework of "bundled query processing" -- a key concept that is established by this project. Regarding Objective 2, we have devised systematically a full set of techniques that are suitable for practical implementation. Even better, all our techniques -- including those published in traditional database venues (like SIGMOD) -- come with strong theoretical guarantees, i.e., bearing the feature of "small and sweet" as stated in the objective. Regarding Objective 3, the entire collection of papers in Section 5.1 serves as the full documentation of the theoretical results we have derived throughout the project. Note that these results have appeared not only in the database community, but also in prestigious venues of theoretical computer science like ACM Transactions on Algorithms and SODA. Most of these results still remain the best till this day. Finally, Regarding Objective 4, all our TKDE, VLDBJ, SIGMOD, and VLDB papers feature extensive experimental results obtained from our system prototypes. These results confirm the efficiency and feasibility of our techniques in practice.

416412.label: Major findings and research outcome
416412.value: As mentioned earlier, this project has produced 5 journal articles (3 in TKDE, 1 in VLDBJ, and 1 in ACM Transactions on Algorithms), and 8 conference papers (3 in SIGMOD, 1 in VLDB, 2 in PODS, and 1 in SODA). All these journals and conferences are top-tier venues in the database area and/or theoretical computer science. This project has laid down a solid foundation for investigating query processing algorithms on tagged data. Here we briefly mention some examples, due to the space constraint. Among the most important findings is a systematic set of theory that we have developed on "bundled query processing" -- a concept that is produced from this project. Such queries inherit the convenience of keyword-based search, without sharing its disadvantage: lack of effective data organization that prevents the design of indexes with attractive theoretical guarantees. Under the framework of this concept, our TKDE'14 paper titled "I/O-efficient Bundled Range Aggregation" proposed a linear-size structure that can support bundled range aggregate queries in logarithmic I/Os, and yet, can be updated with the same cost as a B-tree per insertion and deletion. Our SODA'14 paper titled "Concurrent Range Reporting in Two-Dimensional Space" continued this line of research by examining the bundled version of range reporting on 2D points. The scientific investigation in this project also touched upon several fundamental problems in computational geometry, which prompted us to revisit many of those problems. Our revisiting has been fairly rewarding. Our PODS'13 paper titled "I/O-Efficient Planar Range Skyline and Attrition Priority Queues" developed asymptotically optimal structures for a number of variants of "constrained skyline queries" in external memory. The very same paper also contained an I/O-efficient version of the classic "priority queue with attrition". As yet another example, our VLDB'13 paper titled "Approximate MaxRS in Spatial Databases" provided a fast algorithm for answering "where is the densest region" question -- a very important task in mining multidimensional data. All these algorithms and data structures can be easily adapted to work on tagged data, with no or little sacrifice on the performance guarantees. This project has produced prototype systems that can be deployed to answer a large variety of queries on tagged data. Our source code has been tested by extensive experiments that were designed to scrutinize our algorithms' behavior in numerous tough situations. Our code is both efficient and reliable.

416412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416412.value: Query processing on tagged data is a fascinating topic. During the years of this project, the area has been expanding quickly, as is clear from the number of relevant papers in premium conferences and journals. Most of the discoveries, however, concern the RAM model, whereas I/O efficient query algorithms on tagged data still remain a tough challenge for many interesting problems. This is so even for the following problem that may sound too rudimentary at first glance. The input consists of m sets: S_1, S_2, ..., S_m (the domain from which the elements are drawn is not important). We want to build an index structure such that the following queries can be answered: given any distinct integers i, j in the range [1, m], report the number of common elements of S_i and S_j. In RAM, the problem can be nicely solved using O(n) space, and O(sqrt(n)) query time, where n is the total number of elements in all the sets. In external memory, it would be nice to have a structure consuming O(n/B) blocks and answering a query in O(sqrt(n/B)) I/Os. Unfortunately, such a structure still remains elusive, and has become a well-known open problem in the field.

416412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416412.value: Tagged data are everywhere. Think of, for example, your Gmail account, where you can put any textual labels on your emails. This allows you to search your emails in convenient ways such as: find all mails labeled both as "recreational" and "relationship". Such convenience stems from the important fact that the same mail can carry multiple and arbitrary labels. Similar situation also exists in commercial database systems, where data are increasingly tagged with all kinds of user-defined labels in order to considerably enhance the functionality of the search mechanism. However, unlike Gmail which essentially only needs to support your search on *your* mails, a database system must be able to do so on a gigantic amount of data. Making things even more complicated, the database must integrate such query-by-tag functionalities into the vast set of predicates that can already be supported. How to guarantee space and query efficiency thus becomes a tough challenge. This project aims to tackle exactly this challenge. We have developed a set of new techniques that are able to reduce significantly both the amount of space usage and the time of query answering in database systems.

416512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416512.value: Graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms forming a hexagonal lattice, has attracted increasing attention from physicists and engineers in the last seven years because of its unique electrical and optical properties. Recent theoretical and experimental works have shown that graphene possesses third order optical nonlinearities which are about four orders of magnitude larger than in silicon. Here we propose an experimental study of the nonlinear optical properties of graphene placed on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) optical waveguides. The evanescent field from the waveguide propagating parallel to the graphene layer will enable an increase of the interaction length by six orders of magnitude compared with the normal incidence beam employed in the work by E. Hendry et al. in 2010 and H. Yang et al. in 2011. Our proposed work will include studies of graphene on both straight waveguides and micro-ring structures. The proposed experiments are aimed at determining the nonlinear optical properties of graphene on silicon optical waveguides and to explore possible limitations from linear and nonlinear absorption on potential photonic device applications. We also propose to investigate some possible new applications of graphene-silicon waveguides including their use for a new type of mode-locked hybrid fiber-silicon waveguide lasers, and to assess the suitability of graphene- silicon waveguides for optical frequency conversion, the generation of wideband optical frequency combs and the generation of mid-infrared wavelengths. 在過去的七年里，單層碳原子通過六邊形的晶格形成的石墨烯，由於其自身獨特的電和光的性質，吸引著物理學家和工程師們越來越多的注意力。近期的理論和實驗工作已表明，石墨烯具有比硅大四個量級的三階光非線性。在這裡，我們提出對鋪在絕緣層上覆硅的光波導上的石墨烯的非線性性質進行實驗上的研究。與垂直入射光相比，在石墨烯層中平行傳播的來自波導的瞬逝場使得相互作用長度增大了六個量級。所提出的實驗致力於測定硅的光波導上的石墨烯的光非線性性質，以及探索線性和非線性吸收對潛在的光器件應用可能帶來的限制。同時，我們也提出研究石墨烯-硅波導一些可能的新應用，包括它們在鎖模光纖激光器的應用，以及評估石墨烯-硅波導是否合適用於光的頻率轉換、光的寬帶頻率梳的產生和中紅外波長的產生。

416512.label: Realisation of objectives
416512.value: The first objective was 100% realized, and the integration of graphene on silicon optical waveguides led to several journal publications that described the linear effects of graphene (on optical absorption, optical dispersion and linear effective refractive index change that produced shifts in the center wavelengths of resonators and grating couplers) and nonlinear effects (including studies of the saturable absorption and spectral hole burning). The high linear losses of graphene on silicon waveguides, of about 24dB/mm at midinfrareed wavelengths, precluded the demonstration efficient nonlinear devices for four wave mixing. The second objective was about 80% completed, with the demonstration of several novel graphene on silicon photonic devices including the first mid-infrared graphene on silicon photodetector (published in nature photonics) and the demonstration of graphene on silicon for hybrid fiber-silicon mode locked femtosecond fiber lasers, and the use of graphene to increase the optical bandwidth of waveguide grating couplers. As mentioned in the first paragraph we did not succeed in attempts of using graphene on silicon waveguides for nonlinear frequency conversion because of the high linear optical losses.
