416512.label: Major findings and research outcome
416512.value: The major research fndings include: 1. Graphene placed on silicon waveguides form an electrical heterostructure which can give large optical absorption in the graphene, and the photogenerated carriers can diffuse into silicon and have long carrier lifetime. Strong optical absorption as high as 200 dB/mm loss results from such structures (IEEE JSTQE 20 2014). 2. The large optical absorption of graphene on silicon waveguides which enables it to be used in high efficiency mid infrared photodetectors (Nature Photonics vol. 13, pp.888-892, 2013) 3. Efficient spectral hole burning and saturable absorption of graphene on silicon waveguides was characterised for the first time (Opt Lett. 38, pp.2206-2209, 2013). The saturable absorption allows it to be used for low power mode locking of erbium fiber lasers (IEEE Group Four Photonics Conference, 2013) 4. The high refractive index of graphene can modify the optical dispersion of grating couplers when a monolayer graphene is placed on top of a grating coupler and this was demonstrated to enhance the optical bandwidth of the grating coupler (IEEE Group Four Photonics Conference, 2013). 5. Graphene on silicon-on sapphire waveguides have lower losses at mid-infrared than near infrared because of the lower optical confinement, but optical absorption losses of 24dB/mm are still too high for it to be used in nonlinear wavelength conversion (Asia Communications and Photonics Conference 2014). 6. In the quest to develop mid-infrared graphene on silicon waveguide devices, we advanced the technology of mid-infrared silicon waveguides by engineering novel sub-wavelength grating couplers and wideband grating couplers (Opt Lett vol 37 2012, Applied Phys Lett vol.104 11109, 2014) 7. In the quest to enhance nonlinear interaction of light with graphene, we fabricated silicon slot waveguides and place graphene over the slot. These waveguides exhibited extremely high optical absorption of 960dB/mm. (IEEE Photonic Conference, 2015)

416512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416512.value: There is potential for further improve the fabrication process of the graphene on silicon waveguide photodetectors for the mid infrared wavelength by using a photolithography to define the patterned graphene rather than the hand-crafted placement of exfoliated graphene on the silicon waveguide.

416512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416512.value: One of the highlights from this project was the first mid-infrared graphene on silicon waveguide photodetector which offered the advantages of high responsivity and room temperature operation. Such detectors may find applications in mid-infrared spectroscopy for gas sensing and enviromental monitoring. We also carried out detailed studies of the linear and nonlinear optical properties of graphene on silicon waveguides and developed applications in ultrashort pulse generation by using the saturable absorption of graphene to mode lock a fiber laser, and for the engineering of the optical properties of waveguide grating couplers for enhancing their coupling bandwidth.

416712.label: Project Objectives
416712.value: To develop an effective, efficient and robust framework for fast 3D cardiac MR imaging based on compressed sensing and parallel imaging. To establish an optimal undersampling strategy to guarantee a high degree of incoherence for 3D cardiac MRI. To highly sparsify the cardiac volumes using an effective learning algorithm. 416712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416712.value: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has become one of the major diagnostic imaging modalities for heart diseases. The advantages of cardiac MRI are its noninvasive nature and extremely high resolution. Three-dimensional (3D) cardiac MRI is graining increasing attention as it allows excellent views of the entire heart at any orientation and with any chamber shape. In particular, 3D cardiac MRI can provide detailed information on cardiovascular structures, ventricular shape, myocardial strain and material microstructures. The high quality MRI volume data enable detailed examinations of heart anatomical structures and physiological functions. The main limitation of 3D cardiac MRI is the rather long imaging time required to achieve high spatial resolution for visualizing small structures and vessels. In clinical cardiac MRI, patients need to hold breath in order to reduce respiratory motion artifacts, which is especially challenging for patients with low breath-hold capability. To address this problem, we propose to design an effective, efficient and robust framework for fast 3D cardiac MRI based on compressed sensing and parallel imaging. In particular, an optimal 3D undersampling scheme will be designed to be robust to motion artifacts and guarantee a high degree of incoherence. In addition, the adaptive transform learning algorithm will be employed to capture the intrinsic characteristics of cardiac MRI images, and the compressed sensing technique will be effectively integrated with parallel reconstruction. In this project, we aim to translate the state-of-the-art compressed sensing technology to accelerate 3D cardiac MRI. With the proposed framework, high spatial resolution cardiac MR volume will be achieved with larger spatial coverage, high signal-to-noise ratio and low artifact level. The proposed undersampling scheme and the reconstruction algorithm will be deployed on the clinical MRI scanner for practical 3D cardiac MRI applications, such as the whole heart, late gadolinium enhancement, coronary, cine and perfusion. The proposed technique is expected to decrease the scanning time and the cost, and improve the accuracy of examinations of cardiac structures and functions, for instance, volume computation and functional assessment of ventricular, morphology examination of cardiovascular anatomy, blood flow quantification, left ventricular ejection fraction, and myocardial contractility. 三維心臟磁共振成像（MRI）是如今最精準并且非侵入性診斷心臟病症的影像技術。磁共振成像的优点是无辐射，在临床应用中依赖高品質的三位体数据才可以詳細地检查心臟解剖結構和生理功能。现阶段高品质的三位心脏体数据所需的採集時間很长，故迫切需要研究新的有效方法，以減少數據採集時間，而不會降低心脏體数据的質量。這個項目的目標是（一）建立一個有效的基于壓縮感知和并行成像的三維心臟MRI影像重建框架；（二）研究适合于现有核磁共振成像掃描儀的欠采样算法和重建算法；（三）提高心臟結構和功能檢查的準確性。

416712.label: Realisation of objectives
416712.value: The first objective was to develop a robust algorithm based on new computational techniques to enhance the quality and accurate the scanning process of cardiac imaging. We approached with the parallel block matching method based on a B-spline deformable model to develop a tracking framework. This framework consisted of a set of control points allowed to alter the left ventricular shape according to the tracked material points. The feasibility of this approach was first tested on data from echocardiography. The proposed method successfully tracked the speckles within the 3D echo and also accurately identified the infarcted regions in patients with myocardial infarction. This speckletracking method was capable of operating in real-time using high computational efficient GPU-based implementation technique (Wu H.S. et al. International journal of cardiology 2013). This study also satisfied object number 4 by the implementation of GPU parallel computing technique to accelerate the reconstruction process. The second objective was to establish an optimal undersampling strategy for 3D cardiac MRI. A methodology was proposed to formulate the undersampled dynamic MRI reconstruction as a least squares optimization problem regularized by non-convex low-rank and sparsity constraints to improve the quality of the reconstructed images. It also accelerated the reconstruction of dynamic MRI as it integrated both non-convex low-rank and sparsity constraints into a unified mathematical framework. Results demonstrated image quality were improved (Liu W. et al. Sensor 2016 under review). In the third objective, different parameters and characteristic measurements were carried out. Left ventricular (LV) torsion is sensitive to cardiac contraction and relaxation and it was a useful index of myocardial mechanics to complement standard strain measures. In this project, LV torsion was quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) tagging and echocardiographic speckle tracking. A novel calculation method was developed and results demonstrated that LV torsion calculated from CMR was accurate and more realistic by considering the incompressibility of myocardium (Wu H.S. et al. International journal of cardiology 2014). The forth objective was to accurate 3D reconstruction with parallel computing techniques. The project (Wu H.S. et al. International journal of cardiology 2013) mentioned in objective one partially satisfied this goal. We further investigated novel techniques to improve image quality and speed up the image acquisition process. A regularized parallel imaging reconstruction method embedded with the sparsity-promoting wavelet prior and total generalized variation (TGV) regularizer was proposed. Experimental results obtained from both simulated and in vivo MRI datasets using the proposed method were compared with several representative reconstruction methods and it demonstrated that our method provided superior reconstruction performance in terms of both quantitative evaluation and visual quality (Liu W. et al. Magnetic resonance imaging 2016 Under review). Besides the technique part of developing novel algorithms, we also aimed to investigate many clinical problems and enhanced the use of computer-aided diagnosis. Cardiac atlas was an important ground truth for diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases. A new nonrigid registration algorithm incorporating shape information to produce comprehensive atlases was developed. The experimental results showed that the new registration algorithm outperformed conventional techniques and it produced an more representative and accurate atlas of the cardiac structures (Zha Y. et al. PloS one 2015). A major characteristic of patients with thalassemia was the myocardial iron loading. One of our recent studies investigated the use of T2* MRI to identify over-loading of iron. An effective algorithm was proposed to segment aligned free induction decay sequential myocardium images. Free induction decay images were registered for T2* mapping. Segmented myocardium regions were divided into sectors for a region-based quantification of cardiac iron loading. The proposed method was feasible in myocardium segmentation and was clinically applicable to measure myocardium iron loading (Luo Y.G. et al. Scientific Reports 2015). Furthermore, we also proposed a few techniques to measure cardiac valve calcification and to use level set approach for automatic segmentation of left ventricle. (Wang D. et al. International journal of cardiology 2013; Wu H.S. et al. International journal of cardiology 2013)

416712.label: Major findings and research outcome
416712.value: A registration algorithm was developed to construct cardiac atlas. This algorithm implemented non-rigid registration, combined multi-scale gradient orientation features and utilized cost function for registration to analyze shape information. This cardiac atlas accurately represented heart structure of the Chinese population and the proposed algorithm outperformed the conventional method (Zha Y. et al. Plos One 2015). Another study was carried out to assess myocardial iron loading. In this study, an algorithm to perform myocardium segmentation was developed based on geodesic active contour and T2* MRI was used to measure myocardium iron loading. Experimental results indicated that thalassemia major patients with T2* intensity lower than 20 ms in the cardiac regions were suffered from heavy iron loading. The proposed method was able to subjectively segment and measure cardiac iron loading which beneficial to both patients and clinicians and improved from the conventional method which were labor intensive and operator dependent (Luo et al. Scientific Report 2015). Furthermore, computational fluid dynamics simulation was applied to investigate pulsatile hemodynamics changes in patients with thoracic aortic dissection. Data from computed tomography angiography was used to reconstruct dissected aorta geometries. The proposed simulation approach provided complementary information to clinicians for better understanding of the pulsatile hemodynamics and contributed to the medical industry for the potential application of this technique as a diagnostic tool for patients with thoracic aortic dissection (Ko et al. Journal of X-Ray Science and Technology 2016). We also proposed to investigate the use of delayed-enhancement MRI to study atrial fibrillation. One significant marker of atrial fibrillation was the dimensional and structural change in left atrium. MR imaging enabled us to measure the volume of left atrium and revealed wall scars at high resolution. We suggested the use of delayed-enhancement MRI to collect the volume, functional data and scarring formation of left atrium for analysis and to ultimately distinguish atrial fibrillation from healthy atrium (Wang et al. 6th APHRS & CardioRhythm 2013 Hong Kong). Furthermore, we developed a computational technique to assist the diagnosis of cardiac valve calcification using gray values and thickness based on ultrasound images. Results indicated that the gray values and wall thickness between healthy and calcified cardiac valves had a significant difference (Wang et al. International journal of cardiology 2013). Another technique based on parallel block matching was developed to obtain myocardial deformation fields for functional analysis (Wu et al. International journal of cardiology 2013)

416712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416712.value: MRI is a non-invasive imaging modality that could captures the structure, scar and even the motion of the heart. In this project, we developed several computational techniques to assist the diagnosis of different types of cardiac diseases including myocardial iron loading, cardiac valve calcification, congenital heart disease and atrial fibrillation. One potential further development would be the use of diffusion tensor imaging technique to reveal the fiber integrity of the heart. It has great potential in bringing large impact to investigate myocardial infarction. Studies based on animal models indicated that fiber orientations, sheet structure and fiber track integrity of the heart in myocardial infarction were altered but lack of data and results collected from human individuals. We postulate that fiber helix, sheet angles and fiber anisotropy values were able to be used to distinguish myocardial infarction from healthy heart. Segmentation of the atrium is a common pre-processing step applied on MR images before we attempt to measure any parameters. One new approach is to apply "deeply-supervised 3D fully convolutional neural networks" technique to train an algorithm to perform the heart segmentation. Preliminary work has been carried out and will be applied on human data soon.

416712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416712.value: This project developed several segmentation techniques used to measure different parameters of human heart based on CT, MRI and Ultrasound images. We applied our techniques to segment the left atrium or the whole heart in images from patients with myocardial iron loading, cardiac valve calcification and congenital heart disease. We also proposed to use fluid dynamics simulation to investigate pulsatile hemodynamics changes in patients with thoracic aortic dissection. Furthermore, parallel block matching was applied to study myocardial deformation fields for cardiac functional analysis. We also proposed to use delayed-enhancement MRI to study atrial fibrillation and diffusion tensor imaging to study myocardial infarction. Both approaches have not been widely adopted due to many technical difficulties encountered such as the limited resolution to reveal fine structure of the cardiac tissues and motion artifact caused by the heart. In this project, we have achieved the goals of using computational techniques to assist the diagnosis of different cardiac diseases and further investigated new algorithm to accelerate or improve the accuracy of the segmentation. New MRI modalities including DTI and delayed-enhancement MRI have been introduced and the feasibility of using these new techniques have been tested.

416712.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
416712.value: In this project, we collaborated with Renmin Hospital of Wuhan University in Wuhan and South China University of Technology in Guangzhou to develop an registration algorithm that constructed cardiac atlas. Patients were recruited from the Guangzhou General Hospital and the algorithm was developed in Hong Kong and Wuhan. This non-rigid registration algorithm combined the multi-scale gradient orientation features and cost function for registration to analyze shape information and to construct the atlas. This cardiac atlas accurately represented heart structure of the Chinese population and the proposed algorithm outperformed the conventional method. This study combined the resources from three affiliations and a manuscript was successfully published. We also collaborated with the Second Hospital of Jilin University, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology and the Department of Computer Science and Engineering in CUHK to carry out a study to assess myocardial iron loading. In this study, we worked closely with Dr. Luo and Prof. PA Heng to develop an algorithm to perform myocardium segmentation for the purpose of myocardium iron loading.

416812.label: Project Title(Chinese)
416812.value: 泛凸和多目标约束优化的神经动力学方法

416812.label: Project Objectives
416812.value: In light of our recent findings, the first objective of the proposed research is to extend our newly developed neurodynamic approaches for minimizing pseudoconvex objective functions subject to linear equality and bound constraints to more generally constrained pseudoconvex optimization problems with convex inequality constraints. By means of coordinate transformation and further analysis, the expansion could be accomplished shortly after the project starts. In face of the challenging blockade toward nonconvexity, our second objective is to develop globally convergent neurodynamic systems for solving the most general class of constrained optimization problems with generalized-convex functions (called type-1 invex functions) in terms of the necessity and sufficiency of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker optimality conditions. Its breakthrough will widen the solvability scope of neurodynamic optimization to a new limit. In view of multiplicity in the reallity, our third objective is to develop globally convergent neurodynamic systems for multiple-objective optimization, by means of adaptive scalarization based on weight norms, goal programming, or multi-attribute value functions. Its success will open new doors to numerous applications. In realization of neurodynamic optimization with generalized-convex and multiple-objective functions in engineering, our fourth objective is to apply the conceived outcomes for nonlinear and robust model predictive control in several interested areas. In pursuit of computational methods for financial business intelligence, our fifth objective is to apply the proposed neurodynamic approaches to generalized-convex and multiple-objective optimization for dynamic portfolio selection in financial decision support.

416812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416812.value: Optimization is a ubiquitous phenomenon in nature and an important tool in science, engineering, and commerce. As the counterparts of biological neural systems, properly designed artificial neurodynamic systems can function as goal-seeking computational models for solving optimization problems in a variety of settings. For dynamic optimization in many real-time applications, such neurodynamic approaches are more competent than conventional optimization methods because of the inherently parallel and distributed nature of neural information processing. The past three decades witnessed the birth and growth of neurodynamic optimization with various globally convergent recurrent neural networks developed. Nevertheless, almost all existing results are concerned with convex optimization problems with single objective functions and effective neurodynamic approach to constrained optimization with nonconvex or multiple-objective functions is rarely available. In numerous applications, the objective functions to be minimized are not necessarily convex. The nonconvexity posts a great challenge for global optimization methods. In the presence of the challenge, a special class of nonconvex functions called generalized-convex functions are still widely available in many applications and neurodynamic approaches to generalized-convex optimization is viable. In addition to the problems with generalized convexity, multiple-objective optimization is another interesting and important issue. Because of the multiple-facet nature of reality, multiple-objective optimization is more realistic and practical. While population-based evolutionary approaches to nonconvex and multiple-objective optimization emerged as prevailing heuristic and stochastic methods in recent years, neurodynamic approaches deserve in-depth investigations in their own rights due to their close ties with optimization and dynamical systems theories, as well as their biological plausibility and circuit implementability. In this proposed research, we will develop neurodynamic approaches to constrained optimization in the presence of generalized convexity and multiplicity in objective functions. The research will consist of three coherent parts. In the first part, we will begin with designing neurodynamic models for constrained optimization with generalized-convex functions based on our newly developed neurodynamic models for pseudo-convex optimization. Since many generalized convex functions have convexity-like global properties, it is highly possible to expand existing results for pseudo-convex optimization to cover more generalized-convex problems. In the second part, we will focus on designing and analyzing neurodynamic models for multiple-objective optimization by means of adaptive scalarization. Finally, in the third part, the new results will be applied for intelligent control and dynamic portfolio optimization. It is expected that the accomplishments of the proposed project will significantly advance the frontiers of neurodynamic optimization research from both theoretical and practical points of view. 优化是一门应用十分广泛的学科，在科学研究、工程技术、商业应用中处处可见其用途。作为仿脑模型，人工神经动力学网络是一种有效的求解多种优化问题的工具。由于采取平行分布式的信息处理方法，神经动力学优化在处理对实时性要求较高的动态优化问题时，较之传统的数学优化算法具有独特的优势。 神经动力学优化在过去三十年取得了长足的发展和巨大的进步，多种具有全局收敛性的神经网络相继问世。但是值得指出的是，现有的结果一般只能处理单目标的凸优化问题。对于多目标或者非凸优化问题，仍然没有有效的神经动力学算法。 在大量的实际应用中，优化问题的目标函数并不是一个凸函数。目标函数的非凸性是寻找全局最优解的一个主要挑战和难点。广义凸函数一类特殊的拥有广泛应用背景的非凸函数，针对这类函数采用神经动力学优化算法是可行的。 此外，多目标优化也是一个非常重要有意义的题目。由于现实生活的多面性， 多目标优化具有重要的现实意义。尽管近年来以进化算法为基础的启发式和随机算法取得了较快的发展，神经动力学优化在处理多目标和非凸优化问题上仍具有特殊的优势：神经动力学和优化理论与动态系统紧密相关，神经动力学更符合生物学原理并易于用电路实现。对神经动力学优化的深入研究将有利于解决多目标和非凸优化问题。 本项目致力于研究针对多目标广义凸优化问题的神经动力学优化方法，总体上包括三个部分：第一，在之前成功求解伪凸优化的基础上，设计求解有约束广义凸优化问题的神经网络模型。由于大多数广义凸函数具有类凸性质，扩展现有的结果到广义凸优化问题是一个可行的方向。第二，我们将通过自适应标量化的方法分析并设计求解多目标优化问题的神经网络。第三，我们将应用新的神经动力学优化方法处理智能控制与动态投资组合优化等问题。 本项目的研究将会在理论和应用层面极大地促进神经动力学优化的发展，将神经动力学优化的研究推向新的高度。

416812.label: Major findings and research outcome
416812.value: Numerous results have been made in the project:. First, we developed neurodynamic optimization approaches, based on nonsmooth penalty functions, to generalized convex optimization including constrained pseudoconvex and invex optimization (Hosseini, Wang, and Hosseini, 2013;Li, Yan, and Wang 2014; Yan, Wang, and Li 2014; Liu, Huang, Wang, 2014; Liu and Wang 2015; Zhang, Xia, and Wang 2015; Xia and Wang 2016; ). Second, we developed multi-agent/multi-neurodynamic approaches to distributed optimization and minimax optimization, and analyzed the dynamic behaviors of multiple neural networks (Liu and Wang 2015; Guo, Yang, and Wang, 2016; Liu, Zeng, and Wang, 2017; Le and Wang, 2017; Yang, Liu, and Wang, 2017; Yang, Guo, Wang, 2017, Liu, Yang, Wang, 2017). Third, we also developed collaborative neurodynamic optimization approaches to constrained global optimization with nonconvex objective functions. By utilizing a team of neurodynamic optimization models initialized by using a particle swarm optimization algorithm, we would be able to solve constrained global optimization problems effectively and efficiently (Yan, Wang, and Li 2014; Yan, Fan, and Wang, 2017). Fourth, we developed collaborative neurodynamic optimization approaches to multiobjective optimization. By employing a team of neurodynamic optimization models, we would be able to solve constrained multi-objective optimization problems with Pareto-optimality and well balanced convergence and diversity along Pareto fronts (ICACI2016 and manuscripts to be published).. Fifth, we also explored neurodynamic optimization approaches to bilevel linear and quadratic programming and achieve initial successes (Qin, Le, and Wang 2017). In addition, we applied the developed neurodynamic optimization approaches for intelligent control such as robust pole assignment (Le and Wang 2014, 2015), nonlinear and robust model predictive control (Yan, Le, and Wang, 2016; Shen and Wang 2016), data processing such as nonnegative matrix factorization (Fan and Wang 2017), sparse signal processing (Liu and Wang, 2016), and financial engineering such as portfolio optimization (to be published).

416812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416812.value: There are substantial potentials for the further development of neurodynamic optimization. During this research, we reached the solvability limit of single neurodynamic model for optimization problems. We realized that it is necessary to employ a team of neurodynamic models to cooperative in some ways for solving complex optimization problems such as global and multi-objective optimization. The specific way of cooperation among multiple neural networks depends on the needs. For example, in distributed optimization the cooperation is in form of information exchanges or connectivity via coupling or impulsive interaction. For global optimization, it would be in form of information exchanges and re-initialization. By means of appropriate ways of cooperation, collaborative neurodynamic optimization would be able to achieve much successes. In view of the aforementioned potentials, our further investigations will aim at collaborative neurodynamic approaches to more challenging problems such as combinatorial optimization, machine learning, and their widespread applications.

416812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416812.value: As a brain-like computational paradigm, neurodynamic optimization has been shown to be capable of solving many optimization problems arising in numerous applications. This RGC funded project resulted in many publications that showcase the state of the art of neurodynamic optimization for solving various complex problems in science and engineering. The research findings include theoretical analysis of neurodynamics as well as the modeling and design of neurodynamic optimization models. The research findings also include many several specific applications of neurodynamic optimization in intelligent control, intelligent data and signal processing, and business intelligence. In addition, the research findings also motivated us to focus on our research on collaborative approaches to machine intelligence.

417012.label: Project Objectives
417012.value: To establish a solid theory interpreting the distinct growth behavior of graphene on different transition metals and to understand the influence of the following factors on graphene growth: the lattice mismatch between graphene and substrate materials, the formation of metal carbide, the carbon affinity and the catalytic activity of different transition metal materials. To identify optimized growth conditions, including the temperature, the size and shape of metal particle templates and the type of transition metal materials, to fabricate high-yield, high-quality curved graphene with controllable structures. To develop a complete methodology for fabrication of readily used and scalable curved graphene electrodes, including growth design for high yields, layer-number control, separation of graphene from metal particles and recycling of metal particles after graphene growth. To characterize the electronic, physical, and chemical properties of curved graphene and understand how they are different from flat graphene sheets. To fabricate curved graphene-based supercapacitors and characterize their performance.

417012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417012.value: The objective of this research is to develop a metal particle-templated growth technology for producing curved graphene in large scale and high quality, and to use the curved graphene as the electrode material in supercapacitors. Supercapacitors have the potential to replace batteries as the next generation energy storage device. However, current supercapacitor technology still lags behind batteries due to its limited energy density. One promising approach to address this problem is developing new electrode materials for supercapacitors. In this proposal we will focus on curved graphene, which possesses the superior properties of graphene such as large surface area, high conductivity and good porosity. More importantly, when used as the electrode material, curved graphene sheets will not re-stack together face-to-face and will keep a certain distance between the adjacent layers. Despite these advantages, utilization of curved graphene in devices has been challenging, due to the difficulty of constructing curved graphene sheets in large scale and high quality. In this project we propose to use nano- or micro-sized metal particles as the templates for growth of curved graphene by chemical vapor deposition (CVD). We will seek to understand the growth mechanism of graphene by exploring the lattice mismatch between graphene and substrate materials, the formation of metal carbide, the carbon affinity, and the catalytic activity of different transition metal materials. We will explore the specific effects of the type, size, and shape of transition metal particles, and other growth parameters. The work will be finalized with the actual implementation of the curved graphene into supercapacitor electrodes. Through this study, some long-unanswered, technical questions on the growth mechanism of graphene on metal surfaces/particles will be clarified, and this understanding will enable us to synthesize well-controlled curved graphene materials with high yield. Furthermore, detail atomic scale material characterization studies on their electronic, physical, and chemical properties will enlighten our understanding on carbon nano-materials, which will help extend their application. The proposed curved graphene electrodes will be ready to be implemented into various energy storage units, which will benefit next generation energy solutions, such as non-fossil-fuel based transportation vehicles and ultra high density energy storage for solar and wind plants. Moreover, the fundamental research carried in this project will benefit the realization of other applications of graphene, such as water deionization and filtration, chemical catalysis, sensors, and hydrogen/magnetic storage system. 本項目的目標是開發一個以金屬微顆粒為模板的、可大產量和高品質生長曲面石墨烯的工藝。製成的曲面石墨烯將用於超級電容器的電極材料。 超級電容器具有取代電池作為下一代能源存儲器件的潛力。然而，因為其有限的能量密度，目前的超級電容器技術仍然落後於電池。解決這個問題的一個有效辦法是開發新的超級電容器的電極材料。在這個項目中，我們將專注於開發曲面石墨烯。它具有石墨烯的各種優異的性能，如大表面積，高導電性以及良好的孔隙率。更重要的是，當作為電極材料時，曲面石墨烯的各片層不會面對面重組粘合，而是在相鄰層之間保持一定的距離。儘管有這些優點，在器件中利用曲面石墨烯仍具有挑戰性。這主要是由於現有工藝難以大產量和高品質生長曲面石墨烯。 在本項目中，我們提出以金屬微顆粒為模板、通過化學氣相沉積法（CVD）生長曲面石墨烯。將通過以下幾方面研究石墨烯的生產機制， 包括：石墨烯和基板材料的晶格失配，金屬碳化物的形成過程，碳的親和力，以及不同的過渡金屬材料的催化活性。更具體來說，我們將分別探討過渡金屬的種類、顆粒大小、形狀和其他生長參數的影響。項目的最後，我們將實際應用曲面石墨烯作為超級電容器的電極。 通過這項研究，一些長期未被解釋的、關於石墨烯在金屬及金屬顆粒表面生長機制的問題將得以解答。這將使我們能夠更好的、更高產量的控製曲面石墨烯材料合成。此外，通過在原子尺度上對石墨烯的電子，物理和化學性質進行研究，我們對碳納米材料的理解將會加深。這將有助於更廣泛的推廣這些材料的應用。 本項目研製的曲面石墨電極可被直接應用到各種能量存儲器件上， 從而幫助實現新一代的能源方案， 如非化石燃料為基礎的運輸車輛和配備超高密度能量儲存的太陽能和風力發電廠。此外，在這個項目中進行的基礎研究，也將有利於推廣石墨烯的其他應用，如水的去離子和過濾，化學催化，傳感器，以及儲氫/儲磁系統。

417112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417112.value: 謠言是在社會上傳播的令人懷疑的，通常情況下不真實的資訊。謠言的傳播往往會在受害團體中造成混亂。例如，某公司可以通過散佈對其競爭對手不利的謠言來損害其名譽。相似的情況在日常生活，例如，娛樂圈和政治圈中廣泛存在。謠言的傳播往往會讓受害者感到沮喪和無助。為儘早阻止對自身不利的謠言的傳播，很多公司或團體都加強了對謠言的監測工作，並盡可能在其廣泛傳播之前進行阻止。否則，謠言的傳播有可能失控並且最終造成不可估量的生命和財產損失。隨著資訊傳播技術的發展，尤其是社會化網路的發展，謠言的產生和傳播變得越來越簡單。因此，謠言的自動檢測與可信度排序被越來越多的研究者所關注。當前，謠言檢測的研究工作大多集中在微博平臺。作為社交網路的典型代表，微博是謠言傳播的有效的平臺之一。例如，埃及革命與英國騷亂。但是，傳統的基於話題檢測與跟蹤的方法在謠言監測上的效果並不理想，因為熱點話題僅僅是特定時間段內事件性資訊的描述。本文的觀點是，雖然謠言的產生屬於一次事件，但是公眾的評論，尤其是公眾的觀點對於謠言的傳播有重要影響。使用者觀點的權威與否對於謠言在社交網路上的傳播很重要。然而，現有的用戶權威度計算方法均未考慮觀點資訊。為解決該問題，本文提出了一種基於用戶觀點的謠言檢測與可信度排序方法。在謠言可信度排序的計算過程中，我們主要專注於以下特徵：(1) 基於觀點的用戶可信度；(2) 觀點的不確定度；(3) 觀點的矛盾度；(4) 觀點的影響力。謠言檢測與可信度排序是一個新的研究領域，而且，將用戶觀點引入到可信度計算中是一個全新的想法。此外，本文會為謠言檢測與可信度排序建立一個評測平臺，該平臺將對全世界研究者開放，這對於該課題的進一步國際化研究至關重要。謠言的自動檢測與可信度計算將為政府與公司及時發現公眾對於其政策、產品的觀點起到重要作用。

417112.label: Realisation of objectives
417112.value: Objective 1: Achieved. We collected a corpus of tweets data using the Twitter Streaming API for 8 weeks leading to the UK General Election in 2010. Search criteria specified include the mention of political parties such as Labour, Conservative, Tory, etc., the mention of candidates such as Brown, Cameron, Clegg, etc., the use of the hashtags such as #election2010, #Labour etc., and the use of certain words such as election. The corpus contains around 919,662 unique tweets and 68,620 users. We also collected the following links of all the users. According to the Twitter setting, data can only be revealed at most one-week quantity each time. Thus, data sample will be separated randomly into one-week sized in this case for afterward analysis in order to fit the circumstance, which data is extracted automatically in the future. Thus, the dataset for analysis contains around 44,391 unique tweets and 18,713 users. We have also done the clustering for the data before the annotation. There are 4 subgroups such as conservative party, labour party, liberal democrat party and others. For each subgroup, we have annotated user credibility in the subgroup manually and utilize the majority rule to identify the user credibility manually. The Kappa coefficient indicating inter-annotator agreement was 0.8236 for the binary classification. The conflict labels from the two annotators were resolved by a third annotator. Finally, there are 129 users annotated to be credible. Objective 2: Achieved. The corpus for rumor detection (download: http://alt.qcri.org/~wgao/data/rumdect.zip): we construct two microblog datasets using Twitter (www. twitter.com) and Sina Weibo (weibo.com). For the Twitter data, we confirmed rumors and non-rumors from www.snopes.com, an online rumor debunking service. We obtain 778 reported events during March-December 2015, of which 64% are rumors. For each event, we extract the keywords from the last part of the Snopes URL, e.g., http://www.snopes.com/pentagon-spends-powerballtickets. We refine the keywords by adding, deleting or replacing words manually, and iteratively until the composed queries can have reasonably precise Twitter search results. We use scripts to download the “Live” search results from Twitter. To balance the two classes, we further added some non-rumor events from two datasets published in (Castillo et al.: Information credibility on twitter) and (Kwon et al.: Prominent features of rumor propagation in online social media). The resulting dataset contains 498 rumors and 494 non-rumors. For Weibo data, we obtain a set of known rumors from the Sina community management center, which reports various misinformation. The Weibo API can capture the original messages and all their repost/reply messages given an event. We also gather a similar number of non-rumor events by crawling the posts of general threads that are not reported as rumors. The resulting dataset consists of 2,313 rumors and 2,351 non-rumors. Table 1 in (Ma et al. 2016) provides more details. The corpus for credibility ranking (download: http://www.hlt.utdallas.edu/~zywei/data/UncertaintyCorpus.zip): the dataset we annotated was collected from Twitter using Streaming API during summer riots in London during August 6-13 2011, including 326,747 tweets in total. Search criteria include hashtags like #ukriots, #londonriots, #prayforlondon, and so on. We further extracted the tweets relating to seven significant events during the riot identified by UK newspaper The Guardian from this set of tweets. We annotated all the 4,743 extracted tweets for the seven events . Two annotators were trained to annotate the dataset independently. Given a collection of tweets T = {t1, t2, t3, ..., tn}, the annotation task is to label each tweet ti as either uncertain or certain. Uncertainty assertions are to be identified in terms of the judgements about the author’s intended meaning rather than the presence of uncertain cue-phrase. For those tweets annotated as uncertain, sub-class labels are also required according to the classification indicated in Table 2 in (Wei et. al 2013) (i.e., multi-label is allowed). The Kappa coefficient indicating inter-annotator agreement was 0.9073 for the certain/uncertain binary classification and was 0.8271 for fine-grained annotation. The conflict labels from the two annotators were resolved by a third annotator. 926 out of 4,743 tweets are labeled as uncertain accounting for 19.52%. Objective 3: Achieved. We have 21 publications related to this project. Among them, we select the top 3 publications to briefly explain the achievements we made related to this objective: Wei et al. 2013: An Empirical Study on Uncertainty Identification in Social Media Context Ma et al. 2015: Detect Rumors Using Time Series of Social Context Information on Microblogging Websites Ma et al. 2016: Detecting Rumors from Microblogs with Recurrent Neural Networks Here is the summary: Wei et al. 2013: We propose a variant of classification scheme for uncertainty identification in social media and construct the first uncertainty corpus based on tweets. We perform uncertainty identification experiments on the generated dataset to explore the effectiveness of different types of features. Result shows that the three categories of social media specific features can improve uncertainty identification. Furthermore, content-based features bring the highest improvement among the three and the presence of uncertain cue-phrase contributes most for content-based features. Ma et al. 2015: We propose a novel time series model called Dynamic Series-Time Structure (DSTS) to capture the variation of a wide spectrum of social context information over time far more than the tweet volume feature. We study how well the time series of social context features can capture the variation of these features during the spread of event messages, which is supposed to bene- fit the differentiation between rumors and non-rumors. We utilize two datasets containing hundreds of events crawled from Twitter and Sina Weibo which are the most popular microblogging websites in English and Chinese, respectively. We build classifiers using the DSTS-based features and the annotated datasets. In our approach, we examine two basic settings: (1) given the complete lifecycle of an event about some specific topic, we decide it is a rumor or not; (2) given the event data at the early stage of propagation, we apply our model for early rumor detection. Ma et al. 2016: Utilizing RNN, we model the social context information of an event as a variable-length time series. We assume people, when exposed to a rumor claim, will forward the claim or comment on it, thus creating a continuous stream of posts. This approach learns both the temporal and textual representations from rumor posts under supervision. Objective 4: Achieved. The three aforementioned publications also evaluate and analysis the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for opinion-based user credibility ranking and rumor ranking. Here is the summary: Wei et al. 2013: The overall performance of uncertainty detection approaches is shown in Table 4. Ma et al. 2015: Table 3(a) and 3(b) show the comparison of the model using time series on social context information and different baselines. Ma et al. 2016: Table 2 shows the evaluation results of RNN-based model and different baselines. Please refer to the aforementioned papers for more details and dicusssion. Objective 5: Achieved. The three aforementioned publications detailed the design of an emergent rumor detection benchmark. Here is the summary: The task of rumor detection could be regarded as either a ranking problem or a classification problem. As a ranking problem, we use the evaluation metric widely accepted in information retrieval area, such as P@N, Pooling, bPref etc. As a classification problem, we use Precision, Recall and F-score to evaluate the performance of the proposed method.

417112.label: Major findings and research outcome
417112.value: Thanks to the support of RGC and this project, we explore many research problems related to rumor detection and credibility ranking on social media. At the start of this project, we conducted research on how to effectively measure credibility of users (Li et al.: Pests Hidden in Your Fans: An Effective Approach for Opinion Leader Discovery) and messages (Wei et al.: An Empirical Study on Uncertainty Identification in Social Media Context) based on our previous opinion mining research. Then we incorporated the aforementioned works to help detect rumors on microblog websites. Most of existing work for rumor detection focuses on modeling features related to microblog contents, users and propagation patterns, but ignore the importance of the variation of these social context features during the message propagation over time. Therefore, in (Ma et al.: Detect Rumors Using Time Series of Social Context Information on Microblogging Websites), we propose a novel approach to capture the temporal characteristics of these features based on the time series of rumor’s lifecycle, for which time series modeling technique is applied to incorporate various social context information. Then we argue that hand-crafted features for employing machine learning algorithms require daunting manual effort. Upon facing a dubious claim, people dispute its truthfulness by posting various cues over time, which generates long-distance dependencies of evidence. We hence present a work (Ma et al.: Detecting Rumors from Microblogs with Recurrent Neural Networks) with a novel method that learns continuous representations of microblog events for identifying rumors. The proposed model is based on recurrent neural networks (RNN) for learning the hidden representations that capture the variation of contextual information of relevant posts over time. Since rumor events can be described by large volume of microblog messages, which makes it difficult to understand the key information behind these messages. Therefore, we also study microblog summarization, which aims to identify salient excerpts from the target microblog messages and represent them in a succinct form for easy reading. Traditional summarizers rely heavily of text signal, which is ineffective facing short and informal microblog messages. Therefore, we organize microblog messages as repost trees based on reposting/replying relations and differentiate messages as leaders and followers. Through experiments, we demonstrate that conversation structures indeed helps identify key information and useful to summarization (Li et al.: Using Content-level Structures for Summarizing Microblog Repost Trees; Li et al.: Topic Extraction from Microblog Posts Using Conversation Structures).

417112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
417112.value: This project aims at identifying whether a microblog is a potential rumor based on the comments written by the viewers of that particular microblog. Yet, it did not attempt to detect whether a rumor is a false rumor. Latest research indicated that automatically false rumor detection is a crucial issue to maintain a health Internet economy. Therefore, in the next step, we attempts to propose effective models that can automatically detect false rumors. Another extension is to build a high-level model trying to understand the language components (both semantic and syntactic) and information diffusion patterns of rumors. Most of the works identify rumors and determine credibility based on a set of handcrafted features. In the last stage of this project, we presented a pilot study of using a basic deep learning model, instead of handcrafted features/rules, to identify rumors, which is proven to be effective. Based on this work, we propose to present a deep learning model that can capture richer information and relies on two elements: (1) latent semantic and syntactic structures (LSS), and (2) information diffusion topology (IDT). We’ve submitted a GRF proposal this year regarding the aforementioned ideas, which covers detailed description and discussion.

417112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
417112.value: Rumors are skeptical and sometimes untrue messages that widely propagate in a society. This may lead to chaos in the community involved. To reduce the unforeseeable damages from rumors, companies and governments try very hard to stop rumors spreading as early as possible; otherwise, the rumors may become unmanageable and eventually lead to unrecoverable damage and lost. Due to the advancement of Information and Communication Technologies, creation and spreading of rumors on the Internet is extremely easy. Manually identify rumors from the Internet is very inefficient, which will lead to very high cost and long debunking delay. In this project, we present an effective system that can automatically detect rumors in a relatively early stage. It is especially useful for governments and corporations to detect and track rumors against their policies and products on the Internet. Noticeably, one of the biggest contributions of this work is the open corpus for emergent rumor detection that we compiled and publicized. Since data collection and annotation works are the biggest challenges for microblog websites, the corpuses that we compiled, being the first of its kind, provide a big convenience for future research.

417612.value: 用于模拟高速互联封装问题的全波频域部分元等效电路及其物理降阶理论

417612.label: Project Objectives
417612.value: Developing a full wave frequency domain PEEC model for effective EM modeling of electronic interconnection and packaging structures by incorporating the significant electric properties, such as retardation and radiation effects; specifically, the emphasis will be placed on the general treatment for multilayered circuits. Developing a totally matrix-inversionless generalized Derived Physically Expressive Circuit (DPEC) model for a frequency-independent physics-based model order reduction (PMOR) with guaranteed passivity. The most distinct advancement of this PMOR scheme over the existing DPEC is that there is no any matrix inversion required in both the PEEC model and the PMOR scheme while providing even more clear physical sense in the resultant circuit model. Developing a frequency-dependent PMOR scheme that automatically converts a physical interconnection and packaging structure into a physically meaningful order-reduced circuit model with frequency variant circuit elements; special attentions will be paid to the stopping criterion of the recursive iteration process for a frequency-dependent PMOR in terms of system poles of the resultant circuit model during the DPEC process.

417612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417612.value: As the data rate increases to multi-gigabits per second in digital communication systems, the large-signal deterministic parameters of interconnects and packages, such as timing-jitter and inter-symbol interference, and signal integrity problems become more and more critical to designers. In order to optimize electronic interconnect and package designs, developing an effective analysis approach that can present clear physical sense of the problem becomes ever important for an electronic design industry. Considering the complexity of the interconnection and packaging problem, not only in terms of geometric attributes but also the large number of variables, and the compatibility of a physical model, nonlinear devices and lumped element circuits in a SPICE-like solver, a promising modeling approach must be electromagnetic (EM) based, computationally efficient, as concise as specified with necessary physical essences, and SPICE solver compatible. Developing such a modeling scheme is the main objective of this proposed research. Three major objectives in the project are (1) developing a full-wave frequency domain partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) model for accurate modeling of the retardation and radiation effects; (2) introducing a new frequency domain concise representation of PEEC model that presents clear physical sense and does not require any matrix inversion; (3) developing a frequency-dependent derived physically expressive circuit (DPEC) scheme with effective stopping criterion for a physically sensible circuit model. The proposed frequency-dependent DPEC will be based on a generic node reduction scheme that directly absorbs mutual inductive and capacitive couplings. Such model order reduction scheme will be mathematically systematic and computationally efficient. More importantly, the scheme builds-in with clear physical sense. Since there is no need for matrix inversions, the new DPEC model will be very useful for analyzing a very large scale problem in time domain. The proposed research will be build on top of the DPEC model that was developed by PI’s group in recent years. The impact of the outcomes will be significant to the electronic industry and EDA industry in two aspects: (1) the new DPEC contains full-wave information and is applicable to time domain analysis; and (2) it is highly efficient for very large scale problems as there is no matrix inversion involved. 随着数字通信系统中数据速率增长至每秒数吉比特，通过互联与封装结构的大信号确定性参数，例如定时抖动和码间干扰，以及信号完整性问题对于设计者来说变得越来越关键。为了优化电子互联与封装设计，开发一个能够提供明确的物理意义的有效分析方法对于电子设计产业变得尤为重要。 考虑互联与封装问题的复杂性问题，不仅有几何特征的参数，而且有众多的变量，以及在SPICE类中的物理模型，非线性器件和集总参数电路的兼容性。一个有前景的建模方法一定是基于电磁场的，高效计算的，能够简洁明确反映必要的物理本质，并且具有SPICE兼容性。开发这样一个建模方法是本研究的主要目标。 在本研究项目中有三个主要目标，（1）为了精确描述延迟和辐射效应，建立一个全波频域部分参数等效电路（PEEC）模型；（2）引入一个新的频域PEEC模型简洁表达方式，其不仅能够表达明确的物理意义并且推导过程不需要任何矩阵求逆；（3）建立一个频变的派生物理表达电路（DPEC）方法，其有物理内涵电路模型的推导过程将具有有效的收敛准则。 所提出的频变DPEC将基于能够直接吸收互电感互电容耦合元件的广义节点消除法。这样的模型降阶方法将会具有数学的系统性和计算的有效性。更重要的是，该方法建立在具有明确物理意义之上。既然不需要矩阵求逆，新的DPEC模型将会对时域分析超大规模的问题非常有用。 本研究将建立在近年来由本研究小组创立DPEC理论之上。预期的成果将会对电子产业和计算机辅助分析设计产业的两个方面产生重要的影响：（1）新的DPEC将包括全波信息并且适用于时域分析；（2）由于不需要矩阵求逆，该成果对分析超大规模问题将十分有效。

417612.label: Realisation of objectives
417612.value: The goal set in objective 1 has been achieved. A generalized PEEC model that accurately incorporate radiation effects is proposed by an IEEE transaction paper. The extension of this full wave PEEC model to microstrip case has also been proposed and published in an IEEE transaction paper. This foundation work paves a way for developing an effective EM modeling approach of electronic interconnection and packaging structures using a full-wave circuit model. Objective 2 has been successfully achieved. In this task, a totally matrix-free generalized Derived Physically Expressive Circuit (DPEC) model for a frequency-independent physics-based model order reduction (PMOR) is developed with guaranteed passivity. This work will be published in IEEE Transactions on MTT. Since this approach only involves simple vector outer-product operation, it can reduce the computational workload from O(n3) to O(n) simply by using the GPU acceleration technique. Therefore, the new technique will be very useful for analyzing a very large scale interconnection and packaging problem in both frequency and time domains as one order of magnitude reduction in problem size will result in three orders of magnitude reduction in computing time. This method can be widely used for analyzing S-parameters, time-domain responses, eye-diagrams of various high density interconnection and packaging problems in high speed and high frequency electronic circuits and systems. To achieve the goal set in objective 3, the developed matrix-free DPEC model has been further extended to frequency-dependent problems, such as radiation mechanism of an antenna. With this full-wave DPEC model, a map of the power dissipation on radiation resistive network can be obtained. This map, for the first time, reveals a holography of radiated power by an antenna. This work has been first announced in an invited talk in an international conference in May 2016.

417612.label: Major findings and research outcome
417612.value: In this research project, a brand new physics-based model order reduction (MOR) technique for electromagnetic (EM) modeling of a large-scale electronic interconnection and packaging problem is developed. The method starts from mixed potential integral equation and the well-known Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) model. To prepare for more challenging problems, a few of significant enhancements in PEEC have been done by PI, which include the extension to a general radiation problem and a general meshing scheme for PEEC modeling using mixed triangular and rectangular meshes. The PEEC model allows people to deal with an EM field problem in the circuit domain although the scale of the circuit scale is prohibitively large for any practical application. A new generalized equivalent circuit transformation is proposed by inspiration of the fact that for different mesh variation on a conducting surface the current continuity will be always retained. The new circuit transformation can preserve not only the external I-V characteristics but also all inductive and capacitive mutual coupling. By applying the transformation and the legitimate “lowpass approximation” to all the insignificant internal nodes one by one, the contribution of those insignificant internal nodes is “absorbed” by other significant nodes physically. This absorbing process directly deal with the inductive couplings and coefficients of potential, no any matrix operations are involved. This matrix-free nature completely eliminates the instability and ill-condition issues that faced to all the existing MOR techniques. Additionally, the order-reduced circuit that has a clear correspondence with the physical layout, can not only provide a physical insight but can also reduce the order of the original PEEC model by at least one order of magnitude. It can be shown that passivity of the order reduced circuit model can be well preserved if the lowpass approximation is well controlled. Since this approach only involves simple vector outer-product operation, it can reduce the computational workload from O(n3) to O(n) simply by using the GPU acceleration technique. Therefore, the new technique will be very useful for analyzing a very large scale interconnection and packaging problem in both frequency and time domains as one order of magnitude reduction in problem size will result in three orders of magnitude reduction in computing time. This method can be widely used for analyzing S-parameters, time-domain responses, eye-diagrams of various high density interconnection and packaging problems in high speed and high frequency electronic circuits and systems.

417612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
417612.value: There are three areas that is worthwhile for further investigation: (1) The full-wave version of the developed approach has been applied to radiation problems of antennas successfully. The method enables a systematic derivation of a physically meaningful circuit model of an antenna. By solving the circuit model, the power dissipated on radiation resistive network, either positive or negative, reveals a holography of radiated power by the antenna. This ability of the circuit model for an antenna paves a unique way in antenna research for developing high efficient antennas and a new way to study the radiation phenomena in an EMC problem. (2) It has been shown in the research outcomes that the computational workload in the developed method mainly on the computation of the out-product of a large vector. Therefore, how to efficiently calculate the out-product using the GPU acceleration technique is worthwhile to investigate. (3) More advanced PEEC model that involves inhomogeneous dielectrics is under development. With this advanced model, the extension of the MOR approach developed in this research to include inhomogeneous dielectrics in the EM problem is important to many practical engineering problems.

417612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
417612.value: In this project, a brand new computational technique for accelerating electromagnetic modeling of a large-scale problem is developed. The technique can effectively reduce the scale of a well-known Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) model by at least one order of magnitude. Additionally, the order-reduced circuit retains a clear correspondence with the physical layout of the original EM problem, providing a physical insight. The core of the technique is a new equivalent circuit transformation. By applying the transformation and a legitimate “lowpass approximation” to all the insignificant internal nodes one by one, the contribution of the nodes is “absorbed” by other significant nodes without requiring any matrix operations. Therefore, it completely eliminates the instability and ill-condition issues that faced to all the existing model order reduction techniques. The new method speeds up the computation by three orders of magnitude or five orders of magnitude if GPU acceleration technique is used. This method can be widely used for analyzing S-parameters, time-domain responses, eye-diagrams of various large scale interconnection and packaging problems in high speed and high frequency electronic circuits and systems.

417812.label: Project Objectives
417812.value: Optimization of the fastening mechanism: The current fastening mechanism has only 4 contact points to the fastening substrate. The fastening force is only enough for miniature robot. To extend the use of the mechanism to a larger scale of the robot, or capable of equipping heavier objects, the mechanism has to be improved so as to generated larger fastening force in different directions such as twisting. This fastening mechanism can apply on other fields such as rock climbing, or even on a planet in near-zero gravity to make robot and astronaut fasten on a ground. Dynamic analysis and optimization of the continuum mechanism: The continuum mechanism has high degrees of freedom. One of the excellent features of the continuum mechanism is that it has a certain level of compliance so as to adapt to unstructured environment. However, the compliance is also a drawback in view of position control. In order to improve the positioning accuracy (especially useful for motion planning in autonomous control), the deflection of the continuum mechanism due to the known external force (such as gravity) must be obtained. The modeling also beneficial of selecting the optimal parameters of the setting of the mechanism such as the spring constant and the power of motors so as to fit for different application. Autonomous navigation on unstructured trees: It is aimed to make Treebot capable of navigate on trees autonomously, If the surface map of tree is obtained. We will address the challenge on how the robot can understand the ungraspable location on the surface of the tree. Thereafter, we will develop the autonomous navigation approach for the robot.

417812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417812.value: Automatic monitoring for tree health and forest is a significant issue in many regions in the world. A robot with tree climbing ability should be developed to assist or replace human’s work. Climbing on a tree with irregular shape is a challenging task as the climbing motion and adhesion method need to adapt to a complex and irregular surface. To climb on irregular shape of trees, this project will mainly focus on the three aspects: 1) optimization of the fastening mechanism; 2) dynamic analysis and optimization of the continuum mechanism; 3) autonomous navigation on unstructured trees. It will provide theoretical approaches to analyze and optimize the gripper design for irregular surface climbing, to optimize the continuum mechanism design, and to generate map and navigate in the irregular 3D tree surfaces. The work is of significance not only to the design of autonomous tree climbing robot devices, but also to the development of the fundamental science and technology in grasping and navigation on trees with various parameters and geometry.

417812.label: Realisation of objectives
417812.value: The projects aims to achieve three objectives which are shown as follows. 1. Optimization of the fastening mechanism Gripping and releasing are the basic tasks involved in climbing. The most significant problem of a Treebot is that occasionally, the gripping spines can be stuck on a tree’s surface. As for the Treebot, the spine insertion and withdrawal directions are the same, we focus on the results from the experiments with the same insertion and withdrawal angles. When spines are inserted into a substrate, adhesion forces are generated to fix the robot to the surface. Penetration produces an adhesion force, because of the elasticity of wood. Most barks are soft enough to be penetrated, and the adhesion force is generated by the pressure of the deformation of wood in the penetrated hole. Only penetration can produce the resistant force of withdrawal. We studied the shapes of the tips (i.e. tapered tip with 30-degree cone angle, and a smooth tip.), the inserting force and adhesion force, and the different trunks (i.e., Roystonea regia, and Ficus altissima). Through experiments, we investigated the adhesion forces and find out that: (1) The smooth tip produces larger adhesion forces for equivalent insertion forces than are obtained using the tapered tip. (2) Spine diameter is not a significant factor influencing adhesion. (3) Softer bark also allows larger adhesion forces to generate from equivalent insertion forces. Based on that, we extracted out the threshold curve for the withdrawal force in terms of insertion force. Thereafter, the gripping claws are modelled mathematically to study the specification of linear motor as actuator. It is found that torque limit of the currently available motor in market can be overcome. Hence, we designed spines which can be retractable from penetration. Three aspects are considered in the design: (1) The structure should be light-weight and compact, so that it does not affect Treebot’s locomotion. (2) While the spine is pushed out, the structure should support enough force to prevent the spine from moving back. (3) The force required to pull back the spine should be small. The structure of the retractable spine consists of a frame, a leaf spring, a spring, and a support to hold the spine in place. The leaf spring, as the core component in the retractable spine, has been optimized based on FEA. A chamfer is added at the middle of the leaf spring. While the height of the leaf spring is constant, the angle of the chamfer has a significant influence on the transformation. We studied angles of 0◦, 30◦, 45◦ and 60◦, and found out that a chamfer angle of 60◦ provides the best results , obtaining the largest deformation of the leaf spring for the same pulling force. This design increases the retraction force significantly to 3.5 times. The simulation seems promising, but the realization is really difficult, as the requirement on thin-but-rigid structure of the leaf spring. Hence, another gripper structure has been designed to overcome the problem. It is based on the slider-crank mechanism. The crank fastened to a thin steel string can drive the slider to retract the spine back to the claw. The crank is preset to the dead point by the torsional spring. When a pulling force about 4N is exerted at the string, the spine is retracted. We carried out ADMAS simulation thereafter, following the steps of modeling, adding constraint, exerting load, generating dynamic equations, solution for time and step length, etc. Based on simulation, this mechanism has the benefit of force-saving. Based on the developed prototype and experiment, considering the effect of friction forces in joints, the force to retract spine is 7 N. 2. Dynamic analysis and optimization of the continuum mechanism To analyze the dynamics of the continuum mechanism, there are a number of control, sensation, actuation, energy management, communication and subsystems to integrate into the previous version. (1) We further developed the control system based on a 2-level architecture: STM32 in the lower controller for energy monitoring, obstacle detection and response, and so on; RaspberryPi as the higher one dealing with computer vision, attitude etc. (2) The sensation system include infrared and ultrasonic (to detect the obstacles and wheter the grasping will be safe), vision (to detect the color based path), and IMU (to detect the attitude of head and tail). (3) Energy management subsystem is designed to measure the energy remained in the battery. (4) Actuation subsystem consists of 3 DC bridge circuit, and can realize speed-loop PI control as well as position-loop PID control, so as to tune the continuum body motion speed and body length. (5) The communication subsystem mainly utilize IIC for data sharing among RaspberryPi, STM32, IMU and actuation subsystems. During the experiment, we discovered that the variation of the center of gravity when the front gripper is in motion will have a negative effect on the grasping of the rear gripper. To tackle this problem, reference from birds can be taken, especially the woodpecker which utilizes its tail attaching to trees to maintain the appropriate attitude. Hence, we improved the design by adding an artificial tail to the rear gripper, and validated the effect by experiment. Central pattern generator (CPG) based control has been studied for dynamics of the Treebot. It is a rhythmical motion generator existing in most animals. Compared with the open-loop control of the three motors in the continuum body, close-loop control can further coordinate the independent drives and thus can control the positions of the continuum body better. 3. Autonomous navigation on unstructured trees To navigate the robot from the tree, we explored both mono-camera and RGB-D camera. Mono-camera is light-weighted, and thus can be mounted to the front gripper. Currently, it is still difficult to extract out the tree center line precisely, so we resemble it by a color strip fixed on the tree surface. The strip’s position in image is extracted out as an offset error, which is thereafter fed as an error into the PD controller to correct the position of the front gripper. Motion planning based on the past Treebot’s research are carried out in the improved Treebot version. Autonomous climbing on a straight tree has validated the research. But on trees with bifurcation, there turn out to be some occasions that the claws have instable grasping, 23 out 30 are successful, while 7 occasions fail. We have also been exploring the RGB-D camera for autonomous climbing. Due to its relatively heavy weight, it is not capable to amount onto the Treebot, but can only be employed as the external sensor. During this project we are able to extract out the tree trunk shape for future investigation. We have well addressed all the three objectives. Some of the results had been published in journal or conference papers, and some manuscripts are under preparation and will be submitted when they are ready. In addition, one PhD student were partially supported by this project.

417812.label: Major findings and research outcome
417812.value: The major findings of this project are summaried below from three aspects. 1. Optimization of the fastening mechanism Preventing spines from being stuck into the tree is important and consequently can help to increase the fastening force towards trees as it prevents from sudden uncontrollable force when ungrasping the tree surface. We have studied the design of retractable spines, and found out the effect of shape, diameter and bark characteristics on the adhesion forces. A leaf spring based design has also been investigated, though it is challenging to fabricate. Another crank-slider based design has been realized thereafter, and a prototype robot can be fixed to tree satisfactorily. Part of the results have been published in the conference proceeding (ICRA2014) paper, entitled "Design and Analysis of Gripper with Retractable Spine for Tree Climbing Robots", and part of the results are under preparation for a journal paper, entitled "Improved Design of a Tree Climbing Robot with Retractable Spine." 2. Dynamic analysis and optimization of the continuum mechanism To study the dynamics of the robot, we further improved the previous Treebot with more sensors, more powerful controllers and actuators, as well as communication channels with faster data exchange. To carry out the experiment, bio-mimic tail has been added to the rear gripper, and this optimization can reduce the probability of falling from tree surface. CPG based control is investigated, and close-loop control of the three tendons in the continuum body has been realized to control the position of the gripper better. Part of the research outcome will be published in a journal, with the paper title of "System and Autonomous Climbing of a Biomimetic Tree Climbing Robot". 3. Autonomous navigation on unstructured trees Both mono camera and RGB-D camera are investigated as the sensor for autonomous navigation. Based on mono camera, relative position of the robot with respective to the tree is detected, and the error off-set towards the trunk centerline is fed to the controller. PD based autonomous navigation on the straight tree has been investigated and experiment validates this methodology. RGB-D camera based external vision has been partially studied, and the tree trunk can be geometrically modelled as a cylinder. A journal paper is under preparation, entitled "Tree Modeling Based on a RGB-D Camera". In summary, the project has led to two journal papers, and five conference proceedings. Three manuscripts are still under preparation. Mainly due to the change of the PIs (twice during the project period), it actually took more time for the previous two PIs, the current PI and their teams to conduct the corresponding research, and to achieve the research outcome. We will speed up to publish that three manuscripts when they are ready.

417812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
417812.value: One main effort of this project is to enlarge the payload of the Treebot by increasing the dimension of the robot. One direction, in contrast, is to reduce the size. Spine array has the merit of multiple sharp contact points, and has been validated for rock climbing palm. Tree surfaces, which have more sophisticated curved areas, will place challenges in the mechanism design to fit the grasping locations. Miniaturization of the grasping tools will enable for more grippers than two. This will allow for chained systems providing large payload/mass ratio. Another direction for further research is to work on SLAM on the 2D manifold. Sensory input, such as laser, mono camera, multiple camera, infrared, and so on, can be studied for their pros and cons. Multi-modal sensor fusion is another topic if all single sensors fails to establish the accurate map. The third potential direction is to investigate a more precise kinematic model of Treebot. Currently, the curvature based model is an approximation, without consideration on gravity, attitude of the fixed gripper, payload, etc. With IMU on both the front and rear grippers, and encoder readings on the 3 tendons, we can firstly localize both the two grippers and their attitude by motion capturing equipment, and thereafter, it is promising to extract out a more accurate kinematic model based on parameter learning.

417812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
417812.value: Tree climbing is challenging but practically very useful. In fact, various dangerous tasks for humans, such as branch pruning, environmental monitoring, and so on, can be done by robots. However, the requirement for grasping and the complex surface topography for climbing makes the robot difficult to perform satisfactorily. This project extended our previous research on a biomimetic tree climbing robot in mainly three aspects. (1) Optimization of the fastening mechanism. The new design prevents the spines of the Treebot from stuck into the tree barks, by extracting out the spines. The new design based on crank-slider mechanism shows good performance. (2) Dynamic analysis and optimization of the continuum mechanism. Multiple sensors are integrated, together with a biomimetic tail to support the rear gripper better. Another biomimetic control strategy, i.e. CPG based control, was also investigated to improve the control performance of the Treebot. (3) Autonomous navigation on unstructured trees. Mono-camera plus color-strip enables Treebot for autonomously climbing straight trunk. RGB-D camera can model the tree trunk as a cylinder for future tree map building. The research based on this GRF project has opened a door to the field robotics in forest, and more robotics related research and development are foreseen.
