418112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418112.value: Conventional circuit design and optimization techniques guarantee that all circuit paths meet their timing requirements in all conditions to ensure error-free computing. Such worst-case design methodology, however, may lead to very pessimistic designs because a large design guardband needs to be incorporated to prevent any timing failure. Recently, timing speculation (TS) techniques were proposed to address this problem, wherein we can over-clock the chip and/or reduce the supply voltage of the chip to a point that timing errors occur and then perform error recovery to achieve resilient computing. Such better-than-worst-case design methodology promises great improvement in the energy-efficiency of computation and hence has attracted a lot of research interests from both academia and industry. Since timing error recovery incurs some performance loss and extra energy consumption, it is essential to reduce timing error rate to optimize timing speculated circuits. Most existing TS techniques target on the gate-level implementation of the circuit from the traditional worst-case design flow and try to speed up those frequently-exercised critical paths in the circuit (with possible slower infrequently-exercised paths), using techniques such as gate resizing, body biasing, and selective dual-threshold logic cell assignment. Consequently, the effectiveness of such post-processing techniques relies on the given architecture design and logic structure of the circuit. In addition, while dynamic voltage/frequency tuning can be employed to improve energy efficiency of timing speculated circuits, it is usually applied to the entire circuit and such coarse-grained solution is less resistant to the ever-increasing process variation effects. Motivated by the above, this project investigates novel logic synthesis solutions and architecture designs for timing speculation, which tries to generate optimized timing speculated circuits from the ground up. Moreover, we consider adding fine-grained online tuning flexibility for timing speculated circuits, wherein timing error information for individual chips are collected online and used for chip-specific TS optimization by on-the-fly clock skew and/or voltage tuning. Finally, volume production of timing speculated circuits can only be practiced when there exists an efficient and effective testing methodology for them, which will be also investigated in this project. 為了確保計算結果的正確性，傳統的電路設計和優化技術需要保證所有的電路路徑在任何可能情況下都滿足時序要求。因此，設計中通常需要加入較大的時序冗餘，浪費了電路的性能或增加了它的功耗。最近，學界提出時序前瞻（timing speculation）技術來解決該問題。與傳統設計理念不同，這種設計允許電路中出現定時錯誤（timing error），然後通過在綫糾錯來保證計算結果的正確性。因此，我們可以讓具備時序前瞻能力的電路工作在它的性能和功耗邊界，大大提高計算的能源效率。 與此同時，由於對定時錯誤進行糾錯必然會帶來一些性能損失以及額外的能耗，我們需要優化設計來降低定時錯誤率。當前的設計通常從傳統電路設計結果出發，通過門級電路優化手段來減少電路中敏化率較高的關鍵路徑延遲以達到上述目的。常用的手段包括調整門尺寸、使用門偏壓、以及選擇性的使用雙閾值邏輯單元等方法。這種後處理手段的有效性依賴於給定的體系結構設計和電路的邏輯結構。此外，盡管我們可以採用動態電壓/頻率調整來在綫提高電路的計算效率，通常而言這種手段是施加到整個電路，而由於電路制程變異的日益增大，這種粗粒度的調整效果變得有限。 出於以上考慮，本項目針對具備時序前瞻能力的電路進行全新的邏輯綜合以及架構設計，試圖從頭開始來解決該類電路的設計與優化問題。此外，我們還提出通過時鐘相位以及電壓島等細粒度的在綫調整方式來提高該類電路的計算效率。最後，由於此類電路允許定時錯誤的出現，我們無法使用現有的生產測試手段來檢測由製造引起的電路延時缺陷。我們也會在本項目針對該問題提出有效的測試方法，以利於此類電路的大規模生產。

418112.label: Realisation of objectives
418112.value: We have realized the project objectives in the following aspects. We have proposed a novel in-situ timing error masking technique namely InTimeFix and a novel forward timing error correction technique namely ForTER. With InTimeFix, we introduce fine-grained redundant approximation circuit into the design to provide more timing slack for speed-paths. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed solution can effectively increase circuit timing slack with very low cost. In addition, as a redundancy scheme, InTimeFix can be combined with other timing optimization techniques (e.g., gate sizing) to further improve circuit performance under variation. With ForTER, we predict whether the occurrence of timing errors would propagate to the next level of sequential elements and corrects them without necessarily borrowing timing slack. The two proposed technique can be combined with each other to further improve circuit performance. Moreover, the synthesis for these two solutions require simple structural analysis of the original circuit, which is easily scalable to large IC designs and can be tuned for chip-specific optimization. Not all timing errors are unacceptable. In fact, a large and growing number of applications are inherently error-tolerant, which do not require “strict” correctness but rather approximate correctness. Applications of such kind include multimedia, DSP, wireless communication, data mining and synthesis. We have developed a number of approximate computing techniques at various computing layers to tradeoff computation quality (e.g., accuracy) and computational effort (e.g., energy), by exploiting the inherent error-resilience of many applications. To be specific, we proposed a reconfiguration-oriented design methodology for approximate circuits, and proposed a reconfigurable approximate adder design that degrades computation quality gracefully. The proposed design methodology enables us to achieve better quality-effort tradeoff when compared to existing techniques, as demonstrated in the application of DCT computing. We have also proposed a novel approximate computing framework for iterative methods with quality guarantees, namely ApproxIt, which is able to capture the solution quality of each iteration and use it to guide the selection of approximate computing mode in the next iteration. With the proposed dynamic effort scaling technique, ApproxIt is able to dramatically improve application energy efficiency under quality guarantees. Artificial neural networks are state-of-the-art machine learning techniques for a wide range of applications. We propose a novel technique namely ApproxANN, which approximates the computation and memory accesses of certain less critical neurons based the criticality analysis to obtain energy efficiency under quality constraint. With the proposed solution, ApproxANN achieves 34.11% ∼ 51.72% energy benefit with less than 5% quality loss for various neural network applications used in our experiments. We have also proposed a novel approximate computing technique for large-scale eigen-decomposition, namely ApproxEigen, wherein we focus on the practically-used Krylov subspace methods to find finite number of eigenpairs. With ApproxEigen, we provide a set of computation kernels with different levels of approximation for data pre-processing and solution finding, and conduct accuracy tuning under given quality constraints. To effectively and efficiently manage the quality for approximate computing, we synergistically combine the outputs of several basic light-weight predictors to obtain more accurate predictions. Our solution can achieve 11% to 23% more energy gains under the given target quality requirement, when compared to the state-of-the-art techniques. Finally, without developing efficient and effective test methods for timing-speculative circuits, it is impossible to push forward for volume production. The major difficulty in dealing with timing-speculative circuit testing comes from the fact that the timing behavior of such circuits is non-deterministic. In this project, for the first time, novel test solutions were proposed to address the above problem. With the proposed test flow and the novel test pattern generation techniques, we are able to achieve high fault coverage for timing-speculative circuits without incurring high high design-for-testability cost.

418112.label: Major findings and research outcome
418112.value: As shown in Part C, this project has generated nine high-quality papers, including three papers presented at Design Automation Conference and three papers presented at International Conference on Computer-Aided Design. These two conferences are flagship conferences in the electronic design automation domain with acceptance ratio around 20%. The major findings of this project include novel timing-speculative circuit design methodology that achieve significant improvement in circuit performance, novel approximate design at all computing layers that provide much better tradeoff between computation quality and computational effort, and novel testing solutions for timing-speculative circuits.

418112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418112.value: We plan to further extend the project to combine "computing with memory" technique with approximate computing, which stores a subset of function responses in a lookup table (LUT), and avoids redundant computation when encountering similar input patterns. We expect such combination to provide much better energy-efficiency when compared to state-of-the-art solutions.

418112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418112.value: Conventional circuit design and optimization techniques require error-free computing, which generally lead to very pessimistic designs because a large design guardband needs to be incorporated to prevent any failure. In this project, we investigate timing speculation (TS) techniques to greatly improve computing energy-efficiency. Various techniques at all computing layers were presented to achieve the above objective, including novel circuit design techniques to mitigate timing errors, novel approximation solutions for various applications from simple adders to complex neural network designs. With the successful completion of this project, significant energy reduction can be achieved without sacrificing much computation quality.

418212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418212.value: 由於近年計算機技術的進步和巨大計算能力的普及，計算方法已成為控制工程師解決難於得到解析解問題的切實可行選擇。一個重要的例子是著名的線性矩陣不等式（LMIs）的設計。在該問題中，控制問題被轉化成凸優化形式，並使用確定的全局解得以解決。現在如果一個控制問題可以轉化成LMI形式，那它就是實際可解的。 為此，本研究員及其合作者提出了一個基於計算的方法為準線性變參數（qLPV）系統設計控制器。該方法需要在數值上將給定的qLPV模型轉化成凸張量積（TP）多面體形式，並通過LMIs引入預期的設計目標來設計控制器。凸TP形式可通過使用高維奇異值分解技術來實現。而含數值轉換所需算法並確保LMI設計的TP MATLAB工具箱包也已經被開發出來。值得指出的是，qLPV模型已被廣泛使用於需要廣闊的性能包絡的汽車和航空航天控制的應用中。 我們之前的方法已被成功用於許多應用中。然而，該方法要求控制器必須與qLPV模型含有一樣的TP結構。雖然這有利於實現基於LMI的設計的便利應用，它也限制了設計的靈活性。很多時候，為了得到一個可行解，大量注意力被投注到凸包的成形即TP結構的權重函數張成的空間。即使得到一個可行解，其可能達到的性能在也一定程度上被限制了。與此同時，我們還發現了許多除了模型的TP結構以外的可行的控制器的設計案例。 本項目旨在克服上述限制，並且開發我們的計算方法的框架結構，使之能適用於更廣泛的可行控制器的設計。在可變域內對qLPV模型進行採樣之後，我們立即為系統的離散模型加入了一個新的控制器設計步驟。於是，就可以通過整合離散模型以及它們相應的控制器得到通用的TP結構。在這種情況下，由於存在有通用的TP結構，使用LMIs 驗證系統的綜合控制性能是完全可行的。 本項目將會研究離散控制器的設計和分佈及其對最終的TP結構和系統的綜合控制性能的影響等相關問題。本項目還將解決的一個問題是：在通常情況下，由於高維奇異值分解過程中需要對復雜性和精確性進行折中，綜合的TP模型是原有模型的近似。因此，基於原有模型的綜合控制器的性能將需要通過研究系統魯棒性來確定。 在自動控制系統設計中將人為操縱減到最小的TP多邊形結構計算方法的持續開發過程中，本項目實是一個關鍵步驟。在開發不同的TP結構的基礎上，我們將竭力建立我們所提供的數值方法和現有的分析方法之間的關聯。本項目可促進控制理論在更廣泛的工程問題中的應用，並將提高國內外控制工程師和研究人員的技術知識水平。

418212.label: Realisation of objectives
418212.value: The first project objective is related to analyzing the effects of grid point control system design on the resulting performance structure. Previous studies in this area have focused on the case when the controller does not introduce additional structure over that of the system TP model, which results in a rather straightforward closed loop TP structure. One example in this regard will be the adoption of a pure constant gain as controller. LMI-based performance requirements for the closed loop system in this case have been described in many existing works, e.g., P. Baranyi, Y. Yam, and P. Várlaki, Tensor Product (TP) Model Transformation in Polytopic Model-Based Control, CRC Press. The present project, however, is focused on the case when the adopted controller does induce additional structure over that of the system TP model. No notable work has been conducted on this case in the past. In a related work, closed loop stability was demonstrated for an approximated but not the exact representation of the system model only. The present project realized the first objective with the introduction of a unified TP structure over both system and controller TP structure, resulting in the special form of the system which can be readily tackled with robust control system design. The second objective relates to strategies for the distributive design of grid point controllers to facilitate acceptable overall performance. In this regard, the project has specifically proposed a three steps approach. They include (1) generating the TP model of the system and controller; (2) conducting a unified TP transformation to obtain a common structure of the system and controller. Usual trade-offs between complexity and accuracy will be carried out. Errors in representing the system and controller TP models via the unified structure will be cast as uncertainty term in a reformed dynamic equation; and (3) pursuing a robust control design so the closed loop control will have enough robustness to cover the uncertainty term in the unified structure. The third objective is to incorporate robustness into the controller to overcome errors induced by polytopic approximation above. The objective is realized by the derivation of theoretical results in the form of a Theorem which provides the LMI-based requirement on guaranteeing the performance of robust control. The Theorem is the first of its kind covering the case where the controller is taking on a different TP structure as the system.

418212.label: Major findings and research outcome
418212.value: The present project studied the case of a general Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) system with a gain LPV controller. In previous TP-based designs, one is to generate the TP representation of the given model and then obtain the controller through the Distributed Parallel Compensation (DPC) method. Physically, the TP representation amounts to discretizing the given LPV model over a grid in the hyper-dimensional space of the varying parameter set ho. The dimension of the involved space is the same as the number of the varying parameters. As such, previous practice is equivalent to representing the LPV system model as a nonlinear interpolation of its grid point models and then applying the DPC design approach. Moreover, the previous practice assumes the same nonlinear interpolation functions for the controller, with only the grid point controllers are to be designed. The present project is the first of its kind to tackle the case when different interpolation functions for the controller is allowed in the design, which foreseeably will lead to enhanced design flexibility and hence performance. As the work shows, we have formulated a somewhat different design strategy (as outlined in Section IV of the Paper #2 in Part C). The strategy involves the three steps of (1) generating the individual TP structures of the system and controller, (2) obtaining a unified structure comprising of the system and controller TP structure, and (3) conducting robust control system design. In step (2), upon normal trade-offs between complexity and accuracy in the TP transformation process of generating the unified structure, we managed to express the mismatches in the system and controller TP structure in the special form in terms of Delta_a and Delta_b in eqn (16) (of Paper #2 in Part C). The robust control design in step (3) is then conducted to compensate for the effect of the uncertainty quantities using the DPC approach. In this pursuit, we managed to derive a theorem (Theorem 1 in Paper#2 in Part C) comprising of LMI requirements to guarantee the performance of the closed loop system in the presence of Delta_a and Delta_b (of Paper#2 in Part C). The result here parallels the LMI requirements in previous works for the case where the controller is having the same TP structure as the system. Finally, we also provided a numerical example to illustrate the various features in the applying the research results of the project.

418212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418212.value: The present research opened up a new direction of tackling control system design via the TP approach. Previous works in TP designs normally adopt the same TP structure for the controller as the system. The present project relaxed this practice and provided a basic formulation and theoretical basis in such consideration. Further developments building on the present project include: • The present project has considered only the case of gain controller. The next step will be to consider dynamic controller. The difference between a dynamic and a gain controller lies in a higher dimension of the tensor involved in the former case under the TP transformation process. One expects the similar formulation can be readily extended to the dynamic case. • Application of the present research results to more case studies and application will further strengthened the validity of the present work. Specifically, it will be of interest to focus on showing the enhanced flexibility and performance attained with an open up TP structure in the controller design. • The present project deals with the robust stability performance of controller with open-up TP structure. LMI requirements for additional performance, such as decay rate control, control input constraints, etc., will be of interest.

418212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418212.value: TP-based design approach normally assumes that the controller and system model will have the same TP structure, which fits nicely into the DPC design formulation. The present project tackles the problem when the two TP structures are not the same. The problem is of interest because foreseeably, opening up the TP structure of the controller will potentially allow for more flexibility and hence performance in design. The present project tackles this problem by incorporating the additional step of representing the two simultaneously in a unified TP structure. In the case that the model TP structure or the control TP structure, or both, are not fully included due to dimensionality and complexity consideration, the resulting errors are expressed as a uncertainty in the dynamics equations. As such, these mismatch terms are then to be treated via the design of a robust controller. Moreover, the project produces a theorem containing two LMI conditions that would guarantee the needed robust stability. The theorem is the first of its kind in the present independent controller TP structure case, complementing those in current literatures that assign the same system TP structure to the controller. The project also produces an example illustrating the attained research results.

418512.label: Project Objectives
418512.value: The primitive objective of this project is to explore maximizing Cloud computing capability to support graph processing tasks with a focus on high efficiency and high scalability. We will concentrate ourselves on how to parallelize graph algorithms in Cloud. We will investigate graph storage issues, workload balance issues, preprocessing cost minimization, and I/O-cost reduction, using database techniques.

418512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418512.value: Graph has been widely used as a data structure to maintain complex relationships among entities. There exist many large graphs, for example, online bibliographic networks (DBLP, PubMed), online social networks (Facebook, Flickr, LinkedIn, MySpace), Wikipedia, or even the entire WWW. Such graphs are large, and are keeping growing. For example, in the social network extracted from facebook, where nodes represent persons and edges represent the friend relationships among persons, there are more than 800,000,000 nodes and more than 52,000,000,000 edges (http://www.facebook.com/press/info.php?statistics). One key issue is how to conduct graph processing tasks over large-scale graphs. Cloud computing is built upon a large number of commodity computers connected by a network, where each computer is associated with its own CPU/memory/disk, and is a promising direction to provide high-quality data services. MapReduce by Google provides developers with a simple programming model, using two functions, namely, map and reduce. Developers can develop data services to achieve high scalability and fault-tolerance. Here, a map function is used to generate/distribute a set of key-value pairs, and a reduce function is used to process such pairs with the same key. One MapReduce implementation is Hadoop by Yahoo!. Google, Yahoo!, Microsoft, Facebook, and Amazon all give their cloud computing solutions in MapReduce. However, it has been known to be challenging to parallelize graph algorithms, and it is challenging to support graph processing tasks in MapReduce, due to the programming style of using map and reduce functions. This project is motivated by such strong needs to support graph processing tasks in a parallel manner. In this project, we focus on large-scale graph processing in MapReduce, and explore maximizing MapReduce capability in large graph processing. We concentrate on efficiency, and study several fundamental issues such as graph storage, graph pattern matching, graph traversal, graph partitioning, and graph ordering (topological sorting), which have not been well studied in MapReduce. The key issues are graph algorithm design, graph storage design, workload balancing, and the reduction of iterations of using map/reduce functions in MapReduce. The importance of this project is that the new finding in MapReduce will lead to high quality servers to support complex data analysis upon such large graphs. The academic significance of the project is of two folds. In addition to conference and journal publications reporting the project finding, the methodology and techniques developed will be implemented in a prototype system to demonstrate the strength of our approach. 图是一个被广泛应用在维护各实体之间复杂关系的数据结构。现实应用中会有有许多大图，例如，在线文献网络 (DBLP, PubMed)，在线社交网络（Facebook, Flickr, LinkedIn, MySpace），维基百科，甚至整个互联网。这些图不但很大，而且还在保持不断的增长。例如，从facebook提取出的在线社交网络图中，有超过800,000,000个节点和超过52,000,000,000条变，其中每个节点代表的是一个用户，而每条边代表的是两个用户之间的朋友关系（http://www.facebook.com/press/info.php?statistics）。这里的一个关键的问题是如何去做如此大的图的各种处理问题。 云计算是建立在大量用通用计算机连接起来所组成的网络的基础之上的。在云计算中，每一台计算机都有自己独立的CPU /内存/磁盘。云计算是一种能够提供高质量的数据服务的方法，并且具有很好的前景。由谷歌开发的MapReduce方法为开发人员提供了一个简单的云计算编程模型。使用MapReduce，开发人员只需要实现两个函数，map和reduce, 就可以开发出具有高可扩展性和容错性的数据服务。在MapRecuce中，map函数用来产生和分配一系列键值对，reduce函数则对具有同样键的所有键值对进行统一处理。Hadoop就是雅虎公司实现的基于 MapReduce的云计算解决方案。谷歌，雅虎，微软，Facebook, 和亚马逊也都有自己的基于MapReduce的云计算解决方案。虽然如此，对于图的问题的并行化计算仍然是当今非常具有挑战性的一个课题，而且由于MapReduce的实现只能基于map和reduce两个函数的限制，在MapReduce的框架下解决大图的处理问题更是难上加难。 该项目的动机是就是基于这样一个需求：可以支持大图问题的并行化处理。在该项目中，我们专注于用MapReduce的方法来实现大图问题的并行化处理，并且最大化MapReduce处理大图问题的能力。我们集中在算法效率的提高上。我们主要研究一些图的基本问题，比如图的存储，图的模式匹配，图的遍历，图的划分，图的拓扑排序，等等。这些问题都还没有在MapReduce上得到很好的研究和实现。在MapReduce上实现这些算法的关键问题是图的算法设计，图的存储设计，负载均衡，以及减少使用map 和 reduce函数的迭代次数。我们相信，在该项目中发现的MapReduce在大图上的新的算法会被应用到支持在大图上做复杂数据分析的高质量服务上面。 该项目的学术意义是两方面的。除了在会议和期刊出版物里面报告项目中的新发展以外，我们会用我们的方法和技术实现一个原型系统，以展示这些方法的可行性。

418512.label: Realisation of objectives
418512.value: We report our research outcomes in relation to the main project objective. First, we work on outsourcing shortest distance computing with privacy projection in Cloud computing context. This is because it becomes desirable to outsource large graphs to cloud servers, in order to efficiently perform complex operations without compromising their sensitive information. We take shortest distance query, as a case to investigate the technique issues in outsourcing graph operations. We study a parameter-free, edge-based 2-hop delegation security model, which can greatly reduce the chances of the structural pattern attack and the graph reconstruction attack at the cloud server side. We devise a greedy algorithm to transform the original graph G into a link graph Gl kept locally and a set of outsourced graphs Go kept at the cloud server, and develop an efficient transformation method to support approximate shortest distance answering under a given average additive error bound. This work is reported in VLDB Journal. Second, we study graph workload balancing on Cloud, which is closely related to graph partitioning. It is worth mentioning that balanced graph partitioning is NP-complete. In addition, a static graph partitioning cannot keep all graph algorithms efficient for a long time in parallel on Cloud, because the workload balancing in different iterations for different graph algorithms are all possible different. We investigate graph behaviors by exploring the working window changes, where a working window is a set of active vertices that a graph algorithm really needs to access in parallel computing. We classify nine classic graph algorithms into three categories, and conduct extensive experimental studies on the working window changes for a random graph partitioning. Based on our experimental studies, we propose simple yet effective policies that can achieve workload balancing for the active vertices and reduce the number of edges across different computational vertices in supersteps starting from an initial random graph partitioning. This work is reported in ICDE’13. Third, we propose a high level graph analysis system, called GLog, on MapReduce. The motivation of this work is as follows. It is cumbersome and error-prone for developers to implement complex graph analysis tasks in distributed environments, and in addition developers need to spend long time to learn the details of the framework they need to use. To overcome these issues, we propose a high level query language called GLog and study its evaluation method. We design a RG (Relational-Graph) data model to mix relational data and graph data, and extend Datalog to GLog on RG tables to support various graph analysis tasks. We define operations on RG tables, and discuss translation templates to convert a GLog query into a sequence of MapReduce jobs. And we propose two strategies, namely rule merging and iteration rewriting, to optimize the translated jobs. This work is reported in ICDE’14. Forth, we study continuous pattern detection over a billion-edge graph in a distributed framework. Here, continuous pattern detection is to monitor changes in real applications. The large size and dynamic update of graphs, along with the massive search space, pose challenges in developing an efficient continuous pattern detection system. We leverage a distributed graph processing framework to approximately detect a given pattern over a large dynamic graph. We aim at improving the scalability without loss much accuracy, by reducing the response time and message cost in the detection. In brief, we convert a given query pattern into a SSD plan (Single- Sink DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph)), and propose an evaluation plan with message transitions on the DAG, to detect the pattern in a large dynamic graph. A SSD plan can guide the data graph exploration via messages, and the messages will converge at data sink vertices, which then detect the query pattern. We also conduct join operations over partial vertices during the graph exploration to improve the accuracy of pattern detection. We further design various sink vertex selection strategies and neighborhood based transition rule to reduce the evaluation cost. This work is reported in ICDE’14. Fifth, we study I/O efficient graph processing techniques to convert a general directed graph into a directed acyclic graph (DAG). The conversion is achieved by contracting a strongly connected component (SCC) of a graph to a vertex in DAG, where an SCC is a maximal subgraph of a directed graph G in which every pair of vertices are reachable from each other in the SCC. The converted DAG is simple because it is cycle-free and is small because an SCC is represented by a single vertex. In many real applications that need graph pattern matching, topological sorting, or reachability query processing, the best way to deal with a general directed graph is to deal with its DAG representation. Therefore, finding all SCCs in a directed graph G is a critical operation. The existing in-memory algorithms based on depth first search (DFS) can find all SCCs in linear time w.r.t. the size of a graph. However, when a graph cannot reside entirely in the main memory, the existing external or semi-external algorithms to find all SCCs have limitation to achieve high I/O efficiency. We study new I/O efficient semi-external algorithms to find all SCCs for a massive directed graph G that cannot reside in main memory entirely. To overcome the deficiency of the existing DFS based semi-external algorithm that heavily relies on a total order, we explore a weak order based on which we investigate new algorithms. We propose a new single phase algorithm, which combines the tree construction and tree search phases into a single phase, with three new optimization techniques. They are early acceptance, early rejection, and batch processing. By the single phase algorithm with the new optimization techniques, we can significantly reduce the number of I/Os and CPU cost. This work is reported in SIGMOD’13. In addition, we study an external algorithm to compute all SCCs, and we report it in ICDE’14. Sixth, we study scalable big graph processing in MapReduce. In the literature, there are MapReduce Class (MRC) and Minimal MapReduce Class (MMC) to define the memory consumption, communication cost, CPU cost, and number of MapReduce rounds for an algorithm to execute in MapReduce. Neither of them is for big graph processing, since the constraints in MMC can be hardly achieved simultaneously on graphs and the conditions in MRC may induce scalability problems when processing big graph data. We study a Scalable Graph processing Class (SGC) for scalable graph processing. We define two graph join operators in SGC, namely, EN join and NE join, using which a wide range of graph algorithms can be designed, including PageRank, breadth first search, graph keyword search, Connected Component computation, and Minimum Spanning Forest computation. This work is reported in SIGMOD’14. Seventh, we study auto-approximation of Graph Computing in Cloud. We give an innovative approach which automatically and systematically synthesizes a program to approximate the original program. We show that we can give users some answers with reasonable accuracy and high efficiency for a wide spectrum of graph algorithms, without having to know the details of graph algorithms. This work is reported in PVLDB’14.

418512.label: Major findings and research outcome
418512.value: We summarize the main results below. First, we work on outsourcing shortest distance computing with privacy projection in Cloud. This is because it becomes desirable to outsource large graphs to cloud servers, in order to efficiently perform complex operations without compromising their sensitive information (VLDBJ13). Second, we study graph workload balancing on Cloud, which is related to graph partitioning (NP-complete). Note that a static graph partitioning cannot make all graph algorithms efficient on Cloud, because the workload balancing in different iterations for different graph algorithms are all different. We investigate graph behaviors by exploring the working window changes, where a working window is a set of active vertices that a graph algorithm really needs to access in parallel computing. We classify nine graph algorithms into three categories, and conduct extensive experimental studies on the working window changes for a random graph partitioning. We propose policies to achieve workload balancing (ICDE13). Third, we propose a high level graph analysis system, called GLog, on MapReduce (ICDE14). Forth, we study continuous pattern detection over a billion-edge graph in a distributed framework (ICDE14). Fifth, we study I/O efficient graph processing techniques to convert a general directed graph into a DAG. We study semi-external and external algorithms to compute all SCCs (SIGMOD13, ICDE14, VLDBJ). Sixth, we study scalable big graph processing in MapReduce. In the literature, there are MapReduce Class (MRC) and Minimal MapReduce Class (MMC) to define the memory consumption, communication cost, CPU cost, and number of MapReduce rounds for an algorithm to execute in MapReduce. Neither of them is for big graph processing, since the constraints in MMC can be hardly achieved simultaneously on graphs and the conditions in MRC may induce scalability problems when processing big graph data. We study a Scalable Graph processing Class (SGC) for scalable graph processing. We define two graph join operators in SGC, namely, EN join and NE join, using which a wide range of graph algorithms can be designed, including PageRank, breadth first search, graph keyword search, Connected Component computation, and Minimum Spanning Forest computation (SIGMOD14). Seventh, we study auto-approximation of Graph Computing in Cloud. We give an innovative approach which automatically and systematically synthesizes a program to approximate the original program. We show that we can give users some answers with reasonable accuracy and high efficiency for a wide spectrum of graph algorithms, without having to know the details of graph algorithms (PVLDB14).

418512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418512.value: Graph processing has been studied in Cloud. There are still many remaining issues such as how to make it easy to use and how to further enhance the efficiency. We will continue to work on these issues.

418512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418512.value: The project is to explore Cloud computing capability to support graph processing tasks. We have provided new solutions. Regarding the optimality, we propose a new Scalable Graph Processing Class (SGC) for scalable graph processing in MapReduce, where the optimality is defined in terms of memory consumption, communication cost, CPU cost, and the number of MapReduce rounds for an algorithm to execute in MapReduce. Under SGC, we further show what can be done in this class for high efficiency. We study auto-approximation of graph computing in Cloud. A key question we attempt to answer is: it is more important to find out something meaningful quick from a large graph, and we should focus on finding a way of making use of large graphs instead of spending time on designing approximate algorithms. We give our auto-approximation solution, and investigate the accuracy vs efficiency. We also study workload balancing, because a static graph partitioning, which is NP-complete, cannot make all graph algorithms efficient in Cloud, due to the fact that the workload balancing in different iterations for different graph algorithms are all different. We propose policies to achieve workload balancing. The I/O efficiency and several new techniques for graph computing are also studied.

418712.label: Realisation of objectives
418712.value: The PI and the Co-Is have generated 7 journal papers and 10 conference papers on the design and analysis of physical-layer network coding (PNC) in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) relay networks. The major research outputs are summarized and categorized based on the four proposed objectives, as detailed below. As most of the conference papers are shorter versions of their corresponding journal versions, we will mainly focus on the journal papers. Objective 1: To set up a research framework for implementing PNC in MIMO TWRCs To achieve this objective, we study the PNC design for efficient communications over MIMO multiway relay channels (mRCs). We focus on analyzing the achievable degrees of freedom (DoF) of the MIMO mRC. In journal paper [3], we consider a data exchange model termed clustered full data exchange, i.e., each user in a cluster wants to learn the messages of all the other users in the same cluster. Novel signal alignment techniques are developed to jointly and systematically construct the beamforming matrices at the users and the relay for efficient implementation of physical-layer network coding. Based on that, we derive an achievable DoF of the MIMO mRC with an arbitrary network topology configuration and antenna settings. The DoF results derived in this paper serve as fundamental benchmarks in evaluating the performance of practical communication systems over MIMO mRCs. In journal paper [1], we consider a clustered MIMO mRC, but operating in a new data exchange model, termed clustered pairwise data exchange. Our main contribution is to propose a systematic signal alignment approach to jointly design the beamforming matrices at the users and the relay, based on which an achievable DoF is derived for the MIMO mRC with an arbitrary network configuration. In journal paper [5], we further consider a MIMO mRC with pairwise data exchange. We derive an achievable DoF is derived for the MIMO mRC with an arbitrary network configuration and also analyze the optimality of the derived DoF results. In journal paper [6], we study the DoF of the MIMO multipair TWRC with multiple relays. We establish a general framework for the DoF analysis by combining the ideas of signal space alignment and interference neutralization. The proposed framework involves a joint design of user transmit beamformers, relay precoders, and user receive beamformers. We derive an achievable DoF for the MIMO multipair TDRC with an arbitrary configuration. Objective 2: To bridge the gap between the theory and practice of PNC for MIMO TWRCs The DoF analysis characterizes the system performance in the high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime. The DoF characterization is usually insufficient from a practical point of view since practical communication systems usually work at low and median SNR. Therefore, to bridge the gap between theory and practice of PNC, we also work on analyzing the rate throughput of relay networks. In journal paper [2], we study the transceiver and relay design for MIMO cellular two-way relay channel (cTWRC), where a multi-antenna base station (BS) exchanges information with multiple multi-antenna mobile stations via a multi-antenna relay station (RS). We propose a novel two-way relaying scheme to approach the sum capacity of the MIMO cTWRC. A key contribution of this work is a new non-linear lattice-based precoding technique to pre-compensate the inter-stream interference at the relay, so as to allow efficient interference-free lattice decoding at the relay. We derive sufficient conditions for the proposed scheme to asymptotically achieve the sum capacity of the MIMO cTWRC. In conference paper [6], we propose a novel space-division-based network-coding scheme for MIMO TWRCs, in which two multiantenna users exchange information via a multiantenna relay. We show that the proposed scheme achieves the asymptotic sum-rate capacity of the MIMO TWRC within a marginal gap for any antenna configuration and for any channel realization. In journal paper [7], we study efficient PNC design for communications over a multi-pair MIMO two-way relay system. We show that our scheme performs close to the cut-set outer bound and significantly outperforms the existing schemes in the literature. Objective 3: To investigate the impact of channel uncertainty on PNC All the abovementioned works are based on the assumption that full channel state information (CSI) is available at both the user nodes and the relay nodes. As a matter of fact, CSI error is usually unavoidable in practical systems, e.g., due to channel estimation error. Therefore, to meet objective 3, we study the impact of channel uncertainty on the performance of the proposed PNC schemes. Also, we have studied the channel estimation for MIMO two-way and multi-way relay networks. We find that existing channel estimation methods can be straightforwardly applied to the relay network under consideration, and the analysis of channel uncertainty for conventional communication networks can be directly used for the relay network. We haven’t identified any theoretical novelties in these approaches. Therefore, this part of work was done without generating publications. Objective 4: To explore the potential applications of the EDA precoding principle in other related MIMO communication scenarios To achieve this objective, we study the design of linear precoding for various MIMO two-way or multi-way relay networks. In journal paper [4], we develop a unified framework for precoding designs in non-regenerative multiuser two-way relaying (TWR). The core of our framework is the solution to the max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise-ratio (SINR) problem for multiuser TWR. We solve this problem using a Dinkelbach-type algorithm with near-optimal performance and superlinear convergence. We show that, using the max-min SINR solution as a corner stone, the precoding designs under various important criteria, such as weighted sum-rate maximization, weighted sum mean-square-error (MSE) minimization, and average bit-error-rate (BER) or symbol-error-rate (SER) minimization, etc, can be reformulated into a monotonic program. In conference paper [7], we consider the joint transceiver and relay design for a wireless MIMO switching scheme that enables data exchange among multiple users. The main contribution of this paper is a unified approach to solve the weighted sum mean-square error (MSE) minimization and weighted sum-rate maximization problems in MIMO switching.

418712.label: Major findings and research outcome
418712.value: The major findings of this project have been already elaborated in Section 5.3. We summarize them as follows. 1. We analyzed the degrees of freedom (DoF) of the MIMO multiway relay channel under various data exchange models, including pairwise data exchange, clustered pairwise data exchange, clustered full data exchange, etc. DoF upper and lower bounds are developed to give insights and guidance for the practical design of PNC for multiway relaying. 2. We further explored the potential of distributive relaying, and derived DoF lower and upper bounds for the MIMO multiway relay channel with distributed relays. 3. To bridge the gap between theory and practice, we studied the practical coding design for the MIMO multiway relay channel. We showed that our proposed PNC schemes can achieve the asymptotic sum-rate capacities of the MIMO TWRC and the MIMO cellular TWRC. 4. We also studied the precoding design for MIMO two-way or multi-way relay networks. Efficient algorithms were proposed to solve the formulated problems based on various optimization criteria, including weighted sum-rate maximization, weighted sum mean-square-error (MSE) minimization, and average bit-error-rate (BER) or symbol-error-rate (SER) minimization, etc.

418712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418712.value: So far, the DoF characterization of the MIMO multiway relay channel is still far from complete. Except for some limited network topological configurations and antenna settings, we only have DoF upper and lower bounds for the MIMO multiway relay channel. How to tighten these bounds will be an interesting research direction worthy of pursuing. The capacity analysis of the MIMO multiway relay channel developed in this project is mostly theoretical. To achieve the gain promised by PNC, there are still many practical issues to be concerned, including synchronization, practical lattice coding design, channel sounding, network-layer protocol design, etc. These issues require a lot of further research effort.

418712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418712.value: This project has integrated two milestone inventions, namely the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technique and physical-layer network coding (PNC), which can dramatically enhance the throughput of wireless communication networks. In particular, this project studied reliable and efficient communications over the MIMO two-way relay channel (TWRC), in which two users equipped with multiple antennas exchange information via the help of a single multi-antenna relay. Later, the results were generalized to the MIMO multiway relay channel, where more users and more relays are allowed to play a role in data exchange. This configuration applies to important practical scenarios, such as the next generation wireless local area networks (WLAN), wireless mesh networks, etc. In this project, we analyzed the degrees of freedom (DoF) of the MIMO multiway relay channel under various data exchange models and network topological configurations. We also studied the practical coding design to achieve the fundamental capacity limits of the channel. The proposed analysis will shed lights on the practical PNC design for such systems. In addition, we would like to emphasize that this project is multidisciplinary, including but not limited to information theory, communication networks, and signal processing. In the long run, this project will contribute to the theoretical understanding and practical implementation of MIMO and PNC techniques in general wireless networks.

419012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419012.value: Closed-loop supply chain management has gained great momentum in both practice and academic research because of an increasing awareness of sustainable development. With the rising costs of energy and raw materials, more and more companies are now considering closed-loop supply chain management a strategic activity that can lower production and inventory costs and improve profitability. One important operation in closed-loop supply chain management is remanufacturing, which restores returned products to like-new condition and then resell them to satisfy customer demand. Examples of remanufactured products include automotive parts, tires, electronics products, photocopiers, toner cartridges, among others. The aim of this project is to study approximation algorithms for dynamic remanufacturing systems with stochastic product returns and customer demands. The key feature is that demands and product returns in different periods are correlated. A major domain of applications is remanufacturing systems where product returns in one period depend on demands in the previous periods, which are often observed in practice. The prior studies on dynamic remanufacturing systems mostly assume independent demands and returns to avoid the well-known curse of dimensionality of the dynamic programming formulation, i.e., the state space becomes so large that the optimal policy is computationally intractable. But such simplification greatly hinders the practical applicability of the results. Therefore, we will exploit novel approaches to formulate and analyze such remanufacturing systems. Specifically, we will evaluate decisions and construct approximation policies and algorithms based on alternative cost accounting schemes. The policies aim to balance various costs such as inventory holding, demand backlogging, and remanufacturing/manufacturing costs. More importantly, these policies are easily computable and implementable and will be proved to have constant worst-case performance guarantees. We will firstly analyze a basic model where a remanufacturing firm determines manufacturing and remanufacturing quantities periodically to minimize its costs under correlated demands and product returns. And then we will study more complex systems with product return disposal, manufacturing/remanufacturing capacity constraints, and multi-type of product returns. Each of these extensions will require novel ideas to design cost accounting schemes and derive provably good approximation algorithms. To further demonstrate the value of our approximation policies, we will compare their performance to the myopic policies that are widely adopted as heuristics for problems with a large state space as well as those that ignore the correlation between returns and demands. This project is the first attempt to develop computationally efficient policies with constant performance guarantees for remanufacturing systems. 由于对可持续发展意识的逐渐增强，闭环供应链管理近来在实践和学术研究上都得到很大的推动。随着能源与原材料成本的不断增加，越来越多的企业把闭环供应链管理作为一项能够降低生产和库存成本以及提高盈利的策略。再制造是闭环供应链中一项重要的运作，它将退货或回收产品恢复到如同新产品一样的条件，并再次销售用于满足客户需求。再制造产品的例子包括汽车配件，轮胎，电子产品，复印机，墨粉盒等。 本课题的目标在于研究和开发关于有效控制存在随机产品回收和客户需求的动态再制造系统的近似算法。该系统最主要的特点是不同阶段的需求和回收产品是相关的。一个主要的应用领域在于再制造系统中，一个阶段的产品回收依赖于前阶段的需求。这是一个在实际中经常观察到系统特性。之前的研究大多假设产品回收和前期的需求是相互独立的从而来避免在动态规划中由于高维的状态空间而使得最优策略无法计算的问题。但是该简化大大降低了相应结果的可应用性。因此，我们将利用新的方法来对此类再制造系统进行建模和分析。具体而言，我们将基于另一种成本计算机制来评价决策和构建近似策略和算法。该近似策略将平衡多种成本，如库存成本，需求欠货成本，和制造，再制造成本。更重要的是，这些策略很容易计算并运用于实际中，而且能有最差情况下的表现保证。我们将首先分析一个基本模型，当中再制造商面对相关的客户需求和产品回收，决定每个阶段制造和再制造产品的数量从而最小化成本。然后，我们将研究更复杂的系统，如回收产品的丢弃，制造与再制造的产能约束，和多种类产品回收。每个拓展都需要新的想法来设计成本计算和推导可证明的好的近似算法。为了进一步说明我们近似策略的价值，我们会将它与广泛采用的短视算法或者忽略需求和回收产品相关性的策略进行比较。本课题是第一个尝试开发有常数表现保证且便于计算的再制造系统的控制策略。

419012.label: Realisation of objectives
419012.value: The project objectives have all been successfully realized. We have developed quantitative models for dynamic remanufacturing inventory systems in which stochastic demands and product returns across different periods are correlated. Based on the models, we have designed and applied alternative cost accounting schemes to develop approximation algorithms with theoretical worst-case performance guarantee. And our extensive numerical studies have demonstrated the superior performance of the proposed algorithm. These outcomes have been reported in the paper titled “Approximation Balancing Policies for Inventory Systems with Remanufacturing,” which has been published in Mathematics of Operations Research.

419012.label: Major findings and research outcome
419012.value: The major findings of the project are reported in two research papers, one has published while the other is currently under revision (minor). In the paper “Approximation Balancing Policies for Inventory Systems with Remanufacturing,” we consider a single-product, periodic-review inventory system with remanufacturable returned products, in which the serviceable product used to fulfill stochastic customer demand can be either manufactured from new parts or remanufactured from returned products. Demand and returns follow general stochastic processes and may be correlated, nonstationary, and evolving across different periods. The system costs include remanufacturing and manufacturing costs as well as inventory holding and demand backlogging costs. The objective is to minimize the expected total discounted cost over a finite planning horizon. The optimal policy for this model has a simple structure but its computation can be practically intractable because of the large and high-dimensional state space. Henceforth, we propose an efficient approximation algorithm based on cost balancing techniques to compute manufacturing and remanufacturing quantities in each period and show that the expected cost under this remanufacturing balancing policy is at most twice of the optimal one. Moreover, a numerical study demonstrates that the balancing policy generally performs much better than its worst-case bound. The analysis and results are also extended to cases with capacitated manufacturing and remanufacturing and multiple types of returned products. This paper has been published on Mathematics of Operations Research. Managing perishable inventory systems with positive lead times and finite ordering capacities is important but notoriously difficult in both theory and computation. The optimal control policy is extremely complicated, and no effective heuristic policy has been proposed in the literature. In the paper “Approximation Algorithms for Capacitated Perishable Inventory Systems with Positive Lead Times,” we develop an easy-to-compute approximation algorithm for this class of problems and prove that it admits a theoretical worst-case performance guarantee under independent and many commonly used positively correlated demand processes. Our worst-case analysis departs significantly from those in the previous studies, requiring several novel ideas. In particular, we introduce a transient unit-matching rule to dynamically match the supply and demand units, and the notion of associated demand processes provides the right future demand information to establish the desired results. Our numerical study demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. This paper is under minor revision at Management Science.

419012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
419012.value: The PI will seek possible applications/implementations of the major outcomes of the research in the related industry by exploring collaboration with companies and other organizations. Meanwhile, the PI will continue working on related research topics, e.g., remanufacturing inventory systems, approximation algorithms, and sustainable operations. Several working papers are currently under preparation or review.

419012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419012.value: Approximation algorithms aim to find effective and computationally efficient solutions with worst-case performance guarantee (relative to the optimal solutions) for complex optimization problems. In this project, we develop approximation algorithms to find effective inventory control policies for two classes of systems: remanufacturing systems with sales-dependent product return, and perishable inventory systems with positive replenishment lead times and capacity constraint. For remanufacturing systems, we have witnessed the rapid growth of remanufacturing industry, driven mostly by stringent environmental regulations and the potential economic benefit of remanufacturing. By remanufacturing returned products, companies could save costs in energy and raw material and at the same time establish “environmentally friendly” images to the public. For perishable products, they are ubiquitous and indispensable to our society. Perishable products such as meat, fruit, vegetable, dairy products, and frozen foods constitute the majority of supermarket sales. They also include virtually all pharmaceuticals, which represent a multi-billion-dollar industry. Blood blank is another salient example of perishables. The mode formulations of these two systems share a common characteristic of high-dimensional state space, which results in the intractability of finding optimal solutions. Nevertheless, effective inventory management of these systems has great practical importance as it plays an important role in determining their operational performances. Our algorithms help design effective and implementable inventory control policies. We not only theoretically derive the worst-case performance guarantee but also numerically demonstrate their superior performance. We expect the outcomes would have great application potential in the related industries.

419212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419212.value: Modern distributed storage systems (e.g., cloud storage, data centers, peer-to-peer storage) provide a reliable platform on which individuals and enterprises can archive their data. To provide data availability guarantees in the presence of storage node failures, such systems typically stripe data across different storage nodes using redundancy techniques. However, a storage system often needs to recover any failed nodes to maintain system reliability, or scale up with the number of storage nodes to meet the increasing storage demand. In both cases, the system needs to perform data migration from existing storage nodes to new storage nodes. It is important to minimize data migration (i.e., the amount of data being migrated), subject to the data redundancy requirement as well as other deployment requirements that are essential for a practical distributed archival storage system. In this project, we propose to conduct holistic theoretical and applied studies of a redundancy scheme called non-systematic maximum distance separable (nsMDS) codes, which maintain data redundancy in distributed archival storage systems with an objective of minimizing data migration. A key property of nsMDS codes is that they keep only encoded data, but not necessarily the original input data. Our preliminary studies show that nsMDS codes can minimize data migration in several special cases, and provide a proxy-based implementation for nsMDS codes that can be feasibly deployed in practice. Based on our preliminary findings, we propose two major research directions. First, we propose to conduct detailed theoretical analysis on how nsMDS codes minimize data migration in both recovery and scaling operations under general settings. In addition, we plan to design, implement, and experiment a large-scale, practical distributed archival storage system prototype that uses nsMDS codes, in order to identify the essential engineering guidelines of putting nsMDS codes in practical deployment. The contribution of this research will provide individuals and enterprises with a reliable storage solution that minimizes data migration. Specifically, with the advent of cloud storage, our research provides a cost-saving storage solution for individuals and enterprises to archive their data backups on the cloud. In addition, through both theoretical and applied studies, our research also synergizes the theoretical and systems research communities in designing robust storage systems. To strengthen the impact of this project, we have sought indication of interest of collaboration in this project from both academia and industry such as University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), Huawei Technologies, and Cisco Systems. 現代分佈式存儲系統（例如雲存儲，數據中心，點對點存儲）為個人和企業數據存儲提供了一個可靠的平台。為了提供數據可用性保證，存儲系統通常把數據用冗餘技術分佈在不同的存儲節點。然而，存儲系統往往需要恢復故障節點以維持系統的可靠性，或縮放與存儲節點的數目以滿足不斷增長的存儲需求。在這兩種情況下，系統需要把數據從現有的存儲節點遷移到新的存儲節點，減少數據遷移對於實際的分佈式備份存儲系統便成為不可或缺的需求。 在這個項目中，我們建議為非系統性最大距離可分離（nsMDS）編碼進行全面的理論和應用研究，以最大限度地減少數據遷移，又同時保持數據冗餘為設計目標。我們的初步研究顯示nsMDS編碼可以在幾種特殊情況最大限度地減少數據遷移，和提供一個基於代理式nsMDS編碼實踐。在我們初步研究結果的基礎上，我們提出了兩個主要的研究方向。首先，我們建議進行詳細nsMDS編碼的理論分析，此外我們計劃設計和實驗大型分佈式備份存儲系統的原型。本研究貢獻為個人和企業提供了可靠的存儲解決方案，最大限度地減少數據遷移。

419212.label: Realisation of objectives
419212.value: (i) As per Objective 1, we derived theoretical properties of non-systematic MDS codes, namely the functional minimum storage regenerating codes (FMSR) codes. We have two main results. First, we prove the existence of FMSR codes with uncoded repair (i.e., nodes do not perform encoding during repair), such that the fault tolerance of MDS codes is preserved after any number of rounds of repair. Second, we provide a deterministic FMSR code construction that significantly speeds up the time of encoding coefficient generation. The findings are published at INFOCOM'13 (acceptance rate: 17%). Furthermore, we propose an efficient routing framework for non-systematic cooperative regenerating codes in multi-failure recovery in heterogeneous environments that are commonly found in large-scale wide-area storage systems. We show that by carefully decomposing the recovery operations and distributing the partial recovery results along different routing paths, we can reduce the overall cost of multi-failure recovery. The findings are published at IEEE IWQoS'16 (Full paper) (acceptance rate: 20.6%) (ii) As per Objective 2, we address the heterogeneity of storage nodes in the deployment of MDS codes. We consider a special class of MDS codes called the XOR-based erasure codes, which use only XOR operations for encoding and decoding. We address the problem of speeding up the recovery of a single-node failure for general XOR-based erasure codes. Since the problem is NP-hard in general, we propose a replace recovery algorithm, which uses a hill-climbing technique to search for a fast recovery solution, such that the solution search can be completed within a short time period. We further extend the algorithm to adapt to the scenario where nodes have heterogeneous capabilities. We conduct experiments on a networked storage system testbed, and show that our replace recovery algorithm uses less recovery time than the conventional recovery approach. The findings are accepted for publication at IEEE TPDS, July 2014, in which we specifically address the recovery problem in heterogeneous environments. (iii) As per Objective 3, we propose CodFS, an erasure-coded clustered storage system that realizes erasure coding (including MDS codes) in a distributed setting. CodFS proposes parity logging with reserved space, which comprises two key design features: (1) it takes a hybrid of in-place data updates and log-based parity updates to balance the costs of updates and recovery, and (2) it keeps parity updates in a reserved space next to the parity chunk to mitigate disk seeks. We conduct extensive testbed experiments to evaluate the I/O performance of our CodFS prototype. The source code is published as a public-domain software at http://ansrlab.cse.cuhk.edu.hk/software/codfs. The findings are published at FAST'14 (acceptance rate: 18%). (iv) As per Objective 4, we address the deployment of regenerating codes on Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), a popular distributed file system for data analytics such as MapReduce. We propose CORE, which augments existing optimal regenerating codes to support a general number of failures including single and concurrent failures. In particular, we use multi-threaded design to speed up the encoding operations of regenerating codes, so as to ensure that the encoding operation is not the bottleneck. The source code is published as a public-domain software at http://ansrlab.cse.cuhk.edu.hk/software/core. The findings are published as a short paper at MSST'13 (acceptance rate: 26.6%) and the full version in IEEE TC, 2015. Recently, we also study the performance of HDFS when data is encoded with erasure coding. We improve the task scheduling performance to make MapReduce fit erasure-coded data, the performance of transforming replicated data into erasure-coded data, and degraded read performance. The findings are published at IEEE/IFIP DSN'14 (acceptance rate: 30%), IEEE/IFIP DSN'15 (acceptance rate: 21.8%), and IEEE TC, 2015, respectively. We point out that our CodFS prototype (see above) also leverages extensive parallelization to speed up the write performance. For details, please refer to our paper at FAST'14. (v) As per Objective 5, we study the integration of erasure coding with deduplication and security. We built a new multi-cloud storage system called CDStore, which unifies fault tolerance, security, and cost efficiency by extending erasure coding to support secret sharing and combining our scheme with deduplication. ding with security and deduplication in multi-cloud storage. Our findings are published at USENIX ATC'15 (acceptance rate: 21.3%) and IEEE Internet Computing, 2016. (vi) Beyond our objectives, we also study new constructions of erasure codes. We proposed STAIR codes, a new general code construction that provides simultaneous fault tolerance against both sector and disk failures in a space-efficient manner. The new construction is shown to be more space efficient (i.e., less storage efficiency) than traditional Reed-Solomon codes or regenerating codes that only address one-level fault tolerance. STAIR codes are suitable for archival storage where improving space efficiency is always necessary. The findings are published at FAST'14 (acceptance rate: 18%) and ACM TOS 2014.

419212.label: Major findings and research outcome
419212.value: We explore several areas of research to enable efficient deployment of erasure codes in distributed storage systems. Network coding for cloud storage Recent theoretical studies have shown the use of network coding in improving the recovery performance in erasure-coded storage, and proposed a family of erasure codes called regenerating codes to realize the notion of network coding. However, the practical deployment of network-coding-based storage remains largely unexplored. Our research proposes various designs to address this issue. We propose a construction of functional minimum storage regenerating (FMSR) codes that are proven to achieve minimum repair bandwidth and I/O [INFOCOM'13]. We also show how we apply non-systematic cooperative regenerating codes to address multi-failure recovery in heterogeneous environments [IWQoS'16]. Erasure coding in Hadoop We have put significant efforts to integrate erasure coding with the Hadoop platform, which has been widely used for big data analytics. For example, we integrate systematic regenerating codes into Hadoop to address single and multiple failures [MSST'13, TC'15]; we improve MapReduce scheduling performance on top of erasure-coded storage [DSN'14, LANMAN'15]; we efficiently transform replicated data into erasure-coded data in Hadoop [DSN'15]; we improve degraded read performance in Hadoop [TC'15]. High-performance erasure-coded storage We built our own distributed storage system that realizes erasure coding with high performance mind. Specifically, we design and implement a high-performance erasure-coded storage system called CodFS [FAST'14], which comprises two key design features: (1) it takes a hybrid of in-place data updates and log-based parity updates to balance the costs of updates and recovery, and (2) it keeps parity updates in a reserved space next to the parity chunk to mitigate disk seeks. We also design a greedy recovery algorithm that improves recovery performance for any XOR-based erasure code [TPDS'14]. New erasure coding topics We also explore new issues not mentioned in this project. We propose STAIR codes [FAST'14, TOS'14], a new general code construction that provides simultaneous fault tolerance against both sector and disk failures in a space-efficient manner. We also propose a new multi-cloud storage system called CDStore [ATC'15, Internet Computing'16], which unifies fault tolerance, security, and cost efficiency by extending erasure coding to support secret sharing and combining our scheme with deduplication. We believe that they can open new research areas in erasure coding storage.

419212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
419212.value: We mainly focus on the practical deployment of erasure coding (including both systematic and non-systematic codes) for archival storage, in which updates are infrequent. Future work includes: (i) extending the design for primary storage that involves write-intensive or update-intensive workloads; (ii) including high-performance architectures such as SSDs and emerging non-volatile memories; and (iii) new networked architectures such as data centers and geo-distributed storage.

419212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419212.value: We explore several areas of research to enable efficient deployment of erasure codes (including non-systematic and systematic erasure codes) in distributed storage systems, including network coding for cloud storage, erasure coding in Hadoop-like analytics platforms, high-performance erasure-coding-based storage, etc. Our research specifically demonstrates the practicality of deploying erasure coding in improving storage efficiency in real-world environments. Our results will enable storage system practitioners to effectively deploy erasure coding and understand the design trade-offs with regard to different application scenarios. Our findings have been published in prestigious conference and journals.

419412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419412.value: The aim of this project is to develop a dynamic agent-based model which can automatically analyze human behavior from video streams captured in crowded environments, such as train stations, subways, shopping malls and airports. In recent years, behavior analysis in crowded environments has drawn increasing attentions in the computer vision community because of its wide industrial applications and important scientific values. In video surveillance, automatically detecting abnormal and dangerous behaviors plays an important role in ensuring public safety. In crowd control, recognizing traffic patterns and estimating traffic flows provide valuable information for avoiding congestion. The long-term statistical information from crowd behavior analysis provides guidelines for planning and designing crowded public areas in order to increase their safety and to optimize their traffic capacity. The collective behaviors of crowds show striking analogies with some self-organization phenomena observed in other social processes and other fields such as physics and biology. Therefore, automatic crowd behavior analysis also has scientific values in interdisciplinary fields. As an international city with a high population density, Hong Kong has a large demand for and also provides good opportunities for this type of research work. However, such research is highly challenging because of the frequent occlusions among objects and heavy scene clutters in crowded environments. Many existing works of behavior analysis are applicable only to sparse environments. We propose to develop a novel Mixture model of Dynamic pedestrian-Agents (MDA), which not only characterizes the global patterns of collective behaviors of pedestrians and their shared beliefs of origins and destinations at the macroscopic level but also the interactions among pedestrians at the microscopic level. The model can be reliably learned from the noisy and fragmented trajectories of pedestrians and has various applications, such as recognizing different types of behaviors including abnormal behaviors, predicting the behaviors of pedestrians and inferring their past behaviors if their trajectories are only partially observed, analyzing the personalities of pedestrians and their interactions, detecting stationary groups or obstacles which blocks the traffic, and simulating crowd behaviors in different scenarios. The outcome of this research will have significant impact on intelligent video surveillance, crowd control, traffic management and civil engineering. It will also provide powerful tools for the study of self-organization phenomena in social research and other fields. 項目的目的是開發一個可以自動分析群體行為的動態主體模型。模型可以用於分析火車站，地鐵，商場，機場等擁擠環境中拍攝的視頻流。 近年來，擁擠的環境中的行為分析，因為其廣泛的工業應用和重要的科學價值, 在計算機視覺界得到越來越多的關注. 在視頻監控中，自動檢測異常和危險的行為起著重要的作用，以確保公眾安全。在人群控制中，識別交通模式和估計值，交通流量，為避免交通擁塞估計值，提供了有價值的信息。從人群行為分析得到的長期統計信息為規劃和設計擁擠的公共場所提供重要指導. 從人群行為分析得到的長期統計信息為規劃和設計擁擠的公共場所提供重要指導. 人群的集體行為與其他社會進程和物理學和生物學中觀察到的一些自組織現象驚人類似。因此，人群行為分析在跨學科領域也有重要科學價值。因此，人群行為分析在跨學科領域也有重要科學價值。香港作為一個國際城市，人口密度高，對於這一研究有重大需求。然而，這一研究是極具挑戰性的，因為在擁擠的環境中對象之間遮擋頻繁。我們提出一個新的動態混合主體模型，它不僅在宏觀層面刻畫了行人的集體行為模式，和他們共同的起點和終點，並在微觀層面刻畫了行人之間的相互作用。該模型可以從嘈雜的和零散的行人運動軌跡學習得到，並有各種應用，如識別不同類型的行為，包括不正常的行為，預測行人的行為，並推斷他們過去的行為，分析行人之間的相互作用，並模擬人群在不同情況下的行為。 這項研究成果將對智能視頻監控，人群控制，交通管理，土木工程等領域產生重要影響. 它也將為研究社會科學領域的自組織現象提供強大的工具.

419412.label: Realisation of objectives
419412.value: All the objectives in this project have been realized successfully. (1) Modeling crowd behaviors has many important applications in video surveillance, traffic management and crowd control. It is particularly challenging because object detection and tracking fail frequently in crowded environments. Inspired by research in the science fields, a new Mixture model of Dynamic pedestrian-Agents (MDA) is proposed to jointly model the collective behaviors of pedestrians in crowd, their interactions, and beliefs [1]. This is the first time to jointly model these three key components in crowd scene understanding. From agent-based modeling, each pedestrian in the crowd is driven by a dynamic pedestrian-agent, which is a linear dynamic system with its initial and termination states reflecting the pedestrian’s belief of the starting point and the destination. Then the whole crowd is modeled as a mixture of dynamic pedestrian-agents. This model is well supported by inference and training algorithms, and theoretical analysis. In complete this theory, we added stationary crowd into this model [2-6]. Stationary crowd has very different impact on traffic and interaction than mobile pedestrians, but it was completely ignored in literature. Moreover, beyond collectiveness, we further propose other generic properties, such as uniformity, stability and conflict, to describe crowd systems [7-8] to enrich our model. Finally, set of 94 attributes describing “who”, “where”, and “why” of crowd events were proposed in [9]. (2) Once the model is unsupervisedly learned from real data, MDA has many applications. By modeling the process of pedestrians making decisions on actions, it can not only classify collective behaviors, but also simulate and predict collective crowd behaviors. Pedestrian behaviors are classified and abnormal behaviors are detected in [6]. In [1] and [4], it is used to simulate crowd behaviors. The future behaviors of pedestrian are accurately predicted in [4]. Stationary time of crowd is estimated in [2, 5]. The transition time of crowd flow between sources and sinks is estimated in [7]. The capability of predicting the trajectories of pedestrians with MDA makes it possible to improve crowd tracking. In [8, 9], crowd tracking has been much improved by modeling group structures in terms of the collective behaviors and interactions of pedestrians. Modeling crowd behaviors is also used by us to classify crowd videos [8-9] and predict the attributes of crowd videos [10-12]. The distributions of collectiveness and interactions in MDA are used as descriptors for video classification. Beyond MDA, deep learning is also explored to extract dynamic and appearance features. Crowd counting is another application studied in this project [13, 14]. (3) We have built multiple large scale crowd video benchmarks to compare with the sate-of-the-art methods in various applications. (3.1) The New York Grand Central dataset is built to learn MDA from trajectories, classify crowd trajectories and detect abnormal crowd activities [1]. (3.2) In [3], two datasets are built evaluate modeling the interactions between moving and stationary crowds. (3.3) In collaboration with Shanghai Jiaotong University, the Shanghai World Expo 2010 Crowd Dataset [15] is built for comprehensive evaluation of collectiveness, crowd counting and crowd tracking. It includes 2, 630 annotated video sequences captured with 245 surveillance cameras, far larger than any public datasets. (3.4) Another dataset of evaluating crowd collectiveness, stability, uniformity and conflict is built is [8, 9]. (3.5) A very large scale crowd attribute dataset is built in [10] to evaluate crowd video classification and attribute prediction. It includes over 10,000 crowd videos and annotations of 94 defined crowd attributes. Reference [1] B. Zhou, X. Tang, X. 419412.label: Major findings and research outcome
419412.value: As research outcome, 7 journal papers and 17 conference papers are published, and two postgraduate students obtained their PhD degree with their thesis on crowd understanding and modeling. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (PAMI), and International Journal of Computer Vision (IJCV) are the two best journals on computer vision and machine learning. We published two papers at PAMI and IJCV. 16 papers were published on the top three conferences on computer vision (CVPR, ICCV, and ECCV). Six large scale crowd datasets were built to evaluate the proposed models and compare with sate-of-the-art methods in various applications. Three demo systems of crowd simulation, crowd tracking, and crowd video classification were also built during the project. We find that modeling crowd collective behaviors, especially jointly with pedestrian interactions, and beliefs, can improve pedestrian behavior prediction and classification significantly. Mixture of dynamic agents (MDA) is especially suitable for addressing this problem (Part C.8 No.1). We also find that stationary crowd is very important for modeling traffic flow and interpreting interactions among pedestrians. It was not studied in the past literature. By adding it to the model, the performance has been further improved greatly (Part C.8, No.2 and 6, Part C.9, No. 2, 3 and 14). Beyond collectiveness, we also find other important generic properties and attributes to describe crowd systems and crowd videos (Part C.8, No. 4 and 5, Part C.9, No. 1). The proposed model has many important applications. It can be used to predict and simulate crowd behaviors (Part C.8, No. 1 and 6, Part C.9, No. 12), improve crowd tracking (Part C.8 No.7, Part C.9 No.17), classify crowd videos (Part C.8 No.4, Part C.9 No.1) and crowd attributes (Part C.8 No.5, Part C.9 No.10 and 11), and count the number of pedestrians in crowd (Part C.9 No. 15 and 16). We also built multiple benchmark crowd datasets to evaluate the proposed methods and compare with the state-of-the-art methods (Part C.8 No.1-4, 7, Part C. 9 No.11 and 15). They are much more larger than any existing crowd datasets in terms of size and diversity. Some annotations such as stationary crowd and crowded attributes were first proposed by us.

419412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
419412.value: Our research on crowd behavior understanding has a lot of potential on industrial applications, especially on video surveillance. Many public areas accumulate a large number of people, and traditional computer vision methods do not work well in such crowded environments. The research from this project provides new solutions. We are exploring opportunities of industrial applications and will also apply for funding from Innovation Technology Council to speedup the technology transfer. Crowd systems are also widely studied in physics, biology, and social science. In the future, we will deepen the study on the fundamental problems of crowd systems, and study their universal underlying mechanism. The research outcome of this project could be applied in these domains.

419412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419412.value: The goal this project is to model pedestrian behaviors in crowd. This problem is particularly challenging because there are frequent occlusions and the detection and tracking algorithms fail frequently. In this project, a brand new framework of Mixture model Dynamic pedestrian-Agents (MDA) was proposed. It is the first time to jointly model collective behaviors pedestrians, interactions among pedestrians and also their beliefs. It is also the first time to simultaneously consider stationary crowd and mobile crowd. Together with new inference and training algorithms, MDA is well learned. It has many important applications, including crowd simulation, crowd tracking, crowd behavior prediction and recognition, abnormality detection, crowd video classification, crowd attribute recognition, and crowd counting. Several very large scale crowd datasets with annotations are built. Comprehensive evaluation on these datasets show that the proposed methods output state-of-the-art substantially.
