419512.label: Project Objectives
419512.value: The PI will perform theoretical modeling on the effects of various material design factors (e.g., species of nanoparticles, nanoparticle size, size distribution, and volume concentration) on thermal properties of Antimonide-based nanocomposites. Both uncorrelated and correlated phonon scattering regimes will be studied. Extensive thermal conductivity characterizations will be conducted on Antimonide-based nanocomposites to validate the theoretical predictions. The PI believes that a combined theoretical and experimental study is the key to obtain a deeper understanding on thermal transport in complex nanostructured materials. By systematically examining thermal transport in the nanocomposite materials, we could develop generic material design rules on how to tune thermal properties by using nanostructures, which will advance our capabilities to develop new materials with tailored thermal properties.

419512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419512.value: The objective of the proposed research is to explore generic material design rules for engineering the thermal properties of nanostructured thermoelectric materials. The approach is to systematically examine thermal transport in a model system − Antimonide-based nanocomposites that consist of GaSb/InxGa1-xSb semiconductor embedded with lattice-matched Rare-Earth-Sb nanostructures with tunable size and spacing. Thermoelectric devices can work as both heat engines and refrigerators; however, to date their practical applications have been limited by their low efficiencies. Recently, several reports demonstrated significantly improved thermoelectric efficiencies either by engineering the thermoelectric materials into nanostructures (superlattices [1], nanowires [2, 3]) or by incorporating nanostructures in thin-film or bulk semiconductor matrix (quantum dots [4], nanocomposites [5-8]), primarily by reducing thermal conductivity without substantially deteriorating electron transport. Despite recent great breakthroughs, thermal transport in nanostructured thermoelectric materials has not been well understood yet. For example, it is not clear why some nanostructured materials show reduced thermal conductivities while others do not. As a result, current research on developing nanostructured thermoelectric materials with reduced thermal conductivity is largely empirical based. Therefore, general material design rules to engineer thermal properties of nanostructured materials are currently in urgent need. In order to address the aforementioned issue, the PI proposes to study how to use nanostructures to tune thermal properties in an Antimonide-based nanocomposite system. Our preliminary studies have shown that thermal conductivity of InxGa1-xSb alloy can be reduced by 20% with the incorporation of 0.8 vol% ErSb nanoparticles. In this project, we will investigate, through systematic modeling and experiments, how phonon transport in nanocomposites is affected by various material design factors including chemical composition of nanoparticles, nanoparticle size, size distribution, and nanoparticle concentration. The ultimate goal of the project is to develop generic material design rules that can be used to create novel materials with tailored thermal properties. Thermal transport plays a significant role in the entire energy production, utilization, storage, and management processes. The proposed research will provide previously unavailable data to understand the fundamentals of phonon transport in nanostructured materials. The generally applicable material design rules developed in this work will significantly enhance our capability to tune thermal properties of nanostructured materials; this will not only benefit the development of high efficiency thermoelectric devices but also facilitate designing integrated thermal management solutions in advanced electronic and photonic devices. 本項目致力於探討改善納米結構熱電材料傳熱特性的通用材料設計規則。研究方法為系統地研究基於銻化物納米複合材料的傳熱特性。所研究的材料為在GaSb/InGaSb半導體基底材料中摻雜有晶格匹配、尺寸及間距可變的Rare-Earth-Sb納米結構。 熱電器件可用作熱機和冰箱，但迄今為止，其實際應用受限於較低的工作效率。近來研究表明將熱電材料加工成納米結構（超晶格、納米線）或在薄膜及體態半導體材料中摻雜納米結構（量子點、納米複合材料）可有效提升熱電轉換效率。這主要歸功於納米結構可顯著降低材料的導熱係數但同時又不會大幅度影響電子輸運特性。儘管近年來熱電研究已取得了一些突破，但納米結構熱電材料的導熱特性還沒有得到很好地研究。例如，我們還不清楚為何有些納米材料的導熱係數降低了但有些則沒有。結果導致目前低導熱係數納米熱電材料的開發主要是靠經驗。因此探討可有效改善納米材料傳熱特性的通用材料設計規則非常必要。 為了解決上述問題，本申請人擬研究如何利用納米結構來改變基於銻化物納米複合材料體系的傳熱特性。我們的初步研究表明摻雜體積比為0.8%的ErSb納米顆粒可將InGaSb合金的導熱係數降低20%。在本項目中，我們將以系統的模擬及實驗為手段探討各種材料設計參數對納米複合材料中聲子輸運特性的影響，其中包括納米顆粒的化學成分、納米顆粒的大小、粒度分佈及納米顆粒的濃度。本項目的最終目標是開發通用的材料設計規則，進而可用於創造具有量身定制熱性能的新型材料。 熱輸運在整個能源生產、利用、儲存及管理過程中起到了重要的作用。本研究將為深入理解納米材料中聲子輸運過程提供前所未有的實驗數據。另外，所得到的普遍適用的材料設計規則將顯著提升改變納米材料傳熱特性的能力，這將不僅有利於發展高效率的熱電器件也有助於先進電子及光子器件中集成熱處理解決方案的設計。

419512.label: Major findings and research outcome
419512.value: - We have theoretically and experimentally examined thermal transport in the MBE-grown InGaSb alloys and ErSb:InGaSb nanocomposites. It is shown that ErSb nanoparticles can effectively reduce thermal conductivity of the InGaSb matrix and can potentially enhance thermoelectric figure of merit of nanocomposites. The reduced thermal conductivity is attributed to the stiffness and density contrast between ErSb and InGaSb. As a result, ErSb nanoparticles serve as effective phonon scattering centers and hinder the transport of mid-to-long wavelength phonons. (Publication #1) - We have set up a differential three omega system for thermal conductivity measurements of thin films. The developed experimental system is extensively used to characterize thermal conductivity of InGaSb nanocomposites. With the developed experimental tool, we further studied thermal transport in the c-axis of graphite thin films and revealed that phonon mean free path of the c-axis graphite is as long as 200 nm at room temperature. (Publication #2) - In addition to the InGaSb nanocomposites, we further examined thermoelectric properties of other nanostructured thermoelectric materials including GaZnSb nanocomposites and Bi2Se3 nanoribbons. GaZnSb nanocomposites are prepared by a combined ball milling and hot pressing approach, which can significantly bring down the materials synthesis cost compare to the MBE. Our study shows that thermal conductivity of the hot pressed GaZnSb samples is effectively reduced and overall thermoelectric figure of merit of nanocomposites is enhanced compared to the bulk sample without nanostructures. Thermoelectric figure of merit of Bi2Se3 nanoribbons is found to be as high as 0.17 at 320 K which is two to three times higher than the value for the bulk materials. (Publication #3)

419512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
419512.value: The success of the project shows that embedding ErSb nanoparticles in InGaSb alloys is an effective route to reduce thermal conductivity of nanocomposites and possibly enhance thermoelectric figure of merit. We planned to further extend this idea to develop nanocomposites by ball milling the raw materials into nanoparticles and further hot pressing them into fully dense nanocomposites with embedded grain boundaries. Our preliminary study on GaZnSb nanocomposites shows that thermal conductivity of the hot pressed samples is effectively reduced and overall thermoelectric figure of merit of nanocomposites is enhanced compared to the bulk sample without nanostructures.

419512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419512.value: In this project, we have extensively studied thermal transport in nanoparticle-in-alloy nanocomposites by both theoretical modeling and experimental studies. Our study shows that embedding nanoparticles in the alloy matrix is an effective approach to reduce thermal conductivity and possibly enhance thermoelectric figure of merit. This project also revealed the possible materials design rules for reducing thermal conductivity of nanocomposites. First, the composition of the alloy should be optimized to reach the alloy limit of thermal conductivity. Second, nanoparticles with high stiffness and density contrast with the matrix are highly effective in terms of reducing thermal conductivity of nanocomposites. Beyond the nanoparticle-in-alloy nanocomposites, we first explored the nanoparticle-nanoparticle nanocomposites, which are synthesized by hot pressing nanoparticles into the fully dense composite materials. Our study indicates that thermal conductivity of the hot pressed nanocomposites is also effectively reduced and as a result overall thermoelectric figure of merit of nanocomposites is enhanced compared to the bulk sample without nanostructures.

419612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419612.value: 基因組由長序列的脫氧核榶核酸（deoxyribonucleic acid, DNA）所組成。人類的遺傳病由基因組變異所引致。這些把病患者和常人區分出來的遺傳變異以不同的形式出現，由單位置的替換（SNPs, single nucleotide polymorphisms）到大範圍的結構性變化不等。現今社會流行的複雜遺傳病當中，很多致病的變異還未被清楚瞭解，而且相信它們殊不簡單。舉例來 說，有很多遺傳病異已被發現與二型糖尿病有關，但這些變異每一項只稍微增加患病的風險，而即使把它們一併考慮也只能解釋此病一小部份的遺傳性。為 了大規模地比較病人和常人的生物樣本，全基因組關聯實驗 （genome-wide association studies, GWAS）採用了諸如SNP晶片等高效率測試分法來同時間檢查多至一百萬個SNP是否出現於這些樣本當中。很多時透過這些實驗大量與疾病有統計關連的遺傳 變異會被發現。可是，這些變異不少是處於非編碼區域（即並不生產蛋白質的區域），因此它們所造成的影響不甚清楚。有愈來愈多的證據顯示位於這些區 域的遺傳變異可能對疾病的形成擔當著重要的角色，例如影響到非編碼核糖核酸（non-coding RNAs, ncRNAs）的運作和干擾到有如蛋白質接合等具協調功效的序列。基於我們過往在國際研究公會ENCODE (Encyclopedia of DNA Elements)和modENCODE (model organism ENCODE)裡，從非編碼區域中有系統地找尋功能因子的經驗，我們提議建立一套整合的電腦系統來搜尋和分析與疾病有關的非編碼遺傳變異。建立這套系統的 主要目的是整合不同類型的資訊，來幫助生物醫學研究員去評估個別遺傳變異對疾病擔當功能角色的可能性。我們會搜集各種從新近大型排序計劃中產生的 公共全基因組數據，包括蛋 白質接合，基因活躍度，組蛋白變化（histone modifications），DNA開放度，以及DNA三維長距離交互作用。我們會利用這些數據作特徵來調整我們會較早前建立的機器學習方法，以在人類 基因組非編碼區域中預測具協調功效的序列、它們影響的基因，以及可能產生非編碼核榶核酸的地方。我們亦會從公共數據庫和我們的研究伙伴那裡搜集和 疾病有關的數據，來找出與疾病有統計關連的非編碼遺傳變異。然後，我們會把我們的預測結果和其他現有的方法結合，如序列基元（sequence motif）分析和小核榶核酸影響目標估測，來評估每一個這些遺傳變異對基因協調的影響。我們會妥善整理所搜集到的數據和估測結果以便查閱。我們會把所建立的電腦系統公開成為一個共用的資源，讓生物醫學研究員分析他們各自的數據，同時也會和我們於本地一所醫院的研究伙伴合作，利用這套系統 來分析一些在本地具重要性的疾病的遺傳變異，包括二型榶尿病、肝癌和鼻咽癌。

419612.label: Realisation of objectives
419612.value: For Objective 1, we have used statistical modeling to identify functional distal regulatory modules (DRMs) based on epigenomic information. We have developed methods for associating these DRMs with potential target genes based on the extent of their features that can explain the expression level of the genes. For Objective 2, we have integrated a large number of features of different types to identify non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs). Based on some annotated ncRNAs, we have predicted novel ncRNAs and identified a succinct set of key features of ncRNAs across multiple species. For Objective 3, we have integrated different types of information to annotate non-coding genetic variants. The effects of these variants have been predicted based on the various types of signals at the variant site and its flanking regions, such as evolutionary conservation and histone modifications. For Objectives 4 and 5, we have developed the Variant Annotation System (VAS) for large-scale annotation of genetic variants based on both public and user-supplied data. VAS has been running as a server application, with a backend database containing a large amount of commonly-used signal tracks (Objective 4) and a Web user interface for annotating genetic variants uploaded by the user (Objective 5). For Objective 6, we have used the system on our collaborative projects related to the listed diseases. Our system has contributed to the corresponding RGC-funded collaborative projects, including two Theme-based Research Scheme (T12-402/13N and T12-401/13-R) and one Collaborative Research Fund (C4017-14G).

419612.label: Major findings and research outcome
419612.value: This project has led to the development of the Variant Annotation System (VAS) and corresponding research about non-coding genetic variants, including regulatory elements at non-coding regions and non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs). Regarding regulatory elements, we have investigated the relative contributions of epigenomic features at coding and non-coding regions to gene expression, showing that gene body methylation is as important as promoter methylation in indicating expression levels. Regarding ncRNAs, we have identified a common set of features important for identifying ncRNAs across multiple species, based on a large collection of data from public sources. We have also developed a method that can improve the prediction of RNA secondary structures based on high-throughput structure-probing data. Overall, the project has led to the publication of 6 peer-reviewed articles in academic journals (1 in Bioinformatics, 2 in BMC Genomics, 1 in Genome Biology and 2 in Nucleic Acids Research). The project has helped strengthened our collaboration with the research group of Prof. John Lu at Tsinghua University, as well as our collaborations with multiple research groups in Hong Kong that study various types of genetic diseases. The system we have developed and the research findings that we have obtained from this project have been contributing to the research projects of these groups. The project fund has been used to train 2 MPhil students and 3 undergraduate students.

419612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
419612.value: One important aspect of this project is the identification of genes regulated by a distal regulatory region. This is an important topic and a lot of new developments have been seen in this research area since the beginning of the current project. There are still important parts of this distal regulatory system not yet fully explored in this project, such as the joint regulation of a gene by multiple regulatory elements. These novel parts have been proposed as a new GRF project and it has been recently funded (CUHK14145916). More findings about gene regulatory networks are expected from this new project. Another important aspect is the application of the VAS system in analyzing disease data. In addition to the existing collaborations in diabetes, liver cancer and nasopharyngeal carcinoma, we will seek other collaborations aiming at both applying our developed methods to help study disease genetic variants and getting feedback to improve our methods.

419612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419612.value: High-throughput experimental methods such as microarrays and massively parallel sequencing have enabled the discovery of many genetic variants that are statistically associated with various diseases. However, many of these variants are not directly disrupting protein sequences, but rather in non-protein-coding regions, the biological significance of which is far less clear. Trying to understand these non-coding disease variants is currently one of the top priorities in biomedical research. Our project has contributed toward the tackling of this grand challenge by 1) providing a computer system that provides many types of information about these variants, 2) investigating the relative importance of different classes of genomic regions in quantitatively affecting gene expression, and 3) developing methods for identifying non-coding RNAs (RNAs that do not code for proteins) and predicting their structures, which are critical for their functions.

440412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
440412.value: 媒體、社會組織、政府和社會記憶： 以「公共競爭」模型分析天安門事件在香港的集體回憶 陳韜文 李立峯 綱要 本計劃旨在研究天安門事件的集體回憶如何在香港被建構、角力以及植根，從而了解香港社會如何塑造歷史記憶。 在2009年6月4日，超過十萬名香港人參與燭光晚會，紀念天安門事件二十週年，吸引傳媒大量報道。往後數年的集會人數也同樣觸目。這都證明港人仍未忘記這件在1989年發生的慘劇。本研究以「六四事件」為個案，研究香港如何塑造社會記憶。推而廣之，我們也藉香港的個案，去了解一個社會是如何將歷史記憶保存 ─ 有些甚麼可以代代相傳，又有些甚麼會被淹沒掉。本研究具體關注的問題是：為什麼香港人認為天安門事件值得紀念？經過這麼多年，有甚麼驅使港人仍不遺忘天安門事件？塑造社會記憶的因素包括甚麼？塑造社會記憶的過程為何？ 本研究在社會和理論層面都有著重要性。在社會層面，「六四事件」在香港一直是一個政治象徵、是敏感的議題，也是一個長期困擾中國政府的歷史問題。在理論層面，本研究提出一個政治傳播學的「公共競爭」模型（public contestation model），作集體回憶分析之用。根據這個模型，我們會研究下列問題： （一） 媒體在建構集體回憶的角色； （二） 社運組織在促進和植根集體回憶的角色； （三） 政府影響公共論述的權力及其局限； （四） 集體回憶作為社會建構，如何回應和處理歷史的「客觀事實」 具體而言，「公共競爭」模型認為，集體回憶的建構和植根是各種社會力量在公共領域角力的結果。公眾是集體回憶的主要展示場所，而政府、媒體和社會組織則是「公共競爭」的主要參與者。既然集體回憶是「公共競爭」的結果，這即是說它是可以改變的，甚至可被「製造」的。不過，在「公共競爭」模型底下，集體回憶的社會建構性是受到事件的特性所約制的，是以不能完全偏離歷史事實。此外，本研究強調，香港整體的社會和政治環境也會影響到各種社會力量在「公共競爭」中的動態及最終角力的結果。

440412.label: Realisation of objectives
440412.value: The project has achieved its objectives through a range of empirical studies, including textual and content analyses of news coverage and media discourses, in-depth interviews with movement leaders and commemoration vigil participants, a survey of the Hong Kong public about their memories of historical events and attitudes toward June 4, as well as a couple of protest onsite surveys conducted during the June 4 candlelight vigils. Specifically, the textual and discourse analysis allow us to look into the processes through which collective memories about the Tiananmen Incident were promoted by movement organizations, sometimes apparently with the aid of mainstream media organizations, We developed an analysis of what we now call "memory mobilization" - the process through which collective memories are brought to the fore in public discourses for the purpose of social mobilization. Analysis of media discourses surrounding key controversies about the Tiananmen Incident allowed us to examine how memories were contested by different parties in the public arena in order to serve their own ideological and political interests. Meanwhile, in-depth interviews with the vigil participants and the public opinion survey provided us with data regarding to what extent the vigil participants, supposedly belonging to the mnemonic community surrounding Tiananmen, as well as ordinary citizens pick up the ideas, discourses, and counter-discourses surrounding Tiananmen commemoration. Those data also allow us to update our earlier analysis and findings regarding generational differences and generational transmission of collective memory. Notably, when the project was underway, the Umbrella Movement emerged in late 2014. Although the Umbrella Movement is a "separate" social movement with its own goal and dynamics, memories of Tiananmen also played an important role in the process. We therefore also allocated some resources from this project to conduct an onsite survey of the protesters of the Umbrella Movement, and in part of the survey we asked the respondents their views of Tiananmen and their understanding of whether and how Tiananmen related to the Umbrella Movement. We also conducted a qualitative analysis of media discourses that tied Tiananmen and Umbrella Movement together. From this analysis we also gained an understanding of how ongoing events and social political dynamics can alter the society's collective memory in unexpected manners. We developed an analysis of not only how the past was evoked to influence the present, but also how the present influenced memories of the past. There is no simple one-to-one relationship between the specific studies conducted and the objectives listed in the application. But when the various studies and findings are put together, the project did allow us to fulfill the various objectives.

440412.label: Major findings and research outcome
440412.value: Many of the core findings and research outcome of the project are presented in the five journal articles produced up to now (see Part C). The articles present our analyses of various mechanisms and processes involved in the reproduction, negotiation, and contestation of collective memory surrounding Tiananmen. The article published in the Journal of Contemporary China presented an analysis of the process of generational transmission of collective memory of Tiananmen in Hong Kong, which is crucial to the long-term perpetuation of the memory as the mnemonic community needs to incorporate young people into it. The analysis shows that young people acquire the collective memory of the historical event through various socialization mechanisms. The article published in Media, Culture & Society as well as the one under review at a public opinion studies journal are concerned with the process of memory mobilization. The premise of the analysis is that, although many Hong Kong people tend to treat Tiananmen as an important historical event, collective memory about the event needs to be brought to the fore so that people would actually take actions and participate in the annual commemoration. The two articles tackle the problematic of memory mobilization through analyzing media discourses and individual citizens' attitudes and cognitions respectively. The article published in Telematics and Informatics address the more specific topic of the role digital media played in the mobilization processes behind the annual vigil. It is argued that digital media allowed a more effective exercise of participation leadership on the part of the most active and concerned citizens, thus strengthening the capability of citizen self-mobilization. Finally, the article recently accepted for publication by Memory Studies provides an analysis of how memory of Tiananmen was invoked, contested, and finally largely abandoned during the Umbrella Movement. The analysis showed how historical memories about a past event could be brought to bear on current happenings, and yet also how current happenings, under certain conditions, could force the society to re-evaluate its understanding of the past (or the relevance of the past). The project's findings and outcome are not limited to the above articles. Analyses of the data and materials are still on-going. The investigators expect that more output will be produced in the near future.

440412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
440412.value: As mentioned earlier, recent political developments in Hong Kong, especially since the 2014 Umbrella Movement, has significantly affected how Hong Kong people related themselves to the Tiananmen Incident. In the most recent years, there are strong voices against commemorating June 4 coming from not the state or the pro-government faction, but from the "localist faction" within the oppositional forces. The current project, in other words, has allowed us to come to terms with the perpetuation of collective memory of June 4 in the period before 2014, as well as some data pertinent to the "new era of contestation" of June 4 memory after 2014. Continual monitoring of the situation and additional research and analysis would certainly be valuable.

440412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
440412.value: The Tiananmen Incident in 1989 not only constituted a critical event in the history of China and Hong Kong, it has also occupied an important place in Hong Kong people’s collective memory. Every year, tens of thousands of citizens would gather in the Victoria Park on the 4th of June to commemorate the tragic ending of the student movement. Several questions thus arise: why do Hong Kong people keep commemorating the event? How is collective memory about the Tiananmen Incident constructed, reproduced, negotiated, and sometimes contested in the society? How does the collective memory about Tiananmen influence current political happenings? This project addresses such questions by employing multiple research methods, including surveys of the general public, on-site surveys of participants in the June 4 vigils, in-depth interviews with participants of the June 4 vigils, analysis of media coverage and texts, etc. We developed analyses regarding the memory mobilization processes behind the commemoration activities, how collective memory about the event was contested in the public sphere, and how collective memory about Tiananmen relate to how people deal with current events such as the Umbrella Movement. These analyses are reported in several published studies, and there shall be additional publications to come.

440812.label: Project Objectives
440812.value: To conduct a literature review on recent developments of linear and nonlinear multivariate time-series modelling, outliers in vector time series and multivariate robust estimation methods. 440812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
440812.value: Discrete univariate time-series models have been using for modelling many dynamic economic and financial variables (such as equity returns, interest rates, unemployment rates, foreign exchange rates, GDP series, among many others). Particularly, the class of linear ARMA (autoregressive moving-average) processes has been reasonably successful as a practical tool for characterising and forecasting these variables. On the other hand, many nonlinear time-series models have been proposed in the literature. Nonlinear time-series processes often have the advantage of being able to capture jumps, asymmetries, volatility clustering and time irreversibility which are ‘stylised’ facts observed in many economic and financial time series. Recently, economic globalisation and advancement of computer technologies have accelerated the development of multivariate time-series analysis. Jointly modelling of several time-series variables together allows an analyst not only to study the serial correlation of a single time-series, but also to examine the contemporaneous and lead-lag dynamics among variables (for examples, the price-volume relationship of a trading asset, and the dynamics between sales volume and advertising expenditure of a product). Analogous to the univariate situation, classes of multivariate nonlinear time-series models, such as multivariate GARCH (Generalized AutoRegressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity) models and multivariate threshold processes, have been proposed in the literature. Various statistical tests for linearity in a univariate time-series are available in the literature. It is well-known that there is always a possibility of confounding effects between outliers and nonlinear dynamics of a univariate time-series. Robustness properties of several nonlinearity tests have been well studied and it can be shown that erroneous test results might lead to misspecified prediction problems. To alleviate the adverse effects of outliers, outlier-resistant versions of univariate tests for nonlinearity have been developed. Some of the univariate tests have been generalised to testing for nonlinearity in a vector time-series. However, all of them are based on multivariate least-squares estimation techniques which are sensitive to outliers. In this research, we shall consider two commonly used tests for nonlinearity in a vector time series. The first one is a test for multivariate threshold-type of nonlinearity and the second one is for Volterra-series-type of nonlinearity. We shall investigate the robustness of these two tests to outlying observations. Robustified version of these two tests will be proposed and their asymptotic null distributions will be derived. Monte Carlo experiments will be carried out to compare the power of the proposed tests and the existing tests under the influence of vector time-series outliers. 單維時間序列模型已經廣泛使用於經濟和金融變量建模（如股票回報率，利率，失業率，匯率，GDP系列，等等）建模之上。特別是線性ARMA（自回歸移動平均）模型，相當成功作為一種實用工具建模預測這些常用的經濟和金融變。另一方面，在研究文獻中亦已經提出了許多非線性時間序列模型的理論及應用。非線性時間序列通常都具有的優點是能夠捕捉跳躍，不對稱，波動聚類和時間的不可逆性，這是“風格化”的表徵在許多經濟和金融時間序列中是經常觀察到的事實。 近年來，經濟全球化和計算機技術的進步，加快發展了多元時間序列分析。將多個時間序列變量共同建模，可允許分析師不僅能研究各單一的時間序列互相關，也同期審查超和前滯後變量之間的動態（例如，股票市場的量價關係，銷量和廣告開支間之互動性）。類似單維分析，多元非線性時間序列模型，如多元GARCH（廣義自回歸條件異方差）模型和多元閾值的隨機過程，在文獻中已經提出。 在文獻中有各種單變量時間序列的線性統計測試。眾所周知，一個異常值巳經能完全可能破壞這些統計測試。幾個單元非線性魯棒測試已被學者們深入地研究，它可以顯示出錯誤的測試結果可能會導致誤設預測問題。為了減輕異常值的不利影響，單元非線性魯棒測試版本已經制定出來。 一些單變量的測試已推廣到測試多維時間序列的非線性。然而，所有這些都是基於多元最小二乘估計, 這方法對異常值點非常敏感。在今項研究中，我們將考慮兩種常用的測試多維時間序列的非線性。第一個是一個多元閾值類型的非線性，第二個是為Volterra級數型的非線性測試。我們將研究這兩個測試的魯棒性。這兩個魯棒測試版本將被提出並得到的漸近空分佈。蒙特卡洛實驗將進行比較每個擬議測試在多維時間序列異常值的影響下的測試功率。

440812.label: Realisation of objectives
440812.value: Objective 1: Literature review on recent developments of linear and nonlinear multivariate time-series modelling, outliers in vector time series and multivariate robust estimation methods has been conducted. Based on the review, two papers which focused on the applications of nonlinear multivariate time-series modelling have been written (see Part C of this report). Objectives 2-4: New and robust MTAR-type nonlinearity tests have been examined (see the references in Part C of this report), and we derived the asymptotic null distributions of the test statistics. A Monte Carlo experiment is carried out to compare the power of the proposed test with that of the least squares-based test under the influence of additive time series outliers. The results indicate that the proposed method is preferable to the classical test when observations are contaminated by outliers. Finally, we provide illustrative examples by applying the statistical tests to two real datasets.

440812.label: Major findings and research outcome
440812.value: Recently, economic globalization and advancement of computer technologies have accelerated the development of multivariate time-series analysis. Jointly modelling of several time-series variables together allows an analyst not only to study the serial correlation of a single time-series, but also to examine the contemporaneous and lead-lag dynamics among variables (for examples, the price-volume relationship of a trading asset, and the dynamics between sales volume and advertising expenditure of a product). Ng et al. (2013) applied multivariate time-series techniques to pricing options on stocks denominated in different currencies. Furthermore, Li et al. (2015) quantified financial risk (extreme outliers) in Chinese stock markets under a multivariate threshold autoregression. Previous studies on univariate time series analysis show that classical nonlinearity tests are often not robust to additive outliers. The outlier problem is expected to pose similar difficulties for multivariate nonlinearity tests under Vector Threshold Autoregression. Chan et al (2015) proposed a new and robust MTAR-type nonlinearity test, and derived the asymptotic null distribution of the test statistic. A Monte Carlo experiment was carried out to compare the power of the proposed test with that of the least squares-based test under the influence of additive time series outliers. The results indicated that the proposed method is preferable to the classical test when observations are contaminated by outliers. Finally, we provided illustrative examples by applying the statistical tests to two real datasets.

440812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
440812.value: It should be noted that the MTAR model in Chan et al. (2015) assumes a full transition from one regime to the other, specified by the binary indicator function. Another class of popular multivariate nonlinear processes, called multivariate smooth transition autoregressive (MSTAR) models, however, asserts a continuum of regimes, and the dynamic behaviour of the vector time series changes smoothly between regimes governed by a transition function. Various Lagrange multiplier (LM) tests and general power expansion tests have been proposed for testing MSTAR-type nonlinearity. Most of these tests can be performed using OLS vector regressions, and they are therefore likely to be adversely affected by outlying observations as in the univariate situation. An interesting future research direction would be to explore the possibility of robustifying the LM tests by replacing the OLS vector regressions with the RMLTS estimates discussed in Chan et al. (2015). Research in this direction is in process.

440812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
440812.value: In recent years, there has been growing interest in nonlinear multivariate time-series models in economics and finance. The rapid development of complex theoretical models of economic and financial phenomena has exposed the deficiency of the approximations that are provided by linear systems. And the growth in computing power experienced in recent years has made it feasible to estimate higher dimension and wider range of nonlinear vector time-series models. The class of threshold autoregressive models (TAR) has been widely applied in practice to explain various empirical economic and financial phenomena. Recent financial crises, political instabilities and natural disasters might have created aberrant data that are inconsistent with the rest of the observed time-series. Multivariate time-series analysis (linear or nonlinear) based on contaminated vector observations might lead to erroneous inferences and conclusions. This research project has made significant contributions in two main areas. First, we quantity impacts of multivariate outlier of various types on vector TAR modelling with applications to financial risk management. Second, we developed a new robust test for multivariate threshold-type nonlinearity and demonstrated that this test is useful in practice.

441512.label: Project Objectives
441512.value: To expand and refine a set of theory-driven and research-based intervention programs of learning to read in Chinese for at-risk readers focusing on various aspects of lexical knowledge for word identification with integrated activities for vocabulary building, fluency development and comprehension enhancement. To examine the immediate effectiveness of the first level of the intervention program ERIC at the end of grade one in terms of student performance in word identification, reading fluency and reading comprehension. To examine the cumulative effectiveness of the set of intervention programs (ERIC with ERICA/ERICA+) at the end of grade two for low responders in terms of student performance in word identification, reading fluency and reading comprehension. To examine and compare the long-term impact of the two levels of intervention programs (ERIC vs. ERIC and ERICA/ERICA+; TSP vs ERICA/ERICA+) upon student outcomes in terms of word identification, reading fluency and reading comprehension at the end of grade three. To compare the effects of the two forms of extended intervention (ERICA vs. ERICA+) in delivering reading intervention in grade two and its implications for implementation of extensive intervention programs.

441512.label: Realisation of objectives
441512.value: Objective 1 was successfully completed. The intervention program “Early Reading Intervention in Chinese” (ERIC) for first graders and the intervention program “Early Reading Intervention in Chinese – Advanced” (ERICA) for second graders were developed and tried out with two cohorts of subjects. Teacher feedback was obtained and refinements were made to produce a combined package for long-term use in local schools. Further description of the package will be reported in the subsequent research output section. Objectives 2, 3, 4 and 5 were fully achieved through a careful implementation of the interventions in seven local primary schools in 2012 – 2014 for cohort 1 students, in 2013-15 for cohort 2 students and with a follow-up investigation for maintenance in the end of the school year of 2014- 2015 for cohort 1 students. For Objective 2, program effectiveness of the first level of the intervention program ERIC at the end of grade one was examined. Moderate effect sizes were obtained in character reading fluency (0.39), graded word identification (0.32), Curriculum-based assessment of word identification (0.47), and curriculum-based assessment of character dictation (0.26). Growth modeling analyses also indicated similar patterns of results after controlling the effect of age, IQ and school differences. With respect to Objective 3, the cumulative effectiveness of the set of intervention programs (ERIC with ERICA/ERICA+) at the end of grade two for low responders in terms of student performance in word identification, reading fluency and reading comprehension was less impressive. Only small effect sizes were obtained in character reading fluency (0.22) and curriculum-based assessment of word identification (0.25). No significant improvement was observed in graded word identification, curriculum-based assessment of character dictation and reading comprehension. The issue of low responders needs to be further addressed in future studies. With regard to Objective 4, the long-term impact of the two levels of intervention programs (ERIC vs. ERIC and ERICA/ERICA+; TSP vs ERICA/ERICA+) upon student outcomes at the end of grade three, it was found that students who could catch up after one year of intervention (ERIC) were able to maintain reading fluency at grade level and achieved at the marginal level in terms of graded character identification (with graded standard scores in the 90 range). Low responders, in spite of having ERIC and ERICA/ERICA+ intervention support, remained significantly behind by the end of grade three. It seems that these students might be classified as difficult-to-remediate students and that more intensive and individualized intervention should be offered. Our two levels of intervention were of the same intensity (i.e., approximately 40-hours each year/level). In other words, future studies should take both learning level and instructional intensity into consideration when designing differential intervention programs. Finally, regarding Objective 5, no significant differences were obtained when comparing the effects of the two forms of extended intervention (ERICA vs. ERICA+) in delivering reading intervention in grade two. ERICA+ included additional paraprofessional support with repeated practice coached by paraprofessionals twice a week for about 15 minutes each time for about 20 weeks. It was speculated that lack of intervention intensity for the additional component might still be the key reason of the non-significant results.

441512.label: Major findings and research outcome
441512.value: First, our intervention programs were theory driven and research based. A meta-analysis on the role of phonological awareness in Chinese character recognition was submitted for publication and the revised version was in the final process of approval for publication (Part C Research Output, item 8, no.1). Second, measures of word identification and reading fluency were constructed to measure intervention program effectiveness. In view of the absence of standardized Chinese word identification and fluency tests in Hong Kong, we developed a standardized Chinese character identification scale (HKGCCIT) and a character fluency reading test (SCRFT) with local norms based on a database of Hong Kong Chinese primary school texts. The developments of these measures were presented in international conferences on reading in 2013 and in 2015 (Part C Research Output, item 9, no.1 and no.2). Third, teacher training is essential for intervention success. We were able to develop a tiered model of teacher professional development for supporting students with literacy difficulties. The model of teacher development was presented in an international conference in November 2014 (Part C, item 9, no.3). Fourth, we were able to refine our intervention programs, ERIC and ERICA, into an integrated intervention program package named Step by Step Literacy 《語文童步》with a set of curriculum materials sequenced into four difficulty levels (i.e., four booklets, from level 1 to level 4, with reading passages, student activities, and worksheets) and a set of supporting materials (a teacher’s teaching guide, four sets of CDs of sound recordings of the lessons in both Cantonese and Putonghua, one CD of supporting resources for teacher to download for use). The development of the intervention package was presented in an international conference in July 2015 (Part C, item 9, no.4). Finally, plans for conference presentation and publication of the research study were made. The results of the first phase of the study were reported in an international conference in April 2015 (Part C, item 9, no.5). The results of the two phases of the study were analyzed and the report of the whole research is under preparation for journal publication.

441512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
441512.value: Two major areas of future research are suggested. While the present study demonstrates that early reading intervention in grade one is effective for some students and they could maintain relatively satisfactory performance in subsequent years, there is still a group of inadequate responders who show persistent reading difficulties after two years of intervention. A comprehensive study of the cognitive profiles of adequate and inadequate responders may help shaping the directions for future intervention research. Another area of research that deserves more attention is the issue of intervention intensity. One limitation of the present study is that we did not provide our level two of intervention (i.e., the ERICA program) with increasing intensity due to difficulties with time scheduling in local schools. It appears that students who display persistently inadequate response in the level one of intervention should be given more intensive interventions by decreasing group size and/or increasing instruction time. With our program package Step by Step Literacy made available to all local primary schools, future researchers are encouraged to make use of the package to experiment different forms and duration of intervention to support those who are in need of timely intervention.

441512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
441512.value: Reading research has shown that children who have a poor start in reading are very likely to continue to be poor readers in subsequent schooling years. This longitudinal research investigated the effectiveness of a tiered model of early reading intervention in Chinese for improving student outcomes. In particular, we developed two levels of curriculum materials for grade-one and grade-two poor readers: ERIC (Early Reading Intervention in Chinese) and ERICA (Early Reading Intervention in Chinese – Advanced). The differential effects of these programs were examined. The effect of additional paraprofessional support (ERICA+) was also investigated. The results showed that students who showed adequate response after one year of intervention were able to maintain their performance after intervention. However, a particular group of low responders, in spite of having ERIC and ERICA/ERICA+ intervention support, remained significantly behind by the end of grade three. The overall results of the study indicated that more research efforts should be made to examine the cognitive characteristics of those who display persistent reading difficulties and further investigate the effectiveness of intensive intervention matching student cognitive profiles. With our intervention programs packaged into an integrated package Step by Step Literacy made available for public access, this study opens a window for more intervention studies in Chinese in the years to come.

441812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
441812.value: This proposed study examines the causal effect of personality, social influences and collective efficacy on the development of career self-efficacy, and the subsequent formation of vocational identity among Chinese high school students from Hong Kong, Shanghai and rural Zhejiang. Senior high school is an important stage for early vocational development during which adolescents establish their career self-efficacy and vocational identity. Longitudinal studies of adolescents’ vocational development show that personality and environmental factors contribute to the crystallization of vocational interests, career self-efficacy and vocational identity in a dynamic process. However, western models of vocational development have focused primarily on individual predictors (personality, interests and self-efficacy). In our ongoing cross-cultural study, we found that among Chinese adolescents, vocational development involves both self-efficacy and collective efficacy based on the influence of parents, school, and peers. Using a 3-wave longitudinal design, we propose to follow students from Senior 1 (Grade 10) to Senior 3 (Grade 12) to test the mediational effects of collective and self-efficacy on the temporal causality from the personality and social predictors to vocational identity and commitment. We adopt the Cross-cultural (Chinese) Personality Assessment Inventory for Adolescents (CPAI-A) to highlight the additional contributions of emic interpersonal personality dimensions to supplement the universal individual-oriented traits found in western studies. We add collective career efficacy to the self-efficacy model of vocational behavior to strengthen the cultural relevance of the model to the Chinese context. Using samples from three Chinese regions varying in stages of modernization and socioeconomic backgrounds, we predict stronger contributions from interpersonal personality traits and familial influences to career efficacy among more traditional rural Chinese students as their vocational identity crystallizes in senior high school. We expect increasing gender differences from the rural sample with female students lagging behind the male students in forming a clear vocational identity as they approach the end of high school. Theoretically, this first longitudinal study of vocational development in Chinese adolescents expands western models by including relational variables important to collectivistic cultures. The longitudinal design elucidates the temporal causality of the individual and relational variables in the formation of career efficacy and vocational identity over time. Using a within-culture multi-sample design, we examine the interplay among individual, cultural and socioeconomic variables. On an applied level, the results will contribute to the enhancement of career guidance services appropriate for the development of Chinese high school students living in different urban and rural settings. 高中的時間是早期職業發展的重要階段，青少年多於這一階段發展出他們的職業自我效能和職業身份。探討青少年事業發展的縱向研究指出，青少年的人格及環境因素都在變化多端的過程中影響青少年對不同職業範疇的興趣及職業自我效能，同時亦令個人的職業身份變得更明確。西方的理論模型主要集中於研究個人因素（如人格、興趣、及自我效能）對於職業探索和職業身份的影響。我們在現時的跨文化研究中發現，對中國的青少年來說，職業發展同時涉及自我效能和集體效能兩個因素，而後者通常與青少年父母、學校、及朋輩的影響有關。故此，我們建議將一項橫向研究擴展為一項有三次數據收集點的縱向研究，並透過收集高中一年級至三年級各時間點的數據，去驗證人格、社會因素、及集體效能對於職業自我效能的影響。同時，我們亦將探討上述因素的相互關係與在高中時期成型的職業身份之間的因果關係。透過在不同時間點收集數據，我們可以探索在人格及社會因素如何影響職業身份及職業承諾的時間因果關係中，集體及自我效能所造成的的中介效應。我們使用《跨文化(中國人)個性測量表——青少年版(CPAI-A)》來量度一些在本土文化中與人際關係相關的人格，作為對一些西方研究中所發現具文化普遍性的個人導向人格作額外補充。我們在預測自我效能的模型中加入集體效能的元素，以加強該模型於中國群體中的文化相關性。 我們計劃使用三個具不同現代化程度及社會經濟背景的中國地區樣本，包括香港、上海市區、及浙江省鄉郊地區。因為青少年的職業身份於高中時期變得更明確，我們估計與人際關係相關的人格及家庭因素對高中學生的職業自我效能有顯著影響，而這影響對處於鄉郊地區的高中學生更大。同樣，有鑑於過去研究顯示女生的職業身份發展於高中時期比男生慢，我們預期於高校畢業時，女生的職業身份不如男生明確，而這性別差異於鄉郊樣本亦較大。 本計劃為首個探討中國青少年縱向事業發展的研究，並加入集體文化中重要的 人際關係元素以拓展現時的西方理論模型。此計劃的縱向研究設計亦可闡明個人及人際關係相關因素兩者之間的相互關係，以及此相互關係跟職業自我效能及職業身份的時間因果關係。透過同文化的多樣本設計，我們將可驗證個人、文化及社會經濟因素的相互關係。此外，我們的研究結果亦將為中國的高校學生事業發展輔導服務帶來裨益。

441812.label: Realisation of objectives
441812.value: The objectives of the study were largely achieved. We collected 3 waves of longitudinal data. At Wave I, the valid sample in Hong Kong was 616 Senior 1 students. At the same time, the parents of 338 of these students have completed the parental questionnaires, and the class teachers have completed the teacher questionnaires for 628 of them. The numbers in Shanghai were 812 (students), 749 (parents), and 806 (teachers); and in Zhejiang they were 783 students, 655 parents, and 765 teachers. After attrition, the final longitudinal sample consisted of 1552 high school students who completed all three waves of valid data (488 for Hong Kong sample, 534 for Shanghai sample, and 530 for Zhejiang sample) from three different locations. We compared the etic (individual-oriented) personality variables with the emic (interpersonal-oriented) personality variables as antecedents to a number of vocational variables, including career self-efficacy, vocational identity and commitment. With the 3-wave data, we were able to identify the temporal causality of the antecedents on the outcome variables. First, Wang, Fan, Cheung, Wang, and Li’s manuscript (Part C #8.3) reported that after controlling the vocational exploration at Wave 2, both parental support and career self-efficacy at Wave 2 mediated the relationship between culturally relevant personality traits at Wave 1 and vocational exploration at Wave 3. In addition, career-related parental support at Wave 2 mediated the relationship between Interpersonal Relatedness factor at Wave 1 and environmental exploration at Wave 3;on the other hand, career decision-making self-efficacy mediated the relationship between Social Potency personality factor at Wave 1 and self-exploration at Wave 3. Second, Wang Cheung and Fan’s manuscript (Part C #8.5) reported the interaction effect between parental support and family orientation on career decision making self-efficacy at Wave 1. Third, Fan, Cheung, Wang, Li, and Wang’s manuscript (Part C #8.4) reported that individual and parental perceptions of vocational commitment at Wave 2 separately mediated the relationship between students’ life goal at Wave 1 and vocational identity at Wave 3. Fourth, Fan, Li, and Cheung’s working manuscript (Part C #8.6) reported the temporal increase of career decision making self-efficacy and vocational identity from Wave 1 to Wave 3. Moreover, they reported that the positive increase in career self-efficacy and vocational identity in both Hong Kong and Zhejiang samples was due to the reciprocal influence of self-efficacy with vocational identity from Wave 1 to Wave 3. Such reciprocal influence was only shown from Wave 1 to Wave 2 in Shanghai sample. Fifth, Ho and Cheung’s working manuscript (Part C #8.7) reported that the etic Interpersonal Relatedness factor at Wave 1 strengthened on the positive relationship between collective contributions to career efficacy and career decision-making self-efficacy at Wave 1. Controlling the effect of career efficacy and career decision making self-efficacy at Wave 1, the moderation effect of the Interpersonal Relatedness at Wave 1 on the relationship between collective contributions to career efficacy and career efficacy and career decision making self-efficacy at Wave 3 disappeared. Sixth, Cheung and Ho’s working manuscript (Part C #8.8) reported that career decision making self-efficacy at Wave 2 mediated the relationships between culturally relevant personality traits at Wave 1 and Holland efficacy themes at Wave 2. Our longitudinal study was able to establish the incremental contributions of interpersonal personality dimensions and collective efficacy supplemented western models of vocational development in predicting the development of career self-efficacy and vocational identity over time. The aforementioned studies reported the significant correlations of interpersonal aspects of personality with vocational exploration and collective efficacy ((Part C #8.1 to #8.8). In addition, Wang, Cheung, and Fan’s manuscript ((Part C #8.5) reported that the indigenous trait on family orientation moderated the relationship between parental support and career decision-making self-efficacy. Given that we have 3 waves of data in three Chinese regions, we were able to examine regional and gender differences in the development of career efficacy and vocational identity during late adolescence. Cheung and Ho’s working manuscript (Part C #8.7) reported the gender differences in the moderation of the Interpersonal Relatedness in the relationship between career decision-making self-efficacy and collective career efficacy. The moderation effect was found only in the male sample but not in the female sample. Wang, Cheung, and Fan’s manuscript (Part C #8.3) reported regional differences in joint influences of family orientation and parental support on career decision-making self-efficacy. The pattern of moderation effect was consistent in all three regions. Whereas the positive relationship between family orientation and career decision-making self-efficacy was stronger for high school students with high perceived parental support, the positive relationship between parental support and career decision making self-efficacy was stronger for high school students with high family orientation.

441812.label: Major findings and research outcome
441812.value: This study examined the temporal causality for the personality and social influences as antecedents to vocational outcomes among Chinese high school students in a 3-wave longitudinal design. In addition to western models of personality, we found that indigenously derived interpersonal dimensions of personality provided added value in predicting the pattern of relationships between career decision-making self-efficacy and vocation identity (Part C #8.3). We also supplemented western models of vocation development by including a collective career efficacy construct. The relationship of collective career efficacy to career decision-making self-efficacy is moderated by interpersonal dimensions of personality (Part C #8.7). The roles of parental support and family orientation were also demonstrated to be important antecedents to vocational development among Chinese adolescents (Part C #8.5) The gender differences were found in the pattern of relationships, with male showing lower scores on the interpersonal dimensions of personality. The age and regional differences were found. Younger (versus older) students in Hong Kong tended to have a stronger family orientation. No age differences in family orientation were found among students in Shanghai and Zhejiang province (Part C #8.5). The developmental and regional differences in vocational behaviors were shown. Shanghai students scored higher on the career decision self-efficacy than did Hong Kong and Zhejiang province (Part C #8.5). Over time, however, career decision making self-efficacy and vocational identity increased in Hong Kong, Shanghai, and Zhejiang province. Whereas career self-efficacy and vocational identity influenced with each other from Wave 1 to Wave 3 in the Hong Kong and Shanghai sample, such reciprocal influence only occurred in the Zhejiang sample from Wave 1 and Wave 2 (Part C #8.6). Furthermore, parental perceptions of students’ vocational commitment at Wave 2 partially mediated the relationship between Life Goal at Wave 1 and Vocational Identity at Wave 3 in Shanghai and Zhejiang but not in Hong Kong (Part C #8.4). By incorporating interpersonal dimensions of personality and the role of social environment and support from significant others, results from this study provide a more culturally relevant model for understanding adolescents’ vocational development in collectivistic societies. Career choices in these societies is not based only on individual decisions, but are influenced by parents and significant others. The extent of these influences is mediated by the adolescents’ personality and moderated by gender and regional differences. The study also provides further validation of the Chinese Personality Assessment Inventory for Adolescents as a culturally relevant measure that extends western models of personality.

441812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
441812.value: With the wealth of data collected in this longitudinal study, we have so far analyzed patterns of relationships among specific variables. For instance, the Interpersonal Relatedness factor significantly predicted career self-efficacy and vocational exploration. The subscale of the IR factor — Family Orientation moderated the relationship between parental support and career self-efficacy. We will continue to work on further analysis on the pattern of relationships to see if a more comprehensive model can be supported. The results of this study and some of the instruments used are being made available to the Jockey Club Career and Life Adventure Planning Program (CLAP) for high school students in Hong Kong. This program aims to provide systematic and sustainable career and life planning education and intervention for local young people. We participate in this program so that high school students in Hong Kong may benefit from our culturally relevant measures for their career guidance.

441812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
441812.value: Personality defines adolescents’ career self-efficacy, which in turn affects their vocational identity and commitment. Parental support and environmental influences moderates these relationships. Across Hong Kong, Shanghai and Zhejiang rural area, Chinese high school students who focused on family relations were more confident in career decision-making when they received high parental support. Gender also influenced adolescents’ self and collective efficacy. Although female high school students were more relationally-oriented than male high school students, males who scored higher (vs. lower) on the Interpersonal Relatedness factor were more confident in both the self and collective career efficacy. Using the indigenously derived Chinese Personality Assessment Inventory for Adolescents, it was shown that interpersonally-oriented personality traits could supplement western models of personality in explaining Chinese adolescents’ vocational development. First, the Interpersonal Relatedness (IR) factor significantly correlated with self-career efficacy specific to certain vocational interests. Second, The IR factor also predicted vocational exploration in the social environment. Third, the IR factor strengthened the relationships between self and collective career efficacy. Fourth, family orientation, a facet of the IR factor, influenced the effect of parental support on career efficacy. Taken together, our results underline the value of interpersonally-oriented personality in research of vocational behaviors.

442112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
442112.value: Long before the Ming Empire was established in 1368, copper coins were used as the medium of exchange in regional markets. In 1375 the imperial court began to print paper money and declared these notes the only legal form of state payment, but ordinary people continued to use copper cash as their preferred currency. Because the imperial government lacked the means to withdraw old coins as new ones were issued, and because debased counterfeits were common, at any time, many different types of coins circulated. Cash was used in “strings”. It had been characteristic of Chinese coins, for centuries, to be made with a square hole in the middle so that they might be strung together. Such strings varied in value, local market custom governing the number of different coins each string might contain. Consequently, although copper coins issued by the government at any one time followed a common standard, Ming and Qing China did not have a unified currency. In 1465, the Ming emperor made it acceptable for inland customs dues to be paid in copper cash. 1503, after paper money depreciated badly, the Hongzhi emperor reopened the state mints to cast copper coins. In 1576, the right to mint coins was extended to the provinces. But reverting to coinage immediately brought into play Gresham’s law of “bad money driving out the good”. In consequence, people dissembled their strings, hid the good coins for themselves or sold them to counterfeiters, and paid taxes in inferior coins. My first hypothesis is that copper cash were minted again in the Ming not only because it was convenient for small denomination purchases, but also very largely because it was the portion of the money supply that the government could issue at will. My second hypothesis is that these changes in monetary policy caused high inflation in prices as calculated in copper cash. Since a major function of the copper cash was to pay inland customs duties, I expect that the affected areas were commercial cities along the Yangzi River and Grand Canal with customs houses, while places far from this long-distance trade route, such as Fujian, maintained the old habits of string composition, and the circulation of good-quality coins, throughout the Ming. If so, this project will show a pattern of late Ming coin circulation, and provide an essential framework for research on the regional diversities of economic growth in late-imperial China. 明帝國建立（1368）之時，銅錢已經是中國地方市場的主要交易媒介。1375年明朝發行寶鈔，同時宣佈它是帝國唯一償付的貨幣形式。雖然如此，一般老百姓仍然依循舊習慣使用銅錢。由於明政府對銅錢流通缺乏規範，各地銅錢在使用上存在很大的差異，不同品質和重量的銅錢都同時流通，而劣質銅錢也很普遍。 銅錢是以「串」作為單位使用的，以一根繩子將多個銅錢的方孔串穿起來，便成一串錢。然而，每個地方市場的一串錢應所包含的銅錢數目和質量都不同，市場價格也各異。簡單來說，明代中國沒有一個全國通行的貨幣系統。 1465年，明朝皇帝開始規定銅錢也可用來繳納鈔關稅項。1503年，朝廷更重開了京師鑄幣廠，鑄造銅錢，更在1576年將措施伸展到各省。但新的貨幣政策，隨即使中國出現了格雷欣法則中「劣幣驅逐良幣」的問題，人們紛紛將原來的錢串拆散，把其中質量較好的銅錢收起﹑出售或者繳納鈔關稅項。這個研究的首個假設是，明朝廷重鑄銅錢，不是為著方便地方市場的買賣，而是因為朝廷需要經費，而銅錢正是它能夠隨時開發的資源。本研究的第二個假設是，明朝的新貨幣政策，導致了以銅錢計算商品的通貨膨脹。如前所述，制錢的主要功能是支付關稅，故此沿著長江和運河各鈔關附近的城市，成為新政策最受影響的地方。至於那些如福建省那些遠離鈔關的地區，則直至明末仍然保持著舊有的串錢習慣，而串錢內也有好錢。若這個設想是正確的話，那麼本研究將展示晚明銅錢流通的地域模式，並為中華帝國晚期經濟發展內的地域差異提供一個架構。

442112.value: These objectives have all been achieved, and reflected in my papers presented or published attached in the report. I must say, objective 7 is a little complicated, but thanks to the talk of "Song Coin and Monetary Circulation in Maritime East Asia 1200-1700" by Professor Richard von Glahn, and the talk of "Archaeological Study on Unearthed Coins in East Asia" by Professor Miyake Toshihiko in the CUHK during my research, I have a much deeper understanding of that.

442112.label: Major findings and research outcome
442112.value: With the GRF grant support, I have produced four conference papers (three of them are co-authored), one journal article, and one book chapter (in press), more than I promised (3 essays in total) in my proposal. From these studies, I now have a better understanding of the Ming coinage system as well as coin as a medium of exchange. I have achieved all the adjectives though the objective 7 of Chinese coins in other Asian countries is more complicated than I thought. Besides these, I have investigated and understand the emergence of brass coins, and the concept of the government behind the monetary policy in the Ming. As a concluding remark of the project, I have more confidence in writing a book on the Ming coinage with a different approach from the current literature.

442112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
442112.value: I have plan to write a book on the Ming coinage system. With the grant support, I have presented and discussed my ideas on the coinage with economic historians in different parts of the world in a international conference in Florence. This experience is valuable and I collected some insightful questions, like why Chinese emperors never thought of unified the weight and fineness of the coins? I wish to write a book in English with this as my starting question.

442112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
442112.value: We all have a false impression that the First Emperor had unified the currency of China in 221 B.C. The outcome of this project showed the First Emperor unified only the form of each coin, which was round shape with a square hole at the center. In the Ming dynasty, for instance, the weight and fineness of copper coins varied, but they all carried the price of one cash. My study has reshaped the theory in the literature which states that the monetary system of late imperial China was bi-metallism of which silver and copper cash served as the two kinds of money. I however show that on the aspect of coinage, different kinds of coins circulated and accepted as legal money. It was multi-metallism, instead of bi-metallism, happened in China of the time.

442212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
442212.value: 差異化:導引企業由類同達至獨特技能

442212.label: Project Objectives
442212.value: Conceptualize the transformation of isomorphic IT innovations into unique capabilities, into a Heteromorphism framework. Derive nascent theories and map the successful turnaround processes from the Heteromorphism framework through in-depth case studies. Strengthen the generalization of the findings by developing and validating a research model for Heteromorphism with definition of constructs, hypotheses, and measurement items through an empirical survey.
rows: Conceptualize the transformation of isomorphic IT innovations into unique capabilities, into a Heteromorphism framework.
Derive nascent theories and map the successful turnaround processes from the Heteromorphism framework through in-depth case studies.

Strengthen the generalization of the findings by developing and validating a research model for Heteromorphism with definition of constructs, hypotheses, and measurement items through an empirical survey.

442212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
442212.value: IT innovations are critical for firms to be successful and remain competitive among peers. Quite often, institutional pressure is a major reason to innovate with IT. The literature suggests that institutional pressure leads to numerous mindless IT adoptions that results in isomorphic IT innovations. Institutional pressure can excel IT diffusion, yet it is difficult for firms to derive competitive advantages from isomorphic IT innovations, which forces firms to look and function alike. However, there are observed exceptions of successful cases, in which firms jump on the bandwagon and are still able to develop unique capabilities based on the adopted technology. We believe that firms can develop benefits and competitive advantages from isomorphic IT innovations with the right beacons (processes and driving force). In this study we argue that firms can indeed become heterogeneous under institutional pressure following the right processes and making the right decisions and call this concept Heteromorphism. We posit that IT innovations under institutional pressure can create a critical mass, where firms end up with only assets and resources. Mere assets and resources do not necessarily benefit firms, as the capability to make good use of the assets and resources is critical. We argue that firms can learn to make good use of these assets and resources once they get hands on experience with the technology in the development of capabilities that are unique. Such unique capabilities can make a firm distinctive from other firms and be leveraged to bring competitive advantages. This view is supported by recent IT innovations, effective bandwagon with high degree of confidence, that mindless adoptions are common and yet sustained competitive advantages can be subsequently created. This study utilizes two theories with rather competing results to discuss Heteromorphism, namely institutional theory and the resource based view. We depart from the traditional institutional theory by investigating why institutional pressure does not necessarily lead to isomorphic IT innovations. Instead we study how firms can derive unique capabilities under institutional pressure through a learning process. We will first develop and theorize the Heteromorphism concept through in-depth case studies. Subsequently, a large scale confirmatory study will be designed and conducted to ensure the generalizability of Hetermorphism.

442212.label: Realisation of objectives
442212.value: (1) We have developed a conceptualization describing the transformation of isomorphic IT innovations into unique capabilities based on existing literature and observations. We have further strengthened the conceptualization by confirming the findings with 2 system integrators. A Heteromorphism framework has been proposed to explain the turnaround process. Observations suggest that many IT innovations indeed occur due to institutional pressure and can lead to unsatisfactory outcome. However, various organizations can recover from the unsatisfactory IT innovation and still mindfully turn it into their unique capabilities. Existing literature suggest a juxtaposing view, Institutional Theory and Resource Based View, and posit that firms need to strike a balance between the institutional and resource based determinants. In this study we attempt to bridge these 2 juxtaposing theories through a learning process. We argue that rather than balancing between these 2 it can happen in sequence, where organizations first pursuit social legitimacy and once they are familiarized with the IT innovation through learning, they can turn it into their unique capabilities. We expect that our conceptualization can help organizations to further turn IT innovations into unique capabilities. Moreover, our study suggests that isomorphism may not be the final result of institutional pressure and firms can actually turn homogeneous over time. (2) We proposed a theoretical model by confirming our Heteromorphism conceptualization through in-depth case studies, covering 6 organizations and 14 RFID innovations. A process model for the Heteromorphism turnaround process has been proposed. Our findings suggest that organizations can indeed learn from IT innovations and the learning process can help to turn IT innovations into unique capabilities. However, the transformation from learning into unique capabilities does not always occur, as is suggested by the traditional literature. The case studies suggest that instigations are necessary to catalyze the transformation process. The instigations can arise from external parties or from high level management. Another interesting point that the case studies point out is that organizations often attempt to learn through deliberately outsourcing IT innovations. This goes against the traditional IT outsourcing literature, where the literature suggests that organizations outsource IT when it is not a part of their core competence and when the market can deliver the IT innovation more efficiently. However, our case findings suggest that organizations often perceive RFID as a potential core competence and can help them to attain competitive advantage, yet they intentionally outsource the IT innovation. They do so, because they lack expertise in the RFID field. They therefore outsource the IT innovation and quicken the learning process by observing the system integrator. (3) The case studies have led into initial development of measurement items for Heteromorphism. This is especially needed as the IS field lacks readily available measurement items for the Resource Based View and Absorptive Capacity (the learning process). Our study suggests that the alignment of supply chain strategy and supply chain practices can be considered as a proxy to measure capabilities in our context. Moreover, the degree of IT outsourcing is a proxy that can be used to measure absorptive capacity. Rather than outsourcing the empirical survey, our team validated the proposed theoretical Heteromorphism framework and its further generalizability through conducting in-depth interviews to query on other technologies. This allowed us not only to investigate in RFID and the suggested ERP, but also allowed us to deepen in other technologies such as cloud computing and IoT. The results predominantly confirmed our findings and helped us to better define the measurement instruments. The findings are positive and we are confident that the measurement instruments can be adopted in other large scale empirical studies.

442212.label: Major findings and research outcome
442212.value: Observations suggest that many RFID innovations were initiated due to organizations perceiving institutional pressures. This led to that many organizations innovated with RFID in order to seek social legitimacy. Institutional pressure often lead to that organizations seek for a quick remedy, which often does not align with the organization’s goals and end up with disappointing results. In this study we posit that organizations can still mindfully learn from the unsatisfying IT innovation. Organizations often outsource the initial IT innovation to system integrators, with the aim to propel the learning process. The IT outsourcing is often seen as a test bed and source of knowledge. Under these circumstances, organizations attempt to work closely with the system integrator and absorb the system integrator’s knowledge. Once the organization has absorbed adequate knowledge, they can become more hands on and try use the technology to develop their unique capabilities. This study has two major contributions. The first contribution aims to bridge two juxtaposing theories, namely Institutional Theory and the Resource Based View. Institutional pressure argues that organizations turn homogeneous, as organizations often face similar institutional pressure and therefore take similar course of actions. Resource Based View, on the other hand, argues that organizations need to be heterogeneous in order to survive in a competitive market. We argue that organizations indeed often innovate with IT due to institutional pressure and become homogeneous. However, it does not end here. We found out that organizations can actually turn heterogeneous with IT innovations over time. This can be made possible when the organizations attempt to learn from the IT innovation and have the intention to further explore with the technology. Note that Heteromorphism is more apparent on an organizational level, rather than on an IT innovation level. Often the learning process starts by outsourcing the IT innovation. This brings us to our second contribution, where we argue that organizations often outsource IT innovations with the aim to learn. Existing theories suggests that organizations only outsource when the outsourced IT innovations is not a part of the core competence and can be delivered more efficiently by third parties. Case findings suggest that organizations purposely outsource IT innovations, when they believe that it can become a part of their core competence. Organizations attempt to do so, as a quick way to learn more about the technology. Over time they can internalize the knowledge and derive unique capabilities from the learnings.

442212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
442212.value: This study suggests that IT outsourcing can be used as a form of organizational learning. We believe that studies can further deepen into this area. To the best of our knowledge, existing literature has not studied this phenomenon. It would be interesting to find out whether this phenomenon is also applicable to other IT innovations or even other fields. Moreover, our findings suggest that Heteromorphism can indeed occur over time. It would therefore be beneficial to conduct a longitudinal to further understand the learning process. Currently, we used interviews to query recent decisions. However, a longitudinal study or even an action based study could more accurately capture the learning process. Finally, it would be beneficial to develop a design framework or design theory to help practitioners to mindfully innovate with IT. This would help organizations to develop IT innovations that are inherently aligned with the organization’s goals. Initial groundwork for developing a mindful design theory has been laid in this study and future research in this area is warranted.

442212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
442212.value: In this study we have proposed the Heteromorphism concept, which discusses how organizations can turn unsatisfactory IT innovations due to institutional pressure into unique capabilities. Observations illustrate that many IT innovations occur due to institutional pressure and can lead to disappointing results. This study posits that organizations can still turn the disappointing IT innovation into the organization’s competitive advantage, by mindfully familiarizing and learning more about the IT innovation. An effective way to learn about a new technology is to outsource the development to a system integrator. This allows the organization to explore the possibilities/limitations of the technology and quickly learn more about the technology. Once the organization is familiar with the technology, they can explore how it can translate into their competitive advantage. Often this is done by starting new IT innovation projects based on the same technology aligned with the organization’s goals.

442312.label: Project Objectives
442312.value: To examine why China's film industry has thrived since the turn of the twenty-first century but not during the 1990s despite the fact that the economic reforms had already been implemented. To evaluate four conventional explanations for the revival of China's film industry since the late 1990s. In doing so, to demonstrate how the Global Commodity Chain (GCC) approach can be applied to explicate the organizational structure of the Chinese film industry. Emphasis will be focused on the relationships among different players in the industry, especially those between the stakeholders involved in different stages of the value chain, such as, the former state-owned film studios, the privately-owned film companies, the filmmakers, and the industry players in the distribution and exhibition sectors. To evaluate the effects of transnational and regional integration on the Chinese movie value chain, particularly how global players, including those from Hollywood, and regional linkages especially through the filmmakers in Hong Kong have impacted on the re-industrialization of China's film industry. To deepen our understanding of the impacts of the reform of China's film industry on its stakeholders including how the business models of the film companies and the career of Chinese filmmakers have been influenced and altered by different kinds of forces unleashed by the market reform.
