442312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
442312.value: After the Cultural Revolution, the Chinese film industry experienced incremental reform and there had been ups and downs in its fortunes since the 1970s. By the latter half of the 1990s and after almost two decades of reform, however, film production had dwindled. Yet entering the new century, the seemingly stagnant film industry witnessed a period of sustained growth despite China's accession to the World Trade Organization that facilitated a larger inflow of foreign movies into the Chinese market and that competed with local productions. This points to an empirical puzzle that has been much discussed though seldom seriously tackled: why has China's film industry experienced a steady resurgence since the turn of the twenty-first century? To unravel this puzzle, the current project seeks to evaluate four conventional explanations for the revitalization of the Chinese film industry that emphasize respectively the effects of the market, the state and its actions, the reception of cultural products by the audience, and the presence of regional networks. We propose to critically evaluate these four explanations and their associated propositions for resurgence of the Chinese film industry in the context of an integrative analytical framework that centers on the organizations involved in the different critical stages of the film industry (production, distribution and exhibition) and the relationships among them. Through a systematic analysis of film projects, enterprises, professionals and practitioners, and their different fortunes in the market since 2000, we should be in a better position to forge a more comprehensive understanding of the development of China's film industry. Moreover, this study will not only allow us to develop a better understanding of the Chinese film industry in particular, it will also foster a more rigorous sociological analysis of the post-socialist cultural industries. This will advance our theoretical understanding of the cultural industries and the various local and global, social and political forces that underpin their development. To this end, the current project will contribute to the ongoing public deliberations over the appropriate policies and institutional supports for the development of cultural industries both in China and other parts of East Asia, and help policymakers formulate more comprehensive and evidence-based policy responses. 中國改革開放後的電影產業化：政府、市場、文化與區域融合 不論在政治、經濟或是文化層面，電影對中國都是一個重要的戰略性產業。中國的電影產業自上世紀七十年代經歷多次改革，發展的過程波折重重。踏入千禧年，中國電影業面臨加入世界貿易組織後進一步開放本土電影市場的挑戰。正當業內人士甚至社會大眾也認為中國電影業危在旦夕時，國產片的產量與票房收入卻不斷飆升。本研究探討的正是中國電影業如何在水深火熱的環境中迅速成長。 本研究會評估市場因素、政府行為、觀眾對文化產品的接受程度和地區網絡的影響這四個普遍的解說向度，並分析不同類型的電影製作、發行和放映機構之間的關係。本研究將有助社會各界以社會學的理論架構，更深入地了解中國的文化產業從計劃經濟轉到有中國特色的社會主義市場經濟時所面臨的挑戰和機遇，同時協助政府制定更有效的文化政策。

442512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
442512.value: 本研究比較在南中國建造業, 製造業及服務業男性農民工的性別身份如何受移民及工作環境所影響. 西方對男性性別身份的研究在過去十年如雨後春筍, 特別是對男性陽剛氣質的研究。 但這方面的研究在中國十分缺乏, 對男性農民工的陽剛氣質的研究更是少之又少。 西方的研究發現,男性陽剛氣質影響男性的心理壓力, 情緒, 婚姻關係, 犯罪及越軌行為。 性別研究專家R Connell 認為在每個社會存在著一種霸權式男性陽剛氣質, 這種霸權式陽剛氣質不但合符中產階層及在經濟上成功的男性的存在處境, 更是一種權力層級的展現。 霸權式陽剛氣質一方面合理化男性對女性的壓迫, 另方面又邊緣化勞工階層, 同性戀, 小數族群, 及移民男性。因為這些男性大都缺乏資源去符合霸權式男性陽剛氣質中所要求的理想男性形象。 被邊緣化的男性唯有運用另類手段, 例如強調他們支時家庭經濟的能力, 戰鬥力, 使用暴力的能力 及性方面的風險行為等去塑造另一種其認為值得被尊重的男性形象以及對女性的操控。 對男性陽剛氣質的研究特別適合中國男性農民工的處境, 因為這些由農村到城市打工的農民工面對著雙重的對其性別身份的挑戰。 一方面他們需適應從農村到城市遷移過程中對他們男性陽剛氣質所造成的沖擊。在傳統父權的中國農村中, 男性相對於女性仍處於優勢及男性仍掌控著農村的資源。但這些在農村中處於優越地位的男性, 因為沒有城市戶口, 到了城市後卻變成城市中的邊緣人。第二方面, 在現今中國城市中的理想男性形象以金錢權力掛師, 這些被邊緣化的城市男性農民工, 不但沒權也缺乏經濟能力, 在這情況下, 他們又如何重構一個能自我肯定的男性身份? 這個研究因此問以下的問題: 1) 男性的結構性位置何如影響他們對所謂 “理想男性形象” 的理解及他們自身性別身份的操作及展示? 2) 工作環境, 工作的次文化, 對城市生活的投入程度, 及對資訊科技的使用如何影響不同群體男性對男性陽剛氣質的理解及展示? 3) 男性陽剛氣質的展示如何影響男性的心理壓力, 性別關係, 及次文化? 本研究有三大貢獻。其一, 它探討男性陽剛氣質一概念是否適合中國社會的性況。其二, 它分析中國城鄉及其他結構性不平等如何與性別不平等交織而影響個人的生存, 性別身份又如何受社會環境所影響而改變。 最後, 它補充了近代對中國農民工研究的一個缺口, 對焦在男性農民工的特定處境。

442512.label: Realisation of objectives
442512.value: The main objective of this project is to examine the challenges male migrant workers experience after migration, and to delineate the extent these problems are related to the gaps between expectations and realities, to the differences between their structural locations in rural and urban areas, and to their inability to live up to their ideal notion of manhood. This objective is fully achieved through the publication of the co-authored (by the PI and one of the Co-Is) book monograph by University of California Press in 2016. The book monograph is entitled Masculine Compromise: Migration, Family and Gender in China. Drawing on the life stories of 266 migrants in South China, we examine the effect of mass rural-to-urban migration on family and gender relationships, with a specific focus on changes in men and masculinities. Our findings show how migration have forced migrant men to renegotiate their roles as lovers, husbands, fathers, and sons. They also reveal how migrant men make masculine compromises: they strive to preserve the gender boundary and their symbolic dominance within the family by making concessions on marital power and domestic division of labor, and by redefining filial piety and fatherhood. In sum, the stories of these migrant men and their families reveal another side to China’s sweeping economic reform, modernization, colossal rural to urban migration, and grand social transformations. The second objective of this project is to determine how the inferior status of rural migrants in urban areas and differences in cultural values resulting from urban and rural upbringings may shape understandings and expressions of masculinity by comparing the notions of manhood and their expressions between male migrant workers and male urban residents. This objective is also achieved. In Chapter 3 of our book Masculine Compromise, we delineated how influenced by the urban ideologies of romantic love and consumerism, young migrant men place more emphasis on having a spiritual connection with an intimate partner and connect their dating practices with consumptions. In Chapter 6 of our book, we show how migrant fathers often suffer a double emotional burden: sadness, guilt, anguish and worry about the prolonged periods of separation from their children and feelings of inadequacy because of their inability to measure up to the urban image of the ‘good father’. The third objective of our project is to examine the consequences of masculinity on psychological stress, marital and family relationships, and male subcultures of gambling, drinking, gang fighting and risky sexual behaviours. This objective is also realized. In Chapters 4, 5, and 6 of our book, we examined how the inability to live up to the dominant discourse of manhood in urban areas has caused these rural to urban migrant men sense of guilt and shame, and propelled others to develop a counter discourse of ‘respectable manhood’ that is based on their unconventional domestic roles. This counter discourse rehabilitates these male migrant workers from the humiliation they experience in the cities as second-class citizens and marginalised workers, thus cross-cutting gender and rural/ urban inequalities. The fourth objective of this project is to determine how the organization, subculture and condition of work may shape the ways migrant workers understand and express their masculinity by comparing migrant workers in the manufacturing, service and construction sectors. This objective is achieved in an ongoing sole-author book monograph that the PI is currently working. In this book she explores how the organization, subculture and employment conditions of service, manufacturing and construction work are intersected with rural-to-urban male migrant workers’ gender identity. The fifth objective of this project is to examine how exposure to information communication technologies such as the internet and mobile phones may contribute to migrant workers’ understandings and expressions of masculinity. This objective is also achieved in one of the chapters of an ongoing co-author book monograph the PI is currently working. In this book she examines how exposure to and use of information communication technologies are closely related to young male migrant workers’ self-identity, dating practices and consumption behavior, which in turn are mobilized to express certain notions of ideal manhood. The objectives of this project are fully realized not only through the publication of a 177- page book monograph by one of the world’s top presses, they are met also through the publication of a journal article in an international journal, and the PI’s and Co-I’s presentations of the findings in four international conferences, and invited talks at top universities including National University of Singapore, University of London, University of Oxford, and University of Cambridge.

442512.label: Major findings and research outcome
442512.value: Our findings show that migration has considerably transformed the relationships between migrant men and their lovers, spouses, children, and parents. Young and single migrant men are thrust into the tension between the persistent influence of rural parents in their grown children’s marriage decisions and the increasing cultural legitimacy for individuals in urban centers to pursue love, romance, and sexual autonomy. Married migrant men have found it increasingly difficult to maintain the traditional dominance and privilege of the husband in the realms of marital decision making and domestic division of labor. Migrant men with children find it hard to handle the emotional distance between them and their left-behind children. Migrant men also need to renegotiate their traditional obligation as filial sons from afar. Our exploration of the subjective experiences, strategies and agency of migrant men reveals the complexity of interactions between population movement and gender stratification processes in the context of rural- urban inequalities and changes in the institution of the family in post-Mao China. Our research suggests that although men are viewed as the de facto beneficiaries of patriarchy, migrant men do adjust their caring practices and behavior within intimate relationships to cope with the challenges of migration. This adjustment is a complex process and change is uneven; preserved and adjusted behaviors and attitudes often co-exist and sometimes conflict with each other. The complexity and heterogeneity of men’s responses to migration led us to ask how they might be explained. We developed the concept of masculine compromise to enable us to offer a gendered account of male migrants’ response, change, and agency. In summary, mass rural-to-urban migration might have brought more gender equality in family in terms of care practices, division of labour and distribution of power, but these changing practices are not matched with an equal measure of gender equality awakening. Rural-to-urban migrant men might make compromises when their traditional dominance in the family is challenged, but these compromises are anchored in ideologies of masculinity. The concept of masculine compromise therefore captures the agency and strategies of men in negotiating their changing roles and gender identity in the family, ushered by one of the most significant mass migrations currently happening in human history: rural-urban labor migration in China. It also describes the discrepancy between practices and ideas, delineates the uneven pace of structural and cultural changes, and expounds the tension exerted by these incompatibilities on individuals and families.

442512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
442512.value: The data collected in this project contain intriguing and rich information about the experiences of male rural to urban migrant men who engage in low paid and low status service work such as security guiding and taxing in urban China. Past studies on rural-to-urban migrant workers in China have focused either on the experiences of manufacturing and construction workers, or female service workers. The experiences of male rural to urban migrant workers who have found employment in the service sectors have not been explored. This gap overlooks the richness of the experiences of this particular group of workers in revealing the intricate relationship between migration, gender, service work and inequality. To fill this gap, the PI of this grant is currently working on a sole author book monograph that uses the experiences of male rural to urban migrant workers who have found employment in low paid and low status service work to explore how patriarchy, capitalism, and China's peculiar rural and urban divide intersect to produce and reproduce multiple forms of inequalities.

442512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
442512.value: Past studies on migration, family and gender has shown that migration is not only a central event that changes family life, this change is also a gendered process. How migrant women develop strategies to cope with new challenges in their familial roles posed by either their own migration or their husband’s migration has been widely studied. How migrant men adjust and change their care practices and domestic role to accommodate challenges to family life brought by migration, however, is much less explored. Using the case of male rural-to-urban migrant workers in South China, this project fills the gap by showing how migrant men actively renegotiate their multiple gender identities in both familial and work contexts. It develops the concept of masculine compromise to offer a new approach to focusing on male migrants’ agency through a gendered lens. Our exploration of the interplay between masculinity and migration complicates the interaction between population movement and gender stratification as they unfold and shaped by multiple systems of inequality.

443012.label: Project Title(Chinese)
443012.value: 動機和情感因素在消費者偏好形成過程中的機理研究

443012.label: Project Objectives
443012.value: We aim to experimentally show that people learn motivational value through operant conditioning and affective value through classical conditioning. We examine how motivational and affective components of preference are differentially tapped in different preference and valuation elicitation tasks. We aim to show the qualitative difference between the mere possession effect and the endowment effect in terms of motivation and emotion. We aim to show the qualitative difference between Willingness-To-Pay and Willingness-To-Accept measures in terms of motivation and emotion.

We examine how motivational and affective components of preference are differentially tapped in different preference and valuation elicitation tasks.

We aim to show the qualitative difference between Willingness-To-Pay and Willingness-To-Accept measures in terms of motivation and emotion.

443012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443012.value: Recent research in neural psychology finds that wanting (motivation) and liking (affect) are controlled by different neural systems and each can independently affect decisions (Berridge 1999). In our own research program (Dai, Brendl, and Ariely 2010; Brendl, Lisjak, and Dai 2011) we also showed the divergence of motivational and affective components of preference under natural settings and developed behavioral and reaction time measures of both components. Building on these lines of literature, in this research proposal we seek to understand the processes underlying acquisition and expression of these qualitatively different preferences. In the first part of the proposal, we study how these two components of preference are differentially acquired. Existing literature on associative learning identified many differences between classical conditioning and operant conditioning, but no difference has been discussed or identified in terms of the content of learning. We argue that participants learn the motivational component of preference through operant conditioning, and the affective component through classical conditioning. In the second part of the proposal, we focus on the expression of preferences. We propose that the mere possession effect (Beggan 1992) is a “liking” phenomenon, and that the endowment effect (Kahneman, Knetsch, and Thaler 1990) is a “wanting” phenomenon. That is, merely owning (vs. not owning) an object increases only people’s affective responses toward this object. Alternatively, the implication of losing it turns the mere “owning” into a motivational state that exerts additional forces to avoid loss from occurring. Furthermore, we argue that valuation differences between differentially liked products largely depend on the valuation elicitation methods. When prompted to express Willingness to Pay (WTP), people rely heavily on their affective responses toward the products; whereas when expressing Willingness to Accept (WTA), they rely more on motivational responses toward the products. These differential sources of valuation processes thus lead to varied valuation differences between liked and less-liked products. More specifically, we predict that this valuation difference would be larger in WTP assessment than in WTA assessment. Furthermore, we predict that WTA are more likely to be affected by reference prices (e.g., market prices) than WTP assessment. 神經心理學的最新發展發現動機和情感由不同的神經系統所控制，它們每一個都可以獨立的影響決策過程。我們自己過去的研究也發現了類似的結果在日常決策中出現。我們之前還開發了在日常決策中測量動機和情感因素的行爲方法。在這樣一些文獻和方法的基礎上，本研究計劃分析動機和情感因素在消費者偏好的獲取和表達中所起的作用。 在本研究的第一部分，我們試圖證明消費者偏好中動機和情感成分是通過不同的方式獲取的。現存的研究文獻發現經典性條件反射和操作性的諸多不同之處，但是從來沒有文獻分析人類在兩種不同條件反射下偏好學習過程中學到內容的差別。我們認爲在經典性條件反射中被試學習到的主要是偏好中的情感因素，而在操作性條件反射中主要學到的是偏好中的動機因素。 在本研究的第二部分，我們研究動機和情感因素對消費者偏好表達的影響。我們認爲擁有效應(mere possession effect)涉及的主要是偏好的情感因素，而禀賦效應(endowment effect)涉及的主要是偏好的動機因素。也就是說，擁有或者不擁有一個物品，人對它的偏好主要是情感方面的差別。而當人面臨失去一個他擁有的物品時，他對該物品的動機方面的偏好就會上升。而且，我們認爲不同的價值評估方法可能測量的是人的偏好，或者估價中不同的因素。相對而言，對物品的最大購買意願價格(WTP)更多的受到人對該物品的情感因素的影響，而對物品的最大接受意願價格(WTA)更多的受到人對該物品的動機因素的影響。 總而言之，本研究試圖通過實驗方法分離消費者偏好中的動機和情感因素並系統研究它們在消費者偏好的形成和表達過程中的作用。

443012.label: Realisation of objectives
443012.value: We have conducted a series of studies tested the hypotheses we stated in the proposal. Now we have much better understanding of the differences between motivational and affective learning processes, and how they interact with different value elicitation tasks. For example, for the first objective “We aim to experimentally show that people learn motivational value through operant conditioning and affective value through classical conditioning,” our experimental results confirmed that these two conditioning processes indeed underlie the learning of the two kinds of values. For the second objective “We examine how motivational and affective components of preference are differentially tapped in different preference and valuation elicitation tasks,” we systematically examined the relation between the valuation elicitation methods and the motivational and affective components of valuation by 1) examining at the correlation between different value elicitations and the motivational and affective component measures, and 2) by manipulating the motivational or affective components and examining their influence on valuation from different elicitation methods. For objective 3 “We aim to show the qualitative difference between the mere possession effect and the endowment effect in terms of motivation and emotion,” we indeed in our experimental work found that mere possession effect is more closely related to the affective component of the value and the endowment effect is more closely related to the motivational component of the value. Objective 4 is also confirmed: we found that willingness to pay is more closely related affective component and willing to accept is more closely related to motivational component of value. Overall, this research helps us understand better the psychological underpinnings of preferences and its impact on decisions. Decomposing preference into motivational and affective components can greatly enhance our understanding of human decision making processes, and bringing new research opportunities to the study of judgment and decision making.

443012.label: Major findings and research outcome
443012.value: What are psychological underpinnings of preferences? In this proposal we suggest that motivational and affective components of preference are qualitatively different, and they can be independently learned, activated, and elicited in different value elicitation tasks. A series of experiments support this duality of preference constructions. These findings have important implications for understanding decision making processes, value elicitation methods, learning theories, etc. The outcome of this proposal is a working paper we plan to submit to the Journal of experimental psychology: General, and a few follow up projects in progress. Meanwhile we also used the fund to support several related projects, some of the papers have already been published (see the Part C).

443012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443012.value: We are optimistic that the findings in this project will inspire future research to more systematically study 1) the motivational and affective components of preferences, and 2) how the qualitatively different components of preference differentially impact decision making processes. We will continue to work in this very field and generate more research outcomes that could contribute to the theories of preference construction in particular, and decision making processes in general.

443012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443012.value: Understanding preference is critical to the study of decision making. This project systematically studies how motivational and affective components affect preference construction. We find that motivational and affective components of preferences are learned from different conditioning processes. Relatively speaking, motivational component is learned from operant conditioning procedure and affective component is learned from classical (associative) conditioning procedure. Furthermore, we also find that these different components of preference are differentially tapped in different value elicitation methods. For example, willingness to pay measure is more closely related to affective component of preference and willingness to accept measure is more closely related to motivational component of preference.

443212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
443212.value: 獨立董事強制性發表和公佈獨立意見制度有效嗎？

443212.label: Project Objectives
443212.value: Firstly, we examine the link between negative opinion issuance and the personal characteristics of independent directors, the corporate governance structure and regional institutions strength. By examining what kinds of independent directors in what kinds of corporations and regions have issued negative opinions, we try to assess whether this reform scheme has fulfilled the goal of strengthening corporate governance. Secondly, we investigate the economic consequences of the issuance of negative opinions and address the questions of whether the issuance of negative opinions truly represents effective monitoring and how effective is negative opinion issuance in strengthening corporate governance and improving firm performance. We will link the content of negative opinions, corporate policy changes with firm performance changes. Thirdly, our study examines how negative opinion issuances affect the labor market for independent directors. Particularly, we ask whether opposing independent directors would remain in the firm and continue to communicate with the management. We will examine whether those opposing directors have good chances of reemployment in other listed firms. If this reform scheme is successful, we expect a positive answer to both questions. Fourthly, our study can contribute to the literature by shedding light on the heterogeneity of independent directors by investigating how independent directors exercise their power. Prior studies often use the ratio of independent directors as a proxy for board independence. However, this implicitly assumes that all independent directors are equally willing and competent to fulfill monitoring duties. Our study uses negative opinion issuances as a more accurate measure of the monitoring effectiveness of independent directors. Finally, our study helps us understand institutional transplantation. Like most emerging market economies, the board of directors system in China is borrowed from western countries. The transplantation might bring unexpected outcomes. China’s experiment with making regulatory innovations for a transplanted institution might prompt us to explore in depth what institutional infrastructure is needed to make a transplantation work in an emerging market economy.

443212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443212.value: The independent director system is widely regarded as a critical element of corporate governance in modern corporations. It was transplanted to China in the past decade. To enhance the effectiveness of this system, China made an innovative reform by establishing a mandatory opinion issuance and reporting scheme for independent directors to voice their opinions towards major corporate events. This scheme is expected to provide an outlet for independent directors to alert the market and regulators about inherent corporate problems through issuing negative opinions and at the same time to enhance the accountability of independent directors. This project attempts to assess the effectiveness of this scheme in improving the corporate monitoring role of independent directors. We address this issue from four perspectives. First, we examine the relationship between negative opinion issuance and the personal characteristics of independent directors, the corporate governance structure and the regional legal institution strength. If independent directors with professional skills and experience are more likely to issue negative opinions, if independent directors from poorly governed firms and regions more frequently issue negative opinions, then this reform scheme is likely to have improved the corporate monitoring role played by independent directors. Second, we investigate whether negative opinions truly targeted corporate problems and provided some valuable information for investors and regulators. By looking at stock-price reactions to negative opinion announcements and the likelihood of subsequent financial distress, regulatory enforcement, etc. we try to assess whether independent directors issue negative opinions out of their fiduciary duty. Third, we analyze the long-term effects following negative opinion issuance. The difference-in-difference research design allows us to study whether firms receiving negative opinions conduct active restructuring policies to improve corporate governance and performance. If this reform scheme is successful, we expect firm performance to turn around in 2-3 years. Fourth, we examine the impacts of negative opinion issuances on the market for independent directors. Particularly, we investigate whether opposing independent directors would continue to work with the management, and whether those opposing directors would have good chances of reemployment in other listed firms. Under a successful reform scheme, we expect a positive answer to both questions. China’s experience could deepen our understanding of the effectiveness of transplanting Western corporate governance institutions to emerging markets and whether innovative institutional arrangements to strengthen the institution could enhance the effectiveness of transplanted institutions. 獨立董事制度被廣泛視為現代公司治理中的關鍵元素。這一制度在過去十年中移植到了中國。為了加強這一制度的有效性，中國作了具有創意的改革創新，建立了獨立董事強制性發表和公佈獨立意見的制度，以表達他們對公司的重大事件的見解。建立這項計畫的宗旨是為獨立董事提供一個向市場和監管機構就企業內含問題通過負面意見發出警告的平臺，同時可以加強對獨立董事的問責制。 這一研究項目試圖評估這項改革計畫在改進獨立董事在監測公司管理層方面的效力。我們準備從四個角度研究這一問題。第一，我們審視負面意見發放和獨立董事的個人特徵、 公司治理結構和公司所在區域的法律制度健全性之間的關係。如果具有專業技能和經驗的獨立董事更有可能發出負面意見，如果在管治不佳的公司和地區獨立董事更經常發出負面意見，那麼這項改革計畫很可能改善了獨立董事的監察公司管理層的作用。第二，我們調查獨立董事的負面意見是否真正針對目標公司的問題，並為投資者和監管機構提供了有價值的資訊。我們準備考察負面意見是否引起市場上股票價格的反應，負面意見是否常常伴隨之後出現的財務困境、被監管執法等的可能性。通過這些研究，我們嘗試評估獨立董事是否出於其受託責任而發出負面意見。第三，我們分析負面意見發表後的公司的長期業績的變化。通過雙重差分法的研究設計，我們可以研究接收負面意見的公司是否進行了積極的營運政策的調整，來改善公司的治理結構和業績表現. 如果這項改革計畫是成功的，我們預計公司的業績會在 2-3 年內得到改善。第四， 我們考察負面意見的發放對獨立董事在勞動市場上的後續表現的影響。特別地，我們研究發表負面意見的獨立董事是否繼續與公司管理層合作，發表反對意見的獨立董事今後在其他公司再就業的機會如何。如果這一公司治理改革計畫成功，我們期待這兩個問題都有一個積極正面的答案。 中國的獨立董事改革的經驗可以加深我們對移栽到新興市場的西方公司治理機制的有效性的認識，對在引入西方機制過程中的制度安排創新的有效性的理解。

443512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443512.value: 工作在成年人的生活中處於核心的位置。研究顯示，人們會把一些重要的活動內化為自身的一部份，從而對它們充滿激情。當人們在沒有外在壓力的情況下內化工作為自己的一部份時，會產生對工作的和諧激情（Harmonious passion for vision, HPW) (Vallerand, 2010)。當人們有較高的和諧激情時，他們會投入大量的時間和能量在工作上，並且體驗到積極的情感（Vallerand & Houlfort, 2003), 對工作更加專注（Vallerand, 2010) 並且能產生充滿創造性的想法（Liu, Chen & Yao, 2010)。 雖然和諧激情的重要性已經得到管理學者們的認可，我們對和諧激情在工作環境中是如何產生的仍然瞭解得不多。 基於社會行動理論 (Parsons, 1937; Parsons & Shils, 1951) 及其在價值觀和行為規範標準的強調，我們構建了一個模型，以描述領導如何影響下屬產生和諧激情的過程。在一個組織中，領導者的價值觀在下屬對待工作的態度和行為中發揮著舉足輕重的作用。經過較長時間的磨合，這些價值觀被下屬所內化。我們認為尤其是領導的自我超越性價值觀 (self-transcendent values, STV), 將他人的利益置於自己利益至上的價值觀，會直接和下屬的和諧激情相關。我們假設下屬知覺到的領導支持（Perceived supervisor support) 和團隊氛圍會對領導的自我超越性價值觀和下屬的和諧激情之間的關係起中介作用。我們同時假設，這兩個中介變量，對彼此與和諧激情的關係起到調節作用。 我們打算從中國公司內的研發和R&D團隊中收集數據，檢驗我們的研究假設。選擇這樣的樣本是基於三點考慮：（1）和諧激情已被證明，在這類團隊中對績效起著關鍵作用。（2）中國貧富分化日益嚴重，正經歷急劇的社會價值觀變革。人們在重新思考傳統的道家價值觀，如和諧、純粹和平衡的價值。在中國情景下檢驗我們的價值觀有著特別的意義。（3）基於傳統的中國和西方（歐洲和北美）差異，以及大部份關於激情的研究都是在西方展開的事實，在中國情景下檢驗我們的假設有著特別的意義。我們的研究將拓展有關激情的理論，這些研究結果有助於領導們明白如何促進下屬的和諧激情，同時促進其在市場上的競爭力。

443512.label: Realisation of objectives
443512.value: Over the process, we used leaders' passion for vision as a proxy for self-transcendent values because visions that are inspirational are usually beyond any individual interests, and it was much easier to measure than values. Followers' harmonious passion for work (HPW) was used as a mediator to examine the relationship between Leaders' passion for vision and followers' voice behavior because HPW is not an outcome. We expanded the original model to make by adding voice behavior as the outcome and tested the team climate in a separate study. We found support for all the originally hypothesized relationships as well as the effect on the newly added outcome. Being able to demonstrate the effects of the new construct, passion for vision, enabled us to contribute both to the vision leadership literature as well as passion literature. We studied the construct passion from three different perspectives, the predictor, mediator; and also the dynamics; as well as the compassion of the coworkers.

443812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443812.value: Studio teaching lies at the heart of architectural education, making architecture almost unique in today’s university context. However, it is characteristic of our profession that what is demanded from a design teacher seems to be no more than knowing how to design. In the absence of systematic training, a design teacher falls back on teaching as he himself was taught. It is left to the individual if and how he improves as a teacher. The studio method is undoubtedly an effective approach to teaching architecture, but knowledge of the method is not normally available unless an individual has been fortunate enough to develop under the guidance of a master teacher or works in a school with a strong pedagogic tradition. The untrained design teacher who missed out on both counts has at present few other resources to turn to for help. The proposed research, the ultimate output of which will be a book, intends to build up a body of knowledge on design pedagogy for studio teaching, placing specific emphasis on the design of programs. It will view a program as an action plan for studio teaching consisting of exercises and projects organized in a structured manner under a defined pedagogic idea. Therefore, the pedagogy underlying exercises, projects, and programs will be of primary interest. While it is commonly held that pedagogy is needed most for students in the initial phase of development, the application of design pedagogy extends beyond design fundamentals. The initial idea for this study, and indeed its significance, derived from the PI’s experience organizing a series of teacher’s design workshops for the National Supervision Board of Architectural Education (China). There is a severe shortage of qualified design teachers in China, largely as a result of the accelerated expansion of architectural education. The workshops were a measure to address this problem. The shortage of qualified teachers is compounded by a paucity of good pedagogical resources. This project can thus be seen as a practical and necessary response to both problems. The outcome of this study will have a great impact on architectural education through the education of design teachers. No less importantly, it is a visionary aim of this project to turn the routine job of studio teaching into a field of design inquiry and pedagogic experimentation and in so doing cultivate a new research tradition in this old profession. 設計工作室教學是建築教育的核心，也是建築學在當今的大學環境中顯得獨特的原因所在。可是，我們對一個設計教師的要求僅限於他或她必須具備一定的設計能力。由於缺少對設計教師的系統訓練，一個設計教師往往是以自己過去受教育的方式來教育學生，如何成為一個好的設計教師，這完全取決於個別教師的個人努力。如果一個設計教師有幸在一個經驗豐富的教師指導下工作，或在一個以教學法著名的學校裡受過教育，那麼他或她成為一個好的設計教師的機會就要大很多。除此之外，似乎並沒有其他可以利用的資源。 本研究的最終成果將是一本關於教案設計的專著，其目的在於建立一個關於設計教學法的知識體系。所謂的教案就是一個指導設計教學的，以一個明確的教學目標將設計練習和設計方案以結構有序的方式組織在一起的綱領性文件。因此，這項研究的核心問題是了解不同的設計教案背後的教學法思考。一般認為教學法問題主要針對建築設計的基礎訓練，但是此項研究的內容應該對設計教學具有普遍的意義。 本項研究主要源自於本人近年來與全國高等學校建築學學科專業指導委員會合作舉辦的設計教師培訓班的有關經驗。中國由於建築教育規模的急速擴大而面臨設計教師短缺的問題，而舉辦設計教師的培訓是解決問題的一個有效的途徑。但是我們仍然面臨缺少關於設計教學法的系統知識的難題，此項研究就是針對這個問題。無疑，有關研究將會對建築教育的發展起到推動的作用。同時，我們還期望通過這項研究將設計教學從日常任務提升到學術研究的高度，從而在這一古老的學科中提倡一種新的學術研究傳統。

443812.label: Realisation of objectives
443812.value: How does a design teacher conduct his/her studio teaching? A design teacher teaches usually in the same way as he/she being taught in his/her own education. The lack of self consciousness in the method of teaching is the common problem in architectural education. However, it is also a tendency in recent years that design teaching is treated as a special type of academic research. To realise this goal, one has to know about the basic knowledge on design pedagogy. With this background, the primary task of this project is to build up a theoretic body of knowledge on design pedagogy and to apply it to teaching practice and teacher’s training. To a great extent, the project has accomplished this task. In view of project objectives as per original application, all the points have been addressed with various degrees. For the first point, the theoretic study of “the design of studio programs” has been realised through the study of three key aspects—exercise, project, and program. The second point, the extensive case studies on different types of studio programs and approaches have contributed to the body of knowledge on the design of exercise, project and program. For the third point, the research findings from the theoretic study (point 1) and case studies (point 2) have being applied to the development of the new foundation course at CUHK, the training of design teachers through the NSBAE Workshop on Design Pedagogy and other means of dissemination. For the fourth point, different types of research outputs have been completed and several book publications are still under development. The delay of book and article publication is mainly due to the annual operation of regular studio teaching. Some of the research materials are collected from actual teaching which runs on an annually basis. For instance, the first book draft of the case study on Mr. Lonnman’s space exercise has been completed by the end of 2014 but the revision of the book is only possible after the second run of the teaching in 2016. The same thing happens in the development of the new Introduction to Architectural Design I and II (U1 and U2 studio program) by the PI. In the case study of Mr. Herbert Kramel’s teaching, the progress is slow because Mr. Kramel is an 85 years old man. The plan to overcome the problems will be dealt in 6.2.

443812.label: Major findings and research outcome
443812.value: This research is the first attempt to formulate a body of knowledge on the design of studio programs which previously only existed in individual cases of studio teaching. The major contribution of this research is to prove that it is possible to describe this body of knowledge through three key aspects: exercise, project and program. The study on “exercise” discusses issues such as what are the conditions of an effective exercise and typical exercises in the different times of architectural education. The kit-of-parts method is an invention by the Texas Rangers in the 1950s (article in 2014, conference paper in 2015 and book contracted and in progress, 2016). Another case study is about the Analytique in the Beaux-Arts (an article expected publication in 2016). The study on “project” analyses the design process of various studio projects in terms of “analysis and synthesis model” and “concept and test model”. We have discovered that studio projects based “analysis and synthesis model” place the emphasis on the problem-setting by allocating most of the studio time on analysis while studio projects based on “concept and test model” place the emphasis on the problem solving by allocating most of the studio time on the articulation of design solution. However, it is a challenge to combine both strength in one process. The study on “program” tries to describe three typical types of foundation programs as “exercises plus project” (the most common model of foundation courses), “exercises without project” (Bauhaus Basic Design Course), and “exercises within project” (new tendency). Beside a general survey of different programs, a case study on Herbert Kramel (ETH-Z)’s foundation program has been conducted (book in progress and conference paper in 2015). One important aspect of research outcomes is the application and dissemination of research findings. The annual NSBAE (National Supervision Board of Architectural Education) Workshop on Design Pedagogy has been an important and ideal venue for teacher’s training (workshop reports 2013–15). Through this research, the PI have supervised 6 junior teachers from 4 mainland universities (participating studio teaching, program development and research), 1 M.Phil thesis (Xu Liang 2014), and admitted 2 Ph.D student (Wu Jiawei and Xu Liang). Another application of the research is the development of the new foundation course (U1 and U2, in progress) and joint program development with Zhejiang University and Huaqiao University.

444112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444112.value: The study of ancient texts can be conducted from many angles, one of them being alternative characters. Alternative characters might appear under three conditions: 1) different versions of the same book; 2) multiple sources recording the same matter or event; 3) citations and the texts from which they are cited. This last condition can be further divided into three cases: 1. general citations and the cited; 2. annotations and the text being annotated; 3. leishu (encyclopaedia), excerpts from books, and their original sources (see Wang Yankun’s 王彥坤 “Introduction,” in his Studies on Alternative Characters in Ancient Texts 古籍異文研究). Since characters used in a text are closely linked to their meaning, past scholars would expend great effort in collating and identifying the alternative characters in an ancient text, in the hope of reconstructing its original shape. Great achievements have come out of this type of studies but few have explored the relationship between annotations and alternative characters in ancient texts. The proposed study aims to examine the annotations by Han and Tang scholars, such as Maogong 毛公, Zheng Xuan 鄭玄, Gao You 高誘, Wang Su 王肅, Wei Zhao 韋昭, Guo Xiang 郭象, Cheng Xuanying 成玄英, and Yang Jing 楊倞. Together with relevant excavated texts and other references, the project will compare the alternative characters in ancient texts with their corresponding annotations, in order to analyse the relationship between annotations and alternative characters and offer an in-depth view into how scholars since the Han dynasty had made use of alternative characters for their annotations of ancient texts. An “Alternative Characters in Han and Pre-Han Texts Database” and an “Annotations of Han and Pre-Han Texts Database” will first be set up under the CHANT database system. The two databases will then be collated electronically to display instances of the similarities and differences between the alternative characters and annotations. Analyses will be made on the ways annotators used alternative characters in their annotation of ancient texts. The materials and findings will be compiled and published as reference volumes of alternative characters and annotations of the Han and pre-Han texts, while the two Databases will be made available for researchers’ access. 研究古代典籍有不同的著眼點，考辨異文是其中一環。異文出現的情況有三：（一）同一本書的不同傳本、版本；（二）記載同一事物的各種資料；（三）具有引用與被引用關係的文獻。其中第三種情況又分為三類：一、一般引語與被引語；二、注文與本文；三、類書、書鈔與原書（參王彥坤《古籍異文研究‧前言》）。因為文字內容的差異往往會影響文義理解，故前人研治古書，致力廣徵異文，考察同異，嘗試恢復古書原貌。這種研究已取得很大成就，但古書注解與古籍異文的關係還少人著墨。本計劃擬以漢唐漢至六朝注家，如毛公、鄭玄、高誘、王肅、韋昭、郭象等人的注解為中心，旁參群書，輔以相關出土文獻，比對古書異文及其相關注解，分析注解與古書異文的關係，希望能深入了解漢代以來學者運用異文注解古書的方法。本計劃擬利用「漢達文庫」，建立「先秦兩漢文獻異文數據庫」與「先秦兩漢文獻注解數據庫」，再以電腦進行比對，顯示異文和注解同異，進而探究注家運用異文注解古書的方法，然後出版輯錄先秦兩漢文獻異文及注解故訓材料的工具書。最終將兩個數據庫，開放予學者使用。

444112.label: Realisation of objectives
444112.value: The project aims at exploring the relationship between annotations and alternative characters in Chinese ancient texts. By collecting annotations written by Han and Tang scholars and alternative characters found in the pre-Han and Han periods, the research team has gathered all relevant data in a digital format for further studies and publications. In order to identify alternative characters thoroughly, an “Alternative Characters in Han and Pre-Han Texts Data Analysis Model” (ACDAM) was designed in January 2013. By applying this model to our full texts database in CHANT, the research team has been able to figure out all the similarities and differences of the alternative characters. Three Co-Is led the team to select significant data and perform in-depth analysis amongst themselves in order to explore new theories of the phenomenon with the PI. The selected data has been categorized by research assistants for the database building and compilation editing. After sorting out all the relevant data generated by the ACDAM and collecting the Han and Tang annotations by Co-Is and research assistants, the team has transformed the data to a highly interactive form to build an “Alternative Database” and an “Annotation Database.” These two databases can be operated independently and interactively with a new computing structure named “the Database Interactive Searching Function” 資料庫互動檢索功能, which was designed by our programmer. This new function is capable of fulfilling multiple needs such as searching, matching and comparing among two kinds of data. This is a definite breakthrough in existing searching functions in the field of digital humanities. With the categorized data generated by the ACDAM, the team has made systematic comparison to the alternative characters in 16 ancient texts (i.e., Guoyu 國語, Kongzi jiayu 孔子家語, Liezi 列子, Shuoyuan 說苑, Hanshi waizhuan 韓詩外傳, Zhuangzi 莊子, Laozi 老子, Mozi 墨子, Shangshu 尚書, Shangshu dazhuan 尚書大傳, Xunzi 荀子, Mengcius 孟子, Shiji 史記, Liji 禮記, Xinshu 新書, and Kongzongzi 孔叢子) with relevant annotations written by Han and Tang scholars, such as Maogong 毛公, Zheng Xuan 鄭玄, Gao You 高誘, Wang Su 王肅, Wei Zhao 韋昭, Guo Xian 郭象, Cheng Xuanying 成玄英, and Yang Liang 楊倞. Based on this comprehensive investigation, the investigators went into in-depth analyses that successfully proved the relationship between alternative characters and annotations of ancient texts, and explored the circumstances and methods under which the Han and Tang annotators made use of alternative characters in their works as well. In 2014, the findings was first published by the PI as an article entitled “On the Relationship between Glosses in Han-Jin Commentaries and Variant Readings in Ancient Texts” 論漢晉傳注訓詁與古籍異文之關係 (refer to Part C.8.2) in a referred academic journal. After that, the PI and one of his PhD students compiled and published in 2015 a monograph entitled Collected Exegeses on the Variants in Classical Commentaries 古籍傳注異文訓詁集證 (refer to Part C.8.4). The book contains over 300 essential examples in ancient texts. Its intent was to bring a new understanding of classical annotation methods. In the study, a novel method was introduced to focus on the usage of alternative characters in classical annotations based on the evidence listed inside the book. In 2016, another paper called “Relationships between Philological Commentaries, Textual Interpretation and Alternative Characters” 論古籍之異文、詮釋與注解 (refer to Part C.9.6) written by one of our research assistants was delivered at the “Conference on Digital Humanities 2016.” In addition, the whole research team including PI and research assistants has also carried out researches on specific topics by making use of the research results. A total of 7 articles have been published or accepted for publication in different peer-reviewed journals, 7 conference papers have been delivered in several international seminars, and 3 PhD dissertations and 2 MPhil theses have been written by the research team members who are also post-graduate students of the Department of Chinese Language and Literature in CUHK. The diversity of research findings demonstrates the possibilities that can be inspired by the theories and compiled data. Other than that, ideas and conclusions from the above researches have influenced fields of Chinese studies such as classical Chinese philosophy, ancient texts relationships and the history of scholarship.

444112.label: Major findings and research outcome
444112.value: A Outcome of Theoretical and Thematic Studies After conducting comprehensive studies and investigation of the sorted data, the team has developed theories and completed several research topics. Research results have been published in different ways including peered-reviewed journals and international conferences. Since 2014, three theories have been established: 1. New mode of annotations was discovered in the traditional interpretation works (2014). 2. A further categorization to how the Annotators made use of the Alternative Characters when explaining Ancient Texts (2015). 3. By searching the reasons of the appearance of alternative characters, we have discovered that the way the annotators made use of the Alternative Characters is inevitable, which causes a strong relationship between them (2016). Meanwhile, specific research topics inspired by the above theories have been completed and made a positive impact to various academic fields including: 1. Controversial topics in Chinese studies, especially the history of scholarship 2. Rethinking of the Chinese philosophy 3. Relationship between Chinese ancient texts 4. Authentication in Chinese ancient texts 5. Classical Chinese lexicology B Breakthrough in Research Techniques and Database Establishment The core computing program of this project, named as “Alternative Characters in Han and Pre-Han Texts Data Analysis Model” (ACDAM), was designed and built by our programmer and the research team. By applying this model to our full texts databases in CHANT, alternative characters can be recognized automatically and thoroughly. Its ability to sort all the useful data related to the project is invaluable. Besides, two new databases entitled “Alternative Characters Database” and “Annotations Database” were built to publish the data based on a new structure of database design. With the new design, comprehensive functions such as searching, matching, and comparing can now be operated between two databases. C Monograph and Compilation Editing In 2015, the PI with the assistance of our trained student published a monograph entitled Collected Exegeses on the Variants in Classical Commentaries 古籍傳注異文訓詁集證 (refer to Part C.8.4). It contains over 300 essential examples in ancient texts that can definitely open a new understanding to the classical annotation methods. While the data is generated by ACDAM and then further sorted by Co-Is and research assistants, a book entitled Collection of Variant Readings of the Shangshu 尚書異文資料彙編 (refer to Part C.8.10) has been compiled and is about to be published. Once it is launched, researchers will be able to gather fragments which are not found in extant editions by using this book, and readers also are able to trace the origins of the traditional texts to an even closer degree.

444112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444112.value: Upon the completion of the project, the research findings together with the information from the two Databases have been compiled and published in academic journals and book.As the data is being sorted by our Co-Is and research assistants, the research team is compiling a series of books entitled Collection of Variant Readings Found in Han and Pre-Han Texts 先秦兩漢典籍異文資料彙編. The manuscript of the first book, Collection of Variant Readings of the Shangshu 尚書異文資料彙編 is at the final stage of editing. Three more titles, Collection of Variant Readings of the Zhuangzi 莊子異文資料彙編, Collection of Variant Readings of the Lunyu 論語異文資料彙編, and Collection of Variant Readings of the Mengzi 孟子異文資料彙編 are being prepared for successive compilations. Besides, we can now provide all instances of the three main categories of expressions found in the parallel passages in the Han and Pre-Han periods, viz., synonymous and near synonymous expressions 同義詞 / 近義詞, taboo characters 避諱字, and alternative characters 通假字. We expect to publish reference books and dictionaries of alternative characters about this kind of categories. Such reference books would be beneficial to the study of the language used in the Han and Pre-Han traditional Chinese texts.

444112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
444112.value: The project aims at examining the annotations by Han and Tang scholars. Together with relevant excavated texts and other references, the project compared the alternative characters in ancient texts with their corresponding annotations, in order to analyse the relationship between them and offer an in-depth view into how scholars since the Han dynasty had made use of alternative characters for their annotations of ancient texts. An “Alternative Characters in Han and Pre-Han Texts Database” and an “Annotations of Han and Pre-Han Texts Database” was established under the CHANT database system. The two databases were collated electronically to display instances of the similarities and differences between the alternative characters and annotations. Analyses were made on the ways annotators used alternative characters in their annotation of ancient texts. The present project has succeeded in filling this gap, referencing alternative characters with the related annotations, in order to reveal how scholars since the Han dynasty have made use of alternative characters for their annotations of ancient texts.

444212.label: Project Objectives
444212.value: Uncover the relationship between architectural form and the mission and functions of organized communities from early colonial days until their decline and the rise of professionalization and government-led institutionalization in the 1960’s. That is to say: understand the process of symbolization of architectural identity through organized communities of different natures, as well as the evolution of perception by successive generations. Retrieve, compile and reconstruct archives and documents of architects, architectural firms and institutional bodies, and so rejuvenate these neglected and scattered sources particular to Hong Kong’s urban development. Place Hong Kong’s historical urban transformation in the broad international context of nineteenth- en twentieth-century modernization processes Establish heritage values for the surviving buildings of organized communities, and so contribute to a long-term heritage policy of Hong Kong.

444212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444212.value: 香港殖民地時代早期不同的公共建設，如廟宇、教堂、學校及醫院等，均締造了香港城市發展之多元化。香港最早期的公共建設為市民提供服務和公用空間。時至今天，雖然它們對城市的影響力已有所改變，但當中不少建築物仍然得以保存，並維持其原來的用途。這種獨特的持續性，特別是處於急速的城市發展中，周邊的商業和住宅大廈紛紛重建，這些仍然保留著建築特色的公共建設，成為了香港重點的研究和保育對象。 香港最早的公共建設可追溯至1841年英國佔領香港之初，當時一些華人商行以及一些街坊團體紛紛組成一些社會組織。另外，當時在香港的外國宗教團體，如倫敦傳道會等，雖然規模較小，難以融入華人社會，但仍開始在香港建設教堂、學校及醫院。這些社區組織紛紛建設起屬於自己團體的建築，為了達到團體各方面的目的及形象。大部份的建築在興建期間，就設計概念和籌募建築經費上，均經歷了艱辛的過程。除了要在市區覓得合適的土地，更要在建築的過程和設計上能顯著地反映出該組織的理念。這些建築日後的用途以及改動亦同樣可以窺探出這些建築物的歷史變遷。在二十世紀初，社會組織以及社區建設的數量激增，他們的建築佈局更為精密，同時並以建築群的形式出現。 時至今天，大部份的香港社會組織對他們的社區建設並未有十分深入的研究，這些組織亦未曾以一個組群或社會現象的角度進行研究，同時亦未有分析其社區建設的建築過程。這個計劃將會涵蓋香港富代表性的社區建築，從他們的形成、設計和使用的過程，透過當中的特色以了解該社會組織的本身。同時，這個研究計劃亦會對涉獵參與其中的本地和外地建築師，了解他們在建築上如何配合該社會組織的要求，以及這些建築對改變公共空間起著什麼作用。最後，我們將會紀錄這些建築物的現狀，以鑑定其保育的重點，並為香港的文物保育策略作出貢獻。

444312.label: Project Title(Chinese)
444312.value: 香港三行工會的歷史與香港社會變遷

444312.label: Project Objectives
444312.value: To conduct a thorough historical review in respect of three-trade unions in Hong Kong from the 1840s to the 1930s through the collection and analyses of oral history records of elderly three-trade workers and existing archives on three-trade unions in Hong Kong and the Guangdong Pearl River Delta region. To examine the lives of three-trade workers and their development, adaptation of foreign commercial laws and management systems as well as details of foreign construction technology used in order to understand the impacts that Western systems had on Hong Kong society and its evolution. To compare the differences between Hong Kong’s three-trade unions and those from Guangdong province and observe the transformation towards professionalism as well as the role of government administrative agencies in controlling local societies.

444312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444312.value: From 1841 onwards, Hong Kong experienced a long and sustained period of rapid transformation through technology adaptation, as well as ideological and internal readjustments. New ideas that transcended traditional values were created to build Hong Kong society in a new social and economic order. From a social-historical perspective, this proposed research will study three-trade (sam hong) unions between the 1840s and the 1930s. The objective is to understand the process of how traditional values had evolved from serving as moral purposes to being subordinated to the utilitarian goals of economic and political development of modern Hong Kong. With close connections in China, three-trade workers were the earliest settlers who were capable of integrating modern technology, Western commercial laws and management mechanisms with traditional skills and knowledge in the construction of the city. They fought against the challenges of geographical obstacles, climatic limitations and problems of transport, water supply and housing caused by rapid population growth. To bring out the dynamic and interactive character of the relationships between tradition and western cultural values, the research will focus on: 1.The administrative structure and social functions of Hong Kong three-trade unions to enable analysis of the similarities and differences of three-trade unions in China placed in different political, economic and institutional contexts and understand their social mobility and economic success. 2.Three-trade unions’ social networks such as multiple friendships, dynamic business, regional affiliations, marriage linkages and family ties so as to understand how such networks supported their economic activities from the 1840s onwards and how traditional construction skills were passed down the generations. 3.The growth rates of workers engaged in three trades, their wages, livelihood situations, working conditions and trends of their entry and exit as well as strategies used by the Hong Kong government towards workers to enable Hong Kong function as a trading hub in the Asia-Pacific region. 4.Responses of three-trade unions to political movements in China, their roles in the incessant strikes and revolutionary movements that led to social instability in Hong Kong, the impact of the Hong Kong government’s political and economic policies on three-trade workers, and conflicts between three-trade workers and the colonial government. The ways that Hong Kong three-trade unions responded to Western cultural challenges and the struggles that they went through in different eras are keys to the understanding of China’s modernisation process. 歷史研究一直被認為具備鑒古知今的功能，時至今天，有關香港的歷史研究卻只側重於戰後的經濟發展，而戰前的研究，仍以政治外交為重，鮮有涉及低下階層社會狀況，香港人對戰前香港社會狀況所知有限。 自1841年起，香港長期受到外來科技和思想的衝擊，城市內部急速調整及轉型，突破傳統價值觀念的新思想被視為建立社會及經濟新秩序的良方。中國廣東省的三行工人，是最早在香港落地生根的移民。他們是結合傳統建造技術與西方建造技術、法律體系的先導者，使香港城市藉著建設工程克服因急速人口增長而必須面對的地理環境、氣候、交通、供水、房屋等種種困難。 本研究希望了解1840至1930年代香港三行工人的生活狀況，如工人數量的增長、工資、起居飲食、住房等；以至三行工會在社會經濟及政治轉型的過程中，如何建立、組織；如何把行會一向尊崇傳統道德價值作為行業運作的準則，改為附屬於經濟利益的元素等問題，進而探討1840至1930年代間，本地三行工人如何在傳統價值觀念與現代文明之間作調適、香港低下階層轉型的過程、廣東三行工人工會與香港三行工會的關係，及其對香港社會演變的影響。

444312.label: Realisation of objectives
444312.value: The definition of three-trade unions, evolution, characteristics of the three-trade sector, livelihood situations as well as wages and working conditions of three-trade workers between the 1840s and the 1930s are important as these are the foundation for the understanding of the structure of the Hong Kong community, its origins of social changes as well as its interactions with China in late Qing and the early Republican period. The fragmented and relative scarce source materials as recorded by Hong Kong government reports, contemporary publications, local materials, and oral traditions, have now been analysed and presented as a comprehensive historical review. Up till now, very limited research has been carried out on these valuable data and there is a lack of in-depth analysis. This project is the first defining work in the field that provides original insights on the subject matter. A comprehensive and profound study of social, economic, and technological impacts on the evolution of three trade unions and three trade workers will be published by the Joint Publishing Company. Students, teachers, scholars and those who are interested in this topic will be benefited from the new publication and participate in the discussions. This study fills the existing gap and provides evidence on how traditional values had evolved from serving moral purposes to being subordinated to the utilitarian goals of economic and political impacts of modern Hong Kong and China. The high illiteracy rate of three-trade workers made the subject difficult to explore. Apart from analysis of scattered and tedious archival documentary records, another source of conventional wisdom for this research came from the close connections with 170 veterans in the masonry, painting, bamboo scaffolding, carpentry and bricklaying sectors, who were affiliated with 19 different three-trade unions, among them 72 informants were over 80 years old. Their oral history not only details members’ experiences and contributions to society, but also exposes the special features of three-trade unions. To name a few, in-depth interviews were made with Hong Kong Brick-laying & Construction Trade Workers’ Union, Hong Kong and Kowloon Masons & Plasterers Union (Fei-Pang), Hong Kong and Kowloon Bamboo Scaffolding Workers Union (Tung King), Hong Kong & Kowloon Scaffolders General Merchant Association Limited, Hong Kong & Kowloon Dockyards & Wharves Carpenters General Union, Hong Kong & Kowloon Carpenters General Union, Kwong Yuet Tong, Kwong Hung Athletic Associations Limited and Hong Kong and Kowloon Painters General Union. Moreover, members have donated invaluable original local materials to the project such as certificates of registration of societies, contracts between workers and contractors, unions’ constitutions and membership rosters, and booklets on union affairs These are historical heritage of Hong Kong society that we inherit from three-trade workers. However, we could only find very limited information about some of the organisations and failed to get in touch with any senior member for oral interviews, such as Hong Kong Piling Yee On Union and Man On Union, scaffolders’ organisation Tung King Tong, the Hong Kong Scaffolders General Trade Union, set up by MA Foon in 1891 and the New Tung King Tong established in the 1940s. After the Second World War, there was political disagreement within unions. As a result, some Guomindang supporters broke away from the trade unions and set up new unions. Some of the unions are no longer in existence. Some organisations were not formally registered with the government and were similar to triad groups. Most of them were banned by the government after the riots in 1967. Traditional solidarity alliances such as clans, family ties, geographical and folk beliefs and customs are driving forces behind the formation and expansion of social networks. We were able to participate and record some of the social activities among three-trade workers such as religious ceremonies, traditional festival gatherings, anniversary celebrations. Three-trade workers worship LU Ban, an ancient Chinese carpenter, engineer and inventor, as their patron saint. Each year, members of various trade unions in the construction industry celebrate the birth of Lu Ban. Traditionally, stone workers and their descendants in Cha Kwo Ling hold such celebrations in the local Tin Hau Temple. The only Lu Ban Temple in Hong Kong is located at Ching Lin Terrace. It was built in 1884 with donations by local plastering workers and subcontractors. It has now become a major venue for construction workers to celebrate the birth of their patron saint. According to the tablet inscriptions in the temple, most donors at that time were of Siyi origins, mostly from Shunde and Xinning. On the expansion of the temple in 1888, Kwong Yuet Tong was founded specifically to manage it. Today, Hong Kong painters set up a number of organisations with the Chinese character "Kwong", such as Kwong Ying, Kwong Luen and Kwong Hung, to indicate their origins from Kwangtung, which is nowadays known as Guangdong. The members attend the Tam Kung Festival in Shau Kei Wan each year (Tam Kung is a sea deity worshiped in Hong Kong and Macau). The participations of these events help us to understand and evaluate the reasons for the formation of solidarity and interrelations between various social networks and multiple memberships in associations. The academic pursuit is on identifying the characteristics of structure and transformation of three-trade unions, functions of coherences, relations between social networks and investment cooperation, as well as organisational and structural situations of solidarities. These are reflections of the impacts of social networks that influenced the social and economic development of modern Hong Kong and China.

444312.label: Major findings and research outcome
444312.value: The government’s census data between 1870 and 1931 show that most three-trade workers were engaged in carpentry, plastering and masonry, while scaffolders and painters were in smaller numbers. Their wages did not rise significantly and remained low throughout this period. Early three-trade workers came to Hong Kong alone, leaving their families or spouses in their places of origin. Many workers returned home upon the completion of their projects, resulting in high seasonal turnover of workers. Such frequent movements enabled workers to bring their fellow villagers, friends or relatives to work in Hong Kong, thus strengthening the geographical or kinship bonds among them. According to our interviews, bachelor three-trade workers lived in poor conditions. Permanent workers lived in their employers’ shops, while those engaged in construction lived in makeshift sheds. Part-time and unemployed workers would just settle for a bed in places arranged by trade unions. By the 1970s, Tung King Tong still provided accommodation for workers at its venue. Workers of various trades lived close to one another before the Second World War, which resulted in wide-spread opium-taking and gambling among them. In addition, disputes, fighting and theft were not unusual among the workers at that time. Three-trade unions in Hong Kong often negotiated with employers on wages and benefits for their members. Labour disputes were most prominent in the 1920s. Following the promulgation of the strict Illegal Strikes and Lockouts Ordinance in 1927, strike movements almost disappeared in the 1930s. Three-trade workers were not a main force in the Canton-Hong Kong Strike in the 1920s. CHENG Chuen of the Carpenters General Union was one of the few active participants from the construction industry in the Canton-Hong Kong Strike. The Chinese Communist Party also tried to recruit members from the masonry industry in the 1930s. Our study of the relations between three-trade workers and the government covers the promulgation of related ordinances and regulations, and strike movements. The Hong Kong government never published any ordinances specifically on three-trade workers. But the buildings regulations promulgated over the years involved the occupation and life of these workers. The government published investigation reports on major construction accidents, such as the building collapse in Cochrane Street in 1901 and the Happy Valley racecourse fire in 1918. In the 1930s, the government enacted the Employment Ordinance, which regarded construction as a dangerous trade and strictly prohibited women and children from working in the industry.

444312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444312.value: The examination of the implementation procedures concerning Hong Kong’s development policies, the adaptation of law and administrative management systems, details of technology used as well as the role of government administrative agencies in overseeing three-trade workers are crucial to the evaluation of the impacts that Western systems had on the Chinese community . It helps us comprehend a change in public attitude towards the three-trade sector, from a reactive approach to a proactive approach, in order to better understand public views on the evolving procedures of the sector. The connections established with existing three-trade unions in Hong Kong can facilitate future cooperation with three-trade unions in the Pearl River Delta cities as well as China’s coastal cities. Substantial field work should be followed if time allows and resources are available. For they are essential for grasping the rhythm of transformation of lower class workers towards professionalism, their contributions and the building of social networks among Chinese cities. With existing connections and a historical review as the foundation, future cooperation can be enhanced by cultural exchange activities such as public lectures, exhibitions, conferences and publications among institutions in Hong Kong, China and other countries that are engaged in the subject matter.

444312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
444312.value: Belonging to the lower social strata, three-trade workers spend their whole lives building society. However, their contribution is not highly valued. In the meantime, infrastructure works during economic recession have always been the best political strategy to stimulate economic recovery and the three-trade sector’s employment rate is an important indicator of social stability. This study provides a new and comprehensive overview of three-trade unions and reconfirms the role of three-trade workers. The concepts of time and space in Hong Kong have undergone changes with the emergence of modern infrastructure since the mid-19th century. Efficiency is now a common value pursued by Hong Kong citizens. Nevertheless, they are worried that large-scale infrastructure works would quicken the disappearance of traditional values. In response to society’s concerns, collation of historical materials, reconstruction of oral traditions and collection of historical objects are the responsibilities of this study and these sources of materials have been given great importance in the analyses of the research. The blending of traditional values with new development concepts that we emphasize in this historical study on three-trade workers is a key for sustainable development in the future.

444412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444412.value: 由15至18歲基礎教育後的生涯標誌著由青年期步入成年期的重要歷程，亦是由高中到大學、由學校到工作、與及身份形成的發展階段。本計劃旨在研究香港青少年成長的歷程軌跡，並識別在現今教育及經濟轉型下塑造不同歷程軌跡的重要因素，尤其探討個人如何及為何在中學教育後選擇不同目標。 許多外國研究均認同追蹤研究數據對改善青少年由中學教育到中學後教育及／或工作歷程之政策釐定的必要性，其中包括近期一份主題性報告 “Making Transitions Work”（經濟合作與發展組織，2000a）。在香港，有系統地探討青少年在免費義務教育後的追蹤研究甚少，以往大部份本地的有關研究規模有限，且缺乏全面的理論架構或國際比較性。鑑於香港正朝著後工業的知識型及服務型社會迅速發展，填補此重要的知識缺口實為迫切。 「香港青少年之追蹤研究」（HKLSA）旨在為學術及政策研究提供有用的青少年追蹤數據。具體而言，本計劃會於三年內跟進一組中三至中四（相當於第九至十級）的高中學生樣本，記錄他們的教育與職業選擇，並識別不同歷程選擇的複雜性、穩定性及彈性，尤其將他們的軌跡連結至教育及經濟轉型之上。 整項計劃會分為三個階段進行：2012-13、2013-14、2014-15。建基於「香港學生能力國際評估計劃」（HKPISA）所取得的優勢，本計劃會從中三至中四的學生樣本收集其完成基礎教育後的詳細資料，當中包括認知與非認知表現、教育與職業期望、有關個人、家庭及學校層面因素，與及校內及校外的學習經歷。我們亦會期望延續本計劃，於十年內繼續以電話訪問及網上問卷追蹤學生由學校到工作或進修的歷程。基於本計劃取得的經驗及實證結果，我們會繼續於2015年尋求進一步資助，以延續HKLSA下一階段的研究。

444412.label: Realisation of objectives
444412.value: The four objectives stipulated in the proposal have been achieved to full extent. They are accomplished by the three waves of survey for students in three consecutive school years (2012-13, 2013-14 and 2014-15) and parent, teacher and school questionnaires in accordance with the project proposal. The first wave of survey was completed from April to May 2012. A total of 4670 students, 4562 parents, and 148 principals (or delegates) from 148 schools completed the respective paper questionnaires. The second wave of survey was completed from May to July 2013. To facilitate the implementation and reduce cost in data collection, two online instead of print questionnaires were administered to students and teachers in this wave. A total of 3005 students and 380 career guidance teachers/masters completed the online survey. The third wave of survey was completed from January to April 2014. Online and print questionnaires were administered to students and their parents respectively. A total of 2635 students and 2388 parents completed the survey. The sampled students and schools are consistently representative based on the coverage of different academic and social background of students and different types of schools (government, aided and private schools). On top of the data on Secondary 6 students’ choices of post-secondary education programmes in admission systems such as JUPAS and E-APP collected in the Wave 3 survey (2014-15) proposed originally, an additional survey had been conducted to collect the information on the actual destinations, that is, higher education programmes or job they had undertaken in their first post-secondary year (2015-16). Altogether, the data collected from this longitudinal study offered a comprehensive picture of transition pathways of the sampled students from the entry point to the exit point of senior secondary education. As for the first objective, the cognitive and non-cognitive competencies had been assessed in the cognitive test and student questionnaire in the Wave 1 survey. Cognitive and affective performances in the three literacy domains, that is, reading, mathematics and science were assessed and analyzed (Ho & Lam, 2016; Ho & Lau, 2015; Ho, Wong, Keung & Sum, 2017; see attached publications). Besides, data on students’ educational and career aspirations and other non-cognitive well-being measures had been collected during the senior secondary years (S.4 to S.6) in all three waves of survey. Regarding the second objective, a number of major factors were identified as contributors to adolescents’ transition outcomes. These include (i) at family level, family socio-economic background (Ho, 2016; Ho et al., 2017; Ho & Keung, 2014b); parental education and occupational status (Ho, 2016); family structure (Ho, 2016); parental involvement and investment (Ho, 2014a; Ho & Keung, 2015b; Ho & Lam, 2016); parental aspiration for their child (Ho & Keung, 2014a; Ho & Sum, 2016b); perceived parental aspiration (Ho & Keung, 2014a); parental support (Ho & Keung, 2015a); (ii) at school level, school-mean socio- economic background (Ho & Sum, 2016b); school-mean literacy performances (Ho & Sum, 2016b); career and educational exploratory activities (Ho, Keung, Yeung & Li, 2015; Ho, Wong & Sum, 2015); (iii) at student level, gender (Ho, 2014a; Ho, 2016); prior academic ability (Ho et al., 2017); literacy performances (Ho et al., 2017); career and educational decision making self-efficacy (Ho & Sum, 2016a); and career and educational search competencies (Ho, Sum & Wong, 2016; Ho, Wong & Sum, 2015; Keung, 2016). Objectives three is to examine the transition process of adolescents from secondary to various post-secondary destinations. We have constructed and validated a culture-specific instrument, namely CEDSIS, for measuring career and educational decision making self-efficacy of Hong Kong adolescents during the transition process (Ho & Sum, 2016). Principal component analysis yielded a three-factor structure, which demonstrated good model fit in confirmatory factor analysis. High reliability was found for the whole scale and each subscale, and construct validity was exhibited by the positive correlations with general self-esteem. Among the three sub-scales (“About Future Study”, “About Future Career” and “About Future Planning”), Hong Kong students had the lowest mean on “About Future Planning”, which might indicate that they lacked confidence in making long-term educational and career plans. Overall, evidence indicated that CEDSIS was a valid and reliable tool for effectively and efficiently assessing the educational and career decision-making self-efficacy of secondary students. As for the fourth objective, the transition choices and pathways of adolescents during and after senior secondary years were first identified. During the senior secondary years, transition pathways of the sampled students were rather stable, with a majority (over 90%) of them continuing their studies in a local school, and a small proportion of them (less than 5%) went for overseas studies. The transition after senior secondary years, on the other hand, was more complicated as they entered into various post-secondary destinations. The nine major destinations of the sampled students were: (1) publicly-funded bachelor degree (23%); (2) self- financing bachelor degree (9%); (3) associate degree (15%); (4) higher diploma (19%); (5) foundation diploma (8%); (6) New Yi Jin diploma (4%); (7) studying abroad (8%); (8) repeating S.6 (8%); and (9) being employed (6%). To investigate the formation of and interplay between different types of capital involved in the above transition process, multilevel linear and logic regression models had been used for analysis. Specially, transition outcomes (including educational aspiration and realization) were investigated with regards to the interplay between family socio-economic background, prior academic ability and literacy performances (Ho et al., 2017; Ho & Keung, 2014b; Keung, 2016); between socio- economic background, gender, parental investment, and career and educational exploratory activities (Ho, Sum & Wong, 2016; Ho, Wong & Sum, 2015; Keung, 2016); between parental aspiration for their child, perceived parental aspiration, socio-economic background and literacy performances (Ho & Keung, 2014a). While the various types of capital are contributors to the transition process, different types of student capabilities also appear to have a positive effect. Adolescents with high levels of capabilities such as information search skills, academic ability and self-study skills can increase their expectations of pursuing a bachelor degree. Overall, these capital and factors exhibit different effects when interacting with each other which in turn shape the transition pathways and choices of adolescents which are worthwhile for further analysis. As we revisit the proposed conceptual framework of this study, we found that evidence generally supports the idea that mobilization, formation and transformation of different forms of capital during the transition from senior secondary to post-secondary education need the multilevel support from home, school and even community. We suggest that an integrated framework incorporating Coleman and Bourdieu’ social capital theory and Sen’s capability approach will provide more comprehensive understanding of adolescents’ transition beyond secondary education. The present study suggests that social reproduction manifests itself through students’ and school socio-economic background as well as habitus pertaining to parental expectations, which shape adolescents’ post-secondary pathway leading to higher education or employment. Yet, adolescents’ likelihood of expecting to pursue a higher education qualification can be increased through strengthening their capabilities after taking into account their differing socio-economic backgrounds (Ho, Wong and Sum, 2015; Keung, 2016).
