444412.label: Major findings and research outcome
444412.value: While detailed findings can be found in the published journal and conference papers in Part C, the major ones are summarized below: (1) Educational aspirations and realization of Hong Kong adolescents: Over half of the sampled students aspired for pursuing a bachelor degree, which was followed by sub-degrees including associate degree and higher diploma, S.6 completion, and other certificates and diploma (Ho, 2016; Ho et al., 2017). A “heat-up” effect had been found in students’ aspiration for pursuing a bachelor degree from 2012-13 to 2013-14 (from 51.4% and 66.3%) (Ho et al., 2017). It was found that structural factors such as family socio-economic status (SES), and gender (being male) were positively significantly associated with aspiration and realization for bachelor degrees (Ho, 2016; Ho et al., 2017). However, students’ prior academic ability (AAI score), PISA scores and capabilities including information search and self-study skills, parental aspiration for their child and perceived parental aspiration were important for mitigating the socio-economic inequality in higher educational aspiration (Keung, 2016). (2) Career and educational exploratory activities participated by and search competencies of Hong Kong adolescents: Students’ participation in career and educational exploratory activities were significantly positively correlated with career and educational search competencies, a key capability which was found to be important for successful transition (Ho, Sum &Wong, 2016; Ho, Wong, Sum, 2015). The most popular exploratory activities undertaken by adolescents were talking to significant others, including “friends or classmates” (85% in 2012-13; 90% in 2013-14) and “family and relatives” (79% and 82% respectively), whereas the least utilized resources were those provided by employers such as visiting a job fair (8% and 12% respectively) (Ho, 2016; Ho et al., 2016).Although high-SES students had higher levels of search competencies than low-SES students, the effects of exploratory activities were found to be greater than the effects of SES, indicating that exploratory activities might be useful for empowering adolescents, especially the disadvantaged ones, by equipping them with these necessary competencies. (3) Effects of parental and community involvement on students’ competencies: Parental investment in educational resources and cultural resources at home and their involvement in social communication with their child were significantly associated with students’ literacy performance (Ho & Lam, 2016). Evidence also suggested that home-school-community collaboration and business-school partnership coordinated by university professionals might be promising gateways to nurture adolescents’ career and educational efficacy, especially those from underprivileged families, to make appropriate career and life plans (Ho, 2016).

444412.value: While the present study, being quantitative in nature, has provided information about “how” adolescents enter into different transition pathways, qualitative research can provide information about “why”, that is, the possible reasons and beliefs behind their educational and career choices. To this end, the PI of this study and a scholar from Department of Sociology, CUHK, have started a follow-up qualitative study which receives funding support from Hong Kong Institute of Asia-Pacific Studies (see Section 11). In-depth structured interviews have been conducted with 53 adolescents who participated in HKLSA study. This qualitative research will provide us with an insider’s view and enable us to make sense of the statistical results from the HKLSA study. Furthermore, the PI of this study and scholars from the Education University of Hong Kong and Hong Kong University of Science and Technology have started another follow-up study, which continues to trace the transition patterns of the HKLSA sample in their third and fourth post-secondary years (see Section 1.1). Having gained funding support from the RGC, this study will further extend our understanding to young adults’ transition under the expansion of higher education and the increasing complexity of career world.

444412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
444412.value: In Hong Kong, systematic longitudinal studies about the transition of adolescents after compulsory education are rare. This study is the first-of-its-kind research endeavor in Hong Kong for tracing the patterns of transition of adolescents. The entire project has proceeded in three waves of survey: 2012-13, 2013-14, and 2014-15. Longitudinal data has been collected from a representative sample of 4670 students, who participated in Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2012 in Hong Kong, their parents, school administrators and teachers. The study has not only collected information on students’ cognitive and non-cognitive competencies and their educational and career aspirations, but also tracked their transition pathways from the entry point to the exit point of senior secondary education. A number of important factors have been identified which shape adolescents’ transition choice and destinations. These include, to name a few, at family level, socio- economic background, parental involvement and investment; at school level, provision of career and educational exploratory activities; at student level, career and educational decision making self-efficacy and search competencies. Overall, this longitudinal study has provided an up-to-date profile of Hong Kong adolescents’ transition patterns and comprehensive understanding of its relationship with different types of social, cultural and human capital.

444512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
444512.value: 跨国公司转让价格和全球供应链的整合管理

444512.label: Project Objectives
444512.value: Develop analytical models to study the integrative management of TP and global supply chain in an MNF. Characterize the optimal TP and supply chain decisions under a number of decision structures, including centralized and decentralized supply chain decision structures; cost-based and market-based TP decision structures; and structures with different timing of setting TP. Using analytical and numerical approaches to quantify and compare optimal decisions and the global firm’s expected after-tax profits under different proposed decision structures, and identify the ways these results change when there are changes in some of the key factors in taxation (such as tax rates) and supply chain (such as cost and demand). Demonstrate the economic values of a tax-effective supply chain strategy, which integrates international tax planning and global supply chain decisions.

444512.label: Realisation of objectives
444512.value: The PI has achieved all 4 objectives of the research project. The PI has produced three new papers that are supported by this project. In all three papers, the PI studied the integrative management of a multinational firm (MNF)'s supply chains through internal coordination with transfer pricing (objective 1). Analytical models are developed and analyzed (objective 2). Key factors that will affect MNF's global tax and supply chain decisions are identified (objective 3). Through economic analysis, all three papers demonstrated the value of tax and supply chain integration (objective 4). The three papers are in various stages of review/revision. One paper was submitted to IIE Transactions. Another paper was submitted to Manufacturing & Service Operations Management and was subsequently rejected. Following a suggestion from a journal editor and expert in the area of accountancy and operations, the PI is working with co-authors to re-position the second paper for potential submission to Management Science journal's accounting division or to a top accounting journal such as Accounting Review. The third paper is under preparation for possible submission in the near future.

444512.label: Major findings and research outcome
444512.value: In the first paper titled "Global Sourcing Decisions for a Multinational Firm with Inventory Transshipment and Tax Averaging", we extended an earlier paper by considering two subsidiaries of a MNF whose supply chain decisions are linked by inventory sharing and tax averaging. A transfer pricing scheme is developed in the paper to properly align the interests of the two subsidiaries in order to achieve a higher global profitability. The extended paper finds that the MNF need to design a new coordinating scheme to take into account tax issues such as proper transfer of tax credit and liability between the two subsidiaries as well as supply chain issues such as incentives for inventory transshipment. The second paper titled "The Impact of Tax on a Multinational Firm's Strategic Decision of Selling to a Rival" considers a MNF who produces a product in a low-tax country and sells it in a high-tax country. The MNF faces the decision of whether to sell the product (and at what price) to an external rival in the retail market who has an alternative outside sourcing option. The paper finds that the regulatory rules on transfer pricing will affect a MNF's supply chain decisions in counterintuitive ways. For example, the regulatory restriction on transfer pricing may bring benefit rather than burden to the MNF. The third paper tilted "Ex-post Transfer Pricing and Global Operations Decision in a Multinational Firm" finds that a MNF's choice of timing to set its transfer price will cause operational distortions at its subsidiaries due to certain gaming behavior. The paper also propose a few strategies that will help the MNF to mitigate the negative effects of the operations distortions.

444512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444512.value: The research developed in this project is at the interface of taxation and operations. It has become increasingly important in real world practices, yet has received relatively small research efforts in the academic communities. The PI will continue to work in the interface area in the near future. In particular, the PI will investigate how recent development of tax and tariff system reform in the US and other part of the world will affect a MNF's global supply chain strategies.

444512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
444512.value: A recent survey suggests that 60% of the world's business transactions occur between multinational companies' subsidiaries. This research project studies an important problem faced by a global firm: How to effectively integrate the tax and supply chain decisions among its subsidiaries. In particular, we consider the impact of transfer pricing--an internal pricing scheme regulated by tax authorities--on a global company's supply chain decisions. We find that improper use of transfer pricing has the potential to distort supply chain decisions at subsidiaries. The global firm needs to develop an integrative management strategy that will align both tax and supply chain considerations.

444612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444612.value: China's remarkable economic growth and urban development has inevitably brought many problems in its wake, such as the loss of farmland, haphazard building construction in urban peripheries, and pollution. The relentless occurrence of such problems calls for more effective and efficient measures to manage growth. Monitoring urban growth is naturally the first step to achieving this goal. This project aims to develop a novel spatio-temporal image fusion methodology for monitoring frequent land cover change in rapidly growing areas. Voluminous remote sensing data at multiple spatial and temporal resolutions are available today for land cover change monitoring. There is, however, still no satellite sensor that can provide both high spatial resolution and temporal coverage for monitoring the frequent land cover change in high-growth regions. Given the cost and technical constraints of launching new satellites, an alternative feasible solution is to blend the existing remotely sensed data which caters for diverse land cover monitoring purposes. To date, numerous image fusion methods have focused on the exploration of different spectral and spatial characteristics of multi-sensor data. However, little attention has been paid to the simultaneous enhancement of spatial and temporal resolution. Although spatio-temporal image fusion has recently been attempted, it is still at an early stage. In particular, not only the phenology change of land cover, but also the change in land use/land cover (e.g., the conversion of bare-land into a built-up area), which is critical to the success of spatio-temporal image fusion for monitoring rapidly growing areas, should be captured and fully incorporated in the fused result. This project proposes to develop a framework that draws upon spatio-temporal contextual fusion to generate a time-series of dense high spatial resolution imagery, in support of land cover change monitoring and analysis. The novel fusion approach will capitalize on emerging compressed sensing theory, sparse representation, and sparse unmixing to achieve image super-resolution. An application of land cover change analysis using the generated dense time-series data will also be performed to demonstrate the efficacy of spatio-temporal image fusion. This project will deliver an innovative spatio-temporal fusion methodology to overcome the 'sparsity' and 'missing data' problems of observations in high spatial resolution, which has long been an obstacle to remote sensing technology. Research findings and algorithms generated by this project have numerous applications, such as monitoring of air and water pollution and vegetation growth, though this project focuses on frequent changes in land cover. 中国令人瞩目的经济增长和城市发展不可避免地带来了诸多问题，如耕地的损失、城市周边房屋的违章修建以及污染。这些严峻的现实问题，要求我们采取更有效的措施来管理增长，而监测城市扩展是实现这一目标的第一步。该项目旨在开发一种新的时空影像融合模型，用于监测快速增长区域频繁的土地覆盖变化。 如今，我们可以获取大量不同时间和空间分辨率的遥感影像，但是，仍然没有一颗卫星遥感器能提供同时具有高空间分辨率和高时间分辨率的遥感影像用于监测快速增长区域频繁的土地覆盖变化。鉴于发射新卫星受经费和技术的限制，可行的替代解决方案是融合现有的遥感数据，以满足土地覆盖监测的不同需要。 到目前为止，大量的图像融合算法都主要关注不同传感器数据之间光谱和空间特性的差异，而少有关注空间和时间分辨率的共同提高。尽管最近已有时空影像融合的尝试，但仍处于早期阶段。特别地，除了地表的物候变化，土地利用和土地覆盖的变化(如裸地变为建筑用地)也应被捕获并在融合结果中体现出来。该项目拟开发一个影像融合框架体系，利用时空融合技术产生密集时间序列的高空间分辨率影像，以支持土地覆盖变化的监测和分析。新的融合模型将利用新兴的压缩传感理论、稀疏表示以及稀疏解混技术，以实现图像的超分辨率重建。生成的密集时间序列数据将应用于土地覆盖变化分析，以展示时空影像融合方法的有效性。 该项目所提出的创新性时空影像融合方案将克服高空间分辨率观测中“稀疏”和“缺失数据”的问题，这也是遥感技术一直以来的一个障碍。尽管该项目主要关注频繁的土地覆盖变化，它的研究成果和算法也可应用于其它领域，如空气与水污染监测以及植被生长。

444612.label: Realisation of objectives
444612.value: The implementation of this project has adhered closely to the proposed four interrelated objectives. Specifically, a general framework was proposed to unify spatial-spectral fusion and spatial-temporal fusion for fast land-cover change monitoring. By using sparse representation and the Bayesian theory, some improved spatial-spectral fusion methods based on sparse matrix factorization have been developed to improve the spatial resolution of the multispectral remote sensing image. To increase the temporal resolution of remote sensing image, unmixing-based spatial-temporal fusion models have been proposed. Combining the spectral-spatial fusion method and the spatial-temporal fusion models, both the spatial and temporal resolution of the remote sensing image can be enhanced for fast land-cover monitoring with high accuracy. With respect to the evaluation of spatio-spectral-temporal image fusion methods, the spectral similarity, spatial similarity, and the performance of application (e.g. land-cover classification accuracy), are combined as indicators to measure the performance of the proposed methods. Our methods have been applied to the monitoring of urban heat islands, lake water storage changes, and land-cover changes. Overall, all the proposed objectives have been achieved to our satisfaction.

444612.value: Voluminous remote sensing data at multiple spatial and temporal resolutions are available today for land cover change monitoring. There is, however, still no satellite sensor that can provide both high spatial resolution and temporal coverage for monitoring the frequent land cover change in high-growth regions. To date, numerous image fusion methods have focused on the exploration of different spectral and spatial characteristics of multi-sensor data. However, little attention has been paid to the simultaneous enhancement of spatial and temporal resolution. Although spatio-temporal image fusion has recently been attempted, it is still at an early stage. In particular, not only the phenology change of land cover, but also the change in land use/land cover (e.g., the conversion of bare-land into a built-up area), which is critical to the success of spatio-temporal image fusion for monitoring rapid growing areas, should be captured and fully incorporated in the fused result. To overcome the drawbacks of existing spatio-temporal methods, the spatial-spectral fusion methods based on sparse matrix factorization have been developed to obtain fine spatial-spectral resolution remote sensing images by considering the 'sparsity' and 'missing data' problems of observations in high spatial resolution imagery. Meanwhile, the unmixing-based spatial-temporal fusion models have been proposed to increase the temporal resolution by accounting for both phenological and land-cover changes. By unifying spectral-spatial-temporal fusions, the fine spatial-spectral-temporal remote sensing image can be obtained for precise and fast land-cover monitoring. Through the use of the Landsat ETM imagery and MODIS imagery, the fine daily land cover classification map at 15-m resolution can be obtained using the proposed framework.

444612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444612.value: Based on the proposed spatio-temporal fusion methods, the robust and efficient add-ins of fusion module could be developed for the users of the commonly used software, e.g. ArcGIS. This developed software add-ins will contribute to promoting the applications of spatio-temporal fusion. Meanwhile, considering the ability of improving the spatial and temporal resolution of the remote sensing image, the proposed methods have a great potential in many areas, such as monitoring of the urban heat island, PM2.5, and ecological system. Therefore, further research could be exploration of applications of the proposed spatio-temporal fusion method in other study areas.

The novel fusion approaches developed under this framework capitalize on sparse representation and unmixing to achieve image super-resolution. An application in land cover monitoring has demonstrated the efficiency of the proposed spatio-temporal image fusion method.

445112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
445112.value: This pioneering research proposes to study Tibetan vernacular architecture at its cultural periphery. It aims to determine the factors that have influenced the form and spatial arrangement of domestic architecture in a context where different ethnic and cultural groups have long been residing in close proximity. This study will focus on selected Tibetan settlements on the eastern edge of the Tibetan Plateau along the current border of Qinghai and Gansu provinces, where Amdo Tibetans have lived in side by side with Hui, Baoan and Salar Muslims, Han Chinese and Mongolians. It will investigate house form and spatial arrangement along two historical trade routes: one passing through predominantly Tibetan settlements and the other through villages with a greater ethnic mix, singling out for study houses built with traditional materials and skills. The urgency of this project derives from the adverse effects on traditional architecture in the region brought about, since 2005, by the intense implementation of infrastructure and modern building development. This study will adopt a multi-disciplinary approach. Serving as the co-investigator of the project, the cultural anthropologist will observe and document everyday domestic, cultural and religious practices in individual houses and neighborhoods. Together, we explicate the relationships between architecture and social lives – particularly those that have taken place in the past fifty years, when the state policies of land reform (tudi gaige), ethnic recognition (minzu shibie) and economic reform (gaige kaifang) were all introduced into the region. Such an architecture-based multi-disciplinary study will immediately result in a deeper and more detailed understanding of the derivation of vernacular architecture in relation to community and culture. Moreover, the theoretical framework developed from the project can serve as a model for further researches on vernacular architecture at other cultural frontiers. 此研究是有關文化邊界之西藏民居建築。旨於對不同民族居住互相臨近時對其建築形態，居住空間互相影響，確定其背後有關的種種因素。此研究主要集中於青藏高原以東之邊界，青海甘肅交界的安多藏區。這些地區長期包含其他民族之聚居。其中有回族，保安族，薩拉族，漢族與蒙古族。此研究採選兩條路線。一為藏族聚居為主，另一側屬於多民族聚居地帶。此研究採用跨學科角度作探討框架。人類學者的參與會對當地居民的日常起居，宗教生活作記錄，把 生活文化的認識與對建築的了解結合。從而解答社區生活與日常文化對民居建築所形成實體影響的種種。此研究最後發展出的方法論也有助日後對其他文化邊界地區作相同之建築探討。

445312.label: Project Objectives
445312.value: to classify the international exchange programs involved using a modified version of the classification system developed by Engle and Engle (2003) and elaborated on in the glossary produced by the Forum on Education Abroad (2011). This will raise awareness of environmental/program variables (e.g., service-learning, L2 buddy system, medium-of-instruction) that impact on liberal education learning; to compare the stated liberal education aims of the home institutions with the evolving goals and aspirations of the participants. This will offer insight into the degree of focus of the students and pinpoint differences in understandings; this will provide direction for pre-sojourn orientations and on-going support; to evaluate the impact of contextual/program/individual features (e.g., type of housing, medium-of-instruction, gender, L2 proficiency, service-learning) on the participants' liberal education/‘whole person’ development (e.g.,L2 learning, intercultural competence, personal/intellectual/academic development, global-mindedness, critical thinking) and compare these findings with the liberal education/learning of the control group at each institution (undergraduates on their home campus prior to going on exchange); to provide comparative, mixed-method data that clearly documents the challenges and ‘whole person’ development that the various cohorts and individuals experience over time and space (from the pre-sojourn phase until one year post sojourn); to determine the appropriateness of Deardorff’s (2008, 2009) intercultural competence model, Bennett’s (1993) Developmental Model of Intercultural Sensitivity (DMIS), and Kolb’s (1984) learning cycle to help explain the developmental trajectories of student sojourners from Greater China. (The Intercultural Development Inventory (IDI), an internationally-recognized psychometric instrument which is linked to the DMIS, (Hammer, 2009a, b) will measure the participants' intercultural sensitivity at strategic intervals); to offer concrete, data-driven, theory-inspired suggestions to: a) enhance the ‘whole person’ development of outgoing exchange students from Greater China and other parts of Asia (e.g., optimize liberal education through quality pre-sojourn programming, on-going sojourn support, and re-entry debriefings/curricula); b) bolster internationalization at home (IaH) initiatives in Asian institutions (e.g., maximize the contribution/integration of returnees); c) facilitate on-going evaluation of the liberal education of international exchange students at participating insitutions; and d) encourage other collaborative, institutional EA projects in the region.

445312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
445312.value: The number of students from Hong Kong and Mainland China who participate in international exchange programs has increased dramatically in recent years, with particular growth in semester-long sojourns. While comprehensive institutions of higher education in Greater China typically set liberal education outcomes for students in all Faculties, little is known about the impact of an exchange experience on the ‘whole person’ development of Chinese students (e.g., second language (L2) proficiency, intercultural knowledge and competence, global-mindedness, foundation and skills for lifelong learning). The proposed study, which aims to fill this gap, will involve collaboration between leading comprehensive universities in Hong Kong, Beijing, Nanjing, and Shanghai, and build on earlier ethnographic and experimental-design investigations of L2 student sojourners from Hong Kong (and Beijing). A rigorous pretest, post-test, and delayed post-test (one year later) control group study will investigate the ‘whole person’ development of semester-long exchange students from the four institutions (N = 1,900). Drawing on student development theories, this mixed-method study will begin by comparing the liberal education aims of the home institutions with the students’ own objectives for going on exchange. At strategic intervals, a range of quantitative and qualitative measures will be employed to delve into the nature and impact of the sojourn, and facilitate a comparison with student development on the home campus. Each experimental cohort will be tracked from the selection process until one year post-sojourn, affording a comparison of pre- and post-sojourn learning and individual/group variations in outcomes, taking into account environmental/program characteristics. Data will consist of internationally-recognized measures (e.g., the Intercultural Development Inventory), Entry and Exit International Exchange surveys, focus groups, in-depth semi-structured interviews, ejournals/blogs, academic records, and program documents. By developing a deeper understanding of student learning (e.g., sojourn aims, intercultural adjustment/competence, L2 learning/use, social networks, academic performance/intellectual development, critical thinking, personal growth, global citizenship, identity change, professional goals), concrete suggestions can be made to enhance the selection process as well as pre-sojourn, sojourn, and re-entry programming. Ultimately, this theory-driven research will identify ways to optimize the ‘whole person’ development of exchange students from Greater China and suggest concrete ways to enhance internationalization efforts. The findings will also provide valuable insight for institutions abroad that receive exchange students from this region. Finally, this study will demonstrate the merits of collaboration among institutions and serve as an evaluation model of international/L2 learning for other institutions of higher education in Asia and beyond. 近幾年來中國內地和香港的出國交流學生急劇增加。與此同時，越來越多的學生選擇一個學期的出國交流項目。雖然中國的綜合性大專院校對不同學系的學生在博雅教育方面進行測評，然而很少研究專注於評估出國交流對於中國學生在全人發展方面的影響，比如對學生第二語言發展，跨文化知識及能力，全球意識，終身學習的能力和技巧的影響。此擬議的研究旨在填充此空白。在之前研究（對香港和北京高校出國交流學生的人類學實驗調查）的基礎上，此研究將進一步擴大並涵蓋了來自香港，北京，南京，上海的四所綜合性重點高校，調研人數為1900人。本研究採用實驗組-控制組之對比研究方法，由出國交流前、後以及一年後的評估結果來衡量一學期的出國交流經歷對出國交流學生全人發展的影響。在學術發展理論的指導下，此混合法實驗研究將先對比出國交流學生的出國動機和目的及其所在學校的博雅教育目標。在指定的時間（比如出國前，回國後，回國一年後），研究者將會用一系列定性及定量研究工具來調查學生的出國交流情況以及此經歷對其個人綜合發展的影響。此結果將與同時期未出國學生的個人發展情況進行比較。該研究對於實驗組（即出國交流組）學生的調研將從他們申請交流開始並一直維持到學生回國後一年。此研究將對比學生出國交流前後的個體/小組發展情況及個體/小組間差異。在分析結果的同時交流項目本身的特點以及學生所處的環境都會被列入研究範圍。本研究的數據將包含Intercultural Development Inventory（一種國際認可的跨文化能力測評工具）,出國前後問卷調查，深入的半結構化團體及個人訪談，日記，博客，學生學業記錄，項目檔案等。通過此研究，學校會對出國交流學生及其經歷有更深入的瞭解（比如學生的出國交流目標，跨文化適應能力，第二語言學習及應用，社交情況，學術表現及發展，批判性思維的發展，個人發展，全球化公民，個人身份變化，職業目標等）。此研究將不僅為學校對於出國交流學生的篩選以及出國前後的指導提供建議性的意見，還將對接收中國學生的海外高校提供有價值的建議。此外，該研究還將對中國出國交流的學生提供實質性的建議從而最大程度的優化其經歷。最後，本研究還會展現校際合作研究的價值以及為其他的亞洲及海外高校如何評估學生的出國交流經歷提供參考和借鑒。

445312.label: Realisation of objectives
445312.value: 1. The exchange programs that the participants joined were categorized using a modified version of the Forum on Education Abroad’s (2011) glossary to provide useful contextual information about the study abroad experience of the participants. (Additional details were gathered from the participants.) 2. The internationalization aims of the participating institutions were determined by reviewing: i) strategic plans, ii) University/Faculty websites, program brochures, etc., and iii) reports prepared by the Office of Academic Links (OAL) (or similar office) at each institution, when available. Institutional aspirations for exchange students were then compared with those of the students themselves (as indicated in their application essays (study plans), pre-sojourn questionnaire surveys, and pre-sojourn interviews). A comparison of the institutional and student data revealed differences in sojourn aspirations and expectations. While most of the students had set personal goals for the sojourn, many had vague ideas about aims for other domains (e.g., no specific academic or professional goals). Some viewed the exchange program as a ‘gap year’ (e.g., an escape from the academic pressures of Hong Kong). Few had considered language and culture-learning strategies to optimize their stay abroad (e.g., ways to diversify their social networks and gain access to local communities of practice). The pre-sojourn data also revealed that many of the students were anxious and did not feel well prepared for the sojourn, although the reasons for this differed. For example, students from the PRC institutions tended to be more concerned about a language barrier than the CUHK cohort. The findings provided useful insight into aspects that should be addressed in pre-sojourn orientations (e.g., the difference between a ‘gap year’ and an international exchange program, the benefits of setting specific sojourn goals in different domains, strategies to optimize international experience). The pre-sojourn data also has implications for receiving institutions (e.g., ways to orientate and support the adjustment and learning of incoming exchange students from Greater China). 3. In total, 1620 semester-long international exchange students completed the pre-sojourn questionnaire surveys and post-sojourn questionnaire surveys. ~100 interviewees from the participating institutions (~15 per cohort per semester) also shared their views about their international educational experience in in-depth semi-structured interviews before and after their sojourn (90 minutes for pre-sojourn interview, on average; 120 minutes for post-sojourn interview, on average). The interviewees also responded to email prompts during the sojourn. All of the interviewees completed the Intercultural Development Inventory (IDI) before and after the semester. At CUHK, there was a Control Group (719 students on the home campus prior to participating in an international exchange program) and these participants also completed pre- and post-semester questionnaire surveys to facilitate a comparison of their learning with the cohort that was abroad. A similar Control Group was not possible at the PRC institutions as, unlike CUHK, they did not select exchange students for terms 1 and 2 at the same time. This meant that we could not identify the students who were to go abroad the following semester. (To have comparable groups, it is important to have all students who are planning to join an exchange program.) Compared with students who had completed a semester abroad, the 'at home' groups generally experienced less growth in intercultural sensitivity as measured by the IDI. 4. The study generated comparative mixed-method data that documented the intercultural learning and ‘whole person’ development of the international exchange students before, during, and after a semester in the host country. The pre- and post- International Exchange Experience questionnaires were processed by SPSS; the IDIs were analyzed by IDI, LLC in the USA. For each cohort, an NVivo project database was created to bring together all of the data (e.g., questionnaire survey results, application essays, interview transcripts, responses to email prompts) and facilitate the coding and analysis of the qualitative data and linkage with quantitative findings. Case nodes were also created for each interviewee (focal case participant) to facilitate the development of narrativized accounts of their journeys and help to identify individual and environmental factors that were playing a role in their ‘whole person’ development. The pre- and post- International Exchange Experience Questionnaire survey data (including the IDI results) were compared to gain a sense of the impact of the stay abroad on individual sojourners as well as full cohorts. At CUHK, where there was a control group, the intercultural learning of the students who took part in a semester abroad program was compared with that of students who were on the CUHK campus during the same time period before taking part in their own semester-long international exchange program. The analysis of the questionnaire survey data and interview transcripts shed light on the impact of independent variables (contextual/ program/individual features including program location, type of housing, individual learning objectives, gender, host language proficiency, level of cross-cultural adaptability/openness) on dependent variables (sojourn outcomes including level of satisfaction, academic achievement, host language use/ enhancement, intercultural competence/ networks, personal/ intellectual/academic development, career choices). One year after the participants had returned to their home campus, they were invited to complete a post-post- sojourn questionnaire survey, and the results were linked to the pre-sojourn and post- sojourn findings. A sampling of the interviewees also took part in post-post interviews on Skype to gain a sense of the longer-term impact of the sojourn on their ‘whole person’ development. 5. The mixed-method data was linked to Deardorff’s (2008, 2009) intercultural competence model, and Hammer’s Intercultural Development Continuum (Hammer 2012, 2013), an updated version of the Developmental Model of Intercultural Sensitivity (Bennett 1993). The IDI findings, when triangulated with the qualitative and quantitative data (e.g., interview transcripts, open and closed questionnaire survey responses, responses to email prompts) helped to identify internal and external elements that led to differences in sojourn outcomes. Many of the elements that featured in the theories proposed by Bennett, Deardorff, and Hammer (e.g., intercultural attitudes, behaviors) were found in the database, pointing to the complexity of intercultural development’. The findings also challenged common ‘immersion assumptions’ about study abroad experience. In particular, this study raised awareness of agency and host receptivity as core elements that can impact the intercultural competence development of student sojourners. 6. Drawing on the findings, advice for education abroad administrators and programmers has been offered through various channels (e.g., refereed journal articles, book chapters, and local, regional, and international presentations at international education and applied linguistics conferences, including keynote addresses) and the Study Abroad Research Network of the World Congress of Applied Linguistics (Brisbane 2013; Rio de Janeiro 2017). At CUHK, two intercultural communication courses have also been developed or refined, drawing on the data and findings of this study; these intercultural interventions have benefited many undergraduates. ‘Intercultural Communication and Engagement Abroad’ is a fully online, credit-bearing General Education course for international exchange students to take while they are in the host country (~22 per course). Data from this study (e.g., anonymous excerpts from interview transcripts and responses to email prompts during the sojourn) has also been incorporated into 'Intercultural Transitions: Making Sense of International Experience', a course for students with recent or current international experience. Numerous publications and presentations describe/evaluate these courses. (See Section C). In sum, nearly all of the program objectives were fully achieved. The exception relates to #3 as it was not feasible to have a comparable control group in the PRC institutions.

to evaluate the impact of independent variables (contextual/ program/ individual features including program duration/ location, type of housing, individual learning objectives, gender, host language proficiency, level of cross-cultural adaptability/ openness) on dependent variables (sojourn outcomes including level of satisfaction, academic achievement, host language use/ enhancement, intercultural competence/ networks, personal/ intellectual/ academic development, career choices) and compare these findings with the learning of the control group (undergraduates on their home campus prior to their sojourn, when feasible);
to provide comparative research data that clearly documents the range of potential learning and challenges that individuals experience in different types of programs over time;

to problematize the Developmental Model of Intercultural Sensitivity (DMIS) (Bennett (1993), which is linked to the Intercultural Development Inventory (IDI), an internationally-recognized psychometric instrument used in the study;

to offer data-driven, concrete suggestions to: a) enhance the selection and learning of SA students from Asia (e.g., maximize their development through quality pre- and post- SA curricula/ on-going SA support;b) bolster internationalization at home (IaH) initiatives in Asian insitutions (e.g., maximize the contribution/ integration of SA returnees); c) enhance SA program evaluation/ outcomes-based assessment.

445312.label: Major findings and research outcome
445312.value: 1. The analysis of the pre-and post- IDI results and qualitative findings for each cohort generally supported the notion underpinning the Intercultural Development Continuum (IDC) (Hammer 2013). When the participants developed a more sophisticated’ understanding of cultural difference, their intercultural competence grew. While some experienced significant growth in ‘whole person development’, many others became more ingroup-oriented. A comparison of pre- and post- IDI results and a review of the qualitative data revealed that many sojourners regressed in terms of intercultural competence. These individuals spent nearly all of their free time with co-nationals and became less willing to initiate intercultural interactions in their second language. In general, the findings pointed to the need for research-driven intercultural interventions at all stages of the study abroad cycle (pre-sojourn, sojourn, post-sojourn) to fully optimize and extend the international educational learning of students from Greater China. Interestingly, post-post sojourn findings revealed that the full impact of international educational experience may not be fully realized until long after the students have returned home, underscoring the need for longitudinal studies. 2. At CUHK’s 2013 Learning and Teaching Expo, the PI delivered a keynote address, which stressed the need to scaffold the learning of education abroad students. Following the talk, the PI was invited by the Director of General Education to develop an online intercultural communication course for international exchange students to take while abroad. 'Intercultural Communication and Engagement Abroad', a credit- bearing, elective course has been offered annually since 2014-15. 3. Presentations about this study have been made at local, regional, and international conferences, including plenaries and keynote addresses. 4. With Prof. John Plews, the PI is co-editing a special issue of the journal 'Study Abroad Research in Second Language Acquisition and International Education' (John Benjamins) with the theme ‘Study abroad: To, from, and within Asia’ (2017). This journal includes two articles that focus on the GRF project. As well as numerous articles and book chapters, the PI has co-edited a book with Prof. Susan Oguro 'Intercultural Interventions in Study Abroad'; Routledge 2017) and co-authored a monograph with Prof. Fred Dervin 'Interculturality in Study Abroad', Routledge 2017). Both draw on this project. (See Part C for a list of presentations and publications.) 5. In sum, the analysis of the rich data helped to formulate recommendations for the enhancement of the 'whole person development' of international exchange students from Greater China both in the home environment and abroad, and also identified aspects that merit further exploration.

445312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
445312.value: This study served as groundwork for a pilot study of the academic/social integration of Chinese students who participated in a semester-long international exchange program in Australasia in 2016-17. (A GRF proposal was submitted in October 2016). The PI, Gary Barkhuizen (the University of Auckland) and Phil Benson (Macquarie University) are developing case studies of participants. Lessons learned from the 2013-16 GRF project informed the design of protocols/procedures and also pointed to the need to pay closer attention to language identity elements and the social network formation of study abroad participants. None of the focal case participants in the present study were based in Australasia and the pilot study and 2016-17 GRF proposal will address this gap. Collaboration with my Australasian partners has facilitated the development of an Australian Research Council ‘Discovery project’ proposal under the direction of Phil Benson (Macquarie University). If funded, this project ‘Environmental influences on international student language learning’ will involve seven collaborators in Australia, Hong Kong, and New Zealand. The proposal was submitted in March 2017. Publications and presentations related to the present study are encouraging administrators and educators to pay attention to the quality of international educational experience, with recommendations for both home and host institutions.

445312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
445312.value: This study investigated the ‘whole person development’ of 1620 undergraduates from Hong Kong and Mainland Chinese universities who participated in a semester-long international exchange program, where they took courses in a second language. As well as completing pre- and post- international exchange experience questionnaires, a sampling of students from each cohort were interviewed in-depth before and after their sojourn and responded to email prompts. The Intercultural Development Inventory (IDI), a cross-culturally-validated psychometric instrument, measured the interviewees’ level of intercultural competence before and after their sojourn. Although some students benefited from their international experience (e.g., developed more intercultural sensitivity, enhanced their willingness to use their second language), a complex mix of internal and external elements resulted in different outcomes, with some cohorts regressing in terms of intercultural competence, after their stay abroad. By identifying and acquiring a deeper understanding of the factors that hinder or facilitate the ‘whole person’ development of student sojourners, it has been possible to develop an online course in Hong Kong, which fosters the intercultural learning and engagement of international exchange students. This study has also resulted in the offering of concrete suggestions to optimize the pre-sojourn, sojourn, and re-entry experiences of education abroad students from Asia.

445312.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
445312.value: This study served as groundwork for a pilot study of the academic/social integration of Chinese students who participated in a semester-long international exchange program in Australasia in 2016-17. (A GRF proposal was submitted in October 2016). The PI, Gary Barkhuizen (the University of Auckland/WUN member) and Phil Benson (Macquarie University) are developing case studies of participants. Lessons learned from the 2013-16 GRF project informed the design of protocols/procedures and also pointed to the need to pay closer attention to language identity elements and the social network formation of study abroad participants. None of the focal case participants in the present study were based in Australasia and the pilot study and 2016-17 GRF proposal will address this gap. In 2016-17, the PI was awarded a CUHK Faculty Outward Mobility Grant to visit the University of Auckland, Macquarie University, and the University of Technology Sydney in January 2017 (two weeks). Collaboration with the PI's Australasian partners has facilitated the development of an Australian Research Council ‘Discovery project’ proposal under the direction of Phil Benson (Macquarie University). If funded, this project ‘Environmental influences on international student language learning’ will involve seven collaborators in Australia, Hong Kong, and New Zealand. The proposal was submitted in March 2017. During this project, the PI collaborated with Professor Susan Oguro (University Technology Sydney) to co-author a book for Routledge entitled 'Intercultural Intervention in Study Abroad' (2017) and also co-authored a monograph for Routledge with Professor Dervin (University of Helsinki)(2017). The title of the book is 'Interculturality in Study Abroad'. In October 2016, the PI was awarded the 2016 the Hong Kong Research Grants Council (RGC) 'Prestigious Fellowship under Humanities and Social Science Panel' (HSSPFS) to conduct a project entitled ‘Intercultural communication and engagement abroad: An ethnographic investigation of an online intervention in international exchange programs (Award: HK $831,220.00). This project, which will be conducted in 2017-18, will focus on the online intercultural transitions course that was developed for international exchange students, drawing on data and understandings that emerged from the present study. During the project, the PI was invited to give talks ('distinguished lectures') about this research at universities in Australia, China, Finland, Hong Kong, Macau, and New Zealand.

445812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
445812.value: The position of Assistant Principal (AP) is the gateway to the school management apex for teachers, representing a significant milestone in his/her career. Although the promotion is seen as a logical career movement, the adjustment for the new role is not without challenges to new APs. As a teacher, his activities in schools are prescribed by the timetable with a clearly defined teaching role; he finds his job predictable and controllable. As an AP, he realizes the position is characterized by role ambiguity and role overload; he is often tasked with unanticipated and amorphous responsibilities by the principal. He finds his previous expertise in teaching is no longer an asset to him in the new role. Being the “man in the middle” is not an enjoyable experience; he finds it hard to strike a balance between being accountable to the principal and simultaneously maintaining friendly relationships with teachers. He realizes that the transition from teaching to administration entails a re-orientation in both professional and social roles; the former relates to the acquisition of the technical knowledge required of the job and the latter pertains to being socially accepted by other organizational members. Drawing on the developmental stage theory and using a mixed-methods approach, the proposed study seeks to understand the socialization process of beginning APs in Hong Kong. The literature defines socialization as the process of learning a new role which comprises the professional and the social components; the former relates to task socialization and the latter relates to relationship socialization. As APs move from novice to veteran, they generally go through the developmental stages of initiation, transition, and incorporation. The proposed study aims to investigate the challenges beginning APs face and their coping strategies in their passage way moving from teaching to administration. The qualitative part of this study traces the development of 20 beginning APs from diverse demographic backgrounds and school contexts in both primary and secondary sectors over a period of two years with a view to understanding the content, tactics, and sources of their learning and their adjustment tactics in the various developmental stages. The quantitative part aims to understand the socialization experiences of novice APs in all Hong Kong schools in general. Integrating the two sets of findings, the study provides valuable and timely information to policy-maker and practitioners to help APs develop. 副校長的職位不僅是教師事業發展之重要里程碑，更是通往其學校管理生涯頂峰的途徑。雖然從教師晉升到副校長乃必然性的事業變遷，然而對於新上任的副校長而言，新職位在適應上充滿了挑戰。 一般來說，教師的工作範疇為授課時間表所規限，教學角色明確且清晰。相較之下，副校長的角色定位顯得十分模糊，職務較繁雜。副校長經常被校長要求處理突如其來的雜務，這使當事人感到自己從前在教學累積的工作經驗無從應用。身為夾雜在校長與教師間的中間人也甚具挑戰；既要對校長負責，又要維持與教師的友好關係，兩者間的平衡並不好拿捏。新任副校長隨即意識到，從教學到行政的過渡期需要當事人對自己的專業及社交角色重新定位，前者有利於獲取工作上需要的專業知識，後者關係到與同濟相處是否融洽。 此研究以發展理論為參考，旨在通過混合研究法了解新任副校長的社會化過程。文獻對社會化的定義為學習新角色的過程，由專業及社交兩個部分組成；前者涉及獲取專業知識以妥善履行職務，後者與新角色受同儕的接納度有關。從新手到資深，副校長總歸會經歷一段發展過程，包括啟發期、過渡期及融合期。此項研究旨在探索香港新任副校長所面臨的挑戰，以及在教學過渡行政期間，他們採取了甚麼樣的對策。此項研究質性的部分通過追蹤來自不同背景、於不同學校任職的新副校長，為期兩年，以了解他們在不同發展階段所採取的學習及適應方案。研究量性部分旨在統計香港新任副校長社會化的經驗。研究綜合質與量兩部分，為有關決策者提供有力與及時的資訊以助副校長的整體發展。

445812.label: Realisation of objectives
445812.value: The four objectives set out in the proposal have all been achieved. I am particularly pleased with the response rate in the quantitative part of the study, which can be taken as an indicator of the welcomeness of a study on assistant principals (AP) in Hong Kong. The findings suggest that the preparation of vice-principals in Hong Kong should be urgently attended to. More often than not, the promotion of a teacher to the position of vice-principal is a recognition of his/her contribution to the school in the area of teaching. Unfortunately, the career advancement has often dragged them out from their comfort zone and put them in a new role. To this end, the dual career track practised in the US system can be an avenue to resolve this dilemma.

445812.label: Major findings and research outcome
445812.value: The quantitative part of the study reveals that 1. The findings suggested that acceptance and endorsement of colleagues were the most critical factor affecting AP’s perceived efficacy in Hong Kong schools in which relatively low job mobility was seen in teachers. 2. The promotion of a teacher to the AP position often triggers an abrupt change in the prevailing hierarchical structure in a Hong Kong school given the low staff mobility rate. In the light of a high power-distance school culture as that exhibited in HK, APs are promoted from positions collectively related to other teachers to positions socially remote from the rest of the school; they need to be psychologically prepared to adjust to the change and to be accepted by their colleagues. The results also showed that if APs could be provided with timely and proper feedback on their performance, they would be less anxious in coping with their new position. 3. The regression results suggested that Feedback mechanisms only helped the newly appointed APs (β=.241, p<.05) in adapting to their new role and its effect diminished as APs accumulated more on-the-job experience. It is of particular interest to note the importance of colleagues’ acceptance to the development of APs’ efficacy. The results suggested that newly appointed APs would need the endorsement of their peer colleagues in helping them to psychological prepared for the changing role; they might feel more competent in coping with the changes in the second year of office. However, when they move into their 3 years, they would probably start to realise the importance of getting colleagues’ support if they had to effectively deploy the frontline teachers and to maintain their motivation and commitment to accomplish school objectives. The qualitative part of the study points to three dilemmas posed to the informants: juggling administrative work with teaching, standing by the management or siding with peer teachers, and forced innovation vs. omnipresent conservatism. The findings also reveal strategies employed by the informants in alleviating the impact of the dilemmas for a smoother assumption of their responsibilities, such as attending academic programmes offered by universities and networking with professional peers. Based on the experiences of vice-principals as evident in our study, this study suggests that avenues structuralizing the informal support from external bodies and school sponsoring bodies.

445812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
445812.value: The findings of this study, revealing that principal’s support, colleagues’ acceptance and school feedback mechanisms are the three important elements affecting APs’ smooth transition from the teaching role to administrative role, shed light on the necessity to examine the contribution of APs within the context of group and school-level activities. One of the major challenges found amongst APs in this study is their mediator role in schools; APs are often found themselves being trapped between a rock and a hard place whereby they are held accountable to the principals on the one hand and to gain colleagues’ support on the other. In this connection, the relationship between the principals and the APs holds potentials for school improvement. A brief review in the existing educational leadership literature reveals that this is an unexplored area; to this end, further studies on the strategic role of APs in schools are warranted and timely.

445812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
445812.value: This study attempts to understand the process of socialisation a vice-principal will take in his/her transition from a teaching to an administrative role in the school. The results suggested both personal and school factors would have an effect on their transition. Female APs and those APs working in bigger schools felt less efficacious than their counterparts. The findings also revealed that colleagues’ acceptance and school feedback mechanisms contributed significantly to the smooth transition of APs when they first moved from the teaching role to the administrative role. However, the importance of feedback mechanisms appeared to fade out as they had been progressively settling in their new role in the later years. On the contrary, the importance of colleagues’ acceptance intensified as APs moved to their third year of office. In a cultural context in which harmonious working relationship is highly valued and staff mobility is relatively low, it is important for the policy-makers and practitioners to develop a fair and transparent succession plan with a view to improving the acceptability of the newly appointed AP in schools.

446112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
446112.value: 梁啟超於1902年創辦的《新小說》雜誌，長久以來被視作中國近代小說的開端，他認為小說是啓蒙民智及改良國家不可缺少的工具。本研究對傅蘭雅(John Fryer, 1839-1928)在1895年舉辦的一次徵文比賽中留下的150份未出版的手稿，即近年被發現的《時新小說》，進行初次系統性的批判考察，試圖挑戰或修正以上這主流的論述。《時新小說》的深遠影響建立於一個假設：這批作品在很大程度上啓發及影響了梁啟超之後發起的「小說界革命」。 這批彌足珍貴的小說可以填補中國現代文學史一個被忽視卻又關鍵的環節，其價值遠遠超過僅僅反映晚清時期的文化景觀及社會政治潮流。《時新小說》的不少作者在文學進路及宗教詩學上具有原創的經驗，在中國傳統敘事中糅合了西方敘事技巧，同時又在基督教的主題和思想中融合了儒家、佛教及道教等元素。這表明基督教想像力與象徵方式藉語言、文化的手段進入新的跨語境形式，不僅開擴了晚清讀者的文學、宗教想像，也為中國作家提供了新的思想模式及表達風格。 本研究有三個主要的學術貢獻：第一，補充及修正關於中國現代小說緣起、新文學體裁與白話文的發展的傳統說法。第二，論證宗教維度在中國現代小說的詩學及話語形成中尤關重要。第三，致力將基督教小說放在前沿的研究領域當中，嘗試改變中國文學與文化現代性的研究範式。這個項目在中國現代文學史研究中具有重大的學術意義。

446112.label: Realisation of objectives
446112.value: This project has, to a large extent, achieved most of the proposed objectives by making the first critical and comprehensive attempt to investigate the newly discovered Shi xin xiaoshuo (時新小說 New Age Novels), some 150 pieces of unpublished manuscripts for the fiction contest organized by John Fryer (1839-1928) in 1895. The research findings has challenged and modified the dominant narrative that the story of modern Chinese fiction conventionally commences with Liang Qichao’s (梁啟超) founding of the journal Xin xiaoshuo (新小說 New Novels) in 1902, and that Chinese literary modernity was fundamentally secular or anti-religious. An in-depth study of this invaluable corpus of novels has filled in an overlooked yet crucial chapter in the history of modern Chinese literature. The worth of these works goes beyond the mere reflection of the cultural landscape and socio-political trends of the late-Qing period. Quite a few writers conducted some original experiments in terms of literary approaches and religious poetics. Traditional Chinese narrative techniques were integrated with western rhetorical devices, while Buddhist and Daoist elements were hybridized with Christian themes and thoughts. A typically intriguing example is Qu mo zhuan (驅魔傳) by Guo Zifu (郭子符). Readers are struck by the multifarious and multi-religious celestial world, an ingenious adaptation of the biblical account of the eternal battle between the creator God and the fallen angel-turned-Satan who headed a large gang of devils with vivid Chinese characteristics, for instance, the ghosts of opium (大烟鬼) and of foot-binding (纏足鬼), which symbolized the social evils of late-Qing China. This demonstrated the ways in which Christian imagery and symbolism were transformed by linguistic and cultural manipulation into new contextualized forms which not only expanded the literary and religious imagination of late-Qing readers but also offered new modes of thought and expression for Chinese writers. This project has largely foregrounded the importance of Christian inspired novels in the formation of modern Chinese poetics and discourse. I have published four academic articles, one refereed monograph, one annotated volumes of novels, and presented four papers in international conferences, much more productive than my original anticipated output of three to four articles. The in-depth examination of representative New Age Novels in the monograph and articles have helped to draw some theoretical observations for a deeper understanding of the strategies of the literary endeavours of Chinese Christian writers. The annotated volume has made the rarely known works of Chinese Christian novels readily accessible to the academic world. The republication of major primary texts will be of considerable value to scholars of the history of Christianity in China and of modern Chinese literature.

446112.label: Major findings and research outcome
446112.value: Published in the reputable National Taiwan University (NTU) and Harvard-Yenching Institute (HYI) Academic Book Series, by the National Taiwan University Press, my monograph 《福音演義：晚清漢語基督教小說的書寫》(Attuning the Gospel: Chinese Christian Novels of the Late Qing Period) examines critically the textual strategies of a couple of representative New Age Novels, together with other missionary novels, where Christianity was contextualized and indigenized in the Chinese literary and cultural milieu during the final years of the nineteenth century. The pioneering volume 《道德除害傳──清末基督徒時新小說選》(Daode Chuhai Zhuan: Selected New Age Novels by Late-Qing Chinese Christians) collected and elaborately annotated five representative works of New Age Novels submitted to this contest by the Chinese Christian writers to this fiction contest. This volume has made the original manuscripts much more accessible to scholars in the fields of Christianity in China and of modern Chinese literature. The four refereed journal articles have explored new research themes and approaches by doing a critical textual analysis of several pieces of under-researched New Age Novels. Some writers conducted original experiments in terms of literary creation and religious poetics. For instance, Wuming xiaoshuo (無名小說, Unnamed Novel) by Zhang Tianshu (張佃書) manifested rich intertextual relations with William Burns’ Mandarin translation of the Pilgrim’s Progress by transforming the entire allegory into a piece of traditional Chinese shidiao (時調 popular tune) in twelve stanzas, being sung by one the characters in the novel. The shidiao exhibited the hybridity of multiple religious expressions, with the Confucian, Buddhist and Daoist elements intricately intermingled to accommodate and communicate the Christian thoughts and biblical imagery in Pilgrim’s Progress. Henceforth, the Chinese Pilgrim’s Progress facilitated the introduction of Western narrative elements and Christian poetics for the creation of late-Qing Chinese fiction.

446112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
446112.value: With my established track record in the research and publication of Chinese Christian Novels, including the missionary novels and New Age Novels, I have been invited to play a prominent role in the internationally collaborative publication project "清代基督宗教小說選注", headed by Prof. Wallace Sher-shiueh Li of Academia Sinica (Taiwan), together with Prof. Soon-Bang Oh of Soongsil University (Korea). The multi-volume annotated collection of Chinese Christian novels, including a number of representative New Age Novels, will be published by Academia Sinica. This publication project aims to further contribute to complementing, if not revising, traditional accounts about the rise of modern fiction, the development of new literary genres and vernacular language in China.

446112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
446112.value: This project has filled in an overlooked yet crucial chapter in the history of modern Chinese literature. This project has launched the first critical attempt to investigate the recently discovered Shi xin xiaoshuo (時新小說 New Age Novels), some 150 pieces of unpublished manuscripts for the fiction contest organized by John Fryer (1839-1928) in 1895. Three major academic contributions have been made. Firstly, it has contributed to complementing, if not revising, traditional accounts about the rise of modern fiction, the development of new literary genres and vernacular language in China. Secondly, it has substantiated previous claims about the importance of religious dimension in the formation of modern Chinese poetics and discourse. These novels shed new lights on the process and strategies through which Christianity was contextualized and indigenized in the Chinese literary and cultural milieu during the final years of the nineteenth century. Thirdly, it changes the face and paradigm of research on Chinese literary and cultural modernity by situating Christian inspired novels in the forefront of a new and highly significant field of study. The academic implications of this project for both the modern Chinese literary and intellectual history are profound.

446912.label: Project Title(Chinese)
446912.value: 從知識論角度重新詮釋康德形上學

446912.label: Project Objectives
446912.value: The primary objective of the project is to work out a comprehensive new interpretation of Kant’s metaphysics. Based on a careful study and analysis of the basic principles of Kant’s epistemology, a detailed reassessment of Kant’s major writings in theoretical philosophy will be conducted, distinguishing his later critical ideas from earlier pre-critical ideas in analyzing the development of his work. It aims at a coherent reconstruction of Kant’s metaphysics that has taken his epistemological turn into full account. The project will clarify Kant’s position as regards major metaphysical issues such as the nature of transcendental idealism, the ontological status of things in themselves as well as the transcendental subject and the problem of freedom in a deterministic world-view. The debate between the two-world and the two-aspect interpretations will be discussed and plausible solutions based on my epistemological reinterpretation of Kant’s metaphysics will be offered. The results of my preliminary research support an extreme version of the two-aspect interpretation. By critically reviewing Kant’s metaphysics, the project also addresses current issues in scholarly debate over metaphysics, showing Kant’s possible responses to contemporary understandings on the realism versus anti-realism question, the compatibility of freedom and determinism, as well as the nature of mind and cognition. It will explain Kant’s contributions to age-old metaphysical problems that are still puzzling mankind. The project will show how Kant helps us achieve a deeper understanding of reality by reconsidering metaphysical problems through his particular epistemological perspective.

446912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
446912.value: The project aims at a comprehensive new interpretation of Kant’s metaphysics. Kant is well-known for his critique of traditional metaphysics, but the metaphysical position in his philosophy is ambiguous. There have been heated debates about whether Kant’s distinction between appearances and things in themselves refers to two different realms of existence (the “two-world” interpretation), or is merely a methodological distinction between two different perspectives of one reality (the “two-aspect” interpretation). My past research outlined a new approach to assess Kant’s metaphysics, based on a more radical understanding of Kant’s epistemological turn. Kant was thought to have redefined the legitimate realm of human knowledge and restricted the possibility of metaphysical inquiry by a critical investigation into our faculty of cognition. However, Kant’s revolution is more fundamental: for Kant, metaphysical questions cannot even be asked in a way that was previously taken for granted, but must be thoroughly reformulated and assimilated into an epistemological framework. The one who has best understood this revolution was Hegel, who uncompromisingly identified logic with metaphysics. They differ, however, in the fact that while Hegel tended to subordinate logic and epistemology to metaphysical considerations, Kant is committed to the theoretical priority of epistemology. Taking a fresh look at Kant’s epistemological revolution will shed new light on many old problems. My preliminary work suggests that both the two-world and the ordinary two-aspect interpretations fail to fully appreciate the implications of Kant’s revolution. My approach can be classified under the two-aspect interpretation, but it is a radical form of it that interprets Kant’s position as ontological realism within the framework of epistemological idealism. The project will consist of the following four areas of study: 1. The Epistemology of Transcendental Philosophy 2. The Semantics of Transcendental Discourse 3. The Ontology of Transcendental Idealism 4. The Metaphysics of Transcendental Subject The research will begin with an analysis of Kant’s central epistemological principles and a detailed reassessment of Kant’s major writings in theoretical philosophy. It will then offer a new interpretation of Kant’s revolutionary metaphysics and explain his possible contributions to contemporary metaphysical issues, showing how Kant’s philosophy helps us achieve a deeper understanding of reality. I plan to present my results at international conferences and publish a number of academic papers in scholarly journals, which may be in English, German, or Chinese. The main target of the project is to publish a monograph on Kant’s metaphysics in English by an academic publisher in the US or Europe. 康德以批評傳統形上學聞名，但其本身的形上學立場一向不太清楚，學界對現象和物自身的理論地位有爭議，有人把它們視為兩個存在領域，亦有視之為兩種理解事物的角度。本計劃將從知識論角度重新詮釋康德形上學，康德嘗試為人類知識定下清楚界線，甚至以此為基礎，重新理解形上學問題的意義。黑格爾可謂最了解康德的哲學革命，因為他也把邏輯和形上學徹底地統一起來，只不過黑格爾是以形上學作為根據去理解邏輯和知識論，而康德則以知識論出發重新理解形上學。 本計劃將分為四個部份： 一、超驗哲學的知識論 二、超驗論述的語意學 三、超驗觀念論的存有論 四、超驗主體的形上學 本計劃期望在國際會議發表研究成果，在中、英或德語學術期刊發表論文，最終把結果整理成書，在歐美出版社出版。

446912.label: Realisation of objectives
446912.value: The project was launched on October 1, 2012, but it is based on research that I have been doing since more than a decade. It began with an analysis of the central principles of Kant's epistemology and a detailed reassessment of Kant's major writings in theoretical philosophy such as the Critique of Pure Reason and the Prolegomena to Any Future Metaphysics. Efforts were made to distinguish Kant's Critical ideas from his earlier pre-critical conceptions. In addition to Kant's own writings, a significant amount of secondary literature on Kant's theoretical philosophy have been reviewed. Based on a careful study, a new interpretation of Kant's metaphysics to which I refer as "transcendental functionalism" has been proposed and worked out. Transcendental functionalism is an extreme version of the two-aspect interpretation, as it is committed to the non-existence of noumena or things-in-themselves. The framework I proposed offers plausible solutions to hotly debated problems in Kant's philosophy such as the nature of transcendental idealism, the ontological status of things in themselves as well as the transcendental subject and the problem of freedom. My interpretation also has implications to a variety of problems that are discussed in contemporary philosophy. The results of the project were communicated through the standard academic vehicles, including academic papers and conference presentations. Five papers have been published or accepted for publication in peer-reviewed journals or books in three different languages (English, German and Chinese), the most representative ones being the two journal papers "Kant's Transcendental Functionalism" (in The Review of Metaphysics, 2014) and "Transcendental Concepts, Transcendental Truths and Objective Validity" (in The Kantian Review, 2015). I have also made a number of presentations to leading experts in the field at different conferences or lecture series in Germany, Beijing and Hong Kong. In addition to these publications and presentations arising directly from this project, a few other publications of mine, including a number of papers and a 280-page monograph on Hegel's philosophy (published by Taiwan University Press, 2014), have benefited significantly from the new interpretation of Kant's philosophy that was made possible by this project. All the major objectives, as stipulated in the project proposal, have been achieved. The project also serves as an important foundation for my future research on Kant's philosophy and its impacts on subsequent philosophers and German idealists in particular.

446912.label: Major findings and research outcome
446912.value: There are a dozen of peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations arising directly from the research project, among which the two journal papers "Kant's Transcendental Functionalism" (No. 1) and "Transcendental Concepts, Transcendental Truths and Objective Validity" (No. 3) stand out as the most important ones. The paper "Kant's Transcendental Functionalism", published in 2014 in The Review of Metaphysics (ERA Journal Ranking A; Acceptance Rate around 5%), developed a new functionalist interpretation of Kant that aims to unify his cognitive psychology with transcendental idealism. This interpretation can be called "transcendental functionalism," which determines what functions the mind has to realize if it is to be capable of objective cognition. Transcendental functionalism resolves problems associated with other functionalist interpretations of Kant by drawing a systematic distinction between transcendental cognitive functions and their empirical realizations. The paper "Transcendental Concepts, Transcendental Truths and Objective Validity", published in 2015 in The Kantian Review (ERA Journal Ranking A), analysed Kant's principle of objective validity, focusing particularly on its application to transcendental concepts such as those of sensibility, understanding and transcendental apperception. It distinguishes between two orders of objective validity, based on Kant's distinction between empirical and transcendental truths. The cognitive powers picked out by transcendental concepts are not particular psychological mechanisms, but rather abstract functional structures, and the objective validity of transcendental concepts depends on the realizability of the functional structures by empirical cognizers like humans. This relation in turn helps to explain the nature of transcendental truths. A forthcoming paper "Kant's Concept of Cognition and Its Ontological Implications" (No. 5) will be included in The Palgrave Kant Handbook (New York: Palgrave Macmillan), alongside with contributions from leading scholars in the field such as Paul Guyer and Béatrice Longuenesse. The project also resulted in publications in languages other than English: a paper in German titled "Die Ambition der Kantischen Metaphysik: Entwurf einer transzendental-funktionalistischen Interpretation" (No. 2) appeared in the The New Desire for Metaphysics (Berlin: de Gruyter, 2015), while a paper in Chinese on "Kant's Freedom and Spontaneity" is scheduled to appear in the March 2016 issue of the Journal of Social Sciences and Philosophy in Taiwan. All these papers deal with problems in Kant's metaphysics and epistemology based on the approach developed in the current project. In addition, I also published seven articles on Kant's philosophy in the 3-volume Kant-Lexikon (Berlin: de Gruyter, 2015) and made nine presentations at different conferences or lecture series in Germany, Beijing and Hong Kong.

446912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
446912.value: There are two major lines of further development of the completed project. As demonstrated in the research project, the crucial idea in Kant's revolution is to reformulate and assimilate metaphysical questions into an epistemological framework. The most direct potential for further development is to explore the implications of the epistemological reinterpretation of Kant's metaphysics to various parts of his philosophy, from his moral-political philosophy to his philosophy of art, education and history. This will include a detailed study of other major works of Kant such as the Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, the Critique of Practical Reason and the Critique of Judgment. Another line of potential further development is to examine the impact of Kant's philosophy on other philosophers and German idealists in particular. Interestingly, it turns out that the one who has best understood Kant's revolutionary idea was Hegel, who captured the spirit of Kant’s revolution by an uncompromising identification of logic with metaphysics. Both Kant and Hegel reformed traditional metaphysics by unifying it with logic and epistemology. The project lays a foundation for a new way of viewing the relation between these two great philosophers and possibly a better understanding of the whole tradition of German Idealism.

446912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
446912.value: Immanuel Kant is arguably the most important philosopher in the modern age. He attempted to answer those ultimate questions about reality that mankind has been seeking since the dawn of thought. Many philosophical debates today, not only across the analytic and continental divide but also in the contemporary development of Chinese philosophy, are profoundly influenced by his thought. Kant launched a Copernican revolution in philosophy, fundamentally rethinking the very possibility and limits of metaphysical inquiry. Kant is well-known for his critique of traditional metaphysics, but the metaphysical position in his philosophy is ambiguous. This is because, for Kant, metaphysical questions cannot even be asked in a way that was previously taken for granted, but must be thoroughly reformulated and assimilated into an epistemological framework. The project offered a new interpretation of Kant's metaphysics, based on a more radical understanding of Kant's epistemological turn. By critically reviewing Kant’s metaphysics, the project also addressed current issues in scholarly debate over metaphysics and epistemology, showing Kant's possible contributions to solving problems in contemporary philosophy.
