Compare policy choices and relevant laws in other jurisdictions;
Recommend amendments modernizing relevant laws to best enable the government to meet the needs of all stakeholders.

450012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
450012.value: This project aims to evaluate the regime regulating intellectual property as it relates to the pharmaceutical industry in Hong Kong (HK). While HK’s Patents Ordinance is consistent with the TRIPS Agreement it does not clearly delineate or define several important issues relevant to pharmaceuticals. The project, therefore, will evaluate whether the Patents Ordinance is capable of responding to the needs of the pharmaceutical industry (taking into account both the branded and generic manufacturers) as well as the interests of users and make recommendations to the government with a view to producing a modern and flexible agreement which balances the interests of all stakeholders. While interested parties have at times engaged in dialogue with the government on this issue, there is no sustained, holistic research balancing the often competing interests of stakeholders. This is surprising given the importance of access to medicines and health to a relatively wealthy and aging population and HK’s position as a technology hub attractive to foreign direct investment (FDI). As a result, inconsistencies have emerged between legislators, laws and the courts. For instance, the government, the Secretary for Food and Health and individual legislators has all maintained that HK does not link the registration of a medicine to patent status but the recent decision in Abbott v. Pharmareg (2009/10) indicates otherwise. Other issues, such as the possibility of patent term extensions, evergreening, protection of test data and even limits on compulsory licensing are also unclear and/or unpredictable in certain circumstances. The lack of predictability in the current law has lead to intense industry lobbying and even resulted in HK’s regime repeatedly being deemed to lack predictability and transparency by the US Trade Representative in its annual report on Foreign Trade Barriers (HKAPI, 2007; USTR, 2011). Clarification of the patent regime as it relates to the pharmaceutical industry is therefore necessary in order to maintain HK’s attractiveness to FDI as well as to maintain its health-related commitment to its residents. At present the patent regime does not deal with numerous important issues relating to pharmaceuticals, thus providing little predictability to the industry and potentially failing to meet the health-related needs of residents. This project will evaluate the Patents Ordinance it relates to pharmaceuticals in an attempt to understand fully the interests of all relevant stakeholders and to assess how best to balance these interests with a view to producing recommendations to the government for reform. 本研究項目旨在評估有關香港製藥業知識產權的監管制度。香港的《專利條例》雖然符合《與貿易有關的知識產權協定》，但未明確解釋或規定有關製藥業的幾個重要問題。所以，本研究項目將評估《專利條例》能否夠應對製藥業（包括品牌製造商和普通製造商）的需求並滿足使用者的利益。同時，本研究項目將向政府提供建議以制定與時俱進、機動靈活且能平衡各方利益訴求的條例。 儘管利益團體在該問題上與政府偶有對話，但在如何平衡他們的利益衝突方面鮮有持續性、系統性的研究。醫藥衛生對與相對一個富裕並老齡化的社會的重要性不言而喻，研究領域在此方面的空白不僅令人詫異而且不符合香港吸引外商直接投資的技術中心地位。 立法者、法律和法院之間的矛盾日益明顯。例如，政府、食物及衛生局局長和一些立法者均認為香港的醫藥註冊與醫藥的專利情況無關，但最近法院在Abbott v. Pharmareg （2009/10）上的裁判並非如此。其他的問題，諸如專利條款的續展、“常青”、測試數據的保護以及強制許可的限制等，也是不清楚且難以預測的。 目前的法律在可預測性方面的缺失已經導致了激烈的行業遊說，美國貿易代表在《對外貿易壁壘》的年度報告中甚至屢次認為香港缺乏可預測性和透明度（HKAPI, 2007; USTR, 2011）。所以，無論對保持香港的外商直接投資的吸引力還是遵守香港在衛生方面對居民的承諾，厘清製藥業方面的專利制度是不可或缺的。 因為目前的專利制度尚未處理有關製藥的許多重要問題，所以行業缺乏可預測性，居民的健康需求可能也無法得到滿足。本研究項目將評估涉及醫藥方面的專利條例、了解所有利益相關者的訴求、並就平衡這些利益向政府提供改革建議。

450212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
450212.value: 城市与国家：美国帝国主义、城市规划与菲律宾，1898-1916

450212.label: Project Objectives
450212.value: To identify the built features evident in Philippine urban environments, and their origins; To assess the association between politics, culture, and urban designing, and in so doing to grasp what forms this alliance took, how it evolved, and why civic design was utilised by colonial administrators to bestow ‘civilisation’ upon the Philippines To analyse the cultural character of ‘modern Philippine cities’, thereby clarifying their role as functional centres of national development, the way of life within them, and what kind of national subject was construed through their urban forms To evaluate America’s self-perception, explicating how its individuality, perceived cultural importance, and role as ‘civiliser of the world’ affected the development of urban places in the Philippines and elsewhere.
rows: To identify the built features evident in Philippine urban environments, and their origins;

To assess the association between politics, culture, and urban designing, and in so doing to grasp what forms this alliance took, how it evolved, and why civic design was utilised by colonial administrators to bestow ‘civilisation’ upon the Philippines

To analyse the cultural character of ‘modern Philippine cities’, thereby clarifying their role as functional centres of national development, the way of life within them, and what kind of national subject was construed through their urban forms

To evaluate America’s self-perception, explicating how its individuality, perceived cultural importance, and role as ‘civiliser of the world’ affected the development of urban places in the Philippines and elsewhere.

450212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
450212.value: The aim of this study is to investigate the design of Philippine cities between 1898 and 1916, a period when significant exercises in urban planning took place. The Treaty of Paris (1898) initiated America’s administration of the Philippines. By 1905 Manila was replanned and Baguio built as expressions of colonial sovereignty, and as symbols of a society disassociating itself from its hitherto ‘uncivilised’ state of existence. While scholars have suggested that the importation of urban design practices into the Philippines was exclusively tied to the propagation of the City Beautiful Movement, initial research by this author has explicitly linked Philippine urban design to matters of ‘modern civilisation’, ‘cultural progress’, and the promotion of nationhood. Therefore a thorough investigation is now proposed to further elucidate the meaning of urban designing in the Philippines, and to examine its dissemination with respect to colonial ideals, social advancement, and the shaping of national identity. The inquiry considers how the redevelopment of large-sized settlements alongside the creation of a new city, Baguio, strengthened a centralised sense of nationhood, and how recourse to civic design helped to express this. It thus systematically explores how the conceptualisation and construction of ‘modern cities’ articulated America’s yearning to establish a new culture and disassociate the Philippines from its Spanish colonial past, and its image as a place inhabited by ‘savages’. Using well-established research methods to align American urban design with the evolution of Philippine society, the project shall reinterpret Philippine city development by deviating from the traditional focus on the architect and planner Daniel Burnham. Accordingly, it positions urban design alongside education, politics, and economics as social institutions that have profoundly affected the development of the Philippines as a nation. The study’s findings will deliver significant insights into the forces that existed during the early years of American rule in the Philippines. The study’s methodology is also of importance. It will offer a historical paradigm that investigates the relationship between environmental design, nationhood, and broad cultural transition. This paradigm will not only improve our understanding of Philippine cities before the passing of the Autonomy Act (1916), but it will also be utilised to illuminate complex national identity movements and city design practices which were evident elsewhere at that time. Topics such as the borrowing, imposition, and assimilation of American urban design in Australia and China could, for instance, be profitably reappraised by the methods validated in this study. 此项研究的目的是探讨1898至1916年的菲律宾城市规划，重要的城市建设都在这一时期实施。 巴黎和约（1898）标志着美国在菲律宾统治的开始。到了1905年，马尼拉被重新规划以及碧瑶的建设，不仅传达了殖民统治的信息，也成为社会脱离曾经“野蛮”状态的象征。虽然学者认为菲律宾对城市规划的引进只与城市美化运动的扩展传播密切相关，但本人的最初研究明确地将菲律宾的城市计划和“现代文明”，“文化进步”以及国家建构联系起来。因此，我提出了一个详尽的研究方案，进一步阐明菲律宾城市规划的意义，并审视这一模式在殖民观念，社会发展和国家意识塑形等方面的传播。 这项调查将思考在新建城市碧瑶周边的大型居民区的重建如何加强了国家观念的中心意识，以及城市规划如何辅助地传达这一观念。这一研究将系统地探寻“现代城市”理念的观念化与构筑如何表达美国对建立新文化，切断菲律宾与过去西班牙殖民者的联系和使它脱离“野蛮”之地的形象的渴望。通过使用成熟的研究方法把美国城市规划与菲律宾的社会进程相结合，这项研究将从聚焦于建筑师和设计师丹尼尔. 布尔南的传统做法中转移出来，重新诠释菲律宾的城市发展。因此，我将城市规划与教育、政治和经济并列为深刻影响菲律宾国家发展的社会因素。 此项研究成果将极大地帮助人们深入理解美国在菲律宾早期统治中的力量因素。研究的方法也同样至关重要。它将提供一个探索环境规划、国家建构和泛文化转变的历史范式。这一范式不仅能够提高我们对自治条例（1916）通过之前的菲律宾城市的理解，也可用以阐明当时出现在其他地方的复杂的国家身份认同过程和城市规划活动。由这项研究所确立的方法将有助于重新理解澳大利亚和中国等国家对美国城市规划的借鉴、推行和吸收等课题。

450212.label: Realisation of objectives
450212.value: The PI is very grateful to the RGC’s GRF for the opportunity to undertake, and in due course successfully complete, an original piece of detailed investigation into the formation of the modern Philippine built environment. Thanks to GRF funding a full-time RA was employed for part of the project’s duration. This helped to ensure a vast amount of data could be collected so that the project objectives could in turn be met. What is more, at least in relation to the publication of research findings, owing to the fact that two persons worked on the project both a depth and breadth of source materials were utilized and according original papers with new, significant conclusions could be composed. These works, as touched upon later in this report, are now entering the public domain in the form of journal papers, books chapters, and a monograph. At the commencement of the project four research objectives were formed. These sought to identify the built features evident in Philippine urban environments, assess the association between politics, culture, and urban designing, and in so doing to grasp what forms this alliance took, analyse the cultural character of ‘modern Philippine cities’, and evaluate America’s role ‘civiliser of the world’ and how it affected the development of urban places in the Philippines. The project in this setting explored how urban design was employed by the Americans in the Philippines to express ‘modern civilisation’, and affect a nation’s identity, thereby complementing existing intellectual thought on cities, their designs, and nationhood. Accordingly the work recontextualised the planning history of Philippine cities. The decision to analyse cities during what was an important era in the nation’s history was an original research act to understanding a topic that to date has been dominated by Daniel Burnham. The decision to analyse ideals of nationalism and civility at a key period in Philippine history was purposeful in order to shift scholarship on the plans of Philippine cities towards some of the fundamental ideals of urban planning. As a consequence, to highlight one point, the work described and explained the role of William E. Parsons in implementing Burnham’s plans for Manila and Baguio, and creating new city plans for Cebu and Zamboanga. To date, little thought has been given to the role of Parsons in implementing the ideas offered by Burnham in his city plans of 1905. At the end of 2015, with the project coming to an end, the aims of the work had been fulfilled. On the matter of identifying the built features of Philippine urban environments post 1898 the paper published in 2016 in Philippine Studies offered detailed data on two important matters associated with the evolution of the Philippine built fabric during the American colonial era: the endorsement of spatial forms dissimilar to what had hitherto existed led to the physical and cultural shift of settlements away from plaza majors to new civic centres of symmetrical layout in which buildings, statuary, and green areas were designed in harmony with each other, i.e. as pieces of civic design; urban designing played a critical role in the expansion of local civilization and the construction of nationhood by establishing new sites for public rituals (modelled on American practices and traditions). As the project revealed by the early 1900s the importation of the City Beautiful model from North America to Asia had yielded a revolution in the design and planning of Philippine cities. Thanks to the rise of City Beautiful urbanism in North America in the 1890s, the Philippine Commission thus was able to espouse a design archetype that it believed could enhance the physical and social condition of society. To paraphrase the author Thomas Hines (who wrote in the 1970s about the Philippines), consequently the City Beautiful attained its greatest success in the Philippines and not in the US itself. Although the project was able to accomplish its objectives in doing so it highlighted a number of historical problems/fields for future research. Despite presenting the contribution of urban design upon the invention and assembly of “Filipino national culture” during the early period of American colonial rule in the Philippines more research is required to comprehensively explicate American urban forms in the country and, in particular, the nation-making process. The role of Philippine architects within colonial bureaucracy, to offer one possible field of study, needs to be more fully explored. Presently research on both topics is somewhat lacking. In the case of Filipino designers their activities within the institutional framework of the Bureau of Public Works, a facet of the Philippine Commission, enabled them to receive City Beautiful urban design experience directly yet little is known about their technical and social acceptance (within American dominated society in the Philippines between 1898 and 1941). This, as noted subsequently, will comprise a new GRF application by the PI in the future. Ultimately the GRF-funded project has shown that the image of the modern Philippine city was defined by spatial regulation and grand vistas (established by the American urban planner, and in later decades replicated by Filipino urban planners educated in the US). Given the desire of the Americans to ‘uplift’ and ‘civilise’ Philippine society the work explicitly showed that the urban plan, really, was a means to getting there. As such, given attention to cultural and political evolution in the Philippines between 1898 and 1916, the study recontextualised the planning history of Philippine cities. The decision to base the project’s objectives on issues other than the physical structure of urban environments, e.g. civility, nationalism, etc., meant a historiographical shift on the plans of Philippine cities. Whereas previously authors, particularly those within the fields of Geography, Architecture and Urban Planning have adopted a structuralist perspective, the attention within the milieu of the project to examine the influence of culture and politics upon the fundamental ideals of urban planning meant the narrative of urban design was put into a new intellectual context for the first time. Therefore the work did much more than merely describe the new structure of the built form after 1898. Rather, to reiterate prior comments, it explained why particular urban features became more visible, and indeed in some instances less visible, given the American comprehension of what ‘Philippine national development’ was. So, to sum up, the success completion of the project, and so the accomplishment of goals established at the initiation of the project, has led to a new insights being offered as to the American reconfiguration of Philippine cities in its own image.

450212.label: Summary of objectives addressed

450212.label: Major findings and research outcome
450212.value: The project has led to a number of original research findings, and these have been put into the public domain in the form of published works. In 2016, to give an example, a paper was published in Philippine Studies and a book chapter is due to be published within a series of volumes on cities and urbanism (by the University of Amsterdam Press in 2017). However, notably, the major outcome of the project is a monograph. Some words on this matter are now to be given. In mid-2015 the PI contacted a number of prominent publishing houses/university presses with respect to the publication of the project. As an outcome of this process in late-summer 2015 a MOA was signed by the PI with the University of Hawaii Press. As part of this agreement between the Press and the PI a completed draft book was submitted in December 2015, and in the months following the work has been under external review. As of July 2016, when one full review has been sent to the PI, the work has received very positive appraisal and a recommendation has been made (by the reviewer to the Press) for the work to be published. Comments on the work delivered by the PI include its originality, its thorough use of primary sources, and the capacity to link historical developments in Asia with urban trends in the US (with respect to the development and design of cities). The work too was said by the reviewer to be “an important scholarly work”. In terms of its importance, as originally set out in the GRF application many years ago, the research findings once in published form are intended to sit alongside existing Philippine Studies literature so as to complement them yet, in doing so, add new original knowledge. By way of illustration, notwithstanding the work’s attention to the evolution of the Philippine built form the findings act as a foil to work by authors such as Lico, Reed, and Doeppers. The work put together by the PI in one manuscript separates literature that tangentially discusses American influence on Philippine urban settings. Consequently, as originally envisaged, the outcome of the project – a book – will be of interest to both Americans and Filipinos, and to other individuals interested in the origins, history, and evolution of urban design in contemporary Asian cities.

450212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
450212.value: The project has already been expanded as a consequence of a successful follow-up application to the RGC’s GRF in 2014-15. This second project, focusing on the rise of Filipino architects and their role in shaping Philippine urban environments during the American colonial period, began in early 2015 and is due to end in late 2017. Furthermore another GRF proposal based on the Pensionados Program, i.e. the scholarship scheme set up by the Americans to educate Filipinos in universities in the US, has been forged, and it is envisaged that it shall act as a conduit to further explore in great detail some of the contextual matters touched upon within this now completed GRF project on the Philippines from 1898 to 1916. Moreover, in the light of the project dealing with elements of American cultural importation into Asia a conference has been organized (to be held at CUHK in mid-2017). This event will draw together scholars from Hong Kong, the Philippines, and other SE Asian nations to discuss, analyse, and explain the growing impact of American urban culture in Asia from the mid-late 1800s until the onset of World War Two in 1941. It is hoped the event will aid the PI to place his research findings into a more transnational framework, and by doing so provoke new ideas for research in the near future.

450212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
450212.value: The project has explained the role of urban development and urban design within the framework of early US colonial policy in the Philippines. As discussed within the context of the project US plans consciously propagated civic secularism and Philippine nationhood so as to replace Spanish religiousity. Significantly, the work revealed that by 1916 the American imprint in major Philippine cities had become so visible with the creation of new civic centres that public edifices and statuary to Philippine heroes such as Jose Rizal, linked together by new green spaces and new roadway systems, had replaced the Spanish colonial era plaza majors as the major urban feature in the country. As thus shown in the work, these new civic centres and statues made possible (for the first time) the celebration of national events characterised by public rituals patterned by American traditions and culture. Notably many of these rituals, plus statues, spaces, buildings, and roadways, still exist in the Philippines today.

451312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
451312.value: Beginning ten years ago, Hong Kong’s tertiary educational offerings were diversified, allowing growing percentages of secondary school students to continue to the postsecondary level. Nearly all of the growth, however, has occurred in self-financed community colleges, where students do not obtain the same level of public support as that received by students who study in the UGC-financed universities to Bachelors level. This proposal would allow the investigators to assess the impact this historical change has had on young adults of both gender and those with an immigrant background. The research will also focus on the social contexts of the family and neighborhood. Using aggregate information about different districts of Hong Kong, this research will provide a link between district conditions and children’s postsecondary education outcomes. Census data from 2006 and 2011 will allow us to estimate the likelihood of educational attainment for children since 1996. The results will be used to compare with those from earlier years. 從十年前開始，香港的專上教育課程變得多元化，讓愈來愈多中學畢業生的教育水平得以不斷增長。然而，幾乎所有的增長發生在自負盈虧的社區學院，與大學教育資助委員會(UGC)所資助的本科課程比較之下，社區學院學生得不到同等的政府支持。本份報告會探討這個歷史性的變化對這一群年輕人的影響，特別針對那些有移民背景的青少年男女。研究也將重點放在家庭和鄰里的社會背景。這項研究亦會分析香港不同地區的區域條件，指出居住地區和青少年中學後教育路程之間的聯繫。我們綜合由2006年和2011年的人口普查中，兒童及青少年的教育程度統計，將結果用作與早年的分析對比。

451312.value: Besides the original proposed research objectives, we further extended our study by investigating consequences of higher education expansion in Hong Kong that go beyond employment and earnings as well as comparing the impact of higher education expansion in China.

451312.label: Major findings and research outcome
451312.value: This project investigated the interactions between human capital and immigrants’ integration. In particular, exploiting the setting of “one country, two systems” in Hong Kong, we have examined and published papers on potential factors that affect schooling, work and marriage decisions of Mainlander immigrants in Hong Kong in comparison to the natives. For example, our paper published in Asian Population Studies (Post, Pong and Ou, 2015) finds increasing social distance in terms of greater wage inequality and limited access to postsecondary education for immigrants despite some evidence of assimilation in terms of residential location and home language. Our paper in the Population and Development Review (Pong, Post, Ou and Fok, 2014) examines Mainlander’s integration in Hong Kong via the tendency toward co-ethnic inter-marriage between Mainlanders and natives in Hong Kong. We find an increasing likelihood of exogamous marriage, which was associated with a lower degree of educational homogamy. We suggested that exogamy as a result of cross-border marriage in Hong Kong may have strengthened stereotypes of Mainland women as low status. Further, higher education expansion has consequences that go beyond employment and earnings. A less common area of inquiry is whether higher education expansion affects individuals’ decisions to marry. Another publication (Ou & Pong, 2016) attempts to provide a causal estimate of the relationship between education and educational homogamy (i.e. marrying someone of a similar educational level) using an exogenous policy shock to correct the endogeneity of schooling decisions. Our analysis reveals that women who are most affected by the expansion policy are able women who face high searching costs (or constrained opportunities) in the mating market. Our paper highlights the importance of understanding spillover effects on family formation when evaluating educational policies. We further extended our study by comparing the impact of higher education expansion in China. we find that the expansion of higher education in China decreases unemployment rates, especially among males and high school graduates. However, the policy also decreases women’s labor force participation and individual earnings in highly-skilled white-collar jobs. We further discuss potential channels affecting the observed outcomes. Our results illustrate the strong demand for a skilled labor force in China and the broad economic benefits of higher education. In short, all these studies have targeted the social distance between natives and immigrants, contributing to our knowledge body by addressing this important topic in an interesting setting where Mainlander immigrants and natives share similar ethnicity, languages and cultural values.

451312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
451312.value: Study and compare the heterogeneous effects of the long term consequences of higher education expansion in China and Hong Kong.

451312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
451312.value: This project assessed the overall changes in postsecondary educational access for Hong Kong’s youth, from 2006 to 2011. We further investigated the interactions between human capital and immigrants’ integration. In particular, exploiting the setting of “one country, two systems” in Hong Kong, we have examined and published papers on potential factors that affect schooling, work and marriage decisions of Mainlander immigrants in Hong Kong in comparison to the natives. We found increasing social distance in terms of greater wage inequality and limited access to postsecondary education for immigrants despite some evidence of assimilation in terms of residential location and home language. We also found gender differences in the impact of education expansion on their wages and returns to schooling as well as their marriage decisions. These are compared with the impact of higher education expansion in China. In short, our studies have targeted the social distance between natives and immigrants, contributing to our knowledge body by addressing this important topic in an interesting setting where Mainlander immigrants and natives share similar ethnicity, languages and cultural values. Our research also advanced knowledge of the consequences of educational reforms and the mechanisms behind these policies’ distributional effects across demographic and socioeconomic categories.

451512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
451512.value: 王法與神力：明清時期徽州社會的形成

451512.label: Project Objectives
451512.value: This project unveils the complicated details of the three-century-long lawsuit over the Wangdi Temple. This project identifies the local lineages involved in the worship of Wangdi and the lawsuit over the Wangdi Temple. It also studies the social dynamics created by these lineages. This project offers new insights for the study of Chinese legal history and regional history.
rows: This project unveils the complicated details of the three-century-long lawsuit over the Wangdi Temple.
This project identifies the local lineages involved in the worship of Wangdi and the lawsuit over the Wangdi Temple. It also studies the social dynamics created by these lineages.
This project offers new insights for the study of Chinese legal history and regional history.

451512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
451512.value: If Huizhou徽州was a theatre of state-society interaction in late imperial China, then the main stage in this theatre must be the Wangdi汪帝Temple in Shexian歙縣. Known officially as the Yueguogong越國公, Wangdi was the most respected and worshipped deity in Huizhou. By exploring the worship of Wangdi and the legal dispute over the Wangdi Temple in Shexian in Ming-Qing era, this project unveils the processes and mechanisms of the formation of local society and the transformation of state power in Huizhou. Huizhou lineages are famous for the ferocious lawsuit among themselves and their feverish worship of local deities. It comes to no surprise that they were behind the three-century-old dispute over the control of the Wangdi Temple in Shexian. With the help of the Yueguogong ci mu zhi越國公祠墓志, a crucial temple gazetteer compiled in mid-nineteenth century, in addition to numerous Huizhou archives, this project not only studies the lawsuit, but places the lawsuit within the unique historical and social context of late imperial Huizhou. It shows that all social actors in Huizhou, be they "superior" or "inferior" lineages, have been skillfully invoking the law of the state and the divine power of the Wangdi in their favour. They were equally aware of and skillful in the compilation of written documents as the most important means of self-legitimization and cultural construction. In short, if Huizhou was blessed by the emperor's law and the local deity's power, it remained to be seen which local social actors succeeded in winning the blessing. The contest was fierce, victory short-lived, and fortune constantly changing. Combining the insights of Chinese legal history and regional history studies, this project will therefore (1) excavate the complicated details of the protracted legal dispute over the Wangdi Temple, this being in itself a valuable contribution to the study of Chinese legal history. (2) identify the major lineages involved in the legal dispute, study their origins and development, this being an important attempt to understand the local history of Huizhou. (3) compare the patterns of state-society interaction in various regions of late imperial China, in a bid to answering a bigger question: what are the social and legal foundation on which late imperial China started its modern transformation. 王法與神力：明清時期徽州社會的形成 如果徽州是明清時期國家與社會互動的劇場，則這個劇場的舞臺就是歙縣的越國公祠---祭祀汪帝的廟宇。汪帝（汪華）是徽州地區最推崇的神明。本研究計劃探討明清時期歙縣的汪帝崇拜亦即有關越國公祠的訴訟，以求掌握徽州地域社會形成的過程與機制、以及王朝權力的演變。 明清時期，徽州宗族以健訟著稱，徽州人以熱衷崇拜本地神明著稱。圍繞歙縣越國公祠的訴訟長達三百年，也就不令人驚訝。本研究計劃利用十九世紀編纂的《越國公祠志》這本重要史料，再結合眾多相關的徽州地方文獻，不僅研究這場訴訟的細節本身，而更把這場訴訟放置於明清時期徽州獨特的歷史及社會脈絡內。本研究計劃指出，徽州的各種社會集團，無論「大姓」「小姓」，都極善於利用王朝的法律和神明崇拜的力量來維護自己。這些社會集團都意識到，編纂文字材料，是自我合理化和文化建構的最重要手段，並且因此都擅長於編纂文字材料。簡單而言，徽州是被王法和神力所庇佑的，但究竟哪些社會集團贏得王法和神力的庇佑，則有待爭奪。爭奪是兇猛的，勝利是短暫的，運氣也是變幻莫測的。 本研究計劃結合中國法制史和區域史研究的洞見，將可達到以下目標： （1）理解和重構越國公祠訴訟的漫長複雜過程，這本身就是對中國法制史研究的一項貢獻。 （2）查出徽州哪些宗族參與這場訴訟，研究這些宗族的起源與發展，這本身就是研究徽州地方歷史的重要工作之一。 （3）比較明清時期不同地區的國家與社會互動的模式，試圖回答一個宏觀問題：明清中國是在怎樣的社會和法律基礎上開始現代化的？

451512.label: Realisation of objectives
451512.value: This research project uses the Yueguogong cimuzhi to study the history of the Wangdi Temple in Shexian of Huizhou during the Qing dynasty. My seminar presentation in March 2015 in Jiaotong University has reviewed the content of the book and unveiled an interesting campaign of supplicating for government recognition in the name of Wangdi the deity. I point out the cultural rationality behind the seemingly irrational pursuit of 1.6 taels of silver by concerted campaign of supplication not only to local government but all the way to Beijing, the imperial capital. I reveal the complex dynamics of eighteenth-century Huizhou society in which different social groups appealed to deities or imperial authority to strengthen themselves. My book, to be published in 2015, The Rise and Fall of a Public Debt Market in 16th-Century China: the Story of the Ming Salt Certificate (Leiden: Brill, in print, 184 pp., ISBN 978-90-04-30573-1 [hardback], 978-90-30640-0 [e-book]) also devotes a chapter studying the growth of Huizhou merchants engaging in salt trade in Yangzhou during late Ming and early Qing period. I show how the Huizhou migrants settled in Yangzhou by contributing to defense of the city against the Japanese pirates and established themselves socially and culturally via the worship of deities. I also document the lawsuit over examination quota between Huizhou and Shanxi migrant merchants in Yangzhou. This project therefore sheds new insights on the study of Chinese legal history and regional history.

451512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
451512.value: It is certainly possible to deepen the study of Huizhou during Ming-Qing period. Given the vast archives of Huizhou, the following three research issues could be further pursued. (1) The interaction between the Wang lineage that claimed ownership over the Wangdi temple and other Wang lineages. (2) The interaction between the Wang lineage that claimed ownership over the Wangdi temple and other non-Wang lineages. (3) The management of temple property. The P.I. continues to collect and study Huizhou historical archives in order to identify new sources for the research.

451512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
451512.value: The research project studies an interesting record of the Wangdi Temple in Shexian of Huizhou during the Qing dynasty. Among details of routine management of the temple and its property, the P.I. demonstrates the seemingly bizarre case in which the Wang lineage, claiming ownership over the temple, launched a concerted campaign of supplication for 1.6 taels of silver for the worship of Wangdi. The campaign included letters of supplication submitted to Beijing, the imperial capital. Obviously, the cost of the campaign far exceeded the goal to be achieved: annual appropriation of 1.6 taels of silver from the government. The objective of the Wang lineage certainly should not be interpreted by narrow economic rationality. Rather, the success of the campaign would have greatly enhanced the cultural and political legitimacy of the Wang lineage in the local society. This project therefore reveals the complex dynamics of eighteenth-century Huizhou in which different social groups appealed to deities or imperial authority to strengthen themselves. Hence the title of the project “Emperor's law and deity's power: the making of late-imperial Huizhou (1300-1800)”.

451812.label: Project Title(Chinese)
451812.value: 感官限制对消费者行为的影响

451812.label: Project Objectives
451812.value: To determine if inhibiting the transmission of sensory input relevant to social communication affects consumers’ perceptions of themselves as independent and their likelihood of accepting others’ recommendation for a product. To examine whether the inhibition of visual stimulation (e.g., by closing one’s eyes) while considering product preference will lead individuals to defer a decision to purchase products, and to determine whether this effect is mediated by feelings of uncertainty about product preference. To examine whether the inhibition of smiling facial expression (e.g. by making people stay in a negative mood) will influence people's intention to seek enjoyable experience. To examine whether the inhibition or facilitation of attention in one modality (e.g. auditory) will affect attention in the other modality (e.g. visual) and also the choice of objects that are processed in the second modality.

To examine whether the inhibition of visual stimulation (e.g., by closing one’s eyes) while considering product preference will lead individuals to defer a decision to purchase products, and to determine whether this effect is mediated by feelings of uncertainty about product preference.
To examine whether the inhibition of smiling facial expression (e.g. by making people stay in a negative mood) will influence people's intention to seek enjoyable experience.

451812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
451812.value: Consumers interact with their environment in multiple sense modalities (e.g. smell, touch, sight, sound, and taste). The effects of transmitting information in these modalities have often been investigated (Krishna 2009). However, little has been done to investigate the consequences of having these communication channels blocked. For example, suppose a customer is wearing a mouth mask during flu season. Will this affect her reaction to a salesperson’s recommendation? Or, suppose someone is thinking about which product to purchase with her eyes closed. Will doing so influence her purchase decision? The research to be proposed will attempt to answer these questions. The first project will investigate the effect of inhibiting oral communication. We suggest that wearing a mouth mask leads individuals to feel inhibited when communicating orally to others. If this is so, it may decrease their feelings of social connectedness to a salesperson who recommends a product to them. Consequently, they will be less likely to accept the recommendation from the salesperson. The second project will examine the effect of restrictions on visual communication. We posit that a lack of visual stimulation as a result of closing the eyes could make consumers feel uncertain about where to go and this uncertainty may generalize to psychological movement that is metaphorically related to it (e.g., which product to approach). As a result, these consumers will feel more uncertain about product preference and may be more likely to defer their purchase decision. The research to be proposed will examine these possibilities and the conditions in which they occur. 消費者經常使用不同感官和周圍環境交流（比如，視覺，聽覺，觸覺，味覺等）。之前已有人已經對感官對消費者信息處理的影響進行了研究（Krishna 2009)。但是，對於感官限制對消費者行為的影響還沒有研究過。比如，如果消費者剛好戴著口套，這會影響他對銷售人員推薦的反應麼？還有，如果一個人正好閉著眼睛思考是否要買一個產品，這會影響他的決定麼？我們試圖對這些問題進行解答。 在第一個項目中，我們認為當人們戴口罩時，會覺得與他人交流變的困難。這將降低他們與別人的聯系程度。如果這樣，他們會更加不會接受銷售人員對其的推薦。 在第二個項目中，我們將研究人們的視覺限制。我們認為如果人們閉上眼睛，他們會沒有方向感。從而這個不確定性會傳染到他們對產品的決定（不知道該選哪個）。從而這些消費者會更加不確定他們的產品選擇，因而會推遲其決定。 我們的研究將對這些假設進行探討，以及找出其成立的條件。

451812.label: Realisation of objectives
451812.value: Objective 1 was obtained by a series of studies. We showed that inhibiting sensory communication will influence consumers’ feelings of connectedness to other people. Objective 2 was also obtained in a series of studies in which we found that people reported feeling less certain about their choice if they considered their choice they had made while keeping their eyes closed than open. This is because they may feel more difficult to imagine moving their body to a particular direction when they close eyes. Objective 3 was achieved by several studies in which we found that when people in a negative mood anticipate enjoyable experiences, their preference for them reduces. We posit that anticipation involves smile-like facial-muscular simulations that can conflict with their frown-like expressions. This physiological conflict evokes subjective experiences of difficulty that are attributed to reduced pleasantness of the enjoyable experience. Objective 4 was obtained by several studies which examined when and why an irrelevant auditory signal will facilitate or impair preferences for visually processed target products located in the direction of the signal. With regard to the first three objectives, we need to collect more data and write/revise the papers. Therefore, we still need to continue working on these projects. That's the reason for the under-achievements of each objective.

451812.label: Major findings and research outcome
451812.value: In the first project, we found that inhibiting sensory communication can influence consumers’ feelings of connectedness to other people. In one study, we found that participants who wear mouth mask reported feeling less connected to the spokesperson in the advertisement than those who wear a hat. In another study, we asked participants to watch a video in which a person asks some questions to them. They either answered the questions by talking to a microphone or by typing answers on the screen. We found that people feel more connected to the person if they talked about the answers than if they typed the answers. In the second project, we found that consumer preference is grounded on a sense of bodily movement toward the preferred option and the certainty of preference will decrease if people are uncertain about the direction of their bodily movement. For example, we found that people reported feeling less uncertain about the choice of two products when they consider their choice while moving their body from left to right than without any movement. They also feel less certain about their choice of products if they consider their choice while keeping eyes closed than open. In Shen and Labroo (2015), we found that when people in a negative mood anticipate enjoyable experiences, their preference for them reduces. We posit that anticipation involves smile-like facial-muscular simulations that can conflict with their frown-like expressions. This physiological conflict evokes subjective experiences of difficulty that are attributed to reduced pleasantness of the enjoyable experience. People in a negative (vs. neutral) mood therefore avoid anticipated enjoyable experiences and seek easier-to-simulate unenjoyable ones (studies 1-2). Not engaging facial-muscular simulation or attributing simulation difficulty externally can increase preference for enjoyable experiences among negative-mood people, because these experiences then serve mood-repair goals (study 3). In Shen and Sengupta (2014), we found that listening to an auditory signal from the left will shift people’s visual attention toward the left side and lead them to be more likely to choose a product that is presented on the left side of a display. This effect, however, was reversed when the auditory signal is aversive (e.g. annoying noise). Five studies examined these possibilities.

451812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
451812.value: Future research can be done to examine the following issues: (1) the effect of the feelings of connectedness on product choice; (2) provide more evidence for the underlying process of the effect of movement on choice uncertainty. That is, whether consumer preference is grounded on a sense of bodily movement toward the preferred option; (3) provide evidence for underlying process for why negative mood decreases the choice of enjoyable experiences. That is, whether this is due to the difficulty of simulating smile-like facial expressions when one feels bad; (4) do more field studies for the effect of listening to sounds on the choice of visually-processed products.

451812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
451812.value: People feel less connected to others if their sensory modalities are blocked (e.g. wearing mouth mask), but they feel more connected to others if they imagined themselves talking to others. People feel less certain about their choice of products if they move body in different directions (e.g. move from left to right) than if they do not move, or if they close eyes than keep eyes open. Consumers who are in a negative mood may feel difficult to imagine an enjoyable experience and, therefore, decrease their choice of enjoyable experiences. This happen because simulating enjoyable experiences in mind is associated with making smile-like facial expressions, which becomes difficult when one feels bad. Consumers who listen to a voice from one direction will pay more visual attention to that direction. Consequently, they will be more likely to choose a product that is presented in the same direction of voice. This effect is reversed when the voice is aversive.

451912.label: Project Title(Chinese)
451912.value: 中國2000-2005區間遷移模擬: 區域特徵與空間交互作用模擬誤差的分析

451912.label: Project Objectives

The real and expected migration matrices for the period 2000-2005 will be decomposed into the overall effect, the relative emissiveness, the relative attractiveness and the effect of spatial interaction respectively. rows: To identify the effect of spatial interaction. The real and expected migration matrices for the period 2000-2005 will be decomposed into the overall effect, the relative emissiveness, the relative attractiveness and the effect of spatial interaction respectively.
To assess the extent that the modeling error is due to the explanatory power of origin and destination attributes or the explanatory power of the spatial interaction effect.

451912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
451912.value: Migration modeling is a common approach to describe the migration process and identify significant determinants of migration. This project will model interregional migration in China for the period 2000-2005 using data from 2005 population sampling survey. Much methodological advancement has been made in the modeling and analysis of interregional migration. However, previous migration modeling has been done in a black-box. The overall performance of a migration model is evaluated with the contribution of all explanatory variables including regional attributes and spatial interaction effect. In most cases, distance is considered as just one of the many explanatory variables. No detailed research has been made to examine the following. What are the contributions of spatial interaction and regional attributes to migration? How good have the regional attractiveness, regional emissiveness and spatial interaction been modeled? Which part has been modeled much better? These are important questions as it is not useful to add more regional attributes into a migration model if the spatial interaction is poorly modeled. This project will fill above research gap in regional migration modeling, using the case of interregional migration of China in the period 2000-2005. The research will overcome the problem of spatial autocorrelation in migration modeling and use the notion of migration spatial structure to estimate the effect of spatial interaction. Most previous migration models ignore spatial autocorrelation. Using the eigenvector spatial filtering approach, this project will formulate spatial filtered Poisson migration model for interregional migration in China in the period 2000-2005. Following the notion of migration spatial structure, the real or estimated interregional migration matrices in a migration system can be fully described by four main factors: the overall effect, the relative emissiveness and the relative attractiveness of specific regions, and the effect of spatial interaction between pairs of regions. These factors based on the real and expected migration matrices will then be compared. Estimation approach will be used to assess the contribution of the modeling performance of each of the four factors in the goodness of fit of the migration model. Methodologically, the findings of this project will point to directions to improve migration modeling on whether one should look for more and better regional attributes or should improve the approach to model the effect of spatial interaction. Practically, this study would contribute to a better understanding of migration process and better approaches of modeling migration system. 遷移模擬是描述遷移過程、確定影響遷移的重要因素的常用方法。本研究將使用2005年人口調查資料模擬中國2000-2005的區間遷移。 區間遷移的模擬與分析已取得許多進展。但是，之前的遷移模擬是在黑箱中進行的。遷移模型的整體表現只評估包括區域特徵與空間交互作用在內的所有影響因素的作用。在大部分研究中，距離只是作為一個普通的影響因素。對下列問題至今沒有詳細研究：空間交互作用與區域特徵對遷移有什麼作用？遷移模型對區域吸引力、區域排斥力與空間交互作用模擬程度如何？哪一部分模擬得更好？這些問題非常重要。如果空間交互作用模擬得很差，那麼增加更多的區域特徵因素是徒勞無益的。本研究將以中國2000-2005區間遷移為案例，填補上述區間遷移模擬研究中的空白。本研究將克服遷移模擬中的空間自相關問題，並使用遷移空間結構的概念來估計空間交互作用。 大部分遷移模型都忽略空間自相關問題。本研究將使用特徵根空間過濾法，建立中國2000-2005區間遷移空間過濾泊松遷移模型。根據遷移空間結構的概念，一個遷移系統的實際或者估計的區間遷移矩陳可以由如下四個因素完全地表示：總體影響、相對區域吸引力、相對區域排斥力和空間交互作用。根據實際或者估計的區間遷移矩陳得到的四個因素可以相互比較。本研究將使用評估每個因素的擬合程度對遷移模型總體擬合程度的貢獻。 在方法論方面，本研究的發現將指出改進遷移模擬的方向：是尋找更多更好的區域特徵因素？還是改進模擬空間交互作用的方法？在實際方面，本研究將有助於更好地理解遷移過程，並對發展更好的類比遷移系統的方法作出貢獻。

451912.label: Realisation of objectives
451912.value: Progress in the 1st reporting period 2013: The research project was started in 1 January 2013. As the budget cannot support an RA for 2 years, the original plan is to recruit an RA in the 2nd half of the year. But this is not realized as a good RA candidate took a postdoctoral post in Canada. It is planned that an RA will be recruited in 2014 and the research period will be extended for 6 months up to June 2015. However, some research activities in relation to the project objectives have been carried out and they consist of three main parts. Firstly, migration data and statistics on regional attributes have been collected and preliminary data analysis has been made. Some migration models have been estimated and they will be further refined in the next stage of research. Secondary, based on the initial migration models, the real and expected migration matrices have been decomposed into the overall effect, the relative emissiveness, the relative attractiveness and the effect of spatial interaction respectively. They will be re-estimated once new and better migration models are obtained. Thirdly, the PI has prepared a co-authored journal paper and a conference paper. Progress in the 2nd reporting period 2014: Good research progress has been made in this reporting period. Firstly, a new migration model has been estimated, the real and expected migration matrices have been decomposed again into the overall effect, the relative emissiveness, the relative attractiveness and the effect of spatial interaction respectively. Secondly, based on the decomposed results of the real and estimated migration matrices, preliminary estimation of migration errors has been obtained. It is found that the goodness of fit of various components is in the following order. The relative attractiveness and emissiveness can be modeled very well with R over 0.8. The asymmetric spatial interaction cannot be modeled with R below 0.1. Thirdly, the PI has prepared a co-authored journal paper and a conference paper. Research activities in 2015: Full analysis of the modeling error has been completed. Two sets of results have been obtained. One is based on a Poisson migration model and the result has been published in a paper titled “Modelling Interregional Migration in China in 2005–2010: the Roles of Regional Attributes and Spatial Interaction Effects in Modelling Error” in the top international journal in Population geography: Population Space and Place (early view). The second part of the analysis is based on a network spatially filtered Poisson migration model and a paper titled “Error analysis of regional migration modeling” is under review for the top geography journal: Annals of the American Association of Geographers (revised paper submitted). The result has also been presented in research seminar. In conclusion, the research developed an innovative approach to analyze the error in migration modeling using the internal migration case in China. It is an important advancement in migration modeling research. Three journal papers have been published and one journal paper is under review. Five presentations have been made in three conferences and two seminars. Two research objectives have been fully completed. The approach can be applied to migration system in other countries and regions.

451912.label: Major findings and research outcome
451912.value: Much methodological advancement has been made in the modeling and analysis of interregional migration. However, previous migration modeling has been done in a black-box. The overall performance of a migration model is evaluated with the contribution of all explanatory variables including regional attributes and spatial interaction effect. No detailed research has been made to examine the following. What are the contributions of spatial interaction and regional attributes to migration? How good have the regional attractiveness, regional emissiveness and spatial interaction been modeled? Which part has been modeled much better? To fill above research gap, this research uses a new method to estimate the migration modeling errors by their sources. The research overcomes the problem of spatial autocorrelation in migration modeling and uses the notion of migration spatial structure to estimate the effect of spatial interaction. Following the notion of migration spatial structure, the observed or estimated regional migration matrices of a migration system can be fully described by four main factors: the overall effect, the relative emissiveness and the relative attractiveness of specific regions, and the effect of spatial interaction between pairs of regions. By calculating the contributions of migration factors to the modeling error, this research reveals which factors of the migration process can be modeled more or less accurately using the recent data of regional migration in China. Two sets of results have been obtained. In the first analysis (see journal paper in Population, Space and Place, 2016), a Poisson migration model is estimated for China. Error analysis shows that the modelling errors of the overall effect, the relative attractiveness and emissiveness caused mean relative errors of 4.92%, 11.80% and 10.61% in migration flows, respectively. The spatial interaction caused a mean relative error of 17.74% in migration flows, which was the greatest. In the second analysis (see forthcoming paper in Annals of AAG, 2016), a network spatially filtered Poisson migration model is estimated. Several new error statistics are also used. Error analysis shows that the modeling errors of the overall effect, the relative emissiveness and attractiveness caused the weighted absolute mean errors of 1.20%, 14.60% and 15.57% in migration flows respectively. The spatial interaction caused the greatest weighted absolute mean error of 31.55% in migration flows. Thus the spatial interaction effect remains the most difficult to be modeled in migration modeling. More efforts should be made to improve the approach to model the effect of spatial interaction.

451912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
451912.value: Migration modeling is a typical problem of spatial modeling in geography which is a core research question in the discipline. The issue has become increasingly important with availability of large amount of spatial-temporal data of various flows and interactions in the world. This research clearly shows that the major modeling error comes from the modeling of spatial interaction effect instead of regional attributes. Current research in spatial interaction modeling is not adequate and more efforts can be in this research area to seek new breakthrough in the modeling approach and techniques. Research advancement in this direction will also benefit other spatial-temporal modeling in many fields such as spatial economic analysis, transport modeling, trade and travel studies in addition to migration modeling. Further research grant will be sought to engage new migration research in this area.

451912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
451912.value: Much methodological advancement has been made in migration modeling. However, previous migration modeling has been done in a black-box. The overall performance of a migration model is evaluated with the contribution of all explanatory variables including regional attributes and spatial interaction effect. This research uses a new method to estimate the migration modeling errors by their sources. A network spatially filtered Poisson migration model is estimated. Following the notion of migration spatial structure, the observed or estimated regional migration matrices of a migration system can be fully described by four main factors: the overall effect, the relative emissiveness and the relative attractiveness of specific regions, and the effect of spatial interaction between pairs of regions. Error analysis shows that the modeling errors of the overall effect, the relative emissiveness and attractiveness caused the weighted absolute mean errors of 1.20%, 14.60% and 15.57% in migration flows respectively. The spatial interaction caused the greatest weighted absolute mean error of 31.55% in migration flows. Thus the spatial interaction effect remains the most difficult to be modeled in migration modeling. More efforts should be made to improve the approach to model the effect of spatial interaction.

452112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
452112.value: 本研究探討中文字形學習在熟練讀者、發展中的讀者與有困難的讀者之中的情況。當讀者重複看見一個字幾次後，針對辨認該字的字形表徵會在讀者的記憶中建立起來(Holmes and Davis, 2002)，讓讀者能夠很快速(甚至自動化)地把該字認出來。 針對拼音文字讀者的研究指出，7-9歲的兒童在閱讀短文時能夠不經意地學習字形表徵，即使該字只出現幾次(Share, 1999)。很明顯，這種快速字形學習能力對閱讀發展很重要。研究人員亦發現，快速字形學習與兒童拼讀生字的能力、與及是否有機會把生字拼讀出來，很有關係(Cunningham, Perry, Stanovich, & Share, 2002)。此外，字形組合的知識、字義、和串字練習都跟快速字形學習有關。 目前尚未有很多中文快速字形學習的研究。雖然有研究發現一般的字形知識跟中文閱讀發展有相關(例如 Ho, Yau, & Au, 2003)，但他們沒有針對字形學習。我們 (Liu & Shiu (2011)成功引用了Share (1995)的 OFM範式在中文材料並發現中國八歲兒童能夠快速字形學習。我們亦發現形聲字的快速字形學習在缺乏形音轉譯的情況下仍能發生。 本研究的目標是探討影響快速字形學習的因素，包括：字形結構、意義、形-義、和詞彙背景，並探討這些因素對熟練讀者、發展中的讀者與有困難的讀者的影響是否有分別。本研究亦探討不同的字形學習測驗是否可以替代使用。預期本研究可以增進我們瞭解中國兒童如何可以達到快速的自動化認字，亦會指導我們如何幫助有困難的讀者增強認字能力。

452712.label: Realisation of objectives
452712.value: This project was originally motivated by a simple question of theoretical and empirical dialogue between the American literature on the sociology of higher education and the China case: The western literature has demonstrated that "proximity to college" is an important determinant of the likelihood of attending college in the US. Does this fact provide any insight into the widening urban-rural divide in access to higher education in mainland China? The answer is resoundingly negative: the China case requires an explanation based on a kind of structural exclusion that is far different from any of the popular mechanisms emphasized in the American and European literature. The answer is well supported with (1) publications in the ASR (one of the two topmost general-interest journals of sociology) and the SOE (the topmost specialty journal for basic research in the sociology of education), (2) three conference papers at major international conferences (in addition to conference presentations of earlier versions of the SOE paper), and (3) follow-up qualitative research designed to cross-validate the quantitative findings with case studies that stretched back to the cohorts of the late 1990s and from 2000s onward. Although the research question and the goals of the study are simultaneously theoretical and empirical, my original formulation of project objectives spelled only the techical-operational objectives. In fact, these technical objectives were just intermediate steps to deliver the overarching theoretical and empirical goals of the study. With regard to the theoretical goal, this study has accomplished richer and more significant results than I originally expected. The original guiding framework was anchored on a contrast between what I called the College Proximity Hypothesis and the Gateway Access Hypothesis. As the study evolved, I found it essential to go beyond this original framework. In particular, I am intrigued by Sigal Alon's recent adaptation-exclusion model proposed in her influential 2009 article in the ASR. Alon's model is a seminal synthesis and extension of the longstanding conceptual framework that has dominated the discourse in educational stratification. This model arguably offers the most sophisticated theoretical framework in the literature on comparative educational inequality to date. However, as argued and demonstrated in my joint paper with my former doctoral student (Tam and Jiang 2014), the Alon model can and should be further extended to incorporate both meritocratic and non-meritocratic mechanisms of intergenerational transmission of inequality. Convincing ASR reviewers of the validity of our claim is not easy. Our paper draws on a reanalysis of Alon's own empirical results to show that even the American case necessitates an extension of the Alon model. Both this paper and its lengthy official online appendix have been rigorously reviewed by 8 different ASR reviewers in 3 rounds of review. At the end, we did convince our reviewers and the editors of ASR. Our proposed theoretical framework fully accommodates not only Alon rich results on the evolution of inequality across American colleges of differential selectivity but also the China case of widening urban-rural divide. The newly extended framework facilitates a comparison of the China case with the dominant mechanisms of inequality of educational opportunity in the West. What about the goal of explaining the widening urban-rural gap in college attendance amid a massive expansion of higher education in China? The second publication coauthored with my former doctoral student (Tam and Jiang 2015) in the SOE has thoroughly discussed a structural exclusion hypothesis that differs from all conventional explanations in the Chinese literature and presented nontrivial test results confirming the hypothesis. The core findings of this study brought to light the unintended impacts of Chinese educational expansion policy that had powerfully engendered the widening gap between urban and rural students' college attendance. In addition, I have conducted supplementary research to cross-validate or support this answer. Most of the technical glitches have been described and discussed in previous annual reports. Some of these works have appeared in conference papers attached to Part C of this completion report. A final theoretical note: In delivering these theoretical and empirical goals, I learnt that while proximity does play a role in its impact on the formation of educational inequality, it does not operate on the usual logic of distance as a continuous function of travel cost--a fundamental principle in the science of geography. Distance of college is a non-issue to Chinese students; distance to upper secondary vocational school is a crucial issue because it is a gateway to college but the distance function is highly nonlinear and even discrete. Most importantly, distance to gateway as generator of inequality was entirely endogenous to historical state policy--echoing an enduring theme in the sociological science of education that inequality is usually socially constructed.

452712.label: Major findings and research outcome
452712.value: The China case of widening urban-rural gap in college attendance requires an explanation based on a kind of structural exclusion that is far different from any of the popular mechanisms emphasized in the American and European literature. Departing from all common explanations in the Chinese literature, this study shows that the dramatic increase of urban advantage for the 1989 to 2002 college entry cohorts is entirely due to the concentration of expanding opportunity for upper secondary vocational education in urban areas. This urban concentration was apparently due to an efficiency consideration but it had the inadvertent consequence of powerfully discouraging rural students to stay in upper secondary education, the pipeline or gateway for college education in mainland China. Fortunately, government policy had changed soon after 2002 though the economic incentive of rural students for college also started to decline. While proximity does play a role in its impact on the formation of educational inequality, it does not operate on the usual logic of distance as a continuous function of travel cost--a fundamental principle in the science of geography. Distance of college is a non-issue to Chinese students; distance to upper secondary vocational school is a crucial issue because it is a gateway to college but the distance function is highly nonlinear and even discrete. Most importantly, distance to gateway as generator of inequality was entirely endogenous to historical state policy--echoing an enduring theme in the sociological science of education that inequality is usually socially constructed. 452812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
452812.value: The aim of this project is to study the string-sawing technique seen on jades in Neolithic East Asia. String-sawing is a technique in which one uses a string coated with an abrasive to cut jades by rubbing it back and forth. Jade is a collective term applied to compact aggregates of either of two different minerals, nephrite and jadeite. Nephrite, including actinolite (Ca2(Mg,Fe2+)5Si8O22(OH)2) and diopside (MgCaSi2O6), was extremely popular in late Neolithic East Asia. Nephrite has an extreme toughness due to its interfelted microstructure, which consists of randomly oriented bundles of twisted hair-like fibers (Wen 1992). We propose that because of this nature of the mineral, knapping techniques in the Palaeolithic were no longer suitable for cutting its raw materials and executing on the material with high accuracy and delicacy, giving rise to the sawing technique. Abundant traces of string-sawing have been found on the jades of Xinglongwa, Hongshan and Liangzhu cultures (6000-3000 BC), but many scholars argue that they are the results of wheel cutting, while those who have discussed the string sawing technique have only limited themselves to textual descriptions (Mou 1989, 2003). To define such a technology with objective standards, experiments replicating the use wear, microscopic observations of excavated artifacts, and comparisons of a large amount of data are urgently needed. This standard will then allow sound analyses of the technique in the future, dissolving current disputes in prehistoric jade technology. All these considerations form the basis of the proposed two-year project to analyse excavated specimens from China, Russia, Japan and Korea. We will fully review and use the chaine operatoire approach in our survey, and systematically study the tool marks through digital photography and polarizing and scanning electronic microscopes. The expected results and impact are: 1. Establishment of an international database of standardised features and terminology to systematically define and document the string-sawing technique. 2. Facilitation of future research on the distribution, dispersion and chronological development of this technique with reference to the standards created. 3. As jades have long been highly esteemed in ancient China, the study of its production technology as a dynamic cultural phenomenon will also shed light on the social structures and worldviews of the societies concerned. The impact of this research reaches studies across and beyond East Asia, as the technique has also been found in the New World, such as the Maya and Olmec cultures.

452812.label: Realisation of objectives
452812.value: This study took an archaeological perspective to compare the microwear on prehistoric jades in East Asia, by conducting various experiments on jade sawing, and analyzing the production tool marks. We also studied the role of the string-sawing technique on the production chain of jades, established the temporal and geographical distribution of string-sawn jades in East Asia, as well as explored the role of string sawing in the standardization of jades and the role of jades in prehistoric societies. In East Asia, mainly during the Neolithic period between 8,000 and 4,000 years BP, people were possibly using animal or plant fiber to make strings, which were added with water and sand (possible quartz sand), to create tools for cutting jade. String sawing and blade sawing were two of the most frequently employed prehistoric jade sawing techniques. To understand these techniques better, we conducted several archaeological experiments. Firstly we conducted studies of tool marks left by production tools in order to postulate how archaeologically excavated jades were produced. The string sawing experiment involved the use of quartz sand, hemp rope, bamboo cylinders, wooden strips, and water. These are materials that were not unfamiliar to prehistoric peoples. The blade sawing experiment similarly used a stone blade, sand, and water. Our detailed observations from experimental jade production found that string sawing leaves curved undulating surfaces on the cutting surfaces, while blade sawing leaves horizontal lines. As such, the relief profiles of the cutting surfaces showed marked differences between those produced by the two techniques. These differences are mainly due to the mechanisms of the two methods: string sawing is directed by hand, while the shape of the blade determines the direction of blade sawing. These experimental results provided important clues to solve the debate in identifying the use of prehistoric string sawing versus blade sawing techniques. Additionally, we have conducted in depth research of prehistoric rotary technologies and held an international conference to discuss the topic broadly. So far, there is no possibility that wheel sawing existed before the Bronze Age, which excludes the likelihood that wheel sawing was involved in the production of jades. On the other hand, jades were often processed after cutting, and the visibility of tool marks can also be affected the burial environmental context. Identification of used jade technologies can be made difficult in these situations. However, through this project, we were able to further distinguish between string sawing and blade sawing techniques, as well as conclude the limits of reconstructing production tool marks of archaeological excavated jades, which cannot be fully resolved by experimental archaeology. According to the PI’s cross-regional surveys of the application of string sawing techniques to prehistoric jades, there are over a hundred archaeological sites in which jades have been found, extending from the Baikal region in Siberia to Lingnan in the south, and from the time period of over 10,000 years BP to the Xia-Shang-Zhou period. A total of several thousand jades have been unearthed at these sites. We attempted a comprehensive spatio-temporal categorization of string sawing techniques. Spatially, we inspected large numbers of jades from the Kitoyskaya (8,000 years BP) to Glazkovskaya cultures in research institutes and museums in Novosibirsk and Irkutsk. There was no evidence of string sawing on any jade objects. This discovery is preliminary evidence that the Baikal region cannot be the origin of the string sawing technique. In China, we investigated several tens of archaeological sites from the Northeast to the coastal Southeast, and found that string-sawn jades are densely found along the Wei River and the Yangtze River. The Lingnan region from Guangdong to Hong Kong was also within the region where prehistoric string sawing has been identified. In Hong Kong, there are several hundreds of precious stone rings from three to four thousand years ago, among which only several examples related to string sawing have been found. In Xinjiang, Gansu, Shaanxi, and Tibet in Northwest China, there has been no evidence of string sawing on jades or other precious stones thus far. In the Bronze Age, the string sawing technique is rare in general. In Southwest China, rare cases of string sawing techniques are seen on jades at Jinsha site. After the Bronze Age, the string sawing technique basically disappeared. One of the important results of this investigation is a comprehensive analysis of the oldest jade assemblages excavated in China, which were excavated at numerous sites dated to seven to eight thousand years ago in Northeast China. In particular, Xinglonggou site is where the earliest known evidence of millet has been found as well in China. We photographed the excavated jades from Xinglonggou under the microscope. For the first time, we were able to distinguish between tool marks left by string sawing, blank polishing, slit cutting, hole drilling, and hole enlarging. We were then able to record the successive relationships between the various production procedures. In contrasting the jade technologies between different sites, we suggest that the standardization of jades began seven to eight thousand years BP. The specialization of jades was already very advanced. Jades were only used by some social elites at the time, in which an economy of millet agriculture was beginning to form, likely relating to the tendency for yellow-green jades at the time. String sawing is furthermore an important foundation for the production of paired slit rings. In terms of raw materials, with the cooperation of the Institute of Archaeology at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, we have conducted the identification of raw materials and photographed microwear under the scanning electronic microscope. In terms of Xinglongwa culture, most jades are under 5 to 6 cm, while some of these had maroon red patches on the surface, suggesting that the raw materials were nephrite river cobblestones. We estimate that Neolithic jade raw materials were mainly nephrite river cobblestones.

452812.label: Major findings and research outcome
452812.value: 1. At the “Ancient Chinese Jade Artisanship” Symposium at the Institute of Archaeology at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences on October 9, 2015, the PI introduced the research summarized in the monograph Liangzhu Jades (2015), which has been recognized as a significant academic contribution to the study of jades across the nation. At the symposium, the PI discussed the origin of Yangtze River region string-sawn jades. He demonstrated for the first time that raw materials are string sawn at Mingshanhou site from 6,000 BP, and analyzed the characterization of string sawing in Liangzhu culture jades. 2. Proceedings of the International Conference on Prehistoric Rotary Technology and Related Issues at Hac Sa Macao (2014) demonstrates the seven thousand year history of rotary technologies in East Asia. Rotary machinery was however only used as turning tables, and there is no evidence of their direct use on jades for cutting. The studies included in this publication do not support the hypothesis that Neolithic jades were sliced with rotary blades. 3. In the essay “The Neolithic Jade Revolution in Northeast China” (expected to be published in 2017), we conducted a comprehensive analysis of Xinglongwa culture jades in Northeast China. In particular, all the jades found at Xinglonggou sites were photographed in detail, and established the foundations for studying jade microwear. We demonstrated that string sawing was already used at this stage to slice nephrite blanks into symmetrical paired jades. The differentiation of string sawing techniques in the creation of slit rings is an important direction for the technical analyses of jade production. 4. At the “Multidisciplinary Methods in Archaeology: Latest Updates and Outlook” International Symposium in Novisibirsk, Russia, the PI introduced the string sawing technique as an important technological characteristic of prehistoric jade production in East Asia. It can be said that without the string sawing technique, jades in Neolithic China cannot have thrived. For the conference, the PI completed the essay “Comparative study of Neolithic jade technologies: From Chertovy Vorota to Northeast Asia” (expected to be published in 2017) to discuss the relationship between string sawing techniques of China, Russia, and Japan.

452812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
452812.value: 1. We are currently collaborating with the Institute for the History of Natural Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences to include our research results in the history of prehistoric scientific technologies in China, as well as to strengthen the international understanding of Chinese jade cultures and jade technologies. 2. We are currently working with Russian academics to conduct in-depth analyses of jades in Far East Russia. On the other hand, many more string-sawn jades have been excavated in Japan in recent years. The study of string sawing and jades will have an even greater international impact in the future. 3. The dispersion of the string sawing technique in Russia and the eastern Japan Sea was likely not only one of material exchange, but also involved exchanges and interactions of people and societies. The strengthening of collaborations between China, Russia, and Japan is important direction for future research.

452812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
452812.value: Nephrite is a very hard and tough mineral. Before the existence of metal tools, prehistoric peoples invented a technique that overcomes toughness by flexibility—as in the use of strings with water and sand as the main tool to slice through nephrite raw materials and produce jades. Six thousand years ago, almost all jades in China were processed with the string sawing technique. Our experimental production of jades and the observation of microwear on more than a thousand prehistoric jades reestablished over five thousand years of the technological history of prehistoric string-sawn jades in China. The string sawing technique had already spread into Far East Russia, Honshu Japan, and the coastal Japan Sea by seven thousand years ago, creating a jade culture triangle between Northeast China, Russia, and the coastal Japan Sea. In future years, the PI will be actively collaborating with scholars in Russia, Japan, and Mainland China for further research.
