453012.label: Project Title(Chinese)
453012.value: 儀式、團結、社會合作：探索一種以塗爾幹理論為基礎的解決社會困境的方案

453012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
453012.value: The question of how to induce cooperation in social dilemma games such as the public goods game has been extensively researched. Many of the proposed solutions attempt to preserve the view that human agents are rational egoists and that social cooperation relies on structural arrangements channeling individuals’ self-interest maximizing behavior. In the current study, we take a different approach and explore a “Durkheimian solution” to the problem of cooperation in social dilemmas. It draws on Durkheim’s theory that social order is based on “solidarity” and that ritual performance is a key mechanism in generating emotional bonds of solidarity. We design laboratory experiments to examine whether engaging in acts of simulated ritual performance, such as synchronous or complementary drum beating, can enhance group solidarity and promote cooperative behavior in social dilemmas. We further examine whether, as predicted by the Durkheimian theory, symbols present in ritual performances will be charged with emotional energy and acquire the capacity to influence participants’ attitudes and cooperative behavior in later tasks. 如何使行動者在“社會困境”類型的博弈中進行合作，是一個受到廣泛關注的研究課題。在已有的文獻中，大多數關於該問題的解決方案都立足於個體乃是理性且自利的行動者這一假設，試圖用各種結構性的安排將個人追求自我利益最大化的行為導向合作性的結果。在本研究中，我們從塗爾幹的理論視角出發，探索一種不同的解決社會合作問題的方案。根據塗爾幹的理論，社會秩序的基礎乃是“社會團結”，而儀式表演則是社會團結和情感紐帶形成的重要機制。我們將採用實驗的方法，研究具有儀式表演性質的群體行為――例如以統一節奏擊鼓或者以配合方式擊鼓――是否能增強群體團結並促進合作行為。在研究中，我們還將進一步檢驗塗爾幹的另一相關論點，即在儀式過程中出現的符號是否能獲得“情感能量”並因此影響參與者態度和行為。

453312.label: Project Title(Chinese)
453312.value: 關於珠三角城市設計導則的調研: 廣州, 香港, 澳門和深圳

453312.label: Project Objectives
453312.value: With the shift from rigid top-down master planning to more open-ended multiple stakeholder approaches, many Chinese cities experienced increasing urban fragmentation. This research project investigates the usages and effects of urban design guidelines as a tool to address this fragmentation by negotiating between public and private interests; and to secure and improve the quality of the public realm. The project collects, classifies and analyses the urban design guidelines of the four Pearl River Delta cities, Guangzhou, Hong Kong, Macau and Shenzhen. It explores the reasons for the differences of these guidelines by investigating the individual and intertwined histories and cultures of the four cities, as well as their different legal and spatial conditions. In detailed case studies of selected sites in each city, the study will explore the effects of urban design guidelines and investigate the reasons for their success or failure. The research will be conducted with close links to the design studio teaching, giving students the opportunity to participate in research projects and help modeling in studio studio projects certain guideline effects. With the comparison of the different urban design guidelines of four Chinese cities, the project contributes to a more differentiated understanding of Chinese urbanism. The results of the research allow then comparisons with explorations of the effect of design guidelines in other Chinese, Asian and International cities. The outcome of the research will give designers, planners and policy makers a solid understanding about the potentials and limitations of urban design guidelines in these four cities as tools to balance public and private interests and improve the quality of the public realm.

453312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
453312.value: This research project focuses on urban design guidelines as a tool to shape urban form and direct urban development. It will identify and compare the guidelines of the Pearl River Delta (PRD) cities: Guangzhou, Hong Kong, Macau, and Shenzhen. Due to their individual history and the “One Country two Systems” policy, these cities have different planning systems and design cultures. As Hong Kong and Macau become increasingly integrated into mainland China, the understanding of these differences are important to recognize for a more productive integration process. In the first part, the study identifies the relevant guidelines of the four cities. This includes a historical overview from the early growth of Guangzhou, as Provincial Capital of Canton, to the practices of the Portuguese and British colonial empires to set up their cities, and arrives in the last period of rapid growth, with particular focus on Shenzhen. This part addresses the circumstances, mechanisms, and motives, under which the guidelines were formulated. Interviews with different stakeholders will be conducted, who were involved in or affected by the formulation of these guidelines. The guidelines will be visualized in drawings, allowing a better understanding of their way of operating and facilitating their comparison. In the second part, the guidelines will be organized according to issues they address. On selected sites, their performance over a longer period will be studied. This is crucial, as guidelines can become obstacles when not adapted to changing conditions. The third part will compare how the cities address same issues (e.g. regulating density or open spaces). This part will analyze also the underlying values, aspirations, and attitudes in the four cities. Design guidelines respond to economic and demographic situations, but also follow cultural and aesthetic preferences. Here also will be addressed how the guidelines negotiated between Western knowledge and Eastern wisdom. The study of the different approaches of the cities will allow learning from a wide range of approaches and experiences. In addition, the study aims to find out when urban design guidelines reach their limits. To answer this question the four cities are a good testing ground due to the radical speed and scale of their transformation processes in the last decades. The study will conclude with discussing the questions if and when guidelines can be an appropriate urban design tool to address the challenges of contemporary Asian urbanism.

453312.label: Realisation of objectives
453312.value: The research team decided to use the term “urban rules” to capture not only “urban design guidelines” but also other rules affecting the urban form and public realm in the selected cities. The study was organized as series of four conference papers followed by a book chapter and journal paper. The first three papers investigated the impact of urban rules for three urban conditions: (1) inner city areas, (2) industrial areas, and (3) villages reached by urban expansion. A fourth conference paper addressed recent environmental rules. The book chapter discussed how the research was linked to design teaching (Obj. 5). The identified rules were organized in timelines and tables, and classified according to the system by Lehnerer (A. Lehnerer, Grand Urban Rules, 2010). Based on the particular conditions of the Pearl River Delta, his rule collection was extended by preservation rules; land compensation and small house rules; environmental rules etc. (Obj. 2). The impact of the rules was investigated in case studies (Obj. 4). The comparative approach showed for instance that Guangzhou, Hong Kong, and Macau’s similar streetscape of colonnaded shop-house in the early 20th century resulted from different rules. The change of rules resulted in Guangzhou in strong urban fragmentation, while recent rules tried to preserve and reconnect the streetscape (Obj. 1). The comparative approach also showed that cities addressed similar issues in different ways. It also revealed how one city learned from another. It also captured the different motivations why rules were implemented and how they were followed (Obj. 3). As planned, the project was linked to design studios, and the rule studies used for the course Urban Planning and Design (Obj. 5). Most important obstacle of the project was the restriction of information in Mainland China, where even most basic information sometimes was impossible to obtain. Nevertheless, the team was able to collected extensive planning materials in the four PRD cities as well as in Lisbon and translated the documents from three languages. The team already produced four conference papers, a journal paper and book chapter and plans further journal papers based on the conference papers. The team believes that the developed comparative approach and its organisation according to urban conditions deliver important new insights for designers, planners and scholars (Obj. 7). In particular, the studies of rules of urbanizing villages and transforming streetscapes can be relevant for other cities in Asia and beyond (Obj. 6).

453312.label: Major findings and research outcome
453312.value: The project was organized as sequence of studies investigating rules for three urban conditions: INNER CITY For the study of inner city areas three street spaces were selected: Queen’s Road (Hong Kong), Zhongshan Road (Guangzhou), and Avenida Almeida Ribeiro (Macau). Results were presented at the 2014 Great Asian Street Symposium (Singapore). The paper was further refined and submitted to the Journal of Urban Morphology for peer review. Due to the word limit, only its findings are mentioned: In the 1930s, the selected streets were framed by colonnaded shop-houses. After World War II these streetscapes transformed. Hong Kong’s government relied on revenues from land leases and revised rules allowing higher densities. Key changes were the introduction of the plot-ratio, site coverage and site-class system, resulting in the verticalization of Queen’s Road. Macau’s government relied on income from the gaming and tourism industry. It implemented early rules, which preserved Avenida Almeida Ribeiro’s streetscape. After UNESCO World Heritage listing, the rules for the buffer zones were refined. However, after liberalization of the gaming industry, guidelines for areas outside the buffer zone were repealed. Guangzhou’s government followed Hong Kong by introducing a plot-ratio and site-class system. In the 1990, large developments substituted big portions of Zhongshan Road’s historical streetscape. Reconsidering the importance of heritage for tourism and responding to public concerns, it implemented new rules protecting remaining parts of the historical streetscape. INDUSTRIAL AREAS Another paper for the 2013 IFoU Conference (Tainan) investigated rules for industrial areas, using Kwun Tong (Hong Kong) and the OCT Loft area (Shenzhen) as study sites. The research was later extended to the industrial area of Macau north. VILLAGE AREAS REACHED BY URBAN EXPANSION For the study of urbanizing villages a comparative studio was organized focusing on Hung Shui Kiu (Hong Kong), Taipa Village (Macau) and Baishizhou (Shenzhen). Experts were invited to teach and join the research team. Research results were presented at the 2014 ISUF Conference (Porto). The combination of research and teaching was discussed in a book chapter forthcoming 2016 at University of Florence Press. ENVIRONMENTAL RULES After these studies, contemporary rules addressing environmental issues seemed still missing. The team embarked on the study of such rules in Hong Kong and Macau for the 2015 IFoU Conference (Incheon) and extended the study afterwards to Shenzhen. Another paper is planed to integrate the content of all four papers and reflect on the study of urban rules in general.

453312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
453312.value: The PI developed this urban rule study with the intention to link it with his public space research. Therefore he submitted a new GRF proposal combining both approaches. The new grant would allow him to continue the study of three main streets in Guangzhou, Hong Kong, and Macau with an ethnographic approach capturing the everyday life along the streets. It is planned to add Dihua Street in Taipei to the study to learn from the here applied preservation approach. For this project the research team at CUHK would collaborate with the PI’s long-term research partner at National Taiwan University. In addition, the comparative approach could easily be extended to other Asian cities. This could be developed with the partners of the International Forum on Urbanism network. The study was also developed to inform rule-based design approaches for the development of alternative design scenarios. As first step, a student from the Indian Institutes of Technology was hired as summer-intern and tested different modeling software. The result was that the program “City Engine” would be the most suitable software. It is planned to explore this further with a planned new digital design course for the MSc in Urban Design program (see attachment).

453312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
453312.value: This study investigated how urban rules affected the urban form and public realm of four Pearl River Delta cities, with Hong Kong and Macau having been developed originally under British and Portuguese colonial governments, Guangzhou evolving over 2000 years as provincial capital and Shenzhen being created as laboratory for China’s economic and policy reforms. As these cities share a similar climate, culture, and density, the impact of their specific rules becomes more apparent. These rules were studied according to three urban conditions: Inner city areas, industrial areas, and urbanizing villages, and classified according to the issues they address (e.g. ensuring public health & environment, shaping city images, protecting urban heritage, or boosting economic development). Thus the research informs designers and policy makers about alternative responses to urban issues which are shared also by many other cities. With detailed case studies the project also reveals different motivations behind the rules and the way they were followed. With the link of the research to design teaching, rule-based approaches were developed. Thus the project offers a deeper understanding of specific rules and their effects as critical input for contemporarily digital design approaches.

453312.value: Covering planning regulations in four cities and three languages the project needed extensive background research. This investment will unfold its full potential now, after having collected all materials and formed a strong research team with insights in the planning systems and practices in the four cities. Parallel to this project, the PI developed his other GRF projects investigating the impact of the MTR West Island Line on Community Space. These projects were linked to a series of community activities receiving broad media coverage. The rule research developed parallel providing a deeper understanding of underlying factors of the urban process. In the spring and autumn terms, the PI organized for the MSc in Urban Design program alternating design studios related to both GRF topics. The now submitted GRF proposal aims to join the two research approaches. In context of the study of urbanizing villages, the PI was invited as keynote speaker and partner for the project “Mobilizing the Periphery” of the Metropolitan Lab of ACNB Berlin, investigating urban peripheries in Africa, Asia, Europe and South America offering the opportunity to compare how in different parts of the world villages urbanize, land compensation is arranged and living spaces for arriving migrants created.

453612.label: Project Objectives
453612.value: The first objective is to examine the relation between key country-level institutional variables and the likelihood of corporate guidance issued by the firm after controlling for well-documented firm-level variables. The second objective is intended to supplement the current literature by not only examining the determinants of corporate guidance issuance, but also studying the characteristics of guidance issued by firms. In particular, this study will examine the impact of different institutional environment on two major guidance characteristics that are least understood, i.e. why firms in different countries provides different information in guidance, and how managers bundle corporate guidance with other information in different countries. The last objective of this study is to test whether information disclosed by firms voluntarily, such as corporate issued guidance is also informative (i.e. affect stock prices) outside of US. If corporate guidance is found to be informative in other countries outside of US as well, then it will be interesting to ask whether the informativeness of such information varies across countries because of the different institutional structure in different countries and/or because of the differences in guidance characteristics such as the different information provided and the differences in other information bundled with guidance. Finally, this study can also examine whether established firm-level factors which affect voluntary disclosure behavior of management depend on country-level institutional environments.

453612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
453612.value: This paper explores the effect of an economy’s institutional structure in managers’ incentives of issuing future performance guidance. Following prior literature, this study assumes that the institutional characteristics of a country create incentives different from the established firm-level incentives that influence managers and investors’ behavior and ultimately shape the properties of forecasted information. This study empirically examines the relation between key country-level institutional variables and the likelihood of management issued guidance (i.e. one major type of voluntary disclosure decision) and a broad array of characteristics of guidance issued by firms from more than 90 countries around the world where corporate guidance are mainly voluntary after controlling for established firm-level factors. One major and least studied characteristic of the guidance issued by management around the world is the different information provided in guidance (i.e. what accounts are forecasted?) and the differences in the information bundled together with the guidance (i.e. what information is bundled together with the guidance issued). This study further analyzes whether and how investors’ reaction of corporate issued guidance (i.e. the informativeness of management issued guidance) is affected by both the institutional structure of a country, and the characteristics of the guidance itself after controlling for other documented firm-level factors affecting the informativeness of corporate guidance. Finally, this study will also examine whether established firm-level factors which affect voluntary disclosure behavior of management depend on country-level institutional environments. 本文探讨不同经济体的制度因素对管理者发布业绩预测动机的影响。根据以往文献，本研究假设，一个国家的制度特征对管理层预测所产生的激励机制不同于企业层面所产生的，这种激励将影响管理者和投资者的行为并最终影响预测信息的特征。本研究选取全球90多个以自愿披露预测信息为主的国家和地区的公司为样本，控制已有的公司层面因素，实证检验关键的国家层面制度因素变量与管理层是否自愿披露业绩预测（自愿披露决策的一个重要类型）、以及业绩预测一系列特征之间的关系。关于管理层预测信息特征的研究，近来主要集中在预测所包含的信息（哪些项目被预测）和绑定预测一起发布的信息（什么样的信息与预测信息绑定一起发布）。本课题深入分析对于发布预测的公司，投资者的反应（也就是预测的信息含量）是否受到制度因素和预测信息特征两方面的影响，如受影响又是如何影响的。最后，本研究也将检验已有的公司层面因素对管理层自愿性披露行为的影响是否有赖于国家的制度环境。

453612.label: Major findings and research outcome
453612.value: We examine the relationship of management forecasts and country-level institutional features across 78 countries. We find that the incidence of management forecasts is (a) positively associated with country-level institutional characteristics related to the protection of private business, (b) negatively associated with country-level institutional characteristics related to investor protection, (c) negatively associated with the level of government involvement in the economy, and (d) positively associated with the quality of mandatory reporting. Various properties of management forecasts such as frequency, precision, horizon, attribution, and the type of news in the forecast are also systematically related to these country-level institutional characteristics. In examining whether management forecasts are informative to the stock market, we find that forecasts are informative in nearly all countries. Moreover, institutional characteristics related to protection of private business and investors, and the quality of the mandatory reporting systems enhance the informativeness of management forecasts, and government involvement in the economy is negatively associated with the informativeness.

453612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
453612.value: The data used for this research can be used for examining an array of future research questions. For example, future research can use this data to examine whether the effect of corporate issued guidance to shareholders and internal decision markers varies across countries with different institutional factors.

453612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
453612.value: Our study contributes to the broad literature on cross-country determinants of corporate transparency. Most extant research on corporate transparency in the international setting either focuses on mandatorily reported information or studies general information disclosure without distinguishing between voluntary and mandatory disclosures. As such, our findings are likely to spawn future empirical and analytical research.The study also contributes to the literature on management forecasts. Prior research on management forecasts primarily focuses on U.S. firms. We know little about the prevalence of this form of disclosure in other countries, whether it is informative to investors, and whether and how it is related to country-level institutional characteristics. The international setting provides a rich context to examine the relationship between country-level institutional characteristics and management forecasts and enables us to provide insights that cannot be obtained from within-country studies.

454612.label: Project Title(Chinese)
454612.value: 结构性证券市场中管理公司与银行的关系

454612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
454612.value: Collateralized debt obligations (CDO) played a devastating role during the credit crisis of 2007-2008. Many studies show that securitization has led banks to lower their lending standards and originate lower quality mortgage loans (e.g., Mian and Sufi (2009), Keys et al. (2010)). However, it is not clear why CDO managers, supposedly smart institutional investors, would buy these inferior assets. Anecdotal evidence suggests that many CDO managers were well connected to banks and might be the exit channel for banks to dump bad assets. In this project, we plan to investigate the role of connection between CDO managers and banks in the rapid expansion and abrupt breakdown of structured credit markets. We will first analyze whether connection between managers and banks plays a role in collateral selection and the choice of underwriters in CDO issues. We then plan to examine following two alternatives: 1) collateral manager gains private information through their relationship with asset originating banks and hence relationship is associated with better performance; 2) asset originators use their connections with collateral managers to distribute lower quality assets, leading to a negative relation between connection and CDO performance. We define manager-bank connection as prior employment relation of key personnel in a CDO manager with major banks. We focus on structured finance CDOs which repackage mortgage- and other asset-backed securities, as the incentive distortion is the most severe in this market. Our work will help us better understand incentive problems in structured credit markets. It is surprising that financial institutions, such as hedge funds, private equity funds, and asset managers, actively purchase toxic assets created by banks. Personal relationship and connections might be one part of the picture. Our analysis will also contribute to the literature on social network. Social networking has been shown to improve information sharing and lead to better performance in venture capital investment, mutual funds, and other financial decisions (e.g., Ljungqvist et al. (2007), Cohen et al. (2009, 2010)). The CDO market may be an example of adverse impact of connections in Wall Street. 在2007-2008年的信贷危机，债务抵押债券（CDO）起到了破坏性的作用。许多研究表明，资产证券化已经导致银行降低贷款标准，发行低质量房屋贷款（例如，Mian and Sufi (2009), Keys et al. (2010)）。然而，目前尚不清楚，CDO经理，通常被认为聪明的机构投资者，为何会买这些不良资产。有证据表明，许多CDO经理人和银行有密切的联系，并可能是银行抛售不良资产的退出渠道。在这个项目中，我们计划调查在结构性信贷市场快速扩张和突然崩溃的过程中，CDO经理和银行之间的关系的作用。 我们首先分析CDO管理公司和银行之间的关系是否在CDO的抵押物和承销商的选择中起到了重要作用。然后，我们计划检验以下两种可能性：1）管理公司通过与银行之间的关系获得私有信息，因此它们之间的关系和更好的绩效呈现正相关; 2）银行利用这种关系分销低质资产，从而导致它们之间的关系和CDO的绩效表现呈负相关关系。我们定义的CDO经理和银行的关系是指CDO管理公司的主要人员曾经在该银行工作过。我们专注于结构性金融债务抵押债券，这种抵押债券是将房屋贷款和其他资产作为抵押的证券重新打包，这个市场呈现出最严重的激励上的扭曲。 我们的工作将帮助我们更好地了解结构性信贷市场中的激励问题。令人惊讶的是，金融机构，如对冲基金，私募股权基金和资产管理公司，积极购买银行的有毒资产。私人的关系和联系可能是其中的一部分原因。我们的研究将对社会关系的研究做出一定的贡献。目前的研究表明社会关系可以改善信息共享从而提高风险投资，共同基金和其他财务决策的绩效（例如，Ljungqvist et al. (2007), Cohen et al. (2009, 2010)）。 CDO市场有可能是社会关系在华尔街产生的负面影响的一个例子。

455512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455512.value: It is not uncommon for public auditors to sit on corporate boards. Previous studies have documented that having accountants or other financial experts on boards improves corporate governance [Agrawal and Chadha, 2005. Corporate governance and accounting scandals. Journal of Law & Economics 48: 371-406; DeFond, Hann, and Hu, 2005. Does the market value financial expertise on audit committees of boards of directors? Journal of Accounting Research 41: 153-193]. However, the extant literature has not addressed an important question: does holding directorships in particular and outside positions in general affect the quality of auditors’ main business, audit services? Prior directorship and audit research suggests that outside directorships could affect audit quality in one of two competing ways. On the one hand, outside directorships would enhance audit quality by motivating auditors to build and maintain their reputation or improving their industry expertise. On the other hand, outside directorships could impair audit quality by reducing the time and effort that auditors spend on audit services or threatening auditor independence. Therefore, how outside directorship affects audit quality is an empirical issue. We attempt to answer this question by using the Chinese data. The findings will not only yield important policy implications for the audit profession and market regulators, but also contribute to the growing literature on audit quality research at the individual auditor level. 公衆審計師出任其他公司的董事幷不罕見。以往的研究說明，會計師或其他財務專家擔任董事可增强公司治理[Agrawal and Chadha, 2005. 公司治理與會計醜聞. 法律及經濟學學刊48: 371-406; DeFond, Hann, and Hu, 2005. 市場是否看重董事會下審計委員會的財務專長? 會計研究學刊41: 153-193]。然而，現有文獻尚未研究審計師擔任外部職務時尤其是任職董事時是否對其主業，即審計服務，之質量産生影響。根據以往的董事及審計研究文獻，出任外部董事如何對審計質量産生影響有下述兩種相競爭的可能。一方面，外部董事職務可促使審計師建立幷維持其聲譽或增强其行業專長，從而提高審計質量。另一方面，外部董事職務可能减少審計師在審計業務上花費的時間及精力或降低其獨立性，進而對審計質量産生不良影響。故而外部董事職務如何影響審計質量實屬經驗性問題。我們利用中國的數據對此問題進行解答，論文的發現不僅對審計職業及市場上管制者有著政策性含義，也對個人審計師層次的審計質量研究這一快速發展的文獻作出了貢獻。

455512.label: Major findings and research outcome
455512.value: After collecting the data over an extended sample period (2000–2014), we carefully conducted the tests. However, different from our original predictions, we find no evidence suggesting that taking outside directorships affects audit quality; nor do we find reliable evidence on how the effect of directorships varies by auditor reputation, industry experience, the number of directorships, or other attributes. We therefore overhauled the research project. Specifically, we now primarily motivate the study from how audit partner busyness influences audit quality. The extant literature provides mixed evidence on and explanations of this issue. Sundgren & Svanström (2013 CAR) and Gul, Ma & Lai (2017 JIAR) argue that busyness is associated with worse audit quality while Goodwin & Wu (2016 CAR) suggest that in equilibrium busyness does not necessarily affect audit quality. By showing how an exogenous shock to a partner’s workload (namely being appointed as outside directors) influences his/her practice, we contribute to this line of research. We find that partners strategically reduce their clientele size after taking outside directorships. Importantly, they also adjust their client portfolios by dropping engagements that are more complex or of higher risks and therefore harder to audit. Such evidence is important. First, it suggests that partners consider other duties when optimizing their client portfolio; therefore, partners’ client portfolio formation should be viewed as endogenously determined. Second, given that auditors are apt at optimizing their portfolios to reduce the overall risk, taking outside directorships does not impair audit quality (which perfectly explains why we fail to find that taking outside directorships impairs audit quality). Apart from contributing to the auditing literature, the new angle also sheds light on the corporate director behavior. The bulk of director literature has focused on how directors monitor or advise the firm management. Whether and how holding outside directorships influences the directors’ own main businesses is not well understood. This is at least partly due to the lack of systematic data on and well-accepted methodology for measuring directors’ main businesses. By showing how outside directorships shape auditors’ client portfolio adjustment and audit quality, we provide initial evidence to this important and interesting issue. We are currently writing up the paper based on the new perspective.

455512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
455512.value: We will use the current data set for another research project: “Auditors in the Boardroom”. The main research question of this new project is: How does directors’ accounting expertise influence their performance in the corporate boardroom? The innovation is that we can empirically measure expertise by an auditor-director’s quality in his/her primary business, namely quality of audits in public companies, using well-established methods in the audit quality literature. The current literature on director behavior may look at broad measures such as experience in M&A or directors’ reputations. But to our knowledge, no prior study has looked at quality based on the directors’ main businesses. We will link audit quality of a partner to his/her boardroom performance. Such audit quality measure can be audit reporting errors, rate of restatements, accounting accruals, etc. Boardroom performance can be captured by firms’ accounting quality, financing and operating activities (e.g., related party transactions), sanction records, etc. We expect that an auditor-director with certain attributes (e.g., lower accruals in his audited clients, more conservative, less restatements, etc.) will also bring such attributes to the firms’ behavior through his/her monitoring or advisory role in the boardroom.

455512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
455512.value: It is not uncommon for public auditors to sit on corporate boards. Previous studies have documented that having accountants or other financial experts on boards improves corporate governance. However, the extant literature has not addressed an important question: does holding directorships affect the quality of auditors’ main business, audit services? Using the Chinese data and the difference-in-differences design, we find that auditors reduce the number of engagements and adjust client portfolio by dropping complicated and/or risky clients following an increase in the number of outside directorships. However, there is no evidence on impaired audit quality due to auditors’ outside directorships. Our findings not only yield policy implications for the audit profession and market regulators, but also contribute to the growing literature on audit quality research at the individual auditor level.

455712.label: Project Title(Chinese)
455712.value: 爭議空間與尺度政治：中國城市群城際鐵路規劃研究

455712.label: Project Objectives
455712.value: To explore the formal institutional structure and the ad hoc process for ICR planning. This is to understand multi-level decision-making processes for ICRs and how to put in place planning decisions that cut across administrative boundaries, targeting the facility most important for regional growth within a complex mix of players. Through a grounded empirical research, • To investigate the politics of scale in the ICR planning process to assess if it is emerging as a hybrid, contradictory, and relatively open process. Myriad organizations and agencies are involved in such a process. With the decline of central state control, there is a rise in the power, range of functions and salience of local governments as key planning and investment agencies. Simultaneously, the central state continues to play a critical role in inter-scalar articulation and regional governance, even though its dominance is being decentralized. The inter-connections of these processes comprise an ensemble of socially embedded, politically regularized and strategically selective forces in developing ICRs. • To examine the impacts of politics of scale on individual cities in terms of urban spatial changes and accessibility. This can be used to assess to what extent ICR-induced spatial transformation is a result of planning negotiation and if such result increases accessibility gap between cities. To critically examine the existing literature on the politics of scale and provide new insights to assist in theorizing reconstituted state spaces in contemporary China. To draw lessons from current planning practice. The aspects of the institutional structure which are particularly challenging for regions will be identified and potential strategies for streamlining them will be proposed.

Simultaneously, the central state continues to play a critical role in inter-scalar articulation and regional governance, even though its dominance is being decentralized. The inter-connections of these processes comprise an ensemble of socially embedded, politically regularized and strategically selective forces in developing ICRs. • To examine the impacts of politics of scale on individual cities in terms of urban spatial changes and accessibility. This can be used to assess to what extent ICR-induced spatial transformation is a result of planning negotiation and if such result increases accessibility gap between cities.
To critically examine the existing literature on the politics of scale and provide new insights to assist in theorizing reconstituted state spaces in contemporary China.

To draw lessons from current planning practice. The aspects of the institutional structure which are particularly challenging for regions will be identified and potential strategies for streamlining them will be proposed.

455712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
455712.value: 本研究探究中國城市群城際鐵路規劃過程中出現的尺度政治現象及其空間影響，尤其希望深入瞭解規劃過程的細節與各持份者的談判策略，並分析1）他們如何建立各自的立場；2）如何為自身利益謀劃發展及討價還價；3）最終談判結果如何影響城市空間結構及城市可達性。 地理學家將城市群定義為連綿都市帶或大都市區，一般是指由行政獨立但功能上相互聯繫的城鎮集聚在一個或多個較大中心城市周邊而形成的區域，如珠三角和長三角。通常，城市群發展速度驚人。有些城市群土地面積不大，卻容納超過五千萬人口。由於跨越多個行政區，城市群發展面臨諸多問題。快速發展的同時，存在各自為政的現象，缺乏區域設施協調發展的經驗。學術界對這類問題的深入研究尚不多見。過去二十年，地理學家逐漸意識到中國城市群已經成為資本積累、國家管制及政治協商的新的空間尺度。這種現象與改革開放前實行的國家社會主義或改革開放後出現的新自由主義城市化有本質差別。區域被認為是正在興起的國家管制空間。在這個空間尺度上，代表不同層級與不同部門利益的持份者都在影響區域發展，他們或職能重疊或相互競爭，共同塑造著區域空間。因此，用 “尺度政治”作為本課題的理論切入點將有助於我們對區域尺度上複雜多變的“政治芭蕾舞劇”的瞭解。 區域尺度變得日益重要，但對其理論與實證研究存在不足。這主要表現在三方面。其一，現有研究傾向于採用單一理論來解釋城市區域主義現象，並不十分關注地方實踐。其二，現有研究缺乏對詳細案例的分析，未能揭示社會變革中出現的歷史因素與路徑依賴如何影響政治決策過程。其三，現有研究很少涉及“尺度政治”空間影響的實證分析。正是基於這些考慮才促使我們劃定本課題的研究範圍。 本課題將嘗試從“尺度政治”角度出發來填補現有研究的空白。我們以珠三角城際軌道交通網絡為案例，結合珠三角行政權力分散、區域協調機制不足的現狀，探討該項目的發起、規劃、磋商到實施的過程，並分析其對地理空間的影響。基於試點研究，本課題提出從四方面分析城際鐵路規劃中尺度政治的多重特性，即中央部委間的衝突、不同層級政府間的矛盾、同級城市之間的緊張、國家與市場之間的關係。我們將分析這四方面如何影響所選線路的規劃決策（站點數目與選址、線路走向與設計），最終決策又如何投射到城市空間與城市可達性上。研究成果不但有助於制定區域政策，也能進一步完善社會轉型期國家與空間關係的理論解釋。

455712.label: Realisation of objectives
455712.value: 1) We have fully achieved the objective 1, i.e. to explore the formal institutional structure and the ad hoc process for ICR planning. This is achieved through a thorough investigation on the changing regime of ICR system, and the emerging forces that help to refine such regime. To fully investigate the formal institutional structure, we have looked at three dimensions of China’s railway regime. The first dimension is interministry conflicts. This operates at central level, having great shaping power on scalar politics. The central structure for coordinating regional railways is both monopolistic and highly fragmented, with several key central state actors having respective functions and power. While MOR dominated the railway industry, major project decisions were made through interministerial networking. The second dimension is interscalar tensions. The Ministry of Railway (MOR) hegemony was once the accepted norm, but many new lines were built as joint venture lines (JVs) with local governments. JVs can serve as a vehicle to redefine interscalar structure, because planning decisions have to be negotiated, evaluated and regulated between different tiers of governments. This is a social practice that is fundamentally different from past experience. The third dimension, intercity networking operates at local level. In this aspect, we look at how cities use intercity networking as a political tactic to advance their interests and to influence the outcome of interscalar politics in the name of mutual benefits. This opens up a new window to unravel the co-presence and face-to-face deliberations of the pertinent projects, and how different cities negotiate to shape the trajectory of scalar politics, making use of respective discourses and social practices to forge ahead intercity networking. Within the aforementioned structure, MOR or its successor China Railway still dominated railway regime on at least four dimensions. These are: (1) policy-making including plans, strategies, regulations, and pricing. The State Council plays only a token role (Li, 2009); (2) systemwide train and rolling stock control with only non-core functions devolved to the MOR-owned RRAs; (3) technical standards setting with rules governing non-state railways drawn up with reference to the technical operations of state railways; and (4) revenue settlement with details unknown to other parties. This is within this rich institutional feature that the Pearl River Delta Intercity Railroads have been negotiated, designed, developed, and operated. For the ad hoc planning process of ICR in the Pearl River Delta, we have thoroughly examined the planning process (e.g. line alignment, state selection, and the selection of technical parameters). We have carried out site investigations and interviews in all relevant cities in the Pearl River Delta. The latest fieldtrip to the Pearl River Delta was in August 2017. It is found that the majority percentage of ICRs have evidently influenced by scale politics as we have originally assumed. No single agents could dictate the decision-making process. All agents were constrained by the complex relation of power between them, such as the power to regulate the railway sector, the power to administer the territorial development plan, the access to investment, or the political power seeking to reaffirm the importance of local scale. In other words, even in a centrally monopolized sector, farmers, residents, local governments, localized capital sources, locally specified land assets, and geographical attachments of these forces are increasingly becoming vital and disobedient in shaping planning process. There is no fixed planning process. Each line has its own features in such process. Yet, all agents used scale discursively as a means of materializing their political projects - including/excluding particular political actors to force in their interests. 2) We have also fully achieved the objective 2, i.e. to investigate the politics of scale in the ICR planning process to assess if it is emerging as a hybrid, contradictory, and relatively open process. This is achieved through fieldtrips, interviews, and focus group discussions. As mentioned in point 1), we have verified that myriad organizations and agencies are involved in the planning process of ICRs. With the decline of central state control, there is a rise in the power, range of functions and salience of local governments as key planning and investment agencies. Simultaneously, the central state continues to play a critical role in inter-scalar articulation and regional governance, even though its dominance is being decentralized. The inter-connections of these processes comprise an ensemble of socially embedded, politically regularized and strategically selective forces in developing ICRs. Therefore, we argue that the state railway regime, which is commonly recognized as a centrally constituted, internally coherent, and operationally closed system, is emerging as a hybrid, contradictory, and relatively open system. Local states are no longer passive agents of the centre, which does not entirely retreat its power either. Both are parts of the structure of power. The actors at different scales deploy respective political projects, trying to influence the scalar relations. Another aspect of objective 2 is to look at the impacts of the politics of scale on individual cities in terms of urban spatial changes and accessibility. To fulfill this objective, we conducted a survey on 5,000 passengers along Guangzhou-Zhuhai Line, the first and the only operating ICR line in the Pearl River Delta. Based on the data collected, we have calculated the ‘relationship between ICR fare and Door-to-door Total Travel Cost’ and the ‘relationship between On-ICR-time and Total Travel Time’ to judge the accessibility of ICR stations. To strengthen our effort, we have gone beyond what has been proposed in our proposal. For instance, to measure potential accessibility changes of cities due to the development of ICRs, we are using three geographic information system (GIS) search engines: MapInfo (Pitney Bowes Software), Mapbar (Beijing Mapbar Technology Co.), and CenNavi (CenNavi Technology Co.), other GIS technique, and big data for commercial activities in the Pearl River Delta to gauge the impacts of the politics of scale. One PhD student is doing her research on the impacts of the politics of scale in this direction. A range of interesting findings have been identified and included (will be included) in our publications. 3) We have fully achieved objective 3, i.e. to critically examine the existing literature on the politics of scale and provide new insights to assist in theorizing reconstituted state spaces in contemporary China. Our critical engagement with existing literature has been extremely insightful for us to develop a new theoretical perspective to scale. We deem the emerging scholarship on state spatiality in China to be punctuated by a major inadequacy – the preoccupation with the political economic approach of existing accounts to read “scale” as material (re)construction of power relations. After identifying this inadequacy, we realize that the political discourses for rescaling in China are indeed infused with diverse scalar narratives and notions to evoke particular geographical imaginaries which lead support to scalar reconfiguration. This enables us to combine the political economy of scale with poststructuralist approach in deciphering scale. 4) We have fully achieved objective 4, i.e. to draw lessons from current planning practice. We have identified the aspects of the institutional structure which are particularly challenging for regions and proposed potential strategies for streamlining.

455712.label: Major findings and research outcome
455712.value: In addition to our ongoing effort, we have produced 3 journal papers and 4 book chapters so far. Investigators have attended six conferences to present research findings. Because of this project, the PI has been awarded the Post-Doctoral Fellowship Scheme of CUHK to recruit a senior researcher to work on similar research. With the funding, the PI has collaborated with scholars in Chinese mainland and overseas. The PI has been invited to a range of overseas universities to present research findings from the project. These include the University of Sydney, the University of Melbourne, UCL, TUDelft, Beijing Jiaotong University, and East China Normal University. A video on my presentation on this project was produced by the University of Sydney (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QMEAqmVqxdk), and has been widely circulated through different channels. Most importantly, the research yields some important findings. It is not possible to list all findings here. We just highlight some key findings. Theoretically, we have developed a new theoretical perspective to interpret the scale (also see 5.3, point 3). In the traditional interpretation of political economy, “scale” is read as material (re)construction of power relations. Such theoretical interpretation is illuminating, and stimulates much admirable work which elucidates China’s transition. Nevertheless, the perspective has been subject to increasing criticism since the early 2000s due to its placing too much emphasis on scale as an ontological existence while ignoring scale as an epistemological construct. We have argued that, rather than simply treating scale as material political relations being (re)shaped by scalar political contestations, scale should also be viewed as “a representation device or discursive frame” deployed by actors and groups to (re)shape political relations. Empirically, two key research outcomes are significant. First, we have studied the impacts of the politics of scale. This is a pioneer work, bearing critical policy implications. Second, we have examined the variegated planning processes of ICRs, which has produced a rich reference for policy-making in addition to academic significance.

455712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
455712.value: As this is a pioneer work on the planning process of ICRs and the spatial impacts of the politics of scale, there is a great potential for further development of the research. One PhD student of the PI is now conducting a research on deepening our understanding on the spatial impacts of the politics of scale. The student has completed data collection and analysis. While completing her thesis, we are now drafting journal papers and book chapters. Moreover, the theoretical attempt of combining the political economic approach and the poststructuralist endeavor can be applied to other research. With a similar theoretical lens, the PI will propose new research projects in the future.

455712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
455712.value: Intercity Railways (ICRs) have developed rapidly in China. Yet, the planning regime of ICR remains a mystery to outsiders. To most people, Chinese Railways (CR) is state-owned and operated. It is also notorious for its escalating debt, which threatens the national banking system. Relatively little is known about how the planning regime of CR has changed in order to deal with the debt problem and other thorny issues such as site selection for railway stations and the changing spatial relationship between cities due to the uneven development of ICRs. This research focuses on the Pearl River Delta (PRD) in Guangdong, the first province in China to propose an ICR network. It explores the ways in which key planning decisions (e.g. the number of stations, their location, and the route design and alignment) for the PRD-ICR network are initiated, planned, negotiated and implemented in the context of a diffuse regional power structure and an inadequate institutional environment. It then assesses how the final, negotiated choices affect passengers, the real users of ICRs, and the spatial relationship between cities. The research is thus highly relevant to Hong Kong in its efforts to facilitate cross-border infrastructure projects connecting with the Chinese mainland.

456412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
456412.value: 儘管公司欺詐問題非常嚴重，在轉型經濟體中這個問題迄今為止得到的關注還很少。我們的研究旨在通過研究羞辱制裁（代替法律制裁）是否以及如何對減少中國上市公司的欺詐行為產生影響，來部分地彌補這個研究缺口。以汙名化形式存在的羞辱制裁，是由有關當局為違法者的定罪和懲罰制定一個公共場面，從而引起人們對某個不端行為的反對並在社會中形成標準的非刑事執法機制。在轉型經濟體中，譴責、指責或者訓斥形式的公開羞辱通過股票交易來確保上市公司的公平操作和金融市場的增長。由於經歷了快速制度變遷，轉型經濟體中的正式法律和規範還不健全，在處理公司不道德行為上公開羞辱就很常見。另外，羞辱制裁通過股票交易形成了道德、價值觀和認知模式，因此它在中國就承擔著特殊的任務。所以在轉型經濟體中，我們就可以看到新的制度邏輯是怎樣由執行機制生動地呈現出來的。 利用公開羞辱作為研究背景，我們開發了一個污點化過程模型，包括四個相關的群體：仲裁者（股票交易），傳達者（媒體），違法者（欺詐的公司）和違法者的社會同行（在股票交易中的其它上市公司）。我們的研究關注這四個群體，特別是和中國的制度環境相關的部分。在法律和犯罪學的研究文獻中經常會區分兩種羞辱制裁：分裂型羞辱理論和重新融合型羞辱理論。分裂型羞辱理論主要關注將違法者標記出來，重新融合型羞辱理論追求為違法者提供機會從而重新在團體中獲得尊重。我們假定這兩種羞辱制裁可能對違法者及其社會同行有不同的影響，因此它們對減少未來違法的可能性的影響也會相應不同。 我們的理論框架主要以制度觀點以及來自公司欺詐行為、污點化、媒體和社會的文獻的論點為前提，整合這些理論角度可以幫助我們更深入地檢驗公開羞辱制裁造成的污點化過程。基於這個框架，我們通過檢驗羞辱制裁可能怎樣被用於減少犯罪來推動理論的發展，從而豐富我們對規範、慣例、價值觀如何形成，以及在中國如何正被聲譽制裁影響的理解。文章的實證結果也為中國和其它有類似制度特點的國家的公司、仲裁者以及政策制定者提供借鑒。

456412.label: Realisation of objectives
456412.value: The funded research project was a continuation project from a previously funded GRF project “Corporate Financial Frauds and Internal Governance Restructuring in Transition Economies: A Dual Consideration of the Political and Social Processes” (CUHK458110) that is themed on corporate financial fraud in transition economies. The funded research has produced 9 publications that was accepted, under revise-and-resubmit, under review, and in final preparation to submit to top-tiered management journals. In particular, 1 article was published at Organization Science, one is under R&R at Journal of Management, two are under review at Academy of Management Journal, one is under review at Academy of Management Review (after rejected at Journal of International Business Studies), one is under review at Organization Science, one is under review at JOM, and one was rejected at AMJ and is now under revision for submitting to Strategic Management Journal, and one is in preparation to submit to Administrative Science Quarterly. The preliminary ideas and findings of the funded research also have been presented five times at international and regional conferences including the Academy of Management annual meeting, Strategic Management Society annual international conference, Asia Academy of Management Conference, and International Association of Chinese Management Conference. The funded project has also succeeded in training a doctoral student who will graduate by the end August in 2016. The other co-authors of the papers, though not directly trained from this research grant, are also PhD graduates under the PI supervision and benefited extensively from the engagement in the research project. The fruitful research outputs derived from the research grant have produced insightful research findings, including: 1. The significance role of public shaming in the form of regulatory or administrative governance. The conceptual piece under review at AMR developed a rich theoretical model that explains the cross-level linkage between a country’s moral institution and managerial moral identity, which provides a fresh and contextual perspective to theorize the phenomenon of corporate fraudulence. The piece under R&R at JOM provides strong evidence that alternative governance, namely administrative, relational, and foreign governance mechanisms, are at work in the transition economy of China where formal, legal institutions are still developing. 2. During the course of the research engagement, a series of research has been stimulated to explore a closer and deeper examination of the role of public shaming in the form of media governance on the punishment and deterrence of corporate fraudulence. The two papers under review at AMJ, respectively, examine the role of media shaming on firm valuation with a focus on the power of socio-linguistics in shaping audience mind and influencing their judgement on the fraud firm. We find that firms suffer significant loss in stock return due to the media shaming framing effect, and such effect is further strengthened by prior media coverage and prior media sentiment. The other piece under review at AMJ underscores the side-effects of media coverage on the deterrence of frauds. Using a labeling theory viewpoint, we found significant result that media coverage and its pattern can backfire and turn the fraud firm to have a change of identity and recidivate again. 3. Despite a hard and challenging process, the research has met the objective to provide methodological advances in compiling large amount of textual data and analyze them using advanced textual analytics. A methodology piece has been submitted and under review at Journal of Management. A doctoral dissertation based on this advanced methodology is also produced.

456412.label: Major findings and research outcome
456412.value: [Major findings] Using the context of corporate financial fraud, we examine the effects of media’s use of a shaming news framing on investors’ perceptions of the firms. We applied advanced sentiment analysis that goes beyond the number of counts and positive vs. negative mentions but involves domain-specific knowledge machine-learning and supervised training. We derived a sentiment measure of media shaming based on 1,017 news articles on corporate financial frauds committed by the Chinese listed firms during 2002 and 2012. We then analyzed media shaming toward a specific fraud firm on a daily basis and found that the sample firms experience a significant decrease in the average abnormal return on the next day after the media shaming towards the fraud incident is exposed. In addition, we find that fraud firms that received higher prior media coverage and more positive prior media sentiment suffer more from the negative effects of media shaming. In addition, building on labeling and stigmatization theories, we examine whether and how media coverage influences corporate fraud recidivism. Specifically, we propose that although media plays a governance role by levying reputational penalty on the fraud firm, negative media coverage of the corporate fraud event also exerts labeling effect on the fraud firm by eliciting structural impediments and self-stigmatization, thus resulting in a higher likelihood of recidivism. We further refine that the labeling effect is contingent on the patterns of how media assigns stigmas, including coverage trajectory (change in the average coverage of fraud incidents over time) and coverage dispersion (variation in the coverage of concurrent fraud incidents). Using a sample of corporate financial fraud incidents in China, we find support for most of our hypotheses. In addition, we also studied how the fraud firm can manage the reputational loss during the fraudulent crisis is less well-studied. Drawing insights from crisis communication research, we propose public apology as an accommodative rebuilding strategy used in crisis response to mitigate reputational loss in the context of fraud disclosure. Our empirical tests of 424 corporate financial fraudulence cases from China during 2001-2008 show that a fraud firm’s status is positively related to the likelihood of issuing a public apology, and that such an effect is amplified by the level of regional intermediary development but weakened by market fraud density. [Research outcome] The funded research has produced 9 published or to be published papers, and 5 paper presentations at international and regional conferences.

456412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
456412.value: 1. Our project has clearly demonstrated that reputational governance in the form of public shaming is context-specific and institutionally coherent with the transition economy of China. Therefore, future research may explore more context-specific governance and trace the development of corporate governance system in a more path-dependent way. 2. The project also paves a way to examine corporate governance and fraudulent behaviors in a behavioral and socio-psychological way. For instance, we have adopted labeling and stigmatization theories, as well as theories from sociology and criminology in developing our theoretical frameworks. Future research can integrate inter-disciplinary literatures to study corporate governance and fraudulent behaviors. 3. Our project also shifts the perspective of corporate fraud research from focusing on the fraud firm to the interaction between the fraud firm, media, and public stakeholders. We highlight that public shaming has a more subtle and fundamental function of sanctions that is socio-pedagogical. This may direct future research to enlarge the scope of actors and governance mechanisms in corporate governance research. 4. Future research should continue to capitalize on the advances in textual analytics and the increasing accessibility and availability of textual data to explore further the power of socio-linguistics in management and organization research.

456412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
456412.value: Shaming in the form of ritualized debasement ceremonies, coerced gestures of public contrition, or stigmatizing publicity are on the rise in many countries and in various form of media channel nowadays. Capitalizing on deeply-rooted Chinese shaming culture and the availability of media-provided information in recent years, our study provides a systematic and an advanced textual analysis of the use of public shaming in punishing and deterring corporate fraudulence. Based on 1,017 news articles on corporate financial frauds committed by the Chinese listed firms during 2002 and 2012, we find that the sample firms experience a significant decrease in the average abnormal return on the next day after the media shaming towards the fraud incident is exposed. In addition, we find that fraud firms that received higher prior media coverage and more positive prior media sentiment suffer more from the negative effects of media shaming. In all, our study has the potential to shed important light on the topics of corporate fraud, corporate governance, and media framing. We hope the infusion of different but relevant disciplines helps stimulate more fruitful dialogues that leads us to more enriched understanding of the fraudulence phenomena that are closely attended by managers and stakeholders.

456712.value: 矿产资源、经济发展与地方治理——对中国资源诅咒现象的考察

456712.value: Prof Du, Chuangguo Prof Luo, Yun Prof Zeng, Ming

456712.label: Project Objectives
456712.value: This project will analyze the patterns of resource extraction and utilization of selected natural resources in China at provincial level and below. It will examine how the abundance of natural resources affects local economic development strategy, and employment opportunities in different sectors. This project will analyze the relationship between resource endowment and the quality of local political institutions. Specifically, it will examine how the abundance of natural resources affects the provision of public goods for local residents (such as public education and health care) and the propensity for official corruption. This project will evaluate the impacts of resource endowment on social stability. It will find out if regions with rich natural resources are more prone to social conflicts and popular discontent, and if so, what the causal mechanisms are. In terms of research output, the research team aims to produce a series of research articles for publication in major international referred journals of area studies, political science and/or political economy and presenation at major international/regional conferences.

456712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
456712.value: China’s remarkable economic growth in the past three decades has heavily relied on the consumption of natural resources such as coal, iron, and petroleum. While natural resources play indispensable roles in meeting China’s insatiable need for energy and raw materials to sustain its rapid industrialization and urbanization, the exploration and consumption of these resources have generated serious environmental as well as socio-economic risks. While environmental problems such as pollution and depletion of resources have attracted worldwide attention and extensive studies, the social, political and economic problems have not been adequately assessed or addressed. Indeed, comparative studies of developing countries find that the abundance of natural resources is often associated with underdevelopment, weak political institutions and civil conflicts, a phenomenon generally referred to as the curse of natural resources. Then how does resource endowment affect the quality of political institutions, the mode of local governance and development, and the likelihood of social instability in China? This project aims to assess the risks of resource curse at local levels in China. It is significant both empirically and theoretically. First, it can help us better understand the social, political and economic consequences of resource extraction and utilization in China. The lessons learned from this study can help China cope with the resource-related problems and make sound policies. Second, this research can find more empirical evidence to test the resource curse thesis, an important but highly contested topic in the study of human development and conflict. 中国蕴藏着丰富的包括煤、铁、石油等在内的矿产资源。这些矿产资源对推动中国的工业化和经济的飞速发展起到了巨大的作用。但是，对资源的开采和利用也对中国的环境、经济和社会带来了各种各样的问题。目前，污染和资源枯竭等环境问题已经引起了国内外的广泛关注和研究，但是矿产资源所造成的经济、政治和社会问题，比如群体性事件和政治腐败等现象，却还没有得到足够的重视。 与此同时，国际上对不少资源丰裕国家的比较研究已经发现，丰富的自然资源往往会阻碍一国的经济发展、削弱其政府的管理能力、并引发社会冲突甚至内战，这些悖论被学界广泛称为“资源诅咒”现象。那么，资源诅咒现象在中国是否也存在呢？中国的矿产资源是否会对中国的经济发展和地方治理带来负面影响并威胁到社会稳定呢？ 这一研究意在考察中国地方层级是否存在资源诅咒现象。本研究兼具现实意义和理论价值：一方面，它将有助于我们更好的了解中国矿产资源开发利用所产生的经济、政治和社会后果。这些发现能帮助中国政府与社会认识到问题的存在并制定有效的应对措施。另一方面，本研究通过对中国的实证研究可以检验并进一步发展“资源诅咒”这一国际政治经济比较研究中的重大也是颇具争议的命题，从而对人类发展和冲突解决的学术研究做出不可忽视的贡献。

456812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
456812.value: 通俗詩學讀物是指那些給初學者講授詩歌規則及作法的詩法、詩格之類的書籍，以及一些供初學者誦習模仿的詩歌選本。這些著作雖然不受文化精英的重視，卻流傳極廣，作用巨大。正是這些通俗讀物建構了大眾的詩歌常識，確立了大眾化的詩歌經典，培養了大眾共同的詩歌趣味，形成了共同的文化心理，從而成為整個社會或民族文化認同的一部分。本計劃即是要對明代的通俗詩學讀物加以硏究，主要包括以下諸方面：一、調查蒐集相關文獻，對這些文獻的作者、真僞以及來源加以考察。二、硏究這些通俗讀物的編寫、出版以及傳播的過程，考察文化與商業之間的互動關係。三、硏究其理論內容及價値。四、考察其與詩歌教育之間的關係。五、探討這些讀物的文化意義。硏究明代通俗詩學對於了解明代的整體詩歌文化具有重要意義，對於了解明代民間的詩歌教育、商業出版與學術文化之間的關係甚有助益，亦可為當今處理相應問題提供鏡鑒。 Popular poetics refers to books of poetic rules and forms given to beginners, explaining poetry’s rules and ways, as well as collections given them to imitate through repeated recitation of poetry. These works were not valued by the cultural elites, but were very widely circulated, to enormous effect. These popular readers were what established mass poetic common sense, defined a popularized poetic canon, cultivated common tastes in the masses, and formed a common cultural mentality. They were a part of social and folk cultural identity. This project intends to research Ming dynasty popular poetic readers, primarily including the following goals: (1) Survey and collect relevant material, and investigate the authors of these documents, along with their authenticity and origins. (2) Research processes of composition, publication and transmission of these popular readers, investigating the interaction between cultural and commercial factors. (3) Research their theoretical content and value. (4) Investigate how they were related to education in poetics. (5) Explore the cultural meanings of these readers. Researching Ming dynasty popular poetics makes a significant contribution to understanding the overall system of Ming dynasty poetic culture. It makes very helpful enhancements of our understanding Ming dynasty folk poetic education, and of the relation between commercial publishing and academic culture. It further contributes some perspective on handling analogous contemporary problems.

456812.label: Realisation of objectives
456812.value: 1、本硏究計劃所涉及之文獻，學術界此前幾無人觸及，其數量不明，文獻之作者、時代不清，欲進行此項硏究，最基本的工作乃是文獻之蒐集，版本源流之考辨以及作者與時代之考證。經過數年的蒐集與硏究，本人大體探明這些書籍的範圍、類別以及基本狀況。一、對偶類書籍，以《對類》為代表的一系列讀物。二、詩韻類書籍，在傳統韻書如《廣韻》、《集韻》、《禮部韻略》之外，供作詩押韻時選擇韻藻使用的書籍。元人所編《韻府群玉》、《押韻淵海》，影響至明代，補編、新編不斷，如《均藻》、《五車韻瑞》等，皆其流也。至清御定《佩文韻府》，乃集其大成。三、詩韻與對偶合一之啟蒙讀物，以元人所編《聲律發蒙》為最早，明人增補、改編、重寫，流佈極廣。四、律詩製作類書籍，此類書籍源自金人所編《學吟珍珠囊》、元人所編《詩學大成》，明人改編不絕，在明清兩代流傳極廣，影響極大，有眾多的版本。五、詩法類書籍。有《詩法》、《詩法大成》等書。六、啟蒙詩歌選本。以《千家詩》為核心。以上六方面書籍構成了啟蒙通俗讀物的主體。 2、通俗詩學書籍一般為啟蒙教育用書，需求量大，傳播廣遠。本人以《對類》、《詩學大成》、《韻府群玉》諸書為中心，具體揭示此類書籍編寫、刊刻與傳播的過程。此類書籍不僅在中土流佈，還流傳至朝鮮、日本等國，本人亦蒐集其傳本，考察其在異域之傳播及影響。 3、本人硏究了通俗詩學啟蒙讀物所建構的明人詩學常識。一、《對類》、《詩學大成》皆有類書的框架，建立了整體的知識結構。尤其是《詩學大成》，在類書的知識框架內提供了基本知識（事）；這些知識一方面可供作詩之用（用典），另一方面也奠定了學詩者有關整個世界的常識基礎。二、在詩學範圍內，這些啟蒙讀物提供了詩學常識，首先是對偶、押韻，還包括題材、體裁以及基本的技術知識等。三、律詩的知識與技術乃是核心。 4、本人探討了詩歌啟蒙教育的方式與步驟。啟蒙詩學通俗讀物與啟蒙教育密切相關。啟蒙教育中的偶對訓練促成了大型對偶工具書（亦是課本）的《對類》一書的編纂。聲律的訓練直接導致了《聲律發蒙》等一系列聲律啟蒙讀物的產生。啟蒙詩學訓練以律詩為中心，乃是《詩學大成》等書編集與流行的直接原因。 5、啟蒙詩學讀物雖在啟蒙教育中地位重要，但因其啟蒙性與技術性，在精英文化中則未受重視，鮮有認真的學術硏究。本人認為應該重估其價値：一、在詩學範圍內言，重學詩工夫是宋以後詩學之突出特徵，啟蒙詩學訓練的是最基礎的詩歌工夫，而啟蒙詩學書籍則是基礎訓練的教材，這些教材既具有工具性，但也是工夫論詩學觀念的體現，其詩學意義應該受到重視；精英詩人大多也是經歷了啟蒙詩學教育與訓練，了解精英詩人之啟蒙詩學教育對於理解其詩歌創作具有獨特意義。二、在文學教育範圍內，了解傳統的詩歌啟蒙教育觀念與方式可為今日之基礎語文教育提供借鏡。

456812.label: Major findings and research outcome
456812.value: 1、在文獻方面，確立了相關的文獻範圍，梳理並考辨了基本的文獻。《對類》、《詩學大成》、《韻府群玉》等書，原本歸入類書類，學界未有視其為詩學文獻。本人探討並還原其詩學功能及價値，將其歸入詩學文獻範疇，改編了傳統詩學文獻的觀念與範圍。 2、硏究代表性書籍的編纂體例及其淵源，究明其編集旨趣，揭示其詩學功能，呈現其在技術及觀念方面的意義。 3、論述其在傳統詩學體系中的理論內涵與價値。

457012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457012.value: Anderson et al. (2003) show that selling, general and administrative (SGA) costs increase more rapidly when sales increases than decrease when sales decreases (also see Noreen and Soderstrom, 1994, 1997). This asymmetric response of costs to changes in activity level is referred to in the literature as sticky costs. We extend these studies by examining the stickiness of labor related cost; and provide insights into how the make-up of firm’s employees and agency costs are associated with cost stickiness. We consider the make-up of firm’s employees in terms of employees with tacit versus codified knowledge. Tacit knowledge employees are likely to create an intangible asset, which in turn will lead to firms spending on such employees as if the resource has high adjustment costs (see Hall, Griliches and Hausman, 1986; Lach and Schankerman, 1988). Thus, we hypothesize that the labor cost will be stickier for firms with more tacit-knowledge employees. We measure tacit and codified knowledge employees using two measures: proportion of executives to total employee and the proportion of employees with above college education to total employees. We also examine the difference in labor cost stickiness across family and non-family firms as well as political connectedness of firms as measures of agency costs. We hypothesize that labor cost will be less sticky for family firms than non-family firms because family firms are likely to monitor managers’ resource decisions more effectively than non-family firms. We also hypothesize that labor cost will be more sticky for politically connected firms than non-politically connected firms, because politically connected firms are likely to be under political and social pressure not to adjust labor resource downwards (see Fan et al., 2007). Anderson等（2003）发现公司费用对销售增加的反应速度高过对销售降低的反应速度。 成本这种对公司活动反应的不对称性在文献中叫做成本粘性。 在次基础上，我们研究公司的人力资源构成及代理成本是否与成本粘性相关。 我们提出了下面三个研究假设： 1） 如果公司的员工知识层次越高，公司的成本粘性越高; 2)家族企业的人力成本粘性较低； 3） 有政治联系公司的成本粘性较高。

457212.value: 應用多源遙感技術估算亞熱帶濕潤地區不透水層

457212.label: Project Objectives

457212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457212.value: The aim of this research project is to investigate the combined use of optical remote-sensing data and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data for the assessment of impervious surfaces (IS) in humid subtropical regions, including seasonal variation, and to evaluate the potential impact of IS on water quality, especially on non-point source water pollution. With the rapid urbanization of Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta (PRD), the spread of impervious surfaces (IS) has increased dramatically over the last two decades. It has been widely recognized that IS serves as a key environmental indicator since it affects the water cycle, water pollutants and the energy balance and, thus, relates closely to the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. It has also been reported that IS serves an important role in urban socio-economic studies such as detailed population distribution. Given its importance many methods have been developed to assess impervious surfaces using satellite images, but most of the methods were tested in temperate, continental areas. Few considered the case in humid subtropical areas such as PRD, where there is significant cloud occurrence and different phenology. Due to these differences, difficulties occur when using optical remote-sensing data which is the main data source used in previous studies. Seasonal changes in vegetation, recognized as a key factor in IS estimation, create further challenges. Existing approaches need to be evaluated while additional data sources should be considered in order to establish an advanced assessment of IS in humid areas such as Hong Kong and PRD. The outcome of this proposed research will provide evidence of the seasonal effects on IS assessment due to phenological change, evaluate the potential of SAR data for improving IS assessment and design a synergistic method to identify IS using optical and SAR images. In addition, the environmental impact of impervious surfaces on water pollution will be assessed. Since the PRD region is highly typical of many fast growing areas, the implementation of this project would serve as a model for other humid subtropical regions of the world.

457212.label: Realisation of objectives
457212.value: Over the four objectives of the project, 90% of the research has been completed. Details of the realisation of the four objectives in this project are as follows: 1) The seasonal effects of impervious surface estimation using optical satellite data have been understood. The study demonstrates quite a special pattern of ISE in humid subtropical areas that is different from that in mid-latitude areas. According to the results, winter is the best season to estimate IS from satellite images. Autumn images obtained the lowest accuracy of IS due to the clouds coverage and the water in Variable Source Areas (VSA). Autumn is a rainy season in a subtropical monsoon region, for which clouds occur very often and VSA areas are always filled with water. 2) The potential of radar images for improving impervious surface estimation was investigated and evaluated. A comparison study of ISE between optical and SAR image demonstrates that single optical image provides better results than using single SAR image. Considering both the merits and demerits of optical and SAR images, synergistically fusing the two data sources should be a promising solution. Comparison of three different levels of fusion shows that pixel level fusion seems not appropriate for optical-SAR fusion, as it reduces the accuracy compared to the single use of optical data. 3) A methodological framework was proposed to synergize the optical and SAR images. Three different data sets are used to assess the effectiveness of this methodological framework. Different methods are employed and compared to fusion the two data sources at a mixed level fusion of pixel and feature levels. Moreover, Random Forest demonstrated a promising performance for fusing optical and SAR images as it treats the two data sources differently through a random selection procedure of variables from different data sources. 4) For the explanation of environmental impact of impervious surfaces on water quality in PRD region, we have developed methodology for water quality assessment, but only tested it on other regions. About 40% of the research objective of environmental impacts of IS has not been finished yet, which was due to the limited availability of water quality data. To overcome the problem, the research team have contacted local government department of Hong Kong to get the water quality data under collaboration schema. Then, we could test and validate the proposed methodology in PRD by local water quality data.

457212.label: Major findings and research outcome
457212.value: This project attempts to fuse optical and SAR remote sensing data to improve the accuracy of urban impervious surface estimation (ISE) in humid subtropical regions (HSR). The seasonal characteristics of land covers and its impacts on ISE in HSR are all investigated. Major findings and outcomes are summarized as follows. 1) The study demonstrates quite a special pattern of ISE in humid subtropical areas that is different from that in mid-latitude areas. According to the results, in subtropical monsoon regions, winter is the best season to estimate IS from satellite images. There are little clouds, and most of the Variable Source Areas (VSA) is not filled with water. On the other hand, autumn images obtained the lowest accuracy of IS due to the clouds coverage and the water in VSA. Autumn is a rainy season in a subtropical monsoon region, for which clouds occur very often and VSA areas are always filled with water. Consequently, clouds are confused with bright IS due to their similarly high reflectance, and more water in VSA is confused with dark IS due to their similarly low reflectance. 2) A comparison study of ISE between optical and SAR image demonstrates that single optical image provides better results than using single SAR image. Considering both the merits and demerits of optical and SAR images, synergistically fusing the two data sources should be a promising solution. Comparison of three different levels of fusion shows that pixel level fusion seems not appropriate for optical-SAR fusion, as it reduces the accuracy compared to the single use of optical data. Meanwhile, feature level fusion and decision level fusion obtained better accuracy, since they improves the identification of IS from shaded areas and bare soils. 3) A methodological framework of fusing the optical and SAR images is proposed. Three different data sets are used to assess the effectiveness of this methodological framework. In addition, different methods are employed and compared to fusion the two data sources at a mixed level fusion of pixel and feature levels. Experimental results showed that the combined use of optical and SAR image is able to effectively improve the accuracy of ISE by reducing the spectral confusions that happen easily in optical images. Moreover, Random Forest demonstrated a promising performance for fusing optical and SAR images as it treats the two data sources differently through a random selection procedure of variables from different data sources.

457212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
457212.value: This project aimed to investigate the seasonal effects of ISE, the potential of SAR for improving ISE and the environmental impacts of IS in HSR areas. About 90% of the research objectives have been accomplished during the past two-year research. However, there are some significant issues needed to be addressed in the future research. Firstly, about 40% of the research objective of environmental impacts of IS has not been finished yet, which was due to the limited availability of water quality data. We have developed methodology for water quality assessment, but only tested it on other regions. So, one way of further development is to test and validate the proposed methodology in PRD by local water quality data. Secondly, the SAR used in this project was single polarization data, which carry only limited backscattering information. Great potential for further development goes to multiple polarimetric SAR data with fully polarimetric information, which could promisingly improve the accuracy of ISE compared to single polarimetric SAR data. Last but not the least, application of IS in other research, e.g. urban flood risk assessment and urban heat island, could be important potential further research issues.

457212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
457212.value: Dramatic urbanization processes have happened in many regions and thus created a number of metropolises in the world. As a result, a large increment of impervious surface (IS) turned out to be one of the features of fast urbanization process and has been influencing the urban environment significantly. Therefore, the estimation of IS would be very helpful to monitor and manage the urbanization process and its impacts on the environment. This project attempts to fuse optical and SAR remote sensing data to improve the accuracy of urban impervious surface estimation (ISE) in humid subtropical regions (HSR). Special seasonal patterns of ISE were found in HSR areas. SAR data were found to hold great potential for improving ISE in HSR areas. The major outcome of this research provides evidence of the seasonal effects on IS assessment due to phenological and climatic characteristics, as well as provides an applicable framework of methodology for the synergistic use of optical and SAR images to improve the ISE. Since the PRD region is highly typical of many fast growing areas, the methodology and conclusions of this research would serve as a useful reference for other subtropical, humid regions of the world.
