457612.label: Project Title(Chinese)
457612.value: 国家之间的政治经济历史关系，和跨国并购

457612.label: Project Objectives
457612.value: We will introduce the construct of “historical ties” into international acquisitions research. The international business literature has focused on the institutional distance between home and host countries as the key variable that explains firms’ international acquisition decisions. This project will focus on historical ties between countries as additional factors that affect the international acquisition decisions of firms. Historical ties represent a unique institutional framework that guides the international acquisition decisions of firms. Historical ties are a multi-dimensional, dynamic, and asymmetric construct. The strength of historical ties can also vary in degree. Historical ties have several dimensions, including political, economic, and diplomatic ties and informal ties. They are often asymmetric in character, with an imbalance of power between pairs of countries. The various types of historical ties create an institutional framework within which international acquisitions take place. We will attempt to “bring history back into international business” (Jones & Khanna, 2006) by taking account of how historical ties influence the flow of international acquisitions across countries. Understanding historical ties is of particular importance for the study of international business in the current competitive landscape in which developing country firms are entering and competing in distant developed countries. Many of these developing countries have complex histories of being dominated by developed countries, such as through colonization, invasion, occupation, or alliance. The project will complement “distance” research by developing a theory of how historical ties between home and host countries affect firms’ international acquisitions. Many researchers have adopted the distance perspective in international acquisitions research. Distance can relate to cultural, administrative, geographic, or economic distance between the home and host countries. The project will stress that historical ties between countries go beyond distance attributes, and will examine how such ties influence international acquisition decisions.

457612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457612.value: Firms are increasingly adopting international acquisitions – the most expensive mode of market entry – in an effort to enter and make profits in foreign markets quickly. However, firms are usually unfamiliar with foreign markets, which are often geographically distant from their home countries or have different cultures and institutional environments. Institutional distance scholars have suggested that firms are likely to encounter the liability of foreignness and legitimacy challenges in foreign environments. This presents great difficulties for firms and entails high operating costs that probably outweigh the benefits of operating in foreign markets. It is thus a puzzle both in practice and in research that firms are increasingly acquiring targets in foreign markets despite the great challenges that this presents. Our proposed project suggests that the “historical ties” between pairs of countries go some way toward explaining the strong commitment of certain firms to engage in international acquisitions in distant markets. Historical ties can help to overcome the liability of foreignness and speed up firms’ entry into foreign countries. Historical ties are defined as relations that are officially developed (economic, political, and diplomatic ties) or that evolve historically among people (informal ties) between pairs of countries. Therefore, this project contributes to solve the puzzle, suggesting that historical ties can help to explain firms’ international acquisitions in distant markets. 愈來愈多企業採用「跨国併購」——一種最昂貴但又可以快速進入國外市場並且獲得利潤的海外投资模式。主流的国家体制差异研究指出，国家体制差异令到企業對於在國外市場投資望而卻步，更莫論需要巨大资金成本的跨国併購。研究學者認為，企業在進入國外市場時亦可能要面對陌生的体制環境所带来的不同方面的挑戰比如企业是否被当地的政府，企业，和顾客所接纳和认同。「国家之间的差异」包括体制上的差异， 以及地域上的距離，文化和經濟之间的差异。「体制差异」可以解釋企業在進入國外市場時會遇到的困難。但卻未能解釋为什么企業在面对这些国家差异性带来的困难时，仍坚持海外併購。在这个项目中，我們提出——國家與國家之間的「关系」，就足以補充說明企業在國外市場「非理性」併購。「国家关系」指的是兩個國家政府之間正式確立的關係(即正式關係)，或是兩國人民之間在歷史进程中发展的關係(即非正式關係)。這項研究表明了国家之间關係有助於解釋企業的跨国併購行為。我們亦認為，兩國之間的關係是不對稱因为两个国家在全球经济一体化中拥有的政治经济權力是不平衡。而不對稱的国家之间的關係能更好地解釋跨国併購的目标选择。

457612.label: Realisation of objectives
457612.value: Research topics and issues In study 1 as we proposed in the last mid-term report, we have continued to examine the roles of institutional distance, language differences and diplomatic relationships between home and host countries in international acquisitions (Zhu, Xia & Makino, 2015). Specifically as we discussed earlier, we focus on IT manufacturing and service sectors. Focusing on one industry could help to avoid the noises of different industrial characteristics. We investigate how these dyadic institutional relationships could facilitate or hamper post-acquisition– integration in IT manufacturing vs. autonomy in IT service sectors. In study 2, we aim to understand how property rights protection institutional ties play a role in IT firms’ international acquisition because property rights protection is one of the most critical institutional environments for IT firms to make profits. Prior research suggests that high-tech firms tend to encounter market transaction uncertainties in countries with weak property rights protection (PRP) and that transaction costs will increase significantly with such uncertainties. Basing our study on high-tech firms that have recently been increasingly acquiring targets in these countries, we explain this puzzling phenomenon. In particular, we investigate whether and how high-tech firms can gain value from acquiring targets in host countries with different degrees of PRP. In addition to transaction costs, we take into account market demands for advanced technologies in weak PRP host countries and fierce market competition in strong ones. Overall, we suggest that high-tech firms are likely to increase their performance by acquiring targets in weak PRP host countries where profit-generating opportunities tend to be more frequent than in strong PRP ones (Zhu & Qian, 2015). In study 3, we have continued to examine how historical colonial ties affect the power struggling between acquiring and acquired firms in post-acquisition integration processes and thus post-acquisition performance (Zhi & Zhu, 2016). Recognizing the power imbalance’s role in cross-border M&As, we further examined how a cultural tie - power distance value affects post-acquisition performance (Huang, Zhu, & Brass, 2016). Data Analyses and Results In study 1, we examined 847 related cross-border acquisitions in the information technology industry in 27 home countries and 38 host countries. Results provide strong support for the theory. Specifically, we found that acquiring firms in service information technology industries where post-acquisition autonomy is more important in value creation outperform those in manufacturing industries where post-acquisition integration plays a more important role in value creation. Results also show institutional distance and language differences strengthen this relationship; in contrast, diplomatic relationships weaken the relationship. In study 2, we tested our theory in a sample of U.S. information technology (IT) firms’ international acquisitions between 1995 and 2004. We found that firms differ in their capabilities in gaining value in various levels of PRP host countries. Firms tend to gain more profits in host countries with weak property rights protection but with great market opportunities than in host countries with strong protection but limited market opportunities. Further, when acquirer size increases, acquirers become less able to gain value through acquisitions in host countries with weak PRP; yet when acquirer host country acquisition experience increases, they are more able to gain value through acquisitions in host countries with weak PRP. In study 3, we examined 2,115 cross-border acquisitions in the global information technology industry. We found that the cultural tie - power distance value (PDV) differences - undermine the long-term post-acquisitionperformance of acquirers. This cultural tie is also found to have asymmetric effect on post-acquisition performance. This effect is stronger when acquirers are higher than targets in PDV than when the opposite is the case. This asymmetric effect of PDV difference depends on national status difference, business relatedness, and acquisition experience. Paper Submissions We submitted Study 1 to International Business Review (IBR), study 2 to Journal of World Business (JWB) and study 3 to Strategic Management Journal (SMJ). We will attempt to “bring history back into international business” (Jones & Khanna, 2006) by taking account of how historical ties influence the flow of international acquisitions across countries. Understanding historical ties is of particular importance for the study of international business in the current competitive landscape in which developing country firms are entering and competing in distant developed countries. Many of these developing countries have complex histories of being dominated by developed countries, such as through colonization, invasion, occupation, or alliance.

The project will complement “distance” research by developing a theory of how historical ties between home and host countries affect firms’ international acquisitions. Many researchers have adopted the distance perspective in international acquisitions research. Distance can relate to cultural, administrative, geographic, or economic distance between the home and host countries. The project will stress that historical ties between countries go beyond distance attributes, and will examine how such ties influence international acquisition decisions.

457612.label: Major findings and research outcome
457612.value: In the past two reporting periods, we provided deep understandings of language ties, diplomatic relations, and institutional ties and their roles in international acquisitions through two major studies (Zhu& Qian, 2015; Zhu, Xia & Makino, 2015). In the following reporting period, we focused on historical colonial ties and examined how the colonial ties created an institutional relation framework within which international acquisitions take place (Huang & Zhu, 2016). As we identified the power imbalance plays a great role in cross-border M&As, we further examined how a cultural tie - power distance value between home and host country affects post-acquisition value creation (Huang, Zhu & Brass, 2016). Regarding the colonial ties, the former colonial ties created a power imbalance between colonial and colonized countries, and yet such power imbalance has been challenged by international acquisitions of colonial firms by firms from previously colonized countries. Specifically more and more firms in previously colonized countries such as India actively acquire firms in their former colonial countries such as UK. At the same time, colonial country firms have also continued to acquiring firms in previously colonized countries. First, we found that overall historical colonial ties are likely to facilitate the information exchange between two countries and decrease the cross-border risks taken by acquiring firms. Second, we found the presence of asymmetric effects the colonial ties on the effectiveness of international acquisitions. Specifically we found that the historical power-imbalance between colonial and colonized country firms affected the performance of international acquisitions between these countries. Namely, top managers and employees tended to react to acquiring or being acquired by firms of former colonized or colonial countries. Such power imbalance leads to power struggling in post-acquisition integration processes and thus post-acquisition performance. As to the cultural tie - power distance value (PDV) between home and host countries, we found that when the tie is weak (PDV differences are larger), the long-term post-acquisition performance reduces. We also examined the asymmetric effects of such cultural tie. We found that this effect is stronger when acquirers are higher than targets in PDV than when the opposite is the case. Further, this asymmetric effect of cultural tie (PDV difference) depends on national status difference, business relatedness, and acquisition experience.

457612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
457612.value: We plan to continue working on the conceptual arguments on the impact of "historical ties" on international business practices, particularly the practices of cross-border M&A.

457612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
457612.value: The number of Cross-border M&As has been increasing significantly in recent years. However, our understandings of cross-border M&As are very limited. Based on prior research, we achieve the consensus that cultural differences are likely to cause conflicts between acquirers and acquired foreign targets in post-acquisition integration processes and thereby lead to post-acquisition value destruction. However, cultural distance exists and is not unavoidable in this global world. What’s more important for researchers and business people in the global business world is how we could deal with cultural differences effectively and benefit from cultural differences. Our project addresses this important research question and has far-reaching implications for managers. We proposed that national ties could help to resolve this issue through facilitating the interactions and understandings of different cultures. These national-level ties promote the convergence of people’s mindsets and promote the appreciations of differences. As a result, acquirers could achieve better post-acquisition performance by acquiring targets in foreign countries with national-level ties. This project also has policy implications. The government could help to facilitate the national ties at top levels, which could have positive economic spillover effects on organizations and individuals of tied countries.

457812.label: Project Title(Chinese)
457812.value: CEO偏好，专业背景，和公司风险管理

457812.label: Project Objectives
457812.value: Our study intends to, among other things, enrich our understanding of corporate risk management. While management theory predicts that top managers have profound impacts on firms’ decision choices, the extant literature on hedging assumes that managers are homogeneous across firms. We investigate whether individual CEOs affect risk management decisions, incremental to common economic determinants of such decisions. Taking a new perspective, our study sheds some light on the “under-hedged” behavior observed in some firms. Objective 1 aims to establish individual CEO effects. However, the individual CEO effects can be abstract and are insufficient in mapping to the CEO characteristics that explain a firm’s hedging decision. Therefore, we also examine which particular demographic characteristics of the CEOs are associated with the individual CEO effects. As such, we aim to add to the upper echelons theory (Hambrick and Mason 1984; Hambrick 2007). Our third objective is to provide insights into the implications of managers’ “imprinting their styles” on corporate hedging. Kumar and Robinovitch (2010) find that firms with entrenched CEOs have higher hedging intensity, suggesting that hedging does not necessarily add value to shareholders. . Examining CEO effects and characteristics helps to assess how CEOs, through hedging, affects shareholders’ welfare.

458212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
458212.value: This proposal explores the potential interactions between credit default swap (CDS) market and equity option market. CDS and options are derivatives on the same underlying asset, and can serve similar purposes. However, little is known about the interactions of their trading activities. To investigate the impact of CDS trading on option pricing, I link the option relative mispricing measure (delta-hedged option return) and option volume to the introduction of CDS and CDS trades. The preliminary analysis suggests that the introduction of CDS increases the demand for related options, and further affects the option price. This effect is asymmetric for call and put: put is already expensive (overvalued relative to the underlying stock) before the introduction of CDS, while call becomes as expensive as put after the introduction of CDS. For both call and put, option trading volume increases with CDS trades in the cross-section. This project will provide new evidence on how non-pricing factors affect security prices in option market. This study will also contribute to a growing literature that examines the cross-market interactions of trading and pricing. It enhances the understanding of asset pricing and market efficiency. 本研究计划旨在探讨信用违约互换（CDS）市场与股票期权市场的可能存在的相互作用。尽管(CDS)与期权都是基于同一种标的资产并有着类似目的的金融衍生品，人们对于二者交易活动的相互影响却了解甚少。 研究将期权的相对错误定价（非零的对冲值期权回报率） 与CDS及其交易的引入相联系，以研究CDS对于期权定价的影响。初步研究显示CDS的引入增加了对其相关期权的需求，从而进一步影响期权的价格。而CDS的引入对于看涨期权(Call)与看跌期权(Put)的影响并不是匀称的。在CDS引入之前，相对于看涨期权，看跌期权的价格相对于标的股票价格已经是高估的。而在CDS引入之后，看涨期权的价格上升，并达到与看跌期权相同的高估水平。在横截面水平上，看涨期权与看跌期权的交易量都随信用违约互换交易的引入而增长。 本研究能够提高人们对于资产定价与市场效率的理解。一方面研究为非定价因素如何影响期权市场上的证券价格提供了新的证据，另一方面也丰富了致力于研究不同市场之间交易与定价的相互作用的文献。

458212.label: Realisation of objectives
458212.value: 1. We find that the inception of credit default swaps (CDS) makes the equity options on the same underlying firm more expensive. This finding is statistically significant and economically meaningful. If the CDS and equity option markets are segmented, there should be no effect from the trading of CDS on option prices. We have also shown that our findings are not driven by firm fundamentals. The delta-hedged option returns, which are option prices adjusted by firm fundamentals, are lower after CDS trading. This result is robust to various controls for firm characteristics, market conditions, and sample selection bias. We Further explore several channels and mechanisms through which CDS impact option prices. a). For both call and put options, “limited inter-mediation capacity story” gives a coherent explanation for the higher option premium. We find consistent evidence that in quarters where the broker-dealer’s leverage is greater (smaller), options are more expensive (cheaper). b). In line with the hypothesis of improved “information quality” brought by CDS, we find that option bid-ask spreads are lower after CDS trading, while both option trading volume and open interest increase after CDS trading. c). We also find that the relationship is stronger for call options than put options, which also agrees with the “substitution story” between CDS and put options. The potential substitution between CDS and put tends to pull down the price of put, while not affecting the price of call. 2. Our study shows that the capacity of financial intermediaries has strong impact on securities pricing. In our case, the introduction of a new derivative security, CDS, makes the other, existing derivative (option) more expensive. This finding adds to the growing literature on the various effects of CDS trading on stocks and bonds. 3. In our empirical analysis, we confirmed findings in previous studies that delta-hedged option return is related to a bunch of stock and option variables. We add to the literature the impact of CDS trading on option price. Moreover, we show the cross-section of equity option returns can be predicted by a variety of underlying stock characteristics and firm fundamentals, including idiosyncratic volatility, past stock returns, profitability, cash holding, new share issuance, and dispersion of analyst forecasts. Such predictability is not mechanically inherited from the stock market because these variables do not significantly predict stock returns in our sample.

458212.label: Major findings and research outcome
458212.value: Cao, Jin, Pearson, and Tang (2015) (CJPT (2015)) find that the inception of credit default swaps (CDS) makes the equity options on the same underlying firm more expensive. This finding is statistically significant and economically meaningful. If the CDS and equity option markets are segmented, there should be no effect from the trading of CDS on option prices. We have also shown that our findings are not driven by firm fundamentals. The delta-hedged option returns, which are option prices adjusted by firm fundamentals, are lower after CDS trading. This result is robust to various controls for firm characteristics, market conditions, and sample selection bias. CJPT (2015) further explore several channels and mechanisms through which CDS impact option prices. 1) For both call and put options, the “limited intermediation capacity story” gives a coherent explanation for the higher option premium. We find consistent evidence that in quarters where the broker-dealer’s leverage is greater (smaller), options are more expensive (cheaper). 2) In line with the hypothesis of improved “information quality” brought by CDS, we find that option bid-ask spreads are lower after CDS trading, while both option trading volume and open interest increase after CDS trading. 3) Consistent with the “substitution story” between CDS and put options, we also find that the relationship is stronger for call options than put options. The potential substitution between CDS and put tends to pull down the price of put, while not affecting the price of call. Cao, Han, Tong, and Zhan (2015) (CHTZ (2015)) examine whether the cross-section of equity option returns can be predicted with a collection of well-known stock return predictors. The answer is yes for the majority of these variables, including idiosyncratic volatility, size, past stock returns, profitability, cash holding, new issuance, and the dispersion of analyst forecasts. Such predictability is not mechanically inherited from the stock market because stock return predictability is weak to non-existent for the underlying stocks in our sample and our results hold for delta-hedged option returns. The systematic patterns in the relative valuation of options and the underlying stocks we document have important implications for option valuation and option market efficiency. 458212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
458212.value: There are numerous derivatives, often on the same underlying firms, in the financial markets. However, little is known about the interactions between different types of derivatives. In this study, we show that the inception of credit derivatives, represented by credit default swaps (CDS), makes the equity options on the same underlying firm more expensive. The expensiveness of option due to CDS trading is not completely driven by the increased riskiness of the firm because the delta-hedged equity option returns, which account for underlying stock price movement, are lower. The effect of CDS trading is more pronounced for call options than put options. The evidence is consistent with the view that CDS trading crowds out option trading, option dealers charge higher option premiums due to limited inter-mediation capacity. Our study adds to the growing literature on the various effects of CDS trading on stocks and bonds. Hence, combining all evidence presents a complete picture of CDS influence in financial markets.

458612.label: Realisation of objectives
458612.value: For Objective 1: To disentangle the diverse patterns and systems of welfare provision in grassroots communities in urbanizing rural China. Using Dwyer’s (2000) welfare framework, three aspects of each provision system will be examined: the content and amount of provision, the conditions of entitlement, and membership definition with particular attention to social exclusion. With the help of her research assistant and student helpers, the PI completed a thorough literature review on community-based welfare provision in the contemporary world and urbanization in post-socialist China. The dissertation data of the PI, on the two research sites in Hebei Province, were re-analyzed from the perspectives of the new project. One-month fieldwork for re-interviews and observation in the two townships in Hebei was carried out in July 2014, with the help of colleagues in the Mainland. The PI carried out 10-week ethnographic fieldwork in the two research sites in Zhejiang Province in June 2013, June 2014, and June 2015. Trained local student helpers continued the fieldwork for data collection when the PI left. The PI also carried out three-week ethnographic fieldwork in Guangdong Province, with migrant villagers from the research sites, in July 2013 and May 2015. In total, we completed 29 interviews in L Township in Zhejiang, 33 interviews in H Township in Zhejiang, and re-interviewed 11 villagers in Hebei Province. We also collected over 300 pages of local policy archives, gazetteers, news reports, and meeting minutes. The research team has transcribed, documented, and analyzed the collected data. Regular meetings were held to discuss and understand the mechanisms and processes embedded in the data. With the assistance of her RA and student helpers, the PI compiled complete coding documents and analytic reports. Using the extensive and comparative qualitative data, the PI was able to disentangle the diverse patterns of welfare provision in the four purposefully selected grassroots communities in urbanizing China. The content of the provision in their community welfare systems varies from state-required programs, projects based on the rule of law, locally initiated social service, to cash income. The amount varies from very little to plenty. Conditions of entitlement include compliance with the state, active civil participation, compliance with local rural moralities, and identification with community. Membership definition also has a wide range of variances, from the exclusive definition of locality to universal human rights. The sharp differences in the different dimensions of community welfare are intriguing and lead us to the second objective of the research to explain the distinctive patterns. For Objective 2: To investigate why and how distinctive patterns of welfare provision are established in different communities. Agencies of village cadres in the construction of a “third realm” between the state and the society will be the focus of the inquiries. How the cadres maintain their leadership and coordinate negotiations in the “third realm”, and how those efforts shape grassroots patterns of welfare provision will be probed. Using the ethnographic data from observation, interviews, and archives, the PI investigated why and how the different patterns of community welfare are established in the four purposefully selected townships. The four sites experienced different paths and processes of urbanization, which changed their farm land ownership and collective negotiation power. The role and power of village cadres were transformed in those processes in varied local contexts. They now adopt different goals and strategies of leadership in their interaction with villagers in the “third realm” between state and society. They can be loyal state agents, movement leaders, traditional moral authority, or efficient market leaders in different localities going through different models of urbanization. It is in their varied interaction with the common villagers that the grassroots welfare systems are negotiated and built. For Objective 3: To scrutinize how the different systems of grassroots community provision impact the changing roles of the rural governments, the discourses of citizenship among villagers, and the emerging civil society in post-socialist China. After the PI analyzed the different patterns of community welfare systems in the four townships and their processes of construction, it was clear that the different grassroots welfare provision evinces changing roles of the rural governments, embodied in the village cadres, under varied processes of urbanization. Rural governments can still be the lowest loyal branch of the state system in some contexts, but they can also be organizers of resistance, keepers of local moralities, or stimulators of market economy in other contexts. The rural community-based welfare systems also embed changing ideas of citizenship and civil society in the Chinese countryside. In different contexts of urbanization and social change, citizenship and civil rights can mean very different things: obedience to the Party state, universal human rights and social entitlement, obedience to community moralities, or competitiveness in the market economy. All these ideas will help us understand the emerging civil society in China, which might not be defined in one single and unified discourse. For Objective 4: To generate implications for social service professionals and policy-makers to design and implement community welfare programs and to carry out evidence-based practices in service delivery in the changing contexts of rural China. The research team reviewed existing literature on comparative service programs and welfare policies in grassroots communities in different social and cultural contexts. This topic was included in our data analysis and discussion meetings, and was often brought up during presentations at international conferences. Our research implies that intervention in grassroots community welfare provision in contemporary rural China needs to pay attention to local history of urbanization and political organization, particularly the agency of village cadres. Rural communities can be emphasized as resourceful organizations and institutions in welfare provision in social change, but careful discussion of rights, equality, and justice needs to be included in the planning.

458612.label: Major findings and research outcome
458612.value: Under the forces of urbanization and welfare decentralization, varied models of community-based welfare provision systems have emerged in the urbanizing Chinese countryside. The research compares the different local models and examines the mechanisms for the grassroots diversity to occur. It uses the changing agency of village cadres and their interaction with villagers in the “third realm” between state and society to explain the different local welfare models. Villages in W Township in Hebei Province adopt a “small-town” model of urbanization. Factories were introduced to the area but the villagers still keep their farm land, and there is no consolidated collective power in political institutions. Village cadres remain loyal to the state system and make efforts to implement national welfare policies through their personal networks with villagers. The scope, content, conditionality, and boundary of the village welfare systems in the township usually follow the state’s definitions. Villages in T Township in the same Hebei Province suffered from the “flagship” model of urbanization. Villagers were deprived of farm land, due to lack of collectivity in negotiation power. Disappointed village cadres became active community leaders, who organize the villagers, build community capacity, and use the re-occurring solidarity and collective action to negotiate with rural governments over land compensation and social benefits. Villages in H Township in Zhejiang Province, keeping their farm lands intact and enjoying a long history of collectivity in communities, have experienced steady communal development during urbanization. Cadres in the villages, usually older males with traditional authorities, report responsibly to their village communities. They mobilize traditional rural moralities to bond and educate villagers and build service-oriented village welfare systems. Villages in L Township in the same Zhejiang Province lost their farm land for a new business district. Due to the collective power of negotiation of the villagers, villagers received benevolent compensation and now live in “villages-within-cities”. The village cadres, often younger and male, are regarded as the “capable” members of the communities, who have family financial resources and cherish the spirits of efficiency. They aim to safeguard their village communities through building efficient cash-based local welfare systems. The different rural grassroots welfare systems emerge in different local contexts of urbanization and welfare decentralization, in the interaction of village cadres and villagers, and between state and society. They construct varied discourses of welfare entitlement, rights, citizenship, and social justice, and exert multi-level impacts on the social and political changes in post-socialist China.

458612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
458612.value: Research on community-based welfare provision in different social and cultural contexts will be continued in future. Welfare decentralization and community provision have become increasingly popular policy directions all over the world, together with the revival of communitarian thoughts. However, it remains understudied how community-based welfare provision is constructed in local contexts, how power and inequality are embedded, and how the programs can better serve justice. Future research, with more comparative cases along these analytical lines, can shed light on a better understanding of community organizing and welfare reforms. The current research shows that one major concern in urbanizing rural communities in China is the lack of adequate care for children, older persons, and other needy family members. Future research projects will be developed to address how family, community, institution, and state may coordinate efforts and mobilize resources to provide care in post-socialist China, in a challenging era of population ageing and social changes. Future research will continue to generate implications for social intervention, service practice, and policy making in the areas of community welfare, grassroots service planning, family care, and social organization of care, in the contexts of rapid urbanization and welfare decentralization in China.

458612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
458612.value: This project, based on extensive ethnographic and comparative data, examines four grassroots rural communities in China that are experiencing distinct processes of urbanization and welfare decentralization, inquires how and why different patterns of community welfare provision are constructed and practiced in the local contexts of leadership and negotiation, and probes how the organization of welfare in grassroots communities impacts the changing roles of the state, the discourses of citizenship, and the emerging civil society in contemporary China. It employs the theoretical framework of the “third realm” between state and society to explain the building of community welfare systems in the social interactions of village cadres and villagers. The findings contribute to the scholarship of state-society dynamics in contemporary China, the changing micro-foundation of grassroots governance, the multi-dimensional meaning of community life, and the emerging concept of citizenship in urbanizing China. The study initiates dialogues with international literature on urbanization, decentralization of public welfare, and community-based welfare programs. It reflects on the global trend of emphasizing community in social planning in times of social change, and generates implications for justice-based and context-sensitive policy intervention and service planning in providing and delivering community-based welfare.

459212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459212.value: Household surveys are vital for government statistics and academic research. In recent years, however, high levels of understatement in benefit recipiency have been noted across many household surveys. This understatement has major implications for our understanding of the economic circumstances of the population and the effects of government programs. Few studies to date have provided the trends and reasons for such understatement and even fewer studies have provided solutions to deal with the problem. Our project will first document the trend in such understatement across six popular US household surveys used widely by both the academic and policy communities since 1960. Second, we will investigate how such level of understatement varies across different demographic, social and geographic groups, as well as the designs of the surveys. Third, we will provide solutions for how to deal with such understatement in academic studies. Finally, our project will re-examine a number of previously established empirical results that are based on these household surveys and determine the robustness of these results after correcting for benefit underreporting. The results of our project will provide useful ideas for how one should improve the surveys in order to minimize the bias as a result of this benefit understatement problem. 家庭調查是政府官方數據及學術研究所需要的。但近年有研究顯示家庭調查中關於家庭社會福利收入有較嚴重的漏報，然而這會影響我們對社會經濟問題的了解。相對現在極少數的學術研究會對漏報的原因及趨勢有深入的探討。本學術研究計劃有以下的目標：1. 本研究會採用六份重要的美國家庭調查展示漏報的趨勢 2. 本研究會探討漏報和受訪者的家庭背景及地理的關係. 3. 本研究會探討以往的學術論文結果在沒有處理漏報的問題下會否受到影響。本研究亦會建議日後的家庭調查應怎樣設計才能盡量減少因漏報而產生的問題。

459212.label: Realisation of objectives
459212.value: The objectives of the project have been largely achieved. While there remain some gaps that need to be filled, these will be done via other resources of the PI. Objective 1: Document and understand the extent of benefit underreporting in major US household surveys in 1960-2011. Understand how the design of survey, demographic and geographical characteristics affect the level of underreporting in surveys. The bulk of the project lies with calculating the rate of benefit underreporting of the major household surveys in the US. These rates have further been extended to the years after 2011. While the results for the Health and Retirement Study were computed from a previous research assistant, closer examination of the results suggest that these results are not ready to be circulated, and would require more time for additional checking. I have also studied how the design of the survey affects the level of underreporting. However, the study of how demographic and geographical characteristics affect the level of underreporting is yet completed due to manpower and time availability, and I will use other resources to help in completing this part in due course. Objective 2: Investigate how underreporting of benefits is affected by macroeconomic factors I have examined how the underreporting of benefits is correlated with the general national business cycles, and found that the effect was not strong enough to be of any interest. Nevertheless, a full conclusion is yet ready. My next step would be to look at how macroeconomic factors at a sub-national level affects underreporting. Objective 3: Provide empirical researchers and survey designers suggestions of how to deal with underreporting. I have dealt with this objective, and have provided two suggestions to researchers. First, the use of the complete set of underreporting rates produced by objective #1 to aid researchers to “adjust” the reported amounts in the surveys. Second, advocating the use and make-available of administrative microdata. These points and other recommendations are made in two research outputs of this project. Objective 4: Analyze how the results in previous studies may change if one accounts for underreporting. We look at how poverty rates of the US may change as a result of correcting for underreporting, and how our understanding of the characteristics of the poor would change as a result, the results of which are now part of the research output “Understanding Poverty with Longitudinal Data”. Problems encountered and attempts to overcome problems The primary problem of doing this research was the lack of stable manpower (research assistant) and the inherently long time needed of training. The small number of postgraduate students available has made this exercise difficult, and many would often leave for other employment opportunities before the preliminary training is completed, and the cost of re-training new research assistants was high. Training of undergraduates research assistants had also taken an enormous amount of time, given the nature of this research topic, the background of the research assistant, the other commitments the undergraduate research assistants had, as well as the large amount of preparation work (literature reading, learning of the datasets and programming languages) that had to be done. To overcome such problem, it took quite some time to identify and encourage young undergraduate students who aspired to become researchers, as such individuals would need research experience for their postgraduate applications. A motivated undergraduate student was found and has been working for me on this project since then.

459212.label: Major findings and research outcome
459212.value: After some serious consideration, I have distributed the abundant findings in this project to 3 papers. This is done so to increase chances of publications in recognized academic journals. First, I updated the results and revised my existing working paper “The Under-Reporting of Transfers in Household Surveys: Its Nature and Consequences”. A current version of the paper is available upon request. Second, findings per objectives #1 and #3 have become parts of the coauthored paper “Household Surveys in Crisis” (findings are summarized in the abstract below), which was published at the Journal of Economic Perspectives in the fall of 2015. The paper is attached in this report. Third, findings based on objectives #2 and #4 have gone to a paper titled “Understanding Poverty with Longitudinal Data”. A working version of the paper is attached in this report. This paper looks at measuring poverty with two of the household surveys we used in the project, and parts of this paper come from the results of objectives #2 and #4. Abstract for “Household Surveys in Crisis” , Journal of Economic Perspectives, vol. 29, no. 4, Fall 2015 (https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/jep.29.4.199) Household surveys, one of the main innovations in social science research of the last century, are threatened by declining accuracy, possibly due to reduced cooperation of respondents. We find that many indicators of survey quality have steadily declined in recent decades. While the extant literature has largely emphasized rising nonresponse rates, there are other potentially more important dimensions to the problem. We divide the problem into rising rates of nonresponse, imputation, and measurement error. We document the rise in each of these threats to survey quality. A fundamental problem in assessing biases due to these problems in surveys is the lack of a benchmark or measure of truth, leading us to focus on the accuracy of the reporting of government transfers. We provide evidence from aggregate measures of transfer reporting as well as linked microdata. We discuss the relative importance of misreporting of program receipt and conditional amounts of benefits received. We also discuss some of the conjectured reasons for declining cooperation and survey errors. We end by discussing ways to reduce the impact of the problem including the increased use of administrative data and the possibilities for combining administrative and survey data.

We see that research on poverty will continue to be important in the realm of public policy research. The current draft is expected to be ready for conference presentations by July 2017.

459212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459212.value: Household surveys remain the most authoritative sources of data to understand the economic and demographic changes of the population of a nation. They provide extremely important economic statistics, such as unemployment rate and rate of poverty, and they guide the course of public policies. However, the accuracy of these surveys has been debated recently, and in this project we focus on the issue of government benefit underreporting in major US household surveys in 1960-2011, as well as their implication of public policy making. We find that such underreporting has been substantial and has been rising in recent years. The nature of the survey and the kind of benefit received have strong implications to the degree of underreporting. Surveys that rely on telephone calls have worse reporting performance than those that use more elaborate methods of data collection (such as the case of in-home interviews). Benefits that are transitory in nature tend to have bad reporting, compared with permanent ones (such as retirement benefit). No strong evidence was found regarding the correlation of the business cycle and benefit underreporting. We provide advice on ways to deal with this problem in survey, from simple correction to the use of administrative microdata.

459512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459512.value: A recent and growing body of research studies the divergence in book and tax measures of income starting in the mid to late 1990s and continuing to the present. Some argue that this divergence between book and tax income is evidence of greater tax sheltering activity at the same time that managers manipulate earnings upward (Chan et al. (2010); Desai (2005); Desai and Dharmapala (2009); Tang and Firth (2011)). Some argue that a solution to this growing trend is to reduce the differences between financial and tax measures of income (i.e. greater book-tax conformity). As a result, managers would be unable to simultaneously report high financial accounting income to investors and low or negative taxable income to tax authorities. Opponents of greater book-tax conformity counter that financial accounting and tax accounting serve different purposes and provide evidence that greater conformity between the two measures of income results in the loss of information from earnings (Atwood et al. (2010); Guenther et al. (1997); Hanlon (2005); Hanlon et al. (2005)). The information content in earnings is often measured as the predictive ability and persistence of earnings (e.g. Hanlon (2005); Atwood et al. (2010)). The vast majority of this research has focused on companies in the United States and on the estimated consequences of book-tax conformity. Atwood et al. (2010) conduct an international examination of book-tax conformity, but also focus on the consequences of conformity on earnings persistence and predictability. To my knowledge, no study has explicitly tested the characteristics that lead to differences in degree of conformity in the first place. This is primarily a limitation from research focused on the United States because there is little variation in the factors that could lead to cross-sectional differences in book-tax conformity within one country. These factors, however, are important because they may represent benefits to book-tax conformity that subsume the lost of information content in earnings found in prior literature. This study will compare various estimates of book-tax conformity and examine the determinants of conformity. This paper contributes to the literature on the interaction between financial and tax accounting, also known as book-tax tradeoff. The implications of this paper will also aid regulators and tax authorities in designing more appropriate tax and accounting rules. 自上世紀九十年代中期開始至今，公司在財務會計上對溢利的衡量與其在稅務上對溢利的衡量呈現出較大差異。對於該問題的學術研究最近不斷湧現。有學者認為，會計帳面溢利與應課稅溢利的差異，為公司的如下行為提供了佐證：大幅度的避稅行為，以及操控盈餘使其增加的行為（Chan等(2010)；Desai(2005)；Desai與Dharmapala(2009)；Tang與Firth(2011)）。爲了控制此種趨勢，有學者提出了一種方案，即縮小財務會計和稅務在對溢利的衡量上存在的差異（亦即較高的財務-稅務一致性）。若採用了此方案，經理則無法在同一時間，既向股東報告一個較大的會計溢利數字，又向稅務機構提交一個較低甚至是負值的應課稅溢利數字。 反對財務-稅務一致性的學者認為，財務會計與稅務會計各自存在著不同的目的。他們提供了若干證據，發現財務會計帳面溢利與應課稅溢利較高的一致性會導致溢利所包含的信息量有所損失（Atwood等(2010)；Guenther等(1997)；Hanlon(2005)；Hanlon等(2005)）。溢利所包含的信息量通常用溢利的預測能力及持久性來衡量。 絕大部份此類研究，都是針對美國的公司進行的。這些研究主要關注于估計財務-稅務一致性所導致的後果。Atwood等(2010)進行了一項國際間的財務-稅務一致性的考察。不過該研究也同樣只是考察了財務-稅務一致性對溢利的持久性及預測能力的影響。 據本人所知，當前尚無研究專門檢驗哪些因素導致了財務-稅務一致性程度的不同。此為那些針對美國公司所進行的研究的一大局限，因為在同一國家里，那些可能影響財務-稅務一致性的因素，對不同公司而言往往沒有太大的差異（即較小的截面變化程度）。然而，這些因素是十分重要的。因為這些因素可能關乎財務-稅務一致性所帶來的收益，這些收益有可能會超過以往文獻所發現的財務-稅務一致性帶來的成本，即溢利所含信息量的損失。 本研究將比較若干對財務-稅務一致性程度的估計，并考察影響該一致性程度的決定因素。本文將對研究財務會計與稅務會計間相互關係的學術文獻作出一定貢獻。本研究的結果能引出一些啟示，有助於監管機構和稅務機構對稅務條例以及會計準則的制定與改進。

459512.label: Realisation of objectives
459512.value: Objectives 1 and 2 were fully achieved. First, I identified several different measures of book-tax conformity (BTC) used in the extant US literature and adapted them to the international setting. I also found a method recently developed by Atwood et al. (2010, 2012) which conducts a cross-country comparison of BTC and the consequence of BTC on earnings persistence. I also adapt the measure used by Dyreng and Lindsey (2009) to an international setting. Under this method, regression estimates are used to estimate the cash effective tax rates (CETRs) faced by firms. I compare these CETRs with the statutory tax rates and financial accounting effective tax rates (ETRs) to generate two additional estimates of BTC. Together, these various methods all capture different aspects of BTC. Objective 3 was also achieved. To compare and contrast the various BTC measures, I first examine the differences in the estimation. For example, the traditional measures of BTC compare the tax rates reported in income statements such as effective tax rates (ETRs) against the amount of taxes that are paid such as CETRs or cash tax expense reported in the cash flow statement. The regression estimates following Dyreng and Lindsey (2009) compare a large sample estimate of CETRs against cash taxes paid. The "new" measures from Atwood et al. (2010, 2012) directly estimate the variation from the root mean squared errors of regressions in the tax rates of firms. Since these different measures capture different aspects of BTC, I conduct analysis both by taking an average of the measures and also based on principal component analysis. Objective 4 was only partially achieved. I first examine the correlation and univariate differences between estimated BTC and several economic characteristics that include stock market development, government fiscal needs, and political affiliation. Preliminary results indicated that BTC and lagged BTC are indeed related to these market characteristics (e.g. market capitalization), fiscal needs (e.g. tax expenditures), and political affiliation (e.g. whether the party in power is left or right leaning). However, after controlling for a few characteristics that are likely to relate to BTC such as statutory tax rates and earnings management (Blaylock, Gaertner, and Shevlin 2014), the results are no longer significant. Also, following prior international research on the importance of various institutional factors such as rule of law, disclosure regulation, and market development (La Porta et al. 1999, 2006), I add additional control variables such as legal protection, enforcement, and investor protection. Again, with these control variables, the main results from the tests of my hypotheses become insignificant. As a result, while I was able to develop a new measure of BTC and synthesize it with existing estimates found in the literature, I was not able to establish a direct relation between the proposed economic factors and BTC. The non-result is likely because BTC is derived from a combination of different factors and it is difficult to separate out the specific causal effect of such a relationship. I attempted to identify the determinants of differences in BTC using a number of different economic, political, and institutional variables and the results were either very weak or insignificant.

459512.label: Major findings and research outcome
459512.value: The primary finding of this research is that while the variation in BTC across countries do appear to be related to differences in capital market, fiscal, and political characteristics, the relation is highly correlated with other factors such as the size of the country, tax rates, and economic characteristics. As such, I was not able to establish a direct causal link and the results become insignificant after controlling for other institutional factors.

459512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
459512.value: A potential further development is to identify settings that are more likely to show the direct relation between BTC and capital market, fiscal, and political characteristics. For example, I can attempt to identify a legal shock and use "shock-based causal inference" to more cleanly measure the direct determinants of differences in BTC across countries.

459512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459512.value: This research estimates the degree of integration in accounting and tax rules across countries, known as book-tax conformity. This research also tries to identify the source of differences in book-tax conformity across countries. In the current stage, I was able to estimate book-tax conformity and examine the relation between book-tax conformity and several economic characteristics. However, the results are not significant after controlling for other economic factors.

460112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
460112.value: Unlike other biological motors, the flagellar motor is bidirectional and thus can rotate in clockwise or counterclockwise directions.Construction of this switchable rotary machinery requires assembly of ring structures that permits transmission of proton motive force from the stator to mechanical work of rotor and the filament. In the model bacterium Escherchia coli, the membrane-embedded MS ring composed of FliF is a key substructure to locate the export apparatus, anchor the rod and direct the incorporation of switch proteins FliG, FliM and FliN to form the cytoplasmic C ring. The MS-C ring junction is laid by the cytoplasmic domain of FliF and N-terminal domain of FliG that any interruption of their interaction results in nonflagellate or rotational bias. While the core components of the motor is generally homologous, recent electron cryotomographical analysis suggests distinctive features at MS-C ring interface among ε-proteobacteria, raising a long-standing question about the molecular architecture and mechanistic details of different rotary systems. How individual components are orderly assembled into this supramolecular structure and co-operated to drive rotation in both direction is not clear. We recently determined two crystal structures of FliG from H. pylori and revealed multiple conformations of the C-terminal subdomain that may modulate the stator-rotor interaction and therefore rotational switching. To further understand the signal transmission from the stator-rotor interface to the filament and the structural diversity of flagellar motor, a study of the FliF-FliG molecular contact at the membrane-proximal side of the C-ring has been initiated. We have currently obtained some preliminary crystallographic data of FliF-FliG protein complex and established a platform for in vivo functional complementation assays. In this study, we will apply multidisciplinary approaches in structural biology and molecular microbiology to investigate the physical association and functional importance of FliF-FliG complex in flagellation and motility. Specifically, we will determine the domain structure of FliF-FliG complex by x-ray crystallography. In parallel, we will define the interface of FliF-FliG by mutagenesis and interaction studies and further confirmed by molecular genetics and functional characterization in H. pylori. Organization of individual FliF-FliG module in the inner C ring structure will be mapped by in vivo cross-linking experiments. Our work will generate novel mechanistic details toward understanding flagellar motor assembly and switching, and provide insights into the structural diversity of flagellar motors. In the long term, our findings will enhance our knowledge of macromolecular assembly and provide a framework for rational design of nanomotors.

460112.label: Realisation of objectives
460112.value: Objective 1: Molecular interaction and structure determination of FliF-FliG complex by X-ray crystallography - Our team has purified the binary complex containing the FliF C-terminal domain and the FliG N-terminal domain for interaction and crystallization studies. By using a combination of mutagenesis, pull-down, static light scattering and isothermal titration calorimetry assays, we have further defined their interacting surfaces, studied their stoichiometric ratio and binding kinetics. For the structural analysis, the main obstacle we encountered in the early stage of the project lied on protein crystallization. FliF-FliG crystals were grown in over 3 months and the crystallization was difficult to be reproduced, suggesting that the purified protein underwent some degree of proteolysis in order to generate protein units for proper crystal packing. Therefore, we modified our crystallization experiment with addition of trypsin that allowed us to obtain crystals in one month and with good diffraction quality. For the protein structure determination, phase was solved using a 2.5Å SAD data set collected from selenomethionine labeled crystal. With a native data set diffracted to 2.3Å resolution, the crystal structure of FliF-FliG binary complex was refined with Rfree=22.37% and R=18.84%. Objective 2: Validation of FliF-FliG interaction using in vivo complementation assays - To confirm the findings obtained in Objective 1, we attempted to use the H. pylori FliG-null strain for complementation study. Full length FliG in pILL2157 vector or RdxA vector system was applied, however flagellation and motility cannot be restored. We considered that some other neighboring genes related to flagellar synthesis may be interrupted during the construction of the FliG deletion strain. To overcome the problems, E. coli complementation system was employed. This platform has been adopted to validate the importance of hinge region in the FliG C-terminal domain in rotational switching as reported in our previous funded project (GRF 460110; Lam et al., Structure, 2012). Mutations of equivalent key residues identified in the binding interface of FliF-FliG resulted in non-flagellation. These results are in line with our in vitro findings. Additionally, our findings further demonstrate the conservation of MS-C ring junction among different bacterial species. Objective 3: Organization mapping of FliF-FliG at the motor ring structure – Due to the failure to apply the H. pylori in vivo complementation system as described above, we have applied E. coli system to map the assembly of FliF-FliG. Based on the crystal structure of FliF-FliG, we have constructed various FliG mutants, each carries a pair of cysteine mutation lying on solvent exposed helices 4 and 5 of FliG. Moreover, we have also docked our FliF-FliG structure to the 25Å cryo-EM map obtained in E. coli to explain the molecular assembly at the junction of MS-C ring.

460112.label: Major findings and research outcome
460112.value: In this study, we report for the first time the crystal structure of FliF-FliG binary complex at 2.3Å resolution. The protein complex is consisted of the cytoplasmic domain of FliF and the N-terminal domain of FliG in a 1:1 stoichiometry ratio as validated by light scattering. The two helices of FliF are arranged in an almost 90-degree turn clipping the central cleft of FliG, resulting in an extensive contact that buries the highly conserved hydrophobic residues in both proteins. The binding properties revealed by the atomic structure is in line with the kinetic data using isothermal titration calorimetry. By using in vitro mutagenesis and in vivo complementation assays, we have further confirmed the importance of the hydrophobic patch, specifically residues 551-556, in the formation of FliF-FliG complex. Strikingly, when compared with the apo form of FliG from A. aeolicus, dramatic conformational changes in helices 1, 2 and 5 are noted, and their movement is required to give an open form for FliF binding. Similar to A. aeolicus FliG, the N-terminal domain of H. pylori FliG is folded in an armadillo structure, implying that the overall FliG structure contains 3 ARM repeats, each is connected by a long helix/loop. It is possible that these ARM repeats contribute to the interactions with neighboring FliG units in the motor switch complex, while the connected helices modulate the dynamic of the intermolecular contact during torque generation and rotational switching. We have further docked the FliF-FliG structure to the cryo-EM map of MS-C ring complex. Our results lead us to propose an assembly model to address the long-standing question about the symmetry and molecular architecture at the MS-C ring junction. In our model, the C-terminal cytoplasmic end of FliF acts as a set of anchor to hook up FliGs and the remaining C-ring. Their strong interaction via extensive hydrophobic contact explains how this 3 Mega Dalton motor switch complex is securely anchored to the inner membrane for its function. The structure of FliF-FliG has been deposited to PDB (ID: 5WUJ). There is some delay in publication as we attempted to obtain the crystal structure of the apo form of H. pylori FliG for structural comparison. Currently, a manuscript has been submitted and is currently under reviewed. The PI has also been invited to deliver talks in two international meetings to present the findings.

460112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460112.value: Our work has revealed the structural basis underlying the MS-C ring in flagellar motor. These findings lay a solid foundation for us to further investigate the mechanistic details and regulations of this nano-device. New collaborations with Prof. Wah Chiu (Baylor College of Medicine, US), Prof. Zhang Qinfen (Sun Yat-sen University, China), Prof. Yuan Junhua (University of Science and Technology of China, China) and Prof. Wu Yilin (CUHK) are established. There are several lines of investigation underway, these include 1) x-ray crystallography and cryo-EM studies of H. pylori flagellar motor (WC and ZQ) (supported by NSFC/RGC Joint Research Scheme 2013/14), 2) interactome of motor switch complex (supported by GRF 2013/14), and 3) chemotatic behavior of H. pylori motor switch complex (YJ and WY) (supported by NSFC General Programme 2013/14, and GRF pending).

460112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460112.value: Synthesis of a functional flagellum starts with the assembly of the MS ring protein FliF in the inner membrane followed by the attachment of motor switch components FliG, FliM and FliN to make the cytoplasmic C-ring. This project aims to address one of the long-standing questions - coupling of MS- and C-rings, by using a combination of structural biology and molecular genetics approaches. Our group has determined the first ever crystal structure of FliF-FliG binary complex containing the C-terminal cytoplasmic domain of FliF and the N-terminal domain of FliG. The two helices of FliF are bent by almost 90-degree and are bound in the central cleft of FliG lined by hydrophobic residues that are highly conserved. Interruption of the hydrophobic patch abolishes the formation of FliF-FliG heterodimer, suggesting that similar binding mode of FliF-FliG is exploited among different bacterial species. Noteworthy, structural comparison indicates that binding of FliF induces structural changes of FliG from a closed to open conformation. An assembly model of MS-C rings is proposed with each FliF acts an anchor to support the motor switch complex, which is 3 Mega-Dalton in size. Our findings provide better understanding of type III secretion system and provide new concepts to the design of nano-machine.

460412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
460412.value: Head and neck (H&N) cancers account for 5% of all cancers, are histologically diverse, comprising thyroid and salivary malignancies, squamous cell carcinomas and other malignancies. Although conventional US, CT, MRI and PET are used for differentiating H&N cancer from benign disease, many H&N lesions cannot be diagnosed accurately by these imaging techniques and thus invasive diagnostic techniques including needle cytology or biopsy are required. Elasticity imaging or elastography is an emerging field that measures and displays tissue stiffness properties non-invasively. Analogous to clinical palpation, elastography characterizes tissues because pathological conditions including cancer and fibrosis typically have higher Youngs modulus, equating to stiffness, than benign disease and normal tissues, respectively. In the last five years, research in US elastography (US-E) has mushroomed, in part due to the introduction of real-time US-E on state-of-the-art clinical US systems. Furthermore, US-E is non-ionizing, safe, quick to perform, inexpensive, and acceptable to patients. US-E has been most thoroughly evaluated for breast tumours, where evidence indicates that it increases the diagnostic accuracy when combined with conventional US. Similar data in the H&N is accumulating, with over 30 preliminary studies, including several from the investigators institution, indicating a potential role for lesion characterization in thyroid, lymph nodes, salivary glands and other neck masses. A recent meta-analysis of thyroid US-E documented 92% sensitivity and 90% specificity for malignancy. To date, most US-E data is based on a specific method called strain elastography, which is highly operator dependent as it requires an optimal technique of tissue compressions performed by the operator. Furthermore, data produced by strain elastography is semi-quantitative and indirectly related to stiffness. Recently, a quantitative US-E method has emerged termed shear wave elastography (SWE), which utilizes focused ultrasound impulses to stimulate tissues and, from the velocity of the induced shear waves, produces output corresponding to Youngs modulus. As SWE obviates operator compression, it is more reproducible, and the quantitative output means that it can also be used for lesions that are too large for strain elastography. Currently, there is sparse data about the accuracy of SWE in the H&N. The aim of this proposal is to evaluate SWE for H&N lesion characterization. Quantitative stiffness data for lesions in the thyroid, lymph nodes, salivary glands and other sites will be correlated with tissue diagnosis to determine 1) the diagnostic accuracies of US-E and 2) whether and how US-E can be incorporated into future US examinations in routine practice. 頭頸部（H&N）惡性腫瘤佔所有癌症的5%，組織學類型多樣化，包含甲狀腺及唾液腺惡性腫瘤，鱗狀細胞癌及其他惡性腫瘤。儘管常规影像技術諸如US、CT、MRI及 PET適用於H&N惡性腫瘤與良性病變間的鑑別，但並不能确切診斷很多頭頸部病變，尚需侵入性診斷技術包括細針穿刺細胞學檢查或活檢進一步確診。 彈性成像屬於新兴領域，是一種測量或顯示組織硬度特性的非侵入性技術。類似於臨床觸診，彈性成像可用於定義病變特徵；原因是與良性病變及正常組織分別相比，惡性腫瘤和纖維化等病理狀態的典型特徵為其楊氏模量（Youngs modulus,相當於硬度）更高。在過去五年內，超聲彈性成像（US-E）方面的研究迅速發展；部分原因為實時US-E被引入最新臨床超聲系統。 此外，US-E操作起來無輻射、安全、快速，並且價格低廉易被病人接受。關於US-E應用的評估，於乳腺腫瘤方面開展得最充分；其證據表明US-E聯合傳統US可提高診斷準確性。H&N方面有類似研究數據在累積，超過30項初步研究（其中數個源自申請人研究機構 ）顯示了US-E在定義甲狀腺、淋巴結、唾液腺及其他頸部腫塊病變特徵中的潛能。近期一項meta-analysis表明US-E診斷甲狀腺惡性腫瘤的敏感性為92%，特異性為90%。 迄今為止，大多數US-E數據基於一種名為應變彈性成像(strain elastography) 的特殊技術。該技術需要操作者以最佳方式向組織施壓，因此對操作者依從性甚高。此外，應變彈性成像採集的是半定量數據，與硬度只是間接相關。 近來，一種名為剪切波彈性成像（shear wave elastography, SWE）的 定量US-E興起。SWE運用聚焦超聲脉衝對組織施加激勵而誘發剪切波, 通過測定剪切波傳播速度獲取相應的楊氏模量值。由於SWE 避免了操作者施壓，可重複性更高；定量結果意味著SWE 還可用於體積太大而不適用於應變彈性成像的病灶。目前，SWE 應用於H&N 的準確性的研究數據稀少。本項提案的目的在於評價SWE在定義H&N病變特徵中的應用, 探討甲狀腺、淋巴結、唾液腺及其他部位病變硬度的定量數據與組織學診斷之間的相關性，從而1）確定US-E的診斷準確性2）論證US-E將來是否及如何納入常規超聲檢查。

460412.label: Realisation of objectives
460412.value: 1. The project achieved this objective 100% as a wide range of quantitative stiffness data had been obtained for various benign and malignant thyroid lesions. This study has the largest overall sample size of thyroid nodules (N=401) compared to other published studies of thyroid elastography using identical shear wave elastography technology. 2. The project achieved this objective 100% in terms of analysing the diagnostic accuracies of a large number of stiffness parameters of thyroid lesions, which may be grouped broadly into absolute and relative indices as well as textural indices. Our analyses included more types of elasticity index than any other study published to date evaluating identical US-E technology. A parameter termed SSI_2mm ROI, which equated to the mean stiffness value of a 2mm region of interest placed within the nodule, achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy of all absolute and relative stiffness indices evaluated. This equated to an AUC of 0.60 54.3% sensitivity and 63.2% specificity. 3. This project achieved this objective 100% by analysing different combinations of US-E and grey scale criteria in an attempt to increase diagnostic performance of thyroid US examinations in routine practice.

460412.label: Major findings and research outcome
460412.value: 1. Statistically significant differences were found in stiffness indices on US-E between benign and malignant thyroid pathologies. However, there was substantial overlap in most US-E indices between pathologies including the 2 main groups of benign and malignant pathology, benign hyperplastic nodules and papillary carcinomas. The optimal diagnostic performance of US-E was suboptimal, equating to AUC of 0.60, 54.3% sensitivity and 63.2% specificity. By comparison, conventional ultrasound criteria yielded higher AUCs (0.865 or 0.785). In addition, no combination of conventional US with US-E achieved higher accuracies than conventional US alone. 2. The diagnostic performance results in our project were lower compared to other preliminary studies, e.g. 85.2% sensitivity and 93.9% specificity in a study by Sebag et al. To investigate underlying causes, we analysed the influence of different levels of resting pressure (precompression A-D) applied via the transducer during US-E on stiffness measurements of normal tissue (Norm), benign hyperplastic nodules (BHN) and malignant papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) nodules. The findings showed successive increases in US-E stiffness of all tissue types as precompression levels increased, although the rate was higher for PTC than BHN and Norm (Ps<0.05). US-E stiffness values (kPa) of Norm, BHN, and PTC at baseline precompression (A) were 10.3±3.3, 17.7±7.6, and 22.2±11.9 compared with 21.1±4.2, 42.3±16.0, and 97.6±46.8 at high precompression (D). SWE index differences between precompression levels A and D were 10.8 kPa for Norm, 24.6 kPa for BHN, and 75.4 kPa for PTC. This study found that PTCs show greater SWE stiffening than BHN as precompression rises. Importantly, this project showed that precompression effects on thyroid nodules were not negligible and could potentially explain wide discrepancies in published SWE discriminatory performance results for thyroid malignancy. 3. This project was the first to analyse textural features of US-E images by extracting 15 new gray level co-occurrence matrix US-E textural parameters, which were acquired using different precompression levels (see point#2). Diagnostic performances of each parameter for malignancy were calculated, and optimised models were generated at each pre-compression level. The optimal model comprised two US-E textural features at the highest pre-compression level, which attained AUC, sensitivity and specificity of 0.973, 97.5% and 90.0%, respectively. By comparison, non-textural absolute US-E indices attained AUC of 0.709, 18.8% sensitivity and 95.8% specificity. These preliminary results suggest US-E textural analysis can distinguish benign and malignant thyroid nodules, and SWE spatial heterogeneity is greater in malignant nodules.

460412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460412.value: 3. The project could be developed further as follows: 1. Our study was the first to document the influence of precompression on different types of thyroid nodule. Future work could determine whether precompression can be standardised between different operators, and what is the optimal level of compression that can be performed reproducibly in clinical practice. The ultimate goal would be to develop and standardise a level of compression that can be applied universally and achieves the highest possible diagnostic performance of US-E for thyroid malignancy. 2. Our study was the first to perform texture analysis of thyroid nodules and the results were promising in terms of suggesting that textural parameters may be diagnostically accurate. These results need to be validated in larger, multi-centre studies. We plan to analyse even more texture features and generate optimal models incorporating these with conventional US features. 3. We are presently comparing different types of US-E technology, including the technology used in this project, to determine whether any differences in diagnostic performances are due to technical factors related to the underlying technology or due to intrinsic stiffness properties of the nodules.

460412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460412.value: This research and resulting publications have contributed significantly to the evidence for a recent clinical ultrasound based technology that measures tissue stiffness non-invasively termed ultrasound-elastography (US-E). Concurring with other published studies, we reported significant differences in US-E stiffness indices of benign and malignant thyroid nodules. However, our research, which included the largest sample evaluated to date using a specific quantitative US-E technology, showed substantial overlap in these indices such that accuracies of most US-E indices were suboptimal compared to conventional ultrasound, both in isolation and as an adjunctive technique. Our research also investigated causes for variation in published accuracy results, and we showed that an operator-dependent aspect termed precompression could bias the results in a pattern that matched the published data. Our research also analysed US-E images to extract novel textural indices, which had high diagnostic accuracies for distinguishing benign and malignant thyroid nodules, which reflects the fact that malignancies are spatially heterogeneous. The above results have been published as original papers in several peer reviewed journals. They have influenced future thyroid US-E research appreciably by highlighting areas which are deficient and still need to addressed before US-E can be accepted in clinical practice for thyroid nodule characterisation.

Mol. Genet. 20: 3787-3797.）。而且，擴展CAG重復 RNAs 會形成細胞核聚焦點，尤其是在核仁，核仁是前體核糖體RNA轉錄的亞核位點。核仁應激是前體核糖體RNA轉錄受損觸發的一種狀態。前體核糖體RNA合成障礙與神經退行性病變相關，這就暗示核仁應激參與神經元細胞死亡。然而，在神經退行性病變中誘導核仁應激的信號至今仍未被發現。我們在polyQ細胞模型中觀察了多個核仁應激的信號，結果顯示擴展的CAG重復RNAs通過誘導核仁應激產生毒性。為進一步闡明擴展CAG重復RNAs介導毒性的機制，我們通過RNA與蛋白相互作用的研究找出與擴展CAG重復RNAs互作的蛋白。從此研究中，我們證實核仁素（nucleolin, NCL）是一種特異的與擴展CAG重復RNAs互作的蛋白，並且是直接相互作用，此結果同時在polyQ病人細胞系中得到證實。由於NCL可通過調節前體核糖體RNA的轉錄影響核糖體RNA基因啟動子DNA甲基化，所以我們假設NCL與擴展CAG重復RNAs相互作用可下調前體核糖體RNA的轉錄，最終導致核仁應激。在此研究中，我們將研究1）NCL如何參與擴展CAG重復RNAs介導毒性；2）核仁應激信號如何從核仁傳輸至細胞質誘發線粒體雕亡。闡明擴展CAG重復RNAs與NCL相互作用的細節以及核仁擴展CAG重復RNA參與的應激通路將會為RNA毒性參與polyQ發病機制提供新的見解，並有助於開發新的治療方向。

460712.label: Realisation of objectives
460712.value: Both project objectives have been achieved. 1. investigate how expanded CAG RNAs perturb nucleolin (NCL) function and cause nucleolar stress through the dysregulation of DNA methylation of ribosomal promoter and inhibition of pre-rRNA transcription We have elucidated the mechanism through which expanded CAG RNAs perturb nucleolin function. Our data demonstrated that the interaction between nucleolin and expanded CAG RNAs caused a reduction of binding of nucleolin to UCE DNA element in the rRNA promoter. This leads to DNA hypermethylation of UCE and results in down-regulation of pre-rRNA transcription. 2. delineate how p53 conveys the expanded CAG RNA nucleolar stress signal from the nucleolus to the cytosol to trigger apoptosis via mitochondria Our data demonstrated that nuclear export of p53 is essential for the expanded CAG RNA stress signal to be transduced to the cytosol to trigger nucleolar stress apoptosis.

460712.label: Major findings and research outcome
460712.value: This project aims at investigating how expanded CAG RNAs perturb nucleolin function and cause nucleolar stress through the dysregulation of DNA methylation of ribosomal promoter and inhibition of pre-rRNA transcription. We mainly made use of a transient transfection SH-SY5Y neuronal cell model to express expanded CAG RNAs. In this cell model, we observed specific pre-rRNA transcription defects in cells that expressed expanded CAG RNAs. Further, our chromatin-immunoprecipitation experimental result showed that expanded CAG RNAs interacts with the RRM2 and RRM3 domains of nucleolin. This caused a reduction of the binding of nucleolin to rRNA promoter which subsequently perturbed the binding of RNA polymerase I to rRNA promoter. As a consequence, the pre-rRNA transcription rate was reduced in cells expressing expanded CAG RNAs. The reduction of pre-rRNA level in cells led to the elevation of free ribosomal proteins (e.g. RpL11 and RpL23) which resulted in a reduced interaction between the MDM2 ubiquitin ligase and p53 protein. The elevation of p53 protein in the cytosol then triggered mitochondrial apoptosis pathway. We also observed nucleolar stress activation in a transgenic mouse model of polyglutamine disease. This confirms that what we observed in our cell model also happens in vivo.

460712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460712.value: Research findings of this project have been used to design a peptidylic inhibitor to intervene CAG RNA toxicity of polyglutamine disease. This work is currently supported by the RGC Collaborative Research Fund.

460712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460712.value: Polyglutamine degeneration represents a group of late-onset progressive neurological disorders caused by neuronal cell death. The expression of expanded polyglutamine disease protein has been reported to be the major cause of neuronal cell death. More recent investigations revealed that expanded CAG RNAs also trigger cell death. This project elucidated one of the pathogenic pathways, nucleolar stress, exploited by expanded CAG RNA to activate apoptosis. In the long run, our findings could lead to the development of new therapeutic directions against polyglutamine diseases.
