460912.label: Realisation of objectives
460912.value: After an extensive literature search, we confirm that this is the first randomized trial that aims to address a very important clinical question: should anti-thrombotic drugs (clopidogrel) be withheld before removal of colonic polyps? We managed to recruit 100% of eligible patients as stated in the research proposal. Among them, 212 patients have completed the study and the remaining 4 patients have been scheduled for the randomization visit in January 2018. While closely monitoring for any serious adverse events (e.g. acute coronary syndrome, life-threatening bleeding), we did not perform any unblinded interim analysis as the latter might introduce bias to the subsequent enrolment of subjects. For example, a numerical trend in favor of one treatment arm may render both investigators and patients hesitant about participating in this study. For submission of the current report to RGC, we, therefore, performed a blinded analysis of all the patients who have completed the study (i.e., treatment A vs. treatment B) to avoid bias. We performed both best case and worst case scenario analyses and found that the possible outcomes of the remaining 4 patients would not influence the study conclusion (data not shown). Our plan is to perform an unblinded analysis of the complete dataset in March 2018 for our manuscript. We anticipate that the final manuscript will be ready for submission in April and expect a provisional acceptance in June/July 2018.

460912.label: Major findings and research outcome
460912.value: We screened 386 patients, 212 (Group 1: 103 vs. Group 2:109) were randomized. A blinded analysis (i.e., Group 1 vs. Group 2) of the current data set was performed to avoid any potential bias. Four patients (3.9%) in Group 1 compared to 3 (2.8%) in Group 2 reached the primary endpoint of delayed post-polypectomy bleeding. There was no difference in the 30-day cumulative probability of delayed post-polypectomy bleeding between the two groups (3.9% vs. 2.9%, log-rank test, P=0.683). A total of 15 patients (9 in Group 1 (8.7%) vs. 6 in Group 2 (5.8%)) had immediate post-polypectomy bleeding (P=0.421). There was no cardiothrombotic event. Contrary to current beliefs, we have shown that the risk of post-polypectomy bleeding in patients receiving continuous treatment with clopidogrel was not significantly different from those who withheld clopidogrel before colonoscopy.

460912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460912.value: Current international guidelines recommend withholding clopidogrel for at least 7 days before colonoscopic polypectomy. However, coronary stent thrombosis can occur as early as Day 7 after stopping anti-thrombotic drugs. Contrary to conventional belief, our study shows that there is no clinically meaningful difference between the two treatment groups, suggesting that continuation of clopidogrel therapy does not increase the risk of post-polypectomy bleeding. This finding, if reconfirmed by multi-national trials in the future, will provide strong evidence to revise current international guidelines on the management of antiplatelet therapy in patients undergoing endoscopic procedures with high thrombotic risk.

460912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460912.value: The use of antithrombotic therapy (antiplatelet agents and anticoagulants) is increasing with an aging global population. Clopidogrel is a potent antiplatelet drug that is essential for the treatment of acute coronary syndrome and prevention of coronary stent thrombosis. However, patients receiving clopidogrel also suffer from increased risk of gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding. Colonoscopy is increasingly performed in patients on antithrombotic therapy because recent evidence suggests that coronary heart disease is associated with increased risk of colorectal cancer. Management of patients on antithrombotic therapy undergoing colonoscopy remains a dilemma in clinical practice: should clopidogrel be withheld before a colonoscopy? Current international guidelines recommend that one should withhold clopidogrel for at least 7 days before removal of colonic polyps. However, these recommendations are largely based on expert opinion only. Prospective trial data are not available. The current clinical trial has for the first time shown that interruption of clopidogrel in patients undergoing colonoscopy is not necessary. Our findings will provide important data for international guideline committees to review and revise their recommendations.

461012.label: Realisation of objectives
461012.value: 1. Objective 1: As planned, we determined by immunohistochemistry and immunoreactivity score analysis on clinical prostatic tissues that TLX exhibited a significant increase of nuclear immunoreactivity in prostate carcinoma lesions, and high Gleason-score lesions displayed significant higher TLX immunoreactivity as compared to normal and benign prostatic tissues. 2. Objective 2: As planned, we determined the role of TLX in cellular senescence in prostate cancer by both shRNA-knockdown and ectopic overexpression approaches using different prostate cancer cell line models and immortalized epithelial cell line (with different expression status of AR and p53). (a) Our results showed that knockdown of endogenous TLX could suppress the in vitro and in vivo malignant growth capacities of prostate cancer cells and induce cell-cycle arrest and cellular senescence, whereas its overexpression could promote malignant growth of prostate cancer cells, regardless of their AR and p53 status. (b) Moreover, our results showed that TLX overexpression could suppress cellular senescence in prostate cancer cells and also prevent cellular senescence induced by activated oncogene H-RasG12V and tumor suppressor PTEN loss in primary prostatic epithelial cells. 3. Objective 3: As planned, we determined and characterized the transcriptional targets of TLX in its induction of suppression of cellular senescence in prostate cancer cells. By ChIP and luciferase reporter assays, we demonstrated that the suppression of cellular senescence in prostate cancer cells by TLX was mediated through its differential co-regulation of two senescence-associated genes, namely transrepression of cell cycle-associated CDKN1A (p21) gene and transactivation of longevity- associated SIRT1 gene. 4. Objective 4: As planned, we evaluated the significance of p53 in the TLX-mediated suppression of cellular senescence in prostate cancer cells with different background of p53. Our results showed that the TLX-mediated suppression of p21 in prostate cancer cells was p53-independent. Moreover, we also determined that the SIRT1-mediated suppression of cellular senescence in prostate cancer cells was independent of p53 and p21, further suggesting that the suppression of senescence induced by TLX was via two independent pathways. 5. Objective 5: As planned, we evaluated the functional relationship between TLX and androgen receptor (AR) signaling and its significance in hormone-independent growth of prostate cancer. Our results showed that TLX could suppress AR expression via its specific binding to AR gene promoter and also suppress its transcriptional activity, by recruiting several histone modifiers (HDAC1, HDAC3 and LSD1). It is believed that TLX could promote the castration-resistant prostate cancer progression by it direct suppression of AR signaling. Some of the results as obtained by studies of objectives 1-4 have been published in the Journal of Pathology (2015;236:103-115).

461012.label: Major findings and research outcome
461012.value: Our major findings obtained by this GRF-funded study on the role of TLX in prostate cancer are summarized as follows: 1. In this study, we have elucidated that the functional role of the orphan nuclear receptor TLX in prostate cancer. By expression analysis, we have determined that TLX exhibits an increased expression pattern in clinical prostate cancer tissues and its up-regulation is associated with the advanced progression of prostate cancer. By extensive in vitro and in vivo functional analyses, we have shown that TLX can perform an oncogenic function in prostate cancer via its regulation of cellular senescence in prostatic cells, evidenced by its knockdown triggers cellular senescence and cell growth arrest in vitro and in vivo, whereas its overexpression promotes the malignant growth of prostate cancer cells. Furthermore, overexpression of TLX or enhancement of its activity by specific ligand can effectively prevent drug-induced senescence in prostate cancer cells and also prevent primary prostatic epithelial cells to escape oncogene-induced senescence (OIS) induced by either activated oncogene H-RasR12V or knockdown of tumor suppressor PTEN. We have also characterized that this induced suppression of senescence is mediated through a mechanism of direct but independent transcriptional regulation of two senescence-associated genes, repression of CDKN1 gene and transactivation of SIRT1 gene. In summary, our present study demonstrates a novel role of TLX in the prostate carcinogenesis through its direct suppression of OIS. Some of these major findings obtained in this study have been published recently in the Journal of Pathology (2015;236:103-115). 2. Besides, we have also determined that TLX could act as a repressor of AR in prostate cancer cells. Our findings showed that TLX exhibited an increased expression in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) lesions and also CRPC xenograft tumors. Further functional and mechanistic analyses showed that TLX overexpression could promote hormone-resistant growth in prostate cancer, and this growth promotion function was mediated through the direct repression of AR gene promoter by recruitment of some chromatin modifiers, including histone deacetylases (HDACs) and lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) and suppression of its transactivation activity. Based on these findings, a manuscript is being prepared for publication.

461012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
461012.value: 1. Besides elucidating a mechanistic insight on how the nuclear receptor TLX functions to suppress cellular or oncogene-induced senescence in prostate cancer via its direct co-regulation of two senescence-associated genes CDKN1 and SIRT1, we also showed in this study that the drug (doxorubicin)-induced senescence in prostate cancer cells could be attenuated by a TLX-specific ligand (ccrp2). This noteworthy finding suggests that TLX could be a potential therapeutic target in prostate cancer, and also or targeting TLX for induction of senescence signaling could be a therapeutic strategy for cancer management. 2. In this study, we revealed for the first time that TLX could act as both a transcription repressor and activator in its mediation of senescence suppression in prostate cancer cells. However, the mechanism involved in this transcriptional regulation is still not elucidated. Currently, we are employing the proteomic and chromatin immunoprecipitation approaches to identify the co-regulators involved in transcription process.

461012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
461012.value: Prostate cancer is a common male cancer in many Western and Asian countries. It is currently ranked the 3rd common male cancer in Hong Kong. This cancer is characterized by its initial slow and androgen-dependent growth features. However, many hormone therapy-treated patients will progress to a lethal hormone-independent and metastatic disease (hormone-refractory or castration-resistant prostate cancer), to which treatment options are few and also ineffective leading to high mortality. Oncogene-induced senescence is an important tumor-suppressing mechanism to prevent early cancer development and also advanced progression. Overcoming this process is a critical step in early cancer development. In this study, we demonstrate that the nuclear receptor TLX, which exhibits an increased expression in high grade and also castration-resistant cancers, can act as a promoter of prostate cancer by suppression of cellular senescence via a mechanism of differential regulation of senescence-associated genes. Another noteworthy finding of this study is that either oncogene or drug-induced senescence in prostate cancer cells can be attenuated or blocked by small molecule or ligand-induced activation of TLX, suggesting that TLX is a druggable target and also targeting the TLX signaling could be a potential therapeutic strategy for prostate cancer management.

461412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
461412.value: The aim of this study is to determine the role of postoperative monitoring of circulating cardiac troponin, by using a high-sensitivity assay, to predict major vascular complications after noncardiac surgery. Cardiac death, myocardial infarction and heart failure are amongst the most feared complications after noncardiac surgery. Previous research has focused on preoperative clinical assessment to identify patients at risk of these events. However, existing models are inadequate to predict postoperative vascular complications. In an international prospective cohort study (VISION study; n=16,079), we have recently shown that postoperative measurements of cardiac troponin improved our prediction of adverse vascular outcomes. More importantly, a low concentration of cardiac troponin, one that was previously considered normal, was found to be an independent predictor of mortality at 30 days after surgery. There is now substantial biologic rationale, evidence from clinical trials in the nonsurgical population, as well as data from our own studies to suggest that a very low concentration of cardiac troponin may indicate reversible myocardial injury. This discovery represents a paradigm shift in our strategy for preventing postoperative vascular complications, in that postoperative surveillance of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin may allow the perioperative physicians to identify patients at risk and to initiate timely intervention, such as administration of antiplatelet or other anti-anginal drugs. A study is therefore required to define the prognostic significance of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin in predicting major vascular complications after noncardiac surgery. We propose to carry out an international, multicenter, large prospective cohort study, in 10,000 adults undergoing noncardiac surgery, to evaluate the relationship between high-sensitivity cardiac troponin and the risk of major vascular complications at 30 days and 12 months after surgery. As a secondary aim, we will determine the threshold troponin concentration, beyond which clinicians should start to intervene. We will also explore the value of change in troponin concentration, from its preoperative baseline, in the prediction of postoperative vascular complications. The findings of this study will be of considerable social and economic significance. If, as we believe that it will, our study confirms the utility of cardiac troponin as an indicator of early myocardial injury, this finding should instigate a fundamental change in the practice of perioperative medicine around the world. Specifically, monitoring of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin should be incorporated into routine postoperative care. Future research must be performed to identify appropriate plans for the management of these high risk patients. 本研究的目的在於通過在手術後監測高靈敏度的心肌肌鈣蛋白的含量，從而探討其在非心臟大手術後並發心血管綜合症中的作用。 心源性死亡—心肌梗塞和心力衰竭，是非心臟大手術後最危險的並發症。先前的研究主要集中於在術前進行該並發症發生的臨床評估。然而，現有的模型並不足以對術後血管並發症的發生進行預測。一項國際性的前瞻性隊列研究中（VISION, n=16,079）發現，監測術後心肌肌鈣蛋白可以幫助我們預測不良心血管結果。更重要的是，低濃度的心肌肌鈣蛋白—之前被認為是正常的，目前發現是手術後30天致死的一項獨立預測因素。現在有大量的生物學理論、非手術人群中的臨床試驗的證據，以及我們的研究數據表明，非常低濃度的心肌肌鈣蛋白可能提示了可逆的心肌損傷。這一發現對於我們預防術後心血管並發症的策略是一個模式的轉變，高靈敏度的心肌肌鈣蛋白的術後監測，使得圍手術期間醫生可以確定病人的風險，並且及時進行干預，例如給予抗血小板藥物和抗心絞痛藥物。因此，需要一項研究來確定在非心臟大手術中，監測高靈敏度的心肌肌鈣蛋白對於預防術後心血管並發症的預後意義。 我們計劃進行一項國際性的、多中心的、大樣本量的前瞻性隊列研究，對10,000名接受非心臟大手術的病人進行研究，從而對手術後30天和12個月，高靈敏度的心肌肌鈣蛋白和心血管並發症之間關係，分別進行研究。我們研究的另一個目的，是為了確定心肌肌鈣蛋白的閾值濃度，超過這個數字，臨床醫生應開始進行干預。我們同樣要探索從術前的基線值開始，心肌肌鈣蛋白濃度的改變對於預測術後心血管並發症發生的意義。 本次研究的發現將會對社會和經濟有很重要的意義。如果正如我們所認為的，我們的研究結果可以確定心肌肌鈣蛋白作為早期心肌損傷的一個預測因子，那麼這一發現將會在世界範圍內使得圍手術期間的用藥發生根本的改變。需要特別注意的是，監測高靈敏度的心肌肌鈣蛋白應當納入手術後常規護理中。未來的研究必須制定合理的計劃來管理這些存在高風險的病人。

461412.label: Realisation of objectives
461412.value: We have completed an international, multicenter, prospective cohort study to evaluate the clinical utility of perioperative cardiac tropoinin monitoring in adult patients undergoing noncardiac surgery. Between January 2013 and December 2014, we have recruited a total of 22,609 patients in 23 centres from 13 countries in North and South America, Africa, Asia, Australia, and Europe. In Hong Kong, a total of 2,011 patients were enrolled to the study. In the study, we included a representative sample of patients, ≥ 45 years, undergoing an elective or urgent/emergent surgery, day or night-time surgery, and weekday or weekend surgery and required at least an overnight admission. Overall, 71.2% of all eligible patients were consented and included in the study. Follow-up was completed in 99.7% of patients. In all patients, we measured plasma cardiac troponin concentration during the first 3 days after surgery. In the study, the 30-day mortality was 1.4% [95% confidence intervals (CI): 1.3-1.6%], myocardial infarction occurred in 9.0% of patients, sepsis in 5.4%, stroke in 0.5% and pulmonary embolism 0.6%. The 12-month death rate was 6.2% (95%CI: 5.7-6.8). The rates are higher than we anticipated, and hence the study has suffiucient power to evaluate the association between cardiac troponin concentration and death or major cardiac events. We have adopted the modified Mazumdar approach and determined the threshold cardiac troponin value that increase the risk of death using the Cox regression model at 30-day and also at 12-month after surgery.

461412.label: Major findings and research outcome
461412.value: In the study, we evaluated the threshold of postoperative cardiac troponin concentration that predicted death at 30 days by comparing with a reference group of patients with peak troponin concentration ≤ 5 ng/L. Multivariate analysis demonstrated that peak cardiac troponin concentration ≥ 20 ng/L occurred in 24.0% of patients and was associated with higher 30-day mortality and major cardiac events (Objective 1). Specifically, the adjusted hazard ratio (95%CI) for patients with peak cardiac troponin concentration of 21-64 ng/L was 2.33 (1.02-5.34). At cardiac troponin concentration 65-999 ng/L, it was 7.01 (3.05-16.11) and when cardiac troponin concentrations was ≥ 1000 ng/L, the hazard ratio increased to 21.24 (8.1.9-55.12), Objective 2. Patients with a peak troponin concentration  5, 21-64, 65-999 ng/L had 30-day mortality rates of 0.1%, 3.0%, 9.2%, and 28.1%, respectively. The model that assessed changes between cardiac troponin measurements demonstrated that an absolute change of ≥ 5 ng/L independently increased the risk of 30-day mortality, adjusted hazard ratio (95%CI): 4.70 (3.53-6.27), Objective 3. At 12-month follow-up, cardiac roponin elevation ≥ 20 ng/L was associated higher mortality [adjusted hazard ratio (95%CI): 2.61 (2.05-3.33)], higher rate of major vascular event 3.36 (2.55-4.46) and sepsis 2.98 (2.26-3.92), Objective 4. These data suggested that elevation of cardiac troponin concentrations (≥ 20 ng/L) during the first 3 days after noncardiac surgery is strongly associated with 30-day and 12-month mortality. We have therefore defined the term Myocardial Injury after Noncardiac Surgery (MINS) as an elevation of cardiac troponin concentration that is presumed to be caused by ischemia. MINS is prognostic relevant and is an independent predictor of postoperative mortality (Anesthesiology 2014; 120: 564-78). Perioperative troponin monitoring is also effective in allowing physicians to avoid missing significant myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery. Monitoring of cardiac troponin after surgery is now recommended in high risk patients according to the updated universal definition of myocardial infarction.

461412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
461412.value: Myocardial Injury after Noncardiac Surgery (MINS) is prognostic important and is an independent risk factor for mortality. Although our findings are encouraging, they are derived from observational data. There is a need to conduct large definitive clinical trials to determine whether interventions that minimize postoperative cardiac troponin concentration will improve morbidity and mortality after noncardiac surgery. Our data are evaluated the clinical utility of cardiac troponin monitoring in noncardiac surgery. It is not known if the cardiac troponin monitoring helps to identify clinically significant myocardial injury after cardiac surgery. A large observational study in 5,000 patients having cardiac surgery is now ongoing to determine the utility of cardiac troponin monitoring in cardiac surgery (supported by GRF14101414).

461412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
461412.value: Early detection of injury to the heart is important in identifying patients at risk of death and heart failure after surgery. In the non-operative population, monitoring of an enzyme in the heart, cardiac troponin, predicts major adverse events during longitudinal follow-up. In an international, multicenter, prospective cohort study of > 20,000 patients, we determined the prognostic relevant threshold and the utility of cardiac troponin monitoring to predict death at 30 days and one year after surgery. In the study, we found that even at low concentration, cardiac troponin was found to be strongly associated with morbidity and mortality at 30 days and one year after surgery. Our research showed that cardiac troponin is a sensitive biomarker and hence troponin monitoring will facilitate early detection of significant injury to the heart and allow the attending physicians to initiate timely treatment. Based on our findings, routine monitoring of cardiac troponin has been incorporated to international guidelines for the management of high-risk surgical patients.

461612.label: Project Objectives
461612.value: In Nogo-A knockout (KO) embryos, Nogo-B may be up-regulated as reported in the adult brain. To test whether similar changes occur prenatally, Nogo isoform expression at the ventral midline of the optic pathway and the spinal cord will be examined in Nogo-A KO embryos using antibody Bianca and 11C7, which recognizes Nogo-A/B and Nogo-A, respectively. These results form the basis for later studies on Nogo function. Preliminary findings have shown that Nogo-A/B is expressed on axons and radial glia in the optic and spinal commissural pathways. Blocking Nogo/NgR signaling produces routing abnormalities in the chiasm and the floor plate. If Nogo-A is involved in these processes, the axon crossing will be impeded in the mutants. To test this, we will investigate whether axon routing in these pathways is affected in the Nogo-A mutants. Nogo-B is present at the midline. It may interact with Nogo-B specific receptor (NGBR), in addition to NgR, characterized in endothelial cells. It is possible that NGBR is expressed in developing neurons and mediates the response to Nogo-B at the midline. To test this hypothesis, expression of NGBR will be investigated in the optic pathway and spinal commissural pathway in mouse embryos. Our preliminary findings in co-culture of floor plate and spinal cord explants have suggested that Nogo may act as a diffusible molecule to inhibit growth of post-commissural axons. To further characterize the role of Nogo-A in this action, we will investigate neurite outgrowth from the spinal cord in a co-culture system with floor plate isolated from wild-type or Nogo-A KO embryos. The window when Nogo is released will be determined by using floor plates isolated at different prenatal stages. The responses of pre- and post-commissural axons will be examined. The contribution of Nogo-B in this process will be examined by co-culturing spinal cord explants with floor plate transfected with shRNA that knock-downs Nogo-A/B. If Nogo acts as a diffusible factor to influence spinal neurite growth, it should be present in the supernatant of floor plate cultures and be able to suppress post-commissural axon growth. To test these, we will examine whether soluble form of Nogo exists in conditioned medium of floor plate culture, using Western blot analysis and mass spectroscopy. The conditioned medium will be examined in spinal cord explants for its suppressing effect on post-commissural axons. Moreover, since NgR is present at a basal level in pre-commissural axons, it is possible that NgR is upregulated by binding to diffusible Nogo when the axons approach the midline. To test this possibility, NgR expression will be examined in single spinal commissural neurons cultured with floor plate conditioned medium. In addition to the spinal commissural system, Nogo may serve also as a diffusible molecule in the chiasm. In order to test whether diffusible form of Nogo is involved in inhibitory influences of the chiasm to retinal axon growth, we will examine neurite outgrowth from retinal explants co-cultured with the optic chiasm, and determine whether the inhibition is alleviated by blocking Nogo signaling with receptor antagonist or genetic manipulations of Nogo levels in the chiasm. These results will reaffirm the diffusible nature of Nogo in the control of midline crossing.

461612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
461612.value: Nogo is best known as a myelin associated protein that discourages axon regeneration in the adult central nervous system. It is also expressed in neurons and glial cells during prenatal development, but its roles in neural development are largely unknown. Preliminary findings in our laboratory have shown that two Nogo isoforms (-A and –B) are expressed abundantly on radial glia at the ventral midline of the optic pathway and the floor plate of the spinal cord. The receptor for Nogo, NgR, is expressed on axons that grow across the midline, suggesting a potential role for Nogo/NgR signaling in midline guidance. However, this interaction is complicated by the expression of Nogo-A on the axons as well as the midline glia. In this proposal, we will dissect the functional role of Nogo in axon guidance at the ventral midline, using a transgenic mouse in which Nogo-A is not expressed to investigate the role of Nogo-A in midline crossing. Since Nogo-B has been reported to be up-regulated in brain of adult mutant, we will characterize expression of other Nogo isoforms at the ventral midline of Nogo-A knockout embryos, using immunocytochemistry and Western blotting analysis. Routing abnormalities of axons in the optic chiasm and the spinal cord will be described in the mutant embryos, using neuronal tracing techniques and confocal microscopy. The receptor of Nogo-B will also be examined for its potential role in these guidance processes. In second part of the proposal, we aim to determine whether floor plate derived Nogo may act as a diffusible factor to inhibit growth of post-commissural axons. We will characterize this interaction, using floor plate and spinal cord explants isolated from wild-type and Nogo-A mutants, and floor plates with Nogo-B knock-downed using shRNA. The diffusible nature of Nogo will be further confirmed in the optic pathway, using a coculture system of chiasm and retinal explants. The soluble form of Nogo will be obtained from conditioned medium prepared from floor plate cultures and characterized by Western blots and mass spectroscopy. The effects of this conditioned medium on the growth of post-commissural neurites and the expression of NgR in the pre-commissural neurons will be investigated. Results of these studies will provide insights into the biological role of Nogo and its signaling in neural development, which in turn may improve Nogo related treatments to promote regeneration in diseased and damaged nervous system. Nogo是一種最廣為人知的髓鞘相關蛋白，在成人的中樞神經系統中阻止軸突再生。這蛋白分子也表現在胚胎神經元和神經膠質細胞裏，但其在神經發育中的作很大程度是未知的。在我們實驗室的初步實驗結果表明，兩種異構體NOGO-A和-B大量表達在視神經的中線和脊髓底板的放射狀膠質細胞中。Nogo受體NGR表達於正越過中線的軸突中，意味著一個NOGO/NGR信號傳遞在中線引導軸突生長的潛在作用。然而，Nogo-A亦表達於軸突中，令這作用更顯複雜。在此研究中，我們將剖析Nogo在腹中線軸突導向的作用。我們將利用轉基因小鼠，其中的Nogo-A表達被敲除，檢視Nogo-A在軸突通過中線的作用。由於Nogo-B的表達會在成年的Nogo-A突變動物中被上調，我們將運用免疫組化和Western分析檢視其他Nogo亞型在Nogo-A基因敲除胚胎的表達。在突變的胚胎中，我們會運用神經元跟蹤技術和共聚焦顯微鏡，觀察視交叉和脊髓的異常軸突生長。Nogo-B受體在這過程中的表達亦會被檢視。在第二部分的研究，我們的目標是確定底板Nogo是否可以作為一種可擴散因子，抑制已過中線軸突的生長。我們將深入研究這種作用，利用從正常和Nogo-A突變體分離出的底板和脊髓，以及經shRNA處理減少Nogo-B表達的底板。 此外，利用視交叉及視網膜外植體的共存培育系統，Nogo的擴散作用會進一步在視神經系統中確應。從製備的底板條件培養基中，可溶性Nogo將被分離，再通過Western blot和質譜分析其特徵和序列。這個條件培養液對神經軸突生長和脊髓連合神經元的NgR表達將被檢測。這些實驗結果對Nogo在神經發育中的功能提供重要信息，這可應用於發展Nogo相關的治療方法，改善腦部病變和受創後的神經再生。

461612.label: Realisation of objectives
461612.value: 1. Expression of Nogo isoforms in Nogo-A knockout (KO) mice. The antibody Bianca and 11C7 (kindly provided by Prof. Martin Schwab, University of Zurich) were used to characterize the type of Nogo isoform at the midline of the optic chiasm and the ventral midline of the spinal cord in mouse embryos. Bianca recognizes both Nogo-A and –B, whilst 11C7 binds specifically to Nogo-A. In E14 wild-type embryos, both Bianca and 11C7 stained the neuroepithelial cells in the retina and optic axons in the optic nerve and chiasm. At the chiasmatic midline, Bianca stained prominently the midline radial glial cells whereas the optic axons were stained preferentially with 11C7. In E14 Nogo-A KO embryos, intense staining of Nogo-B was found on the midline glia, suggesting a role of Nogo-B in guiding axon growth at the midline of the optic pathway. Expression of Nogo isoforms was also investigated in the spinal cord of mouse embryos. In wild-type embryos, from E11-E14 when commissural axons are crossing the midline, Bianca staining was localized in the ventral horn neurons and the radial glial cells at the floor plate. Nogo-A was localized on the commissural axons, and is particularly strong in the ventral funiculus. However, no detectable staining of Nogo-A was found at the floor plate, indicating that the Nogo on the radial glial cells at the ventral midline is predominately Nogo-B. Staining of Bianca in Nogo-A KO spinal cord revealed a clear glial raphe, lending further support to the localization of Nogo-B on the midline glia of spinal cord. Furthermore, we have investigated the role of protein kinase-C (PKC), a downstream signaling molecule of Nogo receptor, on axon routing at the mouse optic chiasm. The major findings showed that the conventional PKC isoforms were the major forms present in optic axons at the chiasm. Suppressing these PKC activities with Ro-32-0432 reduced formation of ipsilateral projection, suggesting a crucial function of PKC mediated inhibitory mechanisms, which is known to be activated by Nogo, to the development of partial decussation in the optic pathway. These results support further that Nogo signaling is involved in midline crossing of axons at the chiasm. 2. Axon routing at the optic chiasm and floor plate of spinal cord in Nogo-A mutants. To investigate the routing of axons at the floor plate of spinal cord, a slice preparation of mid-thoracic cord was made from E12 mouse embryo, when active crossing processes are taking place. In wild type preparations, commissural axons labeled by DiI were observed in the floor plate. Many axons have made a turn towards the cranial direction immediately after crossing the floor plate. This crossing pattern was reduced when Nogo receptor signaling was interrupted by the NgR receptor antagonist NEP1-40, but was not affected in the absence of Nogo-A in KO preparations. These findings suggest that midline crossing of the commissural axons is controlled by Nogo-B at the floor plate. The routing pattern of axons in the optic chiasm was investigated in Nogo-A KO mice. The results showed that absence of Nogo-A did not generate detectable abnormality in crossing of the early axons in the chiasm, nor affect the formation of ipsilateral projecting. We concluded that the chiasm routing of optic axons are not dependent on Nogo-A, but likely relies on Nogo-B that is expressed abundantly at the chiasmatic midline as shown in the current study. We have also investigated Nogo-A expression in the mouse optic tract. Immunostaining revealed a strong expression of Nogo-A in superficial regions of the optic tract, where the newly arrived optic axons are resided. Perturbing Nogo-A function with either blocking antibody or NEP1-40 resulted in a shift of newly generated axons and growth cones from the superficial to the whole depth of the optic tract, suggesting Nogo-A is involved in the age-related fiber arrangement in the optic tract. 3. Expression of Nogo-B receptor in the spinal commissural pathway. Nogo-B receptor (NGBR) was examined in mouse spinal cord sections using an antibody form Abcam (ab47080, USA). In E11 spinal cord, NGBR was localized on the ventricular cells around the central lumen and neuroepithelial cells in the mantle layer. Precommissural axons and axons in the floor plate expressed low levels of NGBR. However, the expression was upregulated in these axons when they enter the ventral funiculus. Similar patterns of expression was observed in E12 spinal cord. At E13, NGBR was localized widely in all structures throughout the spinal cord, with the most intense staining in the ventral horn neurons and the radial glial cells at the ventral midline. These patterns suggest a stage specific expression of NGBR. The early axonal expression may mediate decussation of axons at the midline, whereas the late glial expression may prevent recrossing of axons that express high level of Nogo-B in the ventral funiculus. 4. Effect of Nogo on neurite outgrowth from spinal cord. In co-culture experiments using collagen gel, floor plate showed a strong inhibitory effect on the extension of post-commissural neurites from the spinal cord. This effect was abolished by the NgR antagonist peptide NEP1-40. Similar Inhibition of neurite growth was not observed in the pre-commissural neurites when they were grown with the floor plate, nor in post-commissural neurites grown with floor plate derived from Nogo-A knockout embryos. The results provide strong support to the involvement of Nogo-B in mediating the response to floor plate, and showed that Nogo serves its axon growth regulatory function through a diffusible mean. 5. Nogo as a diffusible factor to spinal neurites. The diffusible factors were characterized from conditioned medium of E13 floor plates, and analyzed by Western blot using Bianca antibody. The results showed a truncated form of Nogo with molecular weight of 37 kDa was produced and secreted by the floor plate, which represents probably a cleaved product of Nogo-B in the midline radial glial cells that mediates the diffusible effect to commissural axon growth. 6. Effect of diffusible Nogo from the optic chiasm to retinal neurite outgrowth. Retinal explants were grown with chiasm of E14 embryos in collagen gel. Unlike the spinal cord commissural axons, retinal neurites from either ventral temporal and dorsal nasal retina were able to grow towards the chiasm explant. Blocking of NgR function with NEP1-40 did not show any detectable influence to neurite growth from the retina.

461612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
461612.value: These experiments provide evidences that Nogo-B is the isoform expressed by the midline glia that is likely mediating axon growth in the optic pathway and spinal commissural pathway, and show for the first time Nogo exerts it axon growth regulating effects as a diffusible factor. Further works should be carried out to investigate the diffusible Nogo, how it is generated from the floor plate glial cells and what the functions are in patterning axons in the spinal cord. These issues should be addressed in future experiments.

461612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
461612.value: Nogo is best known as a myelin associated protein that discourages axon regeneration in the adult central nervous system. However, its functions in developing brain are largely unknown. Using immunohistochemistry we have shown Nogo isoforms -A and –B are expressed abundantly on axons in the optic and spinal pathway in mouse embryos. However, Nogo-B is the predominant at the midline, which may regulate crossing of axons that carry Nogo receptor NgR. Blocking NgR function with NEP1-40 strongly impedes the crossing of spinal axons at the floor plate, whilst the crossing is not affected in the absence of Nogo-A in knockout mutants. The crossing of axons in the optic chiasm is not affected in the mutants, supporting that the midline crossing process does not require Nogo-A. However, treatment with NEP1-40 or Nogo-A blocking antibody abolishes the age-related fiber arrangement in the optic tract, indicating Nogo-A is required in guiding axon growth in the optic tract. In culture preparations, spinal axon growth is suppressed by factors released from floor plate. This inhibition is abolished by NEP1-40, but not by culturing with floor plate isolated from Nogo-A mutants. These results indicate that floor plate cells are able to secrete a diffusible form of Nogo to inhibit axon growth. Further analysis shows that a diffusible form of Nogo with molecular weight of 37 kD can be isolated from conditioned medium of floor plates. This novel form of Nogo is likely produced as a cleaved product of Nogo-B from the floor plate. These findings indicate a specific role of Nogo-B at the midline in controlling axon crossing in different regions of the central nervous system.

461712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
461712.value: Diabetes is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. Due to its intricate interplay of genetic, cultural and environmental factors, diabetes is a classic complex disease. A better understanding of the etiology of Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is paramount, as there is a lack of effective preventive measures and therapeutic strategies. Recent advent of high-throughput genotyping technologies has provided the underpinning for genome-wide population-based studies to identify genetic variants that are associated with predisposition to the disease. More than 40 genetic susceptibility loci have been reported thus far from nearly 30 genome-wide association studies (GWAS). These genetic variants, however, confer only a small increase in relative risk, accounting for less than 10% of the estimated genetic contribution to T2D predisposition. Alternative approaches have been put forth to identify the so-termed “missing heritability”, such as the use of whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing to identify and subsequently assess the roles of alleles with frequencies much lower than those examined by GWAS, assessing the roles of structural variations, and finally better quantitative phenotyping. In the present proposal, we proposed a whole-transcriptome analysis to identify biomarkers to complement and extend on the genetic loci identified by GWAS. Our preliminary study of a Chinese family trio with an affected mother-daughter pair and an unaffected father have revealed altered gene expression levels and alternative mRNA splicing between the unaffected and affected datasets. While a few of the alterations overlapped with some of the well-known susceptibility genes, a majority of these isoforms have not been previously reported. We then extended our study to peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) extracted from unrelated individuals and confirmed some of these candidates. We also found potential diabetes-associated differences in the small or non-coding components of the transcriptome. Making use of the direct and complete tabulation of the transcriptome made possible by the new generation DNA sequencers, we shall target additional different tissue types: muscle or adipose tissues biopsy samples. The proposed study shall focus on two key questions: 1) what are the molecular phenotypes of T2D at the transcript level; and 2) whether T2D-associated phenotypes are in concordance with alterations in the transcriptome. Insights gained from this study should provide new molecular understandings of disease, leading to the discovery of new diagnostic biomarkers and molecular targets for therapeutic intervention. 糖尿病是一種十分普遍、可引致死亡的典型複雜疾病。它的形成來自於基因、文化和環境因素之間錯鏦複雜的相互影響。現時由於缺乏有效的預防和治療手段，二型糖尿病（T2D）的病理需要得到更深入研究。高通量基因分型技術為基因組基因變異檢測提供了研究基礎。現時，接近30個全基因組相關性研究（Genome-wide association studies, GWAS）共報告了超過40個二型糖尿病遺傳的相關基因位點（candidate loci）。然而，這些基因變異一共只解釋了不到百分之十的二型糖尿病患者因遺傳因素所帶來的患病風險的少量提升。因此，一些另類方法被提出及採用於尋找這些所謂“失落的遺傳特質”（missing heritability），例如通過全基因組測序或全外顯子測序尋找並檢驗那些比在GWAS研究中發現與二型糖尿病相關的基因頻率更低的等位基因、尋找並檢驗結構性基因變化的作用、以及提升量化基因分型技術。在此計畫書中，我們提出以全轉錄組分析以鑒定新的生物標記，並以此補充和完善通過全基因關聯研究取得的成果。我們在初步研究中使用了由患病的母親和女兒以及健康的父親所組成的父─母─女三聯體家系。該研究表明了患病者與未患病者在信使核糖核酸(mRNA)選擇性剪切存在差異。在全轉錄組分析中所發現的表達差異，只有一小部分基因與已知的二型糖尿病相關基因位點不謀而合，而其餘大部分的之前均沒有被報導過。我們將研究擴展到從非血緣關連的個體中提取的外周血單核細胞（PBMCs）並且核實了其中的部分的相關基因。最後，我們在轉錄組中也發現了一些潛在與糖尿病相關，分子質量較小的非編碼核糖核酸。新一代核酸測序儀技術能直接取得完整的轉錄數據，我們可以利用此優點在其他不同類型的組織進行全轉錄組分析研究，比如肌肉或者脂肪的活體組織樣本。這個研究擬議的主要關注點有兩個：1）在轉錄組的層面上，T2D的分子表徵到底是什麼？2）轉錄組中的表達差異與T2D的表型是否有著相互的關係。從這個研究中得到的經驗可以深化人類對於T2D在分子生物學領域的認識，從而有助於發現新的診斷性的分子標記物和用於治療性干預的分子標靶。

461712.label: Realisation of objectives
461712.value: Revised Objectives 1 and 2 o The project started with RNA extraction from PBMCs collected from case-control Type 2 diabetes subjects, including 10 individuals with T2D and 10 without T2D; o With a clinical research ethics approval, adipose tissues (visceral and subcutaneous) were extracted from recruited subjects, including 12 individuals with T2D and 13 controls without T2D. Total RNA was treated with RiboZero to remove rRNA following the manufacturer’s protocol; o Strand-specific RNA-sequencing was performed on the Illumina platform using the TruSeq stranded RNA-sequencing method. At least 5Gb (and most are 10Gb) of sequencing data was generated for each sample; o Since PBMCs (1) yield more differentially-expressed and spliced genes than adipose tissues; and (2) is obtained from noninvasive means when compared with tissue biopsies, we first conducted the analysis using PBMCs data. Revised Objectives 3 and 4 o Sequencing reads were processed such that all read-pairs with sequences equal to or longer than 35bp on both sides after trimming were retained. Quality-trimmed reads were mapped onto the human genome (hg19) by STAR v.2.3.0e. Gene expression in terms of FPKM and relative abundance of alternatively-spliced transcripts was calculated by Cuffinks v.2.2.1. Differential gene expression was analysed using DESeq2, and genes with Benjamini and Hochberg multiple-testing adjusted p < 0.05 with absolute log2 fold-change > 0.75 were considered to be significant; o In PBMCs, 1,395 differentially-expressed genes and 271 differentially-spliced genes were identified. Whereas in adipose tissues, 895 genes were differentially-expressed and none of the genes were significantly differential-spliced. Given that PBMCs demonstrated a more significant level of transcriptome changes in response to T2D, we chose to focus our analysis mainly on PBMCs; o We adopted an interactome analysis approach, and derived a gene set whereby their expression changes are associated with T2D. We called this T2D-interactome (T2Di) signature; o The T2Di signature was cross-validated with a diverse array of external datasets and independent case-control cohort. External datasets include (1) the largest trans-ethnic T2D GWAS – the DIAbetes Genetics Replication And Meta-analysis (DIAGRAM) study; (2) analysis of genomic properties and meta-analysis with expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) studies including the Multiple Tissue Human Expression Resource Consortium (MuTHER) and Genotype-Tissue Expression Project (GTEx); (3) clinical traits; (4) druggability analysis; and (5), differential gene expressions were further validated by both in-house qPCR replication and external diabetes-related tissues expression data. These results are summarized as follows: o (1) We used the DIAGRAM database to show that our T2Di signature was statistically enriched with low frequency disease-susceptibility variants, suggesting these genes (after excluding established T2D GWAS genes) were enriched with variants associated with T2D, which were not discovered in the original DIAGRAM GWAS; o (2) Established T2D associated genetic variants discovered by GWAS studies deposited in GWAS Catalogue (T2D-GWAS variants) are mostly located within transcriptional regulatory regions, including promoters and enhancers, which are enriched with Expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) property. Therefore, if the T2Di signature discovered in this study is genuinely related to T2D, this T2Di signature gene set is expected to possess properties similar to T2D-GWAS variants. Firstly we affirmed a significant fraction (49.4%; 270/547) genome-wide significant SNPs in the DIAGRAM study (p < 5.00E-8) overlaps with regulatory regions (e.g. transcription factor binding, DNase I hypersensitivity, sequence motif, eQTL, or a combination of them). Similarly, SNPs in perfect linkage disequilibrium (LD) with the T2D-GWAS variants were also enriched in regulatory elements (p = 3.20E-3). o Secondly, we observed enrichment of SNPs in perfect LD with our T2Di signature (75.6%; 875/1157, p = 1.00E-06) overlapped with regulatory elements. We then sought to identify tissue-specific enrichment of regulatory elements in SNPs that were in perfect LD with the T2Di signature. We found that the established T2D-associated variants (in both the GWAS Catalogue and DIAGRAM) satisfying genome-wide significance were enriched in fetal regulatory elements, including fetal intestine, muscle and stomach. It is known that enrichment of GWAS variants in fetal regulatory elements is commonly seen in complex diseases of which growth trajectory plays important pathophysiological roles. In line with such notion, the SNPs in perfect LD with our T2Di signature (a gene based study) were also enriched in regulatory variants in fetal intestine, muscle and stomach, in addition to blood and thymus. o Among the 420 genes in the T2Di signature, 43.3% (182/420) overlapped with TF binding sites together with DNase I peaks. Among them, 17.6% (32/182) were rSNP/eQTL signals with genome-wide significance (p = 5.00E-8) in DIAGRAM or in perfect LD to these DIAGRAM SNPs. These SNPs were associated with expression changes in GTEx (skeletal muscle, whole blood and subcutaneous Fat) and MuTHER (lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCL) and fat). T2Di signature is in perfect LD to DIAGRAM variants with p-values between 7.60E-5 and 3.60E-2 were also enriched in rSNP/eQTL property. The T2Di signature possessed many significant eQTL loci including those expressed in LCL and fat tissue. Finally, we combined cis- and trans- eQTLs and GWAS p-values to assess our T2Di signature. Using the Sherlock statistical framework, we identified 17 (24.3%; 17/70) DIAGRAM-genes to be associated with T2D (p < 0.05) (Fisher p-value for enrichment: 3.32-5) compared to enrichment of 88 genes in the T2Di signature with p < 0.05 (20.9%; 88/420) (Fisher p-value for enrichment: 5.40E-14). We concluded that our T2Di signature possess genomic properties similar to T2D-GWAS variants; o (3) Some of genes in the T2Di signature overlapped with targets of FDA-approved anti-diabetic drugs. For example, NF-kB, PPARD, MAOB and RARA are downstream targets of Thiazolidinedione (TZDs) while P1K3 pathway, IRS1 and IRS2 are that of insulin. Near these known drug targets (first degree connection), two genes in the T2Di signature, namely NCOR2 and PDGFR, are potential T2D drug targets. Using the Drug Gene Interaction Database and manual literature curation, we further identified possible druggable targets including ADORA1/2, DRD4, IL2RB, THRA, TNNC1, TSPO, MMP1 and TLR8; o (4) Since the same gene(s) or biological pathway can be involved in different but related diseases, protein-protein interactions (PPI) and pathophysiological pathways tend to exhibit overlapping symptoms and comorbidity. We expected the T2Di signature to be enriched in genes related to other T2D-associated comorbidities and symptomatology. To test this hypothesis, we mapped the genes to OMIM and GWAS disease genes, and performed disease comorbidity analysis using the U.S. Medicare disease history record, which comprises more than 31 million individuals. Our analysis showed that T2D patients had a relative risk ≥ 1.5 (99% confidence interval >1.0) increased for 70 diseases (ICD-9 codes). Comorbidity analysis of these disease-associated genes indicated that the T2Di signature was enriched with genes associated with 27 comorbid diseases, including male urogenital diseases (RR: 1.86, enrichment p = 3.18E-2, Fisher’s exact test), gastroenteritis (RR: 1.51, enrichment p = 1.77E-3, Fisher’s exact test) and cardiomyopathy (RR: 1.74, enrichment p = 3.66E-3, Fisher’s exact test). Using the ‘diseases symptoms similarity’ captured by large-scale medical bibliographic record, there were also high similarities between the T2Di signature and atherosclerosis (similarity score: 0.74) and male infertility (similarity score: 0.45). The correlations of these comorbidities and symptomatology within the context of PPI with enrichment of shared genomic signatures supported the validity of our T2Di signature. o The T2Di signature was cross-validated with expression data of pancreatic islet, muscle and liver. Expression of selected genes (CEBPB, SREBF1, MLST8, SRF, SRRT and SLC12A9) were confirmed by qPCR in PBMCs obtained from an independent cohort of 66 T2D and 66 control subjects.

461712.label: Major findings and research outcome
461712.value: Case-control comparison of T2D transcriptome identified 1,395 differentially-expressed genes. A tissue-specific interactome of PBMCs was constructed, and these 1,395 differentially-expressed genes were analyzed using a multi-method strategy. A T2D-interactome (T2Di) signature, which consists of 420 genes that is associated with T2D-related comorbidity and symptoms and implicated in inflammation, adipogenesis, protein phosphorylation and hormonal secretion, was developed. The T2Di signature discovered in this project were enriched in pathogenic cell type-specific regulatory elements related to fetal development, immunity and eQTL. These signatures explained part of the residual associations within currently the largest trans-ethnic T2D GWAS – the DIAbetes Genetics Replication And Meta-analysis (DIAGRAM) study, supporting our premise that transcriptome analysis could act as an important complementary approach to GWAS in elucidation of T2D heterogeneity. This study also revealed a novel locus near a well-established GWAS loci AChE, in which SRRT interacts with JAZF1, a T2D-GWAS gene implicated in pancreatic function. The T2Di signature also included known anti-diabetic drug targets (e.g. PPARD, MAOB) and possible druggable targets (e.g. NCOR2, PDGFR). The T2Di signature was cross-validated by an orthogonal computational method, and cross-compared with expression data of pancreatic islet, muscle and liver. Finally, expression differences of selected genes within the signature were experimentally validated in PBMCs from an independent cohort. By combining prior knowledge and transcriptome analysis, we have constructed an interactome to investigate the multi-layered regulatory pathways in T2D. The above-mentioned result was published as reference 2 in Part C (Research Output). We conducted pilot analysis for further research as described in section 6.2. Although strong DNA methylation at promoters is widely recognized to be associated with transcriptional repression, many aspects of DNA methylation remain not fully understood, including the quantitative relationships between DNA methylation and expression levels, as well as relative contribution between promoter and gene body methylation. We conducted an integrated analysis using both whole-genome bisulfite sequencing and RNA-sequencing data. We found that DNA methylation is indicative of the expression class of a gene in general, but strikingly, gene body methylation is a better indicator than promoter methylation. Our results suggest that DNA methylation outside of promoters also plays critical roles in gene regulation. The above-mentioned result was published as reference 1 in Part C (Research Output).

461712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
461712.value: Enlightened by our previous methylation study on DM trios, we set out to compare the methylome, as well as the transcriptome profiles of adipocytes, using a pilot cohort of 12 obese T2D and 13 non-T2D obese patients (BMI > 30 kg/m2). This extended study is expected to inform the key DM pathogenesis pathways under an obese background. After filtering based on an adjusted p value <0.1 and delta β > 0.1, 14 methylation loci were found to be significant. The potential role of these loci are now being investigated. Findings from this study is expected to help prioritize treatments for obese patients, such as metabolic surgery, such that those who are more likely to have DM will receive treatment earlier.

461712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
461712.value: Despite global efforts in establishing the heritability of type 2 diabetes, current catalogue of GWAS variants account for only 10–15% of T2D incidences. An overall objective of this project is to investigate the “missing” genetic variants in T2D using a strand-specific RNA-sequencing approach. Our findings were currently reported in two publications at the moment. The first study described a T2D-interactome (T2Di) signature gene set, and the second publication focused on the contribution of gene-body methylation on transcriptional changes. Additional work is now being done on tissue-specific methylation and gene expression changes in the context of cases and controls in obese subjects. We believe new technologies would lead to new insights to the genetics of T2D, which currently is primarily based on traditional GWAS analysis. This RGC funding support has enabled us to contribute, and continue to pursue the understanding of missing heritability in T2D.

462112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
462112.value: 本專案旨在研究膳食中不同種類的膽固醇酯（CE）對倉鼠血漿總膽固醇（TC）、低密度脂蛋白（LDL）、高密度脂蛋白（HDL）和甘油三酯（TG）的影響。人群每天膳食攝入膽固醇量為400mg, 其中膽固醇酯占30%。膳食膽固醇具有增加人體血漿TC和低密度脂蛋白-膽固醇（LDL-C）濃度的作用，但不同種類的CE如何升高人體或動物血漿TC和LDL-C含量的機制目前尚不清楚。 本研究初步探討了膳食中游離膽固醇（C）、膽固醇棕櫚酸酯（CE-PA）、膽固醇硬脂酸酯（CE-SA）、膽固醇油酸酯（CE-OA）和膽固醇亞油酸酯（CE-LA）（2.6mmol/kg）對倉鼠血漿脂蛋白的組成及含量的影響。研究表明：1）不同種類的CE對血漿膽固醇升高的影響不同，其表現為CE-OA> CE-LA>C>CE-PA>CE-SA；2）同含有飽和脂肪酸（如棕櫚酸和硬脂酸）的CE相比，含不飽和脂肪酸（如油酸和亞油酸）的CE對血漿中膽固醇的升高有更強的作用；3）血漿膽固醇含量的增加受CE種類的影響變化較大，最高為331mg/dl（CE-OA），最低為220mg/dl（CE-SA）。綜上所述，有必要對膽固醇酯影響血漿脂蛋白的潛在機制進行研究。 此外，體外實驗發現，對不同種類的CE，胰腺膽固醇酯酶（PCE）將其水解為游離膽固醇的效率也不同：對CE-OA作用最強，CE-SA最弱。我們認為膽固醇的吸收受CE種類的影響，而CE只有被水解為游離膽固醇後才能被腸粘膜吸收。因此，PCE和激素敏感脂酶（HSL）對CE在腸道內的水解有決定性的意義。通過測定Km, Vmax和Kcat，本實驗將會研究PCE和HSL對不同CE的酶解效率。通過分別給予倉鼠單劑量放射標記14C-CE和14C-游離膽固醇飲食，定量其血漿中14C的量，從而測定CE在體內的吸收。另外，由於膽固醇的吸收會影響糞便固醇的組成，本實驗將會研究膳食膽固醇對糞便中性和酸性固醇含量的影響。膽固醇的吸收是一個複雜的過程，其相關蛋白的表達包括：NPC1L1轉運蛋白、醯基輔酶A：膽固醇醯基轉移酶2（ACAT2）、微粒體甘油三酯轉移蛋白（MTP）以及ABCG5/8。因此，本實驗將會研究膳食中不同CE對NPC1L1、ACAT2、MTP和ABCG5/8的基因調節作用。本課題旨在驗證不同種類CE的吸收對血漿中TC的升高有著決定性的作用。

462112.label: Realisation of objectives
462112.value: We have achieved all the objectives as stipulated in the proposal. Human diet contains both free cholesterol (C) and cholesteryl esters (CE) with the latter approximately accounting for up to 30%. Little is known how individual CE affects plasma total cholesterol (TC). There are four major CE species in human diet including cholesteryl palmitate (CP), cholesteryl stearate (CS), cholesteryl oleate (CO) and cholesteryl linoleate (CL). The overall objectives were to investigate the effect of CE species on plasma TC and the underlying mechanisms. Objective 1 was to study the TC-raising activity of four CE species using hamsters as an animal model. The hamsters were divided into five groups fed one of the five diets containing 2.6 mmol cholesterol (C), 2.6 mmol CP, 2.6 mmol CS, 2.6 mmol CO and 2.6 mmol CL, respectively. The experimental results showed that CS was least while CO was most potent in raising plasma TC. Objective 2 was to test the hypothesis that the hydrolysis rate of CE species in intestine before absorption was one of the factors accounting for varying plasma TC-raising activity of CE species. To mimic the hydrolysis process in the intestine, the mixture was prepared by mixing CE species, sodium phosphate buffer, sodium cholate and pancreatic cholesterol esterase. The experimental result proved our hypothesis that the hydrolysis rate was in an order of CO> >CL> CP> CS, correlating with their plasma TC-raising activity. Objective 3 was to study the cholesterol absorption using the cholesterol balance method in hamsters. The following equation was used to calculate the cholesterol absorption in hamsters fed one of the five diets: Cholesterol Absorption = [(Cholesterol Intake)-(Fecal Cholesterol + Its Derivative + Fecal Bile Acids)]/Cholesterol Intake. It was found that the absorption was in an order of C=CO>CL>CP>CS, correlating well with that of the hydrolysis rate and plasma-TC raising activity. Objectives 4-7 were to study the effect of dietary CE species on sterol transporters, enzymes and proteins involved in cholesterol absorption pathway including NPC1L1, ACAT 2, MTP and ABCG5/8. Real-time PCR was employed to quantify mRNA of intestinal NPC1L1, ABCG5/8, ACAT2, and MTP in hamsters fed the five diets. Results demonstrated that CS group had the least mRNA of intestinal NPC1L1 whereas C and CL hamsters had the highest mRNA levels. Similarly, the mRNA of intestinal MTP in CS was also the least while that in C and CL was the highest. CS group had the least mRNA of intestinal ACAT2. In contrast, C group had the highest mRNA of intestinal ACAT2. In addition, we also had studied the effect of CE species on intestinal ACAT-2 enzymatic activity. It was shown that CS was associated with a lowest activity of intestinal ACAT2. We had carried out additional experiments to study the effect of dietary CE species on protein masses of sterol regulatory element binding protein 2 (SREBP-2), cholesterol 7α-hydroxylase (CYP7A1), LDL receptor, and 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutary-CoA (HMGCoA) reductase, in order to understand completely the effect of individual CE species on cholesterol metabolism. It showed that dietary CS specie was associated with greater gene expression of CYP7A1 and LDL receptor. It was in agreement with the observation that dietary CS increased most the excretion of bile acids and had the lowest plasma TC raising activity. We also carried out additional experiments to study the interaction of β-sitosterol (a popular cholesterol-lowering supplement) with CE species versus with dietary free cholesterol (FC) in the intestinal absorption process. We choose CP as a representative CE species. Male hamsters were divided into five groups and fed one of the five diets containing no cholesterol (NC), 2.6 mmol cholesterol (C), 2.6 mmol cholesterol plus 2.6 mmol β-sitosterol (C+S), 2.6 mmol cholesteryl palmitate (CP), and 2.6 mmol CP plus 2.6 mmol β-sitosterol (CP+S), respectively, for 8 weeks. This additional experiment demonstrated in hamster model that diet containing CP was less potent in raising plasma TC compared with diet containing free cholesterol. β-Sitosterol could suppress the hypercholesterolemia induced by both a free cholesterol diet and a CP diet. We also carried out an additional experiment to study the cholesterol analogs on plasma TC. We synthesized two hydroxyl analogs namely cholesteryl 3β-ethoxy (3CE) and cholesteryl 3β-methoxy (3CM) and studied their effects on plasma TC compared with that of β-sitosterol (SI) in hamsters fed a high cholesterol diet. 3CM and 3CE are the methoxy and ethoxyl analogs of cholesterol. Results showed that SI at a dose of 0.1% could effectively reduce plasma TC by 18%, while 3CE and 3CM had no effect on plasma TC. It was concluded that analogs having the different side chains possessed plasma TC-lowering activity, while analogs or derivatives on the hydroxyl group had no hypocholesterolemic activity. In summary, the project has been successfully completed step by step as stipulated in the original proposal. Humans daily consume about 200-500 mg cholesterol with an approximate of 30% being present in form of cholesteryl esters. Although the data could not be directly extrapolated to what happen in humans, the present study was the first time to demonstrate that for a given amount, CE species had the varying plasma TC-raising activity. The apparent cholesterol absorption among the five CE species was in an order of C>CO>CL>CP>CS. It was evident that CS (cholesteryl stearate) had the poorest cholesterol absorption and thus had the lowest plasma TC raising activity. In contrast, CO had the highest cholesterol absorption and thus the highest plasma TC-raising activity. It was therefore concluded that CS specie had the least plasma TC-raising activity, mediated by its poor hydrolysis rate by PCE (pancreatic cholesterol esterase) and down-regulation of intestinal NPC1L1, ACAT2, and MTP gene expression involved in sterol absorption. The results of this project are significant and have generated 4 journal papers and 5 conference presentations. When this final report was prepared, PI suddently realized there was a typo in the RGC reference number quoted in these publications (462112 --> 461112) and apologize for such a careless mistake.

462112.label: Major findings and research outcome
462112.value: The first outcome of this project was to examine the effect of free cholesterol (C) and individual cholesteryl esters, CP, CS, CO and CL, on plasma TC, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and triacylglycerols (TG) in hamsters. Results showed that addition of CE species into diet at 0.1% (2.6 mmol) differently raised plasma TC concentrations with CO elevating plasma TC to 331 mg/dl while CS raising plasma TC only to 220 mg/dl. It was found that CS was a poor while CO was a good substrate of pancreatic cholesterol esterase. The fecal analysis showed CS-fed hamsters had the highest fecal cholesterol concentration while RT-PCR analysis found CS feeding was associated with down-regulations of intestinal NPC1L1 and ACAT2 as well as MTP, all of three encode the genes of transporters and enzymes involved in cholesterol absorption. It was evident that plasma PC-raising activity of CE species was partially governed by their hydrolysis rates in the intestine, and the relative low raising activity associated with CS was mediated by down-regulation of intestinal NPC1L1, ACAT2 and MTP. The results of this part has been published in the Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry (American Chemical Society journal). The second outcome of the present study was to examine plasma TC-reducing activity of β-sitosterol in free cholesterol (FC)-induced and cholesteryl palmitate (CP)-induced hypercholesterolemia. Male hamsters were divided into five groups and fed one of the five diets containing no cholesterol (NC), 2.6 mmol cholesterol (C), 2.6 mmol cholesterol plus 2.6 mmol β-sitosterol (C+S), 2.6 mmol CP, and 2.6 mmol CP plus 2.6 mmol β-sitosterol (CP+S), respectively. The major finding was that plasma TC-raising activity of dietary cholesterol was a function of its chemical forms in diet, and β-sitosterol could similarly suppress the hypercholesterolemia induced by both dietary FC and CP. The results from this part has been published in Food Chemistry (a key journal in the field of food science). The third outcome of the project was to test the effects of cholesteryl 3β-ethoxy (3CE) and cholesteryl 3β-methoxy (3CM) on plasma TC compared with that of β-sitosterol in hamsters, finding 3CM and 3CE had no effect while SI could reduce plasma TC. The major finding was that cholesterol analogs having the different side chains possessed plasma TC-lowering activity, while analogs or derivatives on the hydroxyl group had no hypocholesterolemic activity. This part has been published in Food & Function ( a Royal Society of Chemistry Journal).

462112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
462112.value: The present project investigated plasma TC-raising activity of different cholesteryl species with different fatty acid moieties, demonstrating that the fatty acid moieties affect their effects on plasma TC. This arouse our interest to study the effect of other cholesterol analogs on plasma cholesterol. For example, phytosterols differ from cholesterol only by one additional ethyl group (β-sitosterol) or methyl group (campesterol) at C24. Considering the tiny structural difference between cholesterol and phytosterols, the former can be absorbed at a rate of 55-60% while the latter only has an absorption of 2%. Phytosterols have been used as a healthy supplement in treatment of lipid disorder. By studying the relationship between the structure and TC-raising activity of sterols, we can develop a new medication in management of cholesterolemia.

462112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
462112.value: Humans consume about 300 mg cholesterol daily with up to 30% being cholesteryl esters (CE), i.e., a fatty acid esterified with a cholesterol. There are four major CE species in human diets including CP, CS, CO and CL. High consumption of free cholesterol elevates plasma TC and increases the risk of coronary heart diseases. However, little is known how individual CE species affect plasma TC. This study was to investigate the effect of individual CE species on plasma TC and the underlying mechanism in hamsters fed the free cholesterol or four CE species. It is known that CE species had to be hydrolyzed to a free cholesterol and a fatty acid before its absorption. Results demonstrated that CO was most while CS was least potent in raising plasma TC. This was because CS specie was poorly hydrolyzed by pancreatic cholesterol esterase (PCE), while CO was a better substrate of PCE. The project explains why individual CE species and some foods with a same amount of cholesterol have the varying plasma TC-raising activity.

463612.value: 轉錄因子Six1在腎纖維化中功能作用

463612.label: Project Objectives
463612.value: To determine the role of Six1 and its cofactor Eya1 in renal fibrosis. We will firstly characterize whether the expression of Six1 and Eya1 is related to the activation of renal TGF-beta/Smad signaling during renal fibrosis in mice. Then we will determine whether renal fibrosis in ligated kidneys will be reduced in Six1 heterozygous mice. Next, we determine the role of Six1 and its cofactor Eya1 in renal fibrosis by delivering Six1 and/or Eya1 expression plasmids into ligated kidneys of a mouse model of obstructive nephropathy. Finally, we will either overexpress or inhibit Six1 and/or Eya1 in tubular epithelial cells to validate the functional role of Six1 in TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis in vitro. To investigate the mechanism of how Six1 promotes TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis We determine whether Six1 promotes TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis by inducing TGF-beta Receptor I expression. We firstly examine whether suppression of TGF-beta Receptor I will abrogate Six1 promotion on TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis. We next investigate how Six1 promotes TGF-beta Receptor I expression during TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis. We will finally determine how Eya1 is involved in Six1 action on promoting TGF-beta Receptor I expression. To develop a therapeutic strategy for renal fibrosis by delivering Six1 and/or Eya1 KD plasmids into diseased kidneys We will determine the therapeutic potential of anti-Six1 approach for renal fibrosis in a mouse model of obstructive nephropathy. By an ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene delivery system, we will deliver knockdown plasmids of Six1 and/or Eya1 into ligated kidneys either immediately or at day 4 after ligation of ureter to determine whether suppression of Six1 and/or Eya1 will attenuate renal fibrosis.

463612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
463612.value: 腎臟纖維化是導致末期腎功能衰竭的共同通路。現在，腎纖維化的治療方法仍然非常有限，和效果不太理想。TGF-beta/Smad作為體內重要的信號調節通路，對腎臟纖維化過程具有關鍵作用。然而，由於TGF-beta的抗發炎特性，使用直接針對TGF-beta的治療可能會對免疫系統引起不良影響。因此，一個有效治療慢性腎病的方法是針對TGF-beta/Smad信號通路下游與纖維化相關的因子。 我們發現一種新而重要的初步調查結果，轉錄因子Six1在梗阻性腎病中的表達是上調，而且這上調是依賴TGF-beta信號的啟動。在腎小管上皮細胞中，過度表達的Six1會促進TGF-beta誘導的纖維化；相反地，壓抑Six的表達會抑制這種誘導。更重要的是，將Six1過度表達質粒轉染到腎臟能夠促進在梗阻性腎病動物模型中的腎臟纖維化。 這些新的研究結果強烈表明TGF-beta可能通過刺激Six1而導腎臟纖維化。此外，TGF-beta誘導Six1表達是取決於它的下游因子Smad3的，並且不是取決於Smad2，提示在TGF-beta/Smad3誘導Six1表達的一個新途徑。基於這些研究結果，我們假設Six1可能在調節TGF-beta誘導腎纖維化起重要的作用。 為了驗証這假設，我們首先在腎臟細胞中過表達或抑制Six1去測試Six1表達如何影響腎纖維化（具體目標1）。然後，我們將研究TGF-beta信號如何在腎纖維化過程中通過Smad2 / 3去調節Six1的表達（具體目標2）。最後，我們將使用超聲微泡介導的基因傳遞系統，將SIX1過度或壓抑質粒轉染到腎臟，以確定Six在梗阻性腎病的小鼠模型中的功能作用，及測試Six1在治療腎纖維化的潛力（具體目標3）。 確定SIX1在腎纖維化的致病作用會提供引發腎病的新機制。我們預測TGF-beta信號通路會是以它的下游因子(Smad3、Smad2和Smad7)去調節Six1的表達。值得一提的是，抑制SIX1在腎臟中的表達會抑制腎臟纖維化。雖然近年來在瞭解腎纖維化過程有新進展，但是目前還沒有一個成功抑制腎纖維化的策略。因此，我們迫切需要一個的防治腎纖維化的新策略。我們建議的研究結果將提供一個新穎及具有臨床效果，在預防和治療慢性腎臟病的新策略。

463612.label: Realisation of objectives
463612.value: 1. Aim 1. To determine the role of Six1 and its cofactor Eya1 in renal fibrosis. By using the obstructive nephropathy model (UUO), we found that expression of Six1 was induced during renal fibrosis in mice in UUO kidneys. Delivery of overexpression (OE) plasmids of Six1 alone or together with Eya1 (a Six1 cofactor) into the left kidney by an ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene delivery technique showed that fibrotic responses in obstructed kidneys were enhanced by Six1 overexpression, and further promoted when both Six1 and Eya1 were overexpressed. In addition, we also found that the expression of Six1 and Eya1 was related to the activation of TGF-beta/Smad signaling during renal fibrosis in mice. Six1 and Eya1 were co-expressed with P-Smad3 and TGF-beta receptor I in UUO kidneys, implying that Six1/Eya1 plays a pathologic role in renal TGF-beta/Smad signaling. Furthermore, by using stable cell lines in which the Six1 or Eya1 is overexpressed, overexpression of Six1 alone or with Eya1 increased extracellular matrix (ECM) expression in TEC and these results were reversed by blocking Six1 expression. These results confirmed the results from in vivo studies. These results implied that Six1/Eya1 plays a pathologic role in renal TGF-beta/Smad signaling-related fibrosis. 2. Aim 2. To investigate the mechanism of how Six1 promotes TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis. In breast cancer, Six1 and Eya2 promote TGF-beta signaling by enhancing expression of TGF-beta receptor I. We found that overexpression of Six1 promoted TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis by inducing expression of TGF-beta receptor I. Suppression of TGF-beta receptor I abrogated Six1 promotion on TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis. In addition, we found that knockdown of expression of TGF-beta receptor I decreased ECM expression in kidney tubular cells even when Six1 is overexpressed, suggesting that upregulation of TGF-beta receptor I is necessary for Six1 action on TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis. We next investigate how Six1 promotes expression of TGF-beta receptor I during TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis. Six1 promoted transcription of TGF-beta receptor I in a dose-dependent manner via binding TRI promoter. As we identified three conserved Six1 binding sites located in promoter of TGF-beta receptor I, we employed promoter reporter assays and chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), and demonstrated that Six1 bound to one of these sites in regulatory sequences of TGF-beta receptor I. Results from these in vitro study demonstrated that that Six1 is a key mediator in renal fibrosis in response to TGF-beta1 by inducing expression of TGF-beta receptor I during fibrosis. 3. Specific Aim 3. To develop a therapeutic strategy for renal fibrosis by delivering Six1 and/or Eya1 knockdown plasmids into diseased kidneys In this aim, we investigated the therapeutic potential of Six1 for renal fibrosis by delivering Six1 knockdown plasmids into obstructed kidneys to study whether the progression of renal fibrosis was altered. Prevention and intervention experiments were included to determine the reduction of Six1 expression was able to inhibit renal fibrosis or affect the progression of renal fibrosis during established renal diseases. The ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene transfer of a Six1 knockdown plasmid in a mouse model of obstructive kidney disease ameliorated renal fibrosis, and this revealed a therapeutic potential for Six1 knockdown in renal fibrosis.

463612.label: Major findings and research outcome
463612.value: TGF-beta signaling plays a critical role in chronic kidney disease. It is well known that in breast cancer, Six1 and Eya2 promote TGF-beta signaling by enhancing expression of TGF-beta receptor I. However, the exact mode of Six1 in renal fibrosis remains unclear. In this study, we tested a novel hypothesis that Six1 may play an essential role in regulating the renal fibrosis in response to TGF-beta1 and that specific targeting Six1 may represent an effective and novel therapy for chronic kidney disease. By microarray and realtime PCR, Six1 expression was upregulated in ligated kidneys of a mouse model of unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO). Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that the upregulation of Six1 expression during renal fibrosis, The functional role of Six1 in renal fibrosis was investigated by generating stable cell lines with overexpressing or down-regulating of Six1. In kidney tubular cells, overexpression of Six1 promoted but knockdown of Six1 suppressed TGF-beta1-induced renal fibrosis, demonstrating the pathological role of Six1 in fibrosis in vitro. We found that overexpression of Six1 promoted TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis by inducing transcription of TRI. Suppression of TGF-beta receptor I abrogated Six1 promotion on TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis. In addition, we found that knockdown of expression of TGF-beta receptor I decreased extracellular matrix expression in kidney tubular cells even when Six1 is overexpressed, suggesting that TβRI upregulation is necessary for Six1 action on TGF-beta-induced renal fibrosis. Furthermore, Six1 promotes expression of TGF-beta receptor I by binding to regulatory sequences of TGF-beta receptor I. More importantly, the therapeutic potential of targeting Six1 in kidney disease was demonstrated in mouse models of obstructive nephropathies by applying an ultrasound-microbubble-mediated anti-Six1 gene transfer technique. This gene transfer of a Six1 knockdown plasmid into the ligated kidneys was able to halt the progression of renal fibrosis. All these results revealed a therapeutic potential for targeting Six1 in chronic kidney disease. In conclusion, Six1 is an important mediator of TGF-beta signaling and plays a pathological role in the development of renal fibrosis. Targeting Six1 may represent a novel and effective therapy to combat renal fibrosis in chronic kidney disease. The research work of this study resulted in 17 publications and 7 presentations in international conferences, and 2 presentations in local conferences, and training of one doctoral student.

463612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
463612.value: 1. To determine whether cofactor(s) of Six1 is required for the TGF-beta signaling during renal fibrosis. Overexpression of Six1 with its cofactors facilitates breast cancer cell metastasis through increasing TGF-beta signaling. Further studies demonstrate that Eya2, one of Six cofactors, is required for Six1 mediation on metastasis and expression of TGF-beta receptor I. This cofactor may play role in Six1 signaling. In kidneys, Eya1, another cofactor of Six1, promoted TGF-beta-induced fibrosis by inducing expression of TGF-beta receptor. Thus, the next step is to study which Six1 cofactor(s) plays a pathologic role with Six1 during renal fibrosis. 2. To develop a therapeutic strategy for renal injury by delivering knockdown the plasmid of Six1 into diseased kidneys We should determine the therapeutic potential of targeting Six1 or its cofactors for renal injury in different mouse models of kidney diseases, including diabetic kidney disease. By an ultrasound-microbubble-mediated gene delivery system, we can deliver knockdown plasmids of Six1 and its cofactors into diseased kidneys at every 4 weeks to determine whether suppression of expression of Six1 and/or its cofactors will attenuate renal injury.

463612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
463612.value: TGF-beta/Smad signaling plays a critical role in chronic kidney disease (CKD). It is well known that in breast cancer, Six1 and Eya2 promote TGF-beta signaling by enhancing TβRI expression. However, the exact mode of Six1 in renal fibrosis remains unclear. In this study, we tested a novel hypothesis that Six1 may play an essential role in regulating the renal fibrosis in response to TGF-beta1 and that specific targeting Six1 may represent an effective and novel therapy for chronic kidney disease. Expression levels of Six1 increased in kidney cells after treatment of TGF-beta1 or under obstructive kidney disease and the increase of Six1 effects depended on the expression of TGF-beta receptor I. Alteration of expression levels of Six1 in kidney cells demonstrated the pathological role of Six1 in fibrosis in vitro. Enhanced Six1 expression promoted but suppression of Six1 inhibited TGF-beta1-induced renal fibrosis and obstructive kidney injury. More importantly, suppression the Six1 levels in diseased kidneys was able to halt the progression of renal fibrosis. In conclusion, Six1 is a downstream mediator of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling and plays a pathological role in the development of renal injury. Targeting Six1 may represent a novel and effective therapy to combat chronic kidney disease.
