466312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466312.value: The long-term goal of this project is to provide efficient genetic tools and scientific knowledge for mushroom genetics and breeding. Specific aims are to (1) construct a high-density genetic linkage map of Lentinula edodes by genome resequencing of a mapping population, (2) mapping of quantitative trait loci (QTL) of growth rate and laccases, and gene expression levels (eQTL) of lignocellulolytic enzymes, (3) provide molecular markers for L. edodes genetic studies and breeding. L. edodes, the shiitake mushroom, is the second most cultivated edible mushroom. Strain improvement of this mushroom is limited because the breeding programmes are unsystematic and inefficient. L. edodes genetics have received attention and some molecular markers are available. However, there are no genetic tools suitable for breeding. The major gap is the lack of a species genetic linkage map. A map will serve as the fundamental genetic resource for understanding the genetic determinants of important phenotypes. Current L. edodes low-density genetic maps are based on DNA fingerprinting markers and applicable only to the particular strains. We need a high-density species genetic linkage map. We have sequenced L. edodes monokaryon L54A genome and obtained many polymorphic markers for map construction. However, the genotyping methods using these markers to construct a genetic linkage map are tedious, expensive and demands great efforts. L. edodes is an efficient lignin degrading white-rot fungus but the regulations of its lignocellulolytic enzymes are poorly understood. To overcome these problems, we propose (a) efficient genotyping by resequencing a mapping population, namely, single spore isolates (SSIs) of L. edodes L54 to construct a high-density genetic linkage map. We will use our L. edodes L54A genome sequence as the reference. (b) We will locate quantitative trait loci (QTL) for mycelial growth rates and laccase activities and also locate expression QTL (eQTL) controlling expression levels of lignocellulolytic genes on the map. The SSI genome sequences will provide a wide variety of markers including simple sequence repeats, single nucleotide polymorphisms, and gene markers. To our knowledge, this is the first time the next generation sequencing technology is used in a genetic approach to construct a high-density genetic linkage map and also the use of eQTL in analysis of lignocellulolytic systems of a fungus. 我國是目前世界上最大的香菇生產國和出口國,而香菇作為第二大食用菌，素有“山珍”之譽，其美味及功效不言而喻。眾所周知，香菇菌種是香菇生產的重要前提，菌種優劣是決定其產量和品質的主要因素。然而，相對於香菇日益增長的生產和需求，香菇優良品種選育技術明顯滯後, 缺乏系統性和高效性。遺傳圖譜作為重要的遺傳信息資源, 有助於發掘、理解重要性狀的遺傳基礎。儘管香菇的分子遺傳研究已經受到關注、一些分子標記業已開發, 但是仍然缺乏適用於廣泛育種的遺傳工具, 其中高密度的遺傳圖譜便是主要的空缺。目前，基於DNA指紋標記構建的香菇遺傳圖譜因其密度低而只適用於特定菌株的育種。因此,香菇高密度遺傳圖譜的構建就顯得尤為迫切。與此同時, 傳統的構建遺傳圖譜的方法卻相當耗時費力。為解決此類問題，本研究計劃擬從以下兩個相關方面進行研究：（a）由於基因組序列可為遺傳圖譜的構建提供多種多樣的分子標記，如微衛星、單核苷酸多態性標記以及基因標記。我們擬以已經完成測序的香菇單核體L54A的基因組為參照，通過對不同單孢菌株的作圖群體進行重測序, 據此進行高效的基因分型, 從而構建高密度遺傳圖譜（ b）基於構建的高密度遺傳圖譜, 分別對漆酶活性和菌絲生長速率進行QTL定位分析，並從全基因組水平 (13,382個基因) 開展eQTL研究, 據此探索揭示重要性狀的遺傳基礎及調控網絡. 本計劃是首次直接將新一代測序技術融匯於經典遺傳學方法中進行真菌高密度遺傳圖譜的構建。本計劃的開展不僅為香菇的遺傳、育種研究提供寶貴的信息資源, 如多種分子標記及高密度的遺傳圖譜,而且對香菇重要性狀的遺傳基礎進行挖掘,著眼長遠,更為最終優化菇種選育技術提供有效的遺傳資源和科學根據。

466312.label: Realisation of objectives
466312.value: 1. Determine genotypes of 50 SSIs by genome resequencing We have grown 48 single spore isolates (SSIs) from L. edodes dikaryon L54 and isolated their total DNA. We performed low-coverage (~0.5 to 1.5-fold) whole-genome resequencing for 20 SSIs using Roche GS-FLX Titanium sequencer and 28 SSIs using the ThermoFisher Ion PGM System. We genotyped each SSI by mapping sequencing reads of each SSI to the L54A reference genome using GS Reference Mapper (454 Life Sciences Corporation). After comparison of mapped sequences and the reference sequence L54A, identical sequences were assigned to genotype “A” whereas sequences with high-quality SNPs were regarded as genotype “B”. After genotyping, there are 444 high quality sequence-based markers to be used to construct the high-density linkage map. 2. Construct a high-density genetic linkage map We generated a high-density sequence-based genetic map based on the genome sequence scaffolds of L. edodes strain L54A. Each scaffold served as a genetic marker for the linkage map. A total of 231sequence-based markers were placed on the map, with an average marker spacing of 1.3 cM. The linkage map spanned a total genetic distance of 292.8 cM and contained 9 linkage groups. Each linkage group is longer than 20cM in length. The average distance of each linkage group is 32.5 cM. The range of each linkage group was from 20.0cM to 67.8cM. The number of sequence-based markers located on each linkage group range from 10 to 65. The interval between markers varies from 0.1cM to 10.5cM. By adding up the length of those mapped scaffolds (markers), the total length of this linkage map is 18.2Mb. They covered 45.3% of L54A genome. The average physical distance of each linkage group is 2.0Mb, so the ratio of physical distance to genetic distance is 58.0kbp/cM in average. The accuracy of the map was confirmed by comparing with previous maps the locations of known genes such as matA and matB. 3. Locate QTL contributing to laccase activities and mycelia growth rates and expression QTL controlling expression levels of lignocellulolytic genes on the high-density genetic linkage map of L. edodes We examined the mycelial growth rates of 48 SSIs on potato dextrose agar plates cultured in the darkness at 25 ℃. We demonstrated that the mycelial growth rate behaves as a quantitative trait. One QTL on LG1 were located using WinQTLCart V2.5. Composite interval mapping(CIM) method with 1.0cM scan window was used to identify the QTL controlling the mycelial growth rate. The length of LOD-1 confidence interval of this QTL is 3.3 cM, and the QTL was mapped in the region from 56.8 cM to 60.1 cM of LG1. The favorable alleles at this QTL came from the parental strain L54A. There are 3 sequenced-based markers, S272, S103 and S231, in this QTL region. S231 is the nearest marker to the LOD score peak. The QTL region is incorporated to the L. edodes genome browser based on GBrowse for user-friendly comparison with other annotated features from the reference sequence. After browsing the QTL region, although there was no annotated gene on S272, the remaining 2 genetic markers are linked with more than one annotated genes, such as nuclease Le1(ncl1) and homologous gene cytochrome-b5 reductase (b5R) as putative loci associated with mycelium growth rate. For the expression QTL (eQTL) identification, we used 48 dikaryon strains from another L. edodes mapping population. The total mRNA of the mycelium growing on softwood of the 48 strains was extracted and sequenced with Illumina Hiseq4000 PE150. The RNA-seq data were then aligned to L54A draft genome by Tophat2, and used for Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNP) calling and gene expression level measurement. To locate the loci affecting gene expression, linear regression analysis is performed between the genotype of each SNP marker and the expression values of each gene, using Matrix-eQTL. 54 local-eQTLs and 8,888 distant-eQTLs (FDR<0.01, P value < 1x10-6) were identified for 1,985 genes, including the eQTLs of 6 laccase genes. 4. Identify polymorphic sequence-based markers for breeding programmes We have obtained a dikaryon mapping population resulted from 3 parental strains, which can give us as many as 9 genotypes. We develop a panel of 71,474 SNPs. These sequence-based SNP markers are resulted from recombination of 2~4 types of alleles, so the genotype variety of these markers is high, which is good for favorable variants to be identified for breeding programmes. 1,559 of them are eQTLs of one or multiple genes, may act as candidate regulators of the expression levels of the corresponding targeted genes. The favorable alleles at these bases can be used as markers for marker-assisted selection.

466312.label: Major findings and research outcome
466312.value: We have sequenced 48 SSIs in total to perform the linkage analysis. We obtained 444 high quality sequence-based markers and constructed the high-density linkage map with 9 linkage groups. For the detection of QTL associated with mycelial growth rate, one loci on the linkage group LG1 has a LOD peak value larger than 2.5, detected by the CIM method. These markers are also applied in QTL mapping for 11 agronomic traits, and 43 markers are detected to be significantly associated with 4 traits (Li et al., 2017). We have also sequenced 48 dikaryons from another L. edodes mapping population, and performed eQTL anaylsis genome-widely. A panel of 71,474 SNP markers was developed and eQTLs of 1,985 genes, including 6 laccases have been identified in this way. The genetic map, genome sequences, experimental design and bioinformatics analysis pipeline are developed and used in genetic mapping (Li et al., 2017), population studies (Xiao et al., 2016), and evolution of L. edodes (Cheng et al., 2015), and other fungi (Cheng et al., 2015). 466312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466312.value: Based on the resequenced genomes of 48 SSIs from diakaryotic parent L. edodes L54, the high density genetic linkage map was constructed with 9 linkage groups. The map obtained is of high density and has more sequence-based markers than previous study. Simultaneously, one QTL associated with mycelial growth rate was determined on the linkage map, and eQTLs affecting gene expression levels were also identified for 1,985 genes. Both of the scaffold markers and SNP markers are linked with annotated genes, so we can locate the causal/regulatory genes around the markers. These eQTL data can serve as database of SNP-gene interaction and gene-gene interaction. In the future, we plan to further specify which genes linked with the QTL region are regulators of mycelium growth rate. The genes on S272, S103 and S231 will be firstly filtered by knockdown assay. The genes targeted by eQTLs on S272, S103 and S231 will also the subjected to experimental evaluation in the future study. In this way, we will identify the real controllers of growth rate, and provide more specific selection markers for breeding use.

466312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466312.value: To have a better understanding of the genetic structure and genetic determinants of phenotypes of L. edodes, we constructed a high-density genetic linkage map of L. edodes. This linkage map with 9 linkage groups was constructed by calculating the recombination frequencies of 231 sequence-based markers. To our knowledge, this is the first time state-of-the-art next-generation sequencing technology is used directly in a genetic approach to construct a high-density genetic linkage map of fungus. Our genetic linkage map was high in density and included large number of sequence-based markers. We used our map to locate the genetic loci controlling mycelium growth rates. Genetic loci affecting the expression levels of 6 laccases and other 1,979 genes is also obtained. The elucidation of the mechanisms of fundamental biological process including wood degradation, mating, growth and development, and agronomic characteristics in L. edodes can be improved by using this map and the eQTL data.

466412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466412.value: Pancreas is a vital gland organ with dual-functional roles as both endocrine and exocrine glands critical to our glucose homeostasis and nutrient absorption respectively. Thus the development and homeostasis of pancreas is of high medical significance. There is increasing evidence suggesting that disruption of the exocrine pancreatic acinar cell development, function and homeostasis may result in chronic pancreatic injury diseases which is related to the onset of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. However, very little is known about the molecular control mechanisms underlying the exocrine pancreas development and acinar cell homeostasis. Foxp4, a member in Forkhead box transcription factor family, has been shown to express highly in acinar cells of different developmental stages in developing and adult exocrine pancreas. However, genetic and functional analyses of Foxp4 in pancreas development and homeostasis have been limited by the early embryonic lethality in the knock-out mutant mice reported previously. To circumvent such embryonic lethality limitation, we employed a conditional knockout approach to study the role of Foxp4 in acinar cell development, functioning, maintenance and homeostasis in pancreas using mouse model. Our preliminary data show that there was an overall reduction in the cell population of pancreas, reduced expression of acinar cell lineage marker protein and disorganization of zymogen granules of acinar cells within the exocrine pancreas lacking Foxp4. These suggest that Foxp4 is critical in the acinar cell functioning, maintenance and homeostasis of the exocrine pancreas. Therefore, we propose to address directly the functional roles of Foxp4 in pancreatic acinar cell development and homeostasis using ‘loss-of-function’ approaches by pancreas-specific and acinar cell-specific conditional inactivation of Foxp4 specifically in developing and adult pancreas. Two different Cre-expressing mouse lines will be used to generate conditional Foxp4 mutant mice at different developmental stages of pancreatic acinar cells for dissecting the roles of Foxp4 in embryonic, neonatal and adult pancreas. In addition, our Foxp4 conditional inactivation mutants with pathological changes in acinar cell population will serve as a valuable tool for searching for novel genetic controls of acinar cell development, homeostasis and clinical implication of Foxp4 function. High-resolution genomic assay technologies will be employed to identify novel genes regulating the pancreas function and homeostasis by comparing expression profile and Foxp4 binding profile in the pancreas of wild-type and the Foxp4 conditional inactivation mutants. 466412.label: Realisation of objectives
466412.value: In this project, we addressed specifically the roles of a Forkhead-box gene, Foxp4, in development, functioning and homeostasis of acinar cells in exocrine pancreas. For objective (1), we used ‘loss-of-function’ approach to study and analyze the phenotypic consequence of the loss of Foxp4 function during panceras development. We utilized the Cre/loxP approach to ablate Foxp4 gene function in a tissue and temporal specific manner. In order to achieve conditional inactivation of Foxp4 in pancreas and acinar cells specifically during different stages of development, we have established different mouse lines: (1) conditional Foxp4 null allele line, (2) Pdx1-Cre transgenic mouse line, (3) Ela1-creERT2 transgenic mouse line. We used the proposed breeding schemes to generate the homozygous Foxp4 recombined null mutants, Pdx1-Cre/Foxp4 and Ela1-CreERT2/Foxp4 conditional knockout mutant mice for studying of Foxp4 function in pancreas. We successfully identified Foxp4 as an important regulator for exocrine tissue homeostasis. Ablation of Foxp4 in pancreas resulted in defective ER stress response eventually leads to deterioration in acinar cell physiology and mild pancreatic damage. For objective (2), we successfully induced acute pancreatitis in both control and Foxp4 null mutant mice by caerulein injection. We showed that both Foxp4 and PCNA +ve cells increased in the recovery phase of induced acute pancreatitis, and those Foxp4 +ve cells co-expressed with PCNA in the control mice. Surprisingly we did not identify any difference in the severity of pancreatitis and the recovery rate in the Foxp4 mutant compared with the control. For objective (3), we have tried extraction of total RNAs from pancreas using different commercial kits and Trizol-reagent. However, the yield and quality of RNAs obtained was not up to the standard for RNA-sequencing. Although RNA-sequencing data was temporary unavailable, we did perform a series of real-time PCR to identify potential Foxp4 targets. We identified that genes involved in ER stress response pathway, exocytosis pathway and zymogen granule components were all up-regulated in Foxp4 mutant. We observed that the phenotype of mild ER stress and partially defected UPR pathways of Foxp4 null acinar cells is similar to that of Mist1 null mice. Strikingly, significant down-regulation of Mist1 protein expression was detected in Foxp4-deficient acinar cell by both immunohistochemical assays and western blotting analyses. Thus our results suggest Foxp4 may regulate both the secretory pathway and the ER stress response pathway in acinar cells by maintaining Mist1 expression.

466412.label: Major findings and research outcome
466412.value: Pancreas is a vital gland organ with dual-functional roles as both endocrine and exocrine glands that are critical to our glucose homeostasis and nutrient absorption respectively. There is increasing evidence suggesting that disruption of the exocrine pancreatic acinar cell development, function and homeostasis may result in chronic pancreatic injury diseases. However, very little is known about the molecular control mechanisms underlying the exocrine pancreas stress response and acinar cell homeostasis. Foxp4, a member in Forkhead box transcription factor family, has been shown to express highly in acinar cells of different developmental stages in developing and adult exocrine pancreas. Our data provides genetic evidence identifying Foxp4 as a critical transcription factor involved in the transcriptional network that regulates exocrine tissue homeostasis by maintaining proper ER stress response. Ablation of Foxp4 in pancreas resulted in pancreatic hypoplasia due to reduction in acinar cell proliferation and partially defective unfolded protein response pathway leading to an increased level of ER stress, mitochondrial injury and appearance of autophagic vesicles. Thus the inactivation of Foxp4 posed a detrimental effect on long term exocrine tissue homeostasis. More interestingly, we demonstrated a significant reduction in protein level of Mist1 in Foxp4-null mice pancreas. This is the first report on the functional role of Foxp4 in the pancreatic exocrine tissue homeostasis by regulating both the unfolded protein response pathway and the Mist1 expression. Our findings provide new insight into the regulatory network that governs the stress response pathway and maintenance of exocrine tissue homeostasis in pancreas. A manuscript of these findings is written up for submission to Journal of Biological Chemistry (Part C8 item1).

466412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466412.value: As we have detected that there is a reduction in acinar cell proliferation in the absence of Foxp4, Foxp4 is likely to act as a cell proliferation regulator of acinar cell at adult stage. However the Ela1-creERT2 transgenic mouse line that we established can only give limited recombination activity in the Foxp4 conditional null allele. It limited our study of the role of Foxp4 in adult stage pancreas. Thus we plan to import a newly available Ptf1a-creERT2 transgenic line as another acinar cell inducible Cre line to inactivate Foxp4 at adult stage with higher efficiency. By using the Ptf1a-creERT2/Foxp4 line with R26R-YFP lineage tracer, we can track whether the acinar cells without Foxp4 would be devoid of proliferation. This will give further insight into the molecular mechanism of Foxp4 as cell proliferation regulator in the pancreas.

466412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466412.value: Recent studies suggest disruption of pancreatic acinar cell homeostasis could lead to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma which is the sixth leading cancer death in Hong Kong. A deeper understanding of the molecular basis of acinar cells development and homeostasis could thus provide the knowledge relevance to the early diagnosis and treatment of this pancreatic cancer. However, the mechanisms underlying exocrine pancreas development and acinar cell homeostasis have been limited. In order to understand the molecular mechanism of exocrine acinar cell homeostasis, we investigated the functional role of a transcription factor, Foxp4, expressed in the acinar cell in pancreas. We found that Foxp4 is a important factor regulating acinar cell functioning and homeostasis in exocrine pancreas. Mutant mice without Foxp4 in the pancreas suffered from weight lost and pancreas hypoplasia. The mutant showed signs of impaired exocrine pancreatic tissue homeostasis. Thus, our study yields new insight in the molecular regulatory mechanisms of acinar cell homeostasis in the exocrine pancreas that will help us to better understand the complex molecular program underlying chronic pancreatic injury diseases involving defects in exocrine pancreas homeostasis.

466612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466612.value: Background There is so far no intervention which has been shown to be effective in preventing cognitive decline in older people with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) - a prodromal stage of dementia. Homocysteine lowering by B vitamins has been shown to lower the rate of brain atrophy in MCI patients, especially in those with elevated plasma homocysteine. Subgroup analysis also suggested benefits in cognitive function in those with elevated plasma homocysteine. Thus B vitamins may have a very good potential to improve cognitive function in MCI patients with elevated plasma homocysteine. We therefore propose to perform a double blind randomized placebo controlled trial of vitamin B12, B6 and folic acid to prevent cognitive decline in older MCI patients with elevated plasma homocysteine. Subjects and Method Clients of residential homes and social centres for the elderly aged ≥75 years will be screened for cognitive impairment by a two stage procedure – Chinese Abbreviated MCI (CAMCI) test and clinical dementia rating scale (CDR). The cognitively impaired (CDR 0.5) subjects will have fasting blood taken for plasma homocysteine. Those with elevated plasma homocysteine (≥13 μmol/L) are then clinically assessed for diagnosis of MCI. 336 of eligible MCI subjects will be randomly assigned to take either one tablet containing folic acid (0.8 mg), vitamin B12 (0.5 mg) and vitamin B6 (20 mg),or one placebo tablet once daily for 24 months. The subjects are followed up at month 12 and 24. In addition to having neurocognitive tests at baseline and follow-up visits, 50 subjects in each trial group will have MRI brain imaging for whole brain and hippocampal volume analysis at baseline and month 24. Plasma homocysteine will be repeated at month 12 and 24. The primary outcome is cognitive improvement as defined by reversion of global CDR score to 0. The secondary outcomes include CDR sum of boxes, neurocognitive test battery Z score, incidence of clinical dementia, Hamilton depression rating scale, whole brain and hippocampal volumes on MRI and plasma homocysteine. Statistical analysis Intention to treat analysis will be adopted. The incidence of cognitive improvement and clinical dementia in trial groups will be compared by Chi square test and multiple logistic regressions. Repeated measures analysis of variance will be employed to compare the trial groups in their changes with time in continuous variables, with adjustments for age, sex, education level and APOE genotype. All statistical tests were two sided and a p-value < 0.05 are considered statistically significant. 有資料顯示很多有認知障礙的老年人都有高的〝同型半胱氨酸〞血漿水平，〝同型半胱氨酸〞是氨基酸裏的新陳代謝物，它也許對腦部有害。有一些維他命B的種類是可以有效降低血漿〝同型半胱氨酸〞，也可以減慢有認知障礙的老年人的腦部收縮。因此，我們進行一項對患有輕度認知障礙和高〝同型半胱氨酸〞血漿水平的長者以維他命B12、B6和葉酸以改善智力功能的研究。 凡住在安老院舍和參加老人社區中心的長者年屆75歲或以上的，便可以參與兩項篩查認知障礙的程序 – 中文簡短認知障礙測試﹝CAMCI﹞和臨床失智評定量表﹝CDR﹞。那些有認知障礙的參加者﹝CDR 0.5﹞需要進行空腹抽血以作檢查“同型半胱氨酸”血漿水平，而偏高者﹝≥13 μmol/L﹞會再經臨床診斷是否患有輕度認知障礙。336名合資格的輕度認知障礙長者將會服食一粒藥丸，為期24個月，這是隨機分配的，藥丸的成分可能是含有0.8毫克的葉酸、0.5毫克的維他命B12，和20毫克的維他命B6或者是對人體無害的安慰劑。 這個研究的主要結果是改善認知方面，即是逆轉臨床失智評定量表的分數到0。而其次的結果包括：臨床失智評定量表的總分數，認知功能測試量表分數，腦退化症的發病率，漢密爾頓抑鬱量表。

466612.label: Realisation of objectives
466612.value: The objective of the clinical trial has not been met yet because the trial is still on-going. There are two reasons for the delay. Firstly, we could not find a local supplier for placebo tablets. After much effort, co-I V Lee managed to find a supplier in the Philippines. In order to import the placebo tablets from overseas, we had to go through a lengthy approval process for the clinical trial certificate from the Department of Health. The certificate was eventually obtained in September 2013. It then took another three months to obtain ethical approval. Consequently, the first subject was randomized in January 2014, one year after the start of the project. The second reason for the delay was the slower than expected recruitment rate. The difficulty was largely due to relatively low prevalence (19%) of elevated serum homocysteine (> 13 µmol/L) in older people with mild cognitive impairment. We addressed this problem by lowering the cutoff concentration to 10 µmol/L and by restricting recruitment to subjects old than 70 years. In addition, we opened up three additional recruitment sites. Between April 2013 and July 2016, we had screened 975 subjects with mild cognitive impairment and 352 subjects (36.1%) were eligible for the randomized trial. Out of these, 279 subjects (79.3%) participated in the trial. To date, 218 subjects (78.1%) have been followed up at month 12, and 111 subjects (39.8 %) have completed the trial at month 24. The month 12 follow up will be completed in October 2017, and the trial will be completed in October 2018. An interim analysis of the available data at month 12 has been performed. The result showed homocysteine lowering by B vitamins tended to improve executive function. This treatment effect was significant in subjects with high vascular risk i.e. diabetes mellitus or aspirin use. This finding if confirmed by further follow-up at month 24 will have significant impact on clinical practice. In addition, with PI’s other resources, 105 subjects had volumetric MRI brain scan at baseline, and the scan is being repeated at month 24. The changes in regional brain volumes will be correlated with vitamin supplementation and cognitive outcomes. All in all, our research team has tried our best to perform the clinical trial with our available resources. Despite the challenges, we have managed to recruit a substantial number of well-characterized subjects for the trial. The interim analysis showed promising results. The full results of the completed trial are likely to have important contributions to the understanding of the role of homocysteine in cognitive decline in older people.

466612.label: Major findings and research outcome
466612.value: Between April 2013 and July 2016, we screened 975 subjects with mild cognitive impairment and 352 subjects (36.1%) were eligible for the randomized trial. Out of these, 279 subjects (79.3%) participated in the trial. 138 subjects were randomly assigned to take methycobalamin 500 mcg and folic acid 500 mcg once daily, and 141 subjects took two placebo tablets once daily. To date, 218 subjects (78.1%) have been followed up at month 12, and 111 subjects (39.8 %) have completed the trial at month 24. The reasons for the delay were the difficulties in subject recruitment and in acquiring placebo tablets initially. An interim analysis of findings at month 12 has been performed. The supplement and placebo group subjects were well matched except that the supplement group had better executive function (average z score 0. 13 versus -0.13 in placebo group), probably because they were slightly younger. At month 12, serum homocysteine was significantly reduced in supplement group (average 13.44 (sd 3.68) to 9.50 (sd 2.29)), while it did not change significantly in placebo group. The change in executive function Z score tended to be greater in supplement group (average 0.17 (sd 6.7) versus 0.05 (sd 0.59) in placebo group; P value 0.159) The change in memory function Z score was similar in two groups (0.04 (0.59) versus 0.07 (0.59) in supplement and placebo groups respectively). In planned subgroup analysis, among aspirin users (22 in supplement group and 24 in placebo group), supplement group had significantly greater improvement in executive function than placebo group (0.37 (sd 0.64) versus -0.07 (sd 0.61); P = 0.021). Supplement group also fared slightly better in memory (0.15 (sd 0.61) versus -0.04 (sd 0.52) in placebo group; P= 0.275). On subgroup analysis of subjects with amnesic mild cognitive impairment and diabetes mellitus (31 in supplement group and 40 in placebo group subjects), supplement group showed more positive changes in executive function Z score and memory Z score than placebo group (P= 0.035 and 0.087 respectively). 5 out of 107 (4.67%) in supplement group and 7 out of 111 (6.3%) in placebo group had cognitive decline according to global clinical dementia rating scale (CDR). The difference was not significant (P value 0.597). Overall, the supplement group had greater cognitive improvement than placebo group at month 12, especially among aspirin users and people with diabetes mellitus.

466612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466612.value: The month 12 follow up will be completed in October 2017, and the trial will be completed in October 2018. With PI’s other resources, 105 subjects had volumetric MRI brain scan at baseline. (53 and 52 in placebo and supplement groups respectively). Follow-up brain scan will be performed at month 24. A full original research paper based on baseline data is due to submitted to an international journal for publication. The finding is that among subjects with amnesic mild cognitive impairment, those with diabetes mellitus (DM) had significantly more impairment in executive function and had slower walking speed than those without DM. This suggested that executive dysfunction may be an early feature of neurodegeneration in people with DM. When month 12 follow-up is completed, a paper to report on the interim analysis (as above) will be submitted for publication. When the final follow-up is completed, another paper based on the cognitive outcomes and regional brain volume changes on MRI will be submitted.

466612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466612.value: 279 subjects with mild cognitive impairment and raised serum homocysteine were randomly assigned to have vitamin B12 and folic acid supplements or placebo tablets once daily for 24 months. To date, 218 subjects (78.1%) have been followed up at month 12, and 111 subjects (39.8 %) completed the trial at month 24. The trial will be completed in October 2018. The reasons for the delay were the difficulties in subject recruitment and in acquiring placebo tablets. Interim analysis of results at month 12 found that the vitamin B supplements lowered serum homocysteine effectively. The supplement group had greater improvement than placebo group in executive function, but not in memory. The treatment effect in executive function and memory was more significant among those with diabetes mellitus and users of aspirin. 4.7% and 6.3% of supplement group and placebo group subjects developed dementia respectively at month 12. Overall, the preliminary results suggested that older people with mild cognitive impairment and high cardiovascular risk had significant cognitive improvement with vitamin B12 and folic acid supplementation. We keenly await the final results at month 24, which will include changes in regional brain volumes on MRI in a subgroup.

467612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
467612.value: 前列腺癌的發病率在過去的二十年中急速上升。現在前列腺癌是香港第三常見的男性惡性腫瘤。患者常死於激素抵抗性癌轉移。研究有效的針對激素抵抗性前列腺癌的治療方法仍然是生物醫學研究領域中的熱點 我們曾經報導，G-1誘導的GPR30的活化可通過維持Erk1/2的活性在體內和體外抑制前列腺癌細胞生長。此機制與乳腺癌細胞不同。在乳腺癌細胞中，腺苷酸環化酶（AC）的刺激同時引起瞬時的Erk1/2活化，伴隨cAMP水平增高從而減弱Erk1/2活性，刺激細胞生長。然而，對於G-1反應的機制，抑制的或者激活的，依然不明確。我們的初步數據顯示，在G-1處理的前列腺癌細胞中沒引起cAMP增高，這與乳腺癌細胞不同。在前列腺癌細胞中，引起cAMP增高的AC激活劑削弱了G-1誘導的細胞生長抑制以及其相關的信號傳導通路的刺激。此拮抗作用可以被蛋白激酶A（PKA）抑製劑逆轉，並且可以被細胞滲透性cAMP類似物模仿。以上結果提示，削弱Erk1/2活性的AC-cAMP-PKA信號通路的激活障礙是G-1誘導的前列腺癌細胞生長抑制的關鍵。在這方面，我們發現在前列腺癌細胞中G[alpha]i1有顯著表達，而在乳腺癌細胞中並非如此，乳腺癌細胞顯著表達的是G[alpha]s。因為GTP結合的G[alpha]i1常在激活G蛋白偶聯受體時抑制AC活性，而活化的G[alpha]s則刺激AC活性，所以在前列腺癌細胞中優勢表達的G[alpha]i1可能是生長抑制的原因。實際上，siRNA誘導的G[alpha]i1基因剔除可阻斷G-1對前列腺癌細胞生長的抑製作用，這提示G[alpha]i1在生長抑制中的功能。此外，我們進一步證明了G-1可抑制前列腺癌細胞移動和侵襲，並通過細胞中GPR30依賴性信號通路的作用減少絲狀偽足和應力纖維的形成。基於上述新發現，我們將探討GPR30和G[alpha]i1在前列腺癌中的臨床意義，闡述對於G-1反應的機制和G-1誘導的及GPR30-介導調控的前列腺癌細胞遷移和侵襲的相關機制，以及研究G-1在體內的通過GPR30作用的抗前列腺癌轉移特性。 我們設想此課題所得研究結果可增強我們對前列腺癌生物學特徵以及在前列腺癌中通過GPR30作用的G-1的抑癌作用的理解。重要的是，這些結果有利於將來研發基於GPR30的抗前列腺癌治療，並且對G-1及其他GPR30特異的激動劑在患者中的新應用打下必要的基礎。 GPR30和G[alpha]i1的表達情況可用作此療法的預測生物標記物。

467612.label: Realisation of objectives
467612.value: As stated in Objective 1, expression of GPR30 and G[alpha]i1 protein in clinical PCa samples were determined as compared to their corresponding adjacent normal tissues. By quantitative RT-PCR and Western blot analyses, we demonstrated statistically significant up-regulation of G[alpha]i1 protein expression in PCa with 92% of the cases with high expression whereas variable expression of GPR30 among the tumor tissues was observed with up-regulation in some cases and down-regulation in others. In addition, G[alpha]s protein was studied and it showed no statistically significant change at both mRNA and protein levels. There was no association of these proteins expression with any clinicopathological data such as Gleason scores. In addition, we fully addressed Objective 2. By GTP-binding assays, we demonstrated that G-1, through GPR30, activated G[alpha]i1 protein to sustain Erk1/2 activation and failed to activate AC for cAMP production in PCa cells. In fact, the chemical-induced activation of AC-cAMP-PKA signaling in the cells attenuated Erk1/2 activity and blocked the cell growth inhibitory effects of G-1. Silencing of G[alpha]i1 expression blocked GTP-binding of G[alpha] protein and the inhibitory effects of G-1 on PCa cell growth. These findings highlight the importance of activation of G[alpha]i1 protein and sustained Erk1/2 activation in the G-1-induced and GPR30-mediated cell growth inhibition in PCa cells. For Objective 3, we found that G-1 not only inhibited PCa cell growth but also impaired the cell metastatic properties by wound healing and transwell migration and invasion assays. Silencing of GPR30 abolished the G-1-induced inhibition of PCa cell migration and invasion, implying the involvement of GPR30 in the inhibitions. In addition, G-1 mediated GPR30 to reduce formations of filopodia and stress fibers in the cells, suggesting how activation of GPR30 influences PCa cell migration and invasion. These findings indicated the functional roles of GPR30 in controlling the PCa metastatic behaviors and provided evidence supporting development of GPR30-targeted therapy for PCa patients. By whole genome gene expression profiling, GPR30-regulated genes were identified and pathway analysis of these differentially expressed genes, we observed down-regulation of cell cycle-related genes including the regulators and machinery elements and up-regulation of genes involved in cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions, shedding light into the link between GPR30 and tumor immunity in PCa. Furthermore, RACGAP1 interactome was targeted by G-1 via GPR30 in PCa cells. In fact, down-regulation of these genes was reported to be associated with cancer cell migration and invasion and also metastatic status of clinical samples. Regarding Rho/Rac/cdc42 activations by G-1, we were unable to observe the activations using Cell Biolabs cdc42/Rac/Rho activation kits.

467612.label: Major findings and research outcome
467612.value: We demonstrated that G-1 activated GTP-binding of G[alpha]i1 protein but not G[alpha]s protein in PCa cells and the activation was mediated by GPR30. In addition, PCa cells predominantly express G[alpha]i1 protein and showed up-regulation in clinical tissue samples. This activation of G[alpha]i1 protein by G-1 is critical in maintaining the induced Erk1/2 activation in the cells. Silencing of G[alpha]i1 protein expression blocked the sustained Erk1/2 activation, resulting in blocking up-regulation of p21 and down-regulation of cyclin B1 expression in the cells and inhibitory effects of G-1 on PCa cell growth. Chemical modulations of AC-cAMP-PKA signaling influenced the duration of Erk1/2 activation and thus inhibition of cell growth by G-1 in PCa cells. As activation of GPR30 in breast cancer cells resulted in transient Erk1/2 activation due to the simultaneous activation of this signaling through G[alpha]s protein to attenuate Erk1/2 activity, our findings implied different G protein activation upon activation of GPR30 by G-1 in PCa cells, leading to different duration of Erk1/2 activation. It suggests cell content-dependency of GPR30 for different G protein coupling and activation. In addition, we comprehensively studied the global effects of G-1 on gene expression profiles of PCa cells. We verified our previous findings of down-regulations of G2 checkpoint regulators expression such as CCNA2, CCNB1, CDC25C, and CDK1 in the G-1-treated cells. Importantly, we demonstrated that G-1 also targeted cell cycle-related genes involved in DNA replication, various cell cycle checkpoints, transitions of mitotic cell cycle phases (G1 to S, G2 to M, and M to G1), chromosome segregation, and cytokinesis to inhibit the cell growth. In addition, G-1 up-regulated genes involved in cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions such as IL6, CXCL2, and CXCL3 that promotes neutrophil activation, accumulation, and recruitment, in line with the previously reported observations of neutrophil infiltration in the G-1-treated castration-resistant PCa xenografts. Finally, we demonstrated the inhibitory effects of GPR30 activation by G-1 on PCa metastatic properties, in contrast to the activation resulting in stimulation of breast cancer cell migration and invasion via CTGF. The G-1-induced inhibition in PCa is likely related to the reduced formations of filopodia and stress fibers in the cells and the reduction was mediated by GPR30. These findings revealed the functional roles of GPR30 in controlling PCa metastatic behaviors. In addition, we observed the down-regulation of GPR30-regulated genes involved in RACGAP1 interactome, potentially contributing the reductions of filopodia and stress fibers formations to impair PCa cell migration and invasion. All these findings lay critical foundations for developments of GPR30-targeted therapy for PCa patients in the near future.

467612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
467612.value: Our data suggested the cell content-dependency of GPR30 for coupling different G[alpha] proteins for different cellular responses upon the activation. In the literature, it was reported that different cancers responded to GPR30 activation with different cell fates. Stimulation of cell growth was observed in endometrial, ovarian, and thyroid cancers whereas the activation resulted in inhibition of bladder urothelial cell growth. Expression of G[alpha]i1 and G[alpha]s proteins in the cells could be a determining factor for cell-fate decision upon activation of GPR30 and investigations of their expression in different cancers along with the AC-cAMP-PKA signaling promote better understanding how GPR30 activated the downstream signaling for different cellular responses. In addition, we identified GPR30-regulated genes in PCa cells that are involved in Cell cycle and cytokine-cytokine interactions. Exact mechanism about how GPR30 regulates the gene expression remains unclear. Promoter analyses of these genes should be performed to gain insights on the regulations and networks of GPR30-mediated signaling in the cells.

467612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
467612.value: Estrogens play important roles in PCa therapies. Evidences indicate that estrogens, in addition to transcriptional regulations in nucleus, trigger rapid cellular responses through GRP30. Previously, we reported that activation of GPR30 by a selective GPR30 agonist, G-1, inhibited PCa growth with sustained Erk1/2 activation, in contrast to breast cancer cells that showed stimulation. Mechanism governing the responsiveness to G-1, either inhibitory or stimulatory, remains unclear. In this study, G-1, via GPR30, activated Gαi1 protein to sustain Erk1/2 activation. Furthermore, PCa predominantly expressed Gαi1, but not Gαs, protein whereas Gαs protein expression in breast cancer cells that previously showed Gαs protein activation by GPR30. Silencing of Gi1 expression blocked the inhibitory effects of G-1 on PCa cell growth. By gene expression profiling, G-1 interfered expression of cell cycle regulators and machinery elements to modulate PCa cell growth and the RACGAP1 interactome to control metastatic properties. In this regard, we demonstrated that G-1 inhibited PCa cell migration and invasion with reduced formations of filopodia and stress fibers. Taken together, our findings revealed the underlying mechanism for sustaining Erk1/2 activation upon GPR30 activation in PCa for cell growth inhibition and the GPR30-mediated pathways to control growth and metastatic properties of PCa cells.

467712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
467712.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder which is currently without effective treatment. Aggregation of amyloid-β peptide (Aβ) derived from the amyloid precursor protein (APP), is believed to be central to the pathogenesis of the disease. FE65 is a brain-enriched multi-domain adaptor protein which has been shown to interact with the cytoplasmic domain of APP and to alter APP processing and Aβ production. At present, the function of FE65 is still not entirely clear; however; it is generally believed that FE65 fulfills its roles by recruiting various binding partners to form functional complexes. In fact, a number of studies have shown that FE65 interacting proteins (FIPs) influence the functions of FE65 including APP metabolism. From a therapeutic perspective, targeting FIPs and/or FE65-FIP interactions could be a possible strategy for AD. To improve our understanding of the physiological and pathological roles of FE65, it is therefore essential to identify the full complement of FIPs. We have recently identified ADP-ribosylation factor 6 (ARF6), a small GTPase functions in the membrane trafficking between plasma membrane and endosomes, as a new FIP. Interestingly, APP has been shown to be trafficked between these two compartments, and endosomes are a major site for Aβ generation. As FE65 alters APP processing, we hypothesize that the interaction between FE65 and ARF6 modulates endocytic trafficking of APP, a process that affects APP processing. The primary objective of the proposed study is to investigate the role of the FE65-ARF6 interaction in relation to APP metabolism in particular APP trafficking and processing. Preliminary study from our laboratory suggests that FE65 can influence ARF6 activation, an essential process for regulating ARF6-mediated endocytic trafficking. The proposed work will give insight into the role of FE65-ARF6 interaction in APP metabolism in particular APP trafficking, and may provide essential information for the therapeutic development of AD. 阿爾茨海默氏病（AD）是一種破壞性的神經退化性疾病，目前並沒有有效的治療方法。由澱粉樣前體蛋白（APP）的剪切產物β澱粉樣肽（Aβ）所構成的聚集物，被認為是AD的主要發病機制。 FE65是一個在腦部富集的多結構域適配器蛋白，其已被證明與APP的胞質域有相互作用，從而影響APP的切割和Aβ產生。FE65的功能目前尚未完全明瞭，但研究者普遍認為，FE65透過與其他蛋白質的相互作用形成功能性的複合物來發揮其功用。事實上，一些研究已經表明，FE65的相互作用蛋白（FIPs）能夠影響FE65的功能如APP的代謝。從治療的角度來說，針對FIPS和/或FE65-FIP相互作用可能是一個可行的治療AD策略。為了增加對FE65的生理和病理作用的理解，我們有必要尋找所有細胞內的FIPs。我們最近發現ADP核糖基化因子6（ARF6）與FE65發生相互作用。ARF6是一個小GTP酶，是質膜和胞內體之間的小泡轉運調節者。研究顯示APP會在這兩個區域之間轉運，而胞內體是產生Aβ的主要區域。由於FE65影響APP的切割，我們假設FE65和ARF6之間的相互作用對APP的胞吞運輸具調節作用，從而影響APP的切割。本研究的主要目的是調查FE65-ARF6相互作用對APP的代謝，特別是APP的轉運和切割所帶來的影響。我們研究小組的初步結果表明，FE65可以調控ARF6的活性，而ARF6的活性對其所調節的胞吞運輸過程有直接影響。本建議書中所列出的實驗將幫助我們深入瞭解FE65-ARF6相互作用在APP的代謝，特別是APP的轉運中所發揮的作用。同時，我們的研究結果可能對AD的治療發展提供一些有用的信息。

467712.label: Realisation of objectives
467712.value: Objective 1: ARF6 is a novel FE65 interacting protein that is found in our laboratory from a yeast two-hybrid screen by using FE65 phosphotyrosine binding (PTB) 1+2 domains as “bait”. In this project, their interaction was confirmed by various biochemical assays including GST-fusion protein pull-down and co-immunoprecipitation assays. Moreover, their interaction was found to be mediated by FE65 PTB 1 domain and ARF6 residues 28-47 which contains the guanine nucleotide binding switch I. Furthermore, in vitro protein binding assay showed that FE65 and ARF6 interact directly. Our results indicate that FE65 and ARF6 interact directly and the interaction is mediated by the FE65 PTB1 and ARF6 residue 28-47. Similar to other small GTPases, ARF6 exists in a GTP bound active and a GDP-bound inactive state. These two states have distinct structures that alter the interactions between ARF6 and its binding proteins. Therefore, it is possible that FE65 binds differentially to these two states of ARF6. In fact, our data shows that FE65 preferentially interacts with GDP- but not GTP-bound ARF6. Typically, ARF effectors bind to ARF-GTP, and this suggests that FE65 does not function downstream of ARF6 as an effector protein. We therefore speculated that FE65 functions upstream to regulate ARF6 activation in some fashion. To test this possibility, we monitored the effect of modulating FE65 expression on the ARF6 activation. Overexpression of FE65 increased endogenous ARF6 activation (as detected using GGA3 pulldown ARF6 assays), whereas FE65 siRNA knockdown reduced ARF6 activation (Fig. 3A, B). These findings implicate that although it preferentially binds to ARF6-GDP form, FE65 promotes the activation of ARF6. Increasing evidence suggests that FE65 phosphorylation regulates FE65-interactor binding. To determine if FE65-ARF6 interaction modulates by FE65 phosphorylation, we attempted to identify novel FE65 phosphorylation sites. We have found two putative sites, FE65 Serine-459 (S459) and Serine-610 (S610). FE65 S459 is highly conserved in various species and is located within FE65 PTB1 domain. Since ARF6 interacts with FE65 PTB1, it is possible that S459 plays a role in controlling FE65-ARF6 interaction which in turn regulates FE65 mediated biological events including APP processing. To explore if FE65 S459 phosphorylation alters FE65-ARF6 interaction, we performed GST pull down and co-immunoprecipitation assays using FE65 phosphomimetic mutants. Both assays showed that FE65 S459 phosphorylation promotes FE65-ARF6 interaction. On the other hand, S610 is located in FE65 PTB2, a domain for APP interaction. In fact, we found that FE65 S610 phosphorylation reduces FE65-APP interaction and FE65-mediated APP processing (This part of study is published in Biochem J. 2015 Sep 15;470(3):303-17). Objective 2: In order to determine the subcellular localization of ARF6 in neurons, we have generated a rat anti-ARF6 antibody. The antibody was tested by Western blotting. We then enquired whether FE65 and ARF6 co-localize in developing neurons. Immunostaining for ARF6 revealed that it was principally a cytoplasmic protein in neurons that was enriched in perinuclear regions but also present in processes and growth cones. To determine whether FE65 and ARF6 co-localize in growth cones, we immunostained neurons and utilized intensity correlation analyses to determine whether there was significant overlap in the distribution of the two proteins in growth cones. ICA compares the scatter plots of two stains against the product of the difference of the pixel intensities of each of the two stains from their respective means. Thus, ICA determines whether the pixel intensities from two signals vary in synchrony and as such is superior to many other methods for determining the extent of co-localization of proteins in cells and tissues. The values obtained from the analyses can be reported as an intensity correlation quotient (ICQ), which is a statistically testable, single value assessment of the relationship between two stained protein pairs; for random staining ICQ=0, for dependent staining (co-localization) 0

467712.label: Major findings and research outcome
467712.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common fatal neurodegenerative disorder. Accumulating evidence indicates that altered production of amyloid-β peptide (Aβ), derived from the proteolytic cleavage of the amyloid precursor protein (APP), is crucial to AD pathogenesis. FE65 is a brain-enriched “scaffold” protein which has been shown to interact with APP and influences APP processing. A number of studies have shown that FE65 interacting proteins (FIPs) influence the functions of FE65 including APP metabolism. In this study, we have identified a novel FIP called ARF6. ARF6 is a small GTPase which is involved in endocytic protein trafficking. Noteworthy, endosome is a major subcellular compartment for Aβ generation. Therefore, identification of ARF6 as a FIP provide a new direction for our group to investigate FE65-mediated APP processing. We have fully characterized the FE65-ARF6 interaction and found that FE65 promotes ARF6 activation. Moreover, FE65-ARF6 interaction also activates Rac1, a small GTPase downstream of ARF6 and is implicated in APP processing. This work has been accepted for publication in FASEB Journal (publication 1 in part C). Additionally, FE65-ARF6 interaction promotes endocytic trafficking of APP and Aβ generation. Evidence suggests that FE65 functions can be regulated by phosphorylation including its interaction with FIP. In order to understand, how FE65-ARF6 interaction is regulated, we have attempted to identify FE65 phosphorylation sites. In this study, we have identified FE65 S459 and S610 as putative phosphorylation sites. Interestingly, FE65 S459 and S610 phosphorylation could alter FE65-ARF6 and FE65-APP interaction, respectively. Moreover, FE65 S610 phosphomimetic studies indicate that FE65 S610 phosphorylation reduces FE65-APP interaction and FE65 mediated APP processing This work has been published in Biochemical Journal (publication 3 in part C).

467712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
467712.value: In this project, we have shown that FE65 activates both ARF6 and Rac1, and ARF6-Rac1 signaling is mplicated in APP processing. Since it does not possess any GEF activities, the exact mechanism(s) that FE65 stimulates Rac1 remains elusive. Therefore, it is possible that FE65 recruits a GEFs to activate ARF6 and Rac1. Owing to different limitations of the classical approaches used for FE65 interactor identification, some crucial FE65 interactors may yet to be identified. Therefore, other approaches may be used, such as proximity-dependent biotin identification, to identify further FE65 interactors which may reveal how FE65 modulates APP processing via ARF6 and Rac1 activation. Although our study has revealed that FE65-ARF6 interaction is mediated by FE65 PTB1 and ARF6 residues 28-47, the exact interaction interface is still unknown. Therefore, determination of the complex structure of FE65 PTB1 and ARF6 is an important step in revealing how they interact. The new information will provide important insights into the identification of small molecules/peptides that block/reduce FE65-ARF6 interaction to lower Aβ generation. The suggested follow-up studies are crucial for the development of strategies to block FE65-ARF6 interaction for reducing Aβ generation.

467712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
467712.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common fatal neurodegenerative disorder. Accumulating evidence indicates that over-production of toxic amyloid-β peptide (Aβ), derived from the proteolytic cleavage of the amyloid precursor protein (APP), is an important process for the disease. Recent studies have shown that FE65 binds to APP to modulate the production of Aβ. However, how FE65 affects Aβ generation is not fully understood. In our study, we found that a small protein called ARF6 that binds to FE65. Importantly, we demonstrated that FE65 enhances ARF6 activity and alter the proteolytic cleavage of APP in various assay systems. Therefore, we have identified a new FE65 interacting protein that work together with FE65 to modulate Aβ generation. Our findings lay a foundation for exploring the potential of blocking the interaction between FE65 and ARF6 as a therapeutic approach for AD.

467812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
467812.value: This study aims to define the clinical history and significance of mitral leaflet (ML) adaptation in ischemic mitral regurgitation (IMR). Mitral regurgitation (MR) (leaking of left heart valve) frequently complicates myocardial infarction (MI) (heart attack) and is associated with doubled mortality and morbidity. Unfortunately, its mechanism is incompletely understood and treatment options are often limited and ineffective. It has been widely accepted that IMR is purely “functional”, because the ML appear grossly normal, but only tethered by left ventricular and annular dilatation, preventing adequate closure. Therefore, contemporary treatment of IMR focus mainly on annular and ventricular remodeling. However, the ML tissues are metabolically active capable of cell activation and matrix proteins production. Recent animal studies has suggested that the ML actively adapt to mechanical stretch by increasing its surface area and thickness, casting doubt on functional IMR being purely “functional”. In clinical settings, our understanding of the natural history of ML adaptation is very limited. Its incidence, timing, clinical significance, and interactions with annulus and ventricular remodeling remain undefined. The clinical data has been lacking because imaging techniques were previously unable to assess leaflet surface area in vivo. Recent advance in real-time 3-dimensional echocardiography (RT3DE) has enabled us to assess mitral valve 3D geometry non-invasively, providing a new way to study ML adaptation in clinical settings. We hypothesize that ML adaptation does occur in IMR after MI, attempting to increase in size to compensate for the tethering caused by ventricular and annular dilatation. To test this hypothesis, we will prospectively study 2 groups of patients presenting with MI, one group complicated with IMR, one group without. We will follow them up with serial RT3DE from the acute phase of MI to the chronic phase for 1 year. The 3D geometry of ML, annulus and left ventricle will be analyzed using a novel software developed and validated collaboratively by the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the University of Hong Kong. We will (1) compare the prospective changes of ML geometry between the 2 groups, (2) define the long-term natural history of ML adaptation, (3) explore how it is related to pathogenesis of IMR, and (4) identify potential factor(s) that affect ML adaptation. We believe the results of this project will significantly increase our knowledge on mitral valve adaptation in IMR. 467812.label: Realisation of objectives
467812.value: We have recruited 143 subjects with acute MI. A total of 104 and 98 subjects have completed 3D echo studies at 6 months and 1 year, respectively. Follow up rate was >90%. Analysis of 3D echo and clinical data has been completed in 88 subjects with a median follow-up duration of 378 days (range=174 days to 539 days). We have confirmed the clinical occurrence of mitral leaflet adaptation by demonstrating that the mitral leaflet area (MLA) increased significantly from baseline to 1 year after MI (12.2±3.2mm2 to 13.4±3.4mm2, p<0.001) (Objective 1). Natural history of mitral leaflet adaptation after MI was defined. Prospective mitral leaflet adaptation was evident in 55% of the MI population for up to 1 year after MI, with enlargement of the MLA by 24.2±20.5% (Objective 2). Leaflet adaptive enlargement in subjects with progression/persistence of IMR (n=47) was significantly less than that observed in subjects with regression of IMR (n=14) (0.9±2.6 vs. 3.4±1.3mm2, p=0.001). These findings suggested inadequate leaflet adaptive enlargement to compensate for leaflet tethering contributes to the development of IMR after MI (Objective 3). 3D echo measurement of mitral annulus, left ventricle and left atrium were obtained from all subjects for analysis of adaptive structural alteration taking placing in these structures and their relations with progression of IMR. We observed a significantly (p<0.05) remodelling of the left atrial volume and mitral leaflet tenting volume in the group of patients with MR regression (Objective 4). Clinical characteristics and therapeutic measures that may affect the occurrence and degree of IMR were also studied (Objective 5). Intriguingly, we found that the use of beta-blockers was significant (p<0.05) associated with favourable remodelling of the mitral valve and regression of IMR after MI. In summary, we have fulfilled all objectives of this project within the study timeline and the preliminary findings strongly support the hypothesis of mitral leaflet adaptation after MI. Potential therapeutic measures for IMR (e.g. beta-blockers) have been identified. We are proceeding with more detail analysis of these data and writing up of the manuscript is in progress. During the screening of patients with MR driven by this protocol, we have also enrolled patients with MR of other aetiologies such as degenerative mitral valve prolapse (MVP) to a valve registry with 3D echocardiography performed on these patients, and was able to generate a good number of publications from these registry data. We have also performed 3D transesophageal echocardiography as clinically indicated in a subset of our patients. In the later part of the project, a new technology known as 3D printing has emerged that allows conversion of digital 3D echocardiographic data sets into tangible 3D objects. The 3D dataset obtained by 3D TEE were used in a subset of patients to develop this technology. We have successfully used this technology to create cardiovascular models of the mitral valve, the left atrial appendage, and the atrial septum for personalised planning of surgical and interventional procedures.

467812.label: Major findings and research outcome
467812.value: A total of 15 full paper on peer-reviewed journals and 8 abstracts in international scientific conferences arose directly from the research project. These research outputs include 2 paper published on journals with impact factor >10 (Circulation, European Heart Journal) and 4 papers on journals with impact factor >6 (JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging, JACC: Cardiovascular Intervention, Circulation: Cardiovascular Intervention, and Journal of American Society of Echocardiography). In these paper, novel mechanisms and therapeutic targets of mitral regurgitation were discovered with the use of high-resolution time-resolved 3D echocardiography. In patients with degenerative MR, we discovered that flattening of the annular saddle shape is associated with progressive leaflet billowing and increased frequencies of chordal rupture and may be important in the pathogenesis of MR in mitral valve prolapse. In addition, we described that the disjunctive annulus is decoupled functionally from the ventricle, leading to paradoxical annular dynamics with systolic expansion and flattening, and may thus require specific intervention. The research project has given rise to several research awards. These include the Distinguished Research Fellow 2016 and Richard Yu Lectureship 2015 awarded to the PI by the Hong Kong College of Physicians; top scoring abstracts awarded to the research group and the PhD student of the PI by the American Society of Echocardiography, the American Heart Association, the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging at the respective annual scientific conferences. A current PhD student was awarded the Young Investigator Award First Prize at the Asian-Pacific Association of Echocardiography Annual Scientific Meeting in 2016, based on her research in 3D echo and 3D printing partially supported by this project. 3D echo data set obtained from this project has led to 2 successful applications of the Innovation and Technology Fund Tier 3 in 2014 (as co-I) and 2017 (as PI). Initial results of the 3D printing study derived from this project were published and a press conference was held in May 2016, attracting wide media coverage. A video describing our findings was produced with the support of the research council one-off impact write up funding and was uploaded to the RGC channel for promoting public awareness.

467812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
467812.value: In future research, our group will focus on the mechanism underlying mitral leaflet adaptation of patients with MI and IMR. An important discovery from our data is that beta-blockade appears to have a long-term therapeutic effect on IMR. A larger prospective clinical trial to test the beneficial effect of beta-blockade on IMR is warranted and underway.

467812.value: This research project has successfully defined the clinical history and significance of mitral leaflet adaptation in ischemic mitral regurgitation (IMR). Mitral regurgitation (MR) (leaking of left heart valve) frequently complicates myocardial infarction (MI) (heart attack) and is associated with doubled mortality and morbidity. 468112.label: Realisation of objectives
468112.value: The objects of this study: (1) To investigate the anti-inflammatory effects of macrolide treatment in patients with influenza lower respiratory tract infections and the impact on viral clearance; and (2) To investigate the impact of macrolide treatment on influenza symptom and disease resolution, are met. In this randomized trial, we aimed to investigate anti-inflammatory effects of macrolide therapy in severe influenza infections in adults. Patients receiving oseltamivir and adjunctive azithromycin were compared with those receiving oseltamivir alone on cytokines/chemokines and pro-inflammatory mediator changes, viral clearance, and symptom resolution; safety profiles were also assessed. Recruited patients were randomly allocated, at 1:1 ratio, to one of the study treatments: (1) azithromycin 500mg daily and oseltamivir 75mg bid for 5 days, both given orally, or (2) oral oseltamivir 75mg bid alone for 5 days. Peripheral blood samples (10 ml EDTA) were collected at baseline (Day 0), at time of completion of treatment (Day 5) and at convalescence (Day 10) for cytokine/chemokine and pro-inflammatory mediator assays. Serial nasopharyngeal flocked swabs (NPFS) were collected at similar time points with standardized techniques for viral load assays (Day 0, 2, 5, and 10). In addition, we performed ex-vivo experiments on inhibition of cytokine response and signal transduction with azithromycin. Altogether 50 patients were randomized to receive either oseltamivir-azithromycin (n=25) or oseltamivir (n=25) treatments. Oseltamivir-azithromycin treated patients were found to have a faster decline in IL-6 (β -0.037, 95%CI -0.067,-0.007, P=0.016), CXCL8/IL-8 (β -0.018, 95%CI -0.037,0.000, P=0.056), IL-17 (β -0.064, 95%CI -0.117,-0.012, P=0.015), and CXCL9/MIG (β -0.010, 95%CI -0.020,0.000, P=0.043) concentrations over time; trends were also shown for sTNFR-1, IL-18, and CRP (Table 2, Figure 1a-f). The percentage reduction in their concentrations from baseline was: IL-6 (-83.4% and -59.5%), CXCL8/IL-8 (-80.5% and -58.0%), IL-17 (-74.0% and -34.3%), and CXCL9/MIG (-71.3% and -56.0%), in the oseltamivir-azithromycin and oseltamivir treated patients respectively. These cytokines’ concentrations were shown to correlate significantly with hypoxemia, tachypnea, and high symptom scores (Table 2 footnotes). No significant difference in IFN-γ and CXCL10/IP-10 decline rates was found. A trend in symptom score reduction was observed (β -0.463, 95%CI-1.297,0.371, P=0.277; percentage reduction from baseline: -79.0% and -70.4% respectively), as well as reduced fever duration and length-of-stay in hospital, but these did not reach statistical significance (Figure 2a)[the median (IQR) of fever duration was 1.0 (0.0-2.0) and 2.0 (1.0-2.0) days, P=0.090; length-of-stay was 4.0 (3.5-6.0) and 5.0 (3.5-6.0) days; and 4.0% and 8.0% had required extended care, respectively]. There was no death in this study. We found no significant difference in viral RNA load change over time (P=0.777), or culture-negativity by day 5 between treatment groups (Figure 2b). The study treatments were generally well tolerated. One patient stopped azithromycin after 3 days because of dizziness, which subsided spontaneously. Incidence of adverse events was similar between the two arms (Table 1). No adverse cardiovascular event was recorded. PBMCs from influenza patients were stimulated with RLR ligand poly(I:C)/LyoVec ex vivo, with or without azithromycin co-incubation. There was induction of IL-6 (P=0.007), CXCL8/IL-8 (P=0.007), CCL2/MCP-1 (P=0.010), CCL5/RANTES (P=0.026), CXCL10/IP-10 (P=0.051), and phosphorylated p38 MAPK (P=0.029) expression by the RLR ligand. The addition of azithromycin resulted in significant inhibition of induction of IL-6 (P=0.017) and CXCL8/IL-8 (P=0.005). A trend of inhibition was shown for p38 MAPK (P=0.061) (Figure 3). We found no significant inhibition of CXCL10/IP-10 or other adaptive cytokines ex vivo. In this randomized trial, we found faster downregulation of the pro-inflammatory cytokine responses in influenza patients with adjunctive azithromycin treatment; viral clearance was not impaired, which was important when considering immunomodulation in infectious diseases. The trend on faster symptom resolution was insignificant, but was likely related to the small sample size, and the study was underpowered to detect differences in clinical variables. Our results indicate the potential of macrolide as an adjunctive treatment for severe influenza infection, which warrant evaluation for clinical efficacy and impacts on disease course. Such information is one of the first to reveal the potential of macrolide for the management of severe influenza, and provide important insights into future adjunctive therapy research. Studies on individual macrolide, the dosing regimens, combinations with other antivirals and/or anti-inflammatory agents, the risk-benefit ratio; and macrolide’s effects on other soluble mediators, cellular immunity, and intracellular signaling pathways such as the MAPKs and mechanistic-target-of-rapamycin (mTOR) should be considered. The strengths of our study include randomization and balanced baseline characteristics, and robust analyses of cytokine and viral load changes over time. It is limited by the small subject number, which is largely due to the exclusion of the immunocompromised and corticosteroid-treated (since we aimed to analyze cytokine changes), and all patients at increased cardiovascular risk, because of reported cardiac arrhythmia/death with erythromycin, clarithromycin, and recently azithromycin, though the absolute risk is small (<0.025% even in high-risk individuals). A recent study on elderly hospitalized with pneumonia showed that survival benefit with azithromycin treatment might outweigh the small cardiovascular risk; others studies showed similar results or no excessive risk.

468112.label: Major findings and research outcome
468112.value: [Please also refer to the output of (1) publication and (2) conference abstract in Part C.] Macrolides can ameliorate inflammation in respiratory diseases, providing clinical benefits. Data in influenza is lacking. A randomized, open-label, multicenter trial among adults hospitalized for laboratory-confirmed influenza was conducted. Study treatments of oseltamivir and azithromycin (500mg/day), or oseltamivir alone, both for 5 days, were allocated at 1:1 ratio. The primary outcome was plasma cytokine/chemokine concentration change over time (Day 0-10); secondary outcomes were viral load and symptom score changes. Generalized Estimating Equation (GEE) models were used to analyze longitudinal data. Major findings and conclusions: Fifty patients were randomized to the oseltamivir-azithromycin or oseltamivir groups, with comparable baseline characteristics (age, 57+/-18 years; A/H3N2, 70%), complications (72%), and viral load. Pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 (GEE: β -0.037, 95%CI-0.067,-0.007, P=0.016; reduction from baseline -83.4% vs -59.5%), CXCL8/IL-8 (β -0.018, 95%CI-0.037,0.000, P=0.056; -80.5% vs -58.0%), IL-17 (β -0.064, 95%CI-0.117,-0.012, P=0.015; -74.0% vs -34.3%), CXCL9/MIG (β -0.010, 95%CI-0.020,0.000, P=0.043; -71.3% vs -56.0%), sTNFR-1, IL-18, and CRP declined faster in the oseltamivir-azithromycin group. There was a trend toward faster symptom resolution (β -0.463, 95%CI-1.297,0.371). Viral RNA decline (P=0.777) and culture-negativity rates were unaffected. Additional ex vivo studies confirmed reduced induction of IL-6 (P=0.017) and CXCL8/IL-8 (P=0.005) with azithromycin. In conclusion, we found significant anti-inflammatory effects with adjunctive macrolide treatment in adults with severe influenza infections. Virus control was unimpaired. Clinical benefits of a macrolide-containing regimen deserve further study.

468112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
468112.value: Our study indicated that macrolide adjunctive treatment can downregulate the pro-inflammatory responses while preserving viral clearance in influenza infections. Our data suggested that clinical benefits of a macrolide-containing regimen should deserve further study in this population. Studies on individual macrolide, the dosing regimens, combinations with other antivirals and/or anti-inflammatory agents, the risk-benefit ratio; and macrolide’s effects on other soluble mediators, cellular immunity, and intracellular signaling pathways such as the MAPKs and mechanistic-target-of-rapamycin (mTOR) should also be considered.

468312.label: Project Title(Chinese)
468312.value: 長非編碼RNA在精原幹細胞老化發展過程調控

468312.label: Project Objectives
468312.value: To identify lncRNA candidates that demonstrate age-dependent expression pattern (Age-lncRNA) in undifferentiated SSC population. Based on GermSAGE and TileMapper analysis of male germ cell transcriptome, we identified a set of spermatogoinia-specific transcripts without protein-coding evidence. By applying lncRNA prediction algorithms, we have predicted a set of spermatogonia-specifc lncRNAs that demonstrated age-dependent expression pattern in SCC cell line and undifferentiated mouse SSC population. We will apply next-gen sequencing to identify more complex Age-lncRNA candidates by using established SSC aging models. To determine regulatory mechanisms and biological consequences associated with Age-lncRNAs regulation. Based on our preliminary data on Age-lncRNA2, we postulate that Age-lncRNAs are regulated by specific signaling pathway or transcriptional regulators. Transcriptional regulations and signaling networks associated with Age-lncRNA will be explored by different bioinformatics approaches. To identify biological function of Age-lncRNAs in aging SSCs, SSC isolation and transplantation will be used to delineate the functional role(s) of Age-lncRNAs in SSC development. To develop a public Age-lncRNA database (lncRNAge) portal. We will develop a public database resource that allows Age-lncRNA search and retrival.

468312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468312.value: 近年來, 生育年齡普遍延遲, 高齡夫婦生育人群數量逐年升高。人們普遍認為卵子老化是高齡產婦更高出生缺陷率的主要成因, 而高齡父親對後代的影響往往被忽視。哺乳動物的精子發生可以分為三個階段: 精原細胞的有絲分裂增殖階段, 精母細胞的減數分裂階段和精子細胞的成熟階段。這個複雜的過程源於位於睾丸基底膜上的精原幹細胞。隨著男性年齡的增長，體內各種分子、細胞、組織以及器官的損傷會不斷的積累，從而逐漸喪失功能, 而精原幹細胞作為精子發生的基礎, 任何由於衰老導致的缺陷都將傳給後代。因此, 開展對精原幹細胞衰老的研究極為重要。雖然近年來人類基因組學和細胞生物學的進展迅猛, 但此領域研究主要關注編碼RNA, 對精原幹細胞發育調控的研究進展十分有限。本研究擬從全新角度探索衰老對精原幹細胞的影響。長鏈非編碼RNA (long noncoding RNA,) 是一類無或少有蛋白編碼能力的複雜長鏈非編碼RNA, 其轉錄本長度一般超過200nt的RNA分子, 其在調節生長發育, 細胞定向分化, 亞細胞結構分佈過程中均有重要作用。儘管如此, lncRNA在衰老對精子發生及精原幹細胞發育調控中的作用尚不清楚且缺乏系統研究。 本課題組先前的研究通過比較不同年齡小鼠精原幹細胞的轉錄組, 結合自組開發的生物信息學工具GermSAGE 和TileMapper, 發現了一個新的睾丸特異 lncRNA (Age-lncRNA2), 且其表達水平與年齡密切相關。由此, 我們推測lncRNA極有可能參與精原幹細胞衰老調控。本研究擬以這些前期工作為基礎，以期篩選出一系列與此相關的lncRNA, 並對其在精原幹細胞衰老過程中的作用及其調控機制進行全面探索。 本開創性課題將填補對lncRNA調控精原幹細胞衰老的研究空白。研究預期結果將有助於進一步深入了解高齡父親對後代的影響, 揭示lncRNA參與精原幹細胞衰老調控的機制, 為精原幹細胞體外增殖和保存及男性不育治療開拓思路, 並為lncRNA在幹細胞發育, 生殖過程中的功能帶來新的認識。

468312.label: Realisation of objectives
468312.value: The three major objectives have been largely addressed and led to novel findings, collaborations and publications. With reference to objective 1, we have established aging mouse model to collect spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) from neonatal and adult stages for transcriptome analysis by RNA-seq. A bioinformatics pipeline known as hybrid transcriptome assembly (HTA) was developed to identify unique long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) that exhibit age-dependent expression patterns. HTA provides a number of advantages to conventional lncRNA annotations. It allows identification of SSC-specific lncRNAs by filtering non-germ cell transcripts. Of the 150,084 lncRNAs (linear and circular forms) identified, majority (58.7%, 8862 lncRNAs) belongs to existing annotated linear lncRNAs. Interestingly, we identified 2804 novel linear lncRNAs (18.6%) that could not be annotated, suggesting they could be SSC-specific. The rest (22.7%, 3423 lncRNAs) fell into circular RNAs (circRNAs) category. To better delineate the biological importance of lncRNAs, functional prediction (cis-regulation, trans-regulation, co-expression, small RNAs precursor and targeted microRNAs), expression dynamics and regulatory features in terms of RNA secondary structure and epigenetic modifications (DNA and histones). Selected lncRNA candidates were validated for stage-specific expression by real- time PCR and size confirmation by Northern Blot. All data were deposited to GermAGE, a lncRNA database for studying male germ cell aging (objective 3). For objective 2, systematic identification in objective 1 has led to identification of 107 age-associated lncRNAs (Age-lncRNAs) in SSC development. These are annotated lncRNAs that did not exhibit SSC specificity (Publication 1&2). We successfully established potential regulatory mechanisms of Age-lncRNAs may regulate SSC functions through different cellular mechanisms, including binding with RNA binding protein, as illustrated by Gas5/ Hsp90ab1 complex (Publication 3), cis-regulatory interaction illustrated Msi1 by (Publication 4) and acting on transcription factor Foxfl1a by Fendrr (Publication 5). The findings were validated by in vitro (neonatal and adult SSC cultures) and in vivo platforms (SSC transplantation). Despite the project has led to the above interesting findings, we encountered technical difficulties on proving CeRNA regulation proposed in the application. Concordant with our previous findings on mouse embryonic stem cells, we narrowed down a number of Age-lncRNA that may exhibit CeRNA function through competitive binding to microRNAs targeting Tet1, a key enzyme in regulating active demethylation pathway. Preliminary experiment using 3T3 cell was successful. However, transfection efficiency in adult SSC culture setup was extremely low. Therefore, the validation took longer than expected, but we are confident that this part can be completed within six months as we have got positive preliminary data with lentivirus transfection platform. For objective 3, we have successfully established the first public online resource (GermAge) for aging SSCs (http://germage.cbiit.cuhk.edu.hk/) that allow searching, visualizing, downloading and analyzing mouse SSCs. A comprehensive information on the background, methodology and significance is provided on the website (http://germage.cbiit.cuhk.edu.hk/index.php/site/page/view/help). In summary, GermSAGE provides an integrated summary on undifferentiated SSCs of mice of different ages. We believe this resource will help scientists identifying importance lncRNAs species associated with aging.

We will apply next-gen sequencing to identify more complex Age-lncRNA candidates by using established SSC aging models.

To determine regulatory mechanisms and biological consequences associated with Age-lncRNAs regulation. Based on our preliminary data on Age-lncRNA2, we postulate that Age-lncRNAs are regulated by specific signaling pathway or transcriptional regulators. Transcriptional regulations and signaling networks associated with Age-lncRNA will be explored by different bioinformatics approaches. To identify biological function of Age-lncRNAs in aging SSCs, SSC isolation and transplantation will be used to delineate the functional role(s) of Age-lncRNAs in SSC development.

468312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
468312.value: Spermatogenic failure is a major cause of male infertility, which affects millions of couples worldwide, and aging of spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) is believed to be a major factor that contributes to male infertility. A Recent discovery of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) as critical regulators in normal and disease development provides new clues for delineating the molecular regulation in male germ cell development. However, few functional lncRNAs have been characterized. Using mouse aging model, we aimed to decode the key age-dependent lncRNAs critical for SSC function. We developed a new approach called Hybrid Transcriptome Assembly (HTA) for identifying important lncRNAs in male germ cell development and deposited to a public database known as GermAGE (http://germage.cbiit.cuhk.edu.hk). Germage provides the first comprehensive web-based and open-access lncRNA catalogue for male germ cell aging. The intriguing results of this study have provided an important foundation for focusing on specific aspects of lncRNA regulations during SSC aging, and led to the discovery of novel aging targets associated with male infertility/subfertility.

468912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468912.value: 血管緊張素II是腎素血管緊張素系統(RAS)中具有生理活性的多肽，與高血壓及二型糖尿病具有緊密聯繫。目前，在成熟的胰腺胰島細胞中發現有具有功能性RAS的存在。眾所周知RAS可以調節不同種類幹細胞/祖細胞的發育，而RAS是否存在于胰島beta細胞中及其對發育過程的作用仍需要更多的研究和探索。與此同時我們知道，活性氧(ROS)是由氧分子不完全代謝產生的副產品，它們的存在造成氧化應激反應，尤其對胰島細胞的活性和功能的維持具有危害作用。近期的研究顯示生理濃度的ROS具有二級信使的功能並調節細胞信號通路。 不同來源的ROS產物使它們具有成形素的功能，在時間和空間的不同方面推動各組織祖細胞的發育。因此，ROS的這些潛在的作用或許能夠促進胰腺祖細胞(PPC)向具有功能的胰島細胞發育，進而在糖尿病病人胰島移植治療方面發揮作用。一種ROS的來源是由血管緊張素II與其相應的受體：血管緊張素II一型及二型受體(AT1 或AT2受體)介導產生的，并激活一系列生成ROS的酶。此現象顯示出局部血管緊張素II誘導的ROS產物在PPC分化過程中扮演重要角色。近期一些研究也顯示血管緊張素II能夠促進胚胎幹細胞，間葉細胞幹細胞，以及胚胎器官形成過程中的增生，分化和營養代謝。綜上所述，根據已有的發現，我們假設在胰腺祖細胞PPC中存在一個局部的RAS,自主分泌血管緊張素II,調控ROS產物以調節PPC的發育，并提供PPC發育成胰島beta細胞過程中所需的重要信號因子。為了檢測這一假設，我們首先將通過體外及體內的實驗描繪在PPC的生長和分化中RAS各組分的表達及其對ROS的影響。其次，通過調節beta細胞轉錄因子及下游信號通路來研究ROS產物如何影響PPC的發育和分化。我們的研究將提供PPC發育調節過程的新機制，并為PPC向胰島素分泌細胞的分化提供新穎的誘導方法，從而使誘導成功的胰島細胞能夠應用在糖尿病人胰島移植的治療中。
