468912.label: Major findings and research outcome
468912.value: (1). In this report, we had an intensive investigation into the effects of C21, a non-peptide angiotensin II type 2 receptor (AT2R) agonist, on islet cell function and survival in streptozotocin (STZ)-treated neonatal rats and human pancreatic progenitor cells (PPCs). (2). Our major research findings are as follows: the C21-treated STZ rats, particularly in the 0.5 and 1 mg/kg dosage groups, had significantly decreased blood glucose and increased serum insulin concentrations, relative to the STZ group; these C21-treated rats also exhibited significantly higher glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) activity, relative to the STZ group, in response to a high-glucose challenge. In addition, C21-treated rats had greater islet-cell mass and up-regulated expression of Insulin and Ngn3 mRNA in the pancreas than STZ rats. Furthermore, STZ+C21-treated rats exhibited increased β-cell proliferation, lower superoxide levels, and enhanced mRNA expression of SOD1, as well as up-regulated phospho-AKT expression; consistently, similar results were also observed in human PPCs.

468912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
468912.value: Future development of the proposed research may include the actions, particularly in relation to the elucidation of the AT2R and ACE2 pathways, as follows: (1). to decode the complex regulatory mechanisms in pancreas organogenesis; (2). to establish a simple yet effective and reproducible in vitro assays to delineate ACE2 axis effects on PPC differentiation and functional ICC maturation in vitro and in vivo; (3). to define the factors/mechanisms that regulate ACE2-induced differentiation of PPCs into ICCs; (4). to confirm whether ACE2 axis components introduced by gene delivery could achieve β-cell regeneration; (5). to clarify the ability of transplanted ICCs produced by ACE2 axis to improve hyperglycemia and glucose tolerance in diabetes models; last but not least, (6). to explore whether the AT2R and ACE2 axes interact with each other locally in determining β-cell mass in ICCs.

468912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
468912.value: Differentiation of pancreatic stem/progenitor cells into insulin-expressing and functional cells that is suitable for clinical islet transplantation opens an avenue for the replacement of glucose-responsive insulin-producing cells in patients with type 1 and/or severe form of type 2 diabetes. Given that the generation of functionally transplantable islet beta-cells has proven to have inherent obstacle, elucidation of the local renin-angiotensin system (RAS) with a mechanism-based approach in islet cell regeneration and differentiation has a clinical significance and value in propelling forward the development of pancreatic stem/progenitor cells and β-cell regeneration. Our study results obtained from this project provide a scientific merit for the undiscovered functional roles of the RAS, particularly the interaction between the classical ACE/AngII/AT1R axis and the newly characterized ACE2/Ang-(1-7)/Mas axis in the proliferation, differentiation, and maturation of pancreatic stem/progenitor cells. In light of these findings and previous reports from other laboratories, it is plausible to propose that the AT1R stimulation could be a repair/regeneration mechanism, involving the AT2R as well as the ACE2/Ang-(1-7)/Mas axis in directing the proliferation and differentiation of the β-cell development in diabetic patients. If confirmed, potential target for the genetic and pharmaceutical manipulation of the RAS may open up an avenue to treating and even curing T1DM/T2DM patients.

469712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
469712.value: In the recent decades, the use of herbal products has been rapidly growing worldwide. Unfortunately, their use in many cases causes adverse effects/toxicities leading to a global concern on safety of herbal medicines and herbal products including functional foods and dietary supplements. Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs), which have been identified in over 6,000 plants worldwide, are one of the most common causes of natural product poisonings in human. It has been reported that about half of PAs are hepatotoxic and many can cause hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (HSOS) in humans. Toxic PAs require metabolic activation to generate pyrrolic metabolites, which bind with cellular macromolecules to form pyrrole-protein adducts leading to hepatotoxicity. However, numerous cases of PA intoxications are reported yearly due to the consumption of PA-containing foods, plants, and plant products, including herbal medicines, teas, and dietary supplements. Apparently, the uncontrollable intoxication is largely ascribed to two factors; (i) a total amount of toxic PAs present in an herbal plant/product, which in most cases contains multiple PAs of different types, cannot be quantified or even estimated because all the PA standards are unavailable; and (ii) the chemical structural specificity towards metabolic activation and metabolic factors that can affect toxic potency of PA-containing products are still not fully understood, although the relationships between the toxicity of PAs and their structural and chemical features have been studied for several decades. The applicants have been studying PA-induced hepatotoxicity for many years. We are the first to determine serum pyrrole-protein adducts in HSOS patients exposed to a PA-containing Chinese medicinal herb. As a continuation of our study, we propose two aims in this proposal: (i) to establish an applicable method for quantifying total amount of PAs in PA-containing Chinese medicinal herbs and natural products without need of all reference PAs; and (ii) to delineate the structural and metabolic factors that affect the pyrrole-protein adducts formation. These aims can not only help to better understand the mechanism of PA intoxications, but also establish a mechanism-based approach to quantify total toxic PAs associated with PA-containing herbal products intoxication. If funded, it is anticipated that the results to be obtained from this proposed study are timely and important for quantifying total toxic PAs and assessing PA-induced hepatotoxicity in PA-containing Chinese herbal plants and natural products. The results will certainly benefit Hong Kong, the Mainland China, and global public health in safety control and prevention of PA-containing products intoxication. 近年来，植物药产品在世界各地的使用正迅猛地增长。然而，植物药以及相关产品，比如功能性食品和营养保健品，在一些情况下也会产生不良反应甚至引起毒性。因此，植物药以及相关产品的安全性已经引起了全球性的关注。吡咯里西啶生物碱是一类非常常见的在人体中能引起中毒反应的化合物，世界各地超过6000种植物中已经鉴定出这类化合物的存在。据报道，大约有一半的吡咯里西啶生物碱是具有肝毒性的，在人体上会引起肝窦阻塞综合症（HSOS）。吡咯里西啶生物碱本身没有毒性，但是在肝脏代谢后可产生吡咯中间代谢物，这种代谢产物可以与细胞内大分子结合，形成吡咯-蛋白质加合物，从而引起急性肝毒性。不幸的是，每年都会有很多由于食用含有或污染吡咯里西啶生物碱的食物，植物以及相关产品引起的中毒事件的报道。很显然，这种无法避免的中毒事件主要归因于两个因素：首先没有一种方法可以定量甚至估算在某种草药或者相关产品中所含的毒性吡咯里西啶生物碱的总量，因为在大多数情况下同一种植物中含有多种不同类型的吡咯里西啶生物碱，而获得所有标准品来测定其含量亦几乎不可能；其次，尽管关于吡咯里西啶生物碱的结构特性与其毒性的关系的研究已经进行了很多年，但是结构与代谢毒性的确切关系以及代谢因素对毒性强弱的影响等方面的机理仍然没有很好的解释。 本研究组已经对由吡咯里西啶生物碱引起的肝毒性进行了很多年的研究。我们第一次在服用含有吡咯里西啶生物碱的中药材引起HSOS的患者的血清中检测到了吡咯-蛋白质加合物。作为这一研究课题的延续和深入，本课研究中我们将进一步研究以下两个课题：(i)，建立一个合适的方法用来对含有吡咯里西啶生物碱的中药材和天然产物中的吡咯里西啶生物碱的总量进行定量；(ii)，阐明结构以及代谢方面的因素和吡咯里西啶生物碱代谢毒性的关系。其研究结果不仅可以让我们更好的理解吡咯里西啶生物碱的中毒原理，而且将会根据毒性机理建立一个有效的方法用来量化从而可以限制使用天然产物中吡咯里西啶生物碱的总量。 本课题预期的研究结果会对量化中药以及其它天然产物中吡咯里西啶生物碱总量以及评价它们的肝毒性起到重要的作用。其研究结果显然会对香港，中国内地，以及世界的公共健康，植物药的安全管理，和预防吡咯里西啶生物碱的中毒等方面起到非常积极的作用。

469712.label: Realisation of objectives
469712.value: Both objectives have been successfully accomplished. For the objective 1, we have developed a rapid, selective, and sensitive UPLC-QTOF-MS method for quantifying total PAs without requiring all corresponding standards. The established method has been fully validated and successfully applied for the quantitation of total PAs in various PA-containing herbs. This newly developed novel method is rapid, convenient, selective, and sensitive, with the advantage of not requiring all corresponding standards. Therefore, it is suitable for a high-throughput screening of PAs in herbal plants and also in PA-contaminated natural products. It provides a novel approach and facilitates quality control of PA-containing herbs/foodstuffs. For the objective 2, the delineation of toxic mechanism of PAs has been conducted in both in vivo and in vitro models. We provided, for the first time, the direct evidence supporting that hepatotoxicity of PAs are induced by the reactive metabolites (DHPAs) rather than the parent PAs, and the toxic mechanism is the metabolic activation mediated by hepatic CYPs to generate DHPAs, which rapidly reacts with proteins to form pyrrole-protein adducts, leading to hepatotoxicity. Our results proved that such metabolic activation to form pyrrole-protein adducts only occurred in PAs having unsaturated necine base, but not in PAs with saturated necine base, and also demonstrated, for the first time, the absence of metabolic activation to form pyrrole-protein adducts of non-toxic platynecine-type PAs (having saturated necine base) in the animal model. Our findings revealed that the primary factors affecting toxic potency of PAs include 1) structural specificity in necine base; 2) structual specificity in necic acid; and 3) CYP ioszyme selectivity in mediating metabolic activation.

469712.label: Major findings and research outcome
469712.value: To date, about 660 PAs have been identified in over 6,000 plants worldwide. PAs are one of the most common causes of natural product poisonings in human. It is well known that natural products normally contain multiple PAs, while the standards for the majority of 660 PAs are unavailable. Therefor, the total content of PAs in natural products including PA-containing herbs and PA-contaminated foodstuffs is difficult to be quantified. In the present work, we have developed a rapid, selective, and sensitive UPLC-QTOF-MS method for the quantitation of PAs without requiring all corresponding standards. The established novel method has been fully validated and successfully applied for the quantitation of total toxic PAs in various PA-containing herbs (Ref 2, 7 in Item 8; Ref 6, 13 in Item 9). Although PA metabolism-induced hepatotoxicity has been known for a long time, our study provided, for the first time, the direct evidence to prove that PAs require metabolic activation to generate toxic metabolites, DHPAs, which bind with cellular macromolecules to form pyrrole-protein adducts leading to hepatotoxicity (Ref 3 in Item 8; Ref 5 in Item 9). We also revealed that the chemical structural specificity towards the metabolic activation and the selectivity of hepatic enzymes mediating the metabolic activation could significantly affect the toxic potency of PAs (Ref 1, 4-6, 8-9 in Item 8; Ref 3-4, 7, 10-11, 17 in Item 9).

469712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
469712.value: Firstly, our newly developed rapid, selective, and sensitive UPLC-QTOF-MS method with the advantage of not requiring all corresponding PA standards is suitable for a high-throughput screening of toxic PAs in herbal plants and PA-contaminated natural products. Therefore, as a novel approach, it has a potential to be accepted globally to screen and predict PA intoxication risk and facilitate quality control of PA-containing herbs/foodstuffs. Secondly, our findings on the toxic mechanism and key factors affecting the toxic potency of different PAs will certainly help for the future development of specific biomarkers for the clinical use and appropriate risk assessment of PA intoxication.

469712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
469712.value: The use of natural products has been rapidly growing worldwide. Unfortunately, their use may cause adverse effects/toxicities leading to a global concern on their safety. Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs), which have been identified in over 6,000 plants, are one of the most common causes of natural product poisonings. Numerous cases of human PA intoxications are reported yearly via consumption of PA-containing plants and PA-contaminated foodstuffs. Apparently, the uncontrollable PA intoxication is largely ascribed to PAs present in natural product, which in most cases contains multiple PAs of different types, but cannot be quantified because all the PA standards are usually unavailable. We have developed a new analytical method without requiring all PA standards, and thus can rapidly determine a total PA content in natural products. PAs require metabolic activation to generate toxic metabolites, which bind with cellular proteins leading to hepatotoxicity. However, the detailed factors affecting toxicity of PAs are largely unknown. Our work identified key chemical structural specificity and hepatic enzyme selectivity affecting toxic potency of PAs. Therefor, using our research outcomes to measure content and toxic severity of PAs, the toxic potency of PA-containing natural products can be rapidly determined in the future.

469912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
469912.value: Pancreatic cancer is one of the most lethal human malignancies. Current available anti-pancreatic cancer therapies are largely unsatisfactory owing to pancreatic cancer’s intrinsic resistance to chemotherapeutic agents. Today, pancreatic cancer has an extremely low 5-year survival rate (<3%), thus effective treatment of pancreatic cancer remains an unmet medical need. Ten commonly prescribed anti-cancer Chinese herbs were screened in our initial project for their anti-pancreatic cancer action using a panel of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell lines including PANC-1, SW1990 and CAPAN-1. We found that the fruit of Brucea javanica (L.) Merr. (Fructus Bruceae), a quassinoids-rich Chinese herb, to be highly effective cytotoxic agent on cultured pancreatic cancer cells. Further experiments also revealed that brucein D (BD), a quassinoid present abundantly in Fructus Bruceae, possessed potent pancreatic cancer cell growth inhibitory action via the induction of cellular apoptosis, while exerting only modest cytotoxicity on normal human fibroblast Hs68 cells. Further mechanistic studies showed that the activation of p38-MAPK pathway and suppression of NF-B activation were associated with BD-mediated pancreatic cancer cell killings. Moreover, preliminary in vivo experiment demonstrated that BD was able to significantly inhibit the tumor growth on a subcutaneous inoculation model of pancreatic cancer in nude mice, while it exhibited no overt organ damage to the experimental animals. Based on our promising experimental results, we hypothesize that BD may possess in vivo anti-tumor activity on orthotopic xenotransplantation model of pancreatic cancer. This proposed project is therefore aimed at further exploring the potential of BD as a novel anti-pancreatic cancer agent using relevant pancreatic cancer animal models. Specially the project will examine the ability of BD alone and BD combined with other anti-cancer agents, notably gemcitabine and 5-FU to inhibit pancreatic cancer growth and enhance pancreatic tumor-bearing animal survival benefit using established orthotopic xenograft pancreatic cancer model. In-depth mechanistic and pharmacokinetic studies will also be carried out to unravel the cellular and molecular mechanisms and metabolism related to the anti-pancreatic cancer action of BD. The rational characterization of the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-pancreatic cancer action of BD, and careful evaluation of its potential toxicity will provide a solid foundation and justification for further clinical development of a new and effective anti-pancreatic cancer therapy from this plant-derived quassinoid. This anti-pancreatic cancer development process will add new therapeutic dimensions to the current limited approaches in the management of this most deadly malignancy in human. 中文摘要: 胰腺癌是人類最致命的惡性腫瘤之一, 現有的針對胰腺癌的臨床治療方法效果欠佳, 主要原因與胰腺癌對常用抗癌藥物的極度不敏感性有關。由於目前有效治療胰腺癌的方法還屬缺如, 因而胰腺癌病人的五年生存率非常低 (<3%)。我們先前對10種常用治療腫瘤中藥進行抗癌活性的篩選, 發現中藥鴉膽子提取物對各種胰腺癌細胞有強大的細胞毒作用。我們還發現鴉膽子裡的主要成分鴉膽子苦素D (Brucein D, 簡稱BD)通過誘導細胞凋亡作用而起到抗胰腺癌細胞增殖的作用, 而其對正常細胞的毒性則非常輕微。在隨後的機理研究中我們發現BD通過啟動P38-MAPK 途徑和抑制NF-κB活性而達致對胰腺癌細胞的殺滅作用。另外, 我們的初步動物實驗結果表明BD對皮下嫁接的胰腺癌動物模型具有顯著的抑制腫瘤生長的作用, 而其對實驗動物的內臟則沒有損傷。 根據以上的實驗結果, 我們設想BD可能具有在原位胰腺癌腫瘤模型中也具有明顯的抗癌活性。本課題旨在進一步探索BD作為一種全新抗胰腺癌藥物的潛力, 特別是要檢測BD單獨或和其它抗胰腺癌藥物如吉西他濱和5氟胞嘧啶的聯合運用在抑制腫瘤生長和改善荷瘤動物生存率的作用和效果。我們也會實施更深一步的藥物作用機理和藥物體內代謝的實驗來闡明BD抗胰腺癌作用的細胞和分子學機理。我們相信系統和合理地提示這些細胞分子學機理和精確地評估其潛在毒性將為未來臨床研發BD成為一種新型有效抗胰腺癌藥物打下堅實基礎。這種新型抗胰腺癌藥物的研發也將為拓展胰腺癌的臨床治療方法提供新的途徑。

469912.label: Realisation of objectives
469912.value: 1. The Objective 1 has been achieved. Bioluminescent imaging (BLI) is a technique that can be used to non-invasively measure the characteristics of tumor growth and metastasis. We examined the therapeutic potential of GEM, 5-FU, BD1 and BD2 either alone or in combination (GEM+BD1, 5-FU+BD1) on the growth of orthotopically implanted human PanCa cells (PANC-1, Capan-2) in nude mice. The results of mice body weights measured twice weekly. In the control group, a sharp rise was observed over the later phase of the experiment. A larger accrual in the body weights of the control mice was mainly caused by more rapid tumor growth in control group than treatment groups. For the rest 6 treatment groups, the body weights slightly cutted down in the earlier phase of treatments and mildly increase over the later phase. Dynamic growth or remote metastasis of PanCa in mice was monitored weekly by bioluminescence imaging. In PANC-1 cell orthotopical tumor model, the tumor volumes in control mice were significantly larger than those of mice from the rest groups since day 7 (p < 0.05). And the tumor volumes of combination groups were significantly lower than in the group treated with BD1, BD2, 5-FU or GEM alone as well as in the vehicle-treated control group on days 21 and 28 (p < 0.05). For Capan-2 cell orthotopical tumor model (inoculate 2×106 cells), the overall tumor growth rate was lower than that of PANC-1-inoculated mouse model (inoculate 9×106 cells). Likewise, the bioluminescence imaging results showed a significant increase in tumor volume in the control group as compared with those of the treatment groups since day 14 (p < 0.05). The tumor volumes in the combination treatment groups were significantly lower than single treatment groups (p < 0.05) on days 21 and 28. On the 35th day, mice were euthanized and the tumors were obtained to measure the volume and weight. The results were in concordance with those from bioluminescence imaging and showed that treatment groups significantly inhibited the growth of tumor (p < 0.001) when compared to control. More importantly, the combination treatment exerted the most potent anti-PanCa effect concerning the tumor volume/weight, as compared to the single treatment groups (p < 0.05). We further studied the distant organ metastasis in mice. After the mice were sacrificed, the whole body and vital organs were imaged using the In-Vivo MS FX PRO Imaging System. No EGFP-labelled tumors were found in organs except the pancreas for all the vehicle- and drug-treated mice. 2. The Objective 2 has been achieved. To gain further insight into the mechanisms underlying the anti-PanCa effects of BD in vivo, the expressions of proliferative markers were detected. From the results, we found that these findings draw a parallel with decreased proliferation as documented by PCNA and Ki-67 immunostainings and decreased the expressions of PCNA and Ki-67 by Western blotting analysis within tumors. It was shown that the GEM/5-FU-induced apoptosis in tumors treated with BD was mediated by the caspase pathway as evidenced by PARP cleavage, designated as sensitive marker of the caspase-induced apoptosis. The decreased levels of pro-caspase-3, 9 and increased levels of cleaved-PARP were consistently observed by treatment with BD alone and in combination. Furthermore, the antiapoptotic molecules, such as Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL, were substantially down-regulated by treatment with BD alone or in combination with GEM/5-FU. Moreover, we found that combination treatment led to a higher amount of apoptotic bodies as compared to single treatment using TUNEL assay. Taken together, these observations unequivocally suggest that BD strongly sensitized PanCa to the GEM/5-FU-induced apoptosis in vivo. Our in vitro results showed that GEM/5-FU alone could activate the NF-κB and Nrf2 pathways resulting in reduced apoptosis, while BD could mitigate the activation of these pathways induced by GEM/5-FU. In this in vivo assay, we also found that BD inhibited both NF-κB and Nrf2 pathways in pancreatic tumor. In addition, our in vivo results showed that BD in combination with GEM/5-FU treatments abrogated the NF-κB and Nrf2 activation and increased the apoptotic index, which corroborated with the results obtained in the in vitro assay. Moreover, modulations of the NF-κB-regulated gene products such as c-Myc, cyclin D1, Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, survivin, XIAP, and Nrf2-related gene products such as HO-1 were shown to be responsible for the therapeutic effects of BD in the orthotopic xenograft model. These in vivo results were congruent with our in vitro findings, indicating that modulations of the NF-κB/Nrf2 activities and NF-κB/Nrf2 related gene products might critically contribute to the anti-proliferative effects of BD on PanCa. 3. The Objective 3 has been achieved. A sensitive LC-MS/MS method with multiple reaction mode (MRM) was applied in quantification of BD in rat plasma, pancreas tissue, and urine. After i.v. administration, BD was distributed to all the tissues (0-6 h) in the body (Vd, 2.95 ± 0.05 L/kg) and fast elimination (t1/2, 2.27 ± 0.10 h; CL, 0.91 ± 0.04 L/h/kg) from plasma. After p.o. administration, BD was distributed to all the tissues (0-8 h) in the body (Vd/F, 3.86 ± 0.13 L/kg) and fast elimination (t1/2, 2.98 ± 0.27 h; CL/F, 0.91 ± 0.05 L/h/kg) from plasma. At 24 h post-dosing of BD (i.v.: 2 mg/kg; p.o.: 20 mg/kg) to rats, a relatively high level of BD was detected in the pancreas samples (i.v.: 851.47 ± 209.24 ng/g; p.o.: 1686.84 ± 877.83 ng/g) and was detected in rat urine (i.v.: 0.16 ± 0.01 mg; p.o.: 0.20 ± 0.05 mg). From the histological study, there was no apparent difference in the structural organization of heart, liver and kidney tissue between the BD-treated and the control group. And from the plasma-specific enzyme levels study, the serum levels of ALT, AST, LDH, CK and creatinine were not altered significantly among the control and treatment groups. Therefore, there was no obvious toxicity for both the mono- and combination treatments of BD to the experimental animals, and the safety profile of BD is believed to be good.

469912.label: Major findings and research outcome
469912.value: The present project aimed to assess the in vivo efficacy of BD in combination with GEM and 5-FU against Pancreatic cancer (PanCa) in an orthotopic model in vivo and investigate the possible involvements of NF-κB and Nrf2 pathways. Our results clearly showed that BD alone or in combination with GEM/5-FU potently inhibited the tumor, and the combination treatment was significantly more effective in reducing the tumor volume and weight compared with the single-drug treatment. These findings drew a parallel with decreased proliferation and increased apoptosis which were evidenced by PCNA and Ki-67 immunostaining and TUNEL staining of the tumor tissues. Moreover, our results demonstrated that the down-regulation of NF-κB and its regulated gene products, such as c-Myc, cyclin D1, Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, survivin, XIAP, as well as the activation of caspase-3 were responsible for the therapeutic effects of BD in the orthotopic xenograft model. In addition, we also found that BD alone or in combination with GEM/5-FU abrogated the Nrf2 activation. These in vivo results indicated that the modulation of NF-κB and Nrf2 activities and their regulated gene products might account, at least in part, for the anti-PanCa effect of BD. More importantly, we have performed comprehensive pharmacokinetic and toxicological studies on BD. After oral and intravenous administration, BD was quickly eliminated from plasma (i.v.: t1/2, 2.27 ± 0.10 h; CL, 0.91 ± 0.04 L/h/kg; p.o.: t1/2, 2.98 ± 0.27 h; CL/F, 0.91 ± 0.05 L/h/kg) and its oral bioavailability was about 1.31%. After oral and intravenous administration, BD could extensively distribute to all tissues (i.v.: Vd, 2.95 ± 0.05 L/kg; p.o.: Vd/F, 3.86 ± 0.13 L/kg), and a relatively high level of BD was detected in the pancreas samples (i.v.: 851.47 ± 209.24 ng/g; p.o.: 1686.84 ± 877.83 ng/g). The parent compound was found in rat urine after oral and intravenous administration of BD (i.v.: 0.16 ± 0.01 mg; p.o.: Vd/F, 0.20 ± 0.05 mg). Toxicologically, after i.p. (3.0 mg/kg) administration of BD to the CAPAN-2 xenograft mice for consecutive 35 days, no overt toxicity was found in the heart, liver and kidney of the mice. To conclude, our experiments have established that BD was capable of inhibiting the PanCa growth and inducing apoptosis when used alone or in combination with GEM/5-FU in vivo through multiple targets. The promising anti-PanCa activity of BD suggested that it holds a promising potential to be further developed into a novel therapeutic agent for the treatment of PanCa.

469912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
469912.value: The following areas are suggested as an extension to the current study, including: 1. To explore an economical and practical synthesis method to prepare BD. Our experimental results indicated BD as a promising PanCa therapeutic agent; however, it was still not commercially available. Although BD had been isolated from Bruceae Fructus by columns chromatography method, the isolation of high-purity BD from Bruceae Fructus was a tedious process, and the low yield could not keep the pace with future clinical application. Chemical synthesis remains a powerful tool to furnish sufficient amounts of BD with high purity for biological and clinical evaluations of its anti-PanCa action. 2. To further evaluate the anti-cancer effects and underlying mechanism of BD using genetically engineered mouse models of pancreatic exocrine neoplasia. GEMM is known to characterize the cellular and molecular pathology of pancreatic neoplasia and cancer, and constitutes one of the best tools to investigate novel therapeutic approaches, chemopreventive and/or anticancer treatments. The establishment of GEMM for the efficacy evaluation of BD should shed light on the anti-PanCa effect and mechanisms of BD from the genetic prospective, and provide further insight into its potential application as a novel therapeutic agent for the PanCa treatment.

469912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
469912.value: Pancreatic cancer (PanCa) is one of the most lethal human malignancies. Gemcitabine (GEM) and 5-FU are currently the first-line drugs for the treatment of advanced PanCa. However, the poor response rate, side effects and development of chemoresistance have compromised their marginal benefit. Hence, the development of novel strategies is in urgent need for the management of this deadly disease. The present research project aimed to assess the in vivo efficacy of BD in combination with GEM and 5-FU against PanCa in orthotopic model and investigate the possible involvements of NF-κB and Nrf2 pathways. We found that BD significantly synergized with GEM/5-FU to exert potent anti-PanCa effects with no significant toxicity in vivo, and the underlying mechanisms were found to be intimately associated with the anti-proliferation, apoptosis and downregulation of the GEM/5-FU-induced activations of both NF-κB and Nrf2 pathways. Moreover, after oral and intravenous administration, BD was quickly eliminated from plasma and extensively distribute to all the tissues and its oral bioavailability was about 1.31% and the parent compound was found in rat urine. The results suggest that combined treatment with BD and GEM/5-FU could lead to a potentially important new therapeutic strategy against PanCa.

470312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
470312.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) poses a serious health-care problem in Hong Kong. It has a uniquely high prevalence among southern Chinese and affects the younger age group of our population. This EBV-associated epithelial malignancy is highly invasive and commonly metastatic. Despite current treatments are efficient for early stage disease, cure rates are hampered by the significant incidences of distant relapse and metastasis. Recently, increasing evidences have begun to emphasize on the prominent roles for tumor initiating cancer stem-like cells (CSC) in therapeutic resistance, recurrence and metastasis. However, the CSC properties in EBV-associated NPC are still poorly understood since only few relevant tumor models and limited clinical materials are available. In an EBV-positive NPC cell line C666-1, we have successfully isolated the sphere-forming cells that exhibited stem-like cell properties including self-renewal ability and in vivo tumor-formation potential. Moreover, expression of stem cell markers including OCT4, NANOG KLF4, SOX2, CD133 and CD44 was significantly elevated in these cells. Importantly, gene expression profiling discovered preferential upregulation of a potential CSC surface marker, CD109 in the NPC spheres. CD109 is a glycosyl phosphatidylinositol-anchored glycoprotein which is expressed on a subpopulation of hematopoietic and mesenchymal stem cells. As a component of TGF-beta receptor system, its overexpression inhibits TGF-beta1-induced growth inhibition. Co-expression of CD109, CD44 and SOX2 were consistently detected as a subpopulation in both EBV-positive tumor lines and primary tumors. CD109+ cells isolated from the NPC cells C666-1 also showed significant sphere-forming ability than the CD109- fraction. Strikingly, overexpression of multiple stem cell markers was confirmed in the sorted CD109+ NPC cells. The preliminary findings suggested that CD109 is a specific CSC marker and play a functional role in the nasopharyngeal CSC. We hypothesized that CD109 expression may contribute to maintaining stem-like cell features in EBV-positive NPC through negative regulation of TGF-beta signaling. In this proposed study, we aim to: (1) comprehensively investigate the CSC properties of CD109+ cells isolated from NPC tumor lines and primary tumors; (2) elucidate the role of CD109 and TGF-beta signaling in maintaining stem-like cell properties in NPC; (3) evaluate the efficacy of CD109 blockade in targeting CSC population in EBV-positive NPC. This research will provide new knowledge on CSC of this common EBV-associated cancer, which can be applied to enhance treatment and improve patient outcome. 鼻咽癌為香港及中國南部地區常見癌症，且嚴重威脅年青人健康。這種EB病毒相關的表皮惡性腫瘤極具侵襲力及轉移能力。早期階段患者的治療效果相當有效，但由於其復發率高及易遠移導致後期階段患者治愈率極低。近來關於腫瘤幹細胞在腫瘤發生、抗藥性、復發及轉移中的功能已成為研究熱點。但由於相關腫瘤模型較少且臨床資源有限，腫瘤幹細胞在EB病毒相關鼻咽癌中的功能尚不甚清楚。在EB病毒陽性的鼻咽癌細胞株C666-1中，我們成功分離出具球體形成能力的細胞亞群，這類細胞展示出幹細胞特性如具備自我復制能力以及在動物體內可形成腫瘤。同時幹細胞標誌物如OCT4、NANOG、KLF4、SOX2、CD133和CD44在該類細胞中明顯增高。更為重要的是，基因表達譜揭示出該類細胞可高表達腫瘤幹細胞表面標誌物CD109。CD109為一糖基磷脂酰肌醇錨定糖蛋白，在造血細胞和骨髓間充質幹細胞亞群中高表達。作為TGF-β信號通路受體系統的一個重要組成部分，其過度表達可負調控TGF-β1誘導的生長抑制。在EB病毒陽性腫瘤細胞株和原發腫瘤中CD109、CD44和SOX2呈現共表達。在鼻咽癌細胞C666-1中分離出的CD109 陽性細胞亞群較陰性細胞亞群表現出顯著的球體形成能力，同時在CD109陽性的鼻咽癌細胞中多個幹細胞標記物高表達。這些初步結果表明，CD109為一特定腫瘤幹細胞標誌物並可在鼻咽癌腫瘤幹細胞中發揮功能。我們推測在EBV陽性鼻咽癌中CD109高表達可能負調控TGF-β信號並有助於細胞維持幹細胞樣功能。我們的研究目標包括：（1）在鼻咽癌細胞株和原發腫瘤中分離CD109陽性細胞亞群並全面研究其腫瘤幹細胞特性；（2）闡明在該細胞亞群維持幹細胞特性過程中CD109和TGF-β信號通路的相互作用；（3）評估在EB病毒陽性鼻咽癌患者中阻斷CD109的有效性。該研究將深入了解EB病毒相關鼻咽癌中腫瘤幹細胞的功能，並希望能提升治療效果和改善患者預後。

470312.label: Realisation of objectives
470312.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a distinct type of head and neck cancer which is consistently associated with Epstein-Barr virus infection. This EBV-associated epithelial malignancy is highly invasive and commonly metastatic. Since the tumor initiating cancer stem-like cells (CSC) have the prominent roles in therapeutic resistance, recurrence and metastasis, isolation and characterization of NPC CSC is important in understanding the tumorigenesis and development efficiency therapeutic strategies for NPC patients. Based on our preliminary study, we recognized that the CSC phenotypes in EBV-positive NPC are distinct from that reported in the EBV-negative cell lines. Thus, in this study, we aim to isolate and characterize the specific cancer-stem cell phenotypes in EBV-positive NPC and explore multiple novel drugs/inhibitors targeting NPC CSC. From the spheroids of an EBV-positive cell line C666-1, we firstly isolated a CD44+ SOX2+ subpopulation with cancer stem-like cell (CSC) properties in EBV-associated NPC. The occurrence of this unique CSC was confirmed in a panel of EBV-positive NPC cell line, patient-derived xenografts and primary tumors. By microarray analysis, we have identified a number of putative CSC-associated genes and microRNAs in EBV-positive C666-1 cells. Notably, several surface markers (CCR7, CD109) and ATP-binding cassette transporter genes (ABCC3 and ABCC11) were significantly overexpressed in the NPC CSC subpopulation. Both CCR7 and CD109 were found to be new surface markers that may be important in maintaining CSC function in NPC cells. The enrichment of CCR7+ and CD109high cell population in the sphere-forming cells was confirmed by flow cytometry. The CD109high cells was found to be a subpopulation of CD44+ cells and overlapped with SOX2 cells. As a specific CSC population, the CD109high cells showed higher sphere-forming ability and clone formation efficiency, overexpressed of a number of stem-cell associated genes including OCT4, CD133, NANOG and CKIT. By IHC study on a large panel of primary NPC, we also found that CD109 expression is correlated with the survival of NPC patients. Importantly, the isolated CD109 high cells showed significantly high tumorigenecity in in vivo nude mice models. However, targeting CD109 by siRNA and blocking antibody showed no significant effect on C666-1 cell growth. It may be due to frequent genetic and epigenetic alterations of the genes involved in TGF-beta pathway which was recently identified in our transcriptome and genome sequencing studies. The genetic lesions in TGF-beta signaling pathways may influence the EBV persistence infection and differentiation of NPC cells, subsequently contribute to the maintenance of CSC properties. Despite CD109 is a useful surface markers for NPC CSC, it may not contribute to the maintenance of CSC properties. Further study of the effect of CD109 blockade in the newly established EBV+ve NPC cell lines will further confirm it role in CSC maintenance. In addition to CD109, we also elucidate the role of other surface marker, CCR7 in NPC CSC. CCR7 is a chemokine receptor that mediates cell migration in response to its ligand CCL21. Overexpression of CCR7 in CSCs is likely to contribute to the frequent cervical lymph node metastases in NPC patients. By flow cytometry and IHC, we found that CCR7 was significantly correlated with CD44 expression in both tumor lines and primary tumors. Notably, CCR7 expression correlated with the presence of recurrent disease and distant metastasis. To investigate the role of CCR7 in NPC CSC, we utilized a CCR7-blocking antibody to neutralize its function in the parental, CD44+ and CD44- C666-1 cells. Observable decrease in cell proliferation was observed in the CD44+ cell fraction when compared to CD44- and parental C666-1 cells. Reduced clone formation efficiency was also found in C666-1 cells treated with CCR7 blocking antibody. The high tumorigenecity of CCR7+ve cell was also ocnfirmed in the nude mice models. Our findings indicated suggested CCR7 is a potential CSC marker and therapeutic target in EBV-positive NPC. In the newly identified NPC CSC, the significant overexpression of ATP-binding cassette transporter genes, ABCC3 and ABCC11, indicated their contributions in resistant to chemotherapeutic drugs and tumor recurrence. ABCC11 is the main transporter for 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) which is one of the main chemotherapeutic drugs for NPC. We have established three drug-resistant (5-FU-, Cisplatin- and doxorubicinresistant) sublines of C666-1 cells. Significant overexpression of ABCC11 and CSC properties were demonstrated in 5Fu- and Cisplatin-resistant cells. Knockdown ABCC11 in the drugresistant cells resulted in significant enhancement of its sensitivity to 5-FU treatment and reduction of spheroid formation ability. High expression of ABCC11 was frequently detected in the primary tumors. The findings implied that ABCC11 may contribute to drug resistant and CSC properties in NPC cells. By microarray analysis, we have identified several stemness-repressing miRNAs were differentially expressed in the sphere-forming cells. Among these stemness-repressing miRNAs, we further confirmed miR-96, miR-183, miR-200a andmiR-200b in the isolated CD44+ and CD109high cell population in C666-1 cells. By transient and stable transfection, we found that ectopic expression of miR-96 and miR-193 significantly suppressed the spheroid formation and anchorage dependent growth of C666-1 cells. Reduced NICD3 and NICD4 in miR-96- and miR-183-expressing NPC cells suggests the involvement of the NOTCH signaling pathway in their tumor suppressive function. The tumorigenicity of cells stably expressing miR-183 was also significantly inhibited in the in vivo nude mice model. The study indicated that miR-183 is a tumor-suppressive miRNA in EBV-associated NPC via targeting NPC CSC properties.

470312.label: Major findings and research outcome
470312.value: In this study, we have successfully isolated and characterized the specific cancer-stem cell phenotypes in EBV-positive NPC. In addition to the CD44+ SOX2+ subpopulation, we also confirmed the CSC properties in the CCR7+ and CD109high NPC cells (Lun et al., 2012; Lun, et al., 2014). We also confirmed that CCR7 and CD109 are useful surface markers for isolation of CSC subpopulation in NPC tumors. These new surface markers will greatly enhance the efficiency of CSC studies in primary tumors and patient derived xenografts (PDX). In our study of CD109 and TGFbeta signalling pathway, we have revealed the frequent epigenetic genetic and genetic alterations in NPC tumor lines and primary tumors. This somatic changes may contribute to the E the involvement of the NOTCH signaling pathway in their tumor suppressive function infection and maintenance of CSC properties in NPC cells (Li et al., 2016). The role of EBV latent genes in NPC CSC was shown in our earlier report (Lun et al, 2012) and summarized in our recent reviews (Lun et al., 2014; Tsao et al., 2015). In the newly identified NPC CSC, we also demonstrated the overexpression of ABC transporter ABCC11 which may contribute to chemotherapeutic drugs resistance and tumor recurrence. The findings suggested that the depletion of CSC may enhance the treatment efficacy of current chemotherapeutic agents. In our recent study, we firstly reported the important role of stemness-repressing miRNAs, miR-96 and miR-193 and Notch signalling pathway in NPC CSC (Cheung et al., 2016).

470312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
470312.value: The identification of specific CSC in EBV-associated NPC allowed us and our collaborator to elucidate the effects of novel drugs targeting CSC in this cancer. We have collaborated with Prof. NK Mak from Hong Kong Baptist University to study the efficiency of a novel Hsp90 inhibitor AT13387 and a CBP/beta-catenin antagonist ICG-001 in reducing CSC population in NPC tumors. Combination with cisplatin treatment, target CSC by ICG-001 can effectively suppress the growth of multiple EBV-NPC tumor lines in the in vivo models. Similar in vivo antitumor effects were also noted in our newly developed small molecules targeting the unique CSC population in EBV+ve NPC. Furthermore, our study also hints the important role of NOTCH and STAT3 signaling pathways in NPC CSC. Elucidation the effects of inhibitors targeting these pathways on CSC will provide important information for enhancing the efficacy of current chemotherapy for NPC patients. In our study, our preliminary findings also indicate the crucial role of CSC properties and differentiation in EBV persistent infection. Elucidating the effect of CSC properties on the EBV lytic replication may provide a therapeutic approach for NPC.

470312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
470312.value: Identification of tumor initiating cancer stem cells (CSC) is an important step to develop efficient therapeutic strategies for nasopharyngeal carcinoma. In this study, we successfully isolated and characterized the CD44+SOX2+ CSC subpopulation in EBV-associated NPC. The CSC properties was confirmed in these cells by both in vitro and in vivo studies. We also revealed that overexpression of ABC transporter ABCC11 in this cells may contribute to the failure of chemotherapy in NPC patients. Our work also provides 2 new specific CSC surface markers, CCR7 and CD109 for further study of CSC in clinical specimens. Importantly, the discovery of multiple key CSC associated genes (CCR7, ABCC11), miRNAs (miR-183, miR-96) and signalling pathways (NOTCH, STAT3) allows us to develop new therapeutic approaches targeting these specific subpopulation, subsequently improve the efficacy of current treatment for NPC patients.

rows: 1. To investigate the optimal growth factor concentration and treatment time for the synthesis of a TDSC sheet;
2. To test the feasibility and effect of wrapping the whole ACL graft with a TDSC sheet on the biomechanical properties of the reconstructed ACL complex in an animal model; and
3. To study the mechanisms of a TDSC sheet in the healing of ACL graft in an animal model.

470512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
470512.value: Both osteo-integration and mid-substance remodeling of graft (collectively called “graft healing”) are slow processes after ACL reconstruction. Faster healing of ACL graft will allow earlier rehabilitation and reduce absence from work and sport. Exogenous administration of stem cells has been shown to promote graft healing. However, the mechanisms of stem cells in this context are not clear. Further, the delivery of stem cells using fibrin glue or atelocollagen is not optimal, thus an improved way of application is required. We are able to stimulate tendon-derived stem cells (TDSCs) to secrete its own extracellular matrix and form an elastic and coherent cell sheet. No external scaffold is required and the TDSC sheet can facilitate arthroscopy-compatible progenitor cell transplantation. Our results showed that progenitor cells in the TDSC sheet expressed higher level of osteogenic, chondrogenic and tenogenic / ligamentogenic markers compared to control (BMSCs) both before and after the same treatment for cell sheet formation. Thus hypothetically they may promote graft healing by engraftment and direct cell differentiation. Our results also showed that the progenitor cells in the TDSC sheet expressed high level of immunomodulatory and trophic factors including BMP-2, TGF-β1 and bFGF which together may promote graft healing. We hypothesize that TDSC sheet may augment graft healing after ACL reconstruction. We consequently want to establish the optimal condition for the development of a TDSC sheet. The potential effect and mechanisms of this optimized TDSC sheet on graft healing after ACL reconstruction will then be studied in a rat model. The study will be divided into 3 parts. In part I, the optimal growth factor concentration and treatment time for the synthesis of the TDSC sheet will be determined. In part II, the feasibility and effect of wrapping the whole, tunnel part and mid-substance part of ACL graft on the biomechanical properties of the reconstructed ACL complex in a rat model will be examined. The TDSC sheet showing the best result in part II will be investigated further in respect of healing mechanisms in part III of the study. Our preliminary result showed that TDSC sheet promoted graft healing, with more chondrocyte-like cells and Sharpey’s fibers observed at the graft-bone interface and tunnel ends, resulting in higher pull-out strength of the tibia-graft-femur complex at week 2 post-reconstruction. In summary, this study will clarify if the TDSC sheet can be developed into an off-the-shelf bio-therapeutic product for the promotion of ligament graft healing.

470512.label: Realisation of objectives
470512.value: All objectives have been achieved. Tendon derived stem cells (TDSCs) were isolated from the mid substance of the patellar tendon of 4-6-week-old male outbred GFP Sprague-Dawley rats, (SD-Tg (CAG-EGFP) Cz-004Osb), weighting 150 to 220 g. TDSC sheet was formed by Connective Tissue Growth Factor (CTGF) and ascorbic acid. To define the optimal growth factor concentration and treatment for the synthesis of TDSC sheet formation, 3 different concentrations and 4 treatment time points were tested. TDSC sheet was assessed based on (1) its ease of handling during surgical operation; and (2) the expression of the highest combinations of osteogenic, chondrogenic and tenogenic/ ligamentogenic markers. In general, higher CTGF concentration and longer treatment times resulted in thicker cell sheet. Considering cost and effectiveness for future application CTGF (25ng/ ml) and ascorbic acid (25uM) were used for the animal study. We also test the feasibility of wrapping the TDSC sheet around graft mid-substance only, tunnel part of the graft only and whole tendon graft during ACL reconstruction. Our result demonstrated that wrapping of whole tendon graft with TDSC sheet was feasible but not the other two conditions. This model was thus used for assessing the efficacy of TDSC sheet for graft healing after ACL reconstruction. Briefly, GFP-TDSCs were incubated with CTGF (25ng/ml) and ascorbic acic (25uM) for 2 weeks after confluence. TDSC sheet was used to wrap the whole tendon graft prior to graft insertion during ACL reconstruction in rats in the experimental groups. Rats undergoing ACL reconstruction with the tendon graft not covered by GFP-TDSC sheet served as controls. The ACL reconstruction complex was harvested at week 2, 6 and 12 for histology, CT measurement and biomechanical test. The fate of the transplanted cells was examined by immunhistochemical staining. To study the mechanisms of TDSC sheet on graft healing after ACL reconstruction, Immunohistochemistry of Collagen Type I, Collagen Type III, Tenomodulin, Sox9, Collagen Type II, MMP1, MMP13 were performed. The above works have been presented in different international conferences and 1 manuscript was published.

470512.label: Major findings and research outcome
470512.value: Our results showed that treatment of TDSCs with CTGF and ascorbic acid promoted the expression of tendon-related markers (Tnmd, Col1a1) and maintained high chondro-osteogenic gene expression (Acan, Alpl) of TDSCs. In general, higher CTGF concentrations and longer treatment times resulted in a thicker cell sheet. Considering cost and effectiveness for future application, CTGF (25ng/ml) and ascorbic acid (25µM) were used for the animal study. Our result demonstrated that wrapping the whole tendon graft with TDSC sheet was the only feasible way to wrap the graft. There were significantly higher tunnel BMD and BV/TV at the metaphyseal region of tibial tunnel at week2 and at the femoral tunnel at week6 in the TDSC group compared to those in the control group. TDSC group showed a time-dependent increase in tunnel BMD and BV/TV at the epiphyseal region of tibial tunnel. There was significant improvement in the ultimate load at week2 and stiffness at week6 in the TDSC group compared to that in the control group. Both the control and the TDSC groups showed similar failure mode during biomechanical testing. The intra-articular graft midsubstance in the TDSC group showed lower cellularity and vascularity, better cell alignment, and higher collagen birefringence compared with the control group. At the femoral tunnel, less fibrous tissue and a higher percentage of Sharpey fibers were observed at the interface in the TDSC group at week2. Chondrocyte-like cells were observed at the interface or on the graft in the TDSC group. This was not observed in the control group. Better tunnel graft healing was observed in the TDSC group compared with that in the control group at week6, as reflected by the higher tunnel graft integrity and slightly more Sharpey fibers at the tunnel interface. The expression pattern of collagen type I, II, III and Sox9 were similar. ColI, ColII, ColIII and Sox9 expressions were higher in TDSC group at week2 as compared with control group. The difference became insignificant at week6 and week12. Tenomodulin expression levels were similar between TDSC group and control group at week2 and week6, however, Tenomodulin expression was higher in TDSC group then control group at week12. MMP1 expression was higher in TDSC group at week2 as compared with control group. There was no difference at week6; however, the expression level was lower in TDSC group as compared with control group at week12. There was no difference in MMP13 expression level between TDSC group and control group at all time points.

470512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
470512.value: Based on the results of this project, TDSC sheet improved early graft healing of ACL reconstruction in a rat model. TDSC sheet enhanced mineralization within the tunnels, osteo-integration of graft and bone tunnel, and improved biomechanical properties of graft. These might due to TDSC sheet increased collagen I, II, III and Sox9 expressions at the early healing stage and reduced MMP1 expression during graft remodeling. With the low immunogenicity, TDSC sheet might be a new treatment for ACL reconstruction. As the formation of TDSC sheet take time and there was not common to have a GMP facilities in operation theater, to further develop and promote the application of TDSC sheet, we have put up a further study to develop a cryopreservation and reactivation method of TDSC sheet for the use of ACL reconstruction in a proposal for General Research Fund 2015/16 (funded).

470512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
470512.value: This is the first study to (1) test the effect of engineered stem cell sheet on graft mid-substance remodeling; and (2) investigate the mechanism of stem cell sheet in the promotion of graft healing after ACL reconstruction. In this study, we present experimental evidences that wrapping the graft with TDSC sheet in ACL reconstruction improved early graft healing in a well-established rat model. TDSC sheet improved ACL graft healing histologically, increased mineralization in the bone tunnels and an increased the biomechanical properties of the graft. These might probably due to the increase in collagens expression and reduction of enzyme expression in the graft during graft remodeling which might improve the graft integrity.

471012.label: Project Objectives
471012.value: To validate the diagnostic utility of microfluidic digital PCR for detection of activating EGFR mutation from plasma of patients with advanced lung cancer
rows: To validate the diagnostic utility of microfluidic digital PCR for detection of activating EGFR mutation from plasma of patients with advanced lung cancer

471012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471012.value: We have established epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor(TKI) as a standard therapy for lung cancer patients with EGFR mutations. In presence of activated mutations at exon 19 and 21 first line EGFR TKI attains higher tumor response rate and longer progression free survival than standard chemotherapy. These activated mutations have become a standard biomarker for personalized medicine in lung cancer. However, tumor sample is not readily available for EGFR mutation analysis. Over 50% of lung cancer diagnosis is made by cytologic examination of specimens from fine needle aspiration. The small quantity of cancer cell is commonly not sufficient for EGFR mutation analysis, and more invasive procedure is required. Alternatively, we may detect EGFR mutation from plasma DNA. Prior studies using various techniques such as direct sequencing, HPLCC or ARMS reported relatively low sensitivity. Our group has adopted a novel technology using a Microfluidic System than simultaneously perform 9180 PCRs at nanoscale. We used direct sequencing of tumor tissue as reference and reported sensitivity of 92% and specificity of 100%, and in addition, we were able to provide a semi-quantitative concentration of the mutant sequence.(Clin Can Res 15:2077, 2009) This new technique should be validated in a large scale clinical trial. ASPIRATION is an ongoing single arm phase II pan-Asia study of first line erlotinib in patients with confirmed activating EGFR mutation. Our group has reached a collaborative agreement with the study sponsor that we shall use microfluidic digital PCR for measurement of EGFR mutation from plasma DNA at base line, 8 weeks and disease progression. Plasma samples from patients with known EGFR wild type will be used as negative control. By correlating our finding with tumor tissue and clinical response/progression, we will be able to validate the diagnositic utilities of this novel technology as a plasma biomarker for personalized therapy in lung cancer. 我們已確立上皮生長因子受體酪胺酸激酶抑制劑作為有肺癌上皮生長因子受體變異病人的標準治療。exon 19 and 21第一線皮生長因子受體酪胺酸激酶抑制劑啓動變異的存在令腫瘤回應率比標準化療高及有更長存活期。這些啓動變異在肺癌治療中漸成為個人化醫學的標準生物標記，但仍欠相應腫瘤標本及時配合上皮生長因子受體變異分析。多過50%細胞學檢查以細針抽吸及細胞學檢查法取得組織，由於癌細胞數量太少及不足夠做上皮生長因子受體變異分析，現沒有相應腫瘤標本及時配合上皮生長因子受體變異分析，所以要用介入性醫療程序。 或者我們可從血漿DNA檢測上皮生長因子受體變異，之前已有研究用各種技術如直接基因排序、HPLCC或ARMS，都發現敏感度不足。我們用新科技微流系統同步進行9180PCRs納米，我們用直接基因排序作參考，得出92%敏感度及100%特異性。再者，我們更提供突變種排序半定量濃度(Clin Can Res 15:2077, 2009)，新技術需要在大型臨床試驗中驗證。 ASPIRATION是第二期泛亞洲上皮生長因子受體變異第一線單臂Erlotinib臨床研究，250個入試病人全部要得到腫瘤組織排序確認及接受單一Erlotinib直到病情惡化。我們與贊助者達成協議，用數位化微流體聚合酶連鎖反應在基線、8星期及病情惡化時量度血漿DNA的上皮生長因子受體變異。把我們的資料與腫瘤組織及臨床反應/惡化情況聯繫，我們將可驗測這技術作為肺癌個人化治療血漿生物標記的角色。

471012.label: Realisation of objectives
471012.value: We completed digital PCR on 208 plasma samples from ASPIRATION and excluded 49 patients for the reason that the corresponding tumors were not confirmed by COBAS EGFR mutation test in centralized laboratory. Among the 159 patients with available tumor EGFR mutation data, 144 patients were positive for EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R mutations in the tumors (81 positive for EGFR exon 19 deletion and 63 positive for L858R mutation). The remaining 15 patients were either negative for EGFR mutations or positive for non-exon 19 deletion/non-L858R mutations, including exon 18 mutation and exon 20 mutation, in the tumors. Total of 144 patients with matched tumor and plasma sample positive for either EGFR 19 or 21 mutations were recruited. In addition, 53 archival plasma samples with proven EGFR wild type in tumor samples were included in analysis. Overall, we confirmed sensitivity was 81%, specificity was 100%, and concordance rate was 83%. We correlated tumor response from the ASPIRATION study and include all patients who had exposure to erlotinib as first line therapy. Some of the enrolled patients had their EGFR mutation tested at local laboratory but not confirmed in central laboratory. We evaluated tumor response to erlotinib in the Intention-to-treat population. For the 117 patients who were tested positive for EGFR mutation by Digital PCR from plasma, tumor response rate was 69.2%, which is not different from the tissue positive population (66.5%). We had also evaluated the progression free survival (PFS) of patient on erlotinib and note that patient with positive EGFR mutation in plasma had a shorter PFS than patients with negative results (9.2 versus 13.0 months). We had optimized the laboratory technique for quantitative measurement of plasma concentration of EGFR mutation. Our original objective is to measure the change in quantitative plasma concentration in response to erlotinib. However, we had failed to obtain the serial samples from the pharmaceutical sponsor. The ASPIRATION is a multi-national clinical study that involved 5 Asia Pacific countries. Serial blood samples were available from only selective investigation sites and Roche, the sponsor of study, decide to keep these samples for their own investigative purpose. Therefore we can only achieve part of third objective.

471012.label: Major findings and research outcome
471012.value: In this study we confirmed the diagnostic utility of Droplet Digital PCR for detection of EGFR mutation. Sensitivity is 81% and specificity is 100%. Tumor response rate of patients with positive EGFR mutation in plasma is similar to patients with positive EGFR mutation in tissue.(69.2% versus 66.5%) An unexpected finding is the observation of shorter progression free survival in patient with positive EGFR mutation in plasma than patient without. This is potentially explained by the higher tumor associated with patient with positive EGFR mutation in plasma. Our finding was first presented in World Conference on Lung Cancer in Sydney in 2013. The final result and its clinical correlation is incorporated into the primary manuscript of the ASPIRATION study. The manuscript is completed and submitted to Lancet Oncology. Decision is pending.

471012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471012.value: The current result implies that detection of EGFR mutation from plasma by Digital PCR is feasible. This technique is ready for commercialization and we are at the process of identifying potential commercial partner. Future research 1. Clinical application of Digital PCR for identification of EGFR exon 20 T790M, a well-known resistant gene that accounts for about 50% of acquired resistance to EGFR TKI. Active phase II/III clinical studies on T790M specific TKIs such as AZ 9291 and CO1686 are ongoing. Diagnosis of T790M resistant mutation will be an important biomarker for selection of patients for this novel therapy. 2. Circulating tumor cell (CTC) is an alternative method for detection of EGFR mutation. To supplement the sensitivity of Digital PCR.

471012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471012.value: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation is one of the most important genetic abnormality that leads to development of lung cancer among the non-smoker. Over the past decade, use of molecular targeted therapy against EGFR mutation is highly efficacious and has been established as first line treatment for patient with advance stage lung cancer that harbor EGFR mutations. However, tumor sample for EGFR mutation testing is not always feasible. In this project, we used Digital PCR for detection of EGFR mutation from circulating free plasma DNA of patients from the ASPIRATION study. We established the sensitivity of testing at 81% and specificity at 100%. In other words this test can accurately pick up the EGFR mutation in 4 out of 5 patients with the blood test and the result would be 100% correct for patients with positive result. This technology will be clinically applicable for patients without accessible tumor samples for EGFR mutation analysis.

471412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
471412.value: With the ongoing pursuit to reduce surgical trauma and minimize wounds, laparoendoscopic single-site surgery (LESS) has emerged and gained popularity as the approach for performing a number of laparoscopic operations. By going through a single incision over the umbilicus, LESS offers the potential of decreasing wound pain, shortening postoperative recovery and hospital stay, and improving cosmetic outcomes. This has been realized in a recent study by our group, which demonstrated superior cosmesis and patient satisfaction scores in those treated with LESS appendicectomy for acute appendicitis. However, the LESS approach is not without problems. It complicates operation by limiting the movements and dexterity of the laparoscopic instruments. Furthermore, the lack of retraction and instrument triangulation renders a seemingly simple procedure more intricate. This may lead to a longer operative time and create a window of danger for developing complications. Surgical robotics was first introduced to the laparoscopic field in 2002 and since then, there has been an exponential increase in the number of robotic systems and procedures being registered around the world. The endowrist technology of Robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery provides seven-degrees of freedom that permits movement of the instrument to resemble that of a human wrist. This significantly reduces the difficulty in performing complex tasks such as suturing and fine dissection. With hand movement being captured and digitalized by the built-in computer, the robotic system is able to filter out hand tremors and therefore improve instrument stability and surgical precision. The presence of a 3-dimesional high-density image with a 10x magnification also enhances the visualization of internal structures. Robotic system is now seen as an “enabler”, making performance of complicated ultra-major surgeries, including pancreatectomy and coronary artery bypass, under the laparoscope a reality. Realizing the benefits brought about by both technologies, and the potential that the robotic system may help overcome limitations of LESS, we propose to investigate and compare the risks and benefits of robotic-LESS (R-LESS) with conventional laparoscopic surgery. This two-part study will first compare the workload performance of the operator in R-LESS with that of human LESS in the porcine model. Then it is followed by a pilot study to assess the feasibility and safety profile of R-LESS cholecystectomy in clinical patients with symptomatic gallstones. Finally a prospective randomized controlled trial comparing R-LESS to conventional laparoscopic cholecystectomy will be conducted to determine its actual efficacy and benefits in a clinical setting. 隨著微創手術對減少傷口創傷的不斷追求，外科界近年發展了LaparoEndoscopic Single Site Surgery (LESS)單孔腔鏡的外科技術，並且逐漸地成為一項被廣泛應用的腔鏡手術方法。理論上，通過單一臍切口的LESS手術能減少傷口疼痛，縮短術後恢復時間和住院需求，並達致更好的術後外觀效果。最近在我院發表的一項有關急性闌尾炎的前瞻性研究中，以上的優點更部份被證實。該報告闡述了接受LESS闌尾切除後的病人均有較好的美容結果及更高的滿意評分。然而，LESS並非完全沒有問題，由於手術器械經單一切口進入腹腔而呈平行姿態，它限制了器械的活動範圍和操作的靈活性；此外，因為欠缺了一般腔鏡手術的拉勾功能及術區的三角分呈，使本來簡單的手術變得複雜。這可能會導致較長的手術時間，且增加併發症的風險。 機器人外科手術在2002年首次引入，自此有關機器人手術的文獻報告數目急遽增加。它的EndoWrist技術提供了七度活動自由，使儀器的操作能像人類手腕一般流暢。這特性可大大減少進行更複雜任務手術的困難性，如縫合和精細的解剖等。通過接收外科醫生手部的動作，及將其于電腦中數碼化，機器人系統可以過濾掉手震和提高儀器的穩定性精密度。它的內置立體圖像及 10 倍放大功能增強了觀察器官結構的清晰度。現在，機器人手術系統被視為enabler，使複雜的大型手術，如胰腺切除與冠狀動脈旁路等都能順利地於腔鏡下完成。 基於LESS術式與機器人系統有互助及克服技術困難的可能性和潛力，我們建議對機器人LESS手術跟常規腔鏡手術的對比研究。這項分兩階段的研究將首先在豬模型手術中比較兩種術式對操作者的工作負苛。然後是試點研究以評估Robotic LESS於膽結石患者的臨床膽囊切除的可行性和安全性。最後是通過一項前瞻性隨機對照試驗去比較Robotic LESS與常規腹腔鏡膽囊切除術，以確定其實際效果和臨床效益。

471412.label: Realisation of objectives
471412.value: Objective 1. To investigate the workload performance, benefits and risks of R-LESS versus human-LESS (H-LESS) approach in a porcine mdoel for two benchmark procedures: cholecystectomy and gastrojejunostomy. This animal study was commenced in February 2013 and completed in June 2014. A total of 24 cholecystectomies and 24 gastrojejunostomies (GJ) were performed in 24 swine. PI (EKNg) and Co-I (AYTeoh) took turns to perform all the stated single incision procedures according to randomization (Robotic vs Human). The primary outcome is the workload of the surgeon that was measured by the validated NASA task load index (TLI). Secondary outcomes including the difficulty in performing the procedures, overall procedure time, time to completion of each step of the procedure, morbidity and mortality rate were also compared between the two groups (Results please see Research Outcome part). This study was finished per proposal though it took a longer duration than initially planned, largely due to the need of having two investigators simultaneously. Objective 2. A prospective pilot series of R-LESS cholecystectomy on human patients to investigate the feasibility and safety profile of the procedure. From August 2014 to August 2015, a total of 10 patients were recruited for this pilot series of R-LESS cholecystectomy. There was one patient for whom the operation was finally converted to open surgery due to unforeseen cholecysto-colonic fistula. Otherwise, the other 9 patients had the pilot procedure of R-LESS cholecystectomy uneventfully. The recruitment of suitable patients during this pilot phase had been slow because patients with a history of complicated gallstones had to be excluded. In addition, upon the explanation of this novel robotic approach as an experimental procedure to the eligible patients, about 25% of them refused to participate. These resulted in the prolonged course of this part of the project and delayed the subsequent commencement of the prospective comparative study in Objective 3 (see below). Objective 3. A prospective randomized controlled trial to compare the benefits and complication rates of R-LESS versus conventional laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) as an elective treatment of symptomatic gallstone disease. This clinical comparative study was finally started from September 2015 till the closure of this project (October 2016). A total of 35 patients were enrolled in this comparative study (17 R-LESS and 18 LC). The last patient with R-LESS was operated in October 2016. There was some delay in the commencement of this comparative study due to the prolonged course of the prior pilot series. After all, we had done our best to restructure our operating list arrangement so as to facilitate as frequent robotic assisted cholecystectomy as possible. Due to the fact that our team can only use the robotic theatre only once every two weeks, a total of 17 patients were finally recruited for R-LESS cholecystectomy arm. During the same period, 18 patients were recruited for the conventional laparoscopic cholecystectomy. When analyzing the perioperative outcomes of these 35 recruited cases, we found no significant difference between R-LESS cholecystectomy and conventional LC in several important clinical parameters (Please see the outcome session). Moreover, patients with the R-LESS cholecystectomy had significantly more early postoperative wound pain. We considered that further enrollment of three more patients in the R-LESS arm (initial target was 20) would unlikely make any difference and thus we decided to conclude the study at this point.

471412.label: Major findings and research outcome
471412.value: Part 1. Animal Study 24 swine experiments were performed (24 LESS cholecystectomy and 24 gastrojejunostomy (GJ)). All GJs created were patent. There was no leakage during the two weeks of survival observation. In cholecystectomy, when compared to H-LESS, R-LESS was associated with significantly lower NASA task load index (TLI) (P<0.001) and reduced difficulty in exposure of the gallbladder (P=0.037), dissection of the calot’s triangle (P=0.003) and ligation of cystic artery/duct (P<0.001) . In GJ, R-LESS was also associated with significantly lower TLI (P<0.001) with reduced difficulty in performing the anastomosis (P<0.001) and closure of the enterotomy (P=0.002). No morbidity/mortality were observed. These indicate that R-LESS approach reduced workload in both benchmark procedures. Part 2. Prospective Pilot Clinical Series of R-LESS Cholecystectomy A total of 10 patients were recruited for R-LESS cholecystectomy. One patient required conversion to open surgery due to the presence of a cholecysto-colonic fistula. For the remaining 9 patients, their mean (S.D.) age was 62.4 (9.1) years and 6 were male. The mean (SD) operation time was 95.6 (27.1) minutes and blood loss was 7.2 (2.6) ml. Mean hospital was 1.9 (range 1-3) days. None suffered from severe adverse events. Two patients needed conversion to conventional laparoscopic approach. This pilot study confirmed that R-LESS cholecystectomy was a feasible and safe procedure in human. Part 3. Clinical Comparative Study 35 patients were recruited, with 17 undergoing R-LESS and 18 laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC). There were no differences in background demographics. None required conversion. There were no differences in mean (SD) operative time [65.5 (20.4) vs 76.1(18.2) minutes, P=0.114), hospital stay [1.5 (0.7) vs 1.2 (0.2) days, P=0.09) and morbidity rates (11.8% vs 0%, P = 0.35). There was also no difference in the overall difficulty experienced by the surgeons during the procedure [NASA TLI: 1.5 (1.3) vs 2.8 (2.6), P=0.073) and the overall post-operative pain on days-1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 4 weeks. There was significantly more pain on D1 after standing for 5 minutes [5.4 (2.7) vs 2.8 (2.5), P = 0.05) in the R-LESS group. No difference in satisfaction scores [7.1 (2.9) vs 8.5(1.5), P=0.079] was observed. We concluded in this study that R-LESS cholecystectomy was comparable to conventional laparoscopic cholecystectomy in the perioperative parameters and safety profile. It did not confer any significant clinical advantage over conventional LC but was found to be associated with more early postoperative wound pain and lower patients satisfaction.

471412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
471412.value: A newer generation of surgical robot from Intuitive (USA) is now available as a prototype and has recently been installed in the teaching hospital (Prince of Wales Hospital). The design of this new robot system is focused on single incision with the 3D-camera-scope and robotic arms all passed through a common trocar port system. One of the Co-Is of the current project, Prof Philip Chiu, plan to make use of this new prototype for an even more complex procedure, namely single incision robotic-assisted oesophagectomy for carcinoma of the esophagus, in human patients. The currently completed project has set a good foundation for our surgical team to move on to the next stage to use newer surgical robot for single-incision surgery. This is one of the reasons leading to an opportunity of potential collaboration with the industrial partner for further clinical research.

471412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
471412.value: Minimally invasive surgery is a standard for many operations nowadays. With advancement of surgeons' skill, there is a desire to further reduce the number of incision for achievement of even better treatment outcomes. This intention was, however, hindered by the intrinsic design problem of equipment which causes paradoxical movement and crushing of instruments inside the patient's body. On the other hand, the extra degree of freedom of the endowrist and also ability to digitally switch the left and right hand instruments in the Da Vinci surgical robot was once considered to be a potential solution for overcoming the difficulties in laparo-endoscopic single-site (LESS) surgery. Our animal study has scientifically verified the feasibility of Robotic-assisted LESS surgery. We also proved that it could reduce the workload strain to the surgeons during LESS operations. Our clinical pilot study confirmed the safety of Robotic-LESS cholecystectomy in patients with gallstone disease. The subsequent comparative study, however, was unable to demonstrate any advantage from using the robot in performing LESS cholecystectomy. It also revealed that patients undergoing Robotic-LESS cholecystectomy had more early postoperative wound pain and lower cosmetic satisfaction. This triggers the need to design more specific robotic system for single incision surgery (the industry is embarking).

472112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
472112.value: Although spinal anaesthesia is preferred for caesarean delivery, it causes haemodynamic disturbances that potentially threaten maternal and neonatal wellbeing. In this area, we are world leaders in the investigation of alpha agonist drugs such as phenylephrine. Previously, we showed that phenylephrine has improved efficacy and less adverse fetal effects than the previous standard, ephedrine. However, there is concern that phenylephrine slows maternal heart rate which can decrease the output of the heart which may not be optimal for placental perfusion. Our present proposal considers a potential improvement on phenylephrine: use of a related vasopressor, norepinephrine that has less tendency to decrease heart rate. Norepinephrine is structurally and functionally related to phenylephrine. Because it causes mild stimulation of heart beta receptors it has less propensity to decrease heart rate and cardiac output and thus may be ideal for obstetric spinal anaesthesia. Norepinephrine is recommended by the manufacturer for treatment of hypotension associated with spinal anaesthesia, but has been rarely been described for this. It is an old drug readily available in hospital pharmacies and most anaesthesiologists are familiar with its use in anaesthesia and intensive care. This prospective double-blinded randomized clinical trial compares norepinephrine with phenylephrine, our current standard, given by infusion for maintaining blood pressure in 104 elective caesarean patients having spinal anaesthesia. The primary outcome is non-invasively measured maternal cardiac output. Secondary outcomes include serial heart rate changes, accuracy of blood pressure control assessed using performance error calculations and assessment of maternal symptoms and neonatal outcome. Umbilical cord blood will be assayed for norepinephrine, epinephrine, glucose and lactate as markers of fetal metabolic state. From experience in non-obstetric patients and preliminary investigation in obstetric patients, we have estimated approximately equipotent concentrations of phenylephrine and norepinephrine. These vasopressors will be administered by intravenous infusion, which we have previously been shown to be highly effective. In addition, we will employ a closed-loop feedback computer-controlled infusion system for delivery that we have recently developed and described. This has the unique advantage of ensuring accurate and objective vasopressor administration, thus minimizing investigator bias arising from manually-controlled delivery. The results from this study will have potential to further knowledge about the nature and management of haemodynamic changes in anaesthetized obstetric patients. Most importantly, if norepinephrine proves to be superior to phenylephrine, the results of this work will provide direction for further research and could contribute to evidenced-based recommendations that would change clinical practice. 剖腹生產手術會優先彩用脊髓麻醉，但它會干擾血液流動力因而有潛在威脅產婦和新生兒健康的可能。我們調查α受體激動劑的藥物(alpha agonist)，去氧腎上腺素(phenylephrine) ，這方面可以說是世界的領導。之前，我們發表去氧腎上腺素具有更好的療效而且相對以往的標準藥麻黃素(ephedrine)，去氧腎上腺素對胎兒有較少不良的影響。然而，關注到去氧腎上腺素會減慢產婦心臟速率使心臟的輸出降低，這對胎盤灌注並不理想。我們在本文提議去氧腎上腺素一個潛在的改善：使用相關的血管加壓素，去甲腎上腺素(norepinephrine)有減低產婦心臟減慢的趨勢。去甲腎上腺素的結構以及功能和去氧腎上腺素相似。由於它輕度刺激心臟β受體，它有較少減低心臟速率和心臟輸出量，因此可能使用在產科脊髓麻醉是理想的。製造商也建議使用去甲腎上腺素治療因脊髓麻醉引起的低血壓，但已很少被描述。在醫院藥房，它是一個隨時可以獲取的藥，在麻醉深切治療部的大多數麻醉師都熟悉怎樣使用它。 這個是前瞻性雙盲隨機臨床的試驗，比較去甲腎上腺素和去氧腎上腺素，我們目前在脊髓麻醉非緊急性剖腹生產的的標準做法是以輸液維持104個案例的血壓。主要的測量是非侵入性量度母體心臟輸出量。次要的測量包括：串行心臟率的變化，使用性能的計算誤差去評估血壓控制的準確性，以及評估孕婦的症狀和新生兒的狀況。胎兒代謝狀態的標誌物可以靠臍帶血內的去甲腎上腺素，腎上腺素，葡萄糖和乳酸檢測。 我們估計約等療效的去氧腎上腺素和去甲腎上腺素的濃度是從以往非產科患者和初步調查的產科病人得知。這些升壓藥會由靜脈滴注，我們先前使用過並證明非常有效。此外，我們將採用一個閉環反饋的計算機控制輸注系統進行傳遞，它是我們最近開發和發表過的。這個升壓藥的管理具有獨特的優勢，確保準確而客觀，因而大大減少調查員手動控制輸注傳遞所產生的偏見。 這個研究結果將有可能加強進行麻醉的產科病人的血液流動力學變化的性質和管理這一方面的知識。最重要的是，如果去甲腎上腺素證明是優於去氧腎上腺素，這項研究的結果將是研究的進一步方向，也可能有助於以證據為基礎的建議，而改變臨床的實踐。

472112.label: Major findings and research outcome
472112.value: The major finding of this project was that norepinephrine is a suitable alternative to phenylephrine for maintaining blood pressure during spinal anaesthesia. The study results showed that norepinephrine had equal efficacy for maintaining blood pressure, with the additional benefit of being associated with better maintenance of maternal heart rate and cardiac output. Fetal safety was confirmed by equivalent Apgar scores between groups and slightly better values for umbilical cord gases in the norepinephrine group. The following research outcomes were achieved: 1) Presentation of results as an oral presentation at a major international anaesthesia conference; 2) Prize for the best research paper at a major international anaesthesia conference; 3) Publication of an abstract in an international peer-reviewed anaesthesia journal; 4) Publication of a full paper in the journal Anesthesiology which is the highest ranked journal of the specialty of Anesthesiology; 5) Accompanying editorial in the journal Anesthesiology.

472112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
472112.value: Following our confirmation of the potential advantages of norepinephrine as a vasopressor in obstetric anaesthesia has established a basis for further investigation of norepinephrine in this context. We have written proposals for further related studies including a comparison of administration by bolus versus and infusion and a classic single bolus dose-response comparison. These studies have recently been granted ethical and institutional approval and have been registered in an international clinical trials registry. A future project is planned to evaluate umbilical cord blood oxygenation as a primary outcome to confirm the secondary outcome findings of the current study.

472112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
472112.value: This project showed that the drug norepinephrine can be used safely and effectively to maintain blood pressure in women who have spinal anaesthesia for caesarean delivery. Compared with the current standard drug phenylephrine, norepinephrine was equally effective for maintaining blood pressure but has the advantage of keeping maternal heart rate and cardiac output closer to the normal baseline. Additionally our results showed that the clinical outcome of the babies was similar with norepinephrine compared with phenylephrine. Assessment of umbilical cord blood at delivery showed slightly higher oxygenation with norepinephrine which may reflect the higher cardiac output and is further evidence for the safety and efficacy of norepinephrine. This is the first study to demonstrate the possible usefulness and efficacy of norepinephrine as a vasopressor in obstetric patients. The results suggest that norepinephrine may be an ideal drug in this context and set a firm basis for clinical use and further evaluation.
