473012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473012.value: Femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) syndrome is a newly defined chronic nonarthritis hip pain that is due to the chronic impaction of the femoral head on the acetabular rim. The cam-type FAI is associated with physical activity and is common in athletes and active young adults. The estimated prevalence is 10%–15%. Cam-type FAI is now recognized as a possible leading factor to osteoarthritis in young patients. Understanding the detailed statistical shape abnormality of the femoral head and the acetabular rim in cam-type FAI is critical in making the right diagnosis and thus taking the right action to prevent further progression. The abnormality in the shape of the femoral head is observed visually or assessed by the femoral head asphericity in the 2D MRI or CT images. However, the osseous abnormalities are so subtle that the radiographs of FAI are prone to be mis-interpreted as ‘normal’ unless the radiologist is experienced enough and careful inspection is taken. On the other hand, the 2D manual assessments are prone to errors induced by the projection angle, tissue occlusion on the radiographs, and inter-rater variability. Currently, there is no published research on investigating the 3D morphological difference in cam-type FAI. In this project, we plan to use the advanced computerized method, i.e., statistical surface morphometry, to objectively quantify the local and global morphological changes in patients with FAI. The morphometric findings from this study will depict a clear picture of the anatomical changes, and provide for the first time the objective, statistical, and quantitative evidence of the shape abnormality in FAI. These findings not only help to deepen the understanding of pathomechanics of FAI, but also contribute to the diagnosis, management, and treatment planning of this condition. In particular, based on these morphometric differences, we will design and develop a computer system prototype to provide the probability of being a FAI patient for a test subject, and provide the grading information. It will be a 'second opinion' that helps the doctor to make the right diagnosis. 股骨髋臼撞击综合症(簡稱FAI)是一種新定義的慢性髖關節疼痛，是由於股骨頭在髖臼緣的慢性衝擊而產生的。曲柄型FAI與身體運動相關，常見於運動員和年輕人群，是目前公認的年輕患者中骨性關節炎可能的主要致病因素，患病率估計為10％-15％。對FAI的正確診斷與治療有賴於對病患者股骨髋臼統計形態學的詳細研究。現時對FAI股骨頭的形態僅可通過二維的MRI或CT圖像進行目測評估。然而，骨形態上的差異是如此微妙，以至於除非醫生具有足夠的經驗，FAI病人的影像數據很容易被誤判為“正常”。目前，還沒有研究定量的探討曲柄型FAI的股骨髋臼三維形態異常。在此項目中，我們計劃使用先進的計算學方法，即表面形態計量統計學，客觀地量化曲柄型FAI患者局部和全局的形態變化。這項研究的結果將有助於加深了解曲柄型FAI的病理機制，也有助於臨床診斷和治療規劃的制定。

473012.label: Realisation of objectives
473012.value: 1. To use the statistical surface morphometry technique to objectively quantify the local and global morphological changes in patients with cam-type FAI. The techniques of performing femoral head and neck alignment, landmark analysis and building statistical distance map was developed and tested. These techniques were also extended to neuroimage analysis, such as investigating the abnormal organization of brain structural network in patients after ischemic stroke [1], developmental dyslexia [2], patients with obstructive sleep apnea [3], as well as predicting cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome [4]. In addition, we also developed a high quality representative brain atlas based on Chinese pediatric population using intensity and sulci landmark [5], a new Chinese brain atlas based on a muti-center MRI datasets of 2020 Chinese adults [6], and a series of tractography atlas for diffusion tensor image quantitation [7]. In order to accelerate the registration, a GPU implementation of FLIRT and ANTs was been developed [8]. The accelerated algorithms could greatly outperform the original algorithm in terms of computational efficiency and shows great potential of clinical applications. The morphometry analysis was performed between normal and FAI group. MRI data was first segmented automatically. Then the affine registration was first performed to align the 3D surfaces among the group, and then the mean images of normal and FAI groups were calculated. As the resolution of the data is high enough, its 3D surface reconstruction result is comparable with that of CT. In addition, we also extended the morphometry analysis to the basal ganglia structures in children with obstructive sleep apnea [9]. 2. To build the statistical surface model of the femur in cam-type FAI and normal subjects. In order to give a more clearly definition of the morphometry analysis, we proposed an approach by considering the curvature information and distance information between neighbouring landmarks, which has also been used to detect the talar dome surface in CT [10]. We also proposed a new midsagittal plane (MSP) extraction method based on 3D scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT), in which the fissure plane is determined by parallel 3D SIFT matching and iterative least-median of squares plane regression [11]. 3. To develop novel computerized image segmentation techniques to segment the femoral head and neck in T1W-MRI data. To improve segmentation, we proposed a series of approaches to balance the noise reduction and detailed image characterization preservation. We have proposed a new technique to enhance image quality using feature-preserving denoising method based on an assumption of spatially varying Rician noise map [12]. In addition, a two-step optimization approach was further proposed to solve the convex denoising model [13]. An optimization algorithm based on a second-order total generalized variation image reconstruction model was also proposed [14]. In order to eliminate the effect of MRI scanners and parameters setting, a histogram-based normalization technique was proposed, and the results showed our proposed method could greatly improve the performance of MRI analysis [15]. To segment the femur in MRI, a 2D slice of the coronal view was firstly selected which was assumed to be the most median image by the user. Then its previous and subsequent slices within 7mm were extracted. After using thresholding method, the initial result of cortical bone was obtained. Using the thresholding result as a binary mask, voxels unmasked with high signal value were treated as trabecular bone and other tissues and removed. Then the summation of these slices was served as input for segmentation. With denoising, thresholding and hole filling, an initial segmentation result was obtained. Then the largest component of the result was used as the initialization for active contour model. The final result was obtained after active contour method optimization. Our segmentation method and its corresponding quality control were also been tested in a project regarding glenoid bone [16]. Further study might be investigated in the future to solve the problems of the likely inclusion of rim of the acetabulum and improving the segmentation accuracy. Recently, we also proposed a series of automatic segmentation methods. By using morphological operations and geodesic active contour, we proposed an effective algorithm to segment aligned free induction decay sequential myocardium images [17]. Based on adaptive distance metric learning, an automatic approach was proposed for DTI segmentation [18]. Based on the K-means clustering and gradient-vector-field-driven deformable model algorithms, a fully automated method was proposed for the segmentation of adipose tissue and visceral adipose tissue using MRI [19]. We also proposed a robust and efficient approach to automatically locate and identify vertebrae in spine CT via a joint learning model with deep convolutional neural networks [20]. These novel approaches could also be used in femoral head and neck segmentation for the performance improvement. 4. To validate the developed segmentation and morphometric analysis method with clinical data. Qualitative and quantitative analyses of the segmentation and morphometric results of the proposed method were performed and compared with two widely used methods, i.e., active shape model (ASM) and traditional graph-cut (GC), with results from manual delineation as the ground truth. The mean dice coefficient of the proposed SP-GC was 0.96, which turned out to be higher than those of ASM and GC (0.88 and 0.94 respectively). The mean normalized error rate of the SP-GC results was 10% and 6% lower than those of ASM and GC, respectively[21]. 5. To employ the statistical difference in providing a 'second' opinion on diagnosis and grading of cam-type FAI by developing a computer-aided system. Before training the MRI classifier, the surface model of the femur needs to be generated incorporating the femur boundary extracted from CT data. However, the accurate automatic segmentation of the femur in CT is still is problem. Thus, a new automatic approach for segmentation of proximal femoral head from CT images was introduced using the statistical Shape Prior into the Graph-Cut framework (SP-GC) [21]. The FAI CAD system included segmentation module, visualization module, probabilistic classification module and knowledge-base updating module. Our image segmentation module was developed based on our technique on vertebral body segmentation [C5, C7, C12]. The visualization module and probabilistic classification module were created based on our previous experience on spine project [C2, C6, C10, C11] and other projects [C1, C3, C4]. Based on the experiences in this project, we extend the system to the assessment of spinal inflammation on MRI in spondyloarthritis. The results demonstrated the CAD system was quick and highly reliable [22]. With this pipeline, we also developed a prototype for computer-assisted surgical planning of the hearing aid implantation surgery, which included a segmentation technique for the mastoid bone, a marching cube methodology to generate the surface of the skull, and a transformation of the results into 2D DICOM images [C14]. The development of these CAD systems would greatly increase the diagnosis accuracy, reduce the surgical risk, shorten surgical time, avoid secondary surgery and decrease surgical cost.

473012.label: Major findings and research outcome
473012.value: In this project, we have developed a series of approaches including MRI image denoising[12-14], normalization [15], realignment [5], segmentation[18-21], as well as morphometric analysis [10, 11, 16]. These approaches have been also used in the orthopedics and neuroimage analysis and showed good performance [1-4, 6, 7, 9, 17]. In order to improve the analysis speed, the GPU implementation of FLIRT and ANTs was been developed [8]. Recently, the deep learning approach was also introduced in orthopaedics image analysis, we proposed a novel joint learning model with deep convolutional neural network to automatically locate and identify vertebrae in 3D CT volumes. This approach could effectively identify the type of vertebra and eliminate false detections, and achieved a large margin with 10.12% improvement of the identification rate and smaller localization errors[20]. Based on these achievements, a series of computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems were developed, and showed good performance [22][C14]. In addition, we also published a few conference articles regarding orthopedics image analysis and bone quality assessment. These preliminary works enhanced our knowledge and quality of imaging processing; enable accurate and efficient extraction of useful information from orthopaedic images with clinical applications, and perform automatic registration of HR-pQCT data for longitudinal bone quality assessment [C8-C9]. Also, we proposed an improved version of the stacked auto-encoder (SAE) neural network, which can be further applied to classify the FAI and normal [C13].

473012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
473012.value: Based on our experiences, deep learning approaches showed excellent potential in biomedical images analysis, which may improve the performance of our FAI analysis. We would introduce the 3D convolutional network by harnessing the deep and hierarchical feature representations for segmentation related tasks in FAI analysis as well as the CAD system.

473012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473012.value: Femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) syndrome is a newly defined chronic nonarthritis hip pain that is due to the chronic impaction of the femoral head on the acetabular rim. Understanding the detailed statistical shape abnormality of the femoral head and the acetabular rim in FAI is critical in making the right diagnosis and thus taking the right action to prevent further progression. In this project, we proposed a series approaches for the FAI analysis and extended them to other related areas. These findings not only help to deepen the understanding of pathomechanics of FAI, but also contribute to the diagnosis, management, and treatment planning of related condition.

473512.label: Project Objectives
473512.value: Identification of EMP5 function. A comparative study on the mitochondrial transcripts between the mutant and WT will identify EMP5 functions in RNA processing, in particular, editing. Functional alterations in the target genes in the mutant will be explored to understand the impact on seed development. Developmental analysis of the emp5 mutant during seed development. We will examine the mutant structure alteration at multiple levels to reveal the developmental requirement of Emp5 for normal embryo and endosperm development, particularly the differentiation of transfer cells. Spatial and temporal expression of Emp5 gene. Using in situ RNA hybridization and protein immuno-fluorescent staining, we will reveal the cells and developmental stages where Emp5 exerts its function during seed development. By comparing transfer cell formation and EMP5 expression in different mutants, a link between transfer cell formation and embryo and endosperm development will be explored. Impact of over-expressing Emp5 on seed development. We will create transgenic plants over-expressing Emp5 in rice and maize and test its effect on seed development.

473512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473512.value: The goal of this project is to reveal the function of EMP5 and the potential mechanism by which EMP5 controls embryogenesis and endosperm development in maize. Embryo and endosperm are the two major tissues of a cereal grain. Their development influences the biochemical composition and agronomic quality of the grain. Understanding how embryo and endosperm are formed could enable the improvement of grain properties through biotechnology or traditional breeding. The emp5 mutant is a nuclear recessive mutation and homozygous lethal. Embryogenesis in emp5 was arrested in transition stage and the endosperm development is arrested at early stage. In addition, the mutant cannot form transfer cells, a type of highly specified endosperm cells responsible for nutrient transport from the mother plant to the seed. By transposon tagging, we cloned the Emp5 gene which predicts a PPR-DYW protein that is targeted to mitochondria. PPR proteins are a recently identified class of proteins that have loosely conserved 35-amino-acid repeats in tandem. PPR-DYW is a subclass of PPR proteins by having a DYW domain. PPRs are implicated in RNA processing in plastids and mitochondria. However, due to its large gene family size, functions of many PPRs are unknown. So far, the characterized PPR-DYW proteins mostly function in RNA editing. Hence, we hypothesize that EMP5 functions in the editing of one or several key mitochondrial transcripts where unedited versions severely compromised the function. This project will use molecular and genetic approaches to achieve these objectives: 1) To determine the function of EMP5 in mitochondria by analyzing RNA processing in the mutant and the WT, particularly RNA editing; 2) To determine the relationship between EMP5 expression and embryo/endosperm development, in particular, the transfer cell formation by analyzing EMP5 expression in conjunction with BETL2 (transfer cell) and KN1 (embryo meristem) protein expression in mutants that are known to affect specific development process. 3) To test the impact of over-expression of EMP5 on seed formation in transgenic plants. This research is expected to define a key function of RNA editing/processing in mitochondria in embryo and endosperm development in maize. Maize has been a powerful model system for functional genomics on seed development in grain crops by having large naked seeds, rich genetic resources and tools. As a major cereal crop, potential application of valued genes can be directly applied to other crops. 植物種子胚和胚乳的發育過程決定種子的大小、營養和質量，因此，了解它們的發生發育機制有助於通過生物技術和傳統育種的手段改善營養和提高質量。本研究的目標是揭示EMP5在玉米種子發育過程中的生物功能並探討潛在的機制。 本研究分離了emp5突變體，確定了突變導致胚胎和胚乳發育停滯，不能形成正常的轉移細胞。通過轉座子標籤技術，克隆了Emp5。初步研究結果表明Emp5編碼一個線粒體的PPR-DYW蛋白質。PPR蛋白是最近發現的一類蛋白質，因含有多個鬆散保守的35個氨基酸組成的重複序列而得名，一類在末段有一個DYW域，而命名為PPR-DYW。PPR蛋白的功能多在葉綠體和線粒體中RNA加工，但由於其家族較大，許多PPR蛋白的功能尚不清楚。鉴于PPR-DYW的功能主要為RNA編輯，我們提出EMP5功能是編輯一個或幾個線粒體基因的mRNA，而這些編輯位點對該基因的功能很重要。本項目將利用分子生物學和遺傳學的方法來實現以下目標：1）通過對突變體和野生型線粒體RNA的比較研究，揭示EMP5在線粒體RNA編輯/加工中的功能;2）通過分析BETL2（轉移細胞）和KN1（胚胎分生組織）的表達模式，確定EMP5表達和胚胎/胚乳的發育之間的關係。3）通過轉基因測試增加EMP5的表達量對種子形成的影響。 玉米是糧食作物種子發育功能基因組學的重要模式植物之一，這主要是因為玉米有豐富的突變體資源、高效的轉座子系統、良好的遺傳背景，加上全基因組的測序，以及裸露種子便於分析觀察等原因，作為一個主要的穀類作物，研究發現的有應用價值的基因可直接應用於其他作物。預計本研究將查明EMP5對線粒體中RNA編輯/加工功能，揭示在玉米胚和胚乳發育的作用，並探索其潛在的應用價值。

473512.label: Realisation of objectives
473512.value: Emp5 encodes a mitochondrion-targeted DYW subgroup pentatricopeptide repeat (PPR) protein. In this project, we characterized the empty pericarp5 (emp5) mutants in maize (Zea mays). Null mutation of Emp5 results in abortion of embryo and endosperm development at early stages. Analysis of the mitochondrial transcripts revealed that loss of the EMP5 function abolishes the C-to-U editing of ribosomal protein L16 at the rpl16-458 site (100% edited in the wild type), decreases the editing at nine sites in NADH dehydrogenase9 (nad9), cytochrome c oxidase3 (cox3), and ribosomal protein S12 (rps12), and surprisingly increases the editing at five sites of ATP synthase F0 subunit a (atp6), apocytochrome b (cob), nad1, and rpl16. Mutant EMP5-4 lacking the E+ and DYW domains still retains the substrate specificity and editing function, only at reduced efficiency. This suggests that the E+ and DYW domains of EMP5 are not essential to the EMP5 editing function but are necessary for efficiency. Analysis of the ortholog in rice (Oryza sativa) indicates that rice EMP5 has a conserved function in C-to-U editing of the rice mitochondrial rpl16-458 site. EMP5 knockdown expression in transgenics resulted in slow growth and defective seeds. These results demonstrate that Emp5 encodes a PPR-DYW protein that is required for the editing of multiple transcripts in mitochondria, and the editing events, particularly the Cto- U editing at the rpl16-458 site, are critical to the mitochondrial functions and, hence, to seed development in maize. We carried out the extensive experiments and key results are summarized in Section 6 below. Main results are published in Plant Cell (Liu et al. 2013). Three more papers were published with the support of this project. In conclusion, the project is well finished and in several areas, we exceeded our expectations.

473512.label: Major findings and research outcome
473512.value: 1). Identification of EMP5 function. After the cloning of Emp5 by transposons tagging and confirmation by multiple allele analysis, we predict that EMP5 functions in RNA editing in organelles based on the sequence information. Subcellular protein localization analysis using EMP5-GFP fusion revealed a mitochondrial localization of EMP5. A direct comparison of the mitochondrial transcripts between the emp5 mutant and the wild type was performed by amplifying the transcripts and analyzing their sequences. 35 sets of primers were designed to cover the predicted 35 mitochondrial protein-coding genes. Analysis of the mitochondrial transcripts revealed that loss of the EMP5 function abolishes the C-to-U editing of ribosomal protein L16 at the rpl16-458 site (100% edited in the wild type), decreases the editing at nine sites in NADH dehydrogenase9 (nad9), cytochrome c oxidase3 (cox3), and ribosomal protein S12 (rps12), and surprisingly increases the editing at five sites of ATP synthase F0 subunit a (atp6), apocytochrome b (cob), nad1, and rpl16. Mutant Emp5-4 lacking the E+ and DYW domains still retains the substrate specificity and editing function, only at reduced efficiency. This suggests that the E+ and DYW domains of EMP5 are not essential to the EMP5 editing function but are necessary for efficiency. Further analysis of the rice ortholog OsEMP5 identified a conserved function of EMP5. 2). Developmental analysis of the emp5 mutant during seed development. We examined the mutant seed developing profile and revealed null mutation of Emp5 results in abortion of embryo and endosperm development at early stages. The emp5-1 mutant kernel can be clearly distinguished from the wild-type siblings as early as 8 d after pollination (DAP), with characteristics of a small size and translucent appearance resulted from arrested embryo and endosperm development. Dissection of the emp5-1 mutant seeds at 8 and 13 DAP revealed that the mutant embryogenesis was arrested at the transition stage, characterized by the establishment of radial asymmetry that was introduced by the formation of an internal wedge-shape meristematic region in the upper part of the embryo. The endosperm development was blocked at the differentiation stage, characterized by the formation of distinct starchy endosperm and aleurone layer. Mutation of EMP5 also inhibits the differentiation of basal transfer cells. 3). Spatial and temporal expression of Emp5 gene. The Emp5 expression was detected by RT-PCR, and the results confirmed that Emp5 was expressed in all vegetative and reproductive tissues tested. Relative high mRNA expression was in stem, leaf, root, and ear and weak expression in tassel and kernels at developmental stages. This suggests that the EMP5 function may not be limited to embryo and endosperm development. Rather, it may have functions in other vegetative tissues during plant growth and development. 4). Impact of over-expressing Emp5 on seed development. We attempted to transform maize with EMP5 in collaboration with Prof. JR Zhang at Shandong University, but we failed to identify reliable transgenic lines. The transformation of over-expressing EMP5 in Arabidopsis was performed. Interestingly, there is no significant phenotype for overexpression of full-length EMP5 in Arabidopsis, but overexpression of truncated EMP5 proteins results in delayed bolting phenotype, and OE-C lines are also obviously smaller than WT plants. These results suggest that truncated EMP5 still had important effects on plant growth and development via regulating the mitochondrial function.

473512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
473512.value: In this study, we revealed that the E+ and DYW domains of EMP5 are not essential to the EMP5 editing function. However, the DYW domain that showed significant similarity to cytidine deaminases was proposed to have catalytic editing activity. We hypothesis that EMP5 associates with a DYW container partner, which can almost completely complement E+ and DYW motif truncation and carry out editing. In the future work, we will try to identify EMP5 interaction protein, it remains a question as to how a PPR protein such as EMP5 carries out the deamination of specific cytidine in mRNA. The editing mechanism is worth further investigation.

473512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473512.value: Understanding the mechanism governing seed development process is both a fundamental question in plant biology and also an important task in agriculture application, as seeds are staple food, and seed quality and size are controlled by the genes governing seed development process. We report here that mutation of Emp5 results in abortion of embryo and endosperm development at early stages. Analysis of the mitochondrial transcripts revealed that loss of the EMP5 function abolishes the C-to-U editing of ribosomal protein L16 at the rpl16-458 site, decreases the editing at nine sites in nad9, cox3 and rps12. Failure to editing causes dysfunction of EMP5 protein, resulting in failed mitochondrial respiration, hence arresting seed development. We also revealed the E+ and DYW domains of EMP5 are not essential to the EMP5 editing function. Analysis of the ortholog in rice indicates that OsEMP5 has a conserved function. These results demonstrate that EMP5 is required for the editing of multiple transcripts in mitochondria, and the editing events, particularly the C-to-U editing at the rpl16-458 site, are critical to the mitochondrial functions and seed development in maize. The revelation of this mutation affects seed size opens the possibility of enhancing the mitochondrial function for crop improvement.

473712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473712.value: 1. Aim The aim of this study is to conduct research into the connection between cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) and poststroke depression (PSD). 2. Project Background CMBs, small foci of chronic blood products in normal brain tissue, can be found in up to 25% of the elderly general population, and indicate underlying vascular pathologies. CMBs are associated with surrounding brain tissue damage, although whether they lead to deficits in neurological function, cognition, and disability remains unclear. CMBs are also common in stroke survivors: they are found in 60% of patients with a hemorrhagic stroke and in 30% of patients with ischemic stroke. Informative longitudinal studies are urgently needed to determine whether CMBs should affect the clinical decisions made in the day-to-day management of stroke survivors and the older population in general. Stroke is the most common severe neurological disorder, affecting 15 million individuals worldwide annually, 5 million of whom are left permanently disabled. Depression is the most common and most serious emotional disorder following stroke, affecting one-third of all stroke survivors. Depression is associated with poor short-term recovery and long-term rehabilitation outcomes, excess disability, cognitive impairment, and mortality in stroke survivors. A new model proposes that chronic vascular burden is a very important factor in the development of PSD. If this model is correct, then examining the association between PSD and CMBs (an indicator of underlying vascular pathology) will provide supporting evidence. 3. Project Description This will be the first longitudinal study to examine the role of CMBs in a large sample (n = 492) of consecutively admitted stroke survivors with PSD. Its results will shed light on the impact of CMBs on PSD risk, symptom severity and outcome. 4. Significance of Project The major strength of this study will be the interplay among several medical disciplines. The project will be carried out with the collaboration of psychiatrists, neurologists, and radiologists, thereby ensuring that comprehensive psychiatric, neurological, and radiological data are collected not only for evaluation in the present study, but also in future studies, e.g., studies of the risk factors and outcome of other poststroke psychiatric morbidity. 1.目的 本研究的目的是對大腦微出血與卒中後抑鬱的關係進行研究。 2.研究背景 大腦微出血是由於急性出血而在正常腦組織中產生的小病灶，其在高達25%的一般老年人群中被發現，並提示潛在的血管病變。儘管目前尚不清楚大腦微出血是否導致神經功能、認知功能及殘疾的缺陷，但其確與周圍腦組織損害有關。大腦微出血在腦中風患者中也很普遍：有60%的腦出血患者和30%的腦梗塞患者被發現存在大腦微出血。目前我們急需大量的縱向研究，以確定大腦微出血是否可以影響那些從腦中風患者和一般老年人群日常管理得出的臨床決策。 中風是一種最常見的嚴重的神經疾病。每年全球範圍內有一千五百萬人罹患此症，而其中五百萬人遺留終身殘疾。抑鬱症是中風之後最常見最嚴重的情緒障礙，其影響三分之一的腦中風患者。抑鬱與腦中風患者的短期痊癒、長期康復效果、嚴重殘疾、認知缺陷以及死亡率有關。一個新的理論模型認為慢性血管負擔是卒中後抑鬱的發展過程中的一個十分重要的因素。如果這個理論是正確的，那麼通過檢測卒中後抑鬱與大腦微出血（一個潛在血管病理學指標）之間的關係將提供支援的證據。 3. 研究計劃描述 這將是首次對被診斷為卒中後抑鬱的腦中風患者進行大樣本（492例）的縱向研究，以確定大腦微出血在其中所扮演的角色。此研究的結果將會闡明大腦微出血對於卒中後抑鬱的罹患風險、症狀嚴重程度以及轉歸的影響。 4. 研究的意義 本研究的重點在於多個相關學科之間的相互協作。本研究項目將通過精神病學家、神經病學家和放射學家的合作來實施。因此可以保證採集到廣泛的精神病學、神經病學和放射學的數據，這些數據不僅可以用於目前研究的評估，也可以用於未來的研究，比如其他卒中後精神疾病的危險因素與轉歸的研究

473712.label: Realisation of objectives
473712.value: MRI examinations were performed in 1456 patients and 531 (36.5%) were included in the study. The main reasons of exclusion were refusal (N = 278), alcoholism ( N = 111), were diagnosed of transient ischemic attacks (TIA) or cerebral haemorrhage (ICH) (N = 140), unable to access the patient (N = 127),with previous neurological diseases other than stroke (N = 53), physically too frail to be interviewed (N = 72), documented history of dementia (N = 39), severe comorbid medical disease (N = 28), severe aphasia (N = 22), deceased (N = 19), restroke (N= 13), non-Chinese ethnicity (N = 13), non-Cantonese speakers (N = 4), have participated in the study before (N =4), and severe auditory impairment (N = 2).The National Institute of Health Stroke Scale total score of admission for both included and excluded groups have no significant difference (p=0.437). The final sample has the following characteristics (N = 531): 60.1% were male, a mean age of 66.25, and an average education level of 7.5 years. Their mean MMSE was 26.5. 381 patients completed the 9 month follow up and 291 patients completed the 15 month follow up. To examine the role of CMBs as a risk factor of PSD. The demographic and clinical variables and radiological characteristics of the patients with PSD were compared to individuals without PSD. Risk factors with a value of P < .10 were then analyzed by multivariate logistic regression analysis using a forward stepwise selection strategy. Two regression models were constructed, a predictive model where only MRI variables with a value of P < .10 (presence of pontine, thalamic and cerebellar CMBs, number of CMBs, presence of basal ganglia acute infarcts, and the number and volume of acute infarcts) were entered and an association model in which demographic and clinical variables were also entered. The statistical analysis was conducted using the SPSS, version 16.0. The level of significance was set at .05. In comparison with the non-PSD group, PSD patients were more likely to have lobar CMB (33.3% versus 19.9%; P=0.022). Lobar CMB remained an independent predictor of PSD in the multivariate analysis, with an odds ratio of 2.08 (P_0.032). Patients with PSD were also more likely to have pontine CMBs (32.0% vs 18.2%; P = .019). The presence of pontine CMBs remained an independent predictor of PSD in the multivariate analysis, with an odds ratio of 2.2 To examine the association of CMBs and severity of PSD, the demographic and clinical variables (age, sex, and NIHSS and GDS scores) and radiological characteristics of the any-CMB and no-CMB groups were compared using the χ2 test, Fisher's exact test and Mann–Whitney U test. The geriatric depression scale (GDS) scores were then adjusted for age, sex and NIHSS, and the ARWMC scores by analysis of covariance. To explore the effect of CMB location, the foregoing analysis was repeated for the no-CMB and lobar, deep and posterior fossa CMB groups. The mean GDS score of patients with lobar CMBs was significantly higher (12.6±2.6 versus 10.4±2.5, p=0.01 after adjusting for age, sex, global cognitive functions, neurological deficits and white matter hyperintensities). To examine the role of CMBs and the outcome of PSD, the demographic and clinical variables and radiological characteristics of the remitters were compared with those of the nonremitters using Fisher exact test, Student t test, or the Mann–Whitney U test, as appropriate. Risk factors with a value of P<0.10 were then analyzed with multivariate logistic regression analysis using a forward stepwise selection strategy. Only MRI characteristics were entered in the first model and clinical variables were added in the second model. If the correlations between any of these putative risk factors were ≥0.50, then additional models were examined to rule out colinearity. In the analysis, the odds ratio of any independent risk factor was interpreted as the risk of nonremission of PSD when all other risk factors were held constant. In comparison with the remitters, nonremitters were more likely to have lobar CMBs (18.4% versus 4.3%; P=0.024). Lobar CMBs remained an independent predictor of PSD in the multivariate analysis, with an odds ratio of 4.96 (P=0.039).

473712.label: Major findings and research outcome
473712.value: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of an association between CMBs and outcome of PSD. The results suggest that lobar CMBs are associated with nonremission of depression in patients with well-established cerebrovascular disease. Our results also suggest that lobar and pontine CMBs are associated with depression in patients with ischemic stroke. This finding suggests that CMBs are not only markers of underlying vascular pathology but that they may also influence the risk of PSD. Finally, our results suggest that lobar CMBs may contribute to PSD symptom severity. We have published two papers in peer-reviewed journals, including STROKE, delivered 14 presentations in international conferences, and trained one PhD student.

473712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
473712.value: Further investigations are warranted to clarify whether CMBs have any effect on the response of PSD to pharmacological and psychological treatments. As the prevalence of CMBs is as high as 23.5% in community-dwelling elderly, it would be logical to examine whether CMBs might also contribute to the outcome of depression in the general elderly population. In addition, further investigations are needed to clarify whether CMBs have any impact on the clinical presentation, treatment response, and outcome of PSD.

473712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473712.value: Stroke is a common and serious disease of the brain. Many patients with stroke have long term physical and psychological disabilities. Depression is common in stroke survivors. The cause of depression in stroke in not fully understood. In the project, we investigated the role of small bleedings in the brain and depression in stroke. We found that these small bleedings indeed increased the risk of depression, related to more severe depression and a reduced chance of recovery of depression in stroke survivors. These findings will enhance our understanding of depression and stroke and will stimulate further research in the prevention and treatment of depression in stroke.

474412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
474412.value: The aim of this project is to improve understanding of the functional properties of embryonic stem cells (ESCs)-derived cardiomyocytes. ESCs, derived from the inner cell mass of blastocysts, are capable of self-renewal and are pluripotent, meaning that they can propagate indefinitely in culture and have the ability to give rise to all differentiated cell types in the body, including cardiomyocytes. ESCs can therefore be an excellent source of cardiomyocytes for research and future therapeutic applications. For successful transplantation, transplanted cells must survive, integrate, and functionally couple with the native myocardium. The functional properties of these potential replacement cells must be better understood before such cells can be used for therapeutic purposes. Calcium transients are important determinants of the excitation-contraction coupling of cardiomyocytes. However, regulation of calcium transients in early differentiating cardiomyocytes is not fully elucidated. Previous studies showed that canonical transient receptor potential isoform 3 (TRPC3) channels are expressed in adult cardiomyocytes and are involved in hypertrophy. However, there is no study on the functional role of TRPC3 in normal cardiomyocytes and during cardiac development. Preliminary data from our group showed that TRPC3 proteins are expressed in ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. In addition, specific TRPC3 inhibitor PyR3 decreased both the amplitude and the frequency of calcium transients in a concentration-dependent manner. These novel data suggested a role of TRPC3 in regulating the calcium transients of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. However, the mechanism underlying how the TRPC3 affects calcium transients is unknown. It has not been elucidated whether TRPC3 forms a signaling complex with sodium-calcium exchanger and/or L-type voltage-gated calcium channels to mediate effects downstream of TRPC3 activation. In addition, whether TRPC3 proteins and canonical transient receptor potential isoform 6 (TRPC6) proteins heteromerize to form functional channels to regulate the calcium transients is unknown. The overall objective of this proposal is to investigate the role of TRPC3 in determining the calcium transients of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. A combination of cell biology, molecular biology, electrophysiological and genetic manipulation techniques will be employed. This project will provide novel and important information on the role of TRPC3 in regulating the calcium transients and contraction of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. Therefore, the present study will be crucial for understanding the complex biology of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. The investigation will also be important for providing insights into the suitability of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes for future transplantation. Altogether, the present study will be pivotal for generating knowledge and revealing therapeutic potentials of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. 這個研究計劃的目的是提高對胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞在功能特性上的認識。 胚胎幹細胞來自囊胚的內細胞團，能夠自我更新和擁有萬能的特性，意味著它們可以無限地被培養，並有能力分化為體內所有的細胞類型，包括心肌。胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞能夠應用於研究和未來的治療，因此是一個很好的心肌細胞來源。能夠達致成功移植，移植的細胞必須生存，並與心臟的天然心肌在結構上和功能上整合。要應用胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞於細胞治療法之前，我們必須更好地理解這些細胞的功能特性。 鈣瞬變（calcium transients）是決定心肌細胞激發與收縮的聯結的重要因素。然而，我們尚未完全理解早期分化的心肌細胞在鈣瞬變的調節。以往的研究表明，經典型瞬時電壓受體通道3（TRPC3）表達於成人的心肌細胞中，TRPC3亦參與於心肌肥大的過程中。然而，現時還沒有研究查明TRPC3在正常心肌細胞和心臟發育過程中的職能作用。我們研究團隊的初步數據顯示，TRPC3蛋白表達於胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞中。此外，TRPC3的抑製劑PyR3能夠濃度依賴性地減少鈣瞬變的波幅和頻率。這些新的數據表明TRPC3能調節在胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞中的鈣瞬變。然而，我們尚未清楚了解TRPC3影響鈣瞬變的機制。再者，我們尚未知道TRPC3是否與鈉/鈣交換蛋白（sodium-calcium exchanger）和/或L-型電壓門控鈣離子通道（L-type voltage-gated calcium channels）組成信令配合物以介導TRPC3激活下游的效果。此外，TRPC3能否與經典型瞬時電壓受體通道6（TRPC6）蛋白結合而形成功能性的通道來調節鈣瞬變仍是未知的。這個研究計劃的的總體目標是研究TRPC3在胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞調節鈣瞬變的作用。我們會使用細胞生物學、分子生物學、電生理和遺傳操作技術以達致目標。 這該研究將對TRPC3在胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞調節鈣瞬變的作用提供新的和重要的信息。因此，本研究將對理解複雜的胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞的生物學至關重要。此外，本研究也將對胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞是否適合使用於將來的移植提供重要的見解。總括來說，本研究將揭示胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞的知識和治療潛力的關鍵。

474412.label: Realisation of objectives
474412.value: [Due to the required format of the present report, figures of the data cannot be shown. All data are available upon request.] Aim 1. To investigate if TRPC3 is involved in regulating the calcium transients of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. By immunocytochemistry followed by confocal fluorescence microscopy, TRPC3 was found to express on the T-tubules of mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC)-derived cardiomyocytes (CMs) (mESC-CMs). By calcium imaging using confocal microscopy, PyR3, TRPC3-specific inhibitor, was found to decrease the amplitude and frequency, and increase the time-to-peak and decay rate of calcium transients (CaTs) in a concentration-dependent manner in mESC-CMs. PyR3 did not affect the baseline of the CaT level. The results suggested that mESC-CMs functionally express TRPC3, which can positively regulate the CaTs. By patch clamping using the voltage clamp mode (in ramp protocol), TRPC3 current was found to be present in mESC-CMs. By patch clamping using the current clamp mode to measure the spontaneous action potentials (APs), PyR3 was found to decrease the rate of AP (AP rate), increase the maximum diastolic potential (MDP), and decrease the slope of diastolic depolarization (DD slope) without affecting the AP duration (AP duration at 50% repolarization, APD50). Apart from using pharmacological tools, to investigate the role of TRPC3 in regulating the spontaneous APs of mESC-CMs, adenoviral plasmids Ad-CMV-DN-TRPC3-CMV-GFP and Ad-CMV-TRPC3-CMV-GFP were constructed to functionally knockdown TRPC3 (with dominant negative TRPC3, DN-TRPC3) and overexpress TRPC3 (with full-length TRPC3), respectively. Adenoviruses were used to infect mESC-CMs. Adenoviruses with DN-TRPC3 decreased, while adenoviruses with TRPC3 increased the TRPC3 current. Similar to blocking of TRPC3 by PyR3, functional knockdown of TRPC3 by DN-TRPC3 decreased the AP rate, increased the MDP, and decreased the DD slope without affecting the APD50. In addition, overexpressing TRPC3 exerted opposite effects on APs. Altogether, all these results strongly suggested that TRPC3 positively regulates the CaTs and the rate of spontaneous APs of mESC-CMs. Aim 2. To determine if TRPC3 regulates NCX1 and/or L-type voltage-gated calcium channels and forms a signaling complex with them to regulate the calcium transients of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes and the mechanism(s) behind the regulation by TRPC3. By immunocytochemistry followed by confocal fluorescence microscopy, mESC-CMs were shown to express the Cav1.3 (alpha 1D) subunit of L-type voltage-gated calcium channels and NCX1. By using the line scan mode of confocal microscopy, the alpha 1D subunit was found to locate on the T-tubule of mESC-CMs, similar to the location of TRPC3. By patch clamping using the voltage clamp mode (in ramp protocol), spontaneously beating mESC-CMs were shown to express L-type voltage-gated calcium current and NCX current. Altogether, TRPC3, NCX1 and L-type voltage-gated calcium channels are expressed in mESC-CMs. By calcium imaging using confocal microscopy, TRPC3 current was found to positively regulate the local calcium release (LCR) from the ryanodine receptor isoform 2 (RyR2). By patch clamping, NCX blocker KB-R7943 at low concentration (1μM) reduced DD slope of APs, and at high concentration (3μM) abolished spontaneous APs, suggesting the positive role of NCX current in determining the DD slope of APs. In addition, overexpressing TRPC3 increased while functionally knocking down TRPC3 decreased the NCX current in mESC-CMs. Since previous work has reported that LCRs via RyR2 increased the forward mode of NCX in adult cardiac cells [1], we speculated that TRPC3 positively controls the NCX current by increasing the LCRs to determine the DD of CMs with spontaneous APs. In summary, we proposed that TRPC3 current contributes to cardiac pacemaker activity by three pathways: 1) TRPC3 permeates both Ca2+ and Na+, which directly evoke membrane depolarization; 2) Ca2+ influx from TRPC3 channel induces LCRs from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) via RyR2, with subsequent activation of an inward NCX current, which exponentially increases the DD; 3) TRPC3 increases Ca2+-dependent phosphorylation of phospholamban (PLB) and RyR2 to support the robust, rhythmic SR Ca2+ cycle, which may increase the LCR and subsequently increase the NCX current as in pathway 2. All these three pathways will eventually depolarize the membrane to a voltage that can activate the L-type voltage-gated calcium channels on the T-tubules, leading to the phase 0 of spontaneous APs. Taken together, our results suggested that TRPC3 regulates NCX1 and L-type voltage-gated calcium channels and forms a signaling complex with them to regulate the CaTs and APs of mESC-CMs. Aim 3. To determine if TRPC3 and TRPC6 form a functional complex to regulate the calcium transients of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. By routine PCR, mRNA transcripts of TRPC6 were found to be present in spontaneously beating embryoid bodies. By immunocytochemistry followed by confocal fluorescence microscopy, however, single isolated mESC-CMs were only weakly stained with a diffused pattern when four different anti-TRPC6 antibodies were used, while the positive control cells were stained strongly. On the other hand, calcium imaging using confocal microscopy on mESC-CMs using ML-9 and hyperforin (non-specific blocker and activator of TRPC6 [2-3], respectively) were also done. Our results showed that ML-9 decreased the frequency of CaTs of mESC-CMs in a concentration-dependent manner. However, hyperforin increased the frequency but decreased the amplitude of CaTs of mESC-CMs. The mixed results from these non-specific blocker and activator are difficult to be interpreted. Given the non-specific nature of these drugs, and the low/no expression of TRPC6 at protein level, we decided to research another TRPC member that is known to form heterotetramer with TRPC3 - the TRPC7 [4]. By immunocytochemistry followed by confocal fluorescence microscopy, positive TRPC7 staining with a regular striated pattern was clearly detected in single isolated mESC-CMs. Some TRPC7 were found to locate near the Z-lines of the sarcomeres, the same position as where the TRPC3 channels are located. Therefore, further investigation would be conducted to investigate if TRPC3 and TRPC7 form a functional complex. Since there is no specific blocker or activator for TRPC7, molecular tools are needed to knockdown and overexpress the function of TRPC7 in order to elucidate its role in determining the spontaneous CaTs of mESC-CMs. Dominant negative of TRPC3/4/5/6 have been proven to be able to functionally knockdown their intact TRPC counterparts [4-5], but no dominant negative of TRPC7 is reported so far. Sequence alignment shows that three amino acids “LFW” lying in the pore region are highly conservative among all TRPCs in different species. Mutation of “LFW” to “AAA” has been adopted to construct the dominant negative of TRPC4/5/6 [5]. Adenoviral plasmids with this mutation has already been made in our laboratory, and we are in the process of testing whether this mutation can generate functional dominant negative of TRPC7. If this mutation is found to be able to exert dominant negative function, in the next phase of our study, we would use this strategy to extend our investigation. References: [1] Bogdanov et al. 474412.label: Major findings and research outcome
474412.value: TRPC3 channels are expressed in mESC-CMs. TRPC3 channel was found to express on the T-tubules of mESC-CMs. By whole-cell patch clamping, TRPC3 channel activity was also detected in spontaneously beating mESC-CMs. TRPC3 regulates calcium handling in mESC-CMs. TRPC3-specific inhibitor PyR3 concentration-dependently decreased the amplitude and frequency and increased the time-to-peak and decay rate of CaTs. A higher concentration of PyR3 even abolished CaTs. On the other hand, given that LCR from the SR plays an important role in achieving AP threshold in cardiac pacemaker cells, the role of TRPC3 on LCR in mESC-CMs were also examined. PyR3 reduced the frequency and amplitude of spontaneous LCR. Altogether, TRPC3 positively controls the CaTs and LCR in mESC-CMs. TRPC3 controls spontaneous APs by regulating the DD. PyR3 markedly reduced the AP rate, depolarized the MDP and decreased the DD slope without affecting the APD50 of spontaneous APs of mESC-CMs. Apart from pharmacological blocker, DN-TRPC3 was also used to knockdown the function of TRPC3 at molecular level. DN-TRPC3 decreased the AP rate, depolarized the MDP and decreased the DD slope without affecting the APD50. On the other hand, overexpressing TRPC3 increased the DD slope of spontaneous APs, further supporting the positive contribution of TRPC3 to pacemaker activity in mESC-CMs. TRPC3 current is positively correlated to NCX current. NCX current was detected in mESC-CMs. NCX blocker KB-R7943 at low concentration reduced DD slope of APs, and at high concentration abolished spontaneous APs, suggesting the positive role of NCX current in determining the DD slope of APs. Overexpressing TRPC3 increased while knocking down TRPC3 decreased the NCX current in mESC-CMs. Ca2+-dependent phosphorylation of RyR2 and PLB are positively associated with the TRPC3 current. Phosphorylation of cardiac RyRs at Ser2809 increases the activation of RyRs and enhances RyR Ca2+ release. In mESC-CMs, PyR3 reduced the phosphorylation of RyR2 at Ser2809 without affecting the total level of RyR2. In addition, phosphorylation of PLB at Thr17 decreases the activity of PLB, the inhibitor of sarcoplasmic reticulum/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) in unphosphorylated state. PyR3 was found to decrease the phosphorylation of PLB at Thr17 without affecting the total level of PLB, suggesting that TRPC3 may accelerate the Ca2+ handling by relieving the inhibition of SERCA by PLB. All results described above were published in form of conference abstracts and/or papers. The role of TRPC7 and the potential functional complex formed between TRPC3 and TRPC7 would be further investigated and future publications are expected.

474412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
474412.value: In this study, TRPC7 channels were found to express in mESC-CMs. Interestingly, TRPC7 channels were found to locate both near M-lines and Z-lines of the sarcomeres; this expression pattern is unique when compared to that of other ion channels (most of which are just located near Z-lines where T-tubules are situated). The function of TRPC7 locating near the M-lines is unknown. Further investigation would be conducted to investigate if TRPC3 and TRPC7 (for those near Z-lines) form a functional complex and to investigate the possible unique role of TRPC7 near the M-lines. Since there is no specific blocker for TRPC7, molecular tools are needed to functionally knockdown TRPC7 in order to elucidate its cellular function. Dominant negative of TRPC3/4/5/6 have been proven to functionally knockdown their intact TRPC counterparts, but no dominant negative of TRPC7 is reported. Sequence alignment shows that three amino acids “LFW” lying in the pore region are highly conservative among all TRPCs in different species. Mutation of “LFW” to “AAA” has been adopted to construct the dominant negative of TRPC4/5/6. We are testing whether this mutation can generate dominant negative of TRPC7. If successful, this will be a new tool for studying TRPC7 function in different cell types.

474412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
474412.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) can propagate indefinitely in culture and have the ability to give rise to all differentiated cell types in our bodies, including cardiomyocytes. ESCs can therefore be an excellent source of cardiomyocytes for research and future therapeutic applications. The functional properties of these potential replacement cells must be better understood before such cells can be used for therapeutic purposes. The aim of this project was to improve understanding of the functional properties of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes (ESC-CMs). Early differentiating ESC-CMs resemble cardiac pacemaker cells and generate spontaneous action potentials (APs). These spontaneous APs determine heart rate. In our study, using a combination of cell biology, molecular biology, electrophysiological and genetic manipulation techniques, we found that canonical transient receptor potential isoform 3 (TRPC3) channel is positive regulator of AP rate; increasing TRPC3 activity increases, while decreasing TRPC3 activity decreases the spontaneous APs. This project has provided novel and important information on the role of TRPC3 in determining the AP rate. Therefore, the present study is crucial for understanding the complex biology of cardiomyocytes with pacemaking activity. The present investigation is also important for providing insights into the possible strategies of manipulating ESC-CMs to make them more suitable for future transplantation.

474912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
474912.value: Ex vivo expansion of long term hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) for clinical application remains a challenge due to that the complex network of molecular and cellular signals that govern HSC quiescent, self-renewal and differentiation remains elusive. Physiological data indicates an oxygen gradient exists in the bone marrow and that the long-term HSCs in the bone marrow reside in a hypoxic microenvironment. Hypoxia inducible factors (HIFs) are the key transcription factors for adaptation to hypoxia. HIF is composed of two subunits, HIF and HIFβ. Among these two units, HIF expression levels are controlled in response to oxygen levels. Cellular levels of HIFα are regulated primarily through degradation of the protein. Investigations from our group show that genetic and pharmacological manipulation of the HIFa pathway in osteoblasts demonstrates a coupling mechanism of angiogenesis and osteogenesis mediated by HIFa. Our preliminary data shows that mice lacking VHL in osteoblasts exhibit differential hematopoietic phenotype including aberrant blood counts, altered HSC and progenitor numbers in the bone marrow when compared with the control littermates. Based on the above findings and given that both HSCs and osteoblast lineage cells reside in hypoxic region of bone and are spatially close to each other, we hypothesize that the oxygen sensing pathway in bone regulates extrinsic signals controlling hematopoiesis and stem cell niche function. The proposal has the following three specific aims. Aim 1 will determine the role of HIFa pathway in osteoblast lineage cells in regulation of hematopoiesis in mouse models with genetic manipulation of the oxygen sensing pathway using the Cre-Loxp strategy; Aim 2 will examine the localization of HSCs in the bone marrow and HSCs self-renewal, differentiation and homing in the mutant mice; and Aim 3 will define the molecular signals emanating from osteoblast lineage cells down stream of the HIFα pathway that regulate bone marrow microenvironment. We expect that the information obtained from this study will facilitate the development of novel therapeutic approaches for HSCs expansion for personalized regenerative medicine in patients with malignant blood diseases.

475012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
475012.value: 子宮內膜異位症是一種常見的婦科慢性疾病，其特徵為子宮內膜腺體和間質於子宮以外部位種植，常導致腹痛，不孕以及痛經。隨之帶來的社會經濟問題嚴重影響著全球婦女身心健康。然而，由於病因仍未明，導致治療方法有限且復發率高。 目前普遍認為新血管形成在子宮內膜異位症的發生發展過程中起到了關鍵作用。綠茶作為一種天然產物已被證實在癌症病人以及老鼠模型中具有抗血管形成的功效。所以，我們推論綠茶同樣能夠抑制子宮內膜異位症中的血管發生從而抑制病灶生長。 我們將在體外以及體內研究綠茶萃取物、綠茶兒茶素和其他血管生成抑制劑對血管形成的影響，進而評估綠茶在子宮內膜異位症中的抗血管形成作用。主要試驗方法： （1）體外細胞培養觀察血管上皮細胞增生、遷移、微血管形成； （2）通過改良的米勒氏血管通透性評價方法測試體內血管通透性； （3）通過動物內異症模型評估異位元病灶血管形成情況。 目前急切需要研發一種治療子宮內膜異位症的新型方案，而抗血管形成治療方法提供了一個新的切入點。天然產物中的抗血管生成小分子比合成抑制劑具有更獨特的優勢。本實驗將評估綠茶在治療子宮內膜異位症中的抗血管形成作用，該臨床試驗結果將為子宮內膜異位症新的治療手段提供依據。

475012.label: Realisation of objectives
475012.value: In this study, we employed our established in vitro and in vivo angiogenesis assays to characterize anti-angiogenic potentials of green tea catechin and its derivative for endometriosis and to compare its anti-angiogenic effects with angiogenesis inhibitor on endometriosis. Green tea epigallocatehin-3-gallate (EGCG) with the highest composition and the greatest anti-angiogenic activity amongst other catechins, a peracetate protected analog as pro-drug of EGCG (pro-EGCG), and an anti-angiogenesis VEGFR inhibitor PTK787 were studied. To compare the therapeutic efficacy of EGCG and pro-EGCG with current anti-endometriosis agent, a clinically used gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogue were also included. For in vitro angiogenesis assays, endothelial cell culture tests were used to measure endothelial proliferation, migration, invasion and tube formation. For in vivo angiogenesis assays Miles vascular permeability assay and experimental endometriosis model in mice were used to measure vascular permeability and endometriotic angiogenesis, respectively. For endothelial cell culture tests, we successfully determined the IC50 values of EGCG, pro-EGCG, PTK787 and GnRH as 50% effective concentrations to decrease the proliferation, migration, invasion and tube formation of endothelial cells in order to indicate the potential anti-endothelial effects of green tea and others on endometriosis angiogenesis. For Miles vascular permeability assay, we also obtained the IC50 values of EGCG, pro-EGCG, PTK787 and GnRH as 50% effective concentrations to decrease the absorption of the extravasated Evans Blue from the peritoneal microcirculation in order to indicate the potential anti-vascular permeability effects of green tea and others on endometriosis angiogenesis. For experimental endometriosis model, we then acquired the effective dose of EGCG, pro-EGCG, PTK787 and GnRH to significantly inhibit the total microvessel area and density in the endometriotic lesions determined by in vivo imaging and immunohistochemistry staining

475012.label: Major findings and research outcome
475012.value: EGCG and pro-EGCG has significant and highest inhibitory effects on the endothelial proliferation, migration, invasion and tube formation in vitro; and also significantly inhibited the vascular permeability and growth of endometrial implants in vivo. Pro-EGCG significantly reduced lesion size and weight, inhibited functional and structural microvessels in the lesions, and enhanced lesion apoptosis (Angiogenesis(1)2013, preliminary data from the original proposal was re-submitted prior to approval of the proposal and then accepted and published in Angiogenesis right after the approval of the proposal; PCT2014, CNpatent2015 & HKpatent2015, US, China and HK patents were filed). VEGFC and VEGFR2 signalling were the potential anti-angiogenesis target in endometriosis (Angiogenesis(2)2013, a mechanistic paper containing preliminary data from the original proposal was re-submitted prior to approval of the proposal and then accepted and published in Angiogenesis). The inhibition by pro-EGCG in all the angiogenesis parameters was significantly greater than that by EGCG and other catechins and angiogenesis inhibitors, with highest bioavailability and greater anti-oxidation and anti-angiogenesis capacities (JSepSci2014, an analytical and pharmacokinetic manuscript published in J Spe Sci; WCE2014(1), a paper presented in 12th World Congress of Endometriosis; Dalian2015, a paper presented in Annual Meeting of Society of Reproductive Medicine, World Federation of Chinese Medicine Societies; a manuscript is submitted to Hum Reprod). Oxidative stress and hypoxic regulatory factors mediated by macrophages in early angiogenesis and development of endometriosis were attenuated by EGCG and pro-EGCG (NOVA2013, a book chapter published in NOVA; PhD(1)2013, a PhD thesis was awarded; WCE2014(1), a poster presented in 12th World Congress of Endometriosis; ACE2014, a paper presented in 3rd Asian Conference on Endometriosis; Croucher2016, a paper presented in Croucher Summer Course 2016 Advances in Immunology in Health and Disease). Furthermore, immunosuppression mediated by myeloid derived suppressor cells to promote the growth, development and angiogenesis of endometriosis were also inhibited by EGCG and pro-EGCG (AJRI2014, another mechanistic paper was presented and published in Am J Reprod Immunol; ACE2014, a paper presented in 3rd Asian Conference on Endometriosis; Croucher2014, a paper presented in Croucher Summer Course 2014 Advances in Immunology in Health and Disease; PhD(2)2013, another PhD thesis was awarded). Biochemistry profiles and physiological angiogenesis in ovary and eutopic endometrium were not affected by either EGCG or pro-EGCG. Oral administration of pro-EGCG has higher efficacy than oral EGCG for endometriosis (ITF2013, a ITF Tier 3 funded to continue the study; CULifeSciShowcase2014, a in-house booklet to promote knowledge transfer published). Lesion sizes under pro-EGCG at 25-50mg/kg po remained underdeveloped after withdrawal. Whereas lesion sizes after withdrawal of Decapeptyl, Vatalanib/PTK787 and EGCG ip rebound (USprovisional2015, a new US provisional patent filed; an abstract submitted to 13th World Congress of Endometriosis). In conclusion, green tea EGCG and pro-EGCG significantly inhibited the development, growth and angiogenesis of experimental endometriosis in mice with high efficacy, bioavailability, anti-oxidation and anti-angiogenesis capacities. Pro-EGCG as an anti-angiogenesis agent will be a novel treatment and new research direction for endometriosis (ReprodSci2016, a research recommendations from a global consortium of investigators in endometriosis published online).

475012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
475012.value: A new HMRF grant was funded to conduct a randomised controlled trial of green eta extract for endometriosis (HMRF2016). In addition, the IP of pro-EGCG for endometriosis will be licensed to a pharmaceutical company for IND and NDA application. In addition, oxidative stress and hypoxic factors mediated by macrophages and immunosuppression mediated by myeloid derived suppressor cells in early angiogenesis and development of endometriosis could be the potential therapeutic targets of EGCG and pro-EGCG (a new GRF grant proposal submitted). On the other hand, the anti-cancer potential and its underlying mechanism of pro-EGCG on endometrial cancer was also studied by another PhD student. The results showed pro-EGCG suppresses endometrial cancer and angiogenesis through regulating tumor-associated macrophages (Croucher2016, a paper presented in Croucher Summer Course 2016 Advances in Immunology in Health and Disease).

475012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
475012.value: Endometriosis is a chronic disorder characterized by the implantation of endometrial glands and stroma outside the uterine cavity, leading to pelvic pain, infertility and menstrual problems. It is associated with high gynecological morbidity and socioeconomic problems as a major challenge to women health worldwide. The underlying cause of endometriosis is still poorly understood, the current treatment are inadequate. Endometriosis is an angiogenesis-dependent disease. Green tea is a natural product which has potent anti-angiogenic activities. We hypothesized that green tea could inhibit the angiogenesis and the progression of endometriosis. In our study, we confirmed green tea pro-EGCG significantly inhibited the development, growth and angiogenesis of experimental endometriosis in vitro and in vivo with high efficacy, bioavailability, anti-oxidation and anti-angiogenesis capacities. There is an urgent need in seeking better therapeutic approaches for endometriosis. Anti-angiogenesis therapy offers a new opportunity for the endometriosis treatment. Small anti-angiogenic molecules derived from natural products may have great potential and advantages over synthetic inhibitors. The results of the study will guide us to clinical trials of green tea as novel treatment for endometriosis in near future.

475912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
475912.value: Copepods form the largest class of small crustaceans and are the dominant component of the zooplankton in the world’s oceans and marginal seas. The role of copepods in the pelagic food web cannot be understood without detail information on their diet in the natural environment. Many studies on the feeding behavior of copepods have considered these organisms primarily as herbivorous grazers of phytoplankton, although numerous recent studies have revealed that most, if not all, copepods can feed effectively as omnivores. The most widely used approaches to study the diet of copepods in situ include the particle removal method and the gut pigment analysis method. The particle removal method is laborious and may require a high level of taxonomic expertise. The gut pigment analysis method is fast and inexpensive, but can only be used to obtain coarse taxonomic information on the ingestion of pigmented prey. More recently, DNA-based methods have been used to obtain dietary information on a variety of organisms, including insects and small planktonic organisms. Copepod diet can be determined by extraction, PCR amplification and identification of prey DNA sequences in copepod guts or fecal pellets. Real time quantitative PCR has been used to determine the quantity of specific prey in gut content. In this proposed study, a next-generation sequencing approach, 454 pyrosequencing, will be used to study the diet of C. sinicus, a key species of the zooplankton in the continental shelf waters along the Chinese coast, during its appearance in the coastal seas of Hong Kong in winter. The approach could produce much greater amount of sequencing data than traditional sequencing methods, allowing detection of even very rare prey items, and has recently been sussessfully employed to study the diets of several mammals and herbivorous invertebrates. We believe that the method will increasingly be used by scientists to study the food of minute, but ecologically and commercially important marine organisms and planktonic larvae. The specific objectives of the project are: (1) to develop a method based on 454 pyrosequencing coupled with PCR blocking to determine the composition and genetic diversity of the diet of C. sinicus; (2) to study the diet of C. sinicus of different developmental stages; and (3) to examine in situ food selection in C. sinicus by comparing the composition of prey in the copepod gut to that in the water. 橈足類動物為細小甲殼類之中最大的一個目,也是在海洋及緣海地區中最常見的浮游動物。由於缺乏有關牠們的食性資料,所以還是不能夠知道牠們在海洋食物網內擔當的角色。很多研究都把橈足類動物當成浮游植物的掠食者,但是近期很多研究都指出他們可能是雜食動物。目前最常用於食性分析的方法為腸道色素分析和顆粒去除方法。顆粒去除方法是很費力的及需要專業的分類知識。腸道色素分析是較便宜及迅速,但只適用於腸道內帶有色素的食物而且所得的資料都比較粗略。其實食性分析可以透過抽取,PCR增強及辨認橈足類動物腸道內食物的DNA去進行。這個新的食性分析方法可以應用於不同的生物上包括昆蟲及細小的浮游生物。中華哲水蚤是廣泛分佈於中國沿海大陸架水域的浮游動物關鍵種之一。本研究將採用焦磷酸測序這種新一代測序方法對冬季出現在香港沿海區域的中華哲水蚤進行食性分析。這個新的測序方法可以提供比以往的測序方法更多的基因序列從而可以探測到稀有獵物的碎件,而且近期更成功地被應用於哺乳類動物和草食性無脊椎動物的食性研究。我們相信這個方法將被更多科學家去應用於細小而且具有生態和經濟重要性的海洋生物和浮游動物的幼體。這個計劃的主要目的有:(1)利用454焦磷酸測序技術和聚合酶鏈式反應阻擋引子方法去測定中華哲水蚤捕食的選擇和成份;(2)進行成年和發育階段後期的中華哲水蚤的食性研究;及(3)透過比較水中生物和中華哲水蚤腸道內的生物成份從而了解中華哲水蚤在野外的食物取向。

475912.label: Realisation of objectives
475912.value: Objective 1: We developed a method based on Illumina sequencing combined with a peptide nucleic acid (PNA) blocker to investigate the diet of marine organisms. We used this method to successfully investigate the diet of the shallow water hydrothermal vent crab, Xenograpsus testudinatus (Ho et al. 2015). The PNA blocked ~80% of the amplification of crab DNA in PCR. X. testudinatus fed omnivorously on a diverse assemblage of organisms including algae, fishes and copepods. Subsequently, the composition and genetic diversity of the gut contents of the much smaller copepod Calanus sinicus were investigated using this method combined with a PNA blocker specific to this species. Adults and C5 copepodites were obtained from coastal seas of Taiwan and Hong Kong. DNA of prey items in gut of C. sinicus could be detected clearly only when the amplification of C. sinicus DNA was greatly suppressed with the use of the PNA blocker. C. sinicus, which is generally considered to be a primary consumer of phytoplankon, fed omnivorously on a variety of zooplankton, as well as phytoplankton and cyanobacteria. Except for one copepod sample from Taiwan, the genetic diversities of the prokaryotes were higher than that of eukaryotes. The eukaryotic diet of C. sinicus from Hong Kong and Taiwan were dominated, respectively, by the ctenophore genus Haeckelia (except one copepodite sample) and the jellyfish Apolemia. Malacostracan crustaceans were also common in C. sinicus from Taiwan (except two copepodite samples). Diatoms such as unclassified Mediophyceae and dinoflagellates such as unclassified Gymnodiniphycidae and unclassified Peridiniphycidae appeared in most C. sinicus samples taken from Taiwan and Hong Kong. Dinoflagellates and diatoms appeared in seawater samples from both areas. Syndiniales that includes parasites of copepods was found in some C. sinicus samples from both Taiwan and Hong Kong. Synechococcus and Propionibacterium were common prokaryotic component in all C. sinicus samples, except one adult sample from Hong Kong and one copepodite sample from Taiwan. Unclassified Actinomycetales were also found in C. sinicus from Taiwan, whereas Skermanella were common only in one sample collected in Hong Kong. Objective 2: We investigated the gut contents of C5 copepodites and adult. The gut content composition of copepodites and adults from the same collecting location did not differ significantly. The diet of C. sinicus was not stages-dependent. PCoA based on gut content composition of all copepods showed clear overlap between copepodites and adults, indicating that the diets of these two developmental stages were quite similar. This was also supported by statistical analysis (ANOSIM, R values < 0.6). Both adult and C5 copepodite of C. sinicus from Hong Kong fed on ctenophores, whereas individuals from Taiwan fed on hydrozoans. Objective 3: The composition of eukaryotes and prokaryotes in the gut contents of C. sinicus did not resemble those in the water column in both Taiwan and Hong Kong, suggesting that C. sinicus was feeding selectively. Common items in the gut content of copepods such as hydrozoans and ctenophores were absent in the water samples. Unclassified maxillopods, which were common in seawater samples, were only found in copepod samples from Hong Kong. Diatoms were present in seawater samples and all C. sinicus samples from Hong Kong. By contrast, diatoms were absent in seawater samples taken from TW2 and in some of the C. sinicus samples from Taiwan. Dinoflagellates were present in all seawater samples collected in Taiwan and Hong Kong, but absent in some of the C. sinicus samples. In Hong Kong, dinoflagellates were more abundant in copepodites than in adults. Unclassified Maxillopoda, the most abundant eukaryotes in seawater samples from both Taiwan and Hong Kong, was common only in C. sinicus from Hong Kong. Unknown Pelagibacteraceae dominated the prokaryotic communities in both Taiwan and Hong Kong. While the OCS155 group was abundant in all seawater samples, Halomonadaceae was abundant only in seawater samples collected from Taiwan. The only common items found in both seawater and copepods samples were the Synechococcus. However, Synechococcus was only found in one sampling site of Taiwan in low amount. Bacteria such as Skermanella and Propionibacterium was absent in the seawater samples. Therefore, we can conclude that C. sinicus is selective feeder of ctenophores, hydrozoans and cyanobacteria.

475912.label: Major findings and research outcome
475912.value: Our study uses NGS to show that Calanus sinicus can feed on a diverse assemblage of organisms including zooplankton, phytoplankton and cyanobacteria. C. sinicus is an important member of the genus Calanus, which is considered to play major roles in the trophic transfer pathway of oceans in the northern hemisphere as primary consumers of phytoplankton. C. sinicus is the most important copepod in the shelf waters of the western North Pacific, from Japan in the north to coastal seas along Vietnam in the south. The diet of C. sinicus is a topic of major concern to marine scientists. The diet of C. sinicus seems to be spatially specific, differing between Taiwan and Hong Kong, but the gut contents of individuals collected from same locations seem to be quite similar. Our results reveal unexpected items such as ctenophores and hydrozoans in the gut contents of C. sinicus. Therefore copepods, which are considered to be primarily herbivorous, may feed on the juvenile stages of their predators. Our findings will likely lead to some re-evaluation of the traditional concept of the marine food web. These results have been reported in five presentations in international conferences. A manuscript based on this research project has been submitted to an international journal and is currently being reviewed for publication.

475912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
475912.value: As the price of NGS is getting lower, larger number of samples can be analyzed to investigate ontogenetic changes as well as spatial and temporal variations in the feeding behavior of the marine organisms. Since Calanus sinicus is a major component of the marine plankton in the shelf waters along the Chinese coast, there is a need to study the diet of C. sinicus in other locations to expand our knowledge to the ecology of this important species. Although our study covered only three sampling sites in Taiwan and Hong Kong, our results revealed that the diet of C. sinicus included some unexpected items such as hydrozoans and ctenophores. In addition, methodology developed in our study can be used to investigate the diet of other organisms, especially other small planktonic organisms. The laboratory of the PI has begun a study of the natural diet of marine cladocerans, which are widely distributed, but whose feeding ecology is only poorly known.

475912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
475912.value: This study investigates the composition of eukaryotes and prokaryotes in the natural diet of adults and C5 copepodites of Calanus sinicus, an important copepod in shelf waters of the western North Pacific. Two genetic markers, variable regions of eukaryotic 18S and prokaryotic 16S rRNA genes, were amplified from the gut contents of C. sinicus collected from coastal seas around Taiwan and Hong Kong and sequenced by Illumnia sequencing. Results showed that the diets of adults and C5 copepodites were similar. Diatoms accounted for 3−38% of the 18S rRNA sequences in the gut contents of C. sinicus from both areas, but dinoflagellates were only found in C. sinicus from Hong Kong. Surprisingly, 18S rRNA sequences belonging to Hydrozoa were common in C. sinicus from Taiwan, whereas 18S rRNA sequences from Ctenophora were common in individuals from Hong Kong. C. sinicus from both areas contained 16S rRNA sequences from the cyanobacteria Synechococcus. Our results support previous suggestions that C. sinicus could feed omnivorously on a diverse assemblage of phytoplankton, animals and bacteria. More importantly, our findings show that large copepods may influence the populations of their predators by preying on their juveniles.
