476212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
476212.value: In plant cells, cellular proteins are sorted to vacuoles via a receptor-mediated mechanism. Vacuolar sorting receptor (VSR) proteins recognize the sequence-specific information, known as vacuolar sorting determinant (VSD), of the cargo-protein and, through receptor-cargo interaction delivers the cargo-protein to an intermediate prevacuolar compartment, before reaching the vacuole. All VSR proteins contain an N-terminal lumenal region, a single transmembrane domain, and a C-terminal cytoplasmic tail. The transmembrane domain and the cytoplasmic tail are responsible for targeting the receptor-cargo to the PVC/vacuole, while the lumenal region is responsible for specific receptor-cargo interactions. It has been shown that the protease-associated (PA) domain located at the lumenal region of VSR is involved in sequence-specific recognition of the Asn-Pro-Ile-Arg (NPIR) motif of cargo proteins such as aleurain. How VSR proteins recognize their cargo-proteins is poorly understood. This proposal aims to address this fundamental question of plant cells by structure determination of the PA domain of VSR isoform-1 from Arabidopsis thaliana (AtVSR1-PA) and its complex with ligand. Site-directed mutagenesis will be performed to locate the structural determinants for the ligand binding in AtVSR1-PA, and we will study how these structural determinants affects receptor-cargo binding in vivo. Domains will be systematically truncated from the lumenal region of AtVSR1 to investigate how these domains modulate ligand binding of AtVSR1. The proposed work will provide a better understanding of how VSR proteins recognize their cargo-proteins. The rules derived from our studies will be useful in predicting potential cargo-proteins within the genomes of Arabidopsis or other model organisms in the future. 在植物細胞中，細胞蛋白通過受體介導的機制被分揀至液泡。液泡分選受體(Vacuolar sorting receptor, VSR) 能夠識別被稱為液泡分選決定子的特定序列，通過受體-配體的相互作用將貨物蛋白在先於液泡之前被運送至液泡前體。所有的VSR蛋白都含有一個N-末端的管腔區域，一個單一的跨膜結構域和C-末端的胞質尾區。跨膜結構域和胞質尾區能夠將受體-貨物蛋白運送到液泡前體/液泡，而管腔區域則負責配體-受體特異性地相互作用。 位於VSR管腔區域的蛋白酶相關結構域能夠特異性地識別如貨物蛋白半胱氨酸蛋白酶的天冬酰胺-脯氨酸-異亮氨酸-精氨酸(Asn-Pro-Ile-Arg, NPIR)基序。目前，我們對VSR蛋白如何識別自己的貨物蛋白還知之甚少。本課題提案通過測定擬南芥VSR異構體-1的PA結構域 (AtVSR1-PA) 及其與配體的複合體結構，旨在解決植物細胞領域這一基礎問題。點突變實驗將用於確定AtVSR1-PA中與配體結合的結構決定簇，我們還將研究這些結構決定簇如何在植物細胞內影響受體與貨物蛋白的相互作用。AtVSR1的管腔區域將被系統地截短，由此得到的結構域將被用於研究它們是如何調節AtVSR1與配體的結合。從我們的研究中所得出的結論將在未來有效地預測擬南芥或其它模式生物基因組中潛在的貨物蛋白。

476212.label: Realisation of objectives
476212.value: First, we have determined the crystal structures of the PA domain of the Arabidopsis vacuolar receptor 1 (AtVSR1-PA) in its Apo- and cargo-binding forms. Apo-AtVSR1-PA was crystallized in 10% glycerol, 0.1M MES, pH 6.0, 30% PEG600, and 5% PEG1000 at 16 °C using the hanging-drop vapor diffusion method. Diffraction data were collected to 1.65 Å using an in-house diffractometer (Rigaku FR-E+). Iodide-derivative crystals of AtVSR1-PA, obtained by quick soaking of native crystals in mother liquor containing 2M KI, were used to determine the phases by the SAD method. To determine the crystal structure of AtVSR1-PA in complex with its cargo-peptide, we co-crystallized AtVSR1-PA and the aleurain peptide (ADSNPIRPVT) in 0.1M HEPES pH7.0, 25 % PEG6000 using the hang-drop-vapor-diffusion method. Diffraction data were collected to 1.9 Å and the phase was determined by molecular replacement using the structure of apo-AtVSR1-PA as the search template. For both the apo- and the cargo-binding forms, initial models were built using PHENIX.AUTOBUILD. The models were improved iteratively using COOT, refined using PHENIX.REFINE, and validated using MOLPROBITY. The AtVSR1-PA contains a seven-stranded beta-sheet surrounded by six helices. AtVSR1-PA undergoes major conformational changes upon binding of cargo peptides – large values of C-alpha displacement were identified in four regions, the switch I (residue 20-27), switch II (residue 44-53), switch III (residue 126-144), and the switch IV regions (residue 174-182). In the crystal structure of the cargo-binding form, the first three residues, 1ADS3, of the aleurain peptide were bound to a cavity of AtVSR1-PA formed by the cargo binding loop, 95RGDCYF100, and the switch III loop. In particular, the conserved Arg-95 residue form a hydrogen bond to the backbone oxygen of Ser-3 of the cargo-peptide. To test the role of Arg-95 in cargo-binding, we introduce a R95M mutation in the N-terminal domain of AtVSR1 (AtVSR1NT) and transiently transfect express R95M-AtVSR1NT in Arabidopsis protoplasts. Pull-down assay and co-immunoprecipitation experiments showed the R95M-AtVSR1NT failed to interact with the aleurain vacuolar sorting determinant (aleu-VSD). Moreover, co-expression of R95M-AtVSR1 and aleu-VSD-GFP in Arabidopsis resulted in secretion of the aleu-VSD-GFP, suggesting failure of cargo-receptor interaction that led to mis-sorting of cargo proteins. The structure of the cargo-peptide binding form suggests that AtVSR1-PA recognize the sequence preceding the NPIR motif. To test this hypothesis, we substituted the Ser-3 of the aleu-VSD to Gly and showed that S3G-aleu-VSD failed to interact with AtVSR1 in-vitro (by pull-down assay and co-immunoprecipitation), leading to mis-sorting of cargo-protein in Arabidopsis protoplasts. Comparison of the apo- and the cargo-binding forms of AtVSR1 revealed that the conformational changes at the cargo-binding loop are propagated to the C-terminal tail of the PA domain, which undergoes a swivel motion that brings the His-181 residue to form a hydrogen bond with Glu-24. We argued that this conformational change, which may translocate the Central domain of AtVSR1 towards the cargo-binding loop, is essential to cargo-receptor interaction. To test this hypothesis, we created a double mutant E24A/H181A of AtVSR1 that destabilize the conformational change. Consistent with our hypothesis, the E24A/H181A mutations abolished cargo-receptor in-vitro as well as resulted in mis-sorting of cargo in-vivo. In summary, through structure determination, site-directed mutagenesis and functional studies, we have achieved all the objectives of this project.

476212.label: Major findings and research outcome
476212.value: 1. Cargo-binding induces large conformational changes in AtVSR1-PA In this project, we have determined the crystal structures of AtVSR1-PA and its complex with a cargo-peptide derived from barley aleurain to 1.65 Å and 1.90 Å resolution, respectively. Structural comparison between the apo- and the cargo-binding forms reveals interesting insights into the mechanism of cargo-receptor recognition. The AtVSR1-PA contains a cargo-binding loop with a consensus sequence of RGxCxF. These residues form a cradle that recognizes the ADS sequence preceding the NPIR motif of sequence specific vacuolar sorting determinant (ssVSD). In the absence of cargo-peptide, the cargo-binding site is occupied by switch III residues, in which the conserved Glu-133 forms a salt-bridge with Arg-95 of the cargo-binding loop. Binding of the cargo-peptide displaces the switch III residues out of the binding pocket. This conformational change is propagated through an interconnected hydrogen-bonded network of switch I-IV residues, causing the switch IV residues of AtVSR1-PA to undergo of a large swivel motion of ~27.5Å that flips the C-terminus by ~180°. We further showed by mutagenesis studies that this swivel motion is essential to cargo-receptor recognition. 2. Residues preceding the NPIR motif are essential to cargo-receptor recognition The AtVSR1-PA was co-crystallized with the aleurain ssVSD sequence, 1ADSNPIRPVT10. Only the first three residues of ADS are observed in the crystal structure, while the other cargo sequences are disordered. Our structural insights that the PA domain recognizes the sequence preceding the NPIR motif is further strengthened by mutagenesis studies. We showed that the S3G mutation abolished the cargo-receptor interaction and resulted in mis-sorting of the cargos in-vivo. 3. The invariant Arg-95 on the cargo-binding loop is essential to cargo-receptor recognition In the crystal structures, the Arg-95 forms a hydrogen bond to the backbone oxygen of Ser-3 of the cargo-peptide. Interesting, R95M mutation broke the cargo-receptor interaction and resulted in mis-sorting of cargos in-vivo. 4. Cargo-receptor recognition between AtVSR1 and its native cargo follows the same rules derived from AtVSR1/aleurain interaction Using barley aleurain ssVSD as a model, we showed that (1) the swivel motion of the C-terminus of AtVSR1-PA, (2) Arg-95 of the cargo-binding loop, and (3) residues preceding the NPIR motif are essential to cargo-receptor recognition. We further showed that these rules also apply to cargo-receptor recognition between AtVSR1 and its native cargo from Arabidopsis (At4g16190). The work described above has been published in the Plant Cell journal (Luo et al., 26:3693-3708).

476212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476212.value: Supported by this GRF grant, we have delineated the rule of the PA domain of VSR protein in cargo-receptor recognition. In particular, we showed that the sequence preceding the NPIR motif of ssVSD is recognized by the PA domain. However, how the NPIR motif is recognized by VSR remains poorly understood. We showed that the swivel motion of the C-terminus of the PA domain, which presumably brings the Central domain of VSR towards the cargo-binding site, is essential to cargo-receptor interaction. This observation supports a model the PA and the Central domains of VSR work synergistically to recognize the full-length of ssVSD. As a result, we believe that structure determination of the full-length N-terminal domains of VSR will further address other domains of VSR contribute to the cargo-receptor recognition.

476212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476212.value: Unlike animal and yeast cells, plant cells sort soluble proteins to the vacuoles by recognizing the sequence-specific information known as vacuolar sorting determinant (VSD) on the cargo proteins, which is ‘read’ by vacuolar sorting receptor (VSR) through protein-protein interaction. In this project, we uncovered how VSR ‘read’ the VSD by determining the structures of the protease-associated (PA) domain of AtVSR1 and its complex with a cargo-peptide. Supported by mutagenesis and functional studies, we showed that the PA domain of VSR contains a highly conserved cargo-binding loop (with a consensus sequence of RGxCxF), which is responsible for recognizing three residues preceding the NPIR motif of VSD. Moreover, cargo binding induces a large conformational change that is essential to cargo-receptor recognition.

476512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
476512.value: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is one of the most common chronic liver diseases worldwide. In Asia, NAFLD affects 15-40% of the adult population. The disease may progress to cirrhosis and liver cancer. Recent data also suggest that NAFLD is the most important cause of cryptogenic cirrhosis. Due to its close relationship with metabolic syndrome and insulin resistance, NAFLD is strongly associated with coronary artery disease and malignancy. The current knowledge on the incidence of NAFLD is incomplete because of the limitations of assessment tools. Ultrasound examination is operator-dependent and can only detect moderate-to-severe liver steatosis. It also cannot be used to assess disease severity. Liver biopsy is limited by its invasiveness and cannot be performed in people without disease. Neither test is suitable for repeated use in longitudinal studies. Recently, new non-invasive tests have been developed for liver assessment. Proton-magnetic resonance spectroscopy is a reproducible and accurate test to quantify liver fat. Transient elastography by Fibroscan estimates liver fibrosis and diagnoses cirrhosis accurately in patients with different liver diseases. With these new tools, it is possible to diagnose NAFLD and assess disease severity in a large number of subjects repeatedly. Moreover, recent genome wide association studies have shed light on the genetic factors associated with NAFLD. In particular, gene polymorphism of patatin-like phospholipase 3 (PNPLA3) is strongly associated with liver fat. However, previous works have been confined to cross-sectional studies and the effect of the gene polymorphism has never been tested in a prospective cohort. From 2008 to 2010, our group performed magnetic resonance spectroscopy and transient elastography in 922 subjects in the general Hong Kong population. Fatty liver was identified in 264 (29%) subjects. In this follow-up project, we plan to repeat magnetic resonance spectroscopy and transient elastography in over 600 subjects without fatty liver at baseline. Dietary and genetic factors associated with incident NAFLD will be studied. The study will provide important longitudinal epidemiological data on NAFLD in Hong Kong. Moreover, the nutritional analysis will provide information regarding dietary components that are most strongly related to NAFLD development. 非酒精性脂肪性肝病是全球最常見的慢性肝臟疾病之一。在亞洲，脂肪肝影響15-40％的成年人口，並可能發展為肝硬化和肝癌。由於脂肪肝與代謝綜合症的密切關係，患者比正常人較易患上冠心病和癌症。 目前，因為評估工具的局限性，醫學界對脂肪肝的發病率並不清楚。超聲波檢查只能檢測出中度至重度肝細胞脂肪變性，它也不能評估疾病的嚴重程度。肝活檢是入侵性的檢查，不可以在沒有疾病的人身上進行。最近，新的肝臟測試讓我們可以安全地為普羅大眾檢查。質子磁共振波譜可精確地量化肝臟中的脂肪，肝纖維掃描則可準確地評估肝纖維化和診斷肝硬化。 此外，最近的全基因組關聯研究已經揭示出脂肪肝的相關遺傳因素。特別是， PNPLA3的基因多態性與肝臟脂肪息息相關。然而，以往的工作只限於橫斷面研究，我們目前尚未知道遺傳因素與新發脂肪肝的關係。 從2008到2010年，本中心以核磁共振光譜和肝纖維掃描進行了香港全民普查，其中29％被確診脂肪肝。在這個跟進項目，我們計劃在基最初600位無脂肪肝人士中重複檢查，以研究脂肪肝的發病率及其相關因素。這項研究將提供重要的流行病學數據。

476512.label: Realisation of objectives
476512.value: Objective 1: In this project, we performed follow-up proton-magnetic resonance spectroscopy, transient elastography and clinical assessment in 565 of 658 subjects who did not have fatty liver at baseline. The response rate was 85.9%. Incident fatty liver was detected in 78 (13.8%) subjects. After excluding 2 men who had significant alcohol consumption of 150 g and 200 g per week, the population incidence of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in 3-5 years was 13.5%, or an annual incidence rate of 3.4%. Among subjects with incident fatty liver, 62 (79.5%) had a second intrahepatic triglyceride content at 5.0-10.9%, while 16 (20.5%) had an intrahepatic triglyceride content of 11.0% or more, a level suggestive of moderate to severe hepatic steatosis. Objective 2: By univariate analysis, older age, male gender, increased body mass index, waist circumference and triglycerides, and decreased high density lipoprotein-cholesterol was associated with incident fatty liver. By multivariate analysis, older age, increased waist circumference and triglycerides, and decreased high density lipoprotein-cholesterol remained as independent factors associated with incident fatty liver. Importantly, 36 of 406 subjects who had body mass index below 23 kg/m2 also developed incident fatty liver during follow-up. Weight gain and rising triglycerides during follow-up were the main reasons for incident fatty liver in those patients. Objective 3: We successfully determined the patatin-like phospholipase domain-containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) rs738409 genotype in all subjects. The genotype distribution was: CC in 249 (44.1%) subjects, CG in 255 (45.1%) and GG in 61 (10.8%), and followed the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. The proportion of subjects harboring the at risk G allele was higher than that in Caucasian reports. There was a trend that subjects with incident fatty liver more likely had the GG genotype than those without (16.7% vs 9.9%; P=0.14).

476512.label: Major findings and research outcome
476512.value: Overall, 78 (13.8%) subjects developed incident fatty liver, among whom only 2 men had significant alcohol consumption of 150 g and 200 g per week. After excluding these 2 subjects, the population incidence of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) at 3-5 years was 13.5% (95% CI 10.6-16.3%; 3.4% per year). The mean intrahepatic triglyceride content (IHTG) at follow-up of the subjects with incident fatty liver was 8.9% (SD 5.3%; range 5.1-35.5%). 62 (79.5%) subjects had the second IHTG at 5.0-10.9%, while 16 (20.5%) had IHTG ≥11.0%, a level suggestive of moderate to severe hepatic steatosis on histology. All subjects with incident fatty liver had liver stiffness measurements fulfilling the reliability criteria. The mean (SD) liver stiffness at baseline and follow-up was 4.3 (1.5; range 2.3-12.1) kPa and 5.0 (4.0; range 3.6-37.4) kPa, respectively (P=0.059). Two (2.6%) subjects had liver stiffness ≥9.6 kPa, a level suggestive of advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, at follow-up, while the other subjects had low liver stiffness on both occasions. By univariate analysis, older age, male gender, smoking, high BMI, waist circumference, fasting glucose, hemoglobin A1c, triglycerides and reduced high density lipoprotein (HDL)-cholesterol at baseline and follow-up, and high baseline fasting insulin and HOMA-IR were associated with incident NAFLD. There was a trend that more subjects with incident fatty liver harbored the PNPLA3 rs738409 GG genotype (P=0.14). By multivariate analysis, metabolic syndrome was the most important factor associated with incident fatty liver. Incident fatty liver developed in 23 of 54 (42.6%) subjects with metabolic syndrome at baseline, compared to 55 of 511 (10.8%) subjects without metabolic syndrome (P<0.001). Similarly, incident fatty liver occurred in 26 of 49 (53.1%) subjects with metabolic syndrome at follow-up and 52 of 516 (10.1%) subjects without (P<0.001). Among the individual metabolic factors, central obesity and reduced HDL-cholesterol both at baseline and follow-up were consistently associated with incident fatty liver. The proportion of subjects with incident fatty liver increased with the number of components of metabolic syndrome in a dose-response manner. Incident fatty liver occurred in 7.1% of subjects without any component of metabolic syndrome at baseline and in over 50% of those with 4 or more components. Similarly, incident fatty liver occurred in 4.3% of subjects without any component of metabolic syndrome at follow-up and in over 50% of those with 3 or more components.

476512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476512.value: Because of the relatively short duration of follow-up, the current project focused on clinical, biochemical and radiological assessments. Clinical outcomes such as mortality, liver-related complications and cardiovascular complications would be more important but require a long duration of follow-up. At present, our team has been following all patients diagnosed with fatty liver at our clinic. We will also engage control subjects who did not have fatty liver from time to time to update their clinical status. In addition, we are currently leading a multicenter prospective study of 12 centers to study the clinical outcomes of Asian fatty liver patients. All patients will have transient elastography examination and clinical assessment at baseline, and clinical outcomes will be updated yearly. By doing so, we will be able to define the natural history of the disease.

476512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476512.value: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is currently the most common chronic liver disease worldwide and has become one of the leading causes of cirrhosis, liver failure and liver cancer. Because of the limitation of previous assessment tools, the incidence of NAFLD has been undefined. In this project supported by the General Research Fund, we for the first time used serial magnetic resonance imaging and transient elastography to study the incidence of NAFLD. During a follow-up of 3-5 years, 13.5% of 565 subjects were found to have new NAFLD (or 3-4% per year). While obesity is strongly associated with NAFLD, 9% of the lean patients in this project also developed incident fatty liver. Recent weight gain and changes in the metabolic profile were the main reasons for developing incident NAFLD. Our study provides important epidemiological data on this disease.

476912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
476912.value: Biofilm-producing bacteria have become a very serious problem because they are very difficult to eradicate by antibiotics, disinfectants, and host defenses. Therefore, novel and innovative approaches are urgently needed for eradicating biofilm-producing bacteria. Photodynamic inactivation (PDI) is a promising alternative for eradicating pathogenic bacteria. PDI utilizes light in combination with photosensitizer to produce reactive oxygen species (ROS) which kill the target cells. Growing evidences show that PDI can effectively eradicate a variety of microorganisms, including bacteria, fungi, and even biofilms. However, the poor penetration of light through biological tissues is the major limitation of the clinical application of PDI. Recent studies showed that ultrasound could also activate photosensitizers to produce ROS, a technique called sonodynamic therapy (SDT). As ultrasound has a unique advantage in tissue penetration and the ability to enhance the permeability of biological membranes, SDT will overcome the limitation to the clinical application of PDI and will be developed as a novel strategy for combating pathogenic bacteria. In order to develop SDT as a new therapeutic technique, ultrasound exposure systems have been set up in our laboratory and investigations of sonodynamic therapy have been carried out. We have observed that ultrasound can activate hypocrellin B, a natural pigment isolated from a traditional Chinese herb Hypocrella bambuase (竹紅菌), and sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B significantly kills cancer cells. Our preliminary data also showed that sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B enhanced intracellular ROS level in liver cancer cells. In our pilot study, sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B caused significant damage of E. coli. This gives us a clue that sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B may be an efficient way to eradicate biofilm-producing bacteria. Thus, in our project we plan to: (1) investigate sonodynamic antibacterial activity of hypocrellin B against Gram-positive and-negative biofilm-producing bacteria in planktonic condition; (2) explore the antibacterial mechanisms of sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B on Gram-positive and-negative biofilm-producing bacteria; (3) investigate sonodynamic antibacterial activity of hypocrellin B against bacteria in biofilms. Our aim is to develop a novel method to eradicate biofilm-producing bacteria in planktonic condition and biofilms using sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B from Chinese herb. We believe that the project will provide a novel strategy for combating biofilm-associated infections, and also shed light on the potential application of ultrasound and traditional Chinese herb in medicine and in the field of infection control. 生物膜產生菌很難被抗菌素、消毒劑及宿主的免疫機制所清除，現已成為一個非常棘手的問題，尋找清除生物膜產生菌的新型方法正迫在眉梢。基於光激發光敏藥物產生活性氧的光動力殺菌技術是一種具有應有前景的新方法。然而，光在生物組織中的穿透能力有限，限制了該技術的實際應用。最近發現超聲可以作為一種新型激發源，可有效活化光敏劑產生聲動力作用。由於超聲具有較好的組織穿透能力，發展聲動力殺菌和抗感染技術將更具應用前景。 為了開展聲動力技術，我們成功搭建了聲動力實驗平臺並開展系列聲動力治療方面的研究工作。目前我們已發現超聲可以有效激發一種中藥竹紅菌素產生活性氧物質，並可有效殺傷腫瘤細胞。最近我們的初步實驗發現竹紅菌素在超聲波的活化下可明顯殺傷大腸桿菌。這提示我們，竹紅菌素聲動力作用可能是一種消除生物膜產生菌的潛在方法。因此，我們擬定此項目並計畫開展以下幾個方面的工作：1. 探討竹紅菌素聲動力作用對懸浮狀態下革蘭氏陽性生物膜產生菌和革蘭氏陰性生物膜產生菌的殺傷作用；2. 探討竹紅菌素聲動力作用對革蘭氏陽性生物膜產生菌和革蘭氏陰性生物膜產生菌的殺傷機制；3. 探討竹紅菌素聲動力作用對生物膜上革蘭氏陽性生物膜產生菌和革蘭氏陰性生物膜產生菌的殺傷作用。目的在於研究發展中藥竹紅菌素介導的聲動力作用成為一種消除生物膜產生菌的新手段，為人類戰勝生物膜相關感染提供新的策略和新方法。

476912.label: Realisation of objectives
476912.value: Biofilm-producing bacterial strains Staphylococcus epidermidis (S. epidermidis) (ATCC 35984), Enterococcus faecalis (E. faecalis) (ATCC 29212) were used as Gram-positive biofilm-producing model bacteria, and Escherichia coli (E. coli) (NCTC 8196) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (P. aeruginosa) (PA 01)) as gram-negative biofilm-producing model bacteria, To examine the effect of sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B on biofilm-producing bacteria in planktonic condition, a single colony of bacterial strains was inoculated in Mueller Hinton broth (MHB) and incubated aerobically at 37°C overnight. Then, bacteria were mixed with fresh MHB followed by shaking at 200 rpm for 4 h for S. epidermidis, 3 h for E. faecalis, E. coli and P. aeruginosa, respectively. The cells were centrifuged at 4,500 rpm for 15 min and re-suspended in 0.85% steriled normal saline to a turbidity of about 1.0×107 CFU/ml. Bacteria were incubated with hypocrellin B (50 μM). After incubation, each sample was taken out at every 10-minute interval, and incubated for 17 h. The fluorescence of the supernatant was measured. The results showed that the uptake of hypcrellin B in S. epidermidis, E. faecalis, E. coli and P. aeruginosa was in time-dependent manner. The uptake of hypocrellin in four strains reached to the plateau at the 50-min incubation. To measure dark toxicity of hypocrellin B, bacteria were incubated with serial concentrations of hypocrellin B (0, 0.5, 5, 50, 500 μM) in the dark for 0 h, 1 h, 5 h and 24 h. Each sample was spread on the Mueller-Hinton agar (MHA) in 10-fold serial dilutions. After further incubation for 24 h colony forming unit (CFU) was counted. The results showed that hypocrellin B had no dark toxicity on P. aeruginosa and E. coli until hypocrellin B with the concentration of 500 μM was incubated for 24 h. However, hypocrellin B showed dark toxicity on E. faecalis when hypocrellin B (5 μM or 500 μM) was incubated for 24 h, and S. epidermidis when hypocrellin B (500 μM) was incubated for 1 h and 50 μM for 5 h. To measure colony forming units of bacteria after sonodynamic treatment, bacteria were sensitized with hypocrellin B at the concentrations of 2.5 μM, 5 μM, 10 μM, 20 μM, 40 μM for 50 min, respectively, followed by ultrasound exposure for 5 min at the intensity of 1.56 W/cm2. After sonodynamic treatment CFU was counted. The results showed that sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B had significantly antibacterial activity. The growth of S. epidermidis, E. faecalis, and E. coli were inhibited after ultrasound sonication in the presence of hypocrellin B ranging from 10 μM to 40 μM. A reduction of 4-6 log in CFU of S. epidermidis and E. faecalis was found after sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B, however, only 2 log reduction in CFU of E. coli was found after sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B. And the growth of P. aeruginosa decreased only after sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B at 20 μM and 40 μM. To measure metabolic activity, NAD/NADH-GloTM assay was conducted. The luminescence was recorded using a GloMax® 96 Microplate Luminometer. The results showed that sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B remarkably inhibited bacterial metabolic activity. To measure bacterial nucleic acid synthesis, DNA synthesis was estimated by chemiluminescent bromodeoxyuridine enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The newly synthesized RNA was detected using Click-iT® RNA Alexa Fluor® 488 HCS Assay. The newly synthesized protein was detected using Click-iT® Plus OPP Protein Synthesis Assay Kit. The results showed no significant change of DNA and RNA synthesis in sonodynamic treatment groups compared to control groups, however, significant inhibition of protein synthesis after sonodynamic treatment. A Gyrase DNA Supercoiling Assay Kit was used to measure DNA gyrase activity. The results showed that the activities of DNA gyrase were not affected by sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B. Membrane integrity and potential were evaluated using a flow cytometry with propidium iodide (PI) staining and DiOC2(3), respectively. The fluorescent signal of cells was analyzed under flow cytometry. The results showed that sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B had more significant effect on membrane integrity and potential than the controls. The production of ROS in bacteria was measured using flow cytometer with 2, 7-dichlorodihydrofluorecein diacetate (DCFH-DA) staining. Bacteria were pre-incubated with DCFH-DA in the dark at 37°C for 60 min and then rinsed twice. Bacteria were then subjected to sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B. The fluorescent intensity of DCF was measured using a flow cytometer. The results showed that a significant increase of ROS in the sonodynamic treatment group than other control groups. To examine the effect of sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B on biofilm-producing bacteria in biofilms, the overnight culture of biofilm-producing model bacteria was diluted with fresh tryptic soy broth at 1:100 and further incubated statically at 37°C for 24. Planktonic bacteria were removed carefully and the wells were then rinsed with normal saline twice. The biofilms were incubated with hypocrellin B (40 μM) for different time durations (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 min) in the dark. The biofilms lysed with sodium dodecylsulfate (SDS) overnight were centrifuged and the fluorescence of the supernatant was measured. The results showed that the uptake of hypocrellin B in biofilms increased with the prolonged incubation time. The formation of biofilms was assessed using crystal violet staining. Briefly, the biofilms after sonodynamic treatment were stained with crystal violet for 10 min. The biofilms were then washed carefully and air-dried for 15 min. The extent of biofilm formation was determined by measuring the absorbance of the stained adherent films at 570 nm. The results showed that sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B reduced more biofilm biomass compared with the control treatments. The viability of bacteria within the biofilms was determined by CFU counting. Biofilms after sonodynamic treatment were washed and then scraped thoroughly. CFU was counted as described above. The results showed that sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B slightly inhibited E. coli only after ultrasound exposure for 10 min. In comparison, 5 min ultrasound exposure together with hypocrellin B could reduce the growth of S. epidermidis. XTT cell proliferation assay kit was also used in the project. After sonodynamic treatment, the activated-XTT solution was added into the washed biofilms. After incubation for 2 h at 37°C, the absorbance of each well was measured at 475 nm. However, the obtained data from the XTT assay are difficult for comparative analysis possibly because hypocrellin B itself has absorption peak at 475 nm and the non-sticking biofilms induced sonodynamic treatment might be washed away. After sonodynamic treatment, biofilms were incubated with a mixture of SYTO 9 and PI in the dark for 15 min. Stained biofilms were observed by confocal laser scanning microscope (CLSM). The results showed that sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B had a more powerful capability of biofilm removal compared with the controls. Moreover, polysaccharide intercellular adhesion (PIA) in biofilms was observed in the project. Bacteria was incubated with wheat germ agglutinin-Oregon Green 488 conjugate and FM 4-64 for 15 min. Protein in biofilms was observed by staining with SYPRO Ruby protein gel stain containing SYTO 9 nucleic acid stain. Stained biofilms were examined under CLSM. The results showed that PIA was found in biofilms of S. epidermidis and E. coli, while protein was found in the biofilm matrix of P. aeruginosa.

476912.label: Major findings and research outcome
476912.value: The uptake of hypocrellin B in Staphylococcus epidermidis, Enterococcus faecalis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli was in time-dependent manner. The uptake of hypocrellin B in four strains reached to the plateau at the 50-min incubation. Dark toxicity test showed that hypocrellin B had no dark toxicity on Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli until hypocrellin B with the concentration of 500 μM was incubated for 24 h. However, hypocrellin B showed dark toxicity on Enterococcus faecalis while hypocrellin B (5 μM or 50 μM) was incubated for 24 h, and Staphylococcus epidermidis while hypocrellin B (500 μM) was incubated for 1 h and 50 μM for 5 h. Sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B increased the production of reactive oxygen species, inhibited bacterial metabolic activity and protein synthesis, and had significantly antibacterial activity. DNA fragmentation was not appeared, and DNA and RNA synthesis and DNA gyrase activity were not affected after sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B. Moreover, Sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B reduced more biofilm biomass and had a more powerful capability of biofilm removal compared with the controls. 2. The comparative studies showed that the response of gram-positive and gram-negative biofilm-producing bacteria to hypocrellin B itself and sonodynamic treatment of hypocrellin B are remarkably different. Hypocrellin B showed dark toxicity on gram-positive biofilm-producing bacterium Enterococcus faecalis while hypocrellin B with the concentration of 5 μM or 50 μM was incubated for 24 h, and Staphylococcus epidermidis while hypocrellin B with the concentration of 500 μM was incubated for 1 h and 50 μM for 5 h. However, hypocrellin B did not have significant dark toxicity on gram-negative biofilm-producing bacteria. In the meantime, we also found that gram-positive biofilm-producing bacteria were more sensitive to sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B than gram-positive biofilm-producing bacteria. 3. We also found that other sonosensitizers from natural products, e.g. curcumin, chlorin e6, etc., had significant killing effect on pathogenic bacteria.

476912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476912.value: The positive findings in the in-vitro study drive us to further investigate the in-vivo efficacy of sonodynamic antibacterial activity of hypocrellin B against biofilm-producing bacteria.

476912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476912.value: Biofilm-producing bacteria are important pathogens resulting in difficult-to-treat infections. The repeated use of antibiotics easily causes the resistance of bacteria. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop novel methods to treat biofilm-producing bacteria. In the present project, we found that sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B, an active compound from traditional Chinese herbal Hypocrella bambuase, had significant killing effect on gram-positive and-negative biofilm-producing bacteria. The findings indicate that sonodynamic action of hypocrellin B have a powerful potential in the treatment of biofilm-associated infections.

477412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
477412.value: 缺血再灌注/缺氧再復氧誘導的內皮功能障礙與一氧化氮和/或內皮源性超極化因子的功能受損有關。我們之前的研究顯示在缺氧再復氧狀態下,內皮中小電導鈣激活鉀通道的活性受抑是冠狀動脈內皮源性超極化因子功能受損的機制。我們也證明缺氧再復氧可抑制TRPC3通道而致內皮[Ca2+]i下降和內皮功能失調。雖然已知內皮[Ca2+]i升高是鈣激活鉀通道激活的先決條件且Ca2+通透性的TRP通道可與其他蛋白質形成信號複合物, 但內皮TRPC通道是否參與鈣激活鉀通道介導的內皮功能卻未見報導。此方面的研究在缺血再灌注/缺氧再復氧狀態下更屬空白。 本項目將研究TRPC3通道是否與鈣激活鉀通道相關聯參與內皮源性超極化因子的功能及缺氧再復氧狀態下TRPC3的抑制是否導致鈣激活鉀通道依賴性的內皮功能失調。項目擬採用多種方法于不同水平進行研究, 包括全細胞膜片鉗紀錄通道電流，細胞內Ca2+濃度測定; 微電極量度細胞膜電位變化及肌動描記器記錄冠狀動脈的鬆弛反應。此外，我們將採用分子生物學方法研究此兩種不同的通道是否于冠狀動脈內皮細胞中存在物理聯繫。 此項研究有助於進一步了解缺血缺氧狀態下內皮功能障礙的分子機制及推動發展新的防治方法。

477412.label: Realisation of objectives
477412.value: The project objectives have been fully realized as follows. Objective 1 aimed to test the hypothesis that TRPC3 channel may associate with KCa channels in coronary endothelial cells and this association plays an important role in the function of EDHF. We fulfilled this objective by successful completion of the three proposed tasks through myograph studies of endothelial KCa channel-related vasoactivity and electrophysiological studies of channel activity in particular direct KCa current recording using whole-cell voltage clamp. The essential role of TRPC3 in the activity/function of IKCa and SKCa channels was revealed by both pharmacological intervention and gene-silencing strategies. Further protein-protein interaction studies clarified whether the significance of TRPC3 to KCa activity/function in coronary circulation is attributed to physical interaction of TRPC3 and KCa channels in the endothelial cells. Objective 2 aimed to test the hypothesis that TRPC3 inhibition contributes to the inhibition of endothelial KCa and endothelial KCa-dependent EDHF function under H-R conditions in coronary arteries. To achieve the goal, we performed mechanical and electrophysiological studies to first compare the impact of TRPC3 inhibition on endothelial IKCa and SKCa channel activity and the channel-related vasodilatory function between normoxic and H-R conditions. We further examined the effect of TRPC3 activator on the activity and function of IKCa and SKCa channels in H-R exposed coronary artery preparations at both tissue and cellular levels. The tasks were satisfactorily completed. In summary, this project was successfully completed with research findings published in peer reviewed journals and reported in both local and international conferences.

477412.label: Major findings and research outcome
477412.value: 1. TRPC3 channels play a fundamental role in the regulation of KCa channel activity in endothelial cells of coronary arteries. 2. The functional association between TRPC3 and KCa channels in coronary endothelium does not involve physical interaction. 3. Inhibition of TRPC3 channels contributes to H-R-induced suppression of endothelial IKCa and SKCa channel activity. 4. Activation of TRPC3 protects IKCa and SKCa channels from H-R-induced inhibition thereby preserving EDHF-type vasorelaxation in coronary arteries. The results derived from this study were published in a number of peer-reviewed journals. In addition, the research findings from this project have been reported at recognized local research conferences as well as well-known international conferences including Experimental Biology and American Heart Association scientific session with abstracts printed in FASEB Journal and Circulation, etc.

477412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
477412.value: By adding new molecular insights into EDHF signaling and the mechanisms of I-R-induced endothelial dysfunction, this study may serve as a basis for future development of novel therapies for I-R injury with targeting TRPC3-KCa axis. Further identification of the upstream signals that control the response of TRPC3 to I-R and studies of the coupling of TRPC3-Ca2+ signal and KCa activation at the subcellular level shall help complete the picture of the role of TRPC3-KCa axis in I-R-related vascular pathology.

477412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
477412.value: TRP and KCa are two distinct ion channel families that are essential to vascular endothelial function. In addition to demonstrating the fundamental role of TRPC3 channels in the regulation of KCa channel activity in coronary endothelial cells, the present study for the first time revealed that TRPC3 inhibition is an important mechanism underlying the loss of activity and vasodilatory function of endothelial KCa channels in conditions involving H-R. Results derived from this study provided new mechanistic insights into coronary dysfunction associated with I-R injury. Furthermore, the findings of protection against H-R conferred by TRPC3 channel modulators on the activity and function of endothelial KCa channels may shed light on potential new therapeutic targets for coronary dysfunction in ischemic / hypoxic states.

477612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
477612.value: Identification and triage patients at risk for poor warfarin control, namely those patients with high/low warfarin sensitivity, to NOAC therapy is a novel application of warfarin pharmacogenetics. The present project translated this novel application of warfarin genotype data for patients with atrial fibrillation into the long-term clinical and economic outcomes. The findings demonstrated that genotype-guided selection of anticoagulants for patients with atrial fibrillation to be the option with preferred outcomes. As genotyping assay becomes more affordable and accessible, it is anticipated that clinicians will be seeing patients who have their genotype results readily available. The urging needs in research are to provide evidence on risk and benefit of applying warfarin pharmacogenetics in all warfarin indications. A GRF application (2015-2016) is submitted, aiming to translate this novel application of pharmacogenetics into clinical practice for patients with any indication of oral anticoagulant therapy. We will design a decision-analytic model of hypothetical patients to simulate life-long clinical and economic impact of pharmacogenetic-guided selection of oral anticoagulants versus other anticoagulation options. A risk-benefit framework will be developed based upon the analytic model findings and inputs from stakeholders of anticoagulation care and experts of genomics generated in a focused discussion.

477612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
477612.value: Warfarin is the most commonly prescribed agent for prevention of stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation. Unfortunately, the anticoagulation control of most patients is inadequate. Patients with certain genes are more sensitive to warfarin effect, putting these patients at higher risk for bleeding. Novel oral anticoagulants (NOACs) recently became available to the market. Advantage of NOACs over warfarin is the drug effect does not affect by the warfarin-sensitive gene. Disadvantages of NOACs are high level of patient compliance required, lack of antidote, and much higher drug cost comparing to warfarin. The current dilemma for healthcare providers are: To use warfarin or to use NOAC? Pharmacogenetic-guided selection of oral anticoagulants is an innovative approach to address the unmet need of oral anticoagulation therapy management. The findings of present project showed it is cost-effective to use genomic testing to identify atrial fibrillation patients with high or low warfarin sensitivity and triage them to receive NOACs, whereas patients with normal warfarin sensitivity could receive warfarin therapy. These results provide evidence to assist doctors in personalized selection of an anticoagulant agent with the best chance of achieving highest quality of life at an acceptable cost for patients with atrial fibrillation.

477912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
477912.value: The proper secretion of various growth factors and the extracellular matrix proteins, and the correct localization of membrane-bound receptors and channel proteins all ensure the normal developmental outcomes of a multicellular organism. In eukaryotic cells, the secretion and transport of these proteins are carried out by small transport vesicles, the trafficking of which starts at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), passes through the Golgi apparatus, and arrives at the plasma membrane. A protein complex called TRAPP (Transport protein particle) is essential for tethering of ER-derived COPII vesicles. Mutations in subunits of the TRAPP complex have been found in two genetic diseases X-linked spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia tarda (SEDT) and intellectual disability with microcephaly. Patients with SEDT suffer from early onset of osteoarthrosis and defects in skeletal development. The disease-causing gene is confirmed to be the TRAPP subunit TRAPPC2/Sedlin/Trs20. Intellectual disability with postnatal microcephaly can be caused by genetic lesion in another TRAPP subunit, TRAPPC9/NIBP/Trs120. How mutations in TRAPPC2 and TRAPPC9 affect the function of TRAPP complex as a vesicle tether has not been fully understood. We have been studying the biochemical properties of TRAPP complex in mammalian cells. We hypothesize that the structure of TRAPP must be compromised in patients suffering from SEDT and TRAPPC9-associated intellectual disability, leading to impairment in vesicle secretion. Our previous studies have shown that TRAPPC2 and TRAPPC9 have intimate relationship in mammalian TRAPP complex. The disease-causing mutants of TRAPPC9 fail to interact with other TRAPP subunits including TRAPPC2. Similarly, a disease-causing, missense mutation of TRAPPC2, D47Y, shows drastic reduction of TRAPPC9 binding. Further, mammalian TRAPPII complex can no longer form in cells isolated from a patient with TRAPPC9-associated intellectual disability. Using biochemical and cell biological techniques that are well-established in our labs, as well as the state-of-the-art BIAcore® surface plasmon resonance technique, we want to elucidate the biochemical consequences of disease-causing mutations found in SEDT and TRAPPC9-associated intellectual disability with postnatal microcephaly in terms of the structure and function of the TRAPP complex as a vesicle tether. The outcomes of these research efforts will provide etiology at the biochemical level to the genetic diseases SEDT and intellectual disability with microcephaly. Second, our research efforts will deepen the understanding of the structure and function of mammalian TRAPP complex, and thus the fundamental process of vesicle trafficking. 各種生長因子和細胞外基質蛋白和膜結合受體和通道蛋白的正常分泌與正確定位，是確保多細胞生物正常發育的重要因素。在真核細胞中，這些蛋白的分泌和運輸是通過運輸小泡，始於內質網（ER），經過高爾基體，到達細胞膜。一個蛋白複合物稱為TRAPP （運輸蛋白顆粒）是ER-衍生COPII泡的拴係因子。 已發現TRAPP的亞基突變會導至X染色體X-linked spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia tarda（SEDT）的和智力殘疾的 小頭畸形。SEDT患者有骨關節病和骨骼發育缺陷。致病基因被確認是TRAPP亞基TRAPPC2/Sedlin/Trs20的。而TRAPPC9/NIBP/Trs120的突變可引起智力殘疾。TRAPPC2和TRAPPC9的突變如何影響TRAPP絡合物作為囊泡拴係因子的功能還沒有得到充分的理解。 我們一直在哺乳細胞中研究TRAPP複合體的生化特性。我們假設，在SEDT和TRAPPC9相關的智力殘疾患者的細胞中, TRAPP的結構受到影響，導致囊泡分泌能力的下降。我們以往的研究表明，TRAPPC2和TRAPPC9在 TRAPP複合體有著密切的關係。TRAPPC9的突變體不能與TRAPP亞基包括TRAPPC2結合。同樣地，TRAPPC2的D47Y突變導至與TRAPPC9的互作下降。此外，TRAPPC9相關的智力殘疾患者中,TRAPPII複合體不能形成。 利用我們實驗室已建立的生物化學和細胞生物學技術，及最先進的Biacore®表面等離子體共振技術，我們希望明白SEDT和TRAPPC9相關智力的殘疾的致病突變對於TRAPP複合體的結構和功能上帶來後果。 這些研究成果將在生化水平上为遺傳疾病SEDT的小頭畸形和智力殘疾的病因提供解释，並加深了解哺乳TRAPP複合體的結構和功能哺，和囊泡運輸的基本過程。

477912.label: Realisation of objectives
477912.value: All objectives have been completed. Objectives 1 was completed in line with our expectation although variations in the biochemical properties of the TRAPP complexes among the cell lines investigated were observed. Objective 2 was completed and generated an amount of data much more than we anticipated. The major findings in this aim are 1. TRAPPII regulates centrosome copy number, probably via its interaction with p150Glued. 2. TRAPPII regulates lipid droplet biogenesis or homeostasis via its recruitment of Rab18 onto lipid droplet surface. The first discovery was straight forward but the second discovey was not. Initially we were concerned that the TRAPPC9 mutant skin fibroblasts isolated from human individual with TRAPPC9 mutation did not present much defect in the early secretory pathway. Such lack of phenotype could be caused by reversion of the TRAPPC9 mutation to wildtype sequence due to selective pressure. Therefore, we initiated a Crispr-Cas9 mediated deletion of TRAPPII specific genes as alternative method of studying TRAPPII function in the secretory pathway in mammalian cells. Again, a lack of significant defect in the secretory pathway was observed in the TRAPPII cells. We eventually found that the real function of TRAPPII was regulating the homeostasis/biogenesis of lipid droplets via Rab18. Objectvie 3 was completed within our expectation Objective 4 was revised to study whether the ASH domains found on various TRAPP subunits were indeed targeted to the centrosome by interactions with p150Glued. This hypothesis was proven not as simple as we thought. Some of the ASH domains from TRAPPII specific subunits seemed to bind to p150Glued. However, Those from TRAPPIII specific subunits did not bind to p150Glued, and therefore, ASH domains could be targeted to the centrosome by different mechanisms.

478312.label: Major findings and research outcome
478312.value: Major findings: During previous research period, we have found that the miR-214 level was efficiently decreased in a dose-dependent manner by the AntagomiR-214 and reached the level lower than 10% of the baseline at a dosage of 4 mg/kg at least in the aged osteoporotic rats. The effective duration for miR-214 at a level lower than 50% of the baseline lasted for 7 days in the osteoporotic rats after the single dosing. The miR-214 level was continuously lowered until 28 days and continuously maintained later at the level lower than 10% of the baseline by the 5 pulsed dosing of the AntagomiR-214 at an interval of 7 days and at a dosage of 4 mg/kg in the osteoporotic rats (Please refer to 2013 annual report). We also found that therapeutic inhibition of miR-214 by (Asp-Ser-Ser)6-liposome encapsulating antagomiR-214 in osteogenic cells could promote bone formation in aged osteoporotic rat model (Please refer to 2014 annual report) . We have found that therapeutic inhibition of miR-214 by (Asp-Ser-Ser)6-liposome encapsulating antagomiR-214 in osteogenic cells could improve bone mechanical properties in aged ovariectomized rats. Furthermore, therapeutic inhibition of miR-214 by (Asp-Ser-Ser)6-liposome encapsulating antagomiR-214 in osteogenic cells didn’t induce any hepatic / renal toxicity (Please refer to 2015 annual report). Research outcomes: During our whole project, we have published three peer reviewed papers and three conference abstracts. For detailed information, please refer to Part C.

478312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
478312.value: In this study, therapeutic inhibition of miR-214 by antagomiR-214 delivered by the (DSS)6-liposome in osteoblasts could promote bone formation to reverse severe postmenopausal bone loss, which would provide a novel bone anabolic treatment strategy to reverse sever postmenopausal osteoporosis and subsequently reducing fracture risk. In further study, we will evaluate the anabolic effects of antagomiR-214 delivered by the (DSS)6-liposome on other disease models with impaired bone formation, including glucocorticoid–induced osteoporosis, inflammation-induced osteoporosis, aged fracture and steroid-associated osteonecrosis.

478312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
478312.value: This nature of the project is a translational research. Based on the experimental data, it has been confirmed that therapeutic inhibition of miR-214 in osteoblastst could promote bone formation in aged ovariectomized rats. The significance and value of the research is to provide a novel bone anabolic treatment strategy to reverse sever postmenopausal osteoporosis, thereby reducing fracture risk.

478812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
478812.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESC) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) have become valuable tools for studying the early embryonic development, for modeling human diseases, and for developing regenerative medicine. However, the application is hindered due to the fact that the current human ESCs and iPSCs have limited developmental potential and survive poorly upon single-cell dissociation. It has been found that the established human ESCs and iPSCs resemble mouse epiblast stem cells (EpiSC) at primed pluripotent state, but differ from mouse ESCs at naive pluripotent state. Although some partial naive human iPSCs have been established, the full naive human iPSCs with favorable features for research and clinical applications are still not available. Moreover, the molecular mechanisms underlying the distinct states of pluripotency remain largely unknown. Hence intense effort needs to be made to investigate the molecular basis and to identify an appropriate approach for generating full naive human iPSCs. The PI has identified some novel reprogramming factors in previous studies and generated two lines of partial naive human iPSCs in her own laboratory recently. The present proposal is based on these works, and takes further steps to study the naive pluripotency in human cells. The aim of this project is to conduct research into the molecular basis that regulates the partial naive human iPSCs, and to generate full naive human iPSCs. We will achieve the aim through the following works: (1) to analyze the transcriptional profile and the core protein network in our partial naive human iPSCs using microarray and proteomics analysis, respectively. By doing this, we expect to shortlist some important pluripotency genes that are absent in the partial naive human iPSCs; (2) to analyze the candidate genes and to identify those that may further reprogram the partial naive cells; and (3) to generate full naive human iPSCs based on the data obtained in above mentioned work, and to carry out thorough characterization of these cells. This work will produce valuable data and allow insightful understanding of the pluripotent cell fate control, thus leading us to a new chapter in cell reprogramming technology. Generation of full naive human iPSCs will facilitate functional studies of human disease-related genes, the creation of human cell-based disease models, and the development of appropriate combined gene and cell therapies. This will promote the application of human iPSCs in both research and clinical settings, which is our long-term goal. 摘要： 胚胎干細胞（Embryonic stem cells，ESC）及誘導性多能干細胞（induced pluripotent stem cells，iPSC）都具有在體外無限增生及分化為各類體細胞的潛能；這對研究人類早期胚胎細胞的分化，以病人細胞進行特定病理過程的體外模擬，以及發展再生醫學都具有極其重要的價值。但是，現有的人類多能干細胞（包括ESC和iPSC）都極其脆弱，不能有效地在單細胞狀態下存活，凍存后死亡率高過90%，這嚴重影響了對其應用的進一步推廣。而小鼠多能干細胞則顯著不同，具有更優越的特性，適於體外操作極保存。研究表明，現有人類多能干細胞與分離於著床后胚胎的小鼠上胚層干細胞（epiblast stem cells，EpiSC）具有許多相似性，可能屬於已經初步分化的多能干細胞，而不再具有初始狀態的多能性。這一認知推動了相關的探索。目前，已有研究報導了不完全人類初始多能干細胞（partial naive human iPSC）的獲得, 但是還未能建立真正的初始狀態的人類誘導性多能干細胞（full naive human iPSC），有關初始多能性的分子機理研究也存在著大片空白。目前，亟需相關研究來進一步推動iPSC理論和技術的發展。 申請者從事iPSC研究多年， 所帶領的實驗室已誘導建立了不完全初始狀態的人類誘導性多能干細胞。在此基礎上，本課題擬對不完全初始狀態的人類多能干細胞的分子特性進行分析，並與現有的人類多能干細胞進行比較，旨在探索初始多能性的分子調控基礎，尋找方法建立真正的初始狀態的人類誘導性多能干細胞。本課題的研究內容包括（1）對已有的不完全初始狀態iPSC進行基因表達及蛋白組學分析，與現有的人類胚胎干細胞進行比較，先擇不完全初始狀態iPSC所缺失的重要基因；（2）對所選基因進行分析，鑒定可以進一步將不完全初始iPSC進行重編程的因子；（3）建立真正的初始狀態的人類iPSC，並對所獲得的細胞進行全面鑒定和分析。 本課題將對人類細胞的各種多能性進行深入的分析研究，將會揭示調控人類細胞多能性的分子基礎，並建立方法誘導真正的人類初始iPSC。這將對大力推動人類iPSC技術的發展，並為將其有效地應用於各項研究及臨床提供可能。

478812.label: Realisation of objectives
478812.value: Summary Accumulating evidence have demonstrated that pluripotency in embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) could be maintained in two distinct states, “naive” pluripotency and “primed” pluripotency. Conventional mouse ESCs represent the “naive” pluripotent state; whereas human ESCs exhibit profound difference from mouse ESCs and represent the primed pluripotency. The primed pluripotency features of human ESCs and current iPSCs have made them very difficult to survive through single cell dissociation, thus largely hindering genetic manipulation and large scale expansion in subsequent applications. Hence, much effort has been made to obtain human ESCs and iPSCs in a “naïve” pluripotency state. In order to gain further insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying the distinct states of pluripotency, in this project, we proposed to perform multi-displinery investigation using various advanced tools and technologies. With intensive effort, we have realized proposed objectives, and obtained new insights with the discovery and achievement made along the study. Research activities: 5.3.1. Integrative bioinformatics analysis of distinct pluripotency states Long non-coding RNAs (lincRNAs) are emerging as important regulators of pluripotency property, yet many of them remain unidentified. We ab initio reconstructed the RNA-seq data of mouse ESCs and EpiSCs available from public databases, and present a large discovery of novel lincRNAs, identified from Ab initio assembly of 15 high-depth transcriptome datasets obtained in mouse ESC and EpiSCs. Among the 5995 candidate lincRNAs, 75.7% were present in ESC single-cell transcriptome data and showed correlation with known coding and non-coding genes, forming 43 co-expression modules. Distinct functional potentials uncovered in individual co-expression modules are highly consistent with their epigenetic features and binding patterns by key pluripotency-factors. Interestingly, two groups of novel lincRNAs are found to be closely associated with naïve pluripotency or totipotency, and single-cell transcriptome analysis in preimplantation mouse embryos has verified the specific enrichment of totipotency-lincRNAs at 2-cell stage (Wang et al. ready to submit). 5.3.2 Identification of transcription modules specifically associated with naïve pluripotency and totipotency states. We noted that a significant sub-population of novel lincRNAs are assigned in the module named ES.M3, which are lowly expressed in 2i or serum culture conditions and shows the specific enrichment of totipotency-lincRNAs at 2-cell stage. Consistently, totipotent marker genes were found in this module, such as Zfp352, Abcb5, Tcstv1, Tcstv3, and Cml2. We further examined previously published single cell RNA-seq data of in vivo early embryo development. Indeed, genes and novel lncRNAs in this module showed remarkably specific expressions in 2-cell stages. This feature of ES.M3 is unique among all the co-expression modules, and suggests its strong association with totipotency (Wang et al. ready to submit). In a summary, our study demonstrates a comprehensive bioinformatics pipeline and provides wealthy information for further elucidation of functions and mechanisms of lincRNAs in controlling mammalian pluripotency. 5.3.3. Direct activation of human and mouse Oct4 genes using engineered TALE and Cas9 transcription factors In order to further reprogram our partial naïve human iPSCs and achieve full activation of the endogenous pluripotency genes OCT4 SOX2 and NANOG, we explored the potential of newly emerged technology on engineered TALE and Cas9 transcription activators. The newly developed TALE and CRISPR/Cas9 transcription factors (TF) offered a powerful and precise approach for modulating gene expression. We systematically investigated the potential of these new tools in activating the stringently silenced pluripotency gene Oct4 (Pou5f1) in mouse and human somatic cells. First, with a number of TALEs and sgRNAs targeting various regions in the mouse and human Oct4 promoters, we found that the most efficient TALE-VP64s bound around −120 to −80 bp, while highly effective sgRNAs targeted −147 to −89 bp upstream of the transcription start sites (TSS) to induce high activity of luciferase reporters (Hu et al. Nuclear Acids Research 2014). In addition, we observed significant transcriptional synergy when multiple TFs were applied simultaneously. Although individual TFs exhibited marginal activity to up-regulate endogenous gene expression, optimized combinations of TALE-VP64s could enhance endogenous Oct4 transcription up to 30-fold in mouse NIH3T3 cells and 20-fold in human HEK293T cells. More importantly, the enhancement of OCT4 transcription ultimately generated OCT4 proteins. Furthermore, examination of different epigenetic modifiers showed that histone acetyltransferase p300 could enhance both TALE-VP64 and sgRNA/dCas9-VP64 induced transcription of endogenous OCT4. 5.3.4 To explore the potential of TALE-epigenetic modifiers in activating endogenous Oct4 and promoting reprogramming Histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac) and histone H3 lysine 4 trimethylation (H3K4me3) are known epigenetic modifications for maintaining the Oct4 locus in an active or permissive status in pluripotent cells; whereas histone H3 lysine 9 and lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K9me3 and H3K27me3) mediate epigenetic repression and are associated with Oct4 gene silencing in somatic cells. In order to activate the endogenous Oct4 gene in somatic cells, which is in a silence status, we introduced epigenetic modification enzymes fused TALE specifically targeting Oct4 promoter. Totally 11 genes encoding epigenetic modification enzymes have been cloned from mouse and fused to most efficient TALE targeting mouse Oct4 promoter. They were transfected into NIH3T3 cells (mouse fibroblast cell line), and the level of endogenous Oct4 transcription was measured using RT-PCR. From these TALE1-epigenetic modifiers fusion proteins, Tdg2, Kdm3 and Kdm4c fused TALE1 significantly promoted the activation of endogenous Oct4 genes in NIH3T3 cells (Hu et al. Nuclear Acids Research 2014). 5.3.5. Analysis of culture condition to maintain the naïve state of pluripotency in human ESCs and iPSCs. In our previous studies, we generated partial naïve human iPSCs using ESC culture medium supplemented with LIF, MEK inhibitor and GSK3β inhibitor, which were known to maintain mouse ESCs at a naïve pluripotency state and have been used for generating partial naïve human iPSCs in other studies. Recent studies further identified other growth factors and signaling inhibitors that could convert human ESC/iPSCs from their normal primed state into a more robust naïve state. The new naïve cells highly resembled mouse ESCs in regard of their gene expression, dependence on LIF as well as good survival upon single-cell dissociation. Based on our previous studies as well as these new findings, we investigated the potential of various combinations of growth factors, cytokines and chemicals, in promoting the survival of human ESCs upon single cell dissociation. We found that three components were essential and sufficient to maintain robust colonization of human ESCs from single cells, whereas addition of another component could maintain the colonies in dome-shaped morphology, resembling the naïve pluripotency state (Chan et al, Stem Cells. 2013, and Hu et al, unpublished). 5.3.6 Analysis of naïve human iPSCs/hESC maintained in different conditions Furthermore, we have analyzed gene expression profiles in naïve vs primed human ESC/iPSCs, published in recent studies by four different groups. Genes enriched in naïve human ESCs from each study are highlighted and compared among all the four studies. We have selected 20 genes for cloning into lentiviral vector. These factors were packaged into viruses, and combined with Yamanaka’s reprogramming factors to induce the reprogramming of human fibroblasts or the partial naïve iPSCs. New factors that can promote reprogramming induction and maintenances of naïve state hESC/iPSCs will be selected for further characterization (Wang et al. unpublished).

478812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
478812.value: Proposal for GRF 2018/19 (PI), “Identification of lincRNAs as novel regulators in totipotent cells through gene co-expression analysis”. Distinct from pluripotency that refers to the cellular properties of inner cell mass in blastocyst stage, totipotency refers to the property in 2-cell embryos, which can support broad differentiation to both embryonic and extra embryonic lineages. Based on our recent finding of the totipotency-associated gene module, we propose to further study the function of totipotency-related lincRNAs or coding genes using both in vivo and in vitro models, aiming to verify their functions and gain insights into totipotency mechanisms. Joint application for TRS 2018/19 (Co-PI) “Expanded Potential Stem Cells: From genesis to disease models”. In 2017, Pentao Liu’s group has reported expanded potential stem cells (EPSC) that can contribute both to the embryo proper and to the trophectoderm lineages in a chimaera assay. We joined Prof Liu in his recent application for the TRS grant, to establish EPSCs from other mammalian species and to investigate the molecular mechanisms of the expanded potential in vitro and totipotency in vivo, to explore applications of EPSCs in basic stem cell and development biology research.

478812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
478812.value: Pluripotency in embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) could be maintained in two distinct states, “naive” pluripotency and “primed” pluripotency. While conventional mouse ESCs represent the “naive” pluripotent state; human ESCs exhibit profound difference from mouse ESCs and represent the primed pluripotency. The primed pluripotency features of human ESCs and current iPSCs have made them very difficult to survive through single cell dissociation, thus largely hindering genetic manipulation and large scale expansion in subsequent applications. This project has made effort to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying distinct states of pluripotency, to gain further insights into regulatory network controlling human naïve pluripotency. With the recent studies showing various distinct pluripotency states, we have performed integrative profiling analysis at both pooled culture and single cell level. Our results identified novel gene modules associated with naïve pluripotency or even totipotency. Furthermore, we employed newly emerged molecular tools TALE and CRISPR/Cas9 transcription factors (TF) to activate pluripotency gene Oct4 and promote reprogramming. We identified optimal biding regions to induce high transcription and observed significant transcriptional synergy between multiple TFs. These results unraveled new mechanistic insights into pluripotency regulation and they are valuable to promote the generation of truly naïve hiPSCs.

479012.label: Project Title(Chinese)
479012.value: Hedgehog 信号通路與骨癌的機制研究

479012.label: Project Objectives
479012.value: To identify and establish an OSA mouse model by upregulating Hh signaling in mature p53 deficient osteoblasts. Our working hypothesis, based upon strong preliminary data, is that with partial removal of p53 tumor suppression, excessive Hh signaling leads to the development of OSA at a high frequency. To determine the cellular and molecular mechanisms of OSA development and characterize the non-cell autonomous roles of Hh activation in mesenchymal progenitor cell proliferation, differentiation and inflammatory responses. Our working hypothesis is that Hh signaling is a risk factor of OSA and that it cross talks with a network of signaling pathways, such as p53 signaling, that are commonly implicated in cancer development, to enhance the growth and metastasis of OSA. We will investigate the roles of Hh signaling and its interaction with those pathways and understand the cancer stem cell properties and the relationship between inflammation and tumor development. To establish rescue methods that effectively inhibit the growth and progression of OSA. Our working hypothesis is that inhibition of Hh signaling and its downstream networks will inhibit OSA growth and metastasis. We will use our Ptchc/+;p53+/-;HOC-Cre OSA mouse mutant models and direct allograft transplantation models to test the effectiveness of tumor arrest by Hh inhibitors, shRNA for identified proto-oncogenes and signaling inhibitors for inflammation. Under the first aim, a potential OSA mouse model has been identified for the in vivo investigation of the cause of OSA. Under the second aim, OSA tumors is confirmed with high level of Hh signaling. Yap and Taz, which are proto-oncogenes and Hippo effectors, have been identified to be upregulated by Hh signaling in the OSA models. Nanog, a stem cell marker is upregulated in OSA. An in vivo imaging system has been successfully set up to monitor the progress for tumor metastasis. The OSA model is confirmed with inflammation. Under the third aim, Hh inhibitor GDC-0449 has been validated to inhibit Hh signaling in our OSA tumor cells and lentiviruses for shRNAs have been generated. Overall, our approach is innovative because it is a signaling base approach to target the source of OSA cancer cells, which is in strong contrast to the current treatments, which are relatively non-specific.

479012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
479012.value: The aim of this project is to determine the signaling pathways that are being deregulated in osteosarcoma and thereby aid the development of improved treatments for this condition. Osteosarcoma (OSA) is the most common pediatric bone cancer. The prognosis for patients with metastatic OSA is poor, with only 20% to 30% survival rate in a 5-year event. Currently, limb salvage and amputation, together with chemotherapy, have been widely used for treating human patients. In addition, little is known about the underlying cause of OSA. Lack of such knowledge is an important problem, because, without it, acquiring the ability to develop a specific and efficacious therapeutic approach is very difficult. There is a fundamental gap in understanding the genetic cause and the pathogenesis of OSA that results in a relatively non-specific treatment of human patients. Continued existence of this gap represents an important problem because a more effective treatment that specifically targets the cancer cells cannot be developed. Our long-term goal is to develop a specific and less invasive method for the treatment of OSA by better understanding the underlying genetic and molecular mechanisms. The central hypothesis in this application is that excessive Hedghog (Hh) signaling leads to the development of OSA, and that removal of a copy of tumor suppressor gene p53 significantly accelerates the onset of OSA. The rationale for the proposed research is that, by understanding the signaling pathways that are implicated in the initiation of OSA, it has the potential to aid development of better therapies. The hypothesis will be tested by pursuing the following specific aims: (1) To identify and establish an OSA mouse model by upregulating Hh signaling in mature p53 deficient osteoblasts. (2) To determine the cellular and molecular mechanisms of OSA development and characterize the non-cell autonomous role of Hh activation in mesenchymal progenitor cell proliferation, differentiation and inflammatory responses. (3) To establish rescue methods that effectively inhibit the growth and progression of OSA. The proposed research is significant because it is expected to vertically advance and expand the understanding of the initiation and metastasis of OSA. Such knowledge has the potential to establish a foundation for clinical trials in humans with the ultimate goal of developing a new therapeutic approach, based on the signaling pathways identified, which will be more specific and efficacious than current methods. This highly specific approach is of particular importance in the development of personalized medicine. 本项目的研究目标是通过研究骨肉瘤（OSA）中调控异常的信号通路，为骨肉瘤的临床治疗提供帮助。骨肉瘤是最常见的儿童骨肿瘤，转移性的OSA病人预后较差，五年生存率仅为20%-30%。目前，对骨肉瘤的发病原因了解甚少，骨肉瘤病人的治疗仍广泛采用保肢或截肢手术联合化疗的方法。此外，由于OSA发病机制相关知识的欠缺，目前尚未研究出有效的特异性的治疗方法。而且遗传因素和OSA发病机制之间的关系仍不明确，目前对患者仍采用的是非个体化治疗。如果仍不能探明二者之间的关系，探究更有效且特异的肿瘤治疗靶点将会受到影响。我们的长远目标是通过更好的揭示和阐明OSA的遗传和分子机制，促进开发一种特异且微创的临床治疗方法。 本课题的主要假设是过多的Hedghog （Hh）信号导致OSA的发生，并且，敲除肿瘤抑制基因p53的一个拷贝能够明显促进OSA的发病。该研究计划通过揭示参与OSA发病过程中的分子信号通路，为研究OSA更好的治疗方法提供帮助。 实验假说将通过实现以下目标进行验证： （1） 通过在p53缺陷的成骨细胞中上调Hh信号来建立OSA小鼠模型。 （2） 证明OSA发生过程中的细胞和分子机制，并鉴定Hh信号的激活在间充质祖细胞的增殖、分化和炎症反应中的非细胞自主作用。 （3） 建立挽救实验以有效的抑制OSA的生长和进展。 本研究计划的重要意义在于能够增强和加深对OSA发生和转移的理解。通过对信号通路及分子机制的阐明，开发比目前更为有效且特异的新的治疗方法，这些新的知识将成为临床实验及治疗的基础。由此而生的新的治疗方法在发展个体化医学中具有非常重要的作用。

479512.label: Project Objectives
479512.value: To derive female Blimp1-GFP ES cells and induce the cells into EpiLC and then PGCLC. To characterize the PGCLCs. The PGCLCs will be purified by fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) based on Blimp1-GFP and live-cell fluorescence immunostain of PGC surface markers. The PGCLCs and EpiLCs will be characterized by the cell specific markers at both mRNA level and protein level. Typical PGC epigenetic markers will be examined by immunostain and western blot. The function of the PGCLCs will be characterized by transplanting them into ovaries and checking their contribution to the oocytes and the resulting offspring. To use high germ-line competent iPS cells to generate PGCLC female germ cells, and to build a scheme to generate germ lineage cells from fibroblasts in vitro.

479512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
479512.value: 提高哺乳動物的生殖力是治療人類不孕不育，提高經濟動物育種和拯救瀕臨滅絕的關鍵。而原生殖細胞的形成是哺乳動物獲得生殖力的根本。通過雄性原生殖細胞發育過程，Saitou實驗室成功地在體外誘導了由小鼠囊胚內細胞團分離的胚胎幹細胞發育成類似上胚層細胞，進而發育成類似雄性原生殖細胞。令人興奮的是這些誘導的原生殖細胞能夠發育成精子並繁育出正常的下一代。因為Saitou實驗室的工作主要集中在雄性細胞系統， 因此我們建議在此項目中建立從雌性Blimp1-GFP胚胎幹細胞到類似原生殖細胞的誘導系統，通過基因芯片系統比較誘導原生殖細胞和從小鼠分離的原生殖細胞在轉錄組上的異同，同時進行體內移植檢測誘導原生殖細胞發育成為卵和繁育下一代的能力。該研究將會為建立體外培育雌性生殖細胞提供新的思路和依據。

479512.label: Realisation of objectives
479512.value: Thanks to the support of RGC ECS grant, we set to establish the in vitro system to induce germ lineage cells from pluripotent stem cells. According to the proposal, we first purchased two pairs of Blimp1-cre mice and two pairs of Gt(ROASA)26-GFP reporter mice from the Jackson laboratory. After obtained the stable stock of the mice, we crossed Blimp1-cre mice and Gt(ROASA)26-GFP reporter and derived multiple embryonic stem cells. We obtained 3 Blimp-1-Cre/Gt(ROSA)26-GFP female ES cells, 5 Gt(ROSA)26-GFP female ES cells by genome typing. We have confirmed the pluripotency of these ES cells by checking the expression key pluripotent factors, the teratoma assay and histology examination of three germ layers. However, unexpected from previous literature report that Blimp1 is a specific marker of primordial germ cells (PGCs), we found that Blimp1 is also highly expressed in ES cells. This leads to early activation of Blimp1 promoter. Therefore, GFP is early expressed at ES cell stage instead of at PGC stage that we expected. When we looked back the Blimp-1-Cre/Gt(ROSA)26-GFP ESCs, we found that Blimp-1-Cre/Gt(ROSA)26-GFP female ESCs are GFP-positive. In the meantime, we found that Blimp-1-Cre/Gt(ROSA)26-GFP male ESCs were GFP-negative and tomato positive, just as the fluorescent color shown by Gt(ROSA)26-GFP cell line. Since Blimp-1-Cre/Gt(ROSA)26-GFP female ESCs are GFP positive, these ESC differentiated cells are all GFP positive. Therefore they are not suitable for tracing the differentiation of female PGCLCs. This result brought the project in predicament. To push the project forward, we decided to switch to Oct4 promoter driving GFP ES cells as a replacement. In our previous studies, we reported that Oct4-GFP fibroblast can be efficiently reprogrammed into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and these iPSC differentiated cells show high germline transmission. Hence, we derived mouse Oct4-GFP ES cells and performed genotyping and picked out female ES cells for further study. Then we set to differentiate Oct4-GFP ESCs into epiblast cell like cells (EpiLCs) by changing ESC medium to EpiLC medium and cultured the cells for 2 days and 3 days respectively. The cells soon lost the ESC colony morphology and became flat. In the meantime, the expression level of GFP is slightly weaker in EpiLCs than ESCs. Lots of dead cells were observed when the cells were cultured in EpiLC medium for three days. We checked the gene expression of the cells and found that the expression of epiblast cell markers were significantly increases, suggesting a cell fate shift to epliblast cell lineage. We then re-suspended the cells in PGCLC medium. Cells formed aggregates in PGCLC medium. After three days, we found that day 2 EpiLC formed aggregates showed patches of GFP positive cells, while day 3 EpiLC formed aggregates were totally GFP-positive. We isolated GFP positive cells by FACS and performed real time-PCR assay. We found that the expression level of Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b was increased in day 2 and day 3 EpiLCs as compared to ESCs. Their expression was significantly decreased in day 2 EpiLC formed aggregates ( D2ag3) and day 3 EpiLC formed aggregate (D3ag3). This phenomenon was agreed with previous report on the typical gene expression change in EpiLC and PGCLCs. Consistently, the expression of PGC genes Tcfap2c and Nanos3 was both increased in D2ag3 and D3ag3 GFP positive cells compared to EpiLCs. Even more, the expression of germ cell markers Mvh and Dazl were also significantly increased in D2ag3 and D3ag3 GFP cells. These data suggest that GFP positive cells in D2ag3 and D3ag3 are PGC like cells. And day3 EpiLCs showed high efficiency in forming PGCLCs. Our early trials to transplant PGCLCs into ovary were not successful. We did not get any allograft after transplantation. Then we tried to transplant PGCLCs under kidney capsule. One month late, we observed that some tissue grew up. We found that some cells in the tissue were GFP positive. After that, we put more effort to improve our techniques in ovary transplantation. At the same time, we also improved our PGCLCs viability by using MACS method using antibody against SSEA1 and β-integrin. We pooled SSEA1 and β-integrin double positive PGCLCs with E12.5 day ovary cells to reconstitute ovary. Subsequently, we transplanted the reconstituted ovary into E12.5 day ovary of C57BL/6 mice. Total 20 mice were transplanted. After several trials, we finally found that some GFP positive cells were observed in the ovary two months after the transplantation. Immunostain with antibody against MVH and GFP confirmed the existence of both GFP and MVH positive cells in ovary, suggesting that they developed into germ cell lineage. However, we have never seen any GFP positive Oocyte. We tried to cross mice with PGCLCs transplanted with wide type C57BL/6 mouse. But no Oct4-GFP positive offspring has been born so far. In the meantime, we used Oct4-GFP MEF generated Oct4-GFP iPS cells. After characterized the pluripotency of iPS cells, we also induced Oct4-GFP iPS cells into EpiLCs and then PGCLCs. Followed previous procedure, we purified the SSEA1 and β-integrin positive cells by MACS and then pool the cells with E12.5 day ovary cells to reconstitute ovary. The reconstitute ovary were transplanted into E12.5 day ovary of C57BL/6 mice for developmental potential check. We can only observed GFP positive cells after two months. None of the cells develop into Oocyte-like cells, which is similar to Oct4-ES cell experimental results. To this end, we have conducted all the proposed experiments and successfully achieved PGCLCs, which is the goal of this project. However, further development of these PGCLCs into occyte and generation of pups are not successful. As the experiments last long term, there might be multiple reasons for not getting the ultimate results. One reason may be although PGCLCs express similar markers as PGCs, these cells may not have the same quality as PGCs. Although Saitou’s lab announce that their protocol can yield functional PGCLCs by develop into functional oocyte for offspring, it hasn’t been verified by other labs yet. Hence, we need to further figure out how solid this protocol is.
