479512.label: Major findings and research outcome
479512.value: By mimicking the in vivo developmental procedure of primordial germ cells, we can efficiently differentiate female Oct4-GFP ES cells into epiblast cell like cells (EpiLCs) and then primordial germ cell like cells (PGCLCs). EpiLCs are highly similar to epiblast cells and PGCLCs are highly similar to primordial germ cells based on the gene expression and epigenetic modification pattern. The induced PGCLCs can survive in both kidney and ovary. However, we haven’t seen later stage germ cell developed in the allograft. The induction procedure should be further optimized. We have presented this study in “ The 8th Guangzhou International Conference on Stem Cell and Regenerative Medicine and the 4th Annual Conference of Chinese Society for Regenerative Cell Biology” in Guangzhou, PRC in December 2015 and “ Germline Stem Cell Conference” in San Francisco, USA in June 2016.

479512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
479512.value: Our study proves that Oct4-GFP ES cells can be used to induce PGCLCs and they can serve as a good model for tracing germline cells. However, our current data showed that no late stage of germline cells was obtained with current protocol. We searched the literature about this protocol which was reported by Saitou’s lab, their protocol has not been widely used in the field yet. Therefore, how solid this induction protocol is needs to be further confirmed.

479512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
479512.value: Overexploitation of natural habitats causes rapid species including mammal extinction. Pollution generated by industries results in the increasing infertility in human beings. Germ cell development is the fundamental procedure for species’ existence. This study endeavors to build up an in-vitro system to reconstitute germ lineage cells to improve mammalian reproductive capability. Using Oct4-GFP mouse embryonic stem cells, we have followed Saitou lab’s protocol and successfully generated primordial germ cell-like cells. The gene expression and epigenetic modification pattern of these primordial germ cells-like cells are highly similar to primordial germ cells. However, although these cells can survive in transplanted ovary for two months, non GFP positive oocytes have observed. In the future, more solid PGCLC induction method should be explored.

490112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
490112.value: In this project, I develop a smartphone application (the “app”) that provides voters important information about their elected officials. A smartphone is defined as a mobile phone that provides advanced computing capability including Internet access and the ability to run third-party applications. Important information includes voting records, community casework, and attendance rate in the legislature. In return, I track user statistics in order to gauge public opinions over elected officials. The app is designed to complement conventional polling methods by mitigating some of their problems, including strategic reporting and low response rate. Public opinions will be extracted anonymously and unobtrusively, allowing us to find out what issues interest voters, how voters view a certain legislative bill, and which candidate enjoys the highest popularity. The app also provides an opportunity to uncover certain voters’ preferences that are difficult to collect through surveys, such as candidate preferences conditional on different socio-economic issues. In addition to facilitating academic research, the app bears a practical value; it can empower voters by reducing their costs of collecting information for assessing their elected officials. The app will be made publicly available free of charge prior to the coming legislative election of Hong Kong, which is scheduled to take place in September 2012. The initial public release of the app targets at the upcoming legislative election, but in the long run the app is intended to provide a platform that allows voters to constantly check the performance of their elected representatives. Because I have no control of who can download the app once it becomes publicly available and because users’ demographic details cannot be easily collected due to privacy reasons, the true causal effects of the app on voters’ choices may be masked from a potential selection bias. That is, it is unclear if the app changes voters’ choices or only voters who would make a certain choice would self-select to download the app. For this reason, I will conduct a controlled randomized experiment in order to evaluate the app’s true effects on voters. 在這個研究計劃中，我會開發智能手機的應用程式（“程式”）。程式將提供選民一些關於民選議員的重要資訊，包括在議會中的投票記錄、地區工作以及在議會內的出席率。同時，我會通過分析程式用戶的瀏覽行為，從而了解民意。設計程式的目的，就是為了補足現有民調方法的一些缺陷，包括受訪者的策略性回答及低回應率。其收集民意的過程，是既不具名、亦不顯眼地進行，但可讓我們找出選民對什麼議題感興趣、哪位候選人最多人支持。程式同時幫我們去找出一些在傳統民調中較難獲得的選民意見，例如在某種議題下選民的投票取向。除了有助學術研究外，程式也有其實質的價值：它能切實地幫助選民以極低的成本來掌握議員的表現，從而在選舉中作出更明智的選擇。 程式將於來屆立法會選舉（於2012年9月舉行）之前發佈，並讓選民可以免費下載。長遠而言，我希望程式能成為一個平台，讓選民可以繼續監察議員的表現。 由於我不能控制誰下載程式，同時基於私隱的理由，我不能輕易地掌握程式用戶的人口統計資料，程式的真正效果可能會因為選擇性偏差而不能反映出來。有見及此，我會進行一個隨機實驗來量度程式的真正效果。

490112.label: Realisation of objectives
490112.value: The first three objectives have been duly achieved. According to the research plan, I developed a well-functioning smartphone application that allowed users to retrieve voting records of elected officials as well as their services at the constituency level. The smartphone app was well-received because it attracted tens of thousands of downloads, which was beyond my initial estimate. From the wide media coverage as well as user comments, I could see that users find the app very useful, as they could become more politically informed of the performance of the legislative councilors. I also obtained valuable data from a political experiment that involved the use of the app as a treatment. The data showed that the app did increase users' political knowledge and political participation. The only objective that fell short was the last one. The design of the app, which aims to provide non-user supplied information, was not sophisticated enough as to track the strategic voting behavior of users. More sophisticated design is required if future researchers want to tease out the strategic voting mechanism.

490112.label: Major findings and research outcome
490112.value: The political effects of communication technology have long attracted the attention of scholars and journalists alike. Some study the democratizing role played by the popular press (Lippmann, 1922; Dahl, 1956; Cater, 1959). Others examine the propaganda and advertising effects associated with radio broadcasts (Barker and Knight, 2000; Horten, 2003; Panagopoulos and Green, 2008). There also exists a wealth of literature exploring television’s effects, ranging from framing public opinions (Iyengar, 1992), discouraging civil engagement (Putnam, 2000), weakening political trust (Mutz and Reeves, 2005), polarizing political knowledge (Prior, 2007), to even undermining democracy (Robinson, 1976). Recent research on communication technology focuses on the Internet(most notably, Castells, 1996), which is arguably the most important communication technology of the past two decades. Many scholars want to know whether the Internet can increase citizens’ political participation. Empirical evidence is far from conclusive, however. While some find that the Internet had little effect on civic engagement (Jennings and Zeitner, 2003) or voter turnout (Bimber, 2001), others show that Internet users are more likely to vote (Tolbert and McNeal, 2003). Interestingly, before researchers settle the debate, the development of the Internet has already moved to a new phase: Web 2.0. The central feature of Web 2.0 is the proliferation of User Generated Content. Instead of passively receiving information produced by journalists, politicians, and pundits alike, Internet users now actively play the role of information provider by sharing their thoughts, observations, insights, and expert views in the blogosphere, Wikipedia, online forums, and a variety of social media. Social media have become a new form of communication in the past decade. Their social significance can be gleaned from their popularity. Facebook alone has attracted hundreds of millions of users. The advantage of social media is that they allow users not only to consume information, but also to produce information with ease. This empowerment effect may have far-reaching political implications. Despite the growing popularity of social media and their perceived significance in political participation, empirical studies of their political effects remain woefully inadequate. The current project has generated useful survey data to answer the above question. The major findings based on an experiment with the smartphone app as a treatment are that by lowering the cost of collecting political information, users are more likely to become more politically informed and more likely to vote. The effect is robust to the inclusion of a variety of demographic variables.

490112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
490112.value: My research shows the possibility and importance of using experimental/quasi-experimental methods in studying political phenomena. Indeed, the discipline of political science has witnessed a substantial increase in the use of experimental methods in the past decade. Unfortunately, such methods remain heavily under-utilized in the study of Hong Kong politics. Conventional studies on Hong Kong politics employ disproportionally qualitative methods. My research has inspired me to adopt experimental methods in two other projects. In the first project, I applied a regression discontinuity design, a quasi-experimental design, to analyze the effect of capturing a District Council office on a political camp's vote share in the subsequent legislative election. In the second project, which is still under way, my co-author and I study the effects of different mobilization cues on vote choice.

490112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
490112.value: In this project, I developed a smartphone application that allows users to retrieve voting records of elected officials prior to a legislative election. I ran an experiment by randomly assigning research subjects into two groups. The treatment received the smartphone app while the control group received none. The experimental results show that those who are exposed to the treatment became more politically informed and more likely to vote. My research has two important implications. First, it shows that the advances of communication technology are conducive to democratic development by allowing ordinary citizens to gain access to important political information such as the voting records of the elected officials. Second, it shows that Internet survey is a promising alternative to traditional survey methods such as phone interviews in soliciting public opinions.

490212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
490212.value: 本研究运用社会资本理论，探讨中国内地流动儿童，留守儿童，以及没有流动经历的城市儿童和农村儿童在教育及心理健康上的差异，如何被他们的身份，居住地点，及蕴藏在多元社会情境中的社会资源所解释。 伴随着农村向城市的人口流动，与父母同往城市的流动儿童和被父母留在农村的留守儿童成为两个快速增长的弱势人群。尽管近年来相关研究逐渐增多，但对流动、留守儿童与城市及农村儿童在教育和心理健康上差异的比较研究并不多见，而对解释这四个儿童群体差异的社会因素的研究尤为缺乏。为弥补现存研究的不足，本研究旨在达成以下目标：1）评估并比较流动、留守，城市及农村儿童的教育与心理健康状况；2）探讨四个儿童群体在教育和心理健康上的差异是由流动/留守的经历所致，还是由城市/农村的身份所致，或是不同地区在社会经济状况上的差异所致；3）揭示蕴藏在家庭，学校，同伴及社区中的社会资本如何影响儿童的教育与心理健康，及其在儿童的身份与 教育和心理健康之间所发挥的中介作用；4）考察多元情境中社会资本的功能 如何因儿童身份的不同而变化。 本研究采用量化研究方法，将在北京，上海和广州三个城市抽取1800名流动儿童及无流动经历的城市儿童，并在江苏，安徽和贵州三省抽取1800名留守儿童及无留守经历的农村儿童展开问卷调查。研究结果对理论和实务都将有显著的长效影响。理论上，本研究将展示多元情境下的社会资本在影响儿童教育与心理健康时的独立作用，交互作用与共促作用，并检验相关的身份变量在其中的调节作用，从而对社会资本理论作出贡献。实务上，研究结果关于多元情境中社会资本的相对优势及 相互影响的发现将对社会服务的设计和发展有所启发，并为社会政策制订提供重要借鉴，以期为实现不同身份人口群体的融合以及城乡和地区发展的平衡产生积极作用。

490212.label: Realisation of objectives
490212.value: This research project started in January 2013 and completed in June 2016. All the four research objectives set out in the study plan have been well achieved with a series of research output generated from the project. The first objective of the research is to assess and compare the educational outcomes and psychological well-being of migrant, left-behind, and native urban and rural children. This is one of the original contributions of the research that fills an outstanding gap in the literature—failing to make systematic comparison among different groups of children with different migration statuses and experiences given the constraint of available data. To achieve this objective, I have conducted survey in three metropolitan cities of China—Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou—where the majority of rural-urban migrants concentrate, as well as in three rural provinces—Guizhou, Anhui, and Jiangsu—where most migrants originates, thus generating a comprehensive study sample including children 1) who migrant with their parents to the urban cities; 2) who are left behind in the rural counties by their migrant parents; 3) are local children born in the urban cities; and 4) who are born and live in the rural counties without any experiences of parental migration. From the six study sites, I have collected a total of 5735 completed surveys, with 1124 from Beijing, 662 from Shanghai, 1342 from Guangzhou, 701 from Guizhou, 970 from Anhui, and 936 from Jiangsu respectively. With such a large and comprehensive sample, I have been able to compare the educational outcomes and psychological well-being across the four groups of children and youths with or without migration experiences and looking into the nuances of their migratory experiences in further details. Generally left-behind children appear to be the most vulnerable group compared to the other three and report more negatively on their education and psychological well-being. And among children living in the rural context, their various experiences of parental migration and their own migratory journeys also make significant differences on their psychological well-being. More detailed results can be found in the publication (Wu, Lu, & Kang, 2015) from this project. The second objective of the research is to identify whether it is the migrant/left-behind status, the urban/rural residence, or the regional varieties on socioeconomic status that lead to the disparities in education and psychological well-being across various groups of children. This is trying to probe into the underlying mechanisms that really explain the differences in the children’s educational and psychological outcomes. Migration statuses and experiences may or may not be the most powerful explanatory factors. The preexisting inequalities between the urban and rural environments, as well as the varying stages of development and socioeconomic statuses of different regions of China could have been the hidden reasons that really contribute to the disparities in children’s well-being. In an invited speech at the Worldwide Universities Network (WUN) Migration Conference, I have presented some findings along this line and tried to answer this question: What really matters for the well-being of children? Who they are (migration status), where they live (rural vs. urban, eastern vs. western, coastal vs. central), and what they have (resources possessed by children and their families). In another presentation, I also tried to examine whether the subjective identity of migrant children, that is, whether they think they are migrants or urban citizens, would influence their psychological well-being, and the results showed significant impact of subjective identity. The third objective of the research is to investigate how social capital embedded in the family, school, peer and community influences children’s educational and psychological outcomes and mediates the effects of their identity and residential statuses. It is the main hypothesis of the study that social capital inherent in the children’s ecological social contexts will contribute to their educational and psychological outcomes with different dimensions of social capital showing varying effects. Moreover, social capital is considered to play a role as mediator that explains how the identity and residential statuses exert effects on children’s well-being. In the survey questionnaire of this study, a number of questions and standardized scales are adopted or constructed to assess the stock of social capital in multiple social contexts. With these comprehensive measures of social capital, I have been able to further develop the theory and build an integrative model to examine the complex interplay among various dimensions of social capital in shaping the child development. And the data do support the above hypotheses. For example, in my paper published in Social Science and Medicine, the results suggest that family and community social capital both predict the psychological well-being of children living in the rural contexts of China, and they also mediate the effects of children’s migration experience and status variables on their well-being. The status of being left-behind is associated with less stock of social capital, which leads to poorer psychological well-being. More analyses are still ongoing to produce more interesting findings. The fourth objective of the research is to examine how the functioning of social capital in multiple contexts might differ across various groups of children with particular identity or residential statuses. In other words, this is trying to test the moderating effect of identical and residential statuses on the operation of social capital. I have been conducting multiple-group analysis in structural equation modeling to model these group differences, including two-group comparison (rural vs. urban sample), four-group comparison (migrant vs. left-behind vs. native urban vs. native rural), and three-group comparison (eastern vs. central vs. western). The analyses are still ongoing and results are being organized, and the trends showing the modifying effects of identity and residential statuses are obvious. Findings from this series of analyses will be presented in future conference and be submitted for journal publication. In summary, this research project has achieve its key aim: applying the social capital theoretical framework to investigate how the disparities in education and psychological well-being of migrant, left-behind, and native urban and rural children from various regions of China are explained by their identity or residential statuses, and by social resources embedded in their multiple social contexts. Findings of this research are informative for both policymakers and social service practitioners in designing social policy and service programs that favor the development of children influenced by migration.

490212.label: Major findings and research outcome
490212.value: This project involves a large-scale quantitative survey conducted in six study sites with a total of 5,735 participants (mean age=12.76 years, 47.5% female) falling under four different identity and residential statuses: migrant, left-behind, urban non-migrant, and rural non-migrant. Some major research findings have been published in peer-reviewed journals and presented in international conferences. Below are a few highlights of the research outcomes: 1) Children’s different migration statuses and experiences had significant influences on their psychological well-being and educational outcomes, and social capital embedded in a range of social contexts did function as a mediator in those associations. As reported in the article published in Social Science and Medicine (Wu, Lu, & Kang, 2015), compared to native rural children without any migratory history, children being left-behind by their migrating parents demonstrated significantly more depressive symptoms. However, children who were left-behind at some time in the past but currently live with both parents appeared to have lower levels of depression. Importantly, these left-behind/migrant statuses were also associated with lower levels of family and community social capital, thus leading to children’s poorer mental health through an indirect pathway. Similar results were also found to apply in the educational outcomes of children with different migration statuses and experiences, and were presented in the 12th Annual Conference of the East Asian Social Policy Network (Wu, 2015). 2) The intersection of migration experiences and family structure also had differing effects on children’s psychological well-being. As presented in an invited speech at the International Conference on Children, Family and Migration in East Asia (Wu, 2016), compared to the native urban children who live in intact families, migrant children living with both parents and native rural children living in intact families exhibited higher level of life satisfaction. Migrant children living with one parent and left-behind children living with one or neither parent showed no significant difference in life satisfaction; however, being left-behind tended to have negative influences on children’s psychological well-being. In addition, family contexts played a mediating role between children’s experience of parental migration and family structure and their psychological well-being. Migrant children and rural native children living with both parents tended to have better family relationships and stronger family-community connections, which in turn enhanced their life satisfaction. Left-behind children, especially those living with neither parent, had significantly poorer family relationships and weaker connection between their families and the community, which led to lower life satisfaction. 3) The well-being of children left-behind by their migrant parents and its relationship with migration experiences and parent-child interactions are not confined to the Chinese migration context, but comparable to other countries experiencing the impact of migration too. In a comparative research between China and Ghana using data from this project, a manuscript currently under review by the journal of Population, Space and Place (Wu & Cebotari, revised and resubmitted with high chance of acceptance) reported that, in both countries, children who live with both parents and have a previous experience of migration and children who currently have a parent away and have not experienced migration themselves appeared to be less satisfied with life. Factors pertaining to parent-child interaction were influential for children’s life satisfaction, with father’s making too many demands showing negative effects, while emotional support from both parents exhibiting positive effects. Left-behind children in China, especially girls, were most vulnerable in their psychological well-being. More research findings are coming out with ongoing data analyses and will be submitted for publication.

490212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
490212.value: This project has great potential for further development. The PI has been moving forward in two promising directions to expand the scope and to enhance the social impact of the research. First, as publications from this project reach the international audience, the PI has been invited to join the International Network of Transnational Families, where researchers from different countries are garnered to exchange ideas and to pool the data (if comparable) from each country together, and work on comparative analyses and collaborative publications. For example, one manuscript of the PI currently under review (revised and resubmitted with high change of final acceptance) is a comparison between China and Ghana in terms of the effects of migration experiences and parent-child interactions on the well-being of left-behind children. More forms and outputs of collaborations are expected with the joint efforts of researchers involved in the network. Second, the PI has also identified an opportunity to further develop the research through combining the survey with the use of big data, an inevitable trend in social science research. One study site of this project, Guizhou province, has become the center of big data application and innovation in China recently. While being invited to give a talk at the 2017 Big Data Expo in Guiyang in May, the PI had discussed with the local government officials and the Directors of the Guiyang Berkeley Innovation Center about possible collaborations of using big data to inform social policy so as to improve the well-being of children influenced by migration. A proposal is under development for that collaboration.

490212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
490212.value: Children influenced by the massive rural-urban migration in China have been paid increasing attention by researchers, policymakers, and the society at large. Applying the social capital theoretical framework, this study aims to investigate how the disparities in education and psychological well-being of migrant, left-behind, urban non-migrant and rural non-migrant children from various regions of China are explained by their identity or residential statuses, and by social resources embedded in their multiple social contexts. The study results suggest that children with different migration statuses and experiences do demonstrate different educational and psychological outcomes, with children who stay behind in their places of origin appearing to be the most vulnerable group. Social resources inherent in the family, school and community all contribute to the well-being of children, and have partly explained the mechanism through which migration statuses and experiences influence children’s educational and psychological outcomes. The research findings advance our understanding of the life experiences of children in the context of migration on the one hand, and also provide valuable insight for policy making and service development on the other hand. Social capital building in multiple social contexts is suggested to be an effective strategy at both policy and practice levels to promote the well-being of children influenced by migration.

490512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
490512.value: 香港廣東話為母語者的最佳個性化線上拼音訓練

490512.label: Project Objectives
490512.value: To identify the Putonghua learning difficulties for high-school native Cantonese speakers. Although some common difficulties for Cantonese speakers learning Pinyin have been captured in the Pinyin study carried out at a university in Hong Kong in 2010, because the population in this study is high-school students, their learning rate and learning patterns are different. The perceptual confusions and spelling errors collected from this population will enrich the current database and therefore facilitate future Pinyin studies. To explore effective teaching methods that promote robust language learning. Traditionally, a test is conducted soon after the teaching sessions. 490512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
490512.value: Second language (L2) learners often fail to distinguish novel speech contrasts in the new language. This inadequate sensibility can be attributed to vague perceptual categories to the target language. Research in the acquisition of L2 phonological system suggests that learners must rely on repeated focused trials to restructure syllable maps in the target language. With increasing demands for effective instruction and learning of Putonghua phonology and Pinyin orthography in Hong Kong, this proposed project aims to use personalized online Pinyin dictation trainings to assist Cantonese speakers to sharpen the perceptual distinction of Putonghua segments and suprasegmentals, and to refine the skill of transcribing Putonghua syllables into Romanized Pinyin letters. The proposal is based on a Pinyin Tutor program used for the past three years at over thirty institutions around the world. The existing Pinyin Tutor has been developed to provide user-focused trainings to certain Putonghua syllables based on the analysis of errors collected in the preceding training items. The current project proposes to explore optimal personalized language training by manipulating the individual variability of phonological working memory, language proficiency, and two pedagogical methods translated from the language acquisition theory Unified Model (MacWhinney, 2007) - cue focusing and graduated interval recall. The idea of robust learning – long-term retention of knowledge and skills – will be elaborated in the context of in vivo experiments by evaluating the interaction of teaching methods and individual variability. In the proposed study, approximately two hundred high-school native Cantonese speakers in Hong Kong with high and low phonological working memory will be divided evenly into two treatment groups and one control group. Participants will take a series of online Pinyin training sessions and a few tests to evaluate their individual variance and Pinyin performance. The effect of self-paced focused learning and system-paced graduated interval recall and their interactions with individual variability and language proficiency will be explored after data analysis. Findings from the proposed study will bring new understandings of how personalized trainings can robustly assist the restructure of L2 phonological system. 第二語言學習者往往不能辨識目標語中不存在于母語的語音對比。這種聽辨敏銳度的不足可以歸結為學習者對目標語語音系統模糊的範疇識別。第二語言語音系統的習得研究表明，學習者需要通過大量有針對性的重複訓練，才得以重新建構目標語的音形對應系統。鑒于香港學生對有效的普通話語音及拼音教學需求的日益增長，該項目希冀以個性化的線上拼音聽寫訓練，幫助廣東話為母語的普通話學習者加強其對聲母、韻母及聲調辨識的敏銳程度，並完善其以拼音字母轉寫普通話音節的能力。 過去三年期間，線上拼音助教系統已在世界各地超過30個機構使用，該項目建立在此前的拼音助教研究項目基礎之上。現有的拼音助教系統能夠根據訓練中產生的錯誤，分析出學習者對拼音掌握的程度，並據此提供有針對性的後續訓練。該項目加入學習者個體差異的因素（語音工作記憶容量、第二語言掌握程度），考察其與由語言習得理論“統一模型” (MacWhinney，2007) 發展而來的兩种教學方法（綫索提示，漸進回顧）之間的相互作用，以探索最佳的個性化語言訓練。強健學習（即持久保留所學知識和技能）的理念，將通過實驗室化教學課程、評估教學方法與學習者個體差異的的形式，在該項目中得到進一步詮釋。 該項目提議，將200個廣東話為母語的香港高中生，根據其語音工作記憶的大小，平均分配入兩個實驗組和一個控制組；並根據一系列在線拼音訓練及一些測試，評估學生的個體差異與學習拼音的情況。該項目將通過統計分析探討兩种學習方法 – “學生自定進度的綫索提示集中學習”與“拼音助教系統控制進度的漸進回顧學習”之效果，以及它們與個體差異之間的相互作用。研究結果將加深我們對個性化的語言訓練可以如何有力協助構建第二語言語音系統的理解。

490512.label: Realisation of objectives
490512.value: Among the five objectives, four of them have been realized, and one of them partially realized due to the restrictions of a limited number of students consistently participated in the project and the data collection environment. Additionally, there are other objectives not stated in the proposal have been realized. They are summarized as follows, I. Completely realized stated and additional objectives: Data collection of the Pinyin Tutor project had lasted for two years. In the first year, the project tracked students consistently using the Pinyin Tutor on the refinement of their phonological perception of Putonghua and Pinyin spelling skills. In the second year, additional data on the production of Putonghua syllables and words were traced at three points of time. Therefore, the project has collected both perception data as a planned objective and production data as an additional objective. The two-year empirical study based on authentic Putonghua curriculum has yielded rich data to examine and identify the difficulties in the perception and production of Putonghua pronunciations by secondary-school native speakers of Cantonese. The study also shows the different learning rate and the various difficulties encountered by students from two types of primary schools: the Putonghua-medium and Cantonese-medium Chinese instructional schemes. Taking a reference to these data, secondary school Putonghua or Chinese teachers can plan their instructional materials and the curriculum to tailor the needs of students accordingly. The data gleaned from Cantonese speakers will also be used to train the intelligent tutoring system to adapt better to this particular population to obtain optimal training effects. II. Incompletely realized objectives: Because the research team could conduct the project in only one local secondary-school, and some students in the study did not consistently participate in the majority of training sessions needed for the experiment, the experimental design could not be completely implemented as planned. In the actual experimental phase, the design had to be simplified from a 2x2x2 research design (two levels of phonological working memory x two levels of language proficiency x two teaching methods) to a 2x2 design (two proficiency levels x two teaching methods). Additionally, because of logistical reasons, the delayed posttest after participants’ summer vacation could not be collected. Although the experimental design is not as diverse and complete as planned, the study involved more qualitative interviews and students’ self-report questionnaires. The qualitative data provide more insights to understand the learners.

490512.label: Major findings and research outcome
490512.value: The project had been conducted for two years to two groups of first-year secondary-school students. Each of the two groups of students received an 8-month dictation training, as well as a pretest, a midway test, and a posttest. Furthermore, in the second year, each student’s pronunciation of Pinyin syllables were recorded for three times during the training period to examine the effect of dictation training on students’ Putonghua production. The project also included surveys on students’ demographic data and cognitive function measurements (i.e. measures of working memory capacity). Results of the statistical analysis on the pretest, midway test, and posttests indicate that the Pinyin training program is beneficial for the students, and students’ skills in Pinyin transcription of Putonghua words have significantly improved between the tests. But the instructional language of Chinese in primary school did not significantly differentiate the students’ skills in Pinyin transcription. However, no matter which language teaching background they came from, the Pinyin training has enhanced students’ Putonghua perception and Pinyin spelling skills. A preliminary survey into the error patterns of specific components in both the transcription tasks and the production tasks shows that there is a correspondence between production and transcription (perception). The most difficult Putonghua onsets for the students are the fricatives and affricates of different places of articulation (zh, z, x). The students also found that rhymes with glides very difficult (iang, un, ui, ue). Regarding the tones, Tone 3 is the most problematic for the students. Surprisingly, the students learned the neutral tone quite well after a period of training, and this was shown in both production and transcription. The error patterns provide us with insights into the phonological learning process of the students, which will benefit educational practitioners future directions in Pinyin teaching. Regarding the comparison of training mechanism, because of the limited number of students consistently participated in the majority of training sessions, referential statistics does not show that the personalized knowledge-tracing group (treatment group) outperform the non-knowledge-tracing group. However, descriptive statistics indicates that students in the knowledge-tracing group do successfully master some of the “difficult” segments in a faster rate compared with the non-knowledge-tracing group. Therefore, the knowledge-tracing mechanism has more potential to increase the phonological sensitivity faster than the regular training method.

490512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
490512.value: The experimental design in the current project was a between-subject design. If there are more schools willing to participate in the study shortly, the experiment will be conducted in a with-subject Latin-Square design. The new design will enhance the statistical power and, therefore, provide more evidence to the strength of target training algorithm. The current and future longitudinal data will be analyzed under the Dynamic Systems Model to examine the micro and macro factors influencing the language learning path and learning rate. In the meantime, the computer-based intelligent Pinyin Tutor will be extended to mobile Apps before June 2016, and thus involve more volunteers to contribute data for the study. Additionally the Jyutping Tutor App will be developed at the same time with the Pinyin Tutor App, and therefore, the study can collect data from learners of Cantonese. With the implementation of new Apps, new research design, and new data analysis scheme, this study will gain more statistical power as well as be used to test the effectiveness of other personalized training mechanisms to optimize further the language training systems.

490512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
490512.value: Learners of a new language often fail to distinguish or pronounce new sounds that are not in their native languages. Learners must rely on repeated focused practice to sharpen their sensibility to the new sounds in the target language. A personalized way of practice taking into consideration of each student’s learning strength and the difficulty is expected to achieve optimal learning effects. This project uses personalized online Pinyin dictation training to assist Cantonese speakers in sharpening the perceptual distinction of Putonghua sounds and their corresponding pronunciations. Over one hundred Cantonese-speaking, first-year students from a local secondary school were invited to practice their Pinyin spelling skills by constantly using the Pinyin Dictation Tutor for eight months during the semesters. The students were randomly divided into two groups by the system to receive personalized or traditional Pinyin dictation training for one academic year. A few Pinyin dictation and pronunciation tests before, during and after the training were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the training. Findings of the study indicate that both groups of students have made significant improvements after training, and the group receiving personalized training have slight advantages in mastering the difficult Putonghua sounds faster than the traditional group.

500112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
500112.value: Regularized minimization problems in high dimensions arise frequently in many fields such as bioinformatics, finance, econometrics, imaging sciences and signal processing. Many mathematical and statistical models for estimation and approximation require solutions of regularized minimization problems formed by the combination of a data-dependent loss function with a norm-based regularization function. Regularized minimization problems in high dimensions present novel and challenging theoretical and computational problems, because they often are nonsmooth, nonconvex, perhaps not even Lipschitz at the solutions. Moreover, in the fast growing research area of scattered data approximation on spheres and manifolds, many new approaches for reconstructing an unknown function are based on a sequence of solutions of regularized minimization problems. On the statistical side, many new results for high-dimensional data analysis require the consistency and fast convergent rate of solutions of the regularized optimization problems when the number of variables is allowed to increase with, and possibly exceed, the sample size. Hence, traditional optimization methods designed for smooth objective functions with a fixed number of variables are not applicable to many important regularized minimization problems in high dimensions. This project aims to develop innovative theories and effective algorithms for regularized optimization problems in high dimensions, where the objective function is the sum of a convex data-fidelity term and a regularization term which can be nonsmooth, nonconvex or even non-Lipschitz. Moreover, the number of variables is allowed to increase with the data size. We will derive new theoretical properties of various regularization functions concerning sparse representation, consistency and convergent rates. Moreover, we will construct efficient algorithms for solving the optimization problems with nonsmooth, nonconvex, non-Lipschitz regularization functions by using smoothing techniques, augmented Lagrangian based split methods and convex approximations. Simulation studies will be conducted to evaluate the proposed algorithms and compare them with the existing algorithms whenever available. Real data involving censored survival outcome and high-dimensional genomic covariates will be used to demonstrate the applications of the new theory and algorithms. The outcomes of this project will have a long-term and significant impact, because regularized minimization problems in high dimensions arise naturally from numerous important applications in scientific fields and urgently need new theoretical and numerical tools for implementation. Our results will attract attention from the international scientific community through publications in leading international journals and conferences, and excellent collaboration with world leading scientists. 高維的正則最小化問題在生物信息學、金融學、經濟學、圖像處理和信號處理等眾多領域都有著廣泛的應用。在許多用於估計和逼近問題的數學模型和統計模型中，我們都需要求解由依賴於數據的損失函數和基於範數的正則函數組成的正則最小化問題。由於高維的正則最小化問題在其優化解附近常常是非光滑的，非凸的，甚至是非Lipschitz連續的，所以高維的正則最小化問題引導出許多新穎的，且在理論與計算上都具有挑戰性的問題。此外，在球體和流形上的離散數據逼近這個快速發展的研究領域中，許多用於重建一個未知函數的新方法都是基於一系列正則最小化問題的解。從統計學的角度看，當變量的數量允許隨著樣本大小而增加，甚至有可能超過樣本大小時，很多高維數據分析中的新結果都需要正則最小化問題解的一致性和快速的收斂速度。因此，那些針對目標函數光滑且變量數量固定的優化問題而提出的傳統優化方法並不適用於很多重要的高維正則化問題。本項目將針對高維的正則化問題開發創新的理論並設計有效的算法，這裡，我們所研究問題的目標函數由一個凸的數據保真度項和一個有可能非凸，非光滑，甚至非Lipschitz的正則項組成，而且變量的數目允許隨著數據量的增加而增加。我們將對不同的正則函數，在稀疏表達形式、一致性和收斂速率等方面得到一些新的理論性質。再者，通過使用光滑化技巧和基於分裂法和凸逼近的增廣拉格朗日函數法，本項目將對帶有非光滑、非凸、非Lipschitz正則函數的優化問題設計有效的算法。同時，本項目還將通過仿真實驗來評估所設計的算法並將它們與一些當時現存的算法做比較。涉及審查的生存結果和高維基因協變量的真實數據將被用於說明新的理論與算法的適用性。由於高維的正則最小化問題是在科學領域的一些重要問題中自然產生的，且迫切地需要新的理論和數值實施工具，本項目的研究成果將有著長期而重大的影響。通過在頂級國際雜誌和會議上發表文章，以及與世界級的科學家之間傑出的合作，我們的成果將得到國際科學家的關注。

500112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
500112.value: Regularized minimization problems in high dimensions arise frequently in many fields such as bioinformatics, finance, econometrics, imaging sciences and signal processing. Many mathematical and statistical models for estimation and approximation require solutions of regularized minimization problems formed by the combination of a data-dependent loss function with a norm-based regularization function. In this project, we developed innovative theories and effective algorithms for regularized optimization problems in high dimensions, where the objective function is the sum of a convex data-fidelity term and a regularization term which can be nonsmooth, nonconvex or even non-Lipschitz. Moreover, the number of variables is allowed to increase with the data size. We derived new theoretical properties of various regularization functions concerning sparse representation, consistency and convergent rates. Moreover, we constructed efficient algorithms for solving the optimization problems with nonsmooth, nonconvex, non-Lipschitz regularization functions by using smoothing techniques, and convex approximations. Simulation studies have been conducted to evaluate the proposed algorithms and compare them with the existing algorithms. The outcomes of this project will have a long-term and significant impact, because regularized minimization problems in high dimensions arise naturally from numerous important applications in scientific fields and urgently need new theoretical and numerical tools for implementation.

500212.label: Project Objectives
500212.value: To synthesize transition metal such as Ni-doped and main-group metal such as Bi-doped thin-film materials, and to study the effects of the preparation process on the structural and optical properties of the materials. To realize ultrabroadband near-infrared emission in the wavelength range from 1100 to 1600 nm, offering the bandwidth larger than 200 nm and optical amplification by a single wavelength pumping. To achieve an understanding of the fundamental mechanism behind ultrabroadband near-infrared emission of non-rare-earth doped materials. To investigate various physical properties and multifunctions of Ni- and Bi-doped materials such as tunable and electric-controlled photoluminescence.

500212.label: Realisation of objectives
500212.value: 1. To achieve the project objective 1 fully, first we have synthesized ceramic or glass targets of transition metal (such as Ni-doped) and main-group metal (such as Bi doped) materials, which can be used for subsequent thin film deposition. During the material’s preparation, we found that the prepared materials can show ultrabroadband near-infrared (NIR) luminescence. Particularly, in Ni-doped ferroelectric (Ba, Sr)TiO3, exceptional peak shift magnitude up to 269 nm is much larger than that of other previously reported Ni2+-doped materials. Through controlling Ba content, the crystal structure of the fabricated samples varies from cubic to tetragonal system, leading to a change from paraelectric to ferroelectric characteristic. Meanwhile, the emission peak from Ni2+ can be finely modulated in a broad spectrum range. The results in our study imply the potential of Ni2+-doped ferroelectric perovskites as a new class of multifunctional materials for the use in optical amplifiers and tunable light sources. On the other hand, a series of Bi doped glasses with ultrabroadband NIR luminescence had been developed through a melt-quenching approach. Through co-doping Ag, enhanced NIR luminescence in Bi-doped glasses is realized owing to plasmon effect. Furthermore, we have successfully deposited thin-film materials of various types of Ni-doped or Bi doped materials by pulsed laser deposition (PLD). Our films can be deposited on various types of useful substrates which are compatible with further measurements and potential device applications. In our studies, conventional dielectrics (LaAlO3, SrTiO3, silica) and semiconductors (Si, GaAs) were used for the synthesis. We have overcome the problems of interdiffusion and film's crystallization through optimizing deposition processing. The effects of the preparation process on the structural and optical properties of the materials have been investigated. The emission peak position of the films can be finely tuned by changing oxygen partial pressure during the thin-film deposition, while the excitation wavelength locates from ultra-violet to NIR regions. The emission peak position of Bi-doped thin films shows a red-shift with decreasing oxygen pressure during growth. By controlling the growth time, the thickness of Ni-doped thin film can be controlled. The emission peak positions of Ni-doped thin films show a blue-shift with increasing growth time. 2. In order to achieve the objective 2 fully, we have carefully measured the fabricated samples, including both Bi- and Ni-doped photonic materials. Photoluminescence (PL) and excitation (PLE) spectra, and the fluorescence decaycurves were measured on FLS920 fluorescence spectrophotometer (Edinburgh Instrument Ltd., U.K.). NIR and mid-infrared (MIR) PL spectra were measured by cooled InGaAs and InSb detectors, respectively. A 450 W Xe lamp, 200 mW laser diodes at the wavelength of 808 and 980 nm were used as the exciting sources. In our measurements, ultrabroadband NIR luminescence in the 1000-2400 nm range has been observed in Bi-doped oxyfluoridegermanate thin films prepared by PLD, which is better than the proposed performance in our proposal. Moreover, the obtained Bi-doped films show emissions peaked at around 1500 nm with full width at half maximum (FWHM) over 450 nm, covering all the O + E + S + C + L bands of optical communication. On the other hand, Ni-doped SrTiO3 oxide thin films grown on piezoelectric Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)0.7Ti0.3O3 (PMN-PT) substrate exhibit exciting ultrabroadband NIR emission under single wavelength pumping, with FWHM over 220 nm covering the NIR spectra range between 1100 and 1600 nm. Based on Ni-doped ferroelectric (Ba, Sr)TiO3 ceramic targets, various Ni-doped ferroelectric perovskites oxides thin films have been prepared by PLD. Under a single wavelength pumping, ultrabroadband NIR luminescence of the prepared Ni-doped thin films can cover optical communication band from 1100 nm to over 1600 nm, with FWHM exceeding 200 nm. Thin film thickness dependent misfit strain can greatly affect the observed luminescence properties, including emission peak position, FWHM, and effective lifetime of the luminescence. 3. To achieve the objective 3 fully, first the dielectric and PL properties of Ni-doped materials were studied through varying measuring temperatures. Since the electron transitions among d orbits of Ni ions are very sensitive to the matrix used, the approach of the temperature dependent crystal structure of oxide compound is powerful to the mechanism study for this project. In Ni-doped materials, the mechanism of the observed tunable luminescence has been explored. Some factors, including the crystal field effect, electron-phonon interaction, temperature and the specific structure of the prepared materials, have been considered. We found that the distribution characteristics of various energy levels play a key role in tuning luminescent properties of transition metal ions. We have investigated the effects of various defects (oxygen vacancy, etc.) and crystal structure transition on the luminescence properties of the films. The PL spectra of as-grown films without any post-annealing and the films annealed under 0.5 atm and 1.0 Pa are compared. On the other hand, systematic investigation has been done to reveal the origin of the luminescence via studying Bi vlusters and valences. We found that NIR luminescence in Bi-doped films comes from Bi species of low valence states, and the valence state of most Bi infrared activecenters (BIA) in films is lower than that in as-made glass. The lifetime of the films is much shorter than that of the glass target, which indicates that different NIR active centers may exist in films and the glass target. In addition, we have studied the luminescent mechanism through the method of the sensitization of Bi-NIR active centers. A typical example is to use Ho ion as second ion and Bi/Ho co-doped films show enhanced ultrabroadband luminescence with high energy transfer efficiency. 4. To achieve the objective 4 fully, first a ferroelectric BaxSr1-xTiO3 (BST) compound was selected as a host because it can provide a specific environment around the Ni2+ dopant, leading to strong coupling between electronic transitions in the Ni2+ ion and vibrational transitions of the ferroelectric hosts. The polarization hysteresis loop of Ni2+-dopedferroelectric hosts has been shown, indicating the multifunctions with both luminescence and ferroelectric properties of the prepared samples. Most importantly, exceptional tunable and ultrabroadband NIR luminescence has been observed in Ni2+-doped ferroelectrics by altering the composition and crystal field. Moreover, we have also demonstrated tunable photoluminescence in Bi-doped thin films through modulating the growth conditions. On the other hand, we have adopted a novel strategy by introducing piezoelectric materials to tunable and multifunctional ultrabroadband luminescence. Tunable PL from Ni-doped SrTiO3 (STO:Ni) thin films grown on piezoelectric PMN-PT substrate has been realized under an external electric field. Consequently, controllable emission of the STO:Ni thin film is demonstrated in a reversible and real-time way, arising from the biaxial strain produced by piezoelectric PMN-PT. Therefore, tunable and electric-controlled NIR photoluminescence has been achieved by coupling Ni-doped perovskite thin films and piezoelectric effect. In summary, all the project objectives have fully been achieved. Non-rare-earth thin-films with ultrabroadband NIR emission have been deposited. The effects of the preparation process on the properties of the materials have been studied. The ultrabroadband NIR emissions can cover the wavelength range from 1100 to 1600 nm, offering the bandwidth larger than 200 nm under a single wavelength pumping. The fundamental mechanisms have been investigated. Moreover, various multi-functions of the materials have been realized.

500212.label: Major findings and research outcome
500212.value: We have published 9 international journal papers (most are A-graded journals) with the GRF grant acknowledged. The PI and two Co-Is have closely collaborated to co-published several journal papers. The PI was invited to write a review feature article entitled “Metal-ion doped luminescent thin films for optoelectronic applications” which is evaluated as J. Mater. Chem. C “Hot Paper”.The PI has presented results in international conferences as keynote/invited speaker, including the well-known Materials Research Society (MRS) meeting in USA. One student was trained and authored several journal papers as the first author,and obtained his PhD degree with high grade. Major findings are as follows: 1. PLD technique has proven to be a powerful technique for depositing non-rare-earth such as transition metal Ni, and main group metal ion such as Bi doped thin-film materials. Optimizing thin-film process is essential to achieve favorable ultrabroadband luminescence properties. (see: Part C: Journal 1,3,5,7, Conference: 1,2,4) 2. In Bi-doped oxyfluoridegermanate films, Bi-doped thin film shows luminescence in 1000~2400 nm, with FWHM over 450 nm. We found that fundamental mechanism behind the ultrabroadband luminescence is related to Bi species of valence states, and the valence state of most Bi active centers in films is lower than that in glass. The PL lifetime of the films is much shorter than that of the glass target, indicating that different NIR active centers may exist in films and the glass. With decreasing oxygen pressure, the emission peak shows a red-shift. The infrared luminescence results from different Bi clusters. (see: Part C: Journal 1,2,5, Conference: 6). 3. For the developed Ni-doped ferroelectric oxides thin films, ultrabroadband NIR luminescence of the prepared thin films covers optical communication band from 1100 nm to over 1600 nm, with FWHM exceeding 200 nm by a single wavelength pumping. The NIR emission can be modified due to chemical substitution induced change in crystal field. (see: Part C: Journal 4,7,8, Conference: 4,5). 4. Tunable and multifunctional NIR luminescence of STO:Ni thin-film grown on piezoelectric substrate is demonstrated using two approaches of strain engineering. The emission of STO:Ni thin film can be tuned under the control of an external electric field in reversible and real-time manner. (see: Part C: Journal 7,9, Conference: 2,3).

500212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
500212.value: Our developed novel non-rare-earth doped ultrabroadband luminescent films in this project will pave the avenue for further investigating multifunctional thin-film luminescent materials and potential device applications. The fabricated ferroelectric Ni-doped thin-films may present unique waveguide by coupling electric-field to the materials. The optical properties of the amorphous Bi-doped glass thin-films could be modified by making composite and adjusting the growth conditions. It is known that integration of active optoelectronics on a wafer is relevant to on-chip interconnection. Electroluminescent (EL) devices based on the obtained results of this project could be designed, which is important for integrated optics and optical communications. For gaining ultrabroadband NIR EL, both high electric-field and injection modes of El devices could be considered based on the developed thin-film photonic materials. In addition, flexible electronic, photonic and optoelectronics devices have drawn considerable attention in recent years, motivated by their numerous applications, such as novel types of displays and wearable sensors. Through further processing our developed thin-film samples such as chemical etching and lift-off, the solid substrates used in this project can be peeled off. The processed thin-films can be transferred to the flexible plastic substrates. Hence, the photonic thin-films can be utilized as flexible optoelectronic devices.

500212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
500212.value: Photonic materials with near-infrared (NIR) luminescence have continuously received much attention, as they are promising for applications in optical telecommunication systems, biomedicine, sustainable energy and light sources. Succeeded by the conventional rare-earth (RE) ions (e.g., Er) doped photonic materials, non-RE such as Ni- and Bi-doped materials are promising as the gain medium in ultrabroadband optical amplifiers and tunable lasers. Noted that thin-film photonic materials are of great interest in planar optical amplifiers and other integrated photonic technologies. In this project, Ni- and Bi-doped thin-film photonic materials with ultrabroadband NIR luminescence have been developed. The fabricated non-RE doped thin-films excited by a single wavelength pumping can present ultrabroadband NIR luminescence (full-width-at-half-maximum>200 nm), covering the whole optical telecommunication window. Interestingly, the NIR luminescent properties can be modulated by controlling chemical substitution, thin-film growth process, strain engineering and electric field. Particularly, the electric-controlled luminescence is realized in reversible and real-time manner. Our success in depositing non-RE photonic thin-film materials will increase the capabilities of the NIR luminescent materials beyond RE-doped compounds. Our results will be very helpful for a better scientific understanding of ultrabroadband NIR luminescence and selection of the potential materials for a new generation of thin-film integrated photonic technology.

500312.label: Project Title(Chinese)
500312.value: 非線性物理模型中之 Nernst-Planck 及 Ermakov-Ray-Reid 模型

500312.label: Project Objectives
500312.value: To isolate and analyse qualitative aspects of boundary value problems for the Nernst-Planck system which are amenable to exact solution in terms of elliptic integrals or via Painleve II reduction for determined classes of valency ratios. To conduct an overarching study of existence and uniqueness, stability, periodicity and positivity aspects of boundary value problems that arise out of a general multi-ion electro-diffusion model. To extend and generalize existing tools in the qualitative theory of single differential equations to handle coupled equations in systems of equations. To investigate stability, periodicity and positivity properties of Ermakov-Ray-Reid systems that occur in physical contexts in nonlinear optics, hydrodynamics and magneto-gasdynamics. To construct by Lie group methods, discrete analogues of Ermakov-Ray-Reid systems which preserve the quantitative properties of their continuous counterparts.

500312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
500312.value: The electro-diffusion model introduced by Nernst (Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1920) and Planck (Nobel Prize in Physics 1918) provides the basis for a macroscopic description of migration of charged particles through material barriers. These transmission processes are of fundamental importance in electrochemistry, semi-conductor theory and the analysis of mechanisms of ionic transport through biological membranes. On the other hand, nonlinear coupled systems of Ermakov-Ray-Reid type arise in a diversity of important physical areas, notably, in optics, rotating ocean eddy theory and magneto-gasdynamics. In some recent work of the PI, a particular class of Ermakov system of equations arises in the search of elliptically (but not spherically) symmetric solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations in fluid dynamics. These systems give rise to some unconventional qualitative problems that are not susceptible to traditional approaches. The existing theories are mainly based on certain symmetry properties of the equations. The theory of Lie group transformations and integrable systems play important roles. These approaches, although very powerful, impose certain limits on the various parameters of the system and they often do not reveal much of the qualitative properties of the solutions. In fact, very little is known about, for example, the positivity, oscillatory, or asymptotic behavior of the solutions. The PI has an extensive record in the analysis of such properties for single differential equations, both ordinary and partial. In this project, the PI's expertise will be extended to analyze the qualitative properties of physically relevant boundary value problems arising out of the Nernst-Planck system in multi-ion electro-diffusion. In a parallel study, fundamental oscillation, stability and positivity properties of Ermakov-Ray-Reid systems are to be investigated within the physical contexts of nonlinear optics and magneto-gasdynamics. More specifically, the Nernst-Planck system leads to some non-standard boundary value problems for which traditional approaches are found to be inadequate. Systems involving several coupled differential equations, in general, exhibit much more complicated behaviors due to the interactions between the unknown variables. Certain techniques useful for studying single equations, such as comparison principles and differential inequalities, no longer work as they stand. Extension and modifications of these techniques will be sought and new tools devised for important nonlinear physical models. 非線性物理模型中之 Nernst-Planck 及 Ermakov-Ray-Reid 模型 Nerst（1920年諾貝爾化學獎得主）與 Planck（1918年諾貝爾物理獎得主）提出 之電擴散模型描述帶電粒子在物體中運行之現象。此理論在電化學，半導體，及 生物膜中離子運送等之研究上，至為重要。另外 Ermakov-Ray-Reid 型之非線性 耦合系統，在多個物理領域中出現，如光學、海洋渦流、磁氣體動力學等。PI在 近日研究一流體力學問題，在尋找 Navier-Stokes 方程一些橢圓（而非球形） 對稱解時，也遇上一類 Ermakov 方程。 此等系統引出一些非典型之定性問題，不能用傳統方法解決。現有之理論主 要基於方程之某些對稱性質，重要之研究方法是李群變換和可積系統。此等方法 雖然有效，但對系統之各個參數有所限制，且通常不能彰顯出解的很多性質，例 如對解的正性，其振動性，和漸近趨向，我們所知者甚少。 對單一之方程，PI在這方面有過不少工作。在此研究項目中，會將研究延伸到多 離子電擴散理論中遇到之 Nernst-Planck 系統邊界問題解之定性研究。同時也 考慮非線性光學與磁氣體動力學中之 Ermakov-Ray-Reid 系統的振動性，穩定性， 正性等基本問題。 因為系統含有數個耦合微分方程，每一個未知量之變動可以很複雜地影響別個未 知量之變動，因此傳統上用來研究單一方程的技巧，如比較原理，微分不等式等， 都不可以直接搬過來用，都需要延伸，或者改良，甚至要尋找全新之工具。

500312.label: Major findings and research outcome
500312.value: We have studied the qualitative properties of the solutions of a Nerst-Planck and Ermakov-Ray-Reid system arising from a model of shallow water waves and proposed new techniques in simulating the evolution of such solutions. We have also discovered new perturbational type of solution of certain Navier-Stokes-Euler equations arising in fluid mechanics. The greater bulk of achievements is in the discovery of many new inequalities of trigonometric polynomials which plays a very important role in the Fourier analysis of numerical computation of solutions of complicated systems of partial differential equations, of which the pertinent type of systems of equations we studied belong to.

500312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
500312.value: The achieved results of the project has great potential for further study of systems similar to those investigated in this project. However, the PI will be retiring from the university and hopefully other researcher in the field will be able to continue the effort.

500312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
500312.value: Most physical phenomena can be modeled as systems of partial differential equations. The ones we were investigating include electro-diffusion model introduced by Nernst and Planck, nonlinear optics, and migration of charged particles through material barriers. In general, the system of PDE's are too complicated to be solved explicitly. In searching for particular solution, we exploit the fact that certain solutions possess some simple characteristics. In so doing, the systems under study reduce to simpler ones, such as the Nernst-Planck and Ermakov-Ray-Reid which are amenable to known analysis. Another example are the serach of elliptically symmetric solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations in fluid dynamics. We study solutions of such system. In particular, we prove the existence of such solutions and provide numerical methods to approximate them. One of the techniques we used is Fourier analysis in which trigonometric polynomials and series are used. In particular, we are interested in various bounds and inequalities satisfied by such series. We have discovered many new properties of the solutions of the pertinent system and trigonometric series which are of great importance in further studies of the subject matter.

500612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
500612.value: Graphene, a single-atom-thick two-dimensional sheet of sp2 hybridized carbon, has attracted a great deal of interest due to its unique properties and potential applications in nanoelectronics. Graphene-based devices are still limited since defect-free graphene exhibits zero bandgap. Graphene oxide (GO) has been considered as a precursor to prepare graphene. Owing to the unique characteristics of GO, there are increasingly attention drawn to GO itself. The synthesis of GO is based on top-down approach so far. In this project, we propose to adopt a bottom-up method developed by the principle investigator’s team to synthesize large-scale GO nanosheets. The method is environmentally friendly, facile, low-cost as well as capable of scaling up for mass production. We will carry out a systematic study on the bottom-up synthesized GO aiming to obtain n and p-type monolayer and few layers GO nanosheets. By employing various chemicals, growth and annealing parameters, the electrical and optical properties of GO nanosheets will be optimized for various optoelectronics devices such as conductive transparent electrodes, organic photovoltaic, and light emitting diodes. 石墨烯是一種單原子層的二維sp2雜化碳膜，它由於具有獨特的性質和潛在的納米電子學應用前景而吸引了人們廣泛的研究興趣。目前石墨烯基器件性能受限於無缺陷石墨烯的零能帶。以前氧化石墨烯（GO）作為前驅體被廣泛地用來製備石墨烯，但是由於GO本身俱有很多獨特的性質，導致人們對GO的研究興趣與日俱增。目前製備GO的技術都是基於自上而下的方法，在本項目中，我們擬採用項目負責人研究組自行開發的自下而上合成技術對GO納米片進行大批量合成。該技術的特點是：製備方法環境友好、方便、成本低以及具備批量生產的能力。我們將系統地開展自下而上合成GO的研究，以獲得單層和少數幾層的n型及p型摻雜的GO納米片。通過對源、生長及退火參數的調製，我們將優化GO納米片的電學及光學性質，以期拓展其在透明導電電極、太陽能電池、光電探測器及發光二極管等光電子器件中的應用。

500612.label: Realisation of objectives
500612.value: The GO nanosheets were prepared by a hydrothermal method using glucose as a sole reagent. The thickness of the GO nanosheets can be tuned from ~ 1 nm to over 1 µm. The lateral sizes of the monolayer and few-layer GO nanosheets are about 20 mm and 100 mm respectively. In addition to glucose, sugar and fructose can also be used to prepare GO with similar structural properties. Based on our experiments, we deduce that most carbohydrates which contain C, H and O in the ratio of 1 : 2: 1 may be used as carbon sources to prepare GONs provided that H and O exist in the forms of hydroxyl, carboxyl or carbonyl groups that may dehydrate under hydrothermal conditions. The growth parameters of the GO nanosheets were optimized in terms of their structural and electrical properties. Thermal annealing method was used to reduce the GO nanosheets in order to tune its electrical properties. A wide range of substrates including Si, sapphire, Cu, Al are used for the annealing. The method is environmentally friendly, facile, low-cost as well as capable of scaling up for mass production. In fact, several review reports regarded our method as one of the most promising approach to prepare low-cost and large-scale GO. Objectives 1 and 2 were completed. The annealed GO nanosheets exhibited p-type characteristics in GO-based field effect transistors. The n-type GO nanosheets can be prepared using glucose and ammonia solution. The optical properties of the n and p-type GO nanosheets were similar. Objective 3 was completed. GO and reduced GO (r-GO) are being investigated intensively as effective hole and/or electron transport layers in both organic solar cells (OPV) and organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs. Our GO exhibited similar transport properties as the conventional r-GO. The wavelength-dependent photoresponse of GO was investigated by fabricating metal-GO-metal photodetectors. The devices demonstrated a broadband photoresponse from290 to 1610 nm covering deep ultraviolet (UV) to near-infrared (NIR), which is the broadest spectral range yet demonstrated on GO. The response times of the photodetectors in the UV and visible range are about 100 ms, which are at least one order of magnitude faster than photodetectors based solely on GO reported previously. The responsivity of the photodetector can be as high as 23.6 mA/W in the visible range. Potential for a self-powered GO based photodetector (photovoltaic) was also demonstrated, and the device shows a prominent photoresponse at zero bias. Objective 4 was completed

500612.label: Major findings and research outcome
500612.value: Graphene oxide (GO) was synthesized by a hydrothermal method using glucose solution as the sole reagent. The bottom-up synthesized GO exhibited similar electrical and optical properties of GO prepared by conventional materials. Our method is simple and environmental friendly. The GO-based photodetectors exhibited photoresponse from 290 to 1610 nm covering deep ultraviolet (UV) to near-infrared (NIR), which is the broadest spectral range yet demonstrated on GO. The method using glucose solution as the carbon source for graphene based nanomaterials has been extended to fabricate graphene quantum dots (GQDs). The GQDs exhibited attractive optoelectronic properties as compared to GO. The GQDs can be doped with S to tune its optical properties. The memory and photodetectors devices were demonstrated using GQD-polyaniline composite. The knowledge gained from the GO-based photodetector was also extended to study an emerging carbon-based materials called polymeric carbon nitride. The polymeric carbon nitride based photodetectors exhibited high photocurrent and optical gain in UV spectral region.

500612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
500612.value: The bottom-up synthesis of GO nanosheets has attracted a lot of attention as a facile, low-cost and environmental friendly method. The GO nanosheets exhibit a wide range of applications especially in broadband photodetection. The synthesis method has been modified and extended to prepare graphene quantum dots (GQDs). The GQDs work led to the award of another General Research Fund project.

500612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
500612.value: We developed a bottom-up approach to synthesize graphene oxide (GO) nanosheets. The GO nanosheets were prepared by a hydrothermal method using glucose as a sole reagent. The thickness of the GO nanosheets can be tuned from ~ 1 nm to over 1 µm. The lateral sizes of the monolayer and few-layer GO nanosheets are about 20 mm and 100 mm respectively. The method is environmentally friendly, facile, low-cost as well as capable of scaling up for mass production. A wide range of application has been demonstrated for GO including broadband photodetectors, transport layer in organic photovoltaic and light emitting diodes, solar cells and field effect transistors.

501012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
501012.value: Numerical simulation of metamaterials offers many challenges in terms of mathematical and numerical issues. For example the lossy Drude polarization and magnetization models are often used to simulate wave propagation in metamaterials, which can be described by Maxwell integro-differential equations. The modeling of pulse propagation in biological tissues is an important research topic when we deal with wave propagation problems inside human body. In this case, we may have to consider a simple Cole-Cole medium model which contains a fractional derivative in time. The Cole-Cole medium model in time domain can be described by fractional Maxwell integro-differential equations. In this project, the PI proposes to develop robust and efficient numerical schemes which will provide engineers with powerful computational simulation tools in developing new metamaterials and studying wave interaction problems with complex dispersive media such as human tissues and metamaterials. 数值模拟的超材料在数学方面提供了很多的挑战 和数值的问题。例如，有损德鲁德极化和磁化 模型通常用于模拟波传播的超材料，它可以是 麦克斯韦积分微分方程描述。 该模型的脉冲在生物组织中的传播是一个重要的研究课题 当我们处理人体内与波的传播问题。在这种情况下，我们可能会 要考虑一个简单的Cole-Cole介质模型，它包含一个分数阶时间的导数。 Cole-Cole介质模型可以描述为在时域分数阶Maxwell积分微分方程。 在这个项目中，PI建议建立强和高效率的数值方案 为工程师提供了强大的计算仿真工具，应用在开发新的 超材料和复杂的色散介质中的波相互作用问题研究,如人体组织和​​超材料。

501012.label: Major findings and research outcome
501012.value: The time-dependent Maxwell’s equations used to modeling wave propagation in dispersive lossy bi-isotropic media are investigated. Existence and uniqueness of the modeling equations are proved. Two fully discrete finite element schemes are proposed, and their practical implementation and stability are discussed. We consider a posteriori error estimates for time-dependent Maxwell’s equations discretized by variable time steps in time domain and edge elements in spatial domain. The stability and optimal a priori error estimate are proved for both semi and fully discrete schemes. Then a posteriori error analysis is carried out for both schemes. We develop a new energy-conserved S-FDTD scheme for the Maxwell’s equations in metamaterials. We first derive out the new property of energy conservation of the governing equations in metamaterials, and then propose the energy-conserved S-FDTD scheme for solving the problems based on the staggered grids. We prove that the proposed scheme is energy-conserved in the discrete form and unconditionally stable. Based on the energy method, we further prove that the scheme for the Maxwell’s equations in metamaterials is first order in time and second order in space. Numerical experiments are carried out to confirm the energy conservation and the convergence rates of the scheme. Moreover, numerical examples are to show the propagation features of electromagnetic waves in the DNG metamaterials. In additional Some immersed finite element methods (with material interfaces) and finite volume element methods, some with two grid versions, are studied for related time-independent problems, which can serve as the first step for finding more proper and efficient numerical methods for Maxwell systems in time domains.

501012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
501012.value: Our approaches and results developed in this project can be served as the starting point for further developments for Maxwell systems with integrals for metamaterials modeling and simulations. In fact we already begun our next phase of research in this directions including for systems of Maxwell type equations coupled with Schroedinger equations. Light-matter interaction at nanoscale is a central topic in the study of optical properties of nanophotonic systems, for example, metallic nanostructures and quantum dots. In view of practical numerical simulation, a semiclassic model is often used for modelling light-matter interaction. The basic idea is to use the classical Maxwell's equations for the electromagnetic field and the Schrodinger equation for the matter. We also begun our investigations of efficient numerical methods for nonlinear Maxwell systems, and will continue our study on a posterior estimators and other more efficient and high order numerical methods for Maxwell systems in metamaterials modeling.
