501112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
501112.value: Alkenes from biogenic and anthropogenic sources constitute an important class of volatile organic compounds in the troposphere and reaction with ozone is a primary removal mechanism. In general, ozone-alkene reactions lead to the production of a wide range of functionalized oxygenated products, including carbonyls, organic acids, and hydroperoxides, and they are also non-photolytic sources of OH, HO2 and RO2 radicals. The general mechanism for these reactions is now widely accepted. It involves addition of ozone across the double bond of the alkene to form a primary ozonide. This reaction is quite exothermic and results in decomposition of the primary ozonide into a carbonyl compound and an intermediate, R1R2COO, a Criegee intermediate, which may decompose, or react. Although many studies have been made of ozone-alkene reactions, the roles and stabilities of these intermediates are uncertain. It is known, however, that they play an important part in controlling the budgets of secondary organic aerosols, ozone, NOx, NOy and HOx throughout the troposphere, and they also play key roles in determining atmospheric composition, the earth's radiative balance and climate. They remained elusive to detection until work by Taatjes, Percival, and co-workers obtained evidence for the simplest Criegee intermediate H2COO by photoionisation mass spectrometry (PIMS). Despite this initial work, no direct studies of the reactions of these intermediates have been performed. This has prevented a full and reliable description of atmospheric degradation mechanisms, which means there is uncertainty in the lifetimes of key greenhouse gases and surface pollutants. This research project will use photoelectron spectroscopy (PES) to detect H2COO and other small Criegee intermediates, and then use this method to study the gas-phase kinetics and mechanisms of Criegee intermediate reactions of atmospheric importance. This will be achieved by a flow-tube, operated under turbulent flow conditions, interfaced to the ionization chamber of a PE spectrometer. In summary, the objective of this work is to characterise the simplest Criegee intermediates and other related intermediates produced in ozone-alkene reactions by PES, and then determine, both experimentally and computationally, channel specific rate coefficients for reactions of these small reactive intermediates with atmospherically important molecules. The significance of this work is that it will allow a more accurate description of atmospheric degradation mechanisms once the rate coefficients for the reactions studied have been incorporated into atmospheric models and this will allow a more accurate determination of lifetimes of atmospheric gases, notably greenhouse gases and surface pollutants. 過氧自由基對大氣對流層中臭氧，氮氧化物，氫氧化物和鹵化氧化物等自由基含量起著舉足輕重的作用，而這些自由基對大氣成分，地球的輻射平衡和任何未來氣候變化的影響無容置疑。然而，我們對它們之間複雜的化學作用的認識，近年通過實地觀測和前沿的計算機模型而增進了不少。透過模型計算和實地觀測結果的比較，顯示一些重要過氧自由基反應的可靠實驗速率係數和分支比是迫切需要的重要數據。 本項目選定的自由基反應，每個反應至少有兩個反應產物通道，而了解這些反產物分佈有助解決一些在大學化學中重要的問題。例如，過氧自由基與XO自由基反應對對流層中的臭氧預算有顯著貢獻，而在平流層中XO自由基的反應則導致臭氧洞的出現。測量它們反應的分支比和通道特定的速率係數，有助確切了解它們如何影響對流層及平流層的臭氧預算。 實試作將涉及應用化學電離質譜（CIMS）和光電子能譜（PES）測量反應速率係數和反應分支比。 PES亦被用來研究反應中間體的結構。這裡透過結合CIMS和PES的檢測優點，檢測所有反應產物，從而首次量化觀測這些自由基反應的質量平衡。此外，應用量子化學方法計算反應表面和通道特定的速率係數有助詳細的了解反應機理，並可與實驗測量的反應係數作詳細比較。 總括而這，這項工作的目標是以在實驗和計算方法，得出過氧自由基及相關自由基在大氣中反應的特定通道反應速率係數。長遠而言這項計劃的意義在於幫助了解大氣中重要的自由基反應，並提供特定的速率係數，以建立更為理想的地方，區域和全球尺度大氣模型。使計算重要大氣數量如臭氧和溫室氣體的濃度的結果更為可靠。

501112.label: Realisation of objectives
501112.value: The objectives of this work is to characterise a few selected simple Criegee intermediates produced in ozone-alkene reactions and to examine the reaction rates of these intermediates using both experimental and computational techniques. Three Criegee intermediates, CH2OO, CH3CHOO and (CH3)2COO, have been characterized experimentally and direct kinetic data of these Criegee intermediates with acetones, acetaldehyde, SO2, NO2 and/or water have been obtained experimentally for the first time. Extensive state-of-the-art ab initio and FCF calculations have been carried out to guide and assist spectral assignments and interpretation of the kinetic data. Although we did not computed any rate coefficients for these reactions, but focused on the determination of the reaction surfaces for the production of CH2OO and (CH3)2COO, and also some isomerization energy surfaces of the two heavier Criegee intermediates, CH3CHOO and (CH3)2COO to provide more relevant information for interpretation of experimental results. Summarizing, we have achieved all the objectives. For the experimental part of the project (revised objectives 1,2, and 4), the UV photoelectron (PE) spectrometer to be constructed in Manchester for the detection of Criegee intermediates and subsequent kinetic studies has been built. The multichannel position sensitive detector has been incorporated into the spectrometer and is working (giving analogue signals), after a long trouble-shooting, the software and hardware interface for data collection (converting analogue signals to digital signals) was found to be the reason of problems in obtaining digital experiment read-outs, limiting the use of the instrument in this study. Nevertheless, with the channeltron detector, the lightest Criegee intermediate, CH2OO, has been detected (spectral signals detected at the predicted energy region according to the simulated spectrum; see E. P. F. Lee, D. K. W. Mok, D. E. Shallcross, C. J. Percival, D. L. Osborn, C. A. Taatjes, J. M. Dyke, Chem. Euro. J. 18, 2012, 12411) via the F + CH4 → HF + CH3 and subsequent CH3 + O2 + M → CH3O2 + M and F + CH3O2 → HF + CH2OO reactions, though the photoelectron signals due to CH2OO are rather weak, as expected (the multichannel detector should increase the sensitivity of detection by 1 to 2 orders of magnitude if reliable read-outs can be achieved). In view of this, experimental studies have been conducted in collaboration with Dr. Craig A. Taatjies, Combustion group, Sandia National Laboratory (SNL), USA, using synchrotron radiation photoionization mass (PIM) spectrometry. Based on the collaboration with SNL, we have been able to obtain spectroscopic and kinetic results on the proposed Criegee intermediates, namely CH2OO, syn-CH3CHOO, anti-CH3CHOO and (CH3)2COO with PIM results. (Revised objectives 1, 2 and 4) Extensive computations have been carried out to complement and to assist interpretation of experimental results obtained (revised objectives 3 and 5). Geometry optimization and harmonic vibrational frequency calculations were carried out using density functional theory (B3LYP or M02-2X functional with 6-311++G** or aug-cc-pVDZ). More reliable relative electronic energies were calculated using the explicitly correlated RHF/UCCSD(T)-F12x methods for CH3CHOO (acetaldehyde oxide), (CH3)2COO (acetone oxide) and their isomers (CH2CHOOH, CH2=C(CH3)OOH, 3-methyl-1,2-dioxetane and dimethyl-dioxirane) while MR methods, namely, CASSCF, CASSCF/MRCI and CASSCF/NEVPT2, have been employed to study the bis(oxy) intermediate, with large basis sets (up to aug-cc-pVQZ quality). In addition, the 1/X3 extrapolation method was used to obtain computed ionization energies (IEs) at the complete basis set (CBS) limit. Franck-Condon factor (FCF) calculations were carried out employing the EZSPECTRUM code, which include Duschinsky rotation within the harmonic oscillator model to assist the assignments of the observed PIM spectra. The results of the calculations on CH3CHOO (acetaldehyde oxide) have been published together with experimental results from SNL in the journal, Science. (See Taatjes et al., Science 340, 2013, 177 and Percival et al. Faraday Discussions, 165, 2013, 45 for details; regrettably, the acknowledgement of the present grant was inadvertently omitted in these two publications.) Although carbonyl oxides, “Criegee intermediates,” have long been implicated in tropospheric oxidation, there have been few direct measurements of their kinetics, except only for the simplest compound in the class, CH2OO (see above). In the study of reactions related to (CH3)2COO, we have also computed the reaction energy profiles of reactions 1 and 2: (CH3)2CI + O2 → (CH3)2CIOO …. Reaction 1 (CH3)2CIOO → (CH3)2COO + I …. Reaction 2 As above, geometries and energies were determined as described above using density functional theory. The aug-cc-pVDZ-PP basis set and associated fully relativistic ECP28MDF effective core potential (ECP) were used for iodine. Higher level ab initio energy calculations were carried out at M06-2X stationary points on the reaction energy surfaces, employing single-reference (SR) methods, namely RHF/UCCSD(T) and RHF/UCCSD(T)-F12x, and multi-references (MR) methods, namely, CASSCF, CASSCF/NEVPT2, CASSCF/CASPT2 and CASSCF/CASPT2-F12. In some cases, extrapolation to the CBS limit was also carried out using the 1/X3 formula, as described above. Simulated PIM spectra were used to assist assignments of observed spectra, resulting from the reactions leading to the production of acetone oxide and other isomers. (Related to revised objective 5) Related works: State-of-the-art ab initio calculations and anharmonic Franck-Condon factor (FCF) calculations on low-lying electronic states of HPS and the ground electronic states of AlH2 and its anion were carried out. The single-vibronic-level (SVL) emission spectrum of HPS, and the photodetachment spectrum of AlH2- were simulated and compared with recently published experimental spectra. It is concluded that our spectral simulation supports the assignments of the molecular carrier, the electronic states involved and the vibrational structure of the experimental laser induced fluorescence, and SVL emission spectra of HPS. However, our simulated spectra do not support the assignment of the reported experimental spectrum to AlH2-. (Related to revised objective 3)

501112.label: Major findings and research outcome
501112.value: In this work, production and reaction kinetics of the larger Criegee intermediates, CH3CHOO and (CH3)2COO, were reported for the first time. For CH3CHOO, the two distinct CH3CHOO conformers, syn- and anti-, were identified based on our computed IEs and FCF simulations. Also, both syn- and anti-CH3CHOO react readily with SO2 and with NO2. Anti-CH3CHOO was found to be substantially more reactive toward water and SO2 than syn-CH3CHOO. Reaction with water may dominate tropospheric removal of Criegee intermediates and determine their atmospheric concentration. An upper limit is obtained for the reaction of syn-CH3CHOO with water, and the rate constant for reaction of anti-CH3CHOO with water is measured as 1.0 × 10−14 ± 0.4 × 10−14 cm3 s−1. Acetone oxide was identified in the observed spectra for the first time. The rate coefficient of the reaction of the acetone oxide with SO2 was measured using photoionization mass spectrometry and pseudo-first-order methods to be (7.3 ± 0.5) × 10−11 cm3 s−1 at 298 K and 4 Torr and (1.5 ± 0.5) × 10−10 cm3 s−1 at 298 K and 10 Torr (He buffer). These values are similar to directly measured rate coefficients of anti-CH3CHOO with SO2. The reaction of(CD3)2COO with NO2 has a rate coefficient at 298 K and 4 Torr of (2.1 ± 0.5) × 10−12 cm3 s−1 is also similar to rate for the reaction of anti-CH3CHOO with NO2. The study confirmed the large rate coefficient for reaction of (CH3)2COO with SO2 and the small rate coefficient for its reaction with water. Product measurements of the reactions of (CH3)2COO with NO2 and with SO2 suggest that these reactions may facilitate isomerization to 2-hydroperoxypropene, possibly by subsequent reactions of association products. Our study showed that Criegee intermediates react far more rapidly with SO2 than typically represented in tropospheric chemistry models. This suggested that the Criegee intermediates could have a substantial influence on the atmospheric oxidation of SO2. In fact, reaction of Criegee intermediates with SO2 will compete with or even dominate over the reaction of OH with SO2, which is currently the only known gas-phase source of H2SO4, in many regions. The products of Criegee intermediate reactions predominantly result in H2SO4 formation, modelled particle nucleation rates can be substantially increased by the improved experimentally obtained estimates of the rate coefficients of Criegee intermediate reactions. Thus, the rate coefficients obtained in this study results in a much better atmospheric chemistry model.

501112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
501112.value: In the study of acetone oxide, data on the acetone oxide removal without added reagents revealed a combination of first- and second-order decay kinetics, which can be deconvolved to derive values for both the self-reaction of (CH3)2COO and its unimolecular thermal decay suggesting a wide possibility of reaction of the Criegee intermediates. Product measurements of the reactions of (CH3)2COO with NO2 and with SO2 suggest that these reactions may facilitate isomerization to 2-hydroperoxypropene. This lead to a subsequent proposal studying the inserting reaction of (CH3)2COO into a hyperoxides (ROOH) which would be a possible mechanism of self-reaction and that could be important particular when other reaction partners are present to facilitate the isomerization. This proposal is awarded in the GRF 2015 exercise.

501112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
501112.value: Carbonyl oxides also known as Criegee intermediates, have long been implicated in tropospheric oxidation, there have been few direct measurements of their kinetics, except only for the simplest compound in the class, CH2OO (which was also a result of the present collaboration between Sandia, Manchester and Hong Kong). In this work, production and reaction kinetics of larger Criegee intermediates, CH3CHOO and (CH3)2COO, were reported for the first time. Reactions of these Criegee intermediates with other compounds presence in atmosphere, such as water, sulphur oxides and nitrogen oxides. These provided essential information to understand the chemistry of these important short-lives compounds. Employing these new kinetic data in modelling the atmosphere will revise and improve the reliability of the results obtained, which will allow a more accurate account for oxidation reactions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in the troposphere, and for determining the lifetimes of key greenhouse gases and pollutants. The possibility of self-reaction of these Criegee intermediates may also be an important pathway for the formation of aerosols which worth further studies.

501212.label: Project Objectives
501212.value: Introduce induced norms for tensors, show the the spectral radius of a symmetric tensor is its 2-norm, and study the other properties of the spectral radius of a symmetric tensor. Introduce spectral minimum for a symmetric tensor, consider the reciprocal of the spectral minimum as a substitute of the norm of the ``inverse'' of that tensor, and study the properties of the spectral minimum of a symmetric tensor. Study some tensor analysis topics for third-order and fourth-order symmetric tensors. Explore practical methods for computing E-determinants when the dimension is two or three. Introduce two new eigenvalue functions, H-index and H-product, and study their relationship with real solvability of real polynomial systems.

501212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
501212.value: 矩阵特征值在矩阵分析的许多研究课题中起一个关键作用。矩阵分析中的几个重要课题都与矩阵特征值紧密相关。例如，对称矩阵的谱半径即为特征值绝对值的最大者；正方矩阵的行列式是其全部特征值之积；而矩阵特征多项式的根恰为其特征值。这些均为矩阵分析中的重要课题。什么是它们在张量分析中的相应课题呢？ 仅在2011年，二个新概念被提出：对称张量的谱半径和正方张量的E-行列式。 在本项目中，我们计划全面研究这二个课题，并引入张量分析中的几个新概念。我们将引入张量范数，并证明对称张量的谱半径即为2-范数。我们还将引入对称张量的谱极小值，并将谱极小值的倒数作为张量逆的范数的替代物。我们还将考虑一些三阶和四阶对称张量的研究课题。对一个三阶和四阶张量，我们将引入四阶积。我们将计划探索一些二维和三维E-行列式的实用计算方法。我们还计划引入二个新的特征值函数：H-指标和H-积。它们均会在实多项式组的实解分析中起重要作用。正定张量的H-指标和H-积总不为零。这是比E-行列式更为显著的。 谱极小值、四阶积、H-指标和H-积均在本项目中首次引进。成功研究这些课题将使张量分析成为和矩阵分析相平行的课目。 线性代数和矩阵分析早已成为各数学分支的基本工具，它们本身又是研究的肥沃领域。在近十年中，数值多重代数和张量分析已成为新的研究领域。张量谱理论的发展证明了这一点。本项目的成功将为这一研究领域构筑一个坚实基础，并将对相关应用领域产生有意义的影响。本项目的成功将在数学理论和应用上都具有意义。

501212.label: Realisation of objectives
501212.value: 1. We studied properties of spectral radius of a high order tensor. We established Fredholm alternative type results for eigenvalues (E-eigenvalues, H-eigenvalues, Z-eigenvalues) of a higher order tensor A. For the positively homogeneous operators FA and TA induced by a higher order tensor A, we showed some relationship between the Gelfand formula and the spectral radius, and present the upper bound of their spectral radii. Furthermore, for a nonnegative tensor A, we obtain the practical relevance for the spectral radius of the operators FA and TA as well as the operator norms of FA and TA. 2. We introduced M-tensors. This concept extends the concept of M-matrices. We denote Z-tensors as the tensors with nonpositive off-diagonal entries. We show that M-tensors must be Z-tensors and the maximal diagonal entry must be nonnegative. The diagonal elements of a symmetric M-tensor must be nonnegative. A symmetric M-tensor is copositive. Based on the spectral theory of nonnegative tensors, we show that the minimal value of the real parts of all eigenvalues of an M-tensor is its smallest H+-eigenvalue and also is its smallest H-eigenvalue. We show that a Z-tensor is an M-tensor if and only if all its H+-eigenvalues are nonnegative. Some further spectral properties of M-tensors are given. We also introduce strong M-tensors, and some corresponding conclusions are given. In particular, we showed that all H-eigenvalues of strong M-tensors are positive. We applied this property to study the positive definiteness of a class of multivariate forms associated with Z-tensors. We also proposed an algorithm for testing the positive definiteness of such a multivariate form. 3. We also introduced Hilbert tensors. Hilbert matrices are a very important matrix class. We extended Hilbert matrices to Hilbert tensors, showed that even order Hilbert tensors are positive definite, and gave an upper bound for the E-spectral radius of a Hilbert tensor. 4. We first showed that the eigenvector of a tensor is well defined. The differences between the eigenvectors of a tensor and its E-eigenvectors are the eigenvectors on the nonsingular projective variety. We showed that a generic tensor has no eigenvectors on S. Actually, we showed that a generic tensor has no eigenvectors on a proper nonsingular projective variety in P^n. By these facts, we showed that the coefficients of the E-characteristic polynomial are algebraically dependent. Actually, a certain power of the determinant of the tensor can be expressed through the coefficients besides the constant term. Hence, a nonsingular tensor always has an E-eigenvector.When a tensor T is nonsingular and symmetric, its E-eigenvectors are exactly the singular points of a class of hypersurfaces defined by T and a parameter. We gave explicit factorization of the discriminant of this class of hypersurfaces which completes Cartwright and Strumfels’ formula.We show that the factorization contains the determinant and the E-characteristic polynomial of the tensor T as irreducible factors. 5. Hankel tensors arise from applications such as signal processing. We made an initial study on Hankel tensors. For each Hankel tensor, we associated a Hankel matrix and a higher order two-dimensional symmetric tensor, which we called the associated plane tensor. If the associated Hankel matrix is positive semi-definite, we call such a Hankel tensor a strong Hankel tensor. We showed that an m order n-dimensional tensor is a Hankel tensor if and only if it has a Vandermonde decomposition. We call a Hankel tensor a complete Hankel tensor if it has a Vandermonde decomposition with positive coefficients. We proved that if a Hankel tensor is copositive or an even order Hankel tensor is positive semi-definite, then the associated plane tensor is copositive or positive semi-definite, respectively. We showed that even order strong and complete Hankel tensors are positive semi-definite, the Hadamard product of two strong Hankel tensors is a strong Hankel tensor, and the Hadamard product of two complete Hankel tensors is a complete Hankel tensor. We showed that all the H-eigenvalues of a complete Hankel tensors (maybe of odd order) are nonnegative. We gave some upper bounds and lower bounds for the smallest and the largest Z-eigenvalues of a Hankel tensor, respectively. Further questions on Hankel tensors are raised. 6. Motivated by symmetric Cauchy matrices, we defined symmetric Cauchy tensors and their generating vectors. Hilbert tensors are symmetric Cauchy tensors. An even order symmetric Cauchy tensor is positive semi-definite if and only if its generating vector is positive. An even order symmetric Cauchy tensor is positive definite if and only if its generating vector has positive and mutually distinct entries. This extends Fiedler's result for symmetric Cauchy matrices to symmetric Cauchy tensors. Then, we proved that the positive semi-definiteness character of an even order symmetric Cauchy tensor can be equivalently checked by the monotone increasing property of a homogeneous polynomial related to the Cauchy tensor. The homogeneous polynomial is strictly monotone increasing in the nonnegative orthant of the Euclidean space when the even order symmetric Cauchy tensor is positive definite. Bounds of the largest H-eigenvalue of a positive semi-definite symmetric Cauchy tensor were given and several spectral properties on Z-eigenvalues of odd order symmetric Cauchy tensors are shown. 7. We gave a necessary and sufficient condition for an even order three dimensional strongly symmetric circulant tensor to be positive semi-definite. We showed that this condition can be a sufficient condition for such a tensor to be sum-of-squares in some cases. 8. A symmetric positive semi-definite (PSD) tensor, which is not sum-of-squares (SOS), is called a PSD non-SOS (PNS) tensor. Is there a fourth order four dimensional PNS Hankel tensor? The answer for this question has both theoretical and practical significance. Under the assumptions that the generating vector v of a Hankel tensor A is symmetric and the fifth element v4 of v is fixed at 1, we showed that there are two surfaces M0 and N0 with the elements v2, v6, v1, v3, v5 of v as variables, such that M0 ≥ N0, A is SOS if and only if v0 ≥ M0, and A is PSD if and only if v0 ≥ N0, where v0 is the first element of v. If M0 = N0 for a point P = (v2, v6, v1, v3, v5)⊤, there are no fourth order four dimensional PNS Hankel tensors with symmetric generating vectors for such v2, v6, v1, v3, v5. Then, we call such P a PNS-free point. We prove that a 45-degree planar closed convex cone, a segment, a ray and an additional point are PNS-free. Numerical tests check various grid points and report that they are all PNS-free. 9. We also applied spectral theory of tensors to hypergraphs and directed hypergraphs.

501512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
501512.value: 大氣中的反應性氮氧化物包括一氧化氮、二氧化氮及其眾多的反應中間體和產物。它們在大氣化學、生物地球化學迴圈以及全球氣候變化中均扮演重要角色,也與光化學煙霧、灰霾、酸沉降以及富營養化等當前主要的環境污染問題密切相關。五氧化二氮(N2O5)是氮氧化物重要的反應中間體之一。國際最新研究表明, N2O5在顆粒物表面的非均相水解機制非常複雜,其水解速率和ClNO2(關鍵水解產物之一)產率均隨氣溶膠理化性質高度變化但內在規律尚不清楚。這些化學過程對目前許多城市(包括香港)所面臨的大氣光化學污染具有重要影響。 在本项目中,我們擬使用併發展目前國際先進的化學離子化質譜儀(CIMS)以測量大氣中的N2O5和ClNO2,然後在香港開展觀測實驗並進行初步的模式分析。本專案將認識華南地區高污染大氣環境中N2O5的非均相水解機制及其對地面臭氧生成的影響。本研究致力於填補當前國際上十分活躍的N2O5大氣化學研究在亞洲高污染地區的空白,相應的研究成果可應用於改進現有空氣品質模式的類比性能,也可為香港開展光化學煙霧控制提供科學支撐。

501512.label: Major findings and research outcome
501512.value: (1)Atmospheric N2O5 and ClNO2 data were measured at Hok Tsui in Hong Kong from 17 August to 20 December 2012. Despite the high levels of precursors, moderate mixing ratios of NO3-N2O5 (with a maximum of 434 pptv) were observed, indicating fast loss and high reactivity. Further analysis revealed a very fast heterogeneous uptake rate of N2O5 (~0.0023 s-1) at the site. An average N2O5 uptake coefficient of 0.038 was estimated from the observational data, which is among the upper range of the previously-reported values. The fast heterogeneous uptake was consistent with the observation of ClNO2. A clear diurnal pattern of ClNO2 was observed with mixing ratio up to 1997 pptv, which is among the highest values ever reported in the world. The elevated ClNO2 mixing ratios were observed in plumes from Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta region compared to the lower levels in maritime air. (2) A comprehensive Cl chemistry module that can be directly incorporated within the MCM framework was developed to assess the impact of N2O5 heterogeneous chemistry. By constraining the observational ClNO2 into the model, significant enhancement of in situ O3 production was found, with increases of 33.7 and 10.3% in the early morning and daytime average (08:00–18:00) net O3 production rates respectively. Our results suggest that N2O5 heterogeneous chemistry was efficient and can significantly increase the ground-level ozone in Hong Kong. (3) Laboratory and field studies found that the N2O5 measurement with a thermal dissociation chemical ionization mass spectrometer (TD-CIMS) subjected to interference from PAN and NO2, which could have contributed to 30–50% of the average daytime N2O5+NO3 signal observed at a polluted site in Hong Kong. The CIMS was reconfigured to an unheated version that detects N2O5 and ClNO2 as iodide-adduct cluster ion which is believed to be free of interferences. The CIMS was optimized and compared with the cavity ring-down spectroscopy technique, and the results indicate that our improved CIMS method is capable of measuring N2O5 and ClNO2 accurately under Hong Kong conditions. The research findings of this project were published in four journal papers; one full-time PhD student (Yun Hui) was trained for one year with the support of the project. The project also supported a research assistant (Tham Yee Jun, a part-time PhD student at PolyU during the period), and some findings of this research were published in his PhD thesis (degree awarded in March 2017).

501512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
501512.value: This is the first study of my group on heterogeneous processes of N2O5. The research area has been further developed to another GRF project and a CRF project.

501512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
501512.value: Reactive oxidised nitrogen compounds, which include NOx (NO + NO2) and their reaction intermediates/products, play key roles in atmospheric chemistry, biogeochemical cycle, and climate. They are also directly linked to environmental pollution problems such us photochemical smog, haze, acid deposition, and eutrophication. Dinitrogen pentoxide (N2O5) is a reactive intermediate of NOx. Recent studies have revealed large knowledge gaps in quantifying loss of N2O5 on aerosol surface and subsequent production of highly reactive chlorine radical. These processes may significantly influence the formation of ozone, a photochemical air pollutant in world’s major cities, including Hong Kong. In this study, we modified and applied state-of-the-art chemical ionization mass spectrometry to measure atmospheric concentrations of N2O5 and ClNO2 and other key species in Hong Kong, then conducted modeling analysis of the data. The findings have improved understanding loss of N2O5 and production of Cl in a polluted coastal area of South China (Hong Kong) and their impact on the formation of ground-level ozone. This study has developed some critical experimental and modeling techniques which laid foundation for further development of this research area. The knowledge and technique have also been transferred to the Hong Kong Environmental Protection Department to support local air quality management.

501612.label: Project Objectives
501612.value: To deposit high quality thin films of iron-based superconducting compounds (BaFe2-xCoxAs2, Fe(Se,Te), Sm-1111, La-1111) on single crystal substrates (STO, LSAT and piezoelectric ones such as PMN-PT etc) by pulsed laser ablation method. Thin films deposited under optimized processing conditions should be well crystallized and highly oriented with controllable orientations. To characterize the crystal structure of the thin films by x-ray diffraction, atomic force microscope and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy and to investigate how the crystal structure may change when the thin films are subjected to lateral stress generated by the piezoelectric effect in the substrates. To characterize the physical properties of the thin films under different stress conditions and to correlate the magnetic and superconductive behaviors of the thin films with their crystal structures (in particular the anion layer height and Fe-As angle). To investigate the relationship among structure, magnetism and superconductivity as well as the origin of the nematic state in the underdoped region by using the external voltage on the fabricated Fe-SCs/piezoelectric heterostrcuture to vary the crystal lattice of the piezoelectric substrate through the anti-piezoelectric, and thus to tune the microstructure of the Fe-SCs thin film, such as the bond length of Fe-As, the bond angle of the As-Fe-As and Fe-As-Fe. To develop a physical picture through experimental results and theoretical analysis, to interpret the mechanism of superconductivity in iron compounds and to make comparison of it with that in cuprate superconductors.

501612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
501612.value: In 2008 Kamihara et al first reported superconductivity in polycrystalline LaO1-xFxFeAs. Since then there has been extensive interest to develop new iron-based superconductors (Fe-SCs) and investigate the mechanism of superconductivity in these compounds. While most of the research in the literature has been focusing on bulk form of the compounds, this project aims at developing thin films of Fe-SCs and investigating the effect of dynamic lattice tuning on their physical properties. BaFe2-xCoxAs2 (BFCA) is chosed as the main system in the study because plenty of studies on BFCA bulk crystals have demonstrated that the physical properties of this system are sensitive to subtle distortion of the structure in the underdoped region. The experimental part of the project will first involve the deposition of BFCA thin films with desired compositions and crystal structures by means of laser molecular beam epitaxy. Structures of the deposited thin films will be characterized and physical properties (including electron transport behaviors under different conditions, magnetic properties and etc) will be determined. Based on the experimental results an optimized processing condition for producing high-quality thin films could be achieved. The second part involves development of epitaxial BFCA thin films on piezoelectric single crystal substrates (lead magnesium nibate – PMNT and etc) and investigation of impact of lattice symmetry on superconducting behaviors in the thin films. Due to the piezoelectric effect, the single crystal substrate would undergo a lattice distortion (up to ~ 1% for PMNT) upon the application of an external voltage, which could induce symmetry change in the thin film via mechanical coupling and in turn could have impact on the electrical transport properties in BFCA. Through in-situ structural characterization and electrical measurements under different strain levels, an direct observation of the structure-property relationship could be achieved, which could help a better understanding of the origin of the superconductivity in the thin films. Once the above materials have been successfully developed, the research may be extended to the development and characterization of other Fe-SC thin films, such as other 122 systems and 1111 as well as the 11 systems. The idea of this project is thought to be original since there is not yet an in-depth and systematic investigation of the kind. We anticipate that the output from this research will benefit the local research in applied physics and materials science. 2008年Kamihara等人首次報道LaO1-xFxFeAs多晶體系具有超導特性，隨後尋找鐵基超導體並研究超導機制成為一個廣受重視的課題。在文獻中報道的研究工作多數針對塊體材料，而本課題則主要研究鐵基超導薄膜以及其超導特性與晶格的關系。BaFe2-xCoxAs2 (BFCA)將是本課題的主要研究對像，原因是其物理性質對晶格變形非常敏感。本課題將開展的實驗部分包括利用激光分子束外延的方法生長BFCA薄膜，並分析其結構、測量其物理性能（特別是在各種外加電、磁場條件下的電輸運性質）。在此基礎上，將薄膜生長到壓電單晶（鈮鎂酸鉛等）襯底上，以研究晶格對稱性隊薄膜的超導行為的影響。其基本原理是單晶襯底存在壓電效應，在電場作用下可以產生一定程度的晶格變形（對鈮鎂酸鉛而言，相對變形量可達2%），從而導致BCFA薄膜對稱性的改變,進而改變其電學性質。這一原理和方法，也可以推廣到其他的鐵基超導體系（122，1111和11體系等等）。本課題的研究思路具有原創性，我們期望通過該課題的研究可以推動本地應用物理研究的發展。

501612.label: Realisation of objectives
501612.value: 1. Optimized processing conditions for making high quality films have been achieved. Pulse laser ablation method was employed in the experiments. The deposition of As-based compounds was rather a challenge due to the highly active nature of As. Nevertheless, through control experiments with variation of processing parameters (vacuum, temperature and etc), it was found that the deposition temperature is the most critical factor that determines the quality of films and a very narrow “window” of deposition temperature was identified through which the deposited films exhibited best properties. For FeSe systems, the deposition was also difficult but the thin film structure and quality was less sensitive to the deposition of As-based systems. 2. The structures of deposited thin films were characterized by means of x-ray diffraction, atomic force microscope and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy. It was found that thin films deposited under optimized processing conditions show a good quality of crystallization and epitaxial nature. 3. The physical properties of the thin films were determined on PPMS. The thin films prepared under optimized conditions exhibited superconducting behaviors at how temperatures. The transition temperature for FeBaCoAs system was ~15K and that for the FeSeTe system was ~8K. The results are consistent with data in literature. 4. Influence of the substrate effect on the physical properties of the thin films was studied. The transition temperature of Fe-based SCs was found to vary for a magnitude of about 7K upon the change of stress state. For the FeSe system, the poling state of the substrate was found to lead to the change of the transition temperature of ~ 2K. 5. The change of superconducting transition temperature (Tc) with bond angle in iron-pnictides was investigated by first-principles calculation based on density functional theory. A Green's function method was adopted to estimate the maxim umeigen value of Eliashberg equation (an indicator of Tc) for NaFeAs with different bond angles. Through calculations the band structure of NaFeAs was obtained. It was found that hole pockets could format the center of the first Brillion zone in the band structure, which confirmed the existence of superconductivity in NaFeAs. The upper limit of the Fe–As–Fe bond angle for superconductivity was found to be 121° and the highest Tc would occur at the angle of 108°.

501612.label: Major findings and research outcome
501612.value: Major findings of the project: 1) Optimized processing conditions for producing Fe-based superconductive (Fe-SC) thin films on buffer-free substrates were obtained (in literature, high quality Fe-SC thin films are only available on buffered substrates) and the deposition temperature was identified as the critical parameter that influences the thin film structure. 2) The influence of band angle on the superconducting transition temperature was confirmed. 3) The influences of piezoelectric substrate on the properties of the thin films were disclosed. A group of data to demonstrate the finds have been obtained. 4) Four journal papers have been published while three more are in preparation.

501612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
501612.value: The thin film/piezoelectric substrate is a common structure for the study of structure-property relationship in functional thin films. While the project focuses on superconducting thin films, it also inspires us on other material families (e.g. half-metal magnetic materials) in which the electron behaviors play critical roles on materials properties and are therefore sensitive to substrate as well.

501612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
501612.value: Superconductors are an interesting family of materials that show zero-resistance to electrical currents and are thus potentially useful for electronic circuits, electrical engineering and etc. The superconducting behaviors were found in materials from metals (e.g. Nb) to oxides (e.g. YBCO), and iron-based compounds are a new group of members to this material family. For both basic and applied point of view, it is important to investigate how the transition temperature (i.e. the temperature at which the material becomes superconducting) of Fe-based superconductors could be modified through material structural changes. In this project, thin films of Fe-superconductors were deposition on single crystal structures. As the substrates possess a unique ferroelectric/piezoelectric property – i.e., the material’s size would change upon the application of an electrical field, it is possible to pass a stress to the thin film and consequently change the transition temperature. This idea was carefully examined in this project, through experiments and theoretical studies and the results are very encouraging. This research paves a new way to develop superconducting thin films with higher transition temperatures.

502012.value: Celebesides、Lagunamides的全合成及其类似物的生物学活性研究

502012.label: Co - Investigator(s)
502012.value: Prof Deng, Hongkui Prof Zhang, Hui

502012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
502012.value: Marine organisms have yielded a diverse array of biologically active molecules that could eventually be developed into therapeutic agents. Structure elucidation of increasingly limited quantities of components from marine natural product extracts heavily rely on advanced nano-scale NMR technologies. Chemical degradation and derivatization were somewhat less involved. Literature precedent suggested that a large number of structural mis-assignments were made in relatively recent years. Total synthesis plays a critical role in marine natural product structure elucidation and also provides materials for biological testing towards pharmaceutical development. Our present studies focus on newly isolated marine cyclodepsipeptides called celebesides and lagunamides. Biological studies of celebeside A indicated that it neutralized HIV-1 in a single-round infectivity assay with an IC50 value of 1.9 μg/mL. Lagunamides A & B displayed potent cytotoxic activity against P388 murine leukemia cell lines, with IC50 values of 6.4 and 20.5 nM, respectively. Structurally, both celebesides and lagunamides are unusual 26-membered cyclodepsipeptides that comprise a polyketide moiety and five amino acid residues. Celebesides A contains an uncommon 3-carbamoyl threonine, an isoserine and a phosphoserine residue, while lagunamides A & B are comprised of three N-methyl amino acids. The absolute stereochemisry of the polyketide moiety in celebesides was not assigned. Preliminary results from our laboratory indicated that at least one of the proposed stereogenic centers of langunamides, probably located at the polyketide fragment, needs to be revised. The important biological properties of these cyclodepsipeptides and their natural scarcity, coupled with their intriguing molecular architecture, render them attractive synthetic targets for further development. To the best of our knowledge, no complete total synthesis of any member of the celebesides or lagunamides has been reported yet. The long-term goal of this research is to develop highly effective agents either having cytoprotective activity against HIV-1 in vitro by inhibiting viral entry or capable of inducing cancer cell apoptosis, through molecular design, chemical synthesis and biological testing of analogues of the celebesides and lagunamides. We are directing our efforts to establish the absolute stereochemistry of celebesides and lagunamides and construction of key analogues by organic synthesis, employing strategies and methods that can be modified for the preparation of analogues. 502412.label: Project Objectives
502412.value: Introduce the dynamic mean-field optimizations in the setup of probability measure uncertainty, for the first time, to our best knowledge. Develop some new stochastic maximum principle (MP) to the optimization problems proposed in 1. Based on 1. and 2., formulate and study some dynamic large-population optimization problems under measure uncertainty. 502412.label: Realisation of objectives
502412.value: (1) We investigate the dynamic mean-field optimizations with measure uncertainty. In absolute continuous measure uncertainty case, the related mean-field optimization can be connected to the classical model uncertainty with drift terms added and controlled. The associated optimal control is obtained in both soft and hard constraint setting. For the hard constraint, the Lagrange multiplier method is introduced with the convexity-concavity principle. The related optimal control is obtained via some Lagrange multiplier which depends on the unspecified consistency condition (CC) variable. By state averaging technique, we obtained the CC variable through a two-dimensional FBSDE systems. In soft-constraint case, we discussed the associated large-population optimization with deterministic drift disturbance. The related CC system is characterized by two sequential FBSDE systems. The optimal control is derived via maximum principle and Hamiltonian system. (2) We develop some new type maximum principle to above two constraints (hard, soft). The related pertubation method is introduced and Hamiltonian system is framed with new adjoint-state equation. We also discuss the related variants of our models such as the general integral system with mean-field game, or stochastic delayed system. We also discuss the relevant decoupling method to Hamiltonian system via Riccati equation which is not standard as some terms are intrinsically negative-positive. Thus, the wellposedness of related Riccati equation should be carefully investigated. To this end, we derive some checkable rank condition. (3) We also study the large-population system with model uncertainty, applying the methods and results given in (1) and (2). We obtained the mean-field decentralized strategy with given characters (e.g., stochastic delay, input constraint, or future state constraint or backward state with BSDE modeling, etc.). The approximate Nash equilibrium of our strategies are also verified with given state and functional estimations. (4) As the by-product, we also derive some large-deviation principle for mean-field game system. This provide some useful estimate to our large-population system with mean-field game analysis.

502412.label: Major findings and research outcome
502412.value: We find the basic relation between Lagrange multiplier to the measure uncertainty with hard and soft constraints. For the hard constraint, some smooth condition should be imposed to derive the characterization of minimum point. As to the soft constraint, some sequential optimization procedure is formatted and analyzed. we also propose some checkable condition to the convexity of underlying control and game problems. We put more focus on the soft constraint with robust disturbance. This is connected to the measure uncertainty with deterministic Radon¡VNikodym derivative. The related optimal controller is designed through some FBSDE system and two-point boundary system. We give some wellposedness results by monotonicity condition or discounting method. The related criteria is presented in given several papers. We also characterize the consistency condition via FBSDE and its state-average by conditional expectation operators. We also propose some new approximate Nash equilibrium definition under current measure uncertainty. Unlike classical approximate Nash equilibrium, the current definition is defined under robust or worse-case sense. Accordingly, the verification is under some perturbation under a family of possible measures. The related estimation is proceeded for give a family FBSDE in our analysis. As supporting result, we also discuss mean-field game of stochastic integral system, backward stochastic system (this is very closed to the terminal constraint under model uncertainty), or stochastic delayed system. The related CC condition and approximate Nash equilibriums are all developed. We also discuss some real application in portfolio selection with model uncertainty and relative performance.

502412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
502412.value: (1) One direction is the discussion of robust mean-field game with risk-sensitive mean-field game. It is well known that risk sensitive control can be connected to robust control via some entropy constraint. By this, it is also interesting to discuss the parallel relation of them in mean-field game setup for large-population system. (2) As another direction, it is also necessary to study the model uncertainty of large-population system with singular measures. Our current project is focusing on model uncertainty with absolute continuity. However, another important class is the measure uncertainty with singular measure family. To this end, an interesting formulation is to consider the large-population with G-expectation setup, which provides a powerful framework to model the singular measure uncertainty.

502412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
502412.value: Large-population system is very important in various fields from economics, finance, biology to management or operational research. such system is very depending on the underlying (probability) measure governing the evolution of state and functional. It is very common for the uncertainty of probability measure thus our project discuss how to analyze the large-population system with measure t. We discuss the absolute measure t with both hard and soft constraints. The related Lagrange multiplier is derived and consistency condition is obtained via maximum principle. We also get the related decoupling of Hamiltonian system with Riccati equation. Due to measure uncertainty, the optimization is in robust sense thus the weight is not positive definitive. Therefore, some new wellposedness condition is introduced to ensure the solution of Riccati equation and related state-average system. Our project provides some theoretical analysis for an important large-population system. It also provide some door for new applications as measure uncertainty is observed often in various fields and it is well documented in various practical applications. Our project also suggests some interesting extension to more general analysis such as mean-field game with singular measure uncertainty, or the structural relation of robust control and risk-sensitive control in large-population setting.

502512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
502512.value: 量子信息科學－量子糾錯

502512.label: Project Objectives
502512.value: Develop mathematical techniques to find new quantum error correcting codes. After Shor has presented his first example of quantum error correcting code, lots of papers on quantum error correction have been published. Most of these results describe specific examples of codes on certain quantum systems, and these codes constructed so far in literature mostly are stabilizer codes. The aim of this project is to develop a new mathematical framework through an operator theoretical approach so as to provide different view to the study of quantum error correction. The research team will explore all possible applications of operator quantum error correction, in particular, the unitary recovery operation scheme recently proposed by the investigator and his collaborators will be one of the platforms in this study. Provide practical and operational quantum error correcting schemes. With experience in matrix and operator theory, the investigator will explore new quantum error correcting schemes as well as improve and generalize some of those existing schemes. The investigator will collaborate with experimentalists and practitioners so that the research team will focus on important problems and explore the possibility of experimental realization for the schemes investigated. The long term goal is to provide simple, practical, and operational schemes to experimentalists and develop new mathematical techniques with wide applicability in quantum error correction. Details of research problems will be mentioned in research plan and methodology. Promote the quantum error correction and other related problems to matrix and operator algebras community. Matrix and operator theory definitely plays an important role in the development of quantum error correction. For instance, the classical Kinll-Laflamme result employs higher rank projection operators in finite dimensional Hilbert space. Exclusively, problems in quantum error correction can also be viewed as a pure mathematical problem in matrix analysis. However, it was observed that most experts from matrix and operator algebras community were not aware of the importance of these problems in quantum information science. This situation may be due to the lack of communication and the different notations and descriptions used between the two communities. Quantum information science is a highly interdisciplinary research area, and hence it is important for researchers from different areas to work together. Another long term goal of our project is to build up a network between mathematicians, especially matrix and operator algebraists, and quantum information scientists so that more mathematicians can be involved in the development of theoretical aspect of quantum error correction. Also, the investigator will involve postdoctoral fellows, postgraduate and undergraduate students in the project so as to build up the workforce in quantum information science.

502512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
502512.value: Quantum information science is a rapidly growing research area. It concerns the study of data storage, transmission, and processing using quantum properties. In particular, researchers are very keen at building a quantum computer to store and process information using quantum states referred to as quantum bits, abbreviated as qubits. One of the most well known processes involving quantum information is quantum computation. If a practical quantum computer is built, it will be able to run quantum algorithms, which can solve problems much more efficiently than the digital computers (using binary bits). However, quantum systems are vulnerable to disturbance from an external environment, which will lead to decoherence in the system. Researchers and engineers have to overcome this difficulty in order to build a working quantum computer to achieve dependable quantum information processing. The idea of quantum error correction is to protect quantum information from errors due to decoherence and other quantum noise during the transmission of information in quantum channels. After Shor and Steane proposed their first examples on how data could be redundantly encoded and recovered in quantum states of a quantum system, this research topic took flight in the last two decades by many researchers, and different approaches such as group theoretical approach, coding theoretical approach, geometric approach, etc, have been developed in this study. One fundamental question of quantum error correction is the existence of quantum error correcting code for a noisy quantum system. Moreover, constructing practical and operational quantum error correcting schemes in actual quantum computing is of great interest to quantum information scientists. Since Hilbert space theory is the theoretical basis of quantum information theory, the research team will investigate these problems through a matrix and operator theoretical approach. The investigator will establish mathematical techniques to find quantum error correcting codes for different quantum channels. Moreover, practical and effective implementation schemes will be suggested for the proposed quantum error correcting codes. The theory and the proposed schemes will be verified numerically and experimentally by the investigator, his collaborators, and other experimentalists. Computer algorithms will be developed for detecting and constructing new correcting codes and quantum circuits. Furthermore, the investigator will collaborate with experimentalists and practitioners so that the research team will focus on important and useful problems in the area. In summary, this project will lead to important new theoretical results, novel proof techniques, and practical implementation schemes in quantum error correction. 量子信息科學為現今一個迅速發展的科學研究課題。其以量子力學理論為基礎，發展更有效存儲、傳送和處理數據的方案。研究人員冀能設計及構建量子計算機（量子電腦），以存儲和處理以量子位元作為單位的量子信息。與現今電腦科技（使用二進制位）相比，量子計算機能更有效地解決一些複雜的運算問題。然而，由於量子系統容易受到從外在環境干擾而產生消相干現象，因此研究人員和工程師必須克服此問題，才能建造可靠的量子計算機。量子糾錯主要為糾正信息在量子通道傳送過程中因消相干現象及其他干擾所產生的錯誤。從肖爾（Shor）和史甸（Steane）提出第一個量子編碼及解碼例子後，這課題在過去的二十年發展一日千里，當中研究人員透過引進不同數學工具如幾何、組合理論、群論、編碼理論等，得出多方面的研究成果。 研究領域中一個基本問題，是在不同噪聲量子系統中有否存在量子糾錯碼。量子信息科學家希望了解能否構建可操作及實用的量子糾錯碼，以應用於量子計算機。由於量子信息理論是建基於希爾伯特空間理論上，研究小組將通過矩陣和算子理論研究這課題，於不同的量子通道中尋找其量子糾錯碼，並設計糾錯碼的量子電路圖。此外，研究員會聯同其他實驗人員以數學模型和實驗方式驗證所提出的理論及設計，同時亦會編寫電腦程式以建構新糾錯碼和量子電路圖，當中研究將專注於較為重要和有應用性的問題。綜上所述，此研究項目冀望能於量子糾錯方面取得新理論成果、證明技術及實行方案。

502512.label: Realisation of objectives
502512.value: The first two objectives of this project are to develop mathematical techniques to find quantum error correcting codes and provide practical and operational quantum error correcting schemes. In this project, the PI successfully achieved these goals and obtained many mathematical results in quantum error correction. The research team first proposed a recursive encoding and decoding scheme for a noiseless subsystem for qudits [Paper 3 in Pact C: Research Output]. They then also studied the collective rotation channels on qudits and determined the maximal noiseless code rates of these channels [Paper 5]. To study quantum error correction, one approach is to consider a related mathematical tool, generalized numerical range, in particular, the higher rank numerical range. The PI and his postdoctoral fellow, Dr. Pan Shun Lau, considered some geometrical properties, i.e., convexity and star-shapedness, of higher rank numerical range, matricial range and the numerical range of matrix sets [Papers 9 and 10] and obtained some new determinantal and eigenvalue inequalities in connection to the classical numerical range [Paper 1]. The PI also obtained other results in degradability of quantum states [Paper 2], time-energy costs of quantum channels [Paper 4], tensor products of rank one matrices [Paper 6], the product of positive semi-definite matrices [Paper 7], and unitary similarity invariant functions [Paper 8]. These results have been published in international peer-viewed journals and have been cited by other researchers in mathematics and physics communities. These results have also been presented in various meetings, workshops, and conferences. The third objective of this project is to promote the quantum error correction and other related problems to matrix and operator algebras community. The PI has achieved this goal by organizing workshops in Hong Kong, attending international conferences and workshops, and visit other institutions. During this project period, a series of three workshops on quantum information science was held in December 2012, January 2014, and December 2014 respectively, and more than forty scholars from Australia, Canada, China, Japan, Korea, Singapore, and the USA joined the event and shared their works. In particular, the PI have built up a strong collaboration with Professor Mikio Nakahara and his Ph.D. student, Utkan Gungordu, of Kinki University, Japan and have a joint project on quantum error correction [Papers 3 and 5]. The PI also worked with another physicist, Professor Hoi-Fung Chau of The University Hong Kong on the topics of degradability and time-energy costs [Papers 2 and 4] and Professor Jianlian Cui of Tsinghua University on the projects of unitary similarity invariant function and product of positive semi-definite matrices [Papers 7 and 8]. For training young researchers, a postdoctoral fellow, Dr. Pan Shun Lau, was recruited in this project. Lau has contributed in various parts of this project and is one of the co-authors of two published papers [Papers 9 and 10] in this project.

502512.label: Major findings and research outcome
502512.value: In this project, the PI obtained results in the area of quantum error correction. First, the PI gave a full explanation of the noiseless subsystem that protects a single qubit against collective errors and the corresponding recursive scheme described by a previous result of PI with his collaborators [Phys. Rev. A 84, 044301 (2011)] from a representation theory point of view, see [Paper 3 in Part C: Research Output]. Next, the PI with his collaborators studied noiseless subsystems on collective rotation channels of qudits. They reviewed the results for the channels on qubits and obtained the maximum dimension of the noiseless subsystem that can be used as the quantum error correction code for the channel, and extended the results to general qudit system, see [Paper 5]. The PI also studied generalized numerical range, which has a close connection with quantum error correction. The PI and his postdoctoral fellow Lau, with their collaborators, showed that the higher rank numerical range and the (p,q)-th matricial range are always star-shaped when the dimension of the system is sufficiently large [Paper 9]. They further showed that the numerical range of the matrix set that is generated by two generators is always star-shaped too [Paper 10]. The PI also solved a conjecture proposed by Drury concerning some determinantal and eigenvalue inequalities for matrices with numerical ranges in a sector [Paper 1]. The PI also considered other problems related to quantum states and quantum channels. He has considered the problem of degradability of states, which is different from that of quantum channels. Necessary and sufficient conditions for state degradability are proved and an efficient method to quickly rule out degradability for a given state is provided [Paper 2]. Next, the PI derived a formula for the time-energy costs of general quantum channels, which was proposed by Chau in [Phys. Rev. A 88, 012307 (2018)]. A lower bound to the time-energy cost for any channels and the exact cost for a class of channels which includes the qudit depolarizing channels and projector channels are derived [Paper 4]. Other related results, such as tensor products of rank one matrices [Paper 6], the product of positive semi-definite matrices [Paper 7], and unitary similarity invariant functions [Paper 8], were also obtained in this project.

502512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
502512.value: With the successful collaboration built during this project, the PI will continue to work with physicists and quantum information scientists in various research areas in quantum error correction and generalized numerical ranges. In particular, based on the theatrical framework proposed in this project, one of the future investigation directions is to explore all possible applications of this operator quantum error correction, in particular in qutrit and general qudit systems. The PI will continue to explore new quantum error correcting schemes as well as improve and generalize some of those existing schemes. Also the PI will explore other properties of generalized numerical ranges and matricial ranges, in particular, higher numerical range and (p,q)-th matricial range, which are motivated by quantum error correction and operator quantum error correction, respectively.

502512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
502512.value: Quantum information science is a rapidly growing research area. It concerns the study of data storage, transmission, and processing using quantum properties. The idea of quantum error correction is to protect quantum information from errors due to decoherence and other quantum noise during the transmission of information in quantum channels. In this project, the research team investigated the so-called noiseless subsystem of a quantum system that protects a single qubit (quantum bit) against collective errors and reviewed and proposed a recursive encoding and decoding scheme for such subsystem in a qudit system (a quantum system described by a superposition of d quantum state where d is an integer greater than two). The research team also determined the maximal noiseless code rates of these channels, that is the maximal dimension of the noiseless subsystem that can be used as quantum error correction code for the collective channel. The research team also studied a mathematical tool called generalized numerical range of matrices, which has a close connection with quantum error correction. They obtained some important properties for two types of generalized numerical ranges when the dimension of the matrices is sufficiently large. 502912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
502912.value: Direct formic acid fuel cell converts efficiently and directly chemical energy stored in liquid fuel into electrical energy through electrochemical reaction which shows great applications in portable electronics and electric vehicles. During this operation, formic acid and oxygen are continuously fed to the fuel cell to generate electricity with the production of carbon dioxide and water as sole products. Formic acid as a fuel has a number of superior properties including high energy density, high theoretical cell potential, high conversion rate and inflammability. Owing to recent technological advances, formic acid can now be produced renewably by fermentation of plant based carbohydrates or by using renewable energy driven electrochemical conversion of carbon dioxide which make it a green energy carrier. The main hurdle for commercialization of fuel cell is the strong reliance on expensive and rare platinum metal as catalyst. This proposal aims to investigate a facile and up-scalable synthetic routes towards gold/platinum and silver/platinum composite catalyst to greatly reduce platinum usage while enhancing the catalytic activity and lifetime. Recently, we developed an electrocatalyst that is composed of carbon nanotubes supported gold nanoparticles coated with a mono to a few atomic layers of platinum islands with an overall platinum loading of 0.3%. This gold/platinum composite serves as a bifunctional catalyst with outstanding specific activity towards formic acid oxidation and oxygen reduction. The enhancement is mainly attributed to the confinement of platinum to stay on the gold nanoparticles surface for maximum utilization in contrast to the large amount of encapsulated platinum atoms which is inactive for platinum nanoparticles. A similar silver/platinum hollow sphere was also prepared with highly increased surface area due to the hollow structures which also shows outstanding formic acid electrocatalytic activity. As both preparations rely on the surface decoration of platinum with the core gold or silver nanostructure, we proposed by preparing different gold and silver core nanostructures for later platinum modification, the catalytic activity, stability and selectivity towards formic acid and oxygen can further be improved. This is because different cores will be exposed to different specific surface with different platinum adsorption selectivity and results in different coverage and activity. Apart from the catalyst itself, the effect of replacing the commonly used carbon support with metal nanooxides will also be studied. We believe that by altering the surface functionalities, the stability and also ion exchange rate of the electrode in either acidic or basic electrolyte will be increased. 甲酸燃料電池是一種能直接而有效地將儲存在液體燃料中的能量轉化成電能的裝置，因而被公認將應用於未來的可擕式電子設備和電動車輛上。在轉化過程中甲酸和空氣不斷輸入燃料電池發電從而只排出二氧化碳和水而不會產生污染。甲酸作為一種燃料擁有很多優點，當中包括高能量密度、 高理論電位、 高轉換率和低易燃性。由於最近的技術進步，甲酸現在已可通過發酵植物中碳水化合物或使用再生能源將二氧化碳電轉化而大量生產，使甲酸成為一種綠色的可再生液體燃料。可是由於制造燃料電池需大量昂貴和稀有的金屬鉑作催化劑而使其商業化變得十分困難。因此，這項建議將調查以簡單而可大量制備的方法制作金/鉑和銀/鉑的複合物作催化劑，希望在提高催化活性和壽命的同時時能大大降低鉑的使用量。最近，我們開發出以附載在碳納米管的金納米粒子上包覆單層原子厚的鉑小島作催化劑而使整體鉑含量降低致0.3%。研究發現此金/鉑複合物表現出傑出的甲酸氧化和氧還原的雙功能催化效能。增強的主要原因是鉑原子被固定在金表面上而使所有鉑原子均能有效地應用，與一般鉑納米粒子只有表面的原子處於活性狀態下大為不同。另外，我們亦制作出類似的銀/鉑空心納米球，以空心結構增加表面面積而提高其甲酸電催化活性。由於這兩種複合物均為鉑表面修飾金或銀核心的納米結構，因此我們提議研究以不同的金和銀核心納米結構以制作不同鉑表面修飾的催化劑，希望因此能提高催化劑的活性、 穩定性和改進對甲酸和氧選擇性。這是因為不同形貌的內核將表現出不同的原子排列的晶面，使我們能研究鉑原子吸附選擇性和在不同的覆蓋後催化劑的活性改變。除了催化劑的本身外，我們亦會研究不同的電極基質以取代常用的碳基電極。我們相信通過改變基質表面功能團，將能提高催化劑在酸性或鹼性電解質中的穩定性和離子交換率。

502912.label: Realisation of objectives
502912.value: This project mainly aims to develop two classes of bimetallic catalyst namely Pt/Au and Pt/Ag. A series of Au and Ag nanostructures were prepared to act as core for later decoration of Pt onto the surfaces through different approaches to yield precisely controlled mixed metal nanostructures. Pt/Au nanostructure Based on the high affinity of halide ions on Au surface, submonolayers of Pt was decorated onto the surface of Au nanostructure by our newly developed method called ions adsorption and in situ electrochemical reduction. First, Au nanoparticles were loaded onto the surface of acid-treated multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) to yield a Au/MWCNTs composite. Ions adsorption was then accomplished by immersing the Au/MWCNTs composite in 0.1M H2SO4 containing K2PtCl4 or K2PtCl6 of different concentrations followed by washing with water. Finally, Au@Pt/MWCNTs composite was obtained via in-situ electrochemical reduction of the adsorbed Pt ions. Our results indicated the Pt submonolayer at the Au surface with coverage of 20% - 90% could be readily controlled by either varying the concentration of Pt ions used or by consecutive adsorption and in situ electrochemical reduction. The slope of this corresponding plotting of CV measured Au and Pt surface area change were found to be 1 for a series of ion adsorption–in situ electrochemical reduction which demonstrate the submonolayers formation. The other structural and chemical identity of the Au@Pt/CNTs were further confirmed by XRD, HRTEM with SAED, SEM with EDX and XPS. The coverage of Pt on the Au surface shows a significant influence on the electrocatalytic behavior of Au@Pt/MWCNTs. The electrocatalytic activities of the Au@Pt/CNTs composite towards methanol and formic acid oxidations were found to be highly dependent on Pt coverage. Au@Pt/CNTs with 27.9% Pt coverage showed excellent activity toward formic acid oxidation, while there was no activity towards methanol oxidation. In contrast, Au@Pt/CNTs with 57.6% Pt coverage exhibited activity for both formic acid and methanol oxidation. Furthermore, catalyst with lower Pt coverage showed excellent performance for methanol tolerant ORR catalysis since it was inactive towards methanol. The specific area activity of ORR showed a two-fold enhancement when compared to the Pt Black. We proposed that in the case of low Pt coverage (<30%), the proportion of isolated monolayer islands and one or two Pt atoms was relatively high. Therefore, no activity for methanol oxidation could be observed, and direct oxidation of formic acid became the dominant pathway. On the other hand, for high Pt coverage (> 40%), the proportion of ensemble structures of more Pt atoms on the Au surface increased, leading to a higher occurrence of the indirect pathway for formic acid oxidation, and resulting in the increase in activity for methanol oxidation. With the success of using Au nanoparticles as core, other Au nanostructures like nanotriangular plate and nanorods were also use as core for ion adsorption–in situ electrochemical reduction to yield other Au@Pt nanostructures. The resultant Pt coverage for same [PtCl4]2- concentration bath used in ion adsorption-in situ electrochemical reduction were found to be different with the trend nanoparticles > nanotriangular plate > nanorods. The corresponding specific activity to wards formic acid of the nanotriangular plate were found to be the highest among these three. These differences may due to the preferential showing Au [111] surface in the triangular nanoplate which enhance both the binding and resultant reactivity. The effect of changing the Pt precursors were also studied which showed that the efficiency of binding for Pt tetrahalide ion is much higher than the Pt hexahalide ions which only shows a maximum binding of below 20% for the whole series of concentration we tested. This greatly favors the preparation of direct formic acid fuel cell as specific activity for is highest when the Pt coverage is below 30%. On the other hand, Pt bromide anions were achieving a significant adsorption of bromide ion even after electrochemical reduction. We think that it may due to the very high affinity of bromide onto the Au surface. The binding is confirmed by the XPS which shows a significant ratio of bromide are shown. Although the bromide present hampers the formic acid oxidation, the stability of the resultant Pt/Au surface is much higher. Pt/Ag nanostructure By using galvanic replacement to prepare PtAg hollow shell, Ag nanoparticle template was first prepared by a seed-mediated growth approach. A predetermined amount of K2PtCl4 solution was added and the solution at 60℃. The product was then separated by centrifugation and was washed with ammonium hydroxide and HNO3 solution respectively to remove any unreacted Ag core to yield the PtAg hollow shell. The galvanic displacement was carried out with different amount of K2PtCl4 solution with a fixed amount of template colloidal solution. The thickness of the hollow sphere increased as the amount of K2PtCl4 added was increased. The thickness can be controlled from 2.3 nm to 7.5 nm by simply increase the K2PtCl4 precursor amount from 150 μL to 550 μL. The hollow spheres with lower thickness consist of a smooth surface while those of relatively high thickness compose of continuous aggregated nanoparticles growing on the smooth outer surface. The structural and chemical identity of the PtAg hollow shell were further confirmed by XRD and HRTEM with SAED. EDX study revealed that the ratio of Pt and Ag was in a range of 4.2 to 7.2 but was found to be difficult to tune by either varying the precursors ratio or reaction temperature. Both the XRD and XPS analysis confirmed the alloying of Pt and Ag. Significant improvement was observed in case of formic acid oxidation. The onset potential for formic acid oxidation negatively-shifted for about 40mV on PtAg alloy as compared to that of Pt black. The activity for formic acid oxidation at 0.3V was enhanced by five-fold as compared to Pt black. Chronoamperometric studies revealed that that the current decrease for PtAg for formic acid oxidations were 12.8%, whereas the equivalent calculations for Pt black were 38.9%. It revealed that the PtAg alloy possess higher stability which may attribute to the higher poison tolerance of the PtAg alloy. The advantages of the PtAg hollow structures for electrochemical catalysis includes: (1) large ECSA would result in higher activity; (2) the utilization of the precious metal could be enhanced significantly since the cores were free of metal; and finally (3) the incorporation of Ag has apparently increase the 5d-obitals vacancy of Pt which could weaken the interaction of Pt and poisoning intermediates, thus leading to an enhancement of catalytic capability. Concerning the fulfillment of the project objectives, objective 1 and 2 are fully completed with the successful development of the Au@Pt/CNT and PtAg hollow shell catalysts which were both fully characterized by various solid-state methods. Their stability in acidic and alkali medium were demonstrated in their corresponding CV measurement. In addition, objective 3 to 5 are also successfully demonstrated by the detailed electrocatalytic study for both group of catalysts. Our study reveals the significant catalytic activity enhancement by the incorporation of Au and Ag to Pt and at the same time find out possible factors that enhance or reduce the overall reactivity. Both Au@Pt/CNT and PtAg hollow shell are proved to be effective catalyst for direct formic acid fuel cell.

502912.label: Major findings and research outcome
502912.value: This project mainly aims to develop two class of bimetallic catalyst namely Pt/Au and Pt/Ag. For the Pt/Au part, a facile route for the fabrication of Pt submonolayers with tunable coverage using Au@Pt core–shell nanostructures and halide-mediated adsorption has been reported. By immersing carbon nanotube supported Au nanoparticle composites in a bath of tetrachloroplatinate(II) ions, Pt(II) ions were found to adsorb on the Au surface and could subsequently be reduced electrochemically to yield a Pt submonolayers coated composite (Au@Pt/CNTs). The coverage of Pt on the Au surface could be easily controlled by varying the concentration of Pt(II) in the bath solution or by repeating the ion adsorption and electrochemical reduction process until the desired coverage was obtained. A strong relationship between the surface Pt coverage of the as-prepared Au@Pt/CNTs material and its electrocatalytic activity towards formic acid, methanol and oxygen was found. Au@Pt/CNTs with low Pt coverage (below 30%) displayed superior performance for formic acid oxidation through a direct pathway without occurrence of CO poisoning, and were inert toward methanol oxidation. Due to their inertness to methanol, such Au@Pt/CNTs demonstrated excellence methanol tolerance as an oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. On the other hand, for Au@Pt/CNTs with high Pt coverage (above 40%) the catalytic mechanism for formic acid oxidation shifted from the direct to the CO-mediated indirect pathway, and the mass specific activity for methanol oxidation was found to increase significantly. By means of this versatile construction process, the utilization of Pt can be significantly enhanced, with good control of fuel selectivity, by simple engineering of the Pt coverage. This work has been published on Nano Research in 2014. In contrast, for the Pt/Ag part, a hollow PtAg alloy nanospheres were successfully synthesized by galvanic replacement reaction between Ag nanoparticles and K2PtCl4 at 60 C. The shell thickness and the atomic ratio of Pt/Ag of the hollow nanospheres could be controlled by varying the volumes of Pt precursor solution. The as-synthesized hollow PtAg alloy nanospheres showed higher electrocatalytic activity and stability towards methanol and formic acid oxidations than commercially available Pt black and will be promising electro-catalysts for DMFCs and DFAFCs. This work has been published on RSC Advances in 2016 In conclusion, by using either halide adsorption-reduction or galvanic replacement to form bimetallic composite electrocatalyst, the utilization of precious Pt can on one hand reduced with extended lifetime.

502912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
502912.value: Considering the precise control of Pt coverage on Au nanoparticles with such simple synthetic protocol, we would like to extend the current scope of Pt/Au mixed metal system to trimetallic system like Pt/Au/Pd, Pt/Au/Ru or Pt/Au/Rh using their corresponding halide salt as precursor. With the precise control of three different metals to formulate a submonolayer core-shell structure, enhancement on the metal surface reactivity and synergetic effect from different metal will be possible. Also, the model of submonolayer is seldom reported in the literature, we would like to collaborate with atom probe facility in Oxford University to investigate the possibility in direct observation of the Pt submonolayer so that a deeper understanding in the geometry and chemical composition can be achieved. For the PtAg hollow nanostructure, as we discovery that this catalyst is more active towards alcohol substrates, we would like to further investigate how this combination is favorable for this group of compounds. We would try to incorporate in-situ IR and Raman spectroscopy to study the mechanism involved in such reaction. Currently, already contact Prof. SG Sun at Xiamen University for collaboration on their facility in in-situ IR and Raman spectroscopy for investigation on this reaction.

502912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
502912.value: We successfully developed an unique approach of ion adsorption–in situ electrochemical reduction which utilizes the specific halide mediated adsorption of platinum halides to gold surface, a series of well controlled Au@Pt/CNTs catalyst with precise Pt to Au surface ratio and ultralow platinum overall loading (0.2 wt%) are prepared. An unprecedented electrocatalytic activity has been observed that when the platinum coverage is below 40%, the catalyst is highly active towards formic acid oxidation but inactive towards methanol oxidation. However, when the coverage is increased to higher than 40%, the specific activity for methanol oxidation increases dramatically and a shifting of formic acid oxidation from direct to indirect pathway is observed. This demonstrate the fine tuning of nanoparticles surface can be easily achieved by a simple, reproducible and up-scalable approach without complicated steps like most of the other nanomaterials reported. Building on this simple route, further investigations can easily be done by using gold core with different geometry, different platinum halides, mixture of different metal halides and different metal cores which can generate a lot of room for catalyst design. This makes it a unique and promising project for future fuel cell catalyst development and even for other catalytic system.

503012.label: Project Objectives
503012.value: To fabricate transparent, stretchable bottom electrodes on elastomeric substrates with solution-processable synthetic and patterning methods. To deposit functional polymer active layers and top electrode on top of the bottom electrode by solution-processable methods. The lateral phase separation and vertical multilayer stacking of the active layer will be engineered.
