503012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
503012.value: 摘要: 聚合物太陽能電池是基於高分子類活性半導體材料實現對太陽能吸收和轉化的光伏器件。此類太陽能電池重量輕、價格低廉、柔性、形式多樣、性能可調、并可以使用溶液法製備。因此，聚合物太陽能電池是最有希望量產、用於應對未來大量能源需求的器件。目前除了提高光電轉換效率与器件使用壽命的研究之外，大量工作關注在開發其相對於無機太陽能電池的優勢。例如，開發高效溶液澆筑/打印法的“卷到卷”技術製備柔性聚合物太陽能電池。該類柔性電池可彎曲、捲曲、并可貼附在如帳篷和皮包等的非平整表面。然而，該類柔性器件彈性有限，無法滿足機器皮膚、可穿戴電子器件、醫療診斷植入器等需要高拉伸性能器件（遠大於1%）的要求。進一步說，彈性的實現也可以提高柔性聚合物電池的在彎曲和捲曲過程中的可靠性，避免斷裂。因此，彈性聚合物太陽能電池的實現具有重要意義。 對彈性有機電子器件的研究剛剛起步。第一篇關於本質可拉伸聚合物太陽能電池的文章剛于2011發表。大量關於如何製備該彈性器件和其性能如何等基本問題仍未解決。為此，本項目意在研發新型溶液法製備高性能彈性聚合物太陽能電池和研究其光、電、機械等性能。其中關鍵難點在於如何製備高性能透明彈性電極。本項目將製備具有表面皺褶的彈性金屬網格或者石墨烯類的透明底部電極。研究其結構、圖案、網格形狀、網格填充度、金屬沉積等條件優化透光率和導電性。合成大片高導電石墨烯并研究其複合電極的混合成份比例。之後，在底部電極上構筑聚合物活性半導體和上電極。實現在彈性基底預拉伸下構筑体相异质结和雙層异质结聚合物太陽能電池。在解除拉伸后，整個器件將自然起皺並可被反複拉伸至其預拉伸水平。研究在反複拉伸/放鬆狀態下彈性材料的光學、表面導電性、皺褶、微納米表面形貌、π-π堆積、共軛長度、激發子壽命等的性能。表徵器件在不同入射角、正反入射、和不同拉伸狀態下的性能。研究材料和器件的疲勞特性。本項目的成功完成不僅將開發出製備彈性聚合物太陽能電池新型技術，并獲得關於有機光電材料及器件在反複伸縮中物理性能等新的基礎知識。

503012.label: Realisation of objectives
503012.value: In summary, all the objectives have been addressed. 1. To fabricate transparent, stretchable bottom electrodes on elastomeric substrates with solution-processable synthetic and patterning methods. Polymer-Assisted Metal Deposition (PAMD) has been developed to fabricate metal thin films and patterned structures on many kinds of organic substrates including plastics, elastomers, papers, and textiles. A typical PAMD process involves three steps: 1) modification of substrates with anchoring polymers, 2) immobilization of catalytic moieties in the polymer layer, and 3) electroless deposition (ELD) on the catalyzed areas. With the PADM principle, a new kind of cost-effective, yet high-performance stretchable, compressible, and abrasion-resistant conductive composite has been developed on the basis of commercially available PU sponge and solution-processed thin metal coating. To achieve nano/micro scale patterning ability with PAMD, a new printing strategy, namely matrix-assisted catalytic printing (MACP), has been developed in our group. MACP is compatible with various printing techniques including scanning probe printing, inkjet printing, and screen printing, for the versatile fabrication of metal patterns (Cu, Ag, Ni, Au) with feature sizes spanning from nanometer to meter scales. 2. To deposit functional polymer active layers and top electrode on top of the bottom electrode by solution-processable methods. The lateral phase separation and vertical multilayer stacking of the active layer will be engineered. Typical organic photovoltaic (OPV) devices have been fabricated on transparent and non-transparent electrodes developed from Objective 1 abovementioned. The metal electrodes were printed on flexible substrates such as PET and PI. In addition to flat substrate, topographical PET substrates with protruded 3D nanopillars were also used as substrate. Electron transporting layer such as ZnO and PEI was then spincoated, followed by spincoating of other functional organic layers using orthogonal solvents. The active used in this project is P3HT:PCBM, a well-understood absorber. Top transparent electrode, being highly conductive PEDOT:PSS, was finally spincoated or transfer-printed on the functional layers, followed thermal annealing. The spincoating and annealing conditions were optimized to achieve suitable layer thickness, and micro-phase separated morphology. XPS, AFM, surface profile meter and optical microsope were used to characterized the structures. 3. To study the materials characteristics of different layers of the device, with and without repeating stretching and relaxing cycles. These characteristics mainly includes optical property, surface conductivity, surface buckling, micro and nanoscale surface topography, pipi stacking, conjugation length, and exciton lifetime. A house-made testing system for bending and stretching ability testing, which includes two pairs of x-y stage coupled with motorized control, a pair of probes for conductivity measurement, one optical stage, one Kethly 2400 multimeter, and one measuring software for real-time recording of the electrical signals of flexible/stretchable conductors and devices. Each functional layers’ adhesion and surface morphology were tested at different bending/stretching conditions. The electrical conductivity of electrodes and J-V characteristics of semiconductor layers were also tested at different bending/stretching conditions. 4. To investigate the device physics and stability of as-made polymer solar cells with and without repeating stretching and relaxing cycles. The J-V characteristic curves of as-made organic solar cells are measured by using a Keithley 2400 source meter under illumination of 100 mW/cm2 (Newport 91160, 300 W, solar simulator equipped with an AM 1.5 filter). The light intensity is calibrated by a standard silicon solar cell. The external quantum efficiency (EQE) of the devices are tested by a standard system equipped with a xenon lamp (Oriel 76175_71580), and a dual channel power meter (Newport 2931_C). The devices were bent/stretched in a glove box and the J-V curves were measured in situ.

503012.label: Major findings and research outcome
503012.value: Major findings include: 1. Initial development of Polymer-Assisted Metal Deposition (PAMD) for the fabrication metal thin films structures on many kinds of organic substrates including plastics, elastomers, papers, and textiles. 2. Initial development of matrix-assisted catalytic printing (MACP) for printing metal electrodes (Cu, Ag, Ni, Au) at room temperature with feature sizes spanning from nanometer to meter scales. 3. Demonstration of the fabrication of several highly stretchable metallic electrodes by PADM and MACP. 4. First demonstration of flexible organic solar cells using printed Cu bottom back electrodes. The organic solar cells were fabricated with via vacuum-free technologies, and achieved the highest power conversion efficiency among those full-solution processed solar cells using the same active materials. 5. First demonstration of flexible organic solar cells using printed nanostructured Cu bottom back electrodes. The nanostructure Cu bottom electrodes effectively improved the power conversion efficiency by ~10%. Both devices showed excellent flexibility. 6. Overall, 10 journal papers have been published under the project support, which are listed in Part C. These results have been delivered in many international/regional conferences and university seminars. Some of the important ones are listed in Part C. One more journal paper is being prepared. This paper will report the first high performance stretchable, full solution processed OSCs. 7. The project PI was invited as Leading Guest Editor to edit a special issue, namely “Hong Kong’s Materials Science and Engineering Research” for Advanced Materials. (Aug 2014 issue)

503012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
503012.value: Most of the research done in this project is initial development and demonstration of materials, processing, and devices that lead to a highly flexible organic solar cells. The understanding is just the first step, and the device demonstrated is of very small area. In the future, much work can be done in two directions. One is how to improve the cell efficiency by using more advanced absorbers. This can be done by applying the known better absorbers to the device, or synthesizing new absorbers, and engineering the flexible devices to improve the light trapping and internal quantum efficiency. Another direction worth exploring is how to fabricate large-area flexible organic solar cells on the basis of the developed know-hows from this project. This can be done by more systematic investigation of the electrode and materials fabrication, structures, processing, stability, and uniformity. Much effort should be spent on the printing technology to allow large-area fabrication, as well as device design to ensure good device properties even at large areas.

503012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
503012.value: Stretchable organic solar cells (OSCs) are of high interest to many new applications including robotic skins, wearable electronics, and bioelectronics. However, the field of stretchable organic electronics is in its infant stage, and the first paper on intrinsically stretchable OSCs was just published in 2011. Many basic questions such as how to fabricate these stretchable devices and what is their performance still remain unclear. To address the challenge, the proposal aims to develop solution-processable strategies to fabricate high performance stretchable OSCs, and to study the optical, electrical, and mechanical properties of the as-made stretchable materials and devices. Through the project support, highly flexible and stretchable metallic conductors as well as OSCs have been developed. The success of this project not only open a novel technical know-how for fabricating stretchable OSCs, but also establish new fundamental knowledge of physical behaviors of organic materials and optoelectronic devices under repeating stretching and relaxing cycles. These know-hows and new knowledge should also advance the academic research on other stretchable electronic devices with diode structures, including photodiodes, light-emitting diodes, sensors, and actuators in the future.

510012.label: Project Objectives
510012.value: MS-NRT: Multi-Scale Near-Regular Texture Segmentation (Research Objective). Multi-Scale Near-Regular Texture decomposition of a woven fabric design allows a fabric designer to quickly identify the repetitive structures in the fabric material at different scales of resolution. At the fabric scale, NRTs can segment repeat patterns; at yarn scale, NRTs can identify weaving structures and yarn density; at the fiber level, NRT can identify twists, cycles, and spirality as well as repetitive multi-yarn compositions. The goal of this phase of segmentation is to focus on the smallest unique region of material that can provide all the information about the fabric design and material properties. In order to generate full identification signatures, we will focus on extracting SIFT descriptors for each such independent region. The SIFT descriptors would then be mapped into short-word codes for fast fabric identification and retrieval. MS-PBM: Multi-Scale Perception-Based Metrics (Research Objective). Perception-Based Metrics (PBMs) have been proposed for general texture classification by a number of researchers. Fabric designers are sensitive to a rigid classification of fabric designs. MS-PBM would allow designers to re-classify and re-evaluate designs. This is a more flexible multi-view classification that would take into account cultural and demographic biases. The multi-scale extension enhances the flexibility of the classical PBM by providing levels of granularity for classes of design.

510012.label: Realisation of objectives
510012.value: The two major objectives proposed in this project have been fully achieved. The first objective was to perform the integration of multi-scale near-regular texture (MS-NRT) segmentation with scale invariant feature based descriptors for fabric material classification. The second objective was to develop perceptual-based metric for color and texture classification in order to aid in fabric color-theme and texture-based design. Both objectives have been completed in full. Multi-Scale Near-Regular Texture Segmentation (Objective 1) This has been achieved in full and tested on real fabric samples. The results have been published in four major journal publications [4] [9] [10] and [11]. In particular, a functional variation-based segmentation method within using a fuzzy calculus framework has been designed, implemented, and tested. This method has been proven to be the most effective in multi-scale segmentation of multi-region colored images of natural textile fabrics. The advantages of our new segmentation method are: (1) a new PCA-based descriptor for segmenting color-texture images better than classical segmentation models; (2) a new nonconvex regularization term to preserve the geometrical structure of the fuzzy membership function; (3) a fast iterative algorithm that solves the augmented Lagrange multiplier method with iterative reweighting. These methods are mathematically important and significant because the fabric textile surfaces are inherently fuzzy due to the hairiness structure of woven yarn. Thus, both color and region extraction are naturally very difficult to achieve with traditional methods. We have performed extensive experiments that include over 10,000 fabric samples to measure the segmentation performance. Our model shows significantly better segmentation results compared with other well-known models. Noise is prevalent in fabric textures. This noise affects negatively the image segmentation phase. However, the noise cannot be simply removed by classical de-noising models because these models only deal with Gaussian white noise. Therefore, we have implemented the structure-plus-texture decomposition into the image segmentation model and designed a new cartoon-based image segmentation. A novel variational model for removing multiplicative noise has been implemented and tested. The model is established on the analysis of the characteristic of textile images. The main contributions of the model are: (1) a cartoon-and-texture decomposition process is incorporated into the model, which can reduce the influence of the random texture noise on the segmentation process; (2) to overcome the drawback of the lightness inconsistency for the segmentation process, a bias field function is introduced to measure the deviation degree between the cartoon image and the piecewise constant approximation of the cartoon image. Thus, the regions of textile images can be more accurately estimated; (3) we use fuzzy membership functions (FMFs) to indicate the regions of images. However, to restrain the FMFs from degeneration, a new penalty term on the FMFs is introduced in our model. Although models in different frameworks may have different mathematical expressions, they usually share common assumptions. Most image segmentation models mainly consist of two terms: the fidelity term and the regularization term. The fidelity term is derived from the assumption that, in the whole/local part of every homogeneous region, the descriptor (usually being a high-dimensional vector whose ingredients include gray/color intensities, textons, etc) for a pixel is sampled from an independent and identical distribution. For example, if the Gaussian distribution is used and the distribution parameters (mean and variance) are given, the descriptors for all pixels in an image can be approximated by globally piecewise constant vectors or local piecewise constant vectors. One of the most important components of the project is the near regular texture pattern identification of color patches and texture regions. These are repetitive texture regions in fabric images that can be organized into groups of repetitive structural forms such as geometric shapes, arrays, and partition groups. Non-regular or stochastic textures have little structural information and pattern composition inference is more difficult to compute. We used the shape geometry of repeated patterns to interpret pair-wise connections between patterns and generate the abstract structural form by unifying the local connections. The local patch connection can be obtained by analyzing the geodesic distance between any spatially adjacent patch pairs in SCF. The geodesic information is extracted from SCF using front propagation, and the neighbor set for each detected patch can be generated accordingly. We can classify the composition structure by the common neighboring topology to reflect the local property of global structure. This work has been published in two papers [1] and [4] and a PhD thesis had been completed on the mathematical formulation of this problem. Perception-based Color Modeling (Objective 2) Fashion designers use color and tone modifications amongst the most frequent fabric design operations. These operations are part of the perception-based cognitive process leading to the creation of new fabric designs. We formulate the fabric design process as a cognitive process that simultaneously considers multiple color tones to form a desired theme as well as texture characteristics in the fabric. The work has been published in three journal papers [2] [11] [12]. In this work, we have incorporated color assembly and texture knowledge in the fabric design process in order to automatically produce the color combinations learnt from a given natural or abstract theme. We have demonstrated that the use of color theme associations can automatically generate new fabric designs that rival complex commercial designs and are otherwise difficult to generate even by experienced designers. Preliminary experiments have confirmed the effectiveness of our developed method and three papers have been published in this area. Furthermore, we have implemented a color theme-based extraction and labeling method that combines de-noising and cartoon-based region segmentation. We have improved the previous cartoon-based region extraction for the retrieving of a theme of colors. The model contains three phases. The first phase, the image segmentation phase, is to partition an input fabric image into several homogeneous regions. From the first phase, we can obtain the color mean of each region and a bias field function. Furthermore, the color mean values of all regions are considered as the theme colors of the input image. The second phase is to retrieve the relevant theme colors from a given data set. The third phase is to reconstruct new images with different appearances of the input image by using the theme colors retrieved from the second phase and the bias field function estimated from the first phase. This method has been published in papers [2] and [12]. A full example of color theme retargeting process has been documentd in [2] and further improved in [12].

Multi-Scale Near-Regular Texture decomposition of a woven fabric design allows a fabric designer to quickly identify the repetitive structures in the fabric material at different scales of resolution. At the fabric scale, NRTs can segment repeat patterns; at yarn scale, NRTs can identify weaving structures and yarn density; at the fiber level, NRT can identify twists, cycles, and spirality as well as repetitive multi-yarn compositions. The goal of this phase of segmentation is to focus on the smallest unique region of material that can provide all the information about the fabric design and material properties. 510012.label: Major findings and research outcome
510012.value: In this project we had five major findings: 1. It is possible to increase the accuracy of region segmentation of micro structures of textile fabrics beyond 98%. That is, were able to isolate both the primary colors used in the actual dying of fiber as well as the texture patterns across fuzzy boundaries with more than 98% accuracy. 2. We developed a new 3D model of woven fabric reconstruction system that is capable of generating any 3D fabric texture or pattern design according to industry standards. This system is called IDSS. 3. A multi-scale representation of fabric structure has been developed and used for both color appearance as well as inherent structural patterns. The multi-scale representation is capable of accurately representing near regular texture patterns of any kind of real fabrics. 4. A color theme design method has been developed to aid designers in generating real fabric patterns based on arbitrary themes obtained from images of various scenes. 5. The most challenging problem with fabric images is noise from hairiness. This causes fuzzy boundaries, specular noise, overlapping, occlusion and color blending. All these problems have been properly addressed. The main result is the ability to count yearn at arbitrary density with 100% accuracy.

510012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
510012.value: The results of this work have opened new venues of research in multi-scale segmentation of material surfaces for the purpose of understanding both appearance and structure. We have employed complex mathematical models that show the power of abstraction when dealing with micro-scale specular noise and fuzziness. These models are unique and cannot directly be compared with existing image processing models for general scenes due to the fact that both light and structure play a significant role in the pixel-based information obtained from images of such micro structures. This has inspired us to think about new problems that can be resolved based on our results. The first problem is photometric stereo. By designing a new imaging system, we can potentially recover the full 3D profile of textile fabrics. This is very important in the analysis of fabric structure, understanding the underlying patterns at yarn and fiber level and color segmentation. The second problem is in the multi-scale data representation of fabric materials. Due to the enormous size of data collected from different materials, we need better data structure representations for searching and matching fabric samples. This would lead to a standard in fabric swatch repositories for the entire industry.

510012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
510012.value: In this project we investigated, implemented, analyzed and tested new strategies for multi-scale representation, acquisition and retrieval of large sets of textile fabrics. We focused on three physical levels of scale: fabric, yarn, and fiber. For every scale we have implemented methods that successfully solved the problems associated with noise, occlusion, illumination and structural deformations. The results of our work marked a significant direction in digital maintenance and information storage and retrieval of fabric textiles. In the process, we developed new mathematical models, algorithms and systems for finding regions of importance in pattern design and color appearance of textile fabrics. We also developed accurate methods for color extraction and yarn count, both of which are challenging problems in the microstructure representation of fabric materials. We also suggested new methods for color design and 3D woven fabric reconstructions. The project has made a significant impact in the textile industry as our system has been used in digital archives of fabric materials.

510412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
510412.value: 受到规模经济驱动，云计算成为信息计算领域服务交付的一个重要过度和模式转变。它提供一种与传统不同的计算模式。在这种模式下，共享池中的虚拟化、动态配置和管理的计算资源按需地通过互联网和其他可用网络提供给客户。由于这种“随收随付”的商业模式的存在，云计算也将导致许多行业的转变和转型。另一方面，随着无线通信和便携式设备技术的进步，移动计算已经融入到我们日常生活中。随着越来越多的移动性，用户需要在移动设备上独立运行或者远程访问移动应用。 云服务在移动领域的应用导致一种新的计算模式的出现，即移动云计算。移动云计算使得移动设备能够充分利云提供的弹性计算资源，并为移动服务产业提供了巨大的机会。据预测，移动云计算服务将在未来20年成为IT行业的首选平台，并能带来巨大的收入。 该项目中，我们将研究如何为开发高性能移动云应用提供支持。通过文献综述，我们将移动云计算分为三种方法：1）将对云服务的访问由传统桌面电脑延伸到移动设备；2）移动设备通过相互合作，本身成为云资源提供者；3）利用云计算技术，开发下一代移动应用，例如，通过将移动设备上运行的应用程序的部分计算任务迁移到云上运行，我们可以创建远远超过传统移动设备负载能力的应用程序。此项目中，我们将专注于第三种方法，因为该方法是未来的一种发展趋势，并且研究领域的主要工作都集中在这种方法上。同时，该方法带来了一些全新的具有挑战性的问题。无论是现有的移动计算模型，还是云计算模型都不适合开发这种类型的移动云应用。我们需要新的编程模型，相应机制和算法。 虽然前人在这方面做过一些工作，但是如何提供一个系统的方法来支持移动云模型下的应用程序开发和运行，尚未得到有效解决。 我们将对移动云计算模式下新的需求和问题进行系统的调查，并提出一个支持开发先进移动云应用程序的编程模型以及执行框架。我们将采用基于组件的编程模型，该编程模型支持应用开发者定义组件，并指定组件之间的依赖关系。执行框架自动地将编程人员创建的组件结构图映射到云和客户端执行，并容许组件和相关数据在云和移动客户端自适应地迁移。在这一过程中，执行框架将处理许多底层问题，例如，云和移动终端之间计算切分和调度，容错，数据管理以及云资源分配等等，以方便开发人员能够专注于应用程序的逻辑。为了证明我们提供的中间件平台的有效性，我们还将建立一个移动云实验床，并基于此演示一些示例应用程序。 该项目将为开发下一代移动应用做出重大贡献。应用开发者和终端用户都将收益于我们的研究成果。我们提出的编程模型和执行框架将为开发者创建高性能移动云应用提供编程抽象和运行支持。即使在面对不可预测的负载和不稳定的网络条件和操作环境中，我们的平台也能保证移动云应用的高效运行。由于我们的研究成果，终端用户也将在移动设备上体验到更多的计算密集型和数据密集型的应用程序，而这类应用在现有移动设备资源受限制的条件下只能提供比较差的用户体验，甚至无法运行。

510412.label: Realisation of objectives
510412.value: We have made efforts to identify the challenging issues in mobile cloud computing. The issues are classified into various layers: resource management, workload management, and applications. Resources in mobile cloud environments include networking, battery, computation and storage from mobile nodes, cloudlets distributed at the network edge and centralized data centers on the Internet. The main goal of resource management is to abstract the resources from various distributed hosts, and provide them as services to consumers. The main problems include job classification, resource prediction and resource provisioning. As the technologies of sensing and computation of mobile devices developed, advanced mobile applications such as gaming, augmented reality and human activity recognition have emerged. One challenging problem we studied extensively is computation partitioning, i.e., to decide for mobile devices which parts of application should be computed on resource-limited mobile devices and which parts should be offloaded onto cloud, such that certain objective like computation time and energy consumption is optimized. Although there are works done on some aspects of computation partitioning, how to provide a systematic approach to support the partitioning for various models of applications and systems has not been adequately addressed. We have developed a set of algorithms and mechanisms on computation partitioning. First, we studied the model of computation partitioning for applications composed of independent computations and for which partitioning decision is done for single user. We take RFID tracking as a case study, and demonstrate that computation partitioning can significantly improve the application performance. In particular, we considered the RFID system that attaches the RFID reader on the moving object, and deployed passive RFID tags in the environment. The moving object collects the noisy RFID readings, and perform continuous estimation of its position in real time. Traditional approaches such as Particle Filter (PF) can achieve high accuracy, but require a large amount of computations on the device. The approaches are hard to be implemented on some mobile devices that are constrained by the computing capabilities and battery. Thus, we proposed an adaptive approach to achieve accuracy and energy efficiency. Our approach can adaptively partition the computations between the mobile device and infrastructure servers or clouds based on the quality of network connections. We evaluated our solution through real world experiments, and showed that our proposed approach with computation partitioning outperforms other approaches in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. We then studied the model of single user computation partitioning for applications composed of dependent computations. We found that most existing works on computation partitioning pertains to this model. We tackle two important issues not solved in existing works. One issue was partitioning of data streaming application. In this work, we aimed at optimizing the partition of a data stream application between mobile and cloud so that the application has maximum speed/throughput in processing the streaming data. To the best of our knowledge, ours was the first work to study the partitioning problem for mobile data stream applications, where the optimization was placed on achieving high throughput of processing the streaming data rather than minimizing the makespan of executions in other applications. We proposed a framework to provide runtime support for the dynamic partitioning and execution of the application. Different from existing works, the framework not only allows the dynamic partitioning for a single user but also supports the multiple tenancy service invocation in the cloud to achieve efficient utilization of the underlying cloud resources. The framework was designed on the elastic cloud fabrics for better scalability. The optimization of the partitioning for each single user was by using genetic algorithm. Through both extensive simulations and experiments on real world applications, we showed that our method could achieve more than 2X better performance over the execution without partitioning. We proceed to study the issues of computation partitioning under dynamic mobile cloud environments. Existing works assume that the computational and data transmission cost of each part of the application remains the same as the application is running. This assumption did not hold in dynamic mobile cloud environments, where the device and network connection status may fluctuate, and thus affects the computational and transmission cost. In this case, the one-time partitioning of the application may yield significant performance degradations. Therefore, we considered updating the partition periodically during the course of application execution, which was named as computation repartitioning in our thesis. We proposed a framework for run time computation repartitioning in dynamic mobile cloud environments. Based on this framework, we took the dynamic network connection to clouds as a case study, and designed an online solution, named Foreseer, to solve the mobile cloud application repartitioning problem. We evaluated our solution based on real world data traces that are collected in a campus WiFi hotspot testbed. The result showed that our method can achieve significantly shorter completion time over previous approaches. We studied the most complex model of computation partitioning, where the application was composed of dependent computations, and the partitioning decision was made for multiple users. In this model, the multiple users compete for the computing resources shared by the users on the cloud. The users’ partitioning decisions were dependent with each other. To achieve high system performance, the users’ partitioning decisions should be considered jointly with the scheduling of computations on the shared cloud resources. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to study the Multiple User Computation Partitioning Problem (MCPP). We showed that MCPP is different from and more difficult than the classical job scheduling problems. In classical job scheduling problems, the computations were allowed to schedule onto arbitrary resources including the mobile devices and cloud resources, while in MCPP the user’s computations cannot be scheduled to other users’ devices. We designed an offline heuristic algorithm, namely SearchAdjust, to solve MCPP. We demonstrated through benchmarks that SearchAdjust outperformed the classical job scheduling approaches by 10% on average in terms of application delay. Based on SearchAdjust, we also designed an online algorithm for MCPP that can be easily deployed in practical systems. We validated the effectiveness of our online algorithm using real world load traces. We demonstrated our research results in two applications: mobile gesture recognition, and mobile augmented reality. Human gesture based HCI is desired by smart phone users in a lot of scenarios. However, most smart phones in current markets cannot support well the complex computation involved in gesture recognitions. In the project, we implemented the gesture recognition by using cloud offloading approach. We showed that this approach can significantly reduce the delay of gesture recognition. This demonstration provided feasible option for integrating human gesture based HCI service on current commodity-based smart phones. In mobile augmented reality, we focus on recognize building in an unfamiliar environment. However, object recognizing is very computation intensive that most mobile devices cannot support well. Thus, programmers have to use smaller image size which lower the recognition ratio to guarantee the recognition process won’t take too long. In the project, we use the computation partitioning in this application, and reduce the processing time for each frame from 3~5 seconds to about 1 second.

510412.label: Major findings and research outcome
510412.value: In the project, we have achieved significant results on computation offloading and partitioning, resource prediction [C2014] and service placement and load dispatching in mobile cloud computing. We first studied how to apply the principle of computation offloading into the design of accurate and efficient RFID tracking method [J2015b]. We proposed a hybrid method for achieving high accuracy and efficiency in object tracking. The method can offload complex computations involved in the particle filtering onto the nearby servers or the cloud. Through extensive simulations and two real world experiments, we showed that the method with computation offloading outperforms the existing methods WCL and PF. We have designed a framework for partitioning and execution of data streaming application in mobile cloud computing [J2013]. We proposed a genetic algorithm to optimize the throughput in the partitioning of applications. We demonstrated our proposed algorithm through simulation and one real world application, namely, QR-code recognition. The results show that the partitioned execution with our proposed algorithm can achieve 2X throughput than the execution without partitioning. We have solved the problem of computation partitioning under network fluctuations [J2014]. We exploited mobility prediction to estimate the user’s future network quality, and designed an online algorithm to periodically update the partitioning during the application life cycle. We collected network traces from our WiFi network testbed, and evaluated the online repartitioning algorithm with two applications. The results show that our algorithm can achieve at least 35% better performance than existing approaches. We developed a series of algorithms to solve the Multiple User Computation Partitioning Problem (MCPP), where there exists a number of users offloading the computations onto a set of cloud servers [J2015a]. MCPP is more difficult than traditional job scheduling problem in parallel computing. We proposed an offline heuristic algorithm, to solve MCPP, and an online algorithm that can be deployed easily in practical systems. The results showed both algorithms have better performance than existing classical job scheduling algorithms. We have studied the joint optimization of service placement and load dispatching in mobile cloud systems, and designed an efficient heuristic algorithm to the problem [J2016]. We have extended the problem to a more practical model, and develop an online algorithm to the problem that can be deployed easily in practical systems. Through evaluation based on the load traces from two real world datasets, it is shown that the online algorithm can achieve good performance in access latency and cost of service providers.

510412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
510412.value: In the future, we will develop an approach to partition the computations with historical execution traces of the application, which specifically include the execution time of each part of applications, and data transmission time on the network. Unlike previous works, our approach requires the trace collection and analysis that can be easily done in practical system, and avoids the real time measurements of resources and workloads, which inherently cannot be accurate and leads to unsatisfactory performance of the partitioned application, or causes too much overhead. Another direction for future research is to study the provisioning of computation offloading as a service to the end users from the standpoint of service provider. The economic cost on the cloud resource should be taken into account. Furthermore, we simplify that the users access to the cloud via separate wireless networks. In practical systems, the users may access to the cloud through the same wireless networks. The users can share and compete for the bandwidth resources. The allocation of network resources to the users should be considered together with the partitioning decision of each user. It is interesting to study the joint network resource allocation and computation partitioning problem.

510412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
510412.value: Computation partitioning between the mobile device and cloud is an important and challenging research topic in mobile cloud computing. There is significant complexity involved in ensuring that the application can achieve adaptive and elastic computation partitioning between the mobile device and the cloud under dynamic environments and variable loads. Although some related issues are well solved, there are still many problems lacking sufficient investigation. The contributions of this project mainly lie in modeling, optimization and evaluation for computation partitioning in mobile cloud applications. We classified computation partitioning into different models by considering two dimensional properties: application dimension and system dimension. On application dimension, we have done partitioning for two types of applications. On system dimension, we have done the partitioning for two types of systems: single user system and multiple users system. To the best of our knowledge, we were the first to systematically study and issues on computation partitioning and provided a set of efficient methods and algorithms which can be used to develop the mobile cloud applications. This project will make significant values in cloud and mobile computing for developing next generation mobile applications. Both the application developers and end users will benefit from our research outcomes.

511212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
511212.value: Compared to conventional vapor compression systems, magnetic refrigerators (MR) are more energy efficient and use a solid magnetocaloric (MC) refrigerant rather than a fluorocarbon fluid, both of which are of huge potential environmental and economical benefits. Since the giant magnetocaloric effect (MCE) was discovered in 1997, tremendous efforts have been spent to develop new MC materials and prototype magnetic refrigerators. Nonetheless, a key challenge in the field of MR is still to develop a novel low cost MC material with excellent refrigeration efficiency near room temperature. With the research background of the project team on MC materials, the proposed study aims to address this important challenge. Recent results by the project team and other researchers show that some metallic glasses exhibit very good properties and excellent refrigeration capacity even compared to giant MCE materials, but their transition temperatures are still too low for room temperature MRs. In this project, magnetic phase diagrams of various binary Gd-TM metallic glass systems will be firstly constructed and the origin of the large refrigeration capacity will be investigated. Based on these findings, attempts will be made to achieve excellent room temperature refrigeration efficiency for more complex Gd-based metallic glass systems by tuning their compositions. In order to achieve a large specific surface area to improve the heat exchange efficiency for a refrigerant and to minimize the eddy current, metallic glass ribbons and wires will be synthesized by melting spinning. The percentage of the expensive Gd element will be further reduced by replacing it with less expensive elements so as to reduce the cost. Another effective way to reduce the material cost is to increase the power density by increasing the frequency of operation of a magnetic refrigerator. In this project, the MCE behavior of Gd-based metallic glass systems will be experimentally examined at a higher frequency range of operation. Based on the new metallic glass system and the idea of hybrid structures for achieving high efficiency with lower magnetic fields, an attempt will be further made to synthesize metallic glass hybrid structures comprising layers of metallic glass ribbons and soft permeable materials, or metallic glass wires wound around soft permeable tubes, and to study their MCE. It is envisaged that the findings of the project will not only be essential for achieving novel MC materials/structures, but also have significant academic merit in understanding the MCE of metallic glasses. 近年來，磁熱效應因為其在磁製冷技術方面的應用前景而受到越來越多的關注。磁製冷技術採用固體磁熱材料作為製冷介質以取代氟利昂氣體壓縮系統，因而更節能也更環保。自從巨磁熵變效應在1997年被發現以後，人們一直致力於開發新型的磁致冷材料，其中一個關鍵的難題是尋找一種新型的在室溫附近具有優異製冷效率的低成本磁熱效應材料，本研究專案就致力於探尋這種具有優異製冷效率的低成本室溫磁製冷材料。本研究組及其他相關研究人員的研究結果表明，一些具有二級相變的非晶態合金表現出與巨磁熵變效應材料相當的磁製冷能力，而且非晶態合金還具有近零磁滯和很好的抗腐蝕能力等優異性能。然而，目前發現的那些非晶態材料的居裏溫度還是太低，不能用於近室溫製冷材料。在本項目中，我們會首先構建一個Gd-TM非晶系統的磁相圖，並研究其高製冷能力的機制。在此基礎上，我們會嘗試摻雜其他元素來獲得Gd-TM基的一系列非晶態合金，希望能夠通過調節合金的成分來獲得在室溫條件下更高的製冷效率。 為了獲得更大的比表面積來提高熱交換效率同時減少渦流損耗，我們將主要製備非晶條帶和非晶線來進行研究。為了降低成本，一方面高成本的Gd元素將會被其他廉價的稀土元素替代，另一方面我們將通過提高磁致冷系統的動作頻率來提高能量密度。最後，通過設計一些非晶-軟磁材料的混合結構來提高非晶態合金在低磁場下的製冷效率。本項目的研究結果不僅對於開發一個新型近室溫高效磁致冷材料有著重大意義，而且對於深入理解非晶態合金高製冷效率的機理有著重要的基礎研究價值。

511212.label: Realisation of objectives
511212.value: Objective 1 (100% achieved) In this project, magnetocaloric (MC) metallic glass ribbons and wires of various binary Gd-TM alloys were successfully synthesized. The magnetic and magnetocaloric effects of the binary Gd-TM metallic glasses including GdxCo100-x and GdyNi100-y were characterized by Quantum Design Physical Properties Measurement System (PPMS 6000) under various testing conditions. When the frequencies of magnetic fields become larger, amorphous alloys response faster and perform better due to their nearly zero hysteresis. Both the Curie temperature (Tc) and the peak magnetic entropy change were found to be able to be tailored by adjusting the compositions. The binary Gd50Co50 amorphous alloy provides a basic alloy for developing high performance multi-component amorphous alloys near room temperature. Objective 2 (100% achieved) The mechanism of large MCE of binary Gd-TM metallic glass was systematically analyzed by studying the coupling effect between atoms. The change of composition resulted in the change of the coupling effect. The relationship between alloy composition and the Curie temperature was determined. In addition, the relationship between the peak magnetic entropy change and the Curie temperature was also determined. In GdxCo100-x binary amorphous ribbons, the relationship between chemical composition and TC is TC=708.8-8.83x, and a strong correlation between the peak value of magnetic entropy change and Tc is established under the magnetic field ranging from 1 T to 5 T. Objective 3 (100% achieved) In this project, tertiary Gd-TM metallic glasses were successfully synthesized with chemical compositions of Gd-Co-Fe and Gd-Co-Al. The effect of minor addition/substitution on the magnetic properties and magnetocaloric effect of GdCoAl metallic glasses was investigated. Not only the peak magnetic entropy change was enhanced through minor addition or substituion, but also the Curie temperature was closer to room temperature. Moreover, due to the replacement of Gd by other elements, the total cost of Gd-TM alloys was reduced. The enhanced magnetic properties were shown to be induced by the enlarged effective magnetic moment. The relationship between alloy composition and the Curie temperature, and the relationship between the peak magnetic entropy change and the Curie temperature were also determined. The origin and the mechanism of their excellent MCE were both related to the coupling effect between the 3d electron in Co and 4f electron in Gd.

511212.label: Major findings and research outcome
511212.value: (1) The magnetic properties and magnetocaloric effect of GdxCo100-x (x=50, 53, 56, 58, 60) amorphous ribbons were investigated. It was found that both Curie temperature (Tc) and peak magnetic entropy change could be tailored by adjusting the compositions. The peak value of the magnetic entropy change and the resulting adiabatic temperature rise of the Gd50Co50 amorphous ribbons is much higher than any other amorphous alloys previously reported with a Tc near room temperature. Moreover, its refrigeration capacity is much larger than of the crystalline alloys. The related work was published in AIP Advances, 5 (2015) 097122 and AIP Advances, 6 (2016) 035302. (2) The Curie temperature of Gd50Co50 amorphous alloy was further increased from 267 K to 277 K by a minor Fe addition as a replacement for Co. The adiabatic temperature rise of the Gd50Co48Fe2 amorphous alloy is larger than those of other metallic glasses near the ice point of water. The related work was published in Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids, 464 (2017) 30-33. (3) The magnetic properties of Gd55Co25Al20 bulk metallic glass was improved by minor substitution of Co with Ni without deteriorating the glass forming ability. The improved magnetic properties of the Gd55Al20Co20Ni5 amorphous rod is induced by the enlarged effective magnetic moment by minor Ni substitution for Co, resulting from the enhanced interaction between the 3d electron in Co and the 4f electron in Gd. The related work was published in Journal of Applied Physics, 115 (2014) 223904. (4) The MCE of Gd55Co25Al20 BMG could also be improved by minor substitution of Al with Zn. Not only the peak magnetic entropy change was enhanced but also the Curie temperature was closer to room temperature. On the other hand, both the glass forming ability and magnetic properties of Gd55Co25Al20 BMG could also be improved by minor substitution of Co with Fe. The related work has been published in Journal of Materials Science, 50 (2015) 1333-1337, and Modern Physics Letters B, 29 (2015) 1550. (5) Alloys exhibiting table-like magnetic entropy change profile are regarded as ideal magnetic refrigerants for an Ericsson magnetic refrigeration cycle. In this work, two Gd-Co-based amorphous hybrids using the Gd50Co50, Gd50Co48Fe2, Gd50Co48Mn2 and Gd50Co45Mn5 amorphous ribbons were further synthesized and achieved obtained table-like peak magnetic entropy change profiles across the ice point of water within different temperature ranges. The related work was accepted for publication in Journal of Alloys and Compounds.

511212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
511212.value: Based on the findings of the present project, the following future work is proposed. (1) The findings of the present project show that the amorphous hybrids are a new candidate for household magnetic refrigerants due to its table like magnetic entropy change profile. More work is proposed to further develop amorphous hybrids with enhanced MCE for industrial applications and it may lead to a formulation of a proposal for industrial funding. (2) The present work has experimentally and analytically investigated the magnetocaloric effect of metallic glasses. It is challenging to further develop simulation models to predict the magnetic properties and magnetocaloric effect of metallic glasses. Preliminary work is being done to simulate the MCE of metallic glasses. It is expected that based on the findings of the preliminary work, a new research proposal will be formulated.

511212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
511212.value: Metallic glasses with excellent refrigeration efficiency have attracted much research attention over the past few decades. There have been extensive research efforts to develop metallic glasses in order to address the issue of room temperature magnetic refrigeration. With the aim of addressing this issue, a series of Gd-TM and Gd-TM-based metallic glasses were successfully synthesized and their magnetic properties and magnetocaloric effect were systematically investigated. By adjusting the chemical composition, the MCE could be tailored. By minor addition such Fe, Al and Zn, the MCE could be enhanced and the working temperature can be more close to room temperature. The mechanism of large MCE was also investigated in this project. The results of the present project do not only lead to a better understanding of the magnetocaloric effect of metallic glasses, but also lay down a good foundation to further develop ideal MCE metallic glasses for industrial applications.

511412.label: Project Objectives
511412.value: To verify experimentally the use of water mist and variable condensing setpoint temperature control on air-cooled chillers for improved heat rejection effectiveness; To investigate the effect of water mist droplet size and generation rate on chiller operation under variable condensing setpoint temperature reset control; To develop the design of a water mist system and method of operational control for improving energy efficiency of air-cooled chillers; and To assess the possible contribution towards the reduction of total electricity consumption in the building sector by implementing mist pre-cooling and variable condensing setpoint temperature control on air-cooled chillers.

511412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
511412.value: This proposed research aims to experimentally validate a novel energy saving method for improving the condenser heat rejection effectiveness in air-cooled chillers, which can be applied to buildings in densely populated cities having to confront water shortage problems. Chillers are used in most commercial buildings for the provision of air conditioning, and they consume a huge amount of electricity. These chillers work at high condensing temperatures based on the summer design conditions, and are inefficient in energy use. It is possible to operate air-cooled chillers at lower condensing temperatures when the outdoor air temperature falls below the summer design conditions. There are no experimental studies to support the operation and controllability of these air-cooled chillers incorporated with variable condensing setpoint temperature at change of weather-load conditions and assisted by water mist pre-cooling. The energy saving potential of its application has to be explored. This project is to set up an experimental rig for verifying and developing a condensing temperature control method integrated with water mist pre-cooling for air-cooled chillers. The rig will comprise of a novel variable condensing setpoint temperature controller and a water mist system capable of producing various mist generation rate and droplet size. Experimental measurements of the chiller operating variables with and without water mist will be carried out. The operating balance between the heat rejection side, the evaporator and the compressor will be analyzed for the lowering of condensing temperature and enhancement of chiller efficiency at diverse weather-load conditions. The influence of water mist generation rate, droplet size and condenser air flow rate on heat rejection effectiveness will be analyzed. The energy savings obtainable by adopting water mist pre-cooling and the variable condensing temperature control method developed in this study will be evaluated for typical commercial buildings in a subtropical climate by mechanistic modeling and simulation. The research outcome will provide an insight to chiller manufacturers to support the development of new products of mist-assisted air-cooled chillers with built-in condensing setpoint temperature controller, and provide useful guidance to building services operators and design engineers in achieving energy saving. The long-term significance of this proposed project rests on its contribution to energy conservation in the building sector with minimal consumption of water. 此研究提案的主旨，是驗證一個嶄新的節能方法，用以改進風冷冷水機的冷凝器排熱效能。這節能方法可以應用於中央空調系統，尤其適合於面對水耗問題的人口密集城市。 商業樓宇普遍地選用冷水機組，以提供空調，亦因此耗用大量電能；在夏季設定工況下，冷水機的運作冷凝溫度很高，能效非常低，當室外溫度低於夏季設計水平時，推低運作冷凝溫度是完全可能的，更輔以噴霧預冷，配合變冷凝溫度設點，以應對環境工況及負荷的變化，是可行的；不過至今未有實驗驗證其運行特性及可控性，相關的節能潛在效益，有待探求。 此研究計劃的一個重要部份，是建立一個實驗裝置，支援改進風冷冷水機能效，驗證噴霧預冷優化運作，開展變冷凝溫度設點的控制方法；實驗裝置包括高壓噴霧糸統，提供變霧化量及液滴直徑，變冷凝溫度設點控制模塊，測量記錄冷水機運作參數，分析壓縮、冷凝排熱及蒸發端的質熱平衡，從而推斷在不同環境工況及負荷率下，可以達至的冷凝溫度下降幅度及冷水機能效改善幅度；同時需要分析霧化量、液滴直徑及冷凝器空氣流量，對排熱功效的影響。 承接上述開展的噴霧預冷及變冷凝溫度控制方法，此研究提案會進一步採用計算機模擬，結合標准的商業大廈處於亞熱帶氣侯下的制冷負荷形態，評估其節能量值。研究的成果，可以提供冷水機制造商有力數據，支援開展噴霧輔助風冷冷水機新產品，帶有內置的變冷凝溫度控制模塊；提供屋宇裝備工程師有效指引，營造建築節能；從長遠的重要性來說，此研究提案，對建築板塊的節能及減少水耗，有肯定的貢獻。

511412.label: Realisation of objectives
511412.value: An air-cooled screw chiller with twin refrigeration circuits and water-mist pre-cooling was modelled by mechanistic equations using TRNSYS. This formed the basis for simulating the chiller operation accounting for energy balance of heat transfer processes and mass balance of refrigerant flow, under conventional control and variable setpoint condensing temperature control. Energy savings obtainable was evaluated for typical commercial buildings in subtropical climate. Types and range of operating variables, instrumentation and number of tests to cover the various weather-load conditions were formulated. A uniform design method developed from number theory was adopted for determining the number of experimental tests, establishing a uniform experiment design matrix which gave the combination of values of the parameters in the tests required. Energy and environmental implications of future climate change and increasing outdoor temperature was also evaluated in terms of carbon emissions and water consumption for cooling in commercial buildings. Detailed design of an experimental chiller rig was produced. Much effort and many months were spent on identifying a suitable chiller and overcoming the problems of getting power supply and roof area for installation. Two tenders were called but the tender offers were very disappointing, probably because of having so many construction projects and lacking of workers in Hong Kong. In result of the disappointing tender offers, the experimental rig was changed to using an existing chiller in collaboration with PolyU’s Facility Management Office, without its support the completion of this project would not be possible. The experimental rig constructed comprised of a setpoint condensing temperature controller and a water mist system capable of producing two generation rates and droplet sizes, equipped with instrumentations for measuring and logging the parameters. Using the rig constructed, measurement of operating parameters were made commencing from August 2015 and would require one year to obtain data covering the ranges and combinations of parameters satisfying the previously established uniform experiment design matrix. Although the project account has to close by Dec 2015, and the PI has retired recently, a project team member will continue with the tests and final analysis. After obtaining the experimental data, the mechanistic models that have been well established can be calibrated for chiller operation in energy and mass balance, and then applied to recalculate the energy performance of chiller systems used in different buildings and climates. This recalculation can be done quite quickly as calculations have been carried out using the before-calibration models.

511412.label: Major findings and research outcome
511412.value: Mechanistic models of air-cooled screw chiller with twin refrigeration circuits, integrated with water mist pre-cooling and condenser fan speed control, were established using TYNSYS. Algorithms were developed to model the interaction between varying setpoint condensing temperature, constant or variable fan speed driving, with or without water mist pre-cooling. The opportunity of reducing the condensing temperature at below-design outdoor conditions and was exploited. The relation between outdoor air state, chiller load ratio and optimum setpoint condensing temperature is to be developed after completion of the experimental tests. Desktop implementation of setpoint condensing temperature reset control and energy saving measures by variable speed driving, water mist pre-cooling and load sharing was carried out, and the potential reduction of chiller electricity consumption in typical office buildings in subtropical climate was assessed. This assessment can be repeated after calibration of the numerical chiller models. Through the design of the chiller experimental rig and implementation with a new DDC driver capable of variable setpoint condensing temperature control in this project, the project team has demonstrated that this novel method of chiller control is applicable to both new and existing chiller plants for energy saving. Let alone new buildings, existing air-cooled multiple-chiller plants can be modified to become variable speed fan driving and bypass the existing chiller control with a new digital control driver for resetting the condensing temperature setpoint. The measured results of changes of air state (temperature and RH) at several locations along the condenser air flow path at diverse weather-load conditions in this project can be used to assess the effectiveness of water mist pre-cooling, including any evaporation of water mist inside the condenser coil which would not moisten the coil surface but enhance the heat rejection effectiveness. Five refereed journal papers were published to report on the findings of the project. The researched results were also publicized in five international conferences in 2013 - 2015. A seminar was delivered to engineers of a leading consulting firm in 2014 to share the principle and method of variable setpoint condensing temperature control of chillers for energy saving. Data set of chiller COP at changes of load and climate conditions were generated in this project. Data of possible energy saving using setpoint condensing temperature reset control together with water mist pre-cooling for air-cooled screw chillers were produced. The data would be useful to building services engineers in evaluating design alternatives and in assessing chiller operation and performance.

511412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
511412.value: In the course of this project, the PI has communicated with Delta Control and chiller suppliers including Climaveneta, Midea, Cold Magic and Carrier about the principle and method of variable setpoint condensing temperature control for air-cooled chillers. Possible collaboration with chiller manufacturers on development of built-in control drivers for operating chillers with this new control method for energy efficiency is to be pursued. The development of chiller control method and numerical chiller models for system simulation achieved in this project also tells that the current AHRI performance rating method for chillers is inadequate, and advancement to a more sophisticated rating method is needed for international application. Because of limited resource and experimental facilities, this project is unable to thoroughly analyze the effect of water mist droplet size and generation rate on chiller efficiency at diverse weather-load conditions. A possible approach may be to build a computational fluid dynamic model to study the heat and mass transfer between the water mist, the cooling air stream and the condensing refrigerant through the condenser coils. This will be an interesting issue for future research.

511412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
511412.value: Chillers are used in almost all commercial buildings for the provision of air conditioning, and they consume huge amount of electricity. These chillers work with high condensing temperature at a high setpoint based on the summer design conditions, and are inefficient in energy use. It is possible to operate air-cooled chillers at lower condensing temperatures when the outdoor air temperature falls below the summer design conditions. This project contributes to energy saving by setting up an experimental rig, verifying and developing a novel method of variable setpoint condensing temperature control integrated with water mist pre-cooling for air-cooled multiple-chiller plant in buildings. Experimental measurements of the chiller operating variables with and without water mist are carried out. Mathematical models are developed and calibrated for system simulation. Energy saving obtainable by adopting water mist pre-cooling and applying setpoint condensing temperature reset control together with variable speed driving is evaluated from the results of system simulation. The research outcome is useful to provide guidance to building services operators and design engineers in achieving energy saving in commercial buildings. The year-round energy saving with minimal consumption of water and its impact on the long-term energy demand of the building sector are assessed.

511612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
511612.value: Advanced analysis has become popular in many national steel design codes. The method allows for geometric and material non-linearities as well as static and dynamic loads and effective length is not required to be assumed in the design process. However, these works are mostly devoted to conventional building frames and little work was done on light-weight and long-span structures which are widely used as walls and roofs of commercial complex, aircraft hangar and stadia. The use of this better design method is particularly important for slender light-weight structures where members are prone to buckling, but design codes are targeted at building frames dominated by sway or non-sway buckling mode, as can be seen in the extensive use of the sway and non-sway buckling formulae, which are not applicable to long-span structures where snap-through and member buckling is much more common. Recent collapse of a roof in Netherland on 7th July 2011, the roof collapse in Charles de Gaulle airport terminal in France in 2004 and other roof collapses during heavy snow showed the danger of this structural form. This project will focus on stability and robustness that failure and progressive collapse could be prevented. The method for static and conventional limit state design has been applied to design a few noticeable structures and detailed in Chapter 6 of the new steel code in Hong Kong, of which the proposer is the first principal drafter (see http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/index_crlist.html ). Further, research of the investigator also makes him to become the member of code drafting committee in China which consumes largest tonnage of steel in the world http://www.gb50017.com/expContent.aspx?catID=7&subcatID=29 and the work by the author is also referenced in the latest LRFD (2010, page 16.1-495). This projects aims to formulate a practical advanced analysis design method for slender and long-span structures and the work is sustainable as it helps to generalize structural design and to change the member-based design to system-based design based on the section capacity check. Advanced analysis has been applied to regular steel building frames but not commonly on long-span structures. This project extends the work to design of slender frames not classified as buildings. Actually the use of the better system-based design method is more needed in this type of slender frames than building frames stiffened by slabs and walls. Buckling effects and initial imperfections are more critical in long-span structures and they will be studied intensively in this project. 高等分析方法在许多国家的钢结构设计规范中已变得流行起来了。这种分析方法优点在于既能考虑静力荷载和动力荷载、考虑结构的几何非线性和材料非线性，同时它不需要估算有效长度系数。然而，以前的工作大多致力于传统的建筑框架结构，很少有涉及到在商业大楼幕墙、屋顶、飞机机库和体育场馆等广泛采用到的大跨度轻型结构。 高等分析方法在更容易屈曲的细长轻型结构的分析设计中有着非常明显的优势，但是目前规范中主要将其用于由有侧移和无侧移屈曲公式计算得到的屈曲模态主导的结构中。在以跳跃屈曲和构件屈曲为主的大跨度结构中，这些侧移屈曲模态计算公式是不适用的；而高等分析方法则不受结构形式限制，理论上可以用于任意结构。 大跨度轻型屋顶结构形式比常规结构有更大的安全隐忧，2011年荷兰一个屋顶的坍塌，2004年法国戴高乐机场候机楼屋顶的坍塌以及其它由于雪荷载而坍塌的屋顶案例都证明了这一点。这个项目就针对大跨度轻型结构，主要致力于从稳定性方面来预防构件的破坏及结构的连续性倒塌。 采用静力分析及传统的极限状态设计法已经成功设计了一些非常著名的结构，新的香港钢结构规范的第六章对这些结构进行了详细的讲述此外，本项目申请人的著作也被最新的美国钢结构设计规范所引用。本项目旨在为大跨度细长结构建立实用的高等分析设计方法，这项可持续的工作能够帮助普及、推广结构设计，让设计人员将基于构件的设计方法转变为基于系统的设计方法，而后者只需要做截面承载力检验。 高等分析在大跨轻质结构中的使用远不如在规则框架结构中广泛。实际上，细长框架结构相对于有板和墙辅助刚度的框架结构更需要一种更好的基于系统的设计模式。初始缺陷及屈曲模态对大跨度轻型结构的影响是非常明显的，本项目将对这些因素进行广泛研究已扩展高等分析在此类结构中的使用。

512112.label: Project Objectives
512112.value: The principal objective is to formulate a set of sustainable neighborhood planning and building design practice guidelines for reducing noise annoyances and stress of residential dwellers by properly utilizing the human audio-visual interactive responses. The success of the formulated guidelines depends mainly on whether the studied landscape features have restorative capability, whether geo-informative models can be used for predicting the view characteristics from residential apartments, and whether the relevant findings can be derived from solid scientific evidences revealed from field observations obtained from sound sampling protocols. The specific aims of the proposed study are to: formulate multivariate probabilistic models to predict the annoyance response or restoration ratings based on factors in relation to sound properties, personal characteristics and neighborhood landscape characteristics; investigate whether natural water landscape features like sea, or other built landscape features like podium or roof gardens can moderate noise annoyance responses and provide stress restoration of dwellers; compare the capabilities of different types of setting and different amount of natural and built landscape features in moderating noise annoyance and restoring stress; reveal the effect of personal characteristics on the moderation and restoration effects of different natural and built landscape features; investigate whether the noise annoyance moderation capability of a landscape feature is positively correlated with its stress restoration capability, formulate a set of best building design and city planning practices for achieving lower noise annoyance and better stress restoration at dwellings.

512112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
512112.value: 過高的噪聲水平已經成為城市居民的迫在眉睫的威脅, 而這些威脅將變得更加普遍。70％的世界人口的預期壽命將會是2050年。長期生活於高噪音水平，不僅可能造成滋擾，也會分散人們的注意力，削弱生產力，甚至可能導致對健康的不良影響。這研究項目的主要目的是制定一套可持續社區規劃和建築設計指引, 以利用’視聽互動’ 來降低噪音煩擾程度及為居民減低噪音所帶來的壓力。所制定的指引的成功主要取決於研究的景觀功能是否有減壓的能力，或是地理信息模型是否可用於預測住宅內可看見的景觀和有關的研究結果是否可以由從現場觀測得到的聲音採樣協議。本研究的長遠目標為城市規劃者和建築設計師提供免費的規劃和設計策略，可用於調節噪音煩擾程度和減低噪音所帶來的壓力。此策略是非常寶貴的，因為可能促進良好的現代都市人的福祉和心理健康，特別是對那些經常面對日常生活的壓力和不能容易享受自然的人。同樣重要的是研究結果可以提供可靠的科學證據政策制定者制定一套的社區規劃設計和建築設計指引促進更好的生活質量。

512112.label: Realisation of objectives
512112.value: The proposed objectives have been achieved by soliciting 2000+ questionnaire responses from residents who could perceive of different combinations of views of sea, urban river, greenery, and/or vegetation noise barrier from their high-rise apartments in Hong Kong. A series of field studies were carried out in five residential estates in Hong Kong. Noise levels were predicted for individual apartments before revealing their relationships with noise annoyance responses. In this study, noise levels in terms of LA10 (1 h), at 1m from the facades of different apartments in buildings were predicted using ODEN software. ODEN is a web-based noise mapping platform utilizing the scheme calculation of road traffic noise (CRTN). Questionnaire surveys were conducted via face-to-face manner in the public spaces located within the five sites. The questionnaire was divided into three main sections and the entire survey was conducted in Cantonese. The first section aimed at identifying the types and proportions of features that would be visible from respondents’ apartments. The proportions of a particular type of visible environmental features were elicited using a five-point verbal scale in Chinese (“Not at all,” “Little,” “Moderate,” “Considerable,” and “Predominant”). The wordings used in the verbal scale had been tested in our pilot studies with a number of laypersons with an aim to remove any ambiguities. The second section of the questionnaire aimed at eliciting the noise annoyance ratings induced by road traffic noises. Respondents were asked to assign their annoyance ratings using an 11-point scale (0–10; where “0” denotes “Not annoyed at all” and “10” denotes “Extremely annoyed”). In the third section, apartment details and personal characteristics of respondents including their gender, age, education level, monthly income, time spent at home, health status, and noise sensitivity were asked. Specifically, they were required to indicate the location, orientation, floor level of their apartments with the aid of a given site map which outlined the locations and orientations of all housing blocks located within the survey estates. In addition, respondents were asked to report the periods they normally stayed at homes each day (i.e., 00:00–06:00, 06:00–12:00, 12:00–18:00, and 18:00–24:00), and they could indicate more than one period. The entire day was broken into four periods, which was a compromise between the level of information required and the ability to match the daily life patterns of Hong Kong people. Additionally, respondents would indicate their self-rated noise sensitivity using a five-point verbal scale (“Not sensitive at all,” “Slightly sensitive,” “Moderately sensitive,” “Very sensitive,” and “Extremely sensitive”). Similarly, all the verbal scales included in this section had been tested in our pilot studies. The collected responses together with the predicted noise levels were employed to formulate multivariate logit models to predict the probability of invoking a high annoyance response from residents. The McFadden’s 2 was applied to check the goodness-of-fit of the models. A stepwise approach was employed for formulating multivariate models. Environmental factors (e.g., view of greenery, sea/urban river, and noise barrier), personal factors (e.g., gender, age, health status, noise sensitivity, occupation) as well as noise levels were input into the model in a stepwise manner. An examined variable would be included into the model if all the following three criteria were satisfied: (i) the variable was significant at 95% level; (ii) inclusion of the variable would significantly improve the McFadden’s 2 value; and (iii) inclusion of the variable would not alter the significance of other variables. Subsequently, the estimated coefficient values for different variables of the models were analyzed and checked against the validity construct. Interpretation was based on the estimated coefficient values and the detailed findings are discussed in the later section.

512112.label: Major findings and research outcome
512112.value: The importance of non-acoustical factors including the type of visual environment on human noise perception becomes increasingly recognized. In order to reveal the relationships between long-term noise annoyance and different types of neighborhood views, 2033 questionnaire responses were collected for studying the effect of perceptions of different combinations of views of sea, urban river, greenery, and/or noise barrier on the annoyance responses from residents living in high-rise apartments in Hong Kong. The collected responses were employed to formulate multivariate models to predict the probability of invoking a high annoyance response from residents (Objective 2). Results showed that the noise annoyance responses of dwellers could be moderated by audio-visual interactions caused by neighborhood sceneries (Objective 1). Views of sea, urban river, or greenery could lower the probability, while views of noise barrier could increase the probability. Placing rows of trees near to a noise barrier generally would lower the probability (Objective 3) and increase the perceived stress-restorative capability (Objective 6). Views of greenery had a stronger noise moderation capability than views of sea or urban river (Objective 4). The presence of an interaction effect between views of water and views of noise barrier exerted a negative influence on the noise annoyance moderation capability. The probability due to exposure to an environment containing views of noise barriers and urban rivers would be even higher than that due to exposure to an environment containing views of noise barriers alone. In addition to the above site characteristics, personal characteristics and daily life patterns also played a role on the annoyance responses (Objective 5). A high annoyance response would be more likely to be invoked for individuals who considered themselves highly noise sensitive or not so healthy. Individuals who were older than 45 yr, or were degree holders were found to be more likely to be highly annoyed. The above findings should provide valuable insights for urban planners and building designers in formulating strategies and practice guidelines to moderate the noise annoyance responses of residents living near a heavily trafficked road by making use of human visual perceptions (Objective 7).

512112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
512112.value: The scope of future study can be extended to cover built environment features in addition to the natural environment features investigated in this study. Of great interest to explore whether built environment features such as buildings will produce negative noise annoyance moderation effects. Above all, the findings can be employed to formulate a table summarizing the effects of different types of natural and built environment features for urban planners and building designers in formulating neighborhood planning strategies to moderate noise annoyance responses caused by road traffic noises.

512312.label: Project Title(Chinese)
512312.value: 用於下行負梯級先導及其于地面建築物連接的自持性三維物理隨機模型的研發

512312.label: Project Objectives
512312.value: Modeling of the downward stepped leader model. Downward stepped-leader preceding the first return stroke of a negative cloud-to-ground lightning flash always originates within clouds and propagates toward ground step-wisely. The leader channel usually shows branching and tortuousity that may be associated with the stochastic behavior of the lightning striking point. Taking account of these observed facts and those good practices in previous modeling studies, a set of criteria and equations describing the leader characteristics (such as channel radius and bending, step length and pause time, speed, charge distribution and current) will be developed and justified. Modeling of the lightning attachment process. Lightning attachment process, which determines the striking distance, may involve an upward positive connecting leader from ground or grounded objects. Due to this, many existing models has paid more attention to the criterion for upward leader inception. However, some researchers pointed out that even if a connecting leader is successfully incepted from ground or an ordinary structure, it starts slowly and does not have too much time to develop. As a result, it has no more influence on the striking distance. With these facts in mind, a set of appropriate criteria and equation describing the attachment process will be proposed and justified. Development of algorithms and computing codes for the proposed models. With the criteria and equations developed in above, specific algorithm for simulating the step leader and attachment process will be proposed and efficient computing codes will be developed accordingly. Validation of the model by comparisons with observed leader properties. With the models and computing codes developed, lightning parameters, such as the leader charge distribution, corona sheath radius, leader tip potential, leader speed, leader current, step length and pause time, ground electric field strength, total charge induced in leader channel and striking distance are computed for typical cases. Comparisons of these computed parameters with those in literature and in practical records will be used to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed models. Application of the model to lightning protection analyses. With the proposed models, lightning striking distance to flat ground and to various structures versus leader potential, leader charges and hence the return stroke strength will be calculated and discussed. In addition, with this 3D stochastic model, the probability of lightning striking to specific zone of a building versus lightning strength can be predicted and analyzed.
