512312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
512312.value: 下行梯級先導是雲地閃電重要的組成部分。因為它發生在首次回擊之前，而正是首次回擊會對人類和周圍環境造成重要危害。當梯級先導由雲中下降到離地面幾十到幾百米的時候，由於先導頭部和地面物體之間的電場強度很大，因而會造成它們之間的空氣擊穿。這個最後的擊穿過程就被稱作雷電連接，而此時刻先導頭部離地面的高度就稱之為雷電打擊距離。很明顯的，正是先導-連接過程決定了物體上的雷電打擊點，因此使得梯級先導和連接過程成為雷電保護領域研究的一個重要方面。 早期的先導-連接過程研究主要集中在打擊到地面和物體上閃電的光電觀測上。 在過去幾十年中，隨著電子計算機運算能力的極速提升，通過數值模擬的方式來研究先導-連接過程變得很廣泛。但是，所有現有的模型都有它們固有的缺陷。一些模型僅僅依賴於物理定理和數學方程，使得先導微觀尺度過程變得模糊，同時某些邊界條件的缺乏都會限制模型的應用；還有一些模型用隨機的方式來描述先導行進行為，但是缺少合適的物理解釋。總的來說，缺少相應的模型將基於充分物理基礎的數值計算與實際的工程應用結合起來。 本研究的目的是研發一種自持性的三維先導-連接過程模型，在這其中既考慮到了梯級先導的物理過程又體現了它的隨機特性。在這個模型中，梯級先導的特性包括：行進方向的隨機性、梯級的長度、每一步的停頓時間以及先導速度等等都可以用一系列的方程和約束條件來描述，使之成為同時體現隨機性和梯級性的先導通道。雷電參數比如：先導電荷、速度、電流、步長和時間、電暈區半徑以及對地打擊距離都可以估算出來。此外，本模型還具潛力作為一個虛擬實驗室來模擬雷電打擊各類建築物的行為，從而對建築物雷電保護提供分析。

512312.label: Realisation of objectives
512312.value: This project aims to develop a 3-dimensional downward stepped leader and attachment model that consider properly both the physical processes and random nature of the stepped leader behavior. There are 5 project objectives, all of them have been achieved. Specifically, In the first project year, based on thorough review of previous studies we succeeded in developing a self-organized 3-D model for downward stepped-leader preceding the first return stroke. Taking account of existing observation facts and previous modelling practices, a set of criteria and equations describing downward leader characteristics including the channel radius and bending, step length and pause time, speed, charge distribution and current were derived. Meanwhile, specific computing algorithm and code were developed and were used to simulate the property of the evolution of downward negative leader (DNL). Furthermore, based on statistics of the simulation results of DNL under various leader initiation conditions, a set of engineering approximations of leader parameters for convenient lightning protection analysis was derived. The results were summarized into a paper with a title of “A 3-D Self-Organized Leader propagation model and its engineering approximation for lightning protection analysis” published on IEEE Transaction On Power Delivery, vol. 28, no. 4, pp.2342-2354, Oct of 2013. Doi:10.1109/TPWRD.2013.2263846. These efforts made Objectives 1 & 5 and part of Objective 3 achieved. In the second project year, based on thorough review of existing facts on different upward lightning, a macroscopic physical model that is able to simulate an upward leader self-initiated from a tall earthed object under various conditions was developed. Also adequate algorithm and code for this upward leader model was composed and tested by applying it to upward positive leader (UPL). These efforts made parts of Objectives 2, 3 & 4 achieved. In the third project year, the model developed for upward leader were used to study UPLs self-initiated from tall structures under various thunderclouds with and without corona space charge layer effect being considered. As the leader initiation criteria, the critical corona sheath length and minimum corona charge as a function of the leader initiation height and the minimum leader initiation height as a function of the thundercloud condition for UPL were estimated and discussed. Evolutions of the speed, charge distribution, current, electric field, conductance and conductivity, and channel size and temperature of UPL under different thundercloud conditions were also obtained and discussed. In addition, this UPL model was validated with two sets of experiment data. Parts of the modelling results on UPL were reported at 33rd International Conference on Lightning Protection held on 25-30 Sep. 2016, Estoril, Portugal, with a title of “A simple physical model for self-triggered upward leaders from high-rise buildings”. Meanwhile the complete modelling results on UPL were summarized into a paper with a title of “A macroscopic physical model for self-initiated upward leaders from tall grounded objects and its application” submitted to the journal of Atmospheric Research, which is now under revision. With these efforts, Objective 3 and parts of Objectives 2 & 4 had been achieved. In the fourth project year, the above DNL model and UPL model were combine to study how an UPL triggered by a DNL from a tall grounded object under different circumstances. First, the space-time electric field profiles caused by a DNL were evaluated. Then, taking account of the vertical ambient electric field profile due to both the thundercloud and the DNL, multiple UPLs triggered from different heights of grounded objects were simulated and discussed. For validations, two cases of lightning attachment (UPL connecting to DNL) reported in two observations were modelled with this DNL-UPL combined model and promising results were obtained. The complete results were summarized in PhD thesis of CHAN Ming Kit as attached. With these efforts, Objectives 2 & 4 have been achieved. Besides, we also tried to couple our leader models into return stroke models. We have developed a leader-return stroke coupled model based on the time domain electric field integral equation (TD-EFIE). With the leader model result as the initial condition of a return stroke channel, a set of equations controlling the evolution of return stroke parameters, such as the current, charge deposit, radius and conductance of the channel, was derived. A trial of this leader-return stroke model yielded preferable results, which were reported at 7th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics (CEEM) held on 4-7 Nov. 2015, Hangzhou, China, with a title of “Dynamic Modelling of Lightning Return Stroke and Its Optical and Electromagnetic Radiations based on Maxwell Integral-equations”.

512312.label: Major findings and research outcome
512312.value: Firstly, a 3-D self-organized model of a downward stepped leader in negative cloud-to-ground lightning was proposed. In the model, the characteristic features of stepped leaders were generalized, so that parameters, such as the leader line charge density, corona sheath radius, step length, step time interval, step advance speed, and the leader charge versus the return stroke current and the striking distance could be predicted. The model predicted leader parameters were qualitatively compatible with observation results. Furthermore, based on statistics of the model results for various leader initiation conditions, engineering approximations of leader parameters for convenient lightning protection analysis was derived. The major results were summarized into a paper published on IEEE Transaction On Power Delivery with doi:10.1109/TPWRD.2013.2263846. [Journal-1] Secondly, a macroscopic physical model that is able to simulate an upward leader initiated from a tall grounded object under thunderclouds was developed. Based on a tri-layer leader channel structure and the energy conservation law, a new equation for estimating the upward leader propagation speed was proposed. Equations for modeling other physical parameters of the leader were also proposed. Especially, a set of initiation and survival criteria for a steady self-initiated upward leader from a tall grounded object was suggested. With the criteria in the model, the critical corona and charge amount as well as the minimum height for successful initiation of UPL from a tall grounded object were evaluated and discussed. The model was then used to investigate the general properties of UPLs self-initiated from tall grounded objects with and without the effect of corona space charge layer near the ground under different thunderstorm conditions. The results could well explain the leader properties observed in literature. The results were reported at 33rd ICLP held on 25-30 Sep. 2016, Estoril, Portugal [Conference-1] and were submitted to the journal of Atmospheric Research for publication [Journal-2], respectively. Thirdly, we coupled our leader models into return stroke model based on the time domain electric field integral equation (TD-EFIE). With the leader model result as the initial condition of the return stroke channel, a set of equations controlling the evolution of return stroke parameters was derived. A trial of this leader-return stroke model yielded preferable results, which were reported at 7th CEEM held on 4-7 Nov. 2015, Hangzhou, China. [Conference-2]

512312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
512312.value: In this research, we proposed and practiced a self-organized macroscopic physical model that can be used for both downward and upward leaders. With these models, the general properties of downward negative leader (DNL) and upward positive leader (UPL) were modeled and discussed separately. However, in reality, both DNL and UPL often appear in the same lightning discharge. In such a case, the DNL and the UPL will have mutual influence to each other, and the present models could not simulate the case accurately. Therefore, a more vigorous fully-combined DNL-UPL model is necessary, which will be our next target in near future.

512312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
512312.value: A lightning stroke to a grounded object often involves a downward negative leader (DNL) and an upward positive leader (UPL). It is the connection of UPL to DNL (the attachment process) that leads the lightning struck to the object. In earlier years, the study of attachment process was mainly based on direct optical and electrical observations. In recent years, the attachment process was also studied by means of numerical modeling. However, all these existing models have intrinsic disadvantages. Some of them relied only on known physical laws and its governing equations, so the obscurity of the leader micro-scale process and the lack of certain boundary conditions limit their usage. Some of them described the leader propagation scholastically but were lack of proper physical explanation. In this study, we have proposed a self-organized macroscopic physical model that can be used for both DNL and UPL. Applications of the model to observed attachment processes yielded promising results. The model can further be coupled into lightning return stroke model to form a leader-return stroke coupled model, which might serve as a virtual lightning lab to simulate the behavior of lightning striking to various structures for engineering lightning protection analysis.

513012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
513012.value: Biodiesel has been blended with diesel fuel for application to diesel vehicles for reducing diesel fuel consumption, CO2 emissions and air pollution. The amount of biodiesel that is allowed in the blended fuel has been increasing. Particulate matter originating from vehicle emissions has been linked to a myriad of adverse health outcomes, ranging from cancer to cardiopulmonary disease, and an array of environmental problems, including global warming and acid rain. The physical and chemical properties of particulate emissions determine their potential influence on the environment and human health. It is known that the use of biodiesel as a blended fuel may lead to a change in both the physical and chemical properties of the particulate. However, there is lack of detailed investigations on these changes. Experiments will be carried out on a 4-cylinder diesel engine which is commonly found on diesel trucks in Hong Kong and in the mainland China. The engine will be tested under different engine operating conditions. At each engine operating condition, the exhaust particulate and co-pollutants will be collected and measured to analyze their physical and chemical properties. The physical properties to be investigated include the size of the primary soot particles, the shape of the agglomerated particles and the nano-structure of the soot particles, as observed under the transmission electronic microscope. On the chemical side, the fraction of volatile substance adsorbed by the particulate, the black carbon content of the particulate, the organic and inorganic compounds in the particulate will be analyzed using different analytical instruments. The amount of particle bound black carbon in the atmosphere can effectively absorb solar radiation thus affecting the energy redistribution and global climate. The organic compounds include carcinogenic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), hopanes and steranes etc. To link engine exhaust with health effect, this investigation will also include analysis of the oxidative potential of the particulate through the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) on cellular level. It is known that ROS are essential intermediates in metabolism with powerful oxidative potential, and are known to be capable of resulting in the oxidative damages. This project provides information and scientific knowledge on the potential impact of biodiesel on the physical, chemical and toxicological properties of the particulate emitted by a diesel engine using biodiesel/diesel blended fuel, which are important for assessing the subsequent influence on our environment and human health. Such information is important but is currently not available. 柴油机燃用生物柴油和柴油的混合燃料后可相应减少柴油的消耗量，并可降低二氧化碳（CO2）和气体污染物的排放量。在生物柴油和柴油的混合燃料中，生物柴油的允许掺混比例呈一直上升的趋势。 机动车辆的颗粒排放物可以造成癌症，心肺疾病等健康问题，同时还会导致诸如温室效应和酸雨等环境问题。这其中颗粒物的物理及化学特性直接决定了其对健康和环境的影响程度。柴油机燃用生物柴油和柴油混合燃料后，可同时改变其颗粒排放物的物理及化学特性，继而改变其毒理性特征和对人体健康的影响。然而，针对其物理及化学特性的改变机理方面仍缺乏详细研究。 本研究将选取一台在香港和中国大陆普遍使用的四缸直喷柴油机开展实验研究。在不同的发动机实验工况条件下，测量和分析排放中颗粒物及其相关污染物的物理和化学特性。在物理特性研究方面，利用投射电子显微镜研究颗粒物的几何尺寸，团聚态颗粒物形状和颗粒物的微观结构等。在化学特性研究方面，将利用不同的分析仪器研究颗粒物中所包含的可挥发性物质，黑碳颗粒和有机物与无机物含量。存在于大气中的黑碳颗粒可有效吸收太阳能辐射能量，从而影响能源的再分配和全球气候问题。颗粒物中有机化合物包含有多环芳香烃（PAHs），藿烷和甾烷等致癌物质。从发动机排放对人体健康问题角度出发，本研究将在细胞水平下，通过活性氧（ROS）的生成情况分析颗粒物的氧化压力。活性氧被普遍的认为是一种在新陈代新过程中具有高氧化压力的中间物并且易造成氧化损伤。 柴油机颗粒排放物在不同燃油混合条件下的物理，化学及毒理学特性的评定对环境和人体健康显得尤为重要，然而至今没有这方面相关研究工作的开展。本项目将为柴油机燃用生物柴油及柴油混合燃料对颗粒物的相关特性的影响提供相关信息及提供科学依据。

513012.label: Realisation of objectives
513012.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. We have conducted experiments on a 4-cylinder direct-injection diesel engine. The engine was operated on the 13-mode test cycle using five fuels, namely, diesel fuel, biodiesel, diesel blended with 10% biodiesel, diesel blended with 20% biodiesel and diesel blended with 30% biodiesel. The 13-mode test cycle allows the engine emissions to be investigated under different engine loads and engine speeds. The exhaust emissions, including gaseous and particulate emissions, were measured with different analyzers. Particulate samples were also collected and analyzed. One of the engine cylinders was installed with a pressure transducer to measure the in-cylinder pressure. The pressure signal was converted into heat release rate for analyzing the combustion characteristics and their correlation with the exhaust emissions. Realization of the project objectives is reported in detail in the below sections. Objective 1. To investigate the effect of diesel fuel blended with biodiesel on the particulate emissions, including the mass concentration and number concentration and size distribution For each fuel and each testing condition, experiments were carried out to measure (a) the particulate mass concentration using a tapered element oscillating microbalance; and (b) particulate number concentration and size distributions using a scanning mobility particle sizer for measuring particles in the size range of 15nm – 780nm. The effects of fuel, engine load and engine speed were analyzed. Objective 2. To investigate the effect of diesel fuel blended with biodiesel on the morphology and nano-structure of the particles For each fuel and each testing condition, particulate samples were collected for the following analyses: (a) particulate samples were observed under a transmission electronic microscope to investigate the primary particle size distribution; and (b) particulate samples were observed under a high-resolution transmission electronic microscope to investigate the nano-structure of the particles. The effects of fuel, engine load and engine speed were analyzed. Objective 3. To investigate the effect of diesel fuel blended with biodiesel on the chemical properties of the particles, including elemental carbon, organic carbon, inorganic ions and organic compounds For each fuel and each testing condition, experiments were carried out to measure the regulated gaseous emissions and the unregulated gaseous emissions. The regulated gaseous emissions include CO2, CO, HC and NOx. The unregulated gases investigated include formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, ethene, propene, 1-3-butadiene, benzene, tolune and xylene. Experiments were carried out, for each fuel and for each operating condition, to collect particulate samples for the following chemical analysis: (a) volatile organic fraction and non-volatile fraction using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA); (b) the oxidation reactivity of the soot particles based on the TGA results; and (c) the organic carbon (OC) and elemental carbon (EC) content were measured using the Sunset OC-EC analyzer. PAHs were analyzed by gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (GC/MS Agilent 6890/5973). Three types of standards were used, including: (1) the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST, Gaithersburg, MD, USA) SRM 1649a urban dust; (2) Chiron AS (Trondheim, Norway) hopanes and steranes; and (3) the Wisconsin State Laboratory of Hygiene organic standard mixtures containing PAHs, n-alkanes, branched alkanes, cyclohexanes, and phthalates. Among the internal standards (I.S.), (2H10) phenanthrene (phe-d10), 1-phenyldodecane, and (2H50) n-tetracosane (n-tetracosane-d50) were obtained from Aldrich (Milwaukee, WI, USA), and (2H12) chrysene (chr-d12) was obtained from Cambridge Isotope Laboratories (Andover, MA, USA). Further chemical analysis include determination of 132 non-polar organic compounds with thermal desorption-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (TD-GC/MS) method for quartz fiber filter samples. Objective 4. To investigate the oxidative potential of the particulate matter via the generation of reactive oxygen species on the cellular level For selected particulate samples, cell toxicity due to diesel and biodiesel samples were established using (a) a sensitive macrophage-based cell viability; and (b) cellular (endo-) and non-cellular (exo-) ROS activity assays on a dose and time dependent manner. RAW 264.7 murine monocytic-macrophage cell line (ATCC, USA) was cultured in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s Medium (Invitrogen, USA) in activated Fetal Bovine Serum (Gibco, USA). Cell viability was analyzed employing MTT dye. The cells at a number of 10,000 (contained in 10 μl) were seeded per well in 96-well plate and incubated with different volumes of particle phase and gaseous phase PM extracts for 4 and 24 h at 37°C and 5% CO2. The yellow MTT dye was then added to samples and untreated cell control at a final concentration of 0.45 mg/ml and allowed for 4 h incubation at culture conditions, followed by replacement of 100 μl supernatant with DMSO to solubilize the formazan, which was spectrophotometrically (Spectramax M2e, Molecular Devices, Taiwan) recorded at 570 nm and compared with untreated controls (positive control) to determine percentage of cell viability. Endogenous ROS (endo-ROS) activity was measured by employing DCFH-DA probe. The non-fluorescent DCFH-DA probe due to its diacetate moiety diffuses into cell, where it undergoes intracellular deacetylation by cellular esterase enzyme to form DCFH, which further on reaction with intracellular ROS get oxidized to DCF, whose fluorescence measured is equated to amount of ROS generated. Reaction volume of 250 μl contained varying concentrations of PM, 10 μl cells and varying volumes of PBS buffer. A 10,000 cells (in 10 μl) were seeded per well in 96-well plate and incubated with particle phase and gaseous phase PM extracts at standard culture conditions for 4 and 24 h. 140 μl DCFH-DA (Final Conc. 20 μM) was then added to the samples and controls, and incubated for another 30 min at culture conditions. Final volume is made to 250 μl with PBS. Untreated cells and cells with H2O2 served as negative and positive controls, respectively. Change in absorbance of DCF per minute was recorded at excitation and emission wavelength of 485 and 530 nm, respectively, and the measured light intensity is normalized with those from standard H2O2 prepared in the concentration range from 50 to 1500 μM. PM induced exogenous ROS (exo-ROS) was measured similarly without cells and DCFH-DA is replaced with DCFH reagent. DCFH reagent is prepared freshly prior to the experiment by incubating DCFH-DA (50 mM) with NaOH (0.1 N) in 1:4 ratio, for 15 min, and diluted with HBSS to get a final concentration of 20 μM DCFH. PM free sample served as control. In addition to the above, the combustion process at each operating condition was obtained by measuring the pressure data and then converting them into heat release rate data to obtain the fuel combustion data at each crank angle for correlation with the other measured results. The investigations have also been extended to include 50% biodiesel and 75% biodiesel investigations for: (a) particulate mass concentration and number concentration and size distributions; (b) particulate morphology and nano-structure; (c) particulate volatility and oxidation characteristics; and (d) regulated and unregulated gases emissions.

513012.label: Major findings and research outcome
513012.value: The use of biodiesel could reduce CO, HC and particulate mass and number but increase NOx concentrations in the exhaust of a diesel engine. Also, more primary particles with smaller size are generated under higher engine speed or lower engine load or when biodiesel is added. Biodiesel and lower engine load favor the formation of immature primary particles while engine speed has less influence on the nanostructure of the particles. Particles from biodiesel and blended fuels have higher mass fraction of volatile substances. With regard to the oxidative reactivity, biodiesel soot has the lowest activation energy at all operating conditions. The soot oxidative reactivity is closely related to the nanostructure properties, volatiles and the oxygen content in fuel. (papers 1 and 3) Biodiesel blending alters nanostructure of the primary soot particles and reduces the temperature required to initiate regeneration of the diesel particulate filter. Hence the use of biodiesel would be beneficial in terms of regeneration of particulate in after-treatment systems. For the unregulated emissions, formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, 1,3-butadiene, propene and ethene emissions increase with increasing biodiesel in the fuel. For the aromatics, biodiesel addition leads to an increase in benzene emission but reduction in toluene and xylene emissions. However, there is no significant change in the total BTX emissions. (paper 2) Concentrations of PAHs, N-alkanes, hopanes, steranes and phthalates increase with increasing engine speed and load and their concentrations were found non-significantly higher in B30 (30% biodiesel) compared to diesel across different engine speeds. Thus, despite biodiesel addition to diesel fuel can reduce the total hydrocarbon emissions, there could be increase in the emissions of certain air toxics, including the PAHs. Following in vitro exposure to the exhaust, gas phase PM of both diesel and B30 exhaust is found predominantly more toxic than their respective particle phase PM. Between diesel and B30 gas phase PM exhaust, the results suggest that the higher rate of combustion capability of B30 and its water solubility, compared to diesel PM, could be the factors that made it potentially more toxic over diesel PM. Endogenous ROS activity of diesel and B30 PM (both particle and gas phase) increase with increasing engine speed. On volume basis, particle phase PM-induced ROS is much higher than gas phase PM-induced ROS. It is evident that B30 exhaust has significantly contributed to higher ROS than the diesel exhaust across all engine speeds. Comparable results were obtained from exogenous ROS analyses.

513012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
513012.value: The original objective of this project was to investigate diesel-biodiesel blends with up to 30% biodiesel in the blended fuel. The investigation was extended to include 50% and 75% biodiesel for particulate emissions, include the morphology, nanostructure, volatility and oxidative reactivity. It is natural to apply the 50% and 75% biodiesel fuels to the investigation of PAHs and oxidative potential of the particulate. Moreover, the current investigations were conducted on an engine dynamometer with steady state operations. It would be useful to extend the study to include experiments conducted on unsteady driving cycles on chassis dynamometers. In this project, biodiesel produced from waste cooking oil was used. However, biodiesel can be produced from other feedstocks such as sunflower, palm oil and jatropha. Different biodiesel fuels have different composition of fatty acid methyl esters and hence different influence on the emissions. This research can be extended to compare the influence of different biodiesels. The use of biodiesel also leads to increase of NOx. One potential approach to reduce NOx emission is to include an alcohol in the fuel mix. Thus, the research can be further extended to include blends of diesel, biodiesel and an alcohol, like methanol or ethanol.

513012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
513012.value: Biodiesel has been commercially used as a replacement fuel for diesel fuel with up to 30% concentration in diesel engines. However there is still concern on the influence of biodiesel on the emissions of a diesel engine, especially when biodiesel produced from waste cooking oil is used. This project is focused on investigating the diesel fuel blended with a waste cooking oil biodiesel on (a) particulate mass concentration, number concentration and size distribution; (b) particulate morphology and nano-structure; (c) unregulated gaseous emissions and chemical properties of the particles, including the PAHs; and (d) oxidative potential of the particulate matter via the generation of reactive oxygen species on the cellular level. Results indicate that using biodiesel could reduce the particulate emissions in both mass and number concentrations. Moreover changes in particulate properties are favorable for its oxidation in after-treatment systems being used in current diesel engines, which is positive in reducing diesel emissions. However, results also indicate using biodiesel could lead to increase in certain air toxics emissions, including PAHs. There could also be an increase in the oxidative potential of the particulate matter. Both of which could be harmful to human health.

513412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
513412.value: 鼻胃管置入是在管餵食、引流或排空中必不可少的臨床程序。在此過程中，須將一根塑料管從鼻腔插入，通過咽喉然後到達胃部。因為鼻胃管置入是一個複雜的盲操作過程，由此可能會引起許多嚴重的並發症和致命的醫療事故。醫護人員通常經過在人體或假人上訓練以獲取這種置入技術。在人體上訓練會使得病人感到不舒適，甚至可能危害病人。而在假人身上訓練，醫護人員不能獲得真實的訓練效果。 為了改善此種技術及臨床教學，提出了一種交互式的智能化的培訓系統，使得醫護人員可以在一個無風險的，具有高保真度的計算機模擬環境中學習鼻胃管置入技術。此系統模擬了真實的人體器官解剖結構、鼻胃管和腔體之間的交互、觸覺反饋、插入阻塞效果以及病人的反應，以達到高度保真的效果。此系統還模擬了一些困難的案例。訓練人員由此可以在此虛擬環境中進行訓練操作，彷彿覺得在給真正的病人進行鼻胃管置入操作。 再則，此系統還提供數量化的尺度以對訓練效果進行自動評估。通過基準於專家的操作表現，將開發一個智能化的評分模塊以對訓練者的熟練程度進行評分。此系統將使用低成本的硬件以使得它能在護理教學中被廣泛採納。訓練者可以自由地並安全地在此系統上按照需要自我訓練多次，由此，為他們提供了更多的學習機會，使得此計算機化的鼻胃管置入訓練系統具有提高置入技巧和縮短訓練時間的潛力。

513412.label: Realisation of objectives
513412.value: The objectives of the project have been realized. 1. The geometry of the nasogastric passage was modelled by making reference to the visible human dataset and human anatomy. 2. Simulation of nasogastric tube (NGT) insertion was achieved respectively by developing physics-based approaches based on engineering mechanics and finite element method, and by developing fuzzy inference algorithms that leverage the experience of expert nurses. In addition to visual and haptic feedback, speech command recognition and audio feedback were also simulated. 3. A custom-designed prototype was developed with force feedback device and a sensor-attached plastic tube imitating real NGT. The feedback forces were calculated in real time by implementing the two force models developed in objective no. 2. 4. Metrics including insertion force, force profile, location and speed over time and the actions during insertion were recordable by logging trainee’s manoeuvres at the graphical and haptic user interface, and the corresponding computational output of the force model.

513412.label: Major findings and research outcome
513412.value: (N.B. In the following, the references inside the square bracket [] correspond to the research output in Part C, with J stands for journal paper and C for conference paper) A virtual reality simulator for learning NGT placement was developed [J1, J2] to facilitate the learning of the clinical skill. Theoretical and engineering research were carried out to realise the idea. The virtual training system was positively evaluated by nurses experienced in NGT placement (submitted to 2017 American Nursing Informatics Association Annual Conference). A number of techniques were investigated to enable effective rendering of haptic feedback forces [J3, J4, J5, J6] [C1, C2]. Researches were conducted to achieve fast rendering of feedback forces using analytical method [J3] and to improve the stability and safety of haptic rendering [J4, J5]. Unlike the use of static rubber mannequin in the conventional training approaches, the simulator was designed based on human anatomy by making reference to the Visible Human dataset. Efficient methods that could be applied for segmentation and feature extraction were investigated and found to be effective tools [J7, J8, J9, J10]. The NGT insertion force was modelled using methods based on physics and fuzzy logic respectively. For the former, a hybrid modelling approach was proposed where finite element method was used to handle the geometrically more complex region between the nostril and the laryngopharynx, while analytical method was used for the less complex region along the oesophagus [J1]. For the latter, experience of nursing experts was leveraged to construct the force model [J2]. Considerable research was conducted to explore effective fuzzy system modelling approaches [J11, J12, J13, J14, J15]. Using fuzzy logic is considered to be more practical since it is difficult to obtain in vivo bio-mechanical data to parameterise the physics-based model [J2]. Besides, the project also produced one China patent filed (Filing number: 2014102205190). A press conference was held on 30 May 2016, which was covered by 9 printed media and 18 electronic media. It is one of the 10 most favourite PolyU research news of 2016. The project had led to the award of a pilot fund of USD1700 by the Halla-Newcastle Problem Based Learning Education and Research Center, Cheju Halla University, South Korea, to evaluate the simulator on local nursing students.

513412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
513412.value: The advanced fuzzy inference techniques developed in the project can be used to further enhance the accuracy and the representativeness of the fuzzy-logic based force model. More expert nurses can be recruited to parameterize the model based on their individual experience in NGT insertion. To provide further and stronger evidence, a large scale controlled trial can be conducted on nursing students to access the training effectiveness, evaluating their competence and confidence in carrying out the procedures after using the simulator. Moreover, an autonomous scoring system can be built based on the quantitative metrics provided by the system. The performance of experienced nurses can be quantified as benchmark with which the performance of trainees is compared to yield representative metrics of their level of competence. The interactiveness of the simulator can be further enhanced by stimulating patient response more comprehensively, e.g. body movement against intubation, facial appearance and verbal feedback, and by recognizing more speech commands of the trainees. The hardware use interface currently used is a general purpose haptic device with 6 degrees-of-freedom. A simpler and more intuitive device can be customized specifically for the training of NGT insertion to promote adoption of the simulator.

513412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
513412.value: Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement is a common clinical procedure where a soft plastic tube is inserted through the nose to the stomach for feeding or drainage. As the tube cannot be seen during insertion, a nurse may not be aware when it is misplaced into the lung instead, which can lead to complications. Training of the skill is conventionally conducted on patients or using rubber manikin. The former can cause discomfort to the patients, while the latter makes use of a static proxy which does not replicate human anatomy and insertion forces. In this project, virtual reality technology is used to enhance the training. A computerized system is developed based on human anatomy. It also provides interactive visual, audio and haptic feedback. The virtual patient can gag or cough depending on where the tube has reached in the nasogastric passage. The insertion forces are modelled based on physics and expert knowledge respectively. Quantitative metrics including insertion force, force profile, location and speed over time and the actions during insertion can be recorded. The computer-based method can facilitate standardized teaching and asynchronous learning. Comments from nurses experienced in NGT placement on the system are positive.

513512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
513512.value: 超高層大廈風火效應及週邊擴展

513512.label: Project Objectives
513512.value: To study room fire dynamics in supertall buildings with openable windows and green balconies, storing high amounts of combustibles, under wind action. To study the spread of smoke and firebrands from a supertall building fire to adjacent buildings.
rows: To study room fire dynamics in supertall buildings with openable windows and green balconies, storing high amounts of combustibles, under wind action.
To study the spread of smoke and firebrands from a supertall building fire to adjacent buildings.

513512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
513512.value: Many supertall buildings of height over 300 m have been constructed in the Far East. Fire protection systems basically follow only those requirements specified in current codes. Several tall building fires have occurred all over the world. People worry whether fire safety provisions in these supertall buildings are adequate. However, very few comprehensive studies have been reported on the dynamics of room fires in such tall buildings. Long-term fire research by the principal investigator indicates that large quantities of combustibles are stored in the tall buildings of dense cities. High ambient wind speeds through room openings at the upper levels of supertall buildings supplies sufficient air to burn up all stored combustibles under high radiative heat flux conditions in a post-flashover fire. Consequently, a big fire results due to the high burning rate. A big fire in a supertall building entrains more air for combustion at lower levels, and spreads smoke and fire to adjacent areas at higher levels. Air, fire and smoke movement not only follow the wind direction, but all other directions too, leading to potentially fast fire spread to neighouring buildings. Smoke will spread easily to rooms of adjacent buildings through openings such as openable windows, the doors to green balconies and to refuge floors due to ambient wind and air flow induced by the big building fire. Firebrands arising from the burning of modern synthetic materials which spread to adjacent buildings through the openings might ignite combustibles inside. Several building fires can readily become established to give an array fire. These scientific phenomena applying to a supertall building fire subject to wind action and having a high heat release rate room fire, as well as the case of firebranding causing multiple fires, are therefore proposed for study in this project. Existing fire models will be modified and applied to the simulation of room fires with high intake air rates under thermal radiation. Wind tunnel experiments with scale building models will be carried out to study the aerodynamics around buildings to better understand smoke and fire spread. The principal investigator is already advising a team of fire officers on the drafting of the next generation of fire codes. The research results will be applied to the drafting of local fire codes for supertall buildings. Further, results are also useful to address the urgent need for a better understanding of supertall building fires in dense urban areas. 在遠東地區許多已建成的超過300米的超高層建築中，只有少部份其配套的消防安全系統符合現行規範要求。世界各地高層建築時有發生火災，使人們開始擔心這些超高層建築的消防安全是否足夠。然而，迄今為止很少有研究報告全面分析在這樣的高層建築中的房間火災狀況。 長期火災研究顯示，密集的城市高樓里存有大量的可燃物。高速自然風通過高層房間開口提供足夠的空氣，使存放的所有可燃物在高輻射熱通量作用下燃盡，導致后轟燃火， 并最終引發高燃燒率的大火災事故。超高層建築中的大型火災會加大低層的空氣卷吸率，促進火勢和煙氣向鄰近的高層區域擴展。空氣，火和煙氣不僅會沿著風向擴散，還會從其他方向快速蔓延，從而引導火勢蔓延到鄰近建築。在外界風和建築火災引起的氣體流動的共同作用下，煙氣通過諸如可打開的窗戶、通往綠色建築陽臺或避難層等鄰近建築的房間開口快速蔓延。現代建築合成材料燃燒的零星火通過開口可蔓延到毗鄰的建築物，并引燃其內部可燃物。這樣的情況發生在建築群時很可能進而導致陣火。 本項目主要研究目的是將以上現象應用于受風作用影響的超高層建築中的高熱釋放率火災，以及零星火受風作用擴散的案例。現有的消防模型將被修改，並應用于模擬熱輻射作用下高卷吸率的房間火災。為更好地了解煙氣和火勢蔓延規律，將在風洞中進行小尺度模型實驗，研究建築物周圍的空氣動力學現象。本項目的首席研究員已經建議消防部門起草新的消防規範。本項目的研究結果可以用於超高層建築的新消防規範。此外，研究結果也有助於進一步強調，應充分了解在人口稠密的城市地區超高層建築發生火災的隱患和可能的後果。

513512.label: Realisation of objectives
513512.value: In this project, both objectives related to wind action on supertall building fires were achieved by completing the five tasks. The problems encountered in performance-based design in determining fire safety provisions were studied. Relevant results had been proposed to the Authority for deciding on the drafting of a new fire code for supertall buildings. Importance of wind effects on supertall building fires was discussed in several conferences. Objective 1: To study room fire dynamics in supertall buildings with openable windows and green balconies, storing high amounts of combustibles, under wind action. Fires in supertall buildings under wind action would have a high heat release rate. Burning combustibles stored in a residential flat of a supertall building under high thermal radiative heat flux was studied. The heat release rate in a post-flashover room fire at height under both cross and direct wind actions was studied in detail. The effects of wind, buoyancy and thermal expansion on a room fire with natural ventilation provision were investigated and compared. The room was taken as a single zone ventilation system of uniform temperature with two openings. A dimensionless system function derived from conservation of enthalpy was analysed and solved under different heat release rates. Air flow patterns of each scenario were also determined. Three steady air flow modes can be identified for fires of different heat release rates. At low heat release rates, the thermal expansion effect can be neglected. At medium heat release rates, the effects of all three factors should be taken into consideration. At high heat release rates, buoyancy effect can be neglected under strong wind. Atria are constructed in supertall buildings of multiple uses, with smoke exhaust systems installed. Stack effect in supertall buildings was estimated by using climatic conditions of three different cities. The necessity of providing appropriate smoke exhaust systems was pointed out. Performance of the natural vents would be affected when installed at height under strong wind. Smoke might even be pulled down by wind action if the building is located near to a tall building or on the hillside. The importance of studying the aerodynamics around a building located adjacent to a vertical wall while designing static smoke exhaust system was pointed out. Key equations of calculating the smoke exhaust rates and the required vent area were modified with wind effect taken into account. The mechanical behaviour of a glass façade in a building fire was studied experimentally in a full-scale burning facility. The temperature of hot air mixed with flame near the glass panes and the glass surface temperatures during the fire were measured. Heat transfer distributions on the heated glass pane surface were simplified from the experimental results. Further, glass panels were fixed to window frames with other materials such as steel, in close contact with the frame or with an air gap in between. During heating of such glass panes and solid boundaries by a fire, thermal expansion of the glass panel along the vertical direction of the glass pane edge would be restricted. Variations of thermal stresses on the glass panel due to non-uniform heating in a fire were studied by specifying appropriate boundary conditions. Based on the experimental results and solutions of thermal force equations, equations for non-uniform temperature distributions of the glass panel were derived. Bending moment, stress and displacement of the glass panel under two typical boundary conditions were calculated to predict the time and conditions for the occurrence of the first crack. Numerical study was carried out on estimating the heat release rate of burning wood chipboard. A compartment with two opposite openings under three different wind speeds was taken as an example. Three different grid sizes were tested. For each grid resolution, three slice file output quantities suggested for measuring errors in the velocity and scalar fields were selected for comparison. The predicted results show that wind action would increase the heat release rate of a ventilation-controlled fire, and decrease the heat release rate of a fuel-controlled fire due to cooling and dilution of air. Objective 2: To study the spread of smoke and firebrands from a supertall building fire to adjacent buildings. Many big building fires happened in the past involved burning furniture foam. The behaviour of furniture foam in flashover fires were assessed by a cone calorimeter under high radiative heat fluxes. Five samples of polyurethane foam, including three different pillow foams, one mattress foam and one expensive fire-safe sofa foam were selected. Both thermal and smoke aspects were studied in a cone calorimeter under heat fluxes of 20 kWm-2, 30 kWm-2, 50 kWm-2 and 70 kWm-2. It was observed that all the foam samples were burnt under heat fluxes above 30 kWm-2. Only one pillow foam sample was not ignited under a low incident heat flux of 20 kWm-2, but it morphed into a mixture of solid and liquid. Under heat fluxes above 30 kWm-2, the fire-safe foam burnt vigorously; the burning showed no differences from foam without fire retardant. The fire-safe foam even released more smoke and toxic gases with higher carbon monoxide concentration. From the above cone calorimeter test, foams commonly used in the market can only withstand small match fires to delay ignition time. Foam products should be protected by additional provisions, such as an external cover, to protect them against big fires. Wind action on firebrands and smoke spread from the burning supertall building to open refuge floors of adjacent buildings were studied. Numerical CFD simulation of the wind effects on surrounding buildings will provide detailed information on the wind flow field, which allows flexibility in exploring different building designs and their impact on the resultant air flow. Smoke spread depends on the surrounding environment in a dense urban area with buildings closely built together. For a building located next to a vertical wall or a taller building, turbulent effects due to incident wind fields would be important. The fire behavior in the compartment of high-rise buildings under wind environment was studied using a wind tunnel of length 30 m, width 1.6 m and height 2.5 m for exploring some effective methods for evaluating smoke movement and control in compartment fire. Wind effects on the indoor air flow pattern and smoke development were studied. The wind speed, distance between the barrier and the fire framework, and other parameters such as the fire height and door width were varied. Scale modelling experiments were performed in a fire wind tunnel at Nanjing University of Technology with associated modelling performed by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) – Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS). An arrangement with two adjacent buildings on each of three sides of a supertall building was considered in the study. Windward and lateral fire spread were investigated. Wind tunnel tests were used to justify CFD simulations with different wind speeds.

513512.label: Major findings and research outcome
513512.value: Major findings are: 1. Wind effects on Supertall Building Fires Both cross-wind and direct-wind effects on room fires in supertall buildings were studied. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) predicted results show that wind action would increase the heat release rate (HRR) of a ventilation-controlled fire, and decrease the HRR of a fuel-controlled fire due to cooling and dilution of air. The HRR in the fire growth phase of wood in a gasoline fire in the same compartment with a single door opening was compared with full-scale burning experiments without wind action. Results indicated that high wind speed in cross-wind ventilation design would not give a high HRR. However, direct-wind situation is hazardous in getting a bigger fire. Further, mechanical behaviour of a glass façade in a fire was studied experimentally in a full-scale burning facility. The temperature of hot air mixed with flame near the glass panes and the glass surface temperatures during the fire were measured. 2. Atrium Natural Vents under Wind Atria are constructed in supertall buildings of multiple uses. Buoyancy of the smoke layer is the key driving force for removing smoke out of an atrium fire by natural vent. Performance of the natural vents would be affected when installed at high levels of supertall buildings under strong wind. Smoke can even be pulled down by wind action if the building is located near to a tall building or on the hillside. Importance of studying the aerodynamics around a building which is located adjacent to a vertical wall while designing static smoke exhaust system was illustrated through CFD simulations. 3. Branding or Spotting Many big building fires happened in the past involved burning furniture foam. The behaviour of furniture foam in flashover fires were assessed by a cone calorimeter under high radiative heat fluxes. Five samples of polyurethane foam, including three different pillow foams, one mattress foam and one expensive fire-safe sofa foam were selected. Both thermal and smoke aspects were studied in a cone calorimeter under high heat fluxes up to 70 kWm-2. It was observed that all the foam samples were burnt under heat fluxes above 30 kWm-2. The fire-safe foam even released more smoke and toxic gases with higher carbon monoxide concentration. Results are used to study smoke spread to adjacent buildings with and without refuge floor with CFD and wind tunnel.

513512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
513512.value: Performance-based design with scientific research support has to be used for developing fire safety provisions for supertall buildings. As demonstrated in this project on wind effects on supertall building fires, heat and smoke emitted in a supertall building fire would spread upward, with air entrained at lower levels. Firebrands generated from burning modern synthetic materials, even for fire safe furniture foam, can reach adjacent buildings under the action of wind, leading to serious consequences. Post-flashover room fires may normally be ventilation-controlled with limited air supply. Direct wind action, as demonstrated, will give higher air intake rates in a supertall building through openings leading to the burning up of all combustibles inside a room. The situation is very hazardous for supertall residential buildings with many openings such as openable windows and with balconies for natural ventilation provision. However, the situation is not so hazardous with appropriate cross-ventilation designs. In addition to including wind effects on smoke and firebrands spread to adjacent buildings in dense urban areas, other fire hazards associated with evacuation patterns, means of escape, means of access, fire resisting construction and upgrading needed for active fire protection systems should be further explored.

513512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
513512.value: Both cross-wind and direct-wind actions on supertall building fires were studied in this project. Numerical simulation with Computational Fluid Dynamics and wind tunnel experiments were conducted to study fire-induced smoke movement out of the building. Wind tunnel experiments with scale building models were carried out to justify the numerical simulated aerodynamics around buildings. Both objectives on studying room fire dynamics in supertall buildings with openable windows and green balconies, storing high amounts of combustibles, under wind action; and studying the spread of smoke and firebrands from a supertall building fire to adjacent buildings were achieved by completing five tasks. High air speeds through room openings at the upper levels of supertall buildings under direct-wind action would burn up more combustibles to give a post-flashover fire. Smoke then spread to adjacent buildings through openings such as openable windows, the doors to green balconies and to refuge floors due to ambient wind and air flow induced by the big building fire. Firebrands arising from the burning of modern synthetic materials which spread to adjacent buildings through the openings would ignite combustibles inside. However, the situation under cross-wind design would not be so hazardous even when under high air speed.

513812.value: To develop a theoretical model to enhance fundamental understanding of the aero-acoustic structure coupling mechanism. To identify the major physics ingredients needed for the suppression of the dipole source by using a panel with a compact cavity and sound radiating path. We shall further survey and study the radiation impedance change with the use of the panel via vibro-acoustic coupling and the flow effect. To identify the key controlling factors such as mass and bending stiffness of the panel, and geometrical configuration of the cavity. Different structural properties are expected for different stopband. To widen stopband, a parametric study will be carried out to examine the acoustic performance when an array of panels with different structural properties and with common or different cavities are used. To validate all theoretical findings with further experiments and design the device.

513812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
513812.value: 對於如何有效地減低在管道內傳播的低頻的風扇嘈音，在技術上仍然是很大的考驗。特別是在一些家庭電器如窗口式抽氣扇、吹風機及家用空調設備中。一般常用安裝在管道內的吸音材料，往往需要很長的路徑方可取得較理想的降噪性能。而有源的噪聲控制是可以提供一個解決方案的，但它要求額外電源供應及其複雜的硬件設備，阻礙了它在行業中的廣泛使用。在這項目中，主要是研發一項新型的被動式方法去利用一對背靠空穴的短振動面板而直接消減由軸流風扇發出的低頻噪聲。當反相位的聲音從風扇的兩邊聚集到一起，破壞性的干擾便會發生。在先前的研究中，基於一個沒有面板的簡化配置上，已經證明這種方法在管道的風扇噪音控制有著巨大潛力。但在擴大的殼體結構上，風扇所提供流動的能力被降低了。在本研究中，使用了面板覆蓋的外殼空腔去解決此問題。當從軸流式風扇直接所產生的偶極性聲波射在面板上，面板造成震動，然後聲波傳播到管道和空穴。通過適當的設計，這些聲波對來自風扇的直接聲波做成破壞性的聲學干擾從而降低了噪音的水平。然而，由於是聲振中的近場耦合，這聲音消除方式是複雜的。這項建議的研究，主要集中在開發一個理論的模型，從而可以徹底分析和理解的聲音消除理論，並建立一個合適的設計工具，以簡化和優化這樣設備的發展。 這新型的設計，將考慮到偶極聲波，振動面板及背聲學之間的完全耦合。由於在短的管道中，聲音被多次反射是特性也將包括在此研究內。也會有系統地評估有關插入損耗方面的影響、面板結構及性質的重要設計參數和幾何結構的空穴等參數。研究將進行驗證模型的實驗及確定數值性預算的結果。也將進行探討此裝置在家用電器產品中的應用。

513812.label: Realisation of objectives
513812.value: The four objectives stated above have been realized. More specifically: (1) A two-dimensional configuration of the duct with two flush mounted membranes covering a side-branch cavity was formed. The dipole source which radiates sound waves to both upstream and downstream with antiphase in the duct was placed at the centre. When an acoustic wave from the dipole source was incident on the panel, the panel was excited to vibrate. The vibration of the panel caused sound radiations that interfered with the radiated wave from dipole source. A simple analytical model was developed by involving the coupling between panel vibration, acoustic pressure inside the cavity and duct as well as sound radiation from the dipole source so that the sound cancellation mechanism by the membrane could be explained. (2) A full set of discretized linear systems with decomposition coefficients relating to cavity pressure and panel displacement as unknowns was obtained. The resultant sound radiation from the panel and its interference with the sound waves from the dipole source was determined based on the solutions of the system. As a result, insertion loss at the outlet of upstream and downstream of duct was predicted. This theoretical model was validated both numerically and experimentally. (3) A commercial software COMSOL MULTIPHYSICS finite element method (FEM) was employed to validate the analytical model in case of mean flow. The numerical simulation was composed of acoustical domain for fluid to describe the sound wave propagation in the flow duct and cavity and the structural domain for the induced vibration of the membrane. As a result, the vibration response and sound pressure distribution in the duct were obtained. (4) The modal analysis based on the analytical and numerical result was conducted in order to explain the role of membrane to undergo sound cancellation mechanism. The flow effect and the influence of the location of the dipole source on the modal response and insertion loss were investigated. The physics behind the cross-modal interaction due to the mean flow was explained. (5) The change of tension and mass on the insertion loss and stopband was investigated so that the optimal value for achieving the highest level of insertion loss in particular frequency range was obtained. (6) The experimental test rig including the duct and tensile machine was manufactured. A speaker and subsonic axial fan was installed at the centre of the duct. The signals from the microphones were acquired through an AD converter (NI DAQ Card 6062E) and the data acquisition process was controlled by the MATLAB program. By using the decomposition of the monopole and dipole as well as the sound reflections inside the duct due to the open ending, the sound pressure of net dipole radiation was obtained. (7) For the fan operation, there was slight deviation between the analytical model and experiment. To understand this, the time dependent sound radiation mechanism and the vibro-acoustics coupling mechanism of the systems were studied by adopting the potential theory and matched asymptotic expansion technique.

513812.label: Major findings and research outcome
513812.value: The performance of the cavity-backed tensioned membrane in controlling subsonic axial fan noise has been investigated analytically, numerically, and validated by experiments. The present work leads to the following conclusions: (1) With a suitable tension in the axial direction to balance the deformation due to the flow, the proposed device with an expansion ratio of 3 achieved a total IL of 10 dB over a frequency range of interest that could cover the blade passing frequencies of the fan with various rotational speeds. (2) The qualitative effect of the flow on the proposed tensioned membrane housing performance was the influence of the symmetrical feature of the dipole source. The odd mode vibration of the membrane was excited by the even mode of the kinematic boundary on the membrane when there was flow. As a result, asymmetrical excitation force and the strong cross-modal coupling in the modal radiation impedance were found due to the convective effect. (3) An asymmetrical feature was observed by off-setting the dipole source away from the centre of the membrane in the duct. It was because of the unbalanced acoustic pressure loading on the membrane. Such off-centre arrangement of the dipole source balanced the asymmetrical behaviour resulting from the flow effect. (4) Experimental studies were conducted on two devices. With a tension of 300N, the proposed device with an area expansion ratio of 5 could reduce the noise radiation of an axial flow fan by about 20 dB and 5 dB for the first and second blade passing frequencies, respectively. The other was a prototype made of a cylindrical cavity covered with four-tensioned membranes enclosing the subsonic axial fan with an expansion ratio of 12.6. With a tension of 220 N, the measured result showed that a significant noise reduction of about 40 dB at the first blade passing frequency of the fan could be obtained. (5) The depth of the backed-cavity played an important role of controlling the motion of the flexible membrane and consequently changing the vortex flight paths. (6) The motion of the inviscid vortex is strongly associated with the membrane vibration at the corresponding time instant if it was initial shedded at the height which was close to the oscillating membrane. (7) With the vortex excitation, the insertion loss spectrum was different from only mean flow effect. The slight sound cancellation was found for low Mach number (0.006≤M≤0.013) while a strong sound suppression was found at the intermediate range of flow speed (0.013≤M≤0.018).

513812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
513812.value: This study allowed the development of broadband and compact fan noise control or engine noise control in Nacelle. For widening the stopband, the membrane proposed in the current study can be replaced by light panel with variation of the width, structural properties as well as inhomogeneous surface or micro-perforated panel. This will lead to the non-uniform acoustic characteristics and the sound suppression mechanism will be different from the proposed method and it is needed to be further investigated. Apart from this, when there is flow, further studies are needed in the following areas: (1) Development of noise measurement system to identify the sound radiation from the membrane, dipole source and aerodynamic noise (2) Fluid-structure-acoustics interaction of the panel housing device with the excitation of unsteady turbulent eddy. (3) Investigation of the behavior of micro-perforated panel housing a dipole source with air flow.

513812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
513812.value: Fan noise control in a short duct such as ventilating fans and hair dryers remains technical challenge. Traditional passive measures such as duct lining often require sufficiently long attenuation path for desirable noise reduction performance. To deal with this, a novel passive silencing device which consists of two tensioned membranes backed with cavities to house the axial fan was developed. The noise suppression was achieved by destructive interference between the sound fields from the axial fan of a dipole nature with anti-phase and sound radiation from the membrane via vibroacoustics coupling. A theoretical model which allowed understanding the fluid-structure-acoustics interaction physics and sound suppression mechanism was developed. It was found that the first and second blade passage frequencies of the axial fan can be reduced by at least 20dB when four membranes with an appropriate tension were used. The results were validated by experiment. The asymmetrical effect due to the air flow which slightly deteriorate the performance of the device could be compromised with off-centre alignment of the axial fan. This study opens the door for numerous possible applications such as mitigation of fan noise inside air handling unit, computers or engine noise control in Nacelle.

514512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
514512.value: 基於電荷存儲的記憶體閃存（FlashMemory）在今天正面臨著尺寸繼續縮小的空間有限，存儲密度很難再繼續增加的困境。在尋找替代目前廣泛使用的閃存的競賽中，在目前來看相變存儲器處於暫時勝出的地位，已可以小批量生產。但由於其較大的漏電流引起的功率損失是難以克服的，從而使其難以成為閃存的替代品。長期來看基於電阻變化的阻變存儲器（RRAM）可能因其低損耗和小的開關電壓而勝出。但開關電壓的不穩定和低重復性也是阻變存儲器所面臨的難克服的問題。另外一種還處於機理研究階段的不太成熟的概念是基於鐵電薄膜電子隧穿引起的阻變存儲器。但較大的漏電流也是難以克服的缺點。我們已証明在鐵電氧化物薄膜中鑲嵌金屬量子點的復合薄膜具有很大的電阻變化特征，但不確定的反轉電壓成為限制其應用的一大障礙。本項目立足於開發和研究一種具有小的讀寫工作電壓，大的電阻轉變，低的損耗功率的RRAM。其中一個創新點是將金屬量子點有規律地鑲嵌在鐵電薄膜而實現一種全新的基於鐵電隧穿結與量子點電荷存儲的非易失性存儲器。制備這種納米復合鐵電體氧化物薄膜和研究其電阻變化和存儲機理是本項目的研究重點。但本項目也將致力於找到結構更簡單的單一金屬氧化物的RRAM薄膜材料。

514512.label: Realisation of objectives
514512.value: 1. To achieve a deeper understanding about the tunneling (direct tunneling or others) and resistive switching mechanism through the ferroelectric tunnel layer. To achieve this objective, we have carried out piezoresponse force microscopy study and conductive AFM measurement of the 5-nm thick BaTiO3 layer. In the mean time, the resistive switching and on/off ratio have been measured. These results revealed the resistive switching nature of the junction, ie. by a ferroelectric tunneling mechanism. During switch of resistance from high to low states, the ferroelectric polarization also switched. Our strain tuning experiment also shows that the strain results in the change of ferroelectric polarization and thus the change of resistance of the ferroelectric tunnel layer. We also deposited BaTiO3 layer on the semiconducting Nb:SrTiO3. The ferroelectric polarization switching also induces the the change of Schottky barrier thickness and therefore the resistance change of the tunnel layer. All these results have enriched our understanding about the tunneling (direct tunneling or others) and resistive switching mechanism through the ferroelectric tunnel layer. 2. To realize the epitaxial growth and pattering of arrays of ferroelectric tunneling structures (FTJ) as well as multiferroic tunnel junction (MFTJ) structures. To achieve this objective, we optimized the pulsed laser deposition condition in terms of temperature and oxygen pressure during deposition and annealing. We have achieved the epitaxial growth of 5 nm-thick BaTiO3 layer on (La,Sr)MnO3 bottom electrode layer which is also exitaxially grown on SrTiO3 substrate. Cross-sectional TEM study reveals the epitaxial and layer-by-layer growth of the multiferroic tunneling layers. The LSMO is ferromagnetic phase and BTO is very good ferroelectric phase. The top electrode is NiFe which is ferromagnetic phase. 3. To explore the possibility of increasing operation temperature of magnetic tunneling for the MFTJ by strain engineering or doping of the ferromagnetic conducting layer. To achieve this objective, we have explored different doping levels of LSMO ferromagnetic oxide. The Curie temperature of ferromagnetic properties can be tuned to room temperature. However, to realize multi-memory states at room temperature is still difficult. Another approach may work better. We implemented PVDF (organic ferroelectric material) two-monolayers as the ferroelectric tunneling layer sandwiched by two magnetic layers as top and bottom electrodes. With this structure, we expect that the multiferroic tunneling resisitive memory states can be further improved. 4. To demonstrate and understand strain effects on the FTJ and MFTJ tunneling characteristics. To realize this goal, we fabricated mechanical strain modification tools to allow applying tensile and compressive strains on the ferroelectric tunneling layer to alter the strain effect and c/a ratio of the ferroelectric layer. With strain applied, the ferroelectric polarization strength is changed, and the corresponding tunneling resistance is also changed accordingly. This result provides a direct evidence of ferroelectric tunneling resisitive switching and also another degree of freedom to modulate the device performance.

514512.label: Major findings and research outcome
514512.value: Multiferroic tunneling junction based four-state non-volatile memories are very promising for future memory industry since this kind of memories hold the advantages of not only the higher density by scaling down memory cell but also the function of magnetically written and electrically reading. In this work, we demonstrate a success of this four-state memory in a material system of on NiFe/BaTiO3/La0.7Sr0.3MnO3 with improved memory characteristics such as lower switching field and larger tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR). Ferroelectric switching induced resistive change memory with OFF/ON ratio of 14 and 0.3% TMR effect have been achieved in this multiferroic tunneling structure. Strain engineering plays a critical role in ferroelectric memories, in this work, dynamic strain-modulation on tunneling electroresistance in a 4-unit-cell ultrathin BaTiO3 metal/ferroelectric/semiconductor tunnel junction is experimentally realized by applying mechanical stress to the junction structure. With an extra compressive strain induced by mechanical stress which is dynamically applied beyond the lattice mismatch between the BaTiO3 layer and the Nb:SrTiO3 substrate, the ON/OFF current ratio increases significantly up to an extremely high value of 10^7; while a mechanical erasing effect can be observed when a tensile stress is applied. This dynamic strain engineering gives rise to an efficient modulation of ON/OFF ratio due to the variation of BaTiO3 polarization. This result sheds light on the mechanism of electroresistance in the ferroelectric tunnel junctions by providing a direct evidence for the polarization-induced resistive switching, and also provides another stimulus for the memory state operation.

514512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
514512.value: During the study work in this project, we conclude that the ultra-thin BaTiO3 can be a very good candidate for ferroelectric tunneling-based resistive memory. This could be another approach for the currently extensively studied resistive memory which is very promising for next generation of non-volatile memory. However, based on this material, it is very difficult to realized multi-function and multi-state memory at room temperature, especially it is difficult to cope it to semiconductor IC technology. However, we found that if PVDF (polymer based ferroelectric material) can be made into 1-2 monolayers and in the mean time its ferroelectricity can be retained, a sandwich structure with ferromagnetic electrodes may realize multiferroic tunneling and therefore a memory device which can be magnetically written and electrically read be realized.

514512.value: Multiferroic tunneling junction-based four-state non-volatile memories are very promising for future memory industry since this kind of memories hold the advantages of not only the higher density by scaling down memory cell but also the function of magnetically written and electrically reading. 514612.label: Project Objectives
514612.value: To retrofit an experimental dual evaporator air conditioning (DEAC) rig previously built into an experimental TEAC rig, by adding an indoor unit in an additional indoor space, so that the intended model experimental validation and novel controller development for a TEAC system, to improve the control over indoor air humidity, may be realized. To further develop the previously developed TEAC model which only considered sensible heat balance, by considering the variations of both indoor air dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperatures, and also the effects of refrigerant pipe lengths connecting the indoor units and the outdoor unit, so that the new TEAC model developed will be available to assist in the development of the novel controller. The new TEAC model will be experimentally validated using the experimental TEAC rig. To develop a novel capacity controller for the experimental TEAC rig, based on the previous extensive controller development work by the PI and Co-Is including the novel controller (CCA-S) experimentally developed for a SEAC system for improved indoor humidity control, and the novel capacity controller (CCA-D) for air temperature only which was developed in a previously funded GRF project. The validated TEAC model will be used in assisting controller development. Extensive controllability tests will be carried out with the novel capacity controller developed using the experimental TEAC rig and the validated model if necessary.

514612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
514612.value: With the increase in living standards, air conditioning has been extensively applied to buildings in the tropics and sub-tropics to provide occupants with a thermally comfortable environment. Consequently, energy use for air conditioning has significantly increased over the last few decades. It is therefore very important to develop energy conscious air conditioning technology to achieve energy saving and contribute to sustainability. Multi-evaporator air conditioning (MEAC) may be regarded as one of the energy conscious air conditioning technologies. However, most MEAC systems currently focus on temperature control only, so that the potential of MEAC technology in achieving energy saving has not yet been fully explored. Therefore in this proposed project, based on previous extensive related research by the investigators on modeling and controlling both single evaporator air conditioning systems and MEAC systems, a novel controller for a three evaporator air conditioning (TEAC) system will be developed. The controller will be able on the one hand to control the indoor air temperature within a preset variation band and, on the other hand, to achieve a reduced indoor relative humidity, when compared to that achieved with on-off based temperature control only as with most current MEAC systems. The successful carrying out of the proposed project will help achieve better thermal comfort for occupants, improved indoor air quality (IAQ) and reduced energy use, through improved indoor air humidity. The long-term significance is the contribution to a) sustainability by reducing air conditioning energy use while improving the thermal comfort of occupants, and b) to the advance of MEAC technology. While the project outcomes are expected to be globally applicable, they will be particularly useful in subtropical Hong Kong where dehumidification using AC systems has always been a challenge. 随着人们生活水平的提高，在热带和亚热带地区的建筑中，空调被更加广泛地用于提供热舒适环境。因此，在过去的几十年里，空调的能耗大幅提高。所以，致力于发展能够实现节能和可持续发展的节能型空调技术显得至关重要。多蒸发器空调系统被认为是节能型空调技术中的一种。但是，目前的大多数多蒸发器空调系统只专注于温度的控制，所以这种多蒸发器空调技术的潜力还没有得到全面的发掘。 因此，在本项目中，基于之前对于单蒸发器空调系统和多蒸发器空调系统建模与控制方面的大量研究，我们将发展一种针对三蒸发器空调系统的新型控制器。一方面，这种控制器可以将室内空气温度控制在一个事先设定的变化范围内；另一方面，相对于目前多数多蒸发器空调系统应用的开-关温度控制，这种控制器可以达到更低的室内空气相对湿度。 本项目的成功实施将有利于提高热舒适性，改善室内空气品质，同时通过控制室内空气湿度降低能耗。从长远来看，本项目致力于 a）降低空调能耗，同时提高热舒适性的可持续发展模式 b）进一步发展多蒸发器空调技术。本项目的成果有望得到全方位的发展应用，尤其是对于像香港这样的应用空调系统减湿一直存在难度的亚热带地区。

514612.label: Realisation of objectives
514612.value: The proposed project objectives were realized through retrofitting an existing experimental rig for a dual evaporator air conditioning unit (DEAC) to a TEAC unit and further developing an existing TEAC model for the current project use, developing a brand new novel capacity controller for improved indoor humidity control, with the following details: Firstly, the existing experimental DEAC rig was converted into an experimental TEAC rig, with its compressor capacity being 6.5 kW at 50 Hz power supply, working together with two IUs of 2.63 kW cooling capacity each. An additional IU of a larger rated capacity of 4.5 kW, with its matching EEV, was added by installing it in an additional IS in the HVAC Laboratory of the BSE Department. Therefore, a new compressor of larger capacity of ~ 12.5 kW at 50 Hz was used. There were also a number of other associated modifications as detailed in the project proposal. Secondly, the previous TEAC model was only concerned with indoor sensible heat balance, and was not experimentally validated. Therefore, in order to use the model for improved indoor humidity control, the TEAC model was further developed taking into account both sensible and latent heat balances on the air side of all IUs. The further developed model, was experimentally validated using the TEAC experimental rig. Thirdly, the development of the novel capacity controller for a TEAC system for improved indoor air humidity control was based on the two previous developed control algorithms: one for a DEAC system for temperature control and the other for a single evaporator air conditioning unit for improved indoor humidity control, respectively. Although the controller developed did not directly control indoor air humidity, it addressed two issues causing possible high indoor humidity when using an on-off temperature only controlled TEAC system: the absence of de-humidification and the re-evaporation of condensate on the surface of an IU while its matching fan was still in operation during an off-period when the indoor air temperature setting was satisfied and the refrigerant supply to the IU completely stopped. This was realized through supplying less refrigerant, instead of completely stopping its supply, and at the same time, running the supply fan at a lower speed. Consequently, improved humidity control, as compared to that under on-off temperature only control, was achieved. Here it was worthy to note that under the control of the novel controller, the matching of output cooling capacity of an IU in a TEAC system to cooling load in an IS was not realized by accurately controlling the refrigerant mass flow rate at a specific value, but rather by the different operating duration at a high speed and a low speed period. Consequently, while indoor air dry-bulb temperature was controlled within a preset dead-band, indoor air humidity was also suppressed at a relatively low level. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the controller developed, it was experimentally validated through extensive control-ability tests using the experimental rig. The controllability test results showed that, with the novel controller, improved control over indoor air humidity and better energy efficiency for the TEAC system was obtained, as compared to the use of traditional On-Off controllers extensively used in MEAC systems. Therefore, the three objectives were fully realized.

514612.label: Major findings and research outcome
514612.value: The followings are the outcomes of the project: 1. The development of an experimental TEAC system, consisting of three indoor spaces (IS) and one outdoor space; 2. The experimental operating characteristics of the experimental TEAC system, in particular, the operating characteristics on both the refrigerant side and air side of each IU/ IS in the experimental TEAC system are the first of its kind in the open literature. 3. The experimentally validated dynamic TEAC mathematical model which helped the development of the novel capacity controller for improved indoor humidity control; 4. The novel capacity controller that can achieve improved control over indoor air humidity and better energy efficiency for the TEAC system.

514612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
514612.value: A number of future possible studies are proposed as follows: 1. For the operating characteristics of the TEAC system, since other operating parameters, such as indoor air humidity and supply fan speed might also affect the operating characteristics of a TEAC system, it is suggested that the influences of other operating parameters in a TEAC system on its operating characteristics should be further studied; 2. The dynamic mathematical model for the experimental TEAC system was experimentally validated and used in assisting the development of the novel capacity controller. Further modeling study on the operating characteristics of an MEAC system having more than three IUs/ ISs s can therefore be carried out, as more complex coupling effects for the operating parameters in the MEAC system can be expected; 3. For the novel capacity controller: while dry-bulb temperature in the three ISs can be directly controlled around their respective settings directly, indoor air RH were indirectly controlled. Therefore, further research on directly controlling indoor air humidity using MEAC systems should be carried out. Advanced control algorithms such as fuzzy logics, ANN may be applied.
