514912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
514912.value: Electrical and electronic systems in modern buildings have proliferated continuously to meet ever-increasing demand of businesses. These systems usually have a lower surge withstanding capability, and are susceptible to lightning-caused disturbances. In the past few years equipment damage caused by lightning surges has been reported continuously. The surge environment in buildings is getting worse, particularly when internal insulated down conductors are employed in a lightning protection system. To protect sensitive equipment against lightning, proper protection measures need to be developed, and should be taken in advance. The application of surge protective devices (SPDs) has been recognized as one of the effective measures protecting against lightning surges. This project aims to develop a systematic procedure using SPDs for achieving a compatible surge environment in high-rise commercial buildings. Note that surges may originate from the supply circuit outside a building or be induced during a direct flash to the building. In this project a framework using system-based compatible surge levels will be introduced for the low-voltage distribution system within a building. A systematic design approach together with the design data will be provided for the SPD application in the building distribution system. A modeling and simulation procedure will be developed as well for studying the non-TEM electromagnetic phenomena in a 3D wire network using a circuit analysis program. This project will provide practicing engineers with an effective means of achieving a compatible surge environment within large buildings. Under the proposed framework compatible equipment can be used in any place in a building without having any change of the protection scheme. The quality of the electromagnetic environment in buildings can then be ensured, and building intelligence be underpinned. 为满足不断扩张的业务需求，现代建筑中的电气和电子系统持续激增。这些系统通常具有较低的浪涌承受能力，容易受到雷电干扰。在过去的几年中由雷电引起的设备损坏报道连续出现，因而建筑中的浪涌环境日趋恶化，尤其是当采用绝缘引下线的防雷保护系统。为了保护敏感设备，防雷击，必需制定合适的保护措施。电涌保护器（SPD）的应用已被确认为防止雷电浪涌的有效措施之一。 该项目旨在建立一个系统的保护程序，利用电涌保护器来实现高层商业楼宇中相兼容的浪涌环境。需要注意的是浪涌可能起源于建筑物外的供电线路或直接雷击建筑物。在这个项目中我们将引进一个基于系统兼容的浪涌水平框架，提供一个系统的设计方法以供使用。针对三维线网络中的非TEM电磁现象我们将提供建模与仿真程序进行研究。 该项目将向工程师提供一个在大型建筑物内实现兼容浪涌环境的有效手段。根据拟议的框架相兼容的设备可以放置与建筑物中的任何地方，而不需改变已有的保护方案。建筑物的兼容电磁环境得以保证，建筑智能化得以支持。

514912.label: Realisation of objectives
514912.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved generally. (a) Cases of lightning accidents or damages were collected from the literature as well as consultancy projects with local railway companies, telecommunication companies, building management companies and developers. Those cases were analysed and problems were formulated for guiding the modelling of building electrical systems and the development of SPD protection schemes for the equipment used in buildings. It has been found that lightning surges in buildings can be generated in different ways, either via service lines connected to the buildings or coupling from external conductors or steel structures of the buildings. Surges on the electrical equipment appear on individual service lines only, and exist between two service lines if they are connected to the same equipment. A two-level protection scheme has been developed to provide protection for electrical equipment against lightning surges. In this scheme, surge protective devices (SPD) are provided at both the entrance and the end of service lines within the building (level 1), and at the equipment (level 2). For the equipment connected to multiple service lines, SPDs need to be provided between the service lines and the safety ground of the equipment, apart from SPDs at the each of service lines. An evaluation procedure for SPD location and selection has been developed. Matlab codes have been developed to implement the algorithms for circuit modelling and surge simulation. With the developed computer models of building electrical systems, SPD protection distance can be determined for practical installations. Separation distance for series-connected SPDs can be determined as well. General guidelines and conclusions for the SPD location and selection were provided. To facilitate computer simulation, a procedure for determining surge models of various protection devices and other nonlinear circuit components has been provided. (b) A full-wave PEEC model for the conductors over a lossy medium has been developed. The electric field integral equation was established first from the Maxwell’s equations. After lengthy theoretical derivation with special analytical techniques being taken, circuit parameters of the conductors are expressed using complex Green’s functions, which are evaluated using the Sommerfeld integrals. Dyadic Green’s functions then were derived for x, y, z current components in air above a lossy ground, as well as horizontal and vertical charge components. A challenge was encountered in the calculation of Green’s functions because of very slow convergence of Sommerfeld integrals. Different techniques have been tested, and the method of modified real-axis integration has been adopted for efficient calculation. The matlab routines have been developed to facilitate the numerical modelling of the wires for surge simulations. In lightning transient analysis, the Green’s functions for vertical wires and horizontal wires are different, and a correction term is introduced to facilitate the modelling of wire structures for circuit analysis. A simulation package has been developed in the matlab platform for simulating lighting surges in a wire system, which includes the routines for circuit parameters calculation, frequency-domain calculation of surges, and conversion between frequency-domain and time-domain results. (c) Surge propagation and attenuation within the building electrical systems have been investigated. The Shanghai Lightning Protection Centre had a large backyard in Shanghai, which was available for large-scale lightning surge testing. A test rig of 50m long overhead lines was set in the backyard to study the propagation of lightning surges over a lossy ground. Impulses were applied to the lines via an impulse current generator. Both surge voltages and currents on the remote lines were measured, and the proposed circuit models of lines over a lossy ground were validated experimentally. Building electrical systems are usually made by cables, such as single-cables in free air, single-core cable in conduits, and multi-core armoured cables, etc. Testing of surges on cables was performed in the laboratory. The laboratory has several cable examples collected in the previous research projects, which include 630mm2, 400mm2 and 185mm2 single-core cables, 400mm2 4/c and 3/c armoured and 25mm2 4/c cables. These cables run straight in the laboratory, and a fast impulse voltage was applied to the cable example under test. The propagation characteristics of these wires then were investigated. Velocity, surge impedance and attenuation coefficient of these lines have been obtained experimentally. A residential building prior to handover to owners was selected for field measurement of surges. An impulse generator was brought to the site to generate impulses to the building electrical systems, and surge voltages along the systems were measured for revealing surge propagation characteristics. Computer simulation has also been performed to reveal the propagation characteristics of surges on single-core cables. As it is difficult to run the cable vertically in the laboratory, surge propagation on cables running vertically has been thoroughly investigated by simulation. Simple equations or formulas have been provided to estimate surge voltage and current on the lines. Surge propagation on a vertical line has been investigated theoretically, and the characteristics of surges at a discontinuity was revealed. Coupling of surges into a building distribution system was also addressed numerically, and simplified formulas for evaluating surge voltages and currents in building electrical systems were derived.

514912.label: Major findings and research outcome
514912.value: Lightning surges generated in building electric systems have been investigated extensively [7-8]. Surges arising from separate grounding systems (cleaning and dirty grounding systems) were examined. SPDs are suggested to provide at the equipment between the service line and the safety ground. Characteristics of waveform and magnitude of incoming surges was provided, and can be used as the reference for surge assessment by the standards. Characteristics of induced surges on a line system within a building were provided as well in [8]. Simplified formulas for evaluating surge voltages and currents in building electrical systems were derived. It is found that induced surges can be effectively supressed with SPDs provided at both the entrance and the end of service lines. Guidelines for suppressing surges in distribution systems are available. A two-level protection scheme would then be sufficient for the protection of lightning surge impinging the equipment. SPD coordination with protected equipment has been extensively addressed, and an evaluation procedure has been worked out [3-4]. In [3] the protection distance offered by a SPD was thoroughly investigated. In [4] guidelines for the “High-Low” SPD combination were provided under both lightning transients and switching transients. Surge models of protective devices such as metal oxide varistors (MOV) has been provided, and an experimental procedure for determining model parameters has been proposed [6]. Modelling of closely-spaced cables was investigated as well [9-10]. An equivalent circuit procedure has been developed to take care of both skin and proximity effects among the closely-spaced cables, and a vector-fitting technique was incorporated to facilitate time-domain simulation of lighting surges. Modelling of non-circular conductors such as plates and rails was addressed [8,10], and the extended PEEC formulation for magnetic plates was developed, and can be used to evaluate the eddy current effect on the cables [2]. Characteristics of surge protection over the lines have been investigated theoretically [1] and experimentally [9]. Surge velocity, impedance and attenuation coefficient of distribution circuits were measured by injecting surge currents into three common wiring systems. Because of its relatively low impedance an armoured cable can cause a significant reduction of surges when it is connected to an overhead line. Both circuit branches and connected loads can alter the waveform and amplitude of a surge significantly. Such results have been verified by the field test carried in a 14-stoery residential building.

514912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
514912.value: Electromagnetic modelling of cables and plates have been well addressed by taking into account both the skin and proximity effects. A lightning transient simulation package could be developed for analysing lightning surges in a cabling system. A Ph.D student is currently working on lightning transient simulation using the PEEC method, and will complete his thesis later this year. This project addressed the effect of lightning strikes to buildings, outdoor services lines (electric power system, telecommunication system, electrified railway system). However, PEEC modelling and simulation of surges induced by lightning in a remote location has not be well addressed. The PEEC formulation in such cases needs to be investigated futher, and a new solution procedure needs to be developed for effective and efficient design and evaluation of lightning protection measures.

514912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
514912.value: Electrical and electronic systems in modern buildings have proliferated continuously to meet ever-increasing demand of businesses. These systems usually have a lower surge withstanding capability, and are susceptible to lightning-caused disturbances. In the past few years equipment damage caused by lightning surges has been reported continuously. To protect sensitive equipment against lightning, proper protection measures need to be developed, and should be taken in advance. The application of surge protective devices (SPDs) has been recognized as one of the effective measures protecting against lightning surges. A two-level protection scheme using SPDs is proposed to provide a compressive protection for sensitive equipment by considering the surges impinging and induced in the system. An evaluation procedure has been provided to facilitate selection and coordination of SPDs with protected equipment. Modelling of system components including various cables, wires and protective devices have been developed for surge simulation. Characteristics of surge propagation on the distribution lines as well as the data have been made available. Such evaluation tools could be used by engineers to achieve a compatible surge environment within buildings. The quality of the electromagnetic environment in buildings can then be ensured.

515012.label: Project Objectives
515012.value: Ductile fracture criteria in microforming: In this task, the validity and applicability of ductile fracture criteria, which are widely used in macro-scale plastic deformation, will be systematically investigated and evaluated in microforming under different stress conditions, deformation modes, and various micro-scale deformation processes via experiments and simulations. The effects of billet geometry size, microstructure, grain size, material properties on the validity and applicability of DF criteria will be investigated. The difference and deviation of the criteria in analysis of DF behaviors in micro- and macro-scale plastic deformation will be identified. The most promising and accurate criteria will be determined for micro-forming processes. Ductile fracture and DF defect: The ductile fracture is caused by tensile stress exceeding the stress strength of materials in forming process. The defect created by DF is called DF defect in this research. The DF behavior and the formation mechanisms of DF defects will be investigated via experiments and finite element simulations. The analysis and prediction of DF defects by simulation will be based on the identified DF criteria in Task 1. The target process will be micro-extrusion. The process, tooling and material variables, including tooling design, deformation condition, billet geometry, material microstructure, grain size and properties, and how they affect the formation and avoidance of DF defects will be explored. The relationship between the affecting variables and defect occurrence will be established. The methods for defect prediction and avoidance will be developed. Case studies: Upon completion of the first two tasks, the defect formation mechanisms, prediction and avoidance methods, and the modeling and simulation techniques will have been revealed, developed and established. The developed methods and technologies will be implemented based on the identified case micro-extrusion case study parts and a real micro product, viz., pogo pin. The objectives of this task are to reveal defect formation in the two categories of case study parts and to verify and validate the developed methods and technologies. Through case studies, the best processes for microforming of the case study parts will be developed.

515012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515012.value: 目前，產品朝著小型化方向發展，這有利於節約材料和能源，促進產品使用，保証微零件產品功能一致性，同時對進一步降低產品重量和體積具有重要意義。在眾多工業領域中，微型產品的需求顯著增加。因此，亟需發展微零件先進制造技術。目前，微制造技術，包括光刻技術和機械加工。雖然光刻技術已經成功地應用於半導體，微電子和微機械系統，但微機械加工技術包括微加工，微注射成型，微鑄造，粉末微注射成型及微成形並不像光刻技術那麼成熟。在這些微機械加工技術中，前四種工藝發展相對成熟。對於微成形，研究人員發展了許多不同的微塑性成形工藝。但微成形韌性斷裂和及其缺陷仍未被系統地研究。為了生產無缺陷的微零件，將宏觀成形的韌性斷裂行為和缺陷的相關理論不能直接應用於微成形斷裂的研究，因為他們有完全不同的變形機制和物理特性。在微成形中，韌性斷裂及其缺陷的研究是至關重要的。不具備微成形缺陷產生和避免缺陷形成的相關知識，要通過微成形生產無缺陷的產品將是困難和不可能的。 在這個GRF項目中，將採用試驗和數值模擬的方法對微成形韌性斷裂及其缺陷的產生進行研究。首先探討微觀尺度塑性變形的韌性斷裂機理和變形行為，然后與宏觀的韌性斷裂機理進行比較。不同的影響因素，包括幾何尺寸，材料性能和微觀結構，和工藝參數將被確定和這些參數對微成形韌性斷裂的影響將被系統地研究。運用微成形韌性斷裂的研究結果，微成形韌性斷裂缺陷將被研究。缺陷預測和預防措施將被建立。通過案例研究，發展無缺陷的微成形方法、試驗和數值模擬技術將被驗証。本項目將集中於以下問題的研究： (1) 微成形韌性斷裂准則研究。探討在不同變形模式，應力狀態，零件尺寸，材料性能和微觀結構下的微成形韌性斷裂准則的適用性和有效性，同時將研究這些參數是對韌性斷裂行為的影響。 (2) 微成形韌性斷裂缺陷研究。韌性斷裂行為和缺陷將採用微擠壓工藝進行研究。利用任務1建立的韌性斷裂准則，通過數值模擬和試驗方法研究不同參數對缺陷產生，缺陷預測和避免缺陷出現的影響規律。 (3) 案例研究和工藝驗証。利用微擠壓和彈簧針的案例分析來驗証總結的工藝。

515012.label: Realisation of objectives
515012.value: For this project, there are three main realized objectives. In detail, they are: Ductile fracture criteria in microforming: First of all, the ductile fracture (DF) criteria, which are widely used in macro-scale plastic deformation, were identified to be systematically studied in the project and then investigated and evaluated in macro-scale plastic deformation. To study the effects of billet geometry size, microstructure and grain size of materials and further material properties on the validity and applicability of DF criteria, different sample sizes, microstructures and grain sizes of materials with different material properties were prepared for micro-scaled deformation. Based on the different deformation scenarios, the validity and applicability of DF criteria were studied and the promising and accurate criteria have thus been determined. Ductile fracture and DF defect: In this project, the ductile fracture in micro-scaled deformation has been extensively studied and the defects generated by DF have also been explored and termed as stress-induced defect. In details, a series of deformation scenarios with scaling sizes were designed and implemented physically. The finite element simulations were conducted. The DF behavior and formation mechanisms of DF defects were therefore investigated via experiments and finite element simulations based on the identified DF criteria. The generally affecting variables of DF and its relationship with defect occurrence were studied, but they were explored less as they are different in different deformation scenarios. The general guidelines for defect prediction and avoidance were studied. For the case studies, they were employed for studying the DF behaviors and mechanisms and further used for exploring the DF criteria and their applicability in micro-scaled deformation. Through establishing the modeling and simulation techniques, the deformation of the case study parts was numerically simulated and the constitutive modeling of the deformation considering workpiece geometry and material microstructural size effects was conducted. By employing the physical implemented case studies, the related findings and the established constative modeling and finite element simulation using the size effect based constitutive modeling and the identified DF criteria were verified and validated.

515012.label: Major findings and research outcome
515012.value: 1) The ductile fracture and its related mechanism in micro-scaled deformation was systematically studied and its behaviors and occurrence were identified, which are found to be different from those in macro-scaled deformation. 2) The size effects arising from both sample geometry and material microstructural grain sizes in micro-scaled deformation on the ductile fracture behaviors were thoroughly studied via physical experiments and finite element simulation using different size scaled samples with different microstructural grain sizes. 3) The size effect based constitutive modeling was developed and the finite element simulation using the size effect based constitutive equation and built-in ductile fracture criterion was conducted, which provides an approach for modelling of ductile fracture in micro-scale considering size effect. 4) The applicability of ductile fracture criteria in micro-scaled plastic deformation was systematically studied and the detailed applicability of different criteria was identified. 5) A series of unique physical experiments were designed and implemented for providing case studies for study and exploration and further as case studies to validate the established models and approaches and verify they are right in detailed implementation

515012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515012.value: 1) The fundamental and basis of size effect: Upon completion of the project, it is found that size effect can significantly affect the deformation behavior and ductile fracture. But what are the basis and mechanism of size effects arising from different sources? This needs to be systematically studied. 2) Size effect affected deformation behaviors: The deformation behaviors affected size effect in micro-scaled deformation are different from those in macro-scaled ones. Therefore, the deformation based manufacturing in micro-scale is different from that of macro-scale. It is thus necessary to study deformation based manufacturing in micro-scale and further to establish the systematic knowledge to support process and tooling design and product quality assurance in micro-scaled based manufacturing via plastic deformation as we cannot directly leverage the established macro-scaled deformation based manufacturing to micro-scaled one. 3) Size effect affected micro-scaled product performance: Similarly, the performance of micro-scaled products made by micro-scaled plastic deformation is different from that made by macro-scaled products. The micro-scaled product performance affected by size effect needs to be thoroughly explored and studied to establish the related knowledge to support product design, manufacturing and further application.

515012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515012.value: The ductile fracture behavior and occurrence in downsized plastic deformation was studied and the applicability of ductile fracture criteria was systematically studied. Since the size effect arising from the down scaling of sample geometry size and material grain size, how the size effects affect ductile fracture and the application of ductile fracture criteria were systematically explored. In addition, the size effect based constitutive modeling of deformation process in micro-scale and finite element simulation were conducted. Through case studies and physical experiments, the findings related to ductile fracture and ductile fracture criteria in micro-scaled deformation were obtained and the validation and verification of the modeling and simulation techniques were conducted.

515812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515812.value: Three-dimensional (3D) auxetic textile structural composites are made with 3D textile reinforcements that have negative Poisson’s ratios (NPR). They shrink when compressed along a perpendicular direction, which results in a unique feature that the materials can concentrate themselves under impact to better resist the impact loads. When properly understood and applied with the advanced textile and composite fabrication technologies, this feature can be exploited for special applications such as impact protection with enhanced protective performance. The most important point to the achievement of this is to properly design the 3D auxetic textile reinforcements and the composite manufacturing process. A survey of the literature has shown that little work has been done for studying this important kind of composites, especially composites reinforced with 3D auxetic textile structure made of non-auxetic yarns. Therefore there is a need for a systematic study of such interesting composites. More specifically, the project will focus on the fundamental issues of the structure and performance of the 3D auxetic textile structural composites. 3D auxetic textile structural reinforcements will firstly be fabricated with high performance yarns using a modified prototype previously developed by the Principal Investigator (PI). Then, 3D auxetic textile structural composites will be fabricated using vacuum assisted resin transfer molding (VARTM) technique. Both the static compression and dynamic impact tests will be conducted to study mechanical performance of the composites. The unit-cell model will be established and the multi-scale approach and the finite element method (FEM) will be used to simulate the mechanical performance of the 3D auxetic textile structural composites made of different constituent materials and structure parameters. Finally, the 3D auxetic textile structural composites with optimized properties will be fabricated for impact protection. 三維負泊松比紡織結構復合材料由具有負泊松比的紡織增強體制作而成。當他們受壓時，會在垂直方向發生收縮，使材料變密實，這種獨特的性能有利於抵抗沖擊力。充分理解和利用先進紡織和復合材料加工技術，這種特有的性能就有可能開發出來，並運用於特殊的沖擊防護。為達到此目的，最重要的是合理地設計三維負泊松比紡織結構增強體和復合材料加工過程。通過現有的文獻分析可以發現，這種特殊的復合材料還未有相關研究，特別是利用普通紗線生產的三維負泊松比織物增強復合材料。所以有需要對這種有趣的復合材料進行系統的研究。 具體地說，本項目將致力於研究三維負泊松比紡織結構復合材料的結構和性能的基礎性問題。首先，基於本項目負責人以前發明的一種原型機器，將用高性能紗線織造三維負泊松比紡織增強體。然後，利用真空輔助樹脂傳遞模塑技術制作三維負泊松比紡織結構復合材料。通過靜態壓縮和動態沖擊測試來分析研究所制作復合材料的力學性能。利用基於單包的多尺度有限元模型，來分析模擬不同組分材料和結構參數與這種復合材料性能的關系。最後，使用最優的結構參數和材料來生產優化的三維負泊松比紡織結構復合材料用於沖擊防護。

515812.label: Realisation of objectives
515812.value: Objective 1: This objective has totally been achieved. Series of 3D auxetic textile structures were successfully fabricated using the previously developed 3D textile manufacturing technique. In these fabricated 3D textile structures, braided yarns with different diameters were used as weft and warp yarns and polyester multifilament was used as stitch yarn. Meanwhile, by eliminating the stitch yarn in the 3D auxetic textile structure, 3D multilayer orthogonal auxetic structures were also successfully fabricated by using ABS tubes and high tenacity polyester filaments as reinforcement materials after a series of tests of different materials. In order to facilitate the arrangement of reinforcements in the reinforcement structure and subsequent composite manufacturing process, a special mold was specially built with stainless steel. For the comparison, 3D non-auxetic textile reinforcements with positive Poisson’s ratio were also fabricated with the same materials and geometry parameters but with different yarn arrangement in the reinforcement structure. The relationship between the Poisson’s ratio and geometrical parameters of the 3D auxetic structure was also established to predict auxetic effect of reinforcement structures and their composites. Objective 2: This objective has totally been achieved. Both 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites were successfully fabricated with the above structural reinforcements via an injection and foaming process by using a modified VARTM manufacturing system. Both soft and rigid polyurethane foams were used as compressible matrix. While soft polyurethane foams were used to produce 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites with 3D textile structures made of braided yarns and polyester filament, rigid polyurethane foams were used to produce 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites with 3D multilayer orthogonal auxetic structures made of ABS tubes and high tenacity polyester filaments. 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites were also fabricated using 3D textile structures as reinforcement and impact hardening microgels as matrix. These composites fabricated exceeded our objective of this project. Objective 3: This objective has totally been achieved. All the 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites as well as pure polyurethane foams fabricated were tested under quasi-static compression and free drop impacts with different impact energy values. For the quasi-static compression tests, a tensile/compression device was modified by setting up two self-designed and fabricated compression plates. For the free drop tests, a special free drop tester built by a company in Taiwan and an Instron 9250 impact tester were employed to test impact protective performance of these materials. The effects of different factors including constituent material properties, reinforcement geometrical parameters and testing conditions on the deformation behaviors and mechanical properties of 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites were experimentally investigated in detail. The experimental study has proved that 3D auxetic composite has better energy absorption ability than non-auxetic composite under both static and dynamic loading conditions due to auxetic behavior. Objective 4: This objective has totally been achieved. The deformation behavior and mechanical performance of both 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites were analyzed using finite element method and successfully simulated under both quasi-static and dynamic compression conditions using ANSYS software. The simulation results were also compared with experimental results and the good agreements were obtained between simulations and experiments, Using the validated finite element models, the effects of constituent material properties, reinforcement geometrical parameters and testing conditions on the deformation behaviors and mechanical properties of 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites were systematically investigated in detail. The finite element analysis has further confirmed better energy absorption ability of auxetic composites. Objective 5: This objective has totally been achieved. Based on the experimental and simulation results, a series of 3D auxetic textile structural composites with better performance were designed and fabricated for impact protection. The application of these composites in different areas such as transportation, protective clothing, sports and medical care has been proposed.

515812.label: Major findings and research outcome
515812.value: 1. New manufacturing processes which can be used to produce both 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites with the same type of materials but with different ways of yarn arrangement in reinforcement structure. These processes are clearly explained in references 1 and 2 in Part C and can be further exploited to produce these composite materials for practical applications. 2. 3D auxetic composites have totally different deformation behaviors and mechanical properties compared with 3D non-auxetic composites under quasi-static compression (references 1, 2, 4 and 5 in Part C) and low velocity impact (references 3, 6 and 7 in Part C). All the experimental studies have confirmed that while the auxetic composites behave more like a damping material with a lower range of compression stress, the non-auxetic composites behave more like a stiffer material with a higher range of compression stress. The pictures of the 3D auxetic textile structure and 3D auxetic composite under compression in reference 2 was selected as the front page of Physica Status Solidi B, a famous journal publishing research papers for auxetic materials and structures. 3. Mathematical model which can be used to theoretically calculate the Poisson’s ratio of 3D auxetic composites for given compression strains (reference 4 in Part C). 4. Various finite element models developed to simulate the deformation behaviors and mechanical properties of both 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites under quasi-static compression (references 4 and 5 in Part C) and low velocity impact (reference 6 in Part C). These models were validated by experimental results and can be used for the prediction of deformation behaviors and mechanical performance of both 3D auxetic and non-auxetic composites with given structural parameters and constituent material properties. 5. 3D auxetic composites have better energy absorption capacity and impact protective performance than 3D non-auxetic composites (references 3, 5 and 7 in Part C). While studies in reference 5 show that 3D auxetic composites can absorb more energy than 3D non-axuetic composites under the same compression stress, studies in reference 7 confirm that 3D auxetic composites can reduce more impact peak force than 3D non-auxetic composites under the same impact energy (references 7 in Part C). 6. Seven refereed journal papers and four oral presentations at international conferences.

515812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515812.value: 3D auxetic textile structural composites are a special type of composite materials with negative Poisson’s ratios. They shrink when compressed along a perpendicular direction, which results in a unique feature that the materials can concentrate themselves under impact to better resist the impact loads. In this research project, 3D auxetic textile structural composites are designed and fabricated based on 3D auxetic textile reinforcement structure. Their deformation behavior and mechanical properties under quasi-static compression and low velocity impact are experimentally and theoretically studied. Both the finite element and mathematical models are developed to understand their mechanical behaviors under these two loading conditions. The significance and value of the project is to provide a basic understanding on the structure characterization, design principle, fabrication method and mechanical performance of 3D auxetic textile structural composites. Due to their better energy absorption ability and protective performance than 3D non-auxetic composites, these 3D auxetic composites will enable new applications in different areas such as transportation, medical care, military and sports, etc. The study will promote the new development of textile structure based products using the latest concept and technologies to increase the competitive capacity of the Hong Kong textile industry.

516212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
516212.value: This project aims to gain a systematic understanding of smart nerve conduits(SNCs) made of shape memory polymers(SMPs) to achieve peripheral nerve regeneration(PNR) by lengthening in a gradual and automatic manner. The specific objectives include the preparation of SMPs with water-triggered step-recovery function(WTSR); fabrication of SNCs with optimal mechanical and shape memory properties mainly by textiles structures and processing technologies; investigation of shape memory effects(SMEs) of SNCs in different programming processes under in vitro and in vivo conditions, respectively; study of the biological properties of SNCs and evaluation of their nerve regeneration efficacy with rat models. SMPs are defined by their capacity to recover an initial shape from temporary deformations upon external stimulation. They have gained increasing attention over the recent decade in biomedical applications. Reported medical devices based on SMPs range from general surgical to intravascular applications and filling materials to drug delivery systems. The main advantage of SMPs as biomaterials is derived from their diversified yet tunable properties, such as tailorable shape-recovery rate and stress, various stimuli and different SMEs. However, there have been few reports on applications of SMPs to nerve regeneration. Yet, the repair of peripheral nerve injuries has been a challenging clinical problem. Although the traditional nerve autograft has inherent disadvantages, in particular, limited sources of suitable donors, it is still considered as “the golden standard” because the current and most widely studied method using artificial nerve conduits fails to demonstrate the same amount of effectiveness as autograft. An alternative method using a manually operated nerve-lengthening device has shown satisfactory results in animal models, but it is too complex to be accepted by surgeons and patients. In our project, we propose a novel kind of SNCs fabricated with SMPs that can achieve PNR by automatic lengthening. This original research will lead to a new generation of nerve conduits with WTSR function, which combines the advantages of both a common nerve conduit and manually-operated nerve-lengthening methods for PNR. It is an entirely new application of SMPs. This breakthrough technology for PNR may create opportunities for minimally invasive surgery and smart biomedical devices using textile structures. Water-triggered SMEs with slow and step-recovery rate(e.g., 1mm/day) will result in new smart polymer functions and programming designs, which may inspire the development of SMPs for further applications. Aside from that, this project can enhance the international influence of Hong Kong in the fields of smart materials and biomedicine.

516212.label: Realisation of objectives
516212.value: We have completed each of the original objectives as outlined. The details are shown as following: Objective 1: To design and synthesize SMPs with WTSR function for PNR applications Achievements to objective 1: We have successfully developed SMPs with WTSR function for PNR application. The SMPs have fulfilled the following requirements: 1) The SMP possessed excellent water-triggered shape-recovery and fixity rate at physiological conditions. 2) The implanted smart nerve conduit possessed step-recovery (long recovery time) that is close to that of peripheral nerve regeneration. To meet the water-triggered shape memory effect at physiological condition, a series of Tg-dependent biodegradable SMPs with rac-lactide:glycolide weight ratio 60:40, 50:50, 40:60, 30:70, and 20:80 were developed. The molecular weight of almost 10^5 g/mol was choose for the synthesized polymer, as the entanglements of molecular chain supported to function as net points. The characteristics of synthesized copolymer networks were determined by GPC and thermo-mechanical experiments between 20°C and 60°C. Results showed the shape recovery ratio and the shape fixity ratio of all the synthesized polymers reached to near 90% and 99%, respectively. In addition, to investigate the water-triggered shape-memory effect, test of the recovery angle versus time was conducted at the temperature of 36°C in water. The macroscopic body-liquid-induced shape recovery process indicating that the SMP with higher Tg recovered slower, while the lower Tg SMP generally recovered faster. Also, the interaction of water with the PLGA copolymers was investigated by FT-IR. After immersing in water, it is obvious that the shape of the bound water spectrum in the 3000 to 3600 cm-1 region is contributed by O-H stretching and is quite different from that of copolymers without immersion. It revealed that the bounded water has direct effects on reducing glass transition temperature as a plasticizer. For meeting the essential requirement of step-recovery, we fabricated a tri-segment SMP-based device with different Tg in each segment for gradual-recovery purpose. High molecular weight poly(rac-lactide-co-glycolide) synthesized through ring-opening polymerization in bulk or in solution. Three different Tgs with approximate interval was desired, in which the gradual shape-recovery can occur in a wide range. The Tg of the copolymers was examined by DSC. The results showed that the Tg of poly (rac-lactide-co- glycolide) copolymer increased from 37.13 to 55.36°C with the content of rac-lactide increasing from 10 to 90 wt %. We selected networks prepared from PLGA-60/40, PLGA-40/60, and PLGA-20/80 for synthesizing the tri-segment SMP-based device with long recovery time, as these copolymers have the most widely and average Tg distribution. Objective 2: To fabricate SNCs by mainly using textile structures and technologies such as porous tubes with braiding and non-woven fabrics by electrospinning Achievements to objective 2: The SNCs with porous tubes has been produced by electrospinning and braiding technologies. To meet the specific requirements of textile fabrication techniques, we alter the molecular architecture of PLLA from semicrystalline to amorphous by replacing L-lactide with rac-lactide and introduce glycolide to the copolymer network. Three types of synthesized copolymers, PLGA-60, PLGA-40, and PLGA-20 were dissolved in dimethylformamide (DMF) and tetrahydrofuran (THF) at DMF:THF = 1:3 (v/v) at the concentration of 25% (w/v), respectively. Then each polymeric solution was injected into the textile apparatus in sequence to fabricate the corresponding component of the tri-segment nerve conduit. By ejecting a series of polymer solutions with different Tgs in sequence, a multi-segment conduit with gradual-recovery function fabricated on the rotating drum surface. Each segment with an individual Tg connected with one another from head to tail. Therefore, we manufactured a conduit with gradient Tgs in macroscopic level. Objective 3: To study the SMEs of SNCs in different programming under in vitro condition Achievements to objective 3: The SMEs of SNCs has been investigated in different programming (stretching and bending) under in vitro condition. The SME was quantified by cyclic thermo-mechanical measurements including the stretching programming and recovering process in single cycle. For all the electrospun networks, shape fixity ratios were near 99% under stress-free conditions, even after three thermo-mechanical cycles. These good shape-fixities are the results of verification at the temperature of 20°C and could prevent uncontrolled implant deployment during implantation. The shape recovery ratios were near 90%, confirming the existence of molecular chain entanglements as net points in the polymer network. Bending tests were performed by programming an angle 0° at 60°C followed by cooling below Tg. The samples were then immersed in water (37 °C) until a maximum recovery was observed, and the angle of recovery (θr) was monitored over time. The whole recovery curve presents an “S” shape and can be divided into three phases: early-immersing stage, accelerating stage, and saturation stage. The comparison of early-immersing time of SMPs with different Tgs showed SMP with lower Tg has an obviously shorter immersing time. Therefore, the gradual recovery application of these synthesized copolymers can be realized by overlapping these recovery time intervals. Objective 4: To investigate the biological properties of SNCs such as biocompatibility and biodegradability Achievements to objective 4: The biological properties of PLGA-based SMPs, including biocompatibility and biodegradability, were determined by Schwann cells in vitro and animal model in vivo. In vitro measurement showed the SNC fabricated from three types of synthesized poly(rac-lactide-co-glycolide) networks possessed the ability of supporting the adhesion and proliferation of Schwann cells. The MTT assay showed the viability of Schwann cells cultured in the synthesized copolymers extract had no significant difference with that in normal condition medium. Cell morphology measurement showed Schwann cells cultured on the three types of PLGA nanofibrous films flattened and extended in a sequential fashion demonstrating the synthesized shape-memory polymers introduced on cytotoxicity on Schwann cells. Also, the biocompatibility and biodegradability were tested by sciatic nerve defect animal model. HE staining measurement showed the implantation of the fabricated nerve conduit did not cause any pathologic damage to rabbit heart, liver, spleen, or kidney. HE staining images of the nerve longitudinal sections from experimental groups revealed the absence of an acute immune response in close proximity to the fibers, indicating the non-inflammatory nature of the fabricated PLGA fibers. In addition, the materials degraded partly in the period of animal model. Since the degradation of polymeric biomaterials may affect the tissue in several ways, the implanted polymeric biomaterials gradually released various chemical products of degradation, including common additives, impurities, monomers, and oligomers. These chemical components would introduce types of toxic reactions in the tissues by slowly migrating from the interior to the surface and the surrounding tissue, causing inflammation or pathologic changes in the tissues of interest.

516212.label: Major findings and research outcome
516212.value: We have made a significant contribution in three major areas this project: 1. Development of two theoretical models to supply guidance for the selection of hard segment and to study the mechanism of the water-responsive SMP We have developed two models named hydrogen bonding model and 3D netpoint-switch-frame unit-cell model for the design of WTSR materials. First, the hydrogen bonding interactions in hard segments of SMPs were systematically investigated, which is helpful in predicting and confirming the mechanical properties, shape memory effect of the WTSR materials for PNR application (Part C8, reference no.1-2). Second, the mechanism of water-responsive SMP was stimulated by 3D netpoint-switch-frame unit-cell model. We have determined that a hydrogen bonding switch responsive to water in smart materials should have a bonding energy smaller than that of the hydrogen bonding between water and the switch, but much larger than that of hydrogen bonding in water. The work provides insights for the rational design of water responsive SMP using hydrogen bindings (Part C8, reference no. 8-9). 2. Synthesis of five types of SMPs with WTSR function for PNR applications We have synthesized five types of WTSR polymers via ring-opening polymerization during this project. First, an amorphous, poly(rac-lactide-co-glycolide) system was designed and developed to exhibit tunable glass transition temperature, water-induced shape-memory function and good biocompatibility, as well as advanced textile-technology capabilities (Part C8, reference no. 5; Part C9, reference no. 2; Part 11, reference no. 1). Second, characteristics of SMPs, including mechanical properties, porous structure, wettability, crystallinity, stress memory and drug delivery capacities were also systematically determined (Part C8, reference no. 3, 5, 6-7; Part C9, reference no. 1, 2; Part 11, reference no. 1). 3. Development of SNCs by textile technologies for PNR application We have synthesized the textile structure based SNCs by electrospinning and braiding technologies and investigated their biocompatibility and biodegradability both in vitro and in vivo. First, we have produced tri-segment SMP-based polymer with three Tgs in sequence by electrospinning and braiding technologies. Excellent water-triggered step-recovery capacity and good biocompatibility were achieved (Part C8, reference no. 3-5; Part C9, reference no. 1; Part C11, reference no. 2). A student was trained by the research project (Part C10). Second, biocompatibility and biodegradability have been determined by cell tests and animal model. The results proved that it has good biocompatibility both in vitro and in vivo (Part C8, reference no. 7).

516212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
516212.value: 1. More material selections for SNC Poly(rac-lactide-co-glycolide) has been presented for biomedical application. However, other biocompatible monomers could also be introduced. For example, the trimethylene carbonate (TMC) monomer with outstanding tensile strength and flexibility has been studied for applications as heart constructs, cartilage implants, and sustained drug release carriers. Therefore, such kinds of monomers may be an excellent candidate to fabricated SNC with more efficient function. 2. Modification of SNC To further mimic the natural regenerative microenvironment, various support cells and/or growth factors could be introduced into our fabricated SNC to improve the regeneration effect. For example, Schwann cells are the main myelin-forming cells in the peripheral nervous system and play a prominent role in neuron regeneration. Meanwhile, nerve growth factor (NGF) is a neuropeptide primarily involved in the maintenance, proliferation, and survival of certain target neurons. Therefore, the mentioned cells and/or growth factors could be potential candidate to be filled in our designed SNC.

516212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
516212.value: Peripheral nerve repair and regeneration have been a unique clinical challenge for surgeons. We have developed a novel kind of smart nerve conduit fabricated from SMPs that can achieve peripheral nerve regeneration by automatic lengthening. Briefly, a series of macromers with different (rac-lactide) to glycolide weight ratios were synthesized and the characteristics of the synthesized networks were studied. Cyclic thermo-mechanical measurements indicated the robustness of molecular structure for shape memory function. Body-water responsive shape-memory behavior was also evaluated by angle recovery measurements. The shape recovery time of the polymer could be adjusted by the selection of comonomer ratio and then the overall gradual-recovery function of a device could be realized by suitable combination of different copolymers. Thus a tri-segment smart nerve conduit was fabricated from this polymer system by textile technologies, showing gradually recover in an in vitro experiment under stimulated physiological conditions, that is, body-liquid environment (37 °C water). In vitro culture and qualitative immunocytochemistry of Schwann cells assessed the biocompatibility of poly(rac-lactide-co-glycolide) networks. In vivo experiments in rabbit animal model were also conducted to ensure the SNC has the required mechanical characteristics and step-recovery capacity under practical conditions. Therefore, the WTSR SMP materials have a great potential in applications of PNR.

516312.value: 二氧化钛纳米管光子晶体与染料敏化太阳能电池的偶合以增强光吸收

516312.label: Project Objectives
516312.value: To fabricate TiO2 nanotubular photonic crystal by well-controlled electrochemical anodization. To couple the TiO2 nanotubular photonic crystal to TiO2 nanotube-based dye-sensitized solar cells. 516312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
516312.value: Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) coupled with photonic crystals (PCs) are now under intensive research due to enhanced light harvesting and hence improved photovoltaic performance of DSSCs. In traditional PC-coupled DSSCs, the PC and absorbing (TiO2) layers are either prepared by different processing methods or formed by different materials. The intrinsic drawbacks in those PC-coupled DSSCs result in low achievable power conversion efficiency. We will develop a novel strategy to seamlessly couple a PC layer (or two PC layers) to an absorbing TiO2 layer by a simple electrochemical anodization method. Both the PC and absorbing layers are TiO2 nanotubes. Compared with the absorbing layer, the PC layer has an additional periodicity along the axial direction of nanotubes which will reflect the photons in the stop band of the PC to the absorbing layer and enhance the light-material interaction time for enhanced conversion efficiency. Compared with other methods to couple the PC layer to a solar cell, our method shows the advantage of good physical contact, good charge transportation and good electrolyte infiltration. Moreover, the photonic bandgap of the PC layer can be continuously adjusted and the PC layer also contributes to the light conversion on the long wavelength edge of the photonic bandgap, which leave plenty of rooms for further device improvement. Assisted by computer simulations, we will optimize the structure of the TiO2 nanotube-based solar cell in order to achieve a high power conversion efficiency that is attractive to industries. Our proposed method also opens a door for the application of nanotubular photonic crystal in other areas. 在染料敏化太阳能电池中引入光子晶体，能有效的增强光子捕获效率，从而提高染料敏化太阳能电池的光伏性能，因此近来引起了科研工作者的广泛兴趣。传统的光子晶体基染料敏化太阳能电池中的光子晶体层和吸收层(TiO2)是不同的方法或材料制备而成，因此其固有的内在缺陷将极大的影响电池的光电转换效率。本项目将通过简单的电化学阳极氧化方法，开发一种新型的单层/双层光子晶体与TiO2吸收层的无缝连接技术。此光子晶体层和吸收层实质上均为TiO2纳米管，相较于吸收层，光子晶体层纳米管还具有轴向的周期性结构，能将波长位于光子禁带区域的光子反射回吸收层，增加光-物质作用时间，从而提高电池转换效率。相较于其他光子晶体耦合方法，此方法具有更好的物理连接强度、载流子迁移性及电解液渗透性。此外，该光子晶体的光子禁带连续可调，且在光子禁带红边区域，光子晶体层亦可参与光电转换，为进一步提高电池性能提供了巨大空间。本项目将通过TiO2纳米管基染料敏化太阳能电池的结构优化，研制具有工业应用前景的高效染料敏化太阳能电池。此新型方法的开发还将极大的促进纳米管光子晶体在其他领域的广泛应用。

516312.label: Realisation of objectives
516312.value: All the objectives are 100% achieved. Objective 1. To fabricate TiO2 nanotubular photonic crystal by well-controlled electrochemical anodization: A periodic current anodization method was used to fabricate TiO2 nanotube photonic crystals. The periodic current pulses used in the anodization normally consist of a high current (HC) density pulse and a low current (LC) density one. The value of the HC was determined to achieve an anodization voltage of around 60 V. The duration of each current pulse and the number of pulses was used to control the lattice parameter and the number of periods in the photonic crystal layer, respectively, and hence its optical properties. The photonic bandgap of the photonic crystal was adjusted by the lattice parameter along the axial direction. Objective 2. To couple the TiO2 nanotubular photonic crystal to TiO2 nanotube-based dye-sensitized solar cells: The electrochemically anodized TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal membrane was detached from the Ti substrate and then adhered to the FTO substrate with TiO2 nanoparticles synthesized by a sol-gel method. After annealing, the crystallized samples were soaked in a dye-containing solvent (N719 in ethanol), followed by rinsing in pure ethanol to remove non-chemisorbed dye before being assembled in solar cells, i.e., sandwiched between two electrodes (FTO electrode and Pt-coated glass counter electrode) with a spacer layer (25 μm thickness, SX1170–25, Solaronix) and melted at 90°C to fix the separation. The electrolyte (DMPD: 1.0M, LiI: 0.1M, 4-TBP: 0.5M, I2: 0.12M, 3-methoxy propionitrile (MePN)) was infiltrated into the cells by placing the electrolyte droplet in the cavity of the active area of the device before the device being sealed with UV epoxy. To increase the dye loading and hence to increase the power conversion efficiency, surface treatment of the bi-layer (or tri-layer) by TiCl4 was tried. Objective 3. To study the origin of enhanced light harvesting in different wavelength ranges, i.e., in the stop band and pass band (including shorter and longer wavelengths than the stop band): Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, optical absorption, I-V, and IPCE were conducted in combination with computer simulation to study the mechanism of light harvesting enhancement. Finite element full wave simulation (COMSOL Multiphysics) was employed for numerical calculation of the reflection spectra. The photonic crystals was modeled as TiO2 nanotubes arranged in a hexagonal lattice in the plane of titanium foil, with the axial geometric dimensions obtained from SEM graphs of the actual samples. The reflection spectra for samples with different dielectric contrast (i.e., samples in air and in electrolyte) was calculated and compared with the experimental results. In order to illustrate the effect of the photonic crystal layer, the spatial distribution of the optical field was also calculated. Objective 4. Assisted by theoretical calculation, to optimize the structure of the photo anode for further enhancement in power conversion efficiency: Computer simulation was conducted to study the structural effects of the photonic crystals on the photovoltaic performance of the assembled devices. The effects of various structure parameters were studied, such as, the lattice parameter of the photonic crystal, the nanotube length, nanotube diameter and wall thickness. The device performance was optimized with the optimized structure parameters of the photonic crystal.

516312.label: Major findings and research outcome
516312.value: • By using a self-detachment process, highly crystallized high quality TiO2 nanotube array (TNA) membrane in the anatase phase can be achieved by annealing at 700 °C. The TNA membrane can maintain its structure integrity and phase (anatase) stability as a result of the absence of the nucleation sites. The electron transport is much faster ( ≈ 4 times) in the 700 ° C-annealed membranes than that in the 400 ° C-treated one, which is mainly attributed to the improved crystallinity and reduced electron trap states. The superior electron transport leads to a significantly improved efficiency of 7.81% (enhanced by ≈ 50%). (Relevant publications: Adv.Funct.Mater. 2013, v.23, p.5952). • To maintain the semitransparency of the DSSC, a thin TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal (NTPC) membrane was attached to a thick TiO2 nanoparticle absorption layer. The TiO2 NTPC was found to offer both PC and light-scattering effects. The combined effects of PC and light-scattering yield the maximum enhancement in PCE (39.5%) when the tailored TiO2 NTPC, with the best matching of its reflectance maximum to the dye absorption maximum, is integrated into a DSSC. Computer simulation was used to explore the optimum structure parameters for the best light harvesting. (Relevant publications: Energy Environ.Sci., 2012, v.5, p.9881; ACS Appl.Mater.Interfaces, 2013, v.5, p.13022; J.Power Sources, 2015, v.293, p.170) • Making use of the blue shift nature of the Bragg position of a TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal (NTPC) under oblique incidence, we demonstrated experimentally that the use of the NTPC can partially compensate the cosine power loss of a DSSC. The strategy used here is to purposely choose the Bragg position of the NTPC to be at the longer wavelength side of the dye absorption peak. When the incident light is tilted, the blue shift of the Bragg position results in more overlap with the dye absorption peak, generating a higher efficiency that partially compensates the reduced photon flux due to light inclination. (Relevant publication: Nanoscale, 2014, v.6, p.13060) • Furthermore, aperiodic photonic crystals (APCs) was proposed to provide unprecedented opportunities for much more versatile photon management, due to increased degrees of freedom in the design and the unique properties brought about by the aperiodic structures as compared to their periodic counterparts. By coupling an APC into the photoanode of a DSSC, we demonstrate the concept of using APC to achieve nearly full-visible-spectrum light harvesting, as evidenced by both experimental and simulated results. (Relevant publication: Sci.Rep., 2014, v.4, p.6642)

516312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
516312.value: The TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal can find more applications in photocatalytic reaction, smart windows and even in photosynthesis. Those applications can be explored in the future, where the functionalities of both the photonic crystal and the TiO2 material itself will be utilized.

517612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
517612.value: This project aims to develop new lead-free ferroelectric transparent ceramics with good photoluminescent and electro-optic properties for multifunctional photonic applications. The work will focus to prepare both up-conversion and down-conversion photoluminescent ceramics by doping erbium/ytterbium and neodymium, respectively, into our newly developed lithium/bismuth co-modified potassium sodium niobate transparent electro-optic ceramics. It is anticipated that, due to the ferroelectric characteristics, the photoluminescence intensity of the ceramics can be enhanced and tuned reversibly by an electric field. In combination with the electro-optic properties, the ceramics can serve as optically active materials and would usher in widespread applications, such as tunable lasers and amplifiers. Unlike the crystal growth process, the fabrication procedures for the new ceramics are simple and fast, so there will be great saving in production cost and time. Moreover, the ceramics can be fabricated into large size and can accommodate high dopant concentrations. As the ceramics will be fabricated by ordinary sintering under atmospheric conditions, there will also be saving in capital investment for special techniques such as hot-pressing and vacuum sintering. The new ceramics are lead-free, so it can help to protect our environment from pollution by toxic lead. In this project, we also hope to elucidate the inter-relationships between the ferroelectric, electro-optic and photoluminescent properties of the ceramics. 本項目旨在研究開發具有光致發光和電光特性的無鉛鐵電透明陶瓷。這工作主要研究Er3+/Yb3+ 和Nd3+ 摻雜鈮酸鉀鈉基透明陶瓷的製備和它們的上轉換和下轉換發光性能。鋰/鉍改性鈮酸鉀鈉是我們新開發的透明電光陶瓷。它具有強電光效應， 高透明度， 製作程序簡單和速度快等優點。 Er3+, Yb3+ 和Nd3+ 等三價稀土離子具有豐富的能級，其摻雜的上轉換和下轉換發光材料在信息顯示和光電子學等領域有著廣泛應用前景。我們預期新材料能結合兩者的特性，尤其是電光效應和光致發光性，並能開拓嶄新的多功能光子應用。此外，新材料是無鉛的，它能幫助保護我們的環境不受污染有毒的鉛。

517612.label: Realisation of objectives
517612.value: Transparent ceramics 1 mol% Er-doped (K0.5Na0.5)1-xLixNb1-xBixO3 (Er-KNN-LB-x) have been successfully fabricated by pressureless sintering through the conventional ceramic fabrication technique. Due to the effective suppression of grain growth by Bi-doping, the ceramics possess fine and cubic crystalline grains with dense structure. The ceramics are optical transparent, exhibiting high transmittances in the near-infrared (NIR) and mid-infrared (MIR) regions (~50% and ~75%, respectively. The good optical transparency may also be derived from the cubic-like crystal structure and relaxor-like characteristics. The ceramics also possess strong electro-optic (EO) response, giving a large effective linear EO coefficient (128-184 pm/V). Owing to Er3+, the ceramics exhibit strong green and red up-conversion photoluminescence (PL) emissions, which are sensitive to the crystal symmetry of the ceramic host. Moreover, the ceramics exhibit a low absorption coefficient of OH− groups and then distinct MIR emissions. Together with the relatively large piezoelectric coefficient (70-90 pC/N), high dielectric constant (~1400) and low dielectric loss (~0.03), the multifunctional transparent ceramics open up the potential applications in electrical/optical interdisciplinary field, such as visible displays, MIR solid lasers and optical attenuators. Besides Er-KNN-LB-x ceramics, KNN ceramics doped with Er as well as co-doped with Er3+/Pr3+ or Er3+/Yb3+ have also been fabricated for investigating the inter-relationships between the dopants and the ferroelectric, EO and PL properties of the ceramics. Under an excitation of 980 nm, the Er-doped KNN ceramics exhibit typical luminescent emission bands at 527 nm (green), 548 nm (green), 660 nm (red) as well as 487 nm (blue). The Raman results also reveal that the ceramics have low phonon energy (~860 cm-1) and thus slow multi-phonon relaxation rate. The sol-gel process and Er3+-doping can produce ceramics with better compositional homogeneity as well as finer and uniform grains. All these are beneficial for improving both the upconversion and luminescent efficiencies of the ceramics, and thus leading to very strong green emissions even at a low quenching concentration of 2 mol%. These suggest that even without using sensitizers, the sol-gel derived Er-doped KNN ceramics are promising candidates for multifunctional optoelectronic applications. Our results also show that the Er-doping induces a phase transition from orthorhombic to cubic-like symmetry as well as inhibits the grain growth arisen from the donor-type nature. The resulting changes in the crystallographic structures and quenching effect have great effects on the PL properties of the ceramics. The effects of lithium (Li)-doping on the PL properties as well as the dielectric and ferroelectric properties of the Er-doped KNN ceramics have also been investigated. Similarly, the ceramics exhibit intense up-conversion luminescent emission at 548 nm (green), weak emission at 660 nm (red) as well as strong down-conversion luminescent emission in near-infrared (1.40 to 1.65 μm) and mid-infrared (2.60 to 2.85 μm) regions. Probably due to the induced structure distortion and reduced local symmetry, the photoluminescence intensities of the green, red as well as mid-infrared emissions are enhanced by the doping of Li+. Our results show that the Li-doping is effective in establishing a dynamic circulatory energy process to further enhance the photoluminescence intensity of the mid-infrared emission at the expense of the near-infrared emission. At the optimum doping level of Li+ (~ 6 mol%), the full bandwidth at half maximum of the mid-infrared emission reaches a very large value of ~ 250 nm. The ceramics also exhibit good ferroelectric properties, and thus they should have great potential for multifunctional optoelectronic applications. The effects of co-doping Er3+/Pr3+ or Er3+/Yb3+ in KNN ceramics have been investigated. Our results reveal that, by selecting appropriate excitation wavelength, simultaneous Vis down-conversion emissions of both Er3+ and Pr3+ can be obtained. Moreover, the PL intensity of the ceramics can be enhanced by the remanent polarization resulting from by the poling process. Our results also show that Yb3+ is a superior sensitizer to significantly enhance the Vis up-conversion emissions (one order of magnitude higher) and partly improve the MIR emissions (at low Yb content). For studying the effects of oxygen and cation vacancies on PL properties, 0.93(Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3)-0.07(BaTiO₃) (abbreviated as BNTBT) ceramics doped with 0.01 mol Er3+ at various sites have been fabricated. Our results also reveal that the vacancies arisen from charge imbalance between the dopants and the replaced ions could increase the PL intensity of the NIR and MIR emission bands at the expense of the visible emissions. For the ceramics containing cation vacancies, a looping mechanism is established such that their PL intensities of NIR emission increase by more than 50 % and 70 % respectively. The ceramics also exhibit good dielectric, piezoelectric and ferroelectric properties. BNTBT ceramics doped with various amounts of Er at the Ba-site have then been fabricated. The ceramics exhibit visible up-conversion luminescent emissions at 532 nm (green), 540 nm (green) and 600 nm (red), as well as broadband down-conversion luminescent emissions in NIR and MIR regions. The quenching concentration for the ceramics is high, about 6%, and both the visible and invisible emissions are very strong. Among the emissions, the photoluminescence intensity of the red emission band increases most significantly by more than 47 times as the Er-concentration increases from 0.005 to 0.07. As a result, the Commission Internationale de L’Eclairage chromaticity coordinates shift from (0.29, 0.69) to (0.49, 0.50), and the emission color changes from green to yellowish green. Owing to the establishment of a dynamic circulatory energy process at high Er-concentrations, the photoluminescence intensity of the mid-infrared emission increases significantly by more than 4 times at the expense of the near-infrared emission. Together with the good ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties, the ceramics should be promising candidates for multifunctional optoelectronic applications. For comparing the effects of various RE ions, Pr3+-doped BNTBT ceramics have been fabricated. The down-conversion PL mechanism and properties have been systemically investigated. The ceramics exhibit a low quenching concentration of (0.005 mol). Owing to the enhancement of multi-phonon relaxation and cross relaxation, the PL intensity of most of the emissions decreases by 50% to 75% as the Pr3+ concentration increases from 0.0025 to 0.02. On the other hand, the PL intensities of the emissions at 654 nm and 741 nm increase by more than 2 times at a concentration of 0.02.

517612.label: Major findings and research outcome
517612.value: Lead-free ferroelectric transparent ceramics with good photoluminescence and electro-optic properties have been successfully fabricated by the normal sintering condition, i.e., pressureless sintering. The ceramics are optical transparent, exhibiting high transmittances in the near-infrared (NIR) and mid-infrared (MIR) regions (~50% and ~75%, respectively). They also possess strong electro-optic (EO) response, giving a large effective linear EO coefficient (128-184 pm/V). Owing to Er3+, the ceramics exhibit strong green and red up-conversion photoluminescence (PL) emissions. Moreover, they exhibit a low absorption coefficient of OH− groups and then distinct MIR emissions. Together with the relatively large piezoelectric coefficient (70-90 pC/N), high dielectric constant (~1400) and low dielectric loss (~0.03), the ceramics open up the potential applications in electrical/optical interdisciplinary field, such as visible displays, MIR solid lasers and optical attenuators. A manuscript has been submitted to an international journal for publication. The effects of rare earth dopants on the optical, ferroelectric, EO and PL properties, as well as their inter-relationships have been investigated. Our results reveal that a small amount of rare earth dopants does not affect the optical properties significantly. However, it can induce a phase transition as well as inhibit the grain growth of the ceramics. The resulting changes in crystallographic structures have great effects on the PL properties. On the other hand, the Li-doping can enhance the mid-infrared as well as visible emissions, via inducing structure distortion and reducing local symmetry. It is also effective in establishing a dynamic circulatory energy process to further enhance the photoluminescence intensity of the mid-infrared emission at the expense of the near-infrared emission. Our results also reveal that cation vacancies can enhance the NIR emissions, via the establishment of a looping mechanism. All the findings have been summarized into seven manuscripts which have been published in international journals. Unfortunately, a wrong project code (PolyU 5194/08E) had been used for the acknowledgement in two of them. The wrong project code is for my previous GRF project "A New Lead-free Transparent Electro-optic Ceramic for Optoelectronic Applications" which focused on the development of transparent lead-free ceramics and their EO properties. It was completed and the final report had already been submitted on March 2012. The two new journal papers were submitted for publication in 2013, more than one year after the completion of the previous project. The papers reported the work mainly on the PL properties of KNN-based ceramics which are definitely not related to the previous project.

517612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
517612.value: Novel lead-free ferroelectric transparent ceramics with good photoluminescence and electro-optic properties have been successfully fabricated by pressureless sintering. Microwave sintering may be considered in improving the uniformity of the grain size and then the optical transmittance. Development work of fabricating the ceramics into various optoelectronic devices, such as visible displays, MIR solid lasers and optical attenuators should also be continued.

517612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
517612.value: Lead-free ferroelectric transparent ceramics with good photoluminescence and electro-optic properties have been successfully fabricated for the first time using the conventional sintering technique, i.e., pressureless sintering that can reduce significantly the capital investment in vacuum or hot pressing equipment. The effects of the dopants on the optical, ferroelectric, electro-optic and photoluminescence properties, and their interrelationships have been investigated in detail for optimizing the overall performances. The ceramics are optical transparent, exhibiting high transmittances in the near-infrared and mid-infrared regions (~50% and ~75%, respectively). They also exhibit strong electro-optic (EO) response (giving a large effective linear EO coefficient of 128-184 pm/V) as well as strong green up-conversion photoluminescence emissions and distinct mid-infrared emissions. Together with the relatively large piezoelectric coefficient (70-90 pC/N), high dielectric constant (~1400) and low dielectric loss (~0.03), the ceramics open up potential applications in electrical/optical interdisciplinary field, such as visible displays, MIR solid lasers and optical attenuators.

517712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
517712.value: Low back pain (LBP) is the most common health problem encountered by pregnant women, especially in the third trimester of the pregnancy. This LBP is considered a non-treatable occurrence, and the pain can be very uncomfortable and frustrating. This project addresses the issue of pain relief and clothing comfort, and proposes an all-round protective maternity wear which integrates five different designs to accommodate various needs during pregnancy. The first design is to relieve the back pain and pelvis pain of the pregnant women by utilizing the shoulder for extended support to the bulging abdomen. The second design is the freely adjustable property of the garment which makes it suitable to be used during the second and third trimesters. The third design provides a protection against the radiation and electromagnetic waves generated from electronic appliances which are easily encountered in daily life. The garment is made from some advanced materials and finishing which are able to screen out certain range of electromagnetic waves. The fourth design is to integrate a brassiere with cushioned wire which supports breast enlargement during pregnancy. In addition to the above designs, the use of auxetic fabric structure of the garment enhances the wearing comfort of the users. Therefore, this project will investigate the use of various materials and pattern of making this maternity wear. The motion analysis will also be performed to study the 3D embryo motion during walking and various pressure sensors will be used simultaneously to record the pressure between the garment and skin at different locations with high pressure level, e.g., shoulder and back. In addition, a new biomechanical model will be developed to determine the preferred load distribution of abdomen weight and the required fabric tension to support different parts of the body. The acceptance of style and materials will be evaluated by subjective assessment (e.g., appearance, hand feel, ease to wear). Overall, this project aims to study the issue scientifically with a view to developing an all-round protective maternity wear for pain relief during pregnancy, and it is believed that the new maternity wear would be a significant improvement over the current maternity garments available in the market. 下背部疼痛是懷孕婦女最常見的健康問題，特別發生在懷孕第三週期。由懷孕而來的下背部疼痛是不能治愈的，痛楚可以令婦女非常不舒適和洩氣。 這項研究針對痛楚舒緩和服裝舒適的範疇，建議一件全面保護的孕婦功能性服裝，這件服裝將結合五個不同設計，以切合婦女懷孕期間的各樣需要。 第一個設計利用肩膊，為擴張的腹部作延伸支持，以減輕背部和骨盆的痛楚。 第二個設計是服裝自由伸縮的特性，使其適用於懷孕第二及第三週期。 第三個設計是透過先進的成衣面料和後處理技術，使服裝能過濾日常電子產品釋出的電磁波輻射，提供有效保護。在第四個設計上，服裝包括金屬襯墊的胸圍，以支撐懷孕期間乳房的增大。 除上述設計外，採用的成衣面料結構亦會增加穿著時的舒適度。 因此，這項研究會探討不同的成衣面料和圖樣，作最後產品採納。 研究過程亦會進行動作分析，以了解在走動時胎兒的三維動作，多個壓力感應器亦會在不同位置同時間紀錄成衣和皮膚之間的壓力，尤其在高壓水平位置 (如肩膊、背部)。 此外，研究亦會研發一個生物力學模型，確定腹部重量的理想負重分佈和所需的成衣面料張力得以支撐身體不同部份。服裝款式和成衣面料的接受程度，將會以主觀評估方式 (如服裝外形、手感、穿著容易) 來評定。 整體來說，這項研究旨在利用科學方法處理這個範疇，研發一件全面保護的孕婦功能性服裝，以舒緩懷孕帶來的痛楚；相信這件嶄新的功能性服裝，相比於目前市面上的同類產品，會是一項重大的進步。

518012.label: Project Objectives
518012.value: Homogeneous depth filter: (a) Experiment: To experimentally investigate the depth filtration of a multilayer nanofiber media with homogeneous properties challenged by sub-micron aerosol. The techniques for making measurements of a multilayer nanofiber depth filter during loading are developed. Properties of each individual layer (efficiency and pressure drop) in the filter can be probed independently without disturbing aerosol loading of the filter. When more aerosols accumulated in the filter through an acceleration loading process, its pressure drop and filtration efficiency increases over time and will be monitored throughout the loading process. Effect of challenging particle size on the depth filter (include partilce penetration/distribution in filter) will be examined. Homogeneous depth filter: (b)Model: To develop an simple yet empirical-free model on depth filtration of nanfiber media: Adopting the approach of Thomas et al.[28], we assume both nanofibers as well as dendrite formed from the trapped particles both collect incoming particles over time. The filter efficiency and pressure drop will be determined without empirical constants. As accuracy is required for the model, instead of using Davis equation, we will develop our pressure drop behavior for nanofibers using our technique for measuring the thin nanofiber layer thickness as well as other pertinent parameters. The model will be compared to the experiments without empirical fit. Inhomogeneous depth filter: To develop inhomogeneous nanofiber media as an optimal filter wherein both filtration efficiency and storage capacity increases. One possible way is to stack up multiple nanofiber layers, each layer having different amount of nanofibers (i.e. packing density). The amount of nanofibers increases from upstream to downstream end within the multi-layer filter. Quality factor, efficiency and solid-holding capacity are assessed. Filter cleaning demonstration: To demonstrate the feasibility of using a back-pulse and back-blow regeneration for a nanofiber depth-filter loaded with sub-micron aerosol.

518012.value: 長期暴露在高濃度的亞微米尺寸的氣溶膠/微粒（譬如污染物和病毒）環境中，會導致慢性疾病。與微米纖維過濾器（纖維直徑：1 - 20微米）不同， 100-300納米纖維直徑的納米纖維可以通過擴散和截取， 有效地捕獲亞微米氣溶膠，然而塗覆在襯底上的薄膜層的納米纖維不具有足夠的固體存儲容量，因此會迅速從厚度過濾器改變成表面過濾器， 並伴有高的壓降。此建議書第一次提出若干方面， 用於改善連續加載亞微米顆粒的納米纖維厚度過濾器的性能。 首先，通過堆疊多個薄的尼龍6製造的納米纖維層，其中每一層由可滲透的平紋棉麻織物材料支撐， 我们開發了一種新型納米纖維厚度過濾器，并且通過實驗研究了在該過濾器中加載亞微米氣溶膠的表现。利用亞微米的氣溶膠發生器產生的濃縮的亞微米的NaCl晶體的高速通過，實現了過濾器的加載。在過濾器表面上顯著生成濾餅之前， 小心地週期性地除去過濾器中的每一層，用於在低濃度和低速度下監測不同的大小在50和500納米之間氣溶膠的壓降和分級效率。通過比較是否在相鄰的納米纖維層之間安裝間隔件的測試結果，確定相鄰層之間的相互作用。 其次，為了建立模型，納米纖維上的沉積微粒是當作樹突纖維結構體。 有別於之前的嘗試，這是一個“無實驗”的模型 —— 懸浮物顆粒加載引起納米纖維和“樹突纖維”形成,每一個成層會用來“吸引”入射粒子。“樹突纖維區”分佈廣泛, 集中在過濾器表面上的結塊，並往下游減小。通過纖維與樹突纖維的相互流量, 或其一流量, 能預測降壓. 預測的結果會和實驗比較, 分柝相互作用. 此模型需要纖維物料上流量的相關降壓分析。通過實驗,測量通過薄納米纖維過濾器的流量，可以得出新的相關降壓; 然而要幾個參數才得到纖維過濾器的流量,當中最困難的是用廓線儀去量度納米纖維過濾器的厚度, 因其只達10微米的數量級。新的相關降壓會用在納米纖維上的流量(Knf ~O(1), 氣體分子的平均自由程跟纖維直徑相若) , 相關降壓會跟廣用的卡林蓋特 - 戴維斯公式（飽和液體蒸氣壓公式, Knf <<1）作比較. 第三，爲了減少趨膚效應，同時增加過濾器的固體吸附量，纖維填充密度和纖維直徑在多層納米纖維過濾器經過改進，使得效率在過濾器的上游降低而在下游逐漸增加。這種設計能使懸浮物顆粒沿著過濾器的濾層深度富集。一系列研究將會展開以最大限度地提高過濾器性能的三個標準：（1）效率，（2）品質因數（效率與壓降比）和（3）過濾器的固體吸附量（即達到過濾器表面形成初期結塊所需時間）。 最後，過濾器以後端脈衝（震動鬆動錨定固體的過濾器），然後通過反吹（恆定流量掃鬆脫顆粒）的清潔方式將被優化，以有效地去除在多層納米纖維過濾器的積聚的結塊和粒子。 由於固體顆粒在反吹過程中可能會由下游向上游遷移，精確有效率由顆粒沿濾層深度在清潔前後的分佈確定。比較兩個不同過濾器固體顆粒沿著濾層深度的分佈確定濾層清潔性優劣，一個濾層有恒定纖維填料和纖維半徑，另一個具有不同屬性。這是第四次標準 - “可清潔過濾器”，相比前三個標準評估濾波器的性能同樣重要。
