518012.value: The homogeneous depth filter of nanofiber has been studied in details. We found that depending on the low efficiency (less fiber packing) or high efficiency (more fiber packing), a low skin and a high skin behavior can be developed. The pressure excursion and grade efficiency of a typical particle size (say 300 nm) have been monitored over time. By mass balance, the pressure excursion and grade efficiency of a typical particle size (say 300 nm) have been monitored over specific mass deposited on the filter. In the low skin situation, a concave upward behavior has been obtained before reaching the cake filtration which yields a linear trend of pressure drop with specific aerosol mass deposited. In the high skin situation, a concave downward behavior has been obtained before reaching the cake filtration which yields a linear trend of pressure drop with specific aerosol mass deposited. We have collected sufficient test data for modelling. Two papers have been published – Leung and Choy, SPTJ 2018, Leung and Choy, Chem. Eng., 2018. This satisfies objective 1. We have developed a capillary filling model to model the filling process at the initial stage. Subsequently we have developed a bridging model to explain test data for low skin as well as high skin cases. We have published 3 papers – Leung and Hau, SPTJ 2016, Leung and Choy, SPTJ 2018, Leung and Choy, Chem. Eng., 2018. This satisfies objective 2. We have positioned a microfiber filter stacked onto a nanofiber filter. We found out that the cake formed is based on the microfiber filter, and the permeability is much higher as compared to that of the nanofiber filter alone. The mechanism have been studied in details. A paper has been submitted to SPTJ for publication in 2018. We have demonstrated cleaning using backpulse alone, backblow alone and backpulse followed by backblow. We found the best is to use backpulse followed by backblow. We have also optimized the backpulse/backblow parameters for nanofiber filter, including pressure force, frequency of pulse, etc. The results have been published in Hau and Leung, SPTJ, 2016a. We have also developed model (more than required by the objective of demo) and the results compared very well with the experiments. The work has been published in Leung and Hau, SPTJ, 2016b. Further we have modeled and experimented repeated cyclic loading-and-cleaning and the work has been published in Leung and Hau, SPTJ 2017. 518012.label: Major findings and research outcome
518012.value: We have studied the loading of homogeneous nanofiber filters and found depending on the fiber packing, it can evolve to a low skin behavior or a high skin behavior. For the low skin the pressure drop excursion is concave upward before reaching cake filtration delineated by a linear trend. For high skin, it is concave downward. In either case, we have developed model that can model the pressure drop behavior. In order to increase the solid storage capacity of a filter, a microfiber filter can be position immediately upstream of a nanofiber filter. The filter formed on the composite is that of a microfiber filter. The advantage of the composite filter is that both the pressure drop is lower and the efficiency can be very high. We have demonstrated cleaning by backpulse, backblow and backpulse followed by backblow. The cleaning can restore the cleaningness to a large extent. We have also developed a model for the cleaning. 6 papers have been published and one paper is currently under review. See previous section on the 6 publications. We have also delivered plenary talks on the subject, one in Korea in Feb 2018 and another in Oct 2016 in San Diego, CA, USA. A MPhil student Curie Hau Wing Yi has been trained. She received her MPhil in 2017 based on “Backpulse and Backblow Cleaning of Nanofiber Filter Loaded with Nano-aerosols”

518012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
518012.value: The loading and cleaning behavior can be extended to real aerosols using diesel dust rather than sodium chloride aerosol generated as in this project.

518012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
518012.value: The loading of very small nano particles under 100 nanometers, 1/1000 times smaller than human hair, over an extended period of time has been investigated using nanofiber filter. We examined the pressure drop and the filtration efficiency over the time period. We have understood the characteristics and also developed mathematical model to exlain the behavior. We have also developed modified filter made of both nanofiber as well as microfiber filter to achieve high efficiency and lower pressure drop. Cleaning of the filter by reversed air jet has been investigated after the filter has been loaded with particles. Various schemes have been investigated and optimal scheme has been determined. We have also developed some mathematical models on the cleaning that explains the test results very well. All the work have been published in 6 papers. We have delivered several plenary speeches over the years around the world.

518312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
518312.value: 地源熱泵技術因其較高的能效比及環保特性已逐漸成為吸引人們作為供熱和制冷系統的選擇。該技術關鍵部分為地熱換熱器,而普通鉆孔地熱換熱器需要大量土地面積及較高安裝成本，成為該技術推廣應用的重要障礙。而，如果采用樁基地作為熱換熱器，即利用建築物的樁作為地熱換熱器的一部分，該“能量樁”設在混泥土的樁基裏, 降低鉆孔費用並減少布置鉆孔的土地面積,近年成為地源熱泵行業關註要點。對於常規樁內U型管埋，其樁基內換熱面積較少，且也可產生空氣阻塞換熱管內部。為了解決該問題，近來有專家學者提出將螺旋管埋設在樁裏面。螺旋管預埋於樁基裏，管裏面的循環水將會與樁及地下介質實現換熱，換熱效率較高和換熱面積更多，且不會產生空氣阻塞問題。 該螺旋管的新型樁基換熱器具有其特殊性，如半徑較粗且長度較短，所以普通鉆孔所采用的典型的換熱模型對其而言不適用，現有模擬模型無法描述設有螺旋管的樁基換熱器的換熱過程。因此，本課題將研究出壹種半無限大多孔介質中的三維瞬態螺旋管換熱模型，地下水對流換熱的影響也會考慮在其中。此外，該螺旋管換熱樁是一種新型的能量樁，應考慮其機械性能熱效應。在樁埋管地源熱泵系統長期的制冷或制熱運行過程中，地下的溫度會發生變化可達20℃左右，會導致樁基的熱機械行為不斷變化，比如樁裏面的壓力變化以及極限承載量的減少，所以傳統的樁基設計方法不再適用。因此，本課題進行熱機械分析, 研究出一種新巖土工程設計方法適用於受熱效應影響的換熱樁。 根據前面提到的熱分析和熱機械分析，設計方針將會被提出從而促進這項新技術能量樁在建築施工行業的應用，尤其是對於人口密集的城市，例如香港。

518312.label: Realisation of objectives
518312.value: The application with the novel Pile Geothermal Heat Exchanger (PGHE) brings new challenges to the development of geothermal heat pump technology. As the special heat transfer feature of PGHE, the traditional heat transfer models of borehole GHE fail to describe the heat transfer performance of PGHE. In addition, the continuous heat rejection/extraction of GHE to/from the piles cause significant temperature variations of piles and the surrounding soil, which can influence the mechanical behavior of the pile foundation severely. Meanwhile, the study of the thermo-mechanical performance of PGHE is very limited. Therefore, this project aims to investigate the thermal performance of the novel PGHE with spiral coils theoretically and experimentally, and to explore the thermo-mechanical behavior of this novel PGHE. To achieve the objectives, this project was conducted by three main stages: 1) established new methods to describe the thermal performance of PGHE when advection exist, 2) established a new analytical model to effectively distinguish the different thermal properties of pile and soil in the heat transfer process of PGHE, and established a new method to describe the thermal performance of PGHE when advection exists, and 3) established a numerical simulation model to study the thermo-mechanical behavior of PGHE in full size. The significant results obtained from this project are summarized as follow. Firstly, in order to achieve the first stage, a solid cylindrical simulation model was established for the estimation of heat transfer around foundation pile ground heat exchangers with groundwater flow (Journal paper 1 in section 8, “The analysis on solid cylindrical heat source model of foundation pile ground heat exchangers with groundwater flow”). In this model, the spiral heat exchanger is simplified as a solid cylindrical heat surface. The analytical solutions of the temperature response in the heat transfer process including heat conduction and convection were obtained. The impact of groundwater flow on the heat transfer has been investigated. The heat transfer processes with and without groundwater flow were compared. It was found that groundwater flow has a considerable effect on the heat transfer process, especially when the groundwater flow velocity attains a certain order of magnitude. If the system is designed reasonably and groundwater temperature is below a certain range, groundwater flow is favorable to the heat transfer between the foundation pile ground heat exchangers (GHEs) and surrounding ground medium, and can improve the energy performance of the heating and cooling system of the ground-coupled heat pump for energy conservation of buildings. To further improve the accuracy of analytical model, a ring-coil heat transfer model of pile foundation ground heat exchangers in the case of groundwater seepage is proposed (Journal paper 2 in section 8, “The research on ring-coil heat transfer models of pile foundation ground heat exchangers in the case of groundwater seepage”). The corresponding analytical solutions on temperature response are acquired based on combined heat transfer case; the model take the spiral coils arrangement and their pitches inside piles into consideration and identify the differences between the new models and those former models which did not treat spiral tube as a series of separate coils along the z-axial direction. The objective 1 (To develop an analytic solutions to describe the heat transfer process of the proposed PGHE with spiral coils in the case of groundwater seepage) is fully completed. In the second stage, a 3-D transient simulation model is established to describe the heat transfer characteristics of the proposed PGHE with spiral coils (Journal paper 3 in section 8, “Numerical and analytical analysis of groundwater influence on the pile geothermal heat exchanger with cast-in spiral coils”). The difference in thermal properties between pile and soil has been fully presented in the simulation model, and its influence is investigated. Then, to describe the heat transfer performance in mathematical method, a novel composite analytical model for PGHE was established (Journal paper 4 in section 8, “A novel composite-medium solution for pile geothermal heat exchangers with spiral coils”). This new model successfully considered both the special geometrical shape of the pile and the difference of thermal properties between the pile and ground soil. Based on the Green’s function theory, instantaneous heat source solutions are firstly derived by the Laplace method, and then a transient solution is obtained by integrating the instantaneous solution over time. This new analytical model was validated by a 3-D finite-element simulation model, and well agreement between the two models was observed. This newly developed analytical model can better describe the heat transfer process of the PGHE with spiral-tubes, especially the pile foundation temperature responses. It can be believed that this new model provides a more accurate tool for the design of PGHE systems, and accurate performance estimation. Thus, the objective 2 (to develop a 3-D transient simulation model with analytical solutions to accurately describe the heat transfer characteristics of the proposed PGHE with spiral coils) is fully completed. In the third stage, to investigate the thermo-mechanical behavior under different thermal loads, a modified direct shear test bed was established. Based on this new apparatus, two groups of interface tests, sand-concrete and clay-concrete, were conducted. The friction parameters (friction angle and adhesion strength) of the soil-concrete interface are enhanced by the high temperature. Compared with the case of normal temperature, the adhesion strength has an improvement of about 63%, and the friction angle increased by 24% at the heating condition. Conversely, the friction properties decrease slightly with the temperature reduction. The objective 3 (to study the interface behavior between soil and concrete under the thermal effect by experiments) is fully completed after the experiment. Based on the data from the interface tests, a finite element model is established to investigate the thermo-mechanical behavior of PGHE. The results show that the heat exchange process of GHE has a great effect on the skin friction behavior of the pile. A 34.4% increase of bearing capacity is observed in the case of heating simulation and a 15.37% capacity decrease has been found in the case of cooling simulation. Additionally, the thermal load induced stress at the pile axis has a limited impact on the concrete strength, but the stress-concentrated area around the spiral heat exchanger tube should be paid more attention on the pile design of structural mechanics. Under such a great stress variation, the pile may suffer from the concrete fatigue for long-term heating/cooling operation. The objectives of 4,5, and 6 were achieved by the proposed simulation model and partial results have been published (Conference paper 2 in section 9, “Numerical simulation of pile geothermal heat exchanger with spiral tube considering its thermo-mechanical behavior”). In summary, achievements in the researches on the thermal and thermo-mechanical performance of PGHE have been made in this project. New models were developed accordingly. Three analytical models have been proposed to describe the heat transfer performance of PGHE in different operation condition, and the thermo-mechanical performance of PGHE is investigated by experimental and numerical methods. These achievements will substantially push forward the development of the application of PGHE.

518312.label: Major findings and research outcome
518312.value: a) A solid cylindrical simulation model was established for the estimation of heat transfer around foundation pile ground heat exchangers with groundwater flow [1]. It was found that groundwater flow has a considerable effect on the heat transfer process, especially when the groundwater flow velocity attains a certain order of magnitude. b) A ring-coil heat transfer model of pile foundation ground heat exchangers in the case of groundwater seepage is proposed to further improve the accuracy of analytical model (with groundwater flow) [2]. The corresponding analytical solutions on temperature response are acquired based on combined heat transfer case; the model take the spiral coils arrangement and their pitches inside piles into consideration and identify the differences between the new models and the former models which did not treat spiral tube as a series of separate coils along the z-axial direction. c) A novel composite analytical model for PGHE was established [3] to distinguish the thermal properties between pile and soil and accurately describe the thermal performance of the PGHE (without groundwater flow). This newly developed analytical model can better describe the heat transfer process of the PGHE with spiral-tubes, especially the pile foundation temperature responses. It can be believed that this new model provides a more accurate tool for the design of PGHE systems, and accurate performance estimation. d) A modified direct shear test bed was established to investigate the thermo-mechanical behavior under different thermal load. Based on this new apparatus, two groups of interface tests, sand-concrete and clay-concrete, were conducted. The results show that the friction parameters (friction angle and adhesion strength) of the soil-concrete interface are enhanced by the high temperature. Compared with the case of normal temperature, the adhesion strength has an improvement of about 63%, and the friction angle increased by 24% at the heating condition. e) Based on the data from the interface tests, a finite element model is established to investigate the thermo-mechanical behavior of PGHE. The results show that the heat exchange process of GHE has a great effect on the skin friction behavior of the pile. A 34.4% increase of bearing capacity is observed in the case of heating simulation and a 15.37% capacity decrease has been found in the case of cooling simulation.

518312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
518312.value: In the direct shear experiment with temperature control, an obvious moisture content variation has been observed in soil sample, which should be the core influence factor on the increase/decrease of the friction parameters. However, it is hard to find the quantitative relationship between the moisture content and the friction parameters, which requires deep-going research, especially in the field of the heat and mass transfer mechanism of the moisture variation in saturated soil. Additionally, in the application of underground electrical cables, many researchers point out that the temperature rise induced by electricity could decrease the moisture content of the surrounding soil, and create heat insulating layer to decrease the heat transfer performance of soil. As a similar heat source, the PGHE may also affect by the moisture content variation in its heat transfer performance, but how and what extent of this influence is need to further research. Therefore, the mechanism of the thermal induced moisture transfer in soil and the influence of the moisture transfer on the thermal and thermo-mechanical performance of PGHE has a very high research value in the further work.

518312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
518312.value: The pile geothermal heat exchanger (PGHE) can considerably reduce the initial cost of ground-coupled heat pump system and promote this system applications in Hong Kong. However, its thermal and thermo-mechanical performance has not been fully examined. In this project, three analytical models have been proposed to describe the heat transfer performance of PGHE in different operation conditions, which provide a systematic tool for PGHE’s thermal design and optimized analysis. In addition, an interface experiment is designed and conducted to investigate the influence of thermal load on the interface performance between pile and soil. Based on the experiment data, a numerical model is established to investigate the thermo-mechanical performance of PGEH. The results show that the cooling process could cause a decrease of friction angle and normal contact pressure at the interface, and as a consequence, the shear resistance decreases with the temperature reduction. These observation results could provide very important reference data for the geotechnical design of PGHE. In summary, the achievements gained in this project will substantially push forward the development of the application of PGHE.

518712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
518712.value: This project proposes a new modeling approach for estimating the hourly origin-destination (OD) traffic demand variations from multiple sources of different types of traffic data throughout the whole year. Different from the conventional OD estimation methods, the proposed modeling approach aims to estimate not only the mean but also the hourly variations (in terms of covariance matrices) of the multi-class OD demands due to day-to-day and seasonal fluctuations in activity patterns over the whole year. For this purpose, the first- and second-moment statistical properties of the observed traffic counts and vehicular travel times are fully utilized to capture the stochastic characteristics of the OD demands. This project proposes to develop advanced models for estimating the stochastic hourly OD matrices by vehicle types throughout the whole year. Firstly, the effects of demand variations (in terms of hourly OD matrices by vehicle types) on the stochastic path choice behaviors by different user classes (or vehicle types) are investigated. A new multi-class stochastic traffic assignment model is developed for congested networks with covariance in demands. Secondly, the statistical properties of the observed link flow variations (i.e., classified traffic counts) and vehicular travel times are studied. In order to capture the stochastic characteristics of the OD demands by vehicle types, a novel multi-objective optimization model is proposed with the use of a bi-level programming framework. In the upper-level problem, with explicit consideration of using multiple sources of observed traffic data, a multi-objective function is proposed to estimate the mean and covariance matrices of the OD demands together with calibration of the parameters in link performance function. In the lower-level problem, a new reliability-based stochastic traffic assignment model is adapted to take full account of different users’ stochastic path choice behaviors under uncertainty. A heuristic solution algorithm is proposed for solving the multi-objective bi-level problem in practice. Finally, all the analyses and developments will be demonstrated with case studies in Hong Kong together with sensitivity tests. The proposed stochastic OD matrix estimation models can be regarded as an extension of the traditional OD estimation models. Apart from the mean OD demands, it can also provide the statistical characteristics of the hourly OD traffic demands and link/path traffic flows. The proposed study has the potential to help planners and engineers better understand the impacts of hourly traffic demand (e.g., morning peak) variations over the whole year for long-term strategic planning and assessment of network performance. 518712.label: Realisation of objectives
518712.value: As far as the project objective 1 is concerned, the effects of stochastic origin-destination (OD) demands, particularly the mean and the covariance of the OD demands, on path choice behaviors were investigated by a new analytical method with closed-form solution. The concept of covariance to mean ratio (CMR) has been adopted to capture the relationship between OD demand variance matrix and link/path flow covariance. Based on the CMR, the closed forms of link/path covariance matrices and link/path travel time covariance matrices were analytically deduced. The new definition of the effective travel time was employed to account for the travelers’ risk-taking path choice behaviors. The stochastic OD demands were applied to network reliability assessment, design-hourly-flow determination and network performance evaluation. In addition, a new dynamic traffic model has been proposed to capture road users’ learning process on travel time variation due to day-to-day demand fluctuation. The effects of the accuracy level of the guidance information provided from Advanced Transportation Information Systems (ATIS) on road users’ behavioral changes over time have also been investigated with the use of the proposed model. With regard to the project objective 2, a generalized OD estimation model was proposed to estimate the peak hour OD traffic demand variation from hourly traffic counts throughout the whole year. Different from the conventional OD estimation models, not only the first- but also the second-moment statistical properties of the observed traffic counts were used to estimate the stochastic OD demands (in terms of mean and covariance matrix). The proposed model was formulated as a bi-level optimization problem. In the upper-level problem, a weighted least squares method was used to estimate the mean and covariance matrix of the OD demands. In the lower-level problem, a reliability-based traffic assignment model was adopted to take account of travelers’ risk-taking path choice behaviors under OD demand variation. It was found that the conventional OD estimation models can be regarded as a special case of the proposed model. However, the conventional OD estimation model may over- or under- estimate the OD demand variance as it ignores the OD demand covariance. A local area network in Hong Kong was used to demonstrate the new features of the proposed model. The proposed stochastic OD estimation method could also be used to estimate the network-wide travel times and determine traffic signal timings. The proposed stochastic OD estimation model was further extended to estimate the mean and covariance of stochastic multi-class (multiple vehicle classes) origin-destination (OD) demands from hourly classified traffic counts. A modified lasso (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator) method in terms of a non-linear constrained model was proposed to address the identifiability problem. An exterior penalty algorithm has been adapted to solve the proposed model. It was found in the numerical examples that (i) the estimated covariance of mode-path choice proportions can reflect the interactions of path and mode choices between different vehicle classes; and (ii) the proposed model based on the lasso method could outperform the conventional least squares (LS) model on overcoming the identifiability difficulty for model application. With respect to the project objective 3, sensitivity tests of the proposed model were carried out under different covariance of the OD demand. It was found that ignorance of the OD demand covariance could over- or under-estimate the mean and variance of the total system travel time. For the application of the proposed OD demand estimation model, the travel time function under various rainfall conditions on urban roads in Hong Kong should be calibrated. Empirical data were collected for calibrating the generalized speed-flow and speed-density functions under different rainfall conditions. The calibrated functions were also validated with an independent dataset collected at the same location. It was found that the generalized speed-flow and speed-density functions are useful for assessing the performance of urban roads, particularly under network uncertainties. To further investigate the relationship between traffic flow and travel times, an analytical reliability-based dynamic traffic assignment model was proposed for assessing the temporal and spatial impacts of a traffic incident on network reliability. The proposed model could be used to estimate the stochastic link flow pattern and route travel time distribution for examining the impacts of a traffic incident on the on-time arrival probability with and without dynamic speed limit control.

518712.label: Major findings and research outcome
518712.value: In relation to the project objective 1, an analytical modeling approach was proposed to fully investigate the effects of stochastic origin-destination (OD) demands, particularly the mean and covariance, on path choice behaviors (see publication nos. (1) and (5)). The concept of covariance to mean ratio (CMR) has been adopted to capture the relationship between OD demand variance matrix and link/path flow covariance. Based on the CMR, a reliability-based traffic assignment model was presented, which appeared to the first time in the literature to account for the spatial covariance between link/path traffic flows as well as link/path travel times in traffic assignment models under demand uncertainty. The proposed stochastic OD estimation method could also be used to estimate the network-wide travel times and determine traffic signal timings (see publication nos. (1), (4) and (8)). In addition, a new dynamic model has been proposed to capture road users’ learning process on travel time variation due to day-to-day demand fluctuation (see publication no. (3)). With respect to the projective objective 2, two optimization models were proposed for stochastic OD demand estimation problems (see publication nos. (5), (6) and (9)). These two models were aimed to estimate the peak hour OD traffic demand variation from hourly traffic counts throughout the whole year. The first model only considered the OD estimation problem for single traffic mode, while the second model extended to estimate traffic demands of multiple vehicle classes. Different from the conventional OD estimation models, not only the first- but also the second-order statistical properties of the observed traffic counts were used to estimate the stochastic multi-class OD demand (in terms of mean and covariance matrix). In connection to the project objective 3, sensitivity tests of the proposed models were carried out with particular attention to the effects of OD demand covariance (see publication no. (5)). It was found that OD demand covariance plays an important role in the evaluation of network performance evaluation, which should not be ignored in application. The generalized speed-flow and speed-density functions under various rainfall conditions were also calibrated based on empirical data for assessing the performance of urban roads, particularly under network uncertainties. (see publication no. (2)). To further investigate the relationship between traffic flow and travel times, an analytical reliability-based dynamic traffic assignment model was proposed for assessing the temporal and spatial impacts of various traffic incidents on the network reliability (see publication no. (7)).

518712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
518712.value: In this project, various static and dynamic models were proposed to address the issues of estimating stochastic OD demands from classified traffic counts with day-to-day and seasonal variations. Robust mathematical models and solution algorithms were formulated and developed for reliability-based traffic assignment model, stochastic origin-destination demand estimation model and calibration of link performance functions in network with uncertainties. The second-order statistical property of the stochastic OD demand were investigated in a spatial manner. However, the temporal covariance of OD demands has not been addressed. Further study is to extend the proposed models and solution algorithms for simultaneously estimation of the spatial and temporal covariance of the multi-class traffic demands between different hourly periods in dynamic or time-dependent road networks. Although the lasso method could overcome the identifiability difficulty to some extent in the proposed OD demand estimation model, multiple solutions may still exist. Further investigation is required to address this issue in practice. It was found in the numerical examples that the efficient deployment of advanced sensors makes data more readily available for estimating the mean and covariance of multi-class OD demands. Thus, how to optimize the sensor locations for classified traffic data collection needs further investigation.

518712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
518712.value: This research appears to be the first devoted exclusively to the topic of Origin-Destination (OD) traffic demand estimation problem in stochastic road networks with uncertainties. The OD traffic demand refers to the number of vehicles between the origin and the destination in a transportation network during a particular time period. It is widely recognized that OD demand stochastically fluctuate from day to day in reality. The traffic demands of different OD pairs as well as different vehicle types have stochastic correlations with each other. However, conventional OD traffic demand estimation studies usually ignored these fluctuations and correlations. To address this limitation, this research project has developed some advanced models to estimate the stochastic relationship of traffic demands between different OD pairs and various vehicle types for given time period over the year. The first- and the second-order statistical properties of the day-to-day hourly traffic count data are fully utilized so as to capture the stochastic characteristics of OD demands. It launches a new avenue of research for estimation of OD demand variation in transportation networks with uncertainties. The outputs of this project can be used to statistically evaluate the network performance, thereby assisting in optimal decision-making for enhancement of the reliability and the efficiency of transportation network with uncertainties.

519012.label: Realisation of objectives
519012.value: The main objective of this project is to develop a general lossless compression scheme that provides standard data format for storing and manipulating DNA sequences. The four objectives as stated in Section 5.1 have been achieved successfully. First, we have developed a lossless compression scheme that takes into account both intra-sequence and inter-sequence similarities in DNA sequences. The lossless compression scheme works by first defining a set of reference sequences. It is then followed by identifying similar subsequences within the set of the reference sequences and the sequence to be compressed. Lastly, these similar subsequences are encoded together to achieve compression. Experimental results show that the proposed lossless compression scheme is able to compress sequences with different degrees of similarities. Good compression gain is achieved in partially similar chromosome sequences as well as highly similar population sequences. Second, we notice that the compressed size will be affected by the compression order of DNA sequences in practical situation. To determine the optimal compression order, two fast search algorithms have been developed for compressing a group of two or more DNA sequences together. The first algorithm is called predictive algorithm. It first compresses a sequence that has the highest similarity to all the other sequences so that this sequence can be used as a reference sequence to compress others. The second algorithm is called a greedy algorithm. In contrary to the predictive algorithm, the sequence that has the highest similarity to all the other sequences is compressed at last so that its sequence length can be minimized before encoding. Extensive experimental works have been carried out. Results show that the two fast algorithms can significantly reduce the complexity as compared to the original algorithm. Besides, the compressed size ranges from 1.9 to 0.039 bpb (bit per base) which mainly depends on the degree of similarities among the sequences to be compressed together. Details about the lossless compression scheme as well as the two fast algorithms have been summarized in the following publications, Kin-On Cheng, Paula Wu, Ngai-Fong Law and Wan-Chi Siu, “Compression of Multiple DNA Sequences using Intra-sequence and Inter-sequence Similarities”, IEEE/ACM Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics, Vol. 12, No. 6, November/December 2015, 1322-1332. K.O. Cheng, N.F. Law and W.C. Siu, “A Novel DNA Sequence Compression Scheme using Both Intra and Inter Sequences Correlation”, Proceedings of APSIPA Annual Summit and Conference 2015, 16-19 December 2015, 237 – 241, Hong Kong. Besides, the source code and experiments results have been uploaded for public download at the following website: http://www.eie.polyu.edu.hk/~nflaw/DNAComp/index.html. As demonstrated in our lossless compression scheme that explores intra and inter sequences similarities, the reference-based compression approach can achieve promising compression ratios for the sequences of the same species. However, the choice of the reference sequence will affect the compression performance. Basically, the reference sequence can be selected as one of the DNA sequences to be compressed or constructed artificially. Regardless of selection/construction, there is a premise that a single reference sequence is sufficiently representative. In fact all existing DNA sequence compression algorithms consider only one single reference sequence. Unfortunately, sequences may have substructures even from the same species. This motivates us to investigate the use of clustering in grouping sequences for compression. In this case, sequences can be well approximated by a single reference sequence in one cluster only. In order to minimize the computational cost of clustering, we apply k-means clustering in a feature space whose dimension is much lower than the lengths of sequences. In particular, a normalized local histogram is constructed to represent characteristics of each input sequence. Then feature-based clustering is applied to group similar DNA sequences together. After clustering, a representative sequence is derived for each cluster. We have developed an algorithm to construct the representative sequence so that its similarity with all other sequences in a cluster is maximized. The representative sequence is then used as the reference sequence in our multiple sequence compression algorithm called RCC. Experiments were conducted to evaluate the performance of our proposed algorithm RCC on five datasets, namely h.mito, s.cere, s.para, s.aure and e.coli. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed algorithm can always improve the bit per base significantly in our testing. For example, in the dataset that contains 3616 samples of a human mitochondrial sequence, the bit per base of our proposed algorithm is 0.01575. For existing state-of-the algorithms that use reference sequence, the bits per base are respectively 0.04029, 0.1873, 0.08070 for RLCSA, GDC and FRESCO. The improvement of the five datasets was in the range of 16.4% - 91.0%. Hence, these results show that our proposed algorithm RCC can improve the compression performance and outperforms all existing state-of-the-art algorithms. In addition to the compression ratios, other issues such as computational complexity, running time and memory requirements are also important. While the proposed algorithm can always achieve the highest compression among the existing state-of-the-art algorithms, it has the longest compression time, despite that the decompression time is much lower than the compression time. This property makes the RCC practical on applications such as public repositories of DNA sequences. The asymptotic analysis shows that the time complexity of RCC depends primarily on local sequence alignment and entropy coding. Thus, the growth rate in its complexity is comparable to other state-of-the-art algorithms if local sequence alignment and entropy coding of similar complexity are used. About the memory requirement, RCC ranks in the middle among the six state-of-the-art-algorithms. Details about the proposed RCC algorithm are summarized in the following paper, Kin-On Cheng, Ngai-Fong law and Wan-Chi Siu, “Clustering-based Compression for Population DNA Sequences”, submitted to IEEE/ACM Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics for possible publication, Feb 2016. In summary, all the objectives have been achieved. Please note that the original budget contains expenses for conference attendance and general expenses. However, those expenses are not used because of the following reasons. We have submitted a conference paper to an international conference which was held in Hong Kong. As the cost for attending their conferences involve only registration, the Department of Electronic and Information Engineering kindly provided that funding. Hence, there is no expenditure on the conference attendance. About the general expenses, the original plan was to use that for advertisement for research staff. However, we have put the advertisement on the department web page, which did not incur any cost. Hence, all the funding was used for hiring the research personnel.

519012.label: Major findings and research outcome
519012.value: We have developed a lossless compression scheme that takes into account both intra-sequence and inter-sequence similarities in DNA sequences. The lossless compression scheme works by first defining a set of reference sequences. It is then followed by identifying similar subsequences within the set of the reference sequences and the sequence to be compressed. Lastly, these similar subsequences are encoded together to achieve compression. As the compressed size will be affected by the compression order of sequences in practical situation, two fast search algorithms have been developed for compressing a group of two or more DNA sequences together. The first algorithm is called predictive algorithm. It first compresses a sequence that has the highest similarity to all the other sequences so that this sequence can be used as a reference sequence to compress others. The second algorithm is called a greedy algorithm. In contrary to the predictive algorithm, the sequence that has the highest similarity to all the other sequences is compressed at last so that its sequence length can be minimized before encoding. The works on the construction of the lossless compression scheme and the study of compression order have been summarized in the following paper, Kin-On Cheng, Paula Wu, Ngai-Fong Law and Wan-Chi Siu, “Compression of Multiple DNA Sequences using Intra-sequence and Inter-sequence Similarities”, IEEE/ACM Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics, Vol. 12, No. 6, November/December 2015, 1322-1332. We have found that substructures exist within the population DNA sequences. Hence, a Reference-based Compression algorithm using the concept of clustering (RCC) is developed. To identify these substructures, k-means clustering is employed to partition sequences into clusters for better compression. In particular, the RCC uses local histograms as features for k-means clustering. Besides, an effective algorithm is developed to construct the reference sequence for each cluster, so that sequences in that cluster can be compressed by referring to this reference sequence. The reference sequence of each cluster is also compressed with reference to a sequence which is derived from all the reference sequences. The works on the RCC and the construction of the reference sequence are summarized in the following paper, Kin-On Cheng, Ngai-Fong law and Wan-Chi Siu, “Clustering-based Compression for Population DNA Sequences”, submitted to IEEE/ACM Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics for possible publication, Feb 2016. In addition to the papers publication, the source code and experiments results have been uploaded for public download at the following website: http://www.eie.polyu.edu.hk/~nflaw/DNAComp/index.html.

519012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
519012.value: In the proposed RCC algorithm, one of the parameters is the number of clusters. This parameter is set so that sequences in one cluster are homogenous and share similar substructures while sequences in different clusters have different sub-structures. The setting of this parameter in the proposed RCC algorithm is heuristic and may not be optimal. In future, we consider using the multi-objective optimization method to determine this parameter. In the RCC algorithm, the objective function consists of two terms. These two terms measure dissimilarity of representative sequences of clusters and that of target sequences respectively. This can be considered as an approach for multi-objective optimization with linear scalarization using equal weight. Therefore, high accuracy could be obtained by using other more general approaches for multi-objective optimization. Besides, other properties may be important in some applications. For example, random access may be useful as it allows accessing to certain part of the DNA sequences without full decoding. In the proposed compression schemes, the reference-based compression hinders the random access. A full decoding is required before accessing any part of the DNA sequences. In order to allow random access, we may divide a sequence into several blocks which are then encoded separately in order to facilitate random access. This will be our future direction.

519012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
519012.value: Due to the advancement of DNA sequencing techniques, the number of individual genomes has now experienced a significant growth which makes storage, data distribution and management difficult. The aim of this project is to develop effective compression strategies for storing the DNA sequences. Traditionally, intra-sequence similarity is exploited for compressing a single DNA sequence which can only achieve an average of 10% compression gain. It is certainly not sufficient for large-scale data storage and distribution. Taking into account that researchers always download a set of genome-wide data in public databases, compression can be achieved by making use of inter-sequence similarity in the dataset. Our proposed scheme works by first defining a set of reference sequences. It is then followed by identifying similar subsequences within the set of the reference sequences and the sequence to be compressed. Lastly, these similar subsequences are encoded together to achieve compression. Results show that a large compression can be achieved. We have also investigated the use of various strategies to further maximize the compression gain. This includes ways to partition a group of DNA sequences to be compressed together into subsets so that different reference sequences can be used in different subsets to improve the compression ratio. Besides, we developed methods to construct an optimum reference sequence so as to optimize the compression performance. Experiments confirmed that these strategies can further reduce the compressed size by up to 91.0% when compared with state-of-the-art algorithms. In summary, this project has developed compression schemes to provide a standard data format for lossless compression of different DNA sequences.

519412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
519412.value: Residential dwellings typically use air-cooled window- or split-type air-conditioner for space cooling which is not energy efficient especially in subtropical climates where the outdoor air is hot and humid. Water-cooled air-conditioner (WAC) is a good alternative, as they are much more energy-efficient and the rejected condenser heat can be utilized for domestic hot water heating. The PI has recently completed successful research into the feasibility of its applications in dwellings. However, because the use of WAC for water heating requires the installation a large hot-water storage tank, which is expensive, occupies large space and less energy efficient. Adding that there is lack of in-depth research on measures to enable independent operation of space cooling and water heating, the application of WAC system in high-rise residential buildings is still limited. The modification of a WAC into a dual condenser unit, coupled with a phase change storage system, is a potential alternative to the conventional WAC system. Phase change materials (PCM), which have high heat storage density and small phase change temperature range, can be utilized to make the hot-water storage tank much more compact. The modified WAC, to be equipped with dual (air- and water-cooled) condensers (AWAC), will enable independent operation of space cooling and water heating. However, given the highly variable use patterns of air-conditioners and hot water in dwellings, whether or not the combined AWAC and PCM storage (AWAC-PCM) system can achieve the independent operation and energy saving objectives is subject to how the system is designed, integrated and controlled. In the proposed study, a prototype system consisting of a WAC, an air-cooled condenser, a carefully designed PCM storage tank, a four-way control valve, and the associated control and monitoring devices, will be assembled and installed in an environmental chamber for experimental studies. The environmental chamber serves to model the year-round operation conditions (indoor and outdoor) of the prototype system, while the experimental studies aim to determine the corresponding performance characteristics of the AWAC, and the PCM storage tank. Based on the experimental results, mathematical models for predicting the system performance will be formulated. Additional simulation studies will also be conducted for investigating the potential energy and environmental benefits for the application of the proposed AWAC-PCM system in high-rise residential buildings using Hong Kong as a case study city. The results will be useful for exploring the potential use of the proposed system in hot and humid climates. 在亞熱帶地區炎熱及潮濕的天氣條件下，居住建築中常用的風冷式分體空調器的節能效果不佳。而水冷式空調器是一種更為節能的替代方法，且在這一空調器中製冷劑冷凝過程中所放出的熱量可以用來加熱生活熱水。本課題的主要研究者在最近一系列的研究中已經指出了此系統用於居住建築的可行性。然而，由於運用該系統需要預先安裝較大的熱水水箱，此水箱會佔用較大的建築空間，同時會不可避免地影響整個系統的節能性，加之相關的領域中也缺乏對製冷系統和熱水加熱系統獨立運行的研究，因此，水冷式空調器在高層建築中仍未得到大規模應用。 將傳統的水冷式空調器改為雙冷凝器構造，並且與相變蓄熱系統結合，可以進一步提升水冷式空調器的節能效果。而通過選用具有較大蓄熱能力且相變溫度範圍較小的蓄熱材料，可以有效地減小熱水水箱的體積。 改造後的具有雙冷凝器的水冷式空調器，可以實現對建築供冷和供生活熱水獨立運行。但是，由於居住建築中對空調和熱水的使用具有易變性，雙冷凝器空調與相變蓄熱結合系統是否能在獨立運行的基礎上實現節能則依賴於整個系統的設計、組合以及控制。 在本課題中將建造一個具有水冷式空調器、風冷式冷凝器、相變蓄熱水箱、四通換向閥及相關控制和監控設備的實驗模型，並且放置在環境艙中對其進行實驗研究。 在實驗中環境艙用來模擬全年的室內外狀況，而實驗的目的是確定在這一情況下雙冷凝器水冷式空調器和相變蓄熱結合系統的運行特性。在實驗所得數據的基礎上，建立一個預測該系統運行性能的數學模型。 以香港地區的高層居住建築為例，本課題還將以能耗模擬為手段來研究運用雙冷凝器水冷式空調器和相變蓄熱結合系統的節能性。所得的結果可以為這一系統在炎熱和潮濕天氣條件下的運用提供參考。

519412.label: Realisation of objectives
519412.value: A storage-enhanced heat recovery room air-conditioner (SEHRAC) that combines AWAC and PCM was proposed. Its performance characteristics, system configuration, and energy benefits when used in residential buildings in Hong Kong were investigated through simulation and experimental studies. Accumulation of heat in the water tank of SEHRAC can result in an increase in tank water temperature, which will unavoidably affect the space cooling and water heating performances of SEHRAC. Measures to enhance the heat storage capacity of the water tank will thus be beneficial to the overall performance of SEHRAC. For achieving this objective, the use of phase change material (PCM) in the water tank was proposed in this study. To confirm and quantify the resultant performance improvement, laboratory experiments were conducted with and without the use of PCM (abbreviated as wPCM and woPCM scenarios). It was confirmed that the PCM could function as an internal heat sink to lower the rate of water temperature increase and to enhance the heat storage capacity of the water tank. As a result, the space cooling and water heating capacities for the wPCM scenario, as compared to the woPCM scenario, were 5.4% and 16.1% larger, respectively. The overall COP was therefore found 6.9% to 9.8% higher. It was also revealed that the use of PCM could extend the heat retention time of the tank water by 21.1%. Considering the significant refrigerant pressure fluctuations during the operation of SEHRAC, the selection of a suitable type of expansion device that can function properly despite the fluctuations is very important. In this study, the use of capillary tube (CT) and thermostatic expansion valve (TEV) in SEHRAC were side-by-side compared with the aim of optimizing the system configuration of SEHRAC. A prototype SEHRAC, which could be switched between the CT and TEV systems, was used for two identical sets of experiments. For each set of experiments, a series of tests under different outdoor temperatures were conducted. It was found that TEV could better regulate the refrigerant flow, maintain a stable evaporator superheat, and minimize the rise in refrigerant vapor content at the evaporator inlet during the operation of SEHRAC. The space cooling and water heating capacities for the TEV system were on average 16.3% to 19.4% and 18.5% to 23.4%, respectively, larger than the CT system. Its overall COP was also found 12.5% to 20.9% higher for the range of outdoor temperatures. The space cooling load and air-conditioning energy use of different residential units in a typical estate in Hong Kong were carefully simulated based on the actual building characteristics and realistic utilization patterns. On the basis of the simulation results, the recoverable heat and water heating demand profiles were formulated for three representative residential units. The profile comparisons indicated that in the air-conditioned season, free water heating objective could be achieved by the use of SEHRAC. It was also estimated that on wider application of SEHRAC, the potential energy and energy cost savings, as well as CO2 emission reduction would correspond to 9.3% of the overall contribution of the residential sector in Hong Kong. The results clearly show that SEHRAC is worthy of application even for dense living environment like Hong Kong.

519412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
519412.value: 1. A detailed mathematical model, which is capable of evaluating the dynamic performance of SEHRAC under time-varying conditions, can be developed. The availability of the model can overcome the inherent shortcoming associated with experimental investigations, which can only provide discrete performance evaluations. 2. As compared to CT, TEV is a more suitable option for use in SEHRAC as revealed from this study. However, it is noted that the space cooling capacity of the TEV-based SEHRAC still drops with operating time. This may be due to the fact that TEV is a linear controller in response to the evaporator superheat, but the refrigerant side operating parameters vary non-linearly during the operation of SEHRAC. Therefore, an electric expansion device (EEV) with multiple feedbacks and advanced control mechanism may be the best option for use in SEHRAC. The experimental results presented in this study may be useful in developing this control mechanism. 3. In this study, the PCM used for performance improvement of SEHRAC is limited to a paraffin/expanded graphite composite material. Other PCMs may also be investigated for use in this circumstance. The resultant performance improvement may be further enhanced if an optimal PCM is used.

519412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
519412.value: Air-conditioning and domestic water heating are two dominant energy end-uses in residential buildings in subtropical climates. In view of this, a storage-enhanced heat recovery room air-conditioner (SEHRAC) was proposed. This installation can serve the purpose of combined space cooling and water heating, and is particularly suitable for applications in subtropical regions, where most households are equipped with air-conditioners to combat the hot and humid summer. To facilitate the wide application of SEHRAC, this study provided an insight into its effectiveness, energy performance, operation characteristics, system optimization, and performance improvement when used for combined space cooling and water heating. The findings of this study can provide insight into combined space cooling and water heating in residential buildings and facilitate a wide application of SEHRAC in Hong Kong.

520012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
520012.value: Vegetation, ripraps and gabions are commonly used in water channel restoration projects for erosion control and bank stabilization. Decades ago most of the flood control channels in Hong Kong were constructed with plain concrete. They are now rehabilitated by using ripraps or gabions with vegetation to restore the natural habitat. The naturalization of water channels increases the flow resistance and raises the issue of flood control reconsideration. The current design guideline of gabion mattresses determines the size of aggregates such that the mattresses remain stable under the extreme flow conditions. In the design guideline no vegetation is considered. Vegetation causes the increase in flow resistance and flow depth. Under the extreme flow condition a portion of the vegetation may be uprooted. During the uprooting process the mechanical force and moment acting on the vegetation will be transmitted to the gabion and causes a significant local increase in the force on the gabion. In depth knowledge about the uprooting of vegetation in non-cohesive soil and its effect on the gabion is still lacking. There is a need to identify the role of vegetation on the stability of gabions. Gabions are porous. The flow over gabions can be subdivided into the surface and subsurface flow regimes. The interaction between the surface and subsurface flows will affect significantly the ecosystem and the mass transfer processes. The presence of vegetation will further complicate the process. There is a need to understand the flow and turbulence structures in this environment. For more accurate numerical modeling of flows through gabions the governing equations should be temporally and spatially averaged and the double averaged Navier Stokes (DANS) equations result. There seems to be no numerical model developed based rigorously on the DANS equations. The main difficulty is on the parameterization of the new form-induced stress terms. In the present proposed work laboratory experiments will be conducted to determine the change in the flow structures in gabion channels with vegetation, as well as the condition for the uprooting of vegetation and its effect on the stability of the gabions. The in-house 3D numerical model for flows through vegetation will be refined and verified to include the proper parameterized terms arisen from the double averaging procedure. The results will lead to a more accurate design of gabion channels with vegetation and will deepen the fundamental understanding of the flow and mixing behavior in the water environment there. 植被，拋石及石籠常用於水通道恢復項目來控制侵蝕及岸的穩定。幾十年來，香港大多數的防洪渠道都是用普通混凝土建造的。現在它們都已經使用拋石或有植被的石籠來恢復自然棲息地。水通道恢復增加了水流動阻力，及带出了防洪能力的再考慮。 目前石籠的設計指引決定石粒大小從而令石籠在極端的流動條件下保持穩定。在設計指引中植被沒被考慮。植被引起流動阻力和水深的增加。 在極端流條件下部分植被可能被連根拔起。在拔起過程中植被所受的機械力和力矩會被傳到石籠局部增加它的所受力。關於植被在無黏性土壤中被連根拔起的過程及其對石籠的影響的認識仍然缺乏，有必要確定植被在石籠穩定性中的作用。 石籠網是多孔的。水流過石籠網可以細分為表層流和次表層流。表層流和次表層流之間的相互作用會顯著影響附近的生態系統和傳質過程。植被的存在進一步複雜這個過程。有需要了解在這樣的環境中流和湍流的結構。 對水流經石籠更準確的數值模擬控制方程應該是在時間和空間上平均而得出雙平均Navier - Stokes（DANS）方程。似乎沒有數學模型席是基於嚴格的DANS方程開發的。主要的困難是如何參數化形狀引起的應力條件。 在本研究方案實驗室實驗會被進行以確定水流場結構在植被石籠渠道的改變，以及植被連根拔起的條件及對石籠穩定性的影響。內部開發的三維流數值模型會進行改良，引入雙平均过程產生的適當參數化項。結果將導致更精確的植被石籠渠道設計和深化那里水環境流動和混合过程的基本了解。

520012.label: Realisation of objectives
520012.value: For the first objective, we investigated experimentally and numerically the flow structure around foliaged plants deployed in a channel with gravels on the bed under submerged and barely submerged conditions. Velocity and Reynolds stress were measured by using a NORTEK Vectrino profiler. Visual observation shows that the initial motion of gravels is easier to be triggered under the condition of flow with barely submerged vegetation. This was confirmed by the measured velocity, Reynolds stress and total kinetic energy (TKE) profiles. The velocity exhibited a speed up in the near-bed region, and the associated Reynolds stress and TKE increase there. A 3D numerical model was then verified against the experiments and used to investigate systematically the effect of degree of submergence of foliaged plants on the channel bed shear stress. The results show that the maximum bed shear stress occurs when the foliage was situated slightly below the water surface, which can enhance channel bed instability. For the second objective, experiments were conducted to investigate the vegetation uprooting mechanics in open channel flow with non-cohesive sediment, and the effect of distribution pattern of vegetation stems on the drag force. Two failure mechanisms were identified, instantaneous failure and erosion failure, which highly influence the time for reaching the failure state. In the experiments plastic artificial submerged vegetation models with root system were buried underneath saturated sand. For instantaneous failure a mechanical moment with increasing magnitude was applied to the vegetation until overturning of the vegetation stem occurred. An approximately linear relationship between the moment and root length was obtained. For erosion failure the vegetation model was deployed in an open channel and subjected to a horizontal force induced by the water flow. The time to failure was recorded and analyzed. A quadratic relationship between the time and the total length of roots was obtained. The findings will be useful in establishing riparian vegetation in river restoration projects. To quantify more accurately the drag force on vegetation, the effect of distribution pattern of vegetation stems was investigated experimentally. The finite artificial vegetation patches of solid volume fraction ranging from 0.005 to 0.121 were used and the stem Reynolds number ranged from 500 – 2600. In the experiments the longitudinal water surface profiles and the flow rates were measured. The momentum equation relating the vegetation resistant force and water surface profile was used to obtain the bulk drag coefficient. The results show that the bulk drag coefficient decreases with increasing stem Reynolds number, decreases with increasing areal density of vegetation at fixed lateral spacing due to sheltering effect, and increases with solid volume fraction at fixed longitudinal spacing due to channeling effect. An empirical equation was obtained relating the bulk drag coefficient to the lateral and longitudinal spacing of stems. For the third objective a Double Averaged Navier Stokes equation (DANS) model is developed to simulate flows in gabion channels. The surface roughness of a gabion channel is large and the vertical profile of the longitudinal velocity will deviate from the logarithmic profile. Also in the layer consists of gravels and water the velocity variation is large due to the blockage effect of stones. The modeling of flow over this layer using the Reynolds Stress Navier Stokes equation (RANS) approach the governing equations need to be spatially averaged. This process generates the dispersive stress which is generally neglected in the models. For the present DANS model turbulence is modelled by the Spalart-Allmaras closure with a modified length scale which is dependent on a zero-plane-displacement parameter relating to the stone characteristics. The dispersive stress is modelled by a sub-length scale closure, similar to the Smagorinsky model used in Large Eddy Simulation. The model has been applied to several cases of flow over gravels. The velocity and Reynolds stress profiles are predicted correctly. The dispersive stress peaks at the correct level and with proper magnitude through calibration of the Smagorinsky coefficient. The effect of dispersive stress on the velocity profile and Reynolds stress profile generally is small. This is mainly because the peak dispersive stress is approximately one order of magnitude smaller than the peak Reynolds stress. The DANS model however is useful if the turbulent mixing phenomenon in the gravel layer is of interest. The dispersive stress can be comparable to the Reynolds stress within this region. The vertical distribution of porosity in the stone layer is also investigated and the effect is minor. The model is a concluded to be a suitable tool for the study of the flow and solute dispersion in gabion channels, especially in the region close to the gravel layer. The objectives have been achieved to satisfactorily. For the first objective, further experiments can be carried out the determine the hydrodynamic stability of channel bed gravels subject to flow through 2D patch of submerged foliaged vegetation. For the second objective, more experiments can be carried out to determine the uprooting moment of vegetation with different geometrical shapes. For the third objective, more sophisticated model for the dispersive stress can be explored. These have not been done in the present project due to resource limitation.

520012.label: Major findings and research outcome
520012.value: The effect of vegetation on gravel bed channel or gabion has been identified. The bed shear stress will be reduced by stem-type vegetation generally. For vegetation with foliage, the upper portion of the flow will be retarded. More flow will be redirected towards the near-bed region, resulting in higher bed shear stress. The increase in bed shear stress will enhance the risk of instability of the gabion channel. Visual observation shows that the initial motion of gravels is easier to be triggered under the condition of flow with barely submerged vegetation. This was confirmed by the measured velocity, Reynolds stress and total kinetic energy (TKE) profiles. Two failure mechanisms for uprooting of vegetation have been identified. Instantaneous failure occurs when the flow is large enough to produce a moment which causes overturning of the piece of vegetation. The overturning moment is related approximately linearly to the root length. Erosion failure occurs when the sands or gravels, in which the piece of vegetation was planted, were eroded to the extent that the anchoring moment of the roots is reduced to the value smaller than that of the overturning moment. The time to failure is related quadratically to the total root lengths. The bulk drag coefficient of vegetation is found dependent on the distribution pattern of stems. The results show that the bulk drag coefficient decreases with increasing stem Reynolds number, decreases with increasing areal density of vegetation at fixed lateral spacing due to sheltering effect, and increases with solid volume fraction at fixed longitudinal spacing due to channeling effect. The results show at the first time that the bulk drag coefficient is not a unique function of the areal density of vegetation. The dispersive stress arising from the spatially averaging of the Reynolds Averaged Navier Stokes equations has been parameterized and included in the DANS model. A sub-length scale closure, similar to the Smagorinsky model used in Large Eddy Simulation, has been used in the parametrization. Modle verification has been carried out in which the dispersive stress peaked at the correct level and with proper magnitude through calibration of the Smagorinsky coefficient. The DANS model is useful if the turbulent mixing phenomenon in the gravel layer is of interest. The dispersive stress can be comparable to the Reynolds stress within this region.

520012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
520012.value: The current design guideline of gabion mattresses determines the size of aggregates such that the mattresses remain stable under the extreme flow conditions. In the design guideline no vegetation is considered. The present results show that the bead shear stress can be enhanced due to the presence of vegetation with foliage and the channel is subject to higher risk of instability. A new design guideline of vegetation gabion channel should be established. The uprooting of vegetation will depend on the soil or gravel characteristics as well. More experiments can be done to investigate the relationship among the root length, soil particle size, cohesive strength and etc. The DANS model has room for improvement. Further experiments can be done to obtain more understanding of the dispersive stress. A more general and accurate closure of the dispersive stress can be included into the model. The DANS model can be extended to simulate the mixing process in the near bed region of vegetated channel.

520012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
520012.value: Vegetation, ripraps and gabions are commonly used in water channel restoration projects for erosion control and bank stabilization. The naturalization of water channels increases the flow resistance and raises the issue of flood control reconsideration. Vegetation causes the increase in flow resistance and flow depth. Under the extreme flow condition a portion of the vegetation may be uprooted. There is a need to identify the role of vegetation on the stability of gabions. The presence of vegetation will also affect the flow structure at the mixing process at the gabion channel surface. In the present project the flow structures around foilaged plants deployed in gravel channel was investigated. The results show that the maximum bed shear stress occurs when the foliage was situated slightly below the water surface due to the existing of a peak flow close to bed, which can enhance channel bed instability. The uprooting mechanisms were examined and the moment causing failure was related to the root lengths and the erosion time. The effect of distribution pattern of vegetation stems on the drag force were determined. A Double Averaged Navier Stokes equation (DANS) model was developed for more accurate simulation of flow through vegetated gabion channels.
