520212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
520212.value: The explosive growth of social media has provided millions of people the opportunity to share their opinions about a multitude of topics, such as politics, sports and especially commercial products of companies. The relationships and interactions among people play a fundamental role for the spread of opinions through their social networks. Monitoring online public opinions and analyzing positive or negative sentiment of opinions can be extremely useful for various business intelligence applications, notably viral marketing and customer relationship management. In recent years, opinion mining and sentiment analysis on social networks have attracted increasing attention from many researchers. The prior work of ours and others undoubtedly provided valuable market information for both consumers and companies, but they were mainly concerned with the content of information and thus are not able to answer the questions related to people’s behavior and social interactions, like how people’s opinions are formed and change, and how people influence each other to propagate opinions through the networks. In this project, we study opinion influence, which is equally important as analysis of opinion sentiment. It helps to identify opinion influencers who are often the targets of companies for advertising and feedback communication. To our knowledge, there is no adequate research to address this need. The main objective of this project is to develop a framework which includes models and techniques for mining opinion influence of individuals on others. To this end, we have identified several critical issues that are relatively under-researched in the past, including: (1) how to effectively define measurable influence so that the influence can directly link to opinion formation, opinion change and opinion propagation; (2) how to model and estimate the influence of one person on another from exiting people’s behaviors based on both the sentiment of the content of opinions they express and their social connections and interactions; and (3) how to formulate the relationship between the individual influence and the collective influence of a group of individuals on someone else. We will develop various probability models for the estimation and prediction of opinion influence on the basis of in-depth analysis of the characteristics of social media networks. The deliverables of this project include new concepts and innovative solutions to challenging issues in opinion influence modeling and computing on social networks. They will contribute to advance the research in opinion mining and add value to practical applications of business intelligence. 社交媒體的爆發爲成千上萬的人提供了一個自由的平臺，令他們可以隨時分享關於政治、體育和商品等話題的意見。社交網絡中，人們之間的關係和交流的行為在意見和觀點的傳播過程中扮演着重要的角色。公眾觀點的抽取和正反觀點的分析是現代商業智能中不可缺少的一個部分。 近年來，社交網絡上的觀點挖掘和情感分析吸引了大量研究者的不斷關注。應該承認現有的工作成果確實爲消費者和公司雙方提供了有價值的市場信息。然而，這些研究工作重點關注的是信息的內容，因而無法對與人們行為以及社交互動有關的問題作出回答，諸如，人們的觀點是如何形成和改變的，人們彼此如何互相影響致使觀點通過網絡不斷傳播。該項目將重點分析和研究不同觀點的影響作用和影響過程，並在此基礎之上識別意見點的影響者（即經常是公司廣告宣傳的主角和給出意見反饋的那些人）。據我們瞭解，目前在這個需求層面的研究工作尚很缺乏。 項目的主要目標在於開發相關模型和技術架構來挖掘個人意見對他人的影響。為此，我們確定了幾個關鍵的、以前研究相對不足的工作內容，包括：（1）如何有效地定義可度量的影響力，以便影響力可以直接和意見形成、變化和傳播相互關聯起來；（2）從現有的人們的行為，基於人們表達的意見內容以及他們在社交網絡上聯係和交互的數量，如何建立模型估量個人作用於其人的影響力。（3）如何確定個體影響力和群組影響力之間的關係。基於深度分析社交網絡的特性，我們將建立不同的概率模型來估量和預測影響力。 該項目的研究成果將包括社交網絡上的意見影響力建模和計算，及其一系列針對富有挑戰性的問題所得到的創新方法。它們將進一步開拓意見挖掘領域的研究領域並且有助於開發商業智能方面的實際應用。

520212.label: Realisation of objectives
520212.value: This project was commenced on January 1, 2013. The main objectives of this project are to investigate the key factors that have a bearing on influence modeling, develop the influence models that can capture the changes of people’s opinions on the social networks and estimate the interpersonal influence using machine learning based approaches, and to evaluate the learned influence models with the appropriate applications. With the efforts of several PhD students, research associate and research assistants, basically these targets are smoothly and successfully completed. Our researches were developed along the following main directions. (1) Influence Role Detection, Influence Modeling and Opinion Prediction After conducting extensive background surveys on social influence from both computer science and management science points of view, we noticed that understanding the role of influence is a precondition of influence modeling. Although all influential users perform influence on others, the way people use to influence others varies and as a result different influence produces different effect. Different influential users play different influence roles. Despite the importance of influence role, the previous work, however, emphasized on influential user identification. Our research then focused on influence role detection. To the best of our knowledge, our work is the first one that targets the problem of influence role detection. By exploring three views of features relating to topic, sentiment and popularity respectively, we proposed two multi-view influence role clustering algorithms (namely MIRC and CMIRC) to group potential influential Twitter users into five categories in terms of influence role. MIRC is an unsupervised approach while CMIRC is a semi-supervised approached that can take advantage of the prior knowledge. Although previous work has studied interpersonal influence as the probability of activating others during information diffusion, they ignored an important fact that information diffusion is the result of influence and dynamic interactions among users produce influence. We proposed a novel temporal influence model (TIM) to explore how influence emerges during communications by dynamically tracking users’ opinion behaviors over time. The learned influence model was validated in opinion prediction. Like other existing influence models, TIM suffered from the following two problems. First, it simply formulated opinions as derived sentiment categories but ignore the content conveyed in the opinions. Second, it only made use of the most recently received information without taking into consideration the long-term historical communication. To keep track of user opinion behaviors and infer user opinion influence from the historical exchanged textual information, later we developed a content-based influence model (CIM) with two alternative learning strategies. One is sentiment category based. The other is sentiment word based. This work was further extended to a content-based sequential influence model. We also noticed that people on social media often have two identities, i.e., the personal identities and the social identities with which people behave to fit the expectations of the others in the same group. We further explored users’ dual identities to build a more comprehensive opinion influence model for a better understanding of opinion dynamics. This work actually integrated both influence role detection and social influence modeling. (2) Information Diffusion Modeling and Prediction Social influence is closely related to information diffusion. We proposed a social representation learning approach to address the information diffusion prediction issue. The model we developed projected a social media user to a vector representation in a continuous latent space, and translated a specific diffusion process as a dynamic group formation towards a certain message under the group influence. To integrate the network structure constraints on information diffusion, it used pre-trained network embeddings as users’ initial representation and then gradually refined the model by the diffusion data. Our later work extended users’ unique representations to two role-based representations (as senders and receivers). Meanwhile, it optimized an objective function based on the diffusion rules extracted from the sequential cascades, and employed the network representation learning loss as a regularization term in the objective function to allow network structure and information diffusion influencing each other. In such a way, the network structural information and the diffusion information were tied more closely. In the recent work, we proposed a predictive network representation learning model to solve the structural link prediction problem. By jointly optimizing the two objectives, i.e., the observed structure preservation and hidden link prediction, the model could not only enhance the predictive ability of node representations but also learn additional link prediction knowledge in the representation space. Right now, we are working on joint user representation learning for both information diffusion and social link predictions. (3) Opinion Sentiment Classification Because of the influence from friends, users’ opinion towards a certain product may change over time, e.g., from positive sentiment to negative sentiment. Sentiment analysis is an indispensable component of dynamic opinion tracking and social influence modeling. Because the sentiment analysis recourses in different languages are not balanced and Chinese is often considered as a low-resource language, we focused on cross-lingual sentiment lexicon learning and cross-lingual sentiment classification in this project. For sentiment lexicon learning, we employed bilingual word graph label propagation to induce sentiment polarities of the unlabeled words for Chinese based on a bilingual graph established with the words in English and Chinese. We also explored co-training based bilingual sentiment lexicon learning, which concurrently learned sentiment lexicons for two languages under the co-training framework. When applying transferring learning to cross-lingual sentiment classification, we found that the performance did not reach to a promising level due to transferred errors. We proposed to integrate into knowledge transfer a knowledge validation model, which aimed to prevent the negative influence from the wrong knowledge by distinguishing highly credible knowledge. While the existing works for cross-lingual sentiment analysis mainly focused on exploiting common sentiment knowledge across the languages, we argued that language discrepancy is inherent and a part of human languages. Most recently, we tried model the language discrepancy in sentiment expressions as intrinsic bilingual polarity correlations. (4) Other Most Relevant Work One of the important influence roles is domain expert who is expected to provide professional knowledge and opinion to explain and convince. Expert finding on social media benefits both individuals and commercial services. We exploited tree representation to model the posts on social media and casted expert finding to the matching problem between the learned user tree and domain tree. Understanding social opinion not only helps customers to decide which produces they would like to purchase but also helps companies to develop online marking and advertising strategies. With product recommendation as an application, we proposed a novel integrated matrix factorization framework to model user preferences and trust relationship in order to describe how user preference changes and influences each other. In overall, the main goals of this project have been completely achieved, and the research results have been published in or submitted to 7 recognized journals and 13 conferences (with RGC funding acknowledgments), including the top conferences in information retrieval (SIGIR and CIKM), computational linguistics (ACL, EMNLP and COLING) and artificial intelligence (AAAI).

520212.label: Major findings and research outcome
520212.value: For influence role detection, MIRC consistently demonstrated the advantage of multi-view clustering approaches over single-view clustering approaches. CMIRC demonstrated its capability to incorporate the prior knowledge that allowed people to use a small number of users whose influence roles are easily identified by a company as the prior knowledge to find out many others for their needs. Two papers were published in SIGIR and the IJCAI SocInf Workshop. For influence modeling, TIM presented in IEEE IS was a dynamic model which modeled user behaviors as a Markov chain and coupled chains together to temporally correlate opinion influence among multiple users. It is the first work trying to model interpersonal influence as the continuous impact on people’s opinion behaviors on social media. CIM published in COLING was a content-based model. It explored how opinion words affect influence modeling and opinion prediction. The advantage over non-content-based models was demonstrated. TIM and CIM were extended into a content-based sequential opinion influence model which was submitted to IEEE TKDE. Modeling user influence with dual identities, submitted to CIKM, is the work integrating both influence role detection and influence modeling. For information diffusion and prediction, we were concerned with both the stable network structure and the dynamic diffusion cascades. We focused on social representation learning approaches and applied the learned representation to predict the potential diffusion in the future. The first work along this direction was included a book chapter be published. Our later work extended user representation learning to role-based (sender and receiver) representation learning, which was submitted to ACM TKDD. The network structure information was used as either initialization or regularization for user representation learning. We also developed predictive network representation learning approaches to solve the structural link prediction problem. The output was published in SIGIR. For sentiment analysis, bilingual graph based sentiment lexicon learning approaches and co-training based bilingual sentiment lexicon learning approaches were published in CL and AAAI. The work on credible knowledge validation and language discrepancy modeling for cross-lingual sentiment classification were published in ACL and submitted to CIKM. As other relevant work, please refer to the publications in ACL and SocialCom for the work of expert finding and opinion influence for product recommendation respectively. To understand how information was propagated over social media, we also conducted studies that tried to summarize the topics on social media. See ACL and TASLP papers.

520212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
520212.value: As previously-mentioned, social influence and information diffusion are closely related. Influence cannot be formed without information propagation and meanwhile the information cannot spread widely without social influence. We have studied both issues with consideration of their inherent connection. We have also analyzed the textual content for understanding and capturing opinion influence. It is our plan to explore content-based information diffusion characteristics, which contributes to rumor detection and information credibility analysis on social media where the spread information is never fully trusted.

520412.label: Project Title(Chinese)
520412.value: 平均場型正倒向隨機系統的最優控制及其金融應用

520412.label: Project Objectives
520412.value: Optimal controls of mean-field forward-backward stochastic systems; Mean-field forward-backward linear-quadratic optimal controls; Continuous-time utility portfolio selection on compensation.
rows: Optimal controls of mean-field forward-backward stochastic systems;
Continuous-time utility portfolio selection on compensation.

520412.label: Realisation of objectives
520412.value: In addition to contributing to the academic literature, our study has important yet practical relevance. With the alarm bells the on-going financial crisis rings, risk hedging has drawn much more attention than ever. Among various approaches of hedging and managing risk, mean-variance and utility portfolios are preferable by institutional investors. Further developing the methods presented by prior research, our approach should help provide risk-management advice for policy makers and institutional investors by better understanding and controlling potential risks. Moreover, our approach is easily implementable with a standard numerical technique, and therefore it provides managers with a usable way to make decisions. In addition, we present a motivation of mean-field linear-quadratic-Gaussian (LQG) games for stochastic integral systems in the accepted paper. Our study adds to the investment literature, since it extends the ideas for helping studying indefinite mean-fields stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control. Except these, we also develop portfolio selection to consider discrete-time (multi-period) portfolios with cone constraints in the investment field (see one paper accepted by Mathematical Finance). During the project period, we also study discrete-time mean-field linear-quadratic optimal stochastic control problems, and extend our ideas to analyze multi-period optimal portfolio selection models with mean-field formulation while the classical embedding technique cannot tackle.

According to mean-field forward-backward linear-quadratic optimal controls, what are conditions of mean-variance portfolio selection in the financial investment market?

Extend the results developed in objectives (1) and (2) to study optimal stopping strategies within the general framework in financial investment over a finite time horizon, such as ontinuous-time utility portfolio selection on compensation.

520412.label: Major findings and research outcome
520412.value: The mean-field type of optimal stochastic control models deals with problems in which either the system dynamics or the objective functional, or both, involve the states as well as the expected values of the states. The current work of this project employ the mean-field formulation to cope with seemingly non-tractable nonseparability in discrete-time portfolio selection problems. In particular, we revisit three challenging, yet practically important, portfolio selection models over a finite-time investment horizon, reformulate them as linear-quadratic control problems of a mean-field type, and derive their optimal strategies with improved solution qualities. Except these, we also introduce forward-backward differentail equations to develop the original idea, and we further consider it in discrete-time model during this project period. We published some papers and completed some working papers.

520412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
520412.value: Although the research in this direction has been well developed for continuous-time control problems, it lacks progress in both theoretical investigation and applications in discrete-time problems. [1] Optimal control techniques proposed in this project can be further employed to study multi-period linear-quadratic portfolio selection models. [2] Our methodologies and techniques on stochastic control can be adopted to study time-inconsistent models. [3] Our methods developed in this project can be applied to mean-variance and manager's compensation utility models with underlying assets following stochastic volatility and interest rates.

520412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
520412.value: As for the theoretical contributions, this study will contribute to the literature on various topics such as continuous-time/multi-period portfolio selection, investment strategies, fund management, incentive compensation, and agency theory. Specific to the literature on portfolio theory and investment, we expect the results to help shed light on the investment strategies on the basis of financial underlying assets in a continuous-time/multi-period framework. In addition, the methods adopted in the current research program will also improve the techniques studied and the implementations developed in the field of investment. This project is believed to be of value and of practical importance with long-term significance, and results derived from it are expected to yield highly publishable work. As one of the international financial centers in the global economy, finally, Hong Kong is currently suffering from the financial storm rooting in the United States and seeking risk-hedging solutions to stabilize the Hong Kong financial markets. Therefore, the project is particularly relevant to Hong Kong since it helps provide risk-management advice for Hong Kong policy makers and institutional investors by better understanding and controlling the risk.

521012.label: Project Title(Chinese)
521012.value: 大序列數據之線上分析處理

521012.label: Project Objectives
521012.value: Formulate a new PBA query type, namely, iceberg-PBA queries, that returns to users only cells that are of high significance. (Addressing Research Issue-A) Design a sequence OLAP engine architecture that works with a big data storage layer and exploits the facilities (e.g., MapReduce) offered by the existing big data infrastructures (e.g., Hadoop) when appropriate. (Addressing Research Issue-B) Research and implement (i) concise index structures and (ii) efficient query evaluation algorithms to meet the very stringent online query response requirement and memory requirement. The index structures should be concise enough to fit in the memory of the OLAP server for efficient query processing, despite the data size. Furthermore, the index structures should be easily maintainable because it is expected to have a large amount of new data arrive periodically. The query evaluation algorithms should exploit the developed index structures to return answers to users very quickly. (Addressing Research Issue-C) Evaluate the developed techniques with the use of real and synthetic data. The evaluation will include the usefulness of the new query type, the online response time and the scalability of the query evaluation methods.

521012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
521012.value: 現實生活中的許多種數據表現出數據之間的邏輯順序並且在本質上是有序的。序列數據的例子包括Web查詢日誌，股票數據，歸檔數據流, 各種系統產生的RFID日誌如供應鏈中的商品跟蹤系統，智能卡的電子支付系統如八達通等。類似於傳統的數據，對於這類數量巨大的序列數據進行存儲並且用一種用戶友好和有效的方式對其進行分析是一種強烈的科技需求。此項目的宗旨是研究和開發一個序列數據在線分析處理（OLAP）引擎。同構建傳統的關係型數據OLAP引擎相比，構建序列數據OLAP引擎在研究上帶來了一些新的挑戰。具體而言，傳統的關係型數據OLAP引擎支持基於屬性值的數據分組，新的序列數據OLAP引擎應該支持基於模式的數據聚合，即數據可以根據他們表現出來的各種模式而被分組並且每組的總計可以被計算出來。此外，隨着當今企業蒐集和存儲TB或者PB級別的序列數據（例如日誌）用作分析用途的情況越來越常見，新型OLAP引擎還應該能夠處理“大數據”。這些因素使得設計和實現一個序列數據OLAP引擎變得富有挑戰性。有趣的研究問題包括：“如何定義基於模式的聚合查詢？”“什麼數據結構應該預先計算，以支持基於模式的聚合查詢的在線評估？”和“如果序列數據非常大，會出現什麼特別的問題？” 儘管目前在OLAP和最近在“大數據分析”（例如MapReduce）方面，業界已經做了很多工作，根據我們的瞭解，很少有工作來討論構建一個對大序列數據進行處理的OLAP引擎。此項目旨在研究開發這種引擎，並且包括以下幾個內容：（i）基於模式的聚合查詢的正式定義以及對查詢結果有用性的調查，（ii）設計和實現合適的數據結構和算法以便有效評估基於模式的聚合查詢，（iii）構建原型引擎，該原型引擎用來評估基於模式的聚合查詢並以交互式速度將結果呈獻給用戶（iv）採用實驗對建議的方法的性能和可擴展性進行評估。這個項目的成功完成將給序列數據的OLAP領域帶來巨大的推動作用。

521012.label: Realisation of objectives
521012.value: 1. Formulating iceberg-PBA queries. (100% achieved) Given an iceberg threshold, among many different variants, we have defined an iceberg PBA query as the set of all iceberg cells whose aggregate values beyond the given threshold under different patterns. 2. Sequence OLAP engine architecture. (100% achieved) We have designed the architecture. Specifically, a set of data sequences S is stored on a secondary storage. As the system operates and answers queries, certain inverted indices and inverted lists are materialized. These materialized indices (lists) are stored in an inverted index store (II store). The II store serves as a disk-resident cache of the previously materialized lists. A replacement policy is employed by the system to control the II store’s content when the II store overflows. 3. Index structures and query evaluation algorithms. (100% achieved) Given an IPBA query “T, F, s” and its statistical requirement (e.g., error bound), our algorithm, SBA, returns the aggregate values of the iceberg cells of an s-cuboid under the given requirement. Given a pattern P instantiated from a pattern template T, SBA uses the inverted list of P for the synopsis S, to decide if the cell C(P) is iceberg and if so, to compute the cell’s aggregate value F(C(P)). 4. Evaluation. (100% achieved) We have evaluated our SBA algorithm using sequence datasets of different sizes and IPBA queries with different templates. Our evaluation results show that our solutions outperform the baselines by at least an order of magnitude.

521012.label: Major findings and research outcome
521012.value: In this project, we have successfully introduced a new type of queries for sequence data. Several statistical based algorithms are developed to evaluate pattern based queries. The results have been published as an CIKM conference paper and a TKDE journal paper. In addition, we have extended the concept and solutions to deal with graph sequences, which results in two IS journal papers. Furthermore, we have also extended the concept and solutions to sequence mining, whose results have been submitted to ACM TODS journal and undergoing a revision. Research Outcomes: 3 journal papers (+1 under review), 1 conference paper, and 1 M.Phil student.

521012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
521012.value: The next step is to extend the concept and solutions to stream data (which is another form of sequence data).

521012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
521012.value: Although there is ample work on online analytical processing (OLAP), there had been little work that discusses about building an OLAP engine for analyzing big sequence data. This project has researched and developed such an engine. The project has formally defined various forms of pattern-based aggregate queries and designed and implemented proper data structures and algorithms for evaluating those queries efficiently. The project has also prototyped the developed techniques as an sequence OLAP engine. Extensive experiments have been carried out and results show that the engine is highly efficient. The project has also been extended to deal with graph sequence data and sequence mining.

521312.value: 無線網絡下抗干擾多址接入跨層方案研究:系統設計與原型實現

521312.label: Project Objectives
521312.value: We propose to design a cross-layer IRMA mechanism to achieve high network throughputs for WiFi networks. The proposed IRMA is designed to be compatible with current WiFi standards and can be incorporated into WiFi technologies, protocols and products seamlessly. We propose to apply a RTS/CTS-like mechanism that can combat both hidden and exposed terminal problems at both the bit level and symbol level. We propose to append some symbol pattern information to the control frames at the physical layer so that these new control frames can not only work normally under high SNR/SINR environments but also be decodable under low SNR/SINR environments. Theoretically, the approach can silence all hidden terminals within the entire interference range and activate all exposed terminals introduced by the standard four-way handshake mechanism. We propose to design a large set of symbol patterns. Each symbol pattern contains a samples/bits sequence which is network-wide unique. We propose to use these symbol patterns to carry different information. We further propose to design a time-based symbol pattern scheme to carry the NAV time, which categorizes different NAV time values and uses different symbol patterns to represent them. We will explore how to make these symbol patterns most effective in carrying different types of information. We expect our design to achieve high performance under various environments. We propose to design a new channel access scheme to allow the exposed terminals to aggressively access the shared channel. As the concurrent transmissions are deliberately checked before each transmitter actually sends the packet, we expect that the channel’s spatial reuse can be highly improved. We propose to design a novel decoder framework that works for both bit-level and symbol-level signals. The decoder can correctly decode the incoming signals into bits under high SNR/SINR environments. However, if the system is under low SNR/SINR environments, the decoder can detect the symbol pattern information embedded in the incoming signal using the novel SLDD decoder. We propose to refine the design of the IRMA scheme so that it can seamlessly adapt to current WiFi networks. We also propose to explore the potentials of the proposed mechanism for other scenarios. We propose to verify the feasibility of the IRMA scheme through hardware experiements and evaluate its performance through simulations. We expect our approach to achieve satisfied performances.

521312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
521312.value: 雖然載波監聽在無線網絡中被廣泛用於避免衝突，該機制卻受制於隱藏終端和暴露終端問題。當前的WiFi標準主要使用四程握手機制（RTS/CTS/DATA/ACK）來克服隱藏終端問題和確認數據包的正確接收，但卻沒有解決暴露終端問題。該握手機制要正常工作必須要滿足兩個假設：節點的數據傳輸範圍和乾擾範圍相同以及所有的控制包都正確接收。在實際的無線網絡裡，這兩個假設常常不能成立。這使得用RTS/CTS機制無法清除來自收發節點周圍的鄰居節點產生的干擾，從而導致遠程隱藏終端問題和CTS衝突問題。而且，用ACK控制包來確認數據包的傳輸導致暴露終端不能同時傳輸數據。這些問題會導致無線網絡的吞吐量顯著下降。目前還沒有一個有效的方法一併解決這些問題。 本項目通過使用信標的相關及檢測操作來解決這些問題。本項目旨在設計實現一個跨層的抗干擾多址接入方案來解決由隱藏終端和暴露終端引入的干擾。具體來說，本項目將研究信標的相關及檢測技術，設計有效的、全網絡唯一的、可以用於表現各種信息，特別NAV 時間信息的信標模式，修改控制幀的結構，設計新的信道接入機制消除暴露終端，設計新型解碼方案以完全靜默隱藏終端，進行原型實現和仿真實驗，以及探討該項目進一步應用於其他場景的潛力。 本項目的成果包括設計實現跨層IRMA機制的一系列方案及技術。該系列方案及技術可以一體化地解決隱藏終端和暴露終端問題，從而大幅提高無線網絡在低信噪比下的吞吐量。 IRMA機制可以兼容現行的WiFi標準，並能與現有WiFi技術、協議及產品無縫對接。所有這些成果將對提升未來WiFi網絡的整體性能產生重要的貢獻。

521312.label: Realisation of objectives
521312.value: The project has achieved the following objectives: 1. We have designed a cross-layer IRMA mechanism to achieve high network throughputs for WiFi networks. The proposed IRMA is designed to be compatible with current WiFi standards and can be incorporated into WiFi technologies, protocols and products seamlessly. 2. We have designed RTS/CTS-like mechanisms, named RTS/S-CTS and IRMA, that can combat both hidden and exposed terminal problems at both the bit level and symbol level. The proposed approaches append some symbol pattern information to the control frames at the physical layer so that these new control frames can not only work normally under high SNR/SINR environments but also be decodable under low SNR/SINR environments. The approaches can silence hidden terminals within the interference range and activate exposed terminals introduced by the standard four-way handshake mechanism. 3. We have designed a set of signatures which are global-unique bit sequences. We have designed various schemes to use these signatures to carry different information. We have also designed mapping scheme, which categorizes different NAV time values and uses different signatures to represent them. Our design can achieve high performance under various environments. 4. We have designed a new channel access scheme to allow the exposed terminals to aggressively access the shared channel. As the concurrent transmissions are deliberately checked before each transmitter actually sends the packet, the channel’s spatial reuse is highly improved. 5 We have designed an SLDD decoder framework that works for both bit-level and symbol-level signals. The decoder can correctly decode the incoming signals into bits under high SNR/SINR environments. If the system is under low SNR/SINR environments, the decoder can detect the information embedded in the incoming signal using the novel SLDD decoder. 6. We have refined the design of the IRMA scheme to make it adapt to current WiFi networks. We have also initialized some interested work by applying the proposed mechanism to other scenarios. 7. We have verified the feasibility of the IRMA scheme through hardware experiments and evaluated its performance through simulations. Through these experiments and simulations, our approaches have achieve satisfied performances.

521312.label: Major findings and research outcome
521312.value: 1. The RTS/CTS mechanism might not correctly work all the time due to either the CTS packets are unable to be decoded at remote hidden terminals or the CTS packets are collided with other packets at the hidden terminals. Both of these drawbacks can deteriorate the throughput of the wireless network. We have designed the RTS/S-CTS mechanism that combats these two drawbacks. The RTS/S-CTS can achieve high throughput improvement compared with the standard RTS/CTS. The work is published in ICNP 2012 [1]. 2. To combat the exposed terminal problem and exploit the concurrent transmissions in wireless networks, we have designed Interference Resistant Multiple Access (IRMA), which can achieve higher throughput compared to the 802.11 standard. IRMA proposes a signature detection method in the physical layer to combat control frames' collisions, thus exploits the concurrency at the transmitter side. IRMA also designs a new NAV update scheme in the MAC layer to differentiate the interference ranges of different transmission links, thus exploits the concurrency of all non-interfering links. IRMA outperforms the 802.11 standard and other protocols significantly. The work is published in TMC [12]. 3. We have proposed a sample-address sample-duration scheme, which uses a short header to contain the critical control information in front of the data packet and leverages the advantages of both the downclocking mode and sleeping mode to achieve energy efficiency, to solve the packet overhearing problem. The finding of this work is published in SECON 2014 [4] and In TMC [15]. 4. We have explored the feasibility of symbol obfuscation to defend against the passive eavesdropping attack and fake packet injection attack during the wireless communications. We have designed a multiple inter-symbol obfuscation (MIO) scheme, which utilizes a set of artificial noisy symbols to obfuscate the original data symbols in the physical layer. MIO can effectively enhance the wireless communications security by achieving information-theoretic secrecy against the passive eavesdropping attack and computational secrecy against the fake packet injection attack. This work is published in TIFS [8].

521312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
521312.value: We have initiated the research in the following topics: 1. We have designed a fast tag identification protocol in RFID systems, which includes a collision tolerant mechanism (CTM) that can identify tags in collision slots correctly. By using CTM, all the tags in the collision slots can be identified successfully if the number of tags involved conforms to the signature detection limit. It outperforms other protocols dramatically. This work is published in PMC [7]. 2. We have applied the signature detection scheme to provide a power control mechanism for mobile ad hoc networks. Some preliminary work is published in EWSN 2016 [7]. 3. We have also designed a concurrent coordination mechanism by using signature detection and cancellation mechanism. some preliminary work is published in a ICCCN 2016 [9].

521312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
521312.value: Though carrier sense multiple access is widely used in wireless networks for collision avoidance, it suffers both hidden terminal and exposed terminal problems. The current WiFi standard mainly uses the four-way handshake mechanism to combat the hidden terminal problem, but it leaves the exposed terminal problem unsolved. This mechanism only works normally when a node's data transmission range is equal to its interference range and all control packets are correctly received. In a real wireless network, these conditions do not hold all the time which lead to both remote hidden terminal problem and CTS collision problem. Moreover, introducing the ACK to acknowledge the data transmission prevents the exposed terminals from transmitting concurrently. All these problems can dramatically reduce the throughput of wireless networks. This project aims to solve these problems by using a novel symbol correlation and detection approach. A cross-layer interference resistant multiple access (IRMA) approach is proposed to detect and resolve the interferences introduced by these hidden and exposed terminals. The proposed IRMA can be incorporated into WiFi technologies, protocols and products seamlessly. The outcomes of this project will make valid contributions to the development of future WiFi networks.

521812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
521812.value: Deep tissue injury is a particularly serious form of pressure ulcers secondary to many disabling conditions and chronic illnesses. It is clearly a biomechanical problem, but with many confounding factors. Unlike other pressure ulcers, deep tissue ulcers start near bony prominence deep under the skin surface. By the time the problem surfaces to the skin, the ulcers have likely become very difficult and very costly to manage. (Mak et al 2010) A damage accumulation and repair theory is proposed for the development of deep tissue ulcers based on the germinal work of Mak et al (2011). The theory covers damages incurred by direct cellular insults and ischemia during loading; and further damage accumulation due to reperfusion oxidative stress and inflammation responses during unloading. The theory to be further developed will track damages that can be reversed by the self-repair capacity of the affected cells. The theory will also register necrosis that cannot be reversed by the affected cells themselves. The repair of such necrosis would take a much longer process involving tissue regeneration by muscle stem cells. The theory will be implemented as anatomically relevant finite element models at the tissue level describing various anatomical features with a heterogeneous system of muscle, fat and skin tissues. The project will also include modeling at the cellular level involving extended ischemic domains due to microvascular occlusion, stiffening edema for necrosis, and an agent-based stochastic cellular automata algorithm for tissue regeneration by muscle stem cells. Estimations of model parameters and model validation will be pursued along with the animal studies that are being conducted under a complementary GRF project (RGC Ref. No. 523810). The theory will be applied to generate a number of model-driven guidelines on the design of prophylactic clinical protocols and assistive devices with a goal to reduce the risk of the onsets of deep tissue necrosis. Examples would include improvements in the design of various special seating systems and mattresses for high-risk patients; and the computer animations of various clinical scenarios and the associated biomechanical processes leading to deep tissue ulceration, for the purpose of clinical education among front-line clinicians. 深部組織損傷是繼發於許多殘疾和慢性疾病的一种特別嚴重的壓瘡。它主要是一個生物力學問題但亦受許多混雜因素影嚮。不像其他壓力性潰瘍，深部組織潰瘍始于皮下深處的骨突位置。當它發展至皮膚表面時，潰瘍的处理可能已經變得非常困難和昂貴。 本研究為深部組織潰瘍所提出的損傷積累和維修理論是建構在麥等人（2011）的基礎工作上。該理論的發展將涵蓋通過在加載過程中給于細胞的直接机械性傷害和缺血狀態的引發，和在卸載過程中再灌注氧化應激和炎症反應所引起進一步的損傷積累。理論包括細胞的自我修復能力及損害的可逆轉性，並追踪不可逆轉的壞死。這种壞死的修復將需要更長並涉及肌肉幹細胞的組織再生過程。該理論將以多尺度有限元模型，涉及一个包括肌肉，脂肪和皮膚不同解剖特徵的宏觀異構組織模型，並模擬在微觀細胞層面上由於微血管阻塞所導致缺血性微域的擴展，組織壞死後的腫脹硬化，並以隨機元胞自動算法模擬牽涉肌肉幹細胞的組織再生過程。參數估計和模型驗證將參照另一GRF項目（研資局編號523810）的動物實驗。

521812.label: Realisation of objectives
521812.value: We regarded we have fully completed the first two objectives and have attempted about 80% of the last two objectives. Please refer to the following for our major achievements, the difficulties we encountered, and the alternatives we have accomplished. With our earlier collaborators at PolyU in experimental studies using a rat model, we gained an overall understanding of the damage-repair dynamics in the tibialis muscles subjected to a small number of episodes of prolonged loading and unloading. The temporal profile of the damage-repair (in term of the number of interstitial nuclei) suggested the length scales for our theoretical modeling. Having said that, we encountered difficulty in using those experimental data directly as they were for our modeling purpose here. The number of interstitial nuclei in the tissues, while it could reflect the intensity of the inflammatory response to the incurred damage, might not be a proportional measure of the damage itself. The inflammatory response, once invoked by certain threshold damage, could flare up fully to a plateau. Such highly non-linear response would make the number of interstitial nuclei not an ideal parametric measure of damage for the purpose of our theoretical modeling. Because of such limitation, we could only use our collaborators’ experimental data qualitatively rather than quantitatively. Parametric analyses were conducted to study the sensitivity of our model predictions to the input parameters. The results of these parametric studies are useful in identifying the parameters which need to be measured more precisely and those which may be less so. We have gone beyond our original “damage and repair theory” (DART), and successfully further developed and implemented the theory in a geometrically relevant model on a finite element analysis platform ABACUS. The work was reported in our 2014 J Biomech paper (Xiao et al., 2014). As an alternative, we were particularly excited by our multiscale multiphysics modeling of how lymphatic dysfunction, as a result of anchoring filaments being disrupted by excessive peri-lymphatic mechanical stress, could lead to the building-up of interstitial pressure, tissue stiffening, vascular occlusion, and finally ischemic damage in the muscle tissues. The work was conducted using ABACUS presented at the 12th International Symposium of Computer Methods in Biomechanics and Biomedical Engineering in Amsterdam in 2014. Another exciting theoretical modeling work related to damage accumulation in DTI development was also completed as an alternative. The work was stimulated by our own in-vitro experimental findings that muscle cells damaged by low but prolonged compressive stress could release toxic biowastes that could compromise other cells in the surrounding and reduce their capacity to support mechanical loads. We demonstrated using the multiphysics modeling platform COMSOL the role of such toxic biowastes in the propagation and expansion of the deep tissue injuries to full-fledged ulcers. The work was accepted for publication in Annals of Biomedical Engineering just earlier this year.

521812.label: Major findings and research outcome
521812.value: We have established three theoretical models to study the propagation of deep tissue injury (DTI) to become full-fledged pressure ulcers. (1) A phenomenological model was developed to simulate how post-ischemic reperfusion damage may contribute to the expansion of deep tissue ulcer in different courses of loading-unloading dynamics. A semi-3D finite element model of a human buttock was used to simulate the process of ulcer evolution based on our damage accumulation and repair theory for DTI. The theory included not only the loading damage, but also further reperfusion and inflammatory injuries upon unloading. The results showed that depending on the model parameters and loading conditions, a deep tissue ulcer may initiate around a bony prominence and expand to affect the entire tissue thickness. The damage evolution can be affected by the tissue healing rate, the loading–unloading pattern and the cushion stiffness. The results may help clinical workers appreciate the importance of proper patient turning and the appropriate choice of cushion. The work was published in Daniel Z.T. XIAO, Shirley Y.Q. WU, Arthur F.T. MAK. Accumulation of Loading and Unloading Reperfusion Injury – Modeling of the Propagation of Deep Tissue Ulcers. Journal of Biomechanics. 47(2014): 1658-1664. 2014. (2) A multiscale mechanistic model was established based on images of different scales. The tissue level model is the highest hierarchy level model which was similar to (1). The fascicles are surrounded by the perimysium and bundled into a whole muscle, formed the second hierarchy level or fascicle level. The muscle fibers were surrounded by endomysium and grouped into fascicles to form the third hierarchical level or fiber level. Porous hyperelastic/ hyper-viscoelastic constitutive relations were assumed in this multiscale model to simulate the physics of interstitial flows. The primary valve-initial lymph system was vulnerable to damage if the average peri-lymphatic tensile strain around the initial lymphatic exceeds certain threshold. Tissue stiffening was simulated as pore pressure built up with lymphatic dysfunction, which could compromise capillary transport leading to ischemic damage, This multi-scale model demonstrated that lymphatic edema can lead to vascular occlusion & apparent mechanical stiffening. Such modeling can be applied to predict the damage propagation in muscle caused by both mechanical and ischemia injury. The work was presented in Daniel Z.T. XIAO, Sing Wan WONG, Arthur F.T. MAK. Multiscale Modeling of Tissue Edema in Muscle Fiber Level: A Finite Element Study. The 12th International Symposium of Computer Methods in Biomechanics and Biomedical Engineering. Amsterdam. October, 2014. (3) Based on our experimental findings that biowastes released by mechanically damaged muscle cells could be toxic to the surrounding muscle, we used COMSOL to simulate the compressive stress distribution and the diffusion of biowastes in a semi-3D buttock finite element model. The in-silico results showed that toxic biowastes released from cells damaged under prolonged low stresses, if allowed to accumulate, can advance the damage expansion to within the critical time zone. The work was accepted for publication in Yifei YAO, Lucas Xian Da ONG, Xiaotong LI, Kinlun WAN, Arthur F.T. MAK. Effects of Biowastes Released by Mechanically Damaged Muscle Cells on the Propagation of Deep Tissue Injury: A Multiphysics Study. Paper accepted. Annals of Biomedical Engineering. September 2016. (DOI: 10.1007/s10439-016-1731-2.)

521812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
521812.value: Cell damage can be caused by various mechanistic pathways such as direct mechanical damage, oxidative reperfusion damage, ischemic damage, biotoxin damage, etc. Cell death as a well defined categorical variable should be measured directly rather than indirectly using its subsequent inflammatory responses. We propose to use ATP depletion monitored using relevant intracellular biomarkers as a common currency to demarcate cell death. Such technique would likely avail us with experimental data that can be more readily used to compare with our theoretical predictions.

521812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
521812.value: Deep tissue injury (DTI) is a serious form of pressure ulcers facing many people of disability. It arises when tissues around bony prominence are subjected to prolonged excessive loading. DTI are difficult to detect initially. By the time they show up on the skin surface, the entire body tissues layer have become necrotic and the condition becomes very difficult to manage clinically. We have first developed and applied a "Damage Accumulation And Repair Theory" (DART) to describe how damage not only can accumulate during loading, but that oxidative reperfusion injury may also contribute to damage accumulation during unloading, at least initially before repair finally kicks-in. We have also developed a multiscale mechanistic model to demonstrate how skeletal loading on the surrounding muscle tissues may cause lymphatic dysfunction. The subsequent build-up of interstitial fluid pressure could occlude capillary transport, which in turn may cause ischemic injury and ultimately tissue necrosis. Thirdly, we have also established a multiphysics model to illustrate how the release and diffusion of toxic biowastes from cells damaged mechanically under prolonged low compressive stresses may compromise the load-bearing properties of the surround cells, allowing the original injury to propagate and expand earlier and faster to become full-fledged pressure ulcers.

523412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
523412.value: Reducing the carbon footprints of buildings to address the sustainable development strategy is a top priority in the agenda of the research community. Currently maintaining thermal comfort and generating hot water in buildings consumes over 30% of global energy supplies. As a continuation of a recently funded GRF project, this project aims to develop phase-change-materials (PCM) based active thermal energy storage(TES) technologies that can maximize the use of solar thermal applications and off-peak electricity for hot water and building heating provisions. Utilizing the latent heat of melting/solidification processes, a PCM based TES system has two perceived advantages: it can store a larger amount of heat in a small volume and at a small temperature difference between the charging source and discharging user, and can potentially complete the charging in a shorter period. The former is critical in space-constrained urban applications, and the latter critical in utilizing natural sources. It is expected that the newly developed TES technology, if successfully applied in Hong Kong, can virtually eliminate the use of fossil energy for hot water provision, and thus cut our residential energy use by 20% and result in both carbon footprint reduction and local air pollution improvement PCM/water emulsion will be experimentally investigated and the storage unit involving heat-exchanger and fluid flow will be designed in comparison with the alternative PCM forms of bulk PCM and PCM microcapsule/water slurry, based upon optimization principles. This will be achieved through multi-disciplinary research collaboration, involving chemical engineering research, heat transfer investigation and optimization design. In the PCM preparation, nano-additives will be used to reduce the supercooling degree, which is related to the thermodynamic metastable phenomenon; and the optimization will be enhanced based on the constructal theory. In the optimization analysis, the material and preparation/processing costs of PCM media will be taken into account. While much of the methodology is common with our recently funded project on media development for building cooling applications, the working temperature for solar thermal building heating and hot water applications will be in the higher range of 40 to 60◦C, which implies further refinement of the system optimization requirement. New PCM materials, nucleating agents and emulsifiers/surfactants will be developed via physiochemical methods, taking into consideration the potential energy needed at the elevated temperatures in the media preparation/ production processes, and the theory and methods developed will have implications for many other engineering applications. 用于太阳能热利用的水基乳液相变材料蓄热技术的研究 努力降低樓宇耗能的碳排放量并實施可持續發展策略已成為現今學術界頭等關鍵的議題之一。近期有研究表明，保持樓宇內部的熱舒適以及為樓宇提供熱水的耗能已超過了全球耗能的30%。作為另一個我們近期獲得的GRF資助項目的延續，本項目意在開發一種利用主動式蓄熱技術的新型蓄能材料，最大化利用太陽能和非尖峰時刻的電能以滿足樓宇的供熱需求。該蓄熱系統由於充分利用相變材料融化及凝固過程中的潛熱而帶來了兩個明顯的優點：該系統可以以更小的體積和更小的溫差為用戶側儲存和提供更多的熱量。同時該系統的利用可以大大縮短蓄能過程所需的時間。前者對於改善如今城市高速發展所面對的空間局限性有極大的意義，而後者則體現了對於自然能源的充分利用。該項新型蓄能技術如果能夠成功地在香港應用，可以極大地減少由於熱水供應而帶來的對于煤炭和石油的需求。對於住宅建築來說，這項技術可以降低20%的能耗，從而明顯地減少二氧化碳排放以大大緩解環境污染的現狀。 我們將通過實驗開發并研究這種新型相變乳漿液的性能，同時我們也將設計該套包含了換熱器及熱流體的蓄能裝置。純相變材料、微膠囊化相變漿液以及相變乳漿液等不同類型的相變材料均會作為備選材料以優化該蓄能系統的設計。這項複合型科學研究涵蓋了化學工程、傳熱學、以及最優化設計等多個領域。在相變材料製備的過程中，將會添加納米材料以降低由於熱力學亞穩態現象而帶來的過冷現象。最優化設計將會基於构型(constructual)理論來進行， 材料製備過程的成本核算也會被涵蓋到整體優化設計的核算中。 該項目所涉及到的技術和理論與我們最近獲得的GRF項目十分類似。與該項關於樓宇製冷應用不同的是，本項目所研究的材料的工作溫度適用於太陽能供熱以及熱水供應的應用，所以其材料的工作範圍是處在40-60◦C這個比較高的範圍，因此這需要對整個系統的優化設計進行更進一步的細化研究。新型相變材料、成核催化劑、表面活性劑及乳化劑的研究開發將涉及到物理化學方法，并充分考慮到對於這種較高溫度相變材料製備過程中所可能帶來的能耗及成本的提升。這些所涉及到的技術和方法將會為其他工程應用提供有益的借鑒。

523412.label: Realisation of objectives
523412.value: 1. PCM emulsion preparation The paraffin, n-octacosane, was chosen as PCM with a melting temperature of approximately 60 °C and a latent heat of 254 kJ/kg. The PCM emulsion consists of PCM, water, emulsifiers (surfactants) and other functional ingredients, such as the nucleating agents for the supercooling suppression. And SiO2 Nanoparticles were used as additives to control the supercooling degree of developed PCM emulsions. Emulsifiers are amphipathic molecules consisting of a non-polar hydrophobic part, mostly a hydrocarbon chain, and a polar hydrophilic part. In this project, the effects of different non-ionic emulsifiers, including nine kinds of binary mixtures of Tweens and Spans, on the droplet diameter distribution, the apparent viscosity and the stability of the emulsions, were evaluated to select the suitable emulsification conditions. To make an emulsion, mechanical energy is supplied for premixing of nuclear agents and for preparing PCM emulsions. 2. Evaluate and characterize the natures of the PCM media. The size distribution of the emulsion droplets was determined by the dynamic light scattering analysis (DLS), using a laser diffraction particle size analyser (Malven Zetasizer, model 3000HSA). The morphology of the PCM-water emulsion was examined using a Leica DM4000 optical microscope at a magnification of 400 - 1,000x. And the surface morphology of PCM droplets was examined using a scanning electron microscope (SEM, JEOL model JSM-6490, Japan), with a magnification larger than 1,000x. These results indicated that the averange droplet sizes of the emulsions ranging from 0.5 to 2 μm. 3. Experimental investigation of the stability, fluid flow and thermodynamic characteristics of the PCM/water emulsions. The storage stability of emulsions was investigated by observing the difference in droplet size and phase separation of the samples after the storage period and/or centrifuge. An idol emulsion product should have little or no stratification and droplet changes after a storage period even the centrifuge. The standard procedure for testing the thermal stability of PCM emulsions under thermal cycles is to subject them to multiple freeze-thaw cycles. Droplets of partial products might be destroyed and form a separate oil layer over emulsions. The volume ratios of the separated oil phase to the total volume of the emulsions were compared to evaluate the thermal stability of samples. Results show that the developed PCM emulsions were stable for months, and there was no distinct growth in droplet sizes and phase separation occurred. The bi-surfactant system with Tween and Span was effective to enhance the stability of the PCM-water emulsion in multiple phase change cycles. The viscosity and the rheology characteristics of the PCM emulsions were determined using a rotation viscometer with the ultra-low viscosity adapter (Brookfleld, DV-E), which can measure the viscosity of all kinds of Newtonian fluids and the apparent viscosity of Non-Newtonian fluids. As the emulsions showed a non-Newtonian fluid behavior, the apparent viscosities at different shear rate (0.6 - 100 s-1) were compared to determine the fluid flow behaviors of the emulsions. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was used for investigating the thermal properties of the PCM candidates and PCM nano-emulsions, such as melting/freezing points, latent heat of fusion and the supercooling degrees.

523412.label: Major findings and research outcome
523412.value: 1. The PCM-water emulsion, n-octacosane in water emulsions, was prepared at a working temperature of approximately 60 °C. Tween 80 and Span 20 (mass ratio: 1/1) were selected as the optimum emulsifiers, and a PCM mass fraction of 20 wt% was found to maintain the fluidity of the emulsion. In addition, the minimum effective concentration of the emulsifiers investigated in this work was approximately 5 wt%. 2. The degree of supercooling was limited in the bulk PCM, and the emulsion prepared at 8,000 rpm but was significant for the samples with small droplets. Hydrophobic SiO2 nanoparticles were used as nucleating agent in the supercooled emulsion samples. The degree of supercooling was effectively controlled at an optimized nucleating agent concentration of 0.3 %. However, multiple phase transitions were observed in the melting and crystallization processes of the PCM, which can be regarded as de facto supercooling. 3. About their fluid behavior, the shear thinning property of a pseudoplastic fluid was observed. The emulsion samples achieved the highest apparent viscosities at 50 °C, as the non-ionic emulsifier molecules aggregated into micelles at the minimum CMC. In addition, the rheological characteristics of the emulsion were quantitatively described by the power law fluid model, and the flow behavior index m and the consistency coefficient K within the non-Newtonian regions at different temperatures were calculated. 4. The emulsion stability was evaluated and discussed. Despite the appearance of a cream layer during the storage period, no distinct droplet size growth was observed, and the uniformity of the emulsions could be restored after being stirred. However, after freeze–thaw treatments, a separated oil layer appeared over the emulsion in all samples because of partial coalescence. High-speed homogenization resulted in small-sized droplets with a uniform distribution, which enhanced the stability of the PCM–water emulsion. 5. Based on the above results, a novel paraffin-based PCM nano emulsion was developed with a long expected service life. The average droplet size of the phase change emulsion droplet is less than 200nm, and its appearance is translucent. Through a long period of standing and repeated freeze-thaw cycles, it can still maintain the original physical properties. Its stability, therefore, is much better than the conventional phase change emulsion, with a good mobility, which is an ideal pumpable thermal functional fluid.

523412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
523412.value: 1. The present work should be further extended to better understand the phase transition mechanism of PCM nanoemulsion preparation by conducting experimental investigations on thermal characteristics and fluidity behavior. As the key factors affecting nanoemulsion formation remain unclear, further fundamental and theoretical research must be performed on this aspect. 2. The fluid stability of PCM emulsions must be investigated at different Reynolds numbers in a uniform heated circular tube to obtain wide applicability of the latent heat fluid in direct heat exchange systems. The reason is that the current experiments and majority of existing reports were only conducted under the static state condition such that the findings are unsuitable for practical engineering applications. 3. Multi-emulsifier system is recommended to stabilize the PCM emulsion. Mixed emulsifiers will form a denser interface film by filling the void spaces in the single-emulsifier system. 4. Although a small droplet size distribution favors emulsion stability, a moderate viscosity is also needed to prevent the droplets from intense movements, as the particle motion is expected to be more drastic as the size decreases.

523412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
523412.value: Solar panels have been widely used for hot water productions in many buildings, and the water storage tank has been the necessary part. Alternative thermal storage in place of the water storage tank can signficantly increase the solar energy utilisation potentials. This project aims to develop a novel phase change material (PCM) /water emulsion fluid for this purpose. The specific desired working temperature, a low supercooling degree, higher energy storage density and a long service life are the desired features of such a fluid. The capacity is enhanced by using the latent heat. Phase change material (PCM)/water emulsions, namely PCM droplets dispersed in water with the assistance of emulsifiers in a micro size, improve the heat transfer in a heat exchanger, requires simpler storage tank design, and have a much lower cost than other forms of thermal storage fluids. And this together with a good fluidity make PCM emulsions of an advantage in TES systems, which can be applied in many fields such as buildings and factories for the energy conservation. It is estimated that the successful application of this technology can potentially help to tackle the global warming problem by reducing CO2 emissions accompanying electricity generation.

523612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
523612.value: The rapid development and utilization of electrical and electronic devices and systems in the broad microwave frequency range of 1-18 GHz (i.e., the L-Ku bands of microwaves) have significantly increased the impact of electromagnetic interference (EMI) pollution on electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), humans, organisms, and the environment. In addition, the increasing interference of wind turbines to navigation radars for air and marine traffic control and the increasing requirements of safety and survivability for military crafts and vehicles against radar detection have called for new advances in EM stealth (or low observable) technology. Hence, there are great socioeconomic demands and benefits for high-performance microwave absorbers to reduce EMI pollution on the one hand and to advance EM stealth technology on the other hand. Core-shell nanocapsules, consisting of a magnetic nanoparticle core and a dielectric, semiconductor or conducting polymer shell in the nanometer size range, have recently emerged as a promising class of microwave absorbing materials because of their greater potential for realizing advanced microwave absorbers with stronger absorption and broader absorbing bandwidths at smaller absorber thicknesses and weights compared to other existing materials. However, the reported core-shell nanocapsules (e.g., FeNi-C, Ni-ZnO, BaTiO3-PANI, etc.) only exhibit relatively strong absorption in some limited frequency ranges with dramatic variations in absorption with absorber thickness due to the limited material-phase variety and architecture designability constrained by their single core-shell arrangement and spherical-shaped isotropic core, respectively. In this research, a novel class of microwave absorbing materials namely “core-multishell nanoarchitectures” (CMSNAs) is proposed for next generation microwave absorbers. The CMSNAs feature an architecturally designed magnetic nanoarchitecture core encapsulated by several layers of shell (called multishell) made of dielectrics, semiconductors, and/or conducting polymers. The core-multishell arrangement serves to broaden the absorbing bandwidth and mitigate the variation in absorption with absorber thickness by the bandwidth-broadening effect in various core-multishell material phases. The architectured core aims to enhance absorption over the broadened bandwidth by an improved EM match of the shape-anisotropically increased magnetic relative permeability of the core to the dielectric relative permittivity of the core-multishell. First, various interesting CMSNAs will be designed and synthesized. Second, the microstructural, electrical, magnetic, and microwave absorbing properties of CMSNAs will be evaluated. Third, microwave absorption models will be established to analyze CMSNAs and investigate their underlying absorbing mechanisms. Finally, CMSNA-based microwave absorbers will be developed, characterized, and demonstrated in the electrical circuit protection and wind power industries for EMI reduction and EM stealth applications. 隨著電機及電子裝置與系統在1–18 GHz寬闊的微波頻率範圍(即L–Ku微波頻段)的迅速發展和廣泛應用,電磁干擾(EMI)污染已大大增加了對電磁相容性(EMC)、人類、生物和環境的衝擊。此外,越來越多風力渦輪機對空中及海上交通控制用的導航雷達造成干擾,以及軍用飛機、車輛和船隻對反雷達檢測能力的要求不斷提升,這對電磁隱形(或低可觀測)技術的進一步發展有著急切的需要。因此,研發高性能的微波吸收材料一方面可抑制電磁干擾污染,另一方面亦可推進電磁隱形技術的發展,對社會和國家的經濟需求與效益有著舉足輕重的地位。 核殼形奈米囊是目前最新穎、被譽為最有應用前景的微波吸收材料。它是一種在納米尺度上將磁性顆粒核心和電介質、半導體或導電聚合物殼有效地結合起來,從而產生傳統塊體、甚至微米材料無法實現的新性能,如在較小的厚度和重量下具有更強的吸收能力和更闊的吸收頻寬。但是,現今報導的核殼形奈米囊(如FeNi-C、Ni-ZnO、FeNi-C、Ni-ZnO、BaTiO3-PANI、BaTiO3-PANI等)不但只在一些有限的頻率範圍內才能表現出較強的吸收能力,而且其吸收能力與材料厚度有著戲劇性的變化関係。其成因有二:第一,其單核殼的構造限制了材料相的種類;第二,其球形各向同性的磁性顆粒核心限制了結構的可設計性。 本研究提出一類名叫「核多殼形奈米結構(CMSNA)」的新型微波吸收材料,作為新一代的微波吸收材料。這CMSNA具有特定設計的磁性奈米結構核心封裝於由電介質、半導體及/或導電聚合物組成的多層殼內(稱為多殼)。這核多殼的新構造主要利用多種材料相引起的頻寬擴大效應來擴闊吸收頻寬,以及減輕吸收能力與材料厚度的變化関係。這特定設計的磁性奈米結構核心主要透過提升其形狀各向異性而增大的相對磁導率,並與核多殼的相對介電常數進行有效的電磁匹配,從而達到在已擴闊的吸收頻寬下曾強吸收能力。首先,我們會對各種有趣的CMSNA進行設計與合成。接着,我們會評估其微觀結構、電性能、磁性能和微波吸波性能。還有,我們會建立微波吸收模型,用以分析及探討其底層吸收機制。最後,我們會發展適用於電磁干擾抑制及電磁隱形的CMSNA微波吸收材料,並展示於電路保護和風能電力工業。

523612.label: Realisation of objectives
523612.value: The three project objectives have been fully achieved with the production of “14” good SCI journal papers as the direct output. The scope of realization is summarized as follows: (1) In line with the proposed objectives, and based on the well-established research collaborative effort between the PI and the Co-I, a total of 14 interesting types of magnetic nanoarchitectures (i.e., the core of the proposed CMSNAs --- “Core-MultiShell NanoArchitectures”) were designed and synthesized by various methods (including hydrothermal, solvothermal, arc-discharge methods, etc.) to exhibit different magnetic materials (including Fe3O4, HoMnO3, Ni, Fe, ZnFe2O4, NbN, etc.) in different nanoarchitectures (including nanoflake, nanodisk, hollow nanosphere, nanoplate, nanobutterfly, etc.) and sizes (from several ten to several hundred nanometers) [Objective 1]. The phase, surface chemistry, morphology, size, uniformity, microstructure, defects, etc. of the magnetic nanoarchitectures were characterized to understand the growth/formation mechanisms [Objective 2]. The dielectric, magnetic, and microwave absorbing properties of the magnetic nanoarchitectures were evaluated in the microwave frequency range of 1-18 GHz, covering the most important L, S, C, X, and Ku bands of microwaves, so as to realize the microwave absorbing performance and the underlying absorbing mechanisms [Objectives 2 and 3]. (2) In order to observe and valid our proposed enhancement effect of shape anisotropy on microwave complex permeability and absorption (i.e., reflection loss) in the magnetic nanoarchitectures in (1), a novel theoretical model for calculating the microwave complex permeability and absorption of the magnetic nanoarchitectures and their microwave absorbers was proposed and developed based on the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation and the Bruggeman's effective medium theory. This model was applied to explain the measured microwave complex permeability and absorption of the magnetic nanoarchitectures and their microwave absorbers with and without magnetic field-induced rotational orientation of the magnetic nanoarchitectures in the microwave absorbers in (1). The good agreement between the measured and calculated results confirmed the validity of our model for the description of the magnetic enhancement and resonance effects. [Objective 3] (3) With the establishment of the experimental and theoretical know-hows in magnetic nanoarchitectures and their microwave absorbers in (1) and (2), respectively, five interesting types of core-shell nanoarchitectures (i.e., the basic form of the proposed CMSNAs) with Fe and Ni magnetic nanoparticles as the core and onion-like C, amorphous CuO/Cu2O, amorphous Al/AlOx, amorphous SnO2, and N-doped onion-like C dielectric layers as the shell were designed, synthesized, and evaluated with reference to the outcome and know-how obtained in (1) [Objectives 1 and 2]. The observed magnetic enhancement and resonance effects in the core-shell nanoarchitectures were described and analyzed by our microwave absorption model in (2), while the observed dielectric enhancement and resonance effects were explained by the Debye dipolar polarization theory. Moreover, the electromagnetic impedance matching theory and the electromagnetic transmission line theory were adopted to design and optimize the core-shell nanoarchitecture-based microwave absorbers in terms of reflection loss, operating frequency, and absorber thickness. [Objective 3] (4) Following the success in (1), (2), and (3), four interesting types of core–shell–shell nanoarchitectures (i.e., the proposed CMSNAs) with Ni and ZnFe2O4 magnetic nanodisks and nanoplates as the core and onion-like C, SiO2, and/or PANI dielectric layers as the 1st and 2nd shells were designed, synthesized, evaluated, and analyzed [Objectives 1, 2, and 3]. The Debye-type multidielectric polarization in microwave complex permittivity was enabled by various core-shell-shell material phases of the CMSNAs, resulting in the bandwidth-broadening effect in the CMSNA-based microwave absorbers. This, together with the enhanced and broadened magnetic natural resonance in microwave complex permeability allowed by the magnetic nanoarchitectural core, effectively assured strong absorption over the broadened absorbing bandwidth and absorber thickness range via an improved electromagnetic impedance match. The study of the effect of shell permutation in the CMSNAs and their microwave absorbers revealed a transformation of magnetic energy into electric energy, and vice versa, between the core and the multishell. An electromagnetic energy transformation mechanism was proposed to provide a useful guide for developing magnetic-dielectric core-multishell nanoarchitectures for next generation microwave absorber applications. [Objective 3]

523612.label: Major findings and research outcome
523612.value: A total of “14” good SCI journal papers have been directly produced from this project. The major findings and research outcome in relation to the project objectives are summarized as follows. (1) A total of 14 interesting types of magnetic nanoarchitectures, which constituted the core of the proposed CMSNAs (Core-MultiShell NanoArchitectures), was designed and synthesized by chemical and/or physical methods to realize different magnetic materials in different nanoarchitectures and nanosizes [Objective 1]. The microstructural, electrical, magnetic, and microwave absorbing properties of the magnetic nanoarchitectures were characterized/evaluated to obtain a physical insight into their growth/formation mechanisms as well as their microwave absorbing performance and mechanisms in the most important L, S, C, X, and Ku bands of microwaves ranging from 1 to 18 GHz [Objectives 2 and 3]. [Journal Paper # 1 to 14] (2) A novel theoretical model for calculating the microwave complex permeability and absorption of magnetic nanoarchitectures and their microwave absorbers in general, and for validating our proposed shape anisotropy-enhanced microwave complex permeability and absorption in magnetic nanoarchitectures in specific, was proposed and developed based on the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation and the Bruggeman’s effective medium theory. This model was applied successfully to explain the magnetic enhancement and resonance effect in the measured microwave complex permeability and absorption of the magnetic nanoarchitectures and their microwave absorbers with and without magnetic field-induced rotational orientation of the magnetic nanoarchitectures in the microwave absorbers in (1). [Objective 3] [Journal Paper # 1, 12, and 14] (3) A total of five interesting types of core-shell nanoarchitectures, having various magnetic nanoarchitectures as the core and dielectric layers as the shell, were designed, synthesized, and evaluated to demonstrate the basic form of the proposed CMSNAs based on the outcome and know-how in (1) [Objectives 1 and 2]. The microwave absorption model developed in (2) was applied to describe and analyze the observed magnetic enhancement and resonance effects in the core-shell nanoarchitectures; the Debye dipolar polarization theory was used to explain the observed dielectric enhancement and resonance effects; and the electromagnetic impedance matching theory and the electromagnetic transmission line theory were utilized to design and optimize the core-shell nanoarchitecture-based microwave absorbers in terms of reflection loss, operating frequency, and absorber thickness [Objective 3]. [Journal Paper # 3, 4, 5, 8, and 13] (4) A total of four interesting types of core-shell-shell nanoarchitectures, which were essentially the proposed CMSNAs, were designed, synthesized, evaluated, and analyzed using various magnetic nanoarchitectures as the core and dielectric layers as the 1st and 2nd shells [Objectives 1, 2, and 3]. The various core-shell-shell material phases of the CMSNAs effectively enabled the Debye-type multidielectric polarization in microwave complex permittivity, leading to broadened bandwidth in the CMSNA-based microwave absorbers. The magnetic nanoarchitectural core effectively enhanced and broadened the magnetic natural resonance in microwave complex permeability. An improved electromagnetic impedance match was enabled, and strong absorption over the broadened absorbing bandwidth and absorber thickness range was permitted. The further investigation on the shell permutation of the CMSNAs and their microwave absorbers gave rise to a novel electromagnetic energy transformation mechanism for developing magnetic-dielectric core-multishell nanoarchitectures for advanced microwave absorbers. [Objective 3] [Journal Paper # 6, 9, 12, and 14]

523612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
523612.value: High-performance microwave absorbers operating in the L-Ku bands (1-18 GHz) of microwaves are urgently needed to mitigate the rapidly increasing problems/concerns of electromagnetic interference pollution in addition to improving the ability of electromagnetic stealth. Our proposed CMSNAs and their microwave absorbers, owing to their strong absorption over a broader absorbing bandwidth and a wider absorber thickness range at a lighter absorber weight, are capable of meeting the technological challenges and application demands for new generation microwave absorbers. Future work on an improved study of the effect of multishell permutation and the electromagnetic energy transformation is important because the distinct dielectric properties of the conducting, semiconducting, and insulating shells will bring about characteristically different interfacial and cooperative effects and hence microwave absorbing properties in the resulting CMSNAs. The interaction and transformation between magnetic and electric energies within various material phases and interfaces of the CMSNAs are of great interesting [Journal Paper # 9]. Moreover, tunable microwave absorbers could be realized intrinsically by doping impurities into CMSNAs [Journal Paper # 13] or decorating nanoparticles on the surface of the CMSNAs. They can also be achieved extrinsically by applying a controlled electric or magnetic field to the CMSNAs.

523612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
523612.value: A novel class of microwave absorbing materials, namely CMSNAs, has been proposed and realized, both experimentally and theoretically, for next generation microwave absorbers. The CMSNAs feature an architecturally designed magnetic nanoarchitectural core encapsulated by several layers of shell (called multishell) made of conducting, semiconducting, and/or insulating dielectrics. The core-multishell arrangement broadens the absorbing bandwidth and mitigates the variation in absorption with absorber thickness by the bandwidth-broadening effect in various core-multishell material phases. The nanoarchitectural core assures strong absorption over the broadened bandwidth by an improved electromagnetic impedance match of the shape-anisotropically increased magnetic relative permeability of the core to the dielectric relative permittivity of the core-multishell. Scientific and technological know-hows about the design, synthesis, evaluation, modeling, analysis, and optimization of the CMSNAs for microwave absorbers have been established and captured. The research output of this project, including the “14” SCI journal publications, the scientific and technological know-hows, the invented/developed CMSNAs and their microwave absorbers, etc., will serve as good references for the related communities involving nanomaterials, electromagnetics, safety, energy, environment, etc. and ranging from the commercial to military marketplaces. It will also strengthen our research profile and lead to further development.
