524212.label: Realisation of objectives
524212.value: As far as the projective objective 1 is concerned, a visual image processing (VIP) algorithm was developed for extracting vehicle signatures such as vehicle color, length and type from normal-resolution traffic surveillance cameras. Time-spatial image processing technique was also investigated to estimate the traffic flow condition and the level of service of road networks from normal-resolution video images. In relation to the project objective 2, the vehicle features (e.g. vehicle color, length and type) extracted by the VIP algorithm were fully examined and utilized for improving the vehicle re-identification (VRI) algorithm. A probabilistic fusion technique of vehicle features was proposed to provide a probabilistic measure (posterior probability) for vehicle re-identification decision. It was found that the performance of the VRI algorithm for color feature is clearly better than for the other two features. The re-identification accuracy after fusion of the three vehicle features outperforms the three features used individually. With respect to the projective objective 3, a vehicle re-identification (VRI) algorithm was enhanced with robust self-adaptive time windows in order to capture the traffic dynamics for real-time application. The VRI algorithm was also extended to consider the general case that multiple video cameras were installed in the road network. A hierarchical Bayesian matching model was proposed to consider vehicle re-identification over multiple detectors as an integrated process for improving the overall matching accuracy. In connection to the project objective 4, a dynamic journey time estimation was developed using the results obtained by the proposed VRI algorithms. The proposed model was formulated as a bi-level optimization problem. The upper level is to minimize the difference of mean and standard deviation between the estimated and observed path journey times. The observed path journey times can be obtained by the developed VRI algorithm. In the lower-level problem, the reliability-based dynamic traffic assignment model was employed to account for travelers’ path choice behaviors under supply uncertainty. In addition, the developed VRI algorithm has been extended for automatic incident detection. The proposed incident-detection-oriented VRI has made use of a flexible time window to further improve the matching accuracy so as to reduce the incident detection time. A screening method, which based on the ratios of the matching probabilities, was adopted to screen out the mismatched vehicles for reducing the false alarm rate. Regarding the project objective 5, the performance and accuracy of the proposed probabilistic re-identification method was evaluated using the video record data of the expressway system in Bangkok, Thailand. Several simulation tests were also carried out to evaluate the performance of the proposed VRI algorithms for travel time estimation under different traffic conditions, e.g. recurrent traffic congestion, freeway bottlenecks and traffic incidents. In addition, the proposed VRI-based incident detection algorithm has been validated with both simulated data and real-world cases in Bangkok. Remark: Prof. SUMALEE Agachai (Professor, Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University) was the Ex-Principal Investigator (PI) of this RGC project. He left the University in February 2015 before end of the project. Change of the PI was approved by the RGC on 20 May 2015. The Ex-PI has however continuously contributed to the remaining works of this project and has rejoined the University in April 2016.

524212.label: Major findings and research outcome
524212.value: As far as the project objective 1 is concerned, a visual image processing (VIP) algorithm was developed for extracting vehicle features or signatures such as vehicle color, length and type from normal-resolution traffic surveillance cameras together with the vehicle lane’s position (see publication nos. (1) and (2)) for vehicle re-identification (VRI) purposes. An alternative approach based on time-spatial image processing technique was also studied for estimation of the level of service of the road network from video records (see publication no. (5)). With regard to the project objective 2, a probabilistic fusion technique was proposed to integrate the vehicle signatures derived from the VIP algorithm (see publication nos. (1) and (2)). Bayesian rule was employed to generate a posterior probability from each individual vehicle feature distance matrix. A data fusion rule was proposed to combine the three posterior probabilities of the three vehicle features for VRI. In respect to the project objective 3, the developed VRI algorithm was further enhanced and extended to the network-wide case. A dynamic self-adaptive time window component was introduced to improve the adaptability of the algorithm against potential significant changes in traffic conditions (see publication no. (1)). In relation to the project objective 4, a dynamic journey time estimation model was proposed to simultaneously estimate the mean and the standard deviation of path journey time in stochastic road networks (see publication no. (3)). In addition to journey time estimation, the developed VRI algorithm has been extended for automatic incident detection (AID) purpose (see publication no. (2)). The results obtained from the developed VRI algorithms can be used for investigating the car following behavior to improve road traffic safety (see publication no. (4)) and also for better understanding of traffic flow dynamics, especially under adverse weather conditions (see publication no. (6)). In connection to the project objective 5, the performance of the proposed algorithms for vehicle re-identification and travel time estimation has been validated based on the simulated data and the video records collected at an expressway system in Bangkok, Thailand (see publication no. (1)). The simulation results show that the proposed VRI algorithm with self-adaptive time window provides reliable estimates of the mean travel time with less than 5% mean absolute errors under different scenarios. The proposed VRI-based AID algorithm has also been validated with simulated and empirical data. Both the results show that the proposed AID algorithm outperforms the traditional vehicle count approach in terms of detection time (see publication no. (2)).

524212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
524212.value: In this project, visual image processing algorithms were proposed for extracting the vehicle features from video records for vehicle re-identification. With the framework of vehicle re-identification, mathematical and statistical algorithms were formulated and developed for travel time/journey time estimation and incident detection problems. However, it is undeniable that the performance of image processing is subject to the effects of inclement weather (e.g., rain and snow) and illumination changes. Under these circumstances, the quality of the video image will dramatically decrease and hence compromise the effectiveness of vehicle feature extraction. The size of vehicle platoon would also affect the performance of vehicle re-identification. Thus, further study is required to enhance the image processing and vehicle re-identification algorithms so as to cater for different weather and environmental conditions. The proposed algorithms for travel time estimation could be further enhanced, in particular to cater for non-recurrent traffic congestion (e.g. severe traffic accident with longer incident duration). As the complexity of the vehicle matching problem would increase dramatically when it comes to the network-wide case with multiple video cameras, the computational time would be impractical for application in large-scale road networks. Thus, the efficiency of the proposed algorithms should be further improved for practical applications to real networks.

524212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
524212.value: In this project, mathematical models and solution algorithms have been developed for two purposes: (i) vehicle re-identification (VRI) based on video image data and (ii) estimation of road network traffic condition (in terms of travel time) by using the VRI results. Video cameras are widely used for traffic surveillance in transportation networks. In order to make use of the available normal-resolution video images for estimation of traffic conditions, VRI is required. In general, VRI is a process of matching vehicle features/signatures from one detector to the next one in the road network. For the first purpose, to re-identify the vehicles from video records, visual image processing algorithm has been developed to extract the vehicle features such as color, size and type. These vehicle features are fused in a probabilistic framework for matching the vehicles. For the second purpose, travel times on selected road networks have been estimated based on the results of VRI. Case studies and simulation tests have been carried out to evaluate the proposed algorithms for VRI and travel time estimation. The results show that the proposed VRI algorithms for travel time estimation perform well under different traffic conditions (e.g. free-flow, recurrent traffic congestion, freeway bottlenecks and minor traffic accidents).

524612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
524612.value: 分析多個利益相關方的利益及維護其利益的適當平衡,是項目能否成功交付的關鍵。分析利益相關方的傳統方法是通過其屬性的主觀評價對利益相關方進行識別和分類。然而,這種方法的準確性在很大程度上取決於項目經理的經驗,也因此受制于他們認知的局限性。現今, 在高度複雜的大型建築項目中, 這種局限性更為嚴重。克服這個問題的一個辦法是使用社會網路分析(SNA)。SNA具有很強的數學和圖形分析功能,已成功在建築行業用於探討不同的合同關係和實踐社區組織問題。這項研究的目的是調查是否可以通過使用SNA來提供更多的項目利益相關方的交互和關係的資訊, 從而提高大型建設項目中利益相關方分析的有效性。具體研究目標包括:(1)研發用來識別、可視化和分析大型建設項目中利益相關方關係的社會網路模型;(2)評估和驗證用於利益相關方分析的社會網路模型的效用及相對傳統方法的優勢;(3)制定在大型建設項目中應用上述模型的方法和程式,來協助、促進和支援利益相關方之間的協同工作。

524612.label: Realisation of objectives
524612.value: The research objectives have been fulfilled mainly through the completion of the following tasks: 1. Develop and refine a social network approach for analysing stakeholders and their interactions in mega construction projects (MCPs), and validate the proposed approach by using real-life MCPs A social network approach for analysing stakeholders and their relationships in MCPs was proposed, the detailed analytical variables and procedures of the approach were demonstrated. The approach and its demonstration were based on the findings of literature review, network analysis, and two case studies in Hong Kong. To cope with the high stakeholder complexities in MCPs, it is essential to assess stakeholder interactions and their impacts on project development through these connectivity structures. A social network approach for analysing stakeholders and their relationships in MCPs was thus developed, with an emphasis on their information exchange interactions. This approach involves the use of four data collection and analysis methods (chain referral sampling, SNA, interview and survey), a software package for network visualisation and exploration, three relationship attributes for relationship assessment (frequency, timeliness, and information quality), and the calculation of two network-level and six node-level metrics. The procedure comprises five major steps: (1) identifying stakeholders (i.e. nodes) and general issues, (2) determining stakeholder relationships (i.e. links), (3) visualising stakeholder network, (4) analysing stakeholder network, and (5) prioritising stakeholders and general issues. Findings show that the proposed approach can identify three critical stakeholder roles in an MCP: central connector, information broker and peripheral actor. The general issues in an MCP can also be prioritised based on stakeholders’ perception on an issue’s importance in the project, and the actual influences of corresponding stakeholders in the real relationship situation. 2. Develop and refine a social network approach for analysing stakeholder-related issues and their interdependencies in MCPs, and validate the proposed approach by using real-life MCPs A network approach for analysing stakeholder-related issues and their interdependencies in MCPs was proposed; the application, analytical variables and procedures of the approach were illustrated. The findings from literature review, SNA, and two case studies in Hong Kong contributed to the development and demonstration of the proposed approach. An effective stakeholder issue analysis in MCPs requires the recognising of the origins of stakeholder issues, as well as the modelling of issue interdependencies and their proliferating impacts on project development. A network-theory based approach for analysing stakeholder-related issues and issue interdependencies in MCPs was developed. This approach involves the application of four data collection and analysis methods, a software package for network visualisation and investigation, and two interdependency attributes for interdependency assessment (the intensity of impact and the likeliness for impact to occur). It also involves the calculation of two network-level, five node-level, one link-level, and two interface-level metrics. The entire process comprises five major steps: (1) identifying stakeholders and stakeholder-related issues (i.e. nodes), (2) determining issue interdependencies (i.e. links), (3) visualising issue network, (4) analysing issue network, and (5) identifying critical issue and issue interdependencies. Findings indicate that this approach can identify the important stakeholders, stakeholder-related issues, issue relationships, and stakeholder-/issue-interfaces, which should be handled with higher priority and care by core project team; corresponding management measures can be formulated based on these results. The approach also included an immediate simulation to imitate theoretically and predict the likely effectiveness of the management measures, mainly based on re-calculation of the two network-level metrics. 3. Develop and validate a systematic and holistic model, and its application guideline, building upon the network perspective, for stakeholder analysis and management in MCPs A finalised social network model for stakeholder analysis in MCPs in Hong Kong, together with an application guideline for the practical use of the model were proposed. Findings from the literature review, two network-theory based approaches for analysing stakeholders and stakeholder-related issues, and four case studies in Hong Kong, contributed to the development of the proposed model and guideline. The main body of the model has seven blocks that are arranged in two parts. The stakeholder analysis part comprises four blocks: (1) setting context and stakeholder analysis planning, (2) social network analysis of stakeholders, (3) network analysis of stakeholder-related issues, and (4) developing and implementing stakeholder management measures. The continuous support part includes three blocks: (1) communication and consultation, (2) monitoring and review, and (3) documentation and reporting. The model is considered particularly useful in public MCPs, and for organisations who act as project proponent or project administrator in an MCP such as the client and management consultant. The guideline for facilitating the practical use of the model comprises three major parts: (1) detailed explanation of the procedures and elements of the proposed stakeholder analysis and management process, (2) practical guidance on implementing the model, and (3) management tools (e.g. documentation templates).

524612.label: Major findings and research outcome
524612.value: The applicability of the proposed approach was validated by two MCPs in Hong Kong. The effectiveness of the approach was confirmed by the core project teams in the two case studies, who reflected that it was a useful evaluation tool of stakeholder relationships, roles and influences; and the results provided a valuable basis for improving their project stakeholder engagement strategies. Experiences from the empirical studies revealed two limitations of the approach when assessing issue importance: (1) overlooking the origins of issues in the issue identification step, and (2) disregarding the issue interdependencies and their propagating effects when assessing the issue importance. These limitations confirmed the need for analysing stakeholder-related issues and their interdependencies in MCPs, and provided directions for the development of the stakeholder issue analysis approach. The issue analysis approach was also tested by two MCPs. The core project teams in the two case studies agreed on the effectiveness of the approach. They opined that the approach unlocked the cause-and-effect relationships between issues, as well as their direct and indirect effects on the project development; which laid the groundwork for formulating suitable issue treatment and stakeholder engagement strategies. Experiences from the empirical studies reflected that the proposed approach was considered particularly useful in public MCPs at the early project stages. This is because: (1) public MCPs often have considerable social interests and involve long engagement process with numerous stakeholders; and (2) an earlier project stage allows greater flexibility to more proactively manage the stakeholders and their issues. The applicability of the proposed model and guideline were validated by experts from the industry and academia using face-to-face discussions and questionnaire survey. The experts confirmed that the model and guideline were comprehensive, practical, objective, replicable and adaptable for application in different MCP types. An important conclusion is that the model and guideline can serve as a systematic and effective management tool to identify, analyse and address the stakeholders, issues, relationships (including both stakeholder interactions and issue interdependencies), and their impacts in MCPs; ultimately improving their project decision making and stakeholder management effectiveness.

524612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
524612.value: 1. Future research can be conducted to explore the impact of national cultural diversity on MCP stakeholder management. National culture refers to the common understandings accumulated from the norms of an entire society or national environment. These deeply rooted values can shape the way that stakeholders (of a nation) perceive about the project, pursue their interests, and interact with other stakeholders. In future, comparative studies can be conducted by applying the social network model in MCPs of eastern and western cultures. The effects of trans-national and trans-regional stakeholder involvement in MCPs may also be worth exploring, because a country can have different subcultures. 2. Longitudinal network studies are needed in future to empirically explore the dynamics of stakeholder relationships and issue interdependencies throughout the entire lifecycle of an MCP. 3. Future empirical studies, using the social network model, can be conducted in other MCP types and contexts to compare the findings and develop more comprehensive stakeholder management strategies. 4. Future research should develop a method to define and generalise the thresholds of network metrics; which can simultaneously take into account the internal and external influential factors, and integrate the network analysis results from previous case studies.

524612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
524612.value: This research revealed the significance of taking a network perspective to analyse and engage stakeholders, and developed a social network approach for investigating stakeholders and their interrelationships in MCPs. It provides an analytical tool to identify completely the project stakeholders and their concerns, visualise the social interactions of stakeholders, examine the characteristics of these connectivity structures, identify the influential stakeholders and important issues which worth high attention, as well as spot out opportunities for improving stakeholder communication. This research explored the methodological potential of using a network perspective to analyse and address stakeholder-related issues, and developed a network-theory based approach for examining stakeholder-related issues and issue interdependencies in MCPs. It provides an analytical tool to identify a complete boundary of project stakeholders and their associated issues, visualise the cause-and-effect relationships between issues, investigate the direct and indirect effects of these interdependencies on MCP development, and to identify the key issues and links that should be handled with special care and urgency. This research developed a social network model and an application guideline, which serve as a systematic and generic reference for MCP leaders to design and conduct a stakeholder management process which suits the characteristics and needs of their MPCs.

524912.label: Project Objectives
524912.value: Developing the Integrated Local Multiple Endmember Un-mixing method for accurate sub-pixel fraction estimation The integrated local multiple endmember un-mixing method aims to provide best endmember fraction estimation at the lowest computation cost. This aim will be realized by integrating high spatial resolution satellite images with low- or medium-resolution multi-spectral images. The computation load for selecting the endmember combination models during the un-mixing processing is reduced because of the adoption of a local approach. Compared with other multiple endmember spectral mixture analysis methods, the advantages of the proposed method are: (a) provision of an optimal endmember spectral combination which improves the fraction estimation results; and (b) reduction of the computation cost by more than 30% by narrowing down to a number of endmembers for a local region. Developing the Sub-pixel-based Multiple Endmember Surface Emissivity estimation method The sub-pixel-based multiple endmember surface emissivity estimation method aims to provide a higher precision surface emissivity estimation at sub-pixel level. Based on the results of ILMEU, multiple endmember fraction images can be obtained with highly accurate land use land cover (LULC) information which will be used to estimate surface emissivity. This method will improve the emissivity estimation accuracy by allowing for the spectral heterogeneities of the mixed pixels for the urban region low- or medium-resolution satellite images. Conducting a case study in Hong Kong The case study will test the performance of the proposed methods and model. An urban redevelopment site area will be chosen for the scenario analysis. The theories and technologies development during this study can be directly used for urban planning, environmental protection studies and regional planning.

524912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
524912.value: Many societal problems have emerged due to recent rapid urbanization. These include regional climate change, environmental pollution, and negative social effects. Such problems dramatically affect the comfort, security and health of daily lives. An example is the urban heat island (UHI) phenomenon, which is regarded as one particularly critical environmental issue, not only in that it affects living comfort but also because it impacts the procurement of sustainable urbanization and hence the continuation of the above social ills. Land surface temperature (LST), as a key variable influencing UHI, is a closely studied. Scientifically, both the estimation of LST and the accurate determination of impervious surface areas (ISA) have been identified as key research issues within the study of UHI. Currently, low- or medium-resolution satellite imagery is used to estimate LST and ISA; the accuracy of this process is limited by the fact that individual pixel elements in an image invariably represent a combination of spectral signatures within the ground area covered by the pixel. The result is problems arising from the mixing of pixels. Of concern is the fact that such pixel mixing significantly limits the estimation accuracy of both LST and impervious surface areas. This project, aims to develop enhanced solutions to pixel un-mixing, and has the following objectives: (a) to develop a new Integrated Local Multiple Endmember Un-mixing (ILMEU) method; (b) to develop a Sub-pixel-based Multiple Endmember Surface Emissivity Estimation (SMESEE) method; (c) to model the relationships between LST and surface parameters, social-economic parameters and other salient factors; and (d) to conduct a case study in Hong Kong to comprehensively assess the performance of the proposed methods. Regarding theoretical development, two methodologies will be introduced for developing the Integrated ILMEU concept: integrated and local. This approach will lead to more highly accurate un-mixing, which will be to sub-pixel level, in surface emissivity estimation. The outcomes of the research will include (a) the development of new theoretical models for pixel un-mixing, (b) implementation of developed algorithms within a prototype software system, and (c) a technical report on the case study, from which conclusions can be drawn concerning the applicability of the new methodology. These findings will be utilized by remote sensing practitioners and policy makers concerned with urban sustainability. The project will generate a number of publications in top-rate remote sensing journals, centered upon the newly proposed ILMEU and SMESEE methods and their applications. 近年来，由于城市化的快速发展，随之而来的许多社会问题开始涌现。诸如区域气候变换、环境污染和其他一些城市化所带来的负面影响，严重影响了人们日常生活的舒适感、安全感和健康程度。城市热岛效应便是一个典型的例子，并被认为是一个非常严重的环境问题。这不仅是因为城市热岛效应会影响居民生活的舒适感，更重要的是它会阻碍城市可持续发展的进程，进而又带来如上所述的其他社会问题。 地表温度是影响城市热岛效应的一个关键因素，相关的研究已经有很多。科学的来讲，地表温度的估计和精确的不透水面面积的计算，这两者都是城市热岛效应研究的关键因素。目前，研究人员主要利用中低分辨率的卫星影像计算地表温度与不透水面面积。但是，在中低分辨率卫星影像上，一个象元实际上可能包含了多种地物的光谱特征，受到这种混合象元的影响，目前的地表温度和不透水面积的计算还存在很大的问题，因此需要对混合象元的问题做更深入的研究。 本项目旨在研发一种改进的像元解混方法。具体研究目标包括：（a）提出一种新的集成式局部多端元解混方法（ILMEU）；（b）提出一种基于子像素的多端元地表发射率估计方法（SMESEE）；以及（c）在香港开展一次应用实证研究，对所提出的理论方法予以验证。理论上所提出的两种方法使用了两个新的概念：集成与局部。这种方法将导致用于地表发射率估计的更高精度的像元解混解决方案。 本研究的成果包括：（a）提出一种新的像元解混方法；（b）将所提出的算法在一个计算机原形系统里予以实现；及（c）一篇关于新方法应用的技术报告。这些理论成果将为遥感应用与决策者提供关于城市可持续发展研究的技术支持。本研究所提出的关于ILMEU和SMESEE理论方法与应用成果将发表于遥感领域的国际期刊上。

524912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
524912.value: The mixed pixel problem of satellite remote sensing refers to the ambiguity caused by multiple features falling inside the extent of a single image pixel. This research aims to provide more accurate and efficient methods for unmixing the mixed pixels in satellite images. The significant impact of this research lies in its theoretical advances, technological progress and applications value. Theoretically, two endmember unmixing methods have been developed: 1) UOC-based SPM; 2) ICK-based SPM. UOC-based SPM method has the following advantages: (i) avoids the expensive computation in determining the endmembers in multispectral images; (ii) improves the accuracy of sub-pixel estimation by using a novel class allocation approach. ICK-based SPM employs MSI to provide additional constraints, and thus it can obtain more accurate results compared with the existing pixel level approaches. In general, the proposed methods can considerably improve the accuracy and efficiency of satellite image pixel unmixing. Technologically, the developed software prototype can implement the proposed methods in this study. It can solve real applications such as (a) multiple endmember spectral extraction; (b) local multiple endmember spectral library construction; and (c) multiple endmember unmixing using a spectral library. Also, it can be built as an add-on function in current remote sensing software package. Importantly, it can serve engineers or researchers involved in urban surface emissivity and urban land surface temperature studies.

525512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
525512.value: Comprehensive planning for large-scale land development is widely believed to bring many benefits to cities. Policy leaders and urban planners like to promote it in urban regeneration and brownfield redevelopment projects so as to achieve larger site amalgamation, provide additional floor space, produce better facilities, enhance urban design and create an improved urban environment. These benefits are particularly useful to the heavily populated city of Hong Kong which faces a severe urban land constraint. Under the existing statutory planning policy of Hong Kong, comprehensive land development is implemented by means of a “Comprehensive Development Area” (“CDA”) zone, which requires the submission of a planning application, master layout plan and development schedule of the entire development project to the relevant public authority for approval prior to actual construction. However, while these regulatory measures aim to discourage piecemeal land development, they are also being criticized by the property industry for causing significant delay to the development process and leading to a sluggish supply of new floor space. These outcomes are considered inefficient and undesirable, especially when Hong Kong is currently experiencing a frenetically speculative property market. Another criticism is that, while the CDA can produce a new development project within the zone, its external benefits to the neighbourhood are arguably overstated. This suggestion is worrisome because the CDA zoning mechanism is increasingly used by the local planning authority in the implementation of urban renewal of Hong Kong (refer to the Figures prepared by the Principal Investigator). It is therefore timely and imperative to carry out a thorough and objective investigation of this research topic. Based on a methodological combination of historical review, quantitative modeling analyses and expert consultations, this research seeks to examine the key factors which account for the time involved in development within the CDA zones, and evaluates the economic and spatial impacts of CDA development projects on the local context. This study is intended to provide a systematic and rigorous evaluation of the performance of the CDA policy in Hong Kong, and shed light on how regulatory controls of comprehensive large-scale land development may cause planning blight, regulatory delay and negative externality in urban development. 大型土地的綜合規劃發展往往被認為會為城市帶來很多好處，城市政府和城市規劃師都喜歡以此促進城市重建，從而實現較大的地塊合併， 提供額外的樓面空間，產生更好的設施，加強城市設計和改善城市環境，這些優點對香港尤其有益。根據香港的規劃政策，土地綜合開發是通過「 綜合發展區 」 （CDA區）進行規劃管制和實施。然而，雖然這些規管措施可以阻止零碎的土地發展，它們也被批評對重建項目帶來重大延誤和導致呆滯的物業供應。另一項批評是雖然 CDA 可以在發展地塊內製造一個全新的發展，其外部的影響和對附近環境卻沒有太多的效益。通過結合歷史回顧、 定量模型分析和專家協商等方法，這項研究旨在審查香港綜合發展區對周邊的影響，和在那些管制環節上存在規管延緩。

525512.label: Realisation of objectives
525512.value: Objectives (1) and (2) are met in the following ways. The database of CDA projects in Hong Kong from 1990 to 2014 was assembled. Analyses were carried out to assess the length of periods in different stages of the CDA projects. The study confirms that planning approval did not appear to constitute a delay. Preliminary analysis, as reported in an MSc dissertation in August 2014 by a student supervised by the PI, show that the scale of the CDA development projects seemed to have an impact on the length of development process. Further analysis by PI, however, reverses this observation. The PI found that there is a huge diversity in the CDA projects and no particular factors are found to account for the different lengths of time required for development. At the time when the PI was prepared to report this finding, he discovered that the same findings and conclusions were reported in Lai, L.W.C., Ho, D.C.W., Chau, K.W., and Chua M. H. (2016). Repeated planning applications by developers under statutory zoning: a Hong Kong case study of delays and design improvements in private residential development. Land Use Policy, 57, 709-718. The PI also found that, as reported in two Town Planning Board Papers published in May 2015 (MPC Paper No. 4/15 and RNTPC Paper No. 8.15), that the Government had commenced an internal policy since 1999 to review the development progress of CDA sites designated for more than 3 years to determine whether the CDA zoning should be amended or rezoned accordingly. This reflects that the apparent issues of regulatory delays have been addressed by the intervening action of the government departments and perhaps explains the pattern behind the findings of the PI and other colleagues on this subject. Objectives (3) and (4) are met in the following ways. Three journal papers were completed to address these two objectives. Two papers, submitted to Urban Studies and Environment and Planning A respectively, seek to identify, quantify and evaluate the market impacts of CDA development on the surrounding housing properties. The paper to Urban Studies relates to the infill redevelopment and physical upgrading of old industrial buildings, under CDA zoning, into upmarket commercial-office uses within an emerging off-centre business hub called Taikoo Place. The paper to EPA compares the impacts of three master-planned comprehensive housing redevelopments, also under CDA zoning, to an existing neighbourhood in an old district of Tai Kok Tsui. The last paper, submitted to Journal of Housing Economics, explores the question about the optimal scale of comprehensive housing development, using a residential new town of Tseung Kwan O as the case study area. All these papers have adopted rigorous quantitative methods to identify and evaluate the findings. A conference presentation was also made to an international audience in 2015 on some preliminary observations. All these three papers have come up with the following interesting and non-trivial findings. First, comprehensive development or physical enhancement of existing infill development under CDA zoning generates a positive impact on the surrounding housing properties. This finding sets my study apart from nearly all the previous local studies that have not been able to identify a clear relationship. Second, the property value impacts on the adjacent residential neighbourhood are not uniform and can vary spatially, temporally and with the different characteristics of the CDA development particularly its spatial relationship with the neighbourhood. Therefore, it is inappropriate to identify a generalized impact across the territory because every case has to be looked into carefully. Furthermore, proximity of the CDA project to its neighbours cannot simply be measured by the Euclidian distance, which was a common approach in all the previous studies. Third, some general principles about the impact of CDA development on its neighbours are identified. The positive impact is likely to affect the immediately adjacent street blocks to the CDA development, and the impact is stronger if and when the design, layout, and facility provision of the CDA development have an explicitly clear connection with the neighbourhoods. In other words, close proximity and short distance of the neighbouring properties to the project do not necessarily receive the positive impacts. Further, the timing of detecting the impact is critical. Adjacent housing properties with redevelopment potential were found to increase in values after CDA project completion, but further property transactions began to pause, presumably due to the holding-out action. Apartments located in old buildings did not have property value increases right after CDA project completion, but the transactions of these units were found to become more active, presumably due to a better appeal of the environment to users. Fourth, using Tseung Kwan O as a case study, the study has demonstrated how to make use of property transaction records to identify an optimal scale of CDA development. The findings and the methodology have policy implications and can inform local regulatory practices on CDA sites. Finally, the study has identified some methodological and data quality issues that can possibly improve future studies on this subject. The study has encountered some difficulties. First, it is about data quality, which seems to have been overlooked by previous studies thus, perhaps, leading to their contrasting results with this study. The property transaction data pool from the EPRC, commonly used by local researchers, is found to have severe limitations insofar as the old housing property transactions are concerned. Instead of using the common approach to delete incomplete records, the team spent a lot of time in verifying and cross-checking each data point with those provided by a property agent. Cleaning of the dataset took up enormous efforts. Second, many site visits were carried out to evaluate the reasons behind peculiar outcomes from our preliminary model estimations. This deepening of our local knowledge of the study areas proves to be extremely valuable to detect possible methodological and data issues in previous studies and support our propositions. Finally, the manuscript review process takes a long time as we aim at publishing our work at the top international journals in our field. We are hopeful that our journal papers can get published eventually.

525512.label: Major findings and research outcome
525512.value: First, no delay has been detected in the planning approval process on CDA development. The length of time required for the development process of CDA sites appears to have little relationship with the project characteristics which can be easily identifiable in the public domain. In other words, the development process is likely to be influenced by some “private” information unique to the projects. Second, comprehensive development or physical enhancement of existing infill development under CDA zoning generates a positive impact on the surrounding housing properties. This finding is in contrast to nearly all the previous local studies that have not been able to identify a clear relationship. Third, the property value impacts on the adjacent residential neighbourhood are not uniform and can vary spatially, temporally and with the different characteristics of the CDA development particularly its spatial relationship with the neighbourhood. It may be inappropriate to identify a generalized impact across the territory because every case has to be looked into carefully. Furthermore, proximity of the CDA project to its neighbours cannot simply be measured by the Euclidian distance. Fourth, some general principles about the impact of CDA development on its neighbours are identified. The positive impact is likely to affect the immediately adjacent street blocks to the CDA development, and the impact is stronger if and when the design, layout, and facility provision of the CDA development have an explicitly clear connection with the neighbourhoods. In other words, close proximity and short distance of the neighbouring properties to the project do not necessarily receive the positive impacts. Further, the timing of detecting the impact is critical. Adjacent housing properties with redevelopment potential were found to increase in values after CDA project completion, but further property transactions began to pause, presumably due to the holding-out action. Apartments located in old buildings that did not have property value increased right after CDA project completion, but the transactions of these units were found to become more active, presumably due to a better appeal of the environment to users. Fifth, using Tseung Kwan O as a case study, the study has demonstrated how to make use of property transaction records to identify an optimal scale of CDA development. The findings and the methodology have policy implications and can inform local regulatory practices on CDA sites. Finally, the study has identified some methodological and data quality issues that can possibly improve future studies on this subject.

525512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
525512.value: The methodology and the data cleaning approach adopted in this study can be used to examine the externality of infill redevelopment projects on the surrounding neighbourhood in different case study areas. However, given the highly congested environment of Hong Kong, it is important to identify suitable spots and avoid spurious influence of irrelevant factors on the outcomes. The study has also identified the following policy implications. First, CDA project can generate positive impacts on the surrounding, provided that its physical design, layout and connections are sensitive and responsive to the neigbhourhood. Second, because the spatial effect is uneven, additional upgrading and improvement works could be considered for those neighbourhoods found to be lacking behind in receiving the benefits. Third, an optimal scale of master-planned residential development could be worked out by paying attention to the inter-relationship between number of apartments, plot ratio and average unit size. This can inform the designation and allocation of appropriate site areas for government land sale. Professional seminars can be organized to promulgate these policy implications to the practitioners.

525512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
525512.value: This study explores the external market effects of comprehensive land development, normally designated under the “Comprehensive Development Area” (“CDA”) zone, on its neigbhourhood. Using case studies in Quarry Bay and Tai Kok Tsui, the study confirms that such development has brought positive impacts on the housing values in the neighbourhood. However, the benefits to the surrounding residential properties are uneven across space and time. Comprehensive infill development that has spatial design, layout and physical connection which are responsive and sensitive to its adjacent residential buildings tend to exert a stronger enhancement to their property values. The timing of the increase in property values and the turnover of transactions of these apartments may also vary, depending on whether the whole residential buildings can be redeveloped. Using Tseung Kwan O as a case study, this research has found that there is an optimal scale of large-scale master-planned housing estate development, defined in terms of the number of apartment units, and is contingent on the target housing classes. Overall, the study finds no regulatory delay in the approval process for CDA development. The development process for such development is not found to vary systematically with the publicly known characteristics of the CDA projects.

525712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
525712.value: 本計劃 研究 先進國家的土地界線系統 是否已經完成了其設計的的管理功能。這研究通過測試各國的土地界線系統內 的功能包括 土地邊界的準確性，土地邊界的穩定性，服務成本，時間和 適用性。本評審系統應用 層級分析法 作為分析基礎。 AHP 是一個以結構技術用作分析複雜的決定。本計劃的研究員採用AHP中的絶對式貳級標準去表現最佳的土地界線系統。其中土地界線系統的層級與關係影響需要作出決定。每個測試的土地界線系統可以對比其他每個系統或對比一個標準化的系統。 土地界線系統是法律和行政設定的土地管理制度之一。它在土地行政的地權確立，土地交易，地界糾紛處理，土地規劃，控制，估值及稅收各項功用中提供宗地界線服務。是次研究計劃目標針對有法律及行政設施的先進國家。很多時即使在有法制有政府及專業服務的土地界線系統仍有未能追上社會發展需要之處。從土地行政推展的角度來看，有需要有一個科學的評審機制去測驗界線系統的比次。 世界每個國家的地籍管理系統，都有不同的構成因素與內容。本研究並不比較法律制度的內容。而比較其表現。它提供具體可以測試的方法，並選擇在三大國際土地界線系統－澳洲業權法系，德國業權法系及契約登記法系的地區國家內過行比較。預期研究結果是國際間的土地界線系統的比較標準及各個系統的比較評值。

526012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
526012.value: This proposal is concerned with protection from noise in residential units of a multi-storey building which can be achieved by attaching balconies or balcony-like structures to the building façade. Different commonly found balcony forms will be included in the study. Balconies are able to provide areas for human activities not possible in the standard indoor living space and thus they are welcomed by many people all over the world. They are regarded as green features by the local authority and also have a property value enhancement effect at least in Hong Kong. While a single balcony can obstruct the direct line-of-sight between the ground transportation lines and the building façade behind the balcony and thereby provide some acoustical protection, the multiple reflections inside and between the balconies of balcony columns on a multi-storey building façade mean that protection from noise is not obvious. These reflections can even result in sound amplification. Classical analysis approaches using path differences and barrier edge diffraction for insertion loss prediction are insufficient. The orientation of the building façade relative to the ground transportation lines adds to the complexity of the problem. It is proposed to carry out a full spectrum parametric study on the insertion loss due to façade balconies (that is, noise reduction due to inserted balconies) using scale model experiments (with and without ground reflections) supplemented by numerical simulations. A few full scale balcony laboratory measurements will be made to provide data for later validations of the scale models and simulations. Measurements of insertion loss and the sound fields inside the balcony cavity will be made. Since analytical solution is not likely for the typical current three-dimension configurations, it is proposed to stick to the empirical approach adopted in previous work by the principal investigator. The numerical simulations will help the analysis of the acoustic mode contributions which will be useful for explaining insertion loss frequency variation patterns. The large database obtained from the scale model tests will also enable predictions using the neural network approach. The effects of the acoustical properties of the receiving room on the insertion loss will also be studied. Apart from the sound fields and insertion loss, efforts will also be made to capture the acoustical coupling occurring between the balcony cavity and the receiving room. The results will find applications in architectural acoustics where coupled cavity effects are of practical and/or fundamental interests. 這項建議關注的是多層建築物外牆陽台或陽台狀結構的隔音效果。研究將包括常見不同形式的陽台。陽台能夠提供另類生活空間，也被視環保設施。同時在香港陽台也具有樓宇增值效果。雖然單一的陽台上可以直接阻礙聲音傳播，從而提供一定的隔音效果，多層建築物外牆之間的陽台內多次聲音反射，卻使陽台的隔音效果不明顯，甚至可能導致聲音放大。普通的分析方法，使用傳播路徑差和障礙邊繞射預測的陽台插入損耗是不可靠的。地面運輸線和建築物外牆的相對方向增加問題的複雜性。這項研究建議使用縮尺模型實驗，並輔以數值模擬，開展全頻譜參數研究。也將會作出插入損失和陽台內部空腔的聲場的測量。數值模擬結果將有助於分析聲場在隔音效果中的貢獻，這將是有益的解釋陽台插入損耗和其頻率變化規律。縮尺模型試驗獲得的大型數據庫，也可幫助神經網絡預測方法的使用。接收室的聲學特性對陽台隔音效果的影響和陽台和接收室之間的聲學耦合也將是研究的對象。研究結果對建築聲學和空腔耦合效應有實際應用和基礎學術貢獻。

526012.label: Realisation of objectives
526012.value: This investigation was carried out mainly by using scale model measurements as the measurement if insertion loss of a balcony in real site was basically impossible (the balcony could not be removed). A 2.4m high scale model consisted of a model building façade and a column of three vertical balconies was used to realize objectives #1 and #2. The vertical separation of two adjacent balconies and the balcony size were roughly a 3 times scale down version of common practical scenario at least for the cases in Hong Kong. Totally, 4 symmetrical and 6 asymmetric balcony forms, which can commonly be found in the residential areas in Hong Kong, were included in this study. The spatial distributions of the insertion losses on the building façade protected by each balcony were obtained by a regular 6-by-6 microphone array with the microphones mounted flushed with the model façade surface. A linear loudspeaker array made up of thirty 6-inch aperture loudspeakers was used to simulate an incoherent line source relevant to traffic noise study. The insertion losses at each measurement point (both the octave band ones and narrowband ones) where obtained by the difference in sound pressure levels with and without the balconies. The effect of source orientation relative to the model façade normal was checked by rotating the model with sound source fixed in place. For the cases of symmetrical balconies, source orientation was varied from 0 deg (source parallel to model façade) to 90 deg in 15 deg interval. The insertion loss spectra so obtained were used to analyse the overall performance and the effect of various wave interactions inside the balcony voids. Traffic noise spectrum weighted insertion losses were used as descriptors for the broadband insertion losses. Wave interactions were investigated using narrowband insertion loss spectra. Objectives #1 and #2 are fully achieved. The original plan was to investigate the effect of receiver room reverberation on the insertion loss of balconies. However, it was known that the balconies on high-rise buildings do not offer much acoustical protection. Also, the effect of reverberation can be normalized using simplified building acoustic approach and thus is somehow understood. During the course of this project, it was brought to the attention of the PI that balconies with sound absorption installation were more important. Therefore, the later efforts in this project were made on understanding the improvement of balconies insertion loss using sound absorption. Scale model was carried out again, but with a 1:4 scaled down model because of the physical size limitation of the PI’s chamber. A receiver room, which was the 1:4 scaled down model of the PI’s acoustic testing chamber, was attached to the model balconies. Insertion loss in this case was described as the reduction of average sound level inside the receiver room (obtained by 6 microphones spanning evenly the volume of the receiver room) when a balcony was used to replace a conventional window opening. Effect of source orientation was also studied. The sound absorptions of materials used were tested in the scale down model receiver room using standard method with 13 microphones. Two sizes of the balcony-receiver room interfacial opening were adopted and the resulted insertion losses were measured. This opening size affected the reverberation inside the receiver room. This objective #3 is fully achieved.

526012.label: Major findings and research outcome
526012.value: Four symmetrical balcony forms, namely Bottom, Side-Bottom, Front-Bottom and Closed were included. The Bottom balcony consisted of the balcony floor only and the Closed balcony had front and side parapets flanking the lower 40% of the balcony height. The Side-Bottom and Front-Bottom balconies have only side or front parapets, respectively. The results are presented in the journal paper and the conference paper listed in Part C. For the balconies without ceilings, the A-weighted traffic noise insertion losses (IL) are affected by their configurations and their orientations relative to the sound source. The Closed and the Bottom balconies provide the highest and the lowest insertion losses, respectively. The performances of the Front-Bottom and Side-Bottom balconies show opposite variation trends as their orientations shift. Balcony ceiling largely erases the insertion losses. Sound amplification can be found at larger azimuthal angles. Under the current balcony configuration, the ILs within the balconies are generally weaker as elevation angle decreases. In the presence of ceiling reflection, resonances can occur perpendicularly between the ceiling and the floor. The results also show that the interferences between sound reaching the façade directly from the sound source, sound reflected from the ground, and sound reflected from the ceiling all play important roles in shaping the IL frequency variations. The couplings between these mechanisms, the acoustic modes and the edge diffractions are also important. The asymmetric balconies are basically those of the symmetrical balconies with one vertical side parapet removed or extended to the ceiling. The IL variation trends of the asymmetric balconies are similar, except that there will be unfavourable source orientation where the acoustical protection is not satisfactory due to direct sound transmission and multiple reflections. However, in the more favourable orientation, the IL can be high even in the presence of balcony ceiling. The IL is enhanced in the presence of sound absorption materials inside the balcony void. The presence of ceiling absorption improves insertion loss. However, when the balcony-receiver room interface is fully opened, the source orientation has small effect on the insertion loss. Peak ILs are found at 45 deg source orientation (due to balcony aspect ratio). For balcony-receiver room interfacial opening on one side of the balcony, the peak IL occurs when the source is nearly parallel to the model façade. A variation of about 3 dBA of traffic noise weighted IL is found for source orientation ranges from -90 deg to 90 deg.

526012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
526012.value: The coupling between the balcony and the receiver room is not exactly known. It was the fourth objective of the original proposal, which was taken out because of budget constraint. However, it is essential for the prediction of sound transmission across a balcony into the receiver room from the outdoor. Further investigation is needed as both finite-element simulation and ray-tracing are not believed to be able to provide reliable answers. It will then lead to the achievement of the third objective of the original proposal.

526012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
526012.value: The acoustical protections, in term of insertion loss, of balconies attached to the façades of high-rise buildings are investigated in this study via scale model experiments. Four symmetrical and 8 asymmetric balcony forms, which are commonly found in residential areas, are tested. For symmetrical balconies, the variation of the insertion loss is not significant when the azimuthal angle is less than 45 deg in the test cases, but sound amplification can be found at larger azimuthal angles. It is expected that this critical angle should be equal to arctan(0.5xbalcony width/balcony depth). Insertion loss decreases as elevation angle decreases. The insertion losses are highly dependent on frequency. Without balcony ceiling reflection, the interferences between edge diffractions, diffracted waves and façade reflections appear to be the determining mechanisms for sound amplification and attenuation. The acoustic modes within balconies with a front parapet also affect the insertion losses. In the presence of balcony ceiling, the vertical standing waves complicate the whole situation. The performances of asymmetric balconies are very similar, except that there are non-favourable source orientations where the balconies offer much less acoustical protection. It is also found that a less reverberant balcony results in higher insertion loss.

526212.label: Project Objectives

To develop a design method applicable to both short and slender FRP-confined CRCs subjected to eccentric loading

526212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
526212.value: A popular strengthening method for reinforced concrete (RC) columns is to wrap them with fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) jackets which provide lateral confinement to concrete for enhanced compressive strength and strain capacity. Existing research has shown that such FRP jacketing is highly effective for circular columns but much less effective for rectangular columns (including square columns as a special case) due to the existence of flat sides and sharp corners in the latter. Rounding the corners can enhance the effectiveness of confinement, but its benefit is limited, particularly for large columns, as the rounded corner radius is limited by the presence of steel reinforcement. A much more effective method for strengthening rectangular RC columns is to implement shape modification before FRP confinement. Modifying a rectangular section to an elliptical/oval section has been examined to some extent by existing research, but this process leads to substantial shape changes which are undesirable in practice for a number of reasons. This project is concerned with the further development of an alternative strengthening technique in which the flat sides of a rectangular section are modified into slightly curved sides before FRP confinement (referred to as section curvilinearizeation or SC). The resulting columns, referred to as curvilinear rectangular columns (CRCs), are much more effectively confined by an FRP jacket than rectangular columns with only corner rounding while the column size increase is limited. For the SC method to be used with confidence in practice, a reliable design theory is urgently needed. Existing research in this area has been very limited and the idea has been studied only by a few researchers. This project is thus proposed to correct the current knowledge deficiencies and to develop a safe and economical design procedure for the SC method. In particular, the proposed project, through a combined experimental and theoretical study, aims to develop: (a) a stress-strain model for the confined concrete in CRCs; (b) a design method for FRP-confined CRCs under eccentric compression; and (c) a theoretical model for the cyclic behavior of FRP-confined CRCs for use in seismic retrofit design. The proposed project will significantly advance the theory of FRP-strengthened RC structures and enable the wider, safer and more economical use of the FRP jacketing technique for rectangular RC columns. The project will also meet a very important socio-economic need in Hong Kong, the rest of China and beyond.

526212.label: Realisation of objectives
526212.value: In this report, the term “rectangular sections” refers to only rectangular sections with unequal section width and depth (i.e., excluding square sections), unless otherwise specified. OVERALL ACHIEVEMENT: We have fully addressed Objectives 1 and 2. REALIZATION OF OBJECTIVE 1: (1) Sixteen (16) small-scale (150 mm × 150 mm) FRP-confined square concrete columns with or without section curvilinearization (SC) were tested under axial compression to examine the axial stress-strain behaviour of concrete in small-scale FRP-confined curvilinearized square columns (CSCs). (2) Fourteen (14) large-scale (300 mm × 300 mm) FRP-confined square concrete columns with or without SC were tested under axial compression. The results of these tests were compared with those of small-scale tests to examine the possible size effect in FRP-confined CSCs. (3) Six (6) large-scale (450 mm × 300 mm) FRP-confined curvilinearized rectangular columns (CRCs) were tested under (concentric) axial compression. The test parameters included the rise-to-span ratio and the corner radius ratio (i.e., corner radius to section depth ratio). (4) Eight (8) large-scale (450 mm × 300 mm) FRP-confined CRCs were tested under eccentric compression. The test parameters included the load eccentricity and the column slenderness ratio. (5) Thirty-two (32) FRP-confined elliptical (including circular as a special case) concrete columns (major axis length = 200 mm) were tested under axial compression. Four sectional aspect ratios (ratios between the major axis length and the minor axis length) of 1, 1.3, 1.7, and 2 were investigated. (6) Finite element (FE) modelling of FRP-confined CRCs/CSCs under axial compression was undertaken. The FE results were found to be in close agreement with test results of both CRCs and CSCs. (7) FE modelling of FRP-confined elliptical concrete columns was undertaken. The FE results were found to be in close agreement with test results and much more accurate than other theoretical models. (8) An advanced stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in square columns was developed based on a new and in-depth understanding of the confinement mechanism in the column section provided by results from a reliable FE model. (9) A new design-oriented stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in CRCs/CSCs was developed based on the axial compression tests of FRP-confined CRCs/CSCs. The proposed model was found to perform much better in predicting responses of the test FRP-confined CRCs/CSCs than existing stress-strain models. (10) A new design-oriented stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in elliptical columns was formulated based on the test data and the numerical results from an FE parametric study obtained using the FE approach. The proposed model was found to offer close predictions of the ultimate condition and the stress-strain curves of FRP-confined concrete in elliptical columns. (11) Theoretical analysis based on Jiang and Teng’s (2012a) model for FRP-confined slender concrete columns was carried out to simulate responses of the test FRP-confined CRCs/CSCs under eccentric loading. The analysis was found to provide reasonably accurate predictions for the test columns in terms of the axial load-lateral displacement curve and the moment-curvature curve. REALIZATION OF OBJECTIVE 2: (1) A unified stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in columns of various sectional shapes (i.e., circular, rectangular/square, elliptical, and curvilinearized rectangular/square sections) has been developed based on the test data in this project as well as those from other researchers. This unified stress-strain model has been adopted by the revised version of the Chinese Technical Code for Infrastructure Application of FRP Composites (GB 50608 2010) (referred to as the Chinese Code hereafter). (2) The design method of Jiang and Teng (2012b) with the incorporation of the proposed stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in CRCs/CSCs was found to provide close predictions for the load-carrying capacities of the test CRCs/CSCs. (3) By using an equivalent method, the design equations in the Chinese Code for FRP-confined rectangular/square columns were found to provide conservative yet still close predictions for the test FRP-confined CRCs/CSCs under eccentric loading. In the equivalent method, the equivalent rectangular/square section and the curvilinearized rectangular/square section are assumed to have the same sectional area and sectional aspect ratio. (4) The slenderness limit for short FRP-confined reinforced concrete (RC) columns in the Chinese Code, which was originally proposed by Jiang and Teng (2013) for FRP-confined circular RC columns, was found to be still applicable to the test FRP-confined CRCs/CSCs in this project. (2012b). “Slenderness limit for short FRP-confined circular RC columns”, Journal of Composites for Construction, ASCE, Vol. 16, No. 6, pp. 650-661. Jiang, T. and Teng, J.G. (2013). “Behaviour and design of slender FRP-confined circular RC columns”, Journal of Composites for Construction, ASCE, Vol. 17, No. 4, pp. 443-453.

526212.label: Major findings and research outcome
526212.value: FINDINGS RELATED TO OBJECTIVE 1: (1) The SC method was found to be highly effective in enhancing the load-carrying capacity of rectangular/square concrete columns; the rise-to-span (r/s) ratio of the curved edges was found to be the controlling parameter of the behaviour of FRP-confined CRCs/CSCs; (2) The effect of r/s ratio is most directly reflected by the second-segment slope of the resulting stress-strain curve of FRP-confined concrete in CRCs/CSCs. The test results on FRP-confined CSCs showed an r/s ratio of around 1/15 may be recommended as the optimum value for the SC method to minimise the increase in the sectional area; (3) The test results showed that curvlinearization of a rectangular/square section leads to a more uniform distribution of FRP hoop strains around the circumference of the section; (4) It was found that curvlinearization of a square section significantly reduces the size effect in FRP-confined square concrete columns: a significant size effect was observed in square concrete columns without SC, but the size effect is not obvious for CSCs; (5) The test results of FRP-confined CRCs under axial compression showed that the corner radius ratio has a significant effect on both the ultimate axial stress and ultimate axial strain of FRP-confined concrete. A corner radius of around 45 mm was identified to be close to the optimum value for a satisfactory enhancement effect for the test CRCs (450 mm × 300 mm). (6) Existing stress-strain models for FRP-confined concrete in CRCs/CSCs fail to predict the stress-strain curves of the test CRCs/CSCs. FINDINGS RELATED TO OBJECTIVE 2: (1) The proposed unified design-oriented stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in columns of various sectional shapes (i.e., circular, rectangular/square, elliptical, and curvilinearized rectangular/square sections) was shown to provide more accurate predictions for the test columns than the existing stress-strain models; (2) The design equations of the Chinese Code (GB 50608 2010) with the incorporation of the proposed stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in CRCs/CSCs were found to provide close predictions for the load-carrying capacities of the test CRCs/CSCs; (3) Much of the outcome of this project serves as the basis for the revision of the Chinese Code (GB 50608 2010), including the unified design-oriented stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete and the optimum value of the r/s ratio of 1/15 for the SC method. Most of the completed work has not been published, but several papers on the completed work will be submitted for publication in journals over the next couple of years.

526212.value: The practical application of the SC method using a novel flexible formwork (with some improvements over the original design detailed in the project proposal) for a rapid and cost-effective shape modification process is being explored in the laboratory.

526212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
526212.value: Existing studies have shown that fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) jacketing/wrapping is highly effective in strengthening circular concrete columns but is much less effective for rectangular concrete columns due to their flat sides and sharp corners. Rounding the corners can enhance the effectiveness of FRP confinement, but its benefit is limited, particularly for large columns. A much more effective method for strengthening rectangular concrete columns is to implement shape modification before FRP confinement. Such shape modifications include the conversion of a rectangular section to an elliptical/oval section or a curvilinear section, with the latter often being advantageous as the resulting increase in section size is more limited. Against this background, this project has been undertaken to understand and model the behaviour of such shaped-modified concrete columns with FRP confinement, with a curvilinearization of square and rectangular sections being the main focus. The research has led to the development of a design procedure to support the practical implementation of FRP strengthening of square/rectangular columns following shape modification.

526712.label: Project Title(Chinese)
526712.value: 電網連接電力電子變換器的分岔分析

526712.label: Project Objectives
526712.value: The first objective is to pursue a systematic formulation of practical models for power converters that are connected to the power grid under practically relevant conditions and parameters. This task will have to take into account the practical conditions at the load and input sides of the converters. The challenge is to provide an appropriate model for the load side or input side which is connected to the grid, which in turn is connected to a variety of possible loads and sources. The next objective is to perform analysis and to compile detailed design information that identifies different operating regimes/behaviors in terms of the choice of control methods and practical parameter ranges. To keep the work tractable, we consider a relatively small number of connected converters as the system under study. Thus, our analysis can be focused on the system under study which is connected to the grid with other interacting systems as equivalent loads and/or sources connected to the grid through appropriate impedances. The challenge here is to produce extensive simulation and experimental data that cover all possible parameter ranges as well as complex load and source connections. The presentation of the results deserve special attention. Indeed, a key feature of this project is the design-oriented analysis, as explained in the above two objectives. The results would not be useful if they cannot be readily used to generate information for practical design. We therefore should complete the process by presenting all results in design-oriented forms. This is an important objective of the project and the choice of the way results are presented must be carefully planned and considered during the analysis process. In particular, the bifurcation results which contain important design information must be presented in terms of practical parameter spaces such that the various operating regimes under practical parameter choices can be revealed to facilitate the decision on the design choice. Clearly, this objective is tightly coupled with the above two objectives concerning modeling methods and analysis approaches.

526712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
526712.value: The current status of research in the identification of bifurcation behavior in power electronics has reached a stage where the salient types of bifurcation behavior, their underlying causes and the theoretical parameters affecting them have been well understood. Currently, the emphasis of research in this field has gradually shifted toward applications that are of direct relevance to practical design of power electronics. One important direction is to apply some of the available research methods in bifurcation analysis to practical power electronics circuits that interact with one another via the power grid. The main difficulty is that the abstract mathematical presentations of the available results are not directly applicable to such practical design problems. In this work we propose to address how research efforts may be directed to bridge this gap. In particular we will study the power converters with either the load side or the input side connected to other possible nonlinear sources or loads. Such situation is important in practice because more power converters are now designed to interface with the power grid which is connected to a variety of possible loads and generating sources through yet another layer of converters. Thus, we can perceive that the system consists of many power converters, each being designed to serve its own source and load, and all interacting each other via the grid. Our approach to analyze this system is to first focus on individual converters, and connect them to other loads or sources via appropriate impedance models representing the grid interface. We will systematically derive appropriate models for power converters that would facilitate the identification of bifurcation scenarios (i.e., loss of stability or change of operating regimes). Analysis will be conducted, aiming to produce design-oriented results. Findings will be classified under different types of converters, as well as different types of load-side or source-side impedances that interact with the converters under study via the power grid. Initial study has been conducted for three-phase voltage source converters under a typical closed-loop control and being fed from non-ideal power grids, and a catastrophic bifurcation phenomenon that is characterized by sudden increase of reactive power and input current has been identified and verified experimentally. The PI has done some prior work in the design-oriented bifurcation of power converters, and this project will build on the success of the previous work to extend the coverage to the complex class of interacting grid-connected converter systems. 此項目針對電力電子變換器在連接電網的實際條件下產生的各種運作模式，包括在負載互動的情況下的出現的各種分岔和其他不穩定狀態。主要研究手段包含建模、實驗、系統分析及仿真，目的是提供一個全面的面向應用和設計的分岔分析方案，提供在不同實際參數空間中的工作模式，有助解決未來電網與普及再生能源接合時所遇到的各種理論及技術挑戰。

526712.label: Realisation of objectives
526712.value: The research team is excited to report that a paper generated directly from this project has been awarded the ANNUAL BEST PAPER (SECOND PLACE) PRIZE for 2015 by the IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON POWER ELECTRONICS which is the top-notch journal in this field: C. Wan, M. Huang, C. K. Tse and X. Ruan, "Effects of interaction of power converters coupled via power grid: a design-oriented study," IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, vol. 30, no. 7, pp. 3589-3600, July 2015. The award was collected in September 2016 at the IEEE ECCE held in Milwaukee USA. The project had proceeded in accordance with the set objectives and research plans. The first objective has been completed and a general modelling approach has been developed, leading to a very convenient analytical platform on which to generate both circuit level and system level models that can be practically used for stability assessment and design. We expect that this work will have a long-term impact as it provides a practical means of transforming a complex system configuration to a system description that can be tracked relatively readily, allowing dynamic performance to be assessed and analyzed for design purposes. The second objective has also been achieved, with the key types of grid-connected converters fully investigated. Voltage-fed converters are typically used as interface connecting the grid to the load, and the most typical control implementation has been selected as the core subject of study, maximizing the applicability of the methods developed. The key novelty is the correct identification of the stability problem under the interaction of multiple converter systems by coupling through the common connection points of a power grid. This result has made significant contribution, and was recognized highly by the research community as evidenced by the award of the IEEE Transactions Best Paper (Second Place) Prize in 2015. We expect that this work will have a long-term impact because mutual interactions of coupled converter systems are known to have significant effects on the safe operation of grid-connected converter systems which are currently the main development trend in power distribution systems. Simulation and experimental data have been collected based on the works achieved in the above two objectives, and a methodology has been derived to organize these data in a design-oriented form in order to proceed to the third objective that leads to design rules and stability assessment guidelines. The main problem is the complexity with the interaction of converters via the grid, and we have derived effective analytical methods to tackle this important problem and make them available for practical design. In our approach, we identify the complete set of practical parameters that would affect the dynamic performance, and develop automatic procedures for generating all relevant design charts that give boundaries of various operating modes. Thus, the conditions for operation in each mode can be clearly obtained in terms of the ranges of selected parameters. The results are therefore directly applicable for design purposes. Again, our work has made available a novel practical procedure for identifying the various parametric regions in which specific operating regimes can be found to exist. In summary, the extent of our work in fulfilment of the set objectives can be considered to be 100%, with results expected to draw wide attention of the research community and the power distribution industry.
