526712.label: Major findings and research outcome
526712.value: The key findings arising from the project correspond to the key objectives set out in the proposal. The modeling method developed provides a platform on which complex system configuration can be described effectively for performance assessment, analysis and design. A demonstration of the versatility of the model can be readily seen from the publication "Low-frequency Hopf bifurcation and its effects on stability margin in three-phase PFC power supplies connected to non-ideal power grid," IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part I: Regular Papers, vol. 60, no. 12, pp. 3328-3340, December 2013. This paper demonstrates how a specific complex circuit configuration can be readily identified with the cause of the instability and the exact mode of unstable operation. A more general application covering a very common grid-connected multiple converter system is demonstrated in our key paper arising out of this project "Effects of interaction of power converters coupled via power grid: a design-oriented study," IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, vol. 30, no. 7, pp. 3589-3600, July 2015. The significant impact of this work lies in the provision of a general approach that can be conveniently used to identify rather complex and subtle behavior of the system that contains a system of interacting converters, with each individual converter designed to be stable, but yet the entire system can operate in a number of regimes include instability and oscillations. This results have been considered significant by the research community, and the paper was voted as the Best Paper (Second Place) by the editorial board of IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics in 2015. This result is expected to influence the way in which grid-connected converters should be designed. Applications are also expected to cover a range of practical scenarios related to multiple converter interactions, and particularly in microgrids and power distribution systems. Maintaining individual converter stability is therefore vital and methods that can be applied to maintain fast transient locally are thus important as they complement the problems associated with instability as a result of interaction via the grid. An attempt was made to address this design issue and was recorded in "Augmented buck converter design using resonant circuits for fast transient recovery," IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics, vol. 31, no. 8, pp. 5666-5679, August 2016. Thus, the key objectives of the project are well met and the findings are reported in the most prestigious journals of our field.

526712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
526712.value: The result from this project is directly related to the design of efficient power distribution system, which is currently undergoing infrastructural transformation due to the pressing need for incorporating renewable sources and the use of microgrids as well as the increased demand of DC loads. This trend is expected to continue in the coming decade, and the need for stable and high-performance grid-connected converters will be an important drive for future research in power electronics. Converters interaction is therefore a topic of high practicality and importance. Our result from this project has opened up a new venue for studying the various problems associated with multiple converters interacting through a distribution grid infrastructure. We plan to extend this line of research to cover a network of converters, and in particular employ the latest network science concepts to establish new methodologies for assessing power network robustness, reliability, and safe operation. Specifically we have proposed further work along a new bold direction focusing on large-scale networked power systems of the future. Knowing the limitations of conventional methods, we will explore innovative approaches for analysis and design, including new thinkings from network science and complexity theory.

526712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
526712.value: The problem addressed in this project is directly related to the design of efficient power distribution systems and specifically relevant to the current trend of development incorporating renewable sources and the use of microgrids. The increased demand of DC loads is also escalating the transformation of current distribution from AC to DC as well as the use of shared distribution systems. The performance of the system is greatly influenced by the mutual interaction of individual subsystems, and this is exactly the problem we have addressed in the project. A key finding from this project is precisely on the identification of the conditions under which interacting converter systems may pose stability threats to the system and hence create challenges in the design of such systems. The research team is excited to report that a paper detailing our work in this important research topic has been awarded the ANNUAL BEST PAPER (SECOND PLACE) PRIZE for 2015 by the IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics which is the top-notch journal in this field. The results are expected to have significant impact on the development of design methodologies for grid-connected power converters and power distribution equipment.

527212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
527212.value: Supercontinuum spectra, which can range from ultra-violet to mid infra-red wavelength, can be generated in optical fibers using various optical pump sources through the interaction of fiber nonlinearity and dispersion near the zero dispersion wavelength – the wavelength at which the second order dispersion coefficient of the optical fiber is zero. The new design freedom available in novel optical fibers that have air-hole running along the fiber length, called photonics crystal fibers (PCFs), enables the engineering of the fiber dispersion and nonlinearity properties to optimize for supercontinuum generation. Wide supercontinuum spectra have many important applications including precision optical frequency metrology, optical coherence tomography, spectroscopy, microscopy, etc. The development of laser-based precision spectroscopy, including the optical frequency comb technique, was cited in 2005 Nobel Prize in Physics. Although supercontinuum generated using femtosecond laser pulses are stable and coherent but ultrafast laser sources require careful handling and are therefore not preferred in practical applications. Supercontinuum generated using picosecond or nanosecond laser pulses are easier to manipulate but are unstable and incoherent because the main mechanism generating the supercontinuum in the long pump pulse regime is noise sensitive. Various methods have been proposed to control the properties of the supercontinuum spectra like modification of input laser light and novel design of the photonic crystal fiber. In this project, we will develop a complete theoretical understanding of the factors influencing both the supercontinuum spectral structure and the noise properties at all wavelengths across the spectrum. We will develop a unified physical picture providing a complete understanding of SC stability under completely general conditions applicable to arbitrary sources and fiber properties, and also to emerging nonlinear materials such as chalcogenide, and tellurite glasses. We also propose a novel multiscale guidance engineering concept which can make use of the state-of-the art PCF design and fabrication facilities available at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University to create novel PCF tapes in which the linear and nonlinear guidance properties vary longitudinally on multiple scales. Finally, we will carry out experimental and theoretical study of the use of feedback control in supercontinuum generation and develop a generic experimental testbed of noise-driven broadband supercontinuum generation to allow studies of active control from a low-feedback regenerative amplifier to a “supercontinuum laser”. The project will lead to novel photonic crystal fiber designs and feedback control configurations to feed into practical applications of developing low-noise sources and possibly low-cost stable frequency comb sources. 光譜範圍涵蓋從紫外至中紅外範圍的超連續光譜，可以通過多個泵浦源在光纖零色散波長(在此波長，光纖的二階色散系數為零)附近同時激發多種相互作用的非線性過程和色散。通過在光纖中設置貫穿整條光纖的空氣孔製造的新型光纖─光子晶體光纖─而獲得更自由的參數設計空間，從而可以針對超連續光譜的產生進行光纖色散和非線性參數的優化設計。超連續光譜在高精度頻率測量、光相干斷層照相、光譜學和顯微學等領域均擁有重要的應用。鐳射超精細光譜的研究，包括光頻率梳技術，在2005年獲得了物理學諾貝爾獎。雖然通過飛秒雷射脈衝產生的超連續光譜性能穩定而且相干性好，但是超快鐳射光源需要高精度的調試和高穩定的環境，因此在工程應用中非常受限。使用皮秒或者納秒雷射脈衝產生的超連續光譜容易操作和使用，但是由於長脈衝激發超連續光譜的主要機制都對雜訊極為敏感，其所產生的光譜穩定性和相干性都比較差。針對改善超連續光譜特性，研究人員提出了不同的方法，例如對輸入光脈衝進行特別優化、設計新型的光子晶體光纖等。在此研究中，我們將開發一個完整的理論，研究影響超連續光譜結構和整個光譜中的雜訊特性的因素。此理論將提供一個通用的物理圖像，對任意光源和光纖特性，包括在採用硫化物、碲酸鹽等高非線性材料情況下超連續光譜的產生和穩定性機制進行分析和解構。我們還提出一種新型的多尺度波導概念，可以基於理工大學的光子晶體光纖設計和製造平臺，對光子晶體光纖設計軸向分佈尺度不同的特別的錐形結構，實現對光纖非線性的控制。最後，我們還將開展採用回饋控制的超連續光譜生成的理論和實驗研究，建立一個通用的雜訊驅動寬頻超連續光譜實驗研究平臺，並對從弱回饋再生放大器到超連續鐳射等主動控制技術進行研究。本研究工作最後將綜合新型光子晶體光纖的設計和回饋控制技術，開發一種實用的低雜訊光源和可能低成本的穩定頻率梳光源。

527212.label: Realisation of objectives
527212.value: 1. To provide a complete understanding of supercontiuum stability ... In this project, we carried out a systematic investigation of the dynamics of supercontiuum (SC) generation in photonics crystal fiber (PCF). Based on our findings, we studied the cascaded third order soliton compression in optical fibers with convex dispersion profiles which does not change with fiber length inside each fiber segment. Our objective is to produce high-coherence supercontinuum by using high-degree pulse compression. Our simulation was carried out using the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) which is commonly used in the modeling of ultrashort pulse and SC generation. We showed that in the cascaded third order soliton compression a 10 ps input pulse can be compressed to ∼20 fs, and the associated bandwidth broadening is significant. The required input power is significantly lower than other pulse compression techniques for the same given compression factor, and the generated SC is insensitive to noise and has high coherence. Even shorter pulse is expected with the optimization of fiber parameters. We showed that the use of the cascaded soliton will be a good candidate in the development of coherent fiber SC sources. The work was reported in the paper by Qian Li, et al., entitled “High-degree pulse compression and high-coherence supercontinuum generation in a convex dispersion profile,” Optics Communications, vol. 301-302, pp. 29-33, (2013). This work demonstrated how a complete understanding of supercontiuum generation will contribute to novel techniques of SC generation. This part of the work contributes significantly to the results obtained in Part 2 and 3 below. 2. To develop a systematic approach … using a fundamentally new concept called multiscale guidance engineering ... In the development of multiscale guidance engineering, we proposed to use a large mode area (LMA) PCF taper to realize self-similar compression of high power picosecond pulses. We designed an LMA PCF the nonlinearity of which varies significantly with the air hole pitch size along the PCF. We proposed a simplified model to design the taper profile. Self-similar pulse compression of a 1 ps pulse to 53.6 fs in a 6.4 m length LMA PCF taper is demonstrated by simulation using the GNLSE and realistic fiber parameters. The compressed pulse shows low pedestal. The large noise fluctuations on the input pulse are also significantly reduced by the self-similar compression. We then compared the simplified fiber taper design method with that from the full design model taking into account the dispersion variation and found that they are in good agreement. Then both the 1 ps pulse and the compressed femtosecond pulse are injected into a non-zero dispersion shifted fiber (NZ-DSF) for SC generation. We found that self-similar compression can improve the tolerance of the SC generated to noise level by 5 order of magnitude. The work was reported in the paper by Feng Li, et al., entitled “Highly coherent supercontinuum generation with picosecond pulses by using self-similar compression,” Optics Express, vol. 22, pp. 27339-27354 (2014). The study on multiscale guidance engineering also led to the discovery of a novel mean to generate high-repetition-rate soliton train source based on self-similar compression in a nonlinear fiber with exponentially decreasing dispersion. We numerically demonstrated that it is possible to generate a 160 GHz train of ∼100 fs pulses by reshaping a dual-frequency signal into a train of solitary pulses. The proposed pulse train generation scheme requires a nonlinear fiber with an exponentially decreasing second-order dispersion profile. The proposed self-similar compression scheme, which is tunable in pulsewidth and repetition rate, also features a compact structure and may find applications in optical communications and modern instrumentation. The results were reported in the paper by Qian Li et al., entitled “Ultrashort pulse train generation using nonlinear optical fibers with exponentially decreasing dispersion,” Journal of Optical Society of America, B, vol. 31, pp. 1786-1792 (2014). 3. To carry out experimental and theoretical study ... In the experimental work, based on the results of the theoretical and simulation investigation in Part 1 of this project, we formed higher-order solitons by coupling femtosecond pulses into the fundamental mode of a highly nonlinear photonic crystal fiber (HNL-PCF) fabricated in our laboratory. We observed experimentally that the higher order solitons then break up into a series of stable and broadband discrete fundamental solitons at the mid-infrared wavelength longer than 2000 nm through the process of soliton self-frequency shift due to the perturbations induced by the higher-order dispersion and nonlinear effects. The maximum soliton red-shift and the tunable wavelength range can be up to 1600 nm and over 400 nm, respectively. This multiple stable and broadband mid-infrared wavelengths generated in such an HNL-PCF can be used as all-fiber multiwavelength ultrashort pulse sources for multiphoton microscopy and ultrafast photonics. The results were reported in the paper by Jinhui Yuan, et al., entitled “Generation of multiple mid-infrared wavelengths by soliton fission in a photonic crystal fiber,” IEEE Photonics Technology Letters, vol. 26, pp. 2209 – 2212, (2014). Further experimental work stimulated by the understanding of the nonlinear dynamic processes in SC generation is the demonstration of an enhanced intermodal four-wave mixing (FWM) process through coupling positively chirped femtosecond pulses into the deeply normal dispersion region of the fundamental mode of a PCF fabricated in-house. In the intermodal phase-matching scheme, the energy of the pump waves at 800 nm in the fundamental mode is efficiently converted into the anti-Stokes waves around 553 nm and the Stokes waves within the wavelength range of 1445–1586 nm in the second-order mode. The maximum conversion efficiency of the anti-Stokes and Stokes waves can be up to 21% and 16%, respectively. The Stokes frequency shift is 5580 cm^(−1). The results of this investigation were reported in the paper by Jinhui Yuan, et al., entitled “Enhanced intermodal four-wave mixing for visible and near-infrared wavelength generation in a photonic crystal fiber,” Optics Letters, vol. 40, pp. 1338-1340 (2015). We have also demonstrated experimentally second-harmonic generation (SHG) near ultraviolet wavelengths by coupling femtosecond pump pulses into the normal dispersion region far away from the zero-dispersion wavelength of the fundamental mode in a PCF fabricated in our laboratory. When the pump pulses with average input power of 500 mW and center wavelength of 820 nm are used, the maximum conversion efficiency of the second harmonics centered at 410 nm can be up to 1.6 × 10^(−6), corresponding to the output power P_(SH) of 520 nW. By measuring P_(SH) at different PCF lengths and studying the temporal dependence of P_(SH), we confirmed that the physical mechanism of SHG is dominated by surface nonlinearity polarization, which is resulted from the local inhomogeneities in the silica core region and at the core-air-silica cladding interface of PCF. The work was reported in a paper by Jinhui Yuan, et al., “Generation of second-harmonics near ultraviolet wavelengths from femtosecond pump pulses,” IEEE Photonics Technology Letters, Vol. 28, No. 16, pp. 1719-1722 (2016). Finally, we were invited to contribute an article in NanoPhotonics on the modeling of frequency comb sources in which supercontinuum generation is a particular route to generate frequency combs. The work appeared in the invited paper by Feng Li, et al., entitled “Modeling Frequency Comb Sources, ” Nanophotonics, Vol. 5, issue 2, pp. 292–315 (2016).

527212.label: Major findings and research outcome
527212.value: The major findings and research outcome of this projects have been reported the journal publications and the conference presentations listed in Part C. Here we will give a brief summary. • We studied the cascaded third order soliton compression in optical fibers with convex dispersion profiles which does not change with fiber length inside each fiber segment. We demonstrated by using numerical simulation based on the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation that it is possible to produce high-coherence supercontinuum by using high-degree pulse compression. The results were presented in the first journal paper output listed in Part C. • We discovered a novel mean to generate high-repetition-rate soliton train source based on self-similar compression of a dual-frequency signal in a nonlinear fiber with exponentially decreasing dispersion. The results were presented in the second journal paper output listed in Part C. • We experimentally demonstrated the generation of multiple mid-infrared wavelengths based on soliton fission in a photonic crystal fiber. The higher order solitons are formed by coupling femtosecond pulses into the fundamental mode of a highly nonlinear photonic crystal fiber. The results were presented in the third journal paper output listed in Part C. • We proposed to generate highly coherent supercontinuum by using self-similar compression of high power picosecond pulses. We utilized large mode area PCF the nonlinearity of which varies significantly with the air hole pitch size along the PCF. Based on the nonlinearity profile and using an effective dispersion to represent the slightly varying dispersion profile, we demonstrated a simplified model to design the taper profile. The results were presented in the fourth journal paper output listed in Part C. • We experimentally generated visible and near-infrared wavelength by using enhanced intermodal four-wave mixing in a photonic crystal fiber. In the experiment, positively chirped femtosecond pulses are coupled into the deeply normal dispersion region of the fundamental mode of a photonic crystal fiber fabricated in-house. The results were presented in the fifth journal paper output listed in Part C. • We experimentally demonstrated second-harmonic generation near ultraviolet wavelengths by coupling femtosecond pump pulses into the normal dispersion region far away from the zero-dispersion wavelength of the fundamental mode in a silica photonic crystal fiber (PCF) fabricated in-house. The results were presented in the seventh journal paper output listed in Part C.

527212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
527212.value: In this project, we established that multiscale guidance engineering of the properties of optical fibers such as exponentially varying dispersion or nonlinearity can be used to generate highly coherent supercontinuum. The self-similar compression of the optical pulses can be adequately described by the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE). We also demonstrated another form of multiscale guidance engineering in which the optical pulses are compressed non-adiabatically through cascaded soliton propagation in three consecutive optical fiber segments for supercontiuum generation (SCG). It is expected that optical fiber segments each with longitudinally varying fiber properties can be cascaded to generate highly coherent supercontinuum. Although SCG is well-understood in optical fibers, passive control of SCG through modification of the optical fiber parameters longitudinally along the optical fibers is hampered by the difficulties to control fiber parameters to the required precision of a centimeter or less. On the other hand, waveguides can be fabricated to nanometer precision. More important, it has been shown that wave propagation in nonlinear waveguides can also be effectively modeled by the GNLSE that includes the appropriate higher order physical effects. Thus the methodologies developed in this project can also be extended to investigate SCG in nonlinear waveguides.

527212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
527212.value: The study of the spectral broadening process of supercontinuum generation (SCG) in optical fiber has been a central area of research in nonlinear optics since its first discovery in 1976. Although experimental and theoretical studies had identified the major underlying physical mechanisms by the late 1990s, the invention of photonic crystal fiber (PCF) and the subsequent observation of SCG spanning more than an octave in bandwidth has revolutionized this field of study since the year 2000. The ability to engineer the dispersion and nonlinearity of PCF by modifying its air-hole microstructure has allowed SCG to be observed using a wide range of optical sources. In this project, we utilized the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation to provide a complete understanding of SCG. We designed and fabricated PCF using a fundamentally new concept that we termed multiscale guidance engineering. Using the state-of-the art design and fabrication facilities available at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, we created novel PCF structures where the linear and nonlinear guidance properties vary longitudinally on multiple scales. We had also carried out experimental studies using PCF tailor-made in-house with specified properties for wavelength generation in both the infrared and ultraviolet regions.

527312.label: Project Title(Chinese)
527312.value: 利用集成方法設計流水動態健康的元朗生態排洪渠

527312.label: Project Objectives
527312.value: The main objective of this project is to develop and apply an integrated physical and numerical modeling approach to investigate a wide range of hydraulic and sediment transport relationships in the modified low-flow channel to ensure that the new naturalization design is hydraulically sound for a sustainable environment for the target aquatic species. The target species in this project are Tilapia spp. and Malaysian trumpet snail. It is important that the design is viable in which the hydraulic and morphological changes in the channel support a range of flow velocity, flow depth and Froude number which are suitable for the target species. Physical moveable bed models with 1:1 and 1:2 prototype to model scales will be used to evaluate various meandering and morphological conditions. As skimming flows may occur around edges of the defectors during high flow rates in the steeper part of the channel which may be detrimental to habitats and aquatic life, a multi-phase computational fluid dynamics model will be developed to account for the changes in the levels of flow turbulence, air entrainment and sediment in suspension. Because gabion baskets are part of the naturalization design for fish habitat enhancement, results obtained from this project will also provide useful guidance on fish habitat rehabilitation and restoration projects on flood channels. The integrated physical and numerical modeling approach developed in this project will form a useful tool for testing design hypothesis in similar channel naturalization projects in other urbanized cities.

527312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
527312.value: Many natural rivers and streams in highly urbanized cities, like Hong Kong, have been converted into concrete channels for flood control purposes. Although these concrete channels can efficiently convey flood water from populated areas, they disrupt the natural equilibrium and eliminate the living habitats of the original rivers. In recent years, many urban cities (e.g. Seoul, Korea) have recognized the benefits of natural rivers and begun to restore natural features in these concrete flood control channels. However, there is a lack of design methodology for environmental restoration of concrete flood control channels. A general stream restoration method for flood control channels in highly urbanized areas is proposed in this project. It consists of three components: 1) conceptual design of low-flow channels to re-establish a natural and self-sustainable stream system for selected fish habitats; 2) evaluation of hydraulic and sediment transport relationships for the modified low-flow channel using physical and numerical models; and 3) confirmation of the original flood control function after channel restoration. Based on this restoration method, a sustainable naturalization design will be developed in this project for flood control concrete channels in the upstream section of Yuen Long Nullah. The naturalization design involves widening and realigning the low flow channel to emulate a natural stream, introducing sediments from the Nullah upstream to establish appropriate flow depth and substrate for aquatic life, and installing gabion baskets to create fish habitat and enhance its rehabilitation. An integrated physical and numerical modeling approach will be developed and applied to investigate a wide range of hydraulic and sediment transport relationships in the modified low-flow channel to ensure that the new naturalization design is hydraulically sound for a sustainable environment for the target aquatic species which are Tilapia spp. and Malaysian trumpet snail. The integrated physical and numerical modeling approach developed in this project will form a useful tool for testing design hypothesis in similar channel naturalization projects in other urbanized cities. 像香港這樣高度城市化的地方，許多天然河流和溪流已改建成以防洪為目的的混凝土渠道。雖然這些混凝土渠道能有效地將洪水調離人口稠密的地區，但是他們破壞了生態平衡和消除了自然河流的原始特性。近年來許多城市（如韓國漢城）已經認識到自然河流的益處，並且開始還原這些混凝土渠道的自然生態特性。然而，混凝土防洪渠道的環境修復方法目前還比較缺乏。本研究項目提出了一種集成方法在高度城市化的防洪渠道內控制流水動態，這個方法由三部分組成（1）從概念上設計低流量渠道為某些魚類生物重建一種自然生態和自我維持的溪流系統；（2）運用物理和數值模型評價改進渠道中流水動力和泥沙輸運的關係；（3）確定渠道修復後原有的防洪功能。在這個項目中我們將針對元朗河上游混凝土防洪渠道開發一種可持續自然生態的修復設計方法。這種自然生態的設計包括拓寬和重組低流量渠道來模仿自然溪流、引入河流上游的泥沙建立適合生物生存的水深和河床、安裝石籠為魚類提供棲息地從而提供渠道生態修復能力。我們將開發一種物理和數值模型集成的方法用來調查這種改進管道中水力和泥沙輸運的關係，以確保自然生態的設計在流水動態上是可靠的，從而為目標的水生生物如羅非魚、馬來西亞喇叭蝸牛提供一個生態可持續的溪流環境。本專案中提出這種物理和數值模型集成法將為其他類似地區的渠道自然化修復工程提供一種有用的設計工具。

527312.label: Realisation of objectives
527312.value: An effective ecological restoration of a flood channel requires comprehensive assessment of river ecosystem for its physical, chemical, biological and social conditions. Two field sampling approaches had been proposed to collect water quality parameters, hydro-environmental variables, e.g. stream hydrology, as well as the target ecological species e.g. Tilapia spp. and Malaysian trumpet snail. The water quality information will be used to establish baseline information for the design of eco-flood channel. The two approaches were the Cell-in-series (CIS) and mesoscale physical habitats (MPH) approaches. Cell-in-series (CIS) field sampling approach was used for the formulation of mass transport in riverine systems and the findings can be used for water quality modelling. In this approach, a stream is divided into approximately a series of homogenous segments or computational cells that is based on the principle of mass balance. It is assumed the stream is a series of completely mixed flow reactors. Cell in-series is suitable for steep, mountainous and shallow streams due to the dominance of advective transport (e.g. upstream of Yuen Long nullah.) On the other hand ecologists tend to follow a functional classification of rivers based on scale for evaluating river health. This includes scales such as catchment, type, sector, reach, transects and patches. Irrespective of the approach the physical component of river channel habitat is with acknowledged significance, particularly in the upstream. The scale of such habitats varies from micro to catchment and even the entire river known as continuum. But for practical applications such as restoration and rehabilitation works, the medium sized scale (mesoscale) has been preferred. Moreover mesoscale habitats can be easily differentiated by visual observation of surface flow behavior because of the unique hydro-morphological features. Therefore, MPH is also being used for field measurement. Correlations, grouping of samples and explanatory power had been used to analyze the sample data for scenarios such as a typical day and flushed state (after a rainfall aided flushing) in dry season and wet season. Both numerical and experimental investigations of vegetated flows in open channel were carried during the project period. This included the study on vegetated flows in a 12-m recirculating open channel. The focus was on the evolution of 3D flows in straight channels with vegetation patches and gabion deflectors especially in the wake regions of the vegetation patches around the leading edge and after the trailing edge. At the same time, the associated bed-load transport and bed deformation induced by the presence of vegetation patches was investigated. In the sediment transport experiment, bed-load transport rate, sorting characteristics of non-uniform sediments and bed topography were measured. Laboratory investigation results on the characteristics of sediment motion in open channels that are partially obstructed by vegetation patches show that the bed at the upstream reach is rarely scoured in the present test cases. However, significant scouring was observed on the non-vegetated side due to the flow convergence towards the open water reach. The scour hole appeared in the middle of this reach, where secondary currents formed. Because of the secondary currents, finer sands were transported to the vegetated side to form a sediment bar or riffle. The complex flow structure at the vegetated reach caused significant sediment sorting. The generation of secondary currents produced finer bed-load transverse transport, resulting in the great decrease in the median particle size and increase in the larger size of the sediments. In addition, RANS model incorporating Spalart-Allmaras (S-A) turbulence closure has been established to solve the flow field. With the bed-load transport and bed deformation equations included in the governing equations, the bed morphodynamics in an open channel partially obstructed by vegetation patch/gabion deflectors can be calculated. The numerical simulations show that vertical velocity profiles throughout the entire channel change from logarithmic type to tangent hyperbolic type between the non-vegetated reach and vegetated reach. The transverse velocity profile plays an analogous manner as the vertical one. The profile is modulated to tangent hyperbolic shape by the vegetation. Transition appears in the undeveloped flow region. A parabolic velocity profile differs from the logarithmic profile in the non-vegetated reach due to no gravity effect. Because of the blockage effect of vegetation, the mean longitudinal velocity on the vegetated side rapidly decreases at the leading edge of the vegetation and then quickly reaches a constant. Because gabion baskets (deflectors) are part of the naturalization design for fish habitat enhancement, both laboratory and field experiments were carried out in the low flow channel to investigate the sediment transport and bed topography evolution due to different deflector arrangements. As channels are partially constricted by deflectors, flow converges to the non-constricted side with higher flow energy. Investigations of hydraulics and sediment dynamics in deflected channels are generally focused on single deflector arrangement. Therefore, this research studied the behavior of hydraulics and sediment dynamics due to more than one deflectors installed in a channel and explored its ecological impact. The knowledge can be applied in channel restoration and rehabilitation, and more importantly to re-introduce ecological functions into a bare concrete channel. In both the field investigations and laboratory measurements, it is observed that the artificial deflectors alternately installed in the two sides of channel transform the straight flow to meandering flow which results in transverse flow motion. Meanwhile more diverse flow regimes for multiple-deflector arrangements are generated with a wide range of Froude number compared to a single deflector. In particular from the ecological perspective, it is observed in the field experiments that with more deflectors installed, more fish will gather at the low energy zones just downstream of deflectors. River bed evolution under the influence of gabions (deflectors) is a complex sediment transport phenomenon. During high flow rates (large Froude number), skimming flows may occur around edges of the defectors generating air bubbles with high velocity which may be detrimental to aquatic life. To accurately simulate these complex phenomena numerically, interactions between the turbulent flow field around the gabions and the mobile river bed as well as occasionally air entrainment have to be properly addressed in numerical investigation. In this research, fluid (which is water in here), air bubbles and sediment particle will be treated as multiple phases. A two-dimensional numerical flume was developed to investigate the characteristics of the breaking waves (mimicking skimming flows around gabions) as well as the bubble entrainment process under plunging breakers. The numerical model is based on the mixing Reynolds averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) equations, which consider the interactions between air bubbles and liquid by an additional shear stress term. The turbulence closure is accomplished by the k- two-equations model, and the Volume of Fluid method is employed to capture the complicated free surface. Bubbles entrained by the breaking process engage in intense interactions with mean flow and alter the local vorticity field as well as the sediment suspension. In order to study the dynamics of bubbly flow and sediment suspension under breaking processes, an integrated numerical model was proposed to solve the air-liquid mixture equations for flows and transient transport equation for sediment and bubble number, respectively. Numerical results of surface elevation and surface displacement variance were compared against experimental data. The turbulence intensity, velocity and shear stress fields, energy dissipation and air entrainment in the breaking processes were analyzed.

527312.label: Major findings and research outcome
527312.value: The field sampling study reveals some important empirical and theoretical frameworks for MPH assessment methods. Firstly, MPHs are more complementary to low flows and less polluted streams. Assimilation and attenuation of MPHs are optimal in low flow conditions which is useful for water quality studies. Secondly, the correlation between levels of pollution expressed as a flushing signature and sampling approach suggests that the explanatory powers of MPH and CIS can be used to differentiate polluted streams against pristine/unpolluted streams. The MPH approach shows highest explanatory power in dry season’s flushed state (53%) which is greater than the CIS approach. Explanatory powers of the CIS approach are about 50% or more for all cases except in flushed state of dry season (36%). (ref: Part C(8-1) & Part C(8-3)). Experiments on bed load transport and bed evolution due to the presence of vegetation patch show that the formation of various bed forms and complicated sediment sorting are induced by the vegetation through readjusting the flow structure. Vegetation patch generally produces a typical two-stage bed channel. The median diameter (D50) generally increases due to the formation of stable bed covered by coarser sediments on both channel sides upstream of the trailing edge of vegetation. Sediment bar formation is caused by downstream surface sediment fining. This phenomenon is similar to the hiding effect of gravel beds where finer sediments are shielded by coarser sediments. (ref: Part C(8-2) & Part C(9-1)). Gabion baskets (deflectors) are part of the naturalization design for fish habitat enhancement. Laboratory experiments and numerical simulations of various deflector arrangements (ref: Part C(8-4) & Part C(8-5)) show that when limited-thickness layer of sediment is added onto the channel, large bed shear stress around deflectors due to flow convergence enables the bed to scour. The eroded sediment, however, deposits on the downstream bed of the deflector, elevating the bed level. At the scour region where the water depth is greater, the region is referred to a pool. The sediment deposit region is called a riffle because of the shallower water depth. Particularly for multiple-deflector arrangements the periodically undulant bed morphology generates a pool-riffle sequence. If air bubbles occur around the edges of a deflector, numerical studies (ref: Part C(9-2) & Part C(9-3)) show that the depth integrated total shear stress in the water column may decrease by 20%. This implies that the sediment deposition process may be enhanced by the lower stress region.

527312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
527312.value: In recent years, fish habitat numerical models have played a significant role in river and ecosystem management. However, these models usually make use of simple fixed numerical values and exact functions to represent complex natural systems. Fuzzy-logic approach has been proposed to replace the exact functions which has distinctive advantages compared to classical modeling techniques using just “high”, “medium” or “low” to describe physical properties such as flow velocity, water depth and substrate in fish habitats. The Institute for Modeling Hydraulic and Environmental Systems of the University of Stuttgart developed a physical habitat model called CASiMiR that incorporated a fuzzy-approach in habitat models. The CASiMiR fuzzy-logic approach can be applied in the present numerical model together with the complementary ecosystem information collected by the MPH and CIS assessment methods to more accurately assess the biotic responses to the changing environmental conditions through the physical-biota relationships.

527312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
527312.value: Lotic or running waters in the form of rivers and streams play a significant role in ecological point of view due to its unidirectional flow, state of continuous physical change, spatiotemporal variation in biota, and interaction and influence with human settlements. River regulation have transfigured world’s many complex lotic systems with floodplains and meandering, braided channels into single channels that support only a fraction of their original biodiversity and species abundance. The situation deemed to be worse in densely populated and developing countries. Where waterways have been engineered to function hydraulically, not ecologically, which is the case for lotic waters in Hong Kong. With a growing awareness of the value of natural ecosystems, a move has been started from manipulation and regulation of rivers to revival, restoration, and conservation. Current engineering approaches attempt to incorporate knowledge from eco-hydrology and fluvial geomorphology of river forms and processes to produce designs that are in balance with natural processes that are sustainable in the long term. The findings of the project aim to assist the design of a near-natural and self-sustainable flood channel in order to establish and restore river corridors and their rich biodiversity with the harmonisation of flood control requirement.

527612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
527612.value: 為緩解日益嚴重的環境污染、化石燃料緊缺、能耗需求增加等問題，充分利用可再生能源，智能電網提供了一種很有前景的辦法。智能電網採用新型的產品與服務措施，結合智能監控，通訊和自愈技術，為用戶有效的、可持續的、經濟的、安全的供電，使電網傳輸與分配系統更加現代化。科研、工程人員和政府在智能電網的發展和應用上開展了大量的工作，主要包括智能計量、可再生能源與區域能源的結合、通信技術、電網運行與電源的動態優化等。 智能電網需要包括終端用戶在內的所有成員的主動參與。在智能電網中，供應側與需求側的有效結合對優化電力的產生與傳輸至關重要。在建筑能耗中，商業建筑能耗超過40%，在香港地區要更高。但現有工作中對商業建筑與智能電網結合的研究遠少於對居民建筑與智能電網結合的研究。智能電網領域內的專家們尚不清楚商業建筑如何有助於實現智能電網，而建筑行業的專家們不清楚智能電網需要商業建筑怎樣以及提供什麼樣的支持。 事實上，建筑負荷的調控能為電網帶來極大的利益，例如建筑負荷的重新分配及限制峰值負荷能夠降低整個電網的峰值負荷，從而減少在保証充足供電量下的能耗損失。同時商業建筑內普遍採用的自動化系統為商業建筑和智能電網的結合提供了有效的平台。因此本項目在建筑自動化系統的基礎上，進行面向智能電網的商業建筑交互式能耗需求管理策略的試點研究。 本項目將使得智能電網的專家們更好的了解商業建筑融入智能電網的潛力，並提供一種將商業建筑與智能電網結合的方法，同時也有助於建筑領域的專家們積極主動的投入到智能電網的發展中來。

527612.label: Realisation of objectives
527612.value: 1. Simplified models are developed for passive and active thermal storages to predict the thermal storage capabilities and load profile alterations of buildings for smart grids. A simplified building thermal mass (i.e., passive thermal storage) model is developed for predicting and characterizing power demand alteration potentials of thermal mass in commercial buildings. And a PCM storage tank (i.e., active) model is developed to predict the power demand alteration potentials during peak load period. 2. The interaction/communication between commercial buildings and smart grids is built. The dynamic price is optimized based on the information of supply and demand of smart grids. Considering the reference electricity load profiles provided by power grids, buildings can predict their altered electricity load profiles accordingly by predicting their power demand alterations. The altered electricity load profile of each building is then aggregated and used by the grid to set proper electricity prices. Further adjustments on the electricity prices will continue until a near optimal operation profile of the grid is approached. 3. Under a given dynamic price, the power demand of buildings can be optimized to minimize the total energy cost using the developed online control strategies both for building with and without active cold thermal storage. The proposed control strategy for the buildings without active cold thermal storage controls the building power demand to minimize the total operation cost considering the accepted indoor environment. For the buildings with active cold thermal storage, a quantitative analysis on the life-cycle cost saving potentials of active cold storage thermal storage systems concerning the operational cost, initial investment and the space cost is conducted. A simulation-based optimal design method is developed and used to optimize the storage capacity and analyze the impact of the capacity on the life-cycle cost saving potentials. Meanwhile, a model-based online control strategy is developed to achieve the maximum cost saving under given dynamic price without any indoor environment sacrifice. 4. Based on the latest enable technologies such as building automation systems, smart meters, and grid energy management system, an implementation structure is developed for the interactive strategy by integrating smart meters into building automation systems. The smart meter collects useful information from both power supply and demand sides and communicates the information for further interaction and optimization. The building automation system provides various energy information of a building and conducts controls and optimizations for building service systems. A simulation test platform is constructed to simulate the interaction between the smart meters and building automation system in real cases. Each model included in the platform is validated by the real data collected in building management system.

527612.label: Major findings and research outcome
527612.value: An interaction between the power grids and commercial building is built. • A simplified RC model considering the influence of building thermal mass is developed to calculate the potential of building power demand alternation. A dynamic price can be optimized by communicating the information of supply and demand sides of power grids. This bi-direction operation mode can effectively relieve the imbalance issue of power grids and the heavy stress during peak load period. • An active thermal storage model is developed and the capacity of thermal storage is optimized to minimize the life-cycle cost. A model-based online control strategy for charging and discharging of active thermal storage is proposed to minimize the cost under dynamic price and maintain the indoor thermal comfort during DR events. A fast demand response responding to urgent requests of smart grids is developed. • The method, shutting down chiller directly, is adopted to achieve immediate power reduction. A model to determine the number of chillers to be shut down is developed considering the indoor thermal comfort represented by PMV index. • After simply shutting down part of operating chillers, a model-based control strategy for the usage of active thermal storage is developed to realize the pre-determined power reduction without indoor thermal comfort sacrifice. The effective methods are developed to enhance the control performance. • A method based on fuzzy approach can effective improve the robustness of online control performance under the influence of model uncertainties and measurement uncertainties. It can enhance the performance of control strategies adopted during demand response period.

527612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
527612.value: Although shutting down chillers directly is an effective method for fast demand response, some big challenges will be facing to. Undoubtedly, the cooling supply would be limited after shutting down parts of operating chillers. In such a case, the existing control strategies would be failure and leads to some serious consequences. A new control strategy should be developed for the condition of limited cooling supply in order to avoid the unexpected problems occurred. In addition, the indoor air temperature and relative humidity will be increased after shutting down part of chillers. An optimal online control strategy not only taking indoor air temperature but also humidity into account should be developed to achieve the best possible indoor thermal comfort without extra power demand consumed.

527612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
527612.value: Compared with traditional power grids, smart grids enable a bidirectional operation (i.e., “two ways” connection with power flow and information flow) to improve power reliability and energy performance. Buildings are the major energy consumers today and their shares are still increasing. Therefore, an interaction connecting buildings and smart grids can be rather helpful for realizing the flexibility and security of power grid operation. A basic structure of the expected interaction of buildings and smart grids is necessary to be developed using the latest technologies (i.e., smart meters). The smart meters are the interface or bridge for the communication between a power grid and buildings to achieve interaction and optimization. Dynamic price is a critic issue to connect the supply and demand sides of smart grids. How to optimize the dynamic price to balance the supply and demand sides of smart grids is very important. Moreover, an effective online control strategy for the building power demand under determined dynamic price can achieve economic saving without indoor environment sacrifice, at least, within the accepted range.

528412.value: 计及信息物理系统互相依存的智能电网安全评估

528412.label: Co - Investigator(s)

528412.label: Project Objectives
528412.value: To develop a complex network model for smart grid systems involving cyber and physical interdependency; To develop methods for structural vulnerability assessment considering cyber and physical interactions in a smart grid; To develop cyber security assessment method against hacker attacks in smart grids.

To develop cyber security assessment method against hacker attacks in smart grids.

528412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
528412.value: The future smart grid will largely enable embedding intelligent computation, communication and control mechanisms (3Cs) into the physical power systems with various active and reconfigurable components, representing an outstanding example of a Cyber-Physical System (CPS). Successful development of smart grids will therefore require careful investigation of the interplays between various cyber and physical components, and consequently their impacts to power system security, which is the primary concern in this project. Traditionally methodologies for power system security assessment are well established. With the fast development of smart grids and fast deployments of various emerging technologies including distributed and renewable energy resources into power grids, the system security can be threatened due to a mix of unusual factors, ranging from traditional ones like equipment outages, as well as those from the cyber domains. Besides, the extreme weather conditions and human interferences like hacker attacks can cause severe threats as well. Traditional security assessment fails to address the evolving and increasingly sophisticated risks and uncertainties within a smart grid. New methods must be developed to address a multitude of new factors stemming from both physical and cyber domains. This project concerns the critical challenge towards transforming today’s power systems into a highly intelligent and flexible smart grid. Security assessment of such a complicated system has to consider cyber and physical systems of a smart grid, as well as their interactions. The findings of the project will contribute to achieving thorough understanding of and the management of the overwhelming complexity of today’s and future electric power systems to ensure high operational security of power systems in the future. With planned smart grid projects locally, in Mainland China and elsewhere in the world, the models and methods arising from this project will undoubtedly bring forward significant benefits to both Hong Kong and China’s power systems. 未来的智能电网将在很大程度上使智能计算，通信和控制机制（3CS）嵌入到包含有各种主动式并可重构器件的电力网络系统中，形成一个典型的物理信息系统（CPS）。为了促进智能电网的有效发展，本项目因此深入研究在电力物理信息系统中各种信息网络和物理器件之间的互动，以及其所带来的对电网安全性的影响。 传统的电力系统安全评估方法已经确立。随着各种新兴的技术，包括分布式可再生能源接入电网和各种智能电网技术的快速发展，电力系统的安全性受到来自于各种非常规因素的威胁。现代电力系统故障可由传统的设备中断引起，也可由信息网络因素引起。此外，极端天气条件和人为干扰，如黑客攻击，也可能会导致严重的威胁。传统安全评估未能考虑智能电网不断发展带来日益复杂的风险和不确定性。因此必须开发新的安全评估方法，以计及由于智能电网中物理和信息网络融合所带来的新的因素。 本项目的研究内容是为应对把现代电力系统改造成一个高度智能化的和灵活的智能电网的关键挑战。复杂智能电网系统的安全评估必须综合考虑智能电网中信息网络和电力物理系统以及它们之间的相互作用。该项目的研究成果将有助于对现在和未来电力系统运行的复杂性获得充分有效的理解，从而通过有效的管理以保障未来电力系统运行的安全性。随着各种智能电网计划项目在香港、中国大陆和世界各地的广泛展开，本研究项目所产生的模型和方法无疑将为推动香港本地及中国大陆电力系统发展起到良好助益。

528412.label: Realisation of objectives
528412.value: The research objectives of this project have been successfully accomplished, and major research outcomes and findings are reported in FIVE top journal publications and TWO conference publications listed in Part C. In line with project objectives 1 to 3, a complex network based framework for power system modeling considering cyber-physical interdependencies as well as vulnerability and security analysis is established. Specifically, with respect to Project Objective 1 on complex network based modeling of smart grids, the team developed advanced models for smart grid from an integral perspective involving topological and electrical aspects for potential applications of security and vulnerability assessment considering impacts from physical and cyber domains. The developed model has been summarized and reported in one IET conference paper. With respect to Project Objectives 2 and 3 on structural vulnerability and security analysis for smart grids considering cyber and physical interdependencies, the team has focused on both prior- and post-contingency analysis for smart grids, of which the former highlights the qualitative assessment of network vulnerability (security) with respect to (cascading) contingency events, while the latter considers the consequent evolvement of the event from individual component outage into islanding/splitting situations of the grid. Accordingly, the research outcomes have been summarized and reported in one IEEE conference paper and one paper in IEEE Transactions on Power System. In addition, in collaboration with colleagues from other department in PolyU, the proposed vulnerability assessment method has been successfully extended to analyze a metropolitan water distribution grid, which is also an important infrastructure in human society. The outcome is reported in a paper in Chaos journal. Lastly, the project team has conducted research works on the probabilistic prognosis of wind power that can impact significantly the security of smart grids with high wind penetration. As we have reported in our mid-term report, the additional research has resulted in three high quality publications including one Invited Paper by IEEE Transactions on Power Systems, which is now a Highly Cited Paper according to SCI.

528412.label: Major findings and research outcome
528412.value: The project achieved several major findings and outcomes, including • A new complex network based smart grid modeling framework, which can address cyber-physical interdependencies involved in smart grid operation. The developed model reflects the properties of power grids from both electrical, topological and cyber perspectives, which are considered as an effective and new approach for smart grid modeling to address concerns from physical and cybernetic domains simultaneously. The outcome is reported in Conference Publication No2 in Part C; • A new system security and vulnerability assessment framework for power grids considering interferences from both physical and cyber domains. Specially, the research has been focused on prior- and post-contingency analysis for smart grids, where qualitative assessment of network vulnerability and security with respect to cascading contingency events that possibly results in islanding situations. Validations of the methods have been achieved through cases studies on both power system as well as water distribution system. The outcome is reported in Conference Publication No1, and journal publications No 1 and No5 in Part C; • Recognizing the significant impact from wind power uncertainties on power system security, the team has extended the scope of investigation to the probabilistic prognosis of wind power generation that can effectively quantify the uncertainties involved in wind generation with associated confidence level. The obtained interval forecast of wind power can be of great value to safeguard system operation and planning with high wind penetration in a smart grid environment. (Journal Publications No2 to No 4 in Part C)

528412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
528412.value: The project has accomplished its goals with significant research outcomes achieved. While the proposed new models and methods for cyber-physical interdependencies oriented system modeling, vulnerability and security assessment for smart grids are developed, future research are still needed to enhance the performance and generalities of these achievements. In order to address the cyber interdependency, the developed models adopt the complex network based approach, which emphasizes the network topological properties. While such models can well reflect information flow and structure vulnerability, additional efforts are needed in modeling electrical energy flow with additional modifications added into the classical complex network models. As such, the resulted model complexity is increased and the computational efficiency is therefore influenced, which should be improved in our future work. In addition, security analysis against cascading failures is particularly focused, since such contingencies can have disastrous consequences. However, there are other kinds of faults(non-cascaded) that can occur in power systems which should also be taken into consideration, and this will need future efforts to extend the proposed security framework in this project. Furthermore, in addressing wind uncertainties, an innovative framework for probabilistic wind prognosis is developed, which has high potentials for future applications to solar power prognosis.

528412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
528412.value: Power systems are evolving into the era of smart grid, where security issues arisen from both cyber and physical domains have to be taken care. Meanwhile, many renewable generations such as wind power with high intermittency and uncertainty also impose security threats for power system operation. To address these concerns, the project sets out to develop new models and methods that can innovatively model and assess system security and vulnerability taking cyber-physical interdependencies into account. In addition, innovative probabilistic prognosis methods for are developed that can effectively quantify the uncertainties of wind generation with confidence level. The developed models and methods have been successfully validated using IEEE Benchmark system and practical data. Based on the achievements in this project, future research efforts can be made to reduce the model complexities and enhance the model performances respectively.

528512.label: Co - Investigator(s)

528512.label: Project Objectives

To investigate the force redistribution and second order effects of supertall structures caused by temperature actions. To investigate the force redistribution and second order effects of supertall structures caused by temperature actions.

528512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
528512.value: 近些年来超高层结构在世界各地特别是亚洲地区发展迅速；仅仅中国近十年内将建造40座400米以上的超高层结构。超高层结构在施工期间暴露在空气中，不象使用期间有外围玻璃幕墙的保护，因而其受到的温度作用不同于使用期间。另外，结构的温度作用有别于其它荷载作用。比如，风荷载作用下，结构低层的受力较大；而温度作用下由于各层变形的累计，结构高层受到的变形和内力最大。因此，基于使用阶段的超高层结构设计不一定能满足施工期间的安全需求。 但是，由于缺乏实际测量的温度数据及温度引起的响应，超高层结构施工期间温度作用的研究仍然不够完善。而中国现行的超高层结构设计规范在温度作用方面完全是空白，设计人员只能简化计算超高层结构的温度作用，从而导致超高层结构实际的温度作用可能被低估。比方，高达600米的广州新电视塔的长期健康监测结果表明该结构施工期间的水平位移与台风引起的水平位移大致相当，且远超过设计分析结果。 近些年来发展的结构监测技术研究结构真实性能提供了一个新方法。本申请人有幸分别承担了600米高的广州新电视塔健康监测系统和632米高的上海中心健康监测系统项目。前者是目前中国最高的结构物，后者在2014年完成后将成为新的最高。 本项目旨在通过数值模拟和现场监测研究上述两个地标结构在施工期间的温度荷载和温度效应。监测系统测量的温度与热传导分析得到的温度将有机结合起来，得到超高层结构实际真实的温度分布。然后将温度引起的结构效应与实测结果进行比较。实测数据中将考虑结构的收缩徐变。最后，本项目将提供超高层结构温度荷载模型和设计建议。本项目将由三位学术界和一位工程界科技工作者共同承担。本项目的完成将提高超高层结构施工的安全性和准确性，同时实际监测的数据将使全世界的科研工作者和工程技术人员受惠。

528512.label: Realisation of objectives
528512.value: 1. The present project uses the 600 m tall Canton Tower (formerly as Guangzhou New TV Tower) as the example. A comprehensive structural health monitoring system with about 800 sensors have been installed on the structure. Hundreds of temperature sensors distributed on four facades and 12 sections of the inner and outer tubes provide the detailed temperature distribution of the structure in different days, seasons, and years. Several heat-transfer finite element models have been developed for different components, including the inner tube and the outer-tube columns. The integration of the field monitoring data and numerical analysis results give a more detailed and accurate temperature distribution of the supertall structure. In particular, the temperature difference between the inner tube and outer tube, and temperature difference between different facades of the outer tube were obtained. 2. The temperature distribution in the above step was input to the finite element model of the whole structure. The associated temperature-induced responses (displacement and stresses) were calculated. The numerical results were compared with the monitoring counterparts and a good agreement was observed. It shows that the temperature-induced quasi-static responses are significant as compared with the responses subject to other loads such as the dead load, wind load and seismic load. However, the overall stress is still much lower than the material strength (about 1/3 of the design value) and the horizontal displacement is within 50 cm (1/1000 of the total height). Therefore the second order effect on the external columns is negligible. 3. A temperature model was suggested, including the temperature difference between the inner tube and outer tube, temperature difference between different facades of the outer tube, and the temperature variation along the height of the supertall structure. These values can be used as the reference of temperature loading when similar skyscrapers in South China will be designed and analyzed.

528512.label: Major findings and research outcome
528512.value: Under the support of the grant, five refereed journal papers have been published and the other one is under review, six international conference papers have been published, and two PhD students have been trained. The main findings and outcomes of the project include: 1) Temperature models for structural design and analysis of supertall structures in South China were derived. One paper was published in Structural Control and Health Monitoring (Vol. 24-4, e1900). 2) Both the numerical and monitoring results showed that the temperature-induced quasi-static responses were in a similar level to the typhoon-induced dynamic responses. The temperature-induced stresses are about 25% the dead load. One paper was published in Engineering Structures (Vol. 143, 91-100). 3) A data fusion technique was developed for displacement and inclination estimation using distributed strain data. Its accuracy is higher than GPS. One paper was published in Engineering Structures (Vol. 67, 29-38). 4) A Kalman-filtering-based technique was developed for predicting the floor settlement of supertall structures. It improves the prediction precision to within 5 mm of actual values. One paper was published in Advances in Structural Engineering (Vol. 17-6, 881-893) and the other in Journal of Civil Structural Health Monitoring (Vol. 3-1, 49-61). 5) One PhD student (Mr. NI Pinghe) was trained.

528512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
528512.value: The present temperature analysis adopts a divide-and-conquer approach, i.e., the temperature models and the associated responses are conducted in two separated steps, each having different models. The process requires considerable manual intervention and is not efficient from the computational perspective. An integrated manner can be further developed by using one common 3D finite element model. The proposed study is being conducted and applied to a supertall building at Wuhan, China and a footbridge at HK PolyU campus.

528512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
528512.value: Supertall structures taller than 300 meters have rapidly developed in recent years in China. The temperature actions on these skyscrapers during the construction stage are more significant and critical than the service stage because: 1) they have no facades/curtain wall outside to prevent them from daily and seasonal temperature changes; and 2) the structural system under construction is incomplete. However, the temperature behavior hasn’t been well studied because of lacking field measurement of temperature data and temperature-induced responses of supertall structures during construction. The present study utilized the 600-m tall Canton Tower (formerly as Guangzhou New TV Tower) and 632-m tall Shanghai Tower as the test-beds to study the temperature loading and the associated temperature actions on supertall structures via the field monitoring and numerical analysis. The real-time monitoring system of the Canton Tower consisting of about 800 sensors provides a comprehensive temperature distribution and temperature-induced responses of the structure. The temperature-induced displacement and stresses were quantitatively analyzed and verified by comparison with the monitoring data. A Kalman-filtering-based technique was developed for predicting the floor settlement of Shanghai Tower. The numerical predicted floor levels were within 5 mm of actual values, much less than the specified 30 mm.

528912.label: Project Objectives
528912.value: To advance multiscale FEM methods for long-span cable-supported bridges that can effectively integrate the global structural model equipped with global sensors and the local structural details installed with local sensors; To develop an effective method for the optimal placement of multiscale sensors that can integrate the global and local sensors, minimize the required number of sensors, and increase the accuracy of response reconstruction; To investigate multiscale damage detection methods that can synthesize the measurement data from different sensors with different scales and frequency ranges; and To determine the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed technology by conducting experimental studies on a laboratory-based test bed of a long-span suspension bridge.

To develop an effective method for the optimal placement of multiscale sensors that can integrate the global and local sensors, minimize the required number of sensors, and increase the accuracy of response reconstruction;
To investigate multiscale damage detection methods that can synthesize the measurement data from different sensors with different scales and frequency ranges; and

528912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
528912.value: Many innovative long-span suspension bridges have been constructed in recent years. These landmark structures are subject to harsh environments, presenting many challenges to professionals in ensuring that these structures function properly during their long service lives as well as in protecting them from destructive failure during strong winds, severe earthquakes, terrorist attacks, and other abnormal events. The structural health monitoring (SHM) technology has been regarded as a cutting-edge approach to providing a better solution for problems. Over the past two decades, significant effort has been dedicated to vibration-based methods for damage detection in terms of measured global structural responses. However, a long-span suspension bridge is a complex structure comprising tens of thousands of structural components of different sizes and connected to one another in different ways. Local damage often does not significantly affect the global responses of a bridge, making global response-based damage analysis inaccurate and sometimes impossible. Moreover, the number of sensors in an SHM system for a long-span suspension bridge is limited, and the sensors may not directly monitor the locations of structural defects. Therefore, the successful application of damage detection methods to long-span suspension bridges is very limited, although some methods have been successfully applied in mechanical and aeronautical engineering. In this context, the current study aims to develop a multiscale SHM technology for long-span suspension bridges. This project involves four major tasks, as follows: (1) the multiscale finite element modeling of a long-span suspension bridge that can integrate the global structural model equipped with global sensors with the local structural details installed with local sensors; (2) the optimal placement of multiscale sensors that can integrate global and local sensors, minimize the required number of sensors, and increase the accuracy of damage detection; (3) the development of multiscale damage detection methods that can synthesize the measurement data from different sensors with different scales and frequency ranges; and (4) the determination of the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed technology by conducting extensive experimental studies on a laboratory-based test bed of a long-span suspension bridge. The findings will advance existing SHM technologies, allow the detection of damages on long-span suspension bridges, and enhance our ability to ensure the functionality and safety of bridges. The research assistants involved will be trained as high-quality researchers throughout the course of the current project.

528912.label: Realisation of objectives
528912.value: A new mixed-dimensional finite element (FE) coupling method is developed to achieve better displacement compatibility and stress equilibrium at the interface between the elements of different types when establishing a multi-scale FE model. Firstly, both linear force and displacement constraint equations are derived based on the principle of virtual work. Then the proposed coupling method is extended to the nonlinear mixed-dimensional FE coupling problems. Finally, the proposed coupling method is applied to a number of test cases including linear beam-to-plate, beam-to-shell and beam-to-solid interface problems, a linear frame structure, and a beam-to-shell buckling problem. The obtained results are also compared with those from the existing methods. The comparison reveals that the proposed coupling method can handle both linear and nonlinear mixed-dimensional FE coupling problems more accurately than the existing methods and that it can be applied to a structure satisfactorily for multi-scale simulation. Multi-type sensor should be optimally installed on the structure to capture the multi-scale response. A dual-type sensor placement method is firstly proposed with the aim of the best reconstruction of structural displacement and strain responses. The unmeasured responses of the key locations are reconstructed using the limited measured response using the transmission matrix composed of mode shapes. Furthermore, the sensor placement is optimized in terms of number and location for the best response reconstruction. An experimental work is designed and conducted on the simply-supported overhanging beam. The dual-type sensor placement method has been extended to multi-type sensor placement for multi-scale response reconstruction. The multi-type sensors include strain gauges, displacement transducers and accelerometers, all of which are widely used in civil engineering structures. The number and locations of the three types of sensors are determined aiming to reconstruct the strain, displacement and acceleration responses to the best. Response reconstruction is performed using the classical Kalman filter, in which the time history of external excitations acting on the structure is assumed to be available. The optimized sensor placement is determined by minimizing the overall response reconstruction error variance at the locations of interest. A simply-supported overhanging steel beam serves as a sample case in the numerical and experimental study to investigate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed approach. To alleviate the necessity of measuring external excitation in response reconstruction, an optimal multi-type sensor placement method for response and excitation reconstruction is also proposed. Joint response and excitation response is developed in the framework of Kalman filter with unknown input (KF-UI), in which minimum-variance unbiased estimates of the generalized state and the external excitations are obtained and structural responses of key locations can then be reconstructed. The asymptotic stability feature of the filter is utilized for optimal sensor placement. The number and spatial location of the multi-type sensors are determined by adding the optimal sensor which gains the maximal reduction of reconstructed responses error. A simply-supported overhanging steel beam under multiple types of excitation is numerically studied to demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of the proposed method, and the experimental work is then carried out to testify the effectiveness of the proposed method. To facilitate an effective stress-related condition assessment of large-scale civil structures, a multiscale FE model with detailed geometry and affordable computation burden is needed. The Stonecutters Bridge, a cable-stayed bridge with a 1,018m main span in Hong Kong, is adopted as a case study in multiscale FE modeling. The twin-box deck of the bridge is modeled with shell elements in detailed geometry such that all stress responses in the bridge deck can be directly computed; other bridge components are modeled using either beam or truss elements. Each segment of the girder is then condensed into a super-element using the substructuring method to reduce the number of degrees of freedom for computation ease. To ensure the established multiscale model consistent with the actual structure in both global and local responses, a novel sensitivity-based model updating that that take into account both the global dynamic properties and local responses of the multiscale model has been developed. As a case study, the proposed model updating method is finally applied to the multiscale FE model of the Stonecutters Bridge, in which the updating objective function is formulated with both global modal frequencies and multiscale (displacement and stress) static influence lines. The response surface method is adopted in the optimization process to reduce computation time. One outstanding obstacle that hinders robust application of FE model updating based damage identification to civil structures is that the point measurements captured by the predefined sensors cannot cover adequately all possible damage location. To overcome the shortages of response acquired by limited sensors as well as take advantages of utilizing heterogeneous responses in damage identification, a response reconstruction combined FE model updating for damage identification of large civil structures is presented. Radial-basis-function (RBF) network is employed to predict the mode shapes using modal properties extracted by experimental modal analysis (EMA) after damage occurrence. The reconstructed responses are finally used to identify the damage in sensitivity-based FE model updating. Besides, the sparse regularization is employed to increase the identification accuracy in the iterations. The same simply supported overhanging steel beam composed of 40 elements serves as a numerical study to demonstrate the procedure and feasibility of the proposed method. The validation of this method is further conducted by a laboratory test. Furthermore, since it is not easy to measure the time series evolution of excitation acting on the structures, the proposed damage identification via response reconstruction is extended from the situation that excitations are needed to the situation that excitations are absent. Response and excitation are reconstructed simultaneously through the implementation of KF-UI. FE model updating is then performed using the reconstructed response and excitation for localizing and quantifying structural defects. A numerical simulation study is conducted on an overhanging steel beam under unknown excitation. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are further ascertained by laboratory tests of the same overhanging beam. Another challenge of damage identification of a large and complex civil structure exhibit in the ill-posed nature and non-global identifiability feature of the inverse problem with a large number of unknowns. Following a divide-and-conquer strategy, a multi-level damage identification method has been proposed. The entire structure is decomposed into several manageable substructures and further condensed as super-elements using the component mode synthesis (CMS) technique. The damage identification is performed at two levels: the first is at substructure level to locate the potential damage region and the second is at the element level inside the suspicious substructures to further locate as well as quantify the damage. In each level’s identification, the damage searching space over which model updating is performed is notably narrowed down, not only reducing the computation amount but also increasing the damage identifiability. Besides, the Kalman filter-based response reconstruction is performed at the second level to reconstruct the response of the suspicious substructure for exact damage quantification. Numerical studies and laboratory tests are both conducted on a simply supported overhanging steel beam for conceptual verification. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed multi-level damage identification via response reconstruction is evaluated on the delicate Tsing Ma suspension bridge testbed.
