528912.label: Major findings and research outcome
528912.value: A new mixed-dimensional finite element (FE) coupling method for mixed-dimensional FE coupling in multi-scale FE modeling has been developed from the project (Wang et al. 2014). The proposed coupling method can handle both linear and nonlinear mixed-dimensional FE coupling problems more accurately and it can be applied to a structure satisfactorily for multi-scale simulation. A dual-type sensor placement method is proposed with the aim of the best reconstruction of structural displacement and strain responses (Zhang et al. 2014). When the time evolution of excitation is available, response reconstruction is performed by taking the Kalman filter as a powerful data fusion tool (Zhu et al. 2013; Xu et al. 2016). When the time evolution of excitation is unknown, joint response and excitation response is implemented using the Kalman filter with unknown input (KF-UI) (Zhang and Xu 2016a). Experimental works show that the proposed methods are effective to produce the superior sensor placements for response reconstruction. The multiscale FE modeling of the Stonecutters Bridge have been established (Zhu et. al 2015) and a sensitivity-based model updating that take into account both the global dynamic properties and local responses of the multiscale model has been performed (Xiao et. al 2015). The established multiscale model is capable of representing the detail stress while enjoys acceptable computational burden. Damage identification via response reconstruction methods have been developed by combining the sparse regularized FE model updating with response reconstruction for both known and unknown excitation cases (Zhang and Xu 2016a; Zhang and Xu 2016b; Zhang and Xu 2016c). The laboratory test results show that the multi-sensing damage identification via response reconstruction does improve the accuracy of damage detection considerably. Furthermore, a multi-level damage identification via response reconstruction method has been proposed for the damage identification of large-scale structures (Zhang and Xu 2016d). Both numerical studies and laboratory tests on the TMB testbed demonstrate that the proposed method does improve the identification accuracy of damage localization and quantization considerably (Zhang and Xu, 2017; Xu et al. 2017). A total of 11 peer-reviewed papers have been published in the top international journals, and one paper is under review. Additionally, one invited lecture, one keynote lecture, and 11 conference papers have been presented at international conferences. Besides, one Ph.D. student has been trained through the project. The research collaboration has been established between the Hong Kong Polytechnic University and the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, USA.

528912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
528912.value: In the multi-level damage identification, the multi-scale model is built using CMS technique and the bridge deck is modeled using beam elements. Thus, structural damage is represented as stiffness degradations on the beams. For more detailed damage, such as cracks, joint loosening and others, more detailed model, such as solid elements on the joints and hotspots, is needed to form a more detailed multi-scale model. A new mixed-dimensional FE coupling method proposed by Wang et al (2014) is promising in building such a detailed multi-scale model. Recently, Sun et al. (2016) developed a new multi-scale fatigue model to describe the collective process of the short crack nucleation and growth in micro-scale and continuous fatigue damage evolution in macro-scale and the micro–macro relationship was established for the fatigue accumulation process. This multiscale damage model is worthwhile to be integrated into the proposed multi-scale SHM.

528912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
528912.value: Many innovative long-span suspension bridges have been constructed in recent years. Their safety and functionality are very important for our society. Since a long-span bridge comprises abundant components of different sizes, damage identification as the core task of structural health monitoring (SHM) should be performed in multiple scales. In this context, a multiscale SHM technology for long-span suspension bridge is developed in this project. It incorporates the following aspects: (1) a new mixed-dimensional FE coupling method for multi-scale modelling, (2) optimal multi-type sensor placement for response reconstruction, (3) multi-type response reconstruction-combined damage identification, (4) sparse regularization to overcome the ill-posedness of damage identification, (5) multi-level damage identification to decrease the computation burden and increase the damage identifiability, and (4) experimental investigations on overhanging beam and a larger TMB test to evaluate the performances of the proposed methods. The project has been successfully completed. The findings and experiences obtained from this exercise can shed light on the damage identification on real long-span suspension bridges.

529212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
529212.value: This proposal aims to develop new low-cost inorganic nanowire membrane composites for the treatment of contaminated water, typically containing oil spills, heavy metallic ions, and organic compounds. The whole process consists of pretreatment of contaminated water using wettability-tuned nanowire membranes for selectively absorbing hydrophobic organic compounds followed by ion-exchange processes based on acid manganese dioxide octahedral molecular sieve nanowire membrane with strong ion-exchange capabilities. The proposed multifunctional highly-selective absorbent membrane materials can be an ideal candidate for the separation and removal of pollutants in water, and the applications of the nanowire multifunctional membranes could lead to a significant reduction of energy consumption via low-pressure-permeability. This proposal is innovative with respect to the choice of membrane materials with unique properties including: (i) high selectivity for solvents that need to be separated. (ii) high surface area and permeability. (iii) good mechanical and thermal stability (up to 380 °C). (iv) good chemical stability (anti-fouling and anti-scaling). (v) good ion-exchange properties. (vi) low cost of the membrane materials. 本項目集中在研發一種新型的且價格低廉的無極納米薄膜複合物，用於對水污染進行治理。主要集中在對含有油污水及含有重金屬離子及有機化合物廢水進行處理淨化。整個淨化過程利用對材料的親水性進行調節，藉以達到選擇性吸附廢水中的有機物雜質。然後基於構成納米線薄膜的錳氧化物八面體分子篩所具有的獨特的可選擇性離子交換廢水中的重金屬離子的特性來處理廢水中的重金屬離子。我們所研發的多功能納米線薄膜吸附劑是一種理想的，可用於處理淨化含有各種污染物的廢水處理劑。應用此納米薄膜水處理劑可有效降低能耗。 此項目具有很高的創新性，主要集中在以下幾個方面： 1. 對所處理的廢水污染物具有高效選擇性 2.此納米薄膜具有高比表面及通透性 3.此納米薄膜具有良好的機械性能及熱穩定性（可達380攝氏度） 4.良好的化學穩定性 5.良好的離子交換能力 6.價格低廉

529512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
529512.value: The linear penalty function method has been one of the most popular and efficient methods for solving constrained optimization problems. The theoretical basis for the successful application of this method is the establishment of first-order and second-order necessary optimality conditions via an exact penalty function and the guarantee of convergence under mild conditions. However, there are a few well known difficulties associated with the linear penalty type approach: too strong conditions for the existence of an exact penalty function and too large penalty parameter required for finding a good approximate solution. The research effort in recent years has been concentrated on generalizing the family of penalty function methods for overcoming these difficulties. It is the objective of this project to pursue a general framework of optimality conditions and solution methods for nonlinear optimization problems by virtue of lower-order penalty functions. We will investigate first-order and second-order necessary conditions via a general exact penalty function and obtain in particular second-order necessary conditions using an l_2/3 exact penalty function. The variational analysis techniques will play a key role in our theoretical analysis. We will study a primal-dual l_1/2 interior-point penalty method for solving constrained optimization problems and establish its global convergence properties. Various numerical implementing issues will be examined to guarantee a fast convergence of our algorithm. Our anticipated results on optimality conditions and solution methods for nonlinear optimization problems by virtue of lower-order penalty functions should make a significant progress in advancing the state-of-art in constrained optimization from a novel viewpoint. 一直以来线性罚函数方法都是最常用且有效地求解约束最优化问题的方法之一。 能够通过精确罚函数建立起约束最优化问题的一阶和二阶必要优化条件和在较弱的条件下即能保证收敛性质， 是成功应用罚函数方法的理论基础。 但是，众所周知要保证线性精确罚函数需要附加较强的条件以及为了得到满意的逼近解线性罚函数方法需要充分大的罚因子， 这些都是线性罚函数方法的主要难点。为解决这些难点，近年来的研究都在致力于引进和研究新的罚函数方法。 此研究项目的目的在于利用低阶罚函数寻求建立非线性约束最优化问题的最优性条件和数值方法的基本框架。 通过精确罚函数， 我们将研究约束优化问题的一阶和二阶必要最优性条件。 特别地， 我们将利用 -精确罚函数建立二阶必要条件。在我们的研究中变法分析将是我们进行理论分析的重要工具。 我们还将利用原始对偶 内点罚函数方法来求解约束最优化问题并建立其全局收敛性性质。为保证算法的快速收敛，我们还将考虑在执行数值算法过程中遇到的各种问题。 我们希望， 通过低阶罚函数研究非线性最优化问题的最优性条件和数值方法获得的结果，能够为进一步研究及求解约束优化问题带来一个全新的观念并能积极推动该领域的进一步发展。

529512.label: Realisation of objectives
529512.value: For objective 1, we studied first- and second-order necessary conditions for nonlinear programming problems from the viewpoint of exact penalty functions and local sharp minima of the nonlinear programming problem via exact penalization. In Meng and Yang (2015), by applying the variational description of regular subgradients, we first established necessary and sufficient conditions for a penalty term to be of KKT-type by using the regular subdifferential of the penalty term. In terms of the kernel of the subderivative of the penalty term, we also presented sufficient conditions for a penalty term to be of KKT-type. We then derived a second-order necessary condition by assuming a second-order constraint qualification which requires that the second-order linearized tangent set is included in the closed convex hull of the kernel of the parabolic subderivative of the penalty term. In particular, for an l_{2/3} penalty term, by assuming the nonpositiveness of a sum of a second-order derivative and a third-order derivative of the original data and applying a third-order Taylor expansion, we obtained the second-order necessary condition. In Meng and Yang (2016), utilizing generalized differentiation tools in variational analysis such as subderivatives and regular subdifferentials, we obtained some primal and dual characterizations for a penalty function associated with the nonlinear programming problem to have a local sharp minimum. These general results were then applied to the l_p penalty function with 0leq pleq 1. In particular, we presented primal and dual equivalent conditions in terms of the original data of the nonlinear programming problem, which guarantee that the l_p penalty function has a local sharp minimum with a finite penalty parameter in the case of pin (frac12, 1] and p=frac{1/2} respectively. By assuming the Guignard constraint qualification (resp. the generalized Guignard constraint qualification), we also showed that a local sharp minimum of the nonlinear programming problem can be an exact local sharp minimum of the l_p penalty function with pin [0, 1] (resp. pin [0, frac12]). Finally, we gave some formulas for calculating the smallest penalty parameter for a penalty function to have a local sharp minimum. For objective 2, we studied inequality constrained nonlinear programming problems by virtue of an l_{1/2}-penalty function and a quadratic relaxation. In Tian et al (2016), combining with an interior-point method, we proposed an interior-point l_{1/2}-penalty method. We introduced different kinds of constraint qualifications to establish the first-order necessary conditions for the quadratically relaxed problem. We applied the modified Newton method to a sequence of logarithmic barrier problems, and designed some reliable algorithms. Moreover, we established the global convergence results of the proposed method. For objective 3, in Tian et al (2016), we carried out numerical experiments on 266 inequality constrained optimization problems. Our numerical results showed that the proposed method is competitive with some existing interior-point l_1-penalty methods in term of iteration numbers and better when comparing the values of the penalty parameter. We also studied nonlinear complementarity problems. In Tian and Yang (2016), we introduced a new penalty method for solving nonlinear complementarity problems, which unifies the existing l_1-penalty method and the natural residual equation-based method. We established the exponential convergence rate between a solution of the penalized equations and that of the complementarity problem under a uniform xi-P-function and studied a perturbed b-regularity condition. Two kinds of numerical algorithms with global and fast local convergence were designed by virtue of the proposed penalty method. Preliminary numerical experiments conducted on test problems from MCPLIB showed that the proposed method is efficient and robust. In Sun et al (2016), power penalty methods for solving a linear parabolic complementarity problem arising from American option pricing required us to solve a series of systems of nonlinear equations (called penalized equations). We studied the relationships among the solutions of penalized equations under appropriate conditions. Additionally, since these penalized equations are neither smooth nor convex, some existing algorithms, such as Newton method, cannot be applied directly to solve them. We applied the nonlinear Jacobian method to solve penalized equations and verified that the iteration sequence generated by the method converges monotonically to the solution of the penalized equation. Some numerical results confirmed the theoretical results and the efficiency of the proposed algorithm. Furthermoew, in Meng et al (2015), we introduced the exact tangent approximation property for a convex set and provided its characterizations, including the nonzero extent of a convex set. We obtained necessary and sufficient conditions for the closedness of the positive hull of a convex set via a limit set defined by truncated upper level sets of the gauge function. We also applied the exact tangent approximation property to study the existence of a global error bound for a proper, lower semicontinuous and positively homogeneous function. In Hu et al (2016), based on the gradient sampling technique, we presented a novel subgradient algorithm to solve the nondifferentiable convex optimization problem with an extended real-valued objective function. An unique feature of our algorithm was the approximation of subgradient at a point via random sampling of (relative) gradients at nearby points, and then taking convex combinations of these (relative) gradients. We proved that our algorithm converges to an optimal solution with probability 1. Numerical results demonstrated that our algorithm performs favorably compared with existing subgradient algorithms on applications considered.

529812.label: Project Objectives
529812.value: To establish a thorough scientific basis for understanding the physiological mechanisms, psychological requirements, responses and behaviours of children with spinal deformities in relation to various clinical situations, the current design and development processes of making orthotic bracewear to control curve progression. To analyse the anthropometry measurements, morphologies and asymmetry of the body, locomotor skills of children with spinal deformities, as well as the rotational deformity and kinematic profiles of the spine in relation to the pressure requirements in order to create adequate corrective forces in the corset design for spine support and halting progression curvature. To examine the psychological relationship between orthotic pressure distribution and the subjective perception of sensory comfort in patients, and formulate a biomechanical model to simulate orthotic pressure distribution in relation to the mechanical and stress strain properties of the fabrication materials, deformations, torsional stiffness and shape recovery characteristics of SMA coil springs, 3D design and geometry of orthoses, etc. Fabric properties and structures which influence the support, cushioning and comfort of the corset, will be identified and associated with the monitoring of curvatures so as to determine the optimal pressure requirements and the most desirable fabrication for the treatment. To design and develop, on the basis of clinical and textile science analyses, optimally fitting adaptive corsets for spine support which can exert adequate pressure on prescribed body regions to control curve progression, improve the physiological comfort of patients, and facilitate the continuous use of the corset for children with different levels of pressure requirements and clinical practices, and therefore optimize the compliance efficacy of the treatment. To undertake wear trials that will evaluate whether the intended objectives of the adaptive corset which control the progression of spine curvatures can be achieved, and determine the effectiveness and practical use of the corset.

529812.label: Realisation of objectives
529812.value: In this study, clinical investigation was carried out to establish a thorough understanding of the physiological mechanisms, psychological requirements, responses and behaviours of children with spinal deformities in relation to various clinical situations, the current design and development processes of making orthotic bracewear to control curve progression. A total of 6 subjects with Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) were recruited. Their X-ray scans, clinical procedures for the casting, development processes of rigid bracewear and the fabrication materials were recorded. The rate of skin temperature and humidity changes when the orthotic bracewear are used was continually monitored and recorded by using a skin temperature and humidity logger. The activity profile when the rigid bracewear was used, and the comments toward the rigid bracewear were also investigated. With the use of 3D body scanner, the 3D body geometry of the patients was obtained and analysed. The 3D models of the subjects at 3 visits over a period of 3 to 6 months were extracted, aligned and compared by using a reverse engineering software so as to evaluate the changes in the geometry and symmetry of the body. Results indicated that the use of rigid bracewear associates with major changes to the torso geometry. Significant changes in the cross-sectional profile of the body are also found. The 3D body scanning technology provides important information on the geometry of the body and quantification of spinal deformity in clinical practices so as to allow more frequent evaluation of orthotic intervention for effective and optimal treatment. Traditional orthotic materials are heavy in weight, bulky and completely unbreathable, which reduce the quality of life, comfort and satisfaction with the orthosis and result in poor patient compliance and even significant curve progression. This study explores the practical use of carbon fibre, fibreglass and fibreglass-carbon composites to develop an orthotic brace. Apart from the mechanical testing, the thermal discomfort properties and in-brace pressure were also examined. Compared to traditional thermoplastic materials, the use of fibre composite materials in orthoses not only improves the prevailing problems of wear discomfort, but also facilitates the control of interface pressures and corrective forces, thus enhancing the quality of orthotic intervention. A new adaptive corset has been developed through new fabrications of fibre composite materials and designs which improves the physiological and thermal comfort of patients, and reliably exert corrective pressures to control spine curvatures, as a means of early management of spinal deformity. A 3D model of the trunk has also been developed based on the typical geometry of a scoliotic patient in this study, to simulate the skin-brace interface pressure in relation to the fabrication material properties and the geometry of the torso by using Finite Element model. The simulation model not only provides a promising solution to the modification of materials for orthotic bracewear by predicting and visualising skin-brace interface pressure patterns, but also effectively optimises the design and development process of orthotic bracewear without the need to fabricate and test the bracewear in a series of wear trials.

529812.label: Major findings and research outcome
529812.value: 1. The pressures induced by orthotic bracewear considerably changed during daily activities. When the spine grows (height and body size increase), the induced pressures also fluctuated. Determining the optimal pressure in relation to the model rectifications and deviations is crucial in the treatment of spinal deformity. Changes in body posture have resulted in statistically significant alterations in the exerted forces. 2. Traditional tests on orthotic materials neglect the importance of thermal properties in orthotic treatment which affect the rate of compliance. By considering the prolonged use and hygiene factors of orthotic braces, orthotic materials with good heat and moisture transmission properties not only provide wearers with more comfort without feelings of dampness, but also control bacteria from exponentially multiplying inside the brace environment. This study therefore provides insights on the prevailing problem of thermal discomfort with traditional orthotic materials and the potential use of carbon fibre and fibreglass composites in spinal orthotic treatment to exert adequate amounts of corrective pressure onto anatomic locations, thus reducing cumbersomeness and improving ventilation. 3. The use of a 3D body scanning system can evaluate changes in the torso geometry of patients with scoliosis. The body images and the dimensions obtained with measurements taken during a six month period of time can be quantitatively compared, thus serving as a means to evaluate the progress of orthotic intervention during the course of treatment. The scans also show that brace intervention causes significant changes in the cross-sectional profile of the body, which may be attributed to the fit, torso anthropometry and force distribution of the rigid bracewear. Therefore, an intuitive understanding of the deformation of the body geometry is imperative for enhancing treatment efficacy. Surface topography assessment consequently provides a safe, quick and consistent extraction of the body dimensions for evaluating the symmetry of the cross-sections of the body so as to make effective adjustments of the brace in terms of its corrective forces. 4. An adaptive corset for spine support is developed through new fabrications and designs with the aim of improving the physiological comfort of patients, and accurately and reliably exerting suitable corrective forces to control the progression of spinal deformation. 5. A biomechanical model that simulates the brace-torso interface pressure in relation to the fabrication material properties and 3D geometry of the body shape has been formulated to evaluate the accuracy of fit and efficiency of support, choice of fabrication materials and effectiveness of various design modifications to the bracewear.

529812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
529812.value: Orthotic bracewear is commonly used to treat patients with spinal deformities. It aims to mechanically control and modify abnormal curvatures and rotation of the spine. However, associated problems, such as discomfort, activity limitations and bulkiness, induce a low rate of patient compliance, and thus the curve may progress to the point of significant physical deformity and even cardiopulmonary problems. As early management of spinal deformity, the adaptive corset developed in this study provides the option of a less intrusive orthotic treatment for children with a small and simple curvature, as opposed to observation, bracing and surgery. On the basis of the biomechanical model, the orthotic pressures and corrective forces can be precisely and effectively simulated and hence, strategically applied onto the 3 anatomical locations, so as to facilitate the 3D design and geometry of orthoses, as well as the choice of suitable fabrication materials for optimal fit and comfort.

529812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
529812.value: This project aims to design and develop an adaptive corset that can provide adequate support to control curve progression and poor posture of children with early signs of spinal deformities, and thus preserve their growth and quality of life for normal daily life activities. A novel approach of embedding 3D carbon fibre reinforcement composites into the corset was employed. The dimensions used address the needs of scoliosis children, practical use and clinical procedures of the orthotic treatment, analyses of body-orthosis interface pressure levels and contact conditions of the orthosis in relation to spine curvatures and body anthropometry. Scientific characterization of the 3D geometry of spinal orthoses and a thorough understanding of the mechanical and stress-strain properties of fabrication materials, as well as deformations of reinforcement materials were carried out. Biomechanical model of skin-brace pressure simulation was formulated. Corset fabrication and structural features when the adaptive corset is applied were formulated. The outcomes of the project will advance our knowledge on the design or elements of orthoses by incorporating modern textiles technologies. More importantly, the project can provide the option of less intrusive orthotic treatment to children with small and simple curvatures as opposed to observation, bracing and surgery.

530012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
530012.value: Marine traffic flow modelling is needed to establish the next generation of vessel traffic services (VTSs), especially in a busy port like Hong Kong. Recent advances in navigation technology have enabled marine traffic flow to be better analysed, providing a basis for the development of better models. Marine traffic has its special features and is fundamentally different from highway, air and pedestrian traffic. Although traffic science has been a prolific field for these latter modes of traffic, the existing understanding of traffic is not very helpful with regard to the marine situation. Some assumptions of many traffic models are significantly violated in marine traffic, such as the presence of traffic heterogeneity and the influence of water currents. For example, the manoeuvrability of a ship is largely related to its length, which can range from a few metres to over 300 metres, while highway vehicle lengths are limited to about 20 metres. Therefore, in marine traffic, heterogeneity of vessels clearly exists in terms of varying ship manoeuvrability. Marine traffic management in busy waterways is a new issue, but the first guideline for VTSs was adopted internationally in 1985. VTSs are used in ports and international waterways. The potential conflict among several ships becomes critical for either high density or highly heterogeneous traffic. Consequently, this proposed study will contribute to establishing the next generation of VTSs by analysing and modelling saturated marine traffic. While new navigation aids (e.g., ECDIS, AIS) may enhance port safety, we will investigate marine traffic flow models both from a theoretical perspective and using numerical experiments. In the proposed study, we will conduct a survey of marine traffic in busy waterways in Hong Kong port and determine field values of marine traffic characteristics. We will then develop theoretical models for studying marine traffic flow using classical traffic theories, which should provide a better understanding of the phenomenon of marine traffic flow in water currents. The marine traffic flow model will be developed based on this new understanding of marine traffic characteristics, and will be verified numerically in the study. The new model should provide substantial benefits to the operation of vessel traffic services in congested waterways, including the enhancement of marine traffic safety.

530012.label: Major findings and research outcome
530012.value: This project is one of the first attempts to extend the traffic flow theory to marine traffic problems. With the recent development of the Automatic Identification System (AIS), abundant marine traffic data has been collated. In our analysis, we have analysed the three fundamental variables of traffic flow. We conclude that marine traffic flow is very similar to highway traffic flow but does not fully fit any existing known fundamental relationships (Huang, Yip and Wen, 2016). A macroscopic model of marine traffic in waterways has been analysed (Yip, 2013). A MPhil student studied the relationship of marine traffic and port characteristics, which contributes the theoretical analysis (Yang 2016). The traffic flow model of marine traffic is applied as hypothetical models to study the different actual situations associated with marine traffic. A passing planning system has been proposed for vessel traffic control (Yip, 2015). The planning of new canal is presented by considering the marine traffic (Yip and Wong, 2015). Numerical experiments with actual and market data have been conducted to study the regional emissions from ships (Chen, Yip, Mou, 2016). Green routing of ships has been analyzed with actual field data (Wen, Gen, Yip, and Wu, 2016).

530112.label: Project Objectives
530112.value: Set up a test platform with suitable testcases using image-source based room simulators. The transfer functions will be extracted and will be incorporated into our previous developed model-based multi-dimensional beamformer design algorithms. Different array configurations will be studied and signal performance indicators will be derived to assess the designs. Study the wave-based models for room acoustic simulation. In particular, the finite difference scheme will be employed. We will study the presence of obstacles via transpiration, and look at the potential impact of viscous and wall effect. Based on selected testcases, we will explore systematic ways of finding the best implementation from user-defined performance requirements and constraints in order to develop a mixed room acoustic simulator. Use the room simulator to study the sensitivity of various design parameters. The foremost errors could be deviations in microphone locations. We will study the robustness of the designed beamformers and propose relevant robust optimization methods. Furthermore, we will study more advanced optimization problems such as optimal placement of microphone elements. The designs can be enhanced significantly by changing array configurations and optimize on the microphone locations at the same time with the filter coefficients. Novel global optimal design formulations will be posed and solution techniques will be developed for solving the problems.

530112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
530112.value: In this project, we consider the design of indoor acoustic noise reduction systems based on distributed microphone arrays integrated with a room acoustic simulator. Apart from communications, it has a lot of potential applications in voice control devices deployed in intelligent home or for factory automation. Being a natural interface between human and machine, speech recognition engine has already been integrated into many telecommunication systems like call centres and mobile phones, including the more recent iPhone’s siri system. The market is predicted to have an annual growth rate of 14.5 percent. Products embedded with multiple microphones are also emerging and being built into notebook computers. Voice control feature is an attractive functionality that can be added to many products like electrical appliances. It provides a natural mean of remote control making the products more user-friendly. However, in real environments like living rooms or factories, speech signals picked up by a microphone can be very difficult to analyze because of other acoustic noise including reverberation. The performance of the speech recognition engine diminishes rapidly when there is a mismatch between the training and testing conditions. There is a pressing need to conduct research on achieving front-end signal enhancement devices in the presence of not just simple, additive random noise, but reverberant and interfering noise. With the advancement of room acoustic simulators, geometry-based and wave-based models have been studied extensively in the literature to predict realistic sound field and the reverberation effect can be modelled fairly accurately. However, very few dedicated beamformers exist currently which are designed with the use of room acoustic simulators. In fact, every room has different characteristics, generic designs may not perform well and the potential has not been explored fully. Furthermore, both geometric and wave-based models have advantages and limitations; it has not been fully explored to combine the strengths of both approaches for a better room simulator. In view of this, we propose to develop a fast and accuracy room simulator and integrate it into the design system for getting better dedicated indoor beamformers. High performance computing techniques including the use of FPGA and GPU will also be investigated. We would select and focus on some specific acoustic applications, suitable beamforming algorithms fulfilling the required performances and user constraints are then developed together with the optimal positioning of microphones. The deliverables include novel designs of indoor beamforming systems implemented on FPGA and GPU. 在这个项目中，基于分布式的麦克风阵列和室内语音模拟器，我们考虑了室内语音环境下的噪声消除系统的设计。它还有很多潜在的应用，除了在通讯中的应用之外，还有在智能家居配置的声控设备的应用或者工厂的自动化应用。作为人与机器之间最简单自然的交互信息，语音识别模块已经集合到很多电信系统中，如呼叫中心和移动电话，包括了最新的iPhone的siri系统。这个市场每年的增长率预计达到14.5%。嵌入多个麦克风的产品也正在涌现，且正移植到笔记本电脑里。声控的特性是一个很有吸引力的功能，以致于它能嵌入到很多电子应用产品中。它提供了一种很自然的遥控方式，使得产品显得更人性化。然而，在诸如客厅或工厂的现实环境里，分析麦克风所接收到的语音信号是很困难的，这是因为中间夹杂着很多噪声，其中包括了回声。当测试的环境与模拟训练的环境不匹配时，语音识别模块的性能就会下降的很快。这就非常迫切的需要从事在有回声而不仅仅是简单的随机噪声的环境下，如何达到最好的信号增强效果的前沿研究。 对于室内语音模拟器的发展，基于几何的模型和基于波动的模型已经在文献中有着广泛的研究。它被用来预测现实的声场，回声效应也相对准确。但是，在室内语音模拟器的环境中，很少能设计专门的波束形成器。实际上，每个房间有着不同的特征，一般设计的效果并不好，潜在的性能并没有充分得以发挥。另外，这两种模型各有优点和局限性，还没有充分利用两者的长处得出一个更好的室内模拟器。考虑到这点，我们计划发展快速精确的室内模拟器，并且将它集合到系统的设计中，以得出更好的特定室内波束形成器。我们也会研究高性能计算的方法和技巧，包括了FPGA和GPU的使用。我们将选取并专注于某些具体的语音应用，发展适当的波束形成算法，解决麦克风的最优摆放问题，从而得出所需的性能，并满足用户的限制条件。具体的实现包括了在FPGA和GPU上运行的室内波束形成系统的创新设计。

530112.label: Realisation of objectives
530112.value: In this project, our main objectives are to investigate different beamforming signal enhancement algorithms for indoor applications. We want to study model-based approach together with room acoustic models. We also want to study more advanced optimization techniques for the designs and study the influence of the array configurations on the performance of the beamformers. Finally, we want to investigate the deployment of the designed beamformers in practical applications, including assistive hearing instruments and accurate voice control devices. Following the objectives of the proposal, we have published 12 journal papers and 4 conference presentations to achieve all the objectives. To summarize, the research team has been investigating different indoor beamforming signal enhancement algorithms. In particular, the use of acoustic models in constructing broadband beamformers has been studied. Influence of array configurations and various beamforming algorithms have been explored. We have explored early and late reverberations in order to enhance the beamformer performance. Also, the optimization problem is of large-scale and we have studied low complexity algorithms to tackle the problems. Applications including assistive hearing instruments and accurate voice control have been investigated. To summarize, we have achieved the following: In the design process, one way to obtain a beamformer is to formulate the problem as an optimization problem to get close to a given target response function. In the formulation, a signal propagation model is assumed so that the beamformer response can be calculated. It is worth noting that most of the previous works on near-field beamformer design are based on the assumption that the defined system is in the free-field, where some explicit form of transfer function can be used to describe the sound wave propagation, such as the Green’s function for the Helmholtz equation. However, in many indoor applications, reflections of sound waves by walls, ceiling and floor are commonly occurred which create reverberant environments. Several geometrical methods have been developed to simulate the acoustic field of enclosed area, such as the ray tracing method and the image source method (ISM). The ISM technique is a simple but efficient approach for simulating room acoustics. More recently, a fast-ISM implementation scheme is developed, which provides a tool to synthesize room impulse responses (RIRs) in an efficient manner, and the resulting impulse responses can be used to describe the acoustic environment while only requiring a fraction of the computation time. By employing a method based on the image source method (ISM) to estimate the room impulse response function, the beamformer design problem is formulated as a semi-infinite optimization problem and indoor beamformers have been successfully designed. We have also studied the generalized sidelobe canceller (GSC) beamformer. In addition, when a room acoustic model is employed in the study to extract the effect of reverberation, we found that the overall reverberation cannot be reduced uniformly. If the pattern of the reverberation is separated into the early and late reflections, the problem is of a multi-criteria nature and it is advantageous to optimize them separately. We have formulated the design problem as multi-criteria optimization problems and showed that better beamformers could be designed for dereverberation. Another acoustic model is based on computational aeroacoustics. Indeed acoustic fluctuations are regarded as weak perturbation of density and pressure in the continuum. The governing equations for the fluid flow are the unsteady compressible Navier-Stokes equations with the equation of state of perfect gas. The time-domain impulse response estimation can be calculated by solving 2-D unsteady compressible N-S equations under the numerical platform Conservation Element/Solution Element (CE/SE). In addition to the accuracy, this method can also handle obstacles by discretizing the domain surrounding the object and imposing boundary conditions suitably. We demonstrated with examples that obstacles would affect the performance of the designed beamfomers. We formulate the optimal design problem with suitable estimated impulse response functions accounting for the reflected waves and show that the performance of the designs can be improved. In considering designing beamformers with different configurations, we have studied the performance limit for which the objective function is driven to zero. We show that it is essential to use both the filter length and the number of sensors in reducing the cost function to zero, subject to some conditions on the desired response. In order to investigate acoustic applications and novel global optimal design formulations, the optimization for voice control device is considered. It is well known that under a strong near-field noise with very low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), the performance of speech recognition is deteriorated significantly. A universal estimator based on neural network has been proposed to enhance the recognition accuracy of microcontrollers by integrating better signals processed by various noise suppression ﬁlters, where a global optimization algorithm, namely an intelligent particle swarm optimization, is used to optimize the inbuilt parameters of the neural network in order to maximize accuracy of speech recognition microcontrollers working within noisy environments. Another hybrid descent method has been developed for the design of the sigmoid filters, which can effectively enhance noisy speech using simple computational operations, while a robust estimator based on an adaptive-network-based fuzzy inference system is used to determine the appropriate operational parameters for the sigmoid function in order to produce effective speech enhancement under variant noisy conditions. Another application on source localization using semi-definite programming has been studied. Similar technique has been applied for the localization of sound sources for different configurations of beamformers. Finally, the design of assistive hearing instruments have been studied, which have a significant impact on speech enhancement when the signal-to-noise ratio is low. The overall speech quality of the assistive hearing instruments may be reduced, as the noise segments still cannot be filtered out. We have studied a new approach to simultaneously boost the speech segments and suppress noise segments in noisy speech. Experimental results with different types of real-world noise indicate that the proposed method achieves better speech quality than does the conventional method. The resulting method provides an improved functionality for assistive hearing instruments. In the realization of filters in reducing the complexity in hardware implementation, we have introduced the notion of integer space generated by the power-of-two space and formulated a more general integer programming problem, which can be employed to design finite precision filters via manifold optimization techniques. In the development of design optimization algorithms, a fast method based on the window functions has been proposed to handle the large-scale nature of the design problem when the discretization points grows and the filter length increases.

530112.label: Major findings and research outcome
530112.value: In the formulation of indoor beamformers, in order to handle reflections of sound waves, the image source method (ISM) is applied to synthesize room impulse responses (RIRs) for the signal propagation model, so that beamformer responses can be calculated and optimized to approach a given target response function. Indoor beamformers have been successfully designed by the least-squares approach [9.1, 8.1]. The indoor generalized sidelobe canceller (GSC) beamformer has also been studied [9.2]. In fact, if the pattern of the reverberation is separated into the early and late reflections, the problem is of a multi-criteria nature and it is advantageous to optimize them separately. We have formulated the design problem as multi-criteria optimization problems [9.3] [8.6]. We showed that better beamformers could be designed for dereverberation. We have also developed another acoustic model based on computational aeroacoustics, in which the time-domain impulse response estimation can be calculated by solving 2-D unsteady compressible N-S equations. This method can also handle obstacles by discretizing the domain surrounding the object and imposing boundary conditions suitably. We demonstrated with examples that obstacles would affect the performance of the designed beamfomers [9.4] [8.9]. In considering array configurations, we have studied the performance limit for which the objective function is driven to zero. We show that it is essential to use both the filter length and the number of sensors in reducing the cost function to zero, subject to some conditions on the desired response [8.12]. In order to investigate applications and novel global optimal design formulations, the optimization for voice control device is considered. An intelligent particle swarm optimization together with a universal estimator based on neural network is proposed [8.3]. Also, a robust estimator based on an adaptive-network-based fuzzy inference system has been proposed [8.4]. A hybrid descent method has also been developed for the design of the sigmoid filters [8.10]. Another application on source localization using semi-definite programming [8.2] has been studied. Similar technique has been applied for the localization of sound sources for different configurations of beamformers [8.11]. Finally, design of assistive hearing instruments have been studied [8.8]. In the realization of filters, manifold optimization techniques [8.5] is proposed which can potentially applied to design finite precision filters in the power-of-two space. In order to handle large-scale multi-dimensional designs, a fast method based on the window functions is proposed [8.7], which can design beamformers with very long filters.

530112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
530112.value: In the present project, we have studied the design of indoor beamforming designs with the image source method and the computational aeroacoustics to integrate reverberant impulse response functions directly. It would be of interest to investigate dedicated hardware platforms so that the computation of the impulse response functions can be carried out in a parallel fashion and the design process can be more interactive. Also, the influence of the array configuration on the overall performance is important. It would be of importance to explore further the geometry of the configurations and more global optimization algorithms for solving the non-convex design problem. Finally, it is advantageous to consider different noise background and to investigate possible optimal beamformer for each type of background.

530112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
530112.value: This project concerns the design of indoor acoustic noise reduction systems based on microphone arrays integrated with a room acoustic simulator. This noise reduced acoustic interface has many important applications and has a lot of potential as a natural control of electrical and electronic appliances for intelligent home or factory automation applications. In many situations, it is important to deploy a microphone array to enhance the required speech signal using beamforming and noise cancelling techniques. In addition, in real environments like living rooms or factories, speech signals picked up by a microphone can be very difficult to analyze because of other acoustic noise including reverberation. The performance of the speech recognition engine diminishes rapidly when there is a mismatch between the training and testing conditions. Here, We have proposed novel formulations and have designed several novel indoor beamformer systems via various optimization techniques. The effect of reverberation has been studied extensively, and the influence of array configurations has also been looked at. After a careful optimization process, the designed algorithms have improved the designs significantly. Applications such as assistive hearing instruments have been studied.

530212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
530212.value: 空間數據庫的索引自動化性能調整

530212.label: Project Objectives
530212.value: Design of tuning techniques for tuning the spatial index size. The query/update cost of a spatial index depends heavily on the index size. By detecting objects with similar movement patterns and treating them as groups, a compact index can be used to manage the groups while preserving the filtering effectiveness of the index. We will design lightweight techniques for detecting groups from their movement patterns. We will also develop tuning operations for incorporating these groups into a spatial index. Investigation of tuning techniques for spatial indexes in commercial spatial database systems. Commercial spatial database systems only support certain spatial indexes. We will develop specific tuning operations for these spatial indexes such that their performance adapts to the incoming workload in online fashion. The indexes should offer low update cost when updates become frequent, and they should provide low query cost when frequent queries emerge. We will also analyze the impact of these tuning operations on the spatial indexes. Development of tuning techniques for road network indexes. In a road network application, the workload includes shortest path queries and live traffic updates of road segments. Existing road network indexes have specific, fixed query/update costs and cannot adapt to a dynamic workload. We will design techniques for adapting the performance of a road network index with respect to the workload. We will also study tuning techniques for a workload with advanced path queries, e.g., reachability queries.

530212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
530212.value: Spatial databases are deployed to process incoming workloads on spatial objects in many location-based applications, e.g., inventory management in ports and warehouses, and the management of fleets of vehicles. It is important to tune the database performance because such applications face potentially massive workloads containing: (i) location updates that are issued from objects (e.g., containers) as they move and (ii) spatial queries that are issued by users (e.g., warehouse staff) to find objects in specified regions. A spatial database administrator can build a spatial index on the data objects for processing queries efficiently; however, the index may incur significant overhead on location updates. The conventional rule is that the administrator should build an index when the workload is query-intensive and should drop the index when the workload becomes update-intensive. This project aims at developing automatic performance tuning techniques for spatial indexes. The dynamic nature of spatial workloads poses new challenges to the traditional “build-or-drop index” approach. First, the amount of queries and updates in the workload varies along time and across different regions. This renders it difficult to decide whether to build or drop a spatial index in advance. Second, the problem is complicated by the bursts of updates and queries in the workloads. For example, bursts of updates emerge when containers/goods arrive at a port or warehouse, and bursts of queries appear in certain regions due to shift of interests, sudden events, e.g., accidents. It is expensive to build and drop an index frequently for dealing with these bursts. Third, in road network applications (e.g., fleet management), the workloads also include traffic updates on roads, e.g., congestion, closure, and re-opening of roads, which affect travel times among different locations on the road network. Unpredictable traffic makes it challenging to tune the performance. Although extensive work has been conducted on spatial indexing, there is only little work on tuning the performance of spatial indexes. We fill this research gap and enable spatial indexes to accommodate dynamic workloads by self-tuning. This research project aims to investigate: (i) techniques for tuning the spatial index size, (ii) tuning techniques for spatial indexes in commercial spatial databases, (iii) tuning techniques for road network indexes, (iv) performance evaluation and prototype tuning tool. Real workloads will be collected for evaluating the execution time and workload throughput of our techniques. This project will benefit location-based applications and will result in index tuning techniques of relevance for commercial spatial databases. 許多位置應用程序採用空間數據庫處理空間物件的工作負載，例如港口管理，倉庫庫存管理，車隊管理。這類應用面臨著巨大的工作量：（一）物件隨著移動的位置更新和（二）用戶發出的空間查詢。所以調整數據庫的性能很重要。空間數據庫的管理員可建立空間索引以加快處理查詢，但是該索引會減慢處理位置更新。據傳統方法，工作量是查詢密集時應建立索引，而工作量變為更新密集時應刪除索引。 本項目旨在開發自動技術以調整空間索引性能。空間工作負載的動態特性引起新的挑戰，使傳統的“建立刪除索引方法”變得不適用。首先，在不同的區域和時間，工作負載的查詢和更新的數量是不同的。因此很難提前決定應建立或刪除空間索引。第二，工作負荷的更新和查詢爆發使問題變為複雜。例如，集裝箱/貨物到達港口/倉庫時引起更新爆發，突發事件和趨勢的轉移導致查詢爆發。為處理這些爆發而經常建立和刪除索引是昂貴的。第三，在道路網中的應用（如車隊管理），工作負載還包括交通的更新，例如交通擁堵，關閉，重開的道路。這影響道路網絡上的駕駛時間。不可預測的交通令這個問題變得更複雜。 雖然已有大量的空間索引研究，很少研究考慮調整空間索引性能的技術。我們填補這方面的研究空白，使空間索引自我調整以適應動態工作負載。本研究項目旨在探討：（一）調整空間索引大小的技術，（二）商業空間數據庫中的索引調整技術，（三）道路網絡的索引調整技術，（四）建立原型調整工具和評估效果。我們將收集現實的工作負以載評估我們技術的執行時間和工作負載處理速率。本項目將有利於位置應用程序，並促進相關的商業空間數據庫索引調整技術。

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
530212.value: Location-based applications, e.g., inventory management in ports and warehouses, and the management of fleets of vehicles, have important contributions to the Hong Kong economy. These applications deploy a spatial database system to manage the locations of objects of interests (e.g., vehicles, goods) and process incoming workloads, which contain: (i) location updates that are reported by objects when they move, and (ii) spatial queries that are issued by users for finding objects within certain regions. The above applications will face increasingly large and potentially massive workloads so it is important to optimize the performance of the spatial database system. The outcome of this research project will have significant impact on transportation and logistics applications, e.g., fleet vehicle management and inventory management in ports and warehouses. Our techniques aim to process efficiently the dynamic workloads faced by such applications. Furthermore, this project will advance tuning techniques in the area of spatial databases, and it will develop tuning techniques relevant for commercial spatial database systems.

530612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
530612.value: Bra is the most important daily apparel for women’s comfort and support. Nevertheless, the bra wearers have limited knowledge of fit, so they tend to adopt compensatory body postures that often cause muscular or skeletal problems. No academic research has investigated the interactive dynamic effects of biomechanical properties (tissue stiffness, thickness, density, shear modulus, Poisson’s ratio and viscous damping ratio) and textile parameters (thickness, density, tensile, shear, bending and compression modulus) on the quality of bra fit (absence of gap, bulging, digging or wrinkle; level of push-in and push-up; pressure sensation and shape appearance). This project proposes a holistic approach to understand bra fitting from a scientific perspective and to correlate this with the subjective assessment. The challenge is to build engineering algorithms to simulate the multi-axial forces and deformations acting on breasts by multiple thin layers of elastic materials. To build the Finite Element (FE) models with true geometrical body data, it requires inter-institutional and interdisciplinary combinations of research expertise including 3D photogrammetry, image processing, material science, mechanical engineering, intimate apparel technology, and biomechanical engineering. To facilitate the fitting experiments, a series of changeable bra components will be prepared for flexible replacement and tension adjustment. Objectively derived data of the viscoelastic breasts and elastic bra materials will be used to develop the nonlinear Finite Element (FE) models to quantify the 3D static and dynamic fitting performance (contact area, deformation, stress distribution and frictional forces) of everyday bra for 48 subjects in 16 groups of breast sizes from 70A to 85D. This project will deliver new-generation unique solutions for the difficult simulation problems in the contact mechanics between elastic materials and viscoelastic breast tissues to simulate the dynamic fitting performance of different bra settings. It will also provide an interesting direction for the future research of 3D Computer-Aided-Design (CAD) of functional soft goods including shoes, school bags, sofa, beds etc. In the long run, it can enable a big leap forward in apparel CAD applications and increase Hong Kong’s competitive advantages in the global fashion business. It also has the potential for bidding for non-RGC funding to develop textile sensors for bra fitting evaluation, or a handheld device to help women to choose their bras with correct textile parameters for better fit in various situations such as breastfeeding, post-surgery or sports exercises such as yoga, jogging and dancing. This will bring long-term benefits to women’s health and their families’ well-being. 文胸是婦女最重要的日常服裝，必須舒適和具承托力。不過，婦女對穿對文胸的知識很有限，往往會採取補償體位，故容易引起肌肉或骨骼的問題。在學術界，還沒有文獻提及生物力學和紡織品參數之間的互動動態,也未有對文胸給予乳房組織的舒適、合身、塑身和承托力方面的效果作出硏究。現今文胸的合身很大程度是取決於經驗者主觀判斷。這硏究的目的是發展出一個全面的方法, 以科學的角度去了解文胸合身的數據, 並和主觀判斷作出關聯。為了文胸合身的硏究, 我們會製作一套具創意的「裝嵌式文胸」。從粘彈性的乳房和文胸物料得出的客觀數據,會用作發展非綫性有限元模型,去量化三維文胸在不同體型的乳房和彈性物料之間的接觸面積、變形、壓力分佈和摩擦力。

530612.label: Major findings and research outcome
530612.value: 1) Simulated the stress distribution between soft breasts and elastic bras. [Ouput 3] The magnitude of average bra-body contact pressure is 1 kPa. Higher pressure is found on the neck, bra neckline and underband, rather than the cups. The bra-body contact mechanism has been explained in details. 2) Built an FE body sub-model with nonlinear materials. [Ouput 1 & 2] Using a breast free vibration experiment, a piecewise mass-spring-damper model was developed to estimate the spring constant and damping coefficients of the effective mass of upper breast and lower breast respectively. The nonlinear material model was used for the FE breast sub-model, but the thorax sub-model used the rigid material. A subject wearing the best-fit bra was scanned, then the geometric body model was developed. The 3D geometric model of the thorax and the soft breasts were reconstructed. The FE body sub-model was developed using tetrahedron element type for the real body geometry. 3) Built an FE bra sub-model. [Ouput 2 & 3] The outline of the bra was extracted from 3D bra geometric model. The FE bra sub-model was developed based on the geometric model of a good fit bra. The material properties of the material model were input in terms of Young’s modulus, Mooney coefficients C10, C01, and Poisson ratio. The bra part used shell elements and the gore, cup edges, strap & band edges all used truss elements 4) Built a contact sub-model [Ouput 3] A glue contact condition was set between the breast and thorax, and touching contact was set between the body and the bra to allow relative sliding of the bodies in the contact interface. The FE contact model involves a "target surface" of the thorax and the bra, to touch with a "contact surface" of the Mooney body. 5) To validate the FE models. [Ouput 3] The simulated pressure distribution was validated with the pressure test experimental data. The magnitude of average bra-body contact pressure is also 1 kPa.

530612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
530612.value: This completed project provided an important basis for further development in this niche research area of finite element analysis of the bra-body mechanical interaction. Two more GRF projects have been granted to extend this work by the same research team. The FE Project 2 is to apply finite element modelling to simulate the shaping effects of different designs of bra components such as wires, gore, cups and straps. The FE project 3 is to optimize the fabric modulus in the design of sports bras with the best comfort pressure and support during running exercise.

530612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
530612.value: This project is the first work successfully applied the nonlinear finite element (FE) modelling of the contact biomechanics between a woman’s soft body and a wired bra composed of a pair of fabric cups, rigid gores and wires, and elastic bands and straps. The FE software was used to build the FE body/bra/contact sub-models. The 3D body-scanned point cloud imported to the Image processing software was used to mesh a geometrical model. A breast free falling experiment was used to determine the nonlinear material properties of a living woman’s breasts. The bra sub-model was developed with pre-tension and nonlinear material properties for the fabric. The FE Interference Fit algorithm was used to achieve the surface-to-surface contact and to predict the 3D mechanical results such as stress distribution.

531212.label: Project Objectives

531212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
531212.value: Hybrid supercapacitors (HSCs) have attracted much research interest due to their potential of high energy and high power density. The bottleneck for HSCs is the development of novel electrodes with a large specific surface area facilitating ultrafast and highly reversible redox reactions occurring on the surfaces of active materials. Electrospinning is a simple and versatile method of producing ultra-thin nanofibers with very high specific surface area and aspect ratio from a wide variety of active materials. This project aims to develop high-performance, environmentally benign and cost-effective HSC devices from electrospun TiO2-based composite nanofibers. The proposal has three main parts: (i) design and optimization of electrospinning parameters to control the composition, structure and morphology of TiO2-based composite nanofibers; (ii) characterization of the structural, morphological, compositional, electronic and ionic conductivity of synthesized TiO2-based composite nanofibers; and (iii) design, assembly, electrochemical characterization and optimization of HSC devices using TiO2-based composite nanofibers. We will use electrospinning to synthesize composite nanofibers based on TiO2 incorporated with highly electrically conductive carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and highly capacitive NiO and Fe3O4. By tuning the electrospinning parameters we will control the composition, structure, morphology, diameter and length of TiO2-based composite nanofibers. These physical characteristics and the electronic and ionic conductivities of the nanofibers will be characterized systematically to provide feedback information for optimizing the electrospinning parameters. TiO2-based composite nanofibers will be used to assemble HSC devices. The electrochemical properties of the HSCs, i.e., volumetric and gravimetric capacitance and energy density, high rate capability and continuous cycling stability, will be investigated. The characterization results will be input into the optimization process of the composite nanofiber electrodes. The final target of the proposal is to develop the next-generation high-efficiency energy storage devices possessing durability and high energy and power density. 杂化型超级电容器是最具发展前景的新一代绿色能源储存与转化技术之一。本项目拟用同轴静电纺丝技术构筑含过渡金属氧化物(Fe3O4,NiO) 和纳米碳管的多孔TiO2/C基系列芯鞘式纳米结构复合纤维，用作高稳定性、高容量和高功率杂化超级电容器(HSCs)电极材料。通过调节静电纺丝参数(电场强度、喷头的类型和流速等)和纺丝溶液的物理性质(高分子聚合物模板的类型、电导率、粘度等)以及后续的热处理参数来控制复合纤维的成分、尺寸、形貌以及孔结构等特性；通过组装HSCs器件来表征其比容量、比功率和循环稳定性等电化学性能。探索电纺参数、纤维成分、结构和TiO2/C 基芯鞘式复合纤维电极材料电化学性能之间的定量构效关系模型。揭示具有高容量、高倍率、长寿命电极材料的基本规律，为设计与开发新一代杂化型超级电容器电极材料提供重要的理论指导。

531212.label: Realisation of objectives
531212.value: Rechargeable LIBs are regarded as a promising power source for electronic devices such as electric vehicles and hybrid electric vehicles. Graphite, as the most intensely used commercial anode material, has a low theoretical capacity of 372 mAh/g, which makes it difficult to meet the demanding for high energy density in energy storage systems. Recently, Sn has been widely studied as an anode material for LIBs due to its high theoretical capacity of 991 mAh/g. However, the rapid fading of capacity that results from the great change in volume during the alloying-dealloying reaction between Sn and Li renders the achievement of a long cycle life difficult. Recent years, great efforts have been devoted to solve the above issues by (a) engineering nanostructure to reduce the volume expansion; (b) incorporating Sn with other phases, including carbon and titanium dioxide (TiO2), not only to prevent the aggregation of Sn but serve as buffer scaffold. Nevertheless, long-term cycling performance of the existing Sn-based anode remains unsatisfactory. To obtain desirable cycling performance, our objective is to scrupulously design a robust porous one-dimensional (1D) TiO2-x-carbon (TiO2-x-C) substrate to encapsulate Sn nanoparticles, in which the firm TiO2-x-C substrate can fully absorb the volume expansion of the Sn nanoparticles in the TiO2-x-C substrate during charging-discharging processes which can be directly observed by in situ TEM and thus achieve a long life. In this project, for the first time, a novel approach of lithiation-induced insertion of Sn nanoparticles into the pores of the highly stable TiO2-x-C nanofiber substrates is presented, which can effectively localize the Sn nanoparticles and allow superior performance. In situ TEM was performed to characterize the structural evolution of the prepared material during the charging and discharging processes. It was found that Li4.4Sn alloy was inserted into the pores surrounding the initial Sn nanoparticles in the TiO2-x-C nanofibers by its large volume expansion. The initial Sn nanoparticle with diameter of about 150 nm could not be recovered after discharging due to the surface absorption between smaller separated Sn nanoparticles and TiO2-x-C substrate. These detached Sn nanoparticles remained in the pores which are able to accommodate their expansions, thus yielding a very long cycle life. During the project study, the Ti(OiPr)4-polystyrene-tin(II)2-ethylhexanoate fibers were synthesized through simple electrospinning. The electrospun Ti(OiPr)4-polystyrene- tin(II)2-ethylhexanoate fibers were treated at 450 ºC in an atmosphere of N2 to obtain porous TiO2-C-SnOx, in which part of the polystyrene turned into carbon and others were burnt out to form pores, followed by treatment in a mixture of C2H2/H2/Ar at 700 °C to achieve porous TiO2-x-C-Sn composite nanofibers. Some parts of the Ti4+ were reduced to Ti3+ by heating in a hydrogen atmosphere, which resulted in the presence of oxygen vacancies and Ti3+ species and thus effectively improved the electrical conductivity of TiO2. In situ TEM was used to observe the structural evolution of the prepared material during the processes of charging and discharging. A typical morphological evolution of Sn nanoparticles encapsulated in the porous TiO2-x-C nanofiber during the first five charging and discharging processes was observed. Obvious volume expansion occurred after the first lithiation,. Apparently, the pores surrounding the Sn nanoparticles in the composite nanofiber were able to absorb the expansion of the Sn nanoparticles without inducing a change in the volume of the TiO2-x-C composite nanofiber substrate, proving the firmness and excellent mechanical properties of TiO2-x-C matrix. The uniform dark contrast of Sn nanoparticles became lighter with the reaction processing. The Sn nanoparticles underwent a volume change of approximately 260 % at the completion of the first charging process. The lithium was gradually extracted from the Li-Sn alloys when the process of delithiation began. The Sn nanoparticles separated into smaller particles after the first discharging process due to the surface absorption force between Sn nanoparticle and TiO2-x-C substrate. The separated Sn nanoparticles did not recover their original volume after the second lithiation. The smaller Sn nanoparticles remained in the pores toward which the initial Sn nanoparticles expanded. These pores were able to accommodate the expansion of the separated Sn nanoparticles with diameter ranging from 2 nm to 30 nm. Ex situ TEM was also used to observe the structural changes in the porous TiO2-x-C-Sn nanofibers after different charge-discharge cycles. The Sn nanoparticles, which occupy the pores that surround them, are unable to convert back to their original state after the first charge-discharge cycle. Obviously, the size of the Sn nanoparticles decreased greatly as induced by lithiation after 1000 cycles. The line scanning demonstrates the uniform distribution of the smaller Sn nanoparticles in the porous TiO2-x-C substrate, facilitating the transport of electrons, which can be proven by the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. It is clearly demonstrated through the high-resolution TEM images that the crystalline structure of Sn and TiO2 does not change after cycling. In addition, no loss of Sn can be found, which demonstrates great stability. In summary, a novel approach of lithiation-induced insertion of Sn nanoparticles into the pores of highly stable TiO2-x-C nanofiber substrates is exploited to address the problem of structural degradation of Sn-based electrode. The in situ TEM observation has proved that during first lithiation Li4.4Sn alloy can be effectively inserted into the pores surrounding the initial Sn nanoparticles in the TiO2-x-C nanofibers by its large volume expansion and after first delithiation the post-formed smaller Sn nanoparticles remain in the pores. Benefiting from the unique structural and compositional features, the as-made TiO2-x-C-Sn nanofibers as anode have achieved a long cycling life of over 10000 charging/discharging cycles in addition to a high specific capacity of 957 mAh/g at 0.1 A/g and good rate capability. It is believed that this novel and simple approach could provide new avenues for synthesizing other high-performance anode material systems that suffer from large volume expansion. Core-shell TiO2@MnO2 heterostructures were also synthesized by combining an electrospinning technique with a hydrothermal reaction. To create the starting materials, TiO2-carbon composite nanofibers were first prepared using a simple electrospinning technique. Then, the carbon in the TiO2-carbon composite nanofibers reacted with KMnO4 to produce ultrathin MnO2 nanosheets on the TiO2 nanofibers. The large surface area of the resulting materials offers sufficient electrode/electrolyte interface to promote the charge-transfer reactions which yield a better rate capability. The highly porous structure not only facilitates Li-ion access, but also accommodates large volumetric expansion during the charging/discharging processes, resulting in an excellent cycle performance. As an anode, this material delivered a high reversible capacity of 891 mAh g-1 at the first cycle and maintained the capacity of 888 mAh g-1 after 50 cycles at the current density of 0.1 A g-1; it also showed a remarkable rate capability of 2 A g-1 while retaining a capacity of 185 mAh g-1 after 500 cycles. Given their enhanced electrochemical performance, core-shell TiO2@MnO2 heterostructures are promising candidate anodes for Lithium-ion batteries.

531212.label: Major findings and research outcome
531212.value: The major research output from this projects is summarized as following: Tin holds promise as an anode material for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) because of its high theoretical capacity, but its cycle life is limited by structural degradation. A novel approach was exploited to insert Sn nanoparticles into the pores of highly stable titanium dioxide–carbon (TiO2−x–C) nanofiber substrates that can effectively localize the postformed smaller Sn nanoparticles, thereby address the problem of structural degradation, and thus achieve improved anode performance. This interesting method can provide new avenues for other high-capacity anode material systems that suffer from significant volume expansion. A method of in situ formation of hollow graphitic carbon nanospheres (HGCNs) in amorphous carbon nanofibers (ACNFs) has been developed by a combination of electrospinning, calcination and acid treatment. The prepared carbon nanofibers contain many HGCNs on which defects such as discontinuous graphene sheets with a large d-spacing in their wall exist and provide extra sites for Li+ storage and serve as buffers for withstanding large volume expansion and shrinkage during the Li insertion and extraction procedure. The synthesis process is simple, low-cost and environmentally friendly, providing new avenues for the rational engineering of high-energy carbon-based anode materials. The amorphous carbon nanotubes decorated with hollow graphitic carbon nanospheres (ACNHGCNs) were successfully fabricated using a novel triple-coaxial electrospinning method and characterized the electro-chemical performance of these ACNHGCNs as anode materials for lithium ion batteries (LIBs). The ACNHGCNs displayed a very high reversible specific capacity. Hollow graphitic carbon nanofibers (HGCNFs) have great promise for many important applications, such as catalysis, sensors, energy conversion, gas storage, and electronic devices. We have studied catalytic etching-wetting-dewetting mechanism in synthesizing HGCNFs with both hollow spherical-like and tunnel-like pores. With in situ transmission electron microscope imaging, we shown that the spherical pores were formed by the evaporation of encapsulated Ni on the surface of amorphous carbon nanofiber and that hollow tunnels are developed through continuous etching of the amorphous carbon under catalysis of Ni nanoparticles. Theoretical calculations and simulations revealed that continuous tunnel etching was driven by the wetting-to-dewetting transition of the Ni-tunnel wall interaction during the catalytic graphitization of the amorphous carbon wall. The above research results have been published in prestigious journals including CHEM, ADVANCED FUNCTIONAL MATERIALS, ENERGY STORAGE MATERIALS, NERGY & ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE, JOURNAL OF THE AMERICAN CHEMICAL SOCIETY.

531212.value: Benefiting from the unique structural and compositional features, the as-made TiO2-x-C-Sn nanofibers as anode have achieved a long cycling life of over 10000 charging/discharging cycles in addition to a high specific capacity of 957 mAh/g at 0.1 A/g and good rate capability. It is believed that this novel and simple approach could provide new avenues for synthesizing other high-performance anode material systems that suffer from large volume expansion. The methodology can be adopted to develop 2D porous Si/graphene (p-Si/G) and 3D free-standing porous Si/graphene-foam (p-Si/GF) composites. The target of the study is to solve the fundamental issues of the working mechanisms of lithiation and delithiation in the free-standing p-Si/GF and explore an optimized free-standing p-Si/GF with high gravimetric/volumetric capacity and long cycle life. Such material can be used as anode electrode directly without the aid of current collector, binder and conductive carbon. The optimized 3D free-standing p-Si/GF is expected to combine the higher capacity of Si, higher conductivity of graphene and higher mechanical strength of GF as well as the capability of nanopores to accommodate the volume expansion of Si during lithiation.

531312.label: Project Objectives
531312.value: A Semi-Coupled Dictionary Learning Model (SCDL) -- Most of the cross-modality learning problems are highly ill-posed. In order to find a stable yet flexible mapping between the modalities while preserving the image local structures, we propose to learn simultaneously a pair of dictionaries, which could characterize the modality-specific signal spaces accurately, and a mapping function, which could reveal the intrinsic image structural transforms in domains spanned by the dictionary pair. The semi-coupled dictionary pair endows the mapping function much flexibility for accurate cross-modality conversion. Algorithms of Image Cross-Modality Transform – The proposed SCDL is a general model, and we can adapt it to tackle different image cross-modality transform tasks. In this project, two representative problems will be considered: image interpolations and boundary detection. Based on the prior information and definitions of these problems, we will design different regularization terms and introduce them into the SCDL model, making the SCDL effective for the given tasks. Algorithms of Cross-Modality Image Recognition – One critically important application of computer vision is image recognition, while cross-modality image recognition is particularly challenging. In this project we will also adapt the SCDL model to conduct cross-modality image recognition tasks such as photo-sketch/sketch-photo face recognition, multi-spectrum face recognition and multi-pose face recognition. Different from cross-modality image transform, cross-modality image recognition emphasizes more on extracting and preserving the discriminative information, while caring less about reconstructing perfectly the images. In this project, we will propose synthesis-based and discriminative-mapping based projection methods to accomplish the different recognition tasks.
