531312.label: Realisation of objectives
531312.value: All the three objectives are well achieved. 1. Objective 1 -- Semi-Coupled Dictionary Learning Model The employed dictionary plays an important role in sparse representation or sparse coding based image reconstruction and classification. However, many dictionary learning models exploit only the discriminative information in either the representation coefficients or the representation residual, which limits their performance. We present a novel dictionary learning method based on the Fisher discrimination criterion (journal paper [J2]). A structured dictionary, whose atoms have correspondences to the subject class labels, is learned, with which not only the representation residual can be used to distinguish different classes, but also the representation coefficients have small within-class scatter and big between-class scatter. The classification scheme associated with the proposed dictionary learning model is consequently presented by exploiting the discriminative information in both the representation residual and the representation coefficients. The proposed method is extensively evaluated on various image datasets, and it shows superior performance to many state-of-the-art dictionary learning methods in a variety of classification tasks. In many dictionary learning and sparse coding based image restoration and image classification problems, using non-convex lp-norm minimization (0 ≤ p < 1) can often obtain better results than the convex l1-norm minimization. By extending the popular soft-thresholding operator, we proposed a generalized iterated shrinkage algorithm (GISA) for lp-norm non-convex sparse coding (conference paper [C2]). Unlike the analytic solutions, the proposed GISA algorithm is easy to implement, and can be adopted for solving non-convex sparse coding problems with arbitrary p values. 2. Objective 2 -- Algorithms of Image Cross-Modality Transform We developed a texture enhanced method, namely gradient histogram preservation (GHP), to transform a noisy image into a clean image with enhanced textures (journal paper [J1]). It enforces the gradient histogram of the reconstructed image to be close to a reference gradient histogram of the original image. An algorithm is also developed to effectively estimate the reference gradient histogram from the noisy observation of the unknown image. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed GHP algorithm can well preserve the texture appearance in the reconstructed images, making them look more natural. We also proposed iteration-wise lp-norm regularizers together with data-driven strategy to transform a blurry image into a sharp image with good edge preservation (journal paper [J4]). First, we extend the generalized shrinkage-thresholding (GST) operator for lp-norm minimization with negative p value, which can sharpen salient edges while suppressing trivial details. Then, the iteration-wise GST parameters are specified to allow dynamical salient edge selection and time-varying regularization. Finally, instead of handcrafted tuning, a principled discriminative learning approach is proposed to learn the iteration-wise GST operators from the training dataset. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, our method achieves better deblurring results in terms of both quantitative metrics and visual quality. 3. Objective 3 -- Algorithms of Cross-Modality Image Recognition Learning a distance metric from the given training samples plays a crucial role in matching images from different modalities. We generalized several state-of-the-art metric learning methods, such as large margin nearest neighbor (LMNN) and information theoretic metric learning (ITML), into a kernel classification framework (journal paper [J3]). The proposed framework can also suggest new metric learning methods, which can be efficiently implemented, interestingly, by using the standard support vector machine (SVM) solvers. Two novel metric learning methods, namely doublet-SVM and triplet-SVM, are then developed under the proposed framework. They achieve competitive image classification accuracies with state-of-the-art metric learning methods but with significantly less training time. Most of the current metric learning methods are proposed for point-to-point distance (PPD) based image classification. In many computer vision tasks, however, we need to measure the point-to-set distance (PSD) and even set-to-set distance (SSD) for cross-modality image-to-video or video-to-video classification. We extend the PPD based Mahalanobis distance metric learning to PSD and SSD based ones, namely point-to-set distance metric learning (PSDML) and set-to-set distance metric learning (SSDML), and solve them under a unified optimization framework (conference paper [C1]).

531312.label: Major findings and research outcome
531312.value: 1. We developed a novel gradient histogram preservation (GHP) algorithm to transform the noisy image into a clean image with enhanced texture. We learn adaptive dictionaries from the noisy image itself to represent and reconstruct the image, and enforce the gradient histogram of the reconstructed image to be close to a reference gradient histogram of the original image. An algorithm is also developed to effectively estimate the reference gradient histogram from the noisy observation of the unknown image. Please refer to journal paper [J1] for details. 2. Many dictionary learning models exploit only the discriminative information in either the representation coefficients or the representation residual. We present a novel dictionary learning method based on the Fisher discrimination criterion. A structured dictionary is learned, which exploits the discriminative information in both the representation residual and the representation coefficients. Please refer to journal paper [J2] for details. 3. We generalized several state-of-the-art metric learning methods into a kernel classification framework, under which two novel metric learning methods are developed and achieve competitive classification accuracies with state-of-the-art metric learning methods but with significantly less training time. Please refer to journal paper [J3] for details. 4. We proposed iteration-wise lp-norm regularizers together with data-driven strategy to transform blurred images into sharp images with edge preservation. Experimental results show that, negative p value is more effective in estimating the coarse shape of blur kernel at the early stage. Our method achieves better deblurring results in terms of both quantitative metrics and visual quality than state-of-the-art blind deconvolution method. Please refer to journal paper [J3] for details. 5. We extend the point-to-point distance (PPD) based Mahalanobis distance metric learning to point-to-set distance (PSD) and set-to-set distance (SSD) based ones, and solve them under a unified optimization framework for image matching and classification. Please refer to conference paper [C1] for details. 6. By extending the popular soft-thresholding operator, we proposed a generalized iterated shrinkage algorithm (GISA) for lp-norm non-convex sparse coding. The proposed GISA algorithm is easy to implement, and can be adopted for solving non-convex sparse coding problems with arbitrary p values. Please refer to conference paper [C2] for details.

531312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
531312.value: In recent years, deep learning based methods have been rapidly developed for image cross-style transformation and classification, yet the interpretability of deep learning methods is a problem. How to integrate the advantages dictionary learning, sparse coding and deep learning and develop new schemes with high performance and interpretability will be a promising direction for future research.

531312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
531312.value: In many computer vision applications, we may need to transform a noisy image, blurred image or low-resolution image into a clean image, sharpened image or high resolution image, and we need to match images with different modality (e.g., image to video) for recognition. In this project, we develop a series dictionary learning, sparse coding and metric learning based models and algorithms to achieve these goals. For example, our methods can enhance image textures while removing noise, and convert a blurred image into a clear image without additional information. A new dictionary learning model was developed to learn discriminative dictionaries from image samples, which are then used to encode and classify images effectively. A generalized iterated shrinkage algorithm was developed for efficient and accurately lp-norm non-convex sparse coding in image reconstruction and classification. Finally, several new metric learning algorithms were developed to efficiently and accurately learn similarity measures to match images, videos, or match images to videos.

531512.label: Project Objectives
531512.value: A Framework to Unify FR and NR IQA Problems – FR-IQA and NR-IQA are usually considered as two very different problems in most literature. However, we will indicate that NR-IQA can be simply unified as an FR-IQA like problem by estimating one or more feature maps of the unknown reference image. This framework will be a novel and effective generalization of FR-IQA and NR-IQA studies, and can improve the performance of both of them. Quality and Distortion Aware Feature Extraction – No matter which one of FR-IQA and NR-IQA is considered the feature extraction is crucial to the IQA performance. In this project, we will investigate the IQA-oriented feature extraction problem from three aspects: HVS relevant, quality aware, and distortion aware. Particularly, the development of distortion aware feature extraction technique will contribute significantly to the NR-IQA study and make the IQA tools more practical. Distortion-Free Feature Map Estimation and Local Quality Map (LQM) Formation – One novel and key step in the proposed framework is the feature map estimation of unknown reference image, which makes it feasible to calculate the LQM of distorted image (in the case of NR-IQA), and consequently converts NR-IQA as an FR-IQA like problem. Three kinds of distortion-free feature map estimation techniques, adaptive filtering, statistical estimation and dictionary learning, will be systematically investigated in this project. Robust Regression Model Learning – The calculated LQM is more informative at characterizing image local structures than the widely used natural scene statistic models for NR-IQA. We will extract effective statistical features from the LQM and learn robust regression models to regress the image quality score by adapting advanced machine learning methods. NR-IQA Database Construction – To the best of our knowledge, all the existing image databases in the IQA community were constructed in an FR-IQA manner, and they are less appropriate for evaluating NR-IQA methods. Moreover, the images in them are often of singular distortion. It is imperative to build a large scale NR-IQA database with images of multiple distortions, and such a database will be established in this project, which will greatly benefit the whole IQA community.

531512.label: Realisation of objectives
531512.value: 1. Objective 1 – A Framework to Unify FR and NR IQA Problems What makes FR-IQA and NR-IQA different is the availability of the reference image, or equivalently the feature map of the reference image. If we can have some estimated feature maps of the reference image, then NR-IQA can be unified as an FR-IQA problem, and consequently they can be performed using the same procedures. We propose to unify FR-IQA and NR-IQA in the following way. The first step is feature extraction. For FR-IQA, the feature maps of reference image and distorted image can be extracted using the same feature extractor; for NR-IQA, we estimate one or more reference feature maps from the distorted feature map and/or the distorted image with some processing (e.g., shifting or local filtering). Once the feature maps are computed, the following procedures for FR-IQA and NR-IQA are basically the same, e.g., similarity computing and regression learning. Our experiments showed that such a framework can improve both FR and NR IQA performance. Objective 1 is well achieved. 2. Objective 2 – Quality and Distortion Aware Feature Extraction Quality aware and distortion level aware features are crucial to the performance of an IQA model. In this project, we developed four feature extraction schemes. The first one aims for effective NR-IQA model learning without using human scored images. We partition the distorted images into overlapped patches, and use a percentile pooling strategy to estimate the local quality of each patch. A quality-aware clustering method is proposed to learn a set of centroids on each quality level. These centroids features are used as a codebook to infer the quality of each patch in a given image, and subsequently a perceptual quality score of the whole image can be obtained. The second one aims for effective and efficient FR-IQA. We found that the image gradients are sensitive to image distortions, while different local structures in a distorted image suffer different degrees of degradations. The pixel-wise gradient magnitude similarity (GMS) between the reference and distorted images combined with a novel pooling strategy – the standard deviation of the GMS map – can predict accurately perceptual image quality with much faster speed than most state-of-the-art IQA methods. The third feature extractor utilizes the joint statistics of two types of commonly used local contrast features: the gradient magnitude (GM) map and the Laplacian of Gaussian (LOG) response. We employed an adaptive procedure to jointly normalize the GM and LOG features, and show that the joint statistics of normalized GM and LOG features have desirable properties for NR-IQA task. The fourth one aims for learning an opinion-unaware NR-IQA model without using human subjective score and distorted images for training. By integrating natural image statistics features derived from multiple cues, we learn a multivariate Gaussian model of image patches from a collection of pristine natural images. Using the learned multivariate Gaussian model, a Bhattacharyya-like distance is used to measure the quality of each image patch, then an overall quality score is obtained by average pooling. Objective 2 is well achieved. 3. Objective 3 – Distortion-Free Feature Map Estimation and Local Quality Map (LQM) Formation In traditional methods, the feature map of the reference image must be available to calculate the LQM of distorted image. In the case of NR-IQA, the reference image is not available, and hence many NR-IQA methods cannot produce an LQM of the distorted image. In this project, we developed two new NR-IQA schemes which can produce LQM while evaluating the quality of a distorted image. In the first scheme, we partition the training images into overlapped patches, and use a percentile pooling strategy to estimate the local quality of each patch. Then a quality-aware clustering method is developed to learn a set of centroids on each quality level. These centroids are then used as a codebook to infer the quality of each patch in a given image, and subsequently provide an LQM of the whole image. In the second scheme, we integrate natural image statistics features derived from multiple cues, and learn a multivariate Gaussian model of image patches. By using the learned multivariate Gaussian model as a universal reference, the quality of each image patch can be measured and hence an LQM can be produced. Objective 3 is well achieved. 4. Objective 4 – Robust Regression Model Learning Our new IQA models can provide an LQM of a given distorted image, and we also developed two corresponding regression methods to yield a quality score of the whole image. In the first scheme, a patch is assigned to several clusters and the local quality is estimated by the weighted average of the cluster centroids. The final score can be obtained by average pooling. In the second scheme, we proposed a Bhattacharyya-like distance metric to match the multivariate Gaussian model of a distorted local patch to the learned latent model. Such a local matching method is more accurate and robust than global matching, and the overall quality score is obtained by average pooling. Objective 4 is well achieved. 5. Objective 5 – NR-IQA Database Construction Database is a must for IQA study. Most of the previous databases in the IQA community were constructed in an FR-IQA manner, making them less appropriate for evaluating NR-IQA methods. In this project, we developed two IQA databases. The first database is specially designed for NR-IQA. 400 naturally images (from 4 categories: people, plants, animals, and manmade objects) were collected and visually examined by 7 volunteer observers. If no less than 5 of the 7 observers found that the quality of an image was very good, the image was retained. In the end, 90 images were selected as pristine images, none of which is in any of the existing IQA databases. Natural image statistical features can be extracted from this database to learn NR-IQA models. The second database is a general IQA database. We resorted to the Internet and selected 196 keywords (in 7 categories: human, animal, plant, landscape, cityscape, still-life and transportation) to search for images. A number of 200,000 images were obtained. After screening and removing those low-quality images, about 7, 000 images remained. We further carefully inspected each of the remaining images multiple times by zooming in and removed those images with visible compression distortions. Eventually, we ended up with 4,744 high quality natural images. 94,880 distorted images were created from them. To our best knowledge, this is the largest IQA database by far. Objective 5 is well achieved.

Distortion-Free Feature Map Estimation and Local Quality Map (LQM) Formation – One key step in the proposed framework is the feature map estimation of unknown reference image, which makes it feasible to calculate the LQM of distorted image (in the case of NR-IQA), and consequently converts NR-IQA as an FR-IQA like problem. Three kinds of distortion-free feature map estimation techniques, adaptive filtering, statistical estimation and dictionary learning, will be systematically investigated in this project.

Robust Regression Model Learning – The calculated LQM is more informative at characterizing image local structures than the widely used natural scene statistic models for NR-IQA. We will extract effective statistical features from the LQM and learn robust regression models to regress the image quality score by adapting advanced machine learning methods.

NR-IQA Database Construction – To the best of our knowledge, all the existing image databases in the IQA community were constructed in an FR-IQA manner, and they are less appropriate for evaluating NR-IQA methods. Moreover, the images in them are often of singular distortion. It is imperative to build a large scale NR-IQA database with images of multiple distortions, and such a database will be established in this project, which will greatly benefit the whole IQA community.

531512.label: Major findings and research outcome
531512.value: 1. We developed a highly effective and efficient full reference (FR) image quality assessment (IQA) model called Gradient Magnitude Similarity Deviation (GMSD) (journal paper [J1]). We found that the image gradient magnitude is simple to calculate but a kind of quality-aware feature. We proposed a new pooling strategy, namely the deviation of gradient magnitude similarity map, and the resulting GMSD index exhibits highly efficient and effective IQA performance. It is among the most accurate FR-IQA models, while it is significantly faster than the other state-of-the-art IQA models. This work has been cited 253 times since its publication in 2014 and it is selected as an ESI Highly Cited Paper. 2. We developed one of first learning based NR-IQA schemes without using human subjective scores by proposing a quality aware clustering method (conference paper [C2]). We later developed another NR-IQA method without using any distorted images and their human scores for training, namely IL-NIQE (journal paper [J3]). We used a multivariate Gaussian model to describe latent image features, and proposed a distance metric to measure the image local quality. On large-scale tests across existing IQA databases, surprisingly, IL-NIQE outperforms all previous NR-IQA methods, including those methods which use human subjective scores for training. A dataset for NR-IQA study was also developed in [J3]. 3. We established by far the largest IQA database in the world, which contains 4,744 pristine natural images and 94,880 distorted images created from them (journal paper [J4]). Associated with this database, we presented three test criteria to evaluate the performance of different IQA models. Our work reveals the weaknesses of existing IQA models, provides insights on how to improve the models, and to shed light on how the next-generation IQA models may be developed. 4. We found that the classical mean square error (MSE) index, which is commonly known as an ineffective perceptual image quality indicator, can be largely enhanced by introducing a structural error term to it. A Perceptual-fidelity Aware MSE (PAMSE) was developed (conference paper [C1]), which is highly efficient and shows good perceptual quality prediction accuracy. 5. We found that the joint statistics of two commonly used local contrast features, the gradient magnitude map and the Laplacian of Gaussian response, are very information for NR-IQA (journal paper [J2]). 6. Inspired by our findings of image quality evaluation, we further developed a new image segmentation quality evaluation index by composing a reference segmentation from multiple references. We also established an image segmentation quality evaluation database (journal paper [J5]).

531512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
531512.value: There are two promising directions for the further development of the proposed research. First is to develop robust deep learning methods for practical NR-IQA study. Most previous methods use hand-crafted features to learn NR-IQA models. By end-to-end deep learning, stronger models can be learned. However, the number of available training samples is very small. How to train a deep model with limited number of samples is a big issue. Second is to build a large scale NR-IQA database with minimal human scoring. Training data are crucial for the success of NQ-IQA. It is very costly to ask human subject to score the images. How to label a large amount of training data but with minimal cost of annotation is a challenging research problem.

531512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
531512.value: With the explosion of image data in our daily life, how to automatically measure the perceptual quality of a given image becomes a very important problem. According to the availability of a reference image, the so-called perceptual image quality assessment (IQA) problem can be categorized into full-reference (FR) and no-reference (NR) ones. In this project, we first showed that FR-IQA and NR-IQA can be considered under the same framework, and then developed several state-of-the-art FR and NR IQA models. In particular, our developed FR-IQA model is not only effective but also efficient; our developed NR-IQA model does not need human subjective scores and distorted images for training, but outperforms all previous NR-IQA models, including those human subjective scores guided methods. Two IQA databases were also established in this project, one of which is by far the largest publically accessible IQA database in the world.

531912.label: Project Objectives
531912.value: This project aims to develop a technique for the effective drag reduction of a generic 3D passenger vehicle (Ahmed model) based on our latest improved understanding of the flow, along with accumulated knowledge in the literature. Specifically, Develop and characterize a flow-induced self-oscillating minijet for unsteady actuation in the active drag control of vehicles, including the dependence of outlet jet speed and pulsation frequency on the inlet flow pressure and structural geometric parameters. Develop an open-loop control technique and investigate different actuation schemes, i.e., producing steady and/or unsteady actuations at different locations and orientations, to manipulate the C-pillar vortices and flow separation from the rear window and vertical base of the model in order to achieve the maximum drag reduction. Investigate how the flow around the Ahmed model is altered under control in order to understand thoroughly the flow physics and drag reduction mechanisms.

531912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
531912.value: The lasting high-rise oil price highlights the necessity and urgency of drag reduction research for vehicles. With passive shaping vehicles approaching an optimum, it is active control that can reduce drag significantly further. In spite of recent numerous investigations, an effective and efficient active drag reduction technique has yet to be developed. Our latest extensive measurements in the wake of a generic 3D Ahmed vehicle model unveil a number of aspects of this flow that failed to be captured in previous studies (Wang et al. 2011). This project is a continuation of this work and aims to develop an effective active drag reduction technique for this flow. Compared with previous investigations, the proposed technique has four distinct characteristics. (1) Arrange actuators based on our latest improved understanding of flow physics. (2) A flow-induced self-oscillating pulsed minijet, developed based on the self-oscillating microvalve technology (Ducloux et al. 2007), will be applied. Given an incident flow, this actuator may generate a pulsed minijet with a frequency variable depending on the input pressure and structural geometric parameters, without any dedicated power supply. Its outlet speed is also controllable. The effectiveness of this actuator will be compared with others such as synthetic jets. (3) Apply unsteady actuation, combined with steady blowing, to capitalize the natural instabilities in turbulence. Actuators will be mounted around the rear window and the vertical base of the vehicle model. Different control strategies, covering actuation strength, frequency, location and orientation, will be investigated to identify the maximum drag reduction. (4) Develop a closed-loop scheme to optimize the control performance, following our previous success in controlling other flows. With pressure signals measured in a number of low pressure regions as feedback signals, PID controllers will be first deployed to generate the actuation signals. Other control algorithms such as the model predictive control may also be explored. Experiments will be conducted in a wind tunnel. The Reynolds number, based on the model frontal area, will be 2.4 x 105. The pressure distribution around the rear window and base of the model will be measured, along with flow, drag and lift forces, using various techniques. The data will be analyzed in detail to understand thoroughly the flow physics and drag reduction mechanisms under different control strategies. 汽车业的迅猛发展、燃油价格的大幅攀升和日趋严重的城市污染均高度放映了汽车减阻研究的重要性和紧迫感。鉴于被动减阻已近极限，本项目旨在深入研究不稳定汽车绕流并研发一种全新的汽车主动控制技术。为此，提出实验研究并解决以下科学问题：（1）三维车模非定常绕流流动机理；（2）车模绕流开环控制；（3）三维复杂流动控制机理。项目具如下特点：（1）基于本课题组对车模尾流特性的最新发现；（2）研发用于汽车气动控制的创新自激式振荡微射流，勿需专门的能量供给装置；（3）采用定常和非定常有机组合的激励方式控制车模尾流中的湍流不稳定性和拟序结构;（4）将车模最优控制方案应用于实车试验。

531912.label: Realisation of objectives
531912.value: Objective 1: Develop and characterize a flow-induced self-oscillating minijet for unsteady actuation in the active drag control of vehicles, including the dependence of outlet jet speed and pulsation frequency on the inlet flow pressure and structural geometric parameters. A flow-induced self-oscillating minijet actuator has been investigated and developed for unsteady actuation in the active drag control of vehicles. The dependence of outlet jet speed and pulsation frequency on the inlet flow pressure and structural geometric parameters has also been documented. Objective 2: Develop an open-loop control technique and investigate different actuation schemes, i.e., producing steady and/or unsteady actuations at different locations and orientations, to manipulate the C-pillar vortices and flow separation from the rear window and vertical base of the model in order to achieve the maximum drag reduction. On the basis of the improved understanding of flow physics, an active control technique is developed using a combination of steady blowing over the rear window and behind the base. The aerodynamic drag of the Ahmed body was measured using a force balance Re = 1.3 × 105 - 2.0 × 105 based on the square root of the frontal area A of the body. Steady blowing S1 was applied along the upper edge of the rear window, which has been demonstrated to be effective in reducing or suppressing the recirculation bubble located on the slanted surface. This actuation led to a maximum drag reduction by 11% at Re = 1.3 × 105 and 12% at Re = 1.7 × 105 and 2.0 × 105. Steady blowing S2 was also deployed along two side edges of the rear window to break the well-known longitudinal C-pillar vortices, and the drag can be reduced by around 6% at all the Reynolds numbers. The effectiveness of combining the two steady actuations S1 and S2 in reducing the drag was evaluated at Re = 1.7 × 105, achieving a maximum drag reduction of 16%, higher than any previous reports based on steady blowing. The influence of steady blowing S3 and S4, applied along the upper and lower edges of the base, respectively, on the drag of the Ahmed body has been investigated. Results show that the drag can be either substantially reduced or increased, depending on the angle of the steady blowing relative to the free-stream velocity. The combination of S3 and S4 at their optimal blowing angles achieved an impressive drag reduction of 17% at Re = 1.7 × 105. The drag reduction reached 26% with S1, S2 and S3 all switched on and 27% with S1, S2 and S4 all switched on. With the combination of all the four actuations, a significant reduction in drag by 29% was obtained, which is significantly higher than those reported in the literature, and is in fact very close to the target (30%) set by automotive industries. Objective 3: Develop a closed-loop control system and determine: (i) the best combination of feedback signals, (ii) to what extent the closed-loop control can improve the effectiveness of drag reduction, as compared with the open-loop control as well as the absence of control. The pressure coefficient at the rear end of the car model has been found to be highly correlated with the drag coefficient and is thus selected as the plant output as the drag is difficult to measure in practice. On the other hand, the flow rate of each blowing is used as the plant input. Using the classical PID control algorism, a closed-loop control system has been successfully developed. The system may find automatically the optimal blowing momentum coefficient and thus gain the maximum drag reduction, as being confirmed by the open-loop control results. The system is further found to be robust, that is, the system may automatically find the new optimum control parameters, thus achieving the maximum drag reduction, when the Reynolds number is suddenly changed. Objective 4: Investigate how the flow around the Ahmed model is altered under control in order to understand thoroughly the flow physics and drag reduction mechanisms. Extensive flow measurements were conducted using pressure scanner, hotwire, flow visualization and particle image velocimetry (PIV) techniques. Flow structures around the Ahmed body with various active control schemes, i.e., individual actuations S1, S2, S3 and S4, two combined actuations (S1 and S2; S3 and S4), three combined actuations (S1, S2 and S3; S1, S2 and S4) and the combination of all (S1, S2, S3 and S4). Under the combination of all four actuations, the drag reduction reaches 29%, and the flow structure under control exhibits a number of changes, compared with that without control. Firstly, in the non-controlled case, the flow separates at the upper edge of the rear window and then reattaches on the slanted surface, forming a small separation region, and the flow remains attached on the rear window downstream. When the actuation is switched on, the separation region over the rear window is significantly increased, resulting in a pressure recovery over the slanted surface. Secondly, the strength of the C-pillar vortices at each side of the rear window is suppressed by the control. Thirdly, without control, the quasi-periodical structures are alternately emanated from the upper and lower recirculation bubbles behind the base. When the control is applied, regions of the two bubbles are enlarged longitudinally. Meanwhile, the alternate emanation of the structures from the two bubbles is eliminated by control. These changes in flow structures produce an increase of the base pressure. Finally, a conceptual model of the manipulated flow structure is proposed.

531912.label: Major findings and research outcome
531912.value: (1) One flow structure model for the Amhed model of high drag regime is proposed for the first time, which includes all the major unsteady structures around the body and their corresponding Strouhal numbers. (2) Steady actuation S1 produced by an array of microjets along the upper edge of rear window can lead to a maximum reduction in drag by 12%. (3) Steady actuation S2 generated through slots along the two side edges of the rear window can produce a drag reduction by 6%. (4) Steady actuations S3 and S4, produced by two arrays of microjets along lines parallel to the upper and lower edges of the vertical base, respectively, can either substantially reduce or increase the drag, depending on the angle of the steady blowing relative to the free-stream velocity. The S3 and S4 at their optimal blowing angles can generate a drag reduction by 11% and 14%, respectively; (5) Combinations of actuations can further enhance the drag reduction performance. A maximum reduction in drag by 16% is achieved by the combination of S1 and S2, and the combination of S3 and S4 results in a maximum drag reduction by 17%. The combinations of S1, S2 and S3 and the combination of S1, S2 and S4 lead to maximum drag reductions by 26% and 26%, respectively. The combination of all the four actuations produces a significant reduction in drag by 29%, and is in fact very close to the target (30%) set by automotive industries. (6) A number of changes in the flow structures around the Ahmed body have been observed with the active control as compared with those in uncontrolled or base flow. For the combination of S1, S2, S3 and S4, firstly, in the non-controlled case, the flow separates at the upper edge of the rear window and then reattaches on the slanted surface, forming a small separation region, and the flow remains attached on the rear window downstream. When the actuation is switched on, the separation region over the rear window is significantly increased, resulting a pressure recovery over the slanted surface. Secondly, the strength of the C-pillar vortices at each side of the rear window is suppressed by the control. Thirdly, without control, quasi-periodical structures are alternately emanated from the upper and lower recirculation bubbles behind the base. When the control is applied, regions of the two bubbles are enlarged longitudinally.

531912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
531912.value: Based on our rich experience and great achievement obtained in this research on the high-drag regime (phi< 30), study on the low-drag regime (phi> 30) is strongly suggested in the future. Compared with the high-drag regime, research on the low-drag regime is rather scarce in literatures. Most previous studies on this regime only focused on its steady characteristics, but details of unsteady flow were ignored. This makes the overall picture on this flow regime remains elusive by now. However, research on the low-drag regime is of great necessity and urgency, since it represents the main characteristics of a flow around typical SUV cars. Investigation should be conducted on the flow around a low-drag Ahmed body to improve our understanding of the low-drag regime and provide an important guideline for further drag reduction research of this body.

531912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
531912.value: Due to constantly rising energy consumption and pollution emission, the necessity and urgency of drag reduction research for vehicles are increasing. This research has gained a relatively thorough understanding of the flow structure around a vehicle, through a rather exhaustive experimental investigations on an Ahmed model, which is the most widely studied 3D simplified car model in automobile industry. A conceptual flow structure model is proposed for the first time. Based on our latest improved understanding of the flow, an effective active drag reduction technique using combined micro-jets over the rear end of the car model has been developed and a maximum drag reduction up to 29% has been achieved, which is much higher than what is reported in the literature and has reached essentially the target of 30% set by European motor industry. Furthermore, a closed-loop control was deployed to enable the system to find automatically the optimal control at different incoming flow velocities, i.e. achieving the maximum drag reduction at different cruising speeds. This research has made a good progress in understanding flow physics and drag reduction mechanisms, and provides an important guideline for engineering application.

532112.value: 研發殼聚醣微膠囊用作口服傳遞柔紅黴素

532112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532112.value: Biomedical material is one of the most rapidly expanding fields in the life science. With the increasing concern and consideration of healthcare towards the community,scientists and manufacturers have tended to exploit many novel technologies to produce the medical textiles in order to satisfy the users’ needs. Chitosan is a linear polysaccharide and it is produced commercially by deacetylation of chitin, which is the structural element in the exoskeleton of crustaceans and cell walls of fungi. Owing to its hypoallergenic nature, it has a number of biomedical uses. Lymphoma is a malignancy of lymphoid system, which is traditionally divided histologically into Hodgkin's lymphoma (HL) and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL). Of which, the incidence of NHL is much higher than HL in Asia. The incidence of NHL is stably increasing over the last twenty years in developed countries. The precise pathogenesis underlying the major of lymphoma remains ill-defined, even though there are some evidences which demonstrates that genetics, infectious agents [For examples: Esptein-Barr-virus, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), human herpes virus-6 and human T-cell lymphotropic virus-1 and bacteria includes Helicobacter Pylori] as well as exposures to pesticides, organic solvents, ultraviolet radiation and hair dyes are important risk factors being associated with lymphoma. Currently, patients suffering from NHL require intravenous injection of chemotherapeutic regimens, including daunorubicin. Daunorubicin should only be administered in a rapid intravenous infusion. It should not be administered intramuscularly or subcutaneously, since it may cause extensive tissue necrosis. It should also never be administered directly into the spinal canal, as this will cause extensive damage to the nervous system and may lead to death. Recently, daunorubicin liposome was also introduced. However, it is also administrated intravenously. Clinically, some patients have allergic response towards intravenous perfusion and this is also an inconvenience method as this wastes patients' time. Here we make use of the microencapsulation technology to encapsulate the daunorubicin into the ingestible chitosan (a linear polysaccharide) shell in order to compare their pharmacological activity with intravenous injection method using animal models. The use of nude mice xenograft model will be the fundamental approach to investigate whether the microcapsules contained daunorubicin can be digested, absorbed and delivered through the lymphatic and circulatory systems to the tumour site to exert its therapeutic activity. 532412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532412.value: Moxa Moxibustion is a common traditional Chinese therapy in which burning Moxa is applied to affected body areas. This method has been employed for thousands of years to achieve certain medical objectives, such as pain relief or anti-bacterial and anti-inflammatory effects. Its therapeutic effectiveness has been demonstrated successfully both in research and clinical studies. However, this traditional approach may cause undesirable side effects, for example: 1) burning of Moxa produces by-products such as smoke and ash; 2) patients are at risk of being burnt; 3) the active ingredients of the Moxa leaf oil are volatile, odorous, unstable in air and easy to dissipate, and difficult to store and transport; 4) it is inconvenient to operate. These side effects limit its further high-potential and high-value applications. This study is aimed at developing a multi-functional smart textile system that will adopt smart fabrics containing encapsulated Moxa oil integrated with thermally-conductive materials to replace the conventional Moxa products. This will efficiently deliver the active ingredients of Moxa to a human body at optimum conditions, i.e., in a precise and controllable way, with maximum convenience and a high level of comfort. Doing so would solve the existing problems mentioned above. Both garment design skill and textile technology will be applied to Moxa Moxibustion textile to enhance the aesthetics and functionality. The smart garment performance will be assessed subjectively in a clinical trial and objectively by a number of instrumental methods. The proposed smart medical textile system fuses advanced technologies with Chinese medicine, textile technology, and design skill. It is expected that the developed smart garment based on electrically-conductive thermal fabric and Chinese medicine, as well as novel garment design, will fill the multidisciplinary gaps and create an innovative form of medical therapy. In addition, this system will not be limited to Moxa Moxibustion but can be extended to other potential applications, such as acupuncture. By creating a new form of medical treatment and producing aesthetic, multi-functional, and high-value-added commercial apparel products, the development of this smart garment will bring great benefits to patients who seek long-term daily medical treatment and to apparel industry. It will also help to accelerate the innovative development of smart garments in medical applications.

532512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
532512.value: GPS高精度定位中周跳实时探测与修复的新方法

532512.label: Project Objectives
532512.value: The primary objective of this research is to develop an innovative method to detect and rectify cycle slips under various operational conditions, providing high precision and reliable PNaVT solutions for GPS applications. More specifically, the objectives of this project are: 1. To develop basic mathematical formulae that integrates both physical and geometric information for CDR. This will be based on the PI’s previous work (Liu, 2011); To generate a large TECR database and investigate the most appropriate TECR threshold for CDR under all the operational conditions in a global context. The TECR threshold, as a key parameter, will be determined from extensive tests and analyses of TECR database. The TECR data will be generated from historical data acquired using different technologies in the past 11 years (to cover at least one solar cycle); To develop novel algorithms to resolve the SIPE problem. A cycle slip search space will be defined based on the expected SIPE value. The TECR threshold will be used in the search process to determine the most suitable cycle slip candidates (unsuitable cycle slip candidates are rejected); To evaluate the CDR method under in various project applications; GPS datasets from Chinese and European projects will be used. The real-time and high-dynamics capacities of this new method will be evaluated. The major outcomes of this research will be a novel method and algorithms for high precision GPS carrier phase data processing that will be beneficial to the large GPS community. The algorithms can be applied by the GPS receiver designers and manufacturers, GPS users/applications and scientific research.

532512.label: Realisation of objectives
532512.value: This project has been successfully completed and the four major objectives have been achieved with the hard work of the PI and his research team. Based on the PI’s previous work (Liu, 2011), the basic mathematical formulae that integrate both physical and geometric information for CDR have been developed and derived. In the PI’s previous work (Liu, 2011), the basic mathematical formulae only for GPS signals (GPS L1 and L2 signals) have been derived. In this project, we have expanded that work to all the GPS signals (GPS L1, L2 and L5 signals) as well as all the other GNSS signals, including Chinese Beidou, European Galileo and Russian GLONASS. All these mathematical formulae have been successfully implemented into one computer program that can be run in a highly automated approach. The computer program has been run and tested with extensive amount of GNSS dataset and its performance has been verified. In the GNSS carrier phase cycle slip detection and repair using the developed method, one critical information is the ionospheric TECR (total electron content rate). Note that TECR is also sometimes called Rate of TEC (ROT) by some researchers. The variation of the TECR or ROT is a concern in the developed method, because it is assumed that the TECR or ROT is basically constant over a short period of time, in order to ensure the correct detection and repair of the carrier phase cycle slips. Thus variation of TECR or ROT can be characterized by its standard deviation, i.e. the so-called ROTI, index of the Rate of TEC. This project investigated the ROTI index at both global and local scales. The GNSS data from different GNSS receivers such as Javad, Leica, Septentrio and Trimble as well as software-defined receivers have been used to characterize ROTI of the different GNSS constellations such as GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and Beidou. The hardware and software GNSS receivers were distributed globally (North America, South America, Europe, Hong Kong and other Asian countries). The global data analysis showed that under very poor condition at low-latitude station, the ROTI can be as large as 5.0 TECU/minute (equivalent to 0.083 TECU/second). In most time, the TEC variation is smooth and the ROTI is about 1.0 TECU/minute (equivalent to 0.017 TECU/second). These numerical analysis results provide very useful information for the cycle slip detection algorithm. One novel algorithm has been developed and implemented into the computer program. This algorithm is developed to overcome the problem of the occurrence of GNSS pseudorange outliers. GNSS pseudorange measurements are needed in the cycle slip detection and repair method developed in this project. However, similar to o GNSS carrier phase measurements, GNSS pseudorange measurements are like to have jumps or interruptions in their time series. In the past no methods have addressed this problem. The recent cycle slip papers such as Zhang X. and Li X. (2012) Instantaneous re-initialization in real-time kinematic PPP with cycle slip fixing, GPS Solut (2012) 16: 315. doi:10.1007/s10291-011-0233-9. And S. Banville and R. B. Langley (2010), Instantaneous Cycle-Slip Correction for Real-Time PPP Applications, Journal of The Institute of Navigation 57(4):325-334 and other methods all did not address the outlier issue in GNSS pseudorange. In this project, the PI has developed a search-based method to overcome pseudorange outlier issue. Both analytical and numerical data analysis results showed that this search-based method can correctly detect and repair carrier phase cycle slips as usual, even if there is any size of outliers in pseudorange measurements. Even in the worst case where the pseudorange measurements are totally missing (not available), the search-based method can still work without problem. The PI has attempted to submit this very innovative method to several top journals such as Journal of Geodesy, GPS Solutions, Journal of Geophysical Research. Unfortunately, this method is too new to be acceptable by reviewers. Thus it was declined to publish. The PI has discussed this new method with a professor at Wuhan University, Mainland China, who is a lead researcher in GNSS and cycle slip detection and our method was highly commended. The PI has rigorously examined all the equations and assumptions of this search-based and they are all solid and valid. The PI has implemented this search-based method in computer program successfully and has tested this method using real world GNSS data extensively. The validity and effectiveness of this method have been proved through numerical data analysis. The innovative research method has been documented and attached to this report. In order to get the findings published and get the priority of finding, it may be submitted to a less competitive journal in the future. The cycle slip detection and repair method (CDR) and the computer program developed from this CDR method have been evaluated using data from different places and from various project applications, such as data from the International GNSS Service (IGS), the Multi-GNSS Experiment (MGEX) network, low-latitude stations (Hong Kong and stations in other countries) and high-latitude stations (such as software receiver data collected in Alaska, USA). The effectiveness of this new method and the computer program has been tested extensively using 1-second high rate GNSS data. This computer program has also been used by the researchers at the GNSS Research Center, Wuhan University, China, a leading research institution both nationally and internationally in the GNSS field. We recently have completed two more draft papers. One is titled “Characterizing the cycle slip occurrences of multi-GNSS measurements recorded in the IGS MGEX project” and the other is titled “Characterization of Inconsistent ROTI Derived from Multi-Constellation GNSS measurements based on Globally Distributed GNSS receivers”. Both of them are in very good shape and they are under my own reviewing. The first was co-authored by a Research Assistant (RA) who was supported by this project for one year but returned to Mainland China to study as a PhD student there. The second one was co-authored by my PhD student, who is now studying as an exchange student in the USA. They will be submitted for journal publications after my own reviewing. If the authors of the two papers were not returning back to Mainland China for his PhD study or not exchanging to USA, the two papers would have been submitted to journals. I am confident that these two draft papers will be published soon.

532512.label: Major findings and research outcome
532512.value: Based on the PI’s previous work, the research team has expanded the cycle slip detection and repair (CDR) method into processing US. GPS, Russian GLONASS, European Galileo and Chinese Beidou signals. This CDR method has been fully implemented into a highly automated computer program. For the consideration of future commercialization and confidentiality purpose, the work of this part has not been published. This computer program has been extensively used by the PI’s group as well as collaborative institutions, e.g. researchers at GNSS Research Center, Wuhan University, China. For instance, the program has been used to process GNSS data which are used for studying atmospheric water vapor (Chen and Liu, 2016), plasma bubble (Kumar et al, 2016), etc. The PI is in discussion with a leading GNSS manufacturer at Mainland China for a possible commercialization of this computer program and implementation of this program into the manufacturer’s hardware (GNSS receivers) and software systems (GNSS data processing programs). We have developed a novel algorithm for cycle slip detection and repair (CDR) under the condition that GNSS pseudorange measurements have large outliers (or even completely missing). This novel algorithm essentially eliminates the necessity of GNSS pseudorange measurements in cycle slip detection and repair, which has never been possible in other cycle slip detection methods. This method has been well documented in details and implemented in our CDR computer program. One draft paper has been completed and can be submitted for publication (Liu, 2017, draft ready for submission). The effectiveness of the CDR method developed in this project heavily depends on the a priori knowledge of ionospheric variation. The research team has studied the parameter, the variation of total electron content rate (TECR) or equivalently the rate of TEC (ROT), by using the index called ROTI. We have used data from both hardware GNSS receivers and software-defined GNSS receivers, deployed in different locations worldwide, to characterize the ROTI (Yang et al., 2017, draft ready for submission). We revealed the inconsistency of ionospheric ROTI when using the GPS modernized L2C and legacy L2 P(Y) signals (Yang and Liu, 2016). We have revealed the detailed relationship of the occurrence of cycle slips with ionosphere scintillations and GNSS systems, with a large amount of data from a typical low-latitude station. We found that every 1000 strong scintillation events (S4>0.6) can result in 200, 124, and 171 cycle-slip occurrences in US. GPS signals, Russian GLONASS signals, and Chinese Beidou signals, respectively, whereas these values are 7, 12, and 12 per 1000 under weak scintillation conditions (0.2 < S4<=0.6) (Luo et al., 2017). In the past, the relationship of cycle slip and scintillation was studied but not considering factor of different GNSS systems.

532512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532512.value: A computer program based on the developed method has been developed and it has been extensively tested through analyzing various different GNSS data sets. In the 8th China Satellite Navigation Conference held at Shanghai, China, in May 2017, the PI discussed with senior engineers of a Mainland China GPS/GNSS leading manufacturer (publicly listed), the Hi-Target Surveying Instrument Co. Ltd, the possibility of commercializing the computer source code of GPS/GNSS cycle slip detection and repair. The senior engineers were very positive and interested in this. Currently, the PI and his group are in the process of obtaining and testing the data sets to be provided by the Hi-Target Surveying Instrument Co. Ltd. By the way, the computer program of GPS/GNSS cycle slip detection and repair has also been used by researchers at the Wuhan University, China.

532512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
532512.value: Global Positioning System (GPS), or more generically the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), has been widely used in many scientific research, e.g. deformation monitoring, earthquake monitoring and practical engineering projects such as engineering surveying. This is because GPS/GNSS can deliver high precision positioning and navigation solutions. However the high precision GPS/GNSS solutions are degraded by the occurrence of sudden jumps or interruptions in the GPS/GNSS signals. The signal jumps or interruptions are called cycle slips and they must be detected and repaired, in the mode of real-time or post-mission, depending on the nature of the GPS/GNSS applications. This project developed a new algorithm for real-time cycle slip detection and repair. This method has many good properties compared to the other existing ones. It is easy to implement and calculation is not complex; it has a minimum requirement of GPS/GNSS data (only a small amount of data from one GPS/GNSS receiver is needed); it is very sensitive and effective to detect and repair those small cycle slips that are hard to be handled in the past by existing methods; it can be used for both real-time and post-mission data processing. One computer program has been developed based on this method and it has been used for many GPS/GNSS research data analysis.

532612.value: 為對稱固體氧化物燃料電池發展高效的同時具有梯度和納米結構的電極 - 實驗和模擬研究

532612.label: Project Objectives
532612.value: To fabricate and characterize innovative symmetrical SOFCs with novel nano-structured and functionally graded electrode microstructures. The microstructure of SOFC electrodes will be characterized using a scanning electron microscope (SEM). The polarization and EIS curves will be measured using an electrochemical workstation. When methane is used as the fuel, the kinetics of steam reforming and water gas shift reactions in the porous electrodes of SOFCs under open circuit conditions will be investigated to derive expressions for the reaction kinetics. To develop transient 2D models to simulate the innovative symmetrical SOFCs with novel electrode microstructures. The polarization and EIS curves of the symmetrical SOFCs will be simulated for model validation and interpretation of the experimental results. To perform extensive simulations using the transient model to: (1) evaluate the novel designs; (2) identify optimal grading of the backbones and optimal infiltration loadings.

532612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532612.value: 固體氧化物燃料電池(SOFC)是高效的電化學裝置, 可將可再生的生物燃料轉換為電能. 但SOFC的廣泛應用主要受到由碳沉積和硫毒化所導致的性能衰減. 最近提出的新穎的對稱SOFC的概念, 可通過交替陰極和陽極氣體的方式, 消除由積碳和硫毒化所帶來的性能損失. 由於使用同一種材料做陰極和陽極, 對稱SOFC的製備也相對簡單和價廉. 儘管對稱SOFC極具發展前景, 其性能仍然低於傳統的SOFC, 因此必須提高其效率, 方可實現大規模應用. 對稱SOFC性能的提高不僅取絕于發展具有優秀的電催化活性和穩定性的電極材料, 也與電極的微觀結構息息相關. 電極的結構對於提高SOFC的性能非常重要, 因為高性能的電極不僅需要大量的反應活性位元, 也需要氣體在多孔結構的快速擴散, 以及電子和離子在多孔固體結構種的快速傳導. 我們前面的研究發現在電極外層使用較大顆粒或孔隙率的梯度電極可有效降低電極的氣體擴散阻力, 從而提高SOFC性能. 此外, 採用在大顆粒表面浸滯上納米顆粒的方式可極大提高電化學反應活性位元並增強SOFC的性能. 在本專案中, 我們提出將梯度結構和浸滯技術相結合的方式發展新穎的納米結構的電極. 該電極將由在梯度電極骨架上浸滯納米顆粒的方式製備, 同可降低氣體擴散損失和增大反應活性位. 我們將製備具有新穎納米結構的對稱SOFC, 並採用氫和甲烷為燃料測試SOFC性能. 我們將測量SOFC的極化曲線和阻抗譜以檢測新電極的性能. 此外, 將發展數學模型研究對稱SOFC的性能. 我們將發展一個高度複雜的2維的非穩態模型, 以類比對稱電極裡伴隨反應的傳輸現象以及阻抗行為. 我們將通過大量的電腦類比, 研究電極多孔結構對SOFC性能的影響, 從而優化多孔電極結構. 本專案將通過實驗研究和數學模型研究並重的方式發展具有新穎電極結構的對稱SOFC. 項目將發展可靠和功能強大的類比工具為設計電極結構提供理論支援. 模擬結果將加深我們對SOFC內部的反應和傳輸現象的理解. 本項目的順利完成將為發展高校和性能穩定的SOFC作出貢獻, 並對可持續能源發展起到促進作用.

532612.label: Major findings and research outcome
532612.value: Both experimental study and mathematical modelling study on solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) have been conducted, with a focus on the electrode microstructure effect. SOFCs with infiltrated electrodes have been fabricated and tested. The SDC+SSC composite structure is used as the backbone for coating SSC nanoparticles by infiltration. It is found that the infiltration technique is effective in increase the reaction sites for electrochemical reactions. The electrode microstructure has been characterized by SEM. Electrochemical performance was measured by an electrochemical workstation. To further increase the SOFC performance at reduced temperatures, new cathode materials have been developed. The B-site substitution with the minor amount of tin in BaFeO3-d parent oxide successfully stabilize the single perovskite lattice structure. Good stability, electrocatalytic activity and ionic conductivity were obtained. As a result, peak power density of over 1W/cm2 was obtained at 973K. Novel phase-inversion method was developed to fabricate new electrode structure with straight pores to enhance the gas transport in the porous layer for gas separation membrane and SOFCs. The combination of the phase-inversion method and the infiltration method is effective in enhancing the SOFC performance. Mathematical models were developed to understand the SOFC microstructure effect on SOFC performance, to predict the effect of various new designs, to understand the coupled transport and reaction process. It is found that the electrochemical reaction mainly take place in a thin layer near the electrode-electrolyte interface (electrochemically active layer - EAL). Thus, it is important to increase the reaction sites in the EAL and to increase the ionic conductivity of the EAL. For comparison, the remainling layer of the electrode is not electrochemically active, thus the reaction sites are not important and it is important to enhance gas transport in this layer. The integration of the infiltration technique and graded backbone is effective in enhancing the SOFC performance. In addition to models at electrode and single cell level. Thermodynamic analyses have also been conducted on SOFC systems, solid oxide electroylzer cell (SOEC) systems etc. Research results have been published as 12 papers in academic journals.

532612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532612.value: The research results explores new structures for enhancing the performance of solid oxide fuel cells. The results can be extendded to other electrocheical systems, such as solid oxide electrolyzer cells and batteries. Currently, the PI is extending his research from fuel cells to electrolyzers and batteries. The previous reseach results on solid oxide fuel cells can be applied.

532612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
532612.value: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) are high temperature electrochemical energy conversion devices with higher efficiency than conventional thermal power plant. In addition to new material development, the optimization of the electrode microstructure is an effective way of enhancing the SOFC performance. This project aims to understand the microstructure properties of SOFC electrodes and explore new electrode mictrostruture for performance enhancement. The research findings provides insights in the coupled transport and reaction process in SOFCs. The information on the electrchemical reaction thickness is significant as it is clear to increase the reaction sites in the electrochemically active layer while the gas transport in the remaining layer should be enhanced. The research is significant in engineering design of SOFC microstructures. The results of the project can directly benefit the SOFC community for developing high performance SOFC for efficient energy conversion.

532712.label: Project Title(Chinese)
532712.value: 開發具有自加熱及藥物釋放功能的智能紡織品用於治療類風濕性關節炎

532712.label: Project Objectives
532712.value: To develop a novel thermo-stimuli drug delivery system based on a smart textile to provide a comprehensive therapy for rheumatoid arthritis. The smart textile combines thermotherapy and pharmacotherapy for optimum rheumatoid arthritis treatment, and overcomes the drawbacks of conventional treatment methods. - The smart textile is integrated with flexible conductive and thermo-sensitive coaxial yarns. - The flexible conductive fibre can generate heat. - The coaxial yarn has a core-shell structure. The core fibre can load drugs up to 200% in weight. The shell polymer has a nano-/micro-scale porous structure. The micropores are the channels through which the drug moves in and out. - A thermo-sensitive polymer will be grafted onto the surface of the shell polymer to form the thermo-sensitive covers for the micropores to enable the coaxial fibre to become a thermo-sensitive coaxial fibre. The temperature-sensitive covers of the micropores can undergo a hydrophilic–hydrophobic transition at the critical temperature of 50 °C, acting as the ‘on-off’ molecular switches. This property can be used to control molecular transport, including drug loading and delivery. - The control of drug loading and release through these stimuli-responsive molecular switches will be one important innovation in this project. To study the effect of temperature on the drug-loading-release behaviour of the smart textile, particularly the loading and release capacity of model drugs at different temperatures and levels of humidity. The smart textile’s physical stability for storage will also be evaluated.

532712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532712.value: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease that can cause chronic inflammation of the joints and other areas of the body. Current treatment of rheumatoid arthritis involves physiotherapy, the use of sticking plaster, and the taking of drugs. Frequent drug intake may cause side effects. The optimal treatment for rheumatoid arthritis is the combination of long-term thermotherapy and the direct delivery of drugs into the joints during thermotherapy. To fulfil these requirements, a flexible and wearable product with self-heating and drug delivery functions needs to be developed. Therefore, I propose to research and develop an innovative wearable smart textile that has the capacity for long-term self-heating and controllable drug delivery as a comprehensive rheumatoid arthritis therapy. The key issues of this proposal include (a) developing a flexible conductive fibre that embeds into the smart textile as the heat generator and (b) developing a coaxial fibre with drug storage and release function, as well as a molecular switch to control drug loading and release at the critical temperature (50 °C). The details are as follows. First, a novel, flexible, conductive yarn will be developed. The heat energy is converted from the electric energy. The heating efficiency can be controlled and adjusted by changing the resistance and weave structure of the smart textile. Second, a coaxial fibre with a core-shell structure and molecular switches will be designed and fabricated through coaxial melt spinning technology. The core fibre is made of polylactic acid/polyethylene glycol copolymer, which can load drugs in its microstructure up to 200% in weight. The shell polymer surrounding the core fibre has a nano-/micro-scale porous structure, in which the micropores are the channels through which the drug moves in and out. Third, to control drug release from the coaxial fibre, a thermo-sensitive polymer will be grafted onto the shell surface of the coaxial fibre to form thermo-sensitive covers (i.e., the molecular switches) for the micropores by a plasma-induced grafting polymerization method. The permeability of drug molecules through the micropores in the shell layer can be controlled by these thermo-sensitive ‘on-off’ switches, according to the environmental temperature. The fourth issue is to design and weave the conductive yarn with the thermo-sensitive coaxial yarn into a flexible and wearable smart textile that has the functions of self-heating and thermo-stimuli drug delivery and can be applied as a comprehensive therapy for rheumatoid arthritis. 類風濕性關節炎是一種炎症性或全身性的慢性疾病，以慢性、對稱性、多滑膜關節炎和關節外病變為主要臨床表現，屬於自身免疫炎性疾病。當前臨床治療方式主要包括物理療法（如採用加熱貼處理病體部位）和藥物療法。然而頻繁的藥物攝入可能會引起副作用。因此治療類風濕性關節炎最佳的方法是對患處進行長時間的熱療處理以及在熱療的同時可控釋放出治療藥物。為實現此綜合治療之目的,一種柔性的並具有自加熱功能以及藥物輸送功能的智能紡織品就急需被開發。因此,本項目將研究和開發一種新型的、並具有長時間自加熱和具有控製藥物輸送功能的、可穿戴的智能紡織品，作為一個全面治療類風濕性關節炎的新的藥物及理療產品。 本項目研究的核心內容主要包括：(a)開發一類柔性導電纖維,可織入到智能紡織品中作為發熱體; (b)開發一種具有藥物存儲和釋放功能的同軸纖維,此纖維表面同時具有控制釋放藥物的分子開關，可在溫度約50°C時控制藥物的釋放和載入。具體技術細節如下：首先,開發一种新穎的、柔性導電纖維。此導電纖維可將電能轉換為熱能。通過改變此導電纖維的電阻和編織結構，可以控制和調節加熱效率。其次, 設計和利用同軸熔融紡絲技術研製一種具有核芯-殼層結構和表面分子開關結構的同軸纖維。同軸纖維的核芯部分由聚乳酸/聚乙二醇共聚物組成，其特點在於此共聚物的載藥量可高達自身重量的200%。同軸纖維的殼層則由具有多孔結構（納米或微米級的微孔）的聚合物組成，這些微孔將作為藥物載入及釋放的通道。第三,為了控制同軸纖維的藥物釋放，利用等離子體誘導接枝聚合方法將熱敏聚合物接枝到同軸纖維的多孔殼層的表面，形成熱敏覆蓋層，使其成為殼層​​微孔的分子開關。通過控制環境溫度的變化，進而可以控制覆蓋在殼層微孔上的熱敏層“關-閉”的“開”或“關”之狀態，實現藥物分子的可控釋放。第四,設計和編織上述導電紗以及同軸紗線成為一個柔性的和可穿戴的智能紡織品，同時具有自加熱功能和熱刺激藥物輸送功能，該智能紡織品將成為一個綜合治療類風濕性關節炎的新型藥物及理療產品。

The smart textile combines thermotherapy and pharmacotherapy for optimum rheumatoid arthritis treatment, and overcomes the drawbacks of conventional treatment methods. - The smart textile is integrated with flexible conductive and thermo-sensitive coaxial yarns. - The flexible conductive fibre can generate heat. - The coaxial yarn has a core-shell structure. The core fiber can load drugs up to 200% in weight. The shell polymer has a nano-/micro-scale porous structure. The micropores are the channels through which the drug moves in and out. - A thermo-sensitive polymer will be grafted onto the surface of the shell polymer to form the thermo-sensitive covers for the micropores to enable the coaxial fiber to become a thermo-sensitive coaxial fibre. The temperature-sensitive covers of the micropores can undergo a hydrophilic–hydrophobic transition at the critical temperature of 50 °C, acting as the ‘on-off’ molecular switches. This property can be used to control molecular transport, including drug loading and delivery. - The control of drug loading and release through these stimuli-responsive molecular switches will be one important innovation in this project. Achievements to objective 1: We have successfully developed a novel smart textile for thermo-stimuli drug delivery. It can generate heat by conducting electricity to control the loading and releasing of the drug. It has two key components: flexible conductive yarns and thermo-sensitive coaxial yarns. The conductive yarn has been synthesized by coating graphene nanoribbon on cotton fiber via wet coating approach. Graphene nanoribbon suspension was first produced by unzipping multiwall carbon nanotube via controlled oxidation reaction. It was introduced into cotton yarn via infiltration. The conductivity of resulted yarn was measured under different stress-strain conditions. The results show that the yarn has a very high conductivity and its resistance (40 × 10 mm) is as low as about 80 Ω at room temperature. It is very flexible and the breaking strain is over 50%. Its conductivity is independent of the bending degree and is insignificantly affected by the strain when the applied strain is less than 20%. The coaxial yarn has been synthesized by grafting poly(N-isopropyl acrylamide) (PNIPAm) / sodium polyacrylate (SPA) copolymer on the cotton yarn via redox radical polymerization of n-isopropyl acrylamide and SPA. The coaxial yarn was studied via optical microscopy. Its drug loading capacity was investigated by measuring the weight difference before and after loading drug solution. The porosity of the PNIPAm/SPA copolymer outer shell was studied via swelling test and methylene blue adsorption test. The results showed that the radius of the inner core is 13.9 μm while the radius of the outer shell is 25.5 μm. The outer shell is highly porous and its pore volume is as high as 0.958 cm³/g in swelled state. Its mesh size is calculated to be about 24.9 nm and its surface area is calculated to be about 833 m²/g. The transition temperature of the coaxial yarn was investigated by measuring the equilibrium swelling ratio of coaxial yarn in deionized water at different temperatures. The results show that its equilibrium swelling ratio is up to 1000% at room temperature. It rapidly decreases with temperature until the temperature reaches 50 °C, implying that the coaxial yarns undergo a hydrophilic–hydrophobic transition at about 50 °C. The mechanism of the coaxial yarn can be explained with polymer network of PNIPAm at a different temperature. Reducing the temperature below the LCST enables the formation of hydrogen bonds between PNIPAm and water molecules. As a result, the PNIPAm molecular chains expand and provides a large pore volume for drug loading. When the temperature is raised above the LCST, PNIPAm’s hydrophilicity decreases rapidly, owing to the aforementioned disassembly of the hydrogen bonds. This causes the shrinkage of the PNIPAm chains and the loaded drug solution is forced out from the coaxial yarn. The smart textile has been finally produced by integrating the conductive yarns and the thermo-sensitive coaxial yarns. The thermo-sensitive coaxial yarns were first weaved as a gauze with the crinkle-weave pattern. Then, the conductive yarns were sewed on the thermo-sensitive fabric. The temperature of smart textile was measured at different applied voltage. The results show that the fabric temperature can be easily controlled by the applied voltage. The fabric can be heated to about 60 °C with solely a 6 V power supply. A low voltage operation ensures the safe use of the smart fabric after loading the drug solution. Objective 2. To study the effect of temperature on the drug-loading-release behaviour of the smart textile, particularly the loading and release capacity of model drugs at different temperatures and levels of humidity. Achievements to objective 2: The drug-loading-release behavior of the smart textile has been investigated. The effect of temperature on drug loading capacity was studied by measuring the mass difference of smart fabric before and after infiltrating in drug solution at a different temperature. Methylthioninium chloride and gentian violet, which are common anti-infective drug and anti-fungal drug respectively, were selected as model drugs. The effect of temperature on drug release behavior was studied by measuring the amount of released drug at a different time interval when infiltrating the drug loaded smart fabric into distilled water at different temperature. The results show that the drug loading capacity of the smart fabric is about 904% by weight at room temperature while that is only about 135% in weight at 60 °C. Moreover, the drug releasing rate at 60 °C is 10 times higher than that at room temperature. In other words, the smart fabric is in “loading” mode at low temperature while it is at “releasing” mode at high temperature. The drug loading capacity of the smart fabric is slightly affected by the level of humidity, due to the increase in the moisture content of the smart fabric. For the vacuum dried smart fabric, the drug loading capacity is about 904% by weight at room temperature. After exposing it to atmosphere with the relative humidity of about 80% for a week, its drug loading capacity slightly decreases to 882% in weight. Objective 3. The smart textile’s physical stability for storage will also be evaluated. Achievements to objective 3: The smart textile’s stability for storage and practical application has been evaluated. Its physical stability for storage has been investigated by measuring the drug loading capacity at different time interval. The resistance change of the smart fabric during consecutive stress-strain cycles and consecutive bending cycles has been conducted to investigate its conducting stability during straining and bending. The conductive stability of the smart fabric during washing has also been investigated. The results show that drug loading capacity of the smart fabric decreases less than 10% after storing it for 20 days. Its conductivity is not obviously affected after 20 consecutive strain cycles and 200 consecutive bending cycles. There is no significant reduction in its conductivity after 10 times of washing. As a result, its physical stability is good enough for storage and practical application.

532712.label: Major findings and research outcome
532712.value: We have made a significant contribution in two major areas during this project: 1. Synthesis of conducting polymer and conducting fabric: We have synthesized several conducting polymer composites via simple solution blending method during this project. First, conducting materials such as carbon nanotube and graphite were functionalized via the chemical method. They were well dispersed into the solvent and blended with various polymers such as silicone rubber and poly (vinyl alcohol). They were found to have excellent flexibility and electrical conductivity. Results have been published in several peer-reviewed journal publications and an international conference (Part C8, reference no. 1-5, 8; Part C9, reference no. 2). Based on those results, we have produced conducting fabric via the wet chemical method. Graphene nanoribbon was prepared and subsequently coated onto cotton fibers to fabricate conductive cotton textile through a simple infiltration. Excellent flexibility and electrical conductivity were achieved. It could be used as the conducting yarn of our smart textile for rheumatoid arthritis. Results have been published in a peer-reviewed journal publication and an international conference (Part C8, reference no. 6; Part C9, reference no. 1). International Association of Advanced Materials Medal - 2016 was obtained because of above results (Part C12). 2. Synthesis of composite hydrogels and investigation of its drug adsorption mechanism We have synthesized two kinds of composite hydrogels and investigated their drug adsorption mechanism. First, we have synthesized Konjac glucomannan/graphene oxide composite hydrogel and used methylthioninium chloride as the model drug during the adsorption test. The results showed that it has good water absorbency and drug adsorption capability toward methylthioninium chloride. Second, we have developed an immobilized poly(vinyl alcohol)/cyclodextrin eco-adsorbent and tested its potential in the removal of ibuprofen from sewage. The results proved that it has high adsorption ability toward ibuprofen. Both composite hydrogels would a potential bio-adsorbent in our smart textile for rheumatoid arthritis. Results have been published in peer-reviewed journal publications (Part C8, reference no. 7, 11).

532712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
532712.value: In this project, we have developed a smart fabric with the capacities of self-heating and controllable drug delivery. It contains two key components: flexible conductive yarns and thermo-sensitive coaxial yarns. The conductive yarns are synthesized by coating conducting graphene nanoribbon on cotton yarns and can be heated up to 60 °C with solely a 6 V power supply, allowing it to be used in wet conditions. By controlling the applied voltage, the temperature of the smart fabric can be easily adjusted. The coaxial yarns are synthesized by coating thermal sensitive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) / sodium polyacrylate copolymer on cotton yarns. Their drug loading and releasing behaviour can be controlled with the temperature of the smart fabric, i.e. “loading” mode at low temperature and “releasing” mode at high temperature. They can adsorb drug solution up to 904% in weight at room temperature. They undergo a hydrophilic - hydrophobic transition at about 50 °C and, above this temperature, drug solution is released from the coaxial yarns. The smart fabric has a great potential in wearable textile products for the combination of thermotherapy and the direct drugs delivery, making thermotherapy at home safer, simpler and more comfortable.
