532812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
532812.value: 醫療信息-物理融合系統（CPS）旨在將智能醫療設備、醫療流程、醫務人員、和患者緊密地結合起來。由於這種系統將會對醫療品質、成本帶來革命性的影響，在人口老齡化問題（中國的該問題尤為嚴重）日益突出的今天，它正越來越多地受到標准化組織、政府、和業界的關注。 醫療CPS有一個無可避免的趨勢：醫療設備間的連接將越來越多地使用無線通訊。一方面，無線通訊可以有效地減少有線連接，提升醫務人員移動的自由度、病患的舒適度、降低被導線絆倒而造成事故的可能性。另一方面，由於無線通信的信噪比比有線通信更易受環境影響，無線通信本身就具有失敗的風險。 為了解決這個新的挑戰，我們建議構建一套限制、評估、消減醫療CPS無線通信風險的框架。與已有類似工作相比，我們有以下創新。 1。保証病患生命安全的風險限制機制。該項機制根據具體的醫療環境上下文，將各設備的回退狀態和設備間的互鎖機制有機融合在一起。針對無線通信丟包和延遲造成競態條件的問題，我們將利用租用機制和分布式交易機制來避免，並對這些機制進行評估。 2。基於混成自動機在線建模/分析的風險評估機制。無線醫療CPS是高度混成的系統，包含了離散的計算機邏輯、連續（並往往是）非線性的生物醫學過程、連續的反饋控制、以及不可靠的無線通信連接。綜合全面的建模/分析需要混成系統工具。特別的，由於很多生物醫學過程難以離線預測，我們將研究採用在線有限時間跨度建模/分析的方法。 3。上下文相關的無線通信資源管理。我們將根據醫療環境上下文中對風險的預測來決策管理無線資源。一方面，我們將根據信道品質和干擾源的監測結果來被動地調整無線通信的參數﹔另一方面，我們也將對有害的干擾源進行主動的監管。 我們將在軟件定義無線電平台上實現上述解決方案。這種平台能夠提供足夠的柔性，並可與高度異構的各種無線通信技術交互。我們將展開基於真實世界數據樣本的仿真/半實物仿真評估，甚至非侵入式的醫院實地實驗評估。 本框架將對社會、跨學科研究、以及業界產生深遠的裨益。

532812.label: Realisation of objectives
532812.value: On Revised Objective 1: The survey report is collectively published in the following articles: [li13] Tao Li (graduated PhD student co-supervised by me), On Coordination of Cyber-Physical Systems - Chapter 2.1 MCPS Standard and Applications, PhD Thesis, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, 2013. [kang15] Kyungtae Kang, Qixin Wang, Junbeom Hur, Kyung-Joon Park, Lui Sha, “Medical-Grade Quality of Service for Real-Time Mobile Healthcare,” in IEEE Computer, vol. 48, issue 2, Feb, 2015, pp.41-49. Article [li13] focuses more on the medical application perspective, while article [kang15] focuses more on the engineering technology perspective. To write the two articles, we surveyed many documents/records on medical accidents, medical workflow with safety interlock requirements, and adoption of wireless enabled medical devices. These documents/records include government databases, white papers, articles in magazines, and peer reviewed published papers. We also met with professionals in the medical domain to hear their stories and collect their opinions. Through this survey, we discover the following facts. Medical accidents are common in practice. Many accidents are caused by human errors in enforcing medical workflow safety interlocks. Although smart medical devices are widely available, these devices are mainly designed for isolated usage. Current practice still heavily rely on human doctors/nurses to coordinate/compose the usage of these isolated smart medical devices. If we could enable networked automatic coordination/interlocking of these smart medical devices, many medical accidents can be avoided. Meanwhile, the networked coordination/interlocking should better be through wireless, so as to guarantee mobility and safety (too many wires can cause trip-over-wire accidents in medical environments). On Revised Objective 2: We propose a holistic theoretical framework on online bounded-time-horizon hybrid automata modeling/analysis for risk assessment and mitigation. This work is mainly summarized by the following paper: [li14] Tao Li, Feng Tan, Qixin Wang, Lei Bu, Jian-Nong Cao, Xue Liu, “From Offline toward Real Time: A Hybrid Systems Model Checking and CPS Codesign Approach for Medical Device Plug-and-Play Collaborations,” in IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems, vol. 25, no. 3, March 2014, pp. 642-652. Specifically, we realize that a medical cyber-physical system is a typical hybrid system, which involves both discrete domain computer logic and continuous domain human vital sign dynamics. To carry out risk assessment and mitigation, we need to model the medical cyber-physical systems. Currently, the best known tool to model cyber-physical systems is hybrid automata, which integrates conventional automata (to model discrete domain computer logic) and differential equation sets (to model continuous domain physical dynamics). When applying hybrid automata to model medical cyber-physical systems, however, we encounter two major challenges. First, unlike machineries, it is impractical to describe a human patient’s vital sign dynamics offline using differential equation sets. Second, the holistic medical cyber-physical systems includes many changing variables, which further complicates the hybrid automata model, making offline verification too costly (in terms of computation time). To address these two challenges, we notice that many human vital signs only change smoothly and slowly. For example, blood oxygen level cannot change abruptly in a zigzag shape. Instead, its change is smooth and slow. In short bounded time horizon, dynamics of such vital signs can be linearized, and modeled by linear differential equations. Exploiting this feature, we propose that the hybrid automata for medical cyber-physical systems shall be built periodically online instead of offline. In each period, the vital signs can be modeled with linear differential equations. Meanwhile, during online modeling, many offline variables’ values are fixed, hence become constants for the respective online modeling period. This greatly reduces the hybrid automata complexity and verification cost. Correspondingly, by verifying the online hybrid automata model, we can assess risks in the near future time horizon, so as to trigger corresponding risk mitigation plans. Based on the above heuristics, we propose a workflow to conduct online periodical modeling of medical cyber-physical systems, verify the model to assess risks in near future, and trigger corresponding risk mitigation plans. We proved the decidability of such model verification, and proposed a framework of mechanisms to handle possible deadline misses and provide seamless coverage of future time horizons. We conducted experiments in controlled lab environments to evaluate the feasibility of our proposed methodology. The results show that relative error of risk assessment is contained below 4%, and deadline misses (which will result in false positive alarms) are contained below 2.2%. On Revised Objective 3: We built a prototype upon software defined radio (SDR) platform, and exploit the flexibility/adaptability of SDR to carry out risk mitigation. The work is mainly summarized by the following paper: [wang14] Yufei Wang, Qixin Wang, Guanbo Zheng, Zheng Zeng, Rong Zheng, Qian Zhang, “WiCop: Engineering WiFi Temporal White-Spaces for Safe Operations of Wireless Personal Area Networks in Medical Applications,” in IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing, vol. 13, no. 5, May 2014, pp.1145-1158. We notice that a major threat to wireless medical cyber-physical systems is the coexistence of WiFi and ZigBee. WiFi is a ubiquitous wireless local area network scheme that transmits with high power. In contrast, ZigBee is a wireless personal/body area network scheme features in low transmission power (so as to protect patients and/or other human users from excessive radio frequency radiation). The high power WiFi transmissions thus can often jam ZigBee transmissions. To mitigate this risk, we need a coordinator to arbitrate the transmissions of WiFi and ZigBee. We propose three schemes to achieve this goal. First, we can use fake WiFi physical layer packet header transmissions to suppress other WiFi transmissions. Second, we can use fake multiple access control layer packet header (more specifically, the RTS packet header) transmissions to suppress other WiFi transmissions. Third, we can use controlled continuous WiFi physical layer preamble transmissions to suppress other WiFi transmissions. The third scheme is different from the other two in that the WiFi suppression transmissions are conducted in parallel with (instead of before) ZigBee transmissions, hence the scheme is more effective in suppressing smart WiFi devices. To avoid suppressing the simultaneous ZigBee transmissions, a band pass filter is applied to the WiFi suppression transmissions, so as to leave side lobes of the radio frequency spectrum for ZigBee. The above proposed schemes are cross layer (particularly, cross physical and multiple access layer) and highly diverse. To implement them, we exploit the high flexibility/adaptability of SDR platform, where the entire stack (including the physical layer) of wireless network can be programmed. The specific SDR platform we use is the Microsoft SORA SDR platform. Experiment results show that using our proposed schemes, even under heavy WiFi interferences, the packet reception rate of ZigBee can increase by up to 116%. Another evaluation on ZigBee electrocardiography show that using our proposed schemes, the application layer signal distortions are bounded within 2% even under heavy WiFi interferences.

532812.label: Major findings and research outcome
532812.value: Through our extensive survey on medical accidents, medical workflow with safety interlock requirements, and the adoption of wireless enabled medical devices, we find the following facts. Medical accidents are common in practice. Many accidents are caused by human errors in enforcing medical device coordination interlocks. If we can enable automatic medical device coordination via wireless networks, i.e. build the so-called wireless medical cyber-physical systems (CPS), aforementioned accidents can be greatly reduced. Based on this survey result, we set out to design mechanisms to assess and mitigate/confine risks with wireless medical CPSs. The first is a framework of procedures and theories to assess medical CPS risks online. With the wireless connections, we can have holistic views of the medical device coordination. The goal of the framework is to build holistic model of the medical CPS, predict risks, so as to trigger risk mitigation/confinement actions in time. We exploit the state of the art hybrid automata to model the medical CPS and apply model verifications online as a risk prediction tool. Our experiment evaluations in controlled lab environments show our framework can contain relative error of risk assessment to below 4%, and contain deadline misses (which will cause false positives in risk predictions) of risk assessment to below 2.2%. Depending on the risk predicted, various risk mitigation/confinement plans can be triggered. Many legacy application layer risk mitigation/confinement plans can be reused. However, challenge lies in the new risks brought about by wireless networks, particularly the coexistence risk of WiFi and ZigBee. WiFi is a ubiquitous wireless local area network standard, while ZigBee is a mainstream wireless personal/body area network standard widely adopted by medical devices. Due to the transmission power differences, WiFi communications can often jam ZigBee communications. We propose different cross layer schemes to suppress harmful WiFi transmissions, so as to guarantee QoS of ZigBee communications. We exploited the high flexibility/adaptability of software defined radio (SDR) to implement our proposed schemes. Experiment results show that using our proposed schemes, even under heavy WiFi interferences, the packet reception rate of ZigBee can increase by up to 116%. Another evaluation on ZigBee electrocardiography show that using our proposed schemes, the application layer signal distortions are bounded within 2% even under heavy WiFi interferences.

532812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
532812.value: The research conducted in this project also fosters the inception of several new ideas worthy of further development. Particularly, the wireless medical CPS research also inspires the Internet of Things research on wireless fieldbus scheduling and wireless leasing protocol (see publications listed as Part C.9 item 1, 2 and Part C.8 item 4, 5). The focus on medical CPS can be further extended to other CPSs, for example on robotics CPS and CPS embedded systems hardware (see publications listed as Part C.8 item 6, 7, 8 and Part C.9 item 3).

532812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
532812.value: Through our extensive survey on medical accidents, we find that many accidents are caused by human errors. If we can use wireless networks to connect medical devices, to build a coordinated medical system (the so-called wireless medical CPS), many medical accidents can be avoided. Based on this survey result, we propose a wireless medical CPS framework that can build holistic models of the medical environment and predict risks online. Evaluation results show that our risk prediction framework can contain relative error to below 4%, and contain deadline misses (which will cause false positive alarms) to below 2.2%. With the risk predictions, various application layer risk confinement/mitigation plans can be triggered. However, a new kind of risk is brought about by the deployment of wireless communications, particularly the coexistence of WiFi and ZigBee. Both are widely adopted wireless communication standards, but WiFi can often interfere ZigBee. We further propose a scheme to effectively suppress harmful WiFi communications, so as to guarantee the ZigBee communications. Experiment results show that using our scheme, ZigBee communication quality can increase by up to 116% under heavy WiFi interferences, and application layer signal distortion is controlled by within 2%.

533012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
533012.value: High resolution satellite (HRS) imagery is an attractive option for surveying and mapping applications, the advantages being the capacity for high quality imaging, short revisit time, and lower cost. However, image matching difficulties have, in the past, caused this option not to be widely used in the derivation of 3D urban data especially in metropolitan areas. Automated reliable and dense image matching is essential for photogrammetric 3D data derivation, however, such matching, in urban areas, is extremely difficult, owing to the complexity of urban textures and the severe occlusion problems caused by the impact of tall buildings on the images. It is of note that most of the traditional digital photogrammetry systems require intensive human interaction to process urban area images. This proposal aims at using HRS imagery for automated 3D point cloud generation in metropolitan areas by solving key problems such as those mentioned above. The project objectives include: (1) The development of an integrated point and edge matching method, incorporated in a hierarchical matching propagation process constrained by self-adaptive triangulations. In this way dense and reliable matching results for HRS imagery in metropolitan areas are able to obtain; (2) The development of an occlusion filtering approach to eliminate possible image mismatches, caused by the occlusion problems on the HRS imagery acquired from metropolitan areas; (3) An investigation to find the best photogrammetric techniques for precision 3D point clouds generation based on the matched results, and evaluate the developed methods using HRS imagery in downtown Hong Kong. The newly developed methods and technologies will enable a cheaper, more automated, image-based creation of 3D urban data from HRS imagery. These features will contribute significantly, to urban modelling and mapping applications. In addition, the up-to-date and easy availability of HRS imagery will enable the maintenance and updating of 3D urban models to 4D urban models, hence bringing in element of time change. This process, currently, has seldom been discussed, because of the limiting impact of high cost when using other technologies such as airborne laser scanning. The newly developed innovative image matching strategy can be applied to other aspects including terrestrial images and video sequences, hence facilitating automated image processing for a broad application area in photogrammetry and computer vision. This proposed research will also advance the use of high resolution satellite (HRS) imagery for various urban applications.

533012.label: Realisation of objectives
533012.value: [Objective 1]: For the first objective, we have developed an integrated point and edge matching method based on the self-adaptive triangulation constraint (SATM) for reliable image matching on high-resolution satellite imagery. Effective matching constraints were developed for reliable edge matching, including the triangle constraint, edge orientation constraint, brightness contrast constraint, and epipolar constraint. A shiftable self-adaptive line cross correlation (SSLCC) was developed for similarity comparison of corresponding edges. A hierarchical image matching strategies was developed for reliable and dense image matching, which includes three tiers: 1) feature-to-feature matching and 2) feature-to-area matching based on the self-adaptive triangle constraint, and 3) triangulation constrained dense matching based on the previous matched results. Experiments using high-resolution satellite imagery and terrestrial images proved that the developed method is capable of reducing matching ambiguity and generating dense and accurate point and edge matches preserving the actual textural features, which is ideal for the subsequent 3D modelling. The related results can be found in our publication (Wu et al., 2012, ISPRS Journal). We further extended this method to process half-meter resolution satellite images (Pleiades-1 images) in Hong Kong and the experimental results shown that the method is able to produce dense and reliable image matching results in urban areas. The results can be found in our publication (Ye and Wu, 2016, ISPRS Congress). [Objective 2]: For the second objective, to account for the severe occlusion problems on the images caused by tall buildings in urban areas, we developed a novel strategy to integrate image matching and image segmentation in the same matching propagation process based on our self-adaptive triangulation constrained image matching (SATM) framework. The strategy includes the following key steps: 1) To carry out image segmentation on a reference image (e.g., left image of the stereo pair) based on a mean-shift algorithm, so that typical image plane such as building roofs, slanted walls, roads can be segmented; 2) To generate an initial disparity map based on the initial corresponding triangulations constructed from the seed matches on a pair of stereo images; 3) To derive depth planes by fitting a plane to each of the image segments using the disparity map using a RANSAC algorithm; 4) To carry out occlusion filtering in the matching propagation process by comparing the disparity of the matching candidates with that interpolated from the depth plane. If the difference is greater than an allowable tolerance, a mismatch is detected that may relate to an occlusion problem, and the matching candidate is discarded. Otherwise, the matching candidate passes through the occlusion filter and is considered a potentially correct match, which will be further verified using other constraints in the SATM method. This strategy is able to avoid mismatches in occlusion areas and further improve the reliability of the dense matching results in high-resolution imagery in urban areas. Experiments using the Pleiades-1 satellite imagery (0.5 m/pixel) covering the northern part of Hong Kong Island shown that the developed method is able to obtain dense and reliable image matching results in urban areas with serious occlusion problems. The related results can be found in our publication (Ye and Wu, 2016, ISPRS Congress). We recently further extended the method by accounting for other matching difficulties in urban images such as shadows by tall buildings to further improve the matching performance. Related results have been summarized and submitted to an international journal (PE&RS) for publication. [Objective 3]: For the third objective, we have carried out research and developments in the following three aspects. 1) We systematically studied the geometric modeling of images with different stereo configuration and analyzed the accuracy of measurement based on error propagation for different baseline lengths, different focal lengths, etc. Monte Carlo simulation and actual experiments were conducted to verify the theoretical analysis, from which optimum configuration of images with the best potential measurement accuracy can be obtained. The related results can be found in the publication (Wu et al., 2015, PE&RS). 2) We developed an integrated 3D mapping model to integrate multiple-source images and other datasets for improved geopositioning accuracy, so that to generate accurate 3D point clouds based on the matched results on the images. An innovative approach was developed for the integrated processing of multiple-source and multiple-resolution satellite images. Satellite images with different stereo configurations and different convergence angles were investigated in order to achieve the best geo-positioning accuracy. The approach is able to improve the rational polynomial coefficients (RPCs) of the images and decrease the inconsistencies between the images and subsequently improving their geopositioning accuracy. Experiments using the ZY-3, SPOT-7, and Pleiades-1 satellite imagery in Hong Kong and Cartosat-1 and Worldview-1 satellite imagery in Spain verified that the integrated 3D mapping model effectively improves the geopositioning accuracies of the various types of images from different satellite platforms. The related results can be found in our publications (Wu et al., 2015, ISPRS Journal; Tang and Wu, 2016, ISPRS Journal). 3) We further studied the classification of the 3D point clouds generated from the previous steps for urban related applications. An adaptive surface filter algorithm was developed for this purpose and the related results can be found in our publication (Hu et al., 2016, ISPRS Journal).

533012.label: Major findings and research outcome
533012.value: We developed an innovative approach for the integrated point and edge matching based on the self-adaptive triangulation constraint for reliable image matching on high-resolution satellite imagery. The developed approach has been verified by using high-resolution satellite imagery in Hong Kong and other images and proved to be able to generate dense and reliable image matching results. The related results can be found in our publications (Wu et al., 2012, ISPRS Journal; Ye and Wu, 2016, ISPRS Congress). We developed an innovative and unique strategy for occlusion filtering by incorporating image matching and image segmentation in the same matching propagation process, so that to avoid mismatches in occlusion areas and further improve the reliability of the dense matching results in high-resolution imagery in urban areas. The developed approach has been validated using the high-resolution Pleiades-1 satellite imagery in Hong Kong and the related results can be found in the publications (Ye and Wu, 2016, ISPRS Congress; Ye and Wu, 2016, submitted to PE&RS). We systematically studied the geometric modeling of images with different stereo configuration and developed an integrated 3D mapping model to integrate multiple-source satellite images and other datasets for improved geopositioning accuracy. The developed approaches have been verified using various types of high-resolution satellite images in Hong Kong and other regions, and the related results can be found in our publications (Wu et al., 2015, PE&RS; Wu et al., 2015, ISPRS Journal; Tang and Wu, 2016, ISPRS Journal). This research has been recognized by an invitation from the International Journal of Image and Data Fusion to contribute a review article (Wu and Tang, 2015, IJIDF) in this aspect. The research and developments also led to a Gold Medal and a Special Merit Award (R. Alekseev Award) at the 44th International Exhibition of Inventions of Geneva in April 2016. The achievements have been covered by various media. Examples of media coverage are attached in the report. Photogrammetric point clouds generated from high-resolution satellite imagery has great potential for 3D mapping and city modelling applications due to its low-cost and quick updating. This research outputs from this project facilitate the use of multiple-source satellite imagery for urban applications.

533012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
533012.value: The developed methods and results from this project can be further extended for 3D city modelling applications, which can contribute to the various aspects in the smart city development in Hong Kong.

533012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
533012.value: This project developed innovative approaches for reliable and dense image matching on satellite images in urban areas by integrating point and edge matching and incorporating an occlusion filtering strategy in the self-adaptive triangulation constrained image matching (SATM) framework, and developed innovative methods for improved geopositioning accuracy of the satellite images, from which to generate accurate 3D point clouds from the satellite images. The developed methods and technologies enable a cheaper, more automated, quick-updating, image-based creation of 3D urban data from high-resolution satellite imagery, which has great potential for 3D mapping and modelling applications in urban areas. The results from this project also facilitate the use of high-resolution satellite imagery for other various applications in the smart city development in Hong Kong.

533112.label: Realisation of objectives
533112.value: This project studied a new class of principle agent problems where the probability distortion plays a key role. It aimed to study how the probability distortion will affect the principle's and the agent's strategies. Such problems had never been considered in the literature. This is an important but challenging unexplored research field. Hence, many fundamental problems remain open and new methodologies await to be developed. In this project, we have developed new methods to solve the proposed interrelated problems and obtained many useful results both from theory and practice points of view. All the proposed targets were addressed in our work. One can see them in the published works in the report. It is the quantile formulation which we have developed to tackle the proposed problems when the probability distortion is involved in the models. Classical tools such as stochastic control and free boundary theories in PDE were widely used to solve the problems as well. Because the class of problems is new and had never been studied before, there are many open problems to be tackled. We hope to propose a new research project to continue the study of this direction in the future.

533112.label: Major findings and research outcome
533112.value: There are many important findings and outcome of this project. For instance, the relaxation method were introduced by the principle investigator in his former research project. In this project, we continued the study and further developed the relaxation method so as to tackle the proposed problems. We have used this technique in the paper "A robust Markowitz mean-variance portfolio selection model with an intractable claim" done by the principle investigator and his PhD student. In this work, we introduced the concept of intractable claims and studied its impact on the mean variance investment strategies. Such model with intractable claims had never been investigated in the literature and we formulated it as a robust control problem. However, because of the time-inconsistent nature of the problem, both the standard penalization approach and the duality method used to tackle robust stochastic control problems fail in solving our problem. Instead, the quantile formulation approach was adopted to tackle the problem. The problem was completely solved and explicit closed-form solutions were obtained. The properties of the mean-variance frontier were also discussed in the paper. This paper has been published in the top-tier journal the SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics in the filed. We believe this is one of the most import outcomes of this project. We have also made many other contributions from this project and list the published papers in the final report.

533112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
533112.value: Because the class of problems proposed in this project is new and has never been studied before this project, there are many open problems to be tackled and many potentials for further development of our research project. For instance, the problems have never been considered when the market is not the Black-Scholes market. In non Black-Scholes market, quantile formulation, the main tool developed in the present project, can hardly been used to solve the problems. New methods are thus called for in order to analyze and solve them. We hope to propose a new research project to continue the study of this direction in the future.

533112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
533112.value: This project aimed to address the impact of twisted believes on people's investment strategies. The twisted believes are mathematically expressed by the probability distortion or weighting function. Because of the existence of the probability distortion function, people's investment strategies have totally changed and many abnormal behaviors appeared in the financial market. It may be one of the possible cause of the financial crisis. We hope the findings of this research project can help people have a better understanding of financial investment, risk management, and financial market.

533212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
533212.value: Air conditioning (A/C) systems with the ability of simultaneous control of indoor temperature and humidity are essential for building a comfortable and healthy environment. However, conventional A/C systems employing chilled water coils for cooling and dehumidification are usually able to maintain indoor temperature while allowing indoor humidity to vary unfavorably. Considerable research has been done on how to design and control A/C systems to achieve better humidity control. Unfortunately, improving humidity control is always accompanied with more energy consumption and/or more complicated systems. The root cause of the unsatisfactory humidity control is the coupled cooling and dehumidification processes at chilled water coils; therefore decoupling these two processes is a straightforward and effective solution. The primary purpose of this study is to decoupling cooling and dehumidification in air handling processes so as to improve the performances of conventional A/C systems in humidity control. This project will first investigate the reachable handling region of the sensible heat ratio (SHR) of chilled water coils using steady-state parametric analysis of heat and mass transfer. A universal model of the reachable region will be developed, which defines the adjustable range of the SHR with various configuration and operating parameters. This model is therefore valuable for optimizing coils’ configurations, selecting coils in design and regulating the air handling process in operation to achieve more adjustable SHR. Then, an air-handling process with new system configuration dedicated to decouple cooling and dehumidification in the reachable handling region will be investigated. Numerical and experimental study will be conducted to characterize the dynamics of the air handling process. Open-loop and closed-loop dynamic responses will be obtained, which will be used to develop robust decoupling control strategy. The control performances under dynamic operating conditions will be tested using both simulation and experiment tests. Lastly, this project will compare the capability for adjusting the SHR, thermal comfort and energy consumption of the new air handling process with those of the conventional one using year-round dynamic simulation. Furthermore, due to the use of three-way valves in the new system configuration, energy consumption and operation strategy of the central chiller plant supplying chilled water to the air handling process will be influenced. Practical application issues will be identified and addressed. This research will generate both theoretical and practical knowledge needed to create more comfortable and healthy built environment in a robust and energy-efficient way in buildings served by conventional A/C systems. 533212.label: Realisation of objectives
533212.value: All four objectives have been realized. To address the first objective, steady-state parametric analysis based on a cross-counter flow heat exchanger model was conducted to investigate the heat and mass transfer at the chilled water cooling coil. The model was used to predict the leaving air temperature and humidity at given inlet air conditions, when the operating parameters including the chilled water flow rate, air flow rate and chilled water temperature were changing. Coils with different configuration parameters including the row number and the fin geometries were analyzed. The cooling and dehumidification capacities as well as the sensible heat ratio under different operating conditions and with different configuration parameters were obtained. To address the second objective, a set of experimental test rig was established. The test rig consists of three sub-systems, i.e., air pre-treatment and supply sub-system, chilled water supply and control sub-system as well as data collection and analysis sub-system. The major components installed in the air sub-system include a centrifugal fan, an electric heater, a humidifier and a cooling coil. The chilled water supplied to the cooling coil is produced by a small chiller. Two three-way valves and one small pump are installed in the chilled water supply and return pipes. Instruments for measuring temperature, humidity and flow rate of the air and the temperature, flow rate of the chilled water are installed and the measurements are collected to the computer by a data acquisition unit. Experimental tests were conducted to test the decoupled cooling and dehumidification capabilities of the cooling coil under different conditions. The two undergraduate students participated in the experimental tests and data analysis, which helped them to gain the first-hand experience in doing research. The experiment test rig will be used not only in further R&D of air conditioning system with independent temperature and humidity control, but also in teaching and learning of relevant subjects in the department. To address the third and the forth objectives, a robust decoupling control strategy using the two PID split-range control logic were developed based on the outcomes of objective one and two. The principle of the decoupling strategy is to adjust the chilled water flow rate to maintain the supply air temperature at its set point and to adjust the chilled water supply temperature to maintain the supply air humidity at its set point. In this way, the simultaneous active control of the supply air temperature and humidity control be achieved and hence the decoupled cooling and dehumidification processes at the chilled water cooling coil. An air-handling unit with a chilled water cooling coil, heater and humidifier were built on TRNSYS platform. The decoupling strategy was implemented in the simulated air-handling unit. A diversity of cases with different typical load conditions were studied using simulation tests. The energy performance of the decoupled strategy was compared with the conventional air handling process without decoupling. The results show that the decoupling strategy can achieve power saving of 30–50%. Occupant’s thermal comfort can also be improved because both the indoor temperature and humidity can be actively controlled, while only the indoor temperature is actively controlled in conventional air conditioning system. Based on the experiment and simulation results, practical suggestions on select and control of chilled water cooling coil were given. It is suggested that, in practical applications to achieve decoupled cooling and dehumidification at the chilled water cooling coil, the heat transfer area should be enlarged and calculated under a higher inlet temperature of the chilled water. As a result, the adjustable range of the sensible heat ratio can be enlarged to match the changing sensible and latent loads in the year round operations. Implementing the decoupling strategy is an effective means to realizing reliable temperature and humidity independent control.

533212.label: Major findings and research outcome
533212.value: The influences of operating parameters, including the chilled water flow rate, chilled water temperature and air flow rate, on the cooling capacity and the sensible heat ratio (SHR) of the chilled water cooling coil were studied experimentally. The total cooling capacity is higher when operating at high chilled water and air flow rates and low chilled water temperature. However, there is a critical value for the chilled water flow rate, above which the performance of the cooling coil will not change significantly. Meanwhile, a higher air flow rate results in a smaller humidity difference between the inlet and outlet air. The experiment results also indicate that the SHR increases with the increase of the chilled water temperature. The adjustable range for SHR is found to increase with the chilled water temperature while the increase rate declines at high chilled water temperature between 0.3 and 1.0. Besides, the adjustable range for SHR decreases when the chilled water flow rate increases. A liner regression model was developed to calculate the SHR of the chilled water coil. The results prove that the chilled water temperature can be used as the primary control variable and the chilled water flow rate used as the secondary control variable. A robust decoupling control strategy based on the two PID split-range control logic were developed and compared with the conventional system without decoupling control in terms of energy consumption. It was concluded that by adjusting the flow rate and the temperature of the chilled water into the cooling coil, the temperature and the humidity of the process air can be controlled independently with a high precision under different working conditions. When such a cooling coil is designed, the heat transfer area should be enlarged and calculated under a higher inlet temperature of the chilled water to guarantee a good performance under various conditions. It was found that the energy saving could reach 30%-50% in simulation tests due to the reduced reheating energy. The influence of typical faults in chillers and air terminals were also investigated. One set of experimental test rig was established. Two undergraduate students was trained in this project. They conducted experiments on the test rig and analyzed the data for their final-year research projects. The test rig can be used to for teaching and research in the coming years. Three SCI journal papers have been published. The funding support has been acknowledged in the published papers.

533212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
533212.value: A new configuration of the chilled water cooling coil and its associated control logic for decoupling cooling and dehumidification has been developed in this project. Although the performance of the control logic was tested and cooling energy saving has been proved using simulation tests, the influence of installing the control devices (mainly two three-way valves and one small pump) in the chilled water pipework is uncertain. Considering there are a large number of cooling coils installed in modern high-rise buildings, the influence of the new devices in the pipework must be considered, which may cause flow-pressure imbalance and influence the chilled water distribution in the whole building. Therefore, the PI plans to investigate the flow-pressure balance problem in the chilled water distribution network after installing the control devices between the supply and return pipes of cooling coils. After this problem is solved, the new technology is ready for practical application. The PI will seek collaboration with the industry to transfer this technology to real products for retrofit of existing air conditioning systems to create more comfortable and healthy built environment in a reliable and energy-efficient way.

533212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
533212.value: Most air conditioning systems aiming to provide a thermally comfortable environment only control indoor temperature, while allow the indoor humidity to fluctuate. It is certainly undesirable because both temperature and humidity significantly influence occupant’s thermal sensation and heath. Improving humidity control is always accompanied with more energy consumption and more complicated air conditioning systems. This project aims to achieve independent temperature and humidity control at minimum energy and retrofit costs in conventional air conditioning systems. The key point to achieve this aim is to decouple the cooling and dehumidification processes in air-handling units, which are commonly used to treat the air to a cold and dry condition and then supply it to the air conditioned space. The feasibility of the decoupled control was first studied theoretically and experimentally. Next, advanced decoupling strategy based on the split range control logic was developed. Then, the performance of the decoupling strategy was tested and compared with conventional air handling process without decoupling. Finally, practical suggestions were provided to achieve independent temperature and humidity control. This research project generates both theoretical and practical knowledge needed for creating more comfortable and healthy built environment in a reliable and energy-efficient way in conventional air conditioning systems.

533312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
533312.value: Through millions of years’ evolution, many organisms in nature have developed hard tissues such as shell-like exoskeletons to increase their chance of survival in severe predatory competitions. These natural biomaterials are normally composed of ordinary constituents but possess extraordinary mechanical properties that are clearly beyond the capability of conventional engineering. For instance, the nacre layer in mollusk shells exhibits toughness 3,000 times higher than that of aragonite, its primary (>95 wt%) ingredient. Understanding the fundamental principles of these natural materials and then duplicating their superiority in engineering should be an efficient approach to improving the properties of man-made materials. Recently, enormous efforts have been dedicated to the research on natural biomaterials such as mollusk shell, bone, and fish scale, giving rise to a number of valuable findings, some of which have been applied to the synthesis of novel materials. However, most investigations so far have been focused on biomaterials that serve as protective armors. Since no evidence have showed that natural evolution has any bias in favor of defenders, it should be of equivalent significance to explore the other side of the coin, the invasive biomaterials. Motivated by this conception, in this proposed research we turn our attention to the teeth of black carp, which is a species of cyprinid fish generally feeding on shelled mollusks such as snails and mussels. The fact that black carp can crush stiff and tough mollusk shells with ease suggests that its teeth ought to be superior in mechanical properties over mollusk shells. To determine such mechanical superiority and reveal the underlying ingenious strategies for material design, a systematic investigation on the teeth of black carp is proposed here, including identification of chemical compositions, microstructure observation and mechanical characterization. The obtained structural and material information provides basis for the follow-up exploration of the correlations between material constituents, structures, mechanical properties and physiological functions. Comparative studies between the black carp teeth and the mollusk shells will be conducted as well to understand how defensive and invasive biomaterials are shaped by each other through competitive predatory interaction in between. The outcomes of this project would not only shed light on the ingenious design principles concealed in natural materials but also provide guidelines for the fabrication of engineering materials such as dental restorative materials. 经过几百万年的进化，自然界中的许多生物都进化出了坚硬的组织（比如壳状的外骨骼）用来提高它们在激烈的捕食竞争中的生存几率。虽然这些天然生物材料的组成成份很普通，但它们具有着比一般工程材料更为优越的力学性能。比如说，贝壳的贝母层中文石占了95%以上，但它的断裂韧性却是文石的3,000倍。理解这些天然生物材料优越的力学性能的背后的机理，然后将这些机理在工程中进行重现和复制无疑是一种提高现有人工材料性能的有效方法。近年来，人们对天然生物材料（贝壳、骨骼、鱼鳞）开展了广泛的研究，取得了很多有价值的成果。有些成果已经应用到新材料的合成中去了。但是，到目前为止，大多数研究都集中在防御性的生物材料上，比如贝壳和鱼鳞。没有证据表明，生物进化会对捕食竞争中的防御方有偏爱。因此，对攻击性生物材料的研究也同样具有重要的意义。受到这个思想的启发，我们将注意力转移到了一种叫“青鱼”的鱼类的牙齿上。这种鱼的特点是以带壳软体动物（比如螺、贻贝）为食。青鱼能够咬碎坚硬的贝壳说明它的牙齿应该具有比贝壳更为优越的力学性能。为了确定青鱼牙齿是否真具有这种优越性并揭示这种优越性的力学机理，我们提出对青鱼的牙齿进行系统的研究包括化学成分的表征，微观结构的观察和力学性能的测量。然后，我们将以得到的结构和材料信息为基础，建立化学成分、结构、力学性能、生理功能之间的联系。此外，我们还将对青鱼牙齿和贝壳进行比较研究，从而了解防御性和攻击性生物材料如何在相互竞争中互相影响。本项目的结果，不仅有助于我们理解天然生物材料中独特的材料设计理念，而且对仿生材料（如：牙齿修复材料）的制备有着重要的指导意义。

533312.label: Realisation of objectives
533312.value: Objective 1: To characterize the structures and mechanical properties of black carp teeth from macro scale to nano scale. The structural characterization of black carp teeth was carried out thoroughly by using optical microscope and field emission scanning electron microscopy imaging. It was discovered that at macro length scale, the black carp tooth consists of two layers: the outer enameloid layer and the inner dentin layer. Like the teeth of many animals, the enameloid of black carp teeth is also made of hydroxyaptite (HAp) crystals. From the outer side to the inner side, the ultrastructure of enameloid exhibits significant variation. In particular, in the outer portion, HAp crystals are parallel bundled to each other while tangled bundled in the middle portion; in the inner portion, the structure exhibits crossed lamellar configuration. In order to examine the crystalline orientation of the enameloid, comparative XRD analysis was carried out. It was found that the HAp crystals of enameloid do not distribute randomly in space. Instead, their distribution exhibit preferential orientation of the c-axis near the surface of enameloid. The mechanical properties, mainly the modulus and hardness, of black carp teeth were characterized by using nanoindentation technique. To capture the possible variation of the mechanical properties (i.e. inhomogeneity) within the teeth, multiple patterned nanoindentations were performed along the prescribed paths. The inter-indentation spacing was chosen as less as possible to achieve the spatial resolution as high as possible. The averaged modulus and hardness of enameloid are about 80 GPa and 4 GPa respectively, while those of the dentin are about 20 GPa and 1 GPa. Moreover, the mechanical properties exhibit gradient within the enameloid layer. For example, the modulus obtained by nanoindentation exhibits decreasing gradient of 0.1 GPa/m. from the surface to the inner of the enameloid. Additionally, nanoindentations on cross-sections of different orientations were also carried out, which revealed that the mechanical properties of the enameloid are also dependent on the direction. Enameloid displays the highest modulus and hardness along the direction perpendicular to the occlusal surface. In order to characterize the wear resistance of enameloid, scratch tests were carried out using Berkovich probe and conical probe, respectively. These two probes have tip radii of different sizes and therefore can be used to examine the wear resistance at different length scales. It was revealed that the occlusal surface of enameloid exhibits superior wear resistance compared to the other sectional surfaces. Upon the completion of above work, the Objective 1 of this project is achieved 100%. Objective 2: To develop an understanding of macro-, micro- and nano- structures of black carp teeth, and their connections to mechanical endurance and wear resistance; to create a comprehensive knowledge base of the design principles linked to their physiological functions. It was observed that the enameloid of black carp will be fractured, under sufficiently high indentation, through ring cracking. From the perspective of structural integrity, ring cracking is much better than the radial cracking if the fracture of materials is unavoidable because the former is much more localized and therefore less destructive than the latter. To shed light on the mechanics behind such preference to ring cracking as exhibited by the teeth of black carp, theoretical modeling and numerical simulation were carried out. We modeled the black carp tooth as a bimaterial containing a brittle coating (enameloid) and an elastic substrate (dentin). Stress field developed in the coating under indentation load was solved. Based on the maximum-tensile-stress criterion, the failure occurrence and the morphology of the resulting crack were predicted. Our results showed that the fracture mode (ring cracking v.s. radial cracking) of the coating is determined by two dimensionless parameters characterizing the systems. One of them is the modulus ratio between the coating and substrate or the modulus mismatch of this bimaterial. There exists a critical modulus mismatch below which ring cracking will be developed irrespective of the value of the other parameter. This finding explained the reason why black carp teeth tend to be fractured through ring crack rather than radial crack. Additionally, experimental verification was also carried out on the synthetic bimaterials containing quartz plates attached on cement substrates. The experimental results showed a good agreement with the theoretical prediction. Considering the physiological function of the black carp teeth, such tendency to ring cracking under indentation load seems not random but designed and can ensure the structural integrity and avoid catastrophic failure of the teeth. The mechanics learned from the black carp teeth also apply to the design of engineering bimaterials. To account for the prominent wear resistance of the occlusal surface over the other sectional surfaces, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were carried out, indicating that the (001) surface of the single crystal HAp exhibits much better wear resistance than the other crystalline planes. This finding in combination with the c-axis preferential orientation as discovered in the XRD characterization explained why the occlusal surfaces of the black carp teeth exhibits prominent wear resistance. This explanation also agrees well with the physiological function of the black carp teeth as the apparatus for grinding and cutting food. Upon the completion of above work, the Objective 2 of this project is achieved 100%. Objective 3: To verify the advantages of the black carp teeth over the snail shell in mechanical properties; to reveal the mechanics underlying such advantages As the natural competitors of black carp teeth, the snail shells (Cipangopaludina chinensis) and their mechanical properties also deserve our attention for better understanding of the black carp teeth. Intuitively, it is nature to attribute the capability of the black carp to crush the snail shell to the better mechanical properties of the teeth over the shell. To very this hypothesis, nanoindentations were carried out on the snail shells. Surprisingly, the measured modulus and hardness of the snail shells were 86.26±7.87GPa and 4.14±0.56 GPa, respectively, which is comparable to those of the enameloid of the black carp teeth. This finding is out of expectation. In order to explain why the black carp teeth can crush the snail shells with comparable mechanical properties, finite element analysis was carried out. In our FEA simulation, we mainly focused on the effect of the geometrical structure of the shell on the stress field due to the squeeze by the black carp teeth. It is found that whether a snail shell is crushable or not, for given pharyngeal teeth, depends on the radius (R) and thickness (t) of the shell. A predation map for black carp teeth is constructed by delimiting the t-R plane into three phasic regions corresponding to three possible consequences of the mechanical competition between pharyngeal teeth and shells. It is interesting to notice that all the freshwater shells chosen at random fall in the crushable regime while the seashells do not necessarily. This feature of black carp teeth can be speculated as a result of evolution in response to its freshwater diet. Upon the completion of above work, the Objective 3 of this project is achieved 100%.

533312.label: Major findings and research outcome
533312.value: Structural and mechanical characterizations were conducted on the pharyngeal teeth and the shells, showing that the enameloid (the outermost layer) of black carp teeth has similar elastic modulus and hardness in comparison to those of the pond snail shells. To shed light on the mechanics of black carp teeth crushing mollusk shell, parametric studies on the geometry of shells were conducted by using finite element analysis (FEA). It was found that whether a mollusk shell is crushable or not depends on the radius (R) and thickness (t) of the shell. A t-R map (predation map) was developed, giving rise to a region corresponding to crushable shells. Subsequent examination indicated that the geometries (R and t) of many fresh water species fall in the crushable region while those of the sea shells are beyond the crushing capability of black carp. Under indentation load, the enameloid of black carp tends to fail through ring cracking while some artificial brittle coatings (e.g. epoxy coated with glass) tend to fail through radial cracking. Inspired by this discovery, the determinants of fracture modes (ring cracking & radial cracking) of brittle coatings under indentation were investigated. Rigorous theoretical analysis and numerical simulation indicated that fracture modes of brittle coating are determined synergistically by two dimensionless parameters which are functions of the mechanical properties and some geometric parameters. A map of fracture modes was developed, whereby the fracture mode should be directly predicated based on the two dimensionless parameters. Experimental verification of the fracture-mode map was also carried out by examining the fracture modes of fused quartz/cement bilayer materials under indentation. The experimental observation exhibited a good agreement with the prediction by theoretical fracture-mode map. Our investigation on the anisotropic wear resistance of black carp teeth showed that the occlusal surface exhibits better scratch resistance compared to the other sections of the enameloid. XRD tests showed the major component of black carp enameloid is hydroxyapatite crystals which exhibit c-axis preferential orientation normal to the occlusal surface. To explain this anisotropic wear resistance, a theoretical scratching model was built up based on the classic wear theory. It was showed that for the given pyramidal scratching tool, solid surfaces with higher toughness/shear strength ratio (e.g. occlusal surface) tend to have better wear resistance. Therefore, the prominent wear resistance of occlusal surface can be attributed to the higher toughness/shear strength ratio of occlusal surface.

533312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
533312.value: Future work can be done in the following two aspects: 1. In the study of fracture modes control for bilayer materials, the failure criterion employed is the maximum-tensile-stress criterion, which may not apply to all materials. Extensive studies can be made by applying other failure criteria, such as maximum-shear-stress criterion or maximum-tensile-strain criterion, into our theoretical framework. 2. Qualitatively, the c-axis preferential orientation of hydroxyapatite has been confirmed by the XRD tests on bulk tooth specimens. However, more quantitative methodology can be employed to characterize the accurate distribution of hydroxyapatite crystals such as Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) in order to obtain insight into the relationship between the structure and mechanical properties at atomic length scale. 3. Our work implied a strategy for prohibiting catastrophic damage of material by controlling the fracture mode. Similar strategies may also exist and deserve our further investigations.

533312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
533312.value: The structural and compositional information and mechanical properties of black carp tooth were firstly understood upon the completion of the present research. The construction of predation map of black carp reveals that black carp teeth can crush mollusk shells with proper shell radius and thickness combination. Besides, the prominent wear ability of black carp teeth due to its preferential orientation of the crystal alignment may be of great value to the design of anti-wear materials. Moreover, the bilayer design strategy adopted by the black carp teeth also can be a practical guideline for the design of the protective coating for materials. In summary, this project not only elucidated the mechanics accounting for the superior mechanical properties of the black carp teeth but provided guidance to the design of synthetic materials and structures for better mechanical properties.

533412.value: 基於諧振光隧穿效應的新型光纖光學液體折射率傳感器

533412.label: Project Objectives
533412.value: To conduct the theoretical study of the ROTE based on both the nano-optics interpretation and quantum mechanics interpretation. To design new refractive index sensor that is constructed by a pair of angled fibers. To fabricate and characterize the refractive index sensor that utilizes the resonant optical tunneling effect.
rows: To conduct the theoretical study of the ROTE based on both the nano-optics interpretation and quantum mechanics interpretation.
To design new refractive index sensor that is constructed by a pair of angled fibers.
To fabricate and characterize the refractive index sensor that utilizes the resonant optical tunneling effect.

533412.label: Realisation of objectives
533412.value: (1) In theory, we have developed the theoretical models using the transfer matrix model (TMM) for the nano-optics interpretation and the potential barrier model (PBM) for the quantum mechanics interpretation. And we have further investigated their analog relationships in terms of transmission spectra and phase delays. Good match has been achieved except for a phase difference of about Pi. This is then solved by considering the Goos–Hänchen effect. (2) In device design, we have found that the s-polarization is more sensitive to the refractive index change than the p-polarization, by a factor of about 100 times. With optimized parameters, the sensor is designed to reach the sensitivity of 81,000 nm/RIU, which surpasses all the developed refractive index sensors. (3) In experimental study, we have fabricated the ROTE sensors using angled fibers that are polished with different angles (e.g., 45 deg, 63 deg and 75 deg) and are then coated with gold films with the thickness of 10 – 30 nm. The device obtains a sensitivity 3,500 nm/RIU in experiment, as compared to the expected 81,000 nm/RIU in theory. The difference is due to the absorption of gold films and the alignment difficulties.

533412.label: Major findings and research outcome
533412.value: The major findings include (1) Our theoretical analyses have found that the nano-optics interpretation and the quantum mechanics interpretation are equivalent in predicting the transmission spectrum, but they have a Pi shift in the phase of transmitted light. This can be explained by considering the Goos–Hänchen effect. This is the first time to find that the Goos–Hänchen effect is essential for the ROTE effect and how it play the role. (2) Our comparative study of the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) effect and the ROTE effect shows that both can be predicted by the TMM model and the SPR effect in a metallic film is the base for the ROTE effect. (3) Our parametric study of the ROTE sensors using dielectric and metallic films has found that the S-polarization gives ~1000 higher sensitivity as compared to the P-polarization. (4) Our experimental study of ROTE sensors using a pair of polished, Au-coated, angled fibers has obtained a sensitivity of 3,500 nm/RIU, which is very high as compared to other refractive index sensors that using lossy films (e.g., metallic films) as the light transmission media. The major research outputs include (1) Published 5 journal papers. The theoretical analysis and discussion was published in IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics as an invited review in 2013. The device design and experimental results of angled fiber sensors were published in IEEE Sensors Journal in 2014. Other related work was published in another 3 papers, one of which has already cited by more than 100 times/year. (2) Trained one PhD student, Ms. Huang Xiaowen, who submitted the thesis in May 2017 with the title “Microfluidics-based Sensors for Artificial Photosynthesis” (3) Established close research collaboration with researchers of other institutes. For example, we have been working with Professor Aoqun Jian at Taiyuan University of Technology on the fabrication and testing of ROTE and SPR sensors. We have also collaborated with Professor Din Ping Tsai of National University of Taiwan on the study of SPR effect. In addition, we have successfully worked with Professor Weixing Yu of Xi’an Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanism, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, on the photopatterning of gold films on angled fiber ends. Moreover, internal collaborations with Dr Yu Wang, Dr Yuen Hong Tsang and Dr Mo Yang have been built up in various aspects like modeling, fabrication and sample preparations.

533412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
533412.value: The theory will be further studies for more layers and will be compared with the multilayer thin film theory. The ROTE sensors will be further developed using the microfluidic structures for biochemical sensing in solutions and using the angled-fiber structures for gas sensing.

533412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
533412.value: The resonant optical tunneling effect (ROTE) is a unique physical mechanism that enables the resonance of the tunneled lightwave in a multilayered optical micro-cavity. This project aims at the theoretical studies of the ROTE and its applications for liquid refractive index sensing. In theory, we have developed the transfer matrix model (TMM) based on the nano-optics interpretation and the potential barrier model (PBM) based on the quantum mechanics interpretations; and we have also studies their equivalences in transmission spectrum. Analyses have shown that the ROTE sensors are advantageous over the other sensors in terms of sensitivity, device size and capabilities. Particularly, its mechanism is new as compared to any of the previous methods, and it could potentially achieve an ultrahigh sensitivity of 10^(-9) RIU (refractive index unit), two orders higher than the best results of current methods. In experiment, we have constructed the ROTE sensors using a pair of gold-coated angled fibers and have obtained the sensitivity of 3,500 nm/RIU, corresponding to about 10^(-6) RIU. It well demonstrates the potential of ROTE sensors. In conclusion, this project has conducted the first systematic theoretical study of the ROTE and has also presented the first experimental study for sensor applications.

540512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
540512.value: The population is aging rapidly in many major cities worldwide, and Hong Kong is one example for a dense city. The needs of this elderly population have evolved due to social, economic, environmental and political transformations. Most research on urban design for the elderly has been focusing mainly on the physical urban environment, campaigning for barrier free and universal design, maximizing older people’s independence and economic affordability. More research is needed to address the integrated relationships between the urban environment and the social needs of the older people. In urban environment, open space is recognized as increasingly significant element to elderly people nowadays, who are becoming more mobile in their living environment. Public open space can enhance the social relations and interactions of elderly people with other people in a city. It offers physical, sociological and psychological benefits and also enhances the quality of life of older people. However, criteria for provision of outdoor spaces affecting older people’s well-being and quality of life are not fully investigated. This study focuses on the social aspects of the elderly people to investigate the extent that public open space can enhance the concept of active aging and improve the quality of life of the older people. Research generally concluded that open space is far from satisfactory in both quality and quantity in dense cities. In addition, the elderly population is relatively concentrated in the older districts that need regeneration, like in the case of Hong Kong. The needs of the elderly have not been effectively incorporated into the planning of urban space. In this context, urban renewal, as a second chance to re-plan our cities with the benefits of learning from existing conditions, should play a vital role to support other policy instruments to integrate and enhance the quality of life of different age groups. In particular, with the issue of land scarcity and intense pressure on economic growth, open space provision as an allocation of public resources, tends to be sacrificed for urban (re)development. Thus, this proposed study focuses on the planning of urban renewal districts to identify the underlying social considerations for providing open space which embraces the needs of the older people in urban outdoor environment, and hence, improve the quality of life of the older people and their integration with city.

540512.label: Realisation of objectives
540512.value: Conducted the research process as planned. Difficulties encountered in recruiting good researchers, as they look for short term job. This was overcome by successful engaging a post-doctoral researcher who has career commitment. No significant change from that of the original proposal. Achieved all the major objectives as stated in the proposal. Details Appointed a research fellow, a research assistant and some student helpers to work on the project as budgeted. Conducted thorough critical review of literature to identify the needs of the older people in public open space. Develop the preliminary conceptual framework and questions for the focus groups and the empirical surveys. Completed focus group exercises for elderly people in two districts (Hung Hom and Kwun Tong) to develop design considerations for the planning of open space which caters the needs of the elderly in urban renewal districts. Carried out observation study in the two districts to observe the ways the elderly people use the open space in the study districts. Based on the findings obtained from the focus groups and the observation studies designed questions for structured surveys, which have been carried out by face-to-face interviews with the elderly people, with the help of student helpers. Data analysed and delivered public presentations and research seminars which help to refine the research findings. Prepared paper for publication with papers published in top tier international journals (see list at research outcome at Part C)

540512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
540512.value: The elderly often spend a considerable amount of time in public parks, particular in highly dense cities. It is commonly recognised that the social dimension of environments have a significant influence on the health and well-being of the elderly. This study has developed design considerations for the planning of open space which caters the needs of the elderly in urban renewal districts, with particular case study to two districts (Hung Hom and Kwun Tong). For generalization, the results of this study highlight that social connection is considered the most important criteria among the three selected parks. The results show what criteria planners should consider in order to better design public parks in urban renewal so as to satisfy the specific needs of the elderly. It has also highlighted that designs of public parks in the future could provide better space and opportunities for incorporating participation in the general planning and design in their local parks.

540712.label: Realisation of objectives
540712.value: With this grant, we have successfully conducted one survey study, one large-scale experimental study, and collected a unique dataset capturing daily observation from a popular crowdsourcing community. These datasets have helped us develop two major research papers: one is about the effects of customer participation on customers' flow experiences, interpersonal attractions and subsequent service evaluation and behavioral outcomes whereas the other is examining how customer participation in the form of online posting ideas can drive their behavioral outcomes such as idea quantity and idea quality. For the first research paper, we have collected data from multiple informants including customer, employees, and their respective supervisors so as to provide a dyadic view of customer participation experiences and how their interactions with the employees can facilitate their flow experiences as well as subsequent service behaviors such as citizenship or proactive behaviors that are rated by the employees. We have also explored supervisors' leadership, employees' similarities with the customers, and service climate as some significant contextual factors that could influence customers' perceived interpersonal attraction with the employees as well as their flow experiences. However, the results are not that supportive and so we are in the process of fine-tuning the conceptual framework as well as searching of other conceptually and empirically relevant boundary conditions. But we found that some findings that relate to the interaction of customer and employee as well as the service climate are particularly interesting and so we finally completed a manuscript in this area and then submitted it to Journal of Service Research for review and now receive a 2nd R&R. Regarding the exploration of the impact of flow experiences on service outcomes overtime, we had a hard time in getting a longitudinal dataset and we are now still in the negotiation process with a few companies so as to solicit their helps in this regard. In terms of the second research paper, the results are more promising than the first one. We have collected a unique dataset that capturing daily observation from a popular crowdsourcing community, Dell's IdeaStorm, to provide another context for examining the effect of customer participation in terms of their online idea posting behaviors as well as investigating the effect of customer participation overtime. A manuscript of this study was submitted to Journal of Marketing for review, but unfortunately it was rejected at the 4th round of revision as the review team questions about the validity of the dataset. But with the valuable feedbacks received in these few rounds of JM revision, we are highly suggested to reposition our paper as examining the role of feedback in influencing customers' online participation rather than examining their psychological perception of enjoyment/flow and more specifically, we are urged to conduct a new experimental study for enhancing the validity of our findings. Hence, we now follow those valuable suggestions and make many new rounds of literature review, new data collection and analyses and finally get the manuscript be submitted to Management Science for review and got a revised revision. Taken together, the project objectives are mostly achieved, except the objective 3, which are not yet satisfactorily addressed due to the data collection difficulties. But with this grant, we have unexpectedly found another promising angle to reposition our paper in the online context with the data from a crowdsourcing community as well as a large-scale online experiment for the examination of the impact of customer participation.

540712.label: Major findings and research outcome
540712.value: For research paper 1: As what we proposed, customer participation indeed can improve one's flow experience whenever he or she sees a fit with their own participation efficacy. Moreover, customer participation can also increase customers' perceived interpersonal attraction of the employees, and which subsequently improve the customers' service evaluation (in addition to flow) as well as their citizenship behaviors. We have also explored some contextual factors that could serve as significant boundary conditions for the effects of customer participation such as leadership styles, leaders' feedbacks, shared similarity with the employees, service climate etc., but the findings are quite mixed and so we are still in the process of fine-tuning. But as mentioned before, we found some interesting findings that pertain to the effects of employees' extra role behaviors on customer participatory behaviors toward the firm via a dual identification mechanism (a component of flow experience) with the service climate as a boundary condition. We completed a manuscript in this regard and now under the second round of revision at Journal of Service Research. Part of the work has also been presented in the 2015 Frontiers in Service Conference. For Research Paper 2: We have completed the data collection from a large crowdsourcing community as well as from a large-scale online experimental study. Our results provide interesting insights about the interplay of the feedback valence, feedback sources and the level of online customer participation on the customers' subsequent idea quality and quantity as well as the ultimate outcome of idea implementation. The progress of our work has been presented in INFORMS Marketing Science (2016), and ANZMAC (2015). A completed manuscript submitted to Management Science and now receives an invited revision.

540712.value: We will continue working on (1) strengthening the conceptual framework of our two major studies with more coherent and solid theoretical foundation; (2) cleaning and reanalyzing the existing dataset as well as collecting new dataset so as to address the reviewers' additional concerns and hopefully can also successfully convince our targeted company to provide us the access to longitudinal study with their customers and employees; and (3) keep exploring additional research topics with the existing datasets that could be developed into publications.
