544112.label: Realisation of objectives
544112.value: The (Expanded) Project Scope: This project is concerned with the association between corporate social responsibility (CSR) and business performance among Chinese manufacturers. It originally has three objectives which link CSR adoption with the negative effect from the increased stress in plant managers and the use of conflict management practices to manage this negative effect. We started the project with in-depth case studies in three sizable Chinses manufacturers. Based on these three case studies, we found the CSR adoption could be highly relevant to three other aspects, namely supplier management, organizational learning, and organizational creativity, and that CSR adoption affects production operations as well as service operations (i.e., purchasing function, human resource function, etc.). In this connection, we added three new objectives to the project and decided to collected data from both production operations and service operations. The six objectives are as follows, 1) To examine if CSR adoption causes extra stress to the plant managers and such extra stress has a negative effect on the association between CSR adoption and business performance. 2) To examine if this negative effect decreases when managers use a cooperative conflict management approach. 3) To examine if this negative effect increases when managers use a competitive conflict management approach. 4) To examine if CSR adoption enhances the effectiveness of supplier partnerships. 5) To examine if CSR adoption enhances the effectiveness of organizational learning efforts with respect to operational improvement practices. 6) To examine if CSR adoption enhances organizational creativity. Note that a) objectives 1 – 3 are original objectives presented in the proposal; b) objectives 4 – 6 are new objectives based on the results of case studies; and c) based on those case studies’ results, all six objectives were examined by using data from manufacturing and service operations. Results: In this project we conducted a large scale survey in China. By using the survey data, the examination of all six objectives were completed. The results concerning Objectives 1 – 3 reveal that CSR dimensions’ performance impacts and the relevant moderating factors including stress in managers and conflict management practices vary a lot among the dimensions. For instance, “environmental management” and “responsible employee practice” behave as the hypotheses predict, whereas “service to community” has minimal levels of implementation and does not lead to improved performance. With the results pertinent to these three objective, we came up with a paper entitled “CSR adoption in Chine: A taxonomy development and performance implications.” It first was submitted to Decision Sciences Journal where it went through two rounds of revision but was rejected finally. It then was submitted to Journal of Cleaner Production (2016 Impact Factor: 5.715) where it currently is under the second review. The results concerning Objectives 3 – 6 reveal that the related hypotheses were rejected. However, with the data concerning supplier partnerships, organizational learning, and organizational creativity, we came up with some meaningful results that led to publications of three papers as follows, Yeung, K., Lee, P.K.C., Yeung, A.C.L., and Cheng, T.C.E. (2013) Supplier partnership and cost performance: The moderating roles of specific investments and environmental uncertainty, International Journal of Production Economics, 144 (2), 546–559. Yang, Y., Lee, P.K.C. and Cheng, T.C.E. (2015). Operational improvement competence and service recovery performance: The moderating effects of role stress and job resources. International Journal of Production Economics, 164, 134-145. Yang, Y., Lee, P.K.C., and Cheng, T.C.E. (2016) Continuous improvement competence, employee creativity, and new service development performance: A frontline employee perspective. International Journal of Production Economics, 171, 275-288. Furthermore, with some results of this project, one conference presentation entitled "The effectiveness of Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) in Chinese pharmaceutical firms: A case study" was delivered in 6th Annual International Conference on Advances in Biotechnology (March 2016 in Singapore). Conclusions: The examination of all six objectives (three original and three new objectives) of this project were completed. With the results relating to the three original objectives, one paper was developed which is under the second review in a top-tier journal (Journal of Cleaner Production). With the results of the three new objectives, three papers were developed and accepted by International Journal of Production Economics. The results of these four papers offer useful managerial insights concerning CSR adoption as well as supplier partnerships, organizational learning, and organizational creativity for businesses in China. To conclude, i am confident that this project was completed successfully.

544112.label: Major findings and research outcome
544112.value: With reference to section 5.3 Realisation of Objectives, this project led to the development of four papers which one is under review and three others are accepted papers. The findings of these four papers are as follows, Paper Under Review (“CSR adoption in Chine: A taxonomy development and performance implications”) Drawing from the stakeholder theory, CSR adoption in this study is manifested by seven dimensions (e.g., customers, employees, suppliers, communities). By using the approach taxonomy development, we find that there are three CSR adoption patterns by Chinese manufacturers, and that manufacturers adopting different CSR patterns achieve different levels of performance outcomes. Accepted Paper #1 (“Supplier partnership and cost performance: The moderating roles of specific investments and environmental uncertainty” accepted by IJPE) We propose that supplier partnership improves the operational cost performance of manufacturers and that its effectiveness is contingent on specific investments. We also propose that environmental uncertainty does not interact with specific investments to strengthen the effectiveness of supplier partnership. Our results indicate that supplier partnership is positively and significantly related to operational cost performance. We also find that the relationship between supplier partnership and operational cost performance is strengthened by specific investments. Accepted Paper #2 (“Operational improvement competence and service recovery performance: The moderating effects of role stress and job resources” by IJPE) We propose that organizational learning with respect to the implementation of operational improvement practices is highly relevant to service recovery performance. We draw on role stress theory and conservation of resources theory to argue that service operations’ peculiar characteristic (i.e., role stress in employees) and two types of important resources (i.e., organization inducement and psychological resilience) moderate the effectiveness of improvement practices in improving service recovery performance. Our result advances knowledge on service operations by establishing linkages between improvement practices and service recovery performance. Accepted Paper #3 (“Continuous improvement competence, employee creativity, and new service development performance: A frontline employee perspective” by IJPE) We argue that operational service employees’ skills in implementing continuous improvement practices can enhance their creativity and new service development performance. Our findings support our core arguments and serve to advance the knowledge of multiple disciplines by showing the linkages among operational improvement practices, employee creativity, and NSD performance.

544112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
544112.value: The Major Lesson: Our paper “CSR adoption in Chine: A taxonomy development and performance implications” (i.e., the paper under review) presents the core findings of this project. With the results from this paper, we found that environmental management (EM) is particularly important for Chinese manufacturers. Chinese manufacturers invest enormous amounts of resources in implementing various EM practices. Yet much of the investment is related to providing evidence to meet requirements of government regulations and customer audits, rendering the real impact on protecting the environment questionable. Future Work: With the support from certain findings of the current project, I am in the process of developing a proposal which aims to test the actual environmental impact of Chinese manufacturers’ investments on EM practices and to offer insights to enhance the efficiency of such investments with respect to protecting the natural environment.

544112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
544112.value: This project offers evidence indicate that CSR adoption is related to enhanced performance for Chinese manufacturers. However, businesses in China have to be aware that CSR is a complex strategy that comprises multiple dimensions concerning various stakeholders. Our findings indicate that different dimensions of CSR are associated with different levels of performance. Thus, businesses in China should not implement all CSR dimensions in the same level. Instead, they have to select those CSR dimensions which are more critical in their particular contexts, and implement such selected dimensions in higher levels. This project also offers insights to other relevant aspects such as supplier partnership and operational improvement practices. More specifically, our results suggest that supplier partnerships in general are effective for Chinese manufacturers. However, managers have to understand that supplier partnerships’ effectiveness is affected by the uncertainty level in the business environment and the specific investments (e.g., a machine useful for the partnering supplier but not so for other suppliers) made by the manufacturers. In regard to our findings on operational improvement practices, managers can learn that operational improvement practices are crucial for service operations because such practices enhance employee creativity, new service development performance and service recovery performance.

544512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
544512.value: 接觸顧客的員工是公司和顧客之間的橋樑（Alexandrov et al., 2007）。因此，他們的情緒表現對顧客評價公司的績效是至關重要的（Homburg & Stock, 2004; Luong, 2005）。在本研究中，我們調查重要的個人特徵（顧客服務的稱許性）和人與環境的交互作用（人職匹配）對接觸顧客的員工的情緒表達的影響，以及不同的情緒勞動對員工的工作結果的影響。具體地說，我們認為在與顧客交流時，高人職匹配激勵員工表現出更多的深層扮演和更少的表層扮演。而高水平的深層扮演和低水平的表層扮演，可能導致更高的角色內績效、組織公民行為和主動行為。因為，這種匹配提供了一種勝任感並激勵員工去完成由組織的情緒表達規則所指出的有關情緒工作的期望。 此外，我們假設，當顧客服務稱許性高時，人職匹配與情緒勞動及工作成果的關係更強。其中的邏輯為，高顧客服務稱許性的員工傾向於將自己更容易被顧客接受的一面表現出來。當他們發現自己與工作不匹配時，這些員工可能會認為表層扮演是一種完成組織所要求的情緒表達規則的途徑。因此，表層扮演可能導致對工作成果的負面影響。關於深層扮演，高顧客服務稱許性的員工可能受到內在激勵而改變自己的內部感受，並以這樣的方式來實現他們想使顧客高興的個人目的。這樣，深層扮演可能會導致更好的工作結果。因此，人職匹配和情緒勞動之間的關係受到顧客服務稱許性的調節。 我們將進行兩個研究，其被試均為300名接觸顧客的員工。這些數據將分別在位於中國大陸的兩家大型五星級酒店收集。研究協議已在項目的首席研究員和負責該公司的管理層之間達成。在兩個研究中，數據將採自員工、他們的直接上級，和相應的顧客。多層次分析將被用來對數據進行分析。 我們的研究預計為社會做出以下幾方面的貢獻：明確選拔和培養與接觸顧客的工作相匹配的員工的重要性; 探索顧客服務稱許性在強化深層扮演和表層扮演上的影響; 並研究在對員工的工作成果（如角色內績效、組織公民行為和主動行為）的影響上，不同的情緒勞動的優劣。

544512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
544512.value: In this project, we uncovered how employees' fitness perception on their work- and leader-related issues affect their emotional labor strategies as well as their work outcomes. First, we found that employees' fitness perceptions on both their jobs (high person–job fit) and organizations (high person–organization fit) would lead them to perform more deep acting and less surface acting, in which resulting in higher service interaction quality and customer satisfaction. In addition, we also found that employees who perceive they are well fitted to the team context are more likely to speak out their suggestions to their team members. However, if they feel that they are not well fitted to the leadership style of their immediate supervisors (e.g., abusive supervision), they are less likely to work effectively at work.

545812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
545812.value: During the past three decades of rapid industrial growth, China has suffered from devastating environmental degradation. Yet somewhat more optimistic views on the prospects for their reversal have emerged in the past few years given the Chinese government’s increased commitment to fighting industrial pollution, the public’s increased concerns regarding the adverse consequences of pollution, and domestic and international civil society’s increased involvement in promoting environmental protection in China. This proposed research seeks to assess these changing environmental governance landscapes in China by studying the environmental management practices of enterprises from the perspective of ecological modernization theory. From this perspective, it will study how far the business community has achieved ecological modernization through the progressive institutionalization of ecological values under various types of changing pressure from government, market, and civil society actors in the process of environmental governance reform. The focus is the extent to which individual business enterprises have moved away from economic logics toward ecological rationality in making their corporate environmental management decisions. This longitudinal and comparative study seeks to capture the dynamics of ecological modernization in China’s industrial sector with the objective of answering five important questions: 1) What are the changing roles of government, market, and civil society actors in the reform process, focusing on various types of pressure these actors may have exerted on business enterprises? 2) What are business enterprises’ changing perceptions of environmental demands made by various stakeholders, their changing strategic responses to these demands, and the extent to which they have adopted various environmental management practices? 3) In what ways do firm- and industry-level characteristics—such as management commitment, type of industry, and connections to international buyers—relate to environmental management practices? 4) What are the regional variations in the business community’s ecological modernization? and 5) In what ways can ecological modernization theory (EMT) be applied to assess environmental governance reform in China? These questions will be answered by conducting questionnaire surveys and semi-structured interviews with executives of manufacturing plants. The study will be built on our earlier studies on corporate environmental governance in the three cities of Guangzhou, Beijing and Shanghai, the three leading local economies in China. It will use the same set of survey and interview questions to extend the analysis of temporal and regional variations in the ecological modernization of China’s manufacturing sector. 在過去的三十年工業快速增長中，中國遭受到毀滅性的環境惡化。然而，在過去的幾年中，人们對中国環境污染逆轉的前景出現了較為樂觀的看法，此乃鑒於中國政府增強了對控制工業污染的承諾，公眾日益關注污染的不良後果，以及國內和國際民間社會更多地參與促進中國的環保工作。 本研究旨在從生態現代化理論的角度，通過研究企業的環境管理方法去評估這些變遷中的中國的環境治理的景象。在這個角度下，我們將會研究商界在環境管治改革下，來自政府、市場、和民間社會等相關方德各類變改中的壓力下，通過將生態價值觀逐步制度化，去實現生態現代化的程度。 當中的重點是個別工商企業在他們的企業環境管理決策下，已經離開經濟邏輯轉向生態理性的程度。 這個縱向和比較研究，試圖捕捉中國的工業界生態現代化的動態，目的是回答五個重要的問題：1、在改革過程中，政府，市場和民間社會等相關方角色有什麼轉變，焦點集中在這些相關方可以對商業企業施加的各類型壓力？2、商業企業對各不同持份者的環境訴求感覺的改變、對這些訴求的不斷變改的戰略回應，以及在何種程度上他們採取了各項環境管理措施是什麼？3、在哪些方面企業和行業特徵 - 例如管理層的承諾、產業的類型、與國際買家的聯繫 – 與環境管理實踐有什么關聯？4、商界的生態現代化的區域差異是什麼？以及5、有什麼辦法可以將生態現代化理論（EMT）適用於評估中國的環境治理改革？ 我們將通過對製造行業的工廠的高層管理人員進行問卷調查和半結構式的訪談去回答這些問題。這項研究將建立在我們較早前在北京、上海、和廣州等三個在中國占主導地位的地方經濟進行的企業環境治理的研究。我們將會使用相同的調查問卷和訪談問題，將時間和區域差異的分析伸延至研究中國製造業的生態現代化。

545812.label: Realisation of objectives
545812.value: In the process of implementing this research project, we administered questionnaire surveys to enterprise management and interviewed management executives in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, as well as the Pearl River Delta Region, between 2014 and 2017. Data was collected from manufacturing enterprises in the Pearl River Delta Region and Guangzhou in order to perform longitudinal analysis and thereby provide a comprehensive view of changes in the ecological modernization paths of business enterprises in the two regions (Objective 2). The survey and interview data collected from manufacturing enterprises in Shanghai, Beijing and Guangzhou mainly serve the purpose of cross-city analysis, enabling a comparison of the practices and performance of business enterprises in their corporate environmental management in these three economically advanced municipalities of China (Objective 3). On the basis of these two sets of data analyses, we identify various contextual factors that impact corporate environmental management practices (Objective 4) and develop strategies that can help promote ecological modernization among business enterprises (Objective 5). As this longitudinal and comparative study is built on our exploratory studies conducted in the Pearl River Delta Region earlier in 2007-2010, we basically used the same sets of questionnaire and interview questions for data collection. In the refinement of the ecological modernization framework for this study, we revised the questionnaire to incorporate the impact of green management on brand development and include green IT as an environmental management practice (Objective 1). To increase the reliability of the survey, we asked both a management executive and the environmental manager of each manufacturing enterprise to complete the questionnaire. In order to reduce mono-method bias, we supplemented the survey with interviews management executives and environmental managers from 10-15 enterprises in each locality. This mixed-method approach, which combined quantitative and qualitative research methods in a single study, enhances the credibility of data analyses by allowing the triangulation of findings. To make data collection from manufacturing enterprises in each location feasible, we communicated with both national and local environmental protection bureaus. With the help of the Environmental Public and Education Centre (CEPE) of the Ministry of Environmental Protection, we were able to connect with the Studio for Media Survey and Research at Tsinghua University and get their agreement to arrange the enterprise surveys and interviews of management executives in Beijing and Shanghai. We sought help from the Guangzhou Academy of Environmental Sciences of the Guangzhou Environmental Protection Bureau to arrange the survey and interviews in Guangzhou and the Pearl River Delta Region. With UGC’s approval to commit part of the funding for this project to finance these data collection efforts, we finalized formal agreements with these two research institutions in 2014 and 2015 respectively, after a long legal process of preparation. Only data collection in the Pearl River Delta Region was completed on schedule, in early 2014. The interviews with enterprise management in Beijing and Shanghai took longer to arrange until CEPE stepped in to help, as most manufacturing enterprises in these two municipalities were reluctant to allow their management executives and environmental managers to speak on the sensitive topic of pollution control. Data collection in Guangzhou turned out to be the most difficult part, as the GZEPB’s deputy chief in charge of external collaboration insisted that a formal approval for our research collaboration with their research academy had to be sought from higher government authorities. The entire approval process, starting in February 2016, went through a number of related local and provincial authorities before the green light was finally given in November 2016. In facing these data collection difficulties and delay, we made full use of the limited data collected at each stage to help prepare journal and conference papers. By integrating information collected from interviews with management executives and environmental managers and environmental officials into survey data collected earlier, we were able to publish four papers on corporate environmental management among manufacturing enterprises in Guangzhou and the Pearl River Delta. The first paper, entitled “Regulatory Compliance When the Rule of Law is Weak: Evidence from China’s Environmental Reform”, published in 2016 in the Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory – ranked first in the discipline of public administration – examined how manufacturing enterprises in the PRD region responded to the increasingly more stringent regulatory enforcement of pollution control regulations as China advanced in the path of ecological modernization (Objective 2). The second paper, entitled “Enterprise-Level Motivations, Regulatory Pressures, and Corporate Environmental Management in Guangzhou, China”, came out in a 2015 issue of the Environmental Management; it examines the effects of internal motivations and external pressures on the integration of environmental management practices within manufacturing operations in China (Objective 2). The third paper, entitled “The Interaction Effects of Institutional Constraints on Managerial Intentions and Sustainable Performance”, appeared in a 2016 issue of the International Journal of Production Economics – a top-ranked journal in industrial and manufacturing engineering, it identified the constraining factors that affected corporate environmental performance (Objective 2). The fourth paper, entitled “Organizational Visibility, Stakeholder Environmental Pressure and Corporate Environmental Responsiveness in China”, which has just appeared in the January issue of Business Strategy and the Environment in 2017, studied the impact of organization visibility and external pressure on corporate environmental management (Objective 2). All four articles have proposed possible strategies for improving corporate environmental management and performance (Objective 5). Our latest effort was a paper presented at the Public Management Research Conference at American University in June 2017, examining the changing patterns and motivations in environmental management among manufacturing enterprises in the Pearl River Delta Region by analyzing 2010 interview records of enterprise executives and the 2014 survey (Objectives 2 & 5). Since the recent completion of data collection, we have started to work on the survey data sets and compiled the interview records. The preliminary results of cross-city analyses are encouraging, indicating variations among manufacturing enterprises in corporate environmental practices and performance in different locations in the face of growing compliance pressure from regulatory stakeholders. The interview data appear to indicate that management executives have increasingly taken corporate pollution control more seriously and environmental managers have received greater management support to help the enterprises gradually migrate to cleaner production technologies (Objectives 3 & 4). More rigorous data analysis with a focus on cross-city comparison will be conducted in the next few months to ensure that the results are robust and the findings reliable. We expect two to three papers to be prepared in this process for possible conference presentations and journal submissions next year (Objectives 3, 4 & 5). In the concluding stages of this project, we would like to iterate that doing environmental research in China is always full of political risks and uncertainties, leaving researchers without much control over the work schedule. We hope that UGC and its members will be considerate and appreciate our diligent efforts. We are glad to have been able to complete the questionnaire surveys and interviews of management executives in individual locations as planned, albeit behind schedule. Finally, we are confident that we can produce impactful research outputs out of these data in the years to come.

545812.label: Major findings and research outcome
545812.value: In the process of conducting field research in the respective locations, we have leveraged the new data collected in this project to strengthen the analyses of data collected in earlier studies. As a result, four journal papers and one conference presentation have been produced. The first major finding relates to the compliance of manufacturing enterprises with pollution control regulations under the growing pressure of regulatory stakeholders. We found that their decisions to adopt basic and proactive environmental management practices were less driven by concerns for legality than by their perceptions of the regulators’ actions and gestures. Enterprises adopted basic environmental practices to avoid potential punishment and more proactive practices to avoid potentially arbitrary impositions from regulatory officials. Regulated enterprises were more likely to adopt both basic and proactive environmental practices if they had less difficulty in understanding the enforced regulations. The second major finding addresses the effects of perceived regulation constraints on the relationship between managerial intentions and sustainable performance. We found that proactive intention tends to have a stronger positive effect on sustainable performance, in particular, under less institutional constraints. Such a positive effect remains significant at low and moderate levels of institutional constraints. By contrast, protective firms tend to achieve lower sustainable performance at all levels of the perceived institutional constraints. The third major finding emerges from our investigation into the relationship between organizational visibility and corporate environmental responsiveness in China. Our study indicates that organizational visibility is negatively associated with stakeholder pressure in the case of Chinese-owned enterprises, and stakeholder pressure has no significant associations with corporate environmental responsiveness. The fourth major finding comes from our longitudinal analysis. It was shown that practices that demand deeper integration of environmental concerns into an enterprises’ operation (e.g., ISO14001) were significantly related to demands from the enterprise’s peers (e.g., industrial association), whereas practices that did not require such a structural integration (e.g., sponsorship of events, incorporating environmental themes in marketing) were significantly related not only to peer demands but also to societal demands and the perceived arbitrary-targeting strategy of regulatory officials. The last major finding is based on our preliminary cross-city analyses. The results strongly suggest regional variations in corporate environmental practices and performance in different locations under increasingly stringent regulatory contexts. At the same time, the growing demands from regulatory stakeholders have triggered stronger management support for environmental managers to technologically upgrade their pollution control facilities.

545812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
545812.value: By building on our earlier studies on corporate environmental governance in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and the Pearl River Delta Region, our project has conducted a longitudinal and cross-city analysis of corporate environmental management in China from the ecological modernization perspective. By using the mixed methods of questionnaire survey and semi-structured interview, we collected a robust set of empirical data for in-depth analysis to answer questions relating to changes and variations in corporate environmental practices among manufacturing enterprises in China’s dynamic and diversified institutional setting. As ecological modernization in China is an on-going process with global significance in environmental terms, it requires close and regular monitoring of the greening progress of China’s industrial sector. Given the proven academic contributions of this study, as demonstrated by the three papers published in top-ranked public and business management journals, it is strongly desirable to conduct another round of study in a few years’ time on manufacturing enterprises’ corporate environmental management in these cities. This will enable researchers to remain up-to-date on the progress of ecological modernization in China and to compare the contextual changes of corporate environment management.

545812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
545812.value: This longitudinal and comparative study examines the dynamics of ecological modernization in China’s industrial sector in driving and motivating manufacturing enterprises to actively and progressively participate in environmental protection. From the ecological modernization perspective, effective environmental protection requires that various environmental interests be institutionalized within the business and industrial system. Therefore, the research focus centers on how corporations respond to various types of pressure from government, market and civil society actors for improving corporate pollution control practices. To address this research puzzle, we have administered questionnaire surveys and semi-structured interviews with executives of manufacturing enterprises in the aforementioned locations between 2013 and 2017. Our project has produced important findings on the deeper integration of corporate environmental practices from the longitudinal study and regional variations in corporate environmental responses to the individual actors’ environmental demands. These results indicate that ecological modernization in China has been progressively evolving while displaying contextual differences across locations. Theoretically, our study has enriched the conceptualization of ecological modernization by applying it in a developing country context. Empirically, it provides solid evidence that the momentum of sustainable development in China has already taken hold. Practically, the findings inform the possible improvement of corporate environmental management and regulatory enforcement in a developing context.

546112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
546112.value: Writing manuals that circulated in the Ming dynasty provided model letters and contracts. Over one hundred books printed, reprinted and pirated works in print, attesting to their popularity. Yet little is known about the concerns that guided the editors of writing guides or the readers who consulted them. The proposed study will produce a book on the life and livelihood of a literary hack, if you will, named Deng Zhimo, who was active from 1599 to 1627 and made his name as “author” of letter-writing manuals. An examination failure, he qualified for no position higher than tutor. He parlayed a post as tutor to the Yu-family publishers in Fujian into a reputation as author and sought-after commentator. He also procured manuscripts and was in-house author. In this capacity, Deng produced dictionaries, fiction, model letters and plays (29 titles) and contributed commentary for six other works. Historians of the Chinese book note his ingenious strategies for building on the success of titles in print. The project will produce a study of editions resolve disputes about what he edited or authored, how and why he copied works in print and at least two other journal articles. The book on Deng Zhimo will shed light on the nature of authorship, based on analysis of the language and themes of his works. It highlights the interplay between editing and writing, recomposing and literary invention. Deng (or his publishers) promoted himself as a man of learning, and even published his personal letters with annotation to ensure readers recognized his learning and associations. He densely annotated his primers, as well. His commentaries furnish invaluable clues to literacies, evidencing varied levels of skill and often unorthodox methods of interpretation. The commentaries and notes are rich in human and material detail and can help scholars to paint a picture of the middlebrow audience for fiction and practical writing guides. Deng Zhimo popularized beliefs such as the Unity of the Three Teachings (of Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism) in his fiction. He also aired views about passion as fundamental to social order, proselytizing for radical understandings of human subjectivity. The project seeks to show how this editor-author contributed to a nascent humanism in China and place his works in comparative perspective.

546312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
546312.value: Global container carriers are using increasingly larger vessels on east-west trunk routes to exploit economies of scale and meet the escalating demand for the containerized trade. This leads to cutting back on port calls to reduce unproductive time and in turn intensifies the competition among ports to keep up the number of port calls from major liners. Hong Kong has been the second largest transshipment hub in the Far East since the early 1990s. The development of the maritime industry has since established Hong Kong as an international maritime center. However, this status quo is under threat from the fast expansion of nearby Shenzhen and Guangzhou ports. Early this year, Maersk announced to cut its ship calls at Hong Kong from 30 per week to 22-23 per week, and transfer the business to Guangzhou (Reuters, 2011). This change has boosted Guangzhou’s throughput at the expense of Hong Kong (The Journal of Commerce, 2011) and thus presented a great challenge to Hong Kong hoping to retain its position as one of the world’s busiest ports. Many researchers studied port choice from shippers’ perspectives. However, the decision of the liners often has more direct impact on port business. In this research, a nested logit model is used to study the port selection behavior of major liners based on their actual port calls along the Chinese Coast, taking into account the shipper’s behavior and strategic port competition. Generally port calls are decided in two stages. First, carriers decide the number of clusters to cover and their combination. Second, they choose the number of port calls and port rotation in each selected cluster. This study has several academic merits. First, nested logic models require the choice alternatives to be independent and mutually exclusive. We propose to extent it for multi-choice problems with dependent and non-exclusive alternatives, such as the selection of a series of port calls in a liner service. Second, this study proposes to integrate port choice modeling with strategic port competition and shippers’ carrier selection. This is an entirely new approach not reported in the existing literature. In a practical sense, this study can serve as a valuable work of reference for the local maritime industry concerning swift responses to liner shipping changes and best strategies to preserve the competitiveness of the industry, its derived logistics sectors and other service industries.

546312.label: Realisation of objectives
546312.value: 1. This research has identified the important factors for global liner shipping companies in selection of hub ports. This research has reviewed more than 80 papers concerning port selection behavior in liner shipping services. The research such as Malchow and Kanafani (2001), Tavassy, Minderhoud, et al. (2011) revealed that the features of both ports/hinterlands and liners would affect the choice of ports in liner shipping. Combined with previous research, we identified the main factors in ports and hinterland are: (1) Port’s facility: measured by number of handling facility, length of terminal or draught (2) Charges in the port (3) Efficiency of cargo handling in port: measured by congestion cost (4) Port’s location: measured by ocean distance, or connectivity (5) Hinterland demand: measured by GDP of hinterland or import/export (6) Hinterland transport: measured by cost or time of inland transportation (7) Authority of port: privatization The main factors of liners are: (1) Ship size (2) Ocean distance/Time (3) Frequency (4) Shipping companies/Shippers (5) Shipping lanes Among all those factors, we find that the ship size growth has become an important factor in the liner shipping service network design. Therefore, the optimal ship size studies, such as Jansson and Shneerson (1982), are also included in this research. From those literatures, we can conclude that the optimal ship size decision problem in liner shipping is a compromise of ship price, operating cost, freight rate and demand. 2. This research has built a database on the liner routes for major carriers visiting Chinese ports (including Hong Kong and Taiwan). That database contain the information of port rotation, frequency, number of ships, and ship sizes for 1059 liner shipping services in 2011 and 2015. The information of liner shipping services are mainly collected from Alphaliner (https://www.alphaliner.com/) and Clarkson (http://www.clarksons.com/). 3. Correspondingly, this research has studied the port development in China from 2011 to 2015. That includes the container throughput, weekly capacity in each route and capacity contribution of each liner shipping operator in 5 port clusters and 11 container ports along Chinese coast during 2011 and 2015. The above data are mainly collected from Alphaliner, Clarkson and China Statistical Yearbook. 4. This research has built analytical models to show the optimal number of ports to call for liner shipping companies with different ship size and round-trip time. In building the analytical models, we assumed that that liners will always call ports with higher demand first. The decision on the number of port calls is analyzed in both transshipment and no-transshipment case, with or without competition. The basic model demonstrates how single operator decides port calls in a liner service from the profit maximizing behavior of that operator. The results show whether to call a port depends on the relative magnitude of the incremental costs of calling the port versus the expected earnings. The liner shipping market in any trade route is assumed contestable. Therefore, in a duopoly market, two operators compete using price discount. The extended model identifies the optimal condition on the number of port calls and price discount in the competition case. The results show when they are two operators, both will offer discounts based on the contestable price when it is hard to fill up the ship. Whether one operator calls more ports than its competitor depends on not only ship size, but also on its market share. We also use the numerical study of liner shipping services between China and North America in 2011 and 2015 to test those analytical models. 5. This research has constructed an ordered logit model to investigate how factors such as duration, frequency and ship size affect the decision on the number of clusters (the port groups that serve the same hinterland)to visit. OLS regressions are applied to estimate those factors’ contribution in the number of port calls. The study is based on information of all liner shipping services calling Chinese coast in 2011 and 2015. From the regression results, we found the statistical evidence on the relationship between the number of clusters/ports visited and ship size: Increasing ship size within a certain range leads to more clusters/ports visit. Beyond that, larger ships visit fewer clusters, not necessary fewer ports. Therefore, for a hinterland with a high demand of shipping, there can be more than one hub in the same region. By calculating the marginal probability for selecting more clusters, we can find that the turning points of ship size in cluster/port call number is close to the theoretical models’ results. 6. In this research, the empirical study has provided a general description of the Chinese container ports, the port clusters, and global liners serving China’s international trade. The port call models have suggested that larger ships may not make fewer number of port calls. That means there could be multiple hub ports in close proximity. As long as there is sufficient demand and port facilities are efficient, the liner service will not skip these ports. Therefore, strategic capacity competition is not necessary, as this would only lead to overcapacity in port supply. In addition, this research has also investigated the operating revenue and costs of 20 major liner operators from 2001 to 2015. Fixed-effect panel data models are applied to investigate the moderating effects of large containership and alliance membership. Therefore, we provide the ship investment and cooperation strategies in different market conditions for different company attributes, which can help the operation decision of liner shipping companies in practice. Also, we have communicated with the liner shipping companies such as ZIM in Hong Kong, to consider about the possibilities in using the result in their daily operation decision.

546312.label: Major findings and research outcome
546312.value: This research contains major findings in three aspects: (1) Hub ports selection behavior for liner shipping companies in practice; (2) Theoretical model on hub port selection behavior; (3) The optimal operation strategies for liners. Many people believed that with the ever increase of containership size, they will call fewer number of ports because they will adopt hub-spoke network. Our empirical analysis found that it is not true for the international liners calling the Chinese Coast. There are ‘turning points’ for liners to change from visiting more port clusters when ship size grows, to visit few number of clusters. But such “turning point” is not significant in number of port calls. Therefore, in shipping there can be two hubs in close proximity, and they can both be on the same main line services, provided they both possess high cargo demands and have similar capacities that can accommodate the larger vessels. The detailed study can refer to ‘Do Larger Ships Visit Fewer Regions/Ports? An Empirical Analysis on Global Liners Serving China, Journal of Transport Economics and Policy’ in the Journal of Transport Economics and Policy by Xiaofan Wu, Meifeng Luo, and Anming Zhang. The theoretical model on liners’ number of port call decision confirms the empirical finding. Whether larger ships calls more or fewer ports depends on the demand in the ports, and the cost to support the call. When demand is low and ships cannot be filled full, larger ships will call fewer ports and charge lower prices; otherwise, they can call more ports and charge higher prices as long as the increment cost does not exceed the revenue that the operators can gain from additional port call. Numerical simulation confirms the theoretical result. The study is presented in the working paper ‘Port Call Decisions of Liner Shipping Services in a Contestable Market’, and about to be submitted to Transportation Research Part B. On the optimal strategies for global liners, we find that quantitative impacts of larger ships and joining alliances on the liners’ performance. The result suggests that liner shipping companies should make the decisions on ship investment and joining alliances based on the market condition, to achieve a better and stable performance. These analyses is in the working paper ‘The Moderating Effects of Large Ships and Alliances on the Financial Performance of Liner Operators: An Empirical Analysis’, and will be submitted to Journal of Operations Management.

546312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
546312.value: 1. Our student used the data from year 2011 and 2015. The structure changes after 2015 have a very significant impact on the market competition and the behavior of players in the competitive market. Future research efforts in understanding the behavior of the few remaining large operators are definitely necessary, especially when all of them are operating in three large alliances. 2. When analyzing the theoretical model of the liner operators’ decision on port call number, the decision on how to call them is not included. However, when applying the model in the design of liner shipping services, the problem of how to call them is necessary, and it has to involve many practical factors, such as the physical limitation on berth capacity and the distance between each ports. 3. The study of effects of large ships and joining alliances in financial performance relied heavily on the available financial information of the company. The future analysis of financial performance may use route specific information on the capacity allocation of each company, if such data is possible.

546312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
546312.value: This study is about what can happen when the ships in the liner shipping industry are becoming larger. It clarifies the contradictory believes in the academia and industry: some thought that larger ships have to call more ports in order to get more cargo, while others believe that they will call fewer number of ports due to the adoption of hub-spoke network. The empirical model helps to identify the current trends, if any, when the ships are becoming bigger. The theoretical model confirms the empirical findings, and further explored its relationship with different factors such as port demand and competition. This empirical-theoretical consistency in our research indicates one important implication: Hub-spoke network in ocean liner shipping is different from that in aviation. Therefore, for Coastal ports, it is important to expand the capacity if demand is high as it is possible to have two hub-ports in one region. Finally, we find that using larger ships and joining alliances may not necessary increase the financial performance. Thus, it is important for liner shipping companies to adopt different strategies in different market condition, as well as its own specific natures.

546412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
546412.value: Improper footwear design causes injuries and illnesses. Literature review indicates numerous studies related to foot and footwear, however the shoe last (a 3D mold for making the shoe) has often been neglected. Shoe designers and manufacturers agree that the shoe-last is the most important component in the shoe making process. The shoe-last dictates styles, fashion, comfort and fit. Although the shoe-last is known as the heart of the shoe-making process, few researches have been done to improve it. There are many problems with the existing shoe-last design system. First the shoe-last design system was developed in 1964 based on anthropometric studies of German children. With the current technology, 3D foot shape may be used to improve shoe-last design. Next, the model shoe-last is made manually by master shoe-last makers. The master shoe-last maker has little knowledge of the foot, but he is guided by his experience, linear foot dimensions, and 2D templates. We might not completely replace the manual work in the shoe-last design process, but we can provide visual clues and guides to help the master shoe-last designers. The shoe-last has design features, manufacturing features and fitting features. Because of the manufacturing features, the shoe-last is not exactly the same as the inside shoe shape. As the shoe designer uses the same shoe last as the shoe manufacturer, there is some incompatibility. There should be a ‘designer shoe-last’ which has a one-one mapping with the manufacturing shoe last. The shoe-last design affects shoe design and foot health, yet it does not provide any clue to the designer. The shoe designer may add high pressure designs on main blood vessels, or may design shoes that do not flex at the right location. It would be useful to provide shoe designers with important foot landmarks to guide them during the design process. The proposed shoe-last will have visual clues about foot anatomical landmarks to help the designers. Since footwear manufacturing requires both physical and digital information, the proposed research will look into both digital and physical representation of the shoe-last without affecting the shoe design and manufacturing process. The research proposes the redesign of the shoe-lasts. It starts from the foot anatomy, 3D foot surface and then creates ‘designer shoe-last’ and ‘manufacturing shoe last’ with anatomical information coded on the surface. It is expected that this research will reduce footwear related problems, improve design cycle and improve production quality. 鞋子設計不當會引發足部受傷和疾病。文獻表明目前有很多關於足部和鞋子的研究，但通常鞋楦（制鞋的三維模型）會被忽略。鞋子設計師和製造商們都一致認為鞋楦是制鞋過程中最重要的因素。鞋楦決定了鞋子的款式、流行、舒適性和適合度。儘管鞋楦被公認為制鞋的核心要素，但很少有研究對其進行改善。 現有的鞋楦設計系統存在很多問題。首先，此鞋楦設計系統是1964年開發的基於德國兒童的人體測量學研究。針對當前的技術，三維足部形狀可以用來改善鞋楦設計。其次，鞋楦模型是由母楦師傅手工製成。母楦師傅對足部研究瞭解甚少，僅憑經驗、二維足部尺寸和樣版進行製造。在鞋楦設計過程中，我們不能完全取代手工作業，但是我們能夠提供視覺化的指導來幫助母楦設計師。 鞋楦具有設計特徵、生產特徵和適合特徵。對於生產特徵，鞋楦和鞋子的內部形狀並非完全一致。鞋子設計師和鞋子製造商使用同樣的鞋楦，在某種程度上會產生不相容的問題。換言之，應該有一種“設計鞋楦”和與其相對應的“生產鞋楦”。鞋楦設計影響了鞋子設計和足部健康，但沒有給鞋子設計師提供任何指導。鞋子設計師可以在主要血管處添加高壓設計，或者使某些位置不易彎曲。如果能在設計過程中給出重要的足部標識，這對鞋子設計師是非常有幫助的。 本研究項目所提出的鞋楦能夠給設計師提高視覺化的足部自動標識。鑒於鞋子製造需要物理資訊和數位資訊，本專案將在不影響鞋子設計和製造過程的前提下，研究鞋楦的物理表現和數位表現。 本研究提出了鞋楦重新設計系統。始於足部解剖學、三維足部表面；然後創建基於足部表明解剖資訊的“設計鞋楦”和“生產鞋楦”。 此研究預計將減少鞋類製造相關問題，提高設計週期和產品品質。

547012.value: 新时代的世界工厂：资本、国家与富士康生产

547012.label: Project Objectives
547012.value: To study the speed and scale of global capital expansion in general and the global supply chain in specific, and see how global brands provide pressure to Foxconn to grow as a mega world factory in order to compete against each other. To discern how production suppliers like Foxconn survive and secure contracts by minimizing its costs and transfering the pressure of increasingly low profit margins to the frontline workers. This will lead to a new typology of globoal factory regime that challenges existing labour process theory and requires new theorization of labour process in the context of speedy globalization. To understand the role of the state in facilitating capital monopology and in shaping the new form of global factory regime by providing land, infrastructural facilities and labour supply on a massive scale that is impossible to imagine a decade ago. To compare and contrast the Foxconn factory regimes in three regions of China in order to see whether regional factors such as the role of local government, labour market and the agency of workers contribute to the similaries and differences in the process of the making of global factory regime. Gender, ethnicity and class subjectivities will be studied in detail at the workplace level. To study new forms of alienation of labour generated both in the production and daily reproduction spheres. We strive to understand why young migrant workers in the late teens to mid-20s, who have been placed in the “first-class” Foxconn factory-cum-dormitory environment, seemed to show greater loneliness and anxieties, and to see fewer alternatives than their peers. Suicide is merely the extreme manifestation of what migrant workers in their hundreds of millions experience. This study instead, looks to understand the lived experiences of the new generation of the Chinese migrant workers and their potential to generate individual and collective resistance. Preliminary studies in Foxconn workplaces have figured out a variety form of labour actions including collective complaints, labour disputes, sit-ins and street strikes which rquire systematic investigation.

547012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
547012.value: When Time magazine nominated workers in China as the runners-up to the 2009 Person of the Year, the editor commented that Chinese workers have brightened the future of humanity by “leading the world to economic recovery.” The new generation of Chinese migrant workers, however, seems to perceive themselves as losing their futures. The Foxconn tragedy has been dubbed the “suicide express” by Chinese and international media. In the year of 2010, a startling 18 young migrant workers attempted suicide at Foxconn production facilities in China, bringing worldwide attention to Foxconn management and its impact on workers. By focusing on Foxconn production, this research attempts to study a new form of global factory regime emergent in China under the context of speedy global capital accumulation and new international division of labour. We looks at the development of Foxconn Technology Group as a case to demonstrate the advent of rapid capital expansion in China and its impacts on the lives of Chinese workers. It also provides an account of the role of the state that facilitates to Foxconn’s production expansion as a form of monopoly capital. Having a workforce of one million in China alone, Foxconn is important and typical of this phenomenon due to its speed and scale of capital accumulation in all regions of China which is incomparable to extant enterprises. We strive to understand this new form of global factory regime and its distinctive managerial mode and labour process that leads to workers’ suffering from work pressure, anxieties and desperation at an unprecedented level. This research is a collaborative study comprised of research institutions from Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. We attempt to study Foxconn facilities in the three regions of China: Pearl River Delta, Yangtze River Delta and Western China. We will conduct about 300 in-depth interviews of Foxconn workers and 50 interviews of Foxconn managers in Mainland China and Taiwan. This will enable us to have a better understanding of the new form of global factory regime and its specific form of labour control and labour resistance. We also attempt to make sense of the lived experiences and potential collective resistances among the new generation of Chinese migrant workers who is now shaping the making of the Chinese working class and also the future of world labour. 2010年，全球最大的電子代工企業——富士康科技集團（下文簡稱「富士康」）陸續發生了18起自殺事件。這一系列慘劇造成14死4傷，引發了社會的廣泛關注，被媒體稱作 「連環跳」事件。所有自殺的富士康員工年齡均介於17到25歲，正值青春年華——他們的悲劇引發了學者的密切關注，並且開展調研，重新審視全球資本積累的形式及其對中國工人帶來的影響。在被譽為「典範」的富士康工作的超過100萬的年輕工人，呈現給我們的更多是他們的焦慮、迷茫和別無選擇。 一直以來，大家都主張中國的崛起是一個由國家主導的全球化過程——改革開放後，國家通過鼓勵外資和對外開放政策，建立了全面依靠合資或外資的出口導向型發展模式 。這種以依靠外國直接投資（FDI）的發展模式，區別於東歐的轉型市場或者東亞的發展型國家模式，雖然帶來了驚人的經濟增長，但同時也產生了普遍性的社會不平等，尤其導致了工人群體的困境。在改革開放以來的30年，香港與臺灣正是對中國大陸輸入資本最多的兩個地區（遠遠高於其他國家或地區）。 對於FDI對中國經濟和社會帶來的影響，我們需要把它放在在一個具體行業或者企業發展及演變成行業寡頭進行深入的分析。關於資本壟斷，我們指的是通過成功的並購和重組，資本以前所未有的速度和規模進行擴張從而使某個工業企業迅速成為全球的主導者。得益於地方政府在其資本積累與擴張中的大力支持，資本壟斷使得某個工業巨頭得以佔有無可比擬的市場份額。富士康以其擴張速度之快、規模之大堪稱製造業中傳奇，對於研究大資本擴張的現象極具代表性和重要性。

547312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
547312.value: This study begins by questioning why the fashion industry appears to relatively behind in attending to its environmental footprints and sustainable issues in need of effective solutions despite the fact that awareness about ethical/eco-friendly fashion has grown in recent years. In order to provide the answers to this question, this study will not only examine the current status of sustainability in fashion industry, with particular focus on fashion design practices as well as on the role of the fashion designer, but also develop the practical yet innovative solutions and alternatives that will compensate for and be a supplement to the current problems and limitations without defying standard marketing logic or diluting aesthetic standards. To achieve the aim of this study several crucial research stages are proposed. The first will involve the investigation of the negative environmental impact as well as current status of the sustainable practices introduced and implemented by fashion industry. The literature has identified the environmental and sustainable issues of relevance in the fashion and textile industry and suggested corresponding solutions. None of the prior research has, however led to concrete and feasible solutions that can be employed at the stage of fashion design or be managed by fashion designers, who are believed to be empowered to influence the market as well as the customer’s perspective on fashion. As a consequence, identifying what has hindered the development and promotion of sustainability in fashion design is the initial task of this study. Secondly, based upon the data collected from the literature review and case studies of sustainable fashion practices, it is possible not only to diagnose what and how serious the most fundamental and common problems are, but also to prescribe the innovative yet feasible solutions and alternatives for sustainable fashion. It is imperative to develop new or at least improved practices and strategies because those introduced to date seem to have failed to attract the majority of people and to educate them regarding the consequences and urgency of their participation and further action. The scope of this study will focus on the fashion design sector and the role of the fashion designer not only to implement sustainability in the industry, but also to ensure it is comprehended by the consumers. The outcome of this research project will be an academic paper which provides an innovative and practical framework for the implementation of sustainability in fashion design. 本論文始於質詢當近年大眾對道德或環境友好時裝的意識有所增長之時，為何時裝業在處理其環境足印及需有效解決方案的可持續性議題上，看來還是較為落後。為了尋求答案，本論文不但會以時裝設計的實踐與時裝設計師的角色為焦點，檢視當今時裝行業的可持續性，更會發展出實用又創新的解決方案和另類選擇，在不違反標準市場邏輯或降低審美標準下，彌補現有的問題與局限。 要達到本論文的目標，建議進行若干階段的研究調查。第一階段將包括逐一調查時裝行業對環境帶來的負面衝擊，以及時裝業引入與實施可持續實踐的現況。文獻中已識別了與時裝及紡織業有關的環境和可持續問題，亦指出了相應之解決方案。但是，在相信時裝設計師有著影響市場及顧客對時裝觀點的能力下，從來沒有一項研究有帶出過在設計階段已能採用的、時裝設計師能駕馭的、實則及可行的方案。由此可見，本論文的首要任務，就是要識別出妨礙發展及促進時裝設計可持續性的地方。第二階段，憑著對時裝可持續性實踐的文獻回顧及個案研究後收集到的數據，不但可以診斷出最根本及常見問題所在之處及其嚴重性，更能對症下藥，為可持續時裝提供可行又創新的解決方案。開發新的、改良的實踐及對策是必須的，因為現有的實踐及對策，看來都不足以吸引大多數人，又未能教育他們關於自身參與及行動的重要性和逼切性。 本論文之範疇將重點放於時裝設計的部份及時裝設計師的角色之上，不單止要在業界履行可持續性，更要確保顧客對此事是了解的。相關的議題如有機紡織品的運用、新發明的纖維及紡織科技之應用、零售階段的成衣包裝和減少廢棄物，對於發展可持續時裝來說都不可或缺，將會被涵蓋於研究之列。此研究計劃的結果將會是一份學術論文，為在時裝設計中履行可持續性提供創新、實用的架構。

547312.label: Realisation of objectives
547312.value: There were five objectives in the original application, to achieve these objective the process and methods used in this project has been stated in the text below. 1. Examined the hazardous environmental impacts created by the fashion industry as well as the current stage of sustainable fashion practices. − Hazardous environmental impacts created by the fashion industry: Numerous negative impacts generated from every stage of a garment’s lifecycle from cultivating and harvesting to post-consumption were examined and the unsustainable results from those impacts were identified. They are various types of pollutions, depletion of resources, waste from manufacture to pre- and post-consumption and unethical working conditions. − Commonly implemented and newly introduced sustainable practices in fashion industry to date: co-creation and co-ownership, up-cycling, waste reduction by innovative pattern making and digital technology, and development of new materials (e.g. biologically grown textiles). 2. Identified various problematic limits and obstacles a fashion designer currently faces when creating sustainable fashion. A number of major obstacles in development of sustainable fashion have been examined and identified: Raison d’etre of fashion (relationship between fashion and the human desires for new items, novel experiences, and constant reformulation of identity), fashion paradox of transience and sustainability, lack of access to information regarding sustainable fashion, and relatively high-priced range of sustainable products which require consumer to defy market logic. 3. Established a conceptual definition of sustainable fashion design which would not only help to draw a clear boundary between genuine practices and superficial “in name only” efforts, but also provide a theoretical platform for developing innovative and feasible practices for the current fashion system. The importance of textile material diversity was realized during an extensive literature review to identify various hazardous environmental impacts generated by the fashion industry. What came to the researchers’ attention was the dominance of certain fibers which resulted in the phenomenon of monoculture and limited the range of material choices for fashion designers. This was an unexpected deviation encountered in this reporting period but the researchers decided to pursue this topic further after having been convinced that this new concept of textile material diversity could be incorporated into the development of sustainable textiles and furthermore, of sustainable design practices. Based on the study of monoculture and biodiversity, the concept of textile material diversity is established and a new sustainable strategy called ‘considerate material decision strategy’ was proposed. This strategy provided a guideline for fashion designers to make more appropriate material choices at the beginning of design process after considering various factors, such as consumer/company attitudes, environmental values, material impacts, production methods and after-sales service. 4. Defined the important roles which fashion producers, including designers and others in manufacturing, should carry out in order to improve the level of sustainability in the fashion industry. To achieve this objective, two surveys conducted during the research period. The first survey questionnaire was designed to diagnose the current standpoint of general public as a consumer group towards sustainable fashion. This questionnaire consists of 3 main parts which were: their basic cognition of sustainable fashion and textiles; their attitude towards environment, social and economic issues in the fashion industry; and finally, their experiences and expectations for sustainable fashion. The second survey questionnaire was designed to collect fashion designers’ views on sustainable fashion; the degree of their recognition of their roles and duties; and finally, the obstacles they face in the development of sustainable fashion design practices. 5. Developed practical and innovative solutions and alternatives for sustainable fashion design that could satisfy both producers and consumers, without defying standard market logic and abandoning its fundamental function as a vehicle to meet human desire, according to the newly established definition of ‘sustainable fashion’. − The sustainable textiles using bacterial cellulose was developed during the project period with the aim of extending the range of material choices for sustainable fashion design practices. Since textiles cultivated from bacterial cellulose is no longer a novel invention, the researchers strove to devise production methods that would eliminate cutting and sewing processes and reduce textile waste. On the basis of the nature of bacterial cellulose which can be engineered to have specific desirable properties for textiles and garment production (e.g., shape and colour), the idea of tailor-shaped cultivation is conceived and developed. Bacterial cellulose textiles in the shape of garment panel can be produced through cultivating them in a garment panel-shaped container (aka bioreactor). A single container can cultivate garment panels in different sizes and grades by engineering its size and shape and adjusting the level of water poured into the container. Various experiments, such as testing different recipes, post-treatments on drying, dyeing, bleaching and producing in various forms (e.g., roll-form, thread, garment-shaped panel) via moulding and tailor-shaped cultivation, were conducted as well. − A revision request was proposed in January of 2016 to extend the project for six months and the approval was made until March 2016. From March to the end of June 2016, a series of patterns (four different kinds of patterns with the elements of “43” and “cross”) for digital printing was designed, and the digital printed fabrics were designed into a collection of garments (total 20 garments) by collaborating with the Mexican fashion designer Carmen Rion (CR). The collaborating collection called “MX+HK” was participated in the Festival International des Textiles Extra Ordinaries 2016 (FITE) and presented in the fashion show during September 2016.

547312.label: Major findings and research outcome
547312.value: 1. The Hazardous environment impacts created by the fashion industry and the current stage of sustainable fashion practices had been examined. Currently, the negative impacts on environment are existed in each step of the garment lifecycle, from the textile to post-consumption. Unreasonable production process and Unethical working conditions caused various types of pollutions and resources wasted. There are some practices of sustainable fashion have been done by some fashion designers, most of these practices can be summarised as co-creation and co-ownership, up-cycling, waste reduction by innovative pattern making and digital technology, and development of new materials. 2. The problematic limits and obstacles the fashion designer facing when creating sustainable fashions had been identified. There are a series of problems which limits fashion designers expand their designs. Some developed sustainable products are not accepted by the customers due to those products cannot actually meet the demand. Moreover, problems like fashion paradox of transience and sustainability, lack of access to information regarding sustainable fashion, and relatively high-priced range of sustainable products also hinder the development of sustainable fashion. 3. A conceptual definition of sustainable fashion design had been established to help designers to have a more clear boundary and provide a theoretical platform for developing innovative and feasible practices. It has been found that the sustainability of textile is an efficient approach for sustainable fashion design. Therefore, experiments to create material diversity had been conducted to develop sustainable textiles. The knowledge of monoculture and biodiversity had been studied, which helped form the concept of textile material diversity and finally proposed a new sustainable strategy called ‘considerate material decision strategy’. This strategy provided a guideline for fashion designers to make more appropriate material choices at the beginning of design process. The production method to produce bacterial cellulose textiles through a garment shape container was researched as well. Related research results had been presented at the international conference in October 2014 and December 2014 respectively. 4. More trials had been conducted with sustainable solutions for fashion design in order to prove that the sustainable fashion is possible to satisfy both producers and consumers. Digital printing was selected as a more sustainable alternative of traditional dyeing and printing to manufactured in quantity. The produced textiles were collaborated designed with a Mexico designers and showed in FITE 2016 in France.

547312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
547312.value: In this project, one sustainable strategy has been proposed and two solutions have been applied for sustainable fashion design. According to the strategy, ‘considerate material decision strategy’, the researchers only explored one kind of bio-textile based on biodiversity theory, which is still stayed in laboratory level and has some obstacles need to be overcome to see if bacterial cellulose textile can be produced in scale. If the problems could be solved, this method would be very meaningful to expand the material diversity. This strategy is also suitable for exploring other new materials in future. Another solution, digital printing, has been employed in the industry within a certain range. The limits of these solution is the high-price, which still cannot be widely accepted by the manufacturer. The researches focus on lower the production cost is also valuable in the future. More importantly, more solutions should be explored and apply for the sustainable fashion design in order to provide examples for the fashion companies to optimise the design, production process and business.

547312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
547312.value: Through the research project, the hazardous environmental impacts have been examined and the problems that fashion designers facing and limiting their fashion designer have been detected. It found that the problems existing in whole garment lifecycle. However, some actions could be done in the design/cultivating stage to improve sustainability of the whole garment making process. One sustainable strategy and two solutions have been researched for sustainable fashion design. The strategy, ‘considerate material decision strategy’ provide a model for researchers and designers to explore the new textile materials. The practice of digital printing textile design and collaborating fashion design provides a path for fashion designers and fashion companies that the sustainable fashion has potentials to further developed and can be widely employed gradually.

547412.label: Project Objectives
547412.value: To provide a comprehensive understanding of Hong Kong's current waste recycling policy and practice, and identify the difficulties in community and household participation from a holistic perspective. To come to an in-depth understanding of how the design of recycling facilities can promote, motivate, and facilitate community and household participation in waste recycling, with particular attention paid to densely populated communities and living environments. To provide a reference for the government, local authorities, professionals, environmental concern groups, NGOs, researchers, property developers and management companies, and communities to help them to plan, design and manage good-quality recycling facilities that facilitate waste recycling. To raise the awareness of and provide a reference to the aforementioned parties to facilitate public design research on the promotion of waste recycling. To generate references for the principal investigator (PI) and other researchers to carry out further long-term and comprehensive research (e.g., longitudinal research, action research) on public design and waste recycling. To improve research methods and tools to make them more rigorous and disciplined and, ultimately, constitute a useful resource for researchers and professionals to conduct investigations on community and household participation in waste recycling in other countries/cities.

547412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
547412.value: 可持續性發展的根本是循環再利用，垃圾廢物的循環再利用是環境保護的關鍵。然而，根據最近香港政府的相關報導，由於只有有限的社區及家庭參與，香港的垃圾廢物回收再利用水準不能讓人滿意。與諸如日本等其他亞太國家及地區相比，香港對人們日常生活中的環境保護和可持續性的回收利用活動只進行了很少的研究。香港之前的相關研究多數集中在區域物流管理，工業廠房建設，垃圾廢物處理和材料研究的技術層面。然而不同於香港，在亞太其他國家和城市，許多政府機構和研究人員已經開始研究人們的日常生活和廢物回收再利用的關係極其重要性。亞太地區的許多城市已經投入了相當大的努力促進社區及家庭範圍內的廢物回收再利用。香港是亞太地區垃圾廢物處理率最高的城市之一，並且其垃圾處理率正迅速提升，然而香港城市廢物循環再利用的研究卻遠遠落後於同地區的其他城市，尤其缺乏對促進社區及家庭廢物回收的公共設施設計進行深度的設計研究。在過去的20年，香港已有一些針對廢物回收的研究和設計，但這些研究和設計最大的不足是它們僅僅從技術和功能層面進行研究，其他諸如生活方式，人居環境，城市和社區的社會及文化等因素從未被考慮到相關研究之中，並且之前的研究和設計都是集中在較小的尺度，只針對特定的情形。因此爲了彌補香港循環環保設施研究的匱乏，一個針對香港循環環保政策的初步研究已於2009-2011年完成，該研究指出了進行全面性的公共循環環保設計綜合性研究的必要性。因此本研究計畫的目的是不但從技術及功能層面，而且從生活方式、人居環境、社會及文化層面對廢物回收設施的設計進行研究探索。此項目的研究範圍集中在社區及家庭層面，包括對現狀的全面檢討評價及其行動研究，從而促進相關公共環保設施的設計並促使香港市民更好的參與到日常的回收環保活動中，同時此項目也為將來類似及相關領域的研究提供依據和說明。

547412.label: Realisation of objectives
547412.value: The research team carried the project as the original plan. There were 7 stages of research activities to meet the planned objectives. (I) Literature and document review • Review of waste recycling trends and current policies. • Review of policies and professional practices related to waste recycling. • Review of Hong Kong waste recycling policies at the community and household levels. (II) Semi-structured interviews with various parties • Government officers (e.g., EPD, ECC and Housing Authority officers): To collect data on waste recycling policies, plans, implementation and management, with a focus on recycling facilities. • Representatives of NGOs and local communities: To collect views and comments on current waste recycling practices. • Other related parties (e.g., property management companies, professional bodies related to property management): To collect data related to the management of waste recycling. (III) Structured interviews (questionnaire interviews) • Case selection: Of the 18 districts defined by the Home Affairs Bureau, residents of different residential estates in six districts of Hong Kong were selected for questionnaire interviews. • Questionnaire survey: To collect general comments from residents of the selected estates on their living environment, general daily routine and methods of waste disposal. (IV) Semi-structured interviews with selected informants • With selected informants: - further information about their lifestyles, particularly issues related to their living environments, daily routines and methods of waste disposal; - their views on current waste recycling policies; - their comments on the design of existing general recycling facilities; - their views on the arrangement of and available facilities for recycling; and - their individual needs, preferences and expectations for waste recycling. • With NGO representatives. To collect: - their comments on the overall policies and facilities for waste recycling; - their comments on the inclusive approach to the design of these facilities; and - their views on and suggestions for waste recycling. • With related management companies (if any in the selected cases). To collect: - their comments on the overall policies and facilities for waste recycling; and - their views on the management issues involved. (V) Case study (system and product design analysis) Referring to the 12 selected sites (cases), site visits, observations of user behaviour, and system and product analysis of existing recycling facilities were carried out as follows. • Waste recycling system related to district and regional policies and logistics arrangements. • Community and residential living environment for the entire recycling system and facility provision. • Logistics arrangements for waste recycling. • Particular facilities related to waste recycling with regard to particular community and household needs and preferences. • Product analysis of the selected facilities considered not only functionality or physical usability, but the attributes for exploration. • Non-participant observations: User behaviour with regard to current recycling facilities was observed. These observations were conducted at different periods of time on different days. (VI) Action research • Selected sites (housing estates) were selected for this action research activity. • One public housing building and one private housing building were selected for the action research. • Site selection was taken place with the relevant government departments and project collaborators. The respondents (households) giving feedback on the designs were randomly sampled. The property manager and waste cleaner(s) of each selected building were also be selected as respondents. • In response to respondents’ views and comments, concepts for improvements to systems and facilities were illustrated to elicit further comments. • Prior to product implementation, some illustrations were be used as the “means” by which to communicate with respondents. • On-site action tests of the selected facilities. (VII) Analysis and evaluation Data were collected throughout the research process. A final stage of analysis was carried out with invited government officers, representatives of environmental protection organisations/groups and professionals.
