547412.label: Major findings and research outcome
547412.value: The findings and gained experience of the project are very satisfactory and encouraging, though the research team faced quite a lot of difficulties, in particular it was difficult to invite housing estates and household users to participate in the action research. The findings of the project show that it is not only personal factors such as norms and attitudes but also contextual factors such as availability of facilities and physical settings that influence pro-environmental behaviour (see Research Publication Outputs [#1-4] in Part C of this report). Ignoring the social, cultural and structural aspects may lead to failure in understanding the issues of public participation in recycling [see #1, 2, 3]. The outputs of the project include journal publications, presentations and other outputs such as postgraduate research study training and tools for teaching. According to the findings, context is divided into three aspects: (1) physical, (2) social, and (3) socio-cultural contexts. Each one of the variables of contexts is indicated as a factor that affected recycling behaviour [#1, 2, 3]. The findings indicate that the availability of nearby recycling facilities, satisfaction with the location of recycling facilities, satisfaction with other residents’ participation, and satisfaction with the neighbourhood and with accommodation are significant predictors of the use of public recycling facilities [#2]. Due to a lack of clear consideration from the users’ perspectives, however, the finding indicate that many public designs do not meet their requirements and preferences [#1, 2, 3]. To explore people’s perceptions and reactions towards design and management, appropriate design interventions and collaboration are important and necessary [#4]. All attempts of intervention are passive in nature, from ‘I urge you to’, enabling approaches and ‘I ask you to’ motivating approaches, to ‘I order you to’ constraining approaches, while attempts of collaboration can be described as active approaches, from ‘I help you to do’ and ‘you need me to do’, to ‘we do together’. Efforts to facilitate active involvement in recycling must also consider different stakeholders and encourage them to voice their views in the early design stage [#4]. Higher degrees of user satisfaction and public participation can be achieved if participants witness follow-up actions based on their comments. As indicated in the project objectives, one of the key mission and goals of the project is to apply and then research methods using in/by design as well as humanities research. Accordingly, the project is able to generate new methods and tools to achieve good public design for recycling. According to the research and teaching experience of the PI as well as various design research publications, these methods such as participatory action research (PAR) are good ways to empower people (ordinary people, users) to express their opinions and to enhance people’s competency in the community [#4]. Through the action and reflection, these methods help and motivate researchers understand the situations and what aspects could be adjusted in future studies.

547412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
547412.value: The project generated some new directions for further research. For example, design interventions and collaboration have great potential to influence recycling behaviour. In-depth and continuous studies conducted in different contexts are required to test and evaluate the effectiveness of intervention and collaboration. Comparative studies in different cities are also essential. Regarding the research methods, PAR is a valuable strategy for public design. Conducting PAR enables researchers to review, plan, evaluate, adjust and implement the design step by step, providing an in-depth understanding of various concerns that are often neglected or misunderstood by designers, professionals and governments. The PI developed new research approaches as well as methods (using in design research) to examine recycling practice and to improve public design and has raised several reflections for design researchers and professionals. Further studies on these approaches and perspectives are necessary. This project provided insights into how to conduct (participatory) action research in public design for household recycling. The key experiences and methods in this project provided references for greater mobilisation and changes in other public design issues. Although it is not easy to conduct PAR in community activities, the PI advocated and proposed that researchers, policymakers and professionals need to take into consideration of conducting action research on public design issues.

547412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
547412.value: In recent years, many studies on recycling mainly focus on policy, waste management, public awareness, and social norms, yet seldom on public design encompassing physical, social and socio-cultural context. By comprehensive review on a territory-wide basis and action research in several selected housing estates, the project brought about a more comprehensive understanding of Hong Kong’s current recycling policy and practice. The project identified the difficulties and barriers in community and household participation. It generated insights and references (i.e., publications and presentations) for those involved in policymaking, design and sustainable development, and raised new research perspectives and approaches for further discussion and investigation. A key finding of the project was that understanding the contextual factors, including the physical, social and socio-cultural factors, is helpful to developing recycling behaviour that is effective and sustainable. Intervention and collaboration as two main approaches are good to influence (i.e., positively motivate and facilitate) recycling behaviour. It also suggested that people’s responses and reactions to the influence determine the effects of intervention. The project involved a practice-led research approach (e.g., participatory action research (PAR)), which is relative difficult and time-consuming, and is seldom considered by policymakers and professionals. The methods and experience generated for carry out action research are useful for public design issues.

547512.label: Project Objectives
547512.value: To specify a GVAR system in which both the country/region specific and global variables are modelled endogenously; To examine the interactions involved in the demand for tourism (measured by inbound and outbound tourist expenditures) in a large number of selected countries/regions; To carry out simulations of China’s contributions to world tourism by considering the shocks to China’s economic growth and the RMB exchange rate; To generate forecasts of the demand for tourism in all destination and origin countries/regions concerned; To provide policy suggestions for key tourism destination and origin countries/regions, with a particular focus on China’s contribution to world tourism.

547512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
547512.value: Given the significant contributions of tourism to the world economy, researchers have been continuously looking for the best ways in which the demand for world tourism can be assessed. This project proposes a new method, known as the global vector autoregressive (GVAR) approach to model the demand for tourism, which is jointly measured by both tourism imports and exports. This research would be the first attempt to link country/region specific tourism demand models with the GVAR modelling framework. This modelling strategy will permit us to examine the spillover effects of tourist expenditures among a large number of countries/regions. The study is related to the modelling of both inbound and outbound tourism in a single system, which can provide very useful information for both policy makers and researchers in terms of their concerns about the imbalance of tourism imports and exports. Enhanced simulation and monitoring opportunities will be made available using the GVAR model for examining the impacts of various shocks to the destination and origin economies on global tourism demand. A particular emphasis of the project will also be placed on the investigation of the role that China will play in stabilising world tourism demand fluctuations through the impulse response analysis and forecasting exercise. 鉴于旅游业对全球经济的重大贡献，研究人员一直在寻找评估世界旅游需求的最佳方法。本研究提出以GVAR这一新方法，同时测量旅游进口及出口额来建构旅游需求模型。这将会是首次尝试把国家/地区特定的旅游需求模型与GVAR建模框架结合在一起。透过此建模策略，我们将可以检视大量国家/地区旅游支出的溢出效应。此外，本研究将建构在单一系统里入境和出境旅游的模型，就政策制定者和研究人员所关心的旅游进出口不平衡的问题提供有用资讯。GVAR建模可提高模拟和监测机会，有助于检查各种冲击对目的地和原地经济在全球旅游需求方面的影响。此项研究也会以脉冲响应分析和预测，重点探讨中国在稳定世界旅游需求波动中所扮演的角色。

547512.label: Realisation of objectives
547512.value: The research team has largely achieved the research objectives of the project. In particular, the GVAR model that incorporated tourism demand variables from 24 countries in the world has been developed. The data analysis and modeling exercise have been completed with interesting results. The study shows that the tourism developments in major tourism receiving and generating countries/regions are interdependent (Objectives 1 and 2). At the same time, the research results also show that China’s real tourism imports and real tourism exports would suffer from a temporary decline in the short run, but rebound in the long run. This suggest that it is important for tourism-related businesses in China to take cost reduction measures to counter the short-term decline in both inbound and outbound tourism demand. In comparison, real tourism imports and exports of other regions would tend to be affected in the short run. Over the long run, a notable example is South America, whose real tourism imports would go down and real tourism exports would go up, suggesting that local businesses in South America should be prepared for increasing inbound tourism demand after the shock to China (Objective 3). The forecasting performance of the GVAR model was evaluated against its competing model – the VAR model and the results demonstrated that the forecasting performance of the GVAR model has improved (Objective 4). Policy implications of the study are provided based on the research findings of the study (Objective 5). In particular, a paper specifically dealing with the policy implications are summarized in a paper entitled “Tourism economic globalization: an emerging research agenda”, which is in the second round of review by Journal of Travel Research, and we are confidence that the paper will be accepted for publication soon.

547512.label: Major findings and research outcome
547512.value: This study examines the interdependence among 24 major countries. It adopts the GVAR approach to quantify the co-movements of tourism demand and to calculate the contemporaneous impact elasticities and impulse responses of exogenous shocks. The results are particularly relevant to tourism policy makers and multinational corporations that monitor their macroeconomic environment, especially in times of turbulence. At the macro level, the contemporaneous impact elasticity is a measure of the level of a country’s global integration, as it shows the scale of co-movements between the country and the rest of the global system. At the corporate level, the elasticity can be used as a general indicator of the variations in local economies. Knowing the magnitude of the changes that their local economies will experience in response to changes in the global environment allows businesses to conduct further evaluations to gauge the effects on their profitability and to make informed decisions about procurement and employment. The impulse response analysis is useful in pointing out the “closeness” between economies. A shock to China’s real income or own price variable would cause short-term synchronized fluctuations across both the developing regions and the developed regions, whereas the long-run effects tend to be evident for the developing regions and for China’s neighboring region. Tourism-related businesses can make use of the information about the length of time before their local economies are likely to restore equilibrium and thus allow for sufficient flexibilities in their production (e.g., flexibility in employment arrangements). The current study fills a gap by modeling tourism demand in a cross-country interdependent setting. It contributes to the theoretical and practical knowledge of tourism demand, especially the endogeneity within worldwide tourism demand. Given the specific strengths of the GVAR approach, it has plenty of potential applications in tourism research. In terms of output, this study generated a review/ meta-analysis article looking at the use of econometric models in tourism demand forecasting, which was published in Tourism Management (a top-tier journal in the field of tourism research). Two articles resulted from the project are currently under consideration by two tourism journals (Journal of Travel Research and Annals of Tourism Research).

547512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
547512.value: Future studies may continue to explore the interdependent nature of global tourism sectors by applying time-varying-parameter techniques to capture the changes in contemporaneous impact elasticities over time. The global VAR approach can be combined with Bayesian statistics to deal with the over-parameterization issue. In terms of the scope of study, the global VAR approach can be applied to a regional context that consists of active intra-regional tourism, or used to explore the interdependence of tourism and other sectors within an economy. The approach can also be used to forecast tourism demand across a range of countries and generate robust forecasts, as it takes into account the interdependence across countries. The research team had already developed a GRF project (Ref. No. 15501415), extending the research into the direction of Bayesian GVAR modeling and forecasting.

547512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
547512.value: This study develops a tourism demand model using an innovative approach named the Global Vector Autoregressive (Global VAR or GVAR) model to measure the interdependence of tourism demand in terms of co-movements among selected major countries worldwide. Recognizing China’s ascending status in the global economy, this study further examines the effect of shocks to the Chinese economy and simulates the subsequent disruptions to China’s top tourism partners. This study makes several contributions. It represents an initial attempt within tourism demand research to study the interdependent aspect of international tourism demand, which is a research direction that worth more attention. In particular, the study provides quantitative evidence of the implications of globalization for tourism sectors around the world. Methodologically, this research expands tourism demand modeling studies by introducing an innovative system-of-equations technique which overcomes the over-parameterization issue that can occur when accommodating a large set of endogenous variables in a model.

548812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
548812.value: The delivery of services involves unique characteristics that can lead to suboptimal service quality, or service failures, in the eyes of consumers. Service failures are to some extent inevitable and often poorly handled by service delivery staff, resulting in significant losses for organizations. It is therefore critical that service firms better understand how to effectively recover from these situations. In an extension to justice theory, the proposed research examines consumer responses to multiple service failure events caused by one service firm, and their impact on responses towards closely affiliated firms. Thus, this research is unique in that it 1) examines consumer responses to service failures in a multiple service provider setting (strategic alliances), as opposed to the currently prevalent investigation of single service provider settings, thereby addressing recent changes in the business environment, and 2) explores the impact of multiple service failure events, as opposed to single service failure events. Data collection will involve an experimental design, with both a Chinese and Australian sample to also investigate cross-cultural differences in perceptions of and behavior to service failure/recovery. Research results will make significant theoretical and practical contributions. 服務遞送之特色可能會導致消費者認為不完美的服務質素或服務失敗。服務失敗從某種程度上講是在所難免，而實施服務遞送的員工經常會處理失當，結果所在組織受到重大損失。因此，服務公司應當了解如何在這些情況下進行有效補救。作為正義理論的延伸，本研究建議審視了由一間服務公司引起的許多服務失敗問題後的消費者反應，以及他們對緊密相關之公司的反應。因此，本研究的特色在於1)審視了在多個服務供應商條件下（戰略聯盟）的消費者對服務遞送失敗的反應，以及與目前常見的對單一服務供應商條件的調查相比較，由此突出商務環境的最新變化；而且2)探討了多個服務失敗問題的影響，以及與單個服務失敗問題的比較。數據收集將包括試驗性設計，在中國和澳洲取樣，并且調查消費者對服務失敗與恢復在看法和行為上的跨文化差異。研究結果在理論與實踐上都有重大的貢獻。

548812.label: Realisation of objectives
548812.value: In order to extend justice theory from a single to a multiple service failure, a model of organizational justice originally proposed by Cropanzano and colleagues’ (2001) and adapted by Weber and Sparks (2003; 2006) to the service failure/recovery settings in strategic airline alliances was utilized. Further refinement to that model provided the basis for clearly differentiating between event and global justice perceptions on consumer responses for various alliance entities rather than only the firm that caused the service failure – the latter typically being the main focus of service failure research to date. A key problem of prior research was that by examining the impact of a single service failure event only, respondents’ event and global justice/fairness perceptions were potentially the same. Thus, in our study, we examined how a series of service failure events impact on global fairness evaluations. As we collected data in both Australia and China, we were also able to identify similarities and key differences for Western versus Chinese consumers. Thus, all objectives of our research project have been achieved. In addition to conducting this research project, the PI also supervised a MSc student who successfully completed her thesis in April 2015 on a closely related topic, investigating multiple service failures in a different (meeting) industry setting. A paper based on the student’s thesis has been accepted for presentation at a major conference in the United States in June 2016, and a journal article is also being prepared. A paper presented at a major services marketing conference. However, the publication of study results in top tier journal has been delayed for a number of reasons, as follows: 1) Several other major research projects (including 2 RGC fundable but not funded projects) that were awarded/approved prior the awarding of this GRF grant had to/have been successfully completed during the project period, with additional research publications from other prior research collaborations/thesis supervisions (please refer to the publication list provided below). 2) The Co-Investigator for this project, located in Australia, semi-retired in 2013, was on long-service leave for several months in summer 2014 and has shifted her research interest to other areas. 3) The research account was temporarily frozen for 3 months in early 2015 which delayed the collection of additional data for this project. 4) There were several problems detected with the quality of that data collected by a market research company that had to be rectified, leading to the need to initiate an additional round of data collection (the dataset provided by the market research company made reference to actual times for the completion of the questions relating to the experiment by each respondent; there was a significant number of responses that were completed in less than 4 minutes when the projected/pre-tested time for completion was 12-15 minutes. This suggested that despite getting compensated well for the participation in the research, respondents simply completed the survey without regard for the questions asked, rendering their responses unusable) With the various challenges now being addressed, the publication of the results of this study will be given top priority. 548812.label: Major findings and research outcome
548812.value: We employed a 2 (Type of Justice: Interactional versus Distributive) x 2 (Service Failure Severity: Severe versus non-severe) x 2 (Service Recovery Outcome: Satisfactory versus Non-satisfactory) x 3 (Alliance Entity: home carrier, partner airline, alliance) factorial design whereby the former three factors were the between-subject factors and the latter was a within-subject factor. Event and global justice perceptions, event and global fairness, satisfaction, and behavioral intentions constituted the dependent variables. The preparation/revision of papers reporting the research findings, aimed at two A+ journals in the field, is still in progress; we will update RGC via the Research Office as soon as they are finalized. Data was collected from two samples, frequent flyers in China and in Australia, consistent with the study objectives to 1) gain insights into Chinese consumers’ perceptions of and behavior to service failure/recovery and 2) contrast their perceptions and behavior with those of Western customers. A total of 400 completed responses each in China and Australia was obtained. Results of repeated measures MANOVA indicated that there were three main effects that were further qualified by interaction effects between type of justice, service failure severity and service recovery outcome. Specifically, event and global fairness perceptions, and subsequent satisfaction and behavioral intentions were the lowest in a service failure situation characterized by low interactional justice, high perceived severity and a non-satisfactory service outcome when the partner airline caused the service failure. In contrast, event and global fairness perceptions, and subsequent satisfaction and behavioral intentions were significantly higher in the same service failure situation when the service failure was caused by the home carrier. However, consumer responses were equally negative towards all alliance entities when multiple service failures occurred, suggesting that all alliance entities are held equally responsible. Examining differences between Australian and Chinese consumers, results indicated that for the latter multiple service failure situations characterized by low interactional justice had a significantly more negative impact on their fairness perceptions and satisfaction and behavioral intentions for all alliance entities than was the case for Australian consumers. There was no significant difference between the two samples for service failure characterized by low procedural justice.

Once the publications for this project are completed, research focus will be shifted to other areas of current/future research interest.

549212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
549212.value: Palliative care for end-stage organ failure patients has been included as one of the key programs to be implemented in 2011-2012 by the Hospital Authority, Hong Kong. Among all the disease groups, end-stage heart failure (HF) patients have the highest mortality rate. Patients at the end stage of HF have health concerns shared by other end-stage patients, including cancer patients. Many guidelines, local and world-wide, have advocated a palliative approach to caring for HF patients who are at the end stage. Studies have shown that end-stage HF patients tend to make frequent emergency room visits and are repeatedly admitted to hospital. Also, these patients suffer from a number of health problems that adversely affect their QOL. There are few experimental studies informing practitioners which models work best for palliative patients in Hong Kong. Randomized controlled trials have been conducted outside Hong Kong which suggest that a multidisciplinary approach to palliative care is possible in order to reduce readmissions, but evidence is not present for other outcomes such as symptom control and carer burden. In an attempt to fill the knowledge gap and inform practice with evidence, this study will be launched to compare the effects of customary hospital-based palliative HF care and an interventional Home-based Palliative HF Program. 香港醫院管理局在2011-2012年度將器官衰竭病人的晚期纾緩照顧納入為重點服務項目之一。在眾多系統疾病中，晚期心衰竭病人的死亡率佔最高。心衰竭病人在生命末段所面對的健康問題與癌症病人以致其他器官衰竭病人相約。全世界以致本地現在致力推動纾緩照顧模式，提供給晚期器官衰竭病人。研究顯示晚期心衰竭病人常要使用急症室及住院服務，他們的健康狀況大大影響了其生活質素。現時比較少有相關的隨機實驗研究，能讓醫護人員獲知那一服務模式對病人最有成效。有海外的研究指出多專業團隊能減少再住院率，但至於徵狀控制、照顧者壓力的成效則未有定案。為了通過科研證據去指導實務，這項研究引用了以家居為基礎的干預模式，比較常規以醫院為基礎的跟進，驗證那一服務模式對病人更最有成效。

549212.label: Realisation of objectives
549212.value: The project objectives were set out to examine the differences in healthcare utilization, evaluated health outcomes, perceived health outcomes between the home-based palliative end-stage heart failure group (HPHP) and the customary hospital-based group. The lived experiences of the end-stage heart failure (ESHF) patients receiving the HPHP program will also be explored as secondary objective. All of the objectives were fulfilled. The team was awarded with half of the amount of the original funding requested but the PI has gained support from the university to convert a part-time doctorate student to the full-time mode. She had the necessary clinical background to help screen eligibility of the cases and collect clinical information. This student will submit her doctorate thesis in autumn 2017. The support of the clinicians at the 3 study sites also was a key factor contributing to the success of the project. One of the study sites had to control the subject number to be recruited because of its heavy clinical commitment but fortunately the Medical Consultant in the other study hospital has lent his full support in making all eligible subjects available for our study. There were no baseline nor outcome differences among the 3 study sites. The project has yielded a number of outputs including conference presentations, publications in high impact factor journals and potential collaboration for further research.

549212.label: Major findings and research outcome
549212.value: The findings have provided evidence to support that the HPHP program is effective in reducing hospital readmissions, enhancing evaluated and perceived health outcomes. The hospital readmission rates were significantly lower in the intervention group as compared to the control group both at 4 weeks (intervention 20.9% vs control 29.3% χ2 =4.41, p=0.79) and 12 weeks (intervention 33.6% vs control 61.0% χ2 =6.8, p=0.009). Both measures of quality of life (QOL), the Chinese Heart failure questionnaire (CHQ) (p<0.01) and McGill QOL (p<0.05), showed a significant difference in the change over time between groups. When individual items were examined, all achieved statistically significant difference with group-time effect, except for ‘fatigue’ in CHQ and ‘physical’ and ‘existential’ in McGill. The intervention group had significantly higher satisfaction with care than the control group (p<0.001). The proportion of patients with improvement/deterioration/no change in symptoms was calculated based on the minimal clinically important difference cut-off reference. Results showed that compared to the control group, the intervention group experienced significantly higher clinical improvement in depression (45.9% vs 16.1%, p<0.05) dyspnoea (62.2% vs 29.0%, p<0.05) and total score (73.0% vs 41.4%, p<0.05). The carer burden was also much lower in the intervention group (intervention 16.07 vs control 23.10, p<0.05). The qualitative analysis interviewing the patients about their lived experiences revealed that the HPHP program provided readily available support for them to manage symptoms at home including drug adjustment, health education and modification for lifestyle to conserve energy and psychological support. The team also conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of the program. When the study group was compared to the control group, the net incremental quality-adjusted life years gain was 0.0012 (28 days)/0.0077 (84 days) and the net incremental costs per case was -HK7935 (28 days)/-HK$26084 (84 days). The probability of being cost-effective was 85% (28 days)/100% (84 days) based on the cost-effectiveness thresholds recommended both by National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence (£20000/quality-adjusted life years) and World Health Organization (Hong Kong gross domestic product/capita in 2015, HK$328117).

549212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
549212.value: Evidence produced in this study has generated interests in the international dialogue. When our paper was published in Heart in 2016, there was an editorial in the same journal cited and discussed our study. The authors wrote ‘The beauty of the study by Wong et al is their ability to leverage an established transitional care model to address palliative needs among community-dwelling patients with heart failure … their hopeful findings should motivate researchers and health system administrators alike to investigate opportunities for upstreaming and normalizing palliative care for patients with serious illness, including advanced HF.’ (Reference: Kavalierators D, Rollman BL & Arnold RM (2016) Homeward bound, not hospital bound: how transitional palliative care can reduce readmission Heart. Doi:10.1136/heartjnl-2016-309385. Our works also attracted international collaborator to investigate the referral system and issues for organ specialist physicians in seeking help from palliative specialists. In collaboration with the Edinburgh Napier University, the team have obtained £30,000 (app HK$616,902) Funded by Lawrence Ho Fund, Edinburgh Napier University, UK to launch a study titled ‘Cross cultural end-of-life clinical decision-making: A comparison of views and experiences of physicians in the referrals of end-stage organ failure patients for palliative care between Hong Kong and Scotland, United Kingdom.’

549212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
549212.value: Heart failure (HF) patients at their end-stage of life face issues that impede their quality of life with physical symptoms, psychological distress, and social loneliness. The palliative care approach has proven to be effective in supporting patients with these needs among the cancer group but less in non-cancer group. The palliative care approach is included in the latest international HF management guideline. This study is one of the few studies that has introduced a transitional care model supporting the end-stage HF patients returning home after an episode of hospitalization. The study has adopted a randomized controlled trial design and has proven that the home-based program provided by a nurse case manager, using an initial 4-week intensive program supplemented by monthly home visits and telephone calls are effective and cost-effective. The intervention program, when compared to the customary hospital-based practice, could significantly reduce hospital readmissions, enhance quality of life, symptom distress and has cost benefits to the system. Patients prefer to stay at home if at all possible without the need for hospitalization. When the biomedical curative approach of adding years to life is no longer possible, the holistic approach of palliative care to add life to years is preferred alternative.

549412.label: Project Objectives

549412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
549412.value: Over the years, research on knowledge has generated notions such as knowledge transfer (a two-community metaphor typical of science and engineering), knowledge management in the domains of business and information management, organizational learning or learning organizations in organizational studies, and constructivist notions such as knowledge mobilization and communities of learning and practice (e.g., in planning, development and health studies). The emergent community paradigm of knowledge has profound implications for praxis in a scientific community, experiential learning, and higher education in general, particularly for applied fields such as tourism and hotel management in which the responsiveness of the academia to industry and governmental practices is very high. With empirical evidence from Hong Kong, the purpose of this research is to evaluate university-industry partnership programs in tourism and hotel management. In particular, the roles and practices of educational institutions in the nurturing of communities of learning and practice in tourism and hotel management will be examined. Industry involvement in tourism and hotel management education will also be researched. In terms of methods, utilization-focused program evaluation will be adopted as the main approach to studying the university-industry partnership programs selected for this study. Notably, to minimize potential conflict of interest, this project (if funded) is going to be completed as an independent undertaking. Deliverable in the forms of journal articles and refereed conference presentations, results of the study will mainly contribute to literature on scientific community, experiential learning, and communities of learning and practice. Practically, this program evaluation research could also result in recommendations for and promotions of better practices of university-industry partnerships in tourism and hotel management in Hong Kong. 549412.label: Major findings and research outcome
549412.value: The roles and practices of university-industry partnership programs in the nurturing of communities of learning and practice in tourism and hospitality, as well as factors affecting such processes have been the focus of this research. The study finds that, with communities of learning and practice being the trend, applied education fields such as hospitality and tourism have increasingly concentrated on the delivery of such authentic learning experience through blended or work-integrated education. In the development and delivery of hospitality and tourism education, effective university-industry partnership programs have served as a valuable approach to bridging the divide between academic knowledge and practical skills. Centering around such communities of learning and practice, alternative forms of learning, learning style and learner preference, as well as pedagogical innovations are likely to emerge as promising areas for future education research. As outcomes from this research project, one conference paper and two journal articles (will) have been published in line with the above conceptual discussions.

549812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
549812.value: 服務人員與顧客之間的緊密關係與顧客的多樣化是服務業的主要特點。這些特點往往使到 傳統的運營管理方法失效；這也使到提升服務的績效成為營運管理者一項重大挑戰。本研究主要是探討服務人員的特質和激勵服務人員的領導模式對營運成績的影響。這研究會從理論和實證的角度探討服務業的轉型領導模式、員工的工作投入、營運成績和公司業績的關係。 我們計劃在服務業進行一項大型的研究。我們會收集員工、顧客和管理層三方面的資料（即員工、顧客和管理層），並利用結構方程模式分析所收集的資料。這研究具有很重要的學術和應用價值。它能嚴謹地利用三方面的資料探討轉型領導模式、員工的工作投入、營運成績和公司業績的關係。這研究與傳統的運營管理研究不同，它提供另一個能提升服務質量和公司績效的方向。這就是透過轉型領導模式對培育員工的工作投入度之影響，以致能有效地提升公司業績。

549812.label: Realisation of objectives
549812.value: Concerning Objective One, the impact of transformational leadership on job engagement, operational performance and firm outcome was investigated in the service industry characterized by a high level of customer contact. When conducting this part, other management practices, for example management commitment and empowerment, and employee attributes, for instance organizational commitment and learning orientation, that might be highly relevant and have potential to attain superior service quality by referring to the literature and the real practice, were identified. Such management practices and employee attributes were also included in the investigation. Data were collected and analyzed. The results reveal that management commitment and empowerment, rather than transformational leadership, affects employee attribute and service quality. Thus, Objective One is achieved. Regarding Objective Two, the moderating effects of employee-customer contact time and switching cost on the relationships hypothesized were explored in the high-contact service industry. Data were collected and analyzed. The findings showed that the studied moderators have no effect, implying that the hypothesized associations are quite robust in the service setting involving high customer contact. Hence, Objective Two is achieved.

549812.label: Major findings and research outcome
549812.value: Major findings: The findings show that transformational leadership does not have an effect on job engagement, as well as operational and business performance in the high-contact service context under study. Instead, other management practices, including management commitment and empowerment, influence employee attribute and operational performance. In the high-contact service setting, customers’ involvement and unpredictable requests introduce variability into service operations. This makes traditional efficiency-oriented techniques of operations management ineffective when dealing with high-contact services. Thus, the findings of this study is significant because they offer an alternative, effective way of enhancing operational performance by adopting proper management practices, such as management commitment and empowerment. Moreover, the results demonstrate that employee-customer contact and switching cost have no moderating effect in the studied context. Such results reinforce that the importance of proper management practices are universal in the high-contact service environment, i.e., such practices are not affected by contact time or switching cost. Research outcome: - A research student has been trained to conduct empirical research in the field of operations management. - One of the papers on this topic is published in a high-impact international journal of operations management, International Journal of Production Economics. - The research work was presented in an international conference. - One conference paper of this research is published.

549812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
549812.value: This research investigates the association among management leadership, employee job engagement, operational performance and business outcome. This investigation focuses on the high-contact service environment. To further develop the research work, it is suggested to replicate this study in the service domain with a low level of customer contact for the purpose to make a comparison between the high-contact and low-contact service settings. Accordingly, data is required to collect from low-contact service shops, such as convenient stores and fast-food restaurants. Analysis is needed to conduct for the comparison between the data acquired from the low-contact service context and from this research. This research examines moderating effect on the association between management leadership, employee attribute, and operational performance. For the purpose of research development, it is recommended to explore three-way interaction effect. For example, whether there is a three-way interaction effect among management leadership, employee work attribute and employee-customer contact level on operational performance. This proposed work has been under investigation in another study.

549812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
549812.value: Nature This research investigates the association among transformational leadership, job engagement, and service quality in the service industry characterized by a high level of customer contact. Significance This research shows that transformational leadership does not have an effect on employee work attribute and operational performance. Instead, management’s commitment has an influence on employee work attribute and a service firm’s operational performance. Moreover, this research demonstrates that customer contact and switching cost have no moderating effect in the high-contact service environment under study, implying that the impact of management’s practice is rather robust in the studied setting. Value This research is an inter-disciplinary study integrating the fields of organizational behavior and operations management. Inter-disciplinary study is widely considered imperative in the service context. Specifically, this research investigates the importance of management leadership and employee work attribute in implementing service operations. It provides a new avenue for service operations management, departing from the traditional efficiency-centric means. This research also offers practical guideline to firms in managing high-contact service operations. Instead of focusing on leadership, management’s commitment and empowerment are useful to improve employee service performance and a firm’s operational performance.

Examine if CEIs lead to corporate and agency benefits in the Chinese manufacturing industry. Based on the above results, propose and compare various theoretical perspectives that might explain the widespread diffusion of CEIs in China. In particular, we suspect that, in a highly institutionalized environment for environmental improvement, executives adopt voluntary environmental initiatives symbolically for corporate image building and personal advantage without achieving substantial pollution reduction.

550212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
550212.value: 我們將研究中國企業的環保措施 (CEIs) 對三個主要領域的影響, 包括公共利益（在污染減排方面），企業效益(銷售增長方面)，和個人動機好處(CEO個人好處方面)。CEIs定義為組織的環保計劃，連同相應的行動，其目的是減輕組織的產品或服務對環境的影響。 CEIs可分為兩大類。一個是自願企業的方案（例如，自願的環保產品投資），另一種是第三方認證或獎項（例如，ISO14001和中國環保獎）. 我們的研究將填補現有文獻中的缺口, 著眼於環保措施對企業和個人利益的影響。特別是，個人利益通常在傳統的環境管理研究中被忽視。在一個制度化的環境中，環境管理的象徵意義使企業直接授益，而沒有真正改善環境。基於CEIs 對公共利益，企業好處和個人動機三個領域影響的研究，我們將對CEIs在中國廣泛的擴散/採用提出不同的理論和解釋。

550212.label: Realisation of objectives
550212.value: In this research, we seek to examine the organizational consequences of Corporate Envrionemental Initiatives (CEIs) in China. In particular, environmental issues are increasingly more serious in the country. We seek to find out the possible factors behind CEIs in China, including corporate benefits, institutional factors and other managerial issues. Through this, we attempt to identify and theoretically explain the reasons behind the widespread diffusion of CEIs in China, including both environmental awards and self-regulatory environmental standards such as ISO 14001, which is also widely adopted in China. We believe that these objectives are achieved in general, although there were some challenges in the data collection process earlier in this research. Data Collection: We collect and combine longitudinal data from multiple sources to construct our research variables. First, we obtained Chinese firms’ announcements of CEIs from a news database named WiseNews. WiseNews is the world’s largest Chinese news database, which covers more than 1,900 Chinese newspapers and magazines such as Shanghai Securities News, China Securities Journal, and Secutimes, and has been widely used in prior studies regarding China. To provide a more comprehensive view of firms’ CEIs in China, we searched WiseNews in the ten-year period 2005 to 2014. Moreover, we focused our search to public firms that were included in the CSI 300 index from 2005 to 2014 for two reasons. First, the CSI 300 index consists of the 300 largest and most liquid Chinese stocks that are widely covered by various news media, thus reducing the bias of news coverage. Second, the CSI 300 index can be used as the market return in the Market model discussed below, allowing a more precise estimation of sample firms’ abnormal returns upon their CEI announcements. Similar to prior CEI studies conducted in the Western context, our search in WiseNews contained the names of the firms under study and the Chinese versions of the relevant keywords such as environment, green, ecosystem, recycle, and waste reduction. We read through the text of the searched results from WiseNews and excluded news articles that were (1) not directly related to CEIs such as public opinion on environmental issues and governments’ environmental policies, (2) concerned with firms that were not the constituents of the CSI 300 index, (3) duplicate reports of the same CEIs in different news media, or (4) confounded with other corporate events such as key executive appointments and annual earnings announcements. After elimination, we obtained 656 CEIs announced by 169 firms. Summary and Significance: We adopt signalling theory to explore when it pays to be green in China and stakeholders' responses in this regard. Signalling theory suggests that in the situation of information asymmetry, one party may need to rely on some observable signals sent by another party to interpret the underlying capabilities of the latter. Applying to our research context, the extent to which Chinese stakeholders value CEIs may depends on how they view the observable signals contained in CEI announcements. Signalling theory thus enables us to hypothesize how the observable characteristics of CEIs and firms may send different signals to Chinese stakeholders of firms, resulting in different reactions to firms’ CEI announcements. Consistent with our signalling logic, we find that the reactions are more negative for process-focused (rather than product-focused) CEIs and state-owned (rather than privately-owned) firms. However, there is no difference in stock returns between self-declared and third-party certified CEIs. Our research is important in several ways. First, while the financial implications of CEIs have been well studied in the Western context, little is known about Chinese firms’ CEIs. Our research fills this gap by studying 556 CEIs in China over a ten-year period 2005 to 2014. Moreover, the negative CARs found in our research challenge the pervasive claim that “it pays to be green” and highlight the importance of taking the national context into account when studying the financial implications of CEIs. In addition to the main effect, our research also documents how market reactions could vary across different CEIs and firms. These findings enable practitioners to gain a better understanding of not only whether but also when it pays to be green in China. Finally, the signalling perspective adopted in our research may offer a fruitful theoretical foundation for future research on CEIs.

550212.label: Major findings and research outcome
550212.value: In this research we examine stakeholders' reactions to CEIs in China. In contrast to the findings in the Western context, we find that Chinese stakeholders react negatively to CEIs. In other words, unlike stakeholders in Western countries, Chinese stakeholders may believe that CEIs would lower the profitability of a firm, i.e., environmental initiatives and business objectives are likely to be in conflict. Previous research in the US suggests that CEIs lower the operational costs of firms, improving their productivity. Through CEIs, firms minimize waste, energy, and material consumption, and reduce environmental compliance costs. By channelling more resources to environmental management, firms can reduce overall operational expenses and improve their corporate images, leading to higher profitability. However, it seems that the same belief is not commonly shared among Chinese stakeholders of firms. For theoretical contributions, the signalling perspective adopted in our research may offer a fruitful theoretical foundation for future research on CEIs. Signalling theory is suitable for studying CEIs because of the opaque nature of environmental management. In other words, it is not clear whether a CEI, when announced, can benefit the announcing firm financially. In this situation, stakeholders need to rely on other observable signals to interpret the financial consequences of the announced CEI. The signalling perspective is particularly useful in the context of China in which information is more opaque and entities are less accountable. Drawing upon signalling theory, researchers can study other interesting questions beyond those addressed in our research. For instance, while our research focuses on stakeholders' reactions to the signals sent by firms announcing CEIs, future research can explore how other stakeholders such as customers, suppliers, and competitors interpret and respond to firms’ CEI signals. On the other hand, in addition to the characteristics of firms and CEIs investigated in our research, researchers can examine how the signalling environment in China may moderate stakeholders’ reactions to CEIs. For example, stakeholders may react quite differently to CEIs announced in more polluted areas or industries. Overall, we encourage researchers to adopt the signalling perspective to enrich our understanding of CEIs in general and the Chinese context in particular.

550212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
550212.value: Future research can explore how other stakeholders such as customers, suppliers, and competitors interpret and respond to firms’ CEI signals. On the other hand, in addition to the characteristics of firms and CEIs investigated in our research, researchers can examine how the signalling environment in China may moderate stakeholders’ reactions to CEIs. For example, stakeholders may react quite differently to CEIs announced in more polluted areas or industries. Overall, we encourage researchers to adopt the signalling perspective to enrich our understanding of CEIs in general and the Chinese context in particular. There are some limitations in our research. As China is undergoing rapid economic, social, and technological development, it is possible that the mindsets of consumers and stakeholders will change in the near future. However, our findings should reflect the scenario in China during a period of fast economic development over the past decade. We believe that, by studying CEIs in China, we can better understand the perceived values of CEIs by some stakeholders. This will enable researchers and practitioners to gain a better understanding of the values of CEIs, providing important implications for operations management and policy formulation.

550212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
550212.value: Although a number of studies have been conducted on the relationship between environmental management and firm performance, most of them are conducted in the Western context. Due to the unique social and economic environments in China, the performance implications of environmental management might be quite different in the Chinese context. We examine the impact of corporate environmental initiatives (CEIs) on the market value of firms in China. We find that, in contrast to the findings in the Western context, Chinese stakeholders of firms react negatively to CEI announcements. The negative reaction is more significant when the announcements are related to processes rather than products, and for state-owned enterprises rather than privately-owned corporations. However, there is no difference whether the CEI is self-declared or third-party endorsed. Overall, our research indicates that Chinese stakeholders consider CEIs to be in conflict with shareholder interest. In particular, CEIs in state-owned enterprises might be considered as signals that firms need to sacrifice profits to shoulder more social responsibility.

550612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
550612.value: Hong Kong is experiencing changes in its weather patterns, with mean weather conditions like temperature, humidity, visibility (due to fog), rainfall, storms, and tropical cyclones being recorded at unusual levels. The changes seen in mean weather conditions in different seasons could affect the number of seasonal visitor arrivals, which in turn could affect employment, planning, and investment in the tourism industry. Seasonal variation in tourism flows can be measured by the fluctuations in visitor numbers from season to season. Weather is the mix of daily atmospheric events including temperature, rainfall, and humidity, whereas climate refers to the average weather pattern in a certain place over many years. Seasonal movement/seasonal tourism demand variation is mainly caused by variation in mean weather conditions (referred to as climate variation) in different seasons. Seasonality in weather patterns can thus be referred to as climatic seasonality. Although prior studies have recognized that climate variables are the major determinants of seasonal variation in tourism demand, no attempt has been made to date to measure the impact of climate variables such as temperature, rainfall, thunderstorms, tropical cyclones, heavy rain days, reduced visibility (due to fog), and humidity on the seasonal demand for tourism. Although a few recent studies have attempted to measure the effects of climate on tourism flows, one drawback common to these previous studies is that while they focused on the impact of climate change on total tourism flows or expenditure, they ignored its effects on seasonal variations in tourist flows. In the tourism literature, other than including economic related variables such as imcome, cost of living, exchange rate, etc, the inclusion of seasonal variation in a climate impact study has several advantages. First, it enables us to identify which climatic variables play a dominant role in shaping the characteristics of tourism demand variation over different seasons. Second, it enables us to identify the differences between the climate impact and the impacts of standard economic variables on seasonal tourism demand. Finally, it enables us to construct a composite climate index for each source market to predict future changes in seasonal variation in Hong Kong’s inbound tourism demand due to climate change. Armed with accurate and essential information on changes in seasonal demand to be derived from the proposed study, policy makers from both the public and private sectors will be in a position to make more informed decisions on tourism planning, marketing, and investment. 香港的天氣正在變化，記錄到的溫度、濕度、（霧造成的）能見度、降雨、風暴、熱帶氣旋這些平均天氣狀況都處于非正常值。不同季節平均天氣狀況的變化可能會影響到遊客的季節度假人次，接著又會影響到旅遊業的就業、策劃及投資。遊客流季節性變動的測量可以用于統計每年季節性遊客人數波動。天氣是每日大氣狀況的綜合，包括溫度、降雨及濕度；與此同時，氣候是指某地多年裡平均天氣模式。季節性運動與季節性旅遊需求變化，主要由於不同季節裡平均天氣狀況（指氣候變化）的變化而引起。因此，天氣模式的季節性可以指氣候季節性。 儘管以前的研究已經認識到氣候變量是旅遊需求季節變化的決定因素，但目前尚無嘗試衡量如溫度、降雨、風暴、熱帶氣旋、大雨的日子、（由霧造成的）能見度降低以及濕度 這些氣候變量對旅遊季節性需求的影響。雖然近來一些研究努力衡量氣候對遊客流的影響效果，但是以前的研究普遍有一個缺點，即它們注重氣候變化對總遊客流或花費的影響，而忽視了其對遊客流季節性變動的影響。 在旅遊文獻中，氣候影響研究不僅應包括如收入、生活成本、匯率等與經濟相關的變量，而且還應包括季節變化，這樣做有幾個好處。首先，它可以發現哪些氣候變化在不同季節旅遊需求變化特點的形成方面起到主導作用。其次，它使我們可以了解氣候影響與標準經濟變量對季節性旅遊需求影響之間的差異。最後，它使我們可以為每個客源市場構建一項綜合氣候指數，從而預測香港入境旅遊需求由於氣候變化造成的季節性變動之未來變化。公共部門與民營部門的決策者掌握了本研究所建議的有關季節性需求的精確信息，就能夠更加充分地做出決策，搞好旅遊策劃、營銷及投資。

550612.label: Realisation of objectives
550612.value: Three of four objectives were accomplished with one major research paper published in a leading journal (A+). The name of the journal is called Journal of Travel Research. For objective 1, through evaluation of existing studies and good understanding of the linkage between tourism demand and climate variables, the following were identified to estimate the role of climate variables in shaping the seasonal tourism demand variation. They are relative temperature (°C) in comparison with that in the tourist origin country, rainfall (mm), humidity (%), number of tropical cyclones, number of thunderstorms, and substitute destination (Singapore) temperature (°C) on seasonal variation in Hong Kong inbound tourism demand using a tourism demand modeling approach. The above analysis indicates that there is a link between seasonal variations in Hong Kong inbound tourism demand and climate variables, but identifying the specific Hong Kong climate variable that has the greatest effect on seasonal variation in each quarter may be useful to develop policy and marketing strategies for the Hong Kong tourism industry. For this purpose, the data of key climate variables in Hong Kong such as temperature (°C), humidity (%), rainfall (mm), number of thunderstorms, and number of tropical cyclones were obtained from the Hong Kong Observatory and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region from 1997 to 2012. This study first considered the AED statistics to examine the link between climate variables in Hong Kong and seasonal variation in Hong Kong inbound tourism demand. For objective 2, to identify the determinants of seasonal variation, this study estimated the tourism demand model by considering climate variables, economic factors, and institutional factors, such as Chinese New Year, Easter, Christmas, and special events. All climate related data were collected from Hong Kong Observatory and all tourism data were collected from Hong Kong Tourism Board from 1997 to 2012. For objective 3, to construct CCI for the selected Hong Kong major markets, the following climate variables were considered: temperature, temperature in the origin country of the tourist, temperature in the substitute destination (i.e., Singapore), humidity, rainfall, and number of thunderstorms. This study recommends that climate variables in both the tourist origin country and the tourist destination must be considered. CCI that leads to seasonal variation may be useful in identifying directional changes in the seasonal variation by visual examination. For objective 4, it was originally planned to develop a website to disseminate the information to the industry practitioners. It was later found out that SHTM has published regular electronic Newsletter at SHTM School official website. It is planned that the results of the study will be published through the Newsletter which is public accessible to all stakeholders interested in the study results.

550612.label: Major findings and research outcome
550612.value: In this study, we quantify the link between climate variables, such as temperature, rainfall, humidity, number of tropical cyclones, and number of thunderstorms, and seasonal variation in the Hong Kong inbound tourism demand using the average Euclidean distance (AED) statistics and tourism demand modeling approach. Seasonal variation is measured as the fluctuation in the number of tourists from one season to another. Based on the smallest AED value, results of this study showed that climate variables play a dominant role in shaping seasonal variation relative to season and country. The fluctuation of tourist numbers from one season to another is determined not only by climate variables (e.g., the temperature of Hong Kong vs. the temperature in the country of origin of the tourist) but also by economic factors, including price and income. The variation in the impact of relative temperature depends on the country of origin.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
550612.value: This study examined the link between climate variables in Hong Kong and seasonal variation in the inbound tourism demand in Hong Kong. The AED statistics measured the deviation between the standardized climate variables in Hong Kong and the standardized seasonal variation in the inbound tourism demand in Hong Kong. The study found that the climate variables with the strongest associations with seasonal variation in different seasons were identified. The climate variable that plays a dominant role in shaping seasonal variation patterns in different seasons is relative to the season and country. Information about daily weather conditions and climate-related activities, such as activities in different seasons, are important to tourists and the tourism industry to plan seasonal travel and efficiently allocate resources in different seasons.

551412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
551412.value: The last two decades have witnessed a rapid structural transformation of the Hong Kong economy from manufacturing to services. Today, service industries contribute approximately 92.6% of the annual GDP in Hong Kong. However, there is no growth without some pain. An emerging problem in the service sector is that service capacity sometimes cannot keep up with the speed of service expansion. As a consequence, consumers may have to wait much longer for their services/products than they did before. Waiting has long been regarded as an important topic in both psychology and marketing. What is the effect of waiting on consumption and spending? Common sense suggests that there should be a negative relationship, if anything, between the two – the longer the wait, the less you spend. In this research, we instead propose that there may actually be a positive relationship between waiting and consumption – waiting can sometimes lead to an increase in quantities consumed. Many human actions are accompanied by costs. These costs are commonly financial or time-related. However, more generally, we believe they can arise from a variety of sources, all of which may contribute to a common “psychological cost”. We propose that waiting is one such type of psychological cost. Psychological costs, once generated, may be compensated for by gains from resources of either the same type or those that are different. Hence, if waiting is indeed a source of psychological cost, a long wait should lead a consumer to compensate for this cost with an increase in the subsequent consumption (if the product or service being waited for is a desired one). We plan to investigate when and how the experience of waiting can spur consumption. The questions we will ask include the following: When does the experience of waiting lead to more consumption, and why? Will the type of product/service that consumers are waiting for change the relationship between waiting and consumption? When and how is windfall compensation after waiting beneficial for firms? And what is the relationship between different characteristics of the waiting experience (e.g., length, surrounding environment, comfort, queuing, etc.)? The current research will provide important contributions to the literature on waiting and consumer behavior, and retailing promotion. Research findings will also have strong implications for marketers and companies. The results should provide knowledge that will help companies strategically manage their customers’ waiting experience. 過去的兩個世紀見證了香港經濟從製造業轉向服務業的結構調整。 今日，服務行業已經佔到了本港國民生產總值的92.6％。然而成長總是伴隨着陣痛。服務業的產能經常不能滿足服務業發展的速度。 所帶來的結果就是，相比從前，現在的消費者不得不為花費更多的時間等待服務或者產品。 “等待”是心理學和市場學中的一個重要研究課題。等待是如何影響消費和開支的？傳統理論一般認為等待和消費之間應該是一種負相關的關係－等待的時間越長，後繼消費和開支越少。基於心理成本理論，在本課題研究中，我們提出等待和消費之間有可能是一種正相關的關係 － 等待的時間越長，後繼消費和開支越多。 許多人類行為都伴隨着某些“成本”。常見的成本大多反映在時間上或是金錢上。然而成本其實可能來自更多不同的來源，綜合起來我們稱之“心理成本”。我們提出心理成本一旦產生，人們會使用來自不同渠道的心理收益來補償自身的這些成本。所以，如果等待實際上是一種心理成本，越長時間的等待，產生的心理成本越多，消費者就需要用更多的心理收益來作出補償。 消費本身可以帶給消費者心理收益（假設消費者消費的服務和產品是其所喜歡的）， 所以等待的時間越長，後繼消費越多。 我們計劃深入研究等待的體驗是何時和怎樣提高消費的。我們將找出下列問題的答案： 究竟何時等待會引起更多的消費？消費者等待和消費的關係是否會因不同的產品和服務類型而有所不同？對等待后的消費者提供金錢補償是否對商家有益？以及除了等待時間以外，等待的其他元素（比如環境，舒適程度，隊列等）是否對消費有類似的影響？ 本研究課題將對等待，消費者行為，以及零售促銷等市場學領域作出重大的理論貢獻。同時本研究課題的研究成果還對商家和業者有很高的實踐意義。我們期待我們的研究成果能夠幫助商家更加戰略性的管理消費者的等待體驗。

551412.label: Major findings and research outcome
551412.value: Five major findings are yielded from this project with a general focus of the role of psychological factors in consumer judgment and decision making. One paper, published in 2014 on JCR, showed that incidentally heightened states of power increases consumer switching behavior. Placing consumers in a high state of power leads to a greater propensity to engage in product/brand switching in a variety of contexts. The effect of this power-activated action orientation was also decoupled from a desire for variety, reversed when greater action was associated with not switching and sated by performing physical action. A second paper, also published in 2014 on JCR, found that when individuals are disposed to construct an image-based narrative representation of the events that surround the use of a target product or service, differences in the visual perspective from which pictures of the target are taken make it difficult to construct this representation and, consequently, have a negative impact on evaluations of the product being described. In contrast, when individuals are simply motivated to acquire information about the target, pictures from different perspectives, which provide more information, increase their evaluations of it. A third paper, published in 2014 on JESP, found that the value of the fluency experience is contingent on how easy or difficult people expect the incoming information would be processed. Specifically, participants had higher evaluations of the target when their experienced processing fluency conformed (vs. did not conform) to their expected processing fluency. The fourth paper, also published in 2014 on JESP, showed that subtle reminders of money lead people to have more negative attitudes toward expressing emotions in public and to avoid expressing emotion in their written communications. In addition, money primed participants judge others' emotions to be more extreme and are disposed to avoid interacting with persons who display these emotions, especially when participants believe that these emotions are expressed in public. The last paper, which is currently under review, find that the longer consumers have to wait, the more they compensate themselves using increased consumption and expenditure. This effect occurs when consumers’ wait times exceed their tolerance thresholds, and is observed for long waits as well as other situational factors that make waiting unpleasant. Further, the effect is observed only for products which deliver positive instantaneous value.

551412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
551412.value: As may be evident from the above section, this project is productive and there is great potential for further development of this research. My first priority is to push the working paper through the review process and hopefully publish it in the following year. I also plan to further extend findings of some of these published papers and develop new research projects accordingly.

551412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
551412.value: The last two decades have witnessed a rapid structural transformation of the Hong Kong economy from manufacturing to services. An emerging problem in the service sector is that service capacity sometimes cannot keep up with the speed of service expansion. As a consequence, consumers may have to wait much longer for their services/products than they did before. This research investigates the effect of waiting for service on subsequent consumer behavior. Across six studies using lab experiments, field observations, and secondary data, we find that the longer consumers have to wait, the more they compensate themselves using increased consumption and expenditure. This effect occurs when consumers’ wait times exceed their tolerance thresholds, and is observed for long waits as well as other situational factors that make waiting unpleasant. Further, the effect is observed only for products which deliver positive instantaneous value. Based on these insights, we develop a dynamic structural model of the effect of waiting on consumption, and estimate it on secondary data of service consumption. Results from the model estimation highlight the trade-off between lost revenues from queue abandonment and increased sales from wait-dependent compensatory consumption, and suggest that managerially, optimal wait times may possibly be greater than zero.

560012.label: Project Objectives
560012.value: We investigate the neural processes associated with orienting attention for pain attenuation. It is hypothesized that a shift in attention followed by the rehearsal of sub-nociceptive images would elicit P2 and N400 among responder patients only, who are comparable to pain-free subjects. The ERPs would correlate with response inhibition ability, tendency towards pain catastrophizing, and amount of pain attenuation. We test how the processes of orienting attention could be influenced by tonic pain in the low back. It is hypothesized that the central N400 would be elicited in responder patients whether the nociceptive stimuli are felt at the painful or nonpainful sites (that is, between-task comparisons). However, there would be differences in the latency and amplitude of P2 and the amount of pain attenuation at different site locations (right leg versus lower back) and interference of the tonic pain in the painful site stimulation task.

560012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
560012.value: 這研究項目是探索通過定向注意力減低慢性腰背痛患者的疼痛的的神經電生理的機制。實驗任務需要被試把注意力從在腰部疼痛部位感應的一個外部誘發的疼痛性刺激轉移及定位到一個自我產生無痛的圖像上。控制任務涉及的外部誘發的疼痛性刺激感應是放在左腿的一個無痛位置。事件相關電位（ERP）範式收習與任務關聯的EEG信號。其他行為測試包含尊注力，反應抑制功能，及疼痛災難化戰略（衹用在患者）。研究結果使研究人員能夠探索定向注意提高疼痛衰減的效果的機制。研究結果將豐富慢性腰背痛患者身心干預措施的理論基礎。

560012.label: Realisation of objectives
560012.value: Objective 1 - Investigate the neural processes associated with orienting attention for pain attenuation. A total of 22 healthy participants were recruited for this part of the study. The participants were to perceive one of six levels of nociceptive external stimuli, categorized as External Low (EL) or External High (EH) salience induced by electrical stimulations (50 ms). After perceiving the external stimulus, participants were to mentally rehearse one of the two learned sub-nociceptive internal images: Internal Low (IL) and Internal High (IH) salience. Participants’ behavioral responses were recorded and EEG signals were captured. The event-related potentials were the fronto-central negativity (FCN; 128–180 ms) reflecting disengagement of attention from the external stimulus, and the fronto-central P2 (200–260 ms) and central P3 (320–380 ms) suggesting shifting attention to and reengaging with the internal sub-nociceptive somatosensory image. Significant differences in the FCN and P2 amplitudes during the orienting to IH and IL salience images only for the EH but not EL stimulus condition are new findings. The results indicated that modulations of the disengagement and shifting processes from the nociceptive external stimulus to the internal sub-nociceptive image only happened if the external stimulus was of high salience and the external-to-internal incongruence was large. The reengaging process was significantly correlated with attenuation of the pain intensity perceived from the external nociceptive stimulus. These findings suggested the external-to-internal orienting attention involved cognitive control. A top-down-dominated reengaging process may account for the attenuation effects on perceived pain intensity after orienting attention. Objective 2 - Test how the processes of orienting attention could be influenced by tonic pain in the low back. This part of the study was aimed to examine how the hyper-vigilance to pain phenomenon would modulate the orienting attention processes among patients with chronic low back pain. The three ERP components obtained from Objective 1 formed the ERP markers for the orienting attention processes. They were FCN (SP3, SP3/P2), P2 and P3. The results of the control task of healthy group were used to compared with those obtained from the patient group. A total of 22 patients participated in this study. The experimental paradigm for the patient participants was to perceive 50-ms external nociceptive stimulations at the ankle (no-pain; for patient and healthy controls) or lower back (painful; only for patients) sites, which was followed by mentally rehearsing well-trained sub-nociceptive somatosensory images. The ratings of the pain intensity perceived from the nociceptive stimulation and the electrocephalogram (EEG) signals of the participants were captured. When compared with healthy controls, patient participants showed significant differences in the latencies and amplitudes of SP3, P2 and P3 elicited over the frontal or centro-parietal regions for the non-pain site particularly when the external stimuli were of high salience. Among the patient participants, differences in the amplitudes of P2 and P3 were observed between the no-pain and painful conditions. At the painful site, high/low salience of external stimulations was found to modulate amplitude of fronto-centrally distributed P3 when patient participants rehearsed high but not low salience images. This contrasts with the non-pain site where the modulation effect of P3 was significant when low salience sub-nociceptive images were rehearsed. The amplitudes of frontocentrally distributed P2 and P3 were significantly correlated with the pain intensity ratings only in the painful condition and when high salience nociceptive stimuli were perceived. The results suggested that the pain-related external-to-internal orienting attention processes were modulated among the patient participants. Among these processes, the reengagement process (P3) to non-nociceptive images at the lumbar painful region appeared to be mostly affected by their chronic pain experience. The findings offer a plausible explanation on the notion that patients with chronic pain are preoccupied by the pain as they fail to reengage to less painful experience such as distraction and mental imagery. Future study should explore factors which modulate reengagement attentional processes among patients with chronic pain.

560012.label: Major findings and research outcome
560012.value: There are three outcomes achieved from the study. First, our results revealed that with adequate training, numeric rating scale would be a reliable method to measure the pain intensity level associated with sub-painful and painful sensation due to electrical stimulation (Chan et al., under review, see Abstract 1). It is noteworthy that the repeatability was found to be highest when stimuli were the most sub-nociceptive or nociceptive. The findings provide evidence on the reliability of using NRS to reflect the pain intensity of the external electrical stimuli to induce sub-nociceptive or sub-nociceptive sensation among the participants in this study. Second, the results obtained from the healthy participants indicated that the event-related potential (ERP) components associated with the external-to-internal orienting attention should be FCN (disengagement process), P2 (shifting process) and P3 (reengagement process) (see Peng et al., under review, Abstract 2). These ERPs were fronto-centrally or centro-parietally distributed. The FCN can be further divided into SP3 and SP3/P2. Our findings are different from the original hypothesis which could be due to the change in the experimental design. After the pilot study, it was decided to use a simple experimental design (not asking participant to rate the rehearsed somatosensory images). The P3 was likely to better reflect the reengagement process to the generated somatosensory image than the originally proposed N400. Third, the results obtained from patients with chronic low back pain suggested that their external-to-internal orienting attention processes were modulated when compared with their healthy counterparts. This included centro-parietally distributed SP3, P2 and P3 elicited when nociceptive stimuli were delivered to the non-painful site (i.e. ankle) (see Peng et al., under review, Abstract 3). When stimuli were delivered at the painful site (i.e. the low back), most of the significant results were found in the amplitudes of P3 particularly when the external stimuli were of higher level of salience (i.e. stronger nociceptive sensation). The amplitudes of P3 were significantly correlated with the pain intensity level felt from the stimuli. Our findings indicated that among the orienting attention, the reengagement process was mostly modulated among patients with low back pain. As a result, the patient may experience obstacle engaging in the less-painful internal feeling. This offers a plausible explanation on the hyper-vigilant painful phenomenon among chronic pain patients who tend to report endured painful sensation without known organic causes.

560012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
560012.value: The results obtained from this study are intriguing but counter-intuitive. The notion that patients with chronic pain have impaired orienting attention function has been reported in previous studies. Common understanding is that patients would have difficulty disengaging from the painful sensation. This results in sustained painful experience due to the painful sensation. New findings generated from this study are that among orienting attention, the reengagement process is mostly modulated. In this study, the reengagement process involved patients with chronic pain to shift from an external perception of nociceptive stimuli to an internally generated nociceptive image. It is therefore plausible that the sustained feeling of pain experienced by patient could be due to their failure to engage in the non-painful internal feeling after the original organic damage has been healed. Future study should test this hypothesis by replicating the study among chronic pain patients who are with or without real organic damages such as in the lower back. It is also worthwhile to design interventions to strengthen the external-to-internal shifting and reengagement processes. Study should test the efficacy of such training on pain attenuation among patients with chronic pain.

560012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
560012.value: This study was aimed to investigate how external-to-internal orienting attention processes were affected among patients with chronic low back pain. The experimental task required the participants to perceive short-lifting external painful stimuli of different magnitudes and then imagine pre-trained sub-painful feelings. Electrical activities were captured throughout the perception and imagining part of the task. The results indicated that the external-to-internal orienting attention was consisted of a disengagement, a shifting and followed by a reengagement process. When compared with healthy participants, patients with chronic low back pain showed differences in all the three processes. Among the patient participants, the reengagement process was the mostly affected particularly when the external stimuli were of higher pain intensity level. This is new finding as previous studies suggested that patients with chronic pain had difficulty disengaging from the painful sensation. In this study, we argue that the inability of reengaging with non-painful internal feeling could attribute more to the chronic pain experience of these patients than the inability of disengaging from the painful stimuli. Future study should further test this hypothesis on patients with chronic pain who are with or without organic causes.
