560612.label: Major findings and research outcome
560612.value: We have synthesized a library of flavonoid heterodimers using click chemistry and used it to screen for dual selective (P-gp and BCRP) modulators. We have identified a potent flavonoid heterodimer (12_9) that can increase the brain penetration of sorafenib, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, by inhibiting P-gp and BCRP at sub-nanomolar concentration in the blood-brain-barrier. Such increase in brain penetration of sorafenib results in reduction of orthologously-implanted glioblastoma. We have filed a patent and presented in an international conference. A journal publication is in preparation.

560612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
560612.value: The patent covering the novel flavonoid heterodimers have been filed and successfully licensed to Athenex Inc. in Feb 2015 for further development.

560612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
560612.value: Glioblastoma (stage IV brain cancer) is difficult to treat because cancer drugs cannot penetrate into the brain. There are transporters present in the blood-brain-barrier that can pump drugs out of the brain. We have discovered a new class of flavonoid derivatives that can increase the penetration of certain cancer drugs by inhibiting the pumps in the blood-brain-barrier. We demonstrated that these flavonoid derivatives are effective in reducing the volume of brain cancer in mouse model. We also demonstrated that the flavonoid derivative and the cancer drug (sorfaenib) are safe in preliminary mouse toxicity study. This discovery has been patented and licensed to a pharamceutical company for further development. It represents a new approach of treating glioblastoma which is otherwise difficult to treat.

560712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
560712.value: Glaucoma is one of two leading causes of irreversible blindness in the world. It is frequently associated with elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) which is considered as the only treatable risk factor. Until now, glaucoma remains incurable although its progression can be retarded by pharmacological reduction of IOP. Lowering IOP is thus far the only proven intervention to effectively delay the onset and slow progression of vision loss. There are multiple approaches and drugs for lowering IOP; however, most of the current medications have considerable side effects and many glaucoma patients develop drug resistance after using these drugs for prolonged period, suggesting the need for novel alternative approaches. Baicalein is a flavonoid derived from the root of Scutellaria baicalensis. It is frequently found in plants and has been widely used in traditional Chinese medicine. Recently, baicalein has been demonstrated to protect retinal ganglion cells from oxidative damage, indicating its potential functional significance in glaucoma therapy as a neuroprotectant. The major focus of this proposal is to examine how baicalein affects aqueous humor secretion and outflow facility, and their relationship to IOP. These questions will be addressed by using an integrated approach to study the effects of baicalein on aqueous humor inflow and outflow using excised ciliary epithelium, arterially-perfused eyes and whole-eye perfusion systems. Because of its pharmacologic relevance to glaucoma, the effect of baicalein on the IOP in living mice will also be tested. The results of these studies can provide insight into the physiological mechanism for regulating aqueous humor dynamics and thereby IOP. More importantly, the outcome of these studies may have a direct translational biomedical significance for the future development of novel anti-glaucoma agents. 青光眼是全世界俩大不可逆性致盲眼病之一，通常与高眼压相关。高眼压被认为是唯一可以被治疗的危险因素。至今，虽然青光眼的病理进展能通过药物降低眼内压而延缓，但青光眼仍是不可治愈的疾病。降低眼内压是迄今为止唯一被证实有效的干预方法，它能有效的延迟发病和减缓视力丧失的进程。目前，有许多途径和药物可以减低眼压，然而绝大多数目前的药物治疗都有相当大的副作用，并且许多青光眼病人在长期使用这些药物之后产生了耐药性。因此，需要寻找新的替代方法。 黄芩素是一种来自黄芩的根的黄酮类化合物，通常能在植物中找到，并且被中医广泛应用。最近，黄芩素被证实能防止视网膜神经节细胞氧化性损伤，这表明黄芩素作为一种神经保护剂在青光眼治疗中有巨大的潜在功能意义。这份研究提案的焦点是研究黄芩素是如何影响眼房水分泌和外流，以及这些和眼内压的关系。这些问题将通过利用离体的睫状体上皮、动脉灌注眼和全眼灌注系统，运用综合性的方法去研究黄芩素对于眼房水流入和流出的影响。由于青光眼的药理学相关性，我们将检测黄芩素对于活鼠眼内压的作用。这些研究的结果将会给我们提供对房水动力学调节和对眼内压作用的生理学机制的深入理解。更重要的是，这些研究的结果可能对发展新的抗青光眼药物有一个重大的生物医学意义。

560712.label: Realisation of objectives
560712.value: Objective 1: To determine the effects of baicalein on aqueous humor secretion rate and intraocular pressure (IOP) using arterially-perfused in vitro porcine eyes. Experiments involving the arterially-perfused in vitro porcine eyes have been completed. We have modified and improved the method of preparing baicalein solution (by increasing its solubility) before injecting it into the eye. With the new method of drug preparation, we are able to show that baicalein, when added to the anterior chamber, significantly decreases the rate of aqueous humor secretion by ~20-25%. This finding is consistent with the results obtained from the trans-epithelial electrical measurements, supporting the inhibitory action of baicalein on aqueous humor production. Objective 2: To determine the effects of baicalein on outflow facility using the acute whole-eye perfusion system. Completed. In collaboration with Prof. Stamer at Duke University, we have examined the effects of baicalein on outflow facility using freshly enucleated mouse eyes. Outflow facility was determined by linear regression analysis of measured flow rates at sequential pressure steps (from 4 to 20 mmHg) using the whole-eye perfusion system. Our results demonstrate that the intracameral administration of baicalein produces a concentration-dependent increase in outflow facility. At 10 µM, baicalein significantly enhances the conventional outflow facility by ~90% in paired preparations. Objective 3: To determine the changes in IOP by baicalein in living mice. Experiments completed. The effect of baicalein on IOP in rodents has been examined. Baicalein is found to lower IOP in different animal species including gerbils, Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats and C57BL/6J (B6) mice. For example, intraperitoneal injection of baicalein significantly lowers baseline IOP in gerbils and SD rats in vivo. At 40 mg/kg, the ocular hypotensive effect is found to be ~20% over the baseline value. In addition, we have investigated whether similar IOP-lowering effects can be observed after topical application rather than intraperitoneal injection of baicalein. Our results show that the topical application of baicalein acts across species and triggers a transient IOP reduction in both SD rats and B6 mice. A greater IOP reduction is observed under dark phase than light phase in both species. In addition, the ocular hypotensive effect elicited by topical administration is smaller than that of intraperitoneal injection. Objective 4: To investigate the physiological mechanism of baicalein-induced responses using excised ciliary epithelium. Completed. Stromal administration of baicalein produces very little effect on trans-epithelial electrical parameters. When added to the aqueous side, however, baicalein is demonstrated to inhibit short-circuit current and fluid transport across freshly excised porcine ciliary epithelium. At 100 µM, it decreases the short-circuit current by 70-80%. The inhibitory effect of baicalein can be prevented by low Cl bath or Cl channel blockers, suggesting that its response is primarily mediated by the inhibition of net Cl secretion across the preparation. Using whole-cell patch clamp techniques, we have demonstrated that baicalein significantly inhibits the outwardly rectifying, swelling-activated Cl currents in non-pigmented ciliary epithelial cells, potentially reducing Cl efflux into the posterior chamber. Furthermore, baicalein-induced response is found to be unaffected by lipoxygenase inhibitor, suggesting that the lipoxygenase pathway is not involved in the regulation.

560712.label: Major findings and research outcome
560712.value: Our results demonstrate that baicalein inhibits the trans-epithelial Cl and fluid flow simultaneously across porcine ciliary epithelium, thereby potentially reducing the rate of aqueous humor secretion. This is supported by the evidence that baicalein inhibits the rate of aqueous humor secretion using the arterially-perfused porcine eyes (ISO 2013). The inhibitory effect of baicalein on trans-epithelial Cl secretion is possibly mediated by the inhibition of swelling-activated Cl channels in non-pigmented ciliary epithelial cells that is believed to be the rate limiting step in aqueous humor production (Tianjin Ophthalmology Forum 2016). Baicalein is also found to significantly enhance the conventional outflow facility, in addition to its inhibitory effect on aqueous humor formation. These results strongly suggest that the ocular hypotensive effect of baicalein is possibly mediated by the suppression of aqueous humor production as well as the facilitation of aqueous humor drainage (ARVO 2015). This finding opens up new possibilities with regard to the potential cellular sites for modulating aqueous humor dynamics and intraocular pressure. Consistent with the in vitro findings, baicalein is demonstrated to lower IOP in rodents. Both intraperitoneal and topical administration of baicalein effectively reduce IOP in normotensive animals in vivo (ARVO 2013 & 2014; AOPT 2015). Furthermore, baicalein is shown to act across species, displaying similar trends of ocular hypotensive effects among different species (ARVO 2015). To the best of our knowledge, there is no clinically-available anti-glaucoma agent that has dual beneficial actions on aqueous humor dynamics (i.e. suppression of aqueous inflow and facilitation of aqueous outflow). In this regard, baicalein may be a potential pharmacological agent for lowering IOP (a patent application is being prepared; JOPT 2014; manuscripts in preparation). In terms of postgraduate student training, one PhD student, Ms. Hoi-lam Li, was recruited in Aug 2013 working on this project. She has spent about several months working in co-I’s lab (Prof. Stamer, Dept of Ophthalmology, Duke University, USA) to acquire the techniques and examine the effect of baicalein on outflow facility in mice.

560712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
560712.value: We have optimized and improved the method for dissolving baicalein so that a much lower concentration of drug can be used to achieve comparable responses. Further work is required to improve and enhance the permeability of baicalein across the cornea. The precise mechanism by which baicalein enhances outflow facility is yet to be elucidated. We speculate that baicalein may regulate the contractility of trabecular meshwork (TM) cells and/or the expression of cytoskeletal proteins and extracellular matrix in trabecular meshwork. To address these questions, we plan to conduct a comprehensive analysis of protein expression in human trabecular meshwork cells using a cutting-edge proteomics approach. It is also in our plan to conduct a randomized clinical trial to examine the effectiveness of this naturally affordable, non-toxic baicalein in lowering IOP for people with ocular hypertension.

560712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
560712.value: Glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness, affecting millions of people of different ethnic groups globally. Normally, the major function of aqueous humor is to nourish the cornea and lens; however, in glaucoma, eye pressure build-up, leading to irreversible damage of our eyesight. Eye drop medications have been used to relieve fluid pressure build-up (by either suppressing its production or increasing its drainage). Since unwanted side effects exist in these medications, our current research efforts aim at exploring more natural eye drop ingredients. Baicalein is a common herbal supplement frequently found in plant life and foods. We found that baicalein exerts a significant eye pressure lowering effect when applied in animal models. The pressure lowering effects of baicalein are associated with 1) an inhibition of aqueous production and 2) a facilitation of aqueous drainage. These dual actions of baicalein will open up new possibilities for controlling aqueous humor dynamics and eye pressure.

560812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
560812.value: Stroke is a chronic and disabling disease which is common among the adult population. Recent studies have found that brain recovery is still taking place long after the original stroke event, if the patient is undertaking active rehabilitation. One of the biggest problems with motor recovery after stroke is the learned ‘non-use’ which a portion of motor impairment of the patient is not resulted from the brain cell damage but of the learned suppression of the movement which will lead to a further depression of motor or perceptual function, and that makes an individual unable to move or develop the paretic upper limb further. Although ‘Constraint-Induced Movement Therapy (CIMT)’ is common and of great efficacious to chronic stroke survivors with mild impairments of upper extremity (UE), by restraining the less affected hand in either a mitt or sling together with intensive training of the paretic limb for 90% of the waking hours in consecutive weeks, it may also be difficult to carry out owing to safety concern. In our previous studies, we proved that sensory cueing would promote post-stroke patients’ awareness of the affected UE after repetitive reminding which will initiate better hand movements and functions. In this study, we intend to substantiate this innovative treatment using a top-down approach - the effects of using sensory cueing to the paretic UE (delivered by an external ambulatory wristwatch device) on enhancing motor control and functional use of paretic upper extremity for patients with chronic stroke in the community. Therefore, the objective of this study is to conduct a randomized controlled trial comparing the effects of sensory cueing via an external device and limb activation training on UE functions in clients with chronic stroke than those who receive placebo or only usual and customary care. The cueing signal is delivered in the form of rhythmic vibration and the schedule is integrated into the repetitive movements of the affected upper limb during self-administered training protocols. This will show whether or not these are associated with improved motor and functional performance after the motor system of the stroke client has been primed. If this new treatment method being evaluated is found to be effective in the randomized controlled trial, the results would represent a significant contribution to the field of stroke rehabilitation and neuroscience. 習慣性廢用是腦中風偏癱患者中常見的現象，患者會忽略或不注意偏癱一側的上肢。另外，很多長期中風患者由於患手活動不理想，會有放棄使或不使用患手的情況，令患手康復減緩。改良式侷限誘發動作治療是文獻已證實其中之一個針對中風病患之復康治療方法，此治療之目的是以手套限制健側手之動作數小時，再加上密集式動作訓練，從而誘發及改善患側上肢在日常生活中之使用。但此方法引發患者很多問題包括安全，當健側手戴上手套進行治療活動時，患者不能使用助行器及柺杖；患側上肢之手腕及手指關節必須是有輕微活動能力，否則難以參與日常生活活動；戴上手套後外出會為異相等等。感知提示訓練是透過戴在患者患手的手錶儀器發出感覺信號(例如震動或聲響)，並且以預先設定的時間發出信號提示給患者，提示後患者須要按照職業治療師的評估而設計的運動計劃做出適合的動作。此治療方法是香港首創，我們已在文獻發表的研究證實感知提示方法能有效提升患者的上肢功能表現，減低中風後偏身偏癱上肢習慣性廢用的情況。本研究的主要目的是探索感知提示訓練對亞急性中風病患者的影響，比較使用安慰儀器的安慰組，以及比較傳統的臨床訓練，能否誘發患側上肢在日常生活中之使用，從而令患者手部及整體功能得以改善。本研究會將香港兩間公共醫院的參與者隨機分為三組 - 干預組、安慰組、及對照組。我們會為兩組干預組進行四星期，每星期五天的治療，參與者戴此訓練器及使用感知提示十四天，每天三小時(固定時間)。在每天這段三小時期間，訓練器會記錄患肢手部活動，定時發出震動及響聲；每當患者意識到這些提示時，要按手錶儀器上的按鍵將提示關掉。每當關掉按鍵後，根據科研人員指示活動患手五次， 及日常生活中盡量使用患手參與活動；安慰組的儀器跟干預組的沒有分別，只是不會發出感知提示；對照組則只使用三星期傳統的臨床訓練, 跟平常的醫院訓練沒有分別。 此外，研究會為患者進行三次測驗，每次測驗包括五項測試：包括手部功能、手部日常生活能力問卷評估、及從儀器上記錄的手部活動量及反應能力。此項研究對腦部康復尤其在認知訓練和機能訓練之結合有莫大益處，研究結果在文獻發表後能提供此治療方法的成效，從而改善中風人士之上肢偏癱臨床治療方法。

560812.label: Realisation of objectives
560812.value: Objectives have been achieved Sensory cueing with limb activation training, original and developed in Hong Kong, which has been renamed by the PI as “Remind-to-Move” (RTM) treatment thereafter, had been proved in PI’s previous proof-of-concepts studies to be useful in adults with stroke or children with cerebral palsy for promoting upper extremity and unilateral neglect recovery. The objective of this present study has been completed. Regarding the use of the allocated budget, a non-local PhD student was admitted in Sept 2013 who is solely responsible to carry out this project under PI’s supervision. Five hundred pieces of sensory cueing devices were developed and fabricated under this project using the allocated budget. The effects of RTM using wearable cueing devices at home for promoting upper extremity recovery in stroke patients after subacute discharge were examined. In a multi-centered randomized controlled trial, 84 eligible participants who had suffered from stroke with less than 6 months in 4 general hospitals in Hong Kong and Guangzhou were randomly allocated to either an experimental, sham (placebo), or control group, stratified by arm functional levels. Patients in the experimental group were treated by RTM using wearable devices, 3 consecutive hours daily, for 4 weeks. The sham group used sham devices. The control group received the usual care (conventional training). A masked assessor evaluated the participants at 0, 4th, 8th and 12th weeks. Outcome measures included arm function tests, motor activity log, movement percentage recorded by wearable devices. All patients allocated to treatment were included in intention-to-treat analysis. The clinical trial was registered at: URL: http://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Trial Registration Number: NCT02952677. Results of the average movement percentage in the experimental group showed as significantly higher than the sham. Arm functions in the experimental group were significantly better than the sham and control groups. The present study demonstrates that RTM via wearable devices could boost the effects of usual care on upper extremity for stroke patients after subacute discharge, and was better at enhancing arm function than sham and control. We found that the RTM concept has potential to be further developed in tele-rehabilitation. The utility of a unilateral accelerometer for monitoring upper extremity performance in subacute stroke patients by comparing its use with other upper extremity functional assessments has also been evaluated. Twenty-four participants recruited were required to wear an accelerometer on the affected wrist for 3 hours a day for the first 4 weeks after discharge from hospital. Assessments for arm functions as well as how long the device was worn, movement amount and movement percentage, were extracted from the accelerometer throughout 12 weeks. Significant improvements in the participants were shown by the arm functions but no significant change could be found using Motor Activity Log or the accelerometer parameters across time. There were moderate to good correlations among the assessment measures but no significant correlation was obtained between any of the assessments and the accelerometer data. These results suggest that the unilateral accelerometer might not be useful to reflect actual arm functions in daily activities, rather, bilateral arm devices using synchronized technology should be developed. We also investigated the brain regions during sensory cueing in both healthy and stroke participants, and explore the neuropathways of arm movements connected to the application of sensory cueing. A case study using block design with Block 1 - baseline condition, Block 2 – placebo condition, and Block 3 - experimental condition respectively was completed. The participants were 2 stroke patients with hemiparetic upper extremity and their 2 healthy counterparts. They were required to wear sensory cueing devices on bilateral wrists throughout the study, and sensory cueing was delivered only in experimental condition. During placebo condition, the participants were told to perform self-regulated hand movements every minute, while the participants just needed to perform hand movements after each sensory cue emitted from the device in the experimental condition. The cortical hemodynamics was recorded by functional near infrared spectroscopic topography (fNIRS). The results showed that activated regions of healthy and stroke participants showed different patterns of neuro correlates. Prefrontal cortex was found to be activated in healthy participants while the same area was less activated comparatively in participants with stroke in placebo condition. Both prefrontal and primary motor cortices were less activated in healthy participants in experimental condition while these areas in stroke participants were more activated instead, which showed that the prefrontal cortex is actively involved in stroke participants during RTM training. This grant also partially supported another 2 studies to investigate the effects of RTM for promoting paretic upper extremity recovery in children with hemiplegic cerebral palsy studying in special schools, and in stroke inpatients suffering from unilateral neglect in hospital, with the use of 500 pieces of sensory cueing devices fabricated because of this grant. Regarding children with unilateral cerebral palsy, we demonstrated that RTM carried similar therapeutic effects with constraint-induced movement therapy (CIMT) in manual dexterity and functional hand use, and was superior to conventional rehabilitation in the special schools. RTM is recommended as an alternative or supplement to CIMT for arm training in children with hemiplegic cerebral palsy. The randomized clinical trial was registered at: URL: http://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Trial Registration Number: NCT02645344. Regarding the study for stroke with unilateral neglect, we found that the combination of inhibitory low frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) at P5 position can be combined with sensory cueing every 10 mins generated from the sensory wristwatch devices to improve unilateral neglect on the hemiparetic side and was better than either rTMS or conventional rehabilitation alone. The clinical trial was registered at: URL: http://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Trial Registration Number: NCT02645331. Under-achievements and attempts to overcome problems The PI encountered two major issues of time delay in this project. Although a PhD student was admitted in Sept 2013 to assist in carrying out the project, there was a half-year delay in the university admission because the appointee was a non-local candidate and the visa to work in Hong Kong was necessary before he started working. Second, the fabrication of 500 pieces of cueing devices was done by a company in Shenzhen, however, there was much time delay behind the schedule in the tendering process from the university as well as in manufacturing since Feb 2014. Therefore, a request for an extension of 6 months was submitted in Dec 2015. The PI encountered two major issues of difficulty in subject recruitment in the 2 hospitals – Tuen Mun Hospital and Kowloon Hospital, Hong Kong. First, there was a period of suspension in data collection from Dec 2013 to Feb 2014 due to yellow alert level after the outbreak of epidemic flu in Hong Kong. The data collection in the 2 hospitals was finally resumed in Mar 2014. Second, the number of subjects recruited in the 2 hospitals was far behind the target during the course of study, most patients did not fulfilled the inclusion criteria due to reasons of readmission to acute care for surgery or other medical reasons such as fracture or cardiac problems, recurrent stroke, receiving Botox injection, and moving away from Hong Kong to China. Two additional trial sites in Guangzhou, mainland China — Guangzhou First People’s Hospital located in Central Guangzhou, and Panyu Central Hospital located in South Guangzhou, where the PhD student worked, were added after midway of subject recruitment.

560812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
560812.value: This study addresses an emerging concept and affordable technology that a 4-week RTM home-based treatment could boost the effects of usual care on upper extremity in patients with stroke following subacute discharge. Future studies may focus on the cost-effectiveness of RTM as an innovative rehabilitation approach in tele-rehabilitation on the hemiplegic upper extremity after stroke, with the use of real-time wireless data communication between patients and the therapists, as well as using synchronized technology of bilateral arm devices for the purpose of calibration per individual. In Hong Kong, there was an average of 25,247 people yearly suffered from stroke in the period of 2008-12 and among them, there was an average survival rate about 86% (Hospital Authority statistical report 2012-2013 from https://www.ha.org.hk/upload/publication_15/491.pdf)but most of them might end up with various degrees of physical disabilities and require certain kinds of rehabilitation. Nowadays, the commercial wearable device is becoming popular. We suggest that RTM concept, be implanted in commercial wearable devices, such as smart watches, and connected to smartphones, in tele-rehabilitation, so that more patients may benefit from it. We found that the RTM concept has potential to be further developed in tele-rehabilitation which forms an important area for future GRF submission.

560812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
560812.value: In our previous proof-of-concepts studies, we have developed a new approach - the “Remind-to-Move” (RTM) delivered by means of vibration cueing via a wearable device to be used for people with hemiparetic upper extremities in adults with stroke or children with cerebral palsy for promoting their upper extremity as well as enhancing unilateral neglect recovery after stroke. This GRF grant supported the massive development of RTM, including the production of 500 pieces of sensory cueing devices, to investigate the effects of RTM for promoting upper extremity recovery in stroke patients after subacute discharge from the hospitals. We demonstrated that RTM via wearable devices could boost the effects of usual care on upper extremity for stroke patients after subacute discharge, and was better at enhancing arm function than sham and control. We suggested that RTM concept has potential to be further developed in tele-rehabilitation for stroke survivors at home in parallel with their institutional rehabilitation. The 500 cueing devices produced in this grant also partially supported another two projects – promoting upper extremity in children with unilateral cerebral palsy studying at special schools, and reducing unilateral neglect after stroke together with brain stimulation. Both applications have been demonstrated with great impact.

561212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
561212.value: The long-term goal of our research is to understand the interaction between the thalamus and the cerebral cortex. The thalamus is reciprocally connected with cerebral cortex. Both thalamocortical and corticothalamic projections send collaterals to the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) of the ventral thalamus. The TRN consists of only GABAergic inhibitory neurons that project back only to the medial geniculate body (MGB), not to the auditory cortex. Over the past decade, scientists have shown that neurons in different stages of the auditory ascending pathway exhibited stimulus-specific adaptation (SSA) [1-9]. It has been speculated that the SSA in auditory cortical neurons could be produced through interaction between the ascending pathway and reciprocal thalamocortical pathway[10]. Recently we found that the SSA of TRN neurons showed either facilitatory or inhibitory effect on MGB neurons [5,11]. However, SSA in the TRN was much greater than that in the MGB[5]. The SSA in the TRN was not affected much by the MGB neurons’ SSA[5]. The first question raised here is whether the SSA of cortical neurons has any correlation with that of their projection MGB neurons. The other questions are how much the SSA of cortical neurons is affected by that of MGB neurons and how much by TRN neurons. We would expect that the influence of the SSA of MGB neurons on that of cortical neurons is likely to be true, and is likely reflected on the early components of the responses, while the influence of the SSA of TRN neurons is reflected on the late components of the responses. In the present study, the questions will be addressed with both the extracellular and intracellular recordings from MGB and cortical neurons with oddball paradigm, while the TRN is manipulated with local drug application. Using intracellular recording, we would be able to measure the membrane potential change of cortical neurons at the subthreshold level to the acoustic stimulus and/or electrical stimulation of the MGB. The results of the proposed study would not only advance our understanding on the novelty detection function in the thalamocortical system, but also add an important piece of knowledge on potential functional implications of the highly integrative brain processes of attention.

561212.label: Realisation of objectives
561212.value: The long-term goal of our research is to understand the interaction between the thalamus and cerebral cortex, which is the foundation of many highly integrative brain functions. In the past decade, scientists from different laboratories have found that neurons in different stations of the auditory ascending pathway showed stimulus specific adaptation (SSA) with different inter-stimulus intervals (ISIs) . Neurons in the IC showed SSA at ISI of 125,250,500 ms, while neurons in the auditory cortex showed SSA at ISI of 375,1000,2000 ms . Recently we found that TRN neurons showed SSA with ISIs of seconds, while the MGB neurons showed SSA with much faster ISIs of < 800 ms. Comparing with SSA of TRN neurons, that of MGB neurons was much smaller. The SSA of TRN neurons either enhanced or suppressed MGB neuronal responses to the following auditory stimulus. We know that the thalamus and cortex are strongly interconnected. Activation of the cortex brings strong modulations of both excitatory and inhibitory effects on the thalamic neurons. The strong corticofugal inhibition is mediated by the TRN pathway. In the present study, we examined whether and how SSA observed in the auditory cortex was accumulated through the multiple stations along the ascending auditory pathway. We focused our attention on the thalamocortical network including the MGB, TRN and auditory cortex and examined the following specific questions: 1) Whether the SSA of cortical neurons has any correlation with that of their projection MGB neurons? 2) Whether the SSA of cortical neurons shows difference toward the acoustic stimuli in oddball paradigm and the electrical stimuli of MGB neurons in oddball paradigm? 3) Whether and how the SSA of cortical neurons is modulated by the TRN? 4) Whether and how the SSAs of cortical neurons in terms of early and late responses show differences before and after the TRN is inactivated, to acoustic stimuli and/or electrical stimulation. Objective 1: To investigate whether the SSAs of cortical and thalamic neurons have any correlation between each other using the same oddball paradigm. We found that the cortical and thalamic neurons have correlation in their SSA when the neurons have direct connections, showing responses to the electrical stimulation of each others. Objective 2: To investigate whether the SSAs of neurons in the auditory cortex show difference toward acoustic stimuli and electrical stimulation of the MGB with the same oddball paradigm. The second question was addressed with intracellular recordings in the auditory cortex using the same oddball paradigm for acoustic stimuli and for electrical stimulation of the MGB. With in-vivo intracellular recording from the cortex neuron, we found that the cortical neuron displayed a great adaptation to the repeated f1 stimuli but remained strong responses to the deviant stimulus f2, when the ISI was 500 ms. There was still some adaptation for repeated f1 stimuli when the ISI was 800 ms. The neuron showed almost no adaptation to repeated f1 stimuli when the ISI was lengthened to 2s. Objective 3: To examine whether and how the SSA of cortical neurons is modulated by the TRN. The SSAs of cortical neurons will be examined with acoustic stimuli in oddball paradigm before and after the TRN is inactivated. To address the question 3, We compared the neuronal responses to repeated acoustic stimuli before and after the TRN was inactivated. The TRN’s feedback inhibition to the thalamus normally affected the late components of the auditory responses of MGB neurons within a single trial. Electrical stimulation of the MGB provides an artificial and short activation of the neurons, while acoustic stimuli activate MGB neurons in a more complicated manner in terms of firing patterns. We divided them into two components: early (<=20 ms re stimulus onset) and late (>20 ms). The TRN's modulation on the cortical neurons was very complicated. That part needed further investigation in terms in a more global manner. Objective 4: To examine whether and how the SSAs of cortical neurons in terms of early and late responses show differences before and after the TRN is inactivated, to acoustic stimuli and/or electrical stimulation. We first mapped the MGB before implanting the stimulation electrodes. We then mapped the neuronal responses to the electrical stimulation as well as to acoustic stimuli of different frequencies before determining the neurons for investigation in the auditory cortex. The SSA of the early and late components of the responses in the auditory cortex to acoustic stimuli in oddball paradigm before and after the TRN inactivation were different. The early component had more good correlation, while the late component become very complicated. Some further cortical feedback to the TRN may play some role in the complicated situation. Further investigation using different approaches such as optogenetic techniques is recommended.

561212.label: Major findings and research outcome
561212.value: In the present study, we addressed the questions with both the extracellular and intracellular recordings from MGB and cortical neurons with oddball paradigm, while the TRN was manipulated with local drug application. We found that the influence of the SSA of MGB neurons on that of cortical neurons was accumulative and was reflected on the early components of the responses, while the influence of the SSA of TRN neurons was reflected on the late components of the responses. With intracellular recording, we measured the membrane potential change of cortical neurons at the subthreshold level to the acoustic stimulus and/or electrical stimulation of the MGB. In the cultured neuronal network, we examined the SSA at the synapse level with whole-cell patch-clamp recording from the cultured cortical neurons. Spatially separated electrical stimulations were adopted to activate different portions of the dendratic inputs. Cortical cultural neurons showed SSA to the electrical stimulations. Single cultured pyramidal neurons shared the similar SSA properties in response to the odd-ball stimulation paradigm as those reported with in vivo preparation. This SSA was not attributable to a reduction of the intrinsic membrane properties in that cultured neurons faithfully followed the intracellular current injection up to 100 Hz. The AMPA receptors mediated excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSC) also displayed stronger SSA compared with the GABA receptors mediated inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSC).The different dynamic of short term synaptic depression characterized by EPSC and IPSC might account for the generation of SSA at the supra-threshold spike level. The heterogeneity of the synaptic inputs is critical to produce the SSA, and contribution of the desensitization of AMPA is involved. We further investigated the influence of the TRN on the SSA of MGB neurons in anesthetized guinea pigs. Intracellular recording in subthreshold level showed SSA of MGB neurons in both EPSP and IPSP forms. The majority of MGB neurons responded to acoustic stimuli with an onset EPSP that followed by long-lasting IPSP components or with only IPSP components. These IPSP components were synchronized with neuronal activities in the TRN. Inactivation of the TRN resulted in a changed neuronal response with minimized IPSP components and thus changed SSA of MGB neurons. Our results suggest that SSA is a network product.

561212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
561212.value: We would like to further explore the synaptic mechanism of stimulus specific adaptation, especially the involvement from presynaptic receptors and neuromodulators. Firstly, we would test the contribution of presynaptic receptors including GABAb receptors and mGluR to SSA, and the agonists and antagonists were applied to examine their influence on SSA; Secondly, the contribution of neuromodulators was also tested in the process of SSA in the brain slice or cultured neural networks; Thirdly, electrical stimulation of neuromodulator-releasing nuclei including dorsal raphe nuclei (DRN) and VTA(Ventral Tegmental Area) to induce the releasing of endogenous neuromodulators of serotonin and dopamine, and further examine the influence of them on SSA on the intact animals; Finally, Cre-dependent ChR2 virus would be used to injected to Cre-dependent animals, and the optical stimulation is applied to examine the effect of endogenous neuromodulators on SSA in both anesthetized and free-moving animals. We hope to unveil the molecular mechanism of the SSA, and the findings of these studies would greatly advance our understanding of the generation of SSA and its functional significance in higher brain function such as attention.

562012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
562012.value: Antibiotic-resistant bugs represent a clinical super-challenge in the 21st century. Resistance of clinical isolates to beta-lactam antibiotics can be overcome by co-administration with beta-lactamase inhibitors. Our innovative engineered fluorescent beta-lactamase P99_V211Cf is a turn-on biosensor for beta-lactam antibiotics and narrow-spectrum class C beta-lactamase inhibitors [Anal. Chem. 2011, 83, 1996-2004]. It represents a proof-of-principle example of the next-generation high-throughput fluorescent screening tool for enzyme inhibitors. Class C (or AmpC-type) beta-lactamases are less susceptible to clinically useful beta-lactamase inhibitors. With the rapid emergence of these problematic enzymes, extensive efforts have been directed to the development of new drugs that can inactivate class C beta-lactamases. High-throughput screening accelerates the discovery of potential drug candidates from chemical libraries. However, it is susceptible to false-positive hits. Many compounds have a high propensity to form aggregates under aqueous conditions, which inhibit beta-lactamase activity through a non-specific mechanism. However, conventional spectrophotometric methods cannot differentiate between active-site-binding compounds (true positive drugs) and non-drug-like aggregation-prone compounds (false positive drugs). Therefore, it is highly desirable to develop a reliable high-throughput screening tool that can identify active-site-binding drug candidates. Using the “active-site-labeling” approach, we successfully developed a novel fluorescent molecular drug target from the class C Enterobacter cloacae P99 AmpC beta-lactamase for in vitro drug screening. The P99 enzyme is labeled with a fluorophore in the close proximity to its active site so as to enable it to fluorescently respond to the drug binding event at the active site. The fluorescent P99 beta-lactamase catalytic activity is maintained so that it can act as a “natural” molecular drug target. By rational design, Val 211 of the cysteine-free P99 enzyme was replaced by a unique cysteine, which was labeled with an environment-sensitive fluorescein-5-maleimide to generate P99_V211Cf. Val 211 is highly conserved in class C beta-lactamases and can serve as a “generic” site for fluorophore labeling in the development of fluorescent drug targets with other clinically relevant class C β-lactamases. In this project, we will solve the crystal structure of P99_V211Cf and elucidate its mechanism of fluorescence enhancement. We will label P99_V211C with different fluorophores and test their properties. We will also engineer the GC1 beta-lactamase (a class C extended-spectrum beta-lactamase) as a new fluorescent screening tool for inhibitors and compare its properties to P99_V211Cf. This innovative “active-site-labeling” strategy will open a possibility for developing tailor-made beta-lactamase-based fluorescent screening tools for inhibitors against each of the extended-spectrum beta-lactamases that mediates antibiotic resistance. 細菌的抗生素耐藥性是21世紀的挑戰，臨床分離株對β-內酰胺類抗生素的抗性，可以用β-內酰胺酶抑製劑與β-內酰胺類抗生素的聯合給藥來克服。我們的創新設計的綠色熒光的酶P99_V211Cf是一類開啟式的β-內酰胺抗生素和窄譜C類β-內酰胺酶抑製劑的生物傳感器[Anal. 562012.label: Realisation of objectives
562012.value: [Objective 1] The fluorescent P99_V211Cf sensor enzyme was prepared and characterized. Preliminary studies on the structure of this important sensor enzyme was performed and we found that its structure was similar to the wild-type P99 enzyme. Consistent with our data, the molecular mechanism of fluorescence enhancement might be explained as follows: a fluorescein was strategically tethered to a flexible loop region in close proximity to the active site of the class C beta-lactamase. This fluorescein molecule serves as a probe for reporting the local environment change in the active site. With the entry of a substrate or an inhibitor to the enzyme’s active site, the fluorescein molecule dislocates from a hydrophobic active site cavity to a more solvent exposed environment, triggering an enhancement in the fluorescence intensity of the biosensor. After substrate- or inhibitor-enzyme binding, with the active site of the beta-lactamase biosensor being occupied, the enhanced fluorescence reaches its maximum level. After that, for good substrates that are susceptible to the beta-lactamase’s hydrolysis, the beta-lactamase biosensor hydrolyzes the substrate and releases the products from its active site after hydrolysis. When the active site becomes unoccupied, the fluorescein molecule returns back to its original position, thereby the enhanced fluorescence signal drops and returns to its basal level. [Objective 2] The P99_V211C mutant was produced and purified. It was labelled with fluorophores fluorescein-5-maleimide and badan. However, the properties of these labelled mutants were very similar to each other. Interestingly, enhancement of the fluorescence intensity of the biosensors was observed when beta-lactam antibiotics were added. [Objective 3] The engineered class C extended-spectrum beta-lactamase has been successfully produced. The GC1 enzyme is an example of molecular evolution of a bacterial enzyme against new beta-lactams in nature. On the other hand, mutations that convert Tyr 221 to Gly or Ala in the P99 enzyme lead to greatly increased ceftazidime resistance. The GC1 enzyme and the Y221G enzyme are the two well characterized class C extended-spectrum beta-lactamases. Using site-directed mutagenesis, we have constructed the two new fluorescent enzymes GC1_A211Cf and Y221G_V211Cf. The GC1_A211C and Y221G_V211C enzymes were expressed and purified. Labelling was successfully performed to obtain GC1_A211Cf and Y221G_V211Cf. Compared to GC1_A211Cf, we obtained a larger amount of Y221G_V211Cf in our production. Therefore, this labelled enzyme was studied in detail. Functional properties of the fluorescent extended-spectrum enzyme Y221G_V211Cf were compared to its non-fluorescent counterpart (Y221G_V211C). Their identity and purity were confirmed by ESI-MS. [Objective 4] Hydrolytic activities of the class C narrow-spectrum P99_V211Cf and the fluorescent extended-spectrum beta-lactamase Y221G_V211Cf were assessed by their hydrolytic degradation of penicillin G, ampicillin, cephalothin, cefoxitin and ceftazidime. Their kinetic parameters were calculated and analyzed. In Y221G_V211Cf, Tyr 221 was substituted by Gly. We found that this change affects the substrate recognition and binding, causing increased values of Km. Also, kcat values were reduced for penicillin G, ampicillin and cephalothin. For cefoxitin, both kcat and Km could not be determined, as the rate of hydrolysis was very slow. For ceftazidime, Km was 28-fold higher than P99_V211Cf and kcat was 1.4-fold higher than P99_V211Cf, consistent with what have been reported in the literature. We successfully engineered the Y221G mutant (a class C extended-spectrum beta-lactamase) as a new fluorescent screening tool for inhibitors and compared its properties to V211Cf. To our surprise, our simple inhibitor screening test provided direct evidence that 2-thiopheneboronic acid is not just a good inhibitor of the narrow-spectrum beta-lactamase P99 (without the Y221G mutation), but it is also a very potent inhibitor of the extended-spectrum Y221G mutant. Importantly, we have demonstrated that the innovative “active-site-labeling” strategy that we have developed might open a possibility for developing tailor-made beta-lactamase-based fluorescent screening tools for inhibitors against each of the extended-spectrum beta-lactamases that mediates antibiotic resistance. We found that the GC1 enzyme and the Y221G enzyme are the two well characterized class C extended-spectrum beta-lactamases. The challenge here was to use protein engineering to turn such enzymes into fluorescent beta-lactamases and screening tools for class C extended-spectrum beta-lactamase inhibitors. Based on our experience with the pivotal P99_V211Cf, we have successfully constructed the new fluorescent enzyme Y221G_V211Cf and tested its properties in detail. The thiol-reactive environment-sensitive fluorophore fluorescein-5-maleimide was used to label the mutant carrying a unique cysteine residue. The fluorescence emission intensity of this fluorophore is very sensitive to the polarity of the surrounding environment. For example, we constructed the Y221G mutant of the P99 enzyme. It was labeled with a fluorophore in the close proximity to its active site so as to enable it to fluorescently respond to the drug binding event at the active site. The fluorescent Y221G_V211Cf extended-spectrum beta-lactamase catalytic activity is maintained so that it can act as a “natural” molecular drug target. By rational design, Val 211 of the cysteine-free Y221G mutant was replaced by a unique cysteine, which was labeled with an environment-sensitive fluorescein-5-maleimide to generate Y221G_V211Cf. We found that Val 211 is highly conserved in class C beta-lactamases and we proved that this 211 position can serve as a “generic” site for fluorophore labeling in the development of fluorescent drug targets with clinically relevant class C beta-lactamases such as the extended-spectrum Y221G mutant. In order to access the capability of V211Cf and Y221G_V211Cf to screen for inhibitors in high-throughput 96-well plate format, a fluorescence experiment was carried out to detect 2-thiopheneboronic acid. This proof-of-principle test provided direct evidence that 2-thiopheneboronic acid is not just a good inhibitor of the narrow-spectrum beta-lactamase P99, but it is also a very potent inhibitor of the extended-spectrum Y221G mutant. Thus, Y221G_V211Cf can become a useful inhibitor screening platform, assisting in identifying appropriate inhibitor partner for the beta-lactam antibiotics for the drug formulation against this extended-spectrum beta-lactamase. This innovative “active-site-labeling” strategy can open a possibility for developing tailor-made beta-lactamase-based fluorescent screening tools for inhibitors against each of the extended-spectrum beta-lactamases that mediates antibiotic resistance.

562012.label: Major findings and research outcome
562012.value: To improve the performance of V211Cf for better cephalosporin detection of the biosensor, we have successfully developed Y150S/V211Cf, a derivative of V211Cf constructed by introducing the Y150S mutation to suppress the hydrolytic activity of V211Cf thereby improving the stability of the fluorescence signal. From our results, Y150S/V211Cf not only demonstrated improved fluorescence signal sustainability over V211Cf, but also showed a rapid response towards cephalothin. These features make it feasible to use Y150S/V211Cf for rapid, specific detection of cephalosporins, and illustrate possibilities for rational biosensor design of catalytically impaired fluorescent enzymes for rapid, sensitive analyte detection purposes. This important finding has been published (Biotechnol. J. 2015, 10, 126–135) (see Part C). We found that V211Cf displayed distinct fluorescence signal patterns toward different kinds of inhibitors due to the differences in their interactions with beta-lactamase. V211Cf not only enables high-throughput screening for inhibitors but can also provide rapid preliminary indication on inhibitor’s potency and stability to beta-lactamase’s hydrolytic action and how the inhibitors interact with target enzyme, thereby speeding up drug discovery and development cycle of class C beta-lactamase inhibitors. This exciting finding was published (Biotechnol. J. 2016, 11, 257–265) (see Part C). A major challenge in our sensor development is to use protein engineering to turn the GC1 enzyme and Y221G mutant into fluorescent beta-lactamases and screening tools for class C extended-spectrum beta-lactamase inhibitors. Based on our experience with the pivotal P99_V211Cf, we have successfully constructed the two new fluorescent enzymes GC1_A211Cf and Y221G_V211Cf. For GC1, the Ala residue at the 211 position was replaced by Cys. Using site-directed mutagenesis, the genes encoding GC1_A211C and Y221G_V211C were obtained. The GC1_A211C and Y221G_V211C enzymes were successfully expressed and purified. Labeling was successfully performed to obtain the fluorescent mutants GC1_A211Cf and Y221G_V211Cf. Complete labeling was confirmed by electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) available in our laboratory. Functional properties of the fluorescent enzymes were compared to their non-fluorescent counterparts. Kinetic and fluorescence properties of engineered fluorescent beta-lactamases have been studied in detail. Mechanisms of fluorescence enhancement were studied. Importantly, we demonstrated that the innovative “active-site-labeling” strategy has the potential to open a possibility for developing tailor-made beta-lactamase-based fluorescent screening tools for inhibitors against each of the extended-spectrum beta-lactamases that mediates antibiotic resistance. The data on the Y221G_V211Cf biosensor development has been submitted to “FEBS Letters” for publication (see Part C).

562012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
562012.value: Further development will include using the thiol-reactive environment-sensitive fluorophore fluorescein-5-maleimide to label each extended-spectrum beta-lactamase mutant carrying a unique cysteine residue at the 211 position. We found that fluorescence emission intensity of this fluorophore is very sensitive to the polarity of the surrounding environment. At this moment, it is not known why binding of the enzyme with substrates became poor after mutating Tyr 221 into glycine. This can be a very interesting structure-function relationship project in future. Furthermore, modeling projects can be started to (i) build the models of V211Cf and Y221G/V211Cf; (ii) compare the models of the active site of V211Cf and Y221G/V211Cf with and without substrate/ inhibitor. Moreover, it will be useful if we could grow some good protein crystals and solve the X-ray structures of the new fluorescent sensor proteins to understand the detailed sensing mechanisms. The data can help the further improvement of these novel inhibitor screening tools and the elucidation of the structure-function relationships of the class C beta-lactamases. In addition, high-throughput screening experiments can be started to discover potential drug candidates from chemical or natural product libraries. The aim will be to develop effective and safe drugs that can inactivate class C extended-spectrum beta-lactamases.

562012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
562012.value: Antibiotic-resistant bugs represent a clinical super-challenge in the 21st century. In particular, bacterial class C beta-lactamases are less susceptible to clinically useful inhibitors. With the rapid emergence of these problematic enzymes, extensive efforts have been directed to the development of new drugs to inactivate class C beta-lactamases. On the other hand, molecular evolution of a bacterial enzyme against new beta-lactam antibiotics in nature can be big bacterial resistance problem. For example, mutation that convert Tyr 221 to Gly in the P99 enzyme lead to greatly increased ceftazidime resistance. Fortunately, resistance of clinical isolates to beta-lactam antibiotics can be overcome by co-administration with beta-lactamase inhibitors. Previously, we proved that fluorescent beta-lactamase V211Cf is a turn-on biosensor for beta-lactam antibiotics and narrow-spectrum class C beta-lactamase inhibitors. However, whether this approach can be applied on a class C extended-spectrum beta-lactamase mutant to screen for inhibitors against extended-spectrum beta-lactamases was not known. Through this project, we have successfully developed new engineered fluorescent beta-lactamase enzymes as screening tools for inhibitors against class C extended-spectrum beta-lactamases including the Y221G mutant. Thus, we have opened a possibility for developing tailor-made beta-lactamase-based fluorescent screening tools for inhibitors against each of the extended-spectrum beta-lactamases that mediates antibiotic resistance.

562212.label: Project Objectives
562212.value: To examine the activation pattern of the parietal cortex, premotor and motor cortices during cued-initiated when compared with self-initiated movement in people with PD To examine the changes in the intracortical inhibitory mechanisms in the motor cortex after the use of visual cues in people with PD To investigate whether the improvements in the movement speed and amplitude relate to the degree of intracortical inhibition in people with PD In the present study, twenty-five healthy and twenty-five PD subjects will be recruited to receive the visually-cued and non-cued training in a random sequence. Subjects will be instructed to perform a finger-pinch exercise with the index finger and thumb for a duration of 30 minutes (Fig 1). Visual cue will be given in the form of an arrow shown on a computer screen to indicate the pre-set force level that subjects have to reach during each pinch (Fig. 2). To address the first objective, subjects will perform the cued-initiated and self-initiated finger-pinch task and the brain activity level will be registered by functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). fMRI is based on the blood-oxygen level dependent (BOLD) signal.[20] An increase in the local neuronal activity will result in an increase in the BOLD signal. We will compare the BOLD signal between the cued-initiated and self-initiated task. The available literature suggests that the local BOLD signal is a function of the synaptic inputs into a brain area and of local neuronal processing, including the activity of excitatory and inhibitory interneurons.[21,22] Hence, the BOLD signal recorded by the fMRI is not a very sensitive measure of cortical inhibition. To address the second objective, electrophysiological tests will be performed using TMS machine immediately prior to and after the cued-initiated and self-initiated task. The intracortical inhibition will be measured by short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI) and the duration of the cortical silent period (CSP), respectively. An increase in SICI and an increase in the duration of CSP after cued-initiated training reflect an enhanced intracortical inhibition on unwanted pathways. To address the third objective, there will be correlation analysis between SICI and CSP duration and the movement speed and amplitude at each assessment interval.

562212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
562212.value: People with Parkinson’s disease (PD) are known to have reduced movement speed and amplitude that affects their arm and hand functions. A lot of studies reported that the use of visual cues (i.e. to indicate force level or distance) could improve movement speed and amplitude. Moreover, the training effect could be carried over to 2-4 weeks after treatment ended. The positive findings of cued-training suggest that motor learning and possibly neuroplasticity occurs in these patients. However the clinical application of visual cue has not been supported by any scientific foundation. We hypothesize that the use of visual cues could bypass the faulty cortical-basal ganglia-cortical circuits and use other available neural pathways, and could enhance intracortical inhibition. The present study aims to (1) examine the activation pattern of the parietal cortex, premotor and motor cortices during cued-initiated when compared with self-initiated movement, (2) examine the changes in the intracortical inhibitory mechanisms after cued-training, and (3) investigate whether the improvements in the movement speed and amplitude relate to the degree of intracortical inhibition in people with PD. Twenty-five healthy subjects and 25 patients with PD will be recruited to receive 1 session of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) measurement when subjects perform both cued-initiated and self-initiated pinch-grip tasks. Data will be acquired in cued-initiated, self-initiated, and rest conditions using a block design. Difference among the tasks in the activation pattern of bilateral parietal, premotor and motor cortices will be analysed. One week after the fMRI scanning session, these patients will receive 2 more sessions of cued-initiated and self-initiated pinch-grip training, arranged in a randomized order. After 30 minutes of training in each session, the intracortical inhibition will be assessed using a transcranial magnetic stimulation machine. We anticipate that with the provision of visual cues, patients with PD will have more activation of parietal-premotor and motor cortices than self-initiated condition, suggesting that the cued-initiated movement could bypass the faulty basal ganglia-cortical circuits and utilize the available parietal-premotor-motor cortical pathway. Furthermore, the use of visual cues will increase the inhibition on competing neural network within the motor cortex and promote the appropriate motor output. Positive findings from the present study will provide scientific evidence that the functional improvement after cued training is associated with corticomotor plasticity. This knowledge will inform rehabilitation practitioners regarding the use of visual cues to better the movement control and to drive activity-dependent neuroplasticity in people with PD 眾所周知，柏金遜病患者的活動速度與幅度均下降，這些活動障礙牽涉到上肢及手功能。一些研究顯示 ，視覺提示（即提示用力程度或活動幅度）可以提高患者的活動速度和幅度。此外，利用視覺提示的訓練效果可在訓練結束後持續2-4星期。這些研究結果表明柏金遜病患者仍具有運動學習能力及可能產生神經的塑性改變。然而，視覺提示的臨床應用還沒有任何科學基礎來支持。 我們假設，視覺提示下活動，運動控制資訊傳遞可能繞過功能障礙的皮層 - 基底節 - 皮層的神經路徑而使用其他可用的神經通路，並且視覺提示可能加強大腦皮質內抑制。本研究的目的是：（1）在提示下與自我啟動兩種不同啟動模式下運動，比較頂葉皮層、運動前皮層及運動皮層的激活模式；（2）利用提示的運動訓練後，檢查大腦皮質內抑制機制的改變； （3）探索柏金遜病患者的運動速度和幅度的改善與其大腦皮質內抑制程度的相關性。 我們將招募25例健康人和25例柏金遜病患者。所有受試者要求分別在視覺提示下啟動及自發啟動兩種不同模式下進行側捏任務，不同任務之間給予恰當的休息。在進行不同側捏任務時，利用功能性磁共振成像測量(fMRI) 記錄兩側頂葉、運動前皮層及運動皮層的激活模式，並進行分析。fMRI掃描一個星期後，所有柏金遜氏患者將會另外接受兩次時長30分鐘的側捏活動訓練。側捏任務則包括提示下啟動及自我發動兩種不同的模式， 其次序是隨機安排的。每次訓練後，利用經顱磁刺激(TMS) 對皮質內抑制進行評估。假設視覺提示下活動，運動控制資訊傳遞可繞過功能障礙的皮層 - 基底節 - 皮層的神經路徑而使用可用的頂葉-運動前皮層-運動皮層路徑，我們預測，在視覺提示下活動，柏金遜患者的頂葉、運動前皮層和運動皮層的激活程度則會較在自發啟動狀態下活動更為明顯。 此外，視覺提示的使用會增加對大腦皮質內的競爭性神經通路的抑制，促使適當的運動輸出。此研究的正面的發現將科學地證明利用提示進行訓練所產生的功能改善與皮質的塑性改變具有相關性。提示的應用可改善運動控制及產生活動依賴的神經塑性變化，使康復專業人員為柏金遜患者選擇提示下訓練的方法有理可依。

562212.label: Realisation of objectives
562212.value: We have completed 2 inter-related studies to achieve all the objectives: 1. To examine the activation pattern of the parietal cortex, premotor and motor cortices during cued-initiated when compared with self-initiated movement in people with PD 2. To examine the changes in the intracortical inhibitory mechanisms in the motor cortex after the use of visual cues in people with PD 3. To investigate whether the improvements in the movement speed and amplitude relate to the degree of intracortical inhibition in people with PD To address objective 1, we have completed Study 1 This study aimed to examine the brain activation patterns during cued- and self-initiated movement in healthy and PD individuals. Twenty-seven patients with PD and 22 age-matched healthy subjects completed the study. Subjects performed a simple finger tapping task in cue-initiated and self-initiated conditions during the scanning sessions. For the self-initiated condition, subjects were instructed to generate a finger tap at irregular intervals between 3s to 5s. In the cue-initiated task condition, subjects were instructed to generate a finger tap in response to a visual cue (“+”) on the computer screen. The rate of the movement was yoked to that generated by the subject in the self-initiated condition. During the rest condition, subjects were asked to relax and view the screen in front of them. Each run consisted of 6 task and 6 resting blocks. All patients performed the task using the hand of their more affected side and during their peak medication state. The brain activations of the finger tapping task during cue- and self-initiated conditions were captured using fMRI. The fMRI data underwent pre-processing and GLM analysis. We then modeled two contrasts for each individual, representing the two task conditions (cue-initiated or self-initiated) compared to the control condition (rest) and these contrast images were entered into the second level analyses. Conjunction analysis was conducted to identify the areas that were commonly activated during self- and cue-initiated movement respectively in both subject groups. Within-group comparisons were conducted by comparing the beta contrast images between the cue- and self-initiated movement using paired t-tests. Between-group differences in each movement condition were evaluated using independent t-tests. Conjunction analysis indicated that both groups had activation in bilateral cerebellum and SMA and ipsilateral precentral gyrus and postcentral gyrus during both self- and cue-initiated movement. Individuals with PD showed higher activation of bilateral cerebellar Crus I during self-initiated movements than cue-initiated movements. When compared with healthy subjects, individuals with PD exhibited lower activation in the inferior parietal lobule and marginally higher activation of the cerebellar Crus II during self-initiated movements, and lower activations of the cerebellar VIIb and VIII during cue-initiated movements. Findings of the study suggest that individuals with PD may underactivate the sensorimotor network and overactivate the cognitive network within the cerebellum. The overactive executive zone of the cerebellum may compensate for the underactive sensorimotor areas of the brain in the PD population. To address objectives 2 and 3, we have completed Study 2: People with PD are characterized by bradykinetic movement and impaired hand function is one disability that affects their independence in daily living. Our previous study reported that one session of training enhanced functional changes and corticomotor excitability in PD individuals, but the study did not have a control group. This study aimed to examine the changes in motor performance, corticomotor excitation and intracortical inhibition after visually-cued hand dexterity training in people with PD and healthy control, and to establish whether the improvements in the motor performance was related to the degree of corticomotor excitation and intracortical inhibition in people with PD. Twenty-six patients with PD (mean age=61.4±5.8 years) and 22 healthy subjects (mean age=61.9±5.9) completed the study. All subjects completed two training sessions: visually cued and non-cued arranged in a random manner with 2-week wash-out period. During cued training, subjects were instructed to grip a force transducer with their thumb and index finger to reach 3 pre-set force levels (i.e. 10%, 15% and 30% of subjects’ maximum pinch-grip force) as fast and as accurate as possible, and to maintain the force for about 3 seconds. The pre-set force level indicated on the computer screen served as a visual feedback. During non-cued condition, subjects were first allowed to look at the computer screen and to learn reaching the pre-set pinch grip force. After they had learnt the level of the force, they were asked to reach the same grip force without looking at the computer screen (no visual cue), and to maintain the force for about 3 seconds. At the end of each set of exercise, they were given feedback about their level of force. The training session lasted for 30 minutes. Outcome measures: The behavioral changes were assessed by movement time and movement accuracy of the pinch grip force at 20% and 60% of subjects’ maximum pinch grip. Corticomotor excitability was assessed using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to obtain the peak motor evoked potential (MEP) and duration of cortical silent period (CSP). TMS was applied to the scalp over the motor cortex contralateral to first dorsal interossei (FDI) muscles. Two-way repeated-measure ANOVA was carried out to assess the effect of group and training on subjects’ behavioral performance and electrophysiological changes. After one session of pinch-grip training with visual cue, PD individuals improved their movement accuracy, movement time and corticomotor excitability to an extent comparable to those of healthy subjects. Since the motor and electrophysiological changes were similar in both PD and healthy control groups, people with PD could have retained their ability to learn motor skills through visually-guided practice. We further found that the decrease in movement error was associated with an increased corticomotor excitation after cued training in the PD group. Training with visual cue might increase corticomotor excitability and enhance the motor output. Cued training might facilitate the use of the cognitive network of the cerebellum as found in Study 1 but future study examining post-training fMRI is needed to confirm this postulation.

562212.label: Major findings and research outcome
562212.value: Results of Study 1: Healthy subjects had higher brain activity in contralateral precentral gyrus during the self-initiated task, and higher brain activity in the ipsilateral middle occipital gyrus during the cue-initiated task. PD patients had higher brain activity in the cerebellum Crus I (bilateral) and lobules VI (ipsilateral) during the self-initiated task and higher brain activity in the contralateral middle frontal gyrus during the cue-initiated task. When compared with healthy controls, PD patients had lower brain activity in the contralateral inferior parietal lobule during the self-initiated task, and lower brain activity in the ipsilateral cerebellum lobule VIII, lobule VIIB and vermis VIII, and thalamus during the cue-initiated task. There was a trend for PD patients to exhibit higher brain activity in contralateral cerebellum Crus II during the self-initiated movements. Findings of the study suggest that individuals with PD may underactivate the sensorimotor network and overactivate the cognitive network within the cerebellum. Results of Study 2: There was no significant interaction for the training effect. The movement errors in reaching 20% and 60% of the subjects’ maximum pinch grip forces were significantly reduced in both PD and healthy subjects after cued-training only (p<0.01). The peak MEP amplitude significantly increased for both PD and healthy subjects after cued-training only (p<0.05). There was no significant change in movement time and duration of CSP. Regarding the changes from the baseline values, both subject groups had significantly more reduction in the movement error for reaching 60% subjects’ maximum pinch-grip force after cued than non-cued training (PD=Cued -4.84±1.85 vs Non-cued 1.69±1.43; Control=-3.34±1.97 vs -1.21±1.53, p<0.01). There was marginally more reduction in the movement time to reach 20% subjects’ maximum pinch-grip force after cued than non-cued training (PD=-6.85±3.88 vs 3.92 4.14s; Control=-2.23±4.22 vs 2.23±4.50s, p=0.063). There was inverse correlation between the movement error for reaching 60% subjects’ maximum pinch-grip and peak MEP (r=-0.42, p<0.05) for the PD group, implying that more corticomotor excitation was related to less movement error. One session of training with visual cue might have increased the motor output of the relevant muscles while suppressing the irrelevant muscle activation. Therefore, it could enhance movement accuracy and movement speed as well as induce corticomotor excitation. Results of study 1 and 2 shed some light on the understanding of brain activation and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying cued-training.

562212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
562212.value: Future study should examine the benefit of cued training in patients with more advanced stage of PD, and during their “off” medication state. It is also important to explore the long-term effect of cued training on behavioural changes as well as electrophysiological and brain activation patterns. If long-term motor improvement after training is associated with an increase in corticomotor excitation, then neuroplasticity is possible. Our study revealed both pathological and compensatory roles of cerebellum in PD, it is important to further explore the relationship of cerebellum and striatum. We propose to examine the short- and long-term effects of visually cued training in a group of moderate and advanced PD individuals. Outcome measures will include behavioual tests (movement speed, movement accuracy), electrophysiological tests (Peak MEP, intracortical silent period), and brain activation pattern using fMRI. Furthermore it is interesting to establish the relationship between electrophysiological changes and brain activation. Functional connectivity studies can be used to explore the relationship between cerebellum and striatum to understanding the role of cerebellum in PD. A better understanding of the PD-related functional and physiological changes of cerebellum may help in developing new treatment and rehabilitation strategy.

562212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
562212.value: The use of visual cue has been found to enhance motor output but the mechanisms underlying the improvement is unknown. We have completed 2 inter-related studies. Study 1 used fMRI and reported that both PD and healthy subjects activated motor and sensory cortices during self- and cue-initiated movement. Individuals with PD exhibited higher brain activity in the executive zone of the cerebellum during self-initiated movement, and lower brain activity in the sensorimotor zone of the cerebellum during cue-initiated movement. These findings suggest that individuals with PD may use more executive control when performing simple movements. Study 2 examined the behavioural and electrophysiological changes after visually-cued training in PD individuals. Results revealed that both PD and healthy subjects had significantly more reduction in the movement error and movement time and more increases in the brain excitation after cued than non-cued training. Furthermore, PD individuals improved movement accuracy, movement time and brain excitability in an extent comparable to those of healthy subjects. The use of visual cues is useful to enhance motor performance and physiological changes of the brain. These information is useful to understand the mechanisms underlying cued training and to develop more innovative rehabilitation strategies for people with PD.
