563012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
563012.value: More than 70% of the Chinese population developed hypertrophic scar (HS) after skin trauma, which is much higher than that of the western population. Pressure therapy is currently the mainstay noninvasive treatment of HS. Despite numerous studies reporting its effect on pacing scar maturation, reducing the incidence of contracture and negating the need of surgical reconstruction, the exact mechanism of pressure intervention on HS remained unclear. Besides, an optimal timing to implement pressure therapy is not available yet. Our pilot study on clinical assessments has demonstrated significant improvement in scar condition as early as on the first 3 months of pressure intervention. Histopathologically, myofibroblast, a specialized fibroblastic population that accounted for the pathological consequences of HS, was absent in normal skin but became abundant in active HS. Interestingly, the myofibroblast population was significantly reduced after the 3-month treatment, with a concomitant increase in apoptosis in dermal layer. Furthermore, the proliferative activity of the epidermal cells in the post-pressurized HS was significantly lower. We hypothesize that pressure intervention promoted HS maturation through suppressing myofibroblast by apoptosis and inhibiting epidermal cell proliferation, and an early application of pressure is more effective in this aspect. The main objective of this study is to (i) explore the in-depth mechanism of pressure therapy on HS maturation and (ii) compare the efficacy of pressure therapy intervened at different duration after skin injury. Therefore, a randomized clinical trial (RCT) is designed in which 60 Chinese HS patients will be recruited for a 3-month pressure therapy program either at an early (wounds just healed up and HS appeared for 1 week) or at a late (wounds healed up and HS developed for at least 3 months) time point. Pressure dose will be adjusted (15-20mmHg) through regular monitoring by Pliance X System. Laboratory assessments will be conducted to investigate the histopathological and biochemical changes in line with the clinical measurement between a) pre-pressurized and post-pressurized HS samples of the same patients, b) pressurized and non-pressurized HS samples of the same patients, and c) early intervened and late intervened HS samples. The present study represents one of the very few pioneer investigations on the mechanism of pressure therapy on HS maturation through a longitudinal monitoring approach. Acquisition of a well-defined and evidence-based therapeutic time window will significantly facilitate efficient management of HS and reduce unnecessary cost of a prolonged period of treatment for patients and the whole society. 超過七成的中國人群在皮膚創傷後會產生增生性瘢痕，發病率遠遠高於西方人群。壓力治療是目前最主要的治療增生性瘢痕無創性療法。許多文獻研究指出壓力治療可促進瘢痕成熟、減少疤痕攣縮和降低重建整形手術的需要，然而，壓力治療的確切作用機制迄今仍不清楚。此外，關於實施壓力治療的最佳時機，仍無法確定。 我們的臨床預試驗結果顯示，在三個月的壓力干預作用下，疤痕情況已有顯著改善。從組織病理學的角度，我們已知有一種特別的成纖維細胞──肌成纖維細胞，主要導致瘢痕的不斷增生的病理過程及結果。肌成纖維細胞在正常皮膚是幾乎不存在的，而在活躍期的增生性瘢痕中則存在大量的肌成纖維細胞。實驗結果發現，肌成纖維細胞數量在三個月的壓力治療後明顯減少，與此同時，真皮層發生凋亡的細胞數量增加，而且表皮細胞的增殖活性在壓力治療後明顯降低。 我們推測：壓力干預可通過引導細胞凋亡，抑制肌成纖維細胞的增長及表皮細胞的增殖來促進疤痕的成熟，並且在疤痕生長初期應用壓力治療效果更為顯著。本研究的主要目的是（一）深入地探索壓力療法對於疤痕成熟的作用機制和（二）比較壓力治療在皮膚損傷後不同時間實施干預的療效。因此，我們選取隨機臨床試驗（隨機對照試驗）設計，將招募60名增生性疤痕的中國患者，對其進行三個月的壓力治療計劃。確定兩個時間點：早期（傷口癒合及疤痕形成時間一週內）；後期（傷口癒合和疤痕形成至少三個月）。壓力的大小劑量將通過Pliance X 系統定期監測調整為15-20mmHg。實驗室評估（病理和生化變化）與臨床特徵評估對應平行進行：（一）相同患者壓力治療前後的疤痕比較；（二）相同患者加壓和非加壓疤痕樣本的比較；和（三）早期干預和後期干預後疤痕樣本的比較。 本研究是為數極少的縱向觀察壓力療法於疤痕成熟機制的先鋒研究之一。獲取一個明確的、以實證為基礎的治療時間，將大大促進疤痕治療的有效性和減少因過長時間治療而引致不必要的病者個人成本及社會成本。

563012.label: Realisation of objectives
563012.value: 1. Objective 1. To explore the mechanism of pressure therapy on HS maturation from the histopathological perspective and/or its correlation with clinical characteristics among the Chinese population. The details of objective realization: 1.1 Clinical perspective The clinical study was completed. Hypertrophic scars collected in the study showed significant improvement in pigmentation, pliability, vascularity and height according to an objective clinical assessments. Meanwhile, in addition to the improvement in physical appearance and clinical characteristics, patients also reported decreased pain and itchiness. Overall, our project has established the practical guideline on how to implement pressure therapy with adequate interface pressure. And we have set up the standard protocol and regular follow-up regime based on the current study. Positive feedback were obtained from both patients and clinicians through interviews. 1.2 Histopathological perspective The effect of pressure therapy on the epidermal and dermal manifestation were examined and completed based on the methods stated in the report. Western blotting was scheduled in the proposal to examine the histopathological outcomes of scar tissues. For the paraffin embedded samples we collected from multi-centers, protein extraction was required prior to conducting western blotting. However, inconsistent results were obtained due to the loss of protein in protein extraction procedure. In order to obtain more specific and accurate results from, we have applied immunofluorescence staining and DAB staining instead to analyze the expression of target proteins. The underlying mechanism on inflammatory cytokines such as TGF β1 and its receptor 1 and 2 (R1, R2) were examined. Furthermore, the potential upstream mechanism of mechanotransduction was also explored in addition to the initial plans. The sub-objectives and our findings were: 1.2.1 The effect of pressure therapy on epidermis. (1) The results demonstrated significant decrease in the expression of Ki-67 and CK6 in the HS samples after three months of pressure intervention. Keratinocyte activation and proliferation in epidermis of HS tissue was downregulated after pressure therapy; (2) The pressure therapy was found to only suppress keratinocytes proliferation and activation, but did not induce their apoptosis. 1.2.2 The effect of pressure therapy on dermis. (1) Pressure therapy was found to downregulate myofibroblast population in human HS tissue in vivo; (2) Pressure intervention was found to induce realignment of Collagen I fibers in HS tissue. 1.2.3 The effect of pressure on regulating TGF-β signaling pathway. (1) Expressions of TGFβ-R1, R2 and pSmad in the dermal regions (but not epidermis) were found to be downregulated after pressure treatment, indicating the potential involvement of TGF-β signaling of pressure therapy on hypertrophic scar. (2) The association we found between myofibroblast and TGFβ receptors indicated that pressure therapy might control the myofibroblast through regulating the dermal TGFβ-R2 and pSmad in hypertrophic scar tissues. (3) TGF-β1 expression did not show significant change after pressure therapy, whereas TGF-β R1 and R2 were found to be downregulated. Since it is the binding form of TGF-β1 and its receptors that could trigger the subsequent signalling cascade, the result indicated that pressure therapy could control scarring through TGF-β1 receptors instead of TGF-β1. 1.2.4 The effect of pressure on regulating mechanotransduction (integrin β1, FAKTyr397, Erk(1/2)). (1) Integrin β1, FAKTyr397, Erk(1/2) significantly decreased in dermis after 3-month pressure therapy (2) When analyzing together with other confounding factors such as subjects' age and post injury days, receiving pressure therapy or not was found to be the only significant contributor to the difference in the intensity of integrin β1. 2. Objective 2. To compare the efficacy of pressure therapy between the early intervention (before HS is formed) and the late intervention groups (after HS is formed); besides, to explore how the myofibroblast population respond to both early and late pressure intervention. In order to enrich the scientific evidence of pressure therapy in terms of time, comparison was made between early and late application of pressure therapy. Two months after injury was taken as the reference time point according to the clinical experiences and previous literature. We found: 2.1 Clinical perspective (1) Early application of pressure therapy demonstrated significant improvement in scar pliability and color. And it provided better outcomes in scar appearance and patients’ subjective feeling when compared with late group. 2.2 Histopathological perspective (1) Early application of pressure therapy appeared to suppress the proliferation of myofibroblasts, but there was no significant difference in the overall α-SMA expression between early and late pressure therapy groups. (2) Early pressure intervention showed better effect in inhibiting keratinocyte activation and myofibroblast proliferation when compared to the late group. (3) Post-injury days was found to significantly contribute to the intensity of integrin β1, FAKTyr397, Erk(1/2) in dermis. Through mapping the intensity of integrin β1, FAKTyr397, Erk(1/2) along with the post-days, we found the increased proteins’ intensity appeared in 1-3 months after injury. This indicated a crucial influence of time on the treatment effect. Since integrin β1 can be regulated by external force, the increase intensity of integrin β1 might explain why early implementation of pressure therapy can achieve a better outcome. 3. Objective 3. With results from 1 and 2, we are able to build up a theoretical model on early pressure therapy of HS among Chinese subjects. Generally, our project team has successfully investigated the effect of pressure therapy on clinical parameters, histopathology and underlying mechanism. From the pre-mentioned results, we have screened out parameters that are crucial for pressure therapy and scar managements: 3.1 Clinical aspects: (1) Magnitude of pressure dosage: monitored through objective measurements could ensure the clinical effect; (2) Time of intervention: 1 to 3 month time. 2. Histopathological aspect: (1) Pressure therapy could control TGF-β signaling through regulating the activity of its receptors; (2) Mechanotransduction might be the upstream mechanism that could regulate epidermal and dermal cell behavior.

563012.label: Major findings and research outcome
563012.value: In this project, we found the positive clinical outcomes after standardized 3-month pressure treatment. We found improvement in the scoring of Vancouver Scar Scale and the objective measurements of ultrasound (scar thickness) and spectrocolorimeter (scar color). The publication of clinical findings has been accepted and is in pressing (Part C). Our project team has attended national and international conference to share the findings, and promoted the close collaboration with surgeons and other medical professionals. We have also provided training to therapists world-wide on the standardized pressure therapy protocol, the selection of treatment timing, and the importance of objective measurements. Our project has also obtained the histopathological results from in-vivo human beings, to explore the mechanism of pressure therapy, and the relationship between clinical and preclinical findings. The 3-month pressure therapy appeared to promote scar maturation by controlling aberrant keratinocytes activation, regulating the activation of TGF β signaling through TGF β receptors, and manipulate the activity level of integrin β1. We found the early (1~3 months after injury) application is crucial for effective managements. Two publications in English regarding the histopathological results are under preparation. We have attended international conference to present our findings and established the collaboration with international research institute such as University of Antwerp (Belgium).

563012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
563012.value: From clinical aspects, we are investigating the efficient ways to optimize the pressure application methods in addition to pressure garment treatments. Even distribution and adequate interface pressure dosage is critical for effective management. Therefore, we are developing standardized 3D scanning and printing protocol and techniques for facial hypertrophic scars. Innovative medical-grade inserts for even distribution of pressure is also under developing. From histopathological aspects, we have pioneered to investigate the effect of pressure therapy through TGF β signaling pathway and its receptors, as well as mechanotransduction in human scar tissues. The results closely related the mechanism of pressure therapy to the clinical manifestation of scars. Further experiments will target at causal-effect of pressure on signaling for scarring on in-vitro and animal models. To find out how does pressure transform to regulate scarring process, we can utilize specific inhibitors on target proteins, or gene knock-out techniques in animal models, to deepen the understanding of the mechanism of pressure therapy.

563012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
563012.value: Pressure therapy has been widely applied in clinics to manage hypertrophic scars. However, due to prolonged scarring process and insignificant outcomes observed, clinicians and patients had reservation on the effectiveness of pressure therapy. In our study, we have further demonstrated the positive clinical effect together with histological outcomes, emphasizing the standardized treatments including the regular measurement of pressure dosage, and monitoring the timing of intervention. Early application of pressure therapy was found to be better according to results from both clinical and histological experiments. Meanwhile, we also explored the underlying mechanism of how does external force affect critical process in scarring. Our project managed to obtain human scar tissues for histological experiments, which could provide a more scientific inference of its effectiveness on human subjects in contrast to the cell or animal models. Furthermore, the scientific design of intervention, clinical assessments, and follow-up in our study can be transformed into standardized guidelines for clinical practice, to benefit more patients suffered from hypertrophic scars.

563412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
563412.value: Background: Radiation induced temoporomandibular joint (TMJ) trismus is one of the common sequalae in nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC) patients after radiotherapy. It causes speech impairment, difficulty in mastication, leading to poor nutritional status and oral hygiene. At present, little is known about the post-radiotherapy change of joint morphology and joint dynamics. Such information is essential for early diagnosis, which is important because delayed treatment increases the difficulty in reversing the condition. Ultrasonography, which is non-invasive, cheap and readily available, has the potential to be the standard imaging tool to provide early diagnosis of trismus. This study is to investigate the morphological changes of the TMJ after irradiation respect to time. The role of ultrasonography in assessing TMJ disorders will be evaluated by comparing with the magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). In addition the correlation between TMJ dose and severity of trismus will be investigated. Methods: The first part is a cross-sectional study on 55 post-radiotherapy NPC patients. Ultrasound scan will be used to assess the joint morphology including the disc dimension and echogenicity of the associated ligaments and muscles, vascularisation and dynamics. The images of a routine follow up MRI scan at about 2 years after radiotherapy will be retrieved and compared with that from the ultrasound scan. The severity of trismus will be assessed by measuring the maximum interincisal distance (MID). The radiotherapy plans of the patients will be retrieved and the TMJ dose will be calculated from the treatment planning system. The correlation between the TMJ dose and severity of trismus will be evaluated using the Pearson correlation test. Another 55 age-matched normal subjects will undergo the same ultrasound examination as for the patients. Comparison of the ultrasound findings between the patient and normal groups will be conducted to evaluate any significant difference between them. The significance of their differences will be calculated by the unpaired t-test. The second part is a longitudinal study on 25 newly diagnosed NPC patients. Baseline ultrasound, MRI and MID examinations will be conducted before radiotherapy. Repeated ultrasound and MID examinations will be conducted at completion of radiotherapy and subsequent follow up visits at 6, 12 and 18 and 24 months after radiotherapy. Trend lines of each parameter will be generated to track the TMJ condition over time. The time point at which the MID fall below 4.0 cm or shows a >10% reduction will be defined as the “onset” of radiation induced trismus. 輻射引起的顳顎關節牙關緊閉是鼻咽癌病人接受放射治療後的其中一種常見後遺症. 它會削弱說話能力, 導致吞嚥困難,營養情況及口腔衛生下降. 現時醫學上對放療後關節形態及活動的變化了解仍很少.其實這些資料可協助及早診斷有關症狀, 而若延遲治療將使復原的機會減低. 超聲波檢查是一種沒有侵略性, 便宜而且方便的造影方法.它有條件用作常規診斷早期牙關緊閉的造影工具. 這項研究是去調查顳顎關節在放療後於不同時間出現的變化. 透過與磁力共振影像比較, 評估超聲波檢查用於量度顳顎關節變化的角色. 同時亦會研究顳顎關節所受劑量與牙關緊閉程度的關係. 第一部份是橫向研究, 將邀請55位放療後有兩年或以上的成年鼻咽癌病人參加. 利用超聲波評估關節對放療後關節形態, 包括關節板的大小, 韌帶及肌肉的反射度, 血管化及活動程序等. 這些超聲波影像將與病人放療後兩年以上所拍之磁力共振影像作比較. 同時將以而以量度病人最大前齒間距離來評估牙關緊閉嚴重程度. 此外,利用電腦計劃系統從取回的病人放療計劃中計算出病人顳顎關節所受的輻射劑量, 從而分析顳顎關節劑量與牙關緊閉程度的關係.另一方面, 將邀請55位年紀配合的正常實驗對象接受同樣的超聲波檢查, 所得的影像將與病人所得的影像作比較, 從而找出他們的分別. 第二部份是縱向研究, 將邀請25位剛診斷有鼻咽癌之病人參加.在他們接受放療前進行基線的超聲波, 磁力共振及最大前齒間距的評估. 此後, 將於放療完結後的6, 12,18 及24 個月重覆進行超聲波及前齒間距的檢查. 有關的參數將以走勢圖顯示其與時間的關係. 而因輻射引起的牙關緊閉開始日期將定義為當前齒間距跌至4厘米以下或顯示有一成的減少出現的時間.

563412.label: Realisation of objectives
563412.value: To achieve the first objective, 114 NPC patients, who had completed radiotherapy for more than four years were recruited. Each subject received an ultrasonography examination of TMJ. In each scan, the thickness of the joint disc, the irregularity of the mandibular condyle, echogenicity of lateral pterygoid muscle and the joint vascularity were assessed. In addition to the ultrasound examination, the maximum incisal distance (MID) of the patient, which was an indication of the severity of trismus, was also recorded. 100 normal adult subjects age matched with the patient group within ±5 years and with no previous irradiation and injury in the TMJ, were recruited as the control group. Each normal subject underwent the same TMJ assessments as for the patient group. The data collected from each parameter was compared between the patient and control group. The MID of the patient group ranged from15 mm to 53 mm (mean = 35.0±9.4 mm), whereas those from the control group were between 27 mm and 61 mm (mean = 47.2±6.5 mm). The difference was statistically significant (p < 0.001). Based on the previous definition of trismus in which adult patients with MID ≤ 3.5 cm were regarded as suffering from trismus, 41.2% of the subjects in the patient group presented with trismus, whereas there was only 4.0% in the control group. For the ultrasound examination, the mean MDT of the patient group was smaller than that of the control group in both transverse and longitudinal scans, with only the former showing significant difference (p = 0.006). For condyle irregularity, the mean values of the patient group were significantly greater than those of the control group in both transverse and longitudinal scans. For joint vascularity, the control group demonstrated a lower percentage than that of the patient group, in which only the transverse scan showed significant difference (p = 0.028). For the relative muscle echogenicity of the lateral pterygoid muscle, about 60% of both the patient and control groups were hypoechoic. Post-RT TMJ changes were characterized by the reduction of disc thickness, increase of condyle irregularity and vascularity were detected in the NPC patients. These parameters could be used to monitor the TMJ condition and provide timely management for patients who present with trismus. To achieve the second objective, all patients recruited under this study underwent ultrasonograhy using the Esaote MyLab Twice ultrasound unit in conjunction with a 4-13 MHz linear transducer (Esaote, Genoa, Italy). The left and right TMJs were scanned separately with the patient lying on a couch and head turned to the opposite side of scanning. Both transverse and longitudinal scans of each TMJ were taken. In each scan, the thickness of the joint disc, the irregularity of the mandibular condyle, echogenicity of lateral pterygoid muscle and the joint vascularity were assessed. The ultrasound examination was able to provide adequate anatomic and physiological information for the assessment of TMJ. One limitation of this study was that the patients were not able to undergo MRI examination due to budget constraint. Instead information about MRI examination on TMJ were reviewed in related articles and analysed with reference to the ultrasound examination. Although MRI is not able to show the bony details as comprehensive as CT, the contour of the osseous structures concerned is available. The sensitivity and specificity for detecting avascular necrosis were 78% and 84% respectively, while they were 30-82% and 84-98% respectively for detecting osseous abnormalities of TMJ. With the high contrast-sensitivity to tissue differences including TMJ, MRI now has replaced CT and acts as the gold standard for diagnosis of TMJ disorder. On the other hand ultrasonography was found to be more reliable for detecting disc displacement and joint effusion, but relatively less accurate for condylar erosion, particularly in the cases with co-existence of osteoarthritis in terms of diagnosis of temporomandibular disorders. Sonography’s sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy for the diagnosis of disk displacement, relative to MR as the standard of reference were 83%, 96%, and 92% respectively. To achieve the third objective, 97 post-RT NPC were recruited. For each patient, the radiotherapy treatment plan was retrieved from. The left and right TMJs were contoured in the corresponding CT slices. The mean TMJ dose of each side was calculated by the generation of the dose volume histogram (DVH). The severity of trismus was measured by the MID. Each patient was instructed to first open his or her mouth with force to the greatest extent. Then the maximum upper incisor to lower incisor distances was measured using a caliper and ruler. The procedure was repeated twice in a time interval of five minutes. The mean value of the three measurements was calculated and recorded. Patients with MID ≤ 3.5 cm were regarded as suffering from trismus. Each subject underwent an ultrasonography examination of the TMJ as described in part I. The TMJ dose and patient demographics including post-RT duration and age were expressed by median and range. The data obtained from ultrasonography and MID measurement are then compared against patient demographics and the doses to the TMJ. The median value of MID was 3.7 cm with range of 1.3-5.2 cm. If MID ≤ 3.5 cm was defined as trismus, over 60% of the subject presented with this condition and 6.2% of them belonged to the severe condition (MID <2.0 cm). From the results of Pearson correlation and t-test, MID was negatively correlated with mean TMJ dose and post-RT duration, indicating that higher dose and longer post-RT duration was related to a lower value of MID (Table 2). Multivariate analysis also showed that there were significant associations of the post-RT duration and mean TMJ dose with the development of trismus when either tested alone or in combination. The mean maximum disc thickness (MDT) of the transverse scan (TS) and longitudinal scan (LS) were 0.15 cm and 0.16 cm respectively, whereas they were 8.14% and 13.21% respectively for the mean irregularity of condyle (Table 3). For the echogenicity of pterygoid muscle (EM) in both LS and TS, over half of them were hypoechoic, whereas about 23% and 18% were hyperechoic and isoechoic respectively. The severity of trismus increased with the mean TMJ dose and post-RT duration in post-RT NPC patients. In the ultrasound examination, the joint disc thickness was found to decrease with increased dose to TMJ. However, the other sonographic parameters did not show definite relationship with TMJ doses and most patient characteristics. It was suggested that radiotherapy techniques such as IMRT which could kept the TMJ dose reasonably low should be used so as to lower the risk of trismus

563412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
563412.value: The current study was a cross-sectional study that was focussed on the changes of the TMJ of post-radiotherapy patients during their follow up periods. With the TMJ assessment protocol develped in this study, which include the ultrasonography, a longitudinal study would be suggested. This would give more detail information about the changes of the the TMJ with respect to time. In addition, treatment interventions for trismus, such as are also suggested in further studies for post-RT patients. The efficacy of such treatment can be assessed by the established protocol.

563412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
563412.value: This proposed study provided early diagnosis of radiation induced temporal mandibular joint (TMJ) disorders and detail morphological and physiological information of the TMJ. The knowledge is useful to provide timely management of the patients, which increases the chance of cure. Furthermore, a better understanding of the cause and progression of the TMJ changes after radiotherapy provides effective preventive measures and better patient care should the condition appears. This study has ascertained ultrasonography as an optimal imaging tool in the assessment of TMJ disorders. In addition, the evaluation of the dose-severity relationships for trismus helps to establish a threshold dose for the TMJ and pterygoid muscle. This provides useful information for radiotherapy treatment planning to limit the dose to the organ and helps to reduce the complication riskfor NPC patients undergoing radiotherapy.

563512.label: Realisation of objectives
563512.value: Skeletal muscle is well known for its mechanosensitive responsiveness; sensors recognize mechanical stimuli and translate the inputs into biochemical signals that undergo complicated molecular cascades and ultimately elicit an appropriate cellular response. The mechanosensitive nature of skeletal muscle is best demonstrated by the response during gravitational unloading and reloading. In response to gravitational unloading, postural muscles, such as the soleus that is composed predominantly of slow-twitch fibers, display the most prominent phenotypic changes, including an increase in fast MHC fibers due to slow-to-fast fiber type shifting, accompanied by a reduction in muscle mass and fiber cross-sectional area due to atrophy. Such remodeling occurs only very mildly in fast-twitch muscles. TRPC1 channel-mediated Ca2+ entry is mechanosensitive. Involvement of TRPC1 signaling in unloading-induced atrophy is evident in a C2C12 model exposed to simulated microgravity. This condition retards myoblast proliferation and inhibits terminal differentiation concomitant with repressed TRPC1 expression. The TRPC blocker SKF 96365 retards proliferation and retains myoblast at the G2/M phase of the cell cycle in a dose-dependent manner, similar to microgravity conditions. Yet the role of TRPC1 in mechanical unloading was unclear until we reported dynamic TRPC1 expression in the soleus muscle when mice were subjected to hindlimb unloading in 2014. Despite a rather stable expression of TRPC1 mRNA transcript, the TRPC1 protein level significantly decreases after 14 days of hindlimb unloading; we confirmed the reduction by immunohistochemistry, in which TRPC1 immunoreactivity was significantly diminished in the sarcolemma of the soleus muscle. These in vivo data echo the in vitro observation that C2C12 cells under microgravity downregulate TRPC1, indicating that TRPC1 expression in skeletal muscle is mechanosensitive. This notion is further supported by the findings that TRPC1 transcripts in the soleus muscle were seven times higher than those in fast-twitch EDL muscle, corroborated by immunohistochemical staining. In contrast, the TRPC3 channel, which is the predominant TRPC isoform in EDL muscle, displays rather stable expression during hindlimb unloading. The preferential expression of TRPC1 in slow muscles rather than in fast muscles fits well with the response of the channel expression upon mechanical unloading. Given the evidence that TRPC1 is mechanosensitive, we initially expected that when the unloaded mouse was allowed to resume normal weight bearing, TRPC1 expression would immediately revert. Surprisingly, TRPC1 expression decreases further in the first few days of reloading. Restoration of TRPC1 expression commences at around 7 days of reloading; however, we are unsure by which day the expression of TRPC1 reaches its lowest point, because we have not examined the time points between day 3 and day 7 of reloading. The expression does not fully return to control level until day 28 of reloading. The time window of TRPC1 protein restoration correlates strongly with the recovery of muscle mass and fiber cross-sectional area and the fiber-type shifting that unloading alters. This correlation prompted us to hypothesize that TRPC1 expression is related to reloading-induced muscle regrowth. The hypothesis led us to further experiments on in vivo TRPC1 silencing in soleus muscles immediately following reloading. By employing focal electroporation of siRNA, we achieved specific downregulation of TRPC1 only within the target muscle, while the TRPC1 channel expression in other regions and even in adjacent muscles remained unaltered. Inhibition of TRPC1 expression lasted for at least 7 days post-electroporation, which allowed sufficient time to observe the effects of TRPC1 suppression in reloaded muscle regrowth. Our hypothesis was confirmed by the observation that silencing of TRPC1 in soleus muscle impairs the overall muscle regrowth process. We demonstrate significant reductions in muscle size, mass, and fiber cross-sectional area in TRPC1 knockdown soleus muscles, compared to control oligo-electroporated reloaded soleus muscles. Moreover, TRPC1 silencing blocks the typical fast-to-slow fiber remodeling in the reloaded soleus, thus establishing the physiological relevance of TRPC1 in reloading-induced muscle regrowth. We subsequently correlated the expression of TRPC1 during the unloading-reloading process with expression of calcineurin (CaN) and NFATc1, which are well known for their roles in fiber-type conversion. A temporal increase in CaN expression and NFAT nuclear translocation precedes the onset of TRPC1 upregulation during the reloading process. CaN inhibitors (FK506 and cyclosporine A) suppress CaN activity and block the recovery of the percentage of MHC I fiber and fiber cross-sectional area in reloaded mice, which is consistent with results from previous reports. We considered the possibility that CaN-NFAT activity modulates TRPC1 expression in reloading muscle. Inhibition of CaN activity results in repression of TRPC1 compared with the vehicle control. This novel finding helps establish the possible role of CaN/NFAT in regulating TRPC1 expression in reloaded muscle, suggesting that the TRPC1 channel participates in CaN/NFAT-mediated muscle regrowth. SOCE regulates gene expression via TRPC1 when Ca2+ entry triggers the activation of CaN followed by dephosphorylation of NFAT, NFAT nuclear translocation, and transactivation of gene expression. The possibility that TRPC1 expression being regulated by CaN/NFAT may represent a novel pathway that deserves further investigation. The detailed pathway of CaN/NFAT leading to TRPC1-mediated SOCE, and the involvement of SOCE in fiber-type conversion have yet to be explored, though it is possible that the PI3K/Akt pathway could be involved in the muscle mass and fiber cross-sectional area recovery mediated by TRPC1. Nevertheless, our findings thus far strongly indicates that TRPC1 is a mechanosensitive channel and that Ca2+ entry via TRPC1 plays an important role in muscle remodeling during mechanical reloading. Both of the study objectives have been addressed.

563512.label: Major findings and research outcome
563512.value: Skeletal muscles exhibit high plasticity in response to mechanical load for growth and maintenance. The involvement of the canonical transient receptor potential type 1 (TRPC1) protein, a component of the store-operated channel, is implicated in the process of muscle atrophy following mechanical unloading. Here, we identified a novel role of TRPC1 in the regulation of muscle regrowth in vivo. Specifically, there were three key findings in our study: (1) The soleus muscle exhibits reduced TRPC1 expression concomitant with reduced muscle mass, reduced myofiber cross-sectional area (CSA), and decreased expression of myosin heavy chain 1 (MHC1) during the unloading period. The expression of TRPC1 remained low at the initial phase of reloading and increased significantly at the late phase of reloading. The results indicate the dynamic expression of TRPC1 upon unloading-reloading process and implicate the role of TRPC1 on mechanical reloading. (2) Manipulation of TRPC1 expression using siRNA in weight-bearing soleus muscles led to a significant reduction in muscle mass and myofiber CSA. More importantly, suppressing the recovery of TRPC1 expression during the reloading process with siRNA injection impairs the recovery of the slow MHC1 profile, suggesting that TRPC1 plays a regulatory role in muscle regrowth following an atrophy-inducing event. (3) Given that previous studies have reported the involvement of TRPC subunits in calcineurin (CaN) - nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFAT) activation in skeletal and cardiac muscles, we showed that inhibition of CaN resulted in decreased TRPC1 expression, consequently impeding muscle regrowth. Here, we propose that a novel CaN-TRPC1 relationship exists that plays an important role in the process of muscle regrowth.

563512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
563512.value: The study of the regulation of TRPC1 in vivo has rarely been reported; most studies are largely reports of in vitro phenomena. In this study, we employ the hindlimb unloading and reloading model to examine the involvement of TRPC1 in the regulation of muscle atrophy and regrowth, respectively. We establish the physiological relevance of the concept that in vivo manipulation of TRPC1 could interfere with muscle regrowth processes following an atrophy-inducing event. The identification of this regulatory role is significant and facilitates a new focus on potential therapeutic interventions targeting TRPC1 or its downstream or upstream pathways to promote muscle regeneration.

563512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
563512.value: Decreased mechanical loading results in skeletal muscle atrophy. The canonical transient receptor potential type 1 (TRPC1) protein is implicated in the process. The study of the regulation of TRPC1 in vivo has rarely been reported. Here we employ the mouse hindlimb unloading and reloading model to examine the involvement of TRPC1 in the regulation of muscle atrophy and regrowth respectively. We establish the physiological relevance of the concept that manipulation of TRPC1 could interfere with muscle regrowth processes following an atrophy-inducing event. Specifically we show that suppressing TRPC1 expression during reloading impairs the recovery of the muscle mass and slow myosin heavy chain I profile. Calcineurin appears to be part of the signaling pathway involved in the regulation of TRPC1 expression during muscle regrowth. These results provide new insights regarding the function of TRPC1; interventions targeting TRPC1 or its downstream or upstream pathways could be useful to promote muscle regeneration.

563712.label: Realisation of objectives
563712.value: Objective 1: 20% achieved We applied to delete Objective 1 in late December 2015 and the request was approved in early January 2016. An amount of ~HK$194,000 was committed in late 2014 for the appointment of a Research Associate for 12 months (2015) for processing the samples for genotyping. When we first contacted the company Illumina to get the most updated price of the GoldenGate chips as originally proposed, we were informed that the product (GoldenGate chips) had already been discontinued. The available similar genotyping chips were the Custom Infinium iSelect HD BeadChips from the same company (Illumina). The custom Infinium iSelect HD BeadChips have a completely different cost structures. First, the marker density is at least 3,072 (and can be up to about one million) per sample. Second, the minimum order is 1,152 samples (instead of multiples of 94 for GoldenGate chips). With a combination of the minimum number of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and the minimum number of samples genotyped, the minimum genotyping cost is about HK$ 1 million. However, the funded amount is only HK$750,000 (compared to the original requested amount of HK$3,049,000). At that time, the “usable” fund was less than HK$600,000. Therefore, we could not even afford to employ a part-time qualified optometrist to recruit new subjects for the study as indicated in Objective 1. Therefore, a request was made to remove Objective 1 and it was approved by the relevant panel. As such, we would use our existing collection of 1,608 samples (908 cases and 700 controls). (Details were also given in annual progress reports for 2014 and 2015). Objective 2: 100% As indicated in the annual progress report for 2013 and suggested by our collaborators, we combined our pilot GWAS (whole genome association study) data (~100 cases of high myopia and ~100 controls without myopia) with another GWAS data for ~2,000 Chinese control subjects (without myopia) that we obtained from our collaborator Prof. Saw (Singapore). Imputation was performed with 1000 Genomes data as the reference panel. This step was very time-consuming and took us a long time to complete because of the tremendous computing time involved. Note that this was done without the appointment of any research assistant/associate (in 2013 and 2014) in order to save the funding for subsequent genotyping work. After imputation, the two GWAS data were combined and re-analysed for genetic association based on single-marker analysis. Pathway analysis of genes with significant SNPs was carried out using MetaCore, and top 3 networks/pathways with the smallest p values were selected. Tagging SNPs were also selected from the genes in these significant networks/pathways. Of the 142 genes in these significant networks/pathways, 110 genes are expressed in the eye according to the information in the UniGene database. To follow up the 110 genes, HapMap Chinese tagging SNPs for these genes were extracted using linkage disequilibrium (LD) threshold of r2 >= 0.8 and minor allele frequency (MAF) of >0.2. The total number of SNPs to be genotyped was ~6,500. Since the then available genotyping chips from Illumina was Custom Infinium iSelect BeadChips and their cost structures were completely different those of the phased-out GoldenGate chips (see above), the minimum genotyping cost was estimated to be ~HK$ 1 million. This means that our usable fund (~HK$600,000) was not enough to even call for a tender for the genotyping service. Although we once thought we had to give up the study because of this unexpected financial constraint, we finally sorted out this problem. Our internal collaborator (Prof. Maurice Yap) was willing to contribute some funds (from his Endowed Professorship funding) for the deficit and the genotyping cost for the follow-up genotyping. To take advantage of the cost of the Infinium iSelect BeadChips, we combined the SNPs for this study and those for another GRF-funded study, we ordered enough iSelect BeadChips for 1,152 samples for ~6,500 SNPs for this study (plus ~2,700 SNPs for another study). Once the minimum number of SNPs (3,072 SNPs) is reached, any further increase in the number of SNPs to be added was charged a very low cost for every 100 SNPs added. Finally, raw genotype data were obtained for ~5,600 SNPs for this study. After QC and data clean-up, good genotype data were obtained for ~5,150 SNPs. In total, 49 SNPs located in 15 genes gave p values <0.01. Of these 15 genes, 7 were found in the top first network/pathway, 3 in top second network/pathway, and 5 in top third network/pathway from the initial pathway analysis of the pilot GWAS data. These SNPs were followed by genotyping the remaining 457 samples of our collection (217 cases of high myopia and 240 controls). It is interesting to note that Objective 2 was a very critical bottleneck of the whole study in terms of budget and time. Objective 3: 100% achieved. The remaining 457 samples were genotyped for 49 SNPs using the MassARRAY platform based on the mass spectrometry of single-base extended primers. After data clean-up, 23 SNPs were found to be associated with high myopia (p<0.001) upon combined analysis of the whole sample set (1,608 samples). We asked our collaborators to validate our results with their own samples. Objective 4: 100% achieved. We asked our collaborators to genotype their samples (~5,000) for these 23 significant SNPs. Of these, 10 were successfully replicated with our collaborators’ samples. Objective 5: 100% achieved. We used public databases (ENCODE, SNP Function Prediction, RegulomeDB, HaploReg, etc) to explore the potential functions of the replicated SNPs. The consistent features are that these SNPs are located in open chromatin regions. However, we are aware of the limitation of this bioinformatic annotation because most annotation data are derived from non-ocular cell lines. In fact, there are only 2 ocular cell lines included in the ENCODE study.

563712.label: Major findings and research outcome
563712.value: (1) During the initial bottleneck of the study, we used our existing sample collection to replicate a Japanese study of high myopia. This study identified a novel myopia gene WNTB7B. The findings were published in Nature Communications in 2015 (see Part C for details). (2) We presented our pathway analysis study in the 15th International Myopia Conference in Wenzhou, China, in 2015 (see Part C for details). (3) We reviewed the basic steps in pathway analysis of GWAS and omics data and published the summary as a review in Biochimica et Biophysica acta in 2017 (see Part C for details). (4) Based on our pilot GWAS data together with other published GWAS data, we studied SNPs in the KCNQ5 gene and published the replication results in BioMed Research International in 2017 (see Part C for details). (5) With great effort and difficulties (financial and time), we successfully applied the principle of pathway analysis to our pilot GWAS data and those from one of our collaborator and identified SNPs in genes involved in top three networks/pathways. We genotyped these SNPs (~5,600) with high-throughput custom-made genotyping assays (Custom Infinium iSelect BeadChips). Of these, ~5,150 SNPs gave good genotype data and 49 SNPs showed significant association with high myopia with a p value of less than 0.001. These 49 initially significant SNPs were followed up by genotyping the remaining samples of our sample collection. Combined analysis of these 49 novel SNPs for the whole sample collection (1,608 samples) showed that 23 SNPs were significantly associated with high myopia at p<0.001 (significant even after correction for multiple testing). Ten of these SNPs were successfully replicated by our collaborators with independent sample sets. A manuscript reporting these major findings is now under preparation.

563712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
563712.value: We propose to follow up this study by identifying the putative causal SNPs in the regions concerned with functional studies. In vitro functional studies should be the first step in this direction. A few relevant cell lines should be used to provide robust results. Instead of the conventional reporter gene assay, we propose to use the recently reported massively parallel report assay (MPRA) to investigate the putative functional effects of a large number of putative causal variants in a single study. MPRA makes use of two advancements in technologies: next-generation sequencing and ability to synthesise a large complex pool of oligos each with a length of up to ~250 bases (the limit of current technology). The new genome editing technique can also be used to confirm the functional differences of the two alleles of a SNP of special interest. On the other hand, in vivo functional studies can be later undertaken using the zebrafish model. We have already purchased the required special instruments for measuring the axial length and refractive errors of zebrafish eyeball.

563712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
563712.value: Myopia is said to be present if distant objects are focused in front of, rather than on, the retina. Recent studies have identified many putative genes involved in the development of myopia in humans. One hurdle of these kinds of studies is the large number of samples (tens and hundreds of thousand) required to give reliable results. In this study, we applied the principle of pathway analysis to our pilot genome-wide association studies to overcome this hurdle. We have successfully used our pilot data to suggest ~5,600 genetic markers (the so-called single nucleotide polymorphisms or SNPs). Genotyping of these suggested SNPs and data analysis identified 49 novel SNPs to be significant in myopia development. Follow-up of these SNPs confirmed that 23 SNPs are associated with the development of high myopia. Our collaborators confirmed 10 of these SNPs with their own samples. Functional studies are required to investigate the potential functions of the associated SNPs.

600112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600112.value: 顆粒物（氣溶膠）的空氣污染已成為世界各地的主要環境問題，包括香港等主要城市。硫酸在新的粒子形成和大氣氣溶膠的酸性有重要的角色。最近的實地觀測和理論計算表明，除了氨，胺在中和硫酸氣溶膠和新粒子形成也可以起到至關重要的作用。另外，在我們最近實驗研究發現，胺可以在氣溶膠粒子取代氨離子。在一般情況下，大氣濃度的胺可能比氨低1-3個數量級 ; 然而，較高的鹼度（較高的pKa值）和較低的氣壓使胺可能與氨在中和酸性氣溶膠反應中構成競爭。胺能形成有機銨鹽，所以對形成細懸浮微粒，霧和雲滴作出相當貢獻。然而，當前對胺的氣體-粒子轉換的知識是相當有限的。特別是，關於胺的熱力學性質的文獻是有限的，尤其是在那些過飽和的液滴。在擬議的研究中，我們將採用電動平衡天秤（EDB），和用拉曼光譜儀來測量懸浮微粒在中和反應中的質量變化和化學變化。實驗數據將被收集用作完善現有的氣溶膠熱力學模型。

600112.label: Realisation of objectives
600112.value: Both objectives has been achieved to the full extent. Modifications of the experimental approach were made to the initially proposed method, due to the very unique features of amines as briefly outlined here: 1. Amine stickiness Amines possess a strong tendency to adsorb to surfaces such as glass walls, stainless steel fittings, instrument inlets e.g in Gas chromatography measurements. For our experiment this had a significant influence on the gas phase conditions, where a stable DMA (dimethyl amine)(g)–to-NH3(g) ratio had to be ensured over the entire reaction period (about 40h). This means generation of gas concentrations had to be constant. This restraint made the usage of the Electro dynamic balance (EDB) impossible, as for that the flow has to be stopped for each read out point. A flow cell using deposited particles was used instead. 2. Aminium sulfates- protic ionic liquid formation – impacting salt stability In the work under this grant we found that secondary and tertiary alkyl- aminium sulfates form room temperature protic ionic liquids at low relative humidity, which means that they will not crystallize nor form any solid structure (at room temperature) (Chan and Chan, 2013). These liquids possess strong inter molecular bonds, that lead to the formation of non stoichiometric mixtures of ions and a portion of free amine molecules in these liquids, that tend to evaporate to the gas phase, not only from the pure ion mixture but also from their moderately concentrated aqueous solutions e.g. at 50% RH. This implied that any drying processes are impossible without amine loss. Also the sampling process was customized to prevent / minimize evaporative losses during sampling. 3. Overlapping Raman bands of NH3 and Amine Overlapping Raman bands of NH3 and Amine made it impossible to get a sufficient accuracy of amine-to- ammonia ratios calculated based on peak intensity or peak areas. Therefore the setup had to be changed to allow an accurate determination of each amine and ammonia. We chose to use Ion chromatography, as in recent most reliably used method for simultaneous amines and ammonia detection. Experimental techniques Generation and detection of mixed ammonia and DMA gas High-purity N2 from a cylinder was used as carrier gas and directed through a H2O (18.2 mΩ) gas wash bottle and recombined with dry N2 at a controlled ratio to adjust the desired RH 10% or 50%. The humidified carrier flow was then split into two electronic mass flow controllers (MKS) á 1000±10 cm3min-1 (adjusted for each RH) and introduced into a permeation device holder. The water bath controlled tube holders were equipped with permeation tubes of either NH3 (VICI Metronics Dynacal, NH3, 2653±127 ng min-1) or DMA (DMA, 3423±288 ng min-1; DMA, 555±62 ng min-1) and a thermo couple (k-type thermocouple sensor and data logger, CENTER 309, Centertek) to control the temperature at 293.2±0.2 K. The permeation rate of the tube was quantified by regularly weighing the permeation tubes followed by at least 3h of re-conditioning to allow both gases to re-equilibrate before next experimental set was started. Combination of the NH3 (1.9ppm) with the DMA flows of either 0.9 or 0.15 ppm resulted in molDMA(g)/molNH3(g) of of 0.07 and 0.46 at 10% RH, as well as 0.07 and 0.49 at 50% RH. Single gas flows were generated by by-passing permeation tube and mixing the wanted gas stream with 1000 cm3min-1 humidified N2. The stability of the generated gas mixtures confirmed with an Ion-Molecule Reaction mass spectrometer (IMR-MS, AirSense, V&F Analyse-und Messtechnik GmbH). Gas flows from both permeation device holders were mixed and split equally into 4 flow cells with each about 500 cm3min-1. The environment inside the custom-made teflon cells was continuously monitored by an inserted temperature and humidity sensor (Sensirion EK-H4, SHT21 Sensor), possessing a temperature of 296±1.0 K and a relative humidity of 10±2% RH and 50±3% RH. For each new data set the tubings valves and fittings was cleaned and dried and conditioned for about 12 h to coat the tubing and cell walls and minimize wall loss during experiments. A second system of humidified high purity N2 at identical RH was prepared for particle conditioning. Particle generation A stock solution was prepared from concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4, 97 wt%, Acros Organics, titrated against standardized NaOH) mixed with ultrapure water (18.2 mΩ) to yield a solution of 30 wt% H2SO4. A few milliliter of the solution were inserted into a piezoelectric particle generator (MicroFab Tech., Inc.). 2000±100 droplets of 60 μm diameter were deposited on a hydrophobic film (FEP Teflon membranes, YSI Inc.). The film was then inserted to a clean stainless steel cell, connected to a stream of humidified high purity N2 (~1000 cm3min-1) to equilibrate for 45 min. The sample films were subsequently transferred into the Teflon reaction cells and immediately connected to the outlet of the gas generation system. RH conditioning and transfer of films were done inside an inflatable glove bag (GLOVEBAG, Glas Col®) to prevent the samples from being exposed to room RH. Particle analysis After the respective sampling time the cell was opened, the film was taken out and submerged into ~12 mL ultrapure water H2O, well mixed and analyzed for cation an anion content by IC (Metrohm, 881 compact IC Pro) as described in Sauerwein et al. (2015). It should be noted that IC yields total values for DMA species including aqueous DMA molecules and DMAH+ ions. The same holds true for NH3 and sulfate, where the distribution of total sulfate between HSO4- and SO42- anions (SO42-(tot) = molHSO4- + molSO42-) in the sapmle is unknown. Each teflon cell could be equipped with quartz windows to allow observations with a Raman microscope (Renishaw RM series). Raman Spectra and Optical images of the particles were recorded for selected data sets to identify the chemical composition and morphological changes as done in Yeung et al. (2009). Measurements of phase transition relative humidities The EDB and Raman Microscope have been used for this second objective. Aminium sulfate particles were generated from bulk mixtures of the corresponding amines and diluted sulfuric acid at a ﬁxed molar ratio of 2:1. The generated droplets were subsequently dried at <3% RH inside the EDB/Flowcell and examined for changes in optical properties, and Raman characteristics that indicate a phase change.

600112.label: Major findings and research outcome
600112.value: Objective 1 DMA and NH3 showed a similar effective uptake into concentrated H2SO4 followed by kinetically favored uptake of NH3 into still acidic droplets. After reaching electrically neutral composition DMA partially displaced NH4+ from liquid particles, leading to 2-4 times enhanced DMAH+ concentrations in the condensed phase. At low relative humidity (10%RH) the crystallization prevented further DMA uptake, while NH3 partitioning continued and eventually almost entirely displaced DMAH+ forming ammonium sulfate. At 50% RH DMA(g)–to-NH3(g) =0.5 and 0.1 yielded equilibrium molDMAH+/molNH4+ ratios of 1.9±0.3, and 0.2 ± 0.02 which indicates an enhancement of DMA of 2-4 times in the condensed phase compared to the gas phase. These equilibrium ratios were further compared with model calculations using the E-AIM Model parameterized with the here measured molDMAH+/molNH4+. For the experimental DMA-to-NH3 gas phase ratios 0.5 and 0.1 the model predicted 0.2 and 0.01. Hence in both cases the calculated gas phase ratios underestimated the molar amount of DMA relative to NH3 in the gas phase, yet, findings are qualitatively consistent. At 10%RH the molDMAH+/molNH4+ ratios equilibrated, regardless of the gas concentration of DMA, is at a value 0.02, showing that NH3 can completely displace DMAH+ from the crystalline particle, despite the presence of up to 0.9 ppm DMA. Calculations by E-AIM yielded gas phase DMA-to-NH3 molar ratios of 0.5, which is in good agreement with our measurements. It can be concluded that DMA is not competitive with NH3 for the available H+ in solid particles even if amine concentrations are significantly higher than in the ambient atmosphere. These results will be published in Meike Sauerwein’s thesis in August 2016 and related publication later. Objective 2 Methyl (MAH), ethyl (EAH), and diethyl ammonium sulfate particles solidiﬁed, while dimethyl, trimethyl and triethyl salts remained as droplets even at <3% RH. Upon dehumidification, the homogeneous MAS droplets turned into crystals as the RH decreased from 19% to 14%. Crystalline MAH particles exhibited sudden increases in full width half maximum of their sulfate peaks at deliquescence indicating a transition from crystalline to aqueous phase. During humidification, water started to condense onto MMAS particles at 32±2% RH. On the other hand, solid EAH sulfate (at above 10% RH) and DEAH sulfate (<3−30% RH) particles had substantially larger fwhm values, which were between those of the aqueous and crystalline particles (see results published in Chan and Chan 2013 and Chu et al. 2015)

600112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600112.value: With the same setup as established under objective one, concurrent heterogeneous reactions of other amines and ammonia or mix of different amines could be conducted. As found in this research, different alkyl-aminium sulfates possess significantly different phase transition and hygroscopic behavior (objective 2). Furthermore the partitioning behavior of amine relative to ammonia shows a strong dependence on particle phase state (objective 1). Further experiments with other amines that form crystalline or amorphous structures are useful to provide a clearer understanding of the ambient partitioning processes. With a slightly modified setup the dependence of the competitive uptake of amine and ammonia on particle size (as often observes in field measurements) could be studied. In a broader sense, the significantly higher hygroscopicity of amines can, once taken up into the particle, significantly influences the particle water content, which in turn can promote particle phase aqueous reaction of various chemicals. Further studies on the implications of the enhanced water content on particle size and thus on visibility would be warranted.

600112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600112.value: By taking one deep breath, a person inhales millions of tiny particles. Out of these million gases, only ammonia, and amines are alkaline, which means they can react and neutralize acidic particles, which we often know from the phenomena “acid rain”. Gas concentrations of ammonia are 1000 times higher than that of amines. However, in field measurements of atmospheric particles amines are often found in larger concentrations (relative to ammonia) than in the gas phase. Our study is the first to explored the simultaneous uptake of amines and ammonia and examine amines hygroscopicity. One of the major findings is that if the particle is liquid, amines rather than ammonia are favorably absorbed, while in solid particles the opposite is the case. Amine sulfates have stronger ability to adsorb water and to stay liquid even at low relative humidity, hence once amines are inside the particle, the formed aminium sulfate can enhance the water content and enhance chemical reactions in the particle and particle size. These properties can then influence the toxicity of particles as well as the visibility on days of high relative humidity.

600312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600312.value: The goal of the proposed experimental research is to study the effect of different types of noise on micromechanical devices. Micromechanical resonators are widely used as sensors and actuators in science and technology in applications ranging from inertial sensing to high sensitivity force and mass detection. Fluctuational phenomena are of paramount importance in mechanical oscillators. For instance, thermal motion limits the accuracy at which the resonance frequency of the oscillator can be measured. In another example, the presence of noise in a bistable nonlinear oscillator enables the system to occasionally overcome the activation barrier and switch from one metastable oscillation state into the other. Depending on the origin of fluctuations, different types of noise possess unique properties. In electrical circuits, for example, Johnson noise due to thermal motion of the charges is Gaussian distributed while shot noise that arises from the discreteness of the carriers is Poissonian. The emphasis of the proposed research will be placed on revealing the effect of non-Gaussian noise on micromechanical oscillators. Even though most fluctuation phenomena in conventional mechanical devices are of Gaussian nature, non-Gaussian noise plays an increasingly important role as devices continue to shrink in size. Due to the different mechanisms through which Gaussian noise and Poisson noise induce switching out of a metastable state, they are expected to yield different dependence of the switching rate on device parameters. By introducing Poisson noise into micromechanical torsional oscillators or doubly clamped beams that are strongly driven into bistability, we plan to identify different aspects of switching induced by Gaussian noise and Poisson noise. Furthermore, we propose to investigate the dephasing in an oscillator whose eigenfrequency is modulated by telegraph noise. Successful implementation of the proposed projects will not only verify the validity of various theoretical approaches, answer open questions and stimulate new theoretical research, but could also lead to new ways of detecting non-Gaussian noise and using them as a probe of the underlying physics of mesoscopic systems. The PI has extensive experience with fluctuational phenomena in micromechanical devices. In the past few years, his group performed an extensive investigation of the switching between coexisting vibration states induced by Gaussian noise on a nonlinear micromechanical torsional oscillator under strong periodic drive. The PI will work closely with Prof. Mark Dykman, a theorist at Michigan State University, to reveal novel behaviors of micromechanical resonators when they are coupled to non-Gaussian noise. 我們建議的實驗研究目標是為了研究不同種類噪聲對於微機械器件的影響。微機械諧振器在科學技術當中被廣泛用作傳感器和製動器，應用範圍從慣性傳感到力和質量的高精度測量。波動現像對於微機械諧振器來說非常重要。例如，熱運動限制了對諧振器共振頻率測量的準確性。又譬如，在雙穩態非線性諧振器中的噪聲會使系統偶然地克服活化能勢壘，並從一個亞穩定振動狀態轉移到另一個亞穩定振動狀態。 根據波動的不同來源，不同種類的噪聲有其獨特的性質。例如，由於電荷熱運動產生的約翰遜噪聲是符合高斯分佈的，然而由於載流子的電荷量化造成的短噪聲卻是符合泊松分佈的。我們建議研究的重要性在於它將揭示非高斯噪聲對微機械諧振器的影響。即使在常用的機械器件中，大部分波動現像具有高斯特性，但是由於器件的尺寸不斷地減小，非高斯噪聲扮演了越來越重要的角色。由於高斯噪聲和泊松噪聲激發系統跳出亞穩態的機制不同，系統在兩個亞穩態之間的轉換速率對於器件參數的依賴性也將不同。通過向被強力驅動至雙穩態的微機械扭轉諧振器或者兩端固定的懸樑器件引入泊松噪聲，我們計劃分辨出由高斯噪聲或泊松噪聲激發的跳轉的不同特徵。進一步，我們計劃用電報噪聲調製諧振器的本徵頻率，進而研究其失相現象。建議研究的成功實施不僅將驗證各種理論方法的正確性，回答尚未解決的問題，並促进新理論的研究，而且可以開創非高斯噪聲檢測的新方法，並利用它們探究介觀系統的潛在物理特性。 主要研究者在研究微機械諧振器的波動現象方面擁有豐富的經驗。在過去幾年裡，他的團隊對於在強力的周期性驅動下，非線性微機械扭轉諧振器由於高斯噪聲的激發而產生的在共存的振動狀態之間的跳轉做了大量的研究。主要研究者將會與來自密歇根州立大學的Mark Dykman教授緊密合作，揭示微機械諧振器與非高斯噪聲耦合時所產生的新現象。

600312.label: Realisation of objectives
600312.value: During the reporting period, we carried out an investigation of effects of non-Gaussian fluctuations in micromechanical resonators. We achieved the project objectives of investigating switching out of a metastable state induced by Poisson noise near a bifurcation point, exploring the effect of Poisson noise in oscillators with equal state population and investigating the fluctuation spectrum of an oscillator with frequency modulated by telegraph noise. Our findings were presented in four international conferences (1 invited talk and 3 contributed talks) and published in Physical Review B (two papers) and Physical Review E. The investigation of switching out of a metastable state induced by Poisson noise was carried out using a double-clamped polysilicon micro-beam. By passing an ac current through the beam in a perpendicular magnetic field of 5T, we excite motion of the beam in its in-plane fundamental mode by the Lorentz force. Motion of the beam generates an electromotive force that changes the transmitted ac power. When the noise force is negligible, the device responds as a simple damped harmonic oscillator. As the amplitude of the ac current increases, the mechanical resonance bends towards higher frequencies because of spring-hardening. Beyond certain critical excitation, two stable oscillation states with different amplitudes coexist between two bifurcation frequencies. Saddle node bifurcations occur at these bifurcation frequencies, where the number of stable oscillation states changes. In the parameter range of our operation, thermal motion of the beam does not lead to switchings between the coexisting oscillation states. Instead, electrical noise sources are used to generate random electrostatic forces between one of the sidegates and the beam in order to induce switchings. To excite the beam with Gaussian noise force, the Johnson noise from a 50 ohm resistor at room temperature is amplified and directly applied to the sidegate. Excitation with Poisson noise involves extra circuitry. First, the Gaussian noise voltage is connected to the trigger input of a pulse generator. Whenever the input voltage exceeds a threshold value, the pulse generator outputs a square pulse. The width of the pulse is chosen to be much smaller than the mean time between successive pulses (ranging from 30 ms to 200 ms). We verified that the time between successful pulses follows Poisson statistics. The pulse signal further controls an rf switch that only turns on when a pulse is present. When the switch is on, a sinusoidal waveform at the same frequency as the periodic magnetomotive force is transmitted to the sidegate. The output of the switch is a train of rf-modulated Poisson pulses of identical duration and height, with about 454 rf cycles in each pulse. Within a pulse, the phase of the periodic electrostatic force is chosen to be identical to the periodic magnetomotive drive. We checked that for all pulse heights and driving frequencies used in this paper, a single rf-pulse does not lead to switching. With the application of Gaussian or Poisson noise, the oscillator resides in the low-amplitude state for various durations before switching to the high amplitude state. After the switching, we reset the oscillator to the low-amplitude state. We repeat this procedure multiple times to build a histogram of the residence time, from which the switching rate can be inferred. To investigate the fluctuation spectrum of an oscillator with frequency modulated by telegraph noise, we fabricated a polycrystalline silicon plate with dimensions 200 um by 200 um by 3.5 um, suspended by two torsional rods at the middle of opposite edges. Two electrodes are located underneath the plate, one on each side of the torsional rods. A torque is generated on the top plate when a potential difference is applied between the plate and one of the electrodes. Angular displacement of the plate is detected capacitively by fixed electrodes underneath the plate. Changes in the resonant frequency are induced by a voltage applied to the left electrode, by the spring softening effect associated with the electrostatic force gradient. The voltage consists of telegraph noise switching back and forth between the two voltages V1 and V2, so that the eigenfrequency of the resonator jumps randomly between the two values omega_0 +- Delta/2. The telegraph voltage noise is generated by a J-K flipflop, triggered by Gaussian noise that is created by amplifying the Johnson noise of a 50 ohm resistor. Switching of the flipflop occurs when the Gaussian noise exceeds a threshold. The rate of switching W is therefore controlled by the Gaussian noise intensity. For all measurement presented here, W is chosen to be much smaller than the eigenfrequency. We checked that the time intervals between switching of the flipflop are random and obey Poisson statistics. The complex vibration amplitude of the plate is recorded using a lock-in amplifier, whose output X and Y are used to construct the complex vibrational amplitude u = X + iY. To explore the effect of Poisson noise in oscillators with equal state population, a similar torsional resonator is driven into parametric resonance, by modulating the spring constant at close to twice the eigenfrequency. When the modulation is sufficiently strong, there emerges two oscillation states with the same amplitude but opposite phase. Under weak noise, the system switches back and forth between these two coexisting states. The occupation probabilities of these two states are identical. We apply Poisson noise and study how it breaks the symmetry in the state population. The problems encountered and solved include detecting the small vibrations of a micromechanical resonator, identifying frequency noise even when thermal noise of the resonator or the detector noise in the electronic circuit is large, and explaining why the scaling relationships for Poisson noise induced switching remains valid far from the bifurcation points.

600312.label: Major findings and research outcome
600312.value: The first finding is that Gaussian noise and Poisson noise induce switching out of the metastable state near a bifurcation point through qualitatively different mechanisms, as reported in Publication 1 in Part C. Near saddle-node bifurcations, the motion in the 2D phase space can be mapped onto that of a Brownian particle in a 1D potential of the form –x^3/3 + eta x, where eta is the system parameter that decreases to zero at the bifurcation point. For Gaussian noise, switching is induced when a large outburst of noise overcomes the deterministic force from the barrier. Since the barrier height scales as eta^(3/2), the switching rate is proportional to exp(-Q), with Qg proportional to eta^(3/2). For Poisson noise, provided that the pulse duration is much shorter than the relaxation time, each pulse translates the system by a fixed distance d_p in the 2D phase space. Since the separation between the metastable state and the saddle point is d_o = 2 eta^(1/2), the system can reach the saddle point if enough pulses occur during the relaxation time before the system relaxes back to the metastable state. Such probability can be obtained using Poisson’s distribution, yielding a switching exponent Qp that is proportional to eta^(1/2) with a logarithmic correction term. In our experiment, the measured critical exponents are 1.31 and 0.61 for Gaussian and Poisson noise respectively. Qp and Qg therefore exhibit different dependence on eta, indicating that the noise statistics affect the dependence of the switching rates on device parameters. The second finding is the effect of telegraph frequency noise on the spectrum of the resonator, as reported in Publication 2 in Part C. Here the eigenfrequency of the resonator fluctuates randomly between two values. When the spectrum is slightly broadened but is still well-fitted by the square root of a Lorentzian, it is not possible to separate the effects of frequency noise from damping by merely examining the width of the spectrum. We show that the frequency noise can be unambiguously identified in the averaged higher moments of the complex amplitude. Remarkably, this method of identifying frequency noise remains valid even when thermal noise of the resonator or the detector noise in the electronic circuit is large so that most conventional methods are no longer applicable. We also investigated the effect of Poisson noise in oscillators with equal state population, as described in the master thesis in Part C.

600312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600312.value: Our results represent the first step towards understanding the effect of non-Gaussian noise on micromechanical resonators. The research will be carried on to the next phase to investigate noise-induced spectral broadening in an underdamped micromechanical resonator, to explore noise-induced spectral narrowing in a zero-dispersion system, and to investigate the fluctuation spectrum of a nonlinear resonator under periodic drive in the presence of frequency noise.

600312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600312.value: The research project studied the effect of different types of noise on micromechanical devices. Micromechanical devices are small, movable structures created with integrated circuits technology. They are widely used as sensors and actuators in science and technology, from accelerometers to barcode scanners. Fluctuational phenomena are of paramount importance in mechanical oscillators. For instance, thermal motion limits the accuracy at which the resonance frequency of the oscillator can be measured. In another example, the presence of noise in a bistable nonlinear oscillator enables the system to occasionally overcome the activation barrier and switch from one metastable oscillation state into the other. Even though most fluctuation phenomena in conventional mechanical devices are of Gaussian nature, non-Gaussian noise plays an increasingly important role as devices continue to shrink in size. Due to the different mechanisms through which Gaussian noise and Poisson noise induce switching out of a metastable state, we find that they yield different dependence of the switching rate on device parameters. Furthermore, we investigated the dephasing in oscillators whose eigenfrequencies are modulated by telegraph noise. The projects hold promise in leading to new ways of detecting non-Gaussian noise and using them as a probe of the underlying physics of mesoscopic systems.

600512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600512.value: Why natural selection mostly favors sexual reproduction is a long-standing problem in evolutionary biology. One approach to studying the evolution of sex is to develop well-defined mathematical models to directly study the evolution of recombination rates under specific selection pressures. If nonzero recombination rates are selectively favored, then the theory suggests that sex should evolve under those or similar selection pressures. The most rigorous of these types of mathematical models consider a recombination-modifier locus linked to two or more linked fitness loci, with natural selection only acting directly on the fitness loci. In the simplest three-locus model, the particular alleles at the modifier locus determine the recombination rate between the pair of selected loci. Even though selection does not act directly on the modifier locus, it can act indirectly: modifier alleles that are more likely to be found with selectively favored fitness alleles will themselves be selectively favored. Determining whether higher or lower recombination will evolve requires calculation of the stability of an initial population equilibrium to the invasion of a new modifier allele. With multiple fitness loci undergoing both selection and recombination, the problem of determining stable equilibria can be both analytically and computationally intractable. For any progress to be made, the selection models should be made as simple as possible, yet contain sufficient biology to yield nontrivial results. Previously, I have developed such a model that I called the multi-locus, haploid-selection, symmetric-viability model, and a student and I have further studied the evolution of recombination rates in this model. Although we obtained several interesting results, the equilibrium solutions of this model seemed too simple to observe situations where increased recombination rates might be favored. The current proposal is to further generalize these selection models to add more complexity to the nonlinear bifurcations of the equilibrium solutions, so as to determine whether selection pressure for increased recombination rates can arise as a consequence of the nonlinearity of the model. 为什么自然选择会常常偏向与有性繁殖，这是长期以来一直在进化生物学中的一个难题。然而我们的着手点是在建立一个完整体系的生物模型上，通过施加一定的环境选择压力，来研究生物的基因重组所带来的进化现象。如果在自然选择中生物偏向于非零的基因重组率，那么理论显示生物应该在相应的自然选择压力下进化。 这些模型中最严谨的是考虑一个控制基因重组的变化子联系着两个或者以上个生存基因， 由仅自然选择来直接作用在生存基因。在这最简单的三个基因的模型里，那些特殊的控制这基因重组的等位基因直接决定两个生存基因之间的基因重组率。 即便自然选择不是直接作用在这个变化子上，但它可以间接作用。因为变化子如果带有选择优势的的生存基因的话，那它常常也会有选择优势。 决定基因重组的高低是否会导致生物进化，这需要让一个新的变化子的入侵，来研究一个初始的人口平衡态的稳定性。在多个生存基因同时自然选择和基因重组的情况，计算一个种群稳定态是非常困难，无论是解析上，还是数值上。生物模型应该构造尽量简单，但是包含足够的生物知识，能得出深奥的结论。 之前我已经研究了一种多基因，单倍体自然选择，对称的生存力的生物模型。我和一位学生进一步研究了一个模型在不同基因重组率的进化。尽管我们得到了许多有趣的结论，但是平衡态的结果看起来还是太简单以至于找不到提高基因重组率的选择优势的情况。现在的提案是进一步推广这个选择模型来增加更多的复杂性来得到非线性的平衡态的分叉。 我们将利用模型的非线性来寻找是否存在提高基因重组率的选择优势。

600512.label: Realisation of objectives
600512.value: Under haploid selection, the equilibrium and stability properties of a multi-locus, diallelic, two-niche Levene model was studied, given certain symmetry properties. This model always admits a fully polymorphic symmetric equilibrium, which may or may not be stable. We have carefully detailed how the symmetric equilibrium may become unstable and result in stable asymmetric equilibria. We have also studied how a recombination-modifier locus may evolve in this model. We show both analytically and numerically what happens when the starting equilibrium is symmetric, asymmetric or polymorphic. When the starting equilibrium is symmetric, modifier alleles that reduce recombination always invade. When the starting equilibrium is monomorphic, we show that a gap exists between the recombination rates of modifiers that can invade and the recombination rate that specifies the lower stability boundary of the monomorphic equilibrium. Similar, but weakened considerations also apply when the starting equilibrium is asymmetric. We have implemented computationally more complicated genetic models containing a larger number of alleles, and more than two niches with the hope that nonlinear effects might result in recombination-modifier alleles that evolve to increase recombination in the model, and then converge to an equilibrium value as occurs in nature. Unfortunately, we did not have much success with these more complicated models and the results of this study were not published.

600512.label: Major findings and research outcome
600512.value: A fast algorithm for computing multi-locus recombination was extended to include a recombination-modifier locus. This algorithm was used to investigate the evolution of recombination rates in multi-locus haploid selection models. The model was also generalised to include multiple alleles and multiple niches, and computations were performed to investigate the role played by recombination. It appears that selection always acts to reduce recombination in these models.

600512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600512.value: The algorithms and software developed can be used to study multi-locus recombination in other selection regimes. This may shed further light on the role played by recombination and sexual reproduction in nature.

600512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600512.value: During typical sexual reproduction, parental genes mix in a process called recombination and the offspring’s genetic makeup is a mixture of the parents’ genetics. What is the evolutionary purpose of recombination? One approach towards understanding sexual reproduction and recombination is to study the evolution of recombination within a well-defined mathematical model. We have constructed a relatively simple model that nevertheless demands intensive computation, and we hope that our research has shed some further light on why recombination might have evolved.
