600612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600612.value: In the final 110m hurdles race at the 2011 IAAF World Championships in Daegu, Korea, Dayron Robles hit and obstructed Xiang Liu with his right arm during the final two hurdles, and was eventually disqualified for the rule violation even though he finished first. The incident, although rare and dramatic, reflects the intensity of competition and the intra-competition correlation, as well as the degree of unpredictability in multi-entry competitions. Nowadays, multi-entry competitions are omnipresent in many social activities. Most of the sports in the Olympic games, including track and field, swimming, biking, gymnastics, etc., are multi-entry competitions. Horse racing, thoroughbred or harness, and greyhound racing are also multi-entry competitions. One distinct characteristic of multi-entry competition is that the final rank based on certain numbers, such as running/swimming time or evaluation scores by the judges, are of primary importance to competitors. In some standard, those finishing in the first few positions, e.g., gold, silver and bronze medalists, are rewarded entirely differently from the rest. There is a vast literature on horse races, a special form of multi-entry competition, in economic, financial and social studies. This is partly because, horse racing provides an ideal scenario to understand market behavior towards risk, such as, for example, the faverate/long-shot bias. This proposed research concentrates on the statistical modeling and analysis of multi-entry competitions. With the convenience of internet access and the broadcasting of many sensational sports events, relevant data are generated on a daily basis at an incredible speed on an astronomical scale. The analysis of multi-entry competitions calls for modern statistical models and methodologies. In view of the recent advances in statistical science and the fast-developing computing technology, it is time we develop cutting-edge statistical techniques specifically for analysis of such data. It is promising to find new statistical models and methods by taking advantage of the latest development in the survival analysis and econometrics that are relevant to multi-entry competitions, particularly those related with multivariate life time models. The results of this proposed research will provide state-of-the-art statistical tools to help practitioners identify the determinants of the outcomes and better understand the within-competition correlation in multi-entry competitions. 在2011年于韩国大邱举行的世界田径锦标赛男子110米栏比赛中，罗伯斯用他的右手臂击打和阻挠刘翔在最后两个障碍的比赛， 最终因违反规则而被取消资格，即使他第一个做参考。这一罕见而戏剧性的事件反映了当今比赛和竞争的激烈程度和内部相关性，以及一定程度上多者竞赛的不可预测性。如今，多者竞赛在我们的日常生活中是常见的。大多数奥运会项目，包括田径，游泳，骑自行车和体操等，都是多人比赛。 赛马，纯种或马具，及赛狗比赛也是。多者竞赛的一个显着特点是根据数字，如运行时间/游泳或裁判评分，来排定的座次是竞争者最为关注的赛果。在一些标准下，那些排在前几位的，如 金，银，铜牌得主，奖励完全与后几位是完全不同的。 在经济，财务和社会的研究方面有大量关于多者竞争的文献，其中包括赛马。这部分是因为，赛马提供了一个理想的情况下市场对风险的理解和行为， 如热门冷漠的偏差。本研究着重于多者竞赛的统计建模和分析。 随着互联网接入和许多体育赛事的轰动性转播的便利性，相关数据每天以惊人的速度和天文数字的量级产生。对多者竞赛的分析需要现代的统计模型和方法。由于统计科学和快速发展的计算技术的最新进展，现在是发现和应用最先进的和专为分析 这样的数据的统计技术的最佳时机。通过利用多相关的生存分析和计量经济学的最新发展，特别多元生存分析模型的最新结果，我们有希望找到新的统计模型和方法。这项研究将提供最先进的统计工具，以帮助实践者识别成因和更好地理解多者竞赛的内部相关性。

600612.label: Realisation of objectives
600612.value: The most important time-to-event model, particularly suitable for multi-entry competition, is the multivariate transformation model. The univariate version of the model encompasses the Cox proportional hazards model and the accelerated failure time model that are popular in survival analysis of time-to-events. More generally, the transformation function can be assumed unknown, leading to the generalized accelerated failure time model that are widely used in econometrics. The maximum rank correlation estimation is common in data analysis using general transformation model. With marginal transformation model, an estimation accounting for the dependence of the multivariate responses is much desired. The conventional approach of general estimating equation cannot be directly applied, as the objective function is not differentiable and not even continuous. We have proposed and analyzed three basic estimating methods to optimally combine the maximum rank correlation estimators based on each marginal model, jointly considering all component information as well as cross component comparison effect. In addition, we considered the versions under prior information. A random weighting re-sampling method is employed to estimate the asymptotic covariance. We derived asymptotic properties for all proposed procedures. Semiparametric transformation models with random effects are useful in analyzing multivariate time-to-event data. With the error and random effect distributions specified, it has been proved in the literature that the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimators (NPMLE) is semiparametric efficient. We considered a more general class of transformation models with random effects, under which an unknown monotonic transformation of the response is linearly related to the covariates and the random effects with unspecified error and random effect distributions. This class of models is broad enough to include many popular models and allows various random effect distributions. We proposed an estimator based on the maximum rank correlation, which does not rely on any further model assumption except for a mild condition of the symmetry of the random effect distribution. We established large sample theory including proving the consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed estimator. A random weighting resampling scheme is employed for inference. Moreover, the proposed method can be easily extended to handle censored data and clustered data. We conducted large scale numerical work to examine the finite sample properties of the proposed methods. Supportive evidence had been found in extensive simulation studies We applied our methodology to analysis of real data, including Framingham cholesterol data, and gene expression profile data of the data of isoprenoid biosynthesis in Arabidopsis thaliana. Even though the data appear not be multi-entry competition at first glance, they involve time-to-events and are fit for the analysis by our proposed methods. In summary, we find that generalized accelerated failure time model is among the best and most general statistical model for analysis of multi-entry competitions, largely because it has minimum model assumption. Our proposed approaches also account for within-cluster correlation. Their effectiveness had been illustrated using simulation examples and real data. The research results are summarized in Chen, et al. (2016a), Chen, et al. (2016b) and Wang, et al. (2016).

600612.label: Major findings and research outcome
600612.value: We find that the multivariate generalized accelerated failure time model is among the best for data analysis of time-to-event data. The maximum rank correlation approach is robust. We proposed several different methods to analyze multivariate generalized accelerated failure time model and account for within group correlation. We also find that a random effect transformation model can be quite helpful. Many unknown factors that may affect the outcome of competitions can be explained away by random effects. We proposed a robust rank estimation method for this model and provided evaluation both theoretically and numerically. The research results are summarized in three papers, Wang, et al. (2016) and Chen, et al. (2016a) and Chen, et al. (2016b). The three papers are being under review or being accepted for publication in statistical journals.

600612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600612.value: During the past few years of research, we realized that the multivariate generalized accelerated failure time model is among the best for analyzing time-to-event data. The main reason is that this is the most flexible model, compared with other popular statistical models, such as Cox's model, accelerated failure time model or linear model. Currently many large data of sizes greater than tens or even hundreds of gigabytes could be available, by web-crawling. We plan to obtain some of these data sets and apply the estimation and inference methods we found in this project. We hope that this research could eventually lead to new scientific findings in real data analysis.

600612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600612.value: In multi-entry competitions, the observed final results are scores such as time-to-finish. They can be viewed as multivariate time-to-event data, where each variable is the time-to-finish for an individual in the competition. In analysis of multivariate time-to-event data, there exist many popular statistical models, such as Cox's model or log-transformed linear model. We find that a more general model that includes these two models are more appropriate in analysis of multivariate time-to-event data. One of the most important problems here is how to properly account for the within-competition dependence, which is usually called within-cluster or within-group correlation in statistical terminology. We proposed several approaches to combine marginal estimation methods in order to obtain more accurate and more robust estimation. We also found that this research is applicable to many types of multivariate data that arise in social science and biological science.

600712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600712.value: Amphidinolactone B is a novel 26-membered macrolide produced by a marine dinoflagellate. Only 80 microgram sample of the macrolide has been obtained, accounting for 0.000011% yield by wet weight of the harvested cells of the cultured dinoflagellate. The macrolide exhibits cytotoxicity against two cancer cell lines, L1210 murine leukemia cells and human epidermoid carcinoma KB cells, giving IC50 values of 3.3 and 5.3 microgram/mL, respectively. These results are very preliminary and much work is needed to understand its mechanism of action and to formulate a structure–activity relationship. The molecular structure of amphidinolactone B as elucidated by modern instrumentation seems similar to the related 26-membered amphidinolide B congeners. Moreover, it possesses an additional unique tetrahydrofuran ring at the C15–C18 positions along with a “but-2-en-1,4-diol” subunit at the C6–C9 positions. This structural profile makes amphidinolactone B a much more complex and challenging molecular target for chemical synthesis. Due to the extremely limited available sample, the C6 configuration of amphidinolactone B could not be elucidated. Any answer to the structural problem would rely on total chemical synthesis, which is a reliable and proven technology not only for accessing amphidinolactone B but also its structural analogues. Authentic samples of two C6 epimers (with opposite spatial orientation of the C6-methyl group) are required for determination of the C6 configuration in the natural form of the macrolide. In addition, the characteristic 2,2,3,5-tetrasubstituted tetrahydrofuran subunit offers an opportunity for the development of new and efficient synthetic methodologies of general application value. The unsolved structural mystery and the promising cytotoxicity of amphidinolactone B justify a rigorous total synthesis program. This proposed study carries the following objectives: (a) to develop a cyclization process for constructing the unique 2,2,3,5-tetrasubstituted tetrahydrofuran subunit with the defined stereochemistry; (b) to establish a flexible and modular total synthesis scheme for amphidinolactone B via ring-closing metathesis (RCM) for assembling the 26-membered macrolactone skeleton; (c) to determine the C6 configuration by synthesis of two C6 epimers of amphidinolactone B; and if manpower and resource allow, (d) to synthesize structural analogues of amphidinolactone B for cytotoxicity screening. Successful results from this study should contribute new chemistry knowledge and would offer opportunities for further study of the structure–activity relationship and mechanism of action of amphidinolactone B. 由海洋腰鞭毛蟲産生的amphidinolactone B 是一種新型的26元大環內酯，僅分離到80微克樣本，以從培養的腰鞭毛蟲採集到的細胞濕重計算，其得率為0.000011％。該大環內酯對L1210鼠科白血病細胞及人類表皮状癌KB細胞呈現毒性，IC50值分別為3.3和5.3微克/毫昇。這些生物活性結果相當初淺，尚需進一步研究以便了解它的作用機理和建立搆傚關繫。Amphidinolactone B的分子結搆經由現代儀器鑑定，與相關的26元環amphidinolide B同繫物結搆相似。此外，它在C15–C18還含有獨特的四氫呋喃環及在C6–C9含有“丁-2-烯-1,4-二醇”亞結搆單元，這些結搆特點使得amphidinolactone B成為一個更復雜、更具挑戰性的化學合成目標分子。由于天然樣本烯少，amphidinolactone B在C6位置的搆型沒能確定，因此要求解其分子結搆問題的任何答案均需依賴化學全合成，這是一種可靠並且被證實的技術，不僅可用于amphidinolactone B的製備，還可用于合成結搆類似物。確定天然amphidinolactone B于C6上的搆型需要分別合成二個C6差嚮異搆體（C6甲基在空間的朝嚮相反）的標準樣本。另外，它特有的2,2,3,5-四取代四氫呋喃環亞結搆單元為化學家提供了一種機遇，來開發具普適應用價值的高傚新合成方法。尚未破解的結搆奧祕和很強的細胞毒性使得開展严謹、细致的amphidinolactone B的全合成計劃成為必要。本項目要實現以下幾個目標：（1） 發展一種環化過程用于搆築特有的、含有所需立體化學的2,2,3,5-四取代四氫呋喃環結搆單元；（2）建立一種基于閉環復分解反應、可變通的、及模塊化的全合成路綫用于合成amphidinolactone B；（3）合成amphidinolactone B的二個C6差嚮異搆體用于確定amphidinolactone B于C6上的搆型；如果人員和資源允許，還將開展（4）合成amphidinolactone B的結搆類似物用于細胞毒性的篩選。本項目的順利開展將産生新的化學知識，並有機會進一步開展amphidinolactone B的搆傚關繫和作用機理的研究。

600712.label: Realisation of objectives
600712.value: The structure of amphidinolactone B was proposed by Kobayashi and co-workers in 2007 but the absolute configuration at C6 was not assigned (Kobayashi, J. et al., J. Antibiot. 2007, 60, 376–379). Up to October 2016, no synthetic study on this 26-membered macrolide had been disclosed in the literature, except for a synthesis of the two diastereomeric C1–C7 acid fragments reported from our laboratory (Dai, W.-M. et al., ChemistrySelect 2016, 1022–1027) [See section 8, journal publication #1]. This project primarily aims to develop a total synthesis route toward accessing the two C6 diastereomers [(2R,6S,9S) and (2R,6R,9S)] of the macrolide and determining the absolute configuration at C6 of the naturally occurring product. As mentioned in objective 1, the formation of the 2,2,3,5-tetrasubstituted tetrahydrofuran (THF) subunit in a stereocontrol manner is unprecedented in the current literature and it is expected to be highly challenging to investigate this process in a complex and difficult-to-accessing macrolactone substrate. It was decided to establish a pentamodule assembly strategy to construct amphidinolactone B with the preformed 2,2,3,5-tetrasubstituted THF subunit along with four other fragments. Objective 1 has been fully achieved with successful synthesis of the two C6 diastereomers [(2R,6S,9S) and (2R,6R,9S)] of the proposed amphidinolactone B using the ring-closing metathesis (RCM) reaction as the key step to form the 26-membered core of the macrolide [See section 9, conference papers #3 and #4]. Objective 2 is to construct the 2,2,3,5-tetrasubstituted THF subunit via the acid-catalyzed hydroalkoxylation of the corresponding 1,3-dienyl alcohol. This task is highly challenging but has been successfully achieved through extensive optimization of the reaction conditions and a deep understanding of the reaction mechanism. From an initial product mixture of eight stereoisomers, the desired 2,2,3,5-tetrasubstituted THF subunit is now obtained in a 50% overall yield for two steps [See section 9, conference papers #1 and #2]. The structure of the synthesized THF fragment was assigned based on its NMR data. Efforts were made to grow suitable single crystals of the derivatives for X-ray crystal structural analysis but without success. Synthesis of the two diastereomers [(2R,6S) and (2R,6R)] of the C1–C7 acid fragment with opposite configuration at C6 [objective 3] has been fully achieved and the results have been published [See section 8, journal publication #1]. With the 2,2,3,5-tetrasubstituted THF fragment (synthesized in objective 2), the two C6 diastereomers of the C1–C7 acid fragment (synthesized in objective 3), and three other fragments in hand, total synthesis of the proposed structure of amphidinolactone B has been successfully accomplished after extensive optimization of the reaction conditions for the RCM reaction to construct the (7E)-ene-6,9-diol subunit [See section 9, conference papers #3 and #4]. However, the NMR data of the synthesized (2R,6S,9S)- and (2R,6R,9S)-amphidinolactone B do not match those reported for the natural product, implying that the proposed structure of amphidinolactone B by Kobayashi and co-workers (Kobayashi, J. et al., J. Antibiot. 2007, 60, 376–379) might be incorrect. The (2R,6R,9S)-stereomer seems close to the natural amphidinolactone B, except for a > 1 ppm deviation for the 13C NMR chemical shift of the C27-methyl group. This indicates that the absolute configuration assigned for C2 might be (2S) instead of (2R). Due to this unexpected finding, it was decided to synthesize extra diastereomers [(2S,6S,9S) and (2S,6R,9S)] of amphidinolactone B other than the two originally planned (2R,6S,9S)- and (2R,6R,9S)-stereomers. By following the analogous approach established in objective 3, the (2S,6R)-isomer of the C1–C7 acid fragment was synthesized by a new post-graduate student after a lengthy period of training. At the same time, the synthesis of the 2,2,3,5-tetrasubstituted THF subunit described in objective 2 was repeated to provide the requisite materials for the synthesis of the extra diastereomers. The unexpected synthesis of the (2S,6S,9S)- and (2S,6R,9S)-stereomers of amphidinolactone B is time-consuming and very demanding on manpower, and the synthetic work is still in progress. As the consequence of the above described new experimental work, synthesis of the “simpler” compounds stated in objective #4 for a structure–activity study in objective #5 could not be fully pursued due to shortage of manpower.

600712.label: Major findings and research outcome
600712.value: One of the major findings is the synthesis of the 2,2,3,5-tetrasubstituted THF fragment via the acid-catalyzed hydroalkoxylation of the 1,3-dienyl alcohol. Three stereogenic elements of the product are involved in this process: the C15 and C16 stereogenic centers and the C13–C14 double bond configuration. The use of a nucleophilic species in the reaction is critically important in suppressing the epimerization of the allylic (C16) stereogenic center, resulting in the formation of fewer stereomers of the products [See section 9, conference papers #1 and #2]. Another major finding is associated with the fragment coupling strategy to assemble the C13–C26 advanced intermediate. An acetylene molecule (C20–C21) was used to connect the C13–C19 THF fragment and the C22–C26 aldehyde fragment through lithium acetylide alkylation and addition reactions, respectively. This is a conceptually different approach from the reported method used for the synthesis of amphidinolide B, G, and H congeners. Subsequently, the resultant C20–C22 propargylic alcohol moiety smoothly undergoes the gold-catalyzed Meyer–Schuster rearrangement under the optimized conditions to form the 21-en-20-one moiety, which is chemo- and stereo-selectively converted into the 21,22-diol via Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation in the presence of the C13–C14 vinyl iodide [See section 9, conference papers #3 and #4]. The third major finding is the newly established RCM conditions for the construction of the (7E)-ene-6,9-diol, since no desired cyclization product could be detected under the usual conditions using Grubbs’ II as the catalyst. Our protocol provides an alternative tool for the assembly of similar functionalized subunit in complex molecules [See section 9, conference papers #3 and #4]. The final major finding is that the proposed structure of amphidinolactone B is incorrect, as proven by our two synthesized (2R,6S,9S)- and (2R,6R,9S)-stereomers. The results of this project indicated that, along with many other known cases, structural assignment based on NMR methods is not always reliable and chemical synthesis remains a powerful tool in natural product research and the development of pharmaceutical products.

600712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600712.value: The immediate adoption of the established total synthesis strategy is for the total synthesis of the (2S,6S,9S) and (2S,6R,9S)-stereomers of amphidinolactone B and the work is in progress. There is a possibility that other stereomers of amphidinolactone B should be synthesized in order to finally determine the correct structure of amphidinolactone B. The acid-catalyzed hydroalkoxylation of 1,3-dienyl alcohols is a potentially useful method for the synthesis of highly functionalized THF compounds. Based on the collected optimization data and our understanding of the reaction mechanism, it is possible to establish an enantio- or diastereo-selective synthesis of THF compounds which are the common structural units in marine natural products. Since a heavy workload is needed, it may be developed into a new project in the future. The reaction sequence based on the lithium acetylide addition with an aldehyde, the gold-catalyzed Meyer–Schuster rearrangement of the propargylic alcohol, and the Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation of the conjugate enone is an efficient synthetic method enabling concomitant fragment coupling and functionalization. It is possible to use this reaction sequence for a new total synthesis of amphidinolide B, H, and G congeners.

600712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600712.value: Marine microorganisms are known to produce a variety of molecules with different shapes and functionalized local structures. These structural features enable the molecules to deliver biomedical properties, such as killing cancer cells. It is obvious that the determination of a molecular structure is the very first step for investigating its properties and potential applications. This project aims to determine the structure of a marine-derived complex molecule called as amphidinolactone B. Since the originally proposed structure is not complete due to a limited amount of the molecule from nature and the inability of the modern instruments to conduct reliable structural analysis, a chemical synthesis approach has been established during this project. Two possible structures of the molecule have been synthesized through an elegant combination of different chemical reactions but they failed to match the naturally occurring substance, suggesting that the proposed structure is incorrect. The results of this project indicate that, along with many other known cases, structural assignment based on modern instrumental methods is not always reliable and chemical synthesis remains a powerful tool in natural product research and the development of pharmaceutical products. The findings from this project suggest other possible structures of amphidinolactone B for further chemical synthesis.

600812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
600812.value: Cyclic codes form a subclass of linear error-correcting codes, and have real-world applications in broadcast systems such as DVB and ATSC; computer applications such as RAID 6 systems; CDMA communication systems and deep-space communication; consumer electronics such as CDs, DVDs, Blu-ray Discs; and cryptography. Though the error correcting capability of cyclic codes may not be as good as some other linear codes in general, cyclic codes have efficient encoding and decoding algorithms. Cyclic codes are also a subject of mathematics and are related to a number of mathematical areas such as algebra, algebraic function fields, algebraic geometry, algebraic number theory, association schemes, combinatorial designs, finite geometries, finite fields, number theory, and semifields. There are two basic approaches to the description and construction of cyclic codes. One is the generator matrix approach. The other approach is based on the generator polynomial. Both approaches have advantages and disadvantages over each other. Most of the cyclic codes in the literature are given in terms of the generator matrix or generator polynomial. Many cyclic codes with good parameters were found with the two approaches. However, the two approaches have limitations in searching for cyclic codes with good parameters and proving properties of cyclic codes. The objective of this project is to investigate another approach to studying cyclic codes -- the q-polynomial approach. This approach will allow us to examine known classes of cyclic codes in a new light, and bring new classes of cyclic codes with desirable parameters. The outcome of this project is expected to contribute to not only the theory of error correcting codes but also their applications in engineering. 循环码是线性码的一个子类，而且被用在许多实用系统中。在广播系统中循环码用在数字图像广播ATSC标准中。在计算机应用方面循环码用在RAID6系统中。循环码也用在码分多址通信系统，深空通信，密码系统，和消费电子产品（例如，CDs, DVDs, Blu-ray Discs)。虽然循环码的纠错能力一般而言没有其它线性码好，但它们有更有效的编码和译码算法。 循环码也是数学的一个分支，并且与数学的一些其它领域紧密相关。例如，循环码与代数，代数函数域，代数几何，代数数论，结合方案，组合设计，有限几何，有限域，数论和半域有密切联系。 处理循环码有两个基本方法，即生成矩阵法和生成多项式法。二者各有其优缺点。许多具有良好参数的循环码都是用这两种方法找到的。不过这两种方法在寻找好循环码和证明码的性质上有一定的局限性。 本项目的任务是探讨一个研究和处理循环码的新方法：q-多项式方法。我们将对已知的循环码用q-多项式方法描述和探讨，并用该新方法构造有良好参数的新循环码。预期本项目的研究成果对纠错码的理论和工程应用有一定贡献。

600812.value: All of the objectives of this project are achieved. We first established a q-polynomial approach to characterising all cyclic codes, and then employed it to study and analyse cyclic codes. With this approach, we proved some properties of cyclic codes. We also settled the weight distributions of some cyclic codes, and constructed some new cyclic codes. This is a big project, and we plan to have a follow-up of this project in the future.

600812.label: Major findings and research outcome
600812.value: A q-polynomial approach to all cyclic codes over finite fields has been developed. This new approach provides a new direction for the study of all cyclic codes over finite fields. With this new approach, new classes of cyclic codes are constructed. Some of the cyclic codes constructed in this project are optimal. In addition, the weight distributions of many classes of cyclic codes are determined in this project. New classes of zero-difference balanced functions are also developed. These functions have applications in coding theory and communication systems. Optimal codebooks are also constructed. This projected resulted in 13 journal papers, published in leading international journals such as "IEEE Trans. Information Theory", "IEEE Trans. Communications", "Designs, Codes and Cryptography", "Finite Fields and Their Applications", and "SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics".

600812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
600812.value: The q-polynomial approach has great potential for studying specific types of cyclic codes. We will employ this approach to analyse BCH codes in the future. It has also potential to study subspace codes, and we will look into this later at a proper time.

600812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
600812.value: Cyclic codes are widely employed in communication systems, data storage systems, and consumer electronic systems. It is therefore important to study cyclic codes. To this end, we wish to develop a new approach to the construction and analysis of all cyclic codes. This project presents a q-polynomial approach to all cyclic codes over finite fields. This approach enhances the theory of cyclic codes and gives a new way to construct and analyse cyclic codes. Many new classes of optimal cyclic codes are constructed. The weight distributions of a number of families of cyclic codes are settled. Optimal codebooks are constructed, and families of zero-difference balanced functions are found in this project. The research results of this project are published in leading international journals.

601212.label: Project Objectives
601212.value: To develop a signal-amplified electrochemical DNA detection based on isothermal circular strand displacement polymerization reaction. With a relatively simple target recycling mechanism, the realization of electrochemical real-time monitoring of the product of isothermal circular strand displacement polymerization reaction will not only result in a simple and sensitive DNA detection scheme, but also exhibit the compatibility of our peptide nucleic acid (PNA) displacement-based immobilization-free electrochemical DNA detection strategy with isothermal nucleic acid amplification. To develop a signal-amplified electrochemical DNA detection based on isothermal exonuclease III-aided target recycling. The feasibility of applying our DNA hydrolysis-based immobilization-free electrochemical DNA detection strategy in real-time monitoring of isothermal nucleic acid amplification will be demonstrated through the development of a signal-amplified electrochemical DNA detection based on isothermal exonuclease III-aided target recycling, with the real-time monitoring realized using an electro-active hydrolysis DNA probe. To use the strategy of isothermal exonuclease III-aided target recycling for other non-DNA analyte detection (e.g., metal ions). To develop an electrochemical real-time loop-mediated isothermal ampliﬁcation (ERT-LAMP) technology. Capable of rapidly amplifying double-stranded target DNA at a constant temperature using only a DNA polymerase, LAMP has found wide applications in DNA based bio-analysis. Adopting our newly-developed displacement-based immobilization-free electrochemical DNA detection strategy, by introducing an electro-actively labeled PNA probe into the LAMP reaction, the exponential amplification can be monitored electrochemically in real-time and the initial amount of the target DNA can be interpreted from the thus obtained amplification curve, resulting in a promising technique for DNA-based point-of-care bio-analysis. To develop an electrochemical real-time isothermal exponential ampliﬁcation reaction (ERT-EXPAR) technology. EXPAR is another powerful exponential isothermal nucleic acid amplification technique which is particularly suitable for amplification of short DNA oligonucleotides. Electrochemical real-time monitoring of EXPAR will be realized by incorporating the PNA displacement-based immobilization-free electrochemical DNA detection strategy.

601212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601212.value: Currently, fluorescence-based real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is the gold standard for nucleic acid detection and quantification. The powerful amplification capability of PCR combined with the sensitive fluorescent measurement results in a technology that has gained wide-spread applications in numerous assays in laboratories performing nucleic acid-based bio-analysis. In recent years, there is a growing need for nucleic acid-based molecular diagnostic techniques that can be utilized in resource-limited scenarios or at the point of care. For the purpose of fulfilling this need, isothermal amplification strategies have emerged as promising candidates as they are exempted from the thermal cycling required by PCR and therefore can be carried out with much simpler and more portable instruments. On the other hand, for the detection part, electrochemistry-based methods, as an alternative for fluorescence-based ones, has gained increasing attention as they have inherent advantages of simple instrumentation, easy miniaturization, user-friendly operation and low cost, which are attractive features for decentralized applications. Although a number of studies have been reported on the integration of isothermal nucleic acid amplification and electrochemical detection, most of them only measure the “end-point” products of the amplification. Little progress has been made in establishing a realistic electrochemical platform for “real-time” monitoring of the isothermal amplification process, which would enable quantification of the initial amount of the target nucleic acid. In this research plan, our team proposes to develop a new electrochemical platform to monitor the process of isothermal nucleic acid amplification in real time. Our strategies utilize novel electrochemical means to measure in-situ isothermally produced DNA products during the amplification process. Unlike the commonly used optical methods, our methods utilize electrochemical signals as a result of the electroactive reporters tagged on nucleic acids or peptide nucleic acids (PNA) to reflect the amount of amplicons as the amplification process proceeds. The proposed study would lead to a robust nucleic acid detection and quantification technology that rivals real-time PCR while providing additional benefits of higher compatibility with point-of-care applications. 目前核酸檢測和定量的標準技術是基於熒光的實時鏈式酶聚合反應(PCR)。這種結合了PCR強大的擴增能力與熒光檢測方法的高靈敏度的技術在許多基於核酸的生物分析中得到了廣泛的應用。近年來，對於能應用在資源有限地區或現場實時診斷的核酸檢測技術的需求日趨強烈。為了滿足這種需求，出現了多種恆溫擴增技術，它們由於省卻了PCR中的溫度循環步驟而可以在更簡單及更具有便攜性的儀器中實現。另一方面，在檢測的部分，電化學方法與熒光方法相比具有所需儀器簡單、操作簡易、適於小型化以及成本低廉等有利於分散型應用的優點。雖然已有若干關於整合恆溫核酸擴增與電化學檢測的研究報導，但這些方法大都只能測量擴增反應的“端點”產物。關於建立一個可“實時”檢測恆溫擴增反應以便確定目標核酸初始量的電化學平台的研究目前鮮見報導。 在本項研究中，我們的團隊將發展一種新的電化學平台，用於實時監測恆溫核酸擴增反應。與普遍使用的光學方法不同，我們的方法通過測量修飾在核酸或肽核酸(PNA)探針上的電活性標記物產生的電化學信號來判斷擴增反應中目標核酸的量。本研究的成果將會是一種可與實時PCR媲美且更適於現場檢測的高效的核酸檢測及定量技術。

601212.label: Realisation of objectives
601212.value: We have achieved what we stated in the five objectives. We demonstrated a new signal amplification strategy through the adoption of enzyme exonuclease III to recycle target analyte. This approach is amenable to both optical (fluorescence-based) and non-optical (electrochemistry-based) sensing strategies. In addition, its usefulness for the detection of DNA analyte was also shown for the ultrasensitive detection of heavy metal ions (e.g., Hg2+). Moreover, we have developed a new isothermal DNA amplification method through analyte-triggered DNA self assembly processes. This approach requires no enzyme and could offer detection sensitivity comparable to PCR-like processes.

601212.label: Major findings and research outcome
601212.value: The PI and his team have successfully completed all the five objectives of the project. In objective 1), they demonstrated a highly sensitive electrochemical DNA sensor that requires no probe immobilization. They demonstrated a novel electrochemical DNA detection method that has the following two notable features. First, it integrates a sensitivity improvement mechanism based on polymerase-aided isothermal target recycling. Second, in contrast to typical electrochemical DNA detection schemes, no probe immobilization step is required throughout the assay, which is realized by utilizing the electrostatic repulsion between the negative DNA backbone and a negative electrode. The combination of these two features results in a simple but highly sensitive electrochemical DNA strategy. The PI team further extended the approach developed in objective 1) for objective 2, where the use of exonuclease III was introduced. In this task, a new electrochemical sequence-specific detection platform was developed using electrochemical molecular beacon and target analyte sequence recycling through the preferential 3’ to 5’ exo-deoxyribonuclease activity of exonuclease III. The strategy takes advantages of 1) the differential diffusivity between electroactive reporter-tagged oligonucleotides and mononucleotides towards a negatively charged electrode surface and 2) the preferential enzymatic cleavage activity of exonuclease III to perform stepwise removal of mononucleotide from the blunt or recessed 3’ end of DNA duplexes. These attributes lead to an ultrasensitive electrochemical detection scheme with a signal amplification property. The improved sensitivity and the inherent simplicity of this method enable this approach to serve as a promising platform for point-of-care applications. Furthermore, the electrochemical ExoIII based sequence-sequence sensing strategy was adopted for the achievement of an ultrasensitive detection platform of metal ions (e.g., Hg2+), as described in objective 3. A highlight of this project is the development of a very novel enzyme-free analyte amplification process through an analyte-triggered DNA self-assembly strategy (JACS 2014). The DNA analyte could be grown into a dendrimer-like structures in the presence of a sequence-specific analyte. By incorporating well-designed DNA probes and nucleotide-linked reporters (either fluorescene or electroactive), this new approach could offer high detection sensitivity and specificity in fluorescent and electrochemical transduction platforms (JACS 2014 and ACS Nano 2015).

601212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
601212.value: We will exploit this new diagnostic platform (i.e., analyte-trigged DNA self-assembly) developed in this project for SNP differentiation for applications in antibiotics-resistance testing and cancer diagnostics.

601212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601212.value: The major contribution of this project is twofold: first, we demonstrated an analyte signal amplification strategy using enzymes that could digest nucleotide. This approach is particularly useful for the detection of analytes of minute quantity. Second, we developed an innovative analyte amplifcation method without the use of any enzyme. This method exploits thermodynamics and kinetics principles of DNA self-assembly and offers a promising pathway to develop into a highly sensitive and simple detection platform for DNA/RNA analytes in a resources-limited setting. For example, in the near future, we expect this platform could be developed into a simple device capable for on-the-spot pathogen screening and/or heavy metal (e.g., Hg2+) detection.

601312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601312.value: Advances in technology have increasingly made available data sets involving tens of thousands of variables. These data can sometimes answer significant questions. For instance, high-throughput microarrays and next-generation sequencing technology can reveal the expression levels and the genotypes for thousands of genes in tens of patients simultaneously. Selecting a small number of genes based on such data for accurate prediction of clinical outcomes leads to a better understanding of the genetic signature of a disease and improves treatment strategies. However, in addition to the difficulty that the number of variables is much larger than the sample size, data analysis is further complicated by the need to consider grouping and interactive effects. In recent years, novel statistical methods have been developed to meet the challenge of analyzing high-dimensional data. The problem is challenging not just because the number of variables p is much greater than the number of observations n. What is even more challenging is that one needs to consider the grouping and interactive effects among variables in addition to their individual marginal effects. For example, suppose that a disease is activated via one or more of several biological pathways and each pathway involves a group of genes. In this case, the expression level of a single gene involved in one of the biological pathways may show little or no power to predict disease status and its effect can only be detected by considering it jointly with other genes in the same pathway. That is, the grouping and interactive effects among genes are critical to accurate prediction of disease outcomes. We propose to investigate a variable selection method that incorporates both the grouping and interactive effects among variables. The method is data-driven and does not require prior information on grouping and interaction, even thought it has the flexibility to incorporate such information. The effort of considering grouping and interaction has a clear reward. In the simulated data and a few microarray datasets, the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of prediction accuracy. Furthermore, the grouping of variables identified by our method may be related to which genes are involved in a pathway, that deserves further investigation. 科技的進步使得有成千上萬變量的數據越來越多。這些數據能用來回答許多重要的問題。舉例來說，新一代的基因測序技術能同時測得病人幾十萬甚至上百萬基因形態與基因表現。從這成千上萬個基因中找出少數能準確預測疾病的類別與臨床療效幫助我們暸解疾病的成因及改善治療方法。但是這個問題極為困難不但因為變量數目極大而且因為變量的交互作用使得必須考慮的變量組合呈指數爆炸性增加。 近年來創新的統計方法被用來迎接高維度數據分析的挑戰。高維度數據分析的挑戰不但在於變量的數目極大，更在於我們必須考慮變量的交互與協同作用。例如，一種疾病可以由好幾條”通路”中的任何一條引發而每條通路都牽涉到一群基因。在這種情況下，一群基因中的一個基因的作用無法被有效的發現除非它與在同條通路中的其他基因被一起考慮。這就是說在這類問題中考慮交互及協同作用是絕對必要的。不這樣做我們就無法準確預測疾病的結果。 在本研究計劃中我們提出一個篩選變量的方法將交互及協同作用列入必要考慮。這個方法是由數據引導不需要數據之外的交互及協同作用訊息，但是若有這樣的訊息我們的方法也有將其妥善使用的彈性。考慮交互及協同作用帶來極大的利益。在數個模擬實驗及真實數據中，我們所提出的方法比所有現存的方法能大幅度更準確的預測疾病的結果。並且有證據顯示我們方法所找出的變量（基因）與所針對的疾病高度相關。

601312.label: Realisation of objectives
601312.value: Epistasis or gene-gene interaction has gained increasing attention in studies of complex diseases. Its presence as a ubiquitous component of the genetic architecture of common human diseases has been contemplated. However, the detection of gene-gene interaction is difficult due to combinatorial explosion. We present a novel feature selection method incorporating variable interaction. Gene expression datasets are analyzed to illustrate our method, although it can be applied to other types of high-dimensional data. The quality of variables selected is evaluated in two ways: first by classification error rates, then by functional relevance assessed using biological knowledge. We show that the classification error rates can be significantly reduced by considering interaction among variables. Secondly, a sizable portion of genes identified based on our classification rule for breast cancer metastasis overlaps with those reported in a gene-to-system breast cancer database as disease-associated and a few of them have interesting biological implications. This is noteworthy since genes were selected by statistical analysis without prior biological knowledge. Recent high-throughput biological studies successfully identified thousands of risk factors associated with common human diseases. Most of these studies used the single-variable method and each variable was analyzed individually. The risk factors so identified account for a small portion of disease heritability. Nowadays, there is a growing body of evidence suggesting gene-gene interactions as a possible reason for the missing heritability (Carlborg and Haley, 2004; Shao et al., 2008; Moore and Williams, 2009; Khan et al., 2011; Zuk et al., 2011). Recent reviews of methods for gene-gene interaction are given by Cordell (2009) and Kooperberg et al. (2010). The difficulty in detecting gene-gene interaction is typical for many high-dimensional data analysis problems. With only tens or hundreds of observations available normally, one needs to deal with thousands or more genes. What's more challenging is that gene-gene interaction requires the consideration of variables defined by combining genes, which makes the massive number of variables even larger. Thus feature selection is particularly crucial for effective data analysis. An important and widely adopted approach to feature selection is to first assume that data follow a statistical model. The effects of the explanatory variables on the response are then estimated by the corresponding coefficients when fitting the data to the model. Those variables with larger estimated effects are selected. As an example, let's assume the data follow a linear regression model. To improve the prediction accuracy and interpretability of ordinary least squares (OLS), LASSO of Tibshirani (1996) adds an L1-norm penalty to OLS to continuously shrink some coefficients to zero and automatically select a subset of variables. The aforesaid approach works well when the number of variables is not very large. To detect gene-gene interaction, however, it must include additional variables defined by products of original variables and thus the number of variables is exponentially larger than n, the sample size. When the number of features is exponentially larger than n, estimating the coefficients accurately is hard. This is because the noise level may be larger than some absolute coefficients and achieving the ideal risk up to a logarithmic factor in oracle inequalities may be too large for practical purposes; see e.g. Fan and Lv (2008). These difficulties are caused by the fact that the approach estimates the effects of all variables simultaneously. Hence Fan and Lv (2008) proposed a feature selection method to first screen variables separately using marginal correlation. After screening, selected variables can be accurately estimated by using methods well-suited for low or moderate dimensional data. Sure independence screening (SIS) of Fan and Lv (2008) substantially improves the performance of LASSO and related methods when variables only have marginal effects on the response variable Y. However, gene-gene interaction often comes with module effects. That is, the effect of some variables can be detected only when considered jointly with other variables. When there is module effect, SIS is not expected to attain the goal of effective feature selection. To generate useful knowledge on the genetic architecture of complex diseases where interactions among genetic, biological, biochemical and environmental factors work together to produce the response, high-dimensional statistical methods are used and current methods face a few major challenges. First, to detect the effect of a gene, it may be necessary to consider the gene jointly with others in the same functional module such as a pathway. Secondly, the genes may interact with each other in influencing the response. Thirdly, the effect of genes on the response may be highly nonlinear. To address these challenges, the proposed method extracts different types of information from the data in several stages. In the first stage, we select variables with high potential to form influential variable modules when combined with other variables. In the second stage, we generate highly influential variable modules from variables selected in the first stage so that each variable interacts with others in the same module to produce a strong effect on the response Y. The third stage combines classifiers, each constructed from one module, to form the classification rule. The overarching idea is that since the feature selection problem involving module, interaction, and nonlinearity is too complicated to be reduced to one single optimization problem based on a model equation, we break the problem into smaller ones. As the nonlinearity, interaction, and module effects can be adequately accommodated within a smaller problem, we then solve each smaller problem and combine the solutions to form the final one. Our method provides a flexible framework to analyze high-dimensional data for classification purposes. It is model-free and considers variable interaction explicitly, which aligns well with the current systems-oriented trend in biology. In summary, to deal with the tremendous complexity created by interactions among variables in high-dimensional data, the proposed method provides a flexible framework to extract different types of information from the data in three stages. In terms of classification error rates, the proposed method outperforms other methods in the literature that ignore interactions among variables. We also demonstrated a significant portion of genes identified using our method have been reported in the literature as disease-associated. Thus we are cautiously optimistic that some more genes identified by us can be replicated or validated by future studies. The proposed method has two advantages: (i) Classification rules derived from the proposed method produce low error rates; (ii) influential variable modules with scientific implications are identified in the process of deriving the classification rule. Remark: One of the objectives is to provide easy-to-use computation software based on the proposed method . Up to now the method is not completely automated. At several critical junctures, expert judgement is still required. That is, it is a powerful method but the execution requires skilful hands.

601312.label: Major findings and research outcome
601312.value: For datasets involving thousands to hundreds of thousands of features/variables, nonlinear effects, interaction effects and module effects are inevitable. However, the existing classification methods generally look the other way due to their inability to address these complicated effects. The proposed method takes a different approach to addressing these critical issues. Instead of imposing a huge model containing thousands of coefficients and estimating them simultaneously, the proposed method begins with a small subset of variables and evaluates its influence on the response. It aggregates highly influential subsets to form the final solution. It is a divide-and-conquer strategy coupled with a mechanism to carefully monitor the information flow throughout the process to avoid overfitting, which is one of the most challenging issues in analysing big and complex data. The empirical results confirm that the proposed method indeed works in the high-dimensional setting and can extract valuable information when other methods cannot.

601312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
601312.value: The method includes quite a few data analysis procedures which can be explained heuristically and intuitively but the existing statistical theories and technical tools are unable to fully explaining the superior performance offered by the these procedures. It would be interesting to develop theoretical framework and analytical tools to analyse the proposed method for a deeper understanding of the performance and limitation of the proposed classification method.

601312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601312.value: The classification method that we developed in this project can deal with nonlinear, interaction, and module effects under ultra high-dimensional setting, which is rare among existing classification methods in the literature. In many datasets that we tested it outperforms existing methods. The variables selected by our method have been reported in the literature as disease-associated. Thus the proposed method not only produces accurate prediction of disease status but also identify important genetic factors worthy of further investigation to understand the disease under study.

601712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601712.value: Since the 1970's Hierarchical Bayesian nonparamtric mixture models have been applied to a wide range of intricate statistical problems for the past few decades. Typically this involves the usage of a Dirichlet process (Bayesian nonparametric prior(BNP)) coupled with a hierarchy of parametric Bayesian modelling. In recent years, two important avenues of research have arisen. First, new classes of Hierarchical models have been introduced that involve hierarchies of BNP (HBNP) processes. The models have been applied to complex models, most notably, arising in Machine Learning/Natural Language processing. The seminal work on this, is the Hierarchical Dirichlet Process (HDP) (by Teh, Jordan, Beal and Blei, JASA (2006)) which involves hierarchies of Dirichlet processes. Since then there have been many notable extensions or variations. The other area of research has been the investigation and or introdcution of random processes that may be seen as alternatives to the Dirichlet process. While several notable processes have been investigated, since the success of the Dirichlet process, it is perhaps only within the last decade that alternatives have been employed in applications on a more regular basis. The rationale for this is that such processes, a notable example being the Pitman-Yor process, exhibit different properties than the Dirichlet process that make them more suitable for certain applications, for instance arising in language models. Furthermore, these processes exhibit features similar to the Dirichlet process which enables usage. The PI has played a role in this development. Our objective in this project is to (i) explore and develop new types of Hierarchical models (ii) identify/derive properties of other random processes that can serve as viable alternatives to the Dirichlet process. In conjunction with this, we shall seek to apply these to exisitng types of applications and compare them with the perfomrance of current methods. Furthermore, we hope to find new situations where these model may be applied. We will also continue our work on identifying links with related fields.

601712.label: Realisation of objectives
601712.value: The project funded nine written works, six of which are published in a peer reviewed outlet. The other three represent continuing works. We believe there will be more publications derived from the support of this grant. In addition, our close interaction with various scholars has fostered a series of works in progress that we envision will lead to important future outputs. The project itself funded visits, or enabled myself to visit, many internationally based scholars whose input and specialized expertise proved crucial to the completion of some of this work. In addition, their participation has played a major role in planned future developments. We shall say more about some specific individuals below. Although we were unable to identify a local PhD student to fund during the project, there were three young scholars whose short term visits were supported by this grant. They acted as "unofficial post-docs and I benefitted tremendously from their expertise. I also continue to collaborate with them. These were specifically 1. Juho Lee of Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH) Korea-who is currently a PhD Student in machine learning supervised by Professor Seungjin Choi. 2. Konstantina Palla, a Post-doctoral Fellow in machine learning at Oxford supervised by Professor Yee Whye Teh. 3. Creighton Heaukulani, who at the time was a PhD Student in the Machine Learning lab at Cambridge under the supervision of Professor Zoubin Ghahramani. I also note that there is a good chance that I will have a PhD student under my direct guidance in the Fall of 2017 who will help me continue some of this work. Overall I am quite satisfied that we have achieved our stated goals in many respects. Moreover, our interaction with various scholars has greatly enhanced my perspective and knowledge in various lines of research and I expect a significant amount of important future research output to arise from those interactions and collaborations. We have marked items 2, 4, and 5 as less than 100 percent, In the first case of 2, we simply have not finished some manuscripts but expect to do so in the near future. In terms of item 4, one of our collaborators had two different pregnancies during the time period of this project, so naturally there have been delays. Nonetheless, our interaction with other colleagues has broadened our view of this topic. An example is our recent article in Statistical Science with Professor Stefano Favaro. There we discussed a not well known connection of Neutral to the Right processes to the study of age ordered alleles arising in population genetics. While we have been aware of connections to population genetics, we have gleaned new insights during the writing of the Statistical Science article that we believe will result in fruitful further investigations. Item 5 we listed as 90% complete. This assessment only reflects the fact that, while we have developed many ideas that we believe will have significant impact in terms of both theory and application, we were not able to complete final versions of these works within the time frame of the grant. However in terms of knowledge gained in this area, I would rate this to be 100% and in fact far exceeds my expectations. This part of the project benefitted tremendously from the input of our visitors and other collaborators. Perhaps the most significant among these, were close interactions with Dr. Creighton Heaukulani, Professor Nathan Ross of the University of Melbourne, Professor Peter Orbanz of Columbia University and Juho Lee of POSTECH. For some specifics, with Dr Heaukulani, we discussed new hierarchical Bayesian nonparametric models that ,for instance , can be potentially used as alternatives to Beta and Dirichlet diffusion trees. More generally our models lead to fairly tractable prior distributions over space of trees and forests. My interactions s with Professor Nathan Ross has perhaps done the most to broaden my knowledge base in terms of the theory of random trees and graphs. As of December 2016, we have drafted a working manuscript that I anticipate, after further discussion on my visit to Melbourne in January 2017, will result in at least four major works encompassing topics such as preferential attachment models, triangular Polya urns, general methodology to identify random structures exhibiting notions of recursive self-similarity and various constructions of trees and graphs. While these developments are contributions to probability models falling under the umbrella of combinatorial stochastic processes, we also feel that some of this will translate into pertinent novel Bayesian prior distribution s that will be useful for statistical inference for phenomena that can be expressed in terms of trees, graphs et cetera.

601712.label: Major findings and research outcome
601712.value: The work on the Indian Buffet process represents a major achievement as it present a unified treatment of important existing models where a systematic analysis was not well understood. More generally, we significantly extend the framework to include many new models and also a previously unknown multivariate extension. This allows the practitioner to focus on the application rather than be encumbered by technical details. Our work on stick-breaking presents explicit results for a significant class of models that are routinely used in applications. From this we have also identified a large class of distributions which connect to other phenomena arising in a size biased sampling setting. These works lay the foundation for future research related to hierarchical models, graphs and trees. There is also the related work with applications to financial models. We anticipate that our work on stable random variables with Devroye will be a highly cited paper on this important topic as it relates both to practical issues of sampling as well as some pertinent distributional identities. Our NIPS publication, with Juho Lee and Seungjin Choi, presents a new class of models that can be used for statistical inference when involving very large datasets associated with models exhibiting certain type of power law behavior.

601712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
601712.value: As we have mentioned in both 5.3 and 6.1 of this proposal the research that was conducted and our interaction with various scholars facilitated by this grant, have laid the foundation for a quite a few projects. Some of which are ongoing and some of which have been outlined in our most recent GRF proposal of this year. We have clear ideas about projects involving hierarchical structures directly connected with relational models, random graphs and trees. More details can be obtained from section 5.3

601712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601712.value: The developments in the project demonstrated significant results both in terms of theoretical developments and practical implementation. Part of this work made transparent the analysis and practical utility of a large class of models which are relevant to feature analysis and relational models, That is to say structures that arise within the context of for instance recommendations systems or other type of statistical factor models involving an unknown and high dimensional feature space. For example companies such as Amazon, Alibaba and Netflix all use forms of recommendation systems that help them tailor make their products to the specific attributes or features(or factors) of their continuing and newer customers. Data structures, which have many similarities in the sense that they may be described in terms of relational models, graphs, trees or more general arrays, arise in a wide variety of disciplines including genetics with relevance, for instance, to potential personalized health care models. All these phenomena are associated with complex and massive amounts of data. The results we have developed fall into classes of models that have been shown to be suitable for handling data of this type. Naturally more needs to be done.

601812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601812.value: Aromatic compounds are important chemical species that are of both academic and practical interest. Benzene and benzyne are among the most important organic aromatic compounds. Heterocyclic aromatic compounds can be derived from formal replacement of carbon groups in benzene and benzyne by hetero atoms/groups. Transition metal-containing metallabenzenes and metallabenzynes are recently discovered heterocyclic aromatic compounds. These compounds are interesting because they could display properties of both aromatic organic compounds and organometallic compounds. Compared with the chemistry of metallabenzenes, that of metallabenzynes is much less developed. Indeed, only the chemistry of metallabenzynes with an osmium center has been previously explored. This proposed study will address the chemistry of metallabenzynes of middle transition metals. The main objectives of the proposed research are (i) to develop synthetic methods to synthesize metallabenzynes of middle transition metals, and (ii) to explore their chemical properties. 芳香性化合物是一类具有特殊化學性質的化合物。最典型的芳香性化合物包括苯及苯炔。把苯及苯炔分子中的基团用含杂原子的基团代替能得到杂环芳香化合物。金属苯及金属苯炔是近年来发现的环芳香化合物。这类化合物可同时具有有机芳香性化合物及金属有机化合物的性質。同金属苯相比，金属苯炔的化学的研究还很少。例如，已知的金属苯炔只局限在那些含有锇的金属苯炔。本项目的主要目的在于发展中过渡金属苯炔的化学。主要研究内容包括（1）发展合成中过渡金属苯炔的方法，（2）探讨它们的化学性質。

601812.label: Realisation of objectives
601812.value: The main objectives of the project are (i) to develop synthetic methods to synthesize metallabenzynes of middle transition metals and (ii) to explore the chemical properties of metallabenzynes of middle transition metals. To achieve the objectives, we have carried out the following research work. We have prepared a series of allenylcarbene complexes and explored their reactions with gold alkynyls Au(C≡CR)(PPh3) or copper(I) alkynyls Cu(C≡CR) in the presence of HNEt3Cl for the synthesis of metallabenzynes. With this method, we were able to synthesize a series of new metallabenzynes. The mechanism of the reactions has also been studied computationally. We have explored the possibility of synthesizing metallabenzynes by [4+2] cyclo-addition reactions of acetylide-carbyne complexes LnM(≡CR)(C≡CR’) with alkynes both theoretically and experimentally. To explore the feasibility, we have carried out computational studies to evaluate the thermodynamics and kinetics of the reactions of alkynes with acetylide-carbyne complexes of osmium, rhenium and tungsten with various ligand environments. The theoretical results indicate that, with proper ligand and metals, the reactions of acetylide-carbyne complexes with alkynes to give metallabenzynes can be thermodynamically favorable with a moderate reaction barrier. To demonstrate that metallabenzynes can be synthesized by [4+2] cyclo-addition reactions of acetylide-carbyne complexes with alkynes, we have made a lot of efforts in synthesizing of acetylide-carbyne complexes of tungsten, rhenium and osmium. During the process, we have developed methodologies to synthesize carbyne complexes of tungsten, rhenium and osmium. We have also successfully isolated interesting 12-membered dirhenium acetylide-carbyne metallacycles. However, we met difficulty in the preparation of stable mononuclear acetylide-carbyne complexes LnM(≡CR)(C≡CR’). Electrophilic abstraction of metallabenzenes can potentially give metallabenzynes. We have prepared a series of rhenium-containing metallabenzenes with an OR group at the ortho position through the reactions of rhenacyclobutadienes with ethoxyethyne. We have studied their reactions with electrophiles such as BF3 or AlCl3. The experiments indicated that it is possible to make metallabenzynes from the reactions. The first metallabenzyne was obtained from the reaction of the osmium(II) complex OsCl2(PPh3)3 with the terminal alkyne HC≡CSiMe3. We have therefore explored the reactions of terminal alkynes with a number of low valent complexes of rhenium and tungsten, for example, [Re(dppm)3]I, Re(OAc)(CO)(PPh3)3, WCl4(dppe) and WH(PMe3)4(2-PMe2CH2). The work led us to isolate a number of 2-alkyne, vinylidene, allenylidene and carbyne complexes. To determine if metallabenzynes are indeed aromatic metallacycles, we have studied their reactions with bromine. Our work indicates that metallabenzynes, like typical aromatic organic compounds, can undergo electrophilic substitution reactions with bromine. To further assess the aromatic character of metallabenzynes, we have carried out computational studies to evaluate structural, energetic and magnetic properties of metallabenzynes. The results support that metallabenzynes can be regarded as aromatic metallacycles. In effort to compare the properties of metallabenzynes with those of typical carbyne complexes, we have studied rearrangement reactions of metallabenzynes to give carbene and cyclopentadienyl complexes both theoretically and experimentally. The study reveals that the ligands as well as the substitutents on the metallacycle can significantly affect the relative energies of the isomers and barriers for their interconversions. To further compare the properties of metallabenzynes with those of typical carbyne complexes, we have studied reactions of typical carbyne complexes with reagents such as bromine, hydrogen peroxide and alkynes. The studies reveal that metallabenzynes behave differently from those of typical carbyne complexes. During the process, we found that low valent rhenium carbyne complexes can undergo metathesis reactions with alkynes.

601812.label: Major findings and research outcome
601812.value: (1) A series of new metallabenzynes were obtained by treatment of the eta-3-allenylcarbene complexes OsCl2(=CAr-CH= C=CHAr)(PPh3)2 with gold alkynyls Au(C≡CR)(PPh3) or copper(I) alkynyls Cu(C≡CR) (R = Ph, TMS) in the presence of HNEt3Cl. Computational studies suggest that the osmabenzynes are formed through electrocyclization of osmium alkynyl-allenylcarbene intermediates followed by protonation with HNEt3Cl [Publications 8]. (2) The rhenacyclobutadiene complexes Re{-C(Ar)C(CO2R’)C(OR)}(CO)4 can react with HC≡COEt to give the rhenabenzenes Re{-C(Ar)C(CO2R’)C(OR)CHC- (OEt)}(CO)4 that are stable enough to be isolated [Publications 4 and 5]. (3) The 12-membered-ring metallacycles [Re{≡CCH=C(R)C≡C}Cl(PMe2Ph)3)]2 which are organometallic analogues of antiaromatic octadehydro[12]annulene have been prepared by heating the methyl carbyne complexes Re{≡CCH=C(R)C≡CH}(CH3)Cl(PMe2Ph)3, which involves an intermolecular -bond metathesis reaction between the Re-CH3 bond and the acetylenic C-H bond [Publication 11]. (4) Unexpected coupling products were obtained from the reactions of rhenacyclobutadienes Re{-C(Ar)C(CO2R’)C(OR)}(CO)4 with ethoxyethyne [Publication 5]. (5) The relative thermal stability of metallabenzynes Os(≡CCH=CHCH=CH)Cl2(L)2 and the corresponding isomeric carbene complexes Os{=C(−CH=CHCH=CH−)}Cl2(L)2 as well as the chlorocyclopentadienyl complexes Os(eta-5-C5ClH4)Cl(L)2 (L = CO, phosphine, pyridine, amine) are found to be strongly dependent on ligand L. It was found experimentally that the metallabenzyne Os{≡CC(SiMe3)=C(CH3)C(SiMe3)=CH−}Cl2(CO)(PPh3) can rearrange to the eta-5-chlorocyclopentadienyl complex Os{eta-5-C5HCl(CH3)(SiMe3)2}Cl(CO)(PPh3) [Publication 7]. (6) The reactions of ReH5(PMe2Ph)3 with terminal alkynes can give rhenium carbyne complexes Re((CCH2R)Cl2(PMe2Ph)3 and/or eta-2-vinyl complexes Re(eta-2-CH2CR)Cl2(PMe2Ph)3. The reaction pathways were found to be kinetic-controlled [Publication 1]. (7) Treatment of [Re(dppm)3]I (dppm = PPh2CH2PPh2) with HC≡CR produced the rhenium vinylidene complex ReI(=C=CHR)- (dppm)2. In the presence of HI, [Re(dppm)3]I reacted with HC≡CR to give the rhenium carbyne complexes [ReI(≡CCH2R)(dppm)2]I and with HC≡CC(OH)RR’ to produce the vinylcarbyne complexes [ReI(≡CCH=CRR’)(dppm)2]I [Publication 9] (8) d2 Re(V) carbyne complexes Re(≡CR)Cl2(PMe2Ph)3 can undergo stoichiometric alkyne metathesis reactions. Theoretical studies suggest that the metathesis reactions most likely proceed through six-coordinate alkyne-carbyne intermediates Re(≡CR)Cl2(eta-2-alkyne)(PMe2Ph)2 that undergo reversible cycloaddition reactions [Publication 10].

601812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
601812.value: (1) We have successfully isolated and structurally characterized of metallabenzynes of rhenium and osmium. It would be interesting to explore the possibility of isolating metallabenzynes of other metals. (2) We have shown that metallabenzenes and metallabenzynes have aromatic character. It would be interesting to synthesize metallacycles of other ring sizes and to explore their properties. (3) We have found that, with proper metals and ligands, metallabenzynes complexes could be thermodynamically more stable than their corresponding isomeric chlorocyclopentadienyl and cyclopentadienylidene complexes. It is worthwhile to explore the possibility of making metallabenzynes using chlorocyclopentadienyl and cyclopentadienylidene complexes as the starting materials. (4) We have discovered that d2 Re(VI) carbyne complexes can undergo metathesis reactions with alkynes. It would be interesting to carry out further experimental and computational work to explore the possibility of using low valent carbyne complexes for catalytic alkyne metathesis.

601812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601812.value: Aromatic compounds are important chemical species that are of both academic and practical interest. Benzene and benzyne are among the most important organic aromatic compounds. Heterocyclic aromatic compounds can be derived from formal replacement of carbon groups in benzene and benzyne by hetero atoms/groups. In the past, many such compounds with a main-group element/group have been studied. More recently, there has been much interest in the chemistry of transition metal-containing metallabenzenes and metallabenzynes, which are derived from formal replacement of carbon groups in benzene and benzyne by transition metal groups. These heterocyclic aromatic compounds are interesting because they could display properties of both aromatic organic compounds and organometallic compounds. However, limited work has been previously carried out in this direction. In this project, we have successfully isolated and structurally characterized a series of new metallabenzenes and metallabenzynes. We have also investigated the chemical properties of these new aromatic compounds. The results obtained in this project expand the knowledge in the chemistry of heterocyclic aromatic compounds.

601912.label: Project Title(Chinese)
601912.value: 高频金融数据模型选择与推断

601912.label: Project Objectives
601912.value: To investigate the feasibility of modeling high frequency financial data with pure jump processes, and develop some test procedures for this purpose. To develop statistical tests to test if the price processes contain jumps, in the presence of microstructure noise. To study the effect of multiple transactions on integrated volatility estimation for high-frequency data, and propose consistent estimators and study their properties. To develop a statistical test for determining if the driving force behind the high frequency data is Brownian motion or fractional Brownian motion.

To develop statistical tests to test if the price processes contain jumps, in the presence of microstructure noise.
To study the effect of multiple transactions on integrated volatility estimation for high-frequency data, and propose consistent estimators and study their properties.
To develop a statistical test for determining if the driving force behind the high frequency data is Brownian motion or fractional Brownian motion.

601912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601912.value: Financial market evolution is often interrupted by various events, such as market crashes, corporate defaults or announcements, central bank announcements, and news releases. These market uncertainties generate significant discontinuities or jumps in financial variables. On the other hand, the existence of microstructure noise in the financial prices has been well documented in the literature. For these reasons, there has been tremendous interest in developing a financial model for option pricing and risk management in the presence of jumps and microstructure noise. The easy availability of high-frequency data in modern financial markets enables improved understanding of market behavior and microstructure. It also allows exploration of strategies and hypotheses over very short time horizons. For instance, there has been tremendous interest in developing financial model for option pricing and risk management, etc. So far, there has been a bewildering array of models for asset pricing in financial econometrics, including Ito's diffusions, pure jump processes, diffusion-jump processes, Levy processes. These are all special cases of the more general Ito's semimartingales. Other types of models, such as the fractional Brownian motion, have also been investigated. In financial modeling, given a financial time series, one has to choose an appropriate model amongst available ones. Since economic theories usually do not suggest a functional form for continuous-time models, researchers and ractitioners alike often use convenient specifications, e.g., for deriving losed-form solutions for various security prices. Since mis-specification of a model may lead to erroneous valuation and hedging strategies, it is very important to develop reliable specification tests for continuous-time models. This presents new problems and challenges for probability and statistical researchers. The main purpose of this project is to investigate some of the issues in the study of high-frequency financial data. In particular, we wish to develop statistical tests for model selections for financial data. After the model is chosen, we would then like to conduct statistical inference for the quantities of interest. These are interesting and challenging problems. We believe that the project, once completed, would be of both theoretical and practical value. 金融市场的不稳定性会使许多金融变量生成跳跃过程。同时微观结构噪声在市场价格的存在使金融问题变得更为复杂。高频数据的普及是我们对这些现象有更深一步的了解。所以目前在期权定价和风险管理方面很多研究工作都在发展带有跳跃过程及微观结构噪声的模型构造与检验。例如，给定一只股票，可能有各种各样的模型去描述它，包括扩散过程，扩散-跳跃过程，分形布朗运动等等。由于选择正确模型的正确性不言而喻，本项目主题之一就是如何去选择一个最佳模型。

601912.label: Realisation of objectives
601912.value: Pure-jump processes have been increasingly popular in modeling high frequency financial data, partially due to their versatility and flexibility. In the meantime, several statistical tests have been proposed in the literature to check the validity of using pure-jump models. However, these tests suffer from several drawbacks, such as requiring rather stringent conditions and having slow rates of convergence. In this project, we propose a different test to check whether the underlying process of high-frequency data can be modelled by a pure-jump process. The new test is based on the realized characteristic function, and enjoys a much faster convergence rate available for existing tests; it is applicable much more generally than previous tests; for example, it is robust to jumps of infinite variation and flexible modeling of the diffusion component.

601912.label: Major findings and research outcome
601912.value: The phenomenon of multiple transactions at each recording time is a common occurrence for high frequency financial data, due to heavy trading of the market and limitation of the recording mechanism. The situation has existed for a long time, but become more common in recent years due to heavier trading. Surprisingly, there has been hardly any study on this important issue, in spite of some ad hoc approaches to treat multiple transactions. In this paper we investigate how to handle multiple transactions, particularly in the context of estimating the integrated volatility and integrated quarticity, which are of great interest in financial econometrics. Two approaches are proposed for this purpose, and their asymptotic properties are investigated. Simulations conform their excellent performances.

601912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
601912.value: There are many interesting open problems to study in the future. For instance, the effect of the non-uniform tick time is unclear and worthy of investigation in both theory and practice. There have been some literature on the estimation of integrated volatilities, e.g., the two-time-scale technique or multi-time-scale techniques of Aït-Sahalia, Mykland and Zhang (2005), Zhang (2006)] or the pre-averaging approach [Jacod et al. (2009)]. But litte is known in the testing situation, and is worthy of study.

601912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601912.value: Financial modeling plays a very important role in many aspects of financial activities, e.g., the study of financial market, prediction, option pricing, etc. However, it is very difficult to do financial modeling due to many complications, such as ultra high-frequency of financial transactions, multiple transactions, microstructure noise, non-uniform tick times, etc. In this project, we attempt to tackle some of the issues and obtain some very interesting results, which are not only of theoretical but also of practical interest.
