602212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602212.value: Development of new methodologies for the synthesis of polymers with novel structures and unique properties is a fundamental important area in macromolecular science. Natural polymers such as DNA and protein have well-defined primary structures with ordered sequences of monomer units. In contrast, most synthetic polymers have random structures and are accessed via one- or two-component polymerization route. Development of programmable polymerization reaction is thus of interest because it may generate bio-mimic polymers with unique materials properties and potential practical applications. Our research group has been actively working on the development of new alkyne polymerization routes to functional macromolecules. It is known that Lewis acid-mediated coupling of terminal arylacetylenes with arylaldehydes and transition metal-catalyzed reactions of alkynes and aldehydes with amines proceed in a one-spot procedure, producing 1,5-dihalo-1,4-dienes and 3-arylpropargylamines, respectively, with high regio- and stereoregularity. In this research project, we plan to explore the utility of these organic reactions for the synthesis of new functional polymers. New monomers will be designed, effective catalyst systems will be explored, regio- and stereochemistry involved in the polymerization will be investigated, and high molecular weight polymers with linear and hyperbranched structures and good macroscopic processability will be prepared. Functional groups will be incorporated into the polymer structures, in an effort to develop new materials with useful electronic, optical, photonic, and magnetic properties. The properties of the new polymers will be systematically investigated and their uses as active materials for the construction of polymer light-emitting diodes, redox-active materials, and precursors for magnetic ceramics will be explored. It is anticipated that this project will establish effective synthetic routes to a large variety of new macromolecules with novel structures, advanced functionalities, and practical applications. 具有新型結構和獨特性能的聚合物的新合成方法的發展是高分子科學中最基本且重要的領域。天然高分子例如DNA 和蛋白質等具有單體單位有序的排列所組成的確定的主結構。與此相反, 而大多數合成聚合物具有隨機的結構, 且是通過一個或兩個的組份聚合得到。因此, 可程式化的聚合反應的發展引起人們極大的興趣, 其原因是該方法可能會生成具有獨特材料性質和潛在的實際應用的仿生聚合物。 我們研究組一直積極地致力於發展從炔到功能性大分子的新聚合路線。眾所周知, 路易士酸調節下得端基芳炔與芳甲醛的反應, 以及金屬催化下炔, 醛和胺的一鍋法反應, 能分別高選擇性, 立體規整地產生1.5-二鹵代-1,4-二烯烴和 3-芳炔丙基胺, 在此研究專案中, 我們計畫, 探討這些有機反應來合成新功能高分子材料的實用性。 我們將設計新的單體, 尋找有效的催化劑, 研究聚合過程中的選擇性及立體化學, 製備線性, 超支化結構及良好的宏觀加工性高分子量聚合物。功能性的基團將被引入聚合物的結構, 竭力發展具有電, 光, 磁性質以及具有光子性質的新材料。系統地研究新型聚合物的性質, 及其作為功能材料的應用。例如: 構建聚合物發光二極體, 發展氧化-還原功能以及可用作磁性陶瓷的前驅體材料。預期該項目將建立有效合成路線, 從而得到大量的具有新結構, 先進功能的大分子, 研究及發展它們的潛在應用價值。

602212.label: Realisation of objectives
602212.value: The purposes of this research project are to (a) design and synthesis of new functional monomers, (b) develop effective methodologies for their polymerization, (c) search for new catalysts and optimize the polymerization parameters, and (d) investigate the structure-property relationships of the polymers and explore their technological applications. Through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we believe we have completed all the objectives. To achieve the goals, we have developed a new programmable polymerization route for the synthesis of new conjugated polymers. The three-component polycoupling reactions of terephthalaldehyde, dibenzylamine and aromatic diynes are catalyzed by indium(III) chloride in oxylene at 140 °C, affording soluble polymers with well-defined structures and high molecular weights in high yields. The resulting polymers are soluble and enjoy high thermal stability. Their thin films show high refractive indices (RI = 1.7529−1.6041) in a wide wavelength region of 400−1600 nm with low optical dispersions (D’ down to 0.005). The polymers are readily metallified by complexation of their triple bonds with cobalt octacarbonyls. Pyrolysis of the resulting organometallic polymers at high temperature under inert atmosphere generates nanostructured ceramics with high magnetic susceptibility (Ms up to 80.7 emu/g) and near-zero coercivity (Hc down to 0.19 kOe). We have also developed a one-pot three-component tandem polymerization route based on the consecutive coupling-addition-cyclization reaction of alkyne, carbonyl chloride and ethyl 2-mercaptoacetate. The polymerization proceeds efficiently at room temperature with high tolerance to the monomer feed ratio, affording thiophene-containing conjugated polymers with high molecular weights in nearly quantitative yields. The obtained polymers are weakly emissive in solutions but emit intensely upon aggregation, demonstrating a novel photophysical phenomenon of aggregation-enhanced emission. Well-resolved fluorescent photopatterns can be generated by exposure of their films under UV irradiation through copper photomasks. The polymers serve as sensitive and selective fluorescent chemosensors for Ru3+ with high quenching constants of up to 8.8 × 100000 L mol-1. We have further developed an efficient one-pot coupling–hydroamination polymerization pathway to functional polymers. The one-pot Sonogashira coupling of alkyne and carbonyl chloride followed by subsequent hydroamination of the resulting product proceed smoothly under mild conditions, furnishing nitrogen-containing conjugated polymers with high regioselectivity, stereoselectivity and molecular weights in excellent yields. On the other hand, soluble polymers with well-defined structures and high molecular weights can be obtained in high yields by one-pot three-component polymerizations of alkynes, sulfonyl azide and optically active amino esters catalyzed by inexpensive copper(I) iodide at room temperature. The obtained polymers enjoy excellent film-forming ability, good thermal stability and high refractive indices with low chromatic dispersions. They are chiral due to the helical rotation of their backbones in a preferred screw sense induced by the chiral pendants. The presence of amidine groups makes them promising materials for CO2 capture.

602212.label: Major findings and research outcome
602212.value: Development of new methodologies for the synthesis of polymers is a fundamental important area in macromolecular science. Particularly, those with good control in polymer structure have attracted much attention because they may generate biomimic macromolecules with unique materials properties and potential practical applications. In this work, several programmable polymerization routes have been developed. They include: (1) indium-catalyzed three-component polycoupling of terephthalaldehyde, dibenzylamine and aromatic diyne, (2) one-pot three-component tandem polymerization of alkyne, carbonyl chloride and ethyl 2-mercaptoacetate, (3) one-pot coupling–hydroamination polymerization of alkyne and carbonyl chloride and amine and (4) copper-catalyzed one-pot three-component polymerization of alkyne, sulfonyl azide and amino ester. These reactions possess unique advantages such as high efficiency, functional group tolerance and atom- and step-economy, generating heteroatom-containing polymers with high molecular weights and well-defined structures in high yields. All the polymers are soluble, possessing high thermal stability and film-forming ability. They exhibit unique properties such as aggregation-enhanced emission, chirality, high light refraction, photopatterning and sensitive and selective detection of metal ion. Heteroatom-containing polymers are a group of novel functional materials with unique electronic and photophysical properties, and are in great demand in a wide range of potential high-tech applications such as fluorescent sensors and photoelectronics. However, they are difficult to synthesis due to their complicated structures which require tedious reaction procedure, harsh reaction condition, painful isolation, severe catalyst poison side-effect, etc. The facile procedures for their syntheses described here will inspire research enthusiasm for further development of efficient polymerization approaches toward polymeric materials with advanced functionalities and useful applications. As you can see in Part C of this report, more than 20 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in articles with high citation indexes and top journals related to the present research fields. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful result.

602212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602212.value: In this investigation, we have developed various multi-component polymerization routes to polymers from alkyne-based organic reactions. By exploration of new catalysts and optimization of reaction conditions, high molecular weight poly(1-phenylprop-2-ynylamine)s, poly(arylene thiophenylene)s, poly(enaminone)s, and poly(N-sulfonylamidine)s are obtained in high yields with high stereo- and regio-regularity. These polymerization reactions enjoy the advantages of high efficiency, functional group tolerance and atom- and step-economy, suffering no drawbacks encountered in conventional polymerization systems. All the polymers are soluble and film-forming and show high thermal stability. They show unique functional properties, such as aggregation-enhanced emission, emission quenching in the detection of metal ions, light refractivity and photopatterning. Such attributes make them promising for use in electronics and optics . Because we have obtained promising results, we are still working on the exploration of new tools to new conjugated polymers. If we are able to get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to explore further the high-technological applications of our polymers in the fabrication of optoelectronic devices such as photovoltaic cells and field-effect transitors.

602212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602212.value: Advancement in technology is associated with the development of new materials and the exploration of new polymerization reactions is of both academic importance and practical implication. Herein, new programmable methodologies for the construction of functional polymers with defined structures are proposed. All the polymers are synthesized with high molecular weights in high yields. They are soluble, film-forming and thermally stable. They show unique properties, such as aggregation-enhanced emission, emission quenching in the detection of metal ions, high light refraction and photopatterning. Materials with such attributes are anticipated to find an array of high-technological applications.

602512.value: 曲面上点的希尔伯特概形的上同调

602512.label: Project Objectives
602512.value: Study the ordinary cohomology ring structure, and the quantum cohomology of the Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces.
rows: Study the ordinary cohomology ring structure, and the quantum cohomology of the Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces.

602512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602512.value: The Yang-Mills theory is a theory in theoretical physics governing the fundamental forces in our natural world. The electro-magnetic field is an example of Yang-Mills fields. The mathematical description of the Yang-Mills theory in terms of algebraic geometry is the theory of stable vector bundles. The Hilbert scheme of points on a surface is a simplest example of the space of Yang-Mills fields on a four dimensional space. The mathematical research of it intertwines with the Yang-Mills theory, which provides many surprising insights for mathematicians. There is another aspect of the Hilbert scheme in that it can also be regarded as a smooth model for the symmetrization of n-fold product of the surface. Due to the various aspects of Hilbert schemes, the research on Hilbert schemes touches different areas of mathematics such as geometry, combinatorics, algebras, and integrable systems. Since the seminal work of Nakajima and Lehn, there is a method developed by Nakajima, Lehn, Sorger, Li, Qin and Wang which formulate the geometric properties of Hilbert schemes in terms of algebras. This has been proven to be very powerful in determining the cohomology ring structure of Hibert schemes. The cohomology ring of a space is an algebraic object associated to the space, which carries a lot of geometric information of the space expressed in the language of algebra and is easier to handle than the space itself. In some special cases, the cohomology ring is completely determined. For general surfaces, the difficulty lies in the appearance of one extra term in Lehn’s formula. One goal of the project is to search for an effective method to determine the cohomology ring of Hilbert schemes on a general surface. Another interesting topic in this area is the crepant resolution conjecture originally formulated by Ruan and expanded by Bryan and Graber, Goates and Ruan. It basically relates the cohomology ring of the Hilbert scheme with the Chen-Ruan orbifold cohomology ring of the symmetric product of the surface. This amounts to the computation of Gromov-Witten invariants of Hilbert schemes. One of the newest techniques is the co-section localization method of Kiem-J.Li. This has been proven to be effective for two-point Gromov-Witten invariants. In this project, we will explore the co-section localization method for n-point Gromov-Witten invariants and prove the crepant resolution conjecture.

602512.label: Realisation of objectives
602512.value: The main objective of the project is to study the ordinary cohomology ring structure and the quantum cohomology of the Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces. The ultimate goal is to prove Yongbin Ruan's conjecture that the cohomology ring structure of the Hilbert scheme can be related to the Chen-Ruan cohomology ring of the symmetric product via a correction from extremal Gromov-Witten invariants. This was achieved in the joint paper with Z.B. Qin ``The Cohomological Crepant Resolution Conjecture for the Hilbert-Chow Morphisms" published on the Journal of Differential Geometry after many years of unsuccessful attempts. The main breakthrough comes from applying Kiem-J.Li's co-section localization unavailable to us in our previous attempts. We proved a universality result by the detailed analysis of the virtual cycle of the moduli space of three-points extremal stable maps to the Hilbert scheme. We also used a method of Jun Li on Hilbert scheme of points on three-folds , and applied the vertex algebraic treatment of the cohomology of Hilbert scheme and the symmetric product due to Nakajima, Lehn, Li-Qin-Wang, and Qin-Wang. Then the result of Cheong who proves Ruan's conjecture for toric surfaces is used to prove the conjecture for general projective surfaces. We also applied Kiem-J.Li's co-section localisation method to study the extremal Gromov-Witten invariants of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces with geometric genus bigger than zero. When the surface has a non-zero holomorphic two form, it will force vanishing of some extremal Gromov-Witten invariants of the Hilbert schemes. The result is in the joint paper with J.X.Hu and Z.B. Qin ``The Gromov–Witten invariants of the Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces with pg > 0" published on the International Journal of Mathematics. In the joint paper with Zhenbo Qin ``Donaldson–Thomas invariants of certain Calabi–Yau 3- folds" published on the Communications in Analysis and Geometry, we compute the Donaldson–Thomas invariants for two types of Calabi–Yau 3-folds. These invariants are associated to the moduli spaces of rank-2 Gieseker semistable sheaves. None of the sheaves are locally free, and their double duals are locally free stable sheaves investigated earlier in the work of Donaldson and Thomas, and us. We show that these Gieseker moduli spaces are isomorphic to some Quot-schemes. We prove a formula for Behrend’s ν-functions when torus actions present with positive dimensional fixed point sets, and use it to obtain the generating series of the relevant Donaldson–Thomas invariants in terms of the McMahon function. We made a great achievement in the theory of Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten theory under the support of the grant. FJRW invariants are Landau-Ginzburg model's analogue of Gromov-Witten invariants for Sigma-model. They were defined by Fan, Jarvis and Ruan using analysis. The algebraic geometric construction was done by Chiodo, A. Polishchuk and A. Vaintrob independently. Working with H.L. Chang and J. Li, we used newly developed p-field theory of H.L.Chang-J.Li and Kiem-J.Li's co-section localisation method to give another construction. This new construction can be generalised to many other cases and used to do effective computations. Since FJRW theory is a quantum theory of singularities and one of the most important ingredients for the famous CY-LG correspondence, our construction will be essential in the study of the phenomenon. The result is contained in ``Witten's top Chern class via cosection localization" published on Invent. Math.

602512.label: Major findings and research outcome
602512.value: The main objective of the project is to study Ruan's cohomological crepant resolution conjecture for the Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces. There have been quite a number of results for the case where the surface is a toric surface. Since there is an induced torus action on the Hilbert scheme, the torus localisation technique can be used. However, for a general surface, new methods are needed. One of the major achievements of our research is to use a newly developed co-section localisation method by Kiem and J. Li. By doing so, we are able to prove that there is a universal property for the three-point extremal Gromov-Witten invariants of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces. Then we used the existing results for toric surfaces to prove Ruan's conjecture. The main result is contained in the joint paper [2] with Z.B. Qin. Another major finding in the project is the algebraic construction of the FJRW invariants. FJRW invariants were defined by Fan, Jarvis and Ruan using analysis. There were algebraic constructions by Chiodo, and A. Polishchuk with A. Vaintrob independently. However, there were no proves that these definitions are equivalent. Also Chiodo and P-V's constructions used K-theory. We found a new algebraic construction using the newly developed theories of p-fields by H.L. Chang and J. Li and the co-section localisation by Kiem and J. Li. We also proved that all existing constructions are equivalent. Our method has an advantage that it can be related to Gromov-Witten invariants construction done by H. L. Chang and J. Li. This will lead to a better understanding of the relations between Gromov-Witten invariants and FJRW invariants and thus Calabi-Yau and Landau-Ginzburg correspondence. The result is published in the joint paper [4] with H.L. Chang and J. Li

602512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602512.value: The algebraic construction of FJRW invariants in [4] used the same methods as Chang-Li's new construction of Gromov-Witten invariants. The methods are p-field theory and co-section localisation technique. The same construction is used to set up a mixed-p-fields moduli which relates FJRW invariants and Gromov-Witten invariants. This new moduli has a potential to calculate the Gromov-Witten invariants for quintic Calabi-Yau three-folds and FJRW invariants for quintic polynomials. Working jointly with H.L. Chang, Melissa Liu and J. Li, we wrote two papers on mixed-p-fields theory under the support of another GRF grant of which I am the Co-I. For the effective computations of Gromov-Witten invariants and FJRW invariants, we need a very complicated packaging tool. It should involve the existing packaging methods such as Givental's formalism, Zinger's packaging and beyond. This is a very challenging task. I will write a GRF grant application this year for the support of this new project.

602512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602512.value: We made two major achievements in the project. One is the proof of Ruan's cohomological crepant resolution conjecture for Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces. There are lots of research results on this conjecture, all for surfaces with a torus group action, where the torus localisation method is used. We used a new method, the co-section localisation theory, which enables us to prove the conjecture for all surfaces. This research also found an effective way to use co-section localisation method on Hilbert schemes which can be useful for other research topics on Hilbert schemes. In fact, our result is already used by other researchers on Hodge-theoretic questions on Hyper-Kahler manifolds. Another major achievement is the algebraic construction of FJRW invariants using the p-field theory and co-section localisation technique. The importance of this construction is that it uses the same method in the construction of Gromov-Witten invariants by Chang and J. Li. Therefore we can use the same methods to construct two totally different invariants, Gromov-Witten invariants and FJRW invariants, at once. This will lead to a possible geometric explanation of Calabi-Yau and Landau-Ginzburg correspondence, which is one of the most mysteries conjectures in mirror symmetry.

603212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603212.value: There has been active research recently on the modeling and numerical simulation of coupled fluid and porous flows. The results find important applications such as predicting the propagation and diffusion of pollutants dispersed in water and simulating the filtration effects of flooding in dry areas. Various mathematical models and numerical methods with different properties have been investigated. A mixed Navier-Stokes/Darcy model involves heterogeneous sub-models in different regions coupled by complicated interface conditions. The coupled system is difficult to analyze and solve. Effective techniques have been developed to decouple the mixed model so that single model solvers can be applied to sub-models locally. However, certain numerical and theoretical difficulties with the saddle-point problem due to the Stokes or Navier-Stokes model still remain. A unified Brinkman model is easier to analyze and solve, but numerical approximation of the limit solution is difficult due to interface layers caused by jumping coefficients in the model. Divergence-free finite elements have been developed for the Navier-Stokes model so that saddle-point problem is avoided due to the divergence-free condition being satisfied automatically. These elements have been applied to the Brinkman model recently. We propose to apply divergence-free elements combined with decoupling techniques to the mixed Navier-Stokes/Darcy model. With a divergence-free element subspace, the divergence-free condition in the Navier-Stokes sub-model is automatically satisfied, and it is thus unnecessary to solve the saddle-point problem in the discrete space. Furthermore, the divergence-free condition is satisfied pointwise in the divergence-free space instead of being satisfied only weakly as in conventional finite element spaces. These advantages help overcome the numerical and theoretical difficulties present in current decoupling techniques. The research will result in new numerical methods and analysis based on divergence-free elements for the construction and analysis of efficient preconditioners, as well as error estimates and stability analysis for decoupled two-grid and time-marching schemes. With the numerical methods and software to be developed we will also be able to conduct large-scale simulation using Brinkman and Stokes/Darcy models. This will enable us to better understand the interface layers of the coupled flows and may lead to new coupling conditions for the mixed model as a more accurate approximation to the limit Brinkman model. The software may also provide a platform for numerical experiments to evaluate and validate various numerical methods developed for the coupled fluid and porous flows, as well as different models and interface conditions such as two-phase flow and non-Newtonian flow.

603212.label: Realisation of objectives
603212.value: Efficient and effective Stokes and Navier-Stokes solvers are essentially important for building numerical software to simulate coupled fluid and porous media flows, where the fluid is modeled by Stokes or Navier-Stokes equations. Furthermore, divergence-free is a key property of the Stokes and Navier-Stokes equations. The divergence-free-related properties of the numerical methods, in particular the finite elements employed, play a major role in the performance of the associated local solvers, and in turn, the overall performance of the global solver for the coupled model, in terms of stability, convergence, approximation accuracy, etc. We have systematically investigated divergence-free finite elements in the context of Stokes and Navier-Stokes solvers. The weak solutions of the Stokes and Navier-Stokes equations, the velocity and the pressure, belong to H1 and L2 spaces, respectively. A natural mixed finite element for these equations would thus be the pair of the continuous polynomials and the discontinuous polynomials of one degree less. On rectangular grids, such an element, C^0-Qk/C^{-1}-Q_{k-1}, is not stable no matter how large k is. However, it may be shown that the Q_k-Q_{k-2} element is stable, but of a sub-optimal order of approximation, for all k >1 in R2. Bernardi and Maday showed the stability and the optimal order of approximation for the Q_k-P_{k-1} element. Ainsworth and Coggins proved the stability and the optimal order of approximation for the Taylor-Hood type of Q_k-Q_{k-1} element, where the pressure space is continuous too. We therefore considered the Q_k-Q_{k-1} element, but focused on discontinuous pressure elements. For k=1, it is known that the Q_1-Q_0 element is not stable because there is a global weakly-spurious mode in pressure in addition to the well-known checkerboard mode. For k>1, there are works on the Taylor-Hood type of element and also works on the piecewise-constant enriched pressure Taylor-Hood element. However, for the most natural choice of discontinuous pressure elements, there is only one work, the so-called divergence-free finite elements, where the velocity is approximated by continuous Q_{k, k-1} X Q_{k-1,k} polynomials, while the pressure is approximated by discontinuous Q_{k-1} polynomials with one constraint at each vertex. We note that, by choosing the divergence space as the discrete finite element space for the pressure, the spurious modes in discontinuous Q_{k-1} space are filtered out automatically. On the other side, the discrete velocity solution is divergence-free if and only if the discrete pressure space is the divergence of the discrete velocity space. Because the divergence of a Q_{k, k-1} X Q_{k-1,k} vector is a Q_{k-1} polynomial, this element creates a perfect match between the two discrete spaces and produces divergence-free solutions for the velocity. Such a thorough investigation leads us to study the stable and discontinuous pressure Q_k-Q_{k-1} elements. For the discrete velocity space, however, instead of using the subspace Q_{k, k-1} X Q_{k-1,k}, we insist on using the whole Q_k space. As the element of full Q_k-Q_{k-1} space is not stable, we stabilize it by reducing the pressure space C^{-1}-Q_{k-1}, i.e., choosing its subspace for the pressure discretization, while still trying to retain certain element-wise divergence-free property of velocity. Three such subspaces are thus proposed, which leads to three new divergence-free elements. The stability and the optimal order of approximation are proved for these new elements. Comprehensive numerical experiments on these elements are conducted to confirm the theoretical analysis as well as reveal the super-convergence for some of these new elements. Efficient and effective Stocks and Navier-Stokes solvers are then developed by using these new types of divergence-free and stable mixed elements, as well as advanced preconditioning techniques for solving the resulting discrete systems, which are the building blocks in decoupled numerical methods for Navier-Stokes/Darcy models. Based on these efficient local solvers, decoupled multi-grid methods have been further proposed and analyzed for decoupling the interface conditions in the mixed Navier-Stokes/Darcy model. The newly developed divergence-free finite elements and decoupled numerical methods have been incorporated into our software system for numerical simulation of fluid and porous media flows. All the project objectives have been successfully achieved.

603312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603312.value: The power of optical micromanipulation is repeatedly demonstrated in laboratory everyday. Micro or nano particles are observed to move in intense laser fields due to optical forces. Since its conception four decades ago, optical micromanipulation has developed into a well established yet rapidly expanding experimental field. Applications can be found in very diverse areas, including physics, chemistry, and biology, or in other areas that small particles play a role. Nevertheless, its theoretical development is lagging significantly behind. Although in recent years, there appears to be more numerical simulations emerging, they do not always provide the needed insights. We believe that developing analytical models and applying them to study optical micromanipulation is of crucial importance, and this can deepen our understanding of the phenomena. Despite a few pieces of excellent work, successful cases of interpreting an experiment using analytical models are rare. To our knowledge, the only exceptions are for Rayleigh particles where one can write down the explicit expression of the optical force using only the incident field (scattered field is not needed). Nonetheless, a great majority of optical micromanipulations involves Mie particle whose size is comparable with the wavelength. Consequently, a successful analytical theory in the Mie regime is strongly sought for. This requires one to write down a corresponding analytical expression for the optical force. This is provided by a recent development, where we derived an analytical multipolar force expression up to electric octopole order. This expression is the first analytical optical force expression that goes beyond the Rayleigh regime and extends into the Mie regime. Given the incident field profile, the analytical expression allows us to evaluate the optical forces analytically without the need of solving the scattering problem. In this proposed research, we shall analytically and numerically separate the scattering force, absorption force, and gradient force. These forces are associated with very different physical processes and their physics are also very different. Once it is done, we will apply the newly obtained formula to analyze the numerical and experimental results for the distribution of small particles under laser illumination. Finally, we shall investigate the organization of a large number of particles under intense laser illumination, where a small optically bound cluster seems to prefer a different phase compare to a large cluster. Our work will advance the understanding of optical micromanipulation in the Mie regime, thus it may open up new possibilities and applications. 每天，光学微操控在实验领域发挥的巨大作用都得到了不断的证实。人们观察到，微米量级或者纳米量级的粒子依靠光力的作用可以在强激光场中运动。自从光学微操控这个概念在40多年前被提出来，它已经成为实验科学中一个完善并仍然快速发展的领域。光学微操控在包括物理、化学、生物等在内的多个涉及微小粒子的领域中被广泛应用着。但是关于它的理论研究却很滞后。虽然在近些年，出现了很多关于光学微操控的数值模拟，但是这些数值计算并不能提供对光学微操控在物理层面上的解释。我们相信，发展解析的理论模型，并且把它们应用于对光学微操控的研究中是至关重要的，这样做可以加深我们对其物理现象的理解。 在采用解析模型成功解释实验结果方面，虽然有一些出色的工作，但却是非常少的。据我们所知，唯一的例外是对Rayleigh粒子的计算，因为对于这种极小粒子，人们可以只考虑入射场（不需要知道散射场的分布）就可以清楚的写出光力的表达式。然而，绝大多数的光学微操控涉及的微粒是Mie粒子，这种粒子的尺度可以和入射波长相比拟。所以，人们急于寻找一套能成功用于Mie范围微粒的解析理论，从而使得人们能够相应的写出作用在Mie粒子上的光力的解析表达式。我们近期的工作为这方面的发展起到了推动作用，我们解析的得到了多极力表达式，力的表达式保留至电八极矩。这个工作第一次给出了作用在超越Rayleigh范围微粒上的光力的解析表达式，这个表达式可用于对Mie范围粒子的计算。只要知道了入射光场，我们就可以采用这个解析表达式来解析的计算光力，而不需要解决Mie粒子对光场的散射问题。 在这项申请的研究项目中，我们将从解析和数值两方面来区分散射力，吸收力和梯度力。这几种力有着截然不同的物理处理过程，他们的物理意义也很不同。这个工作一旦完成，我们就可以把得到的新公式用于对激光照射下小粒子分布的数值和实验结果的分析中。最终，我们将研究强激光照射下大量粒子的排列结构，初步的研究发现，与大量粒子组成的光束缚粒子簇相比，小尺度光束缚粒子簇似乎倾向于具有一种不同的相位。我们的工作将有助于在Mie范围对光学微操控的理解，这样也将开启出现新现象的可能以及产生新的应用价值。

603312.label: Major findings and research outcome
603312.value: We discovered new phenomena in optical trapping such as negative optical torque and optical twist. We developed analytical methods to qualitative understand new phenomena, and numerical method to model them accurately. For the first time, we correctly separated the gradient and scattering force for Mie sized particle. We note that despite some previous works have claimed that they separated the gradient and scattering force, we are more rigorous. We showed that a cluster consisted of a large number of optically bound particles tends to loose its stability with increasing number of particles, due to degeneracy in vibration frequencies. We are preparing a manuscript for this work.

603312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603312.value: The tool that allows us to separate gradient and scattering force will allow us to study optical trapping in an unprecedented angle.

603312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603312.value: We developed new methods, both analytical and numerical. We discovered new phenomena, such as negative optical torque and optical twist, and they are understood from our theoretical framework. For the first time, we separated the gradient force and the scattering and absorption force. The concept of gradient and scattering force is often used in interpreting optical trapping, but their true fact was never known. We show that a cluster consisted of a large number of particles tends to be unstable.

603512.label: Major findings and research outcome
603512.value: There are two publications resulting from this GRF grant: 1. Generalized Onsager Theory of Liquid Crystals, X. B. Xiao and Ping Sheng, Phys. Rev. E 88, 062501 (2013). 2. Determining Hydrodynamic Boundary Conditions from Equilibrium Fluctuations, S.Y. Chen, H. Wang, T.Z. Qian and Ping Sheng, Phys. Rev. E92, 043007 (2015). On the topic of the first publication, below I will briefly recapitulate the research outcome on this part. The Onsager theory is known to be inaccurate in its prediction of the critical transition density for small aspect ratio hard rods. In this research project we have generalized the Onsager theory in two dimensions by taking into account the short-range order as well as the higher-order virial coefficients, up to the fourth order. By carrying out molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on “molecules” comprising linked hard disks with an aspect ratio l ranging from 5 to 13, we showed that the generalized theory is much improved as compared to the traditional theory, with its predictions of the transition density agreeing well with the simulation results. This indicates the importance of short-range order considerations (in conjunction with steric repulsion) for molecules with l<10, a group which includes the most commonly encountered thermotropic liquid crystals. For the topic of the second publication, a brief description of the research accomplishments is as follows. The hydrodynamic boundary condition represents information that is additional to the Navier-Stokes equation, and necessary for its solution. The lack of a first-principles derivation has made the hydrodynamic boundary condition a classical issue for over 100 years. In this research project, we used molecular dynamics to identify, from equilibrium thermal fluctuations, the hydrodynamic modes in a fluid confined by solid walls, thereby extending the application of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to yield not only the accurate location of the hydrodynamic boundary at the molecular scale, but also the relevant parameter value(s) for the description of the macroscopic boundary condition. The use of the orthogonality condition of the hydrodynamic modes was shown to uniquely locate the boundary location to be inside the fluid in both cases, separated from the molecular solid-liquid interface by a distance Δ that is a few molecules in size. The eigenvalue equation of the hydrodynamic modes directly yields the slip length, which is about equal to Δ in the hydrophilic case but is larger than Δ in the hydrophobic case.

603512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603512.value: There is potential for further development of the research in using hydrodynamic modes to identify the suitable boundary conditions for immiscible two-phase flow, which has been a classical issue to many years. In 2003-2006, the PI has worked with Tiezheng Qian and Prof. Xiaoping Wang in resolving the boundary condition for immiscible two-phase flows. The continuum boundary condition was shown to accurately reproduce the molecular dynamics (MD) simulation results. However, there has never been a MD determination of the relevant boundary condition parameters. The hydrodynamic mode approach of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem can help to resolve it. It can not only verify the boundary condition for the immiscible two-phase flow, but also determine the relevant parameter values.

603512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603512.value: Two research topics were carried out with the support of this GRF grant. For the first topic, the classical Onsager theory showed that for liquids with anisotropic molecules, there can be a transition under which the orientation of the anisotropic molecules becomes aligned as the density increases past a critical value. This represented a crucial observation that started the field of liquid crystal theory. However, the Onsager theory is known to be quantitatively inaccurate in predicting the critical transition density. Here, we improved the accuracy of the Onsager theory in two dimensions by taking into account the short range order as well as the higher order virial coefficients, up to the fourth order. We show that the generalized theory is much improved as compared to the traditional theory, with its predictions of the transition density agreeing well with the simulation results. For second topic, we looked into the classical issue of hydrodynamic boundary condition. While in macroscopic flows this is never an issue, since the boundary condition of zero relative motion between the solid and the fluid have served well the predictions of the Navier Stokes equation for the past century. However, at the microscopic level, with the increasing importance of micro- and nanofluidics, the hydrodynamic boundary condition is by no means clear, as even the position of the “boundary” is ambiguous, owing to the well-known fluid molecular structure in the vicinity of the fluid-solid interface. Here we use the concept of hydrodynamic modes and their mathematical orthogonality property, in conjunction with molecular dynamics, to definitively resolve this classical issue. We have not only identified the microscopic position of the hydrodynamic boundary, but also its relevant parameter value.

604112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604112.value: The enormous interest in graphene (a monolayer of carbon atoms tightly packed in a two-dimensional honeycomb lattice) stems from its unique structure and property richness for potential application. Its high structural and chemical quality preserves its unique properties. It is a fascinating material with great potential of application such as in electronic and optoelectronic devices and circuits; however, many issues still need to be addressed in order to fully exploit graphene for future technological applications. Lattice disorder is a critical issue because it can have profound impact on graphene’s extraordinary properties [1-12]. On the other hand, for practical application, disorder structures are often intentionally introduced in order to modify the properties of functional graphene. Current fabrication techniques of graphene device structures heavily rely on the use of electron beam (e-beam) lithography. Graphene which has undergone e-beam processes is inevitably exposed to energetic electrons that induce disorder in graphene structure. Various forms of disorder induced by e-beam irradiation can significantly impact on graphene’s electronic transport properties. Investigations of the property modification by e-beam irradiation have triggered a debate over the origins of the disorder introduced into graphene and the underlying mechanisms. Recently, we discovered [13] that the e-beam irradiated graphene showed many interesting properties, such as the extremely high sensitivity to surface absorbates and ambient changes, pronounced p-type unipolar field effects, a plateau-like feature in the spectrum of the quantum Hall effect and giant negative magnetoresistance effects. In this project, we propose to develop in-situ techniques to study the fundamental issues of disorder induced by e-beam irradiation with an aim to clarify the disorder structures and formation mechanisms. The in-situ techniques combine sample treatment, atomic imaging and property characterization together so that the surface absorption or contamination from ambient changes can be minimized. Based on the disorder structures observed in the in-situ experiments and subsequent theoretical simulations, we will elucidate the property modification of graphene (e.g., doping states, chemical activation mechanisms, changes of density of states and extremely large magnetoresistance effects) by e-beam irradiation. Employing the modern e-beam technology, we plan to explore nano-sized graphene device structures by nano-patterning based on controllable e-beam induced defect engineering and property modification for potential applications. 人们对石墨烯（碳原子二维蜂窝状排列）的强烈兴趣来自于它的独特结构和丰富的潜在应用。它的结构和化学上的高质量决定了它在电子，光电和各种器件方面的广阔应用价值。尽管如此，目前仍有大量关于石墨烯的问题需要解决，特别是石墨烯点阵上的缺陷，因它可以严重的影响石墨烯的独特性能。另一方面， 作为应用， 缺陷又常常被引入，用来调节石墨烯的性质。目前用来制作石墨烯电子器件的主要方法是电子束曝光。电子束对石墨烯的轰击，不可避免的引入各种缺陷结构，从而影响石墨烯的电学性能。 关于电子束引入缺陷的研究引发了对缺陷机制的大量争论。 我们最近的研究发现电子束辐照石墨烯可以得到很多有趣的性质，如較敏感的表面吸附，和对环境的变化反应，p-型的掺杂效应，量子霍尔效应的平台变化以及巨大的负磁阻等。在此项研究中， 我们计划发展原位技术研究电子束引入的缺陷问题，特别是缺陷的形成机制。我们将原位技术与样品制备，观察和性质鉴定相结合， 同时避免表面的吸附效应。通过原位结构观察和理论模拟，我们将解释电子束对石墨烯性质改变的机制（包括掺杂态，化学激活机制，态密度的改变，巨大磁阻等）。应用现代的可控电子束技术，我们将探索纳米尺度石墨烯器件结构和缺陷对性质的调制，以及潜在的应用。

604112.label: Realisation of objectives
604112.value: 1. We have developed several methods to introduce different types of disorder into graphene and study their effects on graphene property modifications. We have achieved all objectives and discovered a number of important properties in graphene related to different types of disorder. We first develop an in-situ technique to study the fundamental issues of graphene containing disorder induced by high energy electron beam (e-beam) irradiation. Through the e-beam irradiation technique, we have successfully induced hydrogenous type of resonant impurities in single layer graphene. We have studied the impurity formation mechanism by measuring the electrical transport properties at different temperatures and magnetic fields. We found that quantum capacitance measurements were very effective to study the property changes caused by this special disorder structure induced by e-beam irradiation. We have identified that the e-beam induced impurities are the so-called resonant impurity states which located in the energy region around the charge neutrality point in graphene. To explain the experimental data, we have carried theoretical analyses on the density of states modification of the single layer graphene devices. Through the detection of the impurities states and Landau energy levels, we concluded that the impurities enhanced the electron-electron interaction in graphene (APPLIED PHYSICS LETTERS 102, 203103 (2013)). 2. Through the study of the resonant impurities induced by e-beam irradiation and by metal clusters, we have clarified the origins of this special type of disorder and the underlying formation mechanisms. We further elucidated the relationships between disorder structures and property modification in graphene. We discovered that single-layer graphene decorated with a high density of Ag resonant impurities showed unconventional phenomenon of negative quantum capacitance. The graphene devices containing resonant impurities induced by e-beam irradiation showed similar negative quantum capacitance property. The negative quantum capacitance means that the resonant impurities may quench the kinetic energy and drive the electrons to the Coulomb energy dominated regime with negative electron compressibility. This novel property was only observed near the charge neutrality point (CNP). Even without a magnetic field, the negative quantum capacitance was still observable near the CNP. We have confirmed this novel phenomenon by measuring graphene transport properties in the quantum Hall regime. We believed that the negative quantum capacitance behaviour is associated with the kinetic energy quenching effect. Due to the magnetic-field-enhanced Coulomb interactions, the negative quantum capacitance effect is largely enhanced in the presence of Landau levels. We have published these important findings in Scientific Report 3(2013)2041, Scientific Report 3(2012)1772, PHYSICAL REVIEW B 89, 075410 (2014). 3. In order to investigate different types of impurities in graphene, we have explored different nano-sized graphene device structures using nano-patterning techniques. The high quality graphene devices are very critical for the study of graphene property modification. For example, to fabricate single layer graphene capacitance devices, the oxide layer is very critical in determining the quality of the devices. This is because the structure and electronic property of the oxide layer in a capacitor may modified the single layer graphene. We therefore have systematically investigated different oxide layers such SiO2, Al2O3, HfO2, ZnO and Y2O3, and their properties in capacitance devices. We finally determined that Y2O3 is the best oxide material for fabricating capacitance devices of single layer graphene. We observed that a very few short-range impurities have been introduced in to graphene by Y2O3. We have conducted comparison for both AC and DC transport measurements at low temperatures and concluded that charged impurities and inhomogeneity are the main reasons causing modification of the experimental data (e.g., the Landau levels characteristics) under a high magnetic field (details are reported in Nanoscale 5 (2013) 1116). The experimental data obtained is very useful for fabricating high quality graphene capacitance devices. 4. In addition to the resonant impurities introduced by e-beam irradiation and metal adatoms, we have also studied the impurity effects introduced into graphene by Ag large clusters and ZnO quantum dots (Scientific Report 3(2012)1772, Nano research 6 (2013) 619); Small 2013, DOI:10.1002/smll.201202855). Different from resonant impurities, Ag large clusters deposited on single layer graphene caused very strong electron localization effect. The density of states and its local fluctuations have been determined by capacitance measurement. We demonstrate that fluctuations of the local density of states (LDOS) in strongly disordered graphene play an important role in determining the quantum capacitance of the top-gate graphene devices. We explained the interaction between ZnO quantum dots and graphene based on an interesting oxygen-assisted charge transfer process between ZnO and single layer graphene. 5. In graphene-terminated black phosphorus heterostructures, we also observed negative quantum capacitance or negative electronic compressibility which is a many-body effect wherein strong correlations give rise to an enhanced gate capacitance in two-dimensional (2D) electronic systems. We observe capacitance enhancement in atomically thin black phosphorus (BP), a newly emerged 2D layered material,. We explain the negative compressibility based on the Coulomb correlation among in-plane charges and their image charges in a gate electrode in the framework of Debye screening (PHYSICAL REVIEW B 93, 035455 (2016)). 6. Disorder effects exist not only in graphene but also in many other 2D materials. We have observed interesting property modifications by different types of disorder in few-layer MoS2 (Nature Communications 6, 6088 (2015)), iodine doping of graphene (Nanoscale, 2014, 6, 13196), high-quality monolayer graphene grown on insulating substrates (Nanoscale, 2016,8, 2594-2600), atomically thin Bi2Se3 topological insulators (Nano Lett. (2015), 15, 2645) and few-layer black phosphorus (2D Mater. 3 (2016) 015012). The results from this project have provided useful information for better understanding the fundamental problems related to different types of impurities and for designing and fabricating graphene based electronic devices for potential technical application.

604112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604112.value: We have systematically investigated how impurities are introduced into graphene and other two-dimensional layered materials in a controlled fashion, and their effects on the properties of graphene and the layered materials. The experimental results indicate great potential for further development of our research in particular in two-dimensional atomically thin nanostructures (not limited to graphene) and nano-device design. We find that the heterostructures made from graphene and atomically thin layered semiconductor materials show novel properties which are worth of further exploration of quantum transport. We will further study the quantum transport phenomena in this type of heterostructures.

604112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604112.value: This project has led to new methods for in-situ structure modification and transport property characterization of graphene. These methods are suitable for studying other two-dimensional atomically thin layered materials. The outcome of this study has provided crucial information much needed for understanding the origins and formation mechanisms of disorder structures induced by high energy electron irradiation and by metal adatoms in graphene. This study has addressed some critical questions related to impurities such as the negative quantum capacitance and their effects on graphene property modifications. We have elucidated the relationship between resonant disorder and property modification in graphene. We have extended our research to some other newly emerging two-dimensional layered materials. The knowledge gained from this study is highly relevant to fabricating graphene-based or graphene-related novel nano-devices.

604512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604512.value: Neuronal networks are models of the brain. In these networks, a large number of neurons are interconnected by synapses. In the brain’s processing of spatially continuous stimuli such as orientation, head direction, and spatial location, many scientists use continuous attractor neural networks as their working model. This is because they are recurrent networks that can represent spatially localized stimuli using states whose activities are concentrated at the corresponding locations in the network. Hence these states are commonly referred to as bumps. In the conventional modeling of neuronal networks, it is often assumed that the efficacies of the synapses connecting the neurons are constant in short time scales. However, experimental data have consistently revealed that they are dynamical in short time scales, ranging from hundreds to thousands of milliseconds. Short-term depression refers to the decrease in synaptic efficacy when a neuron receives signals from other neurons. Synaptic depression enables recurrent networks to generate a rich spectrum of behaviors, enabling them to perform complex computations on time-dependent inputs. This is relevant to the long-standing issue of how information is encoded and manipulated for computation in the brain. It was recently proposed that the brain has a hierarchical modular structure. In this proposal, we plan to study the rules that govern the computation of the outputs in terms of the inputs of a network module. We also plan to study models of spatial navigation in the brain, focusing on the phenomena of path integration and phase precession observed in rat experiments. Path integration refers to the internal mechanism of accumulating velocity and direction signals to calculate the position of the subject. Phase precession refers to how the timings of the population spikes shift relative to the theta rhythms present in the brain. 神經元網絡是大腦的模型。在這些網絡中，大量的神經元透過突觸互相連接。大腦能處理在空間連續的外來信息，例如方向，頭向，空間位置等。科學家採用連續吸引子神經網絡(continuous attractor neural network)來模擬這些功能，是因為這些動態網絡能以局域化活躍的狀態來表徴具有空間局域化的輸入信息。這些局域化活躍的狀態通稱為活動峰。在傳統的神經元網絡模擬中，一般假設突觸的效能在短時程是不變的，但實驗數據顯示，突觸是具有短時程可塑性的，時間尺度從數百到數千毫秒不等。短時程衰減是指神經元在接收其他神經元的信號後產生的效能衰減。突觸衰減導致網絡動態產生一系列多姿多采的行為，使它們能根據動態的輸入信息作運算。所以這方面的研究針對了一個有深遠影響的課題，就是大腦如何把信息編碼和操控以作運算。最近研究顯示，大腦的結構是層級模塊式的。在這研究中，我們計劃探討網絡模塊把輸入轉化為輸出的運算法則。我們也計劃研究大腦空間導航的模型，重點注意在大鼠實驗中觀察到的路徑整合和相位進動現象。其中路徑整合是指積聚速率和方向的信息以計算主體位置的內在機制，相位進動則指群體陣發式發放(population spike)相對於波發放時間的漂移。

604512.label: Realisation of objectives
604512.value: (1) Delay compensation in neural networks with dynamical synapses We addressed the pervasive problem of time delay in neural information processing [8]. To achieve real-time tracking, it is critical to compensate these delays. We showed that in the presence of short-term depression (STD) of synapses, an effectively constant anticipatory time or zero-lag between the tracking state and the stimulus can be achieved, in agreement with head-direction experiments in rodents. We demonstrated a general relation between the intrinsic behavior of neural systems and their responses to external stimuli [8]. We showed that the parameter regions for delayed, perfect, and anticipative tracking correspond to static, ready-to-move, and spontaneously moving network states respectively. Furthermore, when the stimulus moves with the natural speed of the network state, the delay becomes effectively independent of the stimulus amplitude. (2) Dynamical properties of neural networks with dynamical synapses/short-term plasticity We studied the intrinsic dynamics of neural networks in the presence of STD. We found that in the weak inhibition regime, the spectrum of network behavior includes silent states, static bumps, moving bumps, uniform firing, homogeneous spikes, spikes and anti-spikes [9]. In the presence of a static stimulus, there are 4 basic patterns of behaviors and their mixtures, namely, moving bumps, sloshers, emitters, and population spikes. This rich behavior may be employed by neuronal networks to process information. (3) Resolution enhancement in neural networks with dynamical synapses Conventionally, information was believed to be represented by spike rates in the neural system. Based on our work on population spikes, we considered the ability of temporally modulated activities in neuronal networks to carry information extra to spike rates. This is relevant to the processing of multiple stimuli with separations less than the tuning widths of neurons, and hence cannot be resolved by rate decoding. We proposed a model in which STD causes the system to generate population spikes, enabling each individual stimulus to be represented simultaneously, thus enhancing the resolution of the population code. The model produced results in agreement with transparent motion experiments on monkeys and human [3]. (4) Dynamics of bi-modular neural networks We considered networks with two modules, each receiving a different modality of external stimulus. When the stimuli are disparate, we found that the network response depends on the relative strengths of the two modalities. In particular, when the two stimuli have comparable strengths, it is possible that both responses can be suppressed. This is expected to be relevant to the adaptation of human subjects to motion-sickness when their visual and vestibular stimuli are disparate. (5) Stability of networks Stability of neural network dynamics is subject to optimization principles in networks. In fact, insights can be derived from how fluctuations propagate in networks, which is an issue with broad relevance ranging from neural networks to power grids. We made progress in applying the cavity method to predict how fluctuations of the node resources drive fluctuations of flows in the links. It provides guidance on how link resources should be allocated to enhance network stability. In another frustrated system, namely, the binary perceptron, we provided a refined picture of how clustering and freezing take place in the solution space, which could be useful for future efficient algorithmic design [1]. The work was highlighted by J. Phys. A. [2]. The selection of source locations to supply resources on a network also constitutes a frustrated system. In [4] we proposed optimization algorithms taking into account entropy effects. In [5] we introduced antiferromagnetic interactions to increase coverage, analyzed the scaling of parameters with system size, and proposed optimization algorithms.

604512.label: Major findings and research outcome
604512.value: (1) From statistical physics to neuroscience Using statistical physics approaches relating fluctuations and response functions of many-body systems, we demonstrated a general fluctuation-response relation between the intrinsic behavior of neural systems and their responses to external stimuli [8]. We showed that the parameter regions for delayed, perfect, and anticipative tracking correspond to static, ready-to-move, and spontaneously moving network states respectively. The relation is applicable to neural systems with dynamical synapses such as short-term depression, spike-frequency adaptation and inhibitory feedback loop [8,6] and two dimensions [7]. An important application is that it provides a ubiquitous mechanism for delay compensation, enabling subjects to achieve real-time tracking of motional information. (2) From nonlinear dynamics to neuroscience Using techniques in nonlinear dynamics, we discovered a rich spectrum of spatiotemporal patterns in neuronal networks [9]. An important application is the enhancement of resolution through temporal modulations when closely located stimuli cannot be resolved by rate coding, as evident in transparent motion experiments on monkeys and human [3]. (3) From coupled dynamics to neuroscience Using techniques of studying the dynamics of coupled systems, we found that the responses of two modules of neuronal networks to disparate stimuli can be suppressed or become integrated or remain disparate. An important application is in the area of multisensory integration, relevant to practical problems such as the adaptation of human subjects to motion-sickness. A CRF proposal on this topic has been submitted. (4) From the physics of disordered systems to network and neuroscience applications Frustrations are common in disordered systems. Using the cavity method, we derived the relation between the node resource fluctuations and the link flow fluctuations. Besides applying to stability enhancement in power grids, an important application is the stability enhancement of neuronal networks in the presence of stimulus fluctuations. By considering the entropy of the solution space in another frustrated system, namely, the binary perceptron, we provided a refined picture of clustering and freezing in the solution space. An important application is in future efficient algorithmic design [1]. The work was highlighted by J. Phys. A. [2]. Another frustrated system is the selection of source locations to supply resources on a network. In [4] we proposed optimization algorithms taking into account entropy effects. In [5] we introduced antiferromagnetic interactions to increase coverage, and proposed optimization algorithms. An important application is to analyze the optimality of neuronal networks.

604512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604512.value: Based on our study of the coupled dynamics of network modules, the most natural development is to study the integration and segregation in multi-sensory information processing. It has been known that the brain can optimally integrate information across different modalities and different tasks. Research using a Bayesian approach from statistics provides experimental evidence that neural systems can achieve optimal integration and segregation in multisensory processing. To model the essential ingredients that enable neural systems to perform optimally, we will adopt a recently developed successful decentralized network structure, in which the inputs of each modality are fed to a module. There exist the so-called congruent and opposite neurons in the visual-vestibular area of the brain. Congruent neurons respond to similar visual and vestibular stimuli, whereas opposite neurons respond to differing visual and vestibular stimuli. It is plausible that both congruent and opposite neurons play a role in information integration and segregation, since they exist in comparable quantities. We will propose a theoretical framework for information integration and segregation, develop plausible network implementations that fulfill these tasks, and then analyze the experimental data from our collaborator to assess the models. A GRF proposal on multi-sensory integration has been submitted.

604512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604512.value: Time delays are pervasive in neural systems. The transmission and processing of external stimuli by the brain takes tens of milliseconds. Yet in many circumstances, real-time tracking is essential and may even have life-and-death implications. To cope with time delays, the neural system should have a mechanism to anticipate the upcoming motional information. We show that slow, local and inhibitory feedbacks have the ability to enhance the mobility of the internal representations of the external stimuli, to the extent that they can anticipate moving signals. For example, the mechanism may be short-term depression, referring to the reduction of the efficiency of synapses after prolonged firing, or spike-frequency adaptation, referring to the reduction of sensitivity after neurons receive large number of spikes. Furthermore, inhibitory feedback loops in neural circuits also serve the purpose. The anticipation times achieved by these mechanisms are effectively independent of the speed of the moving stimuli, agreeing with experimental data. We discovered that these different mechanisms can be unified by a common relation in statistical physics relating the fluctuations of the systems in the absence of external stimuli to their responsiveness in the stimuli’s presence. Other dynamics of neural systems are also studied.

604712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604712.value: 由于二維細胞培養的局限性，研究人員正在轉向三維培養模型以便可以更加真實地模擬活體環境。細胞在其體內自然環境下有著和二維培養相比非常不同並且複雜得多的形態。然而，建立三維細胞培養體系有一個很大的挑戰，特別是在組織工程中，就是當細胞團簇體積大于~'毫米時，必須建立一個功能性循環網絡來供應氧氣和營養給細胞並帶走代謝廢物。否則，因爲缺乏氧氣和養分並且代謝廢物的積累，內部的細胞將會壞死。目前尚缺乏有效的方法來創建這樣的循環系統。最近微流體被試用于來解決此問題。然而，目前基于鑄模的方法有一些重大的局限：凝膠微管道很難密封；僅用于制備二維通道網絡；不能在類似細胞外基的凝膠內種入細胞。 在這裏我們提出一個新的策略來制備可模仿體內血管系統的管狀凝膠微流體系統來運輸營養和代謝廢物。我們將用微細加工技術來准確制備管狀凝膠微流體通道；特別是，我們提出了一種新方法可以制備任意三維金屬結構，該結構可方便地轉換成三維管狀凝膠微流體網絡。不同于其他微流體方法，我們的方法將允許我們可以在位于該三維管狀凝膠微流體網絡周圍的細胞外基質內種植細胞；這樣就避開了細胞生長的基質的限制。另外，該管狀微流體結構不需要經過管道鍵合但是可以維持高壓力。並且我們有可能對該管狀通道進行血管化來更進一步地模擬人體血管。 該研究將爲細胞培養，組織工程和生物微機電系統等領域提供一個新的，方便的三維細胞培養循環系統從而大大有助于這些領域的發展。這種新技術將解決在相關領域長期存在的瓶頸—如何有效地建立一個組織內血管循環系統。該系統也可用于與三維細胞培養相關的各種研究，例如，趨藥性，幹細胞分化和藥物篩選。從這些研究得到的信息將幫助我們更好地理解一些關于生物細胞的但不能從傳統二維細胞培養獲取的基礎問題。

604712.label: Realisation of objectives
604712.value: Objective 1. To generate 2D hydrogel tubular microchannel for vascularization in vitro. For this objective, we demonstrated different methods of generating 2D hydrogel tubular microchannels for vascularization in vitro. The first strategy is to make a freestanding alginate 3-D microvascular network by in-situ generation of copper ions from a sacrificial copper template of wires. The copper ions will crosslink and gel a thin layer of alginate solution surrounding the copper wire into a hydrogel, thus forming 2D hydrogel tubular microchannels In the second method, we started from photoresist wire structures made by photolithography or 3D printing technology; the wire structures were embedded into a calcium carbonate/sulfate paste. After burning away the wire structure, the alginate solution was used to fill any remaining space and cured into a hydrogel wire or tube. These tubular microchannels can be used as a model for vascularization in vitro. This objective has been fulfilled completely. 2. To evaluate hydrogel tubular microchannel for vascularization in vitro. To evaluate the hydrogel tubular microchannels formed, we tested physical properties of the formed hydrogel, the diffusion of small and large molecules through the hydrogel tube wall (different concentrations of hydrogel), and also studied the culture of both bacteria and human endothelial cells in the hydrogel tube. Also we integrated a solution-pumping system and a pressure sensing mechanism into the tubular microchannels in order to simulate the human blood circulation system, and we grew human endothelial cells on the channel walls and evaluated the growth and orientation of the cells under different conditions. We thus have achieved this objective. 3. To demonstrate a new method for the generation of arbitrary 3D hydrogel microstructures. For Objective 3, we adapted the approaches we used above to generate arbitrary 3D hydrogel microstructures. The 3D printing technique was used to form the arbitrary 3D structures in plastics (e.g., photocrosslinkable resins). Then the 3D-printed structures were molded into alginate structures, with a similar process to the one we used above to make 2D hydrogel tubular microchannels. In this manner, the 3D printing technology (which is very powerful in making arbitrary 3D geometries), combined with the molding technique, allows transferring the printed structures into the hydrogel materials of interest. This objective has also been achieved successfully. 4. To design and fabricate 3D hydrogel tubular microfluidic networks. For this objective, after we obtained the 3D arbitrary hydrogel (e.g, alginate) structures in Obejective 3, a different type of hydrogel that would be used as the matrix for cell culture was used to fill the free space in the alginate structure. After the second type of hydrogel solution (normally with cells encapsulated) was cured, the alginate gel was then dissolved and removed to form the microchannel network in the second hydrogel structure. With this double-molding method, we can make arbitrary 3D hydrogel tubular microfluidic networks with cells encapsulated. The microfluidic networks function as the “blood circulation” system as in the human body to refresh nutrients and remove metabolic waste for cell growth in the long term. In this manner, we can generate large (one the scale of centimeter) 3D culture blocks or artificial tissues, which are difficult or impossible to realize using other methods. This objective is thus also achieved successfully. 5. To evaluate 3D hydrogel tubular microfluidic networks for 3D cell culture and tissue engineering. For Objective 5, with the systems developed above, we demonstrated the culture of human cells on the hydrogel channel walls or inside the hydrogel matrix. We evaluated the proper dimensions of the microchannels and the space between them for long-term culture of cells. Also, we studied the response and orientation of human endothelial cells under various conditions (e.g., different hydrogel materials and concentrations, various pressure levels in the microchannels, and pore sizes of the hydrogels). Our results demonstrated that our technique can fabricate 3D hydrogel tubular microfluidic networks no matter what the hydrogel materials are, and these 3D hydrogel microfluidic networks can sustain and are highly compatible with long-term cell culture. This objective is thus successfully achieved.

604712.label: Major findings and research outcome
604712.value: The research outcome and major findings can be roughly categorized into the following parts: (1) Materials development and cell patterning. Development of proper materials (e.g., surface functionalization) and cell patterning are important in forming hydrogel structures for cell culture, controlling cellular behavior and subsequent study of cells. We have demonstrated two different methods for coating channel surfaces with a surface-antifouling material (e.g., for applications in capturing circulating tumor cells) and for generating chemical gradients on channel surfaces (publications # 11 and # 5). We also prepared new materials for cell study and for 3D cell culture (publications #8, 14). We also demonstrated the patterning of cells with accurate control of cell positions and cell orientations as well (publications #3, 7, 17, 19). (2) Study of cell behavior and their interactions. We have developed new tools for studying the behavior of cells and their interactions with each other and with their environments. We demonstrated the study of individual cells and cell populations. (publications #2, 5, 7, 9, 17, 18, 19). (3) 3D microfluidic cell culture and tissue engineering. As the ultimate goal of this project, we spent much efforts on 3D hydrogel microfluidic networks for cell culture and tissue engineering, and we have achieved much progress. We demonstrated the application of 3D printing to microfluidics (publications #12, 13), and went further to convert the printed structure into hydrogel microfluidic networks for cell culture (publications # 10, 15). Moreover, we demonstrated various applications of microfluidic technology in the fields of tissue engineering (publications # 3, 6, 15, 16, 17). In addition, because of our significant contributions in the fields, we were invited by two prestigious journals to write review articles on related research (publications # 1, 4) (4) Publications. We have published 19 papers from this project in high-profile, peer-reviewed journals. (5) Student training. We have graduated four PhD students who were involved in this project (see section 10). *** Publication # refers to the corresponding articles listed in Part C.

604712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604712.value: For further development, we will apply our accomplishments in three major areas. (1) Build large-scale 3D artificial tissues as a model for drug screening, which will eliminate or minimize the use of live animals or humans for testing drug efficacy. (2) Build a tumor model to study cancer at the tissue level. Cancer development is a very complicated process that we currently know very little about. A major difficulty is the lack of available models for study. Artificial models like the ones we plan to build would provide a possible alternative to real tumors from patients. (3) In the long term, our methods may contribute to generating artificial tissues that can replace human body parts. We are still very far from this goal; however there is a possibility that, with the 3D model and accurate control, we could differentiate stem cells from a patient into the desired tissue for replacement of the diseased part.

604712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604712.value: Because of the limitations in 2D culture models, researchers are turning to 3D cell culture models that can more closely mimic what happens in living organisms. Cells in their natural, in vivo environment assume very different morphologies than in 2D culture and are much more complex. However, one big challenge in 3D cell culture, particularly in tissue engineering, is that when the cell aggregate is large (>~1mm), a functional circulation network must be created to supply cells with oxygen and nutrients and to remove metabolic waste. Otherwise, cells in the interior will die. Currently, there is still a lack of effective methods to create such circulation systems. In this project, we demonstrated a new strategy of generating tubular microfluidics in hydrogels to mimic the blood vessels in the human body for transportation of nutrition and waste. We successfully cultured human cells in these 3D hydrogel networks and further evaluated the growth and behavior of cells, showing that our system is well suited for long-term 3D cell culture. This technique will solve the long-standing bottleneck in related fields, i.e., how to effectively build a vascular circulation system in tissues.

605012.label: Project Objectives
605012.value: To develop an optimized HEOM (for each specified case of study) consisting of the following components: (i) The best scheme for decomposing the influence bath correlation function into its multiple memory-frequency components; (ii) efficient and also justified methods for at least a partial retrieval of the residue influence outside the finite decomposition space back to the HEOM, so that the number of auxiliary dynamics variables is minimized; (iii) a priori accuracy control criteria on the resulting optimized HEOM for systems under study at finite temperatures. To conduct an efficient HEOM evaluation of nonlinear optical response functions and coherent two-dimensional spectroscopic signals. This will involve the development of block-HEOM formalism and the mixed Heisenberg-Schrodinger dynamics implementation of third-order optical response functions. The state-of-the-art numerical filtering algorithm will also be extended to this new development. Experimental results will be simulated for systems such as bio-molecular light-harvesting complexes. To improve the understanding of efficient and robust energy transfer mechanisms. This consists of (i) HEOM-based construction of the energy transfer efficiency landscape in the multiple-dimensional controlling parameters space of the light-harvesting complexes studied earlier; (ii) characterizing the quantum interplay of multi-chromophoric geometries and environmental interactions with the established landscape profiles.
