610212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
610212.value: During the last decade, wireless communications has witnessed an exponential growth. Such growth is expected to continue due to the emergence of diverse services and as we enter a new exciting era of the “Internet of Things”, which is driving the number of wireless terminals from billions to trillions. This era has been referred to by many experts as the next wireless revolution. Unfortunately, great concerns about its impact on global warming have been on the rise. Currently, the global ICT (Information and Communication Technology) industry is already significantly contributing to the greenhouse gas emissions. With the current expansion speed of wireless networks, its carbon footprint will increase exponentially. For this reason, there has recently been a significant interest in developing more energy-efficient networks for a greener world. Improving energy efficiency is also critical for operators and regulators as the energy cost is increasing rapidly with network expansion. Unfortunately, the conventional design approaches for wireless networks may not be effective in terms of energy efficiency, measured in the amount of data transmitted per unit of energy consumption. These approaches are mainly driven by throughput related QoS requirements, which cannot guarantee energy efficiency. Furthermore, only the energy consumed in the data transmission is considered, but the energy efficiency should be measured by taking into account the total energy consumption in the overall system such as the energy used for backhaul data link, cooling, and AC/DC power conversion. Therefore, new design paradigms and approaches need to be adopted to directly optimize the energy efficiency based on practical power consumption models, while taking into consideration QoS requirements. Cooperative communications is a powerful method for improving the reliability and performance of communication systems. Such an approach is maturing in many aspects, but is still in its infancy when it comes to the deployment issues in cellular networks and the design of energy-efficient wireless networks. In this project, we will endeavor to develop novel cooperative approaches to realize green communications in future wireless networks. The objective is to significantly improve the energy efficiency while satisfying specific QoS requirements. Of particular interest is investigating different metrics to measure energy efficiency in a variety of wireless networks, developing energy-efficient base station cooperation techniques, studying user cooperation to improve energy efficiency, and designing green cognitive base station power management. We will also develop cooperative protocols in networks capable of harvesting energy from the environment. 过去十年中，无线通信经历了一个指数增长的阶段。随着各种无线设备的涌现以及“物联网”时代的到来，我们预期这种高速增长的势头将持续下去。许多专家将这个时代定义为无线通信领域的下一场革命。然而，这场革命对于全球暖化的影响已经引起了广泛的关注。目前，信息通信产业的温室气体排放量在全球总排放量中已经占有相当大的比重。随着无线网络的高速膨胀，无线通信的“碳足迹”无疑将会迅速增长。基于这个现实，开发更高能源利用率的通信网络来建设一个更加绿色的地球成为当前一个重要课题。与此同时，随着无线网络的持续膨胀，更高的能源效益对于运营商和政府管理部门来说也具有重要意义。 通信系统的能源效率是以单位能源能够传输的数据量来衡量的。传统无线通信系统的设计忽略了能源效率方面的考虑，而只侧重于与传输速率相关的性能指标。比如，传统的设计只考虑与数据传输相关的能量损耗，而忽略了其它的能量消耗，例如基站通信链路，基站的制冷设备，和模数转换器的能耗等。能源效率的衡量需要综合考虑整个系统的能量损耗，所以我们需要采用一种全新的方式来设计未来通信网络，需要在考虑了用户服务质量的基础上直接优化能源效率。 合作通信是一种能有效改进无线通信系统中传输可靠性和通信性能的技术。这种技术在很多方面已趋于成熟，但是合作通信在基于更高能源效率的无线网络设计中的研究还处于起步阶段。在这个研究项目中，我们会致力于开发全新的合作通信协议以实现未来无线网络中的绿色通信。我们主要的目标是在保证特定服务质量要求的基础上极大的提高无线网络中的能源效率。具体的研究项目包括考察无线网络中用来衡量能源效率的各种指标，开发有效的基站合作方式来提高能源效率，研究基于用户合作的方法来提高能源效率，设计基于感知功能的基站能源管理方案。我们还会设计有效利用可再生能源来进行通信的合作协议。

610212.label: Realisation of objectives
610212.value: With seamless wireless access and the proliferation of mobile applications, the number of smart mobile devices and mobile data traffic have been increasing at an unprecedented rate. This is further accelerated by new application scenarios such as the Internet of Things and Augmented Reality. In order to meet such strong demands, mobile operators have to deploy more and more access points, and thus the energy consumption of wireless networks has been growing at an alarming rate. This has caused growing concern over their environmental impact and led to high demand for green communication systems. This project deals with green communications with a particular emphasis on cooperative technologies for green communications systems. Specifically, the project has covered several important wireless communication systems, including energy harvesting communication systems, dense wireless cooperative networks, and massive MIMO systems. Our research objectives covered energy-efficient base station cooperation (Research Objective 1), energy-efficient relaying protocols (Research Objective 2), cooperative communications for energy harvesting systems (Research Objective 3), as well as investigating the impacts of different system parameters on network energy efficiency (Research Objective 4). Our investigation closely followed the research objectives. One main focus was the development of energy-efficient base station cooperation technologies in dense wireless networks, i.e., Research Objective 1, for which we proposed a novel group sparse beamforming algorithm to enable effective network adaptation to reduce network energy consumption. Given the increasing popularity of massive MIMO systems, we also investigated several key design issues in networks with large-size antennas at each base station. To address Research Objectives 2 and 3, we carried out a thorough investigation of energy harvesting communication systems, where communication nodes are powered by renewable energy sources. Our results showed that cooperative relaying is a key technology for improving the performance of energy harvesting systems. Moreover, communication systems with hybrid energy supplies, i.e., powered by both energy harvesting and grid energy, are very promising, as they use renewable energy sources, while overcoming their intermittent availability by supplementing stable grid energy. Our results provided important design insights into green communication systems and demonstrated the impacts of key system parameters on network energy efficiency, i.e., addressing Research Objective 4. Overall, we believe that we have satisfactorily completed this project. By covering all the research objectives in the project, we are able to produce academically and practically significant research while contributing meaningfully to the training of students in this important area (Research Objective 5). Specifically, as a result of this project, two PhD students (Yaming Luo and Yuanming Shi) have been trained and graduated, and one (Yuyi Mao) will graduate in 2017. In addition, with fruitful research outcomes, we were able to publish seven journal papers, as well as, ten conference papers in IEEE flagship conferences. In particular, one journal paper [journal paper #2] received the prestigious IEEE Marconi Prize Paper Award in Wireless Communications in 2016.

610212.label: Major findings and research outcome
610212.value: Our main findings and research outcomes are as follows: • Energy Harvesting (EH) Wireless Networks: Our investigation on EH networks mainly focused on cooperative relaying protocols to overcome the random energy arrivals. We also investigated systems with hybrid energy supplies. In [conference paper #2], [journal paper #1], the optimal joint scheduling and power allocation algorithm were developed for two-hop EH systems. In [conference papers #4, #5, #6], [journal paper #6], different cooperative relaying protocols were proposed to enhance the performance of EH systems. In [journal paper #4], prospects of powering small cell networks with EH were investigated. In [conference paper #8], [journal paper #5], cellular networks with hybrid energy supplies were investigated, and different optimization approaches were proposed. In [conference paper #10], we investigated different retransmission protocols for systems with EH receivers. • Energy-Efficient Dense Cooperative Wireless Networks: We considered a new network architecture to enable efficient cooperation, i.e., the Cloud Radio Access Network (Cloud-RAN), for which there is a central Cloud that handles all the baseband signal processing. In [conference paper #3] and [journal paper #2], we minimized the total network power consumption of a Cloud-RAN, including both the transmit power of access points and power consumption of backhaul links connecting access points to the Cloud. We developed a new algorithm, which allows to adaptively switch off some access points and the corresponding backhaul links. Moreover, in [conference paper #1], we analyzed the network energy efficiency of dense small cell networks based on the Poisson point process modes for node locations. • Energy-Efficient Massive MIMO Systems: Massive MIMO is a recently proposed technology to improve the spectral efficiency and energy efficiency of wireless networks by equipping each base station with a large number of antennas. However, there are several practical challenges. Here, we focused on the channel state information (CSI) acquisition for massive MIMO. In [conference paper #7] [journal paper #3], we investigated the impact of pilot contamination, due to the reuse of the same pilot in different cells, on the user capacity in TDD massive MIMO systems. In [conference paper #7], we proposed to utilize partial support information of sparse channels to reduce the CSI training overhead using compressed sensing. In [journal paper #9], we also investigated energy efficiency of millimeter-wave systems. In particular, we compared two different hybrid precoder structures, i.e., the fully-connected and partially-connected structures, which showed that they provide tradeoff among energy efficiency and spectral efficiency.

610212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
610212.value: There are lots of interesting directions for further research. Most existing works on EH systems assumed simple energy arrival models, and efficient design methodologies are needed when considering more realistic energy and channel models. Moreover, it was commonly assumed that either the transmitter or receiver is EH powered, while systems with both EH transmitters and EH receivers have received much less attention. As demonstrated in our recent result [conference paper #10], systems with EH receivers will pose additional design challenges, and more efforts will be needed to investigate such systems. Due to its great potential in solving the spectrum crunch problem, mmWave communications are attracting increasing attention. Energy efficiency is one major concern for designing mmWave systems, as high frequency hardware components will consume more power. Thus, it is critical to jointly consider the algorithmic and hardware aspects. For example, there have been lots of investigations on hybrid precoding, which only requires a small number of RF chains. As shown in [journal paper #7], different hybrid structures may bring different energy efficiencies. Considering the important role of mmWave communications in the upcoming 5G networks, it will be critical to develop energy efficiency-aware design methodologies for mmWave systems.

610212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
610212.value: As the success of wireless communication systems continues, there is increasing concern about their growing energy consumption and associated environmental effects. Thus, there has been significant interest in developing energy-efficient wireless networks as one of the key requirements of 5th generation (5G) wireless systems. This project aims at developing effective cooperative technologies for green communications. Our investigation has covered important systems, including renewable energy powered networks, dense cooperative networks, and massive MIMO systems. Many significant research results were produced and helped to unravel important design insights for green communications. Our investigation of energy harvesting wireless systems has demonstrated the great potential of powering communication systems with renewable energy sources. We have developed effective group sparse beamforming algorithms to enable network adaptation in dense cooperative networks to reduce the total network energy consumption. Moreover, our investigation of massive MIMO has provided solutions to key challenges in upcoming 5G wireless systems. The significance and value of this project are extraordinary. The obtained results will have a major impact not only in academia but also industry. They are also expected to play a major role for the sustainable evolution of wireless networks and reduction of their carbon footprint and environmental impacts.

610412.value: 失明的影响不仅是经济上的，也是社会的，它会显着的影响生活质量并约束独立性和行动能力。电刺激已被证明可以在患有黄斑变性和色素性视网膜炎失 明的患者身上产生视觉感知。今天，视网膜假体已是一个激烈的跨学科研究课题。设计一个可使用的视网膜假体是非常复杂的，因为它必须在能源效率和 物理尺寸上比得上生物组织; 这是一个非常具有挑战性的要求。眼下所有的实验产品都非常笨重，耗电量高，以至于为患者带来很大的不便，这些系统需 要在眼内植入笨重的收发器和线圈来实现射频传输。 本项目提出了一个全新的方法来彻底改变这些视网膜假体设备的设计。 这里提出的想法是用光信号通过类似“虚拟现实”设备一样安装在护目镜上的LED 显示器来传送二进制图象数据,而非试图使用射频连 接来发送图像数据或将捕获的图像直接投影病人的视网膜上。 由护目镜上的显示器所产生的光流将外部相机所获取的图像进行数字编码然后被集成在可植入装置上的感光器件探测到。 接收到的光流有两个用处：（ⅰ）它可以被解码成像素刺激电极的电流强度（ⅱ）植入装置通过采集这束光流来为自己供电。 利用此概念，可植入装置的设计将大大简化，它只需要一个单一的感光器，一个解码器，刺激电路和电极的阵列。 此外，植入装置可以由光信号来校正，刺激电路的重要的客户参数，比如说刺激电流， 可以通过发送一组光比特信号来设置。 这种创新的方法有三个优点： （一）小型化和低功耗，不再需要植入射频收发器和线圈; （二）通过光路数字传输实现稳定的数据传输，而无需光感器阵列或将图像投影到视网膜 （三）使用光比特流简单和可靠地实现了植入设备的高效率光学校准。 相比较当前的技术，这将使临床试验过程更加简单。 本项目为开发植入式视网膜假体提供了独特和创新的基础技术。 此外，这里提出的研究将会成为大中华地区视网膜假体研究的先驱并为这个重要的新兴领域提供一个独特的跨学科研究培训机会。 这将进一步凸显香港的创新研究文化。这项技术的开发将深远地影响社会，并会产生显着的知识产权，这将为商业化提供许多的途径。

610412.label: Realisation of objectives
610412.value: The report has been successfully conducted and resulted in a excellent output including: 10 journal papers (8 published and 2 in progress), 5 conferences and 6 PG students graduating (3 PhD and 3 MPhil). The research activities in relation to the project objectives are summarized as follows: Objective 1: Integrate an optical transceiver using an array of LED and polarization photodetectors for data and energy harvesting in a compact and low power retinal prosthesis (100%). With respect to this objective, a novel circle polarization shift keying based integrating front end was designed to improve the performance of the polarization based optical wireless receiver, enabling wireless communication at a data rate of 32 Kbit/s with a Figure-of-Merit (FoM) of 12pJ/bit. At the receiver side, an improved recycling folded cascode operational transconductance amplifier with gain boosting and enhanced phase-margin has been proposed. Among four variants of folded cascade amplifiers that have been implemented in TSMC 0.18-µm CMOS process under same power and area constraints, the proposed amplifier achieves the lowest settling error of less than 0.5% compared to 1.1% settling error by Improved Recycling Folded Cascode (IRFC), 1.4% settling error by Recycling Folded Cascode (RFC) and 30% settling error by conventional Folded Cascode (FC) amplifier. From the optical photodetector perspective, we designed a non-correlated-double-sampling (non-CDS) pixel readout scheme along with a high-resolution successive-approximation-register (SAR) analog-to-digital-converter (ADC) with 13.6b effective resolution (ER). Measurement results from the prototype chip in 0.18-µm technology show that the two techniques improve LDI sensing precision by 6.9 dB and 4.4 dB (compared to a 10b ADC), respectively without analog pre-amplification. Results related to this work have been published in top journal. The polarization data transmission system is connected to a thin photo-patterned micropolarizer array for CMOS image sensors. The proposed micropolarizer fabrication technology completely removes the need for complex selective etching. Instead, it uses the well-controlled process of ultraviolet photolithography to define micropolarizer orientation patterns on a spin-coated azo-dye-1 film. The patterned polymer film micropolarizer (10 um x 10 um) exhibits submicron thickness (0.3 m) and has an extinction ratio of 100. The polarisation-based optical communication was also validated using a demonstration prototype. Objective 2: Design a smart electrode array for cell stimulation and sensing using low power CMOS temperature sensors (100%) We developed a novel method for the fabricating of a high-density carbon nanotube microelectrode array (MEA) chip. Vertically aligned carbon nanotubes (VACNTs) were synthesized by microwave plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition and thermal chemical vapor deposition. The device was characterized using electrochemical experiments such as cyclic voltammetry, impedance spectroscopy and potential transient measurements. Through-silicon Vias (TSVs) were fabricated and partially filled with polycrystalline silicon to allow electrical connection from the high-density electrodes to a stimulator microchip. In response to the demand for higher resolution implants, we have developed a unique process to obtain a high-density electrode array by making the microelectrodes smaller in size and designing new ways of routing the electrodes to current sources. Results related to this work have been published in Sensing and Bio-Sensing Research Journal and resulted in completion of 2 MPhil theses. Apart from that, we also investigated a compact voltage-mode bandgap voltage reference (BGR) as a foundational component for a better temperature sensor. Instead of using overhead circuits, the silicon bandgap narrowing effect is exploited for bipolar junction transistor’s (BJT) curvature reduction and residual curvature correction. Prototype measurements in a 0.18-µm standard CMOS process show that the curvature of the BJT is effectively reduced from its inherent 3.6 mV to 1.4 mV. The proposed BGR measures a minimum temperature coefficient of 8.7 ppm/°C from −55 °C to 125 °C by batch trimming one resistor. After a curvature trimming, it further improves to 4.1 ppm/°C. The BGR has a minimum supply voltage of 1.3 V, 4.3 µA nominal current consumption, 0.03%/V line sensitivity, and 2 mV/mA load sensitivity at 25 °C. The output rms noise in the 0.1∼10-Hz band measures 10.23 µV. Objective 3: Design the encoder circuitry for data transmission and optical energy harvesting (100%). With respect to this objective, we investigated data encoding schemes in the context of the energy harvesting and data conversion revolving around the image sensor. The data to be transmitted is encoded in the proposed analog-to-information (AIC) converter based image sensor which combines an energy-efficient charge-pump bit-image processor (BIP) with an area-efficient successive-approximation-register-single-slope (SAR-SS) hybrid analog-to-digital converter (ADC) via a charge-transfer-amplifier (CTA). This scheme significantly reduces the inefficiency of conventional approaches which is largely due to the way data are compressed after quantization and storage, as is observed in discrete-cosine-transform (DCT) or discrete-wavelet-transform (DWT). In the optical energy harvesting front, we designed an array of 128x96 photodiodes having 21um pixel pitch with a 39% fill factor, generating 9.7 uA at 3500 lux ambient light condition. It is expected to require significant photodiode area to generate sufficient power for running the image sensor at 30 fps. To alleviate this issue, we employed avalanche energy generation (AEG) scheme which lowers the power consumption by enabling only active pixels to be read-out after which they enter into a power generation mode. Objective 4: Build and perform electrical and optical characterization of the retinal prosthesis's building blocks in a laboratory setting (100%). With respect to this objective, we developed a high-density stimulator system that can effectively improve the energy efficiency using the power supply modulation and energy recycling techniques. A comprehensive systematic evaluation platform was proposed to observe the system behavior and performance under large output power dynamic range requirements as well as varying design parameters. To provide a systematic optimization strategy for designing micro-stimulator systems, a comprehensive system model that can evaluate the system behavior under wide input and output dynamic range operations specific to the application requirement is developed. System behaviour and optimization including the parasitic losses throughout the energy flow path, close-loop stability and transient performance are established and analyzed. A verification platform is also developed to validate the proposed models. Measurement results show that the system behaviour match well the simulated ones. To improve energy efficiency of existing micro-stimulator designs, an energy efficient multi-channel power-supply modulated micro-stimulator capable of energy recycling is proposed. The stimulation efficiency is enhanced by recycling the charge from electrodes during the cathodic stimulation phase. A chip prototype fabricated in a standard 0.18-µm BCDLite CMOS process optimized using the proposed model is designed. Measurement results show that the stimulation efficiency is vastly improved over the conventional fixed-voltage supply-based stimulators. Fast reference tracking is achieved under wide stimulation conditions during the inter-phase transition. Improved stimulation safety is also ensured by the reduced heat generation across the current drivers and the intrinsic isolation of the power supply from the electrodes in case of device failure. Results related to this work have been published in IEEE Design and Test Journal as well as a PhD completion. More results are being submitted for publication (1 under review journal and another journal paper in progress).

610412.label: Major findings and research outcome
610412.value: This project resulted in a number of very interesting findings summarised as follows: 1. The fabrication results of carbon nanotube electrodes showed that, when synthesizing the electrode samples downward instead of upward, the impedance was decreased by 90 times, the double layer capacitance was increased by 55 times, the effective surface area was increased by 25 times, the water dipole thickness decreased by half, and interface resistance was decreased by 20 times, when compared to the previous art. A complete process has been derived and tested. 2. The proposed energy-efficient multi-channel power-supply modulated microstimulator is proven to be capable of generating a continuous supply voltage while supporting energy recycling. When compared to the FV-supply based topology, our work can achieve a power saving of 70%. The stimulation efficiency can be improved with an increase in power conversion efficiency and the number of simultaneously driven electrodes. A prototype chip was fabricated and tested. 3. An image sensor with non-CDS PMOS reset pixel and low-noise SAR ADC is proposed enabling to improve imaging performance and power consumption. The SAR ADC is able to achieve high effective resolution without sacrificing energy efficiency thanks to its low-noise time-domain comparator. The proposed imager features the best FoM amongst published works. 4. An AIC using a number of low-power circuit techniques such as fully dynamic CTA, SAR-SS ADC, and capacitive charge-pump, is proposed. The resulting AIC features the best-in-class energy consumption figures. The measured results show that the proposed image compression technique can lead to a four-fold reduction in energy consumption per pixel and a four-fold improvement in frame-rate while the PSNR is only degraded by 5 dB. This makes the proposed design highly suitable for compact high resolution imaging applications which require low power consumption and high bandwidth, such as retinal prosthesis. 5. The proposed optical wireless receiver based on modulation in the polarization domain robustly rejects DC photocurrent generated by the background light. It achieves FoM of 12pJ/bit at data rate of 32 Kbits/s with a sensitivity of -31dBm/mm^2. The receiver can operate at data rate of 512 Kbps with a sensitivity of -18dBm/ mm^2 when sampled twice per bit. 6. The proposed global digital controller for multi-channel micro-stimulator can achieve flexible stimulation with a power consumption of 18 µW/column while enabling global power-supply modulation and real-time TEI monitoring for improved stimulation efficiency and safety.

610412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
610412.value: While many plausible results were achieved, there are some paths for further possible exploration: 1. In order to fabricate implantable electrodes, the substrate is desired to be flexible. However, large area flexible film is not easy to handle. Silicon Migration Technique (SiMiT) is a prospective solution to fabricate large area flexible substrates on bulk silicon. 2. In this project, the bulk tissue reference voltage is assumed to be held constant, halfway between VDD and VSS . However, in the case that residual charge tends to be accumulated in implant sites over a long time frame, we need to consider a dedicated power supply to correct for the background charge build-up. A single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) topology can serve the purpose well with a shared inductor which allocates its energizing and de-energizing time slots to an additional output reference voltage. 3. In-vivo tests will be a natural extension for this work. Due to the very limited budget of this project, this phase cannot be achieved at this stage and was actually revised from the original objectives.

610412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
610412.value: Retinal implants are today possible remedies for patients who have lost their vision due to degenerative eye conditions. About half of all cases of blindness are caused by retinal diseases such as retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) that can improve the vision via high-density multi-channel electrical stimulation. New electrode materials and micro fabrication recipes are needed for developing the future generation of high-resolution retinal prostheses that are fully functional and safe. Therefore, we developed a retinal prosthesis that uses VACNT microelectrodes that are efficient, safe and small and employs TSV polycrystalline silicon interconnects with flip-chip technology to solve the problem of routing for large microelectrode arrays. To efficiently accommodate the high-density microelectrode array, the stimulator design is built on two major conceptual pillars: 1) fully isolated power supply modulation circuits that is decoupled from the loading electrode array; and 2) efficient usage of the energy by the minimization of the Joule heating across the conduction path. A power/energy efficient and area efficient optical wireless receivers for Retinal Prosthesis applications were also investigated. System level and circuit level techniques have been adopted to minimize the active area of the on-chip CMOS photodiode and to reduce the power consumption.

611012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611012.value: With the dimension of transistors being continuously reduced to the sub-50nm regime, it is difficult to turn off the transistor due to short channel effects. The increased leakage current that leads to excessive power dissipation is now a major challenge in integration circuits. New device structures that deviated from conventional transistors have been proposed to extend the scaling process when the transistor dimension is further reduced. Among the many proposed structures, the tunneling Field Effect Transistor (tFET) has been considered the most promising solution for lower power circuits and systems by many major industrial players such as IBM, Intel and Infineon. While a number of tFET structures have been demonstrated, there is still a large discrepancy between the theoretical anticipated performance and experimental results. In addition, the modeling and simulation platform for tFET is still very primitive. Therefore, it is important to develop a modeling and simulation framework to study the physics, optimize the device performance and predict the behavior when such devices are used in circuits and systems. The goal of this project is to develop the core physical model to describe the characteristics of nanowire tFET together with experimental calibration and validation. In addition, a framework to optimize the structural parameters will be developed to enable the optimization of emerging integrated circuit (IC) with tFET. Following the state-of-the-art tFET structure reported, this project will focus on two particular structures: (1) all-silicon nanowire tFET; (2) heterojunction tFET with silicon germanium source. The study will start with deriving the output characteristics based on the non-equilibrium green function (NEGF) for quantum transport together with tight-binding (TB) extended Huckel theory (EHT) and empirical pseudopotential method (EPM) for bandstructure calculation. With the numerical simulation framework established, the effects of various structural parameters will be studied in order to derive explicit equations based on the more macroscopic band-to-band and drift-diffusion models to correlate the output characteristics of tFET to terminal voltages and structural parameters. In addition, a series of test structures will be designed and fabricated to calibrate and verify the model. 隨著被連續地減小到子-50nm的制度的晶體管的尺寸，它是由於短溝道效應的晶體管難以關閉。增加的現在是一個重大的挑戰，導致功耗過大的漏電流集成的電路。新的器件結構偏離傳統的晶體管已經被提出來延長縮放處理時，晶體管的尺寸是進一步降低。在眾多的建議結構，隧道場效應晶體管（TFET）一直被認為是最有前途的低功耗解決方案許多主要工業的球員，如IBM，英特爾和英飛凌的電路和系統。雖然有許多的穿透式場效電晶體結構已被證明，仍然有一個大理論預期的性能和實驗結果的差異。此外，為東帝汶信託基金的建模和仿真平台仍然是非常原始的。因此，重要的是要發展建模與仿真框架研究物理，優化設備的性能和預測的行為時，這種裝置是中使用的電路和系統。 該項目的目標是開發的核心物理模型來描述納米線TFET特點與實驗校準和驗證。此外，將發展到一個框架，以優化結構參數啟用的優化新興的集成電路（IC）與TFET。繼國家的最先進的東帝汶信託基金結構據悉，該項目將集中在兩個特定結構：（1）所有-矽納米線TFET的的（2）與矽異質結TFET 鍺源。所產生的輸出特性的基礎研究將啟動在非平衡格林函數（NEGF）量子傳輸與緊束縛（TB）的擴展Hückel理論（EHT）和能帶結構計算經驗贗勢法（EPM）。隨著數值模擬框架成立，將被研究的各種結構參數的影響，以便得出明確更宏觀的帶帶和漂移擴散方程的基礎上模型關聯的東帝汶信託基金端子電壓和結構的輸出特性參數。此外，一系列的測試結構將被設計和製造成校準和驗證的模型。

611012.label: Realisation of objectives
611012.value: We have gracefully completed all the revised objectives according to plan except that we have employed an alternative approach for objective number 2. When the proposal was drafted, the amount of experimental data for Tunnelling FETs was quite limited. In the last few years, there are tremendous improvement in TFET fabrication techniques and a lot of experimental TFET data were made available. As experimental data is more convincing to verify an analytic model, we have supplemented the atomistic simulation with experimental calibration. The atomic simulation has been used to extract unobservable physical quantity (such as tunnelling probability) while experimental data has been used to valid the complete model. With this new approach, we have developed a complete analytical model for heterojunction TFETs (objective #1) and implemented the model to a circuit simulator provide by the i-MOS platform (http://i-mos.org). The model can be downloaded and executed by researchers worldwide (objective #3).

611012.label: Major findings and research outcome
611012.value: A compact model of a TFET is necessary to simulate circuit constructed using TFETs. Before this project, a circuit simulation friendly compact model does not exist. While there are some physical models published, these models are either not complete (for example, only I-V model but no C-V model) or only cover certain voltage range. The model developed in this work is the first model that is developed with the following features: 1) a complete model including current-voltage, charge-voltage and capacitance-voltage characteristics 2) account for transport in both the tunnelling region and the drift region under the gate 3) account for heterogenous source-to-body material systems that cover a wide range of material pairs 4) including the density of state for lightly doped source for accurate tunnelling calculation 5) including gate-to-channel tunnelling model 6) the model equations and their derivatives are smooth and continuous to ensure convergent in circuit simulation. Most of the physical formulations have been included in the recent publication in TED by Y. Dong. In order to explain the complete features of the model, we decided to write a book chapter to include all the derivations and formulation instead of individual paper to avoid the problem of page limit. The book chapter has been published in an edited book on TFET published by Springer in 2016. Furthermore, the model has been implemented into an online circuit simulator on http://i-mos.org. Researchers around the world can download the source code or directly perform the simulation using the online simulation engine provided by i-mos.org.

611012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611012.value: The model can be enhanced by adding the following: 1) non-ideal effects such as non-uniform channel cross-section and doping 2) parasitics effect such as source/drain series resistance and gate-to-source/drain capacitance 3) new-material system including 2-D material such as graphene and MoSi2 4) including a parameter extraction tools 5) simplify the source codes and improve the smoothing function to improve convergence when implementing the model into the circuit simulator 6) adding a reliability simulation modules to include circuit aging such as NBTI

611012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611012.value: Tunnelling Field-Effect transistor (TFET) is believed to be a solution to overcome the power crisis in modern electronic circuits. To perform simulation of TFET, a compact model is needed. There was no such model before this project. In this project, we have developed a power TFET models including many advanced features. The model has been extensively verified by theoretical data from atomistic simulation as well as experimental data from fabricated TFET. The model is also smooth and continuous to ensure convergent during circuit simulation. In addition to publishing paper, the source code has been released to the users through the i-MOS (http://i-mos.org) platform for users to download. In addition, it has also been implemented into a online circuit simulation engine provided by http://i-mos.org that users can directly perform simulation online. All the tests indicated that the model is fully functional and compatible with the requirements defined by the circuit simulator.

611112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611112.value: Large-scale civil infrastructures such as long-span bridges are icons of civilization and modernization for any society. Maintaining the safety and integrity of these critical infrastructures so that they can provide a relentless and uncompromised service to the public is of utmost importance to society. Structural health monitoring (SHM) has recently emerged as an important technological solution to this issue. The SHM can provide a measurement of the operating and loading environment and the critical responses of a structure to track and evaluate the symptoms of operational incidents, anomalies, and/or deterioration or damage indicators that may affect operation, serviceability or safety reliability of the monitored structure. Due to this important and unique capability, SHM has now become a “standard” integrated part of any newly built long-span bridge worldwide. The proposed study intends to develop a subspace identification technique which is capable of providing online and close to real time assessment, of the health condition of long-span bridges. This technique will be developed under the wireless smart sensor network (WSSN) framework which allows the formation of a dense array of sensors for more accurate damage assessment and the flexibility of adding additional sensors when needed. As compared to the other techniques, the subspace technique does not need a parametric model of the monitored structure and can be easily used in a multi-input-multi-output condition which fits perfectly for the case of large-scale civil engineering structures equipped with a WSSN containing a dense array of sensor. It is believed that the proposed study will enhance the software aspect of the WSSN in terms of providing it with a faster and more reliable damage assessment capability. Such a development will be beneficial to the health monitoring of existing and new long-span bridges. 大跨度橋樑等大型基礎設施是社會文明和現代化的圖示。維護這些基礎設施的安全和完整，以便它們可以服務社會是極為重要的課題。在這議題上，結構健康監測可提供重要的技術解決方案。結構健康監測可以量測設施在外力下的反應，並堆追蹤和評估可能會影響操作或結構安全的異常情況。鑒於此重要和獨特的功能，結構健康監測現已成為世界各地新建的大跨度橋樑的標準配備。本研究課題計劃發展子空間識別技術即時評估大跨度橋樑的時態特性。這子空間識別技術會發展於無線智慧傳感網路架構下，以密集排列的感應器更靈活及準確地評估橋樑操作安全和可能的破壞狀況。與其他技術相比，子空間技術不需要參數化的模型，並可適用於多輸入多輸出的無線智慧傳感網路。本研究將提供大跨度橋樑健康監測更快、更可靠的損害評估能力。

611112.label: Realisation of objectives
611112.value: The objectives of this study were to develop an online recursive identification technique for tracking time-varying characteristics for long-span bridges and to validate the technique using a wireless smart sensor network (WSSN) system. The study has been completed with the assistance of two PhD students, MAN Shin Hang (graduated in August 2015) and ZHONG Kai Hui (to graduate in 2017) and one former PhD student, Dr. Rawlins SHI (graduated in June 2010) and one former MSc student, Ms Melissa WONG (graduated in June 2015). To address the first objective, Dr. Shi and Ms Zhong have helped to develop a total of four online recursive techniques for tracking time-varying characteristics for civil engineering structures. Some experimental results have also been obtained to validate the accuracy and applicability of these techniques. To address the second objective, Dr. Man has investigated one particular WSSN platform, the Imote2 platform, which showed promise as a platform for developing new types of sensors. However, the technical specifications of Imote2 turned out to be rather limited. Furthermore, Imote2 had been discontinued and no further technical support was available. It was hence decided that an alternative WSSN platform, the smartphone system be explored. Smartphones come with a few advantages, such as low price, large amount of memory, high-power CPU, various wireless communication options, making them suitable for use as a WSSN platform. In this study, an attempt to improve the low sampling rate and low accuracy of the built-in sensors in the smartphones had initially been made by Ms Wong who has decided to withdraw from the research due to personal reason. Ms Zhong had also proposed and developed a smartphone based WSSN platform by integrating an Arduino ADK board with an Android smartphone. Unfortunately, due to the delay caused by the Imote2 platform mentioned above, she was unable to directly implement the techniques developed from the first objective on this smartphone platform within the project period. She, however, has agreed to continue this endeavor and is aiming to accomplish this task by the middle of 2017.

611112.label: Major findings and research outcome
611112.value: (1) Two wavelet-based identification techniques have been developed to identify time-varying parameters in a shear-beam building using incomplete and noisy measurement data. As the wavelet multi-resolution expressions can accurately represent arbitrary functions, these wavelet-based techniques can be used to identify various forms of time-varying behavior exhibited by the building's parameters. Two wavelet-based identification techniques, story-by-story and sub-structural, have been proposed targeting different data availability. To minimize the effect of measurement noise, a wavelet decomposition level selection scheme and a multi-rate Kalman data fusion technique have also been adopted. (Publication #1). (2) An input-output recursive combined subspace identification technique was also proposed for tracking modal parameters of a time-varying structure under non-stationary earthquake excitation. The technique incorporated an orthogonal projection and an instrumental variable approach to eliminate the effect of earthquake input and measurement noise, respectively. A bi-iteration subspace tracker was then applied to extract the structural modal parameters. Both numerical and experimental results showed that the proposed technique can closely track structural modal parameters under non-stationary earthquake excitation. (Publication #4). This technique has further been extended to track modal parameters of a time-varying structure under unknown and non-stationary input using through iterative oblique projection and orthogonal projection. (Publication #5) (3) One candidate wireless smart sensor network (WSSN) system, the Imote2 platform, has been researched for possible implementation of the techniques developed above. The connectivity and capability of the Imote2 platform have been explored and tested on the development of a wireless crack sensor. This sensor has been developed by incorporating a laser-based optical navigation sensor board (ADNS-9500) into the Imote2 (Publication #2 and #3). It was however found that the technical performance of Imote2 was rather limited. Furthermore, Imote2 had been discontinued and no further technical support was available. It was hence decided that an alternative WSSN platform, the smartphone system be explored. Smartphones are low-priced and equipped with a large amount of memory, high-power CPU, and various wireless communication options. There are also many low-cost power banks to support these smartphones for long-term operation. These advantages have made smartphones a viable option for the WSSN system. In this study, an attempt to improve the low sampling rate and low accuracy of the built-in sensors in the smartphones was made. An Arduino ADK board which can accommodate some high performance sensors has been integrated with an Android smartphone. (Publication #6).

611112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611112.value: This study can be considered a proof of concept and provides an option for monitoring potentially time-varying characteristics of civil engineering structures. The developed techniques can be programmed in the suggested smartphone-based WSSN system for a quick assessment of a structure’s health condition. Possible further developments of the research include: (1) developing user interfaces such as apps on smartphones for better control of the techniques; and (2) implementing the developed system on practical structures or bridges. These developments can be carried out by undergraduate students as their final-year projects or research projects.

611112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611112.value: Large-scale civil infrastructures are icons of modernization for any society. Maintaining the safety of these critical infrastructures is of utmost importance to society. Structural health monitoring (SHM) has emerged as an important technological solution to this issue. A SHM system can track and evaluate the symptoms of operational incidents, anomalies, or damage indicators that may affect serviceability or safety of the monitored structure. In this study, several time-domain identification techniques which can be used in the SHM system have been developed. These techniques can track anomalies or damages to civil engineering structures. Furthermore, a wireless smart sensor network (WSSN) system allowing the formation of a dense array of sensors for more accurate assessment has been investigated. The proposed techniques do not need a parametric model of the monitored structure and can be easily used in a multi-input-multi-output situation which is perfect for the case of large-scale civil engineering structures equipped with a WSSN system. The proposed study has enhanced the software aspect of the WSSN in terms of providing it with a faster and more reliable damage assessment capability. Such a development will be beneficial to the health monitoring of civil engineering structures.

611212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611212.value: Cooling systems are a major source of carbon emission, contributing to 40-50% of the total building electricity consumption, while buildings themselves contribute to about 90% of total electricity consumption in Hong Kong. Adsorption cooling systems offer a number of distinct advantages as they do not require compressors while the solid adsorbents and their corresponding refrigerants (e.g. water) are environmentally friendly and easy to handle in operation and maintenance. However, studies of adsorption cooling systems have not received enough attention compared to liquid absorbent systems. Adsorption cooling systems require a low-grade thermal energy source with little electricity requirement for other system components. Integrating adsorption cooling systems with waste heat from industrial processes, boilers in hospitals and hotels, commercial kitchens, or solar panels, etc., can substantially reduce the dependence on fossil fuels making them potential candidates for net zero energy building operation. Trigeneration (power, heat and cooling) can be achieved by employing adsorption cooling systems. Major challenges facing commercialization of adsorption cooling systems include low specific cooling power (SCP) and coefficient of performance (COP). In this proposal, a systematic theoretical-experimental research program is proposed to develop new compact and efficient adsorption cooling systems. The present research program includes: 1) development of novel microstructured adsorbents featuring superior adsorption properties compared to currently available adsorbents; 2) performing in-depth analysis on flow/heat/mass transport mechanism involved in the adsorption/desorption processes using nondimensional analysis, analytical modeling and numerical simulation; and 3) design, fabrication and scaled-down testing of new adsorption systems featuring the proposed new composite adsorbents, in order to predict and optimize large-scale operation. A major thrust of the present research will be on developing novel composite adsorbents by embedding carbon nanotubes into adsorbents such as zeolite 13X/CaCl2. The adsorption properties of the new composite adsorbents will be characterized. Advanced heat and mass transfer models involving gas-solid interfacial transfer kinetics will be developed to understand the fundamental parameters governing the component and system performance. A parametric study will be performed to investigate the system operation cycles in terms of COP, SCP and electricity consumption under controlled conditions. The experimental results will be used to verify the developed models and system optimization. This research will reveal the impact of composite adsorbents on adsorption cooling systems and the potential of adsorption cooling systems in large-scale industrial and commercial usages. The findings will provide engineering design tools that can be used for devising novel, practical, environmentally friendly adsorption cooling systems. 冷卻系統是碳排放的主要來源，佔了總建築物用電量的40％至50％，而建築物用電量本身佔了香港的總用電量的90％左右。吸附式製冷系統提供了許多獨特的優勢，它們不需要壓縮機，而固體吸附劑及其相應的製冷劑（例如水）對環境友善，在操作和維護上亦易於處理。然而相對於液體吸收式系統，吸附式製冷系統的研究還沒有得到足夠的重視。吸附式製冷系統需要低級熱能源及少量電力需求來驅動其他系統組件。將工業生產過程中的餘熱和吸附式製冷系統結合，例如醫院和酒店的鍋爐、商業廚房或太陽能電池板等，可以大大減少對化石燃料的依賴，使吸附式製冷系統有潛質成為零碳建築的作業系統。通過使用吸附式製冷系統，可以實現聯合能源生產（冷凝、加熱、以及發電）。吸附式製冷系統的商業化所面臨的主要挑戰包括低比製冷功率（SCP）和熱能使用效率（COP）。在此計劃書中，建議了一個系統性的理論和實驗研究計劃，用以開發新的緊密及高效能的吸附式製冷系統。目前的研究項目包括：1）開發新型的微結構吸附劑，跟目前可用的吸附劑相比，具有優越的吸附性能； 2）採用無量綱分析，理論模型和數值模擬深入分析在吸附/解吸附過程中所涉及的流量 / 熱量 / 質量傳輸機制; 和 3）設計，製造和按比例縮小測試使用新擬議複合吸附劑的吸附系統，以預測和優化大規模運作。本研究的主要目的是發展新型複合吸附劑，將碳納米管嵌入到吸附劑，如沸石13X/CaCl2中。新型複合吸附劑的吸附性能將會經實驗被定性。包含氣 - 固界面轉移動力學的先進傳熱及傳質模型將被發展，用以了解影響組件和系統性能的基本參數。在控制環境下，將進行參數化研究分析系統運作周期，並以COP、SCP以及用電量表示結果。實驗結果將會用作驗證所建立的模型和系統優化。本研究將揭示複合吸附劑在吸附式製冷系統中的影響和吸附式製冷系統在大型工業和商業用途的潛力。研究結果將提供工程設計工具，可用於設計新穎，實用性強，對環境友善的吸附式製冷系統。

611212.label: Realisation of objectives
611212.value: All project objectives have been achieved. Multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-embedded zeolite 13X/CaCl2 composite adsorbents with different MWCNT mass ratios were synthesized for use in adsorption cooling systems. The addition of MWCNTs can form a thermally conductive layer on the composite zeolite particles and fills up the empty spaces between them, creating more paths for heat transfer to increase the overall thermal conductivity. Compared to metals, MWCNTs have a high thermal conductivity (15,000 times higher than zeolite 13X and 10 times higher than pure copper). CNTs not only have high thermal conductivity, but also a much lower volumetric heat capacity of 0.662 J/cm3K, as opposed to 3.442 J/cm3K for copper. This shows that the thermal response of CNTs is faster. There are many small empty spaces between the adsorbent particles. The material properties of the composite adsorbents were investigated through XRF, XPS, BET, TGA and thermal conductivity tests to determine the optimized composition for the cooling system. The MWCNT-embedded composite adsorbent prepared with the highest MWCNT mass ratio of 100:1 has the highest carbon concentration of 12.91 wt%. The addition of MWCNTs in the composite adsorbent can increase the overall specific surface area and total pore volume of the adsorbent. The useful range of water adsorption of composite adsorbents is much higher than that for zeolite 13X. A theoretical model based on the area-contact approach was developed to predict the effective stagnant thermal conductivity of a surface-coated porous material. The modified model was developed to account for an additional layer of coating on the particle. This modified area-contact model can also be employed in different applications where surface-coated porous materials are used. An FEM simulation model was built showing that the modified area contact model has better agreement with the simulation result than the area contact model. This modified area contact model can be applied to predict the effective stagnant thermal conductivity of a surface-coated porous material. System simulation was conducted to investigate the effect of heat recovery, mass recovery, pre-heating and pre-cooling processes and their combinations on the system performance of a double-bed adsorption cooling system. The model developed consists of pressure variations and detailed compressible flow with flow resistance, which other similar studies have not taken into consideration. Thus a detailed simulation of mass recovery, and pre-heating and pre-cooling processes is included in this study. A double-bed adsorption cooling system with silica gel and water as adsorbent–adsorbate pair was built for verifying the simulation models. Based on the simulation results, it was found that the basic cycle provided a COP and SCP of 0.20 and 57.6 W/kg, respectively. By conducting heat recovery for 30 seconds, the COP was increased by 20% to 0.24 compared to the basic cycle. The SCP was also increased to 66.4 W/kg, a 15% increase. The major advantage through conducting mass recovery is in the SCP, which was increased by 40% to 80.8W/kg. Additionally, performing only the pre-heating and pre-cooling process can also bring benefits to the system. Therefore, for adsorption cooling systems that cannot carry out the mass recovery and/or heat recovery cycles, performing pre-heating and pre-cooling process only is recommended. This not only reduces costs, but also simplifies the control program of the systems. Moreover, mass recovery followed by pre-heating and pre-cooling cycle is highly preferred when the SCP is the optimization target, since the SCP was hugely increased by 41% to 81.4 W/kg. An adsorption cooling system with a novel composite material as the adsorbent and water as the adsorbate has been built and the system performance was studied experimentally under various working conditions. A much lower desorption temperature can be utilized to desorb the composite adsorbent when compared with the zeolite 13X adsorbent. Under the same operating conditions, the SCP of the adsorption cooling system using the composite adsorbent is approximately 30% higher than that of the same system using silica-gel as the adsorbent. Although a longer adsorption/desorption phase time (cycle time) is required for the adsorption cooling system equipped with the composite adsorbent, it shows a better cooling performance than that with the silica gel adsorbent if a lower chilled water temperature is required. Various operating sequences (i.e. heat recovery, mass recovery, pre-heating and pre-cooling cycles) of the adsorption cooling system have also been investigated. The heat and mass recovery cycle can considerably improve the SCP and COP of the adsorption cooling system, by about 126% and 125%, respectively. However, heat recovery requires fitting of extra equipment to the adsorption cooling system.

611212.label: Major findings and research outcome
611212.value: The MWCNT-embedded zeolite 13X/CaCl2 composite adsorbents with different MWCNT mass ratios were synthesized. The operational range of water uptake is 0.09 kg/kg for zeolite 13X and 0.5 kg/kg for the composite adsorbents. The effective thermal conductivity is improved significantly, and reached 0.27– 0.8 W/mK at temperature ranging from 30 oC to 70 oC, where the thermal conductivity of zeolite 13X is only 0.08–0.13 W/mK in the same temperature range. It can be concluded that the addition of MWCNTs does not have noticeable effects on adsorption capacity and can improve the effective thermal conductivity of the composite adsorbent. A FEM simulation model of an adsorber was built to predict the performance of different adsorbents. Under the same operating conditions, the MWCNT-embedded zeolite 13X/CaCl2 composite adsorbent performs much better than zeolite 13X. The SCP of the adsorber using the composite adsorbent is improved by 6.5 times compared to zeolite 13X. The modified area-contact model for predicting the thermal conductivity was verified by FEM simulation. According to the modified area-contact model, the coating layer thickness, c, the solid/fluid thermal conductivity ratio, λ, and the porosity, ϕ, are factors that can affect the effective stagnant thermal conductivity. The improvement is higher for a thicker coating layer and higher thermal conductivity of the solid phase. Experimentally verified system simulation was conducted. The simulation can closely predict the performance of the real system, showing the high accuracy of the simulation. Based on the simulation results, the mass recovery followed by pre-heating and pre-cooling cycle is preferred for most adsorption cooling systems to improve both the COP and SCP. For those adsorption cooling systems in which the mass recovery process cannot be carried out, performing the pre-heating and pre-cooling only cycle is preferred. Adsorption cooling system prototypes have been built. A longer adsorption/desorption phase time is required if the adsorption cooling system is equipped with the composite adsorbent. If a high cooling water temperature, above 29 oC, or low chilled water inlet temperature, below 17 oC, is utilized, the composite adsorbent shows a better cooling performance than the silica gel. Besides, the heat and mass recovery cycle made a huge improvement to the COP and SCP of the adsorption cooling system among all the recovery cycles. However, more equipment is required if the heat recovery cycle is conducted. Thus, mass recovery together with the pre-heating and pre-cooling cycle is preferred.

611212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611212.value: 1. The simulations conducted in this study can be classified as detailed adsorber simulation and whole system simulation. The two parts are not inter-connected. Multi-scaled simulation should be conducted to fully study the system performance. 2. The measurement of material properties of the composite adsorbents is not fully completed. For example, the adsorption capacity and effective thermal conductivity of the composite adsorbents should be measured for a larger range of temperatures and water vapor pressures. 3. From the prototype experiment testing results, system design has a very influence on the system performance. Thus, different system designs should be considered to further improve the performance of our system.

611212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611212.value: Adsorption cooling systems (ACS) are environmentally friendly cooling systems that do not use refrigerants or compressors. ACS can be powered by waste heat to largely reduce the energy consumption of buildings. Cooling systems are a major source of carbon emission, contributing to 40-50% of the total building electricity consumption, while buildings themselves contribute to about 90% of total electricity consumption in Hong Kong. One of the core components of the ACS is the adsorbent, and its material properties can largely affect the system performance. A new carbon-nanotube-embedded zeolite 13X/CaCl2 composite adsorbent has been developed with superior adsorption properties. This adsorbent was found to have higher water adsorption capacity, higher thermal conductivity and lower desorption temperature than many traditional adsorbents. Different mathematical model and numerical simulations have been developed to understand the transfer mechanisms between materials in different phases and inside the adsorbent beds. Scaled-down prototypes have been built to verify the model and simulation, and to investigate the real performance of the ACS. Based on the research conducted, the performance of ACS has been improved by 126% and 125% in terms of cooling power and COP.

611412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611412.value: Membrane separation is one of physical separation processes used in wastewater treatment. It can produce very high quality water, but membrane surface fouling or concentration polarization can lead to significant permeate flux declines. Electro-membrane filtration (EMF) has been established as a viable process to mitigate the membrane fouling. There are two key challenges in the way of industrial application of EMF: 1) expensive electrodes (anode and cathode) for the EMF system; 2) the significant amount of extra electrical energy required for EMF operation. This project aims at overcoming the two key challenges by 1) fabricating a composite inorganic tubular membrane with the interal and external surfaces acting as anode and cathode. The electrodes would be made from metal oxides with non-precious metals being the key component; 2) characterizing the membrane-electrode system by finding the optimal conditions for filtration of oily wastewater, a tough effluent to treat. The objectives are: 1) fabricating an EMF composite membrane with Ebonex-based titanium oxide, and a non-precious metal oxide. 2) identifying any synergy between electrochemical technologies (electrophorolisis, electroflotation, or electrooxidation) and membrane separation 3) optimizing the performance of the EMF system by reducing the energy consumption, increasing the productivity and enhancing the product quality. The methodology involves coating of an inorganic membrane with precursor chemicals and then calcinating the precursors to form a layer of conducting metal oxides. The metal oxides may be further treated to improve their conductivity and also to enhance their electrochemical properties in applications such as electrooxidation. The membrane fouling will be measured with different types of electrodes and different electric field strengths in oily wastewater treatment. The permeate flux, the treated water quality, the energy requirement, and also the stability of the electrodes will be investigated. The long term impact of the project could be very significant. It would change current membrane filtration practice (especially for the situation involving the inorganic membranes), a market of over US$10 billions. The success of the project would mean longer service life for the membranes, less consumption of cleaning reagents, and less consumption of energy for enhanced quality of the end product. The technology could find wide utilization in the chemical, environmental and food industries. 膜分離是處理廢水的物理方法之一。它的處理效果很好,可以產出高品質的淨水。 然而,膜污染或濃差極化會導致膜通量降低。電膜過濾 (EMF)已經表明是可以降低膜污染的可行操作。電膜過濾的工業化面對兩大挑戰: 1)昂貴的電膜過濾體系的電極(陽極及陰極); 2)電膜過濾過程中需要的可觀數量的額外電能。 本課題旨在通過如下方法解決以上的兩大挑戰: 1) 製備一種複合的無機管式膜; 該膜的內外壁分別作為陰陽極。電極材料主要為非貴重金屬氧化物。 2) 通過分離難處理的含油污水來檢驗該膜並找到電膜過濾的最佳操作條件。

611512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611512.value: 基於寬禁帶半導體氮化鎵，以AlGaN/GaN高電子遷移率電晶體（HEMT）為代表的異質結電子器件已成功進入射頻微波功率放大器市場，應用于軍用雷達系統及商用無線基站。此外，氮化鎵基電子器件在性能上有望遠超越當前的主流矽技術，成為用於新一代電源轉換器的高壓功率器件，在全球範圍內得到深入廣泛研究。 在許多需要高工作電壓（如高於600 V），失效自保護的功率電子應用中，在新的挑戰出現的同時，部分過去解決的問題也重新浮出水面。對平面型AlGaN/GaN HEMT器件而言，最困難的問題之一在於鈍化距離有源區溝道很近的器件表面。電流崩塌效應不僅會降低電源轉換效率，同時也會導致器件的穩定性及可靠性下降。若缺少適當的表面鈍化，AlGaN/GaN HEMT功率器件很容易受到該不良效應的影響。為抑制電流崩塌，氮化矽（SiNX）鈍化技術被廣泛採用。在功率放大器應用場合，漏極偏置電壓處於中等大小，該技術能有效抑制AlGaN/GaN HEMT器件的電流崩塌。儘管如此，測試結果表明，當漏極偏置電壓高於100 V時，氮化矽鈍化的商用AlGaN/GaN HEMT功率器件沒有足夠的電流崩塌抑制能力。 除電流崩塌問題外，氮化鎵基金屬-絕緣體-半導體HEMT（MIS-HEMT）器件的可靠性已成為另一挑戰。此類器件在其柵電極下方包含一層薄介質層。MIS-HEMT器件由於具備高正向閾值電壓及高柵電壓擺幅等優點而非常適於做功率開關。對於AlGaN/GaNMIS-HEMT器件而言，目前研究最為詳盡的柵介質為氧化物介質，如氧化鋁（Al2O3）和二氧化鉿（HfO2）。然而，這類氧化物會在介質與III族氮化物的介面處引入高密度的介面陷阱，從而影響器件的可靠性。 本研究專案旨在通過系統研究由等離子增強型原子層澱積技術製備的氮化鋁（AlN）薄膜來解決以上問題，即表面鈍化與柵介質材料的技術開發與研究。目標主要在於開發氮化鋁薄膜技術及論證氮化鋁的以下固有益處：（1）與氮化鎵及其他III族氮化物晶格失配度小，從而可能在氮化鋁與下方III族氮化物之間形成高品質且近乎完美的介面；（2）更大的禁帶寬度，可減弱表面態的載流子注入以及降低柵極漏電。本專案的目標為開發基於氮化鋁的表面鈍化和介質複合層技術。

611512.label: Realisation of objectives
611512.value: Objective #1: To develop effective remote plasma pretreatment techniques to obtain epi-ready III-nitride surfaces for the deposition of high-quality AlN thin films Remote plasma pretreatment (RPP) techniques have been developed, featuring NH3-Ar-N2 remote plasma applied to the sample in sequence. The RF (radio-frequency) power of the plasma has been optimized to minimize surface damage. NH3 is used to remove native oxide while Ar is used to remove other particles attached to the surface. N2 plasma plays the most important role of nitridizing the surface. Objective #2: To develop and optimize the AlN thin films with PEALD to achieve the desired current collapse suppression Mono-crystalline AlN thin film has been successfully deposited on c-plane Ga-face (Al)GaN surface. Cross-sectional TEM reveals that the first 2~3 nanometers (4~6 monolayers) of the AlN film is of a monocrystalline nature, while polycrystalline AlN structures start to form as the thickness increases. It has been experimentally confirmed that the AlN thin film deposited on Ga-face GaN contains positive polarization charge (Qp) with a high density, in the range of 1E13/cm2. It is this high-density positive polarization charge that can compensate for any adverse effects of the possible interface traps. In the worse-case scenario, if all of the interface traps are filled with electrons, there should be a total negative interface charge of Qit. As long as Qp>Qit, there should be no net negative charge in the region above the barrier layer, and thus the 2DEG density in the conducting channel will not decrease. As a result, the surface-state-induced current collapse can be totally suppressed. A PEALD-AlN/PECVD-SiNx stack has been developed as a practical passivation structure. This is mainly because a thin AlN film alone is not enough to serve as a passivation layer. The passivation layer typically has a thickness in the range of 50-100 nm for compatibility with the field-plate structures. Such a thickness is difficult to obtain for AlN thin films because of the slow deposition rate (a few nanometers per hour) in PEALD. After several rounds of test iterations, the optimum AlN/SiNx stack has a thickness combination of 4nm/50nm. This passivation stack has been used in many fabrication rounds since 2014 and has been very robust without any instances of failure thus far in terms of providing effective suppression of current collapse. Furthermore, the compatibility of AlN/SiNx passivation stack with the LPCVD-SiNx (deposited at 780 degrees Celsius and used as the gate dielectric) has also been experimentally confirmed. There was a concern about the stability of AlN at temperatures higher than 500 degrees Celsius because AlN tends to crystallize at such high temperatures. The SiNx cap has proven to be an effective protection layer in preventing the underlying AlN from crystallization during the LPCVD-SiNx deposition. Objective #3: To conduct detailed structural and electrical analysis for the optimization of the PEALD grown AlN thin films Transmission electron microscopy has been conducted to reveal the mono-crystalline nature of the PEALD AlN thin films. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has been measured to reveal the reduction of Ga-O bonds at the surface after remote-plasma nitridation. Capacitance-voltage (C-V) characteristics have been measured to quantitatively determine the interface state density at the PEALD-AlN/GaN interface, which is controlled at a level below 1E12/cm2. Objective #4: To carry out detailed device characterization with the aim of identifying the underlying mechanisms and issues related to AlN thin films grown with PEALD Through quasi-static and ac C-V characterization, the major mechanisms of effective passivation by PEALD-AlN thin films have been determined to be the effective compensation of interface traps by positive charge polarization.

611512.label: Major findings and research outcome
611512.value: We have developed a plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition technique that enables the deposition of high-quality AlN thin film on Ga-face GaN-based heterostructures. The AlN thin films exhibit a monocrystalline structure when deposited on a GaN surface. The PEALD technique has several important benefits including in-situ low-damage surface cleaning and nitridation, precise thickness control, and low thermal budget. The PEALD-AlN thin films have been successfully integrated with the fabrication process of GaN-on-Si lateral power devices and can deliver a robust passivation technique that is effective at a wide range of operating temperatures from room temperature to 200 degrees Celsius. The mechanism of the effective passivation has been investigated and revealed to be originating from the compensation of surface traps by the positive polarization charges in the AlN thin films. An AlN-based nitridation interlayer has been proven to deliver a high-quality interface between gate dielectric and GaN with low interface trap density. Such a technique has been widely adopted by research groups around the world in the pursuit of GaN MOSFETs or MIS-HEMTs with improved stability.

611512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611512.value: The fact that mono-crystalline AlN thin film can be grown at 300 degree Celsius using PEALD suggests an alternative way of preparing the extreme bandgap materials (e.g. AlN, Ga2O3, diamond) for device applications. Preliminary investigation is on-going to deploy AlN as the active channel of transistors. A research proposal will be submitted after promising preliminary results are obtained.

611512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611512.value: GaN power switching devices are emerging as promising candidates for next-generation power conversion systems with high conversion efficiency and high power density. Currently, GaN lateral heterojunction structures dominate the technology development because of material and processing maturity. However, since the conducting channel is typically located 10~20 nm away from the surface, the surface states originated dangling bonds or impurity absorption at the surface could adversely affect the current conduction in the channel, causing a well-known problem of dynamic on-resistance degradation. In this project, a robust surface passivation technique has been developed to compensate the surface states with polarization charges inherently produced in mono-crystalline AlN thin film grown by atomic layer deposition method. Significant current collapse suppression and dynamic ON-resistance reduction are obtained in GaN power devices passivated with the new passivation technique. The physical mechanism of the passivation technique has been systematically investigated and verified. This thin film passivation technique will be beneficial to GaN-based power electronics in both high-voltage power switches and millimeter-wave power amplifiers.

611812.label: Project Title(Chinese)
611812.value: 在加權區域中最短路徑問題

611812.label: Project Objectives
611812.value: Design new efficient approximation algorithms for the shortest path problems in the plane and in three dimensions under the weighted region model.
rows: Design new efficient approximation algorithms for the shortest path problems in the plane and in three dimensions under the weighted region model.

611812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611812.value: Computing the shortest path between two points in a geometric environment is a classical problem. While the complexities of the problem in the plane and in some cases in three dimensions have been settled under the Euclidean metric, the problem status is much more open for the well-known extension to the weighted region model. In this model, weights are associated with the regions, and the cost of a path is the sum of the subpath lengths in each region multiplied by the weight of that region. This model allows the path planner to avoid regions that are more difficult to traverse. Our goal is to obtain new efficient approximation algorithms for the shortest path problems in the plane and in three dimensions under the weighted region model. 一個經典問題是計算一條最短路徑連接幾何環境內的任意兩點。在某些情況下,這問題的複雜性已獲斷定。但在加權區域中,這問題的複雜性仍未有定論。一條路徑的值是將在不同區域的子路徑長度乘以區域權,再加起來的總和。區域權可模擬穿過不同的區域,有難有易。這項目是要設計快速的近似算法去解決二維及三維的加權區域中最短路徑問題。

611812.label: Realisation of objectives
611812.value: We have realized the objective of the project. We designed three new approximation algorithms for the weighted region problem and related problems. Each algorithm can report a (1+eps)-approximate shortest path, where eps is the relative error in the range (0,1) specified by the user. For the weighted region problem in the plane, we obtain an approximation algorithm that runs in O((kn + k^4*log(k/eps))/eps * (log (Wn/eps))^2) time, where n is the number of vertices of the input triangulation and W is the maximum region weight. The value k is the smallest integer such that the sum of the k smallest angles in the environment is at least pi. The value k can be as small as O(1) and as large as O(n). So our running time varies from O((n/eps)*(log (Wn/eps)^2) to O((n^4/eps)*(log (Wn/eps)^2). That is, our algorithm is a FPTAS and the running time is nearly linear if there are only O(1) tiny angles. The only FPTAS known previously has a running time that is proportional to n^8 and log (1/eps). So for a fixed eps, we have a much lower polynomial dependence on n. For the weighted region problem in a three-dimensional environment modeled by a tetrahedralization, we designed an approximation algorithm that is sensitive to the distribution of tetrahedra with poor aspect ratio. Let A be any constant fixed beforehand. We call a tetrahedron skinny if its aspect ratio exceeds A. Let k be the size of the largest connected component of skinny tetrahedra. The significance is that if k is O(1), the running time is O(n*eps^{-7}*(log (W/eps))^2*(log (NW/eps))^2), where n is the number of input tetrahedra, W is the maximum input weight, and N is the largest magnitude of the input vertex coordinates. Moreover, the running time remains polynomial in n, 1/eps, and log(NW/eps) when k is O(log log n). This is the first result with a polynomial running time when the smallest angle among the tetrahedra is not bounded from below by any constant. We also obtained an approximate shortest path algorithm for navigating on terrains. The cost objective function can be any linear combination of path length and total ascent, and the segments on the path can be required to satisfy a user-specified gradient constraint. It is the first FPTAS that can approximately optimize a path under such general conditions. Moreover, it runs fairly efficiently with a running time of O((n^2/sqrt(eps))*log n + n^2*(log n)^4)).

So our running time varies from O((n/eps)*(log (Wn/eps)^2) to O((n^4/eps)*(log (Wn/eps)^2). This result appears in the second conference article in Part C. For the weighted region problem in a three-dimensional environment modeled by a tetrahedralization, we designed an algorithm that is sensitive to the distribution of tetrahedra with poor aspect ratio. Let A be any constant fixed beforehand. We call a tetrahedron skinny if its aspect ratio exceeds A. Let k be the size of the largest connected component of skinny tetrahedra. The significance is that the running time is polynomial in n, 1/eps, and log(NW/eps) when k is O(log log n). This is the first result with a polynomial running time when the smallest angle among the tetrahedra is not bounded from below by any constant. This result appears in the third conference article in Part C. We also obtained an approximate shortest path algorithm for navigating on terrains. The cost objective function can be any linear combination of path length and total ascent, and the segments on the path can be required to satisfy a user-specified gradient constraint. It is the first FPTAS that can approximately optimize a path under such general conditions. Moreover, it runs fairly efficiently with a running time of O((n^2/sqrt(eps))*log n + n^2*(log n)^4)). This result appears in the first conference article in Part C. We also solved the minimax regret 1-sink location problem in dynamic path networks. It models the problem of placing the best exit on a path with respect to the maximum evacuation time, where the number of evacuees at different locations can vary within some input ranges. This result appears in the first journal article in Part C.

611812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611812.value: There is still room for further studies in the weighted region problem in three dimensions. Most notably, it is unclear whether there exists a polynomial bound on the complexity of the shortest path. The best known upper bound is only the naive bound of O(2^n), where n is the number of tetrahedra in the environment. If one can obtain a polynomial upper bound, the next step is to investigate whether there exists an FPTAS. It is also worthwhile to study whether one can identify more general cost function beyond linear combination of path lengths and total ascent that can still be approximately optimized for polyhedral surfaces or terrains. Constraints more general than the gradient constraint are also interesting.

611812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611812.value: The unit cost of a path in an environment can vary as some parts may be more difficult to traverse than other parts. The weighted region problem models this variation by assigning different weights to different regions. The cost of a subpath in a region is its length multiplied by the region weights, and the path cost is the sum of the costs of subpaths in different regions. We propose new, efficient approximation algorithms in the plane and in three dimensions for this problem. We also study a related shortest path problem on terrains that optimizes both the path length and the total ascent, which models the additional energy needed in climbing uphill.

611912.label: Project Objectives

611912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611912.value: Recent advances in smart phone technology have led to the proliferation of mobile applications. These applications typically feature event-driven interaction between software, human, and hardware. Since the execution of these applications often involves user interaction and event triggering from hardware sensors, their automated testing is difficult. This severely weakens the use of testing to detect faults in mobile applications. Static analysis provides a promising alternative to testing because it is able to uncover program faults without actual execution. Analyzing event-driven applications statically, however, involves two significant challenges. First, these applications typically involve a large number of event handlers, which rarely have explicit control flows or call relations between one another. Static analysis based on control flow information may conclude that these handlers can be invoked with arbitrary orders. This leads to a lot of handler invocation orders and combinations; many of which are infeasible. As a result, the fault report contains a high rate of false positives. Second, as mobile applications are typically long running and continually adaptive to events, it is impractical to conduct precise analysis of the entire execution for all possible adaptive behaviors. How to abstract them to scale up the analysis, however, remains an open question. In this project, we propose to address these two challenges and develop an effective technique to detect mobile application faults arising from the interactions among event handlers. Our technique will be able to identify common software faults such as null pointer dereferences and resource leaks against an interaction model that describes the feasible execution orders of event handlers. The technique will be evaluated using real Android subjects. Mobile applications like those running on Android and iPhone devices have penetrated into the daily life of people in Hong Kong. Such applications include banking, navigation, scheduling, e-commerce, remote device control, and health care. Many companies invest large amount of human resources in developing dependable mobile applications. This project will greatly facilitate the dependability checking of such applications.
