611912.label: Realisation of objectives
611912.value: Executions of mobile applications are mostly driven by user interaction or system events. During its execution, an application keeps handling received user interaction and system events by calling their handlers. Each call to an event handler may change the application’s state by modifying its components’ local or global program data. Bugs arising from erroneous event handling in mobile applications are significant. Since event handling is subject to non-determinism, failures induced by the related bugs are hard to detect and reproduce. To achieve the first objective, we carried an empirical study of 70 real-world bugs collected from eight large-scale and popular Android applications. Each of these applications has more than 10,000 downloads and are actively maintained with a public bug tracking system. These bugs involve performance issues and reside in event handlers. We studied their bug reports and code fixes to identify their types and root causes. We checked whether manifestation of these bugs require special inputs and identified their common bug patterns. To achieve the second objective, we derive an analysis framework. We formalize the concepts of user interaction event sequences, application states and bounded state space exploration. We propose an application execution model to abstract activity lifecycles, and use the model to drive event sequence generation. A framework based on symbolic analysis was developed. A common deficiency of symbolic analysis is that it is not scalable to inter-procedural analysis of real-life applications. Our approach addresses the problem by identifying and removing equivalent symbolic states. It makes the analysis scalable to millions lines of code. We approached the problem using static analysis and then enhanced it with dynamic analysis. We find that it is beneficial to augment static analysis with dynamic analysis or runtime data for three reasons. First precise static analysis needs to be path-sensitive but carrying such analysis on real mobile applications is not scalable. Second, mobile applications typically make many system library calls. Precise modeling of all these library calls require non-trivial manual effort, which is ineffective when mobile system library evolves frequently. Third, popular mobile applications can involve execution of native code written in C or C++. Effects of these code are not easy to precisely trace. In this connection, we enhance our approach to validating the analyzed symbolic states with runtime data collected from large open source projects. Finally, we worked with Microsoft Research Asia and proposed a technique to locate faulty methods based on a collection of crash reports. To achieve the third objective, we implemented our framework in Java and evaluated using 29 popular Android apps and other open source projects. We set up a web site making our data set and tools available at http://sccpu2.cse.ust.hk/perfchecker.

611912.label: Major findings and research outcome
611912.value: The findings of this project were disseminated by one top-tier journal (TOSEM) and three top-tier conference publications (ICSE, ISSTA and ASE). Two PhD students were trained. Our two publications at ICSE and ISSTA were well received by the software engineering community and received the ACM SIGSOFT Distinguished Paper awards. The data set of our study and static analysis tools are made available to public. We summarize our findings as follows. - Performance bugs reside in the event handler of mobile applications largely lead to the lagging of user interactions, energy leakage and memory bloat. - Small-scale inputs suffice to manifest the bugs. In other words, most of the bugs can be triggered by small volume of input data. - Specific user interactions needed to manifest the bugs. Many of the bugs can only be triggered by specific user interaction sequences. Therefore, test sets driven by a coverage based on statement or branches cannot effectively expose the bugs. Modeling of activity lifecycles is crucial to the bug detection. - Quite a few of the bugs are platform-dependent. They may occur only on specific system library versions or mobile device models. - It takes a significantly longer time for developers to fix a performance bugs than non-performance bugs. This is likely because developers lack effective performance measurement tools for mobile devices. - Three common bug patterns are observed in event handling bugs. First, the event dispatcher thread involves computationally intensive operations. Second, unintended event sequences cause wasted computation. Third, heavy-weight callbacks are frequently triggered. - Removal of equivalent symbolic states can achieve a speedup of several order of magnitudes. As compared with the state-of-the-arts approaches, our technique improves the function coverage and block coverage by 40% and 32%, respectively. - Our analysis framework when applied to 29 popular Android applications detected 18 of them contain a total of 126 unreported bugs. 68 of them were confirmed quickly by the corresponding application developers that they are real bugs. - Experimental results show that the most suspicious function reported by our crash analysis has an overall probability of 51% that it is truly faulty. The overall probability that one of the top 10 most suspicious functions reported by our crash analysis is truly faulty is 66%.

611912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611912.value: Our findings lead to the following future work. - Bug detection can be made possible by generating user interaction sequences with small scale inputs. - We can consider to augment crash analysis with runtime log data. - We can consider to leverage the common bug patterns and generate possible patches for detected bugs. - We can consider to adapt the analysis techniques to iOS applications.

611912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611912.value: The smartphone application market is expanding rapidly. However, random sampling of Android applications available at Google Play store indicates that many of them suffer from various kinds of bugs triggered by anomalous event handling. These bugs cannot be effectively detected by existing tools. To address the problem, we gain better understanding of these bugs via an empirical study. The study identifies the common bug types, their root causes and problematic coding patterns that likely induce these bugs. A static analysis framework augmented with runtime data is developed to help developers to detect bugs in their applications. Promising results were found. Our techniques were well received by the software engineering community. Our work received two ACM SIGSOFT Distinguished Paper awards. To promote impacts, we made our dataset and tools available to the public. Our dataset and tools were also used by prominent research groups in other research institutes such as Oregon State University, Ohio State University, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, the National University of Singapore, the University of Southern California, the College of William and Mary, the University of Alberta and Technische Universität Darmstadt.

612312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612312.value: 隨著智能手機 以及平板電腦的快速普及，迫切需要可適用于全球任何一種語言的基於語音的人機介面。 最近蘋果公司基於iPhone 4s發佈了Siri個人助理，大 部份的人機交互都可以通過語音命令完成。語音識別技術在擁有大量訓練數據的語言上已經趨於成熟，但是對於一些小語種，由於缺乏數據用來訓 練識別系統，語音識別還面臨很大的挑戰。Siri目前只為主要 的歐洲語言提供服務。另一方面，有大量的用戶使用非標準的語言進行日常溝通，而且沒法使用實用的語音識別系統。比如大部份的印度語言，儘 管擁有數以百萬計的人使用，但是沒有足夠多的數據來訓練語音識別系統。在香港，大部份的會議以及官方語言都是通過粵語(一種主要的中 國地方方言)進行。我們建議研究有效的方法來應對這種挑戰—使用有線的訓 練數據來對大詞彙量的、非官方的語言進行語音和語言建模，並且這種方法能夠適用于所有非標準的中國語言。 語音識別系統通過大量的語音數據以及他們的真實標注來進行訓練。中國的語言，包括粵語、上海話、閩南話等，跟普通話有很大的差別，如果不經 過訓練，使用一種 方言的人無法聽懂另一種方言。這些語言沒有官方的書面形式，翻譯人員不熟悉書寫方式，人工翻譯這些語音變得非常艱難。這就意味著訓練數據 非常稀少！ 使用有限數據訓練出來的語音模型難以推廣到其他用戶。除了使用我們以前的方法—多語言語音模型合併和共享—之外，我們建議通過機器學習的方法來有效控制模型的 複雜度，優化系統性能。 爲了訓練語言模型，我們建議通過研究標準語言和非標準語言的語法差異，引進語法翻轉模型。 我們還提議在一個全局優化的單系統中集成語音識別和非標準到標準語言的“翻譯”。與之前的工作有所不同的是，我們採取使用有限狀態 感知識別器合併翻譯過程到整個識別搜索網絡。這個識別網絡能同時輸出真實的非標準漢語（比如說廣東話）的識別結果和標準漢語的識別結果。 最後我們提出從政府獲取和從多媒體資源當中收集廣東話，上海話和閩南話的語音數據庫。這代表第一次用少量數據解決多種漢語方言的語音識別技 術的努力嘗試。

612312.label: Realisation of objectives
612312.value: All project objectives have been achieved. We published a paper using cross-lingual language modeling with syntactic information for low-resource speech recognition. We propose phrase-level transduction and syntactic reordering for transcribing a resource-poor language and translating it into a resource-rich language, if necessary. The phrase-level transduction is capable of performing n -m cross-lingual transduction. The syntactic reordering serves to model the syntactic discrepancies between the source and target languages. Our purpose is to leverage the statistics in a resource-rich language model to improve the language model of a resource-poor language and at the same time to improve low-resource speech recognition performance. We implement our cross-lingual language model using weighted finite-state transducers (WFSTs), and integrate it into a WFST-based speech recognition search space to output the transcriptions of both resource-poor and resource-rich languages. This creates an integrated speech transcription and translation framework. Evaluations on Cantonese speech transcription and Cantonese to standard Chinese translation tasks show that our proposed approach improves the system performance significantly, with up to 12.5% relative character error rate (CER) reduction over baseline language model interpolation, 6.6% relative CER reduction and 18.5% relative BLEU score improvement, compared to the best word-level transduction approach. We published another result using sparse banded acoustic models to significantly improve the recognition accuracy and reduce the computational cost of speech recognition systems. The sparse banded models are trained using a weighted lasso regularization. In addition, we propose new feature orders to reduce the bandwidth of sparse banded models in order to speed up computation. Experimental results on the Wall Street Journal data set show that sparse banded models significantly outperform diagonal and full covariance models by 9.5% and 15.1% relatively. Sparse banded models also run the fastest. The advantages of sparse banded models are also demonstrated on the collected Cantonese data set. Finally, we proposed for the first time to incorporate the linguistically well-known Functional Head Constraint into a code switch language model for speech recognition. Under this constraint, code switch cannot occur between the functional head and its complements. The constrained code switching language model is obtained by first expanding the search network with a translation model; and then using lattice-based parsing to restrict paths to those permissible under the Functional Head Constraint. We tested our system on two tasks of code switch speech recognition, namely lecture speech recognition and lunch conversation recognition. Our system reduces word error rates (WER) from a baseline mixed language model by 3.72% relative in the first task; and by 5.85% in the second task. It reduces WER from an interpolated language model by 2.51% in the first task; and by 4.57% in the second task. All results are statistically significant. In addition, our method reduces WER for both the matrix language and the embedded language.

612312.label: Major findings and research outcome
612312.value: paper proposes using cross-lingual language modeling with syntactic information for low-resource speech recognition. We propose phrase-level transduction and syntactic reordering for transcribing a resource-poor language and translating it into a resource-rich language, if necessary. The phrase-level transduction is capable of performing n -m cross-lingual transduction. The syntactic reordering serves to model the syntactic discrepancies between the source and target languages. We propose to use sparse inverse covariance matrices for acoustic model training when there is insufficient training data. Acoustic models trained with inadequate training data tend to over fit, generalizing poorly to unseen test data, especially when full covariance matrices are used. We address this problem by adding an L1 regularization term to the traditional objective function for maximum likelihood estimation, to penalize complex models. The structure of the inverse covariance matrices will be automatically sparsified using this new objective function. The Expectation Maximization algorithm is used to learn the parameters of the hidden Markov model using the new objective function. We propose for the first time to incorporate the linguistically well-known Functional Head Constraint into a code switch language model for speech recognition. We tested our system on two tasks of code switch speech recognition, namely lecture speech recognition and lunch conversation recognition. Our system reduces word error rates (WER) from a baseline mixed language model by 3.72% relative in the first task; and by 5.85% in the second task. It reduces WER from an interpolated language model by 2.51% in the first task; and by 4.57% in the second task. All results are statistically significant. In addition, our method reduces WER for both the matrix language and the embedded language.

612312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612312.value: We continue to develop the mixed language modeling both in terms of acoustic and language modeling using a Deep Learning framework. We expect to see more results in the future.

612312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612312.value: This project was successfully completed as we proposed a paradigm of "borrowing" from the data of a resource rich language, such as Mandarin, to model a resource poor language, such as Cantonese. Languages such as Cantonese do not have as much recorded data as Mandarin, and we proposed a new way of solving this problem via a WFST network. Finally it is also applicable to other types of linguistic phenomena without a lot of data, such as mixed language.

612412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612412.value: Hong Kong is surrounded by the waters of Pearl River Estuary (PRE) to the west, Mirs Bay (MIB) to the east and continental shelf (COS) to the south and they jointly form Hong Kong Seawaters (HKW). These three water entities have their own inherent hydrodynamics that is mainly governed by flow-topography (effect) interaction forced by monsoon wind stress, tides and buoyancy from Pearl River. Their respective hydrodynamics are mixed coastal-estuarine circulation in the broad PRE, topography-following flow in MIB and monsoon driven upwelling/downwelling shelf circulation in COS. Unlike tidal currents that reverse direction within semi-diurnal or diurnal time scales, subtidal forcing is well known to be the major driver that shapes overall transport (flow) field in the coastal embayment such as HKW, for a time scale beyond tidal periods. Subtidal hydrodynamics is essential for understanding, modeling, and managing seawater properties from shelf offshore to near shore in HKW. COS is tightly linked with PRE and MIB geographically and dynamically, and the underlying hypothesis in this proposed study is that integrated hydrodynamics in the subtidal time scale among PRE, MIB and COS, not each individual itself, governs the dynamic environment of HKW. This scientific subject has rarely been studied in HKW. Based on the dynamic evidence derived from HKW and from the other parts of the world’s oceans, it is hypothesized that: (H1) Monsoon-driven upwelling/downwelling shelf circulation in COS and its associated hydrodynamic response in HKW largely controls the subtidal circulation in HKW. (H2) The shelf circulation in COS is time and space dependent subject to the control of monsoon winds, tides and buoyancy from Pearl River discharge. (H3) Shelf circulation in COS strongly regulates the subtidal hydrodynamics in PRE/MIB, which is modulated by the variable coastline and shelf topography in HKW. Unlike previous studies that have mainly focused on tidal hydrodynamics in PRE, this proposed project, for the first time, integrates the study of hydrodynamics in COS with ones in PRE and MIB to provide comprehensive understanding of hydrodynamics in HKW. The strategy of the study is to combine field measurements of repeat horizontal mappings and mooring arrays with an enhanced spatial resolution of advanced down-scale modeling system to identify the time dependent, three-dimensional integrated hydrodynamics in HKW. As the fundamental theory that governs the water motion and associated properties/materials transport, the study of subtidal hydrodynamics will help advance our understanding of overall marine environmental conditions in the HKW.

612412.label: Realisation of objectives
612412.value: In this study, we adopted both field measurement and the cutting-edge technology of three-dimensional numerical ocean modeling to investigate the oceanic subtidal circulation subject to the controls of winds, buoyancy, tidal forcing and coastal ocean circulation. The in-situ measurements provided observational characteristics of subtidal hydrodynamics, and built physics based for numerical model. The ocean modeling developed then interpolated and extrapolated the spatially and temporarily limited observations to develop holistic understanding of subtidal hydrodynamics of shelf circulation in PRE, MIB as well as in COS. We have conducted two field measurements in PRE, Hong Kong waters and adjacent continental shelf, during wet and dry seasons. The survey region extends from 21.8oN- 23.2oN, 113oE-114.2oE, with total 11 sampling transacts that contains 85 stations. We have also conducted time series measurements of current, temperature and salinity during these two cruises. The scale of field work undertaken by these two surveys is unprecedented in the region. We have developed a novel coupled estuary-shelf numerical model to accommodate the subtidal hydrodynamics in the study region of the project. We have achieved the objectives layout by the project in full extent with high quality research outputs.

612412.label: Major findings and research outcome
612412.value: Combined field measurements with numerical modeling, we have addressed the scientific topics listed in Obj. 1 and Obj. 2 in the four papers (Zu and Gan, 2013; Gan et al., 2013; Lu and Gan, 2013; Zu et al., 2014). Zu and Gan (2013) found that mean (sub-tidal) circulations in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE) and over the adjacent shelf are interactive. The circulation in the PRE during summer is dominated by an advective gravitational two-layer circulation in the upper estuary and the landward part of the lower PRE, where the surface flow pattern also varies with the upwelling winds. The circulation in the seaward part of the lower PRE is governed by both gravitational circulation and geostrophic intrusive current from the shelf. The pattern and intensity of these circulations are largely modulated by variable wind forcing. The cross-shore upwelling shelf circulation off the PRE enhances the water exchange rate between the shelf and the PRE, but the net intrusive transport into the PRE is negatively correlated with the intensity of upwelling-favorable wind stress. Relatively strong water exchange rate between the shelf and estuary occurs during upwelling, which reduces the flushing time of the estuary. Although the ebbing/flooding tide strengthens/weakens the eastward alongshore upwelling current, tidal effect on the upwelling circulation and on the net transport between the shelf and estuary is not significant over the sub-tidal period. Gan et al. (2013) further studied the oceanic subtidal circulation over the continental shelf adjacent to Hong Kong in the northern South China Sea. We found that wind-driven subtidal circulation was formed and maintained by the presence of an intensified westward along-isobath pressure gradient force (PGFm) and bottom frictional effect that led to cross-isobath currents over the unique shelf topography. Lu and Gan (2013) investigated the effects of river discharge, vertical mixing induced by gravitational current on the turn-over rate of water mass in Pearl River Estuary. We found that the bloom occurred in the middle of the well/partially mixed estuary during the dry season when river discharge was relatively small. Zu et al. (2014) further investigated the buoyant river plume over the Pearl River Estuary (PRE) and adjacent shelf during a typical upwelling favorable wind period of the summer monsoon. Mechanical energy analysis in each dynamical region reveals that this is because the system mainly gains energy from tide (wind) in the estuary (shelf), and loses energy to the bottom friction (internal-shear mixing) in the estuary (shelf).

612412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612412.value: The findings of this study built solid foundation for future study of water pollution, eutrophication/hypoxia in the waters around HK, by providing fundamental subtidal hydrodynamics for the transport of pollutant and biogeochemical substances.

612412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612412.value: Unlike periodic reversing tidal current, subtidal forcing is well known to be the major driver of overall transport (flow) field in the ocean for a time scale beyond tidal periods. The subtidal hydrodynamics of Hong Kong waters (HKW) is characterized by interactive hydrodynamics in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE), Mirs Bay (MIB) and the continental shelf off Hong Kong (COS) that surrounds Hong Kong from the west, east and south, respectively. The investigation of subtidal hydrodynamic linkage among COS, PRE and MIB provides understanding of characteristics and variability of COS circulation under controls of complex external forcing and topography, and link dynamics of shelf circulation with the hydrodynamics in PRE and MIB in HKW. This has never been investigated before. This is essential for understanding and managing seawater properties from shelf offshore to near shore in HKW. The general hydrodynamics developed in HKW can be applicable to the shelf-estuary/bay interaction in the other part of the worlds' oceans.

612512.label: Project Objectives
612512.value: To develop a multivariate statistical methods for online quality prediction in batch processes. Such model should correctly describe within-phase and between-phase cumulative effects on quality. Quality-related process analysis will be conducted based on the model. To model the impacts of transitions between phases on product qualities. Sudden transitions and gradual transitions may be modeled in different ways according to their different characteristics. To build statistical quality prediction models for 2D dynamic batch processes, despite the fact that the batches are not independent of each other. To design online quality control strategies either compensating for quality losses within cycle or improving the process from cycle to cycle.

612512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612512.value: Multivariate statistical methods have been widely applied due to their superior ability in handling high-dimensional and correlated process data. However, conventional multivariate statistical methods are ill-suited for batch processes with phases of different process dynamics. In multi-phase batch processes, each phase has its own underlying characteristics, which determines the end product quality in a different way. Transitions between phases occupy short periods of time but can significantly affect product quality, leading to both within-phase and between-phase cumulative effects of process variable trajectories on product quality. We propose to develop phase/transition-based statistical modeling methods which can reflect both types of cumulative effects so as to improve prediction accuracy and achieve better quality-related process analysis. Process dynamics can also vary from batch to batch, effectively, many batch processes, effectively, have two-time-dimensional (2D) dynamics, within-batch dynamics and batch-to-batch dynamics. The existence of the 2D dynamics breaks the precondition of most statistical modeling methods and makes them inapplicable to such batch processes. In this project, the 2D dynamics will also be taken into consideration in prediction model building. On the basis of the proposed multivariate statistical models, quality control strategies for batch processes will then be developed. Because most quality attributes are determined in cumulatively, quality loss can be compensated for within each cycle. For disturbances reoccurring from cycle to cycle or following certain batch-wise dynamics, the idea of iterative learning control (ILC) and run-to-run (R2R) control can be adopted to improve performance cycle by cycle using the proposed 2D model. Injection molding is a typical multiphase batch process with 2D dynamics, and it will be utilized as a research platform in this project. 由于其优异的处理高维及相关特性的能力，多变量统计方法被广泛应用。然而，传统的方法不适用于具有多时段及动态特性的批次过程。批次过程的各个时段具有其特性对产品质量贡献也不同；尽管过渡过程相对较短，它对产品质量有较大的影响；过程动态也是影响质量的重要因素。基于以上特性，本项目提出时段及时段过渡及其对质量影响的分析及预测方法。 过程动态也存在於批次与批次之间。多数批次过程可以看作为二维时间动态系统， 具有批次内动态及批次间动态。本项目将考虑二维时间动态进行质量预测。 基于统计质量预测模型，相应的质量控制方法研究也是本项目研究目的之一。迭代学习控制方法将被采纳用于消除批次重复的干扰。 最后， 注塑过程作为一个典型的批次过程将對以上提出的分析及控制方法的验证。

612512.label: Realisation of objectives
612512.value: This project has been completed in full with 10 journal and 3 conference publications. The venues of these publications are well respected in the community of process monitoring and control. The project studied batch process cumulative effects for both within-phase and between-phase effects. Two important concepts and representations have been proposed: Inner-phase and intra-phase quality evolutions. A phase transition model has been developed and its effect on quality has been modelled and analysed. Although the transition is typically much shorter than the durations of the preceding phase and the following phase, the quality and dynamic impact can be large. For this reason, the impact of phase-transition quality is modelled for intra-phase evolution. Evolution of within-batch and cross-batch dynamics and quality has been represented by a two-time (batch and time) dimensional (2D) model. Various methods have been developed to represent this 2D behaviour through system identification. Based on the model obtained, control methods of 2D nature, feedback control within batch and learning control across batches, have been proposed to meet quality requirements and for process performance improvement. The project objectives have been fully met and findings have been published as detailed in the sections to follow.

612512.label: Major findings and research outcome
612512.value: This project concerned the following aspects of research on batch processes as stated in the above objectives: 1. Modeling 2. Phase-transition 3. 2D dynamics and Control On the modeling, journal papers 3,4,5, 9 and 10 and conference paper 3 have given a comprehensive suite of modeling approaches for evaluating quality using inner-phase modeling [3], 2D identification methods [4], intra-phase and inner-phase based method with consideration of uneven length [5], and methods of incorporating prior controller knowledge [9] and prior process knowledge [10]. These suggested modeling methods pushed the frontier of batch process modeling particularly with our introduction of the concepts of inner- and intra- phase quality evolutions. Phase transition has been considered together with inner-phase evolution for better quality prediction [conference paper 2]. Different modes of operation and transitions were analyzed to give between-model analysis strategies [Journal paper 2]. 2D dynamics and control are considered together in journal publications [6-10]. Based on the repetitive nature of a batch process, iterative learning has been incorporated into Kaltman filter for better state estimation by imposing bounds on changes along the time or batch direction [Journal paper 6]. Using the idea of two-stage optimization, a new control design has been proposed for batch processes to enhance the integrated control of combining MPC with ILC so a good performance and fast convergence can be obtained simultaneously [Journal Paper 7]. Using injection molding as a typical batch process, the welding-line positioning is controlled using 2D model predictive control to exploit batch process reparative nature [Journal 8]. [Journal paper 9] devises an online system identification method for process dynamics by fully exploiting its intrinsic repetitiveness for gradual performance enhancement. The work is further extended in paper [10] by extending the identification algorithm for batch processes to incorporate a priori process knowledge of pole and zero positions.

612512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612512.value: The set of algorithms developed for modeling of quality evaluation in the framework of inner- and intra –phases and associated modeling and control tools proposed represents a key advancement of batch process monitoring and control. It has laid a good foundation for big-data researches for batch process, the PI intends to write a proposal for extending the process monitoring work to the running of multiple similar batch processes to explore their similarity and repeatability. The current project has been focused on the multiple-phase nature and repeatability of a batch process. The parallel running of multiple batch processes has become a common trend in modern manufacturing. The studies of this project serve as a foundation for our next project proposal.

612512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612512.value: A batch process consists of multiple phases and the process dynamics has been found to vary gradually within a phase and significantly across phases. In correspondence, multi-phase monitoring and analysis have been proposed. The quality is modeled and analyzed by examining its evolutions over time and batches. Along time, this project proposes the methods of inner-phase and intra-phase modeling, and along the time and batch, 2D dynamic modeling method is developed. A set of tools have also been developed for batch process monitoring and control.

612712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612712.value: Partial blockages are common in engineered as well as natural pressurized conduit systems that transport liquids. Systems that are prone to blockages include cardiovascular systems, freshwater supply systems, pressurized drainage and sewerage pipes, oil lines, and pumped seawater systems such as those used in Hong Kong for flushing. Blockages are due to a myriad of physical and chemical processes such as material deposition, tubercles (rust), scales, plaque, bio-fouling, ice-formation in cold climate, and inadvertently throttled inline valves. Blockages in engineered systems often result in wastage of energy and financial resources, reduction in carrying capacity, increased potential for contamination. Blockages in cardiovascular systems can result in major health problems and even death. A blockage often begins as a patch in the inside wall of the conduit characterized by rougher than usual surface and small radial protrusion and, if left undetected, can grow to sizeable obstruction of the flow (e.g., see figure 1). While detecting large blockages of any size is a worthy pursuit, it would be even more important and useful to pinpoint such anomalies and deal with them at early enough stage before they grow to an extent where they can cause severe problems and damages. This project is aimed at understanding the modifications made to hydraulic waves by small blockages with the view that such an understanding will pave the way for the development of wave-based blockage detection techniques. Currently all commercial blockage detection methods are intrusive, short ranged and require the system to be depressurised. A wave-based method has an operational range of kilometers allows blockages to be located and detected in real time with minimum disruption to services. The project will focus on blockages with (i) varying extent in the radial direction ranging from small to large amplitudes; (ii) varying extent (length) in the axial direction; and (iii) uniform and non-uniform shapes. Single, multiple-regular and multiple-irregular blockages will be examined. The investigation will be carried out using the theory of multiple-scale and singular perturbation as well as the transfer matrix method in conjunction with experimental and numerical data. The theoretical and experimental results will allow the extraction of much needed physical insights into the modifications imposed on hydraulic waves as they propagate through anomalous region in conduit wall and assessment of the potential of developing methods for detecting blockages at their early stage of development on the basis of decoding measured hydraulic waves. 工程的或者自然的壓力液體輸送管道系統中常常出現非完全阻塞。這些管道系統包括心血管系統，飲用水供水系統，壓力污水排水系統和用於沖洗的海水抽送系統（比如香港現有的狀況）。形成阻塞的原因有多種，比如物質沉澱，銹蝕，水垢，生物汙損，冷凍條件下結冰以及在施工中忘記全開的閥門等。在工程系統中，這些阻塞可以造成能源和財政資源浪費，降低管道的輸送能力，并增加管道系統污染的風險。心血管系統阻塞還能引起重大健康問題，甚至死亡。管道中的阻塞通常由管壁上的小斑塊物形成。這些小斑塊的特點是比普通的管壁表面更加粗糙，並且在管道內部形成徑向突起。如果不經發現和排除，它們在管道中會慢慢形成大的堵塞物（如圖1）。儘管檢測大阻塞物是很值得和重要的工作，但是比之更重要的是找出在這些大的阻塞物形成之前出現的異常情況，并及時處理它們，以免後來形成嚴重的問題和損壞。 本研究項目的目的在於理解管道中的小阻塞物對水力波的改變，并以此作為利用水力波的阻塞檢測技術的基礎。目前所有的商用阻塞檢測方法都是是通過進入偵測，短距離檢測或者需要將系統泄壓來檢測出阻塞物。利用水力波的檢測方法則可以檢測出在發放水力波位置的數公里範圍內阻塞物，並且實時操作而不需要中斷管道系統服務。本研究項目將著重於研究以下阻塞物的變化對水力波的影響：（1）在管道徑向（縱向） 從小到大不同阻塞程度；（2）在管道軸向（橫向）不同阻塞距離；（3）均一和非均一阻塞物。而且，本研究將考慮單個的，多個規則的和多個不規則阻塞物的情況。本研究將使用多尺度分析方法，奇攝動理論，轉換矩陣法以及試驗和數值模擬數據。本研究項目得到的理論和試驗結果將用以理解關於水力波在有阻塞問題管道中傳播時產生改變的原理。同時本研究成果可用於評估發展利用解碼測量水力波的初期阻塞檢測技術方法的可能性。

612712.label: Realisation of objectives
612712.value: Objective 1 “Conduct numerical and experimental study of the waterhammer modulation and damping by one and two blockages in pressurized conduits” has been fully realized. This research investigates the physics of wave-blockage interaction in Water supply systems (WSS) by analytical, numerical and experimental means. Both shallow blockages (i.e., blockages with small radial protrusion) and severe blockages (i.e., blockages with large radial protrusion) are studied. The principle of action invariance shows that wm Em is conserved for small blockages implying Δwm / wm =ΔEm / Em , where wm and Em are the eigenfrequency and total energy of the mth mode and Δwm and ΔEm its eigenfrequency and energy shift due to the blockage. The change in energy is shown to be equal to the work of the radiation pressure during the formation of the blockage. In addition, it is found that a small blockage reduces the potential energy, but increases the kinetic energy of all modes. For a severe blockage, the pipe system is decoupled into two independent subsystems: a subsystem that involves the blockage and another that involves the intact pipe section. The decoupling is lost when the blockage length is such that the fundamental frequencies of the two subsystems are close or equal, resulting in resonance which means that waves within the subsystem involving the blockage are able to penetrate (transmit) to the second subsystem and vice-versa. It is shown that the assumption of small blockage is applicable when the blockage occupies 30% of the cross sectional area. The assumption of severe blockage is applicable when the blockage occupies 30% of the cross sectional area or larger provided that the decoupling assumption is valid. When the blockage and the remainder of the pipe system are coupled, perturbation theory is successfully used to derive a simple frequency relation for the case of a blockage with large radial extent. This study also reveals that Bragg’s resonance plays a key role where the wave-blockage interaction is minimal for certain frequencies and maximal for others. The spacing between consecutive Bragg’s resonance frequencies, where maximal interaction occurs, scales as the wavespeed divided by the blockage length. Therefore, a wideband frequency of the transient generator is required to capture the signature of a short blockage. However, the use of high frequency waves (HFW) excites radial and azimuthal waves and renders the classical one-dimensional water-hammer (WH) theory invalid. Unlike classical WH theory, the resulting wave field is highly dispersive. Therefore, this thesis examines and reviews the behavior of HFW in water-filled pipes and how they interact with blockages. As a result, a high-order numerical scheme has been developed and tested. The results show the strong effects of multi-paths on the propagation of high HFW in WSS and highlight that such waves, although provide the required resolution, have a low range of detectability. Thus, a double pronged approach, where low frequency waves are used for reconnaissance and HFW are used for the localization is desirable in the future. Objective 2 “Compare experimental and numerical results of objective 1 and identify, examine and understand discrepancies between them” has also been fully realized. The results show that the first seven experimental eigenfrequencies capture the main features of those given by the numerical test. In fact, the mean error, i.e. the difference between the numerical and experimental dimensionless frequencies, is about 5% for the first 5 modes and about 20% for the 6th and 7th modes. This good result is obtained notwithstanding the restrictive assumption of the numerical model – both unsteady friction and (more important) the viscoelasticity are not taken into account – and some clear difference between the actual pipe system and the one simulated by the model. The first difference concerns the fact that the pipe has been assumed as straight without modelling the bend effects. It is worth noting that the mean distance between two successive bends is about 10 m. Therefore the effect of the bends may become very apparent at frequencies close to (a/4/10) / ≈ 15 which may affect eigenfrequency at mode six or higher. Second, fluid-structure interaction phenomena have been neglected. However, the anchorage effect is most likely to be small because the transient pressure head injected is very small (less than 1m). Therefore, the pipe displacement is very small too. Eigenfrequencies at higher modes (>7) are not reliable because of the noise/errors and the limited frequency bandwidth. Moreover, since the pressure probe f.s. is too large compared to the maximum value of the pressure, the accuracy of the pressure signal is not as high as it could be. Finally, it must be pointed out that a further source of error concerns the evaluation of the pressure wave speed. To give an idea of the crucial role played by the pressure wave speed, it can be noted that an error of 4% in the value of a produces an error in the eigenfrequency that increases almost linearly from 4% at the 1st mode to 63% at the 7th mode; whereas an error of 1% in wave speed produces an error in the eigenfrequency that increases almost linearly from 0.9% at the 1st mode to 14% at the 7th mode. Objective 3 “Use the understanding gained in objective 2 to incorporate the missing physics in a wterhammer mathematical model and to map each change in waterhammer wave to the process that causes it” has also been fully realized. Two high resolution finite volume (FV) numerical scheme that handles blockages in a mathematically and physically consistent manner are formulated, tested and verified. One scheme uses the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook Boltzmann (BGK) and the other the Kinetic Flux Vector Splitting (KFVS) in the flux approximation. It was found that the KFVS and BGK schemes correctly capture discontinuity fronts in a classical reservoir-pipe system. An oscillation-free collision time formulation has been proposed, tested and found to be robust. The stability of the proposed schemes is guaranteed when Cr<0.5. Comparison between the BGK, KFVS, fixed-grid MOC, and first and second Godunov schemes reveals that the second-order Godunov performs best followed closely by the BGK scheme.

612712.label: Major findings and research outcome
612712.value: Analytical, numerical and experimental study of the waterhammer modulation and damping by one and two blockages in pressurized conduits has been conducted [Louati 2016, Louati and Ghidaoui 2016 (a,b,c,d), Louati et al 2016 (e,f)]. The results show that waves can experience Bragg-type resonance due to multiple scattering from blockages and that such scattering becomes more prominent as the systems’ irregularities, complexity and spatial variability increase (Louati 2016). Application of the principle of action invariance to a small blockage shows that the eigenfrequency shift is directly related to the change in energy. For a severe blockage, the pipe system is decoupled into two independent subsystems: a subsystem that involves the blockage and another that involves the intact pipe section. The decoupling is lost when the blockage length is such that the fundamental frequencies of the two subsystems are close or equal, resulting in resonance where perturbation theory is successfully used to derive a simple frequency relation. Louati et al. 2016 (f) compare experimental and numerical results of the interaction between blockages and waves and examine the discrepancies between them. It is found that the major source of error in obtaining accurate blockage information from the frequency response is the error introduced in measuring the wave speed. The physics of the Bragg condition is explained in [Louati 2016, Louati and Ghidaoui 2016 (a,b,c,d), Louati et al. 2016 (e,f)]. The new understanding of the physics gained in this research provides the basis for a new, robust and efficient technique for blockage detection [Louati 2016, Louati et al. 2016 (e,f)]. Two FV schemes (one using the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook Boltzmann (BGK) and the other the Kinetic Flux Vector Splitting (KFVS) in the flux approximation) for one-dimensional water hammer problems were formulated and applied (Mesgari and Ghidaoui 2016a). The KFVS and BGK schemes correctly captured discontinuity fronts in a classical reservoir-pipe system. Comparison between the BGK, KFVS, fixed-grid MOC, and first and second Godunov schemes reveals that the second-order Godunov performs best followed closely by the BGK scheme. Mesgari and Ghidaoui (2016b) have, for the first time, extended the FV approach to problems involving blockages.

612712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612712.value: A proposal that builds on this research has been submitted. In particular, the understanding of wave-blockage interaction gained from this project will be used to develop robust, efficient and optimization-free TBDDM. The Bragg resonance condition to be derived in the proposed research will provide a direct relation between the blockage length and the Bragg frequencies. Therefore, injecting a transient signal with a wide frequency bandwidth allows the experimental determination of the Bragg resonance frequency. This Bragg resonance frequency provides a direct and explicit means of calculating the blockage length (i.e., no optimization is required). The Bragg resonance and the pattern it imposes are determined by injecting a wide band transient, recording the reflected signals and applying to it a discrete Fourier transform (DFT). Experimentally, a Benthowave 7500 series wave generator capable of generating pulse waves in the 0 to 50 kHz range and GE DRUCK UNIK 5000 transducers capable of measuring minute pressure pulse fluctuations in the target 0 to 4kHz range should allow for the generation and detection of the desired bandwidth. Theoretically, the transient is generated by a delta function in time.

612712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612712.value: In pressurized conduits such as water supply lines and pumped drainage systems, defects may occur during construction, or develop with operation and age. Defects include partially blocked/closed valves, changes in pipe wall thickness due to bio-film build up, corrosion, tuberculation and from material spalling and deposition. These defects generally lead to significantly higher pumping costs due to increased skin and form drag, potential by causing deterioration in the chemical and physical quality of the liquid being transported. The results of this research explained in detail the physics of eigenfrequency shift that a blockage imposes on a wave. Such knowledge has the potential to greatly improve the efficiency of current blockage detection techniques. Indeed, the improved understanding of shift mechanisms will enable the development of a new, robust and more efficient technique for blockage detection that does not require optimization (which current methods need).

612912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612912.value: 世界各地正在兴建的大型数据中心，提供各种云计算服务，例如网络搜索，在线社交网络，在线办公和IT基础设施外包为个人用户和组织（如谷歌，微软，IBM，亚马逊，eBay的，而雅虎正在运行的数据中心，在每个至少有5万台服务器）。因此，数据中心网络最近一直在学术界和工业界研究的一个热点话题。一个基本的挑战是设计的服务器数量庞大的数据中心网络互连，并提供高效率和容错路由到上层应用的服务。在应对这一挑战，研究界已经开始探索了大量的互连拓扑结构，包括FatTree，克洛斯，C-通过，FiConn，DCell和BCube之间迅速增长的替代品，许多改编自早期解决方案在电信和超级计算领域。 提出的解决方案，到目前为止，无论是规模过慢或出现性能瓶颈，取决于服务器的位置，继承的可用性较差，或可太复杂/昂贵的构建。第二，很少的努力一直致力于提供差异化​​的服务/网络数据中心网络尽管事实已经清楚地观察到这种不平衡的网络流量分布。例如，在地图，减少环境中（例如，谷歌推出的一个软件框架，支持分布式计算大型数据集在多台计算机上），其中一些服务器（例如，主节点）的要求比别人更高的网络带宽（例如，从节点）。第三，有没有基准测试方法已经提出来评估不同的数据中心设计，在不同的网络环境和交通环境。 出于这些非常重要的具有挑战性的问题，我们打算在这个研究项目中，开发出一种新型的数据中心互连用干净的石板，它结合了以前的架构优势，同时避免其局限性。特别是，我们将开发一类新的互联网络体系结构，称为FLATNET，扁平化/简化数据中心网络，以使独立的服务器的位置，应用程序的性能。然后，我们将解决，并提出解决以下问题：1）调查的平坦式的建筑和拓扑性质，以及它是如何影响应用程序的性能和发展，以及他们的建筑成本; 2）路由算法的设计FLATNET考虑到其时间复杂度，容错和负载均衡特性; 3）设计的协议和流量管理方案，以提供QoS FLATNET; 4）建立一个基准测试平台，通过它我们可以准确地评估和比较不同的数据中心架构，现实和实际环境下（例如，性能，成本，可扩展性等）。

612912.label: Realisation of objectives
612912.value: We firstly presented the design, implementation and evaluation of SprintNet, a novel server-centric network architecture for data centers. SprintNet achieves high performance in network capacity, fault tolerance, and network latency. SprintNet is also a scalable, yet low-diameter network architecture where the maximum shortest distance between any pair of servers can be limited by no more than four and is independent of the number of layers. The specially designed routing schemes for SprintNet strengthen its merits. However, all of these kind of server-centric architectures still suffer from some critical shortcomings owing to the server’s responsibility of forwarding packets. With regard to these issues, in this project, we then propose a hardware based approach, named ‘‘Forwarding Unit’’ to provide an effective solution to these drawbacks and improve the efficiency of server-centric architectures. Both theoretical analysis and simulations are conducted to evaluate the overall performance of SprintNet and the Forwarding Unit approach with respect to cost-effectiveness, fault-tolerance, system latency, packet loss ratio, aggregate bottleneck throughput, and average path length. The evaluation results convince the feasibility and good performance of both SprintNet and Forwarding Unit. The specially designed traffic-aware adaptive and fault tolerant routing scheme helps SprintNet achieve its maximum theoretical performance. The implementation and evaluation of SprintNet further strengthens the theoretical analysis and demonstrates its feasibility. Furthermore, based on careful investigations we addressed some critical short-comings existed in the server-centric data center architectures caused by depending on servers to forward packets. In order to efficiently solve these drawbacks, we proposed an elegant approach which shifts forwarding tasks from servers to the network aiming to achieve a logically flat data center network. The forwarding unit totally isolates the servers from the network, and makes the data center network completely transparent to servers which brings abundant of advantages. In order to evaluate the feasibility and performance of this approach, extensive simulations are conducted, and the evaluation results convince its efficiency and feasibility. We implemented a green data center network and save as much energy as possible. With the benefit of blocking island paradigm, we presented a general framework trying to maximize the network power conservation and minimize sacrifices of network performance and reliability. The bandwidth allocation mechanism together with power-aware routing algorithm achieve a bandwidth guaranteed green tighter network. Moreover, our fast efficient heuristics for allocating bandwidth enable the system to scale to large sized data centers. The evaluation result shows that achieving up to more than 50% power savings are feasible while guaranteeing network performance and reliability. we formulate the energy optimization problem as a MCF problem and prove its NP-hardness. By drawing the inspiration from an artificial intelligence abstraction technique BI, we propose an efficient bandwidth allocation mechanism BAM and heuristic power-aware routing algorithm PAR. Afterwards, we further designed a Power-efficient Network System by combing BAM and PAR to achieve an energy proportional data center network. Moreover, we have also discussed how to make a reasonable tradeoff between power savings and network reliability. Finally, extensive simulations are conducted to evaluate this green framework. According to our simulation results, the PPS can reach up to more than 50% on the whole for guaranteeing the network performance, and ranges from 20% to 60% for different network conditions (network scales, network loads, traffic patterns, reliability requirements, etc). This result further convinces the feasibility and good performance of our approach. Based on our earlier successful development of DCNSim, a data center network simulator, that enables the study of various static features of data center architectures, we embarked on developing a full-fledged flexible data center network simulator that would enable us to configure various aspects of data center networks and also incorporate more realistic usage scenarios for the data centers. This was in pursuit of the final objective of the project where we planned to develop a integrated benchmarking environment where we could incorporate various architectural alternatives and do a comprehensive evaluation and comparison of the alternatives using objective measures. This effort is still ongoing. The objective to achieve a truly flexible and reconfigurable environment proved to be lot more complex that originally anticipated. However we believe that the efforts towards achieving this goal will bear fruit in the near future. We estimate that we are already at the half-way mark by the time this report is submitted, and consider this as a future direction for this research.

612912.label: Major findings and research outcome
612912.value: We proposed a new data center interconnect termed SprintNet, a novel network architecture for data centers. SprintNet achieves high performance in network capacity, fault tolerance, and network latency. SprintNet is also a scalable, yet low-diameter network architecture where the maximum shortest distance between any pair of servers can be limited by no more than four and is independent of the number of layers. The specially designed routing schemes for SprintNet strengthen its merits. Both theoretical analysis and simulation experiments were conducted to evaluate its overall performance with respect to average path length, aggregate bottleneck throughput, and fault tolerance. We proposed a framework to improve the Efficiency of Sever-centric Data Center Network Architectures. There still exist some critical shortcomings in these server-centric architectures. In order to provide an efficient solution to these shortcomings and improve the efficiency of server-centric architectures, in this research, we propose a hardware based approach, named "Forwarding Unit". Furthermore, we put forward a traffic aware routing scheme for FlatNet to further evaluate the feasibility and efficiency of our approach. Both theoretical analysis and simulation experiments are conducted to measure its overall performance with respect to cost-effectiveness, fault-tolerance, system latency, packet loss ratio, aggregate bottleneck throughput, and average path length. We investigated implementation of Software Defnied Networking (SDN) in order to control and optimize data centers. When forwarding new flows in SDN, the interaction between the switch and the controller imposes additional latency. Such latency is an overkill for mice flows due to the their short transmission time. Moreover, the controller is frequently invoked by the mice flows since the number of mice flows accounts for a large portion of the total number of flows resulting in controller performance degradation, and thus increasing the flow setup latency significantly. To solve this problem, we propose CheetahFlow, a novel scheme to predict frequent communication pairs via support vector machine and proactively setup wildcard rules to reduce flow setup latency. Particularly, in order to avoid congestion along a fixed path, elephant flows are detected and rerouted to the non-congestion path efficiently by applying blocking island paradigm. Extensive experiments show that CheetahFlow prominently reduces latency without any loss of flexibility of SDN.

612912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612912.value: Through this research we demonstrated that the clean-slate approach adopted in designing a highly-scalable and flattened architecture that is achieved with FlatNet provides a scalable approach to address the various issues that arise in designing large-scale data center networks. The results from this project clearly demonstrate that the original vision for this project was achieved. Furthering on this issue, given the rapid adoption of SDN as an approach to design highly configurable network infrastructure, we believe that the investigations in this project can be taken forward toward designing new scalable, efficient and highly configurable architectures to meet the future demands of data center networking. Our intense effort to develop a comprehensive evaluation environment for data center architectures has turned into a longer term goal, through the lessons learnt from this project. We believe that we are at a breakthrough point based on the encouraging results obtained so far. We will be vigorously pursuing this in the future.

612912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612912.value: In this research project, we developed a new type of data center interconnect with a clean slate that combines the advantages of previous architectures while avoiding their limitations. In particular, we developed a new class of interconnection network architecture, termed FlatNet, that flatten/simplify the data center network in order to make the application performance independent of the location of the servers. We proposed solutions to the following issues: 1) The investigation of the architectural and topological properties of FlatNet, and how it affects applications’ performance and development as well as their construction cost; 2) The design of routing algorithms for FlatNet by taking into consideration their time complexity, fault-tolerance, and load-balancing properties; 3) The design of protocols and flow management schemes to provide QoS on FlatNet; 4) The establishment of a benchmarking testbed by which we can accurately evaluate and compare various data center architectures (e.g., performance, cost, scalability, etc.) under realistic and practical environments.

613012.label: Project Objectives
613012.value: We will analyze both Master/Slave structure and MapReduce structure of cloud computing and design R&S paradigms that are suited to these structures. We will develop efficient indifference-zone R&S procedures that can solve practical R&S problems with thousands to tens of thousands of alternatives. We will study the new asymptotic regime in which the number of alternatives goes to infinity and develop a theory on proving asymptotic validities and comparing asymptotic efficiencies under this new asymptotic regime. We will build a small cloud with 100 to 200 processors and use this cloud to test various R&S procedures. We will also test the newly designed procedures on commercial clouds, e.g., Google’s GAE, Microsoft’s Azure and Amazon’s EC2. We will build an interface so that R&S procedures can be easily implemented and tested on either our cloud or at least one commercial cloud. We will also extend our work to Bayesian R&S procedures and other R&S problems, e.g., comparisons with a standard and Bernoulli selection.

613012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613012.value: Selection of the best from a finite number of alternatives is a common problem in computer simulation, where the best is often defined as the alternative with the largest or smallest mean performance. This problem is known as a ranking-and-selection (R&S) problem. Its applications include selecting the best parameters for an (s,S) inventory management policy, choosing the best vehicle dispatching policy, etc. As the simulated system becomes more and more complicated, the number of alternatives may also grow. In practice, simulation users may have to select from tens of thousands of alternatives. However, traditional R&S procedures are typically designed to handle problems with no more than 500 alternatives. Therefore, these large-scale R&S problems are often solved by optimization-via-simulation algorithms, which typically simulate only a small fraction of the alternatives and provide no finite-time performance guarantees. The major reason that these large-scale R&S problems are not solved using R&S procedures is because R&S procedures are often run on a single computer and there is often not enough computing power to simulate all alternatives. Although parallel and distributed computing facilities are available, the costs of purchasing and maintaining such facilities are often prohibitively high and many simulation users simply do not have access to them. However, the rise of cloud computing services has changed this situation. Cloud computing service providers, such as Google's GAE, Microsoft's Azure and Amazon's EC2, provide massive computing facilities that can be accessed by clients operating remotely via the internet. These service providers charge according to the usage of computing time. Therefore, users no longer need to keep a local computing facility. Instead, they can use cloud computing services to solve their large-scale R&S problems. We propose to develop efficient R&S procedures for cloud computing. We will study how to design R&S paradigms under different cloud computer structures, e.g., Master/Slave structure and MapReduce structure. We will then develop efficient R&S procedures under these paradigms to solve large-scale R&S problems. We will test these procedures using realistic R&S problems with thousands to tens of thousands of alternatives using both our constructed cloud and commercial clouds. Furthermore, we will also build an interface so that R&S researchers and practitioners may use the interface to design and implement their R&S procedures without going into the details of cloud computing. The successful completion of this project will represent a substantial advance over the state of the art in both theory and practice of R&S. 计算机仿真是运筹学中最有用的工具之一，我们经常用它来选择最好的系统设计方案。这类问题我们通常称之为排序与选择问题。当所研究的系统越来越复杂，可供选择的方案则可能越来越多。在一些实际工作中，可选方案可能达到上万项。但是，传统的排序和选择方法一般只能解决不超过500个方案的问题，因此无法处理这样的实际问题。在本项目中，我们将研究如何使用云计算工具，利用云计算的超大规模的计算能力去解决超多方案的排序与选择问题。如果此项目可以顺利完成，将对排序与选择领域的理论和实践产生很大影响。

613012.label: Realisation of objectives
613012.value: In this project, we have successfully constructed ranking-and-selection (R&S) procedures that may be used in parallel computing environments. We have applied the procedures to solve practical problems with tens of thousands of alternatives, which greatly improved the capability of R&S in solving large-scale simulation optimization problems. We have also developed an asymptotic regime under which the statistical validity of the procedures may be proved. We have built a small computing cluster with about 100 processors and tested the performance of our newly developed procedures. We have also applied what we have learned in developing procedures that may solve R&S problems with chance constraints and with input uncertainty. Through this project, we have also solved a long-lasting open question in R&S field and showed that indifference-zone procedures may be developed. The project was a big success. In a recent paper on the history of simulation optimization (which will appear in this year's Winter Simulation Conference on the reflection of 50 years of history of the conference), two famous simulation scholars, Michael Fu of University of Maryland and Shane Henderson of Cornell University, listed our work on R&S in parallel computing environment one of the three most important work in the past 10 years in the area of R&S. One objective that we have not fully achieved is the test of the procedures on commercial cloud. There are two reasons for this under-achievement. First, implementation on commercial cloud turned out to be more difficult than what I expected and it requires a lot of computer-science skills that doctoral students in my field do not have. Second, and more importantly, the main-stream research on parallel R&S has focused mainly on private computer clusters. In the original proposal, there was a budget for purchasing high-performance computing facilities. I moved from HKUST to CityU in August 2014. The computing facilities are available at CityU to conduct the experiments. So the budget was largely unspent and was returned to RGC.

613012.label: Major findings and research outcome
613012.value: Through this project, we found that ranking-and-selection (R&S) procedures may be used in parallel computing environment to solve simulation optimization problems with tens of thousands of alternatives, without compromising their statistical validity. The key to this success is to recognize that the statistical properties of the simulation output may be changed when parallel computing is used and to design procedures that mitigate these changes (at least asymptotically). We have also implemented these statistical valid procedures in a small cluster with about 100 processors and tested the performance of our procedures. We found that these procedures are very promising. In addition, we found simple schemes that can speed up pairwise comparisons in current sequential R&S procedures, which may significantly improve the efficiency of the procedures. In the project, we have also got insight on how to remove the indifference-zone in the formulation of R&S. This has been a major hurdle and an open question in many years. We finally had a nice insight based on the law of the iterated logarithms to solve this issue. This was not an outcome we intended to have, but it was a nice breakthrough. Besides, we have also applied what we learned from this project to solve R&S problems with chance constraints and with input uncertainty (using a robust formulation).

613012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613012.value: Our work has drawn a significant amount of attention in the stochastic simulation community in solving large-scale simulation optimization using parallel computing environment. We will also work along this way to further improve the efficiency of the proposed procedures, in particular, in considering how to reduce the communication cost that currently dominates the procedure overhead. Also, we will consider how to solve large-scale simulation optimization using R&S procedures, by a proper discretization of the solutions space. Large-sample theory needs to be built to obtain insights on how this should be done. In additional, we will further pursue the research on indifference-zone free R&S and robust R&S, both of which are byproducts of this project.

613012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613012.value: Stochastic simulation has been widely used in many industries to look for optimal decisions under uncertainty. This type of problem is generally called simulation optimization (SO). To solve SO problems, one approach is to evaluate all possible solutions and find the best of them. This is known as ranking and selection (R&S). Before our project, the largest SO problem that has been solved by using R&S has about a few thousand solutions. In our project, we show that efficient R&S procedures may be developed to take advantage of ubiquitous parallel computing environments. Our procedures maintain the nice statistical properties of existing procedures, but may be implemented in parallel computing environment. With our procedure, we can now solve SO problems with ten of thousands to even hundred of thousands solutions.

613112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613112.value: In the past music synthesis research has been mostly oriented to instrument imitation and data reduction, whereas direct timbral control based on perceptual research has received little attention. In other words, the parameters used in traditional music synthesis have not been perceptually meaningful. For example, additive synthesis requires individual harmonic amplitudes, which are usually not individually perceived and are too numerous for facile control. Currently there is no obvious way to imitate acoustic tones using perceptual control, and it is an open question how to effectively map perceptual parameters onto music synthesis parameters. Most researchers in the field of musical timbre agree that two of the most important perceptual parameters are spectral centroid, which strongly correlates with a sound's perceived brightness, and attack time. These two universally-recognized timbral features strongly influence discrimination and identification of musical instruments. We propose investigating the generality and effectiveness of spectral template synthesis, a perceptually-based technique for synthesizing wind instrument tones. Spectral envelope templates are driven by spectral centroid or other perceptually-related control functions. Control by spectral centroid has the advantage of direct manipulation of a perceptually-salient feature. Unlike other synthesis techniques, spectral template synthesis is designed to track changes in spectral centroid and mimic acoustic tones at the same time. In our preliminary experiments, spectral template synthesis achieved nearly indistinguishable matches for trumpet tones. Will it succeed for other wind instruments with different spectral features? The proposed work will test spectral template synthesis on several representative wind instruments, optimizing spectral envelope clusters into templates, and systematically evaluating synthesized tones in listening tests. We aim to advance knowledge of the relationship between instrument spectra and perceptual features such as spectral centroid, even/odd harmonic ratio, and spectral flux, which have been found to be perceptually important in the multidimensional analysis of musical sounds. These problems are fundamental to computer music, musical acoustics, and psychoacoustics. This work has applications in the synthesis of sounds that are natural and realistic, as well as the production of sounds that go beyond the normal timbral boundaries of acoustic instruments. Modeling an instrument’s spectral dependence on perceptual parameters, we will be able to produce new timbres in a controllable fashion. Understanding how listeners perceive spectral envelopes puts us in a better position to design truly expressive musical instruments, and opens new horizons for interactive music creation tools. The results will be useful to synthesizer manufacturers and music application developers. 過去的音樂合成研究大多傾向於樂器模仿及數據縮減，而感知操控則沒有得到多大的關注。換句話說，涉及在傳統的音樂合成中的參數在感知性而言意義不大。例如，多波表合成能夠以相對較少的控制數據模擬出優質的音調，但是它使用的卻是抽象的合成參數。同樣的，加法式合成運用個別的諧波振幅，但這是較重於質感的。目前並沒有明確的以感知控制模擬音調的方式，而如何有效地映射感知參數於音樂合成參數上還是個未解決的問題。 其中一個最重要的感知參數便是與聲音亮度有強烈關聯的頻譜質心。頻譜質心和起音時間是兩個廣為人知，對樂器的分辨和鑑認有著強烈影響的音色特性。 我們提議探討頻譜模板式合成法的通用性及有效性。它是一種基礎於感性認知的管樂器音調合成技術。頻譜包絡模板驅動於頻譜質心或其他控制功能。通過頻譜質心加以控制的好處在於可以直接地操縱感知性顯著的性質。頻譜模板式合成在記錄頻譜質心變化的同時也模擬原聲音調。這是它與其他合成技術不同之處。 在我們的初步試驗中，頻譜模板式合成法成功調節了與喇叭音調近乎毫無差異的音調。它是否可以成功地用於其他例如有顯著共振聲的巴鬆管及有大量奇次諧波的低音單簧管等擁有不同頻譜特性的管樂器上呢？ 這項提案將對頻譜模板式合成法在好幾種具代表性的管樂器上進行測試，將頻譜包絡聚簇改進成模板，並通過聆聽測試對合成的音調進行有規律的評鑑。我們的目的在於進一步認知樂器頻譜與感知特質如頻譜質心之間的關係。這些問題在電腦音樂，音樂聲學以及心理聲學裡是基礎性的。 這項研究的應用在於合成自然和真實聲音，以及建構超出一般聲學樂器音色音域的聲音。通過建模樂器的頻譜與感知參數的相互關係，我們將可以可控性地建構新音色。通過對聽眾如何看待頻譜包絡的了解讓我們可以更好的設計真正具有豐富演奏效果的樂器，並為交互式音樂創作工具打造新的視野。研究結果將有利於音樂合成器製造商，音樂應用程序製作者以及交互設計師。

613112.label: Realisation of objectives
613112.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. For our overall objective, we succeeded in designing a wind synthesis model based on spectral template synthesis that produced natural and realistic tones with characteristic changes in spectral centroid. The model uses spectral envelope templates driven by spectral centroid control functions. We modeled 8 representative wind tones (Bs, Cl, Fl, Hn, Ob, Sx, Tp, and Tb), and subjects judged the synthesized tones natural and realistic in listening tests. We generated a collection of hybrid timbres to demonstrate the model’s capabilities. We generated 56 hybrid instruments, representing the C(8,2) permutations of each pair of the 8 original instruments, where the spectral templates came from the first instrument and the centroid driving function from the second. Several of the instruments were striking (notably the clarinet and trombone hybrid) and most were considered natural by listeners, even though distinctly different from their parent instruments. The approach is an efficient and effective way to generate new timbres for musicians and audio engineers. Second, as one of our sub-goals, we tested the spectral template synthesis on the 8 representative wind instruments using training and resynthesis, and evaluated the matches in terms of relative spectral error. We evaluated the matches in terms of relative spectral error, which has been shown to have more than 90% correspondence to listener discrimination scores for wind instruments. Most of the matches were less than 10% relative spectral error, and the average was 5%. Third, as another subgoal, we determined the best spectral envelope templates by a divide-and-conquer approach using divisive hierarchical clustering. We also tested another method using a greedy approach with sequential clustering. The two methods gave similar results, though the divide-and-conquer approach using divisive hierarchical clustering was slightly better, though slower. Spectral envelopes with similar centroid values had similar shapes, so most envelopes were accurately reproduced. Fourth, as our third subgoal, we asked listeners identify and express preferences for tones synthesized by the model in formal listening tests to statistically evaluate the model’s effectiveness in terms of realism and expressiveness. Subjects judged most synthesized tones natural and realistic in listening tests, but the results indicated that some attacks were poorly matched due to transients. We found the results significantly improved if some templates are dedicated to the attack and the others the rest of the tone. This particularly helped the noisy attacks of the flute, saxophone, and bassoon.

613112.label: Major findings and research outcome
613112.value: We found that spectral envelopes with similar centroid values had similar shapes, so most envelopes were accurately reproduced. The effective results for the trumpet in our preliminary work was probably due to the strong correlation between spectral centroid and spectral envelope shape. We expected comparable results for the other brass instruments since their spectral envelopes typically cluster well based on dynamic level. The woodwinds and bowed strings provided a good way to test the generality of the model. Next, we applied the approach to other brass instruments such as the horn, trumpet, and trombone. The results were even better than the trumpet because the spectral envelopes of these instruments were smoother than that of the trumpet. Encouraged, we applied the model to other wind instruments such as the flute, clarinet, oboe, bassoon, and saxophone. Instruments with relatively smooth spectral envelopes and pronounced formats such as the oboe, bassoon, and Chinese sheng were ideal cases for the model, which captured their formants well. However, instruments with spectral irregularities such as the saxophone and clarinet were not as well matched. The strong odd harmonic of the low clarinet tones seem to require handling as a special case. Moreover, the time-varying spectral fluctuations of the flute were the most problematic for the model. Indeed, tones with strong spectral incoherence such as the flute had the largest residual spectral errors when the original tones and the synthesized tones were compared. We also applied the model to the violin, which like the flute also had strong time-varying spectral fluctuations. The results were similarly mixed for the violin. Instruments with more spectral envelope variation had larger relative spectral errors. The clarinet is an example of such an instrument since it has a near-absence of even harmonics in low-pitched tones, but not in high-pitched tones. For instruments such as the saxophone, spectral envelopes within the same cluster did not have similar enough shapes that all the envelopes could be accurately reproduced from a single template (even though perhaps close in centroid). We conjectured that these results might significantly improve if spectral envelope templates are indexed by fundamental frequency as well as spectral centroid. So, we tested the dependence of each spectral envelope cluster on fundamental frequency, using 2-3 spectral envelope templates per octave. This is particularly important for the clarinet, since the positions of spectral envelope notches due to weak even harmonics move as fundamental frequency increases.

613112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613112.value: One area for further development of the research is to determine whether there are other perceptual parameters that spectral envelope shape depends on. Within a cluster, significant deviations from the template may indicate that centroid and fundamental frequency cannot sufficiently determine spectral envelope shape. Are such deviations due to a few outliers? We can study the distribution of spectral envelopes to see how to reduce their deviations by mapping them to perceptual parameters such as spectral incoherence, even/odd harmonic ratio, and vibrato-related frequency deviation. Another factor in matching accuracy is our choice of the templates and their centroid mapping. Previous research has only tested simple clustering: 10 clusters in equally-spaced centroid bands from 0 to 2000. Will the matching results significantly improve with finer clusters and more templates? And, given the number of spectral envelope templates in advance, how can we determine the best distribution of bands? Finding the best clustering will not only improve our representation, but also show the underlying dependence of spectral envelope shape on spectral centroid.

613112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613112.value: We designed and tested a music synthesis model for wind that produces realistic tones with characteristic changes in brightness. The model uses spectral snapshots from the original instruments as templates driven by a brightness control function. We modeled 8 representative wind tones (Bs, Cl, Fl, Hn, Ob, Sx, Tp, and Tb), and subjects judged the synthesized tones natural and realistic in listening tests. The brass instruments were well-matched because the spectral envelopes of these instruments were smooth. For the woodwinds, instruments with relatively smooth spectral envelopes and pronounced formats such as the oboe, bassoon, and Chinese sheng were ideal cases for the model, which captured their formants well. We also generated a collection of hybrid timbres to demonstrate the model’s capabilities. We generated 56 hybrid instruments, representing the C(8,2) permutations of each pair of the 8 original instruments, where the spectral templates came from the first instrument and the centroid driving function from the second. Several of the instruments were striking (notably the clarinet and trombone hybrid) and most were considered natural by listeners, even though distinctly different from their parent instruments. The approach is an efficient and effective way to generate new sounds for musicians and audio engineers.
