613312.value: 在許多建築項目中,其外部形狀多擁有複雜的曲面設計,尤其是在玻璃幕牆及簷篷中最為常見。生產這些曲面需要更簡單，更細的分區，或面板。為了提高生產力，這些面板應該是標準的和大小均勻的。把一個複雜的曲面細分為標準面板已經是許多研究的主題。因為其在數學上的複雜度和設計一個高效運算法的難度很高,所以難以取得一個理想的結果。雖然這種技術已經取得了一些顯著的進步,但建築設計師可用的軟件還比較少。 一個典型的策略是這樣的,首先，建築師指定一個初始的設計,假設它是一個有限的曲面,在三維空間中定義的一個標準參數形式，如BSplines。然後，將它以網格或圖案的方式細分。以四邊形網格為例（一種最流行的網格款式）,一種方法是創建一組等距交錯的曲線。然而，這種方法會使面板的大小有很大的差距。因此，初始的網格必須通過一種方法稱為re-meshing的進行修改。其目的是改善網格的標準性。在此階段，原本的曲面是可以根據指定的誤差而作出些許修改的。大部分成功的四邊形網格re-meshing,其初始的圖案或排列方式都會是由建築師所引領。在繪製曲面上的圖案,只有少數的方法是曾被探究的。 我們所提出的研究將會是一些新的方法，使設計者可以使用美學曲線(aesthetic curve) 用於設計不同的曲面圖案。這些曲線可以通過一些高層次的參數來作出規範, 如圖案的方向,線條的間隔（取決於曲線的類型）等。此外，每一款式的曲線圖案，我們將開發一個新的網格標準化算法。我們的算法是跟以前的不相同的, 主要是我們嘗試盡量使用分段的可伸展面板(基本上是一種單向曲面面板)換句話說，一個面板可由兩至三個部分組成,它們可能會是圓錐體, 圓柱體或平面。 為了測試我們所提出的方法，我們將開發一個集成的軟件平台，包括所有的優化演算法會以API 的方式編寫在一個繪圖(CAD)系統中,例如 CATIA。所有的測試工作將會與Gehry Technologies, Asia Ltd. 合作進行。

613312.label: Realisation of objectives
613312.value: We feel that both objectives of the project were accomplished as stated in the project proposal. Furthermore, the research staff who worked on this problem were also able to work on some related research problems. In this sense, the project has been one of the more successful and satisfying ones for the PI. For the objective: Develop operators for generating and quantitatively evaluating a new class of curve patterns on BSpline surfaces. 1. The work reported in the CAD&A paper on developable panel approximation, one of the key ideas was the development of a metric that combines the manufacturability and the aesthetics of quad panel. This metric was based on the observation that it was not merely the uniformity of size that dictates the aesthetics, rather, the rate of change of the size played a critical role. Apart from this, kinks in the architectural lines (which are the basis for the panelisation) are easily visible and considered inelegant; the metric included spatial kink angles (deviations from tangential lines). 2. In an extension of this work, the shape of embedded channels in skyscrapers that house vertical axis wind turbines was studied. It was noted that such structures are aesthetically desirable over horizontal axis turbines mounted on the roof of the building which are more clearly visible and often undesirable to city planners in urban settings. 3. Finally, in the IEEE paper, we examine the tiling of uniform triangular patterns onto complex planar shapes. This work also has direct application in multiple fields, including in architecture. By using an isotropic parameterization of a curved architectural shape, followed by a maximal covering by a uniform tiling, we are able to generate ideal aesthetic designs of large architectural buildings with triangular patterns on the roof or canopy. For the objective: Develop algorithms that will generate rationalized quad mesh approximations of arbitrary input surfaces with the goal of minimizing fabrication costs 1. The reported work in the CAD&A journal provides an iterative algorithm which is designed to yield rationalized panelisation of a curved surface using quad-meshes. By ensuring that these panels are developable (namely, planar, cylindrical, or conical, or C1 connected developable patches), the manufacturability of the panels is guaranteed. 2. In the work reported in the IEEE journal on triangular tiling – we use uniform sized triangles to cover the maximal area of a complex 2D shape. By using isometric paramterization, we ensure that the inverse mapping (effectively draping the triangular tiling onto the original curved 3D surface) yields nearly isometric sizes – this is the goal of the rationalization.

613312.label: Major findings and research outcome
613312.value: We successfully developed a new aesthetics-driven metric for quad-meshing of architectural surfaces. This metric is different form earlier ones in that it adds weight for local variations in addition to traditional ones which use k-means clustering style metrics. In particular, if quad panels vary in size only slightly from their neighbors, we favor such (small) changes along he entire canopy/roof structures. Such variations are of concern in real projects where the building surface is curved along longer spans. Further, we introduce a new algorithm for k-set clustering of quad meshes. Our approach is based on isometric parametrization of the curved surface, which allows for rationalized (2D patterns to be superposed onto the surface. A 2-way mapping between the parameter space and 3D space allows for aesthetic metric evaluations of the implied 3D meshing pattern, and set up the basis for a search process to minimize the aesthetic cost. The approach was implemented successfully.

613312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613312.value: There are some further improvements. The first is to examine the rationalization of the underlying supporting structures for the surface panels. This includes rationalization of sub-frames, stiffeners, and joints. We are working on these problems. The size and complexity of these problems is high, so we will submit more GRF proposals for support of the extended work on this research. Architecture BIM is a rapidly growing area, and will have huge impact in the economic activities of Asia and particularly in HK and China in coming decades.

613312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613312.value: This project is related to architectural design in the detailed stages. When an architect designs a complex shaped building, the surface of the structure may be arbitrarily curved (namely, the mathematical description of the surface involves more complex functions than simple planes/cylinders etc. Typically such surfaces need to be subdivided by using a network of curves on the surface into smaller (but still curved) surface pieces. The size of these pieces is small enough that such pieces can be conveniently produced in factories. Obviously, using fewer pieces is more economical in general, so the subdivision cannot be too dense. If the underlying surface is curved, then, in general, each of the subdivided pieces is different slightly than the other. This induces very high fabrication cost since the pieces are all custom-sized. On the other hand, if we replace very similar pieces by identical sized panels that are close enough to the original size, then we get gaps and overlaps between neighboring panels in the building (although we save a lot of money int eh fabrication). This research produces a result that solves this problem by creating a compromise between the number of such different standard sizes and the aesthetics.

613412.label: Project Objectives
613412.value: A new methodology, based on a Bayesian probabilistic framework, will be developed for identifying the bridge and the vehicle model parameters as well as the dynamic vehicular axle loads, based on synchronously measured vehicle-bridge response data. Considering the uncertainties in the structural and vehicular models and the randomness in road surface roughness and measurement noise, the statistics of the identified dynamic vehicular axle loads will also be determined. In addition, methodologies for optimal bridge and vehicle model selection will be developed. A robust vehicle trajectory tracking algorithm will be developed based on radio signal strength and horizontal acceleration measurements. The accuracy of the vehicle positioning algorithm will be verified by field testing. Other approaches such as direct GPS positioning approach will also be tested for comparison. The performance of the integrated wireless monitoring system will be evaluated by field testing. The pedestrian bridge on the HKUST campus will be utilized as test bed using a specially designed tricycle model vehicle moving on it. During this testing experience will be gained regarding the effect of sensor mobility on the quality and fidelity of measurements as well as on the reliability of wireless communication, power requirements, interference of signals, etc. Based on such experience, an optimal data aggregation scheme based on reliable and energy-efficient communication criteria will be proposed to optimize the dynamic sensor network topology and possible hardware improvements will be proposed.

613412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613412.value: We propose to develop a novel approach for investigating vehicle-bridge interaction based on an integrated wireless monitoring system. Vehicle-bridge interaction refers to the dynamic coupling that occurs between vehicles and a bridge due to the contact forces generated between the wheels of the vehicles and the road surface when the vehicles cross the bridge. A complete understanding of this complex coupling between vehicles and the bridge is critical for bridge design, bridge condition assessment, overweight vehicle control, etc. The dynamic analysis of a bridge with vehicles moving on it and the system identification of vehicles and bridge from measured responses have drawn much attention in recent years. However, most of the existing approaches for solving the above problems are based on finite element method (FEM) modeling and simulation and/or the monitoring of bridge responses, neglecting the loading inducing these responses. To more accurately model such complex systems, direct experimental observation of vehicle-bridge interaction is necessary. One of the largest difficulties associated with monitoring both the vehicles and the bridge using one single monitoring system is that the mobility of the vehicles precludes the possibility of connecting vehicle sensors to the bridge monitoring system via coaxial wiring. This project explores the use of wireless technology to allow the integration of vehicle mobile sensors into a bridge monitoring system. In this project, wireless sensors will be utilized as building blocks of such an integrated system designed for monitoring vehicle-bridge interaction. Both the vehicle and bridge responses will be measured synchronously for the purpose of investigating the vehicle-bridge interaction. Based on such synchronously measured vehicle-bridge response data, the dynamic vehicle loads (including position and magnitude) and the vehicular and structural parameters can be accurately estimated. This is very beneficial for the accurate determination of dynamic impact factors for the performance evaluation of existing bridges, the design of new bridges, the health monitoring of bridges under long-term cumulative vehicle load effect and the fatigue reliability evaluation and updating of the bridge system. In this project, the bridge-vehicle interaction problem will be studied using a statistical framework that explicitly accommodates the uncertainties in both measurement noise and modeling errors (i.e., including uncertainties in bridge and vehicle parameters and road surface roughness). It is believed that this project can make significant contributions to the area of vehicle-bridge interaction based on wireless sensor monitoring, an emerging technology that is believed to hold a bright future.

613412.label: Realisation of objectives
613412.value: The stochastic subspace identification (SSI) method, which is one of the most popular approaches for identifying the dynamic properties of linear time-invariant systems subjected to random excitations, has been extended under this project to identify the bridge frequencies by processing the vibration response data of a traversing vehicle. The uncertainties in the structural and vehicular models and the randomness in the road surface roughness and measurement noise have been explicitly accounted for in this work. A traversing vehicle excites the bridge, while the vibrating bridge affects the response of the vehicle. By processing the vehicle response, assumed to be measured with the help of wireless sensors, the dynamic characteristics of the bridge can be efficiently extracted. The proposed SSI method is able to extract the frequencies of a straight reinforced concrete bridge, using the vibration response of a passing “monitored” vehicle. A comprehensive vehicle-bridge coupling model was developed, which includes a 6-DOF mass-spring-damper model for modelling the vehicle, a finite element bridge model, a road roughness model and a vehicle-bridge coupled model. The response of the vehicle can be estimated from the vehicle-bridge interaction (VBI) analysis, where the dynamic characteristics of the vehicle and its motion are known. A prerequisite for the proposed SSI method is the transformation of the time-variant equations of the VBI system into discrete time-invariant state space format. For this purpose, the equations of motion for the vehicle and the bridge are first discretised in state space, and then transformed to a series of time-invariant vectors by separating the known parameters (related to the vehicle properties) from the remaining unknown parameters. The Hankel matrix is then constructed with the transformed measured vectors, containing the vehicle dynamic properties and the vibration response. With a series of algorithms including the LQ decomposition, orthogonal projection and singular value decomposition, the observability matrix composed of solely the bridge dynamic properties is derived from the Hankel matrix. The results of the proposed SSI method have been validated against the theoretically correct values from the numerical analysis, and compared with the results from the fast Fourier spectra. The bridge frequencies can be efficiently extracted by the proposed SSI method, and the effects of the road roughness condition, the driving speed and the on-going traffic on the estimation of the bridge frequencies have been studied. The position of the vehicle on the bridge in the longitudinal direction indicates the location of the interaction between the vehicle and the bridge. Since in practice the traversing vehicle might move on the bridge with varying speed, determining the points of action of the contact forces requires accurate estimation of the position of the vehicle along the bridge at all times. To this end, a robust vehicle trajectory tracking algorithm based on the horizontal acceleration of the vehicle has been developed. Assuming the vehicle moves in a straight line on the bridge, the contact force between the wheel axles and the bridge deck might be localized by integration of the measured horizontal acceleration. The time-varying location of the contact force then works as input information in the proposed SSI method. Another approach for vehicle trajectory tracking is to utilise video surveillance of the bridge. Image processing techniques can be employed to track the position of vehicles from the recorded video. For the vehicle detection and tracking, most methods assume that the camera is static, and the vehicles are recognised by image differencing. With the combination of the detection and tracking techniques, the driving speed of the traversing vehicle can be efficiently estimated. The performance of the integrated wireless monitoring system can be evaluated by field testing. We spent a lot of effort to deal with technical problems encountered when dealing with wireless sensors. Problems related to the synchronisation of sensors, and algorithms for identification using wireless sensors have been developed. Valuable practical experience has been gained though a number of experimental testings both in the HKUST structural laboratory as well as by testing a pedestrian bridge on the HKUST campus in order to identify its modal properties. The successful use of wireless sensors has been validated repeating the tests using wired sensors. Such testings lead to valuable experience gained regarding the effect of sensor mobility on the quality and fidelity of measurements as well as on the reliability of wireless communication, power requirements, interference of signals, etc. To validate the feasibility of the proposed SSI method and the vehicle trajectory tracking algorithm, a tricycle equipped with sensors to collect both the vertical and the horizontal acceleration is underway. The delay in performing the tricycle tests of objective 3, has been caused due to a combination of reasons: the tasks to be performed under this project have been more challenging than initially anticipated; the PI had to undergo a surgery and medical treatment in Europe that kept him away from Hong Kong for a period of three months; one of the foreign students recruited to work for this project has been adjusting slower than expected. It is expected that the remaining tests, that will lead to full realisation of the last objective, will be completed within the upcoming Spring Semester. The number of challenges encountered in this project have been numerous and we believe that we made significant contributions in the field.

613412.label: Major findings and research outcome
613412.value: The stochastic subspace identification (SSI) method has been extended to allow the identification of the bridge frequencies by processing the data of a traversing vehicle, considering the uncertainties in the structural and vehicular models, the randomness in the road surface roughness and the measurement noise. The bridge frequencies are identified with the proposed SSI method, using as input the vehicle response, and assuming that the dynamic characteristics of the vehicle and its motion are known. The results of the proposed method are validated against the theoretically correct values from the numerical analysis. The proposed method has shown an excellent performance in the identification of the fundamental and even higher mode frequencies of the bridge. This paper is in its final stages of preparation (see paper 1, Part C, section 8) and will be submitted shortly for publication. The use of wireless sensors in the monitoring and the challenges they pose have been addressed in paper 1 (Part C, section 8). A novel Bayesian methodology based on the incomplete modal properties (e.g., natural frequencies and partial mode shapes of some modes) is developed for structural model updating (see paper 3). A two-stage fast Bayesian spectral density approach has been proposed to extract modal properties and their associated uncertainties for the cases of separated modes and closely spaced modes, using a novel variable separation technique that fully uncouples the interaction between spectrum variables (e.g., frequency, damping ratio as well as the amplitude of modal excitation and prediction error) and spatial variables (e.g., mode shape components) (see paper 5). A Bayesian mode shape assembly methodology is also proposed to form the overall mode shapes so that the weight for different clusters is accounted for properly according to their data quality. For the proposed method, there is no need to share the same set of reference dofs for all clusters to obtain proper scaling. It avoids the need of matching the measured and model modes, mode shape expansion and eigenvalue decomposition, which are usually encountered in conventional model updating approaches (see paper 6).

613412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613412.value: Identifying the modal parameters of a bridge is important for various engineering applications, including model updating, structural health monitoring and structural control. The methodology developed in this project uses an instrumented vehicle, or possibly a number of such vehicles, traveling on the bridge to perform the bridge monitoring. A number of important research objectives have been addressed in this project that allow us to feel optimistic about the feasibility of the development of an effective and economic working technology for bridge monitoring. Further development is required to enable the extraction of more information, e.g. higher modes, which will be very helpful especially for bridge health monitoring, since higher modes are usually more sensitive to structural damage. Extending the study to curved bridges is another course of action.

613412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613412.value: In this project we introduce a new methodology for monitoring bridges by, rather than instrumenting directly the bridge, using an instrumented vehicle that travels along the bridge. We propose to use the vehicle response measurements to deduce the modal properties of the bridge, or to update its finite element model at a subsequent step, for the purpose of model updating or structural health monitoring of the bridge. Such a technology can revolutionise bridge monitoring, because a single instrumented vehicle can be readily used to monitor a number of bridges. Note that the direct monitoring of a bridge, i.e. installing numerous sensors directly on the bridge, is highly time consuming and expensive. Therefore, the potential of using a single instrumented vehicle, equipped with a very limited number of sensors, to monitor any desired number of bridges is highly attractive and promising.

613512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613512.value: In wireless communications, RF power amplifiers are usually operated in the Class-A or Class-AB mode in order to preserve modulation accuracy. For a Class-A RF power amplifier, the DC current and voltage are kept constant, and its efficiency is proportional to the output power. For a Class-B RF power amplifier, the supply voltage is kept constant while the DC current is proportional to the output RF current. Thus, for a Class-A RF amplifier, the efficiency decreases in proportion to P_out/P_out(max), while for a Class-B RF amplifier, the efficiency decreases in proportion to (P_out/P_out(max))^1/2. The efficiency of a Class-AB RF amplifier lies in between these values, and can be improved greatly if the supply voltage changes dynamically in accordance with the output power. Some existing designs showed that the loss of power amplifiers can be reduced by two times or more by dynamic supply voltage control. However, a high-efficiency wideband supply modulator is needed to achieve both high efficiency and high linearity for the RF power amplifier. Both linear regulators and switching converters could be used for supply modulation. The efficiency of a linear regulator is very poor when the output voltage is low, while a switching converter is very difficult to achieve a loop bandwidth three times of the signal bandwidth. Many of the existing dynamic supply biasing designs are restricted to narrowband applications such as EDGE, CDMA, and WCDMA whose signal bandwidth is of the order of 100 kHz or a few MHz. For emerging 4G high data rate applications such as LTE or WiMAX, the baseband signal bandwidth is as high as 20 MHz and the PAR (peak-to-average ratio) is about 10 to 12dB for the advanced OFDM modulation scheme. We propose to study and design high-efficiency wideband supply modulators with dynamic supply voltage control. The bandwidth of the supply modulator should be as high as 20MHz with efficiency near or over 90%. To achieve both high efficiency and wide bandwidth, a linear-assisted switching converter would be a good candidate. In this architecture, the switching converter is used to supply most of the power confined within the low to medium frequency range, while the linear regulator (may be a low dropout regulator) supplies power for the high frequency range. Existing designs either employ hysteretic-mode control or voltage-mode control. In this research, we propose to explore new control methods, for example, linear-assisted switching converters with current-mode control. 在無線通信中，射頻 (RF) 功率放大器通常工作在A類或AB類模式，以保證調製精度。對於A類的RF功率放大器，偏置電流和電源電壓保持恆定，其效率與輸出功率成正比。對於B類的RF功率放大器，電源電壓保持恆定，而偏置電流則與輸出的RF電流成正比。因此，對於A類RF放大器而言，其效率隨著輸出功率/輸出功率(最大值) (Pout/Pout(max)) 的降低而降低，而對於B類RF放大器而言，其效率隨著 (Pout/Pout(max))^½ 的降低而降低 。 AB類RF放大器的效率在這兩者之間。然而如果電源電壓可以隨著輸出功率動態變化，則功率放大器的效率可以大大提高。 現有設計表明，動態電源電壓控制可以將功率放大器的損耗降低兩倍以上。但是爲了同時滿足RF功率放大器的高效率和高線性度要求，我們通常需要一個高效率寬頻帶的電源調製器。線性穩壓器和開關轉換器都可用於電源調製。當輸出電壓較低時，線性穩壓器的效率非常差。而效率較高的開關變換器則很難實現三倍于信號帶寬的環路帶寬。許多現有的動態電源供電設計只適用于窄帶應用，比如信號帶寬在100kHz到幾MHz的EDGE，CDMA和WCDMA的信號。新興的4G高數據速率，如LTE或WiMAX，採用先進的OFDM調製方案，此調製方案的基帶信號的帶寬可高達20 MHz，其PAR（峰值和平均值比）則在10至12dB之間。 我們建議研究和設計具有動態電壓控制功能的高效率寬頻帶電源調製器。電源調製器的帶寬應該高達20MHz，與此同時工作效率接近或超過90％。為了同時實現高效率和寬頻帶，線性輔助開關轉換器將是一個很好的選項。在此架構中，高效率的開關轉換器可以提供低頻和中頻範圍內的大部分功率，而線性穩壓器（可以是一個低壓差穩壓器）則提供高頻範圍內的功率。現有的設計採用滯環控制模式或電壓模式控制。在這項研究中，我們提出探索新的控制方法，例如，線性輔助開關轉換器的電流模式控制。

613512.label: Realisation of objectives
613512.value: In this research, all objectives have been achieved, and in particular, most of the objectives were achieved by one PhD student, Min Tan, being trained by working on wideband very-high-frequency (VHF, 30 – 300 MHz) hybrid supply modulators (HSM). Realization of objectives is shown by referring to the appropriate publications and/or Tan's thesis. Objective 1 is realized as discussed in [2016J1]. The HSM with single-capacitor current-integration (SCCI) control switched at a peak frequency of 50 MHz, achieved up to 8% efficiency improvement when compared to published works, and was able to track a 0.8 Vpp sinusoidal signal with high fidelity up to 10 MHz. Objective 2 is realized as discussed in [2016J1]. The bandwidth of the HSM is enhanced by employing our developed SCCI control that reduces the complexity of implementation and controls the ripple current of the linear amplifier (LA) indirectly, such that the average output current from the LA is forced to be around zero. It is common knowledge that the efficiency of the switching converter is higher than the linear amplifier. Hence, by supplying the majority of the load current through the switching converter, the overall efficiency is enhanced, while the LA with a wide bandwidth only need to sink and source the relatively small ripple current. Objective 3 is realized as discussed in [2016J1]. Due to the SCCI control and the fast linear amplifier in handling the ripple current, the measured output voltage ripple is reduced to below 8 mV. Objective 4 is realized as discussed in Chapter 2 and Chapter 4 of [2015T]. In [2015T], the small-signal stability conditions and the large-signal stability conditions were compared. We then proposed the bounded ripple-current stability condition, and computed the corresponding lower bound and upper bound of the current ripple. Objective 5 is realized as discussed in Chapter 4 and Chapter 5 of [2015T]. The major contribution here is to separate the design of the HSM and the power amplifier (PA), such that they can be evaluated separately. Furthermore, performance parameters were suggested (and measured) so that HSMs can be compared fairly. In fact, the above objectives are also realized in [2016J2], a journal paper recently accepted for publication. In this work, we proposed the first fixed-frequency HSM with PWM (pulsewidth modulation) control. It switches at 100MHz and is able to track a 0.8Vpp sinusoidal waveform up to 13MHz with high fidelity. Besides fulfilling the above objectives, the research also led to the design and implementation of high-efficiency linear amplifiers (LAs). For example, the LA used in [2016J1] is a modified version of the amplifier in [2015J]. [2015T] M. 613512.label: Major findings and research outcome
613512.value: This research attempts to establish a more solid foundation for analyzing and designing hybrid supply modulators (HSMs). It covers stability conditions, performance evaluation, design analysis and design optimization. The main findings are summarized below. (1) The stability conditions used in previous HSMs are tabulated, and a large-signal stability condition for HSMs that includes hysteretic control as a special case is proposed. (2) The performance parameters that adequately capture the effects of HSMs on the system are identified, and the methods to characterize them are discussed. Design optimization is discussed quantitatively with suggested design guidelines. (3) An efficiency-enhanced HSM with single-capacitor current-integration (SCCI) control was proposed. This control needs only a simple ripple-current sensor instead of a full-range absolute current sensor. The control also enforces the linear amplifier (LA) to have roughly zero average output current such that efficiency is greatly enhanced. (4) A wideband Class-AB linear amplifier that enables small output voltage ripples is designed and implemented. (5) The first VHF (very-high frequency, 30 – 300 MHz) HSM with fixed-frequency control was proposed. A VHF triangular wave generator that is robust to PVT variations and devices mismatch was also proposed.

613512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613512.value: (1) New hybrid supply modulator (HSM) architectures: The large-signal stability condition proposed in this research opens door for new large-signal based designs. (2) HSM with multiple switching phases: The analysis in this research focuses on single-phase HSMs only. Extending the analysis into multiple switching phases to further reduce the output ripple voltage will be an important topic. (3) HSM and power amplifier (PA) co-design: In this research, the design of the HSM is separated from the whole PA system. In practice, they have to be designed together and jointly optimized for best performance. (4) Wideband high-current Class-AB linear amplifier (LA): It is important to design the LA to drive large current, which could be stabilized with advanced compensation structures developed in this research.

613512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613512.value: The efficiency of a power amplifier (PA) can be enhanced if its power supply voltage can be adjusted (=modulated) according to the output signal level. Such a power supply is called a supply modulator. The supply modulator can be a high-efficiency switching converter or a high-bandwidth linear amplifier (LA). This research is to design a high-performance supply modulator for the PA system. We identified that the best architecture is to parallel a switching converter with an LA, to form a hybrid supply modulator (HSM) that attains high efficiency and high bandwidth simultaneously. We proposed that the HSM and the PA can be separately designed and optimized. For the HSM, we identified the large-signal stability conditions that could be employed to both variable-frequency hysteretic control and fixed-frequency PWM control. Our single-capacitor current-integration (SCCI) control switched at a peak frequency of 50 MHz, and was able to track a 0.8 Vpp sinusoidal signal with high fidelity up to 10 MHz. The proposed HSM controlled the ripple current of the linear amplifier (LA) indirectly, such that the average output current from the LA is forced to be around zero. As the switching converter supplied the majority of the load current, efficiency was enhanced.

613612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613612.value: The combined effects of rapid growth in population and global energy demands, as well as geopolitical and climate change problems necessitate a policy change to renewable energy sources. These energy sources such as wind and solar will have to be harnessed and stored. Electrical energy production and electrochemical energy storage are thus central to any new energy model. The widespread application of electric vehicles (EVs) requires development of power sources with high power/energy densities, long life cycles and safety. Amongst various energy conversion and storage devices, rechargeable Li ion batteries (LIBs) and electrochemical double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), or supercapacitors, are considered the most promising candidates to power EVs. The characteristics of the electrode materials determine the overall electrochemical performance of these devices. Although they have many advantages over traditional batteries, such as lead-acid and Ni metal hydride batteries, the current power/energy densities as well as their charge-discharge performance, are far from the satisfactory levels required to power demanding systems. The overall electrochemical properties need significant improvement. The present proposal is an integral part of the PI’s larger research plan to develop novel electrode materials for LIBs and supercapacitors. We plan to develop composite carbon nanofibers (CNFs) with hierarchical structures using the electrospinning technique. Electrospinning uses an electrical charge to draw nanoscale fibers from a liquid polymer or polymer composite. The charged polymer jet ejects out of the needle, elongates and splits into nanoscale fibers, which are deposited on a collector. Three major advances are expected from the project. i) CNFs with a hierarchical pore structure possessing optimized diameter, surface area and distribution will be developed. The increased Li ion intercalation/extraction sites and optimal contact with the electrolyte arising from the pore structure will enhance the electrochemical performance. ii) Metal oxides, such as SnO2 and MnO2, will be incorporated into the CNFs. These metal oxide nanoparticles possess high capacity/capacitance, but usually suffer from poor cycleability and power densities. The overall performance can be improved through the fabrication of metal oxides/CNF composites. iii) Conductive fillers, such as carbon nanotubes and graphene, will be integrated into the CNF or as the external support to obtain high electronic conductivity. These electrospun CNF composite electrodes containing metal oxides and nanoscale conductors with an optimized hierarchical pore nanostructure will offer the ultimate solution to enhanced power/energy densities, as well as long cyclic life and safety, which are essential to powering future mobile systems including EVs. 随着人口经济的快速增长以及环境的日益恶化，人们对新型清洁可再生能源的需求越来越强烈，能源的储存对于太阳能，风能等新型能源的应用起着至关重要的作用。高功率和能量密度，安全以及长寿命的电源系统的开发是电动交通工具广泛应用的基础。相比于传统的铅酸和镍—金属电池，锂电池和超级电容器等电化学储能器件作为电动交通工具的电源系统具备很多优势，但是它们目前的性能依然远远不能满足电动交通工具对电源系统功率/能量密度以及循环寿命的要求，其性能的进一步提高取决于电极材料的开发。 本申请是申请人“新型锂电池和超级电容器电极材料开发”的研究计划的有效组成部分。在该申请中，我们提出了利用电纺丝制备层次孔结构的纳米碳纤维，电纺丝是通过对聚合物的溶液施加高电压使得它在强电场作用下拉成纤维。通过本研究，我们希望实现下列三个目标：（1） 制备层次孔结构的纳米碳纤维，其直径，比表面积，孔径分布将进一步优化，以提高锂离子嵌锂/脱锂的活性点以及确保电极材料与电解液的充分接触，从而实现优良的电化学性能；（2）合成金属氧化物/纳米碳纤维复合材料。SnO2，MnO2等金属氧化物虽然具备极高的比容量和比电容，但是循环性能以及能量密度较差，通过将其负载在多孔纳米碳纤维中，有望达到优秀的综合性能；（3）填充碳纳米管和石墨烯，使用这些导电添加剂填充到纳米碳纤维内部或者作为外部的基体，可以达到较高的电导率。通过以上手段，我们可以得到同时具备高功率/能量密度以及长寿命的纳米碳纤维电极材料，对包括电动交通工具在内的移动电源系统的进一步发展取到推动作用。

613612.label: Realisation of objectives
613612.value: The two objectives in this project have been fully achieved according to the original research plan without any problems encountered. Many original and interesting results have been obtained and a number of high quality papers were published in the prestigious journals. The major outcome from the project is summarized in the below. CNFs with uniform diameters, optimal porosity and atomic structure were developed by electrospinning polyacrylonitrile (PAN) precursor for high performance anodes in lithium ion batteries (LIBs). It is found that the carbonization temperature played an important role in determining the atomic structure and electrochemical performance of CNFs. With the increase in carbonization temperature, the content of nitrogen containing groups decreased drastically, leading to a low specific capacity of the electrodes made therefrom. CNFs carbonized at 550 °C presented the highest capacities amongst all CNFs carbonized at different temperatures. To improve the electrical conductivity and porosity of CNF electrodes, porous CNFs were prepared by electrospinning Fe precursor/PAN mixture. The Fe precursor functioned as both catalyst for graphitization and sacrificial phase. The porous CNFs possess advantages of a high degree of graphitic structure, a high electrical conductivity, abundant nanopores and numerous carbonyl and carboxyl groups for Li storage, giving rise to a remarkable capacity of 983 mAh g-1 at 0.1 A g-1. The optimal CNFs were then applied to support high capacity active particles for high performance LIB and supercapacitor (SC) applications. Atomic-scale, amorphous SnOx particles were encapsulated in CNF by electrospinning Sn precursor/PAN mixture and carbonized at 750 °C. The SnOx/CNF composites delivered a remarkable capacity of 674 mAh g-1 after 100 cycles at 0.5 A g-1, which was attributed to the ultrafine size, uniform dispersion of SnOx particles and the reversible conversion between Sn and SnOx during cycles. Transition metal oxides including Fe2O3, Fe3O4 and Co3O4 particles were also incorporated into CNFs with controlled diameters, contents and phases. CNFs containing Fe3O4 of 5 nm in size delivered capacities of 687 mAh g-1 at 0.5 A g-1 after 350 cycles and 422 mAh g-1 at 5 A g-1 after 1000 cycles, which are much higher than CNFs containing large Fe3O4 particles of 20 nm in diameter. With a high active material content of 68 wt.%, the Co3O4/CNF electrodes in supercapacitor delivered a remarkable capacitance of 586 F g-1 at 1 A g-1 and 74 % capacity retention after 2000 cycles at 2 A g-1. Si with an ultrahigh specific capacity of 3579 mAh g-1 were also integrated with CNFs for high capacity anodes in LIBs. To accommodate the huge volume expansion of Si particles, the Si particles were monodispersed before encapsulation in CNF films. Graphene oxide sheets and Ni nanoparticles were also added to the Si/CNF composites to improve the electrical conductivity for high rate applications. The optimal Si/CNFs with nanocavities around the Si particles and hollow graphitic carbon spheres presented an exceptional capacity of 1548 mAh g-1 and remarkable high-rate capacities of 770 and 580 mAh g-1 at 2 and 5 A g-1 after 70 cycles.

613612.label: Major findings and research outcome
613612.value: Objective 1: Electrospun CNF films were prepared from PAN precursor for free-standing electrodes, and the correlation between microstructure and Li ion storage performance was investigated. We found that CNFs underwent a transformation from amorphous to graphitic structure associated with the reduction in nitrogen containing functional groups with increasing the carbonization temperature. 550 °C was identified as an optimized carbonization temperature which gave rise to a high nitrogen content and a high capacity of the electrode (J01). To improve the electrical conductivity and porosity in CNFs for high-rate capabilities of CNF electrodes, Fe precursor was incorporated in the PAN solution, which functioned as both catalyst to generate graphitic carbon layers and sacrificial agent to form pores. Exceptional capacities of 983 and 318 mAh g-1 were obtained for the porous CNF electrodes at 0.1 and 3 A g-1, respectively (J02). Objective 2: Due to the tunable electrical conductivity, porosity and freestanding nature, CNFs were used as substrates for supporting high capacity metal (oxides) particles. SnOx/CNF composites were synthesized by electrospinning and carbonization at 750 °C, which delivered a remarkable capacity of 674 mAh g-1 after 100 cycles at 0.5 A g-1. The high capacities were attributed to the presence of atomic-scale, amorphous SnOx particles and the reversible conversion between Sn and SnOx during cycles (J03). Highly conductive carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were added to enhance the high rate capacities of SnOx/CNF electrodes (J04). Other transition metal oxides including Fe2O3 (J04), Fe3O4 (J08) and Co3O4 (J09, J10) were also incorporate into the highly stable and porous, electrospun CNFs for high capacity LIBs and/or supercapacitors. We found that particle size played an important role in determining cyclic stability of metal oxide/CNF electrodes: for example, CNFs containing Fe3O4 of 5 nm in size delivered capacities of 687 and 422 mAh g-1 after 350 cycles at 0.5 A g-1 and 1000 cycles at 5 A g-1, respectively, which are much higher than CNFs containing large Fe3O4 particles of 20 nm in diameter. Si particles with ultrahigh capacities but large volume expansion during lithiation were also electrospun into CNF matrix (J05, J06). By monodipersion and nano-cavity engineering, we were able to prepare optimal Si/CNFs electrode structures that presented an exceptional capacity of 1548 mAh g-1 and remarkable high-rate capacities of 770 and 580 mAh g-1 at 2 and 5 A g-1 after 70 cycles (J11). It is now well-established that CNFs with excellent conductivities, large surface areas and structural stability can serve as substrates/active materials for high performance LIBs and supercapacitors (J12).

613612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613612.value: In addition to LIBs and supercapacitors studied in this project, the research can be extended by employing electrospun CNFs in other energy storage systems like lithium sulfur batteries (LSBs), lithium oxygen batteries (LOBs) and sodium ion batteries (SIBs). Subsequently, we were able to get funding support in 2015 from an ITF project (ITS/318/14) entitled “nanocarbon/sulfur composite electrodes for Li-S batteries with exceptional long-term cyclic and environmental stability.” The CNF-based nanostructures with high electrical conductivity and large surface area can function as ideal sulfur container and interlayers for high performance LSBs. Furthermore, hierarchically porous CNFs with in-situ encapsulated catalysts can be used as an efficient oxygen electrode for LOBs. The high conductivity and uniform dispersion of catalysts endow CNF-based electrodes with high capacities and enhanced cycle life. In addition, electrospun CNF-based composites can also be applied in SIBs by accommodating the volume expansion of active particles as well as facilitating fast electron/ion transport of the electrode. In summary, electrospun CNFs with good mechanical durability, excellent electrical conductivities, and tunable surface areas and porosities have great potential for accelerated development of other emerging energy storage systems alternative to the first-generation LIBs.

613612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613612.value: The current society faces two main energy crises, namely, to develop renewable and clean energy sources and to store/reuse the sustainable energy in efficient and effective ways. To satisfy the latter challenge, electrochemical energy storage systems with high power/energy densities, long cycle life and low cost are under increasing demand. Carbon nanofibers (CNFs) with unique properties, such as excellent mechanical property, high aspect ratio, high electrical conductivity and tunable porosity, have been identified as promising substrates or/and active materials for energy storage devices. Through this project, we have successfully synthesized freestanding CNF-based composites with large quantity and controllable structure by facile electrospinning method. Significant improvements in electrochemical performance have been achieved for rechargeable batteries and supercapacitors, through successful design and synthesis of various CNF-based nanostructures with different functional active materials. The fundamental understanding involving the correlation between microstructure and the electrochemical performance of CNF-based composite electrodes have also been established. On basis of the above reliable results, future studies are being encouraged to extend the application of electrospun CNFs and to further improve the energy/power densities of next generation batteries.

613712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613712.value: Infilled frames are one of the most common structural forms for buildings. Although this structural form has been widely adopted for buildings for many years, it has been extensively reported that in every single disastrous earthquake during the past decades poor seismic performance and severe damage of infilled frames have been observed, including many newly designed ones, particularly in the Izmit earthquake of 1999 and the Van earthquake of October 2011 in Turkey, the Sichuan earthquake of 2008 in China, and the Maule earthquake of 2010 in Chile. Hence, inherent problems relating to seismic analysis and design methods for infilled frame buildings have not yet been solved. In analysis of frame structures, infill walls are considered as non-structural components. As a result, the contribution of infills to the overall seismic behaviour of the structures is ignored owing to: (1) adverse consequences of neglecting the infills’ contribution under earthquakes are not recognised; (2) most of the design codes do not provide detailed guidelines for modelling infilled frames; and (3) numerical infill models available in the literature are either too complicated to be implemented in daily designs or too general to reflect realistic loading conditions or the geometric configurations of buildings. The objective of the proposed research is to conduct experimental studies of seismic performance of infilled reinforced concrete (RC) frames using quasi-static cyclic-load and shake-table tests. Emphasises will be placed on the interaction of frames and infills, and failure modes of frames with different infill configurations. In the proposed studies, large-scale specimens with different types of the connection between frames and infills, different reinforcement arrangements and different infill strengths will be tested. Test results will be thoroughly analysed and compared to validate and improve the existing numerical models. Based on the test results, seismic capacity and the corresponding seismic demands on infilled frame structures will be assessed. This experimental research combined with numerical studies is expected to produce better practical guidelines for seismic assessments and design of frame buildings. Hong Kong has recently been classified as a region of moderate seismicity with an earthquake intensity of VII. In view of the large number of infilled frame buildings in Hong Kong, the proposed research is expected to provide crucial guidance for assessing and designing seismically safer frame structures. The results and design recommendations from the proposed research are also expected to benefit infrastructural development in other countries that are threatened by earthquakes. 鋼筋混凝土填充牆框架作為中高層建築的主要結構形式，儘管已被廣泛採納並應用，但在歷次大地震中，其表現出的不同程度的結構破壞，特別是很多新建結構的破壞，揭示現行結構抗震設計規範仍無法有效滿足結構的抗震要求。在歷次地震中，尤以1999年土耳其大地震，2008年汶川大地震及2010年智利大地震的破壞最為典型，這些地震破壞充分說明現有的框架填充牆結構無論在結構設計上還是模型分析上都未能很好的解決其結構模型的很多固有問題。 在傳統的鋼筋混凝土框架牆填充牆結構設計中，填充牆通常被認定為不參與結構受力的非結構構件，故填充牆對結構整體的抗震性能影響無法真實地反映在結構的計算模型中，具體表現為:（1）未能充分認識到在地震荷載作用下忽略填充牆因素所產生的不利影響；（2）大部分現行結構設計規範都未能提供有效的考慮填充牆的結構設計計算方法；（3）現有研究論文所提供的填充牆計算分析模型或過於複雜或過於簡化，均無法有效地反映結構在真實地震荷載作用下的傳力途徑及其相應的地震表現。 本研究計畫主要目的是通過鋼筋混凝土填充牆框架模型偽動力試驗研究，考察框架填充牆結構的抗震性能及地震表現，重點分析不同的填充牆-框架聯接方式和填充方式對結構整體抗震性能和破壞的影響，進而發展準確實用的填充牆框架結構抗震設計。在研究中，將會進行大量的試驗數值分析以求準確評估結構的抗震性能並探究其固有的結構破壞屬性和破壞特點。 香港已被中國國家規範認定為7度設防烈度的中度地震地區。由於香港擁有大量的鋼筋混凝土填充牆框架結構房屋，並且該類型房屋均未採取抗震設計，結構抗震性能薄弱，故本研究計劃意在充分考慮香港地區設計特殊性的基礎上通過結構模型試驗研究以求獲得更加準確的抗震設計方法以確保該該結構形式在地震中能夠具備有效的抗震設防能力。此外，相應的研究成果和設計建議也可以應用和推動其他受地震影響的國家和地區的結構抗震設計發展。

613712.label: Realisation of objectives
613712.value: The research project under the RGC-GRF grant number 613712 is very successfully completed. All three principal objectives of the research have been attained. This research has led to eight(8) refereed journal papers (three published and five ready for submission) published/under review and to be submitted to the prestigious international journals, and nine(9) refereed conference papers. On the basis of this study, performance criteria for identifying the seismic vulnerability of reinforced concrete infilled frame structures and relevant design recommendations have been made. For attaining Objective 1, the seismic failure mechanisms and structural interaction between masonry-infill and RC frame with different infill-to-frame connections are investigated through large-scale experiments. Because the interaction effect of frame and infill on the overall seismic behaviour of RC infilled frames is usually ignored in structural analysis, errors in predicting the actual modes of failure of the structures and infills can be incurred. In this investigation, ten large-scale infilled RC frame specimens were constructed and tested. The specimens include RC frames with different types of infill configurations, including fully-infilled, slitted and door-/window-opening panels, and with different types of frame-infill connections, including full, partial, and weak- and strong-insolation connections. The seismic failure modes of both infills and frames and the effect of frame-infill connectors were studied. For attaining Objective 2, the effectiveness of different reinforcement-connection details in frame-infill interface to improve the seismic behaviour of the structures was studied by conducting experimental testing of six large-scale infilled RC frame specimens, which have different types of frame-infill connections, including full and partially connected ones and weak and strong-isolation connected ones. The structural interaction between frame and masonry infills and failure mode of connections were investigated. For attaining Objective 3, based on the findings of the experimental investigation into the seismic performance and failure mechanisms of infilled RC frame structures with different frame-infill connection conditions and different types of infill-wall configuration, performance criteria for identifying the vulnerability of bare reinforced concrete frames, masonry infill walls, and frame-infill connectors are addressed and design recommendations are made.

613712.label: Major findings and research outcome
613712.value: (1) Objective 1 Seismic failure modes of infilled reinforced concrete frames and the structural interaction between frame and masonry-infill with different frame-to-infill connection conditions and different types of infill configurations are thoroughly investigated by conducting large-scale experiments. In this investigation, ten large-scale infilled RC frame specimens were constructed and tested. The test specimens include reinforced concrete frames with different types of infill configurations, including fully-infilled, slitted and door-/window-opening panels and with different types of frame-infill reinforcement connectors, including full, partial, and weak- and strong-insolation connections. The seismic failure mechanisms of both masonry infills and RC frames and the effect of frame-infill connectors were studied. This investigation relating to Objective 1 has led to seven(7) journal papers, one published (Research Output journal paper No.: 1,8), one submitted (Research Output journal paper No.: 2) and four(4) ready for submission (Research Output journal paper No.: 3,4,5,7), and seven(7) conference papers (Research Output conference paper No.: 1,2,3,4,5,7,8). (2) Objective 2 Six large-scale infilled RC frame specimens were tested for investigating the effectiveness of different reinforcement-connection details in frame-infill interface to improve the seismic performance of masonry-infilled RC frame structures. The test specimens have different frame-infill connection conditions, including full and partially connections and weak- and strong-isolation connections. The structural interaction between frame and masonry infills and failure modes of reinforcement connector were studied. This study in connection to the objective 2 has led to four(4) journal papers (Research Output journal paper No.: 4,5,6,7) which are ready for submission, and four(4) conference papers (Research Output conference paper No.: 1,3,6,7) published. (3) Objective 3 To make recommendations for the evaluation of seismic performance and design of earthquake-resistant masonry-infilled RC frames. Based on the findings of the experimental results and analysis of the seismic performance and failure mechanisms of infilled RC frame structures with different frame-infill connection conditions and different types of infill-wall configuration, performance criteria for identifying the vulnerability of bare reinforced concrete frames, masonry infill panels, and steel frame-infill connectors have been addressed and design recommendations have been made for seismic design and detailing of masonry-infilled RC frame structures. This study connecting to the objective 3 has led to five(5) journal papers (Research Output journal paper No.: 3,4,5,7,8) and three(3) conference paper (Research Output conference paper No.: 3,4,7).

613712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613712.value: The experimental results of seismic performance and failure mechanisms in this research project can be further used for seismic vulnerability assessment of infilled reinforced concrete frame buildings. The design recommendation of the different configurations of masonry infill and the proposed method of connection detailing between frame and infill panel may be modified. The initial work on the development of reasonable detailing techniques for the frame-infill connection and adequate infill configurations has been started. The seismic behaviour of the modified frame-infill connection details and infill configurations can be further investigated experimentally in combination with the development of a new composite-material damage model for infilled wall panels, thus aiming at producing better practical guidelines for seismic design and vulnerability assessment of reinforced concrete frame buildings.

613712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613712.value: Infilled reinforced-concrete (RC) frame structures are recognised as one of the most common structural forms for medium- and high-rise buildings in the world. Although this structural form has been widely adopted for buildings for many years, it has been extensively reported that in every single disastrous earthquake during the past decades relatively poor seismic performance and severe damage of a considerable amount of infilled RC frame buildings. The objective of the proposed research is to conduct large-scale experiments for a thorough investigation into the seismic performance and failure mechanisms of infilled RC frame structures under seismic loading conditions, thus developing effective and practical methods for seismic design and detailing techniques of concrete frames and masonry-infilled walls. In view of a large number of infilled RC frame buildings in Hong Kong and in the world, the research project is expected to provide crucial guidance for designing safer and well-performing frame structures with masonry infills under earthquake actions. Experimental results and design recommendations of the research are also expected to benefit the infrastructural development in the countries and regions that are threatened by earthquake disasters.

614012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
614012.value: With the popularity of social networking websites, there are now billion of photos available online. Typically, each photo has multiple tags (such as "elephant", "jungle" and "africa"), and the total number of unique tags is already in the millions. Traditionally, these images are annotated manually, which can be tedious and time-consuming. Automatic image annotation is thus highly useful, though also a daunting task, and falls in the realm of multi-label classification. In general, to manage objects in a myriad of classes, a popular approach is to organize them into trees (e.g., ImageNet for images) or graphs (e.g., Gene Ontology in bioinformatics). An exciting challenge for multi-label classification is then on how to utilize these label structures. Existing attempts are often restricted to a particular type of classifier and cannot benefit from the development of more advanced classifiers. Another aspect of the complexity of the task is related to the input data representation. Traditionally, each sample is represented by a vector. However, oftentimes the natural representations of many real-world data are not 1D, but rather 2D (e.g., grayscale images), 3D (e.g., color images), even 4D (e.g., color videos). In order to use conventional dimension reduction techniques (such as PCA) on non-1D data, one has to first vectorize the data. However, this destroys the natural structure in the data and leads to information loss. Moreover, even for 2D data such as images, the resultant feature vector is very long (equal to the number of pixels) and thus suffers from the curse of dimensionality. Recently, a few dimension reduction techniques have been proposed that can be directly used on 2D data. However, their relationships with the traditional 1D techniques are not clear. Moreover, their empirical performance is sometimes only marginally better than their 1D counterparts. The goal of this proposal is to make fundamental advances on multi-label learning, where the labels belong to a structured hierarchy; and the input cannot be naturally represented as vectors. The proposed hierarchy-aware multi-label learning technique is flexible (can be used with any learner), efficient (based on a greedy algorithm), and sound (with optimality proofs); while the proposed dimension reduction technique allows probabilistic reasoning and exhibits strong connection with its 1D counterparts. Empirically, they also demonstrate superior performance over existing methods. Together, this offers a better tool to mine the enormous amount of social multimedia data available on the internet.

614012.label: Realisation of objectives
614012.value: Many real-world applications involve multilabel classification, in which each sample can be associated with a set of class labels. These labels often have strong inter-dependencies. For example, in hierarchical multilabel classification, the labels reside on a tree- or DAG-structured hierarchy. On testing, the prediction paths of a given test example may be required to end at leaf nodes of the label hierarchy. This is called mandatory leaf node prediction (MLNP) and is particularly useful when the leaf nodes have much stronger semantic meaning than the internal nodes. In this project, we proposed novel MLNP algorithms that consider the global label hierarchy structure. We showed that the joint posterior probability over all the node labels can be efficiently maximized by dynamic programming for label trees, or greedy algorithm for label DAGs. The algorithms rely only on probability estimators, which can be obtained by various machine learning models and thus can be used with various types of input data (e.g., one can use kernels for structured data). Moreover, both algorithms can be further extended for the minimization of the expected symmetric loss. Experiments on a number of hierarchical multilabel data sets showed that the proposed method consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art. When the number of labels grows to the hundreds or even thousands, multilabel classification can become computationally inefficient. In this project, we addressed this problem by selecting a small subset of class labels that can approximately span the original label space. This is performed by an efficient randomized sampling procedure where the sampling probability of each class label reflects its importance among all the labels. Experiments on a number of multilabel data sets with many labels demonstrate its appealing performance and efficiency. In hierarchical multilabel classification, popular hierarchical loss functions, such as the H-loss, can only be defined on tree hierarchies (but not on DAGs), and may also under- or over-penalize misclassifications near the bottom of the hierarchy. Besides, it has been relatively unexplored on how to make use of the loss functions in hierarchical multilabel classification. To overcome these deficiencies, we first propose hierarchical extensions of the Hamming loss and ranking loss which take the mistake at every node of the label hierarchy into consideration. Then, we first train a general learning model, which is independent of the loss function. Next, using Bayesian decision theory, we develop Bayes-optimal predictions that minimize the corresponding risks with the trained model. Computationally, instead of requiring an exhaustive summation and search for the optimal multilabel, the resultant optimization problem can be efficiently solved by a greedy algorithm. Experimental results on a number of real-world data sets show that the proposed Bayes-optimal classifier outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Many real-world applications involve multilabel classification, in which the labels can have strong inter-dependencies and some of them may even be missing. Existing multilabel algorithms are unable to handle both issues simultaneously. In this paper, we propose a probabilistic model that can automatically learn and exploit multilabel correlations. By integrating out the missing information, it also provides a disciplined approach to the handling of missing labels. The inference procedure is simple, and the optimization subproblems are convex. Experiments on a number of real-world data sets with both complete and missing labels demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can consistently outperform state-of-the-art multilabel classification algorithms. Sometimes, the samples in multilabel classification may not be presented with all its labels. This can be regarded as learning from weakly labeled data, where labels of the training examples are incomplete. Unlike supervised learning, this involves a difficult mixed-integer programming (MIP) problem. In this project, we proposed a novel label generation strategy. This leads to a convex relaxation of the original MIP, which is at least as tight as existing convex semi-definite programming (SDP) relaxations. Moreover, using the SVM as base learner, this approach can be solved via a sequence of SVM subproblems that are much more scalable than previous convex SDP relaxations. Experiments on various weakly labeled learning tasks demonstrated that it is more suitable on big data sets.

614012.label: Major findings and research outcome
614012.value: In this project, we proposed a number of improvements and extensions to multilabel classification. Specifically, - We proposed novel algorithms for mandatory leaf node prediction (MLNP) that consider the global label hierarchy structure. We showed that the joint posterior probability over all the node labels can be efficiently maximized by dynamic programming for label trees, or greedy algorithm for label DAGs. Moreover, both algorithms can be further extended for the minimization of the expected symmetric loss. Experiments on a number of hierarchical multilabel data sets showed that the proposed method consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art (journal paper #1 and conference paper #3). - We proposed an efficient randomized sampling procedure which selects a small subset of class labels to approximately span the original label space. The sampling probability of each class label reflects its importance among all the labels. This allows multilabel classification to be computationally efficient even when there are a large number of labels. Experiments on a number of multilabel data sets demonstrate its efficiency (conference paper #1). - We proposed hierarchical extensions of some popular loss functions which take the mistake at every node of the label hierarchy into consideration. We also developed Bayes-optimal predictions that minimize the corresponding risks. Computationally, the resultant optimization problem can be efficiently solved by a greedy algorithm. Experimental results on a number of real-world data sets show that the proposed Bayes-optimal classifier outperforms the state-of-the-art (journal paper #3 conference paper #2). - We proposed a probabilistic model that automatically learns and exploits multilabel correlations in multilabel classification. By integrating out the missing information, it provides a disciplined approach to the handling of missing labels. The inference procedure is simple, and the optimization subproblems are convex. Experiments on a number of real-world data sets with both complete and missing labels demonstrate that the proposed algorithm consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art multilabel classification algorithms (conference paper #4). - We proposed a novel label generation strategy for situations where not all labels are present as in multilabel classification. Using the SVM as base learner, this approach can be solved via a sequence of SVM subproblems that are much more scalable than previous convex semidefinite relaxations. Experiments on various weakly labeled learning tasks demonstrated that it is more suitable on big data sets (journal paper #2).

614012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
614012.value: Many of the multilabel classification algorithms studied are based on probabilistic models. In particular, this assumed that the underlying probability estimators (such as the conditional probability that a sample belongs to the child category in the hierarchy given that it belongs to that node's parent class) are accurate. However, this may be problematic when training data are limited. One future direction is to analyze how this estimation error affects the classification performance. We plan to study some theoretical guarantees for the proposed Bayes-optimal classifiers about how errors in the probability estimates will transfer to the classification errors. Another possible direction is that we have only considered minimizing the expected risk with respect to the weighted symmetric loss in this project. Extension to some other losses will be explored in the future. Moreover, we are also interested in how much the hierarchy information used in classifiers can help increase the performance over non-risk-minimizing classifiers and flat classifiers.

614012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614012.value: Many real-world applications involve multilabel classification, in which each sample can be associated with a set of class labels. These labels often have strong inter-dependencies, and are organized into trees (e.g., ImageNet for images) or graphs (e.g., Gene Ontology in bioinformatics). Moreover, some of them may even be missing. For example, many image annotation tasks use crowdsourcing platforms to collect labels. For each image, the workers may only provide a small, incomplete set of answers to the queried labels. In this project, we study how these label structures can be utilized for more accurate multi-label classification. We developed a number of algorithms and showed that such information can be utilized efficiently in a disciplined manner, even when the number of labels grows very large. The proposed hierarchy-aware multi-label learning technique is flexible (can be used with any learner), computationally efficient (many of these are based on a greedy algorithm), and sound (with optimality proofs). Empirically, they also demonstrate superior performance over the current state-of-the-art. Thus, this project offers a set of more useful tools to mine the enormous amount of information, such as social multimedia data, that are available on the internet.

614312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
614312.value: 經過硅和III-V化合物數十年針對不同應用的進步，許多半導體團體希望通過這兩種技術的結合以發展更新更高效的的性能。硅基器件和工藝主要應用於邏輯，信號處理和存儲，而III-V半導體器件一般應用於光子學，比如激光，調製器，LED和微波/RF。近年來，III-V（包括III-氮）器件在高速邏輯和功率開關的應用引起人們越來越多的關注。同時，通過採用成熟發展的硅工藝製作光互連，信號處理，路由和開關，硅光子學已經發展成一個充滿活力的研究領域。在學術界和工業界實驗室，許多令人興奮的研究正在這些領域進行。但是，商用PIC（光子集成電路）仍採用磷化銦（InP）基底，其複雜性不斷提升。採用高度成熟的硅工藝在硅平臺上集成所有器件是所有相關團體的美好願望。爲了達成此目標，人們已嘗試諸如鍵合和直接生長的方法，並且仍在努力研究這些方法。硅上直接外延生長砷化鎵（GaAs）和相關化合物曾是1980年代熱門的研究，但是後來卻因為各種原因被放棄了。由於巨大的晶格常數和結構失配，加之熱膨脹係數差別，生長在硅上的III-V材料質量差于生長在晶格匹配的基底上的材料。雖然一些組已經展示了硅上生長的III-V激光，但是可靠性相關的高缺陷密度並沒有解決，所以沒有繼續發展。在硅產業界的需求下，最近研究興趣聚焦在CMOS兼容的結構和工藝上。結合其他材料體系（比如氮化鎵）和新器件設計已有的知識，人們可以採用許多技術來克服這些材料差異，減少生長缺陷。最近硅光子學和高速電子的發展重新激起了人們對此領域的興趣。之前的數年間，我們香港科技大學的研究組已經研究出一種異質外延生長技術，此技術採用有機金屬化學氣相沉積法（MOCVD），可以在硅上生長具有優良器件質量的III-V和III-氮結構。我們已經展示了高速PIN InGaAs光電探測器和高性能晶體管。在這個項目中，我們提出發展硅上生長III-V技術，以應用在集成光子器件中，包括量子點激光器。我們有大量的變質和選擇區域生長知識，我們可以將此應用於展示硅基的有源PIC概念。我們將會結合最新生長技術，器件結構設計和工藝流程，增加功能進而為未來硅光子系統設計者提供更高級選項。

614312.label: Realisation of objectives
614312.value: Our first objective was met through our success in selective-area growth of high-crystalline-quality InGaAs-based photodetectors with optimized InP/GaAs buffers on patterned (100)-oriented silicon-on-insulator (SOI) sub-strates by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition. The composite GaAs and InP buffer was grown using a two-temperature method. The island morphology of the low-temperature GaAs nucleation layer inside the growth well of the SOI substrate was optimized. A medium temperature GaAs layer was inserted prior to the typical high-temperature GaAs to further decrease the dislocation densi-ties and antiphase boundaries. Both normal-incidence photodetec-tors and butt-coupled waveguide photodetectors were fabricated on the same substrate and showed a low dark current and high-speed performance. This result demonstrates a good potential of integrating photonic and electronic devices on the same Si substrate by direct epitaxial growth. Our second objective was achieved by selective area growth on pre-patterned Si using the aspect ratio trapping (ART) process, in which the defects originated from the large lattice mismatch can be effectively blocked by the dielectric sidewalls. Recent studies also suggest that an addition of a V-grooved Si (111) surface to the ART growth can be beneficial to restrict the generation of antiphase-domains and further enhance the defect trapping efficiency. So far, high crystalline quality III-V channel materials for nanoscale transistors have been integrated on Si using this approach. However, the very small volume of useful materials in the growth cavities limits this technique in photonics device applications which typically require a larger active area. In this work, we use of high density, orderly array of in-plane GaAs nanowires on exact (001) silicon to produce GaAs thin films with good crystalline quality, flat surface and no antiphase-domain boundaries. Such a growth scheme eliminates the need of using misorientated Si wafers and graded SiGe/Ge buffers in traditional blanket heteroepitaxy. Due to the combined advantages from nanopatterned growth and epitaxial lateral overgrowth, low defect density, large-area GaAs thin films have been achieved on industrial-standard Si substrates. The third objective was met by the growth and fabrication of GaAs/AlGaAs QW lasers first. Ellipsometry was used to calibrate the Al composition of AlGaAs. Thick p and n type AlGaAs with a mirror like surface were grown by high V/III ratio and high temperature. The GaAs/AlGaAs broad area QW laser was successfully grown and fabricated on GaAs substrate and showed a pulsed lasing result with a threshold current density of about 800 A/cm2. For the integration of lasers on Si substrate, quantum dot (QD) lasers were studied. A flow-and-stop process of TBA was used to grow InAs QDs with the in-situ monitor EpiRas. QDs with a PL wavelength of ~1.3 μm were grown on GaAs and Si substrates. To decrease the PL degradation problem caused by the contaminations from AlGaAs, an InGaAs insertion layer was inserted in between the AlGaAs and QDs region. Microdisk and a-Si waveguide lasers are designed and fabricated. III-V quantum dot (QD) lasers on silicon stand out for their better device performances and reliability. Direct growth of QD lasers on silicon offers an alluring alternative, using widely available large area silicon substrates. In this project, we demonstrated the first 1.55 µm band InAs/InAlGaAs quantum dot microdisk lasers epitaxially grown on (001) silicon substrates. The lasing threshold for the seven-layer quantum dot microdisk laser at liquid helium temperature is 1.6 mW under continuous optical pumping. The low threshold observed lasing is mainly attributed to a unique combination of the high-quality QDs, and small-volume and smooth sidewall of the microdisk structure, the less sensitive nature of quantum dots to crystal defects and a well-developed InP buffer incorporating quantum dots as dislocation filters. These results thus mark a major step towards an integrated III-V-on-silicon photonics platform.

614312.label: Major findings and research outcome
614312.value: We reported selective-area growth of high-crystalline-quality InGaAs-based photodetectors with optimized InP/GaAs buffers on patterned (100)-oriented silicon-on-insulator (SOI) sub-strates by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition. Both normal-incidence photodetectors and butt-coupled waveguide photodetectors were fabricated on the same substrate and showed a low dark current and high-speed performance. We grew large-area antiphase-domain-free GaAs thin films on silicon substrates. Analysis from XRD ω-rocking curves yielded FWHM values of 238 and 154 arcsec, indicating high crystalline quality. We have successfully developed MOCVD growth of self-assembled InAs quantum dots (QDs). The QDs were grown at 500˚C, with an optimized V/III ratio of 0.375 at a growth rate of 0.63 ML/s. A density as high as 5E10/cm2 was obtained, comparable to the best results obtained by MOCVD in the literature. Strong emission with peak wavelength at 1300 nm was achieved with a narrow full-width-at-half-maximum (FWHM) of 29 meV. The identical QD active structure has been grown on a lattice-matched GaAs substrate, a GaAs-on-V-grooved-Si (GoVS) (001) substrates, and a GaAs- on- planar (001) Si wafer with a 4° offcut angle. 1.3 μm room-temperature InAs quantum-dot micro-disk lasers directly grown on (001) silicon To achieve rapid feedback of the QD performance and to promote high-quality factor and dense integration for short-reach communication links, we fabricated microdisk lasers incorporating QDs active regions on the high crystalline quality GoVS template. A five-layer InAs/InGaAs dot-in-a-well (DWELL) structure was adopted [4]. Effective defect trapping and reduction scheme through the V-grooved structure at the GaAs/Si hetero-interface helps maintain good crystalline quality of the active device region. The devices were fabricated using colloidal lithography followed by inductively coupled plasma (ICP) dry etching and dilute HF wet etching. Characterization was conducted using a micro-photoluminescence (μPL) system in a surface-normal pump/collection configuration. Under continuous optical pumping, room temperature lasing was achieved in 4-µm diameter microdisks with excellent temperature characteristics of 105 K in the 1.3-µm wavelength range. In 300 K, a distinct lasing peak appears at 1308 nm and increases sharply in intensity. The smooth sidewall and vertical etching profile of the disk cavity lead to a low lasing threshold of around 200 µW and a high spontaneous emission coupling efficiency (β) of 10%. The β was extracted by fitting the S-shaped nonlinear characteristics to a coupled rate equation model. Lasing was further evidenced through the pronounced narrowing of linewidth. From 10 K to 300 K, Extension of the optically pumped structure towards practical electrically injected laser configurations The optically-pumped microdisk lasers have shown that these quantum dot structures, grown heteroepitaxially on Si substrates, are excellent candidate sources for chip-scale Si-based photonics. This motivates our further exploration of approaches that allow for electrical injection of the QD gain material. Various types of laser structures have been designed, fabricated, and characterized on native GaAs substrates. These include broad area lasers and ridge lasers with a top-bottom contact geometry and a top-top contact geometry. The fabrication platforms developed here pave the way to fulfilling fully integrated electrically driven lasers on Si.

614312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
614312.value: For our ultimate goal of an electrical injection of the microdisk lasers epitaxially grown on Si, the sensitivity of the whispering gallery modes to the geometry of the contacts requires detailed analysis of an integrative structure. Homogeneous lasing emission along the circular cavity rim also makes it difficult to couple light out, not desirable in an on-chip optical interconnect system. We are now designing various structures of resonators to preserve high-quality cavities with efficient directional output-coupling. Electrically-driven version of these compact micro-lasers will have wide applications for optical interconnects from a system perspective. Moreover, a highly efficient III-V laser on silicon operating in the 1.55 μm band for inter/intra-chip optical interconnect is still lacking. The best 1.55 μm QD lasers, with excellent device performance have been reported on InP substrates. A technology that allows the formation of such lasers by direct growth on the Si substrates would be highly advantageous. A novel two-step growth technique involving selective nanopatterned growth and epitaxial lateral overgrowth is under development in our group to achieve high quality InP-on-Si compliant substrates. We aim to develop an efficient active medium based on self-assembled InAs/InP quantum dots for laser diodes on Si substrates, from optically pumped structures to electrically driven devices.

614312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614312.value: Putting lasers on microprocessors boosts their capabilities and allows them to run at much lower powers, which is a big step toward photonics and electronics integration on the silicon platform, Traditionally, the lasers used for commercial applications are quite large—typically 1 mm x 1 mm. Smaller lasers tend to suffer from large mirror loss. We were able to overcome this issue with “tiny whispering gallery mode lasers—only 1 micron in diameter— that are 1,000 times shorter in length, and 1 million times smaller in area than those currently used, Whispering gallery mode lasers are considered to be an extremely attractive light source for on-chip optical communications, data processing, and chemical sensing applications. Our lasers have very low threshold and match the sizes needed to integrate them onto a microprocessor, And these tiny high-performance lasers can be grown directly on silicon wafers, which is what most integrated circuits (semiconductor chips) are fabricated with. In terms of applications, the group’s tiny lasers on silicon are ideally suited for high-speed data communications. Photonics is the most energy-efficient and cost-effective method to transmit large volumes of data over long distances. Until now, laser light sources for such applications were ‘off chip’—missing—from the component, Our work enables on-chip integration of lasers, an indispensible component, with other silicon photonics and microprocessors.
