615212.value: 面向人体运动学、等速传动及五轴加工的并联机构建模、分析与综合的统一几何理论

615212.label: Project Objectives
615212.value: To study and classify exponential submanifolds using the theory of Lie groups and symmetric spaces. To demystify, using the geometric properties of these submanifolds, mysterious mechanisms introduced in the industry, e.g., the Thompson joint. From this we extract useful and develop general synthesis principles. To apply the synthesis principles to synthesize novel mechanisms for CV transmission and five-face machining. To synthesize and design a high tilt angle parallel rotary table intended for high performance machining of consumer electronics products such as mobile phones and tablet PCs. The rotational motion should have ranges exceeding ±90 degree.

To demystify, using the geometric properties of these submanifolds, mysterious mechanisms introduced in the industry, e.g., the Thompson joint. From this we extract useful and develop general synthesis principles.
To apply the synthesis principles to synthesize novel mechanisms for CV transmission and five-face machining.

To synthesize and design a high tilt angle parallel rotary table intended for high performance machining of consumer electronics products such as mobile phones and tablet PCs. The rotational motion should have ranges exceeding ±90 degree.

615212.label: Realisation of objectives
615212.value: 1. We have successfully classified, up to conjugacy, all exponential submanifolds of the special Euclidean group SE(3). There are all together seven classes of non-subgroup exponential submanfolds of SE(3) which admit a global differential structure. These are the symmetric subspaces of SE(3) treated as a symmetric space under the canonical invariant affine connection. The major challenge is that SE(3) is a non-compact non-semi-simple Lie group, and an affine symmetric space theory instead of a (pseudo-) Riemannian one is used. The exponential submanifolds are also totally geodesic submanifolds under the invariant affine connection of SE(3). They are natural generalization of Lie subgroups of SE(3), filling the gaps between the well known hierarchy of Lie subgroups of SE(3). 2. We have completely decrypted relevant geometric properties of exponential submanifolds, which include the inversion symmetry and its many implications: the identity tangent space is a Lie triple system whose derived system is a Lie subalgebra, the half-angle property of evolution of tangent spaces; relation between an exponential submanifold and its completion subgroup: the completion group can be generated by the corresponding Lie triple system and its derived system, resembling the famous tilt and torsion parametrization of SO(3); rules for synthesis of their mechanical generators. This theoretical breakthrough entitles us to demystify the complex kinematic structure of many mechanisms and systems that defy a group theoretical explanation, and also generalize from it a general synthesis method for exponential submanifold generators. 3. Using the general synthesis rule we acquired in 2., we have carried out a systematic synthesis of exponential submanifold generators. Due to the inversion symmetry of the exponential submanifolds, the joint screws of their generating kinematic chains must obey either mirror symmetry or line symmetry. Together with the half-angle property, a general mechanical generator of an exponential submanifold appears to be a plane/line symmetric parallel mechanism with interconnections. In particular, we have successfully synthesized a two degrees-of-freedom parallel wrist which is modeled after the only two dimensional exponential submanifold of SO(3). It surpasses the Omni-Wrists in terms of both kinematic characteristic and mechanical properties. Other successful examples are also being pursued for further prototype development and potential industrialization. 4. We have established a five-axis consumer electronics products assembly platform with a quotient kinematic structure, consisting of a two degrees-of-freedom exponential motion parallel rotary table and a four degrees-of-freedom SCARA robots. The platform has been verified for the assembly of part of a DJI Phantom remote controller.

615212.label: Major findings and research outcome
615212.value: 1. By treating SE(3) as a symmetric space, we solve the classification problem by classifying all Lie triple systems of se(3). Among all vector subspaces of se(3), there are seven classes of nontrivial Lie triple systems. A Lie triple system naturally leads to a homogeneous space which is diffeomorphic to a corresponding symmetric subspace of SE(3). In the normal neighborhood, the symmetric subspaces are exactly the exponential of their corresponding Lie triple systems [Part C.8: Item 2]. 2. It is also true that se(3) admits the geometric characterization of a screw system, which is more relevant to the robotics community. Therefore, we also gave a screw theoretical identification and characterization of all the Lie triple systems [Part C.9: Item 7]. By resorting to dual quaternion representation, we discover that exponential submanifolds are either subspaces or quadrics of the Study quadric, an algebraic variety of particular interest to robotics. This finding is closely related to many known algebraic geometry problems in robotics [Part C.9: Item 6]. 3. Exponential submanifolds play a very important role in parameterizing their completion groups, which are well studied in the robotics community. By treating the exponential submanifold as a homogeneous space G/H where G is the completion group and H is generated by the derived system of its Lie triple system, we have discovered the general synthesis rule for exponential submanifolds. The parametrization of G by G/H ×H is a surprising generalization of the tilt and torsion angle parameterization of SO(3) [Part C.8: Item 1]. 4. A stiffness analysis of the Omni-Wrist V is carried out in detail [Part C.9: Item 1]. The platform shows a modest tilting stiffness and cannot carry out five-axis machining task. We have implemented it in a five-axis quotient kinematic mechanism for assembly 3C products instead. Owing to the extraordinary rotation range of Omni-Wrist, the platform shows a promising potential in fulfilling 3C assembly task. We have also synthesized a novel parallel wrist that surpasses Omni-Wrists in terms of both kinematic and mechanical properties. The result is accepted to be presented in one of the top symposiums in robotics community, ISRR [Part C.9: Item 5]. 5. The research on exponential submanifolds also leads us to rethinking the classical problem of robot kinematic calibration. An efficient geometric calibration algorithm has been developed, which utilizes the homogeneous space representation of two of the seven exponential submanifolds [Part C.8: Item 3, C.9: Item 3,4].

615212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615212.value: Our work on exponential submanifolds for the past 5 years have paved the way for a very broad spectrum of potential application in robotics. Being a universal configuration space model, the exponential manifolds find immediate application in robot motion planning and control, interpolation and estimation, and more generally harmonic analysis for information processing. We plan to carry out study in one or more of these directions in the framework of other ongoing projects (relating to robot repeatability and workcell calibration). Besides, exhaustive type synthesis of exponential submanifold generators, being a laborious undertaking, has not been completed yet. We also see a high possibility to be able to integrate Lie group based (mainly parallel robots) and algebraic geometry based (mainly foldable/deployable overconstrained linkage) mechanism synthesis methods with the help of exponential submanifolds. These pose even bigger undertaking beyond the scope of the current project, and will be carried out with the help of potential collaborators. Finally, application of exponential submanifolds to kinesiology and rehabilitation robotics receive little attention due to rigidity (referring to the metrical differential geometry) of our current result. It needs to be pursued on the algebraic topology level for these particular applications. We are seeking international collaboration on this.

615212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615212.value: The geometry of configuration space of a robot, as a subset of rigid transformation group, plays a crucial role in design, planning and control of robots that generate these subsets. For forty years since Lie subgroups have been introduced to robotics community, people know very little beyond the geometry of a Lie group. In this project, we have unfolded a new class of configuration spaces, the exponential submanifolds for the robotics community. The result is groundbreaking and fundamental to all aspects of robotics, since any research involving configuration space and state space, its tangent bundle, will necessarily be influenced by the geometry of these spaces. In particular, the project develops a geometric theory that unifies the modeling, analysis and synthesis of mechanisms arising from and for human shoulder and eye movement, constant velocity transmission and five-face machining. Central to this theory is the classification, geometric characterization and mechanism synthesis of the seven classes of exponential submanifolds we have unfolded. But the value of our research and the scale of future research stemming from it are simply unlimited. Therefore, it is safe to say that this research is among the best research that took place in the robotics field.

615312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
615312.value: 熱泳現象是指懸浮顆粒在溫度梯度的作用下而產生的運動。在諸多領域中,熱泳現象可以被用來控制小顆粒在氣體介質中的運動。這些領域包括浮質科學,燃燒,以及微納米制作。由於溫度梯度而在顆粒上所產生的作用力叫熱泳力。對稀釋氣體中的微米顆粒,熱泳力通常與溫度梯度相反,這也叫做正熱泳現象(顆粒從高溫向低溫運動)。然而當顆粒小到一定程度的時候,顆粒可能會從低溫向高溫運動。這種現象叫負熱泳。我們過去的理論工作也預測到負熱泳現象在稀釋氣體中存在的可能,且負熱泳現象與氣體分子和顆粒的相互作用力以及溫度有很大關系。 由於火焰中固有的溫度梯度,負熱泳現象對在燃燒中污染物的形成機理的理解有重要的作用。同時,由於人們通常認為顆粒一般會從高溫向低溫運動,這使得負熱泳現象在許多應用中可能會產生一些負面的影響。在溫度梯度的影響下,為了能夠任意控制顆粒的運動,對負熱泳現象的進一步理解是非常有必要的。遺憾的是,迄今為止還沒有很多關於稀釋氣體中負熱泳現象的工作。當顆粒變得多小的時候才會有負熱泳現象也尚不清楚。 在這個專案中,我們將用理論,數值,和實驗的手段研究稀釋氣體中顆粒的負熱泳現象。負熱泳現象所需的臨界顆粒尺寸將通過理論和數值的方法分析。分子動力學模擬及實驗將用來檢驗理論結果。 專案中所獲得的關於負熱泳現象的知識對顆粒輸運理論將是重要貢獻。這些知識也會對污染物的形成以及用溫度梯度來操控小顆粒提供非常有用的資訊。

615312.label: Major findings and research outcome
615312.value: We investigated the motion of particles in gases and on solid surfaces theoretically and experimentally with temperature gradients. We developed lift force formulas for nanoparticles in gases and found that the force can be either positive or negative, depending on the temperature. On solid surfaces, a theoretical expression that describes molecular diffusion in the weak friction limit is also proposed. The formula clearly shows how the potential, friction, and temperature contribute to the diffusion coefficient. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the diffusion of argon molecules on carbon nanotube surfaces are also performed and the theoretical diffusion coefficient formula is shown to be in good agreement with the MD simulations. In addition, MD simulations are carried out to study the diffusion of nanodroplets on surfaces and a scaling law is found. It is shown that nanodroplet surface diffusion is different from that of single molecules and solid particles. The dependence of nanodroplet diffusion coefficient on temperature undergoes a transition from linear to nonlinear as the surface wettability is weakened due to the coupling of temperature and surface energy. We also develop a simple relation for the diffusion coefficient by using the contact angle and contact radius of the droplet. It works well for a wide range of surface wettabilities and nanodroplets of different sizes. In experiments, we study the motion of nanoparticles in gases under various temperature gradients. Some qualitatively results are obtained. In experiments, only particles of a sufficiently large size are found to have preferential motion. For very small particles, diffusion appears to be a dominant factor, which is more important than effects of a temperature gradient. Other than what we proposed in the project, we also investigate the dynamics of bio-particles, such as DNA, and the detection of DNA, which is an interesting topic. In this area, we developed several methods for sensing DNA particles. These methods are either low-cost, highly sensitive, or ultrafast, which are critical in DNA detection Based on our work, we have published 8 journal papers.

615312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615312.value: Through the project, we found that the effects of a temperature gradient on nanoparticle dynamics are important only at certain particle sizes. For very small particles, the diffusion of particles is dominant. Nanoparticle dynamics shows interesting phenomena only in a certain range of temperatures, which depends on many parameters, such as particle material and size. These requires further exploration. Moreover, the dynamics and detection of bio-particles (e.g. DNA) are an interesting topic, which requires more efforts.

615312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615312.value: In this project, we study nanoparticle dynamics in gases and on solid surfaces. Analytical expressions for the forces and diffusion coefficient of nanoparticles are developed, which are necessary in studying nanoparticle dynamics in gases and on solid surfaces. New methods are also proposed to detect DNA molecules, which has significant applications in biology, medicine, and clinical diagnosis.

615412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
615412.value: Abstract Cement-based materials are typically porous medium. Pore structure represents a fundamental microstructural feature in cement-based materials. The network of pores governs the physical and mechanical properties of cement-base materials such as strength, stiffness, permeability and durability. It is very important to understand and measure the pore structure accurately to optimize the performance of cement-based materials. This proposed project is a fundamental academic research aimed at developing a new approach to measure and to characterize the properties of pores in cement-based materials. The new approach will be based on the impedance or complex resistivity measurement of cement-based materials. A non-contacting electrical impedance measurement device invented recently is going to be used to measure the real part, imaginary part, the module and phase lag of cement-based materials. It adopts a transformer principle and eliminates all the problems involved in the contact between electrodes and fresh cement paste such as electrochemical reactions and shrinkage gap problems. Hence, accurate and reliable impedance data can be obtained. The device can generate electromagnetic waves in a frequency range from 1 KHz to 150 KHz with different amplitude. Based on the physics law, the resistance, capacitance, and induction of the pores in cement-based materials are strongly related to the tortuosity and the interconnectivity of the pores. The frequency of an alternative current (AC) signal is also related to diameter of pores. It provides the solid theoretical background for the interpretation of the characteristics of pores in cement-based materials by using the results of impedance or complex resistivity measurement. In this project, fractal theory will be employed to study pore size distribution and pore tortuosity in the porous media, and a fractal model will be built to analyze the relationship between the electrical impedance response and fractal dimension in cement-based materials based on classical transmission line equivalent circuit. The frequency dispersion and penetration analysis will be used to characterize the size of the pores in cement-based materials. The output of this project may achieve a breakthrough in pore structure characterization for cement-based material and provide a useful tool for the pore size as well as the tortuosity measurement of such materials. 本项目是一项旨在开发测量与界定水泥基材料孔结构性能新途径的基础研究。该途径建立在水泥基材料电阻抗测量的基础上。 非接触式电阻抗测试方法将用于水泥基材料的实部、虚部、模量及相位差的测量。 这一方法采用了变压器工作原理并根除了类似电化学反应及收缩间隙等由于电极与水泥基材料接触所带来的种种问题。因此， 可以得到精确与可靠的电阻抗数据。这一设备可产生1 KHz 到 150 KHz具备不同幅值的电磁波。根据物理学原理，水泥基材料中孔的电阻、电容及电感与孔的大小及孔的连通性紧密相关。交流信号的频率也与孔径有关。这为用电阻抗结果揭示水泥基材料中的孔结构特征提供了坚实的基础。本项目将采用分型理论去研究多孔介质的孔径分布及孔的曲折度并基于传统的等效传输电路建立用于分析水泥基材料的电阻抗效应与其分型尺度关系的分型模型。频率分布与惯入度分析将用于界定水泥基材料中孔的尺寸。 本项目的结果可能在水泥基材料孔结构的界定表征领域取得突破性进展并提供该材料孔结构表征的有用工具。

615412.label: Realisation of objectives
615412.value: 1. The frequency range of the non-contact electrical impedance measurement system has been optimized based on two aspects: the first one is the frequency penetration theory; The second one is the limitation of the materials of transformer core. The penetration depth equation λ=1/2 √(κr⁄σω) relates the pore size to the frequency. For fully monitoring the pore structures, the testable pore size of this system should be larger than 1 mm. The current should not influence the hydration process during test, so the magnetic field of system should be determined as weak as possible. Permalloy was selected as the materials of transformer core because of its high magnetic conductivity in the weak magnetic field. For considering the signal generator and the field shielding, the accuracy of non-contact electrical impedance measurement should be larger than 95%. As a result, a range from 1 kHz to 100 KHz was found suitable for the non-contact electrical impedance measurement. 2. The pore structure of cement paste is a typically disordered system. Research work on the fractal nature of cement paste has been carried out. The hydrated Portland cement paste has been proved to be a fractal microstructure though a variety of pore structure characterization techniques. Firstly, all of the complicated pore clusters could be simplified as cylindrical pores, pore size distribution stands for the fraction volume of the pore volume within a specific pore range. The pore size distribution function can be expressed as: Dv(r)=-dV/dr where dV is the difference in the pore volume; dr is the difference in pore radius. The macroscopic impedance response of cement-based materials under an external electrical stimulus results from the total contributions of electrical paths through which charge carriers travel in the pore solution. Therefore, it is necessary to investigate electrical impedance, inductance and capacitance in a single electrical path within the pore solution. In principle, the electrical response of pore solution can be schematically illustrated in a series model. Basically, the components of an electrical path can be divided into three types: (1) R means the resistance of the pore solution; (2) L stands for the inductance of the electrical path; (3) C represents the interfacial capacitance between the solid and the liquid phase. These three components (R, L and C) can simulate the electrical behavior of an electrical path well through series mode. Based on the fractal characteristic of pores and equivalent electrical components of an electrical path, the fractal electrical network can be drawn with the following assumption: all pore clusters satisfy fractal requirements at all length scales, and are saturated with the conductive solution. It is possible to establish a network analogous to the classical fractal electrical network to describe the electrical response of pore clusters in cement-based materials. It is basically a multistep network in which every RLC cell is linked together by different scaling factors (αβ and γ) in each step. Meanwhile, the topology of the fractal electrical network has the corresponding pore structure network. The pore structure network in the study is composed of two symmetrical branches in each step from the largest cylinder similar to the Itagaki model (more details can be found in the paper “Impedance measurement to characterize the pore structure in Portland cement paste” shown in Part C). From fractal electrical and pore structure networks, the relationship among scaling factors can be derived. The fractal dimension for pore space (Df) can thus be determined by the assumed scaling factors in each step. 3. The frequency dispersion characteristic of porous materials was modeled by de Levie. According to the frequency dispersion of ac signals in porous materials, ac signals of a low frequency can penetrate much deeper in length in a single pore than those of a high frequency. As a consequence, by varying the applied frequency of electrical current, the impedance spectroscopy of specimens can be linked to their pore size distribution by the fractal network. Then the fractal dimension for pore space (Df) can be mathematically determined by the pore impedance fractal model. The cumulative pore volume of cement pastes can be calculated from the pore fractal theory via the fractal dimension Df. Meanwhile, the general effective media (GEM) equation is employed to calculate the bulk porosity development. Then the pore impedance fractal model can be used to calculate the pore tortuosity and pore size distribution for cement-based materials using the results of impedance. 4. To determine the reliability of the non-contact impedance measurement device, Mercury Intrusion Porosimetry (MIP) has also been employed to characterize the pore structure of cement pastes. Portland cement meeting the requirement of ASTM Type I was used to prepare cement pastes with water to cement ratios (w/c) 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 by mass. Cement pastes denoted by F10, F20, F30 and F40 were also prepared; F10, F20, F30 and F40 stood for pastes with the water-to-binder ratio (w/b) of 0.4, in which 10%, 20%, 30% and 40% of cement were replaced by fly ash by mass. Similarly, S10, S30, S50 and S70 represented pastes where 10%, 30%, 50% and 70% of cement were replaced by slag and w/b ratio was 0.4. Also, 5% and 10% of cement in the pastes of SF5 and SF10 with a w/b ratio of 0.4 were replaced by silica fume, respectively. The same batch sample was tested by both the non-contact impedance measurement device and the MIP method at the same curing condition. The porosity and pore size distribution calculated through fractal model could compare with the MIP test results to show the reliability of the non-contact electrical impedance measurement. The results from the fractal model were also compared with quick thermal conductivity meter results and previous literatures. The thermal conductivity of cement-based materials is related to the torturous of pore structures. The fractal dimension for pore space (Df) could be used to predict the thermal conductivity, which could make the comparison with real test results to prove the veracity of the non-contact electrical impedance measurement.

615412.label: Major findings and research outcome
615412.value: Firstly, this is the first time to measure the electrical impedance spectrum of cement-based materials without electrode. The side effects caused by electrode (contacting problem, double layer capacitance and chemical reaction problem) were eliminated successfully in impedance spectra tested by the non-contact electrical impedance measurement system. A fractal characteristic network model is established to describe the electrical response of pore clusters in cement-based materials. By analyzing the electrical equivalent circuit model, a multistep network is developed successfully. Because the frequency range of the system is from 1 kHz to 100 kHz, which can monitor pores with the sizes ranging from 3.2 µm to 2.1 mm right now. In this pore size range, even the most popular method, MIP, cannot achieve an accurate result because of the “ink bottle” effect. The fractal characteristic network model could get a relative high but reasonable results on the macro pore volume, which can reveal the real pore size distribution for analyzing the microstructures and predicting the mechanical properties. This is the first time to figure out pore size distribution of cement-based materials using an in-situ electrical method. We extend the non-contact impedance measurement to monitor the thermal conductivity of pure and blended cement pastes using the developed fractal model. This research fills in the gap of monitoring thermal conductivity of cement-based materials by electrical methods. At the same time, the non-contact impedance measurement and relevant fractal permeability model can be used to make a preliminary evaluation of the real-time permeability evolution of cement-based materials in situ. Besides, by analyzing the pore structure, non-contact impedance measurement can be used to assess the non-steady state migration of chloride ions in cement pastes at an early age.

615412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615412.value: 1) The non-contact impedance measurement system is being upgraded to enlarge its frequency range. 2) The linkage between a certain frequency and the pore size is still needs a further research. More experiments should be conducted if the non-contact impedance measurement system is to be commercialized for detecting the pore size properties of cement-based materials.

615412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615412.value: Various experimental techniques have been developed to analyze pore parameters, for instance: mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) relaxation, scanning electronic microscopy (SEM), and small angle X-Ray scattering. Though much work has been done to study the microstructural development with hydration in cementitious materials, it is still very difficult to explain the pore structure completely. The microstructure of cement-based materials gradually develops as the hydration of cementitious materials continues, hence, it is very difficult to trace pore evolution especially at the early hydration stage because of the methods mentioned above require to stop the hydration of the specimen before test, and some pretreatment processes may damage the microstructure itself. Apart from techniques mentioned above, non-contact impedance measurement (NCIM) is considered as a promising technique in analyzing the microstructure evolution. Comparatively speaking, NCIM usually has high precision and does not require complex pretreatment procedures. Such studies can lead to a deeper understanding of the microstructure development in the cement-based system. What’s more, electrical methods are noninvasive and nondestructive and can treat the micro-structure in situ and in real time. So, NCIM will save a lot of workload, money and time and provide a higher precision in detecting micro-structure of cement-based materials.

615712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
615712.value: The urban transportation planning process typically involves traffic assignment, a way of loading or assigning traffic so that the impacts of alternative transportation improvement schemes can be evaluated. It is important to develop sound principles to model the travel choice behaviors of travelers, so that the resultant traffic loading reflects the actual usage of the facilities. For this purpose, the principle of user equilibrium is commonly used, which states that the travel times on all used routes between the same origin-destination pair are equal and minimal. This principle is appealing; it describes travelers’ tendency to select the shortest routes and at equilibrium, travelers have no incentive to switch to other routes. Nevertheless, the equilibrium solution represents an end result of what can be a very long travel choice adjustment process of travelers. In reality, the travel choice adjustments and consequent traffic loading are just as important to analyze, as the equilibrium may never be reached during a given planning horizon or that the interim network loading patterns may actually be more critical. This proposed research will incorporate dynamic travel choice adjustment processes of travelers into traffic assignment and model the traffic system evolution through its day-to-day (or inter-periodic) dynamics, which will offer great flexibility, allowing different adjustment rules, levels of aggregation and types of traffic model to be incorporated. Moreover, capturing the adjustment processes and evolution of traffic states provides a much richer platform of information to facilitate transportation planning and management. With the popularity of navigation devices providing real-time traffic information and internet social networks sharing travel experiences, travelers learn not only from their own experiences but also those of many others. Would such sharing of information forge a faster convergence to equilibrium, leading to greater stability, or trigger divergence and volatility? Capturing the dynamic adjustment processes of travelers offers a powerful way to investigate how the new dynamics of travel information sharing would influence travel choices, which has important ramifications for transportation management. This project will formulate dynamic travel choice adjustment processes of travelers with different levels and modes of information sharing, analyze their properties, and conduct experiments to investigate how new modes of information sharing would influence their adjustment processes. Finally, we will compare and contrast this travel choice adjustment approach with equilibrium-based traffic assignment models for evaluating transportation management schemes to ascertain the need and value of the new modeling paradigm. 交通配流是城市交通系統規劃中的重要一環。它通過承載或者分配交通流來評估不同的交通改進方案的影響。為了讓交通配流能真實的反映交通設施的使用情況，我們需要建立有效的理論和模型來描述出行者是如何選擇出行的路徑、時間和交通方式等。在已有的各種理論模型中，現階段被廣泛使用的是用戶均衡理論。理論指出，當系統達到平衡的條件時，同一起始點之間的出行者所選擇的路徑，其路徑時間相同且最小。用戶均衡理論之所有得到廣泛的認同，在於它準確地描述了出行者總是選擇最短路徑的動機，同時指出，在平衡條件下任何一個單一個人無法通過改變自己的路徑選擇來減少其交通時間。然而，這樣的交通均衡描述的是一種最終狀態；而這種狀態可能需要在出行者長期不斷調整自己的路徑選擇後才能達到。現實生活中，可能出現規劃期內系統無法達到均衡的情況。另外，不同的網絡配流模型對應著不同的交通均衡狀態。以上兩方面的原因使得研究路徑選擇變化和相應的交通分配結果具有重要的價值和意義。 本研究提出將出行選擇動態調整融合到交通分配中；同時使用逐日（週期間）動態過程來描述交通系統的漸變演化。利用動態過程來描述系統演化賦予了本研究較大的彈性，使其能夠適應多種出行決策調節方法，不同層次的交通聚合模式以及多樣化的交通模型。更進一步的，本研究通過刻畫出行決策的動態調節過程並描述交通狀態的演化路徑，為交通系統規劃和管理提供了一個更廣闊的信息平台。 隨著現在的導航裝置越來越多的利用實時交通信息，出行者除了能根據自身經歷預想出行情況外，還能從其他方面獲得出行指引。社交網絡中傳播的相關信息在此扮演着重要角色。但透過社交網絡分享的交通信息與出行者做出決策之間互相影響的機理並不明確。這種互相作用是促使系統更快的達到平衡狀態且更加穩定，抑或是增加擾動以致系統發散且不穩定尚待研究。深入描述出行決策動態調節的過程正提供了一個強有力有的工具，使得我們能夠進一步研究這一新型的信息共享傳播方式具體如何影響人們的出行決策。這一研究對整個交通系統的管理和優化有着重要意義。 本研究中所述的基於出行決策動態調節的交通分配模型考慮了信息傳遞的不同層次和多種方式，分析了它們的特性，並且通過實驗來驗證社交網絡分享這一新型的出行信息傳播途徑對出行決策的影響和作用。最後，我們將通過比較和對照本模型與基於平衡條件的交通分配模型在不同的交通管理方案下的表現，探明這種新的出行決策機制的用途和價值。

615712.label: Major findings and research outcome
615712.value: Major findings include: 1. Through the formulations developed for the travel choice adjustment process and the accompanying analyzes, we found that though there are similarities between the traditional equilibrium approach and the day-to-day dynamical system approach, mainly in terms of the eventual state of the system, there are also substantial differences, especially in the evolutionary process toward the eventual equilibrium states, which are very important to be depicted and understood, as these interim states may exhibit more severe traffic conditions as compared with the end states (output journal paper #1 and output journal paper #4). 2. The online experiment developed offers a very flexible platform for studying the influence of social network information for influencing travel choices. This technique should be very useful for continuing this type of studies (output journal paper #4 and journal #5) 3. For traffic management, in addition to developing methods for the eventual equilibrium states, it is also important to develop adaptive management schemes vis-à-vis the evolutionary traffic states (output journal paper #3 and output journal paper #4). In fact, such adaptive management schemes should be further developed to cope with the ever changing day-to-day traffic states.

615712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615712.value: This project initiated a new approach for studying dynamic traffic networks through the day-to-day dynamical system approach. As a new approach, even though this project has made a head start, much about the approach still needs to be further investigated, in terms of its properties under a variety of contexts, such as for transport network design problems, traffic control, and provision of information for traffic management. In fact, as a result of this proposal, collaborators of this project have been successful in winning another project in New Zealand to further the investigation started here.

616012.label: Project Objectives
616012.value: Design and implement a holistic, GPU-accelerated genomic data analysis system. Recently there has been some work on GPU-accelerated algorithms for individual genomic computing tasks, e.g., sequence alignment, SNP (Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism) detection, and GWAS (Genome-Wide Association Studies). However, an open and systematic study on GPU-acceleration for the entire set of tasks is still missing. For instance, as SNP detection is usually done on the results of sequence alignment, and a typical approach of GWAS is based on SNP results, we propose to streamline these tasks and adopt GPU-based compression on the intermediate results between these tasks in our system. Study in depth and compare GPU-acceleration for individual genomic computing tasks. Specifically, genome assembly, sequence alignment, SNP detection, and GWAS tasks all have different computational characteristics. For example, genome assembly is data-intensive and requires a large amount of memory whereas SNP detection is computation-intensive; Both SNP detection and sequence alignment are computation-intensive, but they differ in the regularity of the computation and thus require different GPU-acceleration strategies. We will propose suitable techniques for individual tasks based on their computational characteristics, and compare and contrast these techniques to gain insight into their performance impact. Evaluate our algorithms and system on real-world datasets and workloads. Even though our focus is on high-performance data processing techniques through GPU acceleration, our ultimate goal is to make our work useful to genomics computing applications in practice. Therefore, in addition to studying the performance of our techniques in a controlled environment, we will facilitate the transfer of our software to the production environment at our genome institute collaborator site, and evaluate and improve our techniques under real workloads.

616012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616012.value: A DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) sequencer takes DNA samples of humans or other living species, and outputs short sequences, called reads, of up to hundreds of nucleotide bases in digital form. With the high-throughput next-generation sequencing technology, a single sequencer can map large and complex genomes (full sets of DNAs, at scales of billions of bases for humans) in a single run. For instance, BGI (Beijing Genomics Institute), operating the world’s largest sequencing facility, produces terabytes of genome data on a daily basis. Furthermore, these vast amounts of data require complex processing to facilitate scientific discoveries. As a result, genomics applications pose unprecedented challenges to modern computers. Graphics processors, or GPUs, have made high-performance computing inexpensive and widely accessible by packing hundreds of identical computing cores in a single chip. With the massive, parallel processing power, GPUs have made their way into genomics applications through academic explorations as well as proprietary business solutions. Nevertheless, there lacks a large-scale, open, and systematic study of accelerating state-of-the-art genomic computing algorithms with the GPU. Therefore, we propose Gallop, an open-source software package that features new, GPU-accelerated algorithms for genomics applications. Specifically, we are interested in four major computational tasks on genome data: (1) genome assembly, where short reads from an unknown DNA sequence are put together into a complete sequence; (2) sequence alignment, in which short reads are aligned to a reference sequence; (3) SNP (Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism) detection, through which the variation on a single nucleotide is identified between each aligned read and the reference sequence; and (4) genome-wide association study (GWAS), which examines the genomes of different individuals of a species. For each task, we will first study the leading computational models based on effectiveness and popularity, and optimize the CPU-based algorithm. Then, we will design a new GPU-based parallel algorithm that provides the same interface and functionality as the original CPU-based algorithm. Additionally, we will optimize the memory access and disk IO, and schedule the CPU, the GPU, and the IO holistically for efficient co-processing. To our best knowledge, Gallop will be the first GPU-accelerated software package taking on four major genomics computing tasks. We expect to produce innovative algorithms for handling complex computational tasks on massive data, and to gain insight into GPU acceleration for such applications. Gallop will be put in the public domain as well as incorporated into the production systems at our collaborators.

616012.label: Realisation of objectives
616012.value: We have achieved the project objectives to the full extent. Specifically, we have developed a holistic, GPU-accelerated genomic data analysis system, including sequence alignment, SNP detection, and association studies (Objective 1); we have also studied in depth GPU acceleration for individual genomic tasks, including genome assembly, sequence alignment, SNP detection, and association studies (Objective 2); we have evaluated our algorithms and systems on real-world genome datasets and workloads (Objective 3). Our papers were published in international conferences and our software components are used by BGI Shenzhen on a daily basis.

616012.label: Major findings and research outcome
616012.value: We found that genomic data analysis tasks can be accelerated on the GPU by carefully designing suitable algorithms for parallelizable components and integrating these GPU components into the CPU-based system. In particular, we designed GPU-based short sequence alignment algorithms (Lu et al., Distributed and Parallel Databases, 2012) and integrated them with GPU-based SNP detection into a genome resequencing analysis system (Lu et al., SSDBM 2012). We also studied GPU-based large-scale genome-wide association studies (Lu and Luo, Big Data Management, Technologies, and Applications, 2013), and developed a sort-merge-based approach for GPU-based De Brujin graph construction in genome assembly (Lu et al., APWeb 2013). Most recently, we proposed a hashing-based approach to accelerate De Brujin graph construction in big genome assembly on heterogeneous processors including both CPUs and GPUs (Qiu and Luo, ICDCS 2017). Our algorithms effectively take advantage of the GPU's parallel computation and memory bandwidth and accelerate the genome analysis tasks significantly. We have implemented our algorithms, integrated them into holistic systems, and evaluated them in detail on real-world datasets and workloads. Our results show that (1) both SNP detection and genome-wide studies are the most computationally intensive and thus benefit most from GPU acceleration achieving speedups of orders of magnitude over CPU-based implementations; (2) sequence alignment are both computation and memory intensive with irregular memory access patterns. Our GPU-based G-Aligner employs a filter-and-test approach to exploit GPU's computation power for reduced memory access. As a result, its overall performance is several times faster than another optimized GPU-based aligner; (3) genome assembly is memory intensive, both in memory capacity and in access. As such, we proposed firstly sort-based and recently hash-based parallel graph construction to use the GPU's memory bandwidth for acceleration, which outperformed a state-of-the-art CPU-based assembler by up to 20 times.

616012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616012.value: We have worked on accelerating graph construction, which is the most time-consuming component in genome assembly. We are currently working on accelerating the final steps, including edge merging and error correction, after constructing the graph to obtain the complete genome on the GPU.

616012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616012.value: Genome data analysis has great practical impact in life science research as well as in medical applications in the real world. Furthermore, it also poses serious technical challenges to computer science research due to the massive amounts of sequencing data and the complex analysis logic. Current sequencing centers such as BGI Shenzhen are able to produce genome sequencing data from biological samples at a high speed; however, the bottleneck is the analysis speed, which takes days, weeks, and even months on CPU-based computers and servers. Therefore, we proposed to accelerate genome analysis on the GPUs, which have a massive parallel computing power but their hardware architecture and programming interface are specialized for graphics processing. We studied the processing logic of the genome analysis tasks, identified performance bottlenecks, and developed efficient GPU-based algorithms to fully utilize the GPU's parallelism and memory bandwidth. As a result, our algorithms and systems can improve the speed of genome analysis by up to orders of magnitude. Our research pioneers a methodology of accelerating data-intensive scientific applications. Additionally, our prototypes are being used by our collaborators at BGI Shenzhen for their daily analytical tasks.

616312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616312.value: The last decade has seen rapid development in wireless communications. New breakthrough methods have been established for achieving unprecedented data rates over wireless channels, leading to the widespread deployment of broadband wireless technologies such as 3G cellular and Wi-Fi. These technologies are shaping the social, economic and political fabric of the future. However, with the explosive rise in popularity of wireless communications, the issue of data security is becoming ever more critical. Both the magnitude of wireless data and the sensitivity of such data are increasing dramatically, thereby further exemplifying the security issue. Current mainstream approaches to securing wireless links are based primarily on cryptography. Cryptographic algorithms have many advantages and are used ubiquitously in practice. However, it is also quite well-known that they possess certain vulnerabilities, as corroborated by widely publicized attacks on some existing protocols. Of course, preserving the security and privacy of wireless data is one of the most important on-going challenges in wireless communications, and there is strong and on-going motivation for designing new methods with enhanced security. This project will investigate a promising and radically different security paradigm known as "physical-layer security", which can potentially revolutionize the way we design wireless communication systems. The key idea is to intelligently design the physical layer signals in order to ensure robustness against security attacks, rather than the current approach of relying exclusively on higher-layer protocols for providing security. Physical-layer security methods, rooted heavily in the realm of information theory, are exciting and extremely promising as they can complement and significantly strengthen existing security approaches. Most existing work in this area however is quite preliminary, often based on idealistic assumptions. Here we outline a plan for designing novel transceiver techniques which can provide significantly enhanced security in wireless communication systems, without making strong assumptions regarding the whereabouts or capabilities of the eavesdroppers/attackers, whilst also addressing key practical signal processing challenges such as channel estimation, pilot design, and limited-feedback optimization. These issues are critical, but are not yet understood. Our main focus is on enhancing security with a multiple-antenna physical layer, which is representative of most emerging broadband wireless industry standards. This is a project requiring expertise in various areas such as MIMO, signal processing, information theory, coding theory and security. The PI and Co-I have strong backgrounds in these areas, providing the necessary synergistic expertise to ensure the success of this very exciting project.

616312.label: Realisation of objectives
616312.value: All key objectives have been successfully met. The project has produced numerous key contributions, and has led to international journal and conference publications. Objective 1: This substantial objective was aimed at developing a fundamental theoretical framework for designing optimized secure multi-antenna transmission schemes with imperfect channel knowledge. Numerous important contributions were made, and these were reported in three major journal publications and two major conference publications. In [Journal Paper 1], a comprehensive analytical framework was proposed for various optimized adaptive transmission strategies for secure multi-antenna transmission in slow fading channels; considering a basic configuration comprising a transmitter-receiver pair and a single eavesdropper. A generalized theoretical framework was presented in [Journal Paper 2] and [Journal Paper 3] to embrace more realistic wireless ad-hoc network configurations, leveraging tools from the theory of stochastic geometry. In [Journal Paper 2], an ideal case with perfect channel feedback was considered, and this was subsequently generalized in [Journal Paper 3] to embrace practical limited feedback scenarios. These are all substantial contributions, published in top IEEE journals. In addition, one of the related conference papers, [Conference Paper 2], was recognized with a Best Paper Award (Information Forensics and Security Track) at IEEE ICASSP 2014, which is the premier international conference on signal processing. These contributions, collectively, present new fundamental theoretical analysis and optimization tools for multi-antenna secure communications. The objective was met successfully. Objective 2: This objective aimed to develop new transmission strategies for secure multi-antenna communications, leveraging limited channel state information. In each of the major journal (and associated conference) publications, the proposed theoretical framework in each case was employed to propose novel transmission schemes. In [Journal Paper 1], novel artificial-noise-aided beamforming schemes were provided, which were optimized for simple Alice-Bob-Eve configurations. For more general ad-hoc network environments, optimized schemes were presented in [Journal Paper 2] for ideal scenarios with perfect transmitter CSI, and in [Journal Paper 3] for practical limited-CSI scenarios. In each case, the performance of the proposed schemes was studied both analytically and numerically. Comparison with relevant benchmark strategies demonstrated the relative merits of the proposed transmission designs. These contributions, collectively, present new transmission schemes for secure multi-antenna communications with varying levels of channel state information. The objective was met successfully.

616312.label: Major findings and research outcome
616312.value: Below is a brief summary of the major findings in each of the journal papers: [Journal Paper 1]: This paper introduced a completely novel framework for designing artificial-noise-aided secure multi-antenna transmission schemes in slow fading channels. A fundamental communication model was considered, comprising a single transmit-receive pair and a single eavesdropper. Adaptive transmission schemes were presented which were designed to optimize the transmission power and the rate parameters of the wiretap code in order to maximize throughput under a prescribed secrecy outage constraint. The solutions were analyzed theoretically, which provided key insight into the power cost imposed as a consequence of the secrecy constraint. The throughput advantage of the proposed approach over previous non-adaptive strategies was quantified and analyzed, demonstrating appreciable gains. [Journal Paper 2]: This paper extended the previous results to consider networks of transmitters, receivers, and also eavesdroppers. Two different multi-antenna transmission schemes were presented for providing secrecy enhancement: the first based on antenna sectoring, the second based on artificial-noise-aided beamforming. Optimal power allocation strategies were designed and the network-wide performance of the schemes (in terms of network throughput) was analyzed and compared using the theory of stochastic geometry. It was demonstrated that the beamforming scheme exhibited performance advantages over sectoring, particularly when the number of transmit antennas is not particularly large. [Journal Paper 3]: This paper further extended [Journal Paper 2] to account for practical effects of limited feedback channels between receivers and transmitters. In order to account for limited feedback, as well as unknown eavesdropper characteristics, we proposed methods aimed at maximizing throughput under dual constraints: one on the allowable connection outages on the desired transmit-receive channels, the other on the allowable secrecy outages. We proposed novel adaptive transmission strategies for meeting both constraints, optimizing both the wiretap coding rates and the power allocation. Results were also presented regarding how to optimally exploit the limited feedback bits, with a key finding that approximately 20% of the feedback bits should be used for quantizing the channel coefficients, and the remaining 80% used to represent the channel phase. Also, about 8 bits of feedback per transmit antenna were found sufficient to achieve a large fraction (e.g., 90%) of the throughput attainable with perfect feedback.

616312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616312.value: There are numerous avenues for further development. A notable assumption underpinning all results in this project was that the transmitters had multiple antennas, whereas the receivers only had a single antenna. Obvious extensions to multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications is a clear avenue for follow up work. This will impose new theoretical and design challenges, since eigen-beamforming strategies should likely be considered, which will impose more complicated statistical problems. Developing a suitable theoretical framework in this case will require the application of tools from random matrix theory, and the optimization problems will be substantially more involved. An alternative but related direction would be to consider the extension to “massive MIMO” configurations, which is important in the context of next-generation cellular technologies. These extensions are substantial and will be considered for major follow-up proposals.

616312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616312.value: Security is a critical concern in communication systems. In this project, we exploited multi-antenna communications technology to design information-theoretically secure transmission strategies. These novel intelligent communication methods employed optimized transmission rates and power allocation in order to balance the competing goals of providing reliable and high-throughput communications as well as robustness against eavesdropping. Numerous communication scenarios were considered, from the most basic configuration with a single transmit-receive pair with a single eavesdropper, to entire networks of transmitters, receivers, and eavesdroppers. In each case, we provided novel communication mechanisms with superior performance against competing benchmarks. We also developed new analytical theories and methods which may be helpful for communication engineers and may facilitate the design of subsequent, more advanced communication technologies.

616512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616512.value: Impulse noise is a major channel impairment in some real-world communication applications, and can severely limit the achievable performance of a power line communication system which is designed to transmit high-speed data over a conventional power delivery network. Unlike the background Gaussian noise that is very well-understood, the asynchronous impulse noise (caused, for example, by the microwave oven or other electric appliances) is non-stationary and it is often impossible to obtain a reasonably accurate estimate of its statistics. How to recover the transmitted data over the power line without knowing the detailed statistics of the impulse noise is a challenging signal detection problem. This project aims to address the challenge by devising a practical detector that can give close to optimal performance but does not require detailed knowledge of the impulse noise statistics at the receiver. The design of a transmission scheme based on the developed detector suitable for power line communication applications will also be investigated. 在現實通信中，脈衝雜訊是一個主要的通道損害，它可以嚴重限制電力線高速通信系統所能達到的性能。與易於分析的高斯背景雜訊不同，非同步脈衝雜訊（可由微波爐或其他電器產生）是非平穩的，並且通常無法合理準確地估計其統計特性。因此在電力線資料傳輸中，如何在不知道脈衝雜訊統計特性的情況下恢復傳輸的資料是一個極具挑戰的信號檢測問題。該項目旨在通過設計一個實用的檢測器來解決這個難題，該檢測器可以接近最優性能但是並不需要接收端脈衝雜訊的統計特性。同時，我們也將研究基於該檢測器的電力線通信應用的傳輸方案。

616512.label: Realisation of objectives
616512.value: (Citation notation: [J#] refers to the #-th published journal paper and [C#] refers to the #-th published conference paper listed in Part C, where # denotes the integer index.) The original idea of joint erasure-marking and decoding (JED) for a generic impulsive noise channel (assuming the background noise is AWGN) aims to find for e=0,1,2,..., E, the minimum Euclidean metric codeword among all possible codewords and all possible e-erasure patterns and use a suitable stopping criterion (e.g. based on an error detecting code) to determine which of the E+1 found codewords should be the decoding output. Consider the trellis representation of a lattice code. The decoding complexity can be measured by the average number of states per trellis section. In this case, the existing implementation of JED is the joint erasure marking Viterbi decoder (JEVA) whose decoding complexity is (E+1) times that of the Viterbi decoder. In [J1], it is proved that JEVA is equivalent to a metric clipping decoder (MCD) (named the metric erasure Viterbi algorithm MEVA in [J1]). The decoding complexity of MCD is the same as that of the original decoder for the AWGN channel because metric clipping only involves a single operation. Consequently, the existing implementation of JED is E times more complicated than the simplified MCD implementation reported in [J1], which is very attractive especially when the number of erasures (impulsive noise arrivals) is large. This achieved Objective 2. Note that as it turns out, the conclusion is applicable to any linear code. To achieve Objectives 1 and 3, the bit error rate (BER) performance of both JED and MLD over both the Bernoulli-Gaussian and the Middleton Class-A impulsive noise channels, which are the most studied impulsive noise models in the power line communications (PLC) literature, have been evaluated and compared by Monte Carlo computer simulation and by theoretical analysis using the famous Chernoff bounds in [J1]. The simulated BER comparison results show that the simplified JED performs close to the MLD, and the performance loss due to the lack of detailed knowledge of the impulse noise statistics (i.e. JED relative to MLD) is surprisingly small (c.f. Figure 4 of [J1]). Since the Chernoff bounds in [J1] are quite loose compared with the simulated BER results, in [C2], we adapted the unified performance bounding technique originally developed by Biglieri et al. (c.f. reference [11] of [C2]) for fading channels to impulsive noise channels. It is shown that this unified bounding technique is applicable to ANY decoding metric (including those of JED and MLD) and ANY memoryless channels (including the Bernoulli-Gaussian and the Middleton Class-A impulsive noise channels) and it can accurately predict the simulated BER. This achieved Objectives 1 and 3. As it turned out, the application of the unified bounding technique to our problem was somewhat straightforward. Relevant to Objective 4, we discovered that MEVA presents a BER error floor, which has not been reported in the literature before (c.f. [C2]). Thanks to the availability of the aforementioned accurate bounds, we can optimize the metric clipping threshold resulting in the so-called optimized metric clipping decoder (OMCD). We showed that OMCD (a form of JED) can perform close to MLD (without suffering from the error floor problem of MEVA) and our aforementioned conclusion that the performance loss due to the lack of detailed knowledge of the impulse noise statistics (i.e. JED relative to MLD) is surprisingly small should still hold (c.f. Figures 2 to 4 of [C2]). However, since the unified bounding technique we adopted is a semi-analytical method, it does not provide a tractable metric for practical code design for PLC. Instead, we adopted the metric clipping decoder (MCD) and a coarse-fine corner detection to address the synchronization and data detection issues in the presence of impulsive noise (or the salt-and-pepper image noise) in a novel picture-embedding barcoding system called PiCode (c.f. [C1]). In addition, we devised new evolutionary searches for discovering long sequences with an impulsive-like autocorrelation function [J3] and derived a tight correlation lower bound for quasi-complementary sequence sets [J2]. These sequences found important applications in channel estimation.

616512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616512.value: The proposed metric clipping decoder is easy to implement for real-world applications limited by impulsive noise because the metric clipping threshold is the only parameter that needs to be optimized with respect to the impulsive noise channel model and only a few model parameters need to be estimated. However, the impulsive noise channel model may not even be available for some real-world impulsive noise-limited applications. It is of practical interest to devise an adaptive metric clipping threshold scheme based on some estimate of the instantaneous system performance, such as BER and SNR, so that it is applicable for any impulsive noise channel models. Alternatively, in the literature, multiple impulsive noise models have been used to model the time-varying impulsive noise in some PLC and other applications. It would be interesting to design a robust metric clipping decoder with respect to multiple models.

616512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616512.value: The performance of real-world communication systems, such as powerline communications, is often limited by impulsive noise, instead of the background Gaussian noise. Due to the time-varying nature of impulsive noise, it is hard to accurately estimate its distribution. Our previous work showed empirically that even without estimating such a distribution, almost optimal decoding performance can be achieved by using the so-called joint erasure-marking decoder (JED), which performs decoding under some erasure conditions and has a decoding complexity that scales with the number of erasures marked. In this project, we proposed the metric clipping decoder (MCD), which has a complexity similar to that of the conventional Euclidean metric decoder and is therefore much simpler than JED. MCD can be viewed as an equivalent but much simpler implementation of JED. The clipping metric interpretation of JED, i.e. MCD, allows the application of a known unified bounding technique to accurately predict its BER performance for a given impulsive noise channel model. It was discovered that the existing metric erasure Viterbi algorithm (MEVA), which is a special form of MCD, exhibits a BER error floor at high signal-to-noise ratio. By optimizing the threshold of MCD (called OMCD), near optimal decoding without any error floor can be achieved. In summary, the proposed OMCD can achieve near-optimal decoding performance without requiring the detailed knowledge of the impulsive noise statistics at negligible additional complexity compared with the conventional decoder.

616812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616812.value: Collapsible loess soils are metastable and they impose major natural hazards to many parts of eastern Canada, the United States, eastern Europe, southern Africa and in the north and the northwest of China such as Lanzhou. Severe damages and loss of lives caused by wetting induced collapse and failure of loess slopes have often reported. Although research has been carried out worldwide to investigate the mechanical and hydraulic behaviour of loess, the fundamental collapse and failure mechanisms of loess slopes are not yet fully understood. Existing theoretical models are not capable to capture all key features of loess mechanically and hydraulically. In this project, four vital research components are proposed to investigate and understand the fundamental collapse and failure mechanisms of loess induced by rainfalls and to assist engineers for their designs. The four major proposed research components include (i) field monitoring of an instrumented loess slope subjected to natural and artificial rainfalls in Lanzhou and in-situ measurements of water retention ability and permeability functions of loess, (ii) advanced laboratory testing of samples taken from Lanzhou, (iii) development of a new theoretical model for loess and (iv) numerical simulations of loess slopes subjected various climatic conditions. In collaboration with the Institute of Geomechanics, the Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences, who has extensive practical experience in stabilising loess slopes in Lanzhou, it is anticipated that high-quality soil samples, field monitoring data from an instrumented loess slope and in-situ test data will be obtained for calibrating the newly developed theoretical framework and constitutive model to capture key features of loess and to discover new insights of its collapse mechanisms. This new constitutive model will be implemented in a finite element code, which will then be used to assist researchers and engineers to improve their understanding of the behaviour of loess and to assist their designs. The success of this project will provide significant and direct benefits to the mainland China and many parts of the world by minimizing damages and loss of lives resulting from failures of loess slopes. 摘要 在全球諸多地區例如加拿大東部、美國、東歐、非洲南部及中國北部及西北部如蘭州等，處於亞穩定狀態的濕陷性黃土已成為誘發自然災害的主要因素。由黃土邊坡濕陷破壞造成的慘重的人員財產損失也時有發生。儘管黃土的力學及水力特性已被廣泛研究，但黃土邊坡濕陷及破壞的基本原理尚不完全明確。現有的黃土理論模型也不能全面描述其力學和水力特性。本項目擬通過以下四個方面研究由降雨引起的黃土濕陷及破壞的基本原理，為黃土邊坡設計提供依據：（1）選取蘭州地區某典型黃土邊坡進行自然及人工降雨試驗和黃土持水性及滲透性的原位測量；（2）對取自該邊坡的黃土試樣進行先進的室內試驗；（3）建立一個新的適用黃土的理論模型；（4）數值模擬不同氣候條件下的黃土邊坡。本項目將與中国地质科学院地质力学研究所合作完成，該研究所在蘭州地區黃土邊坡加固方面積累了豐富的實踐經驗。預期通過優質黃土試樣的室內試驗、現場監測及原位試驗數據，來驗證新建的黃土理論框架及本構模型，揭示黃土邊坡濕陷破壞的機理。并將新建的本構模型嵌入有限元軟件中，提高科研及工程人員對黃土特性的認識，為黃土邊坡設計提供幫助。本項目的成功實施將最大限度地減少由黃土邊坡破壞造成的人員財產損失，對中國大陸及世界其它諸多地區產生重大影響。

616812.label: Major findings and research outcome
616812.value: The stress-dependent water retention curves of collapsible loess over a wide range of suctions were investigated and the effects of microstructure on the water retention curve and wetting–drying induced volume change in loess were studied. The axis translation and vapor equilibrium techniques were adopted to control suction in the range of 0–400 kPa and 4–140 MPa, respectively. It was found that hysteresis in the WRC of loess was observed for the entire range of suction studied. Stress is found to has a significant effect on change of pore size distributions constricted macropores leading to a shift in the main wetting curve and a less pronounced hysteresis. Intact loess exhibits a stress-dependent wetting-induced collapse and drying-induced shrinkage. During shearing, all unsaturated tests dried to high suctions indicate a strain-softening mode of failure associated with noticeable dilation. There is a continuous increase in peak strength with suction but at a reduced rate, which cannot be captured by the improved Bishop’s effective stress model, as it underestimates the contribution of high suctions by approaching zero degree of saturation. Unsaturated tests at high suctions also show an increased rate of dilation with suction for both values of net stress, which cannot be predicted well by the classical stress–dilatancy models. It is shown that for suction values beyond 8 MPa, dilation angle increases by 2° and 6° per 100 MPa increase of suction under net stress of 50 and 200 kPa, respectively. At suctions of 0 and 200 kPa, the shear stiffness and dilatancy of recompacted specimens increase with temperature. The shear stiffness and maximum dilatancy increase by as much as 47% and 63% at suctions of 0 and 200 kPa, respectively. On the contrary, thermal effects on the stress–strain behaviour of intact specimens are negligible at zero suction. At a suction of 200 kPa, as soil temperature rises from 20 to 60 °C, the shear stiffness and maximum dilatancy of intact specimens decrease by 35% and 68%, respectively. It is evident that intact specimens and recompacted specimens experience opposite thermal effects. All above major findings are reported in papers listed in Part C. Other major outcome of this project include seven papers published in international reputable journals and four research students trained (one M.Phil and three Ph.D students).

616812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616812.value: Due to lack of funding, field and centrifuge model tests of loess slopes were not carried out in this project. With the improved fundamental understanding of the mechanical and hydrological behaviour of loess (both intact and recompacted samples), it will be very meaningful and insightful to conduct some field and centrifuge model tests.

616812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616812.value: By developing a new suction and temperature controlled testing apparatus, the stress-strain relationships and shear strength of loess have been extensively investigated at a wide range of soil suctions and temperatures, relevant to slope stability analysis. Moreover, the stress-dependent water retention curves of the collapsible loess over a wide range of suctions were investigated and the effects of microstructure on the water retention curve and volume change in loess were studied. A theoretical framework to capture key features of collapsible loess was proposed. Findings from this research project has significantly improved our understanding the mechanical and hydrological behaviour of loess and hence enable researchers and engineers to better predict the deformations and stability of loess slopes, which are commonly found in many parts of the world. Another significance of this project is that four international research students have been trained: One MPhil from Bangladesh, the other three PhD students from Iran, the Mainland and Thailand. Not only the PI and co-PIs of the project are from three different places, but the research students are also very international coming from four different countries. This project sets a good example of internationalisation of our post-graduate education and international research collaborative activities.

617012.label: Project Objectives
617012.value: Objective 1: To identify and assess methods of real-time forecasting of future freshwater flows and likelihood of extreme low flow events in an environment of heightened non-stationarity, uncertainty and variability. To achieve this, the use of Bayesian inference, extreme value theory and other statistical methods will be investigated and assessed using real and synthetically-generated flows of various means, variances, extreme values and degrees of non-stationarities. Objective 2: To develop an optimization model using mathematical programming techniques of an integrated water supply system incorporating reservoir and additional storage, seawater desalination, wastewater recycling and seawater flushing. The model will include links and feedbacks between the different components to provide a complete representation of the whole system. The model will be multi-period and multi-node to account for temporal and spatial heterogeneities, and the sequential nature of the problem where the optimal decisions for one time period depends on decisions made in previous time periods. Objective 3: To combine the results of the first two objectives into an overall model to solve to quantify the tradeoffs between cost and water supply reliability, robustness and resilience of the integrated water supply system. The overall model incorporating the real-time forecasting future flows will be solved on a rolling basis, first for one time period then the next and so on. At the beginning of each iteration, the forecasts of future flows will be updated as new observations become available. The problem is a multi-objective one where there exist multiple solutions of different weights attached to the different objectives. Objective 4: Ultimately, to gain insight into best strategies for real-time forecasting of future variables and adaptive decision-making in a highly non-stationary uncertain environment. The expected results are useful in providing a new understanding to decision-makers and water managers on best strategies for forecasting in a non-stationary environment and where observations are scarce. New understanding on methods of utilizing the forecasts for adaptively determining optimal water supply development and operation decisions to maximize system performance while minimizing cost and likelihood of system failure are also to be gained.

617012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617012.value: With global warming, surface water flows are becoming increasingly non-stationary with more frequent, longer lasting, extreme low flow events. This affects freshwater availability for human consumption. Traditionally, water management methods assume stationarity such that future flows mimic past patterns. In a non-stationary environment, a new approach is needed that is flexible and capable of adapting quickly and effectively to new conditions. To achieve this, the continual updating of future forecasts and operational decisions are required. Ideally, with this adaptability and the right infrastructure design, the system should be robust so that it will not fail even under extreme conditions. And should it fail, the system should also be resilient such that it will recover within an acceptable time. The proposed study aims to apply a systems approach to a water supply management problem to determine how might seawater desalination, wastewater recycling, seawater for toilet flushing and additional storage be integrated into a conventional reservoir water supply system as a means of providing added flexibility for improving system performance under uncertainty. Seawater desalination and wastewater recycling are not uncommonly used for overcoming water scarcity, but, to the best of knowledge, have not been examined for their potentials as means of adaptively managing uncertainty. Further, since the technologies are energy-intensive processes, they add a new dimension of energy to the problem. Seawater flushing is practiced on a large-scale only in Hong Kong and provides an alternative worthy of further consideration. A multi-objective stochastic mathematical programming model of the system will be developed and optimized to identify the tradeoffs between reliability, robustness, resilience, cost and energy use for different scenarios of non-stationarity, variability and extremity in freshwater flows. The model will include a real-time forecasting component based on Bayesian statistics and extreme value theory to examine questions of the relative weights to be given to past and new observations, and expert opinion, and also of the confidence to be assigned to forecasts given their past accuracies. The model will be solved on a rolling basis with constant updating of forecasts. The results will give insight into best strategies for real-time forecasting of future variables in a highly non-stationary environment and where observations are scarce. Insight will also be gained into best methods of utilizing the forecasts for adaptively determining optimal water supply infrastructure development and operation decisions to maximize system performance, but at the same time, minimize cost and likelihood of system failure. 随着全球气候变暖，地表径流量不稳定性更频繁、更持久，常出现极端低流量事件。这严重影响着人类的淡水供应需求。传统而言，水资源管理方法是以稳定性为前提的，即未来年份的径流是和之前的径流保持一致性。在非稳定的环境中，急需一种灵活可行的新方法能够快速有效地适应环境的不稳定性，这就要求该方法必须能不断的更新预测和操作决策。理论上，这种能够满足环境非稳定变化的设施系统，即使在极端情况下也能够很好的运行，或是系统在可接受的时间内能够自我修复。 本研究的目的在于提供一种水资源管理的方法，将海水淡化，污水回用，海水冲洗厕所以及存储水池附加到一个传统的供水系统上，在非稳定的环境下能够有效的提高系统的运行效果。海水淡化和污水回用经常用于解决淡水紧缺的问题，但是，迄今为止这些方法都尚未用于解决一些不确定性问题。而且，因为该方法是能源密集型的过程，为该问题添加了一个能源层面的问题。海水冲洗厕所只是在香港大范围的使用，同时提供了一种值得深思的替代方法。 本研究将建立一种优化的多目标随机数学规划模型，来调整在非稳定环境中可靠性、鲁棒性、可弹性、费用以及能量的耗费的平衡。该模型包括一个建立在贝叶斯数据分析方法和极值理论方法的实时监测组件，来判定在给定的新旧条件下的相对权重问题，给出专家级意见，并给出正确的预测信息。 该模型将不断更新预测，所得到的结果将在非稳定的环境以及缺乏观察数据的基础上为实时预测做出最佳策略，决策利用自适应预测确定最优的供水设施，让系统保持最佳运行性能的运行操作，同时减少成本和系统的故障率。

617012.label: Realisation of objectives
617012.value: As described in 2 journal papers published in Water Resources Research and ASCE's Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management, a series of conference presentations, and a manuscript that is still under preparation, we have successfully achieved all 4 objectives of the project. To achieve Objective 1, we developed and compared methods based on artificial neural networks and time series analysis to forecast, in real-time, freshwater flows. We have run tests using synthetic flows generated using regional climate model data and a daily scale rainfall-runoff model. The tests show neural networks to perform better than time series models, particularly when the former are coupled with wavelet decomposition. We have incorporated the outcomes from this part of the research into the 2nd part of the project to achieve Objective 2. To achieve Objective 2, we first developed a reservoir operation model to assess reservoir performance under nonstationary flows. Based on the work, we have published a paper [Yang and Ng, 2016] in ASCE's Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management (JWRPM), a top journal in water management. We then extended the reservoir operation model to include components of seawater desalination and wastewater reclamation to achieve the final outcome of an integrated water supply model. We developed 2 versions of the integrated model. We developed the 1st version as a multi-objective program which we solved using genetic algorithms, and the 2nd as a forward-looking sequential linear program which we solved using linear programming. We have published the 1st version of the model [Bhushan and Ng, 2016] in Water Resources Research (WRR), a top journal in water resources. As for the 2nd version, we have presented preliminary forms of it in a number of conferences, including the 2014 and 2015 Fall Meetings of the American Geophysical Union (AGU), both in San Francisco, US. We have now completed the development of the 2nd version of the model, and have used it to generate valuable results. We are making final analyses as we write up a manuscript based on the 2nd version for journal publication. We plan on having the manuscript ready for submission by the end of this summer. To achieve Objective 3, we have run the models developed for Objective 2 under various scenarios of water demands, and present and projected future climate. From the results, we have been able to gain new insights into reservoir system performance under climate nonstationarity, and quantify the tradeoffs between cost and system performance with and without reservoir-desalination system integration. We have reported some of our results in Yang and Ng [2016] and Bhushan and Ng [2016]. To achieve Objective 4, we have critically analyzed the results from Objective 3 to extract new insights into best strategies for water management under nonstationary climate conditions. In Yang and Ng [2016], we compared reservoir operating rules of different forms and showed the different rules to produce different levels of robustness to non-stationary flows. We found rules based on fuzzy logic (an artificial intelligence method) to lead to a more robust system than conventional linear and polynomial rules based on regression. In Bhushan and Ng [2016], from results giving the tradeoffs between cost and system reliability and vulnerability, we showed integrating desalination operation to reservoir operation as a viable means of adapting existing reservoir systems to be more robust to climate uncertainty. (Conventionally, desalination facilities and reservoirs are operated separately.) Finally, in a third journal paper that is still under preparation (based on the 2nd version of the model developed in Objective 2) that we plan on submitting by the end of this summer, we will further examine the benefits of integrating desalination and reservoir operation as a means of climate change adaptation, as well as show the value of forecast information. As will be discussed in the paper, we find neural networks with wavelet decomposition of the inputs to produce improved forecasting of future flows, and the improved forecasts to lead to greater improvements in system performance than constructing new desalination or reservoir capacity. Though, as we will discuss, where high-quality forecasts are unavailable, new desalination or reservoir capacity may be necessary depending on the system function or functions (i.e., if the system is operated primarily for flood control, water supply or both).
