617012.label: Major findings and research outcome
617012.value: From this project, we have published 2 journal papers in top journals in water resources, viz. Yang and Ng [2016] in ASCE's Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management, and Bhushan and Ng [2016] in Water Resources Research. We have also made a series of conference presentations, including presentations in the 2014 and 2015 AGU Fall Meetings, and the 2015 World Environmental & Water Resources Congress organized by ASCE's EWRI. Moreover, we have generated results for a 3rd journal paper that is still under preparation which we will submit to a top journal before the end of this summer. In Yang and Ng [2016], we examined the robustness of reservoir operating rules to inflow nonstationarity. We developed fuzzy reservoir operating rules using optimization-simulation and compared the rules with linear, polynomial, and artificial neural network rules under stationary and nonstationary inflow conditions. We obtained results for two case studies assuming, in each case, a single reservoir with water supply, flood control, and environmental flow allocation functions. The results showed the fuzzy rules to be most robust to inflow nonstationarity. Further, applying the fuzzy rules to 30 years of projected future inflows show their advantage to be enhanced when recalibrated every 10 years or so, as compared to when there is no recalibration. In Bhushan and Ng [2016], we investigated the potential of integrating seawater desalination and wastewater reclamation facilities to existing reservoir systems to mitigate supply uncertainty due to climate uncertainties. We provided a detailed framework for optimizing the joint operation of the three sources based on multiobjective programming with the double objectives of minimizing water supply risk and vulnerability subject to a minimum limit on resilience and water quality, capacity, and budget constraints. From the results of two case studies, we found the joint operation to improve water supply security albeit at an additional cost that is not minor but still significantly smaller than if the three sources were operated separately in a nonintegrated fashion. In the 3rd paper that is still under preparation, we will present a new forward-looking adaptive model that we developed to optimize integrated desalination-reservoir operation. We developed the model using linear programming with the objective of minimizing overall water deficit while minimizing excess spill from the reservoir subject to mass balance, demand and budget constraints. In the paper, we will also present results giving new insights into the benefits of desalination-reservoir integration and improved future forecasts.

617012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617012.value: The work completed in this project has paved the way for further work on climate change adaptation of water supply systems. We have developed new models to integrate reservoir-desalination operation. However, there is still room for further development to include greater system complexity. For future work, we intend to expand the models to incorporate an energy component to identify new ways of optimizing the energy use of desalination, and by that, reduce the major barrier currently blocking its wider implementation. We also intend to apply the models developed to other case studies of different climates to gain further insights into the potential of reservoir-desalination integration for more robust operation.

617012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617012.value: We investigated the potential of integrating desalination to existing reservoir systems to mitigate supply uncertainty. Desalinated seawater and wastewater are relatively reliable but expensive. Water from natural resources like reservoirs is generally cheaper but climate sensitive. We studied combining reservoir-desalination operation for an overall system that is less vulnerable to scarcity and uncertainty. Results were generated for two cases, one based on the climate and demands of a location in India and the other of a location in California. We found the joint operation to improve water supply security albeit at an additional cost that is not minor but still significantly smaller than if the three sources were operated separately in a nonintegrated fashion. Further, our analysis showed a two-way interaction between the reservoir and desalination plants where the optimal operation of the former is just as much affected by the latter as the latter by the former. This highlighted the importance of an integrated management approach. The study contributed to a greater quantitative understanding of desalination as a redundancy measure for adapting water supply infrastructures for a future of greater scarcity and uncertainty.

617212.label: Project Objectives
617212.value: Objective 1: Comprehensive understanding of MIMO-based RFID systems MIMO exploits spatial diversity to improve the capacity, range and reliability of wireless systems and can be adopted in RFID systems. However, the current Class-1 Generation-2 standard (C1G2) for RFID systems is based on the single-input single-output (SISO) and does not exploit such properties. In this task, we will build up a testbed using current implementations of MIMO based RFID systems for empirical study. More specifically, we will use Universal Software Radio Peripheral 2 (USRP2) to implement a MIMO-based reader and then further make use of this custom reader to communicate with the commercial tags. We will also build a monitor using USRP2 to collect the related data for further analysis and determine which factors limit the performance with MIMO through comprehensive theoretical analysis. Objective 2: Improving the channel utilization in RFID networks In the current C1G2 RFID systems, the channel utilization is very low. In this task, we will exploit the frequency properities and propose a novel approach by enabling the channel contention in the frequency domain instead of time domain, eliminating the empty and collided slots being wasted. We will also design an algorithm based on probability model for handling collisions and missing detection problems in the contention domain. We will further use URSP2s combined with the commercial tags to implement a prototype system based on software radio and evaluate its performance in realistic environment settings. Objective 3: Fine-grained Indoor localization WiFi-based indoor localization has been attractive due to its open access and low cost. But distance estimation based on received signal strength indicator (RSSI) is easily affected by temporal and spatial variance due to the multipath effect, which contributes to most of the estimation errors in current systems. In this task, we will analyze this effect across the physical layer and account for the undesirable RSSI readings being reported. We plan to explore the frequency diversity of the subcarriers in OFDM systems and propose a novel approach to alleviate multipath effect at the receiver. We plan to implement this approach on commercial 802.11 NICs, and then will evaluate its performance in different typical indoor scenarios. Objective 4: Leveraging channel state information for WLAN-based indoor location fingerprinting WLAN-based indoor location fingerprinting has been attractive owing to its open access and high accuracy. Most of them so far rely on the RSSI which is a coarse value that simply measures the received power for a whole channel. In this task, we aim to explore using CSI for location fingerprinting. More specifically, we will leverage the CSI values including different amplitudes and phases at multiple propagation paths, known as the frequency diversity, to uniquely identify a location. We will then design a probability algorithm with a correlation filter to map an object by its fingerprints. Finally we will implement our CSI-based methodology with commercial 802.11 NICs and evaluate its performance in typical indoor scenarios.

617212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617212.value: Channel characteristics are important for many wireless protocols and application designs, such as routing and localization. However, the traditional packet level metrics could be misleading in some cases due to coarse measurement. In this research project, we propose to exploit channel characteristics and leverage the fine-grained physical layer information to design some new techniques and thus enhance the wireless network performance. Nowadays, multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology is emerging as the default choice for wireless networks. It uses multiple antennas to send multiple parallel signals from the transmitter to the receiver. MIMO makes use of a channel characteristic, i.e., spatial diversity, to improve the communication capacity, range and reliability of a wireless network. Recent research shows that MIMO can also be adopted in the radio-frequency identification (RFID) system design to increase the read reliability and range, thus we plan to leverage the spatial characteristic to solve the channel utilization problem in RFID networks. Apart from spatial diversity, frequency diversity is another channel characteristic in wireless networks. WiFi-based indoor localization has been attractive due to its open access and low cost properties. However, the distance estimation based on received signal strength indicator (RSSI) is easily affected by temporal and spatial variance due to multipath effect, which contributes to most of the estimation errors in current systems. How to eliminate such effect so as to enhance indoor localization performance is a big challenge. In this work, we propose to analyze this effect across the physical layer and account for the undesirable RSSI readings being reported. We aim to explore the frequency diversity of the subcarriers in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems and leverage the channel state information (CSI) to alleviate multipath effect at the receiver. Along this direction there are many new issues and challenges to be addressed. To achieve these goals, we propose to complete four critical tasks in this research project. We will first investigate the channel characteristics of MIMO-based RFID systems. We will then explore the spatial diversity to improve the channel utilization in RFID systems. We also propose to leverage the frequency diversity to enhance the indoor localization. Finally, we plan to implement them in real testbed and compare their performance with theoretical analysis. 信道特性對於許多的無線協議以及應用設計，例如路由和定位等都非常重要。然而傳統的基於數據包層面的參數在某些情況下由於粗精度的測量導致不準確。在這個研究項目中，我們打算探索信道特性並利用細粒度的物理層信息來設計一些新的技術從而提升無線網絡的性能。目前，MIMO (多輸入多輸出)技術成為無線網絡的一個趨勢。這個技術利用多根天線從發送端發送多個並行的信號到接收端。MIMO技術利用空間多樣性的信道特性來增強無線網絡通信的容量，距離和可靠性。最近的研究表明，MIMO技術同樣被射頻識別系統設計所採用來提高閱讀的可靠性和范圍。因此我們計劃利用空間的多樣性來解決射頻識別網絡的信道利用問題。除了空間多樣性，頻率多樣性是無線網絡的另一個信道特性。基於無線保真的室內定位技術由於其開放及低損耗的特性成為一個很好的選擇。然而基於接收信號強度指示的距離估計方法很容易受到多徑效應的影響導致其在時間及空間變化。這是導致現有系統中大多數估計錯誤的原因。如何降低這種影響從而提升室內定位的性能是一個大的挑戰。在這個項目中，我們計劃通過對物理層和不準確的接收信號強度指示信息進行分析。我們打算利用正交頻分復用技術中各個子載波的頻率多樣性和信道狀態信息來消除多徑效應在接收端的影響。在這個方面將會有許多新的問題和挑戰需要解決。為了達到上述目的，我們計劃通過四個任務來完成這個研究項目。我們首先探索及分析基於多輸入多輸出的射頻識別系統的信道特性。接下來我們將利用空間多樣性來提升射頻識別系統的信道利用率。我們也將利用頻率多樣性來提升室內定位的性能。最終我們將搭建一個實驗平台來分析它們的性能並跟理論分析做對比。

617212.label: Realisation of objectives
617212.value: For this project, we first designed a new MAC CSMA/SF (Shortest First) protocol to reduce the power consumption of sink-node communication by minimizing energy costs in carrier sense during nodes’ channel contention. CSMA/SF modifies the existing CSMA/CA MAC protocol. Instead of completely contention-based, CSMA/SF ensures nodes with a remaining shorter message will have a higher priority in contention by implementing a distributed scheduling algorithm and incorporating Length Detection scheme. Further, CSMA/SF employs an Anti-Starvation mechanism to solve the starvation problem of the shortest-first protocol. CSMA/SF also optimizes channel utilization by reducing the probability of collisions. The experimental results show that CSMA/SF can reduce overall energy consumption by around 20% and improve channel utilization up to 40%. This work was published in IEEE TWC 2014. For the second task, we attempted to improve channel utilization in wireless networks. In traditional point-to-point wireless communication, significant efforts had been made by existing studies to enhance the utilization of the channel access time. However, in the emerging wireless network using MU-MIMO, considering only the time domain in channel utilization is not sufficient. As multiple transmitters are allowed to transmit packets simultaneously to the same AP, allowing more antennas at the AP would lead to higher channel utilization. Thus the channel utilization in MU-MIMO should consider both time and spatial domains, i.e., the channel access time and the antenna usage, which have not been considered in the existing methods. In this task, we point out that the fundamental problem is that the antenna lacks information of contention nodes in channel contention. To address this issue, we propose a new MAC-PHY architecture design, CUTS, to allow distributed nodes to effectively contend for the channel and utilize the channel in both domains. Particularly, CUTS adopts interference nulling to attach the antenna information in channel contention. Meanwhile, techniques such as channel contention in frequency domain and ACK in frequency domain using self-jamming are adopted. Through the software defined radio-based real experiments and extensive simulations, we demonstrate the feasibility of our design and illustrate that CUTS provides higher channel utilization, with the gain over IEEE 802.11 reaching 470 percent. This work was published in IEEE TPDS 2014. For the third task, we proposed a novel and truly unobtrusive detection method based on advanced wireless technologies, which we call as WiFall. WiFall employs the time variability and special diversity of Channel State Information (CSI) as an indicator of human activities. As CSI is readily available in prevalent in-use wireless infrastructures, WiFall avoids the need for hardware modification, environmental setup, and worn or taken devices. We implemented WiFall on laptops equipped with commercial 802.11n NICs. Two typical indoor scenarios and several layout schemes were examined. As demonstrated by the experimental results,WiFall yielded 87% detection precision with a false alarm rate of 18% on average. This work was published in IEEE INFOCOM 2014. Finally, we designed Pilot, a Channel State Information (CSI)-based DfP indoor localization system in WLAN. Pilot design is motivated by the observations that PHY layer CSI is capable of capturing environment variance due to the frequency diversity of the wideband channel, such that the position where the entity is located can be uniquely identified by monitoring the CSI feature pattern shift. Therefore, a“passive” radio map is constructed as a prerequisite, which includes fingerprints for entities located in crucial reference positions, as well as a clear environment. This work was published in IEEE ICDCS 2013.

rows: Objective 1: Comprehensive understanding of MIMO-based RFID systems MIMO exploits spatial diversity to improve the capacity, range and reliability of wireless systems and can be adopted in RFID systems. However, the current Class-1 Generation-2 standard (C1G2) for RFID systems is based on the single-input single-output (SISO) and does not exploit such properties. In this task, we will build up a testbed using current implementations of MIMO based RFID systems for empirical study. More specifically, we will use Universal Software Radio Peripheral 2 (USRP2) to implement a MIMO-based reader and then further make use of this custom reader to communicate with the commercial tags. We will also build a monitor using USRP2 to collect the related data for further analysis and determine which factors limit the performance with MIMO through comprehensive theoretical analysis.

Objective 2: Improving the channel utilization in RFID networks In the current C1G2 RFID systems, the channel utilization is very low. In this task, we will exploit the frequency properities and propose a novel approach by enabling the channel contention in the frequency domain instead of time domain, eliminating the empty and collided slots being wasted. We will also design an algorithm based on probability model for handling collisions and missing detection problems in the contention domain. We will further use URSP2s combined with the commercial tags to implement a prototype system based on software radio and evaluate its performance in realistic environment settings.

Objective 3: Fine-grained Indoor localization WiFi-based indoor localization has been attractive due to its open access and low cost. But distance estimation based on received signal strength indicator (RSSI) is easily affected by temporal and spatial variance due to the multipath effect, which contributes to most of the estimation errors in current systems. In this task, we will analyze this effect across the physical layer and account for the undesirable RSSI readings being reported. We plan to explore the frequency diversity of the subcarriers in OFDM systems and propose a novel approach to alleviate multipath effect at the receiver. We plan to implement this approach on commercial 802.11 NICs, and then will evaluate its performance in different typical indoor scenarios.

Objective 4: Leveraging channel state information for WLAN-based indoor location fingerprinting WLAN-based indoor location fingerprinting has been attractive owing to its open access and high accuracy. Most of them so far rely on the RSSI which is a coarse value that simply measures the received power for a whole channel. In this task, we aim to explore using CSI for location fingerprinting. More specifically, we will leverage the CSI values including different amplitudes and phases at multiple propagation paths, known as the frequency diversity, to uniquely identify a location. We will then design a probability algorithm with a correlation filter to map an object by its fingerprints. Finally we will implement our CSI-based methodology with commercial 802.11 NICs and evaluate its performance in typical indoor scenarios.

617212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617212.value: In wireless networks, multiple devices communicate with each other using a wireless channel. How to use the wireless channel efficiently has been a major challenge. In the emerging wireless network using MU-MIMO, which is a set of multiple-input and multiple-output technologies for wireless communication, in which a set of users or wireless devices, each with one or more antennas, communicate with each other. In MU-MIMO, considering only the time domain in channel utilization is insufficient. As multiple transmitters are allowed to transmit packets simultaneously to the same AP, allowing more antennas at AP would lead to a higher channel utilization. Thus, the channel utilization in MU-MIMO should consider both time and spatial domains. In this project, we propose a new low-level design, CUTS, to allow multiple devices to effectively contend for the channel and utilize the channel in both domains. Particularly, when multiple devices are competing for the wireless channel, CUTS can attach the antenna information when there is interference among competing devices result in turning wasted interference information into a higher channel utilization. Through real experiments and extensive simulations, we demonstrate the feasibility of our design, which can achieve 470 percent better than the traditional method.

617312.label: Project Objectives
617312.value: Sparse latent structure of multivariate time series: We consider parameter estimation in high-dimensional multivariate time series with sparsity, where the interest is in practical algorithms that work in real systems with low complexity. Low-rank latent structure of multivariate time series: Low-rank structure is a form of matrix sparsity that arises in many applications that can be formulated as matrices with low rank. Such problems are nonconvex and very hard to solve in practice. We are interested in practical algorithms that work in real systems with low complexity. Development of a software package for sparsity: This task is related to the two previous tasks and takes them to a further level by attempting to develop a robust software package for Matlab. The possibility of implementation in hardware will be considered.

617312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617312.value: A deluge of data of increasingly higher dimensionality is shaping the new era of information processing. Modern science and engineering applications are characterized by extremely rapid technological advances in a variety of fields, such as sensor technology, storage capacity, and computing power. This, in turn, renders possible the collection of tremendous, unprecedented amounts of high-dimensional data. The list of applications dealing with large data sets of high dimensions in statistical signal processing and related areas is endless; some examples include high-resolution hyperspectral imaging in astronomy and medicine, positioning and tracking in navigation systems, large-scale speech analysis, analysis of neurobiological signals and DNA sequencing, as well as data processing for social media and networking, such as Google's Page Rank. In the dynamically changing environments that are mostly targeted by the previous applications, the nature of large datasets is inherently time-varying. Consequently, information extraction techniques are required to efficiently exploit statistical dependence structure and correlation patterns in both the cross-sectional as well as the intertemporal domains. Conventional and well-established statistical methodologies, ranging from ARMA modeling and Kalman filtering to supervised and unsupervised learning, perform satisfactorily and are widely applied in scenarios with moderate dimensions. However, unfortunately, the nowadays ever increasing model dimension relative to the sample size makes estimation, inference, and prediction based on classical procedures from statistical decision theory and time series analysis computationally unfeasible and statistically unreliable. The blessing of massive amounts of high-dimensional data turns into the so-called curse of dimensionality, as the number of parameters to be estimated becomes of the same order of magnitude as the number of samples available for estimation. This proposal aims at devising effective ways to deal with the high-dimensionality problem in three individual but mutually reinforcing, supportive, and complementary directions: i) the extraction of latent explanatory variables under the assumption of linearity; ii) the reduction of dimension by exploiting nonlinearity via information-theoretic and nonparametric estimation methodologies; and iii) the identification of hidden structures in general state-space representations and dynamic decision making problems. This proposal aims at devising effective ways to deal with the high-dimensionality problem in three individual but mutually reinforcing, supportive, and complementary directions: i) the extraction of latent explanatory variables under the assumption of linearity; ii) the reduction of dimension by exploiting nonlinearity via information- theoretic and nonparametric estimation methodologies; and iii) the identification of hidden structures in general state-space representations and dynamic decision making problems. 标题：高维海量数据集中的信号探索 摘要： 高维数据的海量涌现开启了信息处理的新时代。在现代科学和工程应用中， 各领域的技术进步非常快速，如传感技术，存储容量和计算能力等。这反过来为收集前所未有的大量高维数据提供了可能。在统计信号处理相关领域，与海量高维数据相关的应用不胜枚举。如天文学和医学领域的高分辨率高光谱成像，导航系统中的定位和追踪，大规模的语音分析，神经生物学信号和DNA序列的分析，以及社交媒体和网络相关的数据处理如谷歌的网页排名等等。 在动态变化的环境中，大型数据集的性质本质上是时变的。而前面提及的应用主要面向的也都是动态变化的环境。因此，我们需要运用信息提取技术来有效地利用在空间域和时间域上统计相关的结构和模式。传统的比较完善的统计方法，比如ARMA模型、卡尔曼滤波器以及有监督和非监督学习，被广泛的运用在数据维度不太高的情况下，并有着令人满意的效果。 然而，随着现在模型维度相对于样本数量的不断增长，基于经典的统计决策理论或是时间序列分析来进行估计、推断以及预测，以现有的计算能力已不可行，在统计上也不可靠。当待估参数的个数和可用于估计的样本个数达到同一数量级之后，大量的高维数据原有的益处却演变成了所谓的维数灾难。 本项目旨在开发有效的方法，从三个相互加强、相互支持、相互补充的方向来处理高维问题。（1）在线性假设下，提取潜在的解释变量；（2）用基于信息理论和非参数估计的方法，通过利用数据内在的非线性来降低维度；（3）辨识一般的状态空间描述和动态决策问题中的隐藏结构。

617312.label: Realisation of objectives
617312.value: The main goal of this project was the development of signal processing and optimization techniques to cope with the ever increasing dimensionality of data, effectively reducing its dimensionality by removing irrelevant components. All the objectives have been satisfactorily completed and the output consists of seven IEEE top journal papers and six conference papers. Objective 1 was focused on sparsity of parameters. Several of the papers deal directly with this issue by developing optimization methods that estimate the desired parameters but making sure that only the really necessary parameters are active, otherwise they become zero and inactive. The objective has been fully accomplished and many lines for future work have become evident. Objective 2 was on the low-rank matrix approximation also to deal with the exploding dimensionality. Rank-one approximations that also have sparse eigenvectors have been proposed obtaining an excellent low-complexity high-performance algorithm. In addition, the topic of outliers in the estimation of large dimensional covariance matrices has been deeply studied, developing low-complexity methods that have the best performance compared to the state-of-the-art methods. One extension of the rank-one approximation was elusive for a couple of years and we now believe it could be solved in future work. Objective 3 deals with the development of software corresponding to the methods proposed in the papers. We have prepared two packages that are ready to be shared: one for sparsity in leading eigenvectors (already shared online) and the other on estimation of covariance matrices with outliers (soon to be shared online).

617312.label: Major findings and research outcome
617312.value: The major findings of this project were the development of sparse and low-rank inducing estimation techniques to cope with the high dimensionality of modern data by effectively reducing its dimensionality and removing the irrelevant components. One major finding is the proposed low-complexity method to compute the sparse leading eigenvector for large matrices. Not only this is the best available method at the present but has also led to a future extension currently in progress. Another major finding corresponds with the methodology developed to estimate high-dimensional matrices contaminated with faulty data or outliers. Our methods outperform the existing methods and are particularly relevant for financial applications and big data. It is also worth mentioning the proposed numerical method for equalized portfolio design (called risk parity portfolio) that are popular among practitioners but lacked adequate numerical methods.

617312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617312.value: The results obtained in this project are numerous but there are even more lines for future research that have been unveiled. Some topics that are currently under investigation include: sparse parameter estimation in some financial models for market data (in particular for VECM modeling), sparsity in portfolio design for index tracking, and low-rank matrix approximation with joint sparse eigenvectors (the completed project solved the problem for only one eigenvector but recently developed optimization techniques may allow to solve the general case).

617312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617312.value: Modern science and engineering applications are characterized by extremely rapid technological advances that lead to a deluge of data of increasingly higher dimensionality. It is the era of information processing. This project has mainly focused on the higher dimensionality issue; in particular, in the process of dimensionality reduction. Indeed, the problem with such high dimensional data that modern technology provides is to extract useful features or identify a reduced subspace to effectively reduce the dimensionality. Mathematically, there are two ways of achieving dimensionality reduction: via sparsity and low-rank matrix approximation. This research project has obtained several results on the topic of sparsity or feature selection, as well as subspace identification via low-rank matrix decomposition. These results find applications in diverse areas such as big data problems, financial engineering, sequence design for radar and communication systems, etc. Some examples include how to deal with faulty data (outliers) in big data systems, how to equalize the risk in portfolio investment, how to design long sequences with desired properties, etc. Overall, the publication output has been superb with 7 top IEEE journal papers and 6 top IEEE conference papers.

617412.label: Project Title(Chinese)
617412.value: 在地理社交网络中的高效查询处理

617412.label: Project Objectives
617412.value: Development of indexing schemes for GSNs that support retrieval based on both spatial and social criteria. Design of various query types for discovery of influential users and interesting groups in GSNs. Implementation of novel query processing algorithms for GSNs.
rows: Development of indexing schemes for GSNs that support retrieval based on both spatial and social criteria.
Design of various query types for discovery of influential users and interesting groups in GSNs.
Implementation of novel query processing algorithms for GSNs.

617412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617412.value: A tremendous amount of online social interactions take place around the world via Social Networks (SNs). A new type of SNs, called Geo-Social Network (GSN), is becoming increasingly popular. In GSNs, such as Facebook Places, Foursquare etc, users can share their locations. In addition to social networking, GSNs offer new opportunities for location-based advertising as enterprises can take advantage of position information for promotion purposes. However, this necessitates specialized query processing mechanisms for retrieving interesting users. For instance, a potential advertising target for a merchant may be a user nearby, who has many friends also in the vicinity of the merchant. In this proposal, we introduce a comprehensive set of queries that retrieve users, or groups of users, based on both social connections and geographical information. Specifically, we first present a general framework for indexing GSNs that supports retrieval based on both connectivity and spatial criteria. Then, we propose and motivate several query types, namely ranges, nearest neighbors, joins, and top-k queries, which can be used for the discovery of influential users and interesting groups in GSNs. Finally, we design a set of algorithms for query processing. The proposal involves several novel and challenging problems that have a strong practical interest. 通过社交网络(SNs)， 世界各地都发生着大量的在线社交互动。 一种被称为“地理社交网络(GSN)”的新型的社交网络正在渐渐地变得流行。在例如Facebook Places或Foursquare等地理社交网络中，用户们能够分享他们的地理位置。除了作为社交网络外，由于企业能够在促销中利用位置信息，地理社交网络为基于地理位置的广告服务提供了新的机遇。但是，这就需要专门的查询处理机制用于检索有趣的用户。例如，对于一个商人，一个潜在的广告目标可能是一位在附近的用户，而且该用户有许多朋友也在此商人附近。 在此提案中，我们介绍一系列的查询，它们在社交联系与地理信息的基础上检索用户或用户组。特别是，我们首先提出了一个通用的框架以用来索引地理社交网络，其支持基于社交连通性与空间标准的检索。然后，我们提出了几种查询类型，即范围，最近邻居，连接和top-k查询，这些查询能够用于发现在地理社交网络中具有影响力的用户和有趣的用户群体。最后，我们设计一套查询处理算法。此提案包含了若干新奇且具有挑战性的问题，而这些问题又具有很强的实用意义。

617412.label: Realisation of objectives
617412.value: Regarding objective 1, publication C1 introduces a general architecture for GSN (geo-social network) query processing. The proposed architecture consists of a social module (SM), a geographical module (GM), and a query processing module (QM). The SM stores exclusively social data (e.g., friendship relations), whereas the GM keeps only geographical information (e.g., check-ins). The QM is responsible for receiving GSN queries from users, executing them, and returning the results. The SM, GM and QM can either be three separate servers, three separate clouds, or a single system (server or cloud). However, the tasks of the three modules are segregated. Specifically, the QM processes a GSN query through an algorithm that builds upon well-defined social and geographical primitive operations. These primitives define a rigorous interface between QM-SM and QM-GM, respectively. The sole duties of the SM and GM (with respect to a given GSN query) are to execute their corresponding primitives on their stored data. The QM eventually derives the final results by combining the outputs of the primitives, optionally exploiting auxiliary indices maintained locally. The segregation of SM and GM allows their administration by different entities, e.g., the SM (GM) can be maintained by a company with expertise in social networking (resp. location-based services). In addition, separating the functionality of SM and GM renders the management of social and geographical data more flexible, because the frequent check-in updates do not burden the relatively static social structures. Finally, the segregation offers several other benefits. First, our framework can readily integrate modifications (e.g., a new, more efficient structure) in the implementation of SM without modifying GM, and vice versa. Second, novel GSN query types and algorithms can be devised, either by using a different combination of existing primitives or by implementing new ones, without the need of altering the SM and GM infrastructures. Last, social (geographical) data can be used independently for pure social (resp. geographical) queries, potentially through the same primitive operations utilized by GSN queries. As a result, a “traditional” social network can adopt our architecture without extra effort. Objective 2 requires ranking functions that assign scores to users based on their on their distance to a query location q, the number of their friends in the vicinity of q, and possibly their connectivity. As an example, assume that a merchant wishes to post an advertisement using a location-based service; promising targets are users with high scores since in addition to being nearby the merchant, they can also influence their friends in the vicinity to visit. We call such a function, Geo-Social Ranking (GSR) function. In order to capture different application requirements, in publication J1, we propose four GSR functions: i) Linear Combination, where the score of a user is the weighted sum of his normalized social and spatial scores ii) Ratio Combination, which is the ratio combination of the two scores, iii) h-Geo-Social ranking function, inspired by the bibliographic h-index, which assigns each user a score based on the number of friends in coincident circles centered at q, and iv) Geo-Social Triangles ranking function, which in addition to distance, takes into account the friends that a user and his friends may have in common, i.e., triangles that are close to the query point. We investigate the behavior of these functions in depth, qualitatively assess their results, and study the effects of their parameters. Moreover, in the context of Objective 3, we design specialized query processing techniques that utilize the individual function characteristics to efficiently retrieve the top-k users. Specifically, some functions can be processed by range queries, while others require incremental retrieval of the results based on the branch and bound framework. All methods are extensively evaluated with real geo-social datasets. Regarding objective 3, in C1 we present propose query processing techniques for several GSN queries. We first address two basic GSN queries; Range Friends (RF), which returns the friends of a user within a given range, and NearestFriends (NF), which returns the nearest friends of a user to a given location. We design various algorithms for every query type, with each algorithm utilizing a different combination of primitive operations. We show that (i) our framework provides flexibility in algorithmic design, and (ii) the algorithm efficiency heavily depends on the number and performance of the involved primitives, which in turn depends on the underlying data management scheme. In addition, we propose a novel GSN query type, called Nearest Star Group (NSG). Given a query location q and an integer m, an NSG query returns a user group of size m, which forms a star sub-graph of the social network, and minimizes the aggregate (Euclidean) distance of its members to q. In C2, we extend our work on query processing algorithms to Geo-Social Keyword (GSK) search, which enables the retrieval of users, points of interest, or keywords that satisfy geographic, social, and/or textual criteria. We first introduce a general GSK framework that covers a wide range of real-world tasks, including advertisement, context-based search, and market analysis. Then, we present three concrete GSK queries: (i) NPRU that returns the top-k users based on their spatial proximity to a given query location, their popularity, and their similarity to an input set of terms; (ii) NSTP that outputs the top-k POIs based on their proximity to a user v, the number of check-ins by friends of v, and their similarity to a set of terms; (iii) FSKR that discovers the top-k keywords based on their frequency in pairs of friends located within a spatial area. For each query, we develop a processing algorithm that utilizes a novel hybrid index.

617412.label: Major findings and research outcome
617412.value: Geo-social networks have created opportunities for novel location-based social interactions and advertising. In publication C1, we focus on GSN queries that extract useful information combining both the social relationships and the location of the users. Towards this end, we propose an architecture that segregates the social, geographical, and query processing modules. Each GSN query is processed via a transparent combination of primitive queries issued to the social and geographical modules, which do not interact with each other. This allows separate (and thus more flexible) social and geographical data management, and permits each module to be optionally operated by a different entity. We first address conventional GSN queries (e.g., find the nearest friends of a user) proposing various algorithms that utilize different combinations of primitive queries. Then, we extend our focus to more advanced queries returning groups of users according to geo-social criteria. In publication J2 we focus on geo-social ranking (GSR) functions for discovering influential users. In order to capture different application requirements, we introduce a general Geo-Social ranking framework and propose four functions that cover several practical scenarios. We investigate the behavior of the functions in depth, qualitatively assess their results, examine their correlation, and study the effects of their parameters. Moreover, we design query processing techniques that utilize the individual function characteristics to efficiently retrieve the top-k users. All processing algorithms utilize a well defined set of primitive operations that are supported by the majority of commercial GSN APIs. Consequently, the proposed techniques can be effortlessly adapted by popular GSN, or other novel applications that can access those APIs. Publication C2 introduces a class of top-k queries that enable retrieval of users, points-of-interest or keywords based on geographic, social and textual criteria. We propose three concrete queries that can be used in various tasks involving context-based search, profile-based advertisement and market analysis. For each query we provide a processing algorithm that exploits a specialized index. Our experiments with real datasets confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed methods

617412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617412.value: We are currently working on integrating diversity to GSN query processing. Assume, for instance, that a restaurant wishes to advertise a promotion to the top-k most influential users (or groups of users) according to geo-social criteria. It is possible that the set of top-k users share many similarities, and the merchant would wish for more diversity, even if the resulting top-k users were slightly inferior in terms of the geo-social criteria. Diversity can be spatial (e.g., the users should be far from each other), social (e.g., they should not have many common friendships), or categorical (e.g., they should have different profiles). Although this is in general a hard problem, we have devised approximate algorithms that provide fast, nearly optimal solutions, even for very large networks. Another interesting topic for further development concerns novel query types and associated processing techniques. Assume, for instance, that a group of friends wish to meet at a point of interest (e.g., a restaurant) that minimizes the time that they have to travel. In addition to travel time, the query could also take into account the previous check-in of the users, so that restaurants with multiple check-ins are favored, the number of “likes”of the restaurants etc.

617412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617412.value: Geo-social Networks that capture social relations of users and their locations are increasingly popular. The combination of spatial and social information has generated novel opportunities for marketing and location-based advertising, and additional requirements for query processing. In the context of this project, we conducted the first systematic study of geo-social query processing. Specifically, (i) we introduced a general framework that segregates the social, geographical and query processing modules, enabling flexible data management and algorithmic design. A query is processed via a combination of primitive operations issued to the social and geographical modules. (ii) We proposed a diverse set of ranking functions and associated processing algorithms for discovering influential users based on their spatial and social properties. (iii) We developed geo-social keyword search, a class of top-k queries that combine all spatial, social, and textual attributes, and may return users, points of interest or keywords.

617612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617612.value: Over the past few years, the nascent research field of optofluidics which studies the manipulation of light and fluids and their interactions on a chip or in a compact system has been attracting increasing research interest for diverse technological innovations and basic discovery. Examples are chemical and biological analysis for lab-on-a-chip applications and biosensing, photonic integration for manipulating light and non-solid matters including particles in fluids, and optofluidics for useful energy generation. Among various material platforms to realize optofluidic chips, silicon as a low-cost semiconductor with mature fabrication processes and a host of demonstrated integrated photonic components offers one useful platform to build optofluidic devices. Recent developments of various silicon photonic biosensors and optical manipulation devices are relevant examples. In this proposal, we seek to study optofluidic manipulation and sorting of dielectric nanometer-sized particles on a silicon chip. Dielectric nanoparticles in the size range of few tens to hundreds of nanometers represent biologically relevant particles such as viruses and biomolecules. Such particles are below the diffraction limit and are difficult to be imaged by using conventional optical microscopes. By optically trapping and fluidically manipulating such nanoparticles, we believe it is possible to trap and route such nanoparticles of known refractive indices in a size-dependent manner and thus enable label-free nanoparticles size-based sorting. Such an optofluidic-based analysis of nanoparticles in liquids can be potentially useful for lab-on-a-chip applications in life sciences and biological and chemical research. Here, as a natural extension of our previous work on optical manipulation of dielectric microparticles in fluids using integrated silicon photonic devices, we target at dielectric nanoparticle size-based optofluidic sorting using integrated waveguides and microresonators in a microfluidic channel on a silicon chip. The working principle is based on the balance between the transverse optical gradient force due to the photonic structure near field and the viscous drag force. We propose waveguide-based particle size-based high-pass and band-pass filters, and microresonator-based particle size-based buffers. We will aim at sorting nanoparticles in fluids with sizes of hundreds of nanometers with a resolution of about 100 nm. We will seek to develop tunable optofluidic devices by tuning the fluidic flow velocity and the optical source power or the laser wavelength. We will also seek to develop advanced optofluidic circuits with multiple trapping and sorting stages. 在過去的幾年中，光流體作為一个新興的研究領域，已經吸引了越來越多的在技術革新和基本機理方面的研究興趣。所谓光流体，即在晶片或一个微縮系統上，利用光，流体以及它們之間的相互作用来进行操控，應用實例包括用於“晶片實驗室”和傳感上的化學及生物分析方法，用於操縱光和包括含顆粒的流體在内的各种非固態物質的光子集成技術，以及广泛有益的能源發電等事宜。在諸多實現光流體晶片的材料平臺中，矽作為一種成本低廉，製造工藝成熟的半導體，且作為基礎性材料，已擁有多种實現了的集成光子器件。因此它為構建光流體器件提供了一個有益的平臺。最近得以发展的各種矽光子感測器和光學操縱器件就是此平臺相關的代表。 在此研究建議書中，我們致力研究基於矽晶片上的光流體操縱和介質納米尺寸顆粒的分類过程。介質納米顆粒的大小範圍可從幾十到幾百納米不等，这相近於生物學中主要的病毒和生物分子的尺寸大小。這些顆粒由於小於光學衍射極限，很難用常規的光學顯微鏡來觀測。採用光學捕捉和流動式操控這些顆粒，我們相信，對這種折射指數已知的顆粒，因各自不同尺寸的影響下，捕捉和傳送納米粒子，即可無需標記地进行按尺寸大小分離。這種以光流體為基礎的對流體中納米顆粒的分析，在生命科學，生物學和化學領域的“晶片實驗室”应用中有很大的潛在應用价值。 作為我們之前的利用集成矽光子器件進行流體中介質微尺度顆粒的操控工作的延展，我們著眼於在矽晶片上的微流通道中，利用集成的波導和微環諧振腔，進行介質納米顆粒的分類。其工作原理是基於光學結構近場的橫向光學梯度力粘性阻力之間的平衡。我們提出了基於波導的對不同尺寸的顆粒的高通和帶通过滤器和基於微環諧振腔的粒子緩衝器。我們將著眼於在流體中對尺寸為幾百納米的顆粒以解析度100納米的精度進行分離。我們還會利用調控流體速度，光源功率和鐳射波段來得到可調的光流體器件。利用多重的捕捉和分類過程，我們還将會致力於發展更先進的光流體網路。

617612.label: Realisation of objectives
617612.value: Realization of Objective 1: We have achieved the major part of Objective 1. We have studied two working schemes in order to achieve “optofluidic size-based sorting of dielectric nanoparticles.” We have experimentally investigated optical manipulation and size-based separation of dielectric nanoparticles with various sizes using silicon nitride (SiN) microring resonators integrated in a microfluidic channel. Specifically, we first demonstrated nanoparticle buffering and dropping in a static fluid using microring resonator-based add-drop devices. We proposed and experimentally verified a design rule to determine the particle transport processes. Furthermore, we have experimentally demonstrated size-dependent separation between 80nm- and 260nm-radius polystyrene (PS) particles using SiN microring resonators under a fluidic flow. However, we encountered difficulties in optical manipulation of small nanoparticles (radius < 200nm) using microresonators due to the limited optical forces. We have therefore under-achieved the original target of “size resolution of about 100 nm” with small nanoparticles using the optical trapping-based scheme. In order to tackle the size-based sorting with resolution of about 100 nm, we studied non-specific binding of nanoparticles with various sizes to the SiN waveguide and microresonator surfaces under a fluidic flow. The size-dependent hydrodynamic force and Brownian motion lead to size-based sorting behaviors. For a particle mixture solution with 80nm and 125nm-radius PS particles with equal concentrations (~1011 ml-1), we observed much stronger binding effects for 80nm-radius nanoparticles, while binding events of 125nm-radius nanoparticles are very rare. In order to detect and quantify the binding events without the assistance of fluorescence imaging, we have further studied detecting different immobilized nanoparticles by characterizing the induced perturbations to microresonator devices. Specifically, we demonstrated label-free detection of single nanoparticles (80, 100, 120nm-radius) using microring-based coupled-resonator optical waveguides (CROWs) by an original light-scattering pattern recognition approach. Our current results mainly focus on sorting and detection of nanoparticles with ~100nm radius. We believe that size-based sorting on relatively large-sized nanoparticles (radius ~ 120 - 500 nm) should be readily followed. Realization of Objective 2: We have partially achieved Objective 2. We have numerically simulated the optical forces exerted on single nanoparticles from an integrated waveguide or a directional coupler using Maxwell Stress Tensor method (COMSOL). We have carried out three-dimensional (3-D) simulations with a sphere model and also two-and-a-half-dimensional (2.5-D) simulations with an effective disk model for calculating optical forces. We have also simulated the fluidic drag force distributions upon laminar flows in the designed microfluidic channels. However, we fell short in modeling in details the resulting dielectric nanoparticle manipulation and size-based sorting using integrated waveguides and microresonators in a microfluidic channel. This is partially because of the difficulties in establishing the validity of the numerical computations of the optical forces without direct measurements of the forces, which are in the pN level. Instead of focusing on direct measurements of forces exerted on nanoparticles, we have given the priority to studying the detection of single nanoparticles binding and the sorting of particles in the 100nm size regime in the presence of a fluidic flow using microring-based CROWs. Realization of Objective 3: We have partially achieved Objective 3. Specifically, we have theoretically and experimentally studied microresonator-based CROWs in a two-dimensional (2-D) array as an advanced optofluidic circuit for single nanoparticle detections. Specifically, we have designed, modeled, fabricated and characterized microring and microdisk-based CROWs on a SiN-on-silica platform integrated with microfluidic channels. We have experimentally and theoretically studied the responses of CROW eigenstate patterns towards binding of PS nanoparticles with various radii ranging from ~ 20 to 120 nm. However, we fell short in demonstrating CROWs as nanoparticle sorting circuits with a 100nm size resolution. We believe that there is no fundamental limitations to utilize the spatially distributed optical fields with a high spatial frequency and high cavity enhancements exhibited in these CROWs for size-based nanoparticle sorting as originally proposed.

617612.label: Major findings and research outcome
617612.value: 1. We have proposed 2-D CROWs for single nanoparticle detection using a mode-field intensity pattern recognition method. We have numerically simulated 2-D microring- and microdisk-based CROWs for single nanoparticle detection. The mode-field intensity distribution at the CROW eigenstate changes significantly upon a nanoparticle-induced perturbation. Our simulation results suggested detection of single nanoparticles with a radius of ~ 20 nm to 100 nm using a correlation analysis for the pattern change (see Publication 2 (manuscript under preparation) and Conference abstracts 7 and 8, Part C). 2. We have designed, modeled, fabricated and characterized microring- and microdisk-based 2-D CROWs on the SiN-on-silica platform integrated with polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)-based microfluidic channels. Our experiments using 2×2 microring-based CROWs revealed label-free detection and counting of single 100nm-radius PS nanoparticles under a fluidic flow. The averaged correlation coefficient change is more than an order higher than the background noise. Our statistics suggest stronger perturbation effects for particle binding in the inter-cavity coupling regions than along the microring arcs. (see Publication 2 (manuscript under preparation) and Conference abstracts 7 and 8, Part C). 3. We have experimentally investigated size-dependent nanoparticle binding to the SiN microring-based CROW surfaces upon a fluidic flow. For a solution with a mixture of 80nm- and 125nm-radius PS particles, we observed through fluorescence imaging ~ 21 binding events of 80nm-radius particles in the CROW device region (~10^4 micron^2) in 10 minutes, with 8 events confirmed by the correlation analysis. We observed no binding events of 125nm-radius PS particles, thus suggesting size-based particle binding. 4. We have designed, simulated, fabricated and characterized SiN microrings for optical manipulation of dielectric nanoparticles in a microfluidic channel with static fluids. The experiments revealed optical trapping and routing of 420nm-radius PS particles using microring-based add-drop devices. We proposed a design rule to determine the particle transport processes on microrings at cavity resonances. We have theoretically and experimentally examined this design rule on microring resonators with different designs. (see Publication 1 and Conference abstracts 1, 2 & 4, Part C). 5. We have experimentally investigated optical trapping and sorting of dielectric nanoparticles using SiN microring resonators integrated with a PDMS-based microfluidic channel under a fluidic flow. Our experimental results revealed separation between different sized nanoparticles (260nm- and 80nm-radius) using a SiN microring resonator. Based on the fluorescence imaging, we observed 12 particles trapped in the microring region, with 11 out of 12 were 260nm-radius particles. (see Conference abstract 6, Part C).

617612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617612.value: In order to optimize the sensitivity of the CROW eigenstate patterns and realize ultra-sensitive single nanoparticle detection, we plan to further explore the key physical parameters of two-dimensional CROWs and the effects on the sensing performance. The proposed course of action includes: (i) optimizing the coupling designs of 2-D CROWs, including both the inter-cavity coupling and the waveguide-cavity coupling, (ii) studying microring and microdisk-based CROWs with a large number of elements and studying the eigenstates with the most sensitive pattern response towards nanoparticle-induced perturbations. We also plan to further study the perturbation effects upon more accurate controls of nanoparticle binding sites. We will engineer the nanoparticle binding sites to preferentially spatially overlap with the largest mode-field regions of the CROW eigenstates (e.g., some of the inter-cavity coupling regions). This is desirable to enhance localized light-particle interactions and thus to enable a large signal-to-noise ratio from recognizing a change in the eigenstate pattern. The proposed course of action includes: (i) designing and fabricating advanced microfluidic channels with a hydrodynamic force-assisted focusing to precisely control nanoparticle sample delivery and binding with alignment in the CROW device regions with high optical mode-fields, (ii) developing a localized surface functionalization recipe on CROW surfaces for selectively and specifically immobilizing target nanoparticles or nano-sized bio-objects (e.g., proteins, DNAs) in the regions with high optical mode-fields, (iii) introducing localized optical force fields based on tightly focused free-space optical tweezers in order to facilitate particle binding at regions with high optical mode-fields.

617612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617612.value: Nowadays, the ability to detect, identify and analyze nano-sized objects in a complex medium is vital for exploring their potential impacts on human health and the environment. However, optical detection of single nanoparticles in a label-free manner is highly challenging due to the extremely small size and a low refractive index contrast of the particles with the surrounding medium. The demonstrated techniques are typically limited by bulky instrumentations, sophisticated protocols and long process times, which make them far from practical applications. In this research project, we proposed and successfully demonstrated coupled-resonator optical waveguides (CROWs) integrated on an optofluidic chip for label-free single nanoparticle detections. The technique leverages on our previous experiences of developing CROW-based biosensors for refractive index sensing and protein detection. The particle sensing scheme in principle only requires a charge-coupled device (CCD) camera for top-view imaging and a laser in the visible wavelengths as a light source. By comparing the pixelized scattering patterns and tracking the correlation coefficients over time, we can identify and count nanoparticle binding events. We have demonstrated detection of successive 100nm-radius polystyrene nanoparticle binding events under a fluidic flow. We envision this technique to pave the way to future point-of-care applications with nanoparticle-related diagnostics.

617812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617812.value: Interfacial dynamics and control of immiscible fluids in mini/micro spaces are relevant to optofluidic, thermal, energy, biological and chemical applications, such as tunable liquid microlenses, light valves and adaptive irises. At the micrometric scale, the relative importance of surface tension and viscous forces dominates inertia and buoyancy forces. For an adaptive tunable liquid microlens, which is a promising technique with potential to applications in photonics, optical communications, optical sensors and miniature cameras, the lens curvature needs to be adjusted dynamically. Therefore, for a fast focusing liquid microlens, transient interfacial and curvature dynamics is also dependent on the fluid inertia and viscous force. It is important to note that previous studies were focused on a singlet liquid lens, such as a convex liquid lens formed by two liquids with a hydrophobic wall. However, a singlet lens that is either convex or concave will cause optical aberrations, such as spherical aberration, coma and chromatic aberrations. To reduce the optical aberrations, a doublet liquid lens, such as an achromats liquid lens or an aplanats liquid lens is needed. These kinds of liquid lenses have several liquid-liquid interfaces, and may have significantly improved zooming and focusing accuracies. However, because different liquids may have different contact angles with the walls of mini/micro spaces under transient condition, the dynamics of fluid-fluid interfaces and fluid-wall interfaces are complex. In this proposed research, the interfacial dynamics of immiscible fluids under high speed actuation in mini/micro spaces will be investigated. Different surface wettabilities will be used to form and control the curvatures of doublet liquid microlenses to optimize imaging quality and dynamic performance. A cylindrical liquid lens will be constructed utilizing flow control and electrowetting techniques. The interfacial dynamics of liquid microlenses in microchannels will be studied. The phenomena of transient surface curvature response, wall surface dynamic wetting, and film formation will be investigated. The velocity flow field inside and outside a liquid microlens will be measured by micron-resolution particle image velocimetry. Optical methods will be used to exploit the deflection/refraction of a laser fringe pattern due to the interfacial dynamics of liquid microlens and the response time will be determined. Based on experimental results, a multiphase model for describing the interfacial dynamics, dynamic wetting and response of micro liquid lenses will be developed. Numerical modeling will be performed and the results will be compared with experimental data to help gain insights into how design processes can be optimized. 在微尺度下不互溶流體多界面動力學與控制的研究與微流控光學，熱力學，能源，生物及化學方面的應用密切相關。比如可控液體微透鏡，光閥門和自適應人工虹膜等。在微尺度，與慣性力及浮力相比，表面張力和粘度起主要作用。自適應液體微透鏡對於光電子技術，光通訊，光傳感器和微型相機都具有極大的應用前景。這種自適應液體微透鏡的表面曲率需要有很好的動態響應。因此，對於快速聚焦液體微透鏡來說，舜態界面與曲率的動力學效應也取決於液體的慣性力及粘性力。值得指出的是，以往的研究主要考慮了單鏡頭液體微透鏡，例如用兩種液體和疏水的表面來構成一個凸液體微透鏡。但這樣制成的單凸/單凹液體微透鏡將產生較大的球差，慧差及色差等像差。為了減少光學像差，需採用多液體構成的消像差透鏡。這種具有多個液-液界面的液體透鏡，有可能顯著地提高變焦與聚焦功能。然而，由於不同的液體具有不同的壁面微觀接觸角，在瞬態調焦時，液-液/液固界面的流體界面動力學將非常復雜。 本研究將對微尺度下高速調制的不互溶流體多界面動力學進行研究。將採用不同的親疏水表面來形成可控曲率的雙聚合液體微透鏡以提高成像質量和動態特性。並使用流動控制和電濕潤方法來形成柱面鏡。並對表面曲率的瞬態響應，壁面動態濕潤和液膜動態形成過程進行研究。採用微分辯粒子圖像速度儀對液體透鏡內外的流場進行分析，並使用光學干涉條紋散射技術對高速調制的不互溶流體多界面動力學效應進行研究，以期找出最優化的微型液體透鏡設計方法。

617812.label: Realisation of objectives
617812.value: To study the multiple dynamically actuated interfaces between immiscible fluids in microspaces, it is important to understand the interaction of immiscible fluids, internal fluid flows and heat and mass transfer. Specifically, the contact line dynamics under different thermal boundary conditions and surface wettabilities are crucial. Therefore, it is important to predict contact line dynamics and droplet dynamics under different surface wetting conditions in order to understand their effects on the response of fluid-fluid interfaces. Numerical study has been conducted to study droplet dynamics on wettability-patterned surfaces. A three-dimensional lattice Boltzmann (LB) model has been built to study the spreading behavior of a micron-scale ﬂuid droplet on a pattern of three hydrophobic/hydrophilic strips. On a solid surface, a hydrophobic strip is positioned in the center of the lattice with a hydrophilic strip positioned on each side of this strip. Under certain conditions, the droplet spans all three strips; otherwise the droplet stretches along or breaks up on the hydrophilic strips. The effects of pattern characteristics and droplet properties on the spreading behavior, the transient curvature and the final shape of the droplet have been investigated. A droplet cannot span three strips when the initial displacement of the droplet is greater than a critical value. This critical value has a functional relationship with the relative width of the strips and the radius of the droplet. A dimensionless linear relationship among the critical value, the relative width of the strips and the radius of the droplet have been proposed. The critical value is also affected by the wettability ratio of the hydrophobic/hydrophilic patterns. The curvature of the liquid can be predicted numerically which can be used to calculate the focus length when applying it in liquid lens design. The synergetic effect of surface charge (wettability), the special frequency of hydrophobic/hydrophilic patterns were simulated numerically. To modify the contact angles and curvature of a droplet, the surface tension of the liquid droplet can be easily modified by adding ethanol into water to form a multicomponent composition. However, under non-uniform temperature conditions, the droplet behaviors caused by the internal flow inside the multicomponent droplet, such as ethanol/water mixture, is quite complex even with a homogeneous surface wettability. To understand the behaviors, we experimentally studied the wettability effects on droplet internal flows and contact angle transition with and without evaporation under different contact angles and thermal boundary conditions. Homogeneous wettability surfaces were fabricated on Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) glass utilizing recently developed micro/nanofabrication techniques. The substrate was made of transparent silicon dioxide coated with an ITO layer of 100nm thickness, which acted as a transparent resistive heater. The ITO surface was chemically modified with a fluoroalkylsilane (FAS) monolayer to make it hydrophobic and the surface temperatures and contact angles can be controlled by the electrodes which were deposited on the two edges of ITO surface by PVD method. The internal flow velocity fields were measured using micro resolution particle image velocimetry (micro-PIV). This will allow us to monitor the contact line dynamics of a droplet under different hydrophobic/hydrophilic fraction ratios. To study the effects of wettability-patterned surfaces, different wettability pattern geometries and hydrophobic/hydrophilic area fractions were fabricated. Wettability-patterned surfaces with various hydrophobic dots and hydrophilic networks, microheater and temperature sensor arrays have been again fabricated on Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) glass. Advanced fabrication and measurement techniques are crucial for the experimental research of this project. The contact line dynamics, pressure-driven forces and heat mass transfer on the patterned surface were measured and analyzed. The heterogeneity of the surface and the patterned wettability, thermal gradient of liquid surfaces were investigated and utilized for liquid contact angle control processes. As before, the prism substrate was transparent glass coated with a 100 nm thick ITO layer as a resistive heater. After deposition of thick gold electrodes, a silicon dioxide passivation layer was deposited on the substrate by STS MESC Multiplex PECVD machine in Nanosystem Fabrication Facilities (NFF) of The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. On the silicon layer, a layer of Teflon was deposited by spinning coating and stabilized following suggested procedures from DuPont™. To fabricate wettability-patterned surfaces, we developed a novel technique that can avoid the problem of sputtering during the implantation of ions into the surfaces which can change the chemical properties of Teflon. In this technique, a new deposition method utilizing atomic layer deposition (ALD) with low temperature and gentle reaction was used. In general, ALD grows a thin film on the surface by exposing the surface to alternate gaseous species which are typically referred to as precursors. The precursors will not be present simultaneously in the reaction chamber but they will be inserted in a sequential manner with non-overlapping pulses (normally within micro seconds). During pulses, the precursors will react with the surface with self-limitation so that the reaction can terminate once all the reactive sites on the surface are consumed. When all the precursors are exposed to the surface, an ALD cycle is finished and the amount of deposition material is also determined. Besides, the temperature of reaction can also be adjusted according to user’s requirements. Oxford OpAL ALD in Nanosystem Fabrication Facilities (NFF) was used as for ALD alumina deposition. By fine tuning the reaction temperature and the thickness of alumina deposition during number of ALD cycles, we are the first group to successfully use this technique for a Teflon patterning on an ITO glass. The height of Teflon layer on the substrate is as low as 60 nm and roughness of the heterogeneous wetting surface is very small-- around 5 nm for Teflon and 25 nm for the substrate. This high degree of smoothness is ideal for investigating the effects of wettability patterns on droplet dynamics, contact line behaviors and heat and mass transfer without serious conflating topological effects, which may disturb the optical transparency of a droplet. Experiments were conducted to study the droplet dynamics and contact line behavior under different boundary conditions. An improved local force model was employed to analyze the critical receding contact angles on homogenous and heterogeneous surfaces.

617812.label: Major findings and research outcome
617812.value: In this research, it is found that under thermal boundary conditions, the internal flow of a two-component droplet can be divided into three stages sequentially, while a pure water droplet only has one stage (Minghao He and Huihe Qiu 2015). This process can significantly affect droplet dynamics and curvature which are important in liquid lens prediction and curvature control. For downward vortex and transition stages, solutal and thermal Marangoni effects dominate. The occurrence of a transition stage indicates buoyancy effect becomes comparable to Marangoni effect as ethanol continuously evaporates, and the occurrence of upward vortex stage indicates most of ethanol gasifies and buoyancy effect dominates. The interfacial contact line dynamics can be measured utilizing a newly developed measurement technique (Changfei Yan and Huihe Qiu 2016). The dynamics of a multicomponent droplet on a heated chemically patterned surface was presented (Minghao et al. 2017). Compared to the dynamics process of a multicomponent droplet on a homogenous surface, it is found that the chemical patterned surface can not only enhance evaporation by elongating the contact line, but also change the process from three regimes for the homogenous surface including constant contact line (CCL) regime, constant contact angle (CCA) regime and mix mode (MM) to two regimes, i.e. constant contact line (CCL) and moving contact line (MCL) regimes. The mechanism of contact line stepwise movement in MCL regimes in the microscopic range is investigated in detail. In addition, an improved local force model on the contact line was employed for analyzing the critical receding contact angles on homogenous and patterned surfaces. The analysis results agree well for both surfaces, and confirm that the transition from CCL to MCL regimes indicates droplet composition changes from multicomponent to monocomponent, providing an important metric to predict and control the dynamic behavior and composition of a multicomponent droplet using a wettability-patterned surface. We systematically studied the full spectrum of dynamics of droplets on hydrophobic-network surface and divided it into different stages: constant contact line (CCL) stage, constant contact angle (CCA) stage, pattern-pinning (PP) stage and moving contact line (MCL) stage. We also developed general models for analysis and accurately predicted the stage transition (critical receding contact angle). Meanwhile, each stage was first successfully predicted by our general models by combining well-known Rowan’s and Erbil’s models and introducing corrected contact line length which indicated influence of chemically patterned surface on evaporation rate.

617812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617812.value: The newly developed wettability-patterned hydrophilic/hydrophobic surfaces can control the multicomponent droplet dynamics and heat transfer. The pattern size, pitch distance and pattern shape are three key parameters affecting the contact line dynamics which need to be optimized. It was found that the droplet contact line was similar to the contour of the hydrophobic islands. The question is whether a shape with smooth curvature like a circle or with sharp curvature like a triangle confines the droplet better if we use the droplet array to form a high numerical aperture micro-lens array based on drop-on-demand generation of water-based molds. The pattern size confines the size of the droplet and the pitch distance controls the interaction of the adjacent droplets. Since the heat transfer efficiency changes with the heat flux, the patterns with different sizes and pitch distances should have different optimal working conditions. Optimization of these two variables is a complicated but interesting topic. Systematic research on this topic would provide key parameters for better control of droplet dynamics, contact line pinning/depinning and irregular droplet shape and droplet array formation which have promising potential in liquid lens array and other droplet microfluidic applications.

617812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617812.value: Contact line dynamics and coalescence of multicomponent droplets at the microscale is relevant to microfluidics, liquid micro lenses, lab-on-a-chip devices and energy research and industrial applications. The current project focused on the fundamental phenomena of droplet dynamics, contact line behavior and heating microdroplets on wettability-patterned surfaces that affect droplet internal flow, shape, evaporation, and interaction in mini/micro spaces. This is the first time a wettability-patterned surface is found to have a significant impact on droplet dynamics, contact line evaporation control and manipulation which resulted in a significant improvement in droplet dynamics and heat transfer. The effects of surface wetting, contact line length, droplet pinning and depinning on droplet dynamics and heat transfer are investigated. It was crucial to non-invasively measure transient droplet contact line and film thickness in mini/micro spaces, especially, near the interface between the micro droplet and the wall surface. A novel visualization technique for a mini/micro space measurement has been developed. Based on our findings, because surface-wettability patterns have a significant impact on the droplet dynamics, pinning/depinning, coalescence, heat and mass transfer processes, the technique helps to better design and optimize microfluidic droplet devices, such as liquid microlens arrays, droplet evaporators, heat food processors, etc.

617912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617912.value: For decades, control theory has been focused on controller design problems. Generations of control engineers and researchers have been brainwashed to believe that control theory is about controller design. The development of the modern control theory has experienced three stages: optimal control, robust control, and networked control. Indeed, in the optimal control and robust control stages, a feedback system is naturally divided into two parts: the plant to be controlled and the controller to be designed. Hence the control problems are naturally formulated as controller design problems under given or approximately given plants. In the networked control stage, a control system consists of three main parts: the plant to be controlled, the controller to be designed, and the communication channels between the plant and controller for information exchange. Nevertheless in the early days of the development of networked control theory, research problems are still fomulated as controller design problems assuming the plant and the communication channels are given. We have recently realized that networked control provides an opportunity for us to re-examine the long-held paradigm. If the channels are assumed to be given and are out of touch by the controller designer, then only the controller is to be designed so to meet the system peformance specifications. Our experience shows that problems formulated in this way are usually very hard to solve. We propose to allow the channels to be partially designed by the controller designer. In this way, we obtain a channel/controller co-design problem. Our experience shows that this formulation has tremendous advantages over the controller design formulation. In this proposed project, we plan to formulate and study several channel/controller co-design problems in networked control. Our preliminary studies have been quite successful. Some nice results have already been obtained, which shows the feasibility and potential of the proposed study. The requested funding is to be used to intensify our further study. Our ultimate goal is to develop a networked multivariable control theory in the channel/controller co-design framework. 几十年来，关于控制理论的研究一直专注于控制器的设计问题。历代控制工程师和研究人员都将控制理论理解为关于控制器设计的理论。现代控制理论的发展经历了三个阶段：最优控制，鲁棒控制和网络化控制。诚然，在最优控制和鲁棒控制阶段，一个反馈系统自然地被划分为两个部分：受控对象和待设计的控制器。因此，控制问题就可以被顺理成章地描述为在给定或大致给定受控对象情况下的控制器设计问题。在网络化控制阶段，一个控制系统由三个主要部分组成：受控对象，待设计的控制器以及连接受控对象和控制器以进行信息交换的通信信道。然而，在网络化控制理论发展早期，研究问题依然被描述为在给定受控对象和通信信道情况下的控制器设计问题。 我们最近认识到网络化控制提供了一个机会来重新审视上述关于控制理论的长期观念。如果通信信道被预先给定并且不能被设计，那么就只能通过设计控制器来达到系统性能的要求。我们的经验表明以这种方式描述的问题通常很难求解。针对这样的困难，我们提议让控制器设计者同时参与信道的设计。这样就形成了一个信道/控制器协同设计问题。经验表明这种问题描述与传统的控制器设计问题相比具有巨大的优势。 该拟议项目旨在描述并研究网络化控制中的几类信道/控制器协同设计问题。我们的初步研究十分成功并取得了一些很好的结果。这充分说明了该项研究的可行性和巨大潜力。申请的经费将用于加强我们的进一步研究。我们的最终目标是发展一套信道/控制器协同设计框架下的网络化多变量控制理论。

617912.label: Realisation of objectives
617912.value: For objective 1, we made a breakthrough discovery. We invented a new channel/controller co-design technique called coding/control co-design, whose solvability condition can be exactly given in terms of a very elegant majorization condition. This research result has opened the door for substantial further study and has led to a new funded RGC GRF project. For objective 2, we have also made great progress. We successfully resolved several optimal control problems, in both the continuous-time case and the discrete-time case. We are able to characterise the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of the optimal solutions. The study towards this objective reveals the importance of of a class of systems called nonnegative systems. The need for in-depth study of nonnegative systems leads to another new funded RGC GRF grant. For objective 3, we have made major initial steps in connecting network control with gap metric robust control theory and two-port networks in circuit theory. The documentation of the research fundings for this objective is underway.

617912.label: Major findings and research outcome
617912.value: For networked stabilisation, we proposed two co-design methods: scheduling/control co-design (C1) and coding control co-design (J4, C6, C7). The latter method shows great potential and connects with a very powerful mathematical tool called majorization theory. The networked stabilizability via coding/control co-design can then be characterised in terms of majorization. We have written several papers (J4, C6, C7) and have proposed a new RGC project, GRF 16208414, to continue the research. For H2 optimal networked control, very good progress has been made (J2, J3, C2, C3, C4, C5). We have connected it with positive system theory and as a result the necessary and sufficient condition for the existence and uniqueness of optimal control is obtained. A new RGC project, GRF 16211516, is successfully funded to continue the research. We established connections between H_infinity optimal networked control in one hand and gap metric robust stabilisation theory and two-port circuit theory in another hand. This turns out to be a very important conceptual advance.

617912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617912.value: The research outcome of this project has led to two follow-up funded RGC GRF grants, 16208414 and 16211516. More research problems have been formulated and more research activities will be conducted. We expect all these research projects to result in a comprehensive theory of channel/controller co-design approach to networked optimal control.
