618312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618312.value: Oxidation and disinfection processes provide effective degradation of some recalcitrant chemicals and essential control of waterborne diseases in drinking water, wastewater, and for groundwater remediation. However, unwanted oxidation and disinfection byproducts may form in some occasions, due to the inevitable reactions of the highly reactive oxidants and disinfectants with other constituents in water. For example, bromate, a well-recognized cancer-causing compound regulated by USEPA, European Commission, and WHO, can form excessively over its drinking water standards after treating bromide-containing water with ozone or hydroxyl radical-based technologies. In recent years, novel sulfate radical-based advance oxidation processes have found their superiority to conventional hydroxyl radical-based processes in oxidative destruction of some target pollutants. Its promising features include the persistent nature of its precursor compounds compared to hydrogen peroxide, its versatile activating means, its wider effective operating pH range compared to that of the Fenton process, and its lower influence by other competing constituents, such as carbonate, bicarbonate, and NOM in real water. These lead to a growing interest in their applications. However, bromate in high quantities is found in our recent study on degrading brominated disinfection byproducts by a sulfate radical-based UV-persulfate process. Our further preliminary investigation shows that bromate is formed from oxidation of aqueous bromide ions by the UV-persulfate process. The conversion from bromide to bromate depends on the persulfate to bromide ratio and up to 100% conversion is possible, which is significant and raises the alarm. This study is thus proposed to investigate in detail the formation of bromate from bromide ions in a number of sulfate radical-based advanced oxidation processes. Factors, including different precursor compounds and activation means, solution pH, NOM, alkalinity and chloride ions that may affect the formation will be examined in synthetic and real waters. The formation kinetics and mechanisms, which are unknown, will be disclosed. Most importantly, some strategies, based on common knowledge in controlling bromate formation from ozonation involving hydroxyl radicals, are proposed and will be examined in controlling the bromate formation, with due consideration for maintaining the oxidation power. The improved understanding of the formation and the control is essential to sustain further development of these promising sulfate radical-based advanced oxidation processes. It will be also of significant scientific merit in understanding the chemistry of the interactions among bromine species and sulfate radicals. 水處理中的氧化和消毒工藝為飲用水、污水和地下水的安全提供了有效的屏障，氧化工藝可以降解水中高危害高穩定性有機污染物，消毒工藝可以有效殺滅水中的病原微生物。然而，在實際水處理中，高活性的氧化劑/消毒劑在氧化/消毒過程中會產生有毒有害的副產物，其中，溴酸鹽是水中常見的一種氧化/消毒副產物，它是一種疑似致癌物，美國環保局、歐洲委員會和世界衛生組織的飲用水規範中都對它的限值進行了規定，採用臭氧或羥基自由基氧化處理飲用水的過程中溴酸鹽會經常超標。近年來，基於硫酸根自由基的新型高級氧化技術具有與傳統的基於羥基自由基的高級氧化技術相比擬的特點和一些優越性，包括：產生硫酸根自由基的物質特性穩定，激發方式通用靈活，技術適用的pH範圍廣，受水質本底物質（如：鹼度和NOM）的影響較小，這些優點使得這種新型的高級氧化工藝應用于實際水處理成為可能。但是，我們在利用UV/過硫酸鹽工藝對含溴的物質（二溴乙醯胺）進行處理的過程中發現了溴酸鹽的形成。進一步研究發現，含有溴離子的水在UV/過硫酸鹽工藝中也會產生溴酸鹽，溴離子轉化形成溴酸鹽的比例可以高達100%，並且形成溴酸鹽的主要貢獻來源過硫酸鹽光解過程中產生的硫酸根自由基。因此，基於硫酸根自由基的高級氧化工藝中產生的溴酸鹽問題應該引起關注。本研究的目的是系統研究各種基於硫酸根自由基的高級氧化工藝中溴酸鹽形成規律，在實驗室配水和實際水體中對不同產生硫酸根自由基的物質、激發方式、pH、NOM、鹼度、氯離子等可能會影響到溴酸鹽形成的因素進行研究，揭示溴酸鹽形成的動力學和機理；並且，參考臭氧和羥基自由基氧化過程中溴酸鹽控制的一些策略，在不影響體系氧化能力的情況下，提出並研究在硫酸根自由基氧化過程中溴酸鹽的控制技術。基於硫酸根自由基的高級氧化過程中溴酸鹽的形成機理和控制技術的研究對於該技術的進一步發展應用非常必要，同時，本研究還可以揭示含溴物質與硫酸根自由基之間的化學反應過程和機理。

618312.label: Realisation of objectives
618312.value: The project started on the date as scheduled. Part 1/Objective 1 of the study aiming at establishing the significance and kinetics of the bromate formation from a number of SO4•--based AOPs with changes of two precursor compounds, S2O82- and HSO5-, and four activation means, including UV at 254 nm and three transitional metals (Co(II), Ag(I) and Fe(II)) was completed. A comprehensive study and tests were conducted at different precursor concentrations and UV/metal dosages, with various solution pHs and concentrations of Br-, Cl-, NOM and HCO3- in synthetic solutions and real water to explore the significance of the bromate formation and the affecting factors. Samples were taken at different time interval to reveal the formation kinetics under different test conditions. It was found that the UV/S2O82- and Co(II)/HSO5- processes produced significant quantities of bromate, while the UV/HSO5- process only produced significant amounts of bromate under extreme conditions (high bromide and HSO5- concentrations). In both the UV/S2O82- and UV/HSO5- processes, increasing precursor concentrations and UV doses increased the bromate formation. The bromate formation was high at acidic and neutral pHs but decreased significantly over 90% with increasing pH from 7 to above 9. In the Co(II)/persulfate process, the bromate formation increased with increasing cobalt and persulfate concentrations and the maximum bromate formation occurred at pH 6. Less BrO3- was formed in the real water samples than in ultrapure water, which was primarily attributable to the presence of natural organic matter. At dosages relevant to those used for micropollutant degradation, the large percentage of conversion from bromide to BrO3- suggests a potential problem of the excessive production of BrO3- in the above three processes. Other pairs including the Ag(I)- and Fe(II)-activated S2O82- processes and the Fe(II)-activated HSO5- process yield insignificant quantities of BrO3- from bromide-containing water. In addition, we also investigated and observe significant bromate formation from debromination of 2,2-Bis(bromomethyl)-1,3-propanediol by the UV/persulfate process, due to the release of bromide from the pollutant degradation. Part 2/Objective 2 of the study was completed, aiming at providing fundamental explanation to the significant bromate formation with respect to the contributions from different highly reactive species including hydroxyl radicals, sulfate radicals and others, and revealing the importance of forming free bromine as the intermediate. Based on the results from Part 1 of the study, three representative cases of high bromate yields, the UV/S2O82-, UV/HSO5- and Co(II)/HSO5- processes, were selected and extensively investigated to disclose the mechanisms contributing to their high bromate formation, with a large number of supplementary tests measuring the time-dependent free bromine concentrations and the speciation and concentrations of radicals/oxidants formed and the establishment of the models describing the involving reactions. In the UV/S2O82- and UV/HSO5- processes, the BrO3- formation mechanisms are similar and are in two steps. It is initiated and involved the formation of free bromine as an intermediate and bromate as the final product. Both steps are primarily driven by SO4•-. Under the test conditions, the rate of the first step driven by SO4•- was slower than that of the second step. The pH dependency of the bromate formation is related to the slower transformation rate of bromide to hypobromite ions in the first step at alkaline pHs. In the Co(II)/HSO5- process, the bromate formation is also a two-step process involving free bromine as a key intermediate and bromate as the final product. In addition to the known oxidation of bromide to bromine by SO4•-, Co(III) also contributes primarily to the bromine formation in the first step. On the other hand, SO4•- is essential for the second step where the oxidation of bromine to bromate takes place, while Co(III) is unable to oxidize bromine to bromate. The results, together with the results obtained from Part 1 of the study have formulated four journal papers including one published in Environmental Science and Technology, one published in Water Research, one submitted to Water Research, and one under preparation. Some results were presented in the 9th IWA World Water Congress, the 12th IWA Leading Edge Conference on Water and Wastewater Technologies, the Gordon Research Conference on Drinking Water Disinfection By-Products 2015, and 248th and 250th ACS national meetings. Part 3/Objective 3 of the study was completed, aiming at identifying alternative strategies for control of the bromate formation in sulfate radical-based AOPs. Based on the common approaches for controlling bromate formation from ozonation involving hydroxyl radicals, 4 approaches, including pH depression, ammonia additions, and chlorine-ammonia and ammonia-chlorine processes, were selected and evaluated in two systems, the Co/HSO5- and UV/S2O82- processes that are found to form more bromate in bromide-containing. Tests were conducted in accordance to the methodologies stipulated in the proposal. The pH depression approach was examined and found not effective at practically-relevant pH and thus not further pursued. The other three approaches, ammonia additions and chlorine-ammonia and ammonia-chlorine processes, were extensively investigated with changes of bromide concentrations, persulfate concentrations and UV/cobalt dosages. For the UV/persulfate process, the ammonia addition shows better performance than the chlorine-ammonia and ammonia-chlorine processes in controlling the formation. The bromate formation with the ammonia addition showed a lag phase, which lasted longer with increasing NH3 dosages. The lag phase showed that the ammonia addition successfully quenched the formed free bromine from being further oxidized to bromate by SO4•-. However, for the chlorine-ammonia and ammonia-chlorine processes, increasing chlorine dosages actually accelerated the bromate formation than the NH3 addition alone, due to the formation of bromochloramine and bromamines and the photolysis of which released bromide and oxidized ammonia to nitrate. For the cobalt/persulfate process, the chlorine-ammonia and ammonia-chlorine processes are more effective than the ammonia addition in controlling the bromate formation. The former two processes were comparable in controlling the bromate formation at different ammonia, chlorine, Co(II) and bromide dosages. The ammonia addition, however, required high dosages of ammonia to effectively control the bromate formation The ammonia addition hardly controls the formation at high cobalt dosages or low bromide dosages, which can be attributable to the relatively slower reaction of free bromine with ammonia, comparing to that with bromamines and chloramines. The results were presented in two prestigious conferences, 250th ACS National Meeting & Exposition, and 12th IWA Leading Edge Conference on Water and Wastewater Technologies, and together with the on-going additional modeling work on chlorine-ammonia-bromide chemistry, will formulate two journal papers to be submitted in late 2017.

618312.label: Major findings and research outcome
618312.value: The major findings obtained from this study have formulated 2 prestigious journal papers (#1 and 2) and 6 conference presentations (#1-6) in four outstanding international conferences so far. We are also working on another 4 journal papers, one (Journal publication #6) submitted and the other 3 (Journal publications #3-5) under preparation. This study provided training of 3 postgraduate students: 2 have obtained their MPhil degree and the other one is expect to obtain his PhD degree in January 2018. This study also involved close collaboration between HKUST and Sun Yat-Sen University, China. The specific major findings are: Significant quantities of bromate are formed from bromide oxidation in the UV/persulfate and cobalt/persulfate processes (Journal publications #1, 2 and 5) and Conference presentations #1, 3, 4, and 6). Using UV/persulfate process to degrade bromated pollutant such as 2,2-Bis(bromomethyl)-1,3-propanediol also leads significant bromate formation due to the release of bromide during the degradation (Journal publication #6). In the UV/persulfate process, the bromate formation increases with increasing persulfate dosage and bromide concentration. The bromate formation is similar for pH 4−7 but decreased over 90% at pH 9. The bromate formation is initiated and primarily driven by sulfate radicals (SO4•−) and involves free bromine as an intermediate. In the cobalt/persulfate process, increasing the PMS and cobalt dosages increase the formation. The bromate yield shows a maximum at 6. The bromate formation is also a two-step process, with free bromine as the intermediate. In the first step, Co(III) produced from the oxidation of Co(II) is the primary oxidant and oxidizes bromide to free bromine. SO4•− is essential for the oxidation of free bromine to bromate in the second step. For both processes, natural organic matter in real water reacts with bromine atoms, free bromine and SO4•− to form less bromate.

618312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618312.value: In this project, we have observed that only the UV/persulfate and cobalt/persulfate processes have high bromate yields while other common SO4•−-driven process, such as the Fe/persulfate process does not. However the Fe/persulfate process suffers from its own disadvantage: the low radial yields from Fe(II) quenching. To balanced the extent of bromate formation and degradation of micropollutants, which are nevertheless coupled processes, we propose to develop an UV/ferrous ion (Fe(II))/persulfate process at a very small dose (a few dozen uM) of Fe(II) that takes the advantage of using the Fe(II) addition to control bromate formation and to activate persulfate to generate SO4•−, which shall accelerated the degradation of some micropollutants while control bromate formation. A proposal is prepared to seek for external funding. With better understanding of the SO4•−-driven processes and effective control on bromate formation, we are extending this study to the applications of these processes in the destruction of emerging contaminants including some pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs) and disinfection by-products (DBPs) with internal funding. One conference paper was presented, one journal paper was submitted and two journal papers are being prepared.

618312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618312.value: To produce safe drinking water from deteriorated sources polluted with pollutants, it becomes essential to include advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) in treatment. However, unwanted oxidation byproducts may form in some occasions. For example, bromate, a well-recognized cancer-causing compound regulated by USEPA, European Commission, and WHO, can form excessively over its water standards. In recent years, the novel sulfate radical-based AOPs have found their superiority to conventional hydroxyl radical-based AOPs in destruction of many pollutants, which leads to a growing interest in their applications. However, bromate in high quantities may form and demands control. In this study, we provided a breakthrough in filling the knowledge gap of the bromate formation in sulfate radical-based AOPs with respect to its significance, factors affecting the formation kinetics, and mechanisms explaining the formation. We found high bromate yields in some of the AOPs under certain circumstances and explained the formation mechanisms. More importantly, we proposed, examined and found some effective strategies to control the formation. The improved understanding of the formation and the control is beneficial to sustain further development of the sulfate radical-based AOPs. It is also of significant scientific merit in understanding the chemistry of the interactions among bromine species and sulfate radicals.

618512.label: Project Objectives
618512.value: We will develop an integrated framework for investigating the joint development of perception and behavior, where the perceptual representation develops through sparse coding and the behavior develops through reinforcement learning. Their development will be explicitly linked, in that they will both seek to find the best encoding of the input under resource constraints. We will validate the performance of this algorithm in one specific sensorimotor task: the joint development of stereo disparity tuning in visual cortical neurons and the control of vergence eye movements. We will also begin an initial investigation into the generality of this framework, by applying it to another task: the joint development of motion selectivity in visual cortical neurons and the control of smooth pursuit eye movements.

618512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618512.value: Behavior and sensory perception are mutually dependent. Sensory perception drives behavior, but behavior can also influence the development of sensory perception, by altering the statistics of the sensory input. It is likely that both sensory perception and behavior develop simultaneously in a coupled process of mutual inter-dependence. Despite this, most past work has treated their development in isolation, considering only the development of either perception or behavior. We propose here to undertake a study of their joint development using a developmental robotics paradigm. In particular, we will embed both learning algorithms perception based on sparse coding with reinforcement learning algorithms for behavior in a robotic platform in order to study the joint development in an artificial embodied agent. We will concentrate on visual perception and vision guided eye movements. We propose to develop an integrated framework, where the development of perception and behavior are explicitly coupled in that they both seek to optimize the same objective function. We will evaluate the performance of this approach on two visual sensorimotor tasks: binocular vergence eye movement control and smooth pursuit eye movement control. 行爲和感官知覺是相互依存的。知覺驅動著行爲，但行爲也可以通過改變輸入感官不同信息的比例，影響感官知覺的發展。知覺和行爲哪個先形成，就好比先有雞還是先有蛋的問題，很難分清。因此，感官知覺和行爲很有可能是在一個相互依賴的耦合過程中同步發展的。不過過去的大多數工作都孤立的對待著他們，或者只考慮知覺的發展，或者只考慮行爲的發展。現在，我們計劃用機器人的視覺與行爲的發展做模板，研究他們的聯合發展過程。要特別強調的是，我們將在機器人系統中同時嵌入用以模擬神經知覺的稀疏編碼學習算法和用于行爲形成的強化學習算法，通過這樣做來進而研究一個模擬生物體的系統的發展。這個研究的重心是視覺感知和由視覺引導的眼球運動。我們將擴大現在在雙眼深度感知和雙眼轉向控制這兩個神經過程的聯合發展中的初步研究成果，進一步增加更複雜的視覺輸入信號和更豐富的強化學習算法。然後，我們將把這項工作延伸到另一種視覺任務，即視覺運動感知和眼球平滑追蹤的結合發展。

618512.label: Realisation of objectives
618512.value: Both research objectives were fully achieved. For the first objective, we developed the active efficient encoding framework, which models the joint development of perception and behavior. Perception refers to the mapping of the sensory input to an internal neural representation. We used sparse coding to model this stage. A sensory input vector is represented as the linear combination of a small number of basis functions, which are drawn from an overcomplete dictionary of basis functions. The sparse set of coefficients combining the basis functions in the dictionary are the internal representation. This representation is learned in the sense that the basis functions start out with random initializations, but are gradually updated so that the sparse linear combinations are better able to model the sensory input vector. Action refers to the mapping from the sparse coefficient vector to one of a discrete set of actions. This is done by a feedforward neural network, where the weights of the network are learned by reinforcement learning. The output of the neural network has a number of nodes, one corresponding to each possible action. The activation of each node corresponds to the probability that the corresponding action is selected. This architecture is described in more detail in the journal paper by Zhang, Triesch and Shi, which appeared in the Journal of Vision in 2016, as well as in the two conference papers that appeared at the International Conference on Development and Learning. For the second objective, we applied the active efficient encoding model to model the development of stereo disparity tuning in visual cortical neurons and the control of vergence eye movements. In this case, the sensory input vector to the sparse coding stage consisted of the concatenation of square image patches from the left and right eye, which were jointly encoded by the sparse coder. The actions generated by the neural network corresponded to changes in the vergence angle between the two eyes. The process of stereo disparity perception and vergence control are important components of depth perception. In order to implement this model, we needed to develop a simulation environment for active eye control. This simulation environment is described in the journal paper by Primakov, Fronius, Shi and Triesch, which appeared in the Journal of Vision in 2016. We also needed to develop a model of stereo disparity tuned neurons, which appears in a conference publication entitled " A Two Layer Disparity Simple Cell Model," which appeared at IJCNN in 2016. We investigated the implications of this joint development model on the orientation alignment of receptive fields between the two eyes in the second paper at IJCNN 2016 listed in section 9.

618512.label: Major findings and research outcome
618512.value: The first major finding of this proposal was the development of the active efficient encoding framework, an online model of the joint development of perception and action in humans and robots. This is a major development, because in contrast to past work, we treat the development of perception and action simultaneously, whereas past work tended to treat these in isolation, i.e. studying the supervised learning of a perceptual representation of the input in order to extract cues hand chosen as being relevant to the desired behavior, which was typically hard coded, or studying the learning of the mapping from a hand-chosen and hard-coded perceptual stage to action using reinforcement learning. A second major finding is that this model leads to an accurate account for the development of visual perception and eye movement control in humans. In particular, we have studied the joint development of stereo disparity selectivity and vergence eye movement control, as well as its interaction with the development of motion selectivity and smooth pursuit eye movements (Zhang, Triesch & Shi, 2016). It turns out that interfering with the normal development of binocular vision in humans leads to deficits in smooth pursuit eye movement control in humans. Our model exhibits the same deficiencies, and matches the results of psychophysical experiments in humans both qualitatively and quantitatively. It also leads to some testable predictions. Finally, a third major finding of this work is the development of anatomically and physiologically accurate system for simulating eye movement control. We developed this model in order to study vergence eye movement control, but the model is generic. It can be used to model other eye movements, such as smooth pursuit, fixational jitter, saccades and micro-saccades. The model can therefore serve as the basis for future development of the work started in this proposal.

618512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618512.value: There are many directions in which the active efficient encoding framework can be extended. One particular direction is to incorporate a hierarchical control strategy for integrating information from different image scales. In the work developed in this project, information from different scales was combined by simple concatenation before being fed into the neural network that generated the action command to adapt the vergence angle. It would be interesting to develop a hierarchical control strategy, where information at coarse scales is used to generate large, yet fairly coarse vergence changes, and information at fine scales is used to generate smaller, more precise changes. We have recently obtained funding from the Research Grants Council to investigate this development, under grant 16244416 entitled "A Coarse-to-Fine Learning Strategy for Binocular Vergence Control ," which runs from January 2017 to December 2018. It would also be interesting to see whether information from other sensory modalities can be incorporated into the active efficient encoding framework. This would enable the fully autonomous and unsupervised development of multi-cue integration for eye movements. We are currently investigating whether the active efficient encoding framework can be used to model the integration visual and vestibular inputs for image stabilization.

618512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618512.value: Both humans and robots interact with their environment through a process known as the perception-action cycle. Through the process of perception, the actor (whether human or robotic) generates an internal representation or understanding of the environment and its relationship to it based on the sensory input they receive. This internal representation is then mapped to an appropriate action to take in the environment. This action changes the relationship between the actor and its environment, which changes the sensory input. In humans, both perception and action must be learned simultaneously. Both must adapt throughout life, since they must automatically adapt to changes in body shape during development. Supported by this grant, the investigators have developed the first model of the joint development of perception and action. They have demonstrated that this model can account for the learning of vergence eye movements, i.e. the control of the two eyes to fuse the images acquired by them. This is a critical step in depth perception. The work in this proposal has led not only to a better understanding of the process of human development, but also to the development adaptive robots that learn in the same way as humans.

618612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618612.value: The last decade has seen a growing interest in the area of networked control systems (NCSs), which have a wide span of applications such as in environmental monitoring, smart transportation, smart grid, etc. In many of these applications, the available resources (sensor communication energy and network bandwidth) are severely limited and a tradeoff between the system performance and the resources is desired. In conventional NCSs design, such a tradeoff is typically achieved by limiting the communication between the sensor and the estimator and between the controller and the actuator. When no data is received, the remote estimator and actuator will run open loop prediction and control which often lead to poor estimation quality and control performance. The main objective of this project is to contribute to the design of NCSs by studying a new NCSs structure where the data exchange between the sensor and the estimator, and between the controller and the actuators are governed by well-established communication protocols. Under the new structure the estimator and the actuator are able to infer partial knowledge of the data at the sensor and at the controller in case they are not sent, thus improved state estimation quality and system performance can be obtained when compared with conventional NCSs design methodologies. Our proposed research methodology has been successfully applied in some of our recent works which demonstrate its feasibility and great advantages. This project is composed of two main thrusts: (1) constructing appropriate communication protocols that improve the closed-loop system performance compared with that under conventional NCSs design methodologies; (2) developing novel state estimation algorithms and controller design techniques which are coupled with the design of appropriate communication protocols. Furthermore, experimental evaluation and validation of the algorithms and methodologies will be carried out. The developed methods will be of major strategic relevance to local industries, since they will provide a more precise and cost-efficient system design, compared to today when most of the cost in system development is spent on ad-hoc expensive system integration and validation techniques, which rely almost exclusively on time-consuming simulations. The project team members have been working actively in the field of networked control recently, and have obtained many important results on packet drop and delay analysis, sensor and control data scheduling, etc. Our past experiences and initial works which demonstrate the feasibility of our research approach enable us to carry out a successful project. 近十年来，网络控制系统（NCS）受到越来越多的关注，在环境监测、智能交通网络和智能电网等领域均得到广泛应用。在很多实际应用中，限于有限的资源（例如传感器传输电池容量和网络带宽），我们通常需要在系统性能和资源消耗两者之间协调权衡。传统的网络控制系统设计中，这种平衡可以靠限制传感器与估计器之间以及控制器和执行器之间的传输来实现。当数据丢失时，远端估计器和执行器将做开环预测和控制，这常常造成系统状态估计质量和控制性能的下降。 该项目旨在通过研究一种新的网络控制系统结构，为网络控制系统的设计做出一定的贡献。在此结构中，传感器与估计器之间、控制器和执行器之间的数据交换由完善的传输协议所控制。与传统的网络控制系统的设计方法相比，在新的结构中，估计器和执行器可以推测出传感器和执行器端的部分未发送数据的信息，从而提高系统估计和控制性能。我们所提出的研究思想已经成功应用于我们当前的部分工作中，同时研究结果证明了它的可行性和优越性。 在该项目中, 我们将创建合适的通讯协议来提高系统闭环性能. 同时我们将根据新传输协议框架，开发新型状态估计算法和控制器设计技术。另外，我们也将进行实验评测和算法方法的验证。 如今系统开发的大部分成本都来源于特别昂贵的系统集成和验证技术，这些技术都极其依靠耗时的数值模拟。与之相比，新方法提供了一个更加精确、更加高效的系统设计，因此对本地工业而言它将具有重大的战略影响。目前该项目组成员正在积极开展对网络控制领域的研究，并且在数据丢失及延迟分析、传感器和数据控制调度等方面取得了许多重要的进展。我们过去的研究经验和早期成果充分表明了我们的研究手段的可行性，也必将保证我们将在这一项目上取得瞩目的成果。

618612.label: Realisation of objectives
618612.value: We have made excellent progress with this funding. Following the original objectives of the project, we have thoroughly analyzed the advantages of bringing novel communication protocols into the closed-loop networked control systems design. For a number of different application scenarios (e.g., remote estimation with smart sensors/normal sensors), we have constructed a novel type of communication protocols, derived the corresponding minimum mean-squared error estimate at the remote estimator, analyzed the communication/estimation tradeoffs, compared the novel protocols with classic periodic communications, etc. In addition to the original objectives, we have successfully applied the developed tools to other areas such as sensor power control, distributed state estimation, and set-valued filtering. The results are fruitful and are summarized and published in 7 leading international journals and 7 leading international conferences.

The major finding is that by properly designing a good communication protocol, greatly enhanced system performance can be achieved even with very limited communication resources. The main research outcomes include publications in 7 leading international journals and 7 leading international conferences as well as training of 2 PhD students.

618612.value: The research outcomes are fruitful and paved the way for a number of exciting future research directions including multi-sensor multi-systems scheduling, multi-agent consensus, communication and control co-designs, etc.

618612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618612.value: This project has conducted a thorough study of communication protocols and their applications in sensor networks, distributed state estimation, power control, etc. The key lies in the differentiation of important/non-important information. Establishing a metric for such a differentiation was the first step, based on which, effective and efficient communication protocols were built and analyzed. We found that by properly designing such an importance metric and carefully designing a communication protocol, we can obtain superior system performance using minimal resources. The developed theoretical tools including state estimation and control algorithms, and efficient sensor scheduling schemes can be used to better analyze and design an important class of networked systems which are seen in a variety of areas in engineering sciences and elsewhere.

618812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618812.value: Watching wide field-of-view moving patterns can induce illusion of self-motion (vection) and visually induced motion sickness (VIMS) (Ji and So et al., 2009). After 64 years of research, mechanism of motion sickness is still not fully understood. This proposed study develops and validates a brain mechanism to explain VIMS. Findings can significantly contribute to image safety standards and development of safer games. Brandt et al. (1998) reported that when most viewers experience sensations of vection, their vestibular cortices will be deactivated as a protective mechanism to deal with integration of inappropriate self-motion signals from visual and vestibular organs. In this study, we hypothesize that VIMS generation is associated with the inability to deactivate the vestibular cortex in a timely manner. We refer this as the ‘cortical reciprocal inhibitory protection (CRIP) theory’. We further hypothesize that eye movements will disrupt the CRIP response and result in higher levels of VIMS. On the other hand, repeated exposure will encourage the normal functioning of CRIP response which in turn reduces levels of VIMS. In Phase 1 of the proposed research, nontrivial hypotheses rooted in the CRIP theory will be tested. In particular, pursuit eye movements are hypothesized to increase VIMS in viewers watching vection provoking stimuli. Phase 2 of the research will use near infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) to measure the regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) in visual and vestibular cortices to verify the cortical deactivation of vestibular cortices (more details in Section 2). Unlike visual cortices, vestibular cortices are less defined in human. In Phase 2A, cortical areas responsive to vestibular stimuli (i.e., physical motion) will be studied and verified. These data will be NEW as cortical responses with physical (rather than galvanic or caloric) vestibular stimuli are rare. In Phase 2B, CRIP will be tested and validated by measuring rCBF responses in the visual cortices (areas V3, 5) and the vestibular cortex (to be confirmed in Phase2A) during repeated exposure to vection provoking stimuli with and without eye movements. We hypothesize that viewers susceptible to VIMS will exhibit less efficient deactivation patterns in their vestibular cortices than those who are not susceptible. Effects of adaptation and eye movements on CRIP responses will also be studied. If this theory is validated, it will be a ground breaking finding and can explain the mystery of susceptibility to VIMS. 經過64多年的研究，人類有視覺誘發性的暈浪感覺 (VIMS) 的原因仍然沒有被完全理解。此研究會開發和驗證一個利用大腦皮質協調機制來解釋VIMS。結果可以顯著地促進更安全的電腦遊戲及其他安全標準的發展。 Brandt等人（1998）報導，當大多數觀眾有視覺誘發性的對流感覺時，他們的大腦前庭皮質將被關閉。這是一種保護機制，作為對視覺和前庭器官感覺有差異的自我處理與整合。在這項研究中，我們假設這種大腦皮質協調保護機制因人而異，有強有弱。 我們進一步假設如果一個人的大腦皮質協調機制是弱的，他們容易有暈浪感覺。我們指這是“大腦皮質相互抑制的保護論（CRIP）”。我們再進一步假設，眼球運動會減弱CRIP機制，並導致更高水平的VIMS。另一方面，反复接觸誘發暈浪感覺的電腦遊戲將鼓勵CRIP機制加強運作，從而降低VIMS 水平。 研究的第一階段，我們將植根於對CRIP理論進行測試,特別是集中測試眼球運動對VIMS的影響。 第二階段的研究將採用近紅外光譜（NIRS）測量大腦皮質血液中的氧水平（rCBF），用於驗證視覺和前庭皮質相互抑制的協調（第2節）。如果CRIP理論能被驗證，這將是一個突破性的發現，可以解釋人類有視覺誘發性的暈浪感覺 (VIMS) 的原因。

618812.label: Realisation of objectives
618812.value: Objective 1 (achieved) - The study will use near infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) to qualify the haemoglobin responses at the vestibular cortices in the presence of physical motion. Such data are relatively unknown due to the challenges in imaging the brain during motion (Nolan et al., 2011). This objective has been achieved through Experiment 1 and Experiment 7. Regional changes in oxy-hemoglobin near cotical Brodmann area 40 was measure by functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) during physical motion in fore-and-aft, lateral, and sway axes. This is unique and novel because past studies did not use physical motion. Results showed that lateral physical motion caused a significant increase in levels of oxy-hemoglobin. Experiment 7 repeated the setting of Experiment 1 using a customized NIRS-compatible manikin to isolate and quantify the influence of motion artifact picked up by the fNRIS measurement probes in Experiment 1. Results indicated that the findings in Experiment 1 were NOT influenced by motion artifact. A working paper is being prepared (Zhao et al., 2017a). Objective 2 (achieved) - The study will use NIRS to examine and validate the ability of the 'cortical reciprocal inhibitory protection' (CRIP) theory to explain individual susceptibility to VIMS. This objective has been achieved through Experiments 2, 8, and 9. Experiments 2 and 8 were the preparatory experiment for Experiment 9. In Experiment 9, participants with low and high susceptibility to VIMS were exposed to customized vection-provoking stimuli with their oxy-hemoglobin levels monitored by the fNRIS systems. Data showed, for the first time, that levels of VIMS susceptibility were related to different patterns of changes in oxy-hemoglobin levels measured near the vestibular cortices. The correlation relationships are consistent with the CRIP theory which predicts that VIMS-resistant participants were able to suppress the levels of oxy-hemoglobin around the vestibular cortices during exposure to vection-provoking stimuli. This is an important finding because it uncovers the neural basis of sensory adaptation for visual-vestibular conflicts. A working paper is being prepared (Zhao et al., 2017b). Objective 3 (achieved) - The study will use NIRS to examine and validate the ability of CRIP theory to explain the known effects of optokinetic nystagmus (OKN) on VIMS. This objective has been achieved through Experiments 3a,b and 6a. Both Experiments 3a and 6a confirmed the correlation relationships between the presence of OKN and the rated levels of VIMS. Results of Experiment 3a were presented at the EHF2013 International Conference held in UK (Guo et al., 2013). The suppression of vestibular signals to reduce VIMS susceptibility as predicted by CRIP theory is hypothesized to be disrupted by the presence of OKN. Results are consistent with the predictions of CRIP experiments but raise some other concerns regarding the nature of eye movements. A follow-up experiment was conducted (Experiment 4) which is described under Objective 5. Objective 4 (achieved) - The study will use NIRS to examine and validate the CRIP theory against the known effects of adaptation due to repeated exposure to vection provoking stimuli. This objective has been achieved through Experiment 10. Results of Experiment 9 suggest that the CRIP neural pattern can indeed explain the resistance mechanism towards VIMS. Since VIMS resistance can be learned through adaptation, Experiment 10 was conducted to test whether the CRIP pattern as revealed by fNIRS signals also changed through repeated exposure to the same vection-provoking stimuli. Participants in Experiment 10 were exposed to the same 20 minute vection-provoking stimulus twice per day and for 10 days or until their rated levels of VIMS reduced to zero. Results indicated that the CRIP patterns changed with repeated exposure. Data are reported in Zhao (2017). Objective 5 (achieved) - The study will test the hypotheses that voluntary eye movements will increase the levels of VIMS in viewers watching vection provoking stimuli. As explained under objective 3, this hypothesis is consistent with CRIP theory. Results of Exp3b indicated that during game play, the use of an eye fixation pointer could not significantly reduce the EMs. In-depth analyses suggest that most of the EMs exhibited by the game players were voluntary EMs rather than OKN. Experiment 4 was conducted to examine the effects of voluntary EMs on levels of VIMS. Results indicated that the presence of voluntary EMs significantly increase levels of VIMS. Three further experiments (5, 6b and 6c) were conducted to investigate the relationships between foveal retinal slip (FRS) in the fore-and-aft axis and the yaw axis as well as after-OKN on levels of VIMS. Results indicated that the decaying time constants of after-OKN correlate with individual susceptibility to VIMS. The finding has been published in Applied Ergonomics (Guo et al., 2017). Also, during exposure to fore-and-aft vection-provoking stimuli, there are interesting interactions among the absence of voluntary eye movement, oscillating frequency, and oscillating amplitude of vection-provoking stimuli. The relevant findings are published in Ergonomics (Chen et al., 2016), and were presented at VSS 2014 (Chen et al., 2014) and VSS2017 (Wei et al., 2017).

618812.label: Major findings and research outcome
618812.value: Consistent with the hypothetical ‘cortical reciprocal inhibitory protection’ (CRIP) theory, our evidence suggests that the interaction between optokinetic nystagmus (OKN) and the vestibular system is correlated with individual susceptibility to visually induced motion sickness (VIMS). Results are published in Applied Ergonomics (Guo, Chen, Wei, So and Cheung, 2017). This finding suggests the central role of the neural velocity storage mechanism in the brainstem. For the first time, cortical haemoglobin responses at the vestibular cortices were measured with and without controlled physical motion using near infrared spectroscopy (NIRS). Results are documented in Zhao (2017 – completed PhD thesis) and Zhao et al., 2017a (a working journal manuscript). Using CRIP theory, activities in similar cortical regions were identified and confirmed with empirical brain studies. Results are reported in Zheng (2016 – completed MPhil thesis) and Wei, Zheng and So (2017). More importantly, participants with different levels of susceptibility to VIMS were found to exhibit different CRIP neural patterns as revealed by NIRS responses. Results are documented in Zhao (2017 – completed PhD thesis) and Zhao et al., 2017b (a working journal manuscript). As partially predicted by CRIP theory, the generation of VIMS is associated with the interactions between visual and vestibular cortical activities. This implies that the strength of vection-provoking visual stimuli is determined by its velocity rather than frequency. Indeed, we found that this hypothesis is true. Results are published in Ergonomics (Chen, Bao, Zhao and So, 2016). Both Applied Ergonomics and Ergonomics are the flagship journals in the field of ergonomics. In addition, the PI has delivered a KEYNOTE speech at VIM2015, Tokyo, on the science of visually induced motion sickness reporting how CRIP theory and an understanding of the brain pathway of motion sickness may lead to reduced nausea among patients undergoing chemotherapy treatment.

618812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618812.value: In this study, we discovered that there is great potential in using EEG to study cortical responses to vection-provoking stimuli. In addition to the 10 experiments conducted to achieve the said objectives of the study, we are conducting extra experiments using EEG.

618812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618812.value: About one-third of the population will feel “sea-sick” after watching virtual reality movies but another one-third will not report any such symptoms after the same VR experience. For centuries, scientists have been trying to explain why. This study takes us closer to the answer. It turns out that when we watch VR movies, nearly all of us will feel as if we are “moving” even though we are physically stationary. This generates “conflicting” sensory information. About one-third of us can reduce this “conflicting” signal representation in our brains by directing less oxygenated blood to the part of the brain that is responsible for making sense of our physical body movements. This makes us more resistant to “sea sickness”. However, one-third of us have not acquired this ability to redirect the flow of oxygenated blood in the brain resulting in “conflicting” sensory signal representation in our brains which leads to a large scale excitation of the autonomic nerves system responsible for increases in heart rates, sweating, nausea and abnormal stomach contraction (i.e., vomiting). The good news is that we can be trained to ignore this “conflicting” signal representation through repeated exposures as our initial findings.

619012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619012.value: Shape analysis is essential for many geometry applications. Traditional shape analysis techniques focus on computing shape descriptors at local scales. They define shape features at each surface point such as curvatures and saliency. Such descriptors are capable of revealing geometric information of the underlying surface up to a local neighborhood, but are oblivious to shape semantics like symmetry and topology. This project aims at introducing a new shape analysis tool for computing shape information at global scales which we call pairwise harmonics. Given a pair of surface points, we define the pairwise harmonic as the cotangent-weighted harmonic field that propagates from one point to the other. Shape descriptors are then extracted from the set of isocurves propagating along the path connecting the two points. Such a set of isocurves is able to capture global shape information and provide a simple way to sense the underlying geometry and even its semantics. Computing the pairwise global properties of the shape also allow the design of algorithms that are more robust towards local surface noise, pose variations and shape topology. Computing the harmonic field for every surface point pair, however, would be computationally prohibitive. Therefore, sampling strategies to identify a sufficiently small set of points that define a handful of good pairwise harmonic fields is a key to efficient algorithms that utilize the pairwise descriptors. Thanks to the overlapping characteristics of propagation paths of harmonics, it often suffices to sample a sparsely distributed set of surface points. We will focus on investigating the use of the pairwise harmonics to solve two geometric analysis problems, namely, intrinsic reflectional symmetry computation and shape correspondence. These problems are known to be challenging due to the nature of the computation difficulties in sensing global shape properties which involve inferring shape semantics. Hence, statistics-based approaches are often necessary to first compute sufficient evidence and then vote for the final results. However, most state-of-the-art voting-based algorithms for computing the symmetry and correspondence employ rather complicated techniques which are time-consuming. We will show that the pairwise harmonics can lead to simpler and more efficient solutions for these problems. 形状分析在许多三维几何应用中都是必不可少的。然而，利用传统的三维形状分析方法计算出的描述符往往只关注于模型的局部特征。这些描述符虽然能够提供局部的几何信息，但是三维模型的语义特征，例如对称以及拓扑信息，则会被忽略。在这个项目中，我们将提出一个新的三维形状分析工具。利用它所计算出的描述符能够提供三维模型的整体信息。首先，对于模型表面给定的两个点，我们计算出从其中一个点传播到另一个点的对偶谐波场。通过在这个场中均匀采样，我们可以得到许多等值线。基于这些等值线，我们定义了可以描述模型整体信息的形状描述符。基于这些描述符的算法对模型局部的噪声，模型形状的改变，以及模型拓扑结构不敏感，因此，算法可以更加鲁棒。在这个方法中，对于不同的应用，如何定义合适的对偶谐波场是重要的一步。而定义谐波场的关键在于如何选取模型表面的点。由于在计算谐波场时，从一点到另一点的传播路径受模型的几何特征影响，因此大部分谐波场对应的传播路径存在着重叠。正因为此，在模型表面选取少量分散的点便可以计算得到足够的对偶谐波场。利用对偶谐波场，我们将研究如何更好的解决两个几何分析问题，即模型的固有镜面对称性以及不同模型间的对应问题。我们将会展示利用对偶谐波场的优越性，即，能够设计出比现有方法更简单有效的算法。

619012.label: Realisation of objectives
619012.value: Shape analysis is a fundamental task in many geometric processing algorithms. The main goal of this project is to develop a novel shape analysis approach that is more global, discriminative, and can effectively capture the variations in the underlying geometry. The idea is to analyze a shape by computing shape descriptors for pairs of surface points rather than individual points as in previous approaches. We fulfilled the first objective by introducing pairwise harmonic fields and defining two shape descriptors on the isocurves of the fields. To fulfill the remaining three objectives, we applied the pairwise harmonic shape analysis mechanism to several geometric applications, developing simpler and more efficient algorithms than the state-of-the-art methods. For efficiency, we devise surface sampling strategies to identify a small number of good pairwise harmonics for specific applications. First, we exploit the intrinsic symmetry information of the shape descriptors for computing intrinsic reflective symmetry axis. The pairwise analysis explores shape geometry in both global and local scales, thus is able to tolerate partially missing symmetry information. Second, we addressed the problem of finding meaningful correspondence between two shapes. The shapes may have rather different surface details, poses and may even be only partially matchable. Existing methods commonly leverage low-dimensional spaces (e.g., conformal mappings) or representations (e.g., shape skeleton) to reduce exponential searching complexities. We design a matching algorithm that operates like the well-known ant colony system and runs in polynomial time. Lastly, we addressed the simultaneous surface segmentation and skeletonization problem. Our solution leverage the fact that isocurves are good candidates of segmentation boundaries and that connecting their centroids produces skeletal segments. These contributions are elaborated in Section 6.1. In view of these results, we consider that the objectives of the project have been fulfilled.

619012.label: Major findings and research outcome
619012.value: We designed the pairwise cotangent-weighted harmonic fields and defined the perimeter descriptor and the distance descriptor on isocurves of the fields. The two descriptors together are able to reveal symmetries of shape between point pairs. Moreover, owing to the inherent smoothness of the cotangent-weighted harmonic fields, the descriptors are insensitive to surface noise and isometric deformation, leading to robust algorithms. We showed that these shape descriptors can infer shape structures and consistently lead to simpler and more efficient algorithms than the state-of-the-art methods for three applications: intrinsic reflectional symmetry axis computation, matching shape extremities, and simultaneous surface segmentation and skeletonization. This work was published in an IEEE TVCG paper [Zheng et al. 2013]. Further, we studied shape segmentation, which is yet another shape analysis problem. We derived a single segmentation field to identify the mesh boundaries to achieve high-quality mesh segmentation. The main idea is to exploit a hierarchical spectral analysis in order to systematically discover the relationship between the desired segmentation boundaries and the algebraic properties of its eigenvectors. We showed that eigenvectors derived from a concavity-aware Laplacian operator of a mesh can explicitly characterize the mesh concavity information. This work was published in the journal Graphical Models [Wang et al. 2014]. We then applied our skeletonization and segmentation algorithms to a dynamic sketching application. Given a segmented model, the goal is to automatically simulate the process of how people draw lines when sketching the 3D model at a specific view. This work was published in the proceedings of the conference Expressive 2014 [Liu et al. 2014].

619012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619012.value: We believe pairwise shape analysis will open up new possibilities in the future. Interestingly, the parallel work of Kaick et al. [CGF 2013] exploits fuzzy geodesics between point pairs for partial shape correspondence and shape retrieval. We believe this kind of pairwise analysis can be naturally applied to more applications such as shape coanalysis and part recognition. It would also be interesting to explore the extension of pairwise analysis to a multiway analysis, which has the potential of revealing even richer information in the surface. A natural application of multiway analysis would be shape matching.

619012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619012.value: The proposed pairwise harmonic approach enables simpler and efficient solutions to be developed for challenging geometric problems, in particular, symmetry computation and shape correspondence. Symmetry is one of the most fundamental phenomena in nature and man-made objects. It is also a crucial element for human recognition in many domains, including arts, biology, mechanical design, and architecture. In computer graphics, symmetry has been used in shape processing applications like remeshing, beautification and shape editing. Shape correspondence is a key component in tasks such as 3D scan alignment and space-time reconstruction, and a preprocessing in diverse applications such as attribute transfer, shape interpolation and statistical modeling. Our simpler and efficient algorithms contributed in terms of ease of implementation and efficiency improvement of these related algorithms.

619112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619112.value: 長期的目標是生產高品質的數字化模型的一個複雜的真實世界中的對象自動獲取一個實用的終端到終端的系統，完成詳細的重建三維表面的幾何形狀的幾何形狀和反射信息。 類似一個雕塑家的雕塑刀使用，用戶移動物體周圍的便攜式聚光燈在一個的捕獲會話產生的三維模型，因此我們長期的系統的光雕刻系統。相對於昂貴的激光掃描儀，只能獲得表面的幾何形狀，在有限的預算中，我們獲得了豐富的表面幾何形狀和反射鏡球，數碼攝像機，便攜式關注的焦點。 使用的幾何形狀和反射信息捕獲的同時，我們的渲染系統支持照片級真實感渲染的對象從小說不限於捕捉的觀點。高品質的數字化模型可應用於3D導航和電腦遊戲。 光雕具有較高的潛力，擴大規模生產高品質的大型和複雜的室外場景表面重建，從而改善目前的大型三維重建系統返回的稀疏或密集的準點集，或表面但在拍攝後的細節損失。

619112.label: Realisation of objectives
619112.value: 1. Fundamental research on geometry and reflectance capture We have built a light carving system consisting of a digital video camera and a chrome sphere on a small budget. The machine learning techniques we have adopted consist of the kernel basis functions where we have successfully derived the normal and BRDF estimation based on the captured images. Shadows have proved to be very problematic in reflectance capture when the normal and BRDF estimation assume no shadow corruption. In the CVPR 2014 paper (see research output), we present the first automatic method to remove shadows from single RGBD images. Using normal cues directly derived from depth, we can remove hard and soft shadows while preserving surface texture and shading. Our key assumption is that pixels with similar normals, spatial locations and chromaticity should have similar colors. A modified nonlocal matching is used to compute a shadow confidence map that localizes well hard shadow boundaries, thus hard and soft shadows can be handled within the same framework. We compare our results produced using state-of-the-art shadow removal on single RGB images, and intrinsic image decomposition on standard RGB-D datasets. 2. Adequate 3D reconstruction for high-quality rendering Our adequate 3D shape consists of shape-from-silhouette from the overlapping views of the target object, thus sidesteping tedious issues involved in conventional approaches which aim at fusing geometric and photometric stereo in multiview reconstruction, where even the the state-of the-art approaches still produce imperfect reconstructions. In the PAMI 2013 paper (see research output), we propose to apply the nonlocal principle to general alpha matting for the simultaneous extraction of multiple image layers; each layer may have disjoint as well as coherent segments typical of foreground mattes in natural image matting, thus providing silhouettes at subpixel accuracy. The estimated alphas also satisfy the summation constraint. As in nonlocal matting, our approach does not assume the local color-line model and does not require sophisticated sampling or learning strategies. On the other hand, our matting method generalizes well to any color or feature space in any dimensions, any number of alphas and layers at a pixel beyond two, and comes with an arguably simpler implementation which we have made publicly available. Our matting technique capitalizes on the nonlocal principle by using K nearest neighbors in matching nonlocal neighborhoods, and contributes a simple and fast algorithm that produces competitive results with sparse user markups. KNN matting has a closed-form solution that can leverage the preconditioned conjugate gradient method to produce an efficient implementation. Experimental evaluation on benchmark datasets indicates that our matting results are comparable to or of higher quality than state-of-the-art methods requiring more involved implementation. In this paper, we take the nonlocal principle beyond alpha estimation and extract overlapping image layers using the same Laplacian framework. Given the alpha value, our closed-form solution can be elegantly generalized to solve the multi-layer extraction problem. We perform qualitative and quantitative comparisons to demonstrate the accuracy of the extracted image layers. 3. Applications for high-resolution imagery to large-scale reconstruction With the successful achievement of the above objectives, we scale up our techniques developed to solve real-world reconstruction problems. Specifically, recall that in objective #1 the normal and BRDF estimation are based on the captured images. To apply them for 3D reconstruction of high-density downtown or urban areas, special attention must be given to building facades where glazing windows are transparent and highly reflective, which makes conventional computer vision algorithms invalid because almost all of them assume opaque surfaces. In the PAMI 2015 paper (see research output), we address the problem of reconstructing transparent objects. While producing reasonable results for complex objects, existing approaches require custom calibration or somewhat intensive labor to achieve high precision. When an overall shape preserving salient and fine details is sufficient, we show in this paper a significant step toward solving the problem when the object’s silhouette is available and simple user interaction is allowed, by using a video of a transparent object shot under varying illumination. Specifically, we estimate the normal map of the exterior surface of a given solid transparent object, from which the surface depth can be integrated. Our technical contribution lies in relating this normal estimation problem to one of graph-cut segmentation. Unlike conventional formulations, however, our graph is dual-layered, since we can see a transparent object’s foreground as well as its background. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations were performed to verify the efficacy of this practical solution.

619112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619112.value: With the techniques developed in this project, we are spearheading a new research direction which we will call "depth-aware shape-from-shading". The research focus of that project centers around normals and BRDF estimation from photos. The estimated geometry information can be combined with RGBD data produced by depth sensors. Similar to different modalities typical of medical imaging, RGB-D can benefit normals and BRDF estimation which in turn will improve RGBD sensing. We are currently formulating the mathematics of depth-aware shape-from-shading and collecting relevant data.

619112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619112.value: We produce a practical end-to-end system for the automatic acquisition of a high-quality digital model of a complex real-world object, complete with detailed geometry and reflectance information on the reconstructed three-dimensional surface geometry. Similar to a sculptor’s use of a carving knife, a user shines a portable spotlight around an object in a capture session to produce a 3D model thus we term our system the light carving system. As opposed to expensive laser scanners which only acquire surface geometry, we acquire rich surface geometry and reflectance on a ‘shoestring’ budget, using a mirror sphere, a digital video camera, and a portable spotlight. With geometry and reflectance information captured simultaneously, our rendering system supports photorealistic rendering of an object from novel, unseen viewpoints not limited to the capture viewpoints. The high-quality digital model can be applied in 3D navigation and computer gaming. Light carving can be scaled up to produce high-quality surface reconstructions of large-scale and complex outdoor scenes, thus improving current large-scale 3D reconstruction systems which return either a sparse or quasi-dense point set, or a surface but with details lost after capture.

619212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619212.value: 5-axis surface machining enjoys tremendous advantages over traditional 3-axis machining, including better tool accessibility, faster material removal rate, and much improved surface finishing quality. It is especially suitable for machining those high precision sculptured surfaces such as aircraft parts, turbine blades, impellers, propellers, jewelry, molds and dies, etc. Unfortunately current 5-axis machining systems still heavily depend on the user to plan an error-free tool path – there is currently not a single commercial 5-axis machining system available that can offer even limited functions in generating error-free tool paths without human involvement. This lack of automation has severely limited the potential usage of 5-axis machining and consequently results in the waste of expensive investment in 5-axis machines. One of the most challenging parts in automatic 5-axis toolpath generation is how to plan the tool orientations in the path. The minimum and also the most critical requirement in this planning is that the tool must not collide with the part surface itself as well as other obstacles (such as fixtures, tool holders, etc.) at any time. This global obstacle avoidance issue poses little difficulty in 3-axis machining since all the obstacles (except the linearly moving cutting tool) are static and well-known algebraic and computational geometry algorithms exist for determining an obstacles-free toolpath. In 5-axis machining, however, because of the rotation of the machine’s table or tool assembly, obstacles become non-static with respect to the part surface, which makes their analysis much more difficult. At present, in all the commercial 5-axis machining systems, global collision avoidance is achieved with intense human involvement through trial-and-error via computer simulation. We propose to conduct a comprehensive study of setup and tool orientation planning – particularly the global collision avoidance problem – in 5-axis machining. The study aims at untangling unknown algebraic properties of global obstacles in the 5-axis setting and developing efficient and practical algorithms for automatic identification of obstacle-free tool orientations. In addition, a new field-based covariant functional algorithm is proposed to compute the tool-axis that conforms to the identified obstacle-free orientation zone during the tool path generation. The new method also takes into account other tool-axis requirements, together with the obstacle-free zone requirement, to achieve a universal solution. The outcome will provide both a theoretical guideline and a practical solution for the much-needed automatic tool path generation in 5-axis machining, and can be immediately used by manufacturing companies allover the world. 相比傳統的三軸加工，五軸加工有著巨大的優勢，包括更大的可加工範圍，更高的材料去除率以及更好的表面加工品質。它尤其適用于加工那些高精密複雜曲面，如飛機零件，渦輪葉片，葉輪，螺旋槳，珠寶和模具等。但在目前，五軸加工刀具軌跡的生成仍然在很大程度上依賴于使用者的參與和判斷；目前的獨立的商業五軸加工系統還未能提供無需使用者參與的準確的刀具軌跡生成方案。這種缺乏自動性的特點嚴重地限制了五軸加工的應用前景，因而導致了對五軸機床昂貴投資的浪費。 在自動生成五軸刀具軌跡的過程中，其中最具挑戰的一個方面是刀具方位的規劃。在其中，一個最基本且最重要的要求是確保刀具在任意時間均不能與工件表面本身以及其他障礙物（如夾具和刀具架等）發碰撞。在三軸加工過程中，由於所有的障礙物（除直線運動的刀具）都是靜態的，並且在確定無干涉刀具路徑方面存在的成熟的代數和計算幾何算法，因此全域干涉避免問題在三軸加工中難度不大；但是在五軸加工過程中，由於機床的旋轉工作臺和刀具組合體的存在，導致障礙物相對於工件表面並非靜止，因此干涉的分析更加困難。目前，在所有的商業五軸加工系統裡，全域干涉避免是通過反復的電腦模擬和密集的人為參來實現的。 在本研究中，我們從全域干涉避免的要求出發，針對工件最優設置和刀具方位規劃進行研究。本研究旨在探求在全域避碰過程的工件設置的問題的代數特性以及開發出實際並有效的無干涉刀具方位的生成算法。在此，我們利用場基協變函數，在確保刀具方位在無干涉區間之內的要求下，對刀具軌跡進行規劃。該算法同時也考慮到了在加工過程中刀軸的其它限制，並結合無全域干涉要求，最終形成一個五軸刀具路徑規劃的通用的解決方案。 本研究的成果，將為五軸加工過程中急需的自動無干涉刀具規劃方法提供理論的指導和實用的解決方案，並能迅速為全世界的製造企業所用。

619212.label: Realisation of objectives
619212.value: All the four point-wise objectives have been achieved. Their realization are best represented and presented by the following publications: (1) Pengcheng Hu, Kai Tang, and Chen-Han Lee, “Global obstacle avoidance and minimum workpiece setups in five-axis machining”, Computer-Aided Design, Vol. 45, No. 10, pp. 1222-1237, 2013. (2) K. Zhang and Kai Tang, “An efficient greedy strategy for five-axis tool path generation on dense triangular mesh”, International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology, Vol. 74, Issue 9-12, pp. 1539-1550, Oct., 2014. (3) Li CHEN, Ke XU, and Kai Tang, “Collision-free tool orientation optimization in 5-axis machining of bladed blisk”, Journal of Computational Design and Engineering, Vol. 2, No. 4, pp. 167-205, Oct. 2015. (4) Ke Zhang and Kai Tang, “Optimal five-axis tool path generation algorithm based on double scalar fields for freeform surfaces”, International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology, Vol.83, No. 9, pp. 1503-1514, Apr. 2016. Traditionally in five-axis machining, when determining the tool orientations that are accessible to a point on a part surface, only static obstacles (i.e., only the part surface itself) are considered. In the presence of non-static obstacles such as fixtures and clamps on the machine table (which are not static with respect to the part surface depending on how it is set up on the machine table) and devices fixed in the space (which are dynamic even with respect to the rotation of the machine table), collision checking is performed by computer simulation on the fly and, if collision is found, a complete re-computation of the tool path is usually required. As a result, five-axis tool path computation has been a tedious and iterative process, requiring excessive human intervention. In this project, we have conducted a rigorous analysis of the algebraic structures of non-static obstacles in the five-axis machining environment and proposed efficient numerical representations for them. Based on these, we then have developed a practical algorithmic solution to the problem of finding a minimum set of workpiece setups for machining a free form surface on a five-axis machine, attending to both static and non-static obstacles. Not limited to the minimum workpiece setup problem, the mathematical models and algorithms developed in this project are expected to help fill a long-standing hole in five-axis machining: determining correct tool orientations at the stage of tool path planning beforehand rather than relying on computer simulation on the fly in the later stage.

619212.label: Major findings and research outcome
619212.value: (1) It is the first work to classify the obstacles in five-axis machining of freeform surfaces that cover both the fixed obstacles and moving obstacles on the rotary tables. (2) We found that through this careful classification, the dynamic visibility can be correctly established. (3) Based on the established dynamic visibility, we have developed an optimization algorithm that is able to find a near-minimum number of workpiece setups for five-axis machining of an arbitrary freeform surface.

619212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619212.value: Total machining time as well as the surface finish quality (which are both affected by the number of workpiece setups) are indeed important optimization objectives. In addition to these, we plan to explore the application of our results for Objective (4) to the minimization of consumption energy - machining a part will consume a large amount of electric energy and different workpiece setups and/or tool paths will require different amounts of electric energy. We want to find a particular workpiece and/or tool path that will minimize this amount.

619212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619212.value: A typical five-axis machine tool has three linear axes XYZ and two extra rotary axes A and B or A and C (depending on the configuration of the machine tool). When machining a complex-shaped part on a five-axis machine tool, as there are many types of obstacles such as fixtures and clamps (to fasten the workpiece), monitoring sensors/devices, etc., typically, the workpiece must be mounted and dismounted many times in order for the tool to be able to "see" every point on the part and machine it. Each mount is called a Workpiece Setup which defines a unique coordinate transformation between the geometry of the part and the machine tool's own coordinate system. Every mount/dismount is time-consuming and requires the machine tool to be re-calibrated. Moreover, the finished surface on the part between two different mounts always leaves a mark. Therefore, we want to minimize the number of workpiece setups (i.e., the mounts). In this work, we have developed an algorithm that automatically finds a near-minimum number of workpiece setups for an arbitrary complex-shaped part.

619312.value: 可持續性能源與存儲在智慧電網中的優化使用研究

619312.label: Project Objectives
619312.value: Optimal exploitation of renewable energy and impact of the volatility of renewable energy sources Exploiting renewable energy helps lower the marginal cost of energy provisioning. However, due to the volatility of renewable energy sources, exploitation of renewable energy introduces uncertainty in the energy supply, requiring realtime control to keep the grid stability with additional operation-cost. Considering these two aspects, we aim at establishing a framework to quantify this tradeoff between benefiting from renewable energy exploitation and controlling the associated cost due to its volatility. Based on this quantified tradeoff, we aim at determining the optimal exploitation of renewable energy. Furthermore, we aim at analyzing (i) how the volatility of renewable energy influences its optimal exploitation and the corresponding tradeoff and (ii) how the energy-users benefit from exploitation of renewable energy. Distributed/efficient algorithm(s) to achieve the optimal exploitation under the framework of supply-demand response Considering the limited computational capability of most household energy-management devices in smart grid, a further question is how to achieve the optimal exploitation of renewable energy in computational-efficiency/distributed way(s). Therefore, under the framework of supply-demand response, we aim at designing distributed/efficient algorithm(s) for energy-users and the intelligent controller to determine their energy demands and provisioning, respectively. In particular, in our proposed algorithm(s), energy-users and controller are able to adjust their demands and provisioning according to the system-state information that takes accounts of the volatility of renewable energy. Incorporation of energy storage and optimal policy for scheduling of renewable energy over time Through providing grid with additional flexibility in scheduling renewable energy collected over time, incorporation of energy storage has been considered as an effective way to mitigate the volatility of renewable energy. Therefore, we aim at determining the optimal policy for scheduling of renewable energy after incorporating of energy storage. We will further analyze the structural properties of this optimal policy, based on which we will quantify how the characteristics of energy storage (including capacity, charging/discharging efficiencies) influence the utilization of renewable energy and the benefit of energy-users. Distributed renewable energy generation and stable cooperation among energy-users A paradigm is that a large number of energy users are equipped with their own equipment to harvest and manage renewable energy, thus forming a distributed renewable energy generation system. We aim at characterizing how energy-users share their private renewable energy based on the cooperative model when energy-users agree to collaborate and based on the noncooperative model when energy-users fail to collaborate, respectively. Furthermore, we aim at quantifying the corresponding individual user welfare and the social welfare under different models. Specifically, collaboration among energy-users in sharing their private renewable energy yields a more efficient utilization of renewable energy, thus benefiting the social welfare of all users. However, some users may suffer from this collaboration due to their voluntary (and excessive) provisioning of energy, resulting in instability of cooperation. Therefore, we aim at designing a mechanism for stable cooperation such that all users self-incentively share their renewable energy.
