619312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619312.value: 智慧電網被認為是一個基於先進資訊與通信技術的、智慧化的電力生產、傳輸與分配網路。智慧電網的目標提高電網運行效率與穩定性、同時解決由於過度依賴于煤炭資源進行電力生產所造成的日益惡化經濟效益與環境問題。為了提高電網運行效率與穩定性，一種被廣泛認可的方案是智慧電網將通過電力生產與消費端雙向資料通信從而實現有效供給與需求回應控制。在供給與需求回應控制中，電能消費者可以獲得電網中能源供給的即時狀態資訊、並根據這個資訊調整它們的需求從而在電能使用的滿意程度與相應付出的代價之間達到一個最優平衡。從另一個角度，電能生產者則可以獲得電網中電能需求的即時狀態資訊、並根據這個資訊調整它們的供給從而避免因過度生產造成的浪費。于此同時，為了降低傳統採用煤炭資源進行電力生產的依賴並緩解由此造成的經濟與環境問題因素，大規模的可在再生能源利用將是智慧電網中的另一個關鍵技術。面對電能需求的快速增長，通過對可再生能源的廣泛利用（例如，太陽能、風能和地熱資源）實現向低碳化電能生產的轉變對未來智慧電網來說是必不可少關鍵技術。儘管可再生能源提供了一種更為廉價、清潔能量來源，它的使用卻對電網運作的穩定性提出了新的挑戰，這是因為絕大多數的可再生能源在生產過程中帶有很強的隨機性，而現有的預測技術往往不能夠即時地對可再生能源的產生進行精確預測。可再生能源的隨機性與有限的預測技術之間的矛盾要求智慧電網必須具有即時的緊急控制能力從而保證電網運行的可靠性。考慮到智慧電網的兩項關鍵技術，即有效的供給與需求回應管理和大規模的可再生能源利用，智慧電網中一個有待解決的關鍵問題是如何在供給與需求回應管理的模型下實現可再生能源與電能存儲介質的優化使用。具體而言，為了系統回答這個問題，本研究計畫對以下三個問題進行探索： （i）可再生能源的優化調度使用與其產生過程中隨機性影響； 如前所述，可再生能源調度使用中的一個關鍵時如何在以下兩個方面達到一個優化平衡，即通過利用廉價的可再生能源以有效降低在電能產生的邊際代價，和由可再生能源產生不確定性引起的、進行緊急控制所造成的額外電網運作代價。如何量化這兩者之間的平衡、同時確定最優的可再生能源調度將對於智慧電網將有非常重要的意義。在此基礎上，分析可再生能源產生過程中的隨機性對此優化平衡的影響以及相應電能用戶所獲得利益也將至關重要。 （ii）能源存儲介質的採用以及可再生能源在較長時間段內的優化調度策略； 總所周知，電能存儲介質的採用是一種緩解可再生能源產生過程中不確定的有效方式。在存儲介質存在的情況下，可再生能源在長時間段內的調度策略將發揮重要作用，因為一個有效的調度策略不僅要能夠滿足當前時隙內用戶電能需求、同時也必須要能夠滿足未來時隙內用戶的需求。於此同時，存儲介質的特性（例如，存儲容量和充放電效率）將對可再生能源的有效使用以及電能用戶所獲利益有重要的影響，因此也有必要對其進行深入的分析。 （iii）分散式可再生能源的產生和能量用戶間的穩定性協作機制； 未來智慧電網一個重要場景將是分散式能源產生系統，即大量電能使用者共存於一個網路，同時它們各自具有獨立的對可再生能源進行採集、管理與調度的設備，這就意味各個電能用戶都將扮演著電能消費者與供給者的雙重角色。在此分散式能源產生系統中，一個隨之而來的重要問題是：具有獨立電能產生能力的用戶如何共用其私有的可再生能源。為了回答這個問題，我們需要考慮兩種不同的模式：即使用者間的相互協作模式以及它們間的非協作模式。更進一步，在協作模式下的一個關鍵問題是如何設計一個有效的、穩定的協作機制。這個機制可以保證不同電能用戶將會自發且自願地共用其私有的可再生能源，從而達到整個網路的最優狀態。

619312.label: Realisation of objectives
619312.value: In this project, we had four objectives to achieve and have successfully completed all these four targeted objectives. Summary of the research outcome related to Objective 1: We established a cost-efficient demand-response framework equipped with a centralized renewable energy source to quantify the tradeoff between the system-wise benefit from renewable energy exploitation and controlling the associated cost due to the volatility of renewable energy generation. Based on this cost-efficient optimization framework, we determined the optimal exploitation level of renewable energy and the optimal energy scheduling decisions of the energy users/energy providers. By further using the aforementioned optimal solutions, we analyzed how the volatility of renewable energy influenced its optimal exploitation level as well as the benefits of energy users. Specifically, by using the principle of first order stochastic dominance, we showed that a stochastically larger renewable energy yielded a deeper penetration of renewable energy utilization in energy provisioning. Consequently, the energy users benefit from a deeper penetration of renewable energy, since this helps lower the marginal cost of energy provisioning. In summary, Objective 1 of this project has been fully achieved. Summary of the research outcome related to Objective 2: Based on the cost-efficient demand-response framework incorporating a volatile renewable energy source, we designed efficient and distributed algorithms for energy users and an intelligent controller to determine their energy demands and the energy provisioning decisions, respectively. Specifically, to tackle the nonconvexity of the cost-efficient optimization framework, we first proposed a polyblock approximation-based algorithm to determine the optimal utilization of renewable energy by exploiting the special monotonic structure. Our algorithm achieves close-to-optimal performance but requires a significantly reduced computational complexity in comparison with the exhaustive search approach. Furthermore, we considered a group of specialized (yet practical) load-shedding cost functions, based on which we convexified the energy cost-efficient optimization problem and provided sufficient conditions for optimality. Using the optimality condition, we proposed a distributed algorithm to determine the optimal utilization of renewable energy and the corresponding optimal energy scheduling decisions. Specifically, the distributed algorithm relies on the supply-demand response and coordinates the energy provisioning problem and the energy supply problem systematically by using the virtual price, a system-wide state information, that takes account of the volatility of renewable energy. In summary, Objective 2 of this project has been achieved. Summary of the research outcome related to Objective 3: The incorporation of energy storage (the battery is our key interest) into the demand response mechanism may couple all the decisions within the total finite time horizon, which poses the the problem of computation as a further challenge on top of the non-convexity problem in Objective 2. In detail, we first aimed to quantify the economic value of a lifetime-constrained battery energy storage system (BESS) operated by a consumer who faces fluctuating electricity prices. We defined the lifetime of the BESS as the serving duration within which the BESS capacity remains above a certain threshold of its initial capacity and define the value of the BESS as the total arbitrage value within its entire lifetime. We showed that when the fluctuating electricity price is assumed to be known by the BESS operator, the total economic value of the BESS can be calculated using iterative linear programming. Furthermore, when the price information remains unknown, finding the optimal economic value of lifetime-constrained BESS has been proven to be a stochastic shortest path problem, and the optimal policy presents the property of a threshold structure. To overcome the problem of dimensionality, we proposed a structure-based aggregation method, i.e., Layer-and-Group, to construct optimal trading policies. The elegance of this approach lies in its circumventing of the need for exhausted value iteration over the entire state space. Instead, the approach works in a hierarchical and parallel fashion, thus significantly speeding up convergence to the optimality. Extensive experimental results showed that this approach can dramatically reduce computational complexity, thus contributing to the computationally tractable optimality without requiring any approximation. We validated our proposed model and algorithm via real battery specifications and electricity market data, and the results showed promising insights for both infrastructure planning and operational management of BESSs in practice. In summary, Objective 3 of this project has been achieved (100%). Summary of the research outcome related to Objective 4: We investigated the cooperative distributed energy generation and energy trading for a future smart grid. We proposed a model in which a group of energy-users, who were equipped with the capabilities of distributed energy generation, were allowed to trade energy in a cooperative manner with the goal of minimizing their total energy provisioning cost while meeting each individual energy user’ s local energy demand. In particular, in our model, each energy user expects to benefit from the cooperative energy generation and trading with the other energy users. We adopted the Nash bargaining game (a cooperative game theoretic model) to formulate this optimization model. Based on the formulated Nash bargaining game, we first jointly determined the optimal energy scheduling decisions (including both the distributed energy generation levels and the trading decisions) for all energy users such that their total energy provisioning cost can be minimized. Then, based on the optimal energy scheduling decisions, we further determined the optimal transaction costs associated with the energy users’ energy trading to ensure that each of them can positively benefit from the cooperation. Furthermore, focusing on Objective 4, we proposed a novel framework of a hybrid energy trading market, in which energy users are connected not only to traditional energy retailers (e.g., the utility companies) but also to local energy networks for bidirectional energy trading opportunities. The existence of local energy market provides new opportunities for energy users and distributed energy sellers to perform the local energy trading in a cooperative manner such that they can all benefit and the utilization efficiency of local distributed energy can be significantly improved. Based on the framework of a hybrid energy trading market, we first quantified the respective benefits of the energy users and distributed energy providers (or energy sellers) from local trading and then investigated how they can optimize their benefits by controlling their energy scheduling in response to the signaling from the local energy trading market. In particular, we investigated two different types of local energy trading market: namely, i) nonprofit-oriented local trading markets, which solely aim to benefit energy users and distributed energy sellers, and ii) profit-oriented local trading markets, which aim to maximize their (i.e., a third-party owner) profit while guaranteeing the required benefit for energy users and distributed energy sellers. For each type of local trading market, we formulated a corresponding optimal trading problem and proposed algorithms to efficiently determine the optimal signaling (i.e., pricing) of local trading market as well as each energy user and distributed energy seller’s optimal energy scheduling. Finally, we formulated extensive numerical examples to evaluate and validate the benefits of the hybrid energy trading market and the performance of the proposed algorithms. In summary, Objective 4 of this project has been achieved. (100%).

Furthermore, we aim at quantifying the corresponding individual user welfare and the social welfare under different models. Specifically, collaboration among energy-users in sharing their private renewable energy yields a more efficient utilization of renewable energy, thus benefiting the social welfare of all users. However, some users may suffer from this collaboration due to their voluntary (and excessive) provisioning of energy, resulting in instability of cooperation. Therefore, we aim at designing a mechanism for stable cooperation such that all users self-incentively share their renewable energy.

619312.label: Major findings and research outcome
619312.value: We achieve the following four major findings: 1. Framework and Analysis for an Optimal Exploitation of Renewable Energy Considering the importance of integrating renewable energy supply in a future smart grid, our proposed cost-efficient demand-response framework can realize an optimal exploitation of renewable energy that achieves the best tradeoff between the system-wide benefit from renewable energy exploitation and associated costs due to the volatility of renewable energy generation. Our analysis validated the hypothesis that a stochastically larger renewable energy yielded a deeper penetration of renewable energy utilization in energy provisioning, which can consequently benefit energy users. 2. Algorithm Designs to Optimize Exploitation of Renewable Energy The realisation of an optimal exploitation of renewable energy necessitates solving multiple-stage stochastic optimization problems, which are usually nonconvex and thus challenging to solve. Nevertheless, our proposed polyblock approximation-based algorithm successfully tackles this difficulty and efficiently achieves an optimal utilization of renewable energy. Based on a mild assumption of the load-shedding cost function, we further propose a distributed algorithm to determine the optimal utilization of renewable energy and the corresponding optimal energy scheduling decisions. Our proposed distributed algorithm exploits the supply-demand response and coordinates the energy provisioning problem and the energy supply problem systematically by using the virtual price that takes account of the volatility of renewable energy. 3. Important Role of Energy Storage Systems and the Optimal Scheduling of Renewable Energy Energy storage systems play an important role in exploiting renewable energy by helping to mitigate the intermittency of renewable energy generation. Facilitated by an energy storage system, our proposed optimal energy scheduling algorithm takes the battery capacity, charging and discharging power rating and efficiency, lifetime, and capacity decaying into consideration. Various practical system implementation insights have been identified, including the threshold-structured policy and the tradeoff between aggressiveness and conservativeness in operating the battery. 4. Cooperative and Stable Sharing Schemes of Distributed Energy Generation Our proposed scheme for cooperative and stable sharing of distributed energy generation can effectively minimize the total energy provisioning cost for all energy users while meeting each individual energy user's local energy demand. In particular, based on the Nash Bargaining model, our proposed optimal transaction costs associated with users' energy trading ensure that each user can positively benefit from the cooperation. Our proposed novel framework of a hybrid energy trading market allows energy users and distributed energy sellers to flexibly trade with traditional energy retailers as well as with local energy networks for bidirectional energy trading opportunities.

619312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619312.value: We plan to extend the proposed hybrid energy trading market to capture the case of multiple coexisting and self-interested local trading markets. The strategic interactions between different self-interested local trading markets will influence the performance of the energy sharing/trading between energy users and distributed/renewable energy sellers and thus influence the overall utilization of renewable energy and the efficiency of energy trading. In particular, we plan to model the strategic interactions between different self-interested local trading markets into two manners, namely strategic cooperative, and selfish noncooperative. In both cases, we will propose efficient schemes to achieve an equilibrium state among different local trading markets and evaluate their performance, including the degree of distributed energy utilization and the efficiency of local hybrid energy trading. In addition, we also plan to further investigate secrecy and privacy issues in the trading and sharing of distributed energy generation. Since the behaviors of energy trading and sharing reveal private information about energy users and distributed energy providers (or sellers), it is a crucial issue regarding how to effectively protect the privacy of energy users and sellers (e.g., by proposing some privacy-preserving schemes) while nevertheless improving the efficiency of trading and sharing distributed renewable energy.

619312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619312.value: The project investigates the optimal exploitation of renewable energy in smart grids. An optimal exploitation solution provides a benchmark regarding how to make best use of renewable energy to reduce conventional carbon-based energy consumption while effectively controlling adverse impacts due to the intermittence of renewable energy generation. To facilitate the optimization of the exploitation of renewable energy, the project further proposes efficient yet practically affordable algorithms to achieve an optimal exploitation solution. The project also investigates the use of energy storage systems and proposes efficient energy scheduling schemes (to charge/discharge energy storage) to optimize economic operations. Finally, the project investigates the optimal cooperative energy trading and sharing for renewable energy utilization in smart grids. The proposed cooperative sharing schemes shed light on the significant benefits of cooperative sharing distributed energy between energy users and distributed energy sellers. The project also proposes a novel framework for a hybrid energy trading market comprised of a utility market and local energy trading market. The hybrid energy trading market provides more flexible and efficient bidirectional energy trading and sharing between energy users and distributed energy sellers and can significantly improve the utilization of distributed energy and benefit both energy users and sellers.

619612.label: Project Objectives
619612.value: Multivariate categorical customer data monitoring: Categorical data such as customer survey and service ratings contain important information from customers' perspective, and should be monitored to assure high service quality. We will focus on the real-time monitoring of categorical data streams that are both cross-correlated and autocorrelated. Multivariate nonparametric service operation monitoring: Targeting the unique characteristics of service operations, where non-normal data are prevalent, multivariate nonparametric monitoring methods for high-dimensional data will be developed to detect changes in service operations in a real-time manner. Profile monitoring of service system relationships: Profiles refer to the functional relationships between the system inputs and the system outputs, which are more complex than the input or output data themselves. We will propose methods to detect and diagnose deviations of such relationships in the service environment.

619612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619612.value: The service industry has become increasingly important in our daily lives and global economies. Reducing service costs and improving service quality will have a significant social and economical impact. In addition, with the development of information technology, the massive amount of data readily available provides us with opportunities to integrate advanced statistical methodologies with system knowledge to better understand, model, and control the quality of service systems. Monitoring, surveillance, and quick detection of abnormal activities have become critical in a variety of service industries that have complex operation systems and process huge amounts of data. Most conventional statistical process control techniques cannot effectively handle the monitoring and surveillance of such a large amount of data on a real-time basis. The proposed research project focuses on developing statistical monitoring and control methodologies for service processes. This involves three fundamental issues: (1) the monitoring of feedback data arising from customers' perception of service quality; (2) the monitoring and controlling metrics of operational performance in service systems; and (3) the monitoring of the functional relationship between operational determinants and the service quality perceived by end customers. The central idea of the proposed research is to develop methodologies to achieve efficient monitoring and reduce variability in service systems. The tasks will be carried out with reference to service processes where data and process knowledge are available. 在我們的日常生活和全球經濟中，服務業已經成為越來越重要的。降低服務成本，提高服務質量將有一個顯著的社會和經濟影響。此外，隨著信息技術的發展，大量的數據隨時可用為我們提供機會集成先進的統計方法與系統知識，以更好地理解，模型和控制服務系統的質量。監測，監視和快速檢測異常活動已經成為各種有複雜操作的服務行業中的關鍵。大多數傳統的統計過程控制技術不能有效地處理這麼大的數據量的實時監測和監督。此研究項目的重點是發展服務流程的統計監測和控制方法。這涉及到三個基本問題：（1）從客戶感知的服務質量監測所產生的反饋數據;（2）監測和控制服務系統的經營業績指標;和（3）對於服務系統的經營指標和客戶服務質量感知之間的函數關係進行監測。

619612.label: Realisation of objectives
619612.value: Categorical data such as customer survey and service ratings contain important information from customers' perspective, and should be monitored to ensure high service quality. We have focused on multivariate categorical data monitoring, and the results have been fruitful. We have published four journal papers on this topic (Li et al., 2014, Li et al., 2014, Shang et al., 2014, Ding et al., 2015). These papers consider both cross-correlated and autocorrelated categorical data monitoring. Targeting the unique characteristics of service operations, where non-normal data are prevalent, multivariate nonparametric monitoring methods for high-dimensional data have been developed. In particular, a general framework for monitoring complex processes with both in-control and out-of-control information using nonparametric techniques has been developed (Liu et al., 2014, Zhang et al., 2015). Finally, we have developed several approaches to monitor the complex relationships in a service process, including monitoring complex networks (Han et al., 2015, Han and Tsung, 2014), monitorng spatial structures (Wang et al., 2014), and the covariance structure between process variables (Shen et al., 2014).

619612.value: We have generated rich research outcomes for all three objectives. In particular, we have made extensive effort on the real-time monitoring of categorical and mixed-type data streams in a service environment (Li et al., 2014, Li et al., 2014, Ding et al., 2015). For example, an efficient LASSO-based monitorng and diagnosis scheme has been developed that can be used for a multistage service process with binary data (Shang et al., 2014). We have also provided novel solutions with several control schemes using nonparametric techniques (Liu et al., 2014, Zhang et al., 2015). In addition, we have developed a control scheme for financial network monitoring with the focus on detecting and diagnosing distribution changes of degree ratio in complex financial networks (Han et al., 2015, Han and Tsung, 2014). We have published 10 journal papers, mostly in leading journals, and one conference paper. We have also trained one PhD student during the period. We have also been invited to present the research results at several international conferences (e.g., INFORMS).

619612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619612.value: Statistical process monitoring and control in a service environment is a broad problem and has great potential for future research. Our research development may not be limited to categorical data monitoring, nonparametric techniques, and profile monitoring schemes. Based on the research outcomes of this project, we will tackle this research further. We will go beyond a conventional service process to focus on a complex service process with big data streams. Technical challenges include the fusion of different forms and heterogeneous sources of data in a service environment. We have several working papers in preparation and also expect to present our new research ideas and results at various international conferences in the near future.

619712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619712.value: Hong Kong is a coast urban city with about 7 million inhabitants. Its sustainable development relies on various hydro-infrastructural systems, such as urban drainage and flood control systems, protecting the city from natural hazards many of which are related to hydrological extremes (e.g., rainfalls, floods, storm surges). Hydrometric data provide basic information needed to support various types of activities dealing with hydrosystem issues involving design, operation, planning, management, and performance assessments. The use of proper data analysis techniques is essential so that useful information with desired quality and accuracy can be extracted and/or synthesized for intended purpose. In the design of hydro-infrastructural systems for urban drainage or inland/coastal flood defense, data on extreme rainfalls, floods, and sea levels are required. These data are generally collected at selected gauging locations over a period of time. More often than not, the data record lengths are not sufficiently long to allow accurate estimations of the design event of desired return period or sometimes the study site is ungauged with no data available. In Hong Kong, with the exception of the Hong Kong Observatory, a great majority of the raingauges have record lengths of 10 years or shorter with some in the 20s, and many drainage and flood defense infrastructural systems in the territory are designed for rainfall events with a return period of 50 years or longer, especially in urban areas. Consequently, there exists a significant amount of uncertainty associated with the extrapolation beyond the at-site data range rendering estimation highly unreliable. Nevertheless, the occurrences of extreme hydrologic events are generally regional phenomena by nature which implies a certain degree of areal-wide similarity and continuity. Hydrologic regionalization is a class of data analysis techniques that take advantage of and utilize the similarities in extreme hydrologic events to pool data from different sites to enhance estimation reliability and/or to transfer information from gauged sites to ungauged locations where the data information is needed but unavailable. The aim of this proposed study is to review, investigate, and apply suitable regionalization techniques to establish reliable magnitude-frequency relationships of extreme rainfalls and sea level statistics in Hong Kong so that various hydro-infrastructural systems for mitigating water-related hazards in the territory can be designed and evaluated by properly considering tradeoff between risks, benefits, and costs of the systems. Hong Kong is a coast urban city with about 7 million inhabitants. Its sustainable development relies on various hydro-infrastructural systems, such as urban drainage and flood control systems, protecting the city from natural hazards many of which are related to hydrological extremes (e.g., rainfalls, floods, storm surges). Hydrometric data provide basic information needed to support various types of activities dealing with hydrosystem issues involving design, operation, planning, management, and performance assessments. The use of proper data analysis techniques is essential so that useful information with desired quality and accuracy can be extracted and/or synthesized for intended purpose. These data are generally collected at selected gauging locations over a period of time. 620512.value: Analyzing and modeling the complex temporal and spatial behaviors of soft errors at system level: We will systematically analyze and model the complex system-level soft error behaviors and impacts on different embedded application types and runtime status, their temporal and spatial characteristics, the interactions of multiple overlapped soft errors, and their effects on different MPSoC configurations. The protocols will coordinate hardware-software cooperation on soft error detection, report, and mitigation. A scalable low-overhead system architecture will be developed to effectively execute and adjust the adaptive hardware-software collaboration protocols for MPSoCs with a growing number of processing units and memories. In the second stage, the statically optimized task schedule will be adjusted at runtime, and checking points will be fine-tuned based on soft error conditions, application runtime status, and MPSoC usage scenarios. 620512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620512.value: All walks of human life have become increasingly dependent on embedded systems such as cellphones, digital video cameras, Internet routers, and wireless base stations. As the complexity and versatility of embedded applications burgeon, multiprocessor system-on-chip (MPSoC) has become an attractive platform for embedded systems, because integrating a system or a complex subsystem on a single chip with multiple processing units provides better performance and energy efficiency and lower cost per function. The advancement of nanotechnologies and three-dimensional integration technologies will help to sustain this trend. While these technologies enable MPSoCs to integrate a growing number of processing units and memories, they also make MPSoCs more susceptible to high-energy particles and electromagnetic interference. Those transient threats often manifest themselves as soft errors and can severely compromise system reliability. For instance, high-energy particles or electromagnetic interference can cause state inversions in electronic circuits, unnoticed by the system or users. This type of silent data corruption will result in unpleasant user experiences or even serious danger, and it is a challenging issue in embedded system design. Traditional soft error tolerant methods dramatically increase MPSoC cost and reduce the performance and energy efficiency due to significant protection overheads. This greatly limits the scalability and flexibility of MPSoCs in embedded systems. The root of this problem is that the traditional methods rely on rigorous but inflexible protections against transient soft errors. They are often designed for worst cases. However, worst cases only account for a small portion of the total MPSoC runtime. Furthermore, it has become increasingly difficult to determine the exact scales and impact ranges of soft errors at design time due to the burgeoning complexity of MPSoC designs and broad usage scenarios of embedded systems. These difficulties have eroded the foundation of traditional soft error tolerant methods. This project aims to systematically develop a hardware-software collaborated protection method and corresponding scalable low-overhead architecture to adaptively mitigate soft errors at runtime. The new protection method will dynamically detect, report, and adaptively mitigate soft errors through hardware-software collaborations under variable interference conditions, application runtime status, and MPSoC usage scenarios. Preliminary results show that the adaptive hardware-software collaborated protection method can improve MPSoC reliability with significantly lower overheads than traditional methods. This project will substantially extend our initial work along many new dimensions.

620712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620712.value: With increasing auto demands, efficient parking management is by no means less important than road traffic congestion control. This is due to shortages of parking spaces within the limited land areas of the city centers in many metropolises. The parking problem becomes an integrated part of traffic planning and management, which is particularly true in Hong Kong due to its high density of traffic and limited road and parking capacity. Traditionally, road traffic congestion and downtown parking problems have been considered separately in most studies in the literature. Only recently have they been investigated jointly in the context of the morning commute, but only to a limited extent. It is a fact that morning commuters often choose their departure times not only to trade off bottleneck congestion and schedule delays, but also in order to secure a parking spot due to limited parking spaces. It is the combination of these two problems that governs the commuters’ departure time choices. Analysis of such a combined problem is new and challenging; particularly when some commuters have reserved parking spots or parking permits and other commuters have to compete for public parking spots on a first-come-first-served basis. This project proposes to investigate the above morning commute problem with both bottleneck congestion and parking space constraints that is prevalent in reality but largely ignored in the literature. The first part of the project will investigate the equilibrium departure time choices and system efficiency for the morning commute in the presence of two classes of commuters: those with and those without a parking permit. The second part will investigate strategies to mitigate the commuting inefficiency of departing early or late arising from both competition for parking spots and bottleneck queuing delays. Tradable parking permits, together with time-varying bottleneck congestion charges and/or parking fees will be considered. The third part will extend the analysis from a single bottleneck to a more general many-to-one network. This extension becomes more complicated but more interesting when competition and interaction exist not only among commuters with or without a parking permit, but also among commuters from different origins or residential locations. The proposed research problem is of great importance. Apart from contributing to the evolving integrated concepts of traffic congestion control and parking demand management, the present project will have the potential to improve our understanding and modeling of the morning commute problem beyond the conventional pure bottleneck models. 隨著汽車需求的日益增加，在可用土地面積有限、停車位緊缺的城市中心區對機動車停放進行有效的管理變得越來越重要，其重要性有時甚至超過了對交通擁堵的控制。在這樣的背景下，停車的管理問題已經成為整個交通規劃和管理中的一個重要環節。在香港，由於其高密度的交通，有限的道路通行能力以及中心區域受限的停車場容量，上述的問題體現得更加明顯。 在以往的研究中，道路交通擁堵和市中心的停車問題往往被隔離成兩個問題單獨進行考慮。直到最近才有一些研究圍繞早高峰出行問題，在有限的範圍內將這兩個擁堵和停車聯合起來進行考慮。由於市中心停車位有限，早高峰出行的人群在選擇他們的出行時間時候，不僅要考慮道路擁堵和到達是否準時，同時也要考慮到能夠找到停車位。正是這些因素同時作用決定了早高峰出行人群的出行時間選擇，而將這些因素結合起來對早高峰出行現象進行分析是具有創新性和挑戰性的。特別是當我們考慮一部分出行人群已有預留的停車位或停車許可證，其他人群則需要基於先到先得機製而競爭公共停車位。 本課題將會對上述基於瓶頸模型，同時停車位緊缺的早高峰出行問題進行研究。課題所關注的內容在現實生活中是非常實際和普遍的，但相應的研究確十分有限，因此本課題的研究必要性是顯而易見的。課題的第一部分將探討在一部分出行人群已有預留的停車位或停車許可證，其他人群則需要競爭公共停車位的情況下，早高峰出行人群出行時間的選擇以及整個交通系統的效率。第二部分將提出並探討能夠有效減少由於競爭停車位以及瓶頸擁堵所造成的交通系統效率損失的措施及策略。其中將著重討論可交易停車許可證機制、動態的擁擠收費以及停車費。課題的第三部分會將之前基於單一瓶頸的分析拓展到更一般的“多到一”網絡。在“多到一”網絡中，早高峰出行者之間競爭和互動變得更為複雜而且有趣，這是因為其不僅涉及到出行者是否擁有預留的停車位，同時涉及到出行者的出發地點。 以上所提出的研究有其獨特的重要性和實際意義，其不僅將會促進對交通擁堵控制和停車需求管理進行綜合考慮這一概念的發展，同時將有可能發展和提高我們對於早高峰出行問題基於傳統瓶頸模型已有的認識。

620712.label: Realisation of objectives
620712.value: Throughout the three and half years research period; we were able to investigate all the study issues raised originally in the proposal. All aspects of the morning commute problem with bottleneck congestion and parking space constraints in the original proposal were addressed. Parking in downtown areas is often a headache for both commuters and traffic managers in most large cities. The problem cannot be solved simply by continuing the construction of new parking facilities due to growing population and car ownership. Thus, the management of parking supply and demand should be considered as an integrated part of urban and transportation systems planning. This is particularly vital in Hong Kong due to its high density of traffic and limited road and parking capacity. However, road traffic congestion and downtown parking problems have often been tackled separately in most previous studies in the literature. The morning commute problem is in general subject to both bottleneck traffic congestion and downtown parking capacity constraints. It is a fact that morning commuters often choose their departure times not only to trade off bottleneck congestion and schedule delays, but also in order to secure a parking spot due to limited parking spaces. It is the combination of the two problems that governs the commuters’ equilibrium departure time choices during the morning commuting. The integrated problem becomes more intriguing and challenging when some commuters have reserved parking spots or parking permits and other commuters have to compete for public parking spots on a first-come-first-served basis, which is the case in most large cities. In this case, the two classes of commuters prefer to choose departure times differently; specifically, commuters without a parking permit are compelled to depart from home earlier due to competition for a limited number of downtown parking spots. As a result, traffic congestion at the bottleneck would be likely to be smoothed out over time. It is thus of immense interest to know whether or not, and to what extent, the system performance in this case can be better in comparison with the two (extreme) cases examined in the literature, namely, the case when all commuters are subject to bounded parking space constraints and the standard bottleneck model case that does not account for parking space constraints. This project investigated the above morning commute problem with both bottleneck congestion and parking space constraints that is prevalent in reality. Apart from contribution to the evolving integrated concepts of traffic congestion control and parking demand management, the research findings improved our fundamental analysis and understanding of the morning commute problem beyond the conventional pure bottleneck models.

620712.label: Major findings and research outcome
620712.value: Departure time choice problem for the morning commute is formulated in the presence of two classes of commuters: those with and those without a parking permit or a reserved parking spot. It is found that departure pattern exhibits quite different characteristics from the standard bottleneck model without considering parking space constraint. Particularly, it is observed that the two classes of commuters prefer to choose different departure times; because commuters without a parking permit are compelled to depart from home earlier due to competition for a limited number of parking spots. As a result, traffic congestion at the bottleneck can be smoothed out over time. Publication: Yang, H., Liu, W., Wang, X.L. and Zhang X.N. Efficient strategies are developed by introducing a parking reservation scheme with expiration times, where commuters with a parking reservation have to arrive at parking spaces for the reservation before a predetermined expiration time. It is shown that if all parking reservations have the same expiration time, it is socially preferable to set the reservations to be non-expirable, i.e., without expiration time. If differentiated expiration times are properly designed, the total travel cost can be further reduced as compared with the reservation scheme without expiration time Publication: Liu, W., Yang, H., Yin, Y. In the case the commuting equilibrium problem of both mode and departure time choices in a bi-modal (auto and public transit) many-to-one network, it is found that parking reservation can help reduce deadweight loss and assigning more reservations to travelers from a specific origin does not necessarily reduce total travel cost of them, while doing so might raise the total travel cost of travelers from other origins. When parking supply is less than the potential demand but is relatively large, it is socially preferred to retain some parking spaces open for competition. However, when the total parking supply is relatively small, all parking spaces should be reserved to travelers. In the case of a bi-modal network, the so-called Downs–Thomson paradox may occur when transit authority have different economic objectives (profit-maximizing or breakeven) and operating schemes (frequency, fare, or both frequency and fare). For various combinations of economic objectives and operating schemes, the conditions for occurrence of the Downs–Thomson Paradox are established. It is shown that the paradox never occurs when transit authority is profit-maximizing, but it is inevitable when the transit authority is running to maximize travelers’ utility while maintaining breakeven. 620712.value: Through the study, we gained a better command of the analytical economic and traffic approach to tackling the various morning commute problem with bottleneck congestion and parking space constraint. We found that the methodology that we developed can be further extended to deal with the morning commute problem with both household and individual travels. 620712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
620712.value: With increasing auto demands, efficient parking management is by no means less important than road traffic congestion control. This is due to shortages of parking spaces within the limited land areas of the city centers in many metropolises. The parking problem becomes an integrated part of traffic planning and management, which is particularly true in Hong Kong due to its high density of traffic and limited road and parking capacity. This project investigates the morning commute problem with both bottleneck congestion and parking space constraints that is prevalent in reality but largely ignored in the literature. The equilibrium departure time choices and system efficiency for the morning commute are examined in the presence of two classes of commuters: those with and those without a parking permit. Various strategies for mitigating the commuting inefficiency are sought by introducing tradable parking permits, together with time-varying bottleneck congestion charges and/or parking fees. The research results contribute to the evolving integrated concepts of traffic congestion control and parking demand management. The research findings help improve our understanding and modeling of the morning commute problem beyond the conventional pure bottleneck models.

620812.label: Project Objectives
620812.value: [Objective 1: Query Formulation for Exploring Open Information Sources] For the online stage, when given a new learning task, we will design new methods to generate queries for retrieving the related source data from an open information source, such as the Web, Wikipedia, Open Directory Projects, etc. We plan to formulate an information gain based criterion to generate the queries while trying to reduce the number of consulted queries to a minimum. Another issue is how to compile the retrieved data in the form of models to store in a knowledge library, for transfer learning with the target task, and for later reuse. [Objective 2: Unify Heterogeneous Knowledge and Create a Knowledge Library] Our second objective is to derive effective and efficient transfer learning methods based on the models and knowledge stored in the knowledge library. The challenge is to handle the heterogeneity, noise and inconsistency of the models and data stored in the library when adding new models to the library. We need to find a way to relate the different data and data labels to the target learning task. A related task is to ensure that these algorithms are highly scalable. [Objective 3: Knowledge Transfer from Data in the Knowledge Library] In the third objective, we solve the target learning problem by using the models added and stored in the knowledge library. We need to design a unified model to make the learning models compatible with different forms of knowledge found in the knowledge library. A requirement is that in the prediction phase, we need to design efficient methods for unifying the diverse range of models we may find from the library, without scanning a huge amount of source knowledge in the library. [Objective 4: Develop and Evaluate Prototype SFTL System] We will develop a scalable prototype system for source-free transfer learning for text classification based on scalable distributed algorithms, and evaluate the developed framework and system on real-world text classification tasks. We will disseminate the research results in the form of high-quality publications, and make the prototype system and algorithms available in an open source manner.

620812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620812.value: Transfer learning is a machine learning process that adapts and reuses knowledge gained from solving different but related problems when solving new problems. It is gaining increasing popularity in diverse application domains, ranging from Web search to recommendation systems. A challenge in the application of transfer learning is how to identify one or more proper source domains to transfer the knowledge from. In the past, source domains are often specified by humans, but selecting the right source domains has been difficult. In this project, we propose a novel transfer-learning framework that requires no specific source data be given; instead, the system can find the sources to use as auxiliary data for transfer learning. This is done by searching on the World Wide Web (WWW) and other resources for data that can be beneficial to a given target learning task. In our approach, known as source-free transfer learning (SFTL), we are given a target task set to learn, where the training data may have an insufficient amount of labeled data only. To build a model, SFTL turns to some very large, open information sources for help by retrieving parts of the open data as sources and automatically transferring their knowledge. In our preliminary feasibility study [52], we have tested an idea of selecting the source data from the Wikipedia website to assist several text-categorization tasks. When we open up to Web scale, we face two new problems. First, we need to address how to automatically generate target-task related queries to find the “right” source data. Second, once the source data are found, we need to know how to calibrate and unify these heterogeneous data sources to enable effective transfer learning. We also need need to design a mechanism to acquire the right distance functions for these data and models. Compared to previous works on transfer learning, the SFTL framework has a major advantage from its source-free nature: users of a learning task no longer need to find the necessary source data to start learning. Another advantage is scalability: unlike many previous transfer learning approaches, which are difficult to scale up to the WWW scale knowledge transfer, our approach would be highly scalable both for the training and the prediction stage. We will use extensive real-world data to carry out this research to develop and evaluate a prototype system in a variety of text classification applications. 在機器學習領域中，遷移學習的優勢體現在，即使數據分布以及特征空間不一致都能夠調整並重復利用輔助領域的知識來幫助目標領域的學習。這一優勢已被用於解決多種不同的實際問題，例如互聯網搜索以及協同過濾技術。然而，在應用過程中它所面臨的一個重要問題是需要指定一個或多個輔助領域以用於知識遷移。這也成為遷移學習在實際應用中的瓶頸，很多研究工作提出的解決方案是請專家人工挑選這些輔助領域。本項目中，我們提出一個全新的遷移學習框架：它不需要人工挑選輔助領域，而是由系統自動選擇適合目標領域學習的數據源。借助在互聯網中進行大規模搜索所獲取的結果，我們抽取有益於目標領域學習的數據來完成這一項技術。這個新的框架我們稱之為免源遷移學習。假設存在這樣的場景，給定的目標任務中只有非常少量的標註數據，完全不足以完成訓練模型的任務。免源遷移學習通過向大規模的開放數據源，例如互聯網，索取部分知識作為可用的輔助數據建立模型。在我們過去的研究中[52]，驗證了從維基百科中選擇輔助領域數據幫助文本分類的可行性。但是，當我們將此應用轉移到互聯網規模的數據源時，存在兩個問題亟待解決。首先，海量的互聯網數據如何自動地產生任務相關的查詢語句去尋求合適的輔助領域數據將變成一個極大的挑戰。其次，即使找到了合適的輔助領域數據，如何統一這些多模態的數據源並遷移到目標數據，用於進行有效地學習，也是一個尚未解決的問題。此時，我們需要設計一個全新的機制去正確度量這些數據、模型與目標領域之間的關系。其次，我們還需要采取不同的選擇策略去有效並快速地整合這些數據以解決目標領域學習問題，特別是在海量數據的情況下。 相比當前的遷移學習的研究工作，免源遷移學習具備一個非常大的優勢：能夠在應用遷移學習框架選擇輔助領域數據的時候節省人工成本，因為它完全實現了自動化選擇。另一個優勢是其可擴展性：較當前的遷移學習方法有所不同，免源遷移學習能夠在模型訓練以及模型預測階段都達到互聯網規模的知識遷移。我們將用大量的實際數據進行這項研究，開發並評估一個可擴展的原型系統，把免源遷移學習應用到多個不同的文本分類任務中。

620812.label: Realisation of objectives
620812.value: We have now fully completed all objectives of the project. First, for the first objective, we have designed a new method to generate search queries automatically from the data descriptions of the target domain, to find potential data sources such as Wikipedia in the online stage. These queries can generate search pages that point to pages and knowledge structures which we can crawl into a database. This part relies on many potential data sources such as the Web, Wikipedia, Open Directory Projects, etc. We use information theory to generate the queries while trying to reduce the number of consulted queries to a minimum. These data are then hashed into a knowledge structure un order to be easily retrievable later. In the source-free transfer learning framework, there are two key issues to solve. First, we must answer what auxiliary data to query. Second, we must know how to use the retrieved auxiliary data to help the target domain task. To address the first issue, we inspect our model to find out the words that are more likely to discriminate the target domain classes. Those words are then extended via a word-to-word relevance matrix to form the queries. To tackle the second issue, we in- troduce a graph-based data-dependent prior or regularizer to the logistic regression model. The retrieved auxiliary data is used to regularize model learning of the target domain task. Our algorithm consists of the following main steps. Given an open knowledge space, such as the whole Inter- net, it would be most desirable to selectively retrieve helpful information on the target domain task. We first generate some keywords based on the learned model, then construct queries based on these keywords, finally query an open knowledge space for the auxiliary data. Keywords are generated by examining the coefficients of the linear model, where the absolute value of a coefficient is proportional to the rate of changes in the dependent variable. To prevent the learning model from overfitting, we use information filtering to remove some empirically common words, like “to”, “they”, etc. Moreover, to make queries be informative, we use keyword expansion based on the target domain labeled data. Using the queries constructed as above, we can query an open knowledge space for auxiliary data. We consider each document as a vertex to form an undirected graph (V,E). Each edge of the graph represents the similarity between the documents i and j. We have shown that the noisy auxiliary knowledge in this process will not harm the discrimination of the classifier used in document classification after transfer learning is done. Then, in each transfer learning iteration, we query for auxiliary data based on the coefficients w of a retrieved model and then update that model with the retrieved auxiliary data. The above query-update cycle repeats for several iterations until an empirical validation error bound is reached. Extensive tests were done in large-scale data such as the 20 newsgroup dataset, and the new algorithm is compared with several baseline algorithms such as regression and support vector machines. In the experiments, we compared to both SemiLogReg and TrAdaBoost algorithms, and found that our source-free transfer learning algorithm performs significantly better when the number of training samples is small. The above result has been reported in AAAI 2014. Subsequently, our work was adapted for news item recommendation on mobile platforms, similar to how Toutiao.com does its news dissemination today. This work appeared on AAAI 2015 and industries such as Microsoft expressed great interest in this work. Overall, we have completed all four objectives well in our project. Our source-free algorithm was accepted into a top venue and is widely known as the first such algorithm for transfer learning in the field of machine learning. Furthermore, our algorithm connects well with existing systems such as search engines, so that the method is highly practical. Furthermore, our iterative transfer learning method SFTL is even better than the well known instance based transfer learning methods such as TradaBoost. Finally, we have resulted in a prototype system as well as publications in several top venues as our report shows. Several PHD students have graduated as a result of the project as well.

620812.label: Major findings and research outcome
620812.value: Transfer learning uses relevant auxiliary data to help the learning task in a target domain where labeled data is usually insufficient to train an accurate model. Given appropriate auxiliary data, researchers have proposed many transfer learning models. How to find such auxiliary data, however, is of little research so far. In this project, we focused on the problem finding the right source domain data in a new transfer learning framework that effectively selects helpful auxiliary data from an open knowledge space. We exploited the World Wide Web for source domains. In this new Source Free Transfer Learning (SFTL) framework, we iteratively query for the helpful auxiliary data based on the learned model and then updates the model using the retrieved auxiliary data. We have found that this new technique can indeed enable automatic constructions of queries and the robustness of the SFTL framework. Our experiments suggest that the framework is capable of achieving comparable performance to those state-of-the-art methods with dedicated selections of auxiliary data. In particular, our work accomplished the following main points: 1. We have successfully designed a novel source-free transfer learning framework to solve a long-standing problem in transfer learning: how to choose the best auxiliary data as the source data? 2. We have published in top venues such as "Source-Free Transfer Learning" in AAAI 2014, "Content-Based Collaborative Filtering for News Topic Recommendation" in AAAI 2015. 3. We have designed a search-engine based prototype system and experimented it on large-scale transfer learning tests, e.g., in 20 newsgroup data 20NG. The result has been very high performance as compared to not using transfer learning in a new domain. 4. Finally, our conclusion is that in any machine learning situations where there is a lack of high quality and sufficient data, exploiting source-free transfer learning improves performance greatly.

620812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
620812.value: In the future, we may apply the source-free transfer learning technique to recommendation systems area. In this area, a major problem is that the system cannot cope with users evolutionary change in interests. The problem is due to the fact that, in any next time window, there is always a lack of sufficient and high quality training data. This problem can be potentially solved using source-free transfer learning. It can also be tackled using a combination of intermediate sources to help transfer between domains.

620812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
620812.value: Transfer learning is a new technique that makes machine learning models more reliable and robust. That is, when one builds a machine learning model, one wishes that the model will work in new situations where there may be a lack of experience in terms of high quality data. In this case, one can adapt an existing model to new domains. The source-free transfer learning algorithms can make this happen automatically by seeking out the useful auxiliary domains. Our proposed system is tested on a number of problem domains including news distribution and recommendation, which is a corner stone for many new media businesses on the mobile platform. Our work is expected to make machine learning models dependable in the sense that people will always get what they expect, instead of getting surprises from time to time.

621312.label: Project Objectives
621312.value: To determine the apparent stability constants and complexing capabilities of HULIS with transition metal ions include Fe (III)/Fe (II) and Cu (II)/Cu (I). 621312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621312.value: HUmic-LIke Substances (HULIS) have recently been recognized to be an important class of organic compounds in atmospheric particulate matter (PM). The results from high resolution mass spectrometry suggested that HULIS possesses abundant carboxyl and reduced N groups, which contain electron lone pairs that can form coordination compounds with transition metals. The interactions with HULIS are expected to influence both solubility and redox potential of transition metals. Transition metal ions are highly redox active in solutions and have been shown to play significant roles in both atmospheric aqueous chemistry and are capable of generating reactive oxidative species (ROS). The latter has been suggested as one mechanism underlying adverse health effects posed by PM. We propose to investigate the interactions between HULIS and transition metals in atmospheric aerosols. More specifically, we propose to study the influence of HULIS complexing on the solubility of transition metals in atmospheric aqueous phase and to investigate how HULIS affect ROS activities of transition metal ions in simulated lung fluid solutions. Iron and copper will be the target transition metals examined as they are the major redox active metals found in atmospheric samples. Ambient HULIS samples of different origins, including freshly emitted biomass burning smoke particles, rural and urban ambient PM, will be used to evaluate their influences on the solubility and ROS activity of transition metals. Results from this study will provide insights into the atmospheric fate of transition metals and the underlying mechanism of PM toxicity on human health. 最近的研究表明，类腐殖酸物质（HULIS）是大气颗粒物的一类重要组分。高分辨率质谱的分析结果显示HULIS当中含有大量的羧基和还原态含氮基团，这两类官能团都含有孤对电子，从而可以和过渡金属形成配合物。这类相互作用有望影响过渡金属的溶解度和氧化还原性质。过渡金属离子在溶液中具有极强的氧化还原活性，已经被证明在大气液相化学和诱导产生活性氧（ROS）的过程当中扮演非常重要的角色。毒理学的研究表明，气溶胶中的过渡金属诱导产生活性氧是导致大气颗粒物健康效应的致毒机理之一。 本项目建议对大气颗粒物当中的过渡金属和类腐殖酸物质（HULIS）之间的相互作用进行研究。具体的研究内容包括：HULIS和过渡金属的配合作用对后者的溶解度有何影响？HULIS将如何影响过渡金属在肺泡组织模拟液中产生活性氧的能力？作为气溶胶中主要的氧化还原活性金属，铁和铜将被作为代表性的过渡金属离子进行研究。包括生物质燃烧烟尘，城市和郊区大气气溶胶等在内的不同来源的HULIS样品，将被用于测试其对过渡金属的溶解度和ROS活性的影响。本研究的结果将有助于更深入全面地了解过渡金属在大气中的作用和对人体健康的致毒机理。

621312.label: Realisation of objectives
621312.value: Objective 1: We chose a method that monitors the fluorescence intensity change to determine the formation constants of HULIS and surrogates of HULIS with metals. Model systems of tyrosine-Cu and Suwannee River Fulvic Acid (SRFA)-Cu were examined to establish and optimize the method. After optimization of the fluorescence instrument parameters, 3D excitation-emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectra with smooth surface and higher resolution were obtained, which were the combination of fluorescence spectra measured from a series of different excitation wavelengths. Then PARAFAC, a type of factor analysis, was applied to decompose the complicated EEM spectra into underlying individual components and to derive at the formation constants of a metal with the different SRFA or ambient HULIS components. Each component represents a group of compounds having similar formation constants with a given metal. Significant variations were observed among HULIS extracted from different samples. The results suggest that future efforts need to be directed at synthetic mixtures of model ligand compounds to extract more quantitative understanding of how a mixture of ligands behave in their interaction with metals. Objective 2: Ambient samples collected at three sites of different characteristics, one suburban site and two urban sites in the Pearl River Delta, were analyzed for HULIS and marker compounds for biomass burning emissions (e.g., levoglucosan, mannosan, and glactosan) and other major aerosol sources (e.g., Ni. V for ship emissions). The marker data along with major aerosol constituents (e.g., sulfate, nitrate, organic and elemental carbon) are used as inputs to an advanced receptor model for source apportioning of HULIS. This effort has led to identification of major HULIS sources for our study region, namely, secondary formation, biomass burning, and ship emissions. Then this information is used to guide the selection of representative HULIS samples for the subsequent experiments involving ambient HULIS samples. We studied the solubilization of metals in aerosol matrix in the presence of HULIS and under the influence of dithiothreitol (DTT), a ligand and also a reagent used as a chemical assay to quantify reactive oxygen species (OS) under simulated physiological conditions. HULIS samples isolated from biomass burning emission particles and from ambient samples collected in different atmospheric environments (e.g., rural, suburban, urban) were tested. Objective 3: We used a cell-free dithiothreitol (DTT) assay to assess the effects of interactions between two representative TMs, copper (Cu) and manganese (Mn), and HULIS. Different proportion of ambient HULIS and select TMs were mixed and measured their ROS formation response. A mixture effect index, defined as the ratio of the STT response by the mixture to the sum of DTT response by components of the mixture, was used to describe the magnitude and direction of the mixture effect. The experiment results indicates that the interaction of HULIS with Cu leads to suppression of oxidative potential of Cu while the presence of HULIS promotes the oxidative potential of Mn. Potential mechanisms were explored to explain the different results. Objective 4: HULIS from biomass burning source samples and ambient aerosol samples were characterized using ultra-high resolution mass spectrometry (UHRMS). Through its capability of reporting accurate mass, UHRMS produces chemical formula information and certain structural information (e.g., double bond equivalence). The identified elemental formulas are a few thousands in number and classified into seven major compound categories, including CHONS-, CHOS-, CHON+, CHON-, CHO+, CHO-, and CHN+ compounds. This has helped in identifying HULIS species that could contain functional groups (e.g., hydroxyl, carboxyl) capable of serving as ligands.

621312.label: Major findings and research outcome
621312.value: Humic-like substances (HULIS) is an abundant class of organic compounds residing in the atmospheric particulate matter (PM). They interact with metal species, which co-exist with HULIS in PM, as observed in the example of nitrocatechol–metal complex during our measurements of nitroaromatic compounds (Chow et al., 2016). HULIS contains significant redox active constituents that generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) in cells. Our work further identifies nitrogen-containing bases, a class of constituent compounds of HULIS and not redox active on their own, would enhance ROS generation catalyzed by quinones and HULIS isolated from multiple aerosol sources (Dou et al., 2015; Dou and Yu, 2017). Through laboratory investigation using a cell-free dithiothreitol (DTT) assay, we found that HULIS suppressed the DTT consumption from low concentration of Cu (e.g. by up to 10~20% for 0.083 μM Cu), possibly due to the organic ligands in HULIS binding Cu and thereby reducing the redox reactivity of Cu (Lin and Yu, 2017). On the contrary, obvious enhancement effects on DTT loss rate were observed in the mixtures of HULIS and high concentration of Mn (e.g. up to around 2 times for 1.67 μM Mn). In addition, we found that higher initial DTT concentration would result in higher DTT consumption rate and the extent of this DTT concentration effect is generally sample-dependent, which to some extent reveals the mechanism complexity involved in the DTT assay. Our work clearly reveals the importance of considering the interactions between components when we evaluate the contribution of individual species to the total oxidative strength (Lin and Yu, 2017). Difficulties encountered in attributing mixture effects to underlying interactions suggest that further work in metal-PM organics interactions should be done using techniques capable of more specific oxidant measurements in order to acquire a deeper mechanistic insight into the interactions. Through this research, we have quantified the major sources of HULIS in the Pearl River Delta region, namely secondary formation, biomass burning, and ship emissions (Kuang et al, 2015). Particle size distribution characteristic of HULIS supports this source identification result (Wang and Yu, 2017). The source apportionment work has facilitated the selection and grouping of ambient HULIS samples for laboratory exploration of HULIS-metal interactions, as significant sample-to-sample variation exists in the chemical composition of HULIS. Chemical composition information has been gained through using ultra-high resolution mass spectrometry (UHRMS) coupled with soft ionization techniques such as electrospray ionization (ESI). The application of ESIUHRMS has led to significant progress in identifying molecular information about HULIS. The identified elemental formulas are a few thousands in number and classified into seven major compound categories, including CHONS-, CHOS-, CHON+, CHON-, CHO+, CHO-, and CHN+ compounds (Lin et al, 2014). Among them, organosulfates (i.e., CHONS- and CHOS- formulas) had prominent presence in ESI- spectra and were further examined for its distribution in ambient PM of different sizes (Kuang et al, 2016). The rich molecular level information provided by UHRMS data needs to be further explored to guide us in selecting the key relevant HULIS constituents for the targeted studies of organic-metal interactions.

621312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621312.value: This research can be further developed in the following few aspects. First, we have identified the limitation of using DTT assay to measure oxidative potential involving metal species. Future studies measuring the specific reactive oxidant species will be more fruitful in understanding the interaction between organics and metals. Second, why experimenting with realistic ambient samples have yielded useful information, the complexity of the real samples make it challenging in building up more quantitative understanding of the organic-metal interactions. Synthetic mixtures mimicking ambient samples will be more fruitful in the next stage of research on this topic.

621312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621312.value: Ambient particulate matter (PM) is a mixture of many individual chemical species. Organic compounds and metals co-exist on PM. Their interactions through metal-ligand complexation have an impact on how ambient PM exert its health effect, as metal and some organics are toxicologically active through generating reactive oxygen species in cells. We selected humic like substances (HULIS), a significant fraction of the organic PM component, as our target organics to study the interactions with transition metals (e.g., Cu and Mn). Through our chemical characterization work, we have advanced our understanding in the sources of HULIS in our region, which mainly come from oxidation reactions of volatile organic compounds, crop burning and hill fires, and ship emissions. The range of chemical compound classes in HULIS as revealed by advanced mass spectrometric analysis are diverse, some of them could serve as ligands to bind with metals. The source information and chemical characteristics of HULIS provide guidance in designing laboratory experiments to probe the fundamental chemical processes, such as the oxidative potential (OP) of metals in simulated physiological conditions. Our laboratory investigation reveals that the complexation of ligands in HULIS with Cu leads to suppression of OP of Cu while the interaction of HULIS with Mn leads to enhancement of OP of Mn. Such results reflect the complexity of realistic organic PM component and also suggest that further work in metal-PM organics interactions should be done using techniques capable of more specific oxidant measurements in order to acquire a deeper mechanistic insight into the interactions.

621912.label: Project Title(Chinese)
621912.value: 使用离散控制理论来提高并行软件质量

621912.label: Project Objectives
621912.value: Theoretical objective: Design a scalable constraint solving system for multi-variable atomicity violations. In order to use the DCT constraint solver, our first objective is to model AVs as a set of constraints on the shared program states visible to multiple threads. We plan to build a formal constraint model for AVs that involves an arbitrary number of variables. This constraint model must scale to a large of number of runtime contexts and the corresponding intra-procedural Petri nets, to allow the efficient computation of the constraint solver. This model will also uniformly model deadlocks, in addition to AVs, to open the possibility of obtaining a globally optimum fix. We also plan to scale the constraint solving process to large number of AVs in order to work with large concurrent programs, as each AV can also be further modeled by multiple constraints. Evaluation objective: Thoroughly quantify the impact of our technique We plan to quantify our technique using real world large concurrent Java programs in terms of both correctness and performance. For correctness, we will leverage our earlier bug detection work to verify the execution correctness of the patched versions. We will also quantify the runtime cost incurred by our solution using a set of standard benchmarks, comparing the fixed subjects to both the original version and the fixes provided by other state of the art techniques.

621912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621912.value: 人工修复并行软件的错误是非常困难的。这项研究使用离散控制理论来提高并行软件质量。和之前的研究相比，使用离散控制能够第一次让自动生成的补丁对程序的并行程度和安全性都有理论上的保证。这项研究提出应用的新的理论，并在试验中进行验证。

621912.label: Realisation of objectives
621912.value: This project sets out to establish a ground break research direction of combining classic theories in the automatic control area and problems of software engineering. Our theoretical objective consists of three steps: the first is to find the correct abstraction from the static knowledge of program structures that can be reasoned by the discrete control theory (DCT); the second is how results of the DCT can be interpreted and translated back to addictives of existing program structures; the third is how to scale such transformations to a very large number of software problems and large sizes of program sources. For the first objective, we have worked with our collaborator to employ a classic representation of processes using Petri Nets to represent communications between program threads. The key breakthrough is the use of static analysis to enumerate all possible problematic states and present them as a set of dynamic behaviours to the DCT theory. For the second objective, the challenge lies in how the produced timing devices can be best represented in terms of programming instructions. We have leveraged our past research experience in experiment with an array of possible design choices of synchronisation implementations and, in turn, designed an optimisation algorithm in placing the minimum amount of instructions into the system. For the third objective, we have strengthened our program analysis algorithms to be able to analyse deep call stacks and the domination relationships of AV problems. We have evaluated our algorithm using real world concurrent systems and known synchronisation problems. The research challenge is the verification of the correctness of the generated patches due to the exponential number of possible dynamic states of the patched system. We have used our past research experience of reducing program state verification computation using partial orders and leveraged a tool we have built called Pecan to exhaustively explore the new states brought by the patch and to check if the problematic states have been enumerated. We have conducted extensive experiments and collected quantitative observation to show that our methods have been effective.

621912.label: Major findings and research outcome
621912.value: We have found that the idea of using theories in dynamic systems to combat concurrency errors in a static way is promising. The static program analysis can help us to enumerate the runtime states in a conservative way without incurring much additional cost compared to the cost incurred by manual approaches. The generated patches, however, have much higher quality compared to human-based solutions in terms of correctness and performance. In addition to the design of techniques, we have also produced tools that allow us to evaluate the ideas using real world software systems and software bugs. We have observed these benefits through collecting measurements through experiments. The findings above and the associated research contributions have led to three top tier papers listed in section 9.

621912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621912.value: There are two directions that can be possibly pursued. The first is to examine other categories of control theory results on dynamic systems and benefits to automatically solving programming tasks, not just fixing programming errors. The second is to study the current theory for low level system software where the synchronisation cost is more significant to the overall system performance.

621912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621912.value: The nature of the research is to replace human beings in repairing problems occurred in software by automatically calculating a patch to existing systems. This research is the first attempt to the automatic patching of concurrency software errors that provide theoretical guarantees to both correctness and performance. This research opens a new direction in synergistic effects between classic research domains and emerging software engineering problems.

622312.label: Project Objectives
622312.value: We shall combine the dynamic theory of crystal lattices with the Gibbs surface approach to develop a new thermodynamic theory and establish a universal equation of state. We shall continue to follow our newly developed surface eigenstress and eigendisplacement models to study comprehensively temperature dependences of surface eigenstress, surface eigendisplacement and surface elastic constants. To simplify the mathematic expression, we shall take the (001) thin films of cubic crystal structure as typical examples in the theoretical study. The theoretical study will build up a theoretical framework with formulas. The values of material properties involved in the formulas will be determined from atomistic simulations. We shall conduct density functional theory based ab initio molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the (001) thin films of cubic crystal structure and their bulk counterparts at different temperatures. The simulation data will provide information about the temperature dependences of surface eigenstress, surface eigendisplacement and surface elastic constants. The ab initio MD simulation will bring insight into the physical mechanism of the solid surface behavior. The expected simulation results will confirm the developed theoretical formulas and determine the material properties involved in the formulas.
