The simulation data will provide information about the temperature dependences of surface eigenstress, surface eigendisplacement and surface elastic constants. The ab initio MD simulation will bring insight into the physical mechanism of the solid surface behavior. The expected simulation results will confirm the developed theoretical formulas and determine the material properties involved in the formulas.

622312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622312.value: Surface energy and surface stress of solids play essential roles in the surface-related physical, chemical and mechanical properties of materials, such as surface-chemistry-driven actuation, adsorption, catalysis, corrosion, electrochemical storage, photoelectronic devices, thermoelectric parts, etc, especially in nanomaterials, which have large values of the surface-area-over-bulk-volume ratio, e.g., graphene is an extreme example with all the carbon atoms in a layer. Since solids can sustain deformation, the surfaces of solids behave differently from the surfaces of liquids. For academic curiosity and industrial innovation, it is necessary to understand and predict surface-related physical, chemical and mechanical properties of materials, which may depend on the sample size when conventional continuum thermodynamic theory is applied. For example, surface elastic constants render strong size-dependent Young’s modulus in nanomaterials. Although great progress has been achieved in the research areas of surface elasticity and the equation of state for solids, the temperature dependences of surface eigenstress, surface eigendisplacement and surface elastic constants have not yet been systematically investigated in theory or in experiment, which are the bottleneck problems and must be solved for the further development of solid surface-related thermodynamic theory. Based on our rich research experience in surface elasticity, atomistic simulations, mechanical characterization of thin films, etc, we propose to study the temperature- and surface-related mechanical properties of materials at small scales. The purpose of the proposed research is to develop a novel thermodynamic theory and a universal equation of state for solid surfaces in order to explain and predict the surface-related mechanical behavior at different temperatures. To achieve this goal, we shall conduct designed experiments, theoretical study, and atomistic simulations. The designed microbridge tests on multilayer films will be the first academic endeavor to measure interface-elastic Young’s modulus at different temperatures. The proposed theoretical study will combine the dynamic theory of crystal lattices with thermodynamic surface treatment. We shall consider nonlinear initial in-plane deformation induced by the relaxation of nanometer-thick films, which will lay the foundation of the novel thermodynamic theory and the universal equation of state for the surfaces of solids. The atomistic calculations will simulate the thermal and mechanical behavior of nanometer-thick films. Successful completion of the proposed project will facilitate the development of solid surface-related thermodynamic theory and technologies, which will have a high impact on both academic research and engineering practice. The anticipated output will become guidelines for the wide applications of surface-related technologies in high-tech industries. 固体材料的表面能及表面应力在与表面相关的物理、化学以及力学性能方面起着很重要的作用，例如，由表面化学驱使的制动、吸附、催化、腐蚀、电化学存储、光电设备和热电部件等。特别是对于有着极大比表面的纳米材料来说，这种作用更为显著。石墨烯就是一个极端的例子，它的所有原子都在同一平面内。由于固体可承受变形，因此其具有不同于液体的表面行为。出于对科学的追求和技术创新的需要，我们有必要了解和预测材料与表面相关的物理、化学以及力学性能。用传统热力学理论来表征这些性能，它们将呈现出尺寸依赖性。例如，表面弹性常数会导致纳米材料的杨氏模量具有很强的尺寸效应。尽管在表面弹性以及固体的状态方程等研究领域已经取得了很大的进展，但是不论从理论还是实验方面，表面本征应力、表面本征位移以及表面弹性常数的温度依赖性都还未得到系统的研究，这已经成为阻碍固体表面热力学理论发展的瓶颈。基于在表面弹性、计算机模拟和薄膜力学特性等方面丰富的研究经验，我们提出研究与表面相关的材料性能与温度的关系。此研究旨在建立一种新的热力学理论和一种普适的描述固体表面的状态方程，以解释和预测表面在不同温度下的力学行为。我们将通过实验、理论分析和计算机模拟来实现这一目标。实验方面，我们会通过多层薄膜的微桥测试来测量在不同温度下界面的弹性杨氏模量。理论方面，我们将结合晶格动力学理论和固体表面的热力学理论，考虑在纳米薄膜中由松弛引起的非线性平面内初始变形，发展新的热力学理论以及固体表面的普适状态方程。计算机模拟将计算纳米薄膜的热学和力学性能。成功完成本课题将大大促进与固体表面相关的热力学理论和技术的发展，这将不论对科学研究还是对工程实践都具有深远的影响。本课题的研究成果将会成为与固体表面相关技术在高新技术产业中广泛应用的指南。

622312.label: Realisation of objectives
622312.value: We adopted the surface eigenstress and eigendisplacement models in the investigation of the surface stress, surface relaxation and surface elasticity of thin films with different surface orientations. Molecular dynamics simulations and first-principles calculations were conducted on face-centered cubic Au (111) and Au (100) thin films with the focus on relaxation-induced nonlinear initial deformation. The simulation results verify the theoretical predictions of the size dependency of surface energy density and surface stress, and the nonlinear scaling law of the size-dependent Young’s modulus of thin films. The mechanism of the size-dependent behaviors was further explored at the atomic bonding level with the charge density field. The Au atomic bonding at surfaces is enhanced compared to its interior counterpart and therefore the nominal Young’s modulus of the Au thin films is larger when the film thickness is smaller. We further developed the surface eigenstress model to study the surface-induced size-dependent ultimate tensile strength of thin films. First-principles calculations and MD simulations were conducted on Au and Si (100) thin films with various thicknesses. The atomistic calculations show that the ultimate tensile strength of Au thin films increases when the film thickness decreases, a typical the-thinner-the- stronger phenomenon, while the Si thin films exhibit the-thinner-the-weaker behavior. Nevertheless, both behaviors were perfectly predicted by a nonlinear scaling law developed from the surface eigenstress model. Moreover, the first-principles calculations put insight into the surface-induced strengthening or weakening mechanism. The surface strengthening and weakening phenomena were explained from an electronic structure point of view. We also extended the surface eigenstress model and included the temperature effect by considering the temperature dependence of the eigen parameters. Nanometer-thick thin films were taken as an ideal system to investigate the surface-induced temperature- and size-dependent Young’s modulus and size-dependent thermal expansion coefficient. The theoretical modeling was to further develop the surface eigenstress model with the consideration of thermal expansion, leading to analytic formulas of temperature- and size-dependent Young’s modulus and size-dependent thermal expansion coefficient of thin films. MD simulations on Ag, Cu and Ni (100) thin films were conducted at temperatures ranging from 300 K to 600 K. The MD simulation results were perfectly consistent with the theoretical predictions. The newly developed surface eigenstress model will be able to attack similar problems in other types of nanomaterials. We also theoretically and numerically investigated the nanoindentation problem with the consideration of surface elasticity. The Hertz contact solution was used as a reference which describes the bulk deformation under an applied load without considering the surface. Due to surface elasticity, the applied load must deform the surface and the bulk such that the applied indentation load P* can be separated into two parts on the bulk and surface, respectively. Based on surface elasticity and the generalized Young-Laplace equation, we analyzed the indentation depth as a function of the applied indentation load. Extensive FEM simulations of nanoindentation were carried out with the commercial software package ANSYS. The numerical results verified the theoretical formulations. According to these theoretical results, a highly reliable and efficient mechanical characterization technique for one-dimensional nanomaterials was developed based on multi-position bending tests by atomic force microscope (AFM) on top-down fabricated suspended nanowires with double-clamped ends and appropriate theoretical analysis considering residual stress and substrate deformation. The reliability and efficiency of the technique were improved through the avoidance of sample manipulation, high sample comparability, precise experimental control, and more data for mechanics analysis. The AFM-based multi-position bending tests were conducted on gold nanowires, showing good testing repeatability and data reliability.

622312.value: 1. A PhD student was trained and she received her PhD degree in August 2016. 2. Four journal papers have been published based on the research results from this project. 3. The surface eigenstress and eigendisplacement model with the direct integration of temperature effects and size effects has been developed. 622312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622312.value: Surface energy and surface stress of solids play essential roles in the surface-related physical, chemical and mechanical properties of materials, especially in nanomaterials of high surface-area-to-bulk-volume ratio. To satisfy academic curiosity and to introduce industrial innovation, it is necessary to understand and predict surface-related physical, chemical and mechanical properties of materials, which may depend on the sample size. Up until now, however, the temperature dependences of surface eigenstress, surface eigendisplacement and surface elastic constants have not yet been systematically investigated in theory or in experiment. These are the bottleneck problems that limit the further development of academic knowledge and industry applications in these areas. In this project we have studied the influences of temperature and surface on the mechanical properties of materials at small scales. Through theoretical modelling, atomistic simulations and experiments, a novel thermodynamic model for solid surfaces has been developed to explain and predict the surface-related mechanical behavior at different temperatures. Based on these theoretical studies, a novel AFM-based technique that can be used to measure the mechanical properties of one-dimensional materials has been developed. The model and characterization technique developed will provide useful guidelines for many applications of surface-related technologies in high-tech industries.

622412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622412.value: Chlorine, chloramine, chlorine dioxide, and ozone are widely used drinking water disinfectants. During disinfection, they may react with naturally occurring organic matter, bromide, and iodide in source waters to produce disinfection byproducts (DBPs). About 600 DBPs have been identified, and 85 of them are quantifiable. There are a countless number of DBPs that are non-quantifiable, unidentified and unknown. Despite the low DBP levels in most finished drinking water, the large amount of water ingested over a lifetime may cause adverse health effects. A vast majority of laboratory-based toxicologic studies have been conducted with individual DBPs, including 60 DBPs for DNA damage in mammalian cells and 16 for mutagenicity in bacteria. However, the toxicologic results of individual DBPs cannot be directly linked to the toxicity of DBP mixtures because of the unlikeliness to achieve the occurrence and toxicologic data of all individual DBPs and the potential synergistic/antagonistic interactions among the DBPs. Only a few studies have examined the cytotoxicity and mutagenicity of drinking water extracts in bacteria or mammalian-cell assays, but the organic extracts from either solid or liquid phase extraction basically exclude inorganic/volatile/highly-polar DBPs and thus cannot adequately reflect the toxicity of DBP mixtures. In this project, instead of taking organic DBPs out of a drinking water sample, the PI proposes to take “most of water” out of a drinking water sample by vacuum evaporation (or vac-evaporation) and purge highly volatile DBPs back to the vac-evaporation concentrate. By doing so, nearly all DBPs can be retained and concentrated, and meantime total dissolved salts in the water sample can also be retained and concentrated. Then, the PI proposes a new approach to evaluating the vac-evaporation concentrate with the embryo-larvae of a marine polychaete Platynereis dumerilii, which is expected to be sensitive enough to the DBP mixture in the vac-evaporation concentrate and meantime to tolerate the relatively high total dissolved salts therein. The primary objective of this project is to develop a new approach for evaluating the comparative toxicity of vac-evaporation concentrates (DBP mixtures) of drinking waters with the embryo-larvae of the marine polychaete. With the new approach, the second objective of this project is to evaluate the comparative toxicity of drinking water DBP mixtures from different disinfection processes. 氯，氯胺，二氧化氯和臭氧是目前广泛应用的饮用水消毒剂。在消毒过程中， 消毒剂会与原水中的天然有机物、溴离子和碘离子反应生成消毒副产物。迄今为止文献所报道的消毒副产物已有约600种，其中仅85种可被定量测定，仍有大量消毒副产物是无法测定的，尚未被鉴定的，抑或是完全未知的。尽管饮用水中消毒副产物的含量很低，但长期饮用可能会对人体健康产生不良影响。对单个消毒副产物的毒理研究已在很多实验室展开， 包括对60种消毒副产物对哺乳动物细胞DNA的损伤和16种消毒副产物对细菌致突变性的研究。然而，由于不可能测定所有消毒副产物的生成和毒理数据，并且各种消毒副产物之间可能存在协同或拮抗作用，根据已测定的所有单个消毒副产物的生成和毒理实验结果并不能直接推算出由所有消毒副产物组成的混合物的总毒性。至今只有少量关于饮用水萃取物对细菌或哺乳动物细胞诱变性及细胞毒性的研究。然而，不论使用固相萃取还是液液萃取，得到的萃取物并不包含无机的、易挥发的和高极性的消毒副产物，所以已有方法并不能真正全面反映消毒副产物混合物的总毒性。 在本项目中，主要研究者提出，通过真空蒸发将尽可能多的水从饮用水样品中去除而得到浓缩液，并将极易挥发的消毒副产物吹洗收集使其重新回到浓缩液中，从而代替把有机物从水中萃取出来的传统方法。这样几乎所有消毒副产物可以保留并浓缩，同时饮用水样品中的溶解盐也被保留并浓缩。在此基础上，主要研究者提出利用一种海洋多毛目环节动物的胚胎幼虫来评估所得浓缩液的毒性。该海洋环节动物的胚胎幼虫对浓缩液中的消毒副产物有足够的敏感度，同时也可以承受浓缩液中较高的盐度。本项目的主要目的是开发一种利用海洋多毛目环节动物的胚胎幼虫来评估饮用水样品真空蒸发后浓缩液的比较毒性的方法。其次，利用这一新方法，评估不同消毒过程产生的饮用水消毒副产物混合物的比较毒性。

622412.label: Realisation of objectives
622412.value: (1) A new, sensitive and accurate approach for evaluating the comparative toxicity of drinking water DBP mixtures has been developed. The new approach improves upon the water concentration method and optimizes the toxicological bioassay. The new concentration method (freeze-drying or rotary evaporation) overcomes the limitations of conventionally used methods (e.g., liquid phase extraction); it not only shows significantly higher efficiency in retaining organic halogenated DBPs, but also retains all inorganic DBPs (and dissolved salts)). For such a high-salt-containing concentrated drinking water, a highly sensitive bioassay based on the embryos of a high-salinity-tolerance marine polychaete, P. dumerilii, was optimized for evaluating the comparative developmental toxicity. Accordingly, the new approach significantly improves the accuracy in evaluating the toxicity of different drinking water DBP mixtures. The results have been accepted or are under review for publication in top environmental journals including Environmental Science & Technology and Water Research. The results have also been presented in several prestigious international conferences. (2) By using the newly developed approach, we evaluated the comparative developmental toxicity of DBP mixtures in disinfected drinking waters with different initial bromide concentrations and pH values and different contact times. Additionally, we studied the DBP formation and the developmental toxicity of drinking waters with different disinfection processes, i.e., with the commonly used disinfectants (chlorine, chloramine, chlorine dioxide, and ozone). (3) According to the comparative developmental toxicity of 30 chlorinated, brominated and iodinated DBPs, toxicity indexes were assigned to total organic chlorine (TOCl), total organic bromine (TOBr) and total organic iodine (TOI), respectively. A correlation between the total organic halogen (TOX) by weighting with corresponding toxicity indexes and the comparative toxicity of a drinking water DBP mixture was established. The combination of analytical and toxicological data can be used to predict the health risk of drinking water. Besides, with the new approach, the toxicity contribution from the interaction between organic and inorganic DBPs was investigated, which provided more information about the health risk of disinfected drinking water and emphasized the importance of toxicity evaluation on DBP mixtures. The results are under review at Environmental Science & Technology.

622412.label: Major findings and research outcome
622412.value: (1) We modified the in vivo bioassay based on the embryos of a cosmopolitan polychaete P. dumerilii, and achieved a much lower relative standard deviation of the percent normal development. By conducting the developmental toxicity bioassay with 30 halogenated DBPs, we obtained some important findings: e.g., aromatic halogenated DBPs generally presented higher developmental toxicity than aliphatic halogenated DBPs; iodinated and brominated DBPs were more toxic than corresponding chlorinated DBPs; N-based DBPs were more toxic than C-based DBPs; and the number and substitution site of halogens affected the DBP toxicity. The results have been published in leading environmental journals, including Water Research. (2) The effects of raw water pH and bromide concentration and disinfection contact time on the developmental toxicity of chlorinated drinking water were investigated. The drinking water toxicity was positively correlated with the formation of brominated DBPs, and decreased with the increase in contact time and pH. Surprisingly, we found that with the increase in bromide concentration, the toxicity of the disinfected drinking water first reduced and then gradually increased. That is, with a low level of bromide in source waters, the chlorinated drinking water showed lower toxicity than that without bromide. Bromide concentration affected the amount and species of halogenated DBPs during chlorination, and the toxicity of the drinking water was affected by both DBP concentration and speciation. The results are under review for publication in top environmental journals. (3) A novel approach for evaluating the toxicity of drinking water concentrated with a new method was developed by using the embryos of high-salinity-tolerance P. dumerilii. The performance of the newly adopted concentration methods, freeze-drying and rotary evaporation, was investigated. Compared to the conventionally used concentration method, the newly adopted methods achieved 2–4 times higher efficiency in retaining organic halogenated DBPs, and also effectively retained inorganic DBPs (and total dissolved salts) as well as drinking water matrices. Factors that may affect the accuracy of the bioassay (including salinity and pH of the concentrated drinking water) were studied, and a more accurate and sensitive toxicity evaluation approach for different types of drinking water was optimized. (4) With the newly developed approach, the developmental toxicity of drinking waters from different disinfection processes was evaluated. The disinfection processes involved the use of four widely applied disinfectants (i.e., chlorine, chloramine, chlorine dioxide, and ozone). According to the toxicity evaluation, we found that the toxicity of chlorine- or chloramine-disinfected drinking water was closely related to its TOX level, while the toxicity of ozone- or chlorine dioxide-disinfected drinking water was significantly influenced by the inorganic DBPs. For high-bromide raw water, ozone induced the highest developmental toxicity due to the formation of a significant amount of bromate, which may remarkably increase the toxicity via synergistically interacting with organic DBPs. For low-bromide raw water, chlorine induced the highest developmental toxicity due to the formation of high levels of organic halogenated DBPs. (5) A relationship was established between the TOX risk index and the developmental toxicity of different drinking water DBP mixtures. The TOX risk was indexed by the levels of TOCl, TOBr and TOI, and their corresponding toxicity indexes. Toxicity indexes were assigned to TOCl, TOBr and TOI according to the comparative developmental toxicity of 30 chlorinated, brominated and iodinated DBPs. The relationship can be used to predict the toxicity of a disinfected drinking water. Additionally, the effect of the interaction on the developmental toxicity of DBP mixtures was investigated. The results provided important information for selecting an appropriate disinfection process for a specific source of water.

622412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
622412.value: (1) We found that with the increase in bromide concentration in source waters, the toxicity of the chlorinated drinking water first decreased and then gradually increased. Bromide is naturally present in source waters, and brominated DBPs have been demonstrated to induce significantly higher toxicity than corresponding chlorinated analogues. The unexpected decrease in toxicity could be attributed to different DBP species formed under low-bromide levels. The PI would propose to further investigate the comparative toxicity, TOX formation, and variation in DBP speciation with varying initial bromide concentrations, which could provide a promising way for controlling the health risk of drinking water. (2) We adopted two new water concentration methods, freeze drying and rotary evaporation. The efficiency in retaining halogenated DBPs was significantly enhanced compared to the conventionally used liquid‒liquid extraction, indicating that the new concentration methods might retain polar or highly polar DBPs and high-molecular-weight DBPs. These DBPs are difficult to extract, and consequently cannot be detected and identified. The PI would propose to provide selective detection of polar halogenated DBPs in chlorine/chloramine/chlorine dioxide/ozone-disinfected drinking waters that will be concentrated with new concentration methods, and to provide thorough identification of some newly detected halogenated DBPs that may shed light on largely unknown TOX.

622412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622412.value: The use of disinfection affords great success in eliminating harmful microorganisms and acute waterborne diseases, but disinfection leads to the unintended formation of DBPs, which are associated with increased spontaneous abortions, and bladder and rectal cancer. Most previous toxicological studies focused on individual DBPs, while a large portion of DBPs remain unknown and humans are exposed to whole DBP mixtures. Because DBPs at their levels in drinking water cannot induce observable effects in bioassays, concentration is required beforehand, and the conventional concentration method results in the loss of organic and inorganic DBPs and hence underestimation of biological effects. Through this project, a new approach to evaluating the toxicity of drinking water DBP mixtures was developed by using efficient concentration methods and optimizing a sensitive bioassay. The effect of raw water characteristics (i.e., pH and bromide concentration) and disinfection scenarios (i.e., different disinfectants and contact times) on the overall toxicity of drinking water was revealed for the first time. Based on the toxicity evaluation with the new approach, we found that disinfection with ozone generated the highest health risk for high-bromide raw water, and disinfection with chlorine generated the highest health risk for low-bromide raw water. Chloramine is a relatively safe disinfectant for raw water containing various bromide and iodide levels.

622712.label: Project Title(Chinese)
622712.value: 锂离子液流电池中质量、电子及离子耦合传输现象

622712.label: Project Objectives
622712.value: Select and synthesize nanoparticles of energy-dense, electrochemically active materialsuitable for the flow battery. In selecting anode active materials, in addition to energy density and stability considerations, particular attention will be paid to avoiding the formation of a solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), which is a common problem in conventional lithium-ion batteries and significantly impacts cell performance. Special measures will also be taken to make the particles of both the anode and cathode materials less than 50 nm in average diameter so they can form an electrochemically active nanofluid with the selected liquid electrolyte. Devise a unique experimental setup in which the charge and flow transport properties of the electrochemically active nanofluids can be characterized and optimized. In addition to their electrochemical properties, special attention will also be paid to limiting the fluid viscosity to minimize pumping power requirements. Design and fabricate a single lithium-ion flow cell to investigate the effects of different electrochemically active nanofluids, cell structure design parameters, and operating conditions on the cell performance. Investigate the rheological and flow characteristics of electrochemically active nanofluids through the porous electrode to understand the effect of nanoparticle size on the pressure drop through the flow battery system.

622712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622712.value: 本项目旨在开发一种新概念液流电池。传统的液流电池是一种可充电电池；在液流电池中，电化学活性物质溶解在电解液中并随电解液流经电化学电池，使化学能直接转化成电能。额外的电解液储存在储液罐中并被泵入电化学电池。液流电池的一个显著特征是能量储存区域与能量转化区域相互分离，因此储能与功率是相互独立的，可以满足不同的应用要求。但是由于受到溶解度的限制，传统的液流电池很难提高离子浓度，导致液流电池功率密度(～20 mW/cm2)和系统能量密度（～30Wh/L）都很低。本项目提出一种锂离子液流电池，这种电池保持了传统液流电池的结构，但采用锂离子电池活性材料替代传统活性材料。通过整合两种不同电池的优点，电池的系统能量密度可以革命性的提高到约400-500 Wh/L并且保持了锂离子电池高电压的特点。为使这种新电池体系实用化和商品化，亟待解决的关键科学问题有，选择更好的阴极阳极材料，选择合适的电解液以最小化工作介质的粘度同时最大化能量密度和电导率。同时，还应优化电池设计，以最大化系统的能量密度和功率密度同时最小化泵功。由于液体电极与已研究成熟的固态电极传输原理不同，因此对于其中质量电子耦合传输现象的加深理解是非常重要的。这种全新的电池设计可以为电动汽车提供更轻且价格更低廉的替代电源。同时这种电池可以在低成本下放大系统。这一优点使得新体系适于大规模公用设施电能储存装置以及诸如风能和太阳能等间歇电网的供电装置。

622712.label: Realisation of objectives
622712.value: During the undertaking of this project, we have achieved much more than what was listed in the objectives. We have selected and synthesized anode active nanomaterials as well as cathode active nanomaterials. In particular, the anode materials we developed can avoid the formation of a solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), which enable a high stability of the battery. With the materials we obtained, special measures were undertook, especially for the materials with particle size less than 50 nm. With the materials developed, we have devised a unique experimental setup to measure and optimize the charge and flow transport properties of the electrochemically active nanofluids. After optimization, we have achieved a relatively low fluid viscosity, which can minimize the pumping power. After that, we have fabricated a single lithium-ion flow cell to investigate the effects of different electrochemically active nanofluids, cell structure design parameters, and operating conditions on the cell performance. In addition, the rheological and flow characteristics of electrochemically active nanofluids through the porous electrode were also investigated, finding that the nanoparticle size has a significant influence on the pressure drop. With the above-mentioned experimental investigations, we have also developed an advanced model for the suspension flow battery, with which the effects of various design and operating parameters on cell performance were investigated. Lastly, a proof-of-concept lithium-ion flow battery pack at laboratory scale were demonstrated. It is shown that the energy density was improved to 3 times that of conventional lithium-ion batteries.

622712.label: Major findings and research outcome
622712.value: With the support of the present RGC grant, we have made significant contributions to the development of lithium-ion flow batteries. The results obtained in this project have been presented in 14 top-rated journal papers, as listed in Sections 8. The major findings are summarized as follows: We have synthesized active nanometerials with high energy density and electrochemical activities for flow batteries and related measures for the materials less than 50 nm were also taken. We have devised a unique experimental setup to measure and optimize the charge and flow transport properties of the electrochemically active nanofluids. After optimization, we have achieved a relatively low fluid viscosity, which can minimize the pumping power. We have fabricated a single lithium-ion flow cell to investigate the effects of different electrochemically active nanofluids, cell structure design parameters, and operating conditions on the cell performance. We have also developed an advanced model for the suspension flow battery, with which the effects of various design and operating parameters on cell performance were investigated. We have demonstrated a proof-of-concept lithium-ion flow battery pack at laboratory scale and the energy density of the battery was 3 times that of conventional lithium-ion batteries.

622712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
622712.value: The present project has primarily focused on the development of a lithium ion flow battery, with which the ion transport in the flow battery were experimentally and numerically studied. The outcome of this project have deepened our fundamental understanding of the ion transport in the lithium ion flow battery and provided the needed information for the design of the flow battery with applications in electrical vehicles.

622712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622712.value: A growing number of electrical vehicles demand small, lightweight power sources with high power density and energy density. Current battery technologies, even the most advanced Li-ion batteries, are unlikely to be able to meet the growing energy demands of a mobile workforce due to their low energy densities, creating a power-hungry problem. In this project, we developed a lithium-ion flow battery with an architecture similar to that of conventional batteries but in which the electro-active materials are those used in today's lithium-ion batteries. Such a design would retain the flexible and scalable architecture of fuel cells and flow batteries, but using the very energy-dense active materials of lithium-ion batteries enabled boosting the system-level energy density by 3 times. This radically new approach to the design of batteries promises to open a window for breakthroughs in battery technology.

622812.value: To develop a theoretical framework for bidirectional mapping between CityGML models and BIM models, using linguistic and schema mediation techniques and taking Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) as an example BIM data standard; To develop a bidirectional mapping between gbXML models and CityGML models, using the theoretical framework developed in this project as a framework validation; To propose an extension in the CityGML standard for including gbXML data, enhancing the interoperability between CityGML and gbXML; and To showcase the potential value of mapping and integration between CityGML models and BIM models.

622812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622812.value: Modeling the built environment digitally in three dimensions can support navigation, urban planning, disaster management, and energy consumption analysis. City Geography Markup Language (CityGML) was developed in recent years as a data standard to represent the geometry and geographical information of buildings in digital 3D city models. On the other hand, the building information modeling (BIM) technology is increasingly used in the architectural, engineering and construction industry to represent the 3D geometry of buildings and incorporate non-graphical information such as construction schedule and cost in building models. Therefore, CityGML models and BIM models have many similarities in context. While people started to create CityGML models of different cities, many BIM models are already available for new buildings and for existing buildings. Mapping between CityGML and BIM models can hence integrate the two domains and reduce the modeling efforts. Currently, Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) and Green Building eXtensible Markup Language (gbXML) are two widely used data standards for BIM models. There have been attempts to map between CityGML models and IFC models. However, those attempts are unidirectional mappings and only focus on downsizing information-rich BIM models to CityGML. In addition, the current proposed mappings are generic and sometimes result in building models with distorted geometry or even unable to be viewed in CityGML applications. Furthermore, mapping between CityGML and gbXML is currently needed but lacking. The proposed project aims to develop a theoretical framework for mapping between CityGML models and BIM models. Firstly, linguistic techniques like prefixing and stemming will be used to relate the elements in CityGML data schema with the elements in BIM data schema. Building regulations, specifications and WordNet will also be used as the corpus for measuring the similarity between the CityGML schema elements and the BIM schema elements. Secondly, the CityGML representation and the BIM representation of different building components like walls and columns will be studied and compared to generalize a meta-schema that enables bidirectional mapping between CityGML and BIM standards. Elements in the meta-schema will be specified with the compatible CityGML applications. Thirdly, different levels of detail in CityGML will be considered and the transformation between complex BIM models and lower levels of detail CityGML models will be developed. Finally, a case scenario will be developed to verify and showcase the CityGML-BIM mapping framework. In the project, mapping between CityGML and IFC will be studied first, followed by mapping between CityGML and gbXML. 三維數碼建築環境模型能夠支援諸如導航、城市規劃、災害管理以及能耗分析等應用。城市地理標記語言（CityGML）是近年發展起來的一種能夠在三維數碼城市模型中，表現建築幾何和地理信息的數據標準；另一方面，建築信息模型（BIM）在近年來逐漸被應用於建築工程領域，用以表現建築物之三維幾何形狀，和嵌入如施工進度和成本之非幾何信息。從展現建築信息的角度而言，CityGML模型和BIM模型有很多相似之處，當人們開始在很多城市採用CityGML標準構建模型的時候，很多在建或已建的建築物之BIM模型卻已經被構建出來並可以用來展現建築的各方面信息。因此，CityGML和BIM模型之間的映射，能夠整合這兩個領域，並且減少雙方構建模型之工作。目前， IFC和gbXML是兩種廣泛使用的BIM模型數據標準。在此之前，研究人員已經嘗試研發一些關於IFC和CityGML模型之間的映射，然而，這些嘗試都是單向映射，單方面的從信息比較豐富的BIM數據標準映射到CityGML數據標準。另外，目前所提出的各種方法過於泛化，有的時候甚至會於建築信息模型中產生錯誤的幾何表達，或是產生無法在CityGML查看器中打開的建築信息模型。此外，CityGML和gbXML之間的映射在當前也顯得非常必要，然而卻鮮見這方面的研究。 本項目旨在建立一個CityGML模型和BIM模型之間數據映射的理論框架。首先，語言學上的一些如添加前綴和取詞根等技術，會被用於尋找CityGML架構標準中的定義元素 和BIM架構標準中的定義元素之間的關係；建築法律法規、技術標準以及WordNet也會被當做語料庫，用以量度這兩個數據架構標準之間定義元素的相似程度。其次，不同建築構件（如牆、柱、樑等）的CityGML數據表達和BIM數據表達也會被分離出來並加以研究比較，以歸納一個可以滿足雙向映射的元數據架構標準，而該架構標準中的元素都會指明能夠兼容的CityGML應用。第三，CityGML數據架構標準中不同的細節層次（Level of Detail）也會被考慮和研究，以創建複雜的BIM模型與低細節層次的CityGML模型之間的數據映射和轉換。最後，本項目建立的數據映射理論框架將會以一個案例研究來驗證和演示。本項目會先研究CityGML和IFC之間的數據映射，然後再進行CityGML和gbXML之間的數據映射。

622812.label: Realisation of objectives
622812.value: All the four objectives proposed in this project have been completed. Objective 1 1.1) Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) is an open BIM data standard that is widely used in the architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) sector. In March 2013, IFC4 was released as the new IFC standard. In this project, changes in IFC4 in the aspects of geographical information system (GIS) have been identified and evaluated using the versioning technique and domain knowledge, with reference to CityGML. The version differences have been compared with the domain knowledge using a linguistic-based method to discover the mapping between IFC4 and CityGML. The missing elements in IFC4 for geographical information have also been identified. This study served as the basis for developing the theoretical framework for bidirectional mapping between CityGML models and BIM IFC models. 1.2) Later in this project, a methodology framework based on text mining and linguistic methods for comparing and mapping between BIM IFC models and CityGML models has been developed and tested. 1008 entities from the IFC schema and 607 entities from the CityGML schema have been compared. Definitions of the entities were used to assist the mapping. The results show that the linguistic-based method can generate reliable mapping candidates, but the recall rate is only 0.375. The result can limit the search space of the mapping between IFC and CityGML. 1.3) A methodology framework based on instance-based and schema mediation techniques for mapping between BIM IFC and CityGML has then been developed. A reference ontology and a CityGML extension have been developed to facilitate the bidirectional mapping. The proposed methodology for mapping between IFC with CityGML was tested on various IFC and CityGML models. The CityGML models generated from our proposed framework keep all the geometric and semantic information from IFC models, while the current method using the BIM Server generates CityGML models that have missing building components and semantic information. Objective 2 2.1) IFC4 has also been enriched to support information for green building design. In this project, changes in IFC4 in the aspects of GIS and green buildings were identified and evaluated using the versioning technique and domain knowledge. The version differences were compared with the domain knowledge using a linguistic-based method to discover the mapping between IFC4 and gbXML. The missing elements in IFC4 for the green building domain were also identified for further investigation. 2.2) In this project, necessary information for green building design and energy simulation has been identified, based on studies on various green building performance and energy simulation software applications. To support the bidirectional mapping between CityGML and gbXML, a data model for green building design and energy simulation is then developed, with reference to the gbXML schema. The data model has also been compared with the entities in the BIM IFC4 schema, and the missing elements in IFC4 have been identified. Objective 3 3.1) CityGML provides a standard means, namely Application Domain Extensions (ADE), to support schema extension for specific domains. The ontology style and development guidelines of CityGML ADE have been studied in this project. Based on the results from the work (2.2), we have developed a CityGML ADE, which contains the necessary information for green building design and energy simulation. The CityGML ADE enables mapping between CityGML and gbXML. Objective 4 4.1) In this project, three use cases have been developed to show how BIM and GIS can facilitate problem solving in the AEC industry. 4.2) The first use case aimed to build 3D noise maps for urban environments using data from BIM and GIS. The Italian C.N.R. model was used for noise prediction. The highlight of this use case study is that by using BIM and GIS integration, the noise mapping can be performed at room level and the design models can be flexibly updated. 4.3) The second use case considered construction supply chain management (CSCM) using BIM and GIS integration. The allocation of consolidation centers for multiple construction sites, which is a problem seldom studied by previous literature, is formulated and solved by integrating BIM and GIS. 4.4) The third case aimed to develop a 3D underground utility management system for urban environments. The system uses modeling functions in BIM as data sources for utility management. Moreover, an algorithm was developed to allow transforming 2D CAD drawings into 3D utility lines.

622812.label: Major findings and research outcome
622812.value: 1) A methodology framework was developed to extract domain terminologies for GIS and green building information, which was used to evaluate the version changes in IFC and the sufficiency of IFC in representing GIS and green building design data. It is discovered that although IFC4 had more entities to represent GIS and green building design data, a number entities to represent GIS and green building design data are still missing. Based on the result, an extension to IFC4 schema was proposed. 2) A linguistic-based method for semi-automatic bidirectional mapping among IFC, CityGML and gbXML has been developed. The method can achieve satisfactory mapping results and can provide suggestions for mapping among IFC, CityGML and gbXML. 3) An instance-based method for bidirectional mapping among IFC, CityGML and gbXML using reference ontology has been developed in this project. The reference ontology was developed based on the studies of necessary information for supporting geographical and green building design information. Moreover, an extension to CityGML, called the Semantic City Model ADE, has been developed to allow CityGML to store data from IFC and gbXML files. 4) Based on the developed BIM-GIS integration, we have developed (i) a noise evaluation framework for urban environments, (ii) a construction supply chain management framework, and (iii) a 3D underground utility management framework. 5) Referred journal papers and conference papers have been published to present the methodology framework and the three use cases developed in this project. 6) The developed translator between IFC and CityGML has been packaged and made available in the project website, at http://ihome.ust.hk/~cejcheng/bimgis/. The website has also included the research methodology, major findings, and developed use cases in this project.

622812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
622812.value: 1) The developed reference ontology and bidirectional mapping are only applicable to IFC, CityGML and gbXML. Although they are the most widely used neutral data standard in the BIM, 3D GIS, and green building domains, respectively, other data standards exist in these domains. In the future, mapping with other data standards in these domains, such as Collada and COBie, would be studied and developed. 2) This study only considered building models. Other kinds of models, such as roads, bridges, and tunnels, could be considered in the future. 3) In this project, only BRep, swept solid and constructive solid geometries have been considered for solid geometry transformation. The clipping geometry in IFC, which is constructed from Boolean differences between swept area solids, half spaces and Boolean results, could be considered in the future.

622812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622812.value: Modeling the built environment digitally in three dimensions can support navigation, urban planning, disaster management, and energy consumption analysis. On the one hand, building information modeling (BIM) is an emerging technology for planning, design, construction and operations of individual buildings. On the other hand, geographical information system (GIS) supports storage, visualization and management of geospatial information of buildings at a regional level. The project aims to develop a theoretical framework for bidirectional mapping between 3D GIS models and BIM models. Linguistic-based, instance-based and schema mediation techniques have been used to develop the mapping framework. This project focuses on IFC and gbXML, which are the representative neutral data standards for BIM, and CityGML, which is the representative neutral data standard for 3D GIS. In this project, the developed integrated BIM-GIS framework has been used for (1) integrated indoor and outdoor noise evaluation for urban environments, (2) selection of suppliers and allocation of consolidation centers in construction supply chain management, and (3) 3D time-dependent clash detection and management of underground utility networks. The integration of BIM and 3D GIS can help address many other problems in the architectural, engineering and construction (AEC) discipline in both macroscopic and microscopic scales.

623112.label: Project Objectives
623112.value: To develop rational synthesis approaches for several chosen nanomaterials which have optical band-gaps covering red, green, and blue colors. In order to build full a color electronic retina, at least three types of nanowires with different band-gaps need to be identified. The candidate materials in this project include CdSe(red), CdS(green), ZnO(blue). Synthesis of these materials needs to be explored and three best candidates need to be identified. To understand optical properties of the chosen nanomaterials. Particularly, photoconductivity property of these materials needs to be explored in order to utilize them for light sensors. To assemble nanowires heterogeneously on flexible substrates. The electronic retina proposed in this work will be eventually built on a plastic substrate. The nanowire light sensing element will be assembled on plastic substrates using printing technique. To fabricate a nanowire-based electronic retina. In this proposed project we aim at fabricating micro-electrodes in contact with nanowires, and interconnects with a novel printing method To fabricate electronic eyes by integrating the electronic retina with optical components. Once the electronic retina is built, we aim at integrating a simple optical imaging system, resembling human eyes, with the electronic retina. To test the electronic eye with external light source and external circuits. Once an electronic eye is built, its functionality will be tested using external circuits together with computer software. We aim at reconstructing the object image projected onto the electronic retina on the computer to verify the electronic eye function.

623112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
623112.value: Semiconductor nanowires possess fascinating physical and chemical properties owing to their unique dimension and geometry. They have been considered as functional materials for nanoelectronics, optoelectronics, biological sensing, energy harvesting, etc. Optical and optoelectronic properties of semiconductor nanowires have attracted extensive research interests due to their size-dependent optical band-gap and the fact that the electronic properties of nanowires are more sensitive to light illumination than those of their bulk/thin film counterpart. Particularly, semiconductor nanowires have been investigated for laser, photodiode, optical waveguide, solar cells, etc. In the past, we have systematically investigated the photoconductivity property of various semiconductor nanowires, and successfully designed and fabricated all-nanowire photodetection circuits. Furthermore, we have demonstrated an all-nanowire gray-scale image sensor. Here we propose synthesis and investigation of several different types of semiconductor nanowires with different band-gaps for color photodetection, and utilization of these nanomaterials to design and fabricate a nanowire-based color image sensor on planar and non-planar substrates. The success of this project will demonstrate the feasibility of nanowire-based electronic eyes with high resolution and sensitivity, which can be used for robotic vision system and eventually bionic eyes. 半導體納米線由於其特殊的尺寸和形狀特性使得它具有奇特的物理與化學性能。迄今為 止，半導體納米線功能材料已經被用來製做納電子，光電子，生物傳感和壓電等納米器件。其中，半導體納米線由於其具有特定尺寸的光帶寬度，以及相比塊狀和薄膜材料，其對光照敏感性極大地增強，因而其光學和光電性能已經在世 界範圍內成為眾多科學家的研究熱點。特別的是，半導體納米線已經被成功 研製 成激光器，光電結，光波導管，太陽能電池等等。其中，我們研究小組已經系統地研究了各種半導體納米線的光電性能，並成功設計和構建了全基 於納米線的光傳 感芯片。另外，我們已經研製成功全基於納米線構建的灰色段圖像傳感器。因此，我們下一步的工作就是合成各種不同帶寬的半導體納米線，並進一步在平面或非平面上構建這種基於全納米線的彩色圖像傳感器。這種彩色圖像傳感器將能使得全基於納米線的電子眼獲得很高的分辨率和敏感性，因而將能廣泛應用於機器人視覺系統，並將使得電子仿生眼成為可能。

623112.label: Realisation of objectives
623112.value: The objectives have been achieved. We have successfully developed several approaches to fabricate various semiconductor materials including CdS, ZnO, etc. The optical properties of these nanowires have been investigated with optical simulations and experimental measurements. These materials have also been fabricated on flexible substrates and flexible electronic retina have been fabricated. Particularly, a printing method to fabricate nanowires and nanowire devices have been developed by us. And image sensing function has been tested with light source and external circuits.

We aim at reconstructing the object image projected onto the electronic retina on the computer to verify the electronic eye function.

623112.label: Major findings and research outcome
623112.value: Our major findings can be summarized as: 1. We discovered that highly ordered array of semiconductor nanowire arrays can be grown readily inside porous alumina templates. In this fashion, nanowire growth and integration can be achieve at the same time thus is very promising for high density device fabrication; 2. We have systematically investigated light propagation inside nanowires, and identified the relationship between light absorption and nanowire geometry, including their diameter and length. These results can facilitate future photonic device design, including photodetector, light-emitting diodes, etc.; 3. We have invented a nanowire printing method to fabricate inorganic semiconductor nanowires on plastic substrates. This printing approach is highly scalable with low-cost. And as metal electrodes can also be printed on the nanowires, all printable photodetectors have been realized. Importantly, we found that the devices made with this approach can demonstrate very high sensitivity. This result can inspire future high performance, flexible optoelectronic device design and fabrication.

623112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
623112.value: The results from this project suggest that semiconductor nanowires can be fabricated into high perform photodetectors on flexible substrates with low cost method. Further development can be suggested as: 1. Currently the single device dimension is rather large, integration density can be further increased in the future. This can be achieve by combining lithography methods. 2. Current photodetectors have a broadband optical response. Selective color response photodetector and full color photodetector should be developed in the future.

623112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
623112.value: The core component of an electronic eye is photodetector. In this project, we have developed approaches to make nanowire-based photodetector with very high sensitivity and mechanical flexibility. Particularly, we have invented a printing method to make both nanowires and photodetector devices. This approach is promising for large scale fabrication of photodetectors. Give the high performance of the photodetectors, they can be used for broad applications, including robotic eyes, artificial eyes for human, or simply sensors for our mobile devices.

623212.label: Project Objectives
623212.value: To develop a general theoretical model that can be used to analyze and predict the steady behavior of a multistage planar thermoelectric micro refrigerator. The effects of various factors on the cooling power capacity, cooling temperature, input power and COP will be explored. The theoretical model will be used to guide and optimize the design of the micro refrigerator. To design and fabricate a low-power, multistage, planar TE micro refrigerator with IC-compatible thermoelectric materials, which can provide a low working temperature for MEMS and electronic devices. The performance of the micro refrigerator will be experimentally characterized. To develop a measurement micro device and experimentally characterize the Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity of SiGe phononic thin films over a temperature range of 80-300 K.

623212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
623212.value: Efficient microscale refrigeration cooling is becoming highly attractive for micro electronics due to its capability of stabilizing the device temperature, increasing the operation speed, improving the reliability, and reducing noise levels. To achieve refrigeration cooling while reducing the system cost and complexity, a microscale refrigeration cooling system that can be directly integrated with the device is in high demand. As one of the few most promising techniques that can be downscaled to micro domain, thin film thermoelectric refrigeration provides an all-solid-state cooling solution, which offers a compact structure, fast thermal response, excellent controllability, high reliability and long lifetime. While conventional Te-based thermoelectric thin films are not appropriate for the integrated electronic cooling due to their high toxity, low mechanical strength, and incompatibility with standard IC fabrication process, normal IC-compatible thermoelectric materials, such as SiGe, are not suitable for refrigeration because of their low efficiency near room temperature. However, recent progress in research on the thermal transport in low dimensional structures shows that it is promising to significantly improve the performance of SiGe thin films through nanoengineering. We propose to develop a novel low-power thermoelectric micro refrigerator based on nanostructured SiGe films of enhanced performance for the on-chip refrigeration cooling of low-power MEMS and electronic devices. We will focus on optimizing the design of the thermoelectric micro refrigerator as well as enhancing the thermoelectric performance of SiGe thin films through nanoengineering. To achieve a high cooling performance and partly offset the request for high-performance thermoelectric materials, a low-power, self-supported, multistage, planar TE micro refrigerator will be designed and fabricated through microfabrication techniques. Its steady and transient behavior will be clarified. Meanwhile, we will develop high-performance nanostructured SiGe thin films by introducing nano pore arrays to form phononic structures. The effects of the phononic nano patterning on all the thermoelectric properties such as thermal conductivity, electrical conductivity and Seebeck coefficient will be experimentally investigated over a wide temperature range. Based on the experimental results, a fundamental understanding of phonon and electron transport in phononic thin films will be developed. The research output will be of both academic and industrial importance. 有效的微尺度冷卻對微電子器件的發展具有相當吸引力，因為這能穩定器件溫度，加快運算速度，提高系統的可靠性并降低熱噪聲。爲了降低系統成本和複雜性，急需發展能和電子器件直接集成的微冷卻系統。薄膜熱電冷卻提供了一個全固態的解決方案，它具有結構緊湊，響應迅速，易於控制，工作可靠，壽命長等優點。然而傳統的基於Te的熱電薄膜由於其毒性和低強度，與傳統的集成電路技術并不相容。而與集成電路技術相容的熱電材料如SiGe又往往在室溫附近效率很低。然而，最近在低維結構熱傳輸的研究表明，採用納米改性的手段，可以大幅度提高SiGe的性能。我們計劃在具有納米結構的高性能SiGe發展一款新型的的低能耗熱電微冷卻器，以用於芯片冷卻。我們將優化熱電製冷器的設計并同時通過納米改性提升熱電材料性能。所獲得的實驗測量結果也將有助于理解聲子和電子在聲子薄膜中的傳輸，這對學術和工業界都具有重要的價值。

623212.label: Realisation of objectives
623212.value: We conducted non-equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations to explore the possibility of using single-crystalline Si-based nanocomposites for thermoelectric applications. The key to improving the performance is to reduce the thermal conductivity k without deteriorating the electrical properties. We demonstrated that k of single-crystalline Si-based nanocomposites can be reduced to the alloy limit by embedding various nanoinclusions of similar lattice constants but different lattice orientations or space symmetries with respect to the matrix. The surprisingly low k is mainly due to the large mismatch between the acoustic phonon densities of states caused by the destruction of lattice periodicity at the interfaces between the nanoinclusions and matrix, which leads to the substantial reduction in phonon group velocity and relaxation time, as well as the enhancement of phonon localization. The increase in thermal resistance induced by lattice structure mismatch mainly comes from the nanoinclusions and the channels between them and is caused by the enhanced boundary scattering at the interfaces parallel to the heat flux. Approaching the alloy limit of k with potentially improved electrical properties by fillers will remarkably improve the figure of merit of single-crystalline Si-based nanocomposites and extend their application. This research also suggests that SiGe is a more promising candidate for thermoelectric applications. We then conducted comprehensive experimental research to achieve high-performance SiGe thin films for their potential applications in integrated microscale cooling. We first developed an integrated measurement platform which can measure the Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity of thin film. Both n-type and p-type polycrystalline silicon-germanium (SiGe) thin films were grown using low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD) and their thermoelectric properties were carefully characterized from 100 K to 300 K. The effects of different annealing treatments, doping concentration, composition and temperature on their thermoelectric properties were also explored. The naturally formed grain boundaries were found to play a crucial role in determining both the charge and thermal transport properties of the films. Particularly, the grain boundaries create energy barriers for charge transport which lead to different dependences of charge mobility on doping concentration and temperature from the bulk counterparts. Meanwhile, the unique columnar grain structures result in remarkable thermal conductivity anisotropy with the in-plane thermal conductivities of SiGe films about 50% lower than the cross-plane values. By optimizing the growth conditions and doping level, high room-temperature in-plane figure of merits (ZT) of 0.2 for p-type SiGe films and 0.16 for n-type SiGe films were achieved at 300 K, which are about 100% higher than the previous record for SiGe alloys, mainly due to the significant reduction in the in-plane thermal conductivity caused by nanograin boundaries. The low cost and excellent scalability of LPCVD render these high-performance SiGe films ideal candidates for thin-film thermoelectric applications. We also proposed a free-standing planar thermoelectric microrefrigerator based on thin film technologies to address the high-performance on-chip cooling and compatibility with microelectronics fabrication. We have developed an analytical model for single-stage and multi-stage planar thermoelectric microrefrigerators and various factors that might influence the performance have been considered. Good agreements with experiments and numerical simulations confirm the accuracy of the model developed. It was found that the free-standing structure can significantly boost the cooling performance. Both thermal and contact resistances were found to be important for the cooling performance of the proposed microfrigerators while they play different roles on the cold and hot sides of a refrigerator. The influence of the contact resistance on the optimal refrigerator design was also discussed. It was demonstrated that microrefrigerators based on IC-compatible low-cost SiGe thin films could potentially achieve a cooling temperature of more than 10 K near room temperature, rendering them competitive against the state-of-art microfrigerators based on toxic conventional heavy metal thermoelectrics such as Bi2Te3 and Sb2Te3. Based on the high-performance SiGe thin films and the optimized design, we fabricated planar single-stage and two-stage thermoelectric microcoolers based on IC-compatible nanograined SiGe thin films and characterized their cooling behaviors. SiGe thin films were grown by low pressure chemical vapor deposition process and patterned into n-type and p-type regions by a selective doping and photolithography process on Si substrates. The contact resistances were found to play important roles in decreasing the cooling performance. We have characterized the contact resistances of SiGe and various metals involving different deposition techniques and post treatments. The mechanisms for different contact resistances were systematically investigated. The maximum cooling temperatures of 9.3 K and 11.2 K have been achieved by the single-stage and two-stage microcoolers respectively with power inputs of less than 100 μW at room temperature (300K).

623212.label: Major findings and research outcome
623212.value: 1. Two PhD students were trained in this project. One of them received his PhD degrees in April 2017. The other PhD student is expected to graduate by the end of 2017. 2. Six journal papers have been published based on the research results from this project. One manuscript is under review. 3. Molecular dynamics simulations show that SiGe alloy is a better candidate for thermoelectric applications than nanostructured Si. 4. An integrated measurement platform that can measure the Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity of thin films over a wide temperature range has been developed. 5. High-performance n-type and p-type nanograined SiGe thin films were grown by scalable low pressure chemical vapor deposition. The influence of various factors including the growth conditions and post-treatments has been explored. 6. The naturally formed column-like grains are found to be able to efficiently suppress the heat transfer in SiGe thin films without much influence on charge transport. By optimizing the film growth conditions, up to 100% improvement over the record of bulk SiGe alloy has been achieved in nanograined SiGe thin films. 7. A free-standing planar microcooler design has been proposed and modeling shows that it has advantages over previous designs. A theoretical model has been developed to predict the cooling behavior of the proposed design. Good agreements with experimental results and finite element method validate the proposed model. 8. Single-stage and multi-stage free-standing planar microrefrigerators based on nanograined SiGe thin films have been developed and tested. Cooling temperatures of more than 10K have been achieved in SiGe thin film microrefrigerators with the power inputs of less than 100 microWatts.

623212.value: The developed high-performance SiGe thin films can potentially be used in many thermoelectric thin-film applications such as thermoelectric microcoolers, micro generators and sensors. Such devices can be developed based on the techniques developed in this research.

623212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
623212.value: Efficient microscale refrigeration cooling is highly attractive for micro electronics due to its unique advantages in microscale thermal management. To achieve refrigeration cooling while reducing the system cost and complexity, a microscale all-solid-state thermoelectric refrigeration cooling system that can be directly integrated with the device is needed. While conventional Te-based thermoelectric thin films are not appropriate for integrated electronic cooling due to their high toxity, low mechanical strength, and incompatibility with the standard IC fabrication process, normal IC-compatible thermoelectric materials, such as SiGe thin films, are also unsuitable for refrigeration because of their low efficiency near room temperature. We have found that the introduction of columnar nanograins can significantly improve the performance of SiGe thin films and the achieved figure of merits can be even higher than those of the best bulk alloy, mainly due to the greatly suppressed heat transfer in those nanostructured thin films. We developed the fabrication techniques to grow high-performance nanograined SiGe thin films and clarified the influences of various factors. We also developed novel low-power planar thermoelectric micro refrigerators based on nanostructured SiGe films of enhanced performance for on-chip refrigeration with low power inputs. A high cooling temperature up to 11.2 K has been achieved by a two-stage SiGe thin-film microfrigerator with less than 100 uW power input, a record for Si-based thin-film coolers. The research outputs from this research will benefit the development of novel thermoelectric thin-film devices.

623312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
623312.value: Before permission is granted for effluent to be discharged into the environment, it is necessary to provide local authorities with evidence that the concentrations of the effluent are within the limits as set out by environmental laws. Special engineering structures are designed to rapidly reduce the concentrations of the effluent in the vicinity of the discharge location by making use of the mixing capabilities of the jet flow. For discharging large quantities of effluent into the environment, the dilution of effluent can be increased further by discharging the effluent through multiple ports rather than a single port. The design of discharge structures is directly related to the behaviour of the jet flows they generate; therefore a successful design depends on accurate predictions of this behaviour. For flows generated by a single port, detailed understanding of the jet flow has led to commercially available mathematical predictive models that are used with reasonable confidence in engineering practice. Flows generated by multiport diffusers are more complex, as individual three-dimensional jets merge into a quasi two-dimensional plane jet, and have received much less attention. As a result, estimates from mathematical predictive models of the trajectory, spread and dilution of multiport discharges can vary significantly. The proposed research aims to further our understanding of multiport discharges, especially during the transition from individual jets to a single merged jet flow, thereby underpinning the development of predictive models. The proposal is based on a two stage, laboratory experimental investigation designed to measure detailed aspects of multiport discharges. During the first stage the light attenuation flow visualization technique will be upgraded to enable measurements of the integrated concentration distribution of multiport discharges. The second stage will consist of several groups of experiments each focusing on different aspects of multiport jet discharges. The first group of experiments will investigate double port discharges in a moving ambient, the second group will investigate negatively buoyant multiport discharges and the final group will investigate horizontally discharged multiport jets in a cross-flow. Results of the experimental data include the dilution and spread along the flow trajectory and the characterization of the cross-sectional concentration distributions. These results will be used to develop an integral model for the prediction of the behaviour of multiport discharges. The model’s predictions and those of commercially available predictive models will be evaluated through comparisons with the detailed experimental data. 當污水被排放至受納水體（如江河，湖泊和海洋等）前，該項目發起者需向相關部門提供有關的數據證明所排污水的濃度符合環境保護法律標準，以獲取排放許可。為達此目的，工程建設者常利用噴射流同周圍水體的高混摻性能，設計方案用來快速稀釋排污口近區的污水濃度。當需排放大量污水時，多噴嘴排污管段（多孔擴散器）明顯地較於單噴嘴排污管段（單孔擴散器）在稀釋污水濃度上有更大優越性。 噴射流的擴散情況直接受其排污管段設計影響，因此，一個成功的排污管段設計則充分依賴於噴射流擴散模型的精確預測。對於單孔噴射流，市場上的商業模擬軟件已可在實際工程應用中幫助使用者達此目的。多孔擴散器產生的多孔噴射流卻因為其複雜的擴散情況，相應的認知和研究相對較少，例如由若干個單一的三維噴射流融合成類似於二維平面噴射流。同時，現有的商業模擬軟件無法對多孔噴射流的擴散情況進行合理有效的預測，不同的模擬軟件所模擬出來的噴射流軌跡，擴散半徑，稀釋度會大有不同。 本研究旨在進一步探索多孔噴射流，特別是當若干個單一的噴射流融合成一個噴射流的過渡區域，以此來為建立一個全面精準的多孔噴射流預測模型提供依據。本研究計劃通過兩個階段，以實驗方法實現對多孔噴射流的探索。第一階段，利用優化配置的光衰減器系統（流體可視化技術的一種）測量多孔噴射流內示踪質的濃度稀釋分佈。第二階段，實行若干組不同初始條件的多孔噴射流實驗，以觀察各自的擴散特性。第一組主要研究在流動受納水體中的雙孔噴射流；第二組側重於負浮力（噴射流密度大於受納水體密度）多孔噴射流；第三組則是在交叉流情況下的橫向多孔噴射流。每組實驗分析結果均包含噴射流的軌跡，擴散半徑，稀釋度和橫截面濃度分佈等，以此為據，建立新的多孔噴射流的預測模型。最後，該模型會同現今一些商業數學模型做比較和評估，從而完善和提高多孔噴射流模型的預測精度

623512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
623512.value: This project exploits a recently developed large area, high quality graphene synthesis process, along with DNA-origami lithography technology, to create new manufacturing techniques for graphene electronics that have not been previous possible. The project represents an integration of graphene chemistry with material science and engineering, nanofabrication, applied physics and nano/bio-interfaced technology. The approach is to define the graphene structures by utilizing the DNA-origami as template, where atomically precise pores (and pore arrays) and edge structures can be shaped, and subsequently to perform comprehensive variable electronic transport measurements on these samples for comparison with theoretical predictions. This project addresses critical deficiencies limiting practical application of graphene: a) the inability to accurately position array of graphene devices; b) the lack of band-gap, and concomitantly the low driving current, of graphene devices; and c) the difficulties to control over the atomic structure and the edges of the graphene nanodevice, especially for spatial features smaller than 10 nm. This project will advance our fundamental knowledge on graphene superlattice structures, which will enable scientific exploration of graphene nanoelectronic devices with novel structures at a size resolution two orders of magnitude smaller than currently possible, with an unprecedented level of control over the atomic structure and the edges of the nanodevices. The broader impacts of this research involve the development of commercial applications of graphene with substantial benefit to society. The outreach efforts of the program will emphasis on training undergraduate and postgraduate students, and improving research infrastructure through establishing international collaborations. 本項目計劃採用我們新近開發的大面積、高質量的石墨烯合成技術，引進DNA折疊體刻蝕技術，來創造一種新的、前所未有的石墨烯電子產品製造工藝。該項目集石墨烯化學，材料科學與工程，納米製造，應用物理和納米/生物界面技術等多學科為一體。我們的策略是利用DNA折疊體作為模板來定義石墨烯結構，以達到原子精度的孔（或孔陣列）和及可控邊界，並隨後對這些結構進行全面的電子傳輸測量，檢驗理論預測。此項目意圖解決以下限制的石墨烯的應用的關鍵問題：a）無法精確實現石墨烯器件陣列精確定位; b）缺乏的帶隙，並且可導電流低; 和c）無法控制原子結構和石墨烯的納米中石墨烯的邊界器件，尤其是10 納米以下尺度。 該項目將大力推進石墨烯超晶格結構的基礎研究，從而實現比現有技術水平小兩個數量級、具有新穎結構的石墨烯納米電子器件，達到對石墨烯器件的原子結構和邊界達到原子精度的控制。本研究涉及的更廣泛影響包括實現石墨烯的商業應用的石墨烯，創造巨大的社會效應。該計劃的工作將重點放在培養本科生和研究生，通過建立國際合作研究，提升我們的研究環境。

623512.label: Realisation of objectives
623512.value: Graphene, along with other two-dimensional materials is a rising star in material field. Graphene nanoelectronics is reported to show many exceptional properties such as unusual quantum confinement effects, half metallic behavior, unique magnetic effects, and the potential for ultra-fast electronics sensors. The major bottleneck for of using graphene for electronics is mainly their intrinsic lacking of bandgaps. Potential solution to open a bandgap includes to the use of quantum confinement and/or edge effects by patterning graphene in the form of a nanoribbon or quantum dot. A major scientific and potentially the most important technological breakthrough has been accomplished by this research which shows, for the first time, large area, high quality graphene synthesis process has been developed along with DNA-origami lithography technology, that enables us to create new manufacturing techniques for graphene electronics. We have demonstrated a successful integration of graphene chemistry with material science and engineering, nanofabrication, applied physics and nano/bio-interfaced technology. With this grant support, we have educated 4 PhD students and 2 M.Phil students, along with 11 peer-reviewed publications in high-profile journals. More specifically, the proposed objectives in the original proposed have been achieved as detailed in the following section. 1) Precise control over the fabrication of porous graphene nanostructure so that the edge and quantum confinement effects can be harnessed. The first step is to prepare DNA origami structures with rationally designed shapes. This is achieved by adapting a previously published method. We first fabricated DNA origami on mica substrate with designed shape structures such as square, W-shape etc. Moreover, we have also demonstrate the possibility of self-assemble the structure into large periodic structures. The other major step involved in this DNA-origami lithographic method is how to assemble on graphene surface and the use of it as the lithography mask. In this process, single strand DNA assemble and forms the origami structures, exposing hydrophilic phosphate groups, while the hydrophobic groups contained inside the structure. In order to deposit DNA origamis to the surface of graphene, the DNA origami solutions were diluted by 50 % ethanol and drop onto the exfoliated graphene. The structures of fabricated DNA origamis has been observed by atomic force microscopy, showing the DNA origami height of around 2 nm. We have also demonstrate the fabrication of graphene point contacts by photolithography. We have shown a scalable photolithography process for the graphene field effect transistors with a consistently high carrier mobility across multiple devices. The graphene sensor arrays were fabricated using the bubble transfer of gold cluster decorated CVD grown graphene (Wu, R.; et al. Carbon, 2016, 98,138–143), followed by a photolithography patterning of the FET channels and a thermal annealing process. The resulting graphene FET devices show extraordinary electrical performance, i.e., a hole mobility of 3593 ± 709 cm2/(V·s), more than two orders of magnitude higher than the mobility of AuNP decorated reduced graphene oxide FETs. Such high mobility arises mostly from the adoption of a protective photoresist in the photolithography process to reduce the photoresist contamination on graphene, as confirmed by AFM, XPS and electrical characterization. In addition, the novel design of the FET in which the graphene is carved into a four-probe configuration allows us to eliminate the contact resistance that dominated electron transport properties. The AuNP-Gr-FETs were readily functionalized by a variety of chemistry steps and were capable of delivering a DNA detection limit of 1 nM. 2) A detailed understanding of graphene chemistry and physics. A major efforts has been put into understand the graphene chemistry and physics, which in turn allows us to control the synthesis of graphene and the device fabrication. Graphene properties are determined by it is structures, in which the grain size of single crystal is the key for controlling the electrical and mechanical properties. We have demonstrate the synthesis of sub-centimeter single crystal graphene, the largest single crystal graphene at the time when the paper is published (i.e. ACS Nano, 2013, 7 (10), 9480–9488). We have demonstrated on how the surface oxygen limited the nucleation density which leads to the large size growth. They has also experimentally demonstrate that the possibility of continued growth for graphene (Gan, L.; et al., Chem. Mater. 2014, 26 (14), 4137–4143). With this technique, we were able to successfully grow millimeter-size secondary single-crystal graphene structures with the same lattice structure and orientation as the original seeds. This is the first time that such concept was proved experimentally. We have also observed that atomic registry has strong impact on controlling the electronic structure and properties of graphene due to localized strain and localized charge distribution. In a recent publication, we has shown the direct experimental evidence of the correlation between the physical structure and chemical reactivity (Ding, Y.; et al. Chem. Mater., 2016, 28 (4), 1034–1039). We report here an experimental observation that the electron transfer chemistry is significantly modified in twisted bilayer graphene (tBLG) by investigating the results of chemical functionalization with diazonium salts. The relative reaction rate for diazonium salts grafting on tBLG is much higher than that on AB-stacking graphene. Gerischer−Marcus electron transfer theory analysis, along with electronic structures calculations, indicates that different reactivity mainly results from the distinct variation of Density of States distribution in the gap region. Our results suggest a venue to separate and sort different stacking modes of bilayer graphene for various promising applications in nanoelectronics. 3) Exploration of porous graphene nanostructure for chemical and biological sensing and energy-harvest applications. We have successfully demonstrated the fabrication of a graphene-based field effect transistor (GFET) incorporated in a two-dimensional paper network format (2DPNs). In this kind of configuration, paper was used as both a gate dielectric and an easy-to-fabricate vessel for holding the solution with the target molecules in question. The choice of paper enables a simpler alternative approach to the construction of a GFET device. We have successfully demonstrates that droplet-shape hollow Ni3S2 nanoparticles, as well as the corresponding partially nickel-filled nanoparticles, can be incorporated into two-dimensional graphene electrodes using a facile process at moderate reaction condition, and then examined as electrochemical supercapacitor materials for energy storage application (Ou, X.; et al.J. Mater. Chem. A, 2014, 2,19214. Ou, X. et al. RSC Adv., 2016, 6, 10280 - 10284.). We found that the shape of the nanoparticles is dominantly droplet-shape, with shape complementary to graphene support, which ensures good contact between them. Our method provides a new approach for controlling the structure of graphene-based nanocomposites and consequently to use them for high performance supercapacitor application.
