623512.label: Major findings and research outcome
623512.value: This project allows us to advance our fundamental knowledge on graphene superlattice structures, which will enable scientific exploration of graphene nanoelectronic devices with an unprecedented level of control. 1. One of the major finding of this research is the development of a new method to control the nucleation density for graphene growth and eventually lead to the growth of sub-centimeter single crystalline graphene grains, with diameter up to 5.9 mm, during the atmospheric pressure chemical vapor deposition. We demonstrates the ability to control the nucleation density by adjusting degree of oxidation and hydrogen annealing duration, and consequently to control graphene grains sizes. In addition, we found that hydrogen plays dual roles on copper morphology during the whole growth process, i.e. removing surface irregularities and at the same time, etching the copper surface to produce small nanoparticles that has only limited effect on nucleation for graphene growth. A bandgap has been observed to open for controlled graphene grown with this method. Such high quality graphene facilitate the deposition of DNA-origami on graphene and enables us to study the structure-property correlations. 2. We have significantly contributed to the understanding of graphene structure and it is electronic and chemical properties. For the first time, we report an experimental observation that the electron transfer chemistry is significantly modified in twisted bilayer graphene (tBLG) by investigating the results of chemical functionalization with diazonium salts. The relative reaction rate for diazonium salts grafting on tBLG is much higher than that on AB-stacking graphene. Gerischer−Marcus electron transfer theory analysis, along with electronic structures calculations, indicates that different reactivity mainly results from the distinct variation of Density of States distribution in the gap region. 3. We have that high-performance electrochemical supercapacitor can be fabricated using high quality graphene materials as nanoparticle support. Our work has resulted a series of published peer-reviewed articles. Moreover, by tuning the nanoparticle structures, we can form a variety of particle morphology that optimized device for energy storage application (Ou, X.; et al.J. Mater. Chem. A, 2014, 2,19214. Ou, X. et al. RSC Adv., 2016, 6, 10280 - 10284.) We found that the shape of the nanoparticles is dominantly droplet-shape, with shape complementary to graphene support, which ensures good contact between them. Our method provides a new approach for controlling the structure of graphene-based nanocomposites and consequently to use them for high performance supercapacitor application.

623512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
623512.value: Our understanding resulted from this research can be applied to many novel new materials. For example, many new 2D materials such as MoS2 and MoTe2 can also be produced from atmospheric pressure chemical vapor deposition. Using the approached developed , it would become possible to control their structure and consequently to use them for different application.

623512.value: Graphene has become an important material for a variety of applications. The major obstacle for application of graphene in electronics is that it lack of bandgap and thus cannot be directly used for semiconducting materials. A major scientific and technological breakthrough has been accomplished by this research, which shows, for the first time, large area, high quality graphene synthesis process has been developed, along with DNA-origami lithography technology that enables us to create new manufacturing techniques for graphene electronics. This project advance our fundamental knowledge on graphene chemistry and physics, which enable us to train undergraduate and postgraduate students in science and technology field, and improves research infrastructure of Hong Kong through establishing international collaborations.

623612.label: Project Title(Chinese)
623612.value: Towards Mass Adoption of Electric Vehicles - Overcoming the Range and Resale Anxieties

623612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
623612.value: The diminishing oil reserves and rising concerns over the environment compels the transportation industry to focus on the development of Electric Vehicles (EVs). However, the key to the successful mass adoption of EVs depends not only on technology advancements, but also the establishment of the associated infrastructure network and market mechanisms. In this project, we will study two major barriers to the mass adoption of EVs, known as the range anxiety and the resale anxiety, and how they can best be alleviated with optimally deployed supporting infrastructure and appropriate service contracts. Range anxiety arises from the limited travel range (typically about 150km) of EVs, that is constrained by battery capacity. The concern that travel requirements may exceed this range precludes many potential adopters from considering EVs. To address this, range extension technologies, such as quick charging and battery swapping, have been proposed by the industry to quickly “refuel” EVs when their batteries are depleted. However, before committing to the significant investment of adopting EVs, users would like to see an infrastructure network with comprehensive coverage that is accessible (i.e., deployed) at reasonable cost. Our first goal of the project is to investigate the optimal deployment of range extension facilities, taking into account the uncertainty in adoption rates at the planning stage due to the wait-and-see mentality of potential users. To promote mass adoption from the economic angle, financing schemes have been designed such that purchase and usage costs of EVs, over the useful lives of the vehicles, are favorable compared to conventional cars. However, the resale anxiety still remains: the uncertain future availability of a second-hand market for used EVs, which hinges on the scale of adoption, poses a significant risk for the purchase. Our second goal is to identify effective designs of financing service contracts and infrastructure coverage plans that jointly mitigate this resale anxiety and the range anxiety simultaneously. In our proposed research, we take into account customers’ adoption behavior under uncertainty. Our proposed models incorporate conflicting perspectives of various agents (government, private firms, and customers), by utilizing techniques from game theory, robust optimization and network location. Our proposed models are well-grounded theoretically and will provide practical methodologies and insights supporting infrastructure network and service contract design decisions for practitioners. This research will serve as the cornerstone of the development of a research program in EV logistics and economics, a high-impact, yet wide-open research area. 由於石油儲備日漸減少和各界對環境保護的關注，運輸行業正致力研發電動汽車。然而，要使電動汽車普及應用，關鍵不僅取決於技術的進步，還須建立相關的基礎設施網絡和市場機制。在這個項目中，我們將研究大規模採用電動車兩個主要障礙--範圍焦慮和轉售焦慮，探討如何能以基礎配套設施和相應的服務合同等方法以舒緩大眾對電動車的焦慮。在我們提出的研究中，我們考慮到用者採用電動車的行為模式。我們所提出的博弈和優化模型涵蓋政府，私人機構和用戶的不同觀點。這項研究將成為電動車作業和經濟研究領域中的一個發展基石。

623912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
623912.value: Nanofluidic electronics refer to devices which exploit surface charge density that gives rise to electrokinetic transport of fluid in and around well-defined microscopic structures with at least one characteristic length scale below 100nm. Analogous to the solid-state electronics where n-type or p-type semiconductors form a conduction channel for charge carriers (free electrons or holes), these devices make use of fluid channels filled with an electrolyte and in which chemical or biological species (ions or molecules) serve as major charge carriers. With the possibility of establishing and adjusting well-defined surface potentials through integrated microelectrodes, unique properties including permselectivity, concentration polarization, and partitioning of molecules arise in the nanostructures especially for characteristic length scales comparable to Debye screening length. Nanofluidic electronics is likely to deliver a new class of devices, which could offer new capabilities besides the increased speed, resolution, and sensitivity in the analysis of biomolecules. The ability to electrically analyze biomolecules in real-time and free of foreign labels is extremely appealing for an integrated portable system and could have vast implications for the future of health care and the quality of human life. Above all, these devices providing controlled environments commensurate with molecules may enable new experiments that bring insight into fundamental studies of biomolecules. The last decade has witnessed numerous reports on the successful demonstration of these devices and their application for molecular analysis. Each of these studies has made a notable contribution towards the proof of concept experiments. Yet, a major bottleneck has remained in the making of more robust and reproducible devices in sufficient quantities to advance beyond a proof of concept. More specifically, the challenge lies with the integration of well-defined nanometer-sized structures (e.g. nanochannels, nanotubes or nanocapillaries). At present, nanostructures can be made by top-down or bottom-up techniques requiring either expensive lithography or tedious assembly. Meanwhile, indirect and yet insightful strategies prescribed to work around this problem appear temporary remedies. Here, based on an innovative fabrication technology, we propose to build and investigate a family of nanofluidic electronic devices for the analysis of biomolecules. The novelty arises from a unique and convenient method of making nanocapillaries and their integration with microelectrodes for electronic gating. Specifically, we propose (1) a nanofluidic diode for biomolecular sensing through modulation of ionic rectification; (2) a nanofluidic transistor for field-effect regulation of DNA translocation speed, and (3) a nanofluidic charge-coupled device (nanofluid-CCD) for separation and enrichment of proteins. 納流控電子是指至少有一维特徵尺度爲100 nm 以下的流控電子裝置 。通過利用物質的表面電荷，該類設備可以實現生物分子在微觀流體通道中的電動学運輸。 類似于固態電子器件中n-型或p-型半導體形成的傳導電荷載體（自由電子或空穴）的信道，這些器件依靠流體通道中填充的電解質以及其中的化學或生物物質（離子或 分子）作為主要的電荷載體，並運用集成微電極來建立和調整納米流體通道（特徵長度與Debye屏蔽長度相當）的表面電位，进而實現一些特定的功能，例如選擇性滲透，物質濃度極化和分子分離。納流控電子提供除了增加生物分子分析的速度，分辨率和靈敏度之外的新功能。這很可能使微流控裝置上升到一個新的台階 。這類通過電學方法來實時分析生物分子，並不需要外部標記的科技正是一個便攜式醫學檢測系統所需要的，並可能對提升未來的醫療保健和人類的生活質量有重大的影響。綜上所述，這些裝置可以爲生物分子的基礎研究帶來新的突破。 過去十年里，我們見證了許多這類装置和相關分子分析應用的成功示範。這些研究中的每一個都在概念證明和實驗拓展上作出了顯著貢獻。然而，大規模制造穩定的和可重複使用的設備是阻礙這類裝置脫離概念性實驗並走上實際應用市場的主要瓶頸。更具體的，定義良好的納米結構（例如集成化納米通道，納米管）是一個重大挑戰。目前，納米結構只能通過昂貴的光刻或繁瑣的微加工步驟，運用自頂向下或自底向上的技術來實現。于此同時，一些間接的但有見地的方法可能是解決這些問題的補救措施。 在這裡，我們提出了一個基于創新性製造技術的納流控電子設備的制造和 生物分子的分析 。我們的創新性來自與一個獨特的，方便的制造納米流体通道的方法及其用于調控的微電極的集成。具體而言，我們准備著手于開發（1）基于離子整流的納流控二極管，用來實現生物分子檢測；（2）納流控場效應晶體管，用於調節DNA轉運速度；和（3）納流控電荷耦合器件（納米流體-CCD），用來分離和富集蛋白質。

623912.label: Realisation of objectives
623912.value: This was a fabrication intensive project and the nanofluidic devices proposed involved three-dimensional nanostructures that are non-trivial to fabricate through lithography-based and semiconductor processing techniques. Thus, a significant portion of our effort has been vested in addressing the issues arising from the fabrication of such nanostructures. A further major effort dealt with demonstrating the intended applications of these nanostructures for the first time. Despite many hurdles, both of the objectives have been met to a reasonable degree. First milestone is the fabrication and characterization of cylindrical nanocapillary structures, crucial for novel nanofluidic diodes and transistors. We managed to fabricate cylindrical glass nanocapillaries as narrow as 50 nm and demonstrated their utility for stretching lambda-phage DNA under physical confinement. Such nanocapillaries are unique in the sense that they are integrated in a glass layer deposited on silicon and patterned without using advanced lithography techniques. The process takes advantage of thermal reflow of a non-planar glass layer on silicon and its subsequent 3D shape transformation into cylindrical microcapillaries. Extended thermal anneal shrinks their diameter, transforming them into nanocapillaries. In addition to fabrication of the nanocapillaries, we developed a model describing their formation mechanism under given process constraints. We reported our results in a peer-reviewed journal article appeared in Biomicrofluidics (Impact factor ~3.36). Second milestone is the development of a methodology for sensing DNA and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) products using the concept of nanofluidic diode. While working on the integrated process for nanofluidic diodes and transistors, we concurrently developed a detection methodology leveraging glass nanopipettes. Glass nanopipettes, although they lack the integrated sample delivery mechanism, can be readily pulled from glass capillary tubes on a commercial bench-top puller and offer a cost-effective rapid route to nanofluidic diodes without the requirement of a cleanroom process. Using nanopipettes, we demonstrated a label-free electrical method of quantifying PCR products from an unpurified PCR mixture. The method leverages intrinsic charge of DNA to modulate ion current rectification in a nanofluidic diode that can be evaluated through current-voltage measurements. Briefly, the bare nanopipette tip exposed to cationic polyelectrolyte poly-L-lysine (PLL) adsorbs a thin layer of PLL on the negatively charged glass surface and thus switches permselectivity to anions; negative currents become suppressed. Subsequently, the same tip exposed to DNA adsorbs a thin layer of DNA on the PLL and accordingly switches permselectivity to cations; positive currents become suppressed. We showed that not only does the reversal of the rectification direction signal the presence of DNA but also report its concentration. This is because the reversal of the rectification direction occurs gradually at a rate commensurate with DNA mass concentration in the range relevant to PCR conditions. We also showed that nanopipettes can be reproducibly used without any degradation to their sensitivity upon regenerating their surface with a PLL coating following each measurement. We further demonstrated that nanopipettes allow the PCR progress monitored through simple electrical measurements. We reported our results in a peer-reviewed journal article appeared in Biosensors and Bioelectronics (Impact factor ~7.47). Third milestone is the demonstration of a unique integrated nanofluidic diode and its use for detection of proteins, specifically Troponin-T (cTnT). cTnT is an important cardiac biomarker released into the circulation by a damaged cardiac muscle due to an acute myocardial infarction. We completed characterization of such nanofluidic diodes integrated into sample-delivery microfluidics using a cleanroom process. The process is an extension of that for the originally proposed structure with a slight deviation in the design to overcome challenges encountered in the process technology. The proposed designs are in-plane structures based on an integrated conical glass nanocapillary. However, with a simple change in the design to an out-of-plane configuration, we achieved nanofluidic diode function based on nanoslit structures and characterized their sensor calibration plots for the selective detection of cTnT. The structure features a planar nanoslit array where each nanoslit is defined at a nominal width of 70 nm over a micrometer-scale silicon trench without the use of high-resolution patterning techniques. Through vapor deposition, a glass layer is placed at a nonuniform thickness, tapering the trench profile upward and contributing to the triangular nanoslit structure. This asymmetric profile is essential for ionic current rectification at various pH values, ionic strengths, and captured target species, which modulate the surface-charge density within the sensitive region of the nanoslit. The nanoslit, unlike nanopores, offers only one-dimensional confinement, which appears to be adequate for reasonable rectification. We also implemented a surface functionalization protocol that employs specific antibodies and differs from the approach described for the detection of PCR products on the nanopipettes. We achieved a label-free detection limit of 10 fg/mL (~0.3 fM) cTnT in buffer as well as 10 pg/mL (~300 fM) in untreated human serum. This ultrasensitive detection arises from monolithic integration of a unique nanofluidic diode structure that is highly robust and amenable to site-specific surface modification. The measurements are found in quantitative agreement with the diode simulations for the first time established on a pH-dependent and salt-dependent surface-charge model. We reported our results in a peer-reviewed journal article appeared in Nano Letters (Impact factor ~13.78). The fourth and last milestone is the demonstration of a unique integrated nanofluidic transistor for the field-effect control of DNA translocation speed. Based on the glass nanocapillaries and their thermal reflow process (established by first milestone), we built a nanofluidic transistor. In the transistor, a single nanocapillary is surrounded by gate electrode (doped silicon crystal) along its entire length. Moreover, we also applied atomic layer deposition (ALD) of an alumina layer to further shrink the nanocapillary controllably down to a 50-nm diameter. We validated the field-effect transistor behavior on the gating of the ionic conductance and transport of proteins. We subsequently studied the gating of DNA translocation by measuring discrete current dips associated with single λ-DNA translocation events under a source-to-drain bias of 1 V. We also extracted the translocation speeds under various gate bias conditions by fitting event histograms of the measured translocation time to the first passage time distributions obtained from a simple one-dimensional biased diffusion model. We observed a positive gate bias to slow the translocation of single λ-DNA chains markedly; the translocation speed was reduced by an order of magnitude from 18.4 mm/s obtained under a floating gate down to 1.33 mm/s under a positive gate bias of 9 V. Therefore, by simply tuning the gate bias, we demonstrated on this device a dynamic and flexible regulation of the DNA translocation speed, which is vital for single-molecule sequencing. Importantly, we realized this transistor through a conventional semiconductor microfabrication process without the requirement of advanced lithography, which can be potentially further developed into a compact electronic single-molecule sequencer. We reported our results in a peer-reviewed journal article appeared in ACS Nano (Impact factor ~13.33). In conclusion, by second and third milestones, we met our goal stated in Objective 1, whereas by first and last (fourth) milestones, we met our goal stated in Objective 2.

623912.label: Major findings and research outcome
623912.value: A key outcome is the development of novel silicon-based nanofluidic devices for label-free biomolecular analysis. An underlying theme in all these is to leverage standard semiconductor processing techniques without the use of advanced lithography so that the devices can be manufactured in batch mode for mass use leveraging the economies of scale. Therefore, their use would not be limited to research settings. The research demonstrated two nanofluidic devices: a diode and a transistor. Nanofluidic diode is similar to an electronic diode and generates a nonlinear (rectified) current-voltage relation. The rectification depends on the surface charge, which can be modulated by the presence of molecules such as proteins and nucleic acids carrying intrinsic electric charge. Thus, nanofluidic diode can be used as a label-free biosensor to detect the concentration of specific molecules. Nanofluidic transistor is likewise similar to an electronic field-effect transistor and modulates carrier transport using a gate bias. Here, electronic charge carriers are macromolecules such as proteins and nucleic acids instead of free electrons or holes. Nanofluidic transistor can be applied to regulate the speed of a single DNA strand, which has implications in pore sequencing. Along these developments, the research also made contribution to fabrication and biosensing techniques. Theoretical modeling and experiments revealed how key parameters influence the critical dimension (diameter) of an in-plane cylindrical glass nanocapillary integrated on silicon, which was later used in the construction of a nanofluidic transistor (see Publication 1 in Section 8, and Publications 1 and 2 in Section 9, Part C). A simple nanofluidic diode was constructed out of a heat-pulled glass nanopipette and demonstrated as a label-free biosensor for detecting nucleic acid amplicons in PCR (see Publication 2 in Section 8, Part C). Nanofluidic diode is based on a conical out-of-plane nanoslit array integrated on silicon and can be used as an ultrasensitive label-free biosensor for the detection of proteins and nucleic acids. It can detect cardiac biomarker protein in untreated human serum down to 10 pg/mL or ~300 fM (see Publications 3 in Sections 8 and 9, Part C). Nanofluidic transistor is based on a single in-plane glass/alumina nanocapillary integrated on silicon. It can slow down the translocation of a single DNA by an order of magnitude under a positive gate bias 9 V (see Publication 4 in Section 8, Part C). These outcomes led to the graduation of a postgraduate student in PhD (see Section 10, Part C).

623912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
623912.value: In either objective, there is room for further development. In objective 1, regarding nanofluidic diode, the process yield can be enhanced significantly with a slight variation. The yield is low (below 20%) and can be increased to above 60% by leveraging atomic layer deposition of alumina to define the nanoslit critical size. Although having already reached ultrasensitive levels, the sensitivity can be also improved by replacing nanoslits with nanopores while maintaining the same integration process. All these developments are being further pursued in our laboratory. In objective 2, regarding nanofluidic transistor, the device can be further developed into an electronic (nanopore) sequencer. Our motivation in developing such transistor is to counter the well-known issue that has been hindering nanopore-sequencing technology: A single DNA strand zips through the nanopore so fast that the measurement electronics has no time to read and resolve individual bases. The field-effect transistor with its gate bias could slow down the DNA strand. There requires integrating the transistor with a sequencer and could be performed in various ways. However, it should be taken into consideration that most nanopores are defined in a thin membrane in out-of-plane configuration unlike in-plane configuration of the transistor.

623912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
623912.value: Macromolecules like proteins and DNA (genes) serve crucial functions within human body and the abnormalities associated with such macromolecules present numerous diseases. Thus technologies that can probe and measure various aspects of proteins and genes are of utmost value for assessing abnormalities and timely diagnosis of diseases. Nanotechnology that has delivered modern computer microchips is among the best candidates for fulfilling this task because it can provide microscopic tools at a critical size comparable to those of macromolecules. Using nanotechnology, this research project has demonstrated two new microchips, one for electronic detection of a specific protein molecule in human blood and the other for facilitating electronic sequencing of a gene in a nanopore sequencer by regulating the transport of a DNA. While the former can be applied to many diseases, the latter has more fundamental implications in sequencing DNA and diagnosing genetic diseases. For instance, protein sensor microchip has been successfully tested on the detection of a protein called troponin in human plasma. Plasma troponin is an indicator of cardiovascular diseases such as acute myocardial infarction (heart attack) and the microchip could be useful for screening patients who show up due to chest pain.

624012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
624012.value: Customer contact centers have become a preferred and prevalent means for companies to communicate with their customers. Modern technology makes real time communication via the Internet not only possible, but also convenient. With the popularity of the Internet, phone calls are no longer the only way of communication in many situations. More and more companies are building web-chat customer contact centers in addition to their traditional call centers. The new mode of contacting customers via web-chat is emerging and growing at a fast pace. The significant relevance motivates us to study the model underlying web-chat customer contact centers for better management of such services. Via phone calls, agents (sales representatives, technicians, etc.) can talk with only one customer at a time. In contrast, agents can chat with multiple customers via web-chat. The multi-tasking nature of web-chat leads us to model a web-chat service center as a many server queue, with each server operating under a limited processor sharing (LPS) protocol. We limit the number of customers that can share an agent simultaneously because the limit itself is a key control decision that can affect the performance of a service center. A customer with a certain amount of request may experience different amount of actual service time depending on how many other customers share the agent with him. Another important decision is staffing, to determine the number of agents to be scheduled at any given time to accommodate the demand. We propose to model such a system mathematically and study it in an asymptotic regime where the size of the service center becomes larger and larger. This makes sense in practice, since most such service centers are huge. Our research will not only lead to novel methodologies for developing mathematical frameworks to characterize the underlying stochastic processes, but also yield insightful approximations in the asymptotic regime. Based on the quantitative insights, we provide efficient and implementable solutions for staffing and control. For a given demand and varying service rates of each agent, which can be estimated from historical data, we propose an approach based on our analysis to calculate the optimal staffing and control decisions so that the labor cost of employing agents is minimized and customers’ experience, measured by waiting time and actual service time, is optimized. 客服中心已经成为企业与客户沟通的一个普遍首选的方式。现代科技使得通过互联网进行的实时通信不仅变为可能，还很方便。随着互联网的普及，在许多情况下，电话服务不再是唯一的沟通方式。除了传统的电话客服中心，越来越多的公司正在建设网络聊天为基础的客服中心。通过网络聊天与客户联系的新型模式正在逐渐形成并飞速发展。这样的重大联系促使我们研究与之相关的模型，以便更好的管理这样的服务中心。 通过电话方式，在任何时间里，客服代理（销售代表，技术人员等）只能跟一个顾客联络。相反，通过网络聊天的形式，客服代理可以同时跟多个客户聊天。网络聊天的多任务的性质让我们用多服务器的排队论模型来模拟这样的网络服务中心，其中每个服务器使用有限处理器共享协议。我们给每个服务器设置一个允许同时服务客户数目的上限，是因为这个上限本身是影响客服中心表现的一个关键控制决策。一个给定需求的顾客可能会经历不同的实际服务时间，取决于与之同时分享这个服务器的其他顾客的数目。另一个重要的决定就是工作人员的数目，如何安排任何给定时间里的工作人员的数目以适应相应的客户需求。 我们为这样的系统建立了一个数学模型，并且在客服中心规模越来越大的渐近方式下对之进行了研究。这在实际中是有意义的，因为大多数这样的客服中心规模总是巨大的。我们的研究不仅使用了全新的方法去构建它的数学框架来刻画隐含的随机过程，同时也衍生了有见识的渐近性逼近方法。基于定量的见解分析，我们为员工配置和控制提供了有效并切实可行的方案。对于给定需求和每个客户代理的不同服务效率，这些可以从历史数据中估计出来，我们提出了一个计算最优员工配置和控制决策变量的方法。这个方法是基于我们对模型的分析，从而使得雇佣员工的劳力成本和以等待时间和实际服务时间来量化的顾客体验达到最优。

624012.label: Realisation of objectives
624012.value: The objectives have been achieved with success. In paper #1 (see Section 8 of the report), we developed an analytical framework for analyzing the fluid model underlying service systems with many limited processor-sharing servers. In a subsequent paper #6, we extend such study to the service and patience time to follow a general distribution instead of an exponential one. Paper #2 made breakthroughs in theoretical analysis of the asymptotic behavior of fluid models for many-server queues. We also applied our analytical framework to study a model motivated by spectrum allocation in wireless communication. The analytical framework we developed is both mature in theory and applicable. In this way, Objective 1 is achieved. The series of papers #1, #3 and #6 has thoroughly studied the asymptotic optimal staffing and control policy for web-chat services in various cases. Paper #1 studies the optimal staffing for the case where a widely adopted policy, lightest-load-first, is applied. Paper #3 extends paper #1 to study the joint optimal decision for both staffing and control policies. The insight we found is that lightest-load-first may not be optimal in many cases. The optimal control policy actually depends on the so-called basic level, which depends on system parameters via an optimization problem. Paper #6 extends paper #3 by analyzing a fluid model with general service and patience distributions and identifying how the characteristics of the distribution impact on the system performances and the design of optimal policy. Thus, we have successfully achieved Objective 2. In paper #3, we proved the interchange of heavy traffic and steady state limits. Paper #5 also studies the optimal staffing and control when the arrival is time-varying. In this way, objectives 3 and 4 have been achieved. Paper #4 developed an analytical framework to obtain diffusion approximation of the stochastic process. We applied this framework to study a call center application and obtain insightful approximations and joint staffing and control policies. So Objectives 5 and 6 are both achieved. Achieving the objectives was not an easy task. It took tremendous effort from myself and three of my PhD students. All of them have already graduated. One became an assistant professor at Shanghai Jiaotong University Antai School of Business upon graduation, one was placed as an assistant professor at Shanghai University after a year post doc at Technion, another also became an assistant professor at Huazhong University of Science and Technology upon graduation. The papers produced in this project were much improved by hiring research assistants and communicating with top researchers in the field. The grant allowed me to have English editors improve the exposition of all my papers. The travels made possible by this grant also enable me to collaborate extensively with my collaborators in Singapore and US, and present the research outcomes in major conferences and workshops.

624012.label: Major findings and research outcome
624012.value: This project has led to significant development in both theory and application. Papers 2, 4 and 6 developed a framework and necessary theory to support it. All papers are motivated by practical applications such as call/webchat service centers, and applied the framework to obtain insightful results as well as practically implementable near-optimal policies. The major findings of this project are as follows: Papers #1 and 3 consider customer service chat systems where customers can receive real time service from agents using an instant messaging application over the Internet. We propose effective routing policies based on a static planning LP. We show that these routing policies minimize the proportion of abandoning customers in the long run asymptotically for large systems. We also prove that the staffing solution obtained from a staffing LP, when used with the proposed routing policies, is asymptotically optimal. Paper #6 extends these results to a more general setting with general service/patience time distributions. The significance of the approximations is that they reveal how general service and patience time distributions impact the system performance, and that they lead to design of routing policies for these systems. Paper #3 shows that the convergence of the fluid model to its equilibrium state holds under some general conditions, solving an open question in the area. Fluid models, in particular their equilibrium states, have become an important tool for the study of many-server queues with general service and patience time distributions. Our method builds on the framework of measure-valued processes, which keeps track of the remaining patience and service times. Paper #4 proposes a unified approach to establishing diffusion approximations for queues with impatient customers within a general framework of scaling customer patience time. The approach consists of two steps. We demonstrate the application of this approach via the single server system with Markov-modulated service speeds in the traditional heavy-traffic regime and the many-server system in the Halfin-Whitt regime and the non-degenerate slowdown regime. Paper #5 considers a band of the electromagnetic spectrum with a finite number of identical channels shared by both licensed and unlicensed users. Our analysis reveals that sharing does not affect the level of service provided to the licensed users in an asymptotic sense even when the system is critically loaded. We also study the optimal sharing decisions of the system to maximize the system throughput rate while maintaining the delay probability of the licensed users below a certain level.

624012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
624012.value: In this project, we have solved several major problems completely. For example, we developed a framework of fluid analysis to address a class of important application models. And in the diffusion analysis, we provide a unified approach which can put many existing methods under a unified framework. So in the main theme, there should not be much left to do in the scope of proposed research. This project has great potential for future research in applications. We only demonstrated the application of the theory we developed in several application in the scope of this project. The method we developed can surely be applied to other types of models. For example, bike sharing (or more generally business models in the emerging sharing economy such as Didi Chuxing) systems can be modeled as a multi-server system. The proposed course of action would be to study the important factors in those applications, and modify the model (sometimes with slight adaptation of the method) to obtain insights and results in those applications.

624012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
624012.value: This project has demonstrated both theoretical and application significance. On the theoretical side, we advanced the state of art in analyzing the difficult yet widely used multi-server queueing model by developing a framework for fluid and diffusion analysis. Our research has been driven by real application in emerging areas, and has led to some innovative models such as the online web chat system, and spectrum sharing in wireless communication. These models are new to the research literature and have their own distinctive features. Thus we needed to develop new method to analyze them. Based on the theory we developed, we were able to obtain operational insights to the applications. For example, we proposed easy-to-implement and optimal staffing and control policies for webchat centers and call centers with outsourcing, both being important applications in the modern society. We also revealed important insights into the spectrum management problem, and proposed optimal control policy to maximize throughput while controlling the delay probability.

624112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
624112.value: The 2008 financial crisis and the ongoing European debt turmoil have made it clear that proper risk management must be conducted in financial industry. From a quantitative perspective, one challenging problem both in theory and in practice is to determine the credit risk of a portfolio, in particular to estimate the probability of the rare but influential event of large default losses. This problem is exactly in the scope of rare-event simulation. Consequently, rare-event simulation in portfolio credit risk has become increasingly important in both financial industry and academia throughout the world including Hong Kong, one of the most important international financial centers. Since most probabilistic models in portfolio credit risk are based on Markov systems, this project will first develop a novel generic rare-event simulation algorithm, called regenerative bootstrap with importance sampling (RBIS), for such systems and then apply it to various models in portfolio credit risk. The RBIS approach is motivated by two difficulties shared by most of the existing rare-event simulation algorithms: (i) they involve computing a certain eigenvalue problem, which has no explicit solution in general; (ii) they involve importance sampling (IS) and the IS distribution is difficult to simulate in general. We will attempt to prove that our RBIS approach potentially has three appealing features. (1) It will resolve the two difficulties simultaneously. (2) It will retain the same level of computational efficiency as others. (3) It is generic and hence will be adaptable to other IS-based algorithms. We will introduce RBIS in the context of estimating the tail probabilities of a Markov-dependent sum, which may appear in a hidden Markov model in portfolio credit risk. The key idea is to exploit the regenerative structure of the Markov chain to construct empirical approximations to the eigenvalue and the IS distribution based on the regenerative cycles. In this project, we intend to first address the computational complexity of RBIS and establish its asymptotic optimality. Second we will adapt the RBIS approach for other important models in portfolio credit risk, including structural model, Markov intensity model, and affine point process model. Last, we will try to relax the regeneration assumption to wide-sense regeneration, which would be a significant extension of great theoretical interest. 2008年开始的世界金融危机和正在进⾏中的欧洲债务危机让人们清楚地认识到⾦融业中⻛险管理的重要性。从定量角度讲，在理论和实际操作中⼀个极具挑战性的问题就是如何确定信⽤⻛险；更加具体的讲,就是如何估计那些罕⻅却很有影响⼒的⼤规模信⽤违约事件所发⽣的概率。这个问题恰好属于罕有事件模拟的范畴。因此，投资组合信⽤⻛险中的罕有事件模拟在世界⾦融业和学术界都变得越来越重要，这其中也包括了国际⾦融中⼼⾹港。 因为投资组合信⽤⻛险领域中的⼤部分概率模型都是基于马尔科夫系统，所以该研究项将⾸先发展针对这类系统的一种全新的罕有事件模拟算法，叫做带有重要性采样的再⽣性⾃助式重抽样法(regenerative bootstrap with importance sampling)，简称RBIS。RBIS⽅法的出发点来源于现行⼤部分罕有事件模拟算法共有的两个困难：⼀、它们都要涉及计算⼀个特征值问题，⽽这个问题在⼀般情况下是没有显式解的；⼆、它们都要使⽤重要性采样 (importance sampling,简称IS)，而⽤到的IS概率分布⼀般情况下很难模拟出来。我们将试图证明我们的RBIS方法具有三种潜在的优点:⼀、它能同时解决上述两个困难；二、它能保持和现有方法同⼀⽔平的计算效率,不会大幅度提高复杂度；三、它具有⼀般性，因此能⽤到其他基于IS的算法。 我们将会在估计⻢尔科夫加和的尾概率的背景下引⼊RBIS 算法，因为这个问题在投资组合信⽤⻛险领域中的隐⻢尔科夫模型中出现。我们关键的想法是要探索⻢尔科夫链的再⽣结构，以此构造之前提到的特征值和IS概率分布的经验近似。在这个项⽬中，我们将首先讨论RBIS方法的计算复杂度问题，并证明这个⽅法的近似最优性。再次，我们会把RBIS⽅法⽤到投资组合信用风险的一些重要概率模型中。最后，我们会试图把减弱再⽣性这个条件；如果成功，这将会是⼀个理论上的重要推⼲。

624112.label: Realisation of objectives
624112.value: The project has three objectives: (i) Theoretically prove the asymptotic optimality of the RBIS algorithm for rare-event simulation in Markov systems, under the assumption that a regenerative structure exists. (ii) Apply the RBIS algorithm to stochastic models in portfolio credit risk and related rare-event simulation problems. (iii) Find remedies when the regenerative assumption fails. For objective (i): Together with one of my PhD students FAN Weiwei, I have rigorously proved the asymptotic optimality of the RBIS algorithm (regenerative bootstrap with importance sampling) for estimating certain rare-event probabilities in Markov chains. We have also conducted several numerical experiments to provide further supporting evidence. In addition, we have extended the proposed method to a more general setting described as follows. The rare event probabilities that we are interested in originally are the tail probabilities of the running average of a Markov chain. We have found that the RBIS algorithm can also be used to estimate the tail probabilities of a functional of the running average of a Markov chain. However, some modification needs to be made to the RBIS algorithm to account for the additional complication. A key step in the RBIS algorithm is to estimate a so-called “tilting parameter”. This parameter is estimated only once in the original setting. By contrast, it is estimated sequentially in the extended setting. Essentially, we have added a “state-dependent” nature to the RBIS algorithm and the proof of this extended version is similar but with more technical complications. For objective (ii): There are a variety of stochastic models for portfolio credit risk. We have focused on a large class of models, called affine point processes. This model generalizes significantly many more elementary models, such as compound Poisson processes or double stochastic Poisson processes. It is a popular model in quantitative finance that can capture the clustering behavior of correlated credit defaults in a bad economy or financial crisis. Although an affine point process itself is not Markovian, when coupled with the underlying intensity process, which is an affine jump diffusion, the joint process is indeed a two-dimensional Markov process. The rare event of interest is that there is a large number of credit defaults in the portfolio within a given time horizon, or that the total loss of the portfolio due to credit defaults exceeds a large threshold. We have rigorously derived a large deviations principle that guides the selection of the “tilting parameter” in the RBIS algorithm. In particular, we have developed a computationally efficient algorithm for estimating the above rare event probabilities. For objective (iii): In order to relax the regenerative assumption, we seek general conditions that can guarantee ergodicity of the Markov process of interest, because ergodicity typically leads to a regenerative structure. However, it seems infeasible to give a specific, easy-to-check condition that implies ergodicity without knowing the specific structure of the Markov process. Therefore, we focus on affine jump-diffusions, which constitute a large class of continuous-time stochastic models that are particularly popular in ﬁnance and economics due to its analytical tractability. Notice that this model is also the underlying intensity process that drives the affine point processes that we use for analyzing portfolio credit risk above. Despite of its importance, no systematic treatment had been conducted for the stochastic stability of affine jump-diffusions in the literature before this project. The primary mathematical techniques we use to establish the stochastic stability of affine jump-diffusions are the Foster-Lyapunov inequalities. More specifically, we explicitly construct a so-called Lyapunov function for affine jump-diffusions, which would have been technically challenging for general Markov processes without the tractable affine structure. We have identified mild technical conditions that lead to various levels of stochastic stability of affine jump-diffusions. These technical conditions are do not depend on strong assumptions so the research results have great generality; moreover, they are simple and easy to verify, thereby facilitating the applications of the research results.

624112.label: Major findings and research outcome
624112.value: First, we have developed the so-called regenerative bootstrap with importance sampling (RBIS) algorithm for computing rare event probabilities in the context of Markov processes. Second, we have proved rigorously that the RBIS algorithm is asymptotically optimal as the probability to estimate goes to zero. This basically guarantees the computational efficiency of the algorithm. These two findings are summarized in the paper “Rare Event Simulation for Markov Chains via Regenerative Bootstrap” that is currently under review for Journal of Applied Probability. Third, we have applied the developed methodology successfully to portfolio credit risk. In particular, we have considered the problem of estimating the probability of credit default when the portfolio is modeled by an affine point process (a particular Markov process that is popular in the literature for credit risk modeling) and develop an efficient simulation-based algorithm to compute such probabilities. This work is contained in the published paper “Affine Point Processes: Approximation and Efficient Simulation”. Last, during the process of investigating the possibility of relaxing the assumption of the RBIS algorithm on the regenerative structure of a Markov process, we focus on the affine jump diffusion processes, which constitute a large class of continuous-time stochastic models that are particularly popular in ﬁnance and economics due to its analytical tractability. This model is also the underlying Markov process that drives the affine point process model used to characterize the dynamics of a portfolio credit risk. We have studied the stochastic stability of affine jump diffusions extensively. Such a property crucial for the existence of the desired regenerative structure for the RBIS algorithm. We have proposed simple conditions that guarantee the ergodicity/exponential ergodicity of affine jump diffusions. This is the first work in literature that thoroughly analyzed the stochastic stability of a general affine jump diffusion, despite the popularity of the model in the past two decades in finance and economics. This work is contained in the paper “Affine Jump-Diffusions: Stochastic Stability and Limit Theorems” that is currently under review for Mathematics of Operations Research.

624112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
624112.value: This project has focused on rare event simulation in portfolio credit risk and its related mathematical models. However, there are a variety of other important classes of rare event problems in quantitative finance. For example, financial systemic risk is of great concern from a regulatory perspective and has drawn considerable attention from both the academia and industry, especially in recent years in the light of the instability of financial markets in emerging economies. Many mathematical models used to analyze the financial systemic risk are based Markov chains. Hence, the computational methods developed in this project can be potentially applied to those problems as well, by exploring proper regenerative structures there.

624112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
624112.value: The 2008 financial crisis, the European debt turmoil that follows, and the instability of financial markets in emerging economies in recent years have made it clear that proper risk management must be conducted in financial industry. From a quantitative perspective, one challenging problem both in theory and in practice is to quantify the financial risk accurately, in particular to estimate the probability of the rare but influential event of large fluctuations. This problem is exactly in the scope of rare-event simulation. We have developed a fast simulation-based computational method for estimating small probabilities that arise in various mathematical models in quantitative finance. We have justified the computational efficiency of this algorithm in theory and demonstrated its usefulness in a variety of problems. This algorithm can be readily applied in practical situations due to its ease-to-use and great generality.

640112.label: Project Objectives

Identify other variables that affect the aggressiveness of individual investors in their order submission strategies.

Identify other variables that affect the aggressiveness of individual investors in their order submission strategies.

640112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640112.value: In this project, we investigate whether behavioral biases affect the order submission strategies of investors. We take advantage of very unique databases provided by the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE), which keeps a real-time record of all the order submissions and executions on securities listed on SSE for the investors, as well as a record of their stock holdings. These databases allow us to track order submissions and executions for every investor in trading SSE stocks. According the disposition effect, investors are more eager to sell stocks that experienced gains than those that experienced losses. We conjecture that investors are less (more) aggressive in submitting the sell order for a stock that is experiencing paper losses (gains). According the house money effect, investors are more willing to assume risk when gambling with the profits that they made. While house money effect does not affect the order submission strategy of selling loser stocks, it affects the strategy of selling winner stocks. After the paper profits reach a certain level, investors will be willing to assume more risk and become more patient in selling the winner stocks. Combining the disposition effect and house money effect implies that for winner stocks, order aggressiveness will first increase with the paper profits (disposition effect bigger than the house money effect), and then later decrease with the paper profits (disposition effect smaller than the house money effect). 本研究利用上海證券交易所的帳戶資料，實證檢驗了上海投資者在投資決策時展現出處置效應（disposition effect）。我們還首次發現投資者在遞單策略上也展現出處置效應。我們用遞單積極度（Order Aggressiveness）來衡量投資者的遞單策略。具體表現在投資者在賣出盈利的股票時傾向于遞交積極度高的賣單以期望儘快變現，而在賣出虧損的股票時傾向于遞交積極度低的賣單而不介意繼續持有股票。我們還發現如果股票的盈利達到一定程度之後，投資者會願意承擔更多風險而變得在賣出股票時更加有耐心。處置效應和賭資效應（house money effect）可以聯合解釋上述現象：隨著盈利規模的增加投資者遞交股票賣單的積極度會先升高（處置效應大於賭資效應），之後降低（處置效應小於賭資效應）。

640112.label: Realisation of objectives
640112.value: The project represents an ambitious attempt in examining whether investors exhibit behavioral biases will affect the order submission strategies. There is a vast literature that investors exhibit disposition effect, whereby investors show a greater propensity to sell stocks trading at a gain rather than a loss. However, there is no study on examining whether the disposition effect will affect the aggressiveness of the order submission strategies. The project benefits from the access to a unique database provided by the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE), which keeps real-time records of the order submissions of all investors trading securities listed on the exchange and of their stock holdings in 2008. This database allows us to track order submissions and executions for every investor who conducts trades of securities listed on the Shanghai market. While containing very comprehensive data, a disadvantage with the database is that access is quite restrictive. Researchers can work with the data only at a designated computer at the center, during SSE working hours, and all computations must be carried out under the careful supervision of the data manager. Working with the data files therefore takes much longer time for us to finish the analysis. We focus on sell order submissions and analyze the relationship between the investment outcomes and order aggressiveness measures. Consistent with the disposition effect, we find that investors are more aggressive in submitting sell orders for stocks with gains than for those with losses. The effect of this is also economically significant. Further analysis finds that the relationship between sell order aggressiveness and losses is significantly negative, but between sell order aggressiveness and gains is quadratic -- order aggressiveness first increases with gains, and then declines after a certain level is reached. This asymmetric relationship between prior investment outcomes and subsequent order aggressiveness for winner and loser stocks is not entirely consistent with the disposition effect, but are consistent with the additional impact of house money effect. The paper has been presented in international conferences, and submitted to top-tier finance journals. Unfortunately, the paper has been rejected despite some reviewers think we are using a very uniquie database, and that we have some interesting results. As such, we will submit the paper to other finance journal and hope to settle for a good outlet.

640112.label: Major findings and research outcome
640112.value: The study focused on sell order submissions and analyze the relationship between the investment outcomes and order aggressiveness using various approaches. We construct order aggressiveness measures, by comparing the order price with the limit order book at the time of submission. Consistent with the disposition effect in Coval and Shumway (2005), we find that investors are more aggressive in submitting sell orders for stocks with gains than for those with losses. The effect of this is economically significant: on average, investors with gains tend to submit more aggressive sell orders, with prices at two pennies less, or roughly about two ticks in the limit order book. Further analysis of the effect of gains/losses on order aggressiveness measures finds that the relationship between sell order aggressiveness and losses is significantly negative, but between sell order aggressiveness and gains is quadratic -- order aggressiveness first increases with gains, and then declines after a certain level is reached. Our results also apply after controlling for competing hypotheses regarding the determinants of order aggressiveness, and are robust to alternative specifications and reference prices in computing gains/losses. This asymmetric relationship between prior investment outcomes and subsequent order aggressiveness for winner and loser stocks is not entirely consistent with the disposition effect, but are consistent with the additional effect of house money effect, whereby investors become less aggressive in selling a winner stock after it has reached a certain level of profit. To corroborate our findings on the effect of behavioral biases on order submission strategies, we conduct additional tests for the disposition effect, using only executed orders. We examine how the size of gains/losses can affect the hazard ratios associated with the investor’s decision to sell/hold stocks. We find that First, the hazard ratio is significantly above one for winner stocks, and significantly below one for loser stocks, providing which is clear evidence of the disposition effect. In addition, Second, for loser stocks, similar to the effect of order aggressiveness, the size of losses is negatively related to the hazard ratio, indicating that investors are more reluctant to sell stocks of bigger losses. Third, for winner stocks, again similar to the effect of order aggressiveness, the hazard ratio first increases with gains and subsequently declines. These results show that the combination of the disposition effect and the house money effect is evident in both the order aggressiveness and the sell/hold decision.

640112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
640112.value: We believe that our results are relevant not only for emerging stock markets like those of China, but also for developed markets. Considerable evidence suggests that investors in developed markets also exhibit behavioral biases through their investment decisions at both the retail investor level. We note that the introduction of electronic trading systems and the ensuing decrease in trading costs has induced more traders to participate in trading. It is not surprising that these new investors are easily subject to behavioral biases in their investment decisions. With more detailed trading records available for individual investors in different markets, it will be interesting to examine how these behavioral biases also affect other trading decisions.

640112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
640112.value: We investigate whether behavioral biases affect the order submission strategies of investors. We take advantage of a unique database provided by the Shanghai Stock Exchange that allows us to track order submissions and executions for every investor, along with the trading performance of individual stocks. Consistent with the disposition effect, we find that investors are less (more) aggressive in submitting sell orders for stocks that experienced prior losses (prior gains). Although the relationship between sell order aggressiveness and prior losses is significantly negative, the relationship between sell order aggressiveness and prior gains is quadratic. Overall, these findings are consistent with the prospect theory that predicts how prior investment outcomes affect the risk-taking behavior of investors, although investors can become either more or less risk averse after prior gains.

640212.label: Project Objectives

To document the change or no change in firms' behavior of meeting or beating earnings benchmarks (measured by financial analysts’ consensus earnings forecasts) after the adoption of clawbacks.

640212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640212.value: Compensation recovery or clawback policies (commonly known as “clawbacks”) have become one of the most notable changes in executive compensation practices in the United States. The policies are initiated by the board of directors so the board can recover compensation that is paid to executives based on misstated financial reports. The provisions have been shown by academic research to lead to a reduction of financial misstatements, and investors consider the adoption as positive news. The clawbacks have also been embraced by the U.S. Congress when it enacted the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act in July 2010. The Act requires all listed companies in the U.S. to adopt and implement the clawback policy. This project will document that, other than reducing financial misstatements, the clawbacks initiated by firms also reduce earnings management using accounting accruals (such as accelerating the recognition of revenues). This is because many means of financial misstatements, such as recognizing revenues prematurely, result in abnormally high accounting accruals. However, the reduction in misstatements and accruals is likely to come with a cost in that clawback provisions cause managers to resort to real transactions (such as reducing research and development expense) as a substitute tool to manage earnings. The reason is that some clawback firms, especially those with higher growth opportunities, face pressure to meet or beat earnings benchmarks (measured by financial analysts’ consensus earnings forecasts) since their stock prices suffer a sharper decline when they miss the earnings targets. Thus, clawback firms with higher growth are more likely to resort to real transactions to manage earnings. Finally, the project will show that those firms experience an underperformance as measured by industry-adjusted operating cash flows and return on assets in the post-adoption periods. Taken together, the study will show that, because of the pressure to meet or beat earnings benchmarks, the high-growth firms adopting clawbacks have to resort to real transactions to manage earnings. Since those transactions are detrimental to firm operations, those firms’ future performance is compromised. Thus, although compensation clawbacks reduce the misstatement accounting information, they force managers of high-growth firms to use real transactions to achieve earnings targets and lead to future underperformance. The study thus will show that clawback provisions have unintended negative consequences. They should be taken into account when other jurisdictions, including Hong Kong, consider imposing the similar regulation on listed companies. 薪酬追回條款（追薪條款）已經成為近年美國高管薪酬實務上最大的變革之一。這種條款由公司董事會自發訂定，董事會可以根據條款追回以前因為財務報告錯編而發出的薪酬。有些學術研究已顯示這些條款減少財報錯編，股市的投資者也將條款的設立解讀為對公司有利的消息。不但如此，美國國會2010年七月通過的《多德•弗蘭克華爾街改革及消費者保護法案》中，也包含類似條款，要求所有美國上市公司訂定及執行追薪條款。 本研究計劃期望找出證據顯示追薪條款在減少財報錯編之外，也減少公司使用會計的應計項目（例如提早認列收入），因為很多錯編財報的手段，如過早認列收入，會造成異常高的應計值。但另一方面，財報錯編及應計值的減少，也可能會有代價，就是追薪條款會致使管理層使用實際的交易事項（如減少研發開支）做為替代的手段。這是因為訂定追薪條款的公司，特別是高度成長期的公司，面臨較大的壓力，需要報出符合或超過市場預期的盈餘指標（市場預期可以用財務分析師公認的盈餘預測值來衡量）。這些公司的盈餘如果不符市場預期時，股價通常會大幅回落。所以引進追薪條款的高成長公司有較強的動機用實際的交易事項去操控盈餘。最後，本計劃也預期發現這些公司在用實際的交易事項操控盈餘之後，與行業相比，營業現金流以及資產報酬率等業績指標會有下滑現象。 總而言之，本研究將指出，因為有符合或超過盈餘指標的壓力，高成長的公司在引進追薪條款之後，還是需要使用實際的交易事項來操控盈餘數字。因為這種行為對公司的經營不利，所以會對未來業績有負面影響。因此雖然追薪條款減少了財報錯編，但卻迫使管理層使用實際的交易事項來操控盈餘數字以達到盈餘的指標，最後還是造成長期業績的下滑。本研究將指出追薪條款的意外的負面後果，可以給全球各地市場，包括香港，在考慮是否跟進類似的規定時做為借鑒。

640412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640412.value: General transformation models, widely used in econometrics and biostatistics, have received a great deal of attention in the literature. The approaches by Chen (2002), Han (1987) and Horowitz (1996), among others, however, require independent error terms, thus imposes rather drastic constraints on the way regressors are permitted to influence the response variable. Chen (2010) and Khan (2001) consider quantile regression for the transformation model that permits general heteroscedasticity, but the resulting quantile prediction converges at rates slower than the parametric rate. In this proposal, we will consider the estimation of two general transformation models subject to multiplicative forms of heteroscedasticity, and the resulting quantile predictors converge at the parametric rate. 廣義變換模型廣泛運用于計量經濟學和生物統計中，并獲得眾多文獻青睞。然 而Chen(2002),Han(1987),Horowitz(1996)等方法均要求隨機誤差項的獨立性，這就對解釋變量如何影響被解釋變量施加了較強之假設。Chen(2010)與Khan(2001)的工作研究了帶有異方差的變換模型的分位數識別與估計。但該類估計存在被解釋變量分位數預測估計量收斂速度慢于‘參數速度’的缺陷。在本項研究計劃中，我們將考慮兩類帶有可乘異方差的廣義轉換模型，并使得被解釋變量分位數預測達到‘參數收斂速度’。

640612.label: Project Title(Chinese)
640612.value: 关于经济灾难,期货和信用市场能告诉我们些什么?

640612.label: Project Objectives
640612.value: We want to know what the joint data of option and credit markets tell us about consumption jumps in terms of both the size and the magnitude. By using both the junior and the senior CDO tranche data which are sensitive to different types of jumps, we aim to obtain a complete picture about the distributions of the potential consumption disasters that are implicit in the financial market. By adopting a general equilibrium model featuring both time varying risk aversion and time varying jump intensity, we aim to identify the parameters of the relative risk aversion from those of disasters. Relying on the generalized method of moments (GMM), we will estimate the model using the spreads of CDX and their tranches written on US firms, as well as the spreads of Itraxx and their tranches written on European firms. As a result, our study is the first to illustrate the degree of heterogeneity in tail risks between the US and Europe.

As a result, our study is the first to illustrate the degree of heterogeneity in tail risks between the US and Europe.

640612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640612.value: While there is mounting evidence that macroeconomic disaster - infrequent large declines in aggregate output and consumption - produce dramatic improvement in the ability of pricing models to reproduce prominent features of US asset returns, the primary challenge for such researches lies in estimating their probability and magnitude. One apparent reason is that disaster events are infrequent and are often absent in small samples. Barro (2009), for example, document that the occurrence of jumps in consumption are minor in the post-WWII period for the US and most of the OECD countries. This scarcity complicates the identification of the expected magnitude and likelihood of consumption disasters. In this study, instead of relying on realizations of consumption time series as have been the case for many prior researches, we follow a complementary path and use both equity index options and credit market instruments to infer the distribution of extreme events as well as risk aversion. The crucial advantage of our proposed approach is that participants in these markets value extreme events, whether they happen in our sample or not. It is widely recognized that prices of both deep-out-of-the-money equity index options and senior CDX tranches are only sensitive to disaster like events. This property provides econometric power to identify the unconditional distribution consumption disaster as well as their representative agent risk aversion. To our knowledge there is no empirical study that has utilized information jointly from both markets to pin down the disaster and preference parameters. To this end, we develop a consumption-based equilibrium model while accounting for disaster component in consumption that is capable of jointly pricing equity index options and credit index tranches while matching the equity premium. We rely on the generalized method of moments to pin down the expected disaster probabilities and magnitude. We will demonstrate the econometric advantage of relying on credit instrument to complement the range of available traded OTM option prices. By fitting the model separately to each market at a time, we will be able to examine the degree of heterogeneity between the credit, stock and option market participant concerning disaster expectations. Our model will also allow us to capture the changing nature in expectation of the severe systematic crash before and after the recent market turmoil. We expect our study to deliver the resonable P-estimates of expected disaster probabilities and magnitude reflected in the financial market for both economists and policy makers. 控制和消除尾部风险对于风险管理者和政策制定者而言都十分重要. 然而,如何测量经济灾难的幅度在实证学上却是一个不易解决的问题.因为灾难是个小概率事件,历史数据往往不能提供精确的测量,而且也不能反映未来灾难的幅度.虽然期权价格对灾难敏感,市场上却很少交易极度价外期权.因此使用期权数据难以估计出严重的灾难.在这个项目里,我们使用信贷违约调期指数(CDX)及其份额(tranches)来估计未来的灾难幅度.信贷违约指数份额相当于极度价外期权,因此可以更好的识别严重的经济灾难.更进一步,我们同时使用在美国和在欧洲的价格数据去检验文献上的一个重要假设:灾难的幅度在不同的国家是相同的.

640612.label: Realisation of objectives
640612.value: The objectives of the projects have been achieved reasonably well. Traditional rare disaster models (e.g., Rietz (1985); Barro (2005)) advocate a consumption jump magnitude that are multiple times larger than ever experienced in the U.S., and they tend to focus on equity pricing. We embed habit formation into a rare-disaster framework that generates both the time varying risk aversion and the time varying disaster rates. We show a consumption disaster component consistent with the U.S. experience (at around 10%) is able to explain various pricing regularities in equity, option and credit markets. In particular, we carefully work out the correlation structure between corporate defaults and consumption jumps. By using both the junior and the senior CDO tranche data, we are able to identify three types of defaults. The first type is idiosyncratic which is mainly for generating firm specific defaults. The latter two types are interpreted as industry-level and economy-wide defaults which are both perfectly correlated with consumption disaster. We further show that consumption disaster that is correlated with the industry-level default is the most relevent for generating the observed corporate bond spreads. Taken together, our model has provided a relatively complete picture about the distributions of consumption disasters. Simultaneously, it has unified, for the first time, the pricing of corporate bonds and CDO tranches. In our model, habit formation generates the time-varying risk aversion. Specifically, as current consumption falls towards the subsistence/ habit level, investors are more worried about the potential further downfall of security prices, and therefore become more risk averse. By using power utility, we have implicitly set the elasticity of intertermporal substitution (EIS) to be reverse of risk aversion. By fitting the model to a wide classes of assets, including aggregate equity, risk-free bond, corporate bonds, options, CDX and CDO tranches, we find that the current model with an average risk aversion of 40 does a quite a good job in pricing. This relatively high value is largely driven by the spikes of investors' risk aversion during disaster times when aggregate consumption jumps towards the subsistence level. In a word, our result shows that a high risk aversion during bad economic times seems necessary to reconcile the pricing of various asset classes. We apply generalized method of moments to estimate jump-related parameters by using the spreads of CDX and tranches written on U.S. firms. In our estimation, we differentiate three types of defaults modeled as Poisson jumps that are correlated with consumption disaster. To accomodate the nature of variable disasters, we allow the jump/default rates to vary across time. In other words, we back out the time series of the three corporate default rates and the time series of consumption jump rates out of the CDO tranche data. We find the senior tranche are effectively at identifying the economy-wide defaults. Adding options significantly contributes to the estimation of industry-level defaults, but helps little in identifying the third type of defaults that are economy-wide. We have also applied a similar estimation procedure to the data of Itraxx and their tranches written on European firms. We find the identified jump intensity and magnitudes are largely comparable to those estimated from the U.S. data. This result suggests that financial and economic crisies are largely contagious which generates the comparable degree of homogeneity in tail risks between the U.S. and Europe. These materials are not included in the published paper. Instead, they are incorporated into another ongoing paper (co-authored with Dan Luo) that uses data of commodities, options and CDO tranches to systematically gauge the heterogeniety in tail risks across various national and financial markets.

640612.label: Major findings and research outcome
640612.value: We develop a tractable model that simultaneously captures the empirical level and volatility of credit spreads, genrates a flexible credit risk term structure, and provides a good fit to a century of observed spreads. We find that a consumption disaster consistent with the U.S. experience and the usual degree of risk aversion (3--5) are enough to match both the high-yield coprorate bond spreads and the credit default obligation (CDO) tranche spreads. We document the junior and the senior CDO tranche data help identify corporate defaults not related to consumptions and the systematic defaults, respectively. Finally, our model implies a time-varying relationship between bond and option prices that depends on the state of the economy and that explains the conflicting empirical evidence found in the literature.

640612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
640612.value: First, in the current implementation we have modelled only two states: Default and no default. But our analytical framework can be extended to allowing for an arbitrary number of states. When interpreting these states as rating categories, we can thus study not only default events but also upgrades and downgrades. The model can also be applied to CDX tranche spreads. Second, we have emphasized the value of matching key moments in credit spreads and options using a single set of parameters calibrated to the real economy. However, going forward, it would be of interest to estimate the full model on observed credit spreads and option prices in order to provide a more comprehensive empirical assessment of the model. Third, while we have allowed for dynamic habit and recovery in our model, we have assumed that physical default intensities are constant over time. It would be interesting to relax this assumption.

640612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
640612.value: Economic disaster such as the Great Depression (1929-1933) have significant impacts on the pricing of financial assets. Previous researches tend to study the impact of rare disasters on individual assets, e.g., the aggregate equity. Further, economic disasters experienced in the U.S. are much less severe than experienced by other countries, e.g., Germany and Japan at the end of WWII. Previous studies that calibrate the rare disaster to international evidences that tend to over-estimate its impact on pricing. Recoganizing the limitation of previous researches, this project applies a rare disaster framework to study the joint pricing of aggregate stock, treasury bonds, corporate bonds, and credit default obligation (CDO) tranches. Besides the concern about the potential economic disasters, this project also accounts for the time-varying risk aversion which could be very high during disaster times. As a result, it is able to generate high risk compensations even the model calibration is solely based on the U.S. experiences. Besides the replication of pricing regularities among various categories of assets, the generated paper has also worked out interesting links between corporate bond pricing and the pricing of CDO tranche data, and between derivative pricing and bond pricing. After two rounds of revision, this paper has been accepted by the Management Science, a top tier journal to financial and business studies.

640712.label: Project Title(Chinese)
640712.value: 誘導專家保持最適量的固執程度

640712.label: Project Objectives
640712.value: Develop a theoretical repeated-game model that will allow us to have a better understanding of the expert’s incentives to acquire information, propose policy or formulate business strategies, and utilize new information that arrives later to update the policy or strategy. Characterize the optimal relational contract, i.e., equilibria that give the principal the highest payoff and investigate whether the incentive for the expert to wait for new information will indeed cause the principal to design incentives that induce the expert to be stubborn and resist new information. Draw new insights and explore applications of our theoretical findings. The specific applications we have in mind are reward systems for politicians, CEO compensation, and merger analysis.

640712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640712.value: Citizens and shareholders (whom we will call the principal) rely on experts such as politicians or Chief Executiv Officers (CEOs) to propose and implement public policies or business strategies. Often, after a public policy or business strategy is initially proposed or implemented, new information will arrive or feedback from the public will be observed. The feedback may be commentaries from political or Wall Street analysts. The new information and feedback may or may not be in support of the original proposal or policy. How would the citizens and shareholders like the expert to utilize the new information? Should the principal design incentives that induce the expert to implement the best policy or strategy after incorporating all the information available? These are the main questions we will investigate in our research project. In particular, we investigate when it may be optimal for the principal to induce the expert to be somewhat resistant to the new information. In other words, it can be in the best interest of the principal to reward the expert for being stubborn. To understand why this may be the case, we should recognize that the initial policy or strategy proposed by the expert does not come from nowhere. The expert has to exert effort to perform information acquisition and analysis beforehand. If the expert anticipates that new information will arrive after making the initial proposal, the expert may want to reduce the initil effort of information acquisition and analysis and wait for feedback and new information to finalize the poicy. To avoid the expert from making a hasty proposal and later use the new information to fine tune or even reverse the proposed policy or strategy, the principal has to reward the expert for being stubborn or punish him for changing his mind in view of new information. Once the expert knows there is a cost to changing his mind, then he will be forced to work harder to prepare a well thought-through proposal or initial policy/strategy. Inducing stubbornness is clearly not costless because it means useful new information will be sometimes dismissed. However, we have good reasons to conjecture that the benefit of inducing at least some stubbornness always outweighs the cost associated with it. This finding can shed new light on why politicians are punished for rationally changing their view in light of new information. TBA

640712.value: On Objective 1, we have successfully developed our theoretical model which allows us to better understand the stated issues. On Objective 2, we have characterized the optimal relational contract. The characterization allows us to show that it is optimal to induce the expert to be stubborn if and only if the precision of the public signal falls into an intermediate range. On Objective 3, our analysis implies that we would like to reward politicians or CEOs less for their success if their success is achieved with approaches consistent with other experts' opinions.

640712.label: Major findings and research outcome
640712.value: Our main finding is that if there is publicly available information that the expert can rely on the formulate policy or business strategy, then it is optimal for the principal to reward the expert more when the expert succeed by not relying on the publicly available information even though the information is useful for guiding the expert to arrive at a good decision. Our findings help us understand why leaders who exhibit seemingly irrational stubbornness can receive high level of support from the public. Our main finding stands in sharp contrast to well known findings in the literature. Existing findings suggest that it is optimal to set a high hurdle for the expert's private information to be utilized but we show that it is optimal to encourage the expert to rely on his private information more.

640712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
640712.value: Our model can be extended into one with two competing experts. This extension is especially relevant if we would like to emphasize the application of incentives of politicians. We can also similarly extend the model into one with two principals. Considering both extensions allows us to investigate whether competition among experts and competition among principals will make the expert(s) more stubborn in equilibrium.

640712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
640712.value: Some political leaders exhibit persistent stubbornness which are seemingly irrational. Yet, they are able to gather support from the majority of the population and win elections. The case at hand is George W. Bush who was known for his stubborn position on tax and stem cell research. His long-known stubbornness seemed to have helped him win the 2004 reelection and some may find it puzzling why votes would prefer a stubborn leader. Our theory explains that it is optimal for the public to reward the leader for being stubborn. This is because a stubborn leader anticipates that he cannot easily change his position, so that he will work hard to find the right policy position in the first place.

640812.label: Project Title(Chinese)
640812.value: 團體成員地位的組合，地位管理策略，與及人口多樣性團體的績效

640812.label: Project Objectives
640812.value: To examine how relational demography affects performance. To examine how status differences affect information elaboration
