640812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640812.value: Social status is an important determinant of human behavior. Though numerous theories have examined how status differences come into being, and how they are then enacted and sustained, this research has not had much play in the organizational domain. Organizations are contexts rich with status hierarchies. Employees belong to many social categories –gender, race, occupation – and these categories are organized along a status hierarchy with some being of a higher status than others. Further, status hierarchies are reinforced in organizations since groups with different status are allocated different levels of resources. In the set of studies we propose to undertake we take the lens of social status and apply it to understanding how the status hierarchy shapes attitudes and interactions in the workplace for individuals who work in diverse groups. Organizations are becoming increasingly diverse with employees differing from each other on a range of attributes such as gender, race, nationality, functional background, etc. Academic research into the phenomenon has developed along two parallel streams. One, the relational demography perspective, has examined how being dissimilar from ones’ coworkers affects the individual employee, and how this effect is not uniform for all employees. The second stream, the diversity perspective, has examined how the demographic composition of the group affects group levels outcomes such as the group’s performance. This stream of work has found mixed results sometimes showing how diversity yields positive outcomes for groups when the group is able to capitalize on the variety of information that it has. However, this has not been systematically studied. We propose that differences in the social status of members of a group will affect their information sharing and elaboration and as a result will affect group performance. 在我們提出的一系列的研究中，我們應用了對社會地位已有的認識來了解社會地位差異如何影響在人口多樣性團體中工作的員工的態度及他們彼此間的互動。企業的僱員越來越變得多樣化，他們在一系列的特性上各有不同：如性別，種族，國籍，功能背景。就這個現象，學術上已經發展了兩派學說。第一種學說，從關係人口學的角度來看，研究個體僱員與其他同事的不相同如何影響這個員工，而這些影響不是對所有員工都是一致的。第二種學說，從多樣性的角度來看，研究團體的人口組成如何影響團體性的結果，如團體的整體績效。基於第二種學說的實證研究得到不一致的結果：有時研究表明當團體能夠利用其所有的多樣化信息時，多樣性能對群體產生正面作用。然而，這一方面還未得到系統性的研究。我們認為在一個團體中，其成員的社會地位的差異會影響他們的信息共享和闡述，進而將影響團體的整體績效。

641212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641212.value: Because of globalization, supply chains have to continuously improve their processes to remain competitive in the marketplace. For supply chain members to make effective process improvement decisions, they need to have accurate and updated information about market demand. In a typical supplier-buyer relationship, the downstream buyer usually has superior information about market demand but may not have incentive to share it with the upstream supplier. This is because of the concern that the supplier may abuse the information for her own benefit, even at the expense of the supply chain. As a result, process improvement cannot be properly managed. To address this issue, members of a supply chain need to consider contracts that align their incentives so that information can be shared effectively to facilitate process improvement. Because of competition, they also need to consider the reactions of rival supply chains to their information sharing and process improvement decisions. In this project, we will develop quantitative models to investigate the following important issues: (1) In a supply chain with process improvement, does the downstream buyer have incentive to share his private demand information with the upstream supplier? (2) How does this incentive depend on process improvement efficiency, contract type and competition with other supply chains? (3) What are welfare implications of information sharing to the supply chain as well as the individual firms? Our investigation will enrich the theory of supply chain management and provide insights to supply chain managers for improving practices related to information sharing and process improvement. 由於全球化，供應鏈需要不斷改善自己的流程來保持市場競爭力。為了能夠做出有效的流程改進決策，供應鏈成員需要有準確的和最新的市場需求資訊。在一個典型的供求關係中，下游買方通常有更優越的市場需求資訊，但沒有誘因分享給上游供應商。這是因為擔心供應商可能濫用資訊來增加她自己的利益，甚至不惜犧牲供應鏈的利益。 因此，流程改進無法合適實施。為了解決這個問題，供應鏈成員需要考慮通過契約來協調各成員的利益，使得資訊有效共享，促進流程改進。因為競爭，他們還需要考慮其他競爭供應鏈對這種資訊共用和流程改善決策的反應。 在這個項目中，我們將通過建立定量模型來研究以下重要問題：（1）在採取流程改進的供應鏈中，下游買方有沒有誘因與上游供應商分享他的私有需求資訊？（2）這種誘因是如何受到流程改進效率、契約類型及與其他供應鏈競爭關係的影響？（3）從福利的角度看，資訊共用對整個供應鏈和對各個企業有什麼影響？ 我們的研究將對供應鏈管理理論有所貢獻，為供應鏈管理者在資訊共用及流程改善相關實務方面提供指引。

641212.label: Major findings and research outcome
641212.value: For two competing supply chains with cost reduction, I have obtained the following results on sharing a retailer’s demand information with a manufacturer. 1. Information sharing allows a manufacturer to make cost reduction decision in respond to demand information. The manufacturer exerts more effort to reduce cost when demand is higher. 2. Without competition, the value of information sharing to a supply chain is negative if the manufacturer’s efficiency in cost reduction is low, and positive otherwise. When the value of information sharing is positive, the manufacturer can use a side payment to induce the retailer to share information. This side payment is zero if the manufacturer’s efficiency in cost reduction is high enough. 3. With Cournot competition, information sharing occurs when the manufacturer is efficient in cost reduction. It is more likely to occur when either information is less accurate or competition is less intense. 4. With Bertrand competition, information sharing occurs when either competition is intense or the manufacturer is efficient in cost reduction. It is more likely to occur when information is more accurate. 5. When the manufacturer is sufficiently efficient in cost reduction, not only the value of information sharing to the supply chain is positive, but also the retailer is willing to share information for free, regardless of whether competition is Cournot or Bertrand. 6. Information sharing generally benefits a manufacturer. It benefits a retailer if the manufacturer’s efficiency in cost reduction is high and hurts him otherwise. I have also conducted some analysis of information sharing in a supply chain with two competing manufacturers selling to a common retailer when there is economy of scale in production (i.e. the marginal cost of production is decreasing in volume). My analysis shows that the retailer has an incentive to share information when the degree of production economy is high or competition is intense. It also characterizes the conditions under which the retailer shares information with none, one, or both of the manufacturers. These results are reported in the paper titled “Information Sharing in a Supply Chain with a Common Retailer,” which has been accepted for publication by Management Science.

641212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641212.value: The modeling framework developed in this project may be applicable to other supply chain structures such as one manufacturer selling to several competing retailers.

641212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641212.value: Effective supply chain management calls for cooperation among firms to improve the overall performance of the system. Information sharing is an important enabler of cooperation because it allows firms to make the right decisions based on the right information. However, these firms also compete for a larger share of the supply chain profit, which creates conflict of interest in information sharing. Our research findings identify cost reduction as a major driver of information sharing and provide useful insights into how it can create incentive for a retailer to share demand information with a manufacturer, and how such an incentive depends on type of competition, competition intensity and the retailer's demand forecasting capability. These insights can help managers improve supply chain performance via more effective information management.

641612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641612.value: Are more investments in knowledge assets ( Skilled human resources/assets and, more importantly, Information Technology (IT) assets that are critical for knowledge management) always good for firm innovation performance? Investments in both human and digital knowledge assets are extremely costly and so knowing if there are any diminishing returns associated with these costly investments in knowledge assets is important. This research program intends to answer this critical question. This research program intends to investigate the relationship between a firm’s investments in knowledge assets and innovation. Among various resources that a firm possesses, its knowledge assets are often regarded as having such characteristics that make them valuable, rare, hard to imitate and substitute. Also, it has been recognized that a firm’s knowledge is often embedded in its employees. The role of the firm is to thus create an environment that facilitates the sharing and recombination of individually possessed knowledge. A key component of this environment is a firm’s information technology (IT) assets, which facilitate the exploration, sharing, and organizing of knowledge. So, firms are investing both in assembling a team of knowledge workers and in acquiring superior IT resources. These knowledge resources are expected to result in product innovations, enabling a firm to gain performance advantages. On the basis of the resource based view (RBV) logic, one may expect a linear, positive relationship between firms’ IT / human capital investments and innovation. We propose that the relationship between these investments and innovation is more likely to follow an inverted-U shape. While IT capital and human capital investments may initially increase a firm’s innovation performance, excessive accumulation of these resources is likely to result in inefficiencies due to increased dynamic adjustment costs resulting from managerial complexity and information overload. We plan to test our predictions using longitudinal survey data collected by the Center for European Economic Research. We will test the interactive effect between these two knowledge resources as theoretically they may play either complementary or substitutable roles in the process of generating innovation. We propose that these two resource bundles interact with each other in complex ways depending on various contingencies. We intend to contribute to the body of work on RBV by recognizing the possible downsides of accumulating strategic resources. Our preliminary findings support the proposed curvi-linear effects and caution both researchers against the dangers of an oversimplified interpretation of RBV. 是否對知識資產（比如技能人力資源/資產、特別是對知識管理十分重要的資訊技術資產）的投資總對企業創新績效是好的呢？由於對人力和數字化知識資產的投資十分昂貴，瞭解這些知識資產投資是否會帶來遞減的回報是一個非常重要的問題。因此，本研究項目致力於回答上述問題。 本研究項目將探索企業對知識資產投資和企業創新績效之間的關係。在企業所擁有的眾多資源中，知識資產被認為具有價值性、稀缺性、難以模仿性和不可替代性等特點。並且，企業的知識通常被認為潛藏于它的員工中。所以，企業的角色是營造一個有利於個體知識相互共享和重新組合的環境。而這樣的環境的一個重要組成部份則是企業的資訊技術資產，因為這些資產有利於探索、共享和組織知識。企業因而不斷對獲取知識型員工和卓越資訊技術進行投資。這些知識資源被認為能夠帶來產品創新，從而使得企業獲得績效優勢。從資源基礎觀出發，人們很容易會認為企業對資訊技術和人力資本投資與企業創新之間是線性的正相關關係。 然而，我們認為這些投資和企業創新之間的關係更可能是一個抛物線的形狀。雖然資訊技術資本和人力資本投資一開始會改善企業的創新績效，過多的積累這些資源可能會導致效率下降，因為管理的複雜性和資訊超載會增加這個過程中的動態調整成本。 我們打算使用歐洲經濟研究中心收集的長期問卷調查數據來驗證我們的預測。另外，鑒於以上兩種知識資源理論上可能在創新過程中存在互補性或替代性，我們還將驗證它們之間的交互效應。我們認為這兩種資源相互影響的方式將比較複雜。通過對戰略資源積累可能會出現的負面影響的認識，我們將對資源基礎觀研究領域做出貢獻。我們初步的研究發現支持知識資產投資與企業創新績效之間存在非線性的關係，揭示了過於簡單化地解讀資源基礎觀所帶來的誤區。

641712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641712.value: Corporate earnings are at the heart of firm valuation and disclosure. Managers practice two forms of earnings management (EM) to influence stock prices in their favor. First, accrual earnings management (AEM) involves accounting choices under GAAP. Second, real earnings management (REM) involves changes in the timing or structuring of operations, investments, and/or financing activities that have cash flow consequences. Our objective is to simultaneously study the AEM and REM activities around corporate stock repurchases and whether these activities can explain the previously documented stock return outperformance after repurchases. We examine whether the outperformance is due to AEM only, REM only, or a combination of the two, as well as the relative impact of the two, especially before and after the passage of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX). Management may prefer REM. First, since it can be disguised as normal business decision making, it is more difficult to detect or be litigated against (e.g., Graham, Harvey, Rajgopal, 2005). This advantage is important in corporate events, given the enhanced scrutiny from investors, auditors, news media, and regulators. Second, Cohen, Dey and Lys (2008) show that management uses AEM and REM as substitutes and has shifted from AEM to REM after SOX. Further, managers who initiate repurchases may prefer certain REM activities (e.g., increased R&D and advertising spending) because their firms can reap the dual benefits of lowering repurchasing cost and improving operating performance after repurchases. Indeed, managers admit their preference for REM in anonymous surveys. We also study specific channels of the outperformance by investigating the impact of firm characteristics such as ownership, monitoring, and information asymmetry on investor understanding of pre-repurchase EM activities. Repurchases differ from most corporate events such as mergers and share offerings where new shares are generally issued, and managers would inflate earnings and thus stock prices; in contrast, the incentive is to deflate earnings and lower stock prices to buy back shares “on the cheap” in repurchases. The preference for conservatism in accounting and auditing standards may make deflating earnings easier. In summary, we will study how much AEM and REM reduce pre-repurchase earnings and whether outside investors fully understand these practices. We will investigate the relative importance of AEM and REM in explaining the post-repurchase outperformance and whether managers use AEM and REM (and different types of REM activities) as substitutes or complements, as well as the impact of firm characteristics. 企业收入是公司估值及信息披露的核心。公司管理者一般采取两种盈余管理方式来影响股票价格向对其有利的方向发展。其一是应计式盈余管理（AEM），涉及GAAP下会计模式的选择。其二是实际盈余管理（REM），涉及那些在运营，投资及融资活动中，具有现金流效应的时间或结构上的变化。我们的目标是通过研究那些与企业股份回购同期发生的应计盈余管理及实际盈余管理活动，来判断我们是否可以用这些活动来解释回购后股票收益优于大盘这一历史记录。 我们将检验收益优于大盘这一现象是否仅由AEM或REM造成，或是由于二者共同作用，同时我们也会考察两者对于收益的相对影响，特别是萨班斯-奥克斯利法案通过的前后。公司管理层可能更偏向使用REM。首先，鉴于REM可以以正常商业决策的形式出现，它将更难以被察觉或诉讼（如，Graham, Harvey, Rajgopal, 2005）。在投资者、审计者、新闻媒体以及法规制定者对于公司的审查日益严格的形势下，这一优势对于公司活动尤为重要。第二，Cohen, Dey，Lys 2008指出管理层曾经把AEM与REM作为互可替代的两种模式，但自萨班斯-奥克斯利法案后，管理层已逐渐从AEM转向REM。再者，发起股份回购的公司管理者可能更倾向于采取某些特定的REM活动（比如增加研发投入和广告支出），因为他们的公司可以从中获取双重利益，即降低回购成本并在回购后提升运营绩效。在匿名调查中，公司管理者承认他们的确更加青睐REM。我们也通过调查公司特征，如所有权，监控及信息不对称等因素，对投资者有关回购前盈余管理活动的理解的影响，研究了收益优于大盘的具体渠道。 回购同大部分的公司活动如并购及新股发行有所不同。在那些活动中，公司会发行新股票，公司管理者将会企图夸大收入以使股价升高。与此相反，在回购中，管理者的动机是通过缩减收入和降低股价，便宜地购入股票。会计及审计标准中的保守倾向使得缩减收入变得较为容易。 总之，我们将研究AEM及REM活动将会在多大程度缩减回购前收入，以及外界投资者是否完全理解这些活动。我们将会调查AEM及REM对于回购后期股票表现优于大盘的相对重要性，以及公司管理者是否将AEM和REM（及不同类型的REM活动）互为替代或互为补足。最后我们还会研究公司特征带来的影响。

641712.label: Major findings and research outcome
641712.value: Prior research finds that investors do not seem to fully appreciate the higher intrinsic value of split firms as stock splits enjoy positive abnormal announcement returns and positive abnormal long-term stock returns. It also shows that brokerage firm produce more information about firms after stock splits, which is an explanation for stock splits. We hypothesize that split firms should aspire to convey their intrinsic value more effectively to investors by engineering significantly positive earnings growth for the firms around splits through understating earnings before splits and overstating earnings after splits, as investors prefer firms with strong earnings growth. Lower pre-split earnings are easier to justify given the preference for conservatism in accounting and auditing standards. More importantly, information production is relatively lower and investors are likely to pay less attention to the understated earnings before splits, whereas the substantially increased information production after splits will help draw investor interest and attention to the positive earnings growth. We also hypothesize that split firms would prefer real earnings management (REM) to accrual earnings management (AEM) as REM is easier to avoid detection. Further, as REM is more costly due to actual deviation from the optimal levels of production, investment, and sales, whereas AEM’s impact are superficial, fairly valued firms may not imitate because they incur real costs while only gaining unsustainable valuation that also create more exposure to litigation for firms and managers. We find evidence consistent with these actions. Specifically, split firms engage in both AEM and REM activities before splits to deflate earnings and after splits to inflate earnings. The levels of earnings-reducing REM but not AEM activities are positively related to abnormal stock returns around split announcements and the post-split abnormal stock returns and operating performance. Our study provides an additional explanation for the positive abnormal announcement effects of stock splits and the long term abnormal returns following stock splits.

641712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641712.value: Our initial plan is to investigate AEM and REM in stock repurchases first, and after a successful investigation we will move to IPOs, and then stock splits. Given that we have examined stock repurchases, IPOs, and stock splits by now, we have reached the natural end of this project well before our initial plan for further development. We will submit the paper soon to international conferences and then to finance and accounting journals.

641712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641712.value: For companies, our research implies that they can manage the valuation of their stocks and help correct any valuation of stocks through a combination of stock splits and real earnings management (REM) around stock splits. As stock investors, among companies announcing stock splits, they would get even greater abnormal stock returns if they invest in firms with abnormally lower earnings due to REM activities. As the firms involved in stock splits have trillions of dollars in market capitalization, the improvement in their valuation or the abnormal returns to investors through the above strategy should not be underestimated.

641912.label: Realisation of objectives
641912.value: We first established the global self-weighted least absolute deviation (SLAD) estimator for finite and infinite variance ARMA models, and then use this approach to study the quasi-maximum exponential likelihood estimator for the double AR model. Its strong consistency and asymptotic normality are established. Furthermore, we introduce a factor double AR model. Based on this model, a score test is proposed to detect causality-in-mean and causality-in- variance simultaneously. The strong consistency and asymptotic normality of its QMLE are established. When the innovation distribution has a heavy tail, we developed an asymptotic theory of LSE of AR models with ARCH-type noises. Furthermore, we developed a systematic procedure of statistical inference for the ARMA model with unspecified and heavy-tailed heteroscedastic noises. When the AR model includes a threshold parameter, we developed a sequence of theory, including the asymptotic theory of LSE in a threshold moving average model and T-CHARM models. When the model has a change-point, we established an estimation theory of change-points in linear and nonlinear times series models, including the double AR model as a special case. Extensive simulation studies was carried out to access the performance of the global QMELEs and test statistics. Our theory and approach have been used the analyze several financial data, including the weekly world crude oil price from 1997 to 2010, the daily exchange rate of United States Dollars to New Taiwan Dollars from 2010 to, 2011, the daily SP500 data , and the causal relationship between Hong Kong stock market and US stock market. Some interesting findings are given.

641912.label: Major findings and research outcome
641912.value: Zhu and Ling (2012) investigated the global self-weighted least absolute deviation (SLAD) estimator for finite and infinite variance ARMA models. The asymptotic theory of the global LAD estimator for finite and infinite variance ARMA models is established in the literature for the first time. Zhu and Ling (2013) studied the quasi-maximum exponential likelihood estimator for the double AR model. Its strong consistency and asymptotic normality are established. An example on the exchange rate is given. Li, Ling and Li (2013) studied the asymptotic theory of least squares estimation in a threshold moving average model. It is shown that the estimator of the threshold is n-consistent and its limiting distribution is related to a two-sided compound Poisson process, whereas the estimators of other coefficients are strongly consistent and asymptotically normal. Ling, Zhu and Chong (2013) first derived the limiting distributions of the residual and the squared residual autocorrelation functions of the nonstationary ARMA model, respectively. We then use them to construct two portmanteau statistics for testing the adequacy of the fitted model. Guo, Ling and Zhu (2014) introduced a factor double autoregressive model. Based on this model, a score test is proposed to detect causality-in-mean and causality-in- variance simultaneously. Furthermore, strong consistency and asymptotic normality of its QMLE are established. Chan, Li, Ling and Tong (2014) developed a simple yet versatile observable mixing function, leading to the conditionally heteroscedastic AR model with thresholds,or a T-CHARM for short. We demonstrate its many attributes and provide comprehensive theoretical underpinnings with efficient computational procedures and algorithms. Finally, we indicate the potential of the approach to random fields. Chen, Li and Ling (2014) first studied the non-stationarity of the first-order double AR model and showed that the sufficient condition in Borkovec and Klauppelberg (2001) is also necessary for strict stationarity. Based on this, it is shown that its QMLE is consistent and asymptotically normal uniformly. Ling (2014) established an estimation theory of change-points in linear and nonlinear times series models. Zhu and Ling (2014) developed a systematic procedure of statistical inference for the ARMA model with unspecified and heavy-tailed heteroscedastic noises. Zhang and Ling. (2014) established asymptotic inference for AR models with heavy-tailed G-GARCH noises. Zhang Sin and Ling (2014) established functional limits of short- and long-memory linear rocesses with GARCH(1,1) noises. Ling, Peng and Zhu (2014) proposed an inference approach for a special bilinear time series model.

641912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641912.value: The double autoregressive (DAR) model is one of ARCH-type time series models and has been extensively used to study the volatility of financial and economic time series. The VaRs based on ARCH-type models are very often used in financial sectors. A lot of empirical evidence shows that, in fitting ARCH-type models, the rescaled errors do not have a finite fourth moment. In this case, no statistical theory for the DAR model has been available up to now. This project has developed the asymptotic theory of global quasi-maximum exponential likelihood estimators (QMELE) and statistical inference for the DAR models. The strong consistency and asymptotic normality of the global QMELE was established under only the stationarity condition. Furthermore, we have constructed test statistics for parameters and model selection under a more general setup. The asymptotic theory of the global QMELE is for the first time to obtain in the literature for the double AR models. Extensive simulation studies was carried out to access the performance of the global QMELEs and test statistics, and real examples was given to illustrate their potentials in real applications. Beside these, we have established a number of theory for the related models and some related statistical inference theory.

642112.value: To study the historical process of frontier formation in Southwest China and the construction of local identities based on the multilayer networks around the Bazi: This study will modify the theory of markets system suggested by Skinner to better understand the long distance trade between interior China, Tibet and upper Burma; even if local groups shared the same infrastructure routes, they still exercised different cultures and different ethnic identities. To study the mutual-creation of social structures, cultural meanings and competitions between the mountains and the Bazi communities. Based on the Zhaozhou case, we will debelop the general framework of a Bazi-based cultural system. This system facilitates ethnic mobilization, resource competitions, as well as the identity reconstruction of the Han settlers and the natives as the Bai, to become the Bazi people.

642112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642112.value: The Yunnan-guizhou Plateau linked the interior of China with Southeast Asia, Tibet and India as a crossroads and cultural transition ground in history. I aim to study the Bazi-based multilayer networks system in western Yunnan. I also want to test a new academic research model to understand the social and cultural institutions facing different civilizations in southwest China. Bazi (壩子) refers to “small basins and relatively flat sectors in a mountainous area”, and is a local term in various languages, including Chinese. The social structure of the Yunnan highland is based on the “spots” of Bazi and the “scope” of mountains as well as the routes crossing the Bazi basins. By investigating four Bazi and their surrounding mountains in the Zhaozhou area, I will study the historical mobilization of identities which include the Lisu, the Laluo, the Menghua, the Bai and the localized Han due to their different responses to the state penetration. Geographic and ecological conditions were the shaping elements for the multilayer networks, and they also influenced the conditions of the agricultural systems, minefields, trade routes and meanings for identities. Through this research, I hope to better understand the regional markets suggested by Skinner, the relationships between the highlands and the lowlands suggested by Leach and the model of Zomia or a “refuge zone” suggested by James C. Scott.

642112.label: Realisation of objectives
642112.value: The four aspects of research objectives have been well sudied, based on six journal articles and six book chapters published in three years. 1) For the historical process of frontier formation, I found that the network based on Bazi basins could extend to mountains communities through caravan transportation based on multilayer agency; 2) for the separation of identieis, I found that there was a historical moblization for ethnic identities when the state changed its policies; 30 for interdependence of communities in the Bazi basins and mountains, I found that the agency of animal traders are crucial and the relationship between agriculture and animal husbandry should be paid more attentionu to further study; 4) I found that, the general framework of Bazi based transportation system has bound the Yangtze River system and the Irrawady River system together in diverse ways. I will initate more studies on this historical and cultural connection based on the continuous reconstruciton of local social agency.

642112.label: Major findings and research outcome
642112.value: The major finding of this research: 1) I found that there is a network based social and cultural system on the borderlands between Southwest China and Southeast Asian highlands; 2) I found that local cultural and identity diversity is based on geographic demarcations between Bazi basin systems and the river valley systems. Ethnic mobilization is based on political movement historically in these systems by different communities as response to the state power, but not beyond the state. 3) In this borderland area between big civilizations, the mechanism of networking is the most crucial element, especially the caravan system for transportation, communication and social maintenance between different communities in different political systems. 4) And, I find that, the facilitation of mule caravan should be based on the regional cooperation between animal husbandry and bean agriculture between communities in the mountains area and the basins. 5) This is the reason that I am applying for a new project to study the regional cooperation between communities in mountains and basins, through the perspective of animal trade and animal rearing, especially on the mules and cooperative social agency between social groups and animals.

642112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
642112.value: Based on the research outcome, I am going to extend my research on regional cooperation between different types of communities through the perspective of animal and human interaction.

642112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
642112.value: This research is based on the interdisciplinary perspective to study the boders between states and between cultural systems, as well as the geographic and ecological limitations of human adapatation and social recreation. It mainly bassed on a historical and anthroplogical research methods for historical archive study and participant observation in data collection. The findings are very significant, which contributes a new way to understand the multilayer borders between China and Southeast Asia, and contributes a new set of knowledge about how to explain cultural diversity and ethnic diversity in this region. This research found that, some new elements including ecology, geography, agriculture and animal training, have been performed important roles to the construction and reconstruction of local societies and human agency. The dynamic of historical transformations also contributed important weight in the shaping of ethnic identities in soical mobilization and separations in this region. This research contributes a new set of knowledge about borderland anthropology and borderland history in general. It opens a new way to develop new knowledg about the big river valley systems (like the Mekong river, the Salween river, the Irrawaddy river) and highland societies study in Southwest China and southeast Asia.

642212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
642212.value: 誰遷移誰留守？中國農村勞動力流動的社會影響

642212.label: Project Objectives
642212.value: Construct a database by merging county-level statistics and surveyed data of labor income/ amount of remittances with the microdata of Census6 (available in early 2012) based on the collaboration with China's National Bureau of Statistics. Document patterns and trends in labor migration by age, sex, level of education and marital status as well as the distribution of incomplete households since the mid-1980s based on PI possessed microdata of previous censuses or national population survey in 1987, 1990, 2000, 2005, and 2010. Are there trends of women’s/ family migration in major sending regions? Develop a typology of disruptive households of labor migration and study the consequences of migration on family structure. What are the main types of disruptive households and how are they distributed by the loss of major roles in the household (husband/father/son/wife/mother/daughter/sibling)? Are duties of farming and care shifted excessively to women or elderly parents left behind in villages? Explain in the family’s choice of an adult member for labor, sequential or return migration by family roles, personal factors, expected labor income/ remittances, and place attributes. Under what condition and at what stage of life cycle does a family choose the husband, the wife, the couple or the unmarried child for migration? What family role is more important than others in terms of its indispensability, intensity, and substitutability? What roles facilitate a labor migration and what roles deter it? Do live-in parents or (rudimentary) boarding school nearby facilitate the migration of married women? Under what condition and at what stage does a migrant family choose to migrate sequentially, return to join family/ start a business? How significant are the effects of hukou relaxation on the sequential migration? In the choice of migration, how similar/ different is the social context of family between China and Mexico/ other developing countries? Study the social consequences on fertility and marital stability. Among the newlyweds, are there significant reducing/ enhancing effects of labor migration on their propensity to give birth/ divorce? What are the effects of migration on the gender (selection) of birth? Who are more prone to divorce in terms of the duration of migration, gender, level of education, number of children, conditions in both the rural origin and the urban destination? How much does labor migration contribute to the fertility decline and increase of divorce rate at provincial and national levels? Study the social consequences on education of the children in high school ages (16 to 18 years old). Under what conditions are children more likely to study in school, stay home farming, or migrate to earn income? Does labor migration of the unmarried enhance their sibling’s propensity to school? Would migration effects on child schooling become less positive or even negative as household disruptions increase orderly with the departure of the father, the mother or both parents? How strong are the enhancing effects of social networks on children’s sequential labor migration? Is school dropout more common in the poverty regions? How does the household registration system reduce the odds and quality of education of the migrants’ children? Study the consequences on the mortality and health of the elderly parent. What are the main differences in male/female mortality schedules (age patterns) between migrating and non-migrating households? What are the effects of labor migration on the mortality of infant, children, labor migrants, and elderly? Does the health of elderly improve or deteriorate? Is there any significant impact of labor migration on increasing life expectancy at the provincial and national levels?

642212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642212.value: In developing countries, labor migration by selected members is a family strategy to avoid the high risks and costs of a family migration. The social costs for the spouse, children, and/or parents left behind, however, are understudied in contrast to surging research on remittances and its positive impacts. The integration of family roles into the process allows modeling labor migration in the social context of a family to study comprehensively its choice about who is migrating and who stay behind, effects of household disruptions as well as the social consequences on family structure, fertility, marital stability, education, and health. Such a study requires a large/ high quality dataset of households consisting migrating and non-migrating members. Most censuses counted migrants only in the destinations. China’s 2010 sixth census (Census6) includes over 100 million migrants in their registered rural households, with rich information on each member’s relationship to the household head, socio-demographics (age, sex, education and completion status, marital status and age at first marriage), migration-specific information (reason, destination and duration), employment (industry/occupation), mortality (death within a year), health (of the elderly) and women’s fertility. Based on the census microdata, surveyed labor income/ remittances, and county-level statistics, we propose to (1) document migration patterns and trends since the mid-1980s; (2) study the distribution of disruptive households and the internal shift of duties by migrant’s role; (3) explain the choice of a member for labor, sequential or return migration by family roles, (expected) labor income, personal factors and place attributes; (4) study effects of migration on newlyweds’ propensity to divorce; (5) study income and disruption effects of father/ mother’s outmigration on the child’s propensity to study in a high school; (6) study migration effects on mortality and health; and (7) evaluate the overall impacts and compare it with other developing countries. This research intends to contribute to a new approach and methodology for studying labor migration in the social context of the family. There are over fifty million married labor migrants in China, leaving tens of millions women, children, and parents are left behind in the villages in "single-parent" or "cross-generation" households. Findings about the social consequences of labor migration have important policy implications for education, urbanization and reform (on its hukou system). Fundamentally, it is about family stability, the education of next generation of migrants, and the health of the population that are all critical to the nation’s future development. 在發展中國家，個體遷移比舉家遷移風險和成本都要小得多。近來研究著重於匯款的正面效應，卻忽略了遷移者的離開對留守配偶，兒童和年老父母造成的社會成本。我們試圖通過對遷家庭的角色分析，全面研究不同成員的遷移對留守家庭的生產、生活、教育和健康帶來的影響。 中國有上億的跨縣勞動力，數以千萬計的婦女，兒童，和年老父母留守農村。內地2010年第六次人口普查（Census6）在遷移出發地統計了包括遷出者和留守者完整家庭信息。基於其微觀數據，我們著重研究1980年代以來的遷移及家庭的變化與趨勢，解釋不同家庭怎樣選擇不同成員遷移，遷移對婚姻，子女教育，老人健康的影響。研究勞動力流動的社會影響具有重要政策意義，有助於教育，城市化和改革戶籍制度改革.

642312.label: Project Title(Chinese)
642312.value: 相信股市：從2007-2008年的金融危機的證據

642312.label: Project Objectives
642312.value: Provide direct and quantitative answers to the question of whether trust in financial institutions affects stock market participation and risk taking? We expect to provide this insight by using the 2007-8 financial crisis as a natural experiment. Study whether trust in financial institutions affect investment decisions after receiving windfall wealth from a suddenly deceased parent. This will overcome concerns about the confounding effect of the crisis through negative wealth shocks. Examine whether the interaction between trust and financial investments are different when individuals inherit from an estate that held stocks. In particular, we are interested in examining whether indirect measures of changes in trust affect individual decision making.

642312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642312.value: Investments in risky assets require that participants have fundamental trust in the asset and the financial market's ability to correctly price the asset. Prior literature suggests that many individuals lack such trust, and that trust can explain participation across individuals and across countries. While the effect of trust on market participation is well documented in the cross section, we know less about the determinants of investor’s perception of the trustworthiness of financial markets. Mistrust might arise from macroeconomic shocks, or personal experiences with biased financial advice. In this project we examine a plausible source of mistrust in financial markets arising from the financial crisis of 2007-8. We hypothesize that if investors are deserting the stock market because of lack of confidence in financial institutions, we would expect the effect to be large for individuals who followed the advice of financial institutions before the crises. In particular, many banks aggressively marketed their stocks to customers which resulted in appreciating share prices. As the crisis unfolded, it became apparent that the prices did not reflect the underlying risk, resulting in massive losses and possibly mistrust. If trust is an important determinant of participation and risk taking, we expect these individuals to be more reluctant to invest in subsequent periods. To identify the effect of trust on investments we propose to study individuals who received windfall wealth due to the sudden death of their parents. If the financial crisis affected individual’s trust in financial markets we expect beneficiaries to liquidate inherited portfolios more often after the crisis than before. Focusing on sudden deaths has two advantages: First, as the timing of sudden deaths is random there should be no difference between individuals receiving windfall wealth before or after the crisis. Second, because the crisis directly affects individual wealth focusing on windfall wealth helps separate the macroeconomic shock from the change in trust. We identify individuals who followed the advice of their bankers and invested in the stock of the bank using information about individuals banking relationship and their stock holdings. As control group we propose to use individuals who invested in the same bank, but who are not account holders. By focusing on the difference in differences between treated individuals and a matched control sample one can attribute the difference to mistrust. Overall, we expect the project to reveal new insights on investor’s perceptions about the trustworthiness of financial markets. 投資於風險資產的要求與會者的資產和金融市場的能力，正確的資產定價的基本信任。在此之前的文獻表明，許多人缺乏這種信任，這種信任可以解釋不同的個體和整個國家的參與。雖然市場上的參與是有據可查的橫截面信任的效果，我們知道的決定因素對投資者的 的可信性金融市場的看法。不信任可能產生的 宏觀經濟的衝擊，或有偏的財務意見的個人經驗。 在這個項目中，我們將研究一個合理的金融市場產生的不信任源 從2007-2008年的金融危機。我們假設，如果投資者是棄 股市由於缺乏對金融機構的信心，我們預期 效果要大的金融機構的建議， 危機。特別是，許多銀行大力推銷自己的股票，導致股價升值的客戶。隨著危機的展開，很明顯的價格並不能反映潛在的風險，造成巨大的損失和可能的不信任。如果信任是一個重要的決定因素的參與和承擔風險的，我們希望這些人更不願投資在後續期間。 要確定投資效果的信任，我們建議研究個人 收到意外的收穫財富由於他們的父母突然死亡。如果金融危機 受影響的個人的信任，在金融市場中，我們期望受益人清算 繼承的投資組合往往在危機之前相比。針對突然死亡 有兩個好處：第一，突然死亡的時間是隨機的，不應該有 經濟危機之前或之後收到意外的收穫財富的個體之間的差異。 第二，因為金融危機直接影響到個人的財富集中在暴利財富 有助於分離的宏觀經濟衝擊的變化信任。 我們確定了個人的建議，他們的銀行和投資 股票的銀行個人銀行業務的關係和他們有關的信息 持有的股票。作為對照組，我們建議使用個人投資於同一個 銀行，但誰不賬戶持有人。通過專注於差異差異 處理個人之間和相匹配的對照樣本，可以將屬性 差異不信任。 整體而言，我們預期該項目上揭示了新的見解投資者的看法 誠信的金融市場。

642312.label: Major findings and research outcome
642312.value: We study how personal experiences affect individual risk taking. To separate the intertwining effects of personal experiences and wealth changes, our identification strategy relies on the decision to keep unexpected inheritances of risky assets. Experience derives from investments in banks that defaulted in the aftermath of the financial crisis. To differentiate the effect of personal experiences, we classify the degrees of experiences into first-hand experiences from personal losses, second-hand experiences from the losses of close family members, and third-hand experiences from living in municipalities where banks defaulted. We find that third-hand experiences result in marginally lower risk taking. Second-hand experiences have a relatively stronger negative effect, whereas the effect of first-hand experiences on risk taking is strongly negative. Overall, our results demonstrate that personal experiences aside from changes in wealth explain substantial heterogeneity in individuals’ risk taking.

642312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
642312.value: At the moment we are looking into a follow up study where we will examine whether changed preferences and/or beliefs can explain why personal experiences affect risk taking. To understand what channel that drives the documented reduction in risk taking, we are considering to conduct lab experiements and use tools from experimental economics to elicit preferences and beliefs. As lab experiments requires funding, the proposed course of action is to develop the research idea into a research grant proposal.

642312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
642312.value: In this study we examine the effect of personal experiences on risk taking in the aftermath of the financial crisis. As a plausible negative personal experience, we identify individuals who trusted the advice of their banks and suffered significant investment losses when the bank subsequently defaulted. We show that individuals with negative personal experiences in the stock market have a significantly lower propensity to hold risky assets in the future. Our findings provide evidence that first-hand experiences can have a causal and sizeable effect on future risk taking, while the magnitude of second- and third-hand effects are substantially smaller. Our study documents that the financial crisis resulted in lower future risk taking, as is evidenced for the generation of Depression babies. The welfare costs of the lower levels of risk taking are likely to be substantial and will lead to significantly lower lifetime consumption. The evidence also raises the question of how and what individuals learn from their past investment experiences. An appropriate response to the personal experiences documented in this study is to diversify the portfolio. Rather, individuals seem to shy away from risk taking and react as suggested by our title: once bitten, twice shy. In future research, it will be interesting to study how individuals learn from their past experiences.

642412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642412.value: In this study we propose and empirically test a valuation model that incorporates a measure of a firm's flexibility (i.e., ability to adapt to yet unknown future challenges and opportunities). The role of flexibility is becoming increasingly important in the wake of increased competitive pressures, where even the most successful companies find it difficult to retain their competitive advantage. Our model builds on the accounting valuation framework and incorporates the insights from the literature on technological change developed in economics and finance. The study contributes to the valuation literature in accounting and finance by capturing the most important component of firm value: its flexibility. It also contributes to the growing literature on the interaction between accounting and real decisions by focusing on the perceived ability to deliver results in the future, as contrasted with the past track record. Finally, it contributes to the literature on the interaction between accounting and industry structure. 本研究项目中，我们的计划是提供一个体现公司经营灵活性（即公司在遇到挑战时的适应能力）的定价模型，并对其进行实证检验。在竞争激烈的当今时代，连最成功的企业都很难保证其优势的持续，所以经营上的灵活性日趋重要。我们的模型建于现有的定价理论框架的基础上，并结合了经济及公司财务文献中有关技术变更方面的研究成果。本研究会对会计及金融文献中的定价理论做出贡献，具体在于体现灵活性对企业价值的作用。本研究也会进一步阐明会计与实体活动之间的相互作用，把侧重面放在未来创造业绩的能力，而不是停留于对过去业绩的记录。最后，本项目也对会计与产业结构的相互作用方面的研究做出贡献。

642512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642512.value: A fundamental aspect of economic development is the process of structural change by which countries move up the production ladder and produce increasingly sophisticated goods as the cost of labor increases. Unfortunately, there is great variation in the success of countries and firms in following this path, but relatively little microeconomic evidence on the factors that determine success. In this project we propose to analyse how manufacturing firms in the Pearl River Delta are reacting to rapidly increasing costs of labor using data from a matched survey of 500 firms and 6000 workers in Guangdong. Collecting our own data enables us to gather detailed information on firm decisions to upgrade technologies and produce new goods, the employment and wages of workers of different skill levels, and factor market imperfections. Matched data on firms and workers, which have not been previously collected in developing countries (except Mexico), enables more rigorous and less biased estimation of the determinants of employment and wages, which can provide new insights into the microeconomics of structural adjustment in developing countries and the performance of the labor market. Using this uniquely rich data on firms and workers in China, we calculate descriptive statistics and conduct econometric analysis to answer three research questions: 1) How have different firms responded to higher labor costs by adjusting employment (number and skill level), capital, technology, or goods produced, and what have been the barriers to such adjustment?; 2) How well have labor regulations been enforced and to what extent have labor costs increased for different types of firms in the Pearl River Delta?; and 3) What is the extent of labor market segmentation for different types of workers and firms? China’s Pearl River Delta is an ideal study site for carrying out research on this topic. As the world’s dominant manufacturer of labor-intensive goods, China is the ultimate case for studying the process of industrial upgrading in response to changing comparative advantage. China is entering a new development phase in which the cost of labor is rising rapidly and the production of labor-intensive goods has begun to shift to other countries. The extent to which Chinese firms can effectively meet this challenges will shape China’s (and by association Hong Kong’s) economic growth trajectory in the years to come. Thus the results of this research will be both of considerable academic interest and have significant policy implications for both China and Hong Kong. 经济发展的一个基本方面是结构的变化。在此过程中国家走向更高的生产阶梯；而且随着劳动力成本的增加，企业生产越来越复杂的产品。国家和企业在走这条道路方面的成功经验非常不同。不幸的是，对决定成功的因素的微观经济证据方面的探讨相对较少。在本项目中，我们将分析在珠江三角洲地区的制造企业如何应对迅速增长的劳动力成本。数据来自与此项目匹配的对600家企业和6000名工人的调查。收集自己的数据使我们能够得到详细的企业的技术进步和新产品生产的决策信息，以及不同类型的劳动力成本和劳动力的技能构成。企业和员工的匹配数据可以实现对工资差异和企业生产率的决定因素有更严谨和较少偏见的估计，但到目前为止中国还没有收集过此类数据。 使用这种独特而丰富的中国企业和员工的数据，我们将进行描述性统计计算和经济计量分析。这些计算和分析要回答三个具体的研究问题：1）劳动力法规是如何执行以及珠江三角洲地区不同类型企业的劳动力成本上升的程度？ 2）不同企业在调整就业（数量和技能水平），资本，技术，或生产产品方面如何应对劳动力成本的提高？调整的障碍（例如，信贷限制，管理能力，劳动者素质等）是什么？ 3）针对不同类型的工人和企业的劳动力市场的分化程度？中国的珠江三角洲是开展此项研究的理想区域。作为世界上占主导地位的劳动力密集型产品的制造商，中国是研究因应不断变化的比较优势促进产业升级的最后（？）的案例。中国正在进入一个新的发展阶段--劳动力成本迅速上升；廉价的劳动力密集型产品的生产开始转移到其他国家。中国在何种程度上可以有效地应对这一挑战将决定中国（包括香港）在未来数年的经济增长轨迹。因此，本研究的结果将具有极高的学术价值，并对中国和香港的政策有重要指导意义。

642712.label: Project Objectives
642712.value: To contribute to the literature on CEO horizon and CEO short-termism, specifically focusing on its effects. To study the effect of CEO short-termism on stock prices and executive actions and produce a working paper publishable in one of the top finance journals.
rows: To contribute to the literature on CEO horizon and CEO short-termism, specifically focusing on its effects.
To study the effect of CEO short-termism on stock prices and executive actions and produce a working paper publishable in one of the top finance journals.

642712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
642712.value: In recent times there has been a growing concern about horizons of corporate managers being too short, resulting in attempts to increase stock prices in the short run at the cost of long term value (e.g., Bebchuk and Fried (2010)).In this discussion, the compensation structure of top managers has been considered an important contributing factor to managerial myopia. However, there is no clear understanding of how exactly managers with greater short term incentives behave differently. Further, the extent to which the market is fooled by actions aimed towards inflating the stock price in the near term by myopic managers is not clear. While some studies have shown an empirical link between equity-based compensation and behavior aimed towards manipulating stock prices (like earnings management), these do not directly answer the questions that we plan to examine: Do managers with short-term orientation behave differently, and if so, how? Do they try to inflate stock prices at certain times, and if they do, to what extent does the market see through this? A unique aspect of our study would be that we plan to exploit the time-varying nature of CEOs’ short-term incentives to inflate stock prices through corporate actions or decisions. The date when executive stock options are going to vest (i.e. become exercisable) are known long in advance. If a large number of deep-in-the money are going to vest in a few months, the CEO is likely to want to increase the stock price until the vesting date. To the extent that many CEOs exercise the options on vesting, such incentives fall (on an average) after the vesting date. We plan to compare stock returns and behavior of such CEOs in the period right before vesting of a large number of deep-in-the-money (when the CEO has strong incentives to increase stock prices), to the period right after vesting. In particular, we plan to examine investments, R&D expenditure, positive/negative news release propensity, and accruals. A crucial aspect of our empirical strategy is that we would identify such periods in advance i.e., before the periods begin. This would help circumvent standard endogeneity concerns in such studies, allowing us to make cleaner causal inferences about effect of managerial short-termism. Our study is likely to be of interest to shareholders of firms, boards of directors interested in setting optimal incentives for CEOs through compensation structures, compensation consultants, financial analysts, and regulators.

643412.label: Project Title(Chinese)

To explore the theoretical implications of these two cases in comparative perspective in the light of recent discourses regarding comparative modernization, corporation vs. network, and law and development.

To explore the theoretical implications of these two cases in comparative perspective in the light of recent discourses regarding comparative modernization, corporation vs. network, and law and development.

643412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
643412.value: This is a book-length project to narrate and interpret the early corporate histories of two giant textbook publishing houses in Meiji Japan (1868-1912) and modern China (late-Qing and Republican periods, ca. 1890s-1930s). They were the Golden Harbor Press and the Commercial Press. Japan and China had consecutively embarked on educational reform modeling from the West, making Western-style textbooks one of the most influential vehicles of cultural transmission for modernity in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The two companies in this study emerged as the most leading textbook publishers in their respective countries. Their roles in the cultural transformation are therefore highly significant. Meanwhile, both broke away from tradition by adopting the Western model of corporation within two years from the time when a company law was first enacted in their respective countries. They therefore make perfect comparison in exposition of the interplay among business, law and education in pursuit of modernity in Meiji Japan and modern China. This study will explore how the modern Western business model of corporation under a company law regime was transplanted into Meiji Japan and modern China through a comparison of the two said cases in the field of education. Our working hypothesis is that although the model of corporation has a strong universal character, outcome of transplantation might have been shaped mainly by the entrepreneurship that negotiated the model as a new alternative within their respective changing business cultural environments as well as opportunities structure. In this approach, while law and institution in letter can be transplanted with remarkably similar features, the economic effects are shaped by human choices bounded by local cultural settings, which were in a dynamic evolutionary process mingling the indigenous and exogenous cultural elements. Our cases therefore can reflect if there were indeed divergent paths of modernizing textbook business with the same Western model, and each with a different outcome. The findings of this project will not only largely enhance our knowledge of the two cases but inform in important way the discourses on comparative modernization, corporation and corporate law transplant, and relationship between law and economic development. The anticipated outcome of this study is to produce international refereed journal articles and to make presentations at international conferences and higher learning institutions. A book manuscript will be prepared as the final outcome. 本項目旨在論述及詮釋兩家重要教科書出版社的早期歷史，即明治時期的金港堂與晚清民國的商務印書館。日本及中國先後開展西式的近代學制，教科書在當時可說是特別重要的近代文化傳播載體。這兩家公司在兩國先後崛起而執教科書的牛耳。其在文化傳播上的作用至為鉅大。另一方面，兩家出版社亦先後在其國家立法引入公司法時馬上轉型擁抱新的西式企業制度。職是之故，他們可以提供很好的案例，讓我們比較中日兩國在商業、法律以及教育三層面的近代轉型交接點上有何異同之處。 首先是西式企業及其企業法規在中日兩國的移植問題。我們的理論假設是，雖然西式企業模式具有強烈的全球性格，移植的結果仍取決於繼受國的企業家，如何回應由移植制度以及故有商業文化的變迁而帶來的新契機。我們的兩個個案，有助探討當時兩國的教科書現代化取徑，是否同中有異， 以致同塗而殊歸。我們的研究成果不特增進有關兩家出版社的知識，而且為比較近代化、企業與企業法移植、法律與經濟發展等課題提供重要的實証知識。我們計劃在國际期刊及國际學術會議上發表相關的成果，並撰寫一冊專書。

643412.label: Realisation of objectives
643412.value: There are three objectives for this project: (1) To construct a narrative of the Golden Harbor Press in the textbook business of Meiji Japan. (2) To construct a narrative of the Commercial Press in the textbook business of modern China. (3)To explore the theoretical implications of these two cases in comparative perspective in the light of recent discourses regarding comparative modernization, corporation vs. network, and law and development. For objectives (1) and (2), we have completed our data collection and yielded unexpectedly rich materials from the archives in Shanghai and Tokyo in particular. This material enables us to construct the narratives of the two publishing enterprises with some breakthroughs. Firstly, we will be able to sort out some of the controversial issues in previous scholarship and produce more archival and empirical based accounts of the companies. Secondly, we have found enough materials to make the connection of the two companies now one of the major building blocks in our narrative construction. Thirdly, with newly collected information, we are now able to elucidate the development of the two companies in the broader context of the modern business sector in both countries, in particular the business and social networks the two publishers had with Sheng Xuanhui and some Chinese corporations based in Shanghai and with Shibusawa Eiichi and Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and its Shanghai branch. Some of the data were used in our conference presentations and published works. The bulk of them will be analyzed further and incorporated into a book manuscript we are preparing. In terms of research discovery, we consider we have achieved far more than we originally planned. It will allow us to produce a book-length manuscript solidly grounded upon archival evidence. It promises to change the way we understand how these companies work and how they react to upheaval changes of their times. Objective (3) was also achieved with breakthrough. Instead of sticking to the three old discourses named in our proposal, we now are moving beyond them and able to develop a new framework to look at the theoretical implications of these enterprises. Our new underpinning theme is about the entrepreneurs and their reaction to the new opportunities created by the change of the legal framework for business. We have a book contract with Routledge and aim at finishing the manscript by summer 2016.

643412.label: Major findings and research outcome
643412.value: We have already published, submitted to journal or book for publication some of our findings. Still under preparation are one journal article and a book manuscript,which is under contract with Routledge. Altogether there will be 10 items. We have also presented partial outcome of our project in 14 international conferences or presentations in Hong Kong, Shanghai, Beijing, Wuhan, Xiamen, Hai Kou, Paris, Florence, Sydney, and Binghamton (NY). Some contents of these papers were presented to different audience from different disciplines, like history, law, and economics, in order to gain more specialised feedbacks for endorsement and improvement of ideas and delivery. See Part C for details of these outcomes. More findings will be presented in our book manuscript. Some of the major findings can be summarized as follows: 1. While the two companies adopted transplanted institutions and followed the development of the legal frameworks largely also transplanted, each retained significant characteristics of local cultural heritage in both business ethics and practices. 2. The divergence of their localization of transplanted institutions was largely due to the sociopolitical and economic environment at the national and global level but also shaped very much by the personal priorities and aspirations of the entrepreneurs of these two companies. 3. Major business decisions of these entrepreneurs were often reactions to new opportunities created by the new legal framework. 4. These entrepreneurs participated in the shaping of the new legal frameworks and in the legitimation of these transplanted law and institutions through their dominance in the textbook business. 5. One salient feature of the entrepreneurial decisions is the dilemma in balancing those prevalent, but often contradictory, business values and aspirations of the times. 6. An important message to emerge in these narratives will be the individuality of entrepreneurship that cannot be accounted for as simple execution of political ideology, self-interest pursuit, or traditional business ethics. 7. A prevailing discourse today is about how global institutions and norms are being transplanted locally with various degrees of adaptation. Our two company case studies should feed good information to that discussion by demonstrating the value of case knowledge in addressing the broader and more general inquiry.

643412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
643412.value: As a result of the completion of this project, the PI is now applying for another GRF grant to study the British publisher Macmillan House in the last decades of the 19th century and the first few decades of the 20th. The subject matter and the historical backdrop of the Macmillan House is completely different from those of the Golden Harbor Press and the Commercial Press. The new project is therefore not considered as a continuation of the completed project but rather a new project in its own right. The approach and methodology will however not be entirely different. In fact the new project is inspired by the completed one and will have one objective set to compare the three companies across three countries and to see modern textbook publishing in a new perspective of global history. While confined more to East Asia, the findings of this completed project will hence constitute a knowledge foundation that facilitates the kind of more global comparison.

643412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
643412.value: This project is about the stories of two major textbook companies in Meiji Japan and in early-20th-century China. They were the main suppliers for the emerging huge demand of textbooks as the two countries underwent education reform modeled on the West. The business is highly lucrative, but also demanding in financing, editing and production. The large investment now required in publishing was unprecedented. From the very beginning, the two companies adapted creatively to the new business institutions and operations transplanted from the West and gained an upper hand in the market. The key model they transplanted was the same: joint-stock company with limited liability. The paths they took advantage of the new corporate model differed and their fortunes diverged after 30 years in business. The Commercial Press in Shanghai became the undisputed leader in the publishing industry in general and the textbook business in particular. The Kinkodo shoseki kaisha became ever more obsolete in the Japanese publishing market and finally lost their last stronghold in textbook publishing, the Tokyo shoseki kaisha, by the 1920s.

643612.label: Project Title(Chinese)
643612.value: 同事的社会影响：理解同事影响员工的过程

643612.label: Project Objectives
643612.value: To understand different forms of social influence exerted by a coworker and the processes through which this influence ensues. To demonstrate the psychological mechanism through which a coworker’s positive influences translate into work output of the focal employee. To provide a more complete and realistic view of the dynamics underlying the influence of a coworker.
rows: To understand different forms of social influence exerted by a coworker and the processes through which this influence ensues.
To demonstrate the psychological mechanism through which a coworker’s positive influences translate into work output of the focal employee.
To provide a more complete and realistic view of the dynamics underlying the influence of a coworker.

643612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
643612.value: Due to the flatter organizational structures and the increasing use of teams, there is increased recognition of the important role that a coworker (or coworkers) can play in facilitating employee job performance behaviors (Chiaburu & Harrison, 2008), including both in-role (task performance) and extra-role (organizational citizenship behavior [OCB]) behaviors (e.g., Hoffman et al., 2007; Williams & Anderson, 1991). I refer here to in-role behavior (or task performance) as the expected behaviors “that are directly involved in producing goods or services, or activities that provide indirect support for the organization’s core technical processes” (Van Scotter et al., 2000, p. 526) and extra-role (or organizational citizenship behavior [OCB]) as “individual behavior that is discretionary, not directly or explicitly recognized by the formal reward system, and in the aggregate promotes the efficient and effective functioning of the organization” (Organ et al., 2006, p. 4). While I know that coworkers can have an impact on each other’s attitudes and behaviors, I still do not know exactly how and why one employee influences another. Though classical research has argued that closely related coworkers affect each other’s work output (Mayo, 1933; Roethlisberger & Dickson, 1939; Salancik & Pfeffer, 1978; Schneider, 1987), there is a limited number of studies research on the underlying mechanisms and the different types of influence that an employee has on another employee (cf. Chiaburu & Harrison, 2008). In other words, our understanding is still limited with regard to the roles that a closely related coworker plays in fostering an employee’s job performance behaviors and the processes through which such an influence is achieved. As such, there is void in our understanding about how and why a closely related coworker exerts an importance influence on the focal employee. Without such an understanding of a coworker, organizational interventions such as pay for performance that are aimed solely at the employee to enhance job performance behaviors (cf. Stajkovic & Luthans, 2001) may be inefficient and ill-suited in affecting employee job performance behaviors. Furthermore, “coworkers have been given comparatively less systematic attention using integrative frameworks, and their influences on focal employees have not been organized” (Chiaburu & Harrison, 2008, p. 1097). Thus, I consider it important to advance our understanding of how and why a coworker influences another employee. I intend to achieve the objective by conducting rigorous, empirically based research using full-time employees working in Hong Kong. 源于组织架构扁平化及团队建构的普及，同事影响对于促进员工绩效的重要作用受到越来越多的认可 (Chiaburu & Harrison, 2008)。员工绩效包括组织中员工的角色内行为（任务绩效）及角色外行为（组织公民行为）（e.g., Hoffman et al., 2007; Williams & Anderson, 1991)。在此，员工角色内行为（任务绩效）是指直接涉及生产产品或提供服务或间接为组织核心技术流程提供支持的预期行为 (Van Scotter et al., 2000, p. 526)，角色外行为（组织公民行为）即员工自行决定、非直接明确为正规奖励制度所认可、总体而言会促进组织有效运作的个体行为(Organ et al., 2006, p. 4)。 虽然已知同事之间会构成对彼此态度与行为的影响，员工如何以及为何会影响他人的问题尚属未知。经典研究已论证关系密切的同事间会构成工作输出的相互影响（Mayo, 1933; Roethlisberger & Dickson, 1939; Salancik & Pfeffer, 1978; Schneider, 1987)，但研究同事影响类型及根本机制的课题非常有限 (cf. Chiaburu & Harrison, 2008)。换言之，我们对于关系密切的同事影响员工绩效的角色以及过程的理解仍然有限。同事影响研究的缺失在实践中可能导致仅强调员工强化绩效的组织干预（如绩效工资制度）对员工绩效失去效力。此外，在综合性框架中，同事系统性地受到相对较少的关注，而他们对于员工的影响尚未结构化 (Chiaburu & Harrison, 2008, p.1097)。因此，我认为推进对于员工如何以及为何影响同事的理解具有重要意义。为实现该目的，我计划以香港全职员工为样本实施严谨的实证研究。

643612.label: Realisation of objectives
643612.value: In terms of the three objectives noted previously, I have satisfied all three objectives fully by examining and demonstrating impacts a coworker has on the "focal employee" by demonstrating that a coworker can influence focal employees' task performance as well as citizenship behaviors through social learning processes (Chen, Takeuchi, & Shum, 2013). In this study, we utilized two datasets collected by the PI to develop a conceptual model (and associated relationship) that illustrates that a coworker can influence the focal employee outcomes (task performance and citizenship behavior) through a reduction in employee's role ambiguity as well as being a role model (through being a good citizen). The findings contribute to the coworker influence literature by showing that one coworker can affect the focal employee in a meaningful manner. I also currently have two manuscripts under review (Takeuchi & Chandrashekar, under review; Takeuchi, Shum, & Chiaburu, under review) from this research effort.

643612.label: Major findings and research outcome
643612.value: Using several datasets collected as part of this research project effort, we find in one of the papers that a coworker can influence a closely related (focal) employee’s job performance behaviors in a meaningful manner through different processes. In this study, The PI and collaborators integrate social information processing and social cognitive theories with social exchange and role theories to hypothesize that there are, at least, three distinct types of coworker dyadic influence. Accordingly, we develop and test a moderated mediation model to explicate such influence. Two multi-source, field-design studies conducted in Hong Kong supported the modeled relationships in that employee role ambiguity partially mediated the relationships between coworker-employee exchange (CEX) and two types of employee job performance behaviors—task performance and organizational citizenship behavior (OCB). Furthermore, coworker OCB fostered employee job performance behavior both directly and interactively, acting as a moderator to weaken the relationships between employee role ambiguity and the two types of job performance behaviors. In addition, in another study (Takeuchi & Chandrashekar), we explicate how observing the abuse of a coworker shapes the focal employee's deviance behaviors. Social learning and information processing perspectives were applied to theorize more comprehensively coworkers’ influences, and the inferences were tested using data from a survey of 527 supervisor-employee-coworker triads in Hong Kong. The data provide empirical support for the hypotheses. They show that there are multiple pathways through which a coworker’s experience affects the focal employee. More specifically, they show that observing the abuse of a coworker by a mutual supervisor promotes deviant workplace behavior, both interpersonal and organizational. The coworker’s response to abuse can also serve as a role model. Theoretical and practical implications are discussed. Finally, in Takeuchi, Shum, and Chiaburu (under review), we extend social exchange theoretical perspective on leader-member exchange (LMX) by proposing a two-side employee–manager social exchange processes: employee reciprocates high quality exchange with the manager [LMX] with enhanced organizational citizenship behaviors [OCBs]), which, in turn, are reciprocated by the manager, in terms of higher reward recommendation. We then hypothesize that such social exchange processes are bounded by the employee’s relational context such that there is a positive interaction between employee’s and close coworker’s LMX on OCBs. We also found that the employee is more likely to incorporate coworker’s social information when s/he has higher uncertainty about his/her exchange relationship with manager. These studies together shed lights on coworker influences that we did not know before.

643612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
643612.value: While we have developed three manuscripts from the current research effort, we have yet to publish the remaining two papers. Thus, we intend to further pursue this research by revising these manuscript such that they can be eventually published at top tier management journals. In addition, I intend to pursue this research area in the near future as well.

643612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
643612.value: The current research projects have demonstrated that one, single coworker who is close to the focal employee can exert significant influence in terms of various employee behaviors such as his/her own role-expected performance (task performance), extra-role behaviors (such as citizenship behaviors), as well as counterproductive work behaviors (such as deviance). While many individuals may believe that a single coworker may not necessarily exert significant influence on an employee, our study collectively demonstrate that this perception is actually very misleading. This depends on the particular coworker being investigated. In other words, someone who is considered close to the focal employee can exert either positive or negative influences on focal employee's work behaviors (citizenship or counterproductive, deviant behaviors), which should be important for managers who need to manage the various interpersonal relationships that exist at work in an effective manner.

643912.label: Project Title(Chinese)
643912.value: 金融發展、存續率已經資本雙向流動

643912.label: Project Objectives
643912.value: Document the empirical relationship between financial development and saving rate using cross-country panel data. Construct an incomplete-market model featuring both heterogeneous households and heterogeneous firms to explain this empirical relationship. Study the two-way capital flows in a two-country model extension. Characterize the optimal Ramsey capital income tax.
rows: Document the empirical relationship between financial development and saving rate using cross-country panel data.
Construct an incomplete-market model featuring both heterogeneous households and heterogeneous firms to explain this empirical relationship.
Study the two-way capital flows in a two-country model extension.
Characterize the optimal Ramsey capital income tax.

643912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
643912.value: This project aims to document the empirical relationship between an economy's financial development and the national saving rate. Our preliminary results show evidence of an inverted-U-shaped relationship. We will develop an incomplete-market model featuring both heterogeneous households and heterogeneous firms to explain this hump-shaped relationship. The key insight of the model will be that financial development tends to reduce the precautionary saving incentives of households but increase firms' ability to borrow and invest. As a result, the aggregate saving rate may rise initially with financial development because of higher investment by firms, but then decline ultimately with further financial development because of substantially reduced precautionary savings by households. The model will also predict that the market interest rate lies substantially below the rate of return to capital in emerging economies, but the gap diminishes with financial development, as observed in the data. Such prediction has important implications for international capital flows. It suggests that if poorly developed economies are open to countries with more advanced financial markets, financial capital will flow from the developing to the developed countries while physical capital(in terms of FDI) will flow from the developed to the developing countries to enjoy high capital returns. Explaining such two-way flows in an open economy model will be another research objective of the project. We also plan to study the optimal taxation of capital income in such economies. Previous studies on the borrowing constraints on households recommend positive taxes on capital income with incomplete markets. The intuition may be explained as follows. Because of incomplete insurance markets there is a precautionary motive for accumulating excess (greater than the optimal level of) capital. A positive tax rate on capital income will therefore be needed to reduce capital accumulation toward its optimal level. We will show that once both households and firms are credit constrained, the optimal tax rate on capital income may be zero, negative or positive depending on the stage of financial development. This is because credit constraints on firms may hamper capital accumulation. A negative tax rate on capital income is then helpful to stimulate capital accumulation to higher level that it would otherwise be. 本課題將研究金融發展與存續率之間的經驗關係。我們初步結果表明這兩者存在一個倒U形關係。我們將建立一個帶有異質家庭和企業的不完備市場的宏觀模型對這一關係來解釋這一經驗關係。在模型中， 金融發展會導致家庭存續率下降而企業的存續將上升。因此， 金融發展對存續率可能產生非線性的作用。我們模型將預測利率比資本回報率低很多。 該模型很好得解釋了興新市場國家金融市場開發時候出現資本的雙向流動。金融資本將會像發展發達國家流動， 而固定資本將向興新市場國家流動。我們也打算用這一模型來研究是否對資本收入加以徵稅。

643912.label: Realisation of objectives
643912.value: Most of the objectives of the project have been realized. The empirical relationship between financial development and saving rate is documented by cross-country panel data. A robust hump-shaped relationship between these two variables emerges in the data. A model with incomplete financial markets is built to explain such a pattern. The model is then extended to an open economy to study capital flows. The extended model explains an interesting two-way capital flows pattern. Namely, financial capital flows from emerging countries to the U.S and fixed capital flows from the US to emerging countries. The last objective is to characterize the optimal Ramsey capital income tax is not fully realized. The Ramsey tax is known to be difficult even with complete financial market. It is very demanding task with incomplete financial market. So far, we are able to work out the Ramsey problem under some special case. We are still working on the general setting.
