643912.label: Major findings and research outcome
643912.value: This project yields two excellent completed papers. One titled "Two-Way Capital Flows and Global Imbalances" is now accepted by the Economic Journal, a prestigious journal. This paper studied an important puzzle regarding capital flows. The Nobel Prize Laurette, Lucas (1990), ponder why capital does not flow from North (developed countries such as the US) to South (developing countries such as China) the standard neoclassical growth theory predicts. To tackle this puzzle, we first show that the capital-flow puzzle is partially a fallacy of aggregation. In reality, fixed capital does flow mainly from North to South, in the form of foreign direct investment (FDI). It is financial capital (portfolio investment) that has been allowing in the opposite direction. Since historically the "uphill" flows of financial capital dominate the "downhill” flows of fixed capital, the net aggregate capital flow (financial plus fixed) shows the reverse pattern. The paper then provides a framework to explain the two-way capital flow puzzle by augmenting the neoclassical growth model with financial frictions under incomplete markets. Our story proceeds as follows. Due to an underdeveloped banking-credit financial system, both households and firms in the South are severely borrowing constrained. As a result, households opt to save excessively to self-insure against unpredictable shocks, and firms have to rely heavily on internal cash flow to finance fixed investment. Since domestic savings by households cannot be effectively channeled to firms where fixed capital formation takes place, fixed capital is scarce in the production sector while savings are abundant in the household sector. In such a world, the rate of financial assets is low while the return on physical investment is high. This enormous arbitrage opportunity implies that financial liberalization between the South and the North will trigger two-way capital flows. The other paper, “ Financial Development and Aggregate Saving Rates: A Hump-Shaped Relationship”, documented a hump-shaped empirical relationship between financial development and the national saving rate across 102 countries. An incomplete-market model featuring both heterogeneous households and heterogeneous firms is provided to explain this hump-shaped relationship. The key insight of the model is that financial development tends to reduce the precautionary-saving incentives of households but increase firms' ability to borrow and invest. As a result, the aggregate saving rate may rise initially with financial development because of greater investment by firms, but then declines with further financial development because of substantially reduced precautionary savings by households.

643912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
643912.value: The framework developed in the project has important policy implication such as capital taxation and capital control. The optimal Ramsey capital income problem however is notoriously difficult to characterize. We have only be able to obtain results in some special cases. We have not fully solve the problem yet for general setting yet. Also, the framework developed in the project can also used to study the relationship between financial development and growth.

643912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
643912.value: This project yields two excellent completed papers. One of them is accepted by the Economic Journal, a prestigious general interest journal in economics. The other is still under review. The project study the implication of financial frictions on national saving, investment, and capital flows. It documented a hump-shaped empirical relationship between financial development and the national saving rate across 102 countries. This sheds light on China's high saving puzzle. The project also studied an important puzzle regarding international capital flows. It helps explain the pattern of two-way capital flows between emerging economies (such as China) and the developed world (such as the United States). Our calibrated model reproduces China's rising financial capital outflows and FDI inflows as well as its massive trade imbalances in the past decades. Our model also predicts that (i) global trade imbalances may be sustainable even in the long run and (ii) the conventional wisdom that the “saving glut” of emerging economies is responsible for the global low interest rate may be wrong.

644012.label: Project Objectives
644012.value: Our project will analyze a market-oriented multi-stage privatization process, instead of a fully government-controlled process. We will seek to find what the crucial factors are and how these factors affect such a staged process. This project aims to determine how factors such as the lockup effect, demand elasticity, performance growth and business fluctuations affect staged privatization from both theoretical and empirical points of view. 644012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644012.value: The recent Chinese privatization program is in the form of staged privatization with multi-stage lockups. The multi-stage lockups are determined by market forces. Our project is to develop a theory and find empirical evidence for staged privatization. Such a theory will be dependent on a specification of a lockup effect on demand. We will show the existence of this lockup effect through our empirical analysis. With such a theory, we can analyze how various factors, such as the lockup effect, demand elasticity, performance potential and business fluctuations, affect a staged privatization process, especially the equilibrium speed of privatization. Our project is the first to analyze a market-oriented multi-stage privatization process, instead of a fully government- controlled process. We also intend to show that staged privatization is efficient in the sense that it can successfully transform an SOE to an efficient firm by the end of the reform program. The lockups in privatization resemble initial public offerings (IPOs). Hence, by studying this reform, we can shed light on our understanding of IPOs from a unique angle. 中国最近的私有化計劃是采取分段私有化．大都数世界各地的私有化是采取多阶段步骤的．多阶段私有化是由市场机制来实现的．这个项目为分段私有化建立一个理论和提供实验证据．

All the published papers are published on top international journals in their own fields. This grant also supported three MPhi students and three PhD students in the fields funded by this project. 644112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644112.value: 经济发展是综合着城市化、贸易全球化和经济增长的一个整体过程。在这个研究计划中我们问三个问题：（1）贸易对一个发展中国家的经济增长有多大的贡献？（2）城市化对以个发展中国的经济增长有多大的贡献？（3）贸易是如何影响一个发展中经济的地区不平等和经济增长的？ 前两个问题是经济学中的热点问题。然而在定量研究的文献中主要使用的是简约方式（reduced form），而大多数结构性的研究(structural studies)则集中在发达经济。在这个计划中，我们旨在建立一个结构性模型将国际贸易以及农村到城市的劳动力转移放在一个动态的框架中加以研究，并且对先前提出的三个问题作出定量的回答。原则上，前两个问题可以分别回答，但在回答第三个问题的时候，就必须同时考虑贸易和城市化，包括它们之间的互相影响。对于像中国这样的一个发展中经济而言，在快速增长的同时地区间的不平等不断放大。如何在地区不平等与经济增长之间取得平衡？这个问题越来越重要。贸易和开放是同时影响经济增长和地区不平等的重要因素。那么，当一个国家的不同地区相对开放程度发生变化时，它对于地区不平等和经济增长将会有怎样的潜在影响呢？ 尤其是中国的沿海地区要比内陆地区增长快得多，那么内陆地区加大开放以后，会妨碍经济增长吗？会降低地区不平等吗？如果是，那影响多少？一种可能的情况是经济增长率的微降伴随着地区不平等的大幅降低，另一种可能是经济增长率的大幅降低伴随着地区不平等的小幅下降。在这两种不同情况下的政策含义有着很大的差别。 我们建立一个模型，同时考虑了对贸易和城市化的两种观点：（1）贸易通过进入国外市场和按照比较优势专业化分工从而促进经济增长，（2）城市化通过人力资本的溢出效用促进增长。这个研究计划的新颖之处在于我们将建立一个三地区的动态的Eaton–Kortum模型，从而使我们能够用一个结构性的方式对这三个定量问题同时加以回答。对于静态分析，由Eaton and Kortum (2002) 和 Bernard, Eaton, Jenson, and Kortum (2003) （之后称为 BEJK模型）发展出来的贸易和地理模型在国际贸易领域中极富影响。这些贸易模型包含了李嘉图比较优势，而且它们的结构非常具有灵活性并且容易处理，这对于定量分析非常合适。同时，对于动态分析而言，人力资本外部性对于思考内生经济增长和城市化是一个非常自然的方式。最终，我们将主要通过对中国数据的微调（calibration）来探讨这个模型的定量的含义。

644212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644212.value: Previous studies (e.g., Diether, Malloy, and Scherbina, DMS, 2002) have found that dispersion in analysts’ earnings forecasts, measured by the standard deviation of forecast earnings per share (FEPS) scaled by the absolute value of the mean of FEPS, is negatively associated with future stock returns in the cross section. Since forecast dispersion is interpreted as differences of opinion, DMS interpret their result as inconsistent with the risk-based explanation, but consistent with behavioral explanation in that stock prices only reflect the valuation of optimistic investors under short-sale constraints (e.g., Miller, 1977). However, our recent study has found that the mean of FEPS positively predicts future stock returns. In addition, our preliminary result also indicates that the standard deviation of FEPS is negatively associated with future returns and the return predictability is more pronounced for the mean than for the standard deviation of FEPS. All these results suggest that DMS’ interpretation of the return predictability of forecast dispersion may not be complete. It is therefore important to understand whether the return predictability of forecast dispersion comes mainly from its standard deviation or its mean or both to help us understand the economic intuition and interpretation. Unfortunately, the mean and the standard deviation of FEPS are positively and highly correlated, which makes it very difficult to disentangle the relative contribution of the return predictability of each component. In this proposed project we first extend the Miller model to a setting in which whether the short-sale constraint is binding is asymmetric. More specifically, the short-sale constraint is binding only when most people want to sell (when they receive bad news), but not when most people want to buy (when they receive good news). Our preliminary model derives two testable implications: (i) future stock returns are positively related to the signal in the mean of FEPS and are negatively related to the standard deviation of FEPS; (ii) the return predictability of the mean and standard deviation of FEPS also depends on whether the signal is positive or negative. We will then empirically examine these two testable implications. Two methods will be used: (i) portfolio analysis and (ii) regression analysis. Hopefully, our empirical results will be consistent with our model predictions. Not only will we propose a simple model to justify the return predictability of forecast dispersion with meaningful economic intuition, but we will also hopefully provide empirical evidence to support the predictions of the model. 以前的研究（例如Diether，Malloy， Scherbina（2002 ，DMS））發現，分析師盈利預測的分散度 (亦即預測每股收益的平均值（FEPS）的標準偏差除以FEPS的絕對值）與未來的股票收益呈負相關。由於預測分散度被解釋為不同的意見，DMS解釋他們的結果與以風險為基礎的解釋不一致，但與行為金融學的解釋一致。亦即，在賣空的限制下，股票價格僅反映了樂觀投資者的估值（Miller (1977））。 然而，我們最近的研究發現，平均FEPS與未來的股票收益率成正相關。此外，我們的初步結果還表明，FEPS的標準偏差與未來股票收益率成負相關。FEPS的平均值對未來的股票收益率的可預測性比FEPS的標準差股更為明顯。所有這些結果表明，DMS對每股收益預測分散度對股價表現的可預測性的解釋可能是不完整的。 因此，重要的是了解每股收益預測分散度對股價表現的可預測性是否主要來自它的標準差或均值，這可以幫助我們了解其經濟的直覺和解釋。不幸的是，FEPS的均值和標準偏差是正面和高度相關的，這使得我們非常難解開每個成分對股價表現可預測性的相對影響。 在這個研究項目中，我們首先把Miller模型加以延伸。我們假設賣空約束是否具有約束力是不對稱的。更具體地說，只有當大多數人都希望出售（當他們收到壞消息）賣空約束是具有約束力的。但當大多數人都希望購買（當他們收到好消息）賣空約束是不具有約束力的。我們初步的模型得到兩個可以測試的檢定：（i）未來股價的表現與平均FEPS的信號呈正相關，但與FEPS的標準差呈負相關;（ii）FEPS均值和標準差對未來股價表現的可預測性還取決於信號是正或負。 然後，我們將實證檢驗這兩個可以測試的檢定。我們將用兩種方法：（i）投資組合分析，及（ii）回歸分析。我們希望，我們的實證結果與我們模型的預測是一致的。 我們不僅提出了一個簡單的模型來證明盈利預測分散度對未來股價表現的可預測性具有經濟意義與直覺的，同時我們也希望提供檢驗證據來支持該模型的預測。

644212.label: Realisation of objectives
644212.value: The major objectives of this project are to examine whether future stock returns are positively related to the change in the mean of forecast earnings per share (FEPS) and negatively related to the change in the standard deviation of FEPS and whether the return predictability of the changes in the mean and in the standard deviation of FEPS depends on the direction of the change in the mean of FEPS. We decompose the dispersion measure of Diether, Malloy, and Scherbina (2002) into changes in mean and changes in standard deviation of FEPS and find that find that changes in the standard deviations of forecasted earnings can work as a complementary disagreement measure that is comparable across stocks and immune from other return-predictive information contained in the scalars of dispersion measures. More interestingly, we find that the change-based disagreement measure is negatively associated with future returns significantly only when changes in the mean forecasts are negative.

644212.label: Major findings and research outcome
644212.value: This project has generated the following paper that has been accepted for publication at Management Science. The major findings are as follows: 1. Cen, Ling, K.C. John Wei, and Liyan Yang, 2015, “Disagreement, underreaction, and stock returns,” Management Science, forthcoming. We explore analysts’ earnings forecast data to improve upon one popular disagreement measure—the analyst forecast dispersion measure—proposed by Diether, Malloy, and Scherbina (2002). Our analysis suggests that changes in the standard deviations of forecasted earnings can work as a complementary disagreement measure that is comparable across stocks and immune from other return-predictive information contained in the normalization scalars of analyst forecast dispersion measures. We also document evidence that the change-based disagreement measure predicts future cross-sectional returns significantly only when changes in the mean forecasts are negative. This finding suggests that the interaction between disagreement and underreaction to earnings news affects asset prices.

644212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
644212.value: After several years of studies on the cross-sectional return predictability (including the current one) in the U.S. and the international markets, it seems that most of these so-called anomalies associated with the cross-sectional return predictability mainly only exist in the developed markets and not in the emerging markets. Now, Professor Feixue Xie, and I are currently working on a project that extends the current study to an international setting but focusing on the pervasiveness of the dispersion effect across countries and the cross-country determinants of the dispersion effect. Our initial finding shows that the dispersion effect is very pervasive and the dispersion effect can be largely explained by the national culture.

644212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
644212.value: In this paper, we find that, in general, changes in the standard deviations of forecasted earnings can work as a complementary disagreement measure that is comparable across stocks. This measure of disagreement can immune from other return-predictive information contained in the numerator of conventional dispersion measures. More importantly, the change-based disagreement measure predicts future cross-sectional returns significantly only when changes in the mean forecasts are negative. This finding suggests that the interaction between disagreement and underreaction to earnings news affects asset prices.

644312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644312.value: 人事管理的各樣主要決定，是建基於準確的表現評審的 (Murphy & Cleveland, 1995; Murphy, Carcia, Kerkar, Martin, & Balzer, 1982)。不準確的評審不單削弱組織的人力資源，亦會令員工感到不公平(Wong & Kwong, 2011)，從而在組織裡產生諸多不良後果 (e.g., Chen, Chen, & Xin, 2004; Li, Bingham & Umphress, 2007; Kim & Mauborgne, 1995; Wade, O’Reilly, & Pollock, 2006)。因此，理解為何及怎樣會有不準確評審是非常重要的；這個命題也成為了在表現審這一研究領域上的中心問題。(Cronbach, 1955; Landy & Farr, 1980; DeNisi, 1996; Murphy & Cleveland, 1995; Murphy, Cleveland, Skattebo, & Kinney, 2004; Wong & Kwong, 2005, 2007). 準確的表現評審由兩個元素組成。一個是評分準確度，另一個是區分準確度(Cronbach, 1955)。評分準確度是指評審的分數，或評審的平均分數，與真實表現的 “真實”分數，之間有多大的差距(Austin & Villanova, 1992; Smith & Kendall, 1963; Latham & Wexley, 1977)。區分準確度是指對一組被評者的評分區分，能多準確地反應他們表現的真正區分。不準確的評分區分，容易對員工造成不穩定，其至是相反的區分(Wong & Kwong, 2005)。 現存的理論及研究集中在評分準確度(e.g., Austin & Villanova, 1992; DeNisi, 1996; Smith & Kendall, 1963; Latham & Wexley, 1977; Lance et al., 1994; Murphy et al., 2004)。可是，雖然很多人事決策依賴準確的表現區分，但區分準確度的研究卻相對較少(Murphy & Cleveland, 1995; Wong & Kwong, 2005a).。 是項計劃，我們整合了兩個相關的理論，即幅度理論(range theory; Janiszewski & Cooke, 2003; Mellers & Cooke, 1994; Parducci, 1965)及參照與調整理論anchoring-and-adjustment perspective (Tversky & Kahneman, 1974; Wong & Kwong, 2000)，提出三組共六個實驗的研究，以了解評分的人如何在評分上區分不同表現。我們依從過往表現評審的研究(Wong & Kwong, 2005a)，把評審理解成判斷與決策的一種。這研究將會增加認識表現評審的心理機制，亦有助管理人員製定能提升評審準確度的有效方法。

644312.label: Realisation of objectives
644312.value: Objective 1. To examine the determinants of performance evaluation accuracy in terms of differential elevation The extent to this objective has been achieved: 100%. We found two sets of findings showing key determinants of evaluation accuracy in terms of differential elevation. These findings were reported in two papers. In the second paper (J2), entitled “Rating Order Determines Rating Differentiation”, we propose and test the notion that the inconsistent differentiation of ratings is a result of anchoring and adjustment. The idea is that raters use the dispersion of information from initial ratings as anchors for their internal differentiation scale. This action instantly leads raters to establish an internal scale, which, in turn, determines their rating differentiation. Accordingly, raters give more differentiated ratings when they start with less (vs. more) differentiated ratees. This prediction was supported by the results obtained from (a) a pilot study with ratings from the gymnastics in London 2012 Olympic Games, and (b) a main study with the initial performance dispersion of ratees being experimentally manipulated. This paper is now under review at Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes. In the first paper, entitled “Both Ends Count: A Range Theory Approach for Performance Evaluation" (J1), we examine range effects in performance evaluation in three studies, showing that the perceived difference in performance attributes between two ratees was greater when the attribute was presented in a narrow range than in a wide range context. This range effect led to preference reversals when people evaluate two ratees with tradeoffs between performance attributes. This pattern did not occur when global range information was presented. We draw upon range theory to offer a theoretical framework describing the range dependent nature in performance evaluation. This paper is now under review at Journal of Behavioral Decision Making. Objective 2. To make significant contribution to the performance evaluation literature by re-directing researchers’ attention to that a comprehensive understanding of performance evaluation requires both accuracy in terms of rating scores and rating differentiation. The extent to this objective has been achieved: 100%. The results from the multiple studies reported in the two papers clearly indicate that a comprehensive understanding of performance evaluation requires both accuracy in terms of rating scores and rating differentiation. Objective 3. To increase our knowledge on performance evaluation by demonstrating the utility of insights from judgment and decision making theories. The extent to this objective has been achieved: 100%. The findings reported two papers clearly show that two major theories from the judgment and decision area are very useful in increase our understanding of performance evaluation. The second paper (“Rating Order Determines Rating Differentiation”, J2) shows the usefulness of anchoring-and-adjustment (Tversky and Kahneman, 1974; Wong & Kwong, 2000) concept from judgment and decision making. The first paper ("Both Ends Count: A Range Theory Approach for Performance Evaluation", J1) shows the usefulness of range theory (Parducci, 1965) from judgment and decision making. Objective 4. To increase managers’ awareness of contextual factors that may alter their rating accuracy in performance evaluation. The extent to this objective has been achieved: 90%. We believe that one effective way to increase managers’ awareness of the implications of our findings is to send the messages via publicly accessible information. This objective has been largely achieved as all findings from this project were reported in international conferences and some were published in international journals. This objective has not yet been fully achieved because not all findings has been published. We expect that all the papers will ultimately be published in international journals in one-two years (depending on the lengths of review).

644312.label: Major findings and research outcome
644312.value: The major findings of this research were written in four papers. The first two papers summarized findings pertaining directly to performance evaluation. In the second paper, entitled “Rating Order Determines Rating Differentiation” (J2), we propose and test the notion that the inconsistent differentiation of ratings is a result of anchoring and adjustment. The idea is that raters use the dispersion of information from initial ratings as anchors for their internal differentiation scale. This action instantly leads raters to establish an internal scale, which, in turn, determines their rating differentiation. Accordingly, raters give more differentiated ratings when they start with less (vs. more) differentiated ratees. This prediction was supported by the results obtained from (a) a pilot study with ratings from the gymnastics in London 2012 Olympic Games, and (b) a main study with the initial performance dispersion of ratees being experimentally manipulated. This paper is now under review at Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes. In the fisrt paper, entitled “Both Ends Count: A Range Theory Approach for Performance Evaluation” (J1) we examine range effects in performance evaluation in three studies, showing that the perceived difference in performance attributes between two ratees was greater when the attribute was presented in a narrow range than in a wide range context. This range effect led to preference reversals when people evaluate two ratees with tradeoffs between performance attributes. This pattern did not occur when global range information was resented. We draw upon range theory to offer a theoretical framework describing the range dependent nature in performance evaluation. This paper is now under review at Journal of Behavioral Decision Making. In addition to these two papers, we extended our scope of investigation from focusing on performance evaluation per se to a more general issues about performance at both individual level and national level. This extension was primarily driven by a PhD student's research interest. Because this extension and the original plan were both related to performance and performance measures, we allowed the student to pursue this extension. This extension turned out to be very successful, resulting in multiple conference presentations and two publications in international journals (Feldman, Wong, & Baumeister, 2016; Feldman, Chandrashek, & Wong, 2016)

644312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
644312.value: Because research on performance evaluation has long focused on score accuracy but not on differentiation accuracy, we believe that our research will have very big potential by direction the entire field of performance evaluation research to this new line of direction.

644312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
644312.value: Rating (in)accuracy in employee/subordinate performance evaluation has been the key issue in human resource management both for researchers and practitioners. This issue is so important because not only major human resource decisions (e.g., selection, hiring, promotion, layoff, etc.) relies on the outcome of employee performance evaluation, but also inappropriate ratings in performance evaluation leads employees to feel injustice and so a wide variety of negative consequences to organizations. This research aims to increase our theoretical understanding of performance evaluation in terms of differentiation accuracy. In the first set of our research, we found that raters give more differentiated ratings when they start with less (vs. more) differentiated ratees. In the second set, we found that the rating difference in performance attributes between two ratees was greater when the attribute was presented in a narrow range than in a wide range context. These findings are generally consistent with the insights from judgment and decision making research, indicating that the psychological mechanisms underlying performance evaluation include anchoring-and-adjustment (the first set) and range calibration (the second set).

644412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644412.value: Using seven decennial census data (1950 to 2010) from the Integrated Public Use Microdata Series and the soon-to-be-released 2010 PUMS data, the proposed study systematically investigates the transformations in the social division of labor in one of the most developed capitalist economies—the American occupational structure. Our analyses will be based on 1950, 1990, and 2010 census classification schemes as “standards” to compare and decipher the extent of changes over time. The adoption of multiple standards is necessary because of periodical changes in the classification scheme. In addition, the study will develop several sets of “pure” socioeconomic score (SEI) from the partial association models as optimal scaling tools to generate different sets of SEI scores. The utility of the proposed method is then demonstrated through a re-analysis of Duncan’s original 45 occupations in the 1950 census, which is invaluable and informative. As expected, Duncan SEI, but not occupational prestige, has high correlations with our preferred “pure” measures. On the other hand, Duncan SEI behaves rather poorly among those occupations with low prestige or social standing. The proposed method is novel and superior in several important ways. First, instead of using arbitrary dichotomies of education (less than HS versus HS+) and earnings (less than US$3,500 versus US$3,500+), researchers can calibrate occupations with more refined categories to address changes in the distributions of earnings and education over time. Second, since the newly constructed scores are parameter estimates derived from statistical models, researchers can obtain standard errors to bound individual status scores and test whether certain occupational categories share similar relative positions. Finally, there is no a priori assumption of invariance in the underlying ratings and this important property permits us to study changes over time that has plagued previous measures. Based on the constructed SEI scores from two different classification schemes, we propose to compare and identify whether there is any rise or fall of individual occupational categories, as would be predicted by changes in the demand and supply structure. The study will also examine whether such changes are related to changing composition of its incumbents, particularly in relation to gender and ethnic compositions. Findings from the study can also provide better evidence whether the Treiman constant indeed exists in the American case. Finally, a useful product is the provision of census-specific socioeconomic status scores so that future researchers can compare, choose, and adopt appropriate measures in their own research. 本研究建議利用美國在過去六十年（1950年至2010年）每十年一度的人口普查數據來研究美國職業的結構變遷。作為一個最發達的資本主義經濟體，了解美國社會分工的轉型會對研究社會分層有重大啟示。分析會根據1950年，1990年和2010年的職業分類作“標準”，比較和解讀不同職業相對位置因隨時間的變更。由於職業分類經常有週期性的變化，採用多重標準作分析是必要的。此外，本研究利用關聯模型(association models)作最佳的量度工具，開發多套“純粹”的社會經濟地位指數（socioeconomic status index）。本建議重新分析鄧肯 (Duncan) 45個職業在1950年的人口普查數據，結果如期所料，我們首選的“純粹”社會經濟地位指數和鄧肯的社會經濟地位指數具較高的相關性，但與職業聲望 (occupational prestige) 的關連卻不大，此外鄧肯的社會經濟地位指數會因不同職業聲望職業的高低而有所偏差，故此分析肯定了利用關聯模型作為研究的可行性。 本研究提供幾個重要突破和卓越領域。首先，研究不是使用隨意的二分法來處理教育（低於高中與高中或以上）和收入（少超過美元3,500與美元3,500或以上），而是採用更精細的分類來處理教育和收入因隨時間而轉變的分佈作適當調整。其次，由於新建成的指數是來自統計模型的估計參數，故提供了標準誤差，從而可以比較和測試不同職業類別是否具有相同的相對位置。最後，在沒有一個先驗假設社會經濟地位不變的條件下，本研究能夠分析及判斷社會經濟地位指數是否真的永恆不變，這是一個一直困擾社會分層研究多年的重要議題。 我們將使用不同的社會經濟地位指數作比較，了解不同職業類別的上升或下降是否與需求和供應的結構變遷有關連。此外，我們也將研究這變遷是否和職業組成的結構改變有關，特別是在性別和種族成分上。研究結果還可提供更好的證據，查核特雷曼常數 (Treiman constant) 是否確存。最後，本研究能提供一系列不同年分的社會經濟地位指數，作研究人員參考和選擇。

644912.label: Project Objectives
644912.value: In the first stage, the methodology of inferring peso event probability from options prices will be developed, refined, and tested on simulated data. 644912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
644912.value: This project proposes a methodology to use options prices to estimate the statistical distributions of the value of the underlying asset, with an eye towards inferring the actual probability of the so-called peso event. A peso event here means an extremely low value of the underlying asset on a future date, which is perceived by market traders as a possible event, but has either never happened in history, or at least not in recent history. A potential peso event, also known as the peso problem, has been proposed by some financial economists as an explanation of some long standing puzzles in finance, such as the equity premium puzzle and the forward premium puzzle. Verifying empirically that these puzzles can indeed be explained by the peso problem is a difficult task, however, as peso events, by definition, are either not observed at all, or inadequately represented in the actual sample of data. As a result, most work along this line remains a theoretical possibility and the effect of the peso problem is illustrated with simulated data. Recently, a study by some researchers proposed to use prices of options written on exchange rates to infer the traders' perception of the peso event in the currency market. This project proposes an alternative methodology of utilizing options prices to infer the perceived peso event and, in addition, to estimate the peso event probability. The proposed methodology will be implemented and evaluated with actual data of the returns on stocks and currencies. The result of this project can fill the void of a very important literature and enhance our understanding of many long standing puzzles. 本文提出一个用期权价格来估计资产的未来价值的统计分布的方法，并用于推算所谓比索事件的概率。 比索事件是指价值大贬值的小概率事件。 这样的事件被市场当时认为是有可能的，但事后却没有发生，或很少发生。 比索事件（也叫比索问题）被一些金融经济学家用来解释金融中的一些长期得不到解决的难题， 例如股权溢率难题和远期溢率难题. 但是验证这样的解释很困难。原因就在比索事件在数据样本中从未出现，或很 少出现。在已有文献中大部分讨论停留在理论的可能性和模拟数据的结果。 最近，有学者提出用汇率期权价格来估计外汇市场交易者心目中比索事件概率的方法。 本文提出另一个用期权价格来推算比索事件概率的方法。 这一方法将用于股票价格和汇率的数据上。本文的结果可以填补这一重要文献的空白，并提高我们对许多长期未解决的难题的理解。

644912.label: Realisation of objectives
644912.value: The first objective is fully achieved. We (the Ph.D student as a coauthor and I) developed both non-parametric and parametric approaches to inferring peso event probabilities from options prices. We tested the approaches on simulated data and confirmed their good performance. The second objective is also achieved. We applied the two approaches to the data of S&P 500 index on which options are frequently traded. We confirmed that there is a peso problem and the measure of peso problem is time-varying with a strong business-cycle interpretation. This makes contribution towards understanding of the equity premium puzzle. We also applied the two approaches to the forward premium puzzle. Although we find similar phenomenon as in the S&P 500 index, these events are not extreme to be called peso problems, because foreign exchange options up to date typically do not cover a wide range of strike prices. Therefore, the paper we wrote is based on the result on S&P 500 index options only.

644912.label: Major findings and research outcome
644912.value: The results show that the actual distributions of the return on S&P 500 index implied from index options through various pricing kernels are more left-skewed than the actual empirical distribution. This confirms the existence of the peso problem. The measure of peso problem is time-varying with a strong business-cycle interpretation. Using the implied actual distribution, the high, observed risk premium can be justified using standard utility functions with generally accepted risk aversion parameters. The work makes contribution towards the resolution of the equity premium puzzle. A paper based on US S&P 500 index options data has been drafted (coauthored with a Ph.D student).

644912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
644912.value: The potential of the methodology we developed in this project lies in its use in markets other than S&P 500 index. As options markets develop and traders become willing to trade on more extreme events, the information contained in the options prices can reveal traders' expectation. Asset pricing research has been hindered by unobservability of investors' expectations. The use of information contained in options prices can potentially overcome such a problem as options market develop.

644912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
644912.value: In the US where a long history financial data are available, a puzzle has been observed regarding the average equity returns. The puzzle is that the average return seem to be too high given that the risk represented by the covariation between equity return and consumption growth is not that high. A potential explanation is that there is a so-called peso problem in which investors fear some bad things may happen, but they did not happen as much. Various research have shown that if the peso problem existed, then the puzzle can be explained. No research, however, has shown that the peso problem actually exists, as expectations of investors are not directly observed. Using information contained in options prices, we show that peso problems indeed exist. The peso problem measure we construct changes over time, peaking after a long run of good times and dropping substantially after market crashes.

645112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645112.value: 电视是重要的广告媒体之一。它占全美广告支出的四分之一。到2008年为止，广告是电视产业中最主要的收入来源，占总收入的50%。电视广告时段通常通过拍卖的方式卖给广告商。对广告商来说，电视广告通常是持续不断而不是一次性的。因而广告商通常会多次参加同类广告时段在不同时期的拍卖。 随着拍卖这种销售形式在近些年的越来越流行，关于参与拍卖人员的行为的研究也越来越多。但是由于数据缺乏，关于电视广告时段拍卖方面的实证研究却很少。这个研究项目的目的就是通过数据来实证研究广告商在电视广告时段拍卖中的投标行为，以及他们对给定时段所愿意支付的最高价。广告商对给定电视广告时段所愿意支付的最高价很大程度上取决于该广告时段的观众群的大小。而这个时段的观众群的大小在拍卖进行的时候广告商是不知道的。广告商通常会对类似电视广告时段随时间推进做重复购买，因而广告商有可能会随着时间对类似广告时段的价值有个学习的过程。因此，在这个研究项目中，我们会把广告商行为中的这个动态过程包括到我们的模型中去。这个研究的结果将对电视台的拍卖机制涉设计，以及如何制定电视广告的促销策略有重要的指导意义

645112.label: Realisation of objectives
645112.value: The above listed objectives of the project have been met at the completion of the project. We built an empirical model to study advertiser's willingness to pay in the auction for TV commercial breaks. In the model we include bidders' characteristics such as their total budget and past bidding history, competition in the market and the characteristics of the commercial break. The models were estimated using a large data set that covers the bidding history as well as the TV viewing history of individual viewers over the period of one year. We find that the bidder's willingness to pay is highly correlated to the TVR of the program. The willingness to pay for TV commercial break also varies across the product categories that the advertiser belongs to. For example, we find that advertisers of food and clothing have lower willingness to pay compared to advertisers from other categories such as financial and banking products. Experienced bidders have lower willingness to pay. To further examine whether the current price menu provided by the TV station for the commercial break is efficient or not, we carried our another study to investigate the TV advertisement zapping behavior of the viewers. Empirical models that includes the characteristics of viewers, TV advertisement, TV program and other control variables such as time of the day and day of the week were developed and tested using the same data set. Estimation results suggest that variables such as the position of the advertisement in the commercial break, viewing history of the program before the commercial break and the past history of being exposed to the same advertisement plays important roles in affecting viewers' zapping behavior. Based on the above model estimation results, we ran simulation studies to test the impact of different pricing scheme on advertisers' revenue hence the efficiency of advertisement spending. Insights on advertisers' pricing strategies were generated.

645112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645112.value: The project aims to understand firms' pricing strategy for the TV commercial slots by looking at both the current strategies adopted by the advertisers when they are bidding for the commercial slots and the actual viewing behavior of the advertisement by the viewers as what eventually matters for the advertisers is the actual number of the viewers of the advertisement rather than that for the TV program. Problem of inefficiency will occur if the size of the viewers of the advertisement deviates from that of the TV program. Models that accounts for the advertiser's willingness to pay for commercial slots as well as viewer's viewing behavior of the commercial break were developed and tested using a large data set from a local TV station that includes the bidding history of advertisers and TV viewing history for the viewers for a period of one year. 645212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
645212.value: 具有非稳定供应商的企业产品定价与购货渠道分散化问题

645212.label: Project Objectives
645212.value: To obtain optimal joint pricing and inventory replenishment strategies for a multiple sourcing firm that faces a risk of supply disruptions and price-sensitive random demands, and to derive conditions under which the optimal policies are simple and could easily be implemented. To study the impact of source diversification on the firm’s profit, its market share, and the price it should charge to its customers. This will provide general justification and important managerial insight for industry source diversification practices. To quantify the impacts of supplier reliability on a firm's profit, its replenishment strategy, and the prices it should charge to its customers. These will provide insight about how a firm should select its suppliers, and will also help to characterize the incentive for the suppliers to improve their reliability.

645212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645212.value: It is quite common for firms to have suppliers that are exposed to some risk of disruption due to natural disasters, accidents, strikes or other events. When facing such suppliers, it is important for a firm to have appropriate mitigation strategies. Two such possible strategies are source diversification and dynamic pricing: the former helps to hedge against the disruption risk of an individual supplier, while the latter could be used to manage the demand flow and realize a higher profit margin with limited stock when suffering a shortage. In this project we will study a firm's joint optimization problem of dynamic pricing and inventory replenishment from multiple unreliable suppliers. Specifically, we will analyze the following single-item, periodic-review inventory model: demands in consecutive periods are independent random variables with a price-sensitive distribution; unsatisfied demand is backlogged; the firm has multiple unreliable suppliers which may or may not be able to deliver each order, and the delivery capability of each supplier is assumed to be Markovian in consecutive periods. We aim at deriving the optimal dynamic policy that simultaneously determines the replenishment quantities and the price in each period over a finite horizon, and exploring conditions under which the optimal policies have simple structures. We will further study the impact of source diversification on the firm and its customers, particularly the impact on the firm's market share, the selling pricing, as well as the firm's profit, and will also investigate the operational and economic effects of supplier reliability. The contribution of this project is in two-fold: it will generate useful insight and efficient strategies to help firms manage supply disruption risks, which is of practical importance in supply chain management; it will also contribute to the literature on supply chains management by proposing a new model that coordinates pricing and source diversification, which is theoretically significant. 由于自然灾害﹑事故﹑工人罢工等等原因，各厂家常常面临不同程度的供应中断风险。当面临这些风险时，厂家必须准备适当的应对策略。分散采购和动态定价是两种可能的策略：前者可降低个别供应商中断供货时的冲击，后者可在供应有限的情况下有效管理需求和取得边际利润最大化。本课题将研究厂家在面对多个具有中断风险的供应商时如何进行动态定价与存货管理。

645212.label: Realisation of objectives
645212.value: We have fully realized all objectives as per original application. Specifically, we studied a the joint pricing and inventory control problem for a firm that has a quick-response supplier and a regular supplier that both suffer random disruptions, and faces price-sensitive random demands. We characterize the optimal ordering and pricing policies in each period over a planning horizon, and analyzing the impacts of supply source diversification and supplier reliability. We show that, when both suppliers are unreliable, the optimal inventory policy in each period is a reorder point policy and the optimal price is decreasing in the starting inventory level of the period; For the special case where the quick-response supplier is perfectly reliable, we further show that the optimal inventory policy is of a base-stock type and the optimal pricing policy is a list-price policy with markdowns. In addition, we show that having supply source diversification or higher supplier reliability increases the firm's optimal profit and lowers the optimal selling price, which benefits both the firm and the customers. We also demonstrate that, with the selling price as a decision, a supplier may receive even more orders from the firm after an additional supplier is introduced.

645212.label: Major findings and research outcome
645212.value: We studied the joint pricing and inventory replenishment problem for a firm that has dual suppliers and faces price-sensitive random demands. One of the suppliers is a quick-response supplier that can deliver an order from the firm in the period the order is placed, or in zero leadtime; the other is a regular supplier with a leadtime modeled as one period when disruption is not encountered. We aimed at characterizing the optimal policies that simultaneously determine the optimal ordering and pricing decisions in each period over a planning horizon, and studying the impacts of supply source diversification and supplier reliability on the firm's optimal profit, its optimal operational policies, its customers, and its suppliers. When the quick-response supplier is perfectly reliable, we showed that the optimal replenishment policy is of a base-stock type and the optimal pricing policy is a list-price policy with markdowns; for the general case where both suppliers are unreliable, we showed that the optimal replenishment policy is of a threshold type and the optimal price in each period is a decreasing function of the initial inventory of the period. In addition, we showed that having supply source diversification or higher supplier reliability increases the firm's optimal profit and lowers the optimal selling price; hence it benefits both the firm and its customers. We also demonstrated that, if the selling price is exogenously given, a supplier is always worse off when an additional supplier is introduced; however, it could be better off when the selling price is also a decision. The research outcome has been reported in two papers: (1) “Dynamic Pricing and Inventory Management with Dual Suppliers of Different Leadtimes and Disruption Risks”, Production and Operations Management, 23(2014), 2058-2074; and (2) “Optimal Pricing and Inventory Policies with One Reliable and One Unreliable Suppliers: Characterization and Comparison”, Annals of Operations Research, 241(2016), 35-51.

645212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645212.value: Some possible extensions to our model include: (a) currently we assume that the ordering leadtime is either 1 or 0. For more general leadtimes, the state space has to be expanded to include pipeline inventory, and the optimization problem becomes high dimensional. A possible solution to the problem will be to develop effective heuristics; (b) noting that disruptions in suppliers may also be correlated, we may consider extending our model to include the case of dependent suppliers.

645212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645212.value: It is quite common for firms to have suppliers that are exposed to some risk of disruption due to natural disasters, accidents, strikes or other events. It is thus important for a firm to have appropriate mitigation strategies. Two such possible strategies are source diversification and dynamic pricing: the former helps to hedge against the disruption risk of an individual supplier, while the latter could be used to manage the demand flow and realize a higher profit margin with limited stock when suffering a shortage. In this project we studied a firm's joint optimization problem of dynamic pricing and inventory replenishment from multiple unreliable suppliers. We derived an optimal dynamic policy that simultaneously determines the replenishment quantities and the price in each period for a two-supplier problem. We further studied the impact of source diversification on the firm and its customers. The contributions are in two-fold: we generated useful insights and efficient strategies to help firms manage supply disruption risks, which is of practical importance in supply chain management; we also contributed to the literature on supply chain management by proposing a new model that coordinates pricing and source diversification, which is theoretically significant.

645812.label: Project Title(Chinese)
645812.value: 条件性资助对师范生质量的影响

645812.label: Project Objectives
645812.value: To evaluate the effects of the conditional grant programs for college students on the teaching track on the quality of incoming teacher trainees. To assess the current sitation in an economic framework and explore the possible channels through which the effects are generated. To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of such programs.

To assess the current sitation in an economic framework and explore the possible channels through which the effects are generated.
To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of such programs.

645812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
645812.value: Teacher quality has generally been believed to be a key factor for improving students' learning outcomes (see a survey by Hanushek and Rivkin, 2006). Yet policies aiming at improving teacher quality often fail to deliver the expected outcomes when other forces are at play. Low-income and disadvantaged areas often lose their potential pool of good teachers to other economically advanced areas; even in areas where the private sector has fast development, the teaching profession sometimes suffers from "a brain drain," i.e., high-quality teachers are driven out of this profession by attractive outside options (Lakdawalla, 2006; Bacolod, 2007). A new direction of public policies is to provide conditional grants for trainees in teacher colleges and commit them to working in disadvantaged regions. Among other countries, the Chinese Ministry of Education announced a huge conditional grant program for the six top national teacher colleges in 2007, which waives all tuitions and fees of students in teaching majors but requires them to teach in their home province for ten years upon graduation. Provincial governments also followed suit and adopted similar practices for provincial-level teacher colleges later on. Despite much policy interest, the effect of such programs is theoretically ambiguous and empirically unexplored. We propose to evaluate the conditional grant programs initiated by both national and provincial level governments; in particular we will focus on the program effect on the quality of incoming trainees. We will develop a conceptual framework to illustrate the channels through which the possible effect is generated and use it to guide our empirical analysis. Next we plan to collect the average and maximal College Entrance Examinations (CEE) scores of students from each province for each major in all national and provincial level teacher colleges from 2005 to 2011. We will first focus on the program colleges and employ the difference-in-differences (DID) approach to examine the change of average score for those majoring in teaching compared to that for those majoring in other areas in these colleges. To eliminate the confounding effect of the major-specific time varying factors, we will further make use of non-program teacher colleges as an additional comparison group and apply the difference-in-difference-in-difference (DDD) approach to isolate the program effect on the scores of incoming students majoring in teaching. Lastly a cost-and-benefit analysis will be conducted to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of the conditional grant programs.

645812.label: Realisation of objectives
645812.value: We have achieved all the objectives as per original application. First, we have evaluated the effect of conditional grant programs on the quality of incoming trainees. We find that such programs did attract high-quality trainees in the short run but this effect weakened in the longer term. Second, we construct a conceptual framework to explain the effects and the channels through which the effects arise. We further test for the channels by conducting heterogeneity analysis. Finally, based on our estimates, we evaluate the cost effectiveness of this program. We find that the program is cost-effective in improving the teachers’ quality if the teacher trainees did become teachers in remote areas. However, we also spot anecdotal evidence that a considerable number of students tend to default. Our calibration shows that such programs would be not be cost effective if the default rate is above certain threshold. We have collected the default rates for each program school to conduct a more thorough evaluation of such programs could be fulfilled. Compared to other similar programs, the program we examined is cost effective for the central region during the period we have examined. However, given that the program effect weakens in the long run, it is not clear whether the effect will be sustainable. Moreover, as the program turned high-performing students from low-income regions, the cost effectiveness for low-income regions is in doubt.

645812.label: Major findings and research outcome
645812.value: First, we find that the conditional grant program increased the overall CET scores of incoming students in teaching majors in program schools relative to other majors. Second, we find that the program effects are heterogenous across regions. While the program increased the CET scores of incoming students from high- and middle-income regions, it turned away high-performing students from low-income regions. Third, we extend our data period to explore the effect in a longer term. We find that the program effect tends to be weaker in a longer term. Fourth, we find evidence that a considerable number of program receivers tend to default after graduation, which casts doubt on the effectiveness of such programs, particularly in the longer term.

645812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
645812.value: This research can be further developed. For instance, we are collecting systematic data on the default behavior of program receivers. In addition, we have compiled detailed admission data for the first- and second-tier colleges in China. This data set can potentially be used to conduct a variety of studies. For example, this data set can be used to evaluate other policy experiments in college admission, e.g., the recruitment of students who commit to providing military services. we are exploring the efficiency implications of different admission mechanisms using this data set.

645812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
645812.value: One recent policy direction to improve teacher quality in remote or disadvantaged areas is to provide conditional grants to teacher trainees in teacher colleges and commit them to working in disadvantaged areas after graduation. Yet little is known about whether such policies can attract better trainees or not. We evaluate a conditional grant program for teaching majors in Chinese normal universities. From 2007 onwards, students who were enrolled in the teaching majors in six major normal universities are eligible for a tuition waiver and decent monthly stipend for four years. In return, they must teach in their hometown provinces after graduation for ten years. We first compare changes in the College Entrance Tests (CET) scores of incoming students in the teaching majors with those for regular majors in those six normal universities and in other universities. We find that the conditional grant program increased the overall CET scores of incoming students in teaching majors in program schools relative to other majors. However, much of the effect arises from students from the high- and middle-income regions whereas students from low-income regions tend to turn away from teaching majors. Our result suggests that the across-the-board policy has failed to achieve its intended goal of improving teacher quality particularly in disadvantaged areas.

646112.label: Project Title(Chinese)
646112.value: 跨国公司与技术扩散：来自台湾企业及其大陆子公司的实证分析

646112.label: Project Objectives
646112.value: We aim at building a unique database by linking the parent firms from Taiwan to their affiliated firms in mainland China, and connecting together the production, trade, as well as research and development activities on both sides. This unique database will be useful in many research topics regarding multinational companies and facilitate our investigation in multinational enterprises. We seek to understand how offshore R&D or other technology related activity affects affiliates’ imports of intermediates. We will focus on the role of offshore R&D, which is an increasingly important phenomenon in China in recent years. With data on both parents’ and affiliates’ R&D as well as product-level data on imports by affiliates, we are able to address the impact on both extensive and intensive margins. We aim at examining the impacts of parents’ and affiliates’ R&D or other technology related activities on affiliates’ export variety. Product turnover is a widespread phenomenon, and it is important to understand what determines a firm’s ability to develop new product varieties. In our project, we will focus on technology-based explanations and international market to identify the linkage between parents’ knowledge intensity and affiliates’ export variety. We are also interested in examining the change in affiliates’ export quality due to technology diffusion. Product quality is an important issue in international trade. In this project, we will examine if offshore R&D or parents’ R&D or other linkages between parents and affiliates improves China’s export quality (measured by unit value as well as the relative position of average unit value of the affiliates’ export as compared to all Chinese exporters for the same good).

646112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
646112.value: This project sets out to investigate technology diffusion from multinational parent firms to their foreign affiliates (affiliated firms and subsidiaries). We will focus on identifying the channels of technology diffusion and the impacts on affiliates’ imports, exports, and product quality. To achieve this goal, we are constructing a unique database that contains measures of technology and performance for both the parent firms and foreign affiliates. We will then investigate theoretically and empirically the sources and impacts of technology diffusion via multinational activities. An important advantage of this project is that we will investigate technology diffusion in two different forms: embodied diffusion through trade in goods and disembodied diffusion through multinational production and offshore (affiliated) R&D. The importance of this study is threefold. First, technology diffusion plays a key role in determining productivity at both the micro and aggregate level. Second, multinational firms are among the most important technology innovators in the world as they account for a large part of global R&D spending. Third, combining the information of multinational parents and their affiliates provides a good lens through which to scrutinize technology diffusion, because multinational firms serve as a natural starting point for examining the diffusion of technology (Keller, 2009). Usually multinational parents enjoy technological superiority and they transfer technology to their affiliates abroad to exploit lower production costs so as to enhance profits. While the pioneering works by Keller and Yeaple (2010) and Brambilla (2009) have laid an excellent foundation for such studies, micro-level research on technology diffusion via multinational activities remains scarce – the R&D sharing within multinationals has not yet been fully explored and the impact of technology diffusion on affiliate performance is still not well understood. To address these important issues, we have started to construct a unique database that includes detailed information on Taiwanese parent firms and their affiliates in mainland China. Linking parent-firm R&D with R&D and international trade activities of foreign affiliates allows us to address novel aspects of technology diffusion via multinational activities including: (1) imported intermediates, (2) export variety, and (3) export quality. We will emphasize on how offshore R&D affects technology diffusion and export performance of affiliates (measured by export varieties and quality). To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first micro-level study of these research questions. Findings of this project can be potentially of interest to both the academic community and policy makers. 本项目旨在研究从跨国公司母公司到其海外子公司的技术转移（或“技术扩散”，在本文中二者通用），其海外子公司泛指其关联企业或下属分公司。我们关注的重点是技术转移的渠道与其对跨国公司子公司进口、出口和产品质量的影响。为此，我们正在构建一个独一无二的数据库，其中包含来自台湾地区的跨国公司母公司与其在大陆的子公司的技术活动与公司绩效方面的相关数据。基于这个数据库，我们将通过研究跨国公司的相关活动来探讨技术转移的来源及其影响。本项目的一个重要优势在于我们将研究两种不同类型的技术转移：一类是通过产品贸易实现的“内涵式”技术转移（即技术转移直接体现于产品内涵中）；另一类是通过跨国公司的多国制造与离岸研发（或称“关联研发”）实现的“非内涵式”技术转移。 本研究的重要性体现在如下三点。首先，技术扩散在宏微观层面生产率的决定中扮演着重要角色。其次，跨国公司在技术扩散中发挥重要作用，通常来说跨国公司在全球研发支出中占据了很大比例，因而成为全球最重要的技术创新主体中的代表。第三，结合跨国公司母公司及其子公司的信息为我们提供了研究技术转移的良好视角，因为跨国公司在文献中被认为是研究技术扩散的一个天然的起点（Keller，2009）。跨国公司的母公司享有技术上的优越地位，他们通常会转移一定技术给其海外子公司以便更大程度的利用当地的低制造成本的优势从而实现利润最大化。尽管这一领域内的研究前沿，例如Keller和Yeaple 2010年的论文与Brambilla 2009年的论文已经为本领域的相关研究奠定了坚实的基础，但是微观企业层面的关于技术扩散如何通过跨国公司活动而实现的研究仍非常稀缺，特别是跨国公司内部研发活动如何在母公司与子公司之间进行分配的问题以及技术扩散对跨国公司子公司活动的影响尚未得到充分的探讨，仍有待进一步的研究。 为研究上述重要议题，我们已开始构建一个关联了台湾跨国公司母公司及其在中国大陆子公司、包含双方详细信息的独具特色的数据库。通过把母公司的研发活动与其子公司的研发、生产、及贸易行为相关联，我们将得以考察技术转移影响的新方面，包括对子公司进口的中间产品的选择、出口产品的数量和品种、以及出口产品质量的多方面的影响。我们将着重强调离岸研发这一新趋势对技术扩散格局与跨国公司子公司出口行为的影响。据我们所知，本课题是世界上首度用微观层面数据回答上述学术问题的研究之一。本课题的研究成果将对学术界和企业相关政策制定方面做出重要贡献。

646112.label: Realisation of objectives
646112.value: Objective (1): We aim at building a unique database by linking the parent firms from Taiwan to their affiliated firms in mainland China. Realization: We fully realized this objective by linking the parent firms from Taiwan and their affiliates in mainland China between the period 2000-2006. This is an ambitious project since we are the first to build such detailed linkage data that combines both parent companies from Taiwan and affiliated firms in mainland China, given the importance of intra-firm trade and MNEs in the global economy and the interesting similarities between the two sides: Taiwan and mainland China. This unique database will be useful in many research topics regarding multinational companies and facilitate our investigation in multinational enterprises. The most time-consuming part and the biggest challenge lies in how to better link such data. The progress took much longer than we expected. There are several reasons for why it took longer than expected to conduct the data matching process. First, parents and affiliates must be matched by names only. There are no common numerical firm identifications we can use. There are firms with similar names, different expressions, and mergers and acquisitions of firms. In many cases we must rely on manual matching. Even with manual matching, in some cases, we are not sure whether the firms are affiliates. In such cases, we conduct several different matching methods and listed results based on “conservative matching” and “liberal matching”. Second, the data matching involves not only the matching between parent firms from Taiwan exchange market and the above-scale manufacturing firms in the National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBSC), but also the matching between parents and firms in China’s Customs, and between parents and firms in both NBSC and Customs. This creates the challenge when we move from import side to export side analysis. The difficulties magnify when we try to extend the sample period beyond 2006. This is also related to the progress achieved in the following objectives which may make some objectives were not fully achieved, and the PI will describe in more detail later. Objective (2): We seek to understand how offshore R&D or other technology-related activity affects affiliates’ imports of intermediates. Realization: We fully achieved this objective by studying the parents’ R&D and affiliates’ R&D activities and their impact on affiliates imports. We also address the role of trade regimes (processing, ordinary and hybrid exports) in these relations. The findings are summarized in Item 6.1 “Major findings and Research outcome”. Objective (3): We aim at examining the impacts of parents’ and affiliates’ R&D or other technology-related activities on affiliates’ export variety. Realization: We fully achieved this objective by linking the parents’ and affiliates’ R&D activities and affiliates’ trading behavior under different trading regimes such as ordinary trade, processing trade, and hybrid trade. We not only analyzed export variety but also import variety, i.e., the varieties that have been imported by affiliates and how this is affected by parents’ R&D. When conducting the analysis on imported variety, we rely on the matched data between the Taiwanese parents and the NBSC data for affiliated firms. That is to say, those affiliates are large firms, who are above a certain scale. When we move from import to export, we encountered more problems because we want to match parents directly to Customs export data that includes all exporting firms, regardless of firm size. In other words, during the matching with the whole Customs data, the name matching issue occurred more often which requires the substantially increased amount of time on manual matching and the checking of the matching results. Furthermore, when we try to extend the sample to the year after 2006, the newly purchased customs data does not contain “ordinary trade” information, but only record the “processing trade”. Thus, we cannot differentiate the hybrid firms and pure ordinary trade firms. This also created the obstacle for the analysis on export variety. Although there is difficulty, we have obtained some meaningful results and fully achieved this objective. In future we plan to further extend our analysis on extensive margin and conduct more thorough analysis using updated sample based on the new sample of finalized matched database using the whole customs data (preferably beyond 2006 if ordinary trade data become available) instead of using the NBSC above-scale firm survey data. Another difficulty of extending the sample is due to the low data quality of the NBSC data since 2007. For example, there is no complete R&D data on affiliated firms in the NBSC data after 2007. Objective (4): We are also interested in examining the change in export quality due to technology diffusion. Realization: We fully achieved this objective by studying the adjustment of export quality of Chinese firms through the channel of imported intermediate inputs that is one of the most important channels of technology diffusion (embodied technology through imports). We show both the quality upgrading along the export side and import side of Chinese firms, and the affiliated firms of Taiwanese parents are a subset of them. We also studied the differential effect between affiliates’ and parents’ R&D on affiliates’ export unit value price. The PI has published several papers about product quality which has been directly benefited from this project.

646112.label: Major findings and research outcome
646112.value: First, we develop a unique data created by linking Taiwanese parent firms that are listed on Taiwan Stock Exchange to detailed firm-level data and customs transactions of their affiliates in China from 2000 to 2006. The dataset and its matching process/methodology are described in our working papers “Multinational R&D, Import Intensity, and Price” (see Part C, Item 8.7) and “Multinational Technology Linkage: An Empirical Study of Taiwanese Parent Firms and Their Affiliates in China” (see Part C, Item 8.8). Second, we conducted the thorough empirical analysis regarding the relationship between affiliates’ and parents’ R&D activities and their impact on affiliates’ trade. We also address the role of trade regimes (processing, ordinary and hybrid exports) in these relations. Our findings suggest that the share of imported intermediate inputs in affiliate total inputs is larger for processing and hybrid exporters as compared to ordinary exporters. We also empirically assess the influence of affiliate and parent R&D on the relation between tariff and import intensity at the firm and product level. Our empirical results suggest that tariff concessions increase import intensity and this effect is augmented by affiliate R&D intensity while mitigated by parent R&D intensity. These results imply a complementary relation between affiliate R&D and imported inputs and a substitutive relation between parent R&D and imported inputs. As imported inputs may contain foreign technology that is difficult to be transmitted to affiliates and affiliate R&D can be a channel of direct technology transfer, our results indicate that parent and affiliate R&D may have different functions that will affect the relationship with imported inputs. In addition, we find that the impact of parent R&D is mainly on ordinary imports while the influence of affiliate R&D is on both ordinary and processing imports. We also find that affiliates’ R&D significantly help improve affiliates' export quality upgrading under trade liberalization while contracting export variety. (See Part C, Item 8.7 and Item 8.8; Item 9.1-9.4). Third, the PI has conducted a series of research regarding how the adjustment of export quality of Chinese firms is affected by imported intermediate inputs that is one of the most important channels of technology diffusion (embodied technology through imports). The studies by the PI have analyzed both the quality upgrading along the export side and import side and the mechanisms. See Part C, Item 8.1-8.6 for research outcomes related to quality upgrading and competitiveness of Chinese firms.

646112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
646112.value: We are in the process of further improving the current working papers according to feedback we have obtained and we will submit the research outcomes (see Part C, item 8.7-8.8) to top journals. We are also in the process of improving the matching with the whole customs data beyond the current sample period and expect to work more firm-product level results based on the updated sample for further analysis. In the near future, we plan to use this data set to analyze more questions. For example, we plan to differentiate imported intermediate inputs by their category and by countries of origin. The literature suggest that imports from OECD countries have a larger effect on export outcomes as compared to imports from non-OECD countries. We aim at furthering this analysis by looking into the connection between multinational R&D and affiliate dependence on imported inputs from different country groups (advanced, middle-income and less developed countries). We have also linked affiliate and parent patent data to the matched data set which makes it possible to analyze parent and affiliate innovation input (R&D expenditure) and output (patents). This may shed light on the weak connection between R&D and patent found among foreign-invested firms in China.

646112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
646112.value: We construct a unique database that includes multinational (parent) firms headquartered in Taiwan and their affiliates in mainland China to study the relationship between parents and affiliates technology-related activities and their impacts on affiliates’ trade behavior. The originality of our unique database allows us to address those novel aspects of technology diffusion via multinationals. Our database combines four different sources of firm-level data on multinational parents in Taiwan and their affiliates in mainland China: (1) Taiwan Economic Journal (TEJ) database; (2) Ministry of Economic Affairs in Taiwan; (3) Manufacturing Firm Census Database from National Bureau of Statistics of China; (4) Chinese Customs Data at transaction-product level. Our empirical findings suggest a differential effect of parent and affiliate knowledge intensity on affiliated firms’ trading behavior. As there is little research combining parent and affiliate characteristics, our pioneering work can be the beginning of a series of empirical investigations in parent-affiliate technology linkage.

Given the importance of such data in studies of FDI, multinational companies, and organizational behavior as well as the challenge in building it, it is a big contribution to the literature by constructing such unique data. Our work has been presented in high-quality international conferences, and obtain good feedback in the field of international trade. We expect the current research outputs will be well received at top general journals such as Review of Economics and Statistics due to its unique empirical contribution or top field journals such as Journal of International Economics and Journal of Development Economics.

646212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
646212.value: Supervisor-directed aggression, or aggressive behaviors initiated by employees that harm their supervisors, is a prevalent and costly problem for organizations. For example, 76% of surveyed employees report engaging in at least one aggressive behavior towards a supervisor (Greenberg & Barling, 1999) and employees aggress against supervisors more frequently than they do against their organizations (Baron, Neuman, & Geddes, 1999). Beyond its frequency, the accumulated evidence suggests that supervisor-directed aggression can result in expensive lawsuits against organizations by victims (Perry, 2000) as well as undermine employee performance, morale, and well-being (Robinson & Greenberg, 1998). Although most research on supervisor-directed aggression has been conducted in the West, recent surveys based on Chinese samples showed that the phenomena also exists and may happen more frequently in the Chinese context (Liu, Kwong, Wu, & Wu, 2010). Consistent with the notion that most individuals do not behave aggressively against others until otherwise provoked, several authors have proposed that abusive supervision, or “subordinates’ perceptions of the extent to which their supervisors engage in the sustained display of hostile verbal and nonverbal behaviors, excluding physical contact” (Tepper, 2000: 178), is a primary cause of supervisor-directed aggression (Tepper et al., 2009). However, despite preliminary evidence supporting the relation between abusive supervision and supervisor-directed aggression, numerous theoretical views suggest that individuals tend to refrain from aggressing against superiors who possess power over themselves (Aquino, Tripp, & Bies, 2001). More specifically, given that supervisors control desirable resources, aggressing against supervisors may cause individuals to lose rewards or suffer punishment (Tepper et al., 2009). Facing these potential aversive consequences, the prevalence of supervisor-directed aggression noted earlier seem to be illogical and counterintuitive. The purpose of the current proposal is to develop a novel theoretical model to explain these conflicting perspectives on whether subordinates will or will not aggress against an abusive supervisor. In particular, by building a self-control model of reactions to abusive supervision, I propose that to pursue potentially greater long-term benefits to the self (i.e., avoiding future punishment or obtaining future rewards), abused subordinates need to possess the ability or motivation to control their hostile emotional reactions and subsequent aggressive behaviors towards abusive supervisors. In addition to its theoretical contributions, the proposed project will provide practical suggestions to organizations on how to eliminate supervisor-directed aggression and thus reduce significant human and organizational costs associated with such destructive workplace behaviors. 下屬對主管進行攻擊是一種普遍存在並且會給組織帶來巨大損失的一個問題。雖然對此問題的相關研究多數以西方國家的員工為樣本，最近以中國員工為樣本的研究調查表明下屬對主管進行攻擊的現象在中國也存在甚至發生更加頻繁。下屬對主管進行攻擊主要是因為他們遇到了虐待型的主管，或者說是他們感知到主管對他們充滿敵意的言語或者非言語的對待。然而即使證據表明虐待型主管與下屬對主管進行攻擊之間有著高相關，一些理論觀點認為，當主管的權力高於下屬的時候，下屬傾向於控制他們對主管的攻擊行為。具體來說，因為主管能夠懲罰或者獎勵下屬，下屬如果對主管進行攻擊的話就很有可能失去獎勵或者受到懲罰。因此普遍存在的下屬對主管進行攻擊的現象似乎顯得違反常理。 本研究的目的就是發展出一個新的理論模型來解釋什麼情況下下屬會或者不會對主管進行攻擊。通過建立一個自我控制模型，我提出為了追求長期的目標和利益（即為了避免懲罰或者為了獲得獎勵），受到主管敵意對待的下屬需要有足夠的能力和動機來自我控制他們的憤怒情緒以及隨後而產生的攻擊性行為。除了具有理論貢獻之外，本研究還為組織如何能減少下屬對主管的攻擊性行為提供具有實踐性的建議。

646212.label: Realisation of objectives
646212.value: All five of the project objectives have been successfully achieved. In particular, by conducting two field studies with hundreds of workers from a variety of industries, including finance, sales, and education, we found that subordinates’ self-control capacity and motivation to self-control work in tandem to affect their aggressive reactions to abusive supervision (#1 objective). Such findings suggest that in order to counter temptations to directly aggress against an abusive supervisor, subordinates should either possess sufficient self-control capacity or be motivated to control their desires to lash out their anger towards abusive supervision (#2 objective). We also found that subordinates were motivated to engage in self-control when they perceive their supervisors hold punishment-based power than reward-based power over them. That is, supervisors’ punishment-based power than reward-based power over them can reduce subordinates’ aggressive reactions towards abusive supervision (#3 objective). Finally, we demonstrated that abusive supervision elicited subordinate hostility toward the abusive supervisor, while self-control capacity mitigates the hostile feelings experienced, and self-control capacity and coercive power together mitigate the tendency to act on hostile feelings (#4 objective). Our findings suggest specific steps that organizations or individual employees might take to counteract aggressive responses to abusive supervision—which, if allowed to continue, can spiral out of control and harm subordinate, third party observer, and organization (#5 objective). In particular, first, our finding regarding the significant buffering effect of self-control capacity on subordinates’ hostile emotional and aggressive behavioral reactions suggests that organizations might implement selection procedures that directly assess self-control capacity. One alternative to implementing selection procedures takes advantage of the fact that self-control capacity is widely regarded to be a dynamic competency that can be developed with training and practice. Second, our results also indicate that hostility drives retaliatory action. Although the implications regarding self-control capacity outlined above apply equally to hostility (given that self-control capacity was found to buffer the effect of abusive supervision on hostility), organizations and employees might take advantage of other techniques that assist individuals in directly dealing with their emotions. Third, Our findings indicate that organizations can also reduce subordinates’ engagement in destructive, vengeful behaviors by creating contexts that maximize individual motivation to self-control. In particular, our findings suggest that punishment or perceived potential negative consequences can be particularly effective at mitigating aggressive behaviors directed toward supervisors. A direct corollary of this finding is that steps should be taken to raise awareness among employees of the negative consequences of engaging in retaliatory actions against supervisors. More subtly, organizations might take advantage of social punishments by strengthening workplace norms for civil behavior through training or generating formal interventions to enhance worker civility (e.g., Leiter, Laschinger, Day, & Oore, 2011). Finally, given that our model suggests abusive supervisors are provocateurs, the most straightforward route to reducing supervisor-directed aggression is to remove or alter aggressive supervisor behavior. Although speculative, research has provided preliminary support that our findings regarding self-control might generalize to supervisors, outbursts may stem from a provocation and the absence of either motivation or ability to regulate their own behavior (see Kiewitz, Restubog, Zagenczyk, Scott, Garcia, & Tang, in press). In this regard, organizations may similarly be advised to select individuals with high self-control capacity for supervisory positions, or to provide training to strengthen supervisors’ self-control capacity. Beyond self-control capacity, it seems prudent for organizations to affect supervisors’ motivation to self-control by informing them of the negative consequences of engaging in abusive acts (see Sutton, 2007).
