646212.label: Major findings and research outcome
646212.value: We conducted two field studies to better understand when abusive supervision results in supervisor-directed aggression. By developing a self-control model, we suggested and found that subordinates’ self-control capacity and motivation to self-control work in tandem (Baumeister & Vohs, 2007): the absence of both capacity and motivation results in the strongest relation between abusive supervision and supervisor-directed aggression. In addition, in accordance with the idea that bad is stronger than good (Baumeister et al., 2001), we found punishment-based power exerts a stronger effect than reward-based power. Finally, in Study 2, we also tested a moderated mediation model, demonstrating that hostility toward a supervisor mediates the relation between abusive supervision and supervisor-directed aggression, self-control capacity mitigates the hostile feelings experienced, and self-control capacity and coercive power together mitigate the tendency to act on hostile feelings. The research has resulted in one top-tier journal article and four conference papers. Please refer to Part C for details on the research outcomes.

646212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
646212.value: One major limitation of our studies pertains to the causal direction of our findings. Coinciding with the dominant perspective in the abusive supervision literature, the model we tested implicitly suggests that abusive supervision is the antecedent of supervisor-directed aggression. However, the cross-sectional design of our studies does not allow such causal inferences. It is also plausible to argue that subordinates’ supervisor-directed aggression leads to abusive supervision (Aquino & Lamertz, 2004). Although it is hard to argue supervisor-directed aggression to be the antecedent of abusive supervision with the moderators and mediators found in our studies, future studies can use cross-lagged panel designs to untangle the causal relation between abusive supervision and supervisor- directed aggression. Moreover, it will be interesting to explore the role that self-control and supervisor power play on the effects subordinate aggressive behaviors on abusive supervision. With this regard, we have completed one field study and two experimental studies to explore when and why subordinate deviance can result in abusive supervision.

646212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
646212.value: We studied the circumstances under which subordinates retaliate against their mean or exasperating supervisor. By collecting two sets of survey data from hundreds of workers from a variety of industries, including finance, sales, and education, we found that workers were more likely to act aggressively toward an abusive boss either when they themselves had insufficient capacity for self-control or when their supervisors could not punish them. These results suggest specific steps that organizations or individual employees might take to counteract aggressive responses to abusive supervision—which, if allowed to continue, can spiral out of control and harm subordinate, third party observer, and organization (Andersson & Pearson, 1999).

646612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
646612.value: Traditional agency theory models presume that the goals of employees and those of the organizations to which they belong are naturally misaligned due to employees' self-interest and effort-aversion. These models consequently prescribe incentives and controls to constrain and direct employees' behavior. Behaviorally oriented research has questioned the universality of goal misalignment, and has instead suggested that employees' intrinsic motivation and reciprocity may frequently substitute for more formal controls. Because, indeed, neither set of assumptions is likely to hold universally, managers must learn to accurately judge the motivations of their employees. This project aims to test the hypothesis that managers will systematically misjudge employee motivation as the result of an asymmetric learning process in which some errors in managers' judgments (being overly-trusting of employees) are more likely to be disconfirmed by feedback than are other errors (being overly-mistrustful of employees). The result of such an asymmetric learning process is the development of a bias among managers towards overly-mistrustful beliefs about employee motivations, and consequently an inefficient over-reliance on formal organizational controls. 647312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
647312.value: Assemble-to-order is a special manufacturing strategy where components are purchased to stock, while the assembly of final products is postponed till product demand becomes known. By adopting the assemble-to-order strategy, firms can customize products on a large scale and at a low cost. Nowadays assemble-to-order is widely applied for various products, such as computers (e.g., Dell), automobiles (e.g., Toyota), accessories (e.g., "Build Your Own Ring" at amazon.com), and footwear (e.g., Nike). Despite the widespread applications and considerable benefits, assemble-to-order systems are "notoriously difficult to analyze and manage" (Benjaafar and ElHafsi, 2006). The difficulty mainly arises from simultaneously managing large numbers of components and products in a dynamic environment. Traditional practices have primarily focused on managing the supply of components. Nevertheless, it becomes increasingly evident that great opportunities exist on the demand side. Application examples in Dell and IBM show that simple demand-management strategies can contribute to substantial cost savings (Breen 2004, Ettl et al. 2007). Demand management, including pricing and order management, is critically important and particularly challenging for assemble-to-order systems. An integrated view of supply and demand management is required and yet, is largely missing in the existing literature. Our project will contribute to the literature by making the first attempt to examine joint pricing, order management, and inventory decisions for assemble-to-order firms. In addition, we will also explore how the firms’ joint decisions influence customers’ purchasing behavior and the overall social benefit. Specifically, we will investigate the following important issues: (1) how to jointly optimize the firms’ pricing, order management, and inventory decisions and how to adjust these decisions dynamically over time. Specifically, the order management decisions include order acceptance and fulfillment decisions; (2) how the joint decisions depend on firms’ operational capabilities (e.g., lead time for inventory replenishment, component procurement costs, assembly capacity, and penalties for late order fulfillment) and market conditions (e.g., market variability, demand sensitivity to price and fulfillment lead-time, and demand substitution); (3) how the joint decisions impact on the welfare of customers, firms, and the society. Outcomes of this project will provide insights for managers to understand the interactions among the demand and supply management decisions. Our results will be particularly useful for managers who seek effective strategies to improve their assemble-to-order firms. 面向订单装配是一种特殊的制造业策略：企业仅仅储存产品的各组件，而等到接受到顾客订单之后才完成最终产品的装配。通过采用面向订单装配的策略，企业可以用很低的成本实现大规模的产品个性化。现今这一策略已经成功运用在很多产品的制造过程中，例如计算机（如戴尔计算机），汽车（如丰田汽车），首饰配件（如亚马逊网站推出的“设计你自己的戒指”），和鞋类 （如耐克）。 尽管面向订单装配系统运用广泛裨益良多，对于这一系统的分析和管理却非常困难(Benjaafar and ElHafsi, 2006)，这主要是由于需要对大量的组件和产品进行联合动态管理。传统的研究和实践主要集中于组件的供应控制方面，但是实践表明产品需求管理方面存在巨大的潜力：戴尔和IBM的应用案例证明，只需简单的需求管理策略就可以帮助企业获得十分显著的收益。 产品需求管理，包括定价和订单管理，对于面向订单装配系统至关重要却极具挑战，因为它需要对于供给和需求双方面的整体理解和把握，而这一整体观却在研究文献中极少涉及。 本项目的主要贡献将在于首次尝试审视面向订单装配系统中关于定价、订单管理、和库存的联合决策。此外，本项目还将考察企业的联合决策对于顾客消费行为和整体社会福利的影响。具体而言，本项目将研究以下重要问题： （1）如何进行企业定价、订单管理、和库存的联合动态优化，其中订单管理包括订单接受和履行； （2）企业的联合决策如何受到企业本身运作能力（例如组件采购成本和订单延迟发货的罚金）和市场状况（例如市场波动，需求的价格弹性，和需求的可替换性）的影响； （3）企业的联合决策对于企业、顾客、和整体社会福利的影响 本项目将帮助企业管理者更好的理解需求和供给管理之间的关系，并有望提出关于改善面向订单装配系统的有效策略。

647312.label: Realisation of objectives
647312.value: 1. This objective has been fully achieved. Because simultaneous decisions on pricing, order management, and inventory is very challenging, we have followed two steps in our study: We first assume that one of the decisions is given and fixed, and examine the joint decisions on the other two aspects; Building on these studies, we then proceed to consider joint optimization of all the three decisions. Consequently, four models have been developed and analyzed, with focuses on different joint decisions: (i) pricing and inventory; (ii) pricing and order management; (iii) order management and inventory; and (iv) pricing, order management, and inventory. The main findings of each model are summarized below. (i) In this paper we examine a joint pricing-inventory decision problem for multiple products which require common resources to produce, procure, or hold. The total availabilities of the resources are exogenously fixed. Orders for the products are stochastic and fulfilled according to a natural first-come-first-serve sequence. Any unmet order is lost. For the case where two products share one resource, we prove the existence of a unique optimal solution to the decision problem. We also characterize the firm's product assortment under the optimal solution and identify a distribution-free product index to determine the assortment priority among the products. (ii) In this paper we propose a heuristic policy for joint optimization of pricing and order-management decisions in Assemble-to-Order systems. The policy, referred to as partial postponement of order fulfillment, consists of two-phase decisions: ex-ante order acceptance and ex-post order fulfillment. The order acceptance decision is made at the beginning of the selling season, at which time the firm determines for each product a fixed fulfill-up-to level, dictating the maximum number of orders to be accepted during the selling season. The order-fulfillment decision, on the other hand, is postponed till the end of the horizon, at which time the firm optimizes over which orders to fulfill (or to cancel) based on the component inventory and the accepted orders. We prove that the policy is asymptotically optimal for the ATO system when the problem scale becomes very large. (iii) To examine the optimal dynamic policy for order and inventory management, we consider a special kind of assemble-to-order systems, referred to generalized W systems, where each product is assembled from a common component and a product-specific component. We examine a periodic review system and focus on simple nested fulfillment policies, where orders are fulfilled in decreasing order of selling prices. We prove that a nested policy is always optimal for two-product W systems. For systems with more than two products, we exemplify that a nested policy may not always be optimal and identify a sufficient condition under which it is. Furthermore, the nested policy is also shown to be asymptotically optimal for large-scale problems. We examine extensions of our model that incorporate holding costs and the case where each product may require multiple units of the common component, and show that our results are robust. (iv) This paper characterizes joint pricing, order fulfillment and inventory policies for generalized W assemble-to-order systems. Demand is price-dependent, stochastic, and lost if not satisfied immediately. We prove the joint concavity of the optimal profit function with respect to the component inventory, implying that a simple gradient-based algorithm can be applied to search for the optimal decision on component inventory. For the case with stationary demand, we prove the asymptotical optimality of a heuristic policy where the product price is fixed over time and order fulfillment policy is nested. 2. This objective has been fully achieved. For all the four models (i)-(iv), we have performed comparative studies of the optimal or heuristic policies regarding various system parameters, as summarized below. (i) We characterize how the firm’s optimal assortment depends on resource availability, demand uncertainty, and a product’s resource requirement. We prove that, when the firm can only offer one product due to resource scarcity, a product should be assigned a high assortment priority when its worst-case base demand is high, own-price sensitivity is low, cross-price sensitivity is high, or resource requirement is low. Monotonicities of the optimal joint pricing and inventory policies in resource availability and a product’s resource requirement are also shown for some special cases. (ii) For the proposed heuristic policy, we illustrate how the optimal order-acceptance up-to levels and the expected demand induced by the optimal prices depend on the compensation level for order cancellation, component inventory, and demand variability. We find, for example, that the firm should accept more orders when demand becomes more variable. (iii) Assuming that an optimal order-fulfillment policy is adopted, we show that the optimal stocking level of a component decreases in the component procurement cost. In addition, for a two-product W system, the inventory imbalance metric, defined as the difference between the total inventory of dedicated components and the common component inventory, is shown to decrease in the procurement cost of either dedicated component. (iv) For small-scale problems, we observe in the numerical study that the proposed heuristic performs better when the cross-price elasticity of each product is lower and the system is more balanced (i.e., the difference between the total dedicated-component inventory and the common component inventory is smaller). 3. This objective has been fully achieved. In all the models, we have evaluated the impact of the joint policies on the firm’s profits. We note that joint optimization of the decisions can bring substantial benefits to the firm, compared to the situation where the decisions are made in isolation. Moreover, we have assessed the performance gap of the heuristic policies in relative to the optimal policies. Our results show that the gap closes quickly as the problem scale increases. In models (ii) and (iv), we further investigate the impacts on consumer and social welfare. In model (ii) we find that the postponed-fulfillment policy, though involving order cancellation by the firm, may lead to a higher consumer and social surplus, compared to the case when the firm commits to fulfilling all the accepted orders. In the numerical study for model (iv), we observe that the social welfare under the heuristic policy converges to that under the optimal policy. In addition to the four models specific for Assemble-to-Order systems, to further characterize the impact of firms’ joint decisions on consumers’ purchasing behavior and resultant consumer welfare, we perform two other studies focusing on consumers’ strategic responses to firms’ selling strategies. The first study (model v) analyzes a firm’s dynamic pricing and capacity/inventory decisions when consumers may wait for sales and other consumers’ reviews of the product. The second study (model vi) characterizes a firm’s joint markdown and inventory decision for perishable goods when consumers may strategically forward buy. The findings in these papers apply not only to Assemble-to-Order systems, but also to other manufacturing and service systems.

647312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
647312.value: The models can be further developed to incorporate more sophisticated product-component structure, more complications on the supply side (e.g., lead time, limited capacity), or/and interaction between the ATO firm and the component suppliers (i.e., a decentralized supply chain). While these issues are beyond the scope of this project, they present fruitful directions for future research projects.

647512.value: 以多級結構的方式理解知識管理與員工工作表現：知識管理系統，領導以及社會網絡的作用

647512.label: Project Objectives

Understand how KMS design is related to job outcomes and how employees’ awareness networks are related to job outcomes

647512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
647512.value: Knowledge management is of great importance in building competitive advantage, so organizations have been seeking ways to improve knowledge management. One of the major challenges is facilitating knowledge access, i.e., helping employees get the knowledge they need to complete their work. Employees often complain that they do not know where to get the knowledge they want or whom to ask. To tackle this challenge, this study proposes to disentangle the various social and technological factors affecting knowledge access. Specifically, it will attempt to bring to knowledge management system (KMS) design what is known about social networks and leadership. The value of awareness networks in facilitating knowledge access is well known and KMSs that seek to cultivate interactions among employees will increase awareness. This research proposes to determine how a KMS can best be designed to facilitate the development of an awareness network. It will also examine the role of leadership in motivating employees to use a KMS to develop their awareness networks. Specifically, this research will develop a two-level model that incorporates KMS design and social networks at the individual level but also leadership at the business unit level to explain the development of individual awareness networks and subsequent job outcomes. KMS design features that facilitate interaction among employees should promote employees’ awareness of others’ areas of expertise, and any such effect should be stronger with increasing transformational leadership. In addition, the existence of awareness networks should mediate the effect of KMS design on job outcomes. We propose to collect multiple waves of qualitative and quantitative data from different sources and use them to test these relationships in a large organization that is going to implement a KMS. This work should provide guidelines for KMS implementation by identifying the KMS design features that contribute most to awareness networks and subsequent job outcomes. It should expand the nomological network related to job outcomes by linking it to technology. And this work will link multiple theoretical perspectives at different levels to develop a holistic understanding of knowledge access and job performance. 鑒於知識管理對於建立競爭優勢有很重要的作用，企業一直在尋求提高知識管理的方法。其中的一個主要的挑戰是促進知識獲取，那就是使員工得到可以幫助他們完成工作的知識。員工經常抱怨不知在哪裡可以獲取知識或者向誰詢問知識。要解決這個問題，本研究著眼于影響知識獲取的社會和科技因素。確切的說，本研究使用社會網絡學和領導學的理論去理解知識管理系統的設計。眾所周知認知網絡在促進知識獲取上的價值。知識管理系統可以讓員工更好地溝通，從而提高認知能力，即知道可以在哪或向誰獲取知識。本研究探討如何設計知識管理系統以促進認知網絡的形成，同時也探討企業領導在激勵員工使用知識管理系統開發認知網絡上的作用。 具體的說，本研究會建立一個兩層結構理論模型，把知識管理系統的設計和社會網絡放在個人層面，而把企業領導放在業務部門層面來解釋個人認知網絡的形成及其對員工工作表現的影響。知識管理系統中那些促進溝通的功能讓員工更好地知道其它人的專長，而此作用在變革型領導的方式下會加強。認知網絡還會影響知識管理系統設計和工作表現的關係。我們建議在一間將要實施知識管理系統的大企業中從不同的渠道收集多輪的定性和定量的數據來驗證我們的理論。 通過發現知識管理系統中那些有助於認知網絡形成以及提高員工工作表現的功能，本研究將會對知識管理系統的實施提供指引。因為加入了科技因素，本研究加深了我們對影響員工工作表現的各種因素的理解。本研究通過將多個理論觀點導入不同的層面進行分析，以求對知識獲取和員工工作表現形成全面的了解。

647512.label: Realisation of objectives
647512.value: The first objective is to “understand the roles of social network and KMS design in affecting job outcomes”. Against this backdrop, we conducted a study to identify the key KMS features that contribute positively to job outcomes and the key drivers of the use of these features. We used a combination of a literature review and a qualitative study to identify and validate the key KMS features. We compared the effects of the magnitude of the use of the four features on job performance and job satisfaction respectively. Using a social network perspective, we identified help-seeking and help-providing ties as the important drivers of the use of the key KMS features and job outcomes. We used a quantitative study to validate our model. Our study sheds light on our understanding of the roles of social network and KMS design in affecting job outcomes. Therefore, the first objective has been fulfilled. The second objective is to “understand the relationship between KMS use and job performance by incorporating contingency factors related to task, system, user and leadership”. Against this backdrop, a mixed methods approach that includes a quantitative study (n=1,441) among knowledge workers in seven business units of a large organization in the finance industry is used to validate the theoretical model and shed light on our understanding of the topic. A follow-up qualitative study (n=48) was conducted in one business unit to cross-validate the findings and explain unsupported findings. Data were collected from multiple sources, i.e., surveys, interviews, and system archives. By examining the contingency factors related to task, system, user and leadership, this study shed light on our understanding of the relationship between KMS use and job performance. Therefore, the second objective has been fulfilled.

647512.label: Major findings and research outcome
647512.value: Regarding the first objective, our major findings showed that help-seeking and help-providing ties were positively related to use of the key KMS features and use of the key KMS features were positively related to two key job outcomes―i.e., job performance and job satisfaction―except that post and search were not significantly related to job satisfaction, whereas comment and rate were not significantly related to job performance. Regarding the second objective, our major findings showed that deep structure use contributed positively to job performance, and contingency factors related to task, system, user, and leadership moderated the relationship between rich KMS use and job performance. Similar pattern of results were also found in the qualitative study. It served to cross-validate the results from the quantitative study, provided a richer and more complete view on how employees experience job success, and explained the unsupported findings from the quantitative study.

647512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
647512.value: Regarding the first objective, some potential venues for future research include but not limited to: (1) examine the content of use of different KMS features; (2) examine some mediating variables, some inter-linkages among different KMS features, and breadth of use or quality of use; (3) examine how the change of networks affects KMS use and job outcomes; and (4) understand the development of peer support networks by drawing from different theoretical lens, e.g., friendship networks, justice and task interdependence. Regarding the objective, some potential venues for future research include but not limited to: (1) test the generalizability of the current model by studying other complex technologies, such as e-healthcare systems and enterprise resource planning systems; (2) identify and examine other contingency factors by drawing from different theoretical perspectives, such as cultural values; (3) use larger samples to validate the model; and (4) examine factors driving employees to create, share, and apply knowledge.

647512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
647512.value: Given that investments in large-scale collaborative systems, such as KMSs, continue to grow, organizations are keen to know how to reap the benefits from such investments. Our research sheds light on our understanding of this important topic. From the perspective of employees, our research indicates it is critical for employees to use a small number of key features (or the relatively more important features) to enhance their job performance. Our work identified some of these features, thus providing employees with ideas about how to better leverage large-scale collaborative systems to accomplish their jobs. In addition, our study indicates employees need to enhance their capacity to absorb new knowledge and leverage their peer support networks to overcome knowledge barriers. From the perspective of organizations, our study suggests organizations should provide adequate training to their employees and leverage power users to facilitate greater knowledge transfer. Organizations should also strengthen training on advanced use of a KMS for employees who are likely to handle nonroutine tasks. Lastly, organizations should also consider planning ahead to construct an effective management team before a KMS implementation. They should consider hiring leaders from either internal or external sources with motivational and inspirational leadership skills to manage implementations.

647912.label: Project Title(Chinese)
647912.value: 產假越長越好？產假延長對中國兒童早期和中長期發展的影響

647912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
647912.value: Over the past few decades, researchers in various disciplines have increasingly realized the persistent and important effects of early childhood conditions on later life outcomes (Almond and Currie, 2011). This motivates many public policies that attempt to intervene early in the lives of children in order to improve future outcomes, including maternity (parental) leave provisions. Despite the wide provision of maternity leave, research on the direct impacts of maternity leave legislation on children’s early and long term outcomes has been relatively scarce. Even in the small but recently growing literature on this (Dustmann and Schonberg, 2008; Baker and Milligan, 2008a, 2010, 2011; Liu and Skans, 2010; Rasmussen, 2010; Carneiro et al., 2011; Rossin, 2011), there appears no strong evidence suggesting beneficial effects of maternity leave provisions. While pre-reform leave policies were already relatively generous and good-quality subsidized child care was widely available in the countries studied so far, evidence from other countries with different institutions is urgently needed to better understand the impacts of maternity leave. This project will contribute to this growing area as the first to analyze the effects of maternity leave expansions on early childhood and later outcomes in China. (China increased maternity leave from 56 to 90 days in September 1988.) China is an interesting candidate for study for at least three reasons. First, the labor force participation rate of prime-aged married women was extremely high in China through the 1980s. A second institutional feature is that a lack of public daycare centers for infants and toddlers pushed parents to seek help from private providers and other family members. So studying maternity leave in China may speak more about how the substitution between parent care and other kinship care influences child development. Last but not least, as China experienced both a national expansion of basic maternity leave and province-specific extensions of leave for certain subpopulations of women, the unique policies provide wider variation in leave coverage both across provinces and over time, substantially enriching the empirical strategies at researchers’ disposal. The project will employ hand-collected policy data and a rich set of Chinese micro-level data to evaluate the impacts of maternity leave on childhood, adolescent, and early adult outcomes. Findings from this project will be important both to academic researchers interested in maternity leave, maternal work, and child outcomes and to policymakers regulating leave durations. 不同領域的研究者在過去數十年間已經廣泛認識到嬰幼兒時期的成長環境和條件對兒童期及成人期的發展有著重要並且持久的影響。基於此共識，許多公共政策試圖對兒童早期進行干預以促進他們日後的發展。生育產假制度就是其中一項重要的政策。 雖然產假制度在各國非常普遍，有關產假政策對兒童早期及長期發展之直接影響的研究仍相對匱乏。現有的為數不多的研究大多採用歐美發達國家的數據，而且沒有發現延長產假對兒童有顯著的益處。對於這些結果一個可能的解釋是這些發達國家（在產假延長之前）本身已有相對完善的福利制度和普及的（受政府資助的）優質兒童保育服務，因而再延長產假的效果微乎其微。但是，這些結果是否具有普遍性，需要其他國家（尤其是不同制度的國家）的證據來佐證。 本研究計劃將是首次針對中國的產假政策對兒童發展的影響所進行的研究。（中國於1988年9月將生育產假從原先的56天提高到90天。）中國至少有三個有別於發達國家的值得研究之處。首先，中國的已婚女性在1980年代的就業參與率極高。其次，由於當時公共幼兒保育機構缺乏，許多父母不得不尋求其他家庭成員提供保育服務。因此，研究中國的產假延長有助於更好的了解父母的照料相對於其他親屬的照料對兒童發展的影響。第三，除了全國範圍實施的產假延長，各省還分別在不同的時間制定政策給予某些合資格女性額外產假。中國這一獨特的隨地區隨時間變化的產假政策為研究方法的多樣化帶來了便利。 本計劃將採用多套不同時期的數據來研究產假政策對中國兒童的早期，青年期，和成年期發展的影響。所獲得的發現將為對產假政策、女性就業、兒童發展等有興趣的研究者，以及制定產假政策的決策者提供重要的參考。

661212.label: Project Objectives
661212.value: To investigate the functional roles of RapGEF2 in neuronal migration and lamination of the cerebral cortex To elucidate the mechanisms by which Cdk5 modulate the phosphorylation and function of RapGEF2 to regulate neuronal migration
rows: To investigate the functional roles of RapGEF2 in neuronal migration and lamination of the cerebral cortex
To elucidate the mechanisms by which Cdk5 modulate the phosphorylation and function of RapGEF2 to regulate neuronal migration

661212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
661212.value: The establishment of neural circuitry in the cerebral cortex requires the formation of a highly organized laminar structure, which is achieved through directional migration of neurons. Newborn cortical neurons generated by radial glial progenitor cells in the ventricular zone (VZ) go through a multipolar stage in the intermediate zone (IZ), which is followed by polarization of their leading process towards the pial surface and migration to their final destination in the cortical plate (CP). Upon reaching the CP, the neurons become mature and are integrated into the neural circuitry. Specification of a stabilized leading process is a prerequisite for multipolar to bipolar transition of migrating neurons in the lower IZ before the start of directional migration in the CP. Defective migration and abnormal lamination due to aberrant extracellular cues, adhesive molecules and cytoskeletal regulators have been implicated in various neurological and psychiatric disorders. However, the signaling mechanisms underlying neuronal migration and cortical lamination are not well understood. Cdk5, a proline-directed serine/threonine kinase, is one of the key molecules that regulate these processes. Based on mass spectrometry analysis, we have recently identified RapGEF2, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor specific for activation of the small GTPase Rap, as a substrate for Cdk5. Our preliminary findings suggest that RapGEF2 is essential for proper neuronal migration and lamination of the cerebral cortex. Silencing of RapGEF2 disrupted radial migration in vivo, with cortical neurons arrested in the lower IZ. Furthermore, we found that Cdk5 phosphorylates RapGEF2 at Ser1124 within a Cdk5 consensus motif (SPRK) in vitro. Our findings suggest a potential regulatory mechanism by which Cdk5 regulates the function of RapGEF2 in the developing cerebral cortex. In this proposal, we will investigate the functional roles of RapGEF2 in directing the orientation and migration of neurons in the cerebral cortex during development. We will then examine how Cdk5 regulates the phosphorylation and function of RapGEF2 during neuronal migration. The molecular mechanisms by which RapGEF2 promotes neuronal migration and morphogenesis of cortical projection neurons will be delineated. Finally, we will conduct studies to identify the extracellular cues that regulate RapGEF2/Rap1 function during neuronal migration.

661212.label: Realisation of objectives
661212.value: This project aimed to elucidate the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying brain development. In particular, we specifically examined the functional roles of cyclin-dependent kinase-5 (Cdk5)-mediated phosphorylation of RapGEF2 in neuronal migration and lamination of the cerebral cortex; this aim was fully realized by addressing the three objectives mentioned above. In order to characterize the functional roles of RapGEF2 in cerebral cortex development (Objective 1), we first examined its spatial and temporal expression profiles in the developing mouse cortex. RapGEF2 expression was upregulated during the critical stages of neuronal migration in the developing neocortex and remained high thereafter. In utero electroporation was used to visualize migrating neurons in the developing cortex, revealing that RapGEF2 was upregulated precisely when migrating neurons acquired a bipolar morphology. To investigate whether RapGEF2 is critical for this polarity acquisition and neuronal migration, we knocked down RapGEF2 expression in utero and used live imaging to confirm that RapGEF2 specifically acts on the multipolar–bipolar transition during neuronal migration. Accordingly, long-term suppression of RapGEF2 caused accumulation of ectopic neurons in subcortical region, permanently affecting cortical lamination. To elucidate the mechanisms by which Cdk5 modulates the phosphorylation and function of RapGEF2 to regulate neuronal migration (Objective 2), we first characterized the phosphorylation of RapGEF2 by Cdk5. In vitro experiments confirmed that RapGEF2 is predominantly phosphorylated by Cdk5 at Ser1124. A rabbit polyclonal antibody that recognizes phospho-Ser1124 was generated in-house, and RapGEF2 phosphorylation at Ser1124 was validated via a phosphorylation assay in vitro and Cdk5−/− mouse brains in vivo. The spatial and subcellular localization of phospho-RapGEF2 was further examined in the developing mouse cortex by immunohistochemistry. The expression of phospho-RapGEF2 was similar to that of total RapGEF2 protein, showing restrictive signals in the bipolar migration zones as well as co-localization with cytoplasmic neuronal marker Tuj1. In order to investigate whether RapGEF2 regulates multipolar–bipolar transition and neuronal migration in a Cdk5-dependent manner, various RapGEF2 phosphorylation mutants were re-expressed in RapGEF2-depleted cortices and confirmed that the RapGEF2 phosphorylation at Ser1124 was essential for the multipolar–bipolar transition and cortical lamination. To explicate the signaling mechanisms by which RapGEF2 regulates neuronal migration (Objective 1 and 2), we first demonstrated that neuronal migration requires, and Cdk5-mediated phosphorylation of RapGEF2 controls, its GEF activity towards Rap1. To explore the upstream signals of RapGEF2 in neuronal migration, we showed that p35, the major Cdk5 activator during brain development, exhibits a similar restrictive distribution pattern as that of phospho-RapGEF2 in the developing cerebral cortex, indicating that p35 expression may contribute to the phosphorylation and activation of RapGEF2. In addition, the extracellular molecules BDNF and Reelin can activate Rap1 and regulate neuronal migration. We showed that Rap1 activation by the treatment of BDNF but not Reelin was suppressed by RapGEF2 knockdown, suggesting BDNF activates Rap1 through RapGEF2 during cortical development. To identify the downstream signaling targets of RapGEF2 in neuronal migration, we determined that RapGEF2 and Cdk5-dependent RapGEF2 phosphorylation are involved in the regulation of N-cadherin surface localization in migrating neurons. Moderate N-cadherin expression in RapGEF2-suppressed cortices significantly rescued the defective bipolar transition and neuronal migration. These results collectively demonstrate that RapGEF2 acts on the multipolar–bipolar transition during neuronal migration via a Rap1/N-cadherin pathway.

661212.label: Major findings and research outcome
661212.value: In this project, we investigated how Cdk5-dependent RapGEF2 phosphorylation regulates the lamination of the cerebral cortex. As a result, we unraveled the key molecular basis underlying RapGEF2-regulated neuronal migration, disturbance of which can cause subcortical band heterotopia and increased seizure susceptibility. Cdk5 phosphorylates RapGEF2 in vivo Cdk5 is a multi-faceted kinase that regulates various aspects of neuronal development and function. We found seven consensus motifs, (S/T)PX(K/H/R), for Cdk5 phosphorylation in RapGEF2 protein and confirmed that Ser1124 is the major phosphorylation site in vivo (Ye et al., Nat Commun, 2014). Furthermore, we advanced understanding of the regulation of Cdk5 activity in the developing cortex. While Cdk5 is critical for neural development, its activity is suggested to be ubiquitous in postmitotic neurons. We present the first demonstration that Cdk5 is preferentially activated in radially migrating neurons during cortical development as evidenced by the restricted expression of p35 in the radial migration zone. Thus, besides the dynamic expression of RapGEF2, Cdk5-dependent phosphorylation provides another level of control of RapGEF2 activity to ensure proper neuronal migration and cortical circuit formation (Ye et al., Nat Commun, 2014). RapGEF2 regulates multipolar-to-bipolar transition and neuronal migration We investigated the mechanisms regulating cortical layer formation and identified RapGEF2 as a specific determinant of multipolar-to-bipolar transition during neuronal migration. Given the Cdk5-dependent regulation of RapGEF2 activity and Reelin-mediated C3G activation, we proposed a sequential regulation model of the relationship between the two major neuronal migration pathways: the Cdk5- and Reelin-dependent pathways. In brief, these two pathways do not simply function in parallel, but rather act on successive neuronal migration phases. Disruption of the previous migration phase results in a failure to unlock responsiveness to signaling molecules that initiate subsequent migration phases. Accordingly, Cdk5-mediated RapGEF2 phosphorylation mainly controls multipolar–bipolar transition as a cellular checkpoint and allows bipolar locomotion in the cortical plate, as well as the subsequent terminal translocation activated through the Reelin-mediated C3G pathway (Ye et al., Nat Commun, 2014). These findings provide novel insights into the pathological mechanisms underlying neuronal migration-associated disorders such as lissencephaly (smooth brain), cortical heterotopias (double cortex), microcephaly (small brain), and autism.

661212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
661212.value: The current project identified the molecular mechanisms by which RapGEF2 controls cerebral cortex formation during embryonic development. Its downstream effector Rap1 plays multi-faceted roles in an array of neurodevelopmental processes, including neuronal migration, dendrite development, and spine morphogenesis. Thus, it is not surprising that disease-associated genetic variants of Rap1 GEFs have been identified, which are often linked to Rap1 deregulation and neurodevelopmental deficits. For instance, overexpression of the autism-associated variants of RapGEF4 (also known as Epac2) leads to impaired development of basal dendrites and altered spine morphology in cultured cortical and hippocampal neurons. Intriguingly, copy number variants of RapGEF2 and RapGEF6 (a close homologue of RapGEF2) have been identified in schizophrenia patients. Therefore, one key issue to be addressed by future studies is to further characterize the physiological functions of the Cdk5-dependent regulation of Rap1 signalling via RapGEF2 and RapGEF6 in psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia. Another topic is whether cortical malformation caused by RapGEF2 depletion can be rescued by the re-expression of RapGEF2 postnatally. We can employ inducible expression system such as Tet-On system to re-express RapGEF2 in migration-arrested neurons at early postnatal stage and examine prenatal migration deficits can be therapeutically treated postnatally. As embryonic neurogenesis and adult neurogenesis share plenty of conserved signaling pathways, a third direction is to investigate whether RapGEF2 is critical for the migration of adult born neurons to their destination such as those from subventricular zone to the olfactory bulb as well as subgranular zone to the molecular layer of hippocampus. The findings will provide novel insights into the disease mechanisms of neurological disorders as well as aid drug development and clinical diagnosis.

661212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
661212.value: Brain development depends on the correct positioning of neurons, establishment of axon-dendrite polarity, formation of neural circuits, and maintenance of the wired neural circuits. These steps are critically controlled by various molecular signaling pathways. Defect in any of these processes greatly impair neural functions. In particular, defects in neuronal migration are associated with various neurological disorders in humans including lissencephaly (smooth brain), cortical heterotopias (double cortex), microcephaly (small brain), and autism. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are poorly understood. Our project aimed to better understand these developmental events by investigating how a protein RapGEF2 regulates specific processes during polarity transition and integration of neurons into a well-organized laminar structure during development of the cerebral cortex. Importantly, activation of RapGEF2 is controlled via phosphorylation by a serine/threonine kinase Cdk5, whose activity is largely restricted to the bipolar migration zone. Alteration of RapGEF2 signaling in the cerebral cortex led to severe brain malformation such as subcortical band heterotopia in mice. Our findings have revealed previously unknown mechanisms of brain development and provide insights into how various neurological disorders occur.

661912.value: To study the effect of East Asian aerosol inputs on microzooplankton bacterivory and herbivory and its impact on microbial food web dynamics To study the response of microbial community to atmospheric deposition of East Asian aerosol at the molecular level using –omics approach

To study the response of microbial community to atmospheric deposition of East Asian aerosol at the molecular level using –omics approach

661912.label: Realisation of objectives
661912.value: To address the first objectives, we conducted a number of experiments between August 2011 and February 2013 at a subtropical coastal site adjacent to the South China Sea. The effect of aerosol deposition on the growth rate (μ) and grazing mortality (m) of different-sized phytoplankton was investigated in microcosm experiments using the dilution technique. Results of these experiments have been published (paper #4). Briefly, a significant enhancement in both phytoplankton growth and microzooplankton grazing were obtained after aerosol addition, but the degree of impact was different in each size fraction. A large increase in growth rate was obtained for micro-phytoplankton, while pico- and nano-sized cells suffered increased grazing pressure in the aerosol treatment. The different responses resulted in a reduced proportion of protist consumption to phytoplankton daily production and increased net growth rate in micro-phytoplankton but the opposite in nano- and pico-phytoplankon, which explains the clear shift of phytoplankton size structure in response to aerosol addition. To address the second objectives, our first attempt is to achieve it through the participation of the EU project - The impact of atmospheric deposition on the microbial food web of the Eastern Mediterranean Sea (ATMOMED). This is a multi-nation collaborative project let by scientists in Israel and Greece (see research output). Unfortunately, the samples collected from the mesocosm experiments did not provide enough biomass for high-throughput next generation sequencing of meta-omics study (sent to BGI for low biomass, high-risk trials, but failed), so we used the DNA and RNA for amplicon study of 16S rRNA to study the community shift of prokaryotic community through the 10 day experiment. The results has been published in Frontiers in Marine Sciences (paper #15). We then tried to conduct a series of microcosm experiments on board a Taiwanese research vessel during two cruises to the Western Philippine Sea in 2013 and 2014. The data analysis has been completed, but manuscript is still under preparation. The western subtropical North Pacific Ocean experiences strong stratification and severe nutrient depletion during summer. We expect that the addition of aerosol would invoke the largest response in the microbial community. In July 2013, we set up a microcosm experiment on a research vessel during a cruise to the western North Pacific Ocean. Triplicates of 20 L carboys were filled with surface seawater and 200 μg/L aerosol was added. No aerosol addition was taken as the control, and all the control and treatment microcosms were incubated on-deck for 3 days. Samples were collected at the end of the incubation for cell counts using flow cytometry, extraction of DNA (bacterial and protist community characterization) and RNA (metatranscriptomics), pigment profiles (HPLC), and nutrient measurement. The addition of aerosol stimulated Chl a concentration (1.45 fold). Autotrophic bacteria, mainly Synechoccocus and Prochlorococcus, the main primary producers in the open ocean, decreased significantly with Prochlorococcus decreased by 5 fold. Heterotrophic bacteria did not shown significant change. Picoeukaryotes increased dramatically (1.85 fold). These results are in agreement with previous studies in other geographic regions. 454 pyrosequencing targeting the 16S rRNA gene was applied to characterize the bacterial community composition. Prokaryotic community metabolic activity profile was decoded by RNA differential expression using the Illumina MiSeq sequencing technology. We got raw 1,530,249,366 and 1,726,717,497 bp for the control and aerosol treatment, respectively. Bacterial sequences dominated the whole sequencing depth. Achaeal and viral sequences increased in the aerosol treatment. The major distribution of the sequences were found to be associated with functional processes such as carbohydrate and protein metabolisms and biosynthesis of cofactors, vitamins and pigments, and amino acids and derivatives. Photosynthesis and nitrogen fixation decreased significantly, which indicate the influence on carbon and nitrogen cycling. Zooming in, we can get a lot of information, such as on different categories of carbohydrate utilization, motility, iron scavenging and heavy metal resistance. More detailed analysis is under taking and the physiological responses of the prokaryotes are being unraveled (paper under preparation). Microbial eukaryotic community composition was characterized by using 454 pyrosequencing targeting the 18S rRNA gene. Dramatic changes were seen in the community composition. For example, the most dominant group in both control and the aerosol treatment, Alveolata, decreased in the aerosol treatment, while Viridiplantae and stramenopiles increased dramatically. More experiments were conducted during the second cruise (April, 2014). At this time, photosynthetic efficiency, primary production and nitrogen fixation of the phytoplanktons in the control and aerosol enriched treatments were also compared.

661912.label: Major findings and research outcome
661912.value: Our study is the first direct assessment of the impact of aerosol amendment on microzooplankton grazing activity. Aerosol input induced significant phytoplankton biomass accumulation as well as community structure shift. A large increase in growth rate was obtained for micro-phytoplankton, while pico- and nano-sized cells suffered increased grazing pressure in the aerosol treatment, resulting to the clear shift of phytoplankton size structure in response to aerosol addition. The picoplankton populations did not exhibit apparent biomass accumulation due to efficient cropping by heterotrophic nanoflagellates. Our results suggest that it is important to consider the role of protist grazing when evaluating the effects of atmospheric deposition on marine planktonic ecosystems under the scenarios of increasing human activity, atmospheric input and natural perturbations. We have conducted aerosol enrichment incubations during two cruises to the oligotrophic northern West Pacific Ocean, in order to evaluate the impact of anthropogenic input of aerosol to the community structure and physiological activities of the prokaryotes and micro-eukaryotes in the Open Ocean. The prokaryotic and eukaryotic community structures in the control and aerosol enriched treatment were compared with 454-pyrosequencing of 16s rRNA, 18s rRNA amplicons and analyzing HPLC samples. The physiological responses of the prokaryotes were unraveled using meta-transcriptomic analysis. It is the first meta-transcriptomics study in this kind experiment, which will provide molecular level insights of the response of microorganisms to the events of atmospheric deposition in oligotrophic ocean. This projected is acknowledged for many publications. Among them, #4, #15 and #17 (under preparation) are the key papers that directly resulted from the proposed research and fulfill the realization of the objectives of this project.

661912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
661912.value: There are several areas are being considered for further development. First of all, I would like to look at the viral dynamics and viral genomics during the events of strong atmospheric deposition. Second, how changes in microbial community can affect higher trophic level, such as mesozooplankton. I plan to organize an international workshop on these topics and then prepare a proposal (either GRF or CRF) to further pursue this research topic.

661912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
661912.value: Atmospheric deposition is one of the sources of nutrient input to ocean, which is particularly important to areas where primary production (photosynthesis) is nutrient limited. Previous studies already show that event of high atmospheric deposition, such as dust storm, stimulate primary production and the growth of larger phytoplankton such as diatoms, whereas the abundance of the small primary producer and bacteria does not change too much. It is speculated that this may be due to that the micro-sized grazers (mainly single cell protists) were also stimulated and the grazing control kept the abundance of small cells low, but there has never been direct observation to prove that. We, for the first time, directly measured size-fractionated grazing rates in aerosol amended dilution experiments and demonstrated the decoupling of growth and grazing mortality in different size classes of bacteria and phytoplankton. Furthermore, we conducted meta-transcriptomics study to elucidate the physiological and functional response of microbial community to aerosol deposit at molecular level. Our results revealed the importance to include protist grazing when evaluating the effects of atmospheric deposition on marine planktonic ecosystems and to understand the molecular mechanisms of microbes in response increasing atmospheric input due to human activity and natural causes.

662012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662012.value: In the adult central nervous system (CNS), mature neurons lose the intrinsic capacity to regenerate injured axons. A model to study such mechanisms is the axon regeneration of dorsal root ganglia (DRG) neurons, which are able to regenerate peripheral, but not central branches in the adult spinal cord. However, a pre-conditioning lesion to the peripheral axons allows the subsequently injured central branches to grow into and beyond the lesion site. A possibility is that the peripheral lesion results in the delivery of putative positive signals to cell bodies to reactivate axon re-growth. Another possibility is that the lesion may also prevent the transduction of negative signals from peripheral targets of DRG axons to cell bodies. Our recent studies implicated TGF-beta/Activin family members as one type of negative signals for DRG neurons that inhibit their axon elongation, likely via the canonical Smad-mediated pathways. Thus, we hypothesize that the TGF-beta pathway may contribute to decreased regenerative ability in mature neurons in adults. A prediction of this hypothesis will be that relieving the inhibitory influences of TGF-beta signaling in these mature neurons may reprogram the neuronal growth states and allow efficient regeneration of adult neurons. In this proposed research, we will examine the role of the TGF-beta/Smad pathway in restricting axon regrowth ability in DRG neurons during development and after injury in adults. 中樞神經系統不能再生的一個重要機制是受損的神經元喪失軸突的再生能力。但軸突再生長能力控制機制並不是完全清楚。我們用背根神經節神經元作為一個模型來研究這種機制。背根神經節神經元能夠再生外周神經，但中樞端在成年脊髓是不能再生的。 一種可能性是，損傷區產生陽性信號以重新激活軸突再生。另一種可能性是損傷阻斷週抑制軸突再生負信號的轉導。我們最近的研究提示TGFbeta家族的成員，作為一種抑制信號， 有可能是通過Smad蛋白介導的途徑。因此，我們推測，TGFbeta信號通路可能降低成熟的神經細胞的軸突再生能力。 在這個研究中，我們將研究TGFbeta/Smad通路是否限制在發育過程中和損傷後的背根神經節神經元軸突再生能力。

662012.label: Realisation of objectives
662012.value: By using conditional knockout mice, we found that neither smad2 nor smad3 deletion in dorsal root ganglion neurons leads to significant axon growth defect during development. Thus we focused on the functions of Smad2/3 in the adult mice. Smad2 suppression in adult dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons promoted axon growth in culture. Both the longest and total axon length was increased. Smad3 suppression had modest effect. Combination of both did not have any additive effect. These results are consistent with our previous result that TGFbeta inhibitors can boost axon regeneration in vitro and in vivo. Part of the result has been submitted for publication. Thus, we have achieved our main aim to test the idea that Smad2/3 contribute axon regeneration of DRG neurons. In addition, we have also tested TGFbeta inhibitors and Smad2/3 inhibition in the optic nerve crush model. Very interestingly, we found Smad3 but not Smad2 inhibition in retinal ganglion cells can promote modest axon regeneration after injury. One of the TGFbeta inhibitors also boosted the regeneration. The findings suggested that TGFbeta/Smad signaling also play a role in the axon regeneration of central nervous system, indicating its more broad application in neural repair. In order for us to study the function of Smad2/3, we have established a replating DRG culture system. Through this system, we screened several compounds including more TGFbeta inhibitors and other compounds, to test whether they can promote axon growth in culture. One of the compounds can activate Gq signaling and promote axon branching of DRG neurons. We then tested it in the optic nerve model. This has lead to our recent finding on the role of Gq signaling in axon regeneration.

662012.value: 1. TGFbeta/Smad2/3 signaling contributes to axon regeneration of DRG neurons. Part of the study has been submitted for publication. 2. TGFbeta/Smad3 signaling contributes to axon regeneration of retinal ganglion cells in CNS. We are currently collecting more data and prepare for publication. 3. 662012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
662012.value: Our proof of principle experiments demonstrated that boosting the intrinsic growth capacity in neurons through modulating TGFbeta signaling enable axon regeneration in neurons of both peripheral and central nervous system. We are currently moving into two directions. One is to examine whether TGFbeta/Smad inhibition also has an effect in the corticospinal tract sprouting or regeneration. Second is to develop better compound to target TGFbeta signaling activity.

662012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
662012.value: The goal of this proposed study is to examine the role of TGF-beta/Smad signaling in restricting axon growth ability in peripheral DRG neurons, and render important insights into the mechanisms of molecular programs in central nervous system neurons. Our study illustrated that an important molecular pathway (TGF-beta/Smad) contributes to the diminished axon regeneration capacity in mature sensory neurons. This finding could potentially apply to other CNS neurons and leads to axon regeneration and even functional recovery after spinal cord injury.

662312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662312.value: Synapses are specialized cell membrane domains that facilitate neuronal communication. A major goal of current research in developmental neuroscience is to elucidate the mechanisms underlying how synapses are assembled. The nerve-muscle synapse, neuromuscular junction (NMJ), which controls all muscle movements, ranging from a simple eyelid movement to the vital breathing process, has been considered as the best model for the study of synaptogenesis due to its large size, simplicity and accessibility. The NMJ is comprised of the presynaptic nerve terminal, the postsynaptic muscle membrane, and the perisynaptic Schwann cells. In the postsynaptic membrane, acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) are highly concentrated for effective communication between presynaptic and postsynaptic cells. AChR is a ligand-gated ion channel which transduces the chemical signals, ACh, into an electrical signal, depolarization, and thereby triggers the actin potential that ultimately stimulates muscle contraction. Over the past decades, significant progress has been made to understand the signaling molecules and their signaling pathways involved in the anchoring and clustering of AChRs in the postsynaptic membrane at developing NMJs. However, the mechanisms underlying the dynamic trafficking of AChRs to/from the postsynaptic membrane remain unclear. Using the simple and elegant Xenopus primary culture system together with sophisticated imaging systems and manipulation techniques, this proposed study aims to understand a series of cell biology questions regarding the trafficking mechanisms of AChRs during the assembly and disassembly of the neuromuscular synapses. Furthermore, we will examine the pathogenic mechanisms of AChR endocytosis in myasthenia gravis, a neuromuscular disease characterized by the weakness of the skeletal muscle contraction. Taken together, the results of this proposed study should contribute to a better understanding on the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the development of synapses in general, and may also shed light on the pathogenesis of several neurological diseases, in which synaptic dysfunction is caused by aberrant changes in postsynaptic receptor trafficking. 突觸是促進神經元之間通信的結構。目前在發育神經科學的研究的一個主要目標是闡明突觸組裝的機制。由於其簡單構造和巨大尺寸, 神經肌肉突觸一直被視為研究突觸形成過程的好模式。乙酰膽鹼受體在此突觸後膜上呈現高度集中狀態，而這種受體群在突觸信息傳導是必需的。過去的幾十年裡，在了解信號分子和信號轉導途徑參與神經肌肉突觸發育過程中已經取得了顯著的進展，然而乙酰膽鹼受體在突觸後膜的動態機制仍不清楚。使用簡單而優雅的爪蟾原代培養系統與先進的成像系統，這項研究的目的是了解了一系列的細胞生物學有關乙酰膽鹼受體在神經肌肉突觸中組裝和拆卸的的問題。此外，我們將研究乙酰膽鹼受體的內吞作用在神經肌肉疾病例如重症肌無力發病機制上的關連。這頊研究結果應有助於更好地理解突觸發育中一般的細胞和分子機制，及由於突觸功能障礙引起的一些神經系統疾病的發病原因。

662612.label: Project Objectives
662612.value: To examine the expression and subcellular localization properties of MMG8 To examine the expression and subcellular localization patterns of MMG8 throughout the cell cycle, immunoblotting and immunofluorescence and time-lapse microscopy will be performed in conjunction with cell synchronization. Our preliminary data have suggested that MMG8 may target the Golgi apparatus through interaction with AKAP450. We will examine MMG8-AKAP450 binding properties, such as stoichiometry, binding domains, and potential direct interaction. RNAi-mediated depletion of AKAP450 or over-expression of the binding domains from MMG8 or AKAP450 will be performed to assess their effects on MMG8 localization. In addition, the subcellular localization of MMG8 mutants deficient of AKAP450-binding activities will be examined. These assays will reveal the role of AKAP450 in the Golgi localization of MMG8. To investigate the molecular basis of MMG8’s association with γTuCs We propose conducting experiments to investigate the following aspects of MMG8’s association with γTuCs. First, we will determine which γTuC is associated with MMG8. Sucrose gradient centrifugation will be performed to separate the γTuRC and the γTuSC and to determine the distribution pattern of MMG8. Following centrifugation, co-immunoprecipitation will be performed with the γTuRC and γTuSC fractions to assess their binding with MMG8. Second, we will delineate MMG8 sequence and structural elements involved in its association with γTuCs. The γTuC-binding domain will be analyzed and compared with those of known γTuC-binding proteins. Third, we will investigate how MMG8, AKAP450, and γTuCs interact with each other. These assays will provide information on how γTuCs are assembled with MMG8 and AKAP450 at the Golgi apparatus. To decipher the role of MMG8 in Golgi-associated microtubule organization and functions First, we will test whether MMG8 is required for γTuC’s attachment to the Golgi apparatus. Second, the role of MMG8 in the organization of Golgi-associated microtubules will be investigated. The patterns of microtubules and acetylated microtubules will be examined by immunofluorescence microscopy; microtubule dynamics will be evaluated by time-lapse microscopy. Third, we will explore the function of MMG8 in cellular activities that require Golgi-associated microtubules. In particular, we will assess directional cell migration in the scratch-wounding assay and evaluate protein trafficking using well-characterized cargos, such as the vesicular stomatitis virus ts045 glycoprotein. In the above assays, MMG8 expression will be inhibited by RNAi. Alternatively, the interaction between MMG8 and γTuCs will be disrupted by over-expression of the γTuC-binding domain of MMG8. The potential effects of such treatments will be evaluated to provide information on MMG8 functions.

662612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662612.value: 在高等真核細胞中，微管形成骨架結構調控細胞內物質的組織分布和運輸，進而在許多細胞功能中發揮至關重要的作用。微管在時間和空間上的分布主要由微管組織中心控制，例如中心體和高爾基體。這些微管組織中心的功能依賴存在於其中的一種高度保守的蛋白質，名為γ-微管蛋白。這種蛋白質與某些其他蛋白質形成複合體，以便啟動微管的組裝和定位微管陣的排列。然而，γ-微管蛋白複合體如何被運送至功能行使位點、以及在這些位點上的調控至今尚不清楚。 我們一直專注於研究細胞增殖、遷移及形態變化過程中微管骨架的調節分子機制。高爾基體是一種膜質細胞器，負責細胞內物質的分類和運輸，微管對其構建和定位有不可或缺的作用。最近，我們發現了一種新的蛋白質，命名為myomegalin異構體8（MMG8），並發現MMG8定位於順式高爾基網、以及與順式高爾基網結構蛋白AKAP450相互結合。MMG8還與γ-微管蛋白複合體相結合，並參與高爾基體上微管的形成。基於這些研究發現，我們推測MMG8由於結合AKAP450而定位於高爾基體，從而在建基於高爾基體並依賴γ-微管蛋白複合體的微管組織中發揮重要作用。本計劃書研究MMG8在高爾基體的定位特點、並探索MMG8參與高爾基體上微管組織的分子機制。我們設計了一系列的實驗達到以下目標：（1）檢查MMG8表達和細胞內定位的性質，（2）揭示MMG8與γ-微管蛋白複合體相結合的分子基礎，（3）闡明MMG8在高爾基體相關的微管組織和功能中的作用。以上研究將對高爾基體上微管組織的分子機制作出深入了解。 由於微管骨架在各種各樣的細胞活動中起關鍵作用，微管動態組織結構的調節是細胞生物學中的重要課題。此外，微管調節的異常已被證實與多種人類疾病包括癌症有關。因此，本研究計劃的成果將不僅有助於了解微管和高爾基體相關的細胞活動的分子機制，也可能為開發新的治療方法提供靶點。

662612.label: Realisation of objectives
662612.value: Objective #1. To examine the expression and subcellular localization properties of MMG8 We have fulfilled this objective by demonstrating the expression and localization patterns of myomegalin isoform 8 (MMG8). Although there are several splicing variant sequences of myomegalin, MMG8 is the only myomegalin protein detected in epithelial cells and fibroblasts. We developed antibodies that specifically recognize MMG8, and performed immunostaining experiments. MMG8 was specifically stained to the cis-side of the Golgi complex in interphase, and was localized to the Golgi particles after Golgi disassembly in mitosis and to the Golgi twins during cytokinesis. We then examined whether the Golgi localization is dynamic by cell treatment at 15C for 3 h. Under this condition, endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-to-Golgi trafficking is reduced and thus proteins that recycle between the ER and the Golgi accumulate in the pre-Golgi compartments. Whereas the treatment delocalized MMG8 from the Golgi, the Golgi localization of GM130, a Golgi matrix protein, was unaffected. We then rewarmed the cells to 37C and found that MMG8 regained its Golgi localization. These results indicated that MMG8 undergoes ER-to-Golgi transport and exhibits a dynamic localization at the Golgi. We identified the Golgi-localizing mechanism of MMG8 and revealed that MMG8 is attached to the Golgi through interacting with the cis-Golgi protein AKAP450. Using co-immunoprecipitation and quantitative immunoblotting, we detected that MMG8 and AKAP450 formed a stoichiometric complex in the cell extracts. Furthermore, the physical association is required for the stability of both proteins: suppressing MMG8 expression led to a proportional reduction in the protein level of AKAP450 and vice versa. We mapped the AKAP450-binding site to 1–389 of MMG8. When transiently expressed, 1–389 exhibited Golgi patterns. By contrast, the expression of 389–1116 did not display any Golgi localization. Therefore, 1–389 serves as the AKAP450-binding and Golgi-targeting domain in MMG8. It has been shown that Golgi-targeting domain has been delineated in AKAP450 to 159–463. When over-expressed, this AKAP450 domain delocalized both AKAP450 and MMG8 from the Golgi complex. We also performed RNAi-mediated depletion of MMG8 and AKAP450 one at a time and treated the cells with the proteasome inhibitor MG132 to prevent the degradation of the nontargeted protein. Whereas AKAP450 depletion inhibited MMG8 localization to the Golgi, MMG8 depletion did not markedly affect the Golgi localization of AKAP450. Altogether, we conclude that MMG8 is targeted to the Golgi through its binding to AKAP450. Objective #2. To investigate the molecular basis of MMG8’s association with γTuCs To address this objective, we performed co-immunoprecipitation assays. Anti-MMG8 immunoprecipitation co-immunoprecipitated γTuCs, which were detected in the immunoprecipitates by immunoblotting of the TuC core components -tubulin and GCP2. In a reciprocal experiment, the immunoprecipitation of γTuCs through anti-GCP3 immunoprecipitation co-precipitated MMG8. In animal cells, there are two γTuCs of distinct sizes, the γ-tubulin small complex (γTuSC) and the γ-tubulin ring complex (γTuRC), which can be separated by using sucrose-gradient (e.g. 5–40% sucrose) centrifugation. We carried out sucrose-gradient centrifugation of MMG8-transfected cell extracts and then immunoprecipitated the ectopically expressed MMG8. MMG8 co-immunoprecipitated TuC components from the γTuRC fractions, whereas the co-immunoprecipitation was not detectable from the γTuSC fractions. Next, we examined whether γTuRC disassembly affects the association of MMG8 with γTuCs. In this assay, γTuRCs were disassembled by silencing the expression of GCP4, a γTuRC component that is required for the complex assembly. The disassembly of γTuRC abolished the coimmunoprecipitation of MMG8 with γ-tubulin and other γTuC components. Together, these two lines of evidence indicate that MMG8 associates with γTuRCs, but does not associate with γTuSCs. We proceeded to delineate the γTuC-binding domain. Various MMG8 regions were cloned and ectopically expressed in mammalian cells for testing their co-immunoprecipitation of γTuCs. We found that γTuCs were co-immunoprecipitated with the fragment 1–389, but was not found in the immunoprecipitate of the region 389–1116. Therefore, γTuCs bind to the amino-terminal region of MMG8. Further truncation of 1–389 eliminated the γTuC-binding activity. These results suggest that the structure formed by 1–389 is required for γTuC binding. It has been known that AKAP450 is required for microtubule nucleation at the Golgi complex (Rivero et al., EMBO J. 2009, 28, 1016-1028). We investigated whether AKAP450 is involved in MMG8 association with γTuCs. To prepare AKAP450-free MMG8, MMG8 was ectopically expressed and then immunoprecipitated under a stringent condition (e.g. radioimmunoprecipitation assay buffer to dissociate AKAP450 and γTuCs from MMG8). The immunoprecipitated MMG8 protein was subjected to a pull-down assay from the extracts of cells transfected with akap450-targeting or control siRNA. Immunoblotting of the pulldowns showed that MMG8 exhibited similar γTuC-binding activities in the control and the AKAP450-depleted extracts. These results revealed that MMG8 associates with γTuCs in a manner independent of AKAP450. Objective #3. To decipher the role of MMG8 in Golgi-associated microtubule organization and functions We have fulfilled this objective by performing the following assays. First, we suppressed MMG8 expression and examined its effect on the Golgi localization of γ-tubulin, the key component of γTuCs. In MMG8-depleted cells, the Golgi attachment of γ-tubulin was abolished without any significant effect on the centrosomal staining of γ-tubulin. These data revealed that MMG8 is required for the recruitment of γTuCs to the Golgi apparatus but is dispensable for their recruitment to centrosomes. Second, we examined Golgi-based microtubule nucleation in the microtubule regrowth assay, which assesses microtubule nucleation after microtubule depolymerization. After microtubule depolymerization under a cold condition (i.e. 4°C) or nocodazole treatment, microtubule regrowth was initiated by transferring the cell cultures to 37°C and nocodazole washout, respectively, and the regrowth was monitored. The RNAi-mediated depletion of MMG8 inhibited Golgi-based microtubule regrowth, whereas the depletion did not affect centrosome-based regrowth. Therefore, MMG8 is required for microtubule nucleation at the Golgi complex. Third, we assayed ER-to-Golgi trafficking of a well-characterized cargo, vesicular stomatitis virus ts045 glycoprotein (VSVG). At 40°C, VSVG is misfolded and thus retained in the ER; however, shifting cells to 32°C allows the protein to fold correctly, which results in its export from the ER and subsequent transport along microtubules to the Golgi. By 40 min after shifting to 32°C, most of the VSVG exhibited Golgi localization in control cells. In contrast, the localization of VSVG to the Golgi was significantly delayed in the cells depleted of MMG8 by RNAi. VSVG acquires linkage to oligosaccharides in the medial Golgi, which confers resistance to the cleavage of VSVG by endoglycosidase H (Endo H). The MMG8 depletion markedly delayed the acquisition of Endo-H resistance, which is consistent with the delay of VSVG trafficking to the Golgi. Collectively, we conclude that MMG8 participates in efficient ER-to-Golgi trafficking that requires Golgi-derived microtubules. Forth, we performed a scratch-wounding assay to assess the role of MMG8 in cell polarization and directional migration. Notably, RNAi-mediated MMG8 depletion reduced cell migration into the wound. To gain insights into the migration defect, we monitored Golgi reorientation in the assay and found that over a few hours after scratch wounding, the MMG8-depleted cells showed drastically lower fractions with their Golgi reoriented toward the leading edge than did the control cells. These results suggest that MMG8 functions in cell polarization and directional migration by regulating the organization of Golgi-derived microtubules.

662612.label: Major findings and research outcome
662612.value: In this study, we identified myomegalin variant 8 (MMG8) to be a novel protein encoded by the multispliced myomegalin gene and found that MMG8 is the only myomegalin isoform expressed in proliferating epithelial and fibroblast cells. MMG8 localizes at the Golgi complex and interacts with the cis-Golgi protein AKAP450. Furthermore, most cellular MMG8 and AKAP450 bind to each other to form a stoichiometric complex. The interaction between MMG8 and AKAP450 has the following functional significances. First, the binding is required for the stability of both proteins. Removal of MMG8 and AKAP450 could be regulated by disruption of the MMG8-AKAP450 interaction, which leads to degradation of both proteins by the proteasome-dependent pathway. Second, MMG8 requires its interaction with AKAP450 for Golgi localization. Both MMG8 and AKAP450 are transported from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi, where the complex is incorporated into the cis-side through the binding of AKAP450 to the matrix protein GM130. In animal cells, the Golgi complex is a major microtubule-organizing center and this Golgi function depends on the presence of γ-tubulin ring complexes (γTuRCs), the principal microtubule nucleators. We demonstrated that MMG8 interacts with γTuRCs through its amino-terminal region and participates in the Golgi attachment of TuRCs. Although myomegalin shows sequence homology to the TuRC stimulator CDK5RAP2, MMG8 does not contain the conserved TuRC-binding domain and the centrosome-targeting domain found in CDK5RAP2, implying that these two proteins have distinct cellular functions. While CDK5RAP2 is involved in centrosomal organization and functions, MMG8 acts at the Golgi in several functions, including microtubule organization at the Golgi, Golgi assembly and structural organization, ER-to-Golgi trafficking, and cell polarization and directional migration. We also identified that MMG8 associates with the microtubule end-binding proteins EB1 and EB3 and contains the EB1/EB3-binding SxIP motif. Moreover, MMG8 is required for the Golgi attachment of EB1/EB3. Interestingly, the function of MMG8 in ER-to-Golgi trafficking requires its binding with EB1/EB3 and thus the attachment of EB1/EB3 to the Golgi. These results indicate that MMG8 captures microtubule tips at the Golgi through its bound EB1/EB3. In summary, this reported work identified a novel Golgi protein that is involved in microtubule organization at the Golgi. These findings represent a substantial advance in understanding microtubule organization and microtubule-dependent events in animal cells. Several research articles have been published or are being prepared for publication based on the findings from this study along with the training of postgraduate students.

662612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
662612.value: We have found that MMG8 and AKAP450 undergo trafficking from the ER to the Golgi complex and localize at the Golgi in a dynamic manner. ER-to-Golgi transport of proteins and membranes is selectively directed by coat protein complex (COP) II vesicles. To gain mechanistic insights into the trafficking of MMG8 and AKAP450, we will explore their association with COP II coat proteins and investigate whether MMG8 and AKAP450 are transported by COP II vesicles. We anticipate that the trafficking analysis will help understanding the homeostasis of MMG8 and AKAP450 at the Golgi complex. In addition to AKAP450 and MMG8, the Golgi-associated proteins CDK5RAP2 and CLASPs have been known as important players in Golgi microtubule formation. We have also found that MMG8 binds to the End Binding (EB) proteins and contains the EB-binding SxIP motif. We will explore the mechanisms of microtubule nucleation, stabilization, and attachment at the Golgi complex and will dissect the functions of AKAP450, MMG8, CDK5RAP2, CLASPs, and EBs in the organization of Golgi-derived microtubules. This work will show how a complex interplay among these different factors controls the microtubule-organizing function of the Golgi, which plays a crucial role in several cellular activities, including cell polarization.

662612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
662612.value: In addition to centrosomes, the Golgi complex has emerged as a major microtubule-organizing center, which is the site responsible for the initiation of microtubule growth and for microtubule attachment, and the microtubule-organizing function of the Golgi is particularly important for vesicle trafficking and cell polarization, movement, and differentiation. The research work presented in this report identified a widely expressed isoform of the little-characterized muscle protein myomegalin and demonstrated the function of this novel isoform, designated as myomegalin variant 8 (MMG8), in microtubule organization at the Golgi. MMG8 is transported from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi and is integrated into the Golgi by interacting with the Golgi protein AKAP450. At the Golgi, MMG8 participates in the attachment of -tubulin complexes, the protein complexes that initiate microtubule growth and mediate microtubule attachment, and thus functions in the organization of Golgi-derived microtubules. Furthermore, MMG8 is indispensable for Golgi structural organization, efficient ER-to-Golgi trafficking, and cell polarization and directional migration. Collectively, this work revealed the role of MMG8 in microtubule organization at the Golgi and provided evidence on the molecular mechanisms of MMG8’s function and regulation at the Golgi. These findings provided new insights into the control of various Golgi-dependent cellular events.

663012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
663012.value: 在脊椎動物的大腦中，乙醯膽鹼酯酶（AChE）依靠跨膜蛋白PRiMA，以四聚體（G4）的形式，錨定在細胞膜上。這種組合需要AChE催化亞基（AChET）中C末端的“t-多肽”參與形成。雖然成熟的AChE 是N段糖基化蛋白已為人熟知，但是糖基化在PRiMA連接的AChE四聚體（G4AChE）複合物的形成過程中所起的作用尚未見研究報道。在大鼠與雞的大腦中，已發現兩種類型的AChE四聚體：完全糖基化AChE（H敏感型）與部分糖基化AChE（H敏感型）。已發現，AChET N端糖基化對形成具有酶活性的AChE至關重要，但是對其聚合體形成過程並無影響。去除糖基的G4AChE酶活性極低，並且集中於內質網（ER）中。利用糖基化變異形式的AChET，我們想鑒定出大腦中G4AChE在內質網與高爾基體中組合時結合的蛋白（有可能是分子伴侶）。與具有酶活性的完全糖基化的AChE相比，去糖基化的四聚體AChE的降解，有可能是由特定的分子伴侶進行調控的。此外，我們推測，在老年癡呆等疾病的病理狀態下，去糖基化的G4AChE可能在內質網中出現聚集。因此，關於G4AChE在大腦中裝配及修飾過程的研究，不僅能為瞭解AchE的調控提供更多的參考，而且有助於發現其酶催化以外的作用。對於AChE裝配過程分子機理的探索，也將為其他分泌蛋白的研究，提供全新的研究模型，開辟嶄新的研究方向。

663012.label: Realisation of objectives
663012.value: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE), a heavily N-glycosylated enzyme, is responsible for the hydrolysis of acetylcholine at the cholinergic synapses. In vertebrates, AChE possesses alternative C-terminal R or H or T peptide, which defines its post-translational maturation, quaternary association, and anchoring. AChET carries various amounts of N-linked carbohydrate side chains attached to the core polypeptide. Glycosylation is probably a useful marker for the progression of AChE forms through different subcellular compartments, since it is known that the glycans adding in the ER are remodeled and matured in the Golgi apparatus. Once assembled, these catalytically active AChE oligomers were stable. After acquiring complex oligosaccharides in the Golgi apparatus, they are transported to the plasma membrane or secreted. N-linked glycans of AChE are employed as both maturation and quality control tags that dictate the destination of this enzyme. Since a large number of human neuronal diseases involve defective protein folding and maturation of AChE, an understanding of AChE biosynthesis is essential. Objectives: [1] To determine the stability of normal and glycan-defective PRiMA-linked G4 AChE. [2] To investigate the regulatory mechanisms for the protein trafficking of PRiMA-linked G4 AChE. [3] To reveal the relationship between glycan-defective PRiMA-linked AChE and neuronal cell death. AChE is known to have a precise biosynthetic pathway and to interact with PRiMA in forming PRiMA-linked G4 AChE. The glycosylation has been demonstrated to affect the protein trafficking of this enzyme; however, the exact molecular mechanisms of how the glycans of AChE affect the trafficking of the G4 complex are still unknown. Here, we hypothesize that the newly synthesized PRiMA-linked G4 AChE in neurons interacts with chaperons, possibly via recognizing the glycans on the enzyme, which directs the complex trafficking from the ER to the Golgi apparatus and finally anchor on the plasma membrane.
