663012.label: Major findings and research outcome
663012.value: [1] By site-directed mutagenesis, we have determined both AChE catalytic subunit and PRiMA subunit are fully glycosylated. Glycosylation of AChE subunit affects its enzymatic activity, significantly. The glycan-depleted AChE has a much higher Km value than that of the wild-type enzyme. The absence of N-linked glycosylation on PRiMA appears not to affect its function in allowing its duties to form a functional G4 AChE. PRiMA is able to mediate the transport of AChE subunit to Golgi apparatus from ER, and which allows the enzyme to achieve higher-complexity of glycosylation. [2] The post-translational modification of glycosylation is not essential for enzyme assembly. The glycan depleted AChE is able to form oligomers in the ER, but not stable. We propose: (i) the deprivation of N-glycosylation leads to incorrect folding of AChE subunit mutant, and thus the formed oligomer dissociates into monomers; (ii) the mutant is less capable of assembling into oligomer in comparison with the wild-type. [3] Glycan-depleted AChE is not able to traffic from ER to Golgi. Several species of AChE, ranging from ~68 to ~76 kDa, are formed in neurons, muscles and other cell types. This phenomenon is due to the different types of glycans acquired by AChE during trafficking from ER to Golgi; while AChE synthesized in the Golgi bores complex glycan chains. The glycosylation of PRiMA in G4 AChE was not required; AChE oligomer transport requires a membrane-bound linkage. [4] The analysis of AChE subunit mutants by transiently expressing defective of single or all N-glycosylation sites in cultured HEK293T cells suggests: (i) the enzymatic activities of AChE-N296Q or AChE-N495 Q accounts 40~50 % of AChE, whereas the enzymatic activity of AChE-N381Q or glycan-depleted AChE has less than 5%; (ii) the glycan composition within three glycosylation sites are similar; (iii) there is no preference on the site of glycosylation of AChE; (iv) the glycosylation at Asn-381 position plays important function on correct enzyme conformation, as well as activity. [5] Over expression of glycan-depleted AChE causes aggregation of inactive enzyme in ER in neurons, muscle and other cell types. Prolong aggregation of AChE leads to cell death. In neurons, tacrine (an AChE inhibitor) blocks AChE activity and suppresses the transcription ACHE. Besides, the folding of AChE oligomer in the ER is very sensitive to the presence of tacrine. The mechanistic studies are carried out at this stage, the mechanisms of the G4 AChE in neuronal cell death will be determined.

663012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663012.value: AChE is a glycoprotein possessing three conserved N-linked glycosylation sites in mammalian species, locating at 296, 381, and 495 residues of the human sequence. Glycosylation at Asn-381 of AChE should play important role on proper folding of AChE, as to achieve full enzymatic activity. However, different N-glycosylation sites contribute similarly to glycan composition of AChE. Also, N-glycosylation of AChEH showed significance effect in controlling the biosynthesis of AChEH dimer form. PRiMA is a glycoprotein containing two putative N-linked glycosylation sites. By using sitedirected mutagenesis, the asparagine-43 was identified to be the N-linked glycosylation site of PRiMA. Abolishing glycosylation on mouse PRiMA appeared not to affect its assembly with AChET, the enzymatic properties of AChE, and the membrane trafficking of PRiMA-linked AChE tetramers. This result is contrary to the reports that glycosylation is essential for conformation and trafficking of membrane glycoproteins.

663112.label: Project Title(Chinese)
663112.value: 香港海域鱼类汞的污染来源和生物动力学

663112.label: Project Objectives
663112.value: To identify the sources of mercury contamination and the geochemical speciation of mercury in Hong Kong sediments; To study the subcellular fate and ecotoxicological relevance of mercury in Hong Kong’s coastal fish; To reveal the biodynamic mechanisms underlying the inter-species and inter-site differences in Hg accumulation in marine fish.
rows: To identify the sources of mercury contamination and the geochemical speciation of mercury in Hong Kong sediments;
To study the subcellular fate and ecotoxicological relevance of mercury in Hong Kong’s coastal fish;

663112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
663112.value: Toxic mercury is among the major contaminants in seafood, marine organisms, and marine ecosystems. Mercury contamination has become a major environmental problem of which the public and the governments must collectively resolve. In Hong Kong, mercury is of utmost concern in the marine environments. It is well known that mercury (especially its organic form: methylmercury) is biomagnified at the top of marine food chains (such as in marine fish). Although the general public in Hong Kong is aware of the potentially dire impacts of elevated metal contamination in Hong Kong’s waters, our explicit understanding of the biological and environmental behaviors of mercury in Hong Kong waters remains poor. Understanding the complexity of how different marine organisms handle Hg and how such handling affects Hg toxicity is extremely challenging. Such complexity is further augmented by the very complicated but unique hydrographic conditions in Hong Kong. Our preliminary studies found that there are large inter-site and inter-species differences in Hg concentrations in marine fish within a rather narrow geographical distance in Hong Kong. There have also been constant debates on the possible sources of mercury in marine fish in Hong Kong. This proposed project will therefore specifically study several fundamental and pressing questions surrounding mercury ecotoxicology and biogeochemistry: 1) the sources of mercury contamination and the geochemical speciation of mercury in Hong Kong sediments; 2) the subcellular fate and ecotoxicological relevance of mercury in Hong Kong’s coastal fish; 3) the biodynamic mechanisms underlying the inter-species and inter-site differences in mercury accumulation in marine fish. We will work on different marine fish with different feeding habits, and from different populations in Hong Kong. The ecotoxicological significances of different subcellular mercury in marine fish (e.g., biological detoxification, bioaccessibility to human consumers) will be studied. This project will take advantage of the several unique analytical techniques and equipments (e.g., multiple collector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, cold vapor atomic fluorescence spectrometry, gamma radiotracers) available in our laboratories to tackle these challenging problems. We anticipate that this effort will take our understanding of mercury in coastal environments to a higher academic level and will help environmental regulators develop polices to protect our coastal environment. The long-term goals of our project will be to understand the fates of this toxic metal and their impacts on Hong Kong’s ecosystems, and to provide scientific advice to regulatory agencies and industries for better management of mercury in the marine environment. 汞是存在于海产品、海洋生物及海洋生态系统中的主要污染物之一。而汞污染问题业已成为需要公众和政府部门共同解决的一个主要环境问题。在香港，汞是海洋环境中最受关注的问题。汞，特别是其有机形态甲基汞，通过生物放大在海洋食物链顶端（例如海洋鱼类）富集是为我们所熟知的。尽管香港的民众已经意识到香港水体中攀升的金属污染的潜在巨大危害，但对汞在水体中的生物和环境行为仍缺乏清晰的了解。理解不同海洋生物如何调控体内金属以及此种机制如何影响其毒性极具挑战。而香港特有的水文条件则增加了这些调控机制的复杂性。 我们之前的研究表明即使在香港这样一个很小的地理范围内，不同位置以及不同种类的海洋鱼类体内的汞浓度都存在巨大差异。对于这些汞的可能来源仍然存在争议。因此，本项目将围绕汞的生态毒理学和生物地球化学的几个基本问题展开研究：1）香港海域的汞污染源及其沉积物中汞的主要化学形态；2）香港沿海水域中汞的亚细胞分布及生态毒理学相关性质；3）造成海洋鱼类汞积累的种间及空间差异的动力学机制。我们将以香港不同栖息环境中的不同海洋鱼类为研究对象，利用目前本实验室特有的几个分析技术和设备（多接收电感耦合等离子体质谱，冷原子荧光光谱，伽玛放射性示踪技术）来探索并研究解决诸如汞在海洋鱼类体内的亚细胞分布及生态毒理学相关特性（金属解毒组分，金属食物链传递可利用组分）等重要问题。我们期望我们的努力能够使对于汞在沿海环境中的理解达到新的学术高度，并有助于环境监管部门制定相关政策以保护环境。本项目的长期目标是理解汞的归趋及其对香港生态系统的影响，为监管部门和生产部门更好的控制此种有毒金属提供科学依据。

663112.label: Realisation of objectives
663112.value: Objective 1: To identify the sources of mercury contamination and the geochemical speciation of mercury in Hong Kong sediments; In this task, we analyzed the concentrations and isotopic compositions of mercury in surface sediments of the Pearl River Estuary to reveal the sources and geochemical processes of Hg in subtropical estuarine and oceanic environments. Relevant geochemical properties such as the organic matter content and percentage of fine particles were also determined. We generally found that the PRE sediments have elevated Hg concentrations compared to those in South China Sea (SCS), indicating significant contamination of Hg in the estuary. There were large spatial variations in both mass-dependent fractionation and mass-independent fractionation of Hg isotopes in the sediments of PRE. The spatial variations of Hg isotopes in sediments reflect three dominant sources of Hg, including industrial waste discharge, continental erosion input, and regional marine background. A triple mixing model indicated that both anthropogenic discharge and continental erosion were the dominant Hg sources to sediments in the river mouth and in the middle of PRE, while regional marine background was the dominant Hg source in the outer part of PRE and ocean sediments in SCS (Yin et al. 2015). We further conducted an experiment (Xu et al. 2016) in the Tibetan Plateau in a mountainous region isolated from direct anthropogenic sources. Mercury concentrations and stable isotopes of carbon, nitrogen, and mercury were analyzed in sediments and biota for Nam Co and Yamdrok Lake. The primary source of methylmercury was microbial production in local sediments despite the lack of direct methylmercury input. Strong ultraviolet intensity led to extensive photochemical reactions and up to 65% of methylmercury in water was photo-demethylated before entering the food webs. This is the first mercury isotope study on high altitude lake ecosystems that demonstrated efficient biomagnification and specific isotope fractionations of mercury under extreme environmental conditions. Objective 2: To study the subcellular fate and ecotoxicological relevance of mercury in Hong Kong’s coastal fish; Extensive studies were conducted in this task. In one study, Wang et al. (2013) investigated the in vivo methylation and demethylation processes in fish after dietary exposure to mercury. This study demonstrates the important role of organ- and species-specific biodynamics in understanding mercury transformation and speciation in fish. The observed in vivo methylation process in tilapia was slow, suggesting that the high %MeHg in fish was likely derived from MeHg ingestion instead of in vivo transformation. Wang and Wang (2015) developed for the first time a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to simulate the uptake, distribution and elimination of inorganic mercury [Hg(II)] and methylmercury (MeHg) in a marine fish. Modeling simulation for the first time demonstrated that the gill was the most important route in Hg(II) elimination in marine fish, with a rate constant of 0.90 d-1. This study showed that the PBPK modeling provided critical information for the uptake, distribution and elimination of Hg(II) and MeHg in the fish body, especially in elucidating the role of each compartment. Wu and Wang (2013) examined the Hg dynamics at the bottom of food chains, namely, marine phytoplankton. We quantified the changes in the Hg(II) or MeHg sensitivity, Hg accumulation, subcellular distribution, as well as thiol compounds induction in the diatoms. This study suggested that moderation of Hg bioavailability was probably more important than internal detoxification in the development of Hg acclimation in marine diatoms. In another study, Wu and Wang (2014) examined the ability of three marine phytoplankton species to detoxify Hg. We found that all algae tested were able to transform Hg(II) into dissolved gaseous mercury (DGM), phytochelatins (PCs) complexes and metacinnabar (β-HgS). These results suggest that intracellular biotransformation might be more important than bioavailability regulation in Hg(II) detoxification in marine phytoplankton. To further understand the implication of Hg isotopic fractionation in source tracking for Hg accumulation in marine fish, Yin et al. (2016) analyzed the mercury stable isotopic compositions in 18 species of marine wild fish from the PRE. Compared with the Hg isotopic compositions of the PRE sediments, marine fish showed significantly higher δ202Hg and Δ199Hg values. The quantified Δ199Hg/Δ201Hg of ~1.26 in fish suggested the photo-degradation of MeHg in the water column prior to its incorporation into the food chain. The data showed for the first time the distinct signatures of mass independent fractionation (MIF) among herbivorous, demersal and carnivorous fish, indicating that different fish species may have incorporated MeHg from various sources with different degrees of photo-demethylation. Xu and Wang (2015) determined the fractionation of mercury (Hg) stable isotopes in a marine fish during the uptake and elimination of Hg(II) from aqueous and dietary sources. We found a mass-dependent fractionation (MDF, quantified by δ202Hg) during the trophic transfer and aqueous uptake of Hg(II), attributable to the biotranformation of Hg. We concluded that Hg stable isotope ratios can be used to trace sources and exposure pathways (aqueous or dietary) as well as to study complicated metabolic processes of Hg in fish. Objective 3: To reveal the biodynamic mechanisms underlying the inter-species and inter-site differences in Hg accumulation in marine fish. Zhu et al. (2013) conducted a large-scale investigation of methylmercury (MeHg) in a total of 614 marine wildﬁsh covering 45 different species collected from the SCS. Biological and ecological characteristics such as size (length and wet weight), feeding habit, habitat, and stable isotope (δ15N) were examined to explain MeHg bioaccumulation in marine fish and their geographical distribution. Feeding habit and habitat were the primary factors inﬂuencing MeHg bioaccumulation. Pan et al. (2014) conducted comprehensive evaluation of total Hg (THg) and methylmercury (MeHg) concentrations in wild marine fish from the PRE. Our results showed that the Hg levels were generally low in the coastal fish, which may be related to the reduced size and accelerated growth rate of the fish due to overfishing. Body size appears to be the dominant factor controlling the interspecific and intraspecific differences in Hg concentrations in the fish. δ13C signatures revealed that fish communities had contrasting carbon sources, which may be responsible for the habitat-specific Hg concentrations. Zhang et al. (2015) collected 166 wild fish samples of 13 species from 13 rivers and lakes across the southern Tibetan Pleteau. Hg concentrations varied greatly within and between species. The long lifespan and slow growth of the fish under the low-productivity environments may be the major biological factors that help to build up the fish Hg levels comparable to those observed in wild fish growing in human-impacted areas. Finally, Peng et al. (2016) conducted laboratory experiments to reveal the mechanisms underlying the low accumulation of Hg in rabbitfish. The results showed that the efflux rate constants of Hg(II) and MeHg were probably the highest ones recorded in fish thus far. Subcellular distribution indicated that some specific membrane proteins in muscle were the primary binding pools for MeHg, and both metallothionein-like proteins and Hg-rich granules were important components in the elimination of both MeHg and Hg(II). The low tissue Hg concentration in the rabbitfish was partly explained by its unique biokinetics.

663112.label: Major findings and research outcome
663112.value: In total, 12 papers were published and all of them are in top international journals (ES&T, Environ Pollut, Chemosphere, Sci Reports, Aquat Toxicol). Some of the major findings are summarized below: PRE sediments have elevated Hg concentrations. The spatial variations of Hg isotopes in sediments reflect three dominant sources of Hg, including industrial waste discharge, continental erosion input, and regional marine background. A triple mixing model indicated that both anthropogenic discharge and continental erosion were the dominant Hg sources to sediments in the river mouth and in the middle of PRE, while regional marine background was the dominant Hg source in the outer part of PRE. At high altitudes, primary source of methylmercury was microbial production in local sediments despite the lack of direct methylmercury input. In marine fish, in vivo methylation and demethylation processes were slow, suggesting that the high %MeHg in fish was mainly derived from MeHg ingestion instead of in vivo transformation. Development of a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model for the first time demonstrated that the gill was the most important route in Hg(II) elimination in marine fish. In marine phytoplankton, moderation of Hg bioavailability was probably more important than internal detoxification in the development of Hg acclimation in marine diatoms. Intracellular biotransformation was more important than bioavailability regulation in Hg(II) detoxification. There are distinct signatures of MIF among herbivorous, demersal and carnivorous fish, indicating that different fish species may have incorporated MeHg from various sources with different degrees of photo-demethylation. Laboratory experiments demonstrated that Hg stable isotope ratios can be used to trace sources and exposure pathways as well as to study complicated metabolic processes of Hg in fish. In South China Sea, biological and ecological characteristics such as size, feeding habit, habitat, and stable isotope (δ15N) explained the MeHg bioaccumulation in marine fish and their geographical distribution. Fish from the PRE generally contained low Hg levels, which may be related to the reduced size and accelerated growth rate of the fish. Body size appears to be the dominant factor controlling the interspecific and intraspecific differences in Hg concentrations in the fish. Carbon sources may be responsible for the habitat-specific Hg concentrations. In fish from high altitudes, the long lifespan and slow growth may be the major biological factors that help to build up the fish Hg levels. Laboratory experiments showed that the unique biokinetics was responsible for the low tissue Hg concentration in the rabbitfish.

663112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
663112.value: There are certainly great potential for further development of the research, including the further application of Hg stable isotopes in source tracking of Hg in the environment and in fish, the development of the PBPK model in understanding the methylation and demethylation of Hg in marine fish, and the understanding of the molecular basis for low Hg accumulation in certain species of fish. These are the topics for further research.

663112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663112.value: Toxic mercury is among the major contaminants in seafood and marine ecosystems. Mercury contamination has become a major environmental problem of which the public and governments must collectively resolve. In Hong Kong, mercury is of utmost concern in the marine environments. Although the general public in Hong Kong is aware of the potentially dire impacts of elevated metal contamination in Hong Kong’s waters, our explicit understanding of the biological and environmental behaviors of mercury in Hong Kong waters remains poor. Understanding the complexity of how different marine organisms handle metals and how such handling affects metal toxicity is extremely challenging. Such complexity is further augmented by the very complicated but unique hydrographic conditions in Hong Kong. This project takes advantage of the several unique analytical techniques and equipment (e.g., multiple collector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, cold vapor atomic fluorescence spectrometry, gamma radiotracers) to tackle these challenging problems. The project provides important understanding of the environmentally and biologically complex behavior of mercury in marine systems. The outcomes are particularly important for the regulation and risk management of Hg in the marine system by government agencies.

663212.label: Realisation of objectives
663212.value: We have managed to complete all of three objectives proposed in this proposal. 1. To confirm the cebpαhkz7 mutant phenotype is caused by the loss of Cebpα function: To confirm the myeloid phenotypes are caused by the loss of Cebpα function, we first carried out a rescue experiment, in which in vitro synthesized wild-type cebpα mRNA were injected into 1-cell stage of fertilized cebpαhkz7 mutant embryos and asked if reconstitution of wild-type cebpα could rescue the myeloid phenotype. However, the ectopic expression of Cebpα by simple mRNA injection caused severe abnormality during early embryogenesis, thereby preventing us from analyzing the development of myeloid cells. We then decided to generate additional cebpα mutant allele by targeting the cebpα gene locus using the CRISPR/Cas9 approach. We identified two additional cebpα mutant alleles harboring premature codon in the coding region. Phenotypic analysis showed that the two cebpα mutant alleles displayed similar myeloid defects. These data confirm that the cebpαhkz7 mutant phenotype is indeed caused by the loss of Cebpα function. 2. To elucidate the cellular basis underlying the embryonic myeloid defects in cebpαhkz7 mutants: To dissect the cellular basis leading to the loss of embryonic macrophages and neutrophils in cebpαhkz7 mutants, we first monitored the expression of pu.1, a marker for myeloid progenitor cells, and we found that the pu.1 expression was intact at 14 hpf in the RBI region where embryonic myelopoiesis is known to emerge. However, myeloid progenitors began to decline from 22 hpf onwards and became undetectable at later stages. From these data, we conclude that Cebpα is required for the maintenance and survival of myeloid progenitors but dispensable for their specification. Subsequent BrdU incorporation assay and TUNEL staining showed that, while apoptotic myeloid progenitors remained rarely detectable, a 2-3 fold increase of BrdU+ myeloid progenitors (as indicated by BrdU/Pu.1 double staining) was found in cepbahkz7 mutants. The increase of BrdU+ myeloid progenitors appeared to be accompanied with a slight decrease of the phospho-Histone 3 (pH3) positive myeloid progenitors, we conclude that the myeloid progenitors in cepbahkz7 mutants are arrested at the S phase of cell cycle, resulting in gradually loss of the myeloid progenitors. 3. To define the genetic relationship between Cebpα and Pu.1, Cebpα and Runx1 in embryonic myelopoiesis: To further dissect the genetic relation between Cebpα and Pu.1 as well as Cebpα and Runx1 during embryonic myelopoiesis, we outcrossed cepbahkz7 fish with runx1w84x mutants, in which the embryonic neutrophils are significantly reduced but not completely absent. And we found that the numbers of mature neutrophils but not macrophages were further reduced in cepba+/hkz7runx1w84x/w84x hetero-homozygous double embryos, indicating that Cebpα plays a critical role in embryonic neutrophil development, presumably the maintenance of mature neutrophils. We were not be able to assay the relationship between Cebpα and Pu.1 because these two genes are localize very closely on the same chromosome, thereby preventing us from generating cebpα/pu.1 double mutants. But we did show that MO knockdown of pu.1 expression in cepbahkz7 mutant fish failed to block the initiation of embryonic myelopoiesis. These observations suggest that both Cebpα and Pu.1 are dispensable for the specification of myeloid progenitors during embryonic myelopoiesis.

663212.label: Major findings and research outcome
663212.value: Macrophages and neutrophils are key cellular components of innate immune system and play critical roles in immune response, organ development and tissue homeostasis. In vertebrates, macrophages and neutrophils arise predominantly from two waves of development: the first or embryonic wave of myelopoiesis initiates early from non-hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) precursors and gives rise to myeloid cells transiently during early development; whereas the second or adult wave of myelopoiesis emerges later from HSCs and produces myeloid cells continually during fetal and adult life. Recent studies in mice and zebrafish have indicated that the embryonic myelopoiesis appears to produce macrophages sustainable in adulthood, underscoring the importance of embryonic myelopoiesis. Yet, the genetic network controlling embryonic myelopoiesis remains incompletely defined. In the proposed study, we have conducted an in vivo study to delineate the role of Cebpα during embryonic myelopoiesis using zebrafish as a model system. We have shown that embryonic myelopoiesis in cebpα-deficient zebrafish mutants initiates normally but fails to produce mature macrophages and neutrophils. We have further demonstrated that the failure of generating mature macrophages and neutrophils in cebpα-deficient mutants is due to cell cycle arrest of the embryonic myeloid progenitors, resulting in the blockage of their survival and subsequent differentiation. Finally, we have also shown that Cebpα is required for the maintenance of embryonic neutrophils by acting cooperatively with another transcription factor Runx1. Our findings reveal a new role of Cebpα during embryonic myelopoiesis.

663212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
663212.value: As the inactivation of Cebpα and Pu.1 does not affect the specification of earliest myeloid precursors, it is reasonable to hypothesize that additional unknown factor(s) is likely involved in the myeloid lineage specification. It would be of great interest to uncover the factor(s) in the future.

663212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663212.value: Macrophages and neutrophils are two key subtypes of white blood cells in human, and they are essential for protection against pathogen invasion as well as for the repair and maintenance of many organs and tissues. Abnormalities in the formation and functions of macrophages and neutrophils are known to closely associate with the occurrences of various human disorders such as infectious diseases and cancers. Thus, elucidating how macrophages and neutrophils are formed and function under normal condition is important for understanding the development of related diseases as well as for developing new strategies for therapeutic treatments of these disorders. In our proposed study, we have utilized zebrafish, a tiny tropical fish which share a high degree of similarities in white blood cell development to study the formation of macrophages and neutrophils. We have shown that transcription regulator Cebpα is critical for the proliferation and survival of myeloid precursors, which are capable of generating macrophages and neutrophils. We have further demonstrated that Cebpα is also required for the maintenance of neutrophils but is dispensable for the formation of macrophages. Our findings have further deepened our mechanistic understanding of macrophage and neutrophil development in general.

663412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
663412.value: Hormones and neurotransmitters that bind to G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) have long been known to regulate many aspects of human physiology. Although GPCRs are not generally considered as essential components for cell growth and proliferation, there is substantial evidence to indicate that G protein-dependent signaling pathways can modulate these cellular processes. Dysregulation of G protein pathways can in fact lead to neoplastic transformation and tumorigenesis in certain cell types. The RGS proteins (regulators of G protein signaling) are a family of GAPs (GTPase-activating proteins) that limit the durations of G protein signals. The involvement of distinct RGS proteins has been implicated in tumor growth, progression, and metastasis. The PI and others have recently demonstrated that upregulation of RGS17 and RGS19, but not RGS20, of the RZ/A subfamily can enhance cell proliferation in multiple cellular backgrounds. Surprisingly, preliminary studies from the PI’s laboratory suggest that oncogenic Ras-induced tumor formation in nude mice is enhanced in the presence of RGS20; nude mice injected with NIH3T3 fibroblasts coexpressing RasG12V (oncogenic Ras) and RGS20 developed significantly larger tumors with extensive vasculature than those animals injected with NIH3T3 cells expressing RasG12V alone. It is also interesting to note that the presence of RasG12V but not wild-type Ras can stabilize the expression of RGS20 in NIH3T3 cells, suggesting that activated Ras may interact with RGS20 and/or prevent its degradation. Since G protein signals have been shown to regulate angiogenesis, the present proposal aims to test the hypothesis that RGS20 enhances oncogenic Ras-induced tumor formation by facilitating angiogenesis. Special attention will be devoted to exploring possible linkages between the signaling pathways operated by Ras and RGS20. Attempts will also be made to establish whether the tumorigenic effect of RGS20 is seen only in association with oncogenic Ras, or if it can similarly be observed with other oncogenes. Given the prevalence of Ras oncogenes in many human cancers, it is important to elucidate signaling networks that potentiate or synergize with Ras signaling. If RGS20 can indeed enhance oncogenic Ras-induced tumor formation, it may be feasible to develop new therapeutic agents to combat Ras-dependent cancers because activation of Gi-coupled receptors has been shown to downregulate RGS20 by proteosomal degradation. Detailed knowledge of how RGS20 regulates angiogenesis would contribute to a better understanding of the actions of GPCRs in tumor biology and could have a major impact in clinical oncology. 激素和神經遞質與G蛋白偶聯受體（GPCRs）結合後，可以發揮調節作用，影響人體生理機能。一般認為G蛋白偶聯受體沒有直接參與在細胞生長和增殖的過程中，但有大量證據指出G蛋白依賴的信號通路可以調節這些過程。G蛋白通路一旦失調，便會導致某些類型的細胞惡性轉化和腫瘤形成。RGS蛋白（G蛋白信號調節器）家族具有GAP（GTP酶啟動蛋白）的活性，可以限制G蛋白信號的持續性。研究顯示有不同的RGS蛋白參與在腫瘤生長、發展和轉移。近期我們發現上調的RGS17和 RGS19蛋白，可以促進多種類型的細胞增殖，同屬RZ/A亞家族的RGS20卻沒有這種作用。在另一系列試驗中，初步結果卻顯示RGS20對在裸鼠體內由致癌Ras誘導的腫瘤形成有增強作用。與注射表達RasG12V（致癌Ras）的NIH3T3成纖維細胞的裸鼠相比，注射共同表達RasG12V和RGS20的NIH3T3的裸鼠，長出的腫瘤明顯較大，血管系統延伸更廣泛。此外，在NIH3T3細胞實驗中，RasG12V穩定RGS20的表達，而野生型的Ras就不能。由此可見激活的Ras與RGS20互有作用，甚或防止其降解。已知G蛋白信號可以調節血管生成，籍此研究我們會說明RGS20是否通過促進血管生成，從而協同癌基因Ras誘導腫瘤形成。我們並會致力於探討由Ras和RGS20調控的信號通路之間的聯繫；以及嘗試釐清RGS20的致瘤效果是否僅與癌基因Ras有關，還是與其他癌基因亦有類似效應。許多人類癌症均與Ras癌基因有關，因此解構對Ras信號有增強或協同作用的轉導網絡，有重大意義。若能證實RGS20可以促進致癌Ras誘導的腫瘤形成，便可望開發針對與Ras相關的癌症的新型療法。已有研究指出Gi-偶聯受體激活後，可以通過蛋白酶體的降解，導致RGS20下調。透過研究RGS20調控血管生成的機制，我們對GPCRs在腫瘤生物學中的作用有更深認識，並可望將成果應用於臨床腫瘤學。

663412.label: Realisation of objectives
663412.value: Objective 1: To demonstrate the specificity of RGS20 for enhancing oncogene-induced tumorigenesis, the effects of RGS20 overexpression and knock down in selected cancer cell lines were examined. Stable knockdown of RGS20 in A549, H1299 and HeLa cells was achieved by specific shRNA. The knockdown of RGS20 in all three cell types did not affect cell proliferation. Nevertheless, the hanging drop assay revealed that the knockdown of RGS20 reduced the size of the cell aggregates. This result prompted us to hypothesize that RGS20 might have a role in augmenting tumor survival by enhancing cell aggregation ability. Indeed, overexpression of RGS20 enhanced the survival of HeLa cells under serum-free condition. Further studies revealed that, besides enhancing cell aggregation, RGS20 also stimulated cell migration, invasion and adhesion. An elevated expression of vimentin concomitant with a reduced expression of E-cadherin was apparently associated with RGS20 expression in both fibroblasts and cancer cell lines. Since loss of expression or deregulation of E-cadherin (a cell surface adhesion molecule) is commonly found during metastasis, while vimentin (an intermediate filament protein) is typically upregulated during metastasis, our results suggest that RGS20 may play a role in cancer metastasis. The ability of RGS20 to enhance RasGV-induced tumorigenesis was examined by the nude mice xenograft assay. After two weeks of growth, mice injected with 3T3/RasGV or 3T3/RasGV/RGS20 cells all developed large tumors, but no tumor could be detected for mice injected with 3T3/Ras or 3T3/RGS20 cells. The tumors arising from 3T3/RasGV/RGS20 cells were larger in size and appeared earlier than those of 3T3/RasGV cells. H1299 and HeLa cells with RGS20 stably knocked down were likewise subjected to the nude mice assay. In both cases the tumor incidence was unaltered by the knockdown of RGS20. These phenotypes were not observed when RGS19 or RGS17 was used instead of RGS20. Because shRNA-mediated knockdown of RGS20 failed to reduce tumorigenesis of HeLa cells (transformed primarily due to the loss of the p53 gene) in nude mice assays, it tends to suggest that the actions of RGS20 may be oncogene-specific or cell type-specific. Although Ras is an oncogene commonly associated with many types of cancers, tumorigenesis is a multifactorial process that often involves different oncogenes. Hence, in order to test the specificity of the effect of RGS20, it is important to assess whether RGS20 can enhance tumorigenesis induced by other oncogenes. Similar studies were performed with oncogenic SrcYF in the NIH3T3 cellular background. Co-expression of RGS20 with SrcYF did not alter the growth characteristics or the tumorigenic potential of the transfectants. These results suggest that the tumor-enhancing actions of RGS20 may be specific to the Ras oncogenes. Objective 2: To test the hypothesis that RasGV may stabilize RGS20 through complex formation, HA-tagged RGS20 was transiently co-expressed in HEK293 cells in the absence or presence of FLAG-tagged Ras or RasGV. However, no formation of a RGS20/RasGV complex could be detected by co-immunoprecipitation assays; the lack of association was not due to technical constraint because known binding partners of RasGV and RGS20 could be pulled down. The ability of RGS20 to interact with other molecules along the Ras signaling pathway, such as KSR, ERK, and Akt, was also examined. RGS20 did not affect the association of Ras to KSR and it did not affect Akt signaling (in contrast to RGS19). The expression of RGS20 appeared to attenuate ERK signaling in HEK293 and NIH3T3 cells. Activities of the other two mitogen-activated protein kinases (c-Jun N-terminal kinase and p38 MAPK) were also unaffected by the expression of RGS20. Further examinations of cell cycle regulators that lie downstream of Ras also failed to detect altered signaling activities in RGS20 expressing cells; no change in the expression level or phosphorylation status of Cdk4, Cdk6, Cyclin D1, Cyclin D3, INK4B, or Rb (retinoblastoma tumor suppressor) was detected in 293/RGS20 cells. Both HEK293 and NIH3T3 cells overexpressing RGS20 did not exhibit altered growth rates. The lack of effect of RGS20 on growth signals and cell cycle regulators are in stark contrast to RGS19 (which stimulates cell proliferation), which reinforces the notion that RGS proteins in the same subfamily can possess distinct functions. Objective 3: To test the hypothesis that RGS20 may promote tumor growth by improving blood supply to the tumor parenchyma, the effect of RGS20 on the expression of angiogenic factors was examined using the RT2 Profiler Human Angiogenesis PCR Array (PAMS-024Z, Qiagen). Among the 84 angiogenesis related genes screened, only S1PR1 and VEGFC were significantly upregulated in HEK293/RGS20 cells as compared to parental HEK293 cells, while significant down regulation was observed for ANGPTL4 (a tumor suppressor), CXCL9, THBS1, THBS2, and PLG (angiogenesis inhibitors). Subsequent validation assays suggest that the changes in target gene expressions were weak and dependent on the cell type under investigation. Nevertheless, it is interesting to note that the Gi-coupled sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor (S1PR1) has indeed been shown to induce tube formation in human endothelial cells in a Ras-dependent manner. These results indicate that RGS20 may facilitate angiogenesis via vessel stabilization and suppression of factors that tend to inhibit angiogenesis. A yeast two-hybrid assay has revealed interaction between RGS20 and VEGF-B 167 but not VEGF-B 186 at medium stringency selection. Interestingly, VEGF-B 167 was up-regulated by over-expressing RGS20 in HEK293 or NIH3T3 cells, and the response was correlated to the amount of RGS20 cDNA used in the transfection. Given that RGS19 has been shown to stimulate the secretion of Nm23 into the culture medium, it is possible that RGS20 might induce angiogenesis through enhanced production and secretion of angiogenic factors such as VEGF-B 167. An in vitro angiogenesis model using the mouse aortic ring assay was therefore established. Conditioned medium from NIH3T3 or 3T3/RGS20 cells were collected and used to culture 1 mm sections of mouse aortic rings for 7 days. Formation of new blood vessels was determined by immunostaining for the marker CD31. Extensive sprouting was observed with the positive control (serum) but not in those samples treated with conditioned media. These results did not support the notion that RGS20 can stimulate angiogenesis. It remains to be determined if the increase in tumor vasculature observed with 3T3/RasGV/RGS20 cells requires a strict in vivo microenvironment which is conducive for tumor growth.

663412.label: Major findings and research outcome
663412.value: The overall project goal was to examine the effect of RGS20 on tumorigenesis. Although overexpression of RGS20 alone did not stimulate neoplastic transformation, its co-expression with oncogenic Ras enhanced colony formation in vitro and increased tumor vasculature in vivo (Publication 1 in Part C). However, there was no change in tumor size and shRGS20-mediated knock down of RGS20 did not affect the tumorigenic potentials of human non-small cell lung carcinoma H1299 and cervical cancer HeLa cells (Publication 1). In human breast adenocarcinoma MDA-MB-231 cells, expression of RGS20 enhanced cell aggregation, migration, invasion and adhesion as determined by hanging drop aggregation, wound healing, transwell chamber migration and invasion assays (Publication 5 and Abstracts 1 and 2). Conversely, shRNA-mediated knockdown of endogenous RGS20 impaired these responses. In addition, RGS20 elevated the expression of vimentin (a mesenchymal cell marker) but down-regulated the expression of E-cadherin, two indicators commonly associated with metastasis (Publication 5). These results suggest that the expression of RGS20 may promote metastasis of tumor cells. However, these effects of RGS20 were distinct from those of RGS19, a close family member which was found to regulate tumorigenesis by upregulating the metastasis suppressors Nm23H1 and H2 (Publications 2 and 3). Additional clues of RGS20 playing a regulatory role in tumorigenesis were obtained by examining the effects of RGS20 on signaling pathways involved in cell proliferation and angiogenesis. RGS20 was found to downregulate the expression of several inhibitors of angiogenesis (Abstracts 1 and 4), and it appeared to interact with VEGFB (Abstracts 1 and 2). Expression of RGS20 had little or no effect on the activity or level of a number of cell cycle regulators tested, but it attenuated ERK responses in different cellular backgrounds (Abstract 4). As the ability of RGS20 to enhance tumorigenesis was subtle but more readily observed in in vivo assays, it may regulate the production of paracrine factors. Since the primary target of RGS20 is the Gi proteins, we demonstrated that Gi signaling can indeed stimulate the secretion of CXCL8 in various cell types including HeLa and MCF-7 cancer cells (Publication 4); it remains to be demonstrated whether RGS20 can affect Gi-mediated paracrine signaling. RGS proteins such as RGS20 and RGS19 are thus likely to contribute to the establishment of the tumor microenvironment and hence affect tumorigenesis and metastasis (Abstract 3).

663412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
663412.value: Our initial hope of demonstrating an angiogenic action of RGS20 was met with limited success. Despite obvious increase in vasculature in tumor derived from RGS20-expressing cells, a clear linkage to angiogenesis could not be established. Nevertheless, by using overexpression and knock down approaches to manipulate the level of RGS20 in different cancer cell lines, the present study shows that RGS20 may play a role in the regulation of cancer cell migration and invasion, and even perhaps metastasis. If the expression of RGS20 can be selectively inhibited, it may represent an alternative means to suppress metastasis. This possibility is enticing because engagement of Toll-like receptors (TLR3 and TLR4) has been shown to induce the expression of RGS20 in monocyte-derived dendritic cells. Since nearly all types of tumor cells express TLR3 and/or TLR4, it is likely that inhibition of TLR signaling may suppress RGS20 expression in tumor cells and contribute towards prevention of tumor metastasis. Another key question which needs to be carefully addressed is whether RGS20 expression is correlated with the metastatic potential of tumor cells in vivo. In this regard, several reports have demonstrated that RGS20 transcript levels are elevated in melanoma and metastatic breast cancer cells.

663412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663412.value: Practically all major physiological functions in the human body are subject to regulation by the family of G protein-coupled receptors. As integral components of G protein signaling pathways, the RGS proteins represent potential molecular targets for the modulation of various biological functions. There is increasing evidence to implicate the involvement of RGS proteins in the regulation of tumorigenesis and cancer metastasis. The present study has provided several lines of evidence pointing to the possible involvement of RGS20 in regulating tumor cell migration and invasion. Since RGS20 can down-regulate E-cadherin and up-regulate vimentin, it may play a role in tumor metastasis by promoting epithelial-mesenchymal transition. A thorough understanding on how RGS20 regulates tumorigenesis and metastasis may yield new therapeutic targets for cancer treatment in the future.

663512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
663512.value: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (Stat3), a key transcription factor in the JAK/Stat pathway, is required for many biological processes. In our previous cell culture-based work, we found that Stat3 plays dual roles in myoblasts: it not only participates in myoblast proliferation but also is required for myoblast differentiation. It remains unclear whether Stat3 affects muscle development, muscle stem cell properties and muscle regeneration in vivo. To address this issue, we have generated muscle progenitor cell-specific knockout mice (designated as Stat3-MKO). Our initial studies showed that Stat3 is not required for normal embryonic or postnatal muscle development in wild-type C57BL/6 mice. However, when bred into the dystrophin-null mice (mdx) whose muscles undergo spontaneous degeneration and regeneration, the Stat3-MKO/mdx double mutant mice were smaller in size 4 weeks after birth, suggesting a defect in postnatal muscle regeneration. Consistently, Stat3-null myoblasts showed reduced growth rate and the Stat3-MKO mice showed defective regeneration after the cardiotoxin-induced injury. All preliminary data indicate that Stat3 plays an important role in muscle progenitor cells in vivo. In this proposal, we will characterize muscle progenitor cells from Stat3-MKO mice in details and study their activation, proliferation, and differentiation. We will also try to uncover the molecular mechanisms by which Stat3 regulates muscle progenitor cells. Our findings should deepen our understanding of the regulation of muscle stem cells in vivo and could provide useful clues for potential application of these muscle stem cells in treating certain congenital muscular dystrophies and for accelerating muscle repair in injured or aged people. 關於STAT3在肌肉幹細胞及肌肉再生中作用的研究 STAT3是JAK/STAT信號傳導通路中一個關鍵的轉錄因子，它在許多生物過程中起重要作用。在我們前期基於細胞培養的工作中，我們發現STAT3有雙重作用：它既參與成肌細胞的增殖也參與成肌細胞的分化。但是我們仍然不清楚在活體動物中STAT3是否影響肌肉發育，肌肉幹細胞，及肌肉再生。為了回答這個問題，我們建立了一個在肌肉幹細胞中將STAT3基因敲除的小鼠模型（簡稱為Stat3-MKO）。我們初步的研究發現在野生型C57/BL6小鼠肌肉幹細胞中敲除STAT3並不顯著影響胚胎期及出生後肌肉的發育。但是，在缺失dystrophin的小鼠（又稱為mdx小鼠， 其骨骼肌在成年小鼠中會不斷地萎縮退化及再生）肌肉幹細胞中敲除STAT3會導致雙基因突變小鼠（簡稱為Stat3-MKO/mdx）在出生4週後體型顯著變小，說明其肌肉再生可能有問題。進一步支持此假設的是：我們也發現Stat3缺失的成肌細胞生長變慢；Stat3-MKO小鼠在cardiotoxin誘導損傷 後肌肉再生減慢。所有初步的結果均顯示STAT3在活體動物的肌肉幹細胞中起重要作用。在本計劃中，我們將深入研究Stat3-MKO小鼠中肌肉幹細胞的活化，增殖，及分化，並了解STAT3調控肌肉幹細胞的分子機理。我們的研究可以加深對肌肉幹細胞在體內功能的了解，及對其用於治療先天性肌肉萎縮症，及加速因損傷誘導的肌肉再生提供有益的線索。

663512.label: Realisation of objectives
663512.value: We addressed all the questions in our proposal and achieved all our objectives. For the first objective (to investigate the role of STAT3 in MuSC in vivo), we generated two muscle satellite cell (MuSC)-specific Stat3-knockout (KO) mouse lines: one on a wild-type background (i.e., Stat3-cKO) and the other on a dystrophin-null background (i.e., Stat3/Dmd-dKO). We either sorted MuSC by fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) or isolated single myofibers from these mice (adult) and then examined the number of MuSC between the control and Stat3-KO mice. We found that deletion of Stat3 alone in MuSC (i.e., Stat3-cKO) did not affect their maintenance or numbers in uninjured muscles. In Stat3/Dmd-dKO mice, before spontaneous degeneration-regeneration cycles starts around 3-week of age, the number of MuSC was also comparable to that of the mdx control. However, in adult Stat3/Dmd-dKO mice, the number of MuSC started to decreases. For the second objective (to investigate the role of STAT3 in MuSC proliferation), we used both single myofibers and primary MuSC sorted by FACS and studied proliferation of MuSC in culture. We found that Stat3-null MuSC were defective in cell proliferation due to enhanced differentiation potentials. For the third objective (to investigate the role of STAT3 during injury-induced muscle regeneration), we injured tibialis anterior (TA) muscles of the control and Stat3-cKO mice with cardiotoxin, and dissected TA muscle at various time point to assess the extent of muscle regeneration. We found that there was a mild delay in muscle regeneration in Stat3-cKO mice. However, with repeated injury, there was more severe defect in the Stat3-cKO mice. Consistently, we observed ag-dependent severe defects in muscle regeneration, reduction in MuSC, increase in macrophage infiltration, and muscle fibrosis in the Stat3/Dmd-dKO mice. For the fourth objective (to identify Stat3 target genes in MuSC), we isolated MuSC by FACS from the mdx control and Stat3/Dmd-dKO mice, extracted total RNA, and performed RNA-seq. We identified Stat3 target genes in MuSC that can explain various defects in MuSC from the Stat3/Dmd-dKO mice.

663512.label: Major findings and research outcome
663512.value: In this project, we made the following key findings: • Stat3 ablation alone in MuSC does not affect skeletal muscle development, and the number and maintenance of adult MuSC in uninjured muscles. • MuSC-specific deletion of Stat3 affected the self-Renewal of MuSC after muscle injury • Stat3 ablation in MuSC of dystrophic mice led to severe muscle defects (enhanced muscle fibrosis and increased macrophage infiltration) • Adult Stat3/Dmd-dKO mice displayed a gradual reduction in the number of Pax7+ MuSC • Stat3-null MuSC were defective in cell proliferation • Loss of Stat3 in Dmd-null MuSC dysregulated genes involved in the regulation of MuSC Proliferation and maintenance • Loss of Stat3 in Dmd-null MuSC induced the expression of many pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine genes • Loss of Stat3 in Dmd-null MuSC induced the expression of multiple pro-fibrotic Genes The above findings were published in a paper by our group in Cell Reports in 2016.

663512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
663512.value: Our findings establish an important role for STAT3 in regulating self-renewal of MuSC upon injury. It remains unclear which upstream signaling molecule regulates STAT3 in MuSC. The JAK family protein tyrosine kinases are obvious candidates. We are trying to generate inducible MuSC-specific JAK knockout mice to address this question. In addition, based on the severe phenotypes observed in our Stat3/Dmd-dKO mice, it would also be interesting to study mutual interaction among MuSC, fibroadipogenic progenitor cells (FAPs), and infiltrating macrophages in such mutant mice.

663512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663512.value: STAT3 is a key signaling molecule in the intracellular JAK/STAT signaling pathway. Previous studies by our group and others showed that STAT3 is involved in myogenic differentiation in cell culture models. It was unclear whether STAT3 also plays a role in regulating adult muscle stem cells (MuSC) in vivo. Here, we generated two MuSC-speciﬁc Stat3 knockout (KO) mouse lines: a single Stat3 knockout line (Stat3-cKO) and a Stat3/dystrophin (Dmd) double knockout (dKO) line. In Stat3-cKO mice, we found that loss of Stat3 in MuSC did not affect normal skeletal muscle growth, MuSC number and maintenance. However, after repeated muscle injuries, Stat3-cKO mice displayed severe defects in muscle regeneration. Consistently, in Stat3/Dmd-dKO mice that undergo chronic spontaneous muscle degeneration and regeneration, there was an age-dependent reduction in MuSC number, and aggravated muscle inflammation and fibrosis. We found that Stat3-null MuSC had reduced cell proliferation due to an accelerated differentiation. We identiﬁed multiple STAT3 target genes that can explain the defects seen in the Stat3/Dmd dKO mice. Collectively, our work reveals a critical role for STAT3 in regulating self-renewal of MuSC upon muscle injury.

663812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
663812.value: Ankyrin-R/B/G, encoded by ANK1/2/3, are a family of very large scaffold proteins that are important for the targeting and organization of many trans-membrane proteins including cell adhesion receptors, transporters, and ion-channels at the specific membrane domains of red blood cells, skeletal and smooth muscle, and neurons. Mutations of ANKs are known to cause a number of human diseases including hereditary spherocytosis, cardiac arrhythmias, ataxia, and bipolar disorders in humans. However, the molecular basis governing the physiological functions of ankyrins is poorly understood and very little is known as to why mutations of ANKs can cause various human diseases, partly owing to the large sizes and the complicated domain organizations of ankyrins. In this proposed research, we plan to address the biochemical and structural bases underlying ankyrins/target membrane protein interactions mediated by the N-terminal 24 ANK repeats of all three ankyrin isoforms. We select L1 family cell adhesion molecule (L1CAM), the voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.2/NaV1.5, and voltage-gated calcium channel KCNQ2/3 as the ankyrin-B/G binding targets for detailed investigations owing to their vital physiological functions and broad tissue distributions. Motivated by a large number of human genome-wide association studies, we plan to explore a new hypothesis that ankyrin-G might be able to directly interact with the Cav1.2 channel in modulating neuronal development and activities. We will also elucidate the structural basis of the interaction between the C-terminal tail regulatory domains with the N-terminal 24 ANK repeats of ankyrin-B/G in order to understand how the regulatory domain of ankyrins modulates its binding to target membrane proteins. Successful execution of the studies described in this proposal will provide a clear picture of the interaction between ankyrins and their membrane targets at the atomic level for the first time. The outcomes of the research are expected to be valuable for understanding the molecular mechanisms governing the physiological functions of ankyrins as well as many human diseases caused by mutations of ANKs. Ankyrin是與細胞內膜結構相關的一類非常大的骨架蛋白。在紅細胞，骨骼肌，平滑肌以及神經細胞等應激性組織的特定細胞膜結構域中，ankyrin對定位和組織許多跨膜蛋白，例如細胞粘附分子，離子通道等，起著非常重要的作用。Ankyrin家族由基因ANK1/2/3 分別轉錄編碼的ankyrin-R/B/G三個成員組成。Ankyrin的基因突變與許多人類疾病密切相關，如遺傳性球形紅細胞性貧血，心律不齊，心臟共濟失調以及躁鬱症等。然而，由於ankyrin蛋白非常大的分子量和複雜的結構域組成，調控ankyrin重要生理功能的分子機制目前大部分還不清楚，而且與疾病相關的突變研究也相應缺乏。 在此研究計畫中，我們將要結合生物化學與結構生物學等研究手段，來闡述ankyrin結合膜蛋白的特性及內在的分子機理。Ankyrin是由N端的24個ankryin repeats (ANK repeats) 組成了其膜結合結構域，中間區域包括一個能夠結合spectrin的ZU5 結構域和另一個連續的ZU5-UPA-DD結構域，但C端通常是一個長度多變並且不保守的調控結構域。我們選擇了L1細胞粘附分子(L1CAM)，電壓門控性鈉離子通道NaV1.2和NaV1.5，以及電壓門控性鉀離子通道KCNQ2/3作為ankyrin-B/G的結合蛋白進行研究，因為這些膜蛋白在人體中廣泛分佈，並且起著非常重要的生理功能。此外，我們還將研究ankyrins自身的C端調控結構域對於其膜結合活性的調控分子機制，為進一步的研究C端調控結構域的功能，以及對ankyrin結合膜蛋白的調控機制研究打下基礎。此研究計畫的成功進行將會首次為ankyrin與其相互作用的膜結合蛋白提供一個原子水準上的清晰認識。預期的研究成果將會更加深刻的理解ankyrin重要生理功能的分子機制，以及為由ankyrin突變導致的人類疾病的研究提供非常大的價值。

663812.label: Major findings and research outcome
663812.value: We have made wonderful progresses in this project. Ankyrin adaptors together with their spectrin partners coordinate diverse ion channels and cell adhesion molecules within plasma membrane domains and thereby promote physiological activities including fast signaling in the heart and nervous system. Ankyrins specifically bind to numerous membrane targets through their 24 ankyrin repeats (ANK repeats), although the mechanism for the facile and independent evolution of these interactions has not been resolved. In the grant period, we have solved the structures of ANK repeats in complex with an inhibitory segment from the C-terminal regulatory domain and with a sodium channel Nav1.2 peptide, respectively, showing that the extended, extremely conserved inner groove spanning the entire ANK repeat solenoid contains multiple quasi-independent target binding sites capable of accommodating target proteins with very diverse sequences via combinatorial usage of these sites. These structures establish a framework for understanding the evolution of ankyrins’ membrane targets and provide mechanistic insights into diseases caused by mutations in ankyrins and/or their binding partners, with implications for other proteins containing extended ANK repeat domains. This work has been published in eLife at the end of 2014. We have also been collaborating with Dr. Vann Bennett's lab at the Duke University Medical School and Dr. Peter Mohler's lab at the Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center to understand the mechanistical bases of metablic and cardiac diseases resulted from ankyrin mutations. These collaborations have been very fruitful and led to two publications as lited in the "Output" section.

663812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
663812.value: We are at multiple fronts of new research on structure and function of ankyrins, and these research are derived from the successful studies in this granting period. We are particularly interested in the mechanistic basis of ankyrin-G's function at axonal initial segaments in neurons. We are also having multiple collaborations with Dr. Bennett's lab to further explore functional roles of ankyrins in human physiology.

663812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663812.value: Mutations of ANKs are known to cause a number of human diseases including hereditary spherocytosis, cardiac arrhythmias, ataxia, and bipolar disorders in humans. However, how Ankyrin performs these critical physiological functions are poorly understood and very little is known as to why mutations of ANKs can cause various human diseases, partly owing to the large sizes and its extremely complicated domain organizations of ankyrins. Intriguingly, the 24 repeats found in human ankyrin proteins appear to have essentially remained unchanged for the last 500 million years. As such, it remains unclear how the conserved ankyrin repeats can bind to such a wide variety of protein targets. In this research, we have solved the three-dimensional structure of ankyrin repeats from a human ankyrin protein while it was bound either to a regulatory fragment from another ankyrin protein or to a region of a target protein. We show that this surface contains many binding sites that can be used, in different combinations, to allow ankyrins to interact with diverse proteins. Other proteins with long sequences of repeats are widespread in nature, but uncovering the structures of these proteins is technically challenging. Our findings reveal new insights into the functions of many of such proteins in a wide range of living species. Furthermore, our structure could help explain why specific mutations in the genes that encode ankyrins (or their binding targets) can cause various diseases in humans—including heart diseases and psychiatric disorders.

664012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
664012.value: 埃希氏大腸桿菌（以下簡稱大腸桿菌）是一類天然存在於恒溫動物末端腸道的細菌。當動物排便時，大腸桿菌隨糞便進入外部環境。因為大腸桿菌與糞便關係密切，世界上許多管理機構將海水和淡水中大腸桿菌的數目作為水體糞便污染的指標。這種做法基於一個重要的假設，即大腸桿菌作為動物腸道的寄居者，不具備承受外部環境生存壓力的能力而隨著糞便污染程度的減輕逐漸消亡。事實上，大腸桿菌在水體中（特別是在陽光的照射下）迅速死亡。然而，許多研究報導表明在無糞便輸入的條件下，大腸桿菌能在土壤和沉積物中生存、繁殖并一直存在。這些發現引起了人們對於將大腸桿菌作為糞便污染指示劑的合理性以及環境介質成為腸道疾病病原體的溫床的關注。除應用領域之外，這些發現也帶來了關於大腸桿菌生態位、生活方式、進化及適應的一系列有趣問題。例如，大腸桿菌如何應對在外部環境下新出現的一系列生存壓力？大腸桿菌如何利用那些與動物腸道營養源不同的營養源并與外部環境中固有的微生物互相競爭？是否所有大腸桿菌菌株都具備在外部環境中存活、繁殖的能力或者是某些菌株與具有更大的競爭力？競爭力較弱的菌株能否在外部環境中逐漸進化并適應？如果能，將通過何種途徑進行？在該項目中，我們將利用牛糞中所有大腸桿菌菌群作為模型，研究以海洋沉積物作為其生存環境對其種群動力學和多樣性的影響。在該微型模擬實驗中，我們將分別測定可溶性有機質及其它微生物群體對大腸桿菌的影響。大腸桿菌種群密度的即時變化將通過微生物培養手段和分子實驗手段進行監測。多樣性變化將通過微生物群落DNA指紋技術進行檢測。我們將在實驗的各個階段觀察大腸桿菌菌落并對其系統進化關係和表現型進行對比。該實驗的最終目的是驗證具有特定基因型和（或）表現型的大腸桿菌菌株在海洋沉積物中是否具有特定的生存優勢。

664012.label: Realisation of objectives
664012.value: Objective 1 We conducted a number of microcosm experiments, each lasting for 99 days, to determine the population dynamics of E. coli in marine sediment after the addition of a fecal community pertaining to feral cows. The population dynamics of Bacteroidales, which represent up to 30 % of the total bacterial population in mammalian feces, were also monitored using qPCR of 16S rRNA gene markers for benchmarking. Both cultivation and qPCR indicated an initial growth of E. coli in sediment after the adding of cow feces. The incubation of E. coli (isolated from the microcosms as discussed below) in 100-KD filtered sediment interstitial water indicated that the species was able to grow using dissolved compounds of marine sediment as the sole nutrient source. After the initial growth in sediment, E. coli exhibited continuous population decay. Nonetheless, the decay was relatively slow that the size of the E. coli population at the end of the incubation was only 1 order of magnitude smaller than at the beginning. In addition to the provision of nutrient, protection from light and anaerobic conditions are other factors that could contribute to the persistence of E. coli in the sediment microcosms. A total of 847 isolates obtained from three different stages of the microcosm experiments were subjected to REP-PCR DNA fingerprinting (stage I: immediately after the microcosms were set up; stage II: after 1 day when culturable E. coli population went up; and stage III; near the end of the experiment and before complete decay of the culturable E. coli population). The isolates of 48 representative REP-PCR genotypes were analyzed using MLST and tested for growth efficiency in interstitial water. The 48 genotypes had significant differences in growth rates in interstitial waters; however, such differences were not related to the phylogenetic distance among the isolates. Objective 2 The 48 E. coli strains of the microcosms were also tested for their susceptibility to protozoan grazing as well as their colicin-producing, colicin-sensitive and colicin-resistant phenotypes. In addition, we investigated the possible roles of temperate phages as a mediator of E. coli adaptation to marine sediment. E. coli may produce colicins against strains of the same or closely related species. Occasionally, strains that are susceptible to colicins may mutate and become resistant. We hypothesize that when a population of E. coli enters marine sediment through fecal input, the colicin-producing, colicin-sensitive and colicin-resistance phenotypes within the population will have different fates in the sediment due to interactions with the bacteria already present in the sediment. The experiments conducted to test this hypothesis included not only the 48 strains of the microcosms but also 47 strains of E. coli isolated from fresh marine sediment. A total of 14 colicin genes were found among all strains tested. Since colicin genes are plasmid-borne, the occurrence and distribution of the detected colicin genes did not have apparent relationship with the phylogenetic affiliation of the strains tested. But colicin genes were more frequently detected among the strains of the microcosms than those of fresh sediment; the diversity of the colicin genes carried by the two sets of strains were also different. Further, growth inhibition tests revealed that the microcosm strains were more resistant to colicins than the strains of fresh sediment. While the microcosm strains were derived from fecal community of cows, those of fresh sediment could have undergone certain degree of selection by the external environment. It is possible that the intraspecific competition for E. coli is relatively low in external environments and that E. coli shed their colicin production and resistant genes as an adaption to marine sediment. For the effects of grazing, we started with the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans for a trial and then marine ciliate Euplotes crassus as a model grazer. Although C. elegans is not a protozoan nor is it supposed to be present in marine sediment, it is well known for its selectivity to E. coli strains as a food source. We tested the 48 E. coli strains of the microcosms for their relative palatability to the wild type C. elegans N2 in an assay, in which the colonies of the 48 genotypes were provided to the worms simultaneously. We observed that the colonies of 11 genotypes were completely grazed, 10 genotypes were partially grazed, and 27 genotypes were not graze after 24 hours of incubation. These results indicate that the E. coli strains isolated from the microcosm experiments had different attractiveness to C. elegans as a source of food. Similar results were observed for the experiments involving E. crassus. Further experiments revealed that E. coli strains with high survivability under ciliate predation tended to aggregate faster, form denser biofilms, grow faster in low nutrient conditions, and have smaller cell sizes. These may be the phenotypic allowing the resistant strains to evade protozoan grazing. Lysogeny plays pivotal roles in the diversification of the ecologic characters of E. coli as a symbiont. We hypothesized that lysogeny could also confer fitness to survival in the external environment. To test this hypothesis, we used the induced phages of an E. coli strain from marine sediment to infect a fecal E. coli strain to obtain an isogenic lysogen of the latter. The three strains were tested for survivorship in microcosms of seawater, marine sediment and sediment interstitial water as well as swimming motility, glycogen accumulation, biofilm formation, substrate utilization and stress resistance. The results indicate that lysogenic infection led to tractable changes in many of the ecophysiological attributes tested. Particularly, the lysogen had better survivorship in the microcosms and had a substrate utilization profile resembling the sediment strain more than the wild type fecal strain. Objective 3 As indicated above, 847 isolates obtained from three different stages of the microcosm experiments were subjected to REP-PCR DNA fingerprinting. Over the course of the experiments, the genotypes dominating the E. coli population of cow feces reduced while some of the REP-PCR genotypes constituting only a minor population in the cow feces increased in relative abundance towards the end of the experiment. In addition to differences in growth rates in interstitial water, the isolates of 48 genotypes exhibited three different types of RADR morphytopes that have no apparent relationship with their phylogenetic affiliation. However, the sediment microcosm environment seemed to have enriched for genotypes that had lower ability to accumulate glycogen. We used a scoring system to classify the 48 genotypes as high and low performers with respect to their ability to grow utilizing resources in sediment matrix and their expression of phenotypes that were relevant to environmental persistence. The high-performer genotypes were more abundant at the later stages of the microcosm experiment. Overall, these results suggested the selection of E. coli genotypes that were better adapted to the environment of the sediment microcosms. Nonetheless, the classification of the genotypes by high- / low-performers did not have apparent relationship with their phylogenetic relationship. One possible reason is that genes conferring the selective advantages were associated with the accessory genome, which cannot be resolved using the core-genes involved in MLST. Further, we developed a novel, genome-sequence independent proteomic fingerprinting method to differentiate E. coli strains by their system-wide expression profile. This method was able to accurately differentiate E. coli strains that were presumably adapted to different niches.

664012.label: Major findings and research outcome
664012.value: Using microcosm experiments of different incubation conditions, we demonstrated that fecal E. coli was able to rapidly reproduce in marine sediment during 24 h of incubation, followed by a slow decay that lasted till the end of the incubation (99 days) (Lun 2016 MPhil Thesis). The initial growth could be stimulated by the availability of dissolved nutrient in the sediment matrix. After that, the anaerobic conditions and the lack of light could have contributed to the slow decay of E. coli in sediment (Liu et al. 2015). Nonetheless, marine sediment appeared to be a selective environment that enabled only a small subset of E. coli to persist (Lun 2016 MPhil thesis). The RADAR morphology, accumulation of glycogen, colicin phenotype, resistance to grazing, ability to form biofilms or flocs appear to be phenotypic attributes that were important to the survival of E. coli in marine sediment (Chen 2016 MPhil Thesis, Teh 2018 MPhil thesis). Nonetheless, there was no apparent relationship between the phylogeny of the E. coli strains and their perceived performance in surviving in sediment. One possible reason is that the genes conferring the presumptive selective advantages were associated with the accessory genome, which cannot be resolved using the core-genes involved in the multi-loci sequence analysis. Lysogeny, a phage-mediated horizontal gene transfer mechanism, has contributed greatly to the genome plasticity of E. coli that underlies a vast intraspecific diversification of phenotypic and ecologic characters. In this project, we demonstrated for the first time that lysogenic conversion by a P2-like prophage had profound effects on the ecophysiology and survivorship of E. coli in marine sediment and seawater (Lai et al. 2018, Lai 2016 MPhil thesis, Zhang 2014 MPhil Thesis). The molecular mechanism causing the observed changes was unclear. None of the 46 genes carried by the P2-like prophage (31 phage structural genes, 6 phage regulatory genes, 1 putative reverse transcriptase and 8 genes of unknown functions) have been reported to have effects on bacterial survival or nutrient utilization. In the applied aspects, we demonstrated that the tracking of the changes in the relative concentration between E. coli and Bacteroidales in seawater could provide an opportunity to differentiate fresh and aged fecal pollution (Liu et al. 2017). We also developed a genome-sequence independent shotgun proteomics method that allowed the differentiation of E. coli strains that were presumably adapted to different niches (Shao et al. 2015).

664012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
664012.value: The results of this project have provided new insights into the role of marine sediment as a secondary habitat for E. coli and the phenotypic attributes that enable E. coli to survive in the habitat. However, the gene repertoire (whether in the core or accessory genome or plasmids) that confers the relevant functions remains not known. Therefore, a possible direction for future development would be to obtain and compare the genome and plasmid sequences of the 48 E. coli genotypes of the microcosm experiments. In addition, the DNA sequences obtained could be used to validate the shotgun proteomics method, which we developed for the differentiation of E. coli that are presumably adapted to different niches.

664012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
664012.value: Escherichia coli is a bacterium capable of surviving in a wide range of habitats inside and outside the mammalian hosts. In this project, we used the E. coli population in the feces of feral cows (presumably free from the influences of antibiotics) and lab experiments to investigate the role of marine sediment as a secondary habitat for E. coli and the phenotypic attributes that enable E. coli to survive in the habitat. The E. coli populations that we tested could survive in sediment microcosms for > 99 days and they were able to utilize the dissolved molecules in the sediment as the sole source of nutrient. There was a strong selective pressure in the microcosms that allowed only a small subset of fecal E. coli to persist. The ability to form biofilms, resist grazing, produce/resist colicins appeared to be important to the persistence. The analysis of the DNA sequences of housekeeping genes suggests that the accessory genome may be more important than the core genome in the provision of gene functions for survival in marine sediment. Overall, this project provided new insight into the evolution, biogeography and ecophysiology of E. coli beyond the well-investigated lab strains, commensal isolates and pathogenic serotypes.

700712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
700712.value: Quantum information processing is the study of quantum systems by information processing means. The success of this approach to tackle both applied and basic quantum mechanical problems include the unconditional security proofs of quantum key distribution (as the answer of sharing secret between two cooperative parties), the construction of quantum error correction codes (as the answer of protecting quantum information in the presence of noise) and the discovery of certain new entropic uncertainty relations (as the partial answer of quantifying ignorance of a quantum state). An under-explored area in quantum information processing is what kind of non-trivial quantum information processing capabilities can be inferred from partial descriptions of quantum systems or quantum operations. Here I propose to investigate along this line by focusing initially on two problems that are of basic and applied interests. They are the maximum possible quantum information processing speed given a partial description of the quantum system (the notion of quantum speed limit) and the constraints imposed on the properties such as the processing speed of a product of quantum operators given only partial descriptions for each operator involved in the product. Then I will apply to results of this study to evaluate the feasibility or performance of existing and proposed quantum information processing systems such as quantum computers and quantum repeaters. 量子信息處理是一門利用信息處理手段對量子系統的研究。這種方法成功地解決了應用和基礎量子力學的問題，包括量子密碼（這提供雙方秘密共享，量子糾錯碼（這保護受干擾的量子信息），和一些新的熵的不確定性關係的發現（這對量化量子態的不知情提供部分答案）。在量子信息處理的領域中，其中一項未被深入探究的是如何使用量子系統和量子操作的局部描述去推斷出非平凡的量子信息處理能力。在這裡，我建議進行這方面的研究，著眼於基本和應 用的問題。它們是量子系統的局部描述如何決定量子信息處理的最快速度（這是量子速度限制的概念），和量子屬性的約束。然後，我將採用這些研究結果，以評估現行及建議中的量子信息處理系統（如量子計算機和量子中繼器）的可行性和性能。

700712.label: Realisation of objectives
700712.value: The first phrase of this project develops the quantum speed limit bounds as well as the mathematical techniques used in the study. The successful development of the tools and results in the first phrase enables the development and interpretation of a new measurement of resources in quantum information processing, namely, the so-called time-energy resource. The final phrase of this project focuses on the applications of the time-energy resource to study the efficiency of unitary quantum evolution, general quantum operation, as well as quantum measurement. In particular, the time-energy resource turns out to be an efficiently computable measure via semi-definite programming. In this way, the three proposed objectives of this project have been achieved.

700712.label: Major findings and research outcome
700712.value: The most important result in this project is the discovery of the first (tight) quantum speed limit (QSL) that constrains the possible evolution time to more than one time intervals [Publication 1]. All previous QSLs can only put lower bounds on the system evolution time. In addition, the method used in the proof of the QSL in [1] is so powerful that it can be used to reprove all the QSLs in the literature to date. Partly based on [1], my former postdoc Dr. C.-H. F. Fung and I found a new measure on the resources needed to perform a general quantum process by introducing a new resource measure known as time-energy [Publication 2]. The notion of time-energy as a resource measure can then be extended to the case of quantum measurement [Publication 8]. Interestingly, this time-energy resource is also found to be related to the information fidelity between the initial and final quantum states [Publication 9]. Although analytical expression for the time-energy resource is hard to find in general, with the help of my collaborators Prof. C.-K. Li and Dr. N.-S. Sze, we show that it can be efficiently computed via semi-definite programming [Publication 10]. Techniques used on our formulation can be used to study quantum security [Publications 3-7] as well as information-disturbance trade-off [Publication 11].

700712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
700712.value: My former postdoc, Dr C.-H. F. Fung continues to work along this time-energy resources independently, with several interesting results regarding the resources needed to realize certain specific quantum channels. Recently, Prof. Mikio Nakahara and I are thinking of the relation between my quantum speed limit results with Finlser geometry. Prof. Nakahara and I will visit each other soon to work on this possibility.

700712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
700712.value: Quantum speed limits (QSLs) are fundamental limits on the evolution time of a quantum system given a partial description of the system. The first part of this project involves the discovery of a new QSL, which can be interpreted as a new fundamental quantum resource needed to perform a quantum operation or measurement. This resource is now known as the time-energy resource. The second part of this project is to study the properties of this time-energy resource, including its efficient computation by means of semi-definite programming as well as to use this time-energy resources to gauge the fundamental limits on the performance of various quantum channels and quantum measurements.
