700812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
700812.value: 發光分子材料在生物探針，光催化，太陽能化學和有機光電方面具有廣泛的應用。儘管螢光有機化合物對這個領域的發展作出了顯著的貢獻，然而，磷光金屬配合物在新型發光材料的設計上更有實用意義。這是因為： 1．吸收和發射能之間大的Stoke躍遷； 2．壽命比螢光有機化合物長1000多倍的激發態 它們的發射三重激發態在衰減回到基態之前有足夠長的壽命，因此在發展太陽能化學反應和生物探針方面頗具吸引力。目前，磷光金屬配合物主要集中在八面體的Ru(II)，Ir(III)，Re(I)等金屬上。磷光性平面金屬配合物顯示了跟八面體配合物完全不同的光學性質。平面配位元幾何性允許各向異性的分子間金屬—金屬，配體—配體相互作用，可以用於功能性超分子結構和聚合物的自組裝；同時，也使得內層金屬離子—分析物/底物相互作用。事實上，磷光性平面金屬配合物，例如Pt(II)，在無機和金屬有機光化學，電子器件和螢光探針等領域引起了廣泛的關注。 磷光性金屬配合物的穩定性，光學性質和激發態的反應性取決於配體和金屬離子。影響到激發態壽命，量子產率和結構—性質相互關係的各種因素的瞭解，有助於螢光性金屬配合物的合理設計。對於實際應用而言，在實驗條件下配合物必須結構穩定，而且抗氧化。 本項目致力於發展新型穩定，發射量子產率高，具有較長激發態壽命的螢光性平面金屬配合物，用於光催化，螢光探針和電子器件。主要集中在很少報導的Au(III)和Pt(II)配合物上，利用密度泛函理論計算，金屬離子和配體對d8金屬配合物的各種電子激發態相對能量的影響，並用這些結果來指導螢光性平面金屬配合物的設計和合成，用於生物探針和光化學反應。

700812.label: Realisation of objectives
700812.value: We have completed the project and achieved all the objectives listed above. 11 papers have been published in peer-reviewed journals: 3 in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 4 in Chem. Sci., 1 in Chem. Commun., 1 in Chem. Eur. J. and 2 in Chem. Asian J. 2 presentations were delivered in international conferences. All these contributions have acknowledged the support from this RGC grant. The important findings are summarized below: [1] Objective 1. We reported a series of robust and bulky platinum(II) complexes supported by tetradentate O^N^C^N ligands. These complexes display emission quantum yields of up to 95%, with emission maxima λmax in the range of 522 to 570 nm, and have good thermal stability with decomposition temperature > 423 oC. The bulky groups at the periphery of the [O^N^C^N] ligand disfavour intermolecular interactions and hence excimer formation in both solutions and films. OLEDs fabricated with these complexes showed excellent current efficiency up to 126 lm W-1, which are the highest among reported Pt(II) and Ir(III)-OLEDs. [Chem. Sci., 2014, 5, 4819]. [2] Objectives 2 and 4. We have performed theoretical analyses on the photophysical properties of several cyclometalated gold(III) arylacetylide complexes, [(C^N^C)AuIIIC≡CPh-4-OMe], with different extents of π-conjugation via replacement of one of the phenyl moieties in the CH^N^C ligand (1) by a naphthalenyl (2) or a fluorenyl moiety (3-exo and 3-endo; HCH^N^CH = 2,6-diphenylpyridine). DFT calculations revealed that there is an additional triplet excited state minimum, 3[π(C≡CPh-4-OMe) / π*(C^N^C)] LLCT, for both complexes 1 and 3-endo. The non-radiative decay rate constant for this 3LLCT / S0 transition exceeds 107 s-1, which is more than three orders of magnitude faster than the knr for the 3IL / S0 transition, thus resulting in low emission quantum yields in these two complexes. [Chem. Sci., 2015, 6, 3026] [3] Objectives 2 and 5. We prepared two classes of cationic palladium(II) acetylide complexes containing pincer-type ligands, 2,2’:6’’,2’’-terpyridine (terpy) and 2,6- bis(1-butylimidazol-2-ylidenyl)pyridine (C^N^C). Complexes supported by C^N^C ligand showed phosphorescence at room temperature and stronger intermolecular interactions in the solid state. X-ray crystal structures reveal PdII∙∙∙PdII contacts of 3.292–3.349 Å. They could form submicron/nano-sized rods and plates with dimensions ranging from 80 nm to 10 μm. Some of these complexes displayed cytotoxic activities with micromolar IC50 values (1.5–2.8 µM). Furthermore, one of them showed a 7.5-fold enhancement in cytotoxicity with IC50 value of 0.2 μM upon visible-light irradiation. [Chem. Asian J. DOI:10.1002/asia.201601414] [4] Objectives 2 and 6. We have developed a series of Pd(II) complexes supported by the C-deprotonated RC^N^NR’ and pentafluorophenylacetylide ligands. These complexes exhibit phosphorescence in the solid state and in solutions at room temperature. Some of them exhibit aggregation-induced-emission (AIE) behavior in solutions. These complexes could act as photosensitizer in light-induced aerobic oxidative C-H functionalization of secondary and tertiary amines, and could act as a photosensitizer for hydrogen production with a maximum turnover number of 175 with a cobaloxime(III) catalyst. [Chem. Asian J., 2014, 9, 534] [5] Objectives 2 and 7. We prepared a series of cyclometalated Au(III) complexes complexes containing bidentate C-deprotonated C^N and cis-chelating bis-NHC ligands. These complexes are luminescent in solution at room temperature with quantum yields and lifetimes up to 10.1 % and 270 μs respectively. Water-soluble Au(III) complexes have also been prepared by using sulfonate-functionalized bis-NHC ligands. The dual fluorescence-phosphorescence of one of these complexes has been used for ratiometric sensing of dissolved oxygen in aqueous medium. One of the complexes displays significant inhibitory activity towards deubiquitinase (DUB) UCHL3. [Chem. Eur. J. 2014, 20, 8604] [6] Objectives 3 and 6. We reported a series of palladium(II) complexes supported by tetradentate [N^C^C^N] and [O^N^C^N] ligand systems with a tertiary amine or spiro-fluorene as a bridging group. These complexes display sky-blue to red phosphorescence with emission quantum yields and emission lifetimes up to 0.64 and 272 μs, respectively. Femtosecond time-resolved fluorescence (fs-TRF) measurements on these Pd(II) complexes reveal a fast intersystem crossing from singlet to triplet manifolds with time constants of 0.6–21 ps. These complexes act as efficient catalysts for visible light-driven, reductive C–C bond formation from unactivated alkyl bromides and [2 + 2] cycloaddition of styrenes. Besides, green and sky-blue OLEDs fabricated with these complexes showed EQEs up to 16.5 %. They were also employed as sensitizers for phosphor-sensitized fluorescent OLEDs (PSF-OLEDs) with EQE up to 14.3%. [Chem. Sci., 2016, 7, 6083] [7] Objective 4. We reported a panel of Au(I) and Au(III) complexes bearing arylacetylide ligands with narrow band-gap. These complexes display interesting luminescent properties: Au(I) complexes (1b-3b) mainly display prompt fluorescence (1IL, τ = 2.7–12 ns) whereas Au(III) complexes (1a-3a) mainly phosphorescence (3IL, τ = 104–205 μs). By using ultrafast time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy, the intersystem crossing (ISC) rate constants (kISC) were found to be on the order of 106–108 s-1 for the Au(I) complexes but 1010–1011 s-1 for the Au(III) analogues. DFT/TDDFT calculations revealed that the energy gap between the singlet and triplet excited states (ΔEST) with effective spin-orbit coupling (SOC) for Au(I) systems is much larger than that for the Au(III) counterparts, thus resulting in the poor ISC efficiency for the former. [Chem. Sci. DOI: 10.1039/C6SC03775E] [8] Objectives 4 and 6. We reported a series of luminescent pincer-type cyclometalated platinum(II) complexes containing tridentate π–extended C^N^N ligand and chloride/ pentafluorophenylacetylide as auxiliary ligand. These complexes are strongly emissive with quantum yields up to almost unity in solution at room temperature. They acted as catalyst for photoinduced reductive cyclization of alkyl bromides with conversions and yields up to 99 % and 78 % respectively (1 mol % Pt catalyst). They also showed excellent performance as emissive dopant in OLED with EQEs of up to 22.8 %. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2015, 54, 2084] [9] Objective 5. We have synthesized an amphiphilic, PEG-functionalized Au(III) complex (AM-Au) with emission quantum yield and lifetime of 4.5% and 117 μs respectively in degassed aqueous solution. This complex can self-assemble into nanoparticles with diameter of ~100 nm in aqueous solution. Although it is non-toxic under dark condition, it shows significant cytotoxicity in the presence of light. ESR measurements evidenced that singlet oxygen (1O2) is generated by AM-Au in aqueous solution upon light-irradiation. [Chem. Commun. 2016, 52, 13273] [10] Objective 7. We reported a luminescent platinum(II) complex, [Pt(C^N^N)(C≡NtBu)]ClO4 (1a, HC^N^N= 6-phenyl-2,2’-bipyridyl), that intercalates between the nucleobases of nucleic acids, accompanied by an increase in emission intensity and/or a significant change in the maximum emission wavelength. The changes in emission properties measured with double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) are different from those with dsDNA used in the binding reactions. Complex 1a exhibited potent anticancer activity towards cancer cells in vitro and inhibited tumor growth in a mouse model. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2014, 53, 10119] [11] Objective 7. A cyclometalated Pd(II) NHC complex displayed potent killing activity toward cancer cell lines (IC50=0.09–0.5 μM) but is less cytotoxic toward a normal human fibroblast cell line (CCD-19Lu, IC50=11.8 μM). In vivo anticancer studies revealed that this complex significantly inhibited tumor growth in a nude mice model. Proteomics data and in vitro biochemical assays reveal that the anticancer effects include inhibition of an epidermal growth factor receptor pathway, induction of mitochondrial dysfunction, and antiangiogenic activity to endothelial cells. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2016, 55, 11935]

700812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
700812.value: Luminescent transition metal complexes have important applications in diverse areas including photocatalysis, cellular imaging and OLEDs. The research accomplished with this funding has provided useful insights into the understanding of structure-property relationship and expanded the scope of applications of Pt(II), Pd(II) and Au(III) complexes. The results in these works revealed that the properties of these metal complexes largely depend on the design and choice of the ligands. It is clear that with further optimization on the design of ligands, it is possible to realize a tailor-made approach to synthesize metal complexes with desired properties for specific applications. Given the tremendous potential of this field of research, we will continue to develop novel luminescent transition metal complexes.

700812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
700812.value: Luminescent transition metal complexes constitute a class of functional materials with interesting properties and diverse applications. The advance in this area has a profound impact on the development of new technologies, thereby bringing about enormous social and economic benefits such as a higher standard of living and increased career opportunities. This project has resulted in the discovery of platinum and palladium complexes as promising materials in OLEDs, photocatalysis and anti-cancer drugs. In addition, this project has facilitated the theoretical studies on the luminescence properties of gold(III) and gold(I) complexes, which are rarely explored in literature. These works have been published in leading international chemistry journals including Angewandte Chemie International Edition, Chemical Science, Chemical Communications, Chemistry-A European Journal and Chemistry-An Asian Journal. The accomplishments made in this project not only shed new light on the understanding of these materials, but also help establish Hong Kong as a world-leading research center for luminescent transition metal complexes.

700912.label: Project Title(Chinese)
700912.value: DNA瞬时电子转移的量子力学模拟

700912.label: Project Objectives
700912.value: We will generalize our open system TDDFT to take into account of the effects of nuclei vibrations in our formalism. This can be done via Ehrenfest dynamics. Care will be taken to treat the effects of the environment on nuclear dynamics. One crucial issue is the computational time. We have demonstrated that it is routine to carry out the TDDFT simulations of nano-devices containing hundreds of atoms up to tens of femtoseconds on a single CPU. To extend the simulation time up to tens of picoseconds, we need (i) to run our computer programs on massive parallel computer clusters; (ii) to implement our method with an approximate DFT method, density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) method; and (iii) to adopt O(N) time-dependent DFTB for electronic dynamics. A numerical code combining all three above will be developed. When the new code is ready, we will apply it to simulate the real time charge transport in DNA. As there are two distinct time scales for the transport, one at femtoseconds and other at picoseconds, simulation time will range from femtoseconds up to tens or hundreds of picoseconds. Two distinct mechanisms have been proposed for DNA charge transfer, the coherent transport and the incoherent hopping process. In majority DNAs, the charge transfer is between the two limits. We will carry out simulations on DNAs of different sequences and analyze the transient charge transfer dynamics in the context of the above two limiting mechanisms. Comparison to experiments will be given when feasible.

700912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
700912.value: 過去幾年我們發展了一系列量子力學方法用於模擬實時電子動力學，特別是複雜體系的動態過程。這裡我們提議利用這些方法去模擬DNA實時電子轉移， 時間從飛秒到幾百匹秒，從而理解電荷轉移機理。 我們將用這一系列量子力學方法，包括線性含時密度函數理論，近似密度函數方法，核電子運動和大規模並行計算。 我們將專注于兩個方面。(1)孤立的DNA；(2)開放的DNA。上述的方法將被運用。 電荷轉移是一個廣泛的現象。我們這個項目將有各種應用。

700912.label: Realisation of objectives
700912.value: We have successfully generalised our open system time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT-OS) to include explicitly nuclear dynamics using Ehrenfest dynamics, and the resulting TDDFT-OS-Ehrenfest method has been applied to simulate the charge transport dynamics of various molecular and nanoscopic systems, for instance, the molecular quantum interference transistor. In addition, an alternative method has been developed to account for the effects of phonon on electron transport: phonons are treated as a both and their effects are included in the self-energy due to electron-phonon interaction. The phonon self-energy is included in the TDDFT-OS formalism to take into account of the phonon effects on electron transport. To improve the efficiency of the simulation, we implement the TDDFT-OS-Ehrenfest method with density functional time-binding (DFTB) theory, and further modify our codes to run parallel computation. O(N) algorithms have been introduced to improve the efficiency of matrix production further. As a result, the resulting TDDFT-OS-DFTB code is quite efficient, and is being used to simulate the charge transports in complex systems including DNA.

To extend the simulation time up to tens of picoseconds, we need (i) to run our computer programs on massive parallel computer clusters; (ii) to implement our method with an approximate DFT method, density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) method; and (iii) to adopt O(N) time-dependent DFTB for electronic dynamics. A numerical code combining all three above will be developed.

When the new code is ready, we will apply it to simulate the real time charge transport in DNA. As there are two distinct time scales for the transport, one at femtoseconds and other at picoseconds, simulation time will range from femtoseconds up to tens or hundreds of picoseconds. Two distinct mechanisms have been proposed for DNA charge transfer, the coherent transport and the incoherent hopping process. In majority DNAs, the charge transfer is between the two limits. We will carry out simulations on DNAs of different sequences and analyze the transient charge transfer dynamics in the context of the above two limiting mechanisms. Comparison to experiments will be given when feasible.

700912.label: Major findings and research outcome
700912.value: 1. Generalised the open system time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT-OS) to include explicitly nuclear dynamics using Ehrenfest dynamics, and the resulting method is termed as TDDFT-OS-Ehrenfes; 2. An alternative way to take into account the effects of phonons due to electron-phonon interaction is developed by treating phonon as a heat bath and its effects included in the self-energy due to electron-phonon interaction, as a result, a unified formalism of quantum transport including phonon has been established; 3. Combined TDDFT-OS with density functional tight-binding (DFTB) method, and resulting TDDFT-OS-DFTB method has been employed to simulate molecular and nanoscopic electronic devices; 4. Implemented the TDDFT-OS-DFTB in parallel computing so that complex open systems and devices can be modelled.

700912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
700912.value: Further improvement on the efficiency of TDDFT-OS-DFTB is warranted to model complex systems and long time dynamics. This can be achievement through fast algorithms for solving coupled differential equations, and implementation of TDDFT-OS-DFTB on massive parallel machines. Another area of development is to the application of TDDFT-OS-DFTB to realistic electronic and optoelectronic devices, for instance, organic light emitting diode (OLED) and solar cell.

700912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
700912.value: In this project, we developed an efficient quantum mechanical method to simulate electron transport of realistic open systems and devices in real time. Effects of phonon or nuclear motion are explicitly taken into account. Further more, the resulting TDDFT-OS-DFTB method is implemented on parallel machine, paving the way for quantum mechanical simulation of realistic electronic and optoelectronic devices. Over the years our work opened the field of first-principles quantum mechanical simulation of open systems, and the development of TDDFT-OS-DFTB method has consolidated our position in the field.

701212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
701212.value: 保險風險理論裡的Gerber-Shiu函數伸延與折現賠償總額

701212.label: Project Objectives
701212.value: One of the main objectives is to emphasize the importance of taking dependency among variables into account in insurance risk modelling. Two general classes of dependent risk processes which serve different purposes are considered. Another main objective is to propose further generalizations of Gerber-Shiu function which can accommodate both the (moments of) discounted claim costs until ruin as well as other variables defined before the time of ruin such as the surplus after the penultimate claim before ruin. From a numerical or computational point of view in generating examples, the project also promotes the use of recursive procedures (e.g. in computing higher moments in terms of lower moments) as well as defective renewal equations. The latter is particularly useful because once a quantity is known to satisfy a defective renewal equation, algorithms are available in the literature in obtaining two-sided bounds and asymptotics. From a technical viewpoint, the proposed project is expected to promote the matrix Dickson-Hipp operators and our novel generalized discounted density which will stimulate and help to solve new research problems in insurance risk theory. With formulas for the higher moments of discounted aggregate claims derived from the proposed project, the computation of the variance, skewness and kurtosis becomes possible. This is important because the distribution of aggregate claims tends to be skewed to the right, and the expectation itself cannot truly reflect the associated risks. Moreover, from a practical point of view moment-based approximations can be performed. Since traditional risk processes without dependency assumption can be obtained as a special case of our model with dependencies, all computational procedures in the proposal are also applicable to the independent case. This allows for comparison of the ruin-related quantities under the independent and the dependent assumptions. Numerical examples will be run to illustrate the potential danger of ignoring dependencies among certain factors in insurance modelling.

701212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701212.value: The proposed project is about insurance risk theory (particularly ruin theory), which involves the application of mathematical tools and statistical models to study how quantities such as income and expenses of insurance companies affect their associated risks. From the perspective of financial risk management, it is very important for an insurer to ensure there is sufficient capital to deal with adverse claims experience. It is risk theory that provides a solid foundation for the quantitative treatment of various risk measures, such as the probability the company ever becomes bankrupt or ruined, the time of ruin, and the amount of shortfall in case of bankruptcy. Much of the above information is contained in a mathematical function known as the Gerber-Shiu function introduced about a decade ago. The goal of the proposed project is two-fold. The first one is motivated by the fact that researchers have been mostly analyzing the same Gerber-Shiu function over the past decade. Although the function contains vast amount of information, only variables defined at the time of ruin can be analyzed. Therefore, we aim at incorporating certain information before ruin in attempt to generalize the Gerber-Shiu function and further unify the study of various general quantities. These attributes of the paths of surplus process leading to ruin are of particular importance since they can serve as early warning of the possibility of bankruptcy and are of interest to both insurers and regulatory authorities. Another aim of the project is to perform the above analysis particularly in risk processes involving dependence between the claim severities and/or the times between claims (in contrast to most traditional analysis in which these dependencies are ignored). In order to ensure that an accurate estimation of the risks faced by an insurance company can be made, it is important to set up a model which correctly describes the occurrences of claims and the amount of the claims. Different insurers may require different mathematical models. For example, certain insurers face the risks of highly infectious diseases which produce exceptionally frequent stream of dependent large claims. In this case, the modelling of ‘environmental states’ describing the possible outbreak of diseases appears appropriate. In contrast, a longer period between two earthquakes is highly likely to result in more serious damage and hence larger claims, and this in turn requires the time elapsed since the last earthquake to have an impact on insurance losses arising from the next one. 建議的研究項目包括保險風險理論（尤其是破產理論），我們將利用應用數學和統計模型來量化保險公司的收入和支出如何影響其相關風險。從金融風險管理的角度來看，保險公司必須確保有足夠的資金來應付可能發生的大額保險賠償。風險理論提供了一個堅實的基礎幫助我們以量化的方式研究各種風險，如公司破產的概率，何時破產，破產時的虧損。大約十年前推出的Gerber-Shiu函數正載有大部份上述信息。 這個研究項目有兩個目標。第一，在過去的十年裡，大部份的研究人員一直在分析著相同的Gerber-Shiu函數。雖然Gerber-Shiu函數包含了大量的信息，但是這些信息全都是破產時的變量。因此，我們的目標是在傳統的Gerber-Shiu函數中加入破產發生前的信息。我們擬議的Gerber-Shiu函數的伸延將統一很多與破產有關的研究。再者，這些破產前的信息對保險公司和監管機構極為重要，因為它們可以用作預警破產的可能性。 第二，我們旨在於一個很真實的模型下進行以上分析。在這個模型底下，每個保險索賠金額與每次索賠之間的時間都息息相關(但在傳統的分析中這些關係經常被忽略）。為了確保可以準確估計保險公司面臨的風險，我們必須建立真實的模型來描述索賠的時間和金額。不同的保險公司可能需要不同的模型。舉例來說，傳染性很強的疾病可能令某些保險公司面臨異常頻繁的巨額賠償。在這種情況下，我們需要適當地模擬在不同環境狀態下可能發生的疾病。可是，如果一間保險公司的主要風險源自地震的索償，模型則必須反映出以下事實：兩次地震之間的時間越長，導致的損害很大可能更嚴重。

701212.label: Realisation of objectives
701212.value: During the entire period of the project, I have published a total of 12 research papers that are supported by this research grant (and the grant is acknowledged in all these publications). The realization of the objectives is summarized below (in relation to the publications in Part C of the report, and the numbering of publications follows that in Part C). - The 1st objective (about the modelling of dependent risk processes) has been addressed in the publication items 2, 3, 5, 7 and 10. - The 2nd objective (about further generalizations of Gerber-Shiu function) has been addressed in the publication items 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 12. - The 3rd objective (about the use of recursive procedures and defective renewal equations) has been addressed in ALL publication items. - The 4th objective (about the use of matrix Dickson-Hipp operators and generalized discounted density) has been addressed in the publication items 3, 4, 5 and 10. - The 5th objective (about the computation of higher moments of of discounted aggregate claims) has been addressed in publication items 2, 4, 5, 8 and 12. - The 6th objective (about the comparison of the ruin-related quantities under the independent and the dependent assumptions) has been addressed in publication items 2 and 5. Therefore, all the project objectives have been achieved.

701212.label: Major findings and research outcome
701212.value: I have produced a total of 12 research outputs as a result of this research grant. In particular, 6 of them are published in "Insurance: Mathematics and Economics" and 2 are in the "Scandinavian Actuarial Journal", and these are widely regarded as the two top journals in Actuarial Science. The major findings are concerned with the discounted aggregate claim amounts until ruin Z in various insurance risk models. Specifically, in publication item 5 it is found that the correlation between Z and the ruin time T sometimes takes on negative values, (which at first glance seems to contradict the intuition that more claims are expected to occur over a longer period). However, we are able to provide probabilistic interpretation of the results. Another related outcome regarding risk models with dividend payments to shareholders is given in publication items 8 and 12. In these two publications, we compute the pairwise correlation between Z, T and the total discounted dividends paid until ruin D. It is found that the correlation between Z and D (i.e. payments to policyholders and shareholders respectively) may take on positive or negative values, and interpretations are given as well.

701212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701212.value: While the current projects focuses on the study of the discounted aggregate claims until ruin, the ideas and techniques developed in the project (such as the use of generalized moment-based discounted densities) have the potential to enable the analysis of strongly path-dependent quantities in insurance risk processes. These possibly include e.g. amount of capital injections or tax payments made, the average surplus before ruin, occupation times before ruin, stochastic integrals involving the discounted values of small perturbations and large claims, etc. At this moment, in addition to thinking about these quantities myself, I intend to ask current postgraduate students to further look into these problems, and I will also discuss these ideas to other researchers in conferences and seminars and explore the opportunities for collaboration.

701212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
701212.value: The analysis of aggregate claims faced by an insurance company is a very important topic, since the insurer typically needs to estimate such a quantity in order to ensure that it has the capacity to deal with adverse claims experience. While claims represent the insurer's payments to its policyholders, another important quantity of interest is the total discounted dividend which is the insurance company's payments to its shareholders (that is also regarded as the value of firm in corporate finance). Whether these two quantities tend to move in the same or in opposite directions is of both theoretical as well as practical interest. Although they both come from the same source (i.e. insurer's surplus), they could both be large if the insurance company survives long enough for both claims and dividends to accumulate. A high positive correlation indicates that the needs of the two groups (i.e. policyholders and shareholders) could be satisfied at the same time, while a negative correlation may suggest conflicting interests between the groups. Our results indicate that the correlation make take on positive or negative values depending on the specifics of the model parameters.

701612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701612.value: Polycyclic structures, including those with embedded seven membered carbocycles, occur in many bioactive natural products, and their efficient construction is a challenge in organic synthesis. This proposal aims to investigate a relatively novel approach for the generation of these systems, through transannular (4+3) cycloadditions, and (5+2) cycloadditions. Whereas most cycloadditions have been investigated in the intermolecular and intramolecular context, the transannular approach is under-investigated, although it may be equally efficient as the intramolecular mode. In particular, the transannular (4+3) cycloaddition of epoxy enol silanes may represent a new entry toward the synthesis of the nanomolar anti-angiogenic natural product, cortistatin A. The realization of the transannular (5+2) cycloaddition through a carbene cyclization cycloaddition cascade reaction could efficiently provide a tetracycle from a monocyclic starting material and would represent the first example of this kind of transannular cycloaddition in the literature. The successful development of these reactions and investigation of their scope would provide a powerful concept to complement existing approaches for the synthesis of polycyclic natural products. 多环的分子結構，包括那些具有七元碳环结构的多环化合物，存在于许多活性天然产物之中。高效地构建这些多元环化合物是有机化学领域的一个挑战。本项计划的目的在于通过研究跨环（4+3）环加成反应和跨环（5+2）环加成反应，为这些多元环体系的合成开发一条相对新颖的合成方法。現今分子间和分子内的环加成反应多数都已经被研究过了，但与分子内的环加成同样高效的跨环环加成反应却较少被關注。尤其需要指出的是，环氧烯醇硅醚的跨环环加成反应可以用于合成具有纳摩尔浓度抗血管生成活性的天然产物cortistatin A。通过卡宾环化-环加成级联反应实现的跨环（5+2）环加成反应，可以从一个单环化合物原料出发高效地构建出一个四环的中间体，这也将是文献中关于此类跨环环加成反应的首例报道。这些反应的成功开发及它们应用范围的研究将为现有多环天然产物的合成方法提供一个强而有力的补充。

701612.label: Realisation of objectives
701612.value: The reaction conditions and scope of the transannular (4+3) cycloaddition has been adequately explored. A total of 7 macrocyclic epoxy ketone substrates have been synthesized, and their cycloadditions were explored. Some of these are extremely favorable. While the typical inter- or intramolecular cycloaddition proceeded from the silyl enol ether derivatives of epoxy ketones under Lewis acid catalysis, we found that some transannular cycloadditions can proceed only base-only conditions, providing an alternative environment with a different set of functional group compatibilities for applications in synthesis. As a bonus, we found that, in the course of examining the conditions for the (4+3) cycloaddition, that when the diene is replaced by an arene, that Friedel-Crafts cyclization proceeded. Due to our mechanistic, computational investigations that found the electrophilic intermediate as an activated epoxide, the cycloadditions AND the Friedel-Crafts cyclizations all proceeded with conservation of optical purity. Using the intramolecular (4+3) cycloaddition, we completed a formal total synthesis of cortistatin A and J. The transannular (4+3) cycloaddition findings were then applied to the synthesis of cortistatin A. After about 20 steps, we reached an asymmetric epoxy ketone precursor to ultimately target cortistatin A, but the desired cycloaddition did not proceed. We believe that some stereoelectronic factors are preventing the usually favorable cycloaddition. Therefore we have re-designed another epoxyketone precursor to try the transannular cycloaddition again. The redeveloped (4+3) cycloaddition is not yet realized and this is why only objective 3 is incomplete. An MPhil student undertook a brief study of a transannular carbene cyclization cycloaddition cascade reaction. The required macrocyclic diazoketone substrate having both cis and trans-double bonds as the dipolarophile were synthesized successfully, but both failed to undergo the desired cascade reaction. After a step by step investigation of each step of the cascade reaction, it was found that it was the final transannular cycloaddition that failed to occur, since the intermolecular cycloaddition proceeded smoothly. In this case, apparently the transannular interactions disfavoured the approach of the dipolarophile to the carbonyl ylide.

701612.label: Major findings and research outcome
701612.value: 1. The transannular (4+3) cycloaddition substrates and their reactions have been investigated and found to generate polycyclic ketones in moderate to good yields. These results are being prepared as a manuscript to be submitted. (8.1) and preliminary results have been communicated at conferences, (9.2, 9.3, 9.7). This was mainly done by a Ph. D. student, Ms. Chan (10.2). When the total synthesis is successful, we can expect an additional publication. 2. The formal total synthesis of cortistatins have been accomplished, making it the synthesis that resulted in the highest yields of the natural products reported so far (output 8.3). The results have been communicated at conferences (9.1, 9.4). The work was done in the second half of the studies of a Ph.D. student, Mr. Kuang (10.3) 3. The cycloaddition parameters and mechanistic studies were followed up by a Ph. D. student Mr. Ng (10.1) but his Ph. D. is not yet completed. His work however, has already been reported in output 8.2 and at a conference (9.5). Computations found that the intermediate is an activated epoxide. 4. In the course of examining the Lewis-acid catalyzed cycloaddition, and after recognizing that the intermediate was an activated epoxide, this fact was exploited by a Friedel-Crafts cyclization of arenes. This reaction can provide optically active substituted arenes, and was reported (Output 8.4) and also presented at a conference (9.6). 5. The transannular carbene cyclization cycloaddition cascade reaction precursors were successfully synthesized, but they did not undergo the cascade reaction as planned. Mechanistic investigations revealed that the final transannular cycloaddition was the problematic step. This was the thesis of an MPhil student (10.4). Since the results were unsuccessful for the transannular cycloaddition, this work has not yet been published.

701612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701612.value: We are very close to completing the synthesis of the redesigned, second-generation transannular cycloaddition precursor. When we have this compound in hand, we will study its cycloaddition, which hopefully would be successful. Then we can use this to approach cortistatin A by the transannular cycloaddition strategy, which is expected to be a total synthesis, not a formal synthesis.

701612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
701612.value: The transannular (4+3) cycloaddition was explored and found to be successful and applicable to the de novo synthesis of cortistatin A, a potent, anti-angiogenic agent, whose formal total synthesis has been already achieved. The latter represents the highest yielding route so far, but the transannular route is expected to be even more concise. Our mechanistic and computational investigations revealed that the reactive intermediate in these cycloadditions is an activated epoxide. We have exploited this mechanism and diverted it to a Friedel-Crafts cyclization to afford optically active substituted arenes.

702112.label: Project Title(Chinese)
702112.value: 锰氧化物中电流所致亚稳态的应力场效应

702112.label: Project Objectives
702112.value: To induce metastable phases in thin films of manganite oxides using electric fields/currents. The response to the application of electric fields/currents differs significantly for different manganites. The generation of metastability strongly depends on the inducing mechanism and process. Effort will be made to gain colossal ER effect and enhanced tenability by selecting suitable doping concentration for various manganites. Studies of the strain effects on the metastability and colossal ER induced by fields/currents. A strain-mediated electric-ﬁeld control of the induced ER and metastability is an essential mission for this project. It is known that tensile strain usually enhances resistivity and shifts TC downward, while compressive strain gives rise to opposite effects. To obtain a comprehensive understanding of the strain effects, both compressive and tensile strain will be studied. Buffer layer engineering and piezoelectric effect will be pursued for this study. The underlying physics will be clarified, especially the correlations between the metastability and lattice distortion. To explore the feasibility using such a controllable metastability to form novel field effect devices. This research aims at developing a simple, efficient, and highly reliable field effect heterostructures composing various preovskite oxides. The e-field modulation via lattice distortion and its impacts on the multiphase coexistence and transport properties of manganites will be investigated. Different heterostructures will be designed and optimized.

702112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702112.value: 钙钛矿锰氧化物中呈现的各种新奇的物理现象（如庞磁阻效应等）及其在微电子器件上的应用前景吸引了广泛的研究兴趣。为了克服庞磁阻效应所需强磁场的局限，我们可以通过压电陶瓷来调制锰氧化物的应力状态，从而控制其电磁特性。目前通过这一技术所能达到的调制深度普遍不到10%，尚不能满足实用器件的需求。 我们近期的研究发现使用电场或电流可以在锰氧化物薄膜上诱导出一系列亚稳态。这些亚稳态对微弱电场，光辐射或应力场均极为敏感，展现出巨大的电致电阻效应（甚至高达1800%）。基于这些结果，我们拟进一步探索通过应力场来调制这类亚稳态的可行性，希望最终可以达到对其磁电物性的高度可控。由于被激活在亚稳状态下的锰氧化物对外加场的微细扰动极其敏感，我们可以期待显著增强的场效应和调制深度。这种亚稳体系与压电陶瓷的结合可以进一步开发出新颖的功能场效应管及高度灵敏的电流调制器件。

702112.label: Realisation of objectives
702112.value: The goal of this piece of research is to achieve tunable electric/magnetic properties by controlled lattice deformation, which is induced by electrostrictive/piezoelectric effects. All three proposed objectives have been fully addressed. I. The first objective is to integrate different perovskite oxides with piezoelectric crystal. Rich variety of oxide heterostructures composed with the ABO3 materials like manganites and ferroelectrics were successfully formed. The systems studied in this project include typical manganites La0.39Pr0.24Ca0.37MnO3, La0.7Ba0.3MnO3, Nd0.0.7Sr0.3MnO3, La0.9Ca0.1MnO3, and La0.5Ca0.5MnO3.[1, 5-9, 15, 20] For application of p-n junctions, electron doped La0.9Hf0.1MnO3 was developed and studied.[26] Moreover, different ferroelectrics like BiFeO3, SrRuO3, Bi0.9Nd0.1FeO3, Bi0.9La0.1FeO3, BiFeO3 were grown and examined.[10, 12-14, 16] To gain the highest piezoelectric effect, PMN-PT crystal was widely used to introduce tunable lattice strain.[3, 12-14, 26] Due to the interesting feature of half-doped Pr0.5Sr0.5MnO3 (PSMO), our efforts focused on this system. Since PSMO locates at the phase boundary, the itinerant FMM state is metastable and its electronic localization with antiferromagnetic order happens at low temperature.[3, 4] II. To address the second objective, strain effect on transport and meta-stability were systematically investigated in the formed hetero-structures through the whole project.[1, 2-6, 9-10, 12, 15] Tunable colossal MR and ER effects were gained in heterostructures composed with manganite and ferroelectrics.[3, 6, 17, 19, 25] We applied a constant current to a micro-bridge to excite manganite into metastable states.[1, 3] The feasibility to modulate electric and magnetic properties by tunable strain was achieved by using PMN-PT crystal.[9, 12, 17, 19, 23] Our studies show that many metastable properties of manganites and ferroelectrics, like magnetoresistance (MR), electroresistance (ER), M-I phase transition, and photoconductivity, are strongly related to the lattice deformation, e.g. modulated through the converse piezoelectric effects of PMN-PT.[1, 3, 5-6, 15] Remarkable resistance modulations were observed in LBMO/PMN-PT (R/Rmax~90%) and PSMO/PMN-PT (R/Rmax~85%), demonstrating excellent tunability of the lattice deformation.[6, 3] The field induced metastable states were found to be strongly depend on the coexistence of multi-phases as well.[1,5-6] It can be understood in the frame of phase separation.[1, 5, 9] Our efforts were also made to develop electron-doped manganite. To confirm the n-type conductance, tetravalent Hf4+, which shows a single tetravalent state only, was doped into LaMnO3. It shows a real n-type conductivity as proofed by XPS and Hall-measurements. The M-I phase transition temperature (TP) and MR effect show a strong dependence on the lattice strain, regardless of whether it is tensile or compressive.[26] Moreover, photoconductivity (PC) were studied and abnormal optical response was observed.[5, 12, 14, 25] LPCMO films exhibited both transient and persistent PC when illuminated by visible light. Such PC could be controlled by electric fields across PMN-PT. Detailed analysis and in situ XRD indicate that such modulations were mainly due to the lattice deformation by applied electric fields via converse piezoelectric effect. The observed transient and persistent PC are believed to have different origins.[5, 9] To understand the strain generated by piezoelectric effect, domain change in the misfit strained ferroelectric thin films was also investigated. It may help to the design of ferroelectric thin film devices.[11] Although is not belong to the perovskite oxides, magnetically doped amorphous carbon was studied as well, for its positive colossal MR and PC (as large as 10^5).[2] We found that the electric transport of Co-C films could be effectively modulated by piezoelectric PMN-PT. We observed, for the first time, strain-induced PC in such an amorphous carbon. Without strain, there is no PC effect. Whereas subjected to strain, it exhibited remarkable PC under illumination of a 532-nm light.[7, 27] It is of great interests as the strain usually cannot affect an amorphous system. It may encourage and promote a new field for further study. III. The third objective is to explore the feasibility for potential applications. To achieve this goal, devices by employing such controllable metastability were designed and fabricated, like the field effect devices using TiO2/PMN-PT, heterojunctions utilizing Nd0.7Sr0.3MnO3, La0.9Hf0.1MnO3 and Nb-SrTiO3; [8, 16] capacitors of metal/ferroelectric/semiconductor; [20-21] as well as switching memory devices.[16, 23] The preliminary results demonstrated a potential for oxide-based devices. These preliminary results have emerged great potential for various applications in the development of oxide-based devices.

702112.label: Major findings and research outcome
702112.value: In this project, rich variety of physical properties mediated by lattice train was observed in mixed-valence manganite and ferroelectrics. The major findings obtained in this project include: 1. Various ABO3 perovskite oxides were epitaxially integrated with ferroelectric crystals. They all showed pronounced tunability by the lattice deformation. In particular, the in-plane tensile strain induced by the PMN-PT crystal provides great feasibility. 2. It was revealed that many metastable properties of manganites and ferroelectrics, like magnetoresistance (MR), electroresistance (ER), M-I phase transition, and photoconductivity, are strongly related to the lattice deformation. 3. The competition between coexisted multi-phases could be also mediated by the applied strain induced by piezoelectric effect. 4. Optical response of these perovskites under strain fields were explored. 5. We also paid attention to the electron doped LHMO compound. Its M-I phase transition, MR and ER effect strongly depend on the lattice strain. 6. Domain change in the misfit strained ferroelectric thin films was also studied. It may help to the design of ferroelectric thin film devices. 7. Different devices by using such tunable metastability, like the field effect devices, heterojunctions, capacitors of metal/ferroelectric/semiconductor, as well as switching memory devices, were designed and constructed. The preliminary results demonstrated great potential for oxide-based devices. 8. Due to its positive colossal MR and PC (as large as 10^5), magnetically doped amorphous carbon was studied too, although it is not a perovskite oxide. Similar to manganite and ferroelectrics, the electric transport of Co-C films could also be modulated by piezoelectric PMN-PT. We observed, for the first time, strain-induced PC in amorphous carbon. It is of great interests as the strain usually cannot affect an amorphous system. Directly arisen from this research project, 27 articles were published in peer-reviewed SCI journals [6 in Appl. Phys. Lett. (IF=4.308), 1 in Sci. Rept. (IF=5.578), 1 in JMCC (IF=4.694), 1 in Appl. Surface Sci. (IF=3.150), 2 in J. Alloy & Compounds (IF=3.014), 3 in J. Appl. Phys. D (IF=2.772), 2 in EPL (IF=2.753), 4 in J. Appl. Phys. (IF=2.171)]. We have also presented 4 invited talks at international conferences. In addition, three RPG students were supported and trained by this project.

702112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702112.value: In this research we have explored optimized manganite/ferroelectric composites to achieve large field modulation mediated by lattice strain. Our studies revealed that the metastable states induced in perovskite oxides could be modulated by lattice deformation. Such a metastability is an intrinsic feature of doped manganites and it may even lie at the core of the phase separated perovskites. The lattice deformation, which could change the Jahn-Teller coupling via modifying Mn-O-Mn bond angles or Mn-O bond lengths, can significantly modulate the transport of manganite/ferroelcetrics. The tunability by lattice strain on the metastable states and MR/ER of manganite may promote our interests in developing all oxides heterojunctions or devices. Further investigation and development should focuse at the heterostructures of manganite and ferroelectrics. The integrated system combining manganite and ferroelectrics can emerge some fascinating features, like the switching of rich functionality, optoelectronic sensitivity, and magnetic tunability.

702112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702112.value: Tunable electromagnetic properties by controlled lattice deformation, which is induced by the electrostrictive/piezoelectric effect, were systematically successfully. Various manganite oxides were integrated with selected ferroelectric materials to gain a pronounced modulation. It also revealed some fascinating features, including controlled switching of rich functionality, the strain sensitive photoconductivity (PC), tunable metastability and ER effect. Our studies give rise to the boost interest for unusual effects and potential to develop novel functional devices of perovskite oxides.

702212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702212.value: The current project plans to explore two different strategies in attempts to improve current classical molecular mechanical force fields for simulations of biochemical and chemical systems, with focus on proteins and small molecules interacting with proteins. Molecular mechanical force fields are the foundation for present-day theoretical and computational studies of many molecular systems possessing significance in basic and/or practical researches in chemical and biochemical processes. With the development of efficient computing platforms, molecular mechanical force fields based molecular simulations start to reach the spatial and temporal scales overlapping with experiments. Due to the unprecedented molecular, atomic, and/or electronic details it provided, molecular simulation steady converts itself into a new territory of “experiments”. The accuracy of the MM force fields, therefore, becomes the top priority for broader applications of molecular simulations in providing quantitative information for the interesting molecular processes. We plan to explore two different approaches: ‘top-down” (from quantum mechanical heaven) and “bottom-up” (from molecular mechanical earth). Even though both approaches are for the goal of improving current generation classical molecular mechanical force fields, the focus of each approach is different. The “top-down” approach is aiming to develop systematic route to improve the description of electrostatic interactions in molecules, with focus on static and polarized interactions. Pauli repulsion, dispersion, and other bonded interactions are not the target of current project. The “bottom-up” approach aims to provide improved description for the structural and thermodynamic properties of proteins and protein/substrate complexes. The goal is to first carry out a comprehensive assessment for popular molecular mechanical force fields, and then through advanced data-mining technique provide new force fields with improved performance. Due to the excessive complexity in the developments of molecular mechanical force fields, the current project does not intend to establish a mammoth program for a complete overhaul of current molecular mechanical force fields; instead, it aims to address several issues within well-defined limited scopes. The specific aims for the current projects are: (1) Development of new electrostatic potentials based classical multipole (charge, dipole, …) model for inter-molecular interactions. (2) Development of a computationally efficient and accurate scheme to describe the polarizations. (3) Development of a water model based on the model of distributed polarizabilities. (4) Large-scale assessment and refinement of current MM force fields. 本研究计划从两个不同的策略来探讨改进用于生物和化学分子体系计算机模拟的分子力学势场，尤其侧重于适用蛋白质分子和小分子配基的势场。现代计算机技术的发展是的基于分子力学势场的模拟在时间和空间尺度上开始与实验重合，从而使得计算机模拟成为一个渔产铜实验手段平行的新的“实验”方法。因此改进分子力学力场的准确性成为分子模拟技术成为更广泛的应用下必须最优先考虑的问题。 我们计划在探索两种不同的方法：“自上向下”（从量子力学的天堂）和“自下而上”（分子力学大地）。虽然这两种方法的目的都是为改善当前通用的经典分子力学力场，每种方法的侧重点是不同的。 “自上而下”的方法的目标是提高分子的静电相互作用的描述，重点发展有系统的研究路线以改进对泡利作用，色散作用，及其他共价相互作用描述。 “自下而上”的方法旨在提供更好的蛋白质和蛋白质/底物复合物的结构和热力学性质的描述。我们的目标是首先对当前流行的分子力学力场进行一个全面的评估，然后通过先进的数据挖掘技术来逐步改进它们。 本项目并不打算建立一个庞大的计划来彻底改革目前的分子力学力场。相反，它的目的是在有限范围内解决的几个明确定义的问题。当前项目的具体目标是：（1）基于经典的静电多极矩发展的新的分子间的相互作用模型。 （2）开发准确描述的极化的新的模型。 （3）发展分布式极化的水模型。 （4）大规模评估和改进目前的分子力学力场。

702212.label: Realisation of objectives
702212.value: We have achieved all the 4 objectives. 4 papers and one PhD thesis have been published on leading international chemistry journals, including J. Chem. Phys.., J. Comput. Chem, J. Chem. Theory Comput., and J. Phys. Chem. B. The important findings are summarized below: Objective 1. A new enhanced sampling method combining the reaction coordinate (RC)-guided sampling and generalized ensemble algorithms with classical CHARMM force field is developed in this study. In this new method, in order to calculate free energy changes more precisely, the RC-guided component is responsible to fast sampling of the relevant conformational changes along a set of predefined collective variables and the generalized ensemble component enhanced the sampling of the remaining degrees of freedom. A testing system to mimic the peptidyl bond is examined with this new method, which shows much better sampling efficiency than the widely used umbrella sampling and integrated tempering sampling. [J. Chem. Phys., 2014, 141, 044108] Objective 2. Two key approximations are developed to improve the efficiency of the density fragment interaction (DFI) approach and thus enable the calculations for large molecules: the electrostatic interactions between fragments are computed efficiently by means of polarizable electrostatic-potential-fitted atomic charges; and frozen fragment pseudopotentials, similar to the effective fragment potentials that can be fitted from interactions between small molecules, are employed to take into account the Pauli repulsion effect among fragments. Our reformulated and parallelized DFI method demonstrates excellent parallel performance based on the benchmarks for the system of 256 water molecules. By constructing the global, block-wise Fock matrix and density matrix, we develop a new SCF scheme in which the inter-fragment interactions can be updated concurrently without converging the fragment electronic structure. Therefore, many highly efficient numerical techniques such as the direct inversion of the iterative subspace method can be employed to converge simultaneously the electronic structure of all fragments, reducing significantly the computational cost. Numerical examples for water clusters of different sizes suggest that the method shall be very useful in improving the scalability of fragment quantum chemistry methods. [J. Comput. Chem., 2016, 37, 321-326] Objective 3. A new polarizable water model combining charge response kernel (CRK) method and polarizable point dipole (PPD) method was developed. We proved that although the CRK matrix of three-site water model has 9 elements, it only carries two independent variables, and these two variables only rely on the water geometry and the in-plane polarizability. Thus besides the CRK matrix located on each atomic site, an additional polarizability residing on oxygen atom specifically inducing dipole moment along the direction perpendicular to the water plane was added in our model. With the addition of the out-of-plane description, some physical properties were much enhanced. [PhD work, unpublished] Objective 4. An adaptive multi-resolution method at different force field levels was developed for the simulation of complex heterogeneous systems such as the protein molecules. The energy functions of the all-atomic and coarse-grained force fields are coupled as a general Hamiltonian for the whole system, and the interactions between two sites are automatically adjusted according to the distance. The atomic structure and thermodynamic properties of the entire system are thus maintained naturally during the simulation processes, which would be very useful in many biomolecular simulations where atomistic details are critically needed. [J. Chem. Theory Comput., 2014, 10, 2528-2536]

702212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702212.value: Molecular mechanical force fields are the foundation for nowadays theoretical and computational studies of many molecular systems possessing significance in basic and/or practical researches in chemical and biochemical processes. It is critical to develop new molecular mechanical force fields and new methodologies to apply more complicated systems and to sample as many as conformations despite of being trapped in energy local minima. It is anticipated that the new enhanced sampling method will be a powerful tool in the study of more complicated molecular systems, especially the ones solvated in explicit water box and enzymatic reactions for which the conformational change is an important factor to control or regulate the target events. The adaptive AA+CG method can be applied into the conventional QM/MM model to build a three-layer force field, in which the active site is described as the QM subsystem, and the environment is described as the MM subsystem by using the AA+CG model. The polarizable water model can be further employed in the multi-resolution approach as the fourth level. At the same time, the DFI scheme also facilitates the large-scale quantum mechanical simulations for water and other large biological system. Its electrostatic interactions between fragments are calculated by simple ESP charges to improve the speed of simulations with moderate accuracy, which sheds light on the speed up of the QM/MM calculations. Our serial methods would play a bridging role on the broad spectrum of force fields from QM to all-atomic MM to coarse-grained models.

702212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702212.value: Thanks to the development of more and more powerful computing platforms, current classical molecular mechanical force fields simulating biochemical and chemical is able to reach the spatial and temporal scales overlapping with experiments. Due to the unprecedented molecular, atomic, and/or electronic details it provided, molecular simulations are evolving into a new territory of “experiments”. Therefore, improving the accuracy of the MM force fields becomes the priority to facilitate molecular simulations into broader applications. Accordingly, polarizable force fields behave better than traditional MM force fields in describing electron distribution in the presence of perturbation. A hybrid all-atomic and coarse-grained model extends the simulation scale by treating the surroundings from longer distance as a more simplified model. The combined umbrella sampling and integrated tempering sampling method significantly improved sampling efficiencies within the limited simulation time. The findings from this project have been published in top international chemistry journals including Journal of Chemical Physics, Journal of Computational Chemistry, Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation, and Journal of Physical Chemistry B.

702312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702312.value: Bioinspired investigations have long been an appealing strategy in chemical research. The 3Fe-4S cuboidal cluster core in iron-sulfur proteins constitutes an intriguing type of naturally occurring ligand for metal ion binding, leading to the formation of catalytically active [1:3] site-differentiated Fe4S4 cubanes, together with heterometallic MFe3S4 cubanes. A number of the metal centers that have been chelated by 3Fe-4S cuboidal cluster ligand are potentially active for group (such as nitrene) transfer reactions, which represent an important type of transformation in both biological system and organic synthesis. The proposed research focuses on the endeavor to exploit and establish the nitrene transfer chemistry of metal-sulfur cubane clusters. Key methodologies in this project are based on the attractive features expected for 3Fe-4S cuboidal cluster-chelated metal centers, including a single reactive metal site and robust cubane cluster core (particularly for tripodal LS3-protected ones), and also the relatively high stability well documented for Ru=NR species reactive toward nitrene transfers. Among the main studies proposed is the exploration of synthetic routes to RuFe3S4 cubanes, particularly those bearing Ru=NR groups and undergoing nitrene transfer toward phosphines, thioethers, alkenes, or CH bonds. Heterometallic MFe3S4 (M = Co, Ni) cubanes and [1:3] site-differentiated Fe4S4 cubanes, which are closest synthetic analogues of the corresponding native clusters, will also be explored about the formation and detection of M=NR (M = Co, Ni, Fe) complexes. The catalytic nitrene transfer reactions to be examined include sulfimidation of thioethers, aziridination of alkenes, and amination of C-H bonds, using catalysts MFe3S4 and nitrogen sources such as PhI=NR and organic azides. The findings in this project would provide insight into the catalytic potential of the ubiquitous native iron-sulfur clusters of iron-sulfur proteins. 生物啓發研究一直是化學研究中富有吸引力的策略之一。鉄硫蛋白所含3Fe-4S缺頂立方烷簇是一種天然的與金屬結合的配体，可形成有催化活性的[1:3]位置區別型Fe4S4立方烷簇，以及異金屬MFe3S4立方烷簇。多種與3Fe-4S缺頂立方烷簇配体結合的金屬中心具有潛在的基團（例如氮烯）轉移反應活性，這類基團轉移反應是生物體係和有機合成中的重要反應。本研究項目致力探索和確立金屬硫立方烷簇的氮烯轉移化學。採用的主要方法建基於與3Fe-4S缺頂立方烷簇結合的金屬中心之特徵，包括單一的金屬反應位置和穩定的立方烷型簇核（特別是經由三足配体LS3保護），以及具有氮烯轉移活性Ru=NR物種的較高穩定性。主要研究内容包括探索RuFe3S4立方烷簇的合成方法，尤其是含Ru=NR基團並能轉移氮烯至膦，硫醚，烯烴或碳氫鍵的RuFe3S4立方烷簇。並探索異金屬MFe3S4 (M = Co, Ni)簇和[1：3]位置區別型Fe4S4簇（這兩類簇最接近相應天然簇）的M=NR (M = Co, Ni, Fe) 配合物的形成和檢測。涉及的MFe3S4簇催化氮烯轉移反應包括硫醚的硫亞胺化，烯烴氮丙啶化和碳氫鍵胺化；所用氮源包括PhI=NR和有機曡氮化合物。本項目研究將有助開拓鉄硫蛋白所含天然鐵硫簇的潛在催化活性。

702612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702612.value: The Pearl River Delta (PRD) has extensive Quaternary clayey aquitards (low-permeability geological units) of marine origin, overlying a regional basal sandy aquifer. The aquitards range in thickness from 20 to 40 m and consist of two distinct units: an upper layer of Holocene age and a lower one of Pleistocene age. Our previous studies have shown that the aquifer-aquitard system is an extremely reducing environment and contains an exceptionally large total ammonium mass. Ammonium occurs at concentrations up to 390 mg/L in the basal aquifer and the concentrations in the pore water in the aquitards are about three to four times higher. This ammonium is natural, areally extensive and originated in the organic-rich aquitards. The generation and migration of ammonium are always associated with complicated microbiological processes. Modern microbiology in contaminated aquifers has been a hot topic over the past 10 years. Relative to aquifers, little microbiological research has been directed at aquitards. The aim of this proposal is to study the roles of microbiology in the generation, preservation and migration of abnormally high ammonium in the aquitards of the PRD. We will investigate the microbial distribution and community structure at three representative sites, and the microbial activities related to the ammonium cycle and their reaction rates using molecular microbiological and isotopic methods. The work will be conducted by an experienced interdisciplinary team with expertise in isotope studies, hydrogeochemistry, microbiology, and numerical modeling. The team will use multiple techniques including field coring and core hydrochemical analyses, sampling of pore water and methane gas, environmental isotope tracers, molecular biology techniques, and numerical flow and transport modeling. The findings of this project will have broad scientific importance not only for the PRD but for other coastal river deltas in Southeast Asia that have aquitards with similar characteristics to those in the PRD. 珠江三角洲存在著廣闊的海相粘土質弱透水層（低滲透系數地質單元）。這些弱透水層覆蓋在區域性的砂質基底含水層上，厚達20-40米，並由兩個不同單元組成：上部的全新統和下部的更新統。本課題組之前的研究表明，該含水層-弱透水層系統處於極端的還原環境中，並存在著大量的銨。基底含水層中氨的最高含量為390 mg/L，而弱透水層孔隙水中銨的含量還要高出其三到四倍。這些銨是在富含有機物的弱透水層中天然產生的，並大量的存在於該區域中。 銨的產生和運移總是伴隨著復雜的微生物活動。在過去的十年中，現代微生物學一直是含水層汙染問題中所研究的熱點課題。相對於含水層，弱透水層中的微生物卻很少被人們直接研究。本提案旨在於研究珠江三角洲弱透水層中與高銨地下水產生，賦存和運移相關的微生物作用。本課題組將會利用分子微生物學方法和同位素手段，調查三個代表性區域的微生物分布和群落結構，以及其活動與氮循環的關系。這個工作將會由一個精通同位素，水文地球化學，微生物學以及數值模擬的經驗豐富的交叉學科團隊來完成。該團隊將應用包括野外打鉆取樣，鉆孔水化分析，孔隙水及甲烷采樣，環境同位素示蹤，分子生物學研究，以及溶質運移數值模擬等多種手段進行研究。該項目的研究結果將會對珠三角以及東南亞類似的海岸帶河流三角洲的研究產生廣泛的學術影響。

702612.label: Realisation of objectives
702612.value: We have completed all the objectives. The completion of all the objectives has led to publication in international SCI journals and conferences. In total, we have published 8 high impact journal papers and there will be a few more in review and preparation and presented our research in 6 international conferences in addition to quite a few presentations in national conferences and universities in Mainland China. Most of the publications are related to isotopic and geochemical studies of the aquitard and aquifer system in the Pearl River Delta (PRD). Two papers are related to microbiological studies. We expected that the microbiological studies could be more productive but the difficulties in sampling and expenses in analysing the samples hindered the productivity. We also achieved something beyond the original scope of the proposal. For example, based on our experience in microbiological studies in the clay-rich sediments in the PRD, we started our study on microbiological processes in the lake mud in Badain Jarain Desert; we speculated that abundant ammonium formed in aquitards rich in organic matter may not be uncommon and this “geologic” source of ammonium may present a large and hitherto unappreciated source of nitrogen discharging to surface waters. Such speculation was later confirmed by the discovery of the high ammonium concentration in coastal areas in the Po River Delta, Italy, Red River delta, Vietnam, and coastal areas in the Netherlands and Spain. We intend to conduct comparative studies on groundwater ammonium among a few coastal river deltas and write up a review paper on naturally occurring ammonium on coastal aquifers.

702612.label: Major findings and research outcome
702612.value: Geochemical studies Core sediments of boreholes from the PRD aquifer–aquitard system were collected for the geochemical analyses. The results demonstrated that the existence and contents of As(III) and As(V) were dominantly directly related to the terrestrial detrital sources. As(III) was speculated to exist on amorphous iron oxide. Sedimentary organic matter was not correlated with any oxidation states of solid arsenic. Good hydrodynamic conditions of the fluvial dominated sedimentary environment seemed to favor the enrichment of As(III) and As(V). Various heavy metals in both sediments and groundwater were analyzed. This study demonstrates that heavy metal mobility in the field is not entirely consistent with the potential mobility as indicated by sediment analysis, due to the complicated hydrogeochemical conditions in the groundwater system. Microbiological studies Based on the investigation on the community composition and abundance of aerobic/anaerobic ammonia/ammonium-oxidizing microorganisms (AOM) in the aquitard in the PRD, it is concluded that AOA amoA gene abundance positively correlated with pH and ammonium concentration, whereas AOB amoA gene abundance negatively correlated with C/N ratio. Overall there is a low diversity of AOM communities in natural aquitard of rich ammonium. Bacterial 16S rRNA gene clone libraries were constructed for microbial identifications and community structures in different strata. Community structures were significantly modified by geological conditions. Higher bacterial diversity was observed in samples from the shallow Holocene aquitard and aquifer, while in the deep and older aquitard and basal aquifer, bacterial diversity was much lower. Isotopic studies and 1D modelling The depth profiles of Cl- and isotopes of δ2H, and δ18O in boreholes in the aquifer-aquitard system in the PRD were obtained directly from porewater samples or by centrifuging the core sediment samples. A one-dimensional (1D) model based on the sedimentation and sea level changes of the PRD during the Holocene was built to investigate the transport mechanisms of Cl-, δ2H, and δ18O. The modeling result shows that diffusion solely is adequate to reconstruct the observed profiles, which indicates that diffusion is the dominant vertical transport mechanism. The effective diffusion coefficient of the aquitard and the aquifer were estimated. Then a model is also constructed to investigate the impact of sedimentation and sea level changes on transport of Cl− in the system. Chloride concentration profiles are reconstructed for nine boreholes, covering a wide area of the PRD. It is further confirmed that diffusion is the regionally dominant vertical transport mechanism across the aquitards in the PRD.

702612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702612.value: The Pearl River Delta (PRD) has extensive clayey aquitards of marine origin overlying a basal aquifer. The aquifer-aquitard system is an extremely reducing environment and contains an exceptionally large ammonium mass of natural origin. The aim of this project is to carry out geochemical, isotopic and geomicrobiologic studies of ammonium-rich aquitards. Various heavy metals in both sediments and groundwater were analyzed. Various geochemical parameters, sedimentary organic matter, and carbonate content as well as major ions, and dissolved organic carbon were also measured. It is concluded that heavy metal mobility in the field is not entirely consistent with the potential mobility as indicated by sediment analysis, due to the complicated hydrogeochemical conditions in the groundwater system. Based on the investigation on the community composition and abundance of microorganisms in the aquitard, it is concluded that community structures were significantly modified by geological conditions. A one-dimensional model based on the sedimentation and sea level changes during the Holocene was built to investigate the transport mechanisms of chloride and oxygen and hydrogen isotopes. The results show that diffusion solely is adequate to reconstruct the observed profiles. The findings will have broad scientific importance not only for the PRD but for other river deltas

703112.label: Project Objectives
703112.value: To study the stoichiometry, geometry, energetics as well as stability anomalies (i.e. magic cluster occurence) among pure and polymetallic Cu-Ag-Au halide clusters. The objective of this task is to characterize mono- and polynuclear ion clusters present in multicomponent electrolyte solutions (e.g. the simplest case would be a binary Cu-Au aqueous fluid) given that such a solution would more closely resemble the compositional complexity of a natural fluid. The aim of this research topic is to use FT-ICR mass spectrometry to a) characterize pure and mixed Cu, Ag and Au ion cluster stoichiometries, cluster stabilities as well as stability discontinuities (i.e. highly stable species) in pure and mixed (e.g. binary, ternary) solutions, b) to interpret ion cluster abundances using ab initio methods and c) calculate thermodynamic properties of individual ion cluster species as a function of temperature. To characterize the stoichiometries, structures, energetics and solvation behaviour of PGE halide clusters MX2-4 (M=Ru, Os, Rh, Ir, Pd & Pt; X=Cl, Br, I). The goal of this research topic centers around characterizing individual PGE clusters, both unsolvated and in the presence of water, using FT-ICR mass spectrometry. These mass spectrometric studies will be complemented using a recently constructed precision leak-valve system used for ion cluster solvation studies. From such PGE ion cluster studies we hope to gain insight into a) the abundance and distribution of individual PGE-containing ion clusters, both mono- and polynuclear, b) the affinity of water molecules to individual PGE ion clusters, c) the thermodynamic properties of individual PGE ion cluster solvation reactions, specifically solvation equilibrium constants determined both experimentally and quantum chemically. To study the speciation and structure of lanthanide halide clusters in low-density water vapor using FT-ICR mass spectrometry and quantum chemistry. The objective of this topic centers around the speciation and solvation of lanthanide-containing ion clusters and builds on insights gained from our ion cluster solvation studies conducted under topic 2. These studies will provide new data with respect to the molecular-scale speciation of lanthanide clusters in low density aqueous fluids and focus on a) the growth of lanthanide clusters according to the stepwise reaction LnnX3n-1 + LnX3 = Lnn+1X3n+2 and b) the stuctures and thermodynamic properties of dry and solvated polynuclear lanthanide salt clusters.

703112.value: 在地殼內估計含有3x10^17公噸的水，相等於全球海洋的五分之一。這些水份流經地殼內的岩層，並在對流過程中向上流動，經減壓後到達沸點。原本的液態水份變為兩種狀態，一種是液體，另一種是低密度蒸氣，兩者擁有截然不同的物理及化學性質。其中的低密度蒸氣在近年引起廣泛注意，被認為在地殼內運送和聚集金屬元素的過程中扮演重要角色。我們對於這些金屬元素在低密度蒸氣中形成的分子結構所知甚少，研究這些由金屬原子形成的原子簇，有助我們了解含有金屬元素的蒸氣如何在地殼內運送及沉澱出如銅和金等金屬礦床。在過去三十年的實驗研究中，我們得知這些原子簇的特性介乎於單一分子和由無數分子組成的固體狀態之間。近期的實驗讓我們得知這些金屬原子簇存在於稀釋的溶液中。迄今類似有助了解這些重要的原子簇的實驗不多，而此次實驗集中研究氯化銅和金在水溶液中產生的原子簇以及它們的多種微觀及宏觀特性。本研究小組的目標將會是利用傅里對變換離子回旋共振質譜儀（FTI-CR/MS）和量子化學為工具，對這些金屬原子簇進行研究。

703112.label: Realisation of objectives
703112.value: I have recruited one PhD student (Y. Zhang, PhD completion date Jume2018) who is presently conducting his graduate research under HKU-703112. As noted for some of out previous RGC funded research projects, it is challenging to recruit students to work in physical geochemistry, primarily because chemists are unaware of this kind of work, and secondly, students with an Earth Science’s training are usually missing the required chemistry background; Y. Zhang and I have conducted a series of FT-MS experiments in which we have examined the abundance and distribution of transition metal clusters with water solvation shells. These FT-MS experiments are in their completion stage and form the backbone of Y. Zhang’s thesis and a series of in preparation manuscripts. We have also undertaken a series of IR and quantum chemical studies that augment these FT-MS experiments, reported both as single author PI papers and in collaboration with our co-experimenters in Iceland (Prof. A. Stefansson) and New Zealand (Prof. TM Seward). Three published and additional four manuscripts have evolved from this work, one has been published by the PI as single author (Lemke, 2017, J.Chem.Phys), two in collaboration with Prof. Stefansson, and four more are currently in their final stage of preparation and will be submitted in early 2018. These cluster FT-MS studies have further been complemented by stand-alone theoretical studies of REE halide clustering reactions in aqueous media using explicit hydration and PCM solution approaches (Lemke, 2018, in review, PCCP), and a CCSD(T) level study of H2O, H2S and NH3 solvated CuCl, AgCl and AuCl complexes (Lemke, 2018, in prep, J.Chem.Phys). Four additional papers as part of HKU-703112P are still in the pipe-line with some of the delay due to a refurbishment out our FT-MS facility that was initiated by the installation of a new wave-tunable IRMPD OPO/OPA laser system. This new set up also forms the backbone of a funded RGC project HKU-17330215 (Metal Clustering and Solvation in Hydrothermal Vapors: IRMPD Spectroscopy and Quantum Chemical Studies) that was awarded to the PI in 2017.

703112.label: Major findings and research outcome
703112.value: Obj1. Our ESI FT-MS studies of mixed Au-Cu halide clusters have demonstrated that 1) electrospray ionization of dilute (0.25-2.5 mM) binary solution of CuCl2/AuCl3 give rise to a wide range of hydrated mono- and polynuclear ion clusters with characteristic ion-molecule structures in which the gold/copper halide core are bound to a dihalide molecule (e.g. Cl2) as in [AuCuCl2]+-Cl2 , [AuCu2Cl4]+-Cl2 and [AuCu3Cl6]+-Cl2, and 2) controlled shift in ESI stock concentration and pH leads to clusters that retain solution specific pH features such as ionization/hydrolysis products at low pH with OH ligands and the occurrence of larger gold(III)-copper(II)-chloride clusters in FT-MS experiments with higher conc. ESI stock solutions; in general, results from FT-MS experiments and quantum chemical calculations demonstrate that gold/copper halide dissolve into aqueous vapors and aggregate towards polynuclear clusters with size-specific cluster structures i.e. [AuCuCl2]+-Cl2(H2O)n vs [AuCuCl4]+(H2O)n, and exhibit a propensity to form stable 3-D network like gold/copper chloride clusters for [AuCunCl2n+2]+(H2O)n with n>3 with important implications for gold and copper speciation in ore fluids. Obj2. Objective 2 of HKU-703112 centers on the FT-MS ion clustering studies of PGE halide clusters, and as part of this theme we have focused primarily on the solvation and clustering behavior of aqueous Pd and Pt halide solutions, the structure of the mono- and polynuclear Pd and Pt clusters with and without a water solvation shell; it is noteworthy that ESI of PGE salts with relatively high Ksp values do not necessarily yield ion mass spectra that can be used for FT-MS, however, mass spectrometric screening yielded high quality ions mass spectra for [PdnCl2n-1]+(H2O)n and [PtnCl2n-1]+(H2O)n that form the backbone of obj2/ in HKU-703112. In general, results from FT-MS experiments show that ESI of aqueous PdCl2 and PtCl2 salts lead to a wide range of Pd- and Pt-chloride clusters with distinct solvation shells, and a shift to larger clusters with increasing ESI solution concentration. Obj3. Objective 3 of HKU-703112 deals with the aggregation and solvation behavior of aqueous REE salts, and we have examined, mass spectrometrically, the aqueous speciation of Ce (and related REE) halide solutions, and complemented these studies with DFT and MP2 calculations. Results from FT-MS experiments of aq. CeCl3 demonstrate that polynuclear cerium clusters [CenCl3n-1]+(H2O)n and [CenOHCl3n-2]+(H2O)n exhibit characteristic pH-dependent hydroxide/chloride exchange equilibria and ESI feed conc. dependent abundances. In conc. dependent ESI FT-MS experiments (0.1-20 mM) we observed a predominance of mononuclear Ce clusters (95% mono- vs 5% polynuclear) when the ESI stock was held at 0.1 mM (pH 6.3), whereas higher ESI stock (20 mM) resulted in predominantly polynuclear Ce (4% mono- vs 96% polynuclear).

703112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703112.value: Results from FT-MS studies undertaken under HKU-703112P have broad implications for the vapor phase transport of metals in ore fluids, and as noted above, have resulted in a successful bid for additional RGC funding (HKU-17330215), in particular, to probe the hydrogen bonding environment within the solvation around metal clusters using a combination of FT mass spectrometry and wave tunable IR spectroscopy; it is noteworthy here that mating both facilities was a complex task and has taken us ~2 years to complete. These new IRMPD experiments, in which we probe the solvation shell configuration of size-selected ion clusters, may thus be considered a direct spin-off of the work conducted under HKU-703112P, and will form the backbone for all future FT-MS IRMPS funding proposals. Building on FT-MS results obtained under HKU-703112P we have also proposed a new RGC funded research program that centers around the speciation of Cd and Hg halide clusters. These proposed new FT-MS IRMPD studies will shed light on the vapor-phase speciation of Cd and Hg and provide a molecular-scale understanding of the metal transport in low density vapor and processes that result in ore level Cd and Hg concentration.

703112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703112.value: Water vapor plays an important role in the solubility, transport and redistribution of metals in the Earth‘s crust. There are however, large knowledge gaps with regard to metal affinity and nature, i.e. speciation, of metals in low-density water vapor, in other words, we know very little about the molecular-level structure of metals in vapor and how individual water molecules impact the stability of ion-pairs such as Au+and Cl-. The experimental studies conducted under this theme thus focus on the mass spectrometric characterization of metal ion clusters and their solvations shells, and how the structure of the metal ion core evolves as a functions of size (between and across potential magic number positions) and degree of microsolvation. In brief, we expect that a combination of ESI FT mass spectrometric and ab initio molecular simulations will provide insight into structure, stability (abundance) and spectroscopic properties of ore forming metal clusters, and by doing so, provide novel insight into how metal complexes behave in boiling fluids. In addition, results from molecular simulations of cluster structures and their thermodynamic properties will provide an important predictive tool for geochemists and ore geologists, and will be most useful for understanding metal fractionation and vapor transport phenomena in high temperature ore fluids undergoing boiling. We have also recognized that metals in clusters undergo rapid and complete redox transformation reactions as in the case of [AuCuCl4]+ vs [AuCuCl2]+(Cl2) or [AuCl2]+ vs Au+(Cl2). These finding may have important consequences for our understanding of the redox behavior of metals in water vapor where volatiles are present, such as dihalides or hydrogen halides.
