703312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703312.value: The palaeo-shorelines record the lake level changes in the past. Lake Manas is a closed and dried lake in Junggar Basin with catchment area of 11,000 square kilometres. The lake is particularly sensitive and important to the study of palaeo-climate changes, because the climate in the catchment area is dominantly influenced by the Westlies at the present. Dating of lake palaeo-shorelines can provide chronological evidence of water level changes. Combining with lake level measurements, the history of lake changes can be reconstructed. Lake Manas and Lake Ailike were connected as one lake in early Quaternary. They were separated by a ridge resulted by uplifting caused by a normal fault. Ages of the shorelines can be obtained by directly dating the sediments using optical dating methods. Though there are radiocarbon ages from lake sediments, their reliability and accuracy were often questioned because of hard-water and reservoir effects. This project will use optical dating to provide chronological control for the lake shorelines, and differential global positioning system (d GPS) to reveal the extent of lake. Dating of sediments in the ridge can expose the uplift rate and the timing of separating the two lakes. 湖面的变化是降水和蒸发之间平衡的结果。湖岸堤记录了湖面过去发生的变化。玛纳斯湖是准格尔盆地中流域达11000平方公里的封闭干湖。因为它处于西风带主导区，它对古气候的变化研究尤其重要。湖岸堤测年提供了湖面变化的年代证据，结合湖面高度的测量，湖面的变化历史就可以重建。玛纳斯湖和艾立克湖曾经是相连通的，正断层的隆升产生的横梁将它们隔开。本研究通过光释光的方法，对湖岸堤的年龄直接测量；通过差分GPS估算湖的容积， 从而重建玛纳斯湖的变化历史。通过对沉积物的测年，揭露出断层隆升的速度以及玛纳斯湖和艾力克湖分隔开的时间。

703312.label: Realisation of objectives
703312.value: All of four objectives have been realized. High-resolution data were achieved by using slope method of OSL signals from quartz for the lacustrine sediments of northeastern side of Lake Manas. The sediments are below 262m a.s.l., which was the last high water level. Magnetic susceptibility of these samples was measured to reveal palaeo- climate changes. The OSL ages suggested that the lake had experienced a rapid deposition process during 400~600 years ago. Such ages agreed well with the ages of last high lake level. It was the age of little ice age. It is concluded that the palaeo-climate of Lake Manas was cold and wet during the little ice age. Sedimentation gaps with age gap of 70ka were found between sediments of little ice age and sediments beneath, from both the varves profile and palaeo- shorelines (6). It implies that Lake Manas probably drained for a considerable time. Lacustrine and Aeolian sediments from various sites above 262m a.s.l. in Lake Manas were studied (11). The OSL chronology provides a framework to define the timing of lake evolution during Late Pleistocene in this region. Lacustrine deposits found in sites above current lake level indicate that the lake was considerably larger in the past. Ages of lacustrine sediments suggest two stages of high lake levels of palaeolake Manas during 27.4~38.3 ka and before 65.9 ka ago, which correspond to the late marine isotope stage 3 (MIS 3) and probably MIS 5, respectively. A steadily retreated lake level (48.1~44.1 ka) was recorded by beach deposits between the two high lake stands. No evidence for Holocene high lake level was found in the studying sites. Lacustrine sediments from the northwestern and southeastern sides of Manas Lake were used to study the paleoenvironmental and neotectonic changes in the area (8,11). On the northwestern side of the lake, lacustrine episodes at around 80-70 ka ago were recorded in the level of 272 a.sl.. On the other side of the lake, a site at 262 m a.s.l., which is a clearly marked line of lake level, recorded a paleoshoreline to near-shore environment at ~80-90 ka ago, followed by a sedimentary age gap between ~80 ka ago and the last ~1 ka. It is concluded that breaks in the sedimentary records are common in the area at an elevation of > 260 m a.s.l.. Large scale aeolian erosion was happened in the area during periods of low lake stands. It is also suggested that a small amount of uplift of the northwestern side relative to the southeastern side of the lake have occurred in the last ~80 ka (8). Uncertainties still exist in the amount, timing and the spatial extent of the uplift. The neo-tectonic activities in the nearby site of north Tianshan were studied in Manas River and associated areas (2,4,7). From ~ 20 ka to ~ 4.8 ka, the height of the fluvial bed of Manas River decreased at an average rate of 2.2 ± 0.6 mm/yr. However, from 4.8 ka to the present, the height of the fluvial bed decreased at an average rate of 13.5 ± 0.6 mm/yr, corresponding to intensified incision of Manas River during the late Holocene. This accelerated incision is very likely caused by the tectonic forces rather than climatic influences alone, suggesting that the tectonic uplift activity was significantly intensified since ~ 4.8 ka in the northern piedmont of Tian Shan. Similar results were recorded in Anjihai River (7). Loess deposits were trapped and preserved at the surface ruptures along fault scarps (4,7). The thickness of the trapped loess is dependent on the size of the ruptures. The minimum and maximum ages of these scarps are constrained by dating the loess preserved at the surface ruptures and the terrace treads, respectively, using the quartz optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating technique. The results indicate that the loess trapped at the ruptures was deposited from the early to mid-Holocene at the Hutubi Fault, and from the mid- to late-Holocene at the Manas Fault. The vertical displacements of the faults were evaluated by measuring the topographic profiles across the investigated fault scarps using the differential global position system (DGPS). Our results suggest that, during the late Quaternary in the studied region, the vertical slip rates of the Manas Fault were between ∼0.74 mm/yr and ∼1.6 mm/yr, while the Hutubi Fault had a much lower vertical slip rate between ∼0.34 mm/yr and ∼0.40 mm/yr. A modified multi-elevated-temperature post-IR infra-red stimulated luminescence (MET-pIRIR) protocol is proposed for dating young samples of Holocene age using K-feldspar (1,5). The protocol utilizes a five-step MET-pIRIR measurement with a moderate preheating of 200C for 60 s, and a narrow IR stimulation temperature increment of 30 C (i.e., the five measurement temperatures are 50, 80, 110, 140 and 170 C). Using this method, the residual doses of the MET-pIRIR signals are generally less than 1 Gy. Holocene aeolian samples from Northern China were tested using the 30C-increment modified MET-pIRIR method. The results demonstrate that similar ages from 140 _C to 170 _C were obtained for our sam- ples, which were consistent with the quartz optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) ages. Based on this observation, the measurement procedures are further simplified to a three-step pIRIR protocol. The first IR stimulation at elevated temperature (110 C) is used to remove the fading affected signals. This is followed by two steps of IR stimulation at high temperatures (140 and 170 C) for equivalent dose (De) measurement. Dating results consistent with the expected ages have been obtained at stimulation temperatures of 140 and 170 C. It is suggested that the first IR stimulation can effectively remove the fading component. The three-step pIRIR method has minimized the experimental procedures, while keeping the age plateau test. Methodological studies of old dating limit and associated parameters were studied (3,9). Six PhD and MPhil students were trained and graduated during the course of this project. They all completed their study within the limited periods.

703312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703312.value: Further study will be paid to the relationship between the evolution of Manas Lake and development of Gurbantunggurt Desert. It is likely that the eroded materials from Manas lake sediments were partially become sands deposited in the Desert. It would be worthwhile to study the timing and scales of climate and sedimentary changes in both parts. Another interesting aspect of future study is the contribution of dust materials to the loess deposited in Chinese Loess plateau. Although it has been proposed that the Junggur Basin is one of source areas for the loess, it is not clear how such materials were transported, sorted and deposited during the Pleistocene, and some in the Holocene.

703312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703312.value: Lake Manas is a closed and dried lake in Junggar Basin with catchment area of 11,000 square kilometres. The lake is particularly sensitive and important to the study of palaeo-climate changes, because the climate in the catchment area is dominantly influenced by the Westlies at the present. It is found that the lake deposits in Manas Lake are continuously in time, with significant eroding and gaps during the last 80 thousand years. The lake level was relatively high 400~600 years ago, when the world climate was under Little Ice Age. There were high lake levels during the last 80 thousand years recorded in shorelines of the lake. However, there are significant gaps in the center of the lake revealed from boreholes. Dating of ridges of the lakes suggests that there is relatively little uplift in the lake areas, compared with the accelerating activities in the last 5 thousand years in the adjacent region of Northern Tianshan.

703412.label: Project Objectives
703412.value: The NANO-SIMS observation for the distribution of phosphate in the sinter-like structure of BIFs of >3.71 Ga. This approach aims to compare the structure of phosphate in the magnetite rich bands of the Isua-BIF with the similar structure from the Lower Cambrian black shale to further test the validity of graphite-apatite assemblage as a biosignature of the earliest life. The Isua-BIF sample will be polished to a smooth surface (<200 nm roughness) for SEM examination at first to determine the target area. The interested area will be recognized by image-recognition technique equipped by NANO-SIMS for phosphorus mapping. Search for the overgrowth of graphite and amorphous phosphate by Hitachi S-4800 field emission SEM at the Electron Microscope Center of the University of Hong Kong. This approach combines with the SIMS results so as to strengthen the usage of graphite-phosphate assemblage as the biosignature for evidence of the earliest life on Earth. The graphite spherules will be measured by NANO-SIMS for carbon isotopic compositions. The measurement of structural Mn for its valence states and hyperfine environment in the Mesoarchaean stromatolites and hematite nanoparticles in BIFs before and after the Great Oxidation Event. The measurements will be carried out on XAFS beamline (14W1) of SSRF. Due to the importance of the crystallographic behaviors of Mn(II) and Mn(IV) in the lattice of magnetite and hematite of BIFs, the Mn(II)- and Mn(IV)-doped hematite and magnetite as standard materials will be thermochemically synthesized and characterized for mineralogy in the Geobiology Laboratory of the University of Hong Kong. The detection and quantification of the UVR-resistant pigments in BIFs before and after the Great Oxidation Event by Raman probe and LC-MS. BIF samples from Neoarchaean to the Lower Palaeoproterozoic eras will be measured by Raman probe at first to identify the existence of the UVR-resistant cyanobacterial pigments. Parallel samples containing rich organic matters will also be measured by NANO-SIMS for carbon isotopic compositions. The BIF segments containing relatively high amount of these molecules will be quantified by LC/MS. Characterization of the phosphatization in the Palaeoproterozoic BIFs and its comparison to that in the Lower Cambrian phosphorites. The single crystals in the aggregates will be measured for the distribution, orientation and crystal sizes by STEM. The ratio of the gel- and crystallized parts will be determined by the combined TEM and energy dispersive X-ray microanalysis. For the 541-Ma phosporite, n-alkanes, isoprenoid, teranes and terpanes along with the UVR-absorbing pigments will be analyzed to determine the contribution of heterotrophic and the phototrophic biomass. The corresponding physiological environments, such as temperature, salinity and depth of seawater will also be determined for the 541-Ma phosphorite by analyzing the patterns of the biomarker profiles. The 541-Ma results combined with the results of the 2.48 Ga BIF will be used to model the structure of the ecosystem in the 2.48 Ga Ocean. Application of synchrotron radiation based XAFS techniques to measure the hyperfine interactions in the BIF materials. For this part of study, we will use majorly beamlines of XAFS (BL14W1) and X-ray microfocus (BL15U) upon the approval of user proposals. XAFS will be used to measure the hyperfine environments of Mn and its valence states in stromatolite and hematite and magnetite from BIFs. The X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy of Mo (usually <2 ppm) will also be tested for its valence states as another independence line of petrographic observation for the redox of the oceans. BL15U will be used for the high resolution (6-10 μm) X-ray fluorescence of BIF samples of complex Trendall bands for elements listed in Fig.6.

703412.value: Objective 1, we have analysed banded iron samples of 2.2 to >3.7 billion years old for in situ trace elemental chemical compositions of magnetite. Results are under preparation for a research paper. Objective 2, we have studied banded iron formation samples from 2.2 to >3.7 billion years old by scanning electron microscopes, electron dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. We have observed a few micrometer-sized spherules of graphite which are different from the metamorphic genetic graphites of around 70 um. However, due to the very small number of them, it is hard to do further isotopic analysis. It is, however, interesting that some of those graphite spherules were observed coexisting with phosphate of nm size. Results will be combined with the other existing results for future publication. Objective 3. We have finished measurements of X-ray absorption near-edge spectra. A research paper is under preparation based mostly on this part of data. Objective 4.The results are surprisingly good, so that this part has been eventually the focus of this study. As the result could be of high impact, we are working on more supporting experiments recently. The results will be submitted lately. Objective 5. This part is done very well with one publication on the topic already. Objective 6. Accomplished. Results will be combined with those of objective 3 for publication. Manuscript is under preparation. Objective 7. Research goal of this study has been accomplished with one publication and the deepening of this direction has led to another publication supported by my next RGC funding.

703412.label: Major findings and research outcome
703412.value: Banded iron formation is the most important sedimentary rock of early Precambrian from Archean to Palaeoproterozoic eras (ca. 3.8 to 1.8 Ga), which is characterised by alternative bands of iron oxides and silica. The genesis of the banding structure has long been a mystery. In this study, Li (2014, Earth and Planetary Science Letters) provide a detailed observation of banding structures with thickness of sub-millimetre to submicrometer. This is the first report of nanometer to micrometer banding structures in banded iron formation and minerals that made those structures were also interpreted for their genesis. In a related study, we studied hematite, the major Fe(III)-oxide mineral in banded iron formation by high resolution scanning electron microscope and transmission electron microscopes. We found the existing of ultrafine crystals of hematite and those of a few tens nm and those of hundred nm. The characterization of hematite of a few nm confirmed the direct transformation of ferrihydrite to hematite in banded iron formations; we also described the pathway from the primary Fe(III)-oxide to diagenetic and secondary iron oxides by electron microscopes, which is essential for the study of this field by the other means. This part of study has been published in Geological Society of America Bulletin. Consideration of the contribution of our study in the understanding of the interactions between ocean the biosphere in Archean, we were invited to write a review paper on the origin and the early evolution of life and the early biosphere on Earth (will be published on Science Bulletin, invited review paper).

703412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703412.value: In this study, we have done detailed observations of the mineral and petrographic features of banded iron formations and interpreted the genesis. We found it of great importance to study the genesis of magnetite in banded iron formations of a wide spectrum of ages. Results of this study indicates the older the banded iron formation, the high the abundant of magnetite in the petrological structures. We suspect the abundance of magnetite might be related to the evolution of the redox chemistry of the ocean from the early Archean to the end of Palaeoproterozoic eras. We realised that the numerous reports of the source of Fe, and activity of deep-sea hydrothermal activity by patterns of rare earth elements might also be related to the genesis of magnetite in banded iron formation. I feel that the finding of the genesis of magnetite in Archean banded iron formation, especially those oldest banded iron formation should provide clues on the possible existence of the earliest photoferrotrophs. Our finding of the mineral ecophysiology of Gallionella in the natural environments of Hong Kong is now developed as a site for my students to study environmental mineralogy and geobiology. I will consider prepare my next RGC proposal on this topic. In this project, we used lots of electron microscopic methods to describe mineral habits and their natures in petrologic structures. Researches begin to realize that the accurate interpretation of isotopic data depends much on the understanding of the mineral and/or petrologic nature of the sedimentary rock, which could only be provided by high spatial observations by electron microscopes. The citations of our papers and reflects from conferences we attended indicate that the research methodology we developed in this project should have impacts in the future in the field of sedimentary rocks.

703412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703412.value: The Earth's atmosphere, ocean and biosphere have experienced about 4 billion years evolution. The earliest 2 billion years was important in the developing of the microbial biosphere, the change of the ocean chemistry and the emergence of oxygen-producing photosynthesis. By the study of rocks of 2.2 to >3.7 billion years old, we find some minerals preserved their primary features, which allows us to further investigate the nature of mineral precipitated by photosynthetic bacteria in the early oceans. We find the very well preservation of banding structures in the studies rocks, in which the thinnest bands might be the result of daily and annual precipitate of minerals by the daily and seasonal change of solar radiations.

703512.label: Project Objectives
703512.value: Circumstellar Disks: Are the circumstellar disks of the binary components in L1551 NE coplanar with each other and their surrounding pseudodisk, as predicted by theoretical models and seen in L1551 IRS 5? Are their circumstellar disks truncated to sizes in accordance with theoretical predictions, as has been shown to be the case in L1551 IRS 5? We plan observations with the EVLA to resolve the circumstellar dust disks of the binary components in L1551 NE. Orbital Motion and Pseudodisk Rotation: Are the binary components in L1551 NE orbiting each other in the same direction as the rotation of their surrounding pseudodisk, as is seen in L1551 IRS 5? We plan multi-epoch EVLA observations to measure the orbital motion of L1551 NE. We also plan further observations of L1551 IRS 5 to refine the orbital parameters of its two main components, and confirm the presence of a candidate third component and address its possible origin. Central Gap in Pseudodisk: Both theoretical models and simulations predict that tidal interactions between the protostellar components and their surrounding pseudodisk should clear a central gap in the pseudodisk. We plan to use the EVLA to search for a central gap in the dust component of the pseudodisk around both L1551 IRS 5 and L1551 NE, and the SMA, IRAM PdBI, and ALMA to search for a central gap in the molecular gas (as well as dust) component of their pseudodisks. Material Streams from Pseudodisk to Cicumstellar Disks: Both theoretical models and simulations predict that material streams should penetrate the central gap in the pseudodisk at the outer Lagrangian points of the binary system. In theoretical simulations, such streams have the appearance of spiral arms that extend from the pseudodisk to the individual circumstellar disks. We plan to use the EVLA to search for dust associated with the predicted accretion streams, and the SMA, IRAM PdBI, and ALMA to search for molecular gas (as well as dust) associated with these accretion streams. The EVLA can provide images in dust at higher angular resolutions, but the other telescopes can provide images also in molecular gas that may prove crucial for separating the different structures present based on their different kinematics. Physical Conditions for Core Fragmentation: Why do some but not other cores fragment? For both L1551 IRS 5 and L1551 NE, we plan to use the SMA to study the change in structure and angular momentum of their host cores from the outer envelope to the inner pseudodisk. By comparing the physical properties of these cores with those measured for the cores of single protostars, augmented by theoretical simulations, we anticipate finding important clues for understanding why some but not other cores fragment.

We also plan further observations of L1551 IRS 5 to refine the orbital parameters of its two main components, and confirm the presence of a candidate third component and address its possible origin.

Central Gap in Pseudodisk: Both theoretical models and simulations predict that tidal interactions between the protostellar components and their surrounding pseudodisk should clear a central gap in the pseudodisk. We plan to use the EVLA to search for a central gap in the dust component of the pseudodisk around both L1551 IRS 5 and L1551 NE, and the SMA, IRAM PdBI, and ALMA to search for a central gap in the molecular gas (as well as dust) component of their pseudodisks.

Material Streams from Pseudodisk to Cicumstellar Disks: Both theoretical models and simulations predict that material streams should penetrate the central gap in the pseudodisk at the outer Lagrangian points of the binary system. In theoretical simulations, such streams have the appearance of spiral arms that extend from the pseudodisk to the individual circumstellar disks. We plan to use the EVLA to search for dust associated with the predicted accretion streams, and the SMA, IRAM PdBI, and ALMA to search for molecular gas (as well as dust) associated with these accretion streams. The EVLA can provide images in dust at higher angular resolutions, but the other telescopes can provide images also in molecular gas that may prove crucial for separating the different structures present based on their different kinematics.

Physical Conditions for Core Fragmentation: Why do some but not other cores fragment? For both L1551 IRS 5 and L1551 NE, we plan to use the SMA to study the change in structure and angular momentum of their host cores from the outer envelope to the inner pseudodisk. By comparing the physical properties of these cores with those measured for the cores of single protostars, augmented by theoretical simulations, we anticipate finding important clues for understanding why some but not other cores fragment.

703512.label: Realisation of objectives
703512.value: Stars form in dense condensations of molecular gas and dust, referred to as cores, in molecular clouds. At masses comparable with and higher than that of the Sun, most stars form as members of binary systems, implying that the formation of binary stars is the primary mechanism of star formation at solar masses and higher. The objective of this proposal is to test, through observations, different theoretical models for how cores produce binary systems. The observations, in turn, serve to constrain and refine theoretical models for how binary protostellar systems grow and evolve. Current theoretical studies suggest that, during gravitational collapse, cores can fragment to produce two (or more) seeds that grow to become binary (or multiple) star systems. Two mechanisms have been proposed for driving fragmentation: bulk rotation or local turbulence. These mechanisms predict different physical parameters for the resulting binary systems: aligned spins and orbits in the case of rotationally-driven fragmentation, by contrast with generally misaligned spins and orbits in the case of turbulence-driven fragmentation. Unfortunately, tidal interactions between the binary components or gravitational encounters with other stars can drive systems towards or away from alignment, thus masking their formation processes. In the work conducted for this project, we demonstrated that the geometrical and dynamical relationship between binary protostellar systems and their parental cores provide the crucial distinction between different fragmentation models (Lim et al. 2016a, 2016b). Specifically, through precise measurements of the physical properties of the binary protostellar systems L1551 IRS5 and L1551 NE (Objectives 1 and 2 below), we showed that these systems formed through rotationally-driven fragmentation. This work constitutes the first time that rotationally-driven fragmentation has been robustly demonstrated, through observations, to form binary stars. Theoretical studies suggest that gravitational torques from the central binary system drive material outwards to create a central gap. Infalling material from the surrounding remnant parental core piles up at the edge of this gap to define the inner boundary of a circumbinary disk. From observations of L1551 NE (Objective 3), we showed that this binary protostellar system is indeed surrounded by a circumbinary disk that exhibits a central gap (Takakuwa et al. 2014). Furthermore, we identified, for the first time, spiral arms in the circumbinary disk of a protostellar system, and non-Keplerian motion in a circumbinary disk. From theoretical simulations, we showed that gravitational torques from the central binary system drive material outwards to create the spiral arms; in between these arms, the same gravitational torques drive material inwards. The combination of inwards and outwards motions explains entirely the observed deviations from Keplerian motion. Theoretical studies suggest that material penetrates the central gap in the circumbinary disk at its Lagrangian points, thus accumulating onto the circumstellar disks of the binary protostellar system. We have found tentative evidence in L1551 IRS for material directed into both its circumstellar disks (Objective 4; Lim et al. 2016a). Finally, we have taken an incremental step forward in addressing the physical conditions under which cores fragment (Objective 5; Takakuwa et al. 2013, 2014, Lim et al. 2016a, b, and Leung et al. 2016). 1. Circumstellar Disks. We conducted observations with the VLA that spatially resolved both circumstellar disks associated with the binary protostellar system L1551 NE (Lim et al. 2016b). We found that the two circumstellar disks in this system, by contrast with those in the binary system L1551 IRS5, have very different relative sizes. Nevertheless, like in L1551 IRS5, the two circumstellar disks are closely parallel with each other. Furthermore, the two circumstellar disks are closely parallel with their surrounding circumbinary disk. In l551 IRS5, the two circumstellar disks have sizes that are somewhat smaller than those predicted for tidal truncation (Lim et al. 2016a). In L1551 NE, the two circumstellar disks have sizes that are much smaller than those predicted by tidal truncation. 2. Orbital Motion and Pseudodisk Rotation. By comparing the central positions of the circumstellar disks in L1551 NE with the central positions of their associated ionized jets from archival data taken with the VLA over a decade earlier, we showed that the binary protostars in L1551 NE are likely orbiting in the same direction as the rotation of their circumbinary disk (Lim et al. 2016b). By comparing our observations of the circumstellar disks in L1551 IRS with historical measurements with the VLA, we were able to provide meaningful constraints on the binary orbital parameters. By combining these constraints with those imposed by the sizes of their circumstellar disks, we showed that the binary protostars in L1551 IRS5 has a near-circular orbit (Lim et al. 2016a). Providing a far superior sensitivity than our previous observation with the VLA, we also found that the putative third protostellar companion in L1551 IRS5 is spurious. 3. Central Gap in Pseudodisk. We showed from observations with ALMA that there is indeed a central clearing in the circumbinary disk of L1551 NE (Takakuwa et al. 2014). By the end of this proposal, we have not yet completing reduction of VLA and ALMA data for observations of L1551 IRS5 to search for such a central clearing. The data reduction of L1551 IRS5 is especially challenging, requiring careful scrutiny of the calibration (as a function of time during the observation) so as to attain an extremely high dynamic range. 4. Material Streams from Pseudodisk to Cicumstellar Disks. At the angular resolution so far achieved, our observations of L1551 NE with ALMA reveal no clear evidence for material streams from the circumbinary to the two circumstellar disks (Takakuwa et al. 2014). Our observations of the same system with the VLA, providing a far higher angular resolution but inferior sensitivity, also provide no evidence for material streams (Lim et al. 2016b). On the other hand, our observations of L1551 IRS with the VLA reveal features that might be tentatively associated with material streams (Lim et al. 2016a). The unambiguous identification of material streams will likely require observations at both high sensitivity and angular resolution with ALMA. 5. Physical Conditions for Core Fragmentation. This is the million-dollar question. Previous studies have shown that the remnant parental core around L1551 IRS5 possesses considerable angular momentum. By contrast, our study of L1551 NE shows that, beyond its circumbinary disk, the immediately surrounding envelope possesses little if any angular momentum (Takakuwa et al. 2013). On the other hand, our observations of the protostar L483 shows that dense molecular gas observed in CS(7-6) traces a rotation and infalling envelope on a global scale. L1551 NE, like L483 and also L1551 IRS5, exhibits similar signatures in CS(7-6), suggesting that the global envelope of this system also is infalling and rotating. Improved studies of L1551 NE similar to those we conducted for L483 are required to clarify the kinematics of its envelope. If our suggestion proves correct, then, as might be expected, the initial angular momentum of cores may be an important factor in determining whether rotation drives their fragmentation. Further progress in addresing this question will require similar studies of other binary protostellar systems as we have conducted for L1551 IRS5 and L1551 NE.

703512.label: Major findings and research outcome
703512.value: Stars with masses of up to a few solar masses form in dense condensations known as cores. Theoretical studies suggest that, during gravitational collapse, cores can fragment to produce two (or more) seeds that grow to become binary (or multiple) star systems. Two mechanisms have been proposed for driving fragmentation: bulk rotation or local turbulence. These mechanisms predict different physical parameters for the resulting binary systems: aligned spins and orbits in the case of rotationally-driven fragmentation, by contrast with generally misaligned spins and orbits in the case of turbulence-driven fragmentation. Unfortunately, tidal interactions between the binary components or gravitational encounters with other stars can drive systems towards or away from alignment, thus masking their formation processes. We demonstrated that the geometrical and dynamical relationship between binary protostellar systems and their parental cores provide the crucial distinction between different fragmentation models. For both L1551 IRS5 (Lim et al. 2016a) and L1551 NE (Lim et al. 2016b), we found that the systems as well aligned, suggesting that they formed through rotationally-driven fragmentation. Furthermore, we showed that L1551 IRS has a (near) circular orbit. The binary properties of L1551 IRS5 resemble those of binary systems on the main sequence having comparable masses and orbital separations. From theoretical modeling, we showed that deviations from Keplerian motion observed in the circumbinary disk of L1551 NE can be explained by gravitational torques from the binary protostellar system (Takakuwa et al. 2014). These torques drive material outwards to create two spiral arms in the circumbinary disk; in between the spiral arms, the torques drive material inwards. Beyond the circumbinary disk, we showed that the surrounding envelope exhibits infall but no appreciable rotation, suggesting that angular momentum is efficiently transferred outwards in the envelope (Takakuwa et al. 2013). Observations of both solar-mass protostars in CS(7-6), tracing gas at relatively high densities, reveal highly extended emission along their outflow axis. For the solar-mass protostar L483, we showed that the observed properties of its CS(7-6) emission is in clear contradiction for outflowing gas along the walls of its outflow cavities (Leung, Lim, & Takakuwa 2015). Instead, the observed properties can be qualitatively explained by infalling gas along the outflow cavity walls of a rigidly rotating envelope. Our model also successfully explains the observed properties of CS(7-6) emission around other solar-mass protostars, and provides a new tool for study infall and angular momenta in parental cores of both single and binary protostellar systems.

703512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703512.value: In our Galaxy, stars with masses comparable with and higher than that of the Sun are preferentially found in binary systems. The physical processes that give rise to the formation of binary rather than single stars are poorly understood, as are those that determine the growth of infant binary systems into mature systems. Current theoretical studies suggest that binary stars form as a consequence of the fragmentation of dense gaseous condensations (“cores”). Two mechanisms have been proposed to drive fragmentation: overall rotation of or turbulence within the core. These mechanisms predict different outcomes for the physical properties of the resulting infant binary system. Unfortunately, gravitational interaction between the binary companions or with other passing stars, either during infancy or later, can alter the physical properties of binary systems. In our work, we demonstrate that the geometrical and dynamical relationship between binary protostellar systems and their parental cores provide the crucial distinction between different fragmentation models. Specifically, we show conclusively for the first time that rotation can indeed drive core fragmentation, and that the binary parameters of the resulting infant binary system resemble those of the general population of mature binary system having similar masses and separations.

703612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703612.value: Zinc oxide is a wide band gap semiconductor recently received extensive attention because of its potential of fabricating devices of UV optoelectronic, transparent transistor, varistor, bio-sensor, and etc. Its excellent efficiency in UV emission makes it an attractive candidate for fabricating light emitting diode, solid state laser, white solid state lighting, and etc. Recent theoretical prediction of room temperature ferromagnetism for transition metal doped ZnO raised the possibility of using ZnO as a spintronic material. This would open up the horizon of devices combining electronic, magnetic and optical functioning, like magneto optical switch, spin-polarized light emitter, high density ultralow power memory, and etc. The understanding of the ferromagnetism is complicated by cluster formation of the doping transition metal and the influence of the intrinsic defects. The major key challenge for realizing ZnO-based device fabrication is the difficulty of p-type doping. Although extensive effort has been devoted, reliable p-type doping of ZnO has not yet achieved. The p-type doping issue is associated with the inability of controlling the dopant and the compensating defects. Despite of its importance, the understanding of defects in ZnO is far from complete and controversial. It could be concluded that lacking the knowledge of defects and their control are the obstacle for realizing ZnO based device fabrication. Green luminescence is commonly observed in ZnO materials regardless of the form or the growth method. The origin of green luminescence (GL) of ZnO has remained controversial. Many electrically active deep traps have been identified in ZnO and they could act as compensating centers. Their microstructures are not known or under debate. We propose to study the defects responsible for the GL and the electrically active deep traps using a multi-spectroscopic approach so as to offer a comprehensive picture on their origins and microstructures. 氧化锌是一种宽禁带半导体材料，由于它在制备紫外光电元件，透明晶体管，压敏电阻，生物传感器等方面具有巨大潜力，近年来被广泛关注。由于氧化锌材料高效的紫外发光，使得它在发光二极管，固体激光器，白光光源等方面有极佳的应用前景。氧化锌掺杂铁磁性过渡金属可以实现室温铁磁性在理论上已经得到证实，氧化锌掺杂铁磁性过渡金属极有可能成为一种新的自旋电子材料。这将开辟电学，磁学和光电功能一个全新的领域，例如，磁光开关，自旋极化光发射器，高密度超低功耗内存等等。由于过渡金属掺杂形成的团簇和ZnO的本征缺陷的影响，使过渡族元素掺杂ZnO材料的铁磁性的研究还一直有争议。在实现氧化锌器件制备的最关键问题是p型掺杂。尽管经过很多努力，也未得到高质量的稳定的p型氧化锌。与p型掺杂相关的是无法控制掺杂量和自补偿缺陷。对于氧化锌缺陷的理解，人们还存在着很大的争议。缺乏对缺陷的认识及对缺陷的控制是制备高效氧化锌器件的一大障碍。形貌和生长方法各不相同的氧化锌材料都可以观察到绿色发射。而绿光的来源却仍然存在争议。氧化锌中的很多电激活深能级俘获阱，可以充当补偿中心。但是关于这些深能级的微结构还没有系统的研究。我们将通过多种光谱结合的方法研究绿光和电激活的俘获阱与缺陷的对应关系。

703612.label: Realisation of objectives
703612.value: We have carried out systematic defect studies on different types of ZnO materials to address the two objectives. The involved ZnO materials include our self-grown PLD grown samples with systematically changing substrate temperature and oxygen pressure during growth, and ion-implanted melted grown ZnO single crystal obtained commercially from the Cermet Inc. We have also included Ga and Cu doped PLD grown ZnO samples in our study. By controlling the intrinsic defects through changing the oxygen pressure and extrinsic doping, we could fabricate ZnO film having electron concentration from 10^{16} cm^{3} to 10^{20} cm^{-3}. Annealing studies on these samples were also performed. We have employed a comprehensive approach for understanding the defects which includes photoluminescence (PL), deep level transient spectroscopy (DLTS), positron annihilation spectroscopy (PAS), X-ray diffraction spectroscopy (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), secondary ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS), and Hall measurement etc. The results are summarised as follows. Objective 1:- PAS study showed that two types of Zn-vacancy related defects, namely VZn1 and VZn2, were identified in PLD grown undoped samples. VZn1 was found in as-grown samples grown with relatively low oxygen pressure. VZn2 was identified in as-grown samples grown with high oxygen pressure and in samples annealed at 900^{o}C. Green luminescences were found in the low temperature PL spectra of the PLD grown undoped ZnO samples, with the shapes and peak positions depending on the initial growth parameters and the annealing temperature. The broad green luminescences (GL) having different shapes and peak position was contributed from more than one type of defect emissions having close-by wavelengths. However irrespective of the initial growth conditions, an identical GL having the same peak position (2.47eV) and shape was obtained after annealing at 900^{o}. In addition, a near band edge emission (NBE) assigned to donor-acceptor-pair (DAP)/free-electron-to-acceptor (FA) transitions was also introduced after the samples were annealed at 900^{o}C. The correlated introductions of VZn2, the GL at 2.47eV and the NBE after annealing at 900^{o}C prompted that the GL at 2.47eV and the acceptor associated with the NBE were related to the Zn-vacancy related defect. The GL and NBE photon energies coincided very well with the transitions between the conduction band and respectively the energy levels of (-/2-) and (0/-) of V_{Zn} obtained by first principal calculation#. Another kind of GL having a different peak position of 2.42 eV and equally separated fine structured peaks was also observed in Cu-doped PLD samples and melt grown undoped sample annealed at 800^{o}C. The fine structured peak separation was ~70 meV, which coincided with the LO phonon energy of ZnO. This GL has been in general attributed to be Cu-impurity. Objective 2:- DLTS study was carried out to melt grown ZnO single crystal implanted with N, O, and Zn ions. E3 (~Ec-0.3eV) is the major deep traps in the as-grown sample. The concentration of E3 had no significant change upon the implantations of N, O and Zn. T2 or D2 (~Ec-0.17eV) was introduced in O-implanted, N-implanted and Zn-implanted samples after annealing at 650^{o}C. Deep traps at Ec-0.11eV and Ec-0.58eV were found in the O-implanted sample. D1 at ~Ec-0.9eV was found in Zn-implanted and N-implanted samples, but not in the O-implanted samples. D1 was thus attitude to V_{O}, for which its activation energy also coincided well with the (2+/0) state of V_{O} obtained by first principal calculation#. Low temperature PL study showed that red luminescence (RL) at ~620 nm was introduced by the N and Zn implantation. Fitting the spectra with the underdamped multimode Brownian oscillator model yielded the zero phonon line at ~2.4eV, which could be due to the transition from the (2+/0) state of V_{O} to the Ev. The RL of the Zn-implanted sample showed distinctive lattice temperature dependence, which was well described by the configurational coordinate model comprising of a "self-activated" optical transition between a shallow donor and the defect which is most likely V_{O}Zn_{i} or V{O}V_{Zn} complexes. Other than the results related to the two objectives, knowledge was gained in ZnO growth and defect control. The knowledge incubated some more research activities, namely the fabrication of an asymmetric double ZnO/ZnMgO quantum well structure which had very low optical lasing threshold, the control of optical properties of ZnO nanostructure through the two-step synthesis approach, and the fabrication of very high quality PLD grown Cu-doped ZnO films used in the ferromagnetic study. #Janotti and Van de Walle, PRB vol.76, 165202 (2007).

(3) Two kinds of GL were found in ZnO materials, one without fine structure peaking at 2.47eV [Wang 2015] and the other one with fine structure peaking at 2.43eV [Younas 2014, Ling 2016]. The 2.47eV GL and a NBE at 3.23eV were associated with the Zn-vacancy [Wang 2015, Ling 2016]. (4) Deep traps at 0.11eV, 0.17eV, 0.30eV, 0.58eV and 0.90eV below Ec were found in the melted grown ZnO samples [Mtangi 2013]. The 0.90eV trap was associated with the V_{O} defect [Dai 2012]. This assignment was compatible with the RL results in the PL study [Dai 2012, Chen 2014]. (5) The knowledge of the PLD technique and defect control incubated the results of the quantum well structure having a very low lasing threshold [Su 2013] and the control of optical properties of ZnO nanostructure [Naeem 2013]. (6) The PI presented these results in an invited plenary talk at the 6th South Africa Conference on Photonic Materials, and an invited keynote lecture at the 11th IUPAC International Conference on Novel Materials and their Synthesis.

703612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703612.value: (1) The unambiguous characterisation of the two kinds of Zn-vacancy related defects found in the PLD grown ZnO samples. This is now in progress. (2) The yielded knowledge on defects, defect control and PLD growth of high quality ZnO would be very useful in the future research involving devices like optoelectronic and photovoltaic etc. Research collaboration with the co-authors at Pretoria University involving ZnO based photovoltaic has just been started. The author has also obtained another RGC GRF project studying the magnetic properties of Cu-doped ZnO. This project is now on-going and involves the use of the knowledge gained in the present project for engineering the Cu-doped samples properties.

703612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703612.value: ZnO is a potential material for fabricating devices of optoelectronic, spintronic, and sensors. Defects play crucial role in determining the materials' electrical, optical and magnetic properties. Understanding concerning the green luminescence, red luminescence and electric active deep traps, their origins and other defects have been gained. Knowledge involving intrinsic defect control and extrinsic doping in pulsed laser deposition growth of ZnO were also gained, which leaded to the successful fabrication of low lasing threshold ZnO based quantum well structure and the control of optical properties of nano materials.

703712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703712.value: We propose to connect two heretofore unrelated fields of mathematics, namely the theory of Frobenius splittings and Poisson geometry. For a variety over a field of positive characteristic and with the action by a torus T, we say that a T-invariant Poisson structure on the variety is Frobenius if its T-Pfaffian defines a Frobenius splitting on the variety. Examples of such Poisson structures, with their origins in quantum groups, include the standard Poisson structures on a class of varieties related to reductive algebraic groups, such as flag varieties, cotangent bundles of flag varieties, and the wonderful compactifications of symmetric varieties. We conjecture that the Frobenius splittings defined by these Poisson structures are the standard ones on the corresponding varieties that have found spectacular applications to geometry and representation theory. Through a detailed study of these concrete examples, we aim at establishing a basic theory of Frobenius Poisson structures, such as relations between Poisson subvarieties and compatibly split subvarieties, properties of the Frobenius forms, and the induced splittings on the compatibly split subvarieties via the adjunction formula and the Poisson Pfaffians. While our project will be the first of its kind in studying the Poisson geometry behind the standard Frobenius splittings on a class of important varieties in representation theory, it will also be a pioneering work on Poisson geometry in positive characteristic, where Frobenius splittings are brought in as a tool for exploring particular features of Poisson structures in positive characteristic that do not exist in characteristic zero. 通过具体且详细地研究李群理论中的一些例子，我们将连接两个迄今为止无关的数学领域，即泊松几何与Frobenius分解.

703712.label: Realisation of objectives
703712.value: Objective 1 is realized as a direct consequence of a thorough study we have carried out (in three papers) on the T-leaves and local formulas for the Poisson structures in the proposal. Partial results of Objectives 2 and 3 are written up in the PhD thesis of student Jun PENG; Partial results of Objective 4 have been written up in preliminary notes.

703712.label: Major findings and research outcome
703712.value: In three publications, we have developed a thorough theory on a class of Poisson structures and investigated some of their properties, such as their formulas in coordinate charts and Poisson T-Pfaffians, which can be made to be defined over the integers and thus also over a field of arbitrary characteristics. The results give immediate applications in particular to positive characteristics and Frobenius splittings. Three PhD students have been trained in the past 4 years partially supported by the grant. One PhD student wrote a thesis on quatization of a class of polynomial Poisson structures, a problem not originally written in the proposal, but the student's thesis opens up new research directions connecting Frobenius splittings and quantum T-Pfaffians.

703712.value: It would be interesting to look at Frobenius splittings from the point of view of quantization, as inspired by the thesis of one of my PhD students. More time is also needed to write up our findings.

703712.value: We investigated on a class of Poisson structures defined on important varieties from Lie theory which can be applied to Poisson varieties in positive characteristics and Frobenius splittings

703912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703912.value: Projective manifolds are model parameter spaces in Nature. For instance the hyperquadric can be taken as the a model for space-time. Among projective manifolds the Fano manifolds play an important role. A Fano manifold is a projective manifold of positive curvature in some sense (which may be regarded as a higher-dimensional analogue of the Riemann sphere) with an ample supply of rational curves (Riemann spheres) filling up the manifold. In the geometric theory of uniruled projective manifolds we have developed a method of studying the geometry of Fano manifolds by means of spaces of special tangent vectors, called varieties of minimal rational tangents (VMRTs). It generalizes various kinds of geometries such as conformal geometry on the hyperquadric as a model for the Minkowski space. Here rational curves play the role of light rays. Among the Fano manifolds of particular importance as model spaces are those admitting large groups of symmetry, especially the rational homogeneous manifolds X = G/P. On such a manifold there are special subvarieties called Schubert varieties, which play an important role in the decomposition of the manifold into cells. Among other things we will study rigidity phenomena exhibited by some of these Schubert varities (including singular ones). We formulate the problem of rigidity of a Schubert variety S on X in terms of deformations of VMRTs when the projective subvariety S is deformed inside X. As examples other problems on rigidity arising from VMRTs will include the question whether complex structures of a Fano manifold can suddenly jump, and the problem of reconstructing a model Fano manifolds from the VMRTs.

703912.label: Realisation of objectives
703912.value: The project focused on rigidity problems arising from varieties of minimal rational tangents (VMRTs). Rational homogeneous spaces G/P of Picard number 1 and Schubert cycles on them were the primary objects of study, as covered in Objectives (1) and (2). In known results on Schur rigidity on irreducible Hermitian symmetric spaces, a key step was to prove Schubert rigidity. A Schubert cycle Z on G/P is always almost homogeneous under the stabilizer H of Z, and we denote by 0 a point on the unique open H-orbit on Z . We want to characterize certain Schubert cycles Z in terms of isomorphism classes of their tangent spaces at general smooth points. More precisely, we want to prove that for locally closed complex submanifold S on G/P = X where the tangent spaces T_x(S) are equivalent under G-action to T_0(Z), S must be an open subset of gZ for some element g of G. This is the problem of Schubert rigidity, i.e., of proving uniqueness modulo group actions of integral submanifolds of the Schubert differential system. In [2] we defined admissible pairs on G/P which include the cases of (Z,X), where Z is a rational homogeneous subspace of Picard number 1 and define a general notion of rigidity which is a generalization of Schubert rigidity for G/P Hermitian symmetric, and we established a major result that (Z,X) is rigid in this sense whenever Z is a nonlinear rational homogenous subspace defined by a Dynkin subdiagram, or when Z is a maximal linear subspace other than a few identified cases where rigidity fails. Thus Schubert rigidity for the subdiagram case is completely settled for G/P. For G/P of Hermitian symmetric type, together with the known reduction (Bryant, Walters, Hong) of Schur rigidity to Schubert rigidity, our method gives a new differential-geometric proof of Schur rigidity for such Z = G'/P'. Our theory of sub-VMRT structure is much more general, and applies to uniruled projective manifolds X equipped with minimal rational components. In [1] and [2] we introduced the notion of sub-VMRT structures. The support S of a sub-VMRT structure is a locally closed complex submanifold X such that, denoting by C(X) the VMRT structure (X,K), the intersections C_x(S) := PT_x(S) ∩ C_x(X) defines a fibered space over S with equidimensional nonempty fibers satisfying some additional properties. In place of methods of Lie algebra cohomology, we introduced and made use of a new nondegeneracy for substructures which is an adaptation of nondegeneracy for mappings of Hong-Mok (2010). Nondegeneracy for substructures is expressed in terms of the second fundamental form at a general smooth point of C_x(S) with respect to the projective second fundamental form of C_x(X) in PT_x(X). While the two notions of nondegeneracy are distinct we checked using root space decompositions that for admissible pairs (Z,X) of subdiagram type where Z is nonlinear, nondegeneracy for substructures holds if and only if nondegenery for mappings holds. Since the latter was established in the long-root cases by Hong-Mok (2010) and in the short root cases by Hong-Park (2011), we have established the rigidity of (Z,X) in [2], Main Theorem 1. In a general setting we proved that a sub-VMRT structure supported on S (on the open set W) which is nondegenerate for substructures, S is rationally saturated with respect to (X,K) in the sense that for every minimal rational curve Γ tangent to S at a point x on S, the germ of holomorphic curve (Γ;x) must lie on S ([2], Theorem 1.4). Under the further assumption that (a) X is of Picard number 1 and (X,K) is a uniruling by lines, i.e., by minimal rational curves whose homology classes are the positive generator of H_2(X,Z) = Z; (b) that the meromorphic distribution D spanned by C(S) is bracket generating in the sense that the subsheaf obtained by taking successive Lie brackets of vector fields starting from local sections of D agrees with T(S) at a general point, we prove the Algebraicity Theorem ([2], Main Theorem 2) ascertaining that there exists a projective subvariety on V on X such that S lies on V and dim(S) = dim(X). The Algebraicity Theorem transforms the support S of a sub-VMRT structure, which is an analytic object, to an algebraic object V. This may be regarded as a partial rigidity phenomenon implying that local deformations of S as supports of sub-VMRT structures are of finite dimension. In the case where there is a model or a set of models for S, the question of rigidity is the Rigidity Problem for sub-VMRT structures formulated in [1]. Results along that line were also obtained [2] such as recognition of maximal linear subspaces of linear sections of sufficiently small codimension in G/P ([2], Theorem 9.2). By introducing a quantitative measure called the degree of nondegeneracy of sub-VMRT structures, we were also able to prove algebraicity of sub-VMRT structures on certain complete intersections of G/P embedded into a projective space by the first canonical embedding ([2], Theorem 9.1). As a prototype for singular Schubert cycles, we consider in the Hermitian symmetric case the Schubert cycle V(x) on G/P =: X defined as the cone of minimal rational curves passing through the base point x. In [3] we described the sub-VMRT structure of V(x) on X and proved the Algebraicity Theorem for V(x) on X ([3], Theorem 4.1) in the case where X is an irreducible Hermitian symmetric space of rank at least 2 other than the hyperquadric Q_n and the rank-2 Grassmannian G(2,n). (In the latter cases it is known that Schur rigidity fails.) Schur rigidity of V(x) can be obtained along this line by means of a procedure of reconstruction of uniruled projective subvarieties, and this is carried out in the thesis work of Xiaoyu Yang at HKU under my supervision in 2016. We also proved a restricted version of Algebraic Theorem for V(x) for the excluded cases of Q_n and G(2,n) by proving that the sub-VMRT structure S modelled on V(x) can be completed to a uniruled projective subvariety provided that S is intrinsically flat, i.e., that S is the image under a VMRT-respecting holomorphic map of some smooth open subset of V(x). Mok-Zhang [2] (84 pages) is a major work in VMRT theory. It lays the foundation of the theory of sub-VMRT structures on uniruled projective manifolds, and also provides the set-up for applications to rigidity problems that are the primary concern of the project, and contains many rigidity results in the direction of Objectives (1) and (2). On top of this, we established in [2] some basic technical tools for the study of sub-VMRT structures such as the Thickening Lemma ([2], Proposition 6.1) and constructed a moduli space of chains of minimal rational curves under some nondegeneracy assumptions. Together with Yan-Ting Lam we obtained some partial results for Objective (3), as follows. Let X be a very general hypersurface of degree d in P^n with d at most equal to n and (d+2)(d+1) > 6n-7. Let X(t) be a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds parametrized by the unit disk D such that X(t) is biholomorphically equivalent to X for t different from 0. Then, the central fiber X(0) is also biholomorphically equivalent to X.

703912.label: Major findings and research outcome
703912.value: We laid in [1] [2] the foundation of a theory of geometric sub-structures, called sub-VMRT structures, on uniruled projective manifolds X, providing a starting point for the study of rigidity of uniruled projective subvarieties on X. When X is G/P of Picard number 1, we considered admissible pairs (Z,X) of rational homogeneous spaces including the cases where Z is of subdiagram type, in which case we proved a rigidity result ([2], Main Theorem 1) called Schubert rigidity when Z is nonlinear or when Z is a maximal linear subspace of X with a few identified exceptions. More precisely, given a locally closed complex submanifold S on X such that T_x(S) is equivalent to T_0(Z) under the action of G = Aut(X), we proved that S must be an open subset of gZ for some g in G. In the symmetric case, our method yielded a differential-geometric proof of Schur rigidity of Z, i.e., given any projective subvariety Y on X such that as homology classes [Y] = r[Z], Y must be a sum of translates gZ of Z . Main Theorem 1 follows from (a) proving that S is linearly saturated and (b) reconstructing S as an open subset of some gZ by the method of adjoining minimal rational curves. For the crucial starting point (a) we introduced a notion of nondegeneracy for substructures expressed in terms of second fundamental forms for the pair (C_0(Z),C_0(X)) consisting of the VMRT of X and the sub-VMRT of Z at a reference point 0 lying on Z, when C_0(X) is considered as a projective submanifold of PT_0(X). In a nutshell our method microlocalizes the rigidity problem. We developed more generally the method of sub-VMRT structures on uniruled projective manifolds X and established in [2], Main Theorem 2, the Algebraicity Theorem showing that under certain conditions S can be completed to a projective subvariety. The method of sub-VMRT structures for rigidity applies in principle to Schubert cycles, and prototypes consisting of cones of minimal rational curves V(x) on Hermitian symmetric spaces were examined in [3] where we proved an algebraicity result on locally closed complex submanifolds modelled on V(x). While Schur rigidity in the symmetric case has been completely settled by cohomological means by Robles-The (2012), our approach is geometric in nature and it applies to the non-symmetric case and also to study Schubert rigidity for singular Schubert cycles on G/P.

703912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703912.value: A major outcome of the project, which went beyond the original formulation, was that we have laid a foundation for the theory of sub-VMRT structures on uniruled projective manifolds and that such a theory was applicable to solve rigidity problems arising from the first two objectives of the project. As a natural outgrowth of the project, we have formulated a further project arising from the theory of sub-VMRT structures. The project, entitled “Geometric substructures on uniruled projective manifolds defined by tangential intersection with VMRTs”, was submitted to the HKRGC in application for a GRF grant, and the proposal was approved in June 2016. The project was started on January 1, 2017.

703912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703912.value: Since the mid-1990s, the Principal Investigator has been working on a differential-geometric theory on uniruled projective manifolds X based on the study of sets of minimal rational curves on them. With some oversimplification X is filled up by lines and the space of lines passing through a general point of X defines a distinguished set of tangent directions at x which we call the variety of minimal rational tangents (VMRT) at the point x. A first nontrivial set of examples are the VMRTs on hyperquadrics, which are precisely defined by the null cones. In the 4-dimensional case the hyperquadric is a compactification of the complexified space time, and the VMRT consists precisely of null directions defined by the underlying holomorphic conformal structure. On a Riemannian manifold there is the distinguished set of subvarieties which are totally geodesic. If we treat X as being an analogue of a Riemannian manifold, and the lines as analogues of geodesics, then there is the set of distinguished subvarieties of X consisting of subvarieties which are linearly saturated and uniruled by lines. As an outcome of the project we have established the foundation of sub-VMRT structures for the purpose of studying such distinguished subvarieties.

704612.label: Realisation of objectives
704612.value: It is crucial to understand the functions and localization of a protein within cells in order to uncover the secret of life processes. Fluorescence sensing has been widely used in cell/chemical biology due to its high sensitivity and convenience in real-time studies of intact systems. Metal ion conjugating with a small-molecule fluorophore is one of the most widely used strategies in fluorescent sensors to identify proteins and small molecules. In this project, the PI and his colleagues have carried out extensive work on design and development of a new class of fluorescence probes to track intracellular proteins. More specifically, (a) We synthesized bifunctional fluorescent molecules consisting of a nitrilotriacetate moiety, a fluorophore (coumarin, fluorescein and BODIPY) and an arylazide. The former coordinates metal ions to make the fluorescent probe specific and the latter as an anchor to 'lock' the probe and the protein of interest (POI) through photo activation. The probes were carefully characterized by NMR, MS and fluorescence spectroscopy. The quantum yield of the probes was ca. 60%, and importantly the probe is tunable and 'turn-on' by 6-40 times upon protein binding. (b) We then examined their cell permeability of the probes (the ligand with a metal bound), and found that these probes (i.e. the ligand with Ni2+, Cu2+, Bi3+ and Cr3+) exhibited excellent cell permeability towards various cells including E. coli, H. pylori, Hep G2 and Hela cells, and even plant tissues. (c) A high-throughput method was therefore established. We showed that the probe has multiple applications: (i) targeting histidine-tagged proteins inside cells as demonstrated with His6-XPA in E. coli and Hela cells, (ii) endogenous metalloproteins in different types of cells and (iii) as a potential new agent to monitor metal trafficking between proteins. The latter is unexpected. Two papers were published (Metallomics2014, 6, 1731-1736; PNAS 2015 112, 2948-2953). This part of the work was highlighted in Nature Biotech and believed to be a breakthrough work on NTA-based technology. (d) We showed that in situ visualization and subsequent identification of intracellular endogenous metalloproteins using a “metal-tunable” fluorescent probe can be achieved. We further validated the method by tracking nickel-binding-proteins from Helicobacter pylori and copper(II) binding proteins in Hela cells. Significantly, we discovered that Cr3+ is associated with proteins mainly localized in mitochondria, altered mitochondrial morphology and perturbed ATP synthesis. To our knowledge, this is the first report on the identification of Cr-binding proteins in cells. The strategy can readily be extended to image metalloproteomes and track subcellular localization of metallodrug targets inside live cells. Importantly we showed that the probe can be used to track transient and/or weak metal-protein interactions. A paper partially based on this work was published in Metallomics (2016, 8, doi: 10.1039/C6MT00169F), another one is in preparation, and a patent entitled "metal chelation-based fluorescent probes for protein or other biomolecule labeling in cells" was filed. (e) We develop a Hpnl-FRET probe by cloning hpnl (and its mutants) between the two FRET partners cfp and yfp to overexpress the Hpnl-FRET probe in E. coli. We extensively characterized the probe which exhibited certain selectivity towards Ni2+, Zn2+ and Bi3+; studied metal-binding properties in vivo (E. coli). A paper was published in J. Inorg. Chem. (2015, 142, 8-14). All of the objectives have been achieved and new projects were initialized. Our work opens a new horizon for tracking and editing metalloproteins in a cell, providing critical information for metalloproteomics.

704612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704612.value: The fluorescence probes we developed in this project have attracted enormous attention from biology community and we received many requests for the use of the probes. The series of the probe was regarded as a ground breaking work on NTA-based technology. In addition to the use of tracking intracellular proteins, we also extend the probes for quantification of His-tagged proteins as an alternative for Western blot. A patent is filed (Chinese patent) and biotechnology companies in US and China expressed their interest to license the compounds. We also further extend the strategy for development of arsenic-binding proteins, allowing arsenic-binding proteins to be tracking. We have used such a probe to understand the mechanism of action of arsenic trioxide for the treatment of leuckmia (APL). These probes may be commercialized. We therefore built up a platform for tracking metal-protein interactions at genome-wide scale together with other techniques developed by the PI, offering a powerful for metalloproteomics.

704612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704612.value: Comprehensive investigation into functions and localization of proteins within cells is crucial. Fluorescence sensing has been widely used in cell/chemical biology due to its high sensitivity and convenience in real-time studies of intact systems. Metal ion conjugating with a small-molecule fluorophore is one of the most widely used strategies in fluorescent sensors to identify proteins and small molecules. In this project, we have synthesized a series of bifunctional fluorescent sensors, and found that the probe can ‘light-up’ proteins (>13-fold). We found that introduction of arylazide in the fluorophore results in anchoring of the protein of interest (POI), allowing those proteins bind metal weakly and/or transicently to be studied. Importantly we found these probes can enter into cells to turn the fluorescence on upon binding to the POI. We used the nickel(II)-bound ligand to visualize histidine-tagged proteins inside cells, providing a novel approach to track protein localization and functions. We also prepared a metal-tunable probe (e.g. Cu2+, Cr3+ and Bi3+-bound) which again enters into both bacteria and mammalian cells, to edit different metal-binding proteins. We finally developed a Hpnl-FRET probe. Our work provide a new library of fluorescence probes for functional study of (metallo)proteins as well as for metallobiology.

704712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704712.value: The Central Asian Orogenic Belt (CAOB) is the largest Phanerozoic accretionary orogenic belt in the world and hosts numerous mineral deposits. Recently published geochemical data, including our own, indicate that the CAOB represents the most significant continental growth of the earth in the Phanerozoic. This challenges the perception of many researchers that the growth of the continental crust was mostly completed in the Precambrian and the amount of juvenile crust produced in the Phanerozoic was insignificant. However, the mechanism of the continental growth and its complicated accretionary processes are presently poorly understood, because a large variety of allochthonous units with different age and nature were accreted in different times, including island arcs, ophiolites, oceanic islands, seamounts, accretionary prisms, oceanic plateaus and microcontinents. The Altai-Mongolian terrane is an important portion of the CAOB, and it was previously considered to be part of the composite Kazakhstan-Baikal continent or the Altai-Mongolian microcontinent. However, our recent geological, geochronological and geochemical studies on gneissic and sedimentary rocks of the Chinese portion of the Altai-Mongolian terrane questioned this interpretation. Our data do not support that the Chinese Altai is part of a Precambrian continent, but instead it represents an active margin on a Neoproterozoic continent. This proposed study will involve an extensive study of granitic rocks in the Altai-Mongolian terrane, including areas in China, Russia and Mongolia. Systematic field investigation, U-Pb and Hf isotopic analyses of zircons will be combined with geochemical, and Rb-Sr and Sm-Nd isotopic analyses of igneous rocks to decipher the magmatic history and tectonic evolution of the region. Hotly debated tectonic models, including our own, will be rigorously tested. Results of this study will provide solid constraints on the continental crustal growth of Central Asia and shed light on the accretionary orogenic processes in general. 中亞造山帶是世界上最大的顯生宙增生造山帶並賦存大量的礦產資源。最近包括我們自己發表的地球化學數據表明這個造山帶代表了地球顯生宙最重要的大陸增長。這對多數學者的觀念提出了挑戰，因為通常認為在前寒武紀大陸已經基本形成，而在顯生宙形成的新陸殼是微不足道的。目前對這種大陸生長的機制和增生過程還不甚了解，因為大量的不同年齡不同性質的岩石物質由異地而來加入到造山帶裡面來，包括島弧，蛇綠岩，洋島，海山，增生楔，海洋高原以及微陸塊，使這一過程極為複雜。阿爾泰造山帶是中亞造山帶的重要地體以往被認為屬於哈薩克斯坦-貝加爾複合古陸或者蒙古阿爾泰微古陸的一部分。然而我們最近在中國阿爾泰針對片麻岩和沉積岩石的地質、年代學和地球化學研究質疑了這一觀點。我們的數據表明中國阿爾泰是一個位于新元古代大陸的活動陸緣而非前寒武紀古陸。此課題申請將對阿爾泰造山帶分佈的酸性岩漿岩開展系統的野外調查，選擇代表樣品進行地球化學分析，包括鋯石鈾鉛鉿同位素和全岩地球化學，銣鍶釤釹同位素等，以期揭示該區岩漿活動歷史和構造演化歷史。激烈爭論的構造模式，包括我們自己提出的模式，將被嚴格地檢驗。此研究的結果將對大陸的形成提供實質的制約，並啟示我們對造山作用的認識。

704712.label: Realisation of objectives
704712.value: The objectives in the original proposal are all realised in this study. Extensive field work has been carried our in the Altai Mountain Range, which straddle China, Russia and Mongolia. About 200 samples, mainly granitic rocks, were collected. Thin sections for these samples were made and observed under petrological microscope to check their freshness and study their mineral compositions. The representative samples were analysed for their major and trace elements and Rb-Sr and Sm-Nd isotopic compositions. Zircon minerals were separated from the large fresh samples and analysed for their U-Pb and Lu-Hf isotopic compositions at HKU ICP-MS laboratory. The results enabled us to compare the evolutionary history of the Chinese, Russian, and Mongolian Altai. Tectonic models such as the distribution of Precambrian basement are rigorously tested. The magmatic and accretionary history of the Altai-Monolian terrane is now elucidated.

704712.label: Major findings and research outcome
704712.value: This study discovered that the previously envisaged Precambrian rocks such as the Terekta Formation in Russia was formed in the Middle Ordovician. In combination with our data from the Chinese and Mongolian Altai, we conclude that the Precambrian basement does not exist in the whole Altai-Monolian terrane, while the Precambrian detritus and xenocrysts in granitic rocks came from the Tuva-Monolia Block (e.g. Cai et al., 2016a). This study clearly shows that the Gorny Altai in Russia had a different evolutionary history from the Chinese and Mongolian Altai. It was developed as an oceanic arc initiated in the Neoproterozoic, but it collided with the Chinese Altai before Devonian, geochemical data for the Yaloman complex in Russia indicate that the Gorny Altai collided with the Chinese Altai at 389 Ma ago and a composite continental arc setting was then formed (e.g. Cai et al., 2014a; Chen et al., 2016). Our data show that magmatism was continuous in the Paleozoic, but peaked at about 400 and 280 Ma. The compositions of the magmas at 400 Ma were very diverse, including the unusual high-Mg rock associations in the Chinese Altai and other magmas with specific tectonic significance (e.g. He et al., 2016). The region experienced high-temperature geothermal gradient, which caused melting of the subducted slab, metasomatized lithosperic mantle, and lower crust. We attribute such a tectonic condition to a possible oceanic ridge subduction (e.g. He et al., 2015). Magmas were also originated both from the mantle and the lower crust and they mixed together to form large intrusions at 546 Ma in the Bayankhonger (Zhang Y et al., 2015). We propose that multiple ridge-trench interaction was possibly responsible for the voluminous magmatism and granitoids intrusion in the evolutionary history of the Altai region (e.g. Cai et al., 2016a). The magmatism in Permian is dated in this study at 270-290 Ma (Cai et al., 2016b, Tong et al., 2014, Cai et al., 2014b), and they intruded in an extensional setting (e.g. Cai et al., 2014b), related to the exhumation (e.g. Li et al., 2015, Jiang et al., 2015). Our structural analysis indicates multiple deformations in the southern margin of the Chinese Altai, correlated to the Devonian-Carboniferous accretion/collision between the Altai-Mongolian and East Junggar terranes and Permian transpressional tectonic respectively (Li et al., 2015, 2016a and 2016b, Zhang J et al., 2015).

704712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704712.value: Geophysical study is necessary to reveal the deep structure of the Altai-Mongolian terrane. I submitted a proposal for the Hong Kong RGC - French ANR Joint Research Scheme last year, but it was not funded. I will seek other opportunities for further study.

704712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704712.value: The Altai-Mongolian terrane was previously considered to be part of the composite Kazakhstan-Baikal continent or the Altai-Mongolian microcontinent. This study indicates that the terrane cannot be a (micro-) continent, because ancient Archean rocks do not exist there and this terrane is mainly made of juvenile crustal materials. In addition, the Gorny Altai in Russia was developed as an oceanic arc near to the Siberia Craton from the Neoproterozoic, while the Chinese and Mongolian Altai were developed as an active continental margin of the Tuva-Mongolian micro-continent in the Early Paleozoic, which was derived from the Gondwana continent in the south. They collided before the Devonian (about 400 million years ago) to form a united subduction-accretion system, then amalgamated with the East Junggar terrane in the Permian (about 280 million years ago). The intensive magmatic activity about 400 million years ago was due to a high geothermal gradient, which caused partial melting of the mantle wedge, subducted slab, and the lower crust. The mechanism was due to subduction of an oceanic ridge, upwelling of the asthenosphere brought heat, energy and materials to the lithosphere.
