704812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704812.value: 鉑化合物順鉑在抗癌臨床上的運用激發了研究者去研發新的有抗癌功能的金屬化合物。儘管在過去的四十年中付出了很多的努力，只有很少的金屬抗癌藥物進入了臨床試驗，其中包括幾個順鉑衍生物和釕化合物。在金屬化合物治療的發展中遇到了一些問題，比如由於金屬和多肽或者蛋白中的巰基相互作用引起的毒副作用，藥物解毒作用和細胞抗藥性。金屬，特別是鉑，跟含有巰基的腎臟酶之間很強的不可逆轉性的作用被認為是導致一些接受鉑化合物化療的病人腎出問題的主要原因。 金屬離子及其配合物有獨特的結構特點和特別的物理，化學，生物特點。跟一般的有機物比起來， 這些特點給與金屬離子及其配合物在生物體系中不可替代的位置。通過正確的選擇配體，金屬化合物可以被調節和合理的設計成有親硫性，或者相反，跟比如半胱氨酸或者蛋氨酸這些含硫供體的生物分子有很弱的親和性。我們被最近報導的和我們目前研究的關於有潛在的抗癌活性和低的急性或者腎臟毒性的金的二硫代氨基甲酸化合物及其衍生物所吸引。雙齒二硫代氨基甲酸配體上的硫原子有強的反位效應，可以禁止生物分子中的硫供體跟金離子配位， 這有可能提高其抗癌活性或者降低毒副作用。 為了解決當今化療劑的有問題的副作用和繼續努力鑑定出新的有抗癌活性的金化合物， 這個課題的主要目的是戰略性的極大促進含硫雙齒供體的金屬化合物在醫學方面的發展。通過合適的選擇和修飾雙齒含硫供體的配體，設計有增強的生物利用度，抗癌效果，生理條件穩定性和癌細胞的選擇性的金化合物是可行的。這些化合物對一系列的癌細胞，抗藥性細胞和正常細胞的體外廣泛的細胞毒性篩选和與其他生物分子的協同作用，還有抗血管增生的活性將會被檢查。那些有潛在作用的藥將會被選擇進行體內抗癌，毒性和代謝學（內源性或異種代謝物）的研究，而且會通過轉錄或者高等蛋白組學的研究方法去研究其活性的機理。這個課題的成功可以促進策略性的設計金屬化合物，尤其是那些有抗癌活性的金化合物，最終會使那些接受著有限治療選擇的經常性的癌症病人或者產生抗藥性的癌症病人收益。

704812.label: Realisation of objectives
704812.value: (i) By appropriate selection and design of different coordinating ligands, we have successfully prepared a series of twenty gold(I) and gold(III) complexes with bidentate S-donor ligands, phosphine ligand or N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) ligands. These complexes were found to display promising anti-cancer activities against a variety of cancer cell lines including the cisplatin-resistant ovarian A2780cis cell line. (ii) By a series of in vitro cell-based experiments, most of the gold(III) and gold(I) complexes were found to show potent anti-migration activities towards cancer cells and growth inhibitory effects on cancer stem cells. The in vivo anti-cancer activities of two gold complexes containing dithiocarbamato ligands have also been examined. These complexes show potent inhibitory activities on the growth of ovarian carcinoma in nude mice models. (iii) The molecular pathways of some highly active gold complexes have been identified by mean of transcriptomics and proteomics approaches. Some of them were found to inhibit thioredoxin reductase, induce oxidative stress, enhance death receptor 4’s expression, activate apoptosis, induce expression of caspase 3, caspase 8 and caspase 9 and/or even inhibit HBV DNA replication. (iv) Most gold complexes are stable in water with minimum amount of organic solvent such as DMSO or EtOH. In the presence of biological reductant glutathione (GSH), the complexes were found capable to form complexes with GSH and/or nanoparticles. Most of the complexes were stable in the presence of the digestive enzyme S9 for 1 hour, indicating that the gold(III) complexes have adequate solution stability and bioavailability. (v) Some gold complexes were successfully encapsulated by PEG or by metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). The encapsulation retains or even enhances the cytotoxicity and anti-migration of the gold complexes. (vi) With the support of the GRF, articles directly related to these works have been published in high-impact journals.

704812.label: Major findings and research outcome
704812.value: (i) Gold complexes. We have synthesized >20 gold(I) or gold(III) complexes, with physical properties including solubility and solution stability examined. Some gold(III) dithiocarbamato complexes were found to form nanoparticles in solutions. The size of nanoparticles is close to irregular vascular structure of tumor-associated blood vessels, suggesting their preference in entering tumor tissue. (ii) Biological activities. Most complexes displayed anti-cancer activities with cytotoxic IC50 values ranging from 200 nM to 18 µM. By wound healing assay, several gold complexes containing carbene and dithiocarbamato ligands were found to exhibit anti-metastatic properties toward cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancers. Sphere-formation assay revealed that some gold(III) complexes could display anti-cancer-stem-cell activities towards drug-resistant cancers. By using ovarian carcinoma-bearing nude mice, two gold complexes containing dithiocarbamato ligands were found to exhibit potent in vivo anti-tumor effects upon 14 days of treatment. (iii) Mechanistic studies. Transcriptomics studies revealed that gold(III) dithiocarbamato complexes exhibit inhibition on the ubiquitin-proteasome systems. Gold(III) complexes containing phosphine ligands could exhibit promising anti-cancer activities via the inhibition of thioredoxin reductase and production of reactive oxygen species. By proteomic approaches, most gold complexes were found to enhance the expression of caspase 3, 8 and 9, and in association with the activation of PARP-1. Hoechst 33258 staining showed that gold complexes could induce DNA fragmentation. A gold(III) pyrrolidinedithiocarbamate (PDTC) exhibited promising anti-hepatitis B virus (HBV) and anti-hepatocellular carcinoma activities. By RT-PCR, this complex showed ability in inhibiting HBV formation intracellularly and extracellularly. (iv) Stability and bioavailability. By UV-vis spectrometry, gold complexes were found to stable in aqueous solutions. Yet, hydrolysis occurs upon prolonged standing. Spectroscopic examination revealed that these gold complexes could form gold-GSH adducts. In the presence of the liver digestive enzyme S9, most gold complexes were stable in the solution, indicating that they exhibit adequate solution stability. By ICP-AES, the gold(III) complexes were found to disintegrate and form metal complexes with different free ions. (v) Encapsulation. We have employed metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) which consist of adenine and zinc to encapsulate some anti-cancer gold complexes. Through Transwell® assay, we proved that the encapsulated gold complexes exhibit a less cytotoxicity towards different cancer cells. Some gold(III) complexes which have good leaving groups display better anti-cancer activities than the gold complexes alone. (vi) Publication. Based on the results directly from this work, we have published articles in journals with high impact factors.

704812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704812.value: With the support from the GRF, a series of anti-cancer active gold complexes have been identified. Given that some of these complexes show adequate bioavailability and specificity towards cancerous cells and tissues, and notably some complexes developed in this project are highly potent towards drug-resistant cancer strains, more detailed and extensive in vitro and in vivo anti-cancer studies have to be launched for these drug leads in the next stage. After that, some anti-cancer active complexes can also be examined for their in vivo toxicity. Large rodent animal can also be employed for the acute and long term toxicological studies.

704812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704812.value: Despite effort and achievement have been made in the identifications of novel anti-cancer drug candidates as well as development of therapeutic options of cancer treatments, cancer remains a global threatened issue nowadays. A number of highly anti-cancer active gold complexes have been developed and identified under the support of this GRF. Some of these complexes are highly potent towards drug-resistant cancer cells and could significantly reduce the size of tumor in mice. Their action mechanisms for their anti-cancer activities have been examined, giving clues for scientists in optimizing the anti-cancer activities of some related gold complexes. Some new materials coined as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have been identified and employed to carry and enhance the stability of the gold complexes in biological systems. All these studies pave the ways for the medical development of novel anti-cancer drugs and give hope to cancer patients who are suffering from relapsed cancers and drug-resistant cancer strains.

705112.label: Realisation of objectives
705112.value: How we have achieved our objectives? Well planned long-term experiments with multiple-measurements: Experimental Designs The biofouling “tubeworms” are threatened by human-induced environmental change, particularly ocean acidification (OA), freshening and warming, because they undergo the notoriously difficult process of larval metamorphosis and calcification. We have made series of simultaneous measurements using tools borrowed from variety of disciplines, especially from molecular biology and mechanical engineering, to understand mechanisms through which tubeworms might adapt or succumb to multiple stressors in high-CO2 future coastal oceans. The major questions we have answered through this project are: Are climate change related stressors in the coastal oceans is more harmful for tubeworms in combination than alone? Our primary aim was to study the tubeworms structural integrity and physiological fitness in response to ocean acidification and multiple stressors. Here, we have tested THREE hypotheses using the calcareous tube-building worm as model system. Specifically, we have tested the hypothesis that tubeworms will form impaired tubes with poor mechanical properties under high-CO2. All these hypotheses were tested using the following experimental approaches: • Larvae of the species was cultured from embryo to adult stage under various projected multiple climate change stressors scenarios for their Hong Kong habitat, • Simultaneous measurements of tubeworms physiological, proteomics, ecological and mechanical properties were made using verity of tools borrowed from molecular biology, biomedical, materials science and mechanical engineering disciplines, • Most importantly, we have used variety of modern proteomics tools, e.g. iTRAQ analysis combined with bioassay, to examine various metabolic and signaling pathways (that are induced and suppressed by chemical cues) expression under projected near-future level of elevated CO2 levels. Interdisciplinary collaborations: The above tasks were executed by a group of graduate students and post-docs in the PI’s laboratory in close collaboration with several local and overseas professors (please see the list of our graduate students and Fig. 1 - attached with this report). We have effectively used our interdisciplinary research team consisting of highly talented graduate students, research assistants and Post-docs with complimentary research skills in this project. This project may not have been accomplished if we have not allowed our graduate students to cross traditional disciplinary boundaries to expand their expertise in the research field of larval biology. For which, we have established strong collaborations within HKU and in Hong Kong and internationally, which allowed us to address all the set three objectives of this project which are largely aimed at studying climate change effects on marine organisms at the developmental, biomineralization and proteomics levels. How far we have achieved our 3 objectives? Objective 1 (Develop response models …. and less saline water): Consequences of global environmental (and climate) change on calcifying coastal marine invertebrates was quantitatively examined through multi-factor, multi-life stages and multiple end-point studies. This objective fully addressed in this project through our 3-year long multiple experiments that collectively examined the interactive effect of decreased pH (7.4 “P”), warming (29oC “T”) and reduced salinity (27‰ “S”) on pre- and post-settlement developmental processes of the calcareous tube-building polychaete worm, Hydroides elegans using several factorial manipulation experiments. The objective was addressed by TWO graduate students (Vera BS Chan and Ackley Lane), both of them are from larval biology background and graduated with full support from this project. Majority of their results were now published in several international journals (listed publication no: 9 and 14). Objective 2 (Measure internal pH regulation … climate change). This is one of the very important and novel objectives of this project. This objective was realized through taking two collaborative steps: 1) we have invited the expert on fluorescent microscopy analyses”, Dr. Takashi Toyofuku and Ms. Sachiko Kawada from Institute of Biogeosciences, Japan Agency for Marine Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC), Japan to our laboratory and established a very strong collaboration involving joint-student training and exchange. As a result of it, our graduate students Vera BS Chan and Roy Li have learned the internal pH measurement technology from the expert and finally used the technique in our laboratory. 2) Visit by Dr Emma Gibbin from École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, 1015 Lausanne, Switzerland to the PI’s laboratory for 2 months to work with our graduate students (Ackley Lane, Roy Li and Camilla Campati) on the effect of climate change on internal pH changes during larval metamorphosis As a results of these two successful interdisciplinary (larval ecology and cellular biology), we were able to map internal pH regulation and changes during larval metamorphosis in marine organisms using the worm as model. These results were published in THREE high impact factor journals (listed as no 6, 11 and 16). Objective 3 (Assess the role of …internal pH regulation, and adaptation to multiple-stressors). We had a much challenging task while we have tried to address this objective, it was much more changing. The challenge was primarily due to incomplete genome analysis of this species. We have been waiting for the complete genome information from one of our previous collaborators, PY Qian for The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, it was completely released to the PI’s group only latter part of 2016. The second, relatively minor, challenge was due to high mortality of larvae while we expose to inhibitors and inducers, especially when we use very high density of larvae (which was necessary for OMICs analysis). We have overcome both of these objectives through multiple tries and talking to several experts during the course of this project. Now we have successfully addressed this objective. Multiple institutional collaborations were established to address this objective. First, we have joint with HKU’s proteomics expert (Ivan Chu), and marine genome specialist (PY Qian) and marine evolution expert (Sam Dupont from Sweden). Our graduate students (Ackley Lane) and post docs (Dr Joy Mukerjee) joint with these experts and executed this objective. Although we have published a good paper on the first part of this objective (listed as no 9) and publication of the proteomics results (2nd part) is still either under review or under preparation (listed as no 14 and 15). Additional work: In addition to what we have proposed in this project, we have taken great lead to study the full-array of biomechanical features of this tube-worm and especially their biomineral response to climate change. We have successfully built a biomechnical model for this species to understand: (1) internal distribution of mechanical stress in a tube, (2) external load that can be simulated to mimic different biological conditions applied to a tube, and (3) complex mechanical behaviour that cannot be observed experimentally was simulated.

705112.label: Major findings and research outcome
705112.value: Findings: By combining several controlled experiments with more complicated designs that include quantitative genetics, fertilization kinetics, proteomics, larval bioassays and parental influence, we have obtained (and presented and published) an in-depth, multi-perspective view study of how economically important biofouling species may fare as conditions shift over a relatively long period of time while our coastal climate is experiencing multiple stressors due to elevated anthropogenic atmospheric CO2. Our major findings are: 1. We have solidly found that “ocean acidification, warming and freshening interactively affect pre- and post-settlement processes in marine benthic invertebrates” (publication no 14) 2. Aragonite structures are more sensitive to ocean acidification (OA) and are more difficult to remove by anti-fouling treatments, thus early developmental stages of the tubeworms are not only sensitive to subtle changes in pH due to OA but may also be important for biofouling control (publication no 4 and 10). 3. Potential sites for calcification were documented with a high intracellular pH values quantified as 8.5 -9.0. These regions were also found to have high levels of calcium ion present. 4. Tubeworms produce a mechanically weaker tube with less resistance to simulated predator attack under ocean acidification (OA at pH 7.8) (publication no 4) 5. The biofouling strength of the tubeworm is likely to be enhanced by warming in the future ocean, and more effective antifouling or removal method may be necessary (publication no 2 and 4). 6. A detailed understanding of the molecular mechanisms of larval metamorphosis and their response to ocean acidification, and revealed a number of candidate metabolic and signaling pathways (and their associated genes and proteins) for prospective tubeworm surveillance in future acidified oceans (publication no 8, 11, and 15). 7. Ultimately, our experience from this project and data strongly argue in favor of studies involving multiple stressors (OA, hypoxia, and warming), long-term exposure, multiple endpoints, multiple life stages and comparisons across species using interdisciplinary approaches to understand mechanisms. Research outcome: This project has made the PI’s group to become one of the highly successful and productive research groups locally and internationally. For example, this project contributed for the publication of >16 publications, and both PI’s and graduate students presented their results > 12 international research conferences. Importantly, 4 students have graduated as a result of this project. Also as stated in other parts of this project, this project helped the PI’s group to establish as very strong “interdisciplinary cross-institutional collaborations”.

705112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705112.value: This project has directed our interdisciplinary collaborative team to design experiments to find solutions for sustainable management of coastal marine biodiversity in a changing climate and to enrich the scientific value of calcifying organisms. This project advise researchers: • To understand how climate change will impact the fitness of several calcifying species along the China coast – which will help identify a climate change tolerant species/strain and develop new coastal management technology to ensure marine biodiversity in a high-CO2 ocean • To identify the interaction between calcification and biomechanics of shells or tubes produced in response to climate change – to develop marine-derived biostructures as scaffolds for bone regeneration • To investigate the significance of community engagement for the sustainability of local coastal diversity and biofouling under climate change. In this regard, the PI and the 2 Co-I’s of this proposal have took several steps: 1. Multiple GRF’s – The PI, Co-I’s and their collaborators (Haimin Yao of Poly U) has successfully applied 3 GRF’s partially based on the result of this project and now there are running in full-swing 2. The PI’s and Co-I’s of this project now intensively trying (already submitted) to secure RGC’s collaborative research projects (CRP).

705112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705112.value: Natural environmental change and anthropogenic activities, i.e. rising CO2, have resulted in ocean acidification, which has the potential to greatly influence the success of this key metamorphic transition by potentially affecting both appropriate calcification process and physiology of variety of marine clacifying species including. Using a model calcifying larval species, this project answered a question: how rising CO2 might affect their physiology and molecular processes? Our results suggest that climate change will disturb fast-growing larvae thereby poses a threat to their survival by affecting their timing and choice of attachment and accelerated growth afterwards. We have also mapped molecular mechanisms whereby climate change stressors, especially ocean acidification will affect calcifying species. In collaboration with mechanical engineers, we have also mapped the architecture of the calcareous tubes and its mechanical properties in response to multiple climate change stressors using tools borrowed from mechanical engineering. The molecular processes that direct the response of tubeworms to multiple stressors and their fitness in terms of tube mechanics was understood to large extent. Ultimately, his study provided new insights into how benthic biofouling communities would develop in near-future-ocean with multiple climate change drivers.

705212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
705212.value: 相干單自旋發射器的輸運性質

705212.label: Project Objectives
705212.value: In this project, we investigate the injection of quantized pure spin current into quantum conductor. In particular, we study an on demand single spin source generated by periodically varying the gate voltage inside the two dimensional topological insulator. We will understand theoretically the nature of the quantized pure spin current. We will develop a theoretical formalism of parametric pumping for spin current at finite bias and finite frequency using non-equilibrium Green’s function method. It will be very interesting to study the shot noise and transient behavior of the single spin gun. We will also study how the quantum information stored in the single spin source can be preserved during the transport process. We will investigate the dephasing and inelastic scattering using two dephasing models: voltage probe and dephasing probe.

We will understand theoretically the nature of the quantized pure spin current. We will develop a theoretical formalism of parametric pumping for spin current at finite bias and finite frequency using non-equilibrium Green’s function method.

It will be very interesting to study the shot noise and transient behavior of the single spin gun. We will also study how the quantum information stored in the single spin source can be preserved during the transport process. We will investigate the dephasing and inelastic scattering using two dephasing models: voltage probe and dephasing probe.

705212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705212.value: Traditional electronics is based on the flow of charge where the spin of the electron is ignored. The emerging technology of spintronics will explore the spin degree of freedom such that the flow of spin, in addition to charge, will be used for electronic applications. So far, progress has been achieved in several areas of spintronics such as the applications of giant magnetoresistive effect, the understanding of material properties of magnetic semiconductors, the improvements of spin injection across a magnetic-nonmagnetic interface, and optical manipulation of spin degrees of freedom. Spin degree of freedom can also be used to process quantum information. It is well known that qubits or quantum bit, the unit of quantum information, is one of the basic building blocks for quantum information science. A large variety of candidate qubit systems have been proposed such as photonic qubit and electron qubit. Recently, an on demand coherent single electron source has been produced experimentally. By applying ac gate voltage, periodic sequence of single electron emission and absorption on nanoseconds generate a quantized ac current. This single electron source can be used as a qubit in ballistic conductors which is an important step towards 2DEG quantum computer. The major problem in the realization of quantum computers is to identify qubits with long coherence time, spin qubits seem to be the ideal candidate. This is because the spin of electron is weakly coupled to the environment compared with charge degree of freedom, the quantum coherence can be maintained at much longer time scale. It is therefore important to study the transport properties of on demand coherent single spin source that can be used as spin qubit. In this project, we propose to generate an on demand coherent single spin source from two dimensional topological insulators using the concept of parametric pumping. We emphasize that the generated spin current has no accompanying charge current and thus is a pure spin source. We will develop a quantum transport theory for time-dependent pumped spin current using non-equilibrium Green’s function method in both adiabatic and non-adiabatic regimes. We will address the following issues: (1). What is the shot noise of single spin source. (2). The transient behavior of the single spin source. (3). The single spin current in the presence of dephasing mechanism. (4). We will also explore other ways of generating coherent single spin source. (5). What is counting statistics of few spin sources. 传统的电子学是基于电子电荷的流动而忽略电子的自旋属性，新兴的自旋电子学将基于电子自旋的流动而非其带电属性。到目前为止，自旋电子学的很多领域已经有了长足的发展，例如巨磁阻效应的应用、磁性半导体材料性质的理解、磁性和非磁性材料界面自旋注入效率的改善以及光学操控自旋属性。此外自旋属性可以用来传递量子信息。众所周知，量子信息的基本单元比特或者量子比特是量子信息科学中的基石。为此人们提出了很多候选的比特系统，例如，光比特和电子比特。近来，实验上已经生产出了急需的单电子相干源。在此器件中，随着交流门电压信号的变化，一系列周期在纳秒量级的单电子发射和接收的过程产生了量子化的交流电流。这个单电子源可以做为在弹道导体的比特信号，这为实现二维电子气量子计算机迈出了重要的一步。实现量子计算机中最大的问题是在长相干时间尺度内识别比特信号，对此自旋比特是非常理想的候选。这是因为相对于电子的带电属性，电子的自旋由于环境的影响更弱，从而使得自旋的量子相干可以保持更长的时间。所以，对于产生自旋比特的单自旋发射源的研究显得尤为重要。在这个项目中，我们提出利用参数泵浦的的概念，在二维拓扑绝缘体中产生相干的单自旋源。非常重要的是在此产生的自旋流并没有伴随电流，也就是说这一个纯的自旋源。我们将基于非平衡态格林函数方法发展一套适用在绝热和非绝热区域的含时量子输运理论。我们将着重解决以下问题：（1）. 单自旋源的噪声问题。（2）. 单自旋源的瞬时行为问题。（3）. 单自旋流受退相干影响的问题。（4）. 我们也会探索其它产生相干单自旋源的方法。（5）. 一些自旋源的计数统计问题。

705212.label: Realisation of objectives
705212.value: We have achieved all the objectives. In particular, we reported on the injection of quantized pure spin current into quantum conductors. We proposed an on-demand single-spin source generated by periodically varying the gate voltages of two quantum dots that are connected to a two-dimensional topological insulator via tunneling barriers. Due to the nature of the helical states of the topological insulator, one or several spin pairs can be pumped out per cycle giving rise to a pure quantized alternating spin current. Depending on the phase difference between two gate voltages, this device can serve as an on-demand single-spin emitter or single-charge emitter. Again, due to the helicity of the topological insulator, the single-spin emitter or charge emitter is dissipationless and immune to disorder. The proposed single-spin emitter can be an important building block of future spintronic devices. We numerically investigated the statistical properties of electrochemical capacitance in disordered two dimensional mesoscopic capacitors. Based on the tight-binding Hamiltonian, the Green’s function formalism was adopted to study the average electrochemical capacitance, its fluctuation as well as the distribution of capacitance of the disordered mesoscopic capacitors for three different ensembles: orthogonal (symmetry index β = 1), unitary (β = 2), and symplectic (β = 4). It was found that the electrochemical capacitance in the disordered systems exhibits universal behavior. In the case of a single conducting channel, the electrochemical capacitance follows a symmetric Gaussian distribution at weak disorders as expected from the random matrix theory. In the strongly disordered regime, the distribution was found to be a sharply one-sided form with a nearly constant tail in the large capacitance region. This behavior is due to the existence of the necklace states in disordered systems, which is characterized by the multiresonance that gives rise to a large density of states. In addition, it was found that the necklace state also enhances the fluctuation of electrochemical capacitance in the case of a single conducting channel. Waiting time is an important transport quantity that is complementary to average current and its fluctuation. So far all the studies of waiting time distribution (WTD) are limited to steady-state transport (either dc or ac). The existing theory cannot deal with WTD in the transient regime. In this regard, we develop a theoretical formalism based on Keldysh nonequilibrium Green’s-function formalism to study WTD. This theory is suitable for dc, ac, and transient transport and can be used for first-principles calculation on realistic systems. We applied this theory to a quantum dot system with an upward bias pulse and calculate cumulants of transferred charge as well as WTD in the transient regime. The oscillatory behavior of WTD is found in the transient regime. We gave a general relation between WTD and experimental measured quantity and demonstrated its feasibility for a quantum dot system in the transient regime. We presented a theoretical study of the tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) and spin-polarized transport in Fe3Si/MgO/Fe3Si(001) magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ). It was found that the spin-polarized conductance and bias-dependent TMR ratios are rather sensitive to the structure of Fe3Si electrode. From the symmetry analysis of the band structures, we found that there is no spin-polarized D1 symmetry bands crossing the Fermi level for the cubic Fe3Si. In contrast, the tetragonal Fe3Si driven by in-plane strain reveals half-metal nature in terms of D1 state. The giant TMR ratios were predicted for both MTJs with cubic and tetragonal Fe3Si electrodes under zero bias. Using the nonequilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) approach, we developed a microscopic ac transport theory in the presence of electron-phonon interaction. Taking into account the self-consistent Coulomb interaction, the displacement current is included. This ensures that our theory satisfies the current-conserving and gauge-invariant conditions. Importantly, the inclusion of self-consistent Coulomb interaction naturally connects the NEGF formalism to the density functional theory (DFT). This allows us to calculate the self-consistent Hamiltonian using DFT within the NEGF framework, which paves the way for first principles ac transport calculation of nanoelectronic devices in the presence of electron-phonon interaction. It is known that the inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) is a powerful tool in studying the inelastic dc quantum transport in molecular devices. The basic idea of IETS is to obtain the information of vibrational spectrum of molecular devices by measuring the second derivative of the dc current with respect to the bias voltage. In the ac transport, we found that the phonon spectrum and electron-phonon coupling strength can be obtained from the second derivative of the admittance with respect to the frequency which is the working principle of the inelastic electron admittance spectroscopy (IEAS). Hence we proposed to use IEAS to probe the effect of the phonon in ac transport. As an example, dynamic conductance of a quantum dot was discussed in detail and the concept of IEAS was demonstrated. We reported on a first-principles investigation of transient heat current through molecular devices under step like pulse of external and gate voltages. Using the nonequilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) approach, an exact solution of transient heat current was obtained that goes beyond the wide-band limit. Combining with density functional theory (DFT), we proposed a time-dependent NEGF-DFT formalism to study the transient heat current under a step like pulse for molecular devices from first principles. Anticipating the huge computational cost in the transient regime, we develop an algorithm to speed up the calculation using the complex absorbing potential (CAP). By adding the CAP to replace the Hamiltonian of leads, the effective self-energy of the Green’s function becomes independent of energy, allowing analytic calculation of the triple integrations in the exact solution of transient heat current using the theorem of residue. With this linear scaling algorithm, the computational complexity is greatly reduced, and a first-principles calculation of transient heat current of molecular devices becomes possible. As an example, we applied our NEGF-DFT-CAP formalism for a molecular device, the Di-thiolbenzene molecule connected by two semi-infinite aluminum leads, and we calculate the transient heat current under an upward gate voltage pulse. The enhancement of heat current was observed.

705212.label: Major findings and research outcome
705212.value: In this project, we reported the investigation of full-counting statistics (FCS) of transferred charge and spin in the transient regime. A general theoretical formulation for the generating function was presented using a non-equilibrium Green’s function approach[7]. This formalism can be generalized to account for spin transport for the system with non-collinear spin as well as spin-orbit interaction. We investigated the valley-dependent transport of a graphene system consisting of a uniaxially stretched graphene sheet connected by two unstrained parts, with the interfaces between the strained and unstrained regions along the zigzag direction[8]. A detailed study on the Fabry–Pérot states in the strained region revealed that they carry opposite lateral currents for different valleys when a bias is applied across the interfaces. The shot noise in a toroidal carbon nanotube (TCN) interferometer under the perturbation of a rotating magnetic field (RMF) was investigated[9]. A general shot noise formula was derived by calculating the current correlation. It was found that photon absorption and emission induce novel features of dynamic shot noise. The oscillatory behavior of shot noise and Fano factor vary with the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) magnetic flux, and they are sensitively dependent on the Zeeman energy, frequency of RMF, and source-drain bias. Using the nonequilibrium Green’s function method within the framework of density functional theory, we investigated various transport properties, such as I -V characteristics, shot noise, thermopower, dynamical conductance, of Au- and Na-encapsulatedWSe2 nanotube heterojunctions[10]. We proposed, for the first time, a valley Seebeck effect in gate tunable zigzag graphene nanoribbons as a result of the interplay between thermal gradient and valleytronics[11]. A pure valley current is further generated by the thermal gradient as well as the external bias. In a broad temperature range, the pure valley current was found to be linearly dependent on the temperature gradient while it increases with the increasing temperature of one lead for a fixed thermal gradient. A valley field effect transistor (FET) driven by the temperature gradient was proposed that can turn on and off the pure valley current by gate voltage. We investigated the full-counting statistics (FCS) of energy flow carried by electrons in the transient regime[12]. We formulated a nonequilibrium Keldysh Green’s function theory to compute the generating function for FCS of energy transport. Specifically, we expressed the generating function using the path integral along the Keldysh contour and obtain an exact solution of the generating function using the Grassmann algebra.

705812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705812.value: InGaN/GaN multiple-quantum-wells (MQW) structure works as the active light-emitting layer in advanced LEDs and LDs which have tremendous applications in the emerging solid-state lighting due to their short-wavelength light emission nature. In this project, we propose to conduct a detailed study on new optical properties of InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars prepared with top-down method. Two kinds of InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars fabricated with inductively coupled plasma (ICP) etching using self-assembled Ni nanodots as the etching mask and focus ion beam (FIB) patterning method, respectively, will be comprehensively investigated by using various techniques of scanning confocal micro-Raman microscopy/spectroscopy, variable-temperature photoluminescence, time-resolved photoluminescence, and scanning cathodoluminescence. Theoretically-predicted optical properties such as Raman light scattering from the localized surface optical phonon mode and unpredicted new optical properties such as redistribution and surface recombination of localized carriers in InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars with different feature sizes will be studied. 由于它们的短波长本质，InGaN/GaN多量子阱激光二极管和发光管在新兴的固态照明等领域具有重大的应用。其中InGaN/GaN多量子阱结构是这些发光二极管的核心光发射层。在本研究项目中，我们提出对于用“自上而下”方法制备的InGaN/GaN多量子阱纳米柱线的新颖光学性质进行深入和系统的研究。我们计划对采用自组装的Ni金属纳米颗粒作为掩膜版加感应耦合的等离子体刻蚀技术以及用直接的聚焦离子束直写两种不同方法制备的InGaN/GaN多量子阱纳米柱线进行深入的多种先进光谱手段研究。这些研究手段包括常温的扫描共焦拉曼显微镜及光谱、变温的光致发光、时间分辨的光致发光以及扫描的阴极荧光等。一些理论预计的新型局域化表面声子振动模和一些非理论预计的新颖光学性质如局域化载流子的重新分布和新引入的载流子表面辐射复合通道将被仔细验证和研究。

705812.label: Realisation of objectives
705812.value: All the research objectives have been realized, e.g., the solid experimental verification of novel surface optical phonon modes predicted by previous theoretical investigation in the InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars which were prepared with two different "top-down" approaches; invention of one unique treatment method, namely first thermal annealing at 1000˚C and then boiling in aqua regia, which was proven to efficiently suppress the surface recombination of carriers on the nanopillar sidewall surfaces; the demonstration of the great improvement in internal luminescence quantum efficiency in the InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars; and the new idea and concept of "negative thermal activation energy" that were suggested on the base of the observed distinct temperature dependence of photoluminescence in the InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars.

705812.label: Major findings and research outcome
705812.value: 1. Rigorous demonstration of the new surface optical phonon modes in the InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars prepared with two “top-down” approaches of self-assembled Ni nanoislands mask + dry etching and direct focused ion beam milling. 2. Feature size dependence of frequencies of the surface optical phonon mode is proven to be well consistent with the theoretical prediction. 3. An efficient treatment approach combining thermal annealing with chemical solution treatment was invented and shown to have a strong suppressing effect on the surface defect states in the prepared nanopillars. 4. Deeper carrier localization was uncovered in the InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars. 5. Significant improvement in internal luminescence quantum efficiency was found in the InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars. 6. A new physical concept, namely "negative thermal activation energy", was proposed to be the most peculiar characteristic for the S-shaped temperature dependence of the luminescence peak in the InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars.

705812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705812.value: Compared with the conventional 2D MQW planar structure, the prepared InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars show greatly enhanced luminescence efficiency and new surface lattice vibrations. Based on these main findings obtained in the completed research, we suggest to do further investigations on the InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars along the following lines: (a) Fabricate InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars-based light emitting diodes, and investigate their electroluminescence; (b) Study recombination dynamics (i.e., transient or time-resolved processes) of carriers in the InGaN/GaN MQW nanopillars.

705812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705812.value: By making nanopilllars and doing in-depth study, we have demonstrated that these nanostructures possess novel optical properties such as new light inelastic scattering and light emission mechanisms which are very different from those in the planar structures. The major findings are of both scientific and technical significance. This research is obviously valuable and very helpful for HK to keep the advanced standing in the field of functional nanostructures and light emitting devices.

706012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706012.value: Stimuli-responsive materials represent an interesting and important class of materials that can undergo transformations in their structure, conformation or phase in response to external stimuli such as light, temperature, media, and others. As responses to stimuli are mainly manifested as transformations in structure, conformation or phase, these will also lead to changes in shape, surface properties, solubility, molecular assembly and hierarchical architecture. While there has been immense interest in the development of stimuli-responsive polymers and organic molecules, corresponding works on stimuli-responsive metal-ligand coordination compounds and their polymers are relatively less extensively studied. Given the versatility and diversity of the metal-ligand coordination mode, geometry and structure, an exploration into the design of stimuli-responsive metal-ligand coordination assemblies would represent challenging areas of research. As changes in the structure, conformation, phase, shape, surface properties, solubility, molecular assembly and hierarchical architecture can be associated with the stimuli-responsive behaviour, introduction of dynamic covalent or non-covalent interactions will be made to generate new classes of stimuli-responsive supramolecular systems, polymers and organogels. Although there has been a growing interest in stimuli-responsive polymers based on metal-ligand coordination interactions, studies of metallosupramolecular systems involving non-covalent metal-metal interactions are scarce. It is believed that by incorporating various metal-ligand coordination motifs, conformational changes would be brought about to control the hierarchical architecture, which could lead not only to changes in the optical behaviour but also the controlled hierarchical assembly that leads to interesting properties such as organogelation and changes in the morphology. In this project, the introduction of metal-ligand moieties into the various stimuli-responsive systems will be explored. Novel classes of stimuli-responsive metal-ligand coordination assemblies will be designed and synthesized. Their stimuli-responsive behaviour and hierarchical assembly will be explored by various spectroscopic methods, and their associated morphological changes will be studied. Attempts will be made to understand and to correlate the spectroscopic, electronic absorption and luminescence properties as well as the factors that lead to the control of the stimuli-responsive properties and the hierarchical architecture of the organized structures. The proposed project should offer not only new opportunities and additional strategies towards the control of the hierarchical assembly of stimuli-responsive systems through the introduction of metal-ligand coordination, but also should give insight into the factors that lead to the control of the stimuli-responsive properties, hierarchical assembly and structure-property relationships and would contribute towards the future design and development of new classes of stimuli-responsive metal-ligand coordination assemblies with tunable properties and morphologies. 刺激-響應性材料是一類引人注目的重要材料。在光、溫度、媒體和其他外界的刺激下，它們可以發生分子的結構、構象或者相態的轉變。這種由外界刺激引起的結構、構象或者相態的轉變，可以進一步導至材料的形狀、表面性質、溶解性、分子組裝及層次結構的變化。雖然科學家已對發展具有刺激-響應性的聚合物及有機分子有極大的興趣，但是在刺激-響應的金屬配合物及相關的聚合物方面開展的研究工作還是比較少見的。由於金屬跟配體有豐富多樣的配位方式、幾何形狀及結構，在探索設計刺激-響應金屬-配體配位組裝方面的工作將是個充滿挑戰性的課題。把動態共價或非共價相互作用引入到由刺激-響應性引起的結構、構象、相態、形狀、表面性質、溶解性、分子組裝及層次結構變化的體系中，將可產生新類的刺激-響應超分子體系、聚合材料及有機凝膠。儘管基於金屬-配體配位作用的刺激-響應聚合物的研究漸漸引起了科學家的興趣，探索非共價金屬-金屬相互作用的金屬超分子體系卻甚少。我們相信，以組合多樣的金屬和配體的基元，利用其構象的轉變來調控層次結構，不僅可以改變它們的光學性質，與此同時可以調控層次組裝，進一步形成有機凝膠或者導致形貌改變等有趣的性質。在此項目中，我們將金屬配體基元引入各種刺激-響應的體系；設計和合成新型的刺激-響應金屬-配體配位組裝；採用各種光譜學方法研究它們的刺激-響應性質及層次組裝的性質，亦對其形貌變化加以研究；探索影響有序結構的刺激-響應特性及層次結構的各種因素包括與光譜、電子吸收和發光性質之間的關係。該項目不僅通過引入金屬-配體配位這一新穎的策略來調控刺激-響應體系的層次組裝，而且進一步理解調控影響刺激-響應性質、層次組裝及其結構性質之間關係的各種因素。這將有助於將來設計和發展在性質和形貌上可控的新型刺激-響應性金屬-配體的配位組裝。

706112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706112.value: Palladium-catalyzed oxidative cyclization reactions have emerged as a novel and powerful tool for the synthesis of complex molecules under mild reaction conditions. Owing to its versatility in constructing carbon–nitrogen bonds, cyclization utilizing oxidative palladium catalysis is among the most effective choices for the synthesis of nitrogen-containing polycyclic structures, which are integral core skeletons of a large number of biologically active alkaloids. In recent years, we have developed a series of palladium(II)-catalyzed oxidative tandem cyclization reactions for the synthesis of nitrogen-bridged polycyclic core structures. In addition, we have developed highly efficient asymmetric catalytic systems that allow these transformations to be fulfilled in high enantioselectivities. This research proposal aims at developing new types of palladium(II)-catalyzed oxidative tandem cyclization reactions in both racemic and enantioselective variants as novel synthetic tools to construct the core skeletons of biologically active alkaloids. Eventually, this program will provide efficient synthetic routes to some classes of bioactive alkaloids and therefore facilitate the understanding of both chemistry and biology of them. 钯催化氧化环化反应已成为在温和条件下合成复杂分子的一种新颖有效的方法。因其在构建碳-氮键反应中的灵活多样性，以钯为催化剂的氧化环化反应成为了合成多元含氮杂环的最有效方法之一。这些多元含氮杂环结构是许多具有生物活性的生物碱的骨架结构。 近年来，我们小组成功研发了一系列二价钯催化的氧化环化串联反应来构建含氮杂环结构。此外，我们还发展了高效的不对称催化体系实现了高对映选择性的转化。这项研究计划的目的是在之前的研究基础上继续发展新型的二价钯催化的非对映选择性和对映选择性氧化环化串联反应作为合成具有生物活性生物碱骨架结构的有效工具。本研究最终将为合成活性生物碱提供高效的方法，并有助于从化学和生物学的角度加深对它们的理解。

706112.label: Realisation of objectives
706112.value: Palladium(II)-Catalyzed Intramolecular 1,2-Carboamination of Alkene for the Synthesis of N-Containing Heterocycles Tandem cyclization via palladium(II)-catalyzed 1,2-carboamination of alkene has proved to be a practical and expedient method for the construction of various N-containing heterocycles. We have strategically combined an initial aminopalladation step with several ensuing transformations, such as π-allyl substitution, C–H functionalization and α-haloamide substitution, to develop a panel of palladium(II)-catalyzed tandem cyclization reactions, affording diverse heterocycles, including pyrrolizidines, dihydropyrroloindoles and isoxazolidines in moderate to good yields and moderate to excellent diastereoselectivities. Enantioselective Palladium(II)-Catalyzed Intramolecular 1,2-Carboamination of Alkene We have developed a catalyst system of Pd(TFA)2/(S,S)-diPh-pyrox to promote the highly efficient enantioselective oxidative cascade cyclization of alkene tethered aliphatic acrylamides under a mild aerobic condition. A series of pyrrolizidine derivatives were synthesized in good yields and excellent enantioselectivity. We have also conducted further experimental and theoretical mechanistic studies to get deep insight into this asymmetric transformation. For the corresponding intramolecular aminoarylation of alkenyl anilides, we have discovered a new catalyst system of Pd(OAc)2/β-isocupreidine to afford a variety of indoline derivatives in moderate to good yields with moderate enantioselectivity. Besides, we also observed promising enantioselectivity for the intramolecular aminoalkylation of alkenyl α-haloamide using a phosphoramidite ligand bearing a spirobiindane backbone. Apply These Tandem Cyclization Reactions to the Synthesis of Biologically Active Alkaloids We have first accomplished a racemic formal synthesis of mitomycin K, a G series member of natural products mitomycins famous for their potent DNA alkylation activity. Later investigation on the enantioselective cyclization has led to the successful preparation of a highly enantioenriched cyclization product amenable for further manipulations. Thus, additional synthetic efforts have culminated in accomplishing the first enantioselective formal synthesis of mitomycin K. To further showcase the potential of our tandem cyclization methodologies, we have also managed to prepare one protein kinase inhibitor and one agonist of the G protein-coupled receptor 5-HT2C, all of which bear dihydropyrroloindole cores.

706112.label: Major findings and research outcome
706112.value: Palladium(II)-Catalyzed Intramolecular 1,2-Carboamination of Alkene for the Synthesis of N-Containing Heterocycles Three novel types of intramolecular 1,2-aminoalkylation of alkene catalyzed by palladium(II) have been developed. The first one involves an intramolecular 1,2-aminoalkylation of N-4,6-dienyl β-keto amides, providing an efficient method for the rapid assembly of pyrrolizidines starting from linear substrates in moderate to good yields and high to excellent diastereoselectivities (D. Xing, et al. Org. Lett. 2013, 15, 4370–4373). The second one concerns an intramolecular 1,2-aminoalkylation of α-iodo, α-bromo and α-chloro-amide substrates tethered with versatile functionalities, affording a diverse range of dihydropyrroloindole, pyrrolizidine and isoxazolidine heterocycles in moderate to excellent yields and moderate diastereoselectivity. (L. Ye, et al. manuscript in preparation). The third one is about 1,2-aminoalkylation of alkenyl amides via tandem aminopalladation/C(sp3)–H activation (functionalization) for divergent synthesis of a series of three-membered or five-membered ring-fused indolines in good yields. The choice of bases and solvents played important roles for the selectivity between the two transformations. This is the first example of Pd-catalyzed C(sp3)–H activation without employment of prefunctionalized reagents (e.g. halogenated and boron reagents) and directing groups, representing a green and economic protocol for the construction of N-containing heterocycles. (W. Du, et al. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2015, 137, 1130–1135) Enantioselective Palladium(II)-Catalyzed Intramolecular 1,2-Carboamination of Alkene We have developed a catalyst system of Pd(TFA)2/diPh-pyrox to promote the highly efficient enantioselective oxidative cascade cyclization of the challenging alkene tethered aliphatic acrylamides under a mild aerobic condition. A series of pyrrolizidine derivatives were synthesized in good yields and excellent enantioselectivity (68–99% yield, 82–94% ee). The experimental deuterium-labeling study indicated a highly anti-aminopalladation selectivity. We have also conducted a theoretical study to clearly account for both the enantioselectivity and the aminopalladation selectivity. An interesting steric-steering effect of the pyridine methyl group in the ligand has been identified along the anti-aminopalladation pathway, but not the corresponding syn-aminopalladation one. Besides, we have also found that some factors, including the steric bulkiness of the bidentate ligands, the anionic counterions/ligands of Pd(II) complexes, the electronic density of the isolated double bond and the acid/base additives affected the aminopalladation stereochemical selectivity or enantioselectivity, or both, using the straightforward deuterium-labeling experiment to provide primary guidance for future development of related enantioselective processes. (W. Du, manuscript submitted) Apply These Tandem Cyclization Reactions to the Synthesis of Biologically Active Alkaloids By taking advantage of our well established Pd(II)-catalyzed enantioselective tandem cyclization of alkenyl acrylamides, we initially achieved a racemic formal synthesis of mitomycin K in 23 steps and 3% overall yield. The subsequent systematic investigation on the substitution-dependent cyclization enantioselectivity revealed dramatic influence of substituents vicinal to the reacting allyl and acrylamide moieties. With the optimized substrate, the corresponding cyclized product was obtained in 78% yield with 83% ee. Further transformation to an advanced synthetic intermediate towards mitomycin K in its enantioenriched form was subsequently realized in 16 steps, which, to the best of our knowledge, represents the first enantioselective formal synthesis of mitomycin K. (Q. Gu, manuscript in preparation) We have also prepared several bioactive molecules by applying our tandem intramolecular aminoalkylation of alkenyl α-haloamides. Straightforward amide reduction and dehydrogenation of indoline to indole readily delivered the dihydropyrroloindole core structures. Subsequent diverse functionalization of these cores afforded a variety of pharmaceuticals-related compounds, such as a protein kinase inhibitor and a G protein-coupled receptor 5-HT2C agonist. (L. Ye, manuscript in preparation)

706112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706112.value: The tandem aminoalkylation reaction via aminopalladation and C(sp3)–H functionalization required activated C(sp3)–H bonds. In order for even broader substrate scope and synthetic application thereafter, we will further investigate the reaction conditions to encompass unactivated C(sp3)–H bonds. Given the promising enantioselectivity obtained in the intramolecular aminoalkylation of alkenyl α-haloamide using a phosphoramidite ligand bearing a spirobiindane backbone, we will screen related ligands of such a skeleton and optimize corresponding reaction conditions in order for a high level of enantiocontrol. As for the moderate enantioselectivity for the intramolecular aminoarylation catalyzed by palladium(II) and β-isocupreidine, we will explore other chiral tertiary amine ligands of different skeletons as well as other types of ligands in future. In regard to the successful enantioselective formal synthesis of mitomycin K, we will employ this cyclization methodology to generate enantioenriched analogues of mitomycins for potential biological and pharmaceutical evaluations.

706112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706112.value: We have established an array of tandem cyclization reactions under palladium catalysis involving simultaneous formation of multiple C–N and C–C bonds, thus providing practical and expedient access to all sorts of nitrogen-containing polycyclic compounds. In addition to the inherent step-economy, all these strategies yield environmental-benign water or other simple inorganic compounds as side products, embodying the concept of atom-economy for modern ideal organic synthesis. We have also integrated chiral ligands into these reaction conditions to further develop corresponding enantioselective transformations, in response to current great demand of enantioenriched small heterocycles for biological and pharmaceutical applications. We have conducted additional experimental and theoretical studies on such an asymmetric process to obtain mechanistic insight instrumental for future development of relevant transformations. In order to exemplify the synthetic potential of our methodologies, we have achieved synthesis of a bioactive natural product mitomycin K and other pharmaceuticals-relevant small molecules. In view of the practical and robust nature of our cyclization methodologies and well-demonstrated synthetic applications, their wide utilization in accessing a broad range of biologically and medicinally important nitrogen-containing natural products as well as unnatural small molecules is well foreseeable in the near future.

706412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706412.value: The mechanical exfoliation technique has not only lead to the Nobel Prize winner material graphene, but also realized for the first time a number of other monolayer 2D crystals, opening up a new paradigm for device applications. Many of the 2D crystals realized so far are of a hexagonal structure where the conduction (valence) band has minimums (maximums) at the high symmetry K points, i.e. the corners of the first Brillouin zone, usually referred as valleys. The two inequivalent valleys constitute another binary degree of freedom for Bloch electron in addition to spin. Their large separation in momentum space makes inter-valley scattering inefficient and hence the valley life time is expected to be long which makes valley index an ideal information carrier for ‘valleytronics’ applications, just like spin in spintronics applications. The primary objective of this proposal is to explore the topological physical properties associated with the valley index of Bloch electrons in several monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides and several graphene-like 2D crystals formed by group IVA elements where inversion symmetry is broken. We plan to explore valley dependent topological physics properties in the bulk bands as well as the edge-state physics. We will explore the possibilities for manipulating the valley dynamics by electrical, magnetic, and optical means, which may form the basis for potential valley based device applications in these monolayer materials. In the meantime, these systems with complex band structures and strong spin-orbit coupling provide ideal platforms to explore the Berry-phase related topological physics associated with the non-central valleys in the Bloch bands which is of fundamental interest. The possible interplay between valley and spin degrees of freedom by the strong spin-orbit coupling may lead to rich application possibilities as well as interesting new physics. 力學剝落技術不僅帶來了贏得諾貝爾物理學獎的石墨烯的發現，而且使得制備一系列單層的二維晶格首次成為可能。這將開辟器件應用的一個新紀元。大部分已實現的二維晶格都具有六角形的晶格結構。在動量空間中，這類晶格的導帶的最低點以及價帶的最高點通常是出現在具有高對稱性的K點，也就是第一布裏淵區的角上。這些能帶的極大或者極小點通常被稱作能谷。在這樣的系統中，除了自旋自由度， 兩個不等價的能谷也構成了布洛赫電子的另一個二重自由度。由於兩個能谷在動量空間相隔很遠，能谷間的散射很難發生，所以能谷極化的壽命預計會比較長。這就使得能谷自由度可以作為一個很理想的信息載體應用於能谷電子學，類似於自旋自由度在自旋電子學中所扮演的角色。這個研究計劃的一個主要目標就是在一些具有空間反演對稱破缺的單層過渡金屬二硫化物以及類石墨烯的二維材料中探索與電子的能谷自由度相關的一些拓撲物理現象。我們計劃研究體材料中的能谷拓撲物理現象以及邊緣態的物理。我們還將探索通過電，磁，光等手段來操控能谷動力學的可能性。這將為潛在的基於能谷自由度的器件應用構成基礎。同時，這些具有復雜能帶結構以及強自旋軌道耦合的二維系統也為研究起源於貝裏絕熱相位的跟能谷自由度有關的拓撲物理現象提供了理想的平臺。這些現象的研究對於物理學也具有根本意義。同時，強自旋軌道耦合所可能導致的能谷與自旋自由度的互動也可能帶來更為豐富的應用可能性以及新的物理。

706412.label: Realisation of objectives
706412.value: Objective 1: This objective has been fully achieved. We have developed three-band tight binding model for group-VIB transition metal dichalcogenides (MoS2, WS2, MoSe2, WSe2, etc.), and extracted the model parameters through fitting first principle band structures. The tight binding model works well in quantitative description of the Berry curvatures, orbital magnetic moments, and inter band optical transition matrix elements at the conduction and valence band edges located at the K and -K points. Objective 2: This objective has been fully achieved. We have discovered valley contrasted orbital magnetic moment and Berry curvatures of the band edge electrons and holes at the K valleys. The latter gives rise to valley Hall effect. We have also discovered the valley dependent optical circular dichroism for the interband transition at the K valleys. Evidences of these valley contrasted phenomena have been observed in experiments by our collaborators as well as other experimental groups. We have also investigate excitons formed by the band edge electron and hole at the K and -K valleys, and charging and discharging effects of excitons under the backgate controlled electrostatic doping of the monolayer. Objective 3: This objective has been fully achieved. We have discovered a strong spin-valley coupling arising from the spin-orbit coupling of the transition metal d-orbitals. In the valence band edge, the exceptionally strong spin-valley coupling results in the effective spin-valley locking, so that the valley dependent controls through the valley Hall effect and the valley optical selection rule realise at the same time the spin controls. These properties allow both spin and valley to be manipulated by the external controls such as electric, magnetic and optical fields, so that both spin and valley can be utilised as potential carriers of information in future electronics.

706412.label: Major findings and research outcome
706412.value: 1. We developed a two-band k.p model and three-band tight binding model for describing the conduction and valance band edges in K valleys in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides. Thee models describe well the Berry curvatures, the orbital magnetic moment, and the optical interband transition matrix elements at the band edges in the K and -K valleys. See publication 3 and 5. 2. We discovered that inversion symmetry breaking together with spin-orbit coupling leads to coupled spin and valley physics in monolayers transition metal dichalcogenides, making possible controls of spin and valley in these 2D materials. Valley Hall and spin Hall effects coexist in both electron-doped and hole-doped systems. Optical interband transitions have frequency-dependent polarization selection rules which allow selective photoexcitation of carriers with various combination of valley and spin indices. The physics we discovered provides a route towards the integration of valleytronics and spintronics in multivalley materials with strong spin-orbit coupling and inversion symmetry breaking. See publication 3, 6. 3. Working together with two experimental groups, we demonstrated the optical generation of valley polarization and valley coherence in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides, based on the valley dependent optical transition selection rules we predicted. We have also identified evidences of symmetry variations between odd-number and even-number thick 2D transition metal dichalcogenides from the second harmonic generation measurement, and the evidence of strong spin-valley coupling from the photoluminescence measurement. See publication 1, 2, 4. 4. We discovered that transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers offer an unprecedented platform to realize a strong coupling between the spin, valley and layer pseudospin of holes. Such coupling gives rise to the spin Hall effect and spin-dependent selection rule for optical transitions in inversion symmetric bilayer and leads to a variety of magnetoelectric effects permitting quantum manipulation of these quantum degrees of freedom. See publication 7. 5. Working together with our experimental collaborator, we have investigated excitons and trions (charged excitons) in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides. In high-quality monolayer MoSe2 and WSe2, unambiguous observation and electrostatic tunability of charging effects in positively charged, neutral and negatively charged excitons are observed from photoluminescence spectroscopy. See publication 10. 6. Working together with two experimental groups, we have also demonstrated the electric tunability of the valley physical properties (i.e. orbital magnetic moment, optical circular dichroism, Hall effect) in bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides and bilayer graphene respectively. See publication 8 and 9.

706412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706412.value: This GRF project has addressed a number of Berry phase related properties associated with the valley degree of freedom of carriers in 2D crystals including monolayer and bilayer transition metal dicahlcogenides, and bilayer graphene. The findings can be readily generalised to other 2D crystals with the hexagonal lattices and with broken inversion symmetry. Future development of the research including: (i) working with experimental groups to further explore the predicted valley phenomena; (ii) exploring device applications of the discovered valley physics; (iii) exploring valley physics in other non-hexaognal 2D crystals and also in 3D.

706412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706412.value: The study of atomically thin 2D materials has grown into a vast research field, with potential in revolutionising material science and device technology. Many of the 2D crystals realized so far are of a hexagonal structure where the conduction (valence) band has minimums (maximums) at the high symmetry K points, i.e. the corners of the first Brillouin zone, usually referred as valleys. The two inequivalent valleys constitute another binary degree of freedom for Bloch electron in addition to spin, which may be utilised as an ideal information carrier for future electronics. This research project has discovered various physical properties associated with the valley index of electrons in hexagonal 2D crystals, demonstrated using the exemplary systems of transition metal dichalcogenides, a newly emerged class of 2D semiconductors of vast interest for electronics and optoelectronics. The valley properties we discovered, including the valley Hall effect, valley magnetic moment, and valley optical selection rules, enable manipulating the valley degree of freedom by electrical, magnetic, and optical means, which form the basis for potential valley based device applications in these monolayer materials.

706912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706912.value: The North China Craton is one of the oldest continental blocks in the world, containing some rocks as old as 3.85 billion years (Ga), and its formation and evolution can provide important insights into an understanding of crustal accretion and amalgamation during early Earth. In the past decade, major advancements have been made in understanding the formation and evolution of the North China Craton (NCC) following recognition of three orogenic belts, named the Trans-North China Orogen, Khondalite Belt, Jiao-Liao-Ji Belt, of which the NS-trending Trans-North China Orogen divides the NCC into the Western and Eastern Blocks, whereas the Khondalite Belt separates the Western Block into the Yinshan Block in the north and the Ordos Block in the south, and the Jiao-Liao-Ji Belt divides the Eastern Block into the Longgang and Langrim Blocks. Now there is a broad consensus that the NCC formed by accretion and amalgamation of these microcontinental blocks along these orogenic belts. In the last few years, researchers have carried out extensive structural, metamorphic, geochemical and geochronological investigations on the Trans-North China Orogen, and produced large amounts of new data. There is now a coherent outline of the timing and tectonic processes involved in the collision between the Eastern and Western Blocks and also much increased knowledge of the pre-collisional history of the crust that subsequently became included in the Trans-North China Orogen. Comparatively, however, less work has been done on the Khondalite Belt within the Western Block and the Jiao-Liao-Ji Belt within the Eastern Block. This has hampered understanding the formation and assembly of the North China Craton. This project aims to carry out an integrated study, including structural, metamorphic, geochemical, geochronological and geophysical (seismic imaging) investigations on the Khondalite Belt in the Western Block. The results of this project will not only determine the timing and tectonic processes of the geological events that resulted in the formation of the Khondalite Belt in the North China Craton, but will also lead to improvements in understanding tectonic processes associated with continental assembly to form a large landmass during Paleoproterozoic time; for instance, whether this belt resulted from the assembly of the Paleo-Mesoproterozoic Supercontinent Columbia. 华北克拉通是世界上最老的克拉通陆块之一，含有38亿年岩石记录。因此，它的形成和演化对于认识早期地壳增生和拼合具有重要意义。过去十年，华北克拉通基底研究取得巨大进展，识别出三条早元古宙碰撞造山带，即华北中部带，孔茲岩带和胶-辽-吉带。其中，华北中部带将华北克拉通分隔成东部陆块和西部陆块，孔茲岩带将西部陆块分隔为北部的阴山陆块和南部的鄂尔多斯陆块，胶-辽-吉带将东部陆块分隔为龙岗陆块和狼林陆块。目前普遍认为华北克拉通是由这些微陆块沿这三条碰撞造山带拼合而成。过去几年中，研究者们对华北中部带开展了大量研究，取得许多新的资料。现在对于华北克拉通东部陆块和西部陆块岩华北中部带拼合时间和过程已经有了很好的认识，对于拼合前的历史也有了解，但对于孔茲岩带和胶-辽-吉带的研究却不多，这大大地限制了对华北克拉通增生和拼合历史的进一步了解。本项目将对华北克拉通西部陆块孔茲岩带开展构造地质、变质作用、地球化学和同位素年代学研究。其研究结果不仅有助于确定孔茲岩带形成的构造过程和时间，也有助于了解全球早元古宙超大陆的拼合历史以及确定华北克拉通是否为哥伦比亚超大陆一部分。

706912.label: Realisation of objectives
706912.value: We have successfully completed all five objectives designed for this project as follows: Objective 1 is determine the nature, spatial distribution and contact relationships of the major lithotectonic units in the Khondalite Belt, especially of high-pressure (HP) and ultrahightemperature (UHT) pelitic granulites in the belt. This objective was completed by three times of fieldwork: May 29-June 15, June 24-July 20 and September 23-October 10, 2013. In the field, the Principal Investigator (Guochun Zhao), two CIs (Yusheng Wan and Ling Chen) and their postgraduates mapped out the spatial distribution of the major lithologies in the Jining, Daqingshan, Wulashan, Qianlishan and Helanshan complexes. Such large scale mappling led to important discovery of high-pressure (HP) pelitic granulites in the Qianlishan and Heliangshan areas. In addition, we have further determined the spatial distribution of ultra-high temperature (UHT) pelitic granulites in the Jining and Daqingshn areas. During the fieldwork, we collected ~600 samples for further petrographic, structural, metamorphic and geochronological studies. Objective 2 is to carry out extensive field-based structural investigations on the Khondalite Belt and determine the nature of the major structural episodes through detailed structural analysis, especially on the early deformation episodes (D1 and D2) which are critical to determining the polarity of the subduciton before the final collision. This objective was completed by detailed structural investigations on the Khondalite Belt, in which we identified three episodes of deformation (D1 to D3) of which D1 is represented by small isoclinal and recumbent folds, D2 produced large-scale asymmetric folds and an associated penetrative axial planar foliation, a mineral stretching lineation and regional-scale ductile shear zones, and D3 is indicated by open to tight folds of varying scales, axial crenulation cleavages and EW-striking thrust faults, involving broadly N-S compression. A paper entitled “Polyphase deformation of the Khondalite Belt: Implications for the polarity of Paleoproterozoic subduction and collision in the Western Block of the North China Craton”. Objective 3 is to undertake an extensive study of metamorphic mineral assemblages, reaction relations, mineral compositions and thermobarometric P-T calculations of HP and UHT pelitic granulites, especially in the Helanshan, Qianlishan, Wulashan and Daqingshan Complexes, in order to reconstruct their metamorphic P-T paths so that they can be related to the structural studies outlined above. This objective has been completed by our detailed metamorphic studies on high-pressure pelitic granulites collected from the Qianlishan and Helanshan regions. Our petrographic examination has revealed four metamorphic stages in the high-pressure pelitic granulites: the early prograde (M1), peak high-pressure (M2), post-peak decompression (M3) and late retrograde (M4) stages, of which M1 is preserved as mineral inclusions within the cores of garnet,represented by plagioclase + biotite + quartz + muscovite + kyanite + ilmenite; the M2 assemblage is garnet + kyanite + biotite + K-feldspar + plagioclase + quartz + ilmenite in the matrix; M3 is represented by sillimanite replacing kyanite and formation of cordierite + sillimanite symplectites (M3-1) and cordierite ± spinel coronas replacing garnet porphyroblasts (M3-2); and M4 is indicated by the formation of staurolite + chlorite in the matrix. We have also applied the Pseudosection modelling for a representative sample in the NCKFMASHTO system to constrains the P-T conditions of M1, M2, M3-1, M3-2 and M4 stages at 9.3-9.7 kbar/656-674°C, 10.2-11.2 kbar/792-805°C, 5.5-5.7 kbar/810-820°C, 4.5-5.0 kbar/780-785°C and 3.4-4.4 kbar/580-610°C, respectively. These mineral assemblages and their P-T conditions define a clockwise P-T path involving isothermal decompression and isobaric cooling following the peak high-pressure metamorphism, suggesting that the high-pressure pelitic granulites underwent initial crustal thickening (M1-M2), followed by isothermal exhumation (M3) and final retrogression and cooling (M4). Such a clockwise P-T path involving near-isothermal decompression is in accord with the P-T paths reconstructed for other complexes in the Khondalite Belt, and, combined with available geochronological data, is considered to record a continent-continent collisional event, which led to the amalgamation of the Yinshan and Ordos Blocks to form the Western Block of the North China Craton. The result of research for this objective have produced a paper entitled “Metamorphism and partial melting of high-pressure pelitic granulites from the Qianlishan Complex: Constraints on the tectonic evolution of the Khondalite Belt in the North China Craton” that has been published in Precambrian Research (2014, v. 242 p. 172– 186). Objective 4 is to utilize SHRIMP and LA-ICP-MS U–Pb zircon geochronology, combined with cathodoluminescence (CL) imaging, to determine the provenance, depositional ages and metamorphic history of the Khondalite series rocks. We have successfully completed this objective by detailed zircon CL imaging and SIMS zirconU-Pb dating on samples collected from the Qianlishan and Helanshan complexes. Our dating results demonstrate that the peak metamorphism of high- to medium-pressure granulite facies metamorphism occurred at ~1.95 Ga, whereas the ultra-high temperature (UHT) metamorphism took place around 30 Ma later following the high-pressure metamorphism. Based on these results and our previous dating results for metamorphic zircons from khondalites, we conclude that the collision between the Yinshan and Ordos blocks occurred at ~1.95 Ga, which was followed by post-collisional extension in association with emplacement of mantle-derived magmas, causing UHT metamorphism at ~192 Ga. The result of research on this objective was partly reflected by a paper entitled “Application of the revised Ti-in-zircon thermometer and SIMS zircon U-Pb dating of high-pressure pelitic granulites from the Qianlishan-Helanshan Complex of the Khondalite Belt, North China Craton”, which has also been published in Precambrian Research (2016, v. 276 p. 1– 13). Objective 5 is to establish a detailed tectono-chronological framework for the Khondalite Belt, based on new data produced from this project. This objective has been 100% completed, which is reflected in Chapter 3 (Archean Geology of The Western Block) and Chapter 4 (Paleoproterozoic Amalgamation of the North China Craton) of PI’s new book entitled “Precambrian Evolution of the North China Craton”.
