706912.label: Major findings and research outcome
706912.value: Major advancements in understanding the early Precambrian history of the North China Craton (NCC) have been made in the past decade following recognition of two Himalayan-type continent-continent collisional belts, named the Trans-North China Orogen and the Khondalite Belt and Jiao-Liao-Jiao Belt. In the last decade, geologists have carried out extensive investigations on the Trans-North China Orogen and produced large amounts of new data and interpretations. There is now a general consensus about the timing of tectonic processes involved in the Paleoproterozoic subduction and collision between the Eastern and Western Blocks. Comparatively, however, not so much work has been done on the Khondalite Belt within the Western Block, which has hindered the further understanding of the formation and assembly of the North China Craton. This forms the justification for this project (HKU7069/12P) in which we have carried out more extensive field-based structural, metamorphic, and geochronological investigations on the Khondalite Belt, which led to the following major findings and research outcomes: (1) Our field geological mapping and subsequent metamorphic studies have led to discovery of high-pressure (HP) pelitic granulites in the Qianlishan and Heliangshan areas. High-pressure pelitic granulites, characterized by a key peak assemblage of kyanite-K-feldspar-garnet, have been considered as a hallmark of continental subduction and collision tectonics because only tectonic processes related to subduction and continent-continent collision can transport the sedimentary precursors of the pelitic granulites to a lower crustal depth where they experience high-pressure granulite facies metamorphism (see peer-reviewed journal publication No. 1 in Part C). (2) Our THERMOCALC pseudosection modeling studies led to recognition of clockwise P-T paths involving near-isothermal decompression for the high-pressure granulite-facies metamorphism of the Khondalite Belt, which reflect continental collisional environments, whereas the ultrahigh temperature (UHT) metamorphism of the Khondalite Belt is characterized by an anticlockwise P-T path, reflecting an origin related to the underplating of mantle magmas (see peer-reviewed journal publication No. 1 in Part C). (3) Our SIMS zircon U-Pb dating reveals that the peak metamorphism of high- to medium-pressure granulite facies metamorphism occurred at ~1.95 Ga, whereas the ultra-high temperature (UHT) metamorphism took place around 30 Ma later following the high-pressure metamorphism (see peer-reviewed journal publication No. 2 in Part C). (4) On the basis of the above major findings and research outcomes, we have established a detailed tectono-chronological framework for the Khondalite Belt, which provides important insights into understanding of geological evolution of the North China Craton (see peer-reviewed journal publication No. 3 and book No. 4 in Part C).

706912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706912.value: The discovery of high-pressure pelitic granulites in the Helanshan and Qianlishan complexes further confirms that the Khondalite Belt in the Western Block of the North China Craton represented a Himalaya-type continent-continent collisional belt. Therefore, the formation of the North China Craton was involved in two two discrete Paleoproterozoic continent-continent collisional events, of which the earlier one formed the EW-trending Khondalite Belt along which the Yinshan and Ordos Blocks amalgamated to form the Western Block at ~1.95 Ga, whereas the second collisional event led to the formation of the NS-trending Trans-North China Orogen along which the united Western Block collided with the Eastern Block to form the North China Craton at ~1.85 Ga. One of the further tests on this model is to determine whether or not those high-grade terrains located at the conjunction of the Khondalite Belt and Trans-North China Orogen underwent two collisional events, which may invite another RGC GRF project for further study in future.

706912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706912.value: The Earth’s surface consists of a number of rigid plates that either drift apart to create new oceanic crust, or collide to generate mountain belts. Determinations of timing and processes of mountain-building events are critical to understanding the assembly and breakup of continents in Earth’S history. This is the case with Paleoproterozoic collisional belt within the Western Block, named the “Khondalite Belt”. In this Hong Kong RGC GRF project (HKU7069/12P), we carried out extensive field-based structural, metamorphic and geochronological investigations on the Khondalite Belt. The research outcomes of this project led to discovery of high-pressure pelitic granulites in the Khondalite Belt, which are generally considered as a hallmark of continental subduction and collision tectonics, and thus further confirm that the Khondalite Belt in the Western Block of the North China Craton represented a Himalaya-type continent-continent collisional belt. This is further supported by the results of our metamorphic studies, which reveal clockwise P-T paths involving near-isothermal decompression for the high-pressure pelitic granulites from the Khondalite Belt. Finally, Our SIMS zircon U-Pb dating indicate that the Western Block formed by collision between the Yinshan and Ordos blocks along the Khondalite Belt occurred at ~1.95 Ga.

706912.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
706912.value: The research outcomes of this Hong Kong RGC GRF project and PI's other RGC GRF projects have led to discoveries of two 1.95-1.85 billion years (Ga) old Himalaya-type collisional belts in North China, namely the 1.95 Ga “Khondalite Belt” and the 1.85 Ga “Trans-North China Orogen”. These discoveries demonstrate that modern-style plate tectonics had already been operative in North China before 1.95-1.85 Ga. These Hong Kong RGC GRF projects undertaken by PI's research group have produced more than 200 papers in leading earth science journals, which have been cited by others for more than 17,000 times. In 2014, PI was recognized as the World’s Most Influential Scientific Minds 2014 by Thomson Reuters. As the first awardee, PI was awarded “2014 State Natural Science Award (Second Prize)” for a project entitled "Paleoproterozoic amalgamation of the North China Craton and the assembly of the Columbia supercontinent". Also in 2014, PI was elected to be the Fellow of Geological Society of American (GSA) and the President of the International Association for Gondwana Research (IAGR). In 2015, PI was selected as one of the “Highly Cited Researchers 2015” by Thomson Reuters, and in 2016, PI was selected as one of the laureates for the 29th Khwarizmi International Award (KIA).

707012.label: Project Objectives
707012.value: The ore-forming mechanism of giant Fe-Ti-V deposits is uncertain. How such large amounts of Fe-Ti oxides were able to accumulate in the layered intrusions in the Panxi region is enigmatic. Our previous work suggests that the oxide ores may have formed either from separation of oxide melts or by settling and sorting of early cumulus titanomagnetite. Although most recent findings support the origin of oxide melts, we will use melt inclusion and isotopic data to further evaluate this possible origin. Unlike the relatively well-known Panzhihua deposit, the Hongge Fe-Ti-V oxide deposit is poorly studied. Ore bodies are hosted in clinopyroxenite and are mainly composed of net-textured ores. We have identified Cr-rich titanomagnetite as inclusions in olivine and clinopyroxene and Cr-poor titanomagnetite as an interstitial phase. We will use textural and compositional data to further document precisely the order of mineral crystallization. Both Fe-V isotope compositions will be obtained to document changes of oxygen fugacity during the magma evolution and formation of oxide ores. A major goal of this work is to utilize our findings to develop a geological model for the occurrence of giant Fe-Ti-V oxide ore deposits in gabbroic intrusions and to use this model to more efficiently explore for new deposits of this type.

707012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
707012.value: Permian layered mafic intrusions in the Panxi region, SW China, are part of the Emeishan Large Igneous Province (ELIP) and host giant magmatic Fe-Ti-V oxide deposits. Our previous work suggests that these intrusions formed from extremely Fe-rich gabbroic magmas and that the giant ore accumulation was due to either suppression of early magnetite crystallization or solidification of immiscible oxide melts in silicate magmas. Our most recent studies have identified several lines of evidence for the genesis from Fe-Ti-(P) rich melts. We propose that these Fe-Ti-(P) rich melts were immiscible in silicate magmas and that immiscibility occurred because of oversaturation of Fe and Ti during the crystallization of silicate minerals. We suggest that the dense, segregated Fe-Ti-(P)-rich melts behaved like heavy minerals and settled downward in a silicate crystal mush to form net-textured and massive oxide ores as part of the cumulate sequence. This project aims to test this model utilizing melt inclusions and unconventional Fe-V isotopes. We will carry out a detailed study of melt inclusions in apatite that occurs in both the oxide ores and in the silicate rocks. Fe-V isotopes, which are sensitive to the status of oxidation of magmas, will be analyzed for bulk rocks and silicate and Fe-oxide mineral separates. The objectives of this study are to use the melt inclusion and isotopic data to place constraints on the origin of the oxide deposits and temperatures and compositions of possibly immiscible Fe-Ti-rich oxide melts. We will evaluate the sequence of crystallization of minerals in the hosting intrusions. rows: The ore-forming mechanism of giant Fe-Ti-V deposits is uncertain. How such large amounts of Fe-Ti oxides were able to accumulate in the layered intrusions in the Panxi region is enigmatic. Our previous work suggests that the oxide ores may have formed either from separation of oxide melts or by settling and sorting of early cumulus titanomagnetite. Although most recent findings support the origin of oxide melts, we will use melt inclusion and isotopic data to further evaluate this possible origin.

Unlike the relatively well-known Panzhihua deposit, the Hongge Fe-Ti-V oxide deposit is poorly studied. Ore bodies are hosted in clinopyroxenite and are mainly composed of net-textured ores. We have identified Cr-rich titanomagnetite as inclusions in olivine and clinopyroxene and Cr-poor titanomagnetite as an interstitial phase. We will use textural and compositional data to further document precisely the order of mineral crystallization.
Both Fe-V isotope compositions will be obtained to document changes of oxygen fugacity during the magma evolution and formation of oxide ores.

A major goal of this work is to utilize our findings to develop a geological model for the occurrence of giant Fe-Ti-V oxide ore deposits in gabbroic intrusions and to use this model to more efficiently explore for new deposits of this type.

707012.label: Major findings and research outcome
707012.value: Objectives set in our original proposal are basically obtained and all the activities related to the project were smooth. As expected, there were no major problems during the project period. The project was in fact a continuation of several previous studies of our research group at HKU but tackled new problems with significant implications. Major findings. 1. There is a major breakthrough in the study of the oxide-bearing gabbroic layered intrusions in the Panxi area, SW China. Two immiscible processes are well documented in a major paper (Zhou et al. 2013): mafic magmas were separated into a more-Fe-Ti-rich magmas to form gabbroic intrusions and felsic magmas to form syentic intrusions. This model is now widely used. This is partly evidenced by the high citation (more than 100 times as of December 9, 2016) of Zhou et al. (2013). 2. The other major achievement is the Fe isotopic study of the Baima oxide-bearing intrusion. I ron isotopic compositions of olivine, clinopyroxene and titanomagnetite of the Baima Fe–Ti oxide-bearing layered mafic intrusion, SW China, are used to investigate Fe isotopic fractionation during the formation of the Fe–Ti-oxide orebodies and to constrain the origin of silicate minerals and Fe–Ti oxides. The results were published in a highly ranked journal, EPSL (Liu et al. 2014) 3. Oxide minerals enclosed in olivine and other silicates, are now well documented to represent melt inclusions. Based on the modeling and reconstruction of mineral compositions, we re-examined the melt compositions immiscible in silicate magmas and results were published in a highly ranked journal, Journal of Petrology (Liu et al., 2014). 4. Origin of those layered intrusions and associated oxide deposits are carefully examined in terms of the discovery of melt inclusions and microtextures. A model involving immiscibilities is well documented and has resulted in several important publications including Wang et al. (2013MD, 2014CG). 5. Through detailed investigation of magnetite compositions, by the PhD student, Liu, clearly established the compositional ranges of magmatic magnetite and we published the results in Liu et al. (2015OGR). 6. An invited review paper with oxide mineralogical data and bulk rock data was published in a text book called “Layered intrusions” by Pang et al. (2015). Pang was a former PhD student of the P.I and worked with the layered intrusions in the Panxi area of SW China. Overall, this project was successful with important findings published in highly ranked journals in the field of the study.

707012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
707012.value: Zhou and his research group have been working on the oxide-bearing mineral deposits associated with layered intrusions in SW China and have made some major achievements in the understanding of their origin. The remaining problems are identified for further studies and include better constraints on the origin of the compositions of melt inclusions in olivine. To do this, more experimental investigation is needed. To better understand the formation of the oxide deposits in the Panxi region will require the comparison of these with those elsewhere in the world. We anticipate to eventually establish a new style of magmatic oxide deposits. Overall, our previous work on these oxide deposits of this project has made a major impact internationally and the geological features are now well known in the world. At the moment, Zhou and his research group have collaborated with Chinese and oversea colleagues to continue our studies on these well know oxide deposits.

707412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
707412.value: Cyclic peptides have emerged as an important class of peptide-based therapeutics. Their resistance to proteolysis makes them invaluable entities in medicinal chemistry and biological studies. However, the chemical synthesis of cyclic peptides still represents a synthetic challenge. Many problematic issues are associated with existing methods. In this project, we aim to extend a novel chemical peptide ligation strategy that we recently discovered to the synthesis of cyclic peptides. Such a strategy would potentially become an important tool in the preparation of biologically relevant cyclic peptides. Daptomycin is chosen as our synthetic target to establish the optimal protocol to perform the chemical peptide ligation-induced peptide cyclization. Daptomycin is a 31-membered cyclic peptide and its total synthesis has not yet been reported. Emerging antibiotic-resistant bacteria pose an ever-more urgent threat. For example, the recently emerging genetic mutation NDM-1 is observed to bypass the last-resort antibiotic defense. Bacterial resistance to currently used antibiotics is generally just a matter of time; thus discovering new chemical agents with new killing modes is particularly important. Daptomycin is an emerging cyclic peptide-based antibiotic—approved by the FDA in 2003—which is lethal to otherwise antibiotic-resistant gram-positive pathogens. However, its mode of action has not been fully understood. The chemical synthesis will enable us to prepare daptomycin analogues for the establishment of structure-activity-relationships and the generation of new antibiotics with improved properties that will offer additional clinical usages. We recently disclosed a serine/threonine-based chemical peptide ligation. A peptide with a salicylaldehyde ester at the C-terminus can readily react intermolecularly with another peptide with serine or threonine at the N-terminus to afford an N,O-benzylidene acetal linked product. Then, the acidolysis easily removes the N,O-benzylidene acetal moiety to generate the natural Xaa-Ser/Thr linkage at the ligation site. We hypothesize that the C-terminal salicylaldehyde ester of one peptide will also be able to react with the N-terminal serine/threonine of the same peptide intramolecularly to afford the head-to-tail cyclized peptide. In this project, we aim to use this chemical peptide ligation strategy to develop a total synthesis of daptomycin and its analogues. We will also explore the scope and limitations of the serine/threonine based chemical peptide ligation in the synthesis of other bioactive cyclic peptides of various sizes, including astin, dichotomin, phakellistatin, lysobactin and kawagucipeptin. Ultimately, this project could provide a new avenue for research in the chemistry and biology of cyclic peptides. N/A

707412.label: Realisation of objectives
707412.value: All the proposed objectives have been successfully completed. In detail, we have developed the first total synthesis of daptomycin. The synthesis involved a hybrid strategy using both solid-phase and solution-phase synthesis. The key features of our synthesis included a practical synthesis of Fmoc-3mGlu(tBu)-OH and a solution to the problem of Kyn preparation, in which an N-Boc-protected Trp building block was ozonolyzed to provide Kyn in a quantitative yield. The synthesis of 3-methyl-glutamic acid (Fmoc-3mGlu(tBu)-OH) was synthesized in 17 steps. The key cyclization step was achieved by a serine ligation, which was previously developed by us for protein chemical synthesis. This result has been published in J. Am. Chem. Soc in 2013 and Chem. Rec. 2014. Furthermore, we continued to develop another 10- steps synthesis of 3-methyl-glutamic acid building block, which provided us a good access to synthesize daptomycin analogues. Thus, more than 20 daptomycin analogues have been synthesized and tested for anti-bacterial activities. From these structure-activity-relationship studies, we have identified the site tolerant of modification, from which we synthesized a daptomycin analogue with a photoaffinity group and an alkyne group with MIC only 2 times less than daptomycin. This daptomycin-based affinity probe will provide a useful tool for the molecular target identification of daptomycin. Our total synthesis of daptomycin took advantage of Ser/Thr ligation-mediated peptide cyclization. It was very successful, thus we continued to explore the scope and limitations of this strategy in the synthesis of the cyclic peptide in general. Synthesis of cyclic tetrapeptides with rigid 12-membered ring structures has been very challenging due to the constrained geometry of the peptide backbone. We used Ser/Thr ligation-mediated peptide cyclization to successfully synthesize nine cyclic tetrapeptides. From the molecular-modeling investigation, the estimated activation energies for the cyclic imine formation and the ring contraction were lowered by 7.3 and 7.6 kcal mol−1, respectively, compared with the direct lactamization process, which enables cyclization. This result has been published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. in 2013. This strategy was also used to synthesize several naturally occurring cyclic peptides, including dichotomin, phakellistatin, cyclomontanin B, and yunnanin C and its analogues. Some of the results were published in Org. Biomol. Chem. and Tetrahedron. Ser/Thr-mediated peptide cyclization and its application has been reported in Synlett. and Nat. Prod. Rep. as invited reviews. Overall, all the project objectives have been fully executed and the Ser/Thr ligation-mediated peptide cyclization developed in this project emerges as an alternative and promising method for the synthesis of cyclic peptides.

707412.label: Major findings and research outcome
707412.value: In this project, the first total synthesis of daptomycin has been accomplished. Daptomycin is the first natural product antibiotic lauched in a generation. Its distinct mechanism of action renders daptomycin a new structural motif for the development of new antibiotic. An efficient route to chemically synthesize daptomycin that allows the assembly of the peptide sequence with precision and flexibility will make it possible to prepare a wide variation of daptomycin analogues, thereby enabling the establishment a comprehensive structure-activity relationship of daptomycin to kickstart the search for optimized analogues. With the chemical strategy we developed, we successfully synthesized daptomycin and more than 20 analogues. In addition, we have developed Ser/Thr ligation-mediated peptide cyclization, which was the key strategy to enable cyclization in the daptomycin synthesis. Furthermore, we demonstrated that Ser/Thr ligation-mediated peptide cyclization offers a general strategy for the synthesis of cyclic peptides, including the high-strained cyclic tetrapeptide which is very difficult to synthesis using other strategies.

707412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
707412.value: The synthetic strategy to prepare daptomycin developed in this project will allow us to carry out the comprehensive medicinal chemistry studies on daptomycin to search for daptomycin-based next-generation antibiotics against resistant bacterial pathogens. Indeed, we have secured a collaborative research grant (CRF), part of which involves the medicinal chemistry of daptomycin.

707412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
707412.value: Cyclic peptides exhibit remarkable biological activities and have attracted a lot of attention in the pharmaceutical industry. Exploration of cyclic peptides for medicinal chemistry requires efficient synthetic methods. In this project, we have developed a new Ser/Thr ligation-mediated peptide cyclization, which offers an promising and efficient strategy for the synthesis of cyclic peptides of various size. As an example, we applied this strategy and developed an effective route to chemically synthesize cyclic lipodepsipeptide antibiotic, daptomycin. Daptomycin has potent bactericidal activity with a unique mode of action against otherwise antibiotic-resistant Gram-positive pathogens, including MRSA. Inevitably, bacteria resistant to daptomycin will emerge, calling upon the daptomycin-based next-generation antibiotics for additional clinical applications and in preparation of future waves of the development of bacterial resistance. Our success in the development of total synthesis of daptomycin will enable us to generate various daptomycin analogues to kickstart the search for optimized analogues.

707612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
707612.value: Southeast China, including Hong Kong, is a very densely populated region. The climate in this region is mainly influenced by the Asian monsoon. However, our understanding of natural variability of Asian monsoons is still limited, and the mechanism of regional climate in response to changing global climate and increasing human activities remains largely elusive. For example, it is widely believed that changes in the sea surface temperature and hydrologic conditions in the Indo-Pacific region would directly influence the monsoon intensity. But new studies indicate that hydrological changes in the Indo-Pacific region are opposite to those in East Asia over the last 2000 years, a critical time interval for understanding the "base-line" of natural climate variability. This finding poses a serious challenge to the long-time conventional view. Largely due to lack of spatially-distributed, high-resolution paleoclimate reconstructions, such as hydrological and temperature changes from tropical Western Pacific and especially in the South China Sea, our ability to assess/re-assess the proposed mechanisms of monsoon dynamics is hindered. Here, we propose to reconstruct ~2000-year-long, high-resolution (5-10 years) surface salinity and temperature records in the South China Sea. We will collect and analyze 6 sediment cores, spreading between 23°N and 5°N, but mainly in the northern South China Sea. Salinity reconstructions will be based on D/H ratios of alkenone and fatty acids, and/or oxygen isotopes of planktonic foraminifera. Quantitative surface temperature changes will be reconstructed using two temperature proxies, the alkenone unsaturation index (UK’37) and/or tetraether index (TEX86). Key issues we will address are: What is the amplitude of surface temperature changes off Hong Kong and in the South China Sea over the last 2000 years? How did salinity changes respond to climatic changes (i.e. temperature)? Were salinity changes in these locations spatially different? Did salinity changes in the South China Sea follow those in the Indo-Pacific region or the East Asian monsoon region? Can we assemble a big picture of hydrological changes in the regions between Southeast China and Indonesia over the last 2000 years?

707612.label: Realisation of objectives
707612.value: All of the project objectives have been addressed and almost completed. Over the past 42 months, we have analyzed more than 1000 sediment samples, mainly from 4 regions in the northern South China Sea, Hong Kong waters, open sea (including Xisha Islands), west of Macau and near Taiwan Strait. We have achieved excellent temperature records over the last 2000 years from the four regions, which reveal spatial heterogeneity and could be linked to regional climatic and circulation system. The proposed measurement of hydrogen isotopes on alkenones is not reliable due to insufficient alkenone amount achieved for isotopic measurements, and could not be published in present form. Instead, we have worked on a sediment core from Xisha Islands, using other types of proxies, which successfully reveals hydrological changes in the northern South China Sea. Analysis of alkenone hydrogen isotopes is still being attempted now. We have managed to publish 9 scientific papers within this reporting period. We still have a few papers to be published, arising directly from this project. Two manuscripts are almost ready to be submitted, while another two manuscripts, addressing spatial heterogeneity of temperature and salinity changes in the northern South China Sea, will take some time to be completed. Three PhD and two MPhil students have been trained in the field of organic geochemistry and paleoclimatology. Three have already successfully completed their PhD/MPhil study, while the other two are still on-going. Three undergraduate students have also been trained for doing research in this field.

707612.label: Major findings and research outcome
707612.value: 1. We have found that coastal regions are more influenced by winter monsoon than open sea, thus the temperature difference between the coastal and open sea regions could be used to indicate winter monsoon evolution (Item 3). 2. Sea surface temperature changes in the east of Hong Kong waters (i.e. Mirs Bay) display an opposite pattern to global temperature changes, likely resulting from intensified ocean mixing due to stronger summer monsoon during warmer periods (Item 6). This phenomenon is supported by longer SST records from the Hong Kong waters and elsewhere. 3. We have found that ocean current strength changes could also alter local sea surface temperatures (Item 2). 4. We have found that spatial heterogeneity of sea surface temperature changes over the last 2000 years in the northern South China Sea, with open sea and west of Macau following global/northern hemisphere temperature changes, while eastern HK waters and Taiwan Strait region following the opposite pattern. 5. We confirm wetter conditions during the little ice age, a relatively cool period, at Xisha Islands, and hydrological changes likely corresponded to solar irradiance changes over the past 2000 years. 6. In general, hydrological (salinity) changes were generally associated with temperature changes over the last 2000 years, involving possible Asian summer monsoon and winter monsoon changes.

707612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
707612.value: Arising from this project, several points (although being based on preliminary results) are worth to be further investigated: 1. The link of typhoon frequency/intensity with regional climate might be revealed from sediment cores. Due to chronological uncertainty, previous reconstructions of typhoon variability are difficult to be linked to regional climate. However, this problem could be potentially resolved if both temperature and typhoon (mainly based on grain size proxy) records could be generated from the same sediment core. If so, more details will be revealed and will help to understand typhoon behavior under the global warming scenario. 2. We have noticed periodic increase in organic matter, likely related to diatom bloom, in the northern South China Sea over the past few millennia. Research could be further developed to confirm the diatom bloom and its association with climatic/environmental conditions. 3. We have also found that ocean water column structure changed as well over the past 2 millennia. Research could be further developed to understand how East Asian summer monsoon and winter monsoon, as well as freshwater input from large rivers, could affect ocean stratification.

707612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
707612.value: We have studied sea surface temperature and salinity changes in the northern South China Sea over the last 2000 years in order to gain some insights on how regional climatic conditions responded to global climatic changes, in the hope of better projecting future regional changes under the anticipated global warming scenario. Our results confirm that coastal sea surface temperatures could be affected by both the East Asian summer monsoon and winter monsoon, and that regional precipitation changes were also linked regional/global temperature changes. In particular, we have found that during relatively warm periods over the past 2000 years, sea surface temperatures were relatively warm in open sea and west of Macau, while cool in eastern Hong Kong waters and regions further to the east that might have resulted from enhanced ocean mixing due to stronger summer monsoon. The spatial pattern of sea surface temperature changes in the northern South China Sea might be applicable to future warmer conditions.

707712.label: Realisation of objectives
707712.value: The objectives have been achieved: 1. We have devised approaches to apply controlled perturbations on interfaces with low interfacial tensions, and shown that controlled minute perturbations, such as sound, and vigorous perturbations such as mechanical shaking, can lead to ripples and induce breakup at the interfaces. 2. Controlled single and multiple emulsions have been generated using different methods, including mechanical vibrations, and all-aqueous electrospray. 3. All-aqueous emulsions with high emulsion stability have been prepared. Among the different approaches tested, protein nanofibrils, as a novel type of stabilizers, offer the highest stability.

707712.label: Major findings and research outcome
707712.value: - All-aqueous multiphase microfluidics allows the generation of droplets and jets in the absence of any organic solvents. - The interfaces with ultralow interfacial tension are highly passive, and can be manipulated with minute perturbations such as sound. - All-aqueous droplets and materials generated from all-aqueous droplets offer superior preservation of bioactivity of bio-actives, suggesting its higher bio- and cyto-compatibility. - All-aqueous droplets provide a platform for assembly of macromolecules for templated fabrication of capsules and particles All these results were presented in various international conferences (e.g. ACS Colloids Meeting, APS Division of Fluid Dynamics Meeting, etc.) and published in important international journals (e.g. Nature Communications, ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces, ACS Macro Letters, Lab on a Chip, etc.), as shown in Part C.

707712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
707712.value: The research has exhibited excellent potential for bio-mimicking liquid membrane-less organelles, delivering delicate biomolecules (e.g. enzymes) as active ingredients and assembling functional compounds. The proposed course of action includes studying the effects of proteins, which represent both an important component in biological systems and a delicate functional biomolecules using the developed all-aqueous droplet systems. The all-aqueous interfaces can be investigated for its applicability in assembling membrane-like structures and its implications for biomembranes. Research grants from both local (RGC) and international (Human Frontier Science Programme) sources are being sought and considered for furthering the important further works mentioned. The advantages of this newly developed systems are being discussed with the industries for developing novel delivery vehicles, such as capsules.

707712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
707712.value: In this project, we proposed the generation of organic-solvent-free emulsions in microfluidics. The costly, toxic, flammable and environmentally harmful solvents can now be excluded following our results. We developed a physical understanding of the formation of these interesting and useful water-based emulsions. The intricate dynamics of liquid jet breakup has shed light on new ways to generate droplets. Excellent control of the size and shape of these emulsions is achieved using novel techniques specifically designed to address the ultra-low interfacial tensions of these systems. Both single and multiple water-based emulsions can now be formed, and they exhibit excellent bio-compatibility. This study is expected to improve the applicability of emulsions, particularly those prepared using microfluidic methods, as well as emulsion-templated materials for biomedical applications. Our works have also led to a new all-aqueous liquid-liquid platform for designing and fabricating new bio-materials with new functions. The materials developed based on this platform is expected to be more customizable, environmentally friendly and compatible with biological active ingredients, thus extending the range of drugs that can be delivered.

710012.value: 後張預應力高強混凝土平板性能化抗火設計

710012.value: Dr LI, Jing Dr TSANG, Neil C.M.

710012.label: Project Objectives
710012.value: To study the failure mechanisms of PT flat slab panels under fire with particular emphasis on the two-way behaviour and membrane action taking into account the influence of thermal deformations, local materials, continuity, restraints, etc.; To evaluate the possible effects of fire spread on irrecoverable loss of initial stress distribution, changes in load-path mechanisms, holistic behaviour of floor, etc.; To assess the long-term effects of transient high-temperature stress relaxation of tendons and transient thermal creep of concrete under limited fire exposure; and To formulate rational guidance on performance-based design for engineers for this kind of structures particularly with the use of high-strength materials.

710012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
710012.value: Structural engineers have been searching for efficient structural forms to satisfy various attributes under the performance-based concept, namely safety, serviceability, durability, constructability, maintainability, environmental friendliness, economy, etc. Taking advantage of desirable properties of both concrete and high-strength steel tendons, prestressed concrete (PC) has become popular for spanning relatively long distances. In tall building projects, the clients and architects often want to reduce the number of columns to enhance the property value. Building services engineers prefer to have flat floor soffits (under-surfaces) to allow convenient installation of services. Post-tensioned concrete flat slab floors have emerged as an economical structural form making use of the two-way action so that loads are carried by spanning in two perpendicular directions. With the rapid advancement of concrete technology, coupled with increases in floor spans and building heights, high-strength concrete (HSC) is increasingly used in high-rise buildings. The tragic 1996 Garley Building fire in Hong Kong with a death toll of 41 and 81 injuries has vividly reminded people of the importance of fire safety and building performance under fire. The building was damaged so badly that it was abandoned and then reconstructed in 2003. Unlike conventional reinforced concrete (RC) structures, PC structures built of high-strength materials carrying higher initial stresses are invariably more susceptible to fire. If a flat slab panel is subject to a fully developed fire, the structural action may deviate significantly from that at ambient temperatures because of the formation of alternative load-paths such as compressive and then tensile membrane actions. As opposed to RC that often has hair cracks to vent the steam released by concrete upon severe heating, PC primarily under compression is more susceptible to the build-up of high vapour pressure and possible spalling under fire. While the prescriptive approach of fire resistant structural design is well established and simple to use, it tends to be conservative, restrictive and expensive. It is uncertain if the prescriptive approach works for PC structures, which are often governed by the design for serviceability limit state. This project on post-tensioned HSC flat slabs under fire, which comprises experimental and numerical components, is therefore proposed: (a) to study the failure mechanisms of flat slab panels with particular emphasis on the two-way behaviour and membrane action; (b) to evaluate the possible effects of fire spread on holistic behaviour of floor; (c) to assess the long-term effects of transient high-temperature stress relaxation; and (d) to formulate rational guidance on performance-based design. 一直以來，結構工程師都致力於追求高效的基於性能化的結構設計形式，滿足結構安全性、實用性、耐久性、可行性、持續性以及環保性的要求。其中，預應力混凝土結構以其充分利用混凝土和高強鋼筋的優越性，在大跨度和高層結構中得到廣泛應用。然而，建筑業主和建筑師對結構大開間的要求以及屋宇裝備工程師對層間淨高的要求，使得後張預應力混凝土平板結構受到青睞，其採用雙向張拉預應力筋使混凝土板承擔樓面荷載的經濟結構形式，在建筑結構中也得到應用。同時，隨著混凝土技術的發展以及建筑結構跨度和高度的不斷增加，高強混凝土在建筑結構中的使用量也不斷增加。 然而，火災的發生對建筑結構的性能及防火安全帶來重大挑戰。1996年香港嘉利大廈火災致使41人死亡和81人受傷的慘劇，至今使人歷歷在目。由於火災后結構嚴重受損，當時已被棄用，直至2003年才得以重建。火災下，傳統的鋼筋混凝土結構內部微裂縫不斷發展，直至明顯的縫隙出現，使得混凝土中的水分以水蒸氣的形式逃逸出去；然而，預應力混凝土結構由於初始預壓力的存在，延緩了裂縫的出現，從而導致混凝土內水蒸氣無法及時排除，以至於更易發生嚴重的混凝土爆裂，使得結構性能更加劣化。目前，規范條款形式的結構抗火設計方法，以其簡單便捷被廣泛採用，並且在通常情況這下，這種設計受諸多條件限制，偏於保守和不夠經濟。然而，這種設計是否適用於預應力混凝土結構，卻是一個尚待解決的問題。 因此基於以上背景，提出了後張預應力高強混凝土平板的性能化抗火研究，以期達到以下研究目的： 1. 研究預應力混凝土平板在火災下的失效機理，重點研究其雙向的行為特征及板的薄膜效應； 2. 研究火災發展對預應力混凝土平板造成的時效行為響應； 3. 研究預應力鋼筋瞬態高溫應力鬆弛對混凝土平板承載力的長期效應； 4. 對預應力混凝土平板的性能化抗火設計提出合理的指導。

710012.label: Realisation of objectives
710012.value: 1. The failure mechanisms of post-tensioned (PT) flat slab panels under fire have been studied experimentally and numerically. A few PT concrete flat slabs with unbonded tendons and a few others with bonded tendons were fire-tested under load in a furnace to study their failure mechanisms. By analyzing the test results, the crack formation mechanisms were examined. In some of the tests, severe concrete spalling was observed in the slabs, with the formation of through holes in the extreme cases. In those slab specimens without concrete spalling, membrane action was observed, which enabled the slab to survive much longer fire duration. 2. Tests were conducted to study the irrecoverable loss of stress in prestressing steel through thermal creep tests and thermal relaxation tests. A model was established to account for the loss of stress in prestressing steel. Numerical modelling was then conducted to study the effects of loss of prestress on the deformation and load-carrying capacity of PT concrete flat slabs. Moreover, the holistic behaviour of PT flat slabs was studied as well based on fire tests. Subsequently, parametric studies were conducted to assess the structural fire performance of flat slab. These tools enable the effects of fire spread on irrecoverable loss of initial stress distribution, etc. to be assessed. 3. The long-term effects of transient high-temperature stress relaxation of tendons have been studied by testing and numerical modelling. The transient thermal creep of concrete under limited fire exposure was studied by numerical modelling. Through material tests of prestressing steel, the thermal creep parameters were obtained and Harmathy’s thermal creep model was updated to account for the stress relaxation of prestressing steel commonly available in the market. Based on available results of transient thermal creep tests of concrete at elevated temperatures, the transient thermal creep model was verified and employed to investigate the structural performance of PT concrete flat slabs in fire. 4. Various practical issues in the structural fire design of PT concrete flat slabs with high-strength concrete have been examined. Some design guidance has been drafted.

710012.label: Major findings and research outcome
710012.value: The major findings of the structural fire behaviour of PT flat slabs under loading are summarised as follows. 1. For PT flat slabs with only the central panel subject to fire, cracks normally appear in the column strips in approximately elliptic cracking patterns, being caused by the tensile stresses associated with negative moments induced by the restraints of the surrounding cold parts on the doubly curved deformation of the central panel. 2. For PT flat slabs with only the central panel subject to fire, cracks normally weaken the slab integrity and relieve the restraints on the deformation of the central panel. They tend to contribute to the development of tensile membrane action, and hence enhance the load-carrying capacity of slab. 3. Enlarging the area of PT flat slabs exposed to fire tends to release the restraints of the surrounding cold panels on the flexural deformation of the central panel, further resulting in the increase of deflections. 4. Concrete spalling is mainly governed by moisture content and compressive stresses. There may be a threshold moisture content, above which concrete spalling under certain compressive stresses can be triggered. 5. Increasing the level of prestressing tends to increase the transient creep strain of concrete and the equivalent load provided by prestressing tendons, further resulting in the decrease of deflections. 6. The tendon arrangements considered have little effect on the central deflection of the slabs but have slight effect on the mid-span deflection of column strips because of the transient creep strain of concrete under fire conditions. 7. The parameters of Harmathy’s creep model for prestressing steel products commonly available in the market were identified and calibrated based on the test results. 8. With the model proposed to account for the stress loss of prestressing steel and other available models, numerical models can be built to analyze the structural deformation of flat slabs under fire.

710012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
710012.value: In the light of the completed research, some of the potential areas for further development are listed as follows: 1. The structural performance of PT concrete flat slabs after exposure to fire and cooling down to ambient temperature needs to be further investigated. A simplified calculation method should be developed to evaluate the residual load-carrying capacity of the slab to facilitate decision making regarding whether to demolish or retrofit. 2. The effects of concrete spalling on the structural fire performance of PT concrete flat slabs need to be investigated taking into account possible adverse effects of spalling on the reduction or loss of concrete cover to tendons.

710012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
710012.value: The research project has improved understanding of how post-tensioned concrete flat slabs perform in fire and after fire. The deformation mechanism, failure mechanism, stress relaxation of prestressing steel, concrete transient thermal creep, concrete spalling and membrane actions at elevated temperatures have been studied through experiments and numerical modelling. The research findings have provided theoretical background, experimental data and numerical modelling methodology for structural fire safety evaluation of post-tensioned concrete flat slabs, as well as formulation of guidance for their structural fire design.

710412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
710412.value: 自從蘋果在 iPhone4S 上面開始使用 Siri 系統，人機溝通就成為一個熱門的討論題目。除了語音識別和文字處理以外，面部表情在這方面也扮演了一定的角色。研究指出，在面對面的溝通上，面部表情提供了55％的溝通效果，而說話的聲調和真正講的話卻只有38％和7％的貢獻。如果電腦能夠識別人面的表情，人機溝通將會更加自然和有效率。 主題模型 (Topic Model) 首先是應用在文字處理上的。在差不多內容的文件內，找尋詞語用法跟文件內容的關聯，然後經電腦找出潛在主題 (latent topic)。從新的文件裡，找出相關的潛在主題，就可以對文件進行分類。 作為一個先導研究，我們提出了時序潛在主題模型 (Temporal Latent Topic Model)。在面部表情的識別上，得到96.29%的識別率，跟最新的研究結果96.26%相差不遠。我們也確立了面部動作編碼系統 (Facial Action Coding System, FACS) 和 潛在主題 (latent topics) 的對應。心理學家制定了面部動作編碼系統，作為對面部表情背後的機制的解釋。每一個面部表情，都由不同的動作單元 (Action Units) 構成，像：提起臉頰 (cheek raiser), 拉開嘴角 (lip corner puller) 等。這些動作單元又由更基本的肌肉活動所組成。潛在主題模型正有這種三層等級關係。最上層的是文件，而詞語就在下層。中間的是文件中的各個主題。可以看見這兩個模型像似之處。我們發現，用我們的時序潛在主題模型找出了的模型很好的與心理學家所提出的動作單元相匹配。同時我們加入了時序信息和區分性信息，令我們的模型與實際上面部表情的機制更配合。 在這個計畫裡，我們再進一步對我們的時序潛在主題模型提出以下的改進。首先，我們將會提出一個連續性模型，以更好的描述連續的面部表情。我們也會對不同主題之間的相關性找出相對的模型。最後，我們將會利用最大間隔學習 (Maximum Margin Learning) 來更好的作出區分性處理，使識別率能更進一步。我們不單會用標準的數據庫作測試，也會用到從攝錄機得來的圖像，使系統更能真實使用。

710412.label: Realisation of objectives
710412.value: 1. We have built a correlation topic model based on our temporal Latent Topic Model. A paper was published in IVCNZ'2015 in Auckland. Two types of facial features were used in the CTM, namely, structural features and transient features. Structural features includes shape transition words (STW) We used 41 out of the 58 facial landmarks provided by the Active Appearance Model (AAM) for facial alignment. Transient features are non-landmark-based -- Facial Appearance Words (FAW), which is based on local binary patterns (LBP). These features undergo a Temporal Pyramid Matching, and Bags of Features are formed and fed to the CTM. Finally, a Bayesian Modeling is used to model the temporal relationship between frames. An accuracy of 91.3% on the CK+ database was achieved, which is satisfactory. 2. Maximum Margin Learning has been incorporated into the Correlated Topic Model. The incorporation of maximum margin learning does not improve much the result of the training. We have also developed a new facial alignment algorithm for large pose faces, so that facial landmarks can be obtained reliably even though the image is not frontal. The paper was selected for oral presentation in BMVC2016. 3. A Continuous Model has been developed, and incorporated into the CTM Model. Bayes Modeling was introduced to model the temporal correlation between facial images in the image sequence. There was 8.5% improvement by incorporating the Bayes modeling into the image sequence. Finally, CTM with Bayes modeling achieve a satisfactory performance of 91.3%. 4. We have collected the 7 basic facial expressions used in the CK+ database for 80 persons. All of them are orientals as mentioned in the proposal, as most existing database is Westerners. Not only plain backgrounds were used, but also more complex background such as playgrounds and offices, and also videos with different lighting conditions, such as at night and under office lighting. We are still in the process of processing the data to conform with other datasets. 5. We have started building a generation system. Unfortunately, we have used up all the funding and have only an incomplete system. We will continue to work on this system, probably with other fundings.

710412.label: Major findings and research outcome
710412.value: In this project, we have developed a Correlation Topic Model for Facial Expression Recognition. We used the Active Appearance Model for facial alignment. 41 relevant landmarks out of 58 are chosen. Two kinds of features were extracted, namely Shape Transition Words (STW) and Facial Appearance Words (FAW). Local Binary Patterns (LBP) were also added. Temporal Pyramid Matching was employed for modeling facial muscle movements. Finally, the features are fed into a Correlation Topic Models, and the Topic Probabilities were channelled to SVM classification. At the end, Bayes Modeling was used to model the temporal relationship between different frames of the facial expression sequences. An accuracy of 91.3% was achieved. It demonstrates that the model do have potentials, and further investigation is worthwhile. More recently, faces in the wild (i.e. faces from uncontrolled environment) become more popular. We also try to work in that direction, which we believe will be the future. In the end, we have to work on uncontrolled facial expression, "in the wild". We have two papers published in the prestige British Machine Vision Conference (BMVC). In BMVC2014, we used a face mask reasoning to facial landmarks localization. We used the dataset "Labeled faces in the Wild" (LFW) and "Labeled Face Parts in the Wild" (LFPW), both commonly used for research on "faces in the wild". The performance achieved, as measured by percentage of pixels that are correctly classified (83.9%) and average recall over all classes (88.6%) are much better than alternative approaches (the best are 81.7% and 86.6% respectively). Based on this work, we have further derived a large pose facial alignment algorithm based on cascaded pose regression (CPR) technique. The work was presented orally in BMVC2016. The acceptance rate was only 10% (for oral paper). We learned a 3D Morphable Model (3DMM) that matches the given 2D models. Works can then be performed on the 3D models. The facial expression "in the wild" can be processed in a similar manner, where the a 3D model can be generated from the sequences, facial landmarks obtained and topic models constructed as usual. The Normalized Mean Error (NME) achieved by our approach, namely, 5.27%, 5.34%, 6.53% and 5.7% (for poses of 0-30 degree, 30-60 degrees, 60-90 degrees, and average) outperforms 5.37%, 6.37%, 9.62% and 7.17% of the alternatives. The performance is significantly better for large pose (60-90 degrees), which shows the power of the model.

710412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
710412.value: We have demonstrated that Topic Models are good candidates for Facial Expression Recognition. The Topic generated (unsupervisedly) by the Topic Model conforms to the Action Units in the Facial Action Coding System (FACS) proposed by Psychologists. We also showed that the Correlation Topic Models have great potential in Facial Expression Recognition. The use of Cascaded Regressor for face alignment paved the groundwork for recognition of facial expression in the wild. Recently, deep learning has been very popular in Computer Vision. We are also exploring the use of deep learning as a feature extractor (instead of using facial landmarks) and then fed to Topic Model for classification. The approach looks promising and combines the advantages of deep learning , how the brain processes visual stimulation and topic models, how human sees the expressions. This is still in the early stage, and we hope that this will eventually evolve to a more mature stage.

710412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
710412.value: It is well known that emotion plays an important role in inter-personal communication. It was found 55% of all human gesture effects on the receiver of the communication were conveyed by facial expressions. Understanding facial expression is very important in Human Machine Interaction. Topic Models try to find relevant topics from documents, and classify the documents from the topics found, based on the vocabularies used in the document. For example, a document may contains words relevant to economics and politics. This provides clues to what the document is about. This idea was borrowed by us for facial expression recognition. The document is the facial expression, while the words is the appearance of the face. We used computer vision methods to get features to describe this appearance. From each document, we get these "words" and we have a large amount of document/word training data. In the topic model, "topics" corresponds to the muscle movements of the face, aka the Facial Action Units described by Psychologists. The topic model will find topics automatically. Topics generated by our topic model conforms closely to the action units proposed by the psychologists, and hence demonstrates the effectiveness of the model.

710512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
710512.value: Image-based rendering (IBR) is a promising technology for photo-realistic rendering of scenes and objects from a collection of densely sampled images and videos. It is able to support a continuum of viewpoints according to users’ interaction in contrast to a set of fixed viewpoints found in conventional images and videos. More importantly, it helps to synthesis intermediate views required by multiview TV displays and other applications. While there has been much progress in intermediate view synthesis using the object-based approach, view synthesis in sports applications still present great difficulty as the audiences usually expect multiview systems to provide large viewing freedom in a continuous manner such as fly over and other special effects. The problem stems from the fact that human objects may only be partially visible due to self-occlusion, etc. By using more cameras in the scene will help to alleviate this problem, but it is still difficult and expensive to ensure that sufficient geometry information can be acquired for reliable 3D reconstruction. This motivates us to study in this proposal a systematic approach to dynamic image-based analysis and synthesis for human in sports and related applications. Our approach is to adopt a densely spaced multiple camera system, and depth cameras in Microsoft Kinect, for instant acquisition of the 3D model of a subject and generation of a subject specific 3D model for subsequent tracking in the field by using another set of less densely spaced, say eight or more, stereo video cameras. Moreover, we shall estimate and then propagate its appearance and deformable 3D model over time, so as to perform realistic view synthesis with a much larger view freedom than conventional image-based approaches. The ultimate aims of the project are to develop a systematic and cost-effective approach for image-based analysis and synthesis of dynamic 3D human model for sports and other applications. This will significant improve the viewing freedom of existing image-based rendering systems and content generation for multi-view TVs and related applications. In the long term, the technology will benefit considerably the content production in Edutainment, digital entertainment, training and education of sport activities. 圖像繪製（IBR）是一種很有前途的視頻技術，它利用密集採樣的真實圖像和視頻合成出在其他虛擬視點的高質量圖像和視頻。並能根據用戶的指示連續改變視點。 雖然IBR在視頻合成上有了很大的進展，其在體育應用的使用仍然存在很大的困難。因為觀眾多期望視角系統可以提供更大的視角自由度，如以連續的方式模擬飛越和其他特殊效果。問題的困難源於場景可能因遮擋而只是部分可見。 雖然在場景中使用多個攝像機有助於緩解這個問題，但這個解決方案非常昂貴和不便。因此，我們需要一種方法以確保有足夠的幾何信息足以達致三維重建。 在此項目中, 我們將會建造一個動態圖像的分析和合成系統用以體育及相關的研究。我們的做法是採用一個多攝像機和微軟Kinect深度攝像機的系統，即時採集和生成一個初步的三維模型，並利用另一組間隔密度較低的立體攝像機繼續跟踪和更新目標三維及其外觀模型, 從而進行比傳統方法自由度更大及更逼真的視頻合成。 該項目的最終目標是開發一個基於圖像分析和繪製的綜合人體動態三維模型重建及合成系統以供運動和其他應用。這將顯著改善現有圖像繪製系統觀看的自由度從而解決多視點電視和相關應用在內容生成中現時的限制。

710612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
710612.value: As symbolized in many logos, mechanical gears have played an utmost important role in our daily life. With the use of mechanical gears, speed and torque can be amplified for various practical applications. For some applications such as the automotive transmission, the gear ratio needs to be flexibly varied in order to satisfy the driving requirement and road condition. Thus, the mechanical gearbox, which consists of a set of mechanical gears and a gear-shifting mechanism, was invented to offer the concept of mechanical variable-speed gearing. However, the mechanical gears inherently suffer from the drawbacks of wear-and-tear, annoying noise and need of regular maintenance. Increasingly, the mechanical gearboxes suffer from the problems of high transmission loss, bulky size, heavy weight and complicated gear-shifting mechanism. Thus, the development of efficient and effective variable-speed gears will exert a long-term impact on our society. In recent years, magnetic gears have been actively developed. Based on permanent magnet attraction for torque transmission, they can offer the merits of contactless transmission, silent operation and maintenance free, hence solving the drawbacks of mechanical gears. Nevertheless, a direct replacement of mechanical gears by magnetic gears cannot solve the problems of mechanical gearboxes. Actually, it is a long-sought goal of many researchers to develop the magnetic variable-speed gears, aiming to offer controllable gear ratios while fundamentally solving the problems of mechanical gearboxes. In order to fully retain the merits of magnetic gears while exploring the concept of variable-speed gearing, the idea of electrically controlled magnetic variable-speed gears is born. Namely, the concept of memory machines will be incorporated into the magnetic gears in such a way that the gear ratio can be online changed by electrical means while the torque transmission is simply based on permanent magnet attraction and does not involve electrical energy. The purpose of this proposal is to develop electrically controlled magnetic variable-speed gears and investigate their promising applications. The objectives are: (1) develop a novel topology with various morphologies which can offer permanent magnet based torque transmission and electrically controllable gear ratios; (2) develop a new analytical approach to model the torque transfer and overall performances; (3) develop a new electromagnetic field approach to optimize the transmission efficiency; (4) develop a new control strategy to achieve electrically controllable gear ratios and hence optimal system efficiency; and (5) explore promising applications and evaluate them in terms of technical performances and commercial values. 機械齒輪在我們日常生活中發揮了極其重要的作用。我們可以利用機械齒輪的作用，改變傳動部件的速度和轉矩，滿足各種實際應用。對於某些應用，如汽車的變速器，變速比需要靈活地改變，以滿足驅動要求和道路情況。因此，工程師就發明了由一組機械齒輪和變速機理組成的機械變速齒輪箱。然而，機械齒輪本身受到磨損的弊端，導致惱人的噪音，需要定期維護。再者，機械變速齒輪箱面對傳動損耗高，體積大，重量大和結構複雜的問題。因此，開發有效和高效率的變速齒輪是非常重要，對我們的社會也將產生深遠的影響。 近年來，磁齒輪已被積極地開發。基於永久磁鐵的物理現象，磁齒輪可以提供非接觸式傳動，寧靜的操作和免維護的優點，從而解決了機械齒輪的缺點。然而，利用磁性齒輪直接替換機械齒輪不能解決機械變速齒輪箱的問題。事實上，許多研究人員長期追求的目標，就是開發一套變速磁齒輪，它既能提供可控的齒輪比，又能同時從根本上解決機械變速齒輪箱的問題。為了充分保留磁齒輪的優點，同時探索變速傳動裝置的新概念，我們就提出了電控式變速磁齒輪的想法。亦即將記憶電機的概念和磁齒輪的概念混合在一起，從而利用電氣裝置在線改變磁齒輪的齒輪比，其傳動簡單地基於永久磁鐵的作用，並且不涉及電功率損耗。 此項目的目的是開發一種新型電控式變速磁齒輪，並探討其廣闊的應用前景。目標是：（1）開發一種新的磁齒輪結構，它既可以提供基於永久磁鐵的傳動，又能利用電控改變齒輪比;（2）開發新的分析方法來模擬磁齒輪傳動和整體性能;（3）制定一個新的電磁場分析方法來優化傳動效率;（4）開發新的控制策略，實現可電控改變齒輪比，從而優化系統的效率;（5）探索廣闊的應用前景，並評估它們的技術性能和商業價值。

710612.label: Realisation of objectives
710612.value: The 1st objective has been fully achieved. A novel magnetic variable-speed gear topology has been developed. The key is to incorporate the concept of memory machine into the structure of coaxial magnetic gear. Specifically, the investigation on using aluminum-nickel-cobalt (Alnico) permanent magnets (PMs) for magnetic gears is first revealed. Then, by artfully inserting a double-deck magnetizing winding into the stationary ring of the coaxial magnetic gear, the Alnico PM pieces in the inner and outer rotors can be dynamically magnetized or demagnetized, thus achieving the ability of changing the numbers of PM pole-pairs in the inner and outer rotors and hence the gear ratio. Consequently, the numbers of PM pieces in the inner and outer rotors and the number of iron segments in the stationary ring can be optimized to provide the desired sets of electrically controllable gear ratios. Meanwhile, various locations of the magnetizing winding in the stationary ring, namely in the air segments only, the iron segments only as well as both the air and iron segments, are assessed so as to minimize the cogging torque. The proposed coaxial topology which belongs to the radial-field morphology has also been extended to the axial-field and linear morphologies. The resulting axial-field magnetic variable-speed gear has the distinct merits of higher torque density and pancake shape. Meanwhile, the resulting linear magnetic variable-speed gear possesses the unique feature of linear motion in the absence of rotary-to-linear mechanism. The 2nd objective has been fully achieved. By taking into account all effective harmonics of airgap fluxes in both the inner and outer rotors of the proposed coaxial magnetic variable-speed gear, the magnetic torques developed at the inner and outer airgaps can be analytically derived. Hence, the torque transfer mechanism can be analytically modeled. Consequently, the equations, which govern the selection of the number of inner-rotor PM pole-pairs, the number of inner-rotor PM pieces, the number of outer-rotor PM pole-pairs, the number of outer-rotor PM pieces, the number of stationary-ring iron segments, the number of turns of stationary-ring upper-deck magnetizing winding and the number of turns of stationary-ring lower-deck magnetizing winding, are derived. Therefore, the overall performances of the proposed coaxial magnetic variable-speed gear including the torque transfer capability and the number of gear ratios can be analytically modeled. The 3rd objective has been fully achieved. By performing the electromagnetic finite element analysis of the proposed magnetic variable-speed gear, the airgap flux densities, torque transfer capabilities and cogging torques at both the inner and outer rotors can be accurately assessed. In order to further assess the magnetizing and demagnetizing processes, the hysteresis loop of Alnico PMs is represented by a parallelogram hysteresis model. By incorporating the hysteresis model into the finite element analysis and taking into account the magnetic couplings between various components, the overall performances including the core losses during magnetization and demagnetization can be accurately calculated. Hence, the torque transmission efficiency can be optimized by iteratively adjusting the design parameters. Moreover, the cogging torques at both the inner and outer rotors are particularly analyzed and hence suppressed by optimizing the location of the magnetizing winding in the stationary ring and also fine tuning the arc length of the iron segments in the stationary ring. The 4th objective has been fully achieved. By using bridge converters to feed bidirectional DC current into the double-deck magnetizing winding of the proposed magnetic variable-speed gear, the Alnico PM pieces can be properly magnetized or demagnetized, hence constituting proper numbers of PM pole-pairs in the inner and outer rotors. Thus, the outer-rotor torque and speed can be electrically controlled with wide ranges under the same inner-rotor torque and speed. Most importantly, there is no electrical energy consumption once the gear changing process is completed. By using electrically controllable gear ratios with seamless transition, the hybrid electric vehicle system can enable the engine operating in the optimal operating line, hence achieving the optimal transmission efficiency and system efficiency. Moreover, when applying to renewable energy systems where power-speed characteristics are nonlinear, this magnetic variable-speed gear can be controlled to help harness more renewable power. The 5th objective has been fully achieved. After consolidating the unique features of the proposed magnetic variable-speed gear, various applications have been explored. Among them, the applications of the proposed gear to engine vehicles, electric vehicles, hybrid electric vehicles, wind power systems and wave power systems are promising. The hardware of the proposed magnetic variable-speed gear, including the magnetic gear, power converter and electronic controller, have been prototyped and tested, hence validating the corresponding technical performances. Moreover, the cost-effectiveness on using Alnico for magnetic gears is brought forward, hence evaluating the commercial value of the proposed magnetic variable-speed gear. It confirms that the proposed magnetic gear takes the definite advantages of lower material cost than those rare-earth-PM magnetic gears and lower maintenance cost than those mechanical variable-speed gears while achieving electrically controllable gear ratios. Additionally, the proposed magnetic variable-speed gear has been further extended to fuse with a PM brushless machine, hence forming a magnetic variable-speed geared PM machine. It not only offers the gearing mechanism for torque and speed transmission, but also provides variable gear ratios for torque and speed variation. This machine exhibits high potentiality for specific electric vehicle applications, where very wide torque and speed ranges are desired.

710612.label: Major findings and research outcome
710612.value: The research outcome is very fruitful, namely 7 international journal papers [J1]-[J7], and 2 international conference papers [C1]-[C2]. Meanwhile, one PhD student has been trained. Concerning the design of the proposed magnetic variable-speed gear, we have first revealed the unique features on using aluminum-nickel-cobalt (Alnico) permanent magnet (PM) material for magnetic gears [J1], and hence proposed three new topologies with emphasis on the design of magnetizing windings in the stationary ring. The first topology is equipped with the double-deck magnetizing winding in both the air and iron segments of the stationary ring [J4]*, the second topology has the magnetizing winding in the air segments only [C2], and the third topology has the magnetizing winding in the iron segments only [J6]. Meanwhile, we have extended the coaxial topology to the axial-field morphology [J5] for electric vehicles and wind power generation and the linear morphology [J7] for wave power generation. Moreover, the magnetic variable-speed gear has been further fused with a PM brushless machine to form a magnetic variable-speed geared PM machine [J3]. * As queried in the mid-term assessment, we would like to clarify that the IEEE Transactions on Applied Superconductivity not only covers applications of superconductivity but also magnet technology for power applications such as motors and generators. Concerning the analysis and control of the proposed magnetic variable-speed gear, we have analytically derived the equations for the coaxial topology [J4], the axial-field one [J5] and the linear one [J7]. Meanwhile, we have employed the electromagnetic finite element analysis to assess their overall performances. Consequently, we have developed the control strategy to realize online gear changing in which the pole-changing process of each PM piece has been elaborated [J5], [J6]. Concerning the evaluation and application of the proposed magnetic variable-speed gear, we have performed a critical comparison of the cost-effectiveness on using different types of PMs [C1], [J2]. It reveals that the Alnico PM exhibits the highest cost-effectiveness, hence justifying the commercial value of the proposed magnetic variable-speed gear. Then, its practicability has been confirmed by various applications: namely, a 6-gear-ratio (dubbed as 6-speed) coaxial magnetic variable-speed gear is designed and applied for engine vehicles [J4], a 8-speed axial-field magnetic variable-speed gear for electric vehicles and wind turbines [J5], a 16-speed coaxial magnetic variable-speed gear for hybrid electric vehicles [J6], and a 8-speed linear magnetic variable-speed gear for wave energy extraction [J7].

710612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
710612.value: The project has been focused on the normal operation that the torque transmission capability of the proposed magnetic variable-speed gears is sufficiently high to withstand the load torque. The extreme operating conditions that the load torque is suddenly or accidentally higher than the torque transmission capability are important which need to be explored. For example, when applying the proposed magnetic variable-speed gears for vehicular transmission, the load torque may be suddenly very high as the vehicle’s wheel gets stuck in a hole, which will cause the phenomenon of magnetic pole slipping. On the one hand, it is a merit to offer inherent protection against overloads. On the other hand, it will create the problem of instability once temporarily overloaded, and it is challenging on how to resynchronize the input and output rotors to recover the operation after reselecting another gear ratio or the temporary overloading has elapsed. Dedicated control should be developed to handle these extreme operating conditions.

710612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
710612.value: Mechanical gearboxes, which consist of a set of mechanical gears and a gear-shifting mechanism, were invented to offer the mechanical variable-speed gearing. However, they suffer from the problems of high transmission loss, bulky size, heavy weight and complicated gear-shifting mechanism. Thus, the development of efficient and effective variable-speed gears will exert a long-term impact on our society. In recent years, magnetic gears have been actively developed. Based on permanent magnet attraction for torque transmission, they can offer the merits of contactless transmission, silent operation and maintenance free, hence solving the drawbacks of mechanical gears. Nevertheless, a direct replacement of mechanical gears by magnetic gears cannot solve the problems of mechanical gearboxes. The project has successfully developed electrically controlled magnetic variable-speed gears. The key is to incorporate the concept of memory machines into magnetic gears in such a way that the gear ratio can be online changed by electrical means while the torque transmission is simply based on permanent magnet attraction and does not involve electrical energy. Hence, they can fundamentally solve the problems of mechanical gearboxes. Consequently, they exhibit excellent technical performances and high commercial values for various applications such as vehicular transmission and turbine transmission.

710712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
710712.value: 本项研究综合利用遥感影像和数值模型，为华南地区东江流域干旱提供预测和影响评估。其方法的新颖性在于通过同化遥感数据和优化水文模型来提高干旱期间的枯水模拟精度。 东江流域是香港的主要供水水源地，提供大约80%的香港淡水消耗量。但随着区域经济社会的快速发展，香港用水也面临着与其他比邻城市，如深圳、东莞、河源和惠州的激烈竞争。尤其在干旱阶段，水资源量难以满足各地区的多种需求，势必影响香港的供水安全。因此，在水资源短缺情况下，干旱预测和影响评估对于香港和相关区域开展及时有效的减灾措施极为重要。开展本项研究的起因正在于此。 当前，遥感影像盛行于干旱监测，数值模型的利用侧重于对土壤干湿状况的评估。然而，由于遥感技术本身的局限性（例如主要能获取土壤上层几厘米的变化情况），如何合理剖析遥感结果仍具挑战性。大范围水文模型模拟通常不具有较高空间精度，其模拟结果难以提供足够小尺度的干旱信息。然而小尺度的信息对于局部区域性水资源评估非常关键。为了克服这个困难，本项研究将集成水文模型和中分辨率成像光谱仪（MODIS）的遥感影像，来提高土壤含水量的模拟精度，达到预测和评估干旱影响的目的。而且，本研究将结合美国环境预报中心和大气研究中心（NCEP/NCAR）全球气象再分析资料来研究东江流域干旱发生的物理机制，并利用两种区域气候模型的模拟结果来探索流域的干旱预报。 本项研究将增强我们耦合遥感影像和数值模型模拟对干旱预测和影响评估的能力。在全球范围内，本研究具有广泛的意义：本研究为水资源研究提供了新的途径。

710712.label: Realisation of objectives
710712.value: The project objectives have been achieved via the 36-month study: Objective 1: Using the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) products and the Variable Infiltration Capacity (VIC) hydrologic model, three drought indices, namely standardized precipitation index (SPI), standardized runoff index (SRI), and soil moisture anomaly index (SMAI), were computed to examine the spatio-temporal and evolution features of drought events. Objective 2: Using the VIC simulation results, a new method was developed for analyzing the terrestrial hydrologic responses to precipitation through using level-based daily anomalous high flow (DAHF) occurrence in a catchment. The VIC model has better performance on the variability simulation of the first level of DAHF. Objective 3: With the NCEP/NCAR (National Centers for Environmental Prediction/National Center for Atmospheric Research) Reanalysis weather data and the indexes of climate patterns (e.g., El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD)), the physical mechanisms underlying drought occurrence were detected. We investigated the features of the teleconnection between ENSO and the climate over the region for identifying the physical mechanism of drought occurrences. Objective 4: We studied the rainfall predication skill of a regional climate model (WRF), and the features of rainfall in the dry seasons in South China were investigated. Objective 5: We used a multiple linear regression model to represent the impact of climate patterns on rainfall anomalies. Normalized climate pattern indexes and normalized rainfall anomalies were used in the regression model. For under-achievements and outline attempts to overcome problems For objective 4, the application of RSM model for exploring drought was under-achievement. However, application of WRF model in this project provides a basis for further exploration of numerical model application in drought prediction. For objective 5, the integration of MODIS products, VIC simulation, two regional climate models for drought prediction was under-achievement. However, we have prepared the prediction numerical scheme using climate patterns and will have an understanding of predictability of drought occurrences.

710712.label: Major findings and research outcome
710712.value: Major findings: 1. The hydrologic response to the elevated CO2 levels for the River basin in South China was investigated. The result was published in a research journal paper (Niu et al., 2013). 2. The terrestrial hydrological processes during a dry climate period in the Pearl River basin were investigated. The terrestrial responses to hydrological processes were analyzed. The result was published in a journal paper (Niu and Chen, 2014). 3. The teleconnection of two climatic patterns, namely the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), with hydrological processes over the Pearl River basin, including the East River, in southern China, were explored. The result was published in a journal paper (Niu et al., 2014). 4. The teleconnection of ENSO with weather variables (i.e., rainfall and temperature) over South China, including the East River basin, revealed that the lag effects of ENSO on rainfall was shorter, less than 3 months. The research result was published (Li and Chen, 2014). 5. A new method for detecting daily anomaly runoff, which will be useful for analyzing drought, was developed, and the method was applied to a headwater catchment in the East River. A research journal paper was published (Chen et al., 2014). 6. Using the climate patterns (e.g., ENSO, IOD), the precipitation anomalies were represented and possible predictability of the anomalies was evaluated (Chen and Chung, 2015). 7. The drought evolution characteristics were analyzed using the VIC simulation results, and the study revealed that the hydrological drought severity would be less than meteorological drought during the developing stage (Niu et al., 2015). 8. A new index was developed using MODIS vegetation data, and then the damages of natural hazards on vegetation were identified. The study indicates that it is possible to use MODIS and the new index to evaluate drought impacts (Sun et al, 2016). 9. With understanding of the variability features of the terrestrial hydrological processes, this project showed one geomorphic index, a basin form factor (FF), can represent the wavelet-based indices for high and low-frequency responses to precipitation variability (Niu and Chen, 2016). Major research outcome 1. We have published 9 peer-reviewed top SCI journal research papers arising directly from this research project. 2. In addition, 15 conference papers and presentations were given in several international conferences. 3. Two PhD and one MPhil graduates have been trained.

710712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
710712.value: From this project, the drought features, new remote sensing index and predictability of rainfall anomalies can be used to develop drought occurrences. Specifically, for the East River basin, the numerical model simulation results can be used to evaluate the water resources security of Hong Kong during drought periods. The teleconnection of ENSO and IOD with weather variables in South China can be useful for mitigating drought impacts on water security for the region. However, to evaluate drought impacts and to mitigate drought damages need more further explorations. Mainly, how to make use of teleconnection of climate patterns need further study and what the physical mechanism of the teleconnection is needs more exploration. How to use rational descriptions of onsets, durations and severities of droughts needs further investigation. How to use more accurate remote sensing data for evaluating drought damages needs more study.

710712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
710712.value: The project aims to integrate remote sensing products and numerical model simulations for drought prediction and impact assessment at monthly and seasonal scales over the East River basin in South China. The project will be valuable for undertaking proper water emergency management measures and devising drought mitigation strategies in Hong Kong and surrounding areas. This project explored the drought evolution and the relationships among rainfall, soil moisture and streamflow during drought periods. Also, for the project, a new index in using remote sensing data has been developed to evaluate the vegetation damages due to natural hazards. Moreover, a new method has been used to describe the streamflow anomaly. The project has enhanced the skill of integration of remote sensing products and numerical model simulations for drought study.
