711112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
711112.value: It has been about 60 years since Watson and Crick first discovered the double-helix structure of DNA. About thirty thousand genes out of 3 billion nucleotides in a genome define every human being uniquely (e.g. hair colour, eye colour, etc.) and define some genetic diseases such as cystic fibrosis. Genome information can give insight into the potential risk of diseases such as heart attacks, diabetes, Alzheimer and other chronic conditions. Consequently, a new breed of biotechnology companies has emerged launching personalized DNA tests so that individuals could test for the genetic risk of potential diseases. As the cost of sequencing the DNA of an individual drops from US$1 million to US$100,000 and to as little as $1,000 in the foreseeable future, the market for personalized DNA sequencing will expand rapidly. At the same time, research groups are paying biotechnology companies to sequence the DNA of all kinds of organisms, e.g. the rice genome in search of higher production yields, the bacteria genome in search of a more effective cure, and the orchid genome in search of more varieties and higher financial returns. DNA sequencing is no longer a pure research activity, but a multi-billion-dollar business. To sequence a genome, sequencing machines output billions of overlapping DNA fragments (known as reads) from the genome, but without information on how these reads link together to form the genome. Then, software is used to help combine these reads to form the genome. Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) technologies (e.g. Solexa and SOLID) can now produce reads of a DNA sequence much faster and cheaper than the traditional Sanger method, making effective sequencing software tools more important for sequence assembly. Without software tools, massive manpower would be needed to manually combine the billions of reads, thus increasing the overall cost for the sequencing task. Drawing from our past research experience in bioinformatics and recent work related to this area, we aim to develop more effective algorithms and software tools for genome assembly. Apart from academic contributions, this project will also benefit biotechnology companies and bioinformatics service providers with further reductions in the cost of DNA sequencing for emerging sequencing-related applications such as metagenomics. 約六十年前 Watson 和 Crick 首先發現了DNA 的雙螺旋結構。目前的研究表明，人體內包含有大約三萬條基因，這些基因由三十億個堿基對所組成。正是這三萬條基因唯一確定了每個人的特征，包括頭發顏色，眼睛顏色，等等，這些基因也確定了患某種疾病風險的高低，比如囊腫性纖維化。 基因組信息能夠幫助我們了解患某些慢性疾病，比如心臟病、糖尿病、老年癡呆癥，的潛在風險。由於基因技術有著巨大的市場需求，進行DNA 測試的生物技術公司不斷湧現，DNA 測序的代價也隨之不斷降低。比如最初對一個人進行 DNA 測試的花費大約是一百萬美元，目前已經降至了十萬美元，在可預見的將來預計可以進一步降至一千美元。隨之而來的是個人DNA 測序市場的日益龐大。同時，各個研究中心也在有目的的對一些特定機體進行測序與分析。比如，為了提高產量而對水稻基因進行研究；為了發現更有效的治療手段對某些細菌基因進行研究；為了得到更多的品種以及更高的經濟回報率，對蘭花基因進行研究。因此，基因研究已經不僅僅在學術上有著重大的理論價值，在實際中也是能夠產生巨大經濟效益的產業方向。 研究基因組測序的通用方法是：通過測序儀產生數以十億計相互重疊的 DNA 片段（reads），然而，我們並不知道這些 DNA 片段是如何拼接成基因組的，這就需要再通過基因拼接軟件的幫助來將這些DNA片段盡可能一致的拼接成原始基因組。 相對於傳統的基因測序技術，新一代基因測序技術（比如 Solexa 和 SOLID）可以更快，更廉價的產生 DNA 片段。如果沒有軟件工具的幫助，我們只能依賴於大量的人力來對數以十億計的 DNA 片段進行拼接，這將極大地增加基因測序的代價。因此，研發高效的基因測序軟件工具對於基因組拼接具有非常重要的作用。 基於我們在生物信息學上的以往研究經驗和近期研究工作，我們擬針對基因組拼接問題設計開發高效的算法和軟件工具。除了學術上的貢獻，本項目還將有助於生物技術公司和生物信息服務提供商進一步降低在一些測序相關應用（比如宏基因組）中 DNA 測序的代價。

711212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
711212.value: 通過量子阱應變弛豫產生寬波帶的發光二極管

711212.label: Project Objectives
711212.value: Investigation of strain-relaxation mechanism in InGaN/GaN QW nanostructures: With the aid of high resolution strain mapping using Raman spectroscopy and emission mapping using near-field scanning microscopy (NSOM), the mechanisms for strain relaxation will be studied. The relations between strain/ emission and ion penetration/ damage of nanostructures will be determined, with the target of developing a “core-crust” model to explain the phenomenon. The model will assist with prediction of optical properties of nanostructures, and thus design of devices based on nanostructures. Design of nano-LED for broadband emission: Tapping on the strain relaxation properties of nano-pillars as determined and quantified from objective 1, a nano-LED can be designed containing an array of nano-pillars of different sizes distributed over the entire emission area of an LED chip. Since each pillar emits at a different wavelength according to its diameter, the overall emission spectral characteristics of the device is a combination of individual spectrum, giving rise to broadband emission. The spectral shape can be tailored for different shades of white emission, by controlling the distribution of the differently sized nano-pillars. Realization of a single-chip phosphor-free white-light LED: The key lies with the fabrication of the non-uniformly sized nano-pillars. To ensure practical adaptability of the approach, nanosphere lithography will be employed, the challenge being dispersing nanospheres of various dimensions over a large-area surface in mono-layer fashion, whilst maintaining close-packing between spheres. When this is done, the nano-pillars will be re-connected via a p-type contact layer by epitaxial lateral overgrowth, completing the device structure for electroluminescence.

711212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
711212.value: Solid-state lighting promises substantial energy savings over conventional electric lighting technologies. Light-emitting diodes (LEDs), unlike incandescent bulbs which emit mostly in the infrared and fluorescent lamps which natively generate ultraviolet light from a mercury discharge, are capable of emitting visible light directly sans color conversion. Coupled with high quantum efficiencies and long lifetimes, LEDs are ideal sources for general illumination. Nevertheless, present day white light LEDs still rely on color conversion. Yellow fluorescence from phosphors, combined blue light from the pump LED, is one common way of generating white light. The other method, making use of multiple chips, typically of the primary colors, generate white light with the aid of additional optics such as diffusers. In other words, there still isn’t a single-chip solution for producing white light without color conversion, perceived as the ultimate way of generating white light. Different approaches have been proposed for achieving this, including multiple junctions (blue and green) LEDs and nanowire LEDs just to name a few, each with its merits and shortcomings. Recently, various experimental findings of ours led to the conception of new idea for generating white light from a single-chip without the need for phosphors. Instead of exciting fluorescence of longer wavelength light from a short wavelength pump source, we propose the generation of shorter wavelength light from strain-relaxed nanostructures from a long-wavelength LED structure. The feasibility originates to the built-in strain in InGaN/GaN quantum well structures, the extent of which grows with increasing Indium content in the well, and this emission wavelength. As a result, starting with a highly-strain long wavelength emission wafer, the range of strain relaxation would be greatly increased, the degree of which depends on the dimension of the nanostructure. Our findings also indicate dependence on the process adopted for fabricating the nanostructures. Through a systematic study on strain relaxation by nano-structuring of InGaN quantum wells, the conditions for achieving the widest possible range of emission wavelengths from a single LED wafer can be determined. The proposed LED device will consist of nano-scale pillar structures with a continuum of diameters, patterned by nanosphere lithography and transferred by plasma etching, each emitting at a slightly different wavelength. Collectively, the active region will emit a broadband spectrum corresponding to white light, with spectral contents which can be adjusted by varying the nano-pillar dimensions and densities. 現今相對於傳統電氣照明技術，固態照明在節約能源方面顯示出極大的優勢。不同於發射光多為紅外光的白熾燈和經水銀放電而發光的熒光燈，發光二極管（LEDs）可以直接發射可見光而無需經過顏色轉換，加之高量子轉換效率和長使用壽命使得發光二極管成為理想的照明光源。 但就目前而言，白光LED仍然依賴於不同顏色光的轉換產生。例如最普遍的方法便是藍光LED發光加上一部分通過泵浦熒光粉產生的黃色熒光來產生白光﹔另一種方法便是利用多芯片技術，通過單色LED和光學元件（如柔光鏡）的匹配來產生白光。換句話說，現在始終沒有一種不通過顏色轉換來產生白光的單芯片解決方案。 為解決這個問題，人們提出了不同的方法。例如多PN結LEDs（藍光和綠光）、納米線LEDs等等，這些方法各有優劣。目前，總結了我們之前相關的實驗結果，我們提出了一個不通過熒光粉轉換而產生白光的單芯片解決方案。具體如下: 我們提出在長波LED上可以通過納米結構的應變弛豫而得到短波進而疊加的方法，這樣的長短波疊加取代了長波通過短波泵浦源激發而得到的方式。它的可行性起源於銦氮化鎵/氮化鎵（InGaN/GaN）量子阱的內部應力效應。量子阱的內部應力隨著銦含量的增加而變強，隨之導致放射光的紅移。所以，有著強應力的長波LED晶片，應變弛豫的范圍應該相當寬，這個度量將通過納米結構的尺寸來精確控制。我們的這個發現同樣依賴於之前納米結構的制備過程。 通過系統研究納米結構對量子阱應變弛豫的機理，單LED芯片可以發射最大可能寬波帶光的條件可以最終被確定。這個LED裝置將通過納米球刻蝕或等離子體刻蝕的方式產生包含一系列不同納米尺寸的圓柱結構，這些結構通過不同應變弛豫程度將發射不同波長的光。最終有源區將會發射相當於白光的寬波帶光譜，而且這個寬波帶光譜可以通過調節納米圓柱尺寸和密度來達到最佳效果。

711212.label: Realisation of objectives
711212.value: The 3 objectives have not only been met but exceeded. For the first objective, the complete mechanism of strain relaxation has been discovered through high-resolution near-field scanning microscopy. This is supported by Molecular Dynamics Simulations. It was discovered that the strain relaxation mechanism depended on only on dimensions of the nanostructures, but also strongly on the starting material itself. The strain relaxation mechanism depends on the emission wavelength (or Indium concentrations) of the InGaN/GaN quantum wells, which has not be reported in the literature before. For the second objective, the nano-LED has been successfully designed, based on understanding of the strain relaxation mechanism. The process flow for the device fabrication has also been developed. Both nanosphere lithography and electron beam lithography are employed for the patterning of the designed nanostructures. The third objective regarding realization of a single-chip phosphor-free white light LED has also been achieved. The nano-LED has been fabricated according to the process flow developed in objective 2. The LED consist of an array of differently-sized micro and nano pillars, each emitting at a different wavelength to generate a polychromatic spectrum whose continuous broadband spectrum is characterized by CIE coordinates of (0.39, 0.47) and color rendering index of 41. The work has been reported in ACS Photonics, a high impact journal in the field of photonics.

711212.label: Major findings and research outcome
711212.value: Through investigative studies on the strain relaxation mechanisms in InGaN/GaN quantum wells, it was discovered that, contrary to common belief, strain relaxation depended on not just on dimensions of the nanostructures, but also on the Indium content of the quantum wells, as well as the strain of the lattice mismatch. Through very precise nano-scale near-field optical spectroscopy, better understanding of the strain relaxation mechanism has been achieved. Lattice parameters deduced from calibrated TEM diffraction patterns verified the change in strain at the edge with respect to Indium composition. It was then demonstrated the change in strain relaxation mechanism with the Indium content of MQWs using molecular dynamics simulations. DFT calculations comparing the potential profiles of strained and relaxed GaN/InGaN/GaN concurs with the experimental observations, that the strain-induced change in QCSE caused a shift in band gap energy of the Quantum Wells. Based on these findings, a monolithic non-phosphor polychromatic light-emitting diode structure comprising a combination of high-density micro-structured and nano-structured InGaN-GaN quantum wells is proposed and demonstrated. Polychromatic emission is realized by taking advantage of the low-dimensional-induced strain-relaxation effect, combining light emitted from strain-relaxed nano-tips at wavelengths shorter than the as-grown by as much as 50 nm with longer-wavelength light emitted from the larger unscathed microdisks. The localized emission characteristics have been characterized by spatially-resolved near-field photoluminescence spectroscopy which allowed both the PL signal and spectrum from individual nano-tips to be optically-resolved and distinguished from emission at the larger-dimensioned regions. The far-field optical properties are evaluated through room-temperature micro-photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, from which PL emission with spectral widths of about 104 nm across a continuous band is observed by fabricating the micro/nano-structures on high In concentration strained InGaN-GaN quantum wells that emit at center wavelengths of ~570 nm.

711212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
711212.value: Our work represents the first recognition of bi-directional strain-induced relative spectral shift at the edge of a micro-/nano- structure. This further leads to the possibility of strain induction in InGaN/GaN quantum wells, a process that will give rise to spectral red-shifting, a phenomenon that has never been reported before to the best of our knowledge. A proposal has been submitted to GRF in order to allow us to explore this phenomenon further.

711212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
711212.value: It is a common agreement that when III-nitride quantum well based light-emitting structure is sized down to micro- or nano- scale, there would be a blue shift in light emission due to strain relaxation of the quantum wells at the sidewall of the structure. However, using Scanning Near-field Optical Spectroscopy (SNOS) that collects near-field PL spectra mapping with sub-diffraction resolution, we are able to detect a change in spectral shift distribution with a change in the lattice mismatch strain existing in the quantum wells. Making use of InGaN/GaN quantum well based micropillars with different Indium composition, we demonstrate that the relative spectral shift at the edge of a micropillar changes from blue-shift to red-shift as Indium composition decreases. This dependency suggests that there is a change in strain relaxation mechanism in micropillars with Indium composition. Furthermore, a monolithic phosphor-free broadband LED has been realized, relying on the concept of strain-induced spectral blue-shifting. The LED consist of an array of differently-sized micro and nano pillars, each emitting at a different wavelength to generate a polychromatic spectrum whose continuous broadband spectrum is characterized by CIE coordinates of (0.39, 0.47) and color rendering index of 41.

711612.label: Project Title(Chinese)
711612.value: 等離子對有機太陽能電池電特性的影響

711612.label: Co - Investigator(s)
711612.value: Prof Chew, Weng Cho Prof Hou, Jianhui

711612.label: Project Objectives
711612.value: Building models for physically understanding electrical properties of plasmonic OSCs An electrical model will be developed by solving 2D and 3D semiconductor equations with the consideration of metallic/organic interface effects and properties of polymer blends including exciton dissociation, bimolecular recombination, etc. Then, by integrating the optical model (developed under grant#HKU712010E) and electrical model, the multiphysics model for OSCs incorporating with arbitrary 2D and 3D metallic nanostructures will be developed. Studying interface recombination/injection between metal and polymer The important mechanism of interface recombination/injection between metal and polymer can be investigated experimentally and theoretically through incorporating metallic NPs into a polymer active layer. By appropriately designing device structures, the dark current which strongly depends on the metallic/organic interface will be studied. According to the recombination/injection model by Scott and Malliaras, the dark current will be affected by the barrier height (between polymer and metallic NPs) and built-in electric field. The roles of barrier height and built-in electric field on the interface recombination/injection mechanism will be studied by changing functional groups and concentration of metallic NPs. The measured dark current-density (J)- voltage (V) characteristics will be analyzed with theoretical results for understanding the physics and evaluating the characteristic parameters of the model. Investigating the effects of non-uniform exciton generation in plasmonic nanostructures With the understanding of PR mechanism in active layer and the spectral overlap engineering between PR and polymer absorption-band from our work (grant#HKU712010E), the guideline to maximize PR enhanced exciton generation (due to the enhanced absorption) will be explored. Since PR produces regionally-concentrated near-field in the active layer, a non-uniform exciton generation will occur. The recombination loss will change due to the non-uniform exciton generation and thus will be theoretically and experimentally investigated. Meanwhile, it is possible that SCLC will be present due to the PR-induced non-uniform carrier formation and unbalance carrier mobilities of typical polymers. SCLC effects can be characterized by the slope of J-V curve and light-intensity dependent short-circuit current. We will first study localized PR (LPR) devices through incorporating metallic NPs into OSCs. We will investigate how recombination loss and SCLC affect the electrical properties of OSCs with different parameters (e.g. active layer thickness, polymer mobility, and metallic NP location in device structures). In the meantime, we will study the change of OSC electrical properties due to surface PRs (SPRs) through metallic grating nanostructures with different grating parameters (including grating period and depth), metals and device architectures. Optimizing the electrical and optical properties of plasmonic OSCs With our knowledge on the optical properties (grant#HKU712010E), we will optimize the electrical and optical properties through combining the metallic NPs and nanogratings for “double” plasmonic nanostructures (including both LPR and SPR) in single-unit OSCs. We will study the metallic nanostructure material (Ag, Au, etc), concentration, location and surface functional group of metallic NPs, metallic nanograting geometry, as well as thickness and carrier mobility of polymers in active layer for realizing practical plasmonic OSCs. Besides commercially available materials, we will investigate various polymers from Prof. Jianhui Hou (Co-I of this proposal) for optimizing device performances. *** Note: In order to show our capability to manage the project, we have already started to work on Objective 1 and obtained some preliminary results as discussed in “Research Plan and Methodology”.

711612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
711612.value: As one of the promising candidates for photovoltaic applications, organic solar cells (OSCs) have drawn considerable attention recently. Many organic semiconductors exhibit very high absorption coefficient, making them promising for photovoltaic devices. However, the short lifetime and diffusion length of excitons result in ultrathin-active-layer configuration (typically few hundreds nanometers) in OSCs. The configuration limits the light absorption efficiency, and thereby the power conversion efficiency. Having unique features of tunable resonance and unprecedented near-field concentration around metallic nanostructures, plasmonics is an enabling technique for light manipulation and management. Although various optical designs and physical mechanisms have been studied both experimentally and theoretically to improve the optical absorption of OSCs by incorporating metallic nanostructures, the effects of plasmonic nanostructures on the electrical properties of OSCs are still unclear. On one hand, incorporating metallic nanostructures strongly affects the electrical performance of OSCs (see “Background of research”). On the other hand, most previous theoretical works mainly focus on the optical properties of plasmonic OSCs, e.g. light trapping, absorption enhancement, etc. Although the improvement of electrical parameters such as fill factor and open-circuit voltage (which cannot be explained by the enhanced light absorption) has been experimentally reported, the physics of the improvement is still not studied in detail. It is highly desirable to study the changes of OSC electrical properties induced by plasmonic nanostructures and their physics, which will open a new way to design high-performance photovoltaic devices and explore novel functionalities of plasmonic nanodevices. The challenges in executing the project lie at: (1) developing advanced optical and electrical models for physical understanding; (2) designing conclusive device configurations and fabrication approaches; (3) bridging optical and electrical physics of plasmonic OSCs. In this proposal, firstly, a classical and efficient multiphysics model (integrated optical and electrical model) for OSCs incorporated with arbitrary 2D and 3D metallic nanostructures (gratings, nanoparticles (NPs), etc.) which cannot be found in literatures will be developed for understanding device physics. Secondly, in order to carefully clarify and address the change of electrical properties due to plasmonic nanostructures, conclusive device structures will be proposed, fabricated and investigated. Thirdly, the experimental and theoretical analysis of the changes of electrical properties for the physical understanding of plasmonic OSCs will be conducted. Together with the investigation of optical properties of plasmonic OSCs funded previously (“General Research Fund” #HKU712010E), our work can contribute to the multiphysics insights and to the optical and electrical optimization of plasmonic OSC performances. 作為光伏應用的候選太陽能電池之一，有機太陽能電池最近引起了極大的關注。許多有機半導體材料具有非常高的吸收係數，使他們成為有前途的光伏器件。然而，激子短的壽命和擴散長度使有機太陽能電池層結構非常薄（通常為幾百納米）。配置限制了光吸收效率和功率轉換效率。具有獨特功能的可調式共振和前所未有的周圍金屬納米結構的近場濃度，表面等離子體光操作和管理是一個有利的技術。 雖然通過將金屬納米結構以改善光學吸收有機太陽能電池的各種光學設計和物理機制已經在實驗和理論上有研究，等離子對有機太陽能電池電特性的影響目前仍不清楚。一方面，等離子對有機太陽能電池電特性性能有強烈影響。另一方面，以往大多數理論著作主要集中在等離子的光學性質如導光捕集，吸收增強等，雖然電特性參數，如填充係數和開路電壓（它不能被解釋由增強的光吸收）的改善已被實驗報導，其改善的物理仍然沒有詳細研究了。 等離子對有機太陽能電池電特性的影響和物理的研究將打開一個新的方法來設計高性能的光電器件和探索新的功能。在執行項目所面臨的挑戰：（1）開發先進的光學和電學模型對物理的理解;（2）設計確鑿的設備配置和製造方法（3）連接等離子有機太陽能電池的光學和電學物理。在此項目，首先，建設為經典的，高效的多物理場模型（集成光學和電學模型），多物理有機太陽能電池的任意二維和三維金屬納米結構（光柵，納米粒子（納米）等）還沒有文獻報告，我們將發展和了解其器件物理。其次，為了認真澄清和解決由於等離子米結構的電特性能變化，決定性的器件結構將被提出，製造和研究。第三，進行物理電特性變化的實驗和理論分析來了解等離子有機太陽能電池。我們的工作可以促進多物理的見解和優化的光學和電學上離子有機太陽能電池電的功能。

711612.label: Realisation of objectives
711612.value: For Objective 1, we have completed the tasks. In the mid-team report (01 Jan 2013 to 31 Mar 20140, we built 2D and 3D models and used it to study different structures such as metallic dipole nanoantenna with the electrically conductive nanoscale layer of grapheme [Opt. Express, 21, 31824, 2013]. In addition, by using our universal eigenvalue analysis in the model of 2D grating, we observed abnormal large group velocity at the plasmonic band edge [Opt. Lett., 39, 158-161 2014]. We also tried to reduce the electron-extraction barrier effects on active layer and the carrier extraction layer systems for improving the performance of organic devices [Organ. Electron., 14, 457, 2013]. In this period of work (1 April 2014, to 31 Dec 2015), we further extend our model to include the exciton delocalization which is important for understanding the dissociation of photogenerated exciton into electrons and holes in organic active layer before extraction [J. Appl. Phys., 120, 213101, 2016.]. Then, we extend our previous model which only study the plasmonic properties of periodic nanostructures to hybrid periodic and random nanostructures [Nanoscale, 7, 16798, 2015.]. Consequently, our models can now comprehensively study plasmonic effects on organic solar cells (OSCs) with a combination of periodic and random plasmonic nanostructures. Besides, the dissociation of the enhanced (due to plasmonic optical effects) photogenerated excitons will be modelled in details. For objective 2, we have fulfilled the targets. In the last report, we developed the low temperature metal oxide based carrier transport materials which would significantly modify the barrier height and built-in electric field of the organic device for understanding the physics and improving the device characteristics parameters [Adv. Mat., 25, 2051, 2013.]. We found that metal nanoparticle would introduce carrier accumulation effects in the organic device [Energy Environ. Sci., 6, pp.3372 – 3379, 2013], favor the electrical conduction [J. Mater. Chem. A, 1, pp.6614-6621, 2013.]. We also observed that metal grid system could improve the collection of carrier [Appl. Phys. Lett., 102, 113303, 201]. In this period of time, we modify the metal nanoparticles with ligand and without ligand and incorporate into polymers to study the effects [IEEE J. Selected Topics Quant. Elect., DOI: 10.1109/JSTQE.2015.2442679.]. We find that the interfacial ligand can help to disperse the metal nanoparticles in polymer and reduce the quenching. To make comparison, we also develop solution-processed metal oxides [Small, 12, 416, 2016, Adv. Mat., 27, 2930, 2015, Light: Sci. & Applications, 4, e273, 2015.] and study the effects of the metal nanoparticles incorporated in the metal oxide based carrier transport layer on device performances [Progress In Electromagnetics Research, 146, 25-46, 2014, Small, 12, pp.416–431, 2016.]. Differently, in carrier transport layer, the metal nanoparticles will promote the hot carrier effects, increase the interfacial area and thus the electrical conduction but not the optical absorption for photocarrier generation. The understanding is very important for using the metal nanoparticles in optimizing the performance in objective 4. For objective 3, we finish the task successfully. In the last report, we investigated the effects of the regionally-concentrated near-field from the surface plasmonic resonances from a 3D metal nano-grating structure on the organic active layers [Appl. Phys. Lett., 102, 153304, 2013.]. We also found that the workfunction (and the potential barrier) can be modified by introducing metal nanoparticles into the metal systems [ACS Nano, 7, 1740, 2013]. In this period of time, we have introduced the plasmonic metal nanostructures in different layers of OSCs including new class of macro-periodic and micro-random metallic nanostructures [Scientific Reports, 5, 7876, 2015.] and integrated metal nanoparticle and nanowire system [ACS Nano, 8, 10980, 2014.] as the electrodes and study the distribution of near and far field of the nanostructures which will affect the spatial uniformity of the exciton generation. We also incorporate metal nanostructure in different region of polymer active layers [Scientific Reports, 5, 8525, 2015, Scientific Reports, 4, 6236, 2014.]. Distinctively, through incorporating metal nanostructures in the region of polymer active layer near to the anode, we demonstrate a new concept of plasmonic-electrical concept of plasmonically induced photocarriers redistribution in experiment and described in detail theoretically. The plasmonic-electrical effect can shorten the transport path of typical low-mobility holes and thus achieve space charge limit breaking in organic semiconductors. The work can open a new degree of freedom to design emerging plasmonic optoelectronic devices. Besides electrodes and active layer, we also demonstrate a new hybrid structure of metal/nanoparticle/dielectric nanostructure to enhanced the in-coupling of light into OSC to improve device performance [Nano Energy, 17, 187, 2015.]. In objective 4, we have optimized both the optical and electrical properties of plasmonic OSCs. In last report, we studied the broaden absorption enhancement of organic solar cells by introducing interstitial lattice patterned metal nanoparticles [Appl. Phys. Lett., 102, 251112 (4pp), 2013]. We also incorporated different shapes of metal nanostructures into the organic active layer of solar cells which would simultaneously improve both electrical and optical properties of OSCs [Adv. Funct. Mat., 23, 2728, 2013]. Finally, the device performance of OSCs was improved to over 8.7% [Adv. Funct. Mat., 23, 4255, 2013] In this period of time, we optimize OSCs by using various plasmonic effects including optical and electrical effects. We simultaneously incorporate Au nanograting structures at anode, Au nanoparticles in active layer and carrier transport layer to improve the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of OSCs from 7.62% to 9.62% [Adv. Opt. Mat. 3, 1220, 2015.] We also describe the plasmonic effects in details [Adv. Mat., 2014, 26, 5368, 2014.]. In the meantime, we optimize device performance by introducing tandem solar cell structures [Adv. Energy Mat., 5, 1500631, 2015, Nano Energy, 21, 123, 2016.], modifying the interfacial layer [Adv. Opt. Mat., 2, 1082, 2014.] and incorporating the polymers from Co-I (Prof. Jianhui Hou) of this proposal [Adv. Mat. Interface, 2, 1500324, 2015.] and other collaborators [Adv. Funct. Mat., 24, 6540, 2014.]. Consequently, besides using our plasmonic nanostructures, we also study the polymer active materials and different device structures to optimizing the device structure. By the time of completion of the project, apart from understanding the fundamental physics, we have proposed new device structures and achieved plasmonic OSCs with PCE of 9.62%. In our recent results, we have already achieved PCE of about 10.5% which has been accepted for publication in Small. Objective 5 of the proposal points out that by the time we prepared the proposal, we had started the project and obtained some preliminary results to support the project. In the 3-year project, we have been carefully monitoring the progress for achieving academic and research merits. The results of our work have been published in high impact journals as described later. Some of our publications have been selected as cover issues such as [e.g., Chem. Comm., 50, 11984, 2014; Adv. Opt. Mat., 3, 1220, 2015; Adv Function. Mat., 25, 4211, 2015; Adv. Energy Mat., 5, 1500631, 2015; and IEEE J. Selected Topics Quant. Elect., DOI: 10.1109/JSTQE.2015.2442679.] and highlighted by journals [e.g., Adv. Energy Mat., 5, 1500631, 2015 as research news in MaterialsViewsChina.com published by Wiley.]. It should be noted that the publications are supported by the research grants which have been acknowledged in the publications.

711612.label: Major findings and research outcome
711612.value: While the optical effects of plasmonic metal nanostructures on improving the photogeneration of excitons and thus the current of OSCs have been well studied, the electrical effects of plasmonic metal nanostructures on OSCs are relatively less studied and their understanding are not clear. In this project, we experimentally and theoretically demonstrate that 1. Plasmonic metal nanostructures [6,7,10, 13, 18, 19, 25, 27] completely embedded in carrier transport layers (CTLs) [11,17, 23, 26, 29] can improve the device performances by hot carrier effects [9], charge accumulation effects [4], increased interfacial area between CTL and active layer and thus improvement the carrier extraction from active layer to electrode and thus improve the device performance. 2. For the plasmonic metal nanostructures interacted with the active layer directly, we find that with a proper design of the plasmonic metal nanostructure in the active layer, the plasmonic nanostructures can shorten the transport path of low-mobility carrier (hole) to anode and fundamentally break the space charge limit of organic semiconductors, which is an intrinsic inherent property of typical organic semiconductors [16, 24, 28]. 3. With the understanding of the electrical effects of plasmonic metal nanostructures, we simultaneous introduces multiple nanostructures in OSCs to optimize the electrical and optical properties of OSCs [22, 30, 31]. Together with the study of different polymer materials [1, 20, 33], the optimized PCE reaches 9.62% while the optimized control device is 7.62% (enhanced by about 26%) [22]. In fact, in our recent studies, by enhancing both electrical and optical properties, we have experimentally and theoretically demonstrated PCE of 10.5%.

711612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
711612.value: For the future development and practical applications of the plasmonic OSCs, it would be good to study: 1. Large area devices, and 2. Stability of devices. Particularly, the change of device performances in OSCs with and without plasmonic nanostructures shall be investigated for optimizing the plasmonic OSCs.

711612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
711612.value: Organic solar cells (OSCs) have been widely investigated for the next generation of large area, low cost and flexible photovoltaic devices. However, most of the polymer active layer of OSCs is only about 100 to 300nm thickness. In order to increase the optical absorption of OSCs, plasmonic metal nanostructure have been incorporated into OSCs to improve light absorption. However, the effects of plasmonic metal nanostructures on the electrical properties of OSCs are still not well understood. In this project, we experimentally and theoretically demonstrate that the plasmonic metal nanostructure can be used to improve the extraction of photogenerated carriers from active layer to electrode by the effects of hot carriers and carrier accumulation induced by plasmonic metal nanostructures embedded in carrier transport layers. Meanwhile, by incorporating plasmonic nanostructures in the proper region of active layer, we can break the fundamental space charge limit of organic semiconductor materials and thus better balance the electron and hole conduction in the active layer. By introducing and optimizing multiple plasmonic metal nanostructures in different layers and regions of OSCs, we have achieved power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 9.62% with 26% enhancement in this project while our latest reported PCE can reach 10.5%.

712112.label: Project Title(Chinese)
712112.value: 基于RFID协同制造云服务平台

712112.label: Project Objectives
712112.value: To innovate a solution to “three-high-problems” widely suffered by RFID manufacturing applications using novel concept of Product Service System (PSS) and advanced cloud/ubiquitous computing technologies. To innovate a scalable RFID-Gateway hardware and software that not only meets technical requirements of typical manufacturing applications but also facilitates shared Product-Service-System (PSS). To establish common services shared by users to search and configure smart object and gateway PSS according to application requirements. To develop a testbed for demonstrating how and how well the proposed framework works to reduce total cost, technical risk and difficulties through systematical sharing of services.

712112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
712112.value: Over the last 5 years the PI has built up a strong research team at HKU on RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) manufacturing applications with substantial supports (over HK$12M) from Hong Kong government funding bodies and industrial collaborators. The developments have been crystalized into a prototype AUTOM platform for RFID-enabled real-time manufacturing. AUTOM facilities have partially been deployed successfully for daily operations within a few industrial collaborators. Substantial benefits have been reported on RFID-enabled real-time traceability and visibility, including faster response time to market, balanced production plans / schedules, stabilized labour and material flows, reduced inventories, optimized space/resource/operator utilization, low scrap and rework, improved productivity, and records for continuous process improvement. However, MANUFACTURERS ARE FACED WITH “THREE HIGH PROBLEMS” (namely, HIGH COST, HIGH RISK AND HIGH LEVEL OF TECHNICAL SKILLS) ASSOCIATED WITH RFID MANUFACTURING SOLUTIONS. These problems have slowed down the progress for manufacturers to adopt RFID solutions. If such “three high problems” are not successfully tackled, large-scale industrial adoption is unlikely to take place. One of the main reasons causing the so-called “three high problems” is due to the fact that almost all RFID manufacturing solutions have been primarily designed and developed for separate applications in individual manufacturers who have to bear high costs, risks and technical skills. This project proposes to solve “three high problems” through two BREAKTHROUGH INNOVATIONS. One significant innovation is to equip our previously developed AUTOM with an emerging business model of Product Service System (PSS) so that PSS-oriented AUTOM facilities can be easily maintained within an industrial park/alliance and shared among member enterprises. The other technical innovation is to elevate AUTOM facilities with cloud and ubiquitous computing technologies so that cloud-based AUTOM facilities work truly in a PSS-oriented fashion. The project pioneers to address technical challenges in realizing PSS-oriented cloud-based AUTOM for RFID-enabled real-time collaborative manufacturing. The cloud-based AUTOM platform solves the “three high problems” through a major shift from individual investments in RFID devices and skills to common RFID-enabled visibility and traceability services shared among multiple members of an industrial alliance. This PSS-oriented sharing approach substantially reduces the start-up investment costs, reduces the level of required specialist skills, speeds up installation processes and streamlines maintenance services, and improves success factors of RFID adoption. 在过去的五年里，项目负责人在香港大学建立了一支研究团队对RFID（Radio Frequency Identification，无线射频识别）在制造业的应用进行研究。在研究与实践的基础上，为实现基于RFID的实时制造，建立了AUTOM平台的原型并在一些合作企业的日常生产活动中得到了实际的应用。这些企业也从RFID的实时可跟踪性与可见性中获得了大量的益处，包括对市场的快速反应，平衡的生产计划和调度，稳定的劳动力和物流，缩减的库存，优化的空间、资源和操作人员的使用，较低的报废率和返工率，较高的生产效率以及可以给未来的持续改进提供参考的生产记录等等。然而，制造商在应用RFID解决方案的过程中，却面临着“三高”问题（分别是高投入，高风险和高技术瓶颈）。这些问题减缓了企业应用RFID解决方案的进程。如果“三高”问题不能够成功的解决，那么RFID技术的大规模工业应用将很难实现。 造成“三高”问题的一个非常重要的原因就是几乎所有的RFID解决方案都是针对不同制造商的不同应用而专门进行设计和实现的，这样就使得每一个制造商都要承担高投入、高风险和高技术瓶颈。该项目提出从两个突破点来解决“三高”问题。一个重要的突破点就是使用新兴的商业模式PSS来对我们之前的AUTOM设施进行改进，使得面向PSS的AUTOM可以方便的在工业园区进行部署和维护，并且可以被其中的多个企业所使用。另外一个突破点是使用云和普适计算的概念和技术来对AUTOM进行改进，从而使得基于云的AUTOM平台可以真正实现面向PSS模式。在项目前期，研究人员将会对该平台实现的技术难点和挑战进行定位和研究。 基于云的AUTOM平台通过一个“转换”来解决“三高”问题，即将每个企业所投入的RFID设备以及技术转换成为可以被企业联盟中多个企业所分享使用的通用的基于RFID的可跟踪和可见的服务。这个面向PSS的分享方法极大的降低了启动阶段的资金投入，以及所需要技术门槛，加速了部署的过程并简化了维护的程序，最终增加了RFID成功应用的砝码。

712112.label: Major findings and research outcome
712112.value: Paper "Physical assets and service sharing for IoT-enabled Supply Hub in Industrial Park (SHIP)" proposes an IoT-enabled SHIP for enhancing the effectiveness and efficiency of sharing physical assets and services. First, an overview of IoT-enabled SHIP is presented by highlighting three key components: Physical Asset Service System (PASS), information infrastructure, and decision support system. PASS is introduced as a new business model for supporting the sharing approach. Second, the relevant state-of-the-art literature is reviewed by examining several representative pilot projects worldwide. Third, future research opportunities are discussed along five dimensions including IoT infrastructure, business models, decision models, synchronization mechanisms, and impact analysis. Research gaps are highlighted and key research questions worthy of further exploration are presented. It is hoped that this work is valuable and beneficial to researchers who wish to extend their research into this new and exciting area, and to identify new research opportunities. The paper "Reconfigurable Auto-ID Enabled Software as a Service (SaaS) Shell for Real-Time Fleet Management in Industrial Parks" presents a software service for manufacturers to share and manage their transport services provided by multiple fleets. This service-oriented fleet management shell encompasses a range of facilities that can be customized by manufacturers for fleet advanced planning and scheduling (FAPS). The paper "A MPN-based scheduling model for IoT-enabled hybrid flow shop manufacturing" introduces a manufacturing Petri Net-based scheduling model for IoT-enabled hybrid flow shop manufacturing. The proposed model switches the schedule of Token sequences in MPN to the trigger sequence of transition. Thus the real-time production behaviors in IoT-enabled manufacturing flow shops could be modelled. The paper "Big Data for supply chain management in the service and manufacturing sectors: Challenges, opportunities, and future perspectives" provides a discussion from analyzing current movements on the Big Data for SCM in service and manufacturing world-wide including North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific region. Current challenges, opportunities, and future perspectives such as data collection methods, data transmission, data storage, processing technologies for Big Data, Big Data-enabled decision-making models, as well as Big Data interpretation and application are highlighted. The paper "A Big Data Approach for Logistics Trajectory Discovery from RFID-enabled Production Data" proposes a holistic Big Data approach to excavate frequent trajectory from massive RFID-enabled shopfloor logistics data with several innovations highlighted. We are particularly pleased that the resulting research outcome could be used to support educational activities. Paper on "RFID-enabled learning supply chain" presents how the teaching and learning supports could be provided.

712112.value: We have identified some research challenges for further investigation. One of them is manufacturing synchronization. We have been working on a number of journal publications. In addition, we have also extended our research into other industrial sectors such as construction and logistics. We are very pleased to share that we were awarded one major ITF project in smart construction of around HK$10M. We are recently awarded another ITF project on smart ecommerce logistics of HK$12M. We expect to achieve some breakthroughs for practical applications.

712612.value: Develop a novel complete domain decomposition method that has a full band physical model and a full band numerical acceleration engine. 712612.label: Realisation of objectives
712612.value: We have achieved all objectives through extensive research activities and peer reviewed top tier journals in the computational electromagnetics society. 1. We have developed a new hierarchical relaxed equivalence source algorithm to handle broadband large-scale complex domain decomposition problems. It uses the new spherical surface to avoid singularity issues caused by conventional EPA method and eliminate the need for tap basis in solving large problems. 2. We have added the equivalence electric charge density and equivalence magnetic charge density into the EPA process to propose a new broadband EPA method. It properly handles the low frequency breakdown caused by the EM decoupling. 3. The new method employs the augmented EFIE scheme that is the first EPA method that is completely loop-tree free. 4. Employing the full band mixed-form fast multipole algorithm to accelerate the large scale computation, we developed the pseudospectral projection based on FFT to rotate the translation and aggregation operators. The resultant operations become very sparse. 5. All presented algorithms have been benchmarked through canonical and practical examples that went with publications and presentations on international journals and symposiums.

712612.label: Major findings and research outcome
712612.value: 1. To improve the working frequency range of principle algorithm (EPA), the new augmented-EPA (A-EPA) method is developed. Not only equivalent currents are used, but also equivalent charges. To avoid the loop-tree basis involved in the low frequency regime, the augmented EFIE operator is employed inside the EPA operator so that only conventional RWG basis and patch basis are employed. The developed new method shows that the low frequency breakdown of conventional EPA method has been properly solved by the newly proposed loop-tree free method [Ref.8.2, Ref.9.3]. To further enhance the near field calculation accuracy due to the field projection error, a new dual basis testing method is developed to enhance the field projection in the equivalence principle algorithm using the rotated CWBC basis [Ref.9.3]. 2. EPA is applied to broadband multi-scale structures efficiently due to the separation of circuit physics from wave physics. However, EPA will introduce tap basis functions that can deteriorate the conditioning of the resultant matrix system. Moreover, extending the EPA to a hierarchical algorithm numerically is difficult due to the tap basis functions. In the newly developed algorithm, we employ one-group-buffer scheme like FMA to maintain the continuities of surface currents without any tap basis functions. Moreover, we exploit meshless sampling schemes to evaluate the integral operators on the relaxed spherical equivalence surface (ES) to represent the relationships between ESs. The term “relaxed” refers that the spherical ES will not touch the internal primary sources. Hence, a hierarchical algorithm is straightforward to implement [Ref.8.1, Ref.9.2]. 3. To increase the bandwidth of the conventional fast multipole algorithm (FMA), the mixed-form fast multipole algorithm (MFFMA) is employed. However, MFFMA has the error control difficulties in the transition regions. In this project, the broadband accuracy of MFFMA is improved by applying rotation techniques. Two kinds of rotation methods are employed respectively. One is the coordinate system rotation technique. The other one is the pseudospectral projection based on FFT. Either of them has certain advantages depending on the number of multipoles. Through rotation, translation matrices become very sparse, which enables us to save the storage as well as the CPU time. Hence, we can increase the number of multipoles in the low frequency regime to shift up the transition region of MF-FMA. The overall accuracy is thereby improved significantly [Ref. 9.1]. 4. Other relevant achievements in this project are available in the attachment.

712612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
712612.value: 1. The hierarchical relaxed equivalence source algorithm we have developed broken several key bottlenecks of conventional EPA methods. It could be further improved to become a more general computing framework as the computational electromagnetics numerical engine. Its computational cost could be further improved by optimize the book keeping process. 2. Its extended application to the large scale signal integrity and power integrity will be an interesting extension in the future since it will come back to challenge the scale of the method itself. While it is applied to layered structures, the oct-tree based tree browsing process will not be optimized. Improved method that considers the special vertical coupling will be able to dramatically enhance the efficiency of the method. 3. The application of the proposed method on the cloud platform will be a good approach in the future. The cloud service has been progressing to a level that could possibly provide huge computing power to the scientific computing needs.

712612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
712612.value: Integral equation (IE) based domain decomposition method (DDM) is optimal to problems with open spaces and long mutual coupling distances, such as stealthy aircrafts, complex antenna systems, photonic band gap structures, and IC interconnects. In this project, the novel IE based full band domain decomposition methods are proposed. They have the following distinct technological features: (1) The proposed method not only provides the full band physical model, but also the full band numerical acceleration engine. (2) By introducing charge terms on equivalence surfaces, the new augmented equivalence principle algorithm will be completely loop-tree free at low frequencies. It will be further integrated with the high frequency equivalence principle algorithm dynamically to serve as the full band physical model. (3) Using the pseudospectral projection to rotate spherical harmonic functions, a new MFFMA will be developed to significantly improve the reliability, efficiency, and accuracy of the full band numerical engine. The proposed novel CEM methods can serve as general computational electromagnetics frameworks to solve multi-band antenna arrays, broadband radar scattering, photonic band gap structures, and complex EMC/EMI problems, etc. It prepares integral equation based CEM methods for distributive platforms such as the cloud computing.

712712.label: Project Objectives
712712.value: [CE] Our first objective is to investigate the role of taggers as a feature dimension in measuring tag similarity. We address three questions: (1) How to model tagger information in addition to tags and resources in semantic analysis? (2) How tagger information can improve the quality of semantic analysis in concept extraction? (3) Given that we are now handling three-dimensional information in taggers-tags-resources instead of the traditional two-dimensional data in tags-resources, will semantic analysis become much more expensive? What computational techniques can we devise to speed up the computations? [DTR] Our second objective is to study the diversified tag recommendation problem. We study how diversification is mathematically modeled and measured, how it is technically achieved, how it impacts people’s tagging behavior, and how it affects resource retrieval effectiveness. [Other applications] Our third objective is to apply our techniques on other applications. E.g., a by-product of the CE problem is a tagger-based tag-similarity measure. This tag-similarity measure can very well be used in tag recommendations. Also, techniques in DTR can be applied to suggest diversified queries in web-based query-recommendation systems.

712712.label: Realisation of objectives
712712.value: We conducted studies to address the three objectives of the projects, namely, (1) Concept Extraction [CE], (2) Diversified Tag Recommendation [DTR], and (3) Other applications [APP]. The studies are mainly carried out by literature reviews, systems and algorithms design, scientific experiments, and user studies. For Objective 1 ([CE]), we focused on the role of users of social tagging systems in how their behaviors/activities/tagging can be used to measure tag similarity, which eventually would lead to the construction of good-quality concept spaces in concept extraction. Our approach to realizing Objective 1 is documented in papers [3, 4, 5]. In [3] and [4], we study how many user-tagging operations are needed to annotate a resource such that the semantics of the resource are well described. The study was carried out using Amazon Mechanical Turk. We discovered two interesting characteristics of a resource’s tag quality, namely, “monotonicity” and “diminishing return”. With these observations, we devised approaches to estimate the number of tagging operations that are needed to well describe a resource (such as a web page, a photo, etc.). We have conducted a user study to illustrate how such estimates allow semantically rich tagging, which has immense impact on the measurement of tag similarity. Also, we show how a good tag similarity measure leads to very effective resource recommendation. In [5], we study how user information in a social tagging system can help to identify “expert users”. The reason why expert identification is important in such a system is that tags given by experts are typically more significant and accurate compared with causal users in the description of the concepts and semantics carried by resources. We apply techniques that are similar to “Topic Modeling” in nature but take into accounts other aspects of users such as location information to infer the significance of a user’s tags. Again, our results lead to more accurate tag similarity measures and thus better concept extraction methods. For Objective 2 [DTR], we have devised probabilistic methods to achieve diversified recommendation. We have implemented a prototype system based on the probabilistic methods. With the prototype, we have conducted an extensive user study. In the user study, we had 56 users judging the recommendations made by our system against those given by top search engines, such as Yahoo!, Bing, and Google. Our study shows that our prototype system is highly competitive against the commercial ones. In many cases, the recommendations made by our system were even better than the commercial search engines. Our results and approach to achieving Objective (2) is documented in [1]. We have also prepared an extended version of our work to be submitted to a top database journal. Besides tag recommendations, our probabilistic model can also be applied in other scenarios. For Objective 3 [APP], we have extended our study on diversified tag recommendation to other areas, such as resource recommendation, query recommendation, and natural-language question-answering systems. In these studies, we apply similar principle of tag recommendation and focus on the effectiveness of our approaches under different domains. Moreover, we have applied some of our techniques in understanding the semantics of heterogeneous information networks, which can be considered as more complex types of resources. We studied how the theory and knowledge obtained through our first two objectives can be put into actions. In particular, we applied our techniques in three research areas: (1) expert identification in social networks, (2) query processing on heterogeneous information networks, and (3) question-answer (QA) systems. Our work on expert identification has been published in ACM KDD [5]. In relation to expert identification, we also studied the impact of our techniques in natural language QA systems. While one of the original goals of our project is to be able to recommend keyword-based queries for web search engines, the current trend of knowledge base research is to be able to answer questions put in natural language sentences. There are two lines of research on such QA systems. One approach is the crowdsourcing/community-based approach (e.g., Stack Overflow). In such systems, a platform is developed on which a community of users contributes to answer questions put forward by other users. For such systems, our work in expert identification ([5]) is very useful since it helps to distinguish experts from the non-experts and thus to rank their answers. Moreover, our work on tag recommendations allows the system to semi-automatically assign tags to questions/answers. These tags provide semantics information of the questions and answers and facilitate QA searching. Another line of research on QA systems is to automatically answer natural language questions (such as services provided by Apple Siri and Google Now). These systems are usually empowered by massive knowledge bases (KBs). One popular approach is to first construct a “curated KB”, which is manually prepared, and then derive from it logical inferences to answer questions. Examples of curated KBs include Yago and Freebase. Due to the extensive labors required in constructing such curated KBs, these KBs are typically limited in scope. Their generality is also limited. To extend their applicability, there are recent works on building QA systems on “Open KBs”, which are knowledge bases that are automatically extracted from massive sources of unstructured text. Our work on concept extraction and tag recommendation find interesting applications in this area of research. For one, terms that are used in an open KB to describe a concept are typically very diverse. That necessitates the process of concept extraction. Moreover, there are often mismatches between the terms used in a question and those used to describe factoids in an open KB. That necessitates query paraphrasing. The latter issue can be solved using techniques similar to those we studied for diversified tag/query recommendation (DTR). Finally, a QA system generally retrieves multiple answers for a given query. Our techniques in DTR can also be used to rank the answers in the answer set. The results of our investigation on QA systems have been published in ACM CIKM 2015 [7]. As we have mentioned, many of the QA systems are empowered by massive curated KBs, such as Yago and Freebase. These KBs can be seen as a type of heterogeneous information networks (HINs). Our techniques in concept extraction can be applied to HINs, which contain complex semantics, to derive “class labels” of objects that appear in them. These class labels enrich the HINs and allow them to answer more questions. A common problem that existing curated KBs face is that much of the data is unlabeled. This is because labeling is mostly manually done. We studied various techniques for propagating tags/labels in a heterogeneous information network. On this research, we have published one conference paper [6] and have written another one, which is currently under review [8].

712712.label: Major findings and research outcome
712712.value: Our studies have resulted in eight papers [1-8], among which seven have been published [1-7] and one is currently under review [8]. Even though many of these publications are very recent, they have been cited 31 times. This project has also supported 5 graduate students. Three of these students (two MPhils and one PhD) have graduated. We summarize our contributions to the topics of research addressed in this project as follows: 1. We devised a probabilistic model to diversify search results of web search engines. We built a prototype search engine based on the probabilistic model. Though a user study, we showed that our system is highly competitive (and in some cases, outperforms) commercial search engines. 2. We devised a location-based model that takes into account resources (such as photos), their location of creation (such as lat-long coordinates) to disambiguate the semantics of tags. We applied our technique to improve the quality of resource recommendation in social tagging systems. 3. Through the Amazon Mechanical Turk platform, we studied the optimal strategy for assigning human intelligence tasks to workers that maximizes the quality of the taggings given to descriptive resources. 4. We devised a probabilistic model that identifies the experts in a social tagging system. Through these experts, we improve the semantics understanding of the tags that are assigned to resources on these systems. 5. We studied massive heterogeneous information networks and investigated how tags could be propagated effectively through objects on the networks to better describe the objects’ semantics. We have also applied our techniques in the design and implementation of natural-language question-answering systems that are powered by knowledge bases (which are heterogeneous information networks). Addition paper (not listed in Section 9) [8] Xiang Li, Ben Kao, Yudian Zheng, Zhipeng Huang: On Transductive Classification in Heterogeneous Information Networks, submitted to ACM KDD 2016.

712712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
712712.value: Our works provide a very effective tool for semantic analysis. This is reflected by the decent number of times our works have been cited by the research community. During the course of our investigation, we found that our works have interesting applications in the labeling of objects in heterogeneous information networks. Since massive knowledge bases (such as Yago and Freebase) are examples of such networks, our works naturally apply to knowledge-base systems. We are now focusing our studies on heterogeneous information network analysis and knowledge-based question-answering systems design. Two research postgraduate students of our research group are now researching on these two topics and have started publishing their findings in top DB and AI conferences.

712712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
712712.value: Web search engines, such as Google and Bing, have become the most convenient way for people to search for information. Users of search engines, however, are non-experts in formulating queries. For one thing, users are usually unfamiliar with the topics that they would like to query on, and for another, they may not be fluent in the language with which the information is written in. Users queries are often ill-formulated. Modern search engines recommend “alternative queries” that are likely to be better expressing the users’ search intents. To improve the quality of query recommendation, the search engines have to be equipped with the intelligence to understand the semantics of ill-formed user queries. This project proposes and evaluates various techniques in understanding information semantics with a focus on tagging information. The project extends the invented methods to applications other than web search engines. These applications include identifying experts in social networks, enhancing knowledge bases, and improving the quality of knowledge-based question-answering systems.

713112.value: 掃描全息系統中對動態目標的景深穩健延展與自動聚焦

713112.label: Project Objectives
713112.value: Our first objective is to develop and demonstrate robust identification of sections of interest for a complex dynamic object. This includes developing a suitable metric to identify the contributions of different sections to the hologram without explicitly reconstructing all the planes. We also seek to investigate coding of the depth information through novel designs of the two pupils, following the recent success of coded imaging in computational photography. Our second objective is to advance autofocusing and extended focused imaging using the computational techniques of inverse imaging. This includes modeling the imaging system and formulating the problem as an optimization, as well as developing computationally efficient algorithms. In particular, we seek to make use of sparsity in the object and parallelization in the reconstruction to accelerate the computations, paving the way for real-time focusing in the future. Our third objective is to advance the applicability of OSH and to enrich the arsenal of biological imaging. The development in this project will further enhance the appeal of holographic imaging for different applications, particularly in life science. With a prototype of OSH and the associated algorithms, we will seek to collaborate with colleagues to demonstrate the use of this modality to achieve imaging and tracking of specific objects in their field of interest. We believe that identifying and tackling the appropriate applications will drive further developments in the right directions.

713112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
713112.value: The past decade saw a transition from film photography to digital photography, which greatly facilitates different post-processing to allow the photographer to express himself or herself artistically. Holography is now following a similar trend. Digital holography permits direct computation on the acquired data, but what sets it apart from many other forms of photography and imaging is the ability to capture three-dimensional information simultaneously. With proper post-processing, one can view and analyze selected sections of an object. This has great potential for scientific applications, particularly in volumetric imaging, pattern recognition, and tracking. In this proposal, our focus is on a particular digital holography system called the optical scanning holography (OSH). We look into the scientific problem of having an object with details at several sections or depths, and we seek to develop algorithms that can robustly identify them and reconstruct those sections from the holographic data. There are two possibilities: (1) For extended focused imaging, the algorithm should put together focused parts from different sections in reconstructing a single two-dimensional image. This is akin to extended depth-of-field imaging for conventional photography. (2) For autofocusing, the algorithm should identify the section with the strongest signal, and seek to reconstruct at that plane while suppressing the contributions from other depths, which act as defocused noise. Our primary objective is to develop robust and efficient algorithms for both cases, and seek to quantify and improve their performances with various parameters such as the number of sections, the amount of noise, and the resolution of the digital holograms. We are also keen to establish their use in imaging dynamic objects, particularly biological specimens, which we believe will further help to establish OSH as an important form of biological imaging, especially noting its strength in fluorescent imaging that has been demonstrated in the past. Finally, through this project, our work can also contribute to educating optical engineers in Hong Kong, benefiting the growth of the technology sector in the region. 在過去的數十年，人們見證了從膠片攝影到數字攝影的發展和過渡，這一過程極大地解放了攝影師們表現其創作思路的能力。如今，全息攝影也走上了相似的發展軌跡。數字全息攝影的技術允許人們對獲取的數據進行直接的計算處理，而該技術最超然于其他攝影與成像技術之處，在於其同時采獲三維信息的能力。在恰當的後期處理幫助下，人們可以觀察和分析被攝物體的任意指定區域。這在許多科學應用中有重要的潛在價值，尤其將對容積成像、模式識別、以及標的追蹤等技術帶來幫助。 在本研究計劃書中，我們的側重點在于一項特定的全息攝影系統，名為光學掃描全息系統。我們著手于被攝物體具有多層細節的情況下成像的技術問題，在這種情況下，我們嘗試開發出妥當的算法以便能夠通過系統獲得的全息數據穩健地分辨出不同層面的信息并將之重構。在研究中有兩個可能的方向：（1），延展景深成像，我們的算法將不同層面的聚焦部份畫面綜合重構于一張單一的二位圖像中。這種形式類似于傳統攝影技術中的延展景深成像的應用。（2），自動聚焦，我們的算法將辨認出被攝物體內攜帶最強信息的層面，并在該層面準確地重構物體畫面，而在其他層面的信息將被視為焦外噪點予以抑制減弱。我們的基本目標是開發穩健高效的算法以滿足上述兩個方向的要求，然後嘗試量化及改進算法的性能，此性能將以各種客觀參數作為標準，如被攝物體層面的數量、噪點信息的強度、以及全息圖像的維度。我們將積極地將此技術改進應用到動態被攝物體上，尤其以生物樣本為重，我們相信這將進一步提高光學掃描全息技術在生物成像領域的重要性，而在過去該技術在螢光成像中的優良表現亦給與了我們更大的信心。而最終，我們會通過此項目為香港的光學工程師提供教育素材，并且使本地區技術領域的發展獲益。

713112.label: Realisation of objectives
713112.value: The three objectives of the project have been satisfactorily achieved. In developing and demonstrating robust identification of sections of interest in a complex dynamic object, we have devised several computational methods that help to push the optical scanning holography technology. For example, a method to suppress defocus noise using combined frame difference and connected component is shown to enhance image reconstruction robustness, the result of which is published in the high-impact Optics Letters journal. Meanwhile, a major technology development for this project is the design of autofocusing and extended focused imaging algorithms. The literature on these has not been abundant, but we break grounds in developing an analytic method based on Fourier transform properties and an iterative method based on entropy minimization, which are the bases of an invited paper at the Japan Society of Applied Physics and The Optical Society Joint Symposia, a proceedings paper at the OSA Topical Meeting in Digital Holography and Three-Dimensional Imaging, the premier conference on digital holography, and a journal paper in Applied Optics. With regards to advancing the applicability of optical scanning holography, we have built a functional system and collaborated with colleagues in biomedical engineering to investigate the performance need for different applications. In doing so, we have identified the resolution need for the holographic system, and sought to improve this using both system and computational enhancements. These include the invention of a double-detection method and configurable pupil coding, published in Applied Optics and Photonics Research, respectively, as well as the use of a spiral modulated point spread function, also published in Photonics Research. We have demonstrated these methods using fluorescent biological specimens, which demonstrates an important advantage of optical scanning holography in capturing images incoherently, making it one of the most suitable techniques for holographic biological microscopy.

713112.label: Major findings and research outcome
713112.value: In this project, we have significantly pushed the technology of scanning holographic microscopy, resulting in the publications of five journal papers and nine invited/contributed conference papers. They include the development of a computational imaging approach to optical scanning holography, which involves modification of the imaging system to code useful information and subsequent postprocessing to improve overall imaging performance; examples include the development of the double-detection method and the configurable pupil approach, published in the Applied Optics and Photonics Research journals, respectively, as well as in conferences such as the OSA Topical Meeting in Digital Holography and Three-Dimensional Imaging, the premier conference on digital holography. Compressed sensing approach has also been developed for optical scanning holography, forming the basis of two conference papers in the OSA Topical Meeting in Digital Holography and Three-Dimensional Imaging and the SPIE meeting on Real-time Photonic Measurements, Data Management, and Processing, as well as a forthcoming journal paper. Robust extension of imaging performance is another important dimension of the project, and we have demonstrated a novel technique for defocus noise suppression and edge extraction, which are the bases of an Optics Letters journal paper and a related conference paper. Meanwhile, we also devise a spiral modulated point spread function method for resolution enhancement, which is reported in Photonics Research journal and a conference paper in the OSA Topical Meeting in Digital Holography and Three-Dimensional Imaging. As for algorithms for autofocusing and extended focused imaging, we devise two new techniques, one being an analytic method based on Fourier transform properties, and another being an iterative method based on entropy minimization; these are subsequently published as a journal paper in Applied Optics, and presented as an invited paper at the Japan Society of Applied Physics and The Optical Society Joint Symposia, as well as a proceedings paper at the OSA Topical Meeting in Digital Holography and Three-Dimensional Imaging.

713112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
713112.value: This project has helped to push the technology in optical scanning holography, and establish it as a leading holographic imaging methodology for fluorescent microscopy. Several computational algorithms have been developed to enhance the imaging capability; going forward, there are several areas for potential development along the research we have conducted. One aspect is the continuous reduction of imaging duration. Through our exploration of sparsity-based method and compressed sensing, we have promising results showing how to reduce the data capture while maintaining or even enhancing the existing image resolution. This will be important for real-time or at least approaching real-time high resolution imaging. Another aspect is the subsequent computational image analysis. With a higher data volume, especially holographic data, machine learning techniques would start to play important roles in image understanding, which can help guide the imaging applications such as tracking or filtering.

713112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
713112.value: Digital holographic imaging is a means to record data about a volumetric object, which can subsequently be processed to show cross-sections of interest. This has applications in many imaging areas, including biological microscopy. This project pushes the technology for scanning holographic imaging through the development of computational algorithms, which includes increasing the imaging resolution, as well as methods for autofocusing and extended focused imaging. Together, these allow the users to have better visual appreciation of the object, making it a viable form of holographic microscopy for use in many biological applications.

713212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
713212.value: Building on the previous successful relevant investigations, this research project aims at developing a novel integrated air-conditioning system comprising a variable-speed ground-coupled heat pump system and a hybrid convective/radiant cooling system for energy-efficient year-round comfort air conditioning applications in sub-tropical and temperate regions. The integration will boost the overall energy efficiency of the system as compared to conventional designs without adversely affecting the microclimate due to direct heat transfer with the ambient air. The contributing factors to the enhanced system energy performance will not only be due to the superior energy efficiency of the ground-coupled heat pump but also the perfect matching of its operation with the actual load demand based on variable-speed control and the utilization of separate convective and radiant heat exchangers for handling the sensible and latent loads of the air to be conditioned. The consequent reduction in total energy consumption for the heat pump system as well as the water pump and air fan operation will be substantial. A comprehensive investigation using computer modelling and simulation will be carried out for a variable-speed ground-coupled heat pump system integrated with a chiller which is equipped with dual heat exchangers for interaction with the conditioned air in handling the sensible and latent loads separately. Both cooling and heating modes will be studied by employing normal and reverse cycle operations of the heat pump system for year-round system performance analysis and identification of energy saving potentials. Additionally, free cooling will be made available during low-load periods by direct circulation of water through the ground heat exchangers of the heat pump system and the radiant heat exchanger without operating the compressor when the ambient air conditions are appropriate in terms of temperature and enthalpy levels. A prototype integrated system will be designed and developed to demonstrate the practicality of the design concept as well as for gathering useful experimental operating data for detailed analyses and validation of the computer model established. It is envisaged that the successful outcome of this research project will make significant contributions to energy-efficient air conditioning system design for sub-tropical and temperate regions based on currently available technologies. In view of the high energy consumption levels imposed by air conditioning systems on buildings and in turn amongst all energy-consuming sectors on a global basis, the positive impact on energy conservation and environmental protection will also be highly significant. 本研究項目之目的是在於開發一種新型的集成空調系統，由變速地耦熱泵系統和混合對流/輻射供冷系統所組成，可於亞熱帶和溫帶地區，提供全年運作之高效節能舒適空調服務。相比傳統的設計，該組合將能提高系統的整體能源效率，而不會產生由於與周圍空氣的直接熱傳遞的原因，而影響周圍的小氣候。令系統的節能性能增強的因素不僅是由於地耦熱泵卓越的能源效率，實亦有賴其操作與實際負荷需求的完美配合，因利用變速控制和獨立的空氣對流和輻射換熱器處理，能有效處理空氣的顯熱和潛熱負荷。從而能夠減少熱泵系統及水泵和風扇的總能量消耗，將是十分的可觀。 研究項目將利用計算機模擬和仿真技術，進行全面探討變速地耦熱泵與配備了雙熱交換器的冷水機組，與空調系統中的顯熱和潛熱負荷所產生的互動情況。研究將包括採用正常和逆向操作的熱泵系統，作製冷和制熱模式的熱泵系統的全年系統性能分析和節能潛力識別的探討。此外，在低負載期間及在適當環境空氣條件下，將直接使用循環水通過熱泵系統，無須使用壓縮機，便可獲取免費冷卻效果。計劃包括原型集成系統的設計和開發，用以示範其實用性及收集有用的實驗操作數據，用以進行詳細分析，作建立計算機模型和驗證。

713212.label: Realisation of objectives
713212.value: The project objectives were in general achieved as planned with the minor exception of the use of a displacement ventilation system instead of radiant panels to interact with the ground-coupled heat pump system with borehole heat exchangers. This was due to the unsatisfactory results obtained based on the use of radiant panels, presumably on account of condensation problems arising from inadequate air-tightness of common building enclosures and high humidity level of the ambient environment. The use of a displacement ventilation system resolved the problem and provided good analysis results.
