713212.label: Major findings and research outcome
713212.value: A detailed parametric model for the novel ground-coupled heat pump system incorporating variable-speed modulation was developed using the Fortran programming language for use in the study of the system performance under different weather conditions. The variable-speed component model was a new self-developed TRNSYS component built based on a parameter estimation technique using the data of refrigerant flow rates and compressor power input for linking with the ground-coupled heat pump system. The adoption of the newly developed constant-polytropic-efficiency approach instead of relying on the conventional constant polytropic coefficient assumption demonstrated that a much improved fitting of the performance characteristics to the manufacturer’s data was achieved. Simplified explicit models for refrigerant coils were also developed to enable the effect of the refrigerant mass flow rate on the coil performance to be assessed more appropriately. The system model was applied to a multi-storey building for computer simulation study of system performance under different weather conditions. The climatic conditions of Hong Kong and Kunming in China were used to compare the effects for sub-tropical and temperate regions. An experimental borehole heat exchanger test rig was designed and built for investigating the heat transfer characteristics with the ground soil. The design of a prototype novel ground-coupled heat pump system was also completed and based on which an actual ground-coupled heat pump system with vertical borehole heat exchangers was made available for energy-saving performance analysis. The site location for the installation of the experimental system was chosen to be within the Stanley Ho Sports Centre in the University of Hong Kong. The year-round performance of the novel ground-coupled heat pump system by simulation showed that a substantial energy saving of nearly 23% was achieved compared to the conventional convective system despite rather high relative humidity level during peak-load period. The results obtained were comparable to the measured operating characteristics of the of the actual ground-coupled heat pump system installed. The optimized system performance for a comfortable relative humidity range of 50 to 70% with respect to energy saving and borehole depth reduction was shown to be 19.4% and 16.8% respectively. It could thus be concluded that the adoption of the novel ground-coupled heat pump system incorporating displacement ventilation would enhance the economic feasibility of its practical application to sub-tropical and temperate regions.

713212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
713212.value: An air-tight building enclosure can be used to enable the effects of incorporating radiant cooling based on the variable-speed ground-coupled heat pump system to be investigated further with a view to enhancing the energy-saving performance already achieved with the current displacement ventilation system. The hybrid integration of radiant cooling with displacement ventilation system in the context of variable-speed ground-coupled heat pump system should be a promising novel idea for achieving excellent energy saving in future building cooling systems.

713212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
713212.value: The research project was aimed at investigating a novel hybrid energy-efficient air conditioning system for sub-tropical and temperate regions based on a variable-speed ground-coupled heat pump system which was classified as renewable energy system. A new enhanced operating mode was adopted for the variable-speed refrigerant compressor to interact with the hybrid system. Encouraging results of the investigations carried out showed that the hybrid air conditioning system was capable of achieving substantial energy saving compared to conventional convective systems. It was concluded that the hybrid system enabled a ground-coupled heat pump system to operate with improved energy efficiency while at the same time allowing the length of the vertical borehole heat exchanger embedded in the ground soil to be reduced. Consequently, both the operating cost and the capital cost could be lowered. This will enhance the applicability of the hybrid system for air conditioning in sub-tropical and temperate regions and promote the progressive adoption of energy-efficient renewable energy systems in the future.

713512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
713512.value: High-throughput sequencing (Next Generation Sequencing) is becoming available at low cost and paving the way for personalized medicine. Nowadays genome sequencing centers operate with a battery of sequencers, each can “decode” a human genome in a week into billions of randomly-ordered short segments (technically called reads, each with tens to a hundred bases). While such huge volume of data makes it feasible to perform different comparative analysis of human genomes, it also gives new challenges for bioinformatics. As the starting point of most analysis is to align (map) the reads to a reference human genome, faster and faster alignment software has been developed to cope with the increasing throughput of sequencers. State-of-the-art software (SOAP3), exploiting compressed indexing with massive parallelism, can align over 100 million reads (or 10 gigabases) per hour on a single sever. Existing alignment software can locate alignments with a few mismatches (errors). When dealing with different human genomes, usually there are still 10% or more reads “unaligned”. Simply allowing more mismatches can align more reads, but it slows down the process drastically and gives more false alignments. Unaligned reads are mainly due to difference of genomes instead of sequencing errors, and they are important for comparative analysis (e.g., comparing a cancer patient’s genome against a normal reference). Current attempts to further align these unaligned reads are rather primitive, either solving the problem partially or being far from high throughput. This project is about the design and engineering of efficient indexing and alignment algorithms in two directions that address the differences of human genomes: (1) SNP-sensitive alignment: Different genomes differ at a few million single positions (SNPs). Databases of such positions exist and should be indexed somehow. When aligning a read, variations due to SNPs should be allowed, while mismatches at random places should be minimized. (2) Alignment with large gap: When a read crosses the boundary of a mutation (e.g., a block removed, moved or inverted), a proper alignment to the reference includes a gap. Existing software lacks an appropriate index for locating a gap efficiently; this project aims at designing the appropriate index. This project targets to produce fast and accurate alignment software to supplement the existing ones. It will enhance the comparative analysis of human genomes, even when the sequencing data have relatively low coverage. Gap alignment is particularly important to RNA-Seq data that involve a lot of natural gaps (due to missing introns). 隨着高通量測序成本不段改進, 現今的高通量基因組測序器每個人都可以在一個星期內將一個人的基因組 “解碼”成數十億的隨機排序的短段, 如此龐大的數據量令基因組的比較分析產生了新的挑戰。這個項目是希望改進人類基因組的索引及測序數據(短讀段)之排對. 現有的排對軟件能容忍少量的錯對。在處理不同的人類基因組，通常有10％ 測序數據未能排對。簡單地增加排對的錯誤率，不但將排對速度大大減慢，並提供更多的錯誤的排對。未對齊的數據，主要是由於不同人的基因分異，它們往往是比較分析過程中很重要的資料（例如，比對癌症患者和正常的基因組比較）。當前對這些未對齊的數據如何作進一步處理，還在起步中, 無論是解決問題的部分或高吞吐量。 此項目就高效的索引和排對算法的的設計和工程,有兩個方向去解決人類基因組的差異：（1）利用現存的數據庫對基因差異的位置引入新索引，在比對過程中減少隨機的錯誤匹配。 （2）設計適當的索引去支持進步有較大的差距的排對, 這些大差距是來自越過基因突變邊界的數據 (例如，塊刪除，移動或倒置)。 此項目的目標是造出快速及更準確的排對軟件。這將加強人類基因組的比較分析，即使在覆蓋深度比較低的測序數據或者核糖核酸測序數據亦能應用。

713512.label: Realisation of objectives
713512.value: In this project we have investigated various approaches to obtain better algorithms and software for aligning next-geneartion sequencing data (short reads) onto a reference genome. Overall speaking, the project was successful, producing several state-of-the-arts bioinformatics tools as well as five journal papers, one conference paper one PhD student. The first approach we considered was to take advantage of existing database on SNPs to facilitate the alignment of reads that are relatively not too similar to the reference genome. We were delighted to have devised an efficient way to index the reference genome together with a SNP database, thus improving the sensitivity of the alignment (SNPAlign 2012) especially for sequencing data with low depth. However, the algorithm seemed to be of theoretical interest only as the SNP database keeps changing and varies from population to population; furthermore, sequencing cost has dropped drastically and it is no longer common to generate low-depth data. Our second approach was to exploit GPU to speed up index-based pattern matching and dynamic programming, which formed the bottlenecks involved in short read alignment. We developed a rather sophisticated algorithm to circumvent the limitation of GPU (limited memory and SIMD model). The software (SOAP3-dp) was a few times faster than existing alignment tools and more sensitive. The ability to conduct dynamic programming rapidly seems to be more useful than using SNP database to take care of dissimilarity between the short reads and the reference genome. Based on SOAP3-dp, we have further developed an integrated tool (BALSA) for short read alignment and variant calling (both SNP and INDEL calling). BALSA has very good performance regarding speed and sensitivity when compared with existing tools (e.g., BWA + GATK). Among others, we were able to take advantage of the parallelism of GPU to re-align erroneous reads together (instead of individually) for better error correction. Other than GPU, we also considered Intel's acceleration hardware called MICA (Xeon Phi coprocessor). GPU and MIC were based on very different architectures and demanded different algorithmic and software development techniques. Our MIC-based alignment tool, called MICA, turned out to have very similar performance to our GPU-based tool SOAP3-dp even though the number of cores in a MIC is about one twentieth of that in a GPU. Meanwhile we have also developed a GPU-based algorithm for RNA alignment, but the improvement was not significant as our DNA alignment tools (the improvement is mainly on speed but not much on sensitivity); we did not publish our RNA alignment result and we decided to give up this direction. Instead we applied some of our indexing and alignment skills to a more complicated problem on multiple sequence (in particular, protein) alignment, which has been studied intensively in the past decade. A new tool (GLProbs) has been produced, which showed drastic improvement when the input is mixed with sequences with diversified similarity. More recently, we made use our GPU-based techniques to index short reads (instead of the reference genome) for building a succinct de Bruijn Graph, which allowed us to build a memory-efficient assembler for metagenomics applications. Our assembly tool (MEGAHIT) was the first to assemble the largest dataset in the Grand Prairie Metagenome Grand Challenge on a single server using a few hundred gigabytes of memory. MEGABIT has been widely used by a number of bioinformatics users (e.g., JGI of the Department of Energy, US).

714112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714112.value: Hydrogen is one of the most important and promising clean and renewable fuels for the current and future needs. Hydrogen generation from water using catalysts under sunlight is an attractive green method to harvest solar energy. However, most photocatalysts function only under the energy-intensive UV light and are unable of hydrogen production under visible light. In this project, novel visible light-driven photocatalysts will be developed for hydrogen generation from water using solar light. Moreover, the photocatalytic oxidation power will be utilized for waste organic degradation. The research methodology is proposed based on our previous work on the synthesis of CdS/ZnS and (CdS-ZnS)/Ag/TiO2 photocatalysts. The new innovation however aims to use the photosensitive and more environmentally-friendly MoS2 in combination with TiO2 to make multi-layer all-solid-Z-scheme MoS2/Me/TiO2 thin films on the indium tin oxide (ITO) conductive glass. The inner-layer MoS2 has a narrow band-gap behaving as a photo-sensitizer, and the outer-layer TiO2 has a larger band-gap that will provide a protective shell and photo-oxidation sites. The catalyst film with a photovoltaic function will be used as a photoelectrode in a two-chamber photoelectrochemical cell (PEC) for hydrogen generation and organic degradation. In addition to photocatalytic hydrogen production, the catalyst film as an electroanode will be integrated with a microbial electrolysis cell (MEC) to construct a two-chamber photocatalytic-MEC or photoanode-assisted MEC (PMEC) for concurrent hydrogen generation and waste organic degradation. During the project, the chemical and processing conditions, including the chemical precursor contents, reaction and aging time, annealing temperature, and use of dopants (e.g. Pt, Ag and Ru), will be optimized to prepare the catalyst film with a high photo-reactivity and long-term stability. The design and structure of the MEC and PMEC also will be optimized to improve the energy efficiency of the systems. The technological development will be carried out in two stages - Stage 1 for the synthesis of MoS2/Me/TiO2 catalyst films and fabrication of PECs for the photocatalytic process and Stage 2 for the development of PMEC for hydrogen generation and waste organic degradation. The reactivity and stability of the photocatalyst films will be examined throughout the research project. Eventually, the novel photocatalysts will achieve a great photo-reactivity with a maximum solar to hydrogen energy conversion efficiency of 8% or higher and a long-term stability of at least 500 hrs in solar irradiation. 714112.label: Realisation of objectives
714112.value: All research objectives have been well achieved. Following the proposal, the photosensitive catalyst materials with little toxicity have been utilized in combination with TiO2 to make multi-layer photocatalyst films. In addition to photocatalytic hydrogen production under solar light, the catalyst film can be used in two-chamber photo cells for concurrent hydrogen generation and waste organic degradation. More specifically, the following advancements are achieved by the research work of the project: (i) synthesis of the composite MoS2/Me/TiO2 catalyst thin film as a visible light-driven and environmentally-friendly photocatalyst with a high reactivity and long-term stability, (ii) utilization of both the reduction and oxidation capabilities of the photocatalytic process for hydrogen production together with organic degradation under solar light, and (iii) integration of the photocatalyst film as a photoanode with MEC for concurrent hydrogen generation and organic wastewater treatment. (1) A novel and environmentally friendly photocatalyst nanofilm, MoS2/Ag/TiO2, was synthesized on a glass-fibre membrane. The composite catalyst film had a multi-layer structure and a high respond to visible light. The multi-layer catalyst film performed well for both photocatalytic hydrogen production and organic degradation in a two-chamber photoreactor under either solar or visible light irradiation. The results showed that hydrogen was produced in the cathode side chamber while the model organic (formic acid) was decomposed in the anode side chamber. The specific hydrogen production rate went through a maximum of 85 mmol/m2-h with a photo-energy conversion efficiency of 0.85% and a quantum yield of 12%. It is apparent that Ag functioned as a nano-conjunction between the TiO2 and MoS2 layers, which allowed the transfer of photo-excited electrons via TiO2→Ag→MoS2 for organic oxidation and H+ reduction (hydrogen evolution) in two different chambers. The MoS2/Ag/TiO2 multi-layer films that use environmentally friendly materials as the catalysts show a great potential in both photocatalytic hydrogen generation for renewable energy and organic wastewater treatment for sustainable water pollution control using solar energy. (2) Novel composite CdS/ZnS catalysts were developed that have a high photo-reactivity under solar light. Two types of the catalysts, suspended nanoparticles and layered nanofilms, were tested. The nanoparticle (CdS)0.8/(ZnS)0.2 catalyst with a core-shell structure was synthesized using the stepped W/O microemulsion technique in a n-hexane/Triton X-100/1-butanol/water system. The two layer CdS/ZnS catalyst was immobilized as a film on a glass slide by chemical bath deposition (CBD). The core/shell and layered film structures would allow to tailor the advantages of the narrow band-gap CdS for its high photosensitivity and the wide band-gap ZnS for its stability. In addition, Ru was deposited on the catalysts to improve their electrochemical property. The photocatalytic experiments were conducted in a photo cell under visible light. A number of organic substances were used as electron donors, including formic acid, methanol and ethanol. Both the suspended nanoparticle and two-layer film CdS/ZnS catalysts were effective in photocatalytic hydrogen generation with simultaneous organic degradation under visible light. The organic matter in water functioned as electron donors for the photocatalytic process, and no hydrogen was produced in the absence of organic. The efficiency of the organic substances for the enhancement of hydrogen production was in an order of formic acid, ethanol and methanol. With the suspended CdS/ZnS nanoparticles in the formic acid solution, a hydrogen production rate of 26.6 µmol/cm2-hr could be achieved, and the corresponding organic removal rate was 0.43 mg/cm2-hr. With the film catalysts and formic acid, the maximum hydrogen production rate was 10.2 µmol/ cm2-hr and the organic (COD) removal rate was 0.18 mg/cm2-hr. The results indicate that the development of novel photocatalysts would lead to a technological breakthrough for renewable energy and sustainable water pollution control. (3) The new photocatalyst films were integrated into the biological MFC and MEC systems for energy and environmental applications. With the light irradiation, the photoanodes can function as an external power source to increase the reduction potential of the cathode to realize hydrogen evolution on the cathode. Meanwhile, the photoanode or photocatalyst film can destruct/oxidize organic pollutants, and the organic products are further biodegraded in the MEC. The photocatalytic MEC with the film photoelectrode was tested for hydrogen generation and waste organic degradation. The reactors were separated into two chambers, including the photoelectrode chamber consisting of the photoanode, and Chamber II as the MEC with a bioanode and cathode. Organic pollutants were added as the test substances in Chamber I for photocatalytic organic destruction and/or oxidation. Meanwhile, hydrogen generation was achieved without any input of external energy sources.

714112.label: Major findings and research outcome
714112.value: (1) Heterostructure CdS/ZnS nanoparticles as a visible light-driven photocatalyst for hydrogen generation from water (Wang et al., 2010; Wang and Li 2013, 2016): (CdS)/(ZnS) nanoparticles were synthesized as a visible light-driven photocatalyst using the stepped microemulsion technique. The composite catalyst exhibited a much greater photocatalytic hydrogen production activity than either pure CdS or the homogeneous Cd0.8Zn0.2S solid solution. (2) Photocatalytic hydrogen generation with simultaneous organic degradation by composite CdSeZnS nanoparticles under visible light (Wang et al., 2014): A visible light-driven CdSeZnS photocatalyst in the form of nanoparticles with a heterogeneous structure was synthesized using the stepped microemulsion method. The composite CdSeZnS was capable of simultaneous photocatalytic hydrogen production and organic degradation under visible light. (3) Photocatalytic hydrogen generation with simultaneous organic degradation by a visible light-driven CdS/ZnS film catalyst (Wang and Li, 2013, 2014): A layered CdS/ZnS catalyst film was synthesized on glass using the stepped chemical bath deposition method. The photocatalyst was effective in hydrogen production together with organic degradation. (4) Composite photocatalyst MoS2/Ag/TiO2 was synthesized on a glass-fibre membrane that had a high respond to visible light (Wang and Li, 2015). The multi-layer catalyst film performed well for both photocatalytic hydrogen production and organic degradation in a two-chamber photoreactor under solar light. (5) Synthesis of MoS2/g-C3N4 as a solar light-responsive photocatalyst for organic degradation (Peng and Li, 2014): A novel MoS2 and graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) composite photocatalyst was synthesized using a low temperature hydrothermal method. The novel MoS2/g-C3N4 composite is shown as a promising catalyst for photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants using solar energy. (6) The synergetic effect of MoS2 and graphene on Ag3PO4 for its ultra-enhanced photocatalytic activity in phenol degradation under visible light (Peng et al., 2014, 2016): A new composite material was synthesized that consisted of silver phosphate (Ag3PO4) sub-microcrystals grown on a layered molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) and graphene (GR) hybrid as a high-performance photocatalyst for degradation of toxic organic pollutants. (7) Integration of the photocatalyst film electrode with MFC/MEC (Li et al., 2017) The new photocatalyst films were integrated into the biological MFC and MEC systems for energy and environmental applications. With the light irradiation, the photoanodes can function as an external power source to increase the reduction potential of the cathode to realize hydrogen evolution, with the destruction of organic pollutants in a different chamber.

714112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714112.value: Applications will be made to the Innovation and Technology Fund (ITF) for continuous development of the photocatalysis technology. In the application, visible light-driven novel photocatalysts will be developed for photocatalytic hydrogen generation from water under solar irradiation. The photocatalytic cathode will be applied in MFC for hydrogen production and organic wastewater treatment. The advantage of the novel photocatalytic cathode for MFC will be (1) a low-cost photocatalyst material with a high efficiency for the cathode, and (2) utilization of the (solar) photo-generated electricity as well by the MFC for hydrogen generation. The novel photo-system is expected to have at least 6% energy conversion efficiency for hydrogen generation. A set of prototype photo-cells will be fabricated with a hydrogen generation rate of more than 30 mL/hr at the solar irradiation level of 50 mW/cm2.

714112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714112.value: Hydrogen is one of the most important and promising clean and renewable energy for the current and future needs. Hydrogen generation from water using catalysts under sunlight is an attractive green method to harvest solar energy. In this project, novel visible light-driven photocatalysts are developed for hydrogen generation from water using solar light. Moreover, the photocatalytic oxidation power also can be utilized for waste organic degradation. The new innovations use the photosensitive metal oxides to make multi-layer thin catalyst films on the conductive glass. The catalyst film with a photovoltaic function is used as a photoelectrode in a two-chamber photoelectrochemical cell (PEC) for hydrogen generation and organic degradation. A layered CdS/ZnS catalyst film was effective in hydrogen production together with organic degradation. The multi-layer MoS2/Ag/TiO2 catalyst film also performed well for both photocatalytic hydrogen production and organic degradation in a two-chamber photoreactor under solar light. In addition to photocatalytic hydrogen production, the catalyst film as an electroanode will be integrated with a microbial electrolysis cell (MEC) to construct a two-chamber photocatalytic-MEC for concurrent hydrogen generation and waste organic degradation. The research outputs will lead to innovative environmental technologies for renewable energy and sustainable water pollution control.

714212.value: To obtain data and new understanding of the evaporation rate and hygroscopicities of human expiratory droplets and to optimize the existing evaporation models of expiratory droplets containing insoluble suspended substances. To develop new understanding of the mechanisms of the exposure of expiratory droplets and droplet nuclei between the infected and the susceptible in an indoor environment with different ventilation methods, in particular the proximity effect of airborne exposure and its relative importance as compared to the direct droplet spray exposure. To study the roles of the near-body microenvironment in the short-range exposure between two people (i.e. less than 1.5 m apart), as compared to the concept of cloud baby or cloud adult in the infectious disease transmission literature. To investigate the effectiveness of surgical masks, N95 masks, personalized ventilation and general ventilation in controlling short-range and long-range exposure of expiratory droplets and droplet nuclei.

714212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714212.value: The 2009 H1N1 influenza pandemic and the 2003 SARS epidemic are the most recent reminders of how rapidly emerging respiratory infectious diseases can spread in the crowded modern built environment. Considerable uncertainties remain about the routes of respiratory virus transmission, and in particular the relative importance of airborne, large droplet and contact transmission. These uncertainties have led to contradictory recommendations of engineering control methods by different leading authorities, for example, during the 2009 influenza pandemic, WHO (2009) recommended the use of surgical masks while US National Academy of Sciences (2009) recommended N95 masks for health care workers. Respiratory infection such as influenza mostly occurs in close proximity to the index patient. It is generally believed that its transmission is unlikely to be airborne but is droplet-borne through close contact. We hypothesize that close proximity infection can be via either droplet-borne or short-range airborne routes. This new hypothesis is partly supported by our preliminary finding of the proximity effect, in which inhaled exposure to expiratory droplet nuclei substantially increases within 1.5 m of the source person, similar to large droplet exposure. An in-depth understanding of short-range and long-range exposure of expiratory droplets between people will bridge one of the gaps towards a better understanding of respiratory infection transmission and its control. Expiratory droplets are the vectors of most respiratory diseases such as influenza and TB. Existing studies of inter-personal expiratory droplet exposure do not consider evaporation of realistic droplets and the detailed impact of body-microenvironment. We plan to carry out detailed experimental and computational studies on the exposure of realistic exhaled droplets and droplet nuclei between two seated or standing thermal breathing mannequins. Respiratory activities due to normal breathing and coughing will be studied using breathing thermal mannequins and real people. Exposure of a mannequin to respiratory droplets of healthy volunteers will be tested. Short-range airborne and direct droplet spray-borne exposure will be evaluated. The roles of the near-body microenvironment will be studied. Large eddy simulation and laser Doppler velocimetry will be used to obtain detailed flow information and turbulence structure. Existing epidemiological data for influenza and tuberculosis will be reviewed and used together with the new exposure data to identify the relative importance of direct droplet spray transmission, short-range and long-range airborne transmission. The new data will also be used to understand the relative efficacy of personal and ventilation control methods, such as masks, general ventilation and personalized ventilation. 雖然一些疾病的確切傳播路徑還存在未知或仍有爭議性，但是人们已知呼出飛沫是多數呼吸性疾病例如流感、肺結核等的載體。人際間呼出暴露過程包括病原人體飛沫釋放、空氣中傳播和蒸發階段以及最後被易感染體吸入或捕獲。對人際間呼出飛沫傳播的認識是开發室內有效通風方法的必要基础，特別是醫院環境例如普通病房、接待室和隔離病房等以及擁擠型室內環境如教室、劇院、公交車、火車和飛機等。对开發避免感染的個人和工程控制方法例如使用口罩和社會隔離等也有效。已存在的關於人際間呼出飛沫暴露的研究沒有充分考慮真實呼出飛沫的蒸發， 并且 僅僅考慮有限的通風條件(取決於通風方式和通風率)和汙染物類型。 本項目的最終目標是改進當前對不同通風條件下人際間汙染物輸運的認知，並為工程師設計機械通風條件下的健康建築提供有意義的數據和指導。特別是本項目將系統研究不同通風條件下人際間汙染物輸運特性，並且評估人對此類汙染物的暴露風險，提供指南以便於設計能避免感染性疾病通過空氣傳播的更有效通風系統。 我們假設鄰近感染可通過飛沫傳播或近距離空氣傳播。我們的初步研究結果可部分證明這一新假設，其中呼出飛沫核的吸入暴露在病源人體的1.5米距離內顯著增加，類似於大飛沫暴露。通過對呼出飛沫在人體之間短距離和長距離暴露的深入研究，可更好地認知呼出感染擴散及其控制問題並填補其間的知识空白。 我們計劃通過詳細的實驗和數值模擬，研究呼出飛沫和飛沫核在兩個具有不同姿勢和活動方式的暖體假人之間的暴露，包括坐、 睡、 站立和行走。我們將采用具有呼吸功能的暖體假人研究由正常呼吸和咳嗽引起的呼出活動，將采用一新型雙層口罩采樣器測試暖體假人對被感染誌願者呼出病毒的暴露，將評估短距離空氣暴露和直接飛沫噴射暴露，將研究由人體對流層和呼出Puff流和射流產生的近體微環境對鄰近效應的作用，將采用大渦模擬和激光多普勒測流儀測速來獲得近體微環境的詳細流場信息和湍流結構。我們將結合已存在的關於流感、非典(SARS)、肺結核、麻疹、水痘的傳染病學綜述數據和該研究所獲取的新的暴露數據，來確認直接飛沫噴射傳播、短距離和長距離空氣傳播的相對重要性。新的數據將被用來認知個人和通風控制方法的相對功效，例如醫學口罩、N95口罩、常規通風和個性化通風。

714212.label: Realisation of objectives
714212.value: Objective 1 To obtain data and new understanding of the evaporation rate and hygroscopicities of human expiratory droplets and to optimize the existing evaporation models. The new understanding is obtained by developing a suitable mathematical model. Our work started from the five stage concept for the evaporation of a droplet containing insoluble particles in the literature. We produced a simple two-stage model, the shrinking process and the equilibrium stage. We also looked into different assumptions in such a model. In determining the threshold relative humidity, we consider both the Kelvin effect (a larger droplet surface curvature requires a higher partial vapor pressure) and the solute effect (nonvolatile solutes require a lower partial vapor pressure to keep equilibrium).We continued our experiment to measure saliva evaporation with an improved set-up. One saliva droplet is released by a pipette onto a Teflon surface. The weight loss of the droplet is recorded continuously by an analytical balance. We generated and tested droplets of different sizes. The test data are used to improve our mathematical model. For the first time, we understand how droplet nuclei are formed as a function of the indoor environment conditions. A journal paper is published in Indoor Air (Liu et al 2017a). Objective 2 To develop new understanding of the mechanisms of the exposure of expiratory droplets and droplet nuclei between the infected and the susceptible, in particular the proximity effect of airborne exposure. We carry out both experimental and computer simulations with two standing mannequins in a room with three ventilation systems will be considered, i.e. mixing, displacement and downward ventilation, with different ventilation rate. We measured the exposure for different distance between the mannequins. The results confirmed the hypothesis in this project – the short range airborne route is important. In our CFD simulation, we had difficulties, as expected, in differentiating large droplet exposure and short-range airborne transmission. As the first step, we considered the inhalation of large droplets greater than 10 m as droplet direct spray exposure, and that of smaller than 10 m as airborne exposure. A journal paper is published (Liu et al 2017b). Objective 3 To study the roles of the near-body microenvironment in the short-range exposure between two people (i.e. less than 1.5 m apart), as compared to the concept of cloud baby or cloud adult in the infectious disease transmission literature. The question to answer was what happens when the micro-environments of two individuals in close proximity interact with each other, and one individual inhales from the micro-environment of the other. In this part of the project, we identified the importance of exhaled flow vortex from the early experimental and CFD simulations. We developed a new water tank for such a study, and borrowed a real nasal cavity model from Albert University (Professor Finley’s group). We found this set up is ideal for this study with the help of laser visualization. We developed an improved breathing machine for use in a water tank. Of course, we considered the similarity requirements. To show the importance of near-body microenvironment, we first tested when the body convection boundary layer and body plume is absent. We identified that re-inhalation of the exhaled air is an important parameter, and our new experimental data shows that the re-inhalation ratio is very low, less than 5% as against the value of >15% in the literature, where the computational fluid dynamics simulation was used. We adopted a water tank study instead of a room as better visualization techniques in water can help us to reveal more physics. Our completed study considered a simple case that the manikin skin is thermally neutral. We are currently testing different ways to heat up the manikin. We purchased a new PIV system to measure in detail the distribution of the air (water) flow around the manikin body. The same real nasal cavity model from Albert University (Professor Finley’s group) was still be used. It produced more realistic exhalation flows. Two journal papers are published (Wei et al 2016, Wei and Li, 2017), and another being prepared on coughing which is a crucial element of short-range airborne route. Objectives4 To investigate the effectiveness of different control methods in controlling short-range and long-range exposure of expiratory droplets and droplet nuclei. This part of the project was difficult. We had an early attempt on 28 influenza A virus patients with failure of detecting any influenza virus in airborne droplet sampling detection in front of each patient for 10-20 minutes followed by RT-PCR and viral culture. This work has been prepared into a joint journal paper with a similar work done in Singapore and Canada, and published. The tests for the effectiveness of masks, personalized and general ventilation in controlling different exposure routes will be done soon. Additionally, as in the original proposal, we mentioned that we only addressed the issue of exposure (via inhalation only, and other possible direct or surface contact routes are excluded), and this does not equal the subsequent infection or disease. The relative impact of vaccination, antiviral use, hand-washing, disinfection and gloves are all beyond the scope of the present project. The results obtained in Objectives 1-3 are used here to shed more lights into how we understand how masks and personalized ventilation affect the exposure due to both short range and long ranger routes. It turned out that we found the surface contact route may be very important as a surprising result as we study the transmission routes. Surface contact route can also lead the exposure at a remote distance as human hand can carry virus from one surface to a remote surface. The surprising result is that the surface can be contaminated rapidly as the surface contamination work develops. We developed and received a new GRF research project based on this side result of this project. As we have discovered the surprising logistic growth of the surface contamination network, we took the impact of surface contact route into consideration when we study the airborne route, though the study of surface contact route does not directly impact the airborne route. However, the surface deposition of directly exhaled droplets and droplet nuclei provides a contamination surface environment close to the patient. The surface contact route and the airborne route were found to have an interesting link. This will be proposed for further study in future. Additional work First, the output of this project has been useful in developing a new short-range airborne model, which is integrated into our multi-route model. The model has been applied in two major studies, one is a comparative modelling study of transmission routes of three diseases in aircraft cabins. Interestingly, we confirmed that influenza may be dominated by the short-range airborne route. We have prepared a journal paper, and it is still reviewed by the co-authors. The other study is to apply it to the possible multi-route transmission in the first nosocomial MERS outbreak in Korea, i.e. Pyeongtaek St. Mary's Hospital. A journal paper is currently under preparation. Second, the PI was invited to give a talk in an ASTM workshop and an ASHRAE conference, which has resulted in two review papers (Wei and Li 2016, and Li et al 2015).

714212.label: Major findings and research outcome
714212.value: The major outcome of this project is that we confirmed the so-called close proximity infection can be both droplet-borne and short-range airborne. We find that a substantial increase of airborne exposure of a susceptible person to droplet nuclei exhaled by the source patient when comes close to the source patient (within 1.5 m). Threshold distance of about 1 m distinguishes the two basic transmission processes of droplets and droplet nuclei, i.e. short-range modes and long range airborne route. The droplet dispersion also varies with humidity. With the same initial size, droplets could form droplet nuclei sufficiently fine enough to be suspended in air for a substantial length of time for the relatively dry air, while droplets could also evaporate 10 times slower and settles down rapidly in the humid air. We thus reveal that transmission occurring in close proximity to the index patient includes both droplet-borne (large droplet) and short-range airborne routes. The mechanisms of droplet-borne and short-range airborne routes are different; hence their effective control methods are also different. A related major finding is that the dried droplet nuclei size was about 30% of the original diameter. The droplet nuclei size at a relative humidity of 90% (25°C) could be 30% larger than the size of the same droplet at a relative humidity of less than 67.3% (25°C). The trajectories of respiratory droplets in a cough jet are significantly affected by turbulence, which promotes the wide dispersion of droplets. We found that medium-sized droplets are more influenced by humidity than are smaller and larger droplets, while large droplets, whose travel is less influenced by humidity, quickly settle out of the jet. The cough flow is also significantly affected by the near-body microenvironment. We identified the importance of exhaled flow vortex from the early experimental and CFD simulations. We developed a new water tank for such a study using a real nasal cavity model. We identified that re-inhalation of the exhaled air is an important parameter, and our new l data shows that the re-inhalation ratio is very low, less than 5% as against the value of >15% in the literature. The findings of this project has been useful in developing a new short-range airborne model, which is integrated into a new multi-route model, which has been useful in evaluating new control methods and investigating outbreaks.

714212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714212.value: The findings on the short-range airborne transmission has a significant implication to the intervention methods. General ventilation alone is not effective in controlling airborne infection, and other methods such as personalized ventilation needs to be considered. Further work should be done on if how personalized ventilation can be done to break the chain of exposure due to short-range airborne. Another possibility is in the development of a better N95 mask. The PI’s team is now working on a new mask design. This study also shows that the transmission route routes can be multiple, and there is a need for developing multiple route transmission understanding of the diseases. A number of subsequent studies have been carried out in our team, currently with a focus on the fomite route. Evaluation of different control methods have been carried out in such a framework with other GRF funding.

714212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714212.value: Considerable uncertainties remain about the routes of respiratory virus transmission, and in particular the relative importance of airborne, large droplet and contact transmission. Respiratory infection such as influenza mostly occurs in close proximity to the index patient. It is generally believed that its transmission is unlikely to be airborne but is droplet-borne through close contact. We showed for the first time that close proximity infection can be via either droplet-borne or short-range airborne routes. This new findings is supported by our finding of the proximity effect, in which inhaled exposure to expiratory droplet nuclei substantially increases within 1.5 m of the source person, similar to large droplet exposure. Our studies of inter-personal expiratory droplet exposure considered evaporation of droplets and the detailed impact of body-microenvironment. We carried out both detailed experimental and computational studies on the exposure of exhaled droplets and droplet nuclei between two seated or standing thermal breathing mannequins. Respiratory activities due to normal breathing and coughing were studied. Exhaled respiratory droplets of healthy volunteers were tested. The roles of the near-body microenvironment were studied. General ventilation alone is not effective in controlling airborne infection, and other methods such as personalized ventilation needs to be considered.

714312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714312.value: 虽然确切性质仍不清楚，越来越多的证据表明肌动蛋白参与了细胞分裂，细胞运动等重要过程。例如，人们普遍认为细胞运动所必需的推进力来自在细胞边缘的肌动蛋白网络的聚合。鉴于肌动蛋白在各种生理过程中的重要作用，精确的理解肌动蛋白网络的力学响应很可能会成为未来找到控制或治愈各种疾病方法的关键之一。此外，可以想象有一天，由肌动蛋白仿生材料推动的微型装置可以在我们体内运送药物或实施手术。 但是，对于肌动蛋白网络是如何抵抗变形的问题，几个重要的细节仍然是不清楚。首先，肌动蛋白丝的热扰动在几乎所有以前的模拟中都被忽略了。接下来，为了执行各种生理功能，细胞内的肌动蛋白网络往往需要承受不同的载荷。然而，人们对这种网络在不同变形条件下的力学响应仍然知知甚少。在这个项目中，我们计划进行数值模拟和实验研究来解决这些问题。具体来说，我们会对随机以及分叉的肌动蛋白网络进行有限元的模拟来仔细研究它们在不同负载条件下的反应。此外，在我们初步研究的基础上，朗之万动力学将会和有限元法结合起来以便捕捉热扰动对于肌动蛋白网络响应的影响。在实验方面，我们会在体外合成不同的肌动蛋白网络并用原子力显微镜来系统地测量它们在不同变形条件下的力学响应。 如果成功的话，这项研究将会解决如何在有限元模拟中考虑热扰动这个悬而未决的问题。这个项目的实验和模拟结果将明确证实或反驳我们的主要假设，即肌动蛋白网络的力学响应依赖于它的网络结构和施加的变形模式，从而大大提高我们对肌动蛋白如何执行不同的生理功能的基本认识以及为未来仿生材料的发展提供了宝贵的信息。

714312.label: Realisation of objectives
714312.value: 1. We have developed a combined finite element-Langevin dynamics (FEM-LD) method to analyze the mechanical behavior of cross-linked bio-filament networks where key factors like thermal fluctuations and large deflections of individual filament have all been taken into account. The validity of this approach was verified by comparing the simulation results with a variety of theoretical predictions. 2. Realistic actin networks, constructed by different crosslinking molecules and with various architectures, were generated in computer whose mechanical response were then systematically examined using the method developed in (1). 3. Robust methods have been established to grow actin networks in vitro as well as to label them in live cells. After that, different kind of tests (such as compressive indentation and enforced stretching) were carried out to examine the behavior of these networks.

714312.label: Major findings and research outcome
714312.value: 1. A novel approach for combining finite element method with Langevin dynamics has been developed allowing us to systematically examine the mechanical response of biopolymer networks (refer to item 8-1 in Part C). 2. We showed that the stress–strain relationship of realistic actin networks typically undergoes linear increase – strain hardening – stress serration – total fracture transitions due to the interplay between the bending and stretching of individual filaments and the deformation and breakage of cross-linkers. Interestingly, the network fracture energy will reach its minimum at intermediate rotational compliance values, reflecting the fact that most of the strain energy will be stored in the distorted filaments with rigid cross-linkers while the imposed deformation will be ‘‘evenly’’ distributed among significantly more crosslinking molecules with high rotational compliance (see item 8-5 in Part C). 3. It was found that, during cell adhesion, a dense actin cortex will be formed in the region close to the adhesion interface, resulting in a significant increase in the apparent modulus of the cell (item 8-2 in Part C). Furthermore, we showed that insertion of amyloid-beta peptide into the actin cytoskeleton (a hallmark in Alzheimer's disease) will lead to a higher bulk viscosity of neurons (item 8-6 in Part C).

714312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714312.value: 1. The combined FEM-LD method developed in this project can be used to investigate how interactions between F-actin and other bio-filaments, such as microtubule or intermediate filament, influence the response of bio-polymer networks, as in the case of real cytoskeleton. 2. Our protocol for growing actin networks in vitro can also be utilized to examine interesting questions like acin-driven motility. Studies along these lines are under way.

714312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714312.value: We have developed a computational method to study the behavior of biopolymer networks. In addition, robust protocols have also been established allowing us the grow actin network in vitro and then experimentally characterize mechanical response. Finding from project will help us better understand, from a physics/mechanics point of view, how cells perform their biological functions (such as migration, spreading and division) as well as provide guidance in the design and development of future biomimetic materials.

714412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714412.value: Ultrafine and nano aerosols attract international concern nowadays because of their detrimental impacts on health, air quality and the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) energy balance. Major fractions of these aerosols are semivolatile organic compounds (SVOCs), which are primarily emitted in vapor phase. After mixing and dilution, SVOCs cool down and nucleate, forming secondary nano aerosols. Due to their low saturation vapor pressures, they further condense and coagulate to grow ultrafine aerosols. Most anthropogenic SVOCs are vehicular exhausts in the urban canopy layer, which exhibits a distinct neighborhood-scale local climate different from that of the ABL. Vast efforts have been devoted to the removal of gaseous pollutants in urban areas. However, SVOC (vapor-aerosol) partitioning is rarely addressed in the urban climate community. To bridge the knowledge gap, this project, LES-SVOC, attempts to elucidate the nonlinearly coupled SVOC dynamics and microphysics in urban areas. The core scientific question is “how building geometry and environmental parameters modify partitioning and surface-to-ABL fluxes of SVOCs for the urban canopy layer”. Experimental and modeling approaches will be sought for complementary solutions. First, the drift flux model will be integrated into our large-eddy simulation (LES) model to examine the dispersion and deposition of nonvolatile particles. Monodisperse and polydisperse particles will also be tested in the wind tunnel to validate the LES. Next, SVOCs will be used instead to study experimentally their nucleation, condensation and coagulation in the persistent recirculating flows in street canyons. Concurrently, the SVOC microphysics module will be incorporated into the LES to handle the phase change in turbulent flows especially the effects of intermittency on SVOC partitioning, dispersion and deposition in urban canopies. Finally, using LES-SVOC, a series of systematic parametric tests will be performed to enrich the theoretical understanding of secondary SVOC aerosol production. Scenario analyses will be conducted to elucidate the mechanism of SVOC transport and removal for the urban canopy layer according to their bulk volatility. Utilizing the datasets developed, improved emission inventories covering SVOC partitioning will be proposed as functions of building geometry and environmental parameters for other air pollution modeling applications. Canopy-level SVOCs directly affect urban inhabitants and the environment. LES-SVOC will contribute to the in-depth fundamental scientific understanding of the multi-scale SVOC phenomena in the urban areas. The results will be useful to improve emission inventories, formulate surface parameterizations and foster effective abatement strategies of SVOCs for the urban canopy layer, in which most people live. 有鑑於對健康、空氣質素和大氣層能量均衡的不利影響，超細和納米氣溶膠研究是現世代的國際關注。氣溶膠的主要成份是起初以氣相排放的半揮發性有機化合物，經過混合和稀釋，氣相半揮發性有機化合物冷卻和成核，從而產生次納米氣溶膠。因為一般半揮發性有機化合物較低的飽和氣壓，它們會再凝結積聚生長出超細氣溶膠。大部份在城市冠層內的人為半揮發性有機化合物都是產生自汽車排放，再顯注的影響大氣層內獨特的鄰里尺度小區氣候。大量的資源已經投放到研究怎樣把氣體污染物從城區移走，可是，半揮發性有機化合物(氣相-氣溶膠)的劃分還是較小在城市氣候中提及到。 為了彌合上述知溝，這個項目嘗試闡明半揮發性有機化合物在城市區域中的動力學和粒子物理學。核心的科學問題是"建築物幾何和環境參數如何更改半揮發性有機化合物在城市冠層中的劃分及其從地表到大氣層的份量"。實驗和電腦模型會同時進行以求相互補充的解釋。首先，我們會把漂移流動模型結合到大渦模擬中以細查非揮發性有機化合物微粒的擴散和沈積作用。單粒徑分佈和多粒徑分佈的微粒都會在風洞中測試以確認大渦模擬的準確度。然後，在實驗中我們會用到半揮發性有機化合物去研究它們在街道峽谷循環氣流中的成核、凝結和積聚特性。同時，半揮發性有機化合物的粒子物理學會合併到大渦模擬中以處理漓流中的相變化，尤其是半揮發性有機化合物在城市冠層中的劃分、擴散和積聚。最後，利用LES-SVOC模型，會進行一連串有系統的參數測試以豐富我們對次半揮發性有機化合物氣溶膠產生的理論認識。我們亦會透過方案分析說明半揮發性有機化合物在城市冠層中的運輸和移走機制。最後，利用到上述新發展的數據庫，我們會改善現有的排放源清單，期望能把建築物幾何和環境參數等等加進函式和其他空氣污染模型中。 冠層內的半揮發性有機化合物會直接影響城市居民和環境。LES-SVOC會對半揮發性有機化合物在城市中的多尺度現象貢獻出徹底的基礎科學理解。科研結果有利改善排放源清單，規劃地表參數和制定有效的城市冠層半揮發性有機化合物減排方案。

714412.label: Realisation of objectives
714412.value: 1. Develop a robust LES in which the nucleation, condensation and coagulation of SVOCs are integrated (LES-SVOC) We modified our LES CFD code to include nucleation, condensation and coagulation of SVOCs in the flows in the urban canopy layer by integrating the drift flux model for particle transport into our large-eddy simulation (LES) code. A source term is included to handle the microphysics of semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs) for modeling the coupling of flow and SVOC microphysics (nucleation, condensation and coagulation). Systematic LES sensitivity tests were conducted to improve our understanding of transport behavior and the physical properties of particles. In particular, we attempted to parameterize the deposition flux and particle partitioning in the urban canopy layer. 2. Investigate how SVOC partitioning and transport depend on building geometry and environmental parameters Sensitivity tests, using the aforementioned computer code, were sought to examine the SVOC partitioning and transport. Our understanding of the models of particle dynamics and microphysics was improved. Different building geometry and flows configuration were adopted in the sensitivity tests to help improve the parameterization of deposition flux and particle partitioning in the urban canopy layer. 3. Elucidate the mechanisms of secondary aerosol production and SVOC removal in urban canopy layer The results from the aforementioned sensitivity tests helped enrich our understanding of the physics/chemistry mechanism. For example, the profiles of concentrations of gaseous and particulate pollutants, the timescales of dispersion and chemical reactions and the life time of pollutant in the urban canopy layer, etc. The findings help improve the SVOC parameterization for air quality modeling applications.

714412.label: Major findings and research outcome
714412.value: A series of systematic sensitivity tests were performed in this project to investigate the behaviors of SVOC transport and microphysics in response to building configuration and urban morphology in the urban canopy layer. After an in-depth understanding of the coupling between flows and chemical reactions, it was found that the aerodynamic resistance and timescales of SVOC physics/chemistry are major factors affecting the plume dispersion, particle formation and deposition flux. The plume dispersion coefficient could be parameterized by friction factor and the timescales. The plume is no longer in the Gaussian form after including particle microphysics. These findings serve the skeleton of the parameterizations for reactive plume dispersion.

714412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714412.value: The aforementioned mathematical scheme of parameterizations paved a foundation for the potential development of a non-computational-fluid-dynamics (non-CFD) model for quick and reliable estimate of gas/particle partitioning and transport at street levels in urban areas. Additional studies will be conducted, focusing on the validity and functionality, in order to improve the accuracy of the parameterizations.

714412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714412.value: Pollutant dispersion over urban areas is complicated by both urban morphology and pollutant composition in the form of physics/chemistry coupling. As such, the conventional Gaussian plume model must be used with caution. The pollutant distribution could deviate from the conventional form if pollution microphysics of SVOCs is considered alongside. Hence, there is a need for advancement in the parameterization of SVOC transport because of the dense population and valuable assets in urban areas. In the project, in-depth diagnoses for the mechanism of SVOC nucleation, condensation and coagulation were conducted. It was found that the aerodynamic resistance and the physics/chemistry timescales are two major factor governing the transport processes, particle partitioning and the SVOC parameterizations. Factor factor and the dispersion/reaction timescales were then adopted to formulate a quick, reliable non-CFD parameterization for street-level SVOC partitioning and transport. The findings could be used to serve as a skeleton for the development of more sophisticated surface models for urban air quality studies. The outcome will be helpful to safeguard stakeholders in particular for accidental release of harmful gases in urban areas.

714712.label: Project Objectives
714712.value: [Definition of different types of spatio-textual joins] We will define novel join operations based on selection or ranking on spatio-textual content. In addition, to the direct definitions based on spatio-textual containment and similarity, we will consider more advanced definitions (spatially filterer or ranked combined keyword searches, approximate joins, spatio-textual assignment problems, spatio-textual joins including a temporal dimension, etc.). Using real data, we will assess the relevance of each definition and its impact to actual users. [Design and implementation of appropriate evaluation techniques for spatio-textual joins] We will design and implement indexing and query evaluation methods for spatio-textual joins. Besides testing baseline implementations that directly extend the state-of-the-art on spatial and set-similarity joins, we will develop tailored methods for this new class of queries. Complexity analysis and experimental evaluation will be conducted to validate the performance of the developed techniques. [Integration of spatio-textual joins in a database system] Spatio-textual joins will be implemented as operators and integrated in a database engine. For this purpose, we will develop selectivity and cost models and study the impact of pre-defined indexes and interesting orders, if the join inputs stem from underlying query operations.

714712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714712.value: Databases become increasingly more complex over the years, as entities can easily be "tagged" with different types of auxiliary information, such as keywords and spatial locations. For example, webpages contain keywords and they may also be associated to locations, photographs in photo-sharing services such as Flickr are assigned descriptive tags and spatial locations, persons in social networks have profile entries (keywords) and addresses. This multi-source enrichment of objects by descriptive information allows for more complex queries and analysis tasks on the data. For example, the photo-sharing site Flickr offers an API, via which users can search for photos by specifying keywords and a spatial search range. Recently, there has been a growing interest by research and industry to use space as another dimension for organizing text and set-valued data. In line with this trend, this project will investigate data management solutions for the efficient support of spatio-textual join queries. Given two collections of objects that carry both spatial and textual information, a spatio-textual join retrieves the subset of their Cartesian product, wherein every pair of objects satisfies some spatial and textual predicates. As an example, consider a social network with spatially and textually tagged persons (i.e., their locations and profiles). A useful task (for friendship recommendation) would be to find pairs of persons that are spatially close and their profiles have a large overlap (i.e., they have common interests). Another application is data de-duplication (e.g., finding photographs which are spatially close to each other and high overlap in their descriptive tags). The project goals include the (i) definition of different types of spatio-textual joins, based on selection or ranking predicates in the two (space and text) dimensions (ii) design, implementation, and testing of appropriate evaluation techniques for spatio-textual joins, (iii) integration of spatio-textual join operations in a database system, and (iv) study of related search problems, such as spatially joining multiple keyword searches. 隨著時間的演進，數據庫變得越來越複雜，其理由是數據實體可以很容易地被“標記”上種類繁多的譬如說像關鍵字或者是空間(spatial)位置這樣的輔助信息。例如，網頁中包含一些可能同時指明地理位置的關鍵字，相片分享服務比如Flickr上的相片有相關的描述性標籤和空間位置，社交網絡中的使用者有其檔案條目(關鍵字)和地址。這種多源性的對象描述中所包含的豐富信息使得人們可以在數據上進行更複雜的查詢和分析任務。比如通過相片分享網站Flickr所提供的API，使用者可以指定關鍵字和空間搜索範圍來搜索相片。近年來，在研究和工業界，人們對使用空間作為另一維度來組織文本和集值(set-valued)數據表現出了越來越大的興趣。 順應這樣的趨勢，本項目將深入探究數據管理的解決方案，以支持高效的空間文本連接查詢(spatio-textual join query)。給定兩個同時包含空間和文本信息的對象集合，空間文本連接查詢會返回它們笛卡爾積中的一個子集，其中的每對對象均滿足特定的空間文本謂詞。舉例來說，考慮一個社交網絡，其中的每個使用者都有空間和文本上的標籤(即他們的所在地和檔案)。為了推薦朋友，一個很有用的的任務是找出配對的用戶，使得他們不僅在空間上接近並且他們的檔案描述也具有很高的重迭(換句話說，他們有著共同的興趣)。另一種應用是重復數據刪除(data de-duplication)，例如找出拍攝地點互相接近並且描述標籤有很大重迭的照片。本項目的目標包括(1)基於兩個維度(空間或文本)上的選擇或排序謂詞，定義多種空間文本連接查詢。 (2)設計、實現以及測試適合空間文本連接查詢的計算技術。 (3)將空間文本連接操作與數據庫系統進行整合。 (4)研究與之相關的搜索問題，例如對多關鍵字搜索的空間連接查詢等。

714712.label: Realisation of objectives
714712.value: Objectives 1 and 2: The objectives have been achieved 100%. Journal Publication 3 (Spatio-Textual Similarity Joins) reports our results on the design, implementation, and evaluation of a novel spatio-textual similarity join operator. In this work, we extended the state-of-the-art PPJ algorithm for textual similarity joins to efficiently evaluate spatio-textual similarity joins with the help of an on-demand spatial index construction. In addition, we proposed a block-based evaluation scheme that greatly reduces the cost of the operator. In Journal Publication 4 (Scaling Similarity Joins over Tree-Structured Data), we implemented and tested an approximate similarity join algorithm for tree structured data with labeled nodes. In Journal Publication 6 (Textually Relevant Spatial Skylines), we developed, implemented, and tested three algorithms for the problem of computing a spatial skyline which also considers the textual content of the objects in the dominance relationships between them. The results show that considering the textual dimension greatly reduces the output size of a spatial skyline and makes the result easily interpretable and useful. In addition, our efficient implementation computes the skyline result very fast compared to a naive implementation. In Conference Publication 2 (Efficient Top-k Spatial Distance Joins), we defined and solved an alternative spatio-textual join problem, where the objective is to find the pairs of spatial objects which have the highest combined similarity to some text keywords. Journal Publication 1 is a by-product of this research, where we used join algorithms to for the efficient evaluation of a matching problem which is a module of an image similarity search function. Journal Publication 2 is another by-product, where we solved an optimization problem with an objective to define a new product that dominates many existing ones w.r.t. its quality, while not dominated by other products. Journal Publication 5 is yet another by-product which studies the continuous monitoring of meeting points for moving users based on their locations. Finally, Conference Publication 1 solves the problem of joining social network users with the places where they check-in, in order to define a similarity between places and use it for recommendation. Objective 3 has also been achieved 100%. We have implemented and tested the designed join operators. Some of the results are reported in Journal Publications 3 and 4.

714712.label: Major findings and research outcome
714712.value: The major findings of this project are as follows: 1) The spatio-textual join is a particularly useful new operator that has a number of important applications, as reported in Journal Publications 3 and 4. After testing the operator on real data we were able to confirm the interestingness of its results. 2) We proposed and tested advanced indexing techniques and algorithms for implementing the spatio-textual join and approximate joins on tree-structured data (see Journal Publications 3 and 4). Our techniques are scalable and make it possible to obtain query results in real time. 3) Locations and textual information can also be jointly considered in the definition of dynamic skyline queries. In particular, the spatial skyline query can be extended to consider the textual relevance of the results to a user-defined set of query keywords. This novel query type is very useful to users who want to restrict the typically huge size of a spatial skyline to include only objects of interest (as expressed by the query keywords). See Journal Publication 6 for details. 4) Top-k join queries can be specialized to have spatial join predicates and ranking by textual relevance. This special class of queries have their own interesting applications and can be evaluated efficiently with appropriate algorithms that we propose in Conference Publication 2. 5) During the course of the project we also studied a number of related problems to spatio-textual joins. These include large-scale matching problems (Journal Publication 1), complex dominance relationships (Journal Publication 2), continuous aggregate query processing (Journal Publication 5) and similarity between places in a geo-social network (Conference Publication 1). 6) Three research students were trained during the project.

714712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714712.value: In the future, we plan to continue studying problems that apply on complex data domains such as spatial and textual. The challenge is that by considering multiple dimensions, the complexity of the problems increases. However the inherent data complexity nowadays renders these problems more and more relevant especially with the increasing availability of new and rich data formats. Therefore, our plan is to collect such data, analyze their querying requirements, study whether the existing research is adequate towards their effective and efficient analysis, and wherever there is a need for the modeling of new queries and the development of novel evaluation techniques, conduct new research.

714712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714712.value: In this project, we have studied the evaluation of joins between collections of objects that carry spatial and textual information. Such objects are, for example, webpages that contain keywords and are associated to locations, photographs in photo-sharing services such as Flickr which are assigned descriptive tags and spatial locations, etc. Given two collections of such objects, a spatio-textual join retrieves the subset of their Cartesian product, wherein every pair of objects satisfies some spatial and textual predicates (e.g., the objects are near each other spatially and contain a large number of common descriptive keywords). A wide range of applications can benefit from spatio-textual joins, like friendship recommendation in social networks and data de-duplication. In this project, we defined and implemented spatio-textual joins and tested their evaluation on different collections of real data. The results demonstrate the applicability of the query as well as the efficiency of the proposed indexing and evaluation techniques. We also studied a number of related problems such as spatially joining keyword search results, approximate joins for tree-structured data, and spatio-textual skyline queries. The results of the project were published in top journals and conferences of data management research.

715612.label: Project Objectives
715612.value: Building on our preliminary findings of metal incorporation enhancement at the metakaolin stage, a systematic analysis of the evolution of metal hosting phases across different temperature and time ranges will be undertaken. By calcining the targeted metal (copper, zinc, lead) compounds with metakaolin under various thermal conditions, this project aims to establish a clear temperature and time range for each metal incorporation mechanism through X-ray diffraction observation. Our expertise in quantitative X-ray diffraction analysis (Rietveld refinement method using the fundamental parameter approach and amorphous content quantification through internal standards) will report the enhancement of target metal incorporation by metakaolin through comparing its efficiency with that of similar oxide and aluminosilicate precursors (alumina, silica, and mullite). An amorphous content quantification protocol employing a more commonly available calcium fluoride internal standard will be also conducted in order to compare the project results to a traditional alumina standard (SRM 676a). This comparison will provide a basis to assist the development of a reliable amorphous content quantification method. Crystalline characteristics (lattice parameters, cation distribution, crystal size, etc.) of metal hosting phases generated from metakaolin and the other oxide/aluminosilicate precursors will be also obtained by Rietveld analysis to evaluate the quality of metal stabilization. Project co-investigator Professor Alexandra Navrotsky, who is a world renowned thermochemist and a member of the U.S. National Academy of Sciences, will analyze the formation enthalpies and surface energies of these phases through her very unique high-temperature oxide melt solution calorimetry technique to further provide direct evidence on metal hosting phase stability. The stabilization effects of incorporated metals in different aqueous environments will be examined by leaching experiments at constant pH (ranging from 2-12), and surface-sensitive characterization tools, e.g. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and atomic force microscopy (AFM), will be used to elucidate the metal leaching behavior on the product surface. Project co-investigator Professor Siu-Wai Chan at Columbia University will provide her expertise in analyzing grain boundary features through high resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to confirm the metal leaching behavior observed through spectroscopy. Based on the mechanistic understanding of copper, zinc and lead incorporation by metakaolin, the influences of other operational parameters, such as sample preparation and compositional design, will be delineated to provide an effective control on the reactive crystallization and viscous sintering processes. Such understanding is crucial to determining the nano- and micro-structural features in metal-bearing products and is also a necessity for developing safe and reliable techniques for environmental and industrial applications.

715612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
715612.value: Metakaolin is a nanocrystalline aluminosilicate material derived from the dehydroxylation of kaolinite and has high chemical reactivity with alkaline solutions. Most metakaolin studies focus on its applications as a pozzolan for concrete, but recent reports have indicated its superior metal incorporation capability for stabilizing hazardous metals after thermal treatments. Understanding of the thermal reactions between metakaolin and different metals is crucial to environmental applications, such as safely incorporating waste sludge and ash with the readily-available kaolinite precursor into the fabrication of eco-ceramics, thermally treating metal contaminated soils with clay additives at temperatures much lower than that of vitrification, and providing a new route of fabricating metal-loaded catalysts or composite materials at lower temperatures than is needed for reacting with common oxide or aluminosilicate matrices. This project aims to systematically quantify the metal incorporation capability of metakaolin under its stable temperature range (below 980C) and to compare this performance with those derived from similar oxide and aluminosilicate precursors (alumina, silica, and mullite). The main focus is on the incorporation mechanisms for copper, zinc and lead, which are usually enriched in waste incineration ash, industrial wastewater sludge, electronic waste, and metal contaminated soils, and are also used as industrial catalysts. Experimental activities will start by calcining the targeted metal compounds (oxide and hydroxide forms) with a metakaolin precursor at different temperatures and over different lengths of time. Then, the high resolution X-ray diffraction technique will be performed on the calcined samples, and a state-of-the-art Rietveld refinement analysis with amorphous content quantification will be implemented to quantify different metal phases and crystalline parameters of the metal hosting phases. Similar protocol will be carried out for the other oxide and aluminosilicate precursors to compare their metal incorporation effects and to identify the different crystalline features of product phases. After identification of the metal hosting phases, experimental calorimetry will then be performed through an international collaboration to measure the formation and surface energies of hosting phases to understand their thermochemical stability. By identifying the grain boundary features and evaluating the metal leachabilities of product phases, the hosting characteristics of different metal stabilization mechanisms will be further examined. Finally, the reactive crystallization and viscous sintering characteristics of metakaolin under thermal conditions will allow the design of a variety of nano- and microstructural features to be used in fabricating functional metal-bearing products. 变质高岭土是高岭土脱羟基后所产生的具有纳米结晶特征的铝硅酸盐材料，当置于碱性溶液中时，变质高岭土具有较高的化学反应性能。对变质高岭土的研究多数集中于该材料在水泥生产中的应用，但是，目前有研究表明：变质高岭土在金属结合方面具有优越性能，并可用于热处理过程中增强重金属的稳定化效果。变质高岭土在环境领域的可能性应用包括：污泥和灰烬等固体废弃物与高岭土原料结合安全成产陶瓷产品；粘土在重金属污染土壤热处理中的应用；常见化合物或铝硅酸盐基体在制作金属负载型催化剂或复合材料的新型方法等。而了解变质高岭土与重金属之间热反应机制，对于变质高岭土在环境领域中的以上应用具有关键作用。 本项目旨在系统的研究变质高岭土在其稳定温度段内（低于980 C）对重金属的稳定机制，包括对重金属嵌入能力的定量研究、与其他简单氧化物或铝硅酸盐原料（氧化铝、氧化硅和莫来石）等对重金属嵌入能力的比较分析。研究将主要着眼于含铜、锌和铅等重金属的固体废弃物，如固体废弃物焚烧灰烬、工业污泥、电子废弃物、重金属污染土壤以及工业催化剂等，研究以上废弃物中的重金属嵌入机制。实验将从不同温度和时间的样品烧结开始，进行烧结的样品制备于重金属化合物（氧化物和氢氧化物）和变质高岭土原料的混合物。烧结后的样品将通过高分辨率X射线衍射技术进行扫描，利用先进的Rietveld精修技术进行图谱分析，得到包括非结晶相在内的所有相的重量百分比，同时得出重金属持有相的结晶参数。对于采用铝硅简单氧化物或者铝硅酸盐原料的反应系统，研究也将采用同样的手段进行，从而比较以上材料对重金属结合机制，并且鉴定不同系统得到的产品相的结晶特征。 在上述实验成功鉴定出重金属持有相之后，建立在国际合作基础上的热量学研究将测定重金属持有相的形成能和表面能，从而更深入的了解上述重金属持有相的热化学稳定性。通过产物相晶界特征和重金属溶出能力的监测，进一步解析不同持有相的重金属稳定机制，最后，利用热反应条件下变质高岭土反应结晶和粘性烧结的特征，本项目还将控制产品的纳米或微米尺度的特征，制作一系列含金属的功能性产品。

715612.label: Realisation of objectives
715612.value: All the proposed objectives were achieved through this project implementation. The systematic evaluations of copper, zinc and lead systems in reacting with metakaolin under various thermal conditions were completed. The outcome provides very promising results in using metakaolin to stabilize these targeted metals. The quantitative X-ray diffraction analysis was conducted via Rietveld refinement method using the fundamental parameter approach, and was successfully applied to the metal-laden samples produced from reacting with metakaolin, alumina, silica and mulite. Together with the successful implementation of amorphous content quantification through the SRM 676a internal standard, all the tested samples can obtain their amorphous contents to more truly reflect the overall property of the products. With a Ph.D. student exchanged to the project collaborator’s high-temperature oxide melt solution calorimetry laboratory, the measured thermodynamic data were found matching well with our crystalline characteristic data generated from our structure refinement analysis. We have thus confirmed that as long as the metal incorporation can be initiated to form spinels or spinel-like crystals, the thermodynamic properties of the products will be similar. Using metakaolin as the precursor can effectively incorporate the target metals to reduce the energy cost of fabrication and still produce quality products. Another product quality assessment work through leaching experiments were also extensively conducted. The comparisons of intrinsic leachability for different production phases show the superior acidic resistance for the metal containing products using metakaolin as a precursor. Surface-sensitive XPS and AFM techniques were also used to observe product surface after the leaching process. TEM analyses indicated the main limiting factor of further narrowing the gain boundaries in this system is largely kinetic-driven, and a more effective way of overcoming this problem can be achieved through providing a porous microstructure for the products. The mechanistic understandings of copper, zinc and lead incorporation by metakaolin were provided through this study and the controlling factors of these mechanisms were also determined by the quantitative X-ray diffraction technique. A variety of nano- and micro-structural features in metal-bearing products were successfully produced with systematic investigations on their processing parameters. These development has successfully created a reliable and experimentally proven technology to promote metal incorporation under thermal conditions, while also fulfills different requirements in the product texture.
