717512.label: Major findings and research outcome
717512.value: A pedestrian-tracking tool was developed to capture pedestrian movement trajectories from video records [J2, J8, C2, C6, C7], which proved highly effective in determining pedestrian movement patterns in both space and time at signalized crosswalks. To understand the interactions between traffic and pedestrians at signalized intersections, effective procedures were established to estimate the traffic volumes [J5, J6, C1, C4, C5, C8], and also the pedestrian behavior and characteristics [J1, J2, J8, J11, C2, C6, C7]. Microscopic pedestrian models based on the cellular automata approach [J1] and logit-based approach [J8] were used to describe individual pedestrian movements, whereas macroscopic pedestrian models based on Bayesian inference [J2] were used to identify the aggregate crowd behavior in a multidirectional context. The findings from these analyses were useful in understanding spatio-temporal pedestrian movements and quantifying the pedestrian exposure to crash and injury risks at signalized intersections. In relation to this exposure to risk, other influencing factors, such as pedestrian jaywalking behavior, geometric design elements, and signal control attributes, were also investigated [J11]. In the crash frequency analyses, road network patterns were found to significantly affect pedestrian-involved crashes in the built environment, showing that the network configuration played an important role in pedestrian crash occurrence [J9]. The quasi-induced exposure method for pedestrian safety at signalized junctions was also studied, and showed that weather conditions and time-of-day were also critical factors affecting pedestrian safety [J7]. These findings provided useful insights for the development of a comprehensive model for predicting pedestrian crash frequency with explicit consideration of both pedestrian exposure and traffic volumes, together with other influencing factors [J12]. In the analyses of pedestrian injury severity, a two-stage bivariate logistic-Tobit model for the pedestrian-relevant safety analysis of signalized junctions was investigated, which helped to identify critical factors influencing the distribution of slight-injury vs. killed-and-serious-injury crashes [J4]. In addition, a Bayesian spatial logit model was developed to study the severity of pedestrian injuries due to traffic crashes at signalized intersections, which further showed that ignoring the spatial correlation could result in reduced goodness-of-fit of the model, underestimated variability and standard error of the parameters, as well as inconsistent, biased, or erroneous inferences [J10]. The above findings provide useful information for the formulation of effective road safety strategies to improve traffic and pedestrian safety [J3, C3].

717512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
717512.value: In most countries, including the People’s Republic of China, the U.S., and most of Europe, traffic drives on the right. Around 65% of the world’s population lives in countries with right-hand drive traffic, with the remaining 35% in left-hand drive countries, including Hong Kong. The different traffic rules lead to different attitudes and conventions for crossing roads, and foreign visitors face an increased risk of injury when using roads as pedestrians. This project adopted a naturalistic approach to studying pedestrian safety problems, based on field observations and statistical modeling tools. However, a cross-cultural study of the safety problems experienced by pedestrians crossing roads in locations with different driving rules, as mentioned above, would require the ability to distinguish local residents from foreign visitors, which is extremely difficult, if not impossible, in field observations. CAVE-based virtual reality technology, which is now reaching maturity, is a promising tool to develop a fully immersive pedestrian simulation experiment to measure the actual crossing performance of pedestrians from countries with different traffic rules. A research proposal on this subject, based on the preliminary findings of this project, was submitted for application to the RGC GRF in the 2017-2018 exercise.

717512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
717512.value: To address the need for sustainable urban development, expectations for knowledge-driven practice in transportation engineering and planning related to pedestrian activity have increased markedly. However, pedestrians remain vulnerable road users, and pedestrian injury and mortality are major road safety issues. In particular, signalized intersections have emerged as the locations most prone to pedestrian–vehicle conflict. Therefore, it is of paramount importance to understand the factors, including geometric design, signal control, and crossing behavior, that contribute to the risk of pedestrian injury and mortality at signalized intersections. In the context of vehicle–vehicle collisions, rich information on traffic volume, speed, and speed dispersion is available for analyzing the risk exposure. However, there is a lack of comprehensive analysis of the corresponding pedestrian exposure, and its implications for injury and mortality risks. In this study, we estimated pedestrian exposure at signalized intersections in Hong Kong through an extensive observational survey. Then, we established profiles for pedestrian exposure to crash and injury risks, and developed models of the pedestrian-involved crash frequency and injury severity to quantify pedestrian safety problems at signalized intersections. The findings will be invaluable for developing comprehensive road safety strategies for pedestrians and thus enhancing sustainable pedestrian safety in the long term.

717812.value: [Joint Optimization Framework]: We formulate an optimization problem for optimal social media service deployment over the long run, which models various charging plans and inter-connection conditions of different cloud data centers. [Demand Prediction]: We build an analytical model to describe information propagation following social connections and content correlations, and use the model to predict future content demand from each region. 717812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
717812.value: This project studies how to effectively deploy social media applications in the emerging multi-provider cloud platforms. Social media applications (e.g., Facebook, Twitter, YouTube) have revolutionized the way of people's communication and information acquisition in today's world. Allowing sharing of messages, photos, and videos among millions of users, social media applications are demanding unprecedentedly large volumes of system resources (storage, bandwidth, etc.), incurring huge operational cost to their operators. For example, YouTube reportedly costs Google more than 2 million USD on a daily basis. Cloud computing technologies have been said to be promising for supporting large-scale social media systems. Especially, the emerging global-scale multi-provider cloud, consisting of cloud data centers owned by different cloud providers over a wide span of geographic regions, is ideal for storing and serving dynamically user-generated contents with services in budget range of the application operator. Nevertheless, how indeed to dynamically deploy a social media application on a multi-provider cloud remains as significant, unsolved challenges: How can the application optimally select services from different cloud providers in different locations, given different charges and various inter-connection network conditions? How should social connections and content correlations be exploited, to efficiently replicate the large volumes of user-generated contents in different locations for timely retrieval? Given the dynamic nature of the system, how can the above be done on the fly, to guarantee service quality and minimize operational cost over the long run? In this project, we seek to answer the above questions with dynamic algorithms, designed to optimize cloud provider selection, content storage, and user services on the fly, and to enable long-term optimal operation of a social media application in a geo-distributed multi-provider cloud. In particular, social influence among users and various correlations among contents will be modeled and exploited, to effectively predict demands for different contents, that would arise from various geographic regions in the near future. These predicted demands will be utilized to enable dynamic provisioning algorithms, which proactively deploy social media services in the multi-provider cloud, and approach the long-term optimality of the system in operational cost minimization --- the optimality that an offline optimal solution achieves based on complete knowledge of the system over its entire span. We seek to verify effectiveness of our algorithms with solid theoretical analysis, as well as large-scale experiments with dynamic realistic traffic on distributed home-built and public cloud platforms.

717812.label: Realisation of objectives
717812.value: We have fully achieved Objectives 1-3 in this project to 100%, and achieved Objective 4 to 80%. Objective 1: For the main goal of designing an optimization framework for content replication and request dispatching for social media applications in a geo-distributed cloud, we proposed an efficient, online content migration and request distribution framework with the following features: (i) future demand prediction by novelly characterizing social influences among the users in a simple but effective epidemic model; (ii) one-shot optimal content migration and request distribution based on efficient optimization algorithms to address the predicted demand; and (iii) a Delta(t)-step look-ahead mechanism to adjust the one-shot optimization results towards the offline optimum. The results were reported in our publication 8.1 listed in Part C. For sub goal (1) in Objective 1, we designed online algorithms for cloud service plan selection, which dynamically make cost-minimizing decisions for an application provider on renting Spot VM instances or on-demand VM instances, or making long-term resource reservations. The results were reported in publications 9.4 and 9.5 in Part C. For sub goal (2), as stated in the midterm report, we resorted to a relatively high-level model to characterize the relationship between VM configuration (e.g., CPU, I/O) and the request processing delay, i.e., a shorter processing delay with higher-grade VMs; we set up optimization frameworks to compute optimal storage/VM rental to serve the VoD or video conferencing users with performance guarantees (e.g., bounded request response delay). The results were reported in publications 9.5, 9.6 and 9.7 in Part C. For sub goal (3), we designed an online algorithm for dynamic content migration and request dispatching in a content distribution network with a proven performance competitive ratio, and the results were reported in publication 9.6 in part C. For sub goal (4), we investigated similar optimization frameworks in two social media services, i.e., mobile social TV and mobile video conferencing, and proposed service deployment and content distribution strategies on geo-distributed clouds. In these systems, the content being distributed is elastic and the distribution persists over multiple time slots. The results were reported in publications 8.2 and 9.1 in Part C. Objective 2: For sub goal (1), we developed an effective epidemic model to characterize social influence among the users in the social media application, and predicted future demand from different regions by mapping the potential requests onto different regions according to the distribution of users and their social connections. The results were reported in publication 8.1 in Part C. We also extensively measured social influence propagation in real-world social networks (Youku and Tencent Weibo) and summarized propagation patterns and influential factors based on large volumes of traces collected. We further designed a neural network-based learning framework to predict the number of potential viewers and their geographic distribution. We then designed proactive video deployment algorithms based on the prediction framework. The results appeared in publication 8.3 in Part C. For sub goal (2), we applied an age-dependent branching process to model information diffusion in a microblogging social network, based on practical observations from Tencent Weibo, a popular microblogging site in China. This model enables careful characterization of the diffusion topology, the different delays for users to respond to new information, and the evolution of the size of the information cascade over time, which we believe more descriptive than the cascade or linear threshold model. We validated our model based on Tencent Weibo traces, and demonstrated its effectiveness in capturing information diffusion dynamics in the real world. The results were reported in publication 9.2 in Part C. For sub goal (3), we investigated time-varying social relationships, and designed a multi-armed bandit optimization algorithm to maximize influence propagation over time. The results were reported in publication 9.8 in Part C. Objective 3: We resolved in publication 8.1 the issue raised at the beginning of Objective 3 of our proposal, and obtained a positive answer to the question whether the subgradient algorithm still converges to the optimal solution, due to the special structure of the integer dual problem (A). We also designed dynamic algorithms to solve the optimization based on the idea of adjusting one-shot optimum to offline optimum using demand predications, and sub goal (1) has been achieved in the case that the content can be downloaded in one time slot. The case that the download of a content may last multiple time slots was investigated in publication 9.6 in Part C. For sub goal (2), we carefully studied the feasibility of designing an efficient online algorithm based on the classical paging algorithm. Our conclusion was that the paging algorithm is not suitable. Instead, we studied new online algorithm design techniques and designed efficient online algorithms in publications 8.5 and 9.6 in Part C. Through our investigation of deploying social media applications in geo distributed clouds, we identified another important, relevant area to investigate: how shall we efficiently upload the large volumes of (user generated) data from geo-distributed generation locations into the cloud, for processing and service to users from the cloud, and how shall we efficiently schedule bulk data transfer across data centers? We carefully studied these issues and designed online algorithms for timely, cost-minimizing bulk data transfer, with rigorous analysis. The results were reported in publications 8.4, 8.6 and 9.3 in Part C. Especially, in publication 8.4, the effect of lookahead windows of different sizes was carefully analyzed. Objective 4: We evaluated our algorithms reported in publications 8.4 and 8.6 using prototype systems implemented and deployed on the cluster in our lab. The evaluation results under real-world setup (practical charging models, social relationships, etc.) were reported in these publications. Algorithms in publication 8.3 were evaluated on the PlanetLab platform. We further verified the effectiveness of our algorithms and reported the results in publications 8.1, 8.2, 8.5, 9.1 and 9.7, using prototype system implementation and extensive real-world experiments under dynamic settings on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2), Google App Engine, or the Linode Cloud. We have made efforts on constructing a cross-institutional cloud testbed, but have found it very difficult due to different policy/security regulations of different institutes and lack of management and technical support in different institutes. So we have largely resorted to real-world public clouds for deploying our prototype systems and evaluating our algorithms in realistic environments.

717812.label: Major findings and research outcome
717812.value: In publication 8.1 listed in Part C, we proposed an efficient, online content migration and request distribution framework with the following features: (i) future demand prediction by novelly characterizing social influences among the users in a simple but effective epidemic model; (ii) one-shot optimal content migration and request distribution based on efficient optimization algorithms to address the predicted demand; and (iii) a Delta(t)-step look-ahead mechanism to adjust the one-shot optimization results towards the offline optimum. We designed online algorithms for cloud service plan selection, which dynamically make cost-minimizing decisions for an application provider on renting Spot VM instances or on-demand VM instances, or making long-term resource reservations. The results were reported in publications 9.4 and 9.5 in Part C. We also set up optimization frameworks to compute optimal resource allocation for cloud-based VoD, social TV or video conferencing applications with rigorous performance guarantees (e.g., bounded request response delay). The results were reported in publications 8.2, 9.1, and 9.7 in Part C. We also extensively measured social influence propagation in real-world social networks (Youku and Tencent Weibo) and summarized propagation patterns and influential factors based on large volumes of traces collected. We further designed learning frameworks to predict the number of potential viewers and their geographic distribution. The results appeared in publication 8.3 in Part C. We developed effective epidemic models to characterize social influence among the users in social networks, and investigated time-varying social relationships over time, for the design of optimization algorithms to maximize influence propagation over time. The results were reported in 9.2 and 9.8 in Part C. We designed novel, efficient online algorithms for content deployment and request dispatching in geo-distributed cloud CDNs in publications 8.5 and 9.6. Through our investigation of deploying social media applications in geo distributed clouds, we identified another important, relevant area to investigate on dynamic upload and inter-datacenter transfer of bulk data. In this topic area, we designed online algorithms for timely, cost-minimizing bulk data transfer, with rigorous performance analysis. The results were reported in publications 8.4, 8.6 and 9.3 in Part C.

717812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
717812.value: A cross-institutional cloud testbed would still be ideal for evaluating cloud-based systems and algorithms, with a set of unified equipment for researchers to experiment on. It will be very nice if such a platform can be built across different institutes in Hong Kong. We have experienced difficulty to build such a platform during the course of this project, due mainly to lack of management and technical support from different institutes, as well as the lack of funding. We look forward to an initiative from the RGC on building such a cross-institutional cloud testbed in Hong Kong.

717812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
717812.value: This project designed dynamic algorithms to optimize cloud provider selection, content storage, and user services on the fly, to enable long-term optimal operation of a social media application in a geo-distributed multi-provider cloud. We model social influence among users for effective demand prediction, that would arise from various geographic regions in the near future. We can utilize the predicted demands to enable dynamic provisioning algorithms, to approach long-term optimality of the system in operational cost minimization. Our models and algorithms can also be adapted to other applications with socially-connected participants, such as video conferencing and online TV. They are also able to facilitate next-generation social media systems with richer functionalities, for more efficient information exchange and dissemination in this digital era.

718612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718612.value: Cold-formed stainless steel structures have been increasingly used in structural and architectural applications. This is due to the aesthetic appearance, superior corrosion resistance, ease of maintenance and ease of construction. Stainless steel is more expensive than carbon steel, but taking into the consideration of corrosion resistance and aesthetic appearance, stainless steel structures have been increasingly used. It should be noted that a relatively new type of stainless steel in civil engineering application called “Lean Duplex” has been developed. The lean duplex stainless steel is much cheaper than the usual high strength duplex stainless steel and yet maintaining the strength of the material. Research on lean duplex stainless steel structures is limited. Connection in structures is one of the important and essential components. Furthermore, structures at elevated temperatures also need to be considered in design calculation. However, research on stainless steel connections at elevated temperatures is rarely found in literatures. Design rules of stainless steel bolted connections can be found in American, Australian/New Zealand and European specifications. However, these design rules are only applicable to ambient temperature (normal room temperature), but not applicable to structures at elevated temperatures. Therefore, it is important to investigate the structural behaviour of cold-formed stainless steel connections at elevated temperatures. The objectives of this research project are to provide experimental and numerical results of cold-formed stainless steel bolted connections at elevated temperatures. Tensile coupon tests on Lean Duplex, Austenitic and Austenitic with Titanium alloy stainless steels were conducted to determine the material properties at elevated temperatures. Finally, design rules for cold-formed stainless steel bolted connections at elevated temperatures are proposed. The research findings have been published in SCI indexed international journals and international conferences. The five objectives of the project have been achieved.

718712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718712.value: 隱式曲面是由三維空間中的座標函數定義的兩維幾何曲面。由於隱式曲面總是封閉的且能容易地區分一個物體的內部和外部，它們頻繁地用於固體的建模。近幾年，表達，製作和操縱隱式曲面的方法已變得強大而有效，在圖形學以及娛樂，計算機輔助設計和醫學影像等相關領域產生了許多新的關注。 儘管如此，為諸如自然生物，材料和機械等具有複雜的非均勻體質的物體構造高質的隱式表達仍是一個極具挑戰的任務。這是因為這類物體內部有非流形元素。這些非流形元素不能用傳統的隱式函數表示。爲了多區域造型和檢測，我們提出一類新的矢量隱式函數。這類函數叫做多相位隱式函數。它們能夠精確且高效地對非均勻體質的物體進行幾何建模。我們提出從有標注的數據計算多相位隱式函數的創新算法。這個算法從機器學習中的相關技術得到啓發，比已有的基於數據擬合的技術更為有效。我們進一步提出開發一個新穎的多相位水平集算法，用於跟蹤和優化動態非流形界面。 從這個研究項目得到的成果將顯著地推進隱式曲面造型和跟蹤方面的最高水準。我們的多相位隱式函數具有緊湊的表達，並且與顯示用的分辨率無關。它們能表達非流形元素，在把傳統的固體建模推廣到非均勻體質物體方面邁出了重要的一步。我們提議的多相位水平集算法能支持拓撲可變的非流形曲面的演變，是對已有的動態界面跟蹤技術的一個重要補充。 這個研究項目亦有重要的實用價值。為諸如自然生物和材料等具有非均勻體質的物體構造高質的數字模型具有重要的意義因為這樣的物體無處不在。這類數字模型在生物醫學研究，科學可視化以及教育培訓等方面具有重要的作用。

718712.label: Realisation of objectives
718712.value: During this project, we have investigated and completed all four (revised) project objectives. That is, we have developed an effective multiphase implicit geometric representation for heterogeneous volume objects each of which consists of multiple internal regions. We have developed an efficient algorithm that can accurately compute the aforementioned multiphase implicit representation from a collection of labeled data points. We have also developed a method for converting a polygonal model of a heterogeneous volume object into our implicit representation. Such a conversion produces a consistent "watertight" implicit model. Furthermore, we have developed a method for reconstructing 3D human models from sparse uncalibrated views using watertight implicit functions. In the following, let us discuss specific research activities that realize these objectives. We define multiphase implicit functions, MIF for short, as a type of vector-valued implicit functions for describing a partition of the 3D space into nonoverlapping regions so that the region membership of any point can be conveniently obtained. A MIF has multiple scalar components, the number of which is the same as the number of regions. Each scalar component is a continuous function of 3D coordinates. The scalar components in a MIF are not mutually independent. Within every region, the scalar component corresponding to that region takes the largest values among all components. Suppose a set of labeled data points are available for a decomposition of the 3D space into multiple regions. Each data point is associated with 3D coordinates and a label indicating its region membership. We have developed an algorithm for computing an analytical MIF from such labeled data points, and adopt multivariate polynomials as the class of analytical implicit functions. We observe that the label associated with a data point is more important than the function value at the same point. Thus our goal becomes seeking implicit functions that maximize the accuracy of predicted region labels. This goal is actually the same as classifier training in machine learning. More interestingly, support vector machines (SVMs) are a type of classifiers that use an implicit function to predict the class label of any testing data point. Therefore, we formulate the optimization of a MIF according to the training of a multicategory SVM where region labels in our problem are treated as class labels used by the SVM. Inside a heterogeneous volume object, the boundary surface of a region may have local geometry that is hard to model using polynomials. Furthermore, one region may have multiple disconnected subregions assigned with the same region label. It would also be hard to model such disconnected subregions using a polynomial. Because the level of structure complexity that can be modeled with a polynomial is limited, we perform adaptive spatial subdivision and represent subdivided boundary surfaces with a piecewise polynomial multiphase implicit. We choose octree-based adaptive subdivision because every subdivided node in an octree is an axis-aligned cube, which facilitates blending operations. Within every octree node, we compute a local polynomial multiphase implicit by solving the aforementioned optimization on the subset of training data falling into the octree node. If the classification error of the resulting implicit exceeds a threshold, we subdivide the octree node and recurse on every child node. Note that even when there is a large number of regions in a volume object, the number of is unlikely to exceed four, and we only need to represent the scalar components corresponding to these regions while leaving the other scalar components undefined. This is because at a non-manifold feature, there are typically only three or four simultaneously adjacent regions. To convert a polygonal model of a heterogeneous volume object into our implicit representation, one feasible strategy would be using multiple manifold meshes to create a volume with multiple internal regions, and further training a MIF to represent the geometry of this complex volume. To facilitate region label determination, we again build an octree for each of the manifold meshes, and obtain a binary label for every internal leaf node of the octree and every half face in the mesh. This binary label indicates whether an octree node or a half face is inside the mesh object or not. We further define a distinct Boolean variable for every participating mesh. Any region created from the meshes can be defined with a Boolean expression over these variables. We draw sample points inside the entire volume as well as near every face of the individual meshes. Then we test every sample point against each of the constructed octrees to determine whether it is inside each of the original meshes. The result is a sequence of binary values. The region membership of a sample point can be determined by evaluating the aforementioned Boolean expressions using these binary values. Finally we apply the aforementioned method to compute a MIF from these labeled training points. For the last objective related to 3D model reconstruction using implicit functions, we propose a two-stage algorithm. In first stage of our algorithm, we first apply the non-rigid dense correspondences (NRDC) algorithm to generate dense correspondences for camera calibration and point cloud reconstruction. Although NRDC works reasonably well in featureless regions, the reconstructed point cloud is still noisy with missing regions and the estimated camera parameters are of low accuracy which causes an imprecise visual hull. A watertight implicit function based template model is used as a deformable prior to fit the incomplete point cloud as well as the silhouettes in images. This can be formulated as an optimization problem. To deform the template model, the updated vertex positions are solved by a constrained Laplacian system. This produces a coarse 3D model. In the second stage, we refine this coarse model with geometric details, such as wrinkles, reconstructed from shading information. To successfully extract shading information from a surface with a non-uniform reflectance pattern (e.g., clothes), we adopt a hierarchical density based clustering algorithm to produce high-quality pixel clusters with uniform reflectance. Geometric details reconstructed from shading information estimated using our new method exhibit superior quality.

718712.label: Major findings and research outcome
718712.value: The geometry of heterogeneous volumetric objects with multiple internal materials can be represented using multiphase implicit functions, which can accurately model non-manifold region boundaries, accurately classify points into the regions they belong to, and correctly retrieve the biological or physical properties at any point within any region. Furthermore, multi-material volumetric objects originally represented as non-manifold meshes or multiple manifold meshes can be converted into multiphase implicit functions. These findings are reported in the first research output in Part C. Research outcome associated with these findings includes the mathematical definition of a multiphase implicit function, an algorithm for computing a multiphase implicit function from a set of labeled data points as well as an algorithm for converting a mesh-based multi-material object into a multiphase implicit object. When complex internal structures of a heterogeneous volumetric object cannot be accurately represented as a single multiphase implicit function, they should be adaptively subdivided spatially, and subdivided boundary surfaces of the internal regions can be represented piece by piece. This finding is also reported in the first research output in Part C. Research outcome associated with this finding includes an octree-based piecewise implicit representation for heterogeneous volumetric objects and a technique for blending multiphase implicit functions residing in adjacent octree cells. Complex texture and art patterns are 2D heterogeneous volumetric objects if texture elements with similar appearance are grouped together as a disconnected internal region. The boundaries of such texture regions can be represented using (multiphase) implicit functions. Accurate depiction of texture region boundaries can improve the quality of texture and art pattern synthesis. These findings are reported in the second research output in Part C. Research outcome associated with these findings includes a new optimization based texture and art pattern synthesis algorithm that explicitly performs boundary deformation and alignment using the level set method. Existing multi-view 3D reconstruction algorithms cannot handle sparse uncalibrated views effectively, and can only produce incomplete surface reconstruction. Representing the unknown 3D surface as a watertight deformable implicit surface can improve the accuracy and completeness of the reconstructed surface. Initializing this implicit surface using a template model can further improve the reconstruction quality. These findings are reported in the third research output in Part C. Research outcome associated with these findings includes a novel two-stage pipeline for reconstructing 3D models of human wearing regular clothes from sparse uncalibrated views using a watertight deformable human model as the template.

718712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
718712.value: Implicit surfaces have a wide range of applications in entertainment, engineering and medical imaging. A conventional implicit function can only model two regions simultaneously. To facilitate geometric modeling of heterogeneous volume objects where multiple regions may be simultaneously adjacent to each other, we propose a novel class of vector-valued implicit functions, called multiphase implicits, that are capable of accurately and compactly modeling complex non-manifold features. Multiphase implicits represent an important step in generalizing traditional solid modeling. Most natural organisms and materials, such as the human body, animals, fruits, and rocks, have complex volumetric compartments and structures. Constructing high-quality digital models for such natural organisms and materials is of vital importance because they exist everywhere, and literally everything we see is either a living being, a natural material or something made from these two. Our proposed multiphase implicits offer a systematic way to model the geometry of such natural objects and materials. The resulting digital volumetric models can play an important role in biomedical research, scientific visualization as well as educational and training activities.

718912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718912.value: The aim of this proposed research is to formulate and develop an effective scene categorization method for classifying natural scenes that are ambiguous by nature. The major causes of ambiguity in natural scenes include the scene content coming from different scene categories and different scene categories sharing common objects. As far as we know, no published method to date has been able to classify these ambiguous scenes successfully. Recently published scene categorization methods perform reasonably well on natural outdoor and indoor scenes, on the condition that these scenes are reasonably distinctive. Their performances deteriorate when a scene is naturally ambiguous. This explains the reason why most methods can only achieve 80~85% of classification success for a common 15 categories data set. In this project, we propose using the idea of sub-scenes to detect and classify these naturally ambiguous scenes. First we will divide a scene into sub-scenes, which can be viewed as a collection of image features that can be classified to one of the known categories. Second, a supervised approach will be employed for learning rules that govern the semantics between sub-scenes. Third, a category-specific bag-of-visual-word philosophy—in which scene features are represented by visual words in a codebook—will be extended to generate two descriptors for each sub-scene from its own features, and its neighborhood sub-scenes. This approach has been proven to be quite effective in increasing classification accuracy. Fourth, similarity between scenes will be formulated by a measure of probability distance and used to train and test a kernel-based classifier. Finally, based on the initial classification, ambiguity of a scene can be detected by measuring the category distributions of the candidate sub-scene codewords. This will result in the generation of a new scene category from the initial category and a list of the sub-scenes with their corresponding categories, as well as determining whether a sub-scene is ambiguous and the probability of it belonging to other scene categories. Developing an effective scene categorization method will help in the understanding of natural scenes and open up the possibility of including complex scene contexts in many areas of vision research and applications such as image/video retrieval from the Internet or image databases, visual surveillance of human activities and the interaction of intelligent vehicle/robots with their environment. 本研究的目的在於對模棱兩可、有歧義的場景建立和探索一種有效的場景分類方法。在自然場景中，造成場景分類有歧義的主要原因包括場景包含了來自不同的場景類別的內容，以及某些對像同時屬於不同的場景類別。據我們所知，迄今已公布的方法中，沒有能夠成功分類這些有歧義的場景。最近發表的場景分類方法在場景類別相當明確的情況下，對於室內和室外場景都有相當好的表現。但是，當場景本身帶有歧義，這些方法往往表現退化。這也解釋了為什麼大多數方法對於15場景的公開數據集的分類正確率只能達到80〜85％。在這個項目中，我們提出使用子場景來檢測和分類這些本身帶有歧義的場景的想法。首先我們將整體場景分割為若干具有某個已知類別特征的子場景的組合。其次，運用監督學習的方法，學習子場景之間的邏輯關系及規則。第三，在場景特征由碼本中的視覺詞語表示的基礎上，特定類別的詞袋模型理念將被擴展，為每個子場景的自身特征和其與鄰域子場景的關系提供兩個描述表達。此表達方法可有效地提高分類精度。第四，子場景與各類別的相似性以度量其之間的距離而表達為概率分布，並用基於核的分類方法進行訓練及測試。最後，基於初始場景分類，子場景類別的分布可以幫助檢測出有歧義的場景。這可激發從最初的場景類別及子場景類別分布來生成一個新的類，並且反饋檢測子場景屬於其他類別的可能性。建立一種有效的場景分類方法，將有助於對自然場景的理解，並能開創在計算機視覺研究諸項領域中利用復雜場景的內在邏輯結構規則的信息的可能。諸如在互聯網或數據庫中圖像及視頻的檢索、人群活動的可視化監控、以及智能車或機器人與環境交互等研究領域中，都可運用場景內在邏輯結構來提升研究。

718912.label: Realisation of objectives
718912.value: All three objectives have been achieved satisfactory. We proposed a methodology for categorizing naturally ambiguous scenes initially. During the span of the project, we formulated supervised and unsupervised sub-scene generation methods, using perceptual rules and enhanced contextual related potentials based on Conditional Random Field. We have also proposed graphical model to train sub-scene prototypes under each semantic classes. These proposed methods were tested on public data sets and proved to perform better than the best published ones. We further research into the problem of scene ambiguity and how scenes appear to be ambiguous to a standard classifier. By using sub-scenes within the context of a graphical model, we are able to effective differentiate them within the top two predictions. Based on this understanding, we have also developed methods in three directions: (1) Hybrid graphical model: combine non-causal and causal cues in natural images in a CRF and Bayesian Network framework; (2) we further improve the hierarchical conditional random field model to resolve problems of the over-smoothing effect of pairwise potential, incorrect inference guidance of higher order potential and uncommon object combinations suppression of co-occurrence potential; (3) Deep learning: we designed convolutional neural network for scene categorization. We have tested all these methods using public data sets and the first two proposed methods perform quite well compare with other leading edge methods. The third showed potential but refinement is needed. In conclusion, we have achieved the objectives of this project and in fact extended a bit further in various directions beyond our objectives to gain knowledge of how best we can do scene categorization in the future.

718912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
718912.value: Scene categorization is a vital task in the artificial intelligence of future mobile machines (autonomous vehicles or robots). Natural scenes are inherently ambiguous that makes object identification impossible. Our proposal of using sub-scene paves a new way of constructing scene semantics that would make logical sense. We believe the recognition success rates of the proposed methods are the best and given improvement on the quality of images (the public data sets contain images of low quality) and when a sequence of images of the scene is being considered, the proposed methods are potentially practical for the real world environments.

719012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719012.value: 近年来，各种水环境中的新兴环境污染物，包括内分泌干扰物、抗生素等，在世界各地引起了广泛的关注。如何在废水处理过程中去除这些污染物值得特别关注，因为废水是上述污染物一个主要的环境排放途径。虽然以前的一些研究表明，这些污染物可以从通过生物吸附和生物降解过程加以去除，但对其中所涉及的微生物降解通路和相关的功能基因的了解还是非常有限的。因此，目前还很难预测它们在废水生物处理过程中的迁移转化。在本研究中，首先将利用实验室反应器富集能够降解所选择的新型环境污染物的菌，并将其分离才纯化。然后，使用具有很高解析度的四极杆飞行时间质谱仪分析确定可能的降解产物。同时使用新一代的高通量基因组测序技术搜索相关生物降解的功能基因。这项研究的成功将为联合使用高分辨率四极杆飞行时间质谱仪（仪器分析）和新一代的高通量基因组（分子分析）探索污染物的生物降解和相关降解基因提供方法学的基础架构。

719012.label: Realisation of objectives
719012.value: Objective 1: To enrich and isolate the effective EP-degrading microorganisms. The previous studies have shown that some EPs may be biodegraded by various microorganisms. In this project, EP-degraders will be enriched in laboratory scale reactors and isolated using the culture method established before. Firstly, we try to establish the detection methods for the target Eps. We reported significant suppressive matrix effects in analyses of six EPs in activated sludge, sterilized activated sludge and untreated sewage by ultra-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Quantitative matrix evaluation on selected EPs supplemented the limited quantification data of matrix effects on mass spectrometric determination of EPs in complex environment samples. The observed matrix effects were chemical-specific and matrix-dependent, with the most pronounced average effect (− 55%) was found on sulfadiazine in sterilized activated sludge. After correcting the matrix effects by post-spiking known amount of EPs, the removal mechanisms and biotransformation kinetics of selected EPs in activated sludge system were revealed by batch experiment. Experimental data elucidated that the removal of target EPs in the activated sludge process was mainly by biotransformation while contributions of adsorption, hydrolysis and volatilization could be neglected. High biotransformation efficiency (52%) was observed on diclofenac while other three compounds (sulfadiazine, sulfamethoxazole and roxithromycin) were partially biotransformed by ~ 40%. The two sulfonamide-degrading cultures were inoculated with the same activated sludge, and were enriched with defined medium in a semi-batch mode for 812 days. After the early acclimation stage (70 days), either SDZ or SMX was added as sole carbon source in the loading feed with incrementally increasing concentrations (50, 100 and 200 mg/L). Our previous study characterized the SDZ enrichment community at day 285 with PCR-cloning approach, and isolated two SDZ-degrading Arthrobacter sp. D2 and D4. We also established the 2-AP enrichment seeded with subculture of SDZ enrichment (at day 767) with an aim to select for the growth of 2-AP degraders. The initial stage was operated for 23 days and was supplied with 100 mg/L SDZ together with 100 mg/L 2-AP as carbon sources, after which SDZ was removed from the feed. The loading concentration of 2-AP was increased to 200 mg/L over the following 22 days. Metagenomic samples were collected from this enrichment at two time points (day 23, SDZ-2-AP enrichment; day 45, 2-AP enrichment) considering the carbon source perturbations and stable 2-AP-degrading ability (measured as TOC removal rate) of the microbial communities. The sulfonamide-degrading consortia described here can stably accomplished complete mineralization of SMX or SDZ within 5 days under high sulfonamide loading. We further selected bisphenol A (BPA) as a targeted compound to enrich a degrading microbial community, established of the prediction method by utilization of metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and target metabolomics and further tested the interaction occurring in the enriched consortia by using pure cultures and co-culture. Metagenomics suggested the present of BPA degradation gene in two Sphingomonas species. Similar method was applied to study characterize the potential cyanide-degrading bacteria. Objectives 2: To characterize and identify the degradation products/metabolites of the three selected EPs using high-resolution liquid-chromatograph quadrupole time-of-flight mass-spectrum (LC-QToF-MS). The possible degradation pathways will be speculated out based on the identification results. For sulfadiazine, two aerobic sulfadiazine (SDZ) degrading bacterial strains, D2 and D4, affiliated with the genus Arthrobacter, were isolated from SDZ-enriched activated sludge. The degradation of SDZ by the two isolates followed first-order decay kinetics. The half-life time of complete SDZ degradation was 11.3 h for strain D2 and 46.4 h for strain D4. Degradation kinetic changed from non-growth to growth-linked when glucose was introduced as the cosubstrate, and accelerated biodegradation rate was observed after the adaption period. Both isolates could degrade SDZ into 12 biodegradation products via 3 parallel pathways, of which 2-amino-4-hydroxypyrimidine was detected as the principal intermediate product toward the pyrimidine ring cleavage. For BPA, genes encoding enzymes involved in 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde (4-HBD)-mediate pathways were detected from the two Sphingomonas species, a Pseudomonas species, and an Achromobacter species, while a partial and a complete 4-HAP-mediated pathway were detected from the Sphingomonas species and the Pseudomonas species, respectively. The present of 4-HBZ and 4-HPAT were predicted in spite of the absent of these compounds from metabolomics analysis in the BPA batch. An assumed that genes involved in degradation of BPA’s intermediates had similar time course expression patterns to BPA conversion and citrate cycle-related genes were then made for detecting acting gene pathway during degradation. Basing the assumption, we speculated both Sphingomonas and Pseudomonas prior utilized intermediates via 4-HBD-mediated pathway rather then 4-HAP-mediated pathway during the first 24 hrs although the dynamics changes of 4-HBD and 4-HAP were similar in the BPA batch. The Pseudomonas may compete with Sphingomonas on 4-HBZ rather than 4-HBD in spite of 4-HBD dehydrogenase presented in the genome. Objectives 3: To sequence the whole genome of the isolated pure cultures using next generation high-throughput sequencing strategy to search for the genes responsible for biodegradation of selected EPs. Compared with five Arthrobacter strains reported previously, D2 and D4 were the only Arthrobacter strains which could degrade SDZ as the sole carbon source. The draft genomes of D2 and D4, with the same completeness of 99.7%, were compared to other genomes of related species. Overall, these two isolates shared high genomic similarities with the s-triazine-degrading Arthrobacter sp. AK-YN10 and the sulfonamide-degrading bacteria Microbacterium sp. C448. In addition, the two genomes contained a few significant regions of difference which may carry the functional genes involved in sulfonamide degradation. For BPA, based on the speculation, we further hypothesized that the Sphingomonas species started BPA degradation, and then Pseudomonas and Achromobacter followed to compete on 4-HBD or 4-HBZ, while 4-HAP may be consumed mainly by the other species. Batch experiments by using pure cultures, co-culture, and mixed community evidenced that participation of 4-HBZ and 4-HPAT and accumulation of 4-HPAT occurred while 4-HBD and 4-HBZ were quickly consumed in Sphingomonas and co-culture experiments, proving the correctness of the prediction by metagenomics and the assumption made by metatranscriptomics. It further confirmed the bacterial interaction occurring in the community during degradation.

719012.label: Major findings and research outcome
719012.value: Established the methods of microbial community analysis methods using different consortia (Publications 1, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, and 11) and the analytical methods of UPLC-MS-MS for emerging pollutants (Publication 15). Constructed the degradation gene database and explore its application in the understanding of emerging pollutants in different communities (Publications 2, 3, 5, 7, 13, and 14). Develop the multi-omics methods (combined metagenomics and metatranscriptomics) in the mixed engineered microbial consortia (Publication 12). Finally, the methods developed in this project were combined to be applied in the study of the degradation of sulfadiazine (Publication 16). Two aerobic sulfadiazine (SDZ) degrading bacterial strains, D2 and D4, affiliated with the genus Arthrobacter, were isolated from SDZ-enriched activated sludge. The degradation of SDZ by the two isolates followed first-order decay kinetics. The half-life time of complete SDZ degradation was 11.3 h for strain D2 and 46.4 h for strain D4. Degradation kinetic changed from nongrowth to growth-linked when glucose was introduced as the cosubstrate, and accelerated biodegradation rate was observed after the adaption period. Compared with five Arthrobacter strains reported previously, D2 and D4 were the only Arthrobacter strains which could degrade SDZ as the sole carbon source. The draft genomes of D2 and D4, with the same completeness of 99.7%, were compared to other genomes of related species. Overall, these two isolates shared high genomic similarities with the s-triazine-degrading Arthrobacter sp. AK-YN10 and the sulfonamide-degrading bacteria Microbacterium sp. C448. In addition, the two genomes contained a few significant regions of difference which may carry the functional genes involved in sulfonamide degradation.

719012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
719012.value: The manuscript on bisphenol A is under preparation and will be finished in the second half of 2017 and submitted to Applied and Environmental Microbiology. Further study is being conducted to investigate the metatranscriptomic profile during degradation of sulfadiazine. Hopefully, it will be finished in in the second half of 2017 and a manuscript will be prepared based on the results.

719012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
719012.value: Emerging pollutants (EPs) in wastewater treatment plants is of particular concern because wastewater is one of the main disposal and exposure routes of these EPs. The study on the biodegradation pathway and relevant microorganism/genes are very limited. In this study, EP-degraders were enriched in laboratory scale reactors and isolated using the culture method. We established the methods of microbial community analysis methods and the analytical methods for emerging pollutants, constructed the degradation gene database and explored its application in understanding emerging pollutants, and developed the multi-omics methods (combined metagenomics and metatranscriptomics) in the mixed engineered microbial consortia. Finally, the methods developed in this project were applied in the study of the degradation of sulfadiazine and bisphenol A. The degradation products of the selected EPs were characterized using mass spectrum. The possible degradation pathways were speculated and confirmed using the reference compounds. The whole genome of the isolated pure cultures was sequenced using next generation high-throughput sequencing strategy to search for the genes which are responsible for biodegradation of sulfadiazine and bisphenol A. The success of this study demonstrated the combination of instrumental analysis and molecular analysis in exploring of biodegradation pathways and degradation genes of emerging pollutants.

719312.value: 普式計算環境下對多用戶數據的私隱保護機制

719312.label: Project Objectives
719312.value: Propose new security and privacy models for data aggregation in multi-user environments with untrusted aggregator and potential colluding users. Investigate theoretical limitations on the accuracy of privacy-preserving aggregation. Design provably secure and private multi-user periodic aggregation mechanisms for various statistics such as sum, average, and variance. The mechanisms should avoid costly communication during each aggregation. Define notions of privacy granularity with which a user can specify the desired privacy level, for example, in clustering applications to balance against the quality of classification. Combine our methods to implement privacy-preserving recommendation applications using real-world data, for instance the publicly available Netflix database, and compare the accuracy of our methods with other existing methods.

719312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719312.value: Handheld devices such as Android phones, iPhones, and iPads have gained tremendous popularity in the past couple of years, and many applications have been developed on these devices to provide users with personalized services. For instance, a restaurant or movie recommendation application can make a suggestion based on a user’s current location, past consumption habit, average ratings, and preference of other similar users. However, as these devices are constantly collecting personal data from the users, there is an increasing concern on privacy infringement in these ubiquitous computing environments. There are current approaches that protect user privacy by refusing to release any sensitive data, but this would make applications less useful and users would not enjoy the benefits brought by these personalized services. We shall investigate how to utilize sensitive user data and study what techniques can give a good tradeoff between user privacy and the utility of collected data. In particular, we will consider several common problems in ubiquitous computing to illustrate our methods with practical considerations. One novel aspect of our framework is that we will combine privacy and security notions to capture the scenario that the aggregator and other users are untrusted. On a high level, our definitions are based on the randomized framework of differential privacy such that when one user changes his input data, the adversary cannot detect this change, because the information received by the adversary has similar distribution as before, or the adversary has limited computational power. We shall investigate the theoretical limitations on the accuracy of privacy-preserving aggregation against computationally unbounded adversaries and under low bandwidth conditions. On the other hand, using applied cryptographic techniques, we shall design mechanisms that are provably secure against polynomial-time adversaries, efficient for periodic aggregation and achieve small error. Moreover, our frameworks allow a user to specify the desired granularity level of privacy to balance against the quality of service he receives. As users place increasing pressure on application developers to respect their privacy, our designs will give evidence that it is possible to achieve both privacy and utility. Moreover, our privacy frameworks will give formal standards for drafting relevant privacy laws. We believe this project will form a solid theoretical foundation and bring us closer to truly secure and private ubiquitous computing.

719312.label: Realisation of objectives
719312.value: Objective 1: We have used two approaches to develop new security and privacy models. In the first approach, the idea is to use random noise to protect sensitive data as in the notion of differential privacy. We have adapted this notion to define models in the client-server setting, in which there is no peer-to-peer interaction. Even for single-round computation of the simple sum aggregation function, we have shown that the additive error incurred must be of order at least square root of the number of users in the system, if we assume that the adversary has unbounded computational power. We have also considered a more realistic model in which users can go offline. In this case, the model ensures that the remaining users can still generate sufficient randomness to maintain privacy of sensitive data. This work has led to a patent “Privacy-preserving aggregation of time-series data”. In the second approach, we use randomization to hide the access pattern of data on the server to preserve the privacy of users, in the manner of oblivious RAM (ORAM). Since users can be compromised or colluded, we have designed privacy models under the secure computation settings, in which we assume the adversary can observe the data access pattern on the user’s side. We have a formal description of the secure computation models that concern computation cost on both the client and the server sides. We observe that asymptotic bandwidth overhead might be inadequate at characterizing practical performance, and instead have formulated models in which the circuit complexity will be the measure of efficiency. Our results are published in the CCS 2014 paper “SCORAM: Oblivious RAM for Secure Computation”. Objective 2: As a first step for designing secure and private aggregation mechanisms for various statistics, we have considered the problem of finding heavy hitters among multi-users in a streaming setting. We have designed a distributed protocol, in which the untrusted aggregator can detect the heavy hitters and their approximate frequencies. Our protocol is scalable in the settings where the volume of streaming data is large, since we guarantee low memory usage and processing overhead by each user, and low communication overhead between the users and the aggregator. This result forms part of the MPhil thesis of Mingfei Li. To design secure mechanisms for more general statistics, currently we have investigated oblivious versions of various common data structures such as linked-lists, stacks and priority queues. We have employed ORAM techniques to implement such data structures, and we have also exploited the access pattern graph on user data to design protocols with low overhead bandwidth. In order to design secure protocols that can perform more general tasks other than summation, we have utilized oblivious data structures to hide the data access pattern when users request data blocks from the server. Our framework can support common data structures such as map/set, priority queue, stack, linked-list, etc. We have performed several case studies to apply our techniques. For instance, we have considered an oblivious dynamic memory allocator that can hide memory usage that is triggered by the common malloc and free operations. We have also considered secure protocols that compute more sophisticated statistics that are needed in applications such as shortest-path distances and maximum flow. The results are published in the CCS paper “Oblivious Data Structures”. Motivated by the recent popularity of the decentralized cryptocurrency Bitcoin, we have designed a distributed private voting protocol on the bitcoin blockchain, which essentially is computing the sum and the majority statistics. Unlike traditional voting, there is also a money transfer attached to the voting result. Specifically, there are two candidates and a group of voters, each of whom holds 1 bitcoin and decides one’s preference between the two candidates. The protocol transfers all bitcoins to the most preferred candidate, while privacy and irrevocability are guaranteed. Our bitcoin voting protocols have been published in the ICICS 2015 paper “How to Vote Privately Using Bitcoin”. Objective 3: In order to consider the notion of security and privacy granularity, we have developed a model in which users can decide the data block size on which atomic ORAM operations are performed. We have analyzed the effect of the data block size on the number of levels of recursions to store the position map used in an ORAM. We have developed protocols that exploit the tradeoffs between data block size and communication overhead. Our techniques show that for data granularity of size at least log^2 N bits, the bandwidth overhead achieved will be close to the theoretical optimum. The result has appeared in the CCS 2015 paper “Circuit ORAM: On Tightness of the Goldreich-Ostrovsky Lower Bound”. Moreover, using a metric space to specify data granularity, we have also discovered that the doubling dimension of the pattern access graph can facilitate efficient clustering of data blocks to achieve lower communication overhead bandwidth. The result has appeared in the CCS 2014 paper “Oblivious Data Structures”. Motivated by private voting verification, we have studied the minimum independent set partition problem. In this problem, each user has some Boolean vector of dimension N, indicating his voting preference. Moreover, a granularity parameter c is given such that the goal is to partition the dimensions into c subsets such that for each subset of dimension, the projection of the N vectors onto those dimensions specified by the subset has maximum cardinality for ensuring privacy. We have shown some hardness results for this problem, which has appeared in the COCOON 2015 paper “On the Complexity of the Minimum Independent Set Partition Problem”. Objective 4: We have designed a private protocol for monitoring heavy hitters, which are useful in recommending popular items. We have analyzed our distributed protocol on the Netflix Contest Dataset, which contains n = 17770 movies with 480189 users’ ratings from 1999-11-11 to 2005-12-31. Our experiments have shown that our protocol can achieve low error and maintain low communication cost. We have also considered using social recommendation techniques in peer-to-peer networks under the setting in which users might not reveal their private data. We have considered our data dissemination protocols on a subgraph of the Twitter-Network crawled by Yang and Leskovec that contains 50,000 peers and 260,000 edges. Experiments show that our protocols have low communication cost and are robust against selfish and colluding users. The results have appeared in the ICCCN Workshop on Wireless Mesh and Ad-hoc Networking 2014. Moreover, we have evaluated our protocols using secure computation in ORAM under the circuit complexity measure. For instance, we have evaluated the performance of various oblivious data structures such as stack, map/set and priority queue. We have also carried out experiments for more complicated tasks such as dynamic memory allocation, random walk on the grid and shortest path queries on planar graphs. The results are reported in the CCS 2014 paper “Oblivious Data Structures”. For our bitcoin voting protocol, we have evaluated the performance to carry out zero-knowledge proofs required in the protocol. Moreover, we have submitted proper transactions on the blockchain to show the practicality of our methods. The results are published in the ICICS 2015 paper “How to Vote Privately Using Bitcoin”.

719312.label: Major findings and research outcome
719312.value: In this project, we developed new security and privacy models. Specifically, we use randomization to hide the access pattern of data on the server to preserve the privacy of users, in the manner of oblivious RAM (ORAM). Our results appear in the CCS 2014 paper “SCORAM: Oblivious RAM for Secure Computation”. Based on our privacy and security models, we have designed protocols for evaluating various statistics and performing different tasks. For instance, we have implemented oblivious data structures such as map/set, priority queue, stack, linked-list. Moreover, our protocols can achieved more complicated tasks such as dynamic memory allocation, random walk on the grid and shortest path queries on planar graphs. The protocol descriptions and experimental results appear in the CCS 2014 paper “Oblivious Data Structures”. In terms of real world-application, we have designed a distributed private voting protocol on the bitcoin blockchain. We have tested the feasibility of our protocol on the blockchain. The results appear in the ICICS 2015 paper “How to Vote Privately Using Bitcoin”. Addressing the notion of security and privacy granularity, we have developed a model in which users can decide the data block size on which atomic ORAM operations are performed. We have analyzed the effect of the data block size on the number of levels of recursions to store the position map used in an ORAM. The result is published in the CCS 2015 paper “Circuit ORAM: On Tightness of the Goldreich-Ostrovsky Lower Bound”. Motivated by private voting verification, we have investigated the complexity of the minimum independent set partition problem. In this problem, a granularity parameter c is given such that the goal is to partition some given set of indices into c subsets to maintain certain privacy guarantees. Our hardness results have appeared in the COCOON 2015 paper “On the Complexity of the Minimum Independent Set Partition Problem”. We have also employed social recommendation techniques in peer-to-peer networks under the setting in which users might not reveal their private data to design protocols for data dissemination. We have tested our protocols on the Twitter-Network. The results have appeared in the ICCCN Workshop on Wireless Mesh and Ad-hoc Networking 2014. Moreover, research graduate students are involved in this project. In particular, 2 PhD and 2 MPhil students have based part of their theses on the results achieved in this project. Finally, this project has led to a patent “Privacy-preserving aggregation of time-series data”, which shows that the results have practical impact.

719312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
719312.value: We have used oblivious RAM as a technique to protect the access pattern of sensitive data. The next step to employ this in a large-scale multi-user setting is to consider generalization of this model that supports parallel accesses. In many applications such as cloud outsourcing, secure processor design, and secure multi-party computation, parallelism is the adopted paradigm and indeed modern computing architectures such as multi-core processors or cluster computing have already supported parallel computing. Hence, a natural future direction is to apply our techniques to oblivious parallel ORAM, which is a basic building block for parallel computing, as in the case for its sequential counterpart ORAM. A central question is how to achieve the optimal overhead in the parallel case. Moreover, in scenarios with multiple CPUs, it is also an interesting direction to investigate any potential tradeoff between the parallel runtime and the total work.

719312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
719312.value: In this project, we have investigated how to utilize sensitive user data and study the techniques that give a good tradeoff between user privacy and the utility of collected data. In particular, we have developed private protocols for tackling several common problems in the multi-user setting. Examples include basic building blocks in computer science such as stack, map/set and priority queue. On a high level, we use a randomization framework to protect the privacy of user data. We have derived the theoretical guarantees of our protocols and also tested their performance in practical scenarios using real-world datasets. As modern users are increasingly aware of their privacy, our designs have shown that it is possible to achieve both privacy and utility. In conclusion, we believe that this project has contributed to (i) forming a solid theoretical foundation for secure and private computing with multi-users, and (ii) illustrating the practicality of our methods.

719512.value: Develop a low cost and high throughput method to fabricate reliable contact electrodes on nanostructured Bi2Te3 alloys for solar thermoelectric generators (STEGs). This method will be applied to fabricate metallic electrodes on other nanostructured thermoelectric materials, such as lead telluride and silicon germanium. 719512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719512.value: 熱電轉換裝置使用熱電材料將熱能轉換成電能，反之亦可行。此裝置沒有移動物件且無噪音，可以用來產生動力或作為固態冷卻，如太陽熱能轉換、廢熱回收、積體電路晶片和高能雷射的冷卻。最近幾年，柰米熱電材料顯著的提升了熱電性能指數(ZT)，因為奈米結構增加了晶界進而降低了材料的熱傳導係數。其中碲化鉍(Bi2Te3)合金半導體是最廣為使用且操作溫度較低的熱電材料。使用奈米碲化鉍材料已被證實可達到高效能的熱電轉換。然而，現行在奈米熱電材料上使用濺鍍方式製作的接觸電極造成了不穩定的接觸電阻，因而降低了裝置的可靠度。濺鍍的真空設備昂貴且耗時，亦不適合量產。由此可知，熱電轉換裝置不僅需要高熱電性能指數的材料，也需要穩定的接觸電極。此外，許多基礎研究均集中在熱電材料本身，卻較少對其接觸界面作探討。 因此，此研究計畫專注於 (1) 用低成本和高產能的方式在奈米熱電材料上製造穩定可靠的接觸電極，(2) 探討接觸界面上熱與電傳遞的行為以利於設計高效能的熱電裝置。此項研究的成果期能促進奈米熱電材料的廣泛使用與熱電裝置的產業化。

719512.label: Realisation of objectives
719512.value: Whereas past work has focused on the enhancement of thermoelectric materials rather than interfacial properties, this project aims to explore the interface between nanostructured thermoelectric materials and metallic contact electrodes. It comprises two parts: (1) fabricating reliable contact electrodes at low cost and high throughput on nanostructured thermoelectric materials, and (2) studying the fundamentals of heat transport at the interfacial region to understand its impact of contact performances. A cost-effective and reliable Ni–Au contact on nanostructured Bi2Te3-based alloys for a solar thermoelectric generator (STEG) is reported. The use of MPS SAMs creates a strong covalent binding and more nucleation sites with even distribution for electroplating contact electrodes on nanostructured thermoelectric materials. A reliable high-performance flat-panel STEG can be obtained by using this new method. The IMC (interfacial metallic compound) between Bi2Te3 and Ni barrier has been investigated and found the difference between the IMC on nanostructured Bi2Te3 and bulk Bi2Te3. The Ni layer electroplated on a zone-melted Bi2Te3 substrate (anisotropic crystal structure) had a small grain size and a high grain boundary density, and one IMC, (Cu,Ni)6Sn5, formed at the interface between SAC405 and Ni after joining. The other (Ni,Cu)3Sn4 phase formed at the (Cu,Ni)6Sn5/Ni interface after thermal aging and grew at a much faster rate with increasing the aging time. In contrast, the Ni layer electroplated on a ball-milled/hot-pressed Bi2Te3 substrate (isotropic crystal structure) had a large grain size and a low grain boundary density, and only the (Cu,Ni)6Sn5 phase formed at the SAC405/Ni interface with a very sluggish growth rate after joining and thermal aging. Since the IMCs were electrically resistive and mechanically brittle, the latter solder joint with a large-grained Ni layer on a ball-milled/hot-pressed Bi2Te3 substrate appeared to have better reliability.

719512.label: Major findings and research outcome
719512.value: We have presented a new technique for deposition of an adhesive, uniform and thick metallic layer onto a nanostructured Bi2Te3-based material pretreated with functionalized self-assembled MPS. The use of an MPS thin layer not only provides a strong covalent binding but also creates more nucleation sites with even distribution for nickel electroplating. The deposition of MPS SAMs followed by the electroplating process on the nanostructured thermoelectric materials can be achieved by low temperature and solution-based processing, which is significantly more cost-effective.

719512.value: This project developed a fabrication method of reliable contact electrodes at low cost and high throughput on nanostructured thermoelectric materials for solar thermoelectric generators, and studied the fundamentals of heat transport at the contact interface to advance our understanding for designing high-performance thermoelectric devices. The findings are expected to stimulate research interest for industrial applications of thermoelectric devices using nanostructured thermoelectric materials for energy generation and energy savings.

rows: 1. To explore and control the deformation modes in the micrometre, sub-micrometre and nanometre regimes, with an emphasis on verifying whether or not deformation twins can be suppressed or promoted in each size regime.
2. To understand the underlying physical mechanisms responsible for deformation twinning in each size regime.

719712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719712.value: With the recent increasing use of micrometre-sized and sub-micrometre-sized metallic materials in technological applications, there are strong needs to understand the microstructure-property relationship in these small-sized materials, especially the evolution of microstructure during deformation. In general, the deformation of metals can occur via dislocations and twinning. Most of the current research on small-sized metallic materials only focus on dislocation-mediated deformation, while studies on twinning are rare. Therefore, the present project will be devoted to study twinning behaviour in small-sized metallic samples in order to provide a more complete picture on the understanding of their deformation mechanisms. The evolution of dislocations during deformation in the small-sized samples has been found to be largely different from bulk samples and is affected by the sample size. It may be expected that twinning behaviour in small-sized samples could be also affected by the sample size. From a theoretical point of view, we argue that the occurrence of twinning, especially for face-centered-cubic metals with low stacking fault energy, should be affected by the sample size according to three regimes of the latter, namely, (1) micrometre regime; (2) sub-micrometre regime; (3) nanometre regime. If the sample size is within the micrometre regime, both dislocation glide and twinning can take place as dislocation pile-ups can be formed during the deformation in this size regime. Dislocation pile-ups can provide sufficient stress concentration to initiate twinning. In the sub-micrometre regime, dislocation glide will be the dominant deformation mechanism as most of the dislocations will leave the sample during deformation, resulting in no dislocation pile-ups for the nucleation of twinning. Twinning is suppressed in the sub-micrometre regime. On the contrary, twinning will be promoted again and becomes the dominant deformation mechanism in the nanometre regime as the stress required for twinning nucleation in this regime is smaller than the one for dislocation nucleation. The above three size regimes are derived from theoretical analysis. The present project will provide systematic experiments to verify such theoretical analysis and determine experimentally the critical size for the transition between each size regime. As suggested by the theoretical analysis, the critical size depends on the stacking fault energy. Therefore, different materials with different stacking fault energy will be studied as well in this project. 近年來，越來越多微米級甚至亞微米級大小的金屬材料被廣泛運用於各種新技術領域，所以有緊迫的需要來深入理解這些微小金屬材料的微觀組織結構和力學性能之間的關系，特別是要理解塑性變形過程中，它們微觀組織是如何演變的。通常來說，金屬的塑性變形可以通過位錯滑移和產生孿晶來實現。目前，絕大部分關於微小金屬材料的塑性變形機理研究都只是從位錯的角度出發，幾乎沒有研究關注孿晶的影響。為了彌補這方面的空缺，本項目將重點研究孿晶的產生和演化規律如何影響微小金屬材料的塑性變形機制。 近期大量的研究表明，在塑性變形過程中，微米級金屬材料的位錯演化規律完全不同於塊體材料的演化規律。基於這些研究成果，可以預計在塑性變形過程中，微米級金屬材料的孿晶產生和演化規律也可能不同於塊體材料的演化規律。對於低層錯能的面心立方金屬材料，單純從理論分析的角度出發，我們認為它們的孿晶在塑性變形過程中的演化規律將遵循三個不同的模式，這些規律取決於材料的尺寸大小。當材料尺寸在微米級別時，位錯和孿晶可以同時產生，這是因為材料尺寸足夠大，可以形成位錯的堆積，進而可以產生足夠大的應力集中，最終導致孿晶在位錯堆積的地方形成。當材料尺寸在亞微米級別時，幾乎所有的位錯都將滑移出樣品，消失在樣品表面，所以不能形成位錯的堆積，進而抑制孿晶的形成。所以，在亞微米級別，塑性變形將由位錯滑移所主導。在納米級別，孿晶將主導塑性變形，這是因為在納米級別，誘發孿晶的應力小於誘發位錯的應力。 以上得到的三個演化規律，只是基於理論分析得出的假設，並沒有得到實驗的驗證。本項目將提供系統的實驗分析來驗證這些演化規律，並找出不同規律之間轉換的關鍵材料尺寸大小。理論分析表明，這些關鍵尺寸取決於面心立方材料的層錯能，所以本項目也將分析具有不同層錯能的多種面心立方材料。

719712.value: 1. The physical mechanism related to the formation and growth of a single nanotwin in micron-sized pillar was discovered. The details are described in Output No. 1. 2. The size effect on deformation twinning in pillars with various sizes ranging from nanometer to micron is found. A smaller pillar leads a larger twinning critical stress. 719712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
719712.value: With the recent increasing use of micrometre-sized and sub-micrometre-sized metallic materials in technological applications, there are strong needs to understand the microstructure-property relationship in these small-sized materials, especially the evolution of microstructure during deformation. In general, the deformation of metals can occur via dislocations and twinning. Most of the current research on small-sized metallic materials only focus on dislocation-mediated deformation, while studies on twinning are rare. The present project studied experimentally and theoretically twinning behaviour in small-sized metallic samples. The research results obtained in the present project describe for the first time how a single nanotwin forms and grows during the compression tests. Furthermore, the size and orientation effects are also investigated in the present project. In summary, the results obtained in the present project have provided fundamental understanding on twinning behavior in small-sized crystals.

720012.label: Project Title(Chinese)
720012.value: 一個利用CPU, GPU 和 FPGA 作混合計算機的統一計算機模型

720012.label: Project Objectives
720012.value: To study the theoretical and practical trade-offs of the proposed unified machine model for systems with multiple heterogeneous computing fabrics. To study the interaction between the operating system and the underlying machine to efficiently support computation using multiple heterogeneous computing fabric.
