741312.label: Project Title(Chinese)
741312.value: 區域制度與跨國子公司的業績

741312.label: Project Objectives
741312.value: One major objective of this project is to develop a conceptual framework—with the institution-based view as its theoretical underpinning—to examine the performance of foreign affiliates of MNCs in subnational regions within host countries. The second major objective is to examine the independent effects of regional economic, political and social institutions on foreign affiliate performance, and their relative influences on that performance. The third major objective is to examine in which regions within a host country the variation in foreign affiliate performance is greatest and the level of foreign affiliate performance is highest. The forth objective is to provide the components of subnational institutions (i.e. regional economic, political and social institutions) and to identify the factors of each component. The fifth objective is to provide implications for theoretical development, international managers, and policy makers.
rows: One major objective of this project is to develop a conceptual framework—with the institution-based view as its theoretical underpinning—to examine the performance of foreign affiliates of MNCs in subnational regions within host countries.

The second major objective is to examine the independent effects of regional economic, political and social institutions on foreign affiliate performance, and their relative influences on that performance.
The third major objective is to examine in which regions within a host country the variation in foreign affiliate performance is greatest and the level of foreign affiliate performance is highest.
The forth objective is to provide the components of subnational institutions (i.e. regional economic, political and social institutions) and to identify the factors of each component.
The fifth objective is to provide implications for theoretical development, international managers, and policy makers.

741312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741312.value: This project examines the influences of the levels of the development of regional economic, political and social institutions on foreign affiliate performance in regions within host countries by drawing on the institution-based view. Previous research on foreign affiliate performance, drawing on the transaction costs economics and the resource-based view of the firm, assumes that the business environment within a host country remains the same (e.g., Brouthers et al.,2003). More recent studies stress that the institutional environments of host countries influence the performance of foreign affiliates (Chan et al., 2008) and suggest that subnational institutions do matter in explaining that performance in regions within host countries (Chan et al. 2010). While subnational institutions are composed of regional economic, political and social institutions, research has yet to develop a conceptual framework to examine the mechanism of how the three aspects of subnational institutions affect foreign affiliate performance in regions within host countries. Besides, most previous studies focus on the average return on foreign direct investment and compare the average performance of foreign affiliates in different host countries (Dunning, 1988). Little is known about “business extremes” (i.e., successes or failures) (McKelvey &Andriani, 2007) as it is the extremes rather than the averages that have more practical implications for strategic actions. Research has yet to examine the content in which the successes and failures occur. This project aims to answer two important research questions (1) what the independent and relative influences do the levels of the development of regional economic, political and social institutions have on the level of and the variation in foreign affiliate performance; and (2) in which regions within a host country the level of foreign affiliate performance is highest and the variation in that performance is greatest. This project intends to develop a measurement of the development of regional economic, political and social institutions. We will choose China as the institutional context of this study as China represents the largest recipient country of FDI and has a large number of subnational regions, the boundary of which discriminates the local economic, political and social situations. The findings of this project will not only provide implications for theoretical development but also to policy makers in different subnational regions of emerging economies on how to attract FDI. The results will be of strategic importance to international managers because they have to learn how to deal with subnational institutions in regions within host countries. 此專案的研究目的在於檢驗跨國企業子公司在單一海外國家的績效。此研究將探討區域制度的結構（如區域經濟、政治、和社會制度）以及區域經濟、政治、和社會制度的發展水準對跨國企業子公司績效的影響。此研究所關注的兩個研究問題是：（1）區域制度對跨國企業子公司績效水準以及績效差異有怎樣的影響？ （2）區域經濟、政治、和社會制度對於以上兩種績效的相對影響力度如何？

741312.label: Realisation of objectives
741312.value: The first major objective of this project is to develop a conceptual framework to examine the sources of variation in firm (foreign affiliate) performance in subnational regions within host countries. The conventional studies, drawing on industrial organization theory, transaction cost theory and resource- and institution-based views, have identified a variety of “conditions” (e.g., industry structure, firm resources and institutions) that explain the performance variation. However, there are two research gaps. First, these conventional studies have adopted the average-centered view which makes the Gaussian assumption that the arithmetic mean of independent random events is normally distributed, irrespective of the form of the original distribution; focuses on the central (average) tendencies of the observed events; and considers outliers or residual values that deviate from the average as unimportant sources of information or even as noise in descriptions of the characteristics of the observed events. However, according to the behavioral tradition of management research, these assumptions are often not appropriate for strategic and international management practices because the behavior of firms (foreign affiliates) is typically characterized as interdependent, self-selected, and biased. Although the average-centered view can explain how mean performance varies between conditions and can identify the conditions that lead to differences in the mean performance, which we call the effects on the mean, it fails to explain how the shape of performance distribution varies within conditions (i.e., the range and configuration of performance variation within conditions), which we call the effects on the variance. To precisely understand the sources of firm (foreign affiliate) performance variation, this project develops a theoretical framework to examine the variance-centered view that explains the effects on the variance. Second, the-above mentioned “conditions” do not sufficiently explain the performance variation. Although a more recent study shows that the host country institutions influence foreign affiliate performance, subnational institutions consist of economic, political, and social institutions which vary across regions within a host country. To address this research gap, this project draws on the institution-based view to develop a conceptual framework that examines the institutional rationale behind the variation in firm (foreign affiliate) performance in subnational regions within host countries. The second objective of this project is to examine the independent and relative influences of the development levels of subnational economic, political and social institutions on the performance of foreign affiliates in different subnational regions within host countries. The development levels of subnational economic, political, and social institutions are defined as the extent to which they are developed and are favorable to foreign affiliates in a subnational region. We also explore whether such relationships vary among subnational regions and foreign affiliates with different characteristics. The third objective of this project is to examine in which regions within a host country the variation in foreign affiliate performance is greatest and the level of foreign affiliate performance is highest. We argue that subnational institutions support the functioning of business transactions, and that subnational economic, political, and social institutions respectively produce different kinds of benefits when they are at higher development levels, which could facilitate foreign affiliate performance, and produce different kinds of institutional hazards when they are at lower different levels, which could constrain foreign affiliate performance. The forth objective of this project is to provide the components of subnational institutions (i.e. subnational economic, political and social institutions) and to identify the factors of each component. We develop a new measurement of subnational economic, political, and social institutions by selecting twelve institutional characteristics as the proxies for the three subnational institutions respectively. Each respective subnational institution is measured by a comprehensive combination of four institutional characteristics. We collect the data from China Statistics Yearbooks (1998-2008), Marketization Index for China’s Provinces (1998-2008), China’s Comprehensive Competitiveness of Provincial Economy Development Report (1998-2004, 2005-2006, 2006-2007, and 2008-2009) and China General Social Survey (2003, 2005, 2006, and 2008). The fifth objective is to provide implications for theoretical development, international managers, and policy makers. Our study develops a contingent and dynamic institutional perspective of firm (foreign affiliate) performance. Establishing foreign affiliates in institutionally better-developed subnational regions does not necessary guarantee a long-term, sustainable high performance. To maintain long-term advantages in institutionally better-developed subnational regions, managers should always be alert to environmental changes and conduct adaptive strategies that can effectively respond to dynamic external environments. Our study also suggests that fluctuation in external environments implies additional risks and costs for foreign affiliates, which can reduce the amount of inward foreign direct investment attracted by subnational regions.

741312.label: Major findings and research outcome
741312.value: First, the project, building on the variance-centered view, illustrates that mean performance is associated with the shape of the distribution curve, as defined by the skewness, kurtosis, and variance. The result showed that the aggregate performance of subsets (e.g., business units within a firm; foreign affiliates within an MNC; firms in a segment; foreign affiliates within a subnational region) is manifested in the shape of the performance distributions of these subsets. The findings clearly revealed that successful firms (foreign affiliates) tend to have a greater positive skew in their performance distributions and that the heavy-tail effects moderate the relationship between skewness and mean performance. This part of the project was accepted by Strategic Management Journal for publication. Second, the results of the project showed that the development levels of subnational economic, political, and social institutions have positive relationships with the level of performance of foreign affiliates. In particular, subnational political institution shows a stronger influence on foreign affiliate performance than subnational economic and social institutions do. Our findings also indicated that the moderating effects of regional competition on subnational economic institution and political institution are negative, whereas the moderating effect on subnational social institution is positive. The moderating effect of regional instability on subnational economic institution is found to be negative whereas the moderating effect on subnational social institution is found to be positive. The findings of this project also revealed that the moderating effect of subsidiary size on subnational political institution and social institutions is positive, whereas the moderating effect on subnational economic institution is negative and that the moderating effect of subsidiary age on subnational social institution is positive. This part of the project was accepted for conference presentations at the 2014 Academy of International Business Conference, at the 2014 Academy of Management Conference and at the 2015 Academy of Management Conference. My PhD student, Mr. Niu Chao, has been trained to work on the institutional rationale of firm (foreign affiliate performance).

741312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
741312.value: First, future research can extend the variance-centered view to research on the micro-foundations of economic growth. Our evidence shows that segments with higher mean performances provide environments that facilitate the entry of high performing firms (foreign affiliates) and the exit of underperforming firms (foreign affiliates). This evidence is consistent with the conventional I/O view that excessive regulations on market entry and a protection of weak firms can weaken the competitiveness of the economy in the long term and the evolutionary view of economic growth that emphasizes the importance of learning (Nelson and Winter, 1982). Thus, the variance-centered view can be used to explain how economic policies on the strategic behavior of the firms affect the growth of an economy. Second, future studies can develop a comprehensive comparison of the relative importance of subnational economic, political, and social institutions on foreign affiliate performance. Our evidence shows that subnational political institution has a stronger influence on foreign affiliate performance. An interesting extension of this project is to integrate the resource-, industry-, and institution-based views (i.e., the “strategy tripod” of international business) and explore how the relative importance of subnational economic, political and social institutions are contingent on firm attributes and industry conditions.

741312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
741312.value: The project develops the variance-centered view which is a complementary approach to the average-centered view for the analysis of firm (foreign affiliate) performance. Strategic and international management research has been dominated by the average-centered view, and most studies seek to explain how events (behavior or performance) vary between conditions; this view assumes that events follow a normal distribution and that events that deviate from the mean are less essential. However, these assumptions are often not appropriate for strategic and international management practices, as the behavior of firms is characterized by interdependent, self-selected events and firms choose actions that not only regress toward the mean but also deviate from it. Given the importance of examining extreme values, the project represents further research in this direction. The project also uncovers the underlying mechanisms of how the development level of subnational economic, political and social institutions influence firm (foreign affiliate) performance in different regions within host countries. Our results clearly show that the three subnational institutions have different magnitudes of impacts on foreign affiliate performance. Probing deeper into the underlying mechanism, we found that the relationship between subnational institutions and foreign affiliate performance are moderated by idiosyncrasies of regional environments and foreign subsidiaries.

741512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
741512.value: 一國兩制三領域: 以中港法律, 經濟學及精算學評估人身傷害賠償

741512.label: Project Objectives
741512.value: The first objective of this research project is to compare the basic legal, economic and actuarial principles used in the assessment of personal injury compensations in Hong Kong and the PRC, and to examine whether personal injury compensation in the PRC is unduly suppressed, leading to under-compensation of the victims. The second objective of the research will be on the construction of general actuarial annuity tables for the PRC based on the most recent evidence. These would be a valuable source of reference for the possible PRC tort reforms in future. The research will attempt to recommend an appropriate method for determining the multiplicand and discount rate with regard to China’s circumstances.

The second objective of the research will be on the construction of general actuarial annuity tables for the PRC based on the most recent evidence. These would be a valuable source of reference for the possible PRC tort reforms in future.
The research will attempt to recommend an appropriate method for determining the multiplicand and discount rate with regard to China’s circumstances.

741512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741512.value: Although Hong Kong is a part of China, the legal systems in Hong Kong and the People's Republic of China (PRC) are fundamentally different. Under the principle of “one country, two systems” prescribed by Hong Kong Basic Law, Hong Kong retained its common law system following the change of sovereignty in 1997. The PRC legal system, in contrast, is similar to those in continental Europe (such as Germany) with influence from socialist law. Although the common law system in Hong Kong is remarkably different from the civil law system in the PRC, the two legal systems share a similar ideological basis concerning the assessment of damages in personal injury litigations. When an innocent party is injured in a tort-based system of law as the result of the negligence of another party, the innocent party should be awarded adequate compensation. The innocent party should receive proper damages to recompense him/her for the wrong suffered, so that he/she may live as fulfilling a life as possible after the injury. There are both similarities and dissimilarities in the way this ideological belief is put into practice. When assessing future pecuniary loss in personal injury litigations, both legal systems often use the multiplicand/multiplier approach. The objective is to calculate a lump sum to compensate the plaintiff for future loss of earnings, the loss of pension rights and to cover future expenses. The lump sum is computed as the product of a multiplicand and a multiplier. The multiplier is used to discount the future pecuniary values into a present-day lump sum amount. For many years, the PRC multiplier figures were difficult to determine on any scientific basis due to insufficient interdisciplinary research in law, economics and actuarial mathematics. Determination of the multiplicand in the PRC system heavily depends on the geographical residence of the victim, which poses a question of fairness. Through systematic analysis and comparison of the relevant laws and cases from Hong Kong and the PRC, this research proposal aims to examine whether personal injury compensation in the PRC is unduly suppressed, leading to under-compensation of the victims. Actuarial tables based on the most recent Chinese population morality experience will be constructed for reference by the PRC Courts. The research will attempt to recommend an appropriate method for determining the multiplicand and discount rate in regard to China’s circumstances. 雖然香港是中國的一部分，香港的法律制度和中華人民共和國的法制是不同的。一國兩制的規定，由香港基本法保留了其普通法制度。中國的法律制度是和歐洲大陸國家（如德國）法律相似。雖然香港的普通法制度是顯著和中國的法律體系不同，有關評估賠償人身傷害訴訟,兩地法律制度有著相似的基礎。當一個無辜的人受傷了, 侵權的法律為基礎，無過錯的一方應當獲得足夠的補償,以補償他的損失，讓他盡可能在傷後生活正常。在這種原則付諸表決的方式有異付諸實踐。在評估未來的金錢損失，人身傷害的訴訟，法律制度經常使用的系數/乘數方法,目標是計算一筆未來的收入損失，賠償原告的損失退休金的權利，並用以支付未來的費用。計算一次付清的補償一個系數和乘法器,成當今一次性乘數是用於貼現未來的金錢價值總結量。多年來，中國的的乘數數字是難以確定,由於跨學科在法律，經濟和精算數學研究不足。中國系統測定的被乘數嚴重依賴於居住的受害人地區，可能影響公平的問題。通過系統的分析和比較，從相關法規及案例國，本研究建議的目的是探討是否造成人身傷害補償受到不適當的抑制，導致補償的受害者。這項研究將推薦適當的方法確定系數和折扣率, 設計精算表以供參考。

741512.label: Realisation of objectives
741512.value: Although the common law system in Hong Kong is remarkably different from the civil law system in the PRC, the two legal systems share a similar ideological basis concerning the assessment of damages in personal injury litigations. When an innocent party is injured in a tort-based legal system in consequence of another party’s negligence, the innocent party should be provided with sufficient compensation so that he or she may live as fulfilling a life as possible after injury. The basic principle underlying the assessment of the quantum of damages is restitutio in integrum. Concerning the common law, Hong Kong (under the British rule for 156) and Singapore (under the British rule for 144 years) share many similarities. Both jurisdictions were (and are still being) under the heavy influence of the English common law. The PRC, founded in 1949 by the Chinese Communist Party, developed a legal system which is under the heavy influence of the communist ideology including Marxism-Leninism and the thoughts of Chairman Mao. However the PRC government is embarking on a series of initiatives of legal transplantation from Anglo-American laws and globally established practices. It issued policy documents urging for more accessibility of law and greater transparency. The PRC legal reform called for more judicial independence and greater effectiveness in the administration of justice. The present investigators argue, with empirical evidence in support, that there are signs of convergence since both legal systems (Hong Kong and PRC) are in fact applying the same multiplicand-multiplier approach in assessing damages. Case studies in PRC (concerning civil law), Hong Kong, the United Kingdom and Singapore (regarding common law) are adopted to explore the broader implications for the convergence. However, there are rooms for improvements, both in the PRC and in Hong Kong. Regarding the PRC, the present investigators constructed general actuarial annuity tables (based on the PRC official statistics) and examined how the PRC courts ascertained the multiplicands-multipliers. It was discovered that different courts from different provinces applied inconsistent methodology. The investigators proposed that the move to a standard method of assessing future financial needs by using actuarial annuity tables that reflect the realities of life in difference provinces of PRC will facilitate fair compromise promptly, keeping with the spirit of the legal reform advocated by the PRC Government. In Hong Kong, whether the claimant should be assumed to invest the compensation in equities against inflation is worthy of examination.

741512.label: Major findings and research outcome
741512.value: When an innocent party is injured in a tort-based legal system in consequence of another party’s negligence, the innocent party should be provided with sufficient compensation so that he or she may live as fulfilling a life as possible after injury. The moral objective underlying this supposition is intuitively appealing. It is therefore not surprising that this jurisprudential notion has been favourably received and widely applied in various common and civil law jurisdictions, despite differences in tradition and culture. Nonetheless, even though the two bodies of law share a similar objective in this arena, there are enumerated differences in the substantive content of the law, and the configuration of the rules. The present authors argue, with empirical evidence in support, that there are signs of convergence since both the common and civil law systems are in fact applying the same multiplicand-multiplier approach in assessing the quantum of damages. Case studies in Mainland China (concerning civil law), the United Kingdom and Hong Kong (regarding common law) are adopted as the research methodology for exploring the broader implications for the convergence. It can be observed from the findings of this project that due to the communist ideology in mainland China, the multiplicand cannot be determined on an individual basis by considering the evidence relating to a claimant’s occupational achievement and educational attainment. Nonetheless, it does not mean that legal reform cannot be carried out in respect of the determination of multipliers in the PRC. It is demonstrated that a more scientific methodology can be applied in constructing a set of actuarial multipliers for use in the PRC, by referring to the latest mortality statistics promulgated by the National Bureau of Statistics of China. There are legitimate reasons for concern that younger victims in the PRC are suffering from under-compensation due to the suppression of the multipliers for claimants at younger ages. It is hoped that the reform proposed in this project, if implemented, would achieve the goal of justice by effectively rectifying the deficiencies of the PRC tort system.

741512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
741512.value: The assessment of compensation in courts is based on the objective of putting injured parties back, insofar as money can achieve, to the position that they would have been in but for the injury. Currently compensation is awarded as a single lump sum. In catastrophic personal injury cases, a very significant proportion of the lump sum is granted for compensating the future losses. The basis of assessment is founded on the actuarial projection of a claimant’s life expectancy. The lump-sum award is assumed to be prudently invested by the claimant. Hence, future inflation rates and investment returns have to be taken into account. However, there are bound to be perplexities in these assumptions concerning the claimant’s future contingency. The logical development of the research is to explore the feasibility (in Hong Kong and PRC) of a structured settlement through which the claimant receives compensation periodically instead of a lump sum during the rest of his or her lifetime. The payments must be completely secure regardless of the solvency of the insurance company obliged to make periodic payment. It must also be adjusted regularly to reflect inflation, in particular inflation of costs related to healthcare, care assistance and rental accommodation.

741512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
741512.value: When an innocent party is injured in a tort-based legal system in consequence of another party’s negligence, the innocent party should be provided with sufficient compensation so that he or she may live as fulfilling a life as possible after injury. In this project, the legal, economic and actuarial principles used in the assessment of personal injury compensations in Hong Kong and the PRC are comparatively analysed. Actuarial annuity tables for the PRC based on the most recent evidence are constructed. The basis of assessment is founded on the actuarial projection of a claimant’s life expectancy. The lump-sum award is assumed to be prudently invested by the claimant. In this research, an appropriate method for determining the discount rate (reflecting various factors including inflation and investment returns) is formulated, so that the annuity tables can be widely adopted in the PRC despite future change of the economic landscape. Lawyers and judges should welcome a tool which cuts down a complicated task to a more manageable size. The move to a standard method of assessing future financial needs by using actuarial tables that reflect the realities of life in the PRC should facilitate fair compromise as promptly as possible.

742012.label: Project Objectives
742012.value: Investigate the characteristics of bloggers in suicide-related online communities: As blogs and social network Web sites become increasingly popular, many virtual communities have emerged. Some of these communities are related to suicide, and more research is needed to reveal their nature and characteristics. We aim to use blog mining techniques to perform systematic content and structural analysis of a large number of blogs in suicide-related communities. Develop methods for suicide intention detection and analysis: It has been found that many suicide attempters, especially adolescents, have expressed their negative emotions and suicide intentions in blogs before their suicide attempts. Some suicide prevention organizations have started monitoring blogs to identify potential suicide ideators and attempters, but this is a very labor-intensive process. With the inputs from suicide prevention experts and social workers, our project aims to explore and evaluate the performance of using blog mining techniques for automatic detection and analysis of suicide intentions in blogs. We will also develop new methods to achieve good detection performance using analyses from multiple perspectives. Evaluate the performance of the proposed techniques for blogs in different languages in suicide detection: We will develop a system for suicide research and prevention for blogs in both English and Chinese. This can allow us to test our proposed blog mining methods in both languages and study the linguistic, technical and cultural issues involved. We will implement and evaluate the performance of the proposed system and techniques in both lab settings and real world organizations. We will make our system available to suicide prevention organizations in order to facilitate their work and allow social workers to reach more people with suicide intentions.

742012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742012.value: 自殺是一個香港和其它現代社會的重要問題，能及時識別有自殺傾向者非常重要，好讓社會機構能盡早找到他們並提供協助。近年，有研究指出許多人在企圖自殺前曾在他們的網誌上表達負面情緒和自殺意圖。為了幫助這些有自殺傾向者，一些防止自殺機構已開始在網誌上搜索這些自殺信息。然而，由於目前大多數識別方法只限於簡單的關鍵字搜索或人手瀏覽，過程需要大量人手，所以未能有效地識別大量企圖自殺個案。另一方面，儘管網絡和網誌分析技術近年大幅改進，但這些分析技術很少結合到重要的實際應用。所以我們嘗試在這個項目中，研究以網誌分析技術防止自殺和探討有關的實際問題。 我們的項目有以下目標。首先，我們將應用網誌分析技術在網誌自殺相關的虛擬群組中，包括以內容分析和社交網絡分析方法研究他們的語言和結構特點，進一步尋找自殺相關的信息。其次，由於現有的網誌分析算法設計通常用於產品和電影評論中，跟自殺信息內容非常不同，因此我們將開發新技術在網誌中自動檢測和分析自殺意念的信息。此外，我們將設計一個能分析英文和中文兩種語言網誌的系統，並評估系統的性能。為了提供高質素分析給防止自殺的機構，我們將進行實驗室測試和實地測試，評估所提出的分析技術之效用。我們的研究結果將在網誌分析和情感分析技術研究上提供重要的見解，亦將有助香港以及其他國家之預防自殺工作。

742012.label: Major findings and research outcome
742012.value: In this research, we have analyzed the postings of suicidal bloggers through textual and temporal analysis. Through the analysis, we have revealed some major characteristics of bloggers with suicide intention and emotional distress. A paper on the findings was published in the journal Crisis in 2014. We have also designed and developed a system that can classify bloggers with emotional distress by automatically analyzing blog posts. The system has been evaluated and the results have shown that the system performs better than existing classification approaches. A paper on the design was under first round revision at the journal MIS Quarterly. The following activities have been conducted in the project: - Review of related literature in suicide analysis - Study of the characteristics of bloggers in suicide-related online communities using text mining and psycholinguistic techniques - Collection and markup of test data sets consisting of suicide or depress-related blogs and control data sets - Development of algorithms for searching and analyzing suicide-related text online - Development of an online search and analysis system for suicide-related blogs and posts - Evaluation of the proposed algorithms and system in lab experiments and user studies - Submission of two journal papers and one conference paper

742112.label: Project Objectives
742112.value: We plan to provide a new angle to the literature of revolutions and study the role played by rumors, i.e., publicly observed unverifiable messages, during revolutions. We plan to enrich the global game literature in two dimensions. First, standard global game models implicitly assume that citizens fully trust the public signal they observe. However, this assumption runs counter to the previous findings in the literature, that individuals tend to distrust signals which are too different from their priors. Our model offers a more general set-up and allows for rumors, where the standard global game model is a special case of this framework. We plan to explore the role played by information transmission, i.e., communication between citizens, in a global game set-up. Typically, in global game models, citizens receive both private and public signals, on which they make their decisions. Communication between citizens are often left out for the sake of simplicity and tractability. In reality citizens do communicate with each other before they make decisions and take action. This is especially true in mass movements such as revolutions. In our work, we allow citizens to communicate in a revolution game, and therefore highlight the effects of information transmission among citizens on political regime changes. We plan to investigate to what extent improved communication technology affects outcomes of revolution. To address this question, we need to enrich our baseline model and accommodate richer set-ups of alternative communication devices.

742112.label: Major findings and research outcome
742112.value: The paper has been accepted for presentation in several high-level international conferences, such as NBER summer institute and SED conference etc, and it has been published by the International Economic Review in 2016. Our major findings are as follows. We study how rumors mobilize individuals who take collective action. Rumors may or may not be informative, but they create public topics on which people can exchange their views. Individuals with diverse private information rationally evaluate the informativeness of rumors about regime strength. A rumor against the regime can coordinate a larger mass of attackers if individuals can discuss its veracity than if they cannot. Communication can be so effective that a rumor can have an even greater impact on mobilization than when the same story is fully believed by everybody. However, an extreme rumor can backfire and discourage mobilization.

742112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
742112.value: This paper lays down a foundation which can be extended to accommodate further analysis of the role of communication among individuals during collective actions. Several research papers have cited this work including some experimental work.

742112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
742112.value: That paper explains why rumors always surround collective actions, including revolutions and bank runs etc and why rumors are very effective in terms of motivating individuals to participate. We find that communication about rumors is the key to understand those questions. A rumor can have an even greater impact on mobilization than when the same story is fully believed by everybody. However, an extreme rumor can backfire and discourage mobilization.

742312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742312.value: In Western conceptualizations, internal control refers to the perception of outcomes as influenced by factors confined to oneself, whereas external control refers to the perception of outcomes as influenced by outside forces such as other people and the environment. We advocate the adoption of a cultural approach to the study of perceived control. In this project, we formulate three hypotheses to address some unresolved issues regarding cultural differences in the perception of control. First, we propose that for individuals from collectivist cultures, internal control may comprise control stemming not only from oneself but also from other people. Second, we contend that both dimensions of internal control are conducive to the psychological functioning of these individuals. Third, we formulate an indigenous model to explain the mechanisms underlying the beneficial role of these two dimensions of internal control on the psychological adjustment of the Chinese. We will test these hypotheses with diverse research design and methods. Apart from a multinational study that will collect data from at least 22 cultural regions, we will also carry out studies in three naturalistic settings among heterogeneous samples. Specifically, the transition to university life among Chinese first-year undergraduates will be examined in a multiple-phase longitudinal study. An intervention study will be undertaken in the context of coping with cancer among Chinese patients. A work context will be the focus of an interview study, specifically examining the onboarding process among new Chinese employees. Results from this project may be of theoretical and practical interest to researchers and practitioners. An expanded conceptualization of internal control may foster the construction or refinement of theories and measures with greater explanatory and predictive power, especially for members of collectivist societies. The proposed indigenous model may provide a more sophisticated account of the role of internal control by specifying the conditions in which its benefits are manifested among the Chinese. Finally, our findings may provide insights for incorporating cultural elements into the design of Chinese intervention programs relevant for local program users. 在西方概念上，內控是指對結果的看法，歸因於與自己有關的因素所影響，而外控是指對結果的看法，歸因於與外界力量，如其他人及環境的影響。我們主張通過一個文化的方法來研究認知控制。在這個項目中，我們制定了三個假設，以解決一些關於文化差異的認知控制仍懸而未決的問題。首先，我們建議在集體主義社會裡，內控的源頭不僅來自個人，也可能包括其他人。第二，我們建議這兩個層面的內控皆有利於人們的心理功能。第三，我們制定了一個文化獨有的模型，來解釋這兩種內控對中國人的心理適應之有益的作用機制。

742312.label: Realisation of objectives
742312.value: Objective 1: We have constructed a Chinese measure that assessed the expanded conceptualization of locus of control. This measure has been pilot tested in samples from both Hong Kong and Mainland China. We have also conducted validational studies to evaluate its psychometric properties. In addition, we have developed an interview protocol specifically for Chinese adults. This protocol has been thoroughly tested and checked by expert judges. Objective 2: We have formulated a new multivariate model that explicates the interplay of cultural, social, and personality factors that influences the hypothesized role of locus of control on psychological well-being. This conceptual model provides a theoretical framework that states the interrelations among a set of major constructs. The model also orients us towards a specific set of research questions and hypotheses tested in our program of studies (see Objectives 3 to 5 below). Objective 3: We conducted a large-scale multinational project in 33 countries worldwide to further evaluate the validity of both the universal disposition and the cultural relativity hypotheses. Researchers in these countries assisted in recruiting participants, translating English measures, pilot testing, and collecting data in their own countries. The entire data collection process lasted for almost two years. The multinational dataset has been made available to the public and some researchers have already worked on our dataset to test their own set of hypotheses. We expect more papers to be published based on our multinational dataset (see Section 6.2 for further details). Objective 4: We have designed a new intervention program tailor made for enhancing a sense of perceived control and the deployment of flexible coping strategies among Chinese cancer patients. This new program has been pilot tested and successfully launched in October 2014. The data collection took about one year to accomplish. The results indicate that the participants tend to perceive greater internal control through obtaining support from their family members and health professionals, without much thought of over-burdening them. Among those participants who have developed these thoughts, they are more likely to display flexible coping strategy than their counterparts who have not yet developed such thoughts. Objective 5: Adopting a multimethod approach, we tested our newly proposed model using a variety of research methods and advanced statistical analyses, namely self-report questionnaire, intervention, longitudinal analysis, systematic synthesis, meta-analysis, and multilevel modeling.

742312.label: Major findings and research outcome
742312.value: In this project, we have constructed a Chinese measure that assessed the expanded conceptualization of locus of control. We have also formulated a new multivariate model that explicates the hypothesized role of perceived control on psychological well-being (see Cheng, Lau, & Chan, 2014). This conceptual model provides a theoretical framework that states the interrelations among a set of major constructs. Adopting a multimethod approach, we tested our newly proposed model using a variety of research methods and advanced statistical analyses, namely self-report questionnaire, intervention, longitudinal analysis, systematic synthesis, meta-analysis, and multilevel modeling. We first conducted a thorough literature review that covers all available empirical studies conducted between 1978 and 2013 (see Cheng, Lau, & Chan, 2014). The results from the meta-analysis indicate that compared to members of individualist countries, those of collectivist countries display higher levels of coping flexibility. Specifically, individuals from collectivist countries are more likely to confront the stressful events when the outcome of these events is perceived as controllable, but they are more likely to alter their thoughts and emotions when the outcome of these events is perceived as uncontrollable. In contrast, their counterparts from individualist countries are more likely to adhere to a particular type of coping strategy regardless of the perceived controllability of the stressful events. The data of the meta-analyses were made available in our paper published in Psychological Bulletin (see Cheng, Lau, & Chan, 2014). Then we conducted a large-scale multinational project in 33 countries worldwide to further evaluate the validity of both the universal disposition and the cultural relativity hypotheses (Cheng, Cheung, Montasem et al., 2016). Researchers in these countries assisted in recruiting participants, translating English measures, pilot testing, and collecting data in their own countries. The entire data collection process lasted for almost two years. We analyzed the multinational dataset using multilevel modeling. The results provided support for both of our proposed hypotheses. We have also designed a new intervention program tailor made for enhancing a sense of perceived control and the deployment of flexible coping strategies among Chinese cancer patients. This new program has been pilot tested and successfully launched in October 2014. The data collection took about one year to accomplish. We have also conducted follow-up in-depth interviews to evaluate the effectiveness of this intervention program by assessing whether it can enhance a sense of perceived control and build flexible coping skills. The interviews further tap into the psychological dynamics involved in making such changes and how such changes contribute to enhance the subjective well-being of cancer patients. The results indicate that the participants tend to perceive greater internal control through obtaining support from their social network members and health professionals, without much thought of over-burdening others. Participants who have developed these thoughts are more likely to display flexible coping strategy than their counterparts who have not yet developed such thoughts.

742312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
742312.value: The multinational dataset has been made available to the public and some researchers have already worked on our dataset and performed secondary analyses to test their own set of hypotheses. We expect more papers to be published based on our multinational dataset. In our multinational project, we have collected and analyzed data from 33 countries within the project period. As of March 2016, six more countries have contributed new data to our multinational dataset, nine more countries are collecting data, and some researchers have contacted the PI expressing interest in collaborating in our multinational project. We thus expect our multinational dataset will continue to grow rapidly in the coming years. The intervention program has been found successful and effective, and we will continue to offer these programs to cancer patients. We also consider the possibility of expanding the scope to patients with other chronic illnesses such as diabetes.

742312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
742312.value: In this project, we have constructed a new conceptual model that advances the understanding of the cultural differences in the role of perceived control on psychological well-being. Our review and synthesis of data from the past decades have shown that individuals from collectivist countries are more flexible in coping. Specifically, they are more likely to confront the stressful events when such an outcome is perceived as controllable, but they are more likely to change their thoughts and feelings when the outcome is perceived as uncontrollable. However, members of individualist countries are less likely to display such flexibility across stressful situations characterized by distinct extents of perceived controllability. Moreover, we conducted a large-scale project in 33 countries worldwide, and this study is the first to shed light on both the universality and cross-cultural variability in the relationships between perceived control and psychological well-being. Finally, we designed a new intervention program tailor made for enhancing perceived control and flexible coping among Chinese cancer patients, and conducted in-depth interviews to evaluate its effectiveness. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of these programs in increasing the levels of perceived control and flexible coping among the patients.

742412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742412.value: This project aims to examine the enforcement of competition in developing countries. The last thirty years have witnessed the proliferation of competition law on an unprecedented scale. More than eighty nations, most of which developing countries, have adopted competition law during this period. Notable examples include China, which adopted the Anti-Monopoly Law in 2007, and Vietnam, which introduced the Law on Competition in 2004. Further afield, a host of African, Middle Eastern, and Central Asian countries also joined the global competition law community. Many of these new competition law statutes bear close resemblance to their developed nation counterparts, especially to Articles 101 and 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the main competition law provisions in the European Union (“EU”). Much of the conventional wisdom and mainstream analytical approaches in international competition law have emanated from the U.S. and the EU. By modeling their competition law statutes after the prevailing frameworks in developed nations, developing countries seem to imply that they intend to apply these approaches. What has been largely ignored thus far is the question of whether these approaches in fact suit developing countries, or whether there are special circumstances that set them apart from developed nations and call for a different, or at least adapted, approach to competition law in developing countries. These are also crucial theoretical issues in comparative legal studies of the processes of legal transplantation. This project aims to answer this important question by examining possible reasons for adaptations in each area of competition law: restrictive agreements, abuse of dominance, and merger review. Separate attention will be paid to the interface between intellectual property and competition law, which presents special concerns for developing countries. All this analysis will be done against a backdrop of development economics. Given the overriding importance of economic growth and broader development objectives, such as poverty alleviation and provision of basic health care and education, to developing countries, competition law and policy in these countries must be implemented in furtherance of these goals. Beyond doctrinal adjustments, the project will examine enforcement-related issues arising from the institutional weaknesses and lack of expertise in developing countries. Attention will be paid to possible solutions to these problems, including the pooling of enforcement resources and expertise in regional networks. It is hoped that this project will contribute to an improved understanding of the implementation of competition law in developing countries. 這項研究旨在探討及評估競爭法在發展中國家的推行情況。過去的三十年，競爭法以空前的規模及速度擴展到全世界。期間，超過80個國家(當中大部分是發展中國家) 先後通過了競爭法。眾所周知的例子包括，在2007年通過了反壟斷法的中國及2004通過了競爭法的越南。很多位處偏遠地區的國家，如非洲，中東和中亞國家也加入了這個全球性的行列，推行了競爭法。許多新立的競爭法法例與一些已發展國家的法例很相似，當中很多新法都與《歐洲聯盟運作條約》中的第101和102條尤其相似。 其實世界各地的競爭法所蘊含的傳統智慧和主流分析方法大多都由美國和歐盟的競爭法衍生及發展出來的。很多發展中國家定立競爭法時，都會參照發達國家的法規框架。就此看來，發展中國家都傾向以這些發達國家的法規框架為立法「藍本」。但迄今為止，很多人都忽略了當中一些很重要的問題。問題在於究竟這些「藍本」是否乎合發展中國家的國情及經濟需要，以及這些發展中國家應否調整相關的「藍本」，甚至定立與這些「藍本」完全不一樣的法規框架以配合特殊的國情需要。 這些也是比較法律研究中，有關「法律移植」的重要理論課題。 相信就每個競爭法領域而言，如限制競爭協議、濫用市場主導地位及併購審查，都會有一些誘因可能令發展中國家調整法規「藍本」。這計劃旨在透過研究這些誘因，解答以上問題。 另外，這研究亦會重點審視知識產權與競爭法的互動。因為這互動會深遠地影響發展中國家競爭法的發展。上述的研究及分析都會以發展經濟學角度出發。原因是發展中國家都很著重經濟增長和多元化發展，並以這兩項為首重的發展目標。這些發展目標包括在發展中國家消除貧困和提供基本的醫療保健和教育。因此，當地執行競爭法及實施競爭政策時，必須促進實現這些目標。 除了在法規層面上進行理論研究及調整，這研究計劃還會審視發展中國家在執法上遇到的問題，例如執法體制有所漏洞及執法機關執行競爭法時缺乏專業知識。 這計劃亦會重點研究這些問題的解決方案，包括在各地區網絡集中執法資源和促進專業知識的交流。希望這計劃有助促使各方理解競爭法在發展中國家的實施。

742412.label: Realisation of objectives
742412.value: The project contains three main objectives: (1) to identify problems facing developing country jurisdictions in their implementation of competition law; (2) to examine the applicability of the prevailing approaches to competition law from industrialized nations to developing countries; and (3) to suggest possible adaptations of these approaches to developing countries by giving specific attention to their development needs and goals. The underlying main objective of the project is to propose suitable approaches for developing countries to enforce their competition laws that reflect their unique economic characteristics and their development needs. Regarding the first objective, the project focuses on four distinct aspects of competition law enforcement in developing countries. The first one is the imperative of using competition law enforcement to facilitate economic growth and development to the extent possible. The project canvasses extensively the development economics literature on the key determinants of economic growth and what is necessary for economic development beyond growth. The second aspect is the distinct ways in which markets function in developing countries that set them apart from their counterparts in developed countries. It consults extensively the industrial organization literature on the unique characteristics of the market structure in developing countries. The third aspect are some unique characteristics of developing country economies in general that may render the prevailing approaches to competition law enforcement in developed countries unsuitable for developing countries. It thus also explores the relevant literature on the unique characteristics of the economy of developing countries, such as the lack of a well developed capital market, small domestic market, poor infrastructure, poor general education level, high barriers to entrepreneurship, heavy presence of the state sector in the economy, significant variations in the productivity of domestic firms, prevalence of the informal sector, limited access to manufacture inputs, and finally, concentration of private wealth and the presence of large corporate groups. The last aspect is the limited enforcement capacity of developing country competition authorities, which may constrain their ability to apply sophisticated enforcement approaches developed in developed countries. In light of the findings under the first objective of the project, the conclusion under the second objective is that the prevailing approaches to competition law enforcement in industrialized nations require adaptations before they can be applied in developing countries. This conclusion moves the project to the third objective, which is to suggest possible adaptations for developing countries. Some adaptations are needed because of the unique economic characteristics of developing countries. Some adaptations are due to the limited enforcement capacity of developing country enforcement authorities. Some further adaptations are needed in order to help pursue development goals. For example, due to the relatively poor access to credit in developing countries, a dominant firm's ability to hurt rival firms through the use of predatory pricing may be greater than in developed countries. Rival firms' ability to withstand losses is reduced in light of their limited access to capital through the financial markets. Therefore, the requirement of a high probability of recoupment of losses in establishing a predatory pricing claim may be inappropriate for developing countries. Another example is the need to simplify the proof of dominance in developing countries. Due to the limited capacity of developing country enforcement authorities and the lack of access to needed market data, it would be much more difficult to conduct in developing countries the kind of thorough market analysis that is done in developed countries in order to define the market and establish dominance. It may be more practical to allow the authority to establish a presumption of dominance upon a showing of a high market share, and shift the burden to rebut this presumption to the accused firm, which is likely to have much better access to market data, to show that it lacks market power. One final example is that developing country authorities need to focus on facilitating productivity growth, which has been shown to be key to economic growth and which is dependent on innovation, when enforcing their laws. This means that the IP-competition interface is going to be crucial to developing countries. An overly pro-patent approach to the interface will restrict technology transfer, which will retard productivity growth. The authority will also need to be cognizant of the fact that innovation takes on a different meaning in developing countries, which is often far from the global technology frontier. For a developing country, innovation often means developing the ability to absorb and deploy an advanced technology developed in an industrialized nation. Technological imitation and adoption requires a significant amount of tacit knowledge and knowhow. Technological investment is often needed to develop an absorption capacity for new technologies. Therefore, developing country authorities should not apply the same definition to innovation as applied in developed countries and need to be sensitive to their countries' needs to acquire technologies from other countries.

742412.label: Major findings and research outcome
742412.value: The major findings of the project are that developing countries need to make special adaptations to the prevailing enforcement approaches fashioned in developed countries to suit their needs. This is important if developing country authorities were to enforce their laws sensitive to the ways in which their markets and economies function, sensitive to the limitations in their resource base and enforcement capacity, and in furtherance of their development goals. The research outcome is an academic monograph, which is still being prepared. The delay is largely due to the huge volume of materials, especially in the various disciplines in economics, that need to be consulted for the project, and the repeated delay in the release of a very important report by the World Bank and the OECD on competition law enforcement in developing countries. The report was not released until mid to late 2017. Many of the arguments and findings from the report need to be incorporated in the monograph to ensure its completeness. It is foreseen that the monograph should be finalized in the coming few months, after which it will be submitted for publication by major university presses.

742412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
742412.value: Potential for further development of the research includes a critical evaluation of competition law enforcement in specific developing countries, and a closer examination of how competition law norms fashioned in developed countries are diffused in select developing countries. Regarding the first potential development, the PI has submitted a GRF application for an academic monograph on competition law in China, which will examine how China should contextualize its enforcement of competition law to reflect the unique circumstances of the country. Regarding the second potential, the PI is exploring the possibility of collaborating with authors from the BRICS countries to examine the diffusion of competition law norms in these countries. The choice of BRICS is due to the fact that there are simply too many developing countries for there to be a comprehensive study of all of them and the BRICS are the economically most important developing countries.

742412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
742412.value: This project explores how developing countries should enforce their competition laws to reflect the unique ways in which their markets and economies operate and the limited enforcement capacity of their authorities, and to pursue economic development goals. This issue is highly significant because most of the prevailing norms in global competition law are fashioned in industrialized nations such as the US and the EU, and do not take into account the different circumstances in developing countries. It therefore provides a blueprint for how developing country authorities should enforce their competition laws going forward.

743112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743112.value: TouchPad mobile devices are increasingly being used in educational contexts. Growing investment is planned by higher education in Hong Kong and the HKSAR Education Bureau in relation to educational uses of TouchPad technology. However, research into educational applications of this technology in Hong Kong is limited. This study will investigate how higher education teachers use TouchPad technology to facilitate their practice. The study will explore both the educational affordances of the technology (Norman, 1988) and the ways in which teachers’ private theories (Churchill, 2005; Griffits & Tann, 1992; Moallem, 1998) mediate these affordances and transform through the process. The research will follow ten teachers from key disciplines at a Hong Kong university (ranging across science, humanities and art) using iPad devices in their teaching over a year. This device is selects as the most popular and widely used TouchPad technology in the World. The study will adopt an explorative multiple case methodology (e.g., Merriam, 1988). Data will be collected through interviews with the teachers, and the provision by the participants of reflective online journals. The teachers will use a website environment designed for the study to record their reflections and report on on-going uses of iPad devices. The research team will use this space to blog about new Apps and emerging ideas for iPad uses, communicate with the teachers and solicit their responses to emerging questions. Electronic means will be actively used to ensure participation over a prolonged time period. The participants will be encouraged to interact and learn from each other's practice by sharing resources, post and share their reflections, comment on others’ contributions, and participate in forum discussions. The main tool for processing the data will be content analysis, including coding of data and development of assertions. The study will (a) explicate areas of affordances of iPad technology that emerge from the ten teachers’ practice, (b) examine private theories that mediate the participants’ understanding of these affordances, and (c) explore how these change through the process of adoption on iPads. The study outcomes will contribute to theoretical understanding of higher education teacher changes through adoption of technology. Furthermore, the study will deliver a set of recommendations for applications of TouchPad technology in higher education and ways to support teachers to effectively adopt such technology in their practices. These recommendations will be useful to teachers and policy makers and will inform development and research involving TouchPad technology in higher education. 擁有繼個人電腦後開發的觸摸板技術(TouchPad)的移動設備越來越多被應用於教育景況中。香港的高等教育機構和香港特區教育局計劃增加觸控技術在教育應用的投資。然而，研究這項技術於香港教育的應用目前是有限的。本研究將探討高校教師如何使用觸摸板技術。是項研究將探討該技術的教育可用性(educational affordances)（Norman，1988），及教師的個人或私人理論(teachers’ personal or private theories) (Churchill, 2005; Griffits & Tann, 1992; Moallem, 1998) 如何調和這些可用性，並於使用觸摸板技術過程中的轉變。 建議的研究將跟進香港一所大學的十名教師在歷時一年的教學中使用iPad於重點學科（涵蓋科學，人文科學和文學）的情況。選擇此設備是由於它擁有世界上最流行和廣泛使用的觸控板技術。這項研究將採用探索性的定性多案例方法（例如， Merriam, 1988）。收集的數據將來自被採訪的教師及參與者於反思日誌提到的素材。教師會使用一個為這項研究設計的網站記錄自己的反思和報告其持續使用的iPad設備的情況。該研究小組將利用此空間博客iPad使用的新的應用程序和新的應用理念，與教師溝通，及聽取他們對新出現的問題的回應。小組會積極利用電子工具以確保參與者延續的參與。小組鼓勵參與者互動，並透過實現資源共享，發布和分享他們的思考，評論他人的貢獻，參與論壇討論，實現從他人的實踐經驗中學習。處理數據的主要工具將是內容分析，包括數據編碼和斷言發展。這項研究將（一）從十名教師教學實踐闡明iPad科技的可用性範圍，（二）審查私人理論對參與者間所理解的可用性的調和，和（三）探討採用iPad的過程中如何產生這些轉變。 這項研究的成果將有助於在理論層面上理解高等教育教師於採用技術過程中所促使的轉變。此外，這項研究將就高等教育對觸控技術的應用提供一系列建議，包括如何有效地採用這種技術於教學實踐中。這些建議將對教師和政策制定者有用，並有助於觸摸板技術在高等教育的發展和研究。

743112.label: Realisation of objectives
743112.value: This study investigated how cases of higher education teachers adopted iPads to facilitate their practices, and underlining private theories that informed their decisions. Changes in these teachers’ thinking (private theories) over extended period of time were explored in order to gain understanding how technology influenced any transformation. The outcomes of the study contribute to the theoretical understanding of higher education teachers’ private theories and changes through adoption of technology. The study concludes that the following set or areas of private theories have strong mediating effect upon teachers’ instructional and technology-using decisions: private theories about learning, students, teachers, roles, technology, lesson design and changes. Under the normal circumstances (i.e., without any intervention or bounding policy and regulations in place), one of these areas of private theories emerges to be the most dominant and strongly frames teachers’ instructional decision-making and iPad using practice. Private theories about students, teacher roles and technology, when one of these dominates a teacher’s thinking, were found to result in outdated and traditional instructional practices, and thus lead to limited or ineffective iPad uses. For any productive change to occur, a shift in a dominant private theory away from these three theories, and emphasis upon theories about learning is necessary. Further analysis focused on understanding of specific iPad using practices of teachers in the study (productivity tools, teaching tools, note taking, communication, file management via cloud, blogging, and content accessing), and link of these practices with the private theories and affordances of mobile technology environments (resources, connectivity, collaborative, capture, analytical, representational and administration). This lead to a set of set of recommendations for applications of iPad technology in the context of higher education in Hong Kong, and how teachers’ private theories mediate the adoption of the affordances of this technology. Finally, in relation to the third outcome, effort concentrated to articulate and provide a framework to support teachers’ effective engagement with the affordances of Touch Pad technology. It was understand that teacher iPad uses were strongly influenced by their private theories about students, teacher roles and technology, and the main affordance and practice utilized were resources and content accessing Apps. From the study, it is understood that an intervention is required to mediate teachers to place emphasis upon their private theories about learning. Such intervention might be achieved by utility of the RASE learning design model (further developed beyond this study).

743112.label: Major findings and research outcome
743112.value: This qualitative study investigated how higher education teachers use iPads to facilitate their practice. The study results provide insight into both the educational affordances of iPad technology and the ways in which teachers’ personal or private theories mediate adoption of these affordances. The study outcomes contribute to theoretical understanding of higher education teacher changes through adoption of mobile technology. Furthermore, the outcomes provide a set of recommendations for applications of iPads and similar technologies in higher education and ways to support teachers to effectively adopt such technology in their practices. The study explored and articulated specific iPad using practices of the participating teachers, resulting in the categories of productivity tools, teaching tools, note taking, communication, file management via cloud, blogging, and content accessing Apps, linking of these practices with the teacher private theories (falling into the categories of learning, students, teacher roles, technology, lesson design and changes) and explicating of affordances of mobile technology environments (including resources, connectivity, collaborative, capture, analytical, representational and administration). Strong focus on content accessing Apps and resources affordance for the teachers in this study indicates that they placed priority on iPads to serve as a tool for access and delivery of information. What is necessary is to engage teachers in exploring other possibilities of technologies, primarily those in which technologies are used beyond delivery of resources, and serve as a tool for learning-centered activities, support and evaluation, and where more emphasis is placed on collaboration, connectivity, representational possibilities and analytical uses of mobile technology. Any intervention and policy should focus in that direction. Further data collection and analysis in the study have been providing more in-depth understanding of connections between the affordances and private theories, and reveal areas of private theories that dominate the adoption of this technology over prolonged period of time. The researchers attempted to understand any changes in private theories through uses of iPads, that is, patterns of teacher change through such experience, and develop a model for effective support for teachers and the application of iPad technology in higher education (with focus on more contemporary, learning-centered practice). Such framework would support teachers to transform their theories for effective utilization of affordances of iPad technology, and inform institutions intending to provide teachers with iPads or similar devices. We are currently adapting the RASE learning design model to fit such context and purpose.

743112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
743112.value: This study explored teachers’ adoption of iPads at an institution in Hong Kong. The P-I is encouraged with the results, and he believes that there are significant possibilities for further research to considers teachers across the region and globally, as well as other related issues. Hence, the P-I has recently applied for two funded research project with the RGC. The initial GRF funding provided an important stimulus in pursuing research related to mobile learning ad teachers. The further project is a direct extension of the GRF study and attempt to take the inquiry beyond Hong Kong and across the Asia-Pacific region (application for Social Sciences Fellowship scheme from the RGC). This project, if funded, will study cases of exemplary Tablet using teachers from across countries in Asia-Pacific. The second application is for RGC/GRF funding to examine design and affordances of pedagogically effective apps, and articulate theory and practical design model to inform effective development of these kinds of mobile leaning resources. This would build upon the current understanding of categories of Apps effectively utilized by the participating teachers in the study reported here. Currently, there is absence of recommendations and a framework to support teachers in selecting and using Apps.

743112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743112.value: This study explored how higher education teachers utilized iPads in their practice. From the study, it was understood that the following categories of Apps were used frequently by the participating teachers in higher education: --Productivity Apps – These include tools such as word-processing, document annotation, multimedia authoring. --Teaching Apps – Tools that support classroom teaching, such as connection to a projector, mark-book, presentation tools and classroom management tools. --Notes Apps – Tools that enable note taking in combination with audio recording, drawing and typing. --Communication Apps – Tools that support communication and social networking. --File management – Tools that allow connectivity to the cloud, network drives and a computer. --Blogging Apps – Tools allow blogging via the iPad device. --Content Accessing Apps – Tools such as e-books and video repositories. How teachers use iPads depends upon private theories, which mediate their instructional decision-making, and which include theories about learning, students, teacher’s role, technology, lesson design and changes. For the most effective iPad use, teachers’ instructional decision making must be predominantly lead by their theories about learning. Other theories were found to have result in more traditional and ineffective or limited iPad use.

743412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743412.value: Over the past two decades, the growing enthusiasm for using eportfolios in higher education (HE) and moves to enhance learning-orientation of assessment in HE have come together in the promotion and exploration of eportfolios as HE assessment. While the potential of eportfolios is widely acknowledged, significant concerns remain about their effectiveness, especially for assessment. The current literature on eportfolios in HE disproportionately focuses on interest, enthusiasm and potential, rather than critical examinations of key variables and their relationship to success. Studies that do adopt a critical perspective reveal benefits but also significant difficulties, ranging from the challenge of adopting new technology to validity and reliability concerns. Research into eportfolios as assessment in HE hence needs further development. Enhancing this research has both global significance and particular importance in Hong Kong. The new objectives of the Hong Kong 3-3-4 curriculum reform have brought a concomitant need for innovative teaching, learning and assessment in HE. The 3-3-4 reform mirrors the global movement for enhancing learning-centered education, generally and assessment, specifically. Eportfolios are being rapidly promoted and adopted as an enhanced means to supporting and assessing new HE curricular outcomes. However, the pervasiveness of high-stakes, test-centric assessment culture in Hong Kong raises concerns about how stakeholders conceptualize and utilize eportfolios as assessment. Research-informed inquiry is needed to guide the 3-3-4 curriculum and investigate the place of eportfolios within this reform. The proposed study will meet this need through systematic research that may inform the global and Hong Kong HE communities and enhance theoretical understandings of both eportfolio use and learning-oriented assessment in HE. This will be accomplished through utilizing a theoretical framework that brings together both conceptual and utility components of assessment and technology. A complementary (qualitative and quantitative) methodology is used to examine eight courses from four disciplines critical to the 3-3-4 initiative: English, Chinese, Mathematics, and Liberal Studies. Data collection will consist of surveys, focus groups and interviews. Participant conceptions and change in conceptions will be examined, as will utilization of technology, structuring of assessment tasks, and eportfolio products. Factor analysis, ANOVA and inductive qualitative coding will allow researchers to demonstrate theoretical validity, develop course-based case studies, and present a comparative analysis across courses. This research is anticipated to expand global research into eportfolio use and innovative assessment in HE and make a valuable contribution to the current Hong Kong curriculum reform. 在過去的二十年内，高等教育界（HE）對使用E-portfolios和提高學習導向評估(learning-orientation of assessment) 逐漸產生興趣，促進了對E-portfolios的廣泛推廣及探索。 雖然E-portfolios的潛力被廣泛承認, 但對於E-portfolios作爲一種嶄新的高等教育評估方式的有效性仍存在疑問。目前有關文獻大多數集中于熱情地推廣E-portfolios的潛力及興趣，但缺乏對E-portfolio成功背後關鍵因素的深入探索。有研究從較深入的分析角度接觸這項目時，發現E-portfolio雖然有顯著的好處，但同時也存在着不少實施困難；例如採用新科技時面臨的挑戰及對其有效性和可靠性的質疑。因此，在高等教育正式使用E-portfolios作爲評估前，還需要進一步的研究及發展。 這項研究具有全球性的影響，特別是在香港。爲了符和全球教育界走向以提升學生學習及相應評估方式為中心的趨向，香港正實施3-3-4課程改革新目標；而相應地高等教育界亦需要有創新的教學，學習和評估方式。在這趨勢下，E-portfolios正被迅速推廣及確認為嶄新的高等教育評估方式。然而，如何在香港的傳統高風險、以測驗為中心(test-centric)的評估文化中概念化和有效實用E-portfolios評估方式亦引起了教育界各方關注。爲了引導3-3-4課程和調查E-portfolios在這個改革的角色、地位，更深入的研究是必要的。 本研究將通過有系統的調查，加強全球和香港高等教育界對E-portfolios的理論、使用和學習導向評估的理解。本研究所使用的理論框架將匯集學生及教師對評估及科技的概念和實用，採取互補的研究方式（包含定性和定量分析），調查3-3-4改革的四科關鍵學科：英語、中文、數學和通識教育等總共八個課程。數據收集將會以問卷調查，焦點小組和訪談方式進行。 參與者的觀念和其變化、科技使用、評估的結構工作和E-portfolios 產品使用將被考究。因子分析(factor analysis)、方差分析(ANOVA) 和感性的定性編碼(inductive qualitative coding)將允許研究人員證明理論基礎的有效性，開發課程案例研究，並為不同課程進行比較分析。 這項研究預計將擴大全球E-portfolio使用量和創新高等教育評估，對目前香港課程改革作出寶貴的貢獻。

743412.label: Realisation of objectives
743412.value: 1. Objectives 1 & 2 have been completed through the analytical process. This can be broken down into three areas, relevant to the steps outlined in prior reports: a. Analysis of quantitative data: all quantitative data have been analyzed. Analytical procedures included i. Assembly and cleaning of data into a viable data set; ii. Analysis of the clean data set through factor analysis, allowing for validation and adjustment of the presumed CATA (Conceptions and Actions in Technology and Assessment) theoretical model; iii. ANOVA and MANOVA carried out at item and factor levels across key variables; iv. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) carried out using the revised factor structure delivered through factor analysis. b. Analysis of qualitative data: all qualitative data have been analyzed. Analytical procedures included: i. Initial read for codes and categories; member checks; ii. Second read for stabilization of categories and establishment of parent/child codes; iii. Team validation exercise and subsequent adjustment of codes and categories; iv. Stable, validated construct of categories and hierarchical codes established. c. Relating and synthesis of quantitative and qualitative data: At this final stage, relationships are established between the two data sets. These relationships allow for exploration of both the CATA model through qualitative, coded responses and conversely, the interpretation of qualitative responses through the validated, adjusted model. Thus, a complementary and productive relationship is established between qualitative and quantitative results. 2. Objective 3 is output-specific (i.e. ‘present findings’). This has been accomplished in the manner anticipated: a. Peer-review journal publications. A particular highlight is the recent acceptance of a paper (Deneen, Brown & Carless, 2016) entitled, Students’ conceptions of eportfolios as assessment and technology. This reports the quantitative findings from our project and appears in Innovations in Education and Teaching International, an ISI-listed journal with a focus on the use of educational technology in higher education. b. Presentation of findings at well-regarded international conferences (e.g. AERA – American Educational Research Association – the most influential conference in the world of educational research). c. Presentation and development work focusing on use of eportfolios for assessment in a higher education context at multiple tertiary institutions, including but not limited to: i. The University of Hong Kong ii. The University of Macau iii. The University of Auckland iv. The University of Otago v. Auckland University of Technology Note: We are continuing to publish findings from the grant, aiming at tier one research journals (see the last two papers under development in part C, 8). Consequently, we have marked this as 90% (see 5.4). This reflects ongoing benefit/impact from the research rather than a deficit.

743412.label: Major findings and research outcome
743412.value: The grant was gained by Christopher Deneen and he was the PI until he moved to Singapore in August 2014. For continuity purposes, he has continued to take a leadership role in the project and its successful completion is due to his key contributions. Accordingly, Deneen is the first author for the refereed outputs and dissemination of project outcomes. Reported findings/Outcomes 1. Technology, learning, and assessment exist together and must be understood as interconnected phenomena in an eportfolio program. 2. Endorsement/acceptance of particular technologies leads to endorsement of conceptions of assessment specifically associated with assessment for learning (AfL). 3. Expression of intention to actively engage with eportfolios and rejection of assessment as irrelevant together contributed to a moderate but statistically significant increase in students’ self-reported Grade point average (GPA). 4. Curricular integration of the eportfolio impacts student and instructor engagement. E-portfolio is not a standalone innovation but one which impacts on how teaching is conducted; and how student learning evolves. 5. A key issue in success versus failure of an eportfolio program is sustained engagement which permits development and reflection over time. Sustained engagement is, in turn strongly impacted by a) curricular integration of the eportfolio b) instructors’ general and specific endorsement of technology. The role of instructor assessment literacy may also underpin the above.
