743412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743412.value: Using eportfolios to develop and assess achievement of curricular outcomes is a global higher education (HE) trend. The potential of eportfolios is widely acknowledged; significant concerns remain, however regarding their effectiveness, especially as an assessment mode. Current literature on eportfolios in HE focuses more on interest, enthusiasm and potential than critical examinations of key variables and their relationship to success. Studies adopting a critical perspective reveal benefits but significant difficulties. This study addresses the problems of understanding eportfolios as assessment in HE and seeks to close the gap between eportfolio adoption and theoretically informed research. It accomplishes this through theorizing and investigating relationships between conceptions and utilization of assessment and technology. Qualitative and quantitative data were gathered from multiple faculties at one university in Hong Kong. Analytical procedures included factor analysis, structural equation modeling, MANOVA and qualitative coding. The overall picture that emerged is that technology, learning, and assessment function together in an eportfolio program and must be understood as interconnected phenomena. Significant findings that support this conclusion include the connection between endorsement of technology and assessment for learning, and instructors’ endorsement of technology as affecting students’ sustained engagement with eportfolios.

744112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744112.value: The purpose of this project is to study the link between the time-varying risk appetite and the subsequent behavior of a broad array of activities of U.S. corporations. Previous studies in this field tend to look at corporate activities in isolation, with little account taken of various features of the corporate sector, such as those encompassing the cost of equity and debt capital, entrepreneurial activities, financing activities, capital structure, and savings. In this project we will operationalize an objective measure of riskiness that is independent of risk-taking attitude—following the conceptualization in Aumann and Serrano (2008)—to predict corporate activities. In our empirical assessments, we will compare the predictive power of Aumann and Serrano (2008)’s riskiness measure for corporate activities to that conveyed in average idiosyncratic volatility. We will treat risky investments as a form of gamble and estimate the riskiness of composite equity investments from the cross section of stock universes. Our approach in estimating the riskiness of equity investments is to take advantage of the stock universe and partition stocks into groups according to a set of salient characteristics, using the dimensions of idiosyncratic volatility and size. We will utilize the daily master file of individual stock returns from the Center of Research in Security Prices for a sample period of June 1963 to December 2010. Through this proposed project we will explore the hypothesis that when the riskiness of investments in the financial market rises, corporate managers reduce the amount of riskier corporate activities. The findings from the project will help to enhance our understanding of how the decisions of corporate managers are affected by the riskiness of investments. 这篇文章的主旨是研究市场风险承受力与美国公司经营活动之间的关系。现有的文献一般局限于单独研究公司经营活动，很少把这些经营策略行为（包括融资决策，投资决策）与市场风险承受力结合起来。 这篇文章中，我们首先估计市场风险承受力。这是一个客观度量，和个别投资者的风险承受力无关。这个度量遵循Aumann and Serrano (2008) AER文章，主要依据市场中非系统回报方差。 并假定风险投资活动类比于赌博活动，从而利用整个股票市场来估计这个市场风险承受能力。 我们的这个度量的优越之处在于我们着眼于整个股票市场，并根据市值及非系统回报方差划分股票，用每天每支股票的收盘价估值。我们的样本从1963年六月至2010年十二月。 我们期望通过这些分析更好的理解市场风险承受能力对于公司经营活动的影响，尤其是市场风险承受能力如何影响到企业经理的决策。

744312.label: Project Title(Chinese)
744312.value: 婦女與越南的中國離散者

744312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744312.value: In the voluminous literature on the history of ethnic Chinese in Southeast Asia, aside a few exceptions the women’s question has rarely been addressed in spite of the fact that women make up a considerable percentage of the Chinese population in Nanyang. The main objective of this project is to investigate the history of Chinese diaspora from the gender perspective with a special focus on the experiences of Chinese women in Vietnam. The study covers the period from the early 20th century, which marked the beginning of the influx of Chinese women to the then French colony, to the mid-1950s when southern Viet-Nam gained its independence and its president Ngô-dinh-Diêm introduced the nationality law and a series of draconian economic, social, and educational measures to force all the Chinese in South Vietnam to become Vietnamese citizens. The present project is structured along two axes: in the first instance it explores the diverse socio-historical circumstances under which Chinese women moved to colonial Vietnam during the first four decades of the 20th century. The second part of the project will investigate the roles of Chinese women in constructing the local diasporic community through an examination of their cultural, economic, and institutional engagements in both the private and public spheres. In the study special attention will be paid to how the class and generation factors impacted Chinese women’s experiences in the host country for far from being a homogenous group, they actually hailed from very diverging social backgrounds and belonged to different age groups. My reconstruction of the history of Chinese women in colonial Vietnam will draw on a broad range of sources taken from both the public and private domains. The public materials include archival documents such as the French colonial government’s regulations on Chinese immigration and the dossiers they kept on the Chinese immigrants; the records of the language-group associations or bangs that managed the affairs of the Chinese immigrants; and the local Chinese newspapers and magazines such as Funu Zhoukan (women’s weeklies) and Funu Ribao (women’s daily). The documentations of a more personal and private nature comprise of biographies, autobiographies, memoirs, literary writings by Vietnamese Huaqiao. The use of such a wide variety of materials will yield a more polyphonic and multi-faceted narrative of the experiences of diasporic Chinese women.

744512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
744512.value: 角度轉換後的物件記憶與熟悉感

744512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744512.value: How do we recognize objects across changes in view? This apparently simple question has proven very difficult to answer. A large body of work has shown that recognizing an object becomes more difficult as it rotates from a studied view. At the same time, however, we also know that people remain highly successful at recognizing rotated objects. How can we explain the fact that object recognition is both sensitive to viewpoint but is also able to generalize across viewpoints? One promising area for understanding this apparent dichotomy is the nature of the memory systems that underlie object recognition. A well-documented dissociation in research on human memory is found between recollection, the experience of remembering a particular personal episode in which an event took place, and familiarity, the feeling that an event occurred without any particular contextual details. Recollection of the presence of an object is likely to be view-specific, given that objects are encountered from discrete views during any particular viewing episode. Signals of object familiarity, however, might be more view-invariant, particularly if the visual system is able to store objects in long-term memory as structural representations or as tightly integrated networks of known views. Evidence supporting invariant familiarity signals from familiar objects come from a recent study of perceiving rapid repetitions of objects in our lab, as well as name priming studies from the past 20 years. In this proposal we adopt a variety of methods for dissociating recollection from familiarity about objects, and then examine the costs in each that accompany changes in viewpoint of an object between study and test. We will test both familiar objects with which participants have existing knowledge, and novel objects that they encounter for the first time in our research laboratory. The results are likely to provide key insights into the nature of object memory networks. 當物件的角度有所轉變後, 我們如何能辨認出它是原來的物件呢？這看似是簡單的問題，但事實上卻比我們想像中困難。很多研究發現人們要成功辨認出角度轉變後的物件是有一定的難度；但與此同時，我們平日卻可以非常輕易地辨認出來那物件有角度的轉變。那我們應如何解釋辨認物件的特定角度, 但又同時能得知該物件其他角度的樣貌呢？在眾解釋當中較為可取的，就是透過兩種不同的記認模式去理解辨認物件的能力。有大量關於人腦記憶的文獻指出記認模式大致可分為兩種: 重拾記憶和熟悉感。重拾記憶是對所經歷或已學習的事物有深刻印象; 而熟悉感則是對所經歷或已學習的事物有大致印象，但未能完全記起事物細節。從近二十多年以促發效果去研究記認模式的結論，以及我們實驗室近期以快速視象測試人們對一些熟悉物件角度轉換辨識的實驗結果, 我們相信當辨認物件是在特定的角度時, 該物件的重拾記憶應是一個特定視圖; 但是, 對該物件所產生熟悉感卻不受角度的限制, 尤其是該物件的結構已儲存在長期記憶中。 在這建議書中，我們將採用熟悉和全新的物件多種方法去識辨重拾記憶和熟悉感在辨認物件時的不同, 從而檢測這兩種記認模式在物件轉換不同角度後的影響。我們會測試. 是次實驗成果將能對了解記認物件的見解帶來重要的啟發。

744812.label: Project Title(Chinese)
744812.value: 港男無定(地)企？探索性選擇策略的模式

744812.label: Co - Investigator(s)
744812.value: Dr Cheng, Sea Ling Prof Tsang, A. Ka Tat

744812.label: Project Objectives
744812.value: Explore the life circumstances and the different strategies of sexual choices contemporary Hong Kong men use to re-define their masculinity. Identify Hong Kong men’s material, affective and sexual desires in light of social changes and how they fulfill them when personal and social resources are increasingly limited. Examine Hong Kong men’s ideals of masculinity – what constitutes a virile (dim) man, a good (hou) man, responsible (fu-zad- yem) man, successful (xing-gung) man, happy (fai- long) man and cool (ying) man. Explore how these men’s relationships and sexual choices are related to normative ideals and cultural logics (of doubt, duty and destiny) and contemporary popular discourses regarding including the iconic "Kong Guy" (kongnam) and "Kong Girls" (kong nu) debate. Understand Hong Kong men’s definition and affirmation of masculinity in Hong Kong and China as Hong Kong restructures its position with Mainland China and the world. Analyze how these men’s relationships and sexual choices produce behaviors and lifestyles that challenge current social and scientific understandings of masculinity, identity, desire and the erotic.

744812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744812.value: This study is about what it means to be a virile/capable man in Hong Kong. It seeks to develop a model of understanding HK men's strategies of sexual choices at a time of dramatic global, regional, and local transformations. In three consecutive annual sexual well-being global surveys by Durex, Hong Kong ranked second lowest in terms of sexual activity frequency. However, this is not the only indicator of Hong Kong men’s lack of virility and potency. In the last five years, popular discourse of “Kong guys” and “Kong girls” suggests that Hong Kong men lack financial and emotional capacity as partners and providers for women. The Department of Health recently launched a website to advise men on how to cope with social and emotional problems such as unemployment, bankruptcy, domestic violence, gambling, divorce and suicide. Middle-aged men are over-represented among suicide cases. The Legislative Council recommended the establishment of a Men’s Council to address men’s problems. The Equal Opportunities Commission has an ongoing project titled "Men in Pain." It would be no exaggeration to say that a crisis of masculinity exists in Hong Kong. The city has been repositioned politically, economically and socially in significant ways on the world map since the hand-over. The global financial crises have restructured the region's economy and the opportunities of individuals therein. Gender relations have been reconfigured in relation to these structural changes. Many Hong Kong men have sought newfound economic and sexual ventures in the mainland, creating a well-known phenomenon of "second wives" across the border. Yet due to a volatile global market and the rising value of the RMB, some of them no longer command the financial and erotic prowess to attract women, whether in the mainland or Hong Kong. Cross-border gender relations have undergone dramatic renegotations. Middle-aged Hong Kong men in particular face multiple challenges to their masculinity- unemployment and lack of financial security combine to threaten their sense of identity in the family, workplace and society. Through multiple in-depth interviews and focus groups with 40 Hong Kong middle aged men, this study explores Hong Kong men’s crisis of masculinity and the strategies they use to pursue their manly pride when personal, social and professional resources become increasingly limited. The concept of “flexible masculinity” is used to document the practices different groups of men employ to reproduce or challenge hegemonic masculinity which in turn re-invent ideals of masculinity and sexual culture. 港男無定(地)企？探索性選擇策略的模式 本研究探索香港男性的男子氣概 (masculinity) 现状和背後的意義。在全球、区域和本地的轉變下，此研究揭示一套了解香港男人性選擇策略的模式。 杜蕾斯公司近三年贊助的全球性生活质量調查報告發現，港人性生活/行为次數屢居全球倒数第二。但缺乏性行為不是唯一判断港男缺乏陽剛面與性能力的指标。近五年，有关「港男」、「港女」的論述充斥於公眾討論，背後引申的含义是香港男性缺乏经济和交際能力，無法吸引伴侶。 因此，男性缺乏阳刚面与(性)能力的問題引起各界關注；香港衞生署最近設立網站，為男性提供處理面對社會和情緒問題的建议，包括︰破產、家庭暴力、賭博，以至離婚等问题。中年男人的問題，尤其是自殺，常被社會放大。立法會也提議設立男士小組，平等機會委員會更已開展名為「性別定型及其對男性的影響」的研究計劃。總而言之，香港男性的剛陽氣/才能正面臨崩潰的危機。 回歸後，香港無論在政治、經濟或社會上都面臨重組；金融風暴重塑地方經濟，也改變個人的機遇，處於社會結構轉變中的兩性關係也在改变中。內地變成香港男仕追求事業和性生活的天堂，產生「包二奶」等跨境問題。然而，全球化市場快速轉變，以及人民幣升值使得本港和大陸女性眼中「港男」的光環不再；「港男」無論经济和性吸力， 都不大如前。跨境性別關係面臨重大轉變，中年男性面对的挑战尤其明显。失業加上財困，使男子氣概严重受损，家庭、工作和社會的身份備受威脅。 本研究採用深度訪問和聚焦小組方式的研究方法，訪問四十位香港中年男性，並研究香港男性缺乏男子氣概的原因。探討他們如何在社會、專業知识技能和個人資源有限的境况下，追求生活價值和榮譽的策略。借用「靈活的男子氣概」(flexible masculinity) 一概念，了解不同男性怎樣透過再生產或挑戰主流的男性定型，來重新定義男子氣概和性別文化。

744812.label: Realisation of objectives
744812.value: All the objectives were achieved satisfactorily. We are also pleasantly surprised by the unexpected outcomes that have been generated through the study which is really most useful to our understanding of personal life and families in times of political turbulence. We are glad to have produced concrete outputs including articles, book chapters and new research grants that have important theoretical and methodological implications in the field of masculinity, HK families and social movement participation. At the first stage of the project, we started by examining what constitutes a good guy in Hong Kong. This study focused on those age 30 to 60 and explored the strategies that they have used to re-define their masculinity through constraining their present and future sexual encounters as a way to reassure their partners as well as to adhere to the “ideals” of a good man and a good husband. At the second stage, we have chosen to examine their ideals of masculinity through inviting them to talk about what constitutes a “bad” guy (and the different kinds of bad behaviours that men identify as worst crimes in intimacy) by way of asking them how they feel about being a “pok guy” (Cantonese slang term for a bastard or cad that is often used as a curse and a derogatory remark). We hope to have a more in-depth understanding of men's self-reflections for the construction of the theoretical frameworks that would illustrate more complex accounts of the relationship between masculinity and heterosexuality at different levels of social construction. These include at the level of social institutions such as the law, education, the state and the media; at the level of social and cultural norms; at the level of social relationships and everyday practices, and at the level of individual subjectivities. What interests us most is the ways in which the talk about what makes a guy a bad guy or in Cantonese a “pok guy” would somehow always led to talks about the politics and how do they look at the Occupy Central Movement. The way these guys define themselves for or against the proposed movement and the 3 male leaders is most illuminating. The puzzles and our initial attempt to resolve them have made us realise how we should think about researching into HK men by introducing a new starting point, HK politics and analyse the images of the patriarchal figures in HK society. We therefore have ventured into exploring how HK or HK politics, is, in fact, an analytical approach for the understanding of social reality and HK men's personal life and social identity. As we moved along with the political currents, we have found interesting narratives that are most useful to our understanding of the relationship between public and private, the personal and the political as well as making the HK context an important analytical category. This unexpected turn was theoretically enlightening. In terms of methodology, we decided to include other team members and international collaborators in the analysis of the narratives during an international conference. We then came up with an innovative methodology called "collaborative focus group analysis" combining focus group with a reflecting team. We are glad to find that the project has the most exciting developments yielding important theoretical and methodological contributions. Journal articles, book chapters and conference presentations are produced on different aspects of the project. Last but not the least, we have also made good use of our experience to develop two new research grants. First, a new GRF proposal entitled "Personal life and political participation: Practices of intimacy in times of political turbulence" was submitted with a view to carry on our exploration of HK men and their families. We got 3.5 marks for our first submission in 2015. The proposal was revised and re-submitted again in 2016 year and we do hope that we will be able to broaden our concerns and provide a better understanding of issues of masculinity, identity and intimacy and family life in difficult times should we be able to get the GRF grants again. Second, another proposal entitled "Men Managing Relationships: A Comparative Study of Men’s Diverse Practices of Intimacy in the UK, Hong Kong and China" will be submitted to ESRC soon. Professor Stevi Jackson of University of York (UK) and I have been working on a bilateral project Gender, Intimacy and Modernity, East and West: An exploratory comparative study since 2010. This produced excellent results with most encouraging feedback from the ESRC. In 2015, we expanded our UK-HK team to include Dr. Christine Skinner (University of York), Dr. Liu Jieju (SOAS), Dr. Jacque Gabb (Open University, UK), Dr. Travis Kong, Dr. Dennis Tang (Department of Sociology, HKU), and Dr. Celia Chan (Department of Social Work & Social Administration, HKU) creating an international research team to carry on our studies of men, family and intimacy. This ESRC grant application is entitled, “Men managing relationships: A comparative study of men’s diverse practices of intimacy in the UK, Hong Kong and China”. This is a strong international cross-disciplinary team combining expertise from social work, social policy, sociology and Chinese studies. In the proposed project, our over-arching research question is: How are men’s practices of intimacy shaped by different socio-economic, cultural, spatial and political contexts and with what consequences for their everyday lives? Our comparative study recognises that it is insufficient to take what is already known about western contexts and compare China and Hong Kong against them. Effective comparison means designing research to answer the same research questions in all locations, taking account of local conditions and social, economic and political circumstances. This will be the first five-city study of urban men: Hong Kong, Beijing, Hangzhou, London and Leeds and has the potential to theorise new masculinities that questions the hegemony of Western conceptualisations. We regard these new grant application as important output of this GRF project as these new initiatives are most important to the further developments of new theories and methodologies on researching into personal life. The international collaboration involved are useful to help us advance scholarship in the field of gender/sexuality and personal/political life. Recently, I am also honored to be invited by Sari van Anders, Editor of Annual Review of Sex Research to write a review of sexuality and intimacy in China in the past ten years based on a synthesis of scholarship in the field (25,000-30,000 words). Our experience in this GRF project and the new grant applications would be most relevant and useful. We also feel that this review is one of the best ways to disseminate our findings and consolidate what we have learnt from HK men and their families.

744812.label: Major findings and research outcome
744812.value: The study begins with exploring the personal life and sexual choices of HK men by asking the questions: (1) what is a good guy? (2) what is a bad guy (pok guy). Interestingly, the study has evolved in response to political events in HK as we sought ways to understand the impact of politics on Hong Kong men’s lives and the way the interviewees compared themselves to other patriarchal figures as a way to re-define themselves and justify their life choices. On top of the initial interviews at the beginning stage about their everyday life and intimate relationships, we have also produced publications and derived new data from two sources at the second stage of the project: (1) two sets of interviews with five paired men, who were strangers to each other, conducted before and after the Umbrella Movement; (2) a focus group with a mix of men and women. All participants in interviews and focus groups were Hong Kong Chinese. The men interviewed and the members of the mixed focus group came from a variety of class backgrounds and a range of occupations, ages, sexualities and political orientations. The rationale for the paired stranger interviews with men was that we wanted to establish a quasi-homosocial environment for ‘men talk’, recognising that men do not talk to women in the same way that they talk to each other. Two rounds of interviews were conducted with each pair. Three pairs were interviewed both before and after the Umbrella Movement (first in July 2014, when Occupy Central was active and then in April 2015). All the interviews with the remaining two pairs were conducted after the Umbrella Movement. Stories about how do these guys see themselves in relation to other guys (especially the male politicians and patriarchal figures were central to these accounts documented in our publications and documentary films. Besides the pair strangers interviews method, the project has also helped us develop new ways of doing research. In our conference “Changing Practices of Intimacy and Family Life in a Globalised World”, we encouraged dialogues that reversed the usual relationship between researchers and the researched through the formation of a reflecting team (adopted from family therapy). This research strategy appreciates the power of genuine collaboration in the researcher-participant relationships. Importantly, participants have direct access to the ideas of the researchers and can challenge them directly. The process itself can generate new themes.

744812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
744812.value: This overlapping ‘private’ realm of familial relationships and the ‘public’ world of politics could potentially create a dialogue between social movement literature and that on and family practices. We consider our contribution to be able to fill some gaps in the two areas of study. What the umbrella movement – and the wider democracy movement – have been fighting for is not only democracy but greater autonomy and freedom from control by China. One consequence of this resistance to political authoritarianism is a parallel resistance to domestic authoritarianism which our study reveals. Our aim in the future projects, is to consider how the experience of political turbulence has affected family practices and practices of intimacy within families, in particular in relation to challenges to hierarchical harmony in Chinese families and the wider political culture. These ideas have been incorporated in our new research grant applications and we hope to have the opportunities to dig deeper into our initial formulations should we get new resources to do more.

744812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
744812.value: The study contribute to our understanding of HK men and HK families. We show how HK men can engage in critical and emotional reflexivity through their observation and participation in politics. The break from routines have enabled these guys to tell stories of self-transformation in which they portrayed a move away from acceptance to the status quo within family and society towards a new view of both. Some guys can present themselves as a reformed patriarch after their exposure and new social experiences. All of them, to some degree, spoke of forging a new sense of independence from authoritarian families. These narratives suggest that Hong Kong politics has, for some, created spaces for men to "do" gender and family in new ways, creating new Chinese family practices, which can accommodate to changing relationships – albeit not without difficulty and compromise. The family practices that they have engaged in are also their attempts to achieve ‘negotiable intimacy" rather than authoritarian rule. We show how democracy in family and society can interact to produce new social norms and practices. We also created a new research methodology called "collaborative focus group analysis". Our new grant applications are attempts to consolidate these new development.

744812.value: A series of documentary on HK men called Kong-lo Chronicles 港佬列傳 were produced from the interviews. 1. Kong-Lo Chronicles Part 1 (Pre-Umbrella Movement) This film is about 6 Hong Kong men, a taxi driver, a fireman, a journalist, a village head, a small trader and a civil servant. I paired up each guy with another guy from a very different background to examine their ideals of masculinity through inviting them to talk about what constitutes a “bad” guy (and the different kinds of bad behaviours that men identify as worst crimes in intimacy) by way of asking them how they feel about being a “pok guy” (Cantonese slang term for a bastard or cad that is often used as a curse and a derogatory remark). The ways in which they talk about what makes a guy a bad guy or in Cantonese a “pok guy” somehow always led to talks about politics. The way they define themselves for or against the Occupy Central Movement is illuminating of the complex accounts of the relationship between masculinity and heterosexuality. 2. Kong-Lo Chronicles Part 2 (Post-Umbrella Movement) In the post-umbrella movement phase, we interviewed these 3 pairs of men again to explore further their observations and experiences of the occupation. The dramatic moments and events that people have seen or participated in during the occupation have helped elucidate how the specificity of Hong Kong politics can provide us with new analytical insight for looking at social issues, the making of self-identity, and intimacy. 3. Politics and practices of intimacy Part 3 (Evaluation of the Umbrella Movement) A focus groups was conducted with 11 participants from all walks of life in June, 2015 to investigate the consequences of the umbrella movement (for both participants and opponents) on family life and intimate relationships. The film was called: Practices of Intimacy and the Umbrella Movement: A Collaborative Focus Group Analysis (親密關係與雨傘運動：協作聚焦小組分析) Discover Society: I was invited to organise a special issue for Discover Society on the Umbrella Movement and its social impact. 744912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744912.value: Symptom management and functional enhancement are pressing concerns for patients with schizophrenia. Even when symptoms are managed under medication, residual symptoms and medication side-effects hinder optimal functioning and community participation. Stress management is equally crucial as stress can trigger or exacerbate psychotic symptoms. Aerobic exercise has proven effective in improving mood, quality of life, social interactions, memory and even symptoms of schizophrenia from numerous intervention trials. Tai-chi exercise is a series of movement forms based on Chinese martial arts and traditional philosophies of calmness, acceptance and self-restraint. It synthesizes benefits of both exercise and relaxation into a holistic, mind-body intervention which can potentially target the multidimensional manifestations of schizophrenia. The cardinal role of stress on schizophrenic prognosis roused academic interest on the association between the Hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and symptoms. The HPA axis controls bodily stress response which is manifested in salivary cortisol. If Tai-chi can potentially influence symptoms and other disabilities, knowing how the HPA axis responds to Tai-chi would be significant to understanding the mind-body interactions of mental illness. Using a 3-arm randomized control design, this study aims to investigate the impact of a Tai-chi exercise program on the symptoms, stress levels, motor and memory deficits and functioning disabilities of patients with schizophrenia. Furthermore, it will explore the association between cortisol rhythm with symptoms and deficits. It is expected that a model of interactions among the studied variables will enable a more holistic understanding of the manifestations of schizophrenia. 135 patients diagnosed with schizophrenia will be randomized into a (i)Tai-chi group, (ii)Exercise comparison group or (iii)Waitlist control group. Twenty-four sessions of 1-hour Tai-chi classes (Wu-style Cheng-form) will be conducted twice a week over the course of 12 weeks. Three subsequent booster sessions will be held for 3 months after class completion to encourage regular practice. All participants will be assessed at 3 time points: (i)baseline, (ii)after 12 weeks, and (iii)after 24 weeks. They will be assessed in their positive and negative symptoms, cortisol and subjective stress levels, movement deficits in coordination and sequencing, memory and functioning. Building upon a pilot trial conducted by the team on residential patients with psychosis, this community-based study is the first to systematically explore the effects of Tai-chi on multifaceted deficits of schizophrenia. Tai-chi is a sustainable, cost-effective intervention with evident clinical merits. This study will enable better understanding of the mind-body effects of schizophrenia, thereby informing intervention design for the Chinese population. 研究撮要 精神分裂症患者即使在藥物的有效幫助下，仍然會受到病患或藥物副作用的影響，對日常生活和社交發展造成相當的阻礙。對精神分裂症患者來說，能夠有效地控制症狀和增強日常生活能力是十分重要的，而教導病患者如何處理和應付壓力，減少觸發或加劇精神病症狀的發生，對醫護人員來說同樣極之重要。 研究顯示，帶氧運動能幫助患者改善情緒、提昇生活質素、有助社交互動、改善記憶力，甚至部分精神分裂症的症狀。太極運動起源於中國武術，包含了東方傳統的哲學思想，著重平靜、接納、自我調控和身意合一，是一種全面的介入，能夠有效地對精神分裂症患者產生正面效用。 由於壓力對誘發精神分裂症扮演著重要的角色，學術界希望了解下丘腦垂體腎上腺軸及與精神分裂症症狀的關係。下丘腦垂體腎上腺軸控制身體對壓力之反應，顯現於唾液皮質醇之中。假使太極運動能對精神分裂症症狀產生正面的效用，了解下丘腦垂體腎上腺軸如何對太極運動作出相對的反應，將會為明白精神病患者的身心互動關係帶來一大貢獻。 研究計劃會採用隨機控制的試驗研究設計，目的是為了更系統地研究太極運動對於精神分裂症患者的症狀、壓力、記憶力、活動能力、壓力荷爾蒙和日常生活能力的影響，對於精神分裂症患者的復健，希望有更全面的了解及掌握。 135位精神分裂症的患者會隨機抽簽進入太極組、運動對照組或等候控制組。太極組將參加二十四節吳式鄭家太極拳(為期十二個星期，每星期兩節，每節一小時)。運動對照組會用相同時間進行踏步等肢體運動。太極組完成訓練後的三個月內，會舉行複習班以鼓勵組員練習。所有參加者於參加組別之前、十二個星期後和二十四個星期後接受評估。 研究團隊的先導研究發現，練習太極運動對住院精神病人有明顯的保護性功效，可以減慢動作不協調及人際疏離等現象，是次研究計劃將會是首次全面有系統性地研究太極運動對於精神分裂症症狀的影響。太極運動是一項能持續而且有臨床果效的介入手法，是次研究結果會令到精神分裂症之身心互惠影響更加清楚及明顯，亦為日後華人精神分裂症患者之介入手法奠下基礎和發展方向。

744912.label: Realisation of objectives
744912.value: The primary objectives of this study have been fully achieved. We conducted a 3-arm randomized controlled study on 153 patients with schizophrenia (fully matched with our proposal). We had examined the effects of Tai-chi, as compared with exercises and no intervention controls, on positive and negative symptoms, motor deficits, memory deficits, and functioning disabilities as well as stress level and cortisol level. Please refer to the finding section (6.1) and the outputs (8.3,8.4, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.6, 9.7, 9.8, 9.11) for details. The secondary objectives of exploring local schizophrenic patients’ diurnal cortisol levels, patterns, associations with their symptom severity, stress level, motor and memory deficits, functioning, as well as the interactions among all these factors have also been fully achieved. We have reported these related findings in 3 manuscripts (8.1, 8.2, 8.3) and 3 conference presentations and published abstracts (9.8, 9.9, 9.11). In addition to the above objectives, we also examined the psychometric properties of the measurement tool used in this study (8.2, 9.10), and the pathway between neuropsychiatric symptoms, functioning, memory and stress (8.4, 9.9). The research student trainined with this grant also conducted a review study on the relationship between Tai-chi and neurosciences; and presented the findings in a conference (9.11). All these objectives are extra to the original proposal but outputs are derived directly from this study.

744912.label: Major findings and research outcome
744912.value: Research data from this study demonstrated the benefits of Tai-chi on adults with chronic schizophrenia. Findings showed that, when compared with the control group, Tai-chi exercise is able to reduce motor deficits (in terms of balancing, motor coordination and sequencing) and improves backward digit span, and response to stress for adults with chronic schizophrenia. Exercise group displayed significant decreases in motor deficits, negative and depressive symptoms, and improves forward digit span, daily living function, and mean cortisol [Item 8.3, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.6, 9.7, 9.8]. Comparing therapeutic effects between the Tai-chi and Exercise conditions, we found no statistically significant difference on therapeutic effectiveness between two conditions, except that the exercise group showed better symptoms management than the Tai-chi group. Interestingly, Tai-chi group demonstrated greater symptom manifestation at 3-month and 6-month time points [Item 8.3, 9.6, 9.7]. Our hypothesis (Hypothesis I) of Tai-chi leading to multidimensional improvements for people with chronic schizophrenia compared with moderate exercise intervention or a control group is partially supported by empirical data. This study also aimed at examining the relationships between diurnal cortisol patterns and perceived stress, lifestyle factors, psychotic symptoms, neurological deficits, and daily functioning in patients with chronic schizophrenia (Hypothesis II) based on the neural diathesis-stress model. Our data demonstrated the hypothalamic- pituitary-adrenal axis as potential mediator of the effects of lifestyle factors on psychotic symptoms and neurological deficits. Evidence demonstrated that higher levels of perceived stress and body-mass index and less physical activity significantly predicted flattened diurnal cortisol slopes. In addition, flattened diurnal cortisol slope at baseline significantly predicted greater psychotic symptoms and neurological deficits in 3-month time, when baseline status is taken account for [Item 8.5, 9.6, 9.11]. Our research output also made additional contribution to the holistic understanding of the manifestation of schizophrenia symptoms. We conducted analyses on examining the pathways between neurological soft signs to functional outcomes in chronic schizophrenia patients. We found no direct effects from motor and sequencing deficits to daily life functioning. Rather, sequencing and motor deficits showed significant negative indirect effects on daily functioning with working memory, negative and disorganized symptoms as potential mediators [Item 8.4 & 9.9]. Our research output further extended to the validation of the consensus five-factor model of the Positive and Negative Symptom Scales (PANSS) and its convergent validity in the local context. Results generated from the study support the conventional five-factor structure o model off the PANSS as a robust measure of symptoms in schizophrenia [Item 8.2 & 9.10]. Lastly, the research student trained in this project also examined the effects of Tai-chi from the perspective of neuroscience (9.5).

744912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
744912.value: The therapeutic effects of Tai-chi program over exercise and control group had been examined in our research study. Tai-chi exercise is able to reduce motor deficits (in terms of balancing, motor coordination and sequencing) and improves backward digit span, and response to stress for adults with chronic schizophrenia. The exercise group showed better symptoms management than the Tai-chi group. It is meaningful to further explore the underlying mechanisms accountable for such difference. In addition, data also demonstrated an increase in the mean cortisol level in both the Tai-chi and exercise groups, showing stimulations on the physiological stress coping system in patients. Further study is needed to investigate the potential impact of this stimulation on the chronically depressed hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis in this population. Our study focused primarily on adults with chronic schizophrenia who are receiving residential healthcare services. It would be meaningful to future examine the effects of Tai-chi or exercise program on individuals with schizophrenia with different severity. Such endeavors would help us better understand the therapeutic effects of Tai-chi and exercise program in schizophrenia rehabilitation.

744912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
744912.value: Data collected from the present study demonstrated the potential benefits of practicing Tai-chi in schizophrenia rehabilitation. When compared with having no exercise, practice of Tai-chi was not only found effective in alleviating motor deficits, but also effective in enhancing working memory and in our response to stress for those who suffered from schizophrenia. Exercise program also demonstrated improvements in memory and daily functioning. For symptoms management, exercise program showed better effects than the Tai-chi group during the study period. In addition, our findings leaned to support the stress-diathesis model of schizophrenia; with data suggested that impaired responses to daily life stress resulted in more severe symptoms of schizophrenia in 3-month time.

745312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745312.value: 有些人性格樂觀，另一些卻是悲觀的。研究發現，悲觀的人在幾十年後的生活中，碰到不少如健康狀況不佳等問題。與此相反，樂觀的人，生活中往往有正面的成果。雖然學者對悲觀歸因風格有何相關及結果有很多的研究，關於其原因的卻所知甚少。為解決這不足，我們會聚焦於一個生物/個人的可能成因 - 睡眠。我們將調查樂觀/悲觀歸因風格和睡眠變量 (即睡眠質量和晝夜偏好) 之間的因果關係。睡眠質量指的是等待睡眠期、睡眠時間、習慣性睡眠效率、睡眠障礙、睡眠藥物的使用、和日間功能障礙。晝夜偏好指的是一個人是否在早晨或一天的其他時間更清醒和活躍。 睡眠質量和悲觀之間的因果關係的假設是有原因的。首先，睡眠不佳會產生不良的生理和心理的結果。它傷害了解決問題的能力，從而帶來挫折感和對生命的無奈。其次，不良的睡眠會導致白天嗜睡，精神萎靡，這繼而使人對日常活動失去動力，無心克服困難，從而帶來一種悲觀的前景。第三，睡覺本身會成為一種頑性問題。這種 “習得性無助感”是悲觀的一個主要組成部分。 同樣，晝夜偏好會影響歸因風格。我們以前的研究結果顯示，偏好晚上活動的人學業成績較差。夜貓子學習不佳，可能是因為他們的晝夜型和學校的時間表失配。這會打擊學生的自我效能感，導致悲觀情緒。此外，早起的人通常被視為兢業勤奮，而夜貓子則被視為事事拖延。這樣的看法可能會使後者嘗試改變他們醒著的時間。然而，由於晝夜偏好主要是由生理因素決定，夜貓子的屢戰屢敗可能會產生一個負面的自我感知、預期的失敗、和社會的尷尬。這些都可以是悲觀情緒的前因。 我們將在兩年間把關鍵的變量測量三次。這樣的設計使我們能夠推斷出睡眠與悲觀間長期和短期的兩種因果關係。我們將在一個已有超過六千人的樣本中選取部份參與者進行追蹤研究。他們當中一些人已經在早前的調查中為我們提供了有關悲觀歸因風格、睡眠質量、和晝夜偏好等數據。這些人其後將完成更多的調查問卷。

745312.label: Major findings and research outcome
745312.value: The present project found bidirectional causality between optimism and sleep quality. There is clear evidence that optimism was predictive of sleep quality measured later. While this relationship (total effects) was significant across the three chronotypes, the direct effect of optimism on sleep quality and the indirect effects through anxiety and stress, (but not depressive mood) were only significant for the intermediate circadian preference group. In other words, the aggregated effects of optimism on sleep quality were invariant of chronotype. However, both the direct effects of optimism itself and its indirect effects via anxiety and stress on sleep quality were, albeit significant together, somewhat weak by themselves. Hence, for the morning-type and evening-type students, the effects emerged as significant only when combined into a total effect. Taken together, people who are pessimistic generally have more anxious mood and stress symptoms, which adversely affect sleep. Causation in the opposite direction was also demonstrated. Sleep quality significantly predicted optimism longitudinally, but only in the evening-type and the intermediate-type. While both the direct effect and the indirect effect through depressive symptoms were significant for the intermediate-type, sleep quality only influenced optimism in evening individuals indirectly through depressive symptoms. Good sleep reduces depressive mood and consequently encourages an optimistic explanatory style, while poor sleep results in depressive mood and thus pessimism in non-morning chronotypes. Individuals with different circadian preference showed different responses to poor sleep in terms of their mood symptoms and their attributional style. Morningness has a specific protective effect against the potential damage of poor sleep on optimism, though not against the damage of pessimism on sleep quality. On the other hand, morningness does not give students the same immunity against the adverse effects of pessimism on sleep, although it is equally valid to predict that early risers can sleep even better if their optimism is further enhanced. Consistently, the morning-type group indeed slept better and were more optimistic in both Wave 1 and Wave 3 than the other two chronotypes. To summarize, the present study contributed to the literature in several ways. First, it demonstrated the bidirectional causation between optimism and sleep quality. Second, it introduced anxiety and stress in addition to depressive mood as possible explanations of the causal links. Third, it underlined chronotype as an important moderator of these effects, highlighting the unique role of morning-type in minimizing the effects of poor sleep quality on optimism.

745312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745312.value: Future intervention studies may validate the above models in both patient (e.g., insomnia) and high-risk (e.g., evening-type with high pessimism) populations.

745312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
745312.value: While both sleep and optimism have been found to be predictive of well-being, few studies have examined their relationship with each other and the other variables related to this relationship. We found that there were correlations among sleep quality, depressive mood, stress symptom, anxiety symptom and optimism. Moreover, more advanced statistical analyses showed a bidirectional effect between optimism and sleep quality. Path analysis demonstrated that anxiety and stress symptoms partially mediated the influence of optimism on sleep quality, while depressive mood partially mediated the influence of sleep quality on optimism. Poor sleep affects mood symptoms and optimism differently for different circadian preferences (chronotypes). Optimism and sleep quality were both cause and effect of each other. Depressive mood partially explained the effect of sleep quality on optimism, whereas anxiety and stress symptoms were mechanisms bridging optimism to sleep quality. This was the first study examining the complex relationships among sleep quality, optimism, and mood symptoms altogether longitudinally. Clinicians should target sleep in treating pessimistic patients presenting with depressive symptoms and a non-morning chronotype. At the community level, improving sleep health can potentially reduce the risk of developing depressive mood and pessimism.

745412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745412.value: The law is centrally involved in acts of classification, and it has ultimate control over all the legally-relevant categories that fall within its domain. This project focuses on 'self-classification' (or 'self-definition') as a topic for legal theory, that is the desire (and potential right) to classify oneself in relation to a legal category. The categories discussed are 'man' and 'woman', considered in relation to transgender identities. The label 'transgender' is applied to identities that conflict psychologically and experientially with the sexual classification assigned officially at birth, and with the social roles associated with such assignments. It encompasses a diverse range of affirmed, adopted, asserted, or aspired to identities which do not confirm to normative assumptions about binary sex/gender identities. In the Hong Kong case of W v Registrar of Marriages (2010), the court found that, for the purposes of marriage, the assigned sexual identity registered at birth ('male') was decisive and rejected the application of the male-to-female transgender woman plaintiff. The project approaches this as a legal, ethical, historical and linguistic question. Firstly, it considers in general how law approaches questions of classification in relation to familiar or everyday categories. Objects, events and people are classified in a wide variety of ways, and law draws on both internal and external resources. In Nix v Hedden (1893) the issue at stake was whether a tomato was a 'fruit' or a 'vegetable'. This project considers whether and in what ways self-classification should be distinguished from other forms of legal classification. Secondly, it places transgender decisions in the context of other important social categories such as 'parent', 'family member', 'spouse' in welfare and family law, and 'race' and 'sex' in employment and anti-discrimination law. In Edwards v A-G Canada (1930) the question at stake was whether the category 'person' included 'woman'. The project tracks the tension between treating such terms as technical legal concepts and taking them as ordinary words which may change meaning in direct response to social changes, arguing that legal interpretation is grounded in socio-political change, but in unpredictable and mediated ways. Thirdly, the project seeks to place transgender issues at the heart of debates about legal interpretation, definition and classification. It argues that far from being a marginal or 'exotic' phenomenon, transgender jurisprudence raises fundamental questions about authority and expertise, the autonomy and limits of law, the control of definition, and the understanding of language within legal interpretation. 跨性別(變性)人士的法律學: 自我歸類和法律 法律是集中處理有關歸類的事宜，而且它本身也對一切與法律有關的類別擁有最終的控制權。這次專題研究集中探討"自我歸類"這一項法律理論。"自我歸類" 是指個人渴望(和擁有潛在的權利)去把自己歸納入其中一個法律類別。被討論的類別包括"男人"和"女人"，當中會研究和討論跨性別(變性)人士的身分和法律如何定義以上所提及的術語。

745412.label: Realisation of objectives
745412.value: The objectives of this project have been very substantially met, in terms of the publications complete for under review, conferences, and in terms of creating momentum for future work. In particular, I have set out a novel approach to transgender jurisprudence, focussing on ordinary language, as well as offering an integrated historical, legal, definitional approach to legal sex and issues of law’s understandings of sexual identity. I gave papers at a range of conferences and received very positive feedback on my work. The overall groundwork for this project was laid by my book, Word Meaning and Legal Interpretation (2014), where the basic themes, legal topics, and theoretical frameworks were set out and the wider definitional an legal questions presented. The subsequent publication are all specialised off-shoots from this work, and the culmination of this is the manuscript The Tyranny of Ordinary Meaning: Corbett v Corbett and Legal Sex. The project is currently being reviewed by Palgrave. The major frustration has been the slow pace of academic review, notably in the case of the Law and Literature article (which was originally completed in mid-2015 but the special issue was delayed). My detailed proposal to Palgrave for a monograph was submitted in early August. While Palgrave have responded positively (see attached proposal and email exchange), I am still waiting for their definitive response. I have completed a first draft of the work (68,000 words), which is more or less ready for submission (also attached). However it makes no sense to put this in a finalized form before receiving the referees’ comments, as they may ask for specific changes or additions. This has caused a delay. Nonetheless I am confident that this book will be published in 2017, putting the seal on the project. One of the causes of the delay with this book is that it is highly interdisciplinary and therefore does not fit easily into publishers’ categories or lists.

745412.label: Major findings and research outcome
745412.value: The major findings of this reproach are essentially two-fold: the first is that the notion of legal sex lacks any secure foundation or jurisprudential basis. Looked at historically, it is a very late construct of legal reasoning, arising out of socio-cultural challenges to marriage law another institutions where sex plays a significant role. The second is that law relies on what is in effect a crypto-category, ordinary language, to deal with bedrock concerts or very fundamental social categories like man and woman. These two findings are related, in that ordinary language is used to fill the vacuum of legal principles, and judges appeal to ordinary language as if it were a stable category of the world simply available for importation into law. from setting out the basic principles and categories in my book Word Meaning and Legal Interpretation, and giving several conference papers, I have move on to a series of interlocking papers which culminate in the study of self-classification an the legal and social issue stat arise if legal sex were to be abolished. All these strands and the historical analysis come together in my forthcoming book: The Tyranny of Ordinary Meaning: Corbett v Corbett and Legal Sex, which I expect to be published by Palgrave in 2017. In addition, I have also added a postcolonial element to this project in my piece on Hong Kong law and ‘colonial modernity’, and intend to also write further on the question of expertise in law and linguistics, i.e. the issue of who gets to say what words mean and to what effect?

745412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745412.value: The first priority is finalising the publication of the monograph, which should be completed in the coming months. This research has led to a related project on the classification of animals within law (Humanities and Social Sciences Prestigious Fellowship Scheme award, HK$582,700, Defining Fundamental Concepts: The Legal Personhood of Animals,). This project brings many of the insights and analyses from the Transgender jurisprudence project, linking it in particular to legal personality and what I term ‘bedrock concepts’. The line of work from the GRF to the HSSPFS will I believe prove very fruitful in the coming years, in particular since I bring my own, distinct perspective from language studies to this complex intellectual, social and ideological problems.

745412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
745412.value: Law classifies individuals into male and female, and this legal status accompanies individuals throughout their lives in their interaction with the state. What is striking is that this status has no clear basis in law; it emerged out of the rise of the administrative state in the 19th century, drawing on cultural and theological understandings that go back centuries. The lack of an explicit legal foundation emerges in judicial reasoning, where judges are faced with a lack of a long history of cases, and no statutory or doctrinal legal basis. They tend to seek justification in biology, in linguistic definition, or in social values, but in an unsystematic and ad hoc manner The case of Corbett v Corbett (1971) emerges as key to the understanding of legal sex on a global scale, as the judge (also trained as doctor) set out a basic set of criteria fro defining sex. However what underlay the decision was the ordinary meanings of the words man and woman. Law looks to ordinary language to solve its definitional problems, and this is arguably highly problematic in its lack of reference to an individual’s own self-understanding and self-labelling.

745712.label: Project Objectives
745712.value: To apply literary historical analysis to the publications produced by the first American missionaries to China in the 1830s, 1840s, and 1850s in order to assess the influence of these missionaries on the subsequent development of United States print culture, early US-China relations (cultural, diplomatic, economic), and the disciplinary study of China in the United States. To highlight the crucial historical significance of the first American missionaries whose knowledge of the Chinese language and work on *The Chinese Repository* enabled their central involvement as translators in diplomatic proceedings between China and the United States during the two Opium Wars and the Taiping Rebellion. To develop historical analysis of these missionaries' impact on American national development through analysis of print culture that appreciates the denominational styles (Baptist, Dutch Reformed, Presbyterian, etc.) of Christian belief and missionary activity. To consider the assumptions that the missionaries had about race and gender as they pursued their goals of printing and preaching in Canton while trying to reach out beyond the Hong factories to the population beyond. To interpret descriptions of the collaboration between the American missionaries and the Chinese converts such as Liang Ah-fa and Liang Ateh, who were crucial to the missionary projects and played a significant role through their proselytizing and dissemination of tracts in inspiring the Taiping Rebellion. To orient the printing of *The Chinese Repository* and the other print endeavors (dictionaries, commercial almanacs) in relation to the British foundations of China-based and Malacca-based printing by Robert Morrison, William Milne, and Samuel Dyer, who were vital collaborators in the early stages of the Americans’ efforts. To redefine the early-national public sphere in the United States (pre-Civil War) by conceptualizing the global and national audiences for the *The Chinese Repository*; to revise understandings of the early-American print culture and the dynamics of its putative “imagined community” (viz. B. Anderson) by appreciating the role of American missionaries whose various senses of faith motivated them to try to control of the general economy of their print publication in global contexts based in Guangdong.

745712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745712.value: In the early 1830s, the first missionaries from the United States arrived in Canton (Guangzhou), China. Elijah Bridgman and Samuel Wells Williams spent the next twenty years publishing an astounding number of books, pamphlets, and the monthly journal *The Chinese Repository* (1832-1851). Inspired by the example of British missionaries, these Americans chronicled their times, including the First Opium War (1839-42), the ensuing revolutionary energies in China, and the rise of the United States to international respectability as a China trading partner. As the Canton Trade system fell apart with the opening of other treaty ports after the Treaty of Nanjing (1842), Bridgman and Williams progressively shut down their Canton operations and moved to Shanghai. Nevertheless, their Canton printing endeavors had pushed the boundaries of print technology in ways that shape the study of United States and China to this day. *Publishing China* produces articles, conference papers, and the first scholarly monograph on the Guangdong-based printing activities of these first American Missionaries in China. I pay literary historical attention to the practices of material print culture and their textual representation in order to describe and interpret the early nineteenth-century history of the cultural, economic and political relations between China and the United States. While considering the general system of their publication enterprise, I will focus critical attention on William’s massively influential ethnographic and historical overview of China *The Middle Kingdom* (printed significantly in an original and revised edition, 1848; 1883) and on the remarkable *The Chinese Repository*. Ambitiously global in their scope, the missionaries were motivated to print by convictions of Christian faith. The carnage of opium war and revolutionary violence tested both their evangelical designs and their faith in the power of the press to a point of exhaustion and near failure. As Bridgman and Williams imagined audiences for their texts in China and won Chinese converts such as Liang Ah-fa to aid them in their work, they express ambivalent opinions the Chinese people. Furthermore, the spirit of romantic heroism behind their publication network depended on a model of evangelical masculinity. The writings by Eliza Bridgman (Elijah Bridgman’s wife) and Henrietta Shuck (the first woman missionary to China) provide perspectives that challenge the systems of labor upon which Bridgman and William depended and highlight the ways in which printing technologies and history fold into each other at every turn. 在19世紀30年代初，從美國抵達廣東（廣州），中國第一位傳教士。以利亞布里奇曼和三畏了未來20年，一個驚人的數字出版的書籍，小冊子和60頁的月刊，中國信息庫（1832年至1851年）。靈感來自英國傳教士的例子，這些美國人記載了他們的時間，其中包括第一次鴉片戰爭（1839-42），隨之而來的革命能在中國，甚至美國的崛​​起，作為中國貿易夥伴的國際體面。他們成為有影響力的翻譯和外交官參與了至關重要的條約的談判。威廉姆斯成為了第一位教授在耶魯大學的中國研究在188？廣州貿易體系土崩瓦解與中國其他通商口岸的開放，布里奇曼和威廉姆斯關閉其廣，搬到了上海。然而，廣東印刷的方式塑造研究美國和中國這一天的努力已經推動了印刷技術的界限。 該項目生產的第一本學術專著的廣州印刷動盪的幾十年，從19世紀30年代到19世紀60年代的第一個美國傳教士在中國的活動。我的研究將考慮一系列的出版物，包括威廉的大量有影響力的人種學和歷史概述中國的古村（1848年，1883年），印刷兩個版本的顯著。然而，重點將是顯著的中國存儲庫，它提供了一個無與倫比的窗口，中國和美國在一個特別重大的時代，每個民族的歷史文化，經濟和政治關係的早期歷史。 真正意義上的全球範圍內，這些印刷企業的動機是基督教信仰的信念，進行了測試，革命暴力和戰爭的大屠殺，面對即將耗盡的地步。布里奇曼和威廉姆斯由於中國在過去幾十年想像的觀眾，他們似乎在屈尊俯就和殖民時代，而在其他時間不知所措和困惑。此外，他們的故事的中國叢報帶來了重要的困境有關如何穩定美國的問題，並就如何適當定義一個公共領域，致力於向西擴張在早期的美國，但在內戰的邊緣。 最後，浪漫背後的假設這些傳教士的出版物網絡依賴模型上的陽剛之氣，最終還是沒能辜負了刺耳的英雄主義的浪漫標準。的書面伊麗莎·布里奇曼（以利亞布里奇曼的妻子合作者）和Henrietta的是彈簧的第一個女人傳教士向中國提供的觀點，挑戰了系統的勞動賴以布里奇曼的和威廉的浪漫的印花依賴，和突出的方式中，印刷技術和歷史折疊成對方一動不動。

745712.label: Realisation of objectives
745712.value: All of the objectives were realised. In fact, this research opened up a very productive perspective on related events in law, diplomacy, and commercial cultures. The resulting publications (including a book monograph and articles) applied literary historical analysis to the output of the first American missionaries to China in the 1830s, 1840s, and 1850s. This opened up a perspective on commerce and diplomacy that happened in China with consequences for the United States. Because the missionaries were translators and interpreters who also published the monthly journal *The Chinese Repository,* they are deeply insightful in regard to any significance that the Opium Wars and Taiping Rebellion holds for understanding the political, economic, and cultural development of the US. The publications tracked the ways ideologies related to race and gender permeated their practice of printing and preaching in Canton, China, and South and Southeast Asia.

745712.label: Major findings and research outcome
745712.value: The publications and lectures result from research that draws from a richly descriptive cross-cultural archive. The publications present key moments in early relations among the twenty-first century’s superpowers through memoirs, biographies, epistolary journals, magazines, book reviews, fiction and poetry by Melville, Twain, Whitman, and others, travel narratives, and treaties, as well as maps and engraved illustrations. Paying close attention to figurative language, generic forms, and social dynamics of print cultural production and circulation, I have shown how authors, editors, and printers appealed to multiple overlapping audiences in China, the United States, and throughout the world. The major findings have inspired substantial 4-star publications, which include: 1. The scholarly monograph *The New Middle Kingdom: China in the Early American Romance of Free Trade* (Johns Hopkins University Press, in press, Spring 2017; 150,000 words, 400+ pages) puts US merchants, missionaries, and diplomats at the center of the first century of US cultural development from the Revolutionary War until the first decades after the US Civil War. It reconfigures cultural history to develop a global context for understanding the interrelated developments of American commerce, evangelism, foreign policy, law, and literature in regard to China. 2. “Henry James and the China Trade” (2014) is an article in the top-tier (Q1) journal Modern Fiction Studies (Johns Hopkins University Press). Henry James is not usually read as having much to do with China or transpacific commerce. However, his writing reflects a sustained awareness of the early nineteenth-century China trade’s effect on the visual and cultural landscape of New England where the first American millionaires deposited fortunes amassed in a world system of commerce. References to the China Trade resonate in James’s intensely visual literary style through which he verbally sketches social landscapes that convey an aura of national culture. These social landscapes eventually register his deep alienation in regard to the moral implication of American fortunes. 3-“Reading for Contexts of American Orientalism from the Far East to the Far West.” American Literary History (ALH, with Oxford University Press) 25.3 (Fall 2013): 638-649 is a journal article that encourages more substantial engagement with US missionaries to China as a way of developing the under appreciated impact of the China trade on early US cultural development. Furthermore, there are a couple more articles under review at top journals, including “The Holy Wars and Sacred Fonts of the Mission Press in South China: Printing Mongolian in the Chinese Repository" with American Quarterly.

745712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745712.value: There is great potential for further development. I am currently working on a follow-up project related to the impact of US extraterritoriality in China on post-Civil War America. This book will follow on the *The New Middle Kingdom* and trace the fascinating stories of US diplomats who were also literary writers and prominent politicians in the US before heading to China after the Second Opium War. My new MPhil student will be writing her thesis on one of these: Anson Burlingame. Furthermore, I have several parallel projects related to the global circuitry of newsprint related to the First Opium War; this December I will go to London as an invited participant of a roundtable related to opium being held by King's College London.

745712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
745712.value: When US missionaries arrived to China, their fellow citizens imagined the Middle Kingdom as the wealthiest empire in the world. Its geographical distance did not deter commercial aspirations—rather, it inspired them. Starting in the late eighteenth century, merchants from New York, Philadelphia, Boston, Salem, Newport, and elsewhere cast speculative lines to China. The resulting fortunes shaped the cultural foundation of the early republic and funded westward frontier expansion. The publications from this GRF argue that—for the merchant princes who speculated in the global Far East, as well as the missionaries and diplomats who followed them—Manifest Destiny spurred more than the coalescence of the fractious regions into the continental Far West. It also promised a golden gateway to the Pacific Ocean through which the nation would realize its historical destiny as the world’s new Middle Kingdom of commerce. Examining the influential accounts of westerners at the center of early US cultural development abroad, Johnson conceives a romance of free trade with China as a quest narrative of national accomplishment in a global marketplace. Spanning a full century, from the post-Revolutionary War era to the Gilded Age, The New Middle Kingdom highlights the importance of China in antebellum US culture.

745712.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
745712.value: There are additional ways that the GRF translates into scholarly impact that does not produce a discrete research publication but has enduring and substantial qualitative effects. First, this research has complemented my ongoing relationship with the Fulbright Scholar Program. As Head of the School of Modern Languages and Cultures (SMLC) and member of the American Studies Program, I help host a visiting professor each year and support a research conference in line with the visiting fellow's interests. My work through this GRF has enabled me to work with visiting professors such as John R. Haddad, Haiming Lui, Monica Chiu, Scott Laderman, George Wang, and Grace Wang. Second, this research on the history of US missionary printers in China has motivated me to participate in the broader media landscape of Hong Kong regarding US politics. In my appearances on RTHK Radio3 and PearlTV, I try to lend a historical perspective on US politics for Hong Kong audiences. My research into the early years of western media in China has enabled me to formulate a transnational perspective on the way that political views travel across the oceans and get reinterpreted to fit different social contexts. Over previous three years I have been on the radio about twenty times and on television twice.

745912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745912.value: Both executive functioning (EF) and emotion regulation (ER) are important domains within our self-regulatory system. Neuroimaging data indicates that the functioning of these two processes heavily involve the prefrontal cortex (PFC), which undergoes dramatic development in the early childhood period. Results from behavioral research also demonstrate a parallel rapid improvement of preschoolers’ EF and ER functioning. Most of the results from this line of research, however, come from cross-sectional studies or short-term longitudinal studies (two time-points) of age-related changes in preschoolers’ performance. To understand the individual patterns of growth of EF and ER among preschoolers, we need studies that can track the developments of individual children. Our proposed research adopts a longitudinal design with closely spaced multiple time-points, which enables us to examine the person-specific developmental EF and ER trajectories in Chinese preschoolers and the interaction of these two domains across early child development. Although a variety of early child EF and ER measures have been developed in the recent decades, to detect “longitudinal” changes in EF and ER, more reliable measures that are sensitive to individual changes are needed. We will develop and fine-tune a new battery of age-sensitive EF and ER tasks that can accurately measure the rapid changes in preschoolers’ EF and ER. Another important goal of the present study is to investigate the mutual influence of EF and ER and their co-variation across the 3 years of the preschool period. The longitudinal nature of the study will allow us to investigate the timing and the direction of influence between the two processes. Having four times of measurement will permit investigation of how the growth of one dimension of EF influences other dimensions, as well as how it is related to ER development. In addition, we will examine how child characteristics such as temperament and child gender, influence the way EF and ER develop. These findings will explore variations in EF and ER development among preschoolers with different background and constitution. Our results will both carefully describe the general normative pattern of growth of EF and ER in the preschool period, and also gain insight in the way EF and ER co-develop across early childhood. 執行功能和情緒調節是重要的自我管控功能。神經影像學的研究資料顯示這兩個功能的運作很大程度上涉及前額葉皮層，在幼兒期前額葉皮層會有迅速的發展。行為研究的結果顯示執行功能和情緒調節在幼兒期間會有同步及迅速的發展。然而，這些研究結果大部份來自橫斷性研究或使用了兩個時間點的短期縱貫性研究來探索幼兒的表現與年齡相關的變化。要了解幼兒的執行功能和情緒調節之間的發展模式，我們需要長時間跟踪個別兒童發展的研究。是次研究計劃採用縱貫性設計，加上緊密排列的多個時間點，讓我們能夠檢定幼兒的執行功能和情緒調節在整個學齡前期的發展和互動。雖然兒童早期執行功能和情緒調節的研究在最近的幾十年裡已有一定的發展，但要有效地檢測兒童的執行功能和情緒調節的“縱貫性”轉變和發展，採用更高敏感度及更可靠的量度方法是必須的。本研究將設計及採用一套吻合個別幼兒年齡的執行功能和情緒調節的測量方法。本研究的另一個重要目標是研究幼兒的執行功能和情緒調節在三年的學前幼兒期中的相互影響和變化。本研究的縱向設計讓我們可以了解兩個管控功能之間互相影響的時間點和互相影響的方向。使用四個時間點的長期縱貫性研究讓我們探索不同領域的執行功能如何互相影響，及這些執行功能如何影響情緒調節的發展。此外，我們將研究兒童的氣質和性別如何影響執行功能和情緒調節的發展。這些研究結果將揭示在具備不同背景兒童的執行功能和情緒調節的發展可以有的變化。我們的研究結果會將仔細描述執行功能和情緒調節在學齡前幼兒的正常增長模式，也讓我們了解執行功能和情緒調節在幼兒時期的相互發展方式。

746512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
746512.value: Over the past two decades, a distinctive youth dance drug culture has established a global presence. Hong Kong (HK) witnessed the decline of heroin use among young persons (under 21 years of age), and a significant rise in youth psychoactive drug use (ecstasy and ketamine especially) in a range of entertainment settings. Like elsewhere, HK witnessed the rise of psychotropic drug use in settings beyond clubs and discos, with young people extending use to other public and private locales. Internationally scholars have suggested that youth recreational drug use has increased and become more accessible, acceptable and integrated into youth culture. While there is accumulating research documenting the patterns of drug use among young people in the dance scene and beyond, less is known about the drug marketplace in which young people obtain their drugs. Internationally, research suggests that “social supply” - where users supply or facilitate drug supplies for friends and acquaintances for free, as gifts, in exchange – is of increasing importance to youth drug culture, and at the same time, adds a new dimension to the organization and structure of drug markets. Moreover, it also underscores the significance of the nature of drug markets especially at the lower levels – is embedded in social relationships. The proposed study bridges the two areas of our ongoing research - the organization of the local drug market and the trends of youth drug use and its associated culture. How do youth, as users, find their way into supplying others? How do they negotiate identity in the context of friends and supplying? How do we understand the nature of this “social transaction” and associated emergent culture around using and selling – the rituals, rules, practices, social relations (e.g. trust, sharing, reciprocity)? The overall objective of this study is to understand the social and cultural context in which drugs are obtained, distributed and consumed by young people in HK and to assess how the local context fits within the international scene. The study will involve the collection of four main data sets, including interviews with law-enforcement officials (n=5) and drug workers (n=5), in-depth interviews with users’ (n=50), in-depth interviews with drug dealers (n=10), and 5 focus groups with friendship groups (4 to 6 persons per focus group). The findings and analysis will provide an important case comparison with other locales, and contribute directly to current theorizing about the role of social relationships in drug markets. 摘要 過去二十年間，一股獨特的年輕人跳舞文化席捲全球，香港亦同時見證了（二十一歲以下）年輕人吸食海洛英的沒落。取而代之，年輕人於娛樂場所中濫用精神科藥物（尤以搖頭丸和K仔）的數字大幅上升，如同世界各地的經驗，本地年輕人濫用藥物亦不再只限於的士高和夜店等場所，而已擴展至各式各樣的公共及私人場地。各地學者均指出，年輕人的消遣性藥物濫用不單愈來愈普遍，而且在年輕人之間變得愈來愈容易接觸、愈來愈可接受，甚至已成年輕人文化的一部分。雖則學術界早已累積不少紀錄年輕人於不同場所濫藥的文獻，但有關年輕人如何得到/買賣毒品的情況，我們仍所知甚少。 世界各地的研究均指出，「社交供應/買賣」(social supply)這概念於年輕人間變得愈來愈普及－意即濫藥人士以免費、禮物或交換形式提供或協助提供毒品予相識和朋友。與此同時，此等「社交供應/買賣」亦對毒品交易市場的組織與結構帶來新衝擊。再者，「社交供應/買賣」這概念也點出毒品市場之底層實在不得不依靠社交網絡關係這事實。而是項研究就正旨在連結「本地毒品市場之結構」和「年輕人濫藥趨勢及其相關文化」這兩大研究題目，並望能回應以下疑問：濫藥年輕人是如何提供毒品予他人？朋友之間是如何建立買/賣家的身份？如何理解「社交買賣」(social transactions)及其相關文化，包括當中的慣例、規則、手法及人際關係（例如信任、分享及互惠關係）？ 本研究最大的目的就正是要理解本地年輕人於怎樣的社會及文化境況下獲得、分配及消費毒品，並嘗試將本地狀況放諸於國際環境中。本研究會依靠四個主要資料來源：訪問執法人員(n=5)及協助濫藥人士的工作者(n=5)、訪問濫藥人士(n=50)、訪問毒品拆家(n=10)和五個朋輩聚焦小組(約4至6人一組)。研究所得，望能有助比較本地和外地經驗，並進一步豐富現存有關毒品買賣中社交人際關係的理論。

746512.label: Realisation of objectives
746512.value: The four project objectives were successfully completed. All four data sets were collected, transcribed, edited, and have been used for analysis. We were successful in drawing from a range of referral sources for the different data sets. Data set 1 includes ten interviews with frontline workers to obtain a broad context for understanding consumption and supply of different drugs. Data set 2 includes in-depth interviews with consumers to understand their relationship to other users (gifting, sharing), to suppliers, and to the market (n=50). Data set 3 includes 10 in-depth interviews with dealers to examine market dynamics, risks and perceived identity. Data set four includes four focus groups with friendship networks to understand group dynamics of consumption. Originally we had intended to conduct five focus groups, but with many attempts at rescheduling due to “no shows”, we opted to interview members of this group individually, so that the total number of in-depth interviews with users and dealers to 64 (52 users and 11 dealers). Based on the data collected, we are among the few teams at present, to develop an in-depth understanding of the immediate marketplace for different types of drugs in Hong Kong, and the ways in which young people in Hong Kong obtain their drugs of choice. An understanding of these factors is important as the settings for use have greatly changed since the emergence of the dance drug scene. Although initially dance and similar entertainment venues represented one of the most important sites for drug consumption, this has changed, due to a range of factors, including policing, shifting and mobile entertainment sites. It is also due to consumers’ changing motivations and meanings derived from using particular drugs like ketamine, methamphetamine and cocaine. There has been a shift to using in a wider range of settings, both public and private in nature. It is in this context of a broader range of consumption settings that young consumers obtain their supply of drugs, and develop different rationales around sharing and dealing.
