746512.label: Major findings and research outcome
746512.value: Among the most significant themes for current and future publications: Normalization and social supply – there is a range of drug use among HK youth from recreational to chronic. Aspects of normalization – cultural tolerance, accessibility – are key among some groups, but less so with others. These aspects are connected to obtaining drug supplies – trust, sharing, and taking turns in purchasing. When purchasing, profit-making does occur but is not the norm; the idea of “proper” dealer is absent. Differentiated marketplace – there are distinct markets for different ethnic groups. Among local Chinese, access is across drug types. For Caucasians – the main access is to cannabis and cocaine; and for Nepalese – cough syrup and heroin. These main drugs “choices” are shaped by class, language, and cultural positioning. Social supply: social inclusion and exclusion – Local Chinese users develop multiple social networks to obtain drugs and establish a culture of trust and sharing, furthering their inclusive position within drug using groups as well as within the market. This is in contrast to ethnic minorities where given their marginal economic position, limited language and knowledge of the market rely on drugs available in the open and semi-open market like heroin, furthering their exclusion from drug using peers (reluctance to share), and the community. These themes feature in three international conference/seminar presentations. At the invitation of the pioneer in social supply, I presented our findings as a comparison to the UK (1/2014). I organized and presented the findings on a panel on social supply at the American Criminology Society (11/2014). As an invited plenary speaker for an international conference at Aarhus University, my presentation focused on agenda setting for ethnicity and drug research, underscoring the marketplace's centrality to differential access and its consequences for ethnic minorities (10/2015). This third presentation has resulted in an invited publication with Drugs: Education, Prevention and Policy. A comparison of normalization and social supply in cross cultural comparison features in a near completed article for the International Journal of Drug Policy. This piece will be an important contribution linking the two concepts. I have plans for other journal articles on drug market dynamics, gender and social supply, and the role of social supply in altering market conditions. The study findings will be a central component in my book documenting the shifts in HK’s drug market. Results were presented at two community events and a training course.

746512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746512.value: One of the most important findings is the discovery of the "doubly hidden nature" of drug use among ethnic minority youth. Given differences in social networks, social capital, and language, local Chinese and ethnic minority consumers have differential access and sources for drugs. The latter rely principally on purchasing drugs in public spaces, thereby increasing potential legal and health harms. This group of heroin users has had difficulties accessing health and social services. Therefore, I am finalizing a public policy proposal for January 2016 submission, entitled: Opening doors, creating pathways - A qualitative study of social harms and service access of young people from ethnic minority backgrounds in Hong Kong. This study seeks to understand how these youth experience health and social harms including alcohol and drug use, and how these young people access support services. It also examines what resources exist within these communities that young people can draw on for support or that prevent harms from occurring. A second development – At the request of the HK police, I have signed an MOU to work collaboratively on (1) conducting a survey with officers on their knowledge, experience and challenges in working with ethnic minorities, and b) developing training curriculum.

746512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746512.value: While heroin has a long history in Hong Kong, this changed in the late 1990s as a distinct youth dance drug scene emerged. This new leisure scene, witnessed around the globe, took hold in Hong Kong, resulting in drug market diversification. Heroin use declined; psychotropic drugs especially ketamine, increased. While studies have looked at the reasons for the popularity of psychotropic drugs, this is among the first in Hong Kong to examine the relationship between consumption and supply. Drawing on the concept of social supply, this research asks how young people obtain psychoactive drugs. It seeks to understand the socio-cultural context in which youth obtain, distribute and consume drugs. Based on qualitative interviews - 10 frontline workers, 52 young drug users, and 11 dealers - and four focus groups with friendship groups, the results suggests that consumers adopt a range of supply strategies. These strategies are dependent on knowledge and access to specific drugs and dealers, closeness and trust among peers, perceived legal and social risks, and perceived distinctions between consuming, sharing and dealing. These results have implications for treatment (understanding perceptions of use and associated practices) and for policy (considering the sometimes blurred distinctions between possession, dealing and trafficking).

746812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
746812.value: This research investigates Hong Kong people’s political values, chiefly the understanding and support of democracy, and examines how these values are related to their evaluation of the past, present and future economic condition in Hong Kong, and, regime performance, i.e., the performance of the Hong Kong government. The evaluation of regime performance in Hong Kong will consist of the dimensions of (1) quality of democracy, (2) rule of law, (3) lack of corruption, (4) political competition, (5) government accountability, (6) protection of freedom, (7) equality, and (8) government responsiveness. By dint of a household survey adopting the core questionnaire of the Asian Barometer Survey (ABS), which is a cross-national survey on political values undertaken in 18 Asian regions, the research taps the political attitudes of Hong Kong people on various political dimensions, including democracy, traditional values, alternative political forms, other value questions, and how they evaluate the political and economic performance of the current regime. By using confirmatory factor analysis, a method to test hypotheses and build theories by fitting the variables for a structural equation model, this research analyzes the relations of the evaluation of economic condition and regime performance, and political values in Hong Kong. The data collected will be compared with the findings of the previous waves of surveys done in 2001 and 2007. The research will generate three journal articles. The first article will analyze the overall model of political values, and evaluation of the economic condition and regime performance. The second one will compare the changing political values in Hong Kong over time by comparing results in the different waves. The third one will investigate the democratic support in Hong Kong as a semi-democracy in comparison with other Asian polities, which then allows us to test theories on democratization concerning the relations between political values and democratic consolidation. 本研究旨在探討香港人的政治價值觀念，主要針對其對民主的瞭解及支持程度，以及這些價值觀念如何影響他們評價香港的過去、現在和未來的經濟狀況及政府表現。有關政府表現的討論將涵蓋下列各個範疇：(1) 民主的質量，(2) 法治，(3) 貪污，(4) 政治競爭 ，(5) 政府問責 ，(6) 自由保障 ，(7) 平等及 (8) 政府的回應。 是次研究採用家居問卷調查的方式，以亞洲民主動態調查 – 一項於十八個亞洲地區進行有關政治價值觀的跨國調查 – 的核心問卷為藍本，搜集港人在不同範疇的政治態度的數據，其中包括民主、傳統價值、另類政治模式、其他價值問題，及他們如何評價現任政府的政治及經濟表現。然後利用驗證性因素分析、一種用來測試假設及透過結構方程式模型處理變項來建立理論的研究方法，分析港人對經濟狀況及政府表現的評價與其政治價值觀的關係，並將收集之數據與2001年及2007年進行的調查結果比較。 本研究將發表三篇期刊文章。第一篇分析港人政治價值觀的整體模式，以及對經濟狀況和政府表現的評價。第二篇利用比較不同波的調查結果，勾畫香港於不同時期政治價值的變遷。第三篇藉香港作為半民主政體與其他亞洲政體的比較，研究各地對民主的支持程度，從而檢測民主化的理論，進一步探討政治價值觀與民主深化的關係。

746812.label: Realisation of objectives
746812.value: 1. The research allows us to assess the change of political values in Hong Kong in various aspects, over the three waves of Asian Barometer surveys in 2001, 2007 and 2012 respectively, and assess the impacts of various political events on political values of Hong Kong. 2. Over the three waves, we find that actually assessement of economic performance is not a chief factor in explaining political values in Hong Kong. In contrast, education level, age, and immigrant status serves to explain political values (in particular support for democracy) much more strongly in this Wave III survey. . 3. Hong Kong has a reasonably high support for democracy, even if compared with other countries in the Asian region where democratic institutions are already in place. Comparatively, Hong Kong is only lower in terms of rate of political participation and level of political efficacy, although both have seen some progress in recent years. 4. There is a rise in political efficacy and political participation in recent years. The Wave III survey, however, saw remarkable trends of polarization, with some respondents becoming more conservative if compared with past waves. This may have to do with political conflicts in Hong Kong in recent years, and change of the demographics (e.g. a higher proportion of immigrants from China). Overall speaking, we can see that political values in Hong Kong is under constant change, because of the frequency of political movements and conflicts in Hong Kong. We hope that the next wave (Wave IV),, to be conducted in early 2016, would allow us to assess the effect of previous movements (e.g. the Umbrealla Movement) on the political values of the Hong Kong people.

746812.label: Major findings and research outcome
746812.value: 1. The Wave III survey, conducted in late 2012, showed a more polarization of political opinions and values in Hong Kong. While there are more people who are in support of democratic values, as reflected in the survey, the proportion of people who harbored more conseravative values also increased. 2. The most important variable that can explain the difference in political attitudes is 'immigrant status' or birthplace. Respondents who were born in mainland China are in general more conservative, and more inclined to support pro-government parties/candidates in their vote choices. 3. Compared to other Asian regions, Hong Kong have a reasonable level of support for democratic values. Despite the fact that Hong Kong cannot democratically elect its government, the political views of Hong Kong people are relatively liberal, in many aspects more liberal than their counterparts in other Asian regions who have their government elected. Hong Kong remains low in the rate of political participation and political efficacy, if compared with other Asian regions. 4. Education, age and birthplace remain reliable predictors of support for democracy in Hong Kong. In contrast, economic evaluation, a common facotr in other countries, is not much related to the democratic values of Hong Kong.

746812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746812.value: The research team has already obtained GRF funding in the 2015/16 exercise to carry out the Asian Barometer Wave IV survey, based on the Wave IV core questionnaire. The survey will be conducted in January to March 2016. This survey will allow us to compare the continuity and change in the political values of Hong Kong from 2001 to 2016. As the first AB survey after the Umbrella Movement, the Wave IV survey results will also allow us to assess the impact of the Umbrella Movement on the political values of Hong Kong. The data on political values will continue to be compared with the corresponding waves of other Asian regions. The research team is writing a book on the change of political attitudes in Hong Kong, as reflected from Asian Barometer surveys since 2001. This will serve as a comprehensive recap of value changes in Hong Kong since the handover.

746812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746812.value: This project forms part of the Asian Barometer Survey, a cross-national survey on political values that covers 18 Asian countries/regions. It uses a standardized questionnaire of 180+ questions, many of which on political values and democratic values, to tap the views of respondents in different countries. Because it uses the same methodology and questionnaire all over Asia, the data allow us to compare political values of Hong Kong with other Asian areas (and outside Asia as well). The Wave III survey on Hong Kong, conducted in late 2012, showed that Hong Kong has a reasonable level of support for democracy, compared to other Asian regions. It shows a trend of polarization of opinions, with more people becoming conservative yet more people becoming firm supporters of democracy. People who have higher education, younger, and who were born in Hong Kong in general has higher support for democracy.

747212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
747212.value: Many important economic problems can be represented as an Intergroup Prisoner’s Dilemma (hereafter IPD). For example, members of the parliaments of EU countries need to vote whether their country will contribute funds to help avert a debt crisis. In this case, each group’s decision is decided by the strategic decision of its members. When the incentives are such that not cooperating is the dominant strategy for each group, but joint cooperation Pareto dominates no cooperation for all groups, then the problem constitutes an IPD. Achieving cooperation is challenging in such environments. While the Prisoner’s Dilemma played by individual players has been studied extensively, the IPD has received considerably less attention, and in particular has not received much attention in the economics literature. Earlier research outside of economics has provided evidence that groups cooperate less than individuals in a prisoner’s dilemma. This literature, however, tends to focus on small groups of sizes 2 and 3. It does not formally analyze how an individual member in an IPD may make her decision based on her expectations of the decisions of her in-group and out-group members. It also ignores how bounded rationality—in particular, the possibility that individuals make errors in their decisions in complex environments—may affect individuals’ decisions, especially when the group size is large. Because of these omissions, while this literature takes into account the possibility that an individual may have concerns beyond her own material payoff (social preferences), it does not address how social preferences, bounded rationality, and strategic decisions jointly affect individual behavior and intergroup cooperation. This project develops an integrated approach to study the IPD that takes into account both social preferences and bounded rationality. Our analysis also explicitly recognizes that an individual in an IPD strategically responds to the decision of members of her group as well as members of the other group. We shall conduct three theory-informed experiments to study how differences in the incentive structure of the IPD and the group sizes of the IPD affect cooperation and individuals’ decisions. We shall also investigate whether gradually growing the size of groups will help facilitate cooperation in large group IPDs. Our integrated approach will provide new insights regarding important mechanisms that determine individual behavior and intergroup cooperation in an intergroup prisoner’s dilemma. They will inform theoretical and policy discussion regarding possible ways to facilitate intergroup cooperation in challenging environments. 不少重要的經濟問題可看成「群組間的囚徒困局」(Intergroup Prisoner’s Dilemma)。例如，歐盟成員國的國會議員投票決定其國家是否花錢來幫助歐盟避過債務危機。在這情況，每一群組(上例中的每一成員國)的決定是由其成員(上例中每一成員國的議員們)的策略性行為所決定。當相關的誘因使不合作成為每一群組的恆優策略,但對所有群組而言，合作「帕累托優於」(Pareto dominates)不合作時，有關的問題便成為一個群組間的囚徒困局。要在此等情況下達成合作是極困難的事。 大量研究集中於傳統的囚徒困局(即決策者皆為個人)。可是，群組間的囚徒困局並沒有受到同樣的重視。此一問題在經濟學文獻中亦未受重視。我們對文獻中關於此問題的研究有以下三點總結。第一點，經濟學以外的實證研究發現，在囚徒困局中，群體比個人更多選擇不合作。這些研究多考慮由二至三人組成的小群組。第二點，某一群組的一位特定成員的決定，應會受此成員對本身群組的其他成員及其他群組的成員行為的預期所影響。現有的文獻並未對此一問題作出嚴謹的分析。第三點，在複雜的決策環境中，特別當群組有大量成員時，每一個人在決策時皆可能犯錯。此一「有限理性」(bounded rationality) 的問題及其與群組間的囚徒困局之關係並未受重視。 在此研究計劃中，我們將建立一個整全的進路來分析「社會喜好」(Social preferences，即決策者可能會有物質利益以外的考慮) ，有限理性及策略性行為如何一起決定在群組間的囚徒困局中個人的行為及群組間的合作。我們將會進行三個以理論為根基的實驗。這些實驗會考察「誘因」及群組成員數目的改變如何影響群組間的合作及個人的行為。我們亦將探討逐步地增加群組成員的數目會否有助推動龐大群組間的合作。我們建立的整全進路，將有助瞭解在群組間的囚徒困局中，影響個體行為及群組間合作的重要機制。我們的研究成果，將有助深化關於如何促進群組間的合作之理論研究及政策討論。

747212.label: Realisation of objectives
747212.value: Building on recent work on social preferences, this research studies how social preferences affect cooperation in the inter-group prisoner’s dilemma (hereafter IPD). While conducting this research, we received very useful feedback in seminar and conference presentations. This feedback, together with the deeper understanding we gained about the IPD as our research progressed, taught us several lessons. We shall first highlight these important lessons, and then discuss how they have shaped our approach in achieving the three objectives in our proposal. First, our original focus was on how successful prior interaction can affect behavior in the IPD. It eventually became clear to us that it is important to also consider how failure in prior interaction can affect behaviour differently in the IPD. Second, regarding how increases in the size of the groups affect behavior in the IPD, our original focus was on the symmetric IPD. We were interested in comparing behavior in a symmetric IPD played by, e.g., two 3-person groups to behavior in a “larger” symmetric IPD played by, say, two 5-person groups. In such a comparison across a 3 vs. 3 IPD and a 5 vs. 5 IPD, any change in behavior between a 3-person group and a 5-person group can be due to either the increase in a group’s own size from 3 to 5, or the fact that the group is now playing against a larger, 5-person group instead of a 3-person group. When moving from a 3 vs. 3 IPD to a 5 vs. 5 IPD, the size of the community consisting of the interacting groups increases from 6 to 10. One can, however, consider an alternative comparison that involves comparing the behavior of a symmetric IPD played by two 3-person groups and an asymmetric IPD played by a 3-person group and a 7-person group. Such a comparison also involves an increase in the size of the community consisting of the interacting groups from 6 to 10. In such a comparison across a 3 vs. 3 IPD and a 3 vs. 7 IPD, any behavioral difference between a 3-person group in the 3 vs. 3 IPD and a 3-person group in the 3 vs. 7 IPD is purely due to the fact that the latter is now playing against a larger out-group. On the other hand, since a 3-person group in the 3 vs. 3 IPD and a 7-person group in the 3 vs. 7 IPD both face a 3-person group, any behavioral difference between such two groups across the 3 vs. 3 IPD and a 3 vs. 7 IPD is due to the fact that the 7-person group in the 3 vs. 7 IPD has a larger own group size. Enriching our study to include the asymmetric IPD also enables us to study theoretically and experimentally the unexplored question of how smaller and larger groups may behave differently in an asymmetric IPD. We now discuss how our research addresses the three objectives in our proposal. Given the approach we take, we find it easier to first discuss objectives 2 and 3, and then objective 1. Objective 2: To empirically study how increases in group size in an IPD affect individual behavior and the incidence of intergroup cooperation. Our first set of experiments found that successful prior interaction increases cooperation in the symmetric IPD. In addition, using the natural language classification game introduced in Houser and Xiao (2011), we conducted another experiment to examine subjects’ chats in the IPD experiment, and found novel evidence that successful prior interaction increases individuals’ concerns for the welfare of their out-group. We developed a theoretical model to study how bounded rationality, social preferences, and pivotal voting affect cooperation in any symmetric IPD played by two groups of equal but arbitrary size. The experimental results provide support for this theoretical approach. We then generalized our model to asymmetric IPDs played by two groups with unequal and arbitrary sizes to generate novel predictions. For example, the generalized model predicts that conditional on experiencing successful prior interaction, individuals in the small group will cooperate more than individuals in the large group. On the other hand, conditional on experiencing failed prior interaction, individuals in the small group will cooperate less than individuals in the large group. In our experimental analysis, we use an IPD played by a 3-person group and a 7-person group (the 3 vs. 7 treatment) to test the above predictions. Our design has the novel feature that subjects’ decisions in the prior interaction only determine whether such interaction succeeds or fails stochastically. This design enables us to handle statistically the problem that success or failure in prior interactions are endogenously determined by the players and can be correlated with their unobservable individual characteristics. Our data from this 3 vs. 7 treatment support the theoretical predictions. Objective 3: To empirically study whether gradually growing the size of groups will help facilitate cooperation in the more challenging environment when the IPD is played by large groups. We then analysed the implications of growing the size of the community that contains the interacting groups in the IPD. Specifically, we considered the case when the community changes from consisting of two 3-person groups (the 3 vs. 3 treatment) to consisting of a 3-person group and a 7-person group. Our theoretical analysis shows, counter-intuitively, that such an increase in the size of the community can actually increase the overall rate of cooperation, mainly because the 3-person groups in the 3 vs. 7 treatment will cooperate more than the 3-person groups in the 3 vs. 3 treatment. Our experimental analysis found that when prior interaction either succeeded or failed, the cooperation rate of individuals in the large community (the 3 vs. 7 treatment) and the cooperation rate of individuals in the small community (the 3 vs. 3 treatment) are not statistically significantly different, though numerically, the larger community actually has a higher cooperation rate both under prior success or failure. Our experiment also finds that conditional on prior interaction being successful, individuals in the 3-person groups in the 3 vs. 7 treatment cooperate more than individuals in the 3-person groups in the 3 vs. 3 treatment. Objective 1: To empirically study how different changes in the material incentives faced by members of groups in an IPD affect individual behavior and the incidence of successful intergroup cooperation. We used the theoretical model to conduct computational exercises, and generated a rich set of predictions regarding how changes in the different material payoff parameters affect behavior in both the symmetric IPD and asymmetric IPD. However, we did not conduct experimental analysis concerning how changes in the material payoff parameters may affect behavior in the symmetric IPD. The reason is that based on our better understanding of the problem, as well as feedback received in seminars and conferences, we have re-prioritized various research questions related to the IPD. In particular, in our experimental analysis, we have enriched our design to emphasize both prior success and failure, and we consider both the symmetric and asymmetric IPD. Generally, we have expanded the scope of our theoretical and experimental analysis to much richer settings to allow for the originally unconsidered importance of prior failure and asymmetric groups sizes.

747212.label: Major findings and research outcome
747212.value: We developed a theoretical model to study how bounded rationality, social preferences, and pivotal voting can affect cooperation in any symmetric one-shot inter-group prisoner’s dilemma (hereafter IPD) played by two groups of equal but arbitrary size. The model demonstrates a plausible mechanism through which success in prior interaction can increase cooperation in the IPD. Our experimental analysis considered several treatments in which subjects always played the IPD only once. In the baseline, subjects did not engage in any prior interaction. In the other treatments, they engaged in prior interaction and were always successful in such interaction. We found that successful prior interaction increases cooperation in the IPD. In addition, using the natural language classification game introduced in Houser and Xiao (2011), we conducted another experiment to examine subjects’ chats in the IPD experiment, and found novel evidence that success in prior interaction increases individuals’ concerns for the welfare of their out-group. These theoretical and experimental findings are reported in the working paper entitled “Prior Interaction, Identity, and Cooperation in the Inter-Group Prisoner’s Dilemma.” The support of the RGC has been acknowledged. This paper is currently under journal review, and has been cited in several papers, including in a recent publication in the journal Theory and Decision (Liu and Riyanto, 2017). We then generalized the model to any one-shot asymmetric IPD played by two groups of different but arbitrary sizes. This significantly generalized model generates novel predictions regarding how groups of different sizes in an asymmetric IPD may react to success or failure in prior interactions differently. In particular, the model predicts that conditional on experiencing successful prior interaction, individuals in the small group will cooperate more than individuals in the large group. On the other hand, conditional on experiencing failed prior interaction, individuals in the small group will cooperate less than individuals in the large group. In our experimental analysis, we use an IPD played between a 3-person group and a 7-person group to test these predictions. Our design also has the novel feature that subjects’ decisions in the prior interaction only determined whether such interaction succeeds or fails stochastically. Our data from this 3 vs. 7 treatment in which prior interaction succeeds or fails stochastically support the theoretical predictions. We experimentally analysed what happens when the relevant community grows from consisting of six people interacting as two 3-person groups (the 3 vs. 3 treatment) to consisting of ten people interacting as a 3-person group and a 7-person group. Our theoretical analysis shows, counter-intuitively, that such an increase in the size of the community can actually increase the rate of cooperation in the community, mainly because the 3-person group in the 3 vs. 7 treatment will cooperate more than the 3-person groups in the 3 vs. 3 treatment. Our experimental analysis found some support of this novel prediction. We also used the theoretical model to conduct computational exercises, and generate a rich set of predictions regarding how changes in the different material payoff parameters affect behavior in both the symmetric IPD and asymmetric IPD. These theoretical and experimental findings are reported in a working draft entitled “The Impact of Group Size and Prior Interaction Failure on Cooperation in the Inter-group Prisoner’s Dilemma.” The support of the RGC has been acknowledged. We have recently been invited to submit our work in this research to a special issue on “Social Preferences and Environmental Policies” in the Journal of Environmental Economics and Management for review and possible publication. We are currently revising this manuscript extensively to meet the 15/09/2017 deadline of submission.

747212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
747212.value: To our knowledge, this study is the first that theoretically and experimentally studies how the decision rules of a group—in this case, majority voting, together with bounded rationality and social preferences—affect cooperation in an inter-group social dilemma. Under majority rule, each member’s decision has the same weight on the group’s decision. In many settings, some members—either due to their formal role as leaders, or their stronger abilities to persuade fellow members—can have more impact on the decisions of the groups. A promising direction is to extend the analysis both theoretical and experimentally to consider the effects of different decision rules that groups may adopt. Our theoretical model generates novel predictions supported by the experiment. An important limitation of the model, however, is that it assumes that every decision-maker cares about both his/her material payoff and has social preferences. This assumption is a good place to start. The literature, however, suggests that the population consists of both people who only care about their material payoffs and people who behave as assumed in our model. Future analysis can consider a model that features both kinds of agents to generate novel hypotheses that can be tested in the laboratory.

747212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
747212.value: Inspired by recent work that shows that people often care about both their own material payoff and the welfare of others (that is, they have “social preferences”), this research studies unexplored questions regarding how social preferences can affect cooperation in the inter-group prisoner’s dilemma (hereafter IPD). Theoretically, we contribute to the literature by developing a rich model that can study how social preferences affect cooperation in any IPD played by two groups of any (equal or unequal) sizes. We derived predictions regarding how success or failure in prior interaction, differences in group sizes in an IPD, changes in the size of the community consisting of the groups interacting in the IPD, and changes in material payoffs, affect cooperation in the IPD. Experimentally, we provided novel evidence that successful and failed prior interaction have positive and negative effects on cooperation in the IPD, respectively. We also showed experimentally that consistent with the predictions of our model, the effects of prior interaction on cooperation in the IPD depend crucially on the sizes of the groups. For example, we find that conditional on prior interaction being successful, individuals in the small group cooperate more than individuals in the large group in an IPD.

747512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
747512.value: 競爭對企業永續政策的影響

747512.label: Co - Investigator(s)
747512.value: Dr Cruz, Jose Dr Nunez, Manuel

747512.label: Project Objectives
747512.value: We will analyze the two-stage models with the monopoly and duopoly settings under the two levels of competition and find the optimal strategy for the firm(s). In particular, we will provide a road map for firms facing a similar situation (e.g., in terms of firm size, market share, and/or cost structure), when they make operational strategic decisions among the three options: green resource development, recycling, and no action. By comparing the optimal strategies between the monopoly and duopoly settings, we will identify the system parameters where the firms switch from unsustainable to sustainable, or the opposite. The region of system parameters where the firms switch from doing nothing to green resource development or recycling implies that competition stimulates firms to embrace sustainability, while the region where the firms switch from sustainable to unsustainable implies the opposite. We will complete the full model for the extension of imbalanced market. We will consider a duopoly setting with one firm having high demand and/or low investment costs, and one having low demand and/or high investment costs, and investigate if the asymmetry in market size and costs will affect the role of competition on a firm’s sustainability practice. We will construct the dataset by using the (to-be purchased) KLD dataset. In particular, we will review various scoring systems in the management literature to identify the appropriate measures of degree of sustainability, and construct various competition measures to test our hypotheses. We will use the dataset to validate the assumptions in the theoretical model, e.g., whether sustainability stimulates a firm's demand or not. We will use empirical regression models to further discuss and validate the effect of competition on a firm’s sustainability level, e.g., we will examine whether competition intensity is positively correlated with a firm’s degree of sustainability.

747512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
747512.value: 永續性策略漸漸的成為企業節省成本（例如利用回收或研發新科技來減少稀土元素的使用）或是贏得綠色商品愛好者的重要因素。因此，在競爭資源及需求的前提下，建立一套長期戰略來達成永續性目標遂變成為決策者的優先任務之一。本計畫探討企業在競爭之下如何達到最佳的永續策略，以及競爭強度如何影響企業永續素養。 首先，我們建立一組動態模型來分析企業營運策略。其中，我們尤其考慮有關於綠色生產流程或資源以及再利用及回收稀有資源計畫等策略。我們考慮兩種層面的競爭：（１）企業間競爭其生產線所需之一關鍵及稀有的資源，此外此資源的單位成本隨總消耗量而成長，及（２）採用永續策略的企業間對市場需求的競爭。我們希望能藉由整合競爭條件以及此一動態模型來探討企業之最佳策略（維持原狀，開始回收計畫，或開發綠色資源），以及此兩種競爭型態對企業的永續素養的影響（例如，競爭是否導致企業採行更多永續策略）。 其次，雖然本動態模型可幫助企業更深入了解其策略走向，實際上的商業環境仍是遠遠的比模型來的複雜。為了更深入討論及證實競爭在永續素養上的影響，我們計畫建立一實證模型來驗證競爭強度以及企業的特質（例如，市占率及產業特性）對企業採用永續策略的影響。除了有關於產品及環境的永續策略外（如綠色生產／資源或回收計畫），我們也將考慮有關企業形象及雇員福利計畫類型的永續策略。利用這四大分類，我們將研究競爭對其有何不同的衝擊。 總言之，我們預計對運籌管理文獻達到兩個主要的貢獻：從提倡永續策略的角度來分析競爭的影響，以及提供一實證模型來研究競爭對企業永續素養的影響。首先，大部分的文獻在基於企業願意接受永續素養的大前提下來探討如何找到最佳執行永續政策的方法。大多數的論文對這大前提的支持論點多偏重在傳統的因素上，例如消費者，政府，或是非營利組織的壓力。但是因為永續策略有其額外的成本需求，在很多情況下，這些傳統因素並不足以促使企業採取永續策略。了解競爭在永續策略採用的影響，政府或是社會規劃代理人可以更有效率的來設計鼓勵或減低競爭強度的誘因以促使企業永續化。其次，本計畫介紹一實證模型以用於研究競爭的影響以及對於本計畫之動態模型提供實證。大多數永續策略運籌管理文獻以理論模型來討論永續性影響，但我們卻是利用實證的數據及模型來探討其影響，本實證方法應可在本領域中開啟一嶄新的研究角度，例如，競爭強度如何影響一企業的永續素養。

747512.label: Realisation of objectives
747512.value: Firms nowadays face strong competition from their competitors, from their powerful buyers, and even among their own corporate functions. In this project, we engaged significant efforts in understanding the effects of different aspects of competition on firms’ sustainable (or socially responsible) policy adoptions. Specifically, we first focus on the situation in which firms compete for limited, key resources, and complete Objectives 1 to 3. Next, we introduced the Kinder, Lydenberg, and Domini (KLD) database and construct various scores from literature to complete Objective 4. With this KLD dataset, we validated the model assumptions used in Objectives 1 to 3 (i.e., Objective 5). Finally, we emphasized on the outcome of Objective 6 by validating the insights derived from the model studying the effect of competition for limited resources, investigating the impact of competition among corporate key functions, and lastly studying how competition among supply partners affects firms’ adoption of sustainable initiatives. First, we detail how we completed Objectives 1 to 3. Consider that the cost of using the limited resource increases with its entire industry consumption in the previous period. Using a two-stage game theoretical model with single firm and multiple-firms settings, we analyzed firms’ optimal strategies when they make operational decisions among the three options: doing nothing, recycling programs to replace limited natural resources, and alternative technologies. Next, we compared the optimal strategies between the single-firm and multiple-firms settings, and identified the system conditions in which firms switch from environmentally irresponsible to responsible policies. We found that even if such a switch proves too expensive for individual firms, or resource costs are expected to remain low, competition for resources would still push firms to incur switching costs as they become more environmentally responsible. We note that, in addition to analyzing a duopoly setting with only two firms, we realized Objectives 1 and 2 by extending the setting to multiple-firms setting to ensure generality. We finished the game-theoretical model with the extension on imbalanced market, in which some of the assumptions, such as equal demands and costs, are relaxed. We showed that the relaxed assumptions still lead to similar insight that higher competition for limited resources motivates firms to be more environmentally responsible. We acknowledge that, although we also did analysis on how the asymmetries change firm decisions, reviewers asked us to simplify this part of analysis. For example, in the earlier version of the first output (see Part C), we specifically modelled the two choices, recycling or alternative resources, and studied the conditions when one wins over the other. We also discussed the case when there are multiple asymmetric Nash equilibria using a correlated equilibrium. However, because these structural results cannot be tested in the empirical model, thus creating disconnection between the game-theoretical and empirical models, we decided to drop the discussion in the paper output. With the game-theoretical model as a motivation, we next used the key KLD database to empirically test the insights as well as the model assumptions from the model, and further study the role of various competition aspects to firms’ corporate social responsibility (CSR). The KLD database records firms’ various CSR strengths and concerns. However, because of the changed ownerships in 2011 as well as changing business environments, the indicators that KLD collected changed overtime. Therefore, to complete Objective 4, we manually regrouped the indicators and reviewed the management literature on the usage of KLD to construct appropriate proxies to fit various needs. As a result, the completed, cleaned dataset is used in all three paper outputs in Part C. Moreover, with the dataset, we are able to test the assumptions used in the theoretical model, thus achieving Objective 5. In particular, using fixed-effects analyses, we found empirical evidence to support the assumption that firms with higher CSR have higher demands as well as profit margin and sales growth. These results, documented in an earlier version of the third output, support that CSR can either motivates higher demand or allows firms to charge a higher premium. However, when we present this work in other institutions and conferences, the audience was more interested in the supply chain formation question (i.e., a supplier with a high CSP is more likely to be selected and how to induce buyers to deviate from this selection rule) instead of the valuation question (a supplier with a higher CSP can achieve higher demand and/or premium). As a result, the paper in its current form focuses on the formation question. Finally, we spent significant efforts on Objective 6, empirically investigating the effect of competition on a firm’s CSR, as it delivers important messages to firm managers and governments during their decision processes. First, using the KLD database (only the environmental area), we found that competition for resources increases a firm's adoption of environmentally responsible strategies. In addition, tests that use the Chinese government's 2010 rare-earth supply suspension as an exogenous shock suggest a causal interpretation for our finding. In sum, competition intensity on the input market indeed encourages firms to be more responsible; see the first output for details. However, although competition for limited resource motivates firms to be more environmentally responsible, adopting responsible initiatives is not costless. In addition to the monetary investment costs onto these initiatives, they could distract firms’ managerial attentions, in particularly on innovation. Fixed-effects panel analyses on approximately 1,000 U.S. public manufacturing companies for the 2001-2012 period reveals that increasing ESG (socially responsible actions on environment, society, and governance) leads to significantly lower innovation output. An instrumental variable approach and a difference-in-differences approach both confirm that increasing ESG indeed leads to decreased innovation output. Internal competition needs to be carefully managed to avoid significant loss on firms’ competitiveness; see the second output for details. Lastly, we studied the competition from supplies’ major buyers. Consumer pressure for sustainable products becomes a key driving force to firms to become sustainable. That said, a product requires not only the selling firms’ but also their suppliers’ collective efforts in order to be sustainable. Using firm-level CSR measures from the KLD dataset and buyer-supplier pairs from the Compustat Segment dataset, we introduced CSR similarity between buyers and suppliers as a selection criterion for supply-chain formation and examine why socially responsible (irresponsible) buyers often source from responsible (irresponsible) suppliers. Although CSR similarity can partially explain supply-chain formation, it fails to fully explain the deviations. Concerns over sourcing costs moderates the effect of responsible buyers sourcing from responsible (and usually expensive) suppliers, leading to the deviation in which responsible buyers source from irresponsible suppliers. Moreover, supplier information transparency offered by a firm’s CSR status moderates irresponsible buyers’ sourcing from irresponsible suppliers. Finally, if one party improves its CSR, then the other party will do the same, even after we endogenized the selection process. Thus, supply-chain competition also encourage firms to become more responsible as shown in our third output. In sum, the six objectives were achieved. Based on feedbacks from either reviewers or audience in institutional or conference presentations, we extended the objectives to further study the impact of competition on firms’ CSR adoption and repositioned the papers so that they can be better perceived during the review process.

747512.label: Major findings and research outcome
747512.value: In our first output, we incorporated competition for limited resources to explicitly model a firm’s valuation and, hence, its decision whether to adopt environmentally sustainable strategies (e.g., recycling programs, alternative technologies). Even if switching to environmentally responsible alternatives proves too expensive for individual firms, or resource costs are expected to remain low, we showed that competition for resources would still push firms to incur switching costs as they become more environmentally sustainable. Moreover, we found empirical support that competition for resources encourages firm's adoption of environmental strategies. This paper was majorly revised for the Journal of Operations Management. However, because the disconnection between the game-theoretical model (requested to be more complicated by the reviewers) and the empirical model, it was rejected in the second round review. It is now under review in another quality journal. In our second output, we differentiated between two types of CSR: ESG, which addresses remote stakeholders’ interests, and employee-related CSR, which addresses internal stakeholders’ interests. We found that that while increasing employee-related CSR exhibits a positive impact on firm innovation, increasing ESG leads to significantly lower innovation output. Supplementary analyses rule out alternative explanations such as resource allocation or shifting to quality innovation. We concluded that although employee-related CSR enhances firm innovation, ESG may distract attention and create cognitive complexity for managers and employees. Our study suggests that firms should carefully design and implement their CSR strategies. Although this paper is rejected by Management Science (the only submission so far), it has high potentials as the Associate Editor encouraged us to resubmit. We are now revising this paper and will submit it soon. In our third output, we found that although buyers tend to seek suppliers in similar CSR status for easy communication and aligned goals, they can deviate from this path if the supplier costs are high or the value of information transparency from CSR signals are high. Moreover, in the battle between suppliers and buyers, buyers often can induce their suppliers to be more responsible, should they want it. Such a relation sheds us understand a key aspect of CSR promotion: CSR pressure placed upon downstream firms could be propagated along the chains, thus forcing firms on these chains to be more responsible. This paper has been presented in many OM conferences, and will be ready for submission soon.

747512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
747512.value: As motivated in 6.1, firms nowadays face various type of competition, and CSR can be helpful in improving their performance, if it is designed carefully. One direction for me to further develop is to study other types of competition on firms’ adoption of CSR as well as the consequence due to their adoption. Moreover, the KLD dataset is comprehensive and rich and we will further use it in studying how CSR can help to enhance firm performance. In particular, I teamed up with a coauthor to study which types of CSR will help firms to execute more merger and acquisition deals. We are writing up this paper now, and should have the draft ready by the end of the year.

747512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
747512.value: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) becomes a buzzword for many firms under competition. In this project, we considered various forms of competition and studied their effects on firms’ CSR initiatives. Using a game-theoretical model, we first found that firms subjected to competition for limited resources are more likely to be forced to switch to environmentally responsible options. Moreover, we provided empirical evidence to support such a causal relationship. Second, while resources competition is a powerful driver to induce a firm’s environmental CSR efforts, it creates managerial attention competition to the focal firm’s other functions. We found that firms engaged in CSR related environment, society, and governance are more likely to do worse in their innovation performance. Firms, while being responsible, still need to pay attention to its other key functions to survive. Finally, we extended competition to the supply chain level, and investigated how a supplier’s CSR initiatives can be influenced by its major buyers. We empirically found that consumer pressure indeed can be propagated along the chain to make the focal supplier more socially responsible. Our study on the three aspects of competition help firms to strategically deploy their resources and managerial attentions as well as to maintain their supply chain relationships.

747612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
747612.value: Meditation has a long history in human civilization. It is a mental exercise still prevalent around the world. Meditation training may exert an influence over the structure and functioning of our brain—a phenomenon known as neuroplasticity. Popular audiences in the East and West have largely accepted the idea that meditation improves mental wellbeing and brain functioning. There is, however, little scientific exploration of the changes in brain mechanisms incurred by long-term meditation practice. The few existing studies on the neural consequences of meditation mainly focused on the effect of one type of meditation only. There are, however, many schools of meditation (e.g. Buddhism has schools of Theravāda, Mahayana, and so on) and within each school exists different forms of meditation (e.g. focused attention meditation, open presence meditation, and compassion meditation). Despite this, it is still unknown whether different forms of meditation exert general or specific effects on brain architecture and functions. To address this issue, the proposed work aims to characterize the neural correlates of two forms of meditation prevalent in Hong Kong: focused-attention meditation (FAM) and loving-kindness meditation (LKM). To probe for the long-term consequences of brain functions in relation to different forms of meditation, we will recruit long-term meditators who are experts in either FAM or LKM, and two groups of matched controls who are interested in meditation but without prior experience. While inside a 3T Magnetic Resonance Imaging scanner, they will: (1) perform a well-established computerized task measuring attention, and (2) engage in emotion processing, based on an experimental protocol that we have previously validated. Based on our preliminary findings, it is predicted that the pattern of brain activation will be dissociable between FAM and LKM meditators, independently of tasks (attention or emotion). This proposal represents the first systematic study that directly compares between two different forms of meditation at the neuronal level. Understanding whether different forms of meditation exert differential effects on the brain has both theoretical and practical significance. First, it will advance knowledge in how the human brain adapts, functionally, to different forms of mental exercises and experience. Second, people may be in a better position to choose among different forms of meditation in order to best address their needs (e.g. improving attention or promoting emotional wellbeing). Ultimately, the proposed work on meditation will contribute toward rehabilitation and intervention programs for those suffering from mental illnesses, such as depression and anxiety disorder. 冥想是一種廣為流傳并且历史悠久的心靈修煉方法。它能影響我們大腦的結構和功能，也就是從某種程度上重塑我們的大腦（也即神經可塑性）。冥想能促進心理健康和提昇大腦功能，這一觀點已普遍為大眾所接受。然而，大腦在長期冥想後發生的變化，當中到底包含著什麼科學道理，卻鮮為人知。現有的少量研究往往只偏重於其中一種冥想方法；那麼，不同的冥想方法對大腦的結構與功能是否會有以及會有怎樣的特異性影響呢？ 為回答這一問題，本研究探索了與香港目前較為流行的兩種冥想方法：專注冥想及慈心冥想相關的大腦變化。我們招募了分別修習這兩種冥想方法的人士作為主要研究對象，另外將對冥想感興趣但卻無相關經驗的人士作為配對組。所有參與者在磁力共振成像儀內完成一項已經被普遍使用的注意任務，和一項在我們之前研究中證明了其有效性的情緒加工任務。根據我們預實驗的結果，無論在注意任務還是在情緒任務中，修習兩種不同的冥想方法的人士的大腦的活動都有所不同。 本研究首次系統地將兩種冥想方法在神經的水平上進行了比較。瞭解不同方式的冥想是否會對大腦造成不同影響在理論和實踐上都具有重大意義。首先，我們會瞭解人類的大腦是如何在功能上適應不同方式的心靈修煉。第二，人們可以憑藉研究結果，依據自己的需要（例如提升專注力或促進情緒健康）選擇適合的冥想修煉方式。而最終，這些研究結果有望應用於相關心理疾病，例如抑鬱症或焦慮障礙的治療干預和康復當中。

747612.label: Realisation of objectives
747612.value: The two objectives were fully realized. Objective 1: To investigate the trait effects of long-term meditation on attention and emotion processing at both behavioral and neuronal levels. The morphology and the functioning of our brain depend on experience. It has been widely suggested that meditation is one of the forms of experience that can bring about improved mental-wellbeing. Existing studies, though few, suggest that meditation is an effective mental exercise that can improve mental-wellbeing and bring about corresponding changes on the brain. We investigated the trait-effects of long-term meditation on emotion-processing at the neuronal level by studying the structural and functional changes of the brain associated with Loving-Kindness Meditation (LKM). Ten Chinese male expert meditators of LKM, and 15 Chinese male meditation novices (who had no prior meditative experience) were invited to undergo structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan (Study 2) and functional MRI (fMRI) scan during the viewing of affective stimuli in an Emotional Processing Task (EPT) (Study 3). The two groups were matched in age and years of education. Based on the MRI/fMRI results, we further investigated the trait-effects of mindfulness on attentional bias regarding threat, which is also known as negativity bias. Negativity bias is an inherent ability in human beings that allows us to pay more attention to threats at an early stage of processing, so that we can evade danger more efficiently. We recruited 22 Chinese male expert meditators to undergo an event-related potential (ERP) study to examine the early stage of affective processing (using EPT) associated with negativity bias (Study 4). Objective 2: To compare the above effects between two different forms of meditation (i.e. focused-attention meditation and loving-kindness meditation). Most of the existing neuroimaging studies on meditation examined the effects of one form of meditation only. Therefore, what remains unanswered is that whether different forms of meditation would lead to the same general effects, or the effects would be specific to the experience induced by a particular form of meditation. Objective 2 of our project aims at bridging this gap in research by examining whether two different forms of meditation can induce domain-specific changes at both behavioral and neuronal levels. To this end, we focused specifically on comparing the Focused Attention Meditation (FAM) with LKM. These two forms of meditation have very different training foci. FAM stresses on sustaining attention, on the contrary, LKM emphasizes on cultivating a state of universal love and compassion. We recruited 22 Chinese male expert meditators (11 for FAM and 11 for LKM) and 22 matched meditation novices to participate in our experiment (Study 1). Both expert meditators and meditation novices were asked to perform two experimental tasks while undergoing the fMRI scan, both during meditative and non-meditative states. The two experimental tasks are the EPT employed in Study 3 and the Continuous Performance Test (CPT), which is for measuring sustained attention. The behavioral performance and patterns of neural activity of the expert meditators and meditation novices when performing the CPT and EPT, during both the meditative and non-meditative states, were compared.

747612.label: Major findings and research outcome
747612.value: Objective 1: Study 2 (Leung, Chan, Yin, Lee, So & Lee, 2013), Study 3 (Leung, Chan, Yin, Lee, So & Lee, 2015) and Study 4 (Ho, Sun, Ting, Chan & Lee et al., 2015) Study 2: As LKM heavily emphasizes on the regulation of emotion, it was hypothesized that LKM expert meditators, relative to novices, would have more gray matter volume in brain regions involved in affective processing. Our results were in line with the hypothesis, showing that expert meditators indeed had relatively more gray matter volume in the right angular and posterior parahippocampal gyri than novices (Leung, Lee et al., 2013). As these brain regions are known to be very important for affective regulation and empathetic responses, our findings suggested that long-term LKM practice could possibly induce structural changes in the brain associated with affective regulation. Study 3: As LKM heavily emphasizes on the regulation of emotion, it was hypothesized that LKM expert meditators, relative to novices, would have different patterns of brain functional connectivity in regions involved in affective processing during the EPT. Consistent with our hypothesis, it was found that expert meditators exhibited stronger functional connectivity between the amygdala and anterior cingulate, premotor, and primary somatosensory cortices during positive emotion processing than novices (Leung, Lee et al., 2015). As these brain regions are important components for empathetic responses, emotion recognition and regulation, our findings suggested that long-term LKM practice could possibly induce functional changes in the brain associated with processing of emotion (in particular positive emotion processing). Study 4: As mindfulness facilitates detachment from habitual reactivity, it was hypothesized that trait-mindfulness would hint at the level of negativity as perceived by affectively negative stimuli, which would be reflected by behavioral and ERP data. For ERP data, an increased P2 amplitude (an early ERP index) at the frontocentral location of the brain for the affectively positive, as compared to the affectively negative stimuli, represents a diminished negativity bias. In line with our hypothesis, it was reported that expert meditators, who had high mindfulness scores, perceived less negativity from affectively negative stimuli. They also exhibited increased P2 amplitudes at the frontocentral location of the brain for affectively positive compared to affectively negative stimuli, which reflected diminished negativity bias. These findings suggested the role of mindfulness in reducing negativity bias, possibly via reducing effort to suppress attention on affectively negative stimuli associated with negativity bias. Objective 2: Study 1 (Lee, Leung, Hou, Tang, Yin, So, Lee & Chan et al., 2012) Study 1: It was hypothesized that FAM and LKM groups would show distinct patterns of neural activity when performing the CPT and EPT. This is because of the different training foci of FAM and LKM. Consistent with our hypothesis, our results revealed meditation-specific effects on the neural activity and behavioral performance. More specifically, our findings suggested that long-term practice of FAM enhanced attentional performance, whereas long-term LKM practice could benefit regulation of emotion.

747612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
747612.value: Our findings provide initial evidence on the behavioral changes and neuroplastic changes regarding the brain, which are associated with long-term practice of meditation and trait-mindfulness. Furthermore, different forms of meditation practiced are associated with specific behavioral performance and distinct neural activation patterns for sustained attention and the processing of emotion. Future studies could extend this line of research by further investigating the causal effect of meditation training: Whether these behavioral and neuroplastic effects of long-term meditation could be induced by short-term training in meditation through conducting studies with a longitudinal design. In particular, it would be important to test whether short-term training in FAM and short-term training in LKM would induce behavioral and neural changes specific to attention and the processing of emotion respectively. Furthermore, because the practice of meditation may facilitate sustained attention and reduce negativity bias, future studies could also examine whether and if so, how different forms of meditation training could help improve different kinds of cognitive and affective dysfunctions observed in people with psychiatric disorders respectively. This includes patients with depression, anxiety or bipolar disorders, or people with neurodegenerative diseases, such as mild cognitive impairment, dementia or Alzheimer’s disease. Previous studies have showed that these disorders are associated with structural and functional abnormalities in various brain regions such as the prefrontal, cingulate and limbic cortices, which are important for cognitive and affective processing. Therefore, the potential of the application of meditation training to alter the abovementioned abnormalities or even to prevent their onsets amongst at-risk individuals warrant further investigation.

747612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
747612.value: The structure and the functioning of our brain depend on experience, and our wellbeing depends on the integrity of our brain. The current research has contributed to a better understanding on how experience – long-term meditation, a form of mental exercise – affects our behavior and the structure and functioning of the human brain. Meditation practice, which has a focus on attention in its training, is linked to changes to brain regions that are important for attentional performance. Similarly, meditation practice that has a focus on regulation of emotion in its training is connected to changes to brain regions that are important for processing of emotions and empathic responses. Our findings suggested that different types of meditation practices are associated with specific neural effects, which is related to the corresponding foci of trainings in meditation. Findings from the current research is important for the design of rehabilitation and intervention programs for people who suffer from different clinical conditions, and thus have respective different needs (e.g. the needs to improve attention in patients with dementia or promote emotional wellbeing in patients with depression).

747812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
747812.value: This is a socio-legal and applied linguistic project that uses sociolinguistic and discourse methods to study legal bilingualism in Hong Kong, now practiced for more than two decades. At the macrosocial level, I shall compare cross-jurisdiction discourse on bilingualism and contrast ideologies. I hope to reveal the distance between conceptualization and practice in bilingual legal policies, and situate Hong Kong within a typology of bilingual and multilingual jurisdictions. The findings will pinpoint the milestones that are yet to be reached if Hong Kong were to become fully legally bilingual, and provide the necessary conceptual framework and socio-political context for any investigation into legal bilingualism in Hong Kong. At the microsocial level, I shall study verbal behaviour in the courtroom, using especially self-representation as a diagnostic of legal bilingualism in Hong Kong. Self-representation is a likely site where institutional and laymen conceptions of law and justice clash, and language provides a channel for understanding that tension. Despite their growing presence in lower courts, the voice of self-representing litigants is seriously underrepresented in the academic literature. By collecting courtroom language data involving self-representing litigants and interviewing them regarding their courtroom experience, I shall evaluate how language use and competence as extralegal factors may influence the delivery of justice and assess the adequacy of existing institutional support for self-representing litigants, especially whether reference materials provided in English or the newly engineered ‘common law Chinese’ are comprehensible to lay people. The outcomes may lead to recommendations for policy implementation that improves access to justice. I will also use the data to uncover the motivations behind, and the effects of code-switching under, the institutional constraints of the Hong Kong courtroom setting. I will argue that features of the bilingual setting, such as the use of code-switching, may be a communicative strategy exploited by legal professionals and linguistically competent litigants. Legal bilingualism offers a platform from which to examine the institutionalization of linguistic ideologies, to analyse professional discourse as a source of power, and to explore routes to linguistic empowerment. My research project will advance both socio-legal and applied linguistic scholarship by contributing to lift linguistic barriers to justice, develop a bilingual legal system in Hong Kong, and portray the sociolinguistic landscape of Hong Kong. 這是一個橫跨社會學、法律學和應用語言學的研究計劃。我會用社會語言學角度和話語分析的方法， 研究在香港實行了超過二十年的雙語法律制度。在宏觀社會層面上，我會比較不同司法制度的雙語或多語運用和其牽涉的意識形態， 及探討雙語法律政策在構想和實踐之間的距離。本計劃將會指出香港雙語法制尚待完善之處， 並透過剖析概念架構和社會政治背景， 強化香港雙語法制的討論基礎。而在微觀社會層面上，我會探究法庭上的語言運用，特別是無律師訴代表訟人的話語。無律師代表訴訟人大多不諳法律，大眾對法律的解讀很可能與法律專業的判斷有異，構成衝突。我希望從他們的話語去理解衝突的成因， 繼而發掘消弭矛盾的可能性。雖然越來越多無律師代表訴訟人參與低等法院的審訊，現今的學術文獻仍缺乏能代表他們的聲音。通過收集他們在法庭的語言數據，和訪問其上庭經驗，我將評估無律師代表訴訟人的語言能力如何影響案件的審判和裁決。我亦會衡量他們得到的支援是否足夠，例如政府提供的中英雙語法律參考文本是否清晰易懂。研究結果可以為香港法律政策的實施提供意見，避免語言成為公義的絆腳石。除外，所得的數據亦會有助理解在法庭上使用語碼轉換(「中英夾用」)的動機及影響。我認為語碼轉換可以是法律專業人士和語言能力高的人，在法庭上採用的一種溝通策略。雙語法律制度提供的平台， 可用以審視關於語言的意識形態如何制度化， 專業話語如何和權力掛鉤， 及如何通過語言去改善權力不均。本計劃將不但推進社會法律學及語言學，更有助解除大眾面對法律時的語言障礙及協助香港雙語法律制度的發展。

747812.label: Realisation of objectives
747812.value: During the project period, courtroom observations have been conducted in lower courts in Hong Kong (Objective 3 and 4), such as district courts and tribunals, and unrepresented litigants were approached and interviewed (Objective 6). Based on the observation data, the courtroom behavior of the litigants and their interactions with legal professionals have been analysed. The interview data revealed their motivations for self-representation and their perception of the trial experience. These findings are reported in [Journal Publication #3]. The biggest problem I encountered was that although courtroom observations were allowed in the open courts of Hong Kong, the judiciary did not grant me access to the audio recordings of the trials I attended. Such access was a matter of discretion by the trial judges and no reason was given for their refusal. This means that I had to rely on notes I took during the observation for my analysis, and was unable to perform micro linguistic analysis of the trial interactions as typically required by discourse studies. Despite the challenge, I was able to present a big picture of courtroom behavior of unrepresented litigants in Hong Kong in my publication and offer an explanation of such behavior based on my interview data. I have also situated my findings on self-representation in Hong Kong in the wider context of legal bilingualism (Objective 2). To characterize legal bilingualism in Hong Kong (Objective 5) and the power relationships involved in the relevant discourse (Objective 1), I compared the bilingual legal practice in Hong Kong with other bilingual and multilingual jurisdictions both in terms of the way bilingual and multilingual statutes are interpreted in legal cases [Journal Publication #1] and the way bilingual and multilingual language policy has been promulgated [Journal Publication #2]. This comparative investigation has formed the basis of a monograph (under contract with Oxford University Press) that I am currently writing [Publication #4], where I explore legal bilingualism and multilingualism as a global phenomenon.

747812.label: Major findings and research outcome
747812.value: Journal Publication #1: The paper shows that the equal authenticity principle, commonly adopted by balanced bilingual or multilingual jurisdictions, changes in meaning, value and function as it travels across jurisdictions with different sociopolitical realities. I illustrate how the framing of the concept has subtly shifted in the process of statutory drafting and interpretation when it was appropriated by the Hong Kong judiciary, in contrast with the way the idea was first conceived and applied in Canada and later in international treaties, especially in situations where discrepancies between two language texts are alleged. Journal Publication #2: This article situates legal multilingualism within a wider understanding of multilingualism and language policy. It first surveys status labels assigned to languages in multilingual jurisdictions. It then compares, across jurisdictions, rhetorical strategies deployed in promoting and opposing specific proposals about language status, in both official and public discourses, and analyses contradictions and dilemmas embedded in them. The argument extends Goodrich’s (1984) observation that legal discourse is pre-eminently a discourse of power. But if use of legal language is political, it is suggested, then the processes of negotiation which establish a language for such use are even more so. Journal Publication #3: Drawing both on observation data collected in Hong Kong courtrooms and on interviews with litigants, this article explores how LiPs in Hong Kong engage, and struggle, with the justice system, and how changing patterns of interaction in these courtrooms reflect a postcolonial legality. It illustrates strategies LiPs adopt in presenting their case, which are not displayed by represented litigants or professional advocates, and explains their behaviour in linguistic and sociocultural terms. It is argued that the communication gap between laypersons and legal professionals is ideological and structural, and cannot be bridged simply by adopting present approaches to either assisting or educating the former. Publication #4: The monograph aims to answer these questions: a) To what extent is legal bilingualism and multilingualism a global phenomenon? b) How, and how far, does choice of legal language(s) affect the way in which justice is delivered? c) What challenges face jurisdictions which attempt to conduct their law in two or more languages?

747812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
747812.value: The project not only bore fruit but has seeded my upcoming project on language rights and inspired further work by myself and others. My PhD student Matthew Yeung is currently doing follow-up work to my project; he has already studied the resources the Hong Kong government has made available to unrepresented litigants and he has done an ethnographic case study of one litigant by following him from case preparation, through to the trial and his post-trial thoughts about his litigation experience. My other PhD student Jade Du is looking into bilingual trials in mainland China. As for myself, through the project I have become interested in the issue of the extent to which language may be regarded as a right and have submitted a new GRF proposal (for 2015-2016) as I plan to carry out further research on this topic.

747812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
747812.value: The project investigated what happens when people go to court without a lawyer in Hong Kong, a phenomenon that has become increasingly common since the handover. Through observing trials and interviewing such unrepresented litigants in Hong Kong, I report their courtroom behavior, document their trial experience, and offer an analysis of their interactions with legal professionals and of their perception of justice. Given the prevalence of unrepresented litigation in Hong Kong, my study contributes to understanding litigation behaviour and litigant satisfaction from a bottom up perspective. I also analysed the wider context of legal bilingualism in Hong Kong, including the power relationships involved in the relevant discourse. It is clear that the impact a bilingual policy has on the Hong Kong judiciary is also shared by some other jurisdictions. Through cross-jurisdiction comparisons I have shown how some of these jurisdictions handle the impact differently, from legal interpretation to promulgation of language policy. This not only shows that my project may be of interest to jurisdictions beyond Hong Kong, but also reveals the motivation and vision behind bilingual and multilingual policies in different jurisdictions. My upcoming research will also follow this comparative angle.

748012.label: Project Objectives
748012.value: Our first objective is to identify sources of idiosyncratic volatility and to link specific trading strategies to changes in IV. Do passive strategies, such as market-making activity, always reduce volatility? Do aggressive strategies that take liquidity always increase volatility? Are the determinants of IV different in up vs. down markets? Our second objective is to examine whether high levels of IV, or IV that is attributable to certain traders or strategies, prolong “crisis” periods of low or declining stock prices.

748012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748012.value: Volatility in financial markets appears to be closely connected to periods of crisis in these markets, as demonstrated by the crises of 2007 and 2008. It is less clear to what extent this elevated volatility affects real economic activity and whether it can spread through different markets and thereby transmit systemic risk. Moreover, we know surprisingly little about how volatility actually arises, i.e., what exactly makes security prices fluctuate. In this proposed project, we examine how idiosyncratic volatility – the portion of total volatility that is firm-specific, rather than common to all stocks – arises. Idiosyncratic volatility is important because it complicates trading, arbitrage, and the essential price discovery function of markets. It is clear from the literature on market microstructure that trading activity affects security prices, but we have surprisingly little evidence on how exactly volatility comes about, which traders cause it, and what kind of trading strategies increase or decrease idiosyncratic volatility. To address this question, we will employ a unique data set that allows us to track all trading activity of each trader and each stock over time, so we can identify how each trader and each trading strategy is related to firm-specific volatility. We will contribute to the literature by • Identifying sources of idiosyncratic volatility; • Linking specific traders and specific trading strategies to changes in idiosyncratic volatility in the cross-section of stocks and over time; and • Examining whether high levels of idiosyncratic volatility can prolong “crisis” periods of low or declining stock prices. 如我們所知，金融市場的波動性是和宏觀經濟的波動息息相關的。 2007和2008的金融危機就是一個很好的例子。然後，我們所不了解的是，金融市場的大幅波動到底對實體經濟有多大程度的影響，是否會波及到其他的市場從而引發系統性風險。此外，更令人驚訝的一點是，我們根本不清楚波動性究竟是什麼引起的。 本項目主要目的是研究股票價格波動中的非系統性風險是如何引起的。非系統性風險之所以重要，是因為它複雜化股票交易，套利，市場重要的價格發現功能。證券市場微觀結構的研究表明交易活動影響證券價格。但令人驚訝的，很少有研究表明波動性究竟是如何來的，什麼樣的交易員和交易策略對它有直接的影響。 我們將採用獨特的數據庫來解決這個問題。這個數據庫的獨特之處在於它能夠跟踪每個交易者和每隻股票的所有交易活動，這樣我們就可以識別每個交易者和每一個交易策略是如何導致價格波動的。 本項目的主要貢獻是： • 發現和展示非系統性風險特質波動的來源; • 發現和展示交易員和交易策略與非系統性風險特質波動的關係； • 展示是否大幅的非系統性風險會延長危機時期。

748212.label: Project Objectives
748212.value: Resolve the outstanding question of whether the effect of optic flow on the control of locomotion toward a goal is indirect through recalibrating the perceptual straight ahead and thus affecting the perceived target egocentric direction. Develop an understanding of what role non-visual information (such as vestibular, proprioceptive, and motor information from the movement of the limbs) plays in the control of walking toward a goal. Separate the use of the heading and the target egocentric direction strategies and provide a quantitative description and analysis of how these two strategies contribute to the control of locomotion toward a goal, and how their contributions are affected by different sources of optic flow information that affect heading perception. Establish a direct link between the improvement of heading perception and the increased reliance on the heading strategy in the control of locomotion, which can shed light on the perception-action coupling in the control of self-motion.
