748212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748212.value: Although goal-directed locomotion tasks are commonly experienced in our daily life and much research in the last two decades has investigated what visual strategies people use to accomplish such tasks, no consensus has been reached. Specifically, there is an on-going debate on the use of two strategies in the control of locomotion toward a goal, i.e., whether people align their instantaneous direction of travel (i.e., heading) specified by optic flow with the target (Gibson, 1950), or use the target egocentric direction and steer to center the target in their straight ahead (Rushton et al., 1998). Although the findings from previous studies support the use of both strategies in the control of walking toward a goal, it still remains in question (1) whether the effect of optic flow on locomotion control is indirect through recalibrating the straight ahead and thus affecting the perceived target egocentric direction, (2) what role non-visual information (such as vestibular, proprioceptive, and motor information from the movement of the limbs) plays in the control of walking toward a goal, and (3) how the reliance on the heading and the target egocentric direction strategies changes with the availability of different sources of optic flow information. In the current project, by examining (1) whether discrepant optic flow causes an immediate as well as an enduring shift of the perceived straight ahead in the visual control of steering toward a goal, (2) the time course of such shifts, and (3) how different sources of optic flow information affect such shifts, we determine the extent to which optic flow can recalibrate the straight ahead and affect the perceived target egocentric direction in the control of locomotion toward a goal. Then, by conducting parallel walking studies, we examine how non-visual information is used in the control of walking toward a goal. Last, we take a control theoretic approach to separate the use of the heading and the target egocentric direction strategies to quantitatively evaluate their respective contributions to the control of steering and walking toward a goal, and then systematically examine how their contributions are affected by different sources of optic flow information. The findings from the current project will help to resolve the existing debate in the field on whether and how people use heading and target egocentric direction for the control of locomotion and will be applicable to the design of effective navigational interfaces, biomimetic robots, and unmanned vehicles. 尽管在日常生活中目标导向的自主运动十分常见，在过去的二十年中也已有大量的研究探讨此类任务，但人们在控制此类自主运动时所采用的策略究竟是基于何种视觉信息目前还无定论。具体来讲，现有的争论主要集中于两种依赖于不同视觉信息的控制策略的使用，即人们究竟是依赖于光流信息，使其所指示的自身瞬时运动方向始终对准目标（运动方向策略，Gibson, 1950），还是依赖于目标相对于自身的方向这一视觉线索，在行进中使其始终位于自身的正前方（目标参照方向策略，Rushton et al., 1998） 来确保自身朝向既定目标行进。虽然迄今为止这两种策略各有实验支持，然而以下三个方面的问题还未澄清（1）光流信息对目标导向的自主运动控制的影响是否是通过影响目标参照方向这一视觉信息而间接实现的（即光流信息能否重新校准人们对自身正前方的知觉从而影响到人们知觉到的目标参照方向），（2）非视觉信息（例如来自于前庭系统，本体感觉系统的信息以及伴随着肢体运动所产生的运动神经信息）在控制朝向目标行走中有什么作用？以及（3）人们对于不同控制策略的依赖性如何随着不同类型光流信息的可获得程度而改变。本项目利用虚拟现实技术模拟由操纵杆控制的虚拟朝向目标行进任务，首先探讨（1）偏离的光流信息（光流信息所指示的运动方向偏离于被试身体正前方）是否导致被试知觉到的自身正前方产生即时和长效的偏移，（2）此种偏移的时间进程，以及（3）不同类型的光流信息如何影响这种偏移。 我们旨在确定在朝向目标行进时光流信息在何种程度上重新校正人们知觉到的自身正前方，从而影响其知觉到的目标参照方向这一视觉信息。随后，虚拟朝向目标行进任务将由实际朝向目标行走任务所代替，我们旨在探讨伴随着实际行进所产生非视觉信息在控制朝向目标行走中的作用。最后，本项目将引入控制理论方法以分离运动方向以及目标参照方向这两种不同控制策略的使用，从而定量地测评它们在引导人们朝向目标行进（虚拟行走和实际行走）中所起的作用，最后系统检验这些控制策略的作用如何受不同类型光流信息的影响。本项目的研究结果在理论上有助于解决现有的有关人们是否以及如何使用运动方向和目标参照方向策略控制朝向目标行进的争论，在实际中 也具有重要的应用价值， 有助于推进高效的导航型人机界面，仿生机器人及无人驾驶车辆的研发。

748212.label: Realisation of objectives
748212.value: Regarding Objective 1, we have achieved it 100% by conducting a series of experiments to examine whether the effect of optic flow on the control of locomotion toward a goal is indirect through recalibrating the perceptual straight ahead (SA) and thus affecting the perceived target egocentric direction. We found that discrepant optic flow caused an immediate and an enduring shift of the perceived SA during locomotion (Siu, MPhil thesis, 2013). Furthermore, we have conducted walking experiment using a virtual reality (VR) setup to examine how adding optic flow information in the scene affected such shifts and whether such shifts increased with prolonged exposure to discrepant optic flow. We found that discrepant optic flow during walking recalibrates perceived SA in egocentric space, and this recalibration increases with the exposure to discrepant optic flow when the display contains rich optic flow information (J. Chen et al., 2014). Last, we found that participants have more difficulty in dealing with high attention demanding task at high than low travel speed. Attentional load affects the early stage of steering control but does not affect the final heading error (R. Chen & Li, 2014). Regarding Objective 2, we have achieved 100% by conducting a series of steering and walking experiments using a VR setup to examine the relative effectiveness of various types of optic flow information and the contribution of non-visual information to locomotion control. We found that visual heading defined by optic flow was used to guide walking toward a goal. The relative effectiveness of optic flow and non-visual information depends on the specificity of the information (Li et al., 2014). We then studied what training method could improve visuomotor control of self-motion and found that action gaming (for as little as 5 hr) and enhancement in visuomotor control, which suggests that action video games can be beneficial training tools for driving (R. Chen, Wong, & Li, 2015; R. Chen, Chen, & Li, 2015; Li, Chen, & Chen, 2016). We also found that current manual tracking can enhance smooth pursuit eye move, which is a fundamental property of eye-hand coordination (Niehosters, Siu, & Li, 2015). Regarding Objective 3, we have achieved it 100% by conducting a series of experiment to examine how enriching the optic flow field affects the control of heading specified by optic flow and the control of target egocentric direction during goal-oriented locomotion. We used a control-theoretic approach to separate the control response specific to these two cues in the visual control of steering toward a goal. The findings provide direct support for the claim that people use the heading specific by optic flow as well as target egocentric direction to steer toward a goal and suggest that the visual system does not internally weigh these two cues for goal-oriented locomotion control (Li & Niehorster, 2014; Niehorster, PhD thesis, 2013). Furthermore, the neural network that processes optic flow has a primary role in the identification of scene-relative object movement (Rushton et al., under review). Regarding Objective 4, we have achieved it 100% by conducting a series of experiments to examine whether an improvement in heading perception leads to an increased reliance on the heading strategy in the control of locomotion. We found that participants had an increased reliance on heading specified by optic flow for steering control with increasing travel speed even in the presence of the target egocentric direction cue. The increased reliance on heading was tightly linked to an increased reliability in perceiving heading from optic flow as the magnitude of flow increases with travel speed (Li, Chen,& Niehorster, 2013; R. Chen, MPhil thesis, 2016; R. Chen, Niehorster, & Li, under review). Furthermore, we studied how people perceive heading from optic flow in the presence of a moving object, and disentangled the effects of object position and motion on heading judgments in the presence of a moving object (Long, Niehorster, & Li, 2015; Long, MPhil thesis, 2016). We found the surprising utility of target drift in natural heading judgments (Li et al., 2015), and during self-movement, people are better at judging whether an object is moving than whether they will hit it (Rushton et al., 2015).

748212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748212.value: Enlightened by the findings from the completed research project, we plan to study the neural mechanism underlying goal-oriented locomotion control in humans. This is due to the fact that while many neurophysiological studies have examined the neural systems engaged in the perception of heading and target egocentric direction cues during self-motion, no study has examined the neural bases for the visual control of goal-oriented locomotion l in humans. We plan to addresses this question using both task-activation and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Specifically, we plan to identify the brain networks subserving the heading and the egocentric direction strategies using individual differences in the reliance on these two strategies for steering control. To uncover the common (i.e., task-independent) neural bases for the visual control of goal-oriented locomotion, we plan to examine whether the brain networks identified using the steering control task also subserve the control of walking toward a goal. Last, we plan to examine how extensive training to use a specific control strategy modulates the activities and connections of the identified brain networks using both the steering and walking tasks.

748212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748212.value: Goal-directed locomotion tasks are commonly experienced in our daily life and much research in the last two decades has investigated what visual strategies people use to accomplish such tasks. Specifically, there is an on-going debate on the use of two strategies in the control of locomotion toward a goal, i.e., whether people align their instantaneous direction of travel (i.e., heading) specified by optic flow with the target (Gibson, 1950), or use target egocentric direction and steer to center the target at their straight ahead (Rushton et al., 1998). Although the findings from previous studies support the use of both strategies in the control of walking toward a goal, it still remains in question (1) whether the effect of optic flow on locomotion control is indirect through affecting the perceived target egocentric direction, (2) what role non-visual information plays in the control of walking, and (3) how the reliance on the two control strategies changes with the availability of different sources of visual information. This completed research project addressed these important questions in the field. The findings help to resolve the existing debate in the field and are applicable to the design of effective navigational interfaces, biomimetic robots, and unmanned vehicles.

748612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748612.value: Trading activities in the option market can predict future stock returns, as has been shown by previous studies. This is consistent with the view that some informed traders take advantage of the high leverage in the option markets to capitalize on their private information. However, little attention has been paid to the information sources of these predictabilities. This project aims to bridge the gap by investigating the information content of trading activities by the option traders. Specifically, we study extent to which the predictive power of option trading lies in the earnings-related or analyst-related corporate news. The corporate events we focus on are the earnings announcements, the management guidelines, the earnings restatements, the analyst recommendation changes, and the analyst forecast changes. We contribute to the literature by answering the following three questions. First, do option trading activities have predictive power on the magnitude of the upcoming earnings-related and analyst-related news? Second, do option trading activities have predictive power on the future stock returns? More importantly, what proportion of the stock return predictability is from the earnings-related and analyst-related corporate events? Third, are the informed option investors following the momentum trading strategy after the announcement of a certain type of corporate event? In other words, do they believe that the market has not yet fully incorporated the information? Our project, therefore, differs from the existing literature, which merely documents the predictive power of option trading on stock prices, by further pinpointing the information sources of the predictability. We also provide a new perspective regarding the informational leading role of the option market relative to the stock market. 過去的文獻已被指出期權市場的交易活動，是可以預測未來的股票收益率。這樣的觀點，和文獻中關於資訊交易者利用高槓桿的期權市場，來套現他們的私人信息，是一致的。然而，文獻很少探討這些預測能力的訊息來源為何。本文的目的，在探討期權市場中的資訊交易者所擁有的訊息內容。具體來說，我們研究期權交易的預測能力是否來自於與盈餘發佈或分析師相關的新訊息。我們專注於企業的盈餘公告，管理準則，盈利重報，分析師推薦的變化，與分析師預測的變化。我們通過回答以下三個問題對文獻做出貢獻。首先，期權交易活動是否能預測與企業盈利發佈和分析師報告的內容？次者，期權交易活動對未來的股票收益的預測能力為何？更重要的是，有多少比例的股票收益的可預測性是從企業的盈利和分析師相關的事件而來？三，資訊交易者在企業新聞發佈後，會採取動能交易策略還是反向交易策略？換句話說，他們相信市場尚未完全反映訊息了嗎？因此，本文對既有文獻的貢獻來自於進一步探討期權市場對股票市場預測性的訊息來源。我們也對兩市場訊息的相對主導地位提供了新的視角。

748612.label: Realisation of objectives
748612.value: In this paper, we combine these two strands of the literature. If analysts indeed tip investors about upcoming analyst news, for the reasons discussed above, options markets might be the ideal place to exploit such information. We therefore study the patterns in options prices prior to analyst news events. First, we establish that options prices predict the stock market’s response to analyst news.4 Second, and most importantly, we distinguish between three potential explanations for this finding: tipping (from analysts to options traders), reverse tipping (from options traders to analysts), or common information (of analysts and options traders). As discussed below in detail, our results are most consistent with the tipping hypothesis. Our findings are related to those in two independent studies by Hayunga and Lung (2013) and Lung and Xu (2014). Hayunga and Lung (2013) show that options trading reflects information about analysts’ recommendation consensus changes. Lung and Xu (2014) show abnormal option trading activities before analyst initiations, and the authors relate this pattern to analyst tipping. We differ from these two papers in several key aspects: First, we conduct a more comprehensive analysis of the channel through which the lead-lag correlation between informed options trading measures and analyst-related news can be manifested. We exclude a third possible channel, i.e., the common-information channel, which is neglected by Hayunga and Lung (2013). Second, we have a more complete sample of analyst-related events as a result of including the analyst forecast revision in the analysis. Third, we decompose the predictability of options trading on stock returns regarding days with specified analyst-related events and other days. Last but not least, we have a better execution of the estimated standard errors in the pooled OLS regressions. We double-cluster the estimated standard errors along both firm and time dimensions. Our paper also makes contributions to the literature by settling the debate on whether the options market leads the stock market in the price-discovery process. Many papers have linked the informed options trading and lead-lag relation between the option and stock markets to corporate events, such as earnings announcements (Xing et al., 2010; Roll et al., 2010; Jin et al., 2012; Johnson and So, 2012), mergers and acquisitions (Cao et al., 2005; Chan et al., 2013), and bankruptcy (Ge et al., 2013). However, there are other studies arguing that options do not contribute to the equity price discovery process. Chan et al. (2002) show that stock net trading volume can predict future options quotes revisions, but not vice versa. Their results suggest that informed investors only initiate their trades in the stock market. Muravyev et al. (2013) find that options quotes do not contain any non-public information about future underlying stock prices, and it is the stock price that leads the options quotes in the price discovery process.

748612.label: Major findings and research outcome
748612.value: We study the role of analysts and options traders in the information transmission between options and stock markets. We first show that the predictive power of option implied volatilities (IVs) on stock returns more than doubles around analyst-related events, indicating that a significant proportion of the options predictability on stock returns comes from informed options traders’ information about upcoming analyst-related news. We examine three explanations for this finding: tipping, reverse tipping and common information. We find that analyst tipping to options traders is the most consistent explanation of these predictive patterns.

748612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748612.value: The project can be extended to use data on signed option volume to study which components of option volume predict stock returns.

748612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748612.value: Our paper provides evidence that options trading can predict excess stock returns because informed investors choose the options market to trade on their private information about upcoming analyst-related news, namely the analyst recommendation change, analyst forecast revision, and analyst initiation. Our results are most consistent with the analyst-tipping hypothesis that some options investors receive tips from analysts about their future reports. The results are more pronounced when the options market is more liquid.

748712.value: 隨著跨部門、跨組織的合作上升，協同模式普遍被認為是一個減少公共服務分散化和不協調性的服務方式。然而，不少學者對於協同服務的績效和成果保持了遲疑的看法。我們希望透過網絡研究的方法更進一步了解社會福利機構組織之間的連繫如何影響其服務績效。其中，我們假設服務對象能透過組織之間的連繫、協調及互動，取得更全面的服務信息及資源。所以，我們以組織為分析單位，並建立了一個網絡分析的研究模型，希望以實証方法測試不同的社會網絡理論，如中心性“centrality”、結構洞“structural holes”、封閉性“closure”及物以類聚“homophily process”，如何影響公共組織的協同服務績效。 我們選擇香港及台北作我們的研究地點，因為港、台兩地都曾進行一系列社會服務民營化的措施，並各自擁有獨特的中華文化背景。在這兩個城市，我們希望收集有關組織互動、背景、特點、以及服務績效的數據。我們會利用一個社會網絡分析軟件去分析組織的網絡結構和特性，並了解與其服務績效之間的關係。透過我們的研究，我們希望釐清有關組織協同服務的網絡範圍。我們亦希望建立一個解釋組織網絡如何對服務使用者產生正面影響的模型，並通過測試這個模型，更進一步深化學術界對協同服務的了解。此外，把網絡理論應用於亞洲，能進一步擴大現存理論的應用範圍。同時測試網絡結構四個互助競爭的理論亦能幫助政策制定者及機構決策者了解如何建立有效的組織網絡，並增強組織的網絡能力。

748712.label: Realisation of objectives
748712.value: Objective 1: To examine the structure of interactions among public service providers implementing collaborative services. From Nov. 2012 to Apr. 2016, our research team has completed the investigation of the structure of interactions among public service providers implementing collaborative services. Following methods in Provan and Milward’s (1991, 1995), Galaskiewicz’s (1979) and Liu and Chan’s (2015) studies, we selected approximately 96 social service providers in our research sites to conduct in-depth, face-to-face interviews with directors or top managers of CBOs in four urban poor communities in both Taiwan and Hong Kong. Interview questions include organizational functions and basic information, advocacy and public policy participation activities, as well as their external relationships with governments, funders and other nonprofits. More specifically, our study examines factors that might influence the roles of these public service providers in Taiwan and Hong Kong in terms of their external relationships. From 2012-2014 (Hong Kong) and 2014-2016 (Taipei), we focused on collecting data in Hong Kong and Taiwan. First, we selected housing estate communities that are located in a relatively remote area, meaning it makes the most sense for the local residents to access services from their local organizations. A large percentage of the residents have lower monthly incomes below the poverty line in Hong Kong and Taipei. To obtain a list of the relevant organizations, we asked local residents to identify organizations that had provided essential social services to them in the past 12 months. From that data, we obtained a list of organizations that provide essential social services both within and outside the public housing estate. Our team then conducted site visits to those organizations to confirm their presence. At the same time, we also conducted a block-by-block search to identify additional organizations providing essential social services in the community. Essential social services are defined as services which address problems pertaining to the family, childcare, youth, unemployment, the elderly, or health, as well as consulting services. Building on this information, we then followed Provan and Milward’s (1991, 1995) network data collection procedures. Using our master list of organizations providing services to the target population in two public housing estates, we conducted an initial mail/phone survey to the social service agencies, followed by a second round of in-person interviews with the managers of the agencies, and a third follow-up phone call for missing data and data accuracy. We also maintained a collection of documentation on funding and policy initiatives. Through multiple steps, we were able to reach beyond the agencies already well-integrated into known networks. To achieve a decent response rate, our team went through multiple channels to reach our respondents. For instance, in Hong Kong, on average, it took four contact attempts (or 70 days from our first contact) before we could schedule an interview. We were able to interview 28 out of the 31 social service agencies in one district and 28 out of 32 in another between 2012 and summer 2013, and that gave us response rates of 90.32% and 87% respectively. Objective 2: To test an empirical model that explains how network centrality, structural holes, closure, and homophily processes influence the performance of public service providers Our second objective was on examining the characteristics of network on the performance of public service providers. To examine the exchange structure of this network, we adopted a network analysis technique called blockmodeling (Galaskiewicz and Krohn 1984; Wasserman and Faust 1994) and other basic statistical tools. This method helps to examine the extent to which exchange relations involve particular subgroups or “positions” based on structural equivalence. Structural equivalence groups actors together into similar positions based on having similar relationships with other actors in the overall network (Breiger, Boorman, and Arable 1975; White, Boorman, and Breiger 1976; Wasserman and Faust 1994). Other network features have also been investigated, such as network centrality, structural holes, closure, and homophily processes. Papers Writing Three papers have been written from the data collected from Hong Kong sites (See research outputs for details). In particular, to examine the network characteristics within a social service network, we adopted a network analysis technique called blockmodeling, which cluster actors who share similar relationship patterns (Wasserman and Faust, 1994). This method helps us examine the extent to which exchange relationships involve particular subgroups or “groups” based on structural equivalence and has been applied in other community studies (e.g., Knoke and Rogers 1979). Structural equivalence clusters actors into similar groups based on similar relationships with other actors in the overall network (Breiger, Boorman, and Arabie 1975; Wasserman and Faust 1994; White, Boorman, and Breiger 1976). For example, if a secular youth center and a faith-based family center in the community both mentioned partnering with the same government welfare agency and the same local representative’s office, then the welfare agency and the local representative’s office were considered to have a degree of structural equivalence in the network. This does not indicate that they had a relationship with each other; rather, it indicates that these two organizations shared a similar group because they performed a particular role in this community. CONCOR was used to partition the two transposed matrices based on the receiving ties, namely, the working and client referral relationships (Breiger, Boorman, and Arabie 1975). A four-blockmodel with two rounds of partitions was chosen because of the following considerations. Because we aimed to examine cohesiveness among social service providers sharing the same background, we selected a four-blockmodel that can reflect both in-group relationships and out-group relationships among the welfare and political actors. Preliminary results show that public service providers serve the roles of social service provision and allocation, representation, and deliberation, yet with variations between Taiwan and Hong Kong. For instance, public service providers in Hong Kong reported that they play very minimum role in advocacy and policy participation while those in Taiwan reported a relatively higher degree of advocacy and policy participation. Furthermore, this study discusses the extent to which public service providers have been involved in the policy making process or advocacy activities also varies depending on the resources, community influences of the public service providers and their external relationships with the government. Outcomes Research outcomes include publication, working papers, and a public research website to disseminate research results: Lee and Liu (Factors Influencing Network Formation, 2013); Liu and Chan (The Challenges of Implementing Collaborative Governance, 2015); Liu (Politics in the Social Service Network, under review); Liu (Mapping the Help-seeking Networks, working paper); Liu (Mapping Social Service Networks, working paper); Liu and Liu (Restructuring Community Care for Elderly Services, working paper). Below I briefly outline the findings supported by the GRF research.

748712.label: Major findings and research outcome
748712.value: Outcomes Research outcomes include publication, working papers, and a public research website to disseminate research results (Please see Part C). Barriers for Collaboration Liu and Chan (2015) find that the development of an effective social service delivery system remains a challenge to policymakers and implementers. This study reveals that organizations with government funding have to follow guidelines, have strict eligibility requirements for clients, and are less flexible. These organizations are less willing to extend their partnership to more local, political, and younger organizations. They fit into Kettl’s (2006) model and face more challenges to manage across boundaries. Politics within Networks Lee and Liu (2013) examine the factors influencing network formation among social service nonprofit organizations (NPOs) in Hong Kong and aim to illustrate the value of comparative studies of network formation. The findings show that program needs and joint-action experience have a consistent positive impact on network partnerships. However, organizational size and the degree of resource dependency affect network size only for NPOs established after 1990 while NPOs that were established after 1990 are more likely to form network partnerships if they are large-sized and not receiving government subvention. Effective network is essential for clients Liu (working paper) show that two different types of social service providers developed under a parallel social service system in Hong Kong, namely a top-down welfare bureaucracy which has been required to maintain its non-partisan status, and one bottom-up system made up of politically affiliated organizations which operate their services in order to gain political support from the local residents. We reveal the interaction patterns among these different types of social service providers and provide implications for policy makers who are interested in building integrative services or networks within a local community. Recognize the importance of collaboration, but without allocating staff time for dealing with networking activities From the Taipei study (Liu 2016), about 76% of the respondents have already adopted inter-organizational cooperation as part of their organizations’ mission. Also, about 68% of the respondents also find that collaboration can help organizations to reach their service goals more effectively, when compared with serving alone. However, organizations are only willing to devote staff’s time and utilize staff’s personal connections to engage with other agencies. For instance, 64% of the respondents reported “rely on staff’s personal networks to build up collaboration capacity with other organizations” and only less than half reported “allocate staff’s time to work on cross-agency cooperation.”

748712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748712.value: Previous studies have focused on finding the optimal formula to make public service collaborations effective. In the past decades, systems have been transformed and redesigned to become more collaborative and effective, with experiments including one-stop service locations in the United States, integrative centers in Hong Kong, and the “no wrong door” policy in the United Kingdom. Through understanding the collaborative networks, our publications and working papers can advance the development of an effective social service delivery system. Lee and Liu (2013) suggest that the government and umbrella organizations (such as HKCSS) can play a more significant role in facilitating partnership among nonprofits of different needs and capacities. Liu and Chan (2015) provides a list of challenges for implementing collaboration, including leadership, funding competitions, and political interference. Liu (working paper) demonstrates the interaction dynamics between the two systems, namely the welfare actors and the political actors, and how the interactions between the two groups affect the services accessibility by local low-income families. These findings can help policy makers to design effective policies for collaborative initiatives, including increasing funding, establishing network coordination agency at the community level, reduce tension between competition and increase collaboration through policy incentives.

748812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748812.value: The main objective of this project is to investigate how the sensitivities of the chief executive officer’s (CEO) and the chief financial officer’s (CFO) equity-based compensation to stock prices affect a firm’s timeliness in remedying internal control material weaknesses (ICMWs) after they are publicly disclosed, and how the CEO and the CFO differ in their role in remedying different types of ICMWs. We will conduct this study by using the data of mandatory disclosures of ICMWs in the US as a result of Section 302 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (2002). Internal control is “a process, affected by an entity’s board of directors, management and other personnel, designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the achievement of objectives” (Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission framework). It is an important part of the operational systems of a firm. Existing research on the determinants of effective internal control mainly focuses on the characteristics of the audit committee and the board of directors (Goh 2009; Krishnan 2005; Zhang, et al. 2007). Limited attention has been paid to the management’s function in internal control. This study will fill this literature gap by looking into the roles of the CEO and the CFO in strengthening a firm’s internal control. The CEO and the CFO constitute the key personnel of firm management and are directly involved in building the internal control of the firm. Section 302 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (2002) specifically requires CEOs and CFOs to certify and assert to stakeholders that the management has taken appropriate steps to ensure that the disclosure process and internal control of the company are capable of consistently producing reliable financial information. Our proposed project that links the CEO and CFO compensation to the remediation of ICMWs is particularly relevant to the understanding of the determinants of effective corporate internal control. Moreover, our comparison of the different functions of CEOs and CFOs in terms of internal control will add to the literature on the differences between the two positions (Jiang, et al. 2010; Chava and Purnanandam 2010; Kim, et al. 2010). 这项研究的目的是考察公司总裁和财务总监持有的股份报酬对公司内部控制问题修复的影响。美国2002年Sarbanes-Oxley法案要求公司披露内部控制是否可靠以及所存在问题。在这一制度背景下，我们可以观测到哪些公司内部控制存在缺陷，以及公司是否在短期内及时修补内部控制存在的缺陷。公司股票价值会因为内部控制问题的披露而急剧下跌。因此，我们预测管理层的股份报酬对促使他们及时修复内部控制问题起到积极作用。我们将利用美国的数据对上述预测做检验。

748812.label: Realisation of objectives
748812.value: 1. Research performed to achieve the three objectives 1.1 Hypotheses We develop three hypotheses regarding the effects of CEO equity compensation incentives on the remediation of material weaknesses (MWs) in internal control following their initial public disclosure. H1a: Ceteris paribus, CEO price sensitivity (i.e., the sensitivity of CEO stock and option portfolios to stock price, or delta) has a positive impact on firm promptness in remedying MWs in internal control. H1b: Ceteris paribus, CEO volatility sensitivity (i.e., the sensitivity of CEO option portfolio to stock return volatility, or vega) has a negative impact on firm promptness in remedying MWs in internal control. H2: Effective boards of directors mitigate the negative impact of CEO volatility sensitivity on firm promptness in remedying MWs. 1.2. Research design We exploit the shift in disclosure regime (brought about by Sarbanes-Oxley Act, or SOX), which caused significant stock price declines for firms reporting MWs in internal control, to investigate how managers respond to losses in their stock price-based wealth through changing/remedying ineffective internal controls. By analyzing managers’ remediation behavior, we investigate the tradeoff between equity benefits and costs in moving away from ineffective internal controls under the more transparent, post-SOX disclosure regime. More specifically, firms’ initial disclosures of MWs under SOX present a quasi-experimental setting where we attempt to identify a causal relation between managers’ equity incentives and their remediation behavior in a short window of one year following MW disclosure. In this setting, remediation incentives derive from market reaction to unanticipated MW disclosure and managers’ pre-existing (i.e., pre-disclosure) equity holdings. Therefore, the equity incentives are exogenous to determination of managers’ subsequent remediation behavior. This quasi-experiment helps us examine the causal effects of equity incentives on internal control decisions. To test our hypotheses, we collect a sample consisting of 323 unique firms in the Audit-Analytics database that disclosed MWs in internal control for the first time under SOX between November 15, 2003, and August 27, 2006. Our sample begins on November 15, 2003, one year before the first batch of SOX 404 audit opinions under Auditing Standard No. 2 (or AS2) became available, so that all disclosed MWs can be checked with subsequent audit opinions in firms’ annual reports to confirm their remediation status. Our sample ends on August 27, 2006, one year prior to the earliest adoption of Auditing Standard No. 5 (or AS5), which provides a different set of guidelines for auditors to express an opinion on internal control effectiveness compared with AS2, to avoid potential confounding effects of the disparities between AS2 and AS5. 2. Results and the realization of our three research objectives Our empirical results are consistent with our three hypotheses. Specifically, we find that, ceteris paribus, as CEO price sensitivity (delta) increases, firms are more likely to promptly remedy MWs in internal control. In contrast, as CEO volatility sensitivity (vega) derived from option holdings increases, firms are less likely to promptly remedy MWs in internal control. In terms of economic significance, our results suggest that a one standard deviation increase in CEO delta from its mean increases the likelihood of timely remediation of MWs by 12 percent, whereas a similar increase in CEO vega reduces the likelihood of timely remediation of MWs by 9 percent. Finally, we provide evidence that effective boards of directors mitigate the undesirable, negative effects of CEO vega on remediation of MWs. Our results shed light on the CEO tradeoff between equity benefits and costs in moving away from ineffective firm internal controls under the more transparent, post-SOX disclosure regime. Our results imply that when the price-driven losses managers suffer from public revelation of internal control weaknesses exceed any risk-driven benefits they enjoy under a weak control system, these personal losses not only impel managers to remedy existing weaknesses, they also act as a credible threat to deter managers from choosing ineffective internal controls in the future. This evidence suggests that the disclosure regulation in SOX provides a channel for a compensation structure that creates high delta, rather than one that creates high vega, to facilitate market-based discipline on managers, thereby strengthening firm internal control. Our results are consistent with evidence of a decrease in the (positive) relation between executive delta and earnings management from the pre- to the post-SOX period (Cohen et al. 2008; Jiang et al. 2010) and enhance our understanding of how equity compensation structures influence internal control quality in the post-SOX environment. Our additional analysis concerning the difference between CEO and CFO incentives shows that both of them play important roles in the remediation of internal control weaknesses. Specifically, the price sensitivity for both CEOs and CFOs has positive effects on remediation promptness. In contrast, the volatility sensitivity for both CEOs and CFOs has negative effects on remediation promptness and the undesirable, negative effect of volatility sensitivity appears more severe for CFOs than for CEOs. In summary, we have fully achieved the three research objectives set forth for our project.

748812.label: Major findings and research outcome
748812.value: This project examines how CEO equity incentives affect remediation of material weaknesses (MWs) in internal control disclosed pursuant to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX). We find that sensitivity of CEO equity portfolios to stock price (CEO price sensitivity, or delta) has a positive impact on firm promptness in remedying MWs, whereas sensitivity of CEO equity portfolios to stock return volatility (CEO volatility sensitivity, or vega) has a negative impact on firm promptness in remedying MWs. In addition, we provide evidence that effective boards of directors mitigate the undesirable, negative effect of CEO volatility sensitivity on remediation of MWs. This project makes three main contributions. First, it sheds light on the CEO tradeoff between equity benefits and costs in moving away from ineffective firm internal controls under the more transparent, post-SOX disclosure regime. Second, our results on executive volatility sensitivity (vega) add to an emerging literature that explores the economic settings in which option compensation, and the induced risk-taking behavior, can be excessive or value-destroying. Third, this study contributes to the literature on the role of boards of directors in monitoring managerial behavior. We find an interactive effect between board effectiveness and CEO incentives, specifically, that effective boards mitigate the undesirable risking-taking incentive caused by CEO option holdings. In summary, our findings shed light on the effects of equity compensation structures on internal control quality in the more transparent, post-SOX environment. This project has helped to train my former PhD student Ms. LIU, Xuejiao and led to her doctoral thesis titled "The effects of CEO equity-based compensation on firm promptness in remedying material weaknesses in internal control." This project generates a paper coauthored with LIU Xuejiao and entitled "CEO equity incentives and remediation of material weaknesses in internal control." The paper was submitted to the "Journal of Business Finance and Accounting." We received revision request and many comments from a reviewer and the editor. We are now revising the paper to accommodate the reviewer's comments to resubmit it to the journal.

748912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748912.value: Transit-oriented development (TOD) refers to a combination of characteristics about the built environment which promotes walking and the use of public transportation (Ewing and Cervero, 2010). The characteristics of TOD neighbourhoods range from the road network, parking availability, public transport services, pedestrian and cycling facilities, general land-use pattern, housing types and density, pubic and private facilities and public space (Loo, 2009c). These various characteristics can be grouped under the three dimensions of density, diversity and design, the “three Ds” of TOD as suggested by Cervero and Kockelman (1997). This project sees TOD as a sustainable urban transport strategy not only in a large part of the developed world facing various problems associated with an automobile-dependent lifestyle but also in the developing world undergoing rapid motorization. It provides much-needed Asian evidence on the “three Ds” of TOD, and addresses an important gap in the literature by explicitly recognizing the variability of local geographies in shaping different TOD neighbourhoods within one city. As a step further, it investigates the quantitative inter-relationships among the “three Ds” of TOD at the station-neighbourhood level. The methodology is transferable to other cities, and the findings will be interpreted carefully as lessons learnt from a specific case study. In recent years, the co-benefits of TOD beyond the transport realm have been increasingly recognized (Cutts et al, 2009; de Nezelle et al, 2011; Litman, 2006). Co-benefits are defined as both direct and indirect benefits beyond traditional transport impacts measured by the increased public transport usage, reduced automobile usage, and various emissions and congestion benefits resulting directly from “less cars on the street”. Examples of key TOD co-benefits include improved livability, quality of life, social equity and public health. Yet, there is no systematic study on these co-benefits, as compared to the rest of the city. By providing scientific evidence on these co-benefits and their magnitudes, this research project would have a long-term impact on widening people’s concept of TOD from a people-centred and place-based perspective. Moreover, this research project measures the impacts of the “three Ds” of TOD on station-level patronage by distinguishing among station-neighbourhood, network and city level factors (Loo, Chen and Chan, 2010). Methodologically, multilevel analysis is used to disentangle effects of factors at different spatial scales on public transit patronage. With the above findings, policy-makers in different parts of the world will be able to make more appropriate integrated policy to promote sustainable urban transport. 公交導向型發展”(Transit-oriented development, TOD) 意在塑造有利於使用公共交通工具及步行的整體小社區規劃及發展模式。其範疇包括公共運輸系統，土地利用及房屋密度等。無論是對發達或發展中國家來說，TOD都是一個可持續的城市運輸及發展策略。此研究項目集中研究TOD的三個方面，即密度(Density)，多樣性(Diversity)及設計(Design)。這三方面一般簡稱為“3D”。以香港的六十多個地鐵站的小社區為案例，研究隊伍將量化地調查和分析“3D”各個方面之間的相互關係。研究的結果將能令各界對TOD在亞洲區的實踐有更深入的了解。另外，研究也希望能帶出TOD社區的多樣性及反思TOD是一種單一模式的概念。最後，我們將研究和量化TOD的共同利益(Co-benefits)。共同利益是指TOD在交通領域外對社會直接和間接的利益。例如，減少使用小汽車是否有利於提升社區內人民的生活質素及大眾健康？此研究項目的結果將有助世界各地制定更合適的政策以推廣可持續城市運輸及發展策略。

748912.label: Realisation of objectives
748912.value: The PI has been very grateful for the opportunity to work on this exciting research projects. All the proposed research objectives have been realized, though the process was full of challenges. Substantial amount of time and efforts has been devoted to overcome these challenges and to realize the proposed objectives according to the proposed methodology. A summary is provided below: Objective 1. Provide much-needed Asian evidence on the “three Ds” of TOD by quantifying them Based on the general and broad principles of the 3Ds of density, diversity and design, this project has explored ways of describing different types of TOD neighbourhoods relevant to the local geographical context. In the context of Hong Kong, 20 variables directly relevant to the 3Ds were collected from various official sources of data and direct fieldwork around 60 metro stations (as of 2012). For Density, these variables include DEN01 on population density (number of residents / land area), DEN02 on employment density, DEN03 on residential development intensity, DEN04 on commercial development intensity, DEN05 on mixed commercial-residential development intensity, and DEN06 on overall development intensity. For diversity, these variables are DIV01 on comprehensive development, DIV02 on diversity of land uses, DIV03 on household size, DIV04 on diversity of housing types, DIV05 on levels of other public transit services, DIV06 on convenience of other public transit, and DIV07 on income. For design, they are DSN01 on road connectivity, DSN02 on road density, DSN03 on open space, DSN04 on covered walkway, DSN05 on presence of expressways, DSN6 on the metro exit system, and DSN07 on retail shops within the station. Details of the rationale, data collection process, and results are documented in the MPhil thesis of Frederic Daniel du Verle (2013) and our paper (2017) in the International Journal of Urban Sciences. Some other information that I hoped to get, such as the civil servant employment (density) and occupation of residents (diversity), was not available. Objective 2. Be a pioneer project to investigate the quantitative inter-relationship among the “three Ds” of TOD at the station-neighbourhood level within a city Based on the quantified indicators above (Objective 1), the principal component analysis (PCA) is applied to see whether there are common built environment characteristics underlying specific types of metro neighbourhoods, recognizing that it is neither possible nor desirable to have uniformly high density, diversity and same design in every TOD neighbourhood. Five major types of TOD neighbourhoods are identified in Hong Kong based on the factor loadings associated with the five factors identified. Factor 1 mostly describes the dense economic urban neighbourhoods – typically the CBD. Factor 2 are areas with good station-neighbourhood integration. Factor 3 are neighbourhood with a great diversity of people and activity. Factor 4 are mostly residential neighbourhoods with large families. Finally, factor 5 is distinguished by good station design and integration with other transport networks. They are named the CBD-, integrated community-, balanced-, residential- and station-type TODs respectively. Details of the rationale, data collection process, and results are documented in the MPhil thesis of Frederic Daniel du Verle (2013) and our upcoming paper in the International Journal of Urban Sciences. Objective 3. Examine and assess the co-benefits of the “three Ds” of TOD systematically Various co-benefits of the “three Ds” of TOD have been identified. Co-benefits are defined as both direct and indirect benefits beyond traditional transport impacts measured by the increased public transport usage, reduced automobile usage, and various emissions and congestion benefits resulting directly from “less cars on the street”. Examples of key TOD co-benefits include improved livability, quality of life, social equity and public health. The co-benefits associated with the “Three Ds” of TODs are numerous. Density, for instance, is conducive to increased social interactions, the provision of more neighbourhood lower-order facilities, and generating the labour pooling effects for spatial agglomeration to happen. Diversity is conductive to higher vibrancy at street level, less crime, and more non-local residents on the streets. Design is conductive to more physical exercises, better public health conditions, less traffic injuries and better quality of life. All these “intangible” values beyond the metro patronage and carbon reduction should be properly reflected in the whole planning process. In Loo and du Verle (forthcoming) and my invited talks (especially at the Seoul Metropolitan Forum in November 2015, the Low-Carbon Cities in June 2014 and the Symposium of Space-time Behavior and Smart City & The 9th Conference on Spatial Behavior and Planning in January 2014), I have highlighted that the co-benefits of TOD beyond the transport realm need to be recognized. Objective 4: Measure the impacts of the “three Ds” of TOD on station-level patronage by distinguishing among station-neighbourhood, network and city level factors This objective has, once again, been achieved through integrating the findings from objectives 1 and 2. Based on the results of the PCA, the factors were then regressed to the key variables of metro, other public transport, and walking trips for residents living in the TOD neighbourhood. The results have been documented in a Chapter of the thesis of du Verle (2013). While the PI has successfully obtained the MTR station patronage data at a more disaggregate level in 2009 (see Loo, Chen and Chan, 2010), the MTR Corporation was no longer able to share station patronage data for research purposes. Hence, the project has mainly relied on the data of the Travel Characteristics Surveys conducted by the Government. As this project progressed from January 2013 to December 2015, the PI has also been increasingly convinced that the success of TOD needs to be measured beyond patronage data and be extended to other non-economic benefits, such as enhanced walkability of the city and other co-benefits. The success of TODs needs to be judged not by patronage only. Through a systematic comparison of the travel behaviour of residents living near 60 metro and 60 non-metro neighbourhoods, it is found that the former group exhibited more sustainable travel behaviour of walking more and driving less Objective 5: Tease out the policy implications behind the above findings This objective requires the PI to reflect upon the findings of the entire project. Hence, while many policy implications at different stages of the research have been shared in her invited talks over time, she expects that the major output will be her invited Plenary talk at the Forum on “From Paris Agreement to Post-carbon Cities: Earth Day Forum 2016”, April 22, 2016. At the occasion, key government officials including Ms Christine Loh, the Undersecretary for Environment of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) Government, will also be attending. The final presentation file will be uploaded after the event. Overall, it is expected that the findings of this project will continue to create an impact on government policies and the Hong Kong society through the PI’s role in various advisory bodies to the Hong Kong SAR Government, including the Transport Advisory Committee.

748912.label: Major findings and research outcome
748912.value: This project has provided training to five postgraduate students, including Frederic Daniel du Verle (2013) on “Transit-oriented Development in Hong Kong” (MPhil), Samantha Laura Nichols (2015) on “Sustainable Transport in Hong Kong: Reshuffling the Transport Hierarchy based on Geographical Characteristics and Trip Characteristics Variations” (MPhil), Linna Li (2014) on “Interaction between Regional Development and Inter-city High-speed Railways in Chinese Mega-city Regions” (PhD), Zi Yang (2016, expected) on “Transport Geography and Spatial Analysis” (PhD), and Bo Wang (2017, expected) on “The Role of Distance in the Information Age” (PhD). The theses of du Verle and Nichols are almost fully based on this project, while the theses of Li, Yang and Wang are partially related. In addition, the findings have been/will be shared in five talks, including the 33rd International Geographic Congress, Beijing (August, 2016), Forum on From Paris Agreement to Post-carbon Cities: Earth Day Forum 2016 (April 2016) (invited plenary talk), the Seoul Metropolitan Forum (November 2015) (invited plenary talk), the Low-carbon Cities: Land Use and Transportation Interventions (June 2014) (invited plenary talk) and the Symposium of Space-time Behavior and Smart City & The 9th Conference on Spatial Behavior and Planning (January 2014) (invited keynote speech). Last but not least, the findings of the research project have resulted in three internationally refereed journal papers with one in Chinese (Chinese Academy of Sciences) (SSCI), one under revision after reviews in the Landscape and Urban Planning (Elsevier) (SCI; Impact Factor: 3.037) and a final one under review in the International Journal of Urban Studies (Taylor & Frances) (Special Issue invitation). As a social science project with five integrated objectives, the PI has only worked on the high-quality research papers upon the completion of all data analysis and synthesizing the various findings (instead of producing short papers on part of the project only). It is expected that more research outputs, including journal papers, will result directly from the findings of this research project.

748912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748912.value: The PI has been reflecting upon the findings of this research project and she is convinced that further development in two directions will be very beneficial. The first direction is related to Objective 3, that is, the co-benefits of TOD development. More studies on residents’ perceptions of the co-benefits of the metro transit system will further enhance our knowledge about TOD. This may require surveys of residents’ opinion beyond this project. The second direction is related to Objective 5, that is, the policy implications. As this involves discussion with the management of the MTR Corporation and the relevant Bureaux, including the Transport and Housing Bureau and the Environment Bureau, as well as engagement with the general public, this process will take time. Nonetheless, the PI is actively pursuing these two directions. She hopes to include part of the findings and further development in her invited Plenary Talk at the World Symposium on Transport and Land Use Research 2017, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. July 3-6, 2017 and to develop a further GRF project in due course.

748912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748912.value: Transit-oriented development (TOD) refers to a community development model that seeks to build healthier communities and stronger economies while reducing their carbon footprint. It is a mixture of housing, retail and/or commercial development and amenities integrated into a walkable neighborhood and centred around quality public transport. Based on the general and broad principles of the 3Ds of density, diversity and design, this project has explored ways of describing different types of TOD neighbourhoods. 20 variables directly relevant to the 3Ds were collected around 60 metro stations (as of 2012). Then, the principal component analysis (PCA) is applied. Five major types of TOD neighbourhoods are identified. They are named the CBD-, integrated community-, balanced-, residential- and station-type TODs respectively. Various co-benefits of TOD have been identified. Co-benefits are defined as both direct and indirect benefits beyond traditional transport impacts. Through a systematic comparison of the travel behaviour of residents living near 60 metro and 60 non-metro neighbourhoods, it is found that the former group exhibited more sustainable travel behaviour of walking more and driving less. For municipality governments and policy-makers, the project shows that the intangible and non-economic benefits of TOD need to be recognized.

749312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
749312.value: 企業在追逐合法利潤的同時履行其社會責任，已經成為全球商業領袖不得不關註的一個話題。有的企業家認為企業承擔社會責任會增強企業的競爭力，提高利潤；而另一部分企業家則擔心企業承擔社會責任，會占用企業有限的資源，從而降低企業的商業利潤。因此，人們對於企業是否承擔社會責任認識不一而足。學者們於是一直致力於探究企業社會責任和財務業績之間的關系以期為這一爭論提供理論和實證的支撐。過去的四十年中，人們對企業社會責任和財務業績之間的關系進行了大量的研究，得出了不同，甚至是相反的結論。總之，企業社會責任和財務業績之間的模糊關系尚需進一步的探究。 本研究課題假設：從短期來看，履行社會責任（例如減少碳排量，恪守公平貿易原則等）可能給企業帶來額外負擔，從而導致財務績效水平降低。然而，基於長期發展視角，履行社會責任可以提升公司形象、改善業務關系，利於企業長期可持續發展。因此，企業社會責任和財務業績之間是一種悖論關系。基於這種假設，本研究提出了三個相互關聯的研究目標：a) 構建企業社會責任(CSR)和財務業績(CFP)的關系模型；b) 通過國際建築行業研究實證檢驗CSR-CFP模型；c) 調查一系列商業案例以進一步解析CSR-CFP關系。 基於相關理論及前人的研究成果，本研究首先構建一個CSR-CFP矛盾關系理論模型。隨後，通過檢索《工程新聞記錄》、《財富》雜誌以及企業年報等權威資料，以獲取關於國際建築企業社會責任的大量縱向面板數據（Panel data），並通過對該數據進行回歸及滯後分析進行假設檢驗。為了增加實證結論的可信度，該結果將用國際建築企業的案例分析進行交叉驗證。案例分析會運用訪談、小組討論、研討會等一系列定性研究方法，最終得到一組解析CSR-CFP矛盾關系的商業案例。 本研究從提出CSR-CFP矛盾關系假設到運用交叉檢驗方法上都體現出一定的創新性。同時，建築業作為一個異質性行業，其企業社會責任尤為值得大家重點關註。因此，本研究項目具有很高的學術價值和實用價值。在學術上，本研究為懸而未決的CSR-CFP關系提供了新的見解，這種見解可望實現CSR-CFP關系理論突破。在實踐中，本研究作為CSR的實證依據有助於企業高層進行科學決策，有助於CSR政策的制定。此外，本研究總結的商業案例可以作為建築企業制定CSR政策的範例。

749312.label: Realisation of objectives
749312.value: Objective 1: On the basis of theories, specifically on theories in relation to the CSR phenomena, neoclassical economies, systems think as well as stakeholder theory, we developed the model that the short-term effect of CSR is a negative CFP, whereas the long-term effect of CSR is a higher CFP by considering the time effect on the CSR-CFP links. This model provides fresh answer to the question regarding the disputed CSR-CFP link, and will help divert researchers' attention away from the "allies-and-adversaries" dichotomy towards the paradoxical dynamics between CSR and CFP. The model has been tested in the manuscript "The paradoxical nexus between corporate social responsibility and financial performance in the international construction business", which is under review. Objective 2: 1. International construction business and CSR in the international construction market have been largely explored. A journal paper titled “Nexus between contracting and construction professional service businesses: empirical evidence from the international market” has been published, where contracting and construction professional service businesses in the international market were explored. Another paper titled “Diversification in the international construction business" explored the diversification patterns portrayed by the construction companies in the international construction markets. Dr. Wilson Lu has published one book chapter "Lu, W.S. (2014). Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) in international construction, pp 198-217. In Liu, J.Y. (ed.) Frontiers and Key Trends in Construction Management Research. China City Press: Beijing (in Chinese). ", which describe CSR in international construction. There is a section in the chapter to introduce the GRF project. 2. Regarding nexus between corporate social responsibility and corporate financial performance, we did lots of work. Firstly, a critical review of empirical studies regarding relationship between CSR and CFP from 2002 to 2011 was published, titled “A decade’s debate on the nexus between corporate social and corporate financial performance: a critical review of empirical studies 2002 – 2011”. In this review, 84 empirical studies were identified, wherein positive relationships between the decomposed CSR and CFP are confirmed by most of the studies while some did argue for a nonsignificant or a negative relationship. Secondly, we did empirically test the CSR-CFP model. Virtuous nexus was proved by analysing the construction enterprises in China (with paper “Virtuous nexus between corporate social performance and financial performance: A study of construction enterprises in China”), while curvilinear relationship is as the result by testing the international construction companies (with paper “The curvilinear relationship between corporate social performance and corporate financial performance: evidence from the international construction industry”). Thirdly, a little different from the curvilinear relationship between CSR and CFP, time effects were considered to explore the short-term and long-term effects of CSR on CFP. A manuscript titled “The paradoxical nexus between corporate social responsibility and financial performance in the international construction business” is under review. Objective 3 When we did the empirical test, business cases of international construction companies were collected to do the case studies. CSR activities implemented in the international construction market have been explored which is shown in the journal paper titled “Corporate social responsibility disclosures in international construction business: trends and prospects”. In this research, CSR reports were collected from their websites or Global Reporting Initiative databases to provide an understanding of the idiosyncrasies of CSR disclosure and offered suggestions for future reporting exercises for helping interpret the CSR-CFP link.

749312.label: Major findings and research outcome
749312.value: 1. The review for empirical studies of the CSP-CFP relationship published in the decade between 2002 and 2011 shows that CSP-CFP nexus is still a line of inquiry that remains inconclusive. Among 84 empirical studies reviewed, positive relationships between the decomposed CSR and CFP are confirmed by most of the studies while some did argue for a nonsignificant or a negative relationship. 2. The curvilinear relationship of CSP on ROA and EPS, as specific CFP measures is confirmed with strong support, by using a panel data set of 30 international construction companies and 210 firm-year observations over the sample period from 2007 to 2013. 3. Focusing on the international construction business and considering time effects, we find that implementing CSR programmes is slightly detrimental to CFP in the short term but will benefit CFP in the long term. In other words, the impact of CSR on CFP is not immediate and unchanging. This is proved by using Vector Error Correction Model (VECM) to analyse a panel of sixty-seven international construction companies from 2006 to 2015. In summary, the hypothesis of a paradoxical link between CSR and CFP is confirmed. This research can be used as evidence to refute CSR short-termism.

749312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
749312.value: 1. The research was undertaken in a confined, construction-related business sector. Future research is encouraged to test the hypothetical paradoxical link between CSR and CFP in a more general setting so that the results can be generalized, or even utilized to ultimately develop a theory. 2. Although the paradoxical link between CSR and CFP has been confirmed using statistical methods, when and how CSR programs will become allies of CFP remains unclear. Future research is recommended to discover empirical evidence to articulate the ‘epistemological link’ for managing CSR programs that lead to positive CFP. 3. Use of the panel VECM model method does not allow precise definition of the ‘long’ or ‘short’ term. Further research is recommended to apply other statistical methods to find the time frame in which CSR investments make a return, thereby helping managers to enhance their discretionary judgment.

749312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
749312.value: The research project is to prove the CSR-CFP relationship is not static but a dynamic process changing over time. It takes time to materialize CSR. A significant practical use of this research is to provide evidence for the assertion that business executives should be relieved from short-termism in assuming social responsibility. It is suggested that not only may CSR not immediately lead to higher financial performance but that it may actually result in a negative impact on a firm’s financial performance in the short term. Shareholders should therefore take a long-term view when looking at executives’ CSR strategies.

749712.label: Project Title(Chinese)
749712.value: 傳統團結與政治制度：廈門和台中的比較研究

749712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
749712.value: This project is a comparative study of civic culture in two Chinese cities: Xiamen, a commercial hub on the southeastern coast of China, and Taichung, a city of comparable size located directly across the Straits in Taiwan. I explore how citizens of these two cities use one particular set of cultural values – the “guanxi complex” – to manage risk and cultivate a sense of security in their lives. The guanxi complex is generally understood in social-scientific literature as a form of entrenched traditional culture responsible for the characteristic “informal dimension” in Chinese political and economic institutions. My study focuses on how political context affects the meaning of the guanxi complex. Xiamen is governed under market socialism, Taichung under liberal democracy. How is this difference in regime type correlated to differences in the ways citizens understand and use the guanxi complex to manage their social and economic lives? I set out with the following hypothesis. In Taiwan, the primacy of electoral contests in political decision-making serves to channel political conflict into a formally institutionalized political realm. This reduces the intensity of political significance invested in informal bonds of social solidarity. This, I hold, will be reflected in a greater emphasis of the affective over the instrumental dimensions of guanxi-complex-based solidarities. In other words, I predict that Taichung’s civic culture will exhibit a relative emphasis on the affective meanings of guanxi, ganqing, renqing, etc. Xiamen, by contrast, with its relatively less institutionalized mechanisms for the formal mediation or adjudication of political-economic disputes, will exhibit relatively more focused concern on the instrumental or purposive dimension of these values. My research methods are ethnographic. To test my hypothesis, I will use participant observation and depth interviews to study the ways that the guanxi complex is deployed as a resource for “civil security” (Loader & Walker 2007) the everyday lives of individual citizens and civic associations. The project detailed here builds on more than a decade of previous experience researching police and civil society organization in Taiwan and China. The funds I request will enable six months of field research in each city, as detailed below. This project will provide a corrective to the “lexical fallacy” in contemporary guanxi studies, contribute a comparative ethnography of everyday security in two contemporary cities to the political anthropology of China, and contribute to cross-disciplinary discussion about the character of civil security and its relation to political institutions. 該項研究目的是在中國的兩個城市，廈門與台中，從事公民文化的比較研究。我研究這兩個城市的市民如何使用一組特定的文化價值觀 - “關係情結” - 在他們的生活中管理風險與培養安全。在社會科學文獻中，關係情結被看為一種華人根深蒂固的傳統文化，特別重要為作“非正式尺寸“的作用。在當代中國的政治經濟機構複雜時，本研究要更進一步瞭解政治背景如何影響關係情結的意義。

750012.label: Project Objectives
750012.value: To present a version of Harsanyi's theorem which is stripped of problematic idealizing assumptions and is accompanied by a philosophical account of the meaning of the evaluative comparatives it uses. To provide a novel account of what concerns with fairness, equality, and giving priority to the worse off really amount to, and to use the Harsanyi-like result to axiomatize theories which adopt these concerns, separately and in combination. To analyze two important but relatively unexplored options for distinctive Kantian contractualist responses to the Harsanyi-like result: the rejection of continuity, and the denial of global coherence requirements. To articulate assumptions standardly made about evaluative measurement in moral philosophy, to contrast these with standard treatments of measurement in the physical and social sciences, to argue that the assumptions in moral philosophy are seriously mistaken, and to present an alternative account. To develop the best argument for utilitarianism, to compare and contrast utilitarianism with alternatives and (most likely) argue in its favor, and to offer a striking and novel conclusion about what it really amounts to. To complete a series of approximately 13 articles on the above topics, 3 of which are already published, 4 of which are either under review or at the "revise and resubmit" stage, with the majority of the remainder already well-developed. To use the articles to write an accessible book, *The Structure of Good*, aimed at a broad audience in moral philosophy and related areas. The book is already under contract with Oxford University Press.

750012.label: Realisation of objectives
750012.value: The main goal of the project was to develop a novel account of utilitarianism, and to use this to articulate how alternatives to utilitarianism should also be understood. A secondary goal of the project was to argue that when utilitarianism is understood along these lines, it is correct. The plan was to first develop the overall account in a series of articles, and then to write a draft of a book bringing together all of material to a broader audience. I am very pleased with the overall project. I have not made as much progress on the book as I would have liked because the development of the account of utilitarianism turned out to be extraordinarily complex. This account is provided in the core paper `Utilitarianism with and without expected utility’, currently under review, but already published as a Working Paper (as is standard practice in economics). We have been working on this paper almost nonstop for four years, and the full development of the theory turned out to require the development of a number of background papers, of interest in themselves. Thus each of the following was written to elaborate on various aspects of the core paper: — `Representation of strongly independent preorders by sets of scalar-valued functions’ — `Continuity and completeness of strongly independent preorders’ — `Representation of strongly independent preorders by vector-valued functions’ — `Representation of strongly independent strict partial orders by scalar-valued utility functions’ The first two have already been submitted and published in a public archive as Working Papers. The other two are worked out, and will each take about 3 to 4 weeks to write up (depending on the availability of my coauthors). In addition, we discovered another remarkable result along the way that is connected with a different way of looking at utilitarianism. This is essentially a version of Harsanyi’s original aggregation theorem that assumes neither continuity nor completeness. This is contained in — `Aggregation for general populations without continuity or completeness’ One of the bonuses of this paper is that it solves a big problem in value theory that I had no idea how to approach when I designed the project, and this unanticipated bonus will form a further major article (not yet written) and central part of the eventual book. The final item in the same vein is the following: — `Utilitarianism and uncertainty’ This provides an abstract version of the aggregation theorem of the core paper, showing its applicability to a huge range of ways of representing uncertainty. This will take a bit more work, mainly as there is such a vast body of work on the representation of uncertainty. The development of the ``What is utilitarianism?’’ part of the project therefore turned out to be vastly more challenging, complex, time consuming and mathematical than anticipated, and it is still ongoing. Since the rest of the project was essentially to address the question “What follows from this account of utilitarianism?”, some aspects of this part of the project had to be delayed. Nevertheless, I have made quite a lot of progress with it: — `Risk-free approaches to the priority view.’ Erkenntnis 78 (2013): 421-449. This criticises the use of evaluative measurements in standard approaches to the ethics of distribution in moral philosophy. It’s part of the overall project, but I finished it before the GRF officially started. — `Distributive equality.’ Mind 124 (2015): 1045--1109. This gives a semi-formal account of what egalitarianism is, essentially based on the account of utilitarianism. At about 25,000 words, it’s one of the longest papers Mind (one of the top generalist journals) has ever published. — `The priority view.’ Economics and Philosophy 33 (2017) 215–257 Another long paper, this gives a semi-formal account of the priority view, again based on the account of utilitarianism. — `Probability in ethics’. The Oxford Handbook of Philosophy and Probability. A. Hájek and C. Hitchcock, Oxford University Press: 705--737. This provides an accessible account of how I think various topics in the ethics of distribution fit together; it is meant to give a broad audience a taste of what the book will be about. Apart from this, I have notes for another four or five papers in this vein, including a project with a new coauthor, Lara Buchak, on egalitarianism and nonexpected utility theory. (One of the beauties of the account of utilitarianism, along with the account of the other distributive theories it leads to, is that it does not presuppose expected utility theory, and is compatible with a vast range of nonexpected utility theories.) Aside from not making as much progress on the book as I would have liked, two aspects of the project are not fully developed. First, I proposed to try to understand a contractualist response to utilitarianism in terms of either the rejection of continuity, or the denial of global coherence requirements. Since six of the above papers ask what happens when continuity is rejected (it turns out to be quite complicated in general settings), that question is now well understood. It just turns out not to be very useful for contractualism. I haven't made any real progress on how the denial of global coherence requirements might help contractualism however. This is not really my fault, as contractualists don't offer much help. However, it's clear that the place to look for ideas is in a recent body of literature on choice functions I didn't know about when I started the project. But this involves very different ideas from the utilitarianism material, and I didn't have the cognitive capacity to think about this at the same time. I will get around to this once the utilitarianism material is complete. Second, although I've talked a lot about evaluative measurement in the two papers on the priority view, published in top journals, this material still feels incomplete. The thing to do next is to connect the core account of utilitarianism with the literature with some results on measurement dating back to the 1970s, but again, I had to finish the utilitarianism material first. I still plan to finish the book, but all these papers have to be completed first. It’s hard to explain this without going into details, but one of the benefits of working out the theory at a level of mathematical generality that is inaccessible to virtually all moral philosophers is that it eventually becomes clear that the theory is very simple. In effect, the abstraction shows that a lot of the detail that characteristically accompanies discussions in this area just turns out to be distracting and unnecessary clutter. Burrowing deeply into the minutiae of utilitarianism will turn out to have made the eventual book shorter, more accessible, and better.
