753312.label: Major findings and research outcome
753312.value: Whether conflicts adversely affect international trade and investment is a crucial issue in this increasingly globalized world. Several studies focus on the reduction in trade flows in the immediate years following the wars and how fast trade value recovers. Nevertheless, it is equally important to understand whether past conflicts among countries generate long-term war memories that affect their contemporary trade and investment, in terms of both the absolute and relative levels. Whether historical conflicts cause current economic exchange to fall short of the level that could have been reached had there been no war-induced animosity is an intriguing question. In this study, we utilize the Japanese invasion of China from 1937 to 1945 to examine this issue. To identify the long-run impacts that the Japanese invasion of China has had on contemporary trade and investment between these two countries, we employ the difference-in-differences (DD) estimation method. Specifically, our identification strategy is to compare both the Japanese investment in a Chinese region and the trade between this region and Japan with the corresponding values of other foreign countries, and then examine the variations in these differences across Chinese regions that suffered different degrees of civilian casualties from the Japanese invasion. In those Chinese regions that suffered greater civilian casualties, Japanese multinationals were late in making direct investments, launched a smaller number of enterprises, and invested a smaller amount. Specifically, a one-percentage-point decrease in the ratio of civilian casualties would cause the number of direct investment projects from Japan to increase by 7.9%, the contemporary investment from Japan in 2001 to increase by 23.3%, the accumulated investment from Japan until 2001 to increase by 16.3%, and the investment from Japan to enter half a year earlier. Those Chinese regions hit harder in the Japanese invasion imported less from Japan, although their exports to Japan were much less affected or even unaffected. Hence, they have less aggregate trade with Japan at present. Specifically, a one-percentage-point decrease in the ratio of civilian casualties would, in a single year of 2001, cause China's imports from Japan to increase by 14.7%, and its total trade with Japan to increase by 15.9%. Our study shows that historical animosity still matters in international trade and investment, despite the trend toward an increasingly globalized world. If the Chinese and the Japanese could turn the historically rooted dark page, their bilateral trade and investment might reach a much higher level.

753312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
753312.value: We can extend this cross-region study to cross-country study of the impact of the Second World War on their contemporary trade and investment.

753312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
753312.value: In this study, we exploit one of the most important conflicts of the 20th century between what are currently the world's second and third largest economies, that is, the Japanese invasion of China from 1937 to 1945, to investigate the long-term impact of conflicts between countries on cross-border trade and investment. We find that Japanese multinationals are less likely to invest in Chinese regions that suffered greater civilian casualties during the Japanese invasion, and these regions also trade less with Japan. Our study shows that historical animosity still influences international trade and investment, despite the trend toward an increasingly globalized world.

753512.label: Project Objectives
753512.value: To investigate whether managers' internal/external attributions for performance in earnings press releases affect the stock market reactions and analysts' forecast revision around the earnings announcement dates. To investigate whether more credible attributions have a stronger impact on stock price reactions and analysts' forecast revisions. To help managers improve disclosure practices in earnings press releases.

To investigate whether more credible attributions have a stronger impact on stock price reactions and analysts' forecast revisions.
To help managers improve disclosure practices in earnings press releases.

753512.label: Realisation of objectives
753512.value: Overall, we have achieved all of the objectives proposed in the project. During the execution of the project, there were a few factors that took us longer time than what we expected. First, we have decided not only to manually code press releases but also to use the manual coded work and the existing work from the concurrent research to conduct computational textual analysis. This change increased the contribution of our work to the research and to the society, but also delayed the project. Second, the transition of the fund between two institutions took more than 6 months to finish. Third, a part of the research proposal was done by a competing study which started after our proposal but got published. We needed to spend time differentiating our project from this competing one. Eventually, we overcame this issue, and did find interesting and important results that contribute to the prior and current research and practices significantly. Fourth, the analysis for analyzing documents actually required much computing time. Each variation took us a week to finish. Adjusting dictionaries also normally took one or two months. In spite of the obstacles discussed above, in this project, we use a textual analysis approach to classify these causative explanations (i.e., managerial attribution of performance) and investigate how they affect the precision and accuracy of analysts’ earnings forecasts. We find that firms’ idiosyncratic causative explanations for earnings improve the forecast precision around press release dates, and this effect is more pronounced for bad news earnings; industry-wide causative explanations for bad news earnings, but not for good news earnings, also improve analysts’ forecast precision. We further find evidence that idiosyncratic causative explanations for bad news earnings improve analysts’ forecast accuracy around earnings press release dates. Overall, causative explanations for earnings help improve the precision and accuracy of analysts’ earnings forecasts mainly when firms release bad news earnings. Cross-sectionally, improvement of forecast precision and accuracy is more likely for firms facing high information uncertainty (i.e., the great ambiguity of linking new information to firm value and performance) and for firms with focused operations. Our study should be of interest to regulators concerned about disclosure practices. Our results showing that voluntary causative explanations for earnings in press releases help lower market uncertainty imply that encouraging such voluntary disclosures may help capital markets to function well. Our research also has implications for money managers, analysts, and the investment community at large. Our findings regarding certain types of causative explanations for earnings are more useful to analysts in firms with high information uncertainty or focused operations imply that analysts or investors may pay much attention to disclosed information under the conditions discussed above for the valuation analysis. The weak results regarding the effect of causative explanations for earnings on analyst precision and accuracy for firms with diversified operations suggest that investor relation managers of these firms should put much effort into communicating business information to analysts and investors. Regarding the market reactions to causative explanations (i.e., managerial attributions) for earnings, and their assessment of credibility, they have been done by Kimbrough and Wang (2014) at Accounting Review when we have done a part of our analysis. We cited their study in the manuscript. In fact, we have also examined market reactions to causative explanations using our sample. However, in our setting requiring high analysts’ following, we do not observe the differential market returns associated with causative explanations for bad news or good news earnings. Instead, we focus on the effect of causative explanations for earnings on analysts. We differentiate industry-wide causative explanations (i.e., external attributions) and competitive move, structural change and firm idiosyncratic causative explanations (i.e., internal attributions) for good news and bad news earnings to detect whether credibility of attributions versus informational role of them have impact on analysts, and find that informational role of causative explanations for earnings seems to explain our results. We not only manually code and improve the word lists described in the prior studies (e.g., Koo et al. 2016 and Baginski et al. 2004), but also use computational textual analysis to conduct our empirical tests. Therefore, our analysis can be easily extended to other international settings such as Hong Kong to help regulators around the world. We identify several conditions where causative explanations for earnings are effective or ineffective so that managers may consider improving disclosure practices in earnings press releases in these ineffective situations. Overall, we have achieved all the objectives in this project and have potential to extend to address more regulation-related questions in Hong Kong.

753712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
753712.value: The proposed bilingual reading study 2013 (BR2013) is the fourth in a sequence of surveys, from 2004 (BR2004), 2007 (BR2007) to 2010 (BR2010). The studies involve a three-year cycle of assessments of reading and measures trends in children’s Chinese and English reading attainment; the reading habits and attitudes of students; and an assessment of policies and practices relating to literacy. The theoretical framework and research instruments used in the study will be based on the “Progress in International Reading Literacy Study (PIRLS)” organized by the International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement (IEA). PIRLS is a five-yearly cycle of assessments that measures trends in children’s reading attainment, policies and practices relating to literacy. Some 35 countries worldwide participated in PIRLS2001, 45 participants in PIRLS2006 and 55 participants in PIRLS2011, including Hong Kong(HK). Bilingual reading comprehension tests will be administered and questionnaires given to principals, Chinese and English language teachers, parents and students. Teacher consultancy groups will examine changes in current practice in the teaching of reading, assist in the interpretation of data and their implications. 2,400 primary 4 students at differing ability levels, 2,400 parents, 40 principals and 80 teachers will participate in the study. Through involvement in BR2013, Hong Kong society, schools and the education authority will obtain data about changes in children’s standardised reading attainment. The study will also gather information about changes in classroom reading instructional approaches and how these influence students’ reading performance. Baseline data about students’ levels of reading attainment, demographic background, support from home, school policies, the curriculum and classroom practices will be assembled into a background reference data bank. Scrutinised in the research is the impact of the medium of instruction (MoI) in Chinese on reading performance. The MoI in HK is topically under review. Although Cantonese, the lingua franca in HK, is widely used in schools, Putonghua is increasingly being adopted by many schools as the MoI. The concept of “reading across the curriculum” will also be examined. The outcomes will provide a platform for reflecting on practice and making decisions about ways to elevate bilingual reading proficiency. The findings will be of interest to policy makers, reading material designers, curriculum and syllabus planners, teacher trainers, reading test designers and parents. 本次中英雙語閱讀研究（BR2013）是繼2004（BR2004），2007（BR2007）和2010(BR2010）之後的第四次追蹤研究。本系列的研究期為三年一次，內容包括評估和預測學生中文和英文閱讀的成就，習慣和態度；同時也包括對相關閱讀策略和實踐的評估。 本次研究的理論框架和研究工具是借鑒“全球閱讀進展研究（PIRLS）”這項研究是由國際教育評估協會 （IEA）舉辦。 PIRLS是一個5年的循環追蹤研究，內容包括學生的閱讀成就，有關機構的閱讀政策和實踐。2001年參與的國家有偶35個；2006年45個；2011年55個，香港是參與者之一。 雙語閱讀的研究包括學生閱讀能力的評估，並邀請學校行政人員，家長，教師，學生填寫問卷，收集影響學生閱讀的資料。也邀請教師顧問組討論教學法的轉變，協助分析本研究獲得的數據。 研究樣本包括不同閱讀能力的2400個小四學生，2400個家長，40位校長和80位老師。 通過BR2013的研究，本研究團隊將向香港社會，學校，教育當局提供一些有關香港學生雙語閱讀能力進展的數據，老師教授閱讀的策略，以及影響學生閱讀能力的因素。並建立一個數據庫，內容包含學生的閱讀能力平均水平，學生的背景資料，家庭的支援、學校的政策、課程、教材、教法。本研究亦探究教學語言、普通話教學、跨學科閱讀等項目。 研究結果能反映香港閱讀教學實踐的狀況，並提供提升雙語閱讀能力的建議。研究人員相信政策制定者、課程教材設計者、教師培訓者、閱讀評鑒學者和家長對本研究產生興趣。

753712.label: Realisation of objectives
753712.value: The BR2013 research has been completed and its objectives achieved. The project met its target of recruiting a sample of 2131 Primary 4 students and their bilingual reading literacy was investigated. The associated research article is attached: the research venture concerned embracing the PIRLS framework and its theoretical underpinning. Both quantitative and qualitative enquiries were pursued, the reading comprehension tests being in Chinese and English, thus enabling the bilingual language proficiency of Primary 4 students to be assessed. Two types of text passages were used in the tests, literary and transactional, each presented in booklet form and containing both English and Chinese passages. Each booklet contained one literary and one informational text. The Chinese version was translated from the original English version, equivalence being verified by International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement language experts who used forward and backward translation procedures to ensure equivalence. To ensure that order effects were also taken into consideration, rotated order forms of different sequences and combinations of type of text and type of language were presented. Equal numbers of students were assigned to answer the different booklets. An independent teacher focus group oversaw matters, ensuring appropriate and neutral oversight of the research. The reading tests and questionnaires were scrutinized by language teachers and school principals who examined the effects of having used either Cantonese or Putonghua as the MoI in their school. Also gathered were details of enrolment and school characteristics, average class sizes, the MoI employed, the resources available and instructional time allocated on the weekly timetable. The validity of all such responses was verified by the teacher focus group. Attention was also directed towards observing the impact of the "reading across the curriculum" innovation (where pertinent) on students' bilingual reading performance. For example, the questionnaire asked whether the school concerned was using Chinese and English reading across the formal curriculum and whether equal numbers of the students examined had been taught in Chinese and in English. School principals and teachers were also asked whether they were seeking to promote reading in Chinese and English across all subjects rather than confining usage to selected subjects on the curriculum. To obtain a more complete picture, the questionnaire also gathered information about the students’ reading habits at home, their self-concepts as readers, their attitudes towards reading and the extent to which their parents used English and Chinese in their leisure time at home.

753712.label: Major findings and research outcome
753712.value: Statistical analyses of the students’ assessment revealed that the Hong Kong students’ mother tongue reading literacy was far beyond the average L1 reading performance level in most countries. For English proficiency, the Hong Kong students obtained a mean of 413 (SD = 78). Some 15.6% of the students exceeded the international mean total score of 500. In other words, the English reading proficiency of these students’ was judged to be equivalent to that of students with English as their mother tongue. Comparatively, the Hong Kong students’ average English reading literacy score was approximately equivalent to a score of 75% of the level on the parallel Chinese reading literacy scale (Chinese mean raw score: 549; English mean raw score: 413). Regarding the effects on students’ reading prowess in using Cantonese and/or Putonghua as MoI, the researchers found that no statistically significant differences in performance across the five modes of MoI used in Chinese lessons (F = 2.155, df = 2126, p = 0.072) were found in analysis of variance analyses. No evidence was found to suggest that using Putonghua as the MoI had had any noticeable beneficial or negative impact on the students’ Chinese reading literacy. To investigate the impact on Chinese and English reading proficiency of implementing differing “reading across the curriculum” policies, questionnaires were distributed both to Chinese and English language teachers. Analyses showed that over half of the Chinese (50.6%) and English (65.9%) teachers adopted the mode of teaching reading as a standalone subject, and about 10% of teachers (10.4% Chinese teachers; 7.3% English teachers) taught reading using a cross-curricular approach. No statistical evidence was found that the students receiving a “reading across the curriculum” experience outperformed the others. The results might perhaps imply that neither the Chinese nor the English teachers had had extensive experience of teaching in Chinese or in English across the curriculum. Looking at the affective attributes of students, the research found that, although many students had only modest reading motivation, they nevertheless performed fairly well on the reading measures. The following impressions gathered from the socially Hong Kong context, were that (a) Hong Kong parents had quite high expectations of their children’s educational attainment; (b) Hong Kong schools strongly encourage parents to take some responsibility for monitoring students' homework; (c) Hong Kong schools provide students with a supportive learning environment and staff communicate frequently with parents about the children's educational progress and achievements.

753712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
753712.value: A proposed study for 2016 has been submitted to the RGC GRF. With a grant from the RGC, the 2016 study will be Phase 4 in the sequence of surveys, and will continue to measure trends and patterns in children's bilingual reading literacy attainment. It will also survey factors such as policy and practice changes and look closely at issues surfacing in the preceding three surveys. The study will continue to investigate the effects of using Cantonese or Putonghua as the MoI on literacy standards. As the primary school curriculum now witnesses more self-directed learning in students’ reading performance in Chinese and English, the proposed research will also explore this innovatory learning approach initiated by the EDB.

753712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
753712.value: The bilingual reading ability of Hong Kong students continues to be a concern of the Government, parents and schools. The accurate monitoring of students’ literacy attainment is hence important, and this third round of research will monitor the bilingual reading attainment of Primary 4 students; the influence on performance of the MoI used in the children’s school; and the impact of the "reading across the curriculum" initiative on reading prowess. As before, the research will employ quantitative and qualitative measures, including children’s reading comprehension of reading material in Chinese and in English. The views of the children, their parents and teachers will be gathered, the research being overseen by n independent teacher focus group. The data be analyzed in order to obtain a picture of students’ literacy prowess and factors influencing performance, what is happening in school and how parents can help at home.

753812.value: 知覺組織與注意力搜尋

753812.label: Project Objectives
753812.value: To identify how perceptual organization prioritizes attention in a search task reflected in both visual and motor selection mechanisms by tracking observers’ eye movements and manual response times. (Experiment series 1) To characterize the limitations and constraints imposed on the attentional search with perceptual organization in both spatial and temporal dimensions. (Experiment series 2) To psychophysically clarify the possible locus for attentional modulation of perceptual grouping. (Experiment series 3) To formalize the development of a biologically plausible computational model that shows the relation between attention and perceptual grouping. (Experiments 3, 4)

To characterize the limitations and constraints imposed on the attentional search with perceptual organization in both spatial and temporal dimensions. (Experiment series 2)
To psychophysically clarify the possible locus for attentional modulation of perceptual grouping. (Experiment series 3)
To formalize the development of a biologically plausible computational model that shows the relation between attention and perceptual grouping. (Experiments 3, 4)

753812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
753812.value: We survive and thrive by interacting with the world in a timely and appropriate manner. For example, at an airport pilots monitor their planes’ control buttons for a safe landing, security officers scan X-ray monitors for threatening items; travelers look for their luggage on a belt, and lovers search each other’s faces to plant a goodbye kiss. In these scenarios, attention plays a vital role in selecting the most important information to guide their actions. Any miscalculation or misjudgment could lead to unthinkable consequences. The practical and theoretical importance of how attention guides visual search has attracted psychologists for decades, yet we are still far from having a complete picture. One of the unanswered questions we want to investigate in this research proposal is how attention is directed by the relation between parts of a scene (perceptual grouping). Most objects are comprised of multiple parts, e.g. a cat has a head, body, tail, and ears. Although these parts are distinctive and easily separable, we effortlessly combine them into a whole (cat) because they usually move in the same direction (common motion/fate). This property of our minds saves us from having to process the movements of each individual part separately, and it changes how our minds selectively attend to and prioritize information when searching a scene. However, most attention models have overlooked this. We propose to address this neglect by examining how the law of continuity (co-linearity) modulates our selective attention in visual search. To do this we use a search task with a distractor involving elements which comply for their salience with the law of continuity. We have previously found that when a target is grouped with elements supporting good continuity, the target search is harder than when it is not ie perceptual grouping of elements interferes with rather than enhances the search task. This result is opposite to what current attention models predict. We plan to examine the causes of this interference through a series of experiments which (a) examine eye movements (Series 1), define the conditions whereby organizational continuity works (Series 2), identify their relation to other components in existing attention models (Series 3), and explore the possibility of generalizing the observations to other perceptual laws (Series 4). We expect our results to provide support for a more complete theory of attention based upon perceptual grouping. 知覺組織與注意力搜尋 視覺搜尋與我們的日常生活息息相關。從在放學的孩童中尋找自己的孩子，在家中找尋鑰匙，到機場安檢人員搜尋危安行李，或是醫檢人員從 X-光片中搜尋可能的腫瘤，都需要注意力先將可能範圍縮小，再進行分析。在各種情況下，若市搜尋作業失敗，都有各種不可預期的堪慮後果，因而心理學家在過去幾十年中，無不竭盡心力想要了解注意力搜尋的機制，但離能夠關詳其全貌，仍有一段距離。 本研究所探討的問題是注意力如何被知覺組織影響。大部分的世間物體都由好幾個部件組成，比方說，貓可以被分為頭，頸，身，腿，尾等明顯的部分，但是我們在觀察一隻貓的活動的時候，很自然的以整體的角度去觀察，這是因為各個部分雖然明易區分，卻有著共同的運動速度與方向，因而引導了注意力以”整體”作為處理的單位，目前的注意力模型中卻對 “整體”與”部件”的討論明顯缺乏。 本研究使用研究室的簡單線條刺激，探討知覺上靠著 “連續性” 而造成的 “整體” 如何影響視覺注意力搜索。我們計畫利用眼動儀，知覺模型，與心理物理學方法討論知覺組織如何與視覺注意力交互影響。

753812.label: Major findings and research outcome
753812.value: Major findings: We have established from short-latency saccades that a long collinear distractor reduces the perceptual salience of the target, a factor which poses a counter-intuitive condition in which a target on a salient region becomes less salient. With binocular fusion and continuous flash suppression, we narrow down the possible neural locus to early visual cortext (V1). Further, the boundary conditions we have established suggest this search impairment requires collinear grouping resides in region with high local contrast. These are important elements to be considered in a future model. Research outcome: Chow, H.M., Jingling, L., *Tseng, C.H., (2013) Collinear integration affects visual search at V1. 753812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
753812.value: The rich visual worlds are comprised of multiple parts, and we effortlessly combine them into a whole perception and changes how our minds selectively attend to and prioritize information. In this study, we focus on how one factor that is commonly use for visual scene organization (collinear grouping) to modulate our attention. We used a visual search task in which observers are instructed to look for a small oblique bar overlapping on a structure organized by collinear bars, or non-collinear bars. We found out the structural organization is a key factor that could faciliate or inhibit human performance to detect the small oblique slant target. To this end, we have define the limitation and constraints of how attention is manipulated, and identify possible brain sites that carry out this calculation. Further more, we also arrive the conclusion that this is a very influential factor for our attentional deployment that requires further investigation.

754312.label: Project Title(Chinese)
754312.value: 會計盈餘相關的資訊風險是如何影響權益價值的? 根據封閉式基金折扣得到的證據

754312.label: Co - Investigator(s)
754312.value: Prof Chen, Feng Prof Hope, Ole-Kristian Prof Li, Qingyuan

754312.label: Project Objectives
754312.value: To examine whether information risk associated with accounting earnings affects U.S. investors’ valuation of equities in international markets. To study how the impacts of earnings opacity on equity value vary with investors’ information acquisition costs. To show that closed-end fund discounts are affected by the firm characteristics of the underlying firms in the fund holdings as evidenced by the underlying firms’ financial disclosure quality.
rows: To examine whether information risk associated with accounting earnings affects U.S. investors’ valuation of equities in international markets.
To study how the impacts of earnings opacity on equity value vary with investors’ information acquisition costs.
To show that closed-end fund discounts are affected by the firm characteristics of the underlying firms in the fund holdings as evidenced by the underlying firms’ financial disclosure quality.

754312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
754312.value: We propose to examine the impact of information risk on equity value by documenting the correlation between the closed-end fund discounts and the fund-level earnings opacity. Closed-end funds have two sets of prices for the same underlying assets: the net asset value (NAV), which is based on the stock prices of the firms in funds' holdings and therefore is set by the investors of the underlying firms; and the fund price, which is set by the fund investors on U.S. stock exchanges. If the fund investors and the investors of the underlying firms react differently to the information risk associated with accounting earnings disclosed by the underlying firms, we will observe a correlation between our earnings-based proxy for information asymmetry (i.e., the fund-level earnings opacity) and the fund discounts (i.e., the extent to which fund prices are less than the net asset values of the funds). In our proposed project, we focus on the Closed-end Country Funds (CCFs) which invest in listed firms in a single foreign country. For these CCFs, the fund investors are U.S. investors on U.S. stock exchanges and the investors of the underlying firms are domestic investors in foreign stock markets. Compared with local investors, U.S. investors face a higher level of uncertainty about foreign firms’ future cash flows and higher costs to overcome these uncertainties. Faced with an additional information acquisition cost, U.S. investors could set a lower price for the fund as a demand for price protection against the uncertainty caused by the poor financial disclosure of foreign firms. Therefore, we hypothesize a positive correlation between the closed-end country fund discount and our proxy for information asymmetry, the earnings opacity of the underlying firms in the fund portfolio. This positive correlation would be consistent with information risk being priced by investors of the closed-end country funds. We further propose to examine whether the hypothesized correlation is mitigated for funds with more U.S. cross-listings, with underlying firms following accounting standards similar to U.S. GAAP, with a higher level of institutional ownership, and with a higher percentage of underlying firms being audited by the Big 4 audit firms. 在本研究中我們通過考察封閉式基金折扣和企業盈餘不透明性之間的關係,來驗證資訊風險對權益價值的影響。封閉式基金的特點是對同一個資產有兩個價格。一個價格是基金的資產淨值; 它是根據基金組合中各家公司的股票價格來計算的。另一個價格是基金本身的股票的價格; 它是由基金股票的買賣雙方決定的。兩個價格的不同就會導致基金的折扣(或者基金溢價)。如果基金的投資者和各家公司股票的投資者對公司盈餘透明度所導致的資訊風險的反應不一樣的話, 我們預期會看到公司盈餘透明度 (根據基金組合中的公司來計算出一個綜合的指標) 和封閉式基金折扣之間存在顯著的相關性。 我們著重研究封閉式跨國基金。這些基金主要投資于非美國的企業, 而基金本身的股票卻是在美國交易所買賣。因此,基金股票的投資者主要是美國投資者,而基金組合中的國外企業的股票買賣主要是由國外投資者進行。相對於那些在本國市場上買賣本國企業股票的當地投資者, 美國的基金投資者對當地企業的未來的業績預測面臨著更大程度的不確定性, 並且需要付出更高的成本去克服這些不確定因素。既然美國投資者需要付出更大的代價去獲得當地企業的資訊, 當這些海外企業會計披露比較差的時候, 美國投資者就會給基金的股份一個比基金淨值更低的價格以作為他們所要求的價格保護。所以, 在我們的研究假設中, 基金折扣應該是跟基金組合中上市公司的盈餘模糊程度存在正相關關係的。這種正相關反映了基金投資者對資訊風險的定價。我們進一步研究是否這種正相關關係會被削弱, 當基金持有更多的在美國跨市場上市的外國企業; 當這些國外企業的會計準則跟接近美國的會計準則; 當基金的投資者中有更高比例的機構投資者; 以及當這些國外企業的審計師有更高比例的四大會計師事務所。

754312.label: Realisation of objectives
754312.value: I am very happy to report that we successfully achieved all the project objectives. Specifically, in one of the output papers, “Earnings Opacity and Closed-End Country Fund Discounts", we show the evidence that the difference between the fund’s NAV and its trading price (i.e., the fund discount) is positively associated with the earnings opacity of the underlying companies. This finding supports our objective #1. In addition, consistent with the notion that the impact of earnings opacity is smaller when investors' acquisition cost is lower, we find that such a positive is weaker for those funds with more U.S. cross-listings in fund holdings, with underlying companies following financial reporting standards similar to U.S. standards, and with less segmented local markets. These findings pertain to the #2 project objective. In another output paper, "Flight to Quality in International Markets: Political Uncertainty and Investors’ Demand for Financial Reporting Quality," we find that mutual-fund managers shift their equity holdings to stocks with higher financial reporting quality during election periods when political uncertainty is higher. Such a flight-to-quality effect is less pronounced for countries with higher transactions costs. These findings help to achieve the objectives #1 and #2. In summary, both papers support the #3 objective of this project: the characteristics of underlying firms in a fund portfolio affect this fund's valuation and the fund managers' investment decisions.

754312.label: Major findings and research outcome
754312.value: I am very happy to report that we successfully published two papers in the world-leading journals: (1) "Flight to Quality in International Markets: Political Uncertainty and Investors’ Demand for Financial Reporting Quality.", Forthcoming in Contemporary Accounting Research (CAR). The main findings are: We employ national elections as exogenous increases in systematic risk in the local markets and accordingly use an international sample of mutual funds that focus on local markets. We find that mutual-fund managers shift their equity holdings to stocks with higher financial reporting quality during election periods when political uncertainty is higher. Such a flight-to-quality effect is less pronounced for elections with larger expected electoral margins in the pre-election period (i.e., when the incumbent is more likely to win the election) and for countries with higher transactions costs. In contrast, the effect is more pronounced when governments have greater involvement in the local economy. (2) “Earnings Opacity and Closed-End Country Fund Discounts". Forthcoming in Journal of Accounting, Auditing and Finance (JAAF). The main findings are: we find that the difference between the fund’s NAV and its trading price (i.e., the fund discount) is positively associated with the earnings opacity of the underlying companies. Such a positive association is consistent with the notion that U.S. investors face higher information acquisition and processing costs when compared with local investors, and therefore earnings opacity exacerbates the information disadvantage of U.S. investors, leading to a larger fund discount. We further show that the positive relation varies predictably with U.S. investors’ information acquisition and processing costs and with the extent to which host stock markets are segmented from the U.S. market. Specifically, we find that the positive relation between earnings opacity and fund discounts is weaker for those funds with more U.S. cross-listings in fund holdings, with underlying companies following financial reporting standards similar to U.S. standards, and with less segmented local markets.

754312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
754312.value: We find that mutual fund managers shift towards high-earnings quality stocks when the political risk is higher. An interesting question is who trades against the mutual-fund managers during various market uncertainty events. According to Ben-Rephael (2014), when fund managers tend to flight-to-liquidity during market crises, longer-horizon institutional investors actually take the opposite trades. Similarly, it is possible that equity funds without immediate redemption concerns would hold opaque assets in high uncertainty periods. This would be an interesting area for future research.

754312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
754312.value: Our research project aims to provide the evidence on how the firms' reporting quality (FRQ) affects the value of funds' portfolios and in turn how it affects fund managers' investment decisions. Our findings suggest that lower FRQ of underlying firms in a fund portfolio has a negative impact on the value of such a portfolio. Accordingly, fund managers avoid investing in the low-FRQ stocks when they facing a high level of market uncertainty. Our studies provide insights into the fund managers' investment behaviors.

754412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
754412.value: How do undergraduates learn expert words in their academic discipline when the words are taught in a non-native language? It is a challenge for undergraduates in Hong Kong to achieve expertise in professional life when the language of learning is not native. This project will investigate the cognitive processes that are used to learn expert words when words are taught in a non-native language (English). The method will be based on techniques used in experimental psychology that are designed to test predictions derived from theories of new word learning. Studies of expert word learning in native language learners show intensive exposure to expert words during study does not necessarily lead to faster or more accurate spoken word recognition. Expert words remain slower to recognise than words that are acquired early in life. The reason why expert words do not benefit from repeated exposure is an open question. One question that has not yet been explored is whether individual differences in cognitive processes such as verbal short term memory, attention and cognitive control explain the ability to learn expert words. The proposed study will answer this question. A unique feature of the study is that expert word learning will be examined in Chinese speaking students who are naïve about English expert words when they begin to study. Furthermore, as Chinese and English have distinct vocabularies with no overlap in sound or word structure, it will be possible to control for familiarity with expert words in each group prior to instruction. This methodological control is not possible in studies of expert word learning in a native language. The study will test 120 students from the University of Hong Kong who are all learning an expert vocabulary in a Problem Based Learning (PBL) environment. Participants will therefore be relatively homogenous in the pedagogical method used and the motivation of the students to learn new expert words in English. The project will add to what is known about the cognitive processes used to acquire an expert vocabulary in a second language. The outcomes include a novel methodological and theoretical contribution to the field of expert word learning as well as practical implications for teaching expert words in native and non-native languages. The study is relevant to understanding higher education in Hong Kong and to all other learning environments where expert words are taught in English.

754412.label: Realisation of objectives
754412.value: The first objective has been met following three experiments with over 100 undergraduates giving a large enough sample size to draw some theoretical conclusions. Understanding the cognitive processes that are used to learn new words is based on well-established theories of verbal short-term memory (STM). These theories assume that learning new words in either the native or the non-native language requires a mechanism for rehearsing and storing words. The serial memory hypothesis predicts serial order memory capacity will have a significant effect on the ability to acquire expert words in naïve learners. One test of this hypothesis is whether the capacity of serial order memory to predict expert word learning is independent of other processes such as attention and cognitive control, factors that also contribute to new word learning in bilingual speakers. We tested the serial memory hypothesis in languages that are linguistically distant (Chinese and English) so as to minimise the effect of extant vocabulary on new word learning while at the same time controlling for individual differences in the exposure to expert words, learning environment and motivation. We found that serial order memory capacity independently predicts the acquisition of expert words in two cohorts of undergraduates, and the total variance accounted for in expert word learning by this variable is 60%. Significant positive correlations were found between the overall expert word learning scores and several measures of STM including serial order STM (r = .52, p < .01), digit span (r = .50, p < .01) and word span (r = .45, p = .02), though not for nonword span (r = .36, p = .06). There was a negative pattern of correlations between Stroop performance (a measure of attentional control) and serial order STM, and between Stroop and digit span (both rs = -.29, ps = .13). However, there was no significant correlation found in attentional measures with overall expert word learning scores (Stroop: r = -.25, p = .21, Flanker: r < .01, p = .99). A significant positive correlation emerged between English language vocabulary (BPVS) and expert word learning scores (r = .51, p < .001). In addition, the number of hours exposed to academic materials was also significantly linked with the overall word learning scores (r = .55, p < .001). The regression shows that both serial order STM and number of hours exposed to academic materials significantly, simultaneously and independently predict expert word learning performance (using a measure of number of new words learned over a six month period)), with serial order STM being the strongest predictor (β= .60, p < .001) followed by the amount of exposure to academic materials (β= .39, p < .01). No other significant predictor emerged in the model despite inclusion of over a dozen other variables. A one year follow up of maintenance of expert word learning using a writing to dictation task found a different pattern of results however. Two sets of multiple regression analyses were conducted to investigate the predictive power of the two measures of expert word acquisition. Given one aim of the study was to investigate the roles of STM and attentional control in long term expert word learning (maintenance), both of the significant STM measures (serial order reconstruction and delayed nonword repetition) predicting expert word acquisition and attentional control measures (verbal Stroop and Flanker effects) were included in a regression model predicting writing expert words to dictation after twelve months. Regression analysis showed that measures of IQ specifically performance on Raven’s progressive matrices (β = .48, p < .05) and overall Stroop effect (β = .42, p < .05) had significant predictive effects on writing-to-dictation expert words but no variables predicted expert word (lexical decision) after twelve months. The results suggest writing-to-dictation measures are most sensitive to measuring vocabulary maintenance perhaps more than lexical decision although performance on the latter task was at ceiling. The results have implications for theories of expert vocabulary acquisition in bilingual speakers because both serial order memory capacity and attentional control impact on expert word learning. One methodological problem with studies of expert word learning in a native language is difficulty controlling for pre-instruction familiarity with expert words either directly or indirectly i.e. via knowledge of synonyms. The project avoids this methodological problem by examining the trajectory of new word learning in naïve participants - i.e. Chinese speaking students who are learning expert words in a second language (English). As Chinese and English have distinct vocabularies with no overlap in sound or word structure, it is straightforward to control for familiarity with expert words across participants. Therefore one long term impact of the project is that we can offer a new cognitive explanations of expert word learning in bilingual speakers. The broader long term impact is for development of theoretical models in the domain of science of learning (specifically language and memory) in monolingual speakers. Another outcome of the project is a database of over one hundred expert words for health sciences that can be used to teach students in allied health professions. This database will be published in a single authored forthcoming paper in press in Bilingualism: Language and Cognition. The second long term outcome of the project will be better knowledge about the methods of instruction in a non-native language at the tertiary level based on evidence from undergraduates with similar language profiles and demographic backgrounds. It is necessary for all undergraduates to acquire expert vocabularies that define their profession. Although learning expert words does not make the learner an expert per se, knowledge of expert words is essential to understand key discipline specific concepts, to RGC Ref No.c01522 Page 4 GRF1 communicate in professional life and to maintain life-long learning after graduation. An important challenge for students in Hong Kong is that the language of instruction is typically English – the lingua franca of professional communication locally and globally. The results of the project will reveal the trajectory of expert word acquisition in different academic disciplines that form the core learning environments at the tertiary level in Hong Kong. The value of this knowledge base lies in the fact that traditional measures of vocabulary knowledge in English (for example examination performance) are not sufficient to ensure the acquisition of an expert vocabulary. The immediate application for learning and teaching will be the development of a glossary of expert terms that will be made freely available to all tertiary institutions in Hong Kong. By the end of the project, we will have isolated the cognitive mechanisms that best predict expert word learning in first year undergraduates over the first two years of the degree. In the very long term the results will lay the foundation for a cognitive neuro-scientific model of expert word learning that can be tested using brain-imaging methods in our future research projects.

754412.label: Major findings and research outcome
754412.value: The results support studies showing a correlation between memory for serial order and new word learning in bilingual adults (Majerus et al., 2008) and developmental studies showing an association between capacity of serial order memory and vocabulary development in young children (Majerus, Poncelet, Greffe et al., 2006). The study shows for the first time that serial order STM predicts expert word learning in a second language in bilingual Cantonese-English speaking adults. The findings can be understood by the model of vocabulary acquisition proposed by Gupta (2003), which assumes that serial order STM is essential during language acquisition. Serial order STM allows for activation and rehearsal of sequences of phonemes, and hence increases the chance of forming a stable and accurate long-term lexical and phonological representation for long term storage. Burgess and Hitch (2005) also proposed an account of serial order and new learning on the basis of a Hebbian adjustment of long term connection weights between serial order STM system and the language network, which includes lexical and sublexical language systems. The lexical system stores familiar word forms and the sublexical system stores phonological information. When a new word is presented for learning, a new lexical node is formed in the lexical system, while phonemes are activated in the sublexical system. STM system encodes and temporarily stores the order of phonemes in the sublexical system simultaneously, allowing the rehearsal of phoneme order in the language network and thus helps to build up a stable long term phonological representation of words (Burgess & Hitch, 2005). Both models explain the present findings by pointing out the assumed relationship between memory for serial order and the language network in new word learning. These models do not however take a strong view on the role of attention in new word learning and maintenance. The results show that attentional control is important for both processes. In the initial stage of acquisition, performance on attentional control tasks made a unique contribution to new learning adding to the role of serial order memory and the two processes are independent predictors of expert word learning. By contrast, only attentional control predicts long term maintenance after twelve months specifically on a task of lexical word retrieval (writing to dictation), a more demanding task. These results are compatible with a recent model of STM and verbal learning developed by Majerus (2013).

754412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
754412.value: There is a possible source of error in the tests measuring expert word learning. First, the results of the test in Phase 1 (supposed to serve as our baseline) suggest that participants had known some target words by the time they were initially tested. Second, the learning time period between Phase 1 and Phase 2 data collection was short (about two months). Although there was significant improvement in Phase 2 compared to Phase 1 across participants, improvement was relatively small (under 10%). The expert word learning measure was thus not sensitive. Another limitation of this study is sample size (n= 128) was small and non-significant results are difficult to interpret. The novel findings of a role for attentional control in expert word learning need to be replicated. Moreover, the RT measure in the lexical decision task was significantly and negatively correlated with expert word learning. A diffusion model analysis of RT distributions is needed based on more data. Future studies can investigate attentional control, STM measures, and learning of L2 expert words in bilingual speakers using neurolinguistic methods. Relationships between existing vocabulary knowledge in L1 and L2 with observed expert word learning in L2 is an area to explore in future.

754412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
754412.value: Past research has shown a strong association between phonological short-term memory (STM) and vocabulary learning in first (L1) and second (L2) language. Recent studies are also suggestive of a role for attention in vocabulary learning. This study examined the role of memory for serial order and attentional control in the learning of English expert words among Cantonese native speakers. Participants were freshman students at the University of Hong Kong. There were 2 phases of data collection. In Phase 1, expert word learning (via a lexical decision task), attentional control, verbal STM, general cognitive ability, visuo-spatial memory, and general language knowledge were assessed. In Phase 2, expert word learning was re-assessed. The results indicated that serial order memory was the strongest predictor of L2 expert word learning followed by the number of hours exposed to academic materials. Suggestive associations were also observed between attentional control and short term memory measures and between attentional control and a measure of word learning. The results highlight the importance of both attention, memory and frequency of exposure in learning expert words. These results have implications for pedagogy and for theoretical models of verbal learning in a bilingual language environment that characterises the University of Hong Kong.

754912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
754912.value: The percentage of Internet users in China has increased from 8.5% in 2005 to 36.2% in 2011. Shanghai has reached 64.5% in the proportion of Internet users among its population in 2010. In an increasingly digitally-connected society, access to the Internet for all is a great challenge for most countries. However, little is known about the challenges in relation to the divide between those who have Internet access and those who have not in China. The divide presents a challenge in social exclusion, and it hinders the disadvantaged groups in accessing better and timely services enabled by the Internet, a technology which could greatly improve their well-being and participation in society. The digital divide experienced by children in low-income families poses very serious threat to social development. In more resourceful countries, explicit policy measures are in place to ensure full Internet access for school age students. Without bridging the digital divide, it will greatly limit the learning opportunities and outcome of children in low-income families and exacerbates the risks of intergenerational transmission of poverty. Another indirect consequence of the digital divide that hinders the Internet access of children in low-income families is their parent’s inadequate Internet knowledge and negative perception about the Internet. Some hesitate to install computer and Internet access, which are expensive items for them, at home. Even when there is Internet access at home, without parents’ proper guidance, and involvement, children would easily be attracted to games, social media, and entertainments. This creates tensions and frustrations between parents and children when parents attempt to direct their children’s attention to their studies. The tensions might actually ruin the purpose of helping children to benefit from the use of the Internet as children react negatively to the demands and control of parents. This study will conduct the first ever comprehensive measure of digital divide among low-income families in Shanghai, and investigate the educational and social implication for them. Representative samples of low-income and ordinary households with children (10-17) will be obtained and interviews will be conducted with the children and their parents. This study will unveil the little-known parental factors and within family dynamics that exacerbate the effect of digital divide among children in low-income families in their educational and social outcome in Shanghai, and identify policy options that could effectively address the problem in Shanghai, and eventually in other parts of China. 中國的互聯網使用者由2005年的8.5%增加至2011年的36.2%。上海市作為一個在多個社會及經濟領域均處於領導地位的中國城市，互聯網使用在2010年時已佔人口的64.5%。 在這日益透過互聯網達至緊密連繫的世界，中國和其他很多國家都面對同一挑戰：即如何讓所有人都能上網。不過，目前對中國因數碼隔膜而未能上網的人士仍然所知甚少。數碼隔膜會造成社會排斥，而且阻礙弱勢社群利用互聯網使用更佳及更適時的服務以改善他們的生活和獲得更多參與社會的機會。怟收入家庭兒童面臨的數碼隔膜，更會對整體社會發展造成嚴重的後果。很多較富裕的國家/地區都有明確的政策措施以助學童上網。若非如此，低收入家庭兒童的學習機會及成效便會受損，更會進一步增加跨代貧窮的風險。 數碼隔膜對低收入家庭兒童的影響亦會因其家長欠缺上網知識和負面觀感間接造成。部份家長對在家中安裝上網有所犹豫，特別是當有關費用對家庭開支造成壓力。就算家中可以上網，又會因缺乏父母適當的管教及參與，兒童多會上網作遊戲及娛樂用途。當父母想指導子女多上網做功課學習時，便會很容易造成緊張氣氛、挫折感及反效果。 本研究旨在量度上海的數碼隔膜情況及了解其對低收入家庭兒童的影響。同時，亦會探討父母及有關家庭因素對子女使用彑聯網學習中的角色和效果。我們會在上海抽取具代表性的一般兒童和低收入兒童 (10-17歲) 的樣本，並會訪問有關兒童和家長。

754912.label: Realisation of objectives
754912.value: A multi-stage sampling procedure was applied to obtain a representative sample of ordinary families and low-income households with children aged 9-17 in Shanghai. Interviews were conducted with both the children and their parents in each sampled household. Questionnaires for parents and children were designed respectively. A valid sample of 796 low-income households and 799 non-low-income households was obtained. The proportions of low-income households and households on social assistance programme (dibao) were over-represented in the sample. Post-stratified weighting based on urban-rural districts and income level was applied to obtain representation of the overall population of households with children aged 9-17 in Shanghai. The data collected were sufficient enough to address the research questions. Three conference presentations were made (one of them being a keynote presentation), and two articles were published in internationally refereed journal article. Six focus group interviews were conducted with children and parents of low-income families with and without computer separately. The information collected helped to obtain insights regarding the study to triangulate the findings from the quantitative data. The focus group interviews also provide us information regarding policy measures of the local governments to address digital divide (though the government has done very little to address the issue). Thus far, the study team is focusing on the data collected regarding Shanghai. The comparison between Hong Kong (objective 5) has just started. Since we have collected data regarding the situation in Hong Kong in 2010, and data (N = 1530) of a more recent study regarding the use of Internet/Smartphone among secondary school students in Hong Kong has just been collected, a very comprehensive comparison could be completed in the coming months.

754912.label: Major findings and research outcome
754912.value: Our findings indicated that about 20% of the children from low-income families had no Internet connection at home compared with only 5% among those from non low-income families. There was an even more obvious gap in smartphone usage too. The findings suggest that the digital divide for low-income children in Shanghai is getting smaller or even closing, but the urban-rural divide might be a factor in aggravating digital exclusion. Low-income-no-Internet children reported significantly lower scores on all dimensions of digital literacy, academic performance, aspirations, perceived efficacy, self-esteem, family and peer relationships. On the contrary, low-income children with Internet access did not show significant differences with non-low-income group across all dimensions. Whilst we cannot conclude that there is a direct relationship between Internet access and improved developmental outcomes, the strength of the association suggests that there may be value in efforts being focused on assisting families in the lowest income strata, and on agricultural household registration, to acquire home Internet access. In examining the methods used by Shanghai parents in supervising children’s Internet use, the confidence of parents in helping children to benefit from the Internet and protect them from possible threats, and the factors affecting parents’ confidence in their parenting practices, the findings show that Shanghai parents used restriction most frequently in internet supervision. More than one-fifth of parents had limited confidence in helping their children benefit from the Internet and one-eighth in protecting their children from possible Internet threats. Multiple regression models show that better Internet knowledge, an authoritative parenting style, more involvement in children’s online activities and a positive attitude towards the Internet are factors which were associated with higher parenting confidence in internet supervision. Findings also suggest that efforts in assisting parents review their attitude towards the Internet and learn new supervision methods are important, especially for parents on the lower socio-economic strata.

754912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
754912.value: With the lowering price of computer access and equipment, we can envisage that digital divide in terms of home Internet access in major urban centres, like Hong Kong and Shanghai is fast diminishing. Future studies should focus on second or third tier cities/towns and even rural areas to see if they are making similar progress. In very recent years, smartphone and handheld devices with Internet access has become more common among school children. Our recent finding in Hong Kong shows that handheld devices such as smartphone and tablets have become the primary equipment for Internet access among girls (boys still use desktop or notebook computers as their primary devices for Internet access). Unless desktop or notebook computers, supervising children using handheld devices are even more challenging. Studying the impact of using these new devices to family and parenting methods and relationships are important to inform frontline practices.

754912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
754912.value: This study explored the issue of the digital divide in Shanghai with particular attention to children from low-income families. It examined whether a difference in the Internet access of children was associated with their academic and psychosocial attributes. Data were collected in 2013/14 from a household survey with a representative sample of about 800 each from low-income and non-low-income families with children aged 9-17. About 20% of the children from low-income families had no Internet connection at home compared with only 5% among those from non low-income families. There was an even more obvious gap in smartphone usage too. Our findings suggest that the digital divide for low-income children in Shanghai is getting smaller or even closing, but the urban-rural divide might be a factor in aggravating digital exclusion. Preliminary group comparisons show that low-income-no-Internet children reported significantly lower scores on all dimensions of digital literacy, academic performance, aspirations, perceived efficacy, self-esteem, family and peer relationships. On the contrary, low-income children with Internet access did not show significant differences with non-low-income group across all dimensions. Whilst we cannot conclude that there is a direct relationship between Internet access and improved developmental outcomes, the strength of the association suggests that there may be value in efforts being focused on assisting families in the lowest income strata, and on agricultural household registration, to acquire home Internet access.

755612.label: Project Objectives
755612.value: In this project, we continue searching for measures of oil shocks that are priced across financial markets. Different definitions of exogenously specified shocks can lead to different model implications. We will compare these model implications with real data to find the best measure. We will investigate why oil inventory changes are significantly priced in the cross section of stocks but not changes in spot prices. This is our major research question. Both measures represent the scarcity of oil in our economy; and they are significantly correlated. We will also look at the cyclicality of oil shocks. The comovement of the shocks with business cycles determines their risk prices. We will study the integration of commodity futures and stock markets. Do oil futures and stocks comove? In particular, we hope to connect both oil futures premia and cross-sectional stock return spread to the same oil-related risks. We will relate real quantities with prices. When we sort stocks into portfolios by their exposures to oil inventory growth, this relates asset prices to macro quantities. In future research, we will look at oil spot and futures prices, oil producers' and users' stock returns as well as quantity data such as inventory, production, consumption, and reserves. A structural dynamic model to reconcile these data will be proposed.

756112.label: Project Title(Chinese)
756112.value: 「怪異」、「外族」與宋代中華文化身份的發展

756112.label: Project Objectives
756112.value: To demonstrate the cultural significance of Song dynasty writings through the examination of the parallels between their representation of monstrosity and society’s reception of foreignness. To demonstrate how the recurrent theme of monstrosity and its relationship with foreignness may reflect a larger social issue concerning the Han ethnicity’s germinating desire to reinterpret and reorient its sense of cultural identity according to the ideology of the self and otherness.
rows: To demonstrate the cultural significance of Song dynasty writings through the examination of the parallels between their representation of monstrosity and society’s reception of foreignness.

To demonstrate how the recurrent theme of monstrosity and its relationship with foreignness may reflect a larger social issue concerning the Han ethnicity’s germinating desire to reinterpret and reorient its sense of cultural identity according to the ideology of the self and otherness.

756112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
756112.value: This study considers the inseparable relationship between the development of the concept of cultural identity by the Han ethnic and their conceptualization of otherness during from the Song dynasty, and charts society’s changing perception of this relationship through the representation of monstrosity in literature. Monstrosity – a term I use throughout this project as incorporative of any beings or themes of supernaturalism, ranging from ghosts to animal spirits – is a concept that is conventionally associated with the strange writings (zhiguai 志怪) of the Six Dynasties period. By looking at the ways the connection between foreignness and monstrosity is supposed and represented in the early strange writings and how this idea evolved with different implications during the Song dynasty, this project considers the impact of society’s growing apprehension of foreignness on the way monstrosity is evoked by contemporary writers both before and after the fall of Kaifeng. More importantly, it aims to look into the set of ideologies that informs and dictates this literary trend and to correlate it to the development of the notion of cultural identity at this particular historical conjuncture. In many of the Song dynasty stories, for instance, it is possible to identify a characteristic tendency to relate monstrosity to foreignness and to present it as decadent and anarchic, which parallels society’s growing resistance to and apprehension of foreignness. By drawing on such examples, I hope to investigate the extent to which, as society’s perception of foreignness shifted from the Tang dynasty's model of acceptance and incorporation to abhorrence - as resulted from society's growing awareness of the threat of the barbarians from the north - the presentation of monstrosity in contemporary writings can be analyzed as reflective evidence of society’s reaction to the cultural and political milieu of the time. It is further hoped that the results can shed light on the influence of non-literary forces on the development of literature in the Song dynasty. By contextualizing the presentation of the trope of monstrosity in Song literature within the social desire to formulate a sense of cultural identity by the Han ethnic, I intend the importance of this study to lie in the foregrounding of the manifestation of the concept of cultural identity in China in the literary, as well as the proposition of its importance to our understanding of the cultural politics which occurred between the tenth and the thirteenth century. 中華文化身份的觀念起緣於宋代，與當時我者（self）和他（other）之概念的發展有着不可分割的關係。本計劃旨在研究以上關係，藉着析論社會如何透過文學作品中的「怪異」（monstrosity）主題，探討其對社會發展的一些影響。 本計劃把「怪異」一詞定義為任何有關超自然的生物或主題，包括鬼、神和各種各樣的動物精魂等。在認同這概念與六朝志怪小說一脈相承之餘，透過了解當時社會把「怪異」定位為「外族」（foreignness）的傳統，觀察這觀念在宋代社會的恐外情緒（xenophobia）下所產生的變化。隨著漢人對外國化的觀念就由唐代的包容轉至憎惡，文學作品表現「怪異」的方式，很大程度地反映了社會對當時的文化、政治環境的反響。本計劃冀望通過以上的研究，了解文化和社會因素對宋代文學發展的影響。

756312.label: Project Objectives
756312.value: to examine junior secondary school students’ connectedness to school and parents, purpose in life, and their relations to students’ academic, personal-social, and career life skills development; to examine relationships between level of implementation of guidance programs in schools, junior secondary students’ life skills development, connectedness, purpose in life, and characteristics of students (e.g., socioeconomic status; ability).

756312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
756312.value: 本研究是有關高小學生和高中生的生活技能發展研究的延展，重點對焦於初中生，通過質化與量化的方法收集資料，從而探索「人生目標」和「聯繫性」對學生生活技能發展的影響。是次研究結果將對輔導從業員和決策者在改善香港和世界其他地方中學生的輔導方案帶來具價值的參考。 2013至14學年標誌著香港實施3-3-4新學制及其相關輔導方案的第五個年頭。在此背景下，本研究有兩個主要目標：（1） 檢視初中生與他們學校和家長的聯繫性、人生目標，及此兩項變項與他們的學業、個人與社群和事業生活技能發展方面的關連作用;（2）檢視輔導方案在學校的實施水平、初中生的生活技能發展、聯繫性、人生目標和學生的特點（例如：社會經濟地位、能力），及各變項間的關係。 生活技能是促進學業進步、提升個人社交發展，以及協助籌劃事業的日常能力。家長的聯繫性是指兒童與他們父母的關連性，包括親密度、溝通、關注、支持、尊重和共情同感。學校的聯繫性可概念化為學生對他們教育環境包括依附、尊重、個人接納、支持和參與的從屬性。「人生目標」是通過超越自我積極為世界貢獻所追求的有意義事情的個人意圖。 本研究先以質化階段所得的資料建立研究概念及修飾初中生的大型調查問卷內容。訪問學生和教師則以焦點小組模式在三所中學進行。在主研究中，為確保具備各種能力和社會經濟地位學校的學生組群，我們將調查80所學校共約11,200名學生和640名教師。當中大約100名中一學生及100名中三學生將就他們的學業、個人與社群及其他生活技能、與教師、同輩和家長的聯繫性、人生目標，以及對學校實施輔導方案的看法接受問卷調查；而每所學校也有8位教師將就學校實施輔導方案填答問卷。有關的學生和教師將於12個月後再次接受類似的問卷調查，評估聯繫性、人生目標，以及輔導方案對各項生活技能發展的縱向影響。

756312.label: Realisation of objectives
756312.value: The objectives of the project were achieved successfully. From the main survey in 2013, the project team obtained data from 17,385 students in classes S.1 and S.3 from 79 secondary schools in Hong Kong. The project team also received questionnaires from 657 secondary school teachers and guidance personnel. Correlation and regression analysis were conducted to examine the relationship of the secondary students’ connectedness to parents, connectedness to school, connectedness to teachers, and connectedness to peers, their meaning and purpose in life, and students’efficacy in applying life skills in academic, personal-social, career and talent development. In the follow-up survey 2014, the project team collected additional data from students now in S.2 and S.4 who had participated in the main survey (when in S.1 and S.3). Although all participating schools in the main survey agreed to participate in the follow-up survey, some withdrew a year later for a variety of reasons not connected with the project. Finally, data from 10,808 students in S.2 and S.4 from 51 secondary schools were obtained. The project team also received questionnaires from 466 secondary teachers and guidance personnel. The researchers were able to match the main survey and follow-up survey data for 6496 students (2796 boys and 3657 girls; gender data missing on 43 students). Hierarchical linear modeling was conducted to examine the extent to which the level of implementation of the guidance program in schools is longitudinally related to students’ connectedness to parents, connectedness to school, connectedness to teachers, connectedness to peers, meaning and purpose in life, and self-efficacy in academic, personal, social and career and talent development, beyond the influence of students’ abilities and socioeconomic level. In addition, teacher and student focus group interviews were conducted in 3 secondary schools before the main survey and 3 schools after follow-up survey. The findings from the quantitative and qualitative data analyses were useful for the project team in understanding students’social connectedness, meaning and purpose in life, life skills development and the relations with the level of implementation of the guidance programs in Hong Kong junior secondary school students. Reports on the study have been sent to all participating schools and uploaded to project webpage. Seven papers on the findings have been presented in international conferences. Two international journal papers have been published. Three papers are under review and two other papers are in preparation.

756312.label: Major findings and research outcome
756312.value: Data from focus group discussion with students, teachers and guidance personnel from secondary schools indicated that students tend to interpret meaning in life in terms of its influence on future career path and life goals. High achievers tend to set goals for future achievement whereas goals of low achievers are more short-term. Formal guidance activities and informal interactions with teachers, schoolmates and professionals also enhance connectedness, promote meaning in life, and develop life skills (Yuen, Chung et al., under review). Teachers agreed that life goals are important for students. Creation of a caring culture in schools can make students feel valued, and can facilitate development of both connectedness and life skills. Schools must provide more supportive learning opportunities and resources to strengthen development of life skills (Yuen, Lee et al., in preparation). Quantitative data indicated evidence for validity and internal consistency of the Hemingway Measure of Adolescent Connectedness (Chinese Short Form), Life Skills Development Self- Efficacy Inventory and The Meaning in Life Questionnaire (Datu & Yuen, under review). Findings in the main survey indicated that peer connectedness, school connectedness, presence of meaning in life, and search of meaning in life are all associated significantly with students’self-efficacy in applying life skills (Yuen & Datu, under review). A follow-up survey with students indicated that presence of meaning in life, search for meaning in life and school connectedness at Time 1 are associated significantly with students’ level of self-confidence in applying life skills at Time 2 (Yuen, Datu et al., under review). Evidence for validity and reliability was obtained for an instrument to assess teachers’ perception of the level of implementation of guidance programs (Yuen, 2014 July). Teachers’ data also indicated that guidance and counseling activities are now being implemented in Hong Kong secondary schools to a reasonable extent (Yuen, 2014 November). Data from 10,808 Chinese adolescents in school years S.2 and S.4, and 462 teachers were analyzed using hierarchical linear modeling. Results indicated that after controlling for differences between schools (socioeconomic status and ability of student intake) the schools with stronger implementation of guidance curriculum, individual and group guidance at Time 1 had students who were more likely to report higher presence of meaning in life and connectedness to teachers at Time 2―but with no significant increase in life skills self-efficacy (Yuen, in preparation).

756312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
756312.value: It is also important to investigate further the possibility that deficits in life skills in the academic, career, personal and social domains may impede the formation of connectedness to parents, schools, peers and teachers as well as meaning and purpose in life. Future research might seek to investigate school students’actual application of life skills and efficacy more objectively through direct classroom observation and discussion with their teachers and parents. Future studies should examine more closely the association between life skills development, classroom social environment, and school characteristics. There is a need to conduct longitudinal research of sufficient duration to study the long-term effects of career and life planning, talent development and guidance programs in schools on students’academic, career, personal-social and talent development. A case-study approach in schools could be conducted to understand various factors contributing to the development, implementation, and evaluation of school guidance programs in the Hong Kong context. Parents, class-teachers and guidance professionals should work together to enhance students’meaning in life, social connectedness and to foster their self-efficacy in applying life skills.

756312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
756312.value: The project involved 17,385 junior secondary students (S.1 and S.3) in Hong Kong, and investigated relationships among the variables of meaning in life, connection with their parents, schools, teachers and peers, confidence in their own ability to apply life skills in academic, personal, social and career domains, and the level of implementation of guidance activities within their schools. Data were collected from students and their teachers by focus group meetings and survey questionnaires. A follow-up study with 10,808 students in S.2 and S.4 was conducted 12 months later. Additional focus group meetings with students and teachers were then held in another 3 secondary schools. Findings indicated that peer connectedness, school connectedness, meaning in life, and time spent in physical exercise are all associated significantly with students’ life skills self-efficacy. After differences between schools due to socioeconomic status and ability of student intake were controlled, schools with higher level of implementation of guidance curriculum, individual and group guidance had students who were more likely to report higher presence of meaning in life and connectedness to teachers. This was not reflected in greater confidence in applying life skills. Schools must strive to provide more supportive learning opportunities to strengthen students’ life skills development.

757412.label: Project Objectives
757412.value: The main objective of the project is to develop and validate the relationship between new governance principles and efficient coordination of post-humanitarian disaster health and nutrition relief efforts. In order to achieve this main objective, the project will conduct research as outlined below: • To elaborate on existing humanitarian response law and governance structures, to derive requirements that should be addressed by an inclusive local-global model of humanitarian governance, and to provide validation criteria (in terms of greater efficiency, flexibility, participation and timely coordination) that will inform the implementation of a new system of humanitarian response. • To articulate a functional model of effective humanitarian governance that will address the identified requirements. The functional model will be derived by comparing three typologies of post-disaster health and nutrition response programs: one state-led, the other multilateral and finally the third, a hybrid of state-civil-society collaboration. This comparison will also provide insights into how governments, civil society and international organizations effectively interact to achieve a global decentralized yet coordinated process of humanitarian assistance. • To determine what distinctive forms of local-global interaction lead to best practices in open-source humanitarian response. • To contribute to humanitarian law and new governance scholarship based on research findings.
