757412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
757412.value: As research on law and humanitarian aid has expanded in the last 30 years, findings have led to valuable insights into the influences, opportunities and constraints of humanitarian intervention following natural disasters. Efforts have been made in recent years by the United Nations (UN), the European Union (EU) and the International Law Commission (ILC) to develop a growing body of disaster response principles. Two major General Assembly resolutions have been passed: (1) An Agenda for Peace (A/RES/47/120[B]) and (2) Strengthening of the coordination of humanitarian emergency assistance of the United Nations (A/RES/46/182). The latter resolution created the position of the Emergency Relief Coordinator and the Inter-Agency Standing Committee, which has provided a foundation for international coordination of humanitarian response by multiple actors (Heintz & Zwitter, 2011). With growing awareness of the devastation wreaked by major natural disasters, alongside developments in information technology and regional and global integration of governance networks, the parameters of humanitarian aid are becoming more global. At the same time, recent experience has shown that the success of humanitarian aid efforts is ultimately measured by the extent to which local actors are effectively involved in decision making processes concerning relief efforts. Understanding the role of such emergent virtual and actual networks of states, international organizations, civil society groups and private sector actors in humanitarian post-natural disaster health and nutrition aid therefore requires a new understanding of the interplay between law, globalization and governance. Such an examination extends the discussion of new governance scholars to the peripheries of global decision-making, and responds to observations within analytic jurisprudence of the need for legal research to “broaden its focus not only geographically, but also in respect of the range of concepts, conceptual frameworks, and discourses it considers” (Twining, 2005). This research project seeks to advance our understanding of the interplay between law, governance and new forms of decision making to address health and nutrition post-disaster relief efforts. It will do this by comparing three typologies of networked humanitarian assistance programs: one state-led, the other multilateral and finally the third, a hybrid of state-civil-society collaboration in order to understand how such emergent networks offer insights into how governments, civil society, international organizations and local actors may effectively interact to achieve a global decentralized yet coordinated process of post-natural disaster health and nutrition humanitarian assistance. 在過去的30年裡, 關於法律和人道主義援助的研究不斷增加，而這些研究對自然災害後的人道主義干預所帶來的影響，機遇和制約都有了寶貴的見解。 聯合國（UN），歐洲聯盟（歐盟）和國際法委員會（ILC）近幾年也研發出更多的災難響應原則。其中通過了兩個主要的聯合國大會決議：（一）和平議程（A/RES/47/120 [B]）和（二）加強聯合國緊急人道主義援助的協調（A/RES/46 / 182）。後者設立了緊急救濟協調員的職位和機構間常設委員會，為多參與者國際緊急救助協調運動奠定了基礎 (Heintz & Zwitter, 2011)。 隨著人類對於大自然災害所造成的破壞的意識不斷增強，資訊科技的發展，以及區域和全球治理網絡一體化，人道主義援助的參數變得更加全球化。與此同時，近日經驗顯示，人道主義援助的成功與否，最終取決於當地的參與者有效地參與救災工作的決策過程的程度。所以如果我們欲了解這種新興的虛擬和實際國際網絡，國際組織，民間社會團體和私營部門參與者在健康和營養人道主義援助工作的地位，就必須先對法律，全球化和治理之間的相互作用有了新的認識。這樣的 考究才能開擴治理學者對全球決策的討論，和響應法學上對法律研究的要求:“不僅擴展地理層面上的重點觀察，也應擴展其概念的範圍，概念框架，和論述”（Twining, 2005）。 本研究目旨在通過比較三項類人道主義援助方案(國家主導，多邊合作和混合國家民間社會合作)，以推進我們對於“開源治理”這一種新形式人道主義理解, 和探究各國政府，民間社會，地方參與者和國際組織能如何有效地互動，設一個分散但協調的立全球自然災害後的健康和營養人道主義援助過程。

757412.label: Realisation of objectives
757412.value: Each of the research objectives of this project has been achieved. They will be discussed in detail below: I. First Objective: Develop and validate the relationship between new governance principles and efficient coordination of post-disaster humanitarian relief. The culminating output of the project, Governing Disasters: Engaging Local Populations in Humanitarian Relief (Cambridge University Press, 2016) provides an analysis of the relationship between new governance principles and post-disaster relief coordination. According to one reviewer, “The book… and supporting chapters appear complete and well-researched. The topic is clearly relevant and the mode of inquiry is consistent throughout the chapters and case studies” (Reviewer A, Cambridge U. Press). Professor Daniel Farber of UC Berkeley Law noted in relation to the book manuscript, "This important and carefully documented book shows… that [community involvement] can make a major difference in the effectiveness of disaster relief." II. Second Objective: Elaborate on existing humanitarian response law and governance structures, derive requirements/validation criteria of humanitarian governance model. This second objective is addressed in the CUP publication. According to one reviewer, “Chapter 1 is a good recitation of governance theory… Chapter 2 discusses humanitarian aid quite well. ” (Reviewer B, Cambridge U. Press). The principles of humanitarian governance are elucidated through both case study and survey analysis. According to a reviewer, “one of the key features of this book is that it offers empirical data derived from survey work.” (Reviewer A, Cambridge U. P.) III. Third Objective: Articulate a functional model of effective humanitarian governance through comparison of three typologies of assistance. The manuscript compares international, state and public-private partnerships to derive principles of effective humanitarian governance practice. According to a reviewer, “the chapter organization is logical and progresses through the issues of disaster law… Part II follows with a discussion of international-led disaster responses… Part III discusses state-led responses to disaster relief …Part IV discusses public-private partnerships…” (Reviewer B, Cambridge U. Press) IV. Fourth Objective: Identify best practices in local-global coordination. The survey chapter 12 outlines best practices in local-global coordination in humanitarian response. According to a reviewer, “the role of NGO’s and civil society is well stated.” (Reviewer B, Cambridge U. Press) V. Fifth Objective: Scholarly contribution. The project resulted in 1 book (ranked A* by RQF), 6 journal articles (over half of which are A ranked (ARC) or in a top 10-13% journal, with the remaining in a top 25-28% journal), 1 book chapter (in an A ranked book, RQF), 2 book reviews (one in an A* publication, ARC), 1 policy entry (in an A publication/blog, RQF), 18 conference papers and 2 workshop contributions. According to a reviewer, “I think the empirical work will probably be the primary novel contribution of the volume to the literature.” (Reviewer A, Cambridge U. Press)

757412.label: Major findings and research outcome
757412.value: The principal finding of the 69-person survey and seven case studies is that there is a statistically significant correlation between the level of engagement with a local community, existing capacity for consultation and coordination and perceived effectiveness of response. The significance of the research is that it offers insights into the importance of local generation and application of knowledge in building strong institutions that can respond to disasters. These insights can be useful in the development of international law and policy regarding disaster response. First, in examining case studies of international-led relief efforts, the distinctions between post-disaster approaches in Haiti and Indonesia provide some useful insights. While a variety of factors in Haiti, including high levels of social and economic inequality, poverty, malnutrition, unemployment and mortality, all contributed to the challenges surrounding post-disaster relief efforts, these challenges were compounded by limited understanding of the local context, limited situation analysis, inequitable distribution of resources to earthquake affected areas, non-alignment of resources with actual needs and harm to the local private sector. On the other hand, in Indonesia, following the 2004 tsunami where international institutions engaged individuals in a long term process of decision making regarding redevelopment goals, resource use, materials and design through a “community driven development strategy,” projects achieved higher satisfaction and usage rates because they were developed on the basis of local knowledge of needs, resources and preferences. Local participation enabled quick response to the most urgent needs and reduced the problem of marginalization . In addition, projects adopting a community driven development (CDD) model were completed 18 months ahead of schedule, they produced more output than any other program, and they cost 56 per cent less than those adopting a conventional approach. Where local institutions were engaged directly in the rebuilding process, capacity was built, which was key to the true and sustainable recovery of the affected communities . Second, in state-driven relief efforts, useful insights can also be drawn from comparing local engagement efforts in Japan and the United States following the Tohoku earthquake and tsunami of 2011 and Hurricane Katrina of 2005. The key differences in these cases lie in variation between what might be described as a centralized, robust, unified response in the case of Japan and factionalized and overlapping response in the case of the United States. These differing features and approaches impacted the quality of local collaboration. Finally, in the area of public-private partnerships, helpful insights can be drawn by examining the response of a village community in Daidanaw, Mynamar following Cyclone Nargis and the work of Second Muse in grassroots crowd-designed open-data platforms for disaster response. These community decision-making approaches emphasizing partnership, collaboration, sharing of resources, local access to and creation of knowledge resulted in positive examples of harnessing the “power of mass collaboration” in the case of Second Muse and timely, unified, efficient, and rapid recovery in case of Diadanaw where pre-existing capacity for consultation enabled careful planning, systematic and coordinated follow up with only modest targeted loans. Given the challenges in localized disaster response, practitioners at the international, state and local levels had a number of policy suggestions for improving the overall quality of local-global coordination in humanitarian relief efforts. These suggestions fell in the categories of local capacity building and training, logistical support at the local level, improvement in networking and coordination, initiating planning at the community level, accountability and information sharing and greater attention to cultural sensitivity and language.

757412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
757412.value: There is high potential for follow up research in the future. Since many of the institutions studied in this project have only started implementing community driven redevelopment response programs, useful insights can be gleaned by examining long term impacts of such approaches including linkages between program design/capacity training approaches and capacity development, recovery rates, efficiency and regulatory integration in a few years time.

757412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
757412.value: With growing awareness of the devastation caused by major natural disasters, alongside developments in information technology and regional and global integration of governance networks, the parameters of humanitarian aid are becoming more global. Understanding the role of emergent virtual and actual networks of states, international organizations, civil society groups and private sector actors in humanitarian post-disaster aid requires a new understanding of the interplay between law, globalization and governance. Drawing on extensive case studies and a global survey of 69 members of the humanitarian relief sector, this project suggests that the key to the efficacy of post-disaster recovery is the primacy given to local actors in the management, direction and design of relief programs. The project output examines the interplay between law, governance and new forms of decision making to address post-disaster relief efforts. It compares three instances of networked humanitarian assistance programs: state-led, multilateral and a hybrid of state-civil-society collaboration in order to understand how the operation of such emergent networks offer insights into how governments, civil society and international organizations can effectively collaborate with local actors to achieve a global decentralized yet coordinated process of post-disaster humanitarian assistance.

758412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
758412.value: During our life-span development, we acquire perceptual expertise in different domains. Some domains are universal, such as face and word recognition, while some domains are considered optional, such as music training. Recent research has suggested that musicians have enhanced visuospatial abilities and different brain organizations in some cognitive functions compared with non-musicians. However, it remains unclear whether these changes can influence learning in other domains. Here we aim to address this question by investigating the influence of music reading experience on word reading, including both English word and Chinese character reading. First we will examine the influence of music reading experience on visual span in word reading. Musicians, in particular pianists, have to read two lines of music notation at the same time. This experience may expand their visual span in reading especially in the upper/lower visual fields. Consistent with this speculation, recent studies show that musicians have increased activity in early visual areas in music reading compared with novices. This visual span increase may also help reading other types of stimuli. Here we compare musicians’ and non-musicians’ visual spans in reading music notation, Chinese characters, English letters, and novel symbols to examine possible transfer effects. The transfer effect of visual span in reading has never been examined, and the distinct reading pattern in pianists offers a unique opportunity for this examination. We will then explore the influence of music reading experience on hemispheric lateralization in word reading. Recent research has shown that processing in different domains may influence each other in multi-domain experts due to competition in brain resources. Similarly, musicians, who master both music notation and word reading, may have atypical word processing due to the competition, depending on how brain resources are recruited for different domains. Previous research showed that visual processing in both music and English reading is left-hemisphere lateralized, whereas that in Chinese reading is bilateral/right hemisphere lateralized. We thus hypothesize greater competition between music and English reading than between music and Chinese reading. We will first test this hypothesis with computational modeling, followed by behavioral and electrophysiological examinations. This research will contribute to our understanding of how brain areas are recruited for different tasks and how different expertise domains influence each other. It also has important educational implications for how to facilitate learning in multiple domains. The focus on English and Chinese reading will provide particular relevance for the biliterate environment of Hong Kong.

758512.label: Project Objectives
758512.value: Identify the comovement among arbitrage spreads across different asset classes. We plan to base our study on common arbitrage strategies employed by hedge funds. After we calculate arbitrage spreads for individual strategies, we plan to use techniques, such as principal component analysis, quantile regressions and logit regressions, to identify the comovement among these arbitrage spreads. Establish a direct link between aggregate liquidity and comovement among arbitrage spreads from different markets. We plan to investigate whether aggregate liquidity can help explain the comovement in arbitrage spreads. We expect variation in the aggregate liquidity level is related to the first principal component of arbitrage spreads from different asset classes. This relationship between aggregate liquidity and arbitrage spreads is stronger when the aggregate market is illiquid, and weaker when the aggregate market is liquid. We plan use the noise measure in Hu, Pan, and Wang (2010) as the major variable for aggregate liquidity. But we are also going to test other liquidity variables such as TED spreads, default spreads and hedge fund flows.

758512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
758512.value: 這個項目的主要目的是研究總的流動性和在不同市場的套利利差的關係。在總市場的流動性水平和套利資本的量密切相關，而這又是保持類似的資產在相同的價格至關重要的因素。在正常的市場與高流動性的時候，投資銀行和機構投資者，如自營交易部或對沖基金有雄厚的資金部署，套利利差將接近於零，任何大的價格差異將在很短的時間內消失。在金融危機爆發時流動性凍結了，套利力量的有效性減弱，導致持續性的錯誤定價。 這種觀察到的“套利限制”已經得到了許多理論和實證研究，但他們中的大多數都集中在個別市場。而我們是調查套利價差在不同的套利市場的系統組成部分，並最重要的是它和總市場的流動性水平的關係。換言之我們感興趣的是，整體市場流動性的衝擊如何影響所有金融資產類別的套利機會。 我們計劃首先計算在不同的金融市場的各種流行的套利策略的套利價差。我們預計 不同的套利市場的套利價差往往一起移動，而這聯動性和總的流動性水平的變化有關。 因為計算套利價差不是一件容易的事，我們會進行若干基於對沖基金風格指數的回報的初步測試。這是因為我們觀察到對沖基金的套利可看作是實現套利策略的收益。另一方面，套利利差可以預測這些策略的預期收益。因此，分析對沖基金的回報可以幫助揭示動態套利價差。我們的初步分析表明，一個主要的系統因素可以解釋十個對沖基金風格指數的回報率33％的變化。這個結果支持我們的假設，即從不同的市場往往看似無關的套利價差實際上都在一起移動。我們還發現，這種聯動性可以解釋為總的流動性的變化，並可用胡，潘，王(2010）中提出的噪聲測量代理來量化。套利利差和總的流動性之間的關係在平常的時間和危機時期都非常的顯著。 過去的2008年金融危機凸顯了嚴重的流動性短缺對金融市場的影響。據我們所知，這個項目第一個研究總的流動性和套利機會的關係。我們的研究還對市場流動性和效率具有豐富的政策含義。

758712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
758712.value: Scientific studies that examine the long-term dynamics of natural disasters (>100 years, covering periods of different climate characteristics) have received special attention in recent years. However, explanations about the causal mechanism of drought in northwestern China that rely on paleo-environmental reconstructions at individual sites to examine drought yield diverse results. To address this issue, the PI tried another approach in his recent studies. He reduced the Gan-Ning-Qing Region (GNQR, a macro region which shares ~30% of the total land area of northwestern China) into several geographic units. Based upon the fine-grained historical drought records of each geographic unit, spatial weighting techniques were applied to reveal the annual oscillation of drought for the entire GNQR over the last millennium. He further explored the connection between North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) and drought in the GNQR at multi-decadal to centennial timescales. Ultimately, he confirmed the connection and also worked out the causal mechanism between NAO and drought in the GNQR, which challenges the existing explanations of drought in northwestern China. Although the PI has scientifically established the NAO-drought relationship in the GNQR, two important issues remain unresolved: First, it has been suggested in other studies that precipitation in northwestern China is also determined by El Niño-Southern Oscillation and North Atlantic sea surface and air temperature, in addition to NAO. The individual roles and combined impacts of these phenomena in causing drought in the GNQR need to be identified. Second, previous studies conducted by the PI cover the GNQR, which is only part of northwestern China, a region that is located at the present-day northern limit of the Asian Summer Monsoon. The hydrological balance and effective moisture of the region is controlled by the interactions of Asian Summer Monsoon, Winter Monsoon and Westerlies. Throughout this unique geographic setting, it has yet to be determined if the causal mechanism of drought in other regions of northwestern China will be different from that in the GNQR. This project seeks to investigate the above issues because they are imperative for comprehending the causal mechanism of drought over the entire northwestern China region. The associated findings are vital for predicting the future impacts of, and developing proper counter-measures against, drought. Given that drought has been a limiting factor for the economy and society in northwestern China, this project is not only of academic interest but also of practical value. 近年，人們都非常重視自然災害的長期動態（>100年，當中包括不同的氣候時期）的科學研究。不過，那些透過個別地點的古環境重建序列去追索中國西北地區干旱的形成機制的相關研究，結論不一。就上述的爭議，項目負責人在他近期的研究中嘗試了一種新的方法。他首先將甘寧青地區（佔中國西北地區總面積約百份之三十）分成若干區域，並將每個區域詳盡的歷史干旱紀錄定量並進行空間加權處理，重建了當地過去一千年的年尺度的干旱變化。而且，項目負責人進一步探索在數十年至百年尺度下北太平洋擺動（NAO）與甘寧青地區干旱的關聯，最終確定兩者的因果關係並理清它們之間的聯系機制，而有關的結果對現存的中國西北地區干旱的解釋作出挑戰。 雖然項目負責人已經用科學的方法去解釋 NAO 與甘寧青地區干旱的關係，但有兩個相關的問題是仍未解答的： 第一，其他的研究曾提及，除了 NAO 外，厄爾尼諾現象及北太平洋海面及空氣溫度均對中國西北地區的降水構成影響，我們需要進一步去認清以上因素對甘寧青地區干旱的個別及複合影響。 第二，項目負責人早前的研究只覆蓋甘寧青地區，甘寧青地區只是中國西北地區的一部份，同是亦位處於現在亞洲季候風的北部邊緣，當地的水循環同時受制於亞洲夏季季候風、冬季季候風與及西風帶的相互作用。基於甘寧青地區地理上的獨特性，當地的干旱形成機制可能有別於中國西北的其他地區，但這一點尚未驗證。 這個項目主要就以上的問題作深入的探討，從而更全面地去認識整個中國西北地區的干旱形成機制，而有關的結果對於預測干旱所帶來的影響與及制定干旱防治的措施是非常重要的。在干旱已經局限中國西北地區社會及經濟發展的大前提下，相信除了學術價值以外，這個項目亦有相當的實際意義。

758712.label: Realisation of objectives
758712.value: Drought is about the periodic deficiency of precipitation (i.e., drought/precipitation anomalies). Northwestern China [NW China, with the Gansu-Ningxia-Qinghai Region (GNQR) included] sits at the present-day northern fringe of the Asian Summer Monsoon. The precipitation regime there is influenced by multiple atmospheric circulation systems such as the Asian Summer Monsoon and the Westerlies. Hence, the hydro-climate in NW China is characterized by substantial regional differences (Zhao 1986). In NW China, drought happens in one region, while the other region can be in opposite weather condition. Besides, such pattern is reversed in alternative periods. Such regional hydro-climatic difference is especially apparent between the region influenced by the Asian Summer Monsoon and the region influenced by the Westerlies (Chen et al. 2015). Subject to the abovementioned geographic configuration of NW China, the PI based on historical drought/flood and other precipitation related documentary records to reconstruct two different and yet, inter-related paleo-climate reconstructions to capture the footprints of drought/precipitation anomalies in NW China, covering the periods with and without instrumental precipitation records. The PI’s research focus is about tracing the long-term dynamics of drought/precipitation anomalies in NW China as well as its driving mechanisms, as the knowledge of such dynamics is vital for (1) improving projection about the regional water resource uncertainty within the context of global warming, and (2) forecasting the societal impacts of precipitation change in the coming decades. Chinese historical documents are accurate in chronology and explicit in their description of dry-wet conditions. They are useful in locating disaster events in a long time span, particularly when the events are recorded on an annual basis. Also, they contain a wide spectrum of climate variability and encompass the evidence of past changes at a range of time-scales (Zhang et al. 2010). In parallel, the availability of other proxy data depends on the properties of the proxy media itself. For instance, trees for dendrochronology tend to concentrate in places favorable to plant growth. Also, the distribution of cave speleothems, ice cores, and lake sediments are confined to certain geographic regions. Therefore, the PI relied on historical documentary records to perform paleo-climate reconstruction. Regarding the first reconstruction, the PI based on the dryness/wetness grade series of 19 sites in northwestern (NW) China (Sha’anxi, Gansu, Ningxia, and Qinghai), which are primarily derived from historical documents, to reconstruct the annual geographic extent of drought anomalies in NW China in AD1470–2008. The advantage of this method is the emphasis on incorporating the spatial influence of climate change into the construction. This reconstruction is primarily designated to address the first project objective. Regarding the second reconstruction, the PI divided his study area (Sha’anxi, Gansu, Ningxia, and eastern Qinghai) into two macro regions according to the approximate present-day 400 mm isohyet, which is the threshold value in distinguishing the arid/semi-arid region (mainly influenced by the Westerlies) from the humid region (mainly influenced by the Asian Summer Monsoon) in NW China. The 400 mm isohyet is also the natural divide between animal husbandry and agricultural regions. Then, he employed historical drought/flood disaster records to work out the decadal precipitation indices of the two regions spanned AD580–1979. After that, the PI based on the difference of the precipitation indices between the two macro regions to derive the intra-regional precipitation variability (IRPV) index of NW China. The index represents the relative change of precipitation between the arid/semi-arid region and the humid region in NW China, with the direction and the magnitude of precipitation change taken into account. If the precipitation change in the two macro regions moves in opposite directions and becomes more extreme, the index value will be positively/negatively deviated away from zero, and vice versa. The advantage of this method is about its originality, because it focuses on “exploring regional variance” rather than “deducing regional resemblance”. The above method deems to be very suitable in examining the hydro-climatic dynamics in NW China, where the precipitation regime is typified by salient intra-regional differences. The reconstructed IRPV index of NW China is primarily designated to address the second project objective. The PI also compared the two reconstructions with other paleo-climatic records in nearby regions (which are derived from tree-ring chronologies, cave speleothems, ice cores, and lake sediments) to ensure their validity, making sure that they did satisfactorily capture the hydro-climatic information to be investigated. Then, the PI statistically compared his reconstructions with the following climatic forcing proxies to find out the driving forces of the geographic extent of drought anomalies as well as the IRPV in NW China: Asian Summer Monsoon, Arctic Oscillation, Atlantic Multi-decadal Oscillation, North Atlantic Oscillation, Pacific Decadal Oscillation, El Niño Southern Oscillation, Eastern Tropical Pacific Ocean sea surface temperature, Indo-Pacific warm pool sea surface temperature, and China-wide land surface temperature. The above climatic forcing proxies were chosen as they are suggested to have significant influence on the hydro-climate in NW China in literature. For climatic systems, transient dynamics appear to be the rule rather than the exception in nature, because climatic processes are influenced by exogenous trends or pre-dominated by complex endogenous dynamics (Grinsted et al. 2004). Hence, it may be inappropriate to apply traditional techniques (which make the assumption that the statistical properties of the time-series do not vary with time) to analyze non-stationary climatic variables or their mutual dependencies. Hence, the PI employed moving correlation analysis and wavelet analysis in this project. Regarding the moving correlation analysis, the correlation between two time-series is calculated over a moving window. Regarding the wavelet analysis, it is a powerful tool that is already in use throughout science and engineering. By performing a local time-scale decomposition of the signal in time-series, wavelet analysis is germane in analyzing non-stationary systems. The continuous wavelet transform decomposes the time-series into both time and frequency components, the calculation of the wavelet power spectrum quantifies in the time-frequency domain and the distribution of the variance of the time-series (Torrence and Compo 1998). Through the above steps, the PI found out the individual roles and combined impacts of various possible causative factors in triggering drought/precipitation anomalies in NW China [i.e., the first project objective, the findings are published in The Holocene (Impact Factor in 2014: 2.283)], as well as the mechanism which modulates the variation of drought/precipitation anomalies across different regions of NW China at various time-scales [i.e., the second project objective, the findings are published in PLoS ONE (Impact Factor in 2014: 3.234)]. References: Chen J, Chen F, Feng S, Huang W, Liu J, Zhou A (2015) Hydroclimatic changes in China and surroundings during the Medieval Climate Anomaly and Little Ice Age: Spatial patterns and possible mechanisms. Quaternary Science Reviews 107: 98-111. Grinsted A, Moore JC, Jevrejeva S (2004) Application of the cross wavelet transform and wavelet coherence to geophysical time series. Nonlinear Processes in Geophysics 11: 561-566. Torrence C, Compo GP (1998) A practical guide to wavelet analysis. Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society 79: 61-78. Zhang D, Li HC, Ku TL, Lu LH (2010) On linking climate to Chinese dynastic change: Spatial and temporal variations of monsoonal rain. Chinese Science Bulletin 55: 77-83. Zhao S (1986) Physical Geography of China. Beijing, China: Science Press.

758712.label: Major findings and research outcome
758712.value: Based on the PI’s reconstruction of the geographic extent of drought anomalies in northwestern (NW) China in AD1470–2008, the following drought periods were revealed: the AD1470s–1490s, 1620s–1640s, 1700s–1720s, 1770s–1790s, 1860s–1870s, and 1910s–1930s. The most extremely dry years were AD1928 and 1929. Besides, the PI found that the influence of El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) on the geographic extent of drought anomalies in NW China was non-stationary at the inter-annual to multi-decadal time-scale and that the correlation switched from positive to negative since the late Little Ice Age (LIA, AD1400–1900). This non-stationary relationship was mediated by the variance of ENSO and the strength of Asian Summer Monsoon. Based on the PI’s reconstruction of the intra-regional precipitation variability (IRPV) index in NW China in AD580–1979, the PI found the anomalous periodicities/unusually strong fluctuations of IRPV in the LIA, which was caused by the change of hydro-climatic regime in NW China during the period. The PI presented new evidence about the unusual climatic periodicities in NW China during the LIA mentioned in previous studies, which is not only characterized by increasing amount of precipitation in the arid/semi-arid regions of NW China throughout the LIA, but also characterized by intense variations in precipitation between the arid/semi-arid and the humid regions in NW China within the period. At the multi-decadal to centennial time-scale, the variability of the IRPV in NW China was dominated by ENSO. At the centennial to multi-centennial time-scale, the variability of the IRPV was dominated by the Indo-Pacific warm pool sea surface temperature and China-wide land surface temperature. While some meteorological and paleo-climate/environment studies also highlight the tele-connection between ENSO activities and drought/precipitation anomalies in NW China, the teleconnection is often demonstrated to be inter-annual to decadal. However, the PI found that ENSO drove the drought/precipitation anomalies in NW China at the multi-decadal to centennial time-scale. Even though some scholars mentioned the tele-connection between ENSO activities and precipitation change in NW China and the regions nearby at the long-term temporal scales, the relationship in the pre-instrumental period has not been validated quantitatively. The PI presented the quantitative validation of the low-frequency tele-connection between ENSO and precipitation change in NW China covering both pre-instrumental and instrumental periods. The tele-connection was found to be a consistent feature inherent to the climatic regime in NW China, which could be traced back to the early fourteenth century.

758712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
758712.value: In this project, the PI based on historical documentary records to trace the long-term dynamics of drought/precipitation anomalies in northwestern (NW) China – a region covered by the Westerlies and the Asian Summer Monsoon. In Japan, her geographic configuration is quite similar to that of NW China, as the hydro-climate in eastern Japan is influenced by the Asian Summer Monsoon, while the one in western Japan is influenced by the Westerlies. Hence, the precipitation patterns of the two regions in Japan are quite different. Also, there are abundant climate related historical documentary records in Japan, just like the case of China. Given the above circumstances, the long-term (multi-decadal to centennial) precipitation difference between eastern and western Japan in relation to climatic forcings (say, various kinds of atmospheric circulations and also solar activity) could be a potential research topic. Through the conference grant support of this project, the PI has the opportunities to approach some Japanese scholars who also use historical documentary records to study long-term climate dynamics. Discussion is still underway. If the collaboration with those Japanese scholars could be materialized, the PI could apply the approach/methods adopted in this project to study the long-term hydro-climatic variability in Japan.

758712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
758712.value: Scientific studies that examine the long-term dynamics of drought over the northwestern (NW) China region have received special attention in recent years. However, these studies are often constrained by the availability of instrumental precipitation records. This project seeks to address this issue. The PI based on historical drought/flood records to trace the geographic extent of drought anomalies as well as the intra-regional precipitation variability in NW China, covering the periods with and without instrumental precipitation records. Moving correlation and wavelet analyses were applied to find their major determinants. Results show that El Niño Southern Oscillation (Indo-Pacific warm pool sea surface temperature) is the major multi-decadal to centennial (centennial to multi-centennial) determinant of the hydro-climatic variability in NW China. The associated mechanism is anchored with the change of Asian Summer Monsoonal precipitation, while it is driven by different factors at different time scales. The above findings are important for predicting the future impacts of, and developing proper counter-measures against, drought. Given that drought has been a limiting factor for the economy and society in NW China, this project is not only of academic interest but also of practical value.

759012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
759012.value: This study will test and elaborate on the theoretical perspectives of multi-layered governance in the internationalization of academic science by exploring the global competition and collaboration strategies of research universities in the new world economies. Competition for symbolic, intellectual and financial resources is increasingly urging governments, universities and individual researchers to be strategic in their partnerships and to follow cost-benefit rationales. However, research universities are complex institutions with a multitude of economic, social and political commitments diffused across local, national, and global planes. As academic departments and research units come under increasing pressure from all sides, university strategists are eager to better understand how they can be equally successful in preserving integrity, increasing quality and positioning their institutions for partnerships that generate benefits and reduce costs. This study scrutinizes academic partnership strategies in China and Russia to illustrate how research universities in the new world economies approach the calibration of stakeholder relations at home and abroad to mitigate resource asymmetries and enhance cumulative advantages. The “global higher education matrix” (Jones 2008; Jones and Oleksiyenko 2011) will be used to identify and compare collaborative/competitive patterns across the universities’ understructures (individual/academic unit strategies), structures (institutional/university-wide strategies) and superstructures (internationalization funding and policies at the level of local and national governments, and global agencies). The matrix enables the correlation of data from multiple levels of governance structure with information on local, national, regional and global demands. The analysis will be conducted across four case studies: two research universities in China (Peking University and Tsinghua University), and two research universities in Russia (Moscow State University and National Research University "Higher School of Economics"). The cross-case analysis will show similarities and differences in geopolitical, economic and cultural configurations that shape the research universities’ challenges and opportunities in reconciling the collaboration/competition pull and push factors in the internationalization of academic science. The study will provide valuable data for university strategists in Hong Kong, China, Russia and elsewhere on research university partnerships and mitigation of asymmetries in administrative and funding schemes in the age of accelerating global competition. The project will refine the concept of multi-layered governance in the internationalization of university research. The study will also complement the data-set collected by the PI in Canada, the US, Hong Kong, Singapore, Korea, Malaysia and Central Asia, allowing for broader scale comparative analysis and successive publications on strategic international partnerships in research universities. 本研究通過探索在新的全球經濟下研究型大學的全球性競爭和合作策略，測試和闡釋在學術科學國際化的形勢下多層治理的理論觀點。 對象徵性、知識分子及財政資源的激烈競爭越來越迫使政府、大學及研究學者在選擇合作夥伴時需要更具策略，並採用成本效益的原理來分析得失。然而，研究型大學是非常複雜的機構， 他們承擔了來自地方、國家以及全球的經濟、社會和政治的各種承諾。作為承受著來自各方日益增長壓力的學術部門和研究單位，高校策略家們很熱切地期望更瞭解高等院校如何能在維持正義誠實、提升品質、替大學尋求定位以產生效益降低成本的夥伴合作關係等各方面取得相同的成功。 本研究深入探究中國和俄國的學術夥伴合作策略，闡釋在新世界經濟形勢下研究型大學是如何處理及調校與國內外各利益關係人的關係，以緩解資源配置不對稱的問題，並增強積累的優勢。本研究將運用“全球高等教育矩陣” (Jones 2008; Jones and Oleksiyenko 2011) 來識別和比較大學的下層結構層面（個人或學術單位的策略）、結構層面（機構或大學層面的策略），以及上層結構層面 （國際資金以及地方、國家政府和全球機構層面的政策）合作和競爭模式。來自多層次治理結構的數據，以及地方、國家、區域和全球性需求的資訊及關聯將透過這個矩陣展現出來。 本研究將通過四個案例進行分析，包括中國（北京大學和清華大學）和俄國（莫斯科國立大學和國家研究大學高等經濟學院）各兩所研究型大學。這種交叉案例分析將會展示地緣政治、經濟和文化結構上的異同，及該些異同如何影響研究型大學在學術科學國際化形勢下協調合作/競爭中各種推拉因素所帶來的機遇和挑戰。 本研究將為香港、中國、俄國以及其他地方的高校策略家們提供有價值的資料。在全球競爭日益激烈的情勢下，這些資料將有利於研究大學夥伴合作，及緩解行政和資金不對稱等問題。本計畫將優化研究大學國際化形勢下多層次治理的相關概念。研究結果將補充由計畫主持人自加拿大、美國、香港、新加坡、韓國、馬來西亞和中亞所建立的數據庫，藉以擴大有關研究型大學的策略性國際合作夥伴關係的比較研究以及今後相關文獻的發表。

759112.label: Project Title(Chinese)
759112.value: 運用多重任務訓練方法學習外科手術技術技能

759112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
759112.value: 外科手術室 是一種極為註重安全的環境，在這種環境中，外科醫生除了需要組織自己的工作空間，與他們的團隊進行有效的溝通，作出明智的決定，同時還要確保外科手術技術技能的精準度。手術過程中的各種壓力使得這種已經很繁重的多重任務環境進一步複雜化。考慮到初級外科醫生在手術中所需要面對的種種挑戰，外科教育領域的領導者已經開始著手開發和驗證各種新的訓練方法，讓初級外科醫生能更好地適應手術室中的種種挑戰。有一種觀點是，外科手術學員應該在安全的模擬環境下進行有壓力技術技能訓練，使他們能開發出自適應的應對策略，從而有可能有助於降低在手術過程中的技術表現對壓力的敏感性。另外一種觀點是，訓練課程的開發人員在設計訓練方法之前應考慮外科專家和新手在手術技術操作表現時的差異，從而有目的的進行課程設計。外科手術教育工作者必須考慮到由醫生工作時間削減這種趨勢所導致的培訓時間上的限制，所以在製定培訓計劃時，我們希望有一種訓練方法可以略過一些達到專業水準所必須的訓練環節，同時技術操作的自動化程度和穩定性不會受到影響。多重任務訓練方法可能可以滿足上述要求，因為這種訓練方法要求學員在練習他們的手術技術技能的同時進行一種分散注意力的認知任務（一種手術過程中常見的壓力來源），這值得我們去深入研究。首先，多重任務訓練可以讓手術技術技能的控制更加自動化。其次，多重任務訓練使得學員在一種手術過程中經常遇到的壓力下進行訓練。再次，多重任務訓練可以使學員對認知任務和技術技能任務這兩個方面的學習同時進行並互不影響。簡而言之，多重任務訓練可以讓外科學員的手術技術技能在時間上高效率地達到專業水準。為此我們提出了一系列的研究來驗證多重任務訓練是否可以作為一種可行的方法來a）促進腹腔鏡手術技術技能的熟練程度和自動化水平，b）提高手術技術操作在常見的術中多重任務壓力下的表現的穩定性，c）在提升手術技術技能方面的同時，促進外科手術中的非技術技能層面的學習，比如說，對各種安全事項的檢查，d）促進將來對更具挑戰性的腹腔鏡技術技能的學習。

759212.label: Project Title(Chinese)
759212.value: 術與技：後革命的中國建築文化：1973-1989

759212.label: Project Objectives
759212.value: To move beyond a simple descriptive evaluation of the architecture’s collective aesthetic merits towards a more complete, complex, and conceptual intellectual history of China’s architectural development between 1973 and 1989. To understand Chinese architecture’s rapid internationalization during this period of time and reposition the era as a vital moment in the history of China’s architectural and cultural production. To insert Chinese architectural education, exchange and discourse within broader international histories of postmodernism. To trace the conceptual and etymological roots of architectural discourse in China between 1973 and 1989. To reassess China’s role as an earlier, more active, and more dynamic influence in the international architectural community between 1973 and 1989 than previously considered.

To understand Chinese architecture’s rapid internationalization during this period of time and reposition the era as a vital moment in the history of China’s architectural and cultural production.
To insert Chinese architectural education, exchange and discourse within broader international histories of postmodernism.

To reassess China’s role as an earlier, more active, and more dynamic influence in the international architectural community between 1973 and 1989 than previously considered.

759212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
759212.value: This project examines modern Chinese architectural education, exchange, and discourse between 1973 and 1989. It seeks to understand three significant but unexplored dimensions of the era: the international expansion of Chinese architectural construction and exchange beginning in 1973; the profound changes in architectural education following the advent of economic reform beginning in 1977; and the impact of this internationalization on Chinese architectural discourse over the course of the 1980s. This project will begin by mapping out the personal and professional networks that extended beyond China into Hong Kong, Taiwan, the United States and Europe immediately following the Cultural Revolution, laying an important discursive, pedagogical, and professional foundation for the swift period of development that would follow. Historicizing curricular reform and pedagogical development within four of China’s most prominent architectural institutions, including Tsinghua University (Beijing), Tianjin University (Tianjin), Tongji University (Shanghai), and Southeast University (Nanjing) represents an important second stage of my research. A close examination of primary source material from the period, from portfolios of students’ design work to early Master and Ph.D. research theses, offers new critical perspective on the era’s disciplinary challenges as well as its exciting, unpredictable potential. Early international exchanges brokered by each of these major universities with architectural departments in Japan, the United States, and Europe also deserves attention as evidence of China’s shift towards more contemporary, internationally-inclined pedagogical strategies. The project’s final section will chart the conceptual and etymological roots of Chinese architectural discourse over the course of the 1980s. The emergence of domestically published journals, privately-established practices, and independently organized salons, among other examples, may be seen as constituting a fragile but powerful blossoming of architectural culture that remains poorly understood today. Ultimately, this work aims to re-position the era as a vital moment in the history of China’s architectural and cultural production by providing new and critical insight into the country’s pedagogical, discursive, and diplomatic development within the realm of architecture at the time. Re-framing China within the broader international discourse of postmodernism in the 1970s and 1980s also provides a new and important voice to an as-yet emerging field of study. More generally, it asserts China be considered a more active and international influence in architectural practice and study at the time than has been previously considered. 這項研究，“術與技：後革命的中國建築文化：1973-1989“，計畫通過探討1973-1989年間中國建築的發展歷程、話語流變及教育狀況從而檢視這一時間段在中國建築發展史上的重要意義. 我從三個看法想瞭解時代重要的影響：中國從1973建築交流的國際化；1977之後建築教育的變化；和80年代建築術語的發展。 研究有三個目標。 第一個就是追蹤中國建築師擴張的國內和國際網路。文化大革命完了之後，從中國到臺灣，香港，美國，和歐洲的聯繫就開始。這個交流從建築教育，話語，和職業的角度來說有非常重要的影響。 第二個目標是分析中國四個主要建築院校，即清華大學、天津大學、同濟大學、東南大學建築系的相關文件及材料。學生的設計方案，博士論文，等等，都很有意思的資料，從它們可以看學生與老師們對什麼研究話題有興趣。這些大學的交流也值得注意，露出中國國際化的計畫。 最後的部分關於80時代中國建築話語的影響與源頭。雖然國內雜誌，建築辦公室，當時學生的建築理論沙龍對建築法杖有非常重大的影響，但是我們還不太瞭解它們的歷史。用後現代主義理論來分析中國1973-1989的建築歷史有好處。希望這樣的研究對國際建築歷史來說也有貢獻。

759212.label: Realisation of objectives
759212.value: The project's objectives have been achieved in nearly all respects. In general, my work has helped illuminate post-Cultural Revolution architectural development and exchange, a previously under-examined period of time in China's architectural history. I've expanded the scope of my own knowledge concerning this period, and through my three research outputs, I've also contributed to the field of Chinese architectural historical scholarship. Each of my three peer-reviewed articles offers a new perspective on China's architecture in relation to economic liberalization and internationalization over the course of the late 1970s and 1980s. Each article maintains its own unique focus on a particular dimension of China's architectural production at the time. These topics include the rise of the international hotel in China over the course of the late 1970s and 1980s, the expansion of China's architectural exchanges and transformations within the Chinese design institute, as well as China's architectural engagement with numerous countries within the African continent. More generally, I've worked to better understand shifts in China's architectural educational system at the time and their impact upon the country's architectural production. I have engaged in an interactive research initiative with staff from the Journalism and Media Studies Centre. Together, we have launched a research website, which is still under internal design, that will enable people to search for names of Chinese architects who graduated from each of China's major architectural institutes as well as projects they may have helped design. Through my work, I'm now able to see the particular kinds of architectural discourses that took shape within China at the time, and the extent to which they intertwined with international architectural trends. The moment seems even more vital and important than I initially anticipated.

759212.label: Major findings and research outcome
759212.value: My research outcomes comprise three internationally recognized, blind peer-reviewed academic journal articles: 1. “Non-Aligned Architecture: China’s Designs on and in Ghana and Guinea, 1955-92.” Architectural History 58 (2015): 261-91. Externally refereed. 2. “Practicing Reform: Experiments in Post-Revolutionary Chinese Architectural Production, 1973-1989.” Journal of Architectural Education 69, no. 1 (March 2015): 27-38. Externally refereed. 3. “Envisioning Reform: The International Hotel in Postrevolutionary China, 1974-1990.” Grey Room 58, no. 1 (Winter 2015): 84-111. Externally refereed. The findings contained within these three outputs include a deeper, more substantial analysis of the first international hotels built in China during reform; a reassessment of economic and design changes taking place within the institutional framework of the design institute; as well as a more in-depth history of China's architectural involvement with Ghana and Guinea than has been previously published. Collectively, these findings offer exciting insight into the history of socialist Chinese architectural design.

759212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
759212.value: There is great potential for further development in all aspects of this research. Following the publication of my three articles, I have found significant international interest in these topics. I have additional material that could comprise a book-length study of this period. I hope to pursue this project in the future, funding permitting. My GRF-funded research has led to a number of exciting opportunities. From September 22-29, I will attend the first Asia-in-Africa international conference, "Africa-Asia: A New Axis of Knowledge," to be held at the University of Legon in Accra, Ghana. The event is anticipating 300 participants from around the work. I will be presenting a portion of my GRF-funded work on Chinese architecture in Ghana. I was recently invited to contribute an essay to an architectural guide on Sub-Saharan Africa to be published by DOM publishers, a well-known German publisher. The guide represents the first publication that introduces Sub-Saharan architecture to a general public. I am currently in discussion with the Ullens Centre for Contemporary Art (UCCA) in Beijing, China's preeminent venue for contemporary architectural and artistic exhibitions, about curating an exhibit on China's first reform-era international hotels, including many of the projects I researched as part of my GRF.

759212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
759212.value: My research project, "Of Art and Science: Post-Revolutionary Architectural Culture in China, 1973-1989," examines the industry of design in China amid the gradual end of the country’s tumultuous Cultural Revolution (1966-1976) and the swift economic transformations that followed. Although the period is often dismissed as a transitional and relatively insignificant moment in China’s architectural history, my research repositions reform-era shifts in architectural discourse, practice and expression as crucial to the project of reform itself. Reassessing the era offers valuable insight, not only into the intellectual formation of China’s current architectural establishment, but with respect to the dynamic, rapidly internationalizing forms of Chinese architectural production and expression taking shape today. Using broad organizational themes of exchange, education, and engagement, my work seeks to illuminate how architecture itself conditioned the practices necessitated for economic liberalization. International hotel design, the transformation of the design institute as a state-controlled mechanism for design, international architectural exchange with African countries--collectively, these topics illuminate a range of unexamined projects that may be said to constitute the design of reform.

759212.value: During my research trip to Ghana in May/June 2015, I participated in a round table discussion organized by ArchiAfrika, a local organization devoted to raising awareness with respect to architectural culture throughout the African continent. I presented my research to a group of local architects and interested residents. Following my trip, I remained in contact with Dr. Lloyd G. This conference should lead to interesting possibilities for future collaboration. This past academic year, I was awarded a Geddes Visiting Fellowship at the School for at the Edinburgh School of Architecture and Landscape Architecture at the University of Edinburgh. As part of the fellowship, I spent one week in Edinburgh meeting with faculty from the University and also delivered several lectures on my research, much of which was funded by my GRF grant. I delivered a version of my eventually published paper on Chinese architecture in Ghana and Guinea (see research output, "Unaligned Architecture: China's Designs on and in Ghana and Guinea, 1955-1992, Architectural History 58 (2015): 261-91. 759512.label: Project Title(Chinese)
759512.value: 知識產權在促進香港和大陸時尚業的作用

759512.label: Project Objectives
759512.value: To examine a set of theoretical and policy issues underlying IP protection of fashion designs by fully considering the economic and social circumstances of Hong Kong and mainland China. To explore the challenges that lie ahead for the fashion industries in Hong Kong and mainland China in the context of the recent IP reforms in Europe or the United States. To propose a viable model of IP law designed to increase the creative competitiveness of the fashion industries in Hong Kong and mainland China. To consider how IP enforcement in China can be improved for merchandizing fashion products in the Chinese market. To discuss the legal challenges for the fashion industry posed by the counterfeit culture that has grown rapidly amid the rise of the so-called “shanzhai phenomenon” in mainland China.

759512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
759512.value: Fashion is a crucial part of a pluralistic society in which knowledge-intensive creations are core to the evolution of human life. In Hong Kong and mainland China, fashion has become increasingly important in the economic and cultural fabrics of Chinese society. Therefore, it is important for both Hong Kong and mainland China to develop creatively competitive fashion industries, thereby promoting a robust cultural environment for enhanced creativity and innovation. This issue also carries significant policy and practical values because China has become the world’s largest luxury market. This project seeks to explore what kind of intellectual property (IP) system Hong Kong and mainland China should adopt in order to boost their fashion industries to be as competitive as those headquartered in Paris, Milan, London, and New York. The central question to be addressed is how and why potential changes to IP protection of fashion designs in Hong Kong and mainland China would foster and enhance the creative competitiveness of these two regions. The project examines a set of theoretical and policy issues underlying IP protection of fashion designs by considering the economic and social circumstances of Hong Kong and mainland China. It explores the challenges that lie ahead for the fashion industries in these two regions in the context of the reforms that have been made and are to be implemented in the Europe Union or the United States. The project will consider the merits of these recent reforms. Moreover, it will examine how IP enforcement in China can be improved for fashion products. In particular, it will discuss the legal challenges for the fashion industry posed by the counterfeit culture that has grown rapidly amid the rise of the so-called “shanzhai phenomenon” in mainland China. Based on the examination of these core issues, the project will propose a viable model of IP protection designed to increase the creative competitiveness of the fashion industries in Hong Kong and mainland China. 本項目研究在香港和中國大陸為時尚產業提供知識產權保護的相關理論和政策性問題。它探討了歐盟和美國相關法律變革對香港和中國大陸時尚產業所帶來的挑戰。同時，它研究中國如何加強對知識產權執法來為時尚或者奢侈產品提供更好的法律保護。本項目特別會研究在大陸​​不斷發展的假冒文化對時尚產業提供知識產權保護所帶來影響。通過以上研究，本項目將會就加強香港和中國大陸為時尚產業提出一個可行性的知識產權保護框架。

759512.label: Realisation of objectives
759512.value: The project reviewed the economic and social circumstances of Hong Kong and mainland China. It identified that a major economic and social issue in Hong Kong and mainland China is the rapidly growing income inequality. For example, the research found that, although Hong Kong is an international hub for merchandizing luxury/fashion products, it had 1.187 million people living in poverty in 2012, which is nearly 20% of the city population. Income inequality in mainland China has been worsening too. The project explored the challenges that lie ahead for the fashion industries in Hong Kong and mainland China in the context of the recent IP reforms in Europe or the United States. To this end, it studied in the recent high-profile fashion brand litigations in Europe and the United States. For example, the project examined in detail the litigation between Christian Louboutin and Yves Saint Laurent concerning the trademark protection of the red-sole color mark. With respect to anti-dilution protection that is crucial to fashion brands, the project examined the recent developments in the European Union and the United Stated. It further compared China and Hong Kong anti-dilution law with its counterparts in the European Union and the United States. The project also conducted case studies concerning fashion brands in mainland China and Hong Kong. It examined Hong Kong cases such as Guccio Gucci SpA v. Gucci and the cases that Hermès litigated in China. The cases selected dealt with legal standards for protecting fashion designs and brands. They were also concerned with enforcement of intellectual property rights. Through case studies, the project identified trademark protection as the most important form of intellectual property protection for fashion companies and designers. Moreover, it revealed the potential problems with the relevant legal standards contained in intellectual property statutes, as well as the challenges that judges and lawyers may face when they apply laws. Case studies also helped my project identify major issues in enforcing intellectual property rights in mainland China. I organized a conference entitled “Charting the New Frontiers of Intellectual Property Protection of Fashion Brands and Designs.” The conference was held at the University of Hong Kong on May 10, 2015. It identified that fashion is one of the world’s most important creative industries. In the context of the growing importance of the fashion industry, this conference brought together leading practitioners and scholars to share their perspectives on hot topics and recent trends in intellectual property protection of fashion designs and brands. Moreover, I co-edited a book on luxury brand protection with Barton Beebe and Madhavi Sunder, two leading intellectual property scholars. The editing process helped me identified research issues and methods for addressing intellectual property protection of fashion designs and brands. A few papers collected in the book discussed the relevance of social justice for protecting fashion and luxury goods. They confirmed that the social justice approach I applied to my project had revealed major problems existing in the stronger protection of fashion and luxury goods.

759512.label: Major findings and research outcome
759512.value: Social inequality has been growing around the world in general and in mainland China and Hong Kong in particular. The project argues that intellectual property protection of fashion designs and brands must respond to the need for promoting social justice. From this perspective, any proposals that are intended to provide stronger intellectual property protection of fashion designs and brands must consider their implications for affecting the capabilities of the poor to achieve individual human development and further participate in economic, social, and political activities in society. Moreover, the project puts forward the idea of “ethical responsibility initiative.” It requires fashion and luxury companies to take on an ethical responsibility to actively disseminate information about the plight of human life under absolute poverty. The project further examines how trademark law should be reformed to foster and promote the ethical responsibilities of fashion and luxury companies. The project identifies trademark protection as the most important form of intellectual property protection for fashion brands. Anti-dilution protection is a key form of trademark protection for fashion designs and brands, in particular luxury brands. The project makes suggestions about how fashion companies and designers should better use Hong Kong and maindland China intellectual property laws to promote anti-dilution protection of their brands. The project puts forward proposals to reform global anti-dilution law that will impact legal protection of fashion designs and brands in mainland China and Hong Kong. Moreover, the project offers suggestions on how fashion and luxury companies could effectively enforce their trademark rights in mainland China and Hong Kong. Research outputs are as follows: a. 1 edited volume to be published by Oxford University Press; b. 6 papers published in law journals and edited volumes; c. 2 papers under review; d. multiple lectures and presentations delivered at leading conferences and law schools such as the University of Pennsylvania Law School and UC Davis Law School.

759512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
759512.value: Further research is needed to examine the growing patterns of social inequality. The project focuses on income inequality as a major standard to weigh social impacts of stronger intellectual property protection of fashion designs and brands. Social inequality could also be examined from other perspectives, such as gender inequality and racial inequality. Moreover, further research could be done to explore the implications of stronger intellectual property for dealing with other forms of social inequality. It is expected that fashion and luxury companies will launch new litigations. There will be a need to monitor whether there will be new intellectual property issues arising from those litigations. The production and consumption of fashion products have impact on environmental protection. For example, the wide use of cotton as materials of fashion products has negative impact on the preservation of water resources. The waste treatment of used fashion products has impact on environmental protection. Therefore, further research is needed to study the impact of stronger intellectual property protection of fashion designs and brands on environmental protection.

759512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
759512.value: This research project examines how fashion designs and brands should be protected by intellectual property law in mainland China and Hong Kong. We do need to protect intellectual property rights that fashion companies and designers enjoy. The project finds that trademark protection is essential for fashion companies to do business in both mainland China and Hong Kong. It puts forward proposals to revise trademark law in order to better protect fashion designs and brands. The proposals focus on anti-dilution protection, a key form of trademark protection. On the other hand, as our society has become increasingly unequal in terms of income distribution, intellectual property protection of fashion designs and brands must respond to the need for promoting social justice. This research project proposes an “ethical responsibility model” to deal with social injustice that may be caused by intellectual property protection of fashion designs and brands.

760112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
760112.value: This project examines an, as yet, unexplored intersection of two international research agendas - health communication and health literacy. Drawing on predominantly process data such as patient surveys, researchers in the fields of health, psychology and sociology have established a causal relationship between clinical communication and patient outcomes, both in terms of satisfaction and health status. While some work has been undertaken in the relatively new field of discourse analysis in healthcare, particularly work on studies of real-time clinical communication, the connection to patient literacy has not been explored. Drawing on patient health literacy assessments, researchers in the relatively new field of health literacy have established patient health literacy as a factor associated with poor health outcomes. These research agendas have; however, developed independently. Additionally, the research undertaken in these fields has been predominantly in monolingual, English dominant contexts. This project seeks to explore an intersection between health communication and health literacy in a unique multilingual context – Hong Kong. The project’s hypothesis is that patient health literacy data can inform and reshape provider patient communications. The clinical consultation in dentistry will be the site for a case study of health literacy and clinical communication. The proposed research program will, therefore, explore the following related issues within dentistry: How is clinical communication situated in conceptual models of (oral) health literacy? What constitutes multilingual clinical communication in Hong Kong? How do adult oral health literacy assessments inform clinical interactions? In order to make evidence-based recommendations for appropriate community intervention programmes in clinical communication, we first need to understand the dimensions of the issue. The development of a robust corpus of clinical discourse will be the first step. We will then explore evidence of more complex dimensions of what constitutes (oral) health literacy. This will enable us to understand areas of connect and disconnect between the oral health literacy expectations of oral health care workers and the oral health literacy levels of their patients. Project outcomes will include: a refined theoretical model of oral health literacy; a typology of patterns of clinical discourse; and the development of training materials and a workshop for dentists and their support staff. 摘要: 本計劃査考一個到目前為止仍未探討過的兩個國際研究議題 - 醫療溝通與醫療讀寫能力。借鑒一系列主要數據如病人調查，於醫療、心理學和社會學等領域的研究人員在臨床溝通和患者的治療效果（滿意度和健康狀況）之間已建立了一個因果的關係。雖然篇章分析(discourse analysis)應用在醫療健康（特別是在實時臨床溝通）領域分面的研究已在進行中，但在病人讀寫能力方面的探討卻並未開展。研究人員在不同的測試中已證實病人的醫療讀寫能力可導致不理想的醫療結果。可是此類研究事項屬於個別性質，而且大多已英語為主。這計劃試圖探討在香港這多元的語言系统中，醫療溝通與醫療讀寫能力的交匯點。 這計劃的假設是病人的醫療讀寫能力數據可以建議及改善提供者與病人之間的溝通。牙科臨床諮詢為課題的研究地點，所以此研究將會探討以下牙科的相關問題：口腔讀寫能力的概念模型甚樣應用於臨床溝通上？香港的多元語系在臨床溝通上由什麼組成？成人的口腔讀寫能力測試可甚樣提升臨床上的溝通？ 要在臨床溝通上提供有證據基礎的建議給將來的社區改善項目，我們首先要了解此課題的各層面。發展健全的臨床論述主體是第一步，之後再探討口腔讀寫能力在更複習層面上的組成成份。這將會讓我們了解口腔提供者對口腔讀寫能力的期望與病人口腔讀寫能力的水平之間的關係。計劃預期的結果包括：口腔讀寫能力的改進理論模型；臨床論述上的類型學模式以及開發訓練材料和工作坊給與牙科醫生及其工作人員。

760112.label: Realisation of objectives
760112.value: 1) To re-conceptualise health literacy with regard to clinical communication in multilingual contexts. This has been fully achieved through our development of a new conceptualization of mediated interpreting has been presented and published to an international audience. 2) To examine the impact of health literacy assessments on clinical communication. This has been fully achieved. The results of the health literacy assessments were used for descriptive (cohort trends) and discriminatory purposes (selection of case studies) in the multiple methods approach. 3) To examine multi-party formulations involving health care workers as spoken interpreters. This has been fully achieved with an original typology published by "Social Science and Medicine" (IF2.8) which describes the patterns of engagement of health care workers in face-to-face interpreting events. 4) To disseminate the findings of the project to the professional community through a workshop for dental professionals and publications in medical education and communication journals. This is well achieved and ongoing. Within the lifespan of the project, we have achieved significant local and international dissemination. Workshops and symposia have shared findings with dentistry and the wider health sciences professions. Peer-reviewed international publications and prestigious international presentations have been achieved and are ongoing.

760112.label: Major findings and research outcome
760112.value: The major findings add new insights as to the communicative dimension of oral health literacy in multilingual consultations and support approaches building personalized care and patient empowerment. 1) Three patterns of mediated interpreting were identified from the recorded corpus of triadic and multi-party multilingual formulations: i. dentist designated expansions ii. dentist initiated interpretations iii. assistant initiated interpretations to both the dentist and patient. Pattern three, rather than negatively perceived as has been found in the literature, was framed more positively in our corpus analysis in responding to either patient difficulties or specific clinical task routines. 2) The project resulted in the novel application of visual text analytics software in representing themes and interactions in clinical consultations. Leximancer ™ software across the transcribed corpus indicated prominent themes while application of Discursis™ software illustrated temporal and topical structures and their distribution across turns-at-talk. Combining visual analytics with detailed Conversation Analysis of interpreter-mediated turn construction units (TCUs) was novel to the field of healthcare communication. Conversation analysis supported earlier findings regarding patterns of interpreting in adult dental consultations, however, the role of the nurse interpreter in parent/ primary caregiver education and patient management was more distinctive in the pediatric corpus. 3) The undergraduate project indicated that consultation opening question types in the majority appear to be similar across the two healthcare contexts of dentistry and medicine. Results suggest that linguistic and cultural differences, along with the specific contextual demands of return visit consultations directly influence the formulation of opening questions in dentistry in Hong Kong. 4) The Master of Dental Surgery (MDS) in Paediatric Dentistry project’s multiple methods study of the interactional corpus examined the body language of the dental team and child patients (age 5 to 12 years) during routine paediatric dentistry checkups and consultations. A new coding system was developed to analyze how verbal as well as non-verbal communication strategies are used together to achieve cooperation of young patients. This study demonstrated how video-analysis and non-verbal coding system can enhance the understanding of non-verbal interactions between the dental team and their patients. 5) The ongoing PhD project is exploring how multilingual and multicultural clinical consultations co-construct intercultural understandings. Pilot analysis of miscommunications has been presented in international and local meetings and transcript/ data analysis sessions. 6) Methodological contributions include new approaches to multiparty videoing in clinics and application of Transana™ for transcription and data management of a unique systematic archive in Chinese multilingual settings.

760112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
760112.value: Analysis of the extensive transcribed video database by the project team is ongoing with further publications in progress. The PhD student research is contributing original lines of analysis from this extensive corpus of transcribed video records. The team has joined a new Hong Kong-Macau initiative to promote Conversation Analysis in the region and hosted a HKU event with a Finnish collaborator in 2016. The Oral Health Literacy research agenda continues to be expanded with a GRF application by one of the project team members (McGrath) currently under review. The project PI (Bridges) joined a Finnish consortium examining healthcare interactions funded by the Academy of Finland/SRC (2016-2019) and hosted a project PI (Professor Johanna Ruusuvuori) in Hong Kong during 2016. In 2017, they plan to explore EU funding opportunities for cross-site (Finland-Hong Kong) discourse-based research in healthcare communication.

760112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
760112.value: This project examines the intersection of health communication and health literacy which were previously independent research fields. With the expanding global movement of healthcare professionals and their patients, issues of language and culture are adding to the interactional complexity of clinical communication. In a multilingual environment such as the biliterate and trilingual territory that is Hong Kong, healthcare professionals providing public services require complex repertoires of communication skills. Where spoken interpretation is required between the provider and patient, this is often conducted by auxiliary staff. While previous studies examined medical interpreting mainly in the context of interactions with immigrant communities in English-dominant countries, this study adopted an interactional approach to understanding the complexities of multilingual clinical consultations in an Asian medical context. Outcomes include: - new conceptualizations of ‘mediated interpreting’ in healthcare; - approaches to personalized care and patient empowerment in Hong Kong; and - innovations in multiple method approaches through principled adoption of health literacy and patient satisfaction assessments, Conversation Analysis, non-verbal observational analysis, and visual analytic approaches to examine the systematic and extensive video archive. The study is, therefore, contributing new understandings of how global intersections impact on health literacy and clinical communication within multilingual communities in Asia.

760212.label: Project Objectives
760212.value: The overall goal is to establish a WT1-reporter hESC model to identify, isolate, and characterize the human WT1 epicardial progenitor cells, and evaluate their therapeutic potential. Three independent but complementary specific experimental objectives will be pursued: Objective 1: To identify human WT1 epicardial progenitor cells by creating WT1-reporter human embryonic stem cell lines. To test our hypothesis: A. human WT1 epicardial progenitor cells are derived from ISL1 primordial cardiac progenitors; B. human WT1-derived cardiomyocytes display unique epicardial features, two independent hESC lines will be generated in this proposal. With a genetic lineage tracing strategy, we will examine whether hESC-derived WT1+ are able to differentiate into cardiomyocytes, smooth muscle and endothelial cells. The functional and structural properties of human WT1-derived cardiomyocytes will be further assessed to determine whether they have characteristics for better functional integration or display unique epicardial signatures, such as shorter action potential durations etc. 1). 760212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
760212.value: 心血管疾病是世界上的第一致死疾病。虽然近年来发展了治疗心血管疾病的各种医药和手术治疗手段，但是没有能在根本上解决治愈问题。干细胞治疗可以替换疾病心肌细胞为正常健康的心肌细胞，为将来高效的治疗多种心血管疾病提供了希望。为了进一步促进这方面的研究，最重要的是发现真正适合用于治疗心血管疾病的心脏干细胞。最近，科学家们新发现了一种来源于心外膜的小鼠心脏干细胞。这种来源于心外膜的心脏干细胞从心脏的表层向内迁移，可以进一步分化成心肌细胞、主动脉的平滑肌和心脏内皮细胞。更人兴奋的是，科学家发现一种小鼠在心肌受损下激活的成体心脏干细胞，表达和心外膜的心脏干细胞一样的重要基因标记，并且具有进一步分化成新心肌细胞的能力。在大量小鼠实验的基础上，我们假设人类也存在来源于心外膜的心脏干细胞，并且此心外膜心脏干细胞将是适合用于治疗心血管疾病的心脏干细胞来源。为了验证这一假设，我们将利用人类多功能干细胞为研究材料，进行体内和体外的实验，来检测和揭示人类心外膜的心脏干细胞的特性和用于治疗心血管疾病的潜力。

760212.label: Realisation of objectives
760212.value: The main hypothesis of objectives 1 and 2 was that the WT1+ cells are epicardial progenitor cells during human heart development. We were trying to address this hypothesis by creating WT1-reporter hESC lines to determine the multipotency and differentiation potential of human WT1+ epicardial cells during in vitro cardiogenesis. The originally methods proposed involving BAC recombineering, construction of gene-targeting vectors and genetic manipulation of hESCs were technically challenging and leading to conflicting results. Multiple alternative approaches have been attempted to pool out the WT1+ cells during in vitro cardiac differentiation of hESC. First, a lentiviral-based approach was initially attempted for establishing a stable reporter hESC line. For that, lentiviral vector containing EGFP reporter driven by WT1 promoter (pLV-WT1-EGFP) was constructed and applied to transducer hESC line (HES2). Preliminary study showed that the EGFP signals mirror the expression profile of WT1 during cardiac differentiation. However, the dynamic range of the EGFP signals was in a narrow range that the identification of the WT1+ cells using FACS turned out to be limited. We then adopted a published protocol to obtain the WT1+ epicardial lineage by manipulating the WNT signals during cardiac differentiation [1]. By introducing additional WNT signals (BMP4) at specific time point (day 4) during cardiac differentiation, we were able to generate an epithelial-like cell population which was WT1+, representing the epicardial lineage (Figure 1). Our attempt to further differentiate the WT1+ population however did not lead to functional cardiomyocytes. As an alternative approach, we then proceed to characterize the functional role of WT1 by studying the consequence of forced overexpression of the protein in early-staged hESC-derived cardiomyocytes (CMs) (day 20-30 post-differentiation). Significant overexpression of the different isoforms of the WT1 protein was achieved by lentiviral-based vectors (pLV-EF1-EGFP-WT1ABD-T2A-Puro) (Figure 2A). Overexpression of both WT1 isoforms resulted in significant electrophysiological changes. qRT-PCR analysis showed down-regulation of several Ca2+ handling genes transcript (Figure 2B); the action potential (AP) profile of the WT1-overexpressed hESC-VCMs demonstrated significantly depolarized maximal diastolic potential (MDP), APD shortening (Figure 2C&D), parameters resembling immature or epicardial CMs properties [2]. Consistent with the findings in mice that 77% of those Wt1+ cells co-express cardiac progenitor marker – Isl1 [4], indicating that adult Wt1+ cells might need to re-enter the Isl1 progenitor stage to gain multipotency, we previously reported the discovery of WT1 in hESC-derived ISL1+ and NKX2.5+ cardiac progenitors [3] and the existence of WT1 in human heart by immunostaining. Taken together with the present observations, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of ISL1+ human ventricular progenitors (HVPs) by using the kidney capsule model of the immunocompromised NSG mice. After transplantation for 2 months, an apparently pure, fully vascular human ventricular muscle wall (MLC2v+) was formed and sustained on the surface of the murine kidney in post-transplantation, suggesting coordination of vasculogenic paracrine cues derived from the HVPs. Moreover, purified GFP-labeled HVPs injected intra-myocardially into the hearts of the NSG mice migrated to the epicardium in 2 weeks post-transplantation. These data demonstrate that the transplanted HVPs showed decent survivability and functional integration, therefore implying promising therapeutic potential. Based on the above collective data set, one manuscript has been submitted and is being revised for publication. Another is in preparation and will be submitted in the coming 8-12 weeks.
