760212.label: Major findings and research outcome
760212.value: By manipulating the WNT signals [1], we found that a WT1+ population can be derived from in vitro cardiac differentiation of our hESCs. However, our initial attempt to further differentiate the WT1+ population failed to obtain cTNT+ cardiomyocytes, with the WT1 expression remained high. These results are not consistent with the published data in animal studies showed that the in vivo multipotent WT1+ cells give rise to cardiomyocytes, smooth muscle cells and endothelial cells during heart formation [5]. Our results suggest possible insufficiency of the in vitro system that we have enrolled as our model, as compare to the complex in vivo system of the animal studies. On the other hand, our WT1 overexpression study signified possible deterministic roles of the protein in the epicardial lineage. Overexpression of the WT1 protein in early-staged hESC-CMs significantly altered the electrophysiological properties. The overall altered AP phenotype as revealed by patch clamp assay suggested that the WT-overexpressing CMs displayed an altered electrophysiological phenotype with depolarized MDP and shortened APD that resembled properties of immature and epicardial lineage. However, the cardiac ion channels and Ca2+ handling genes transcripts expression profile were only subtly changed. Further investigation will be needed to address whether a higher level of WT1 protein overexpression can lead to more drastic functional changes of the hESC-CMs. Moreover, evaluation of the ISL1+ Human ventricular progenitors (HVPs) in transplantation models logically provides insight regarding the therapeutic potential of the WT1+ epicardial cells, given the close developmental relation of the WT1+ and ISL1+ progenies demonstrated by previous studies in mice and human.

760212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
760212.value: As pointed out in the last section, possible insufficiency of the in vitro system that we used for obtaining the human WT1+ population may have affected subsequent differentiation of the population to cardiomyocytes, smooth muscle cells and endothelial cells, therefore producing conflicting results that are apparently inconsistent with the animal studies. Strategies of further differentiation of these WT1+ cells with supplementation of other cell types such as cardiac fibroblasts may impact on the potency and differentiation potential and address whether the in vitro system is insufficient. Further development of the WT1 overexpression strategy such as well control expression level and the optimal timing of the protein overexpression during cardiac differentiation is warrant for potential successful derivation of the epicardial lineage for therapeutic and other applications.

760212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
760212.value: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the world. While a wide array of medical and surgical therapies has been developed, few are curative. Novel therapeutic strategies such as stem cell therapy that replaces diseased, dysfunctional cells with healthy, functional cardiomyocytes could potentially provide more effective treatment for many forms of CVD. An optimal source of cardiac stem cells for achieving cardiac repair and regeneration is highly desired. We hypothesize that WT1-expressing epicardial cells are multipotent cardiac progenitors in human and might be a cellular source for cardiac repair and regeneration in CVD patients. In this work, we could generate human WT1+ epicardial cells during hESC differentiation. However, the potency and differentiation potential of these in vitro derived human WT1+ epicardial cells require further characterization and demonstration. On the other hand, our overexpression study apparently strengthened the deterministic roles of the WT1 protein in the epicardial lineage. Further development of the WT1 overexpression strategy (e.g., via induction by select transcription factors) may also be a promising approach to derive the human WT1 epicardial cells to realize their potential therapeutic and other applications.

760512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
760512.value: 除了生物信号之外，细胞也会对机械信号起反应。越来越多的证据表明，通过控制基质的强度或者施加外力为间充质干细胞营造一个机械微环境可以影响细胞的存活率，趋向性，增殖能力和分化能力。然而，我们对于间充质干细胞如何感受机械信号的了解实在是比较贫乏，这就阻碍了我们合理地将力学方法运用到基于生物反应器的组织工程上。 细胞-基质粘连素是一种连接细胞和细胞外基质（ECM）的结构，在细胞和它周围微环境的双向信号传导方面起着非常重要的作用。成纤维细胞在单层培养时，产生三种经典的细胞-基质粘连，分别叫做局部复合素（FC），局部粘连素（FA）和纤维粘连蛋白（FBA）。第四种细胞-基质粘连，被命名为三维基质粘连素（3DMA）。它最近被证明会在成纤维细胞生长在它自身分泌的细胞外基质的时候产生。在成纤维细胞单层培养中，机械作用力和细胞-基质粘连之间的联系被认为是通过内在或者外在力诱导的局部复合素（FC）形成局部粘连素（FA）然后形成纤维粘连蛋白（FB）的过程中产生的。然而，证明力学作用诱导的三维基质粘连素（3DMA）的直接证据还很缺乏。 我们的最终目的是通过生物反应器培养出有功能作用的组织。然而如果不了解间充质干细胞在三维模型中如何通过基质粘连素（MAs）感受机械力信号，这个目标就不可能实现。基于我们以及其他研究人员报道的基于力学诱导的间充质干细胞的变化，以及我们尚未发表的非常让人兴奋的关于干细胞-基质相互作用的数据结果，我们设想在三维模型中机械力可以通过干细胞-基质粘连素的成熟增强间充质干细胞-基质间的相互作用，同时增强间充质干细胞的有关功能，包括迁移，增殖和分化能力。这些不仅在科学研究层面让人兴奋，而且同组织工程的实际应用密切相关，（1）可以在我们建立好的三维模型中研究间充质干细胞-基质粘连素的性质；（2）可以证实加上机械力作用之后间充质干细胞-基质粘连素的特定成熟性的时间空间变化；（3）可以阐明机械力刺激所诱导的间充质干细胞-基质粘连素在影响细胞活性方面的功能重要性。 这项工作会直接影响到这整个研究领域，通过立即产生新的理念--关于间充质干细胞在三维模型中如何感受机械力信号和研究间充质干细胞-基质相互作用和细胞活性的联系。而长期的影响在于，有助于在生物反应器内研制功能性的组织器官时运用合理的力学刺激方法。

760712.label: Realisation of objectives
760712.value: We have fully completed Objectives 1, 2 and 3, and completed 85% of Objective 4 (please see below). The remaining experiments for Objective 4 will be completed within the next 3-4 months. Objective 1: The NZBWF1/J mouse spontaneously develops clinical features of lupus nephritis such as anti-dsDNA antibody production, proteinuria, and systemic and intra-renal inflammation, and is an established murine model of lupus nephritis. Female NZBWF1/J mice with active disease were administered PBS, control IgG or murine anti-annexin II antibodies that block annexin II binding to plasminogen (0.5mg/kg body weight) by tail vein injection once weekly for periods up to 10 weeks. Administration of anti-annexin II antibodies exacerbated disease progression as demonstrated by a significant increase in serum urea and creatinine levels and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (P<0.05 for all, compared to control IgG), but had no effect on anti-dsDNA antibody level or body weight when compared to control mice. Kidney histology in NZBWF1/J mice with active disease treated with PBS showed increased mesangial proliferation, glomerular hypertrophy, accumulation of matrix proteins, and mononuclear cell infiltration into the periglomerular and interstitial space. Similar findings were observed in mice treated with control IgG. In mice treated with anti-annexin II antibodies, further kidney deterioration was observed as denoted by the presence of glomerulosclerosis, intense infiltration of immune cells and tubular atrophy. Objectives 2 and 3: Iron-containing Dynabeads were administered by intra-cardiac perfusion into control and treated NZBWF1/J and BALB/c mice, and were trapped in the glomerular capillaries. Glomeruli containing Dynabeads were isolated from BALB/c and NZBWF1/J mice, concentrated using a magnetic stand and used to assess the expression of annexin II expression and markers of inflammation, fibrosis and fibrinolysis. Annexin II was weakly expressed in the glomeruli of BALB/c mice and its expression did not change with age. Similar finding were observed in pre-nephritic NZBWF1/J mice. Gene and protein expression of annexin II increased in NZBWF1/J mice from 24 to 32 weeks of age when their kidneys demonstrated proliferative nephritis and decreased thereafter with glomerulosclerosis. Annexin II co-localized with p11, its binding protein, in the glomerulus. At the ultrastructural level, immunogold labelling of annexin II was occasionally detected in mesangial and endothelial cells in Control mice. In NZBWF1/J mice, increased immunoglold labelling of annexin II was observed along the cell membrane of mesangial cells, within the mesangial matrix, in endothelial cells and podocytes and in electron-dense deposits present in the glomerular basement membrane. Increased glomerular expression of annexin II was accompanied by increased expression of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), fibronectin, laminin, collagen, IL-6, TNF-alpha, MCP-1 and RANTES, but decreased expression of tissue- and urokinase-plasminogen activator (tPA and uPA respectively). Increased glomerular annexin II expression was also accompanied by increased mesangial proliferation and apoptosis, the latter determined by TUNEL staining and increased cleaved caspase 3 expression. Annexin II contributed to plasmin generation in the kidney. Objective 4: Mesangial cells were isolated from the kidneys of BALB/c and NZBWF1/J mice and used to assess the role of annexin II in cellular functions pertaining to cell proliferation, apoptosis, induction of coagulation and fibrinolytic mediators, inflammation and fibrosis. When compared to mesangial cells derived from BALB/c mice, mesangial cells from lupus-prone mice exhibited a 1.5-fold increase in cell proliferation, increased IL-6 and MCP-1 secretion, increased activation of MAPK, PKC and AKT/PI3K signaling pathways, and increased expression of annexin II, p11, PAI-1, tPA, fibronectin and collagen. Increased MAPK and AKT/PI3K activation contributed to increased annexin II expression. Gene silencing of annexin II significantly decreased mesangial cell proliferation, IL-6 and fibronectin expression. One of our post-graduate students was given this research proposal as his 4-year PhD project, but after working on the project for 20 months, informed us that he had to leave Hong Kong and return to China for personal reasons. It took many months before we identified a suitable research staff to continue with the study. We have completed 85% of Objective 4 and the remaining experiments will be completed within the coming 3-4 months.

760712.label: Major findings and research outcome
760712.value: In our previous study that was funded by the RGC GRF, we demonstrated that anti-dsDNA antibodies bound to annexin II on the surface of human mesangial cells and through this interaction, mediated downstream inflammatory and fibrotic processes. In this study, we furthered this study to investigate the effect of anti-annexin II antibodies, with known activity to suppress annexin II binding to plasminogen, on pathogenesis in NZBWF1/J mice. Treatment of mice with anti-annexin II antibodies had no effect on anti-dsDNA antibody production, but exacerbated nephritis as depicted by increased serum urea and creatinine levels, proteinuria, glomerulosclerosis, interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy, when compared to control mice. Our data suggest that by inhibiting annexin II binding to plasminogen and subsequent generation of plasmin may contribute to disease progression. Intra-glomerular annexin II expression, at the transcription and translation levels, increased during proliferative nephritis in NZBWF1/J, but decreased during glomerulosclerosis and co-localized with p11, suggesting that the biological functions of annexin II is mediated by its heterotetrameric rather than its monomeric form. At the ultrastructural level, annexin II localized to the cell membrane of mesangial cells and mesangial matrix and also with electron-dense immune deposits in the glomerular basement membrane. Increased annexin II expression was accompanied by increased fibrinogen, plasminogen, t-PA, fibronectin and collagen but not u-PA expression. Annexin II increased plasmin generation. Mesangial cells isolated from NZBWF1/J mice synthesized more annexin II than mesangial cells from BALB/c mice and this was accompanied by increased cell proliferation, secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines and fibronectin expression, which were all significantly decreased following annexin II gene silencing. Taken together, our results demonstrated that annexin II plays a critical role in plasmin generation, and in inflammatory and fibrotic processes in lupus nephritis. Part of the data have been submitted to Clinical Science and the manuscript is under revision. Another manuscript is currently being written up, which describes the role of annexin II in the coagulation/fibrinolytic cascade in lupus nephritis. Part of the data generated from this study have also been included in three invited reviews published in Special Issues in Clinical and Developmental Immunology, Frontiers in Immunology, and Clinical Immunology. Data generated from this study have been accepted for poster presentation at three international meetings, of which one abstract was presented at the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week 2016 - the top ranked international nephrology conference.

760712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
760712.value: In this study, we demonstrated that anti annexin II antibodies contributed to pathogenesis in lupus-prone mice. In order to determine whether anti-annexin II antibodies also plays a role in the clinical setting, further studies will be conducted to investigate the presence of annexin II-binding immunoglobulins in lupus nephritis patients and their role in fibrinolysis. We have already measured annexin II-binding IgG level in patients with lupus nephritis, patients with non-lupus renal disease and healthy subjects and demonstrated that seropositivity rate was significantly higher in lupus nephritis patients compared to control groups, and was associated with anti-dsDNA antibody level and disease activity. This suggests that annexin II-binding IgG are pathogenic. Further development of this research project will include the generation of annexin II knockout mice to validate our in vivo and in vitro data and confirm the role of annexin in plasmin generation in the kidney. Since annexin II was also observed in podocytes, glomerular endothelial cells and proximal tubular epithelial cells, we will apply for funding support from the Food and Health Bureau and RGC General Research Fund to investigate the role of annexin II in resident renal cells and their contribution to kidney inflammation and fibrosis.

760712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
760712.value: Kidney involvement, i.e. lupus nephritis is a severe organ manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus and accounts for much morbidity and mortality. Lupus nephritis is common in this locality, and is characterized by production of autoantibodies and immune-mediated kidney injury. The underlying mechanisms that initiate onset of lupus nephritis remain to be fully elucidated. Although treatment of lupus nephritis has improved considerable over the past decades, a proportion of patients will progress to end-stage renal failure. Identifying key factors that contribute to pathogenesis may lead to novel therapeutic intervention to further improve clinical outcomes. We previously demonstrated a pathogenic role of annexin II in inflammatory processes in lupus patients. Seropositivity of annexin-II binding IgG were significantly higher in lupus nephritis patients compared to healthy subjects or patients with non-lupus renal diseases. To explore the pathogenic nature of annexin II binding IgG, we administered anti-annexin II antibodies to lupus-prone mice and demonstrated that they exacerbated kidney injury. Annexin II expression was increased in proliferative nephritis and contributed to increased cell proliferation, apoptosis, plasmin generation, cytokine release and fibronectin synthesis. Our data provide further insight into the pathogenic role of annexin II and anti-annexin II antibodies in lupus nephritis.

761812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
761812.value: 許多神經性疾病成因都源於神經回路中興奮性和抑制性突觸傳遞的失衡。在負責感知重力的前庭神經核團中亦發現類似現象。當在前庭神經回路的發育關鍵期內干擾正常的GABA能抑制性神經信號的傳遞時，我們發現這不但會導致腦內空間圖譜的重構，而且還會推遲初生動物對感知重力所引發行為的出現。因此我們認為調控GABA能神經突觸的傳遞效率會對實現正常的與前庭相關行為具有非常重要的作用。 最近，作為逆向信使的內源性大麻素被認為是引起GABA能神經突觸長時程壓抑 (iLTD)的主要原因。因此我們推測，在前庭神經核團中調節內源性大麻素引起的iLTD會影響個體空間識別能力的形成。首先，我們使用膜片鉗的方法確認內源性大麻素是由突觸後神經元釋放, 然後作用在突觸前膜的受體上，從而影響突觸前膜釋放GABA的效率。通過使用內源性大麻素受體的激動劑和拮抗劑，我們將評估這一逆向神經信號通路對iLTD的產生和感知重力所引發行為出現的相關性。研究結果， 對了解如何通過調節前庭突觸中內源性大麻素受體的抑制性神經信號， 影響發育過程中與前庭相關行為的表現具有重要意義。 我們初步的實驗結果顯示, 內源性大麻素誘導的iLTD只出現在發育期，有別於一般認為成熟期的抑制性神經傳遞水準要高於發育期。由此，我們進一步推測在成熟期的前庭回路中降低抑制性神經傳遞水準能恢復誘導iLTD這種電生理現象。而抗抑鬱精神藥fluoxetine就是一個理想的藥物來檢測我們的推論。我們將嘗試採用這種抗抑鬱藥，通過其降低細胞外GABA水平來檢測它是否能夠恢復成熟期內iLTD，以及由此實現前庭相關的生理功能。這項研究會對治療成年前庭神經疾病提供有益的借鑒。

761812.label: Realisation of objectives
761812.value: Using whole-cell patch-clamp technique on rat brainstem slices, we demonstrated that type B neurons in the medial vestibular nucleus (MV) are the major contributors to long-term depression (LTD) of GABAA receptor(R)-mediated postsynaptic current. We found that the expression of such plasticity of type B neurons is restricted by neuromodulator serotonin (5-HT). Interestingly, the probability of inducing such LTD decreased with postnatal maturation (from 70% at P5 to 20% at P28). To test whether the induction of LTD in MV neurons is regulated via a presynaptic mechanism, we tested another neuromodulator endocannabinoid (eCB) which is known to mediate presynaptic plasticity in the forebrain. Our immunohistochemical results showed age-dependent expression of cannabinoid receptor type 1 (CB1R) by MV neurons. By applying CB1R antagonist (AM251) to the recording chamber for patch-clamp study, we observed that the proportion of P57 neurons showing GABAAR-mediated LTD decreased to 30%. Similar results were observed in P57 rats in which the MV was infused with AM251 at P1. On the other hand, the proportion of LTD-expressing MV neurons in P810 rats increased to 70% with bath application of CB1R agonist WIN55. Similar results were observed in in P810 rats in which the MV was infused with WIN55 at P1. These demonstrate that CB1R mediates developmental regulation of presynaptic plasticity of GABA synapses in the MV. To elucidate the mechanism underlying change in the proportion of LTD-expressing cells in rats that were pretreated at P1 with CB1R agonist/antagonist, drugs that act on the degradation or biosynthesis of 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG, an endogenous ligand of CB1R) were used. In the presence of JZL184 (known to inhibit the degradation of 2-AG, thereby increasing the concentration of 2-AG), the proportion of LTD-expressing cells in P5-7 rats could restore back to 70% as in the control. We also conducted experiments in P8-10 rats pretreated with WIN55 at P1. Orlistat (known to inhibit the biosynthesis of 2-AG, thereby reducing the concentration of 2-AG) decreased the number of LTD-expressing cells to 30% as in the control. These results suggest that the level of endogenous 2-AG governs the induction of LTD in MV neurons of early postnatal rats. With the use of Cnr1 knockout mice, we further confirmed that eCB can presynaptically mediate basic synaptic transmission and CB1R plays an important role in GABAergic LTD. Unlike other forebrain neurons, Group I metabotropic glutamate receptor does not contribute to the release of endogenous eCB from postsynaptic MV neuron. We therefore tested other potential candidates, viz. 5-HT receptor and cholecystokinin (CCK) receptor. Agonist of 5-HT2 receptor increased the probability of LTD induction in P8-10 MV neurons from 25% to 75%. On the other hand, antagonist of 5-HT2 receptor decreased in P57 cells the probability of LTD induction from 80% to 30%. Similarly, agonist of CCKB receptor increased in P911 MV neurons the probability of LTD induction from 25% to 50%. On the other hand, antagonist of CCKB receptor decreased in P58 cells the probability of LTD induction from 70% to 50%. Altogether, we demonstrate that 5-HT receptor and CCK receptor are involved in triggering the release of 2-AG which in turn suppresses inhibitory synaptic transmission in the MV. To investigate the effects of eCB in the expression of vestibular behavior during postnatal development, rats pre-implanted at P1 with Elvax loaded with WIN55 or AM251 were tested for innate vestibular behavior as well as for vestibular-related learning behavior. With the use of negative geotaxis test for gravity detection, we found that the emergence of re-orienting behavior was accelerated from P7 in control rats to P5 in AM251-treated rats, but delayed to P9 in WIN55-treated rats. In dead reckoning test (in dark) for spatial navigation, adult rats pretreated with WIN55 at P1 showed difficulty in finding their way home. Interestingly, such effects were not observed in adult rats pretreated with AM251 or WIN55 at P12, indicating a critical period in the first 2 postnatal weeks during which eCB in the MV modulates the acquisition of vestibular-related spatial navigation. Therefore, our results highlight the importance of eCB signaling in developing MV synapses for the expression of vestibular behaviors. Given that antidepressant fluoxetine (a serotonin reuptake inhibitor) is known to restore ocular dominance plasticity in adult rats, we investigated the role of fluoxetine on the reactivation of LTD plasticity of MV neurons and in turn its impact on the vestibular circuitry implicated in motor learning. We found that interference of GABA transmission in the MV with bicuculline (antagonist of GABAAR) at P1 resulted in derangement of spatial navigation in adult rats. Such behavioral deficit was not observed if bicuculline was administered after P14. This enables us to identify a critical period during which navigational behavior is shaped by GABA transmission in the MV. However, simultaneous treatment of bicuculline with fluoxetine during P21-28 resulted in a severe navigation derangement in adulthood. We therefore investigated the effect of fluoxetine on synaptic plasticity. In P28 rats that were fed with fluoxetine from P21, there was a significance increase in the proportion of MV neurons exhibiting GABAAR-mediated LTD (53% compared with 22% in the control). Interestingly, this high occurrence of LTD was comparable to that observed in normal rats

761812.label: Major findings and research outcome
761812.value: In this project, multi-disciplinary approaches were employed to address the contribution of neuromodulator to synaptic plasticity of inhibitory synapses in developing vestibular circuitry and subsequently to behavioral expression of vestibular functions. Type B neurons in the medial vestibular nucleus (MV) of rats are the major contributors to long-term depression (LTD) of GABAA receptor(R)-mediated postsynaptic current. During postnatal development, MV neurons showed significant changes in their electrophysiological properties. The expression of such plasticity in type B neurons is controlled by neuromodulators such as serotonin (5-HT) and eCB. [Ma et al. 2014; Li et al. 2017] MV neurons showed age-dependent expression of cannabinoid receptor type 1 (CB1R). We further observed that chronic infusion of the rat VN with CB1R agonist or antagonist at P1 resulted in (1) persistent modulation of LTD, (2) shifting the time for postnatal emergence of gravity-detection behavior, and (3) derangement of spatial navigation in adulthood. These results provide physiological evidence that eCB plays an important role during postnatal development of the vestibular system. We also identified a postnatal critical period during which eCB shapes GABA transmission in the MV and in turn modulates navigational behavior Data from Cnr1 knockout mice confirmed that eCB can presynaptically mediate basic GABAergic transmission. We also showed that both 5-HT receptor and cholecystokinin receptor are involved in the release of endogenous eCB for LTD induction. Activation of each of these receptors increases the probability of LTD induction by increasing the release of 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG) from postsynaptic MV neurons. Our pharmacological and behavioral results in rats further revealed a postnatal critical period during which eCB in the VN regulates the expression of vestibular-related behaviors. Altogether, these results for the first time unveil the functions of eCB-LTD during postnatal development of the vestibular system. [Shi et al.; in final preparation for submission – manuscript attached] Additionally, rats treated with the antidepressant fluoxetine (a serotonin reuptake inhibitor) from P21 were found to exhibit an increase in LTD expression to a level comparable with the neonatal stage. In these fluoxetine-treated rats, perturbation of neurotransmission in the VN could also induce impairment in spatial navigation at the adult stage (a phenomenon normally observed in neonates only). Thus, our findings demonstrated that reactivation of synaptic plasticity in the vestibular circuits for spatial learning can be made possible even in the mature sensorimotor system.

761812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
761812.value: We are the first group to demonstrate that endocannabinoid modulates the efficacy of GABAergic synapses within the VN in an age-dependent manner, thereby regulating activities of neural circuitry responsible for the expression of vestibular behavior. Our findings open up a novel research direction about the role of the neuromodulators in processing sensory information for guiding navigation. Research in these directions will shed light on the design of drugs for neuromodulator-based strategies that could rescue disorders for restoration of balance function. Furthermore, our findings provide the basis for investigating the effects of antidepressants on synaptic transmission in neural circuits mediating sensorimotor functions. In the future, mechanisms by which neuromodulator regulates synaptic plasticity can also be delineated with the application of combined techniques of optogenetics and chemogenetics in brain slices ex vivo and in awake animals. Data made available will unveil our understanding of the determinants for the reactivation of neural plasticity in adults and in turn their contribution to the treatment of neurological disorders.

761812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
761812.value: This project identified a novel period for consolidation of neural circuits for vestibular-related behavior during the early postnatal stage. This period was defined by characteristic neuronal activity and surface protein expression. Perturbations to the vestibular system during this period delayed emergence of vestibular reflexes and, furthermore, permanently deranged navigation performance in rodents. During this period, endocannabinoid and serotonin modulation the long lasting reduction in GABA-mediated synaptic transmission in the central vestibular system was found to be critical for correct development of vestibular functions. In addition, the neuronal release of endocannabinoid was found to be dependent on cellular signals triggered by neuromodulator serotonin and cholecystokinin. Interestingly, we observed treatment with the antidepressant fluoxetine (which increases extracellular serotonin) changed characteristics of the vestibular system back to a neonatal state. This was accompanied by impairment in spatial navigation induced by treatments which are effective in neonates only under normal circumstances. Our results therefore highlight the importance of neuromodulators in the processing of information for spatial navigation, and reveal the applicability of antidepressant in re-opening plastic processes involved in cognitive functions.

762312.label: Realisation of objectives
762312.value: Objective 1: Dissecting the roles of Sox2 in hair type specification by lineage analyses Predicting the spatiotemporal dynamics of hair follicle patterns in the developing mouse. We developed an expansion-induction (EI) model in which we applied the prediction that new follicle formation is driven by the physical growth of the embryo. The model accurately describes the positions of additional follicles emerging from skin explants. The EI model provides a simple and robust mechanism for predicting secondary space-filling patterns in growing embryos. This work was published [Cheng et al Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2014] and has been recommended by F1000 Prime. Sox2 maintains hair identity by repressing tertiary hair We addressed whether increased formation of tertiary hair and/or the secondary hair is mis-specified to tertiary hair in Sox2sLOF mutants by lineage analyses. In Sox2CreERT2/+ mice CreERT2 replaces the Sox2 gene, creating a null allele and is under Sox2 control. Using Sox2CreERT2/+ mice we determined cell fate and lineage of Sox2+ DP cells, tagging DP cells, and the fate of their descendents during follicle morphogenesis. We fate mapped DP cells in the different hair types of Sox2+/CreERT2; R26R-tdTomato (control) and Sox2Ysb/CreERT2; R26R-tdTomato. In control Sox+/CreERT2; R26R-tdTomato, all primary hair in P9 DP and 80% of secondary hair were labeled with tdTomato but none of the tertiary. Sox+/CreERT2 only labels the primary and secondary hair DP . Abnormally, in P9 SoxYsb/CreERT2; R26R-tdTomato mice approximately 6% of the SoxYsb/CreERT2; R26R-tdTomato tertiary hair were labeled with tdTomato. Down-regulation of Sox2 in the DP causes a fate switch of secondary DP progenitors into tertiary hair. Objective 2: Genes and pathways regulated by Sox2 and Sox18 in hair follicle pattern and Morphogenesis SOX2 controls hair pigmentation by repressing Agouti and antagonizing BMP signaling. We determined the transcriptomes of DP cells from E15.5 Sox2Egfp/+, Sox2Egfp/Ysb, Sox2Egfp/lcc, Sox2Egfp/+;Sox18LacZ/LacZ, and Sox2Egfp/Ysb;Sox18LacZ/LacZ mice and of P2 Sox2Egfp/+ and Sox2Egfp/Ysb. We identified Sostdc1, Corin as potential Sox2 targets. Comparing Sox2Egfp/+ control and Sox2sLOF mutants, we identified changes in Wnt signaling (Rspo1, Sfrp2, Sostdc1), Bmp signaling (Sost, Sostdc1) and melanogenesis (Corin). Agouti (Agp) controls the shift of eumelanin (black pigment) synthesis to pheomelanin (yellow pigment) generating a yellow stripe. Primary hairs are black and Agp is not expressed. In Sox2sLOF mutants, we found a yellow band in primary hairs, and the yellow band is extended in the secondary hairs. Hence the coats appear “yellow”. Agouti (Agp) in Sox2sLOF primary DP was ectopically expressed. Agp is initially expressed in secondary hair at P2, is sharply up-regulated at P4, and expression is diminished at P7. In Sox2sLOF mutants Agp is also initially expressed at P2 in secondary hair but expression is higher. Agp continued to be highly expressed in the secondary DP until P7. We identified Agp as a direct SOX2 target. Our data suggest Sox2 directly represses Agp expression. In Sox2sLOF mutants Agp is strongly upregulated in DP cells due to the absence of Sox2. Sostdc1 is down-regulated in the DP and ectopic Bmp signaling was found in follicular melanocytes in Sox2sLOF mutants. BMP signaling promotes the synthesis of phaoemelanin. Taken together, Sox2 expression in DP may play a central role in controlling hair pigmentation. The ectopic and extended expression of Agp and elevated Bmp signaling in melanocytes underlies aberrant yellow pigmentation in Sox2sLOF mutants. Objective 3. The impact of loss of Sox2 and Sox18 function on hair morphogenesis. Sox2 and Sox18 synergise to control hair morphogenesis and hair growth Hair morphogenesis is delayed in Sox2Egfp/Ysb;Sox18LacZ/LacZ double mutants. The induction of primary hair placodes at E14.5 was not altered in double mutants. At E15.5, primary and secondary hair placode were morphologically undistinguishable from controls. However at E17.5, in double mutants, the follicles in mutants still resembled earlier stage hair follicles unlike controls Although primary hairs were specified in Sox2Egfp/Ysb;Sox18LacZ/LacZ double mutants, morphogenesis and growth is compromised. In hair depilation assays we found Sox2sLOF mutants had lower hair regrowth rate and Sox2Egfp/Ysb;Sox18LacZ/LacZ double mutants had even slower regrowth rate after hair depilation at telogen stage. The onset of hair regeneration is not compromised in the mutants but the growth rate of the hair is retarded in Sox2sLOF mutants and is arrested in the Sox2Ysb/Ysb;Sox18LacZ/LacZ double mutants. DP cells from both Sox2sLOF mutants’ and double mutants have higher proliferation rate but had lower passage potential. Sox2 and Sox18 may regulate DP cell cycle and self-renewal. In mutants early exhaustion of progenitors may lead to slower hair regrowth. Notch signaling (NICD, Wnt5a, Hes) was downregulated in the hair placode at E15.5 in Sox2Egfp/Ysb;Sox18LacZ/LacZ mutants but not in Sox2sLOF or Sox18 mutant. This may compromise the self-renewal ability and hair regeneration ability.

762312.label: Major findings and research outcome
762312.value: Mammalian hair performs important functions such as for physical protection, thermoregulation, tactile sense and social interactions. Understanding their ability to grow and renew throughout life is particularly relevant to regenerative medicine. We addressed the fundamental question in Biology of how patterned arrays of hair follicles within epithelia are controlled. We have developed a novel approach to analyze hair follicle pattern in a quantitative way. This approach can be applied in other 2D repetitive pattern analyses. In addition, we have also proposed a new mechanism for hair follicle formation and this mechanism is able to accurately predict the hair follicle patterns This work was published in PNAS and this manuscript is recommended by F1000Prime. A fundamental goal in skin reconstitution is to achieve the correct pattern of sweat glands, follicles, their associated sebaceous glands, hair types. Hair type specification is an important process to establish functional skin appendages. However, the mechanism of hair type specification is not clear as there are no hair-type specific genetic manipulation reagent. We have investigated Cre activity Sox2CreERT2 in the dermal condensate during embryonic stages and in the dermal papilla in the neo-natal stages. We have shown that Sox2CreERT2 has hair type specific activity and can trace the lineages of the embryonic dermal condensate to the postnatal stages. This is the first inducible Cre line has been shown that have hair type specific Cre activity and would be a valuable tool to study hair type specification. Furthermore, we have shown that reduced dosage of Sox2 causes fate switching of the secondary dermal condensate (thicker hair-type) to tertiary dermal condensate (thinner hair type). Our study suggests that Sox2 plays a pivotal role in controlling hair type specification and the dosage of Sox2 may be related to hair miniaturization (a process before progressive alopecia). A manuscript describing these findings is in preparation. Our analyses suggest Sox2 may regulate hair pigmentation by direct repression of the Agp gene and by antagonizing Bmp signaling, explaining the yellow pigmentation phenotype of Sox2sLOF hair. We also demonstrated that Sox2 and Sox18 play a critical role in maintaining the DP self-renewal and the hair regeneration ability. Bioinformatics analysis of the transcriptome data from Sox2sLOF mutants, Sox18 mutant and the double mutants suggested that Sox2 and Sox18 may synergistically regulate Notch signaling in dermal condensates and the regulation are both direct and indirect.

762312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762312.value: Our result indicated that Sox2 may serve as a critical factor for hair pigmentation, hair type specification and hair size. These findings expand our understanding of Sox2 and Sox18 regulatory network in the dermal papilla and provide insight for the development of therapeutic approaches for progressive alopecia. Ectopic expression of Sox family of genes and over-activation of Notch signaling are frequently observed in many pathological conditions such as cancer development. The regulation mechanisms of Notch signaling by Sox family of genes is still elusive and context dependent. Our result has indicated that the DP may serve as a system to investigate the interaction of Sox2, Sox18 and Notch signaling. Transcriptional-direct and indirect mechanisms may be involved in Sox2, Sox18 and Notch regulatory networks in DP. The indirect regulation of Sox2 and Sox18 to Notch signaling components may involve protein-protein interactions. These interactions could be analyzed by further studies examining the protein interactome of Sox2 and Sox18 in the dermal papilla.

762312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762312.value: A fundamental goal in skin reconstitution is to achieve the correct pattern of sweat glands, follicles, hair types. We asked the fundamental question of how patterned arrays of hair follicles are controlled. Using the expression pattern of Sox2, in developing and growing skin, we developed a mathematical model that predicst the spatiotemporal dynamics of hair follicle patterns. Dermal papilla (DP) cells, hair follicle stem-like progenitors, are pivotal for induction, morphogenesis and growth of hair. Loss of expression of Sox2 and Sox18, in the DP causes changes in hair: a shift in proportions of hair types and changed pigmentation. We found Sox2 maintains proper proportion of hair types by repressing the formation of tertiary (kinked) hairs. Sox2 regulates yellow pigmentation by controlling the cyclic expression of the Agouti gene in the DP and BMP signaling activity in pigment producing melanocytes. We found Sox2 and Sox18 synergise to control hair growth and regrowth by controlling the Notch signaling pathway. Our study is relevant to human skin diseases e.g. hereditary hair loss/overgrowth and basal cell carcinoma. Hair follicles are potential rich sources of adult stem cells. Our studies are relevant to regenerative medicine, for potential applications for skin wound healing,hair replacement or restoration.

762412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
762412.value: 瑜伽和有氧運動對早期思覺失調患者的神經認知功能和腦部結構的影響－利用隨機對照臨床研究 研究背景 思覺失調症經常與認知問題和腦部結構的改變有關，如海馬體的體積縮小（Wright et al., 2000）。認知問題是預測社交和職業長期機能的其中一項重要指標（Green et al., 2000）。鑑於藥物治療對認知問題未見明顯成效（Addington, 2007），越來越多的研究開始集中在使用非藥物治療。近年研究顯示有氧運動不但對認知功能有益，更能有效地逆轉海馬體結構的改變（Pajonk et al., 2010）。除了有氧運動，其他運動亦可能對神經認知系統有良好的幫助。其中一种就是身心運動瑜伽。研究指出瑜伽除了可改善健康者的認知功能和腦部結構（Dash et al., 1999; Lazar et al., 2005），還能為一些女性精神病患者帶來幫助（Duraiswamy et al., 2007）。此項隨機對照臨床研究的目的是探究有氧運動和瑜伽對早期思覺失調女性患者的神經認知功能和腦部結構的長期形響。本研究亦會探究這兩種運動方式帶來的不同影響，以及對臨床和功能改變的影響。 研究方法 本研究從香港三家醫院共選取了120名早期思覺失調的女性患者（病期少於五年），這些病人被隨機分配到三個研究組別。第一組參與為期十二星期的綜合瑜伽治療（共40人）、第二組參與十二星期的有氧運動計劃(共40人)、第三組則為候補的對照組。研究小組在研究開始和十二星期療程結束時，紀錄下所有120名參與者的生理健康、病徵、認知功能、身體識別能力、服藥的依從性、生活質素、以及藥物副作用以作比較。此外，研究小組同時會收取每組首20 名參與者在十二星期前後的磁力共振影像，以關注腦部結構的改變。研究小組會於一年後跟進各參與者的認知功能，以發現治療的長期功效。 綜合瑜伽治療包括呼吸練習、體位法和放鬆法，由專業的瑜伽導師帶領練習，每次一個小時，每週三次，共12個星期。有氧運動計劃則包括二十分鐘的跑步機行走和三十分鐘的健身單車運動。每次運動為時五十至六十分鐘，每星期三次，為期十二星期。 研究假設 研究的主要結果是觀測不同運動對早期思覺失調患者的認知功能（記憶力和注意力）和腦部結構（海馬體和前扣帶皮質的體積）的影響。研究小組預料有氧運動和瑜伽都會對早期思覺失調女性患者的認知功能和腦部結構帶來好處。不過，不同的運動則會帶來不同的益處，有氧運動將有利於海馬體和記憶力，而瑜伽將有利於前扣帶皮質和注意力。 參考資料 Addington, J (2007). 762412.label: Major findings and research outcome
762412.value: When comparing all the three groups with a mixed-model, Group×Time interactions were statistically significant in verbal acquisition and retention, working memory, and attention, measured by HKLLT, Digit Span forwards and backwards tests, and Letter Cancellation test, respectively. The effect sizes were moderate-to-large for both yoga and aerobic exercise. Overall symptom severity improved both in yoga (F=11.87, P<0.01) and aerobic exercise (F=6.76, P=0.012) groups, largely related to improvement in the general subscale (with age, length of illness and antipsychotic dose as covariates). Negative symptoms improved in the yoga group (F=11.70, P<0.01). Depressive symptoms improved in both yoga (F=10.38, P<0.01) and aerobic exercise (F=8.79, P<0.01) groups after the 12-week intervention. Both yoga and aerobic exercise significantly improved the health-related quality of life assessed by the SF-36. Both types of exercise significantly improved ‘physical health (F=6.21, P=0.015 for yoga; F=15.52, P<0.01 for aerobic exercise), and ‘psychological health’ (F=9.37, P<0.01 for yoga; F=6.36, P=0.015 for aerobic exercise). We did not find significant changes in either congruent (F=1.3, P=0.28) or incongruent (F=1.7, P=0.18) conditions of the Stroop Color and Word Tests among three groups. There were no significant changes in Figure Rating Scale (F=0.04, P=0.96) for body perception, and Compliance Rating Scale (F=0.53, P=0.59) for medication adherence. When comparing the changes of hippocampal gray matter volumes among three groups using the FreeSurfer Linear Mixed Model, corrected by age and intracranial volume, aerobic exercise was associated with increased hippocampal gray matter volume (F=7.52, P=0.01), mainly related to increases in the left hippocampus (F=5.13, P=0.03). Yoga did not show significant changes in total hippocampal volume (F=1.07, P=0.31). The change in VO2 max/kg over time in all three groups was compared. The Group×Time interaction was not statistically significant between the three groups (F=0.77, P=0.47), with a trend of increased VO2 max/kg in aerobic exercise groups (7.7%). The correlation between the change in cognition and fitness parameters failed to reach statistical significance (total: r=0.07, P=0.42 for verbal memory, and r=0.06, P=0.51 for working memory). However, there was a positive correlation between the number of sessions participants attended and the change in working memory (total: r=0.26; P=0.02).

762412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762412.value: This study indicated the beneficial effect of exercise intervention on cognitive impairment, which was also demonstrated in structural brain changes. This important finding can potentially overcome the limited cognitive effect of pharmacological treatment in people with psychosis. The results has been presented in international academic conferences and local press conferences. Exercise intervention has been promoted among people with psychosis through community events, NGOs and hospital mental health services.

762412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762412.value: Impairments of attention and memory are evident in early psychosis, and are associated with functional disability. In a group of stable, medicated women patients, we studied the effect of aerobic exercise or yoga on cognitive impairments and clinical symptoms. A total of 124 female patients were randomized to 12 weeks of yoga, aerobic exercise or waitlist group. The primary outcomes were cognitive functions including memory and attention. Secondary outcome measures were the severity of psychotic and depressive symptoms, and hippocampal volume. We found both yoga and aerobic exercise groups demonstrated significant improvements in working memory with moderate to large effect sizes compared with the waitlist control group. The yoga group showed additional benefits in verbal acquisition and attention. Both types of exercise improved overall and depressive symptoms after 12 weeks. Small increases in hippocampal volume were observed in the aerobic exercise group compared with waitlist. Both types of exercise improved working memory in early psychosis patients, with yoga having a larger effect on verbal acquisition and attention than aerobic exercise. The application of yoga and aerobic exercise as adjunctive treatments for early psychosis merits serious consideration.

762712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
762712.value: The efficacy of T-cell based AIDS vaccine requires the induction of high frequencies of CD8+ effector and memory T cells. Viral-vector vaccines that induce such immunity can prevent or control pathogenic AIDS viral infections, but issues of pre-existing immunity and safety surround their implementation. To date, few AIDS vaccines elicit high frequency of HIV-1 specific CD8+ T cells in clinical development. Delivery of vaccine antigens to dendritic cell (DC) via various DC surface proteins improves antibody and CD4+ T cell responses, but which DC receptor targeting would intensify CD8+ T cell immunity remains elusive. Programmed death-1 (PD-1) binds to its ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2 expressed on DCs. In recent years, we have exploited this process for targeting of HIV-Gag to DCs as a fusion protein linked with the soluble domain of PD-1. By intramuscular immunization via electroporation (EP) of the fusion protein in the form of DNA vaccination, we elicited robust anti-Gag antibody titers in mice, with both IgG1 (Th2) and IgG2a (Th1) responses detected. Importantly, high frequencies of Gag-specific, broadly reactive and polyfunctional CD8+ T cells were induced. These responses were dose-dependent, long-lasting and conferred protection against pathogenic intranasal Vaccinia-WR-Gag challenges. Since similar CD8+ T cell responses have not been found with other antigen DC-targeting methods, we hypothesize that soluble PD-1-based DC-targeting may engage a distinct immune pathway in shaping the adaptive CD8+ T-cell immunity when compared with other DC-targeting molecules. The overall objective of the proposed study is, therefore, to determine the underlying mechanism of a sPD-1-based AIDS vaccine in mouse models with three specific aims: Aim 1: To determine the immunogenicity and efficacy profiles of two DC-targeting proteins in potentiating HIV Gag-specific CD8+ T-cell responses (year 1); Aim 2: To determine the involvement of DC subsets in potentiating HIV Gag-specific CD8+ T-cell responses (year 2); Aim 3: To determine the protective role of CD8+ T-cell immunity elicited by distinct DC-targeting vaccines (year 3). Our findings will not only lead to an improved design for an effective AIDS vaccine but also provide useful information to understand the fundamental T-cell immunity. 透過誘導高頻率活化性（effector）與記憶性（memory）CD8+ T細胞可維持以T細胞為基礎之愛滋病疫苗的效力。雖然病毒載體疫苗有能力誘導前述免疫能力，可防止或控制愛滋病病毒的感染與致病性，但要實施卻需考量體內對該載體的預存免疫力與安全性課題。至今，很少臨床實驗中之愛滋病疫苗可刺激高頻率且專一性的HIV-1 CD8+ T細胞。透過樹突細胞（Dendritic Cell）上的表面蛋白傳送疫苗抗原進入樹突細胞，可加強抗體與CD4+ T細胞的反應，但哪些樹突細胞接受體有助於增強CD8+ T細胞的免疫能力仍屬未知。程序性死亡因子1 (Programmed death-1，PD-1)與其在樹突細胞上表現之配體PD-L1及PD-L2結合。近年來，我們利用此結合能力，透過融合式蛋白與PD-1之可溶性區域結合，將HIV-Gag抗原送入樹突細胞內。透過電穿孔（Electroporation）將去氧核醣核酸疫苗（DNA Vaccines）態的融合蛋白在肌內免疫後，小鼠體內產生大量可被偵測之IgG1(Th2)及IgG2a(Th1)抗Gag抗體。尤為重要的是，我們發現此方法同時誘導高頻率具Gag專一性，廣泛性反應及多元功能的CD8+ T細胞。這些免疫反應為劑量依賴性，长時效性，並對透過鼻腔給予之致病性Vaccinia-WR-Gag產生保護功效。因類似的CD8+ T細胞反應並未在其他以樹突細胞為目標傳送抗原的方式上發現，故我們假設以可溶性PD-1為基礎的樹突細胞目標傳送抗原方式，可能透過不同於以其他樹突細胞為目標的分子之途徑，來雕塑CD8+ T細胞的後天免疫能力。因此，本計畫以小鼠為模式動物，其目的是利用可溶性PD-1為基礎之愛滋病疫苗來確認三個特定目標:一、確定兩種以樹突細胞為目標的蛋白對HIV Gag 專一性 CD8+ T細胞之免疫能力與效力（第一年）。二、確定參與此HIV Gag專一性之CD8+ T細胞反應的樹突細胞種類（第二年）。三、確定以樹突細胞為目標的特定疫苗所引發的CD8+ T細胞免疫效力的保護能力（第三年）。我們的發現不只可以增進設計有效愛滋病疫苗的能力，同時也提供有關T細胞免疫能力的重要基礎知識。

762712.label: Realisation of objectives
762712.value: The overall objective of this grant proposal is to investigate the mechanism of a soluble PD-1-based vaccine in amplifying antiviral CD8+ T-cell immunity. With our key emphasis on the induction of HIV-specific CD8 T cells, we propose a focused research program with three specific aims: 1) to determine the immunogenicity and efficacy profiles of two DC-targeting proteins in potentiating HIV Gag-specific CD8+ T-cell responses; 2) to determine the involvement of DC subsets in potentiating HIV Gag-specific CD8+ T cell responses; and 3) to determine the protective role of CD8+ T-cell immunity elicited by distinct DC targeting vaccines. To achieve these goals, we hypothesized that vaccine involving different DC-targeting proteins might result in distinct anti-HIV immune responses. To test this hypothesis, we have conducted proposed and additional experiments based on three specific aims. First, we not only compared two DC-targeting proteins PD1 and anti-DEC-205 (JCI 2013) but also investigated the differences between PD1 and CTLA4 (Paper in preparation) in various murine models. We found that only PD-1-based vaccine engaged antigen-cross presentation for inducing HIV Gag-specific CD8+ T cell responses in a CD4-independent way. This finding has important implication for AIDS immunotherapy considering the CD4 loss after HIV infection. We, therefore, achieved 100% of this project objective. Second, we constructed the DC-targeting vaccines that conjugated with a luciferase reporter gene to investigate the kinetics of antigen expression in vivo after DNA vaccination. We found no significant differences between PD1 and CTLA4 DC-targeting strategies in term of timing and duration of gene expression at the sites of vaccination. Therefore, these two DC-targeting proteins did not affect the level of protein expression in vivo. Moreover, these two DC-targeting proteins bind to bone marrow-derived dendritic cells effectively. We, however, were not able to isolate enough number of dendritic cells at the sites of vaccination probably due to their rapid homing to lymph node after antigen-uptake. We also attempted to conduct immunohistochemical staining of DC subsets with similar results. We, therefore, addressed 100% of this project objective. Third, in order to determine the protective role of CD8+ T-cell immunity elicited by PD1-based DC targeting vaccine, we developed a mouse malignant mesothelioma challenge model that consistently expressed the cognate HIV antigen Gag p24. The reason of developing this model is simply due to the lack of HIV infection in mice. We found that PD1-based vaccine-elicited CD8+ T cells not only prevent but also cure Gag-mesothelioma by overcoming tumor-induced immunosuppressive environment (Cancer Res. 2014). Furthermore, PD1-based vaccine led to antigen spreading that induced tumor-antigen reactive CD8+ T cells and conferred protection against the lethal challenge of wild-type malignant mesothelioma by eliminating myeloid-derived suppressor cells (Oncotarget 2015). We, therefore, achieved 100% of this project objective as well. In summary, we have worked very hard on the proposed study with three high impact SCI publications acknowledging this grant support, while another paper is in preparation. We revealed not only a promising vaccine strategy but also some mechanisms underlying the vaccine efficacy. This study also resulted in graduation of two excellent (top 10%) Ph.D. students at HKU.

762712.label: Major findings and research outcome
762712.value: In this study, we focus on the mechanism investigation of a PD-1-based vaccine in amplifying antiviral CD8+ T-cell immunity. Specifically, we discovered that PD1-based vaccination potentiated CD8+ T cell responses by enhancing antigen binding and uptake in DCs and activation in the draining lymph node. When compared with anti-DEC205 antibody-mediated DC targeting, PD-1-based vaccine increased IL-12-producing DCs and engaged antigen cross-presentation. The high frequency of durable and protective GAG-specific CD8+ T cell immunity induced by PD1-based vaccination suggested that this kind of vaccines could potentially be used against HIV-1 and other pathogens. The results of this study have been published in Journal of Clinical Investigation in 2013. Subsequently, we also investigated the differences between PD1 and CTLA4 in various murine models (Paper in preparation). We found that only PD-1-based vaccine engaged antigen-cross presentation for inducing HIV Gag-specific CD8+ T cell responses in a CD4-independent way. This finding further indicated that PD-1-based vaccine might have important implication for AIDS immunotherapy considering the CD4 loss after HIV infection. To determine the mechanism of CD8+ T-cell immunity elicited by PD1-based vaccine, we demonstrated that antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell correlates with the elimination of malignant mesothelioma that expresses HIV Gag P24 antigen in immunocompetent BALB/c mice. Furthermore, it remained highly immunogenic in tumor-bearing animals and led to therapeutic cure of preexisting mesothelioma. Also, these CD8+ T cells function by releasing inflammatory IFNγ and TNFα in the vicinity of target cells as well as by initiating TRAIL-directed tumor cell apoptosis. Importantly, repeated DNA vaccinations achieve an active functional state, not only preventing the rise of exhausted PD1+ and Tim-3+ CD8+ T cells but also suppressing tumor-induced myeloid-derived suppressive cells and Treg cells, with the frequency of antigen-specific CD8+ T cells inversely correlating with tumor mass. The results of this study have been published in Cancer Research in 2014. Subsequently, we further investigated the efficacy and correlation of protection on the PD1 vaccine-mediated antigen spreading against wild-type mesothelioma. We found that PD1 vaccine-mediated antigen spreading induced tumor-specific cytotoxic CD8+ T cells. Adoptive cell transfer experiments further demonstrated that antigen spreading-induced CD8+ T cells conferred efficacious therapeutic effects against established wild type mesothelioma and prevented the increase of exhausted PD1+ and Tim-3+ CD8+ T cells. We show that efficacious CD8+ T cells capable of eliminating both tumor cells and MDSCs are likely necessary for fighting wild-type malignant mesothelioma. The results of this study have been published in Oncotarget in 2015. Overall, our discoveries provide new insights into quantitative and qualitative characteristics of PD1-vaccine-elicited functional CD8+ T cells.

762712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762712.value: We are now seeking for research funding to study the promising PD1-vaccine in humans. The key discovery made by us is to enhance vaccine immunogenicity by delivering HIV antigen via PD1 to dendritic cells more effectively. After four years of study, we demonstrated that this PD1-based vaccine strategy has resulted in high levels of qualitatively enhanced HIV-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, which confer significant protection in mice after lethal Gag-mesothelioma challenges. The study also revealed underlying mechanisms of this new discovery, which have significant implication to AIDS vaccine and vaccines against other pathogens. With this critical discovery in the world, the ultimate goal of future proposal is to bring this promising PD1-based vaccine into human trials, phase I as the first step and phase II/III as the second step. Once the new vaccine works in human with reliable safety profiles during phase I, it will warrant for further phase II/III human studies. The new discovery will be useful not only for preventing HIV infection but also for immunotherapy of treating 36.9 millions of infected people because a high frequency of HIV-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T cells is important for both suppressing viral replication and clearing persistent infection (so-called HIV latency).

762712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762712.value: Since 1981, AIDS pandemic has led to 40 million deaths and another 36.9 million people currently living with HIV, the AIDS virus, worldwide. To date, this pandemic still grows in a speed of over 2 million new infections each year while there remains the lack of therapeutic cure and effective vaccine. Currently, most failed AIDS vaccines are weak and not protective in humans. In this study, the discovery made by us is to enhance vaccine potency by a promising PD1-based vaccine. After four years of study, we demonstrated that this vaccine resulted in high levels of qualitatively enhanced viral specific T cell responses, which may confer significant protection in mice after lethal challenges. The study also revealed some correlates of protection on our new discovery, which may have significant implication to AIDS vaccine and vaccines against other pathogens.

762912.label: Project Title(Chinese)
762912.value: BLU基因對抑制鼻咽癌腫瘤的發生及其訊號傳遞機制的研究

762912.label: Project Objectives
762912.value: Our central hypothesis for this application is that BLU plays critical roles in the control of cellular invasion, angiogenesis, and metastasis in NPC development. Aim #1: Determine whether the BLU gene inhibits tumor growth through anti-invasion and anti-angiogenesis activities Aim #2: Investigate how BLU suppresses tumor growth through TSP1- and VEGF-mediated signaling pathways We aim to decipher a novel tumor suppressive pathway mediated by BLU gene in NPC and to understand molecular mechanisms in the network regulation of tumor angiogenesis and metastasis. Using well-established methods and other new approaches, we will determine whether BLU controls tumor growth activities by interfering with cellular migration, invasion, metastasis, and angiogenesis. We will investigate whether and how these activities are regulated depending on expression of BLU in NPC. Using both in vitro and in vivo approaches, we will investigate whether BLU acts alone or collaborates with other genes, such as TSP1 and VEGF, to inhibit cell growth through inactivation of the angiogenesis and metastasis pathways in tumorigenic cells. We will investigate if novel tumor suppressive pathways are present in established NPC cell lines and primary tumor samples. We will determine whether genes TSP1 and VEGF may directly control the growth of NPC cells. Since TSP1 is a well-studied negative regulator of tumor progression and metastasis in other tumors and it has not yet been reported to be related to the BLU alterations, we will explore the role of TSP1 in NPC development and examine how BLU regulates the expression of TSP1, and whether one or more other genes, are needed to collaborate with BLU and TSP1 during the regulation of tumor invasion and metastasis. We will compare and analyze expression profiles of BLU transfectants and other BLU-associated gene transfectants (TSP1), with negative control clones and parental HONE1-2 cells, to identify novel genes or signaling pathways associated with the control of NPC progression. We will determine if alterations of the BLU gene on chromosome 3p21.3 are critical events in the regulation of NPC invasion and metastasis, and reveal new directions for the further exploration of mechanisms of tumor growth control.

762912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
762912.value: 早前透過細胞融合和染色體轉移技術，我們發現染色體3p21.3區段可抑制鼻咽癌腫瘤的生長。后來證實該區段為人類染色體上一個最重要的腫瘤抑制區域，其與包括鼻咽癌在內的許多人類散發性腫瘤的發生發展有關。眾多的研究人員隨后發現3p21.3區段有超過十個以上的抑瘤基因。現已知道，至少其中的RASSF1A和BLU基因與鼻咽癌腫瘤的生成有密切關聯。基因啟動序列高度甲基化常導致鼻咽癌及其他腫瘤中的BLU基因表達缺失。本研究團隊早前曾發表報告，證明鼻咽癌細胞中BLU的表達能於動物實驗中抑制腫瘤的生長，然而BLU基因詳細的分子抑瘤機制仍未清楚。 我們曾發表其它兩個抑瘤基因通過抑制血管新生，從而抑制鼻咽癌細胞生長的研究報告。其中MMP19基因，於鼻咽癌腫瘤組織中有規律地與BLU基因一同表達。本研究團隊還發現ADAMTS9基因能透過抑制血管新生而阻礙癌細胞生長，此基因已被發現與TSP1基因（Thrombospondin-1）有關連，通過控制血管內皮生長因子路徑而控制腫瘤的生長和血管新生。另一方面，E2F是能直接控制TSP1表達的基因，目前有研究顯示BLU基因亦受E2F控制。總括而言，不同研究團隊的結果均顯示BLU有與血管新生訊號路徑連結, 而抑制腫瘤生長的可能性。但在癌症發生發展過程中，這個由BLU或其他基因（如TSP1）所控制的訊號傳遞網絡仍未被充分了解。 為了核實BLU在癌症發展和抗血管新生訊號傳遞路徑上的角色，我們研究了一些已知與癌症擴散和血管新生有關, 卻從未在鼻咽癌中被探索的基因。與僅有載體而無BLU基因的對照細胞比較，鼻咽癌細胞中過度表達的BLU，可產生對血管新生基因VEGF189和 TSP1表達的抑制。分析所有BLU轉染的鼻咽癌HONE1細胞，發現TSP1的表達均被抑制85%至99%。 由於TSP1和VEGF在細胞內的訊號傳遞網絡中互相連結，因此BLU轉染細胞中的VEGF蛋白濃度亦大幅下降三至四倍。為了確定這些從轉錄和轉譯層面所得到的初步研究結果，我們進行了基因的功能測定，以便確定VEGF 和TSP1在BLU介導的控制腫瘤生長和血管新生抑制中的角色。我們測試了BLU轉染細胞的遷移能力，並發現BLU過度表達的細胞的入侵能力較對照細胞為低。以上結果進一步為體內血管新生分析所確認，即BLU轉染的細胞表現出對人類臍靜脈內皮細胞（HUVEC）細管形成的抑制。 以上的初步結果充分顯示出BLU基因在控制腫瘤入侵和擴散能力方面的重要作用，揭示了細胞中由BLU和TSP1控制的新的腫瘤抑制訊號傳遞路徑。此研究計劃提出，分別以體內和體外試驗測試BLU的抗血管新生和抑制細胞入侵的能力、BLU單獨或與其它基因（如TSP1）合作下通過抑制血管新生路徑對癌細胞生長的影響。3號染色體短臂上抑瘤基因的缺失和失活是鼻咽癌發生發展中已知的重要致癌因素，故預計此研究將提供有關癌症惡化和擴散的重要資訊，並有助於發現與診斷和治療有關的分子靶向。

762912.label: Major findings and research outcome
762912.value: BLU expression is frequently down-regulated in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and many other tumors due to promoter hypermethylation. Functional evidence shows that the BLU gene inhibits tumor growth in animal assays, but the detailed molecular mechanism responsible for this is still not well understood. Our current findings resolve a long-term unanswered question, namely how BLU induced tumor suppressive function in NPC cells. In current studies, we find that 93.5% of early stage primary NPC tumors show down-regulated BLU expression. Using a PCR array, overexpression of the BLU gene was correlated to the angiogenesis network in NPC cells. Moreover, expression changes of the MMP family, VEGF and TSP1 were often detected in different stages of NPC, suggesting the possibility that BLU may be directly involved in the microenvironment and anti-angiogenic activity in NPC development. Compared to vector-alone control cells, BLU stable transfectants, derived from poorly-differentiated NPC HONE1 cells, suppress VEGF165, VEGF189, and TSP1 expression at both the RNA and protein levels, and significantly reduce the secreted VEGF protein in these cells, reflecting an unknown regulatory mechanism mediated by the BLU gene in NPC. Cells expressing BLU inhibited cellular invasion, migration, and tube formation. These in vitro results were further confirmed by in vivo tumor suppression and a matrigel plug angiogenesis assay in nude mice. Tube-forming ability was clearly inhibited, when the BLU gene is expressed in these cells. Up to 70 to 90% of injected tumor cells expressing increased exogenous BLU underwent cell death in animal assays. Overexpressed BLU only inhibited VEGF165 expression in differentiated squamous NPC HK1 cells, but also showed an anti-angiogenic effect in the animal assay, revealing a complicated mechanism regulating the angiogenesis and microenvironment in different NPC cell lines. The relationship of BLU controlling tumor growth with other angiogenesis genes was confirmed; this has not yet been reported thus far in NPC. In summary, these studies indicate that alteration of BLU gene expression influences anti-angiogenesis pathways and is important for the development of NPC.

762912.value: 6. In the current study, we found that many genes associated with angiogenic factors, cytokines, growth factors and receptors, adhesion molecules, and other matrix proteins were identified. Because of consisteny of these findings, we analyzed expression profiles of BLU transfectants, and discovered many novel genes or signaling pathways associated with the control of NPC progression. Therefore, we obtained important results for elucidating the molecular mechanism of tumor suppression played by the BLU gene in NPC. These known genes may play important roles associated with alteration of BLU gene in NPC development. Therefore, current results provide future directions for the exploration of BLU-mediated therapeutic targets in NPC and signaling regulatory mechanisms involved in the chromosome 3p21.3 region and angiogenesis networks in human tumors. These findings strongly suggest that BLU is an important TSG in the regulation of NPC development.

762912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762912.value: Many studies found that BLU gene was inactivated, or loss of function, in tumor samples. About 10 years ago, we already knew that BLU gene can suppress tumor growth in mice, but detailed molecular mechanism responsible for tumor suppression is still not understood. In current studies, we find that 93.5% of early stage of nasopharyngeal carcinoma show decreased expression of BLU gene, suggesting that inactivation of this gene may play an important role in the tumor. Using a PCR array technique, expression of the BLU gene by artificial gene transfection was correlated to the blood formation in cancer cells. Moreover, expression changes of the MMP family, VEGF and TSP1 genes were often detected in different stages of tumor, suggesting the possibility that BLU may be directly involved in the anti- blood formation activity in tumor, because we already know that these genes have these functions. Cells expressing BLU inhibited invasion, migration, and blood tube formation of cells, indicating that that this gene has a potential to suppress tumor growth. These results were further confirmed by the tumor suppression assay performed in mice. In summary, current studies indicate that alteration of BLU gene expression is important for the development of nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

763012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
763012.value: 背景: 全球多達七千萬人患有癲癇，為公共醫療系統帶來沉重負擔。癲癇是其中 一種最常見的嚴重神經系統疾病，每10個成年人中便有一個曾經癲癇發作。在 長期服藥治療的情況下，仍有三分一的患者持續病發。在癲癇的多個病變中， 海馬硬化性顳葉癲癇（MTLE-HS）是被公認為最抗藥的類型。MTLE-HS的病 情能夠以臨床特徵、腦電圖、放射學和病理變化的方法明確地分析。患者通常 在青春期前發病，癲癇發作時意識模糊，有機會導致身體傷害，甚至死亡。因 此，癲癇可以對患者的身心發展構成嚴重障礙，影響學業和就業。雖然部分患 者幼年時曾發生長時間的熱性驚厥，MTLE-HS的病理變化仍然未明，亦無有效 的預防措施。 遺傳變異對產生癲癇的影響逐漸受到醫學研究界關注。一個在歐洲人種進行的 全基因組關聯研究未能發現引致局灶性癲癇的常見基因變異。我們在香港華人 進行了類似研究，只發現了一個達到顯著性要求的常見基因變異，結果令我們 開始認為癲癇是由多個罕見基因變異的加成效果所引致。鑑定這些罕見基因變 異需要對疾病組和控制組的編碼區進行基因測序。此方法對MTLE-HS這種特徵 明顯的疾病尤為適合，因為當特徵相似的病人得到有效分類，預計潛在的遺傳 結構會更一致。該方法已在其他腦部疾病的研究中被證實能有效找出罕見基因 變異，包括精神分裂症和自閉症。 計劃：我們將對基因組中所有基因編碼區進行測序，從而發掘直接導致癲癇或 頻繁出現在患者的基因突變。我們計劃利用新一代測序技術，對50 個MTLE- HS患者及其父母進行測序。這個方法容許我們找出家庭獨有的變種基因，甚至 能找出引致疾病的新基因突變。結果將會利用傳統的Sanger測序去驗證，並進 一步於額外500個癲癇病例中進行相同驗證。當中包括100名MTLE-HS病例和 正常人，以確認基因突變在MTLE-HS和其他癲癇症的影響。 意義：本計劃的基礎是建立於我們過往在癲癇遺傳學的研究成果上。研究結果 將令我們發現新的MTLE-HS遺傳標記，對癲癇的神經生物學有引導性作用。有 證據指出MTLE-HS在部份病人中隨時間惡化。雖然MTLE患者初步會對抗癲癇 藥物治療反應良好，但往往在成年早期時對藥物開始產生抗藥性。在這種情況 下，醫生會建議部份人用手術把前顳葉切除。若果能夠利用遺傳標記及早識別 有患病潛伏危險的人仕，便可對他們進行及早治療，避免手術的必要。我們亦 可以根據結果所揭示的基因突變的影響模式，去發展基因療法。

763012.label: Realisation of objectives
763012.value: Objective 1: DNA on parents was only available for 23 MTLE-HS patients, so we sequenced 23 complete trios, along with 4 patients who had only a single parent available, and 27 additional probands with no parental DNA available, for a total of 48 affected MTLE-HS cases. Objective 2: De novo mutations: KGGSeq was employed for the discovery and annotation of de novo variants in the 23 trios. The predicted damaging effects and gene intolerance scores were annotated per-gene and per-variant. In addition to QC described above, each de novo variant requires a read depth >=8X for a callout. Mutations found in any of the 3 population databases (dbSNP141, ExAC, 1000 Genome phase III) were excluded. The non-synonymous to synonymous ratio was calculated and compared with different exome sequencing studies. In total, 27 de novo variants were identified, with 23 validated by Sanger sequencing, and no recurrently de novo mutated genes over 23 trios. Of these, 19 were non-synonymous mutations and 3 were synonymous mutations. The non-synonymous to synonymous variant ratio of the de novo variants was 6.3:1, which is higher than the neutral rate of 2.8:1 20, and is higher than that reported in patients with intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, and schizophrenia. When we look at the ratio between studies, our ratio (6.3:1) is higher than intellectual disability studies, ASD studies, and schizophrenia studies. This ratio suggests that de novo mutations might be an important contributing factor for the pathogenesis of MTLE-HS. Objective 3: De novo mutations identified were validated using Sanger sequencing. 23/27 were validated, with insufficient DNA or inability to design working primers the causes of lack of validation.

763012.label: Major findings and research outcome
763012.value: 23 de novo variants (DNVs) were identified and validated with many known to cause neuro-psychiatric disorders. By comparing population controls, enrichment of rare variants was observed in the gene SEC24B. Integration of gene-set data describing neuronal functions and psychiatric disorders suggests additional enrichment signal on FMRP targets. Analysis of differentially expressed genes of MTLE-HS surgical specimens also supports the role of FMRP targets. Studying clinically well-defined MTLE-HS patients revealed the complex genetic architecture behind MTHE-HS. Multiple genes carry DNVs and rare variants among FMRP targets could contribute to MTLE-HS pathogenesis.

763012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
763012.value: Given the limited sample size, unfortunately this study can only be considered a pilot. Additional samples should be analyzed for more definitive conclusions regarding the role of de novo mutations in MTLE-HS. Our finding of rare variants in SEC24B needs to be supported by sequencing a much larger sample of MTLE-HS patients, which we can do through collaboration in the ILAE network. Functional analysis of this gene is also needed to understand its role in epilepsy. We are presently collaborating with a group in the US who have also conducted a sequencing study of MTLE-HS patients, to see which of the genes we have found are also implicated in their sample. Once they have provided the information to us, we will be ready to publish our findings, as presently they do not make a very strong paper. We hope to submit a paper in the next month or two.

763012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
763012.value: The project was an attempt to find mutations which are not inherited from the papers and which may predispose to a rare form of epilepsy, mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis. We sequenced the coding regions of the DNA for 23 MTLE-HS patients and their parents and looked for variants that the patients had which they did not inherit from their parents. 23 variants were found and several of the genes they were in have been previously known to be implicated in neuro-psychiatric disorders. Without replication in a larger sample, however, it is difficult to say with certainty whether these variants are causing disease, however.
