763312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
763312.value: Hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus are strongly related to obesity in Hong Kong Chinese. Obesity elevates blood pressure through multiple mechanisms. Lipocalin-2 (also known as neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin) is secreted by fat cells. It is known to be associated with obesity and insulin resistance, but our recent findings in mouse and man suggest that it may also play an important role in hypertension. Mice deficient in it does not develop endothelial dysfunction and hypertension when fed on a high fat diet. When these mice receive lipocalin-2 replacement, they develop endothelial dysfunction. In man, plasma lipocalin-2 level increases with obesity and hypertension. Variants in the gene encoding lipocalin-2 are associated with raised plasma level of lipocalin-2 and hypertension. We postulate that lipocalin-2 adversely affects the relaxation of blood vessels and causes hypertension. We propose to give lipocalin-2 to lipocalin-2 knockout mice for 8 weeks and observe the changes in blood pressure and endothelial function. We shall use two models of obesity (diet-induced and genetic); lipocalin-2 knockout mouse fed with a high fat diet, and a double knockout mouse deficient in both leptin receptor and lipocalin-2 on normal diet. In 800 people who have had measurements of flow-mediated dilatation of the brachial artery to assess endothelial function, we shall measure their plasma lipocalin-2 level. We anticipate that the plasma level of lipocalin-2 will be significantly related to endothelial function in man, and in mice, 8-week administration of lipocalin-2 will lead to endothelial dysfunction and elevation in blood pressure. In over 1900 participants of the Hong Kong Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence cohort, we will also investigate whether or not serum lipocalin-2 level can predict the long-term development of hypertension. This project will provide important insights into one of the mechanisms by which obesity can lead to hypertension, and may lead to the development of new classes of therapeutic agents. 在香港的華人，肥胖與高血壓和2型糖尿病是有密切關係的。肥胖通過多種機制提升血壓。載脂蛋白-2（也被稱為中性粒細胞明膠酶相關脂質運載蛋白） 是由脂肪細胞分泌的。我們知道它與肥胖和胰島素抵抗有相關性，但最近我們在小鼠和人的研究結果發現，它可能在高血壓也發揮了重要的角色。缺乏它的小鼠當餵以高脂肪的飲食時不會發展血管內皮功能障礙和高血壓。當這些小鼠接受載脂蛋白-2補充時，它們便開始患上內皮功能障礙。人類的血漿載脂蛋白-2水平會跟隨肥胖和高血壓而提高。載脂蛋白-2基因編碼的變異與血漿載脂蛋白-2水平以及高血壓相關。我們假設，載脂蛋白-2對血管的鬆弛產生不利的影響和導致高血壓。我們計劃給予載脂蛋白-2基因敲除小鼠8週的載脂蛋白-2，觀察血壓和血管內皮功能的變化。我們將使用兩種肥胖的模型（飲食引起的和遺傳性）: 餵以高脂肪飲食的載脂蛋白-2基因敲除小鼠，以及正常飲食的缺乏瘦素受體和載脂蛋白-2雙基因敲除小鼠。在800名曾經以肱動脈血流介導的擴張來評估血管內皮功能的人，我們將測量他們的血漿載脂蛋白-2的水平。我們預期血管內皮功能和血漿載脂蛋白-2水平將顯著相關，也預期載脂蛋白-2輸入小鼠體內8週會導致血管內皮功能障礙和血壓升高。在超過1900名香港心血管疾病風險因素調查的參與者中，我們也將探討血漿載脂蛋白-2水平是否可以預測長期高血壓的發展。此項目將提供關於肥胖導致高血壓機制其中之一的重要見解，並可能導致新類型治療藥物的發展。

763312.label: Realisation of objectives
763312.value: Animal studies Amelioration of vascular inflammation, endothelial dysfunction and hypertension in lipocalin-2 knockout mice During the first year of the project, we made the unexpected and important discovery that instead of the native form, it is the deamidated form of lipocalin-2 that causes vascular inflammation, endothelial dysfunction and hypertension in mice fed on a high fat diet. We found that administration of lipocalin-2 in combination with non-esterified free fatty acids, especially linoleic acid (18:2n-6), caused endothelial dysfunction and vascular inflammation in lipocalin-2 knockout mice. Linoleic acid treatment facilitated the deamidation of lipocalin-2, reduced its interactions with matrix metalloproteinase 9 (MMP9), and increased the circulating level as well as the accumulation of this adipokine in the arterial wall. A human lipocalin-2 mutant with the cysteine 87 residue replaced by alanine (C87A) evoked endothelial dysfunction in the absence of combined treatment with linoleic acid. C87A contains a reduced amount of polyamines and exhibits reduced capacity to form heterodimeric complexes with MMP9. Blockage of the latter formation with a MMP9 inhibitor promoted the stabilization and deamidation of lipocalin-2. These results demonstrated that activation of lipocalin-2 by deamidation plays a causal role in causing endothelial dysfunction under conditions of high non-esterified fatty acids intake or dietary obesity. We monitored the blood pressure of lipocalin-2 knockout mice and wild type mice throughout 24 hours using implanted sensors and radiotelemetry. Firstly, we found that lipocalin-2 knockout mice had significantly lower 24-hour average blood pressure compared to wild-type controls (122.4±15.6/108.7±16.2 mmHg vs. 142±16.3/123.4±15.6 mmHg, p<0.01). Moreover, the diurnal variation in blood pressure was blunted in wild type mice on high fat diet but maintained in lipocalin-2 knockout mice despite the same high fat diet. Thus, we have fulfilled the first objective of the grant proposal, namely, to demonstrate that lipocalin-2, in particular, its deamidated from, acts together with a high fat diet to cause accumulation of lipocalin-2 in the arterial wall, provoking inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Mice deficient in lipocalin-2 are resistant to these harmful effects and the elevation of blood pressure caused by high fat diet. Beyond the objectives of the RGC proposal, we are delighted to report that we have carried out further experiments to understand the mechanism whereby lipocalin-2 causes atherosclerosis and to demonstrate the therapeutic potential of suppressing lipocalin-2. We discovered that lipocalin-2 caused vascular inflammation through neutrophil activation. Neutrophils derived from lipocalin-2 deficient mice could not form neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) upon stimulation by linoleic acid. Replacing with lipocalin-2 and adding linoleic acid restored NET formation. Our results suggested that lipocalin-2 plays an indispensable role in the development of atherosclerosis by promoting neutrophil activation and chronic vascular inflammation. In double knockout mice deficient in apolipoprotein E as well as lipocalin-2, atherosclerosis did not develop even when the mice were fed a high fat diet. In another model of hypertension, in which hypertension in mice was induced by the infusion of angiotensin II or the combination of aldosterone, uninephrectomy and 1% saline in drinking water (ANS), knocking out lipocalin-2 reduced mineralocorticoid receptor expression and prevented the development of hypertension and fibrotic changes in the heart and kidneys. Human studies Lipocalin-2 and hypertension The plasma concentration of lipocalin-2 had been measured by immunoassay in 1925 subjects of the Hong Kong Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence Study (CRISPS) using previous grants, including RGC grant HKU780210M. The results showed that plasma lipocalin-2 level was higher in men than in women (median [IQR] 37.7 [30.5-47.9] vs.31.6 [25.4-40.4], p<0.001). It was significantly related to age (r=0.15, p<0.001) and systolic blood pressure (r=0.15, p<0.001). In women, it was also significantly related to waist circumference (r=0.16, p<0.001), BMI (r=0.09, p=0.004), diastolic blood pressure (r=0.14, p<0.001) and fasting plasma glucose (r=0.089, p=0.004). The funding from the current proposal allowed us to study the relationship between plasma lipocalin-2 at baseline and the development of hypertension. Over a median follow-up of 5.4 years, 239 subjects developed hypertension among 1116 subjects that were normotensive at baseline. In multiple logistic regression analysis, the baseline level of lipocalin-2 in plasma was a significant independent predictor of new-onset hypertension (p=0.017). We concluded that plasma lipocalin-2 concentration is related to systolic blood pressure, and is higher in men and in people with hypertension or predisposed to developing hypertension. Lipocalin-2 and endothelial function Endothelial function was not assessed in CRISPS. Therefore, to study the relationship between lipocalin-2 and endothelial function, we measured plasma lipocalin-2 concentration in the stored blood samples of subjects who had measurements of brachial artery flow-mediated dilatation (FMD) in studies of endothelial function led by Prof HF Tse. The brachial artery was imaged using high-resolution ultrasound (7.5MHz linear array, Agilent Sonos 5500; Philips, Andover, MA). Arterial diameter and flow velocity were measured. Scans were taken at baseline, after tourniquet inflation for 5 minutes, and after sublingual glyceryl trinitrate spray. The percentage change in brachial artery diameter following reactive hyperaemia compared with the baseline was calculated. The coefficient of variation of FMD determination was 5%. Complete data were available for 245 subjects. Among these subjects, 151 had hypertension, 80 had diabetes mellitus and 240 were on lipid lowering therapy. Our results showed that plasma lipocalin-2 correlated with serum creatinine (ρ=0.23, p<0.001) but not FMD (ρ=0.005, p=0.94). Lipocalin-2 levels were lower in subjects on lipid lowering therapy (p=0.023). FMD correlated inversely with age (ρ=-0.14, p=0.03). Diabetes was associated with a lower FMD (p=0.044). Thus, surprisingly, the plasma level of lipocalin-2 was unrelated to FMD, an index of endothelial function. Endothelial function varies even within an individual, and is influenced by factors such as ageing and diabetes as found in our study, and also by diet and drugs. Most of the study subjects were on lipid lowering therapy, and those who had hypertension and diabetes were treated. Control of risk factors could have a favourable effect on endothelial function. The correlation of lipocalin-2 with creatinine is consistent with it being a marker of renal injury. This study was planned before the deamidation of lipocalin-2 was elucidated; it is possible that it correlates better with endothelial function. Deamidated lipocalin-2 and cardiovascular risk factors Accordingly, we went beyond the original objectives of the proposal to conduct a further study on deamidated lipocalin-2 in man. We previously demonstrated in man and mouse that lipocalin-2 is unstable in plasma and is modified by polyamination. Polyaminated lipocalin-2 is rapidly cleared whereas deamidated lipocalin-2 is not, so the latter may accumulate in arteries and induce endothelial dysfunction. We think that activation of lipocalin-2 by deamidation is a key mechanism mediating obesity-induced inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. Therefore we measured polyaminated and deamidated lipocalin-2 in normal healthy people in the community and determined their relationships with cardiovascular risk factors. One hundred normal healthy adults, comprising 59 men (mean age 47.7±7.5 years) and 41 women (mean age 48.2±7.2 years), were studied with informed consent. Blood pressure was measured three times using an automated sphygmomanometer, and a questionnaire was used to record the subjects’ medical history and lifestyle. The serum level of non-polyaminated lipocalin-2 was measured and was found to correlate positively with body mass index, waist circumference, heart rate, diastolic blood pressure and triglyceride levels in the blood, but negatively with circulating adiponectin. This provides the first human evidence that non-polyaminated lipocalin-2 may be involved in cardiovascular disease development.

763312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
763312.value: Lipocalin-2 is a blood protein the function of which is to mop up excess iron and also to deprive bacteria of iron. Our studies in mice deficient in lipocalin-2 showed that there is less inflammation and dysfunction in arteries, and lower blood pressure. In man, we found that the blood level of lipocalin-2 correlated with obesity and blood pressure. In a cohort of normal people without hypertension to start with, a high baseline blood level of lipocalin-2 was a predictor of the development of hypertension 5 years later. To our surprise, we did not find a significant relationship between the blood level of lipocalin-2 and artery dysfunction in our cardiac patients, but that could have been due to the fact that they were taking medications to control their blood pressure and lipids. We discovered that the deamidated form of lipocalin-2 stays in the circulation longer than the native form and may be the culprit causing cardiovascular disease. Further studies will be conducted to understand the implications of this novel finding.

763712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
763712.value: 椎間盤是脊柱的運動關節,並同時提供震動緩沖功能。椎間盤退變可引發背痛和坐骨神經痛，是導致勞動能力喪失甚至殘疾的重要原因。退變過程中，椎間盤的核心部分髓核逐漸由凝膠樣轉化為纖維軟骨樣，椎間盤的正常結構與功能因此受到嚴重損害。究其原因，髓核中的細胞構成變化-即年輕髓核中的脊索細胞逐步為軟骨細胞樣細胞所替代，與椎間盤的成熟及退變密切相關。脊索細胞特異性表達一種粘附分子-鈣粘蛋白2，該蛋白在胚胎形態發生和組織完整性維持中具有重要作用。鈣粘蛋白2 也可調控軟骨內骨化過程中間質細胞向軟骨細胞的分化。本課題組前期研究首次揭示了椎間盤發育及退變中鈣粘蛋白2 的表達變化及潛在意義，因此本研究擬通過基於人、鼠椎間盤的體內體外試驗，進一步了解鈣粘蛋白2 及β-鏈蛋白在椎間盤發育及退變中的特殊作用。預期本研究的完成，將有助於深入了解椎間盤發育及退變中鈣粘蛋白2 的基礎功能，為椎間盤退變的再生修復提供新的依據。

763712.label: Realisation of objectives
763712.value: Intervertebral discs (IVD) are the major motional units in the spinal column and its degeneration is associated with low back pain. IVD requires an integration of various compartments to confer its mechanical function. The core of IVD, the nucleus pulposus (NP) is believed to play a central role in the integration and therefore the integrity of IVD. An understanding in the maintenance and regulation of NP cells is important to their engineering and to facilitate future development of therapeutics for treating IVD degeneration. Previous mouse model studies have implied that early events of IVD degeneration may be associated with a deregulation of cell adhesion activities. Cadherins are transmembrane glycoproteins that mediate calcium dependent cell adhesion, and may interact with β-catenin to regulate intracellular signaling. Our pilot microarray data have revealed expression of Cdh2 gene, encoding cadherin 2/N-cadherin in rodent NP. To date, the function of cadherin 2 in IVD and its relationship to IVD degeneration is not clear. In this study, we hypothesize that (1) cadherin 2 is required for normal IVD development and homeostasis, and (2) cadherin 2 regulates NP cell fate and phenotype via β-catenin activity. We aimed to study the expression pattern of cadherin 2 in rodent and human discs during development, aging, and degeneration, and to investigate its function in the NP via a gene and protein ablation strategies. Objective 1: To fully characterize changes in cadherin 2 expression during IVD degeneration in humans and rodents. We postulate that disc ageing and degeneration may be related to a change of NP phenotypic state and hence NP dysfunction due to a loss of cadherin 2 function. We performed immunostaining to examine the expression pattern in the mouse IVD at fetal stages to 2 years of age. We also examined the expression in degenerative rat tail IVD induced by puncture injury by immunostaining and Western blots. Furthermore, we also collected degenerative and non-degenerative human IVD samples and quantitatively measured the cadherin 2 expressing cells. Study in human fetal IVD samples was achieved by a collaboration with Prof. Judith Hoyland team in University of Manchester, UK. Moreover, we examined the cadherin 2 expression in NP progenitors based on the recent discovery. Altogether, we gathered evidence for the expression status of cadherin 2 in rodent and human in relation to growth, ageing, and degeneration of the IVD. This objective was completely achieved. Objective 2: To examine the effect of loss of function of cadherin 2 on IVD homeostasis by gene knockout and protein ablation studies. We postulate that cadherin 2 has an important role in maintaining NP integrity and cell phenotype. As stated in the proposal, we tested the loss cadherin 2 protein function in IVD by injecting cadherin 2 specific antibody into the rat adult NP and examined the disc phenotype over time. On the other hand, we generated conditional knockout (CKO) mice by ablating the Cdh2 gene (encoding cadherin 2) in the notochord, and hence the NP, via Foxa2 enhancer driven Cre mediated recombination. We examined the disc structure and the expression of various NP cell markers and disc related matrix proteins at various age of the mutant to characterize the phenotype. The homozygous was unexpectedly inviable by 1 month old. We could therefore only follow and analyze the phenotype of adult mice in the heterozygous mutants. These include studying the expression of NP markers, matrix proteins, and apoptotic markers. Because of the significant change in NP cell morphology, we conduct further experiments such as transmission electron microscopy and immunostaining for vacuole-related markers in an attempt to delineate the cell phenotype. Altogether, we successfully established the in vivo models and characterized the effects of loss of cadherin 2 on the NP cells in various aspects. This objective was completely achieved. Objective 3: To compare β-catenin activity in cadherin 2 expressing and non-expressing NP cells. β-catenin can interact with and hence its activity can be sequestered by cadherins. We therefore tested if loss of cadherin 2 in the mutant NP cells could result in a change in β-catenin activity. We originally proposed to generate cadherin 2 knockout mutants in the background of TOPGAL to help analyzing β -catenin activity in the NP during IVD development and growth. However due to the viability issue in the mutant, we decided to reserve the resources to generate more knockout mice for phenotype characterization. Instead, we examined the β-catenin activity in the mutant by studying its nuclear localization. In addition, we examined the expression of β-catenin in induced rat disc degeneration where cadherin 2 expression in the NP was found to be reduced. On the other hand, we also found that sorting of the CDH2 negative bovine NP cells for transduction experiments was not efficient enough to conduct a reliable study. After due consideration, we decided to knockout CDH2 gene in a chordoma cell line (JHC7), which we confirmed to express cadherin 2, by using CRISPR-Cas editing so as to study its function on β-catenin activity. While we have modified the plan due to these obstacles, we believe this new initiative may as well provide a useful model for future follow-up investigations.

763712.label: Major findings and research outcome
763712.value: Cadherin 2 expression was weakly detected in mouse notochord and upregulated in the mouse NP at birth, with strong expression in the large vacuolated NP cells in young adults. In ageing IVD (1 year to 2 years of age), the NP cells were replaced by small chondrocyte-like cells with reduced expression of cadherin 2. In a puncture-induced rat disc degeneration model, the notochordal NP cells were also replaced by rounded chondrocyte-like cells with reduced level of cadherin 2 expression. Human NP cells at fetal stage exhibited homogeneous expression of cadherin 2. However, in adolescent non-degenerated NP and adult degenerated NP, cadherin 2 expression became heterogeneous (12.1% and 13.5% positivity respectively). Fragmentation of NP cell mass and a mild reduction of disc height was found after 8 weeks of cadherin 2 neutralizing antibody injection into the rat tail discs, compared with the IgG injection control. Cdh2 conditional knockout (CKO) mouse mutants, driven by Foxa2 enhancer-Cre mediated recombination, displayed significantly smaller body size by 1-month old, and showed a remarkable loss of the vacuolation in the NP cells. Moreover, the mutant exhibited hypomorphic NP and AF structures with irregular annulus organization and reduced disc height. At molecular level, CKO mutants at E15.5 showed normal expression of the notochordal NP marker keratin 19, but decreased collagen II and aggrecan deposition as well as reduced vacuolation as suggested by Rab32 staining. At P0, the NP showed complete loss of keratin 19 expression. Conditional Cdh2+/- mutants displayed interrupted vacuolar space in NP under transmission electron microscopy (TEM) at 1-month old, indicating 50% loss of cadherin 2 could lead to a disruption of the vacuolar structures. The heterozygous mutants were viable, but developed a fibrocartilaginous NP containing cell clusters in the lumbar discs by 3-month old with upregulation of collagen I and II, a phenotype resembling mature human discs. Such change was not found in the coccygeal discs, suggesting that cadherin 2 may possibly interplay with mechanical factors or disc geometry/size in regulating NP cell activity and ultimately disc homeostasis. By western blot analysis, we demonstrated that the expression of β-catenin was decreased along with cadherin 2 in the rat disc degeneration model. In the E15.5 CKO mutant, nuclear expression of β-catenin was also found upregulated. At P0, the NP showed further increase in nuclear β -catenin expression. This suggests that the regulation of NP cell phenotype by cadherin 2 might in part involve β-catenin signaling.

763712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
763712.value: An interesting finding of the heterozygous Cdh2 mutant is the degenerative changes in the lumbar but not tail discs. This implicates a potential cross-talk of cadherin 2 with mechanotransduction. We are utilizing the tail looping model (established by Dr. D Sakai in Tokai University) to test if the Cdh2+/- mutant will develop accelerated disc degeneration in response to mechanical loading. We also attempted to generate a Cdh2 deficient chordoma line by CRISPR technology. This mutant cell line may provide a unique tool to understand cadherin 2 function in NP cell phenotype regulation and its relationship to β-catenin signaling. By introducing exogenous recombinant Cdh2 gene constructs we may also define the critical domains for its activity. To understand if the change of NP cell phenotype in the CKO mutant is related to altered β-catenin signaling, we are also generating a mouse model which has Foxa2 enhancer-Cre driven activation of β-catenin. We will examine if constitutive β-catenin activation in NP cells may reproduce the phenotype in particular the loss of vacuolation and hence provide important mechanistic insights. Moreover, we are preparing a manuscript (attached in the report) aiming to publish, along with the additional data, in PNAS or similar major scientific journals.

763712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
763712.value: Intervertebral discs (IVD) are joints of the spinal column that provides motion and absorbs shocks. IVDs can undergo degeneration which may result in low back pain and nerve compression (sciatica), causing disability and significant loss of work hours. Understanding the regulation of IVD cells at molecular levels is important to the management of its degeneration in future. We found that cadherin 2 is required to upkeep the native properties of the nucleus pulposus cells, and a loss of its function can lead to degenerative changes in the lumbar discs in animal models. Together with the finding of reduced cadherin 2 expressing cells during IVD maturation and degeneration process in humans, our study implies that a decrease of cadherin 2 function is linked to the initiation of degenerative changes in the IVD. Our study has therefore indicated an important role of cadherin 2 in the homeostasis and structural integrity of the IVD, providing new insights into the etiology of its degeneration and potential means to rejuvenate the disc cells for a regain of function.

764112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
764112.value: 原發性肝癌，是全球第三大的癌症死亡主因。大多數肝癌發生在亞太和非洲地區，但發病率在西方國家正穩步增加。對於早期肝癌患者，手術有最好的治療結果，雖然手術後癌症復發仍是普遍現象。值得注意的是，大多數已確診的患者都屬於晚期肝癌。雖然化療僅有輕微的療效，但化療仍然是晚期肝癌的主要治療方法。最近的證據顯示癌幹細胞對癌症的復發和耐藥性有重要的作用。應繼續這方面的研究，以提高肝癌的治療效果。 不久之前，我們的研究顯示生長因子「上皮素顆粒素前體」 （granulin-epithelin precursor, GEP) 具備潛力用作標靶療法。GEP 通過 P44/42 MAPK 和 AKT 調控癌細胞生長, 並通過 VEGF 調控癌血管生成。 此外， GEP 抗體治療亦令肝癌細胞的生長受到抑制。最近，我們發現 GEP 透過調節藥物轉運基因 ABCB5 調控化療耐藥性。更重要的是，GEP 和 ABCB5 的表達水平， 標示手術後的癌症 復發比率。 表達 GEP/ABCF1 的肝癌細胞增強了化療耐藥性，細胞集落形成能力， 和在免疫力低的小鼠生長癌瘤。特別的是，GEP 抗體治療可抑制與幹細胞相關的信號， 提供針對肝癌幹細胞的證據。然而，只有一半肝癌標本表達 ABCB5， 而大多數的肝癌患者都對化療具有耐藥性。因此，除了 ABCB5， 我們因此偵查其他藥物轉運基因，以研究它們調控化療耐藥性和肝癌幹細胞特性的能力。 我們有系統地用基因組方法研究藥物轉運基因。重新分析肝癌全基因組表達譜，在超過 170 個肝癌和肝組織標本中，探討藥物轉運基因的表達水平。 一組基因與 GEP 有顯著相關的表達水平，而 ABCB5 亦在其中， 這發現與我們最近的一份報告相吻合， 進一步證明研究方向的正確性。 重要的是，ABCF1 與 GEP 的表達水平有更緊密關連。 這數據已經在獨立的肝癌和肝組織標本中，以定量實時 RT-qPCR 方法驗證。 我們證明了在人類肝組織中的 GEP 和 ABCF1 表達水平顯著相關 （P<0.001）。 所有肝癌都有表達 ABCF1，而肝癌相比肝組織表達更高的 ABCF1 水平（P<0.001）。高的 ABCF1 表達水平，亦標示高的癌症復發比率 （log-rank test, P=0.001）。 在功能上，ABCF1 抑制肝癌細胞對化療藥物的敏感度。更重要的是，表達 GEP/ABCF1 的肝癌細胞，亦表達與幹細胞相關的信號，包括β-catenin, Oct4 和 Nanog。 因此，我們建議進一步研究 GEP/ABCB5/ABCF1 的分子和生物功能細節。 研究有兩個具體目標: 1. 檢查表達 GEP/ABCB5/ABCF1 的細胞， 在肝癌細胞株和臨床標本中的特點。 2：探討 GEP/ABCB5/ABCF1 在化療耐藥性和肝癌幹細胞的作用。這項研究將加深對肝癌化療耐藥性的理解，為提高肝癌的治療策略奠定基礎。

764112.label: Realisation of objectives
764112.value: Objective 1. To characterize the GEP/ABCB5/ABCF1 expression in HCC cell lines and clinical specimens: 100% achieved. The expression levels and co-expression patterns of GEP/ABCB5/ABCF1 have been examined in HCC cell lines and clinical specimens [Cheung et al. Oncotarget 2016; Cheung et al. Cancer Cell Int 2014 and 2016; Fung et al. AACR Proceedings 2016]. GEP protein levels were significantly higher in primary HCC tissues compared to their adjacent non-tumor liver tissues, and associated with venous infiltration [Cheung et al. Oncotarget 2016]. GEP expression levels significantly associated with the viability of isolated cancerous hepatocytes and success rate of subsequent primary culture establishment [Cheung et al. Cancer Cell Int 2014 and 2016]. GEP positive cells isolated from HCC clinical specimens exhibited higher levels of stem cell marker (CD133), pluripotency-associated signaling molecules (β-catenin, Oct4, SOX2 and Nanog) and chemodrug transporters (ABCB5 and ABCF1). Expression levels of GEP and pluripotency-associated genes were further examined which GEP and β-catenin showed significant correlation. Notably, HCC patients with high GEP and β-catenin levels demonstrated poor recurrence-free survival [Cheung et al. Oncotarget 2016]. In addition, the HCC cells were selected and expanded under chemotherapeutic agents as we have previously described. The cisplatin-resistant (CR), doxorubicin-resistant (DR) and fluorouracil-resistant (FR) showed an increase of 10-30 fold in resistance to their respective chemotherapeutic agents. The chemo-resistant HCC cells with acquired resistance demonstrated elevated expression levels of drug transporters and stem cell markers compared with the parental cells, and further boost upon chemotherapeutic treatments [Wong et al. Molecular Cancer Therapeutics 2014]. In summary, GEP-positive HCC cells directly isolated from clinical specimens and cell lines showed elevated levels of drug transporters and stem cell related molecules. Objective 2. To examine the role of GEP/ABCB5/ABCF1 in chemo-resistance and tumor-initiating cell properties: 100% achieved. The HCC cell lines and clinical specimens have been examined in vitro and in vivo for their chemo-responses (including drug sensitivity and efflux ability) and cancer stem cell properties according to GEP/ABCB5/ABCF1 levels [Cheung et al. Oncotarget 2016; Fung et al. AACR Proceedings 2016; Wong et al. Molecular Cancer Therapeutics 2014]. The enhanced ability to initiate tumor formation in immuno-compromised NOD SCID mice and nude mice models have been demonstrated in GEP positive cells with elevated ABCB5/ABCF1 levels [Cheung et al. Oncotarget 2016; Cancer Cell Int 2014 and 2016]. In addition, GEP positive cells possessed preferential ability to form colonies and spheroids, and enhanced in vivo tumor-initiating ability while their xenografts were able to be serially subpassaged into secondary mouse recipients. Minute number of GEP positive cancer cells were able to form tumor in immunocompromised mice within a short define period (1000 cells in four weeks formed tumor). Functional study demonstrated that GEP protected HCC cells against anoikis (programmed cell death induced by anchorage-dependent cells that detached from extracellular matrix) [Cheung et al. Cancer Cell Int 2014 and 2016]. Furthermore, HCC cells that survived under chemotherapeutic agents showed upregulation of hepatic cancer stem cell markers CD133/GEP/ABCB5, and enhanced colony and spheroid formation abilities [Wong et al. Molecular Cancer Therapeutics 2014]. Importantly, GEP blockage by antibody sensitized HCC cells to the apoptosis induced by chemotherapy for both HCC cell lines and the chemo-resistant subpopulations, and counteracted the chemotherapy-induced drug transporter expressions and Akt/Bcl-2 signaling. Furthermore, drug transporter over-expression would reduce intracellular drug levels indicating enhanced drug efflux efficiency when cells were exposed to chemotherapeutic agent. Immunoevasion has been emerging feature of cancer stem cell and GEP modulated HCC cells the ability to evade natural killer cell recognition [Cheung et al. Cancer Immunology Research 2014; Oncoimmunology 2015]. GEP down-regulated the surface expression of MHC class I chain–related molecule A [MICA, ligand for NK stimulatory receptor NK group 2 member D (NKG2D)], and upregulated human leukocyte antigen-E (HLA-E, ligand for NK inhibitory receptor CD94/NKG2A). In the co-culture assays, GEP suppression in HCC cells rendered NK cells enhanced expression of the stimulatory receptors NKG2D and CD69, increased secretion of functional molecules IFN-gamma and perforin. Blockage of GEP by antibody restored the natural killer cytotoxic activities. In summary, GEP modulated drug sensitivities and cancer stem cell features.

764112.label: Major findings and research outcome
764112.value: Cancer stem cells have influential function on disease progression, recurrence and drug resistance. Comprehensive characterization of hepatic cancer stem cell features are warranted. The present study demonstrated that granulin-epithelin precursor (GEP) is a hepatic cancer stem cell marker in human primary liver cancer associated with recurrence [Cheung et al. Oncotarget 2016]. GEP co-expressed with stem cell marker (CD133), pluripotency-associated signaling molecules (β-catenin, Oct4, SOX2 and Nanog) and drug transporters (ABCB5 and ABCF1) [Cheung et al. Oncotarget 2016] [Fung et al. AACR Proceedings 2016]. GEP positive cells isolated from primary liver cancer demonstrated elevated drug transporter levels with enhanced cancer stem cell features in cell-based assays and animal models [Cheung et al. Cancer Cell Int 2014 and 2016]. Blockage of GEP suppressed liver cancer growth, enhanced drug sensitivity and activated immune response [Wong et al. Molecular Cancer Therapeutics 2014] [Cheung et al. Cancer Immunology Research 2014; Oncoimmunology 2015]. The research platform developed in the current study facilitated the characterization of GEP binding partners/receptors through interaction with heparan sulfate [Yip et al. Carcinogenesis 2014]. In addition, expedited the work that GEP overexpression has been partly contributed by increased gene copy number [Yung et al. BMC Cancer 2015]. The patient cohort accrued in the present study accelerated the examination of ABCB5 sequence variation in liver cancer patients and healthy individuals. The ABCB5 genetic variation was associated with liver cancer risk and aggressive cancer features [Cheung et al. ABC Proteins Symposium 2014; Leung et al. AACR Proceedings 2014; Cheung et al. ATP Binding Cassette Transporters Symposium 2015]. This translational study demonstrated that GEP/ABCB5/ABCF1 modulated hepatic cancer stem cell features and specific targeting provided new insights for therapeutics development. The result of the present study has been published in six peer-reviewed research articles and one conference abstract. The research platform and patient cohort accumulated directly supported the publication of additional two referred research articles and three conference abstracts. The current study has trained two PhD students and filed/granted three patents.

764112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
764112.value: Biomarker: Elevated granulin-epithelin precursor (GEP) expression has been demonstrated in over 70% of primary liver cancer tissues, associated with recurrence-free survival, drug resistance and immune activity against cancer. Similarly for the escalated serum GEP levels in liver cancer patients. We and collaborators are building an algorithm with biomarkers reported by our group and others in tissue/blood for disease and treatment monitoring. Treatment: Targeting GEP resulted in liver cancer growth inhibition, enhancement of drug sensitivity and immune response activation. Development of clinical therapeutics against GEP include antibody humanization and nanoparticle-mediated systemic delivery for siRNA-based cancer therapy which are underway. The research platforms built further facilitate the research work on development of small molecule inhibitors against GEP for cancer treatment.

764112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
764112.value: Primary liver cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death worldwide. Treatment options are limited and prognosis remains poor. Surgery is the mainstay with the best survival outcome for early-stage patients. However, the majority of the patients have been diagnosed at advanced stage and curative surgery not applicable. Chemotherapy has marginal efficacy and sorafenib is the only FDA approved targeted drug with survival benefit of three months for advanced stage patients. Research effort should continue to understand the mechanism of drug resistance to strengthen treatment efficacy. Cancer stem cells have shown pivotal role on cancer progression, recurrence and drug resistance. Nonetheless, the precise characteristics of hepatic cancer stem cells remain unclear. The present study demonstrated that granulin-epithelin precursor (GEP) is a hepatic cancer stem cell marker in primary liver cancer associated with recurrence. GEP co-expressed with stem cell marker (CD133), pluripotency-associated signaling molecules (β-catenin, Oct4, SOX2 and Nanog) and drug transporters (ABCB5 and ABCF1). GEP positive cells isolated from primary liver cancer possessed enhanced cancer stem cell features in cell-based assays and animal models. Blockage of GEP suppressed liver cancer growth, enhanced drug sensitivity and activated immune response. This translational study provide new insights on prognosis and treatment strategy.

764512.value: 精子在射精后无法马上与卵母细胞受精，但是需要在女性生殖道内通过获能过程获得受精能力。此过程中包括精子头部细胞膜上分子的再定位，使精子能够与卵母细胞的外壳（透明带）结合。获能的精子通过与透明带上的糖序列结合，诱发顶体反应，从而启动受精过程。在此结合过程中存在缺陷是男性不育的主要原因。 尽管精子透明带相互作用十分重要，但它的调控机制还不清楚。为了解决这个问题，研究人员希望在精子表面找到负责精子透明带结合的分子（受体）。越来越多证据表明， 透明带受体是一个多分子结构，其中涉及在精子获能中聚集的几种蛋白质的协同作用。唾液酸化路易斯-X是透明带上主要的聚糖分子。我们发现，唾液酸化路易斯-X可以抑制精子透明带结合，但不影响精子顶体反应，由此表明有其它分子在精子透明带相互作用中参与诱导精子顶体反应。 我们已经在获能精子的细胞膜中分离出几种唾液酸化路易斯-X的结合蛋白。其中至少一种蛋白能够抑制精子透明带的结合。另外，我们还检测到在获能精子上存在唾液酸酶活性。阻断其活性会降低精子对透明带的结合能力以及进行顶体反应的能力。相反，经唾液酸酶处理的透明带会提高精子结合能力和诱导顶体反应的能力。 我们假设，精子透明带结合至少涉及两种与精子获能相关的事件。首先，精子唾液酸化路易斯-X结合蛋白介导初始的精子透明带结合，但这种作用并不影响精子顶体反应。第二，精子唾液酸酶改变透明带上的糖链结构，为进一步精子透明带结合和诱导精子顶体反应作准备。这两个事件依赖于精子获能，使唾液酸化路易斯-X结合蛋白和唾液酸酶曝露在精子表面。 为了验证此假设， 我们将研究精子获能、唾液酸化路易斯-X结合蛋白的表达、唾液酸酶的活性和精子透明带相互作用之间的关系，并且与临床辅助生育的受精相关联。此项研究结果将使我们更好地理解精子透明带的相互作用，为去唾液酸的透明带是否能应用到临床从而提高受精而提供线索。另外，此研究结果还能为是否能通过检测精子表面唾液酸化路易斯-X结合蛋白含量或/和唾液酸酶活性从而预测精液样本的受精能力作精子功能测试提供指征。

764512.label: Realisation of objectives
764512.value: Capacitated spermatozoa initiate fertilization by binding to the carbohydrate sequences on the zona pellucida (ZP). Defective spermatozoa-ZP binding leads to subfertility, and is an important cause of reduced fertilization in assisted reproduction. The regulation of spermatozoa-ZP interaction is unclear partly due to lack of knowledge on the identity of the ZP receptor on spermatozoa. Accumulated evidences indicate that the sperm ZP receptor is a multi-molecular structure involving coordinated actions of several proteins that are assembled during capacitation. With the use of ultrasensitive mass spectrometry, we have identified sialyl-Lewis(x) (SLeX) sequence (NeuAcα2-3Galβ1-4(Fucα1-3)GlcNAc) as the most abundant terminal sequence on the glycans of human ZP, and the major carbohydrate ligand for spermatozoa-ZP binding. We hypothesize that spermatozoa-ZP binding involves at least 2 capacitation-dependent events. First, sperm SLeX-binding protein mediates the initial spermatozoa–ZP binding but such interaction does not affect acrosome reaction. Second, sperm sialidase modifies the carbohydrate chains of ZP for further spermatozoa-ZP binding and induction of acrosome reaction. The two events are dependent on capacitation, which enable exposure of the SLeX-binding proteins and sialidase to the sperm surface. Objective 1: To determine the role of sperm SLeX-binding protein in spermatozoa-ZP interaction. Blue native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (BNG) and Western ligand blotting were developed and used to identify the solubilized ZP/SLeX-binding protein complexes on capacitated spermatozoa.The results provided direct evidences on the existence of multimolecular ZP receptor complexes on capacitated human spermatozoa (Part C, Section 8, No. 4; Section 9, No. 2 and 3; Section 10, No. 1). Affinity chromatography was then used to identify the SLeX-binding proteins on human spermatozoa. A total of 4 proteins with Mascot protein score higher than 65 were identified by mass spectrometry analysis. They are chromosome 1 open reading frame 56 (C1orf56), ZP-binding protein 1 (ZPBP1), heat shock-related 70 kDa protein 2 (HSPA2) and sperm acrosome membrane-associated protein 1 (SPACA 1). HSPA2, ZPBP1 and SPACA1 have reported to be involved in spermatozoon-oocyte interaction. Therefore, we only focus on C1orf56 in the following experiments. We demonstrated for the first time that human sperm surface C1orf56 is involved in spermatozoa-ZP binding. This conclusion comes from three observations: (1) Immunofluorescence staining localized C1orf56 to the acrosomal region of capacitated human spermatozoa, a region that binds ZP; (2) Anti-C1orf56 antibody suppressed spermatozoa-SLeX/purified ZP3/solubilized or intact ZP binding and ZP-induced acrosome reaction and (3) Purified C1orf56 from spermatozoa bound to human ZP. Objective 2: To establish the relationship between capacitation, acrosome reaction and the location of the SLEX-binding proteins on human spermatozoa. By using Western blot, we demonstrated that the amount of C1orf56 in the uncapacitated and capacitated spermatozoa were similar. Similar observation was obtained by flow cytometric analysis; the percentage of uncapacitated and capacitated sperm with positive C1orf56 immunoreactivity were 12.4±1.3% and 11.5±0.6% respectively. However, the C1orf56 immunoreactivity and its intensity on the acrosomal region of spermatozoa increased after capacitation in vitro as demonstrated by immunostaining. This suggests the translocation of sperm C1orf56 during capacitation. To determine whether C1orf56 are in the acrosomal matrix, the acrosomal matrix was isolated using nonionic detergent, which releases proteins from the membrane and the cytoplasm but not from the acrosomal matrix of spermatozoa. The expression of C1orf56 in the acrosomal matrix was then demonstrated by Western blotting. Objective 3: To establish the relationship between capacitation, sialidase activity and spermatozoa-ZP interaction. Glycoconjugates terminated with SLeX suppress spermatozoa-ZP binding but do not affect acrosome reaction (Pang et al., 2011), suggesting that other molecules are responsible for induction of acrosome reaction. In this objective, we hypothesize that capacitation induces the surface expression of sperm sialidase which desialylates the ZP glycans and unmasks ZP ligand for inducing sperm acrosome reaction. In mammalian cells, four sialidases have been characterized. Since sialidase-2 was not reported to be expressed on cell surface, we have only determined the expression of sialidase-1, -3 and -4 on human spermatozoa. Our results showed that only sialidase-1 and -3, but not sialidase-4, can be detected on sperm acrosomal region. Interestingly, similar to C1orf56, capacitation process can also induces the translocation of sialidase-1 and -3 on spermatozoa. Capacitated spermatozoa possessed sialidase activity, which increased the production of 4-methylumbelliferone (a sialidase substrate) in a time-dependent manner. To confirm the role of sialidase on sperm-ZP interaction, two sialidase inhibitors (didehydro-N-acetylneuraminic acid (DANA) and siastatin B) were used. Both inhibitors at the concentrations used did not affect sperm viability, motility and acrosomal status. On the other hand, DANA and siastatin B at the concentration of 1 mM significantly suppressed the ZP-binding capacity of human sperm by 40% and 47% respectively. ZP-induced acrosome reaction was also significantly suppressed by the sialidase inhibitors. Similar suppressive effects on sperm-ZP binding and ZP-induced acrosome reaction can be observed using antibody against sialidase-1 and -3. We further demonstrated that, ZP treated with exogenous sialidase had significantly increased binding to and acrosome reaction inducing activity on human spermatozoa. Desialylation was confirmed by the reduced binding of the hemizona to the lectin FITC-MAA. Objective 4. To determine the relationship between sperm surface SLEX-binding protein, SLEX-binding ability, surface sialidase activity and fertilization rate in vitro Normozoospermic and asthenozoospermic semen samples according to WHO criteria (WHO, 2010) were processed by Percoll discontinuous (45% and 90%) density gradient centrifugation. Asthenozoospermic samples had significantly (P<0.05) lower percentage of motile spermatozoa than normozoospermic samples. We demonstrated that normozoospermic sample has a higher sperm surface c1orf56 expression than that of asthenozoospermic sample. In addition, poor quality sperm isolated from a percoll gradient have decreased expression of c1orf56. These data suggest that reduction in sperm surface C1orf56 expression maybe a possible cause of fertilization problem in reproduction. However, in another collaborative study with the 6th Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, China, which included 11 men with in vitro fertilization rate <30% (Group A) and 24 men with in vitro fertilization rate >70% (Group B), no significant difference on their C1orf56 expression can be detected. On the other hand, sperm surface sialidase activity was demonstrated to be significantly lower (~25%) in Group A when compared to Group B.

764512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
764512.value: - Infertility affects about 15% of couples of reproductive age. Although assisted reproduction with intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) can improve their fertilization, the cost and the associated risks of the micromanipulation procedure may not justify men with mild fertilization problem to undergo ICSI. These men are in need of method to enhance their fertilization potential. We showed that desialylated-ZP produced by sialidase treatment has a higher sperm-binding capacity when compared to the control ZP without treatment. The results suggest that removal of sialic acid from ZP may applied clinically to enhance fertilization in assisted reproduction. Further studies are required to confirm this hypothesis. - Standard semen analysis in assisted reproduction treatment (ART) provides only limited information on the sperm fertilizing ability and defective ZP interaction can occur in 13% men with normal semen parameters. There is no easy method of identifying these patients. To improve the clinical management, it is important to diagnose defective ZP interaction by reliable test before commencing ART. Our results indicate the possible use of sperm sialidase activity determination as sperm function test for prediction of the fertilization potential of semen samples. The clinical value of our results can be evaluated in the future.

764512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
764512.value: Successful fertilization is initiated by the binding of the capacitated spermatozoa to the zona pellucida (ZP) of the oocyte. It is initiated by the binding of the capacitated spermatozoa to the ZP of the oocyte. The mechanisms of spermatozoa-ZP binding are unclear. Accumulated evidences indicate that the sperm ZP receptor is a multi-molecular structure involving coordinated actions of several proteins. In this study, our results provided direct evidence for the expression of a multimeric protein complex on the plasma membrane of capacitated human spermatozoa that is capable of binding to the ZP. Furthermore, chromosome 1 open reading frame 56 (C1orf56) and sialidase on capacitated sperm were demonstrated to play a complementary role in regulating the spermatozoa-ZP interactions in humans. The outcome of this project gives a better understanding on the spermatozoa-ZP binding. Clinically, the results indicate the possible use of sperm surface sialidase activity as sperm function test for prediction of fertilization potential of semen samples in assisted reproduction.

764612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
764612.value: 微生物在生態系統中扮演著重要的管理角色，特別在營養動力學及炭﹑氮﹑磷和硫的生地化循環。隨著人類活動的增加及相繼帶來的富養化作用，在過去二十年，沿海地區的缺氧現象變得更頻密和嚴重。少量研究指出缺氧能夠改變氧化還原作用中的平衡和其有關的生地化循環過程。可是，至今仍沒有研究顯示缺氧可否直接影響海洋沉積物的微生物郡落的架構和功能。 在環境轉變下，微生物群落架構會因而改變。當中，這些群落架構會維持不變（抵抗力）或會改變但最後回復本來的架構（恢復力）。可是，海洋沉積物的微生物郡落對於缺氧的抵抗力和恢復力仍然不明。而且，微生物群落架構的改變對生態系統功能構成的影響亦不確定。因為在同一個郡落裡的其他仍然存活的種類亦可能擔當死去種類的角色，繼續維持生態系統功能的穩定性（功能性重疊）。畢竟，至今仍未有報告指出在缺氧情況下，海洋微生物郡落會否出現功能性重疊。如果會，它的影響又會是什麼程度？ 利用宏基因組及基因微陣列技術，我們可以對微生物郡落架構及其功能進行確切的分析。 本計劃的主要目標： 1. 研究缺氧對海洋裡表面沉積物的微生物郡落架構的影響； 2. 研究因缺氧改變的微生物郡落對生物地質化學循環過程的影響；以及， 3. 了解海洋微生物郡落的抵抗力﹑恢復力和功能性重疊。 本計劃是首個探究缺氧如何影響微生物郡落及管理養分循環的生物地質化學循環過程的科學研究。研究成果將會在海洋微生物郡落的架構及功能性重疊提供重要的理解。

764612.label: Realisation of objectives
764612.value: The project has been successfully completed. Following the research plan and methodology stipulated in the proposal, laboratory and field experiments have been carried out to meet the three project objectives. Major findings and outcome generated from the laboratory experiment (i.e. a 28-days microcosm) have been published in Marine Pollution Bulletin 85:425–432, a leading SCI journal in the field. There has been increasing concerns of interactive effects of hypoxia and other stressors on the marine ecosystem. Therefore, additional experiment has been carried out to investigate the effects of the flame-retardant BDE47 (an important emerging chemical of concern that occurs ubiquitously in the marine environment), to further investigate both the independent and interactive effects of these two stressors on the bacterial community in surface marine sediment. The results have also been included in the publication (Marine Pollution Bulletin 85:425–432). The structure and function of the microbial communities in the natural sediments between the hypoxic, and normoxic zones as well as the transplanted sediments (normoxic to hypoxic, and hypoxic to normoxic) in Tolo Harbour, Hong Kong were compared. Examination of 10 years of water quality monitoring data collected by the Environmental Protection Department, Hong Kong Government, revealed that the Tolo Harbour and Channel in Hong Kong are characterized by a hypoxic gradient during the summer months when vertical stratification is marked. A manuscript that reports this field study is under preparation. The microbial community composition was analyzed by high-throughput bacterial 16S rRNA gene next-generation sequencing. Multivariate PERMANOVA analysis using UniFrac measures visualized in Principal Coordinates Analysis (PCoA) was used to reveal the differences and shift in microbial communities. To assess the functional changes of microbial communities in response to hypoxia, metagenomics shotgun sequencing of environmental DNA was performed on the Illumina HiSeq platform. The metagenomes of the normoxic and hypoxic microbial communities sampled generated approximately 4.93 Gbp clean sequencing data. Identified genes were compiled into a non-redundant catalog of 1,099,099 genes. The frequency of annotation groups involved in biogeochemical processes, namely sulfur metabolism, nitrogen metabolism, carbon metabolism, carbon fixation pathways in prokaryotes and methane metabolism were evaluated.

764612.label: Major findings and research outcome
764612.value: 1) In the 28-days microcosm experiment, T-RFLP analysis and clone libraries sequences revealed that hypoxia affected both the composition and structure of bacterial communities in the marine surface sediments. Hypoxia resulted in more Bacteroidetes, Epsilonproteobacteria and Verrucomicrobia, but less Alpha-, Gamma- and Deltaproteobacteria and Firmicutes, and these phyla contributed to the major differences between the hypoxia treatment and the normoxia control according to the SIMPER analysis. Hypoxia also reduced the alpha-diversity, species richness and genetic diversity of bacterial communities in marine surface sediments (Marine Pollution Bulletin 85:425–432). 2) Additional experiment was carried out to test whether hypoxia would interact with other stressors to affect the microbial communities in the marine surface sediments. Both hypoxia and BDE47 alone significantly altered the bacterial community and reduced the species and genetic diversity. UniFrac analysis revealed that BDE47 selected certain bacterial species and resulted in major shifts in community structure, whereas hypoxia changed the relative abundances of taxa, suggesting slower but nonetheless significant shifts in community structure. These two stressors targeted mostly different taxa, but they both favored Bacteroidetes and suppressed Gammaproteobacteria (Marine Pollution Bulletin 85:425–432). 3) In the field study, multivariate PERMANOVA analysis using UniFrac measures visualized in PCoA demonstrated that the microbial communities of normoxic and hypoxic basal samples were divided into two groups, indicating that the two sediments harbored distinct microbial communities. In particular, a higher degree of variation was observed among the microbial communities of hypoxic sediment than normoxic sediment, as indicated by the closer clustering of the normoxic samples in PCoA. Moreover, the microbial community composition of both hypoxic and normoxic basal samples were stable across all sampling times (week 2, 6, 10). 4) Multivariate PERMANOVA analysis on normoxic and hypoxic basal and transplanted samples from the same origin showed a clear compositional shift of the transplanted communities from the microbial communities of the basal samples at week 2 and week 6. Nonetheless, at week 10, the microbial communities of transplanted samples clustered strongly by site of origin when analyzed with unweighted UniFrac distances in PCoA, suggesting that the microbial communities were resilient to the effects of the transplant. 5) Despite structural changes were evident, multivariate analysis of the frequency of annotation groups that are involved in biogeochemical processes suggested that these microbial functions of normoxic and hypoxic basal and transplanted samples were largely similar, indicating functional redundancy of the microbial communities in marine surface sediments.

764612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
764612.value: The findings and outcome from the laboratory microcosm experiments have already been published in the SCI journal Marine Pollution Bulletin (85:425–432). A second manuscript that describes the results generated from the field study is under preparation, and will be submitted to a SCI journal.

764612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
764612.value: Because of eutrophication resulting from increasing anthropogenic activities, hypoxia is on the rise globally. While microorganisms play a pivotal role in regulating key ecosystem processes (i.e. trophodynamics and biogeochemical cycles of carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur), the present study provides an understanding on the impact of hypoxia on marine microbial communities, which enables us to assess the severity and consequences of hypoxia. Results of this project showed that hypoxia significantly altered the bacterial community in surface marine sediment and reduced both species diversity and genetic diversity. Therefore, the microbial communities were not resistant to hypoxia. Results of the field transplant experiment further demonstrated that microbial communities altered by hypoxia could return to the original composition shortly after hypoxia, indicating a relatively high level of community resilience. Furthermore, the microbial function involved in the biogeochemical processes of normoxic, hypoxic and transplanted sediments were generally similar, suggesting functional redundancy of the microbial communities. Overall, results of this novel study provided important insight on the structural and functional responses of marine microbial community to hypoxia.

764812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
764812.value: 高血壓作為引發缺血性心臟病及繼發的中風，心功能衰竭或腎臟衰竭的主要風險因素，其發病率逐年上升。據統計，高血壓已成為全世界人口的主要死亡原因之一，其直接導致的死亡人數高達每年七百萬以上。引發高血壓的原因，除了水鹽平衡失調外，在血管緊縮素II(ANGII)和抗利尿激素(VP)控制下的心血管功能對於維持人體正常灌注過程也具重要意義。我們近期研究指出胰泌素(SCT)在機體水鹽平衡控制方面具關鍵作用。此外，曾有學者提出SCT在心血管系統中的潛在功能: SCT可以調節心肌收縮力，並對動脈收縮幅度和頻率都有顯著影響。基於上述發現，我們假設，除ANGII和VP外，SCT同樣可起到維持正常血壓的作用。我們使用原發性高血壓大鼠(SHR)，胰泌素敲除小鼠(SCTKO)，胰泌素受體敲除小鼠(SCTRKO)對SCT與高血壓間的關係進行了初步研究。為檢測SCT及SCTR是否同SHR的漸進型高血壓相關，我們測量了大鼠部分組織內SCT和SCTR的表達水準。值得注意的是，在SHR大鼠心臟中，SCTR未存在顯著的表達(僅及對照大鼠的0.34%)，說明在高血壓的發展過程中，SCTR的表達被顯著及特異性的抑制。同時我們還發現大鼠內SCTR的表達水準和年齡顯著相關：自1月齡始到5月齡止，SCTR轉錄活性隨年齡逐漸下降。這一趨勢和SHR大鼠體內高血壓的發展和cAMP反應活性的下降相吻合。綜上所述，SCTR在SHR大鼠內表達水準的改變趨勢說明SCT和SCTR對心血管功能和血壓調控具潛在作用。為進一步研究兩者間關係，我們測量了野生型，SCTKO和SCTRKO小鼠尾部動脈收縮壓，並發現SCTKO和SCTRKO動物的收縮壓顯著高於野生型。這一結果進一步驗證了SCT-SCTR調控路徑的破壞可能誘發高血壓。有鑑於此，我們提出如下假設：SCT和SCTR是調控新血管功能及血壓的關鍵因素。這一研究專案將著重驗證上述假設，並可能為未來抗高血壓藥物的研究提供關鍵性幫助。

764812.label: Realisation of objectives
764812.value: Objective 1 In previous reports, we have found that SCTR is required for the ANG-induced aldosterone biosynthesis, but the molecular mechanisms remained unclear. The SCTR/AT1aR heterodimer has been previously reported to mediate the central function of ANG in water-drinking behavior. Hereby, we hypothesized this dimer also bridge other actions of ANG, such as ANG-induced aldosterone biosynthesis. We first proved the co-existence of functional AT1R and SCTR in the ZG layer. Transcripts of at1aR, at1bR, at2R and sctr were detected in the primary ZG cells obtained from C57 and SCTR-/-. IHC staining showed the presence of SCTR in mouse adrenal ZG and cAMP assays responding to SCT confirmed the SCTR there are functional. Using the AT1R antagonist, candesartan, it is clearly showed that the AT1R in primary ZG cells are functional and can be inhibited by its pharmaceutical antagonist. The ANG-induced aldosterone is mediated through phosphatidylinositol-calcium (Ca2+) secondary messenger system, we further explored the effects of SCTR on ANG-inducible Ca2+ mobilization. Although the SCTR-/- ZG cells can still be activated, the ANG-dose-dependent response (ranging from 0.1 nM to 1 μM) was absent, unlike the C57 ZG cells. Time-course measurement (from time 0 to 240 min) clarified the disrupted ANG-induced (10 nM) aldosterone release in SCTR-/-, consistent with the observations in last reports and the altered Ca2+ influx pattern. These data the absence of SCTR disrupted the Ca2+ influx induced by ANG and the subsequent aldosterone release. We have previously specified the impact of synthetic SCTR transmembrane (TM) peptide 2 on disassociation of SCTR/AT1aR. With the employment of STM2 and its mutant (STM2 mut), we further investigated the role of SCTR/AT1R in this ANG-induced Ca2+ influx. The presence of either STM2 or its mutant peptide did not alter the response of ZG cells to extracellular potassium (60 mM). STM2 abolished the ANG-mobilized Ca2+ influx like the AT1R antagonist candesartan, which could be partially recovered by STM2 mut. However, the inhibitory effects of STM2 was absent in SCTR-/- ZG cells, showing that it is the SCTR/AT1R that mediates the ANG-mobilized Ca2+ influx. Of note, STM2 mut could not rescue the inhibitory impact completely, indicating the involvement of AT1bR which shares high homology with AT1aR, as well as dimerizes with SCTR. In the C57 ZG cells, pre-incubation with STM2 abolished the ANG-induced aldosterone, but can be partially recovered by STM2 mut. The presence of STM2 did not change the effects of ANG in aldosterone production in SCTR-/- ZG cells. These results further confirmed the presence and involvement of SCTR/AT1R in the ANG-induced aldosterone production. Objective 2 In previous report, the interaction between SCTR and V2R is confirmed by BRET assay. TM peptides were also employed as biophysical tools to decipher the dimerization interfaces. cAMP signaling modification were observed with receptor dimer formation, where SCT-induced cAMP production was potentiated (Emax from 98.75 ±0.72 to 152.50±0.29% and EC50 from 51.44±9.90 to 2.48±0.25 nM) and Vp-induced cAMP was blunted (Emax from 89.75±5.92 to 45.23±2.88% and EC50 shifted from 6.36±0.15 to 84.20±21.7 nM). Here, on top of cAMP signaling, the effect of SCTR/V2R dimerization on the phosphatidylinositol-calcium signaling pathway was investigated. For intracellular calcium response, cells transfected with SCTR only showed a typical sigmoidal response curve. In the presence of V2R, however, the calcium signals were mostly abolished. In V2R-transfected cells, a response was observed only at 1 µM Vp, while the presence of SCTR had no significant effect on maximal response nor potency. To confirm further the function of GPCR oligomerization in mediating changes in signaling, cells were incubated with STMIV or DMSO vehicle control prior to cAMP measurements. The previously recorded potentiation in SCT stimulated cells co-expressing SCTR+V2R was reversed by STMIV (Emax=71.01±4.16%) vs vehicular control (Emax=141.03±6.15%), but there was no significant change in potency (EC50=6.48±1.72 vs EC50=6.04±1.34 nM). For Vp-induced cAMP, disrupting heteromer formation restores both the maximal response and the potency of V2R. Emax was raised from 47.95±5.28% in the vehicle control to 75.75±4.11% with STMIV treatment. There were no significant changes in maximal response nor potency between vehicle or STMIV treated cells expressing V2R only as STMIV does not inhibit V2R homomer. These data collectively indicate that SCTR/V2R heteromer reduce function of SCTR in response to SCT. To elucidate the effect of dimerization on V2R mutants, BRET assays were performed. Interestingly, SCTR was found to specifically rescue a mutant form of V2R, R137H, which causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (NDI). Other V2R mutants (A89P, Q174R) which lead to the same disease but through different mechanism were not rescued by SCTR co-expression. This indicates the specificity of SCTR’s relationship with a certain form of the disease. Visual evidence was also collected by confocal microscopy. Co-expression of SCTR can only rescue the surface expression of the R137H, but not the other forms of V2R mutations. NDI leads to polyuria and polydipsia, upsetting the balance of body water/salt homeostasis. Therefore, this particular ability of SCTR to rescue the surface presentation of R137H V2R mutant shifted our focus on how SCTR/V2R dimerization could potentially influence the functioning of this mutant. By assaying cellular signaling, rescue by SCTR brought about the partial functioning of R137H in response to both SCT and Vp stimulation. The signaling modifications in WT V2R was also preserved in the SCTR-rescued R137H mutant.

764812.label: Major findings and research outcome
764812.value: With the support from this grant, we worked on secretin’s role in water/salt homeostasis through SCTR/AT1aR and SCTR/V2R receptor complexes. First, the co-localization of SCT, SCTR and aldosterone synthase CYP11B2 in the adrenal cortex indicates the connection between SCT/SCTR and aldosterone regulation. Indeed, using SCT/SCTR knockout animals, SCT was found to increase the expression of CYP11B2. Together with our observation that SCT was unable to directly control expression of various ENaC subunits in the kidney tubule cells, we concluded that SCT can indirectly regulate salt homeostasis in the kidney via aldosterone synthesis. Furthermore, with co-injection of ANG and SCT stimulated a significantly higher plasma aldosterone release than ANG injection alone, we found that the SCT/SCTR axis magnifies the effects of ANG on aldosterone release. The presence and involvement of SCTR/AT1R receptor complex was found to be responsible for this magnified ANG-induced aldosterone production. With confirmed co-expression of SCTR/At1aR at the zona glomerulosa (ZG) layer in the adrenal gland and by monitoring calcium influx, the absence of SCTR was found to disrupt Ca2+ influx induced by ANG and subsequent aldosterone release. The specific involvement of SCTR/AT1aR receptor complex was established by utilizing the biochemical tool of receptor TM peptides. For water/salt homeostasis in the kidney, SCTR/V2R heterodimerization was confirmed by BRET technique. Such receptor complex was found to potentiate SCT- induced cAMP and blunts Vp-induced cAMP responses. For cellular calcium, SCT-induced calcium flux was blunted but there was no effect to that of Vp- induced. These signaling modifications were considered as a specific result of receptor complex formation through the use of TM peptides. Of interest, SCTR dimerization was found also to be able to functionally rescue a V2R mutant (R137H) that is responsible for causing the disease nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (NDI). In summary, our data show that the heterocomplexes of SCTR/AT1aR and SCTR/V2R play an essential roles in mediating water/salt homeostasis. The results from this project were published in several publications (please refer to Part C).

764812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
764812.value: Our data suggested neutral lipids (cholesteryl ester) are accumulated after low Na+ diet feeding in C57, but not in SCTR-/- mice. With our published paper indicating SCT/SCTR is involved in lipid balance, it is interesting to see this impaired accumulation of cholesterol in SCTR-/- mice fed with low Na+ diet. This could be caused by the failure of cholesterol uptake from blood. Thus, blood lipid will be determined and detections of the lipid droplet in the adrenal gland can be performed. Also, we observed ANGII can induce SCT secretion, but it is still unclear whether the increase originates through central or peripheral ANGII, or both. Therefore, we will try to block the central ANGII pathway to observe the effects of circulating ANGII on SCT release. Our recent data suggest the involvement of SCT in vascular physiology by using the secretin knockout mouse model. As water/salt homeostasis is tightly related to blood pressure, the possible role of SCT/SCTR in hypertension could be investigated.

764812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
764812.value: Water/salt homeostasis is a very important aspect in maintaining the health of a human being. Our findings show that SCTR/AT1aR and SCTR/V2R receptor complexes are essential water homeostatic key players performing crucial physiological functions in our body. Our work deciphers the involvement of SCT to regulate salt homeostasis via ANG-induced aldosterone synthesis. We also provided evidence on SCT’s role to control water balance by alternating cellular signaling. Our work is fundamental to the area of water/salt homeostasis research and is important for understanding the actions of SCT, ANGII, Vp in relation to water/salt homeostasis in our body. Having one-third of therapeutics on the market nowadays targeting GPCRs, and with receptor complex formation regulating cellular physiology, this project implicates on the future development of drugs treating water/salt homeostasis diseases.

765212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
765212.value: 醛糖還原酶（aldose reductase, AR）是多元醇通路的關鍵限速酶。本實驗室先前已經證實醛糖還原酶及其下游的生物化學變化（如NAD(P)H 氧化酶，JNK，NF-kB和蛋白激酶C在外周神經系統的活化）在糖尿病神經病變的發病機制中具有重要作用。我們也曾證實含有Thy1-YFP的醛糖還原酶基因敲除老鼠（其感覺神經元和運動神經元的軸突和神經末梢表達黃色螢光蛋白）在糖尿病狀態下具有更佳的華勒變性和神經再生，這些變化源於吞噬反應和血管再生趨於正常化。隨後在對野生型以及醛糖還原酶基因敲除小鼠神經組織的蛋白質組分析比較中我們找到了其中可能的機理。與野生型小鼠相比，醛糖還原酶基因敲除小鼠的神經組織中有親環素A和磷酸甘油醇異構酶的表達變化，從而通過誘導MMP-9的表達而對小神經膠質細胞/巨噬細胞浸潤產生影響。另外，體外實驗初步結果顯示，在高血糖條件下，醛糖還原酶基因敲除小鼠的背根神經節細胞比野生型有更長的神經突起。於此相關的是，RhoA活性與神經突起生長，血管生成，細胞吞噬，細胞骨架生長以及糖尿病痛性神經病變相關。本實驗室近來成功培育出了Rho蛋白GTP酶活化蛋白(RhoGAP) ——Deleted in Liver Cancer 2 (DLC2)基因敲除小鼠，並將其與Thy1-YFP轉基因小鼠雜交，為對其進行無創性外周神經纖維研究提供了便利。 DLC2基因敲除小鼠的外周神經和脊髓具有更高的RhoA和pErk活性，並對熱刺激與炎症性刺激疼痛表現出高度敏感。爲了進一步研究DLC2/RhoA/pERK信號通路在其中的作用，我們將會使用與在醛糖還原酶基因敲除小鼠身上誘導糖尿病相似的方法來對DLC2基因敲除小鼠進行糖尿病的誘導。本計畫的目的是在體內體外水平上研究DLC2/Rho/pErk信號通路在神經損傷的情況下對華勒變性，巨噬細胞聚集以及神經再生過程的作用，以及這一通路如何影響在許多患有糖尿病神經病變的病人身上表現出的疼痛加劇或無痛性反應。現今，雖然醛糖還原酶抑製劑已經在日本上市，醫學界對這些病人所能提供的治療方法仍然非常有限。我們這一創新性的研究將為糖尿病神經病變的分子機制提供更深入的瞭解，並可能對這一疾病提供新的療法。

766012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766012.value: 研究背景: 齲齒是高發的口腔疾病，全世界多達50億人受齲齒危害。齲齒的發生很大程度上取決於生活習慣（飲食和口腔衛生），通過有效的行為干預，可以達到預防齲齒的目的。幼兒期是建立健康習慣的關鍵時期，在這個階段建立良好的健康習慣有利於終生保持牙齒健康。常規的健康教育 (CE) 著重傳播資訊和提供建議，然而，這並不足以改善人們的健康習慣。針對這種現狀，此研究引入兩項創新元素進行口腔健康干預，包括動機式會談 (MI) 和互動式齲齒風險評估 (RA)。該隨機控制實驗將比較三種干預方案 (CE、 CE+MI、 CE+MI+RA) 在改善幼兒口腔健康習慣、預防齲齒方面的作用。 研究方法: 此研究將從12所幼稚園招募690名口腔健康習慣（刷牙及飲食）欠佳的3歲兒童及他們的家長，他們將被隨機分為三組。第一組（CE）的家長將會收到宣傳單張，提供他們口腔健康知識和建議。第二組（CE+MI) 的家長除了收到單張外, 將由經過培訓的口腔衛生員個別進行動機式會談。在第三組 (CE+MI+RA)，除了單張和動機式會談，互動式齲齒風險評估將被用來激勵家長，並協助他們作出決定和設定目標。在項目初始以及12個月和24個月後，家長將完成一份問卷，幼兒將接受牙齒檢查。三種干預項目的有效性將在12個月和24個月後被評估並比較。兒童的新發齲齒將為主要觀測指標，家長在保護幼兒口腔健康方面的親職效能感和幼童的口腔健康習慣變化將作為次要觀測指標。 意義: 此研究旨在建立有效的行為干預方案以達到預防齲齒的目的，此研究的結果將提供科學依據，以便公共衛生專業人士、牙醫及牙科輔助人員（護士及牙科衛生員）選擇適當的方法，促進兒童的口腔健康。

766012.label: Major findings and research outcome
766012.value: Our findings showed that motivational interviewing was more effectiveness than prevailing health education in changing parents' self-efficacy to protect children's oral health, improving preschool children's oral health behaviors, and preventing early childhood caries. When the interactive caries risk assessment tool was incorporated to assist motivational interviewing, the outcomes were further improved. 766012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
766012.value: Motivational interviewing has great potential in changing health behaviors. However, its effectiveness in changing oral health related behaviors is yet to be tested. This is the first randomized controlled trial we completed. Further studies can be planned to test motivational interviewing in other age groups, targeting other oral health behaviors, and incorporating more useful tools into dental counseling.

766012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766012.value: This randomized controlled trial provides useful evidence on the effectiveness of motivational interviewing (with and without interactive communication tool) in motivating parents to improve children's oral health behaviors and prevent oral diseases. The findings serve as useful reference for public health workers, dentists, dental hygienists and other dental auxiliaries to choose the best method and improve people's oral health.

766112.label: Major findings and research outcome
766112.value: By whole-exome sequencing (WES) of liver tissue DNA of 24 sporadic PBA patients we identified and validated (in both tissue and blood) 48 patient-unique, damaging mutations. These variants are distributed among 27 genes (some recurrently mutated -at different sites- in our patients) that belong to pathways implicated in liver development, immunity processes, or linked to ciliopathies. Variants are inherited and often form either compound heterozygotes or suggest digenic inheritance. From this one can conclude: De novo variants (either SNVs or CNVs) do not seem to play a role in BA Biliary atresia is a genetically heterogeneous disease whereby different genes can lead to the same or similar phenotype. Biliary atresia is also an oligogenic disease whereby more than one mutated gene are needed in an individual for the disease to manifest Genes with potentially damaging mutations can be grouped into pathways related to implicated in liver development, immunity processes, or linked to ciliopathies. These genes are recurrently mutated in different patients and at different sites

766112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
766112.value: As stated, the interesting results of this project have served as a springboard to obtain funding for follow-up. Mutations of the causative genes of polycystic kidney disease, PKD1 and PKD2, and other “Mendelian” disorders were detected in this exome survey on 23 isolated BA patients. The patients bearing such mutated genes also had additional mutations in other biologically related genes. Our study has come up with new targets that may help us interpret pathogenesis of the disease. However functional testing of the genetic effects and see if these mutations either alone or in combination results in a phenotypes related to the disease is necessary. Therefore, we should: 1: Check more patients for mutations in those recurrently mutated genes or at exome level. 2: Functionally test those genes with damaging variants (Zebra fish)

766112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766112.value: This project aimed at finding out which genes were mutated in patients with biliary atresia. To this end, we have explored the genes of 24 patients (not more because reagents are very expensive) We found that: 1: The disease can result from mutations in different genes 2: These mutated genes are biologically realted=> diferent genes = same disease 3: Patients can have more than one gene mutated, which complicate things a bit. 4: These nasty mutations are inherited from the parents. Yet, the patient has additional mutations (inherited from a different parent) that all together give rise to the disease. That is: mutations from the father + mutations from the mother = disease. That is why the parents are not affected.

766212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766212.value: 前言: 進食是一種對維持人體健康和生活質素不可或缺的能力。可是,罹患根本性進食功能障礙(包括味覺問題,咀嚼及/或吞嚥)的人數正續漸增加。原因包括年老,癌症,電療,藥物治療,心身疾病等。醫學界到現時還未制訂出客觀性的診斷數據,傳統的治療都是靠行為實驗和藥物治療並以反覆試驗的方式進行,但成效有限。如果進食功能障礙的原因能被準確地診斷,醫生便可以縮窄和制定個人化的治療方法。 重點: 由已刊登的研究,我們假設進食功能障礙患者的腦神經網絡聯繫有位置和時間上的誤差。功能性磁力共振造影是一種非侵略性的、對特定刺激有反應的腦功能掃瞄技術，首席研究員之前已研發出一個全新的，用於口、顎的電腦三維功能性磁力共振分析技術，但該系統和其結果只能局限於3D診斷。加上時間部分可似製作出一個四維的（4D），高解像度的（一毫米的空間分辨率，少於一秒的時間分辨率）空間﹣時間網絡分析系統以研究受刺激進食時的腦部激活。一個健康成年人進食時的4D腦部激活資料庫亦有助未來參考以作出準確的進食功能障礙診斷。 目的：我們希望1）建構一個由電腦控制的功能性磁力共振系統以分析進食時的4D腦部功能，2）設立一個精簡的健康成年人進食時的4D腦部激活資料庫，3）尋找可能的進食功能障礙診斷標誌。 研究方法：一個4D的、由電腦控制的刺激傳送系統和分析系統會被優化以作受刺激進食時的腦部激活分析。五十名健康的成年人（十八至三十五歲）會接受口腔感覺和功能測試（味覺,咀嚼及吞嚥），其結果會與功能性磁力共振一同分析來設立進食時的物理性診斷標誌。 重要性：我們的創新和高解像度4D腦部激活分析系統是全世界首個客觀性和標準的結果，解釋腦部如何控制進食。我們的健康成年人腦部激活資料庫和物理診斷標誌能作為進食功能障礙的客觀診斷正常標準，醫護人員可以根據這標準改善患者治療，跟進，和回復其正常進食生活水平。

766212.label: Realisation of objectives
766212.value: Objectives 1 -3 are achieved in particular tasting and retronasal smelling function are being investigated using fMRI and the corresponding essential networks were identified. Four related repots were published/accepted (IF: 0.967, 2.053, 2.5 and 5.463). Two manuscripts are under mid-review, including one submitted to NeuroImage. Concerning objective 3 in particular, other than what is needed for taste, smell, swallowing and mastication, the research team also explored a prove of principle experiment by extending the model to dental anxiety correlation and was able to gain positive results. Three manuscripts are now being draft summarizing the corresponding findings. We anticipate that we can finish publishing all related reports in peer reviewed IF journals in 24 months.

766212.label: Major findings and research outcome
766212.value: The team managed to design and create an functional, efficient and reliable system to monitor through fMRI the brain responses during simple taste, and retronasal simple smell perception and able to assay the connectivity of various activated brain regions so to decipher the brain physiology of smell/taste sensation. As prove of principle experiment, the team also explore the system's successful utility on dental fear concerning visual, sound or combination with initial satisfactory results.

766212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
766212.value: Future research targets include more basic study of all five basic taste elements (current investigations available in literature biased to sweet taste only), and perhaps explore to include corresponding congruent simple smell. Next development could be on changes of human brain taste and smell sensation decoding alongside with aging, development of eating disorder especially obesity as well as metabolic disease like diabetes.

766212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766212.value: Human eating/drinking behavior is significantly affected by sight, smell, taste, texture sensation and our brain's appreciate of it. Eating is an activity that keep all living beings alive. Eating disorder will cause diseases in human. Obviously our brain could be 'trained' to appreciate the food we take and the process involves complex interactions between the neural connections of all the senses involved together with memory and emotion. This project studied the basic science of taste, smell and their combined sensation/processing in human brain. The team created a robust method for the related research and is able to decipher the brain regions activated and how these regions are connected. Their initial success will inspire further explorations of this very important human physiological function particularly how variation of such might be associate with human aging and/or disease.

766412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766412.value: PECAM-1 (platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule 1, also known as CD31) is a cell adhesion molecule expressed on the surfaces of many immune cells and endothelial cells. The coexistence of PECAM-1 on leukocytes and endothelial cells leads to a very important role for PECAM-1 in leukocyte transmigration across blood vessel in response to inflammation. PECAM-1 promotes cell adhesion and transmigration through PECAM-1/PECAM-1 homophilic interactions and heterophilic interactions with a number of other molecules expressed on immune cells. Many vascular diseases such as angiogenesis, atherosclerosis, arthritis, thrombosis, and vascular disorders are closely related to PECAM-1. PECAM-1 may also be involved in tumor cell re-localization. To facilitate a deep understanding of these processes regulated by PECAM-1, it is important to determine the structures of PECAM-1 and PECAM-1 complexed with its ligands. In this study, we propose to: (1) solve the crystal structure of the N-terminal three domains D1-D3 of PECAM-1; (2) solve the complex structure of D1-D3 with CD38; and (3) solve the crystal structure of the remaining three domains D4-D6 and complex structures of D4-D6 with various metal ions. The structural information will provide insights into the molecular basis for the homophilic and heterophilic cell adhesion and transmigration processes regulated by PECAM-1 and help treat PECAM-1 related diseases. PECAM-1（血小板内皮细胞粘附分子1，也称为CD31）是一种在许多免疫细胞和内皮细胞表面上表达的细胞粘附分子。PECAM-1在免疫细胞和内皮细胞上的共存导致了PECAM-1在响应炎症反应时免疫细胞沿血管迁移过程中扮演了一个非常重要的角色。 PECAM-1通过PECAM-1/PECAM-1同种的相互作用和与其他免疫细胞上表达的分子异性相互作用促进细胞的粘附和迁移。许多血管疾病，如血管生成，动脉粥样硬化，关节炎，血栓形成，和血管异常都与PECAM-1密切相关。 PECAM-1也有可能参与肿瘤细胞的重新定位。为了深刻理解这些受PECAM-1调控的过程，一项重要的工作是测定PECAM-1以及PECAM-1与它的结合配体的结构。在这项研究中，我们提议：（1）测定PECAM-1的N-末端三个结构域D1-D3的晶体结构，（2）测定D1-D3与CD38复合物的晶体结构，以及（3）测定剩下的三个结构域D4-D6的晶体结构及D4-D6与不同金属离子的复合物结构。这些结构信息将提供受PECAM-1调控的同种和异嗜细胞粘附和迁移过程的分子基础，并帮助治疗PECAM-1相关的疾病。

766412.label: Realisation of objectives
766412.value: 1. To solve the crystal structure of the N-terminal three domains D1-D3 of PECAM-1. We have successfully determined the crystal structure of PECAM-1 D1-2 trans-homo dimer. Both D1 and D2 adopt the classical Ig domain conformation that comprises of two layers of β-sheets possessing antiparallel β-strands with each being anchored by a pair of cysteines forming a disulfide bond. The dimer interface includes hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions. The Small-Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS) envelope of PECAM-1 D1-6 supported such a dimer formation in solution. Cell adhesion assays on wildtype and mutant PECAM-1 further characterized the structural determinants in cell junction and communication (Scientific Reports, under review). 2. To solve the complex structure of D1-D3 with CD38. In addition to the PECAM-1/PECAM-1 homophilic interaction, heterophilic interactions between PECAM-1 and human CD38 were also reported by other groups to regulate the leukocytes adhesion to endothelial cells. We had proposed to study the complex structure between PECAM-1 and CD38 through co-crystallization of the N-terminal three domains of PECAM-1 (D1-D3) and the ecto-domain of CD38. Human CD38 had successfully been expressed and crystallized in our group. However, our gel filtration shift assay showed that PECAM-1 cannot bind CD38 directly, therefore they cannot form a complex. As a backup plan, we determined crystal structures of the complexes of CD38 with the nanobodies. Since CD38 is highly expressed in several hematologic malignancies including multiple myeloma (MM), these structures set the stage for the development of clinical therapeutics as well as diagnostic screening for myeloma (Scientific Reports, 2016). 3. To solve the crystal structure of the remaining three domains D4-D6 and complex structures of D4-D6 with various metal ions. We have expressed and purified the the whole extracellular region of PECAM-1 (D1-D6) protein. Due to the flexible nature of the protein, no crystals have been obtained so far. We have, however, solved the low resolution molecular envelop from Small Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS) data. The SAXS envelop demonstrated that two PECAM-1 D1-6 molecules could form a trans-homophilic dimmer in solution, which further validated the interaction of D1-2 determined in our crystal structure (Scientific Reports, under review).
