766412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
766412.value: In this project, we have demonstrated the trans-homo-interaction mechanism of PECAM-1 D1-2. However, to fully understand the homophilic interaction of PECAM-1 and its function in cell junctions, the structure of full length or whole extracellular region of PECAM-1 needs to be determined. The structure will provide insights into understanding the multiple functions of PECAM-1 in endothelium integrity, immune response, and diapedesis.

766412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766412.value: Cell adhesion involved in signal transduction, tissue integrity and pathogen infection is mainly mediated by cell adhesion molecules (CAM). One CAM member, Platelet–endothelial-cell adhesion molecule-1 (PECAM-1), plays an important role in tight junction among endothelia cells, leukocyte trafficking, and immune response through its homophilic and heterophilic binding patterns. Both kinds of interactions, which lead to endogenous and exogenous signal transmission, are derived from extracellular immunoglobulin-like (IgL) domains and cytoplasmic immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibitory motifs (ITIMs) of PECAM-1. To date, the mechanism of trans-homophilic interaction of PECAM-1 remains unclear. Here, we present the crystal structure of PECAM-1 IgL1-2 trans-homo dimer. The dimer interface includes hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions. The Small-Angle X-ray Scattering (SAXS) envelope of PECAM-1 IgL1-6 supported such a dimer formation in solution. Cell adhesion assays on wildtype and mutant PECAM-1 further characterized the structural determinants in cell junction and communication. Our results provide insights into understanding the multiple functions of PECAM-1 in endothelium integrity, immune response, and diapedesis.

766812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766812.value: 肥胖目前在全球呈流行趨勢，已經成為全球性的重大公共健康問題。肥胖是一系列慢性代謝性疾病包括2型糖尿病、脂肪肝及心血管疾病的主要危險因素，這些疾病是老年人群的主要致死性疾病。慢性炎症導致脂肪因子和促炎因子的異常分泌是聯繫肥胖及其相關的心血管代謝疾病的主要因素。因此，闡明巨噬細胞在肥胖狀態下的炎症反應的調節至關重要。 脂肪細胞型脂肪酸結合蛋白（A-FABP）是肥胖相關的病理狀態的主要調節因子。在人類，血清A-FABP水平是2型糖尿病、脂肪肝及頸動脈粥樣硬化的獨立風險因素。我們最近發現A-FABP通過在c-Jun氨基端激酶（JNK）和轉錄因子激活蛋白-1（AP-1）之間形成正反饋環而在巨噬細胞炎症反應中發揮重要作用。內質網應激通過激活JNK和核因子κB（NF-κB）等主要炎症信號通路而觸發肥胖狀態下的脂肪組織炎症。然而，內質網應激在免疫細胞是如何與慢性炎性代謝性疾病相聯繫的尚未知曉。 A-FABP與內質網應激均與肥胖密切相關並參與了相似的炎性信號通路，因此本研究的目的是探討A-FABP與內質網應激在毒性脂質誘導的巨噬細胞炎症反應中的相互作用及其機制。此外，自噬可通過自我降解的過程以減輕內質網應激，因此我們還將研究自噬在炎性疾病中的病理生理作用。本項研究不僅有助於增強我們對肥胖相關炎性疾病的病理通路的理解，還將為治療肥胖相關疾病的新藥開發提供理論基礎。

Therefore, we did not perform the site-directed mutagenesis, transient transfection and also ChIP assay to follow up. In addition to the proposed experiments in the project, we have also extended our study to investigate the roles of A-FABP and autophagy in the regulation of foam cell formation so as to evaluate the clinical relevance of our findings. This part was assigned as the project for our student of master of medical science (Mr. Wong Tak-sui) and he was trained with several laboratory techniques such as Western blot analysis, immunofluorescene staining, quantitative PCR and cell culture. 766812.label: Major findings and research outcome
766812.value: 1. ER stress mediated toxic-lipids (palmitic acid)-induced A-FABP expression is regulated through increasing transcriptional activity. 2. The unfolded protein response IRE-1 and PERK signaling pathways are involved in ER stress mediated toxic-lipids-induced A-FABP expression. 3. Suppression of XBP-1 and TNF-alpha attenuated toxic-lipids-induced A-FABP expression suggesting that ER stress mediated toxic-lipids induced expression of A-FABP through the IRE-1/ PERK-XBP-1/ TNF-a/ JNK/ A-FABP pathway. 4. A-FABP deficiency protects against toxic lipids-induced ER stress and inflammation in macrophages. 5. Prolonged treatment of palmitic acid (PA) induces ER stress and the expression of A-FABP but impairs autophagic flux in macrophages. 6. Elevated A-FABP modulates PA-induced ER stress and inflammation via suppression of autophagy in macrophages. 7. The mRNA and protein expression of autophagy related protein 7 (Atg-7) were induced in A-FABP deficient macrophages when compared to that in wildtype macrophages. Knocking down of A-FABP increased the expression of Atg7 in macrophages. Conversely, adenovirus-mediated over-expression of A-FABP diminished both basal and PA-induced Atg7 expression suggesting that the presence of A-FABP attenuates the expression of Atg7 contributing to defective autophagy. 8. Ligand bound A-FABP interacts with janus kinase 2 (JAK2) to suppress its activity while JAK2 regulates autophagy in hepatoma and glioblastoma cells. Treatment of PA induced the activation of JAK2 while PA-induced autophagy was greatly impaired in the presence of JAK2 specific inhibitor AG490 which was accompanied by significantly enhanced ER stress. Similar result was also observed by the use of silencing RNA specific for JAK2 suggesting that JAK2 is indispensable for PA-induced autophagy in macrophages and its suppression further promotes ER stress. 9. The PA-induced activation of JAK2 in A-FABP deficient macrophage is more pronounced than that of wildtype macrophages. Similar result was also observed when RAW264.7 macrophages pretreated with A-FABP inhibitor BMS309403 followed by PA stimulation. On the contrary, adenovirus-mediated over-expression of A-FABP abolished PA-induced activation of JAK2 in A-FABP deficient macrophages. This result confirms the effect of A-FABP on attenuating JAK2 signaling. PA-induced Atg7 expression was reduced in the presence of JAK2 inhibitor AG490. The basal and PA-induced Atg7 were also dramatically decreased in RAW macrophages when JAK2 was knocked down. These data indicated that A-FABP suppresses JAK2 activation which in turn reduces the expression of Atg7 leading to defective autophagy. We here demonstrated a nonconventional role of A-FABP in the regulation of autophagy which potentiates toxic lipids-induced inflammation in macrophages by instigating ER stress through inhibition of JAK2 dependent autophagy.

766812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
766812.value: A-FABP is a negative regulator to PPARgamma activity leading to the inhibition of the PPARgamma-LXRalpha-ABCA1 cholesterol efflux pathway and contributes to foam cell formation. Autophagy is also essential for cholesterol efflux from macrophage foam cell. We speculate that A-FABP may inhibit cholesterol efflux from macrophages by inhibiting autophagy which contributes to foam cell formation. To evaluate the physiological relevance of our findings, Mr. Wong Tak Sui Derek, the Master of Medical Science student investigated the roles of A-FABP and autophagy in macrophage foam cell formation. We showed that acetylated-low density lipoprotein (AcLDL) treatment induced lipid droplet accumulation in both WT and A-FABP deficient macrophages. The lipid droplets were co-localized with LAMP-1, suggesting that the autophagosomal-lysosomal autophagy participates in the lipid droplet metabolism. We showed that AcLDL-stimulated lipid droplet formation was reduced while the colocalization of lipid droplet and LAMP-1 was enhanced in A-FABP deficient macrophages compared to the WT macrophages. We confirmed the results by using adenovirus-mediated over-expression of A-FABP in A-FABP KO macrophages. Over-expression of A-FABP enhanced AcLDL-induced lipid droplet accumulation in the macrophages and reduced AcLDL released into the medium and was accompanied by impaired autophagy suggesting that A-FABP promotes AcLDL-induced foam cell formation via inhibition of autophagy.

766812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766812.value: Increased ectopic accumulation of lipid in non-adipose tissue is implicated in the pathogenesis of obesity-related inflammatory complications such as atherosclerosis and steatohepatitis by promoting macrophage infiltration and activation. In this study, we identified that endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and the fat tissue derived hormone adipocyte fatty acid binding protein (A-FABP) which are the key players of chronic inflammation could interplay to regulate lipid-induced inflammatory responses. Our findings show that A-FABP acts as autophagy inhibitor to instigate toxic lipids-induced ER stress through inhibition of JAK2-dependent autophagy (a self-degradation process of unfold protein), which in turn triggers inflammatory responses in macrophages. Thus, the A-FABP-JAK2 axis may represent an important pathological pathway contributing to obesity-related inflammatory diseases. We also further evaluate the clinical relevance of our study by investigating the roles of A-FABP and autophagy in foam cell formation. Our findings may allow the development of new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of obesity-related inflammatory diseases by targeting this signaling pathway.

767012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
767012.value: Kinesin-1 is a molecular motor protein that transports cargo along the microtubule by utilizing chemical energy from ATP hydrolysis. The kinesin-1 motor carries various cargos essential for neuronal development and functioning. However, it is still not fully understood how the reduction or dysfunction of kinesin-1 would be involved in neurological disorders despite kinesin-1’s functional significance in normal neurons. N-methyl-d-aspartate receptors (NMDAR) are well-known for their roles in synaptic plasticity and excitotoxicity. The subcellular localization of NMDAR determines its function; synaptic NMDAR activation regulates synaptic plasticity, whereas extrasynaptic NMDAR activation leads to excitotoxicity. In our preliminary study, we found that kinesin-1 interacts with NMDAR through the tail domain of its heavy chain, Kif5b. In Kif5b+/- mice, the NMDAR level is reduced in the extrasynaptic surface but not in the synaptic surface compared with their wild-type littermates. Because NMDAR interacts with neuronal nitric oxide synthase and mediates nitric oxide production upon stimulation, we investigated and found that nitric oxide production is severely disrupted in the hippocampus CA1 region of Kif5b+/- mice. These data reveal NMDAR is a novel cargo of kinesin-1, and strongly suggests that kinesin-1 might be involved in NMDAR mediated excitotoxicity. However, the exact mechanism of how kinesin-1 delivers NMDAR towards extrasynaptic regions and whether kinesin-1 plays a role in the cerebral ischemic insult remains unclear. Building on our extensive experience in working with genetics and functions of kinesin-1 dependent trafficking, we propose to investigate the role of kinesin-1 in NMDAR trafficking and the biological significance of this kinesin-1/NMDAR interaction. We are particularly interested in: (i) identifying the subunit and domain of NMDAR responsible for binding with kinesin-1 to elucidate the molecular nature of this interaction; (ii) characterizing the role of kinesin-1 in transporting NMDAR toward the extrasynaptic surface; (iii) carefully analyzing the phenotypes of Kif5b+/- mice regarding calcium influx, nitric oxide production and excitotoxicity; and (iv) investigating whether the levels of kinesin-1 are regulated by NMDAR activity and the effect of Kif5b overexpression on NMDAR-mediated toxicity. By completion of this project, we will provide an answer as to how kinesin-1 mediates NMDAR trafficking in neurons. We will also reveal whether Kinesin-1 is a player in mediating damage in cerebral ischemia. This study will not only extend our knowledge in the field of intracellular transportation but may also provide us with a promising target to formulate a novel therapy for stroke treatment. 一型運動蛋白是一種分子馬達蛋白，它利用ATP水解的化學能沿著微管運輸貨物。一型運動蛋白像馬達一樣運送著各種神經元發育和功能必不可少的貨物。儘管一型運動蛋白在神經元正常功能中很重要，然而我們對它在神經系統疾病或功能障礙中所起作用的了解仍然不很充分。 N-甲基-D-天門冬氨酸受體（NMDAR）在突觸可塑性和興奮性毒性中的角色是是眾所周知的。 NMDA受體的亞細胞定位決定了其功能; 突觸NMDA受體的激活調節突觸可塑性，而突觸外NMDA受體的激活導致興奮性毒性。在我們的前期研究中，我們發現驅一型運動蛋白重鏈KIF5B的尾部與NMDA受體相互作用。與野生型小鼠相比，在KIF5B / - 小鼠中，突觸外細胞膜表面NMDA受體的蛋白水平降低了，突觸內膜表面NMDA受體的蛋白水平沒有變化。由於NMDA受體與神經元型一氧化氮合酶相互作用並介導刺激後一氧化氮的生產，我們的研究發現，KIF5B / - 小鼠海馬CA1區一氧化氮的生產有嚴重缺陷。這些數據揭示NMDA受體是一型運動蛋白的貨物，並表明，一型運動蛋白可能參與NMDA受體介導的興奮性毒性。然而，一型運動蛋白運送NMDA受體到突觸外地區的確切機制，以及一型運動蛋白是否在腦缺血損傷中起作用尚不清楚。 我們對一型運動蛋白的遺傳和功能的研究有著豐富的經驗。在此基礎上，我們提議研究一型運動蛋白在NMDA受體運輸中的作用以及kinesin-1/NMDAR互動的生物學意義。我們特別感興趣的是：（一）了解與一型運動蛋白結合的NMDA受體亞單位和結構域，闡明這種相互作用的分子性質；（二）表徵一型運動蛋白在運輸NMDAR到突觸外表面中的作用;（三）仔細分析了解KIF5B / - 小鼠在鈣離子內流，一氧化氮生產和興奮性毒性等方面的表型;（四）調查一型運動蛋白水平是否受NMDA受體的活性的調控，以及和KIF5B過度表達對NMDA受體的介導的毒性的影響。 該項目完成後，我們將闡明一型運動蛋白是如何介導的神經元NMDA受體轉運的。我們也將揭示一型運動蛋白是否介導腦缺血損傷。這項研究不僅將在細胞內運輸領域擴大我們的知識，也有可能為中風的治療提供了一個新希望。

767012.label: Realisation of objectives
767012.value: We first tried to identify which subunits of NMDAR were responsible for binding with Kif5b. By immunoprecipitating the Kif5b from 293T cell lysates, in which the NMDAR subunit tail and Kif5b tail were co-expressed, we found both NR1 and NR2B tails, but not NR2A tail, in the precipitant. By co-immunoprecipitation assay, we found that Kif5b tail is sufficient to bind with NR1 or NR2B cytoplasmic tail. Moreover, deletion of microtubule sliding domain (892 to 914 a.a.), but not the autoinhibitory domain (919 to 926 a.a.), was able to abolish the binding between NMDAR tails and Kif5b. We then continued to narrow down the binding region within NR1 and NR2B tail. By GST pull down assay, we found that only the C2 cassette of NR1 was able to bind with Kif5b tail. Moreover, we identified that the distal end of NR1 C2 cassettes (927 to 938 a.a.) was necessary for this interaction. Similarly, for NR2B, we identify that the intermediate tail (1161 to 1180 a.a.) was necessary for this interaction. By expressing NR1 and NR2B tails in a cell-free system and incubating the proteins with GST-bound Kif5b tail fragments, we found that the interactions between NR1/NR2B and Kif5b were direct. To investigate the role of kinesin-1-NMDAR complex in vivo, we overexpressed dominant-negative Kif5b fragments into COS7 cells together with GFP-NR2B and NR1-1a and examined the subcellular distribution of GFP-NR2B. We found that all of these dominant-negative Kif5b fragments could prevent GFP-NR2B from colocalization with Golgi apparatus and targeting to the cell surface, suggesting that Kif5b may involve in the outward trafficking of NMDAR. We transfected the primary neurons from both wild-type and Kif5b+/- mice with GFP-NR2B and did the surface labeling. We found that the total NMDAR were reduced in Kif5b+/- neurons. We then co-stained the transfected neurons with PSD-95, a postsynaptic marker, to distinguish synaptic NMDAR and extrasynaptic NMDAR. We found that the exptrasynaptic NMDAR but not synaptic NMDAR was reduced in the Kif5b+/- neurons. These data suggested that Kif5b may involve in the extrasynaptic targeting of NMDAR. To investigate the effect of Kif5b on NMDA mediated calcium influx, we assessed the activity of NMDARs by Fluo-3 to image calcium influx on primary culture neurons. Calcium influx induced by NMDA was significantly reduced in Kif5b+/- neurons. We depolarized neurons by KCl (50 mM) or used Bicuculine to inhibit the inhibitory GABA receptors, then found similar levels of calcium influx in both genotypes, suggesting that the synaptic NMDAR was not altered. We used Bicuculine then MK801 and then NMDA to specifically activated extrasyanptic NMDAR, we found a reduced extrasynaptic NMDAR mediated calcium influx in Kif5b+/- neurons. We also studied the amount of NO emission from acutely prepared hippocampus slices from wild-type and Kif5b+/- mice by an NO-sensitive electrode. Activation of NMDARs by NMDA (50 μM) or glutamate (4 μM) plus glycine (20 μM) increased NO emission in both genotypes, while the amount emitted by Kif5b+/- slices was significantly less, suggesting the hypo-function of NMDAR in Kif5b+/- neurons. After we treated the wild-type and Kif5b+/- neurons with NMDA (50 μM) plus glycine (20 μM) to induce excitotoxicity, we found Kif5b+/- neurons had much better resistance to the excitotoxicity. Also, we found Kif5b+/- mice had better resistance to ischemia-induced neurodegeneration than wild-type mice.

767012.label: Major findings and research outcome
767012.value: We showed that a decreased level of kinesin-1, a microtubule-dependent molecular motor, confers neuroprotection by reducing extrasynaptic N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) targeting and functioning. We found that kif5b, the heavy chain of kinesin-1, could directly interact with NMDAR and regulated its trafficking. Specifically, we found that the Kif5b tail could bind with the cytoplasmic tails of NMDAR subunits (NR1 and NR2B). We also found the C2 cassette within NR1 and the intermediate tail within NR2B were necessary for NR1/NR2B’s bindings with Kif5b. A loss of 50% of Kif5b protected the neurons against excitotoxic insult and ischemia-provoked neurodegeneration through the hypofunction of NMDARs. Decreased kinesin-1 reduces the formation of the Kif5b-NMDAR complex in vivo, prevents NMDAR concentrating at extrasynaptic sites and inhibits calcium influx and NO emission mediated by extrasynaptic NMDAR activation to confer neuroprotection. Our findings reveal that kinesin-1 reduction benefits and protects the neurons against neurodegeneration by reducing the cellular response to NMDAR mediated excitotoxic insult, which is likely to be an intrinsic event in the early stage of neurodegeneration.

767012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
767012.value: First, these finding could lead to the development of therapeutic strategies that fine-tune the intracellular transport machinery to postpone or halt neurodegeneration. For example, based on the sequences of the binding domains within Kif5b or NMDAR, we can design some small competitive peptides to attenuate the interaction between Kif5b and NMDAR to confer neuroprotection. Second, the detailed binding information between Kif5b and NMDAR could shed a light on the structural study to illustrate how kinesin realize specific bindings with various cargoes. For example, we can express the binding fragments within Kif5b/NMDAR and use NMR to study their structural changes.

767012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
767012.value: Neurodegenerative disorders have been placing mounting pressure on both personal life and the public health system. Despite the difference in the pathology, the progressive loss of synapse, a region that connects neurons, and the death of the neurons in distinct brain regions are the main causes of the functional deficits. Intriguingly, the brain, to some extent, would develop tolerance towards the detrimental insult. However, our understanding on how the brain develops and regulates the intrinsic tolerance is still elusive, thereby limiting the efficacy of the intervention towards the degeneration. Our project builds on the hypothesis that the intracellular transportation is one of the hubs controlling and responding to the change in the environments. We thereby identify a previous unknown protein transport complex consisting of kinesin-1 and NR2B-containing NMDA receptor. The reduction of this complex specifically decreases the pro-death signaling and protects brain against ischemic insult. We also provide the details of this interaction, which is useful and informative to design potential intervention. Therefore, this finding not only deepens our understanding in how the brain reacts to the insult, but also suggests that manipulation of the transportation system might be a promising target to slow the progression of synaptic and neuronal loss.

767412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
767412.value: 全世界超過兩千萬人受到人T細胞白血病病毒I型(HTLV-I)的感染，其中約3%的人會發展爲凶險而且致死率極高的成人T細胞白血病(ATL)，而另外1%則罹患各種形式的神經病變。盡管發病過程很長而發病原因很多，但發病與HTLV-I的原病毒載量呈現正相關。HTLV-I原病毒的表達在轉錄水平上由多功能的反式激活蛋白Tax所介導，Tax可通過細胞轉錄因子CREB及輔激活蛋白CBP與CRTC(又稱爲TORC)等而強力刺激病毒長末端重複(LTR)的轉錄。我們過去已研究Tax、CREB和CRTC在此過程中的調控作用，特別是闡明了CRTC在Tax誘導的LTR激活中的必需功能。CRTC的活性主要通過磷酸化進行調控，揭示調控CRTC活性的蛋白激酶不僅是HTLV-I生物學研究的重要課題，也可進一步發展有關激酶的小分子刺激劑和抑制劑，爲防治ATL提供新的策略。 LKB1腫瘤抑制基因是Peutz-Jeghers癌症多發綜合症的突變基因。LKB1是一種蛋白激酶，可修飾並激活AMPK及SIK等AMPK樣激酶，而後者可使肝臟中的CRTC磷酸化並激活。然而，LKB1及AMPK激酶在HTLV-I生物學中的作用尚不清楚。HTLV-I在LKB1缺失細胞中活躍轉錄的現象促使我們對LKB1在Tax誘導的LTR活化中的作用進行更爲深入的探討。我們已取得的初步實驗結果表明LKB1可與Tax相互作用並通過其激酶活性抑制Tax的功能。LKB1在HTLV-I感染細胞的表達可抑制病毒轉錄，而敲減LKB1則可增強HTLV-I轉錄物的表達。採用藥物激活LKB1同樣可以在HTLV-I轉化的T細胞中抑制HTLV-I蛋白的表達。 在本項研究中，我們將全面深入研究LKB1在HTLV-I轉錄及致腫瘤發病過程中的作用。首先，我們將在HTLV-I轉化的T淋巴細胞及HTLV-I分子克隆所感染細胞中採用過表達和敲減等方法研究LKB1對HTLV-I轉錄的抑制作用。其次，我們將闡明LKB1抑制HTLV-I轉錄的分子機理，逐一探討LKB1與Tax的相互作用、LKB1在LTR的募集以及AMPK、SIK1/2、CREB和CRTC的作用。再次，我們將揭示LKB1對HTLV-1致瘤性轉化的影響，確定LKB1及SIK1/2在HTLV-I感染細胞中表達和活性並釐清LKB1對HTLV-I轉化細胞增殖和侵襲能力的影響。最後，我們將對一組LKB1和SIK1/2的小分子刺激劑進行篩選，確定其在感染細胞及聯合免疫缺陷小鼠中的抗HTLV-I及抗腫瘤活性。

767412.label: Realisation of objectives
767412.value: All four specific aims stated in our original proposal have been achieved fully and successfully. All proposed experiments have been done and many additional studies have also been conducted. Several high-quality research articles on this topic of cellular regulation of HTLV-1 gene expression have been published in Retrovirology and Journal of Virology. 1) We fully characterized the negative regulatory function of not only LKB1 tumor suppressor but also its downstream salt-inducible kinases (SIKs) in the activation of HTLV-1 long terminal repeats (LTR) by the oncoprotein Tax. Activation of LKB1 and SIKs effectively blunted Tax activity in a phosphorylation-dependent manner, whereas compromising these kinases, but not AMP-dependent protein kinases (AMPKs), augmented Tax function. 2) We found that activated LKB1 and SIKs associated with Tax and suppressed Tax-induced LTR activation by counteracting the function of CRTCs and CREB. Enforced expression of LKB1 or SIK1 in cells transfected with HTLV-1 molecular clone pX1MT repressed proviral transcription. On the contrary, depletion of LKB1 in pX1MT-transfected cells and in HTLV-1-transformed T cells boosted the expression of Tax. We demonstrated that SIKs but not AMPKs are the downstream kinases of LKB1 kinase in the regulation of HTLV-1 transcription. 3) On one hand, we characterized the expression and activity profiles of LKB1 and SIKs in HTLV-1-transformed ATL cells C8166, MT2 and MT4. On the other hand, we found that activation of LKB1 inhibits proliferation of these HTLV-1-transformed T cells. The analysis has also been extended to Jurkat T cells acutely infected with HTLV-1. Our findings lent support to the notion that LKB1 and SIKs are cellular kinases critically involved in cellular response to HTLV-1 infection and cellular regulation of Tax-activated HTLV-1 transcription. 4) We carried out several rounds of screening for anti-HTLV-1 and antiproliferative activity of small-molecule activators of LKB1 and SIKs. Particularly, we found that treatment of HTLV-1-transformed C8166, MT2 and MT4 cells with metformin led to LKB1/SIK activation, reduction in Tax expression, and inhibition of cell proliferation. Our findings laid a solid foundation for further analysis of the anti-HTLV-1 and anti-ATL activity of metformin and other LKB1/SIK activators.

Activated LKB1 and SIKs associated with Tax and suppressed Tax-induced LTR activation by counteracting CRTCs and CREB. Enforced expression of LKB1 or SIK1 in cells transfected with HTLV-1 molecular clone pX1MT repressed proviral transcription. On the contrary, depletion of LKB1 in pX1MT-transfected cells and in HTLV-1-transformed T cells boosted the expression of Tax. Treatment of HTLV-1 transformed cells with metformin led to LKB1/SIK1 activation, reduction in Tax expression, and inhibition of cell proliferation. Our findings revealed a new function of LKB1 and SIKs as negative regulators of HTLV-1 transcription. Pharmaceutical activation of LKB1 and SIKs might be considered as a new strategy in anti-HTLV-1 and anti-ATL therapy (Tang et al., Retrovirology, 2013). 2) We characterized the regulatory role of group I p21-activated kinases (Paks) in Tax-induced LTR activation. Both wild-type and kinase-dead mutants of Pak3 were capable of potentiating the activity of Tax to activate LTR transcription. The effect of Paks on the LTR was attributed to the N-terminal regulatory domain and required the action of CREB, CREB-regulating transcriptional coactivators (CRTCs) and p300/CREB-binding protein. Paks physically associated with Tax and CRTCs. Paks were recruited to the LTR in the presence of Tax. siRNAs against either Pak1 or Pak3 prevented the interaction of Tax with CRTC1 and the recruitment of Tax to the LTR. These siRNAs also inhibited LTR-dependent transcription in HTLV-1-transformed MT4 cells and in cells transfected with an infectious clone of HTLV-1. Taken together, group I Paks augment Tax-mediated transcriptional activation of HTLV-1 LTR in a kinase-independent manner (Chan et al., Retrovirology, 2013). In addition, we also extended our analysis of the regulatory role of CRTCs to other oncogenic viruses including hepatitis B virus. We found the overexpression of CRTC1 in hepatitis B virus-infected hepatocytes and tissues. We then went on to define an essential positive regulatory role of CRTC1 in hepatitis B virus transcription (Tang et al., Nucl. Acids Res., 2014). On the other hand, our continuing work to analyze how CRTCs and CREB are regulated in the context of HTLV-1 transcription led to another new finding on the suppression of Tax activation of HTLV-1 LTR by SIRT1 deacetylase (Tang et al., J. Virol., 2015). 3) We demonstrated the suppression of type I IFN production by HTLV-1 Tax through interaction with and inhibition of TBK1 kinase that phosphorylates IRF3. Induced transcription of IFN-β was severely impaired in HTLV-1-transformed ATL cells and freshly infected T lymphocytes. The ability to suppress IRF3 activation was ascribed to Tax. Expression of Tax alone sufficiently repressed the induction of IFN production by RIG-I plus PACT, cGAMP synthase plus STING, TBK1, IKKi, IRF3 and IRF7, but not by IRF3-5D, a dominant active phosphomimetic mutant. This suggests that Tax perturbs IFN production at the step of IRF3 phosphorylation. Tax mutants deficient for CREB or NF-kB activation were fully competent in the suppression of IFN production. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments confirmed the association of Tax with TBK1, IKKi, STING and IRF3. In vitro kinase assay indicated an inhibitory effect of Tax on TBK1-mediated phosphorylation of IRF3. Taken together, our findings suggested a new mechanism by which HTLV-1 oncoprotein Tax circumvents the production of type I IFNs in infected cells. Our findings have implications in therapeutic intervention of ATL (Yuen et al., J. Virol., 2016).

767412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
767412.value: We published three research articles in Retrovirology and Journal of Virology on cellular regulation of HTLV-1 gene expression. Another related paper concerning Tax function in HTLV-1 infection and retroviral induction of innate interferon production was also published in Journal of Virology. This demonstrates again to the world that we continue to be highly active and productive in HTLV-1 research. Our future studies will focus more on two important areas: anti-HTLV-1 drug discovery and viral evasion of DNA sensing. We currently have zero public funding to support our continuing work in this field and have to rely upon private donation which is unstable and unsustainable in Hong Kong. I have to work harder to obtain new funding from RGC or another source so that our research on HTLV-1 will not be interrupted in the next few years.

767412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
767412.value: The development of many types of cancer is caused by chronic infection of virus. Human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1) was the first human retrovirus discovered and it is the cause of adult T-cell leukemia (ATL), a highly aggressive and fatal blood cancer. Treatment options for ATL are limited and current treatments are unsatisfactory. Unraveling new mechanisms that control HTLV-1 gene expression will provide new strategies for treatment. Particularly, drugs targeting protein kinases hold great promises for precision treatment of cancer. Therefore, identification and characterization of cellular protein kinases that control HTLV-1 gene expression might lead to the discovery of new therapeutic agents for precision treatment of ATL. In this study we have found that a group of cellular protein kinases named LKB1 and SIK1-3 partner with a viral oncogenic protein named Tax to control the expression of HTLV-1 genes. Since small-molecule activators of LKB1 and SIK1-3 protein kinases are available and have been used successfully to treat other diseases such as diabetes. Repurposing these agents for the treatment of HTLV-1 infection and ATL represents a new strategy in rational design and development of anti-HTLV-1 and anti-ATL agents for prevention and control of ATL and other HTLV-1-associated human diseases.

767512.label: Realisation of objectives
767512.value: Periodontal disease as a common oral disease is induced by microbial plaque biofilms, and if uncontrolled the resultant dysregulated immuno-inflammatory response results in substantial destruction of tooth-supporting tissue and bone in susceptible individuals, and eventually leads to multiple tooth loss. Innate immunity is the front line of host defense against various forms of infectious and inflammatory diseases including periodontal disease. Our previous RGC-funded studies demonstrate that human gingival epithelia serve as a crucial and active biological barrier against microbial invasion (Jin 2011). This research work encourages us to explore novel approaches to tackling microbial biofilms, enhancing innate immunity and modulating dysregulated immuno-inflammatory response for preventing and controlling periodontal disease. Currently, one of the hot research fields in nanomaterials and nanomedicine is to develop nanotechnology-based novel drug delivery systems for health care. Our preliminary experiments on mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs)-encapsulated Chinese herbal extracts suggest that appropriate adjustment of the research methodology and focus should be made within the framework of the project. This enables us to refine the experimental protocols for subsequent studies and maximize the effectiveness of the nano-encapsulated herbal extracts. A series of experiments and tests have been undertaken in the study, and the following novel findings have been made in connection to the setting objectives: 1) Establishment of a new nano-encapsulation methodology using commercial MSNs. We provide the first evidence that MSNs-encapsulated Scutellaria baicalensis extract and MSNs encapsulated-chlorhexidine (CHX) (Nano-CHX) at 9:1 (w/w) (Nano-MIX) significantly enhance synergistic antibacterial effects on common oral bacterial biofilms, which may be further developed as novel antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory agents for clinical oral care. 2) Refinement of MSNs-encapsulation methodology via new synthesis of two shapes of MSNs in our labs, and evaluation of the anti-biofilm and anti-inflammatory efficiencies of the MSNs-encapsulated herbal extracts. Interestingly, the spherical MSNs (S-MSNs) exhibit higher loading efficiency and releasing rate of Scutellaria baicalensis (SB) extract (Bacalin as its biomarker) with reference to the MSNs wire (W-MSNs). As such, the newly synthesized S-MSNs are selected for the subsequent experiments and assays in our project. The loading efficiency and/or releasing rate of S-MSNs-encapsulated Zanthoxylum niticdum extract, epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG, a biomarker of green tea extract), Lonicera japonicae extract and chlorogenic acid (the biomarker of Lonicera japonicae extract) have been evaluated, respectively. 3) Cellular interactions and formation of the epithelial “nanocoating-like barrier” with MSNs in human gingiva. The novel finding on the penetration and accumulation of S-MSNs at the superficial layers of gingival epithelia shed new light on further development of S-MSNs-encapsulated herbal extracts (e.g. SB/Bacalin) as new antimicrobials and immunomodulators/ enhancers of innate host defense. 4) Enhancement of host modulatory/anti-inflammatory effects of S-MSNs-encapsulated Bacalein and SB extract in human gingival epithelial cells (hGECs). These nano-drugs can be markedly uptaken by the hGECs, and Nano-Bacalein and Nano-SB significantly down-regulate the gene expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g. IL-6 & IL-8) in hGECs. The relevant intracellular signaling pathways are being investigated. #The reasons for under-achievements and outline attempts to overcome problems: According to our pilot studies on mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs)-encapsulated Chinese herbal extracts and current research trend in nanomedicine/Nanomaterials, the research focus and approaches have been adjusted as appropriate within the framework of the project. Subsequently, the experimental protocols have therefore been refined, and the related research work has been undertaken. The findings in this final report reflect our main work and outputs of this project. In the present study, we find that nano-baicalein significantly down-regulates the gene expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines in hGECs, while the study on the relevant intracellular signaling pathways is under investigation, and the results would be presented internationally and submitted for publication. Notably, our novel findings on the formation of epithelial “Nanocoating-like barrier” with MSNs in human gingiva (Li et al, 2016, Nanomaterials) strongly inspire us to further the current study on developing nano-based, dual-drugs delivery system for controlling common infection and inflammation like periodontal disease. Meanwhile, further research funds will be sought for translational studies, and patent applications could be made for potential development of novel anti-infection/inflammation agents in clinical oral health care.

767512.label: Major findings and research outcome
767512.value: 1) Establishment of a new nano-encapsulation methodology using commercially available mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs)  The loading/releasing profiles of MSNs encapsulated-chlorhexidine (Nano-CHX) were tested. Nano-CHX exhibits potent antibacterial effects on common oral biofilms [Paper 1]  The loading/releasing profiles of MSNs-encapsulated Scutellaria baicalensis extract (Bacalin as its biomarker) were analyzed, and they were then mixed with Nano-CHX at 9:1 (w/w) (Nano-MIX) for further experiments. We provide the first evidence that Nano-MIX enhances synergistic effects against oral bacterial biofilms. The novel nano-encapsulated drugs may be developed for oral care [Paper 2]. 2) Refinement of nano-encapsulation methodology via new synthesis of two shapes of MSNs and evaluation of the anti-biofilm/anti-inflammatory efficiencies of MSNs-encapsulated herbal extracts.  The spherical MSNs (S-MSNs) and MSN wires (W-MSNs) were synthesized and their surfaces were labelled by fluorescent groups. They were characterized and the anti-biofilm effects were assessed. The S-MSNs-encapsulated CHX enhances its anti-biofilm efficiency via effective releasing and close interactions with microbes [Paper 3].  The S-MSNs exhibit higher loading efficiency/releasing rate of Scutellaria baicalensis (SB) extract than W-MSNs. The newly synthesized S-MSNs are therefore selected for the subsequent experiments.  The loading efficiency and/or releasing rate of S-MSNs-encapsulated Zanthoxylum niticdum extract, epigallocatechin gallate (a biomarker of green tea extract) and Lonicera japonicae extract/its biomarker-chlorogenic acid have been evaluated, respectively. 3) Cellular interactions/formation of the epithelial “Nanocoating-like barrier” with S-MSNs in human gingiva.  The endocytosis/exocytosis of fluorescent S-MSNs in human gingival epithelial cells (hGECs) were analyzed, and their penetration efficiency was evaluated in the reconstructed human gingival epithelia (RHGE) and porcine ear skin models, respectively. This pioneering study indicates the notable penetration/accumulation of S-MSNs at the superficial layers of RHGE. These findings shed new light on development of S-MSNs-encapsulated Chinese herbal extracts (e.g. SB/Bacalin, Zanthoxylum niticdum and green tea extract) as new antimicrobials and immunomodulators/enhancers of innate host defense in human gingiva [Paper 4]. 4) S-MSNs-encapsulated Bacalein and SB extract enhance the anti-inflammatory effects in primary human gingival epithelial cells (hGECs).  Baicalin, baicalein and SB extract could be effectively encapsulated in the amine-modified MSNs (Nano-BA, Nano-BE & Nano-SB) with prolonged release beyond 48 h. These nano-drugs were markedly uptaken by the hGECs. Notably, Nano-BE significantly down-regulates the gene expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g. IL-6 & IL-8) in hGECs. The relevant intracellular signaling pathways are being investigated and reported (Li et al. under preparation).

767512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
767512.value: According to our novel findings on formation of epithelial “Nanocoating-like barrier” with MSNs in human gingiva, further study is highly warranted on the development of dual-drugs delivery system by MSNs for maximizing the control of pathogenic microbial biofilms and inflammation simultaneously. As Nano-CHX and Nano-Baicalein demonstrate notable ant-biofilm and anti-inflammation effects respectively, novel hybrid MSNs containing both CHX and baicalein could be developed for effectively controlling the growth of microbial biofilms and resultant destructive inflammation in human gingiva. The hybrid MSNs could potentially ‘arm’ the gingival epithelia via forming a ‘Nanocoating-like layer’ for constant control of microbial biofilms and inflammation on a long-term basis. In a recent RGC-funded project, we will further investigate the effects of spherical MSNs-encapsulated chlorhexidine and herbal extracts on the persisters of P. gingivalis (the major pathogen of periodontal disease), and the interactions of P. gingivalis persisters with human oral/gingival epithelial cells. Further competitive research funds and promising supports for translational studies will be sought to conduct both in vitro and in vivo studies. Meanwhile, patent applications can be made for technical innovation and development of new nano-drug products for oral health care.

767512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
767512.value: Oral health is highly integrated into everyone’s general wellbeing and quality of life. Periodontal (gum) disease as the main cause of multiple tooth loss in adults not only badly affects oral health, but also links closely to systemic diseases like diabetes. This pioneering study has focused on one of the hot research fields in nanomaterials and nanomedicine, i.e. nanotechnology-based novel drug delivery systems. It has intensively explored novel nano-based biological approaches to tackling microbial biofilms and favorably regulating unwanted immuno-inflammatory response for preventing and controlling gum disease. Notably, the newly produced nanoparticles (S-MSNs)-encapsulated Chinese herbal extracts (e.g. Scutellaria baicalensis and chlorhexidine - a common antimicrobial agent) at 9:1 (w/w) (Nano-MIX) greatly enhance synergistic effects against oral bacteria. These new nano-drugs (e.g. Baicalin, baicalein and Scutellaria baicalensis extract) well contribute to reduction of inflammatory response. This study also discovers the formation of “Nanocoating-like barrier” with S-MSNs in human gingiva with great potentials to enhance the defense of gun tissues, and effectively control oral infection and inflammation. Taken together, the present research findings shed new light on the development of nanoparticles-encapsulated Chinese herbal extracts as new antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory drugs for oral health care in the near future.

768112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768112.value: Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF) is becoming a major public health concern worldwide due to the wide geographical distribution of its causative agent CCHF virus (CCHFV) and the ability to cause severe viral haemorrhagic fever with high mortality rate in humans. CCHF is transmitted by ticks, with the potential of human-to-human transmission. Although most human infection cases occur sporadically, recent climate and environmental changes favouring the reproduction and survival of ticks may increase the occurrence of human infection cases and trigger community outbreaks. To date, ribavirin, a broad-spectrum antiviral drug, is the only promising treatment against CCHF. Like other members of the genus Nairovirus of the Bunyaviridae family, CCHFV is a segmented negative-stranded RNA virus containing three genomic RNA segments, namely the small (S), medium (M), and large (L) segments. The S segment encodes the nucleocapsid protein (NP), while the M and the L segments encode the glycoproteins and the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase respectively. The RNA genome segments are encapsidated by CCHFV NP to form individual S, M and L ribonucleocapsids (RNP). Encapsidation of the CCHFV genomic RNA by NP is essential in the replicative cycle of the virus and the packaging of the genome into the virions. A critical step for RNA interaction and encapsidation by NP appears to be the oligomerisation of the NP molecules. The characteristics of oligomerisation and RNA binding for CCHFV NP and other members of the Nairovirus genus remain to be determined. The present proposal aims to unravel the molecular details of RNA interaction and encapsidation of CCHFV NP by determining the X-ray crystallographic structures of CCHFV NP and RNP. The structures will provide insights on the replication mechanism of this virus and may identify key sites for the development of specific antiviral drugs against this highly pathogenic virus. In addition, it has recently been shown that CCHFV NP in infected cells is subjected to host cell caspase cleavage and the caspase activity is not beneficial for the viral replication cycle. Furthermore, interaction of human MxA protein, an interferon induced antiviral protein, with CCHFV NP would also result in the inhibition of CCHFV replication. Thus, the interaction of CCHFV NP with caspase and human MxA protein will also be explored. By deciphering the interaction of CCHFV NP with these proteins, we hope to develop new antiviral therapeutics against this virus by mimicking the binding of these proteins to CCHFV NP. 克里米亞 - 剛果出血熱（CCHF)因其病原體CCHF病毒（CCHFV）的地理分佈廣,而且造成高死亡率的病毒性出血熱,正在成為一個重要的公共衛生問題。CCHF是由蜱傳播，但有潛在的人傳人風險。雖然人類感染個案偶爾發生，但最近的氣候和環境變化有利於蜱的存活和繁殖,因此可能會增加人類感染的機率,甚至觸發社區爆發 。至目前為止，對CCHF 唯一比較有效的治療是使用廣譜抗病毒的藥物,利巴韋林。 CCHFV和布尼亞病毒科家族的其他成員一樣，是一個節段負鏈RNA病毒,包含小的（S），中（M），和大（L）3基因組RNA片段。其中,S片段編碼核衣殼蛋白（NP），而M和L段分別編碼糖蛋白和RNA-依賴性RNA聚合酶。 RNA基因組片段會被CCHFV NP包裝形成單獨的S，M和L 核糖衣殼（RNP）這種核糖衣殼化是在病毒複製週期和包裝過程中不可缺少的。 而CCHFV NP寡聚化和RNA相互作用是基因組被衣殼化的關鍵步驟。 CCHFV NP和其他布尼亞病毒科家族成員的NP和RNA相互作用與寡聚化的特性仍有待確定。本方案希望通過解釋CCHFV NP和RNP X-射線晶體結構解開CCHFV NP的分子細節以及其與RNA相互作用的分子機制。X-射線晶體結構能對這種病毒的複製機制提供可靠証據，更可以識別關鍵位點以便發展針對性的抗病毒藥物。最新研究表明，在受感染細胞中被激活的胱天冬酶會分解CCHFV NP, 從而不利於病毒複製循環。此外，人類干擾素誘導抗病毒蛋白MxA會與 CCHFV NP結合，從而抑制CCHFV複製。因此，CCHFV NP和胱天冬酶及MxA蛋白的相互作用也將被探討。我們希望通過破譯這些蛋白質的相互作用開發新的抗病毒療法。

768312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768312.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is endemic in Hong Kong, Southern China and Southeast Asia. In Hong Kong, there are more than 1000 new cases diagnosed each year and more than half of these new cases present at advanced stage with stage III or IV disease. Chemoradiation is the standard treatment for advanced diseases. Patients are treated with induction chemotherapy followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy. The dose of radiotherapy is standardized at around 70Gy to gross tumor irrespective of T stage or response to treatment. Patients with T3 or T4 NPC are problematic for radiotherapy since the tumor extends to skull base or intracranially where the tumor is encroaching on cranial nerves and brain tissue. High dose radiation is required for adequate local control but high dose radiation is associated with risk of radiation late toxicities such as skull base necrosis, cranial nerve damage, carotid aneurysm and brain necrosis. With standard dose of radiation the chance of local recurrence is more than 30%. We have previously shown that radiation dose escalation with intensity modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) to 76Gy in gross tumor can improve local control to more than 90% but had significant morbidity and late complications. Since not all patients with T3-4 disease have local recurrence after radiotherapy, we need a means to select patients who are not responding well to radiation for more aggressive treatment. Dose escalation can be limited to poor responders instead to all patients. Also, tumor reduces in size after induction chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Radiation dose escalation can be concentrated in the residual tumor that remains active after treatment so that the area of high dose radiation can be limited to the most resistant part of the tumor instead of the initial tumor volume at diagnosis. FDG PET/CT is biological imaging. The FDG uptake in tumor reflects its metabolic activity and high FDG uptake indicates aggressive tumor. In this project, we hypothesize that PET/CT can be used for early response assessment and poor responder will benefit from radiation dose escalation. The project involves 2 studies: an initial pilot study that observe the change in FDG uptake during chemoradiation and testing out the feasibility of dose escalation to residual biological tumor volume. The second part involves a prospective randomized study where poor responder will be randomized to dose escalation or standard dose of radiotherapy. With this study, we can customize radiation and dose according to individual tumor response during treatment. 鼻咽癌是於香港，南中國及東南亞常見之癌症。在香港，每年有約有一千例新症，其中過半為第三，四期的晚期患者。這些晚期患者的標準治療為放化療。患者會先接受引導化療然後接受同步放療及化療。不論腫瘤大小或治療反應，常規的腫瘤放療劑量均為約70戈瑞(Gy)。放療於鼻咽癌第三或四期的患者會有相當困難。因這些患者的腫瘤侵蝕顱骨或伸延至顱內而貼近腦組織或腦神經。放療需要高劑量以控制腫瘤，但高量放療也會造成傷害例如顱骨壞死，腦神經受損，頸動脈瘤及腦組織壞死。常規放療後的鼻咽癌復發比率為30%。根據我們以往的研究顯示，利用強度調控放射治療以增加腫瘤的放療劑量至76戈瑞可改善腫瘤的控制率至90%，但有相當多的副作用及後遺症。由於不是所有的第三，四期的病人都會於放射後復發，我們需要一種有效的方法以識辨對治療反應不良的患者以加強治療。這些反應不良的患者會受惠於放療劑量之提升。另外，腫瘤於化療後會縮小。放療的增量區域可以集中於治療後依然活躍的腫瘤部份以治療腫瘤最頑強的部位。正電子掃描為生物造影。掃描中放射糖份的攝取反映腫瘤的活躍程度。於此研究中，我們假設正電子掃描能監測腫瘤對治療的早期反應並反應不良的患者將受惠於放療劑量之提升。研究分為兩部份：第一部份為前期研究以觀察腫瘤於治療期間在正電子掃描上的變化， 並試用治療後的剩餘腫瘤範圍以作放療增量治療。第二部份為前瞻性的隨機研究。對治療反應不良的患病會接受常規或增量放療。我們期望此研究能根據治療反應以制定個人化的放射治療。

768312.label: Realisation of objectives
768312.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) with skull base invasion or intracranial extension (T3 or T4 disease) are at risk of local failure. With modern radiotherapy using intensity modulated radiotherapy, dose escalation in tumor can be achieved by giving a boost dose to tumor. However, because of the proximity of the tumor to critical neural structures, dose escalation will entail possible permanent neurological damage. In this study, we aim to see if early response noted on PET scan during chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced NPC can predict prognosis and help in selection of high risk patient for radiation dose escalation. Patient with T3 or T4 NPC were eligible. Patients underwent 3 cycles of induction chemotherapy before concurrent chemoradiation. PET scan were performed before and after induction chemotherapy and at 30Gy of radiation to see the pattern and timing of metabolic response of tumor. For tumor that showed complete metabolic response (mCR), the dose to tumor was maintained at 70Gy. For those who did not achieve mCR, an additional boost dose was given to the residual biological tumor volume (BTV) as delineated on the post-treatment PET scan. The total dose to residual BTV was 76Gy. For automatic contouring of the BTV on PET scan, we developed an in-house method using signal to background ratio. Alternatively, for cases which the signal to background ratio could not delineate the tumor, the commercial PET-edge algorithm was used. From December 2010 to September 2015, 51 patients with T3-4, N0-3, M0 NPC were recruited into study. All patients completed 3 cycles of induction chemotherapy. All except one patient had post-induction reassessment PET scan. One patient did not have post-induction PET scan since the PET machine was out of service at that time and she was withdrawn from study. Two patients had stable disease and progressive local disease after induction chemotherapy respectively. These two patients had intracranial disease and the local extent of tumor was considered too extensive for radical radiotherapy with unacceptable toxicity. They also withdrew from study and continued with palliative treatment. Another patient had complete response noted on post-induction chemotherapy, however, she refuse radiotherapy or further treatment. These 4 patients who did not complete treatment or study assessment were excluded from analysis. Total 47 patients (35 males and 12 females) were included in outcome analysis. The mean age at diagnosis was 53 (range 21-78). Twenty-seven patients had T3 and 20 patients had T4 disease, the overall stage were Stage III for 20 patients, Stage IVA for 19 patients and stage IVB for 8 patients. The median follow up after completion of radiotherapy were 28 months. Objective 1: To assess the pattern of change in FDG uptake during treatment for locally advanced T3, T4 nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Fifty patients had pre- and post-induction chemotherapy PET scans. Two patients with extensive intracranial disease with brain invasion showed no response to induction chemotherapy with static and progressive disease respectively. Forty-eight patients showed regression of tumor and decreased metabolic activity on post-induction PET scan. Taking SUVmax in primary tumor less than 1.25xliver background activity as a threshold indicating mCR, 16 patients had complete metabolic response (mCR) after 3 cycles of induction chemotherapy. Mid-course PET scan were performed for 44 patients at around 30Gy of radiotherapy, and 25 patients achieved complete metabolic response (mCR) during radiotherapy. For patients who did not achieve mCR, residual BTV on reassessment PET scans after treatment were delineated for boost dose of radiation. It was more difficult to delineate the residual tumor volume on the mid-course PET compared with the post-induction scan because of diffuse increase in background activity due to inflammatory response to radiation. We concluded that early response to treatment can be observed on PET scan with 33.3% patient achieving mCR after induction chemotherapy and 56.8% of patients achieved mCR during radiotherapy after 30Gy. We also concluded that the post-induction PET scan would be most useful for assessment of early response and for delineating the residual tumor volume for radiation boost. Objective 2: to evaluate the value of FDG PET as early response assessment and prediction of outcome. All three patients who did not have radiotherapy had subsequent disease progression. Two died of disease and one is still surviving with disease. Forty-seven patients who completed primary treatment with chemoradiotherapy were included in survival analysis. All survival time was counted from completion of radiotherapy. Among the 15 cases who achieved mCR after induction chemotherapy, all patients were disease free without relapse at time of analysis. Among the 32 patients who did not achieve mCR after induction chemotherapy, one patient had persistent disease in NP and neck nodes after chemoradiotherapy and was salvage with surgery. She was disease free after surgery. She was counted as NP and regional failure but not as event in progression failure. Another patient had recurrence in nasopharynx at 31.5 month post-radiotherapy. Both patients had boost dose to nasopharynx. One patient developed regional recurrence in neck nodes at 47.6 months after radiotherapy. Six patients developed distant metastases. The 3 year NP control, regional control, distant metastases free, progression free survival and overall survival were 89.4%, 96.9%, 79.5%, 49.2% and 81% respectively among patients who did not achieved mCR after induction chemotherapy. The corresponding survival rates were all 100% among patients who achieved mCR after induction chemotherapy. The difference in progression-free survival was statistically significant (p=0.045) We concluded that early response with mCR on PET after induction chemotherapy predicts for very favourable outcome after chemoradiotherapy. Boost dose in NP appears to be effective in local control but did not prevent disease progression outside NP. Distant failure is the major cause of disease progression and death. 3. To investigate the effect of dose escalation in incomplete responder in improving local control and survival. In the original proposal, our plan was to start a part II randomized study after observing the pattern of response in the initial 30 patients in the part I of study. Patient who achieved mCR will not have boost, those who did not achieve mCR will be randomized to boost or no boost to see the effect of dose escalation in incomplete responders. However, after observing the initial response, we changed the plan to expand the number of patients in the part I of study instead of proceeding to part II. The reasons are recruitment is slower than expected and we only observe 1 NP failure in the initial cohort. Also, the boost dose was well tolerated and none of the patient had grade 3 or more toxicity from radiotherapy. We considered a randomized study will not be ethical or practically feasible. Instead, we increased the number of patients in the cohort and observe for long term outcome for patients with and without boost. However, patient with boost will mostly be the ones who did not achieve mCR. Eighteen patients did not have boost and 29 patient had boost dose to NP and the 3 year NP control rate were 100% and 87.8% respectively. The corresponding progression-free survival and overall survival for patients with and without boost were 94.4% and 90% vs 73.9% and 84.6% respectively. The major site of disease relapse is distant metastases.

768312.label: Major findings and research outcome
768312.value: 1. PET scan can detect early response during chemoradiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma. One third of patients achieved complete metabolic response after 3 cycles of induction chemotherapy and 56.8% of patients achieved complete metabolic response during radiotherapy after 30Gy. 2. Complete metabolic response after induction chemotherapy is a strong prognosticator with 100% 3 years progression free survival in responders compared with 49.2% in patients who did not achieve complete metabolic response. 3. Boost dose to residual biological tumor volume on PET is feasible and well tolerated. The methodology for delineated biological tumor volume on PET scan for radiotherapy was validated and published (publication 1 in Part C). We also compared the prognostic value of biological tumor volume on PET scan with anatomical tumor volume on MRI and found that the nodal volume is predictive of outcome (publication 2 in Part C, manuscript under revision). 3. Local control rate at 3 years was 100% and 87.8% among patients with and without boost. There were 2 local failures among the group. One patient had persistent disease salvaged by surgery, only 1 out of 47 patients had progressive disease in nasopharynx after chemoradiation. 4.Patients who did not achieve complete metabolic response after induction chemotherapy are at high risk of developing distant metastases. The preliminary findings were reported in ASCO and ESMO meeting and the manuscript is under preparation.

768312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
768312.value: PET scan after induction chemotherapy is useful to select high risk patients for intensification of treatment. Radiation dose escalation to tumor resulted in good local control, however, distant metastases became the dominant pattern of disease failure. Patients with incomplete response should be considered for intensification of systemic treatment besides dose escalation. Options that can be considered include giving additional agents besides cisplatin during radiotherapy or to give adjuvant treatment after chemoradiation. Additional chemotherapy or other novel treatment like target therapy or immunotherapy can be considered to reduce chance of distant failure. This will require further clinical trials to test out tolerance to treatment as well as efficacy. Given that PET scan can detect early response, there is a potential for PET scan to be used as a new modality of disease response assessment to other novel treatment. Besides measuring change in tumor size, metabolic response may be a more sensitive way to measure response to target therapy or immunotherapy which may not induce regression of tumor but suppress tumor growth. Further studies to evaluate the potential of PET scan in response assessment are warranted.

768312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
768312.value: Patients with locally advanced (T3/4) nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) are treated with combined chemotherapy and radiotherapy. PET scan is a whole body imaging which shows the uptake of glucose in tumor which reflects its metabolic activity. From 2010 to 2015, patients with T3 or T4 NPC were recruited into study. Patients underwent 3 cycles of induction chemotherapy (IC) and then concurrent chemoradiotherapy. PET scan was performed before and after IC and at mid course of radiotherapy to evaluate response during treatment. Complete metabolic response (mCR) is achieved if PET scan shows no active disease. Sixteen out of 48 patients (33.3%) achieved mCR after IC and 56.8% of patients achieved mCR during radiotherapy. Early response after IC is associated with very favourable outcome with 100% 3 years disease free survival in responders compared with 49.2% in patients who did not achieve mCR. Relapse among non-responders is mainly due to distant metastases. We concluded that PET scan can detect early response to treatment for NPC and mCR after IC is a very favourable prognostic factor. Patients who did not achieve mCR are at risk of developing distant metastases and should be considered for intensification of treatment.

768712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768712.value: Neuromuscular junction (NMJ) of skeletal muscle is a synapse that transmits an impulse from the nerve ending of a motor neuron to the muscle. When an action potential reaches the nerve ending, a neurotransmitter acetylcholine (ACh) is released and ACh will initiate a muscle contraction by binding to nicotinic ACh receptors (AChR) on the muscle membrane. NMJ is clinically important because abnormal neuromuscular transmission can cause myasthenic syndrome. Myasthenic syndrome is characterised by the presence of ocular, bulbar, respiratory symptoms and a decremental response of compound muscle action potential to repetitive nerve stimulation. The most severe form of myasthenic syndrome can be fatal because of generalized muscle paralysis and respiratory failure. Myasthenic syndrome can be caused by botulinum toxins, auto-antibodies against NMJ components, such as AChR, and single-gene defects collectively called as congenital myasthenic syndrome (CMS). CMS is characterized by an early onset of the symptoms and the absence of auto-antibodies. CMS is caused by mutations of genes encoding proteins located in the presynaptic, synaptic and postsynaptic regions of NMJ. Up to date, 13 disease genes of CMS have been identified, i.e., AGRN, CHAT, CHRNA1, CHRNB1, CHRND, CHRNE, COLQ, DOK7, GFPT1, LAMB2, MUSK, RAPSN, and SCN4A. CHAT mutations cause presynaptic CMS, COLQ and LAMB2 mutations cause synaptic CMS, and the rest causes postsynaptic CMS. Though dysfunction of NMJ is clinically significant, the proteins involved in neuromuscular transmission, development, maintenance, and assembly of NMJ have not been completely identified. During studies of genetic defects of CMS, we have encountered a consanguineous CMS family without mutations detected by bi-directional sequencing of all the known CMS genes. We hypothesize that the CMS of this family is caused by a novel disease gene. Using homozygosity mapping, we successfully mapped the disease gene to a 21 MB identity-by-descent (IBD) region on chromosome 6q by high-density single-nucleotide polymorphism microarrays. Since no known CMS genes have been identified on chromosome 6, this result confirmed the hypothesis that CMS of this family is caused by a novel disease gene. To identify the novel disease gene, we aim to sequence all the genes in the IBD region for the disease-causing mutation. 768712.label: Realisation of objectives
768712.value: Here, we aim to determine the molecular basis of CMS in a consanguineous family with limb girdle type of CMS by microarray analysis and whole exome sequencing (WES). There are two clinically affected siblings (P1, P2) and clinically unaffected father, mother and sisters (S1 and S2). Homozygosity mapping were performed using high-density single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) microarray (Affymetrix SNP 6.0). Mutations were identified by WES and Sanger sequencing. A region of homozygosity (ROH) of 20 MB was mapped on chromosome 6q15-21. This ROH region is the only ROH region that is present in all the clinically affected siblings (P1 and P2) and absent in all the clinically unaffected siblings (S1 and S2). WES showed a novel single-nucleotide variant (SNV) of the AK9 gene located in this region. This SNV creates a cryptic 5′-UTR signal in intron 5 of the AK9 gene. This cryptic 5′-UTR sequence in intron 5 of the AK9 gene probably causes splicing signal to be interfered by translation signal leading to leaky splicing. Intriguingly, assuming S1 and S2 may have homozygous mutations but clinically unaffected, another ROH of 25 MB was found on chromosome 11p13-q12 in all siblings (P1, P2, S1 and S2). WES showed a disease causing RAPSN mutation homozygous in all siblings and heterozygous in the parents. The RAPSN gene is located in ROH region on chromosome 11. Since RAPSN-associated CMS is only manifested in P1 and P2 but not in S1 and S2, the disease phenotype in P1 and P2 should be determined by the novel disease-modifying AK9 gene. AK9 is located in the cytosol and is involved in production of NDP and NTP. This function linked up with N-glycosylation of proteins, which is known to defective in patients with CMS with limb girdle type since NTP is required for synthesis of dolichol phosphate and nucleotide-sugars for N-glycosylation of proteins. The gene AK9 is a novel disease-modifying gene for limb girdle myasthenia. The disease phenotype in our patients is of digenic inheritance. A homozygous RAPSN and AK9 mutations cause limb girdle myasthenia rather than classical CMS are identified. This is the first time that this specific genotype-phenotype correlation is reported. This novel link of AK9, N-glycosylation, and RAPSN will pave a new way for studying the biology of NMJ and synapses.

768712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
768712.value: Myasthenic syndrome is characterized by the presence of ocular, bulbar, respiratory symptoms and a decremental response of compound muscle action potential to repetitive nerve stimulation. The most severe form of myasthenic syndrome can be fatal because of generalized muscle paralysis and respiratory failure. Single-gene defects causing myasthenic syndrome are called as congenital myasthenic syndrome (CMS). There is a special type of CMS that caused only limb-girdle myasthenia. Here, we aim to determine the molecular basis of CMS in a consanguineous family with limb girdle type of CMS by microarray analysis and whole exome sequencing (WES). Homozygous RAPSN and AK9 mutations cause limb girdle myasthenia rather than classical CMS are identified. RAPSN and AK9 should be included in the gene list for limb girdle myasthenia in addition to genes related to defective N-glycosylation. This will improve genetic testing of CMS patients. This novel link of AK9, N-glycosylation, and RAPSN will pave a new way for studying the biology of neuromuscular junction and synapses. Since both RAPSN deficiency and N-glycosylation defects could both cause limb-girdle myasthenia, increasing the nucleotide pools in NMJ by dietary supplements may be a new way of treating patients with congenital myasthenia.

769912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
769912.value: Ever since Sydney Ringer showed, in the 1880s, that Ca2+ in the now famous Ringer’s solution is critical in maintaining muscle contraction, Ca2+ has been well established as a universal messenger for regulating virtually all aspects of life. More than 80 years had passed until the 1960s, when it had become clear that the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) in muscle is the site for storage of Ca2+ and its release is what triggers muscle contraction. This marked the emergence of the concept that mobilization of intracellular Ca2+ stores is a major mechanism of cellular signal transduction. In the early 1980s, Berridge and colleagues showed that agonists, such as acetylcholine, can activate the synthesis of a second messenger molecule, inositol trisphosphate (IP3), which can then signal the mobilization of Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the equivalent of SR in non-muscle cells. During the late 1980s, we showed that the Ca2+ stores can be mobilized by two other messengers unrelated to IP3 and identified them as cyclic ADP-ribose (cADPR), a novel cyclic nucleotide synthesized from NAD, and nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NAADP), a linear metabolite of NADP. Their messenger functions have since been well documented in a wide range of cellular systems spanning three biological kingdoms. It is now clear that cADPR acts on the ryanodine receptor in the ER. Most recently, in an article published in Nature, the targets of NAADP have been shown to be the two pore channels in lysosomes. This proposal focuses on: Aim 1. To develop methods for investigating the NAADP-signaling pathway. Aim 2. To elucidate the mechanisms of the NAADP-signaling pathway. 自從Sydney Ringer在19世紀80年代发现鈣離子是在著名的林格氏液中維持肌肉收縮的關鍵，鈣離子作為一種 調節生命幾乎所有方面的普遍信使的地位已被确立。直到20世紀60年代，超過80年過去了，才发现肌肉中的肌漿網（SR）是鈣的儲存網站，鈣从SR中释放觸發肌肉收縮。這標誌著細胞內鈣離子的動員 是一個主要的細胞信號轉導機制。在20世紀80年代初，Berridge和同事发现，受體激動劑，如乙酰膽鹼，可以激活一個第二信使分子,三磷酸肌醇（IP3), 的合成，IP3 然後可以動員鈣離子从內質網（ER）中,相當於非肌細胞中的SR, 释放。在20世紀80年代後期，我們發現两个与 IP3無關的鈣库動員劑，並确定它們是環腺苷二磷酸核糖（cADPR），一個從NAD合成的新穎環狀核苷酸，和鹼酸酰胺腺嘌呤二核苷酸磷酸（NAADP） ，一個線性的NADP代謝物。他們的信使功能在跨越三個生物王國的多种细胞系統中都得到了很好的证明。現在已經很清楚，cADPR是作用于ER上的兰尼碱受體。最近，一篇發表在“自然”的文章證明NAADP是作用于在溶酶體上的兩個孔道。這項建議的重點是： 目標1。發展研究NAADP信號通路的方法。 目的2。闡明NAADP信號通路的機制。

769912.label: Realisation of objectives
769912.value: This project has only one revised objective: To develop methods for investigating the NAADP-signaling pathway. This objective contains two sub-aims. Sub-aim 1. Cell models for investigating the NAADP-dependent Ca2+ signaling. NAADP, an endogenous Ca2+ mobilizing nucleotide, mobilizes Ca2+ from acidic organelles through two pore channel 2 (TPC2) in many tissues and primary cell types. Yet, few culture cell lines were found to be NAADP competent, which made it difficult to study its role and underlying mechanisms. In this project, we have established or characterized three NAADP competent cell models: mouse ES cells, TPC2-overexpressing HeLa cells, INS-1E cells, and demonstrated that NAADP/TPC2 signaling is involved in neural differentiation, autophagosome-lysosomal fusion, and glucose-induced insulin secretion. Therefore, we have successfully completed Sub-aim 1. (1) The NAADP-TPC2-Ca2+ signaling modulates neural differentiation of mouse ES cells The mechanisms of neural differentiation of embryonic stem (ES) cells remain largely unknown. Here we examined the role of NAADP-TPC2 signaling in the neural differentiation of ES cells. We found that the mouse ES cells are responsive to NAADP and possess the key components of NAADP-signaling pathway. The expression of TPC2 was markedly decreased during the initial ES cell entry into neural progenitors, and the levels of TPC2 gradually rebounded during the late stages of neurogenesis. Correspondingly, TPC2 knockdown accelerated mouse ES cell differentiation into neural progenitors but inhibited these neural progenitors from committing to neurons. Whereas TPC2 overexpression inhibited mouse ES cell from entering the early neural lineage. Interestingly, TPC2 knockdown had no effect on the differentiation of astrocytes and oligodendrocytes of ES cells. Taken together, our data indicate that TPC2 signaling plays a temporal and differential role in modulating the neural lineage entry of ES cells, in that TPC2 signaling inhibits ES cell entry to early neural progenitors, but is required for late neuronal differentiation. Above findings were published in Plos One, 8: e66077 (2013). (2) The NAADP-TPC2-Ca2+ Signaling Inhibits Autophagosomal-Lysosomal Fusion by Alkalinizing Lysosomal pH. Autophagy is an evolutionarily conserved lysosomal degradation pathway, yet the role of NAADP-TPC2 signaling in autophagy regulation was not known. Here we found that HeLa cell line can be reconstituted to be NAADP competent by overexpressing a wildtype, but not a pore-mutant, TPC2, and treatment of TPC2-overexpressing cells with Ned-19, a NAADP antagonist, markedly inhibited NAADP-induced Ca2+ release, indicating that NAADP can activate TPC2 for Ca2+ release. On one hand, overexpression of TPC2 in HeLa or mouse ES cells inhibited autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion, thereby resulting in the accumulation of autophagosomes. Treatment of TPC2-expressing cells with a cell permeant-NAADP agonist, NAADP-AM, further induced autophagosome accumulation. On the other hand, TPC2 knockdown or treatment of cells with Ned-19 markedly decreased the accumulation of autophagosomes. Interestingly, inhibiting mTOR activity failed to increase TPC2-induced autophagosome accumulation. Instead, we found that overexpression of TPC2 alkalinized lysosomal pH, and lysosomal re-acidification abolished TPC2-induced autophagosome accumulation. In addition, TPC2 overexpression had no effect on general endosomal-lysosomal degradation but prevent the recruitment of Rab-7 to autophagosomes. Taken together, our data demonstrate that TPC2-NAADP-Ca2+ signaling alkalinizes lysosomal pH to specifically inhibit the later stage of basal autophagy progression. We have published above findings in. J. Biol. Chem. (2013) 288, 24247-24263, and Commun Integr Biol. (2013) 6: e27595. (3) The NAADP-TPC2-Ca2+ Signaling is required for glucose-induced insulin release. NAADP was shown to play an important role in the glucose-induced Ca2+ signaling in beta-cells, yet it is unknown whether the NAADP-TPC2-Ca2+ signaling is involved in glucose-induced insulin release. We found that a popular beta-cell line, INS-1E, was responsive to NAADP and contained detectable TPC2, TPC1, and CD38, three key components in NAADP signaling. In addition, treatment of INS-1E cells with NAADP antagonist, NED-19, blocked glucose-induced Ca2+ oscillation and insulin secretion. Likewise, TPC2 knockdown in INS-1E cells significantly inhibited glucose-induced Ca2+ oscillation and insulin secretion, whereas TPC2 overexpression promoted it. Interestingly, we found that CD38 knockdown in INS-1E cells failed to affect glucose-induced Ca2+ oscillation and insulin secretion, suggesting that CD38 is not responsible for NAADP production in INS-1E cells. Taken together, our data indicate that the NAADP-TPC2-Ca2+ signaling is required for glucose-induced insulin release (manuscript in preparation). In addition, we have established TPC1 knockdown or overexpressing INS-1E cells, and are currently examining whether TPC1 is also involved in glucose-induced Ca2+ signaling and insulin release. We also established the TPC1 and TPC2 double knockdown INS-1E cells and plan to assess whether TPC1 and TPC2 double knockdown abolishes glucose-induced insulin secretion. Sub-aim 2. Methods for measuring endogenous NAADP levels and NAADP-mediated Ca2+ release. (1) An improved method for measuring endogenous NAADP. The group of Prof. Lee Hon-Cheung, the original PI of this project, has successfully completed this aim before he retired from HKU. A manuscript entitled “An Improved Enzymatic Cycling Assay for NAADP” was published in Messenger 2, 96–105, 2013, in which this grant was acknowledged.requires the synthesis of 32P-labeled NAADP and the preparation of Currently available assays for NAADP include a radio-receptor assay that microsomes from sea urchin eggs. To circumvent the inconveniences, Graeff and Lee had developed a fluorometric assay for NAADP instead, which has been successfully used in measuring endogenous NAADP in various cells. Graeff, whose research was supported by this grant, used a mutant of the Aplysia ADP-ribosyl cyclase, which can catalyze a base-exchange reaction at neutral pH to produce NADP from NAADP, to further improve the sensitivity of this assay. The resultant NADP can then be measured by coupling its production to a cycling assay involving glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase and diaphorase. The coupled-enzyme cycling assay has sub-nanomolar sensitivity and is a simple, continuous assay requiring minimal sample manipulation. It can also be set up in a multi-well high throughput format. The assay can be adapted to measure cyclic ADP-ribose phosphate (cADPRP) and nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide (NAAD) as well. The results provide the first evidence indicating that cADPRP is a naturally occurring metabolite present in red blood cells and liver. This improved fluorometric assay for NAADP compares favorably with the radio-receptor assay, currently the most sensitive assay for NAADP. (2) Develop the Ca2+ sensors for measuring lysosomal Ca2+ release. The current available NAADP-induced Ca2+ measurement actually reflects the global cytosolic Ca2+ increases, which is the combinatory results of local lysosomal Ca2+ release and subsequent Ca2+ induced Ca2+ release (CICS) from ER. Therefore, we have designed two genetically encoded Ca2+ indicators to simultaneously measure lysosome luminal and extra-luminal Ca2+ changes. We first constructed the LAMP1-GECO1-expressing HeLa cells, in which GECO1 (green fluorescence) is expressed at the outer surface of lysosome, and found that treatment of LAMP1-GECO1-expressing HeLa cells with GPN induced the localized lysosome extra-luminal Ca2+ increases. We also constructed the Cathepsin B-R-GECO1-expressing HeLa cells, in which Cathepsin B-R-GECO1 (red fluorescence) was partially localized with lysosomes, and found that GPN treatment decreased lysosome luminal Ca2+ levels, reflected by the decreased red fluorescence inside lysosomes. Likewise, in HeLa cells co-expressing Cathepsin B-R-GECO1 and LAMP1- GECO1, we found that GPN treatment increased green fluorescence (lysosome extra-luminal Ca2+ increase) while decreased red fluorescence (lysosome luminal Ca2+ decrease). Therefore, these data indicate that Cathepsin B-R-GECO1 and LAMP1-GECO1 can be applied to simultaneously measure lysosome Ca2+ changes (manuscript under preparation). We are currently applying these two Ca2+ sensors to measure NAADP-induced Ca2+ changes in a variety of cell types. In summary, we have successfully completed Sub-aim 2 as well.

769912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
769912.value: NAADP, one of the most potent endogenous Ca2+ mobilizing messengers, mobilizes Ca2+ from an acidic lysosomes-related store. The Ca2+-signaling pathway mediated by NAADP is ubiquitous and the functions it regulates are equally diverse, including fertilization, insulin secretion in pancreatic islets, and neuronal differentiation. Therefore, decoding the molecular mechanisms involved in this novel signaling pathway is important not only for scientific reasons but also has clinical relevance. In this project, we have established or characterized three NAADP competent cell models: mouse ES cells, TPC2 overexpressing HeLa cells, INS-1E cells, and demonstrated that NAADP/TPC2/Ca2+ signaling is involved in a variety of cellular processes: neural differentiation, autophagosome-lysosomal fusion, and glucose-induced insulin secretion. A sensitive and simple coupled-enzyme cycling assay has also been developed in this project to measure endogenous NAADP in sub-nanomolar range in various cells. Besides, two Ca2+ sensors have been engineered to accurately measure lysosomal Ca2+ changes, which could further facilitate the detection of NAADP-induced Ca2+ changes. Given the pivotal role of NAADP-mediated calcium signaling pathway in a wide variety of cellular processes, understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in this novel signaling pathway is important not only for scientific reasons but also have clinical relevance.
