773612.label: Major findings and research outcome
773612.value: 1. In the in vitro cell model, we reported the presence of a 5-HT [5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT); serotonin] analog in aqueous phase cigarette smoke. Furthermore, we found a time-dependent elevation of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) level after 5-HT treatment, which was blocked by apocynin [a NADPH oxidase (NOX) inhibitor], in line with 5-HT-induced expression of NOX2. We also observed 5-HT-induced elevation of IL-8 at both mRNA and protein levels, which was inhibited by TEMPO (a free radical scavenger), and inhibitors for p38 MAPK (SB203580) and ERK (U0126), in agreement with the time-dependent phosphorylation of p38 MAPK and ERK. Our findings suggest that 5-HT presented in the bronchial epithelium of smokers may be involved in cigarette smoke-induced oxidative stress and inflammation via activation of p38 MAPK and ERK pathway after formation of free radicals. Submitted to Free Radical Research (under review). 2. We further found that except 5-HT, an analog of 5-HT [serotonin creatinine sulfate monohydrate (SCSM)] like cigarette smoke medium (CSM) caused dose-dependent elevation of IL-8 release in BEAS-2B cells. Similar elevation of IL-8 release was observed from primary human normal bronchial and tracheal epithelial cells (NBECs and NTECs respectively). Dose-dependent induction of phase II enzymes, NAD(P)H:quione oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1) and heme oxygenase 1 (HO-1) was found after CSM exposure in BEAS-2B cells and NBECs. In contrast, SCSM caused only induction of NQO1, indicating the involvement of 5-HT on the regulation of NQO1 in airway epithelial cells. The CSM-mediated induction of NQO-1 and HO-1 might be responsible to airway inflammation, as this was inhibited by selegiline [a selective monoamine oxidase (MAO)-B inhibitor], resulting in the inhibition of CSM-induced elevation of IL-8 release. The data will be used to write up a full manuscript for submission. 3. In the in vivo rat model, epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) in the presence of cigarette smoke (CS) exposure was found to reverse CS-induced elevation of serum 5-HT without significant effect on lung function. CS-induced airway resistance (i.e. enhancement of Penh) was observed after 1-month CS exposure, which was sustainable. A trend of CS-induced reduction in 5-HT level was observed in the bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL), which was normalized in the presence of EGCG. We found CS- and EGCG-induced increase in NQO1 expression in lung homogenates, which was normalized in the combination treatment of CS and EGCG. The results will be submitted as an abstract to European Respiratory Congress to be held in London in September 2016.

773612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
773612.value: • In the in vitro cell model, we should perform the experiments using selective MAO-A inhibitor clorgyline on CSM- or 5-HT-induced inflammation, in comparison to selegiline (a selective MAO-B inhibitor). The mechanisms on the regulation of NQO1 and HO-1 expressions after CSM and 5-HT will need further investigation. CSM-elicited induction of phase II enzymes (NQO1 and HO-1) in airway epithelial cells is of relevance to carcinogenesis as lung is a target organ for carcinogenesis mediated by cigarette smoke. • In the in vivo rat model, interventional studies using EGCG or selegiline are warranted to explore the complex interplay of 5-HT and its receptors in the development of CS-induced lung damage and enhancement of airway resistance. As phase II enzymes play important roles in the detoxification of reactive electrophils to noncarcinogenic metabolites, induction of these enzymes in humans could alleviate cancer risk in individuals exposed to cigarette smoke. Future studies on the molecular mechanisms of phase II enzymes by CS and EGCG could lead to the development of novel drugs that might induce phase II enzymes, with little toxic effects. These studies would have immense potential in the development of new strategies in halting the progression of CS-mediated COPD in humans.

773612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
773612.value: Cigarette smoking is the major contributor for developing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a common airway condition characterized by losing lung function at an accelerated rate with aging. Despite pharmacological treatments, the morbidity and mortality of COPD remain high. The airway lesions are inflammatory and bronchospastic, but alveolar lesions with destruction of airway sacs are ischemic. Using cigarette smoke (CS)-exposed rat model to simulate COPD, we found CS-induced elevation of circulating (serum) levels of the monoamine neurotransmitter serotonin [5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT)], similar to clinical findings in COPD patients. In support, we have identified the presence of a 5-HT analog in the aqueous phase cigarette smoke. After incubating the cigarette smoke medium with airway epithelial cells in culture, i.e. cells lining the airways, oxidative stress and inflammation were present, which was similar to incubation with 5-HT alone via similar molecular signaling pathways, suggesting potential mechanisms for CS-mediated COPD pathogenesis. Our animal study found that the major component of green tea extract, EGCG, led to a reduction in serum 5-HT level, possibly through the phase II enzyme NQO1. These findings allow better understanding of the link between 5-HT and COPD, and provide further insights into strategies for new therapeutic treatments.

774012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
774012.value: Stroke is the second most common cause of death worldwide and is the predominant cause of permanent disability among older people. The mouth becomes a very unhealthy place after stroke, where yeasts and pathogenic bacteria multiply at an accelerated rate. Poor oral hygiene results in increased dental plaque, gingival bleeding, and the harbouring of oral opportunistic pathogens. Dental plaque acts as a reservoir of pathogenic microorganisms which results in additional oral health problems and also can cause life-threatening medical complications; most notably aspiration pneumonia and/or recurrent stroke. The first six months following stroke is a particular vulnerable period to survive. Removal of dental plaque and its associated pathogenic microorganisms is challenging in this compromised state of reduced manual dexterity and weak state following a stroke. Powered (electric) toothbrushes can be of assistance in plaque removal in frail elders. For more resistant oral pathogens, anti-plaque/anti-microbial mouthrinses can offer additional help in controlling dental plaque and thereby prevent harbouring potentially life threatening oral pathogens. Over the years the Faculty of Dentistry and the Stroke Rehabilitation Unit of the Department of Medicine in Hong Kong have been actively working together to address the problems of oral health associated with stroke; and specifically the challenge of safeguarding the life and health of stroke survivors during the vulnerable rehabilitation period. We are now proposing to involve stroke patients during out-patient rehabilitation in a randomized clinical trial to test the effectiveness of powered tooth brushing and a chlorhexidine anti-microbial mouthrinse in reducing dental plaque accumulation and oral pathogens; and how this affects their general and oral health status. We anticipate that all participants will benefit from the oral health promotion initiatives and that the advantages will be long lasting. We expect to demonstrate a ‘gold standard’ of oral health preventive care, as part of stroke rehabilitation, that can reduce (or has potential to reduce) serious medical complications after a stroke. If proven effective this oral health preventive care regime (which is relatively easy to implement and at low cost) could widely be adopted in stroke rehabilitation globally. 中風是全球第二大死因，也是一個相當普遍的成因導致中風長者永久殘障。在中風病發後，患者的口腔衛生情況通常會變差，甚至會成為酵母菌和致病微生物激增的溫床。 口腔衛生欠佳會引致牙菌斑增加、齒齦出血，更會有可能窩藏致病的口腔病菌。 牙菌斑作為收集致病微生物的貯存庫，最終會增加口腔衛生的問題，甚至會引起危害生命的併發症，尤其是呼吸道肺炎以及/或發生週期性的中風。因此，在中風後的首六個月將會是患者繼續生存的最關鍵時刻。 由於中風患者身體虛弱及活動能力變差，所以患者清潔牙菌斑及相關的口腔病菌時會面對一定的難度。因此，使用電動牙刷可以有助身體虛弱的老年患者清除牙菌斑；而對于頑固的口腔病菌，使用抗菌漱口水就可有助進一步控制牙菌斑，及預防有可能形成對生命造成威脅的口腔病菌。 多年來，香港大學牙醫學院與內科學系中風康復科一直共同積極研究與中風病發後相關的口腔健康問題，尤其在患者處於最艱辛的復康期內，如何去保護他們的生命及健康。我們現建議正接受門診康復治療的中風患者參與此項隨機臨床的試驗，藉此測試電動牙刷及洗必泰（chlorhexidine）抗菌漱口水對減低牙菌斑積聚及致病口腔病菌的成效，並對患者口腔健康及整體健康狀況的影響。我們期望所有參與者能夠從這次口腔健康的積極推廣中受惠，而所得到的益處亦將會是持久的。我們希望驗證出一個‘黃金標準’的口腔衛生預防護理項目作為中風復康療程的其中一部份，並因此能減低（或有可能減低）中風後嚴重的併發症。若此口腔衛生預防護理制度被證明有效（相對地容易執行及費用便宜），將適合在全球中風復康療程上廣泛採用。

774012.label: Realisation of objectives
774012.value: The response rate to the clinical trial was 78.7% (74/94). There were significant improvements in plaque levels (oral hygiene) among both groups (P<0.001). Those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme [powered tooth brush (with professional oral hygiene instruction) and twice daily use of 0.2% chlorhexidine gluconate mouth rinse] had significantly lower plaque levels at the end of the clinical trial than those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme [manual tooth brush (with professional oral hygiene instruction], P<0.01. After controlling for other baseline factors (in the regression analyses), the percentage of sites with moderate to abundant plaque was lower by a value of 0.21 among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme compared to those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme, p<0.001. There were significant improvements in gingival bleeding levels among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme [powered tooth brush (with professional oral hygiene instruction) and twice daily use of 0.2% chlorhexidine gluconate mouth rinse], p<0.001. However, no significant improvement in gingival bleeding levels was observed among those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme [manual tooth brush (with professional oral hygiene instruction], p>0.05. At the end of the clinical trial, the level of gingival bleeding was significantly less among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme compared to those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme, p=0.01. After controlling for other baseline factors (in the regression analyses), the percentage of sites with gingival bleeding was lower by a value of 0.13 among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme compared to those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme, p<0.001. Among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme there was no significant change in the prevalence of AGNB (p>0.05) or the viable counts of AGNB (p>0.05). Likewise, among those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme there was no significant changes in the prevalence of AGNB (p>0.05) or the viable counts of AGNB (p>0.05). At the end of the clinical trial, between the oral hygiene care groups, there was no significant difference in the prevalence of AGNB (p>0.05) or viable counts of AGNB (p>0.05). Among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme there was no significant change in the prevalence of yeast (p>0.05) or the viable counts of yeast (p>0.05). Likewise, among those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme there was no significant changes in the prevalence of yeast (p>0.05) or the viable counts of yeast (p>0.05). At the end of the clinical trial, between the oral hygiene care groups there was no significant difference in the prevalence of yeast (p>0.05) or in viable counts of yeast (p>0.05). Among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme there was no significant change in the prevalence of s. aureus (p>0.05) but there was a significant reduction in viable counts of s. aureus (p<0.05). Among those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme there was no significant changes in the prevalence of s. aureus (p>0.05) or the viable counts of s. aureus (p>0.05). At the end of the clinical trial, there was no significant difference between the oral hygiene care groups in terms of the prevalence of s. aureus (p>0.05) or viable counts of s. aureus (p>0.05). There were significant improvements in health-related quality of life (physical health – PCS 12 scores) among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme, p<0.01. No significant improvement in physical health (PCS 12 scores) was observed among those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme, p>0.05. After controlling for other baseline factors (in the regression analyses), physical health (PCS 12 scores) was higher (better) by a value of 3.63 among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme compared to those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme, p<0.05. Among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme there was no significant change in oral health-related quality of life in terms of GOHAI scores (p>0.05), OHIP-14 scores (p>0.05) or OHTS scores (p>0.05). Likewise among those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme there was no significant change in oral health-related quality of life in terms of GOHAI scores (p>0.05), OHIP-14 scores (p>0.05) or OHTS scores (p>0.05). At the end of the trial, between groups, there was no significant difference in GOHAI scores (p>0.05), OHIP-14 scores (p>0.05) or OHTS scores (p>0.05) Secondary objectives were to determine if participation in the 3-month clinical trial had an effect on plaque, gingival bleeding, oral pathogens, health- and oral health-related quality of life at 6-months. At 6-months review the response rate was 61% (57/94). There were significant improvements in plaque levels (oral hygiene) among both groups from pre-intervention to 6-months (p<0.001). After controlling for other baseline factors (in the regression analyses), the percentage of sites with moderate to abundant plaque at 6-months was lower by a value of 0.09 among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme compared to those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme, p<0.05. There were significant improvements in gingival bleeding among from pre-intervention to 6-months among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme (p<0.001) but no significant change among those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme (p>0.05). After controlling for other baseline factors (in the regression analyses), the percentage of sites with gingival bleeding at 6-months was lower by a value of 0.08 among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme compared to those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme, p<0.01. There were significant improvements in physical health (PCS 12 scores) among both groups from pre-intervention to 6-months (p<0.01). After controlling for other baseline factors (in the regression analyses), physical health (PCS 12 scores) was higher (better) by a value of 4.35 among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme compared to those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme, p<0.05. In terms of oral health-related quality of life, controlling for other baseline factors (in the regression analyses), GOHAI scores at 6-months was higher (better) by a value of 1.91 among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme compared to those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme, p<0.05. In terms of oral pathogens (ABNG, Yeast or S. aureus) there was no significant difference in prevalence of oral pathogens with respect to intervention group (p>0.05).

774012.label: Major findings and research outcome
774012.value: Both oral health promotions significantly reduced plaque levels (improved oral hygiene). However the advanced oral hygiene care programme [powered tooth brush (with professional oral hygiene instruction) and twice daily use of 0.2% chlorhexidine gluconate mouth rinse] was more effective than the conventional oral hygiene care programme [manual tooth brush (with professional oral hygiene instruction] in reducing plaque levels (improving oral hygiene). Controlling for other baseline factors, plaque levels at the end of the trial was lower by a value of 0.21 among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme. The advanced oral hygiene care bundle significantly reduced gingival bleeding but no significant reduction in gingival bleeding was observed among those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme. Controlling for other baseline factors, gingival bleeding levels at the end of the trial was lower by a value of 0.13 among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme. Neither oral hygiene care programmes significantly reduced the prevalence nor the viable counts of AGNB. Likewise neither oral hygiene care programme significantly reduced the prevalence nor the viable counts of yeast. Neither oral hygiene care programme significantly reduced the prevalence of s. aureus. The advance oral hygiene care programme significantly reduced the viable count of s.aureus. However, there were no significant differences in viable counts of s.aureus at the end of the clinical trial between recipients of the different oral hygiene care programmes. There were significant improvements in health-related quality of life (physical health – PCS 12 scores) among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme but not among those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme. After controlling for other baseline factors (in the regression analyses), physical health (PCS 12 scores) was higher (better) by a value of 3.63 among those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme. Neither oral hygiene care programmes significantly improved oral health-related quality of life (in terms of improvement in GOHAI, OHIP-14 or OHTS scores). The effect of receiving the advanced oral hygiene care programme was evident at 6-months (3-months after the clinical trial). Those who received the advanced oral hygiene care programme had significantly less plaque, gingival bleeding, better health(PCS 12 scores) and better oral health-related quality of life (GOHAI scores) at 6-months compared to those who received the conventional oral hygiene care programme. No significant improvement in the prevalence and viable counts of oral pathogens were observed.

774012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774012.value: The findings of this clinical trial showed evidence of how oral hygiene care during stroke rehabilitation can reduce plaque levels and gingival bleeding. The use of a relatively simple and inexpensive method of oral hygiene using a powered toothbrush and twice daily rinsing with chlorhexidine (0.2%) proved more effective than using a manual toothbrush alone (which is the conventional oral hygiene care currently used in stroke rehabilitation). Furthermore, there was evidence of improvement in health-related quality of life. The effect of undergoing oral hygiene care during stroke rehabilitation had a lasting effect 3-months after the trial had finished (at 6-months) in terms of oral hygiene, gingival bleeding, health- and oral health-related quality of life. This provides further evidence of the value of the powered toothbrush and mouth rinsing programme supporting its widespread use. It would be useful to determine the effectiveness of longer oral hygiene care programmes in stroke rehabilitation. The study findings did not identify significant changes in the prevalence or viable counts of oral pathogens. Given that a key aim of oral hygiene care during stroke rehabilitation is to reduce opportunistic pathogens consideration of other chemical agents in controlling oral pathogens is warranted.

774012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774012.value: Following stroke the mouth typically becomes very unhealthy and this may effect recovery from stroke. A clinical trial was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of an advanced oral hygiene care programme (use of an electric toothbrush and a mouth rinse) versus a conventional oral hygiene care programme (use of a tooth brush). Both programme were effective in improving oral hygiene but the advance programme was more effective. The advanced programme was also more effective in reducing gum bleeding. Neither programme was effective in reducing oral pathogens (microorganisms). The advanced programme was more effective in improving physical health. Even after the clinical trial the effect of receiving the advanced oral hygiene care programme was evident in terms of improvement in oral hygiene level and gum bleeding at 6-months compared to those who received the conventional oral hygiene programme. They also fared better in terms of their health and oral health based on patients-own views. Neither programme was effective in reducing oral pathogens (microorganisms) levels at 6-months.

774212.value: 於妊娠早期，在母體血液循環系統的母體單核細胞遷移到孕期子宮內膜，分化成一種特殊類型的巨噬細胞，名為蛻膜巨噬細胞。 這些巨噬細胞佔妊娠子宮內白血細胞總數的百份之二十至三十。與其他組織中的巨噬細胞的功能相比，蛻膜巨噬細胞通過與其它免疫細胞和胚胎滋養層細胞的相互作用來調節母體免疫耐受和胎盤發育。蛻膜巨噬細胞的異常水平或活動與流產、胎兒宮內生長受限、先兆子癇等妊娠並發症有關。儘管蛻膜巨噬細胞在妊娠過程中有重要的作用，孕婦子宮中調控蛻膜巨噬細胞分化的因素仍不清楚。 胎盤蛋白14(Glycodelin-A)是一種在孕期子宮內膜很豐富的糖蛋白。它在母體對胚胎免疫耐受和胎盤發育起著重要的作用。同時它也調節宮腔內多種細胞的活性和分化。 顆粒巨噬细胞集落刺激因子(GM-CSF)誘導血液單核細胞分化為巨噬細胞。我們的未公佈的數據表明，在GM-CSF誘導單核細胞分化過程中加入glycodelin-A 所產生的巨噬細胞(glycodelin A極化的巨噬細胞)有許多與蛻膜巨噬細胞相似的特性，包括高水平吲哚胺2,3-雙加氧酶-1（IDO-1），白細胞介素-6，-1β和-10的表達。此外，與GM-CSF分化的巨噬細胞相比，Glycodelin-A-極化的巨噬細胞抑制外周血單個核細胞的增殖和滋養層細胞的入侵的能力更强。 IDO-1是一種參與在免疫耐受和組織重塑的免疫調節酶。先前的研究表明IDO-1抑製劑1-甲基-色氨酸會引起對胎兒的異體排斥。此外，宮內發育遲緩也證明與IDO-1水平降低有關。 我們假設glycodelin-A參與由人類單核細胞分化成蛻膜巨噬細胞的過程。我們將通過以下實驗証此假設：(1) 比較glycodelin A極化的巨噬細胞與從孕期子宮組織新鮮分離的蛻膜巨噬細胞; (2) 研究glycodelin-A和另一種已知的誘導單核細胞分化成蛻膜巨噬細胞的分子白細胞介素-10對誘導巨噬細胞的分化的共同作用; (3) 研究IDO-1 對glycodelin A極化的巨噬細胞的生物活性的作用; 以及 (4) 研究glycodelin-A如何增強IDO-1在巨噬細胞中的表達。 此項研究將提高我們對蛻膜巨噬細胞分化以及蛻膜巨噬細胞在妊娠免疫耐受和胎盤發育中作用的認識。它也可能為我們提供治療流產、胎兒宮內生長受限和先兆子癇的新策略。

774212.label: Realisation of objectives
774212.value: Glycodelin-A (GdA) is an abundant glycoprotein in the decidua during early pregnancy. It plays an important role in regulating the cellular activity of different immune cells that reside in the decidua. In this study, we hypothesize that decidual GdA polarize the differentiation of human monocyte into decidual macrophage. This action in turn regulates the immunotolerance toward fetal antigens and placental remodeling at the feto-maternal interface. There were 4 objectives in this project, and they had all been achieved. Objective 1. To compare decidual macrophages with GdA-polarized macrophages GdA was purified from amniotic fluid by affinity chromatography. Its identity was confirmed by tandem mass spectrometry. Insoluble particles and endotoxin were removed by a 0.22 μm filter and endotoxin removing kit, respectively. Buffy coats were obtained from Hong Kong Red Cross Blood Transfusion Service. Human monocytes were isolated from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and differentiated into macrophage for 9 days. Decidual macrophages and primary trophoblast was isolated from tissues obtained from patients undergoing surgical termination of first trimester pregnancy. Control macrophage (MCSF treatment alone), GdA-polarized macrophage (MCSF + GdA treatment), peripheral blood macrophage and decidual macrophage were submitted for expression profile analysis using microarray. The expression of M1, M2 and decidual macrophage markers was determined by flow cytometry. The cytokine profile of the macrophages was analyzed by membrane-based cytokine array and ELISA. Macrophages were co-cultured with autologous T-cells and primary trophoblast to study their effect to mediate immunotolerance toward fetal antigens and placenta remodeling, respectively. T-cell proliferation and cell cycle, trophoblast invasion and differentiation as well as macrophage phagocytosis were determined. Objective 2. To study the effect of GdA on IL-10-induced differentiation of monocyte Macrophage were differentiated by IL-10, GdA or both (Control macrophage, GdA-polarized macrophage, M2 macrophage [M-CSF + IL-10] and GdA-polarized M2 macrophage [M-CSF + IL-10 + GdA]). The expression of specific macrophage markers and the activities of these macrophage were determined by the methods described above. Objective 3. To determine the role of IDO-1 on the biological activities of GdA-polarized macrophages The IDO-1 expression in the macrophages were determined by qPCR and western blotting. The IDO-1 enzymatic activity was determined by the kynurenine assay, which measured a metabolic product of IDO-1 known as kynurenine. The role of macrophage-derived IDO-1 in the invasiveness of JEG-3 cells and proliferation of T-cells were studied using the IDO-1 competitive inhibitor L-1-methyl-tryptophan. Objective 4. To investigate the mechanisms of IDO-1-inducing activity of GdA The mechanism involved in GdA action was studied at two level. First, the involvement of 2 GdA receptors L-selectin and siglec-7 were determined by (1) immuno-precipitation with the recombinant form of the protein; (2) the expression of these 2 receptors on monocyte and macrophage surface; and (3) antibodies to block the fluorescence-labeled GdA on the monocytes and macrophage. Second, the intracellular pathways ERK and PKC were analyzed by western blot and PKC activity assay kit, respectively. The role of the ERK signaling molecules was confirmed by specific inhibitors.

774212.label: Major findings and research outcome
774212.value: - GdA treatment did not affect the viability of monocytes and macrophages (Lee et al., 2012). Compared to control macrophages, GdA-polarized macrophages have a higher IL-10 secretion. GdA-polarized macrophages inhibited the proliferation of autologous T-cells via induction of G0/G1 cell cycle arrest. It also inhibited invasion of trophoblast cell line JEG-3, which probably caused by the reduction of uPA expression and activity. GdA (Lee et al., 2016b). - The pathway analysis in microarray study shown that both GdA-polarized macrophage and decidual macrophage had up-regulated components of Wnt signaling pathway, tryptophan metabolism pathways and VEGF signaling pathway when compared to control macrophage and peripheral blood macrophage, respectively (Lee et al., 2016b). - GdA-polarized macrophage has increased IDO-1 and CD209, while M2 macrophage (polarized by IL-10) has increased NRP-1 and CD209 expression when compared to control macrophage. In GdA-polarized M2 macrophage, the expression of the 3 decidual macrophage markers increased significantly, which hints that GdA and IL-10 might induce a decidual macrophage like phenotype in a complementary manner (Lee et al., 2016b). - The spent medium from GdA-polarized macrophages exhibited a significantly higher level of CCL-2, IL-13 and IGFBP-1; factors critical in the early fetomaternal defense and placental development. GdA down regulated phagocytosis, similar to M2 macrophage (Lee et al., 2016b). - GdA-polarized macrophage exerts its suppressive effect on trophoblast invasion and T-cell proliferation via IDO-1 activities. The invasiveness of JEG-3 cells and proliferation of T-cells was down-regulated by IDO-1 inhibitor (Lee et al., 2016b). - GdA, but not recombinant glycodelin without glycosylation, induced IL-6 production in monocytes and macrophages. GdA interacts with L-selectin to induce IL-6 production from monocytes and macrophages by activating the PKC and ERKs signaling pathway. The increased IL-6 production, in turn, suppresses IFN-γ expression from T-helper cells, which may play an important role for inducing a Th-2 cytokine environment that flavors the immuno-tolerance of the fetoplacental unit (Lee et al., 2012). - GdA suppressed the secretion of TNF-γ by macrophages. The reduction of TNF-alpha relieving its otherwise-negative effects on sperm motility in sperm/macrophage co-culture. Removal of sialic acid from glycodelin-A abolishes this protective effect on sperm motility, which indicated the involvement of sialic acid-dependent receptors (such as L-selectin and siglec) may involved in regulating such effect (Lee et al., 2014). - GdA up-regulate the expression of HLAG in trophoblast (Lee et al., 2016a). Using recombinant HLAG, our date shown that HLAG has similar action as GdA to drove the differentiation of macrophages towards the decidual macrophage lineage, including reduced expression of M1 macrophage marker CD86, increased expression of M2 macrophage marker CD163 and higher expression and activity of decidual macrophage marker IDO-1. It also have similar effect to GdA-polarized macrophage such as inhibit autologous T-cells proliferation, increase trophoblast invasion and enhanced phagocytosis and increased secretion of IL-6 (Lee et al., 2015).

774212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774212.value: 1. In addition to regulates feto-maternal defence, one major role of decidual macrophage is to promote spiral arteries remodeling. Decidual macrophage interacts with the endothelial cells and endovascular trophoblast in spiral arteries by secretion of various vascular regulatory factors. We are currently studying the effect of GdA on decidual macrophage-mediated spiral artery remodeling. 2. Based on the important role of GdA in regulating immune cell and trophoblast functions during early pregnancy, it is reasonable to speculate that deficiency in the normal functions of GdA may contribute to the pathophysiology of various pregnancy-associated diseases. We have started to determine the placental expression of GdA and its receptors in the pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia, intrauterine growth restriction and gestational trophoblastic disease. 3. We have shown that GdA binding to L-selectina and siglec-7 to monocyte and macrophage via carbohydrate recognition. Removal of sialic acid, the outmost sugar residue of the glycan chain, has demonstrated to abolish the GdA binding ability as well as the GdA-mediated biological functions. In a recent study on its molecular structure using x-ray crystallography indicated a unique structure of glycodelin in presenting its glycan chains. Further study of glycodelin with homogeneous glycan structure is required to define the mechanistic aspects of these GdA-derived glycans.

774212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774212.value: Macrophages comprise 20-30% of the leukocytes in the pregnant uterus. The monocytes migrate from bloodstream into the decidualized endometrium and differentiate into decidua-specific macrophages upon exposure to the local microenvironment. Decidual macrophages secrete immunomodulatory factors that contributes to immune tolerance. Aberrant levels of decidual macrophages are associated with fetal loss and pregnancy complications. Despite its importance in pregnancy, little is known about the factors regulating differentiation of decidual macrophages. Glycodelin-A (GdA) is a decidua-abundant glycoprotein regulators immune cell function. The project tested the hypothesis that decidual GdA polarize the differentiation of human decidual macrophage in the deciduas. Our results clearly demonstrated the role of decidual GdA in driving the monocyte differentiation into a decidual macrophage-like phenotype, which promotes fetomaternal tolerance and placental development via indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase, chemokines, cytokines and angiogenic factors. The project also studied the mechanism of action of GdA on macrophage differentiation. The outcome of this project gives a better understanding on the differentiation of decidual macrophage, and the role of decidual macrophage in pregnancy. In long term, the present findings enhance our understanding of the cause of pregnancy loses and provide the basis for development of new treatment strategies.

774712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
774712.value: The discovery of induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells offers us a new source of adult pluripotent stem cells that can be used in patient-specific cell replacement therapy or to establish cell models for understanding of disease pathogenesis. One challenge of iPS cell technology is to ensure the pluripotent nature of the reprogrammed cells and also to manipulate their differentiation to a desired cell lineage. Because epigenetic regulations, such as DNA methylation and histone modifications, are crucial in regulating gene expression patterns and maintaining a cell identity, it is believed that epigenetic reprogramming is a key event in redirecting a differentiated cell fate to the pluripotent iPS cell state. Previously we have discovered the phenomenon of epigenetic memory and identified the crucial function of H3.3, a histone H3 variant, in maintaining the expression of donor differentiation genes using somatic cell nuclear transfer reprogramming approach. Our findings demonstrated that removal of H3.3 methylation at lysine 4 position leads to an erasure of heritable epigenetic memory, thus promoting a reversal of differentiated cell status. Recent studies have also revealed a significant number of transcribed genes in iPS cells that have a similar expression pattern to the parental differentiated cells, indicating an inheritance of parental memory. The memory status in iPS cells has been found partially associated with DNA methylation. However, its effect on the functional competence of iPS cells generated from different parental cell types remains controversial. Based on our previous findings, we hypothesize that methylation of H3.3 is a major mechanisms of maintaining an active epigenetic memory in iPS cells that subsequently affects the differentiation plasticity. We aim to manipulate the differentiation plasticity of iPS cell through the memory status of parental cells. Overexpression of H3.3 in parental cells would allow us to consolidate the memory status in iPS cells, which can efficiently induce iPS cell differentiation to a desired cell type for transplantation purposes, and thus eliminate the risk of teratoma formation in the recipient. In contrast, removal of H3.3 lysine 4 methylation in parental cells would erase epigenetic memory, which can be used to generate “memory-less” iPS cells for disease modeling and stem cell banking. Studies on the epigenetic memory in iPS cells can provide novel insights on the regulation of stem cell differentiation plasticity, which will expand our knowledge of the functional normality of iPS cells and lead to more efficient clinical applications of iPS cell technology. 誘導性多功能幹細胞的發現為我們提供了一個新的成熟多功能幹細胞來源。這些細胞可以被用於患者特異性細胞替代治療或建立研究疾病發病機理的細胞模型。誘導性多功能幹細胞技術的關鍵在於使這些重新編程的細胞能夠保持多功能性并能操縱他們分化成為我們想要的細胞類型。因為諸如DNA的甲基化和組蛋白修飾的表觀遺傳調節在基因表達和維持細胞特性中起重要作用，表觀遺傳重組被認為是將分化狀態的細胞重新轉化為誘導性多功能幹細胞過程中的一個關鍵環節。以前我們發現了表觀遺傳記憶現象并通過體細胞核置換重組技術證實了組蛋白異構體H3.3在維持供體分化基因表達中的重要作用。我們的發現證明了去除組蛋白異構體H3.3第四個賴氨酸的甲基化將清除那些可遺傳的表觀遺傳記憶，進而促進分化細胞狀態的逆轉。最近的一些研究也發現在誘導性多功能幹細胞中大量的轉錄基因具有與分化母細胞相似的表達模式，這也說明了母體記憶的可遺傳性。誘導性多功能幹細胞中遺傳記憶狀態也被發現與DNA的甲基化有部份的聯繫。然而這些對從分化的母細胞轉化成為的誘導性多功能幹細胞的功能影響仍然存有爭議。基於我們之前的發現，我們推測H3.3的甲基化是維持誘導性多功能幹細胞表觀遺傳記憶的主要機制。這些遺傳記憶會影響後來分化過程的可塑性。我們的目標是通過調節母體細胞的記憶狀態來影響誘導性多功能幹細胞的分化可塑性。在母體細胞中超表達H3.3可以使我們鞏固誘導性多功能幹細胞的記憶狀態進而有效的誘導多功能幹細胞分化成需要的細胞類型來用於臨床移植。這也可以消除在受體中形成畸胎瘤的風險。相反，在母體細胞中去除H3.3第四位賴氨酸的甲基化可以清除表觀遺傳記憶并用來產生“無記憶”的誘導性多功能幹細胞以供建立疾病模型和幹細胞庫。對於誘導性多功能幹細胞的表觀遺傳記憶研究可以為理解幹細胞分化的可塑性調節提供新的視角，也可以擴展我們對誘導性多功能幹細胞正常功能的認識并使得誘導性多功能幹細胞的臨床應用更為有效。

774712.label: Realisation of objectives
774712.value: For objective 1, we have constructed a gene targeting construct with a 3x HA sequence being incorporated into the 3’ end of mouse H3.3a genomic sequence (obtained from BAC clone). The constructed H3.3-HA sequence was electroporated into mouse embryonic stem cell (ESC) line L4 for homologous recombination. The recombinant cells were undergone neomycin selection. Individual clones were picked and expanded. Real-time RT-PCR confirmed the expression of H3.3-HA in the ESC clones and Southern blot analysis confirmed the single 3x-HA insertion at the H3.3a locus. Differentiation of the ESC to hematopoietic and neural lineages was optimized. Differentiated H3.3-HA cells were isolated by cell sorting and subject to ChIP-seq analysis using anti-HA antibody, which reflects the H3.3 enrichment pattern in the reprogrammed cells. The ChIP-seq results demonstrated H3.3 enrichment in a number of gene loci that were active in the hematopoietic or neural lineage in the reprogrammed iPSC, indicating that H3.3 is involved in the epigenetic memeory of iPSC. For objective 2, H3.3 gene was cloned into a Tet-On lentiviral overexpression plasmid. It has been shown feasible to overexpress H3.3 gene in mammalian cells by lentiviral gene delivery system. H3.3 was then overexpressed in ESC, followed by hematopoietic or neural differentiation. The H3.3-overexpressing differentiated ESCs were subjected to iPSC reprogrammed and HA-H3.3 ChIP experiment. Our results demonstrated further enrichment of H3.3 at the parental lineage gene loci and this was associated with higher degree of parental lineage gene expression in the iPSC. Therefore, these results suggest overexpression of H3.3 in the parental lineage cells can consolidate the memory status in iPSC. For objective 3, a H3.3 K4 mutation was introduced into the H3.3 inducible lentiviral plasmid. By inducing overexpression of the H3.3 K4 mutant in hematopoietic or neural differentiated ESC and during the iPSC reprogramming period, we noticed that the efficiency of reprogramming dropped significantly. By analyzing the very limited number of iPSC clones, we found high degree of variability of H3.3 enrichment between clones. One clone demonstrated loss of H3.3 enrichment at the parental lineage gene loci, while the other two clones demonstrated random patterns of H3.3 enrichment. It is therefore uncertain if the H3.3 K4 mutant was sufficient to erase the H3.3-mediated epigenetic memory at this stage. We hypothesize that in combination of the manipulation of other histone variants or DNA methylation may lead to more complete erasure of epigenetic memory in the iPSC.

774712.label: Major findings and research outcome
774712.value: The major findings of this project included: 1) we demonstrated the involvement of H3.3 binding at the parental lineage gene loci is important to the epigenetic memory of iPSC; 2) we can consolidate the degree of iPSC epigenetic memory by introducing H3.3 binding to the parental cells before reprogramming; 3) depleting functional H3.3, although not completed, can partially erase the degree of epigenetic memory in the reprogrammed iPSC clone. We believe our findings can provide valuable information on the reprogramming strategy in the iPSC technology. The outcomes of this project are: 1) this work was presented as poster presentation in two international conferences: The Croucher Foundation Advanced Study Institute (ASI) on Stem Cells: Biology and Applications at Hong Kong in 2015, and EMBO conference: Chromatin and Epigenetics at Germany in 2015; 2) a manuscript based on the findings from this study is attached with this report, which will be submitted in the coming month.

774712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774712.value: Based on the epigenomic and transcriptomic analyses, we have identified several candidate genes which could play important role leading to the biased differentiation plasticity of iPSC derived from different parental cell types. Our project provides clues in the mechanism of epigenetic memory in iPSC, which could potentially be utilized to enhance the efficiency of iPSC cell differentiation to a lineage of interest.

774712.value: The discovery of induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells offers us a new source of adult pluripotent stem cells that can be used in patient-specific cell replacement therapy or to establish cell models for understanding of disease pathogenesis. It is believed that epigenetic reprogramming is a key event in redirecting a differentiated cell fate to the pluripotent iPS cell state. Our work has shown that the binding of a histone H3 variant, H3.3, at the parental lineage gene loci is associated with the persistent expression of parental lineage genes in the reprogrammed iPS cells, which is referred to the epigenetic memory. The parental memory in iPS cells can be consolidated by overexpression of H3.3 in the parental cells before reprogramming. In contrast, disabling the wild-type H3.3 function through overexpression of a H3.3 lysine 4 mutant demonstrated partial incompleted erasure of epigenetic memory in iPS cells. Studies on the epigenetic memory in iPS cells can provide novel insights on the regulation of stem cell differentiation plasticity, which will expand our knowledge of the functional normality of iPS cells and lead to more efficient clinical applications of iPS cell technology.

775712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775712.value: Nucleotide excision repair (NER) is a versatile DNA repair system that can remove a wide variety of DNA lesions caused by UV irradiation and bulky chemical adducts which result from exposure to environmental factors or chemotherapeutic drugs. In humans, defects in nucleotide excision repair proteins can cause several genetic disorders such as xeroderma pigmentosum, Cockayne syndrome and trichothiodystrophy. More than 30 proteins have been demonstrated to be involved in NER process. The detail molecular mechanism by which these proteins cooperate to fulfill their functions on damaged DNA remains largely elusive. XPA participates in multiple steps of NER pathway from damage recognition to dual incision. Besides binding to DNA, XPA can interact with a number of NER core factors including RPA, ERCC1, DDB2 and TFIIH. The importance of XPA is underscored by a simple fact that in the absence of XPA, stable pre-incision complex is not formed, thus NER cannot occur. Although the interaction among XPA, RPA and the damaged DNA has been extensively studied during the past decade, the roles of two proteins in NER pathway remain controversial. In addition, our in vitro binding data showed that XPA physically interacts with PCNA, a clamp protein that is supposed to be recruited to facilitate gap-filling DNA synthesis in the post-incision stage. This observation indicates that PCNA is important not only in the DNA re-synthesis step but also in other steps of NER. The molecular mechanism and functional significance of this interaction remain elusive. Furthermore, XPA has recently been revealed to physically interact with damaged DNA binding protein DDB2, and the interaction is required for the stimulatory effect of DDB on CPD excision in vitro. The direct interaction between XPA and DDB2 raised the possibility that XPA may participate in early steps of NER process. In this project we will develop a new structure-based paradigm for functional profiling of XPA including the following aims: (i) To determine the crystal structure of XPA-MBD/RPA70AB/Y-shaped DNA ternary complex; (ii) To elucidate the molecular mechanism of interaction between PCNA and XPA; (iii) To characterize the molecular interaction between DDB2 and XPA. The results from our proposed study will provide important insights into the mechanism by which XPA serves as an accessory protein to coordinate with RPA, PCNA, DDB2 and other core factors in DNA damage recognition and incision. The completed study will contribute to a better understanding of the molecular basis of NER-associated human diseases. 核苷酸切除修复(NER)是一个能修复多种类型的DNA损伤的通路，可以除去各种紫外线照射和化疗药物所导致的DNA损伤。核苷酸切除修复蛋白的缺陷可能会导致一些遗传性疾病如着色性干皮病(XP)，科凯恩综合征(CS)和发硫失养症(TTD)。已发现超过30个蛋白参与核苷酸切除修复过程，但这些蛋白质如何相互协作去修复受损DNA的详细的分子机制仍不十分清晰。 XPA参与了NER机制的多个步骤，包括损伤识别及DNA单链双切。除了结合DNA，XPA还能与一系列参与NER过程的重要蛋白如RPA，ERCC1，DDB2及TFIIH有相互作用。如果缺失XPA，NER修复路径会受阻，因此XPA的重要性不言而喻。尽管XPA与受损DNA及RPA的相互作用在过去十几年中被广泛研究，但其在NER通路中的具体作用仍有争议。另外，我们开展的体外结合实验结果表明XPA与PCNA有直接相互作用。PCNA一般被认为在NER通路后期的填补切口及修复合成中出现及发挥作用，所以我们的初始数据暗示PCNA可能介入了NER过程的不同步骤。PCNA与XPA相互作用的机制及意义仍需进一步探索与开展。鉴于此我们希望在项目支持期间完成以下目标：(1) 解析XPA，受损DNA及同RPA的作用，并期获得复合物的三维晶体结构 。 (2) 阐明PCNA和XPA之间的相互作用机制。我们的研究结果将为XPA，作为一个辅助蛋白，如何协同RPA,PCNA及其他核心蛋白去识别，切除并修复DNA损伤提供重要的信息。这也将有助于我们进一步了解与NER相关的疾病的分子机制。

775712.label: Realisation of objectives
775712.value: (i) Previously, we carried out fluorescence polarization assay to identify the Y-shaped DNA fragment binds to both XPA-MBD and RPA70AB with relatively stronger binding affinity. Based on the NMR titration & chemical shift assignments of both XPA-MBD and RPA70AB domans, we were able to figure out that XPA-MBD and the Y-shaped DNA fragment bind to the different region of RPA70AB surface. Interestingly, this observation is dinstinct from a previous report. We also setup crystallization screening for the tertiary complex of XPA-MBD, RPA70AB and Y-shape DNA fragment. We have obtained microcrystals of the XPA-MBD/RPA70AB/Y-shaped DNA ternary complex. But we faced the challenge to grow the high-quality crystals ready for the diffration data collection even though we tried a number of stategies such as screening Y-shaped DNA fragments with different length, using addictive screening and microseeding. (ii) Built on the preliminary data, we expanded the objective to study the interaction of RPA heterotrimer with XPA-MBD and Y-shaped DNA fragments. We purified RPA heterotrimer which essentially contains RPA70 that lacks N-terminal 181 amino acids, RPA32 that lacks N-terminal 42 residues and full-length RPA14 expressed in E. coli. We put tremendous efforts into crystallizing the RPA heterotrimer together with XPA-MBD and Y-shaped DNA fragment, and we have got two-dimentional flake crystals. The crystal optimization is underway. (iii) It is well established that PCNA recruits DNA polymerase δ and/or polymerase ε for the DNA re-synthesis step of nucleotide excision repair. Interestingly, our preliminary data from pull-down assay and NMR titration confirmed that PCNA physically interacts with XPA in vitro, raising the possibility that PCNA may play multiple roles in NER pathway. We further identified XPA contains APIM motif which serves as a putative PCNA binding motif as summarized in a previous report. In addition, a recent functional study has also demonstrated that XPA interacts with PCNA at replication foci, suggesting nucleotide excision repair plays a role in UV-induced post-replication repair. Intriguingly, the cell-based assay has shown a large portion of PCNA is ubiquitinated when being pulled down with proteins containing APIM motif. Considering that PCNA ubiquitination is required for post-replication repair, we were interested to know if the interaction between PCNA and XPA is modulated by post-translational modification, especially ubiquitination. We have established the protocol for large-scale synthesis of mono-ubiquitinated PCNA, and we have evaluated if ubiquitination on PCNA have any effect on the association with XPA-MBD domain. Based on our observation from the NMR titration, we found that PCNA ubiquitination does not affect its binding to XPA-MBD domain. We then focused on the crystallization of PCNA with a short fragment of XPA that contains a putative PCNA-interacting motif, but we have the difficulty in obtaining the crystals. It happened that I met an international expert who shares the similar research interest at a DNA repair conference. I realised that his lab has difficulty crystallizing PCNA with APIM motif as well. So we extended this objective by studying the molecular basis of ubiquitinated PCNA interaction with another EBV viral protein BPLF1, as highlighted in the mid-term report. Now we have successfully determined the crystal structure of BPLF1 deubiquitinase domain in complex with ubiquitin, we expect a manuscript will be put together soon.

775712.label: Major findings and research outcome
775712.value: We have previously provided the molecular basis of XPA interaction with RPA subunit RPA32 (Part C, research output No. 1). Then we further identified that XPA can also interact with RPA70 subunit by using fluorescence polarisation and NMR titration. Furthermore, we provided evidence that XPA-MBD domain specifically interacts with RPA70AB domain and this interaction does not interfere with the DNA binding. We went on to crystallise XPA-MBD domain in complex with RPA70AB domain and Y-shaped DNA fragment. We also put tremendous efforts into structural analysis of RPA heterotrimer in complex with XPA-MBD domain and DNA fragment, we have successfully got crystals of the complex, currently the crystal optimization is underway. We also identified that XPA binds to PCNA, but the binding is relatively weak, which might explained why we haven't obtained the crystals of PCNA in complex with XPA APIM motif after extensive trials. But we have extended this objective and identified that a EBV viral protein BPLF1 can efficiently deubiquitinate ubiquitinated PCNA in vitro, and suspected that PCNA deubiquitination might facilitate viral infection. We went on to crystallise the BPLF1 deubiquitinase domain in complex with ubiquitin, and recently have successfully determined the crystal structure of this complex. This structure actually lays a foundation for us to design inhibitor to block BPLF1 enzymatic activity and protect the host from acute EBV infection. This funding also provided the critical support for us to develop further in the area of DNA damage response, especially for me as a junior faculty member. We have two other publications (Part C, research output No. 2 & 3) directly benefited from this funding support.

775712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775712.value: As mentioned, we are expanding the objectives and have crystallised RPA heterotrimer in complex with XPA-MBD and Y-shaped DNA fragment, we are currently working hard to optimise the crystals and if successful, the results will provide critical insights into the mechanism by which XPA coordinate with RPA in the DNA damage recognition and incision. We have also obtained the crystal structure of BPLF1 deubiquitinase domain in complex with ubiquitin, we are making BPLF1 mutants to verify structural findings. At the same time, the structural findings will facilitate our functional design to decipher the role of BPLF1 in early viral infection. Lastly, based on this structure, we can apply structure-based drug design to develop some inhibitors to block BPLF1 deubiquitinase activity, which might have implications in drug development against acute EBV infection.

775712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775712.value: Faithful transmission of genetic information from parent to daughter cells is central for eukaryotic life. However, eukaryotic cells are constantly facing challenges from both environmental insults and endogenous toxins, defects in DNA replication pathways are a major cause of cancers and premature aging. Nucleotide excision repair, as one of the major DNA repair pathways in eukaryotic cells, plays a major role in eliminating helix-distorting lesions caused by environmental agents such as Ultraviolet light (UV)-induced cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs) and pyrimidine-pyrimidone (6-4) photoproducts (6-4PPs). Defects in NER can lead to the inherited multisystem disorders such as xeroderma pigmentosum (XP), Cockayne syndrome (CS) and trichothiodystrophy (TTD). Patients with XP exhibit an extreme sensitivity to sunlight and have more than 1000-fold increased risk to develop skin cancer. Approximately 20% of XP patients suffered from neurological symptoms. We combined X-ray crystallography, macromolecular NMR and biochemical approaches to study the human XPA-containing complexes that are key intermediates in the lesion recognition and excision steps of nucleotide excision repair pathway. The obtained data as well as ongoing study should provide critical insights into the early steps of nucleotide excision repair pathway, and further our understanding of molecular basis of NER-associated human diseases.

775812.label: Realisation of objectives
775812.value: Objective 1 was to investigate the synergistic induction of LTB4DH expression at the cellular level. Through a bioactivity-guided fractionation procedure, we isolated gallic acid from Radix Paeoniae Rubra, L-leucine, calycosin and formononetin) from Radix Astragali (Wei L et al, 2011; Cheng YY et al, 2015). All fractions were assayed by RT-PCR and Western blotting techniques. LTB4DH induction was verified by commercial gallic acid in combination with L-leucine, calycosin or formononetin. We subsequently investigated the effects of LTB4DH inducers on the activities of human neutrophils (Cheng YY et al, 2015). After treatment with LTB4DH inducers, human neutrophils were assayed for chemotaxis in Transwell plate and cell apoptosis by FITC-Annexin V staining. Gallic acid and calycosin in combination suppressed LTB4-induced chemotaxis and cell survival of neutrophils. We further synthesized gallic acid-L-leucine conjugate. Interestingly, gallic acid-L-leucine conjugate effectively induced LTB4DH expression in a concentration- and time dependent manner (Cheng YY et al, manuscript 1). Importantly, gallic acid-L-leucine conjugate suppressed the production of inflammatory mediators (e.g., NO, PGE2, LTB4 and TXB2) in activated macrophages. Collectively, LTB4DH inducers may help resolution of inflammation via modulating inflammatory response in neutrophils and macrophages. Objective 2 was to elucidate the molecular mechanism underlying LTB4DH induction. We examined the effects of gallic acid, L-leucine, calycosin, formononetin and gallic acid-L-leucine conjugate on various signaling pathways including various MAP kinases, PKC, GSK-3β, Nrf2/HO-1, NF-kB and AP-1. We initially found that the active compounds may induce LTB4DH via PI3K and p38 pathways. In particular, gallic acid may target ROS-sensitive p38 pathway, whereas formononetin, calycosin, gallic acid L-leucine conjugate may modulate PKC, ERK and PI3K/Akt pathways, leading to the activation of Nrf2/HO-1 pathway and inhibition of NF-kB and AP-1 pathways (Cheng YY et al 2015; Cheng YY et al manuscript 1 and 2). Utimately, the activation of Nrf2/HO-1 pathway is the major mechanism supporting the induction of LTB4DH expression. Objective 3 was to evaluate the in vivo cardioprotective effects of LTB4DH inducers. We have evaluated LTB4DH inducers in two different models of myocardial infarction induced by isoproterenol injection and coronary ligation (Cheng YY et al, 2015; Cheng YY et al, manuscript 2). Regardless of drug administration, intraperitoneally or by oral gavage, gallic acid, L-leucine, calycosin and formononetin were readily absorbed into the circulation system. We have found that gallic acid in combination with L-leucine, calycosin or formononetin could effectively suppress neutrophil infiltration and reduce infarct size in two mouse models of myocardial infarction.

775812.label: Major findings and research outcome
775812.value: LTB4DH is an important multi-functional enzyme for metabolizing/detoxifying exogenous and endogenous toxic and pro-inflammatory lipid mediators including LTB4. Pharmacological induction of LTB4DH represents a novel approach for resolution of inflammation in myocardial infarction and other inflammatory diseases. In the present project, we focused on the identification of the active compounds from Chinese medicines Radix Peoniae rubrae and Radix Astragali for synergistic induction of LTB4DH. We subsequently characterized the molecular mechanisms underlying the synergy of GA with L-leucine, calycosin or formonotetin. We also verified the in vivo cardioprotective effects of LTB4DH inducers in myocardial infarction models induced by either isoproterenol injection or coronary ligation. 1) Major findings: We have identified gallic acid from Radix Peoniae Rubr and three active compounds (i.e., L-leucine, calycosin and formononetin) from Radix Astragali following the initial bioactivity-guided fractionation in HepG2 cells as the cellular detector. As outlined in Publication 1 and 2, our strategy is especially useful to identify two or multiple compounds for the synergistic regulation of gene expression such as LTB4DH. We believe that this approach will be adapted as a general strategy for molecular characterization of complex Chinese medicines. Publication 1 and 2 confirmed that gallic acid in combination with L-leucine, calycosine or formononetin could effectively induce LTB4DH expression. Our results suggested that LTB4DH inducers not only attenuated the survival and chemotaxis of neutrophils in response to LTB4 stimulation, but also suppressed the oncogenic transformation of HepG2 cells and the polarization of macrophages (Paper 1, 2 and 3). Importantly, we also found that LTB4DH inducers could effectively reduce neutrophil infiltration and infarct size in rodent model of myocardial infarction (Paper 2 and 4). Moreover, we also generated a new gallic acid L-leucine (GAL) conjugate by direct amidation of gallic acid with L-leucine. We found that GAL could inhibit the production of pro-inflammatory mediators (e.g., Nitric oxide, LTB4, PGE2 and TXBA2) in activated macrophages. In summary, we have demonstrated that LTB4DH inducers may be useful for resolution of inflammation and cardioprotection in myocardial infarction. 2) Research outcome: We have generated 4 peer-reviewed publications, two submitted manuscripts, one patent application and 4 conference abstracts. We have also trained 3 PhD students: two students successfully completed their thesis defense, whereas one is still working on the further development of the proposed studies in GRF grant.

775812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775812.value: The present study demonstrated a novel mechanism for resolution of inflammation in myocardial infarction through specific degradation other than formation and action of the key pro-inflammatory mediator leukotriene B4 (LTB4). Importantly, specific control of LTB4 level was achieved by synergistic induction of LTB4DH with two natural products (i.e., GA in combination with L-leucine, calycosin or formononetin). These results may lead to three important scientific questions: 1) How critical is LTB4DH induction in the cardioprotective effects of LTB4DH inducers? 2) Can LTB4DH inducers affect the survival, growth and differentiation of other cell types (e.g., macrophages, cardiomyocytes and endothelial cells)? 3) Can LTB4DH inducers exhibit similar therapeutic effects in human subjects? To address Question 1, we may acquire the transgenic techniques to generate a strain of LTB4DH-knockout mouse, and subsequently investigate the cardioprotective effects of LTB4DH inducers in LTB4DH deficient mice. Question 2 actually means many research projects down in the road towards the better understanding on the importance of LTB4DH induction. To address Question 3, we need to initiate clinical research on the pharmacological potential of LTB4DH inducers. It is noteworthy that the present project may pave the avenue for future characterization of Chinese medicines for the treatment of myocardial infarction.

775812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775812.value: The aim of the present study was to discover a novel mechanism by which inflammation in myocardial infarction could be resolved by specific degradation other than the formation and action of the key proinflammatory mediator leukotriene B4 (LTB4). The present study investigated whether Chinese medicines could induce the metabolic enzyme LTB4 12-hydroxydehydrogenase (LTB4DH) for specific degradation of LTB4. We initially achieved the pharmacological induction of LTB4DH by two Chinese medicines Radix Peaonae Rubra and Radix Astragali. We subsequently identified GA, L-leucine, calycosin and formononetin as the active compounds from the specific herbal extracts. We further demonstrated that GA in combination with L-leucine, calycosin or formononetin could not only attenuate chemotaxis and survival of neutrophils in response to LTB4, but also significantly reduce neutrophil infiltration and infarct size in a rat model of myocardial infarction. Moreover, we learned that LTB4DH inducers could regulate different signaling pathways towards synergistic induction of LTB4DH. These results demonstrated that specific degradation of LTB4 could effectively resolve inflammation in myocardial infarction. Importantly, the present study also suggests that molecular characterization of Chinese medicines not only improve current understanding the gene regulation by multiple compounds but also leads to the discovery of novel therapies for myocardial infarction.

775912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775912.value: 摘要 下腰痛（Low Back Pain）是全球導致殘疾的主因，對社會經濟和公共醫療系統都構成負面影響。而椎間盤退變是導致下腰痛的致病因素。椎間盤的退變可分為化學性和結構性的轉變，其中身體的“炎症反應”屬於化學性的轉變﹐它會加速椎間盤退變和並令痛楚加劇。椎間盤退變有多方面的風險因素，包括遺傳﹑系統性（如新陳代謝改變)﹑和環境因素。根據一個中國南方人的大型研究發現，超重和肥胖顯著增加青少年和成人患上椎間盤退變的機會和嚴重程度。 超重和肥胖問題已受到全球性的關注﹐ 情況亦越來越普遍。然而真正影響健康的並不是體重（BMI），而是肥胖（脂肪）。積存在腹部的脂肪越多﹐患上癌症﹑二型糖尿病﹑心臟疾病，免疫系統疾病，退化性關節炎﹑和下腰痛的風險是亦會越高。以往人們假定椎間盤退變是由於肥胖增加了下腰部的負重量。然而，非負重區的椎間盤退變正正為這個假定提出了反證。反之﹐腹部脂肪的屯積會增加脂肪細胞因子(Adipokines) 的生產，這些細胞因子是重要的代謝介質﹐而且能促使炎症發生。因此，脂肪細胞因子亦可能促使椎間盤的退化﹐並引致下腰痛。 研究人員根據一個中國南方人的大型研究﹐確定了遺傳﹑代謝和環境因素為椎間盤退變的主要因素。本研究將利用磁力共震素描﹐了解脂肪細胞因子和椎間盤退變的關係。這一項研究將分析1,000名參加者的脂肪細胞因子數量和中央肥胖情況﹐與其椎間盤退變的嚴重程度﹐以及其他脊柱畸形和痛楚的關係。在以大型人口研究識別出脂肪細胞因子和椎間盤退變的關係後﹐研究人員將進行體外培植脂肪細胞和血清﹐在不同的肥胖類別中評估脂肪細胞因子對健康的動物纖維環和髓核細胞的直接影響。這些研究將幫助我們理解脂肪細胞因子對椎間盤的影響，而研究結果將有助於進行世上第一個關於基因-脂因子-代謝-環境 （IGAME）與椎間盤退變的相關性研究。

776312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776312.value: The Iroquois homeobox (Irx) genes encode the TALE (three amino acid loop extension) class of homeodomain-containing transcription factors. In Drosophila the iroquois genes were identified as prepatterning genes that provide positional information to facilitate the proper sensory organ development. The functions of Irx genes in mammalian development are not well known. The Irx3 and Irx5 genes are two linked genes on mouse chromosome 8, they have overlapping expression patterns in the developing inner ear. To investigate the functions of Irx3 and Irx5 genes, we have generated several reporter knock-in mutant mouse lines: Irx3lacZ, Irx5EGFP, and a double mutant mouse line Irx3-Irx5EGFP. Both the Irx3 and Irx5 single mutant mouse strains display hearing impairment, but the Irx3/5 double mutant die before birth. Our initial phenotype analysis shows that the Irx3/5 double knockout mutant has a shortened cochlea and an increased number of hair cells. In the mutant cochlear epithelium, the positions of the sensory domain and the lesser epithelial ridge are shifted, the greater epithelial ridge is missing. In addition, the coordinated temporal and spatial control of cell proliferation and prosensory gene expression appears abnormal. The novel phenotype of the Irx3/5 double mutant suggests that the Irx3 and Irx5 genes play essential roles in patterning the cochlea epithelium and are required for the specification of sensory and non-sensory cell fates. The aim of this project is to elucidate the roles of Irx3 and Irx5 genes in mammalian inner ear development. We will generate an additional inner ear specific conditional Irx3/5 double mutant to circumvent the embryonic lethality. We will analysis the abnormal inner ear phenotypes of the Irx3 and Irx5 mouse mutants. We will identify the genes and pathways regulated by Irx3 and Irx5 in patterning the cochlear epithelium and in determining sensory cell fate. An Irx3/5 mediated genetic regulatory pathway for patterning the cochlear epithelium and regulating sensory cell fate will be constructed in this study. This is the first study of the conserved function of Iroquois genes in mammalian species in tissue patterning for sensory organ development. The results of this project will shed light on the mechanisms underlying sensory and non-sensory cell fate decision, which will contribute to our understanding of the pathogenesis of human hearing disorders. Iroquois （Irx）基因編碼TALE類同源框轉錄因子。在果蠅中，Iroquois基因是前模式構建基因，它們提供位置信息並促進感覺器官發育。Irx基因在哺乳動物發育中的功能仍不明確。Irx3和Irx5基因在小鼠8號染色體上連鎖，並在內耳發育中具有重疊的表達模式。為了研究Irx3和Irx5基因的功能， 我們構建了一系列報告基因敲入突變體小鼠：Irx3LacZ，Irx5EGFP，以及一個雙突變小鼠Irx3-Irx5EGFP。Irx3和Irx5單突變小鼠均表現出聽力損傷，然而Irx3/5雙突變小鼠會在出生之前死亡。初步的表型分析顯示Irx3/5雙敲除突變體具有較短的耳蝸和較多的內耳毛細胞。在這一突變體的耳蝸上皮細胞中，感覺域和小上皮嵴移位，同時大上皮嵴喪失。此外，細胞增殖和前感覺基因表達的時空調控表現異常。Irx3/5雙突變體的獨特表型表明Irx3和Irx5基因在耳蝸上皮細胞模式構建以及感覺和非感覺細胞命運特化的過程中具有重要作用。 這一研究旨在闡明Irx3和Irx5基因在哺乳動物內耳發育中的作用。我們會構建一種在內耳中特異性敲除Irx3/5的雙突變小鼠以避免胚胎期的小鼠死亡。我們將分析Irx3和Irx5小鼠突變體的異常內耳表型，並識別在耳蝸上皮細胞模式構建和感覺細胞命運決定中被Irx3和Irx5調控的基因或通路。 在本研究中，一條由Irx3/5介導的調控耳蝸上皮細胞模式建成和感覺細胞命運特化的基因調控通路將被勾勒出來。這是功能保守的Iroquois基因在哺乳動物感覺器官發育的組織模式構建中的首個研究。這一研究的結果將闡明感覺和非感覺細胞命運決定的根本機制，並有助於我們理解人類聽力障礙的發病機理。

776312.label: Realisation of objectives
776312.value: Objective 1. To identify the multiple roles of Irx3 and Irx5 in inner ear development through analysis of morphological defects of a series of Irx3 and Irx5 mouse mutants A. Cellular expression patterns of Irx3 and Irx5 in the inner ear The aim of this project was to dissect the roles of Irx3 and Irx5 in inner ear development. We first examined the dynamic expression profiles of the Irx3 and Irx5 genes. Using the reporter mouse lines, by X-gal staining and immunostaining of Irx3lacZ/+ and Irx5EGFP/+ embryos, as well as by RNA in situ hybridization of wildtype and mutant embryos, we have analysed the expression patterns of Irx3 and Irx5 in the developing mouse cochlea from E9.5 to E18.5. Both of the Irx genes were expressed in the prosensory domain of the otocyst. Irx3 continued to express in broad regions of the cochlear epithelium at later stages (E12.5-16.5), but Irx5 became restricted to non-sensory regions of the GER, LER and lateral sulcus from E14.5 onwards. Irx3 and Irx5 overlap in multiple cochlear epithelial cell types, but also display distinctive expression patterns in the organ of Corti. B. Morphological defects of Irx3 and Irx5 mutant inner ears Using a variety of experimental platforms including histological sections, immunostaining with cell type specific markers, cell proliferation assays by BrdU labelling, whole mount paint-filling experiments, scanning electron microscopy and dye tracing experiments, we have investigated the inner ear phenotypes of the single Irx3-/-, Irx5-/- and double Irx3/5-/- mutants. The abnormal inner ear phenotypes are summarized as follows: 1. Irx3-/-, Irx5-/-, Irx3/5-/- mutant embryos had enlarged and shortened cochlear ducts. In the Irx3/5-/- double mutant, the three cochlear chambers were malformed. Most interestingly, the Irx3/5-/- double mutants had loss the ductus reunien, a structure that linked the vestibule with the cochlea. 2. In the Irx3/5-/- mutants at E16.5, there were numerous supernumerary vestibular hair cells in the GER region of the cochlear epithelium. Furthermore, these sensory hair cells were contiguous with those in the saccule, suggesting a loss of cellular boundary between these sensory regions. 3. Analysis of E16.5 Irx3/5-/- mutant spiral ganglia demonstrated abnormal innervations to the disorganized vestibular and cochlear sensory organs. 4. The Irx3-/- and Irx5-/- single mutants had delayed hair cell differentiation. At E16.5, only one row of inner hair cell could be observed; but by E18.5, differentiated inner and outer hair cells could be detected, with additional ectopic inner hair cells detected. In the Irx3/5-/- double mutant, a severe delay of cochlear hair cell differentiation was observed at E18.5, the arrangement of these cochlear hair cells was disorganized. 5. In all the Irx mutants examined, the differentiation of supporting cells was also delayed, but specification of supporting cell types was not affected. The multiple inner ear phenotypes of the Irx mutants suggest that Irx3 and Irx5 have extensive and essential functions at different stages of cochlea development. In summary, we have analysed the expression patterns and inner ear morphological defects of the Irx3 and Irx5 mutants and completed Objective 1. Objective 2. To identify the genes and pathways regulated by Irx3 and Irx5 in patterning the cochlear epithelium and in determining sensory cell fate A. Analysis of genes involved in neurosensory specification and hair cell differentiation To understand how Irx3 and Irx5 affect sensory domain specification, mutant otocysts were analyzed with markers for neurosensory fate. We found that the single mutants had mild phenotype, and we focused our analysis on the Irx3/5-/- double mutant. At E9.5, Sox2+ domain was expanded, accompanied with a loss of posterior Pax2 expression in the Irx3/5-/- mutant. Moreover, Irx3/5-/- otocyst displayed an expanded NeuroD positive domain and generating an ectopic stream of delaminating neuroblasts. The expression of Tbx1, which suppresses neurogenesis, became restricted to the posterior otocyst. In wildtype cochlea, neuroblast delamination declined from E11.5. However, in Irx3/5-/- cochlear epithelium, NeuroD+ cells could be detected as late as E14.5, suggesting a prolonged neurosensory competence in the mutant cochlea. These results indicate that Irx3 and Irx5 are required to control inner ear patterning from early otocyst stage by regulating neurosensory cell competence. Irx3 and Irx5 could suppress neurosensory fate determination during inner ear development. In Irx3-/- , Irx5-/-, and Irx3/5-/- mutants, cochlear hair cell differentiation was delayed, with increased severity in the double mutant. It has been reported that Sonic Hedgehog secreted from the CVG neurons affects the progression of hair cell differentiation. In the Irx3/5-/- mutant embryos, due to prolonged and increased generation of neurons, the expression of Shh was upregulated, which was consistent with the delayed hair cell differentiation phenotype observed. Therefore, the hair cell differentiation delay was likely a secondary defect, as a consequence of abnormal neurosensory competence of the Irx mutant cochlear epithelium. B. Analysis of genes involved in cochlear patterning Based on the cochlear phenotypes of the Irx mutants, we hypothesized that the primary defect could be abnormal cellular patterning in the developing cochlear epithelium. We assessed the expression of several sensory and non-sensory markers. At E14.5, Bmp4 was expressed in the LER in the cochlear epithelium, but was absent in Irx3/5-/-. Sox2 which marked the cochlear prosensory region was up-regulated in the GER domain, suggesting a transformation of non-sensory cell fate to the sensory cell fate. In E16.5 mutant cochlear epithelium, Gata2+ cells were shifted to the ventral side of the cochlea, Lmx1a+ cells were extended to the middle of ventral cochlear epithelium. These data suggest that Irx3 and Irx5 are part of the mechanism in defining the patterning of the sensory and non-sensory domains in the cochlear epithelium. To understand how Irx3 and Irx5 regulate neuro-sensory/non-sensory patterning, we assessed the expression of genes involved in otocyst patterning at E10.5. In wildtype otocyst, a clear boundary of sensory (Sox2+) and non-sensory (Lmx1a+) region was observed. However, in Irx3/5-/- otocyst, there were overlapping sensory and non-sensory domains, with an expanded Lmx1a and Sox2 double positive cell population. In the anterior otocyst, both Irx3 and Irx5 were co-localized with Lmx1a expression domain, and complementary to the Sox2+ neurosensory competent domain, suggesting that Irx3 and Irx5 may cooperate with Lmx1a to restrict Sox2 expression and specify non-sensory fate, and to define the boundary of neurosensory and non-sensory cells. To test the hypothesis that Irx3 and Irx5 may suppress Sox2 expression, we used a gain-of-function approach to overexpress Irx3/Irx5 with or without Lmx1a, and assessed the levels of Sox2 expression in different cell lines. By cell transfection experiments, we found that over-expression of either Irx3 or Irx5 was sufficient to suppress Sox2 expression at both RNA and protein levels. By bioinformatics analysis of the conserved enhancer regions of the Sox2 gene locus, we identified a number of Irx and Lmx1a binding sites, suggesting potential direct regulation of Sox2 gene expression by Irx3 and Irx5 during inner ear development. In conclusion, we have completed Objective 2 and discovered a novel molecular regulatory mechanism for Irx and Sox2 gene functions in the mammalian inner ear.

776312.label: Major findings and research outcome
776312.value: The aim of this project is to elucidate the roles of Irx3 and Irx5 in mammalian cochlea development. We have shown that Irx3 and Irx5 are expressed in the non-sensory domain of the otocyst, and in the ventral cochlea epithelium at later stages (E12.5-18.5). However, Irx3 is unique in its expression in the sensory region in the organ of Corti. In addition, Irx3 and Irx5 are both expressed in the periotic mesenchymal cells. The expression patterns of Irx3 and Irx5 suggest that they could be involved in early patterning at the otocyst stage; and that Irx3/5 could have gene-specific as well as shared redundant roles during inner ear morphogenesis (see Liu et al., Cell and Tissue Research). The Irx3 and Irx5 mouse mutants displayed complex inner ear dysmorphology, indicating that these two genes have multiple functions at different stages and in different cochlear cell types. The Irx3-/-, Irx5-/-, and Irx3/5-/- mutant embryos had enlarged and shortened cochlear ducts, abnormal or absence of ductus reuniens which separate the vestibule from the cochlea. In the Irx3/5-/- mutant, the patterns of sensory and non-sensory domains in the cochlea epithelium were shifted; the boundaries for the sensory cells in the saccule and the organ of Corti were merged. These data suggest that Irx3 and Irx5 are essential patterning genes that define the sensory and non-sensory domains in the cochlear epithelium. The developing cochlea epithelium consists of multipotent progenitors that differentiate into a number of cell types for hearing function. We have shown that the Irx3/5-/- mutant otic epithelium has acquired an extended neurosensory competence and neurogenesis. The abnormal spiral ganglia with enhanced Shh signaling would contribute to the delayed hair cell differentiation phenotype observed in Irx3 and Irx5 mutants. Therefore, in normal cochlea, Irx3 and Irx5 may function to suppress neurosensory fate commitment. Similar to Irx3 and Irx5, Lmx1a and Sox2 are also required to define non-sensory cell fates in the inner ear. Based on the expanded Sox2 expression domain, and increased Sox2-Lmx1a double positive cells in the otic vesicle of the Irx3/5-/- mutant, we hypothesized that Irx3 and Irx5 could cooperate with Lmx1a to transcriptionally suppress Sox2 expression. By cell based gain-of-function experiments we have shown that overexpression of Irx3, Irx5 or Lmx1a could indeed suppress Sox2 expression, supporting the requirement of Irx3/5-Lmx1a-Sox2 regulatory pathway for non-sensory cell fate determination (see Liu et al., manuscript in preparation for PNAS).

776312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776312.value: Our findings on the functions of Irx genes in inner ear development has opened up the following future studies: 1. The loss of the ductus reunien in Irx3 and Irx5 mutants may be due to abnormal epithelial-mesenchymal interactions. How the ductus reunien formed during inner ear development is not well known and warrant further study. 2. As Irx3 and Irx5 are required to define non-sensory cell fates, which have significant contributions to the regulation of endocochlear potential and inner ear function. The postnatal developmental and physiological functions of Irx3 and Irx5 need to be further investigated. 3. Making use of the Irx3 and Irx5 reporter genes, it will be possible to isolate Irx-expressing cells in the developing ear and perform RNA seq and transcriptomic analysis to identify downstream target genes to delineate their transcriptional regulatory mechanisms. 4. Other Irx genes of the IrxA cluster are also known to be expressed in the developing inner ear. Further studies on other members of the Irx gene clusters will be necessary to decipher their specific and redundant roles. We shall apply for RGC GRF and CRF grants with other collaborators to continue with the study on Irx genes and inner ear development.

776312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776312.value: Irx3 and Irx5 are two linked genes of the IrxB cluster in the mouse genome. Both Irx3 and Irx5 mutants display hearing deficit. Irx3 and Irx5 have overlapping expression domains in the non-sensory cells of the developing inner ear, and they share some degree of functional redundancy. The Irx3 and Irx5 mutant mice displayed multiple inner ear morphological and cellular defects. Our phenotype analyses have demonstrated that Irx3 and Irx5 are essential patterning genes required for defining the boundaries of sensory and non-sensory domains in the cochlea epithelium. Irx3 and Irx5 could suppress the neurosensory competence of the cochlear epithelial progenitors, in order to maintain the non-sensory cell fates. Furthermore, we have identified a novel genetic regulatory mechanism: Irx3 and Irx5 may cooperate with Lmx1a to regulate Sox2 expression for non-sensory cell fate determination in the inner ear. This is the first study on the function of Iroquois genes in mammalian inner ear and sensory organ development. The results of this project will contribute to our understanding of the pathogenesis of human hearing disorders. Our data also suggests that Irx3 and Irx5 may represent new therapeutic targets for hair cell regeneration and sensorineural deafness.
