776412.label: Project Objectives
776412.value: To develop an extensible statistical and bioinformatics framework for identifying genetic variants for Mendelian and complex diseases using exome sequencing data. To implement this framework into a user friendly software tool for the use of the genetics research community.
rows: To develop an extensible statistical and bioinformatics framework for identifying genetic variants for Mendelian and complex diseases using exome sequencing data.
To implement this framework into a user friendly software tool for the use of the genetics research community.

776412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776412.value: In the past few years, genome-wide association studies using massively parallel single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) genotyping technologies have uncovered hundreds of common sequence variants that contribute to the risk of many common diseases and associated physiological traits. However, a large number of disease-related genetic variants remain to be identified, especially those that are too rare to be efficiently studied using SNP genotyping arrays. Next generation sequencing (NGS) technologies offer the ability to examine all sequence variants in the genome, and are rapidly becoming less expensive. In the past 2 years, NGS has been applied to DNA enriched for coding sequences (using targeted capture technologies) to efficiently study sequence changes that alter protein structure and function. Such exome sequencing studies have successfully identified the mutations responsible for a number of rare Mendelian diseases, and are beginning to be applied to complex diseases. However, the task of identifying disease-relevant changes among the huge number of variants present in any individual’s exome poses substantial difficulties, and the field is only beginning to develop and refine the necessary computational tools. The proposed project aims to develop a powerful statistical and bioinformatics framework for knowledge-based genetic mapping of human diseases using exome sequencing data. It will include methods for integrating information from diverse bioinformatics resources with exome sequence data to identify the sequence variants associated with human genetic diseases. For rare Mendelian diseases, we will develop a thorough procedure for filtration and prioritization of sequence variants at multiple analysis levels including genetic, sequence-variant, and gene function levels. For complex diseases, we will develop a comprehensive knowledge-based weighting profile for sequence variants, and statistical methods for weighted analyses of sequence variants to establish disease-related variants. This proposed framework will have important advantages over existing tools, including comprehensive knowledge-based prioritization and statistical association tests, and the efficient processing of large sequencing datasets. A computer program will be developed to implement the framework, with Spinocerebellar ataxia as an example of rare Mendelian diseases, and Hirschsprung’s disease and Hepatitis B Infection as examples of complex diseases. It is envisaged that the computer program will substantially ease the complex procedure of exome sequencing analyses for genetic mapping of human diseases, and will become a solid base to be extended to a comprehensive knowledge-based analytical platform for future whole-genome sequencing studies of human diseases. 儘管全基因組關聯研究已經發現了數百個與常見疾病或生理徵狀相關的基因位點，但大量的疾病基因位點（尤其是那些頻率較低且沒有被通用基因陣列覆蓋的）依然等待被發現。在過去兩年里，結合新一代測序技術與外顯子捕捉技術，全外顯子測序逐漸廣泛地應用於多種遺傳疾病的研究，并已成功發現諸多少見孟德爾遺傳疾病的致病基因。然而，從數以萬計的編碼序列變異位點中辨識出真正的相關位點或基因具有相當大的困難，而這也對生物計算工具提出了新的需求。 本研究課題旨在開發能夠從全外顯子序列數據中有效尋找疾病基因的統計學及生物信息學工具體系。該體系將包括多個可以整合全外顯子序列數據與多種生物學數據資源的方法。針對少見孟德爾疾病，我們將制定一個完整的多水平的（遺傳水平，序列位點水平及基因水平）基因篩選及優化步驟。針對常見複雜疾病，我們將為序列變異位點提供基於知識的加權檔案，進而開發關聯疾病與加權位點的統計方法。相對於其他現有工具，本研究課題中的工具體系具有多項優勢，包括對全方位的生物學知識及統計關聯方法的有效利用以及對高通量序列數據的快速處理。並且，我們將編碼并開發該工具體系相應的計算機軟件；其將大量簡化全外顯子數據的分析步驟，從而有效尋找人類疾病的致病基因。該軟件也并將延伸成為未來全基因組測序研究中的可靠分析平臺。

776412.label: Realisation of objectives
776412.value: Objective 1: We have developed methods for evaluating the pathogenicity of rare coding variants for mendelian disorders, including a inheritance-mode-specific method integrating information from comprehensive list of genomic features as well as several existing methods. We have also developed multivariate gene-based and pathway-based tests that enhance statistical power for complex diseases. These methods were published in mainstream genetics / genomics journals. Objective 2: We have implemented the methods in a number of freely available software including KGGSeq, wKGGSeq and MGAS. Using these methods and software we have been able to identify disease-causing mutations in 2 families with rare diseases. The software have been taught in international workshops and are being used by the research community.

776412.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776412.value: As exome sequencing analysis is nearing maturity the next big challenge in human genomics is the interpretation of whole-genome sequencing data including regulatory regions. The methods and tools we have developed for genome-wide association studies and exome sequencing analysis will form a solid platform for this development, which will involve efficient computation as well as the integration with omic datasets with information on genome annotation, genome architecture and regulatory elements.

776412.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776412.value: The human genome contain approximately 20,000 protein coding genes, in which sequence changes (mutations) may cause rare inherited malformations or disorders (Mendelian diseases). Exome sequencing is a new genomic technology that can characterise the sequence of all protein coding genes and detect mutations in these sequences, of an individual. However, as every person contain numerous mutations, it is difficult as well as time-consuming, even for an expert, to go through every mutation and find the disease variant. The main goal of this project is to develop bioinformatic tools to perform this task in an accurate and efficient manner, to come up with a short list for further consideration by expert. We have developed a number of methods (KGGSeq, wKGGSeq, ISPP), published in reputed journals (Human Mutation, Bioinformatics and Nucleic Acids Research. In addition, using our methods we have identified novel disease causing mutations for dilated cardiomyopathy and familial spastic paraplegia.

776512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776512.value: Neural stem/progenitor cells (NSCs) have limited capacities of growth and differentiation, offering possible regeneration therapy for stroke and neurodegenerative diseases. Hypoxic/ischemic stimulation mediates the growth and differentiation of NSCs into mature neurons. However, the mechanisms of hypoxia/ischemia-mediated neurogenesis are largely unknown. In hypoxic/ischemic brain, nitric oxide and superoxide are simultaneously produced and they rapidly react to form peroxynitrite. Recent progress indicates that peroxynitrite could promote endothelial cell growth for angiogenesis and hypoxia-induced muscle cell proliferation. However, whether peroxynitrite contributes to adult neurogenesis in hypoxic/ischemic brains is still unknown. The cell growth-promoting effects or cytotoxic effects of peroxynitrite could be dependent on its concentration. Because peroxynitrite has short lifetime, lack of technical methods for accurately monitoring peroxynitrite is a major obstacle. The development of a sensitive and specific peroxynitrite probe makes it possible to address whether peroxynitrite can promote adult neurogenesis under hypoxia/ischemia. Thus, we recently developed new peroxynitrite-specific probes and conducted pilot studies. Our preliminary results showed that hypoxia increased endogenous peroxynitrite formation, and the increased peroxynitrite was correlated with the up-regulation of vascular endothelial growth factors (VEGF) and the enhanced proliferation and neuronal differentiation of NSCs. Also, peroxynitrite decomposition catalysts reduced the neuronal differentiation whereas low dose of peroxynitrite promoted neuronal proliferation and differentiation. Therefore, we hypothesize that peroxynitrite can act as cellular signaling molecule to promote neurogenesis for brain repair by activating VEGF signaling in ischemic/hypoxic neural stem/progenitor cells. To verify this hypothesis, this proposal will address three specific questions: (1) Whether peroxynitrite positively modulates neurogenesis in adult NSCs under normoxia and hypoxia in vitro. (2) Whether endogenous peroxynitrite play a role in promotion of neurogenesis in post-ischemic brains in vivo. (3) Whether neurogenesis-promoting effects of peroxynitrite are related to activation of VEGF signal pathway in NSCs under hypoxia/ischemia. We will use primary cultured neural stem/progenitor cells and middle cerebral artery occlusion animal model to detect peroxynitrite production, and to investigate VEGF signaling, the proliferation and differentiation of neural stem/progenitor cells. After verifying the hypothesis, we can develop the new concept that peroxynitrite functions as a cellular signaling to regulate adult neurogenesis in hypoxic/ischemic neural stem/progenitor cells. The study will advance current knowledge about the molecular mechanisms of hypoxia/ischemia-mediated neurogenesis. Using this knowledge and our new peroxynitrite probe, we can seek for drugs targeting on peroxynitrite signaling, which may have implications for developing therapeutic approaches to promoting brain repair in stroke and neurodegenerative diseases. 神經幹細胞的生長和分化潛力為中風和神經退行性疾病的治療帶來希望。缺血缺氧能刺激神經再生，但其機製不明。缺血腦組織可產生超氧自由基和一氧化氮，兩者同時存在而反應生成過氧亞硝基。研究顯示，過氧亞硝基能促進新生血管形成和肌細胞增殖， 但對神經再生的作用未有報道。 由於缺乏直接而靈敏的方法檢測過氧亞硝基，長期以來過氧亞硝基的生理病理作用不太清楚，一般認為，過氧亞硝基具有神經細胞毒性作用。為探討過氧亞硝基在神經再生中的作用，我們發展了敏感而特異的過氧亞硝基熒光探針。應用該過氧亞硝基熒光探針和其他技術，我們觀察了過氧亞硝基在調節神經再生中的作用。初步的研究顯示， 低濃度過氧亞硝基能促進血管生長因子表達和神經幹細胞生長和分化，本項目旨在通過一系列實驗證明過氧亞硝基的調節神經幹細胞增殖和分化的作用和其相關機製。我們將回答以下三個問題﹕(1)是否過氧亞硝基能在體外缺血缺氧實驗系統調節神經幹細胞增殖和分化﹖(2) 是否過氧亞硝基能在缺血缺氧動物實驗模型顯示調節神經幹細胞增殖和分化作用﹖(3)是否血管生長因子是過氧亞硝基的作用靶點﹖本研究將提高對神經再生調控的分子機製的認識和發展新的分子靶標，為中風後遺症和參經退行性疾病的治療提供新思路。

776512.label: Realisation of objectives
776512.value: With the support of RGC GRF grant, we conducted a series of experiments and have achieved almost all of the goals designed in our original proposal. Objective 1. 1) We developed and verified a new updated fluorescent probe HKYellow-AM to be an effective tool for detecting peroxynitrite formation for this project. 2) We used primary cultured neural stem/progenitor cells under hypoxic conditions to mimic the increased endogenous ONOO- formation and investigated the correlation between peroxynitrite level and the statuses of NSCs self-renewal, proliferation and differentiation. To verify the roles of peroxynitrite in modulating neurogenesis, we the investigated the effects of peroxynitrite decomposition catalysts (PDCs, FeTPPS and FeTMPyP) and a natural peroxynitrite scavenger uric acid on modulating neurogenesis in the hypoxic NSCs experiments. We applied neurosphere assay, BrdU incorportation, Ki67 staining and immunostaining with different biomarkers to explore the roles of endogenous peroxynitrite in modulating the self-renewal, proliferation and neuronal differentiation of NSCs. In addition, we used HKYellow-AM to sort the normoxic NSCs into ONOO- relatively high NSCs and ONOO- relatively low NSCs to compare their ability of self-renewal, proliferation and differentiation. We used PDCs treatment to elucidate the functions of peroxynitrite in modulating NSCs differentiation and proliferation. 3) We applied both synthesized peroxynitrite and peroxynitrite donor SIN-1 to produce ONOO- and conducted the studies on the effects of extraneous ONOO- on modulating NSCs self-renewal, proliferation and differentiation. We used neurosphere assay, BrdU incorportation, Ki67 staining and immunostaining with different biomarkers to explore the roles of exogenous peroxynitrite in regulating self-renewal, proliferation and neuronal differentiation of NSCs. We also use the LDH and MTT assay to monitor the cell cytotoxic effects. Objective 2 1) We detected the change of peroxynitrite level in both clinical samples and MCAO model. In MCAO model, we used different ischemic time and investigated the relationship between peroxynitrite and neurogenesis. BrdU incorporation and detections of different biomarkers with immunostaining and western blotting were used to explore the potential correlation of peroxynitrite level and neurogenesis. 2) We investigated the roles of endogenous peroxynitrite in modulating neurogenesis by co-treated with PDCs in MCAO model. Interestingly, peroxynitrite is commonly considered as cytotoxic factor in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. In short-term cerebral ischemia (1.0 hour) plus 7 days reperfusion rat model, we found that the peroxynitrite could be a redox signaling to promote neurogenesis. Therefore, the cytotoxicity or neurogenesis-promoting effects of peroxynitrite are dependent on its concentration. Objective 3 1) We first retested the VEGF expression by immunostaining and extracellular VEGF release by Elisa kits in different groups in vitro. We found slightly increase of VEGF expression but no significant change of extracellular VEGF in exogenous peroxynitrite treatment. After carefully reviewing our protocol for detecting HIF-1α previously, we found it can degrade quickly when preparation and that was why we did not find the change. Then we re-investigated the role of peroxynitrite in HIF-1α expression and we found dramatically increase of HIF-1α in peroxynitrite treatment. We also detected its expression in hypoxic condition and used HIF-1α inhibitor to confirm the potential mechanism. 2) We then investigated the roles of HIF-1α and its Wnt pathway in modulating neurogenesis in hypoxic NSCs. Several cellular events could contribute to the stimulation of Wnt/β-catenin signal pathway, including increasing β-catenin engagement, the nuclear translocation of β catenin, β catenin interaction with lymphoid enhancer-binding factor 1/T-cell factor 1 (LEF-1/TCF-1) transcription factors and activation of target genes. We detected β catenin engagement and downstream LEF-1 expression by using western blot, nuclear translocation of β catenin by immunostaining, and activation of target genes by report gene assay. Moreover, we also detected the other potentially related pathway including AKT, STAT3 and Cav-1. Others related research activities: We further explore the potential application of peroxynitrite and its related pathway as drug targets. We also conducted some experiments to investigate the cytotoxicity of peroxynitrite in cerebral ischemia injury. We also published several invited review articles in the related research field. In conclusion, peroxynitrite could have dual roles in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Peroxynitrite could be cytotoxic factor as well as cell growth signaling for the self renewal, proliferation and differentiation, dependent on the concentration produced. Low doses of peroxynitrite could be a cellular redox signaling to stimulate neurogenesis for brain repair in post-stroke brains.

776512.label: Major findings and research outcome
776512.value: 1) HKYellow-AM is a novel fluorescent probe with high specificity and sensitivity: The results have published in Chemical sciences 2016,7:5407-5413 2) Increased peroxynitrite level is correlated with neurogenesis promotion: In rat MCAO model, increased 3-nitrotyrosine (3-NT, footprint for peroxynitrite formation) level was highly associated with the increased NSCs marker nestin expression and almost all the BrdU positive cells showed 3-NT positive. We extended our studies to clinical stroke patients. Total 179 patients with ischemic stroke and 49 controls were tested in the study. Increased nitrotyrosine level has been found in the patients’ plasma. Thus, enhanced neurogenensis could be associated with the formation of peroxynitrite in post-ischemic stroke. 3) Peroxynitrite enhanced self-renewal, proliferation, neuronal differentiation of NSCs After sorting by peroxynitrite probe HKYellow-AM, we found that NSCs with high peroxynitrite level had high capacity of self-renewal and proliferation. PDCs (FeTMPyP and FeTPPS) treatment reduced hypoxia-induced peroxynitrite formation, NSCs proliferation, self-renewal and neuronal differentiation. Meanwhile, exogenous peroxynitrite formation promoted NSCs proliferation, self-renewal and neuronal differentiation. In MCAO model, increased neurogenesis was attenuated by PDCs treatment. Those studies indicate that peroxynitrite plays important roles in promoting neurogenesis. 4) Peroxynitrite-induced neurogenesis was partly through activating HIF-1α correlated with enhanced Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway We found the peroxynitrite treatment dramatically upregulated HIF-1α expression and PDCs treatment decreased hypoxia-induced HIF-1α accumulation. HIF-1α inhibitor Digoxin could attenuate peroxynitrite induced cell proliferation. Furthermore, the downsteam signaling goes to Wnt signaling pathway. Peroxynitrite activated Wnt pathway and PDCs treatment attenuated hypoxia induced Wnt pathway activation. Increased P-Akt and P-Stat3 by peroxynitrite which indicated the multiple signaling pathway involved in the process. 5) The threshold of peroxynitrite from neurogenesis to neurotoxicity We found the dose-dependent effects of peroxynitrite on switching neurogenesis to cytotoxicity. Peroxynitrite concentration at nanomole level could promote neuorgenesis but at micromole level would induce neurotoxicity. We also investigated that relationship between peroxynitrite formation and neurogenesis in cultured NSCs under oxygen-glucose deprivation plus reoxygenation (OGD/RO). We have submitted a manuscript for reporting the discoveries which have been attached in the report. 6) Drug discovery for promoting neurogenesis by targeting peroxynitrite and its down-stream signaling pathways We used peroxynitrite and its related Wnt signaling as targets for drug screening of effective compounds from Chinese herbal medicine. As II, an active compound isolated from Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge revealed its neurogenesis-promoting effects. As II stimulated neurogenesis through Wnt/β-catenin in post-ischemic brain in vivo and hypoxic NSCs in vitro. The manuscript has been prepared and attached in the report. 7) We have published several related papers to explore the cytotoxicity of peroxynitrite in cerebral and hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury. Those works have been conducted by the students whose studentships were partly supported by this funding. 8) We also published several review articles in related to the projects. 9) We attended several international conferences to report the research progress about the research projects.

776512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776512.value: Based on the achievement of our studies, we expect following potential directions for further studies: (1) Given that both neurogenesis and cytotoxicity occurred in ischemic stroke accompanied by changing peroxynitrite levels at different time points, it will be interesting to investigate how these functions are regulated by different peroxynitrite levels during ischemic stroke. For example, what is the potential switch during the increasing of peroxynitrite level? (2) To further explore the molecular mechanisms of peroxynitrite in regulating proliferation and differentiation of NSCs. In particular, how peroxynitrite regulates HIF-1a signaling pathways and beta-catenin signaling pathway are valuable to be further studied. (3) As our results indicated the important biological function of peroxynitrite in neurogenesis and peroxynitrite scavenger showed neuroprotective effects in ischemic stroke, it is very interesting and important to address the dosage and treatment time of these drugs to avoid inhibiting post-stroke neurogenesis for brain functional recovery. Due to the limitation of funding and research period, we could not achieve the goals. We plan to seek for more funds from RGC GRF grants or other funding sources to continue our studies in this direction.

776512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776512.value: The prevalence of stroke becomes one of the major disease burdens worldwide. The discovery of post-stroke neurogenesis shed a light on stroke treatment. In ischemic brain, free radicals are considered as important factors responsible for neurotoxicity. Recent progress suggests that free radicals could be cellular signaling for stimulating neurogenesis in post-ischemic brains. Peroxynitrite is one of the reactive nitrogen species, which is generated from the reaction of nitric oxide and superoxide. The roles of peroxynitrite in inducing neurotoxicity have been widely studied but its function in modulating neurogenesis is unknown. This project aims to fully understand the roles of peroxynitrite in modulating neurogenesis. The major discoveries include (1) Peroxynitrite at low concentration has neurogenesis-promoting effects but high concentration induces neurotoxicity; (2) Short term exposure to brain ischemia could stimulate adult neurogenesis, which is correlated with the peroxynitrite formation; (3) Peroxynitrite promotes NSCs proliferation, self-renewal and neuronal differentiation; (4) Peroxynitrite partly contributes to hypoxia induced neurogenesis through affecting HIF-1α and Wnt/ β-catenin pathway; (5) Peroxynitrite could be a drug target for modulating neurogenesis. The study brings novel insight into understanding the underlying mechanisms of post-stroke neurogenesis for brain repair and provide new direction for drug discovery to treat ischemic stroke.

776812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776812.value: The goal of this work is to find keys to structural and functional plasticity of sensory pathways in early postnatal life. In the visual pathway, inhibitory (GABAergic) interneurons are the last to mature but are required to drive onset of the critical period for ocular dominance. Closure of this postnatal period is coincident with consolidation of extracellular matrix molecules into perineuronal nets about the GABAergic interneurons. Do GABAergic interneurons in the vestibular pathway for gravity detection serve a similar role? Our preliminary study revealed progressive intensification of glycan-rich perineuronal nets around maturing GABAergic interneurons in the rat vestibular nucleus (VN) during postnatal weeks 1 - 2. Treatment of postnatal animals with chondroitinase ABC to disrupt chondroitins in perineuronal nets at the VN delayed postnatal acquisition of negative geotaxis, an innate behavior indicative of gravity detection. If the gravity-detection pathway is anatomically in place, what mechanism underlies the delay? Given that semaphorin 3A binding to signaling receptor complexes at GABAergic neurons triggers structural and functional plasticity at developing synapses and that our preliminary results indicate preferred binding of semaphorin 3A to E-type sulfation of chondroitins found at perineuronal nets in the adult rat, we hypothesize that the sulfation pattern of chondroitins at perineuronal nets determines availability of semaphorin 3A for binding to receptor complexes at GABAegic interneurons and in turn plasticity in the central vestibular synapse. We aim therefore (1) to determine expression of semaphorin 3A and its localization to chondroitin sulfate moieties of perineuronal nets in the VN during the postnatal period for acquisition of the innate behavior indicative of gravity detection; (2) to assess GABAergic interneurons in the VN for changes in (i) AMPA receptor-mediated currents and (ii) dendritic arborization when the neuron is exposed to a semaphorin 3A gradient with/without perturbation to perineuronal chondroitin sulfate moieties. The importance of the E-sulfated chondroitins at the perineuronal net will be reinforced by comparison of structural, functional and behavioral results between the N-acetylgalactosamine-4-sulfate 6-O-sulfotransferase knock-out mice and the wild type litter-mates. Results will indicate how sulfation patterns of chondroitins are remodeled to reset synaptic plasticity for expression of the gravity detection behavior during postnatal development. We expect findings to apply across sensory systems and thus to inform therapeutic and training paradigms with prospects for improvements in learning and memory as well as post-traumatic recovery and rehabilitation. 這項研究之目的，是於初生期內找出能影響感官神經通路在結構上及功能上可塑性的因素。我們初步研究顯示，在大鼠初生後的兩周期間，前庭核內-胺基丁酸神經元漸趨成熟，跟神經元周圍外網的聚醣基質同步形成。另外，初生動物的前庭核神經元周圍外網的聚醣基質，經軟骨素酶破壞後，能延遲先天性重力感知行為的出現。 如果感應重力的神經通路已經形成，是甚麼機制導致該等延遲? 已知semaphorin 3A 能跟-胺基丁酸神經元上的信號受體結合，並誘發發育中的突觸產生結構上與功能上的可塑性。又我們的初步研究顯示，在成年大鼠身上，semaphorin 3A傾向跟神經元周圍外網中的E類硫基化軟骨素結合。因此我們假設在-胺基丁酸神經元周圍外網的軟骨素硫基化模式能決定多少semaphorin 3A 能與其受體結合，繼而影響中樞前庭突觸之可塑性。 因此，我們的目標是 (1) 在初生的大鼠，找出當重力感知行為出現時，semaphorin 3A在前庭核中的表達狀況，及其在前庭核神經元周圍外網與軟骨素結合的情況﹔(2) 在該等神經元周圍外網的基質軟骨素遭干擾，並前庭核內-胺基丁酸神經元受semaphorin 3A影響時，評估該等神經元的AMPA受體電流及樹突形態會否改變。為了進一步認清前庭核神經元周圍外網中E類硫基化軟骨素的重要性，我們會比較 N-acetylgalactosamine-4-sulfate 6-O-sulfotransferase基因剔除小鼠和野生性小鼠在有關結構、功能及行為上的異同。這些結果將顯示軟骨素的硫基化模式如何經重組，而透發中樞前庭突觸的可塑性，以至於初生期出現先天性重力感知行為。 我們預期這發現能被應用到不同的感官系統，從而帶來改善學習與記憶的治療及訓練方法，並可促進創傷後的復原。

776912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776912.value: 弗德賴希共濟失調 (Friedreich ataxia, (FRDA))，最常見的遺傳性共濟失調，是一種由於線粒體功能失常的多系統疾病特別是目中樞神經系統和心臟。除了神經系統進行性損傷令患者從三十歲需要使用輪椅，心臟的病變（肥厚性及擴張性的心肌病變）最終是令患者致死的原因。雖然可以從超過96﹪患者找到線粒體共濟蛋白（frataxin）的基因突變，有關於弗ﾑY德賴希共濟失調的病機研究往往受制於缺乏能確實重演該疾病的細胞模型。這樣也阻礙治療的發展。例如，用從患者的皮膚纖維母細胞和/或淋巴細胞進行的分子研究已證實共濟蛋白的喪失導致鐵超載，自由基產物增加；一些治療策略，以減輕細胞氧化應激如艾地苯醌（idebenone）卻未能隨機對照臨床試驗，以改善FRDA患者的心臟功能。發展一個能精確模擬病理主要方面的細胞模型，是治療藥物篩選的前提。理論上，從FRDA患者提取病變組織進行直接功能表征的研究，將為每個患者提供急需的病理機制和藥物反應，但卻受到明顯的倫理道德，後勤的和技術方面的原因。缺乏合適而可靠的細胞疾病模型阻礙了對候選藥物的病理生理和功能確定性的系統分析。能夠產生具體誘導多能幹細胞（iPSCs）則為人類研究疾病提供了一種新模式，並為個體化藥物測試奠定了基礎。事實上，各種疾病具體誘導的多功能幹細胞（iPSCs）及他們心臟的衍生細胞都已成功地概括了細胞原型和/或人類心血管疾病的發病機制。在這裡，我們提出結合使用最先進的人力和iPSC技術，詳細的電生理研究，和全面的技術評估線粒體功能，發展細胞FRDA模型以獲得新的了解其疾病病理機制，驗證藥理作用，和進行高通量藥物篩選。該方法提供了幾乎無限的體外源以研究FRDA特異心肌細胞的體外實驗和藥理藥物試驗，繞過需要和限制獲得活體組織。該結果則會大大提高對其病理機制的理解，從而帶來新的治療方案。成功的這種方法則可進一步擴展研究其他人類心臟疾病。

777212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777212.value: Congenital heart defects (CHD) happens in 1% of live births. It is the most common human birth defect. The study of genes modifying complex disorders such as CHD generally depends on the use of mouse models. Col2a1 encodes type II procollagen, the major cartilage matrix protein. During embryogenesis Col2a1 is differentially transcribed to give IIA mRNA containing an exon (exon 2) and IIB mRNA, which lacks this exon. We produced IIA procollagen deficient mice by deleting exon 2 of Col2a1 and observed that mice homozygous for the IIA null mutation (IIA-/-) display heart malformations resulting in perinatal lethality to near normal phenotype, depending on the strain background of the mice. Our hypothesis is that the variability of the heart defects in IIA-/- mutants is the result of one or more gene(s) at other loci which modify the effect of the IIA-/- genotype on the heart development. In order to test the hypothesis (supported by a previous RGC grant), three IIA-/- genotype congenic mouse lines with genetic background of the C57BL6/N (Line#1:C57), 129/sv (Line#2:129) and ICR (Line#3:ICR) strains were established. Our findings suggest a recessive modifier in the Line#1:C57 mouse line interacts with homozygous IIA null mutation to produce the heart defect phenotypes. Genome-wide linkage analysis was performed and a significant linkage on chromosome 15, at 60cM was detected in a recessive model. To further fine mapping, we generated regional specific congenic mouse lines and exhausted all available SNPs in the region between the mouse lines. Finally, we mapped the modifier located within 1.2 Mb region in mouse. Therefore, we are in a unique position to use our finding in mouse to help to understand of CHD. In this proposal, we will to detect genetic variants for CHD in mouse. Our aims are 1) identification of the genetic variant leads to CHD in mouse 2) Initial function characterization of the gene suspected to cause or modify the severity of CHD detected in mouse. 777512.label: Realisation of objectives
777512.value: O1. (100% achieved) Characterizations of the bindings of Mp1p-LBD2 and AFMP4p against aselected list of lipid molecules, including C6-ceramide (CER), arachidonic acid (AA) sphingosylphosphorylcholine (SPC), and palmitic acid (PLM), have been accessed by using NMR titration and isothermal titration calorimetry methods. In summary, the relative binding affinities for Afmp4p were: AA > PLM > SPC > CER & relative binding affinities for Mp1p-LBD2 were: AA > CER > PLM > SPC. Key pro-inflammatory AA lipid has the highest affinity and selected for further studies. O2. (100% achieved) We have shown that AA could displace PLM in PLM-presaturated Afmp4p and Mp1p-LBD2 samples using NMR competition binding assay experiments. This demonstrated that Mp1p and AFMP4p proteins can effectively trap proinflammatory lipids over common saturated lipids, such as palmitic acid and these results were consistent with the significantly higher binding affinities of both proteins towards AA over PLM observed at section O1. O3. (100% achieved) Since complete resonance assignments and subsequent structure determination of the lipid part by NMR-based structure modelling will be beyond the time limit of the present project, we have turned to and successfully applied x-ray crystallographic technique to solve the complex structures of Mp1p-LBD2 and AFMP4p binding with the high affinity ligand, arachidonic acid, as well as those structures binding with palmitic acid. O4. (100% achieved) Base on the structural information obtained from the protein-lipid complex structures and NMR chemical shift perturbation plots, we have designed and constructed a number of Mp1p-LBD2/Afmp4p mutants. In summary, most of the charged or non-polar alanine mutations showed no or small impact on the binding affinities of Afmp4p/Mp1p-LBD2 with AA while a number of steric blocker mutations to bulky tryptophan residue produced significant effects in diminishing the AA binding including I80W, D106W and A37W for Afmp4p and L264W, L305W, V261W, S325W, I268W and I328W for Mp1p-LBD2. Insertion of these mutated Mp1p-LBD2/Afmp4p genes into P. marneffei and A. fumigatus were not successful. But we were able to insert these mutated Mp1p-LBD2/Afmp4p genes into originally non-pathogenic fungus Pchia pastoris. We have shown that Pchia pastoris will extend its intracellular survival in macrophages with transfection of Afmp4p/MP1p-LBD2 gene. But no such gain of virulence function was observed for the transfection of the mutated Afmp4p/MP1p-LBD2 genes with impaired lipid binding. Combining these results, Afmp4p/MP1p-LBD2 are important virulence factors for intracellular survival of A. fumigatus/P. marneffei and their ability to trap pro-inflammatory mediators is essential for their observed virulence.

777512.label: Major findings and research outcome
777512.value: Aspergillus fumigatus and Penicillium marneffei are emerging as significant pathogens, which are causing respiratory, skin and fatal systemic mycosis in immunocomprimised patients in Southeast Asia and China. Despite their medical significance, there is little knowledge about the molecular mechanisms underlying their pathogenesis, and how they can evade the host defense to survive in the harsh intracellular environment of macrophages. Since Mp1p and Afmp4p are found abundantly in the sera of patients infected with these pathogens, we hypothesized that they are virulence factors of P. marneffei and A. fumigatus, respectively, and they contribute to host immune evasion through trapping of pro-inflammatory lipid mediators. Indeed, we have shown that Mp1p knockout strain of P. marneffei and Afmp4p knockout strain of A. fumigatus has poor intracellular survival in cell model and impaired virulence in mouse model compared with their wild type strains[publication-1]. We have prepared isotopically doubly labeled samples of 13-C/15-N-protein of Mp1p-LBD2 and AFMP4p and obtained their resonance assignments by triple resonance NMR approach[publication-2]. We have also shown that MP1p-LBD2/Afmp4p can bind to a series of pro-inflammatory mediators including C6-ceramide, arachidonic acid (AA) and sphingosylphosphorylcholine, as well as the saturated lipid, palmitic acid. In particular, their binding with AA is very tight and AA can effectively displace PLM in PLM-saturated Mp1p-LBD2/Afmp4p samples using NMR competition binding assay[publication-1]. Interestingly, we have found that each MP1p-LBD2 unit can bind up to two molecules of lipid ligands[publication-3], which was confirmed by the observation from our crystal structures of their complexes[publication-3]. Site-directed mutagenesis on MP1p-LBD2/Afmp4p were performed to impair their binding to the pro-inflammatory mediators[publication-1,publication-3]. We have shown that Pchia pastoris will extend its intracellular survival in macrophages with transfection of Afmp4p/MP1p-LBD2 genes. But no such gain of virulence function was observed for the transfection of the mutated Afmp4p/MP1p-LBD2 genes with impaired lipid binding. Combining these results, Afmp4p/MP1p-LBD2 were demonstrated to be important virulence factors for intracellular survival of A. fumigatus/P. marneffei and their ability to trap pro-inflammatory mediators is essential for their observed virulence. The present project has contribute towards a better comprehension of the fucntion of lipid binding by these cell wall proteins of P. marneffei and A. fumigates, and provide important insight into host defense evasion and pathogensis by these fungi, which may extend to other fungi or pathogenic bacteria. Such knowledge may lead to better chemotherapautic intervention of fungal diseases in future.

777512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777512.value: (1) Sequence analysis on the Mp1p protein showed that there is another ligand binding domain near the N-terminal of Mp1p, Mp1p-LBD1. The structure and function of this 166 residues Mp1p-LBD1 domain is unknown but our preliminary NMR binding titration data showed that it can also bind to a number of pro-inflammatory mediators. We hypothesize that Mp1p is designed as a multi-target virulence factor to trap different key pro-inflammatory mediators using these two ligand binding domains. The present work can be continued and extended to characterize the structure and binding properties of Mp1p-LBD1. This will help to delineate the ligand binding specificities of the two ligand binding domains of Mp1p with pro-inflammatory mediators and to better define the importance of their roles in the pathogen’s evasion of host defense. (2) Given that we have constructed the Mp1p knockout (KO) strain of P. marneffei, to obtain in-depth understanding of the virulence mechanism of Mp1p, a comparative metabolomics profile study of macrophage cells infected with wild type and Mp1p knockout strains of P. marneffei will reveal the biomarkers and pathways affected by the Mp1p virulence factor.

We have shown that Mp1p of P. marneffei and Afmp4p of A. fumigatus are important virulence factors for their pathogenesis by knockout experiments in cell and mouse models. We have also shown that MP1p-LBD2/Afmp4p can bind to a series of pro-inflammatory mediators by ITC and NMR methods and determined their crystal structures with the key pro-inflammatory lipid, arachidonic acid. 777612.label: Major findings and research outcome
777612.value: Besides the major finding, the implication of NRG3 gene (Tang et al., PLoS Genetics 8:e1002687) CNVs in HSCR, our CNV analysis revealed that 9 CNV regions were called by two CNV analysis platforms with a total of 147 genes encompassed by the CNVs called. Among these, the most relevant genes and genomic regions are: • Long duplications (>3Mb) on chrX, encompassing PCDH11X which is thought to play a fundamental role in cell-cell recognition essential for the segmental development and function of the central nervous system. • Midnolin (MIDN) on 19p13—interacts with known HSCR gene, that is NRG1, as suggested by DAPPLE • Duplications disrupting ephrin-A2 (EFNA2) which, like SEMA3A, is crucial for migration, repulsion and adhesion during neuronal, vascular and epithelial development • Three SOX genes (Del: SOX6; Dup: SOX1 and SOX11) were deleted or duplicated. Although not CNVs could be validated our data implicated CNVs in pathology. We then moved on to study the effects of selected CNVs in iPSC from two HSCR patients in whom CNVs had been detected and whose exome sequencing data was also available. We compared RNAseq at different stages and linked variation in expression with CNV presence in the genome (see details in the file uploaded section C). We integrated all genomic data available for this patient to perform an integrative analysis using Genemania (a tool for association network analysis) under the assumption that damaging genomic variations (CNVs and/or SNVs) alter expression of interacting partners and that a possible driver mutation might affect all cell stages, particularly on neuronal lineage. We considered pathways and protein-protein interactions. A common mutated gene VCL appears to link the differences in gene expression observed at different stages and cell lineages with genomic variants. This gene is a major HSCR candidate gene currently being followed up.

777612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777612.value: The identification of genes with CNVs and/or single mutations that seem to account for differences in expression between patient and controls cells open a whole new field of research.

777612.value: This project aims to find out what causes Hirschsprung disease (lack of nerves in the gut). We have looked for genes deleted or duplicated (CNVs) as well for genes with smaller genetic variations. We found that these mutated genes affect the signals whereby the cells of a fetus form the nerves of the gut

777712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777712.value: Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) play an important role in the development and progression of diabetic vascular complications. The cellular receptors for AGEs are important modulators of the biological effects of these compounds and the interaction between AGEs and their numerous receptors can lead to either favorable or unfavorable outcomes. Experimental studies have shown that engagement of AGEs with their proinflammatory receptors such as the receptor for AGE (RAGE), drives the activation of a number of proinflammatory signalling pathways, and is involved in the pathogenesis of diabetic complications. On the other hand, the binding of AGEs with the “clearance” receptors like AGE-R1 promotes their degradation and thus reduces their harmful effects. It has been suggested that it is the balance between the proinflammtory RAGE receptor and the AGEs clearance receptors that determines the final outcome of cellular activation by AGEs. Serum and tissue levels of AGEs are elevated in diabetes but how the diabetic state affects the expression and the regulation of these cellular receptors for AGEs is poorly understood. We plan to investigate the expression of the RAGE and AGE clearance receptors in type 2 diabetes and their mechanism(s) of regulation. This is important because modulation of RAGE and AGE-R1 expression can limit the pathological effects of AGEs and these receptors are potential therapeutic targets. Improving our understanding of the regulation of these receptors is essential for the development of theses receptors as novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of diabetic vascular complications.

777712.label: Realisation of objectives
777712.value: Objective 1 (achieved) Experiments were performed to investigate the effect of insulin, RAGE ligands, and oxidative stress on RAGE, soluble RAGE and AGE clearance receptors expression in THP-1 cell and human monocyte derived macrophages in vitro. We have shown that in vitro, insulin not only increases both full length RAGE and esRAGE expression, insulin can also stimulate the shedding of sRAGE from membrane-bound receptor. We have further shown that insulin-induced shedding of RAGE is mediated by the sheddase ADAM10. On the other hand, insulin, RAGE ligands and oxidative stress have minimal effects on AGE clearance receptors expression in vitro. In view of the positive effects of insulin on RAGE, we proceeded to measure serum ADAM10 level in patients with type 1 diabetes and evaluate the relationship between insulin and RAGE isoforms in vivo. Objective 2 (achieved) A cross sectional study was carried out to determine whether the expression of AGE clearance receptors was reduced in patients with type 2 diabetes. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were isolated from patients with type 2 diabetes and from a group of matched non-diabetic controls, and quantification of RAGE, AGE-R1, AGE-R2 and AGE-R3 was performed by flow cytometric staining and Western blot. AGE-R3 was significantly reduced in diabetic patients compared to non-diabetic control subjects whereas the expression of RAGE was significantly increased. Objective 3 (achieved) Type 2 diabetic patients recruited were treated with thiamine 300 mg daily for a period of 3 months to investigate the effect of thiamine on AGE clearance receptors and RAGE. Expression of RAGE was significantly reduced by thiamine and there was also a trend towards an increase in AGE-R3 expression.

777712.label: Major findings and research outcome
777712.value: Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) play an important role in the pathogenesis of diabetic vascular complications and they exert their biological effects via specific cell surface receptors. The binding of AGEs to RAGE drives the activation of proinflammatory signalling pathways and mediates many of the pathological effects of AGEs. There are a number of RAGE isoforms and the soluble forms of RAGE can act as a decoy for RAGE ligands and is a self-limiting means to block RAGE activation. We have investigated the mechanism(s) on how soluble forms of RAGE are generated and the regulation of these processes. We have shown that in vitro, insulin not only increases both full length RAGE and esRAGE expression, insulin can also stimulate the shedding of sRAGE from the membrane-bound receptor. This is consistent with our clinical data showing that type 1 diabetic patients have higher serum levels of esRAGE and sRAGE and these results have been published in Diabetic Medicine. We have further shown that the sheddase ADAM10 plays a major role in both constitutive and insulin-induced shedding of RAGE and these data have been published in PLoS One. We have found that insulin can increase ADAM10 expression and activity in vitro and serum ADAM10 level was increased in type 1 diabetes. Taken together, our data suggest that insulin plays a significant role in the regulation of RAGE and soluble RAGE isoforms. The binding of AGEs to “clearance” receptors detoxifies AGEs and promotes their degradation and clearance. The AGE-receptor complex (AGE-R1, AGE-R2 and AGE-R3) is expressed in macrophages. We have evaluated the expression of RAGE and AGE clearance receptors in peripheral blood mononuclear cells in type 2 diabetic patients. Our data show that the balance of expression of cellular receptors for AGEs is altered and favors the activation of cellular pathways by RAGE-AGEs interaction. The expression of AGE-R1 and AGE-R2 was similar between diabetic patients and non-diabetic controls, but AGE-R3 was significantly reduced in diabetic patients whereas the expression of RAGE was significantly increased. As a result, the final outcome of activation by AGEs might be tipped towards injurious proinflammatory cellular events. These findings have been presented in the American Diabetes Association Annual Scientific Meeting. We have proceeded to determine whether treatment with thiamine can enhance AGE clearance receptor expression in type 2 diabetes. Expression of RAGE was significantly reduced by thiamine and there was also a trend towards an increase in AGE-R3 expression.

777712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777712.value: We have identified ADAM10 as the major sheddase involved in the ectodomain shedding of RAGE and insulin increases ADAM10 expression. We plan to further investigate whether it is feasible to modulate ADAM10 activity by pharmacologic means and stimulate shedding of RAGE. Since we have found that RAGE expression was significantly reduced by thiamine and there was also a trend towards an increase in AGE-R3 expression, we intend to perform further study using benfotiamine, a synthetic derivative of vitamin B1, which has a greater inhibitory effect on glycation than thiamine.

777712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777712.value: Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) play an important role in the development and progression of diabetic vascular complications. The cellular receptors for AGEs are important mediators of the biological effects of these compounds and the interaction between AGEs and their numerous receptors can lead to either favorable or unfavorable outcomes. We have shown that the expression of the receptor that mediates the harmful effects of AGEs (RAGE) is increased whereas the expression of the clearance receptor that detoxifies AGEs is reduced in patients with diabetes. Hence, the balance of the expression pattern of cellular receptors for AGEs is altered in diabetes and favors the activation of injurious proinflammatory cellular pathways. We have identified A Disintegrin And Metalloprotease 10 (ADAM10) as the main sheddase that is responsible for cleavage of RAGE at the cell surface to form soluble isoforms of the receptor and this process is stimulated by insulin. Cleavage of RAGE is a means to self-limit the activation of RAGE and the soluble isoforms generated can also act as decoy for AGEs. Hence, modulation of ADAM10 activity may potentially be a novel therapeutic approach to lessen the pathological effects of AGEs.

778012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
778012.value: 肥胖被認為是一種慢性低度炎症的狀態，其脂肪組織是炎症反應的主要部位。在肥胖脂肪組織中，巨噬細胞和淋巴T細胞高度集中，其產生的細胞因子、趨化因子造成對脂肪細胞的浸潤。而脂肪組織的炎症誘發了肥胖相關的代謝綜合症。因此，研究脂肪組織中抑制和促進炎症的信號通路對尋找控制或抑制脂肪組織炎症的方法具有重要的臨床指導意義。 當化學刺激作用於血管內皮細胞膜時，可使花生四烯酸在環氧合酶的作用下氧化，並在前列腺素E合酶作用下合成前列腺素E2（PGE2）。在巨噬細胞中，PGE2作為一種內源性的抗炎介質能結合其受體4（EP4）並減弱脂多醣（LPS）誘導的促炎因子的基因表達，諸如單核細胞趨化蛋白-1（MCP-1）、干擾素誘導蛋白10 （IP10）、白介素-8 （IL-8）、巨噬細胞炎症蛋白（MIP）-1α 以及巨噬細胞炎症蛋白-1β（MIP-1β）等。目前尚未有相關文獻報道EP4和脂肪炎症的關係，但我們可以推測EP4可能在脂肪組織中發揮着與在巨噬細胞中類似的抗炎作用。 預實驗表明EP4在脂肪組織的局部炎症反應中發揮著至關重要的作用。尤其是，PGE2抑制了脂多醣誘導的脂肪組織炎症，而這種抑制效應在EP4拮抗劑的作用下抵消了。從敲除EP4基因小鼠分離的脂肪組織中，我們並沒有觀察到PGE2有類似的抗炎作用。除此以外，我們有證據表明敲除EP4的小鼠具有明顯改變的代謝表現型。綜合考慮，這些初步的發現支持了我們的假設，EP4的激活抑制了脂肪組織的炎症反應。在本研究中，我們將使用基因遺傳學及藥理學的方法技術分別從體內體外模型中去考察EP4在對抗脂肪組織炎症中的作用。本研究的最終目的也為了闡明EP4是否可以作為潛在的靶點去緩和肥胖誘導的炎症及其相關並發症。 本研究組首次發現報道了EP4在巨噬細胞、動脈瘤以及動脈粥樣硬化中的作用。且本項目研究員及合作研究員在前列腺素、炎症、代謝及心血管領域具有豐富的專業背景知識，而這些也使得我們有足夠的能力去完成所計劃的實驗。 該項目的研究結果也將會提供充分的理論依據去證明EP4是否可作為一個潛在的治療靶點來治療代謝炎症相關疾病。

778012.label: Realisation of objectives
778012.value: We have conducted all proposed experiments and achieved all the objectives as per original application. We have confirmed that PGE2-EP4 signaling functions as an anti-inflammatory mediator in adipose tissue. We have illustrated that deficiency of EP4 enhances adipose tissue inflammation in mice and that EP4 agonist decreases adipose tissue inflammation and protects mice against obesity. We have provided evidence that targeting EP4 may mitigate inflammation in adipose tissue. Interestingly, we have incidentally found mice lacking EP4 manifest disrupted lipid metabolism attributable to impaired triglyceride clearance – although the clinical relevance of these findings need to be clarified. These preliminary data have opened more research questions – which is worthy of investigation in the future. The grant has helped us to generate two publications at international journals (one more in preparation), five international conference presentations, and trained a total of seven undergraduate and postgraduate students.

778012.label: Major findings and research outcome
778012.value: Major finding 1: We have tested the hypothesis that endogenous prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) suppresses inflammation in fat by activating EP4 receptors. In mouse adipose tissue, PGE2 attenuated lipopolysaccharide -induced mRNA and protein expression of chemokines, including interferon-γ-inducible protein 10 and macrophage-inflammatory protein-1α. A selective EP4 antagonist reversed, and structurally different selective EP4 agonists mimicked these actions of PGE2. Adipose tissue derived from EP4-deficient mice did not display the same response to PGE2. These findings established the involvement of EP4 receptors in the anti-inflammatory effect of PGE2 in adipose tissue. Experiments performed on adipose tissue from high-fat–fed mice demonstrated EP4-dependent attenuation of inflammation during diet-induced obesity. Furthermore, adipose tissue and systemic inflammation was enhanced in high-fat-fed EP4-deficient mice compared to wild-type littermates, and in high-fat fed untreated C57BL/6 mice compared to mice treated with EP4 agonist. These findings provide in vivo evidence that PGE2-EP4 signaling modulates inflammation. Major finding 2: Upon high fat feeding, EP4 knockout mice displayed reduced body weight gain compared with their wild type littermates. The present study investigated the cause of the lean phenotype in EP4 knockout mice. These mice show a 68.8% reduction in weight gain with diminished fat mass, which could not be attributed to reduced food intake, fat malabsorption or increased energy expenditure. Plasma triglycerides in EP4 knockout mice were elevated by 244.9%. The increase in plasma triglycerides is independent of changes in hepatic very low density lipoprotein (VLDL)-triglyceride production or intestinal chylomicron-triglyceride synthesis. However, VLDL-triglyceride clearance is drastically impaired in EP4 knockout mice. The absence of EP4 in mice compromised the activation of lipoprotein lipase (LPL), the key enzyme responsible for trafficking plasma triglycerides into peripheral tissues. Deficiency of EP4 reduced hepatic mRNA expression of the transcriptional factor cAMP response element binding protein H and LPL activators, including apolipoprotein A5 (by 40.2%) and apolipoprotein C2. In summary, the lean phenotype of EP4 deficient mice resulted from reduction in adipose tissue and other peripheral organs accretion due to impaired triglyceride clearance, identifying a new dimension in the roles of endogenous EP4.

778012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
778012.value: By utilizing both pharmacological and genetic approaches we collectively establish a primary role for EP4 receptors in the anti-inflammatory action of PGE2 in mouse adipose tissue and illustrate that targeting these receptors could represent a novel strategy to mitigate obesity-induced inflammation. Although the immunosuppressive actions of prostaglandin E2 are well recognized, the adverse effects related to broad biological activities among its four EP receptors make it impractical as a therapeutic agent. Compounds that interact specifically with the immune-suppressive EP4 receptor may allow a wider, more practical exploitation in the therapy of inflammatory diseases. Now, the anti-inflammatory role of EP4 has been demonstrated in adipose tissue, but the efficacy and safety of EP4 agonists in combating obesity needs to be established and its usefulness in humans is completely unknown – which warrants investigation in the future.

778012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
778012.value: We have confirmed that PGE2-EP4 signaling functions as an anti-inflammatory mediator in adipose tissue. We have illustrated that deficiency of EP4 enhances adipose tissue inflammation in mice and that EP4 agonist decreases adipose tissue inflammation and protects mice against obesity. We have provided evidence that targeting EP4 may mitigate inflammation in adipose tissue. Interestingly, we have incidentally found mice lacking EP4 manifest disrupted lipid metabolism attributable to impaired triglyceride clearance – although the clinical relevance of these findings need to be clarified. Our work has discovered new dimensions in the roles of endogenous EP4.

778212.label: Realisation of objectives
778212.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved by applying cell culture and molecular techniques as well as animal models of kidney inflammation and fibrosis, and an overview of how they have been achieved is summarized below. The details are presented in section 6.1 and the research output list are detailed in Part C. For objective 1: To explore the in vitro anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic potential of BM-MSCs in PTECs exposed to a protein-overload milieu Using a co-culture model of human proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTECs) and bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs), we showed that concomitant stimulation of BM-MSCs by albumin excess was a prerequisite for them to attenuate albumin-induced IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α, CCL-2, CCL-5 overexpression in PTECs. This finding delineates the anti-inflammatory potential of BM-MSCs. In addition, albumin induced tubular epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), as shown by E-cadherin loss and α-SMA, FN and collagen IV overexpression, was also prevented by BM-MSC co-culture. This finding delineates the anti-fibrotic potential of BM-MSCs For objective 2: To dissect the paracrine and cellular mechanisms (in BM-MSCs) and intracellular signaling pathways (in PTECs) governing these potential beneficial effects of BM-MSCs BM-MSC mitigated albumin-induced IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α, CCL-2, CCL-5 overexpression in PTECs was partly mediated via deactivation of tubular NF-κB signaling. This finding delineates a major intracellular signaling pathway governing their beneficial effects. Albumin-overloaded BM-MSCs per se retained their tri-lineage differentiation capacity and overexpressed hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) and TNFα-stimulating gene (TSG)-6 via P38 and NF-κB signaling. Albumin-induced tubular CCL-2, CCL-5 and TNF-α overexpression were suppressed by recombinant HGF treatment, while the upregulation of α-SMA, FN and collagen IV was attenuated by recombinant TSG-6. Neutralizing HGF and TSG-6 abolished the anti-inflammatory and anti-EMT effects of BM-MSC co-culture in albumin-induced PTECs, respectively. This finding delineates the paracrine and cellular mechanisms of BM-MSCs in mitigating albumin-induced inflammation and fibrosis in PTECs. For objective 3: To investigate the potential in vivo renoprotective efficacy of exogenously applied BM-MSCs in a protein-overload nephropathy animal model of renal injury that resemble important causes of CKD in human albumin-overloaded mice treated with mouse BM-MSCs had markedly reduced BUN, tubular CCL-2 and CCL-5 expression, α-SMA and collagen IV accumulation independent of changes in proteinuria. Exogenous BM-MSCs were detected in their kidneys. These data suggest anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic roles of BM-MSCs on renal tubular cells under a protein overloaded condition, and these effects are mediated via the paracrine action of HGF and TSG-6.

778212.label: Major findings and research outcome
778212.value: We showed that the secretome of BM-MSCs acted on tubular cells and contributed to their anti-inflammatory and anti-EMT effects. Specifically, the stress of albumin overload activated BM-MSCs and enhanced their anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic potential. HSA-stimulated BM-MSCs attenuated the activation of NF-κB signaling in PTECs when subjected to albumin overload. Furthermore, albumin brought about upregulation of a number of paracrine factors in BM-MSCs. Among the 34 factors detected by cytokine array studies to be induced by albumin, the anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic factors, HGF and TSG-6, were regulated by P38 and NF-κB, as inhibition of these pathways prevented the HGF and TSG-6 responses. We showed that recombinant HGF dose-dependently attenuated HSA-induced mRNA expression of TNF-α, CCL-2 and CCL-5 in PTECs, while TSG-6 prevented tubular EMT by inhibiting upregulation of α-SMA, FN and collagen IV. In addition, these two factors at least partially contributed to the modulatory effect of BM-MSCs on tubular inflammation and EMT. Since BM-MSCs and PTECs were grown in a physically separated co-culture setup, it can be inferred that HGF and TSG-6 secreted by BM-MSCs acted in a paracrine manner. This observation might provide one mechanism for MSCs to promote renal recovery. Finally, we showed in an animal model of overload proteinuria that BM-MSC treatment reduced serum BUN. Immunohistochemical staining further revealed that the suppressive effect of BM-MSCs on CCL-2 and CCL-5 protein expression mainly occurred in proximal tubular cells, which is consistent with our in vitro findings that BM-MSCs inhibited cytokine and chemokine expression in protein-overloaded PTECs. In addition, BM-MSCs treatment significantly attenuated the abnormally upregulated fibrotic markers such as α-SMA and collagen IV at both mRNA and protein levels in renal cortical tissue, supporting an additional antifibrotic effect of BM-MSCs. Immunohistochemical staining confirmed that tubular interstitial deposition of α-SMA and collagen IV was ameliorated by BM-MSC treatment. (Output 1, Part C). As these results shed light on the regenerative potential of MSCs in chronic kidney disease, and we took one step further to show that in the short-term adriamycin nephrosis model, iPS-MSCs conferred a substantial anti-apoptotic effect on tubular cells, associated with a downregulation of Bax and Bax/Bcl2 ratio and an upregulation of survivin expression. In vitro, conditioned medium from iPS-MSCs significantly limited albumin-induced tubular apoptosis and enhanced tubular proliferation (Output 2, Part C). We have used these novel findings to secure another competitive grant (Other impact, Part C) in 2014.

778212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
778212.value: Together, the results generated from this project suggest that BM-MSCs have the potential in reversing kidney inflammation and fibrosis, thereby preventing organ failure. Given that protein overload is a general phenomenon observed in most forms of chronic kidney disease (CKD), stem cell therapy using BM-MSCs or their derivatives has a distinct therapeutic potential for many different models of CKD, and one of which is iPS derived BM-MSCs. Our results lay a solid foundation for studying other biologic aspects using iPS derived BM-MSCs in the realm of chronic kidney disease and we have submitted another HMRF application which was successfully funded in the 2015/16 exercise.

778212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
778212.value: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is an important cause of mortality. CKD has risen from being the 36th commonest cause of loss of adjusted life years worldwide in 1990 to the 19th rank in 2013. This is mainly due to the lack of specific therapy. While stem cell therapy for heart and blood disorders has gathered momentum over the past decade, its utility in kidney regeneration is only beginning to be investigated. Our findings showed that bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) can ameliorate experimental models of CKD by antagonizing inflammation and fibrosis, both being important biologic responses to disease insult that prompts the progression to ultimate kidney failure. We further showed that an improved version of stem cells, called induced pluripotent stem cells, may be an even better form of stem cell therapy as shown in another disease model called Adriamycin nephrosis. All in all, our findings open the door for the development of new therapeutic targets to retard or even halt the progression of CKD to ESRD, and thus have the potential of saving millions of diabetic patients worldwide from having to undergo dialysis.

778312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
778312.value: 無機多聚磷酸（polyP），由幾十到幾百個的磷酸組成，是解開現代分子生物學一個重要疑團的關鍵。PolyP早於十九世紀在酵母中被發現（在某些物種，polyP的含量能達到細胞乾重量的10％以上），但之後卻像“分子化石”般被遺忘。直至二十世紀末才由已故的Arthur Kornberg領導的研究團隊，釐清polyP在生物學中多個範疇上既重要又基本的功能，例如能量學，信息傳導，壓力反應，細胞生長以及病原體的毒力。PolyP普遍地存在於很多生物當中，儘管現時對polyP在原核生物和真核生物的功能上取得重大進展，但在高等真核生物中，我們對polyP所擔當的角色仍知之甚少。 最近，我們已確定在分泌基質小泡的成骨細胞（其中一種重要的骨細胞）中含有大量polyP，而其濃度是在人體中觀察到的最高。細胞外polyP亦在受體調控的磷酸化中，扮演重要的信息傳遞的角色。此外，我們還觀察到polyP能被鹼性磷酸酶—礦化過程中一個重要的關鍵酶—水解。鹼性磷酸酶的分子缺陷會導致低磷酸酯脢症（hypophosphatasia），一種由骨礦化缺陷引起的骨代謝疾病。再者，鹼性磷酸酶也能引起與慢性腎病或糖尿病有關的血管鈣化。 雖然現在很清楚polyP在礦化及其信息傳遞起著關鍵作用，但無論是在分子機制或相互作用方面，我們對於polyP是如何控制並發揮其作用卻知道得很少。 在此，我們提出解開polyP在骨礦化功能上的精確機制。我們集合了多聚磷酸生物化學和酶學的專家（在香港大學的PI和CoI）以及礦化、鹼性磷酸酶和基質小泡蛋白組學專家（在里昂大學的兩位CoIs）組成一個跨學科的國際研究小組。 在第一階段，我們將會從包括鹼性磷酸酶的候選名單中測試出能水解polyP的蛋白酶，並確定該蛋白酶的活性將如何影響磷酸的數值以及在基質小泡和成骨細胞培養中的羥基磷灰石形成過程。在第二階段，我們將使用親和層析來確定目標蛋白酶與細胞外polyP的特異性結合。在第三階段，我們將應用生物物理技術來剖析蛋白-polyP的相互作用以及在前兩個階段歸納出的機制，從而確定這些結果在生物學上的意義。 總的來說，此項目將澄清大分子polyP與礦化之間的相互作用。引用Kornberg的話：此研究能令“make a forgotten polymer unforgettable”。

778512.label: Project Objectives
778512.value: -This project has one single over-arching objective and that is to quantify whether increased year-to-year variability of wildlife population growth-rates could significantly lower the stochastic growth rates of real species in the real world. 778512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
778512.value: 即使在短期内不会体现出来，野生动物种群的自然成倍增长依然具有着微妙而固定的数学含义，尽管这些含义还未曾被广泛的在自然环境中研究过，他们却很可能有巨大的生态影响。如果种群增长率存在着年际波动，那么能够量化实际增长率的随机增长率λs，将会低于表面平均增长率。一个在一年中减少了50%的种群将不能得到恢复如果他们在下一年中增长50%，这是由于半数种群数量50%的增长值远低全部种群50%的减少值。即使从增长率λ1=0.5和λ2=1.5似乎可以得到平均数1，种群实际最终只达到其原有数量的0.75倍。 事实上，“随机增长率” λs并不是年增长率的数学平均值，而是几何平均值。这种几何平均值不是通过增加种群的增长率，或者是除以种群数量(当 ̅ (Σ ) ⁄)。而是把它们相乘， 然后取倍数的幂（当λs =√Π )。其结果是当干扰波动增加时，λs的减少。而这恰恰几乎可以被减少到时间方差的一半。 这将无疑对于气候变化的生态效应具有重要含义。传统的研究多关注于平均气候属性的变化所产生的效应，但是如果气候的多变性持续加剧那么仅仅这一因素就可能增加野生动物种群的λ的年际变化同时降低其λs的数量值。尽管这些原理已经被理论人口学家良好的建立，我们仍然不明确它们在实际应用中的重要程度。虽然天气属性已经被众所周知会对野生动物种群的增长率产生影响，同时我们也知道气候正在变得更加多变，但我们却不了解这将会对λs产生大还是小的影响，也不清楚加剧的气候多变性所产生的生态效应与平均气候属性所产生的生态效应在尺度上的比较结果。 在香港，气候已经得到充分的研究，但是气候变化所带来的生态影响却没有得到足够的研究，并且同世界上其他地区一样，我们对于加剧的气候多变性对λs所产生的影响几乎一无所知。虽然数学理论已经被良好的建立起来，它和实际野生动物种群的相关程度还未被充分的量化。香港不仅有良好的长期气象数据，同时也拥有米埔自然保护区中自1979年起对国际重要湿地鸟类种群的长期变化的监测数据。我们将运用这些数据来初次检验是否加剧的气候多变性能够足够大到对这些野生动物增长率产生重大的生态影响。 如果我们发现加剧的气候多变性产生的效应大于平均气候属性产生的效应，这一结果将能对我们对于气候变化的生态效应的看法产生巨大的改变。这一研究不仅是为了浓厚的科学兴趣，更对香港乃至全球的生态、经济和社会具有重大意义。

778512.label: Realisation of objectives
778512.value: The original objectives have all been achieved, with several notable findings. Objective 1: this was the over-arching objective of the project and it has been achieved - we have found that the observed levels of variability in the short-term vital rates of wildlife populations can indeed substantially impact the stochastic rates of population growth in the longer term. Objective 2: as planned, we tackled the over-arching Objective 1 in the context of weather/climate impacts, and found that variability in temperature, particularly over shorter time-scales, can have important effects on the stochastic growth rates of wildlife populations in the long-term. Objective 3: as planned, using detailed long-term data on weather and on the bird populations of Mai Po Reserve in Hong Kong, we built analytical models of the relationships between population growth rates and temperature. The analytical methods which we developed included significant advances which allowed us: to partition the impacts of variability over different time-scales (daily, seasonal, and annual variability); to distinguish any effects of environmental covariates on detection probability from genuine effects on population growth rates per se; and to reconstruct the spatial distributions of migrant species during the breeding season when they are not in Hong Kong. The analysis for the Black-faced Spoonbill all went smoothly and no significant challenges were encountered. As outlined in the Interim Progress Report (June 2014), we studied Common Moorhens instead of Little Egrets, because the data for Little Egrets proved heterogeneous and challenging, with mixing of nomadic, migratory, and non-migratory sub-populations. In 2014, we also reported challenges of heterogeneity in the mark-recapture data for the two Prinia species, but after persevering we were able to construct workable models albeit with some caveats. Nonetheless, additional analyses were still completed for the substitute species Grey Plover as proposed at that time. While grappling with the Prinia data we also built models for a number of additional water bird species including Black-tailed Godwit and Saunders Gull. In all these species, relationships between population growth rates and temperature were detected. In most cases these were modelled as quadratic functions where population growth rate increased to an optimum and then decreased. For the two Prinia species, over the range of temperatures observed, we found that population growth rates were better modelled as accelerating functions of temperature. Objective 4: we succeeded in quantifying the stochastic population growth rate λs and found that the impacts of temperature variability could be substantial. We found that the effects can differ considerably between different species and that some forms of variability are much more important than others. In the Black-faced Spoonbill, temperature variability can reduce population growth rates λ by about half. In Common Moorhens, it can reduce it by about a quarter, and in both Prinia species there is actually a slight increase of just over 10%. In all species, seasonal variability in temperature was the main driver impacting stochastic population growth rates. The impacts of annual variability were found to be negligible, with reductions in population growth rates of only around 1%. In most of the species, the effect of daily variability in temperature was also negligible, except in Black-faced Spoonbills where it could reduce the population growth rates by about a third. Objective 5: We were able to model the impact of historical changes in variability, as compared with changing averages. Black-faced Spoonbills are migratory, and spend the summer in Korea, where temperature variability was found to have decreased from the 1950s to the late 1990s, but the effects of this were then cancelled out by quite a sharp increase in variability since then. Variability within Hong Kong itself, was much lower and did not show such pronounced trends. In the Black-faced Spoonbill, the impact of a change in variability was found to be comparable with the impact of a change in the average. For the other species which are resident in Hong Kong, the variability has not yet changed in a way which could have driven large changes in population growth rate. Objective 6: In future climate scenarios, variability is not yet so well-predicted as mean temperature, but we were able to model the impact of changing variability and compare it with the impact of a change in the mean. In the Common Moorhen we predict that any impact of changing temperature variability will be dwarfed by change in the mean temperature. In the Black-faced Spoonbill, sensitivity of population growth rates to mean and variance are more comparable, but while the impact of change in the variance is estimated with higher precision, the realized effect of changing variance is expected to be lower than the effect of changing mean temperature. In both Prinia species, the sensitivity of population growth rate to changing variability could be estimated with high precision, but the effect size is extremely small. As well as achieving these original objectives, further lines of inquiry have been developed.

778512.label: Major findings and research outcome
778512.value: The project has produced notable findings, some of which have challenged contemporary thinking on prominent issues. In achieving its central goal (Objective 1), we have shown that prevailing levels of environmental variability are large enough to have a substantial impact on the stochastic growth rates of wildlife populations. Here, focusing on the climatic component of environmental variability (Objective 2) and using long-term bird population data from the Mai Po Nature Reserve, we developed new analytical models which allowed us to partition out the effects of variability over annual, seasonal, and daily time scales (Objective 3). Across the four key species studied, we found that year-to-year temperature variability did indeed have only a minor impact (around 1%) on stochastic population growth rates, but we found that shorter-term variability, particularly seasonal variability, could have a substantial impact (Objective 4). For the migratory Black-faced Spoonbill, we found that temperature variability on the summer breeding grounds in Korea had shown appreciable trends through time, decreasing steadily from the 1950s until the late 1990s, and then increasing more rapidly since then, returning back to original levels (Objective 5). These changes were large enough to boost stochastic population growth rates over the first four decades, before falling back. Looking ahead, we modelled the impacts of future changes in temperature variability and compared them with the impact of a change in mean temperature (Objective 6). Findings differed between species. For Black-faced Spoonbills, we found that the sensitivity of stochastic population growth rates to temperature variability and mean temperature are more similar (Pickett et al. 2015, Section C.8). The analytical methods developed in this case are themselves a significant output of the project: they allow us to partition the impacts of variability at different time scales, and they allow us to distinguish effects of temperature on population growth from effects on detection probabilities. As well as looking at the impacts of temperature on Black-faced Spoonbills, we also considered the impacts of habitat loss and we predict that this, like changes in temperature, will also have a negative impact in coming decades, particularly in the wintering areas of Taiwan and southern China (Pickett et al. in review, Section C.8). Finally, we have conducted a review of how climatic variability and other factors may drive the redistribution of species, drawing together what is known, and identifying areas for future research (Bonebrake et al, in press, Section C.8).

778512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
778512.value: The project has yielded several interesting findings, and aside from our main current priority which is to complete publication of these core project results, our findings have highlighted several ways in which this investigation could also be taken further. We have found that variability in temperature can impact population growth rates substantially, but one striking feature of our findings is that the impact differs noticeably between species. Furthermore, climatologists are constantly developing and improving their ability to predict future climate scenarios, and it would be valuable to update our own prediction of climate impacts as new climate models appear and develop. In particular, the climatological predictions of temperature variability are not yet as well-developed as the climatological predictions of temperature itself, and as this field develops, our ability to quantify future impacts of changing variability will develop as well. Especially in endotherms, it is likely that there will be many different mechanisms through which temperature affects population growth rates. There may be direct effects on thermal physiology, but there may also be diverse indirect effects on the species they eat, and on the wider ecological systems upon which they depend. It would be valuable to explore these mechanisms further.

778512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
778512.value: In the relationship between organisms and their environments, it may seem natural to focus on average conditions, but environments are rarely static and we also need to consider fluctuations around the average. If it is sometimes too hot and sometimes too cold, an environment which might seem perfect on average may in fact be quite inhospitable. For several decades, theorists have known about the mathematics of how this environmental variability could impact the long-term growth rates of wildlife populations, but there had been few attempts to quantify whether it is actually important in practice. Those studies which had looked at the question had concentrated on year-to-year variability and they had found that the impact was extremely small. Here we developed new analytical approaches which allowed us to estimate the impact of variability over different time scales; considering not only year-to-year variation, but also shorter-term seasonal and day-to-day variation. We applied these models to long-term population data on four bird species from Hong Kong’s Mai Po Reserve. We found that temperature variability could have important impacts on population growth rates, reducing them by as much as half in some cases, with seasonal variability being the most important component driving this.

779312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
779312.value: ATM信号传导对鼻咽上皮细胞中EBV裂解复制的作用 鼻咽癌是在生活中国南方地区包括香港的广东人中的常见癌症。EBV病毒感染与鼻咽癌有密切的相关性，并被认为是导致鼻咽癌的原因之一。体外实验揭示，EBV容易感染人类B淋巴细胞，并导致其转化成不断增殖的类淋巴母细胞系。EBV在人记忆B淋巴细胞中以潜伏形态存在，形成终生持续感染。人上皮细胞被认为在EBV裂解复制，以及释放可经唾液传播具传染能力的EBV病毒颗粒的过程中起重要的作用。虽然在上皮细胞中的EBV复制是EBV感染的一个关键步骤，但是由于缺乏有代表性的细胞体系，其复制及感染的诸多过程尚待探索。我们实验室已经建立了一系列已有EBV感染的细胞系，其中一些可被诱导出现EBV裂解复制并释放具传染性的EBV病毒颗粒。在诱导EBV裂解复制的过程中，我们可检测到ATM的激活。ATM激活在DNA损伤和修复反应中的作用已有众多文献报道。但ATM在EBV裂解感染中的作用还未知，甚至到目前有相互矛盾的结果。我们的初期结果显示，在用特异的ATM抑制剂抑制ATM的活性或用针对ATM的shRNA 敲下ATM的表达后，有EBV感染的鼻咽癌细胞中的EBV裂解复制以及具传染性的EBV病毒颗粒的产生均有明显降低。另外，我们还观察到ATM信号传导的重要成分在细胞里的聚集，包括磷酸化H2AX在EBV复制区的的聚集。这些结果提示，ATM激活对有EBV感染的细胞中的EBV裂解复制有积极的作用。我们推测，ATM激活和磷酸化H2AX的聚集（DNA 损伤反应的标志）可能对EBV复制区的形成提供平台，以有助于EBV DNA的复制。我们将对ATM通路的关键成分，包括MRN, MDC1和H2AX，进行特异基因敲除实验，研究其在EBV复制区的形成和裂解期EBV DNA复制中的介入作用。通过本研究，我们将建立并诠释ATM信号传导对鼻咽癌细胞中EBV裂解复制的作用。我们将获得关于ATM信号成分与EBV病毒复制关键蛋白之间的相互反应的重要信息。EBV的裂解感染对肿瘤的发生和发展有关。研究调控EBV裂解感染的机理对了解鼻咽癌的发生以及对鼻咽癌的有效治疗提供新的治疗标靶均有启发意义。

779312.label: Realisation of objectives
779312.value: Objective 1. Using the HONE1-EBV cell model, which could be used to undergo lytic induction by treatment with TPA/sodium butyrate or expression of BZLF1 lytic EBV protein, we have confirmed the co-localization of the ATM signaling components (including p-ATM (S1981), p-H2AX (S139), pKAP1, RNF8, MDC1, p53BP1 and others) with the EBV lytic proteins (Zta and Rta) and core replication proteins (including Zta, Rta, EA-D, BALF2 and others). The ATM signaling components and core replication proteins of EBV also co-localized with BrdU incorporation and with EBV genome (confirmed by FISH). This close interaction suggests functional interaction of ATM signaling component with replication of EBV episome during lytic reactivation of EBV infection. Interaction of ATM signaling components and viral replication components was also confirmed by immunoprecipitation. Objective 2. We further elucidate the action of ATM in lytic reactivation of EBV. We identify a key target of ATM signaling is phosphorylation of Sp1 at serine residue 101. We performed mutational analysis to confirm the role of Sp1 mediating the ATM action. Sp1 may serve as a key mediator to recruit the viral replication component to the lytic replication site of the EBV genome. The interaction of Sp1 with viral replication proteins e.g. BALF2 and BALF5 was also confirmed by immunoprecipitation. Objective 3. Inhibition of ATM signaling including siRNA silencing of ATM expression as well as the use of specific inhibitor of ATM abolished the formation of H2AX foci as well as lytic replication of EBV genome. Silencing of key components of H2AX foci including MDC1 and RNF8 also abolished the lytic replication of EBV in the presence of EBV lytic protein, BZLF1. The failure to undergo viral replication due to defective ATM signaling, and abortive formation of H2AX foci was further confirmed by RT-PCR determination of EBV episome copy in HONE1-EBV cells and generation of infectious EBV particles harvested from HONE1-EBV induced to undergo lytic replication. Interestingly, we have also identified that the EBV-encoded lytic protein (BZLF1) could also intervene interaction of MDC1 and RNF8 suggesting a role of lytic reactivation of EBV in genomic instability of EBV-infected nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
