779312.label: Major findings and research outcome
779312.value: ATM activation has been reported in lytic reactivation of EBV in infected cells. However, the role of ATM activation in regulating lytic infection of EBV remains unclear. In our study, we confirmed that ATM plays an important role in the lytic replication of EBV in human epithelial cells. We further elucidate the role of ATM in lytic reactivation of EBV using epithelial cell system by identifying its interacting partners and key mediator. The ATM, together with multiple crucial functional components involved in DNA repair, forms a functional complex and interacts with the core replication proteins of EBV including Zta, Rta, EA-D, BALF2 etc.. The formation of this large functional complex is mediated by the activation of Sp1 by ATM (a kinase) which recruits the key proteins in this functional complex. The ATM targets phosphorylation of Sp1 at serine residue 101 to initiate the cascade leading to the formation of the replication complex of EBV. Inhibition of ATM signaling effectively abolished the formation of H2AX foci as well as lytic replication of EBV genome. Silencing of key components of H2AX foci, e.g.MDC1 and RNF8, also abolished the lytic replication of EBV. These findings have been accepted for publication (Hau et al., J. Virology, 2015). We further showed that the EBV encoded lytic viral protein, BZLF1, may induce genomic instability in EBV-infected cells by interfering the action of key ATM components e.g. RNF8 and MDC1; hence affecting DNA repair in EBV-infected epithelial cells (Yang et al., Lab Investigation, 2015)

779312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
779312.value: The elucidation of ATM in lytic reactivation of EBV may lead to the identification of new therapeutic targets to prevent or inhibit replication of EBV episome in infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Accumulating evidences have indicated that the development and progression of nasopharyngeal carcinoma are associated with EBV infection. Inhibition of replication of EBV episome in infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells may provide an effective way to control EBV replication which may have direct impact on growth and malignant properties of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The finding that EBV-encoded BZLF1 interferes interaction of key components of DNA damage repair signaling molecules suggests a role of lytic EBV infection in development and progression of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Hence targeting lytic EBV proteins or EBV lytic reactivation may suppress progression and development of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The future directions will include examination of the effects of inhibition of lytic reactivation of EBV on progression of nasopharyngeal carcinoma in preclinical in vivo and in vitro nasopharyngeal carcinoma models. Current chemotherpeutic agents readily induce DNA damage and induce lytic reactivation of EBV. Our data suggests that inclusion of inhibitors of DNA damage repair and/or silencing of EBV lytic genes may have therapeutic benefits in treatment of nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

779312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
779312.value: Current treatment of nasopharyngeal carcinoma often induces DNA damage and lytic reactivation of EBV. Our study confirms the role of key DNA damage repair kinase, ATM, in playing a rucial role in reactivation of EBV by phosphorylation of residue 101 of Sp1 to recruits viral DNA replication proteins to form EBV replication compartments. We also showed that lytic reactivation of EBV and the expression of viral lytic gene, namely BZLF1, induces genomic instability in EBV-infected epithelial cells through interfering interaction of key components of ATM signaling cascade. Based on the findings from this study, a role of ATM and lytic reactivation of EBV in promotion of progression of nasopharyngeal carcinoma is proposed. Our study has contribute to the understanding of development and progression of nasopharyngeal carcinoma and open up novel treatment targets in the treatment of nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

779512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
779512.value: 近來,心功能衰竭(心衰)的治療有了長足發展。儘管如此，在香港乃至世界範圍內，心衰由於其高發病率、高死亡率及高醫療費用消耗，仍是目前重要的健康問題。神經激素阻斷是藥物治療收縮性心衰的關鍵機制。腎素-血管緊張素-醛固酮（RAAS）系統以及交感神經（SNS）系統阻斷藥的應用大大降低了心衰病人的發病率及死亡率。然而，由於左心室心肌重塑自心肌損害之初就已經開始，心衰的發病率及死亡率仍居高不下。持續過度的交感神經興奮與心衰發病過程密切相關，并增加其死亡率。因此，臨床上應用β受體阻滯劑拮抗SNS系統來治療心衰。遺憾的是，有相當一部份心衰患者對β受體阻滯劑產生耐受或者達不到最佳應用劑量。因此，一種新型調節SNS系統的非藥物治療方法可能會改善臨床癥狀和/或預後。 最近，有研究表明腎臟交感神經軸參與了心衰的病理生理過程。在心衰患者中，腎臟感知傳入神經信號增加直接影響中樞交感神經的傳出，從而導致整體交感神經張力過高。眾所周知，除了心臟性去甲腎上腺素過多，腎性去甲腎上腺素過多在交感神經激動中也起了重要作用。也就是說，心衰病人的腎臟交感神經傳入信號增加可導致腎血流降低及RASS系統激活。RAAS系統激活引起血管緊張素II及醛固酮增加繼而引起血壓升高及鈉潴留。交感神經興奮加重左室重塑，通過以下途徑：去甲腎上腺素、血管緊張素II和醛固酮的直接作用；以及血容量增加、動脈壓升高導致鈉潴留的間接作用。因此，腎臟交感神經軸是治療心衰新方法的合理靶點。遺憾的是，目前沒有藥物能直接作用于腎臟交感神經軸，即使神經激素治療的益處源自于對RAAS系統的拮抗，而RAAS系統卻部份受腎性腎上腺素控制。 試驗性研究表明，腎去神經支配術是一種治療心衰的新型非藥物治療方法，此方法同時切斷腎交感神經軸的傳入支與傳出支。相對於外科手術，經導管腎去神經支配術是創傷更小的一種術式。此種術式已經被用來治療難治性高血壓，難治性高血壓具有與心衰相似的腎交感神經軸過度興奮的病理生理機制。所以，這可能是一種有效治療心衰的新方法。我們計劃通過臨床相關的缺血性心衰大型動物模型，研究經導管去腎交感神經術在左室功能及重塑方面的長期作用以及其可能存在的潛在影響。此研究結果將為心肌梗死後心衰患者的治療提供重要依據：作為非藥物治療新方法，經導管腎去交感神經術能有效改善左室心肌重塑和功能。

779512.label: Realisation of objectives
779512.value: To address Objective 1, we performed catheter-based radiofrequency (RF) bilateral renal denervation (RD) in 8 adult pigs and compared with 8 controls with ischemic HF induced by myocardial infarction (MI) via coronary embolization of left circumflex artery followed by rapid ventricular pacing for 4 weeks (MI+HF). All animals were treated with daily oral metoprolol ZOK (50 mg) plus ramipril (2.5 mg). Catheter-based RD was performed using the EnligHTN System (St. Jude Medical) that consists of an expandable basket with 4 electrodes to deliver the RF energy. We performed serial echocardiogram and invasive assessment on the index of cardiac contractility (dP/dtmax/IP) to assess left ventricular function. Our results showed that RD significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction as determined by echocardiogram (+9.6% vs + 2.1%, P<0.05), and increased the dP/dtmax/IP as compared with control group (P<0.05). Moreover, these parameters at 10 weeks were significant improved in the RD group as compared with their MI+ HF status, but not in the control group. To address Objective 2, we measured serum B-type natriuretic peptides (BNP), serum norepinephrine (NE) levels at different sites as baseline, immediately after MI (post-MI), at MI+HF and at 10 weeks follow-up. Moreover, detailed histological analysis on the renal sympathetic nerve was determined at both renal arteries. Our results showed that there was non-significant reduction in serum BNP at 10 weeks after RD as compared with controls. However, both the arterial and coronary sinus NE (P<0.05), and renal NE spillover (-54%, P=0.06) at 10 weeks were decreased in RD group only as compared with MI+HF status, but not in the control group. Histological examination showed significant reduction of renal sympathetic efferent nerves (tyrosine hydroxylase+) at proximal, middle and distal portion of renal artery after RD as compared with control group (-65%, P<0.05). In conclusion, we have successfully achieved all our study objectives in this project and demonstrated that bilateral RD using catheter-based RF to destroy renal nerves and reduce renal NE spillover is a potential novel non-pharmacological approach for treatment of HF.

779512.label: Major findings and research outcome
779512.value: Catheter-based radiofrequency (RF) renal denervation (RD) has been shown to decrease renal norepinephrine (NE) spillover in animal model and human with hypertension. Nevertheless, the therapeutic effect of RD on renal NE spillover and cardiac function in systolic heart failure (HF) is unknown. In this project, we performed bilateral RD in 8 adult pigs and compared with 8 controls with ischemic HF induced by myocardial infarction (MI) via coronary embolization of left circumflex artery followed by rapid ventricular pacing for 4 weeks (MI+HF). All animals were treated with daily oral metoprolol ZOK (50 mg) plus ramipril (2.5 mg). Catheter-based RD was performed using the EnligHTN System (St. Jude Medical) that consists of an expandable basket with 4 electrodes to deliver the RF energy. We performed serial echocardiogram and invasive assessment on the index of cardiac contractility (dP/dtmax/IP) and measured serum B-type natriuretic peptides (BNP), NE levels at different sites as baseline, immediately after MI (post-MI), at MI+HF and at 10 weeks follow-up. Moreover, detailed histological analysis on the renal sympathetic nerve was determined at both renal arteries. Our results showed that RD significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction as determined by echocardiogram, and increased the dP/dtmax/IP as compared with control group (P<0.05). While there was only non-significant reduction in BNP, both the arterial and coronary sinus NE (P<0.05), and renal NE spillover (-54%, P=0.06) at 10 weeks were decreased in RD group only as compared with MI+HF status, but not in the control group. Histological examination showed significant reduction of renal sympathetic efferent nerves (tyrosine hydroxylase+) at proximal, middle and distal portion of renal artery after RD as compared with control group (-65%, P<0.05). In conclusion, in porcine model of ischemic HF, bilateral RD using catheter-based RF effectively destroy renal nerves to decrease renal NE spillover and improves left ventricular contractile function compared with medical therapy alone. Our findings suggest that bilateral RD using catheter-based RF to destroy renal nerves and reduce renal NE spillover is a potential novel non-pharmacological approach on top of conventional medical therapy for treatment of HF. Based on these findings, we have presented two abstracts in major international cardiology congress and the full publication is now under preparation.

779512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
779512.value: In a clinical relevant large animal model of ischemic HF, our findings suggest that bilateral RD using catheter-based RF to destroy renal nerves and reduce renal NE spillover is a potential novel non-pharmacological approach on top of conventional medical therapy for treatment of HF. These results should provide important proof-of principle data to perform clinical trial to investigate the safety and efficacy of this approach for treatment of patients with HF.

779512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
779512.value: Despite recent advances in treatment, heart failure (HF) continues to be a major health problem in Hong Kong and worldwide owing to its high prevalence morbidity, mortality and health care burden. Neurohormonal blockade is the key to pharmacological management of patients with systolic HF. Persistent and excessive activation of sympathetic tone is associated with progression of HF and increased mortality. Recent studies suggest that a “sympathorenal axis” may be involved in the pathophysiology of HF. Experimental studies have suggested that renal denervation is a novel non-pharmacological therapeutic approach that directly targets both the efferent and afferent limb of the sympathorenal axis for treatment of HF. Catheter-based renal denervation is a less-invasive and morbid therapy than other potential surgical options to achieve renal denervation, and has been applied in patients with refractory hypertension that shares a similar pathophysiology of excessive activation of sympathorenal axis. Our results showed that catheter-based renal denervation on cardiac function at 10 weeks follow-up in a clinically relevant large animal model of ischemic HF. The results of this study provide important insight into the development of novel non-pharmacological therapy with catheter-based renal denervation to improve cardiac function in HF.

779712.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
779712.value: 脂肪组织是重要的代谢和内分泌器官。减少肥胖和改进脂肪功能可以保持能量平衡和防止老化疾病。 SIRT1是一种细胞内信号蛋白调节蛋白质的乙酰化状态。它具有潜在的抗衰老药理活性剂。 SIRT1的抗老化功能主要是由于其对能量代谢的调节作用。我们的实验室已设计出SIRT1脂肪组织选择性转基因小鼠。 在这些小鼠中获得的结果表明，脂肪组织增加SIRT1的活性可提高能源平衡和全身胰岛素的敏感性。 重要的是，脂肪组织SIRT1的功能改变影响生物素的含量，以及生物素依赖酶的活性。现有的临床和药理的证据支持生物素补充在糖尿病动物和人类的作用。 本研究的目的是阐明SIRT1调节生物素和生物素依赖的酶活性，以及如何影响脂质代谢血管功能。预计结果将进一步阐明SIRT1的抗衰老机制，并发展SIRT1-在老化相关的代谢和血管疾病的靶标治疗。

779712.label: Realisation of objectives
779712.value: Objective 1: We have optimized a HPLC method for biotin quantification and evaluated genes involved in biotin uptake (MCT1 and SMVT), ligation (HCS), and hydrolysis (biotinidase). The results demonstrate that the decreased biotin content in AD-SIRT1-TG mice was not due to the direct regulation of these genes by SIRT1. On the other hand, the enzyme, acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) was down-regulated by SIRT1 over-expression and the decreased ACC protein level led to the reduced biotin accumulation in adipose tissues of AD-SIRT1-TG mice. This conclusion was further confirmed by treatment with both siRNA and ACC inhibitors in mice. Since ACC act as intracellular biotin reservoir, SIRT1 negatively regulate biotin level by targeting ACC. In this part of work, we have also monitored the biotin homeostasis of a transgenic mouse line overexpressing the SIRT1 mutant, H363Y. The results demonstrated that when SIRT1 function was inhibited, biotin accumulation in adipose tissues was significantly enhanced. These mice also exhibited an increase of histone biotinylation which induced abnormal epigenetic modifications and chromatin remodeling. In addition, ACC isoforms ACC2 (the mitochondria form of ACC), rather than ACC1 contributed to biotin homeostasis in adipose tissue. The new anti-ageing concept of "Prevention of the biotin excess by adipose SIRT1" has been summarized in our review article published in "Diabetes & Metabolism Journal". Objective 2: The molecular events between acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) and SIRT1 was investigated on both in vitro and in vivo models. The result demonstrated that SIRT1 deacetylases ACC and mediates its degradation. ACC is the major storage reservoir for intracellular biotin. Biotin binds to the biotin carboxyl carrier protein (BCCP) of ACC. Mutation of the biotinylation site on BCCP inhibited the regulation of this protein by SIRT1. Furthermore, biotin supplementation treatment inhibited SIRT1-mediated degradation of ACC. In vitro deacetylation assay demonstrated that biotin, and its metabolite, biotinyl-5'-AMP, acted as SIRT1 inhibitors by competitively occupying the binding pocket of NAM and NAD. The above results have been published in American Journal of Translational Research. Objective 3: Deterioration of adipose function represents the one of the most important determinant of ageing. In this part of work, we found that selective overexpression of a dominant negative mutant of SIRT1, SIRT1(H363Y), in adipose tissues accelerates ageing in mice by disrupting the chromatin remodeling process at the epigenetic levels. These mice developed hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia, ectopic lipid deposition, insulin resistance and glucose intolerance at a much younger age than their wild type littermates. The metabolic defects attributed largely to the enhanced accumulation of biotin in adipose tissues, which inhibited endogenous SIRT1 activity, leading to decreased lipid storage capacity and adiponectin production. The enzyme acetyl-CoA carboxylase 2 plays an important role in biotin accumulation within adipose tissue of SIRT1(H363Y) overexpression mice. Calorie restriction prevented biotin accumulation in adipose tissues, abolished abnormal histone biotinylation and completely restored the metabolic and adipose functions of these mice. On the other hand, overexpression SIRT1 in adipose tissue exhibited calorie restriction mimicked phenotyping by down-regulation biotin accumulation. Furthermore, the effects of CR were mimicked by short term restriction of biotin intake, suggesting an approach potentially translatable for human to prevent ageing associated metabolic disorders. The above results have been published in the top journal of the field “Diabetes”.

779712.label: Major findings and research outcome
779712.value: Major finding 1: SIRT1 expression and activity decline progressively in adipose tissue. Overexpression of SIRT1 in adipose tissue prevents ageing-induced hyperglycemia, dyslipidiemia, ectopic lipid deposition, insulin resistance and glucose intolerance. [please refer to the summary in Pharmacology & Therapeutics 2012] Major finding 2: SIRT1 in adipose tissue reduces biotin accumulation, an effect also elicited by calorie restriction or limiting the intake of dietary biotin. Dysfunction in adipose SIRT1 enhances biotin accumulation and accelerates metabolic ageing. [please refer to the publication in AJTR 2013] Major finding 3: SIRT1 regulates biotin content in adipose tissue by counter-regulating acetyl-CoA carboxylase 2, a major intra-cellular reservoir of biotin and the regulator of its metabolism. [please refer to Diabetes 2015] Major finding 4: Biotin accumulation in adipose tissue causes abnormal epigenetic modifications of histone, in turn inhibiting SIRT1-mediated deacetylation reactions. A biotin metabolite, biotinyl-5'-AMP has been identified as a potent endogenous SIRT1 inhibitor. [please refer to Diabetes & Metabolism Journal 2014]

779712.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
779712.value: 1. To investigate SIRT1's role in chromatin remodeling by biotinylated histones. In-house anti-biotinylated histone antibodies will be developed and ChIP-based sequencing will be performed to identify specific genes involved in the anti-metabolic ageing effects of adipose SIRT1. Additional funding needs to be sought to carry on the study. 2. The unpublished results from the study suggest that SIRT1 induces mitochondrial stress signaling in adipose tissue, which in turn activates a series of anti-metabolic ageing mechanisms. Thus, how SIRT1 triggers the mitochondrial stress signalling will be investigated. A new GRF-RGC grant has been awarded for this part of work. 3. The protective effect of adipose SIRT1 on ectopic fat accumulation will be further elucidated, by targeting its relationship with adiponectin, another anti-ageing molecule derived from adipose tissue. A grant application for carrying this study has been submitted to HMRF.

779712.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
779712.value: SIRT1, a longevity regulator, plays an important role in maintaining our body's energy homeostasis. The expression and activity of SIRT1 progressively decrease in adipose tissues. The present study reveals that selective activation of SIRT1 in adipose tissue elicits similar anti-metabolic ageing effects as caloric restriction - the only non-pharmacological anti-ageing approach. Mechanistically, SIRT1 prevents biotin accumulation in adipose tissue by counter-regulating acetyl-CoA carboxylase 2. As a consequence, the amount of a biotin metabolite, biotinyl-5'-AMP, is significantly reduced. The latter also acts as a potent SIRT1 inhibitor. We believe that this regulatory circuit represents an important anti-ageing mechanism for future therapeutic development.

780112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780112.value: When starved of key nutrients or placed in certain hostile environments, bacteria initiate a coordinated set of cellular processes known as the stringent response. Two intracellular signaling molecules: guanosine pentaphosphate (pppGpp) and guanosine tetraphosphate (ppGpp), collectively referred to as (p)ppGpp or alarmones, are rapidly synthesized. They ‘reprogram’ the cellular machinery to shut-down non-essential processes and promote the recycling of cellular materials to conserve resources. Cells switch from a growth to a survival mode. In many pathogenic (disease-causing) bacterial species, the stringent response is triggered by sub-lethal concentrations of antibiotic agents. It is also activated during the infection process. Activation of the stringent response has diverse cellular effects; such as dramatically increasing antibiotic tolerance, and promoting the formation of tough, matrix-encased multicellular communities called biofilms. Infections caused by the Gram-positive bacterium Staphylococcus aureus are a major cause of serious illness and death. Cells commonly form tough biofilms within infected sites, which are extremely persistent and difficult to eradicate with antibiotics. In S. aureus, the Rel protein (SA-Rel) synthesizes (p)ppGpp alarmones in response to nutritional starvation. However, (p)ppGpp production during many other clinically-relevant types of stress remain to be established. Furthermore, the putative relationships between alarmone levels and S. aureus biofilm formation are obscure. In preliminary work, we have shown that two previously-uncharacterized S. aureus proteins, SA-RelQ and SA-RelP, can also synthesize pppGpp and ppGpp. Intriguingly, they also synthesize pGpp – a third, poorly-studied alarmone. Here, we build on our exciting preliminary findings to dissect the molecular basis of the stringent response pathway in S. aureus. Specifically, we will quantify the amounts of pppGpp, ppGpp and pGpp produced in S. aureus cells grown in biofilms; or subjected to various stress-inducing conditions; such as oxidative conditions, pH extremes or treatment with sub-lethal concentrations of antibiotic agents. We will establish which of these conditions trigger the expression of SA-Rel, SA-RelQ and SA-RelP, and identify how their respective activities combine to regulate alarmone levels. We will investigate the respective abilities of the alarmones to inhibit a pivotal guanine nucleotide biosynthesis pathway. By gaining a detailed molecular knowledge of how the stringent response is mediated in S. aureus, we will better-understand how cells within tough, clinical biofilm communities will behave during challenging conditions; e.g. after treatment with antibiotic agents. Such knowledge will be invaluable for the rational development of more effective prevention or treatment strategies for infections caused by S. aureus and related bacterial pathogens. 當處於細菌缺乏關鍵性營養或處於不利的生長環境時，細菌體內會產生一系列稱為「應緊反應 (stringent response)」的細胞協調過程。細菌細胞內快速產生兩種信號分子︰五磷酸鳥苷（pppGpp）與四磷酸鳥苷（ppGpp），它們被統稱為(p)ppGpp或信號素。它們能夠將細胞系統「重置」︰停止非必要的細胞進程和促進細胞物質循環再用的程序以節省細胞資源。細胞由此從生長模式轉為生存模式。在很多病原（致病原）內，應緊反應是由次致死濃度的抗生素引發的。同時，在細菌感染宿主的過程中應緊反應也會受到刺激。刺激的應緊反應會產生多種細胞效應：例如強烈增加對抗抗生素的活性，以及觸發細菌形成一種被基質包圍的多細胞群落，稱為生物膜(biofilm)。 金黃葡萄球菌是一種革蘭氏陽性菌，其引發感染會導致嚴重疾病與死亡。細菌細胞通常會在感染部位形成堅固的生物膜，導致細菌擁有極強的對抗性及難以用抗生素消除。在金黃葡萄球菌內，Rel蛋白（SA-Rel）負責(p)ppGpp信號素合成以應對營養缺乏。然而，在其他臨床相關的壓力環境中，(p)ppGpp的產生過程仍有待進一步的研究。此外，信號素濃度以及金黃葡萄球菌生物膜形成之間的關係尚未明確。 我們先前的工作發現兩種過去不典型的金黃葡萄球菌蛋白，SA-RelQ與SA-RelP亦具有pppGpp和ppGpp合成能力。有趣的是，它們還可以合成一種很少被研究的第三個信號素pGpp。這裡，我們通過先前的發現去深入了解應緊反應機制的分子行動方式。將專門量化金黃葡萄球菌細胞生物膜中的pppGpp、 ppGpp及pGpp的含量，以確定其量是否與不同貧養環境的誘發條件（如含氧量）、極端酸鹼度或使用次致死濃度的抗生素等有關條件。我們亦將建立以上條件以誘導SA-Rel、SA-RelQ與SA-RelP蛋白的表達，然後確定它們如何協同調節信號素的活性水平。我們會研究不同信號素抑制關鍵鳥嘌呤核苷酸合成的路徑。通過在分子水平上研究金黃葡萄球菌中應緊反應的傳導細節，我們將更好地了解臨床上頑固的生物膜群落經抗生素處理後，細胞對不利環境中的存活情況。這些研究對我們合理建立更有效的方法來預防及治療金黃葡萄球菌和相關病原體引起的感染具有重大的價值。

780112.label: Realisation of objectives
780112.value: This grant has been a chastening experience for the PI. He will continue to work in this area through his own manpower/financial resources, as some of the research areas described in the original proposal still require additional experiments to reach a more impactful conclusion. Over the past 2 years, progress within this field of research has moved-on at lightning pace, and there have been a number of high-profile publications that have directly affected the path of this grant (as outlined below). Thus, we have had to change tact several times, in response to ongoing developments. Obstacles encountered and remediatory actions taken We managed to obtain some of the PyDPA fluorescent material from the Korean research group that originally synthesized this compound (as included in objectives 2 and 3). However, in our hands, we found that the fluorescence readings (enhancements) upon the binding of (p)ppGpp molecules were not stable, and were affected by the presence of many other nucleotides (e.g. those present in the cell at high levels). We did not pursue the use of these molecules, as results could not be relied upon to be scientifically robust. Gaca et al. (J. Bacteriol, 2015) described how the E. faecalis RelQ protein could synthesize pGpp, and that its (p)ppGpp synthesizing activities was stimulated by pGpp, ppGpp and pppGpp. We had previously reported the use of the E. faecalis RelQ protein for the synthesis of pGpp, ppGpp and pppGpp (Choi et al., PLoS One, 2012). We were using the E. faecalis RelQ protein as a direct comparison for the S. aureus protein, and had quite a lot of data for it. However, due to this publication, we could not include the majority of these (now-unoriginal) data in our publications. Even worse, Geiger et al. (Infect Immun, 2014) published a detailed report into the biological and biochemical activities of the S. aureus RSH, RelP and RelQ proteins. They studied growth rates in mutant strains; determined rsh, relP and relQ transcription levels; and quantified cellular pppGpp and ppGpp levels. We were in the process of performing many similar experiments at the time, and this publication really knocked the wind out our sails. We found that pppGpp and ppGpp could inhibit the activities of hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyl-transferase (HprT) and guanylate kinase (GMK) enzymes at micromolar levels in a competitive manner. However, of note, Gaca et al. (mBio 2013) published that the E. faecalis HprT protein (which is highly homologous to the S. aureus HprT protein) was effectively inhibited by pppGpp at micromolar levels. They further explored the pppGpp-mediated inhibition of the E. faecalis GMK protein. Then, Liu et al. (Mol Cell, 2015) published a detailed investigation into the inhibition of GMK enzymes (including S. aureus GMK, as well as S. mutans and L. monocytogenes) by pppGpp and ppGpp. This group further published a crystal structure of the S. aureus GMK protein with pppGpp present in the ligand binding site. Thus much of the scientific novelty was removed from this area of our investigation. Furthermore, more recently, R. Corrigan et al. (PNAS, 2016) directly demonstrated that pppGpp and ppGpp directly bound the S. aureus HprT and GMK proteins with high affinity (much greater than GTP), thus inhibiting their activities. However, in ongoing experiments, we are testing the inhibitory activities of pGpp (and some other compounds), and these will be reported when completed. I met Dr. Rachel Corrigan, at the recent Microbiology Society Annual Conference (2017) in Edinburgh (where I was presenting my research in this area). She presented preliminary data indicating that the S. aureus Rel protein forms a direct binding interaction with the RelP protein, but not the RelQ protein. She further noted that the RelP and RSH proteins bound to themselves, i.e. they formed homomultimers. We have found that the N-terminal domain of the S. aureus Rel protein is monomeric (see attached draft manuscript). Taken together, this indicates that the amino acid residues responsible for homo-multimerization are located within the C-terminal domain. Due to the factors outlined above, I decided to prioritize the efforts to characterize the biochemical activities of the Rel, RelP and RelQ proteins from S. aureus, and extend this, to include other Rel, RelP and RelQ protein homologues encoded by other (pathogenic) bacterial species. We compared and contrasted, in great detail, the biochemical activities of full-length Sa-Rel protein and the N-terminal (catalytic) domain (Sa-Reltrunc). The kinetic parameters by which they respectively hydrolyzed and/or synthesized pppGpp, ppGpp and pGpp alarmones were determined (see attached manuscript draft). Then, we compared and contrasted these activities with those of (previously uncharacterized) diverse bifunctional Rel protein homologues, including those from Corynebacterium matruchotii (Cm-Rel), Actinomyces gerencseriae (N-terminal domain, Ag-Reltrunc), and Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn-Rel). All these Rel proteins possessed potent alarmone (pGpp, ppGpp and pppGpp) hydrolysis activities (in the absence of ribosomal/RNA-components), whereas their respective abilities to synthesize pGpp, ppGpp and pppGpp alarmone varied considerably. Ag-Reltrunc was notably distinct in its ability to synthesize pGpp. To the best of my knowledge, this is the first report of any Rel protein having this biochemical activity. A highly-detailed kinetic analysis was performed on Sa-RelQ and Sa-RelP, to identify their most likely roles in (pp)pGpp metabolism within S. aureus cells. Their activities were compared and contrasted with those of (the previously studied) RelQ from Enterococcus faecalis (EF-RelQ), and the RelP and RelQ homologues from Streptococcus mutans (Sm-RelP, Sm-RelQ); as well as some novel SAS homologues from lineages that were highly divergent from RelP and RelQ, including Fn0926 from F. nucleatum, and the SAS from Treponema sinensis (Ts-SAS). The general biochemical properties of Sa-RelQ were comparable to those of EF-RelQ, in that their kinetic parameters were reasonably similar, and they were both auto-stimulated (feed-forward regulated) by (pp)pGpp alarmones. Most notably, the (p)ppGpp synthesizing activities of Sa-RelP, were NOT stimulated by (pp)pGpp alarmones; they were actually slightly inhibited. Sa-RelP catalyzed the GTP+ATP reaction with highest catalytic efficiency, whilst Sa-RelQ catalyzed the GDP+ATP reaction with highest catalytic efficiency. However, the Km values for the Sa-RelP enzyme were considerably lower than those of Sa-RelQ, indicative of a different role in the modulation of the stringent response in S. aureus. EF-RelQ, Ts-SAS, SA-RelP and Sa-RelQ had potent pGpp synthesizing activities, but Fn0926 did not. The SAS homologues also possessed the abilities to synthesize the innosine-based alarmones pppIpp, ppIpp and pIpp alarmones (from ATP + ITP/IDP/IMP), with varying efficiencies; indicating differences in substrate (nucleobase) binding specificities. Intriguingly, the biochemical properties of the S. mutans RelP and RelQ proteins were highly different to those of the S. aureus RelP and RelQ proteins (see attached document for preliminary results). As included in objective 4, we also looked at factors affecting the transcription of the rel, relP and relQ genes in S. aureus cells under conditions mimicking amino acid starvation, induced by mupirocin or serine hydroxamate (SHX). Using quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) we found that in response to mupirocin, rsh was upregulated 2.74-fold, relP was downregulated 0.5-fold, and relQ was relatively-unchanged. SHX elicited minor transcriptional effects. Taken together our results clearly indicate that SAS homologues possess a wide range of biochemical properties across bacteria. Thus, whilst we faced some notable initial setbacks, this project has taken an extremely positive turn, and we remain optimistic about the way things will progress.

780112.label: Major findings and research outcome
780112.value: Major Findings We have performed an extremely in-depth biochemical analysis of three proteins from the bacterial pathogen Staphylococcus aureus that are responsible for the synthesis and hydrolysis of alarmone molecules. We demonstrate that the two SAS proteins: Sa-RelP and Sa-RelQ can catalyze the synthesis of pppGpp, ppGpp and pGpp alarmones; but these enzymes have notably different properties. The Sa-RelP enzyme has a much higher catalytic efficiency than Sa-RelQ, with considerably lower Km values for GDP and GTP. This means that Sa-RelP can produce pppGpp and/or ppGpp alarmones when GTP and/or GDP are at lower concentrations within the cell. This will be important when guanosine nucleotide pools become disturbed (grossly imbalanced) during periods of cellular ‘stress’; so that the stringent response can be initiated, especially when such conditions cannot be detected by Rel/ribosome-complexes. In addition, we demonstrate that the bifunctional Sa-Rel protein has the ability to hydrolyze all three (pp)pGpp alarmones with high efficiency. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of a RSH homologue having the ability to degrade pGpp; a recently discovered alarmone, whose role (or relative importance) in the stringent response remains to be fully established. Furthermore, the (pp)pGpp hydrolyzing activities of Sa-Rel do not require activation from ribosomal activating complexes. T his indicates that even under basal conditions (non-stringent control) Sa-Rel can effectively degrade (pp)pGpp within the cell, preventing their toxic accumulation. In exciting (very) recent work we have dissected the biochemical activities of diverse SAS proteins belonging to 5 different lineages (see attachment for results). We have shown the activities of some SAS proteins are stimulated more than 100-fold by alarmones, whilst other are actually inhibited. This reveals that only some SAS proteins have ‘feed-forward’ autocatalytic stimulation. Research outcomes One manuscript will be submitted (to the journal ‘Microbiology’) in August 2017. The draft version is attached to this grant report. This paper describes most of the work conducted on the Sa-Rel, Sa-RelQ and Sa-RelP proteins. Three conference papers have been presented (at international conferences) describing work funded by this grant. One PhD student has been trained, whose project was entirely within the remit of the work described in this GRF grant. He has just submitted his thesis, and will be examined in September 2017. We have established collaborations with a leading protein X-ray crystallographer, who is actively working on solving proteins structures for the Rel and SAS protein homologues we are working on.

780112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780112.value: This grant can be developed in several main ways. The biochemical activities and biophysical properties of ‘RelP (SAS2)’ and ‘RelQ (SAS1)’ family proteins exhibit notable variations. This suggests that it would be prudent to reevaluate their classification as distinct protein families. It seems highly-likely that RelP and RelQ homologues possess a spectrum of biochemical/biophysical properties that overlap significantly with those of the other SAS phylogenetic lineages present within diverse bacterial taxa. Based on the results discovered during this grant, it seems likely that (pp)pGpp molecules do not universally stimulate alarmone-synthetic activities, and RNA does not universally negatively-modulate alarmone-synthesizing activities. The characterization of 2-4 diverse homologues from ca. 4-6 different bacterial SAS lineages should be sufficient to establish a robust set of sequence-(predicted)-structure-function relationships. This should be performed in parallel to efforts aimed at establishing the activities of the long (bifunctional) RSH protein within the same hosts. Our results indicate that it is quite conceivable that some long Rel proteins have the ability to synthesize pGpp, in addition to ppGpp and pppGpp within the cell. Furthermore, the role of other hydrolases (e.g. Nudix family proteins) should be investigated, to determine if they play a role in alarmone molecule interconversion and/or degradation.

780112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780112.value: Bacteria possess certain ‘hard-wired’ responses that allow them to adapt their mode of growth to promote survival under harsh conditions. The ‘stringent response’ is one such ‘hard-wired’ response, switching bacteria into ‘survival mode’ when certain nutrients are scarce, or after exposure to antibiotic drugs. Two different families of proteins, named ‘Rel’ and ‘SAS’ play pivotal roles in the stringent response, by producing molecules called ‘alarmones’ inside the bacterial cells. These alarmones are the molecular ‘signals’ that switch bacteria into survival mode. Here, we have investigated the activities of Rel and SAS proteins in a selection of disease-causing bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus. Our research has shown that the two different ‘varieties’ of SAS proteins (RelP and RelQ) have very distinct properties, and synthesize three different types of alarmone molecules in differing amounts. This means that the RelP and RelQ proteins help the bacterial cells avoid death, by subtly different mechanisms. We also show that ‘Rel’ proteins usually only make two different types of alarmone molecule, even though they have the ability to destroy all three different types of alarmone molecules. Understanding the precise details of these mechanisms is very important for understanding exactly how bacteria cause infections, and resist antibiotic treatments.

780312.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780312.value: 在促性腺激素分泌细胞和生长激素细胞之间存在一个调控生长激素释放的反馈环路。我们的研究发现，从促性腺激素分泌细胞释放出的促黄体激素能够作为一种旁分泌信号来诱导生长激素细胞中生长激素的分泌，而促黄体激素的诱导作用又能够通过生长激素诱导生长激素合成及分泌的作用而被进一步扩大。与此同时，释放出的生长激素也可以通过局部反馈调控来抑制促性腺激素分泌细胞中促黄体激素的释放。最近我们的研究已经进一步延伸到垂体激活素和卵泡抑制素系统，并且发现:（1）在草鱼垂体中，促性腺激素分泌细胞和生长激素细胞分别是激活素和卵泡抑制素的主要来源。（2）生长激素可以通过JAK2/STAT5, MAPK和PI3K/Akt信号通路来提升垂体中激活素基因的转录水平。（3）激活素通过Smad2和Smad3可以抑制生长激素和促黄体激素诱导的生长激素mRNA表达，并且降低生长激素和促黄体激素的分泌和基因转录。（4）激活素和生长激素也可以提升卵泡抑制素（一种可以阻断激活素活性的结合蛋白）基因的表达。（5）在垂体内，激活促黄体素激素受体可以降低激活素，卵泡抑制素，Smad2和Smad3 mRNA表达水平。基于这些发现，我们推测激活素和卵泡抑制素系统可能是垂体内一种新的反馈环路组件。在此反馈环路中，由局部生长激素的释放而引起的促性腺激素分泌细胞中激活素的生成可能在另一反馈层面上去抑制促黄体素激素和生长激素诱导的生长激素的合成和分泌；随后，激活素和生长激素诱导局部卵泡抑制素的表达能够逐渐地减少激活素的抑制作用；最后，生长激素及激活素水平的降低能够引起促黄体激素释放量的增加，进而对垂体激活素-卵泡抑制素系统的功能进行下调。在本项目中，有如下几个工作重点:（1）验证垂体内生长激素和促黄体激素的局部释放具备调控激活素和卵泡抑制素的功能；（2）阐明生长激素激活垂体激活素-卵泡抑制素系统的受体后信号机制；（3）确立激活素和卵泡抑制素在草鱼垂体中调控生长激素和促黄体激素合成及分泌的功能角色；（4）阐释激活素抑制生长激素和促黄体激素基因表达的分子机制，特别是Smad2和Smad3在该机制中所扮演的角色。我们的研究将会对垂体内自分泌与旁分泌通信系统的复杂性提供一些新的发现。

780312.label: Realisation of objectives
780312.value: Since the initiation of the project in 2012, the research activities leading to the realization of the objectives put forward for the research proposal are summarized as follows: (1) To confirm the presence of activin/follistatin system in the carp pituitary, cDNAs of grass carp activin beta-A (Act-A) & beta-B (Act-B), their binding protein follistatin and downstream effectors for intracellular signaling, including Smad2, Smad3 & Smad7, were cloned and confirmed to be single-copy genes in the carp genome. Their deduced a.a. sequences and 3D protein structures were found to be highly homologous to their respective targets in mammals. Using RT-PCR, their transcript signals could be detection in various tissues including the carp pituitary. Grass carp Act-A, Act-B and follistatin were produced in CHO cells and their bioactivities in terms of activating Smad-binding elements (SBE) in 5’promoter (for activins) and neutralizing the effects of exogenous activins (for follistatin) were also confirmed by functional studies in alphaT3 cells. In the same cell model, over-expression of carp Smad2, Smad3 & Smad7 were also effective in modifying the transactivating activity conferred by an activin-responsive Luc reporter. Using Northern blot & in situ hybridization, Act-B was found to be the dominant form of activins expressed in carp pituitary. Using RT-PCR coupled to LCM capture of immuno-identified pituitary cells, Act-B signal was detected mainly in carp gonadotrophs while the signals for follistatin & activin ActRI & RII receptors were expressed ubiquitously in different cell types at the pituitary level. Besides, transcript expression of follistatin, Smad3 and Smad7 but not Smad2 could also be up-regulated in carp pituitary cells by Act-A and Act-B treatment, suggesting that a functional activin/follistation system is present in the carp pituitary. Apparently, local production of activins (especially Act-B from carp gonadotrophs) not only can up-regulate the downstream effectors Smad2 & Smad7 coupled with activin receptors but also induce pituitary expression of the activin-binding protein follistatin, presumably for signal termination. (2) In carp pituitary cells, growth hormone (GH) treatment was found to up-regulate transcript expression of Act-A, Act-B, follistatin, Smad3 and Smad7 but not Smad2 while the opposite was true by removal of endogenous GH with immunoneutralization using GH antiserum. Interestingly, parallel treatment with the functional analog of luteinizing hormone (LH), namely hCG, was shown to inhibit Act-A, Act-B, follistatin, Smad2, Smad3 and Smad7 mRNA expression, and again, removal of endogenous LH by LH antiserum was also effective in triggering the opposite effects. Apparently, the inhibitory effects by hCG were mediated by LH receptor as similar treatment of FSH was not effective in altering transcript expression of these target genes. Using inhibitors for various signaling pathways, GH-induced Act-A, Act-B, follistatin and Smad3 & Smad7 mRNA expression were found to be mediated via JAK2/STAT5, MAPK and PI3K/Akt pathways. However, the corresponding responses induced by hCG were not sensitive to the blockade of cAMP/PKA, PLC/PKC and Ca2+-dependent pathways and our attempts to elucidate the post-receptor signaling for hCG inhibition using a pharmacological approach were not successful. In carp pituitary cells, Act-A and Act-B treatment consistently increased follistatin, Smad3 and Smad7 mRNA levels and these stimulatory actions could be blocked by co-treatment with hCG. Similarly, GH-induced Act-A, Act-B, follistatin, Smad3 and Smad7 gene expression were also sensitive to the blockade by hCG, suggesting that local interaction of GH & LH could alter the functionality of pituitary activin/follistatin system via modulation of activin, follistatin & Smad expression. (3) At pituitary level, Act-A and Act-B could also exhibit reciprocal regulation on LH and GH expression. In carp pituitary cells, treatment with Act-A and Act-B were found to suppress basal secretion, cell content and transcript expression of GH and LH, while the opposite was true with removal of endogenous activins using the activin-binding protein follistatin. Besides, activin treatment was also effective in reducing the half-life (T1/2) of GH mRNA as well as suppressing basal expression of GH primary transcript, suggesting that the inhibitory actions of activin on GH gene expression can be exerted at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels. The transcriptional effect of activins was also confirmed by transfection studies in GH3 somatotroph cell line using Luc reporter carrying a 986 bp grass carp GH promoter. In this case, GH promoter activity expressed in GH3 cells could be down-regulated by Act-A and Act-B treatment. These inhibitory effects could be mimicked by Smad2 and Smad3 expression and blocked by over-expression of dominant negative (DN) mutants of Smad2 and Smad3 or by gene silencing using siRNA for Smad2 and Smad3, respectively. Using 5’deletion of target promoter, the activin-responsive sequence was mapped to the region of -742 to -446, overlapping with 3 putative SBE sites in GH promoter. However, site-directed mutagenesis of these putative sites were ineffective in blocking activin inhibition on GH promoter activity. Apparently, activins could inhibit GH gene expression in carp pituitary by down-regulation of GH promoter activity via Smad2 & Smad3 and this inhibitory effect presumably was mediated by Smad binding to non-canonical SBE sites in GH promoter. (4) To study the transcriptional regulation of LH gene expression by activins, the full gene of grass carp LH beta (LHb) subunit was cloned and a 1.4 kb LHb promoter with multiple consensus sequences for SBE sites was isolated. The LHb promoter was subcloned into Luc reporter and used in transfection studies in alphaT3 gonadotroph cells. In this cell line, the carp LHb promoter activity detected could be up-regulated by LH-releasing factors in fish models, including sGnRH and PACAP. These stimulatory effects were also mimicked by similar treatment with cAMP analog, PKC activator or Ca2+ ionophore but totally abolished by pharmacological inhibitors for PKA, PLC, PKC and Ca2+ channels, suggesting the possible involvement of the cAMP/PKA, PLC/PKC and Ca2+-dependent cascades. Treatment with Act-A and Act-B, in contrast, caused a drop in LHb promoter activity and these effects could be mimicked by over-expression of Smad2 and Smad3. Besides, the inhibitory effect on LHb promoter by activins was also blocked/partially reverted by co-treatment with follistatin, blocking of activin ActRII receptor, over-expression of Smad2 & Smad3 DN mutants, or transfection with siRNA for Smad2 & Smad3. Parallel experiments of sGnRH and PACAP induction with co-treatment of activins also revealed that the stimulatory effects of sGnRH and PACAP on LHb promoter activation could be down-regulated by Act-A and Act-B. Given that LHb promoter activity induced by cAMP analog, PKC activator and Ca2+ ionophore could also be blocked by activin treatment or over-expression of Smad2 & Smad3, it would be logical to assume that up-regulation of Smad2 & Smad3 by activins might inhibit LHb promoter activation by sGnRH & PACAP mediated through the cAMP/PKA, PLC/PKC and Ca2+-dependent cascades.

780312.label: Major findings and research outcome
780312.value: In this research project, using grass carp as a model, two isoforms of activins (Act-A & Act-B), their binding protein follistatin, as well as the downstream effectors of activins, namely Smad2, Smad3 & Smad7, were cloned and confirmed to be functional proteins by expression studies in alphaT3 cells. Transcript signals of these newly cloned components of activin/follistatin system were found to be widely expressed at tissue level including the pituitary. In carp pituitary, despite low level of Act-A signal, Act-B was the major form of activins detected and its signal could be located mainly in carp gonadotrophs. Follistatin signal, together with the signals for activin receptors, were found to be widely expressed in different cell types within the pituitary. In carp pituitary cell culture, transcript expression of follistatin and Smads could be up-regulated by activin treatment, implying that a functional activin/follistatin system is present in the carp pituitary. In our studies, we also have the novel findings that transcript expression of Act-A, Act-B and follistatin were under the differential modulation by GH and LH released locally at pituitary level. In this case, GH could act in an autocrine/paracrine manner to up-regulate Act-A, Act-B and follistatin gene expression whereas LH could exert the opposite effect to inhibit basal as well as the stimulatory actions caused by GH in carp pituitary cells. Apparently, GH treatment could induce pituitary Act-A, Act-B, follistatin and Smad gene expression via JAK2/STAT5, MAPK and PI3K/Akt pathways, although the post-receptor signaling for LH inhibition is still unclear. In carp pituitary cells, Act-A and Act-B could also exert reciprocal inhibition on GH and LH secretion, protein production and transcript expression and the opposite effects were noted by removing endogenous activins using their binding protein follistatin. By transfection studies in GH3 cells, GH promoter activity was shown to be suppressed by Act-A & Act-B and these effects were mediated by Smad2 & Smad3, presumably via non-canonical SBE within the region of -747 to -446 in the GH promoter. In parallel studies in alphaT3 cells, LHb promoter activity could be up-regulated by sGnRH and PACAP but down-regulated by Act-A and Act-B. Furthermore, co-treatment with Act-A or Act-B was effective in reducing the stimulatory actions by sGnRH & PACAP and these inhibitory effects were also mediated by Smad2 and Smad3. (These findings have been submitted for publication as listed in part C.)

780312.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780312.value: Our study has provided new information on the functionality and post-receptor signaling of an intrapituitary activin/follistatin system related to GH and LH regulation in carp model. In grass carp, our recent study has demonstrated that local production of prolactin (PRL) could exert autoregulation on its own production and PRL release & gene expression were also under the paracrine modulations of GH and LH in the carp pituitary (MCE 399:267-283). Therefore, it would be logical to extend our study to examine the functional interaction between PRL and activin/follistatin system at the pituitary level, which will shed light on the new components for autocrine/paracrine regulation of PRL in lower vertebrates. Given that (i) grass carp is a commercial fish with high market value, and (ii) GH and LH regulation are highly relevant for growth promotion and induced spawning in culture fish, our findings also raise the possibility of using recombinant follistatin as a means to neutralize the inhibitory actions of endogenous activins on GH and LH secretion and protein production, which may have the potential for future development of biotechnology for finfish culture.

780312.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780312.value: Using grass carp as a representative model for carp species, two isoforms of activins (Act-A & Act-B), their binding protein follistatin, as well as the downstream effectors of activins, namely Smad2, Smad3 & Smad7, were cloned and confirmed to encode the functional proteins by expression studies. Expression signals of these gene targets, together with corresponding signals for activin receptors, were located in the carp pituitary. In carp pituitary cells, transcript expression of follistatin and various members of Smads could be induced by Act-A and Act-B. Similar Act-A/B treatment was also effective in reducing GH and LH secretion, protein production & transcript expression and the inhibitory effects on GH and LH gene expression were mediated by Smad2 & Smad3 production. Act-A, Act-B, follistatin and Smad transcript expression were also up-regulated by GH released locally in carp pituitary cells and these effects were mediated by JAK2/STAT5, MAPK and PI3K/Akt pathways. In contrast, LH released locally was found to have the opposite effects and co-treatment with LH could also block the stimulatory actions of GH. Our findings, as a whole, indicate that a functional activn/follistatin system is present in the carp pituitary and contributes to autocrine/paracrine regulation of GH and LH expression.

780512.label: Realisation of objectives
780512.value: A very important task has been to obtain a valid measure for thermal stress in Hong Kong, from Urban Climate (UC) Class Map developed by the Planning Department (http://www.pland.gov.hk/pland_en/p_study/prog_s/ucmapweb/ucmap_project/content/reports/final_report.pdf). However the methodology of the UC-Class Map was based on geographic variables which are not directly related to biological sensation of human being to thermal stress and the UC Class Map developed by the Planning Department was for the year 2006 and 2009, not for the baseline year 1998-2001 of the cohort study needed for the assessment. We had encountered difficulties including unsuccessful attempts to seek for collaboration and data from the Planning Department in order to derive the UC-Class Map of 1998-2001, and also to obtain spatial meteorological variables from the Hong Kong Observatory necessary to derive a Physiological Equivalent Temperature (PET) map with sufficient precision for Hong Kong. Eventually, after several meetings with overseas and local experts and supports with data from Hong Kong Polytechnic University and University of Sciences and Technology, we have developed the PET maps (Lai et al. 2015) and the UC-Class Map (unpublished) of year 2001 for Hong Kong, using alternative approaches. For Objective 1 (100% realization) about health effects of long term thermal stress environment, which cannot be assessed directly but only indirectly through modifying effects of thermal stress environment on health effects of particulate matters (PM). We have found the main effects of PM from another study using the same cohort (Wong et al. 2015) (http://dx.doi.org/10.1289/ehp.1408264) which has cleared the ground for the assessment. We have now found for this study that elders living in higher thermal stress environment are subjected to higher risk of long and short-term exposure to PM (unpublished reports). These findings with corroboration of the data generated from a recently published ecological study (Kioumourtzoglou et al, 2015)(10.1097/EDE.0000000000000422), provide support for the hypothesis that thermal stress environment has long-term effects on health. For Objective 2 (80% realization) to determine whether ventilation or chemical compositions of PM could provide the explanation for modifying effects of thermal stress on health effects of PM, we have now obtained the UC-Class and PET data and clarified the methodology for assessing interaction between short-term exposures of the two factors by a PhD candidate working for the RGC project (Sun et al, 2015). We are now in the process of assessing this objective.

780512.label: Major findings and research outcome
780512.value: 1. For thermal stress exposure: We have developed the 2001 UC-Class Map and PET maps for Hong Kong. 2. For health effects of long term thermal stress environment: We have found that elders living in higher thermal stress environment were subjected to higher risk of long and short term exposure to PM (unpublished reports). Our cohort study with corroboration of the data generated from a recently published ecological study, has provided support for the hypothesis that thermal stress environment has long-term effects on health. 3. For determination of whether ventilation could be an explanation for modifying effects of long-term thermal stress: We have clarified the methodology in assessing interaction between short-term exposure to thermal stress and PM on health effects (Sun et al, 2015).

780512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780512.value: 1. Further work for the project: We are now in the process of assessing interaction between short term exposure to thermal stress and PM in different thermal environment strata. We have so far published the methodology for assessing interaction between short-term exposure between the two factors by a PhD candidate working for the RGC project. A very important next step would be to in assess the effects taking into account linearity of the interaction effects and then to assess the contrast of the interaction effects between homogeneous thermal stress strata. 2. Potential for further development: After determining whether the modifying effects of long-term exposure to thermal stress environment could be related to ventilation or not, we may proceed to identify the actual factors or agents with a view to further demonstrating causality for long term health effects of thermal stress environment. 3. Course of actions: 1 Study for ventilation behaviors of people in different thermal stress environments in different seasons. 2 Chemical composition of PM species in different thermal stress environments in different seasons. 3 Explore other possible explanations for the modifying effects of long-term exposure to thermal stress environment.

780512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780512.value: A very important task has been to obtain a valid measure for thermal stress in Hong Kong in order to assess the health effects of living in high thermal environment. From the Urban Climate (UC) Class Map developed by the Planning Department (http://www.pland.gov.hk/pland_en/p_study/prog_s/ucmapweb/ucmap_project/content/reports/final_report.pdf) and with provision of location-wide temperature and wind speed data from Hong Kong Polytechnic University and University of Sciences and Technology, we have developed the maps which represent thermal stress environments in different places of Hong Kong. For a cohort of 66,820 subjects who had participated in the Elderly Health Service of the Department of Health in 1998-2001, we estimated the degree of thermal stress they experienced at their residential address and followed up by the end of year 2011. We used statistical modeling to show that elders living in higher thermal stress environment were subjected to higher risk of premature death due to all natural causes and in particular to cardio-respiratory diseases, for exposure to particulate pollutants. This has suggested that long-term exposure to high thermal environment is hazardous to health. We have yet to determine whether the observed relationships between increased health risk and living in high thermal environment are causal.

780612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780612.value: 肝癌（肝細胞癌，HCC）是全球第五位最常見的癌症，尤其流行於亞洲和香港。肝癌致死率極高，主要是因為其症狀出現較晚，腫瘤轉移頻繁以及治療方案有限。所以，發展可靠的早期診斷方法及有效的治療措施是迫切需要的。因此而言，更好的了解肝癌發生及轉移的分子基礎至關重要。近年來，表觀遺傳改變對人體癌變的影響越來越受到重視。然而，以往的研究主要集中在DNA的異常甲基化，而其他表觀遺傳學改變在肝癌中的病理學意義尚未完全闡明。為了深入理解表觀遺傳失調在肝癌中的作用，我們最近研究了90個上游表觀遺傳調節因子的表達水平，全面覆蓋了原發性肝癌及其非腫瘤肝臟樣本中的表觀遺傳調節事件。我們的初步數據顯示，組蛋白甲基轉移酶SET結構域分支1（SETDB1）是人肝癌中表達最頻繁上調的表觀遺傳調節因子之一。SETDB1是一個H3K9特異性組蛋白甲基轉移酶，負責常染色質中的基因轉錄後沉默。SETDB1介導的表觀遺傳沉默對幹細胞再生及細胞命運走向非常重要，但是SETDB1在人肝癌中的作用卻知之甚少。有趣的是，我們的初步數據顯示，肝癌中SETDB1的表達上調與腫瘤惡化表型緊密相關，而且利用shRNA敲低SETDB1的表達可以顯著抑制肝癌細胞生長。我們的初步數據還表明，PTEN/AKT/SP1通路的失調以及miR-29家族成員的表達降低可能導致肝癌中SETDB1的頻繁上調。基於上述發現，以及SETDB1在轉錄後基因沉默中可能的作用，我們進一步假設，SETDB1的表達上調可能通過對重要腫瘤抑制基因亞群的表觀遺傳沉默來導致肝癌的發展及轉移。在此項研究計劃中，我們希望通過以下方法來充分研究SETDB1在人肝癌中的病理作用：1）確定SETDB1在人肝癌樣本中的表達及臨床病理學意義；2）闡述SETDB1在體外及體內模型中的分子及細胞功能；3）調查導致人肝癌中SETDB1表達上游的上游調節因子的改變；以及4）描述SETDB1的下游靶點及其在肝癌發生發展中的作用。我們相信，此項研究會提高我們現有的對肝癌發生的分子基礎的認識，並將為新的診療手段的發展提供新的見解。

780612.label: Realisation of objectives
780612.value: • The proposed experiments have been performed accordingly. • The four research objectives have been addressed. • The project has been successfully completed. • The major research findings have been reported in a manuscript published in Hepatology (IF: 11.711, Ranks 4/78 in Gastroenterology and Hepatology) Major findings 1. Frequent up-regulation of SETDB1 in human HCC Whole transcriptome sequencing (RNA-Seq) analysis on 16 pairs of HBV-associated HCC and their non-tumorous liver identified SETDB1 as the most significantly up-regulated epigenetic modifying enzyme. To confirm this initial observation, we performed qRT-PCR analysis on an extended HCC cohort consisting 5 normal livers and 92 pairs of primary HCC. We found that SETDB1 expression was significant up-regulated in human HCC samples as compare to their corresponding non-tumorous liver as well as normal liver controls. Up-regulation of SETDB1 (> 2 fold) was observed in 41/92 (45%) of HCC cases. Expression of SETDB1 protein also determined in tissue microarrays. Overexpression of SETDB1 was observed in 35/89 (39%) of informative cases. Our findings thus confirmed the frequent up-regulation of SETDB1 in human HCC samples. 2. Stepwise up-regulation of SETDB1 in multistep liver carcinogenesis Furthermore, we observed a stepwise increase of SETDB1 expression from normal liver, chronic hepatitis livers, cirrhotic liver, early HCC, to advanced HCC (P > 0.001), suggesting that increase expression of SETDB1 contribute to multistep hepatocarcinogenesis. Finally, we compared the SETDB1 expression in 23 cases of HCC with non-tumorous liver, primary HCC and extra-hepatic metastases available. Our results showed that SETDB1 expression was up-regulated in all extra-hepatic metastases examined as compare to the non-tumorous liver. Higher SETDB1 expression in extra-hepatic metastases was observed in 21/23 (91%) cases when compared to the primary HCC samples. The above findings suggested that SETDB1 up-regulation contribute to HCC development and metastasis 3. Clinicopathological and prognostic significance of SETDB1 up-regulation in human HCC To access the clinicopathological and prognostic significance of SETDB1 overexpression in human HCC, we correlate the SETDB1 expression levels with various clinicopathological features and patients’ prognostic data. We found that overexpression of SETDB1 was significantly associated with the presence of tumor microsatellite formation (P = 0.044) and poorer 5year survival of HCC patients (P = 0.047), thus confirmed the clinicopathological and prognostic implication of SETDB1 overexpression in human HCC. 4. SETDB1 is essential for HCC proliferation and migration. In order the investigate the functions of SETDB1 in human HCC, we established SETDB1 stable knockdown models in Hep3B and MHCC97L cell lines with two independent shRNA sequences. We showed that stable knockdown of SETDB1 significantly suppressed HCC cell proliferation and cell migration in vitro. Furthermore, orthotopic implantation model demonstrated that knockdown of SETDB1 drastically impeded in vivo tumorigenicity and lung metastasis. These findings strongly suggested that SETDB1 functions as an oncogene in human HCC. 5. Molecular mechanisms contributed to SETDB1 up-regulation in human HCC. We also investigated the molecular mechanisms that lead to the frequent up-regulation of SETDB1 in human HCC. To this end, we demonstrated that at genetic level, SETDB1 gene was frequently amplified (24/31) in HCC and directly contributed to the increased SETDB1 mRNA expression. At transcription level, we identified SP1 as a transcription factor that control SETDB1 expression. Overexpression of SP1 in HCC promoted SETDB1 up-regulation. At post-transcriptional level, we discovered miR-1 as a negative regulator of SETDB1. Loss of miR-29 in human HCC relieved post-transcriptional control of SETDB1 and thereby facilitated SETDB1 overexpression. 6. SETDB1 epigenetically silenced important tumor suppressor gene in human HCC. We showed that knockdown of SETDB1 inhibited the transcriptional repressive H3K9me3 in HCC genome. We identified 828 novel SETDB1 downstream targets through RNA-Seq analysis and conformed that SETDB1 installed H3K9me3 and epigenetically silenced tumor suppressor genes, IGFBP3, CXCL3 and NOS3 etc. Our findings provided a molecule explanation to the oncogene function of SETDB1. Publication: Wong CM, Wei L, Law CT, Ho DW, Tsang FH, Au SK, Sze KM, Lee JM, Wong CC, Ng IO. Up-regulation of histone methyltransferase SETDB1 by multiple mechanisms in hepatocellular carcinoma promotes cancer metastasis. Hepatology, 2016, 63:474-87

780612.label: Major findings and research outcome
780612.value: 1. We demonstrated that SETDB1 is frequently up-regulated in human HCC at both protein and mRNA levels 2. We showed that up-regulation of SETDB1 was significantly associated with HCC progression and metastasis and representing a more aggressive molecular subgroup 3. We demonstrated that SETDB1 is indispensable for HCC growth and metastasis in both in vitro and in vivo. 4. We demonstrated that up-regulation of SETDB1 in human is due to gene amplification, hyper-activation of SP1 transcription factor and loss of miR-29 microRNA. 5. We showed that SETDB1 regulates histone 3 lysine 9 tri-methylation (H3K9me3) and epigenetically silenced a subset of tumor suppressor genes to promote HCC growth and metastasis. The major research findings have been reported in a manuscript published in Hepatology (IF: 11.711, Ranks 4/78 in Gastroenterology and Hepatology)

780612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780612.value: Our findings demonstrated that SETDB1 is frequently up-regulated in human HCC and associated with poor survival rate. These findings suggested that SETDB1 could be a potential biomarker for HCC diagnosis and prognostication. Further validation with larger and independent cohorts will confirm this notion. Our findings also demonstrated that SETDB1 is indispensable for HCC growth and metastasis. Indicate SETDB1 is a promising therapeutic target for HCC treatment. The oncogenic function of SETBD1 is likely mediated by its H3K9me3 histone methyltransferase activity and consequently epigenetically silencing of multiple tumor suppressor genes. Unlike genetic changes, epigenetic silencing is reversible, and therefore, small molecular inhibitor specifically targets SETDB1 may be a potential drug for novel HCC treatment approach

780612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780612.value: Liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC) is the 5th common cancer in the world and particular prevalent in Southern China and Hong Kong. The mortality of HCC is extremely high many due to lack of reliable biomarker for early detection and limited treatment option for late advanced HCC patients. Therefore better understand of the molecular mechanisms is essential for the development of new therapeutic regime for the deadly disease. HCC development is a multipstep process driven by accumulation of mutation. Recent studies revealed that epigenetic alterations, which refer to stable changes of chromatin structure and gene expression without change of DNA sequences, also play important role in human carcinogenesis. In this study, we identified SETDB1 is an important epigenetic regulator and oncogene in HCC. SETDB1 is frequently overexpression in HCC which lead to inactivation of multiple important tumor suppressor genes, thereby promoter liver cancer formation and cancer metastasis. Our study suggested that SETDB1 could be a promising biomarker for HCC detection and a novel therapeutic target for HCC treatment.

rows: To demonstrate that F4H5 can dissolve emulsified silicone oil droplets

780912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780912.value: Our project concerns the development of new surgical techniques. Silicone oils are fluids used for the repair of retinal detachment. Its use is associated with many complications. The stakes however, are high. Unless successfully treated, patients with retinal detachments usually become totally blind in their affected eyes. That is why despite known complications, silicone oils are often deployed because there is little alternatives in many cases. Much of the complications of silicone oil are directly related to its propensity to disperse into droplets. These droplets obstruct the outflow of fluid and cause the built up of pressure within the eye (glaucoma). Silicone oil induces glaucoma and consigns a patient to life-long medication, surgery or progressive sight loss. Emulsification of a tamponade in the eye occurs as a result of fast eye movements (saccades). Our work in the past has led to the development of one oil blend that is more resistant to emulsification yet easier to inject and remove. During the course of this work, we have found a way of measuring the extent of emulsification using a particle counter. This gives us an objective measurement to quantify emuslfication and a basis for this new project. For patients who already have emulsified droplets in the eye, they are hard to remove. The reason is that once emulsified, the droplets are coated with proteins and sugars that make them stick to the biological surfaces that make up the different structures inside the eye. Repeated operations rinsing the eye with water and air have proven ineffective. In the past, we have demonstrated that the ampiphillic solvent (F4H5) is highly efficient at dissolving silicone oil. The proof of principle is already established. This solvent is biocompatible and its interfacial tension is much lower than air. We believe that F4H5 will make better contact the biological tissues to which these droplets are adherent and dissolve them. This project involve a number of experiments that will hopefully show that with new surgical techniques combined with the F4H5, we could more completely remove emulsified droplets from the eye. If successful, the next step is to conduct clinical trials. It is hoped that F4H5 could prevent or even reverse glaucoma and other complications assocaited with emulsification of silicone oil. 我們的項目涉及發展一項新的外科技術。矽油是一種用於修復視網膜脫落的液體，但這種技術的併發症很多，風險亦很高。若未能成功治癒，受視網膜脫落影響的眼睛通常會完全失明。因此，儘管使用矽油存在相當高的風險，在沒有替代品的情況下，使用矽油仍然在所難免。 許多併發症與矽油的特性有直接關係。矽油很容易分散成液滴，這些液滴會阻礙液體流出，並導致眼壓上升，誘發青光眼。病人視力會下降，並可能需要接受手術或終身接受藥物治療。快速眼球活動（掃視）亦會引致眼內填塞的乳化。我們過去研發了一種更耐乳化、更容易注入和移除的混合油。在研究的過程中，我們發現可以利用粒子計數器，去量度乳化的程度。這種量化乳化的方法為我們的新項目提供了一個客觀的量度基礎。 如果病人眼睛內的矽油已經乳化成液滴，便很難被移除。因為當矽油乳化成液滴後，液滴會被蛋白質和糖覆蓋著，並粘附在眼內不同的組織上，即使反複用水和空氣沖洗眼睛亦無法移除。過去，我們已經證明了中極兩性的溶劑（F4H5）能有效溶解矽油。這種溶劑是生物相容的，其界面張力亦比空氣低。我們相信F4H5能與生物組織結成一個好的接觸點，從而有效溶解粘附在眼內組織的液滴。這個項目涉及大量的實驗，我們希望透過新的外科技術結合F4H5，可以全面地去除眼內被乳化的液滴。 如果以上實驗成功，下一步便會進行臨床試驗。我們希望F4H5能防止甚至逆轉青光眼和其他與矽油乳化相關的併發症。

780912.label: Realisation of objectives
780912.value: Objective 1: To demonstrate that F4H5 can dissolve emulsified silicone oil droplets We found out that F4H5 could not dissolve the emulsified silicone oil droplets because the emulsified silicone oil droplets are coated with a layer of hydrophilic surfactant. This layer of surfactant hinders the contact between F4H5 and silicone oil. Using in vitro experiments, we also demonstrated that F4H5 did not have a significant higher efficiency in removing the emulsified silicone oil droplets from the in-vitro eye chamber model than the control balanced salt solution (BSS). An in vivo randomised clinical trial was carried out with our collaborators and this showed that F4H5 has limited capacity in removing silicone oil droplets in actual patients. It is likely that F4H5 can remove those droplets in human that are not already stabilised with surfactant(see output). Objective 2: To develop a new technique for rinsing the eye to get rid of emulsified droplets Instead of removing the emulsified silicone oil droplets by dissolving them into F4H5, our group has refined the strategy. We developed a new technique to remove these droplets by a double emulsification approach. A novel rinse based on F4H5 with a fluorosurfactant as the additive was used. Emulsified silicone oil droplets normally remain in the eye cavity suspend within the intraocular aqueous fluid. This is a system of oil-in-water emulsion. The new approach is to further emulsify the oil-in-water emulsion to become an oil-in-water-in-F4H5 double emulsion system. By this way the unwanted emulsified silicone oil droplets are then encapsulated in the stable aqueous globules. Our results have shown that significantly less droplets was remained in the ex-vivo porcine eye cup model after washing with the novel rinse than washing with the control balanced salt solution (BSS). The rinse has an acceptable compatibility with the retinal cell lines.

780912.label: Major findings and research outcome
780912.value: F4H5 is capable to remove the emulsified droplets in the 3D-printed eye models using the double-emulsification approach in the presence of fluorosurfactant. The F4H5-based rinse shows an excellent biocompatibility with the retinal cell lines for 7 days in-vitro. Any remaining rinse in the eye cavity should be able to vaporize and leave the eye cavity through the diffusion in blood capillaries. This rinse therefore shows a great potential for the use in removing leftover emulsified SO droplets in retinal surgeries.

780912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780912.value: Animal studies (e.g. rabbit) should be conducted to investigate the compatibility of the F4H5-based rinse in-vivo. More importantly, the feasibility of the use of this technique within the surgical setting should also be demonstrated before any clinical trials are conducted.

780912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780912.value: The dispersion of silicone oil as droplets after the use of silicone oil in vitreoretinal surgeries is correlated with a lot of complications. These emulsified droplets are difficult to remove in the current clinical practice. In this study, we developed a F4H5-based cleaner that can wash away the emulsified silicone oil droplets. The cleaner acts simply like a household detergent to wash away the oil on the dishes. The emulsified droplets will be encapsulated by the rinse as a form of large droplets. These droplets are easily to been seen and the eye surgeons can easily remove these large droplets by current surgical instruments. The rinse has an acceptable compatibility with retinal cells and should not cause adverse effect to the intraocular tissues.
