781112.value: Prof McGrath, Colman Prof Yang, Yanqi

781112.label: Project Objectives
781112.value: To investigate the association between health-related events during different stages of childhood and the occurrence of DTE at both subject- and tooth-levels in a group of children who are participants of the “Hong Kong Children of 1997” birth cohort.
rows: To investigate the association between health-related events during different stages of childhood and the occurrence of DTE at both subject- and tooth-levels in a group of children who are participants of the “Hong Kong Children of 1997” birth cohort.

781112.label: Realisation of objectives
781112.value: 1. Sample selection The participants in this study are a representative sample of Hong Kong children who have taken part in the project of ‘Hong Kong Children of 1997’ birth cohort. The sample group offers a unique opportunity to study risk factors for delayed eruption of permanent teeth. The sampling frame of this study is local secondary schools in Hong Kong (obtained from the Education Department, HKSAR). A random sample of 45 schools (approximately one tenth of all local secondary schools) was selected; these secondary schools will be the primary sampling unit. Within each school all students who were born between 1 April and 31 May 1997, and have been participants of the ‘Hong Kong Children of 1997’ birth cohort, were invited to participate in this study. To avoid undue disturbance in selected schools, the number of students selected from each school will be limited to 40. Parents or primary caregivers were asked to provide written informed consent and students were asked for their assent. The exclusion criteria are students who cannot complete the clinical examination, or whose complete data set of health-related events is not available. 2. Data collection: Clinical examinations to assess tooth eruption The clinical examinations of the children were carried out in 45 secondary schools. Parents or primary caregivers provided written informed consent and students provided their assent before the clinical examinations. The eruption of the 28 permanent teeth (two incisors, one canine, two premolars, and two molars in each quadrant) of the participating children was assessed by two trained and calibrated examiners. The examiners did not have access to information of the children’s health-related events. Each child’s tooth eruption status was recorded according to widely accepted clinical emergence staging. The criterion for eruption was emergence through the gingivae, which was investigated with a mirror and a portable fiber-optic examination light, together with digital palpation in doubtful cases. The tooth eruption status was dichotomized into “not emerged” or “emerged”. A tooth was considered to have “not emerged” if it was not visible during clinical examination. A tooth was considered to have “emerged” into the oral cavity if it was seen in any stage ranging from visibility of the tooth through the gingival mucosa to the achievement of occlusal approximation. Ten percent of children were randomly selected and re-examined in each school to continuously monitor intra-examiner reliability. 3. Data collection: Extraction of data of health-related events The information of health-related events was obtained from extant data of the ‘Hong Kong Children of 1997’ birth cohort. Socio-demographic information, mother’s health and health-related habits, family history of diseases, birth characteristics (gestational age, mode of delivery, and birth-associated congenital conditions, type of hospital), feeding habits, and child’s growth, development, anthropometric assessments, illnesses, medications, hospitalization, diet, and health-related habits have been documented for this group of children since birth (assessed and recorded at 0, 3, 9, 12 months and then annually). Moreover, the information of health-related events were also obtained by questionnaires filled by the parents. 4. Analyses of associations between DTE and health-related events Information of DTE at the tooth level was used to generate information at the subject level, so as to assess the association of DTE with health-related events. At the subject level, bivariate associations between the DTE and the independent variables were assessed using ANOVA for continuous variables and the chi-square test for categorical variables. Variables with a P value of ≤0.25, and variables currently thought to be influential for DTE from published reports (pre-term birth, low birth weight, nutritional deficiency, low body weight, low socio-economic status, severe childhood diseases, hormone disturbance, excess fluoride intake) were entered into the multivariate model. Multinomial logistic regression was used to examine the influence of independent factors on the probability of experiencing DTE at the individual level. The procedures described by Hosmer and Lemeshow were adopted for the variable selection, fitting of the logistic model, model building, assessment of model fit, and interpretation of the logistic model. The significance of each variable was assessed through the Wald statistic, and the model fit was evaluated using the likelihood ratio test. Purposeful variable selection was used to obtain a parsimonious model. The estimated coefficients were presented as odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Statistical significance for this part of the analysis was set at the level of P < 0.05.

781112.label: Summary of objectives addressed
781112.value: Objectives Addressed Percentage achieved 1.To investigate the association between health-related events during different stages of childhood and the occurrence of DTE at both subject- and tooth-levels in a group of children who are participants of the “Hong Kong Children of 1997” birth cohort.Yes100%
rows: To investigate the association between health-related events during different stages of childhood and the occurrence of DTE at both subject- and tooth-levels in a group of children who are participants of the “Hong Kong Children of 1997” birth cohort.

781112.label: Major findings and research outcome
781112.value: Complete clinical data and information of health-related events were available from 514 children, i.e. the response rate AT THE SUBJECT LEVEL was 76.9% (n/N = 514/668). AT THE TOOTH LEVEL, maxillary central incisors were found to have emerged in all participants, followed by maxillary and mandibular first molars (99.9%), maxillary lateral incisors (99.6%) and mandibular canines (98.8%). Except for the maxillary (61.8%) and mandibular second molars (81.8%), over 90% of all other teeth had emerged (Conference Abstract No. 1). The intra-examiner ICC was 0.99 for both examiners and the inter-examiner reliability was 0.97, indicating excellent agreement within and between the examiners (Paper No. 1). Children were divided into delayed tooth eruption (DTE) and complete emergence (of 28 permanent teeth) groups based on clinical examinations. Bivariate analyses showed that the average birthweight in the DTE group was significantly lower than the complete emergence group (mean difference 0.2 kg, P = 0.006). The finding was confirmed by logistic regression analyses. In the adjusted regression model, it was found that for every 1 kilogram increase in birthweight, the odds of having DTE would be lowered by 0.49 (odds ratio 0.49, P = 0.006) (Paper No. 1). Mode of birth delivery was significantly associated with DTE (P = 0.037) (Conference Abstract No. 2). Infants who had higher birth weight z-scores and those who had grown slowly during the first three months of life were more likely to have complete permanent teeth emergence in both the unadjusted (P < 0.01) and adjusted models (adjusted for gender, gestational age, mode of delivery, type of feeding, parental education, and health status, P < 0.01). However, no significant association was found between the growth trajectories and permanent tooth emergence in either unadjusted or adjusted models (P > 0.05) (Paper No. 3). Further statistical analyses were conducted to investigate the association between DTE and the adiposity statuses [weight-height ratio (W/H) and body mass index (BMI) for general obesity; waist circumference (WC) and waist-hip ratio (WHR) for central obesity; and triceps skinfold thickness (TRSKF) for peripheral obesity]. The mean value and standard deviation were 31.1 (6.3) for W/H, 19.8 (3.7) for BMI, 70.4 (9.4) for WC, 0.82 (0.06) for WHR, and 11.8 (4.5) for TRSKF, respectively. After accounting for sociodemographic factors, analysis of covariance identified that W/H, BMI, WC, and WHR were negatively associated with DTE (P < 0.01) (Paper No. 2).

781112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
781112.value: Future studies could be designed to gather specific detailed information and other potential risk factors for DTE. Malocclusion and familial patterns of tooth emergence should also be taken into consideration in future studies. In addition, further studies are needed to clarify the effect of the DTE risk factors identified in this project, and to elaborate the biologic pathway through which such effect takes place. Other investigations, especially experimental studies and research on the molecular mechanisms triggering the abnormal function of tooth eruption could also be conducted to further expand our knowledge of the risk factors for DTE.

781112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781112.value: Dental eruption is a physiologic process that strongly influences the normal development of the craniofacial complex. The 28 main adult teeth start to form at around birth but the eventual eruption of the complete set can span more than a decade. Delayed tooth eruption (DTE) can directly affect the accuracy of diagnosis, treatment timing, and treatment planning for dental patients. DTE may also reduce the efficiency of caries prevention programs planned for children and adolescents. Thus, DTE has a significant impact on proper dental care. Our uniquely large prospective cohort study among randomly selected Hong Kong children expands the current knowledge on the risk factors for DTE. We found that lower birth weight, weight-height ratio, body mass index, waist circumference, and waist-hip ratio were associated with DTE. The findings of the study can help clinicians when making diagnoses and formulating treatment options, and when explaining and discussing the occurrence of DTE with patients and their parents. Our data on observed variations in dental eruption timelines can also serve as a valuable clinical tool for appropriate treatment planning.

782212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
782212.value: 該項目將開發一種磁共振擴散的新方法來研究體內肌細胞內脂質（IMCL）的顯微組織,確定IMCL在骨骼肌中的擴散行為。在骨骼肌中，IMCL包含了小的球形液滴內。IMCL液滴是細胞能量儲存的主要水庫,日益被認為是一個動態的功能性細胞器。我們推測，磁共振（MR）可以探測脂質的質子在IMCL液滴微觀結構中的擴散和限制。我們進一步假設IMCL擴散特性，可作為敏感的指標，檢測IMCL液滴的大小，代謝紊亂和代謝的干預措施期間的變化。該項目將系統地檢驗我們的假設。使用7T核磁共振成像掃描儀，我們將首先優化MR採集和分析的特點脂質在體內的擴散。在正常和非正常的條件下，我們將確定IMCL在SD大鼠模型中擴散特性。我們將MR結果與病理結果比較, 探討IMCL液滴大小的直接估算。這個新的無創性MR方法的發展將促進體內的脂滴動力學和代謝的研究。

782212.label: Realisation of objectives
782212.value: 1. We have accomplished most of what was proposed in the original application, specifically related to Objectives 1, 2 and 3. 2. Scientifically, we have successfully demonstrated that IMCL lipid dynamics can be monitored and charaterized in vivo using the diffusion MRS we have developed in the past 5 years in our laboratory. 3. Technically, we have developed and demonstrated the efficacy of diffusion MRS to the MRI community worldwide about its potential to sensitively probing into lipid droplet dynamics. 4. In addition, new research directions have been developed, in particular, to deploy diffusion MRS concept developed in this project to interrogate other biological processes in vivo, including heart muscle, liver, aging brain tissue, and extracellular matrix etc. 5. A number of journal and conference papers have been published. More importantly, the findings and methods developed from this GRF grant have been presented in several key MRI meetings (i.e., ISMRM annual meeting), winning society awards for the PI.

782212.label: Major findings and research outcome
782212.value: Intramyocellular lipid (IMCL) droplets are dynamic organelles whose morphology reflects their vital roles in lipid synthesis, usage, and storage in muscle energy metabolism. In this project, we developed noninvasive means to measure droplet microstructure in vivo. Then we investigated the molecular diffusion behavior of IMCL with diffusion magnetic resonance spectroscopy. In brief, using extremely large diffusion weighting, we measured the IMCL apparent diffusion coefficients (ADCs) in hindlimb muscle of rodents from normal feeding, 60-h fasting, streptozotocin-induced diabetic, and high-fat-diet-induced obese groups. IMCL ADCs decreased markedly with diffusion time, confirming the restricted diffusion of lipid molecules within IMCL droplets. IMCL droplet size, determined by transmission electron microscopy, was closely correlated with ADC. IMCL ADC was sensitive to metabolic alterations, decreasing in the 60-h fasting and diabetic groups while increasing in the obese group. These findings indicated that the IMCL droplet size decreased following 60-h fasting and in STZ-induced diabetes but increased in high-fat-diet-induced obesity. In conclusion, MR diffusion characterization of IMCL droplet size provides a unique means to examine the intracellular lipid dynamics and metabolic abnormalities in vivo.

782212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
782212.value: Yes, this novel diffusion MRS approach can be adopted to study other physiological events in vivo, for example, degradation of extracellular matrix in vivo, liver tissue aging and brain tumour characterisation, gas diffusion etc. The work has attracted attention of the international MRI community and motivated others to deploy this technology to investigate lipid metabolism in vivo.

782612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
782612.value: The prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is reaching epidemic proportions worldwide. Diabetic complications, such as stroke and heart attack, are the top causes of death among senior citizens in Hong Kong. Peripheral insulin resistance and defective insulin secretion by pancreatic β cells are the two major features of T2DM. β cell dysfunction, which is characterized by impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, is observed in the early stage of T2DM. Therefore, in order to understand the pathogenesis of this disease, it is of great importance to elucidate the molecular mechanisms responsible for the dynamics of insulin secretion from β cells. However, the cellular components that control nutrients-stimulated insulin secretion remain poorly characterized at this stage. APPL1 is a multi-domain intracellular adaptor protein that plays an important role in mediating the metabolic and vascular actions of insulin in its major target tissues, including stimulation of glucose uptake in adipocytes and muscle, inhibition of hepatic glucose production and promotion of endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation. Our recent study demonstrated that APPL1 expression in pancreatic β cells is markedly decreased in several types of mouse models with obesity and diabetes. Furthermore, glucose-stimulated insulin secretion from pancreatic β cells is blunted by APPL1 deficiency, but is augmented by APPL1 overexpression, suggesting APPL1 as an important regulator for both actions and secretion of insulin. The major objective of this study is to employ the tissue-specific APPL1 transgenic and knockout mice established in our laboratory to comprehensively investigate the patho-physiological roles of APPL1 in controlling β cell mass and insulin secretion under both healthy and diabetic conditions, and to elucidate the detailed molecular and structural basis whereby APPL1 modulates nutrients-stimulated insulin secretion. The results from this study is expected to shed new light on the pathogenesis of β cell dysfunction in T2DM, and to provide scientific evidence for developing novel therapeutic agents to stop the global epidemic of this chronic disease, which is projected to affect 366 million people worldwide by 2030. 2型糖尿病 (T2DM) 患病率逐年增長，成為一種全球流行的慢性疾病。卒中，心臟病等糖尿病拼發症是香港老年人的首要死因。外周胰島素抵抗和胰腺ß細胞胰島素分泌障礙是T2DM的兩大主要特征。T2DM發病的早期就出現了以葡萄糖刺激的胰島素分泌受損為主要表現的ß細胞功能障礙。因此，為了進一步理解糖尿病的病因機制，闡明ß細胞胰島素動態分泌的分子機制非常重要。然而目前對於哪些細胞成分參與調控營養物質刺激的胰島素分泌尚知之甚少。 APPL1是一個擁有多個功能結構域的銜接蛋白，它介導了胰島素在其主要靶組織的代謝和血管活性作用，既參與外周組織胰島素敏感性調節 (包括促進肌肉和脂肪細胞葡萄糖攝取及抑制肝細胞葡萄糖合成) ，亦能促進胰島素誘發的內皮依賴性血管舒張。我們最近的研究發現，肥胖及糖尿病小鼠模型的胰島ß細胞中APPL1表達水平明顯下調。同時，葡萄糖刺激的胰島素分泌在APPL1基因敲除小鼠胰島ß細胞出現顯著障礙，而在APPL1轉基因小鼠胰島ß細胞則明顯增強。這些結果提示APPL1對於胰島素的活性作用及分泌均有重要的調節作用。本項目擬采用本實驗室建立的ß細胞特異性APPL1敲除及轉基因小鼠,進一步闡明APPL1在健康和糖尿病狀態中對胰島細胞功能 (包括ß細胞團塊和胰島素分泌) 的調控作用及其病理生理機制，探討APPL1調節營養物質刺激的胰島素分泌的分子和結構基礎。研究結果將有助於揭示T2DM胰島細胞功能紊亂的新機制,為研發治療T2DM的新藥提供理論基礎，進而有望減慢這一將於2030影響36.6億人的慢性疾病的全球流行 。

782612.label: Realisation of objectives
782612.value: Research activities related to objective 1: We found that beta-cell overexpression of APPL1 alleviated streptozotocin (STZ)-induced type 1 diabetes, which was mainly due to the anti-apoptotic and proliferating effects of APPL1 on pancreatic beta cells. In addition, we demonstrated that beta-cell specific APPL1 overexpression improved glucose intolerance and reversed the defective glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in db/db diabetic mice. Further analysis indicated that APPL1 specifically regulated glucose- and arginine- but not free fatty acid-induced insulin secretion. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed that beta cell mass was increased but alpha cell mass was reduced in db/db diabetic mice and STZ-treated mice with beta-cell overexpression of APPL1. These changes were mainly due to increased beta cell proliferation and reduced beta cell apoptosis, as revealed by BrdU and TUNEL in-situ detection assays, respectively. Research activities related to objective 2: Our previous report demonstrated that complex formation of SNARE protein was decreased in islets of db/db diabetic mice. Here we further showed that beta-cell overexpression of APPL1 restored the complex formation SNARE protein to a level similar to healthy controls, and this restoration was accompanied with increased glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in pancreatic islets. Co-immunoprecipitation and GST pull-down assays revealed that the BAR domain of APPL1 directly interacted with syntaxin 1 (STX-1) (one of the component of SNARE proteins). Mutation of key residues (including lysine 152 and lysine 160, which are responsible for the membrane targeting and ubiquitination of APPL1) in the BAR domain, largely abolished the interaction between STX-1 and APPL1 and the potentiating effect of APPL1 on glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. As described above, we found that beta-cell overexpression of APPL1 protected beta cell from apoptosis and inflammation under diabetic conditions. We further explored the underlying mechanism how APPL1 confers these beneficial effects on beta cells. QPCR, immunoblotting and flow cytometry analysis revealed that overexpression of APPL1 abolished the diabetogenic agents (such as STZ and cytokines cocktail [TNF-alpha, IL-1beta and IFN-gamma]) induced apoptosis and inflammation, whereas downregulation of this adaptor protein resulted opposite effects. Further analysis revealed that APPL1 attenuated NF-kappaB activation, leading to reduced expression of inflammatory factors (such as inducible nitric oxide synthase and monocyte chemotactic protein 1) and apoptotic genes (such as FAS and caspase 3). Mechanistically, APPL1 abolished diabetogenic cytokines-induced NF-kappaB activation by preventing phosphorylation and degradation of IKappaB-alpha in pancreatic beta cell, which in turn reduces insulitis and beta cell loss. Research activities related to objective 3: Immunoblotting analysis and immunohistochemical staining revealed that insulin signalling pathway, including phosphorylation of Akt at serine 473, FoxO1 at serine 276 and GSK3beta at serine 9, was impaired in islets of db/db diabetic mouse mice, and this impairment was revered by transgenic overexpression of APPL1. In contrast, APPL1 deficiency attenuated insulin actions in pancreatic islets. Co-immunoprecipitation assays indicated that APPL1 blocked the interaction between the endogenous Akt inhibitor TRB3 and Akt, leading to increased plasma membrane translocation of Akt and its subsequent activation. Knockdown or pharmacological inhibition of Akt largely abolished the potentiating effect of APPL1 on insulin secretion. In contrast, overexpression of TRB3 diminished the beneficial effects of APPL1 on beta cell functions. Finally, we found that adenovirus-mediated expression of constitutively active Akt rescued the decreased expression of SNARE proteins and impairment of insulin secretion in the islets of APPL1 knockout mice.

782612.label: Major findings and research outcome
782612.value: Major findings: In this GRF project, we found that the adaptor protein APPL1 exerts protective actions on pancreatic beta cells in both type 1 and type 2 diabetic conditions. On one hand, APPL1 potentiates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion by upregulating SNARE protein expression via an Akt dependent pathway. On the other hand, APPL1 preserves beta cell mass by inhibiting beta cell apoptosis and inflammation via inhibition of NF-kappaB activity in diabetogenic environment. In line with our findings, a recent study identified that loss function of APPL1 causes diabetes in human subjects, and expression of APPL1 is positively associated with glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in human pancreatic beta cells (Prudente S et al., Am J Hum Genet. 2015 Jul 2;97(1):177-85.). Taken together, these findings suggest a novel role of APPL1 in regulating beta cell functions, and APPL1 represents a promising target for treating diabetes. 782612.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
782612.value: Our findings clearly indicated that APPL1 participates in regulating insulin secretion and beta cell mass maintenance in genetic-inherited type 2 and streptozotocin (STZ)-induced type 1 diabetic mouse models. However, the pathogenesis and autoimmune response of STZ-induced diabetes are distinct from human type 1 diabetes. We will therefore cross transgenic mice with beta-cell specific overexpression of APPL1 with non-obese diabetic mice (NOD, which display similar immune response to human type 1 diabetes), and determine whether beta-cell overexpression of APPL1 prevents beta cell apoptosis and insulitis in NOD mice. On the other hand, APPL2, a close homolog of APPL1 with same domain organization and high similarity in protein sequence, is also abundantly expressed in mouse pancreatic islets, but its expression is elevated in type 2 diabetes. Thus, we will further explore whether APPL2, like APPL1, plays a crucial role in modulating beta cell function in diabetic condition using beta-cell selective APPL2 knockout mouse model in the future study.

782612.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
782612.value: Pancreatic beta cell dysfunction, featured by diminished glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and reduced beta cell mass, contributes to the development of diabetes. The adaptor protein APPL1 is an insulin-sensitizing molecule in peripheral tissues such as liver and skeletal muscle, but its role in beta cell function is poorly understood. In this study, we demonstrated that APPL1 is a novel regulator of insulin secretion and beta cell mass maintenance. Protein expression of APPL1 is dramatically reduced in pancreatic islets of rodents with type 1 and type 2 diabetes or islets treated with the diabetogenic cytokines. Functionally, APPL1 promotes glucose-stimulated insulin secretion by activating the exocytotic machinery SNARE protein via an Akt dependent pathway in pancreatic beta cells. In addition, APPL1 protects beta cell against apoptosis by alleviating intra-islet inflammation and inducing Akt activation in mouse models of type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Together with our previous findings, APPL1 not only sensitizes insulin actions in peripheral tissues, but also maintains pancreatic beta cell functions in diabetic conditions. Our findings raise the possibility that the restoration of beta cell APPL1 may represent a promising strategy for improvement of beta-cell functions, by enhancing both insulin secretion and beta cell mass, in diabetes.

783212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783212.value: The adult human body contains about 100 trillion cells derived from a single-cell fertilized oocyte, which divides and differentiates to give multiple cell types. During early development, cells communicate via signaling pathways that direct their progressive specification, which usually involves changes in gene expression. Signaling pathways must be precisely regulated to fine-tune various developmental fates. Hedgehog (Hh) signaling represents one such pathway, which has been extensively studied because its deregulation has been shown to cause various developmental defects and cancers. Because Hh signaling proteins induce different developmental fates in a concentration-dependent manner, Hh activity has to be precisely regulated both temporally and spatially. The Hh signaling protein, Sonic Hh (Shh), which is synthesized in the notochord and floor plate at the ventral midline, spreads dorsally in the developing neural tube to maintain a gradient that specifies the generation of distinct neuronal subtypes. The multi-PDZ protein, PDZ domain-containing protein 2 (Pdzd2), is expressed in adult heart, brain, pancreas and hypertrophic chondrocytes, but its expression during early development remains unclear. Pdzd2 exerts a novel signaling function via the proteolytic cleavage of its C-terminal to generate a secreted protein, sPdzd2. Recent RNA in situ hybridization analysis revealed the early expression of Pdzd2 in both chicken and mouse paraxial mesoderm at a developmental stage when the cell fate of neural tube is specified. We hypothesize that sPdzd2, secreted from paraxial mesoderm, is a novel regulator of Shh signaling to modulate early neural tube patterning. We have employed the chick neural tube system to test this hypothesis, and found that overexpression of sPdzd2 downregulated Hh-induced neural patterning genes Nkx2.2 and Olig2. Furthermore, we also demonstrated that sPdzd2 counteracted the Shh-induced Gli transcriptional response in mammalian cells. In this proposal, we will investigate the regulatory function of sPdzd2 on Shh signaling in both chick and mouse neural tubes using both gain-of-function and loss-of-function approaches. In particular, mice with conditional ablation of Pdzd2 in paraxial mesoderm will be generated to study the in vivo relevance of sPdzd2/Shh crosstalk. The mechanism underlying the modulatory effects of sPdzd2 on Shh signaling will also be explored in vitro. Together, the proposed studies will provide novel insight into sPdzd2 regulation of Shh signaling, which is of major biological interest and a prerequisite for devising future strategies to modulate Hh signaling for guided differentiation of stem cells and for suppressing cancer cell proliferation. 成人體內包含有大約100兆個細胞，而這些細胞起源於一個受精卵。受精卵經過分裂和分化而最終形成了種類繁多的不同類型細胞。在早期的發育過程中，細胞間資訊的傳遞是通過特異性的信號通路來進行，這通常涉及基因表達的變化。信號通路必須精確調節才能夠微發育的終點。Hedgehog(Hh)信號通路已經被廣泛研究。此信號的錯誤調控被證實可以引起發育缺陷和癌症。由於不同的Hh信號調控蛋白濃度能夠導致不同的發育結果，因此Hh的活性需要在時間和空間上精確調節。Hh信號蛋白，Sonic Hh（Shh）在脊索和腹中的神經地板上合成，然後呈梯度分佈于神經管背部以指導形成不同神經元亞型。 包含PDZ結構域蛋白2（sPdzd2）在成人心臟，腦，胰腺和肥大軟骨細胞中都表達，但其在早期發育中的表達尚不清楚。Pdzd2通過其C-末端的蛋白水解切割產生分泌蛋白，sPdzd2來發揮新的信號轉到功能。最新的RNA原位雜交分析顯示，Pdzd2最早表達於雞和小鼠的近軸中胚層。在這個時候，神經管內細胞的命運已經被確定下來。我們推測，分泌於近軸中胚層的sPdzd2是一個新的調控Shh信號的因數，它能夠調控初期神經管的構型。為了檢驗這一假設，我們採用了雞胚神經管作為模型，發現過度表達sPdzd2使Hh-誘導的神經構型形成的基因Nkx2.2和Olig2表達下調。此外，我們還發現sPdzd2能夠抵消Shh誘導的Gli在動物細胞中的轉錄反應。 在這份計畫書中，我們將用增益功能（gain-of-function）和喪失功能（loss-of-function）的方法來探討在雞和小鼠神經管中sPdzd2對Shh信號的調節作用。特別是用近軸中胚層中特異性敲除Pdzd2的小鼠來研究sPdzd2/Shh在體內的功能。同時還在體外進一步研究sPdzd2對Shh信號介導的調控機理。總之，這份研究能夠為我們對sPdzd2對Shh的信號調節提供新的認識。這不僅具有生物學意義，而且為將來設計新的調控Hh信號通路來引導肝細胞的分化和抑制癌細胞增殖奠定了理論基礎。

783212.label: Realisation of objectives
783212.value: Objective 1: Effect of sPDZD2 overexpression on Shh signaling in chick neural tube (100% realized) We have convincingly demonstrated a negative regulatory role of sPDZD2 on Hh signaling by electroporation. Both sPDZD2 overexpression by itself and coexpression with Ihh showed a counteracting effect of sPDZD2 on Hh signaling as indicated by the statistically significant inhibition (~50%) of expression of the Hh downstream targets Nkx2.2 and Olig2. Of particular interest is the ability of sPDZD2 to block the long range effect of Ihh overexpression on the control side of the transfected neural tube. The negative effect of sPDZD2 on Hh signaling was also confirmed using a Gli-luciferase reporter fibroblastic cell line. Addition of sPDZD2 into culture medium could attenuate the stimulatory effect of Shh. sPDZD2 could also counteract the stimulatory effect of purmophamine (activator of Smoothened, which mediates signaling downstream of the Hh receptor Patched) but the effect was less dramatic suggesting that sPDZD2 can act both upstream and downstream of Smo (see Objective 3 below). To show that the sPDZD2 counteracting effect on Hh signaling is of physiological relevance, detailed Pdzd2 expression during early mouse (E8.5, E9.5, E10.5, E11.5, E12.5 and E14.5) and chick (HH11-16, HH21 and HH24) development was studied by RNA in situ hybridization analysis with Shh/Ihh as reference control. Interestingly, Pdzd2 was found to be expressed in paraxial mesoderm, at the distal mesenchyme of limb buds, and then later at the distal tip and mesenchymal condensation (interzone region) of developing digits. The close proximity of Pdzd2 and Shh/Ihh expression is supportive of sPDZD2 serving as general regulator of Hh signaling during early neural tube and limb development. Dual fluorescent in situ hybridization analysis was also conducted to define the expression domains of Pdzd2 relative to the marker genes Pth1, Pthrp and Gdf5 during digit development. Pdzd2 expression only partially overlapped with that of Gdf5 in the interzone and became restricted to the periphery of the more specified interzone between M (metacarpal) and P1 (phalange 1). The dynamic expression of Pdzd2 at the interzone region suggests that Pdzd2 might exhibit early and late function in digit patterning and joint formation/maintenance, respectively. Objective 2: Generation and characterization of Pdzd2 knockout mice (100% realized) We have revised our gene targeting strategy to avoid a hotspot of recombination within intron 24. Using guide RNAs (gRNAs) targeting introns 22 and 23, we employed the Crispr/Cas9 strategy to delete exon 23 (the largest coding exon that encodes also the caspase-3 cleavage site required for proteolytic cleavage to generate sPDZD2). Four founder mice were generated and crossed against C57/BL6 to generate F1 heterozygous progeny. PCR genotyping followed by DNA sequencing of the recombination junction confirmed successful deletion of exon 23. Heterozygous-heterozygous (Het-het) crosses of the various founders gave Pdzd2 null mice and preliminary genotyping analysis revealed early embryonic lethality around E10.5. RNA in situ hybridization analysis to confirm decreased PDZD2 expression in Pdzd2 -/- mutant limb buds and phenotypic analysis are still ongoing. We would look for enhanced Gli1 expression in the Pdzd2-deficient limb based on our hypothesis that sPDZD2 serves a negative regulatory role on Hh signaling. Objective 3: Defining the mechanism of action of sPDZD2 on Hh signaling in vitro (100% realized) Based on the negative effect of sPDZD2 on stimulation of Hh signaling by Shh and the Smo activator purmophamine, we argued that sPDZD2 acts both upstream and downstream of Smo. To address the upstream signaling mechanism of sPDZD2, we first studied the ability of sPDZD2-Fc in pulling down Shh-AP in vitro. There was no discernible interaction of sPDZD2 with Shh. However, co-transfection of V5-sPDZD2- and HA-Patched 1 (PTCH1)-expressing plasmids into 293 cells followed by immunoprecipitation (IP) analysis (using either anti-V5 or anti-HA antibody) detected interaction of sPDZD2 with PTCH1. Recently, the ciliary G-protein-coupled receptor GPR161 was shown to negatively regulate the Shh pathway via cAMP signaling. To test the notion whether sPDZD2 exerts its negative effect on Hh signaling via GPR161, we performed IP analysis similar to the PTCH1 study. Importantly, V5-tagged sPDZD2 (or sPDZD2-Fc) and Myc-tagged GPR161 reciprocally pulled down one another in IP assay, suggesting interaction of sPDZD2 with GPR161. Further deletion analysis defines a stretch of 10 amino acids within the extracellular loop 2 of GPR161 to be the sPDZD2-interacting interface. Interestingly, RNA in situ analysis detected overlapping expression of Gpr161 and Pdzd2 in mouse limb buds during early development, consistent with their functional interaction in vivo. Taken together, our findings support an action of sPDZD2 both upstream and downstream of Smo. sPDZD2 counteracts Hh signaling by interacting with Ptch1 which acts upstream of Smo. On the other hand, sPDZD2 can exert negative effect on Hh signaling via Gpr161 by a cAMP-dependent mechanism.

783212.label: Major findings and research outcome
783212.value: RNA in situ hybridization analysis revealed expression of Pdzd2 in the paraxial mesoderm in E9.5 mouse embryos. Since PDZD2 is proteolyically processed to generate sPDZD2, we suspected that sPDZD2 as signaling molecule may modulate Hh expression in the nearby developing neural tube, similar to Fgfs. Moreover, human PDZD2 was mapped to 5p13, where the disease-associated gene of a Brachydactyly A1 (BDA1) family was localized. Mutations of the IHH locus (at 2q35) were previously known to cause BDA1. We argued that sPDZD2 may cause BDA1 by affecting IHH expression in early limb development. In this project, we have taken three approaches to test the role of sPDZD2 as novel regulator of Hh signaling in both early neural tube, and limb and digit development, and have made the following important findings: First, sPDZD2 was shown to negatively regulate Hh signaling by chick neural tube electroporation. sPDZD2 overexpression counteracted Hh signaling by inhibiting Nkx2.2 and Olig2 expression. Co-expresssion of sPDZD2 with Ihh dramatically reduced the long-range activating effect of Ihh on Nkx2.2 and this negative effect of sPDZD2 on Hh signaling was also demonstrated in a Gli promoter-luciferase reporter cell line. Interestingly, sPDZD2 could counteract both Shh- and purmophamine-induced Gli reporter activity, suggesting an action both upstream and downstream of Smo. Consistent with being a physiologically relevant regulator of Hh signaling, Pdzd2 transcripts were found to express in close proximity to Shh and Ihh transcripts during early limb bud and digit formation, respectively. Second, Pdzd2 null mice were produced using a Crispr/Cas9-based strategy. Het-het crosses of four founders indicated early embryonic lethality, supporting a critcal role played by Pdzd2 in early mouse development. Phenotypic analysis of neural tube and limb bud defects in early Pdzd2-/- mice are still ongoing but preliminary data are consistent with sPDZD2 playing a negative regulatory role on Hh signaling. Third, sPDZD2 was shown to bind to PTCH1 and GPR161 in immunoprecipitation analysis. This points to sPDZD2 negatively modulates Hh signaling by acting both upstream (via Ptch1) and downstream (by cAMP-dependent mechanism via Gpr161) of Smo. To facilitate identification of sPDZD2-interacting proteins, sPDZD2 function was studied using the insulinoma cell line INS-1E as model. Importantly, PDZD2 expression and processing were found to be regulated by glucose and recombinant sPDZD2 was shown to stimulate expression of beta genes including insulin and Glut2 in INS-1E cells. Our findings were presented in two international conferences and two PhD students were trained (see Part C). The manuscript of one full-length research article is under preparation and it will be submitted to eLIFE soon (see Part C).

783212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783212.value: Hh signaling is subjected to elaborate regulation by multiple positive (e.g. Gas1) and negative (e.g. Hip1) regulators. How sPDZD2 interplays with these modulators and other coreceptors of Hhs like Cdo and Boc remain unclear. It would be worthwhile to test whether the sPDZD2-PTCH1 interaction detected in this study affects normal Hh regulation by these other regulators. The specific domain /amino acids within PTCH1 that mediate the sPDZD2 interaction would need to be further defined. Breeding of the Pdzd2-/- mice generated in this study with Ptch1 and other relevant mouse mutants would reveal any possible genetic interaction. Regarding the downstream interaction of sPDZD2 with GPR161, generation of double Pdzd2/Gpr161 mutant mice and their phenotypic analysis will reveal the physiological relevance of this novel regulation. Gpr161 mice are known to show dysregulation of Hh signaling in neural tube and limb bud, which would most likely be exacerbated in the double mutant mice. Another critical question worth addressing is whether PDZD2 is the underlying disease-associated gene causing BDA1. In collaboration with Dr Bulman at Canada, we would further test whether PDZD2 expression and function is defective in the BDA1 patients. Grant applications will be submitted to secure funds for addressing all these important questions.

783212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783212.value: Hedgehog (Hh) signaling proteins are critically required for early developmental processes, including neural tube patterning and limb and digit formation. Hhs induce different developmental fates in a concentration-dependent manner and their activity has to be precisely regulated both temporally and spatially. Indeed, deregulation of Hh signaling has been shown to cause various developmental defects and cancers. Here, we demonstrated that the secreted form of the multi-PDZ domain-containing protein PDZD2 is a novel negative regulator of Hh signaling. Pdzd2 was expressed in close proximity to Hhs during early neural tube and limb formation in mouse and chick embryos. sPDZD2 negatively regulated Hh signaling in chick neural tube, counteracting both the short- and long-range effects of Hhs. Hh signaling induced by recombinant Hh and a chemical activator was also suppressed by sPDZD2 in a reporter cell line . Pdzd2-deficient mice are embryonic lethal and preliminary phenotypic analysis of neural tube and limb bud defects is suggestive of sPDZD2 playing a negative role on Hh signaling. sPDZD2 bound to the Hh receptor PTCH1 and also the orphan receptor GPR161 in immunoprecipitation analysis, suggesting regulatory mechanisms upstream and downstream of PTCH1. In summary, our findings provide the first evidence to support sPDZD2 as a novel negative regulator of Hh signaling.

784012.label: Project Title(Chinese)
784012.value: 就業與自殺的関係研究

784012.label: Co - Investigator(s)
784012.value: Prof Caine, Eric Dr Chang, Shu-sen

784012.label: Project Objectives
784012.value: Examine the secular trend in suicides among the employed and the unemployed during the times of both economic recession (2001-2003) and expansion (2004-2010) as captured by the unemployment rate of Hong Kong. We hypothesize the suicide rate among employed ones react differently in the periods of economic recession and expansion. Establish baseline and reliable information for suicides among the employed ones, we examine all the suicides files from Coroner court data during the period 2001-2010 and characterize the profile of the suicide among the employed and unemployed. We also compare them with the general population based on Census data. We hypothesize that demographic, social-economic profile of suicides among employed ones would be different from the general population. Investigate trends in suicide in different sectors among the employed for the period 2000-2010. We hypothesize that suicide rate among skilled professionals behaves differently from the less skilled ones. More specifically, suicide rate among the skilled professionals (e.g nurse, doctor and managers) increases during the period of economic recession and has minimal effect on less skilled workers (e.g clerks and service workers). Compare and contrast the characteristics of suicides by occupation, and compare the profiles of decedents over time, especially for the teacher profession which has received much attention in the past years. We hypothesize that suicide is more common amongst relatively younger cohort of workers. Occupation which has experienced substantial and rapid change would induce higher risk of suicide in comparing to others with a more stable environment.

784012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784012.value: Suicide is the 7th leading cause of death in Hong Kong with about 1000 deaths each year with the rate 14.0 per 100,000 in 2010. The number of suicide attempts or deliberate self harm would be ten to twenty times higher than that of death figures. It is estimated Hong Kong looses HK$1.6 billion annually because of potential lost economic productivity and 65% of these losses arise from suicides among employed in the 20-59 year old age range. Hong Kong's suicide rate is higher than that of other developed countries (Australia, 11.0; USA, 10 and UK, 8 per 100,000) whereas they have a higher unemployment rate (7%-11%). With a very low unemployment rate in Hong Kong (i.e 3.2% in 2011), in order to be able to reduce the suicide rate in Hong Kong further, suicide prevention among the employed ones is the key and shall be the next priority. Furthermore, there has been remarkably few studies to inform community and professional responses to suicide among the workforce in Hong Kong. The relationship between suicide and unemployment has been extensively studied demonstrating an increase rate of suicide among the unemployed, the profile of suicide among the employed ones has been much less frequently studied especially the relationship between suicide and occupation. Here we assess the valuable mortality data from Coroner court and Census and Statistics Department which provide relevant information of suicide on individual base among the employed ones. The present project therefore, in the short run, provides a description of suicide pattern among the employed population and the relationship between occupation and suicide to determine any high risk occupation in our community. More importantly, in the long run, the results can be used as a useful and valuable reference for designing effective and holistic suicide prevention programs. With the identification of risk factors of suicide and stressors among the current sample, strategies can be carried out to improve the psychological health of the employed. Our aim is to develop effective suicide prevention programs for the 3.5 million working population. Reducing a small risk in a large population is more effective than for a high risk in a small population. Here we target people in the middle years of life—the portion of Hong Kong’s population that contributes the greatest number of people to the overall burden of deaths, and most heavily to our region’s related economic losses. 這項研究是透過死因庭的數括去探討香港就業人仕的自殺情況。 香港，自殺是第7位主要死因，每年造成將近一千人喪生，自殺率在2010年為每十萬人14例。企圖自殺或蓄意自傷的數目則高於死亡數字達十到二十倍。據估計，香港每年因此而損失的經濟生產力高達1.6億港元，這當中有65%是因20-59歲之自殺者所導致的損失。 香港的自殺率高於其他發達國家(以每十萬人計，澳洲自殺率為11.0；美國為10，而英國為8)，而它們的失業率(7%-11%)卻比香港高。香港是一個低失業率城市(在2011年為3.2%)，為能進一步減低自殺率，預防在職人士自殺是一個關鍵及須優先處理的問題。然而，之前卻少有研究能夠提供相關的資訊，以幫助社區及專業人士因應香港在職人士的自殺問題。 先前已有許多關於自殺與失業的研究指出，失業者的自殺率較高；但較少有研究探討在職人士自殺的特徵，特別是不同行業與自殺的關係。我們將根據死因裁判庭及政府統計處的資料，評估在職人士的自殺問題。 短期而言，本計劃將能描述就業人口中自殺者的特徵，以及職業和自殺的關係，以了解社區裡是否有任何職業是處於高自殺風險。更重要的是，從長遠來看，這些研究成果將能提供有用而寶貴的參考資料，以協助我們設計有效及整體性的預防自殺計劃。當我們在這些研究樣本中確認了自殺的風險因子與相關壓力源之後，將能採取適當的對策以改善就業人士的心理健康。 我們的研究目的是要為350萬工作人口建立一個有效的預防自殺計劃。若能在大群眾樣本中將所有人的風險略為減低，將比在小群眾樣本中去除特定高風險因子更有效。此計劃將以中年人口為目標，他們占去了香港整體自殺負擔的大多數，並導致最嚴重的經濟損失。

784012.label: Realisation of objectives
784012.value: In examining the topic of employment and suicide, we have managed to make full use of the data from the WHO and other statistical agency to publish a landmark paper in British Medical Journal entitled: Impact of 2008 global economic crisis on suicide: time trend study in 54 countries. it shows that the middle age group has been severely disrupted by the Global economic crisis. The impact of unemployment is very much felt by the middle age group and young adults. However, the impact in Hong Kong is less significant as the economic crisis is not as severe as in 1997 and the Hong Kong people has built up some resilience in facing the economic crisis. We have also looked at the how the suicide rate being among the different types of workers being affected the economic crisis. It seems that managerial types are mostly affected whereas the impact on some clerical work and/or low skilled workers is still limited. Due to the difficulties in getting the data from teachers, we have looked at the another profession, nurses in Hong Kong to examine the risk and protective factors, it has been showm the life style has been shown to be correlated with the suicidality and it is NOT the work itself rather individuals' profiles are more related to the suicidality. The project has provided much insight of the relationship of employment and suicide and they are useful in promoting suicide prevention in the workforce. The Korean experience has also provided important insight in dealing with suicide prevention in different types of workers. The managerial staff are more vulnerable at the time of economic crisis.

784012.value: The mental health of workers are very important not only for its well being but for the productivity as well. It is important to understand the risk and protective factors of suicidality of different kinds of professions during the period economic crisis, for example, the risk or sometimes the fear of being laying off could impose much stress to the workers. 784012.value: No health without mental health. To be able to identify the risk and protective factors in mitigating suicidal risk is an important public health problem. Sometimes, the type of job has been highlighted as one of the important risk factor, however, it is the life style of the workers has been shown to be an important factor in determining the depression level and suicidality among nurses in Hong Kong. Also, for the managerial staff would face a higher risk than those in the middle management, it is important to provide additional support for managerial staff in the time of economic crisis. It is important to understand the risk and protective factors of suicidality of different kinds of professions during the period economic crisis, for example, the risk or sometimes the fear of being laying off could impose much stress to the workers. A more humanist approach should be used by the employer to its workers during the period economic crisis. The risk or sometimes the fear of being laying off could impose much stress to the workers. Also, it is the person who are in managerial position requires much more effort to adjust to the changes. Empathy and sufficient support should be given to those who might be at risk of losing its job or being laid off.

784812.label: Project Objectives
784812.value: The mechanisms that control fibronectin synthesis, secretion and its degradation in mesothelial cells (HPMC) under physiological conditions and in LPS-induced peritonitis will be investigated. We have chosen to focus on Gram-negative E. coli-complicating peritonitis in this study since we have demonstrated that this bacterium can induce cell detachment and EMT in HPMC with a subsequent increase in fibronectin synthesis. Parallel in vitro studies will be undertaken in the presence of decorin to determine whether decorin can suppress mesothelial cell inflammation and fibrogenesis. We will delineate how changes to fibronectin can alter mesothelial cell function and behavior. We will focus on cellular effects that are applicable to cell proliferation, signaling transduction pathway, markers of EMT and senescence, and induction/reduction of inflammatory and fibrotic mediators. We will determine how LPS can induce structural, inflammatory and fibrotic changes to the peritoneal membrane with time in a rat model of LPS-induced peritonitis treated with or without decorin and determine whether repeated episodes of peritonitis (‘multi-hit’) can cause EPS.

784812.label: Realisation of objectives
784812.value: We have fully completed Objectives 1 and 2, and have completed 85% of Objective 3. The remaining experiments for Objective 3 will be completed within the next 3-4 months. Objectives 1 and 2: Native fibronectin was constitutively expressed in cultured mesothelial cells, whereas its isoforms extra domain A (EDA+) and EDB+ fibronectin were undetectable under physiological conditions. Spent dialysate obtained from PD patients at the onset of peritonitis significantly increased native fibronectin expression and induced EDA+ but not EDB+ fibronectin expression in mesothelial cells, accompanied by increased expression of SNAIL, ZEB and vimentin (markers of EMT) and decreased expression of E-cadherin (epithelial marker), mediated in part through increased activation of ERK, p38 MAPK, PKC and PI3K signaling pathways and secretion of TGF-beta1 and IL-1beta. Co-culture of mesothelial cells with dialysate effluent and decorin attenuated the expression of fibronectin and markers of EMT induced by dialysate effluent. Exogenous LPS induced native and EDA+ fibronectin expression after 48h, mediated through increased activation of MAPK, PKC and PI3K signaling pathways. EDA+ fibronectin increased vimentin and ZEB2 expression, and secretion of TGF-beta1, IL-6 and MCP-1, but had no apparent effect on cell proliferation, cytoskeletal rearrangement or expression of collagen, SNAIL or focal adhesion components in mesothelial cells. Objective 3: In animal studies, C57BL/6N mice were randomized to receive (1) no treatment, (2) sterile PBS and (3) LPS in PBS once every 5 days by intra-peritoneal injection, an experimental model of recurrent episodes of peritonitis. We investigated whether repeated episodes of peritonitis could induce progressive peritoneal fibrosis and encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis, the latter an uncommon but devastating cause of intestinal obstruction characterized by fibrotic encapsulation of the bowel that occurs in patients on long-term PD. Mice showed marked submesothelial thickening after exposure to 6, but not fewer challenges of LPS, and this was accompanied by mesothelial denudation and increased collagen, fibronectin and EDA+ fibronectin deposition. Repeated episodes of peritonitis induced progressive peritoneal fibrosis but not encapsulating peritoneal sclerosis. Due to the high cost of recombinant decorin, studies were undertaken to generate our own. The generation of mouse recombinant decorin was rather challenging due to putative glycosylation sites and its large size. However, cloning and transfection techniques have been modified to accommodate these parameters and we are now in the process of generating sufficient recombinant decorin for our in vivo studies. It is envisaged that the effect of decorin on LPS-mediated submesothelial thickening will be completed within the next 3-4 months.

784812.label: Major findings and research outcome
784812.value: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is an established form of renal replacement therapy for patients with end-stage renal disease, and is the principal dialysis modality used in Hong Kong. Although PD has greatly improved the quality of life in patients, a major disadvantage is that it contains unnatural constituents that cause sustained inflammation in the peritoneal cavity, injury to mesothelial cells and progressive peritoneal fibrosis leading ultimately to inadequate dialysis. These processes are exacerbated by peritonitis episodes. In this study, we demonstrated that mice exposed to 6, but not fewer challenges with LPS induced influx of infiltrating cells, mesothelial denudation and substantial submesothelial thickening, the latter attributed to increased TGF-beta1 and CTGF expression and accumulation of native and EDA+ fibronectin and collagen. In control mice, peritoneal membrane histology and thickness did not change throughout the study period, with constitutive expression of native fibronectin but not EDA+ fibronectin and collagen. Dialysate effluent obtained at the onset of peritonitis induced native and EDA+ fibronectin in cultured peritoneal mesothelial cells and this was accompanied by a loss of E-cadherin expression and epithelial morphology, and the acquisition of an elongated, fibroblastic appearance indicative of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition. Decorin attenuated these fibrotic changes. To delineate the functional role of EDA+ fibronectin in mesothelial cell fibrogenesis, human recombinant EDA+ peptide was generated. Incubation of mesothelial cells with EDA+, but not EDA- peptide induced native fibronectin, alpha9beta1 integrin, vimentin and ZEB2 expression, significantly reduced E-cadherin expression, and increased secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines suggesting that increased EDA+ expression may contribute to peritoneal inflammation and fibrosis through induction of EMT, increased matrix protein expression, altered cell-matrix interaction and secretion of pro-inflammatory mediators. Part of these data have been accepted for either oral or poster presentation at 3 international meetings, which include the Gordon Research Conference, International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis, and American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week 2015, the latter is the top-ranked nephrology meeting. One manuscript has been submitted to Kidney International and is currently under review (second-ranked nephrology journal) and another manuscript is currently being written up for submission also to Kidney International.

784812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
784812.value: In this study, we demonstrated that fibronectin and its isoforms played an important role in peritoneal inflammation and fibrosis, whereas decorin, a dermatan sulfate proteoglycan that possesses putative anti-fibrotic properties inhibited fibronectin expression. We further demonstrated that onset of peritonitis was accompanied by a marked decrease in dialysate decorin level and this reduction was attributed to the inhibitory effect of TGF-beta1, IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-8 and HGF. Replenishing peritoneal decorin level by supplementation in PD solutions may be beneficial to PD patients. In experimental models of PD and peritonitis, we will determine whether the addition of decorin to PD fluids can attenuate peritoneal inflammation and fibrosis and preserve the dialytic function of the peritoneum. We have also demonstrated that decreased miR-200c expression, consequent to PD exposure, is accompanied by increased fibronectin expression in mesothelial cells, suggesting that miR-200c may regulate peritoneal fibronectin expression. Our research grant application to investigate the role of miR-200c in peritoneal fibrosis was submitted to RGC General Research Fund 2015/2016 round and received funding for 2 years.

784812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
784812.value: Many patients on long-term PD exhibit structural and functional alterations to the peritoneal membrane resulting in technique failure. Mesothelial cells line the peritoneal cavity and provide the first line of defence against chemical or bacterial injury. Constant exposure to PD fluids induce epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in mesothelial cells, and increased cytokine secretion and matrix protein synthesis resulting in sustained peritoneal inflammation and fibrosis. Fibronectin is one of the first matrix proteins to be synthesized during tissue fibrosis. We demonstrated that spent dialysate increased fibronectin expression in mesothelial cells, mediated in part through increased TGF-beta1, IL-1beta and TNF-alpha secretion, and activation of the MAPK and PI3K signaling pathways. Spent dialysate also induced EDA+ fibronectin, an isoform of fibronectin that is only synthesized during pathological conditions in adult cells, and it functioned to increase matrix protein synthesis and EMT in mesothelial cells. Furthermore, increased EDA+ fibronectin expression was observed in mice with LPS-induced peritonitis, associated with submesothelial thickening and increased cell infiltration. Decorin significantly decreased fibronectin expression in mesothelial cells and may serve as an anti-fibrotic mediator. Our findings provide insight into the pathogenic role of fibronectin and its isoform in peritoneal fibrosis in PD and PD-associated peritonitis.

784912.label: Project Objectives
784912.value: To investigate the regenerative ability of human pulp/dentin tissue and its vasculature by using prevascularized multicellular macrotissues constructed by DPSCs and gene-modified HUVECs. To determine the synergistic effects of VEGF and SDF-1 genes-transfected HUVECs in microtissues on angiogenesis and odontogenesis of engineered pulp tissue constructs. To study the crosstalk between prevascularized engineered tissues and host tissues; and to analyze the mechanisms of interaction between implanted cells and recruited host cells to stabilize and mature newly formed blood vessels. To explore the extent of blood vessel development and innervation in regenerated pulp in order to determine which procedure to use (one-step or multi-step procedures) in further animal study and clinical trials

784912.label: Realisation of objectives
784912.value: Dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) and human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) were successfully assembled into prevascularized microtissues. HUVECs were self-assembled into vascular-like structures in-vitro, which following transplantation in vivo, anastomosed with the host vasculature. Transplanted cellular constructs gave rise to vascularized pulp-like tissue and induced host tissue vascular cells in a paracrine manner. The effects of gene-modified DPSCs in in-vivo vasculogenesis for dental pulp regeneration have been evaluated. Our results showed that the root segments were filled with well-vascularized pulp-like tissue. H & E staining showed pulp-like tissue regeneration within the root canals in all cell-transplantation groups (DPSCs-alone, DPSCs/VEGF, DPSCs/SDF-1α, DPSCs/VEGF + DPSCs/SDF-1α). The DPSCs/VEGF + DPSCs/SDF-1α groups showed a significantly increased regenerated tissue length than that of the DPSCs and DPSCs/SDF-1α groups. Perfused vessels and non-perfused endothelial-lined lumens were found in all cell-transplantation groups but there was no significant difference among cell groups. Immunohistochemical staining for human mitochondria, CD31, vWF and DSPP confirmed the human cell origin, perivascular structures and newly deposited dentin-like tissues in the regenerated pulp-like tissue, respectively.

784912.label: Major findings and research outcome
784912.value: The present study described the novel approach of utilizing prevascularized cellular constructs of gene-modified DPSCs for pulp regeneration. The results confirmed that DPSCs and HUVECs synergistically act in osteo/odontogenic differentiation and angiogenesis in 3D microtissue spheroids. Furthermore, results showed that both of these processes are likely to be regulated by a combination of factors, such as concentration of angiogenic growth factors, ECM deposition, and remodeling, all of which are in turn influenced by the presence of DPSCs and HUVECs. The results further demonstrated that DPSCs mediated the angiogenic process in vitro, largely via the expression of the angiogenic factor VEGF. These findings provide insight into the complex intercellular cross talk occurring between DPSCs and ECs in the context of angiogenesis and pulp regeneration. Findings of the current study also highlight the significance of developing a 3D microenvironment that supports cell-cell interactions, which can in turn contribute toward an optimal atmosphere for successful pulp regeneration strategies. Unraveling these effects should further elucidate the process of pulp regeneration and also open new avenues to the development of more effective therapies in regenerative endodontics.

784912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
784912.value: The results of the present study suggested that although prevascularization can enhance vascularization within a cell construct, this strategy does not allow the regeneration of full-length pulps when only the apical region is available for vascular connection. However, in the root segments, which the apical opening was larger than average, ingrowing host tissue appeared to push the cell transplant toward the coronal end. Taken together, the foregoing suggests the need to define a critical defect size and a critical apical opening size for pulp regeneration. This knowledge would allow for standardization in studies of regenerative therapy and a predictable outcome. For example, prevascularized DPSC constructs can be successfully used to regenerate pulp of up to 5mm in length and can be applied for pulp regeneration in teeth with an open apex. In cases such as a tooth with a closed root apex, which full-length pulp regeneration is required, we propose a multiple transplantation approach, where 3- to 4-mm segments of pulp are regenerated at once and multiple transplantations are performed at intervals to allow vascularization of the transplanted tissues.

784912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
784912.value: Stem cells residing in the pulp cavity of tooth show a high potential to be used in regenerating the necrotic pulp tissue. However, tooth having only a blood supply from its small apical opening demands additional methods to enhance blood supply during tissue regeneration. This study aimed to grow dental pulp stem cells and endothelial cells (blood vessel forming cells) together to fabricate a cell construct with pre-formed vessels, to inject it into root canal of the tooth and to transplant into the mouse sub-cutaneous tissue (beneath the skin). After 4 weeks of transplantation, formation of pulp-like tissue with improved blood supply was observed. This method could be a promising approach to develop more effective therapies in future root canal therapy.

785112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
785112.value: HIV-1 has evolved various mechanisms to escape human immune surveillance. Since the discovery of HIV-1 in 1981, multiple vaccine concepts and vaccination strategies have been tested and failed for HIV/AIDS. Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) are likely to be a key component of protective immunity conferred by an effective HIV-1 vaccine. However, elicitation of potent bnAbs by vaccination has yet to be achieved. Potent bnAbs are uncommon in natural infections. Although in addition to four well-known monoclonal bnAbs (bnmAbs) b12, 2G12, 2F5 and 4E10, three panels of new bnmAbs have been recently reported, including PG9/16, VRC01, PGTs and 3BNCs, they were isolated from a very limited number of infected individuals in chronic infection and may contribute to their “elite controller” status (long-term no or slow decrease progression). Majority of these bnmAbs target the CD4 binding site on gp120. We and others have reported that, unlike bnmAbs against other viruses, HIV-specific bnmAbs were highly divergent from their germline-like predecessors, and the germline-like Abs lacked measurable binding to HIV-1 envelope (Env) glycoprotein, which may explain why immunogens designed to include the structural determinants of known bnmAbs failed to elicit them. Based on these observations, we hypothesized that extensive somatic hypermutation may be required for development of HIV-specific bnAbs and their somatic maturation may be initiated by non-HIV primary immunogen(s), leading to elicitation of intermediate Abs (iAbs) that can bind to Env and quickly mature to bnAbs upon HIV-1 infection or vaccination (secondary immunogen). Such iAbs may exist in some uninfected human individuals due to pre-exposure to primary immunogen(s), which enables the immune system to rapidly respond to HIV-1 infection, thus effectively contain the virus. This proposed study is to test our hypothesis using b12 and VRC01 as model bnmAbs. Our recent study indicates the existence of b12 iAbs in nonimmune human and rhesus macaque antibody repertoires and the existence of possible primary immunogens for b12. In this study, we will identify b12 and VRC01 iAbs from nonimmune human and macaque antibody repertoires, then identify possible primary immunogens that may trigger the somatic maturation of naïve B-cells expressing b12 and VRC01 germline-like Abs, and further test the primary immunogens in combination with Env trimer in rhesus macaques. Guiding the immune response using primary and secondary immunogens is a novel approach for HIV/AIDS vaccine development. Our study may eventually lead to development of an effective HIV/AIDS vaccine that can elicit high titers of potent bnAbs. 785112.label: Realisation of objectives
785112.value: 1. Generation of immortalized human naïve B cell libraries by optimized EBV transformation with improved efficiency. Different approaches have been tried alone or combined to get desirable EBV immortalization efficiency. Finally, an optimized EBV transformation method with high efficiency was generated. Based on this method, an immortalized human naïve B cell library with the diversity of the BCR repertoire at about 6×106 was generated from healthy donors. 2. Generation and characterization of HIV-1 envelope-specific B cells from immortalized human naïve B cell libraries by isolation with magnetic beads. An HIV-1 envelope-specific B cell line (LCL-P4) was generated after 4 four rounds of panning the library against YU2-Env protein. Limited mutations were scattered on both CDRs and FWRs of variable regions. Interestingly, LCL-P4 heavy chain shared great similarity to PG16 in amino acid sequences. Besides, LCL-P4 also preferentially bond with HIV-1 envelope gp140 trimer rather than with gp120 or gp41monomer. These data highly suggested that LCL-P4 may also bond with the conformational epitope as PG16. Besides, it was found that HIV-1 envelope trimers could activate the intermediate B cells as detected by Ca2+ flux assay, suggesting this HIV-1 intermediate B cell line may be used as a biosensor to evaluate the immunogenicity of HIV-1 vaccine candidates. 3. In vitro strategy for de novo discovery and maturation of human antibodies based on coupling mammalian cell surface display and SHM. A lenticyte display system was constructed for the expression of human full-length IgG1, based on two lentviral expression plasmids with different antibiotic selection genes. Besides, this novel system was successfully used for full-length human antibody library construction. In addition, an AID-induced somatic hypermutation model was generated by induction of AID expression in vitro. AID-induced mutations were detected in both B and non-B cell lines. These two methods combined could be used for the de novo discovery and maturation of human antibodies. In summary, we have isolated five b12 intermediate antibodies (iAbs) from a recombinant antibody library constructed using mRNAs prepared from the PBMCs of 300 HIV-1 uninfected human individuals and 10 b12 iAbs from a nonimmune rhesus macaque using phage display technology. We then constructed three recombinant yeast display libraries using genomic DNA from various sources, including plant leaves, bacteria, see microbes, etc., and isolated five non-HIV (poly)peptides that specifically bind to human and macaque b12 germline and iAbs using yeast display technology. We further tested these polypeptides alone and in combination with HIV-1 envelope glycoproteins in rabbits for the possibility that the polypeptides as primary immunogens can initiate the somatic maturation of b12 germline or iAbs. We have finished the rabbit immunization and characterized the immune sera and purified rabbit IgGs for binding and neutralization activities compared to rabbit sera and purified IgGs from control groups of rabbits. The results showed that priming rabbits with the polypeptides and boosting with SF162 envelope trimer and an engineered envelop gp120 (RSC3) induced cross-clade neutralizing HIV-1 antibodies, which are significantly more potent than control rabbit IgGs. The results further indicated that the order of the secondary immunogens for boosting was also very important for eliciting cross-clade nAbs. We have achieved the objectives of the project and results were reported at AIDS Vaccine 2013 conference (Yang Z*, Li J, Yuan T, Chen L-Q, Lou Q, Ying Y, Zhang M-Y. Elicitation of broadly neutralizing HIV-1 antibodies by guiding the immune responses using primary and secondary immunogens. AIDS Vaccine 2013, Barcelona, Spain, Oct. 7-10, 2013. 785112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
785112.value: Given that in vitro affinity maturation platform based on AID-induced SHM was generated, HIV-1 antibody affinity maturation process was expected to be tracked in vitro. To this end, the unmutated germline sequences of b12 can be cloned into full length human antibody expressing vector to generate a stable germline b12-expressing CHO cell line, followed with the exogenous expression of AID. Finally, affinity matured antibodies will be enriched by magnetic approach. After three to five rounds of selection, FACS will be conducted for further affinity maturation of gp140-specific antibodies. The phylogenetic relationship of antibody members in the b12 clone lineage will be verified based on the sequences of all intermediate and mature antibodies. Non-HIV immunogens identified in the project need to be optimized for enhanced immunogenicity. Immunization protocol also needs to be optimized for elicitation of neutralizing antibodies with broader spectrum and more potent neutralization activity. This study would contribute to the better understanding of the antibody affinity maturation pathway of currently known bNAbs that may provide valuable information for HIV-1 vaccines design.

785112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
785112.value: • A fundamental challenge for developing an effective and safe HIV-1 vaccine is to identify vaccine immunogens that can initiate and maintain immune responses leading to elicitation of broadly neutralizing HIV-1 antibodies (bnAbs) through complex maturation pathways. • The present study provides a proof-of-concept that non-HIV (poly)peptides might serve as primary immunogens to initiate immune responses towards elicitation of cross-clade neutralizing antibodies. • Although priming with non-HIV (poly)peptides and boosting with gp140SF162 trimer and RSC3 elicited better neutralizing antibody responses than immunizing with gp140 and RSC3 in the absence of the non-HIV immunogens, the effect of non-HIV-immunogens was marginal and the responses overall were relatively weak; much weaker than mature b12. Other strategies for further improvement may be investigated in further studies, including multiple secondary immunogens, different boosting strategies and different adjuvants, etc. • Non-HIV immunogens based on the putative germline antibodies of more potent bnAbs (e.g., VRC01, PG9, PGT128, PGT151, 10E8, etc) may also be identified to validate various strategies.

785412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
785412.value: Background: Bisphosphonates (BPs) are considered to be the gold standard to treat bone loss in postmenopausal or aged patients and to prevent and reduce cancer-related bone complications. Despite their great clinical benefits, a severe complication of BPs treatment, known as bisphosphonate related osteonecrosis of the jaw (BRONJ) has been reported recently. The large number of patients under BPs treatment for various medical indications and the unknown underlying pathophysiology of BRONJ render a serious concern of patients, clinicians and society. Key issues: The etiology and pathophysiology of BRONJ remain poorly understood due to the lack of appropriate experimental model. Dogs and rodents have been used as animal models. However, the ethical issues and high costs of dogs and the lack of intracortical remodeling in rodents limit the use of these animal models to study BRONJ. We have recently developed an ovariectomized rat model demonstrating intracortical remodeling in jawbones. Intracortical remodeling process of this animal model mimics the condition seen in humans and provides an appropriate experimental model for BRONJ studies. Several factors such as inflammation and oral bacterial infection are proposed to play key roles in the initiation and progression of BRONJ. However, there are no clear data in the literature for this hypothesis, which we intend to test in the present proposal. Objectives: 1) To investigate the induction and progression of BRONJ using an ovariectomized rat model with progressive periodontal diseases, and 2) to assess the significance of oral bacterial infection onto the disclosure of underlying BRONJ. Methods: Ovariectomized rats will be treated with intravenous zoledronic acid, a high potent BP or saline vehicle. Cotton ligature is placed subgingivally at the first molar of lower jaw to induce periodontal disease. Two species of peridopathogenic oral bacteria are inoculated into the mouth of the rats. Micro-CT, quantitative PCR, histology and immunohistochemistry examinations are used to investigate morphological and histopathologic changes of jawbones under various experimental conditions. Significance: For the first time this animal model of ovariectomized rats will provide comprehensive data both to assess the impact of inflammation and bacterial infection on the induction and unmasking of BRONJ, and to elaborate eventual correlations among these factors. Any further understanding of BRONJ is of crucial clinical significance to prevent and treat this disease. 背景：雙膦酸鹽（bisphosphonates BPs）是治療絕經婦女或老年患者骨質疏松的公認藥物，也可用來預防和減少癌症患者與骨相關的並發症。盡管其臨床意義顯著，近來此藥物産生的嚴重副作用，即雙膦酸鹽相關性颌骨壞死（Bisphosphonate related osteonecrosis of the jaw，BRONJ）陸續有所報導。需要使用BPs治療各種疾病的患者衆多，而BRONJ的病理機制至今未知，成爲困擾患者，臨床醫師和整個社會的難題。 關鍵點：由于缺乏合適的動物模型，目前對BRONJ 的病因和病理學機制所知甚少。狗和齧齒類動物已被用來研究BRONJ，但是，使用狗作為實驗動物受倫理學及價格的控制，齧齒類動物卻缺少皮質骨內骨改建的生理過程，因此兩者的使用均有所限制。我們進來建立了卵巢切除的大鼠模型，發現其頜骨內出現皮質內骨改建的現象，與人類生理過程相似，因此我們認為此模型可以用來進行BRONJ的研究。 許多因素如炎癥和口腔細菌感染可能在BRONJ 的發生和發展過程中起著重要作用，不過至今並無相關文獻報導。它們將是我們目前研究的重點之一。 研究目的：1）使用卵巢切除伴實驗性進行性牙周炎的大鼠觀察BRONJ的發生和發展過程；2）評估細菌感染在BRONJ發病過程中的重要性。 試驗方法：卵巢切除的大鼠靜脈注射zoledronic acid（BPs的重要成員）或生理鹽水。于大鼠下頜第一磨牙處行棉線結紮以誘導牙周炎的發生。將兩種牙周炎相關的口腔細菌接種至大鼠口腔內。用Micro-CT，定量PCR，組織學和免疫組化等方法研究頜骨形態學和組織病理學的變化。 重要性：我們首次使用卵巢切除大鼠深入研究BRONJ，不僅評價炎癥和細菌感染在BRONJ發生發展過程中的作用，也將進一步揭示各種因素間的相互關係，為預防和治療此病提供重要的理論基礎，具有很大的臨床意義。

785612.label: Project Objectives
785612.value: Understanding the evolution and lineage development of the pdm/09-like swine influenza virus and its reassortants; The pdm/09-like virus has frequently been transmitted to pigs by independent interspecies transmissions (23, 26, 36, 42). In considering the general susceptibility of pigs to the virus, the continual introductions from humans may consequently lead to an established swine virus lineage, similar to what had happened after the 1918 and 1968 pandemics. Our systematic surveillance of this virus in the pig population allows the process towards possible lineage establishment to be identified. This may also assist in understanding the relationship between the emergence of the CS lineage and the 1918 H1N1 pandemic strain. Even though different pdm/09-like reassortant viruses have been detected in many regions, most of them were transient (5, 9, 14, 19, 35, 36, 42). Our surveillance has identified H3N2-pdm/09 and H1N1-pdm/09 reassortant viruses that appear to be becoming established in the field (unpublished data). This allows us to elucidate the impact of reassortment on the process of virus evolution and lineage development. Understanding the pathogenicity and transmissibility of these novel reassortant swine viruses in pigs; As all of our swine specimens were collected from slaughtered pigs at abattoirs, the understanding of the prevalence and spread of the H3N2-pdm/09 and H1N1-pdm/09 reassortant viruses in the field is not clear. Animal experimental studies of the pathogenicity and transmissibility of these viruses would define their epizootic potential and threat to agriculture. Understanding the pathogenicity and transmissibility of these novel reassortant swine viruses in ferrets as a model of their potential to disseminate in humans and their replication kinetics in human cells. As swine viruses change through evolution, their pathogenicity and transmissibility to humans may change. Viruses from the same genetic lineage can differ in these attributes. Thus, representative strains isolated from different time points will be tested. These will be compared with contemporary seasonal flu strains for their pathogenicity and transmissibility in ferret models. These studies will evaluate the risk posed by these H1N1 and H3N2 swine viruses and show how they gradually build up their adaptation in mammals. Experiments in human cells will further assess this risk. Identify possible determinants of pathogenicity and transmissibility in these viruses. Based on the experimental and phylogenetic studies, correlation of sequence patterns with functional attributes will be investigated for possible future testing.
