840012.label: Major findings and research outcome
840012.value: Objective 1. The complexity of issues embedded in Objective 1 was addressed through comparative studies of (for example) rural villages, towns and major cities in order to focus on these issues. The main contextual factors were found to be the demographic profile, geographic location, economic prospects, historical degree of assimilation, available resources, local ideology and political leadership, and ethnolinguistic vitality in the community. Objective 2. The Accretive and Balanced Models of trilingual education are more effective than the Transitional and Depreciative Models in promoting additive trilingualism in students. Objective 3. The Accretive and Balanced Models of trilingual education and their sustaining factors represent important contributions to the international literature, and the project team members have produced extensive research outputs (including as edited book), organised four international symposia and undertaken training programmes to disseminate these models. A project website www.ied.edu.hk/triling was also created for the project network to share, discuss and disseminate their findings in relation to Objectives 1, 2 and 3.

840012.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
840012.value: An emergent area from the research is the chronic shortage of ethnic minority teachers capable of teaching in a multilingual context. This shortage is being addressed in areas such as Sichuan, Guizhou, Yunnan and Qinghai, where members of the research teams have continued experimenting with innovative programmes with regard to teacher education in support of strong trilingual models. These innovative models would be an excellent area for further research, with a view to providing policymakers with scalable models.

840012.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
840012.value: Language education policies are significant because they can influence students' sense of identity and life chances. Vulnerable languages, such as those used by ethnic minorities, can be marginalised or strengthened, depending on the sensitivity of the policy and how it is implemented. This project addressed a challenge facing primary schools in ethnic minority regions of China, which was the expectation (from separate policy streams) that they should teach the minority language, Putonghua and (from grade 3) English. Many schools lacked the resources--especially suitably trained teachers--to enable the effective teaching of the three languages. Our project investigated the ways in which schools in 11 ethnic minority regions responded to the challenge. We identified four models. Two models were generally effective in promoting the learning of the three languages, while the other two sacrificed the ethnic minority language in favour of Putonghua and, to a lesser extent, English. The research identified the demographic, geographical, economic, social, political and linguistic factors underpinning these models, so that lessons could be drawn from promoting the effective models more broadly. The project then disseminated the findings widely, through academic publications, symposia (to which policymakers were invited) and professional development programmes for teachers in ethnic minority regions.

841212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
841212.value: 讀寫困難會為兒童的學業發展帶來重大的影響，也可以引起兒童行為及社交問題。儘管有不少研究著眼於及早識別兒童讀寫困難傾向，但至今為止仍相對缺乏針對學童延遲於高小階段才出現讀寫困難的研究。西方研究指出，約有百分之二十至四十六以英語為母語的兒童延遲於小學四至五年級出現讀寫困難徵象。全球人口雖然以華人最多，但至今仍未有針對華語兒童延遲於高小出現讀寫困難的情況作研究。由於中文與拼音文字語言於視覺、字形、語音、語素有顯著分別，引致華語學童延遲出現讀寫困難的起因、風險因素、徵象與拼音文字語言兒童或有所不同，針對華語學童延遲出現讀寫困難的研究將別具意義。研究重點將集中於分析有延遲出現讀寫困難兒童的執行功能、口語運用、語言認知能力的相互關係，區分延遲出現讀寫困難的子類型，並找出上述各種能力對不同讀寫困難組別學童的讀寫能力的影響。 透過分析本港以粵語為母語的高小學生的讀寫及相關認知能力，本計劃旨在：（一）研究不同延遲出現讀寫困難的子類型，包括較弱的讀字能力、較弱的閱讀理解、較弱的讀字及閱讀理解能力，及各子類型的特徵；（二）比較延遲出現讀寫困難及早期出現讀寫困難學童對於未顯示為有讀寫困難學童在讀寫能力及相關認知的異同；（三）分析延遲出現讀寫困難及早期出現讀寫困難學童的口語能力、執行功能、語言認知能力、讀寫能力的相互關係。 本計劃視讀寫困難為一種複合性障礙的表現，不同層面的執行功能、口語運用、語言認知歷程可引致延遲出現讀寫困難不同的特徵及異質性。三百名以粵語為母語的兒童將會接受每年一次，為期兩年（小學三至四年級），針對兒童的口語運用、執行功能、語言認知能力的一系列測試。本計劃將透過潛藏轉移模式、徑路分析、檔案分析：（一）分辨不同讀寫困難類型的兒童；（二）分析不同讀寫困難類型兒童的口語運用、執行功能、語言認知能力、讀寫能力的相互關係；（三）比較在不同測試上發展模式的個別差異。 是次研究結果具有多重意義。在理論層面上，我們對讀寫困難的異質性、華語學童延遲出現讀寫困難的特徵及其子類型會有更佳的了解。在應用層面上，研究人員可透過對延遲出現讀寫困難的認知，發展出早期識別工具及適當的介入計劃。本研究結果可以協助綜合不同讀寫困難類型兒童的讀寫能力，釐清整個讀寫能力發展模式內的跨文化及文化局限成份。

841212.label: Realisation of objectives
841212.value: All three objectives stated in the project were achieved. This project attempted to examine the nature and profile of Hong Kong Chinese readers with reading difficulties (RD) followed through four grades from second grade. Particularly, this project investigated the characteristics and profiles of late-emerging RD children, and their subtypes as well as how LRD developed differently from dyslexia (or early reading difficulty) and typically developing children. The children were assessed at three time points (Time 1, 2, 3) in the 3-year time frame. A total of 425 children was recruited from grade 2 to 4. Among 425 children, 209 and 98 children completed the reading-related cognitive-linguistic and literacy measures in Grade 3 and Grade 4 respectively. The main focus of our analyses was on matched samples of 8 children with LRD, 38 children with dyslexia, and 149 typically developing children in grade 3. Children’s performances on the Grade 3 Chinese word reading, one-minute word reading and text reading measures were used to determine the LRD group. A wide range of measures for cognitive, linguistic and literacy skills were developed and administered to the children individually for Time 1, Time 2 and Time 3. The measures used included word reading, Chinese word dictation, one-minute word reading, reading comprehension, text reading, visual-orthographic knowledge, morphological skills, syntactic skills, discourse skills, oral retell, oral vocabulary knowledge, working memory, rapid naming, and executive functioning. Information about children’ demographics, such as socioeconomic status and parents’ educational levels and developmental history, was also collected. Pilot studies were carried out using a small sample to try out the measures. A series of data analyses was conducted. Based on the pilot studies and longitudinal data collected, Three papers were published in the top journals in the field. One book chapter was accepted for publication. Four papers were also presented at international conferences. Another paper is in preparation for Journal of Learning Disabilities.

841212.label: Major findings and research outcome
841212.value: This project investigated the characteristics of LRD and dyslexia at different developmental stages in the Chinese-speaking children. In this project, a longitudinal cohort of Chinese Hong Kong children from Grade 2 to Grade 4 was used to investigate the nature of the reading-related cognitive-linguistic and literacy difficulties experienced by the LRD who encountered unexpected reading difficulties in the 3rd grade. This cohort was evaluated when children were in Grade 3 because it is in this grade that most children begin learning formal reading and writing in Hong Kong kindergarten schools. With age and Raven’s nonverbal reasoning statistically controlled, the LRD group and dyslexic group were lower than the control group on cognitive-linguistic measures (including rapid digit naming, radical function, word order, oral retell, sentence order, reading comprehension, and executive functioning), while the LRD group performed worse than the dyslexic group on the radical function, sentence order, and executive functioning measure. The LRD group continued to have these persistent difficulties in the 4th grade. The morphological identification, sentence order, and radical function measures distinguished the LRD group from the dyslexic group. Together, these findings suggest that morphological skills, syntactic skills and visual-orthographic knowledge may be useful in understanding LRD in Chinese. These three aspects of cognitive-linguistic processes may have significant impact on reading comprehension and have implication for creation of targeted intervention strategies for Chinese children with LRD.

841212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
841212.value: Future studies are needed to confirm the present findings and to conduct longitudinal studies with more time points (e.g. Grade 1 to 6) and increasing sample size (e.g. n=500 or more children) in order to better understand the nature and causes of LRD and the overlap and differentiation among the LRD and dyslexia. Further studies that analyze comorbidities and additional cognitive-linguistic skills are needed to replicate our findings with a larger sample size and more time points from junior to senior primary school grades.

841212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
841212.value: This project comprised a longitudinal examination of reading-related cognitive-linguistic skills and literacy skills in children with late-emerging reading difficulties (LRD) who encountered unexpected reading difficulties in the senior primary school grade. The causes, characteristics and consequences of children with LRD, dyslexic children, and typically developing children were examined and followed up from Grade 2 to Grade 4. Using Grade 3 as a starting point, children with LRD performed more poorly than their dyslexic peers in visual-orthographic knowledge, morphological skills, and syntactic skills but both LRD and dyslexics were worse than their typically developing peers on all cognitive-linguistic and literacy measures. Furthermore, children with LRD showed persistent difficulties in visual-orthographic knowledge, morphological skills, and syntactic skills in the 4th grade. Together, these findings suggest that morphological skills, syntactic skills and orthographic knowledge may be useful in early identification of Chinese children at risk of becoming LRD. Thus understanding the cognitive-linguistic causes and its mechanisms underlying dyslexia and LRD allows better informed identification and intervention for further work on research and practice in Chinese language.

841512.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
841512.value: Over the past decade, policymakers in East Asia have implemented new policies and programs aimed at increasing the capacity for leadership in schools (Cheng & Walker, 2008; Hallinger, 2011; Walker & Kwan, 2008). The rationale for overhauling school management systems (e.g., school based management, quality systems, accountability structures) and developing new approaches to the recruitment, selection, training, and evaluation of school leaders is based upon an increasingly substantial empirical knowledge base concerning the contributions that instructional leadership makes to school performance (Hallinger & Heck, 1996; Leithwood et al., 2006; Robinson et al., 2008). At the same time, scholars have noted that this knowledge base consists largely of theory and empirical research from Western cultural contexts (Cheng, 1995; Hallinger, 1995, in press; Walker & Dimmock, 2002). This limitation of the knowledge base on school leadership in East Asia represents the focus of this project. The proposed project seeks to contribute to the development of the knowledge base on principal instructional leadership in four East Asian societies: Hong Kong, Mainland China, Vietnam and Thailand. The fund would support data collection in Hong Kong, as well as the planning and synthesis of data collected by teams of researchers in all four societies. The data collected in Mainland China, Thailand and Vietnam will be collected and initially analyzed by collaborating researchers in those societies using their own funds. The research will be conducted in three overlapping stages using methods designed to explore how principals enact instructional leadership from ‘indigenous perspectives’ (Bajunid, 1996). That is, we begin with a very broad framework derived from prior research (see Section 2), but without a functional definition of the role or its composite practices. The stages of the research process consist of: • Literature reviews within each of the four societies, • A qualitative research design that employs open-ended and semi-structured interviews with a sample of 30 primary school principals in each country, • Case studies that employ intensive observations, event sampling of leadership practices, and reflective interviews with a sample of 5 primary school principals in each country. These methods will enable us to generate propositions necessary for building grounded theory about how instructional leadership is exercised within and across these societies. Thus, the project will refine the existing knowledge base in school leadership and lay the foundation both for theory building and the conduct of contextualized, large-scale quantitative studies in the future.

841512.label: Realisation of objectives
841512.value: Objective 1: Two forms of literature reviews were conducted throughout the term of the project. The first aimed to establish the state of the knowledge base of educational leadership across Asia. The purpose of these reviews was to provide the broader context of the state of the English-language knowledge base across Asia in general and in the targeted countries more specifically. The second group of reviews was country specific for each of the three target societies – Hong Kong, China and Vietnam. The China and Vietnam reviews included literature written in both English and Chinese, and Vietnamese, respectively. In line with the nature of the specific literature base the Hong Kong the review included English literature only. All reviews were shared at conferences and published (see 6.1). Objective 2: Empirical data were collected and analyzed from each of the three East Asian societies about how primary school principals understand and enact their role as instructional leaders. Data were collected in all sites, mainly through interviews, and were analyzed by cross-country research groups to maximize accuracy and contextual understanding. Interviews in all sites were conduced in the local language. Theoretical models of instructional leadership were constructed and published for both China and Vietnam. All Hong Kong data was collected and analyzed, but has not been published, we expect it to be soon. Overall, empirically based understanding of conception and enactment and an initial level is complete. Objective 3: Commonalities and differences across the three societies were identified in three phases of the study. First, commonalities/differences were identified in terms of the overall formal knowledge produced across Asia and the three societies; for example, the corpus of literature published in different countries. Second, commonalities/differences identified through the three comprehensive, society-specific literature reviews were identified and analyzed. Third, commonalities/differences were identified and synthesized, and propositions generated, from the results of the qualitative research into instructional leadership in East Asia. Objective 4: As in objective 3, findings derived from the empirical data were compared with western research on leadership/instructional leadership. Again, commonalities and differences were identified. For example: western research suggests principals actively coordinate curriculum, whereas this did not appear common in East Asian schools; principals in the three societies reported spending more time actually in classrooms than their western counterparts; and the importance of smooth, more harmonious relationships appear a dominant feature in east Asian schools and shapes the practices of principals in fundamental ways. The emphasis on harmony seemed to go beyond the importance of trust as discussed extensively in western literature. It should be restated that all findings were collect from interviews with principals and that further research is needed before firmer conclusions can be drawn. Note: While explicitly targeting the 3 societies included in the research project we ran, concurrently, an identical project (self-funded) with research teams in Singapore, Taiwan and Malaysia – these can be seen in the two Special Issues of Journal of Educational Administration we edited. In addition, our work in China around this project lead to us writing separate case studies of leadership for learning in migrant schools in Shanghai – this is now ongoing.

841512.label: Major findings and research outcome
841512.value: Over 12 years, East Asian research publications represented less than 6% of total worldwide publication (in English) output in ELM. HK accounted for half of the scholarship. Dominant publication patterns across East Asia included school leadership, change, and cultural contexts. There was a recent surge in the volume of research conducted in the region. For the first time we now have a clear, if initial, picture of the knowledge base in ELM across Asia. Journal outputs (JO) 7,12, 17-21, Conference Outputs (CO) 10-12 A set of systematic literature reviews of the ELM literature in China, Vietnam (Eng. & Chinese, and Vietnamese respectively) and HK (English) over an extended time period. These show the number of papers, dominant themes, methodologies, key areas covered and shifts in focus in each society. Second stage reviews of China showed a move away from a strong emphasis on political ideology (labeled political prescription) toward leading learning and more sophistical research methodologies. The reviews provided the first set of country specific, systematic literature reviews of ELM in the 3 societies. JO 6, 15 & 16, CO 9 (HK); JO1, 8, 10, 13 & CO 8 (CN); JO 11, 14 & CO 7 (VN) Findings from the reviews allowed comparison across the 3 societies in terms of key, current themes, the political influence on the principalship, research capacity and impact, and the relationship between culture and leadership. JO9 Multi-dimensional models of instructional leadership (IL) were constructed from the data for the 3 societies. These were constructed using a common structure to allow comparison while also showing the dynamic nature of IL in each society. Each model included major dimensions and associated sub-dimensions to capture how IL is enacted. As far as we know these are the first data based models on IL in the 3 societies. CO2 & 5(HK); JO 1&4, CO1, 4 & 6 (CN); JO5, CO 3 (VN) Commonalities and differences across the 3 IL models were identified and analyzed. In terms of school mission, Vietnamese mission was largely determined by the MOE. Although Chinese principals also largely based mission on MOE initiatives, they had more room to express their school’s uniqueness. Principals across all 3 societies remained highly visible in classrooms, but in somewhat different ways and through different structures. JO3 The way principals across the 3 societies enacted IL differed in various ways from western (US) research –including mission development, the importance of harmony and relationships with district/central officials. JO3.

841512.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
841512.value: 1. We collected interview data from five additional provinces in China (self-funded) and are analyzing this data. When complete it will allow a more complete understanding of IL in China (empirical findings reported were from Guangdong, and some from Shanghai) as well as allow us to identify variation across different regions (e.g. rural/ urban.) 2. Initial data collected in Shanghai resulted in interesting peripheral data about IL (in the context central equity and quality policies) in migrant schools (see JO2). This investigation will be continued around the theme of leadership for learning in high needs schools. 3. Findings from qualitative studies will be used to design a contextualized (culturally) appropriate questionnaire around IL to collect quantitative date for further theory building. A pilot questionnaire will be developed and piloted in Hong Kong, and then across 5-8 societies. 4. We are considering a similar study, using a similar methodology, to examine IL practices in secondary schools – probably starting with junior secondary schools. 5. We plan further investigation into the detail and enactment of leadership practices identified in the initial models to get a better handle on what they actually look like in practice. This will further inform leader development programmes.

841512.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
841512.value: This research studied how and why primary school principals in three East Asian societies – HK, China and Vietnam - exercise instructional leadership (IL). IL refers to the practices principals use to improve classroom teaching and student learning. We thought this important because most of what we know about IL comes from western countries such as the US. Before we collected data we needed to know how much was already known about school leadership across Asia, and then in the three societies. This was important because knowledge - how much we do and do not know – helps determine what we look for in research. We reviewed existing literature and found little research about IL, especially in China and Vietnam. We collected data through interviewing 20 principals in each society and then transcribed and analyzed this data. This allowed us to build an understanding of IL in each society. We used the data to suggest models of what principals do to promote learning in their schools. Since we had information from three societies, we could see what principals in the different places did the same, and differently, and also compare this to what principals do in countries like the US.

842212.value: 中國文學研究的現代進程是近十多年學界的研究熱點之一，本計劃旨在通過蔡元培和胡適的紅學論爭，考察實證主義文學研究的性質，推進相關的研究。 蔡元培的《石頭記索隱》不但是紅學史上的名著，同時亦標誌著一種學術研究的形態和規範。研究者普遍認為，蔡元培的索隱紅學與胡適的新紅學，分別代表了兩種不同的研究範式，二者的論爭亦因而具有廣泛的學術意義。 由於胡適本人有極強的方法論意識，經常在其著作中談論治學方法，加上新紅學逐漸在研究上取得主流地位，因此近代學者對新紅學所採用的科學考證方法，並不感到陌生。相較之下，學者對索隱派的學術範式尚缺乏深入的探討，迄今仍未能清楚說明索隱紅學的學術根據與本質特徵。這些闕失不僅有礙大家客觀地理解索隱派的實際影響，還令索隱紅學與新紅學之間的界線逐漸變得模糊起來，引發出不少新的問題。 針對現有研究的不足，本計劃試圖全面考察蔡元培的索隱紅學，闡明此一研究範式的學術觀念和操作方法，並且重新檢討其有別於新紅學的本質特徵。本研究除了有助釐清紅學史上一個長久而重大的問題外，亦能深化大家對20世紀上半葉中國實證主義文學研究的理解。 中國文學研究的現代進程是近十多年學界的研究熱點之一，本計劃旨在通過蔡元培和胡適的紅學論爭，考察實證主義文學研究的性質，推進相關的研究。 蔡元培的《石頭記索隱》不但是紅學史上的名著，同時亦標誌著一種學術研究的形態和規範。研究者普遍認為，蔡元培的索隱紅學與胡適的新紅學，分別代表了兩種不同的研究範式，二者的論爭亦因而具有廣泛的學術意義。 由於胡適本人有極強的方法論意識，經常在其著作中談論治學方法，加上新紅學逐漸在研究上取得主流地位，因此近代學者對新紅學所採用的科學考證方法，並不感到陌生。相較之下，學者對索隱派的學術範式尚缺乏深入的探討，迄今仍未能清楚說明索隱紅學的學術根據與本質特徵。這些闕失不僅有礙大家客觀地理解索隱派的實際影響，還令索隱紅學與新紅學之間的界線逐漸變得模糊起來，引發出不少新的問題。 針對現有研究的不足，本計劃試圖全面考察蔡元培的索隱紅學，闡明此一研究範式的學術觀念和操作方法，並且重新檢討其有別於新紅學的本質特徵。本研究除了有助釐清紅學史上一個長久而重大的問題外，亦能深化大家對20世紀上半葉中國實證主義文學研究的理解。

842212.label: Realisation of objectives
842212.value: 原訂四項目標已全數完成，主要研究員全面考察了蔡元培和胡適的著作，並且針對所訂目標，把研究成果整理為三篇學術文章。 論文一為〈索隱的合法性及其局限：蔡元培、胡適紅學論爭的範式意義〉。文章首先回溯蔡元培紅學的發展歷程，詳細闡明索隱派賴以成立的學術信念和操作方法（目標1）；繼而與胡適的紅學作對比，指出新紅學的內在矛盾，並以證偽方式深入剖析新、舊紅學範式的界線問題（目標3）。 論文二為〈比興與微言之辨：論蔡元培紅學的經學淵源〉。文章考察了索隱源出《春秋》學此一流行說法的不足，並斷定蔡氏索隱的詮釋取向實與傳統《詩經》學有更為密切的關係，而他所列舉的三種研究方法中，亦多與傳箋之學相契合（目標2），迥異於20世紀中國實證主義文學研究（目標4）。 論文三為〈索隱的有效性：論《西遊記》唐僧師徒的宗教象徵解讀〉。文章旨在通過胡適所抨擊的《西遊記》哲理索隱，從另一角度展示20世紀中國實證主義文學研究的性質（目標4）。

842212.label: Major findings and research outcome
842212.value: 一、找出新、舊紅學的分界：蔡元培舊紅學與胡適的新紅學，原是截然不同的學術取向，然而後世學者卻令二者的界線逐漸糊塗。〈索隱的合法性及其局限：蔡元培、胡適紅學論爭的範式意義〉運用了證偽方法，辨識出新、舊紅學的本質差異，解決了聚訟不休的難題。 二、確認蔡氏紅學的傳統根源：蔡氏紅學與傳統學術有密切的關係，過去學者多以為前者源出於傳統《春秋》學。在〈比興與微言之辨：論蔡元培紅學的經學淵源〉檢討了流行說法的不足，並闡明《詩經》傳箋之學對蔡氏的影響，展現其與20世紀實證主義文學研究的不同。 三、建立索隱研究的評鑑架構：索隱可以概分為歷史解讀，以及哲理解讀兩類。紅學為歷史索隱的代表，為了進一步展示索隱研究與20世紀實證主義文學研究的差異，〈索隱的有效性：論《西遊記》唐僧師徒的宗教象徵解讀〉考察了哲理索隱的特點，建立了評量索隱有效性的可能架構。 四、培養本科生：指導了學生搜尋與胡適相關的中、英文資料，提升其研究能力。

842212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
842212.value: 本研究是本人近年致力探討的20世紀中國實證主義文學研究的其中一個項目，旨在深化有關現代中國文學研究史的探索。 本研究以蔡元培紅學為基點，為解決了新舊紅學的分界、索隱紅學的傳統根源以及索隱的評鑑架構等問題，釐清了胡適倡導實證主義文學研究時所針對的傳統範式。 本人將會在這些基礎上，進一步考察(1)胡適的文學批評觀念，以及(2)20世紀上半葉融會傳統索隱與現代考證的實證主義代表人物陳寅恪的文學觀念與批評實踐。

842812.label: Project Objectives
842812.value: With reference to the two overarching questions, we intend to study and explain whether and how the current education policies in Hong Kong support the development of participatory citizenship; the school policies and governance structures support the nurturing of participatory citizen; the key personnel and school leaders involved in school governance perceive citizenship, participatory school governance and their role in nurturing participatory citizens; the students understand citizenship and school civic missions; the students recognize the impact of participatory school governance on their development as participatory citizens; and the tentative framework for students’ participation in schools and citizenship development could be developed.

842812.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
842812.value: This research brings together two areas of substantive concern to schools and societies. Citizenship education is the first of these areas. Societies must prioritise preparing young people for their citizenship responsibilities, and schools play a key role in preparing young people for citizenship. This role is often referred to as the ‘civic mission of schools’. Hong Kong, as a Special Administrative Region of the People’s Republic of China, is a unique environment in which to consider this mission. Since its return to China in 1997, the Hong Kong government has been developing its own form of democracy, which relies fundamentally on an active citizenry. Developing participatory citizenship, therefore, is a key aspect of the civic mission of schools that involves the ‘teaching’ aspect, including teaching and learning with formal and informal curricula, and the ‘practising’ aspect, which treats a school as a miniature political community, where learning is achieved mainly through the actual participation of students in school governance. Arguably, unless the students learn in a structure that offers them experience of the principles of citizenship, such as participation in governance, the effect of civic learning of students remains questionable. The key issue is how to achieve this participatory culture in schools. The answer involves investigation into the second substantive area: student participation in school governance. Hong Kong launched school-based management (SBM) in the mid 1990s, enabling schools to introduce a participatory element into their governance. This project investigates the extent to which Hong Kong schools support the development of a student participatory culture against the backdrop of SBM. It will explore whether and how school governance can contribute to nurturing participatory citizenship. This study is important in many respects. First, it will enrich the literature on participatory school governance and the relationship between nurturing participatory citizens and the democratisation of school governance. Specifically, the facilitating and hindering factors will be identified. Second, it can be useful to education policymakers in formulating policies that promote participatory citizenship among young people. Third, the results will offer valuable references to school practitioners in promoting participatory school governance. By simultaneously considering the civic mission of schools and school-based governance, this study creates a new area of research for further development. 本研究匯集了兩個學校和社會都非常關注的獨立範疇。公民教育是第一個範疇。社會必須以培育青少年的公民權責為優先，而學校在培養青少年的公民權責方面有重要的角色，這個角色常常被稱為「學校的公民使命」。香港，作為中國的一個特別行政區，在實踐「學校的公民使命」方面擁有一個獨特的環境。自1997年香港回歸中國，香港政府一直發展適合香港的民主模式，而這個模式有賴積極參與的公民為作基礎。因此，培育積極參與的公民實在是學校的公民使命的重要目的之一。要達到此目的，必須透過「教學」和「實踐」。教學層面包括在正式和非正式課程的教與學，而實踐層面則指將學校視為小型的政治社區，讓學生主要透過實際參與校政學習公民權責。某程度上，除非學生在一個能給予他們實踐公民權責的經驗的架構中學習相關原則，譬如參與校政，否則學生的學習成效成疑。問題的關鍵在於如何在學校內推廣此參與文化。 答案在於對第二個獨立範疇：「學生參與校政」的探索。香港自1990年代中期開始實施校本管理，令學校可於校政引入參與文化。本研究探討於校本管理的背景下，學校對於學生參與文化的發展的支持程度，以及參與校政能否及如何培育積極參與的公民。本研究於以下幾方面有重要的影響：第一，它能豐富校政參與及培育積極參與的公民與校政民主化之間的關係的文獻，尤其是促進和妨礙學生參與校政的因素；第二，研究結果有助教育政策制定者制定有效促進青少年的公民參與文化的政策；第三，研究結果能讓學校教育工作者作為推廣校政參與的重要參考。透過同時探索學校的公民使命及校本管理，本研究將創造一個新的研究範疇供長遠探究。

842812.label: Realisation of objectives
842812.value: In addressing the Revised Objective 1 on the Hong Kong educational policies, we reviewed policy documents on civic, national and moral education, such as, Guidelines on Civic Education in Schools (1996), Learning to Learn: The Way Forward in Curriculum Development (2000). Also reviewed were documents related to School Management Initiative, such as, The School Management Initiative - Setting the Framework for Quality in Hong Kong Schools (1991), IMC Service Agreement. We interviewed two members of the “troika” in the educational reform in 2000, on policy related to students participation in school governance. In addressing the Revised Objectives from 2 to 5, we conducted both quantitative and qualitative data collection. For the quantitative study, 112 schools (51 schools covering student and teacher samples, and 61 schools covering only teacher samples), including 3209 students, 1010 teachers, 78 principals and 13 school supervisors were involved. For the qualitative data, four schools of different bandings, based on a scale measuring the degree of participation, were selected for the case studies. Related school documents were analysed. More than 50 individual and group interviews (with school supervisors, principals, teachers, tutors, students), and 8 participant observations of various related school events were conducted. However, due to the busy schedules of the supervisor and directors (parents) of the case study schools, only the supervisor of 1 out of the 4 case study schools was interviewed. Notwithstanding this, reference could be made to the survey results because some supervisors had taken part in it. It is because of this unanticipated event, we consider that we have achieved 98% instead of 100% for item 3 in the table of “Summary of objectives addressed to date” below. For the development of theoretical framework in the Revised Objective 5b, we are developing a theoretical framework relating School Civic Mission, Managing Civic Education Curriculum, School Culture, Teachers belief on Students Participation and Students Participation in School Governance by using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM). We plan to publish the completed theoretical framework in an international journal the latest in the end of 2016. Since we are still working on the framework, we consider that we have achieved 98% for item 5b in the table of “Summary of objectives addressed to date” below.

842812.label: Major findings and research outcome
842812.value: i.) Theoretical framework Based on SEM, we are developing a theoretical framework, connecting School Civic Mission, Managing Civic Education Curriculum, School Culture, Teachers belief on Students Participation and Students Participation in School Governance. A simplified model is shown in the Attachment I. ii.) Educational Policy With the launch of School Based Management in HK, school governance can in principle be more flexible, and introducing participatory element into school governance become possible. However, the study revealed that in the policy documents of both areas, civic education and school management, students participation in school governance was not encouraged. As for civic education, the focus is on teaching and learning. As for school management, representations from alumni, not students, are included in the IMC. This could imply that the policy-makers are holding a construct of a child as immature, irrational, incompetent, dependent. Thus, they need to be represented by alumni, their adult senior fellows. iii.) Students’ perception of good citizenship The study revealed an eclectic understanding of the conception of “good citizenship” of the students, with Personally Responsible Citizen ranking first, Justice Oriented Citizen, the second, Participatory Citizen, the third. It also reveals that the Patriotic Citizen was ranked the lowest contradicting the HKSAR government's great efforts in promoting patriotism. iv.) School civic mission The study revealed a perceived implementation dip between the stated civic mission of the schools and the implemented civic mission in schools by the students. v.) Students’ participation in school governance and Students Council The study revealed that schools were much more inclined to inform and consult students through formal and controlled channels, especially, the Students Council (SC). However, the SCs were usually strongly controlled by teachers and rarely had the opportunities to share power with schools. As for the scope of participation, student participation was limited to trivial operational matters, or implementation within the broad policy framework already made by the school authority. Hence, it was concluded that SCs in Hong Kong are close to tokenism and students participation was nearly a “mission impossible”. This could result in negative impacts on students’ citizenship development, cultivating students to be non-questioning, non-participatory, cynical, passive and docile. vi.) Facilitating and hindering factors about students participation The two most important facilitating factors identified were “students believe that their participation in school governance is valuable” and “school has formal channels to collect students’ opinions. One unexpected finding was that the item “has negative impact on students’ academic results” did not show itself as a significant hindering factor.

842812.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
842812.value: As pointed out in Research Output we have identified several reasons that account for the difficulties of promoting genuine students’ participation in school governance, which should be further pursued in both research and developmental work, particularly those related to teacher education. The two most important and related reasons are first, the ignorance of child’s rights, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Child and second, the deficiency model construct of childhood that emphasizes a child as immature, irrational, incompetent, dependent and needs protection, among teachers. This study also revealed that, there is a gradual shift of the construct of child from the deficiency model to one emphasizing that a child is mature, competent, autonomous being, with independent thinking, capable of being a social actor with agency, globally. The shift in the paradigm of construct of childhood may widen the gap of understanding between students and teachers. In addition, the findings also indicated that the influence of hieratical power structure of the organization layers of the schools on participation on school governance may cause decision deprivation from layer to layer. This idea should be followed by future research projects.

842812.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
842812.value: Using a large scale questionnaire survey with samples of school supervisors, principals, teachers and students in Hong Kong secondary schools which was backed up by in depth case studies of four secondary schools, this study concludes that Student Councils in Hong Kong are close to tokenistic and students’ participation in school governance is nearly a “mission impossible”. This could result in a negative impact on students’ citizenship development, cultivating students to be non-questioning, non-participatory, cynical, passive and docile citizens, which may be damaging to the nurturing of a democratic culture needed for Hong Kong’s democratic development. In addition, this study revealed that the ignorance of child’s rights, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Child and the deficient model of the construct of child, emphasizing a child as immature, irrational, incompetent, dependent and needs protection, among teachers, are two significant factors contributing to the tokenism and “mission impossible”. In order to advance the civic mission of schools in nurturing political literacy critical thinking and participatory citizens, much more research and developmental work in addressing the issues identified, particularly those related to teacher education, should be promoted with urgency.

842912.label: Project Objectives
842912.value: The proposed project will provide an in-depth analysis of China’s HRD policies for Africa that are being implemented in both countries. In particular, it will examine the wider rationale for the multiple HRD strategies outlined in the 2010-2012 Action Plan by FOCAC. The 20+20 university partnership scheme between China and Africa will provide an ideal lens for the analysis over this period. Through these higher education development strategies, the research will theorise the central role of partnership in China’s explicitly ethical discourse on South-South cooperation and mutual benefit between China and Africa. Detailed analyses will be provided for the multiple, overlapping dimensions of university partnership in terms of African trainees, students, researchers and language teachers in the selected Chinese universities. Within China’s general HRD strategies for Africa, this research will provide an overview of the changing role of long- and short-term training for Africans attending the 20 Chinese universities in the 20+20 scheme. Moreover, it will especially examine the Africans present in the six partnership universities in China which are twinned with universities in the case study countries. Equally, the project will provide an analysis of the outcomes, in terms of perceived symmetry and mutual benefit, based on participation in the 20+20 cooperation scheme, in the six African universities in the above case study countries. Furthermore, the project will contribute to the literature on South-South academic cooperation, offering some answers to questions on whether and how such a programme may work more effectively. Finally, the proposed study will build analytic capacity both in CUHK and in ZNU in understanding China’s discourse, policy and practice of development cooperation in higher education, with particular reference to Africa.

842912.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
842912.value: 于2009年召开的中非合作论坛宣布了中非合作2010-2012年行动计划，实施中非高校20+20合作。这些合作伙伴大多具有双方合作的历史。这一计划也将于2012年之前为非洲国家提供2万名短期培训以及5,500名长期政府奖学金的机会。另外，该计划还宣布中非高校合作的其它形式，如科技、研究交换、博士后支持，以及为非洲孔子学院的语言支持。 本项目将以中非合作论坛的高校20+20合作计划，来研究其根据、特点、质量及连贯性。自2000年以来，中非合作论坛已经作为一个特殊的泛非机制持续运作，提供对非的援助、贸易、经济合作与投资，以及在人力资源发展方面（HRD）的合作。 包括中非合作论坛在内，对于中国与非洲的经济关系已经有了相当的研究。但是，很少有研究聚焦于中国对人力资源发展的合作上。本项目从分析新型的中非大学伙伴关系的多种维度来填补这一空白，并会特别注意中国已经提供的层面。 这项研究将回答更大的研究问题，也就是关于中非合作论坛为非洲提供的能力建设项目，为优先提供长、短期培训的依据，及把中非高校合作作为中国推行能力发展计划的选择。更广泛而言，一个这样的问题就出现了：中国所喜欢的伦理讨论，如南南互学、双赢的经济合作、互惠互利、人员交换等等，是怎样与20+20的中非能力建设项目所展现的那样一致——从某些衡量角度而言，后者更是一种单向的、不对称的中非合作关系。 这一项目将运用案例研究的方法，伴随着定性的小组访谈、参与者观察、以及定性的档案化数据的形式，来为所有20所中国参与的大学进行备档，并深度调研在其中9对接受教育的非洲学生、受训人员、教师与研究者，了解他们的经验与体会。 通过培训、传播和发表，这项研究将会加强香港及大陆为非洲提供人力资源现行政策的批判意识和分析能力，并会激发由内地大学的国际化给香港的大学带来的启示。

842912.label: Realisation of objectives
842912.value: Objective 1: Through the lens of the 20+20 scheme of university collaboration between Africa and China, it was possible to tease out the many synergies amongst China’s HRD policies for Africa. The detail of these has been laid out in the series of FOCAC declarations and action plans. This has been particularly the case since the Beijing Summit and 3rd Ministerial Conference of 2006, and most recently the Johannesburg Summit and 6th Ministerial Conference. In the latter conference, it can be plainly seen that the 20+20 inter-university cooperation is part of whole range of collaborative and partnership endeavors. China’s HRD cooperation is not confined to relations between the formal education system in China and its counterpart in Africa. There are HRD and knowledge sharing pledges relating to science, technology and knowledge sharing. One of the most ambitious pledges from Johannesburg related to the support of vocational training centres and colleges for capacity building in Africa. Clearly, one of the iconic forms of China’s HRD cooperation has been the provision of Confucius Institutes and Classrooms to Africa. There are over 46 Confucius Institutes across Africa, and they are responsible for many short- and long-term scholarships and training courses in China. Further dimensions of China’s HRD support cover partnerships through cultural exchange as well as support to people-to-people collaboration, including volunteers to Africa. Objective 2: Partnership is at the core of China’s HRD cooperation, and provides the thread that runs through almost all of the HRD activities. It is central to the Confucius Institute arrangements with Africa, as well as the 20+20 scheme. But it also goes back into the history of China’s relations with Africa, since it was university partnership which was at the beginning of HRD cooperation. The research was able to analyze the symmetry in the claims of win-win cooperation and mutual benefit. Overall, it was clear that there was symmetry, but the fact that China was the main financier of the 20+20 scheme, and that the funds remained in Chinese universities did suggest a degree of financial asymmetry. By contrast in the African Confucius Institute arrangements, the funds were attached to the partner universities in Africa and there is joint China-Africa management. It should be underlined that unlike many development partners, China’s HRD cooperation is almost exclusively at the higher education level. Objective 3: Over time there has been a diversification of both long- and short-term training supported by China. The overall trend since the beginning of FOCAC in 2000 has been upward. But though most of the short-term training schemes involve trainees going to China, there have been some examples of these being carried out sur place in Africa. This was the case in one of the case-study universities in Kenya. It may also be assumed that the training of 200,000 local technical and vocational personnel, promised in the Johannesburg action plan, will also be carried out locally. It should also be noted that in ‘China’s position paper on the implementation of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development’, there were plans for the further development of South-South cooperation and development through the establishment of an Academy with that name. It is in China and provides a wide range of training. As far as the case-study universities are concerned within the 20+20 scheme, there was some movement of staff and students in both directions (for very short visits), but the scale of the movement was very much less than in the established long- and short-term training schemes. This was principally because the funding of 20+20 has been constrained. The annual bidding process may have been a constraint on longer term planning. Objective 4: Certainly, warm relations had developed between those charged with 20+20 in the case-study universities. The universities sought to ensure that their particular strengths whether in marine life, textile engineering, agriculture or education were matched in terms of staff and students being exchanged. It was noted that in the science-based 20+20 partnerships, the relatively small amounts of 20+20 funding did not make it possible to organize joint research projects between the partners. The scale of the interaction was therefore in large part influenced by the available funding. Thus, short-term exchange visits were possible, but not long-term attachments. To an extent, the 20+20 exchange students and staff were helped by the presence of other elements of HRD cooperation. Thus a single case-study university in Africa might have a Confucius Institute as well as a 20+20 scheme and an on-going partnership with China. This synergy assisted the 20+20 scheme. But the 20+20 brand was itself sometimes less visible than some other dimensions of HRD cooperation. Objective 5: Doubtless, the project has significantly increased understanding of South-South cooperation through the range of seminars that have been provided in case-study universities, as well as in other academic centers in Hong Kong, Edinburgh, London, Toronto and New Delhi. As to the improvement of the modalities of South–South cooperation, it would be beneficial if the members of the 20 universities in China and their counterparts in Africa could meet to exchange views and insights. This happens with the Confucius Institute program, where the African Confucius Institutes meet annually as a group, as well as in a world-wide convention. Again, this is essentially an issue of money. Papers presented by the lead researchers have also contributed. Objective 6: The project has organized a whole series of seminars throughout its life. These have been held in ZNU, HKIEd (now EdUHK), CUHK and HKU. It has been important for graduate students to appreciate the complexity and relevance of China’s cooperation in Africa. This has certainly happened, and has benefited not only the rather small numbers of students linked to the 20+20 scheme but to other larger groups of students from Africa studying in case-study universities in China. In addition to assisting understanding in the above universities and their African partners, the project has also been able to provide insights through a whole series of seminars in Japan, UK, Canada, USA, Germany and Switzerland.

842912.label: Major findings and research outcome
842912.value: The 20+20 initiative has been a small-scale but successful scheme for building bridges between a very wide range of universities in China and Africa. These cover many of the most prestigious universities in China as well as in Africa. The selection criteria for becoming a member of the 20+20 family included that the Chinese partners should already have some experience of working with Africa. This meant that the 20+20 dimension of partnership was inevitably seen as just adding value to existing expertise on Africa. In the case of Peking, Shanghai Normal, North East Normal and Zhejiang Normal, for example, there were already many well-established connections with Africa. One of the conclusions from the research is that while there were meetings amongst the Chinese university members of the 20+20, there don’t appear to have been any parallel workshops amongst the African 20+20 community. This meant that even in the same country, e.g. Kenya and South Africa where there two 20+20 universities each, there was little learning through exchange in the way that has been commonplace amongst the Confucius Institutes based in Africa, with their regular regional meetings. One of the disappointments in the research was that Pravina and Kenneth King were not able to carry out their final review of the case study universities in Africa. This was because of a short term medical problem (2-3 months). But there was no readiness in the University of Hong Kong to take account of this inevitable slippage in the project timing. Hence, very regrettably it didn’t allow project extension for real implementation afterwards; and hence some HKD 133,000 were sent back to the Funding Council and the original project plan was not 100% completed. Regardless of this, the project had begun to bed down in the case study universities that were visited. Good relationships had been formed, and there had been some valuable traffic of students and staff in both directions. One of the early findings was that UNESCO Paris had hoped to turn this collaboration between two large partners into a tripartite project along with UNESCO. To that end, a launch meeting was arranged in Paris in 2011, and both sets of partners were invited from the 20+20 universities, but this initiative doesn’t appear to have continued after the original meeting.

842912.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
842912.value: Based on the findings of the project, there are potentials as below for the further development of the research with suggested actions: 1. China-Africa collaboration through university partnerships has carried its legacy in the new times, especially since the 2010s. It builds up on new models for international development, hence is worthy of continuous funding for research. 2. In the new era of Xi’s China for the new “One-Belt & One-Road” framework, Hong Kong universities are in the unique position to join the new adventure in terms of university partnerships in Africa. Substantial research should be funded on the new ways of higher education internationalization in Hong Kong. 3. Meanwhile, through these endeavours of research, the research capacity of Hong Kong Universities should be substantially strengthened.

842912.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
842912.value: The 2009 Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC)’s 2010-2012 Action Plan announced the twinning of 20 Chinese and 20 African universities, with most partners having a history of collaboration with Africa and China respectively. The Plan also offered short-term training for 20,000 Africans and 5,500 long-term scholarships by 2012. This project studies the rationale, character, quality and coherence of this cooperation, using the 20+20 university partnership of FOCAC as a lens. While substantial research has been conducted on China’s economic relations with Africa, including those covered by FOCAC, few studies addressed China’s HRD cooperation. The project addresses this gap by analysing the multiple dimensions of this new China-Africa inter-university partnership, and pays particular attention to what is delivered in China. With a case study methodology, it addresses the larger questions on FOCAC’s capacity-building programme for Africa. This research, through its training, dissemination and publications, strengthens critical awareness and analytic capacity in Hong Kong and in the Mainland on China’s current human resources policies for Africa, and raises implications for Hong Kong’s universities of these trends in the internationalisation of Mainland universities.

843112.label: Project Objectives
843112.value: To identify the practical difficulties experienced by school teachers when teaching students with ASD in local classroom environments and settings. To compare the differences between primary and secondary school teachers in terms of the difficulties encountered. To conduct systematic reviews to identify (and meta-analysis if and when appropriate to quantify) specific areas of the effects of two commonly used intervention strategies, namely, TEACCH and positive behavior support on the teaching of students with ASD (note: systematic review of Social Stories has already been conducted previously by other researchers). To design and implement a training course for teachers of students with ASD that will integrate three existing interventions into a consolidated strategic model. To evaluate the proposed integrative teaching model described above in terms of the academic and social performance of students with ASD. We are also interested in investigating whether the effectiveness, if any, is different between primary and secondary school settings.

843112.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
843112.value: Effective teaching strategies can provide appropriate support to students with special educational needs (SEN), including learners with autism spectrum disorders (ASD), to help them to adjust within ordinary school settings. The inclusion of students with ASD in ordinary schools is challenging for teachers in Hong Kong (CSNSIE, 2003; Sin et al., 2010). Commonly used intervention strategies were primarily developed in western countries; whether the interventions are culturally sensitive to local students are to be evaluated systematically. In this research, we initiate to use a holistic approach as the conceptual framework and to develop a consolidated intervention strategy based on the principles of three well-developed methods: social story, TEACCH, and positive behavior support. The proposed integrated intervention is designed to be culturally sensitive to the learning needs and the behavioral characteristics of students with ASD in ordinary schools in Chinese-speaking populations. We plan to recruit 180 teachers and 180 students, from 60 primary and 30 secondary schools, having close interaction with students with ASD. Focus group interviews of teacher participants will be conducted to identify the practical challenges encountered in teaching students with ASD. Findings from the interviews will be used to refine the consolidated intervention strategy. The teachers will then be equally allocated to three groups: (i) Experimental Group I – training provided on the three well-developed methods mentioned above; (ii) Experimental Group II – same training as Experimental Group I plus additional training on the consolidated approach; (iii) Control Group – without any training. The social behavior of the student participants will be observed for one year; their change in academic performance will be assessed. Quantitative and qualitative outcome measures will be collected at pre-, midway, and post-intervention stages by taping classroom teaching and learning activities. Focus group interviews will be conducted among teacher participants, parents and classmates of student participants to obtain feedbacks on learning and teaching. The study is the first one in attempting to derive an evidence-based intervention strategy that is culturally sensitive to Chinese speaking populations. The integrative approach could potentially have a big impact on teacher education for inclusive practice in Asian countries. The study is timely from the practical perspective given the urgent need for consolidation of the professional development of teachers for inclusive education. The research team also plans to conduct an evaluation of the intervention approach in Singapore concurrently and other Chinese speaking populations in Asia shortly after for comparison purposes. 有效的教學策略可以提供適當的支援給有特殊教育需要（SEN）的學生、包括自閉症譜系障礙（ASD）的學生，並幫助他們適應普通學校的環境。在普通學校納入有ASD的學生對老師來說是具有挑戰性的。 常用的介入策略主要是由西方國家開發，但當應用在本地學生時，這些介入策略在文化上是否有充足的敏感程度，需要有系統性地作出評估。 在這項研究中，我們率先使用一種全面的方法作為概念框架，以發展出一個綜合介入策略，此策略建基於三個已發展方法的要點上，包括：社會故事(social story)，TEACCH，積極行為支持(positive behavior support)。這綜合介入策略目標包括對在普通學校讀書並患有ASD的華語學生具有文化敏感性。 我們計劃從60所小學及30所中學中，招募與ASD學生有密切互動的教師和學生各180名。我們會為參加的教師進行焦點小組訪問以識別現實中教導ASD學生的挑戰。訪談結果將被用於改善綜合介入策略。參加的教師將平均分配分為三組：（一）實驗組I – 他們會得到上述三個已開發方法的培訓（二）實驗組II –得到與實驗組I相同的訓練，再額外得到綜合方法的訓練;（三）對照組 – 沒有任何培訓。 參加學生的社會行為會被觀察一年;學習成績變化亦會進行評估。在介入階段和介入後階段，課室中的教學及學習情況都會被錄音以收集定量及定性的資料。參加教師、學生的家長和同學們會進行焦點小組訪問以獲得學習和教學的反饋。 這項研究是第一個試圖推導出一個以證據為基礎的介入策略，此策略將對華語人口來說具文化敏感性。在包容性教學實踐方面，這個一體化的方法對亞洲國家的教師教育可能有著很大的影響。有見於對在鞏固包容教育上，教師專業發展有著迫切需要，這項研究從實際角度來看是非常及時的。 研究小組還計劃會在短時間內在其他亞洲的華語地區進行評估以作比較。

843112.label: Major findings and research outcome
843112.value: 1. The present study attempted to examine practical challenges in including learners with ASD in an ordinary school setting. The principal participants reported several challenges, including school dilemma about the development of inclusive education, understanding and managing psycho-social behavior, peer acceptance and support, teamwork to create an inclusive environment; and home-school collaboration. It was expressed that having proper mechanisms in place in a child’s school environment is critical for them to be accepted as a valued member of the class. Discussion: Schools should develop effective strategies to create an inclusive classroom environment for learners with ASD to increase student engagement in social interaction and learning-teaching activities. Implications to education policy and school resources are discussed. 2.Teacher participants of the experimental group showed enhanced capacity in using inclusive instructions, managing ASD behavior and working collaboratively. This group of teacher participants also had a higher level of self-efficacy in inclusive classroom practice. Student participants of the experimental group improved in terms of academic and social performance. Conclusion: The present study provided initial findings to support the effectiveness of the integrated model for learners with ASD in the inclusive school environment. Implications of the research findings to teacher professional development and inclusive classroom practice will be discussed. The Hong Kong experience may also offer insight to Asian countries that are experiencing educational changes. 3. The experimental group had 44 pairs of teacher-student participants. Another group of 22 pairs was recruited as the control group (delayed intervention) for data comparison. Results from the 21 pairs of teacher-student participants in the experimental group showed that after the intervention, there was an improvement in the mean scores of teachers’ acceptance attitude and their efficacy (to use inclusive instructions, to use the collaborative approach, and to manage ASD behavior) toward the inclusive education. Teachers applied strategies of TEACCH and positive behavior support (PBS) more frequently. Thirteen of the twenty-one The student participants’ academic reports (Learning Achievement Measurement Kit -LAMK standardized tests developed by the Education Bureau of HKSAR Government) were collected. These participants’ Chinese level improved later. As to the students’ classroom, aberrant behavior assessed by the teachers, mean scores of lethargy and stereotypy were improved. A group of 16 pairs of teacher-student pairs received two years of intervention and the results showed positive outcome in terms of student academic and social performance.

843112.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
843112.value: In October 2015, one pilot study was developed as an outgrowth of this line of research work with the target group extended to kindergarten teachers of young children with ASD in regular classrooms (aged 3 to 6 years old). Teacher training with practical component and school-based consultation and support with input from ASD experts were provided to the kindergarten teachers. The purposive samples of 30 kindergarten teachers and their students are diagnosed with or suspected of having ASD were recruited (n=32). The teacher participants from the experimental group received teacher training and school-based professional support from ASD specialists. The control group received delayed teacher training. In July 2016, this pilot study was completed. The preliminary finding indicated that the kindergarten teachers showed a higher level of efficacy for inclusive practice. For students, they showed improvement in classroom adjustment and social interaction.

843112.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
843112.value: The focus is to upgrade teachers’ capacity in teaching students with ASD in local primary and secondary schools. For teachers who participated in this project, they attended training workshops and seminars on ASD behavior and concepts of the integrated model being studied by the research team. This model is based on three well-known intervention strategies: social story sentence structure (auditory means), the Treatment and Education of Autistic and Related Communication Handicapped Children (TEACCH; visual support), and positive behavior support (preventive and proactive perspective; strength-based approach). The teachers also received school-based consultation and support from ASD experts. Pre- and post-intervention data was collected to measure the project outcome. Results of the study indicated that the teachers showed enhanced capacity in using inclusive instructions, managing ASD behavior and working collaboratively. The teachers also showed a higher level of self-efficacy for inclusive practice. For students, they improved in terms of academic performance and social interaction to some extent. This project provided initial findings to support the effectiveness of the integrated model on teacher efficacy and inclusiveness of students with ASD. The findings also indicated that teacher training with practical component and professional input from ASD experts could further enhance teacher’s capacity for inclusive practice.

843212.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
843212.value: Hong Kong, along with other OECD nations, shares a concern with how well school is preparing young people, including poor and ethnic minority students, for further education and careers, as well as life more broadly beyond school. It was partly this concern that led to the changes to senior secondary schooling in Hong Kong introduced to transform this phase of education into a modern mass system that successfully prepares young people to undertake further study and confidently pursue work and careers. How well have the changes worked, and how does Hong Kong’s system compare against other systems? To find out, our plan is to track a sample of young people from the beginning of senior secondary schooling through to university, technical institutes and/or employment. What students decide to pursue when, why, and how are crucial questions for understanding how the current arrangements in senior secondary are working. The sample will be structured so that young people from a range of different backgrounds and school settings will be included and the relative influence of background and setting can be measured. While we investigate transitions in Hong Kong, teams of other researchers (independently funded) will be conducting the same study in six major cities in Europe, North America and Australia. By studying Hong Kong within this wider framework, we plan to assess differences and similarities in student transitions and the factors that influence them. Important factors that will be considered include institutional arrangements, organization of schooling, curriculum, types of schools, university selection, and students’ backgrounds. Survey instruments will be used to assess student interests and plans, student well-being, achievement (low and high achievers will be identified) and school engagement. The key questions will be: Where achievement is constant across nations, how do student characteristics and institutional arrangements influence destinations? How do Hong Kong students compare to their international peers? What are the barriers to better transition and the best improvement strategies, particularly for young people from disadvantaged backgrounds? This will be a multi¬level study that will seek to contextualize Hong Kong students’ key experiences and attributes and the effect of these on school transitions. The aim of the study is to develop a theoretical framework that can account for the post-school destinations of students in Hong Kong. Such a framework will have a local dimension, making it distinctive within the cross-national study of which this is a part. 香港中學如何為青少年做好就業及升讀高等教育的準備？近年來香港的教育制度不斷轉變，令青年人有更好的條件做好準備，迎接將來的挑戰。本研究將探討香港教育制度轉變所帶來的成效，以及比較香港與世界各國教育制度的差異。 本研究的對象為社會上不同階層的高中學生，探討現行教育制度對他們高中畢業出路的影響。本研究將會聯同歐洲，北美和澳洲不同城市的研究人員進行比較研究。通過比較，分折世界各地的數據，找出其間的異同與優劣，從而歸納出影響香港高中學生就業及升讀高等教育的因素。 研究議題包括：香港學生的特征和教育制度如何影響他們畢業後的出路？香港學生如何在國際上接軌？高中學生畢業後在升學及就業上會遇到什麼困難？弱勢社羣的學生在選擇畢業後的路向所面對的困難。 研究旨在建構一套理論框架來詮釋影響香港高中學生畢業後出路的因素，也希望有關理論框架能廣泛應用於香港以至世界不同地區。

843212.label: Realisation of objectives
843212.value: To flourishingly identify a cohort of young people at the beginning of senior secondary to provide baseline data on Hong Kong students regarding the preparation for further study and careers, more than 5000 S4 students from 54 schools, were invited to participate in this study. At first, only 52 schools agreed for participation, and 2 more schools consented after careful consideration. The study involves questionnaire study for students, teachers and principals from the 54 schools, focus interviews for 132 S6 students and in-depth interviews with the 26 of them, concerning the different journeys of young people through school and beyond to investigate how the engagement in schools and learning; 21st century skills; plans for the future; home and family contexts influence students’ intentional destinations. Finally, 54 schools (which are more than twenty schools as proposed originally) agreed to participate in the research project. In each school, all S4 students were invited to participate in the online questionnaire and assessment test. The choice of the whole year-level cohort was to ensure that young people from all backgrounds, all ability levels and in all programme areas were represented. The participation from each school was voluntary and subject to students’ and teachers’ agreement. The questionnaires and assessment test that was designed by Hong Kong Institute of Education (HKIEd) (now retitled as The Education University of Hong Kong) in collaboration with the research team at the University of Melbourne were the standardized instruments that were being used across all participating cities in the International Study of City Youth (ISCY). Questionnaires and interviews conducted at the outset of the study were tailored to investigate Hong Kong students in respect of their school completion plans and Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination (HKDSE) intentions, school and parents influence on students’ life plans, students’ reflection on themselves as ethical citizens with the 21st century skills and opinions to government about educational issues (which is known as Objective 1). Cross-sectional research has been conducted to compare intentional destinations (asked when student participants were in S4) and the real destinations (known as the current pathway students are taking for a small sample of S6 students) for students from different schools (which is known as Objective 2). This could also help for a small sample of S6 students with the part to examine how young people’s perceptions of themselves as learners and their behaviors vary according to the type of school they take in the senior years of secondary schooling, which comprises variations in program provision and learning opportunities; and according to the family background of students, the availability of resources to support learning and further education work (which is to realise Objective 3). Moreover, there were sessions in the questionnaire and interviews requiring student participants to rate whether the school provision of support structures, programs and activities could be satisfactory that students would be guided through the completion of school successfully in a way that they are encouraged to set goals and plan to attain them, so as to achieve Objective 4. Upon the completion of data collection process, journals, book chapters and press release were productively prepared, comparing institutional arrangements that comprise senior secondary education, emphasis on generic skills, career and life planning education and vocational education (to realise Objectives 5 and 6) . To draw a comparison between the institutional arrangements in Hong Kong and other ISCY cities and participating countries, e.g. Australia, USA and France, both the national and state levels of comparison were involved in relevant literature review.

843212.label: Major findings and research outcome
843212.value: The following research findings were carried out up to the last progress report. Finally, approximately 5900 students, 600 teachers and more than 40 principals have participated in questionnaire survey respectively. The findings indicated 94 percent of the students intended to remain at school and more than 90 percent planned to undertake the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education (HKDSE). More than 80 percent of the students agreed that they had received help from their schools in career planning, and about 70 percent stated that their parents expected them to study at university. In early 2015, about 10 out of 54 schools agreed to participate in our focus group interview upon our further invitation, the students’ focus group interview was conducted between February and April in 2015, yet teachers’ focus group interview took more time to complete until May 2016. Totally, more than 160 students and 30 teachers were invited to join the focus group interview, so as to give comments on the current school support on the career and life planning. Invitations of follow-up sessions were sent to more than 160 S6 students from different schools since July 2015, while about 130 of them agreed to take part in (of which about 20 of them participated in an in-depth interview). The participation is on a voluntary basis. The sessions foregrounded the identification of the intended destinations of student participants, so as to compare intentional destinations and the real destinations for students from different types of schools. The follow-up interviews revealed that they would prefer to study local or overseas bachelor degree or sub-degree programmes. The students regarded further study as the preferred pathway due to keen competition in society. They also worried that having a low qualification would undermine their personal competitiveness and hence hinder their fight for a brighter future. Significantly, the students were more concerned with their personal development in society and the challenges they would be facing in the workplace and labour market. Issues regarding the youth skills development, transition from school to work and educational pathways etc. have been further discussed in a special issue published in February 2017 on Educational Research for Policy and Practice journal themed as ‘School to work transitions: Preparing students for the future’, and in the book ‘Transitions to Post-School Life: Responsiveness to Individual, Social and Economic Needs’ (contracted awarded by an intentional publisher, Springer) edited by the research team.

843212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
843212.value: Further research activities had been carried out as envisaged during this reporting period. In order to further investigate the current practice of school-to-work transition, a new research project named “Vocational Education and Training for Youth Development” sponsored by a privately-funded organization has been started. This research aims at examining the role and problems of egalitarianism for enhancing Vocational Education and Training (VET) in Hong Kong, identifying a mechanism to evaluate the current VET System and Qualifications Framework, and exploring possible options for a local version of VET system. However, it should be noted that an international report template in collaboration with the University of Melbourne’s research team for data sharing with participating schools had yet to be established due to unavailability of international data concerning the data collected in the other participating countries. Nevertheless, it has been foreseen and has already been stated in the mid-term progress report that ‘the comparative aspect of the study should be excluded as international data may not be available before the project deadline. It was also stated that the intended comparison can be made when international data in respect of other participating countries is available and after the submission of this final report’.

843212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
843212.value: This research project is the first systematic local study in relation to school-to-work transition under the New Senior Secondary (NSS) Curriculum implemented in 2009, when the government emphasized this reformed curriculum would favour multiple pathways for senior secondary graduates. It is therefore valuable to know if the prospects of students meet this key objective of the NSS reform. Under the keen competition in Hong Kong, the exploration of students’ intention and destination of their study and career may provide a clear picture on how general youth can seek their aspiration in reality. Moreover, since the adoption of Career and Life Planning Education in 2014 was deemed as a critical educational endeavor in Hong Kong, it is appropriate to conduct an initial review for future implication on practices. From this research, a deeper understanding could be achieved through measuring S4 students’ perception of their 21st century skills or competencies. Remarkably, 21 century education should focus more on soft skills learning rather than knowledge-led education. This research hopes to contribute by drawing public’s attention to the potential weakness on skills or competencies of current students in Hong Kong, which should further focus and assist from all parties in the society.

843612.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
843612.value: The transition period from high-school to post-school education or employment is a time of significant changes and challenges that requires psychological adjustment for many adolescents. Many decisions regarding further education, career choices, and living arrangement have to be made. The period signifies the transition to adulthood and independent life. Post-school transition for young people with disabilities is often more complicated than that of their peers without disabilities. They face a range of problems such as unemployment, low community participation and inactive adult life (Blackorby & Wagner, 1996; Dewson et al, 2004; Madaus, 2005). In Hong Kong, in comparison with their peers, individuals with special education needs (SEN) are likely to have the same difficulties after leaving school. While there is an increasing concern among prominent education researchers in Western countries on post-school transition for SEN students (Neubert & Moon, 2006; Test et al., 2009; Winn & Hay, 2009), the research effort on this topic is far from adequate in an Asian setting. Given that there is evidence of cultural variation in the concepts of childrearing and family practices for SEN students (Blacher, 2011; Harry, 1992), there is always an urgent call for evidence-based study on post-school transition adaptation among young SEN adults in a Chinese cultural setting (Rehabilitation Advisory Committee, 2007; Sin, 2010; Ng, 2005). Hong Kong has launched the reform in restructuring the academic system in 2009. The concern among policymakers, academics, schools and families is whether SEN students have adequate post-school options leading to a higher level of community inclusion (Sin, 2010). This study will be the first attempt to identify the critical elements that have impacts on the post-secondary education outcomes for SEN students in a Chinese cultural setting. With reference to the theoretical concepts of life quality, the environmental factors (e.g. social support and opportunities), individual factors (e.g. adaptive behaviour and health condition), and transition success (e.g. education or employment placement, quality of life and socialization) will be systematically examined. Insider perspectives from SEN graduates and stakeholders will be studied. The findings will provide insights for policymakers to refine the secondary education curriculum for meeting SEN, for stakeholders to improve the transition programs and support for SEN students, and for academics to solicit the essential factors for transitional support. The resultant outcome aims at facilitating successful community inclusion of SEN graduates and responding to the United Nations Convention of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (2008). 從高中到後中學教育或就業，對一般青少年來說，是一段充滿改變與挑戰的過渡時期，需要心理上的適應。在這段時期，青少年要為升學、就業選擇、住宿安排等作決定。這時期表徵著踏入成年人和獨立生活的階段。比起普通年青人，有殘疾的年青人所面對的離校過渡期通常都更為複雜。他們要面對各種問題，包括失業、低社區參與和非活躍的成年人生活((Blackorby & Wagner, 1996; Dewson et al, 2004; Madaus, 2005)。在香港，有特殊教育需要的人士很可能面對相同的困難。 正當西方國家著名教育研究者對於有特殊教育需要的學生的離校過渡有漸長的關注(Neubert & Moon, 2006; Test et al., 2009; Winn & Hay, 2009)，亞洲對於這題材的研究非常缺乏。正因有證據顯示文化因素影響父母對有特殊教育需要學生的教養方法和家庭教育觀念(Blacher, 2011; Harry, 1992)，實在有逼切需要去進行關於在中國文化的環境下，有特殊教育需要的青年人在離校過渡適應的實證基礎研究(Rehabilitation Advisory Committee, 2007; Sin, 2010; Ng, 2005)。 香港在2009年推行了教育系統的改革。政策制定者、學術界、學校、家庭均關注有特殊教育需要學生在離開中學以後是否有足夠的出路選擇可以達至更高層次的社區共融(Sin, 2010)。本研究會是第一項嘗試去辨析在中國文化背景底下，什麼關鍵性的元素會影響有特殊教育需要學生的後中學教育。本研究會根據生活質素的理論，有系統地檢查環境因素(如:社會支持和機會)、個人因素(如:適應行為和健康狀況)、和成功的過渡因素(如:教育或就業、生活質素和社交)。本研究會調查有特殊教育需要畢業生和各持份者的觀點。 研究結果將有助於: 政策制定者改善中學教育課程、持份者改善過渡期的計劃安排和給予有特殊教育需要學生的支援、和學者研究過渡期支援不可缺的因素。研究結果旨在促成有特殊教育需要畢業生成功的社會融合，以回應聯合國殘疾人權利公約(2008)。

843612.label: Realisation of objectives
843612.value: In regard to the change of the academic structure in secondary, all students are provided with the 12 years free education in Hong Kong. This research was a timely study for examining the post-school outcomes of senior secondary graduates with special educational needs. The study covered the existing post-school placements and available opportunities for the new senior secondary education graduates with SEN, barriers, guidance and support and areas for improvement. As stated in the proposal, four major research methods were applied to study our topic of interest: 1) Literature review on local and overseas policies and practices; 2) Questionnaire study; 3); Focus groups and 4) Case studies. During the period, the study followed closely with stages specified in the proposal. The team reviewed the policy, support and practices for SEN students from literature, visits and sharing in local and regional organizations, so as to build up the theoretical framework and areas of concern for further study. With the support from the schools and parents, a number of students with disabilities in mainstreaming and special schools were invited to take part in the study. In total, 710 students in grades 10 to 12 (S4 to S6) participated in the survey. Among them, 586 (82.5%) are S6 students, 95 (13.4%) S5 and 29 (4.1%) S4 students. The total number of SEN students with different categories was 98 (12 HI, 5 VI, 2 PD, 4 ASD, 9 CD, 8 ADHD, 45 SpLD, others 13). To prepare the focus group interviews to a wide range of stakeholders, the research team sent invitations to all Hong Kong secondary schools and special schools. 18 schools agreed to participate in this study and 40 focus groups were invited in this qualitative study. The subjects included a wide range of these stakeholders (60 teachers, 19 social workers, 37 parents of SEN students and 72 SEN students) for their understanding of post-school outcomes for SEN students, difficulties, support and their expectations. The data collected were useful for further analysis. With reference to the proposed objectives, the first three objectives, including support, practice and barriers, have been addressed by findings generated from the focus group interviews. The fourth objective, aiming at the recommendations for informing policy change and updates of support, has been addressed by findings generated from the focus group interviews and also key findings from the main survey and the follow-up survey study (two rounds).
