846012.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
846012.value: 現今的學校管理制度下，校長越來越不可能單靠個人的領導來影響學校生活的各個方面。隨著全球學校管理權責下放運動的推及，以及學校不斷面臨更具挑戰性的教育目標，以團隊為基礎的領導勢必成為學校高效運作和持續發展的核心動力。然而，團隊領導的形式和機制在研究文獻中仍然非常少；而從團隊的角度，考察香港及中國內地學校領導運作的研究則更為稀缺。 團隊工作的一個突顯優勢在於它讓校長啟動參與式群體過程。在此過程中，團隊成員共同努力，就複雜的問題做出有效的決策、並展開聯合行動。然而，相當多的研究證據表明：管理團隊往往不能發揮他們的潛能；此外，文化以及人際關係的因素可能會促進或阻礙參與式群體過程。 基於團隊研究中輸入-過程-輸出的理論框架，本項目著重研究區內三種類型小學的學校管理團隊：香港的本地學校、中國內地的本地學校、在香港和內地的國際學校。它旨在從多個層面增進對學校管理團隊機制的瞭解。該項目主要圍繞六個問題展開研究：1）在這三種類型學校中，學校管理團隊的人員組成有什麼特點？ 2）在這三種類型的學校中，管理責任和領導職能是如何分佈的？管理團隊成員的角色是怎樣相互聯繫的？ 3）學校管理團隊的組成和結構性特點如何影響參與式群體過程？ 4）哪些文化及人際關係因素會阻礙或者促進學校管理團隊的過程？ 5）學校管理團隊內部的參與式群體過程與決策全面性、決策實施質量，及學校效率是否有關聯？ 6）這三種類型學校之間，學校管理團隊的特點和模式可能會有哪些明顯的差異？ 本項目的重要性源於幾個特點。首先，將研究焦點從校長領導轉向學校管理團隊應該能夠更好預測學校的績效。其次，它將驗證這一地區學校管理中是否存在文化特異性，回應有關學校管理中有關普適性-差異性的討論。三，研究將提供富有情境內容的知識基礎，其結論可以為如何優化團隊領導結構提供指引。最後，該項目將會為未來在區內開展的學校管理團隊研究奠定有利的基礎。

846212.label: Realisation of objectives
846212.value: Objective 1. Examine the overall proficiency level of listening skills of fluent speech spoken by native English speakers among Chinese undergraduate students learning English as a second language We have successfully recruited and tested over 200 undergraduate in the PI and collaborators’ universities (The Education University of Hong Kong, City University of Hong Kong and Chinese University of Hong Kong). These student participants have a wide range of English listening proficiency and major in different disciplines; thus, give us a representative sample of Chinese undergraduate students in Hong Kong. We assessed the native English listening comprehension skills in these students using audio of BBC/CNN news and a self-developed test. On average, these students were only able to obtain 60% accuracy. Although the performances were above chance level, such substandard performance of native English comprehension is an alarming phenomenon. It is important to note that the performance level shown above was obtained a noise-free environment. In reality, noise such as multi-talker babble is present in normal circumstance and may hinder the comprehension of nonnative spoken language. Our results have further shown that the accuracy rate dropped below chance level when students were instructed to identify native English fluent speech in adverse listening conditions (e.g., multi-talker babble and factory noise). Objective 2. Identify and classify the perceptual difficulties in perceiving native English fluent speech which are not attributable to poor vocabulary knowledge We created a set of cognitive-linguistic tests, including receptive vocabulary test and tested our student participants. By a series of hierarchical regression analyses, we found that vocabulary knowledge directly predict the performances of native English fluent speech comprehension. Other than vocabulary knowledge, we have provided evidences that part-word recognition in a speech gating task directly predict the performances of native English fluent speech comprehension. The part-word recognition skill also mediates the effect of phonemic awareness and phonological memory on native English fluent speech comprehension. Further to cognitive-linguistic skills, we found a significant correlation between the amount of exposure to the native fluent English in daily life and the performances of listening comprehension ability. This is an important finding because it reveals that listening skill for second language is complex and requires good quality and quantity of linguistic input. 3. Examine the relations between the perception of fluent speech and cognitive-linguistic skills, such as phoneme perception, categorical perception of phonemes, phonemic awareness, speech production, and phonological memory The skills listed in objective 3 were assessed in our study. These skills were correlated with general listening ability and contributed unique variance to general listening ability; thus, were proven to be important linguistic correlates of general listening ability. To further examine the interplay among these variables, we made use of the data to test a series of mediation statistical models by the Sobel test and bootstrapping test. We obtained three mediation statistical models and constructed a phonological development model specific to the second language fluent speech comprehension is proposed (Wong et al., TESOL Quarterly, 2015).

846212.label: Major findings and research outcome
846212.value: First of all, we have observed substandard performances of native English comprehension skills among Chinese undergraduate students learning English as a second language (ESL) (Wong et al., 2015). The results of the listening test revealed that our participants could only obtain 60% accuracy when listening to BBC/ CNN news, even though they had passed the English requirement for university entry. Our results further showed that our participants were poor at decoding English reduced forms (e.g., contraction, elision, assimilation). The average accuracy rate was as low as 58%, a surprising results given English language education has a long history in Hong Kong and there are ample learning opportunities and educational support in Hong Kong. Our correlational analyses also indicated significant and strong link (Pearson correlation ranges from 0.32 to 0.63) between the overall listening performances and various cognitive-linguistics skills such as English vocabulary knowledge, English minimal pairs discrimination (e.g., /ship/ vs. /sheep/) and phonological working memory. The regression analyses showed that receptive vocabulary and perception of reduced forms contributed 5 to 8% unique variance to listening comprehension for native English. Moreover, results further show that part-word recognition in a speech gating task and receptive vocabulary predicted perception of reduced forms via a direct pathway, whereas phonemic awareness and phonological memory predicted perception of reduced forms via an indirect pathway (through part-word recognition). The results of the project have confirmed a significant role of the ability to process reduced forms (e.g., contraction, elision, assimilation) of English words in comprehending native spoken English by Chinese undergraduate learners of English. Additionally, we also found a strong link (Pearson correlation = .30 and .33 respectively) between speech perception and production in processing British and American English among Chinese undergraduate learners (Wong et al., 2013). Also, it is worth to note that the listening performances were largely affected when the ESL listeners are exposed to a noisy environment such that a lot of phonetic signals are either lost or distorted (Tsui & Wong, 2014). The accuracy rate of reduced forms identification was 23%, 45%, 57% under the conditions of “multi-talker babble”, “speech-shaped noise” and “factory noise”, respectively. We have also found from the English production errors that Chinese ESL learners made use of their Chinese phonetic reduction system to mentally represent and process L2 English sounds and therefore they fail to accurately decode the English connected speech (Dealey & Wong, 2016).

846212.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
846212.value: I am thankful to the RGC for providing me the ECS grant to embark on a meaningful research. My interest in second language listening comprehension is strengthened. In the current ECS project, I have identified individual difference, error profile and cognitive-linguistic correlates of connected speech/ reduced forms perception. I would like to study the learning mechanism underlying the acquisition of reduced forms perception. Hence, I applied and obtained an internal research grant (ref no. RG72 / 2015-2016) from the Education University of Hong Kong and have been carrying out a project titled “The learning mechanism of connected speech perception in Chinese learners of English as a second language.” From my research, I have also realized that poor reduced forms perception in Chinese ESL learners is partly attributed to the reliance of subtitles and transcription. To test the speculation, I have submitted a GRF grant entitled “The immediate and long-term effects of subtitles on the comprehension of English connected speech in Chinese learners” (RGC ref no: 18608817) in the 2017/18 round to examine the interplay between subtitles and reduced forms perception in a bimodal audiovisual listening context.

846212.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
846212.value: This ECS project has shown that Chinese ESL undergraduates who have learnt English for almost twenty years and have passed the university entry examination are still having difficulties in understanding English spoken by native English speakers. This project has revealed that the root cause of this listening difficulty is the deficit in processing reduced forms in English (the pronunciation deviated from the citation forms of English, e.g., yeshay for yesterday). This study not only provides the overall accuracy of the listening performances but the specific areas of difficulties through error analyses. The Chinese ESL learners make wild guess of native spoken English some time and make systematic errors some time. Educators can make use of the information provided by me to devise training materials. In addition, I have identified the proximal (near) and distal (far) cognitive-linguistic correlates that impact on nonnative listening comprehension. We can now better understand the core skills for the development of nonnative listening skills and the pathway of the development. As listening skills cannot be mastered within a day, the information is useful for educators and the learners to understand what skills are needed in the course of the development of listening comprehension.

846412.label: Project Title(Chinese)
846412.value: 香港職前數學教師的知識能力：新高中課程改革期間其預備情況及強弱項

846412.label: Co - Investigator(s)
846412.value: Dr LEUNG , Allen Yuk Lun Prof WONG, Ngai Ying

846412.label: Project Objectives
846412.value: How well are pre-service mathematics teachers in Hong Kong equipped with subject knowledge, pedagogical content knowledge, and beliefs in order to accomplish mathematics teaching? Is the professional knowledge of pre-service mathematics teachers in Hong Kong up to international standards? What strengths and weaknesses do the Hong Kong mathematics teachers have compared to teachers from other parts of the world, i.e., pre-service mathematics teachers from the West and other East Asian countries? What relationships among professional knowledge, beliefs, and teaching exist amongst the Hong Kong pre-service mathematics teachers? Are these patterns adequate for the paradigm shift from "content" to "process" of curriculum reform?

846412.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
846412.value: During the period of the New Senior Secondary (NSS) curriculum reform, teachers’ professional knowledge will be of utmost importance in coping with the challenge both in adapting to the new curriculum and managing the paradigm shift associated with such a momentous change. This investigation evaluates the professional competency of pre-service mathematics teachers in Hong Kong and clarifies the extent to which they are prepared for the change. This serves as an indication of how our teacher preparation system is meeting the challenge. To evaluate this, a mixed method approach that comprises both quantitative and qualitative methods (such as interview and observations) will be used. Questionnaires and mathematics tests will be used in the first phases of data collection, followed by qualitative methods in the second phase. For the qualitative part, considering the need to link the teachers’ beliefs and practices, we adopted the case study approach. The cases will be identified through quantitative methods. Through revealing the knowledge and beliefs of the teachers and how they approach classroom teaching, the research team will be in a strong position to assert the linkage between beliefs and practices. Interviews will be conducted and preceded by observation of classroom teaching during the participants’ teaching practice. In-depth case studies will also be conducted to portray how the professional knowledge and beliefs of pre-service mathematics teachers affect their teaching. Personal statements and teaching journals will also be collected. The results of empirical studies will be compared to the results collected from teachers in other educational regions such as: Germany and Australia (Schwarz, et al 2008, Corleis, et al 2008), and South Korea (Leung & Lew 2010) to identify strengths and weaknesses of Hong Kong teachers. The data and results from a prior research supported by Internal Research Grant (2010-2011), which is conducted by the same principle investigator of the Hong Kong Institute of Education, will serves as a reference of pilot comparison. The results of this investigation will lead to the development of plans and measures to improve the quality and professionalism mathematics teacher education in Hong Kong, in particular, to help the system meet the challenge of curriculum reform. 面對新高中課程改革的挑戰，教師的專業知識是為適應新課程及教學管理模式的轉變中重要的一環。本研究的目的旨在討論香港職前數學教師如何在專業知識上面對課程改革帶來的變化，也是作為我們的教師訓練體系中，用以迎接挑戰的一個重要指標。我們將以量化和質化的方法（如訪談和觀察）作為是次研究的方法。在第一階段，我們將會以問卷調查和數學知識測試的形式收集數據，而在第二階段，則以質化研究方法進行。對於此部分，由於考慮到教師的教學理念及實踐之間的關係，我們將以個案研究進行研究。通過分析教師的學科知識和教學理念，以及觀察他們如何在課堂中教授。研究後我們將會得出教師的教學理念和實踐之間的關係。透過觀課、課後會談、個人資料及教案分析，個案研究等，將深入分析職前數學教師的專業知識和教學理念如何影響他們的教學。研究結果也會與其他地區，例如：德國和澳洲（Schwarz, et al 2008, Corleis, et al 2008），韓國（Leung & Lew 2010）等相關研究的結果作比較，以分析香港教師的優點和缺點。過去由香港教育學院內部研究基金（2010-2011）支持的相關研究調查的數據和結果，也將作為試點比較的參考。是次調查的結果將有助促進數學教師的教育專業發展並提高他們的素質，從而協助師訓體系去迎接課程改革所帶來的各種挑戰。
